column2: The patient is a 56-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage IV renal cell carcinoma. He has no significant past medical history, but he smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He reports feeling fatigued and has noticed some back pain. He has not received any previous systemic therapy for his cancer. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His organ function is adequate, and he has no gastrointestinal conditions that could increase the risk of bleeding. He has not had any major surgeries or traumas within the past 28 days. He does not have any clinical signs of active bleeding or bleeding diathesis. He has not received any radiation or tumor embolism therapy within the past 14 days. He has not received any chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biological therapy, study medication, or hormonal therapy within the past 14 days or 5 half-lives of the respective substance (whichever is longer) before the first intake of the study drug. He has no present toxicity > CTC 1° from prior anti-tumor therapy, and his toxicities have not worsened in severity.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of liver cancer. He was diagnosed with liver cancer 6 months ago and has been receiving chemotherapy treatment for the past 3 months. He has been experiencing severe pain in his abdomen for the past 2 months. The pain is dull and constant and is rated as 8 out of 10 on a pain scale. He has been taking painkillers, but they only provide temporary relief. He has never received any other treatment for pain relief. He has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is married and has two children. He is retired and used to work as a construction worker. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no allergies to any medication. He is able to lie flat or sit prostrate for 30 minutes without any discomfort. His performance score is 2. He has not participated in any other clinical trials for pain relief. His imaging studies did not show any evidence of encephalic tumor or metastasis. He does not have a cardiac pacemaker or metal stand. His anticipated survival is more than 3 months.

65 year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and congestive heart failure presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath and lower extremity edema over the past week. He has been taking his diuretic medication as prescribed but has not seen any improvement. He reports feeling fatigued and has had difficulty completing daily tasks. Physical exam reveals elevated jugular venous pressure, bibasilar crackles, and 3+ pitting edema in his lower extremities. Labs reveal a serum sodium level of 133 mmol/L. Chest X-ray shows bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary vascular congestion. Patient is admitted to the hospital for acute decompensated heart failure with hyponatremia. Despite receiving IV loop diuretics and fluid restriction, he continues to have minimal weight loss and worsening symptoms. He is therefore considered for the Tolvaptan for Advanced or Refractory Heart Failure clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of inadequate clinical response and severe hyponatremia.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who presents to the periodontics clinic with a history of bleeding gums and bad breath. He has a history of smoking 10 cigarettes per day for the past 20 years and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. Upon examination, he is diagnosed with chronic periodontitis and three walled intrabony defects (IBD) of 4mm depth in his lower left molar. He has a platelet count of 250,000/mm3 and good oral hygiene (PI score of 1.2). He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his periodontal health and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old female diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 2 years ago. She is currently taking levodopa-carbidopa 25/100 mg three times daily and pramipexole 0.375 mg once daily. Her Hoehn & Yahr stage is 2 in the clinical "ON" state. She complains of constipation and has a GSRS score of 3. She consumes less than 20 grams of fiber daily according to the Block Fruit/Vegetable/Fiber screener. The patient is willing to make dietary changes to follow a Mediterranean diet and/or receive standard of care for constipation during the intervention period. She is able to complete daily and weekly questionnaires and 12 dietary recalls over approximately 10 weeks. The patient is able to provide stool samples during the study collection periods. She is willing to avoid strenuous exercise and alcohol such as beer, wine, and cocktails 24 hours prior to each of the 3 study visits. The patient is able to fast (no food or drink, except water, or decaf tea) at least 12 hours before each study visit. She is willing to discontinue taking prebiotic, herbal, or high-dose vitamin or mineral supplements that may impact inflammation during the pre-baseline period and throughout the study protocol.

65 F with a history of metastatic breast cancer presents with progressive weakness and numbness in her lower extremities. MRI reveals a T12 vertebral body lesion with epidural extension causing compression of the spinal cord. She has a Bilsky radiologic score of 1c-2. She has been on multiple lines of chemotherapy and is currently on a break from treatment due to side effects. Her performance status is KPS 60, and she has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. She is not a surgical candidate due to progressive systemic disease and poor functional status. She has not received radiotherapy to the same region of the spine previously. She is willing and able to lie flat for at least 20 minutes for radiotherapy treatments.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV colon cancer that has metastasized to the liver and lungs. The patient has had two cycles of chemotherapy with FOLFOX regimen but has experienced progression of the disease. The patient is currently experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and shortness of breath, and has lost 10lbs in the past month. The patient has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. The patient is a former smoker but quit 20 years ago and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a Karnofsky performance score of 80%. The patient has no active brain metastases, and tumor biopsies can be obtained for correlative pharmacodynamic studies. The patient has measurable disease by CT scan and has not received any other anticancer therapy in the past 4 weeks. The patient is willing to undergo PET scans and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has a negative pregnancy test and is using effective contraception. The patient's ANC is 2,000/mm3 and platelet count is 120,000/mm3. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who experiences discomfort and cramps during menstruation. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has tried home remedies like heating pads and pain medications in the past to alleviate pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of daily ginger tea consumption in reducing period discomfort. She is willing to refrain from taking pain medications, herbal supplements, and home remedies during the study period and agrees to drink ginger tea daily. She is not taking oral contraceptives, does not work night shifts, and is not lactating. She does not have any uterine problems such as fibroids or polycystic ovarian syndrome that cause secondary dysmenorrhea.

A 45 year old woman is scheduled to undergo pelvic surgery for the removal of a uterine fibroid. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is able to read and speak English fluently and is willing to provide informed consent. She is willing to be admitted overnight after the surgery and be contacted by phone for follow-up. She is not taking opioids for any chronic pain syndrome. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve post-operative outcomes for future patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has end-stage renal disease due to hypertension. He has been on hemodialysis for the last year and is on the waiting list for a deceased donor kidney. His PRA is 80% and he has a sum DSA of 600 MFI. He has been on the waiting list for a year and is very anxious to receive a kidney transplant. He has no history of malignancy or serious medical or psychiatric illness. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 140/90 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 8000 /mm3 Plt: 300000 /ml Creatinine: 10 mg/dl BUN: 80 mg/dl. He is married with two children and works as a manager in a retail store. He has no history of allergies or significant surgical procedures. He is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control with his wife during the study since he has no plans to conceive a child in the next year. He understands the purpose and risks of the study and is willing to sign a statement of informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of open-angle glaucoma who requires surgery due to the failure of previous medical treatment. He has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to medications, and he has not undergone any ocular surgery in the past. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are controlled with medications. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes, and his intraocular pressure is 28 mmHg in the right eye and 27 mmHg in the left eye. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has been informed about the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who recently tested positive for HCV genotype 1a during routine blood work. He has a history of heavy alcohol use in the past but has been sober for the past year. He does not have any significant medical history or co-morbidities. He is currently not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat his HCV infection. He is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and all protocol requirements. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and voluntarily signs and dates an institutional review board (IRB) approved informed consent. His lab results show normal liver function tests and no other significant abnormalities.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with urothelial carcinoma of the bladder. He underwent cystectomy with no macroscopic residual disease. Pathology reports showed that the cancer was of high grade and had invaded the bladder muscle (T3a). He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no prior history of cancer. Imaging studies did not show evidence of metastatic disease. His recent blood work and cardiac evaluation were within normal limits. He does not have active inflammatory bowel disease or any severe acute co-morbidities. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive adjuvant radiation therapy after surgery for high-risk bladder cancer.

A 29 year old female presents to the clinic complaining of palpitations and chest discomfort. She reports experiencing episodes of rapid heart rate, usually at rest, that can last for several hours. She also feels lightheaded and dizzy during these episodes. She has no history of heart disease, hypertension or diabetes. She is not taking any medications. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Her physical exam is otherwise unremarkable. She underwent a 24-hour Holter monitoring which revealed an average heart rate of 105 bpm with a maximum of 125 bpm. The ECG showed sinus tachycardia with no other abnormalities. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

23-year-old male with type 1 diabetes, diagnosed at age 16, currently practicing carbohydrate counting and functional insulin therapy. He is covered by social security and able to read and understand the study protocol. The patient has no history of substance abuse or psychological conditions that would prevent him from following the study protocol. He is compliant with his diabetes management and is interested in participating in this study to contribute to research efforts in diabetes care.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of systemic sclerosis and dystrophic calcinosis cutis. She has multiple calcified nodules on her arms and legs that are causing significant pain and disability. She has tried various treatments in the past, including calcium channel blockers and colchicine, but has not experienced any significant improvement. The patient is currently taking prednisone for her systemic sclerosis. She is willing to participate in a pilot study to investigate whether topical sodium thiosulfate is an effective therapy for calcinosis cutis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not allergic to sulfa or zinc.

A 70-year-old male with no significant medical history, currently taking only one medication for hypertension, presents for a Phase 1 clinical trial assessing the pharmacokinetics of XNW4107 in healthy adult elderly males and females. The patient is 5'11" tall, weighs 93kg, and has a BMI of 28.2. He is willing to abstain from alcohol, caffeine, and xanthine-containing beverages or food for 48 hours prior to study drug administration until discharge from the clinical unit. The patient has not donated blood or plasma within the last 30 days and has not received a blood transfusion within the last year. He is willing to contracept and understands that he must be non-pregnant and non-lactating. The patient has no history of seizure disorder, Clostridium difficile infection, or positive testing for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). He has not tested positive for HIV Ab, HBsAg, or HCV Ab. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has no other conditions that would make him unsuitable for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by the rheumatology department. She complains of diffuse musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances. She has been on various medications including pregabalin, amitriptyline, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) with partial relief of her symptoms. She has no history of peripheral polyneuropathy, diabetes mellitus, chronic renal failure, hepatitis, or malnutrition. She denies alcohol abuse and has a normal fasting glucose level. She is not pregnant and has no pacemaker or defibrillator. She is able to lay the palms of her hands and soles of her feet on the plate electrodes for Sudoscan testing. She is not taking any medications with anticholinergics, tricyclic antidepressants, antihistamines, or muscle relaxants. She is interested in participating in this study to help further understanding of fibromyalgia and to potentially improve diagnosis and treatment options for this condition.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman residing in the United Kingdom who frequently shops at two high street retailers that participate in the Cancer Loyalty Card Study (CLOCS). She has been diagnosed with ovarian cancer within the past two years and is currently undergoing treatment. She has been informed about the CLOCS study by her healthcare team and has expressed interest in participating. As part of the study, she will be asked to complete a short questionnaire about well-established ovarian cancer risk factors and common symptoms. She will also provide consent for the study team to access her loyalty card purchase data from the participating retailers for up to 7 years prior to her diagnosis. Her participation in the study will help researchers investigate whether purchase behavior can be used as an opportunity for cancer symptom surveillance to detect significant changes in purchase behaviors of ovarian cancer patients prior to their diagnosis.

A 62-year-old woman with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with coronary artery disease. She is scheduled for off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery (OPCAB) in the following week. Her diabetes is well-controlled with metformin and insulin therapy. She has never smoked and has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or stroke. Her ejection fraction is above 50%. She is currently on losartan and amlodipine for hypertension. Her physical examination reveals no significant findings. Her baseline laboratory tests and electrocardiogram are within normal limits. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of moderate periodontitis. She has not undergone any periodontal therapy in the past 6 months and is not currently on any antibiotics or systemic statin therapy. She has a moderate probing depth of 5-6 mm and clinical attachment loss of 4-6 mm. Her intraoral periapical radiographs show vertical bone loss of ≥ 3 mm. She has more than 20 teeth and is not a smoker, alcoholic, or pregnant or lactating. She has no known allergies to RSV. The patient is in good general health and has no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was diagnosed with colon cancer during a routine colonoscopy. The biopsy confirmed that it was colon adenocarcinoma. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy for colon cancer. The tumor is deemed surgically resectable and has a diameter of 1 cm. The patient's ECOG Performance Scale is 1. The patient's MSI testing has been confirmed and the archival tissue block containing colon adenocarcinoma is available prior to enrollment. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent/assent for the trial. The patient has a measurable primary lesion by lower endoscopy or CT-imaging. The patient has no histologically confirmed disseminated disease by CT or PET-CT staging. The patient's laboratory values for hematological, renal, hepatic, and coagulation functions are within normal range. The patient has not received any steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. The patient has no known history of active TB or known hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or any of its excipients. The patient is not currently participating or receiving study therapy or has participated in a study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of treatment. The patient has not been diagnosed with immunodeficiency.

50-year-old male with a history of vascular disease and mild to moderate hyperhomocysteinemia. The patient has been diagnosed with hypertension, dyslipidemia, and atherosclerosis, and is currently being treated with beta-blockers, statins, and antiplatelet therapy. The patient is interested in exploring natural supplements as an adjunct to his current treatment regimen and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) on homocysteine levels. The patient has not taken any methionine or SAMe supplements in the past three months and is not currently taking B 100 or other high-dose B vitamin supplements.

Patient is a 45yo woman with a diagnosis of systemic scleroderma who has been experiencing recurrent painful digital ulcers in her hands. She has tried several medications but has not had significant improvement in her symptoms. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction. She is not currently taking any medications for erectile dysfunction. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He is in good general health with no significant medical history. He has not received any treatment for his myeloma yet. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial, which aims to evaluate hematopoietic progenitor cell mobilization in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients undergoing upfront autologous transplantation. The patient will be undergoing mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells (PBPC) for high dose therapy and autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). The mobilization will be accomplished by using cytokines, most commonly granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF), either alone or in combination with chemotherapy or plerixafor. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the mobilization process and data will be collected to evaluate the efficacy of the mobilization regimens, their cost, associated healthcare resource utilization and impact on post transplantation outcomes.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman between the ages of 50 and 65. She has been experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes and is looking for a potential treatment option. Her body mass index falls within the range of 18 and 38 kg/m2. She does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past year, nor does she have any clinically significant abnormal laboratory results or ongoing conditions that could interfere with the interpretation of vasomotor symptoms. She is not currently experiencing uncontrolled hypertension and does not have a history of hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, or abnormal thyroid function.

A 25-year-old right-handed female presents with a history of restricting-type anorexia nervosa. She reports feeling fatigued and weak, with a BMI of 16.2 kg/m2. She has no history of substance use disorder or psychiatric illness. She is not currently taking any psychoactive medications. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no contraindications for fMRI or intranasal oxytocin administration. She has no food allergies that cannot be accommodated through substitutions to the laboratory test meal.

This is a 52 year-old female who has been experiencing fatigue, pruritus, and yellowing of the skin and eyes for the past 8 months. She was diagnosed with Primary Biliary Cirrhosis (PBC) after undergoing liver biopsy which showed destruction of interlobular and septal bile ducts. She has been on ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) for the past 6 months and is still experiencing symptoms. Her serum bilirubin is currently 2.5 mg%, and her serum albumin is 3.2 gm%. She has positive antimitochondrial antibody test and her liver biopsy, taken within the past 6 months, is compatible with the diagnosis of PBC. She has undergone ultrasound, computed tomography (CT) and cholangiography of the biliary tree which exclude biliary obstruction. She has not received any immunosuppressive agents in the preceding 3 months, and her blood tests show WBC of 4,000 mm3, granulocytes of 2,500 mm3, and platelets of 120,000mm3. She has no ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, or variceal bleed. She is willing to use an adequate form of birth control if needed. She does not have epilepsy requiring the use of dilantin, or any malignant disease within the past 5 years. Her creatinine clearance is 80 ml per minute, and she has no severe lung disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores whether methotrexate improves the therapeutic effects of UDCA in PBC.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing joint pain, particularly in the hands, for the past 8 weeks. She works as a secretary and has noticed that her symptoms have been affecting her ability to type and write. She has not received any prior treatment for her joint pain. She has no history of inflammatory joint disease or other medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and has no allergies. Her blood tests reveal an elevated ESR and CRP level. Her serology tests are positive for anti-CCP and RF. She has no history of tuberculosis, histoplasmosis, or listeriosis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male who was diagnosed with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) six months ago. He has received chemotherapy as a primary treatment but did not achieve complete remission. His PET scan showed that he had a relapse with multiple enlarged lymph nodes. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has no significant cardiac history and his blood pressure is well controlled. He has no history of drug abuse or long-term alcoholism. His lab results show that his absolute neutrophil count is 2.5 × 109/L, platelet count is 120 × 109/L, Hb level is 100g/L, and his liver and kidney function tests are normal. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no central nervous system involvement and has no other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing feelings of sadness and anxiety for several months. She has difficulty sleeping and concentrating, and often feels overwhelmed. She has noticed a decrease in her appetite and has lost weight as a result. She has been feeling hopeless and has had thoughts of self-harm. She has not been taking any psychotropic medications and has not made any recent changes to her medication regimen. She has a history of Major Depressive Disorder and has been previously diagnosed with co-morbid symptoms of anxiety. She scored in the mild-to-severe range on the BDI-II and mild-moderate on the BAI. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of depression and anxiety.

Patient is a 57-year-old male from the United States who has recently been diagnosed with high-risk localized prostate cancer. He reports no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His BMI is 26, BP: 135/80, HR: 75/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for a PSA level of 15 ng/mL, and a biopsy showing Gleason score 9 prostate cancer with involvement of 5 of 12 cores. Imaging studies show no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has been referred for surgery, but has elected to participate in this clinical trial.

A 9-year-old Caucasian boy presents to the emergency department with a non-operative fracture of his left forearm after falling off his bike. He weighs 25 kg and has no known medical history. His parents are present and give consent for his participation in the clinical trial. The boy is calm and cooperative but complains of moderate pain in his arm. He rates his pain as 6 on a scale of 0-10. He is able to speak English fluently. The initial assessment reveals no signs of hypertension, coronary artery disease, or any other exclusion criteria. The patient is classified as ASA I. He has no prior allergies to ketamine. His baseline vital signs are within normal limits.

This is a 48-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for several weeks. An abdominal ultrasound revealed a solid lesion in her pancreas. She has been referred to undergo an endoscopic ultrasonography guided fine needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) procedure to obtain a tissue sample for diagnosis. She meets the inclusion criteria for this prospective randomized trial comparing the diagnostic yield of stylet-free, solid lesion EUS-FNA using the 22 G FNA vs the 25 G FNA needle. She does not have any suspected diagnosis of lymphoma, GIST, sarcoidosis or other lesions in which a large amount of tissue will be required for diagnosis, and does not have any significant coagulopathy or use of anticoagulants, which are exclusion criteria for this trial. She is willing to sign the informed consent and participate in the study. Her procedure will be performed by experienced endosonographers with a lineal echoendoscope, and she will be monitored for immediate complications during and after the procedure. The cytological analysis of her tissue samples will be used to evaluate the diagnostic yield of the 22 G and 25 G needles, and she will be followed up for the next 6 months to assess clinical and radiological progression.

A 6-month-old male infant presents with a history of cholestatic liver disease, characterized by elevated liver enzymes and direct bilirubin. The infant is diagnosed with parenteral nutrition associated liver disease (PNALD) and has been receiving parenteral nutrition for the past 2 months. The infant is dependent on parenteral nutrition for nutritional support and is unable to tolerate enteral feeding due to severe vomiting and diarrhea. The infant has been treated with ursodiol and a reduction of copper and manganese from PN. The infant has no known allergies to seafood or egg protein. The infant's liver function tests have shown two consecutive direct bilirubins > 2.0 mg/dl, one week apart. The infant's triglycerides are within normal range. The infant's parents have provided consent for the infant to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer 2 years ago and underwent prostatectomy. He has been on active surveillance since then, with regular follow-up appointments and PSA monitoring. His latest PSA level was 6 ng/mL, which is slightly elevated compared to his previous levels. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. He has no allergies to medications and is able to tolerate imaging procedures without any issues. The patient has no bilateral hip prostheses and is able to undergo imaging procedures without any contraindications. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of rhPSMA-7.3 (18F) injection in patients with prostate cancer.

A 28-year-old Hispanic male with simple obesity presents with a waist circumference of 100 cm. He is currently working as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a BMI of 32.1 kg/m2 and is concerned about his weight gain. He has tried several diets and exercise programs in the past, but has not seen significant results. He has no history of endocrine disorders, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, or abnormal liver and kidney functions. He is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of eating disorders. He is not taking any medications that affect his weight or appetite. He has no history of surgical weight loss or postoperative adhesions. He has not participated in any clinical studies for weight loss in the past 3 months. He has no skin ruptures, allergies or scar constitution. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial for simple obesity treatment and is able to understand and sign the informed consent.

Parents of a premature baby born between 2007 and 2010, at 29-32 weeks of gestation, may be eligible to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of palivizumab administration on airway reactivity (AHR) in premature babies. The trial aims to investigate the link between early RSV infection and chronic respiratory morbidity and evaluate the effect of palivizumab on respiratory morbidity, airway inflammation, and allergy. Participants should not have any mechanical ventilation or chronic diseases, such as bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), cystic fibrosis (CF), congenital heart disease, congenital anomalies, known immunodeficiency, or receipt of other RSV investigative vaccines or therapies. The trial will evaluate airway reactivity through a methacholine challenge test and determine PC20. Respiratory morbidity will be assessed through questionnaire and telephone interviews, and additional evaluations will include IGE, eosinophil count, and exhaled NO. The study will include two groups of 37 participants each, born before and after the approval of Synagis for this group in Israel. If interested, please contact the study coordinator for more information.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing persistent cough, fever, and night sweats for several weeks. He has undergone sputum and chest CT scans which have confirmed the diagnosis of MDR-TB with visible lung lesions. He has no known allergies or any other medical conditions. He has voluntarily agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of adjunctive recombinant human Interleukin-2 therapy in treating MDR-TB. The patient has provided written informed consent and will undergo standard anti-MDR-TB chemotherapy regimen for 24-months, with the addition of low-dose rhIL-2 given subcutaneously every other day for 30 days in each of four courses. The patient will be followed up for a minimum of 36-months or until the end of the study. The patient will undergo regular sputum and imaging tests to monitor the progress of the treatment.

A 45-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife after he complained of a severe headache and dizziness. He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, for which he takes medication inconsistently. On arrival, his blood pressure was measured at 160/100 mm Hg. The patient reported that he had not been taking his medications as prescribed. The headache resolved after receiving intravenous fluids and pain medication. The ED physician counseled the patient about hypertension, its risks, and the importance of medication adherence. The patient agreed to follow-up and was given an appointment with his primary care physician for a week after discharge. The patient provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being 19 years or older and having a diastolic BP of 90 mm Hg or systolic BP of 140 mm Hg. He is not excluded from the study as he is willing to provide informed consent and is not on any pain medication that could compromise his ability to consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced colorectal cancer. She has not received any prior systemic anti-cancer treatment and her relapse or metastases occurred more than 12 months after adjuvant chemotherapy. She has at least one measurable lesion and an ECOG performance status of 1. Her main organ function meets the required criteria, with an HB level of 95g/L, ANC of 1.8 × 109/L, PLT of 90 × 109/L, BIL <1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT and AST <2.5 × ULN. Her serum Cr level is also within the normal range. She has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina pectoris or Grade III or IV heart failure (NYHA classification). She has not received anlotinib or any other immune checkpoint inhibitor before. She has no known or clinically suspected brain metastases, autoimmune disease or organ transplantation. She has not undergone any severe wounds or surgery in the past 4 weeks. She has not received glucocorticoid or immunosuppressive agents. She has no history of a second malignancy during the past 5 years. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has given her written declaration of consent to participate in the clinical trial. Her estimated life expectancy is over 12 months.

72-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents to the cardiology clinic complaining of chest pain with exertion and shortness of breath. He underwent a cardiac catheterization, which showed severe aortic stenosis and concomitant coronary artery disease. The patient is accepted for TAVI and PCI by the multidisciplinary Heart Team. The patient is asymptomatic at rest, but experiences chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion. He is able to walk only one block before experiencing symptoms. He is currently taking aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the safety and efficacy of FFR-guided complete coronary revascularization before (within 1-40 days) or after (within 1-40 days) TAVI using the Edwards SAPIEN Transcatheter Heart Valve®.

56-year-old male with a history of stable coronary artery disease, who presented with chest pain and shortness of breath. He underwent cardiac catheterization and was found to have a significant blockage in one of his coronary arteries, for which he required percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the use of iodinated contrast media. He has been on optimal medical treatment for his CAD and has no history of kidney disease. The patient agrees to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. A biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma in the right lung. Staging tests revealed that the cancer has not spread to any other part of the body, but it cannot be surgically removed. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago. He does not consume alcohol and has no known drug allergies. The patient's performance status is good, with an ECOG score of 1. The patient has not undergone any previous treatments for lung cancer. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

This is a 58 year old male who was admitted to the ICU with septic shock and multi-organ failure due to pneumonia. His INR is 1.8 and he is actively bleeding from his gastrointestinal tract. 6 yo M with a diagnosis of mucopolysaccharidosis type IH (Hurler syndrome) currently being followed by genetics and metabolic clinic for management. A 58-year-old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia for the past 5 years is seeking participation in a clinical trial. 28-month-old male toddler with a confirmed diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) as confirmed by the ADOS-2 (module 1). The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months, including persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed, and difficulty sleeping. The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection 5 years ago. He received interferon-based therapy for 48 weeks and achieved sustained virologic response (SVR). The patient is a 20-year-old woman who recently got married and lives in a rural area in Gaibandha district, Bangladesh. The patient is a 16-year-old female high school student who has been diagnosed with asthma and prescribed albuterol inhaler and a daily inhaled corticosteroid. The patient is a 58-year-old non-smoking male who was diagnosed with lung cancer. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension that is well controlled with medication. A 35-year-old female diagnosed with psoriasis is currently being treated with biologic medication injection at two separate sites during her dermatology clinic visits. She has been experiencing pain during and after the injection of the medication, which has been causing her anxiety and distress. She has a good understanding of English and is willing to participate in a research study that aims to evaluate the efficacy of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) in reducing the pain associated with biologic medication injection. She will be required to undergo the injection of medication in one thigh without TENS therapy to establish a control for how painful the injection experience is. In the second step, she will undergo the injection of medication in the other thigh with TENS therapy applied to the skin of the thigh approximately two centimeters from the site where injection of the biological medication takes place. She will be given a brief survey to determine her pain level immediately after both steps. The study will be conducted at the Department of Dermatology at Wake Forest School of Medicine, and only individuals who meet the inclusion criteria and have a good understanding of English will be eligible to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with peripheral artery disease in his right leg. The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of advanced breast cancer that has metastasized to her liver and lungs. The patient is a 55 year old male who presented to his primary care physician with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss. As this clinical trial is an ancillary/correlative observational study, no specific patient description is necessary. Patients who have previously provided tissue samples to the Children's Oncology Group (COG) tissue repository and meet the inclusion criteria are eligible for this study. The study will use tissue samples from ten human primary osteosarcoma cases and matched normal tissue where available. The samples will be analyzed for genetic biomarkers related to osteosarcoma using PET sequencing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH).

A 55-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of restless legs syndrome (RLS) for over a year. Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with prediabetes according to the American Diabetes Association. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of greater than three months. His liver involvement is less than 50%, and he has at least one measurable colorectal liver metastasis and at least one other measurable metastasis. He is expected to be able to comply with follow-up requirements and has no contraindications to oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, leucovorin, ipilimumab, GLA-SE, or nivolumab. He has not received any other anticancer therapy within two weeks prior to the start of the study, and any adverse events due to previously administered agents have recovered to less than or equal to grade 1 at baseline. He is a male with a history of surgical sterilization, and his partner uses an effective contraceptive method. He is willing to use condoms and abstain from heterosexual activity for the course of the study through seven months after the last dose of study medication. He has signed informed consent and is affiliated with or a beneficiary of a social security system.

45yo male with a history of hypertension and smoking, with an unruptured intracranial aneurysm detected incidentally on a routine CT scan. The patient has been taking aspirin and clopidogrel, but recent P2Y12 assay has shown resistance to clopidogrel. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare two different antiplatelet preparations (dual-antiplatelet and triple-antiplatelet) to determine the most effective treatment for his condition. The patient is willing and able to communicate with the researchers and has provided informed consent.

A 42-year-old female patient with a history of chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1, who has not received any previous treatment for the condition. The patient is currently under the care of a healthcare provider in the Russian Federation and is being considered for treatment with the paritaprevir / ritonavir - ombitasvir regimen, with or without dasabuvir and ribavirin in line with the current local label. The patient must provide informed consent prior to inclusion in the study and must not be participating in any concurrent interventional therapeutic trial.

The patient is a 30 year old Asian female diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) based on the Revised 2003 Rotterdam criteria of PCOS. She has been trying to conceive for 2 years with no success. She has not undergone any ovarian stimulation treatment in the last 30 days and has no history of thromboembolism. She has no history of ovarian malignancy, severe endometriosis, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, severe uterine factor subfertility, or severe tubal factor subfertility. She has not undergone treatment for malignancy in the last 5 years. Her partner has no severe male factor subfertility requiring testicular sperm extraction (TESE) or oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. They do not require preimplantation genetic screening or diagnosis. She is not over 40 years old and has not received a stimulation dose over 150 IU of exogenous FSH. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares clinical outcomes between IVM and minimal stimulation IVF in patients with PCOS.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness for several years. She was diagnosed with osteoarthritis in her left knee three years ago and has tried various treatments, such as physical therapy, pain medication, and corticosteroid injections without significant improvement. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She also has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit five years ago. She has no known allergies and is up to date on all age and gender appropriate cancer screenings. She is willing to maintain contraceptive therapy for the duration of the study. She has not been exposed to any investigational drugs or procedures within the last month and is not enrolled in any concurrent study that may confound the results of this study. She has no active infectious diseases and has not been diagnosed with HIV, HTLV, HBV, HCV, CMV or syphilis. She has a resting heart rate of 80 bpm and a systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg. She is willing and able to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, as it is a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies on the association of low-calorie sweetened beverages with cardiometabolic outcomes. Therefore, there is no patient description required.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it is a population-based study aiming to recruit a random and representative sample of individuals within several Zambian communities for markers of Hepatitis B Virus (HBV). However, eligible participants for Part 1 of the study must be 18 years or older and currently reside in a selected household. For Part 2 of the study, eligible participants must have tested positive for HBsAg by rapid point-of-care test and have been a participant in Part 1 of the study. Exclusion criteria include being unable to provide informed consent or unwilling to travel to a hospital in their province, but there is no specific patient description for this study.

The patient is a 50 year old male presenting with symptoms of prostatostasis for the past 6 months. He has experienced difficulty in urination, decreased urine flow rate, and feeling of incomplete emptying of the bladder. His uroflowmetry test revealed a maximum flow rate of 12 ml/s and an average flow rate of 10 ml/sec. His prostate volume, as measured by TRUS, is 26 ml and his TRUS picture showed evidence of prostatostasis. He scored 15 on the I-PSS questionnaire and 18 on the IIEF-5 questionnaire. He has no history of diabetes mellitus, neurogenic disorders or pelvic trauma. He has not undergone any surgical interventions on the pelvic organs. He is not currently taking any supplements to improve erectile function, anti-androgens, anti-depressants, or finasteride. He has not been diagnosed with BPH. He is willing and able to comply with the scheme of visits according to the protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old Mexican woman who has been recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. She has been referred for elective colorectal anastomosis surgery which is scheduled in 2 weeks. She has a BMI of 25 and has no significant medical history except for hypertension which is well controlled with medication. She is entitled to the Mexican Institute of Social Security and has provided her informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She is willing to be randomized into either the group with mechanical bowel preparation or without mechanical bowel preparation. She has been made aware of the potential benefits and risks of both groups and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

24-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2 who has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. She has not undergone any surgery of the gastrointestinal tract and does not have any history of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. She has not participated in any other clinical trial with an investigational drug within the past 2 months. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. She has not donated blood within the past 4 weeks and has no laboratory values outside the reference range that are of clinical relevance. She has agreed to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site. She is not pregnant and is using adequate contraception during the study and until 1 month after study completion.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with vitiligo for the past 5 years. She has multiple depigmented areas on her face, trunk and limbs, with the largest area being approximately 10 cm2 on her left forearm. She has a history of using topical corticosteroids and calcineurin inhibitors to treat her vitiligo, but has not seen significant improvement. She has no history of UV photosensitivity or systemic treatment for vitiligo. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no plans for pregnancy. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her condition.

The patient is a 50 year old female with a history of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) diagnosed by a glaucoma specialist at Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center. She has a vertical cup-to-disc ratio of >0.8 in one eye and a mean deviation in visual field worse than <10 dB in the other eye. She has a family history of glaucoma and hypertension, which is managed with medication. She has no other ocular pathology that may interfere with visual field, disc imaging, or accurate intraocular pressure (IOP) readings. She is not pregnant or nursing, and does not have diabetes mellitus or any severe heart, liver or kidney disease. She has not had any ophthalmic surgery in the last three months and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical study. She has had experience with visual field examinations in the past two years and meets the false positive/false negative ratio criteria. She is willing to participate in the study and able to complete the study according to the requirements.

A 28-year-old woman comes to the clinic seeking treatment for opioid dependence. She has been dependent on opioids for the past 3 years and has tried several times to quit without success. She is currently using heroin and oxycodone and is experiencing severe withdrawal symptoms, including nausea, vomiting, and muscle aches. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of BNX sublingual tablets versus BNX sublingual film for the treatment of opioid dependence. The patient is in good general health, has no history of significant medical disorders, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has a reliable method of contraception and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 3 years ago. She is currently taking methotrexate (MTX) 20mg orally once a week, but she has been experiencing mild gastrointestinal side effects. She works as a librarian and is married with two teenage children. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially alleviate her side effects of MTX. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to be trained in administering the medication subcutaneously via the VIBEX MTX auto-injector device. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with recurrent genital herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection. He has had at least four episodes of genital herpes in the past year and is currently asymptomatic. He has a negative result on the HIV Ab/Ag assay and is willing to use contraception during the study participation. The patient is willing to collect a swab each day from his genital area during the swabbing periods, which are 8 weeks prior to and upon the administration of study drug. He does not have any serious medical conditions, malignancy, or immunosuppression that may interfere with the assessment of the efficacy of UB-621. He has not been exposed to HSV vaccine and has not been treated with systemic steroids or other immunomodulating agents within 30 days prior to screening or planned treatment with systemic steroids or immunomodulators during the study period. The patient has normal renal and hepatic function and no ECG abnormalities or cardiovascular conditions.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 2 years ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, muscle weakness, and cognitive impairment, which have affected her daily activities. She is classified under PDDS category 4, which means she is able to walk for more than 500 meters but needs a walking aid. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a injections and has been advised to incorporate physical activity into her lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is able to participate in light to moderate physical activity for 45 minutes once a week. She has no history of serious cardiovascular disease or advanced musculoskeletal disorders.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 2 years ago. Since then, he has been experiencing symptoms such as persistent cough, shortness of breath, and weight loss. He also has elevated liver enzymes and mild ascites. A biopsy confirmed the presence of chronic GVHD in the lungs and liver. He has not received any systemic immunosuppressive therapy for chronic GVHD yet. His renal, hepatic, pulmonary, and cardiac functions are adequate. His Karnofsky performance score is 70%. He is willing to use a reliable method of birth control during the study period. He has signed the written informed consent form.

A 42-year-old female patient with a recent diagnosis of endometrial cancer, scheduled for primary surgery at the University of Chicago Hospital. The patient is proficient in English and has no prior history of cancer treatment, except for a previous basal cell carcinoma. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve sexual function after gynecologic cancer treatment, as sexual health is an important aspect of her life.

A 36-year-old woman, who is currently 35 weeks pregnant with twins, is seeking medical attention due to her history of postpartum hemorrhage. She has had two previous pregnancies, both of which resulted in postpartum hemorrhage and required hospitalization. The patient is currently experiencing no symptoms and is seeking preventative measures to avoid another hemorrhage. She has been advised to participate in the ROTEM® Obstetric Hemorrhage Pilot Study and is willing to provide consent. The patient has a history of gestational diabetes, but is otherwise healthy. She does not have any coagulation defects or thrombocytopenia. She has not received anticoagulation therapy and is not currently enrolled in the "Tranexamic Acid for the Prevention of Obstetrical Hemorrhage After Cesarean" study.

An 67-year-old male with a history of major depressive disorder without psychotic features and generalized anxiety disorder. He has been on sertraline 100mg daily for the past 12 weeks with mild improvement in his symptoms. His MADRS score is 25. He has no history of suicide attempt or plan. He has no significant past medical history, but he has mild hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no history of neurological disorders, cardiac, renal or respiratory failure, or any other medical illnesses that may interfere with the study of positive valence system functions in depression. He has no contraindications to MRI scanning. He is able to provide written consent for research assessment and treatment.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma after experiencing persistent abdominal pain and weight loss. The CT scan showed a mass in the pancreas measuring 4 cm. The biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. The patient underwent surgery to remove the tumor followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. During the course of chemotherapy, the patient experienced a decrease in muscle mass and strength. The patient does not have any significant medical history apart from hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. The patient agrees to participate in the study to validate Total Psoas Area (TPA) measurement as an independent prognostic factor of overall survival in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of progressive dysphagia and weight loss over the past 3 months. An upper endoscopy revealed a mass in the middle third of the esophagus, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies, including CT scan and endoscopic ultrasound, showed no evidence of distant metastasis, and the tumor was staged as T3N0M0. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his blood work is within normal limits. He has no history of prior malignancy or significant comorbidities. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has agreed to use effective contraception during treatment and for 90 days after completion of study treatment.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman diagnosed with anorexia nervosa. She has been struggling with disordered eating patterns for the past 5 years and has a history of rapid weight loss and malnutrition. She has not had her menstrual period in the past year and has experienced frequent bone fractures over the last few months. She has not taken oral contraceptive pills or any other hormones in the last 8-12 weeks and has not been on any medication known to affect bone metabolism in the last 12 weeks. She has not had a fracture in the last 6 months and is not currently pregnant. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates whether growth hormone can help improve her bone health. She is willing to attend eight visits, six of which can be conducted at her home physician's office, and undergo two bone density scans, hormonal, and nutritional evaluations over a 12-week study period.

A 32-year-old female has been using cocaine on an average of once a week for the past 6 months. She is in good health and has a normal EKG. She is not pregnant, nor breast-feeding and is using effective contraceptive methods. She has no history of major psychiatric illnesses, including bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or anxiety disorders. She has no major medical illnesses such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has never been treated for chemical dependency within the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to examine the effects of carvedilol on cocaine use in humans.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with no prior medical conditions or history of allergies. He does not take any chronic medications and is a non-smoker. He has normal blood count, liver function tests, and EKG. He has no history of trauma to the limbs or neuropathic pain. His blood pressure is within normal limits. The patient is capable of understanding the experiment procedure and has signed an informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been diagnosed with periodontitis, a gum disease that affects the supporting tissues of the teeth. He has a history of smoking and has been experiencing bleeding gums, bad breath, and tooth sensitivity. Upon examination, his dentist has found that he has deep pockets between his teeth and gums, indicating that the disease has progressed. To treat his condition, he has been invited to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the effectiveness of two types of gum surgery. One surgery uses a product derived from his own blood (PRGF), while the other uses an animal-derived bone graft and membrane that have been in the market for 30 years. The trial will follow him for 12 months and assess his gum health through measurements and non-invasive technologies. He will also be given questionnaires to evaluate his preferences and the impact that each surgical treatment had on his everyday life. One intra-oral x-ray will be performed before the surgery and after 12 months to assess if new bone has formed around the teeth involved in the surgery. To be eligible for the trial, he must be 25 years or older, have clinical evidence of periodontitis, and have no medical history that includes diabetes type 1, hepatic or renal disease, or other serious medical conditions or transmittable diseases. He must also not have undergone periodontal surgery in the same area selected for the study within the past 12 months.

As this clinical trial is focused on evaluating an interactive game designed to increase people's ability to identify cancerous moles, there is no specific patient description required for this study. The study is open to residents of the United States who are at least 18 years old and capable of reading English, and who are members of the panel assembled by the survey provider. Individuals under 18 years old will be excluded from the study.

Patient is a 65-year-old male who suffered a stroke three months ago. The stroke was of ischemic origin in the carotid artery distribution and resulted in motor impairments in the left arm. The patient has some ability to complete 10º of wrist or finger extension from a 60 - 65 º flexed position and has been able to voluntarily activate slight movements in the wrist and fingers. The patient has a score of less than 56 on the UE subscale of the Fugl-Meyer Assessment and is able to attend therapy 2 days/week or 4 days/week for 2 weeks. The patient has a score of at least 16 on the Mini Mental Status Examination and is able to discriminate sharp from dull and light touch using traditional sensation tests. The patient does not have any major post-stroke complications and is free of pre-existing neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease, Multiple Sclerosis, or dementia. The patient does not have legal blindness or severe visual impairment and has a life expectancy of over one year. The patient does not have severe arthritis or orthopedic problems that limit passive ranges of motion of the upper extremity. The patient does not have a history of sustained alcoholism or drug abuse in the last six months and does not have a pacemaker or other implanted device. The patient is not pregnant.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital due to sudden onset of severe headache and left-sided weakness. A CT scan revealed the presence of an intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in the right basal ganglia region of the brain. The patient is currently stable and has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. The patient has provided informed consent for participation in the study. There are no general contraindications for undergoing an MRI. The patient is above 18 years of age and is cooperative. The patient will undergo an MRI scan within 7 hours of admission to the hospital to determine the underlying pathology of the ICH. The MRI scan will include axial T2, axial DWI, Sagittal T1, T2 flair, and axial GRE-sequence. Susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI) and Chemical Shift Imaging (CSI) multivoxel spectroscopy will also be performed. The patient will undergo another MRI scan after 8 weeks to rule out underlying pathology. After 3 months, the patient will be seen in the outpatient-clinic for follow-up evaluation.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who drinks alcohol occasionally, at least two units per week. She has no history of alcoholism, psychiatric disorders, drug abuse or dependence, or regular use of psychoactive drugs. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days. She has no major surgeries or organic diseases in the past three months. Her body mass index is 22 kg/m2, and she weighs 60 kg. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than five coffees, teas, colas, or other stimulant or xanthine beverages daily. She does not take any regular medication and has not participated in any clinical trials with drugs in the past 12 weeks. She has no allergy, intolerance, or adverse reactions to alcohol, soy, or lactose. She has no history or clinical evidence of gastrointestinal, liver, renal, or other disorders. She is able to understand the nature and consequences of the study and the procedures to be followed. She has no positive serology to Hepatitis B, C, or HIV. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using effective contraceptive methods. She has no history or presence of breast cancer.

A 52-year-old male with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer presents with worsening symptoms and progression of disease despite previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient reports a persistent cough, shortness of breath, fatigue, and weight loss. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds in the left lung and palpable lymph nodes in the neck. Imaging studies confirm the progression of lung cancer and metastasis to the lymph nodes. Laboratory results are within normal limits. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial testing a new anti-cancer drug combination of Entinostat and GSK525762C for advanced and refractory solid tumors and lymphomas. The patient meets the inclusion criteria, including the requirement of having received previous therapy with at least one combination chemotherapy regimen for metastatic disease. The patient is willing to have serial biopsies and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study and for 7 months after completion of entinostat and GSK525762C administration. The patient is signed up for the trial and will be monitored for any adverse effects throughout the study.

This is a 23 year-old male who was diagnosed with high-grade osteosarcoma in his right femur 2 years ago. He underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cisplatin followed by surgery with limb salvage. Postoperatively, he received adjuvant chemotherapy with ifosfamide and etoposide for 6 cycles. However, 6 months later, PET-CT showed progression in the right distal femur and right pulmonary nodules. He received salvage chemotherapy with gemcitabine and docetaxel for 4 cycles but the disease still progressed. A biopsy confirmed recurrent osteosarcoma. He is now seeking alternative treatments and interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, normal organ function, and measurable lesions according to RECIST 1.1. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has no history of autoimmune disease, CNS metastases or other malignancies.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) three years ago. He underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) from his brother who was a full HLA match. He received a reduced-intensity conditioning regimen before the transplant. He had no complications during the transplant and the post-transplant period. However, he developed acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) of the skin, liver, and gut. His skin rash is widespread, covering more than 50% of his body surface area. His bilirubin level is elevated, and he has abdominal pain and diarrhea. His aGVHD was treated with corticosteroids (methylprednisolone) at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day. However, despite the steroid treatment, his aGVHD has not improved, and his symptoms have worsened. He has no history of other significant medical problems, and his vital signs are stable. He is not taking any other medications except for the steroids. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive itacitinib in combination with corticosteroids to manage his aGVHD symptoms.

The patient is a 19-year-old Caucasian male who has previously participated in a study assessing his psychopathological risk. He has no history of neurological illness or trauma involving the brain, and has no sensory impairments that would interfere with his ability to complete neurocognitive tasks or interviews. The patient has an estimated IQ above 70. He has signed a consent form to be contacted for future follow-up studies. The patient will undergo a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan which includes structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), resting state functional MRI (fMRI), and fMRI during concurrent task tapping attention and emotional processes. The patient will also undergo a psychopathological evaluation, self-rating evaluation measuring temperaments and assessing possible behavioral problems, and a neurocognitive evaluation. The patient is willing to provide a drawing of a biological-genetic sample (saliva).

The patient is a healthy male or female aged between 18 and 50 years, with no history of chronic diseases, immunosuppression, or immunodeficiency. They should have no major surgery of the GI tract, including cholecystectomy or appendectomy, in the past 5 years, and no history of gastric stapling, lap band, or surgical procedure for the treatment of obesity. The patient should not have taken systemic antibiotics, antifungals, antivirals, or antiparasitics (intravenous, intramuscular, or oral) within the last 6 months, or oral, intravenous, intramuscular, nasal, or inhaled corticosteroids, cytokines, methotrexate or immunosuppressive cytotoxic agents, large doses of commercial probiotics, anabolic steroids, or intrauterine devices, among others. They should have a BMI between 18 and 35 kg/M(2), and their vital signs should be within the acceptable range. The patient should not have used antacids, laxatives, or enemas within the last 3 months, or diagnostic colonoscopy within the last 6 months. They should have no acute disease at the time of enrollment, chronic, clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, dermatologic, endocrine, GI, hepatic, or renal functional abnormality, or central nervous system disease. The patient should not have clinically significant abnormal results on electrocardiogram or active behavioral or psychiatric conditions that would be incompatible with a safe and successful participation in the study.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who underwent a sleeve gastrectomy procedure 5 years ago due to morbid obesity. Despite initial success with weight loss, he has experienced gradual weight regain over the past year and is now looking for a revision surgery. He reports experiencing occasional gastro-esophageal reflux disease symptoms, but they are manageable with medication. His past medical history includes type 2 diabetes and hypertension, both of which have improved since his initial sleeve gastrectomy surgery. His BMI is currently 38, and he is otherwise healthy.

A 30-year-old Caucasian male who is dissatisfied with the appearance of his flanks due to moderate excess bilateral fatty tissue. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any recreational drugs. He exercises regularly but has not seen a significant change in the appearance of his flanks. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications. He has no history of skin cancer or any other skin diseases, and he has no tattoos or scars in the treatment area. He is not currently pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant. He has not had any previous surgical interventions or laser treatments on his flanks. He has no electrical implants in his body and does not have any chronic or acute infections in the treatment area. He is willing and able to refrain from artificial tanning during the course of the study.

This is a 45-year-old female who is scheduled to undergo elective hysterectomy at Mayo Clinic in Arizona. She has a history of motion sickness and has experienced nausea and vomiting after previous surgeries. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and has an ASA classification of II. She is not pregnant and does not have any allergies to medications. She does not have any conditions that would impair her ability to complete study assessments. She has not taken any antiemetics within 12 hours of the surgery and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials involving an investigational product. She is interested in participating in this study to potentially reduce her risk of postoperative nausea and vomiting.

A 68-year-old male presents to the cardiology clinic for a routine check-up. He denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. The patient has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well-controlled with medication. The patient has never smoked and does not consume alcohol. On physical examination, his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Cardiac auscultation reveals a grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border. No other abnormalities are detected in the heart, lung, or abdominal examination. His echocardiogram shows severe aortic stenosis with a mean gradient of 45 mmHg and an aortic valve area of 0.7 cm². He is diagnosed with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis and is offered participation in a clinical trial comparing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) to clinical surveillance. The patient is informed of the nature of the study and agrees to its provisions.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Pompe disease. She has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue for several years, which has progressively worsened over time. She has difficulty walking and climbing stairs, and has noticed a decline in her overall physical ability. Her diagnosis was confirmed through genetic testing, which revealed a mutation in the GAA gene. The patient has been prescribed enzyme replacement therapy and has been receiving treatment for the past 6 months. She reports some improvement in her symptoms, including increased energy and improved muscle strength. She is interested in participating in a long-term study to monitor the outcomes of Pompe disease and enzyme replacement therapy. She is in overall good health and has no other significant medical history.

A 56-year-old Caucasian man with a family history of hypertension presents with high blood pressure readings. He has been experiencing headaches, dizziness, and occasional chest pain for the past few weeks. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications. His blood pressure is consistently over 140/90 mmHg over multiple visits. He has never been treated for hypertension before and has not taken angiotensin II receptor antagonists or calcium channel blockers. He has no history of stroke, diabetes mellitus, or cognitive impairment. His serum potassium level and serum creatinine level are normal. He has no known allergies to any drugs. He is willing to participate in a research study on the effects of olmesartan on cerebral glucose metabolism, vascular inflammation, and adipose tissue. He signs the informed consent form and is enrolled in the study.

58-year-old male with a history of right shoulder pain and weakness for the past year. Imaging studies revealed severe rotator cuff arthropathy, and the patient's orthopedic surgeon recommended reverse total shoulder arthroplasty. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. He has no known allergies and is able to communicate in English. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and participate in follow-up surveys.

The patient is a 26-year-old female with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She lives an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. She has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent to participate in the drug interaction study between raltegravir and UK-453,061.

A 57-year-old male presents with a history of recurrent throat pain and discomfort for several months. He has a history of tobacco and alcohol use. He was diagnosed with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV positive) six months ago and underwent concurrent chemoradiation. He had a complete response to the treatment, but he developed a persistent sore throat and difficulty swallowing. Imaging studies revealed a recurrence of the disease with multiple lymph node metastases in the neck. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no significant comorbidities. He has no history of autoimmune disease, HIV infection, or hepatitis B or C. His laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient is willing to undergo a biopsy to obtain a tumor specimen for testing.

52-year-old male with osteoarthritis of the right knee and scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) within the next month. The patient has a history of mild to moderate knee pain with limited range of motion and difficulty performing activities of daily living. The patient has no significant comorbidities and is otherwise healthy. The patient is interested in participating in a study comparing the effectiveness of the ROMTech PortableConnect device only rehabilitation program following TKA to an active comparator group of continuous passive motion with a standard of care combination HHPT and OPPT rehabilitation program. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing and able to participate in all study assessments, questionnaires, and procedures.

45-year-old male patient who suffered a severe traumatic brain injury in a motorcycle accident six months ago. He has remained in a vegetative state since the accident, with no signs of improvement in his level of consciousness.
