He is currently not on any sedative drugs or medications that could interact with the study treatment. There is no history of any neurological antecedents or metallic implants.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with rectal cancer that is still in the early stages. The tumor is localized in the rectum and has not spread to other parts of the body. The patient is scheduled to undergo minimally-invasive surgery to remove the tumor. He has no significant medical history, and his overall health is good. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent to participate in the study and has already given consent for donation of tissue for research at the time of surgery. A useable tissue sample will be taken as part of routine surgery. The patient understands the purpose of the study and is interested in contributing to research that may improve the accuracy of predicting outcomes for patients with early rectal cancer.

This is a 52 year old male with a biopsy-proven solid tumor that has metastasized and is not amenable to surgery. The patient has measurable disease by scans and no curative or more effective treatment options exist, according to the investigator. The patient has a Zubrod performance status between 0-2

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 22. He is currently on atypical antipsychotic treatment and has been for the past year. He reports experiencing auditory hallucinations and occasional delusions. He is able to maintain a part-time job and lives with his family. He has a history of substance abuse, but has been in recovery for the past year. He has no other medical conditions and is not currently taking any other medications. He has regular follow-up appointments with his psychiatrist. He is interested in participating in the study to help further research on schizophrenia and potentially improve his own treatment.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and has been experiencing neuropsychiatric symptoms related to the disease, such as hallucinations and delusions. He has previously participated in an antecedent pimavanserin study and completed it successfully. He has a designated study partner/caregiver who is fluent in the local language and agrees to participate in study assessments. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and his study partner/caregiver is not an employee of ACADIA. The patient does not have any medical conditions that would increase the risk associated with taking study medication, nor does he require treatment with a medication or other substance that is prohibited by the protocol. At screening, the patient's baseline health and psychiatric condition meet all pre-specified entry criteria for the study.

45-year-old male with a history of smoking and frequent urinary tract infections presents with hematuria and dysuria. The patient has no known history of bladder cancer or other cancers. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Urine cytology showed atypical cells suspicious for malignancy. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate new diagnostic tests for bladder cancer. The patient will provide urine and blood samples for the study. The patient has no known allergies and is willing to undergo all tests and procedures required for the study. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and is committed to following all study requirements.

A 45-year-old man with a history of liver cirrhosis and esophageal varices presents to the emergency room with a sudden onset of vomiting blood. He reports a history of alcohol abuse and also has a history of hepatitis C infection. He is currently on medications for his cirrhosis, including lactulose and spironolactone. He has no other significant medical problems. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

50 y/o male with a history of HPV-associated oropharynx cancer, currently in remission. He presents with no evidence of distant metastasis and a pathologically-proven diagnosis of T1-3 (up to 6 cm), N0-2 (AJCC 8th edition) p16 positive squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He has a smoking history of less than 10 pack-years and is not actively smoking. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. He has no comorbid conditions that would prevent him from receiving concurrent weekly cisplatin. The patient has no history of allergic reactions or severe immunosuppression. He understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent.

A 30-year-old male smoker presents for a clinical trial investigating the effects of sulforaphane (SFN) on the immune response to live attenuated influenza virus (LAIV). The patient reports smoking half a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 10 years. He has no history of respiratory infections in the past 4 weeks, and no chronic medical conditions that would preclude his participation. He is willing to avoid corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications for 1 week prior to study entry and throughout the study. He reports no allergies requiring medication in the past year and has no history of hypersensitivity to egg proteins, gentamicin, gelatin, or arginine. His physical exam is unremarkable. He is willing to avoid antioxidant vitamins and cruciferous vegetables as well as juices/drinks with vitamin supplements added for 2 days prior to Day (-1) of the protocol and throughout the subsequent study. The patient is willing to complete a food diary and avoid contact with immunocompromised individuals for 3 weeks after receiving LAIV vaccine. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo nasal lavage, blood samples and nasal biopsies for the study.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness and worry, as well as physical symptoms such as headaches and muscle tension, for the past several months. He has visited his primary care physician multiple times over this period, but has not received a clear diagnosis or effective treatment. He is interested in participating in a study that could help him better understand and manage his emotional symptoms. He has a history of mild depression and anxiety, but no history of suicide attempts or severe mental illness. He is currently employed and has a moderate level of impairment in his work and social functioning. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate voluntarily.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with early stage cervical cancer after undergoing a biopsy. She has no significant past medical history and her performance status is 0 by the ECOG criteria. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker and has no known drug allergies. She is physically fit and has no cardio-respiratory, hepato-renal or hematological issues. Her tumor is confirmed to be adenocarcinoma of the cervix and is less than 2cm in size. She has not received any prior radiation or chemotherapy treatment or undergone major pelvic surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the consent form.

A 45-year-old male with a history of high blood pressure and elevated triglyceride levels presents to the clinic. He reports feeling tired and sluggish throughout the day despite getting enough sleep. He also mentions that he has been struggling to lose weight despite following a strict diet and exercise regimen. The patient's physical exam shows a waist circumference of 96 cm, blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, and fasting glucose levels of 115 mg/dL. The patient meets the criteria for metabolic syndrome according to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of dapagliflozin on metabolic syndrome, insulin sensitivity, and insulin secretion. After confirming the patient's eligibility, he is randomized to receive either dapagliflozin or placebo for a period of 3 months. Throughout the study, the patient's glucose, insulin levels, lipid profile, creatinine, and uric acid are monitored. The patient is excited to contribute to research that may help improve his condition and the lives of others with metabolic syndrome.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) for the last 12 months. She has had trouble sleeping, has frequent nightmares related to the traumatic event she experienced, and feels easily triggered by reminders of the event. She is fluent in English and willing to give informed written consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have any comorbid mental health disorders and has not participated in attention bias modification treatment (ABMT) in the past. She does not have a history of seizure disorder, but she is currently taking a hypnotic medication to help with her sleep. She is not currently participating in formal psychotherapy. The patient has no vision loss or other unstable medical conditions.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing worsening symptoms of COPD for the past year, including shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing. He has a history of at least 2 exacerbations in the previous 12 months that required treatment with systemic glucocorticoids and/or antibiotics. His post-bronchodilator FEV1 is less than 80% of the predicted normal value, indicating moderate to very severe airflow limitation. He is currently in the stable stage of COPD but is concerned about the risk of acute exacerbation. He has no significant chronic hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, or gastrointestinal abnormalities or malignant tumor except for lung cancer. He has not had any COPD exacerbation that required treatment with antibiotics and/or systemic corticosteroids or an acute exacerbation of any other diseases in the 4 weeks prior to screening. He is not allergic to amikacin or other aminoglycosides. He has not participated in any interventional clinical trials in the three months prior to screening and does not have mental diseases or cognitive disorders that could interfere with treatment and follow-up. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who suffered a first-time TIA and stroke three weeks ago. He has been experiencing persistent oral and pharyngeal dysphagia since then, which has made it difficult for him to eat and drink normally. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication for these conditions. He had no problems with swallowing before the stroke. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His physical exam shows mild dysarthria and some weakness in the right upper and lower extremities. His blood pressure is well-controlled, and his lab work is within normal limits. He is able to follow commands and participate in rehabilitation activities. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his swallowing function and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and has previously participated in a BCX9930 trial for PNH. He experienced improvement in his PNH during the previous trial and is interested in continued access to BCX9930. He reports occasional episodes of hemoglobinuria, fatigue, and shortness of breath, but is otherwise in good health. He is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or lactating. He has no other clinically significant medical or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with his ability to participate in the study. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent. He is interested in evaluating the long-term effectiveness and impact on quality of life and general well-being of BCX9930 treatment, and his satisfaction with the medication.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing sudden vision loss in his left eye. He reports no trauma to the eye, but he has noticed a lot of floaters and reduced visibility of the fundus. The patient has no history of vascular retinal disease, uveitis, age-related macular degeneration, or recent ocular traumatism, retinal laser treatment or vitreo-retinal surgery. He smokes 10 cigarettes a day but is otherwise healthy. The patient has provided oral and written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese woman who has been recently diagnosed with HBsAg-positive status during a routine checkup. She has no history of liver disease or any other significant medical conditions. She works in a hospital as a nurse and has had no known exposure to HCV risk factors such as drug abuse, tattoo, or blood donation. She is married and has two children, both of whom are healthy. She has heard of HCV infection but does not have any knowledge about it. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to learn more about HCV infection and how to prevent it. She is interested in receiving education about HCV infection and HBV/HCV co-infection and is willing to undergo testing for HCV infection. She hopes that by participating in this trial, she can contribute to the development of a comprehensive screening strategy for HBsAg-positive patients.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who are actively involved in the Roving Caregiver Program in Grenada and have children between the ages of 0-2 years old. The ideal participant would be a parent or guardian who is willing to learn and implement the principles of Conscious Discipline, a community-based intervention program aimed at improving social-emotional connections between parents/guardians and children. Participants should be residing in at-risk communities served by the RCP, and must be enrolled in the program. The study will involve CD training provided by certified Conscious Discipline Paraprofessionals (CDPPs) who will travel to the communities and villages throughout Grenada. Post-intervention, the study will assess the ability of parents to implement CD skills with their children and neurocognitive outcomes using the INTERGROWTH 21st Neurodevelopmental Assessment (INTERNDA). The study is looking for participants who are committed to improving the neurodevelopment of their children and are willing to actively participate in the CD training and implementation process.

A 64-year-old woman diagnosed with atrial fibrillation presents with a history of stroke and is currently on oral anticoagulation therapy. She has been taking warfarin for the past 6 months and is experiencing difficulty managing her PT/INR levels. Her PT/INR levels have been inconsistent, and she has had to make frequent trips to the clinic to have her levels monitored. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new PT monitoring system that utilizes a low sample volume and is heparin insensitive, which may provide more accurate and convenient monitoring of her PT/INR levels. She is willing to comply with study procedures and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a healthy newborn baby boy with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. He was born to a 28-year-old mother who had an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. The family lives in a rural area in Guinea-Bissau and has access to basic healthcare services. The baby has no overt illness or gross malformations. The parents have given their consent for their baby to participate in a clinical trial investigating the impact of oral polio vaccine (OPV) at birth on mortality, morbidity, growth and immunological response to BCG. The trial aims to determine whether not receiving OPV at birth has any negative effects on the baby's health and immune system. The baby will be closely monitored throughout the trial and will receive standard care and vaccinations as recommended by the World Health Organization.

A 55-year-old Taiwanese female diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. She has no history of eye surgery, eye injury, or eye disease. She wears glasses with a prescription of -2.00 D in the right eye and -1.75 D in the left eye. The patient has been experiencing blurred vision, difficulty seeing at night, and glare sensitivity. Her ophthalmic examination revealed the presence of bilateral cataracts with a preoperative astigmatism of 1.25 D in the right eye and 1.50 D in the left eye. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the postoperative visual function following bilateral AcrySof Toric Intraocular Lens implantation. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the follow-up visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who underwent a routine colonoscopy that revealed a non-pedunculated polyp in the colorectal area. The size of the lesion is between 10-25 mm, and the non-lifting sign is positive. The patient has a history of smoking and is currently on medication for hypertension. He has no previous history of colorectal cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed informed consent. He has no contraindications for colonoscopy and is in good overall health.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with overactive bladder syndrome. She has tried several medications for symptom control but has not had significant improvement. She has been referred for placement of a neuromodulator and has undergone a successful Stage 1 implantation. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of diabetes or renal disease. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the course of the trial. The patient is able and willing to complete all study-related procedures and materials. She speaks English fluently and has no scheduled or planned MRIs or diathermy.

The trial is looking for childhood cancer survivors who received CNS-directed therapy for leukemia or non-Hodgkin lymphoma, are in remission and completed treatment at least 3 months ago, and are enrolled in school. The child must demonstrate a deficit in attention or memory on baseline cognitive assessment screening and have evidence of problems in learning and adaptive functioning. The participating parent or caregiver must be fluent in English and live with the child, with no known major psychiatric conditions that preclude study participation. The trial aims to test an educational and skills training intervention for parents of childhood cancer survivors with neurobehavioral dysfunction. The parent participants will receive 8 weekly face-to-face training sessions with a therapist over approximately 2-3 months, with phone assistance provided after each session to measure study adherence and behavioral implementation between the sessions. Both parent and child participants will complete battery testing and questionnaires at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months to collect preliminary data on the indirect therapeutic impact of the parent training intervention on the child's academic, cognitive, and behavioral functioning.

Patient is a 32-year-old male veteran who served in Operation Iraqi Freedom. He is seeking compensation and pension (C & P) benefits for a disability related to his military service. He has a history of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and has been experiencing symptoms of substance abuse. He is not currently receiving VBA Compensation for PTSD. He is able to participate psychologically and physically and is willing to give informed consent and complete assessments for the study. He is between the ages of 18-65 years old and is not anticipated to be incarcerated or move during the study period. He is seeking treatment for his substance abuse issues and is interested in learning about the relationship between substance use and PTSD.

56 yo male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with sudden onset blurred vision in the left eye. Exam reveals retinal hemorrhages and vein dilation and tortuosity in all 4 quadrants consistent with a diagnosis of central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). Best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is decreased in the left eye and macular edema is present. The decision has been made to treat with aflibercept (Eylea®) and the patient is considered a candidate for the Hermes Study. The patient has not received any previous treatment for CRVO and the duration of the condition is less than 4 months. The patient agrees to participate in the study and has given written, informed consent. The patient does not have any other retinal diseases in the study eye, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has effective contraception. The patient is covered by the French Health Insurance.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She requires intravenous chemotherapy treatment for at least 6 months. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. Her blood work shows no abnormalities and her coagulation values are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is affiliated with the French social security system. She has no known infections or immunosuppressive conditions. She has no contraindications for the placement of the implantable catheter in either the thoracic or humeral location. She is not a protected adult or deprived of liberty.

32F with a history of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome diagnosed at the age of 6, presents to the clinic with a relapse of proteinuria and edema. She is currently taking prednisone and cyclosporine for maintenance therapy. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and she denies any symptoms of infection or cardiovascular disease. Her past medical history is significant for a single episode of cellulitis 2 years ago that was treated with antibiotics. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her laboratory results show proteinuria of 4.5 g/24h with hypoalbuminemia (albumin 2.4 g/dL) and mild renal impairment (creatinine 1.2 mg/dL). Renal biopsy was performed at the time of initial diagnosis and showed minimal change disease. The patient is willing to participate in the SUCCESS trial to contribute to the development of a NS database in China.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath for the past few months. She reports a history of hypertension, for which she takes medication, and has no known allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. Her physical examination is unremarkable, except for mild pallor. Her hemoglobin level is 11 g/dL, which is below the normal range for women. She has not received any experimental pharmacologic agent in the prior 2 months. She is an outpatient at the Stanford Health Care (SHC) Medical Center, and her body mass index is within the eligible range for the study. She has no palpable splenomegaly and does not have any contraindication to RBC mass/plasma volume testing.

62-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presented to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of blurry vision and difficulty reading. On examination, the patient was found to have best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/80 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) showed central foveal thickness (CFT) of 420 μm and 390 μm in the right and left eyes, respectively. Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) revealed macular leakage consistent with diabetic macular edema (DME). The patient had a history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy and had undergone vitrectomy surgery in both eyes without the use of silicone oil or gas. She had no history of intraocular surgery within the past 3 months and her HbA1c was less than 10.0%. The patient was randomized to receive either intravitreal ranibizumab (IVR) or intravitreal dexamethasone implant (IDI) and will be followed monthly for 6 months. She also meets the inclusion criteria of having macular leakage on FFA and CFT more than 300 μm in the 1-mm central macular subfield on SD-OCT.

The patient is a 45 year old female who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She manages her diabetes with insulin injections and has been advised to monitor her blood glucose levels regularly. She is a busy working professional and often finds it challenging to keep up with her diabetes management. She has had difficulty operating the current blood glucose monitoring system and has been looking for a more user-friendly and efficient alternative. She is fluent in English and has no known physical, visual, or neurological impairments. She is willing to participate in this study to evaluate the Investigational Blood Glucose Monitoring System and hopes to find a solution that can help her better manage her diabetes. She is excited to contribute to the research to help others with diabetes.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with idiopathic epilepsy six months ago. She has been on anti-epileptic medication and has been experiencing no more than two fits per month. Her CT brain imaging showed no abnormalities. She is experiencing mild to moderate cognitive impairment, as indicated by a Mini Mental State Examination score of 18. She has no other medical disorders and is otherwise healthy. She is currently not taking any other medications. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her cognitive function.

Patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ALS two years ago. She has been taking Riluzole and has completed the last visits in the ONO-2506POE014 study. The patient has no relevant medical history or presence of cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic, endocrine/metabolic, neurologic, lymphatic, haematologic, immunologic, musculoskeletal, connective tissue, dermatologic, genito/urinary, or psychiatric diseases or disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, may pose an unwarranted risk to the patient. The patient is willing to continue with the study and is judged tolerable for the continued treatment with ONO-2506PO and Riluzole from a risk and benefit point of view.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with confirmed EGFR gene sensitive mutations through tissue biopsy. She has no prior treatment history and is in overall good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. She is a non-smoker with no significant medical history, except for mild asthma that is well-controlled with inhalers. She has 2-3 small metastatic lesions in the lung and a single lesion in the liver. Her bone marrow and organ function are normal, with no evidence of any significant comorbidities. She is able to understand and provide written informed consent for the clinical trial. She is willing to comply with the treatment and follow-up requirements. She has no contraindications for radiotherapy, EGFR-TKI, and chemotherapy. She has a mild-moderate pulmonary function dysfunction with FEV1 >50%.

John is a 25-year-old male who works as a mechanic in a car repair shop. He accidentally injured his right index finger while working with a machine. The injury resulted in a defect in the pulp of his finger that is greater than 1.5 cm in length. John is right-handed and uses his index finger for most of his work. He has no other medical conditions and takes no medication. John is interested in participating in the study as he wishes to preserve the length of his finger and restore sensation to the pulp. He has no injuries to the dorsum of his middle phalanx and his wound is not extremely contaminated. John meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II non-small cell lung cancer. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy and is now 8 weeks post-treatment completion. She has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 10 years ago. She lives with her husband and two adult children. She reports feeling fatigued and short of breath with minimal exertion. She has not been exercising regularly and spends most of her day sitting or lying down. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has an Eastern Cooperate Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her physician has approved her participation in the study and expects her to have a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her quality of life and overall health. The patient provides written informed consent and will be randomly allocated off-site to one of two arms (1:1 ratio) after baseline assessment. She is eligible for the exercise rehabilitation intervention and will receive a multimodal program which includes a 90-minute program at the hospital gymnasium in a supervised environment a minimum of once but up to twice per week. Rehabilitation will include aerobic (brisk walking) and resistance training and 30 minutes of 8 style Tai Chi). She will be advised to walk on days of non-attendance - this will be individualized with the aim to have participants increase to 30 minutes walking per day. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and then by blinded assessors at 12 weeks and 6 months post-baseline. She will provide fresh faecal samples (500mg) before and after the completion of the program for the gut microbiota and metabolites analysis.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years. She has a history of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and has undergone several rounds of ovulation induction with timed intercourse with no success. She has now decided to undergo in vitro fertilization (IVF) with egg donation. She has no history of uterine pathologies and her partner has a normal sperm concentration. They have agreed to a single embryo transfer and ICSI fertilization. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial, and is willing to participate in the study to help advance fertility treatment options.

Patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of recurrent patellar dislocation. He has experienced multiple episodes of dislocations over the past year, which have caused significant pain and disability. The patient has undergone conservative management including physical therapy and bracing with little improvement. He is otherwise healthy with no history of previous surgeries for patellofemoral disorders. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction with or without lateral retinaculum release.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who has been diagnosed with primary hyperoxaluria and has been on dialysis for the past 6 months. She has a history of recurrent kidney stones and has undergone multiple surgeries to remove them. Her plasma oxalate levels have been consistently high despite being on dialysis. She has been taking vitamin B6 for the past 3 months to help manage her condition. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. She is sexually active and uses oral contraception. She has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She has no other medical conditions that would make her ineligible for the study. She is willing and able to swallow size 4 capsules twice daily for 6 weeks.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. She has been treated by multiple daily insulin injections for the past year and has been using Freestyle Libre® continuous glucose monitoring system for the past 6 months. Her current HbA1c level is 8.2% and she has experienced difficulties in managing her blood glucose levels. She owns a smartphone and has access to the internet. The patient is willing to use IRTA© to adjust her insulin treatment according to CGM data. She has no plans for pregnancy in the next 6 months and is able to provide written consent and non-disclosure agreement. The patient has no history of acute illness or any other CGM system use.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He is a former smoker who quit smoking 10 years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing, especially during physical activity. He is currently using an inhaler to manage his symptoms. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his time sitting or lying down. He is retired and lives alone. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other major health issues. His BMI is 28.5, and his SpO2 is 92% at rest. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his physical activity levels and overall health. He is able to walk on a treadmill for 5 minutes without experiencing significant shortness of breath or chest pain. He has not had any recent exacerbations of his COPD.

45-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents for a routine eye exam. She reports occasional blurry vision and mild discomfort in her left eye. Visual acuity is 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye. Fundus examination reveals mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes. The patient is informed of a clinical trial investigating the use of optical coherence tomography angiography in patients with retinal vascular disease. She is interested in participating and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. Her menstrual cycles are regular, occurring every 28-30 days, with a normal flow. She has no history of any hormonal disorders, such as polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Her BMI is within the normal range, and her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. She has not undergone any previous IVF/ICSI treatments and is willing to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) after experiencing episodes of blurred vision, numbness, and weakness in her limbs. She has a mild form of the disease with an EDSS score of 3.5. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to establish a new imaging evaluation technology for accurate diagnosis and prognosis evaluation of MS. She has never had brain surgery or trauma and has no history of brain disease or other neurological or psychiatric conditions. She is not currently experiencing severe depression symptoms or alcohol or drug dependence. She is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and is not allergic to MR contrast agents. She is excited about the opportunity to potentially help advance the understanding and treatment of MS.

Patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male from the United States who has been diagnosed with glaucoma. He has undergone prior trabeculectomy surgery that has failed to control his intraocular pressure. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. His visual acuity is 20/40 in both eyes with a cup-to-disc ratio of 0.9 in the right eye and 0.8 in the left eye. His intraocular pressure is 32 mmHg in the right eye and 30 mmHg in the left eye despite maximum tolerated medical therapy. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing and able to participate in the study, and is able to understand and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy for his cancer. He has a performance status of 80%, and his liver function is Class A according to Child-Pugh classification. His lab results show an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3, a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3, and a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL. His bilirubin level is within the normal range, and his albumin level is greater than 2.5 g/dL. His AST and ALT levels are slightly elevated, but not more than 3 times the upper limit of normal. He has no history of other major illnesses, and his cardiac function is normal. He is not pregnant or nursing, and his pregnancy test is negative. He agrees to use an effective contraception during the study and for 3 months after the end of the study. He has no other malignancy within the past 5 years except for a previously treated basal cell skin cancer.

56yo man presents to the ED with chest pain radiating to his left arm and neck, with associated shortness of breath and diaphoresis. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He is currently taking aspirin, metoprolol, and atorvastatin. An ECG is ordered and reveals ST-segment depression in leads V1-V4. Cardiac troponin levels are drawn and the initial value is within normal limits. The patient is afebrile and in no acute distress. He is admitted for further evaluation and observation.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is in good health with no history of any medical disorders such as cardiac, hepatic, renal, or neurological disorders. She has no history of thromboembolic disease, blood disorders, diabetes, gestational hypertension, or pre-eclampsia. Her pregnancy is singleton and in cephalic presentation between 38 and 42 weeks of gestation. She has no history of multiple pregnancies, polyhydramnios, fetal macrosomia, antepartum hemorrhage, or prolonged and obstructed labor. She has not undergone any previous instrumental delivery and does not have a scarred uterus. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis presents with jaundice, severe fatigue, and abdominal swelling. He reports a recent episode of gastrointestinal bleeding and has noticed an increase in the amount of ascites in his abdomen over the past few weeks. He denies any recent travel or exposure to toxic substances. He has been adhering to his prescribed antiviral medication and has not had any recent alcohol use. His liver enzymes are significantly elevated, and a CT scan shows evidence of liver cirrhosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the natural course of his condition and to potentially receive more intensive management for his acute-on-chronic liver failure.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was involved in a high-speed motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries including severe hemorrhage. The patient was found unconscious at the scene and was transferred to the emergency department where he was diagnosed with hemorrhagic shock (HR>100 b/min and/or systolic BP<90 mmHg). The patient was immediately enrolled in the clinical trial and randomized within 3 hours of injury and 1 hour of admission to the emergency department. The patient is unconscious and unable to provide consent, therefore, consent was obtained from a Personal Consultee. The patient is now receiving either the viscoelastic haemostatic assay (VHA)-guided transfusion strategy or non-VHA guided transfusion strategy in order to correct the trauma-induced coagulopathy. The patient's vital signs are closely monitored by the trauma team and the patient's progress will be closely followed throughout the study.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with malignant melanoma on his right upper arm. He underwent wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy, which showed a positive result for metastasis. He then received adjuvant therapy with interferon-alpha but developed severe side effects and had to discontinue the treatment. The PET-CT scan showed multiple metastases in the liver, lung, and bone. The patient was referred to an oncologist for further management. The oncologist discussed the option of participating in a clinical trial using gene-modified T lymphocytes. The patient is HLA-A*24:02 positive and has MAGE-A4 expression in his tumor tissue. He is otherwise healthy with a PS ECOG of 0. Laboratory tests showed normal results, and he is willing to comply with the study protocol. He signed the informed consent and is ready to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male with a history of multiple myeloma presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, bone pain, and decreased appetite. He was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 3 years ago and has had multiple cycles of chemotherapy with little success. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has measurable disease with a serum M-protein level of 1.2 g/dL. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He is a former smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of drug or substance abuse. He has not received any other treatments for his multiple myeloma in the past 30 days and is not currently taking any medications that are strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4 or CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and understands and has signed the informed consent document.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has not received any previous treatment for this condition. She reports experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss over the past few months. She also reports feeling short of breath and having occasional chest pain. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she is ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities. She has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV), and hepatitis C virus (HCV). She has signed a written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is not under tutelage and has not had any cancer in the last 5 years, except for a non-melanoma skin tumor. She does not have central nervous system or meningeal involvement by lymphoma. Her renal and hepatic functions are normal. However, her bone marrow reserve shows a neutrophil count of 1.2G/l and a platelet count of 80G/l, which are related to bone marrow infiltration. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial.

As this study pertains to stunting prevention in Afghanistan, a patient description is not applicable as it does not involve the recruitment of individual patients. The study aims to implement a stunting prevention program in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health through its Public Nutrition Department in selected locations with high stunting rates. The program will target pregnant and lactating women as well as children aged 6-23 months, providing them with specialized nutritious foods and wheat soya blend. An operational research study will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed interventions on preventing stunting and developing viable nutrition programs under real operational conditions.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain that started about 2 hours ago. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are controlled by medications. He denies any recent history of trauma or surgery. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. Upon examination, his vital signs are stable and his ECG shows ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin levels are elevated, confirming a diagnosis of NSTEMI. The patient has undergone CMR imaging and has agreed to participate in the EARLY-MYO-CMR-II Registry. He has provided written consent and is willing to comply with the follow-up requirements. He is expected to be followed for up to 5 years.

The patient is a 72-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He reports shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue. An echocardiogram shows calcific aortic valve stenosis with an initial aortic valve area of 0.8 cm2 and a mean pressure gradient of 45 mm Hg. His NYHA functional class is III. The heart team, including an experienced cardiac surgeon, determines that he is at high risk for surgical valve replacement with an STS score of 9%. He has a documented aortic annulus size of 24 mm on pre-procedure diagnostic imaging. He understands the study requirements and the treatment procedures and provides written informed consent. He is able to return to the study hospital for all required scheduled follow-up visits. He meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Sophie is a 25 year old female who recently visited the hospital with severe pain in the right flank. Upon conducting a computed tomography scan, it was revealed that she has a 10 mm urinary stone in her right kidney. She has not had any previous history of urinary stone disease. Sophie is willing to participate in the clinical trial for the Enhanced Lithotripsy System and has provided informed consent for the study. She has no history of cystinuria or urinary tract infections and her urine pH is above 5.5. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to conceive during the study period. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. Sophie has no coagulation abnormalities and is not taking any prescription anticoagulants. She is physically fit and able to lie still for up to 30 minutes or roll from her back to her side. Sophie does not have any known sensitivity to medications used before, during, or after the treatment procedure.

62-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years and diagnosed with stage III lung cancer. The patient is scheduled for thoracic surgery and has no history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac conditions. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no known allergies or contraindications to colchicine. He is currently taking no medications, and his estimated glomerular filtration rate is above 60 mL/min/1.73m. The patient has been informed of the study and is willing to participate.

A 65-year-old woman presents with a history of osteoarthritis (OA) in her left knee for the past 5 years. She has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for the last 2 years with limited pain relief. She has radiologic evidence of OA with a K-L score of 3. She is willing to discontinue NSAIDs during the study and adhere to study requirements for rescue treatments. She has been using a stable dose of NSAIDs for the past 3 months. She does not have any history of inflammatory joint disease, tumors or infections of the spinal cord, or neuropathic disorders. She has not experienced any trauma to the index joint or carpal tunnel syndrome in the past 6 months. She is not scheduled for joint replacement surgery during the study period and is willing to undergo MRI if needed. She has not used systemic corticosteroids in the past 30 days or undergone intra-articular corticosteroid injection in the index joint within the past 12 weeks. She has not been exposed to anti-nerve growth factor (NGF) antibodies in the past and is willing to practice highly effective contraception during the study if she is of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is expecting her first child. She is scheduled to have a cesarean delivery in two weeks. She is experiencing nausea and vomiting during her pregnancy and is concerned that it will continue during and after the surgery. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is able to speak English fluently. She is excited to be a mother and is eager to have a successful and comfortable delivery. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies or sensitivities to medications or other substances. She has not tested positive for COVID-19 and has taken all necessary precautions to ensure the safety of herself and her unborn child. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is open to trying new methods to reduce intraoperative and postoperative nausea and vomiting during her cesarean delivery.

The patient is a 35-year-old man with a history of bipolar disorder. He has been experiencing mood swings and difficulty in managing his symptoms. He has been receiving psychiatric treatment at a local mental health center for the past year. His current medication regimen includes lithium and an atypical antipsychotic. He has reported some side effects from his medication, including weight gain and fatigue. He has expressed interest in exploring alternative treatment options and improving his self-management skills. He is fluent in English and has access to a computer and the internet. He is willing to participate in weekly coaching sessions and engage in practice with the Virtual Provider program. He is also open to having his prescriber appointments audio recorded.

58-year-old male with a history of colon cancer, who underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor and subsequent chemotherapy. During surveillance imaging, he was found to have 2 liver metastases, each measuring less than 5 cm in size. He underwent radiofrequency ablation of both metastases and is currently in remission. He has a performance status of 1 and no evidence of extra-hepatic disease. His liver function tests are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the study to receive adjuvant consolidative radiotherapy to potentially prevent recurrence of his liver metastases. Past Medical History: Colon cancer, treated with surgical resection and chemotherapy. Family History: Negative for any cancers.

50 year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and no previous cancer diagnosis presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. Chest X-ray reveals a mass in the right lung, and subsequent CT confirms a 7 cm mass in the right upper lobe with lymph node involvement. Biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutation detected in plasma cf-DNA by ddPCR. Patient has not received any chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or systemic anti-cancer treatment. The patient has a WHO performance status of 1 and laboratory values that meet the criteria for the study. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and comply with the study protocol.

A 68-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU after a cardiac surgery procedure. The patient had a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He had no history of asthma, psychiatric illness or vestibulo-cochlear disease. The patient developed a fever of 38.5°C and a new persistent radiological infiltrate. Purulent tracheal aspirations were noted, and the patient had a leucocyte count of 12,000/ml. The patient was diagnosed with hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) and was empirically treated with intravenous (IV) piperacillin/tazobactam. The culture sensitivity test revealed that the patient's infection was sensitive to amikacin. The patient was eligible for the clinical trial and was randomized into the nebulized amikacin group. The patient's renal function was normal with a creatinine clearance of 85 mL/min. The patient provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m² and his HbA1c level is 8.5%. The patient has not been treated with any antidiabetic agents before. He has normal kidney function with a creatinine clearance of 75 mL/[min*1.73 m2]. The patient is sexually active and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study. He has no history of cardiovascular events or high blood pressure. The patient is not currently taking any medications and has not tested positive for viral hepatitis.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was admitted to the surgical intensive care unit after experiencing severe abdominal pain and vomiting. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Upon admission, he was found to have a perforated gastric ulcer requiring immediate surgery. Postoperatively, he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress. He has been in the surgical intensive care unit for 3 days and is expected to stay longer due to his comorbidities and postoperative complications. He is able to follow simple commands but is weak and fatigued. He complains of muscle weakness and difficulty moving his arms and legs. He is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being over 18 years old, staying in the SICU for at least 24 hours, and not having ongoing discussions about goals of care. There are no exclusion criteria for his case.

The patient is a 35-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV infection. The patient has been on zidovudine (AZT) for less than 120 days and has a CD4 count of less than 400 on two consecutive visits within one month prior to the entry. The patient has not received any other antiretroviral therapy, immunomodulators, biological response modifiers, or cytotoxic chemotherapy for Kaposi's sarcoma within the last 30 days and has not received ribavirin within the last 60 days. The patient has no history of intolerances to AZT or didanosine (ddI) evidenced by peripheral neuropathy, seizures, pancreatitis, gastrointestinal toxicity, or hematologic toxicity. The patient is not currently undergoing radiation therapy for Kaposi's sarcoma and has no active substance abuse that would impair compliance with study procedures.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been paraplegic for five years following a spinal cord injury. He has been experiencing chronic pain and has been on long-term opioid therapy. He has a history of low testosterone levels and has been diagnosed with osteoporosis. He has been taking vitamin D and calcium supplements and has been receiving weekly Fosamax for osteoporosis prophylaxis. He has been following a standard physiotherapy exercise program to maintain his bone and muscle health. He has no history of bone diseases or calcium oxalate stones. He is not taking aromatase inhibitors or 5-alpha reductase inhibitors. He has no history of prostate or breast cancer, and there is no suspicion of liver tumors. He is not known to have any hypersensitivity to testosterone or the excipients of Nebido.

A 32-year-old woman has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She has been taking anti-TNF-alpha medication for the past year, and her symptoms have been managed quite well. However, she has noticed that her energy levels are low, and she has been losing weight recently. She has a history of lactose intolerance and is worried about the effect of supplements on her digestive system. She does not smoke and is not using any other medication or nutritional supplements. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of nutritional supplements on Crohn's disease.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is a laboratory-based study using cryopreserved samples from infants with leukemia. Therefore, no individual patients will be directly involved in this study.

This is a 65 year-old male who was admitted to the ICU with respiratory distress due to exacerbated chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The patient required intubation and mechanical ventilation for respiratory support. The duration of intubation and mechanical ventilation is predicted to be greater than 48 hours. The patient has no history of tracheostomy and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient is conscious and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

27F with a history of seizures since childhood was referred to the Surgical Neurology Branch for evaluation of her condition. The patient has been taking anti-seizure medication for several years with some success, but still experiences seizures periodically. On examination, there were no focal neurological deficits. MRI revealed a small lesion in the temporal lobe that could be the cause of the seizures. The patient has been informed that she may require surgery to remove the lesion, and has consented to participate in this study that will allow evaluation and treatment of her condition by the staff of the Surgical Neurology Branch. In addition, the patient has agreed to allow a portion of the removed tissue to be used for research purposes. She is able to provide informed consent for herself.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has reached 37 weeks of gestation and is experiencing some difficulty with the progression of her labor. The patient has no history of previous uterine surgery and is not carrying multiples. Her Bishop score is not greater than 4 points. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of orally administrated solution of Misoprostol (Cytotec®) with vaginal slow-release Misoprostol (Misodel®) during labor.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. He has been experiencing symptoms of damaged endothelial function such as chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has no significant history of liver or kidney damage or IDDM (Insulin Dependent Diabetes Mellitus). His lipid profile shows elevated levels of small-dense LDL and oxidized LDL. He has also shown a decrease in paraoxinase activity and increased levels of CRP and insulin. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of irbesartan, ciprofibrate, and their combination in improving his endothelial function and reducing his cardiovascular risk.

A 30-year-old male presents with occasional headaches and neck pain. He works in a desk job and spends most of his day in front of a computer. He has no history of chronic pain conditions, depression, or anxiety disorders. He does not take any medications shown to lower seizure threshold. He has no metal implants above the waist and no family history of seizures. He is not pregnant nor has brain tumors or lesions. He is interested in participating in clinical research studies and has no objections to the use of TMS.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. He has been experiencing pulmonary symptoms, including coughing and shortness of breath, and has been diagnosed with Pseudomonas aeruginosa presence in the airways. He has not yet received antibiotic therapy for this. The patient has no known contraindications to a biopsy of the nasal mucosa. He does not have diabetes or a history of exposure to tobacco smoke. He does not have any other chronic diseases or clinical conditions that may influence the assessed parameters and the course of the study. The patient has not had an acute respiratory infection within the past 2 weeks leading up to the first visit of the study.

This clinical trial is looking for healthy male participants aged between 30 and 55 years old, with a BMI within the range of 18.5-29.0 kg/m2. The study requires participants to have regular bowel movements and be able to complete the study. The participants must also have AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels within the normal range, and an average QTcF < 450 msec. Participants must not have a history of liver or biliary abnormalities, bleeding diathesis, or any pre-existing conditions that may interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or elimination of the study drug. Additionally, participants must not have had exposure to more than four new chemical entities within 12 months prior to the first dosing period. Participants must be willing to follow the procedures outlined in the protocol and give written informed consent. Participants with a positive pre-study Hepatitis B surface antigen or positive Hepatitis C antibody result within 3 months of screening, positive test for HIV antibody, or a history of anaphylaxis or severe allergic responses to drugs are excluded from the study.

A 45 year old female patient presents with oral discomfort and pain while eating for the past 3 months. She complains of a burning sensation in her mouth and has noticed white patches on her tongue, gums and inner cheek. She has no history of taking corticosteroids or any other medications for the past 6 months. The patient has controlled diabetes and hypertension, and no history of recent dental filling or drug administration. Upon examination, she is diagnosed with oral lichen planus. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is randomized to the group that will receive curcumin paste. The IL-33 level in saliva is measured at baseline and at the end of 4th week, while pain and clinical parameters are measured at 2nd and 4th week. The patient is closely monitored for any adverse effects or changes in her condition throughout the study.

Patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman with no history of structural hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal disease and BMI of 25. She has no history of endocrinopathy, stroke, or MI. She is not currently taking any medications, including estrogen, progestin, anabolic steroids, or glucocorticoids. She has not traveled across more than 3 time zones within 7 days of admission and is not currently working night shifts. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse within the last 2 years, and no history of depression, psychosis, or mania. Her weight has been stable, with no gain or loss of more than 2 kg in 3 weeks. Her hemoglobin, creatinine, and ALT levels are within normal limits. She has no history of deep-vein thrombophlebitis, congestive heart failure, or cardiac arrhythmias. She has no known allergies to estradiol valerate, castor oil, or sesame oil. She has no history of smoking within the last 2 years, untreated gall bladder disease, or carcinoma. She has provided voluntary, written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been diagnosed with psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing flare-ups of her skin lesions, which have become increasingly severe over the past few months. She has tried several topical treatments and phototherapy, but none of them have provided significant relief. She has no known allergies or medical conditions other than psoriasis. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the trial period. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve her psoriasis symptoms.

10-year-old female diagnosed with left-sided spastic cerebral palsy is being recruited for a study on upper extremity selective voluntary motor control. She must be able to follow simple instructions and have no significant ataxia or dystonia. She must not have undergone orthopedic intervention or botulinum toxin injection to the upper extremities in the last 6 months and must not have any orthopedic problems or medical conditions that prevent her from participating in the assessment. The study will involve assessments of her manual skills, quality of upper extremity movement, upper extremity function, and selective movements of the upper extremity. The study aims to determine the relationship between upper extremity selective motor control and upper extremity functions in unilateral cerebral palsy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and requires surgery. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She also has a family history of thyroid disease, but she has not been diagnosed with it. She has no known allergies to medications or dyes. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is generally in good health and exercises regularly. Her calcium levels are elevated, and she has been experiencing fatigue and muscle weakness. She is scheduled for a total thyroidectomy or bilateral neck exploration for PHPT at the Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no prior experience with mind-body practices such as yoga or meditation. She works as a graphic designer and experiences occasional stress due to work demands. She reports that she has difficulty sleeping occasionally but has not sought medical attention for it. She is interested in learning more about the potential benefits of yoga breathing practices on overall health and quality of life. She has no history of neurological disorders, head trauma, or spinal injury. She does not have any respiratory or allergic disorders and is not currently taking any medication that acts on the brain. She is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is willing to participate in an 8-week yoga breathing intervention and undergo MRI scans before and after the intervention.

A 55-year-old male carpenter is seeking treatment for a chronic shoulder problem. He reports that he has been experiencing pain in his right shoulder for the past 6 months, which has been interfering with his ability to work. The pain is described as aching and sharp, and is localized to the back of his shoulder. He has tried over-the-counter medications, physical therapy, and cortisone injections, but he has not experienced significant improvement. An MRI showed an irreparable rotator cuff tear. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or significant medical problems. He is right-handed and works with his hands frequently. He has no history of prior shoulder surgery or injury, and there is no history of shoulder problems in his family. He is willing to participate in the study and has no known allergies. He speaks English fluently and is able to read and write.

10-year-old Caucasian male with a history of oligoarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) diagnosed 2 years ago is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. He has a history of swelling and stiffness of his right knee and ankle, left wrist, and right third metacarpophalangeal joint. He has received treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and methotrexate, but has not been on any biologic medications. His JIA has been well-controlled for the past 6 months with no active joint inflammation. He has no other significant medical history and is up-to-date on his vaccinations. He has no allergies to medications. He lives with both parents and has two siblings. He attends school and has good academic performance. His parents are willing to provide informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial. His physical exam shows no active joint inflammation or deformities.

A 26-year-old male who has been taking topiramate for the management of his epilepsy for the past 2 years. He has been experiencing seizures since he was 18 years old and has tried multiple medications before starting topiramate. He is currently taking a daily dose of 200 mg of topiramate orally and has been seizure-free for the past 6 months. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of metabolic syndrome. He has been experiencing occasional memory lapses and has become concerned about the possibility of developing postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) after undergoing surgery. He is scheduled for a non-cardiac, non-neural surgery and has been classified as ASA II. He has no history of chronic alcohol or drug abuse, renal or liver dysfunction, cerebrovascular accidents, or permanent ventricular pacing. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to undergo either propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia. His MMSE score is within the normal range, and he is cooperative and able to understand the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 22-year-old female college student who is a member of the University of Nebraska at Omaha Wellness Center presents to the Injury Prevention and Care Clinic with a history of ankle injury. She reports that the injury occurred while playing basketball with friends a week ago. She describes a sudden twisting motion of her ankle with immediate pain, swelling, and difficulty bearing weight. She has been using ice, elevation, and rest to manage the injury. She has no history of previous ankle injuries, surgeries, or other significant medical conditions. She reports no current pain or discomfort other than her ankle. She has been able to attend classes and perform her daily activities with minimal difficulty. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the accuracy of diagnostic techniques for ankle injuries.

Pt is a 63yo M with a history of COPD and CHF, presenting to the ED with severe shortness of breath and hypoxemia. After initial management, the patient was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress. The patient is now stable and receiving mechanical ventilation via an endotracheal tube. The patient will be included in the study as they meet the inclusion criteria. The patient has not experienced a sudden cardiac arrest and has not been diagnosed with ARDS while in the ED. The patient is not on chronic mechanical ventilation and has not been transferred to another hospital.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with secondary lymphedema in her left leg due to past surgery for ovarian cancer. She had been undergoing regular follow-up and rehabilitation in the lymphedema outpatient clinic before the Covid-19 pandemic. Since the pandemic started, she has been avoiding going to the hospital unless necessary due to the risk of infection. She has been able to do self-manual lymphatic drainage and exercises regularly at home to manage her swelling. She has not had any cellulite attacks or increase in swelling, but has noticed a slight decrease in mobility due to being confined at home. She has been paying close attention to hand and foot hygiene and has not been diagnosed with Covid-19 nor has any of her family members. However, she has been experiencing anxiety and depression related to the pandemic and fears of infection. She has been using compression stockings regularly and has not experienced any weight gain or changes in eating habits. She is willing to participate in the study and answer questions over the phone.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian man with a diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and a medical prescription for long-term oxygen therapy. He has completed the pulmonary rehabilitation program at The Ottawa Hospital Rehabilitation Centre between January 30th 2008 and March 31st 2011. He is medically stable and able to perform activities of daily living independently, although he is not as active in the community as he used to be due to his respiratory condition. He has been experiencing moderate to severe exertional oxygen desaturations as measured by pulse oximetry during his daily activities. He has not had an exacerbation of his respiratory condition over the last 6 weeks and has not been diagnosed with any other co-morbid conditions that could affect the consistency of the 6-minute walk test. He speaks English fluently.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester has been scheduled for an elective cesarean delivery due to a previous cesarean delivery. She has no known medical issues and is otherwise healthy. She has a BMI of 25 and is not taking any medications. She has no history of allergy to carbetocin. She will be receiving spinal anesthesia for the procedure.

56-year-old male with a history of glaucoma diagnosed 8 years ago. He has been on multiple topical medications including prostaglandin analogs, beta-blockers, and alpha-agonists, but his intraocular pressure (IOP) has remained elevated at 26 mm Hg in the right eye and 28 mm Hg in the left eye. He has no history of intraocular surgery or laser treatment within the last 90 days. His medical history is notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He has no known allergies or contraindications to anesthesia. He has been referred to the study to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of cyclocoagulation using High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) with the EYEOP1 device. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of age-related cataracts who is seeking treatment for his vision impairment. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He has noticed a gradual worsening of his vision over the past year, with difficulty reading and driving at night. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of a 600μm pre-cut compared to a stab-incision in cataract surgery. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent. He is willing to undergo preoperative pregnancy testing if necessary.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer last year. She underwent adjuvant chemotherapy with docetaxel, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide (TAC) and completed treatment a year ago. She is currently living with her husband and two children. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no history of heart disease, diabetes mellitus, or Parkinson's disease. She is not pregnant or lactating. She does not have evidence of breast cancer recurrence or metastatic disease. She has no history of renal failure or ionizing radiation exposure in the past year. She is interested in participating in the study to assess the potential subclinical cardiovascular damage caused by the TAC chemotherapy. She is willing to undergo MIBG scintigraphy, echocardiography, and blood biomarker testing to assess her cardiovascular health.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of stroke, including sudden onset of weakness on the right side of her body and difficulty speaking. After a thorough evaluation, her diagnosis was classified as cryptogenic stroke. She has no known history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac issues, and her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is able to carry out both 48-hour and 7-day monitoring and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She provides informed consent and is randomized to the 7-day monitoring arm. She is discharged from the hospital and follows up as an outpatient for the duration of the monitoring period.

A 35-year-old male presented to the endocrinology clinic with complaints of recurrent episodes of dizziness and confusion for the past 6 months. He reported that these episodes typically occurred in the morning and were preceded by sweating and palpitations. He also reported blurred vision during these episodes. The patient had a history of mild hypoglycemia, which was effectively managed with dietary modifications. However, despite adhering to a strict diet, his symptoms persisted. Physical examination was unremarkable, except for a blood glucose level of 50 mg/dL. Laboratory investigations revealed low blood glucose levels with elevated serum insulin and C-peptide levels. An abdominal CT scan revealed a small (1cm) lesion in the pancreatic tail. MRI and endoscopic ultrasound were performed but were unable to confirm the nature of the lesion. The patient was advised to undergo surgery for resection of the pancreatic lesion. However, due to the small size and location of the lesion, the surgeon was unable to locate it during the procedure and performed a blinded resection of the pancreas. The patient was subsequently diagnosed with insulinoma.

A 67-year-old male was recently diagnosed with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. He reports a history of urinary urgency, frequency, and a weak urine stream for several months. Biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate without neuroendocrine differentiation, signet cell or small cell histology. He underwent a bone scan and CT scan, which revealed metastatic lesions in the bone and soft tissue. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He has no prior pharmacotherapy, radiation therapy or surgery for metastatic prostate cancer. He has not received treatment with 5-α reductase inhibitors, estrogens, cyprotoerone acetate or androgens, systemic glucocorticoids, herbal medications or investigational agents that inhibit the AR or androgen synthesis. He is willing to maintain ADT with LHRH agonist or antagonist or has had a bilateral orchiectomy. He is able to swallow enzalutamide capsules whole and is willing to comply with study requirements throughout the study. The patient has no history of seizure or any condition that may predispose to seizure. He has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease. He has not received bisphosphonates or denosumab within 2 weeks prior to day 1 unless administered at stable dose or to treat diagnosed osteoporosis.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with soft tissue sarcoma after experiencing a persistent, painful mass in her left thigh. She underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by radiation therapy, which led to a partial response. However, the cancer recurred 6 months later and she was found to have multiple metastases in her lungs. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is eligible for doxorubicin therapy. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any other significant medical conditions or allergies. Her laboratory tests are within normal limits, including adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial for a new treatment option and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has been experiencing frequent headaches for the past 3 years. She describes the headaches as throbbing, usually on one side of her head, and accompanied by sensitivity to light and sound. The headaches typically last for several hours and are often accompanied by nausea or vomiting. She has a provisional diagnosis of migraine with aura. She reports having 2-3 headache attacks per month. She is fluent in English, and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. She has no history of seizure disorder or Axis-I psychotic disorder, and has stable cardiac conditions. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the relationship between stress and her headaches.

Patient is an 28-year-old woman with type-1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at the age of 24. She has been on insulin treatment since then and has maintained a normal weight with BMI of 22.
