She does not have any severe complications related to diabetes and her liver and kidney function tests are normal. Her hemoglobin level is within the normal range and she does not have macroalbuminuria. She does not have any systemic diseases and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the effect of GLP-1 and/or GIP on insulin secretion in type-1 diabetes mellitus.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who recently had a stroke. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. She has mild to moderate impairment in the left upper limb and difficulty with tasks that require attention and memory. She is able to follow instructions and has a good understanding of the task. The patient is motivated to participate in rehabilitation and open to new and innovative approaches. The patient is independent in her daily activities but feels frustrated with her limitations in her motor and cognitive abilities. She is willing to commit to the 12 sessions of 45 minutes within a 4-6 week period. The patient has no vision disorders that would interfere with the task and her cognitive functioning is within the inclusion criteria.

A 42-year-old male patient with a history of Barrett's esophagus presents for evaluation of dysplasia. He reports no abdominal symptoms such as bloating and abdominal pain. The patient is informed about the study and provides written informed consent to participate. He has no known other gastrointestinal diseases or infections and has no history of GI bleeding or stricture in the upper gastrointestinal tract. The patient reports normal renal function with a creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known allergies to Methylene blue or Fluorescein. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 4 weeks.

A 40-year-old man was diagnosed with aggressive B-cell lymphoma with secondary involvement of the central nervous system (CNS). He has a history of smoking and heavy drinking, but is otherwise healthy. He has already received systemic treatment for the lymphoma but has relapsed. He has not received any treatment for the CNS involvement. He is willing to participate in the study and has adequate organ function. He has no history of bleeding disorders, hemophilia, or clinically significant hepatic impairment. He understands and is willing to comply with all study evaluations and procedures.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with XLH at the age of 5 years. She had a positive family history of X-linked hypophosphatemia. She has been treated with oral phosphate and activated vitamin D analogues since her diagnosis. She experiences chronic pain in her lower back, hips, and legs, which has been worsening over the past few years. She experiences fatigue and exhaustion, which affects her daily life activities. Her latest physical examination showed the following results: A young woman, alert and oriented, with no apparent distress. Weight: 60 kg Height: 165 BP: 116/78 HR: 82/min RR: 16/min Hgb: 12.1 g/dl WBC: 6800 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 3900/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 33 U/L ALT: 25 U/L Alk P: 140 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl ESR: 35 mm/hr Vitamin D: 35 nmol/L. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her consent to the study requirements.

30 F diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) at the age of 22, presented with a desire to conceive. She has a history of Raynaud's phenomenon, photosensitivity, joint pain, and mouth ulcers. Her current medications include hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and mycophenolate mofetil. She has been stable on this regimen for the past 6 months with no active disease manifestations. Her obstetric history is significant for 1 prior miscarriage at 8 weeks of gestation. She has been referred to the interdisciplinary research group on pregnancy and rare diseases (GR2) to participate in a prospective study to evaluate the complications of pregnancies in women with rare diseases and to improve their management and quality of life. She has provided written consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C during a routine medical check-up. He has been feeling fatigued and has noticed a decrease in his cognitive abilities, which has affected his work performance. He was advised to undergo interferon-free antiviral therapy (Sofosbuvir +/-Daclatasvir +/- Ribavirin or Sofosbuvir/Ledipasvir +/- Ribavirin) and was referred to a clinical trial evaluating the effect of such therapy on neurocognitive performance, mood, quality of life, and fatigue. He is fluent in German and has no history of depression, psychosis, or drug abuse. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 16-year-old Caucasian male presented to the clinic with a history of recurrent panic attacks. He reported experiencing at least one 4-symptom panic attack per week over the last 4 weeks. The patient reported symptoms including heart palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, choking sensation, chest pain, nausea, dizziness, and fear of losing control or dying. He also reported avoiding situations that may trigger these attacks, such as crowded places or being alone. The patient had no history of major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, or substance abuse. He denied any family history of psychiatric illness. The patient's physical examination was unremarkable, and laboratory tests were within normal limits. The patient met the DSM-IV-TR criteria for panic disorder with no other co-morbid psychiatric diagnoses.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and fatigue for the past few months. Upon evaluation, he was found to have a liver mass that is suspicious for primary liver cancer. He has a history of hepatitis B infection but has been noncompliant with antiviral therapy. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no significant past medical history and takes only over-the-counter pain medication occasionally. His liver function tests are mildly elevated, and his platelet count is within normal limits. He has no significant comorbidities and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to undergo a diagnostic liver biopsy as part of his clinical care and is open to the possibility of an additional research biopsy. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent.

A 30-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 3 years ago is currently on a stable ART regimen. He has been taking his medication regularly and has achieved an undetectable viral load for the past 2 years. His CD4 count is above 500 cells/mm3. He has no history of opportunistic infections. He works as a graphic designer and lives with his partner who is HIV-negative. He has no children and does not plan to have any in the near future. He does not smoke or use recreational drugs, but he does consume alcohol socially. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of heart disease, arrhythmias, or any other significant medical conditions. He has not received any immunosuppressive therapy in the past. He has no history of tuberculosis, fungal infections, or chronic hepatitis B or C. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 4 months after completion of therapy. He understands the study requirements and has provided written consent to participate.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who is in good health and has no history of significant acute or chronic diseases. She has not received any anthrax vaccines or therapies, nor been exposed to anthrax in the past. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use appropriate birth control methods during the study. She has no history of Type I hypersensitivity reactions to food, drugs, or other substances. She does not have a current drug or alcohol addiction and has tested negative for HIV-1, Hepatitis B surface antigen, and Hepatitis C antibody. She has not had cancer within the last 5 years, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin or in situ carcinoma of the cervix. She has not participated in any other clinical trials of an investigational compound within the last 60 days and has not been previously exposed to raxibacumab.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) for over a year. He reports difficulty urinating, weak stream, and the need to urinate frequently, particularly at night. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is within normal limits. He has not had any previous surgeries or treatments for BPH, and does not have a history of prostate or bladder cancer. He is willing to undergo surgery to alleviate his symptoms and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with liver cirrhosis. He has no history of liver transplant or known or suspected hepatocellular carcinoma or cholangiocarcinoma. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and meets all the inclusion criteria, including leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, hemoglobin, total bilirubin, and creatinine levels within normal limits. He has not taken any statin medication before and is not currently using any systemic medications that interact with statins. He has had an abdominal imaging test (CT, MRI, or ultrasound) within the past 18 months. He is willing to comply with the trial protocol and follow-up and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He will be randomized to either receive simvastatin orally once daily or placebo once daily for up to 6 months. After completion of the study treatment, he will be followed up at 30, 60, and 90 days.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN3) within the past 12 weeks. She has no history of invasive cervical carcinoma, and her biopsy results have confirmed the presence of CIN3 lesions. The patient reports that she has never been pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. She has no known immunocompromised condition or autoimmune conditions, and she is not currently taking anticoagulant medications. The patient is fluent in English and Spanish and has the ability to read and speak both languages. She is willing to use an effective form of contraception during the study and is not planning to become pregnant within the next 6 months. The patient has not been treated previously with 5-fluorouracil or imiquimod or other medications for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. She has no concurrent vaginal, vulvar, anal lesions, or symptomatic infections, and has not had a prior hysterectomy. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed a written informed consent document.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male volunteers between the ages of 18 and 55 with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 30 kg/m2. Participants must be nonsmokers and have no clinically significant abnormalities in their medical history, physical examination, vital signs, or clinical laboratory values. They must also have a normal ECG and not be taking any drugs that induce or inhibit cytochrome P450 or P-glycoprotein. Participants cannot have a history of alcohol, drug, or substance abuse within the past 12 months or any other factor that the Investigator thinks will increase subject risk with participation. Additionally, participants must be willing to use barrier contraception during sexual intercourse for three months after the last dosing with GCC-4401C. Overall, the study is seeking healthy male volunteers who can understand and comply with the requirements of the study and have signed the informed consent form.

A 62-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a history of melena and syncope. He reports feeling lightheaded and weak for the past few days, but the symptoms have worsened over the last 24 hours. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, and takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. Physical examination shows a pale and diaphoretic male with a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and a hemoglobin level of 7.5 g/dL. An urgent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals an actively bleeding duodenal ulcer with a Forrest classification of IIa. Primary endoscopic hemostasis is achieved with the use of an epinephrine injection and hemostatic clips. The patient is then considered for supplementary angiographic embolization as part of a clinical trial investigating its efficacy in preventing rebleeding.

55-year-old male with a missing lower molar has been recommended for dental implant placement by his dentist. The patient's medical history is unremarkable and he reports no allergies. He has good oral hygiene with a plaque index below 25% and a bleeding index less than 20%. He has no history of head/neck radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The patient has controlled diabetes with HbA1c levels below 7.5%. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of periodontal disease. The patient has a minimum surgical height of 7mm and a thickness of at least 6mm at the programmed implant site. The soft tissue height above the implant is ≤ 2mm. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the growth of peri-implant soft tissues using a heterologous dermal membrane graft or a 2 mm healing screw as a vertical support of the limbs positioned at the moment of surgical insertion of the implant.

A 65-year-old male with a 5-year history of Parkinson's disease presents with freezing of gait (FOG) that has been progressively worsening over the past year. He is currently taking levodopa/carbidopa 25/100mg three times daily, which provides partial relief of his motor symptoms. He reports that his FOG episodes occur mainly when he is turning or walking through narrow spaces, and they have led to several falls in the past year. His Hoehn & Yahr stage is 3, and he scores 17 on the FOG questionnaire. He has no history of cognitive impairment or major depression. He wears glasses for mild myopia but has no other significant visual or hearing impairment. He has no significant medical or psychiatric illnesses and has not undergone deep brain stimulation or pacemaker implantation. He is willing to discontinue his current medication regimen during the study.

A 63-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage II colorectal cancer and is currently undergoing treatment. She is generally inactive and experiences symptoms that impact her quality of life, such as fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and low mood. She is interested in participating in a community-based Nordic pole walking (NPW) program to see if it can help improve her physical function and overall health-related quality of life. She has not engaged in NPW within the last six months and is approved by her treating physician to participate in the study. She is able to communicate fluently in English and is motivated to take part in the study.

A 19-year-old woman is seeking an abortion at 17 weeks of pregnancy. She has a history of uncomplicated pregnancies and deliveries. She has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of mifepristone or misoprostol. She has not had any vaginal bleeding and her cervix is closed. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to follow the study procedures.

A 17-year-old Hispanic male presents to the clinic for his routine HIV medical appointment. He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection last year and has been receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) since then. He is compliant with his medications and has no history of treatment failure or drug resistance. He lives with his mother and two younger siblings and attends high school. He reports no history of psychiatric symptoms, substance abuse, or other major medical issues. He is able to understand spoken English and willing to participate in the study. He is informed about the study and provided with a consent form to sign. His mother signs the parental consent form as well. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the study and is considered a newly engaged patient in HIV medical care.

Patient is a 50yo man with a history of metastatic melanoma who has undergone multiple lines of treatment including immunotherapy and targeted therapy. The patient's disease has progressed despite several lines of treatment and he is now experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and decreased appetite. Imaging studies have revealed progression of disease with new lesions in the liver and lung. The patient has been referred to participate in a Phase 1 clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of mRNA-2416, an investigational agent that will be injected directly into the patient's tumors, alone or in combination with durvalumab, an approved immunotherapy. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the Dose Escalation and Dose Confirmation period of the trial, with multiple lesions that are easily accessible for injection, and a diagnosis of advanced metastatic solid tumor malignancy. The patient will undergo a pre-treatment biopsy and an on-treatment biopsy, and will be monitored closely for any adverse events. The patient will need to use a highly reliable method of birth control as part of the trial. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 35-year-old male patient was discharged from the hospital after being diagnosed with COVID-19 through RT-PCR. He owns a smartphone with internet connectivity and is available for follow-up through a mobile app. He has no previous history of chronic diseases, but he is currently experiencing mild symptoms such as cough and fatigue. He is not a healthcare worker and was not discharged to a care center or medicalized hotel. He is willing to participate in the trial and follow the protocol provided by the healthcare professional.

The patient is a 42-year-old mother of a 8-year-old girl who is obese with a BMI of 31. She has tried various diets and exercise programs for her daughter but has not had much success in reducing her weight. She is highly motivated to improve her daughter's health and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to find effective treatment options. She is the primary caregiver for her daughter and has a mobile phone with a texting plan. She is fluent in English and has no severe medical or mental health conditions that would limit her ability to attend appointments. She is not planning to move out of state in the next 3 months. She is excited to learn about new strategies to help her daughter lose weight and improve their family's overall health habits.

The patient is a 36 year-old male who works in a large manufacturing company. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a history of occasional back pain but has never sought treatment for it. He woke up this morning with severe low back pain that started suddenly and has been progressively worsening throughout the day. The pain is located in the lower back and is rated as an 8 out of 10 on the visual analog scale (VAS). He has no history of any other medical conditions or surgeries. He is not taking any medications and has never had any allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no family history of back pain or any other medical conditions. He has not taken any sick leave in the last month.

A 44-year-old woman has been experiencing frequent headaches and neck pain, which has prompted her to visit the doctor. She has a history of hypothyroidism and is currently taking levothyroxine. Her neck pain is more prominent on the right side, and an ultrasound reveals a nodule in her thyroid gland. After further evaluation, the doctor recommends a thyroidectomy, which she agrees to. She is scheduled for the elective surgery at Aarhus University Hospital. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history apart from her hypothyroidism. She works as a librarian and enjoys hiking during the warmer months. She is interested in participating in research studies and has signed up for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with bilateral adrenal tumors during a routine abdominal ultrasound. She has been experiencing mild symptoms such as weight gain, high blood pressure, and increased thirst. Her blood tests revealed slightly elevated cortisol levels, indicating subclinical Cushings syndrome. The investigators have offered her the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial to undergo adrenal venous sampling (AVS) to determine if the overproduction of cortisol is from one or both adrenal glands. If it is from only one, the investigators will offer the patient an operation to remove the affected gland. The patient is not currently using any steroids in any form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment with taxanes and has completed 4 cycles so far. She reports experiencing numbness and tingling in her hands and feet, which started after her second cycle of chemotherapy. She rates the intensity of her symptoms as 7 out of 10 on a scale of severity. She has no history of alcoholism or substance abuse, and she does not have significant cognitive impairment. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study. She is married and works as a teacher. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

A 23-year-old female recently started experiencing unusual thoughts and behaviors. She has been feeling anxious and paranoid about her surroundings and has been having trouble sleeping for the past month. She is currently unemployed and has no history of mental illness. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help alleviate her symptoms and potentially prevent the onset of psychosis. She currently does not have any pre-existing gastrointestinal, heart, or kidney disease and is not taking any medications. She does not consume more than 2 drinks of alcohol per day and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. She is willing to undergo laboratory and genetic testing as part of the study.

This is a 56 year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II colorectal cancer 6 months ago. She underwent surgery and completed her adjuvant therapy 2 months ago. She is currently experiencing fatigue and has difficulty with daily activities such as climbing stairs and carrying groceries. She is interested in participating in a study that could potentially improve her quality of life and help her regain her strength. She enjoys staying active but is not familiar with resistance training and prefers to exercise at home. She is willing to participate in a 12-week home-based exercise program and is open to exploring meditation as well.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male, an IT professional, has been smoking for 15 years, starting from his college days. He smokes about a pack of cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking several times without success. He is concerned about his health and the health of his family members, especially his young children. He has no significant past medical history, and his family history is negative for any major illnesses. He does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. He exercises moderately for about 30 min. every day. He has never used any smoking cessation medication before. He is interested in quitting smoking and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of bupropion and varenicline treatments. He is not currently taking any medication, and he has no known allergies to any medications.

The patient is an 80-year-old female with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has experienced shortness of breath and fatigue during exertion for the past year, and her echocardiogram revealed severe aortic stenosis with a valve area of 0.6 cm² and an estimated mean gradient of 40 mmHg. Her STS score is 8 and her EuroSCORE is 15. She has no significant coronary artery disease and her left ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. She has previously undergone percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement in the left anterior descending artery. She is currently taking aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo transcatheter aortic valve replacement if deemed appropriate by the heart team.

A 30-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m² who has never smoked and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no significant medical history or abnormal laboratory findings during screening. She has a negative serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) pregnancy test and is using an acceptable form of contraception. She has no history of allergic responses to Lamotrigine or related drugs or any of its formulation ingredients. She has no history of difficulty with swallowing or any gastrointestinal disease that could affect drug absorption. She has no food allergy, intolerance, restriction, or special diet that could contraindicate her participation. She is willing and able to follow the protocol requirements and has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 36-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent headaches for the past year. She also reports occasional episodes of dizziness and blurred vision. She has no significant past medical history, takes no medications, and has no history of allergies. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. Upon physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented, with no apparent neurological deficits. Her blood pressure is normal, and her heart and lung sounds are clear. A CT scan of the brain showed a brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM). The patient is scheduled for embolization treatment, and she has agreed to participate in the study. The patient does not have any contraindications to undergo MRI examination.

A healthy 25-year-old male who is interested in participating in the study as a volunteer. He has no history of chronic illness, and he is not currently taking any medication. He is sexually active and uses barrier methods of contraception to prevent pregnancy. He has no history of drug abuse or addiction and is willing to undergo a urine screen for drugs of abuse. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

A 65-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with end-stage renal disease due to hypertension presents with complaints of fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss. He has been started on peritoneal dialysis (PD) 2 months ago and has been trained to perform PD at home. His medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for which he is on medication. He has no known drug allergies. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals a thin built with mild bilateral pedal edema. Laboratory results show a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, serum albumin of 2.8 g/dL, and a serum creatinine level of 2.1 mg/dL. The patient's PD adequacy is within target range. Nutritional assessment reveals an inadequate protein intake of 0.8 g/kg/day. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to educate him about optimizing his dietary protein intake using wechat technology. He meets the inclusion criteria and provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

An 93-year-old male patient is admitted to CHU Brugmann Hospital due to a positive RT-PCR test for SARS-CoV2. The patient reports a dry cough, shortness of breath, and mild fever. He has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and benign prostatic hypertrophy. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and tamsulosin. The patient lives alone in his home and has not had any known contact with COVID-19 positive individuals. He has been compliant with social distancing guidelines and has not left his home except for essential doctor visits. Upon admission, his vital signs are within normal limits except for a mild fever of 100.4°F. He is placed in isolation precautions and started on supportive care and oxygen therapy. The patient is enrolled in the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of being over 90 years of age and having a confirmed SARS-CoV2 infection.

A 35 year old woman has been suffering from major depressive episode for the last 2 years. She has failed to respond to at least one well-conducted antidepressant treatment as documented by the MGH-ATRQ scale. She also complains of fatigue, low energy, and loss of interest in daily activities. Her mood is mostly depressed, and she has a tendency to feel hopeless and helpless. Her appetite is decreased, and she has lost some weight over the last few months. She has difficulty sleeping and often wakes up earlier than usual in the morning. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenic disorder, neurodegenerative disease, or addiction to any toxic substances. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is able to undergo N2O diffusion via a facial mask. She has signed an informed consent and is affiliated with a social security scheme. She is eligible for the clinical trial as a depressive patient.

This is a 26-year-old female who is 13 weeks pregnant and wishes to terminate her pregnancy. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and occasional pelvic pain. She has no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. Ultrasonography reveals a single intrauterine pregnancy with a craniocaudal length of 68 mm. She is eligible for the trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of being above 18 years of age with a single intrauterine pregnancy between 12 and 14 weeks, and wishing to terminate the pregnancy. She does not have any exclusion criteria such as uterine abnormalities or coagulation disorders.

A 30 yo F with patchy hair loss on the scalp for the past 8 months is seeking treatment for her alopecia areata. The hair loss has been localized to 2 patches and involves less than 50% of her scalp. She has not received any medication for alopecia areata for at least 2 months prior to starting the study and has agreed to join the study by signing written consent. She does not have any other scalp lesions within the treated area and does not have any medical conditions such as autoimmune diseases. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who has been struggling with weight gain and has a body mass index (BMI) that falls between the 85th and 98th percentile for their age. They live on Oahu and have a primary care provider at a medical access point. The child is due for or scheduled for a well-child/physical exam visit during the months of the pilot study. The child does not have any chronic diseases that would affect participation in the study, such as diabetes mellitus, polycystic ovarian syndrome, gastroesophageal reflux, gallbladder disease, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, pseudo tumor cerebri, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, Blount's disease, or obstructive sleep apnea/sleep disturbance. The child and their family are interested in participating in a community-based intervention that links food, physical activity, and health, with a goal of preventing further weight gain and promoting healthy behaviors.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been struggling with severe depression for the past few months. She has failed to respond to multiple treatments, including antidepressant medications and therapy. Her depression has caused significant impairment in her daily functioning and she has been referred for electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) treatment at St Patrick's Mental Health Services. The patient has no history of alcohol or substance abuse in the past six months, and she is not pregnant or currently breastfeeding. She is physically healthy and able to provide informed consent. The patient meets the DSM-V criteria for major depressive disorder and has a Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score of ≥20. She has no major neurological or organic brain disorder, and there are no contraindications to ketamine or midazolam.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of knee osteoarthritis (OA) for the past two years. He has been experiencing pain, stiffness and difficulty walking for the past couple of months. The pain is localized to the medial side of the knee and is worse with prolonged standing and walking. The patient has tried various conservative treatments, such as physical therapy and over-the-counter painkillers, but has not experienced any significant improvement. The patient is otherwise healthy, with a BMI of 25 and no history of autoimmune rheumatic diseases or blood disorders. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for his knee OA.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with severe pain on her right flank. She reports that the pain started suddenly and has been constant for the past few hours. The patient has a history of renal colic and has experienced similar episodes in the past. She reports that she has tried over-the-counter pain medications without relief. Upon examination, she is alert and oriented, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She rates her pain as 8 out of 10 on the visual analogue scale. The patient has no known allergies to medications and has not taken any analgesics in the past 6 hours. She has no history of renal, pulmonary, cardiac, or hepatic failure, and has not undergone renal transplantation. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with HIV. She is currently in her 20th week of pregnancy and attends regular antenatal care visits at a local clinic in Tanzania. Her CD4 count is 350 cells/mm³, and she is not currently on antiretroviral therapy (ART). She reports no history of opportunistic infections, and her viral load is undetectable. She has not taken any multivitamin supplements during her pregnancy so far. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study protocol. She has no known allergies to any of the study supplements.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the hospital with symptoms consistent with COVID-19. He was confirmed positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection by PCR and was admitted within the first 48 hours of hospitalization. He is currently experiencing moderate respiratory distress with a WHO clinical status of 4. He has not required invasive mechanical ventilation and does not have any established limitation of therapeutic effort. He has no prior history of colchicine treatment for any other condition and is not currently receiving immunosuppressive agents, corticoids, or interleukine-1 antagonists. He is not allergic to colchicine and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent.

A 32 year old man with a history of HIV infection and current treatment came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He reported experiencing mild vision changes and difficulty reading. Upon examination, he was diagnosed with cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in his left eye. His CD4 T-cell count was greater than 150 cells per microliter, and his platelet count, hemoglobin, and total neutrophil count were all within normal limits. He agreed to participate in a clinical trial to see if elevated CD4 counts from HIV medications are effective in controlling CMV retinitis. After receiving systemic maintenance therapy with ganciclovir, foscarnet, or cidofovir, he has been receiving anti-CMV therapy for 6 months. His CMV retinitis is non-progressive, and the location of the infection is not immediately sight-threatening. He has agreed to discontinue anti-CMV therapy and be closely monitored for progression of the retinitis. He will be examined every 2 weeks for the next 3 months, and then every 3 weeks for the following 3 months. Blood and urine samples will be taken to test for levels of HIV and CMV in the blood and urine, and he will be interviewed about his vision and how it affects daily activities.

Patient A is a 20-year-old female who has had no more than 4 sexual partners in her lifetime. She has no history of abnormal PAP test or cervical biopsy result. She has also never had external genital or vaginal warts and has never tested positive for HPV. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an investigational HPV vaccine and is between 16 and 23 years of age.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with colon cancer. She is scheduled for a partial colon resection with primary anastomosis via laparotomy. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has a BMI of 28. She reports occasional constipation and bloating, but no other significant gastrointestinal symptoms. She has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past. She is currently taking aspirin and vitamin D supplements. She has been advised to undergo intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) opioids for postoperative pain management. She is fully informed about the clinical trial and is willing to participate.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to her lungs, liver, and bones. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy but the cancer continued to progress. She is now experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has undergone 2 courses of chemotherapy before, but her oncologist recommends her for this phase I clinical trial that combines docetaxel and temozolomide. She has no brain metastasis and her MRI and CT scans show stable disease. Her lab results show an absolute granulocyte count of 2,100/mm³, a platelet count of 130,000/mm³, and hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL. Her creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL, bilirubin level is normal, PT is normal, and her sodium and potassium levels are normal. Her AST and ALT are 1.2 times the upper limit of normal, and alkaline phosphatase is 1.8 times the upper limit of normal. She has no decompensated cardiac arrhythmia or other severe cardiovascular disease. She has no peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1 and no history of severe hypersensitivity reaction to docetaxel or other drugs formulated with polysorbate 80. She is negative for hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, and HIV. She has not had a pulmonary embolus in the past 3 weeks and is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to use 2 methods of effective contraception.

Patient is a 25-year-old male with no significant medical history. The patient presents with a compound class II cavity in the lower right first molar. The cavity has caused some sensitivity while eating hot or cold foods. The patient maintains good oral hygiene and reports no spacing or crowding issues. The patient has healthy periodontium with no evidence of gum disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understand the procedures involved.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of Overactive Bladder (OAB) for the past year. She reports frequent urges to urinate and sometimes leaks urine before reaching the bathroom. She has tried lifestyle modifications such as bladder training and pelvic floor exercises, but her symptoms have not improved. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker with a BMI of 25. She is currently employed and reports that her OAB symptoms are affecting her ability to work and participate in social activities. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve her condition and contribute to medical research.

A 10-month-old baby boy has been diagnosed with unilateral cerebral palsy. He was born at 35 weeks gestation and spent 2 weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit due to respiratory distress syndrome. He has been receiving regular physical therapy and occupational therapy since he was 3 months old. He can roll over and sit with support but has difficulties using his right arm and leg. He has no history of seizures or surgical interventions. His parents are interested in enrolling him in the HABIT-ILE clinical trial to see if it can improve his motor function and everyday life activities.

The patient is a 53 year old male who has been experiencing cough, fever and shortness of breath for the past 10 days. He lives in a community that has been significantly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. He works as a sales representative and travels frequently for work. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 28 and his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. His oxygen saturation levels are low and he has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for management of ARDS related to COVID-19 infection. He has been placed on mechanical ventilation but his condition is deteriorating. The medical team has suggested ECMO therapy as a potential treatment option and he has given his consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 57-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease was referred to the clinical trial. He had been diagnosed with CKD stage 5 six months ago and had never received renal replacement therapy. He had no history of bleeding or thrombotic events. His laboratory studies revealed a low platelet count of 120,000/mm3, an INR of 1.1 and fibrinogen levels of 340 mg/dL. He had no history of liver disease, malignancy or bleeding disorders. He was not on any antiplatelet drugs, erythropoietin or desmopressin. He had not received PRBC, FFPs or Platelet Transfusions in the past 3 months. The patient was willing to participate in the study and provided informed consent.

The patient is a 58 year old male who presents to the clinic with a chronic cough and shortness of breath. He has a 30-pack-year history of smoking and quit smoking 2 years ago. Upon further evaluation, the patient is diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stage IIB. The patient is currently employed as a construction worker and has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale. His serum bilirubin and ALAT are within normal limits. He is able to take oral medication and is willing to comply with study and follow-up procedures. The patient has no other malignancies within the last 5 years and is not nursing. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing peripheral neuropathic pain for the past 6 months. Her pain is located in her right leg and foot, and it is caused by nerve injury from a previous surgery. She has tried various pain medications, but none have provided relief. She does not consume alcohol or sedatives. She has a history of depression, but it is currently controlled with medication. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to any medications. She is not currently participating in any other clinical studies and has not participated in any during the past 30 days. She is not at risk of non-compliance and is not a woman of childbearing potential or lactating. She meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

As this study is a secondary data analysis of the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), there is no specific patient description required for enrollment. The participants in the original study were all pregnant women living in the geographical area of Avon, UK, who were expected to deliver their baby between 1st April 1991 and 31st December 1992. Therefore, any woman who met the inclusion criteria for the ALSPAC study is eligible for this secondary analysis.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. She has undergone a lumpectomy and is now postmenopausal. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperthyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke and does not use any illicit drugs. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her oncologist recommends hormonal therapy with Aromasin (Exemestane) to prevent the risk of cancer recurrence. She is willing to participate in the post-marketing surveillance study to monitor the safety and efficacy of Aromasin. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 58-year-old man diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy. He will receive a central venous catheter for the administration of chemotherapy. The expected duration of chemotherapy-associated neutropenia is at least 5 days, and the expected duration of central venous catheter use is at least 10 days. The patient has no known allergies to chlorhexidine or silver-sulfadiazine. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical or psychological conditions that would prevent him from completing the study or signing informed consent. The patient has not been enrolled in this study before.

The patient is a 50 year old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes. He has a Medtronic Cardiac Rhythm and Heart Failure (CRHF) device implanted with the Optivol® and Cardiac Compass® diagnostics for the past 2 years. He has experienced some clinical events in the past year, including a hospitalization due to heart failure, which required a medication change. He has also been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and renal deficiency. He is currently taking medications for his hypertension and diabetes, and his blood pressure and blood glucose levels are well controlled. He is a retired teacher and enjoys spending time with his family and grandchildren. He also likes to read and watch movies. He is willing to participate in this study and give informed consent.

A 72 year old woman arrives at the clinic with her daughter complaining about her mother's behavior. The patient has a previous diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and has been having episodes of agitation, including yelling and physical aggression towards her daughter and caregivers. The patient has become more and more withdrawn, and despite the efforts of the caregivers, they have not been able to calm her down. The patient has no other significant medical history and is taking no other medications. The daughter is her primary caregiver and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her mother's quality of life. The patient is medically stable and has no planned changes in her environment for the duration of the study. The daughter is available to give informed consent and represents the patient's legal representative. The patient is compliant with oral medication and able to take escitalopram. The patient has not been previously treated with citalopram and has no history of intolerance to it. The patient's Modified Hachinski score is less than 4.

The patient is a 63-year-old female who has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee. She experiences pain and disability in her knee joint, which has been ongoing for several years. She has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and corticosteroid injections, but has not experienced significant relief. She has been deemed a candidate for surgery and is interested in participating in this study to determine the best type of cutting guide for her total knee replacement. She has no known history of infection, sepsis, osteomyelitis, osteoporosis, metabolic disorders, or neuromuscular disease. She has never had an MRI and is willing to undergo one as part of the study. She understands the study requirements and is willing to return for follow-up visits.

This is a 7 year-old male with cerebral palsy and history of recurrent aspiration pneumonia. He has a gastrostomy tube in place for enteral feeding but it is frequently dislodged, requiring replacement. The patient has been scheduled for a PEG procedure to provide a more stable and long-term access for feeding. The patient's parents have been informed of the risks and benefits of the procedure and have consented to their child's participation in the study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of CO2 insufflation during the PEG procedure. The patient has no known contraindications to the procedure and is able to provide informed consent.

A 50-year-old woman came to the clinic with persistent lower back pain that radiates to her left leg for the past year. She reported that the pain has been getting worse and is unresponsive to conservative treatments such as physical therapy, medications, and injections. She has been diagnosed with degenerative disc disease and spinal stenosis at the L4-L5 level. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She works as a teacher and has been on leave for the past six months due to her back pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of Osteocel Plus in her TLIF procedure. She has been informed about the study requirements and is willing to comply with the follow-up protocol. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. She has signed the informed consent form and is ready to participate in the study.

50-year-old male with a history of tumor-induced osteomalacia (TIO) who underwent surgical excision of the underlying tumor three years ago, but continues to experience persistent symptoms of osteomalacia. He has a fasting serum phosphorus level of 2.3 mg/dL and an FGF23 level of 200 pg/mL. He has not received any treatment with pharmacologic vitamin D metabolites, phosphate or aluminum hydroxide antacids, or medication to suppress parathyroid hormone within the past 2 months. He has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years, and no history of allergic reactions to tetracycline, benzodiazepines, fentanyl, or lidocaine. He is willing to provide access to prior medical records to determine eligibility, and is willing and able to complete all aspects of the study, adhere to the study visit schedule, and comply with the assessments.

A 55-year-old female with a history of idiopathic overactive bladder for the past 8 months presenting with urinary urgency, frequency, and nocturia. She reports having to urinate every hour during the day, and at least twice at night, causing significant disruption to her sleep. She has tried several medications in the past, including anticholinergics and mirabegron, but they provided limited relief and caused bothersome side effects. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of bladder surgery or other conditions that may affect bladder function. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of MEDITOXIN® for the treatment of her overactive bladder symptoms.

56-year-old male with a 6-month history of progressive weakness and atrophy of both upper and lower limbs, difficulty with speaking and swallowing, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with ALS based on clinical and electrophysiological findings according to the El-Escorial criteria. He has been on riluzole for the past 3 months but has noticed little improvement in his symptoms. His ALSFRS-R score is currently 23, and his FVC is 45%. He has no history of other motor neuron diseases and is not currently undergoing any experimental treatments. He has not undergone tracheostomy, enteral or parenteral supply, and has no severe psychiatric disorders. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of palmitoylethanolamide in combination with riluzole to potentially improve his clinical and electrophysiological parameters.

A 68-year-old man presents with a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in both eyes. He reports difficulty recognizing faces, reading, and performing activities of daily living. He has undergone low vision rehabilitation and is currently using a magnifying glass to read. He is a retired accountant and has been married for 45 years. He has two adult children and three grandchildren. He is fluent in English and has no significant hearing or communication problems. He has no history of psychiatric illness, but does report feeling frustrated and helpless due to his vision loss. He scored 1 error on the cognitive screening measure (SPBS) and has access to a telephone. He is interested in participating in a study that might help him learn new problem-solving skills to manage his vision loss.

A 45-year-old male presented with a painful lump in his left thigh that had been growing slowly for the past 6 months. He has no significant past medical history, and he does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Physical examination revealed a firm, non-tender mass measuring 10 cm x 8 cm. MRI showed a lobulated, heterogeneous soft tissue mass in the left thigh with an enhancing rim and central necrosis. A biopsy was performed that confirmed a diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma. The patient is scheduled for surgery to remove the tumor, and he was offered to participate in a clinical trial investigating soft tissue sarcoma hypoxia using an investigational radiotracer, 18F-FMISO. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not pregnant and has no medical conditions that would compromise his safety or successful participation in the study.

Patient is a post-menopausal woman between the ages of 40 and 70 years with symptoms of vaginal atrophy. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has no known history of narcotic addiction, drug abuse or alcoholism. She has not used any sex steroids including phytoestrogens, hormonal intrauterine device or herbal medicinal products with known estrogenic effects within 3 months prior to baseline. She has no significant acute illness at the screening visit and is judged to be healthy on the basis of medical evaluation. The patient

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with neovascular glaucoma. He works as a computer engineer and has noticed gradual vision loss in his left eye over the past few months. On examination, his best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in his left eye was <0.01 (Snellen chart), while his BCVA in his right eye was >0.1. Intraocular pressure measured by Goldmann applanation tonometer was >21mmHg. Neovascularization was observed in the iris and anterior chamber angle. He has not received any intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF drugs in the last 3 months and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. He has no history of other ocular diseases that affect ocular examinations or systemic diseases that may affect the anti-neovascular effect of KDR2-2. He is willing to comply with follow-up for more than 28 days and has provided written informed consent. He is eligible to participate in the KDR2-2 Suspension Eyedrop in the Treatment of Neovascular Glaucoma (KDR-NVG) Trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of lung cancer, which has metastasized to his liver and bones. Despite undergoing several rounds of chemotherapy, his cancer continues to progress, and his doctors have informed him that his cancer is now advanced and cannot be cured or controlled with treatment. The patient is experiencing significant pain due to his metastatic cancer and is looking for alternative treatment options. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not have any significant cardiac or renal history. He is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study drug. He is able to swallow and absorb oral tablets normally. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been experiencing situational erectile dysfunction for the past 6 months. He is in a committed relationship with his partner but has difficulty maintaining an erection during sexual activity with her. He has tried taking medications for ED, but has experienced poor adherence due to side effects and concerns about long-term use. He reports feeling anxious and stressed during sexual activity, worrying about his ability to maintain an erection and satisfy his partner. The patient has no history of other medical or mental health conditions. He is fluent in English and interested in participating in a 6-session mindfulness-based psychosexual therapy (MBPST) group with 6-10 other men. The patient is willing to abstain from using medications for ED for the duration of the study and is comfortable with sharing his experiences in a group setting.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a construction worker and suffered a rotator cuff tear while lifting heavy equipment on the job. He has no significant medical history and has never undergone any surgeries before. He is currently experiencing pain, weakness, and limited mobility in his right shoulder. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m² and is considered to be in good physical health. He has been recommended for an elective surgical intervention on the shoulder with an indication for anesthesia via brachial plexus block. The patient has no known allergies to bupivacaine and does not have any cognitive impairment or active psychiatric condition. He does not have any coagulopathy and does not suffer from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. There is no infection at the site of the puncture for the block.

A 42-year-old male with a history of alcohol use disorder for the past 5 years. He lives with his partner of 3 years who has been supportive of his recovery journey. He has made some progress with therapy and medication but has experienced relapses in the past. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves a smartphone-based system that can assist him and his partner in managing his alcohol use disorder. He is comfortable with using a smartphone and does not have any physical or mental condition that limits his smartphone use. He has not experienced any serious interpersonal violence with his partner in the past year.

A 45-year-old female patient was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis six months ago. She has been experiencing moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness, especially in her wrists, fingers, and knees. Despite receiving treatment with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNF), her symptoms have not improved significantly. Her treating physician has made the decision to commence RoActemra/Actemra treatment in accordance with the local label as the patient needs RoActemra/Actemra monotherapy. She has not received RoActemra/Actemra treatment before but has been on DMARDs and TNF inhibitors. The patient is willing to participate in the non-interventional study to evaluate the efficacy of RoActemra/Actemra in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. She is 5'4" tall, weighs 160 lbs, and has no history of autoimmune disease or any joint inflammatory disease other than rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has recently undergone surgery and radiation therapy for stage II invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. She has completed chemotherapy and is currently on adjuvant endocrine therapy. Her BMI is 29 kg/m2, and her body fat percentage is 35%. She experiences fatigue and has gained weight since her diagnosis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve her body composition and overall health. She has no history of diabetes or hypertension and is not on insulin therapy. She has access to the internet and email and is willing to participate in Zoom calls for the dietitian counseling sessions. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/78 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rumination disorder based on the Rome III criteria. She has been experiencing frequent regurgitation of recently ingested food and is seeking treatment for her symptoms. She reports no history of alcohol or substance abuse and denies any current depression or anxiety disorder. She has no significant medical or neurological history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon examination, she has normal vital signs and no evidence of any other psychiatric or medical conditions that would impair her ability to participate in the study. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the interventions being tested.

The patient is a 57-year-old male smoker who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has already received one cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for his metastatic disease but unfortunately, he has experienced disease progression. He has a history of hypertension but it is currently well controlled on medication. He has no other significant medical history and his performance status according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) is 1. His labs are within normal limits and he has no evidence of brain metastases. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period.

This is a 32-year-old male who sustained a spinal cord injury resulting in paraplegia due to a motor vehicle accident three weeks ago. He presents with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale B and has been receiving standard care for his injury. He has expressed interest in participating in the SATURN study and is willing to receive open-label NeuroAiD in addition to his current treatment regimen. He has no history of dementia, demyelinating disease, autoimmune disease, or any other conditions that would limit clinical assessment of outcomes. He has provided informed consent for inclusion into the SATURN database.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been diagnosed with gastric cancer that has spread to his liver. He underwent platinum/fluoropyrimidine based chemotherapy for his gastric cancer, but unfortunately, the disease has progressed within 6 months of completing the first line of treatment. He is now looking for second line treatment options. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his CT scan shows both measurable and non-measurable disease. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy and his blood work shows his hemoglobin, platelets, and white blood cell count are within normal limits. He has a history of smoking for about 20 years but quit 5 years ago. He does not have any other significant medical history, and he is not currently taking any medication except for occasional pain medication for his cancer. He is married, with three children, and works as a teacher. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the study.

45-year-old male diagnosed with ALS two years ago is referred to participate in a clinical trial of Supported Treadmill Ambulation Training (STAT) at Carolinas ALS/Neuromuscular Center at the Carolinas HealthCare System. The patient is able to stand independently and ambulate for six minutes with the use of a walker. The patient's vital capacity is over 65% predicted. The patient has no history of heart disease or other unstable systemic disease. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the training and assessment procedures. The patient is excited to participate and hopeful that this intervention may improve his gait and function.

8-year-old boy with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) diagnosed 2 years ago. Following initial therapy, he achieved remission and completed therapy per protocol. He had been in remission until approximately 2 months ago when he was noted to have headaches, vomiting, lethargy and diplopia. MRI of the brain showed diffuse leptomeningeal disease. He began intrathecal therapy with methotrexate and Ara-C, but the disease continued to progress. He was then switched to intrathecal liposomal cytarabine, but this too failed to control the disease. He was then referred to our institution for consideration of experimental therapy. On admission, he was alert and oriented. Vital signs were stable. Neurological exam revealed bilateral papilledema, a positive Romberg test, and ataxia. The rest of the exam was unremarkable. MRI of the brain and spine confirmed diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement. Bone marrow biopsy showed no evidence of leukemia. He was deemed eligible for the study and informed consent was obtained from his parents.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for several months. He has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and has been treated with venlafaxine extended release (venlafaxine XR) for the last 12 weeks without significant improvement. He has given consent to participate in a clinical trial testing the effectiveness of combining buprenorphine with venlafaxine XR to treat difficult to treat depression. The study requires him to undergo an 8-week course of either low-dose buprenorphine or placebo augmentation of venlafaxine XR. The goal is to achieve remission of symptoms. The patient will undergo cognitive testing and MRI scans at the beginning and end of Phase 2. At the end of Phase 2, the blind will be broken for all participants. The patient who was on placebo in Phase 2 will be allowed to begin taking buprenorphine immediately for Phase 3, which will last approximately 8 weeks. Buprenorphine will be tapered off under the guidance of the P.I. after the study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is above 50 years, diagnosed with major depressive disorder, has a Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score of >/= 15, and has a clinical relationship with a primary care physician. The patient is not excluded from the study based on the exclusion criteria.

A 35-year-old woman visited the clinic complaining of heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, and pressure. She has been experiencing these symptoms for 6 months and has failed medical management. She is currently not pregnant and intends to use contraception throughout the study period as she has no intention of further childbearing. She has a normal pap smear within the last 36 months, and her cervix is suitable for tenaculum placement as determined by pelvic exam. She has been diagnosed with at least one intra-mural fibroid with a minimum diameter of greater than or equal to 3 cm and all fibroids with a diameter less than or equal to 8 cm with a prevailing pathology of fibroids determined through ultrasound. She is willing to participate in the study and complete all study-related procedures and evaluations. She has no history of thrombo-embolic disease, gynecologic malignancy, chronic pelvic inflammatory disease, or pelvic mass outside the uterus other than uterine fibroids. She has not undergone prior endometrial ablation, uterine artery embolization, or uterine artery ligation. She has no underlying bleeding disorder, is not using anticoagulation therapy, and is not unsuitable for MRI examination.

The patient is a healthy 6-month-old infant who has been previously vaccinated with Prevenar. The infant's parents have been consistently providing appropriate care and attention to their child's health, including following the recommended vaccination schedule. The infant is currently in good health, with no history of chronic illnesses or other health conditions. The family has no history of adverse reactions to vaccines. The infant is expected to be available for the entire study period. The parents are willing to provide informed consent for their child's participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who had COVID-19 infection 4 months ago. She was hospitalized for two weeks due to severe COVID-19 symptoms, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She recovered from the illness but now complains of persistent taste and smell disorders, including hypogeusia and hyposmia. She reports that food tastes bland and that she cannot detect certain smells anymore. She also complains of oral discomfort, including dry mouth and occasional ulcers on the tongue. She has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies but no other chronic medical conditions. She has not undergone any oral or nasal surgery or radiotherapy in the past. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help understand the long-term effects of COVID-19 on oral and olfactory health.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has been diagnosed with psoriasis. She has tried several treatments in the past including topical creams and light therapy, but has not seen significant improvement with these options. Her dermatologist has recommended starting treatment with Enbrel, and she has agreed to participate in this observational study to assess the real-life management of psoriasis patients treated with Enbrel according to the new reimbursement criteria. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study as she is over 18 years old and is starting treatment with Enbrel in alignment with the reimbursement criteria. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study and will be followed for at least 1 year.

62-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago, presenting with a tremor in his right hand and difficulty walking. He is currently being treated with levodopa-carbidopa, but has noticed a decline in the effectiveness of the medication over time. He has a brother and a sister who are both over the age of 40 and willing to participate in the study. The patient has a history of smoking and social alcohol use, and has been diagnosed with anxiety and depression in the past. He is interested in participating in the study to help further research on the genetic factors associated with Parkinson's disease.

This is a 63-year-old male patient with end-stage renal failure who is dependent on hemodialysis. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. He has no history of tobacco or alcohol use. He recently presented with symptoms of brachiocephalic fistula (BCF) transposition and his physician has recommended surgery. Due to the patient's comorbidities, altered pharmacokinetic drug handling, and multiple medications, safe sedation is of utmost importance. The patient has not taken neuroleptics or benzodiazepines within the past 2 weeks nor has he been chronically using alcohol or opioids. The patient has no active lung disease or significant cardiac disease, and his left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than 30%. The patient has not had a recent cerebrovascular accident. The patient has agreed to participate in the study comparing sevoflurane with propofol sedation in ESRF patients undergoing BCF transposition.

Patient is a 10-year-old boy who was diagnosed with ADHD at age 7. He has been receiving treatment with methylphenidate (Ritalin) for the past 2 years but has not experienced significant improvement in his symptoms. He exhibits symptoms of hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention, which have resulted in poor academic performance and difficulty with social interactions. The patient has no history of comorbid psychiatric disorders or conduct disorder. He is currently in the 4th grade and is struggling to keep up with his schoolwork. His parents are concerned about his academic progress and his ability to succeed in school. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is excited about the possibility of finding a more effective treatment option for his ADHD.

A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of vertigo, nausea, and imbalance that started suddenly 2 days ago. He describes a sensation of spinning and had difficulty maintaining balance while standing, walking, or turning around. He denies any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear pain. He has no significant medical history, and his family history is unremarkable. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. On examination, he has horizontal-rotatory spontaneous nystagmus and gait instability. Audiometry reveals no hearing loss. He is diagnosed with acute vestibular neuritis and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial investigating the role of corticosteroids and vestibular exercises in recovery of balance. He does not have any contraindication to receive corticosteroids.

This is a 45-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She was admitted to the hospital with a fever, chills, and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with septic shock and started on norepinephrine and vasopressin infusions for the management of her condition. She has been receiving treatment for the past 3 days and her blood pressure has stabilized. The treating physician has decided to start reducing her vasopressor dose in order to wean her off of the medication. She has consented to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the incidence of hypotension based on the discontinuation order of norepinephrine and vasopressin in patients receiving concomitant norepinephrine and vasopressin infusions for the treatment of septic shock. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old Hispanic father of two children, aged 7 and 9, who reside in the Greater Houston area. He is currently overweight with a BMI of 30 and has been struggling with his weight for several years. He has no major medical conditions that affect his physical activity or dietary intake. He is eager to participate in the Papás Saludables, Niños Saludables program to improve his health and the health of his children. His children are both healthy and attend the TCHP Center for Children and Women Clinic. The father is able to read and write in Spanish and English, as is his co-parent, the children's mother. The family is willing to wear an accelerometer for a 7-day study period at baseline and 4 months later. The father has not lost more than 10 pounds recently, is not in a current weight loss program, and is not taking medications to lose weight. He has passed the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) health screener and is approved to participate in the program.

A 35-year-old male patient diagnosed with HIV infection is currently taking tipranavir/ritonavir 500/200 mg every 12 hours for the past 6 weeks. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 8 years and has a history of viral failure despite previous treatment with protease inhibitors. His HIV viral load has been undetectable (<50 copies/mL) for the past 16 weeks. The patient has a resistance test that showed the presence of major mutations in the protease gene. His current regimen has been well tolerated except for occasional gastrointestinal adverse events. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the security of the dose reduction of ritonavir in HIV-infected patients in treatment with tipranavir/ritonavir 500/200 mg every 12 hours. He is able to follow the treatment period and has an inhibition quotient (IQ) of 70. The patient has signed the informed consent and is currently not experiencing any AIDS-defining illnesses.

A 50-year-old male patient with a history of solid tumor and lymphoma has failed to respond to standard therapies. He has completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy four weeks ago and has recovered from associated toxicities. He has no history of seizures or brain metastases. He has an ECOG performance status of 2 (Karnofsky greater than or equal to 60 percent) and is expected to live more than 3 months. He has normal organ and marrow function, with an absolute neutrophil count greater than or equal to 1500/mcL, platelets greater than or equal to 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin less than 1.5 times institutional upper limit of normal, AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) less than or equal to 2.5 times institutional upper limit of normal, and creatinine less than 1.5 times institutional upper limit of normal. He is willing to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) for the duration of the study participation and for 30 days after completion of the study. He understands the study requirements and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

50-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV). Patient reports no prior treatment for HCV and is currently not on any medications for the condition. Patient has tested positive for HCV genotype 4 and has no history of other chronic liver diseases. The patient is currently not positive for HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM Ab, or anti-HIV Ab. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of sofosbuvir in combination with pegylated interferon and ribavirin for the treatment of HCV genotype 4.

The patient is a 55 year old man with a history of peripheral artery disease (PAD) diagnosed by his primary care physician. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He experiences intermittent claudication in his left leg and has difficulty walking more than a few blocks without having to stop and rest. He also reports occasional numbness and tingling in his feet. He takes aspirin daily and has had a recent lipid panel showing low serum HDL cholesterol levels (34mg/dL). He has been referred to a specialist for further management of his PAD. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a BMI of 28 and his blood pressure is well controlled on medication. He denies any history of liver or muscle problems and is not allergic to statins or nicotinic acid. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve his lipid levels and potentially prevent the progression of his PAD.

The patient is a 42-year-old Caucasian woman who is overweight with a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. She was recently diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance with plasma glucose values of 9.5 mmol/L after a glucose drink consumption during OGTT screening. She has a regular sleeping pattern and sleeps for about 8 hours per night. She has been following a stable diet for the past three months and has not gained or lost more than 2 kg. She does not take anticoagulants and does not have any food allergies or intolerances. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 200mg of caffeine per day.
