She is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve her health and is willing to commit to a 12-week high-intensity interval training program.

This is a 12-year-old girl who was diagnosed with ALL in [**11/2010**]. She underwent standard induction chemotherapy and central nervous system prophylaxis, followed by consolidation, delayed intensification, and maintenance chemotherapy. She completed her treatment in [**10/2013**] and has been in remission since then. Her family history is unremarkable for any genetic diseases. She has not received any allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. She has no known allergies to medications or any known medical conditions. She currently has a good performance status and is able to attend school regularly. She has regular follow-up consultations with her oncologist and is compliant with her scheduled blood tests and imaging studies. She and her parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have agreed to participate.

A 30-year-old female with a BMI of 25.5 came to the clinic seeking a natural approach to weight loss. She has tried various diets and exercise regimens in the past without much success. She reported no significant medical history, and all her vital signs were within normal limits. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a tea leaf extract preparation on carbohydrate and fat absorption. She was informed about the study protocol and provided with the necessary information. She met the eligibility criteria and provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male from Upper Egypt, with a history of HBV related liver disorder, presents with symptoms of jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal pain. He was diagnosed with HBsAg positive chronic infection and is eligible for the clinical trial. He has no history of dual infection with other viruses, auto-immune or alcoholic hepatitis. The patient has been experiencing symptoms for the past few weeks and his condition is worsening. He is willing to participate in the study to receive treatment and help researchers better understand the prevalence and characteristics of hepatitis D virus infection among HBsAg positive individuals.

Patient is a 33-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 3 years with no success. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and is now undergoing her second IVF/ICSI cycle at the Department of Reproductive Medicine at Ghent University Hospital. She has at least 2 good quality blastocysts remaining after fresh embryo transfer. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent and willing to accept a single embryo transfer. Her BMI is within the range of 18 to 35 kg/m2. The patient has no family history of genetic abnormality, has not undergone any preimplantation genetic testing, and has not experienced three or more clinical miscarriages or recurrent implantation failure. She does not have severe endometriosis or an abnormal uterine cavity, and her cycles do not require surgical sperm recovery procedures, total asthenozoospermia, or globozoospermia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the cryopreserved blastocyst's implantation potential after genetic screening.

45-year-old male with a diagnosis of unilateral inguinal hernia scheduled for hernioplasty in the ambulatory surgery unit. He has no history of recurrent hernia, allergies, ongoing infections, or diabetes. The patient has never had a previous rejection of prosthetic material (mesh). He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of dexamethasone added to the usual treatment with bupivacaine in the local infiltration of the surgical area on postoperative pain. The patient will be able to comply with the pain evaluation through the visual analogue scale and follow-up visits at 8 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 8 days.

A 42-year-old male patient with a history of failed root canal treatment presented with pain in the right maxillary region. The pain started a month ago and has been gradually increasing in intensity. The patient also reported swelling in the same region. His medical history is unremarkable, and he denies any allergies or chronic diseases. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, the right maxillary region was tender to palpation, and there was a visible swelling. The patient's vital signs were within normal limits, and there were no signs of systemic illness. Radiographs revealed a periapical lesion in the right maxillary first molar. The patient was informed about the surgical procedure and signed a consent form. The patient was randomized into the MTA+PRF group and underwent apical resection. Routine radiographs were taken in the 1st, 3rd, and 6th months, and a CT scan was taken in the 12th month. The primary healing of the periapical tissues was evaluated, and the outcomes were measured. The patient has been under control for long-term outcomes of the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female student who has been experiencing occasional feelings of sadness and anxiety for the past few months. She is generally healthy and does not have any history of mental illness. She owns a smartphone with an Android operating system. She does not smoke, and she is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She does not have any known gastrointestinal issues such as IBS or IBD. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of probiotics on mood and is willing to take a daily dose of either probiotics or placebo for six weeks.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing cough and fever for the past 7 days. He has not been in contact with anyone known to have COVID-19, but he has been traveling frequently for work. The cough is dry and persistent, and the fever has been intermittent, ranging from 100 to 102 degrees Fahrenheit. The patient has not noticed any other symptoms, such as shortness of breath or loss of taste or smell. The patient has a history of cholecystectomy and is currently experiencing severe abdominal pain that requires emergency laparoscopy. He is informed of the study and agrees to participate. The patient is affiliated with the French social security system and provides written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 59 year old man came to the clinic complaining of lower back pain that has been progressively getting worse over the past few months. He also reported a recent weight loss and fatigue. The physical exam revealed tenderness on palpation over his lower back and decreased range of motion. His MRI showed a lesion in the lumbar spine suggestive of a possible infection or tumor. He has no history of bleeding disorders or any other medical conditions that would make him unfit for spinal biopsy. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has a BMI of 36. She has struggled with her weight for many years and has tried various diets and exercise programs, but has been unable to lose weight. She has a past medical history of hypertension and sleep apnea, which she manages with medications. She is of Han Chinese ethnicity and resides in Taiwan. She is interested in undergoing sleeve gastrectomy surgery to help with her weight loss. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate her nutritional status before and after the surgery. She has no history of kidney dysfunction, mental illness, severe eating disorders, alcohol or drug abuse, stomach ulcers, or redo bariatric surgery. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is committed to providing accurate food and supplement records during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing tremors in his right hand and arm for the past year, which have progressively worsened. He also reports stiffness and difficulty with movements, especially in the morning. He has been taking levodopa-carbidopa 25/100mg three times a day for the past 6 months, which has helped with his symptoms. He has no significant medical or surgical history and is able to walk unassisted. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help further the understanding of his condition and potentially improve treatment options for himself and others.

The patient is a 35-year-old female scheduled for elective hand surgery due to carpal tunnel syndrome. She has a history of mild hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. She has no previous history of neuropathy, coagulopathy, or allergies to any medications. She is not pregnant and her body mass index is within the normal range. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or any infections in the supraclavicular area. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 3 years ago. She has been in remission for the past 6 months and has not experienced any symptoms during this time. Her Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) is less than 150 and her C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels are within normal range. She has no history of hypercalcemia or short bowel syndrome, and is not pregnant. She is willing to participate in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial to examine the effectiveness of vitamin D treatment in maintaining remission of her Crohn's disease.

The patient is a 72-year-old man with a history of hypertension and no prior history of atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and has been seeing his primary care physician regularly for check-ups. He is willing to provide consent to participate in the study and to use personal health information to ascertain endpoints from the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Medicare Claims Database and to access data from health records. He has health insurance by Medicare Parts A & B (Medicare Fee-for-service).  The patient is generally in good health, but is concerned about his risk for stroke. He is interested in participating in the study to determine if an AF detection intervention can help reduce his risk of stroke. He has no allergies to adhesive and does not have any implanted cardiac devices. He is compliant with his medications and is able to follow study instructions.

The patient is a 52-year-old female with a history of Type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. Despite being prescribed medication for her diabetes, her HbA1c levels have consistently been above 8% at the last three measurements. She has difficulty adhering to her medication regimen and struggles with lifestyle changes such as diet and exercise. The patient is fluent in Danish and is seeking additional support to manage her diabetes. She has not participated in any other intervention research projects during the trial period and is not currently being treated by a psychiatrist or psychologist. The patient has no issues with vision or blindness.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with fair skin (phototype II). She has no history of allergies or sensitivities to topical products. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not used any anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive drugs in the past month. She has no active skin diseases. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and attend all scheduled medical evaluations and product applications. She has no plans to start using new drugs or cosmetics during the study. The patient has undergone an integral skin test in the region of interest and is eligible for the trial.

Patient is an 68-year-old retired Israeli man who has been experiencing insomnia for the past 2 years. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 72/min. He speaks Hebrew fluently and is computer literate. He has no significant visual or hearing impairment and has healthy dominant hand functioning. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and no history of significant psychiatric or neurological illness. He has not been diagnosed with any other sleep disorders. He is interested in participating in a study that could help him improve his sleep quality.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is generally healthy and has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions or allergies. He has good oral hygiene, with no history of periodontal disease, oral ulcers, or oral mucosal lesions. He does not wear removable dentures and has not received any special oral cleanings. He is willing to participate in the study and able to follow the instructions provided by the investigators. He has signed the informed consent form and is committed to completing the study.

56 yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and non-valvular atrial fibrillation (diagnosed 3 months ago) presenting to the cardiology clinic for evaluation and initiation of oral anticoagulation. Patient is a retired veteran with coverage under the Department of Defense healthcare plan. Patient has no history of valvular procedures or transient causes of AF. Patient has not been on any oral anticoagulant therapy prior to this visit. Patient is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia, respectively. Patient has no known drug allergies. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Non-valvular atrial fibrillation (diagnosed 3 months ago) - No prior history of oral anticoagulant therapy

A 30-year old teacher has been experiencing symptoms of viral conjunctivitis for the past week. She complains of redness, itching, and foreign body sensation in her left eye. She has noticed some tearing and lid swelling as well. She denies any history of seasonal allergies or herpetic eye disease. She wears glasses for nearsightedness but has not used any ocular medications during the past week. She does not wear contact lenses. She had a mild cold two weeks ago, and one of her students had a red eye at that time. She does not have any significant medical history or allergies. She is not pregnant and has no bleeding disorders. She has no history of ocular surgery or chronic ocular disease.

A 7-year-old male child presents to the Nephrology Unit at Assiut University Children Hospital with steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome. The child was diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome at the age of 4 and has had multiple relapses despite receiving steroid therapy. The family history is unremarkable for kidney diseases. The child is currently on cyclosporine therapy and is being closely monitored by the medical team. The child has reported experiencing some side effects such as gastrointestinal disturbances and tremors since starting the therapy. The child's vital signs are within normal range, and there are no abnormalities detected during physical examination. The child's laboratory results show that the proteinuria has decreased significantly since starting the cyclosporine therapy. The medical team has recommended the child participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of cyclosporine therapy in children with steroid-dependent or steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome.

44 year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, Stage II-B. She underwent a biopsy after presenting with vaginal bleeding and a pelvic exam that revealed an abnormality. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her receive the most effective treatment for her cancer. She is willing to undergo further clinical staging to determine her eligibility for the trial and is committed to adhering to the study protocol. She is of childbearing potential but has agreed to use effective contraception during the trial. She currently has no evidence of septicemia or severe infection and her renal and hepatic function are within normal limits. She has signed an informed consent form and is willing and able to comply with the required follow-up visits.

The patient is an adult (above 18 years) who has been diagnosed as HIV-positive and has not been prescribed ART in the past three months. The patient is seeking care at the study clinic for any HIV-related reason or has been referred for HIV testing and care. The patient is not pregnant and intends to return to the clinic for further HIV care in the coming year. The patient is willing to be traced by phone or in person for follow-up care if needed and is physically, mentally, and emotionally able to participate in the study. The patient is also willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has not been previously enrolled in the same study or the SLATE I study.

A 25 year old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a temporal bone fracture resulting in facial nerve paralysis. The onset of the paralysis was immediate and he has experienced a complete loss of function. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is willing to undergo surgical intervention and meet the criteria for facial nerve exploration. He is not pregnant and is fit for surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic, burning pain in her feet and legs for the past 3 years. The pain is described as a sensation of pins and needles, and it is worse at night. She has seen multiple specialists who have been unable to identify the underlying cause of her symptoms. She has also undergone a skin biopsy which showed reduced intra-epidermal nerve fiber density in her legs, confirming the diagnosis of small fiber neuropathy. She rates her current pain level as 7 out of 10 on a VAS pain scale. The patient has been tested for autoantibodies and was found to have elevated levels of both TS-HDS and FGFR3 antibodies. She has no other medical conditions that could be causing her symptoms, and she is willing to comply with the study protocol. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if IVIG treatment can improve her symptoms and increase her intra-epidermal nerve fiber density.

This is a 65 year old male with a history of prostate cancer and radiographic bone metastases. He has previously undergone chemotherapy for metastatic disease and is currently receiving gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH) analogue therapy. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and a serum testosterone level less than or equal to 50 ng/dL. The patient has adequate organ function and a screening calculated ejection fraction of greater than or equal to 50% by multigated radionuclide angiography (MUGA) scan or Echocardiogram. He has not received Strontium-89, Samarium-153, or other radioisotope within 3 months of registration and has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds similar to sodium fluoride F-18 (NaF). The patient has not had a seizure disorder or known history of brain metastases. He is not currently receiving any herbal products and has not undergone radiotherapy within the last 4 weeks. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to TAK-700 or related compounds and has not received prior therapy for treatment of metastatic castrate resistant prostate cancer with

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo an otorhinolaryngological surgery. She has a history of mild asthma and has never had any issues with anesthesia or surgery in the past. She currently takes an inhaled corticosteroid for her asthma and has no other significant medical history. Her BMI is 22.5, and she weighs 60 kg. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits. She has no known allergies to any of the medications used in the study. The patient has normal renal and hepatic function, and her magnesium levels are within normal limits. She has not been taking any medications that could interfere with the study.

A 45-year-old man living with HIV came to the clinic for a regular check-up. He was diagnosed with HIV 10 years ago and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) ever since. He is currently taking TDF and lamivudine for HIV infection. He is a former intravenous drug user and has a history of unprotected sexual activity with multiple partners. He was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection after testing positive for HBV surface antigen twice, six months apart. He has no history of liver disease or liver function abnormalities. He has no allergies to any food or medications, and no history of previous treatment for HBV. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to monitor the long-term effects of TDF on HBV in HIV/HBV co-infected individuals.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent surgical treatment followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Currently, she is on third-generation AI therapy (letrozole) for the past 6 months. She complains of joint pain and stiffness in multiple joints, which started a month after starting AI therapy. The pain is rated at 6 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications like Tylenol and ibuprofen, but they provided only temporary relief. She has no known history of inflammatory or metabolic arthropathies or any other chronic illnesses. She does not have any allergies to NSAIDs or any other medications. She is willing to try acupuncture as an alternative treatment for her joint pain.

Patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes who presented to the urology clinic with complaints of intermittent right flank pain and hematuria. A CT scan revealed significant right hydronephrosis with minimal parenchymal thickness. The patient was evaluated for percutaneous nephrostomy drainage to relieve the obstruction and prevent further renal damage. The patient is currently scheduled for a nephrectomy due to the poorly functioning kidney. The patient has no history of malignancy and is willing to undergo a radioisotope study to assess the effect of percutaneous nephrostomy drainage on the imaging of the hydronephrotic kidney. The patient has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her right knee for the past year. She has tried conservative measures such as physical therapy, weight loss and corticosteroid injections, but they have provided little relief. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently well controlled with medication. She is not on any anticoagulation therapy. The patient has been scheduled for an elective total knee arthroplasty to alleviate her knee pain and improve her quality of life. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Xarelto for VTE prophylaxis after her surgery. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a diagnosis of primary open angle glaucoma. She presents with blurred vision, halos around lights, and occasional eye pain. Her visual field test shows characteristic defects and her optic nerve head appearance is consistent with glaucoma. Gonioscopy reveals predisposition to angle closure. She has not undergone cataract or glaucoma surgery and has no degenerative changes in the retina. She does not have any abnormalities preventing reliable measurements, ocular inflammation or disease, corneal disease, or fixation issues. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of phaco-trabeculectomy on anterior segment changes by optical coherence tomography.

A 45-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 5 years ago is being prescribed an anti IL-6 biotherapy treatment. She has been experiencing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness for the past few years that have significantly impacted her quality of life. She has been on various medications in the past, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), but her condition has not improved. She has 24 permanent teeth in her mouth, with 6 teeth showing signs of periodontitis. She has no known allergies to tocilizumab, saccharose, polysorbate 80, phosphate disodique dodécahydrate, or phosphate monosodique dehydrate. She has not had any surgeries in the past month or taken antibiotics in the last 2 months. She is willing to participate in the study and has expressed her written free and informed consent to do so.

A 60 year old male came to the clinic with a diabetic foot ulcer on his left foot. He is a known diabetic for 10 years and has been taking oral hypoglycemic agents. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and he is a smoker too. His wound was examined and staged as Wagner stage 3. He was enrolled in the phase 1 clinical trial of ALLO-ASC-DFU (ALLO-ASC-DFU-101) and treated with ALLO-ASC-DFU sheet. The treatment was successful, and the wound healed completely after 6 months of treatment. He is now being recruited for the follow-up study to evaluate the safety of ALLO-ASC-DFU treatment for 23 months. The patient is willing to participate and has given his written informed consent to comply with the study requirements.

Patient A is a 45-year-old man with a known history of HIV infection, diagnosed 10 years ago. He has been on Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy (HAART) for the past 8 years with good adherence and a current HIV viral load of less than 50 copies/ml. He presents with complaints of fever, night sweats, and weight loss. He was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) after a biopsy was taken from a lymph node. Further evaluation revealed that the NHL is of the large cell type with an International Prognosis Index (IPI) score of 2. He underwent standard first-line chemotherapy and achieved a complete remission. However, due to the poor prognosis associated with his initial presentation and HIV status, he has been chosen to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety of intensive chemotherapy followed by peripheral blood cell transplantation. He meets all eligibility criteria and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. His CD4+ T cell count at the time of NHL diagnosis was 250 cells/mm3 and his HIV viral load is currently undetectable.

The patient is a 20-year-old male diagnosed with Fanconi Anaemia Subtype A. He has been treated with ex vivo gene therapy on the FANCOLEN-I trial. His past medical history is significant for recurrent infections, fatigue, and anemia. He has been receiving regular blood transfusions to manage his anemia. He lives with his parents and younger siblings. He is currently enrolled in college, majoring in computer science. He is interested in sports and likes to play soccer with his friends. He is compliant with his medical treatment and follows up regularly with his healthcare team. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the long-term follow-up study to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of the gene therapy treatment. He is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and protocol requirements. He is optimistic about the future and hopes that the gene therapy treatment will improve his health and quality of life.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and underwent allogeneic bone marrow transplantation 6 months ago. She is currently on tacrolimus and prednisone for Graft Versus Host Disease (GVHD). She developed a persistent cough, fever, and difficulty breathing for the past 2 weeks. She also noticed a sharp pain in the right side of her chest. A chest CT scan showed a 3 cm cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe with surrounding infiltrates. A bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was performed, and the culture grew Aspergillus fumigatus. Based on the diagnosis of acute invasive aspergillosis, the patient will be evaluated for eligibility for this clinical trial comparing voriconazole to amphotericin B. She has no known history of hypersensitivity or intolerance to azole antifungal agents or conventional or lipid formulation of amphotericin B. She is a non-smoker and has no history of CMV pneumonia. She will be informed about the study, and if she agrees to participate, she will be randomized to receive either voriconazole or amphotericin B. She will be monitored for efficacy, safety, and toleration of the treatment.

Patient is a 23yo female who wears glasses and has no prior experience with contact lenses. She has a history of myopia and astigmatism, with a prescription of -3.50 diopters sphere and -1.00 diopter of refractive astigmatism in both eyes. She is interested in trying contact lenses for the first time and is willing to wear them on an extended wear basis for up to 7 days and 6 nights. She is in good general health and has no known ocular or systemic diseases that would interfere with contact lens wear. She is able to keep all specified appointments and is willing to adhere to the instructions set forth in the protocol. She has read and understands the Informed Consent Form and is able to give informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with colorectal cancer approximately one year ago. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor, and although the margins were negative, he was found to have liver metastases on imaging. He has been undergoing chemotherapy and has had a good response with significant reduction in the size of the liver metastases. He has a good performance status with an ECOG score of 0. He has no other significant medical history and his blood tests are within normal limits. He is interested in exploring the option of liver transplantation to further improve his chances of survival. He has signed informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 70-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) and has experienced two or more AF episodes lasting over an hour in the last six months. He has been treated with rate control and rhythm control drugs in the past three months, but his symptoms have not improved. He has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for several years. He has never had a stroke or transient ischemic attack. He also has a history of coronary artery disease and underwent a bypass surgery two years ago. His left atrium size is 5.5 cm, and his ejection fraction is 45%. He is willing to undergo catheter ablation if randomized to that arm of the trial. He is able to understand and sign informed consent.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of prostate cancer. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer six years ago and underwent prostatectomy followed by radiation therapy. He was doing well until he started experiencing back pain and stiffness about 3 months ago. The pain has become progressively worse and is now radiating down his legs. He has been taking over-the-counter painkillers but they have not been effective in relieving the pain. He has also noticed that he has been losing weight unintentionally and feels tired most of the time. He has been referred to an oncologist who has ordered imaging studies which reveal metastatic disease to the spine. The patient is able to walk independently but has some difficulty with prolonged standing and walking. He is a retired accountant and lives with his wife. He enjoys playing golf and watching sports on TV. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. There are no other significant findings on his physical exam.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman recently diagnosed with Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma. She is scheduled to receive the CHOP chemotherapy regimen. She has no significant medical history, but she is allergic to penicillin. She currently takes over-the-counter vitamins and supplements. She reports a history of mild nausea and vomiting during previous chemotherapy treatments. She has good liver, kidney and adrenal function. She has no history of diabetes. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the effect of combining aprepitant with CHOP on nausea and vomiting.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is currently undergoing treatment at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) and is interested in learning more about clinical trials as a potential option for her treatment. She has no prior experience with clinical trials and is looking for more information on the process and what to expect. She is accompanied by her husband, who serves as her primary caregiver and is also interested in learning more about clinical trials. They both speak English fluently and are able to provide informed consent. The patient is generally in good health and able to participate in the focus group discussions.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. He requires chemotherapy and blood product support, which will be administered through a single lumen Broviac or double lumen Hickman-type central venous catheter (CVC). The CVC is planned to remain in situ for 6 months from the start of the study. The patient has no history of thrombophilia or bleeding disorder and has not had a previous CVC removed due to any complication. The patient and their parents are willing to participate in the trial and understand the study requirements. The patient is being treated at a pediatric hematology and oncology center.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic pain and fatigue for several years. She is a homemaker and a mother of two children. Her pain is widespread and often accompanied by stiffness and tenderness in muscles, joints, and soft tissues. She also frequently experiences headaches, sleep disturbances, and cognitive difficulties such as memory problems and concentration issues. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS), possibly triggered by a car accident a few years ago. She has tried various medications and non-pharmacological interventions, but none of them provided significant relief. She is not currently on any medications specific for FMS, including anti-depressants, gabapentinoids, tricyclics, opioids, and medical cannabis. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) as a potential treatment option for FMS. She has no history of major psychiatric disorders, systemic inflammatory disorders, active malignancy, or chronic ongoing infection. She has not undergone HBOT for any other reason prior to inclusion and is not currently suffering from chest pathology, inner ear disease, claustrophobia, or any neurological conditions that would exclude her from participation. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and undergo awake brain MRI testing.

A 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success visits the clinic. She has a history of one unsuccessful fresh embryo transfer and is now undergoing frozen embryo transfer cycles. She has no known medical conditions and has never been pregnant before. She is not a smoker and does not have polycystic ovarian syndrome. She has undergone endometrial preparation using hormonal replacement method and has achieved favorable thickness of endometrium. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of intrauterine injection of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) before frozen embryo transfer (ET) on cycle outcomes. She has given informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

This is a 25 year-old male who enjoys playing basketball regularly. He was playing a pickup game when he landed awkwardly on his right foot, resulting in an acute inversion ankle sprain. He experienced significant swelling, pain, and difficulty bearing weight on the affected ankle. He was evaluated by his primary care physician and diagnosed with a Grade II ankle sprain. The physician recommended rest, ice, compression, and elevation (PRICE) and prescribed nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief. The patient followed these recommendations for the first few days after the injury, but continued to experience significant pain and difficulty walking. He was referred to a physiotherapist who recommended functional treatment, including early mobilization and pain-depending weight bearing, and limited functional immobilization by an orthesis. The physiotherapist also recommended supervised physical therapy twice a week for 6 weeks. The patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial and was screened for eligibility. He met the inclusion criteria for the study and was randomized to the intervention group, which included functional treatment plus whole body vibration (WBV) exercises. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and hopes to return to his pre-injury level of activity as soon as possible.

A 38-year-old woman with a BMI of 36 kg/m² came to the bariatric surgery clinic to discuss her options for weight loss. She had tried multiple diets and exercise programs but has been unable to lose significant weight. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She works as a receptionist and spends most of her day sitting. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is interested in laparoscopic bariatric surgery and has been cleared for surgery by her primary care physician. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any underlying cardiopulmonary diseases.

55-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of stage IV adenocarcinoma of the lung with a metastatic lesion in the right femur. The patient has been receiving palliative radiation therapy for the femur lesion and is still recommended to receive 3 more rounds of radiation treatment. The patient is currently on concurrent therapy with anti-androgen hormonal therapy for prostate cancer. His ECOG performance status is 2. Past Medical History: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia, and Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with an FEV1 of 70% predicted. The patient is a former smoker with a 30-pack-year smoking history and quit smoking two years ago. No prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 30 days. The patient is able to understand and sign a written informed consent document.

54 year old female recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the bone. She reports experiencing significant pain in her lower back and hips, and has been experiencing increasing difficulty with mobility. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She is currently prescribed ibandronate tablets as part of her treatment plan. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials evaluating the efficacy or safety of ibandronate, and has not been found to have any contraindications to the medication. She is willing to participate in this observational survey to help assess the efficacy of ibandronate in breast cancer patients with metastatic bone disease.

32-year-old female with a history of migraines for the past 2 years. On average, she experiences 5 moderate to severe migraine attacks per month lasting between 8 to 24 hours. She has tried several preventive medications but without significant improvement. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing and able to complete the study questionnaire(s) and paper diary and agrees to limit her consumption of grapefruit juice to no more than one 8 ounce glass a day. She has not previously taken telcagepant.

A 54-year-old man presents with a severe headache that started abruptly while he was at work. He describes the headache as the worst headache of his life. He also reports nausea and vomiting. On examination, the patient is alert and oriented. His blood pressure is elevated at 160/95 mmHg. Neurological examination is significant for nuchal rigidity and photophobia. CT scan of the head shows blood in the subarachnoid space consistent with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. MRI with angiogram confirms the diagnosis of a ruptured saccular aneurysm. Hemoglobin level at presentation is 90 g/L. He is started on nimodipine, analgesics, and antihypertensives. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

A 52-year-old Chinese woman was diagnosed with primary hypercholesterolemia and has been taking a stable daily dose of 10 mg of rosuvastatin for 4 weeks prior to the screening visit, without any other lipid modifying therapy (LMT). Her LDL-C level at the screening visit was found to be >2.6 mmol/L (100 mg/dL) and ≤4.9 mmol/L (190 mg/dL), indicating inadequate control. She has no history of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or statin-induced myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. She has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, myocardial revascularization, transient ischemic attack, or stroke, carotid revascularization, endovascular procedure, or surgical intervention for peripheral vascular disease within the past 3 months. Her blood pressure is stable, with systolic blood pressure (SBP) is <160 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) <100 mm Hg at study entry. She has no history of severe congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association Class IIIb or IV) within the past 12 months, and no clinically significant uncontrolled endocrine disease known to influence serum lipids or lipoproteins, according to Investigator's medical judgment. She is not currently pregnant, has no history of cancer within the past 5 years, and is not dependent on the Sponsor or Investigator. She is capable of giving signed informed consent and is willing to use contraception consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and stable angina for the past 6 months. He has been taking medication for the treatment of CAD for the past 2 years and has been stable on these medications for at least 30 days prior to study start. He has a history of reproducibly positive exercise tests, having completed treadmill tests on 2 separate days within the past week. He is willing to refrain from drinking alcohol and smoking during the study procedures. He has no clinically significant abnormality on screening laboratory safety assessment. He is able to withhold medications that may result in hypoglycemia within 8 hours of dosing. He has no history of myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization within the past 2 months, and has no acute myocarditis or pericarditis. He is not obese, and does not have clinically significant hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia. He has no history of drug (including alcohol) abuse within the past 6 months. He has not taken any medications that may interfere with the study drug in the time frame specified. He is willing to comply with the pre- and post-dosing fasting requirements of the study. He has no history of multiple and/or severe allergies, or anaphylactic reaction or intolerability to prescription or non-prescription drugs or food. Overall, he meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

As this clinical trial is focused on adult male circumcision, the patient description would be as follows:  The patient is a 30-year-old male who has decided to undergo voluntary medical circumcision. He is in good health with no known medical conditions and has no allergies to lidocaine or bupivacaine. He is sexually active and has no history of sexually transmitted infections or genital ulcers. He has been counseled on HIV prevention and has undergone HIV testing. He has received group counseling on the procedure and the potential risks and benefits. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial and will be randomly assigned to receive either the 4-4-2 mix or the 3-3-4 mix of lignocaine and bupivacaine. He will be monitored for pain and adverse events during and after the procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU after experiencing severe chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with a pulmonary embolism (PE) and is at high risk for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) due to his immobility and critical illness. He has no history of bleeding disorders or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). He weighs 85 kg and is expected to have an ICU stay of more than 72 hours. He is currently on mechanical ventilation and requires vasoactive drug infusion to maintain his blood pressure. The patient has no history of prior DVT or PE. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient is eligible for the study and will be randomized to receive either low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) or unfractionated heparin (UFH) for thromboprophylaxis during his ICU stay. He will undergo regular leg ultrasounds and diagnostic algorithms for PE throughout his stay. The patient's progress will be closely monitored and any adverse events or complications will be recorded. The results of this study will help determine the most effective and safe thromboprophylaxis method for critically ill patients like him.

The patient is a 60-year-old Caucasian male who has a history of chronic sun exposure due to his occupation as a construction worker. He has noticed a persistent dryness and scaling of his lower lip, which has been gradually worsening over the past few months. The physical examination shows a thickened and roughened lower lip with some discoloration and mild tenderness. A biopsy of the affected area confirmed the diagnosis of actinic cheilitis. The patient has no prior history of skin cancer or any significant medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and understands and signs the informed consent. The patient is able to comply with the attendance at the clinical settings during the days of medication and follow-up visits.

A 62 year old man with a diagnosis of prostate cancer and scheduled for robotic prostatectomy. He has no significant past medical history and takes only a daily multivitamin. His PSA level is 5.6 ng/mL, with a biopsy showing Gleason score 7 (3+4) adenocarcinoma involving 50% of the biopsy cores. He has no evidence of metastatic disease on imaging studies. He is married, retired, and lives an active lifestyle, including golfing and hiking.

A 30-year-old female who has a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis with ragweed pollen for the past two years. She experiences nasal congestion, sneezing, itching, and watery discharge in her eyes and nose during the ragweed season. She has undergone a positive skin prick test to ragweed allergen at Visit 1. She is in good health and is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant. She is willing to attend all study visits and follow the instructions given by the investigator. She has no history of asthma, smoking, lower or upper airway infection, nasal anatomical deformities, and hypersensitivity to any of the investigational products' ingredients. She is not currently participating in any clinical trial and has not been exposed to any investigational treatment within the last 30 days. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse or any acute or chronic disease that would affect the study objectives or subject safety. She is capable of understanding the study procedures and providing written informed consent.

The patient is a 54-year-old man diagnosed with hepatitis B virus (HBV) related cirrhosis with concomitant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past year. He has been on antiviral treatment for HBV for the past 6 months, and his liver function tests have been stable. He recently underwent upper endoscopy, which showed F2 esophageal varices without any evidence of bleeding. He has no significant comorbidities, and his physical examination is unremarkable except for stigmata of chronic liver disease. His AFP level is 200 ng/mL, and liver biopsy confirms the diagnosis of HCC. He has no history of esophageal variceal bleeding, and he has not received any previous treatment for varices. His ECG is normal, and his pulmonary function tests are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study. He is compliant with follow-up visits and medications.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse and liver cirrhosis diagnosed by a gastroenterologist. He has a history of decompensation, including hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, and variceal bleeding. He presents with moderate ascites and complains of decreased urine output and fatigue for the past week. He has no history of renal disease or transplantation. His medications include lactulose, spironolactone, and furosemide. His vital signs are stable, and his physical examination is significant for abdominal distension and tenderness. His labs show a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL and a blood urea nitrogen of 25 mg/dL. His baseline serum creatinine level is not available. His cardiac assessment is normal. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of back pain and stiffness for the past year. He is a construction worker and reports lifting heavy objects regularly. He also reports occasional numbness and tingling in his legs. He denies any history of urinary tract infections or problems with urinary incontinence. He is able to provide informed consent for their data to be included in the study. He has not had any spinal surgery or pre-existing neurological conditions affecting the central, peripheral, or autonomic nervous system. He does not have a urinary catheter for any reason and he is not a prisoner. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. He is willing to undergo digital rectal examination and ultrasound bladder scanning.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders version IV criteria. She has no history of dermatological lesions, asthma, or allergic disease, nor does she have diabetes, chronic hypertension, vasculitis, or substance use disorders except for occasional cigarette smoking. She is not pregnant and is not currently taking any oral medication that could affect the metabolism of prostaglandins such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or corticosteroids. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the niacin skin test accuracy in schizophrenia patients and hopes that her participation will contribute to the understanding of this condition.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was brought to the emergency department by his family members. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He complains of sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body, slurred speech and facial drooping. His symptoms started about 3 hours ago. He states that he has never experienced these symptoms before. His blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg, his heart rate is 70 beats per minute and his respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. His blood glucose level is 120 mg/dL. He is not taking any anticoagulant medication. He has no history of any major surgery or severe trauma in the past 3 months. He is able to give his consent for participation in the study.

56-year-old female with a history of heart failure, presenting with complaints of leg weakness, making it difficult for her to exercise. She reports feeling very tired and fatigued after walking only a short distance. She has been on several heart failure medications, including diuretics and ACE inhibitors, but has not seen much improvement in her leg strength. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking Coumadin. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the medication clonidine can improve her leg weakness and allow her to exercise more comfortably. She is willing to wear the clonidine patch and attend study visits over the course of three months. She has no significant kidney or liver disease and is medically able to receive clonidine.

50 year-old male with a history of bladder cancer, previously treated with a platinum-based regimen, now with metastatic disease to the lungs, liver and bone. The patient has a performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. Imaging studies show measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 criteria. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, clinically significant cardiovascular disease or gastrointestinal disease. The patient has not received systemic cancer therapy or investigational therapy within 3 weeks of first study drug administration and has not undergone radiation or major surgery within 4 weeks of first study drug administration. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has already undergone one round of chemotherapy but has relapsed. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. Upon examination, the patient has signs of bone marrow failure including anemia, granulocytopenia, and thrombocytopenia. The patient's leukemic cell count is 25%, and his white blood cell count is 15,000/mm3. He has no history of symptomatic coronary atherosclerotic heart disease, and his liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study. The patient does not have any active infections and is afebrile. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of arsenic trioxide in treating his relapsed AML.

A 24-year-old male with complete paralysis of all four limbs due to a spinal cord injury is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new tool called the brain computer interface (BCI). He is able to communicate through eye movements and has no difficulty reading text on a computer screen. He is able to understand and follow instructions and is excited about the possibility of controlling technology through his brain signals. He has no history of seizures or open head lesions. He is not currently taking any medications, and he does not have any allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and help researchers improve the BCI technology for people who are paralyzed.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital for sepsis due to a severe urinary tract infection. He has been experiencing fever, chills, and lower abdominal pain for the past week. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. His renal function has been normal in the past, with no history of kidney disease. He is not a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. On admission, his blood pressure was elevated at 160/90 mmHg, but has since been controlled with medication. He has been started on antibiotics for his infection and is being closely monitored in the intensive care unit. Blood and urine samples have been collected for analysis of NGAL, inflammatory markers, and other novel biomarkers that may be involved in renal function recovery. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with HIV for 2 years. He has been on Zidovudine (ZDV) treatment for the past 6 months and has not experienced any side effects. His viral load at the time of diagnosis was 50,000 copies/ml, and his CD4 cell count was 250 cells/mm3. He has not taken any other anti-HIV drugs except for ZDV. He is currently working as an office clerk and has a good support system. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the best dosing schedule for Delavirdine (DLV), ZDV, and Indinavir (IDV) in HIV-positive patients. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 65 year old man who underwent a total knee replacement surgery and required a urinary catheter during his hospital stay. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. He has no known allergies to medications or medical devices. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the UroShield device to prevent urinary tract infections associated with catheter usage.

56-year-old male with a history of smoking, diagnosed with stage II lung cancer. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. The patient has a history of COPD and has undergone pulmonary function tests, which showed a decrease in lung function. The patient is a candidate for surgical treatment, but due to COPD, the patient is at high risk for postoperative complications. The patient has agreed to participate in a randomized trial to assess the effect of comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation on functional and surgical outcomes, functioning, and Quality of Life (QoL). The patient will be evaluated and randomized by the physician data manager and will be assigned to either the Intervention Group (IG) or Control Group (CG). The IG will receive an overall rehabilitation treatment based on 10 sessions of pre-operative outpatient PR, early inpatient post-operative PR, and long-term exercise beginning 1 month after surgery and lasting for 15 sessions. The CG will receive Standard Care (SC) based upon physiatrist counseling the day before surgery and early inpatient post-operative PR. The patient will be followed up for 6 months after surgery, and the primary outcome of this study will be the 6 minutes walk test (6MWT). The investigators expect that the comprehensive rehabilitation intervention in lung cancer patients eligible for surgical treatment may reduce pain, comorbidity, depression, and deconditioning and improve QoL.

This is a 42 year old male with a family history of HD. He has been experiencing difficulties with fine motor skills and mild cognitive impairment. Genetic testing confirmed that he has the CAG expansion > 35 repeats and is in the pre-symptomatic stage of HD. He has no other significant medical history and has not participated in any clinical pharmacological trials. He is able to undergo and tolerate MRI scans. He is interested in participating in this study to help researchers better understand the progression of HD and potentially provide insight into biomarkers for early detection and treatment.

Patient is a 25-year-old African American woman who has been smoking cigarettes for the past three years. She typically smokes 10-15 cigarettes per day and has noticed that she experiences strong cravings for cigarettes throughout the day. She has difficulty falling asleep at night and often wakes up feeling tired and groggy. She has a family history of smoking-related illnesses and is concerned about the long-term health effects of smoking. She is currently not using any tobacco products other than cigarettes and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use contraception during the study and is able to read and speak English fluently. She does not have any cognitive impairment or untreated mental illness that would interfere with informed consent. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the relationship between her smoking behavior, sleep patterns, and addiction.

A 27-year-old Japanese male, born and raised in Japan, with both parents of Japanese descent, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has not resided outside of Japan for more than 5 years and maintains a Japanese lifestyle, including diet. He must be non-fertile, either surgically sterilized or practicing an effective contraceptive method. He has no history of cancer and his serum testosterone levels are within range at screening.

This is a 6-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD). His diagnosis was confirmed by genetic testing, MRI imaging, and elevated levels of very long chain fatty acids (VLCFA) and adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). He is currently experiencing symptoms of the disease

As a clinical trial specialist, it is important to note that this study does not involve direct patient participation. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this clinical trial. Instead, this study is focused on developing and evaluating intervention techniques against HIV transmission during the recent infection period using a combination of injection-, sexual- and social-network-based contact tracing methods. The study aims to locate "seeds," defined as drug users and other people who have recently been infected, and target members of their networks and people who attend their venues. This study is exploratory in nature and will involve screening and testing individuals for HIV antibodies, LAg, and HIV RNA, as well as follow-up interviews and testing to assess the effectiveness of the interventions.

A 32-year-old male construction worker was involved in a motor vehicle accident while driving to work. He sustained multiple fractures and lacerations and was admitted to the trauma surgery service at Froedtert Hospital. He is generally healthy, a non-smoker, and does not have any significant medical history. He is married and has two children. He speaks fluent English and is able to identify a support person who can attend a session with him. He does not have any evidence of moderate to severe cognitive impairment and meets the DSM-5 definition of a traumatic stressor for PTSD. He scores a 4 on the 5-item PTSD subscale of the 9-item screen. He is eligible for the RAC Pilot clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male patient with an unruptured aneurysm in the middle cerebral artery has been referred to participate in this clinical trial. He has no history of cerebrovascular, psychiatric, or neurological disease. He speaks Norwegian fluently and has no alcohol or substance abuse history. He has no vision or hearing deficits and is not suffering from aphasia. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and has never had any major surgery. He is interested in participating in this study to help researchers better understand the relationship between memory function and brain activity among SAH patients.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male volunteers aged 18-56 years with a BMI between 18.0 and 32.0 kg/m2 and weighing at least 50 kg to participate in a study to identify and quantitate metabolites of asimadoline. Participants must be in good general health with no clinically relevant abnormalities, and willing to comply with study procedures and restrictions. Exclusion criteria include any disease or condition that might affect drug absorption or metabolism, known hypersensitivity or allergic reaction to asimadoline, chronic use of systemic medications, current or recent history of drug or alcohol abuse, and positive screens for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV. Participants must also be willing to use an approved method of contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 25 year old woman from Nairobi, Kenya. She is married and has one child. She works as a sales assistant in a local store and has completed high school education. She is generally in good health and does not have any chronic medical conditions. She reports having a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently menstruating. She has had sexual intercourse with her husband as her only sexual partner. She has not been diagnosed with HIV or any other sexually transmitted infection. Recently, she has started experiencing symptoms of bacterial vaginosis, such as a fishy odor, discomfort during sex, and increased vaginal discharge. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the required protocol. She is willing to take oral metronidazole twice a day for seven days and abstain from alcohol during and for 48 hours after treatment. She is willing to answer short questionnaires on her economic status and sexual risk behavior.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with primary biliary cholangitis at West China Hospital. She experienced fatigue, itching, and jaundice for the past few months. She has a medical history of osteoporosis and hypertension. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not been diagnosed with any other autoimmune diseases. She is currently taking ursodeoxycholic acid as prescribed by her doctor.

This study is seeking individuals of any age who have abnormal immune function characterized by recurrent or unusual fungal infections, recurrent or chronic inflammation, or other types of immune dysfunction. The study is also looking for first- or second-degree genetically related family members (such as parents, siblings, children, and first cousins) of individuals with immune disorders. Healthy volunteers who are at least 18 years of age and have no history of immune disorders are also eligible to participate for comparison purposes. Patients with primary immune deficiencies and other conditions associated with fungal infections, specifically Candida spp. infections, will undergo evaluations that include history/physical, blood sampling, genetic testing, and possible tissue sampling. Relatives might also be screened for clinical, in vitro, and genetic correlates of immune abnormalities. Healthy volunteers will be enrolled as a source of control samples for research testing. Among the aims of this protocol are to better understand the genetic and pathophysiologic factors that lead to defects in host defense and to use modern and evolving methods in molecular and cellular biology to elucidate the pathogenesis of this particular susceptibility. Participants will provide blood samples and buccal (cells from the inside of the mouth near the cheek) samples, and participants with immune disorders will also be asked to provide urine samples, saliva or mucosal samples, or skin tissue biopsies, and may also have imaging studies (such as x-rays) to collect information for research. No treatment will be provided as part of this protocol.

A 56-year-old Hispanic male patient presented to the hospital with a history of dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The physical examination revealed jugular venous distension, bilateral pedal edema, and bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. His laboratory study showed elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 20%. Despite optimal medical management, the patient's symptoms persisted, and he was classified as NYHA Class IV heart failure. The patient was informed about the EVAHEART®2 Left Ventricular Assist System clinical trial and was found to be eligible for the study. He agreed to participate in the study and provided written informed consent.

A 7-year-old male with a history of hereditary severe FX deficiency, based on his lowest reliable FX:C recorded. He underwent a genetic testing which confirmed a mutation in the F10 gene causing a documented severe bleeding phenotype. The child's parent/guardian provided informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of FACTOR X in the prevention of bleeding when given as routine prophylaxis over 12 months. The child has no clinically significant liver disease, renal disease, or other coagulopathy or thrombophilia, and has no history or suspicion of inhibitors to factor X. The child is not known to have hypersensitivity to the investigational medicinal product or its excipients. The child has no history of unreliability or non-cooperation and is not planning to be absent from the locality of the investigational site for more than 4 weeks between the Screening Visit and the End of Study Visit at approximately 6 months post-Baseline.

Patient is a 15-year-old girl with a history of depression and anxiety. She has been experiencing symptoms such as feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and low self-esteem. The patient has been recommended for cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) by her healthcare provider. She is an English-speaking resident and lives with her legal guardian. The patient has not previously received mental health services and does not have any conditions that would impair her ability to engage in the Bridging the Gap program. The patient is not currently experiencing a manic or psychotic episode and does not have a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder. The patient does not have issues with substance abuse and is not currently involved with child welfare.

A 56-year-old male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with persistent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the pancreas, and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. The tumor is deemed unresectable and locally advanced. The patient has not received any prior treatment for pancreatic adenocarcinoma and has not undergone radiotherapy in the abdominal area. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an expected survival time of greater than 12 weeks. Laboratory blood tests indicate adequate organ performance. The patient has no history of heart failure or significant cardiac arrhythmias. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have limited legal capacity.

A 22-year-old sexually active woman with a history of consistent and correct condom use for the past year. She has no known drug allergies and is in good general health. She is currently not pregnant and not breastfeeding. She has tested negative for HIV within the past month and has no history of sexually transmitted infections. She is willing to participate and sign an informed consent form, undergo pelvic examinations with colposcopy according to the protocol throughout the study, and abstain from using any vaginal product other than the study product. She is willing to be sexually abstinent from Day 1 until completion of study product use on Day 10. She has no clinically detectable abnormalities on her vulva, vaginal walls or cervix. She is not currently experiencing any symptoms of bacterial vaginosis or vaginal candidiasis.

This clinical trial is not seeking new participants but will continue with two specific individuals who have already been enrolled in the study. Therefore, there is no need for a patient description for this trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing tremors and stiffness in his hands and legs for the past year. He is currently at stage 2 of the Modified Hoehn & Yahr (H&Y) scale, and has a MoCA score of 24. He is otherwise healthy and has no other neurological or orthopedic problems. He enjoys walking for exercise but has noticed that his gait has become slower and more unsteady. He also experiences difficulty with tasks that require fine motor skills, such as buttoning his shirt or using utensils to eat. The patient is able to communicate clearly and effectively, with no speech and visual problems. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his understanding of how dual task affects his upper and lower extremity skills, and to help with the development of treatments for Parkinson's disease.

A 20 year old gay man named Evan, who lives in the Chicago metro area and owns a smartphone with an unlimited text messaging plan, is interested in participating in the clinical trial. Evan has never received the HPV vaccine before and is concerned about his risk of contracting HPV due to his sexual practices. He has had multiple sexual partners in the past and understands the importance of protecting himself against sexually transmitted infections. Evan is fluent in English and has been using text messaging for over 2 years. He is committed to keeping the same cell phone number for the next 9 months and is willing to participate in the study to increase his chances of receiving the HPV vaccine.

The patient is a 2-month-old male infant who was diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) through post-natal blood testing. He was born full term with a birth weight of 3.2 kg (50th percentile). The family has no history of thrombosis, and the patient has not been exposed to androgen therapy. The infant is not taking any medications that affect body composition. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of testosterone on their child's health and development.

The patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her third trimester. She has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during a routine screening at 28 weeks of pregnancy. She is a first-time mother and has no significant medical history. Her pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) was 28, indicating overweight. She has been managing her GDM with diet and exercise under the supervision of her obstetrician. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of being screened for GDM between 24-32 weeks of pregnancy and being a singleton pregnancy. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has no history of metabolic disorders, fertility drug therapy, night shift work, or working in air crew, therefore she meets the exclusion criteria. The study will assess the impact of "Chrono Nutrition" (CN) factors on maternal and fetal outcomes in GDM pregnancies. The patient will be randomly assigned to the intervention or control group to evaluate the effect of CN intervention on birth weight in participants with GDM pregnancies. The expected results of this study will provide valuable insights into the impact of CB factors on GDM pregnancies and the feasibility of high interference CN factors in pregnancy.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been experiencing pain in his lower leg for the past six months. He has a history of peripheral arterial disease and underwent stenting of the femoropopliteal artery in his right leg two years ago. However, he has been experiencing symptoms of restenosis, including rest limb pain, and has developed a non-healing ulceration on his foot. His Rutherford classification is 4 and his target lesion has been viewed angiographically with ≥50% stenosis. He is being considered for treatment with the JetStream Navitus device for simultaneous tissue excision and aspiration of the restenotic lesion. He meets all inclusion criteria for the study, including having a main target vessel reference diameter of at least 5 mm and one patent distal run-off vessel with brisk flow. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with follow-up evaluations.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has just given birth to a baby boy at 35 weeks and 4 days of gestation. The baby was born via vaginal delivery and weighed 2.2 kg at birth. The baby has been admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to being born late preterm. The baby is otherwise healthy and has no known genetic or metabolic diseases. The baby does not have any abnormalities of the digestive system or severe congenital heart disease. The baby's parents have provided written informed consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial investigating systemic nutritional management for late preterm infants in China. The baby will be randomly assigned to either the group applicating the systemic nutritional management of late preterm infants or the group not applicating the systemic nutritional management of late preterm infants. The baby's growth and nutritional status will be monitored throughout the study, and any short-term or long-term complications will be documented.

The patient is a 2-year-old girl who was born weighing 4 kg. Her parents have a history of obesity and she has gained weight rapidly in her first year of life, crossing multiple percentile lines for weight for age. Currently, she is in the 90th percentile for weight and 75th percentile for height. Her parents are concerned about her weight and are interested in learning more about healthy nutrition, activity and sleep. They are fluent in English and reside within the Toronto Public Health catchment area for home visiting. The child does not have any developmental delays or known genetic disorders. The family is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a fractured left arm and multiple contusions. He reports a pain level of 7 out of 10 on the visual numerical scale. The patient has no known allergies and currently takes no medications. He denies any history of renal or hepatic disorders. He is conscious and alert with a Glasgow score of 15. The patient has not received any intravenous analgesia yet. He is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 50-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with malignant glioma. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no other significant medical history. His Karnofsky performance status is 80, and he has undergone standard therapy for his cancer, but it has now recurred. He has not had recent cranial surgery. His HLA-A *02 or HLA-A *03 blood cell haplotype has been documented by PCR analysis or flow cytometry. Survivin expression on his tumor cells has been documented by immunohistochemistry. He is free of systemic infection and has a white blood count of 4,500/mm^3, platelets of 150,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin of 12.0 g/dL. His AST/ALT is within normal limits, as is his total bilirubin and serum creatinine. He is not on corticosteroid therapy. He understands the investigational nature of the study and is willing to sign an Institutional Review Board approved written informed consent form. He is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use acceptable contraceptive methods during treatment and for three months after its completion. He has not undergone any experimental drug therapy within the past 30 days or standard of care drug therapy within 28 days prior to randomization. He has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH), GM-CSF or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agent. He has a life expectancy of more than 4 months and is willing and able to follow protocol requirements.
