The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He will undergo curative primary radiotherapy treatment with a total dose of 70 Gy delivered in 35 fractions. The patient has no significant medical history and is in good general health. He has no contraindications for radiotherapy treatment. The patient has been informed about the standard follow-up program and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is willing and able to comply with the follow-up visits and testing schedule.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been suffering from moderate to severe atopic dermatitis for the past 5 years. She has been using various topical creams and ointments, but they have not provided satisfactory relief from her symptoms. She has no history of allergies and is not currently on any medications. She works as a teacher and has no plans for pregnancy. She has a history of excessive alcohol intake, but she has reduced her intake in the past year. Her skin is dry and scaly, with intense itching and redness in the affected areas. Her EASI score is 8.5 and SCORAD score is 29. She has not received any recent UV therapy or immunobiological treatment for her condition. Her blood tests show no signs of hepatic or renal insufficiency, anemia, thrombocytopenia, or leukopenia. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled visits.

45-year-old African American woman diagnosed with infiltrating carcinoma of the breast on diagnostic biopsy. The tumor is ER-negative, PR status undetermined, and HER2-negative. The patient is scheduled for a mastectomy and has agreed to participate in the study. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. The patient is willing and able to sign an informed consent form.

A 44-year old woman was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer after experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Unfortunately, the cancer has progressed and has spread to her liver, lungs, and bones. She is experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath. She has no significant past medical history and doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is willing to provide fresh tissue for biomarker analysis and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive molecular profile directed treatments. She hopes that this trial will provide new treatment options that will improve her quality of life and extend her life expectancy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing migraines for over 10 years. She has been diagnosed with chronic migraine by a neurologist and meets the diagnostic criteria listed in the International Classification of Headache Disorders. Despite trying multiple preventive medications, she has not found relief and continues to experience migraines on most days of the month. She has not received onabotulinum toxin A for migraine or any other medical or cosmetic reasons requiring injections in the head, face, or neck during the 6 months prior to study entry. She does not use medications containing opioids or barbiturates on more than 4 days per month for the treatment of migraine or for any other reason. She is willing to comply with the electronic headache diary during the run-in period and commit to monthly subcutaneous administration of the investigational drug or placebo. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and weighs 65 kg. She has not been treated with an investigational drug or device within 30 days of study entry, nor has she been exposed to a monoclonal antibody targeting the CGRP pathway.

A 32-year-old male patient was brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. He was the driver of the car and was not wearing a seatbelt. Upon arrival, he was unconscious and had a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 7. His vital signs were unstable with a heart rate of 130 beats/minute, blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg, respiratory rate of 28 breaths/minute, and oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. The patient had sustained multiple injuries including a head injury, multiple rib fractures, a left femur fracture, and a right humerus fracture. The initial laboratory workup showed elevated serum creatinine levels of 1.8 mg/dL and a urine output of 20 mL/hour. The patient was admitted to the resuscitation bay of Edouard Herriot Hospital where he will be monitored for the next 24 hours for the risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) using the Nephrocheck® test. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and will be considered for participation if he is not anuric and does not oppose to participate.

55 year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with a recent diagnosis of mild renal impairment (CLCR 72 mL/min). He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia, respectively. He has no history of bleeding disorders, recent surgeries or hospitalizations. He has never taken rivaroxaban or erythromycin before. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 80 kg. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed an IRB approved informed consent form. He has no history of significant medical illness or other conditions that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's Disease for the past 7 years. Despite taking medications for the past 5 years, she is still experiencing motor complications such as tremors, stiffness, and difficulty with movement. She has had stable doses of antiparkinsonian medications and parkinsonian features for the past 60 days. She is currently taking levodopa, carbidopa, and entacapone. She has not had any intracranial surgery or implantation of a device for the treatment of Parkinson's Disease. She has not received chemotherapy, cytotoxic therapy, or immunotherapy within the past 6 weeks and has not received any vaccinations within the past 30 days. She has not been treated with neuroleptics within the past year and does not have any medical disabilities that would interfere with the assessment of efficacy and safety in this trial. She is willing to undergo the surgical procedure and sign informed consent.

A 52 year old male with a documented diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma with AFP serum test levels of 60 IU/ml. The patient has no prior history of immunomodulatory therapies or participation in experimental research treatment studies. The patient has not taken any locally available immune modulators, and has no evidence of active or acute cardiac disease, epilepsy, or life-threatening diseases unrelated to HCC. The patient is willing and capable of providing informed consent and has readily available contact information. The patient has no medical conditions such as active alcohol or substance abuse, or psychological issues that would interfere with adherence to the requirements of this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with keratoconus, a progressive eye disease that causes the cornea to become thin and bulge outwards into a cone-like shape. Despite using glasses and contact lenses, she is experiencing increasing difficulty with reading and driving due to blurriness and distortion in her vision. She has never had any previous corneal surgeries nor has she had any significant ocular or systemic medical conditions. She is willing and able to comply with the required follow-up visits and has signed the informed consent form. She is not pregnant nor nursing at present and has no plans to become pregnant during her participation in this investigation.

This is a 62 year-old female who presented with sudden vision loss in her right eye. She was diagnosed with Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy and started on standard medical treatment within the past month. She has no history of hemorrhagic disease, thrombophlebitis, or infection lesions. She has controlled hypertension and is not classified as a severe hypertensive patient. She does not have atrial fibrillation or aortic regurgitation. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and potentially receiving EECP therapy in addition to standard medical treatment.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. She has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy for metastatic disease. The patient reports some shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. She also reports fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work such as office work or light housework. The patient has measurable disease, with a lesion measuring 25 mm in the right lung. Her laboratory studies show normal levels of leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, and platelets, as well as normal total bilirubin and creatinine clearance. The patient has no history of allergic reactions to paclitaxel and has not received prior therapy with paclitaxel. The patient is able to take oral medications and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use appropriate double barrier birth control methods during the study. The patient is HIV-negative.

A 46-year-old woman with uterine fibroids has been advised by her gynecologist to undergo a total laparoscopic hysterectomy. She has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding for the past few months and has become anemic as a result. She has no history of any other major medical conditions and has never undergone any surgeries before. She is not allergic to any medications and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a supportive family and has taken a week off from work to recover from the surgery. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and hopes that her participation will help other women in the future who may undergo similar surgeries.

This is a 6 month-old female infant who is scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia for an inguinal hernia repair. She has no significant past medical history and has been growing and developing appropriately. She was born at full term and has been meeting all developmental milestones. The surgery is expected to take approximately 45 minutes and she will require orotracheal intubation by direct laryngoscopy. She has no known risk factors for difficult airway management and has not had any previous surgeries.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) that has progressed despite treatment with multiple lines of therapy, including chemotherapy and immunotherapy. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to any medications. His most recent CBC shows a white blood cell count of 50,000/mm3 and hemoglobin of 10 g/dL. His performance status is 1, and he is able to perform most normal daily activities without assistance. He has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of participating in this expanded access program for venetoclax and has provided informed consent. He is not eligible for any other venetoclax clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is generally healthy and does not have a history of cancer. She is a non-smoker and has not smoked for over a year. She does not consume large amounts of alcohol and drinks less than 3 alcoholic drinks per week. She occasionally drinks tea, but consumes less than 6 cups or glasses per week. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She has no difficulty swallowing capsules or tablets. She does not have any metabolic disorders that would affect the study drug. She does not have any serious acute or chronic diseases or active infections. She has no known hypersensitivity to green tea or probe drugs. She has not been diagnosed with invasive cancer within the past 5 years. She has not participated in another clinical intervention study within the past 3 months. She is willing to refrain from consuming tea and related products, as well as oral herbal/botanical supplements during the study. She is also willing to limit the consumption of cruciferous vegetables to ≤ once a week during the study. Finally, she is willing to refrain from consuming caffeine-containing food or beverages for 72 hours before, during, and for 8 hours after study drug administration, and to avoid food items that affect drug or carcinogen metabolizing enzymes for 72 hours before, during, and for 8 hours after study drug administration.

A 27-year-old male patient visited the emergency department with severe pain and limited range of motion in his left shoulder after a fall while playing football. Examination revealed anterior shoulder dislocation without any associated fractures or neurological or vascular injuries. He has no history of shoulder surgery or previous reduction attempts for the current dislocation. He is otherwise healthy and able to understand the nature of the study and give written informed consent. He is willing to follow all study requirements and procedures and complete all questionnaires. He has no known allergies to medications and has not received methoxyflurane within the past 3 months.

A 27-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia and nicotine dependence comes to the clinic for a research study. He has been stable on his current medication for the past 3 months and has been smoking at least 15 cigarettes per day with an expired breath CO level of >10 ppm. He has been diagnosed with cognitive deficits in prefrontal cortex-related tasks including VSWM, CPT, and WCST. His IQ score is above 80. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse or dependence within the past 3 months. He is able to give informed consent for participation. The patient is not pregnant nor planning on becoming

A 42-year-old male presents with a diagnosis of unresectable malignant melanoma stage IV. He has no significant medical history except for a previous diagnosis of hypertension for which he is taking lisinopril 10mg daily. A recent PET/CT scan demonstrated at least one measurable lesion. The patient is planned to undergo systemic therapy with BRAF/MEK inhibitors. He is currently asymptomatic with no evidence of metastasis to other organs. He is an active smoker, smoking about a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 15 years. His BMI is 27, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He has no contraindications for MR-imaging or gadolinium-based contrast agents. The patient is aware of the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who presents with a persistent cough and chest pain for the past few months. He has a long history of heavy smoking, with a 45 pack-year history. He reports a recent unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds over the past two months. A chest x-ray reveals a suspicious mass in the right lung, and a CT scan confirms a 3 cm mass in the right upper lobe with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is referred for further evaluation with an endobronchial ultrasound procedure to obtain a definitive diagnosis and determine the extent of the disease for accurate staging. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial to help researchers gather data and improve the diagnostic and staging process for lung cancer.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather healthy volunteers who are 18 years or older and able to provide informed consent. They must be able to be positioned properly in the investigational device and be still during the exam to reduce the potential of motion in the images. Subjects who have a metal screw, plate, or artificial joint are eligible to participate. However, pregnant individuals and those with a history of high radiation exposure or who have undergone radiation therapy are excluded from the study.

As this is a study on mental health in professional dancers and their knowledge on recovery strategies and nutritional needs, there is no specific patient description required. Participants would include professional dancers and their teachers at the Norwegian University of Dance, as well as art students at the Oslo National Academy of the Arts who will serve as a control group.

63 yo M with a history of stable angina pectoris, referred for elective coronary angiography. The patient reports a 2-year history of exertional chest pain, relieved by rest and nitroglycerin. The patient's past medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a 20-pack year smoking history. The patient has no known drug allergies. The patient is currently taking amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin. The patient has no prior history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, or arrhythmia. The patient's physical examination is unremarkable, with a normal heart rate and blood pressure. The patient's oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, with evidence of moderate coronary artery stenosis on angiography requiring further routine assessment with Fractional Flow Reserve (FFR). The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 28-year-old male with a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis to short ragweed pollen for the past 2 years is experiencing symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and nasal congestion. He reports that his symptoms are affecting his daily activities and sleep. He has tried over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal sprays, but the symptoms persist. He denies any history of asthma or respiratory infections in the past month. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has never been exposed to systemic corticosteroids for any indication. He is generally in good health and is willing to participate in the study. He has no known hypersensitivity to corticosteroids. His physical examination reveals no nasal deformities or obstructions. He is able to provide written informed consent.

A 60-year-old male presents with abdominal discomfort and hematuria. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication. A CT scan reveals a mass in the left kidney, and a biopsy confirms the presence of renal cell carcinoma. The patient has no history of cancer or other major medical conditions. He is scheduled for an elective nephrectomy and is interested in participating in the study investigating the effect of anesthesia on cancer recurrence and survival.

The patient is a 26-year-old healthy male with no current medication use and no history of allergies to paracetamol or lamotrigine. He is interested in participating in a clinical study investigating the interaction between paracetamol and lamotrigine. The patient is fully informed about the study and willing to provide informed consent.

This is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with osteomyelitis, which is a bone infection. She has been experiencing pain and tenderness upon palpation or probing to bone, and her recent radiograph and MRI results were consistent with osteomyelitis. She has also had elevated levels of C-reactive protein, indicating inflammation in her body. She has not received more than 24 hours of potentially effective IV antibacterial therapy for her osteomyelitis within the past 96 hours. She has no prior history of osteomyelitis or failed course of therapy for osteomyelitis. She has no infection associated with a burn wound, with a sacral decubitus ulcer, or with multiple sites of osteomyelitis. She has no Gram-negative bacteria by Gram stain in the absence of Gram-positive organisms. She has no Gram-negative bacteremia. She has no concomitant endocarditis, necrotizing fasciitis, or prosthetic material at the site of infection at the time of study initiation. She is not infected with an organism known prior to study entry to not be susceptible to dalbavancin (dalbavancin mean inhibitory concentration [MIC] > 0.12 μg/mL) or vancomycin (vancomycin MIC > 2 μg/mL). She is not taking any concomitant systemic antibacterial therapy for Gram-positive infections (eg, rifampin, gentamicin). She is not known to have any hypersensitivity to glycopeptide antibiotics. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is not a sexually active female of childbearing potential who is unwilling or unable to use an acceptable method of contraception from at least the first dose of study drug until the last pregnancy test.

The patient is a 10-month-old infant residing in Western Pennsylvania, who has received at least two doses of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine and Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccine. The infant has been diagnosed with acute otitis media (AOM) within the past 48 hours, with at least two of the following symptoms: decreased or absent tympanic membrane mobility by pneumatic otoscopy, yellow or white discoloration of the tympanic membrane, opacification of the tympanic membrane, and 1+ or 2+ bulging of the tympanic membrane with either marked erythema or otalgia. The infant has an AOM-SOS score of greater than or equal to 3. The infant has not experienced toxic appearance, otalgia for a period greater than 48 hours, spontaneous perforation of the tympanic membrane or drainage, and temperature greater than or equal to 105 degrees F. The infant does not have tympanostomy tubes in place or a history of tympanostomy tubes, unrepaired or repaired overt or submucous cleft palate, high-arched palate, Down's syndrome, serious underlying disease, renal or hepatic insufficiency, immune dysfunction or deficiency, or chronic gastrointestinal conditions. The infant has not received systemic corticosteroids or more than one dose of

Pt is a 40yo M with a 7-year history of rheumatoid arthritis. Despite being on DMARD therapy for 3 months, he has been experiencing moderate to severe fatigue and anemia. His DAS28 score is 4.0, indicating active disease. He has not had any previous treatment with an anti-TNF agent or cell-depleting therapies. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 31-year-old female employee of the National Institutes of Health with no known history of skin conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of digital photography in diagnosing psoriasis, hand rashes, and unusual moles. She has never had a skin cancer screening before but is willing to participate in this portion of the study. The patient is able to stand for the lower extremity and back photograph but may need assistance due to a previous ankle injury. She is willing to complete the questionnaire and follow all study procedures. The patient understands the importance of this research in monitoring disease in the US population and is excited to contribute to this effort.

An 80-year-old woman comes to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial for an influenza vaccine. She has no significant medical history and has never received any vaccination in the past six months. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the procedure of the trial. Her physical examination is normal, and she has no fever. She is not taking any medications that affect the immune system, and she has not received any blood products or immunoglobulin products in the last six months. She has no history of anaphylaxis or allergic reactions to vaccines or drugs. Additionally, she has not been diagnosed with Guillain-Barre syndrome or ADEM in the past. Her immunological tests for HBs antigen, HCV antibody, and HIV antigen and/or antibody are negative. She is eager to participate in the trial to help advance research in influenza vaccines.

Pt is a 65yo M with a history of osteoporosis, presenting with severe back pain for the past 2 weeks. Imaging revealed a vertebral compression fracture, and he was recommended for percutaneous vertebroplasty. The patient is anxious about the procedure and is concerned about the pain that he may experience during and after the procedure. He is willing to participate in the study and has expressed his consent to participate. He has no contraindications to the procedure and is affiliated to a social security scheme. He has been seen in preoperative anesthesia/radiology consultation more than 4 days before the date of the vertebroplasty. The patient can understand the information related to the study and has no linguistic, psychiatric, or cognitive reasons that would prevent him from participating in the study.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of encephalitis that occurred two years ago. She has been experiencing neurological sequelae, such as difficulty in walking, speaking, and performing daily activities. She has been on medications, but they have not shown any significant improvement in her condition. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of coagulation disorders or allergies to anesthetic agents. She has never been diagnosed with cancer, and her heart, lung, liver, and kidney functions are all normal. The patient is motivated to participate in the clinical trial to improve her quality of life and reduce her dependence on medications.

A 40 year old man came to the clinic complaining of difficulty in breathing, fatigue and joint pain. He is obese with a BMI of 40 kg/m2 and has a history of hypertension, high cholesterol and type 2 diabetes. His blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg and his fasting blood sugar is 200 mg/dL. A physical examination showed signs of peripheral neuropathy and mild swelling in his ankles. He reports that he has a sedentary lifestyle and has not exercised regularly for many years. He is interested in participating in a study to improve his health and reduce his risk of metabolic syndrome. He has received medical clearance from his physician and is willing to commit to a resistance training program.

A 60-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee, diagnosed according to the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) clinical and radiographic criteria, is currently taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain management. Despite the medication, she is still experiencing significant pain in the knee joint. She is willing to undergo a washout of analgesics and follow the treatment plan, visit schedules, and study procedures as per the protocol requirements. The patient does not have a history of rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune disorders, or any other painful syndrome that could interfere with the assessment of pain at the study joint. She does not have any cardiac, respiratory, neurological, psychiatric disorder, or any other medical condition that is not well controlled with treatment.

58-year-old male diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and has recently quit. He presents with cough and shortness of breath. Imaging studies revealed a right upper lobe lung mass that is 5 cm in size with mediastinal lymph node involvement. PET/CT and MRI of the brain showed no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 70 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently. He has no significant comorbidities and has normal liver and kidney function. He is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves proton beam radiation therapy and chemotherapy. He has no prior or simultaneous malignancies within the past two years and is not actively being treated on any other research study. He is a non-smoker and has no contraindications to using a recognized method of birth control if applicable.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with persistent atrial fibrillation. Despite taking antiarrhythmic medication, the patient has had recurrent episodes of AF and has been scheduled for a repeat ablation procedure. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including having at least one episode of AF documented within the last 2 years and being willing to provide written informed consent. The patient does not have any contraindications to systemic anticoagulation with heparin or warfarin or a direct thrombin inhibitor. The patient does not have any moderate to severe valvular disease and is not pregnant. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is interested in participating in the study and learning more about the potential benefits of the hybrid approach compared to the endocardial approach for treating recurred atrial fibrillation.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who presented to the emergency department with symptoms of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. The patient is currently taking aspirin for cardiovascular prophylaxis. Upper endoscopy showed a bleeding peptic ulcer with major stigmata of hemorrhage, which was successfully treated with endoscopic hemostasis. The patient has not taken any anti-secretory drugs in the past 48 hours and has not undergone gastrectomy or vagotomy. He has given informed consent to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old healthy female without any significant medical history presents for participation in a clinical trial. She doesn't consume alcohol or smoke cigarettes. Her BMI is 22.5 kg/m2. She is not currently taking any medications and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is currently using an oral contraceptive as her primary mode of birth control. She understands the study's dietary regimen and is willing to comply with it during the study period. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to any drugs, and all her laboratory tests, including vital signs, ECG, and clinical laboratory tests, are within normal limits.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking at least 10 cigarettes per day for the past 3 years. She has tried quitting in the past but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help her quit smoking. She has no known allergies and has not been exposed to a nicotine vaccine in the past. She is in good health and has not experienced any serious or unstable clinical disease in the past 6 months. She has not used any smoking cessation therapy within the past 30 days and is willing to use birth control during the study. She is able to follow the study protocol and has not used illicit drugs in the past 12 months or experienced any psychiatric disorder in the past 3 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman with a history of pancreatic adenocarcinoma diagnosed 6 months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy but developed jaundice and pruritus in the last 2 weeks. On examination, she appears jaundiced with abdominal tenderness. Her bilirubin level is 17 mg/dl, and her CA 19-9 level is 1200 U/ml. An abdominal CT scan showed a dilated common bile duct with a 16 mm high-grade stricture at the level of the ampulla of Vater. The patient is not a candidate for surgery due to metastasis to lymph nodes beyond the field of surgery. She has no history of coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, or surgically altered anatomy. The patient has not undergone previous treatment with bile duct stent.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who has completed high school and has been fluent in French since childhood. She is currently working as a librarian and has no history of cognitive complaints. She has no known medical conditions, and her family history is negative for dementia. She is not taking any medications that may interfere with memory or metabolic measures. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She does not have claustrophobia or any metallic objects in her body. She is right-handed and has a score of 90% on the Edinburgh Inventory. She is affiliated with a social security system. The patient has signed informed consent form prior to study entry.

The patient is an African American individual diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and has been relapse-free for the past 30 days. The patient is able to ambulate with or without assistance and has a Patient-Determined Disease Steps score of 0-5. The patient reports daily engagement in sedentary behavior for 480 minutes or more per day and has a health contribution score of less than 14 as calculated from the Godin Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire. The patient does not have any major musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, cardiopulmonary, or metabolic diseases that can influence physical activity and sedentary behavior levels. The patient is interested in participating in a 12-week pilot study that aims to reduce sedentary behavior in African Americans with MS through the use of text messages and newsletters, which will provide tips and strategies for interrupting prolonged periods of sedentary behavior and replacing it with light physical activity. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and provide informed consent for participation.

Patient is a 25-year-old female from the United States who is interested in enhancing the volume of her lips. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and has never had any cosmetic procedures on her lips before. The patient has a realistic expectation of the aesthetic results and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25 year old Black/African American man who identifies as gay. He is sexually active with multiple partners and reports having engaged in condomless anal intercourse in the past 6 months. He also reports having at least one heavy drinking episode per week, consuming more than 14 drinks per week on average. He owns a smartphone and is an English speaker. He has never been diagnosed with HIV or received PrEP. He is currently not in a monogamous/exclusive relationship. He has no history of alcohol treatment or psychiatric treatment in the past 3 years. He has no current diagnosis of bipolar disorder or schizophrenia, and his Brief Michigan Alcoholism Screening Test score is less than 5. He does not have a lifetime diagnosis of substance use disorder and his ASSIST score for any individual substance is less than 27. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help reduce his alcohol use and sexual risk behavior.

The patient is a 60 year old man diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease 4 years ago. He experiences tremors and stiffness in his limbs, making it difficult for him to perform daily activities. He is currently taking medication to manage his symptoms. He has a history of falls and is worried about his balance. He lives with his wife and has retired from his job as a mechanic due to his condition. He enjoys spending time with his grandchildren but finds it challenging to keep up with them. He is able to stand on his own but has difficulty maintaining balance for extended periods. He has no history of cognitive impairment and is able to follow verbal commands. He is motivated to participate in the study and hopes to improve his balance and quality of life.

32-year-old female presents to a rural general practice office with a complaint of cough and shortness of breath for the past 10 days. She reports that the cough is productive with yellowish-green sputum and is associated with chest pain and fatigue. She denies any fever, chills or night sweats. She has a history of asthma but has not used her inhaler for over a year. On physical examination, the patient appears well-nourished and in no respiratory distress. Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes and rhonchi. The chest x-ray shows no signs of pulmonary infiltrates. The general practitioner records the provisional diagnosis of acute bronchitis and prescribes an inhaler and antibiotics. The patient is offered participation in a clinical trial evaluating the usefulness of C-reactive protein testing in patients with acute cough or lower respiratory tract infections. The patient consents to participate in the study and the C-reactive protein test is performed.

The patient is a 13-year-old male who sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI) more than a year ago. His parents have noticed that he has difficulty with his memory, particularly in school. He has trouble retaining information and struggles to recall what he has learned. He is fluent in English and has no history of neurological injury or disease, nor significant psychiatric illness. He does not have uncontrolled seizures or other unstable medical complications. His parents are interested in exploring treatment options to improve his memory and overall academic performance.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. He is a non-smoker with no history of cardiovascular or metabolic disease. He participates in moderate to vigorous physical activity for at least 2 hours per week. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of intense exercise on neural responses to food. He has no contraindications to MRI scanning and is willing to undergo fMRI sessions.

The patient is a 6-year-old child born to a mother who was prescribed methadone during pregnancy due to opiate dependency. The child is being considered for participation in a clinical trial investigating the effects of drug exposure during pregnancy on vision in children. The child will be required to undergo eyesight testing by a specialist paediatric orthoptist, which will include acuity, stereoacuity, and looking for squints or nystagmus. More specialized tests such as eye movement recordings and visual evoked potentials may also be conducted. The child will also be seen by a paediatric ophthalmologist who will examine the back of their eyes and check for any need for glasses. The child's medical history will be taken, and if any problems are noted during the visit, the child will be referred to relevant services. The study is expected to run for 2 years, and the data collected will be added to an existing database for children born to opioid-dependent mothers prescribed substitute methadone during pregnancy. The aim of the study is to investigate whether the eyesight problems observed in these children at 6 months of age are still present as they grow older. The findings will be important in informing mothers on drug use during pregnancy and in managing affected children.

A 45-year-old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital is interested in participating in a physical activity study. She is married and has two children. She has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of her working hours sitting or standing. She has a BMI of 28, and her waist circumference is 34 inches. She has no history of chronic diseases and does not take any medication. She is interested in improving her physical activity level and overall health. She is willing to participate in any of the intervention groups in the study.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who has been diagnosed with severe heart failure for the past 6 months. Despite receiving stable medical therapy for HF, she still experiences severe symptoms and is in New York Heart Association Class III. Her left ventricular ejection fraction is between 20% and 35% and her left ventricular end diastolic diameter is between 55 mm and 80 mm. She has not had a myocardial infarction or cardiac revascularization procedure in the last 90 days nor is she expected to have one in the next 180 days. She is able and willing to comply with the required follow-up schedule and provide written informed consent to participate in this study. However, she does not have an implanted spinal cord stimulator or have a history of having an implanted upper thoracic spinal cord stimulator which is now explanted. She is not pregnant, nursing, or of childbearing potential. She has no bleeding tendency, renal insufficiency, active myocarditis, early postpartum cardiomyopathy, or critical valvular heart disease that requires valve repair or replacement. She has not taken any of the excluded drugs within 30 days of enrollment. Her life expectancy is estimated to be more than 1 year as assessed by the investigator.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of recurrent Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the disease has come back. The patient has tested positive for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and has been diagnosed with severe chronic active EBV (SCAEBV) syndrome. Her Karnofsky score is 60%. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study, and her HLA type will be checked to determine if there is a CTL line that is a match with her donor. The patient's tumor tissue is positive for EBV, and she meets the eligibility criteria for treatment. She is not currently receiving any investigational agents or tumor vaccines and has not received alemtuzumab or other anti-T-cell antibody within the past 28 days. The patient is not HIV positive and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to utilize a more effective birth control method during the study and for 3 months after the study is concluded. The patient's tumor is not in a location where enlargement could cause airway obstruction.

15-year-old male diagnosed with intracranial germ cell tumor with histology yet to be determined. The patient is a resident of a participating country and has provided written consent for trial participation and treatment according to the protocol. The patient has no other tumor entities other than primary intracranial germ cell tumor or CNS GCT as a second malignancy. There are no medical, psychiatric, or social conditions that are incompatible with trial treatment or treatment according to the protocol. The patient is not participating in any other clinical trial for treatment of germ cell tumors and is not receiving concurrent treatment within any other clinical trial. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has not received any treatment not given according to protocol prior to registration.

Patient is a 25-year-old male with congenital heart disease who requires cardiac surgery. He has a history of hypertension, but is currently not taking any cardiovascular active drugs. He has no history of aortic valve or aortic disease, and does not have any severe arrhythmias. He has no other significant medical history and is generally healthy. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of peripheral and/or autonomic neuropathy and/or cardiomyopathy, with a Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 50. The patient has been diagnosed with amyloidosis through biopsy and has one of the following targeted TTR mutations: Ser77Tyr, Thr60Ala, Tyr114Cys, Leu58His, Glu89Gln, Ser77Phe, Thr49Ala, Ile107Val, Val30Ala, Gly47Ala, Gly47Glu, Leu55Arg, Kys70Asn, Ile84Thr, Ile107Met. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use two acceptable methods of birth control throughout the study and for three months from the end of the study. The patient is not expected to undergo liver transplantation within 12 months after enrollment and has not received an investigational drug/device or participated in another clinical investigational study within 60 days before Baseline (Day 0). The patient is willing and able to comply with the study medication regimen and all other study requirements. The patient does not have chronic use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), primary or secondary amyloidosis, TTR-associated amyloidosis with V30M mutation, prior liver transplantation, renal insufficiency, liver function test abnormalities, New York Heart Association (NYHA) Functional Classification ≥ III, or other causes of sensorimotor neuropathy.

A 56-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with a new diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. Biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. Imaging shows a 4.5 cm mass in the right lung, with no evidence of metastasis. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. The patient has not received any prior systemic anticancer therapy or surgical resection for NSCLC. The patient has biopsy tissue available for PD-L1 and correlative studies testing prior to therapy. Pulmonary and cardiac function tests have been deemed adequate for thoracic surgical intervention. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. The patient has signed the consent form and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, and laboratory testing.

32-year-old male, who served in the Marine Corps for 4 years, deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, presents with symptoms of PTSD, including nightmares, flashbacks, and hypervigilance. He was diagnosed with PTSD by a mental health professional and his symptoms are confirmed by the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS-5) for DSM-5. He is willing to refrain from using all other formulations of cyclobenzaprine and antidepressants while participating in the study. He is able to read and understand English and provides written informed consent. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. He has no history of serotonin syndrome, severe allergic reaction or bronchospasm or known hypersensitivity to cyclobenzaprine or the excipients. He does not have a seizure disorder and his BMI is within the acceptable range. He has not received any other investigational drugs within 30 days before screening and has not participated in any other study with TNX-102 SL. He is not a family member of investigative staff.

A 24-year-old healthy man with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2 has agreed to participate in a clinical trial for AVT02. He has no history of clinically significant disorders or allergies to any medications. He has never been exposed to adalimumab or other anti TNF-alpha molecules in the past. He has no plans to receive any live vaccines during the study. He has not participated in any drug study in the last 5 months. He takes no regular medication and has no history of chronic infections. His blood pressure is normal, and he has no significant deviations in his electrocardiogram (ECG) or vital signs. He has not had any recent infections or hospitalizations. He has agreed to sign a patient information and consent form (PICF) and undergo protocol-related procedures.

A 60-year-old male with a history of peripheral arterial disease and stenotic lesion located in the superficial femoral artery (SFA). The patient has not undergone previous implantation of stents or stent grafts in the target vessel. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical study to evaluate the technical success and acute safety of the EverFlex™ self-expanding peripheral stent with Entrust™ delivery system.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with uncomplicated cholelithiasis during a routine medical check-up. She has no past medical or surgical history and has never had any operations in her upper abdomen or intestine. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, and her American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification is I. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use drugs. She is a vegetarian and eats a balanced diet. She exercises daily for 30 minutes and has no history of any chronic diseases. She is interested in participating in the study to understand whether there are any differences between standard laparoscopic cholecystectomy vs single port cholecystectomy for uncomplicated cholelithiasis.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no underlying medical conditions is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up.

Pt is a 19yo F who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia at age 11 and underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She achieved remission after 2 years of treatment and has been in remission ever since. However, she has been experiencing growth delay and fatigue, as well as decreased muscle and bone mass. She has been referred to the endocrine late-effects clinic where she was diagnosed with severe GH deficiency (peak GH<5mcg/l on stimulation). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the long-term effects of GH replacement therapy on development of bone, muscle, and fat mass, vascular risk, and quality of life. She meets all of the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the study for the next few years. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to GH or its preservative. She is able to provide informed consent and is committed to attending all required visits and assessments.

The patient is a 49-year-old healthy individual who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating whether an anti-inflammatory medication can impact daily life. The patient does not smoke and has no current medical disorders or chronic infections. The patient is not taking any hypnotic or psychotropic medication, steroids or opioids, and does not have any psychiatric disorders. The patient's BMI is within the acceptable range of less than 35. The patient is available to attend two sessions at the UCLA campus for blood draws, questionnaires, and computer tasks, and is willing to take either naproxen or a placebo twice daily for four weeks. The patient is also comfortable receiving daily text message reminders to take their pills and complete daily questionnaires, and is willing to fill out questionnaires online two and four weeks after the study period.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) two years ago. She has been taking disease-modifying therapy (DMT) with moderate success, but she still experiences frequent relapses that significantly impact her daily life. She has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. She is in good overall health and is able to perform daily activities without assistance. She is sexually active and uses barrier contraception. She is willing to participate in a long-term open-label extension study of ublituximab to evaluate its safety and efficacy in treating her relapsing multiple sclerosis. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 60-year-old male retiree was diagnosed with stage III COPD five years ago. He has a history of smoking, but quit 10 years ago. He has been on inhalers and oxygen therapy for the past year, but still experiences shortness of breath and difficulty walking even short distances. He lives with his wife who helps him with daily activities. He used to be an active person who enjoyed hiking and fishing, but now feels limited by his condition. He doesn't have any other significant medical history or comorbidities. His BMI is 27. He is compliant with his medications and oxygen therapy. He is motivated to improve his exercise tolerance and overall quality of life.

53 y/o male with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis for 6 months. Patient has suboptimal nutritional status with protein catabolic rate less than 0.85 g/kg/d calculated by three point urea kinetic modeling on at least 2 occasions over the past 6 months. Patient has also experienced unintentional weight loss of more than 2.5% of initial body weight and currently weighs less than 90% of ideal body weight. Biochemical parameters of malnutrition have been identified with serum albumin no greater than 3.7 g/dL and serum transferrin concentration less than 250 mg/dL. The patient has no active autoimmune, inflammatory or infectious disease, and it has been at least 6 months since any documented malignancy. There are no unusual dietary restrictions, and the patient has not had peritonitis in at least 3 months.

This clinical trial is an observational study and does not require patient participation. Instead, it aims to collect data on patients diagnosed with infectious endocarditis in specific regions of France during the year 2008. Patients who meet the inclusion criteria will be identified by clinicians, microbiologists, and cardiac ultrasonographists, and their data will be collected for analysis. Therefore, there is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has a history of peanut allergy and allergies to milk and egg. She has experienced anaphylactic reactions in the past and is constantly vigilant about avoiding these foods. Her parents have noticed that she has been feeling left out at social events and school due to her food allergies, and they are interested in exploring new treatment options. The patient has undergone allergy testing and has been confirmed to have food-allergen (FA)-specific IgE levels and positive skin prick tests (SPTs) for peanut, milk, and egg. She has also reacted positively during a Double-blind Placebo-controlled Food Challenge (DBPCFC) to small doses of these foods, defined as a cumulative dose of =/<444 mg food protein. The patient and her parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of biologics to improve outcomes for patients with multiple food allergies. Specifically, they are interested in Cohort B of the trial, which involves treatment with omalizumab for 8 weeks, followed by 24 weeks of treatment with dupilumab, in addition to multifood allergen oral immunotherapy. They are willing to comply with all study requirements and are excited to potentially improve the patient's quality of life and reduce the risk of severe reactions.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is generally healthy and does not have any chronic diseases. She has no history of cancer or any known allergies to soy proteins. The patient has not consumed any soy protein within the past week and is not taking any medication likely to affect gastrointestinal, liver, or kidney function. She has not taken antibiotics within the past 3 months, nor has she undergone chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The patient is not currently on oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the most effective amount and type of soy isoflavones needed in the diets of healthy men and women to prevent cancer.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of multiple myeloma came to the clinic with a relapse and progressive disease after undergoing several treatments. The patient has received three treatment options in the past, including alkylating agents, proteasome inhibitors, and immunomodulators, but the effect was not good. The patient is voluntarily joining this clinical trial and has signed informed consent. He is within the age range of 18 to 65 and is expected to survive for more than 12 weeks. The patient has not received autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in the past 90 days. The patient has normal bone marrow hematopoietic function, liver function, and renal function. The patient has good hemodynamic stability and ECOG physical status score of 2. T cells can be successfully expanded in vitro. The patient is willing to use contraception within one year after treatment. Other than multiple myeloma, there is no other uncontrolled active infection, autoimmune diseases, or immunodeficiency diseases. The patient has no definite neuropathy or psychosis, including authors of dementia or epilepsy, and no signs of lung or intestinal tumor infiltration.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather it involves students and teachers from approximately 10-15 state junior secondary schools in Indonesia. The trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness, acceptability, and feasibility of a specially adapted version of Dove Confident Me Single Session among Indonesian adolescents that will be integrated into UNICEF's Life Skills Education curriculum. To participate in the trial, students must be in grade 7 through 9 in state junior secondary schools in Indonesia and must speak Bahasa Indonesia with moderate-high literacy levels. Additionally, students must have access to a device with online access (e.g., laptop or iPad). Non-Bahasa Indonesia speaking students and students from religious or private schools are excluded from the trial.

A 14-year-old girl came to the hospital with symptoms of lower abdominal pain and discomfort during urination. She has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and has been prescribed antibiotics in the past. She is scheduled for a transabdominal pelvic ultrasound to rule out any underlying issues. She is otherwise healthy, has never had any major surgeries, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She meets the inclusion criteria for the LifeFlow Fluid Study and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing chronic knee pain and stiffness for several years. He has a history of degenerative joint disease and has tried various non-surgical treatments without significant improvement. He is interested in exploring the option of a robotic total knee arthroplasty (TKA) procedure and has been referred to a participating center for evaluation. His BMI is 28, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. He is willing to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits. His laboratory results are unremarkable.

28-year-old healthy female with no known medical conditions, not pregnant or breastfeeding, and a BMI of 22 kg/m2. The patient has no skin infections, lesions, scars, moles, or tattoos at the application site, and has not been exposed to excessive UV radiation. The patient has no known hypersensitivity or allergy to NSAIDs.

65-year-old M with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease for the last 5 years is currently on a stable dopaminergic treatment regimen. However, he is experiencing motor fluctuations with a minimum of 2 hours/day of "off" time, and has a Hoehn & Yahr stage between 2.5 and 4 when in the "on" state. The patient has a prior therapy with L-dopa for approximately 2 years and a beneficial clinical response to L-dopa. He is experiencing moderate to severe Parkinson's disease symptoms and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of preladenant. The patient is capable of maintaining an accurate and complete symptom diary and adhering to dose and visit schedules. He has results of Screening clinical laboratory tests clinically acceptable to the investigator and agrees to use a highly effective method of birth control while in the study and for 2 weeks after the last dose of study drug. The patient does not have any form of drug-induced or atypical parkinsonism, cognitive impairment, bipolar disorder, untreated major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, or other psychotic disorder, history of repeated strokes or head injuries, severe or ongoing unstable medical condition, or allergy/sensitivity to investigational product(s) or its/their excipients. The patient has not received any investigational drugs within 90 days immediately before Screening.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) 8 months ago for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. She is currently on stable doses of immunosuppressive therapy for graft versus host disease (GVHD). The patient has no known history of hypersensitivity to eggs or egg protein. She has not received the 2011-2012 influenza vaccine and has not had a proven influenza disease since September 1, 2011. The patient's platelet count is within normal limits, and there is no known latex hypersensitivity. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is available for the duration of the trial.

A 45-year-old female was brought to the hospital with severe headache, nausea, and vomiting. She reported feeling a sudden onset of the headache while at work and it had continued to worsen over the past few hours. She denied any history of trauma, hypertension, or previous headaches. On physical examination, she was found to have nuchal rigidity, photophobia, and a decreased level of consciousness. Her vital signs were stable. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the head was performed, which showed evidence of subarachnoid hemorrhage. She was admitted to the neurocritical care unit and underwent a lumbar puncture to collect cerebrospinal fluid. The cerebrospinal fluid showed evidence of bilirubin, confirming the diagnosis of subarachnoid hemorrhage. She was started on nimodipine and closely monitored for any signs of vasospasm. Her condition improved over the next few days and she was discharged from the hospital with instructions for follow-up imaging and appointments with her neurologist. She was approached to participate in a clinical trial investigating the time sequence of changes in bilirubin levels in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients with spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage and agreed to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been living with HIV for 10 years. He has been on the EFV/emtricitabine (FTC)/truvada (TDF) regimen for the past year and a half and has been clinically stable with an undetectable viral load. He reports experiencing moderate symptoms of depression and anxiety. He has no known history of CNS infections or neurological disorders. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (EGFR) is 75 ml/min. He is willing to switch to EVG/COBI/FTC/TDF for the purpose of this study. He does not have any metallic implants and is not claustrophobic.

A 28-year-old female who experienced a traumatic event 2 years ago and has been diagnosed with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). She reports experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and hyperarousal symptoms. She also reports difficulty falling and staying asleep, which has led to fatigue during the day. She has tried medication but has not found it to be effective. She is interested in participating in the CBT and yoga program to alleviate her symptoms and improve her sleep quality. She speaks English fluently and does not have any medical conditions that would interfere with her ability to participate in the yoga portion of the program.

This clinical trial is seeking normal volunteers and patients with Alzheimer's disease for a study on regional brain phospholipid metabolism using PET scan. The study is open to individuals between the ages of 18 and 90 years old. Normal volunteers must have no past or current medical conditions that would interfere with brain function, no history of alcoholism, psychiatric or neurological illness, head trauma with loss of consciousness, history of exposure to central nervous system toxin, history of central nervous system infection, metabolic, endocrine, connective tissue disease, hypertension or other cardiovascular disorder, abnormal renal, liver or pulmonary function, blood or coagulation disease, malignancy, psychopharmacological treatment, neurodegenerative or neurodevelopmental disorder, stroke, epilepsy, or require regular medication. Patients with Alzheimer's disease must have a diagnosis of possible or probable Alzheimer's disease according to NINCDS-ADRDA criteria and no past or current medical conditions that would interfere with brain function. Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding are not eligible to participate in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. She has been diagnosed with cholecystitis and has been advised to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no significant medical history and her physical examination is unremarkable. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is currently taking no medications other than occasional over-the-counter pain relievers. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with gallstones and is scheduled to undergo an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain, especially after consuming fatty foods. The pain is localized on the right upper quadrant of the abdomen and radiates to the back. She is otherwise healthy, with no major medical conditions and is not pregnant. The patient is able to communicate effectively in both English and Spanish, which are the languages used in the study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially decrease postoperative pain and improve cosmesis.

This is a 54 year-old female with a history of colon cancer. She underwent surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II disease. She presents with abdominal pain and a CT scan reveals multiple liver metastases. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer. She undergoes 18 weeks of first-line chemotherapy with FOLFOX regimen and has a partial response. She is now being considered for maintenance treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing metronomic chemotherapy with conventional chemotherapy. She has no known allergies to chemotherapy agents and has an ECOG performance status of 1.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who presents with symptoms of acute rhinosinusitis, including anterior mucopurulent drainage and nasal obstruction. She has a history of seasonal allergies but is otherwise healthy and takes no regular medications. She has not had any recent surgeries or traumatic injuries. She is not pregnant and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She is able to read and understand the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. She has not used any topical or oral antimicrobial medications in the past 30 days. Her temperature is 100.2F and she reports facial pain and pressure. She has no comorbidities that require antibiotics or antiviral therapy. She is not currently hospitalized and does not have any visible abscesses, incisions, or nasal polyps on physical examination.

The patient is a 21-year-old sexually active woman living in eThekweni-metropolitan Durban, South Africa. She is in a monogamous relationship with her boyfriend and has been sexually active with him for the past year. She reports using condoms inconsistently and is concerned about her risk of contracting HIV. She has a private smartphone and is conversant in isiZulu and English. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and recruit other women if needed. She has never used PrEP before and is not planning to start using it in the near future. She is willing to attend a virtual group-based gender-enhanced workshop to learn more about PrEP and HIV prevention. She is aware that the workshop may be audio-recorded and is comfortable with this.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who was admitted to the Department of Geriatric Orthopedic Rehabilitation a week ago for hip replacement surgery. She has a medical history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She takes medications for both conditions. She has no known allergies to any medications or probiotics. Her current bowel movements are normal and she does not experience any abdominal pain. She is able to sign an informed consent for the study.

A 58-year-old woman presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and ankle swelling. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are both well-controlled with medications. She has not experienced any previous heart attacks or strokes. The patient underwent an echocardiogram, which showed an ejection fraction greater than 40% and structural heart disease. NT-proBNP levels were elevated at 450 pg/ml. The patient is classified as NYHA Class III. The patient is being asked to participate in the CAYMUS HFpEF study to assess the effectiveness and safety of carvedilol SR in HFpEF patients. The study will involve taking carvedilol SR or a placebo for a period of time and monitoring the patient's NT-proBNP and hsTn levels. The study is seeking to determine if carvedilol SR is effective in reducing the risk of heart failure rehospitalization and mortality in HFpEF patients. To be considered for the study, the patient must be over 19 years old, have chronic heart failure NYHA class II-IV and preserved EF, and elevated NT-proBNP levels. The patient must also not have any contraindications to beta-blockers or be listed for heart transplant. The study requires informed consent prior to any study-specific procedure.

This is a 68-year-old man who underwent a radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer approximately two years ago. Since the surgery, he has been struggling with stress urinary incontinence, which has had a significant impact on his quality of life. He has tried conservative measures and pelvic floor muscle training without significant improvement. He is now considering surgery to manage his incontinence and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two emerging devices: the periurethral Pro-ACT balloons and retrourethral AdvanceXP male sling. The trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of the two devices, as well as their cost effectiveness. To be eligible for the study, the patient must have mild to moderate SUI (24-hour pad test < 300g) without detrusor overactivity on urodynamics. The trial will last for 12 months, during which the patient will be followed up with four visits to evaluate the efficacy of the devices, including pad usage, 24-hour pad test, quality of life, and patient satisfaction. The patient is excited about the opportunity to participate in this trial and hopes that the results will help him and other patients with SUI following radical prostatectomy.

45-year-old male presenting with recurrent episodes of vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness in the right ear. The patient has been diagnosed with Meniere's disease by an otolaryngologist and has experienced at least 2 definitive spontaneous episodes of vertigo lasting 20 minutes or longer, along with hearing loss on at least 1 occasion. The patient has not undergone any ear surgeries or intratympanic perfusions of steroids or gentamicin. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing age and is willing to use agreed contraceptive methods. The patient does not have any medical conditions that make Viagra contraindicated. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of sildenafil (Viagra) compared with placebo on symptoms during one acute attack of Meniere's disease.

The patient is a 2-year-old boy who has recently been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. His parents noticed that he isn't as social and communicative as other children his age. He has difficulty making eye contact, responding to his name, and engaging in play with others. He prefers to play alone and has a limited interest in toys. He is able to say a few words but doesn't use them to communicate effectively. He is a picky eater and has trouble sleeping through the night. He is currently receiving speech therapy twice a week. He lives with his parents and an older sibling who does not have autism. His parents are both working professionals and have limited time to engage with him during the day. He attends a daycare center and will be starting preschool in the fall. He has no known vision or hearing problems. His developmental level is above 9 months on the Visual Reception Scale of the Mullen Scales of Early Learning and on the Adaptive Behavior Composite of the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales. English is the primary language spoken by his family.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with chest pain upon exertion. He reports the pain is relieved with rest. He has never had a stress test before. His EKG is normal. His cardiac enzymes are within normal limits. He is currently on antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28, and he leads a sedentary lifestyle due to his desk job. He is willing and able to perform the treadmill stress test. He has no history of MRI, and he reports no contraindications to MRI. His GFR is 70, and he has no known allergies to contrast agents.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male presents with symptoms of upper abdominal discomfort that have been ongoing for the past month. He reports occasional vomiting, especially after meals, and a decreased appetite. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He denies any alcohol or tobacco use. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory tests show normal complete blood count, liver function tests, and serum electrolytes. He tests positive for Helicobacter pylori infection via stool antigen test. Endoscopy is scheduled to evaluate the cause of his symptoms, and he is deemed eligible for this clinical trial assessing different fluorescein sodium dosages for the detection of gastric intestinal metaplasia.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who is in good health and within 20% of normal weight for her height and body build. She has a history of regular alcohol consumption within the past 6 months, but has not made recent changes in her patterns of alcohol consumption. She is not currently trying to quit alcohol and does not have a past history of DSM-IV alcohol dependence or abuse. She does not have any liver disease or neurological disorders. The patient is capable of giving written informed consent and agrees to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is using one of the contraception methods listed in the protocol. She does not smoke more than 10 cigarettes a day and can abstain during the admission period. She has not used prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements, within 14 days prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient has not participated in a clinical trial and has not received an investigational product within 30 days, 5 half-lives or twice the duration of the biological effect of the investigational product. Her QTcB or QTcF is not greater than 450msec, and she will not donate blood or blood products in excess of 500mL within a 56 day period.

A 42-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metastatic melanoma and has measurable disease. The patient has no active major immunologic illness, no active systemic infections, and no primary or secondary immunodeficiency. The patient has fully recovered immune competence after prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy as evidenced by an absolute neutrophil count of > 1,000/mm^3 and no opportunistic infections. The patient has a performance status of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) 0-1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient has no major cardiovascular, respiratory, or coagulation disorders. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and fertile patients must use effective contraception during and for 4 months after study treatment. The patient has not received prior cyclophosphamide and fludarabine as part of a preparative regimen on National Cancer Institute (NCI) Surgery Branch adoptive cell therapy studies unless sufficient numbers of CD34+ stem cells (more than 2 x10^6/kg patient weight) have been obtained prior to the administration of chemotherapy. The patient is eligible to participate in this phase II clinical trial, which aims to determine complete clinical tumor regression in patients with metastatic melanoma treated with a myeloablative lymphoid-depleting preparative regimen comprising cyclophosphamide, fludarabine, and total body irradiation followed by autologous tumor-reactive tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte infusion, autologous CD34+ stem cell transplantation, and low-dose or high-dose interleukin-2.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF) at a young age. She is currently being followed up in a CF care center and has a positive sudoral test with Cl > 60 mmol/L. The patient has a FEV1 ≥ 40%, indicating mild to moderate lung damage. She has never experienced renal insufficiency or any recent pneumothorax, emphysema, puncture, or pleural biopsy. The patient has not experienced haemoptysis superior to 60 ml in the last 30 days. She is currently not experiencing any acute pulmonary exacerbation pathology, such as cough or sputum increase, decrease in tolerance to effort, loss of weight, lack of appetite, or deterioration of respiratory function. The patient has never had any medical history of intolerance, toxicity, or allergy to tobramycin or hypersensitivity to aminoside. She is part of the National Health Insurance program (Sécurité sociale) and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who presented to the hospital with a history of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He denies smoking or alcohol use. His physical examination reveals an irregularly irregular pulse with no murmurs or other significant findings. An electrocardiogram confirms atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. Transthoracic echocardiogram shows normal ejection fraction and no evidence of valvular heart disease. However, transesophageal echocardiogram shows that the patient has non-valvular atrial fibrillation, making them eligible for the study. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the AFCLTEE measurement can predict the outcome after DCCV.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who is overweight according to her age and sex-based BMI percentile. Her BMI is in the 90th percentile, and her parents are concerned about her health. She consumes at least 16 oz of sugar-sweetened beverages per day, including soda and fruit juice. She is generally active but spends most of her time playing computer and video games. Her parents have tried to encourage her to eat healthy foods and engage in physical activity, but they have been unsuccessful in changing her habits. The child does not have any serious medical conditions or elevated psychopathology as assessed by the Child Behavior Checklist. The parents are willing to participate in the study and adhere to the intervention protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia by her primary care physician. She has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. The patient has a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and has been taking iron supplements for the past month, but her symptoms have not improved. Her primary care physician has decided to treat her with Monofer® according to current practice. The patient has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications.
