She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and will attend hospital visits as part of her standard treatment. The patient is willing to undergo pre- and post-treatment blood tests to assess the efficacy and safety of Monofer®.

The patient is a 54-year-old man diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through dynamic imaging and elevated alphafetoprotein levels. He has no history of other tumors but has a history of heavy alcohol consumption for the past 20 years. He has been diagnosed with Child-Pugh A liver disease and his renal and hematopoietic functions are well preserved. He is scheduled to undergo surgical therapy for HCC and the tumor has been accessed by contrast-enhanced CT. There is no evidence of remote metastasis, and he does not have any other hepatobiliary diseases.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with periampullary cancer and is scheduled to undergo pancreaticoduodenectomy in the coming weeks. He has no history of major surgeries or chronic diseases. He is a non-smoker and only drinks alcohol socially. He lives a sedentary lifestyle and does not exercise regularly. He has no known allergies or food intolerances. He is able to read and write in English and has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 6-month-old infant diagnosed with hyperinsulinism due to inactivating mutations of adenosine triphosphate-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels. The infant has been on diazoxide therapy but failed to respond to the maximal dose (15 mg/kg/day). The infant is experiencing persistent hypoglycemia and requires a high glucose infusion rate (greater or equal to 10 mg/kg/min). The parents have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in an open-label pilot study to assess the effect, safety, and tolerability of sirolimus for the treatment of hyperinsulinism. The infant has confirmed bi-allelic mutations in either ABCC8 or KCNJ11 genes. The infant has not been diagnosed with any laboratory abnormalities that indicate clinically significant hematologic, hepatobiliary, or renal disease. The infant has not had any recent surgical procedures, and the parents are willing to comply with study schedules and procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who participated in the primary study 108890 (NCT00435396) and received 3 doses of GSK Biologicals' candidate CMV vaccine according to a 0-1-6 month schedule. He completed the Year 2 follow-up study 109211 (NCT00435396) and is now being invited to participate in the long-term follow-up study at Visit 8 (Year 4) and Visit 9 (Year 5) as the vaccine group. He has no history of CMV infection or any other immunodeficient condition. He is generally healthy, with no chronic medical conditions or use of immunosuppressive medication. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol, including returning for follow-up visits.

50-year-old female with no significant medical history who is scheduled for a routine mammogram in the next 4 weeks. She has no personal or family history of breast or any other cancer. She has no current symptoms or concerns related to breast or other cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from providing blood samples for the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma two years ago. He received six cycles of R-CHOP (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone) as the first-line treatment and achieved a complete response. Unfortunately, he relapsed nine months later and received R-ICE (Rituximab, Ifosfamide, Carboplatin, Etoposide) as the second-line treatment, but the tumor continued to progress. He then received a third-line treatment with R-DHAP (Rituximab, Cytarabine, Cisplatin, Dexamethasone) and underwent an autologous stem cell transplant (aSCT). However, after six months, the tumor recurred again. The patient has been evaluated and found to have CD20/CD22-positive diffuse large B-cell NHL and meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 50-year-old male smoker presents with a cough and shortness of breath. A chest X-ray shows a mass in his left lung. A biopsy confirms non-small cell lung cancer that is ALK-positive by an FDA-approved assay performed centrally. The patient has received one prior chemotherapy regimen for metastatic disease, but no prior ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status score of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. He is able to swallow and retain oral medication. His organ system function is adequate, with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1.8 x 109/L, platelets of 135 x 109/L, hemoglobin of 11 g/dL, total bilirubin of 1.2 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) of 1.5 x ULN, and creatinine of 0.9 x ULN. He has brain metastases but is asymptomatic at study baseline and is not on corticosteroids. He agrees to use adequate contraceptive measures during the study and for 90 days after the last dose of study medication. He is willing and able to comply with the trial and follow-up procedures and is able to understand the nature of the trial and give written informed consent.

The patient is a 32 year-old male who is overweight with a BMI of 29.5 kg/m2. He has a family history of Type 2 diabetes but has not been diagnosed with the disease himself. He is in good health overall and does not have any significant medical history. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is sexually active with one partner and uses condoms for contraception. He is willing to use contraception during the study period. He has not taken any prescription medication within the past 2 weeks and has not used over-the-counter medication, except for occasional paracetamol. He has not donated blood or plasma recently. He is not a vegan or vegetarian and does not have any dietary restrictions. He is able to communicate reliably with the study investigators and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

A 50-year-old man was recently diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has no history of falls or freezing of gait. He experiences mild tremors and stiffness in his arms and legs, and he has difficulty with fine motor skills. He is currently taking medication for his Parkinson's symptoms but has not received any physiotherapy. He is able to walk independently and is willing to attend physiotherapy sessions as part of the trial. He speaks English fluently and is interested in participating in the study.

Looking for individuals in Egypt who have poultry in their household and are willing to participate in a study to determine the incidence and transmission of avian influenza viruses in humans exposed to poultry. Eligible individuals must be willing to sign a consent or assent form, complete a study questionnaire, and permit the withdrawal of blood, nasal washes, nasal swabs, and throat swabs. Participants must be at least 2 years old and not have any known immunosuppressive conditions or immune deficiency diseases, including HIV infection, or ongoing receipt of any immunosuppressive therapy. Participants will be monitored for 6 years with annual follow-up visits to measure seroprevalence and exposure variables, and biweekly or weekly visits to measure incidence of infection, measure secondary transmission rates, monitor symptoms, and assess immunological response. All residents of a household will be invited to participate, and field nurses or physicians will visit each household to collect data and samples.

A 25-year-old male with a history of Hemophilia A and regularly treated with recombinant factor VIII (rFVIII) has been experiencing recurrent episodes of bleeding into his joints. He has had several joint surgeries in the past and is looking for a new treatment option that can help prevent future bleeds. He has no known allergies and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. He is interested in participating in the OPERA study to receive long-term prophylactic treatment with Afstyla® and to contribute to the research on the effectiveness and safety of this new treatment option.

42-year-old male with a history of occasional gallbladder pain and cholecystitis has been advised to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient has no known allergies and is not on any regular pain medication. He has never had any surgery before and has no history of chronic pain or liver disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the adequate dose of nalbuphine for post-operative pain management. He is able to cooperate with the evaluation surveys and has no history of dementia or other psychiatric diseases.

A 55-year-old woman has been diagnosed with epithelial ovarian carcinoma. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy 10 months ago but has now been confirmed to have persistent disease with multiple metastases. Her EGFR expression was found to be positive by an outside reference lab. She has not received any further treatment since her initial chemotherapy 10 months ago. She has measurable disease at baseline and at least one recurrent lesion that can be used to assess response. She has recovered from the effects of recent surgery and chemotherapy. She has no history of prior cetuximab or other therapy targeting the EGFR pathway or prior history of chimerized or murine monoclonal antibody therapy. She has no other invasive malignancies or unstable cardiac disease. She has not had an acute hepatitis or active or uncontrolled infection. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the overall response rate, time to progression, and 1 yr survival with cetuximab.

45 yo M with a history of IV drug use and chronic hepatitis C genotype 1, confirmed by positive serum HCV RNA. Liver biopsy performed 14 months ago revealed stage 2 fibrosis. Patient has no history of prior treatment with pegylated interferon, standard interferon or ribavirin. No history of co-infection with hepatitis B or HIV, no post-transplant history, no history of end-stage renal disease, no history of immunotherapy. Patient is willing to use effective and continuous contraception during the treatment and for 4 months thereafter. Past Medical History: - Chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 - IV drug use - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Depression - Anxiety - Tobacco use - No history of alcohol abuse - No significant family history of liver disease

A 31-year-old female who has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a Digital Home Ovulation Test. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has been tracking her cycles for the past 3 months. She is in good health and has no known medical conditions. She is not taking any medications or supplements that may affect her menstrual cycle. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is married and works as a teacher. She has no children and has never been pregnant before. Her family history is negative for any fertility issues. She is willing to comply with the investigational procedures and give informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old male from Delhi, India. He has been experiencing a persistent cough for the past two months, along with fatigue and weight loss. He is a smoker and works as a laborer in a construction site. He is married and has two young children. He does not have any significant past medical history, but he admits to not having a balanced diet and rarely getting any sun exposure. He has not been vaccinated against tuberculosis. Upon examination, he is found to have pulmonary tuberculosis and is sputum positive. He does not have any signs of secondary immunodeficiency states, hepatitis B and C, or seizure disorder. His renal and hepatic functions are normal, and he does not have any hematological abnormalities. He is willing to comply with the treatment regimen and is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of Type 1 diabetes and has been using an insulin pen for the past year to manage her condition. She injects insulin at least four times a day and uses a 6mm x 32G pen needle. The patient reports experiencing discomfort during injection and is interested in trying a new pen needle that may improve her injection experience. She is willing to use either the BD NEXT pen needle or her current pen needle for a week each, in a randomly assigned sequence, to evaluate and compare her injection experience with both. The patient uses the Sanofi-aventis SoloSTAR® pen, and her daily insulin dose is greater than 10 units. She is willing to keep her diabetes medications, diet, and exercise the same during the study and is able to read, write and follow instructions in English. The patient is not pregnant and has not participated in any clinical studies within the past 30 days. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study for approximately three weeks.

The patient is a 60 year old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer that is estrogen receptor positive. She has been prescribed aromatase inhibitor therapy as part of her adjuvant treatment plan. However, she has been experiencing joint and muscle pain since starting the medication. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of kidney stones, hypercalcemia, hyperparathyroidism, or malabsorption syndrome. She has a performance status of 1 on the WHO/ECOG scale. Her baseline Vitamin D level is below 50 ng/mL. She is not taking any additional Calcium and Vitamin D supplements aside from the study medications and is not taking cholestyramine, orlistat, phenytoin or phenobarbital. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and has provided signed informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who is currently hospitalized due to a suspected blood clot in his leg. He has been on heparin therapy for the past few days to prevent the clot from getting larger. However, his platelet count has decreased by 40% since starting heparin therapy, and he has developed signs of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), including new thrombosis and fever. The doctor suspects that he has acute HIT and wants to enroll him in a clinical trial to compare the safety and efficacy of two different drugs - danaparoid and argatroban. The patient has no previous history of HIT, but he has a history of hypertension and diabetes. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

28-year-old female with a history of infertility for 2 years. She is married and has been trying to conceive unsuccessfully for the past year. Her menstrual cycle is regular with a cycle length of 28 days. She has no significant past medical or surgical history. Her BMI is 25. She has undergone initial infertility workup including hysterosalpingography (HSG) and semen analysis for her husband, which showed no abnormalities. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and is now planning to undergo controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) for in vitro fertilisation (IVF). She has 6 follicles in the right ovary and 5 follicles in the left ovary, all of which exceed 11 mm in diameter. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has consented to participate.

A 38-year-old woman living in Petropolis had been feeling increasingly anxious and sad over the past few months. She has trouble sleeping, feels fatigued, and has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed. She decided to make an appointment with her primary care physician to discuss her symptoms. After completing a General Health Questionnaire, her score was above the positive screen threshold at two different time points, which indicated her need for further evaluation. Her physician referred her to the study, and she met the inclusion criteria of having a positive diagnosis of depression or anxiety per the Mini Mental State Examination. The patient has no history of bipolar disorder, mania, or severe suicidal ideation. She is not pregnant and does not have any cognitive impairment that would limit her ability to participate in the study. She is willing to participate in the study and receive either enhanced usual care or enhanced usual care plus group psychological intervention.

A 52-year-old woman with suspected gynecological cancer is scheduled for explorative laparotomy through a middle-line incision. She has a history of hypertension and is currently under treatment with lisinopril. The patient is able to understand and express herself in Swedish and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists class 1 status. She has no contra-indications for epidural or intrathecal anesthesia. The patient has no physical disabilities and is expected to be mobilized on the day after surgery. She has no history of mental retardation or psychiatric or mental disorders that would make it unsuitable for her to participate in the study. The patient has been informed about the study and has signed an informed consent form.

A 50-year-old man with a history of heart failure presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema in his legs. He has been diagnosed with NYHA Class III heart failure despite optimal pharmacological heart failure therapy. A 12-lead electrocardiogram shows a sinus rate of 60 bpm, QRS duration of 160 ms, and PR interval of 280 ms. His creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dL, and his left ventricular ejection fraction is 30% based on an echocardiogram. He is willing and able to undergo a device implant and participate in all testing associated with the clinical investigation. His life expectancy is more than 180 days, according to his physician's discretion. He is 50 years old, and he provides informed consent. He has not had previous cardiac resynchronization therapy and does not meet the general indications for antibradycardia pacing. He does not have a neuromuscular, orthopedic, or other non-cardiac condition that prevents normal, unsupported walking. He has not had an atrial tachyarrhythmia that is permanent or persistent within 180 days prior to enrollment. He is not hypersensitive to a 0.7 mg dose of dexamethasone acetate. He does not have surgically uncorrected primary valvular heart disease, require dialysis or have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has not had a myocardial infarct, unstable angina, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft during the 30 days prior to enrollment. He does not have hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy or infiltrative cardiomyopathy, and he does not have a mechanical tricuspid prosthesis. He is not enrolled in any concurrent study that may confound the results of this study.

A 42-year old female was diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetes mellitus. She has been on peritoneal dialysis (PD) for 8 months. She lives with her husband and two children. She is compliant with her dialysis regimen and has not experienced any major complications. However, she did have an episode of exit-site infection 2 months ago, which was treated with antibiotics. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She reports good hygiene and follows the recommended exit-site care. She has no known allergies to medications. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She works as a teacher and is able to continue working while receiving PD. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve care for PD patients.

The patient is a 3-year-old child who was brought to the Pediatric Emergency Department with a history of vomiting and diarrhea for the past 24 hours. The child has no significant past medical history and has not received any interventions for the current symptoms. The child is lethargic, irritable, and has decreased urine output. The child's weight is 15 kg, and the blood glucose level is within normal limits. Upon evaluation, the child is diagnosed with dehydration and requires IV fluids. The child meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of intravenous fluids with dextrose for dehydrated children.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with moderate scoliosis. She has a Cobb angle of 15 degrees as measured on a radiograph. She has been experiencing mild discomfort in her back, but it has not significantly affected her daily activities. She is currently being treated with a combination of physical therapy and a back brace. She has no significant medical history, and her parents are both affiliated with social security. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to follow the instructions given by the investigators during the experimentation period.

A 45 year old man presented to the clinic with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has been managing his diabetes with oral hypoglycemic agents and insulin injections but his blood sugar levels were not well controlled. He is also obese, with a BMI of 40 kg/m2. His HbA1c was 8.5% in the latest lab study. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, and no ongoing psychiatric disorder. He is interested in bariatric surgery to improve his diabetes control and achieve weight loss.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of IBS for the past year. She has experienced abdominal pain, bloating, and irregular bowel movements, which have significantly affected her quality of life. She works as a nurse and finds it difficult to manage her symptoms while on shift. She has tried various diets and supplements to alleviate her symptoms but has not found any significant relief. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand her triggers and improve her quality of life. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medication. She lives in the Netherlands and has access to the internet to fill in the online questionnaire.

A 56-year-old man presented to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both under control with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His ECG showed ST-segment depression and he was scheduled for percutaneous coronary intervention. He has never taken statins before and is not allergic to any medication. He has no history of liver disease or fibrate use. His blood test result showed normal levels of AST, ALT, and CPK, but his LDL cholesterol level was high. He agreed to participate in the study and was randomized to receive either atorvastatin 80mg or placebo before and after the procedure. He will be followed up for 30 days with blood tests and in-person interviews to monitor for any major cardiovascular events.

A 17-year-old Caucasian woman who is pregnant for the first time and seeking prenatal care. She reports that she is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and has not experienced any complications thus far. She is not currently experiencing any symptoms and has not been diagnosed with any chronic medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of teenage maternity on obstetrical and perinatal outcomes. She meets the inclusion criteria for group A in the study, which requires maternal age of < 18 years and nulliparity.

A 42-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) who has been advised to start Ocrevus treatment by her neurologist. She has no significant medical history other than hypertension which is well controlled with medication. She is not currently taking any immune suppressant medication and has not taken steroids in the past 2 months. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to give informed consent. She is willing to have blood drawn as scheduled in the protocol and is willing and able to complete all procedures and evaluations related to the study. She has not received any experimental drug within 30 days of enrollment.

A 7-year-old boy from a rural area in India is eligible for this clinical trial. He lives with his parents, grandparents, and two younger siblings. He attends school regularly and enjoys playing soccer with his friends. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He has received standard childhood vaccines and has not had the flu vaccine before. His family members are also eligible for enrollment in the surveillance arm of the study.

45-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to the liver and lungs. She has undergone adjuvant chemotherapy with an anthracycline drug and has failed to respond to the treatment. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath. She is being considered for treatment with albumin-bound paclitaxel and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of this treatment. She is otherwise in good health and has no history of heart disease or other significant medical conditions. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 30-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital came to the clinic complaining of difficulty in controlling her blood sugar levels. She recently started working in night shifts and noticed that her blood sugar levels were consistently high compared to when she worked during the day. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes, with her mother and maternal grandmother being diagnosed with the condition. She is of average weight and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has no history of psychiatric illness, eating disorders, or bariatric surgery. She is currently not taking any medications for diabetes or any other chronic conditions. She is willing to participate in a research study investigating the effects of night time eating on glucose tolerance and the role of the MTNR1B risk allele.

A 62-year-old male smoker who has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue for the past few months. A CT scan revealed a mass in the right lung and lymph node involvement. Biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of advanced nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer (nsNSCLC). The patient has no history of brain metastasis or bleeding diathesis. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and the patient has normal hepatic, renal, and bone marrow function. The patient has not received prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease and completed systemic anticancer therapy or radiotherapy for locally advanced nsNSCLC over a year ago. The patient is willing to be randomized to either BI 695502 plus chemotherapy or Avastin® plus chemotherapy followed by maintenance monotherapy with either BI 695502 or Avastin®.

A 32-year-old healthy male is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of Dolutegravir on whole-body insulin sensitivity, lipid and endocrine profile. He is HIV-negative and has no underlying medical conditions. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and exercises regularly. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He has no known allergies to any medication including Dolutegravir. He takes a daily multivitamin supplement, but no other medications or herbal supplements. He has never participated in a clinical trial before but is interested in contributing to medical research. He understands the informed consent process and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including using contraception if needed.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who works full-time and has two children aged 5 and 8 years old. She is concerned about her children's diet and wants to ensure that they are eating healthy, especially when dining out. She frequently takes her children to fast-food restaurants for meals. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effects of a healthy default kids' beverage policy on children's fast-food restaurant meal orders and dietary intake. She is fluent in both English and Spanish and is available to participate in a telephone dietary recall the following day. She is a responsible parent and is willing to provide consent for her children's participation in the study.

We are looking for volunteers who are willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at studying the effects of prolonged prone positioning on the eyes. The purpose of the study is to better understand the physiological changes that occur in the eyes during prolonged prone positioning, which can lead to post-operative vision loss. We are seeking individuals who are able to tolerate lying prone for 5 hours, and who do not have any sensitivity to proparacaine hcl 0.5% or tropicamide 1%. Volunteers will undergo various tests including measuring intraocular pressure, visualizing the optic nerve imaging, refractometry, ultrasound, corneal thickness pachymetry, measurement of proptosis, measurement of pupillary reflex. There will be two sessions each lasting 5.5 hours, with the first session being on a flat Jackson table and the second session being on a Jackson table elevated by 6 inches. If you are interested in participating, please contact us to learn more about the study and to see if you are eligible to participate.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years. She was diagnosed with Asherman's Syndrome after a dilation and curettage procedure following a miscarriage. She has undergone multiple surgeries to remove adhesions, but her endometrial lining remains thin, measuring less than 6mm during previous IVF cycles. She has not responded to standard therapies and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments. She has no significant medical history, is not currently pregnant, and is not taking any medications that would exclude her from participation in the study.

A 25-year-old healthy female with a body mass index of 22.5 kg/m^2 and a body weight of 60 kg is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of food and pH on the relative bioavailability of BMS-986165. She has no significant medical conditions and has never been pregnant. She has not received any live vaccines in the past 60 days. She is interested in contributing to medical research and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 4-year-old male child presents for a closed reduction procedure of his left elbow that he sustained in a fall. The child has no significant medical history, and his developmental milestones are age-appropriate. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. The child's weight is 18 kg, and his height is 105 cm. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities in the airway or respiratory system. The child's parents have provided informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 6-month-old baby boy who has recently been diagnosed with congenital syphilis. His mother tested positive for syphilis during her pregnancy but did not receive adequate treatment. The baby has been experiencing symptoms such as rash, fever, and irritability. The rash is characterized by small, red, and flat spots on his skin. He has also developed swollen lymph nodes. The baby is otherwise healthy and has been meeting his developmental milestones. He is currently receiving treatment for syphilis and is being closely monitored by his healthcare providers. The parents have been informed about the importance of completing the full course of treatment and preventing future cases of congenital syphilis. The medical team is conducting this retrospective survey study to better understand the clinical presentation and laboratory findings of patients with congenital syphilis who have received treatment.

The patient is a 55 year old man who was diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) six months ago. The diagnosis was made after he complained of pain in his lower back and blood in his urine. Imaging tests revealed the presence of a large tumor in his right kidney and metastases to his lungs and bones. He has been receiving treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors and checkpoint immunotherapy for the past six months. He has experienced some side effects such as fatigue, nausea and diarrhea, but they have been manageable. He has been informed about the study and is willing to participate in the plasma concentration monitoring of his treatment drugs for the next 6 months.

45-year-old female with a history of achalasia, presenting with difficulty swallowing, regurgitation, and chest pain. Eckardt score is 7 indicating moderate to severe achalasia. The patient has not had any previous esophageal or gastric surgery and does not have esophageal diverticula. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and provide informed consent. There are no significant comorbidities noted.

Patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of metastatic colorectal cancer to the liver. His liver metastases are unresectable and are hypervascular based on visual estimation by the Investigator. His target tumors are measurable using standard imaging techniques. The patient has a performance status score of 1 and is expected to live for at least 3 more months. He has not received any radiation, surgery or chemotherapy in the last 4 weeks. His liver function test results are within the normal range and he has no history of hepatic encephalopathy. The patient has no contraindications to angiography and hepatic artery catheterization and has no evidence of pulmonary insufficiency. He has no active uncontrolled infection or significant underlying medical or psychiatric illness that would preclude safe delivery of TheraSphere® treatment. The patient is not pregnant and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year old male was admitted to the hospital due to shortness of breath and coughing for the past week. He had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. On examination, he was tachypneic with respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. Lung examination revealed bilateral crepitations. ECG showed sinus tachycardia with no ST-T wave changes. Chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates. The patient was diagnosed with ARDS and was started on mechanical ventilation. Transthoracic echocardiogram showed signs of right ventricular dysfunction with an apical four-chamber view showing a right ventricular end-diastolic area to left ventricular end-diastolic area ratio of greater than 0.6. He was started on inotropic support and fluid management. The patient was willing to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) 24 hours ago for septic shock secondary to pneumonia. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease stage 3. The patient received a computed tomography (CT) scan with intravenous contrast for further evaluation of his pneumonia. His baseline serum creatinine was 1.5 mg/dL, and it has been stable for the past year. However, 24 hours after the CT scan, his serum creatinine has increased to 2.5 mg/dL. The patient has not had any urine output since the CT scan was performed. The patient is currently receiving vasopressor support for his septic shock, and his blood pressure is well controlled. The patient is not pregnant and does not have cardiogenic pulmonary edema. The patient's arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.38 and a potassium level of 4.0 mmol/L. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

A 23-year-old male was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after presenting with severe fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of AML with normal karyotype. He received standard induction chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. The patient was then referred for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) and received a matched unrelated donor transplant. The patient has since completed the transplant and is currently in remission. The patient has available records of MICM and NGS results at the time of diagnosis, making them eligible for this study. The patient has no active malignancy and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 21-year-old male student in his second year at Jimma University who has been using khat for the past month and wishes to reduce or stop its use. He is able to read and write in both Amharic and Oromo languages. He does not have any severe substance use other than khat, nor is he experiencing any ongoing acute episode of severe mental disorder or current suicidal ideation. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol as outlined by the researchers.

This is a 30-year-old pregnant female who was recently hospitalized for preterm labor at the Robert Debré Hospital due to frequent and regular uterine contractions (at least 3 in 30 minutes), significant cervical changes, and before 37 weeks of amenorrhea (SA). She is carrying a single pregnancy and is currently between 24 + 0 and 32 + 0 weeks of gestation. The patient is not opposed to participating in the clinical trial and is a beneficiary of social security. She does not have any psychiatric pathology and is capable of understanding the technology used in the trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing anal incontinence for the past 2 years. She reports frequent episodes of involuntary leakage of stool or gas, which have significantly impacted her quality of life. She has tried various conservative treatments such as dietary changes, pelvic floor exercises, and medications without any significant improvement in her symptoms. She has no history of pelvic organ cancer or inflammatory bowel disease. She has completed childbearing and has no plans for any future pregnancies. She has not undergone any pelvic organ surgery in the past year and is not scheduled for any in the next year. She does not have insulin-treated diabetes. Her Wexner score is 12, indicating severe anal incontinence. She has been informed about the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no history of chronic medical conditions. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the safety and potential benefits of Korean Red Ginseng intake for 24 weeks. He understands and agrees to the terms of the trial, including the need to sign a written agreement and to use contraception if he is a woman of childbearing age. He does not have any known allergies to the ingredients in the test food. He is not pregnant or lactating. He does not have severe renal or hepatic disease, autoimmune diseases, uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or thyroid dysfunction. He is not taking any medications that would disqualify him from participation, including antipsychotic medication, investigational drugs, or health supplements other than vitamins and minerals. He does not have any medical conditions that would likely affect the test result and make him unfit for participation.

A 60-year-old male retired school teacher presented to the clinic complaining of weakness, fatigue, and difficulty performing activities of daily living. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year, and they have been progressively worsening. He also reported a loss of appetite and unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds in the last 6 months. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He had a myocardial infarction two years ago, and he underwent coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, and metoprolol. The physical examination revealed poor muscle tone, decreased grip strength, and slow walking speed. His bone mineral density test showed a T-score of -2.5, consistent with osteoporosis. His body mass index is 19.5, and his body fat percentage is 8%. He scored 5/12 on the Short Physical Performance Battery test. He is up to date on all age and gender-appropriate cancer screening.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy adult who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research. The patient has not received any previous H5N1 influenza vaccinations and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days. The patient is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2. The patient is currently sexually abstinent and agrees to remain so or use medically effective contraception during the 7-month study period. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would limit their ability to be evaluated for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently admitted to Massachusetts General Hospital due to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and managed to recover after a week of inpatient care. He owns a smartphone and is willing to participate in a study that aims to improve heart failure management after discharge. He has established a primary cardiologist at MGH and has access to the internet. He is discharged home and is expected to continue with self-care. He is fluent in English and does not have any moderate or severe cognitive impairment. He is interested in using the AMAZE™ smartphone-based application to monitor his health metrics and is willing to enter his daily mood, symptoms, weight measures, and vital signs such as blood pressure (BP) and medication adherence in the app. He is willing to use the app for the duration of the study, which is 60 days.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent a prosthetic joint surgery 2 years ago for his left knee joint. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication for both conditions. He presents with complaints of pain, swelling, and redness around the surgical site. The patient has no fever and no history of recent trauma. A physical examination reveals tenderness and swelling around the knee joint. The patient underwent surgery, and four deep bone biopsies were taken from the interface between the implant and the affected bone. The tissue samples were cultured, and S. epidermidis was identified. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial as he has a confirmed S. epidermidis infection after prosthetic joint surgery. He provides informed written consent and is 18 years or older. The patient is eligible for the study and will be followed up for an average of 26 months after discharge to assess the primary outcome of cure.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of asthma that has been poorly controlled for the past few months. She has been using her inhaler more frequently and has had to use her nebulizer at home on several occasions. She also reports experiencing dyspnea during physical activity and even during restful periods. She has been referred to a secondary, out-patient respiratory clinic for lack of asthma control. She has received a diagnosis of asthma from a pulmonologist and has had at least two consultations at a pulmonologist-lead asthma clinic. Her ACQ6 score is 1.2. She is able to provide written informed consent. She is not currently pregnant and does not have any severe diseases that would exclude her from participating in the study. She speaks and understands Danish. She has not received any training in breathing exercises by physiotherapists in the last 6 months. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her asthma control and quality of life.

A 35-year-old female presented with a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis with symptoms of nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itching and sneezing during the pollen season. She has been using nasal corticosteroids and an antihistamine for symptom control. Her medical history was insignificant for any chronic medical conditions or surgeries. She has never smoked and has no family history of allergies or asthma. She works as a secretary in a city office building near a busy intersection with heavy traffic. Her symptoms are worse on days when she has to walk to work instead of taking a cab. She experiences occasional cough and wheeze but denies any shortness of breath or chest tightness. She has never been diagnosed with asthma or required emergency room visits. She avoids outdoor activities on high pollen days and uses air conditioning in her apartment. She has completed her education until high school and is currently unmarried. She is willing to participate in clinical trials to find a better solution for her allergy symptoms.

The patient is a 22-year-old healthy male volunteer with no significant medical history. He does not smoke or use any prescription medications. He has a BMI of 23 kg/m2, and his physical examination and clinical laboratory test results are normal. He is willing to commit to the confinements and return visits during the entire period of the study. The patient has no history of rectal bleeding, passage of mucus rectally, and irregular bowel habits such as frequent diarrhea or constipation. He has not used any rectal enema or laxative within 7 days prior to dosing and has not used any over-the-counter medications within 7 days prior to dosing. He has not participated in another clinical trial within 28 days prior to dosing. The patient must provide a voluntary written informed consent prior to initiation of screening and must be capable of following the verbal and written study instructions. He is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been experiencing upper abdominal discomfort and nausea for the past few weeks. He has a history of smoking and social drinking. He has never been diagnosed with H. pylori infection before but has been experiencing symptoms that are consistent with it. He has no allergies to any medications and has no history of any major medical conditions. Upon physical examination, there is tenderness in the epigastric region. An endoscopy is performed and a biopsy confirms the presence of H. pylori. Standard proton pump inhibitor-based triple therapy is initiated, but after completion, the patient is still symptomatic and has a positive urea breath test. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial investigating the additive effect of endonase on second-line eradication therapy for H. pylori.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of strabismus presented with complaints of double vision and misaligned eyes. She had a history of corrective strabismus surgery in both eyes during childhood. The patient had no history of ocular pathology or family history of glaucoma. She was scheduled for recession strabismus surgery through a fornix approach of the medial rectus muscle of the left eye. The patient was able to comply with topical treatment and the post-operative appointment schedule. She had no personal history of allergic drug reaction or allergic conjunctivitis. The patient was not on any medication and had no significant medical history. Pre-operative examination revealed a mild degree of hyperopia in both eyes and normal intraocular pressure (IOP) measurements. She was included in the study and randomly assigned to receive either Loteprendol etabonate 0.5% (Lotemax) or Dexamethasone 0.1% (Sterodex) drops following surgery, in addition to topical Ofloxacin 0.3% (Oflox) eye drops.

A 50-year-old male office worker has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath upon physical exertion. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His father had a heart attack at the age of 60. Upon consultation with his physician, he was recommended to undergo coronary angiography to evaluate the function of his coronary arteries. He has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate. He is willing to undergo a non-invasive test to determine the flow reserve score analysis software for coronary angiography. He is willing to provide the results of his coronary CT angiography, which was performed within the last 60 days. He has signed the informed consent and understands the exclusion criteria. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last three months.

A 35 year old female patient complains of chronic constipation, with less than 3 bowel movements per week for the past 12 weeks. She reports straining during more than 25% of her bowel movements, and lumpy or hard stools during more than 25% of her bowel movements. She also reports a sensation of incomplete evacuation during more than 25% of her bowel movements. She has no history of loose or watery stools, and she has not been diagnosed with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). She has not undergone any GI tract surgery or any other clinically significant medical or surgical history that could limit her ability to complete or participate in the clinical trial or confound the study assessments. She is willing to comply with the Interactive voice response System (IVRS).

The patient is a 14 year-old adolescent diagnosed with type 1 diabetes three years ago. She is currently on insulin therapy and her HbA1c is within the target range. She has no other known medical conditions and is not taking any other medication. She is physically active and participates in sports at school. She has a BMI in the normal range for her age and height. She has no family history of cardiovascular disease.

60F with a history of heavy smoking (40 pack-year history), was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the lung 6 months ago. She underwent resection of the primary tumor, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy (cisplatin and pemetrexed) and radiation therapy. However, recent imaging studies have revealed metastatic disease to the liver and bones. She has already received one line of palliative chemotherapy and an EGFR inhibitor as she has an EGFR driver mutation. She is currently experiencing pain in her bones, fatigue, and mild dyspnea on exertion. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. Her recent pulmonary function tests revealed an FEV1 of 1.2L (45% predicted) and a TLCO of 40%. She has no history of autoimmune disease or interstitial lung disease. She is willing to undergo lung SBRT to treat part of a lung lesion and to receive pembrolizumab in combination to further palliate her condition. She has adequate organ function, and her tissue sample is available for the study. She is willing to provide informed consent for the trial. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive within the next 120 days. She is willing to use two methods of birth control or be surgically sterile during the trial and for 120 days after the last dose of study medication. She has not received any investigational medicinal products or used any investigational devices within the past 4 weeks. She has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, or anti-Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) antibody. She has no evidence of active central nervous system (CNS) metastases or carcinomatous meningitis. She has no history of psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with her participation in the trial. She has no history of HIV, HIV 1/2 antibodies, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for the past 5 years. He currently takes daily opioids for pain management, which is not providing adequate relief. He is also experiencing some anxiety and depression related to his pain and feels that it is taking a toll on his quality of life. He has not had any prior experience with meditation but is willing to try a new approach to managing his pain. He is fluent in English and has the ability to feel warm and cold temperature sensations in both hands. He is not currently pregnant and does not have any pre-existing delusional, bipolar, or borderline personality disorders.

52-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with intermittent chest pain for the past 24 hours. EKG showed ST depression in leads V1-V6 and troponin levels were elevated. The patient was diagnosed with a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and treated with aspirin, heparin, and nitroglycerin. The patient has been stable on initial medical therapy for the past 24 hours and has been pain-free for 6 hours prior to enrollment in the clinical trial. The patient has no history of asthma or liver disease and has normal liver enzymes. The patient does not have a history of recurrent chest pain since hospitalization and is not on an IV nitroglycerin drip. The patient is eager to participate in the study and sign the necessary consent forms.

45-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis for the past 8 months. She has tried topical treatments and phototherapy with limited success. Her psoriasis has affected approximately 20% of her body surface area and she has a PASI score of 18 and a sPGA score of 3. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or other autoimmune diseases. She has not had a clinically significant flare of psoriasis in the past 12 weeks. She has no history of congestive heart failure, cerebro-cardiovascular events, or serious bleeding events. She has no active systemic infections and has tested negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to biologic therapies. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of subcutaneous SHR-1314 for the treatment of her psoriasis.

The patient is a 28-year-old sexually active male who is uncircumcised and interested in getting circumcised for personal reasons. He has no history of sexually transmitted infections and is in a monogamous relationship with his partner. He has no known allergies and takes no medications. He has a normal penile anatomy and no penile diseases. The patient is willing to follow the hygiene and wound care instructions and agrees to have swab samples taken during the trial. He understands the study procedures and requirements and agrees to abstain from sexual intercourse for 6 weeks post device removal and masturbation for 2 weeks post device removal. He agrees to return to the health care facility for follow-up visits as instructed. The patient is willing to have anonymous video and photographs taken of the procedure and follow-up visits.

This is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection two years ago. He has been on first-line antiretroviral therapy (ART) that includes a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) and two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs). Recently, he has experienced a rising viral load, with at least two consecutive measurements above 500 copies/mL, despite adhering to his treatment regimen. As a result, he has been referred to participate in a clinical trial called D²EFT, which aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of two different second-line ART regimens. He will be randomly allocated to receive either dolutegravir and darunavir/ritonavir or dolutegravir and two prespecified NRTIs, or the standard of care regimen of two NRTIs plus a ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitor. The trial will last for 96 weeks and he will be followed up at weeks 4, 12, 24, 48, and 96. The study will also collect data on the cost-effectiveness of the different regimens, medication adherence, viral loads, safety, and quality of life data. He will need to provide written informed consent and meet certain eligibility criteria, including having failed first-line NNRTI + 2N(t)RTI combination therapy according to virological criteria, being aged 16 years or older, and having laboratory variables within specified ranges. He will also need to be willing to use appropriate contraception if he is a woman of child-bearing potential.

10 year old male with occasional constipation presents for a clinical trial on the efficacy of pea hull fiber. The patient denies any known food allergies and is not currently taking any medication for diarrhea. The patient has not taken antibiotics within the past four weeks and is willing to discontinue probiotic supplements for a minimum of two weeks prior to the study. The patient is willing to consume pea hull fiber and control snacks daily for two-week periods and complete daily questionnaires and bi-weekly GSRS assessments throughout the entire 8-week study. The patient is also willing to be interviewed for the Automated Self-Administered 24-Hour-Kids-2014 (ASA24-Kids-2014) one time per 2-week period throughout the study. The patient and their legal guardian are willing and able to provide a valid social security number for study payment purposes.

The patient is a 22-year-old male who regularly uses cannabis and has been diagnosed with dependence on the drug. He has no history of dependence on other substances or alcoholism. He is generally healthy with no known CNS disease or history of head injury with loss of consciousness. He is not pregnant, and has no history of infection that might affect the CNS. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between genetics and the psychogenic effects of cannabis in vulnerable individuals. He is willing to undergo brain imaging procedures in order to measure THC-induced dopamine release and provide genetic information related to neurotransmitters dopamine (D2, DAT, COMT), GABA, glutamate and the cannabinoid receptor CB1. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study, and has provided informed consent.

A 28-year-old male, originally from a malaria-endemic region in sub-Saharan Africa, is seeking medical care for a routine check-up. He is currently residing in a non-endemic area and has not traveled to any malaria-endemic areas in the past year. He denies any symptoms of malaria, such as fever, chills, headache, or body aches. His medical history is unremarkable, and he takes no medications. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His physical examination is normal, and he has a body weight of 70 kg. Blood tests reveal a positive result for P. falciparum monoinfection with a parasite density of 400/µL. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets all the eligibility criteria of the study, including being able to swallow oral medication and having no contraindications for the study drugs. He signs the informed consent document and agrees to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

This is a 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (PD) for 9 years. He has tried various medications to control his symptoms, including levodopa, but is experiencing complications and side effects. His UPDRS score improves by 40% after taking his morning dose of levodopa. He is interested in participating in the double-blind placebo surgery trial to potentially improve his quality of life and reduce his symptoms. He has no history of epilepsy, brain surgery, severe depression, or other neurological disorders. He is in overall good health and has no medical contraindications for surgery. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study for its full duration.

The patient is a 55-year-old female diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer. She has been experiencing chronic pelvic pain for the past 6 months despite being on various oral analgesic medications. The pain is described as sharp, stabbing, and intermittent with a severity score of 7/10 on a visual analog scale. The patient has reported side effects of nausea, vomiting, and constipation from the oral analgesics. She has no history of bleeding disorders or mental disabilities. The patient understands and consents to the experimental nature of the trial and is willing to undergo superior hypogastric plexus chemical neurolysis with added pulsed radiofrequency neuromodulation at S3 nerve root.

The patient is a 32-year-old French-speaking woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. She has been experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past 6 months and has a BDI II score of 15. She has been prescribed medication for her depression but has not noticed any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of physical activity on depressive symptoms. She reports that she is physically able to perform active walking and has an IPAQ score of 400. She does not have any history of alcohol or substance dependence, psychotic disorders, or anti-social personality. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is hoping that the physical activity program will help improve her mood and quality of life.

A 25-year-old healthy female presents for a clinical trial investigating the bioequivalence of olmesartan medoxomil tablets. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. The patient reports no allergies and is able to swallow medication without difficulty. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use an effective form of contraception throughout the study period. The patient is fully informed of the study risks and procedures and provides written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently experiencing an expanding annular lesion on her leg. She recently spent time in wooded and grassy areas where Lyme disease is endemic. She has no history of diabetes, cancer, autoimmune diseases, or severe skin diseases such as psoriasis or atopic dermatitis. She has not taken oral corticosteroids in the past two weeks and has not used investigational drugs in the past month. She is not currently on any anticoagulation medication and has not experienced excessive bleeding after cuts or procedures in the past. The patient is willing and able to give her consent to participate in the study. She will undergo between 2 and 4 punch skin biopsies of the affected area and will return for 4 follow-up visits over the course of a year. She will also complete two health questionnaires and receive therapy for Lyme disease if necessary. The patient will be compensated for her time and inconvenience.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by a neurologist. The child has mild-to-moderate symptoms of ASD, with delayed language development, difficulty with social interactions, and repetitive behaviors. The child is currently not taking any medication for ASD or its comorbid conditions. The parent/guardian is willing to participate in the study and able to be present for all consultations. The child has no history of organic brain damage, meningitis, epilepsy, or encephalitis. The child has not been on conventional medication such as Fluoxetine, Methylphenidate, Atomoxetine, or Risperidal for less than 2 months or used any new medication for ASD or its comorbid conditions for the duration of the study. The child is eligible for the study and will be assessed using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) and Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist (ATEC) measures at each consultation, receive an individualized homoeopathic remedy, and be monitored for 12 weeks.

A 67-year-old male patient was referred by his neurologist for a clinical trial involving Parkinson's disease. He was diagnosed with PD five years ago and has been on a stable regimen of dopaminergic medication for the past three months. He reports experiencing tremors, stiffness, and difficulty with balance and walking, which have led to impairments in his daily activities. He reports no history of psychiatric or medical conditions other than PD, and is not taking any psychoactive medications. He is able to independently walk for 6 minutes and has no known holes or fissures in the skull, metallic objects or implanted devices in the skull, or injuries or surgeries that cause unusual gait. He scored 28 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and does not experience freezing of gait. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for PD.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing pain and discomfort in his jaw for several months. He has difficulty opening his mouth fully and experiences a clicking sound when he chews. The patient has a history of dental work and has been diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder (TMD) by a dentist. He has not received any treatment for his TMD yet and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of different physiotherapy practices in TMD. The patient does not have any neurological or psychiatric conditions, dental or orofacial infections, and does not have any other diseases diagnosed in the shoulder and neck areas. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 20-month-old girl who has had a history of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in the past. She is healthy and has no chronic illnesses or suspected immunodeficiencies. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in the study. The patient has not received any immunoglobulins, monoclonal antibodies, blood products, or ribavirin in the past 3 months, nor has she received any investigational RSV vaccines. The patient has not had any nasal obstructions due to anatomic or structural causes, acute or chronic rhinosinusitis, or any other causes. The patient is seropositive to RSV, as defined by a serum neutralizing antibody titer above the threshold described in the study's analytical plan. The patient meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 15. He has been on insulin pump therapy for the past 5 years and is currently using Lispro U100. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He finds it challenging to estimate the carbohydrate content of his meals accurately and often experiences postprandial hyperglycemia. He does not have any significant complications related to diabetes, such as neuropathy or retinopathy. He has never experienced severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia requiring hospitalization. He does not take any medication that affects gastric emptying, such as Motilium, Victoza, Ozempic, Trulicity, Byetta, or Symlin. He is not allergic to any of the trial products. He is willing to participate in the trial and understands the study's requirements. He has a nearby third party who can assist him in case of severe hypoglycemia. He does not plan to travel more than 3 hours away from Montreal during the trial period.

A 32-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder (AUD) presents seeking treatment for his addiction. He reports having a minimum of 5 years of heavy drinking, consuming at least 5 drinks per day on 5 different days per month. He has a preference for alcohol as his drug of choice and is seeking treatment for his AUD. He has been diagnosed with alcohol dependence as per DSM-IV criteria. He has no major psychiatric disorders that required hospitalization or daily medications for over 4 weeks in the past year. He reports no chronic use of medications that may affect study results or brain function. He has no major medical problems that can impact brain function or the use of a ketogenic diet. He has not experienced head trauma with loss of consciousness for more than 30 minutes. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no ferromagnetic objects in his body that are contraindicated for MRI of the head and is able to lie comfortably flat on his back for up to 2 hours in the MRI scanner. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

45 year-old male with a history of hypertension and elevated fasting blood glucose levels. The patient has been experiencing occasional headaches and fatigue. He has a BMI of 29 and a waist circumference of 102 cm. The patient is not currently on any medication for his blood pressure or glucose levels. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or any other significant medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of Valsartan on insulin sensitivity.

42-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma in the thigh with a tumor size of 8 cm. The biopsy results revealed a grade 2/3 (FNCLCC) tumor. The patient has no history of previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He is otherwise healthy with a normal bone marrow, liver, and renal function. His Karnofsky index is 90%. The tumor is deep and located outside the compartment. The patient is being considered for participation in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy trial using EIA (etoposide 125 mg/m2 iv days 1 and 4, ifosfamide 1500 mg/m2 iv days 1 - 4, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 day 1, pegfilgrastim 6 mg sc day 5), followed by local surgery and radiotherapy, and additional 4 cycles of adjuvant EIA. The patient will undergo MRI and CT scans and FDG-PET to assess the treatment response.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis for the past 10 years. The psoriasis covers approximately 5% of her body, including her arms, legs, and torso. She has tried various topical treatments in the past, but has not achieved satisfactory results. She is willing to avoid prolonged exposure of the treatment area to ultraviolet radiation and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She has not received any investigational drugs or devices within the past 60 days and is not concurrently participating in another clinical study. She provides both verbal and written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55 year old man presents to the emergency department with chest pain that radiates to his left arm and jaw. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. His ECG shows ST-elevation and he is diagnosed with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction. He is treated with aspiration of thrombus and primary PCI in the infarct related coronary artery. He has no signs of infection, pulmonary embolism, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, arrhythmias, abnormal renal and/or liver function, autoimmune disease, or malignant disease. He consents to participate in the study, and his demographic variables are recorded. Intracoronary thrombus is retrieved by standard aspiration catheter, washed with saline and stored on formalin. The composition and characteristics of the coronary thrombi with respect to cell types, genetic expression, and presence of specific markers of inflammation, platelet activity, endothelial activation, coagulation and fibrinolysis will be investigated in relation to the levels of these markers in the general circulation. The mRNA expression of selected signal molecules will also be performed. Peripheral venous blood samples will be drawn and analyzed for signaling molecules and corresponding mRNA expression in circulating leukocytes.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of advanced adenomas and high-grade dysplasia detected on a recent colonoscopy. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He is willing to participate in the study and provide mandatory tissue for research purposes. The patient has a negative pregnancy test result and his hemoglobin, platelet count, white blood cell count, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, total bilirubin, serum calcium, and serum creatinine are all within normal limits for the institution/lab. He underwent colonoscopy 40 days prior to randomization and all adenomas or polyps >= 2 mm in size were removed. The patient is not diagnosed with colon heritable cancer syndrome (familial adenomatous polyposis [FAP], hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer [HNPCC]) or inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis). He is able to swallow pills and has no bleeding diathesis. The patient has no history of current or prior rectal cancer, and no history of pelvic or rectal radiation therapy. He has no history of invasive carcinoma =< 5 years, except subjects with Dukes A/B1 carcinoma =< 5 years prior to pre-registration or any stage of colon cancer if >= 3 years post surgical resection. The patient is not on non-study investigational agent(s) =< 3 months prior to randomization and has not undergone chemotherapy =< 6 months prior to randomization. He has not used regular NSAIDs =< 6 weeks prior to randomization, defined as a frequency of 7 consecutive days (1 week) for > 3 weeks (Exception: low dose aspirin [81 mg] for those subjects who are chronic users of aspirin prior to the beginning of the study).

This clinical trial aims to evaluate the clinical performances of two different nano-hybrid resin composite systems used for anterior diastema closure and tooth reshaping at 4 years. The study is being conducted at Hacettepe University in Ankara, Turkey and is approved by the Ethical Committee of Ministry of Health. The trial requires 23 patients who are at least 18 years old, physically and psychologically able to tolerate conventional restorative procedures, and have no active periodontal or pulpal diseases. Patients must be willing to return for follow-up examinations as outlined by the investigators. The trial excludes patients with uncontrolled parafunction, insufficient oral hygiene leading to caries lesions more than twice yearly during the previous 2 years, those who are pregnant or nursing, and those with periodontal or gingival disease. The selected patients will receive 76 direct composite resin restorations for maxillary anterior midline or multi-diastema problems. The teeth to be restored will be cleaned with pumice-water slurry using a rubber cup, and the appropriate shade of restorative material will be selected using a standard VITAPAN Classic shade guide. The surfaces to be restored will be etched using 35% phosphoric or orthophosphoric acid for 30 s according to the restorative system used. Nano-hybrid resin composite systems to be used on each patient will be randomly selected. The esthetic, functional and biological properties of the restorations will be evaluated at baseline, 1-2-3 and 4 years using FDI Criteria establishing a score-range of 1-5.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has been experiencing neuropathy symptoms for the past 6 months. He reports numbness and tingling in both feet and has noticed a decrease in his balance and walking ability. He is retired and lives alone. He does not regularly exercise but tries to maintain a healthy diet. He has no history of foot or lower limb surgery, neurological or rheumatologic diseases. He has not received any physiotherapy intervention or offloading devices for his neuropathy symptoms. His most recent HbA1c is 7.5%. He takes oral medication for his diabetes and hypertension. He reports no history of depression or anxiety. He is able to walk independently and does not use any walking aids. He is interested in participating in the trial to try to improve his balance, reduce his neuropathy symptoms and improve his gait.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 5 years. She experiences significant fatigue that has been impacting her daily activities and quality of life. She reports that the fatigue is not always correlated with her level of pain or disease activity. She takes methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine as prescribed by her rheumatologist. She has no other serious physical or mental illnesses. She is willing to participate in a longitudinal study to explore factors that may influence her fatigue over time.

A 30-year-old non-smoking female with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and a weight of 60 kg has provided informed consent to participate in the AZD1981 Midazolam CYP4503A Induction Study. She has no clinically significant disease or disorder and has no abnormal findings in her physical examination, clinical chemistry, haematology, urinalysis, vital signs, or ECG at baseline. She has not taken any medication for the past 2 weeks prior to the study. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for all study visits.

Pt is a 55yo male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 10 years ago. He is currently managed with metformin and glipizide, and his HbA1c is 7.5%. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, but his father had a myocardial infarction at the age of 65. He is compliant with his medications and has no known allergies. He has no history of claustrophobia or ferromagnetic materials in his body. His carotid ultrasound plaque thickness was found to be 1.2 mm on a routine exam last year. He has no history of pancreatitis, severe renal disease, or gastrointestinal disease. He is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage III nasopharyngeal carcinoma. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for a palpable lymph node in the neck. Her liver and renal function tests are normal with no signs of any other severe intercurrent disease. She has no allergies to any related drugs. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. She is expected to receive gemcitabine (1000mg/m² d1,8) and cisplatin (80mg/m², d1) every 3 weeks for 2 cycles before radiotherapy. After induction chemotherapy, intensity modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) will be administered with a total dose of GTVnx 70Gy, GTVnd 66Gy, CTV1 60Gy and CTV2 54Gy for 33 times in total, concurrently with gemcitabine. She will be followed up with nasopharyngeal endoscopy and magnetic resonance imaging for 1 year, 2 years, and 3 years after radiotherapy to evaluate the curative effect. Additionally, chest CT, abdominal B-ultrasound, bone scan or PETCT examinations will be reviewed to exclude distant metastases. Biopsy diagnosis will be performed for patients suspected of local residual and recurrence.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He has been receiving lenalidomide maintenance for the past 6 months. He complains of frequent diarrhea, which has been graded as grade 1 according to the CTCAE 5.0 criteria. He has been experiencing this diarrhea for at least 4 out of 7 days for the past 3 weeks. He has lost about 3kg of weight due to the diarrhea. He has no history of bowel obstruction or hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis.
