He has not used any bile acid sequestrant drugs for the treatment of diarrhea. He is not currently experiencing any infections. He is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 19-year-old female student was admitted to the emergency room after a suicide attempt by overdose of sleeping pills. She had a history of depression and anxiety and had been seeing a therapist for the past year. She reported feeling overwhelmed by school work and family expectations. She was raised by a single mother who struggled with alcoholism and had a history of abusive relationships. Her father left the family when she was young and she had no contact with him. She had no previous suicide attempts and no history of substance abuse. She agreed to participate in the study and provided informed consent. Her mother also agreed to participate as an informant.

Family of 5 living in a rural area in Northern Senegal, with the father being the primary milk supplier to the local milk factory. The family consists of parents and three children, aged 3, 6 and 9. The 3-year-old child is eligible for the study and will be included. The family has limited access to healthcare and experiences food insecurity, with the children's diet lacking in essential micronutrients. The 3-year-old child has been diagnosed with anemia and has been receiving sporadic treatment at a local health clinic. The family has agreed to participate in the study and receive daily micronutrient-fortified yogurts for their 3-year-old child. The study will assess whether the provision of fortified yogurts can improve the child's anemia and whether it can incentivize the milk supplier to increase their milk delivery to the milk factory. The family is excited to participate in the study and hopes that it will improve their child's health and nutritional status.

This study is seeking participants who have tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and have been diagnosed with Covid-19 disease. The patient must be at least 18 years of age and have had positive PCR tests from nasal/throat swabs as well as samples from the deep respiratory tract during the period from January 1st, 2020 to July 31st, 2020. There are no specific exclusion criteria for this study. This study aims to evaluate the pathways of delirium outcome in Covid-19 patients, so if you have experienced delirium as a result of Covid-19, you may be an ideal candidate for this trial. By participating in this study, you will be helping to further the understanding of Covid-19 and its effects on the body, which will ultimately help to improve the care and treatment of Covid-19 patients in the future.

A 35-year old female office worker has been experiencing compulsive buying episodes for the past year. She has accumulated a significant amount of credit card debt due to her impulsive shopping behavior. She tends to buy things she doesn't need or can't afford, and she feels guilty and ashamed afterward. She has tried to control her spending by creating budgets and avoiding shopping malls, but it has been unsuccessful. She is currently single and lives alone in an apartment. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and she doesn't smoke. She has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension that is controlled with medication. She has no previous history of seizures or psychiatric disorders, and her Beck Depression Inventory score is below 30. She is currently not on any medications or psychotherapy for compulsive buying. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help her control her shopping behavior.

A 25-year-old female presents to an allergy clinic with complaints of seasonal allergies. She has been experiencing symptoms of sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes, and throat for the past 3 years during the ragweed pollen season. She has tried over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal sprays, but they only provide temporary relief. On examination, she has clear nasal discharge, pale nasal mucosa, and bilateral conjunctival injection. Skin prick testing reveals a positive reaction to short ragweed extract. Her blood and urine analyses are within normal limits. She has never received allergy immunotherapy. She is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the trial period. Her lung function test shows a predicted value of 90%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of ragweed mix given by intralymphatic node injections.

A 32-year-old male with a history of non-seminomatous GCT was diagnosed with relapsed disease after completing first-line cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy. The patient underwent two cycles of HDCT and PBSCT as salvage treatment, with normal or declining tumor markers at the time of screening. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 0 and last dose of HDCT was administered 10 weeks ago. The patient's lab values meet the eligibility criteria for the trial. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to etoposide, no active infection requiring systemic therapy, and no current evidence of any condition or therapy that might confound the results of the trial. The patient is willing to use two forms of contraception and comply with study requirements.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago and has been on hormone therapy since then. He recently underwent a biopsy that showed progression of the cancer, indicating that the hormone therapy is no longer effective. He has no history of other significant medical problems and has a life expectancy of at least 24 weeks. He is castrate, having undergone surgical castration. He has not received any prior systemic therapy for his prostate cancer. He experiences occasional pain in his lower back and hips. He is a retired accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His PSA level is 25 ng/mL.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from plaque psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and lotions, but they have not provided any significant relief. Her psoriasis affects her elbows, knees, and lower back, and she experiences occasional itching and redness. She is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. She has not received any topical or UVB therapy within the past 2 weeks or systemic retinoids, etanercept, adalimumab, or efalizumab within the past 3 months. She is not currently on any other topical agents or immunosuppressives. She is interested in participating in this study to explore a new treatment option for her psoriasis.

Patient is a 30-year-old female with a history of a deep cavity in the lower left first molar, causing severe pain and discomfort. The tooth has been diagnosed with irreversible pulpitis and requires root canal treatment. The patient has no known systemic diseases or allergies to local anesthetics or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She has not taken any analgesics in the past seven days or any other medications prior to presenting for treatment. The patient has not undergone any previous root canal treatment or received any antibiotic prophylaxis. There is no evidence of an open tooth apex or pacemaker use. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to compare the incidence and intensity of post-obturation pain, evaluate the overextension of filling material radiographically, and assess the relationship between pain and analgesic intake in patients with vital and devital teeth undergoing carrier-based obturation with two different sealers (iRoot SP, AH Plus).

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer four months ago. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He underwent a prostatectomy and is currently undergoing radiation therapy. The patient reports experiencing fatigue and occasional nausea. He is able to perform his daily activities but has had to reduce his work hours due to the treatment. The patient is otherwise in good health and has no other medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study to help identify blood markers that could potentially aid in the development of immunotherapy treatments for cancer. The patient has provided informed consent and will undergo blood sample collection for analysis.

A 24-year-old male presents to the dental clinic with a complaint of sensitivity to hot and cold beverages in the lower left side of his mouth. He reports no pain or discomfort while chewing or biting. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Clinical examination reveals a large carious lesion on the distal surface of the mandibular left first molar, extending to the occlusal surface. The tooth is vital and not mobile. Radiographic evaluation confirms the presence of the carious lesion extending close to the pulp, but with no signs of periapical pathology. The patient is diagnosed with a deep carious lesion in the mandibular left first molar that requires vital pulp capping. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial since he is an adult in good general health, has an active carious lesion deep into the dentin involving occlusal/incisal and/or proximal surfaces of a permanent tooth, and has no clinical symptoms of irreversible pulpitis or periapical pathology.

A 14-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating an alternative method for oral glucose tolerance testing. She has no prior history of intestinal surgery, and her CF team confirms that she is not currently experiencing an active flare. She has not been on steroids and has no known allergies or intolerances to dextrose, fructose, or corn derivatives. She is able to tolerate oral feedings and has no other medical conditions. Her parents have provided written consent for her participation in the study.

56-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of stage IIB breast cancer. She has undergone neoadjuvant treatment and is scheduled for surgical resection of the tumor(s) within approximately 7 days following the [F-18]CP-18 PET/CT scan. She has an adequate size breast tumor (≥1.0 cm) that should be amenable to imaging. Her tumor tissue is obtainable following surgery in order to perform immunohistochemistry staining using caspase 3 and/or other apoptosis biomarkers. She has a previous baseline (pre-neoadjuvant treatment) diagnostic imaging exam including but not limited to MRI, CT, mammography, or [F-18] FDG PET/CT scan that identifies breast tumor location. Her renal function values as defined by laboratory results are within the following ranges: Serum creatinine ≤ 2x institutional upper limits of normal and BUN < 2X institutional upper limits of normal. She is capable of complying with study procedures and has provided written informed consent. She is not nursing or pregnant, has not been involved in an investigative, radioactive research procedure within the past 14 days, and does not have any other condition or personal circumstance that, in the judgment of the investigator, might interfere with the collection of complete data or data quality.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman is scheduled to undergo an elective cesarean section. She is in good health and has not had any major medical issues in the past. She is currently 38 weeks pregnant with a singleton pregnancy. She has not had any complications during her pregnancy and her baby is estimated to be of normal weight. She has never had any allergic reactions to medications and has not been diagnosed with any neurological conditions. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve pain management during her cesarean delivery.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male, retired, with no significant past medical history, presented to his primary care physician for a routine checkup. He has a family history of colon cancer in his father, diagnosed at age 65, and his paternal uncle, diagnosed at age 58. He has never undergone colon cancer screening and reports no symptoms related to his digestive system. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 27, and he reports no significant changes in his weight over the last year. He has access to the internet, is fluent in English, and reports no difficulty reading. He is interested in participating in clinical research and is willing to complete all study requirements through the study website: http://HealthStudy.wustl.edu.

The patient is a 56 year-old man who has been diagnosed with advanced neuroendocrine cancer. His cancer has been histologically or cytologically confirmed to be low or intermediate grade carcinoid or islet cell carcinoma. He has measurable disease, defined as at least one lesion that can be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded) as >= 20 mm with conventional techniques or as >= 10 mm with spiral CT scan. He has not received any prior systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy for his cancer. He has not received prior bevacizumab or any other therapy targeting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) or VEGF receptors (i.e., SU11248, PTK787/ZK222584, Sorafenib, GW786034). He is on a stable dose of somatostatin analogue for 2 months prior to start of protocol. He has not received prior interferon (not counted toward prior cytotoxic chemotherapy). He has unresectable or metastatic disease. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1 (Karnofsky >= 70%). His blood pressure is no greater than 140 mmHg (systolic) or 90 mmHg (diastolic) for eligibility. He has leukocytes >= 3,000/mcL, absolute neutrophil count >= 1,500/mcL, platelets >= 120,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal institutional limits, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase [SGOT])/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase [SGPT]) =< 3.0 X institutional upper limit of normal, creatinine =< 2.0 OR creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 for patients with creatinine levels above institutional normal (calculated by Cockcroft Gault formula), prothrombin time (PT)/international normalized ratio (INR)/partial thromboplastin time (PTT) within 1.2 X the upper limit of normal. He has no known history of myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, admission for unstable angina, cardiac angioplasty or stenting within the last 12 weeks and has asymptomatic class II heart failure. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident (CVA) within the last 6 months and no history of venous thrombosis in the last 12 weeks. He has no serious or non

A 14-year-old healthy Filipino boy comes to the clinic for his routine check-up. He is a student and is in good health with no underlying disease. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He is up-to-date on all his vaccinations and has not had any adverse reactions to any vaccines in the past. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. His past surgical history is insignificant. He is not on any medications. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. His parents are literate and have provided their consent for him to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male with a body mass index within 20% of his ideal weight. He has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, endogenous, gastrointestinal, hematologic, neurologic or hemorrhagic disease. He has not taken any prescription drugs in the 14 days immediately prior to starting the study that had the potential to interact with the study medication. He is not currently using any substance that could induce or inhibit drug metabolism enzymes. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who recently suffered a spinal cord injury at the T12 level after a car accident. He is currently receiving in-patient care on the rehabilitation ward and is expected to be admitted for at least 4 weeks. He has no prior history of urinary tract infections and is generally in good health. His blood work shows normal renal function and he is not on any medications that would interact with cranberry capsules. He is willing to participate in the study and take the cranberry capsules as directed.

The patient is a 38-year-old female diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) two years ago. She has been on interferon beta-1a therapy, but her symptoms have continued to worsen. She currently experiences fatigue, numbness in her legs, and difficulty with coordination. Her Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score is 3.5. She is willing and able to receive at least 2 lumbar punctures as part of the study requirements. She has no comorbid conditions that preclude participation and is not infected with HIV. She has not been previously treated with cladribine and has not received treatment with natalizumab during the last 6 months. She has not received immunosuppressive or myelosuppressive therapy, and does not have moderate or severe hepatic or renal impairment. She is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during cladribine tablets dosing and for 6 months after the last dose in each treatment course. She is not intending to breastfeed on a cladribine tablet treatment day and/or during the 10 days after the last cladribine tablet dose.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is currently 20 weeks pregnant with her first child. She had a routine ultrasound at 18 weeks which showed abnormal uterine artery Doppler with a mean pulsatility index (PI) of 1.8. She is concerned about the potential risks to her baby and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce the risk of fetal growth restriction (FGR). The patient has a history of well-controlled asthma, for which she uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. She has no known allergies and takes no medications other than prenatal vitamins. The patient has no family history of pregnancy complications or fetal growth restriction. She has never smoked and does not use recreational drugs. The patient is married and works as a teacher. She is excited about her pregnancy and is eager to participate in research that could help her baby.

A 42 year old active-duty Air Force member presents with a history of hypertension and a BMI of 28. She reports a family history of heart disease and diabetes but has not been diagnosed with either condition herself. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the impact of genetic test information and health coaching on reducing her risk for these conditions. She has internet access and is willing to provide informed consent. She has had a physical exam within the last 12 months that included blood pressure, height, weight, fasting blood glucose, and lipid panel. Her fasting blood glucose and triglycerides were found to be slightly elevated, but she has not been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes or coronary heart disease. She is not expected to deploy in the upcoming 6 months and has no chronic conditions that would significantly affect study outcomes.

The patient is a 26-year-old Hispanic male who has been using amphetamines for the past 3 years. He started using amphetamines to enhance his academic performance in college but eventually developed a dependence on the drug. He currently uses amphetamines at least once a week. He has a history of depression and anxiety and has been on medication for the past year to manage his symptoms. He works as a freelance graphic designer and is currently living with his girlfriend. He has completed college and has a bachelor's degree in graphic design. He has normal vision and hearing and has no contraindications for magnetic resonance imaging. He is willing to cooperate with the completion of the questionnaire evaluation and follow-up evaluation. His Mind

A 47-year-old woman with a history of ovarian cancer presents with recurrent disease that was previously treated with a platinum-based chemotherapy regimen. She has undergone surgery 3 weeks ago, and her oncologist recommends enrolling her in a clinical trial that involves a combination of liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and benign uterine fibroids. Her vital signs are within the normal range, and she is in good physical condition. Her physical exam is unremarkable, and there is no evidence of ascites or lymphadenopathy. Her recent CT scan shows measurable disease with a largest lesion of 3cm. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has no other prior cancer therapy that would preclude study therapy. She has a good performance status and a life expectancy that is not specified.

A 35-year-old male veteran who served in Operation Iraqi Freedom is seeking treatment for Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). He reports experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and anxiety related to his military service. He has been diagnosed with PTSD by a mental health professional and his PTSD Checklist (PCL) score is greater than or equal to 50. He has a supportive family, including his wife and two young children, who are willing to participate in the study. They have daily contact and are interested in learning how to better support him. The family has access to a computer and internet, and are willing to take the online educational training and surveys. The veteran is open to participating in the study and hopes to gain some tools to better manage his PTSD symptoms.

Patient is a 14-year-old boy with a history of sickle cell disease who presented to the emergency department with severe pain in his legs and back. The patient reports that the pain began two days ago and has been getting progressively worse. He has been taking his home pain medication regimen, but it has not been providing adequate relief. The patient has a history of multiple vaso-occlusive crises and has been hospitalized several times in the past year. He has been compliant with his medications and follow-up appointments with his hematologist. The patient is currently using a demand PCA for pain control and is able to tolerate oral pain medications. The patient's sleep habits have been poor due to pain and discomfort, and he often experiences disrupted sleep. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with the assigned arm of the study. The patient and his parent speak English fluently.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with stage II colorectal cancer and is scheduled for radical colon cancer surgery (CME). He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloody stools for the past few months. His BMI is 26 and his ASA score is II. He has not received any radiotherapy or chemotherapy before the operation. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. He is able to describe his symptoms objectively and is able to follow the study's follow-up plan.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer four months ago after she noticed a lump in her left breast. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed infiltrating ductal carcinoma, ER/PR-positive and HER2-negative. Imaging studies showed multiple lung and liver metastases. She was started on chemotherapy with Taxol (paclitaxel) every three weeks and has completed two cycles so far. The patient experienced some side effects from the Taxol, including hair loss, fatigue, and mild neuropathy. She has no history of other malignancies and is otherwise healthy. She has a negative serum pregnancy test and uses birth control. She has signed informed consent for the study and is willing to be randomized to receive either Taxol or ABI-007. She is hopeful that the new formulation of paclitaxel will be more effective and have fewer side effects.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He has no history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy. His cancer has been staged as stage III. He is in good health with a performance status of 1. He does not have any concurrent malignancies or a history of other malignancies. His bone marrow function is normal, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2.0x109/L and platelets of 120x109/L. His liver and renal function are also normal, with a serum bilirubin and serum transaminase levels less than twice the upper limit of normal, and creatinine clearance of 85 ml/min. He does not have any serious co-morbidities. He is not allergic to cisplatin or capecitabine. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and has a good support system at home.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of high cholesterol and triglyceride levels. He has a family history of heart disease and is concerned about his risk for developing cardiovascular disease. He is currently taking simvastatin to manage his high cholesterol levels but has not seen a significant improvement. His diet consists of high-fat and high-carbohydrate foods, and he does not exercise regularly. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing to adhere to the American Heart Association (AHA) diet and utilize adequate birth control methods if needed. He has no plans to become pregnant or lactate. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to potentially improve his lipid levels and reduce his risk of developing heart disease.

A 30-year-old male with a genetically inherited disorder of extremely high cholesterol is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been diagnosed with Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia and has a family history of high cholesterol. He has not been taking any lipid-lowering medications and is not currently pregnant or lactating. He has no other medical conditions or laboratory abnormalities that could affect his safety during the trial.

54-year-old postmenopausal Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with osteoporosis and has not taken bisphosphonates or SERMS in the last two years. She has not taken estrogen replacement hormones in the past year and has not had a non-traumatic bone fracture within the last year. She has no significant uncontrolled cardiac, vascular, renal, pulmonary, endocrine or rheumatologic disease and has no history of malignancy. The patient is not anemic and does not have a significant history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is not currently taking any investigational drug and is not on any medications that interfere with metabolism or renal clearance of study drug, oral or systemic glucocorticoids of > 5 mg/day prednisone (or equivalent) over the past year or thiazide-type diuretics. The patient's screening labs (calcium, vit D and PTH, CBC) are normal. She weighs between 50 and 90 kilograms and is willing to participate in a 3-week daily subcutaneous injections of Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (1-36) study.

A 55-year-old female patient presents with a non-healing pressure ulcer on her sacrum. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. She has been receiving care for the ulcer for the past 4 months without any improvement. The ulcer is about 4 cm in diameter, has fibrinous tissue, and is less than 2 cm deep. The patient has an ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI) of 0.9. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial. She has no history of neuropathy or perforant ulcer of the foot, and is not pregnant or lactating.

A 45-year-old HIV-positive man comes to the clinic for a regular follow-up visit. He has been on a regimen of efavirenz (EFV), emtricitabine (FTC) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) for the past 8 months, and his viral load has been undetectable for the past 6 months. However, he has been experiencing moderate affective symptoms, including anxiety, irritability and sadness. He has no history of CNS opportunistic infections or active CNS infections, but he has a history of depression and anxiety. He reports no current significant substance abuse or dependence and/or heavy alcohol use. He has an estimated glomerular filtration rate (EGFR) of 75 ml/min. He agrees to switch to a new integrase inhibitor, elvitegravir (EVG) boosted with cobicistat (COBI), given as the EVG/COBI/FTC/TDF Single Tablet Regimen (STR), for the purpose of the study. He does not have any metallic implants or claustrophobia, and does not have any medical conditions or medications that significantly affect cerebral blood flow or function. He is willing to undergo advanced neuroimaging to assess the biological changes in the brain associated with EFV-based regimen and the switch to EVG-based regimen, as well as neuropsychological testing to evaluate changes in cognition, emotion, and sleep quality.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing voice changes for the past year. She describes her voice as hoarse and strained, and sometimes experiences vocal fatigue after prolonged speaking. She has been diagnosed with glottic insufficiency by an otolaryngologist and has completed a voice combination evaluation with a speech pathologist. The patient is able to comprehend and follow instructions well, and scores a 27 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) survey. She is fluent in English and meets the age requirement of being 18 years or older. The patient does not have any uncontrolled respiratory diseases or significant GI disease. She has not undergone gastroesophageal surgery or surgery for an abdominal hernia. The patient is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who underwent a total knee replacement surgery three months ago. He has been experiencing persistent pain, swelling, and drainage from the surgical site. After several medical consultations, the patient was diagnosed with a prosthetic joint infection (IPA) on his knee prosthesis. He is currently under medical care in the department of Infectious and Tropical Diseases. The patient did not object to participate in the study that aims to measure the quality of life of patients with IPA using the EQ-5D-3L validated quality of life questionnaire and the EVA scale. The patient is over 18 years of age and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. He has no psychological or psychiatric support outside the service, and he is not under any legal protection or participating in another study on measuring quality of life. The patient has no cognitive impairment that may affect his ability to understand the questionnaire.

A 30-year-old woman, currently a member of Kaiser Permanente Northwest, is considering pregnancy in the near future. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 30, which classifies her as obese. She has a computer with internet access and is fluent in English. She has not been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal disease, cancer, or renal disease that would require a special diet or medication. She has not undergone bariatric surgery or used prescription weight loss medications in the past three months. She is willing to participate in the Prepare study and understands the importance of a preconception weight loss program to improve her own health and the health of her future child.

This is a 62 year old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes who was hospitalized for community-acquired pneumonia. Despite appropriate antibiotic therapy, he developed sepsis, and his blood pressure dropped significantly, requiring vasopressor support with norepinephrine at a rate of 0.3microgram/kg/min. He has no history of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency and is not taking any serotonin modulator medication. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 31-year-old female office worker presents with acute non-specific low back pain for 3 weeks, without leg pain. She does not have a history of back pain. Her BMI is within the normal range. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She exercises occasionally and walks to work. She has no known allergies and is not on any medication. She speaks fluent English and can provide informed consent. She has not had any radiation exposure in the last 6 months and has not had any previous lumbar spine surgery or scoliosis. She has no diagnosed osteoporosis and is not pregnant. She has not received manual therapy for this episode of NSLBP. She has no history of depression or litigation.

A 42-year-old woman who lives in a rural area in the northeastern United States presents with a rash and flu-like symptoms. She recalls being bitten by a tick while hiking a week ago. The rash appeared a few days later and has since spread. She is experiencing fatigue, muscle aches, and headaches. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She does not use tobacco or illicit drugs and drinks alcohol only socially. She is a teacher at a local elementary school and is married with two children. She is concerned about the possibility of Lyme disease and seeks medical attention. She has not received any previous treatment for Lyme disease.

50-year-old male with a history of glaucoma and currently on medication to manage intraocular pressure. He has had regular check-ups with his ophthalmologist and his most recent visit showed visual field changes consistent with glaucomatous optic neuropathy. He has no history of eye surgery except for uncomplicated cataract surgery three years ago. He wears contact lenses for nearsightedness and is comfortable with contact lens use. He has no known allergies to silicone or ocular anesthesia. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and has been receiving transfusions of packed red blood cells (PRBC) for the past 6 months. She has an IPSS score of Low and an ECOG index of 1. She has no history of peripheral neurological disease and is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the mechanism of action of thalidomide. Her iron, B12 vitamin, and folic acid levels are all within normal limits. She has not received any intensive chemotherapy in the past 3 months and has not been treated with thalidomide in a previous protocol. She is willing to subject herself to regular clinical and biological follow-up throughout the study and is willing to take a contraceptive treatment for the duration of the study. She is willing to sign the informed consent and is not pregnant or in a period of lactation.

A 45 yo F who has been experiencing rectal bleeding and discomfort during bowel movements for the past 6 months. She has tried over-the-counter remedies with little relief. She has been referred to a surgical specialist department for further evaluation and treatment. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to participate in the study to help researchers better understand hemorrhoidal disease and its treatments.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rectal cancer and has undergone radiation therapy. She is experiencing severe pelvic radiation disease (PRD) symptoms, including rectal bleeding, pain, and difficulty with bowel movements. She has tried multiple conventional treatments, but none have been effective in managing her symptoms. She is in good physical condition with a WHO-performance status of 1. She does not have any bone metastases as confirmed by a bone scan. She is not pregnant and has no history of pregnancy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of systemic mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) injections for the treatment of severe and chronic PRD refractory to standard therapy. She understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old female who works in higher education and considers herself to be in good health. She has no pre-existing medical conditions and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and does not smoke or consume excessive amounts of caffeine. She has no relevant food intolerances/sensitivities and has not taken antibiotics within the past 4 weeks. She has no known active infections and does not suffer from frequent migraines or sleep disorders. She has access to the internet and has a bank account for payment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing the effects of a wild green oat extract on cognition and stress.

A 45-year old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) two years ago. She experiences joint pain, swelling and stiffness, especially in her fingers and wrists. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and Raynaud's syndrome. She lives with her husband and two children. She works part-time as a librarian but has had to cut back on her hours due to her RA. She is currently taking methotrexate 20mg a week and ibuprofen as needed for pain. She reports some improvement in her symptoms with methotrexate, but she still experiences pain and stiffness on most days. She is interested in participating in this study and willing to commit to attending all study visits. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding, and uses adequate contraception.

A 32 yo F with a BMI of 24 kg/m2 presents with a history of 3 failed IVF cycles despite transfer of good-quality embryos. She is a non-smoker and has no history of hypothyroidism. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no history of polycystic ovary syndrome or endometriosis. She has never been pregnant before and has not undergone any prior pregnancy termination. Her current male partner has no known medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of multiple doses of subcutaneous NT100 vs placebo following IVF in women with a history of repeated IVF failures.

A 35 year old woman came to the clinic with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 8 years. She has been taking oral antidiabetic medications for the past 2 years, including thiazolidinediones (TZDs), to control her blood sugar levels. She has a history of mandible fracture due to trauma and requires a bone graft surgery to repair it. She is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol and does not use any recreational drugs. Her blood glucose and HbA1c levels are well controlled with her current medication regimen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of TZDs on bone marrow differentiation and osteoblast formation.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with advanced adenocarcinoma of the stomach. He has no prior history of cancer and his performance status is 1. He has a measurable lesion according to RECIST criteria version 1.1. He has not received any prior chemotherapy and is not currently undergoing radiation therapy. His organ functions are adequate and he is expected to have a lifespan of more than 3 months. He has signed an informed consent indicating his awareness of the investigational nature of the study. He has no active infection or severe heart disease, but does have a history of controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He has not had any myocardial infarctions in the preceding 12 months and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have central nervous system metastases or peripheral sensory neuropathies with impaired functional activities. He does not have gastrointestinal obstruction or bleeding inducing mal-absorption of oral chemotherapeutic agents.

63-year-old male with a history of hypertension presented with shortness of breath, fatigue, and intermittent chest pain. The patient was diagnosed with severe mitral regurgitation secondary to posterior leaflet prolapse. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 45%, left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 6.2 cm, and a regurgitant volume of 80 ml. The patient was referred for surgical repair of the mitral valve. The patient underwent a successful repair with a bioprosthetic valve implantation. Postoperative echocardiography showed a residual regurgitant volume of 10 ml with good valve function. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in the study as a candidate for the creation of a patient-specific mitral valve model for surgical planning and training.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with probable Alzheimer's disease according to DSM-IV and NINCDS-ADRDA standard. He has been taking donepezil (10mg/day) for the past 6 months. His K-MMSE score at screening was 18. He lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no other significant medical history, and his physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any other abnormalities. His AST and ALT levels were within normal limits, and his hemoglobin and platelet counts were normal. He has no history of CNS disease, depression, schizophrenia, alcoholism, or drug addiction. He has no hearing or visual impairment. He is able to visit the hospital with his wife.

58 year old woman with a medical history significant for osteoarthritis of the hip and hypertension. The patient has been experiencing worsening hip pain over the past several years, and imaging studies have revealed significant joint damage. The decision has been made to undergo a total hip replacement surgery in the Orthopedic Surgery department of the CHU Amiens-Picardie. The patient has been informed about the possibility of donating residual human tissue fragments for basic science research, and has consented to participate in the study. The patient has tested negative for HIV and hepatitis.

A 10-year-old child is brought in by their parents for assessment due to concerns about anxiety and behavioral problems. The child struggles with social interactions, often feeling nervous and overwhelmed in new situations, and has difficulty making and keeping friends. They also experience episodes of intense anger and frustration, sometimes leading to physical outbursts. The child's parents report that these issues are impacting the child's daily life and functioning, including their school performance and relationships with family members. The child is in 5th grade and attends a local public school. The family speaks Danish at home and the child is fluent in Danish. The child is not currently receiving any treatment for their symptoms and has not been previously diagnosed with any developmental or mental disorders. The family has agreed to participate in the study and signed informed consent forms. The child meets the inclusion criteria for the study, with scores on the SDQ indicating elevated levels of emotional and behavioral difficulties and functional impairment. The child and parents have identified anxiety and behavioral problems as the top problem to address in the study. The child is eligible for the study and will be randomized to either receive the Mind My Mind program or treatment as usual.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma 8 months ago. She has been on topical treatment with timolol and latanoprost. Her visual field defect has been stable for the last 3 months. She reports difficulties with reading and recognizing faces. Her past medical history is unremarkable except for mild hypertension, which is controlled with amlodipine 5 mg daily. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no known allergies. The patient is interested in participating in this trial and is willing to commit to daily eye yoga exercises for 4 weeks. She has no history of autoimmune diseases, neurological or mental diseases, diabetic retinopathy, addictions, or photosensitivity. She is not pregnant and has no history of retinitis pigmentosa or pathological nystagmus. Her blood pressure is well-controlled, with a measurement of 130/80 mmHg during her last visit.

A 50-year-old male with a history of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, diagnosed by histological findings, with multiple nodules and no invasion, who has refused open surgical treatment and is looking for alternative treatment options. He has failed first-line systemic therapy and is looking to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Levamisole Hcl in the treatment of patients with advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. He has a Child-Pugh liver function score of 6 and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1. He is negative for HBV DNA and has no other major organ dysfunction. He is willing to use reliable contraceptive methods during the trial and eight weeks after its completion. He has no history of alimentary tract hemorrhage or gastrointestinal bleeding, myocardial infarction, or poorly controlled arrhythmia. He has not been treated with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers in the past 28 days or has no history of psychotropic drug abuse. He has no other factors that are unsuitable for entering into the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease by her neurologist. She has a history of memory loss, difficulty with decision-making, and decreased ability to perform daily activities. She is currently taking donepezil to manage her symptoms. She lives with her daughter who is her primary caregiver. Her daughter has noticed that her mother's cognitive abilities have declined over the past year, and she is becoming increasingly forgetful. The patient has undergone an amyloid PET scan, which has confirmed the presence of amyloid plaques in her brain. She has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) score of 15 and a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) global score of 1.0. She has a responsible caregiver who will accompany her to all procedures. The patient has no significant neurologic or systemic disease, and her screening laboratory tests are normal. She is not currently taking any medications that may affect her immune system. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, and she does not have any major psychiatric disorders. She has no contraindications for the lumbar puncture procedure. She is postmenopausal and not currently taking hormone contraceptives. The patient's BMI is 28. She has no pacemaker, aneurysm clips, artificial heart valves, ear implants, metal fragments, or foreign objects in her eyes, skin, or body. She is willing to participate in the study and has the capacity to consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with bladder cancer. He underwent TURBT (Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumor) and the pathology report showed muscle-invasive bladder cancer. He is married with two children, and he is retired. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently on medication for both conditions. He is a former smoker, but he quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not excessively. He is concerned about the side effects of the surgery, particularly the impact on his urinary and sexual function. He has no history of prostate cancer or prostate-related symptoms. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo either prostate capsule sparing cystectomy or nerve-sparing radical cystoprostatectomy. He is able to read and write in English and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a confirmed clinical diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has a history of smoking for 30 years and has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for the past 5 years. He has been prescribed domiciliary noninvasive positive pressure ventilation to help with his respiratory insufficiency. The patient has been using the ventilation for the past month and is willing to participate in the French multicenter prospective cohort study for patients with COPD undergoing domiciliary noninvasive positive pressure ventilation. The patient is not suffering from any neuromuscular disease and is not taking any medication that may interfere with the study.

A 40 year old mother of a 3 year old child with asthma comes to the Pediatric Care outpatient clinic for her child's routine check-up. The mother is concerned about her child's health as she has had frequent asthma exacerbations in the past. She is aware of the importance of flu vaccination for her child and is interested in getting vaccinated herself to protect her child. She has no history of allergic reactions to vaccinations or eggs. Her blood pressure, heart rate, and other vital signs are normal. She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive influenza vaccination at little or no cost. She is eager to take part in any intervention that may help protect her child from the flu.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy (OPMD) confirmed by genetic testing with a (GCN)13 size PABPN1 mutation. The patient has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and has a score of 270 on the Sydney Swallow Questionnaire. The patient has not had any prior treatment with IV trehalose or botulinum toxin. She has no history of pharyngeal myotomy, esophageal dilatation, head and neck surgery, or radiation. The patient is ambulatory and uses a cane for stability. She has not had a previous stroke or been diagnosed with diabetes. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse within the last 5 years. The patient has no evidence of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection. The patient is not currently receiving anti-coagulant treatment. She is not participating in another clinical trial and has not completed an interventional trial within the last 90 days. The patient is willing to undergo weekly IV infusions of trehalose or placebo for 24 weeks followed by an open-label extension period of 24 weeks.

A 50-year-old man has recently had a heart attack and underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to open up the blocked artery that caused the heart attack. He is now stable and is being considered for enrollment in the Late TIME study. He has an ejection fraction of 40% as assessed by echocardiography. He has no history of sustained ventricular arrhythmias or any other serious medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is willing to undergo a bone marrow aspiration procedure to collect the stem cells or placebo infusion 2 to 3 weeks after his heart attack. He is aware that he will be randomly assigned to receive stem cells or placebo and will be followed up for 24 months. He understands that he will undergo several baseline assessments, including a physical exam, blood draws, an electrocardiogram (ECG), an echocardiogram, and a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) test. He is willing to comply with all follow-up visits and studies, including wearing a small ECG machine called a Holter monitor for 24 hours after the infusion and recording his temperature twice a day for a month after the infusion. He is also willing to practice an active form of birth control if he is a woman of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with malignant lymphoma 2 years ago. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has recurred and is now refractory to treatment. She is experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. Her ECOG PS is 1, and she has an expected survival of at least 12 weeks. She has at least one measurable lesion per Lugano response critieria 2014 for Lymphoma. Her lab results show ANC: 1.8×109/L, PLT: 120×109/L, Hb: 100 g/L, TBIL: 1.2 ULN, AST: 2.0 ULN, ALT: 2.3 ULN, Cr: 1.2 ULN, INR: 1.5 ULN, and aPTT: 1.2×ULN. Her QTC results are Female 460 ms. She has no prior history of allergy to macromolecular protein preparations or JS004 components. She is not enrolled in any other clinical studies and has not undergone any major surgeries within the past 4 weeks. She has not discontinued previous immunotherapy due to immune-related adverse reactions, and no immunosuppressive agents have been used within the past 4 weeks. She has no history of allogeneic bone marrow transplantation or solid organ transplantation. She has no symptomatic, untreated, or ongoing treatment for central nervous system (CNS) metastases. She has no unresolved toxicities from prior anticancer therapy. She has no history of autoimmune disease within the previous 2 years, primary immunodeficiency, or rapid allergic reaction, eczema, or asthma beyond the control of topical corticosteroids. She has no concomitant diseases that are not under control, including but not limited to: persistent or active infection, unexplained fever > 38.5°C, or heart disease, active peptic ulcer disease or gastritis. She is negative for HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 36-year-old female who has been experiencing excessive worry and anxiety for the past 8 months. She reports feeling tense and on edge most of the time, and has difficulty controlling her worry. She also experiences physical symptoms such as muscle tension, restlessness, and fatigue. She has difficulty sleeping due to racing thoughts and worries about the future. She has no history of depression or any other psychiatric illness, and no history of substance abuse. She has never taken any psychotropic medication in the past. She has tried therapy for her anxiety, but has not experienced significant improvement. She is currently using an effective form of contraception. Her Hamilton Anxiety Scale score is 20, and her Clinical Global Impressions Severity Scale score is 5.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history. She has not traveled to countries where Shigella infection is endemic within the past two years. She is willing to participate in an inpatient stay lasting up to 11 days and an outpatient follow-up lasting 6 months from challenge. She is willing to not smoke during the inpatient stay and is available for all planned follow-up visits. She has passed the written examination on day -1 and demonstrated comprehension of the protocol procedures and knowledge of the study. She is willing to sign an informed consent form and is willing to not donate blood for up to 6 months after completion of the inpatient phase of the study. She is willing to refrain from participation in another investigational vaccine or drug trial at least until after completion of the 6-month follow-up safety call. She has negative serum pregnancy test at screening and negative urine pregnancy test on the day of admission to the inpatient phase. She is willing to use an effective method of birth control within two months of challenge and during the entire study. She has no chronic diseases and takes no medications. She is not allergic to fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. She has not used antibiotics during the 7 days before receiving the challenge inoculum dosing and has not used prescription and/or over the counter (OTC) medications that contain Imodium, acetaminophen, aspirin, ibuprofen, and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, during the 48 hours prior to investigational product administration. She has not received any investigational drug or any investigational vaccine within 60 days preceding challenge or is planning to use any investigational drug or vaccine during the 6 months after receipt of the study agent. She has not received a licensed, live vaccine within 28 days or a licensed inactivated vaccine within 14 days of receiving the challenge inoculum. She does not have any conditions that would jeopardize the safety or rights of a participant or would render her unable to comply with the protocol.

A 54-year-old man with a history of smoking and alcohol abuse presents with a lump in his neck and difficulty swallowing. Biopsy results confirm squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The tumor measures 30mm in diameter and there are nodal neck metastases. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 80 and is able to comprehend the study's purpose. He signs the informed consent documents in the presence of the staff. The patient has not received any previous chemotherapy or biological therapy nor radiation therapy for the treatment of head and neck cancer. He has no history of serious hematologic, cardiovascular, liver or kidney disease. The patient is not pregnant nor lactating at the time of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with essential hypertension 5 years ago. He has been taking antihypertensive medications for the past 3 years, but his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. He reports experiencing occasional headaches and dizziness. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no family history of hypertension or cardiovascular disease. His current blood pressure readings are consistently above 150/90 mmHg, even after taking medications. He is interested in participating in the SPYRAL PIVOTAL - SPYRAL HTN-OFF MED study to see if renal denervation can help lower his blood pressure without the use of antihypertensive medications. He is willing to discontinue his current medications and comply with the study protocol.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of primary infertility and a planned In Vitro Fertilization procedure is a potential candidate for this clinical trial. She has undergone hysterosalpingography which suggests that she may have a septate or arcuate uterus, which is a known congenital uterine anomaly that can cause infertility. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She has not had a prior office hysteroscopy to confirm the uterine abnormality. The investigators will evaluate her eligibility for the study based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

This is a 62 year old female with a history of blepharoptosis and blepharochalasis. She has noticed that her eyelids have become droopy and the skin on her upper eyelids has become loose, causing her vision to be obstructed. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has not had any previous eyelid surgeries and does not have any neurologic or systemic diseases that would influence eyelid position. She is interested in undergoing surgery to correct these symptoms and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the changes in periocular skin sensation following eyelid surgery.

45-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presents with recurrent metastatic disease to the liver and bone despite multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. She has measurable tumors by radiological evaluation and is willing to undergo further treatment despite the likelihood of side effects. Her liver function tests are within normal limits, and her renal function is satisfactory with a serum creatinine within normal limits. Her corrected serum calcium level is within the normal range, and her serum phosphorus level is above the lower limit of normal. Her absolute neutrophil count and platelet count are within acceptable limits, and her hemoglobin level is above 9 g/dL. She has no clinically significant abnormalities on urinalysis, and her coagulation function is adequate. She agrees to use effective contraceptive methods during the study. She has no history of cardiac disease, myocardial infarction, unstable arrhythmia, or evidence of ischemia on ECG. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have any active, uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infections requiring systemic therapy. She has not undergone major or minor surgery within the last 4 weeks, and she has not received radiation therapy or systemic chemotherapy or monoclonal antibody or other immunotherapy within the last 4 weeks. She has no history of allergic reactions attributed to excipients or chemical products used in the final GO-203-2c drug formulation. She does not have a known infection with HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. She does not have risk factors for gastrointestinal perforation or pulmonary hemorrhage. She is not currently receiving or having received treatment with any other investigational agent within the last 4 weeks, and she has no serious and/or poorly controlled non-malignant disease that could compromise protocol objectives.

The patient is a 55-year-old female diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma. She has been experiencing blurred vision, headache, and eye pain for several months. The patient wears glasses and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her current intraocular pressure is less than 21 mm Hg and her visual field test shows a mean deviation of -10 dB on Humphrey visual field testing. She has not had any ocular surgery or trauma in the past 6 months and her IOP treatment regimen has been stable for at least 4 weeks prior to injection. The patient is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study and complete the full sequence of protocol specified injections, procedures, and evaluations. She does not have any concurrent use of glucocorticoid medications administered by any ocular or systemic route or history of autoimmune or neurologic disease. The patient is a suitable candidate for the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with colon cancer that has spread to her liver and lungs. She has undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor in her colon and is now considered to be in the first line of treatment for her metastatic disease. She is currently receiving a combination of 5-FU (IV), IRINOTECAN, and BEVACIZUMAB chemotherapy. The patient is in good general health with a WHO performance status of 1. She has a life expectancy of greater than 3 months and is willing to be followed up for at least one year. The patient has no history of other cancers and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. She is willing to provide written consent and is affiliated with social security.

The patient is a 45 year old male with a history of low back pain for the past 5 years. He has tried multiple conservative treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and medications, but none of them provided long term relief. As a result, he has been scheduled for an open back surgery which is expected to last between 60-120 minutes. He is otherwise healthy with no known medical conditions and has a body mass index of 25. He works as a construction worker and spends most of his day working outdoors. He is a non-smoker, consumes alcohol occasionally, and exercises regularly. He has provided his consent to participate in the study and has a prestudy core temperature of 36.5 degrees Celsius (oral).

A 3-year-old girl, who was diagnosed with severe obesity with a BMI ≥97th percentile, is being referred to participate in a clinical trial. Her parents are the primary caregivers and are fluent in English (written and oral). The child does not have any diagnosed developmental delays or Prader-Willi syndrome. The family resides within the Toronto Public Health catchment area for home visiting. They are concerned about their child's weight and are interested in participating in a study that could help improve their child's weight status. They are willing to commit to the study's requirements, which include attending group parenting education sessions, receiving public health nurse home visits, and one-on-one check-ins with an interdisciplinary team at STOMP. They are also willing to complete questionnaires before the start of the trial and after 6 months to help evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has noticed a decline in her memory and physical performance over the past few years. She reports difficulty remembering names, appointments, and where she put things. Additionally, she has noticed a decrease in her ability to perform daily activities, such as climbing stairs and carrying groceries. The patient is generally healthy and takes only a multivitamin daily. Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and osteoarthritis. She reports that she leads a sedentary lifestyle, with only occasional walking for exercise, and has a body mass index of 27. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no history of cancer, stroke, heart disease, or major psychiatric illness. She has not had any fractures or amputations in the past 6 months and has not had any head injuries. The patient has normal hearing and vision. Her MMSE score is 28 and her TICS score is 35. She has not participated in any other clinical trials or taken any dietary supplements containing resveratrol, quercetin, or P. cuspidatum in the past 90 days. The patient is willing to be randomized to either the resveratrol or the placebo group and is able to participate in all aspects of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with essential hypertension for the past year. He has a family history of hypertension and is currently not taking any antihypertensive medications. His blood pressure readings during his last 3 visits were 150/90 mmHg, 148/92 mmHg, and 152/94 mmHg. He has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a blood pressure reading of 150/90 mmHg. He has no signs of organ damage or any other comorbidities. The patient is motivated to participate in the trial and is willing to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 19-year-old female with cystic fibrosis who has been attending annual reviews at the hospital since the age of 12. She has no history of hyperglycaemia or unexplained weight loss, but has experienced occasional episodes of coughing and shortness of breath. She is currently taking regular medication for her CF, including nebulisers and antibiotics, and has been compliant with her treatment regimen. The patient is well-nourished and has a body mass index (BMI) within the normal range. She has no other medical conditions and has not undergone any previous surgery. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the importance of early detection of CFRD. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 65-year-old male presents with severe pain and limited range of motion in his right shoulder, which has been ongoing for the last year. He reports no previous history of shoulder surgery but has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. Physical examination reveals significant tenderness to palpation over the right shoulder joint, limited active and passive range of motion, and crepitus with movement. Radiographs show degenerative joint disease with significant osteophyte formation and subchondral sclerosis. The patient is diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the right shoulder and is a candidate for reverse total shoulder arthroplasty using the Trabecular Metal Reverse Shoulder System. The patient meets all inclusion criteria, is willing and able to provide written informed consent, and is willing to cooperate in the required post-operative therapy and follow-up evaluations as described in the Informed Consent.

John is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent seizures since childhood. He has been diagnosed with glucose transporter type I deficiency (G1D) and has been on a ketogenic diet to control his seizures. He has a BMI of 25 and has not experienced any major side effects from his current treatment. He is not taking any medications other than his prescribed anticonvulsant. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is married and has two children. He works as an engineer and has a stable job. He is interested in participating in clinical research to potentially improve his condition and reduce the frequency of his seizures. He is able to comply with the study requirements and has no metal implants or claustrophobia. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

52-year-old female with a history of breast cancer, currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Herpes Zoster vaccine. She has no history of previous vaccination against Herpes Zoster or Varicella within the last 12 months. She is of childbearing potential, but is willing to practice adequate contraception during the entire treatment period and for two months after the completion of the vaccination series. She has a life expectancy of greater than one year and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol. She has not received any live vaccine in the past 30 days and is not currently experiencing any acute illness or fever. She has no known allergies or reactions to any component of the vaccine or study material and equipment.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a 2-year history of joint pain, swelling, and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and shoulders. She reported morning stiffness lasting more than an hour and difficulty with daily activities such as opening jars, buttoning clothes, and brushing her hair. She denied any other significant medical history and is currently not taking any medication. Her family history revealed that her mother and sister both had rheumatoid arthritis. Upon physical examination, bilateral swelling and tenderness were noted in her hands and wrists, with limited range of motion. The patient was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and started on oral glucocorticoid therapy with a dose of 10 mg/day of prednisone. She was advised to follow the American College of Rheumatology guidelines for the prevention of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis, including adequate calcium and vitamin D intake and regular weight-bearing exercise. She was approached to participate in a clinical trial aimed at reducing the risk of osteoporosis secondary to glucocorticoid therapy. The trial involves the use of tailored educational materials and feedback to the patient's physician regarding behavioral risk factors for osteoporosis. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is interested in participating in the trial to learn more about osteoporosis prevention and improve her overall health-related quality of life.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. She has been experiencing occasional palpitations and shortness of breath. Her echocardiogram showed mild left atrial enlargement and mild mitral regurgitation. She has been prescribed anticoagulation therapy to prevent stroke. She is scheduled to undergo circumferential ablation of the pulmonary veins as part of her treatment plan. The patient will be asked to provide up to 40ml of blood for blood tests including blood count, fibrinogen, factor VIII, D-dimer, P-selectin, von Willebrand factor, and TEG - Thromboelastography. The samples will be collected before and after the procedure from the peripheral femoral venous sheath, arterial line, right atrial sheath, and LA sheath.

The patient is a 25-year-old female college student with a history of seasonal allergies. She has been experiencing symptoms of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis for the last two pollen seasons. Her symptoms include sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, and itchy and watery eyes. She has a positive skin prick test to birch pollen with a wheal diameter of 5 mm and specific IgE levels of 2.2 kU/L. She is asymptomatic to all other allergens during the birch pollen season. Her FEV1 is 90% of predicted value. She is sexually inactive and has no childbearing potential. She is willing to use appropriate contraception during the study period. She is able to be compliant with respect to the completion of the daily record card and taking of the investigational products. She has no past or current disease that may affect the outcome of the study. She has not received any desensitisation treatment to birch pollen or any other Betulaceae sp. within the previous 10 years. She is not currently using inhaled/systemic steroids or long-acting systemic corticosteroids. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse.

Samantha is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the presence of estrogen receptor-positive and HER2-negative breast cancer. The tumor is multifocal and unilateral and measures 3 cm in diameter. Samantha has never received any prior treatment for cancer. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her laboratory tests show adequate bone marrow, renal and liver function. Samantha has signed the consent form and is willing and able to comply with the study scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, radiological exams, tumor and blood specimen collection and other procedures. She is currently not pregnant and has agreed to use two highly effective forms of contraception throughout the period of taking study treatment and for at least 90 days after the last dose of study drug. Samantha has never taken letrozole or any CDK inhibitor or anti-cancer therapy before. She has no known hypersensitivity to the study drugs or excipients. Her medical history is significant for hypertension that is well-controlled on medications. Samantha is not currently taking any medications that are not permitted for the study. Her baseline QTc is within normal limits.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of heart failure for the past 2 years. He has been on optimal medical treatment but still experiences shortness of breath and fatigue during daily activities. He has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% and a left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) of 60mm. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has a pacemaker implanted due to second degree atrioventricular block, with a right ventricular pacing of 50%. He has no history of ventricular arrhythmias or severe valvular disease. He is able to understand and willing to provide a written informed consent. He lives with his wife and is able to perform activities of daily living independently.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who is undergoing a de novo renal transplant due to end-stage renal disease. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been on dialysis for the last 2 years. The patient has no history of allergy or intolerance to any medications. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and will be available for all scheduled follow-up visits. The patient is not currently pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period.

A 29-year-old female presents with chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea that has persisted for the past 8 months. She has tried non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and hormonal treatments, but has not experienced any significant improvement in her symptoms. She reports that her symptoms have been interfering with her daily activities and affecting her quality of life. She has a confirmed diagnosis of endometriosis and is currently receiving standard of care treatment. She is experiencing moderate to severe pain during her periods and has been experiencing pain during intercourse as well. She is sexually active and is using birth control pills for contraception. She has no significant medical history and no known allergies. She is willing to participate in the study and provide information through questionnaires and other routine standard of care visits.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with severe mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP), affecting his oral, nasal, and esophageal mucous membranes. He has developed blisters and erosions on his mucosal surfaces, causing difficulty in swallowing and speaking. He has not responded well to dapsone treatment and is experiencing significant disease activity. The patient is otherwise in good health, with no history of cardiac or respiratory disease, and no evidence of liver or renal insufficiency. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and has not received any immunosuppressive treatment in the past. The patient has read and understood the information letter and is willing to sign the informed consent form. He is not currently pregnant or lactating, and is willing to use effective contraceptive methods during and for 12 months after the study. The patient has updated vaccinations and is affiliated with a social security category. The patient is able to comply with the study protocol and is willing to avoid excessive exposure to sunlight during the study participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American male who was diagnosed with Covid-19 and was admitted to the hospital due to worsening symptoms. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He reports experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue for the past week. He has been on oxygen supplementation since admission and is currently receiving treatment with remdesivir and dexamethasone. His vital signs are stable, and he has no known history of cardiovascular disease. He is willing to participate in the study and provide the necessary information for the registry.

A 30-year-old male with a history of chronic jaw pain and discomfort was diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder (TMD) at the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill (UNC-CH) Orofacial Pain Clinic. He has been experiencing pain in the temporalis and masseter muscles, and occasionally at a site beyond the boundary of the muscle being palpated. He has no history of facial injury or surgery and is not currently receiving orthodontic treatment. He does not have any systemic inflammatory disorders such as lupus, kidney failure or renal dialysis, heart disease or heart failure, chronic respiratory disease, hypertension, uncontrolled diabetes, epilepsy or seizures, hyperthyroidism, trigeminal neuralgia, or cluster headache. He also does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not have any active or uncontrolled psychiatric disorders or recent psychiatric hospitalization. He has never received acupuncture treatment for TMD before and is not currently using NSAIDs or steroidal medications. He is fluent in English and has signed an informed consent form to participate in the study. He plans to live in the area for the next 2 months.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hypertriglyceridaemia (triglyceride level > 5.5 mmol/l). She has been on statins for the past year but her LDL-C levels have remained normal, while her apoB levels remain high. The patient has also been experiencing some numbness and tingling in her hands and feet, and is concerned about potential nerve damage.
