She has no known history of diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or liver disease. The patient has a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease. She has not been pregnant or breastfeeding in the past year, and has no active malignant disease. The patient is not currently taking any medications that could affect lipoprotein metabolism significantly.

A 35-year-old female patient was diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) two years ago. She has been on various antidepressant medications, but none of them have been effective in reducing her symptoms of depression. She has experienced feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and worthlessness, as well as a lack of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has also had trouble sleeping and has experienced significant weight gain. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently taking BCI-024 in combination with BCI-049 as part of Protocol #CBM-IT-01. She is willing to provide written informed consent and has demonstrated compliance with all the protocol requirements of the precursor study. She is interested in participating in the open-label extension study to evaluate the tolerability of the increased dose of the combination treatment and to potentially reduce her symptoms of depression.

A 32-year-old female with a history of major depressive disorder for the past 6 months, currently being treated with antidepressants and psychotherapy, is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess her physiological signals, sleep patterns, vocal characteristics, activity, location and phone usage. She reports having measurable skin conductance/electrodermal activity and owns a working Android smartphone that she uses regularly. She also has access to a Windows PC and the Internet every day. The patient is able to read, understand, and provide written informed consent in English. She has no history of psychosis, mania, hypomania, epilepsy, untreated hypothyroidism or cognitive impairment that would impede adherence to study procedures. She is not currently participating in any other research studies and is willing to wear the physiological sensor (E4) bands, fill out the surveys, and record a weekly diary.

A 56-year-old woman presents with symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) including vaginal bulging and pressure. She has had three vaginal deliveries, the last one being 10 years ago. She is postmenopausal and has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. Her medical history is notable for hypertension, and she takes medication for it. She has tried conservative measures such as pelvic floor exercises and pessary use, but her symptoms persist. She is interested in surgical management of her POP, and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the GYNECARE PROSIMA* Pelvic Floor Repair System. She does not have a history of previous mesh repair for POP, and is not currently being evaluated or treated for chronic pelvic pain. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant in the future. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman complaining of chronic iron deficiency anaemia. She has a history of chronic fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath on exertion. She has been taking iron supplements for the past year but her symptoms have not improved. She has been referred for a consultation and gastroscopy. In addition to routine coeliac serology testing (IgA TTG, EMA, and total IgA immunoglobulin level), she will undergo a whole blood transglutaminase-based rapid test for coeliac disease as part of this clinical trial. She will also provide a sample of 25 μl of capillary venous blood for the point-of-care test, Simtomax, which will detect both IgA and IgG antibodies to DGP, as well as the total IgA level. Biopsies will be taken from the duodenum during gastroscopy, and the histology will be analyzed for the presence of villous atrophy (Marsh 3a-3c) and a positive IgA-EMA or IgA-TTG to diagnose coeliac disease. The patient will be excluded from the study if she has a coagulopathy (INR > 1.3 Platelets < 80) or active gastrointestinal bleeding identified at endoscopy or suspected carcinoma identified at gastroscopy.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of hemorrhoids for the past year. He reports discomfort, itching, and occasional bleeding during bowel movements. He has tried over-the-counter treatments such as creams and suppositories, but they have not provided much relief. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon examination, he is found to have grade III hemorrhoids. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares two different surgical techniques for the treatment of his condition.

Sophie is a 38-year-old single mother of two children, ages 14 and 16, living in the United States. She works as a nurse and is passionate about health and wellness. She wants to make sure her children adopt healthy behaviors and avoid harmful ones. She has had conversations with her children about health risk behaviors in the past, but she feels like she needs more guidance on how to approach these topics. She is interested in participating in this study to gain more knowledge about how to effectively communicate with her children about unhealthy eating, marijuana use, and sedentary behavior. She believes that this study will help her become a more effective parent and promote healthier behaviors in her children.

The patient is a healthy newborn baby boy born to a mother who is HIV-positive. The mother had a full-term pregnancy, and the baby weighed 3.2 kg at birth. The family resides in an area where tuberculosis is prevalent. The baby has not experienced any complications during pregnancy or delivery. The mother is aware of the clinical trial and has consented for her baby to participate. The family plans to remain in the area for at least four months. The baby has not been in close contact with anyone with tuberculosis.

A 57-year-old woman was diagnosed with biliary cancer after experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss. A CT scan showed a mass in the bile duct and liver metastases. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Her performance status is 1, and she is able to perform all activities of daily living, but with some difficulty. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril. Her liver, kidney, and hematological function tests are within normal limits. She has no active infections or uncontrolled systemic diseases. She has never been pregnant and is not breastfeeding. She is able to give written informed consent. She has no history of psychiatric or other disorders that may impact consent. She has not received any prior MEK, RAS, or RAF inhibitors. She is not receiving any potent inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4/5, CYP2C19 or CYP1A2.

A 12-year-old male with a history of low-grade glioma presents with progression of tumor despite previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has normal organ function and a performance status corresponding to a Lansky/Karnofsky score of 80. The patient has not previously been treated with a MEK inhibitor and has no known history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to trametinib. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for the patient's involvement in the study, and the patient has assented to participate as well. The patient must be able to ingest and retain enterally administered medication and have no clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities limiting the absorption of the medication. The patient's tumor tissue will be required for central review, and the patient must have a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. The patient must also belong to one of the specified study groups, and must not have any uncontrollable medical disease, HIV infection, hepatitis B or C, or any other malignancy. Furthermore, the patient must not have had major surgery within 2 weeks prior to starting trametinib, nor be pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 50-year-old male of African American ethnicity residing in a predominantly minority neighborhood in Florida. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels, which led to the recent prescription of a statin medication. He has been taking the medication for a month but has missed a few doses due to forgetfulness. He is interested in improving his adherence to the statin medication to reduce his risk of cardiovascular disease. He is a current smoker and has tried to quit smoking in the past but has not been successful. He is willing to participate in a phone-based behavioral intervention to improve his adherence to the statin medication and potentially quit smoking. He is able to speak and understand English well.

65-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in morphologic complete remission who is scheduled to undergo haploidentical allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. The patient has no prior history of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation but has received chemotherapy in the past. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has adequate physical function as measured by cardiac, hepatic, renal, and pulmonary function tests. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is not currently receiving any investigational agents. The patient does not have any active or uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infections and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have HIV or active Hepatitis B or C.

A 12-year old girl was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) six months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and is currently in remission. She had a bone marrow transplant four months ago and is currently on immunosuppressive therapy. She recently developed a fever of 102°F that is not responding to antibiotics. A chest X-ray revealed a new pulmonary infiltrate. Her blood cultures are negative. A bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was performed and revealed Aspergillus fumigatus. She is started on liposomal amphotericin B, but her kidney function deteriorated, and the medication was discontinued. Her medical team is considering Voriconazole as an alternate treatment option for her invasive aspergillosis. She is alert and oriented, but weak and fatigued due to her recent illness. Her past medical history is significant for asthma, but she does not have any other allergies. She lives with her parents and her younger brother. She is currently homeschooled due to her medical condition.

75-year-old female with a history of hypertension and osteoporosis who presents to the emergency department with a fall resulting in a hip fracture. She undergoes surgical repair and is admitted to the hospital for post-operative care. She has a past medical history of mild cognitive impairment but is not currently experiencing delirium. She has a MMSE score of 20 adjusted for age and education. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to prevent delirium. She reports no allergies to medications and is not currently taking any cholinesterase inhibitors. She is able to participate in interviews and complete questionnaires.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Huntington's disease. He has a CAG polyglutamate repeat expansion of 40. He is experiencing cognitive impairment, with a baseline MMSE score of 16. He has a caregiver who is his wife, who spends at least five days per week for at least three hours per day with him and is familiar with his cognitive, functional, and emotional states, as well as his personal care. He has no major medical illness or unstable medical condition that may interfere with his ability to comply with the study procedures and abide by study restrictions. He is willing and able to give informed consent to participate in the study.

A 12-year-old boy with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has limited participation in physical activities due to poor balance and motor coordination. His parents report that he has never been able to ride a two-wheeled bicycle and has expressed interest in learning. He is currently receiving occupational therapy to improve his motor skills. He is in good health and has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in physical activities. His weight is within the limits for the equipment used in the intervention. His parents are willing to commit to the study and are able to transport him to the study site for the intervention sessions.

Katie is a 20-year-old female who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma 6 months ago. She has been receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She reports having moderate to severe pain in her lower extremities and back for the past week. She rates her pain as an 8 out of 10 on a pain scale. She is currently taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief but has not found them to be very effective. She is fluent in English and is able to travel to the acupuncture clinic. Her parents are supportive and willing to participate in the study as well. She has no history of cognitive impairments and is expected to complete the study schedules and procedures. She is interested in exploring integrative medicine to manage her pain and improve her quality of life.

This is a 32 year-old male who was admitted to the hospital in Jakarta with a high fever, chills, and cough. He reported feeling fatigued and weak for the past few days. He denied any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. Initial tests for Dengue virus and Salmonella Typhi were negative. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this observational study and agrees to the collection and storage of specimens for laboratory testing and future research. He is currently undergoing evaluation for a possible infectious disease of unidentified etiology.

A 28-year-old man who is a heavy smoker and drinks coffee regularly presented to the clinic with concerns about dental erosion. He has noticed increased tooth sensitivity and discoloration in his front teeth. He brushes twice daily with a fluoride toothpaste but does not floss regularly. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He has no history of allergies or orthodontic treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of wearing an intraoral device for a total of four hours. He is able to give written consent and is willing to use fluoridated toothpaste during the study period.

Maria is a 35-year-old female who was diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago. She has not been on antiretroviral therapy because she was asymptomatic until she noticed that her vision became blurry. She was referred to an ophthalmologist and diagnosed as having CMV retinitis. Her visual acuity was 20/200 in her right eye and 20/40 in her left eye. She has no history of any previous ophthalmic disease or surgery. She does not use any medications or drugs. She has no allergies to any medications. Her physical exam was unremarkable except for the presence of CMV retinitis. Lab studies showed a CD4+ count of 40 cells/mm3 and an HIV viral load of 200,000 copies/mL. She had no other active opportunistic infections. She was eligible for the study and was willing to participate.

A 28-year-old Caucasian female is seeking medical attention due to recurring skin issues. She has a history of Atopic Dermatitis (AD) and has experienced severe itching, dry skin, and rashes for several years. She has not been diagnosed with Eczema Herpeticum (EH) or recurring Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infections. She is currently taking oral antihistamines and topical corticosteroids to manage her symptoms. She is in good general health, does not have any skin diseases other than AD, and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is not taking any systemic immunosuppressive drugs or chemotherapy, is not undergoing immunotherapy, and has not received phototherapy in the last 30 days. She does not have any autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency, or active fungal, bacterial, or viral infections at the time of the screening. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, weighs 55 kg, and is willing to give written informed consent. She is eligible to participate in the study as Group 3.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment as it is an observational study that will be conducted using data from two large ongoing cohort studies, the Nurses' Health Study and Health Professionals' Follow-up Study. Participants in these studies were healthcare professionals who did not have a history of chronic diseases at baseline. Therefore, no patient description is required.

A 56-year-old male with a history of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and end-stage liver disease is scheduled for liver transplantation. The patient has been diagnosed with cirrhosis and has been on antiviral therapy for the past 3 years. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, jaundice, and abdominal discomfort. He has no history of venous or arterial thrombosis, immunodeficiency, or immunosuppression. The patient has not received any other immunoglobulin product within the last 3 months prior to the study entry. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse within the last 6 months. The patient has provided written consent for participation in the clinical study and understands all aspects of the study.

The patient is a 65 year-old male who has been undergoing haemodialysis for the past 2 years due to end stage renal disease. He is able to walk independently without any walking aids for 20 meters. He currently exercises less than one training session per week and is interested in improving his physical function and overall health. He is on a stable medical regimen for the past 4 weeks and is expected to maintain this regimen for the duration of the study. He is able to understand and communicate in the language used in the study and has no known psychological disorders or dementia. He has not participated in any other study with investigational drugs within the past 30 days. He is interested in participating in this study and has provided informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman who works as a graphic designer came to the clinic with complaints of pain and limited range of motion in her right shoulder. The pain started gradually 6 months ago and worsened over time. She also reported difficulty in performing daily activities that require shoulder movement, such as reaching for objects on a high shelf, combing her hair, and carrying a bag. She denied any history of shoulder dislocation, fracture, or surgery. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is under control with medication. Physical examination revealed positive Neer's sign, Hawkins and Kennedy test, and Empty and full can tests. The patient was diagnosed with sub-acromial impingement syndrome (stage 2) according to Neer's classification. X-ray showed a decrease in sub-acromial space. The patient was found to have restricted thoracic extension motion in the +ve occiput to wall test. The patient has no spinal deformities, diabetes mellitus, radiculopathy, history of breast cancer, stroke, or Shoulder hand syndrome. She has no ligamentous laxity. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the effect of mulligan thoracic sustained natural apophyseal glide on sub-acromial impingement syndrome.

Maria is a 35-year-old woman who is 32 weeks pregnant with her second child. She has a history of gestational diabetes in her first pregnancy and was able to control her blood sugar with diet and exercise. Her current pregnancy has been complicated by gestational hypertension, for which she is taking labetalol. Her BMI is 42 kg/m2 and she has been advised by her obstetrician that she will likely require a cesarean delivery due to her history of shoulder dystocia in her previous delivery. She has never had any surgical procedures before and is concerned about the risks associated with a cesarean delivery. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the difference between Pfannenstiel and midline vertical skin incision at time of cesarean section in preventing wound complications in the morbidly obese patient. She understands that there is no direct benefit to her as a participant, but hopes that her participation will contribute to the overall knowledge about best practices for cesarean deliveries in the obese population.

Patient is a 56-year-old Chinese man who came to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with non-ST segment elevation ACS. He has a past medical history of hypertension, controlled with medication. He is married, has two children, and works as a banker. His BMI is 25, blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and heart rate is 80 bpm. His recent laboratory results show normal liver and kidney function, and he is negative for hepatitis B and C. He is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 25-year-old female with PKU, who has not been treated with a phenylalanine-controlled diet, is eligible for the study. She is affiliated with a social security scheme and has read and signed the informed consent. She does not have any other diseases that may cause oxidative stress or is not taking any medication known to cause oxidative stress. She is not pregnant and has confirmed this with a negative pregnancy test. Her metabolic balance will be evaluated through plasma amino acids and organic acids commonly accumulated in the urine of PKU patients. The study will also measure her plasma concentrations of antioxidant vitamins and trace elements.

The patient is a premature infant born at 27 weeks and 5 days of gestation. The infant is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and is receiving respiratory support via continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). The infant weighs 900 grams and has a head circumference of 25 cm. The parents have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in the clinical trial to reduce Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP). The infant has no major congenital malformations or congenital malformations of the eye identified prior to randomization. The parents have been informed about the importance of follow-up ophthalmic examinations as an outpatient and long-term follow-up. The infant is not experiencing any intrauterine congenital infections or life-threatening impairment of renal, hepatic, or cardiac function. The infant will be randomized to receive either 80 mg inositol/kg/day or placebo, administered in divided doses every 12 hours (40 mg/kg/dose). The study drug will be administered daily, starting within 12 to 72 hours of birth and continued until the earliest of 34 weeks postmenstrual age, 10 weeks chronologic age, or the time of hospital discharge or transfer. The infant will be monitored closely throughout the study for any adverse events and will undergo customary newborn intensive care procedures including repeat eye examinations until ROP status is final. Longer term data will also be collected at 22-26 months corrected age to evaluate growth, neurodevelopmental testing, overall health status, rehospitalizations, surgeries, and diagnoses, including ophthalmic diagnoses and treatments since discharge.

A 62 year old man comes to the clinic with symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and smoking. The patient has undergone angiography which showed 90% stenosis in his left anterior descending artery (LAD) and 70% stenosis in his right coronary artery (RCA). The patient was advised to undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with Orsiro Mission DES. The patient agrees to participate in the BIOFLOW-VIII registry and signs the informed consent for data release. The patient is geographically stable and willing to participate in all follow-up assessments. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any known intolerance to aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors, heparin or any other anticoagulation/antiplatelet therapy required for PCI, stainless steel, Sirolimus or contrast media which cannot be pre-treated.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic with complaints of muscle weakness and fatigue. She had noticed that she had difficulty climbing stairs and standing up from a sitting position. She also experienced difficulty in combing her hair and lifting heavy objects. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism, both of which were well-controlled with medication. She denied a history of smoking or alcoholism. On physical exam, there was decreased muscle strength in the proximal and distal muscles of the upper and lower extremities. There was no muscle atrophy, fasciculations or sensory abnormalities. Laboratory tests revealed elevated levels of creatine kinase (CK) and positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA). A muscle biopsy was performed which showed evidence of muscle inflammation and necrosis. An electromyography (EMG) was consistent with a myopathy. The patient was diagnosed with polymyositis and started on oral prednisone therapy. She was informed about the MASC project and agreed to participate in the study. She provided written informed consent and agreed to donate blood, serum, DNA, and RNA for the biobank. She will undergo monthly follow-up visits for clinical assessment and laboratory testing. The study will aim to identify factors associated with the development of myositis and to improve the understanding of the pathophysiology of the disease.

A 28-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with a recent diagnosis of seminoma after orchiectomy. The tumor was located in the primary testicular site. The patient has no prior history of treatment with radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Alpha-fetoprotein levels before and after orchiectomy were normal. The patient has an ECOG score of 1 and a PNN count of 1700, platelets count of 110,000, and bilirubin levels within the normal range. The ASAT and ALAT were also within the normal range. The patient has normal serum creatinine levels at 90 µmol/L. The patient has signed informed consent to participate in the study and is affiliated with social security. The patient meets the specific inclusion criteria for cohort 1, which is grade I. There is no evidence of HIV, Hepatitis B or C infection. The patient has not had any other cancer within the past 5 years except for treated skin cancer (Basal Cell). The patient has no visceral metastasis or cerebral metastasis. The patient does not have any physical or mental condition that would be incompatible with the treatment. There is no history of uncontrolled or severe cardiovascular or hepatic pathology. The patient is not deprived of liberty or under guardianship and is able to undergo medical monitoring.

A 17-year-old male with Cystic Fibrosis (CF) presents at the CF center for his regular follow-up. He has been diagnosed with CF since he was 8 years old and has been on intravenous antibiotics cycles for the past 2 years. His FEV1 is 55% predicted and he weighs 65 kilograms. He has no Burkholderia cepacia infection and is not on the lung transplantation waiting list. He is currently undergoing PEP-MASK therapy and is willing to adhere to the protocol procedures. The patient is able to perform the NMBW test and spirometry. The patient has not had a pulmonary exacerbation within the last two weeks and is not undergoing non-invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen therapy.

A healthy 10-month-old infant is being sought for a clinical trial that aims to assess the safety and protectivity rate of Bio Farma's Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine. The infant should not have received any previous measles or rubella vaccines, nor should they have had a history of measles or rubella infection. The parents of the infant must have been informed about the study and be willing to comply with the trial's schedule and instructions. The infant should not be currently suffering from any illness, especially infectious diseases or fever. The trial is being conducted in Indonesia as part of the Indonesian National Program of Immunization.

The patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman in active labor. She is a first-time mother and has been experiencing contractions for 8 hours. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she has no known contraindications to epidural analgesia. She has no history of neurological illness, fetal abnormalities, or recent analgesic usage. She has a Body Mass Index of 25. She communicates fluently in English and is interested in receiving epidural analgesia for pain relief during labor. She has been informed about the study and has provided her written consent to participate.

A 28-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child and speaks Hebrew is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She is currently in her second trimester and has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy. She plans on having a natural childbirth and is interested in exploring relaxation and guided imagery techniques to reduce pain during labor. She does not have any background systematic conditions such as high blood pressure or diabetes and is not taking any chronic medication. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or Caesarean sections.

The patient is a 45-year-old individual who has been experiencing persistent pain and discomfort in their arm, which is affecting their daily activities. They have been referred to the Orthopaedic Hand and Upper Extremity Service at Massachusetts General Hospital for further evaluation and treatment. The patient is fluent in English and has the ability to read and write in English. They have no history of mental illness or language problems that would hinder their ability to complete the enrollment forms. The patient is not pregnant. They will be informed of the study and will be given the opportunity to participate, given they meet the inclusion criteria.

This is a 43-year-old female with a history of gastric ulcer and chronic gastritis. She has been experiencing episodes of abdominal pain, bloating and nausea for the past year. Despite treatment with proton pump inhibitors, her symptoms have persisted and she has lost weight. After further evaluation, she was diagnosed with a gastrointestinal tumor that requires surgical treatment. The surgical team has recommended the use of the Microcutter stapling/cutting device. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of this device and has consented to a 1-month clinical follow-up evaluation.

A 48-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with primary breast cancer during a routine mammogram. The tumor is located in her left breast and is classified as stage T2N0M0. She has no history of other types of cancer, autoimmune diseases, or HIV. She is currently not taking any systemic immunosuppressive therapy or chronic opioids medication. She has not received any pre-operative chemotherapy or radiotherapy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effect of propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia on circulating tumor cells. She speaks German fluently and has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

58yo man recently diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma after presenting with left flank pain and hematuria. CT scan showed a 10 cm left renal mass with multiple lung and bone metastases. Biopsy confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma. He has no significant past medical history and is an ex-smoker. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status 1. His oncologist recommended treatment with an immune checkpoint inhibitor and he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the potential of 89Zr-DFO-Atezolizumab PET/CT scans in patients with renal cell carcinoma. He is able to lie still for a 30 to 60 minute PET/CT scan and understands the study requirements. He is willing to undergo a pregnancy test on the day of 89Zr-DFO-Atezolizumab administration.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with primary HER2-positive breast adenocarcinoma. She is scheduled to undergo treatment with adriamycin, cyclophosphamide, followed by docetaxel and trastuzumab. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or previous heart failure, but has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to medications or contrast agents. The patient has a baseline LVEF of 65% by echo and adequate echocardiography image quality for strain analysis. The patient is able to tolerate five 60-minute CMR examinations over 15 months and agrees to give informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and has been receiving LHRH agonist therapy for more than 6 months. He is experiencing fatigue, which is affecting his daily activities. He reports feeling tired throughout the day and having difficulty concentrating. He is married and lives with his wife. They have two adult children who live nearby. He is currently retired and enjoys reading and watching sports. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally, but is willing to limit his consumption to one drink per day for the duration of the trial. He is able to read and write in English and is willing to consume Red Bull™ Sugar-Free Drink as part of the study. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to caffeine or contraindications to Red Bull™ use.

This is a 35-year-old male who sustained a spinal cord injury (SCI) approximately 2 years ago and has been living with the consequences of the injury ever since. He has been diagnosed with an ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS) grade B, which means he has some sensation below the injury level, but no motor function. The injury occurred in the thoracic region, specifically T8-T9. He has undergone rehabilitation and fitness conditioning to improve his overall health and prepare for the transplantation of autologous human Schwann cells (ahSC) as part of a clinical trial. He is eligible for the trial based on the inclusion criteria and has undergone an MRI to determine the size and location of the injury. The MRI showed a lesion length of 2.5 cm and volume of 1.8 cc, both of which are within the limits set by the trial. He is committed to the trial and understands the potential risks and benefits involved. He will be monitored closely for any adverse events and will undergo safety and efficacy assessments at various points throughout the trial.

30 yo Caucasian female G2P1 at 38+6 weeks of gestational age presented to the anesthesia outpatient clinic for elective caesarean section surgery following a previous caesarean delivery. She reported feeling anxious about the upcoming surgery due to her previous experience with surgery. She denied any past history of psychiatric illness or medication use. She has been taking prenatal vitamins and iron supplements throughout her pregnancy. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has no known allergies. She reported no physical symptoms except for occasional mild back pain. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is married and has a supportive partner. She works as a teacher and has been on leave for the past month in preparation for the delivery. She reported feeling well-rested and has been sleeping well. Her family history is negative for any major illnesses. She is able to read and understand the survey questions. She consented to participate in the study and her anxiety levels will be assessed using the STAI-Continuity and STAI-State scales. Her eligibility for the study will be determined based on the results of the assessment.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no prior medical history. He has a BMI of 22 and a total body weight of 70kg. He has not taken any medications, including herbal supplements or vitamins, within the last 7 days. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and he does not consume caffeine or grapefruit regularly. He is willing to use contraception during the clinical trial. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. He is available to be hospitalized for the required duration of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

This is a 38-year-old male diagnosed with focal epilepsy with partial onset seizures. He has been experiencing at least 2 partial onset seizures per month for the last 3 months, despite being treated with 2 concomitant antiepileptic drugs. His seizures are well-characterized according to the 1989 International League Against Epilepsy classification, and he has had an EEG reading and brain MRI/CT scan performed within the last 5 and 2 years, respectively. He has had at least 8 Type I seizures during the 8-week Baseline Period, with at least 2 Type I seizures during each 4-week interval of the Baseline Period. He has never been randomized in this or any other study with BRV as a dosing arm. He has no history or presence of status epilepticus during the year preceding V1 or during Baseline, nor does he have a known history of psychogenic nonepileptic seizures. He has no ongoing psychiatric disease other than mild controlled disorder.

The patient is a 50-year-old African American woman with type 2 diabetes and evidence of kidney disease. She has been diagnosed with diabetes for more than 10 years and has been experiencing proteinuria of more than 150mg per day for the past year. She is currently on a stable dose of an ACE inhibitor. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and she is currently on amlodipine 5mg once a day for that. She is also taking metformin 1000mg twice a day for her diabetes. She has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. She does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. She is slightly overweight with a BMI of 28. Her vital signs are within normal limits, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, pulse rate of 70 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98%. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who received a renal transplant one year ago due to end-stage renal disease. He is currently taking oral cyclosporine as part of his immunosuppressant regimen and has been receiving his medication from Avella Specialty Pharmacy for the past year. He works as a software engineer and lives with his wife and two children. He has a history of non-adherence to medication in the past and has missed a few doses of his cyclosporine since his transplant. He reports feeling overwhelmed with work and family responsibilities, which has led to forgetfulness and difficulty adhering to his medication regimen. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him improve his medication adherence and potentially improve his quality of life. He is not currently pregnant, a prisoner, or institutionalized and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. She is currently receiving chemotherapy but has relapsed and is not responding to alternate therapies. She has an ECOG status of 1 and her renal and hepatic functions are within normal limits. Her corrected QT interval is 460 ms. She has no active gastrointestinal conditions and has not undergone major surgery within the last 28 days. She is not currently using any investigational drugs or undergoing cancer-directed therapy. She has no active infections and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use adequate birth control throughout the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of VS-4718 and to help find the right dose for future clinical trials.

75 y/o male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who is unable to tolerate or declines cytotoxic chemotherapy. ECOG performance status is 1. Patient has no untreated active infections at the time of study entry and normal organ function with Creatinine < 2 mg/dl, total serum bilirubin within institutional limits unless due to hemolysis, Gilbert's syndrome, or ineffective erythropoiesis, and AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) ≤2.5 X institutional upper limit of normal. Life expectancy of at least three months. Patient has not received chemotherapy or study drugs for >3 weeks prior to starting the study. Women of childbearing potential should be advised to avoid becoming pregnant and men should be advised to not father a child while receiving treatment. All men and women of childbearing potential must use acceptable methods of birth control throughout the study. The patient has not had prior therapy with demethylating agents for leukemia treatment within the last four months. No clinical evidence of CNS or pulmonary leukostasis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or central nervous system leukemia. No serious or uncontrolled medical conditions. Patient has not received concurrent use of any other investigational agents. The patient is willing and able to provide informed written consent according to federal and institutional guidelines.

A 16-year-old male was referred to the addiction clinic by his school counselor for cannabis abuse. His parents noticed a change in his behavior, such as being more secretive, isolating himself, and poor academic performance. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications. He has been using cannabis for about a year, smoking at least 2-3 times a week with his friends. He also admits to occasional tobacco and alcohol use. He spends most of his free time playing video games or scrolling through social media on his phone. He reports difficulty falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, and feeling tired during the day. He denies any other medical, psychiatric, or substance abuse history. On examination, his vital signs are within normal limits. He appears alert and oriented, and his mood is anxious. He has no tremors, nystagmus, or other neurological signs. Laboratory tests are normal except for a positive urine drug screen for THC. The patient is enrolled in the clinical trial after obtaining parental consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who tested positive for HIV antibodies during a routine screening. He reports no symptoms and has never received any treatment for HIV. He has a history of alcohol and marijuana use, but denies any current substance abuse or dependence. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has not had any recent sexual partners and reports consistent condom use in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

A 7-year-old girl living in a low-income country has been experiencing a persistent cough and episodes of rapid, shallow breathing for the past few weeks. She has not been vaccinated against pertussis and has not received any other vaccinations. She lives in a crowded household with her parents and three siblings. Her mother reports that her younger brother also has a cough and difficulty breathing. The girl has not been hospitalized for her symptoms but has missed several days of school due to her coughing fits. Her family has limited access to medical care and cannot afford expensive treatments.

A 65-year-old man who has been experiencing severe knee pain and difficulty walking for the past two years. He has been diagnosed with severe osteoarthritis in his right knee and has not found relief with conservative management. He is scheduled for a primary total knee arthroplasty to improve his mobility and reduce his pain. He has no history of chronic narcotic use and is not taking any corticosteroids. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. The clinical care team has determined that he is eligible for tourniquet use during the surgery.

A 58-year-old man recently presented with unexplained weight loss, night sweats, and fatigue. He has noticed enlarged lymph nodes in his neck and groin area, and he has experienced intermittent fever for the past 2 months. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no family history of cancer. Physical examination showed enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and groin area, and he was referred for a biopsy. The biopsy indicated a diagnosis of non-follicular lymphoma, specifically lymphoplasmacytoid lymphoma. His staging evaluation revealed that he meets the criteria for no initial treatment according to GELF criteria for advanced stage disease, and he is eligible for this clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form. He has not had any prior treatment for lymphoma and has not received radiation therapy in the past. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He is male, 58 years old, and meets all the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male with no significant medical history. He has not tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and has not been in close contact with anyone who has. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing to participate in up to 10 visits to the study center and is able to comply with all study requirements.

A 35-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, genotype 1, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. He was diagnosed with HCV infection 4 years ago, and his viral load has been consistently high. He has also been diagnosed with HIV infection 2 years ago and is currently on stable ART (antiretroviral therapy) regimen. His CD4+ count is 502 cells/mm^3, and his plasma HIV-1 RNA is below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ). He has not received any prior HCV treatment or any investigational or commercially available direct acting anti-HCV agents other than sofosbuvir. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past 6 months. He is currently employed as a sales representative and is married with two children.

35-year-old female with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and a family history of diabetes. She has no personal history of diabetes or major psychiatric disorders. She is not currently taking any medications that may affect glucose homeostasis and has no history of uncontrolled asthma or upper respiratory infections in the past month. She does not regularly perform high-intensity exercise and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She drinks alcohol occasionally and does not smoke cigarettes, cigars or marijuana. She has never donated blood in the past three months and does not suffer from claustrophobia.

A 28-year-old man comes to the clinic seeking help for his methamphetamine addiction. He has been using methamphetamine for the past 2 years and has tried to quit multiple times in the past without success. He reports using methamphetamine at least once a day and describes experiencing severe cravings and withdrawal symptoms when he tries to stop using it. He has a history of depression and anxiety and has been on antidepressant medication for the past year. He is currently not using any other drugs except for nicotine. He has a stable job and is motivated to quit using methamphetamine. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of tyrosine in reducing his methamphetamine use. He is able to provide informed consent and is committed to attending group psychosocial interventions as part of the study.

A 38-year-old male presents with chronic hepatitis B infection for the past 2 years. He has been diagnosed with HBeAg positive chronic hepatitis B and has a serum HBV DNA level of 1.5 x 10^5U/ml. His ALT level is 8 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) and his total bilirubin level is within normal limits. He has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma, liver disease acute exacerbation, creatinine level of ≥1.5mg/dl, or hemoglobin level below 100g/L. He has not used immunosuppressants, immunomodulators, or cytotoxic drugs within the last 6 months or anti HBV drug therapy within the last 6 months. He has no history of liver transplantation or drug allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 26-year-old man who has recently started outpatient treatment for heroin addiction at Archway clinic. He has been attending counseling sessions regularly and is motivated to maintain abstinence. He has at least 14 weeks remaining in the treatment program. The patient is eligible to participate in a clinical

67-year-old male with a history of hypertension and intermittent chest pain presented to the cardiology clinic with symptoms of dizziness and syncope. After evaluation, he was diagnosed with complete heart block and indicated for permanent pacemaker implantation. He is compliant with medications and has no history of allergies. He is able to walk and move independently without assistance. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 29. He is willing and able to give written informed consent for the study. He does not have any history of CRT implantation, upgrade or revision of implanted device, contraindications to pacemaker implantation, and gravidity.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial as it does not involve patients or medical interventions on patients. This trial is focused on investigating the optimal learning environment and protocol for dvSS® simulation activities using medical students as robotic-naïve research participants. The study aims to understand the learning curve students can achieve by simulation-based training and then to directly apply that training to a safe in vivo model in order to determine training interventions that can inform a robotic curriculum both locally at GWU and throughout the country.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of psoriasis, which was diagnosed by a dermatologist five years ago. He has recently developed pain and swelling in his right knee, ankle, and wrist. The pain is worse in the mornings and improves with activity. He has never been diagnosed with any other inflammatory rheumatism. He has not received any biomedicine treatment, but he has been using over-the-counter non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for the past two weeks with mild improvement in symptoms. He is fluent in French and has no cognitive, mental, or psychic disorders. He is not under tutelage or curatorship and is not currently pregnant. He is interested in participating in the APACHE cohort study.

The patient is a 57-year-old male smoker who recently received a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer at stage IIIA. He has a history of heart disease and hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for the past few months, which has been gradually worsening. He has never participated in any regular exercise program and leads a sedentary lifestyle. The patient is able to perform activities of daily living but has difficulty with more strenuous activities due to his reduced lung function. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his physical fitness prior to undergoing lung resection surgery. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen and has no known drug allergies. His medical history includes coronary artery disease and hypertension for which he is taking medication. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. The patient has no other clinically limiting comorbidities and is motivated to participate in the rehabilitation program.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and underwent chemotherapy for 6 cycles. After the treatment, he achieved complete remission (CR) and was scheduled for allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (Allo-HSCT). He had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications. He was a non-smoker and denied alcohol or drug use. His physical exam was unremarkable with no cardiopulmonary or neurological abnormalities. His vital signs were within normal limits. He received the transplant from a matched unrelated donor and had no complications during the post-transplantation period. He underwent routine monitoring for minimal residual disease (MRD) and was found to have a positive MRD. He was then randomly assigned to the HMA+DLI group and started on hypomethylating agents (HMA) therapy combined with donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI). The therapy was well tolerated with no significant adverse effects. He is closely monitored for any signs of relapse and will continue to receive follow-up care in the study.

A 32-year-old male patient was brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. The patient was found to have a subdural hematoma with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) of 6. The patient has no significant past medical or surgical history. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is married with two children. The CT scan showed a large subdural hematoma with midline shift of 12mm. The patient has been scheduled for emergency craniotomy with TBI. The patient's vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, a heart rate of 92 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. The patient's oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The patient's family has given their consent for the patient to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been experiencing subacromial shoulder pain for over three months. The pain is primarily felt during abduction and is accompanied by dysfunction. She has no history of surgery or significant injury to the affected shoulder. She has not received any prior treatment for the pain. The patient does not have any other joint issues or medical conditions that may interfere with the study. She is able to understand spoken and written Norwegian. She is not pregnant and is not currently taking anticoagulant medications. The patient has not had shock wave therapy or supervised exercises before.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) according to the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. The patient is postmenopausal or surgically sterile, and is willing to practice effective methods of contraception if they are of childbearing potential. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, 1, or 2. The patient's bilirubin, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels are all within the normal range. The patient's calculated creatinine clearance is ≥ 30 mL/min. The patient has not undergone major surgery or radiotherapy within the last 14 days. The patient has no evidence of current uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions, active hepatitis B or C virus infection, or known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive. The patient has no serious medical or psychiatric illness that could potentially interfere with the completion of treatment according to this protocol. The patient has no known allergies to any of the study medications, their analogues, or excipients in the various formulations of any agent. The patient has not been diagnosed or treated for another malignancy within the last 2 years. The patient has no neuropathy, sensory, with or without pain, motor, or autonomic on clinical examination during the screening period. The patient has not participated in other clinical trials involving investigational agents within 21 days of the start of this trial and throughout the duration of this trial. The patient has not undergone prior chemotherapy treatment for AML. The patient's cardiac ejection fraction (EF) is ≥ 40%. The patient is not currently undergoing systemic treatment with strong inhibitors of CYP1A2, strong inhibitors of CYP3A, or strong CYP3A inducers, or use of Ginkgo biloba or St. John's wort.

5-year-old male with a diagnosis of autism presents with chronic abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation. The patient has a history of delayed developmental milestones and socially withdrawn behavior. The patient's parents report that the child has difficulty communicating his needs and that he has a limited diet consisting primarily of carbohydrates. The patient has been referred to Massachusetts General Hospital for Children for evaluation of his gastrointestinal symptoms, which require endoscopy and biopsy for disaccharidase activity evaluation. The patient does not have a history of bleeding disorders, hypoalbuminemia, unstable respiratory or cardiac conditions or any other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. The parents have provided consent for the child's participation in the study.

45 yo F with a BMI of 40 kg/m2, referred for bariatric surgery due to long-standing morbid obesity. The patient reports experiencing several episodes of apnea during sleep, and has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) for which she uses continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. The patient has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. Physical examination is notable for a large neck circumference and Mallampati class IV airway. Lung function tests show normal spirometry results, and normal diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). Echocardiogram is normal. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl diagnosed with Hereditary Angioedema (HAE). She completed the SHP643-301 (SPRING) study and is currently experiencing acute attacks of HAE. The patient is not responding well to alternative treatment options, and her parents have given their consent to participate in the expanded access program for lanadelumab treatment. The patient has a parent or legal guardian who understands the nature of the program and can provide written informed consent for the child to participate. The patient does not have any liver function test abnormalities, and her caregiver is willing to self-administer lanadelumab at home after receiving documented training during the SHP643-301 (SPRING) study. The patient's female caregiver, who is of childbearing potential, has agreed to comply with the applicable contraceptive requirements of the protocol for the duration of the expanded access program and for 70 days after completion. The patient does not have a known hypersensitivity to lanadelumab or its components.

A 21-year-old Yale student, majoring in psychology, is interested in participating in the Yale Wellness Project. She has been feeling stressed and overwhelmed with school work and extracurricular activities. She has noticed that her sleep has been affected and she is having trouble focusing on her studies. She has tried various methods to alleviate her stress, such as exercise and talking to friends, but has not found them effective. She is interested in participating in the Emotional Intelligence, Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) & SKY Yoga Breathing programs to see if they can help improve her overall well-being. She is willing to commit to attending the workshops and completing the required assessments. She understands that there is a possibility of being assigned to a no-treatment control group, but is still interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 58 year old male who was diagnosed with cirrhosis and Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein thrombosis. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption for several years. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and distension for the past few months, and a recent abdominal ultrasound showed the presence of large esophageal varices. His liver function tests indicate that his Child-Pugh score is B. He has not had any previous history of variceal bleed or endoscopic variceal ligation or sclerotherapy. His gastric varices are of low risk. He does not have any significant cardio or pulmonary co-morbidities. He has not had any previous treatment for his portal hypertension. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and diabetes is admitted to the intensive care unit with acute kidney injury. Her serum creatinine has increased to 2.5 times above her baseline, and her overall urine output has been less than 0.5 ml/kg/h for the previous 12 hours. She has an arterial line in place and has been in critical care for 24 hours. She is not receiving acute renal replacement therapy, and her treating clinician has determined that she is not intravascularly hypovolemic. The patient is expected to remain in critical care for at least another 48 hours. The patient is not actively bleeding, and there is no need for RRT due to intoxication of a dialyzable toxin. She has no history of chronic renal replacement therapy or renal transplant. She does not have severe hyponatremia or hypernatremia. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent.

32 yo M presents with a 4-day history of redness, itching, and watery discharge in his right eye. He denies any pain or vision changes. His medical history is significant for seasonal allergies and he currently takes loratadine as needed. On examination, his right eye has conjunctival injection and mild mucoid discharge. After a thorough ophthalmic exam, the diagnosis of acute adenoviral conjunctivitis is suspected. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of FST-100 Ophthalmic Suspension for this condition. He is able to provide informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria. The patient denies any known allergies to medications and has not used any ocular anti-inflammatory medications in the past.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with non-small-cell lung cancer. She underwent a biopsy and the histology showed adenocarcinoma. Her lung function tests have shown adequate respiratory function for necessary surgical treatment. She has been staged as stage IIIA (T3 N1) according to the TAKO guidelines. She has no other significant medical history and her WHO status is 1. She has no history of brain metastasis or other distant metastasis equivalent to stage IV disease. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy for NSCLC and has not undergone any surgery or radiotherapy for NSCLC. She is not currently taking any experimental drugs or non-approved medical procedures. She is willing to implement effective contraception as required during the study period. She has adequate hematological, renal, and hepatic functions. She has no active infection requiring IV antibiotics, active ulcer, unstable diabetes mellitus or other contraindications to corticotherapy. Her initial work-up has been completed within three weeks prior to first infusion and includes a chest CT scan, abdominal CT-scan, brain CT scan if indicated, PET-scan, bronchoscopy and mediastinoscopy, and pulmonary function tests. She has signed initial consent prior to protocol-specific procedures.

A 56-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of rectal cancer to the lower two-thirds of the rectum and a history of hypertension visited the clinic for a consultation. He has previously undergone surgery for benign prostatic hyperplasia and is currently taking medication for his hypertension. He has no other medical conditions and has not received any radiotherapy or chemotherapy for his rectal cancer. He is willing to meet all requirements of the clinical trial and is able to provide written informed consent and HIPAA forms prior to admission. His ECOG status is 2, and his life expectancy is estimated to be more than 3 months. He is aged between 18 to 80 years old. He is not pregnant or lactating. He is not taking any medications that would produce bleeding diathesis, and he has no history of significant cardiac disorders. His INR and PTT levels are within the acceptable range for the trial, and his platelet count is above 100K.

The patient is a 9-year-old child with spastic cerebral palsy. The child is classified as GMFCS level III, meaning they can walk with assistive devices such as crutches, walker or a wheelchair for long distances. The child's gait is abnormal and interfering with their physical function. The child has been referred for assessment and treatment of gait abnormality and is a candidate for orthopaedic surgery involving at least 2 levels, in one or both lower extremities (e.g. knee & ankle). The child has not undergone previous gait laboratory analysis that has been seen by the treating surgeon. The child has no history of orthopaedic lower extremity procedures within the previous 2 years.

A 55-year-old man with moderate osteoarthritis has been advised to undergo total knee arthroplasty. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He also takes medication for acid reflux. He has no known allergies to medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and leads an active lifestyle. He is scheduled for a 4-hour surgery and will receive general anesthesia. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with a peanut allergy. He experiences severe allergic reactions to peanuts, which include difficulty breathing, hives, and swelling. Despite avoiding peanuts, he has had several accidental exposures, which have resulted in hospital admissions. The patient is otherwise healthy, and he is not taking any medications for his peanut allergy. He has not participated in any other interventional studies for the treatment of food allergy in the past 6 months. The patient's parents are willing to ensure that he uses an effective method of contraception if he is female of childbearing potential. The patient is able to perform spirometry maneuvers in accordance with the American Thoracic Society (ATS) guidelines (1994). The patient's parents are willing to provide signed informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with acromegaly. She has been experiencing symptoms such as enlargement of the hands and feet, protrusion of the jaw, and thickening of the skin for the past 2 years. She has been receiving somatostatin analog monotherapy for the past 6 months but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is currently not pregnant or nursing and has no history of untreated thyroid or adrenal insufficiency. She is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the impact of different acromegaly treatments on quality of life.

59-year-old male with a history of COPD, hypertension, and coronary artery disease was admitted to the ICU with respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. The patient is receiving sedation and paralytic agents to facilitate mechanical ventilation. The initial chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates. Arterial blood gas analysis indicated hypoxemia with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 150. He was started on empiric antibiotics and received a 500 mL bolus of crystalloids for hypotension. The patient had a previous myocardial infarction and was treated with percutaneous coronary intervention three years ago. Upon examination, the patient appeared uncomfortable on the ventilator, with labored breathing and diffuse crackles on lung auscultation bilaterally. The cardiac examination revealed no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. ECG revealed normal sinus rhythm. The patient was deemed critically ill and met the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with esophageal adenocarcinoma 8 months ago. He received chemotherapy with cisplatin and fluorouracil but experienced disease progression. He underwent chemoradiation with carboplatin and paclitaxel but developed severe side effects, including nausea, vomiting, and fatigue. CT scan showed progression of the tumor. He is currently experiencing difficulty swallowing and has lost 10 pounds in the last month. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to take oral tablets.

Pt is a 35yo F with a history of benign ovarian cysts and scheduled for an elective gynecological abdominal surgery. She has no known allergies, past medical history, or chronic medical illnesses. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has not received antibiotics in the preceding 7 days. She is not pregnant, and does not have a pacemaker device or on anticoagulant therapy. The patient will receive 2 gm cephalosporins preoperative per hospital policy.

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of knee pain during activities such as going up and down stairs, squatting, and kneeling. She reports no previous injuries or surgeries in her lower limbs and does not have any neurological, vestibular, visual, or hearing impairments. She has been diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome and experiences pain in both knees. The pain is described as a dull ache that worsens with prolonged sitting and physical activity. The patient reports no pain during collection procedures but expresses a willingness to perform exercises as instructed by the researchers. She has not previously received any treatment for patellofemoral pain syndrome.

50 year-old female with a history of ovarian cancer that has recurred after previous treatment with two lines of systemic therapy. She presents with abdominal/pelvic pain and imaging reveals measurable disease in the abdominal/pelvic region. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She is willing and able to operate the NovoTTF-100L(O) System and is amenable to receiving weekly paclitaxel. She has no prior disease progression on weekly paclitaxel for recurrent disease and no brain metastasis or leptomeningeal spread of the tumor. She does not have a known allergy to medical adhesives or hydrogel and is not currently receiving concurrent anti-tumor therapy beyond weekly paclitaxel. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception throughout the entire study period and for 3 months after the end of treatment. Her previous participation in clinical trials is allowed.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who recently underwent excision of a large malignant tumor from her upper eyelid. The surgery resulted in a significant defect on her upper eyelid, affecting her vision and causing cosmetic disfigurement. She has no history of previous surgeries or medical conditions that would affect her eligibility for the study. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the results of the modified Cutler-Beard technique with tarsoconjunctival graft for reconstruction of the upper eyelid.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with high-grade osteoblastic osteosarcoma in his left femur. He has no significant past medical history, and he denies any history of smoking or drug use. He is a high school student and is very active in sports, including football and basketball. He has undergone a biopsy, and tumor tissue samples are available for analysis. He has received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and his response to treatment is being evaluated. His clinical data, including chemotherapy received, event-free survival, and overall survival, are available for analysis. He is being followed up closely by his oncologist and is receiving ongoing treatment.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with advanced prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent a radical prostatectomy and received radiation therapy. His PSA levels remained stable for about 2 years after treatment, but recently, his PSA levels have been rising. The patient underwent a bone scan and CT scan, which revealed bone metastases. The patient is currently undergoing androgen deprivation therapy and has been on this treatment for about 6 months. He is experiencing mild fatigue and occasional hot flashes. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He has no history of seizures or serious CNS diseases. He has no history of medication or drug abuse. He is in overall good health and is able to perform his daily activities without difficulty. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with high-risk multiple myeloma. He has received two rounds of induction therapy with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone, but has not achieved a complete response. His disease has been characterized by high-risk cytogenetics, including t(4:14) and deletion p17. He has no prior history of radiation therapy or other malignancies. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, and a recent echocardiogram and MUGA scan showed an ejection fraction of 55%. His baseline laboratory studies are as follows: Bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL SGOT: 32 U/L SGPT: 28 U/L Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Absolute neutrophil count: 1200/ul Platelet count: 120,000/ul The patient is willing to undergo apheresis to collect a minimum of 4 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg. He is aware of the teratogenic potential of lenalidomide and agrees to comply with mandated contraception guidelines. He has no contraindications to lying supine for approximately 30 minutes during each treatment session. The patient is fully aware of the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide voluntary written informed consent before participation.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it focuses on developing and evaluating the effectiveness of a parent-based intervention for middle school students to prevent or reduce sexual risk behavior or tobacco use. The study aims to recruit African American or Latino 6th or 7th grade students and their residential mothers or primary female caregivers. The study excludes 8th grade students and fathers or primary male caregivers.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has no past medical history of note, and she is generally healthy. She lives alone in an apartment close to work. She is interested in participating in a clinical study to help advance medical research. She has not received any previous vaccination against pneumococcal disease nor has she been diagnosed with Pnc pneumonia. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She has no known allergies. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic bronchitis and COPD. He has a smoking history of 20 pack years and has quit smoking for the past 8 months. He has been on maintenance pulmonary/COPD medications for the past 2 years. He has a productive cough for more than 3 months in each of the past 2 years. His pre-procedure post bronchodilator FEV1 is 50% of predicted. He is willing to undergo 3 bronchoscopy procedures that include lung biopsies and multiple MCS treatments. He has not had an acute pulmonary infection or pneumonia in the past 6 weeks and has not had a CB and/or COPD exacerbation requiring steroids and/or antibiotics in the past 6 weeks. He does not have clinically significant bronchiectasis or other respiratory disease other than chronic bronchitis and COPD. He has not undergone lung surgery, and he is not on anticoagulant therapy or >10 mg of prednisolone/day. He is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to get pregnant during the study duration. He has not received chemotherapy within the past 6 months and is not expected to receive chemotherapy during participation in this study. He is able to read, understand, and sign a written Informed Consent and agrees to continue not smoking for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who had an abnormal Pap smear result during her regular gynecological check-up. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is not pregnant and has never had a hysterectomy or pelvic radiotherapy. She has been referred to the Center for Cervical Diagnosis for further evaluation. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and has voluntarily signed the Patient Informed Consent Form specific to the study. She is mentally and physically able to undergo a colposcopy exam. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve the diagnostic accuracy of cervical cancer detection.

65 year-old man who has been experiencing mild forgetfulness, such as forgetting names or appointments, and feeling less mentally sharp in recent months. He is in good overall health and living independently. He has no history of neurodegenerative disease or dementia, major psychiatric conditions, neurological disorders, active alcohol or substance abuse, head trauma or systemic diseases affecting brain function, or uncontrolled hypertension or cardiovascular disease. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to assess the cognitive impact of 4-week memory training programs done twice weekly, either during simultaneous aerobic exercise, sequentially after aerobic exercise, or without aerobic exercise. The patient is willing to wear a physical activity monitor and keep exercise and cognitive activity logs during the entire study. The patient understands that the study is a pilot study and secondary aims may not be tested in the community site.

32F with a history of epilepsy since childhood, taking 3 anticonvulsant drugs with no significant seizure control. The patient reports having at least 6 seizures per month, with each seizure lasting for about 2-3 minutes. The patient has tried several different medication regimens in the past but none of them have been successful in controlling her seizures. The patient is interested in alternative treatment options and has been researching the Atkins diet for epilepsy. The patient has a BMI of 23 and no history of kidney, heart, or renal disease. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of hypercholesterolemia. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the Atkins diet can help control her seizures.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma 2 years ago. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but unfortunately, her cancer has relapsed. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her cancer and is willing to participate in this clinical trial as a first-line treatment option. She has no history of epilepsy or other central nervous system diseases, and she does not have any graft-versus-host reaction or a need for immunosuppressants.
