Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of heart disease, and her most recent cardiac evaluation showed normal heart function. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraception during the trial. Her recent laboratory results showed normal creatinine, ALT/AST, and bilirubin levels. She is willing to voluntarily participate in this study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain and stiffness for the past few years. She has been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis knee based on X-ray findings, and her pain score is 9 points on Lequesne's index. She has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications but has received minimal relief. She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history, allergies or medications. She has a BMI of 26 and has not undergone any knee surgery or intra-articular injection therapy in the past 6 months. She is post-menopausal and has no history of infections or autoimmune arthritis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore a potential new treatment option for her knee osteoarthritis.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian man who was recently diagnosed with a solid pancreatic mass. The mass was confirmed through cytological and histological examination. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort, as well as persistent fatigue. He has no significant past medical history, but his family history is positive for pancreatic cancer. He has not undergone any prior surgical treatment or received chemo-radiotherapy. He is not currently taking any medication. He works as a construction worker and is married with three children. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent for EUS with elastography and FNA biopsy.

13 year-old male with a history of Tourette's Disorder, confirmed by the K-SADS-PL. He has been experiencing tics that cause impairment in his normal routines, including academic achievement and social activities. He has not taken aripiprazole within 30 days of the Screening visit, and has not received any investigational agent in a clinical trial with Once-weekly aripiprazole at any time. He has no history of neuroleptic malignant syndrome and weighs more than 16 kg. He is able to swallow tablets and tolerate oral medication. He has no significant psychoactive substance use disorder within the past 3 months and has negative drug screen. He is not currently taking any medications not allowed per protocol and is not requiring CBT for TD during the trial. He does not have any abnormal laboratory test results, vital signs, or ECG results.

The patient is a 75 year old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents with shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue and occasional chest pain. He has been diagnosed with pure aortic regurgitation and has been experiencing symptoms for the past 6 months. He has been advised that he is not a good candidate for surgical aortic valve replacement due to his high risk status. Echocardiography and computed tomography findings suggest that he is suitable for TAVI using a SAPIEN 3 THV. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the feasibility and safety of this procedure for patients with pure AR. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and has provided written consent to participate.

The patient is a 22-year-old female nursing intern who has been working in a hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic for the past few months. She has been exposed to patients with COVID-19 and has been experiencing symptoms of psychological distress, including anxiety and depression, which have been affecting her daily life and work. She has a history of anxiety and depression and has been taking medication for this for the past year. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

55-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension for the past 5 years. The patient has been taking 40 mg of Telmisartan for the past year, but despite regular medication, his blood pressure readings have not been consistently controlled. He reports no symptoms other than occasional headaches. The patient has no known allergies and is currently not taking any other medications. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for this eight-week clinical trial comparing the effect of a fixed-dose combination of Telmisartan 40 mg plus hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) 12.5 mg to Telmisartan 40 mg alone on diastolic and systolic blood pressure in patients who fail to respond adequately to telmisartan monotherapy. The patient has no history of pre-menopausal women, hepatic and/or renal dysfunction, secondary hypertension, or clinically relevant sodium depletion, hyperkalemia, or hypokalemia. He has not experienced any recent history of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiac surgery.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was diagnosed with advanced stage IV lung cancer with metastasis to the bone and liver. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy with minimal success. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication for both conditions. He does not have any past medical history of autoimmune disorders, HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, meaning he is ambulatory and able to carry out light work. He has adequate bone marrow reserve, renal and hepatic function, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2000/microL, platelet count of 120,000/microL, serum creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL, serum total bilirubin of 1.0 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase within normal limits, and SGOT/SGPT within normal limits. He does not have symptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases or any inguinal lymph node involvement. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore other treatment options and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 50 year old male diagnosed with kidney cancer that has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic). The patient has not received pazopanib hydrochloride treatment prior to registration in this trial. The cancer is confirmed to be non-clear cell renal cancer, including chromophilic (papillary), chromophobic, oncocytic, sarcomatoid, collecting duct (Bellini's duct), translocation-type carcinoma or medullary renal cell carcinoma. The patient is in good general health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has adequate blood counts with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) greater than or equal to 1500, platelets greater than or equal to 100,000 and hemoglobin greater than 9.0 g/dL. The patient's total bilirubin is less than 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are less than or equal to 2.5 x ULN. The patient's urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPC) is less than 1 and prothrombin time (PT) or international normalized ratio (INR) is less than or equal to 1.2 x ULN. The patient is post-menopausal or using adequate contraception if of childbearing potential. The patient is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up and willing to return to the Mayo Clinic enrolling institution for follow-up.

A 4-month-old baby girl is brought into the clinic for enrollment in a clinical trial. She was born at 33 weeks gestational age and was transferred to the participating hospital after birth. The baby girl is currently in good health, without any respiratory symptoms. Her parents are able to provide follow-up medical care at the participating site and have agreed to participate in the study. The baby girl has not received palivizumab or any other immunoglobulin preparation containing RSV-specific antibodies. Her parents have been informed about the study and have signed the informed consent form approved by the Institutional Review Board. The baby girl will be followed for one year to determine the incidence of severe RSV LRTI requiring hospitalization among infants born < 35 weeks gestational age in Brazil.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She has no previous history of cancer or other significant medical conditions. She underwent a successful pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) and is currently recovering from surgery. She speaks fluent French and has a good understanding of the language. She is willing to participate in the study and has no opposition to the information provided. She is affiliated with the social security plan and is a beneficiary. She has no other medical or psychiatric conditions, and her cognitive abilities are intact. She lives alone, is retired, and enjoys reading and gardening in her free time. She has no history of smoking, drinking, or illicit drug use. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of cancer research and to learn more about the psychological impact of cancer surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent oral discomfort for the past few months. He reports having lesions in his mouth that appear white and lacy in appearance. He also reports experiencing pain and sensitivity to hot and cold foods. He has no history of heart, pulmonary, liver, or kidney disease, chronic pain syndrome, or drug addiction. He has not undergone any recent operations and has no history of heart, metabolism, CNS, infectious, circulation, systemic, malignant, or immune system affecting diseases, blood coagulation disorders, or allergic reactions to pharmaceuticals and antibiotics. He has not been pregnant before. He is willing to participate in the study and is available for follow-up examinations.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is currently abstinent from alcohol and drug use, with no history of substance abuse, HIV or any neurological condition including stroke or seizure. He is not taking any prescription medication or over-the-counter medication (including herbal remedies or diet aids) within 14 days of the imaging session. He has no implanted or embedded metal objects or fragments in the head or body that would present a risk during the MRI scanning procedure, and has not had exposure to ionizing radiation that in combination with the study tracer would result in a cumulative exposure that exceeds recommended exposure limits. He has normal laboratory test results within the normal reference range for the population or investigator site. He is willing to follow study procedures, and has given written informed consent approved by the ethical review board governing the site. He meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of heart failure NYHA class III. He has been on optimal medical therapy including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. Despite medical management, he continues to experience dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. His echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% with a dilated left ventricle. He is a candidate for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) with implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) backup. His electrocardiogram (ECG) shows left bundle branch block (LBBB) with QRS duration of 150 ms. A suitable device for CRT-ICD has been selected, and the patient is scheduled for LV lead implantation. The patient has agreed to participate in the ERACE study and has signed written consent.

A 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and clinically significant diabetic macular edema (DME) in his left eye, with hard exudation within 500μm of the central foveal diameter accompanied with contiguous retina thickening. The edema locates within 500μm of the central foveal diameter, and retina thickening field > 1DD and within the 1DD central fovea. The patient has undergone previous treatment of antidiabetic drugs within three months preceding the screening, and his blood-glucose concentration is predicted to be unchanged and stable during the whole study. The patient's Best-Corrected Visual Acuity (BCVA) score of the study eye is between 78 and 19 letters, inclusively, and the BCVA score of his fellow eye is ≥ 24 letters. The patient has not received any previous anti-VEGF drug treatment or intraocular or periocular injection of steroid drug within 6 months preceding the screening. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and has signed the Informed Consent Form.

A 55 year old woman comes to the clinic for a bone density checkup. She has experienced menopause three years ago and has noticed her bones becoming weaker recently. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her BMI is within the range of 18 to 35kg/m2 and her weight is 60kg. Her T score is -2.5 and she meets the inclusion criteria for the study. She has not taken any bisphosphonate or other medication affecting bone metabolism within the last three months. She has normal serum calcium and 25-(OH) vitamin D levels. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help her with her bone density issues.

This clinical trial is looking for healthy volunteers only. Therefore, no specific patient description is needed. Anyone who meets the inclusion and exclusion criteria and is willing to participate as a healthy volunteer may be considered for the study.

The patient is a 78-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is not eligible for intensive chemotherapy due to his age and comorbidities. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 2. He has not received any prior treatment for AML, except for 1 dose of cytarabine to control hyperleukocytosis. He is not eligible for an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. His AML is de novo and has not spread to the central nervous system. He has an ECOG Performance Status score of 2. The patient has not received any immune suppressive agents for the past 4 weeks before the first administration of cusatuzumab. He has no known allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to cusatuzumab or azacitidine or its excipients. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility and if he meets the criteria, he will participate in the study to determine the efficacy of cusatuzumab in combination with azacitidine.

A 32-year-old male patient is brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle accident. He reports severe pain in his left leg, and examination reveals an open fracture of the tibia and fibula (Type II) with visible bone fragments. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and he reports no allergies. He is alert and oriented with a normal blood pressure of 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. Laboratory tests reveal no abnormalities. The patient is admitted to the hospital for surgical intervention and is eligible for the clinical trial on preventing infections in orthopedic patients. He consents to participate in the study and is randomized to receive intravenous cephalosporin and aminoglycoside for 72 hours as antibiotic prophylaxis. The patient is monitored throughout his hospital stay for any signs of acute kidney injury or secondary infections at sites other than the fracture site.

The patient is a 38-year-old HIV-1 positive man who has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for 6 months. His CD4 count has been consistently above 450/µl and his plasma HIV1-RNA is below 200 cp/ml. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has not experienced any significant side effects. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares intermittent therapy (IT) to continuous therapy (CT) for HIV-1 infection. He is sexually active and agrees to use acceptable methods of contraception during the study period. He is able to comply with the protocol and signs the informed consent prior to screening. The patient has never had a CD4 count below 100/µl and has not been treated with abacavir or nevirapine in the current ART. He does not have hepatitis B or C and has not had an AIDS-defining event in the past 18 months. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

As this is a clinical trial focused on dental caries prevention in children, the patient should be a child between 6 to 8 years old. Let's assume the patient is a 7-year-old girl who attends a primary school in Tartu city. She has no history of significant dental problems and her dental hygiene is considered good by her dentist. Her parents have signed and returned the informed consent form for her participation in the study. She has no eating disorders and is willing to continue being part of the study, including consuming the test products provided by the teachers during school days.

A 29-year-old man presented to the emergency department with severe pain and swelling in his left testicle. He reported that the pain started suddenly 2 days ago and has been getting progressively worse. He has no history of trauma to the area, but he did report a recent urinary tract infection. On physical exam, his left testicle is enlarged, tender and elevated. His temperature is 38°C, blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 90 beats per minute. Laboratory work up showed an elevated white blood cell count and urine culture was positive for E. coli. The diagnosis of acute epididymitis was made, and he was started on antibiotics and analgesics. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial examining the effect of local cooling of testis in patients with epididymitis to relieve pain and reduce analgesics consumption.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been sexually active for the past 5 years. She has been using condoms for contraception but is interested in a more effective form of birth control. She is interested in the DepoProvera injection and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare self-administration versus clinic administration. She speaks fluent English and has access to a working telephone. She has no history of breast cancer or acute liver disease, and is not currently pregnant or trying to conceive in the next year. She has no known hypersensitivity to medroxyprogesterone acetate or any other components of DMPA. She is willing to follow up for one year and is interested in learning more about the cost effectiveness of self-administered DMPA.

Patient is a 50yo man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years. He has been on oral hypoglycemic drugs for the past year. His recent HbA1c level was 7.5% and his glucose control has been stable based on his visits to the hospital. He is willing and able to monitor his peripheral blood sugar and adhere to a regular diet and exercise regimen. He has been treated with HMS5552 for 52 weeks and has completed the safety visit. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent form and participate in the clinical trial to observe the clinical remission rate of diabetes mellitus and beta cell function after discontinuation of the hypoglycemic drug.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with mycosis fungoides, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. She has stage IA disease and has been experiencing symptoms for the past six months. She has at least three visible skin lesions that are being monitored by her dermatologist. She has a history of mild sunburn and is willing to avoid sunbathing for the duration of the study. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She is willing to use effective contraception if sexually active. She is not currently on any topical or systemic treatment for her CTCL, but has previously used topical steroids. She does not have a history of sun hypersensitivity or other photosensitive dermatoses. She has not received any systemic immunosuppression due to drugs or infection with HIV or HTLV 1. She is willing to participate in the study and follow all study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old mother residing in the Metro Vancouver Regional District. She has primary custody of her 8-year-old daughter and 11-year-old son. She is interested in promoting her children's physical activity and outdoor play but is hesitant to allow them to engage in risky play. She is able to speak, read, and understand English. She has not participated in any similar studies in the past.

A 52-year-old Caucasian female with Fitzpatrick Skin Type 2 presents with moderate to severe wrinkles on her upper and lower cheeks, upper and lower lips, and periocular and perioral areas. She is in good health and has no history of keloid formation or hypertrophic scarring. She has not received any treatments with dermabrasion, ablative laser, or radiofrequency in the past year, and has not received any non-ablative laser treatments in the past 6 months. She has not received any botulinum toxin injections in the areas to be treated within the prior 6 months. She is a non-smoker and has no active, chronic, or recurrent infections. She is not allergic to any analgesic agents, Aquaphor®, topical or local anesthetics, or chlorhexidine, povidone-iodine or epinephrine. She has not received treatment with an investigational device or agent within 30 days before treatment or during the study period. She is willing to provide written informed consent, understand and willing to comply with all study related directions from investigator and follow-up visits.

This is a 55 year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed 5 years ago. He has been on metformin tablets for the past 3 years, with a dose of 2000 mg per day. His HbA1c levels have been consistently above 8.0% despite the medication. He has hypertension and dyslipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is compliant with his medications but has expressed difficulty in swallowing tablets due to a history of esophageal stricture. He has given informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer him an option for easier medication administration.

The patient is a 44-year-old female who presents to the emergency department with a fever of 38.5 °C and persistent cough for the past 5 days. She reports experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue as well. The patient had no travel history outside the country nor had any exposure to a confirmed COVID-19 patient. Her past medical history is significant for asthma and seasonal allergies. The patient takes albuterol and inhaled corticosteroids for her asthma. The physical examination reveals normal vital signs except for mild tachypnea. The lung auscultation showed bilateral crackles. The patient has no other significant physical findings. A chest x-ray shows bilateral ground-glass opacities. The laboratory workup includes a CBC showing a normal range of white blood cell count, normal platelet count, and a mild elevation of C-reactive protein. The patient is referred to participate in the clinical trial to determine the risk stratification of patients with suspected COVID-19 presenting to the ED.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. He has a history of chronic pancreatitis and has been undergoing routine imaging tests to monitor his condition. During his most recent imaging tests, a cystic tumour was detected in his pancreas, and his physician has recommended further evaluation. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and it is estimated that he has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. He is over 18 years of age and is capable of giving written informed consent. The patient has not had pancreatitis within the previous 3 months, and he is not allergic to fluorescein dye. He is willing to undergo EUS-guided nCLE as part of his routine diagnostic evaluation, and he meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

Patient is a 43-year-old woman from the United States who has recently been diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She is married and has two children. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. Her family history is significant for breast cancer in her grandmother. Her BMI is 26, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. Her laboratory study is unremarkable. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She is interested in participating in a neoadjuvant treatment clinical trial to improve her chances of survival.

A 25-year-old Caucasian male, who is generally healthy and physically active, is interested in participating in a study on itch mechanisms following injection of morphine. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to any medications. The patient does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has no history of drug addiction or any significant medical conditions. He is in good mental health and speaks fluent English. He has no skin diseases, moles, scars, or tattoos in the area where the injection will be administered. He is not taking any medications, including painkillers or antihistamines, and has not participated in any other trials within the past week. The patient is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow the study protocol.

This is a 48-year-old female diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil. She underwent a left tonsillectomy and biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis. A PET-CT scan was performed which showed no evidence of distant metastasis. She was staged at T2N1M0. After discussion with her multidisciplinary team, she was recommended to undergo curative radiation therapy with an anterior/posterior low neck field technique using a MedTec S-frame mask. She has no known allergies and is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 8 years presents with dyslipidemia. He is currently taking metformin to manage his diabetes but has not been prescribed any medications for his dyslipidemia. He reports occasional smoking and moderate alcohol consumption. He has not participated in any studies involving radioactive isotopes or larger x-ray investigations in the past 6 months and has not donated blood in the past 3 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of type 2 diabetes and dietary regulation on VLDL1- and VLDL2-triglyceride metabolism.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been wearing soft contact lenses for 5 years. She currently wears lotrafilcon B lenses on a daily wear modality for at least 3 days per week, 8 hours each day. She has no known ocular or systemic conditions that may affect the study outcome variables. Her visual acuity is correctable to 20/20 with her current lenses. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the performance of fanfilcon A lenses when worn on a daily wear modality over approximately 1 month in comparison to the lotrafilcon B lenses. She is willing and able to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule for the study. The patient has not undergone refractive error surgery and is not currently participating in any other concurrent clinical or research studies.

A 67-year-old Caucasian man, retired and living alone in his home, is concerned about his sedentary lifestyle and unhealthy eating habits. He reports that he spends most of his day sitting in front of the TV or computer and does not engage in any physical activity. He also admits to consuming unhealthy snacks and fast food on a regular basis. He feels isolated and would like to connect with others who are facing similar challenges. He speaks fluent English and has completed high school education. He has no history of cognitive impairment and has passed the TICS test. He does not have any visual or hearing impairment. He has not been engaged in structured physical exercise for the past 6 months. He does not have any health conditions or illnesses that would affect his participation in the study. He is willing to participate in a 12-week intervention followed by a 12-week maintenance phase. He is interested in using technology-based solutions to improve his health and social interactions.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 23, who maintains a healthy and balanced diet and has no history of smoking or any chronic medical condition. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the glycemic index, glycemic load, and insulinemic index of Spanish breads, as she is curious about the effects of different types of bread on her blood sugar levels. She has no known food allergies and is willing to follow the study requirements and procedures. She does not take any medication to treat blood pressure, glucose or lipid metabolism, nor has she taken any nutritional supplements in the past three months. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer three years ago. She has undergone a mastectomy and has been receiving treatment with CDK4/6 inhibitors. However, she has recently developed metastatic disease in her liver and lungs. She has no history of allergic reactions to taxanes, but her neuropathy is Grade 1. Her performance status is 1, and she has adequate kidney, liver, and hematologic laboratory values. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore additional treatment options.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it does not involve patients but instead focuses on the training of medical professionals in performing endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP). The study aims to evaluate the effect of different lengths of time for trainees to attempt selective cannulation during hands-on ERCP training on the success rate of cannulation, self-satisfaction of performance, and post-ERCP pancreatitis. The study will include individuals between the ages of 18-90 years old without prior endoscopic sphincterotomy. The exclusion criteria include individuals with a history of partial or total gastrectomy, duodenal stricture, ampullary carcinoma, previously failed selective cannulation, chronic pancreatitis with PD stone, minor papilla cannulation, papilla fistula, severe diseases of heart, lung, brain, and kidney, hemodynamical instability, pregnant women, and individuals who refuse or are unable to give written informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman with a history of chronic gastric ulcers. During a routine endoscopy, a biopsy revealed gastric epithelial neoplasia. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or medication use. The patient has never undergone any surgical procedures and has no known allergies. The patient is concerned about the diagnosis of gastric neoplasia and is interested in exploring all treatment options. The patient has been advised that her lesion meets the inclusion criteria for a clinical trial evaluating the safety and feasibility of using a thulium laser for endoscopic submucosal dissection. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the procedure.

45yo male with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2, sedentary lifestyle, and no history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or cancer. He has been weight stable for the past 6 months and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce his risk for cardiovascular disease and cancer. He is not currently taking any glucose lowering or weight loss medications. He is able to give written informed consent and is post-menopausal for at least 2 years, but is not on hormone replacement therapy.

56yo female with osteoarthritis of the right knee and scheduled for total knee replacement surgery. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and is a non-smoker. She reports no history of chronic pain and is currently not taking any long-acting opioid medications. She has a Motor Activity Assessment Scale (MAAS) score of 4 and is able to walk independently. She is not on any anticholinergic medications and has no history of autonomic neuropathy or other conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is able to communicate effectively and has no bilateral procedures planned for the near future.

The patient is a premature infant born at 30 weeks gestational age with a birth weight of 1200 grams. The infant is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and has been predominantly fed with breast milk (mother's milk or donor milk) since birth. The infant is appropriate for gestational age (AGA) with a birth weight between the 10th and 90th percentiles on the Fenton growth chart. The infant is a singleton birth and is currently 20 days old. Enteral intake of unfortified breast milk is at 70 mL/kg/day. The infant's mother has expressed willingness to continue breastfeeding for at least 28 days from the start of the study. The infant has not undergone any major surgery requiring general anesthesia, and has not received pharmacologic doses of glucocorticoids in the past 72 hours. The infant is not ventilator-dependent and does not require ≥ 40% fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) on day one of the study. The infant has not been diagnosed with grade III or IV bilateral intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) prior to or on study day one. The infant has not experienced feeding intolerance to breast milk feedings on study day one and has not consumed more than 3 feedings or 12 hours of continuous feeds of fortified breast milk prior to study day one. The infant does not have a fluid restriction < 120 mL/kg/d and has not had a history of creatinine >2.0 mg/dL 7 days prior to or on study day one. The infant is not currently receiving or planning to use probiotics.

This is a 35 year old male who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 2 years. The pain is described as a dull ache that is present at all times and worsens with prolonged sitting or standing. The patient has tried various treatments such as physical therapy, chiropractic, and pain medication but has not experienced significant relief. The patient is currently taking ibuprofen as needed for pain management. The patient has no history of peripheral pain or neuropathy but reports occasional headaches. The patient is an OHIP patient and is interested in participating in this study to explore a non-medication based approach to managing his chronic low back pain.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at the age of 24. He has two younger siblings who are also affected by the same condition. His parents are unaffected. He has been experiencing progressive vision loss and night blindness for the past 20 years. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to identify the genetic cause of his condition and potentially contribute to the development of new therapies.

The patient is a 12-year-old child with a family history of bipolar disorder. The child's mother was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and has been hospitalized multiple times due to severe depressive and manic episodes. The child has been experiencing emotional dysregulation and mood swings for the past year, which has affected their academic performance and social relationships. The child's CBCL-Total score is 65, indicating a high level of emotional and behavioral problems. The child has no history of autism spectrum disorders or intellectual disability. The family is interested in participating in the study to receive early intervention and improve the child's prognosis. They are willing to provide written informed consent for the trial.

42 yo M with a history of chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea for the past year, referred for further evaluation. Patient has no known history of gastrointestinal bleeding, dysphagia, gastric outlet obstruction, or known intestinal stenosis. No history of upper gastrointestinal or abdominal surgery altering gastrointestinal anatomy or postabdominal radiation. Patient has no known history of congestive heart failure, renal insufficiency, or in poor general condition (American Society of Anesthesiologists class III/IV). Patient does not have claustrophobia or any metallic parts, pacemaker or other implanted electromedical devices, or artificial heart valves. Patient is not pregnant or suspected to be pregnant. Patient is not currently participating in another clinical study. Past Medical History: - Chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea for the past year.

A 30-year-old woman gave birth to a premature baby at 30 weeks gestational age. The baby is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit and has been receiving enteral feeds since the first week of life. The parents have given consent for the baby to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the use of measuring gastric residuals in premature infants. The baby does not have perinatal asphyxia or any major congenital malformations. The baby is not currently requiring vasoactive drugs or experiencing respiratory failure.

45-year-old male from Indonesia presents with fever, cough, and difficulty breathing. He reports feeling unwell for the past week and has been experiencing progressively worsening symptoms. Upon examination, he has a high fever (39.5°C), tachycardia (heart rate 120 bpm), and low blood pressure (90/60 mmHg). His oxygen saturation is 88% on room air and he has crackles in his lungs on auscultation. Blood work shows a white blood cell count of 18,000/uL and a procalcitonin level of 5.2 ng/mL. Chest X-ray shows infiltrates in both lungs. He is diagnosed with community-acquired sepsis and is admitted to the hospital for further management. The attending physician determines that an infection is the primary cause of illness leading to hospitalization. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the observational study of the causes, management, and outcomes of community-acquired sepsis and severe sepsis in Southeast Asia. Informed consent is obtained and the patient is enrolled in the study at one of the participating hospitals in Indonesia.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of moderate plaque-type psoriasis involving 5% of her body surface area. She has been diagnosed with psoriasis for the past 5 years and has tried various topical treatments without significant improvement. She currently has a PASI score of 8. Her past medical history is significant for well-controlled hypertension and her current medications include lisinopril (20mg/day) and hydrochlorothiazide (25mg/day). She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has no history of autoimmune disorders or immunodeficiency diseases. She has not received any biologic agent/monoclonal antibody within the past 5 half-lifes prior to baseline. She has not received ultraviolet light treatment, cyclosporine, oral corticosteroids, methotrexate, oral retinoids, mycophenolate mofetil, thioguanine, hydroxyurea, sirolimus or azathioprine within the 4 weeks prior to baseline or had topical psoriasis treatment within the previous 2 weeks prior to baseline. She has a negative urine pregnancy test within 48 hours of randomization and is willing to use two forms of contraception as required by the study protocol. She has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2 and her blood pressure is well-controlled at 130/80 mm Hg. She has no active or unstable cardiovascular disease, and no history of gallstones or cholecystectomy. She has no hematologic or solid malignancy diagnosis within the past 5 years. She has no current diagnosis of major depressive disorder or any anxiety disorder requiring treatment with atypical antipsychotics, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or borderline personality disorder. Her screening lab tests are within normal limits, including serum bilirubin, AST, ALT, and neutrophil count.

Patient is a 25-year-old male who had a surgery for ulcerative colitis and now has an ileostomy for the last 5 months. He is currently using a convex ostomy appliance for the last month with a diameter of 30 mm. Over the last two weeks, the patient has experienced leakage (seeping) under the baseplate at least two times. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the last 2 months. The patient is not currently suffering from peristomal skin problems (i.e. bleeding or broken skin (weeping skin)). The patient has given written informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical investigation to investigate newly developed 1-piece convex baseplates for ileostomy patients.

The patient is a 35 year old female suffering from post-partum depression with symptoms of sadness, anxiety and difficulty sleeping. She has no prior history of depression, but has a family history of depression. She is currently not taking any medication for her symptoms and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has a negative urine drug screen and is not taking any medication that could alter her sleep pattern. She has a PSQI score of 7 indicating some sleep disturbance. She meets the DSM-IV criteria for Major Depressive Disorder and has a Hamilton Depression Rating Scale total score of 18. She is willing to wear the assigned light glasses for 2 hours prior to bedtime and 1 hour upon waking for 7 days. The patient has no other comorbid Axis I disorder or any other unstable medical condition that would confound the study results. She is able to provide informed consent and is compliant with the study procedures.

A 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus with a history of skin biopsy consistent with the diagnosis of SCLE. She has been intolerant to anti-malarial therapy or has been taking anti-malarial therapy for at least 3 months with residual disease activity. Her total cutaneous lupus erythematosus disease area and severity index (CLASI) activity is at least 10 with at least 2 areas with at least level 2 erythema or 3 areas with at least level 1 erythema. She has positive SS-A and/or SS-B antibodies and a stable dose of topical steroids no stronger than medium-potency for at least 2 weeks from screening. She has been stable for the past 3 months with no anticipated changes in therapy. She has been taking prednisone ≤ 10 mg/day (or equivalent) and stable doses of methotrexate ≤ 20 mg/week, azathioprine ≤ 150 mg/day, and 6-mercaptopurine ≤ 150 mg/day for 12 weeks prior to screening.

The patient is a 32-year-old man with type 1 diabetes for the past 10 years. Despite intensive insulin therapy, he has been experiencing frequent episodes of hypoglycemia unawareness, which has led to multiple emergency room visits. He has also developed mild neuropathy and retinopathy. The patient has been deemed eligible for islet transplantation alone and is being considered for participation in a clinical trial studying the effect of pre-transplant rapamycin treatment on islet engraftment. The patient does not have overt kidney disease, chronic liver disease, hepatic hemangioma, severe cardiomyopathy, or untreated coronary artery disease.

The patient is a 43-year-old male with a history of psychiatric disorders and chronic hepatitis C infection. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite for the past few months. His blood work showed elevated ALT levels (>30 U/L). He was diagnosed with HCV infection after a PCR-based assay test confirmed the presence of HCV-RNA in his blood for more than 6 months. He has no history of other liver diseases or cirrhosis, severe cardiac or neurological disease, co-infection with hepatitis B or HIV, hepatocellular carcinoma, or autoimmune disorders. His neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits. He would be eligible for the clinical trial investigating the use of IFN-alpha-2a and ribavirin in treating chronic hepatitis C in patients with psychiatric disorders or drug addiction.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor five weeks ago, and his craniotomy site has adequately healed. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for GBM or GS. He is willing to submit sufficient and of adequate quality tumor tissue representative of glioblastoma to perform MGMT promoter methylation status testing. His Karnofsky performance status (KPS) is ≥ 60, and he is stable or decreasing corticosteroids within 5 days prior to study treatment start. He is not taking any strong inducer or moderate or strong inhibitor of CYP3A4 within 7 days prior to randomization. He is willing to forego the use of Tumor Treating Fields therapy (Optune®). He has adequate organ function, and his serum pregnancy test is negative. He is using an effective method of contraception and willing to comply with the protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with follicular lymphoma. He presented with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of grade 2 follicular lymphoma. He has a positive BCL2/IgH rearrangement in both peripheral blood and bone marrow. His clinical stage is III and he meets the criteria for treatment due to progressive disease and a bulky tumor measuring 12 cm. He has no prior treatment for this condition. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not use any recreational drugs. He is married and works as an accountant. He has a good performance status with no significant comorbidities. His labs show a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL and a platelet count of 90 G/L. His cardiac and pulmonary function tests are normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of oral Fludarabine, Mitoxantrone und Rituximab induction therapy and Rituximab maintenance on the depth of remission measured by BCL2/IgH PCR.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who works as a firefighter. He has no significant medical history and is in good physical health. He has a BMI of 24. He is sexually active with his partner, who is using an intrauterine device for birth control. He has not traveled to West Africa in the last 12 months, nor does he have a history of exposure to Ebola. He has never received an Ad26- or MVA-based candidate vaccine in the past. He has no known allergies to vaccines or vaccine products. He does not have diabetes, thyroid disease, or uncontrolled hypertension. He has no major psychiatric illness or substance abuse problems. He is willing to participate in the study and is available for the duration of the study visits and follow-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman from Senegal who was recently diagnosed with HIV-1 infection during a routine health checkup. Her viral load is 15,000 copies/ml and her CD4+ T-cell count is 450 cells/µl. She has not received any antiretroviral therapy yet. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies or autoimmune diseases. Her liver and kidney function tests, blood cell counts, and hemoglobin levels are all within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written informed consent after receiving oral and written information. The patient is fully committed to following the instructions and attending all follow-up appointments. She is not pregnant and has not received any other vaccines or immune-modulating medicines within the past 3 months. She does not have any active chronic infectious diseases such as HIV-2, HBV, HCV, or TB. The patient is an ideal candidate for this clinical trial as she meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

43 yo healthy Japanese female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of a polyvalent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (pPCV) compared to PNEUMOVAX™. She has no history of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) within 3 years of Day 1 and has no known hypersensitivity to any vaccine components. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use contraception during the study period and for at least 30 days after completing the study. She has never participated in a clinical trial within the last 2 months and does not have any medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in this study according to the investigator's opinion.

A 55-year-old Native American woman presents to the Absentee Shawnee Tribal clinic for a routine check-up. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but otherwise, she is in good health. She denies any symptoms of heart palpitations, shortness of breath, or chest pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to screen for atrial fibrillation (AF) using a smartphone-based ECG device. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and her medical history does not include a known history of AF. The patient is excited to participate in the trial as she believes it is important to identify potential health issues early on and take preventative measures to reduce her risk of future health problems. She understands the potential benefits of early identification of AF and the importance of anticoagulation therapy in reducing her risk of stroke. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and give informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is an 18-year-old female who has recently graduated from high school and is preparing to attend college within the next six weeks. She has been diagnosed with anxiety and depression and has been receiving mental health services at the CC Waterdam clinic for the past three months. She is highly motivated to get better and feels that she needs additional support to manage her mental health during the transition to college. She owns a smartphone and is comfortable with texting. She is fluent in English and has no conditions that would impair her ability to engage in the Text2Connect intervention. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory loss and difficulty concentrating. She has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and has a mild to moderate dementia as measured by the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score. She lives with her daughter and son-in-law who are her primary caregivers. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well managed with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is not currently taking any medication for her Alzheimer's disease. She has no history of Parkinson's disease, Pick's disease, secondary or pseudodementias, currently diagnosed epilepsy, endocrine disorder, significant heart disease, drug or alcohol abuse, or kidney or liver dysfunction. She is willing to use appropriate birth control methods if applicable. She has no known sensitivity to the study drug.

A 26-year-old American woman who works as a customer service representative for a technology company is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has no significant medical history but has been feeling anxious and worried about her health lately. She is interested in learning more about preventative health measures and is willing to participate in a study that can help her understand how to better take care of herself. She has access to a computer and the internet and is comfortable using technology to gather information. She has a Mechanical Turk approval rate of 98%.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital due to worsening shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been taking medications for both conditions for the past 5 years. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. On admission, he was diagnosed with acute decompensated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. His BNP level was found to be elevated at 150pg/ml. He was treated with diuretics and discharged after 4 days of hospitalization. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to be contacted by telephone at the end of the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis for the past 2 years. She complains of redness, itching, and tearing in both eyes every spring and fall. She has tried over-the-counter allergy eye drops with temporary relief but is looking for a more effective treatment option. She has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. She has no known allergies and does not smoke. On examination, there is bilateral conjunctival injection, chemosis, and tearing. There is no discharge or corneal involvement. The rest of the ocular exam is unremarkable. The patient has been prescribed Relestat Ophthalmic Solution 0.05% as standard of care in clinical practice and is willing to participate in the study to help evaluate the safety and efficacy of this treatment.

A 45-year-old male with a history of symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease (sGERD) for the past 6 months. The patient has been experiencing moderate to severe upper abdominal pain on at least 3 out of the 7 consecutive days of the run-in period. The patient has reported episodes of heartburn 2 or more days during the 7 days prior to the screening visit. The patient had a normal endoscopy within 14 days of Visit 1, and has no history of esophageal, gastric or duodenal surgery except for closure of an ulcer. The patient has no history of severe liver disease, including cirrhosis and acute or chronic hepatitis. The patient does not have any other diseases or conditions listed in the protocol. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive treatment for upper abdominal pain associated with his sGERD.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of COPD diagnosed by GOLD and FEV1 of <80% predicted and FEV1/FVC <70%. He was recently diagnosed with primary lung cancer and is scheduled for single lobectomy surgery according to China guidelines on diagnosis and treatment of primary lung cancer. The patient is a former smoker who quit smoking two weeks before the operation. He has an ASA Classification of Anesthesia Risk in category 2 and his SP O2 is >90% before surgery. The patient's hemoglobin is 12g/dl and his BMI is 23. He has not taken systemic corticosteroids in the preceding 1 month before baseline and has not had pneumonia or a history of recent myocardial infarction, heart failure, tuberculosis, or known or suspected human immunodeficiency virus infection.

65-year-old post-menopausal female with a history of osteoporosis, with lumbar spine BMD T-score of -3.2 and femoral neck BMD T-score of -2.8. The patient is currently taking 1000mg of elemental calcium and 500 IU of vitamin D daily for 6 months. The patient is not on any medication that affects bone metabolism or systemic steroids, anticoagulants, anticonvulsants. The patient has no history of rhPTH use or known hypersensitivity to study drug. The patient's vitamin D3 level is within normal limits. The patient has normal thyroid function and no history of kidney disease, hypercalciuria, hypercalcemia or hyperparathyroidism. The patient has no history of active or treated tuberculosis or significant liver disease or gastrointestinal disease or cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old female healthcare professional working as a nurse in a hospital setting. She is experiencing moderate levels of stress due to the challenges of her job, which include dealing with patients who are in pain or facing serious health issues. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the effectiveness of self-care interventions mediated by the senses, such as aromatherapy, music therapy, and mindfulness meditation, to help reduce her stress levels and improve her overall well-being. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to sign a term of free and informed consent to participate in the study. She works during regular daytime hours and does not have any relevant dermatological findings that would exclude her from participation.

32F with a history of alcohol dependence and binge eating disorder presents to the clinic. The patient reports frequent episodes of binge eating at least three times a week for the past two weeks. She also reports a history of alcohol abuse and states that she consumes alcohol frequently on weekends. She reports no prior formal psychotherapy for binge eating or any other psychiatric disorder in the past 30 days. The patient also reports no history of severe hypersensitivity to any medication or environmental allergens. She is in good physical health and has no clinically significant laboratory screening test results or cardiovascular disease. The patient is currently not pregnant nor lactating and reports adhering to an acceptable form of contraception. She is literate in English and able to read, understand, and complete the ratings scales and questionnaires accurately. The patient has no history of non-response to topiramate for the treatment of binge-eating or alcohol disorder.

The patient is a healthy, 30-year-old male who does not have any chronic medical conditions. He leads an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. He has no history of smoking or illicit drug use. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He has a regular sleep schedule and is able to commit to staying awake and fasting for the duration of the 24-hour blood draw period. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

67-year-old female resident of New Mexico with a previous diagnosis of breast cancer who completed primary treatment (surgery, radiation, chemotherapy) and is not currently being treated for a recurrence. The patient reports mild-to-moderate physical functional impairment, experiencing limitations in at least two functions on the Short Form 36-item Physical Function Subscale. She is capable of speaking, reading, and understanding English and is currently participating in less than 120 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity. The patient is living independently and is able to walk 3 blocks without stopping to rest. She has a family member or friend available to be present during remote assessment of performance tests. The patient does not have any severe impairments or pre-existing medical limitations for engaging in daily light-intensity physical activity. There are no severe hearing or vision deficits that would inhibit communication with the research team via videoconferencing and tablet use. She is willing to use a tablet computer and videoconferencing software to communicate with a study team member during the assessment. The patient has enough space (14 feet by 3 feet) to safely conduct the physical function tests and is not at high risk for falls.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who works as a computer programmer in a software company. He has a history of multiple sexual partners in the past and he is sexually active. He does not have any significant past medical history and is not on any regular medications. He has no known allergies to any medications or vaccines. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has a BMI of 25 and has normal blood pressure. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to the development of an HIV vaccine. He has no history of HIV infection and is willing to undergo HIV testing as part of the study. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including receiving the vaccine and attending regular study visits. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study period, as required by the study protocol. He has access to a participating HIV Vaccine Trials Network (HVTN) clinical research site and is willing to be followed for the planned duration of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who sustained a closed femur fracture in a motor vehicle accident two days ago. He was brought to the hospital immediately and underwent an IM nailing procedure for fracture fixation. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He lives with his wife and two children. His occupation is a construction worker. He is able to understand and communicate in English. He will be eligible for the study as he meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma that has progressed despite castration therapy. He has experienced a rise in PSA on two successive determinations and has a PSA level of ≥2ng/ml. He has also developed bone disease progression with two or more new lesions on bone scan. The patient has undergone orchiectomy and has been on LHRH agonists for the past 6 months. The patient has clinical metastases that have been confirmed on imaging studies. Radiation therapy is recommended for the prostate gland and bone metastases. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate hepatic and renal function. The patient has not received any systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy, radiation, or other experimental therapy within the preceding 4 weeks. The patient has no prior history of autoimmune disorders requiring cytotoxic or immunosuppressive therapy, or autoimmune disorders with visceral involvement. The patient does not have significant cardiovascular disease, active bleeding disorders or evidence of chronic or acute disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). The patient is not receiving therapeutic anticoagulation for reasons other than venous catheter patency.

The patient is a 3-year-old girl who has been suffering from constipation for the past year. She has difficulty passing stools and experiences pain during defecation. Her stools are typically hard and infrequent, occurring only twice a week. She has not been using diapers for the past year and has sufficient toilet training. Her parents have tried various interventions, including dietary adjustments and over-the-counter laxatives, but have not seen any significant improvement. The patient has no history of other medical issues and is up to date on all age-appropriate vaccinations. Her family history is negative for gastrointestinal disorders. Her parents are fluent in the local language and have given written informed consent for her participation in the study. She has not used any labeled pre- or probiotics or antibiotics in the past 4 weeks and has not used laxatives in the past 2 weeks, making her eligible for inclusion in the study.

Maria is a 50 year old woman who has been on dialysis for the past 2 years due to end-stage renal disease. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has a BMI of 32 and undergoes regular exercise and dietary modifications to manage her diabetes. Maria recently received a kidney transplant from an Expanded Criteria Donor (ECD) 4 months ago. She is currently taking tacrolimus and mycophenolate mofetil as part of her immunosuppressive regimen. Her serum creatinine and electrolyte levels have been stable since her transplant surgery. Maria's nephrologist has recommended her to participate in this study to evaluate the use of sirolimus as a base therapy in kidney allograft recipients from ECD donors. Maria has given her informed consent to participate in this pilot study. She is not pregnant nor lactating at the time of enrollment.

A 62 year old woman with complaints of blurry vision and difficulty seeing at night is seeking treatment for her eye condition. She has a history of cataracts and her ophthalmologist has recommended phacoemulsification surgery with intraocular lens implantation. Upon examination, her anterior chamber depth (ACD) was found to be less than 2.68mm and the anterior chamber angle width on gonioscopy was ≤Shaffer 2, indicating a shallow anterior chamber and narrow angle. She does not have a history of primary or secondary glaucoma, peripheral anterior synechiae, or any previous ocular surgeries. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate changes in anterior chamber angle configuration after phacoemulsification and IOL implantation in eyes with similar conditions as hers.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar I disorder for 10 years. She has a history of multiple manic and depressive episodes and has been hospitalized several times in the past. She is currently experiencing severe agitation and restlessness, which is causing her distress and interfering with her daily activities. She is not currently taking any medication for her bipolar disorder as she has been non-compliant with her previous prescriptions. She has a history of substance abuse, specifically cocaine and alcohol, and is in recovery. She lives with her husband and two children and works part-time as a receptionist. She has no known allergies and has never been treated with ADASUVE before. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical exam is unremarkable.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months. The pain is primarily located in the area of the iliac crest and occasionally radiates to the lower limb, making it difficult to sit or stand for long periods of time. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. He has no history of trauma or any chronic medical conditions. He is generally healthy, with no known allergies or medication use. He is seeking further evaluation and possible treatment options for his persistent low back pain.

Patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD and is currently attending elementary school. He has been experiencing difficulties in paying attention, completing tasks, and following instructions. His parents have tried medication, but they would like to explore non-pharmacological interventions to help their child. The patient has no history of moderate or severe neurological or psychiatric disorders. The family is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial and commit to attending Cog-Fun treatment sessions with their child for three months.

The patient is a 54 year-old male who was diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, decreased appetite, and unintentional weight loss for several months. He underwent a diagnostic endoscopy which revealed a large mass in his stomach. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma. The cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes and the liver. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of heart disease or other serious medical conditions. He is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has not undergone any previous cancer treatments such as chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. He understands that he may receive a combination of chemotherapy and Precision Cell immunotherapy, and that there may be potential risks and benefits associated with the treatment.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who has been experiencing a persistent ringing sensation in both of her ears for the past year. She reports that the tinnitus has been affecting her daily life, causing her to experience difficulty concentrating and sleeping. She has visited several ENT clinics and undergone various treatments, but her symptoms have not improved. She does not have a history of psychiatric or neurological diseases, and has no known conditions that could explain her tinnitus. She has also not been exposed to loud noise that could have caused hearing loss. Her hearing test results show no cochlear or retro-cochlear damage, and she does not have any conductive or mixed hearing loss. However, she has been diagnosed with systemic vascular disease and has been taking medication for the condition. She does not have Meniere's disease or any other vestibular disorders. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Sulodexide.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a 7-year history of Parkinson's disease. He has been taking a combination of levodopa, dopamine agonists, and MAOB inhibitors for more than 3 months, and his motor symptoms have been well controlled. However, he has been experiencing impulse control disorders, including pathological gambling and hypersexuality, over the past few months, which have negatively impacted his personal and professional life. He is currently married and works as a financial advisor. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. His BP: 130/80, HR: 85/min, and his BMI is 28.6. His lab results are normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of pimavanserin in treating impulse control disorders in Parkinson's disease. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol, including taking the study drug as prescribed and attending all study visits. He is not planning to have any significant changes in his medication regimen during the study period. He has no history of allergic reactions to drugs in the same class as pimavanserin. He is willing to use effective contraception methods during the study period, as he is not planning to father a child during this time.

52-year-old female diagnosed with type II diabetes presents with a chronic foot ulcer that has been present for 8 weeks. The patient reports a history of poor glucose control and has a hemoglobin A1C level of 10.2%. The ulcer is located on the plantar aspect of the right foot and is classified as a Wagner grade 2 ulcer. The patient reports no rest pain or critical ischemia, and the ankle-arm index is 0.8. The patient is not currently taking any prostaglandins or vasodilators for the ulcer, nor any corticoids. The patient has no known history of HIV or hepatitis infection, suppression of the immune system, or hemophilia. The patient has not received chemotherapy in the past 60 days and is not currently participating in any other studies. The patient is able to give informed consent and does not have any mental disabilities.

The patient is a 46-year-old male who underwent an elective surgery and is currently in the intensive care unit for postoperative care. He requires mechanical breathing support with intubation and ventilation. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He has no prior history of sedation or adverse reactions to sedatives. The patient is an ASA II status. He has no known allergies to medications. He is able to communicate and understand the study requirements. He is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old female dentist with a history of neck pain for the past 4 months visited the clinic seeking treatment. She has been practicing dentistry for 8 months and treats approximately 6 patients per day, with each appointment lasting an average of 30 minutes. She has no history of cervical fracture or radiculopathy, and has not undergone any surgery to her neck or shoulder. She has not been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, and is not on any long-term anticoagulant or corticosteroid therapy. Her neck pain is rated as moderate to severe on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), and she reports difficulty with maintaining proper posture while treating patients. She has tried various treatments for her neck pain, including massage and stretching exercises, but has not experienced significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of Bowen's technique on postural neck pain among dentists, and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

Patient is a 56-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for 20 years and has recently experienced symptoms of dyspnea and fatigue. Imaging studies have revealed a malignant pleural effusion in the right lung. The patient's granulocyte count is 2,500/mm^3 and platelet count is 120,000/mm^3. His performance status is CTC 1. He has no allergies to talc and no surgical contraindications to talc usage. He is not pregnant or nursing and uses effective contraception. He has not undergone any prior intrapleural therapy or surgical pleurectomy. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female of Indian ethnicity, with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications or supplements. She does not smoke or consume alcohol, and she has not participated in any other biomedical studies in the past 3 months. She reports exercising moderately for 3-4 hours a week. Her fasting blood glucose levels are within the normal range of 3.4-6.1 mmol/litre (62-110 mg/dl). Her hemoglobin levels are within the clinically acceptable range for females. She has no known food or cosmetic allergies. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period and she is not lactating. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is willing to be informed about any medically relevant personal test results by the study physician.

42-year-old male with a history of glaucoma and currently taking bimatoprost (Lumigan 0.01%) to reduce intraocular pressure. The patient has noticed that his fingernails have grown longer and become less brittle since starting the medication. He is interested in participating in a study to investigate the effect of topical application of bimatoprost on nail growth and brittleness. The patient does not have any nail injuries, deformities or infections, is not on any hand lotions or creams containing essential fatty acids, and does not have any allergies or sensitivity to prostaglandin agents. The patient is willing to avoid nail biting, nail polish, artificial nails, and nail trimming and filing for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old HIV-positive male who has experienced significant unintentional weight loss over the past year, resulting in a weight 12% less than the lower limit of Ideal Body Weight for his frame size. The weight loss is associated with AIDS-related wasting, and not due to any other disease process. He is currently taking a stable regimen of HIV anti-retroviral treatments for the past 6 months. The patient is willing to return to the clinic regularly for study visits and is able to complete a 3-day food intake diary with instruction. He is willing to abstain from any illegal or recreational drug substances for the duration of the trial and from taking any other medications or substances known to affect appetite or weight gain. The patient is able to read and write in the study-related documents translated into the primary local language and is willing to use effective contraception for the duration of the study and for two weeks after the last dose. The patient has no history of thromboembolic events or any first degree relative with a history of thromboembolic events. He does not have any active AIDS-defining illness or any other clinically significant or uncontrolled medical problems. The patient has not undergone systemic treatment with glucocorticoids within the 12 months prior to study entry.

Unfortunately, as this is a follow-up study for infants who were previously enrolled in a different study, there is no patient description to generate. However, the inclusion and exclusion criteria are provided in the study description.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) during her third trimester. She has a medical history of hypothyroidism, which is being managed with levothyroxine. Her BMI is within the normal range. The patient has been recommended for induction of labor due to her ICP. She has not had any previous deliveries and has not undergone an elective caesarian section. She has been receiving ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) treatment for her ICP. The patient is willing to participate in the retrospective cohort study to determine the impact of ICP on delivery procedures and fetal and maternal outcomes in induced labor, and the possible impact of UDCA treatment.

Patient is a 25-year-old female who presents with a history of allergic reactions to multiple antibiotics, including penicillin, aminopenicillins, and cephalosporins. She reports experiencing symptoms such as hives, swelling, and difficulty breathing after taking these medications in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if she is truly allergic to penicillin and if she can safely take the medication in the future. She is currently not taking any antihistamines and is in good overall health. She is eager to contribute to medical research and hopes that her participation in this study will help others with similar allergies.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma). He has never received chemotherapy or biologic therapy for his cancer. The patient reports a 30 pack-year smoking history and has quit smoking 2 months ago. He presents with shortness of breath, cough, and weight loss of 10 pounds over the last 3 months. The patient has no history of brain metastases, and a CT scan of his brain was negative. He has measurable disease documented by CT of the chest and upper abdomen. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 1, and his laboratory studies show: ANC: 4,500/mm3 Platelet count: 210,000/mm3 Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL Serum creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL Creatinine clearance: 75 mL/min Serum bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL SGOT: 24 U/L SGPT: 18 U/L INR: 1.0 UPC ratio: 0.2 The patient is willing to provide his smoking history and agrees to use effective contraceptive methods during protocol treatment and for at least 6 months following completion of bevacizumab treatment.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis came to the clinic with complaints of joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. She was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 5 years ago and has been taking methotrexate and prednisone regularly.
