Her blood pressure was elevated, and her LDL-cholesterol level was higher than normal in the latest lab work. She reported smoking cigarettes and was worried about her cardiovascular risk. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial that aimed to reduce her risk of cardiovascular disease through pharmacist intervention.

Patient B is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with depression and anxiety. She has been experiencing trouble falling asleep and staying asleep for the past 6 months, which has been affecting her daily functioning. She is currently being treated for her mental health conditions at the Department of Psychiatry at Diakonhjemmet Hospital. She reports feeling tired and fatigued during the day, which has been making it difficult for her to concentrate at work. She denies any substance abuse and has no history of mental retardation or dementia. She is fluent in Norwegian and able to provide informed consent. She is interested in participating in the cognitive behavioral therapy course for insomnia offered at the hospital.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has a history of coronary artery disease and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement 6 months ago. He was started on dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin and Clopidogrel), which he has been taking regularly. He is currently experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion, despite optimal medical therapy. He was advised to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with or without valve replacement. He has been evaluated by a cardiologist and a cardiothoracic surgeon and deemed a suitable candidate for surgery. He has no history of bleeding disorders or recent bleeding episodes. He has no allergy to any medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He lives with his wife and two adult children. He is a retired accountant and enjoys playing golf in his free time. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with the use of dual antiplatelet therapy during surgery.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and underwent a donor stem cell transplant with her sister as the donor. She had a history of osteopenia before the transplant and her bone mineral density decreased by 7% in the lumbar spine on her DXA scan done 3 months after the transplant. The patient complains of lower back pain and difficulty walking. She is currently taking calcium and vitamin D supplements, but her symptoms have not improved. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of significant medical problems. She has no known allergies to medications. She is still menstruating, but has no plans for pregnancy. She is willing to use adequate contraceptive methods during the study period. The patient understands the investigational nature of the study and has signed an informed consent form. She is able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to receive two doses of denosumab subcutaneously as per the study protocol.

Patient is a 42-year-old female with a history of fibromyalgia diagnosed by a rheumatologist based on American College of Rheumatology criteria. She complains of chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and difficulty breathing. She has tried multiple medications for symptomatic relief but has not seen significant improvement. She has no history of smoking or pulmonary disease but has a history of mild spinal injury due to a motor vehicle accident. Her pain is rated at 7 out of 10 on a numeric pain rating scale. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of muscle energy techniques and breathing exercises in improving her functional outcomes.

The patient is a 30-year-old Caucasian male who is generally in good health. He has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 20-28 kg/m², and he is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He does not have a history of chronic diseases. He does not consume n-3 FA rich fish, and he has no allergy or intolerance to fish or fish oil. He is not a regular alcohol or drug user, and he has not participated in any other investigational drug or device trial within the last 30 days. He is willing to attend the investigator's orders and comply with the study conditions, including the consumption of the study drugs according to the dosage recommendation. The patient is able to provide written confirmation of his willingness to participate in the study after receiving detailed spoken and written explanation about the study contents.

A 66-year-old man was diagnosed with stage IV prostate cancer that has not responded to hormone therapy. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He also had a myocardial infarction 2 years ago, which was treated with angioplasty and stenting. He has no history of congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular accident, or atrial fibrillation. He has bone metastases, which cause him significant pain, and his SWOG performance status is 2. He has not received any chemotherapy, biological therapy, or radiotherapy in the past. He has not undergone surgery for prostate cancer, but he has had an orchiectomy. His PSA level is greater than 5 ng/mL. He is not currently on any anticoagulation therapy.

The patient is a 62 year old male who has been experiencing pain in his right hip for over a year. The pain limits his ability to perform his daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. He has tried physical therapy and pain management but they did not provide significant relief. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of neurological or cognitive disorders. He is a retired engineer and enjoys spending time with his family and participating in community events. His BMI is 30 and he lives 70 km away from London, Ontario. He speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help advance medical research.

A 62-year-old retired woman, who has been leading a sedentary lifestyle for the past two years, is interested in participating in the Neural Activation and Connectivity in Response to Exercise and Cognitive Training study. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any psychotropic medication, beta blockers, or calcium channel blockers. She has completed the screening process for the parent study, EXACT, and meets the inclusion criteria. The participant is physically able to perform the exercise and cognitive training program and has no contraindication to MRI scanning.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been experiencing recurring pain in his lower back for the past six months. He has tried various treatments such as physiotherapy and medication, but the pain has not subsided. Therefore, he has been advised by his physician to undergo surgery for his back problem. The patient has agreed to undergo the surgery and general anesthesia is required for the procedure. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and his American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) status is 2. The expected duration of the anesthesia is more than 30 minutes and the patient needs endotracheal intubation. The patient speaks Finnish fluently and can communicate effectively in the language. There is no history of significant disorders of the autonomic or central nervous system in the patient's medical history. Additionally, there is no family history of malignant hyperthermia or clinical history of anaphylactic reactions against inhaled anesthetics.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) at an early stage. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue lately. He was diagnosed with heart failure and his doctor is concerned about the progression of his condition. The patient has not undergone renal replacement therapy and is not on corticoid therapy. He has no history of infections or cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test new biomarkers for heart failure in early stage CKD.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing fatigue, fever, and unexplained weight loss for the past few months. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has also noticed that she bruises easily and has frequent nosebleeds. Her blood work shows abnormal white blood cell counts, and a bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). She has not received any chemotherapy yet. She is concerned about her prognosis and is willing to participate in clinical trials to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis two years ago. She has had multiple flare-ups despite being on various medications including mesalamine, prednisone, and azathioprine. Her current disease activity is moderate-to-severe, as confirmed by a raised fecal calprotectin level and endoscopic disease activity Mayo 2. She is experiencing abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and urgency to pass stools. She has lost some weight due to decreased appetite. She does not have any other significant medical history. She is married and works as a graphic designer. She has good English language skills and is able to understand the patient information sheet and consent form. She has been recommended induction therapy with vedolizumab and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the faecal loss of vedolizumab and its correlation with serum drug levels and UC disease activity.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, who has developed metastatic disease to the liver and lungs. HER2 testing has been negative, and the cancer has been confirmed to be triple-negative breast cancer. The patient has undergone one line of chemotherapy in the non-curative setting and has not progressed within one year following completion of curative-intent chemotherapy. The patient has no active brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases, no serious or uncontrolled medical disorders, and has recovered from the effects of any prior surgeries. The patient has not had prior treatment with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies in the metastatic setting, nor has she been treated with bicalutamide, enzalutamide, or any other androgen receptor blocker. The patient must have a positive androgen-receptor (AR) status to be eligible for this study. The patient is willing to follow instructions for methods of birth regulation for the duration of treatment and up to 5 months post-treatment completion. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests, tumor biopsies, and other requirements of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer. She noticed a lump on her left breast during a self-exam and sought medical attention. The biopsy confirmed her suspicion, and she is now seeking treatment. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has no significant medical history, and her only medication is a daily multivitamin. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. Her BMI is 25, and her blood pressure is normal. She has no allergies. She is fluent in English and Spanish. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. She has a baseline mammogram and clip placement. Her ECOG performance status is 0. She has normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by echocardiography. Her organ function tests are within normal limits. She is not pregnant and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study. She has not received any prior chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, biologic therapy, investigational agent, targeted therapy, or radiation therapy for breast cancer. She has no history of other malignancies.

A 32 year old patient with Churg-Strauss syndrome presents with refractory asthma, eosinophilia, and pulmonary infiltrates. The patient has been receiving corticosteroid therapy and has also been prescribed other immunosuppressive agents such as cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine A, Rituximab, and azathioprine, but the condition is still not stabilized. The patient has also shown symptoms of cardiac involvement such as arrhythmias and failure. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. The baseline serum creatinine is <1.5 mg/dL, left ventricular ejection fraction is >55%, and pulmonary functions are adequate with oxygen saturation at room air of >90%. The patient has no history of malignancy except for localized cutaneous basal or squamous cell carcinoma in situ of the cervix. The patient is willing to undergo the proposed combination of high dose chemotherapy, antibodies, and radiation followed by stem cell transplant as part of the clinical trial. The patient is not allergic to cyclophosphamide, rituximab, mepolizumab or azathioprine.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing migraine headaches for the past 5 years. She has an average of 8-10 migraine episodes per month, each lasting between 4-72 hours. The patient reports that her headaches are usually accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried several medications for her migraines, including triptans and NSAIDs, but has not found significant relief. The patient is currently not taking any medications for her migraines and is willing to try new treatments. She wears glasses for mild myopia and is willing to switch to the Avulux device if it helps reduce the frequency and severity of her migraines. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to complete all scheduled study visits.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and weight loss. Biopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of advanced pancreatic cancer. He is currently in good general health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of allergies or other significant medical conditions. He has never received chemotherapy or radiation therapy before. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the treatment and follow-up procedures. He understands the risks and benefits of the study, and has provided signed informed consent. His measurable objective lesion meets the RECIST 1.1 criteria. He is a non-lactating male and has agreed to take effective contraceptive measures during the study period. He meets all eligibility criteria for the study and is therefore a suitable candidate for the trial.

51 year old man with a history of progressive muscle weakness and difficulty controlling his movements, for which he has been seeing a neurologist for several months. He has undergone several tests, including blood work and imaging studies, which have not provided a definitive diagnosis. He has recently been referred for electromyography to further investigate his neuromuscular disorder. Past Medical History: Hypertension, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, Hyperlipidemia, Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), Coronary artery disease (CAD), and Chronic kidney disease (CKD). He is currently taking several medications including metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and albuterol.

A 12-year-old girl with a history of B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who experienced her first relapse with bone marrow blast percentage of 10% and was treated with multiagent chemotherapy for 4 weeks with complete response. She will now be randomized to receive either one cycle of blinatumomab or one block of standard high-risk consolidation chemotherapy. The patient has no prior history of CNS involvement and has no clinically relevant CNS pathology requiring treatment. Her renal and hepatic function is normal, and her peripheral blood counts are within normal limits. She is not currently on any other investigational device or drug study and has no chemotherapy related toxicities. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to immunoglobulins or any of the products or components to be administered during dosing. She is post-menarchal and is willing to practice true sexual abstinence while receiving protocol-specified therapy and for at least 6 months after the last dose of blinatumomab or for 12 months after the last dose of chemotherapy. The patient and her legally acceptable representative have provided informed consent and written assent based on local regulations and/or guidelines prior to any study-specific activities/procedures being initiated.

33-year-old G2P1 woman at 39 weeks and 3 days of gestation was admitted to the hospital in labor. Her prenatal course was uncomplicated, and she had no significant medical history. Her initial cervical exam was 4 cm dilated, and the fetal heart rate tracing was Category II. During labor, the amniotic fluid was noted to be meconium-stained. The patient progressed to complete dilation and was taken to the delivery room for a spontaneous vaginal delivery. The infant was born non-vigorous with poor muscle tone and respiratory effort. The infant was immediately randomized to either endotracheal suctioning or routine resuscitation. The study team obtained consent from the mother, who speaks English. The infant's birth weight was 3,400 grams, and Apgar scores were 3 at 1 minute and 7 at 5 minutes after delivery. The infant was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit for further management.

A 34-year-old woman was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 2 years ago after experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She underwent surgical resection of her ileocolonic region 6 months ago and has been on medication since then. She has a history of taking adalimumab for 3 months before the surgery, but it was discontinued due to tolerability issues. She is at an increased risk of recurrence of active Crohn's disease and is willing to participate in the study. She is not currently experiencing any active infections and has no known malignancies. She is willing to undergo screening for HBV and has adequate blood and liver test values. She has a baseline CDAI score of less than 200. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent pain in his right shoulder and arm for the past year. He has been diagnosed with a rotator cuff tear and is scheduled for unilateral orthopedic humerus surgery. Patient A is willing to undergo a peripheral nerve block technique for his surgery and is 18 years of age or older. He has no history of neuropathy in the affected extremity. Patient A is able to cooperate with the procedure and has agreed to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 33-year-old Hispanic male who was diagnosed with asthma at the age of 12. He has been using a daily inhaled steroid for the past year and has been taking a beta-agonist as needed for symptom relief. He is a non-smoker and has not experienced an asthma exacerbation in the past 6 weeks. He has been experiencing moderate to severe asthma symptoms, including wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing, despite his current treatment regimen. His FEV1 is less than or equal to 70 percent of predicted normal. He is not currently using unstable doses of steroids and is not participating in any other interventional trials. The patient is interested in participating in the study to determine whether inhaled Combivent® CFC MDI can provide superior bronchodilator efficacy compared to Albuterol HFA MDI in the treatment of his moderate to severe asthma.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of advanced lung cancer. He has previously undergone standard cancer treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but has not experienced any improvement in his condition. He is experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath, which has severely impacted his ability to perform daily activities. The patient has a performance status of 1 and is expected to live for more than three months. He has no significant medical history and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past four weeks. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a newborn baby boy who just underwent heart surgery in the Pediatric Cardio Vascular Surgery Intensive Care Unit. He is currently being fed through a nasogastric tube and has not shown any signs of infection. The baby is 2 days old and has a gestational age of 38 weeks. He is not using any narcotic drugs and has no factors that could interfere with feeding. The parents have provided informed consent for the baby to participate in the study.

35 year old Filipino male with no known allergies or medical conditions, who has been prescribed Prevenar 13 vaccine as a preventive measure against pneumococcal infections. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide consent for inclusion in the study. He has not experienced any adverse reactions to vaccines in the past.

A 58-year-old female with a history of COPD is seeking to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the long-term effects of a pulmonary rehabilitation maintenance program. She has a history of smoking for 20 years and has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. The patient experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion and has difficulty performing daily activities. She has undergone a pulmonary rehabilitation program in the past and has noticed improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a maintenance program to further improve her quality of life and manage her chronic respiratory disease. The patient has no contraindications to exercise training and is willing to commit to a long-term program.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He underwent a previous PCI via the radial artery without any complications. He is scheduled for an elective PCI procedure via the right radial artery. He takes aspirin and clopidogrel daily and has discontinued them 5 days before the procedure, as instructed. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not sexually active, and his menses are not applicable. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 200000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl Beta hcg: not applicable. He is willing to give written informed consent and meet all inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

There is no patient involvement in this clinical trial as it is a qualitative case study exploring the experiences of maternity staff in England while implementing the Baby Friendly Initiative standards. This study is focused on the perspectives of the staff and does not involve any patients or their care.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works in a desk job and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and has a history of gout in his family. He is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol regularly. He has no history of kidney stones, xanthinuria or malignancy. He is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. His latest sUA value is 9.2 mg/dl, which is higher than the normal range. He has no clinically relevant abnormalities in vital signs, ECG, physical examination or laboratory values, except for slightly elevated liver function tests with ALT and AST both at 1.3 times the upper limit of normal. He has not donated blood or received blood transfusions in the last 3 months.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma. He has confirmed liver cirrhosis and chronic hepatitis C virus infection. He has one or more hypervascular liver masses more than 2 cm and alpha-fetoprotein greater than 400 ng/mL, which has doubled in value during the past three months. He has been deemed unresectable and has not had any prior surgical resection. He has not had any tumor invading the main portal vein or occupying more than 50% of the liver volume. He has Child-Pugh class A or compensated Child-Pugh class B liver dysfunction. He has no extrahepatic metastasis and no documented brain metastases or clinical evidence of CNS disease. He has an ECOG performance status of 0-2, absolute neutrophil count greater than 1,500/mm^3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, and platelet count at least 75,000/mm^3. He has no prior serious bleeding event unrelated to liver disease, no bleeding diathesis, no coagulopathy, bilirubin no greater than 3 mg/dL, transaminases less than 5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), albumin at least 2.5 mg/dL, PTT less than 4 seconds above ULN, INR less than 1.5 (for patients receiving warfarin), and creatinine less than 1.5 g/dL. He has no thromboembolic event within the past 12 months and no clinically significant cardiovascular disease. He is not pregnant or nursing and has had a negative pregnancy test. He has no active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics, no serious non-healing wound/ulcer or bone fracture, and no variceal bleeding within the past 6 months. He has not had any malignancy within the past 5 years except localized nonmelanoma skin cancer. He has no ongoing psychiatric or social situation that would preclude study compliance. He has no known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or other recombinant human antibodies. He has had no more than 1 prior biologic therapy and no concurrent interferon or interleukin-2. He has had no more than 1 prior antineoplastic chemotherapy and at least 4 weeks since prior invasive surgery, including open biopsy. He is not currently undergoing hepatic transplant, has had at least 4 weeks since prior anticancer therapy, and is not undergoing concurrent platelet-stimulating factors or full-dose anticoagulants or thrombolytic agents. He is not taking any chronic daily antiplatelet drugs.

This is a 12-year-old female with cystic fibrosis who has been experiencing symptoms of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malabsorption. Despite receiving enzyme replacement therapy, she continues to have difficulty maintaining adequate nutritional status. She has a history of low fecal elastase and has been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis based on her presentation, genotype, and sweat chloride levels. She is currently in fair-to-good nutritional status but has had difficulty gaining weight and maintaining proper growth due to her EPI. She has not had a history of fibrosing colonopathy or distal intestinal obstruction syndrome in the past six months, nor is she currently receiving enteral tube feedings. She does not have any chronic diarrheal illness unrelated to pancreatic insufficiency, and she has not had any liver abnormalities, liver or lung transplant, or significant bowel resection in the past. She is interested in participating in the SIMPLICITY study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Liprotamase Powder for Oral Solution as a new treatment option for her EPI.

The patient is a 19-year-old Caucasian male who has been struggling with moderate to severe acne vulgaris on his face. He has tried various topical treatments and medicated cleansers but has not seen significant improvement. He has approximately 30-40 inflammatory lesions and 50-60 noninflammatory lesions, including open and closed comedones. He has not used any acne medication for at least 4 weeks prior to the study. He is not using any other medications and has no significant past medical history. He is not currently sexually active but is willing to use an effective method of contraception throughout the study. He is willing to comply with study requirements and procedures, including mandatory photography. He weighs 72 kg and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

65 yo male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, coronary artery disease, and poor left ventricular function. Patient's most recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 30% and moderate mitral regurgitation. Patient has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath on exertion and has been admitted for aortocoronary bypass surgery. The patient has a Parsonnet score of 8. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 40-pack-year smoking history. The patient's renal function is within normal limits, with a creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus or liver disease. The patient's BMI is 28. The patient is able to understand and give informed consent for this study.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male or female volunteers between the ages of 18 to 55 years old, with a BMI of 18 to 32 kg/m^2. Participants should not be taking any prescribed or over-the-counter drugs or herbal remedies in the 2 weeks prior to screening. Women of child-bearing potential should agree to use 2 methods of adequate contraception throughout the study and for 30 days after study drug administration. Participants should not have a known or suspected history of alcohol or drug abuse, and should be willing to abstain from alcohol, caffeine, and nicotine-containing products throughout the period of in-patient confinement. Participants who have received any experimental drug within the 12 weeks leading up to the start of study drug treatment or who are currently enrolled in another clinical trial will be excluded.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old woman who has not used any hormone contraceptives for at least 28 days. She has a regular menstrual cycle that occurs every 28 days on average, varying from 25 to 35 days. She is a non-smoker and has a Body Mass Index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 24.9. She weighs more than 50 kg and is willing to use lubricated condoms with spermicidal or a diaphragm with spermicidal during the study period. She has a systolic pressure up to 130 mmHg and diastolic pressure up to 85 mmHg. She has no history of clinically significant hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she is not using prescription or nonprescription drugs or dietary supplements within 7 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of study medication. She has not used any hormonal methods of contraception, including oral and transdermal contraceptives, injectable progesterone, progestin subdermal implants, progesterone-releasing IUDs, postcoital contraceptive methods, or hormone replacement therapy for at least 28 days before the first dose of the study medication. She has not used an injection contraceptive of Medroxyprogesterone Acetate one year before the beginning of the study and has not had sexual intercourse without a contraceptive method within the last 14 days. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and is looking to participate in clinical trials to find better treatment options. He has a BMI of 32 and is generally healthy, with no history of cancer or anemia. He does not drink alcohol or abuse any medications. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet but struggles to maintain his blood glucose levels. He has not been prescribed insulin and has no history of pancreatitis. He is not claustrophobic and weighs less than 130 kilograms. He has no known allergies to any medications and is willing to take metformin as part of the trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of advanced colorectal cancer. He was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon 2 years ago and underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX. He had a good response to the initial treatment, but unfortunately, the cancer has progressed and metastasized to his liver. He is currently receiving second-line chemotherapy with FOLFIRI, but his disease continues to progress. He has a good performance status and is able to carry out his daily activities without assistance. He has no history of thromboembolic disease or cardiovascular disease. He has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. He has provided tissue samples for analyses. He has adequate protection for women of child-bearing potential as he is not sexually active. He is willing to participate in clinical trials to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome and underwent Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with stent implantation. The patient weighs 75 kg and has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. He has a glomerular filtration rate of 65 ml/min and does not require hemodialysis. The patient has no known contraindications for Ticagrelor or Prasugrel. He has a sinus rhythm and does not have severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. His ejection fraction is within normal limits, and he does not have cardiogenic shock. The patient does not have severe left ventricular hypertrophy or severe valvular disease. He has diffuse coronary atherosclerosis. The patient has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who has a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. She presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath, fatigue and swelling in her legs. Her blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg, and her heart rate is 110 beats per minute. Laboratory workup reveals elevated serum creatinine levels on admission. She has no history of atrial fibrillation or obstructive uropathy. She denies any recent exposure to potential nephrotoxic drugs such as metformin, antibiotics, chemotherapeutics, iodinated contrast agents and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents. She has never been diagnosed with ascites and has not needed positive inotropic agents. Her medical history includes a hysterectomy and she takes lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for her hypertension. She has never been diagnosed with heart failure before.

75-year-old male with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) presents with fatigue, night sweats, and a 10-pound weight loss over the past 3 months. Blood tests show an elevated white blood cell count and enlarged lymph nodes on imaging studies. The patient has not received any prior treatment for CLL and has no history of allergies to medications. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal liver and kidney function. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the initial treatment of CLL and meets the eligibility criteria for the study investigating bendamustine in combination with rituximab in adults age 65 or older.

This is a 58 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented to the emergency department with chest pain and was diagnosed with a large anterior myocardial infarction due to occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending coronary artery. The patient underwent successful primary stented PCI 8 hours after symptom onset. The echocardiogram performed 24 hours after PCI showed a reduced LV ejection fraction of 40% with 4 akinetic segments in the LAD perfusion territory. The patient was referred for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of intracoronary injection of autologous bone marrow-derived mononuclear cells (BMNCs) in patients with large myocardial infarction. The patient has no history of cardiogenic shock, multivessel coronary artery disease, serious renal or hepatic disease, blood cell disorders, cancer, or terminal illness.

Patient is a 27-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He maintains a healthy lifestyle and exercises regularly. He is a non-smoker and abstains from alcohol and drug abuse. He has not participated in any other clinical trials with investigational drugs within the last two months. He has a Body Mass Index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2. He consents to participate in the trial and is willing to comply with the dietary regimen required by the trial site. His laboratory values are all within the reference range and he has no history of relevant allergies or hypersensitivity. He has not undergone any surgery or has any gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, hormonal, or neurological disorders. He has not donated blood in the last four weeks, has not engaged in excessive physical activities within the last week, and has no history of fainting spells or blackouts.

A sexually active 27-year-old African American female presents to the clinic with a history of recurrent vaginal infections including bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis. She reports having more than 4 episodes of sex with her male partner in the past month. The patient has been tested negative for HIV. On examination, she reports fever, itching, and burning sensation in the vagina. Laboratory tests confirm the presence of bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing the efficacy of vaginal suppositories for reducing the rates of vaginal infections. She is willing to comply with the study visit schedule and procedures during the 12-month period of follow-up. She agrees to not participate in other research studies involving drugs, medical devices, or vaginal products for the duration of the study. She is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and does not have any medical condition that would contraindicate the use of the study product. She is willing to abstain from sex or use non-latex condoms for 24 hours following insertion of each vaginal suppository and abstain from alcohol during and for 48 hours after treatment.

This study is looking for individuals who have previously participated in a bridging study for a recombinant human papillomavirus 16/18 bivalent vaccine in preadolescent girls. The study aims to evaluate the immuno-persistence of the vaccine in girls aged 9-17 years, comparing to young healthy adults of 18-26 years who received the standard 3-dose schedule. The researchers will collect serum samples to test the seroprevalence and geometric mean concentrations of anti-HPV16 and anti-HPV18 antibody on 54 months after dose 1. The ideal participant should have received at least one dose of the vaccine, be able to fully understand the study content, and comply with the requests of the study. Participants with coagulation dysfunction, abnormal blood clotting function, or coagulopathy may not be eligible for this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who recently underwent surgery for a craniofacial injury resulting from a car accident. The injury caused a volume defect of approximately 50cc in her right cheek and temple area, resulting in a noticeable asymmetry in her facial appearance. The patient has fully recovered from the surgery and has been cleared by her physician to participate in the study. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is willing and able to comply with follow-up examinations, including radiographic studies. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders or substance abuse. She is not currently pregnant and has not received chemotherapy or radiation treatment in the past 12 months. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the fat grafting procedure will improve her facial appearance and quality of life.

A 30-year-old African American woman, who resides in New Haven, Connecticut, has a history of incarceration and is currently under probation. She reports a history of substance use, including intravenous drug use, and has been diagnosed with depression and anxiety. She reports that she has engaged in sexual activity with both men and women in the past and is currently not in a monogamous relationship. She has never been tested for HIV but reports no symptoms. She is interested in participating in a study focused on HIV prevention and is open to learning about new methods of prevention. She is willing to recruit other women in her risk network to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old man with a history of Hepatitis C and hepatocellular carcinoma is being evaluated for liver transplantation. He has never received treatment with PegIFN alfa-2a or ribavirin before. His Child-Pugh-Turcotte score is 6, and his Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score is 15. He has a single tumor that is 5 cm in diameter. He has no other significant medical history and is currently taking no medications. He is willing to give written consent and agrees to use double contraception during the study. He has no known allergies to any medications or history of intolerance to PegIFN alfa-2a or ribavirin use.

30 yo female with a history of depression since adolescence who has failed multiple antidepressant medication trials. She presents with persistent sadness, anhedonia, decreased energy, poor concentration, sleep disturbance, and suicidal ideation. She has no history of neurological or seizure disorders, and is right-handed. She is fluent in English and can comprehend the instructions for the EEG and TMS. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate brain-based biomarkers in response to TMS in MDD.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has a history of recurrent ear infections and has had several episodes of otitis media in the past year. She reports that these infections usually occur after a cold or upper respiratory infection. She has tried various treatments, including antibiotics and decongestants, but her symptoms persist. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if her poor Eustachian tube function is contributing to her recurrent ear infections. She is in good overall health and has no significant medical history. She lives with her husband and two young children. She is willing to participate in a study that involves testing her Eustachian tube function and monitoring her response to a viral upper respiratory infection. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been on dialysis for three years due to kidney failure caused by hypertension. He has been on the waiting list for a cadaveric renal transplant for six months. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse but has recently quit both. He has no history of cancer or myelodysplastic or -proliferative disorders. He has no current infections or bleeding episodes. His blood pressure is controlled with medication. He is willing to participate in the trial and follow the trial instructions.

This is a 34-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with gingival recession. She has been experiencing sensitivity in her teeth and discomfort during brushing. The periodontist has recommended a free gingival graft to help cover the exposed roots and improve her oral health. The patient has been informed that a small piece of tissue will be removed from the roof of her mouth to be used as the graft. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any medical conditions that would prevent her from undergoing the procedure. The patient does not smoke and does not have a severe gag reflex. She has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

A 35-year-old female patient with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) is being sought to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a slow titration schedule for Tecfidera. The patient should have no prior treatment with DMF and should have had a recent complete blood count (CBC), including lymphocyte count, that does not preclude participation in the study, in the judgement of the investigator. The patient should not have a recent history or ongoing GI illness or any other current condition with GI signs and symptoms that may interfere with assessment of study endpoints. The patient should not be receiving concomitant disease-modifying therapies for MS, and should not have a history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions or known drug hypersensitivity. The study requires the female patient of childbearing potential who are not surgically sterile and male subjects to practice effective contraception during their participation in the study.

A 32-year-old female diagnosed with primary immunodeficiency disease (PIDD) and prescribed with HYQVIA (Immune Globulin (Human) 10% with rHuPH20) for immunoglobulin treatment. She has been on this treatment for 6 months and is willing to participate in a non-interventional post-marketing safety study to assess the long-term safety of HYQVIA. The participant has no known hypersensitivity to any of the components of the product and is willing and able to comply with the study requirements. She is of child-bearing potential and agrees to inform the investigator if she becomes pregnant or plans to become pregnant during the study. There is no history of participation in another interventional clinical study involving a medical product or device within the past 30 days. The patient is not a family member or employee of the investigator.

Patient is a 28-year-old male who suffered from a severe traumatic brain injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident. He was admitted to Memorial Hermann Hospital Trauma Center and has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 8. He is able to speak English and has no known history of brain injury, psychiatric disorder, neurological impairment or deficit, seizure disorder, recent infection, renal or hepatic disease, cancer, substance abuse, immunosuppression, or HIV. He has not undergone any surgical procedures to manage unstable pelvic fractures, spinal cord injury, or any Grade I solid or hollow visceral injury of the abdomen and/or pelvis. He has no contraindications to MRI and is willing to return for follow-up visits. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

48-year-old female presents with a recent diagnosis of non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm (NF-PanNEN). She underwent an endoscopic ultrasound fine needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) that confirmed the diagnosis. A 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT scan showed a single pancreatic lesion with hyper-enhancing pattern and no evidence of lymph nodes, liver, or other distant metastases. The lesion is 20mm in diameter and there are no inner calcifications. The patient reports no symptoms related to the tumor. She has no known bleeding disorder, and is not on anticoagulants. INR and platelet count are within normal limits. The patient is able to undergo endoscopic ultrasound examination. She has not been previously enrolled in any other studies and is able to provide written informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II presents with symptoms of depression, including persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. She has a history of not responding to conventional antidepressant therapies and has been drug-free for at least three weeks. She has no current suicidal ideation or behavior, and she is able to provide informed consent. Her medical history is unremarkable except for the bipolar disorder, and she has no history of alcohol or drug abuse or dependence. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is using a medically accepted means of contraception. She has no history of ulcerative colitis or toxic megacolon, glaucoma, or narrow-angle glaucoma. She is not currently using nicotine or nicotine products. The patient has no hearing or vision problems that would interfere with testing. She is currently stable on lithium treatment. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of the muscarinic cholinergic receptor antagonist scopolamine administered via transdermal patch on clinical symptoms of depression.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with psoriasis for 8 years. She has been on a biologic treatment for the past 2 years and is currently stable. She has concerns about the safety of vaccines and their effectiveness on patients like her who are on biologic therapy. She wants to participate in this study to better understand the potential risks and benefits of vaccines for psoriasis patients on biologics, especially in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. She is willing to attend educational sessions and provide feedback on the information provided to her.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of biliary obstruction. She has experienced recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and jaundice, and has been diagnosed with suspected biliary sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. She has a normal common bile duct diameter and serum bilirubin level. The patient is also obese with a body mass index (BMI) of 32. She has not undergone any previous procedures at the ampulla of Vater. The patient has a past history of acute pancreatitis, which occurred 6 months ago. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the primary needle knife fistulotomy (NKF) to conventional cannulation methods for biliary access in patients at increased risk for post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (PEP). The patient has provided written informed consent for the trial and is between the ages of 18 and 90.

A 35-year-old woman named Emily has been suffering from migraines with aura for the past 5 years. She experiences migraines an average of 8 days per month, with each episode lasting around 12 hours. She has tried various medications with no significant improvement in her symptoms. Emily has no history of major systemic illness but had a minor car accident 6 months ago that resulted in whiplash. She has not received chiropractic care for this condition or any other condition. Emily is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study procedures and commit to the 14-week period of the study. She is not currently taking any prophylactic medications for migraines and is not a heavy drinker or substance abuser. Her medical history does not indicate any diagnosis of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who participated in a previous study investigating the effects of non-surgical periodontal therapy with and without minocycline HCl microspheres, 1 mg. She has a history of periodontal disease and underwent scaling and root planing treatment during the previous study. She is a non-smoker and has not taken any antibiotics in the past six weeks. She reports no history of cardiac conditions or other uncontrolled medical conditions. Her HbA1c level is <7 and she is not currently taking any medication that may impact periodontal conditions. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is interested in participating in the 9 and 12 month follow-up study to determine the effects of non-surgical periodontal therapy on systemic markers of inflammation.

The patient is a 52-year-old female with a history of ER-positive breast cancer that has become refractory to hormone therapy. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with limited success. Her current treatment plan includes participation in the phase I-II trial with HSP90 inhibitor AUY922 (Clinical Trials no NCT00526045A). She has no known allergies and her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of heart disease or other major illnesses. She is willing to undergo a 89Zr-bevacizumab PET scan as part of the side study protocol to evaluate the effect of HSP90 inhibition by AUY922 on VEGF.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who experiences frequent episodes of bloating, nausea, and abdominal discomfort after eating. She has consulted with her primary care physician and undergone several diagnostic tests, including an upper endoscopy and abdominal ultrasound. All tests were negative for underlying gastrointestinal conditions, but her symptoms persist. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help diagnose her condition and potentially identify a treatment plan. She has no history of chronic heart or respiratory disease, liver disease or malabsorption syndrome, and has not undergone any abdominal surgeries except for an appendectomy. She is not currently taking any medications that may alter gastric motility, and is not on hormone replacement therapy. She is willing and able to eat the test meal and provide breath samples as required by the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with NMOSD two years ago. She has experienced multiple relapses requiring rescue therapy within the last year. Her current treatment regimen includes prednisone and azathioprine. She has an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 5.5. She has had a positive result for AQP4-IgG antibodies. She has no history of malignancy or other significant medical history. She is willing to comply with the visit schedule and treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not received any investigational drug or other experimental therapy within the last 4 weeks. She is not allergic to SHR1459 or any of its ingredients. She has no severe and uncontrolled conditions that may affect her safety, trial compliance, evaluation of the endpoint, or the need to use medications not permitted in the protocol. She is not currently receiving B-cell targeted therapy, biological agents, or BTK inhibitors. She is not currently receiving any live virus vaccine. She has not received any glucocorticoid therapy within the last 6 months. Her ECG examination during screening is normal. Her ALT, AST, and bilirubin levels are within the normal range. Her white blood cell count, neutrophil count, lymphocyte count, and platelet count are all within the normal range. Her eGFR is above 60 ml/min. She is able to undergo MRI scans. She has no history of clinically significant CNS trauma. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling with sleep apnea and has been recently diagnosed with prediabetes. She is overweight with a body mass index (BMI) of 32.2 and reports excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring. She has never been diagnosed with diabetes and her blood glucose levels have been consistently high, but not high enough to meet the criteria for diabetes. She does not have a history of severe hypertension or bleeding disorders. She is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with assessments. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the mechanisms of prediabetic states in sleep apnea and potentially identify new treatments to prevent the development of diabetes.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for several months. She has noticed a loss of appetite and has unintentionally lost weight. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol consumption. She has no significant past medical or surgical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon examination, the abdomen is tender and distended. The lab results show elevated levels of liver enzymes and a CT scan reveals a large mass in the liver. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of advanced fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC). The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate. She has a good understanding of the study requirements and is willing to comply with study restrictions. She provides written informed consent and agrees to return for required assessments.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who suffered a severe traumatic brain injury after a car accident. He was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Score of 4 and is currently intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. A CT scan showed a diffuse axonal injury and moderate cerebral edema. His past medical history is notable for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is not taking any anticoagulants. His family is available and willing to consent to his participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has recently undergone conization due to positive HPV DNA test results. She has no history of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or cervical cancer. Her latest PAP test result was negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. She is not pregnant and has not undergone any gastrointestinal (GI) surgeries. She does not have any known GI dysfunctions and does not require long-term antibiotic treatment. The patient is seeking to participate in a clinical trial to understand the effect of oral U-relax on vaginal environment health promotion and the HPV DNA test index change from positive to negative. She is willing to participate in the trial for the duration of the 360-day trial period and to undergo all health-related conditions monitoring during the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and weight loss for the past few months. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. Upon endoscopy and biopsy, he was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction (AEG). The CT scan and ultrasound endoscopy confirmed the early stage of cancer (cT1N0M0). The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has a Karnofsky score of 80 and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials and has signed the Clinical Trial Agreement.

45 yo M with a history of recurrent hemorrhoids and anal fissures presenting for elective hemorrhoidectomy. Past Medical History: - Hypertension controlled on lisinopril - Hyperlipidemia controlled on atorvastatin - History of hemorrhoidectomy and sphincterotomy [**6-1**] - History of anal fissure and recurrent hemorrhoids - No known allergies - Non-smoker - Social alcohol use: 2-3 drinks/week

A 7-year old boy was diagnosed with ADHD last year. He experiences difficulty paying attention, is easily distracted and has trouble following instructions. He also has a tendency to interrupt others and struggles with impulse control. His parents have tried various behavioral interventions and medication to manage his symptoms. He is currently taking medication that has improved his symptoms, but his parents are concerned about the long-term effects of medication on his development. The patient has an average IQ and is in the second grade. He enjoys playing video games and watching cartoons. He has access to a tablet and reliable internet connection at home. His parents are interested in enrolling him in the Mega Team study to improve his executive functioning and emotional regulation while playing video games. They are willing to commit to the study protocol and schedule weekly calls with the research staff.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who suffered a left-sided hemiplegia following a stroke six months ago. She has been experiencing difficulty breathing and is often short of breath. She has reduced thoracic expansion and has limited use of her left arm due to ankylosis. She is currently at Brunnstrom stage 5 and has a Modified Ashworth score of 2 in her upper extremity. She does not smoke and has no hearing or vision loss. She is able to answer the level of consciousness survey and has no acute pain or bronchitis. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her lung function and overall respiratory health.

A 54-year-old male presents with a 2-month history of progressive dysphagia and odynophagia associated with an enlarging right cervical mass. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender, 5 cm mass in the right level II neck lymph node. Flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy shows a 2 cm fungating squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil with mild tongue base involvement. CT and PET scans show no evidence of distant metastases or nodal involvement outside of the right neck. Laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient is diagnosed with stage IVa squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil with nodal involvement and is deemed a candidate for definitive surgical resection followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, no active infections, no autoimmune disease, and is able to give informed consent and comply with the protocol. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial testing the safety of the anti-OX40 antibody, MEDI6469, given prior to surgery in patients with advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

We do not require a patient description for this clinical trial as it does not involve patient enrollment or intervention. Instead, it aims to examine the relationship between signal strength and macular thickness measured by stratus OCT.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has been diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease and is in need of an elective vascular procedure that requires a groin incision of at least 8 cm. He is able to provide informed consent, has a support system to help him care for his wound post-surgery, and is willing to comply with follow-up appointments. He has no other major medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who has recently been diagnosed with a brain stem glioma after experiencing headaches, nausea, and difficulty with coordination. MRI scans have confirmed the presence of a tumor in the brain stem. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. Her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial that combines Thalomid™ and carboplatin with radiation therapy to treat her tumor. They have been informed of the study's potential benefits and risks and have given written consent for their daughter to participate. The patient's blood work and kidney function are within normal limits, and she is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 6 weeks. The patient will begin treatment within 3 days of registration for the trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who lives in a rural area of Afghanistan. She presents to a Malaria Reference Center with symptoms of malaria, including fever, chills, headache, and body aches. She reports that these symptoms have been present for the past 3 days. Upon examination, a peripheral blood slide confirms uncomplicated malaria infection with Plasmodium falciparum. The patient does not have any signs of severe malaria and has no known cardiac, renal, hepatic, or other severe disease. She weighs 60 kg and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of Artekin with standard malaria treatment regimens. She provides written informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria for the study. However, she is excluded from the study if she has received Artesunate or Chloroquine in the past one month, Fansidar in the past one and a half months, or Artekin in the past 3 months.

A 28-year-old male with type 1 diabetes mellitus for 5 years is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a new formulation of insulin degludec. He manages his diabetes with insulin injections and has a BMI of 23 kg/m^2. His HbA1c is 8.5% based on central laboratory results. He has no history of drug allergies and has never participated in a clinical trial involving investigational products. He is in good health, exercises regularly, and has no other underlying medical conditions. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the study protocol.

This is a 55 year-old female who has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. Despite being on metformin 1000mg twice daily and adhering to a strict diet and exercise regimen, her hemoglobin A1c level has remained consistently above 7%. She has no known history of renal insufficiency or malabsorption syndrome. She is not currently taking any vitamin D supplements at doses greater than 400 international units daily. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if vitamin D supplementation could improve her blood sugar control.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been on opioid substitution therapy (OST) for the past 2 years due to a history of intravenous drug use. He was recently diagnosed with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and has not yet started any treatment for it. He visits a community pharmacy on a daily basis to receive his OST medication and has a good relationship with the pharmacist in charge. He has no evidence of decompensated liver disease and his fibrosis score is within the acceptable range for the study. He has no other co-infections such as HIV or HBV. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the SuperDOT-C study. He is interested in receiving treatment for his HCV infection and is open to the idea of receiving it under the supervision of the pharmacist at the community pharmacy.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) due to severe respiratory distress. She has a history of asthma and has had several hospitalizations in the past for exacerbations. Upon admission, she was started on invasive mechanical ventilation but was successfully extubated after 24 hours. She is currently on non-invasive respiratory support (NRS) with high flow nasal cannula (HFNC). Her oxygen saturation is 88% on 60% FiO2. She is alert and cooperative but appears tired due to labored breathing. Her parents are concerned about her condition and are willing to consider enrolling her in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of HFNC versus continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for NRS. They have no concerns about the study procedures and are willing to provide consent for her participation. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for Group B (Step-down) as she requires NRS after extubation. She has no history of midfacial/craniofacial anomalies or air-leak syndrome. She has not been managed on HFNC or CPAP for the past 24 hours. She is currently receiving standard care in the PICU and will be followed up for 6 months.

A 25-year-old female patient has been experiencing sudden, brief attacks of involuntary hyperkinetic movements. She has been diagnosed with psychogenic paroxysmal hyperkinetic movement disorder and her attacks can be triggered by sudden movements or prolonged exercise. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no history of brain tumors, strokes, or trauma. She is currently not taking any medication that affects the central nervous system. She is willing to undergo three neurophysiological tests to determine what areas of her brain are responsible for her disorder. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to abstain from alcohol and caffeine for 24 hours before the study.

A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic with a history of chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and stiffness. She has been experiencing these symptoms for more than 3 months and has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia. She has tried various treatments, including painkillers, massage therapy, and physical therapy, but she has not found any significant relief. She is interested in participating in an internet-based cognitive behavior therapy trial for fibromyalgia. She has no history of severe psychiatric disorders and is motivated to participate in the 10-week treatment program. She is excited to learn more about cognitive behavioral therapy and hopes that it will help her manage her fibromyalgia symptoms.

A 63-year-old woman presents with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (PsAF) for the past 10 months. She has been on treatment with class I and class III antiarrhythmic drugs (AAD), but these have been ineffective in controlling her symptoms, which include palpitations, fatigue, and shortness of breath. She has no significant past medical history, except for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for an irregularly irregular heart rate of 110 beats/minute. Blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and BMI is 26. She is eager to explore other treatment options and is willing to participate in the clinical trial for iCLAS™ Cryoablation System. She is scheduled to undergo an atrial ablation procedure for her PsAF and is willing to comply with all the follow-up evaluations for the full length of the study. She has no known contraindications to atrial ablation, TEE, or anticoagulation.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a traumatic spinal cord injury at C5 level resulting in complete paralysis. He was hospitalized shortly after the injury and underwent a tracheotomy due to respiratory complications. He is currently receiving mechanical ventilation and has been in the hospital for 2 weeks. He has been experiencing difficulty with breathing and coughing up secretions. He is able to give meaningful consent and is willing to participate in the study. He has no history of thoracic trauma, pleural effusion, or ongoing sepsis. He is hemodynamically stable and not currently receiving amines.

45-year-old female diagnosed with relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphoma who has failed at least 2-4 prior combination chemotherapy regimens and is not eligible for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The patient has a performance score of 1 and is expected to survive for more than 12 weeks. The patient has a confirmed CD19/22-positive lymphoma and has been diagnosed for more than 6 months. The patient has no symptoms of central nervous system involvement and has adequate venous access for apheresis. The patient has no active hepatitis B or C, HIV infection, poorly controlled hypertension, or a history of mental illness. The patient is not taking immunosuppressive agents within 1 week due to organ transplantation or other diseases that require long-lasting administration. The patient has not suffered from unstable pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, or other major arterial/venous thromboembolic events 30 days prior to assignment. The patient is willing to take contraceptive measures before joining the trial and has provided written voluntary informed consent.

65 F with a history of congenital heart disease and a previous surgical repair of an atrial septal defect. She now presents with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue. Echocardiogram shows residual shunting across the atrial septum and mild pulmonary hypertension. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial as a patient with residual leakage after surgical treatment for congenital heart disease. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve treatment options for others with similar conditions. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the required follow-up visits.

27 yo M with no previous ophthalmic medical history, presenting with refractive error and no other ocular complaints. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the effect of eye opening/closure on the quality of IOP (intraocular pressure) related patterns recorded with SENSIMED Triggerfish. The patient is willing to be randomized to two 24-hour recording sessions, one with the recorded eye open and the other with the eye closed, using an ophthalmic patch. The patient has given written informed consent prior to any investigational procedures. No contraindications for silicone contact lens wear or allergy to corneal anesthetic present. The patient is able to understand the character and individual consequences of the investigation. The patient has not participated in any other clinical research within the last 4 weeks.

A 42-year-old female presents with a lump in her left breast that was discovered during a regular self-examination. She reports no pain or discharge from the nipple. She has no significant medical history and no previous surgeries. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is married and has two children. She has a sedentary lifestyle and works as an accountant. She is concerned about the lump and wants to undergo treatment as soon as possible. The lump was biopsied and confirmed as invasive breast carcinoma, stage II. The tumor size is 3.5 cm by clinical assessment. HER2-positive breast cancer is confirmed by ASCO/CAP guidelines. She has no other health issues, and her laboratory findings are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent for all study procedures.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 presents to a tertiary medical center for a scheduled cesarean delivery due to gestational diabetes. She has no history of prior cesarean deliveries or other surgeries. The patient has a history of hypertension that is currently well controlled with medication. She reports no allergies or complications with anesthesia in the past. The patient is informed about the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study. She is able to attend a wound evaluation at the Tufts Medical Center 2 weeks after the surgery and is willing to receive phone calls to assess outcomes at both 2 and 6 weeks post-operatively. She is not currently experiencing any active infections in the location of the Pfannenstiel skin incision. Based on the eligibility criteria, the patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with early-stage proliferative diabetic retinopathy. She has a history of diabetes for 10 years and has been taking insulin for the past 5 years. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. She has undergone vitrectomy due to non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage and fibrocellular proliferation without tractional retinal detachment. She has not undergone vitrectomy before. She has no history of severe intraoperative complications or postoperative silicone oil tamponade. She is currently not menstruating and has not experienced a stroke, thromboembolic event, or myocardial infarction in the past 6 months. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of intravitreal conbercept after vitrectomy.

This is a 7-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with bilateral inguinal hernia and is scheduled for surgery. He has no known neurological disorders or coagulation disorders. He is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. He is eligible to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the analgesic efficiency of caudal block and ultrasound-guided ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerve blocks for pediatric patients undergoing bilateral inguinal hernia surgery. He will be randomly assigned to receive either the ultrasound-guided ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric block or the caudal block, and will be evaluated for analgesia with the FLACC pain scale, analgesic requirement, complications, and parental satisfaction. The evaluation will be performed by a researcher who does not know which group the patient belongs to.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with extreme obesity for several years. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 45 and has unsuccessfully attempted to lose weight through diet and exercise. She has recently been referred to a bariatric surgery program and is considering undergoing bariatric surgery as a last resort. She is fluent in English, has access to a telephone and a computer with internet access, and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have any active suicidal ideation, serious mental illness, severe depression, severe anxiety, or post-traumatic stress disorder. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if telephone-based CBT can be effective in reducing binge eating and improving her surgical outcomes.

Pt is a 49yo M with a history of GIST who previously received imatinib but showed progression after treatment. The patient is currently not on any therapy for GIST. The patient has an ECOG PS of 1 and is otherwise healthy. The patient has a history of hypertension, which has been well controlled with medication. The patient has no known allergies to medications. MRI scans show multiple measurable lesions consistent with GIST. The patient is willing to undergo biopsy or provide an archival tumor tissue sample for molecular pathology report to confirm mutation status. The patient is willing to comply with the contraception requirements outlined in the study protocol. The patient has no active bleeding or gastrointestinal abnormalities that exclude them from the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic soft tissue wounds on her feet for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years and has been struggling to manage her blood sugar levels. The wounds are located on the sole of her feet and have not healed despite regular debridement and disinfection. The wounds are not infected and have been scored as Grade/Stage 2A according to Armstrong et al.'s classification system. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed a written informed consent. She does not have any contraindications for rESWT. The patient's blood sugar levels are regularly higher than 7mmol/L before meals and regularly higher than 11mmol/L one to two hours after meals.

A 29 year old woman who is 7 weeks pregnant comes to the clinic for a check-up. She is a first-time mother and is excited about her pregnancy. She is concerned about maintaining a healthy diet and weight during and after her pregnancy. She has a BMI of 27, which falls under the overweight category. She has no history of eating disorders or chronic illnesses. She speaks fluent English and has access to the internet with email. She plans to deliver her baby at UNC Hospital and intends to stay in the area for a year after delivery. She is willing to undergo study procedures, provide informed consent and assent for her baby's participation in the study. She is interested in the Pregnancy Eating Attributes Study and is willing to participate in the study.

Pt is a 25yo M with a 3-month history of a skin ulcer on his right arm that has been getting progressively worse over time with no other past medical history. A biopsy of the lesion was performed and confirmed the diagnosis of cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) caused by L. peruviana. The patient is eligible for the study as he is male, between 12 and 70 years of age, and has a confirmed diagnosis of CL with a positive identification of the Leishmania parasite and identification of L. peruviana by PCR.
