The patient's lesion is clear of superinfection, and he has normal laboratory blood test values. The patient has negative serology tests for HIV-1/2, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), and hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody. The patient is willing to give written informed consent, be housed in Lima for a minimum of 20 days and up to 63 days, able to attend all required follow-up visits, have a permanent address, and be reachable by study site personnel. The patient has not had previous exposure to Leishmania vaccines or investigational products within 30 days. The patient has not used injected or oral corticosteroids within 6 weeks prior to the first vaccination or initiation of chemotherapy, and has no history of autoimmune disease, immunosuppressive states, or significant psychiatric illness. The patient does not have a history of drug addiction, alcohol abuse, anaphylaxis, severe allergic reaction to vaccines or unknown allergens, or allergic reaction to eggs. The patient is not taking any medication that may interfere with the evaluation of the safety or the immunogenicity of the vaccine, and does not have any acute or chronic illness that may interfere with the evaluation of the safety or the immunogenicity of the vaccine.

This clinical trial is an observational cohort study and does not involve patient recruitment. Instead, it studies data from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) - Heidelberg, which started between 1994 and 1998 and recruited 25,540 adults from the local general population. The study aims to evaluate associations between diet, lifestyle, metabolism, and risks of major chronic diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes. The study investigates the potential mediator of associations between pre-diagnostic red meat consumption and cardiovascular disease risk by assessing prediagnostic iron status. The study involves a random subcohort of 2738 participants and all validated incident cases of myocardial infarction (n=556), stroke (n=513), and CVD death (n=327) that occurred until the closure date of the study on 12-31-2009. The study does not have any inclusion or exclusion criteria for patients as it is an observational cohort study.

A 56-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with lung cancer after presenting with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He has lost significant weight over the past few months and has little appetite, which has become a concern for his family and healthcare providers. He is currently not receiving any cancer treatment and has not been previously treated with immunosuppressors. He has no other known wasting diseases such as AIDS, trauma, or end-stage renal disease. He is able to communicate and understand the study requirements and has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old Hispanic woman presented with a history of abdominal pain, bloating, and frequent diarrhea for the past year. She has tried various over-the-counter remedies without relief. She was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome by a gastroenterologist and started on a low FODMAP diet which has helped somewhat but she still experiences frequent flare-ups. She has no other chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications except for occasional antacids. She speaks and understands English fluently and has a telephone at home. Her IBS Severity Scale score is 85, indicating moderate to severe symptoms. She has not taken any extraneous probiotics in the past four months and has no known allergies or contraindications to the study medication. She is not pregnant and has no family members who are immunosuppressed. Her oral temperature is within normal range and she has no history of cardiac disease, stroke, bowel ischemia, or other risk factors for these conditions.

A 52-year-old male with a history of chronic renal failure and receiving hemodialysis three times a week presents with pruritus that is not responsive to conventional treatment. The patient has received systemic therapy of more than two consecutive weeks of antihistamine or antiallergic drugs, as well as local therapy with ointments or moisturizers prescribed by a doctor. Despite this, the patient's pruritus remains severe, impacting their quality of life. The patient is not currently experiencing acute symptoms and is not likely to have any significant treatment changes during the study period. The patient has no history of malignant tumors, atopic dermatitis, chronic urticaria, drug or alcohol dependence, or allergies to opioid drugs. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and uses contraceptive methods. The patient is capable of reporting VAS scores and is otherwise suitable for participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with locally advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient has previously received treatment with at least one other ALK inhibitor but has either progressed on or is intolerant to the therapy. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has at least one target lesion per RECIST version 1.1. The patient has recovered from toxicities related to prior anticancer therapy to NCI CTCAE version 4.03 Grade <= 1. The patient has not received systemic treatment with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers within 14 days before enrollment. The patient has no prior therapy with brigatinib and has not received ALK-inhibitor therapy within 7 days before the first dose of study drug. The patient has not received any investigational systemic anticancer agents within 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, before the first dose of study drug. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy within 14 days before the first dose of study drug, except for stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) or stereotactic body radiation therapy. The patient has not received antineoplastic monoclonal antibodies within 30 days before the first dose of study drug. The patient has not had major surgery within 30 days before the first dose of study drug. The patient has no current spinal cord compression (symptomatic or asymptomatic and detected by radiographic imaging).

Patient is a 38-year-old woman from the United States who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been diagnosed with low ovarian reserve. Her partner is a 40-year-old man with no known fertility issues. They have no children and have never undergone any fertility treatments. The patient's BMI is 27.9 and she has no significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve her chances of becoming pregnant.

A 14-year-old girl with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) presents with difficulties in executive function, motor performance, and mood. She has a BMI in the obese range and is taking medication that has resulted in weight gain. The patient has limited participation in physical activities and expresses a lack of interest or motivation to exercise. She attends Gateway Academy, a private school for children with academic and social challenges, and is enrolled in the Fit Club fitness program. The patient's parents have provided consent for her to participate in an 18-month exploratory pilot study examining the impact of regular physical exercise on improvement in academic performance among adolescents with ASD. The patient is conversational in English and has an IQ of 70, as provided by Gateway Academy with parental consent. The patient does not have a dual diagnosis of cerebral palsy or any other major neurologic condition and has no uncorrected hearing or vision problems.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness for the past 4 months. She was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis by her primary care physician and has not received any treatment for her condition yet. She has no history of taking methotrexate or any other disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). She has been taking over-the-counter pain relievers and NSAIDs for her symptoms, but they only provide temporary relief. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to try a new treatment option for her rheumatoid arthritis. She is currently not taking any steroids or NSAIDs and is willing to remain on a stable dose if needed for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male presenting to the Department of Pulmonary Medicine and Sleep Disorders at AIIMS, New Delhi for a flexible bronchoscopy to investigate his chronic cough and shortness of breath. He has no history of uncontrolled hypertension or coronary artery disease. He is not pregnant and consents to participate in the study. His oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. The bronchoscopy will be performed via the nasal route. He has no history of nasal or throat allergies and has not used any nasal vasoconstrictors in the past 24 hours. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend follow-up visits.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bilateral cataracts. She reports a history of progressive vision loss over the past few years, with difficulty seeing at both near and far distances. She has previously worn glasses for correction but is interested in exploring the option of becoming spectacle independent. The patient reports no other significant medical history other than well-controlled hypertension. On examination, her visual acuity is 20/80 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. She has a mild astigmatism in both eyes. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her visual outcomes and decrease her reliance on glasses after cataract surgery. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits and other study procedures.

The patient is a male with a confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer who has previously received definitive surgery or radiation therapy or cryoablation. The patient must not have evidence of metastatic disease and must have hormone-sensitive prostate cancer as evident by a serum total testosterone level greater than 150 ng/dL. The patient must have evidence of biochemical failure after primary therapy and subsequent progression. The patient must have a PSA doubling time of less than 12 months, and the baseline PSA must have reached a minimum of 2 ng/mL but be no greater than 50 ng/mL. The patient must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1. The patient must have granulocytes of 1,500/mm^3 or higher, a platelet count of 100,000/mm^3 or higher, and serum creatinine within normal institutional limits or creatinine clearance of 50 ml/min or higher for patients with creatinine levels above institutional normal. The patient must not have any uncontrolled intercurrent illness, ongoing or active infection, cardiac arrhythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient must not have gastrointestinal (GI) tract disease resulting in an inability to take oral medication, malabsorption syndrome, or a requirement for intravenous (IV) alimentation. The patient must not be receiving any other investigational agents or receiving concurrent anticancer therapy. The patient must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to MK-2206 or bicalutamide. The patient must agree to use barrier contraception during and for 3 months after discontinuation of study treatment.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman from New York who experiences severe menstrual pain with a pain score of 8/10 on the visual analog scale during her periods. She has been previously diagnosed with primary dysmenorrhea and has tried various over-the-counter pain medications with little relief. She has no other pain conditions or diagnosed gynecological disorders. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not currently using any hormonal medications or contraceptives. Her BMI is 22, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min, and her laboratory studies are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a research study that aims to better understand the underlying mechanisms of menstrual pain and improve treatment options.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has undergone a double lung transplant due to a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He is currently stable and is on regular follow-up with his pulmonologist. He has a history of smoking for 20 years, but has quit 5 years ago. He reports occasional cough and mild dyspnea on exertion, but overall reports improvement in his quality of life after the transplant. He is fluent in German and has no issues with communication or computer handling. He has been advised to undergo a bronchoscopy as a routine follow-up for post-transplant evaluation. He is scheduled for an outpatient bronchoscopy and has consented to participate in the study. He does not require oxygen at rest and does not need peri-interventional sedation. He is willing to rate his anesthesia experience using a visual analogue scale.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who recently visited a doctor complaining of fatigue, bone pain, and recurrent infections. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. Physical examination revealed anemia, multiple lytic bone lesions, and elevated serum protein levels. A bone marrow biopsy showed 70% plasma cells, confirming the diagnosis of multiple myeloma, stage III. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive the latest treatment options. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a manager in a local company and his job requires him to travel frequently. He enjoys playing golf in his free time and is an active member of his local community center. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial. He has no history of chemotherapy treatment and has not undergone radiotherapy or surgery for his multiple myeloma. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his laboratory results show adequate renal and hepatic function. He has no significant neuropathy and is HIV negative.

32 F with a history of psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis for the past 3 years, currently experiencing active symptoms including joint pain and stiffness, skin lesions, and fatigue. She has been treated with methotrexate and leflunomide in the past, but did not achieve adequate control of her symptoms. She has also been treated with one TNF inhibitor, which was discontinued due to intolerance. She is currently not taking any medication for her PsA. She has no other active inflammatory arthritic syndromes or spondyloarthropathies. She is not pregnant and agrees to use reliable birth control during the study and for at least 12 weeks after stopping treatment. She is interested in participating in this study to potentially find a more effective treatment option for her PsA.

The patient is a 28-year-old sexually active woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent HIV transmission. She has a history of regular Pap smear screenings and has received normal results within the past year. She is not currently pregnant and has no history of adverse reactions to silicone, latex, or titanium dioxide. The patient is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study and agrees not to use any intravaginal products during the duration of the study. She is in general good health and has no conditions that would interfere with the study. The patient is eager to help advance research and contribute to the development of a safe and effective method of HIV prevention.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 12 years. He has been on oral hypoglycemic agents but has not been able to achieve adequate glycemic control with HbA1c levels persistently above 7.5%. He has a history of coronary artery disease with a successful percutaneous coronary intervention performed 5 years ago. He has also been diagnosed with peripheral artery disease and has undergone a surgical bypass procedure for a left femoral artery occlusion 2 years ago. He has been compliant with his medical regimen and has been following a healthy diet and exercise program. He has no history of pancreatitis.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who recently underwent cardiac surgery and needs to be monitored for at least 48 hours. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently taking medications for both conditions. She has no known allergies to adhesive patches or sticking plasters. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to give informed consent. She has no plans for an MRI examination and does not have any open wounds or severe thorax deformity that would make recording not possible.

A 25-year-old healthy male with no history of chronic pain or psychiatric disorders is seeking to participate in a clinical study to better understand the brain pathways involved in pain perception and relief. He has no known allergies and takes no regular medications or supplements. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He has good dental hygiene and has never had any dental surgery before. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. He is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the advancement of pain research and to learn more about how pain is processed in the brain.

The patient is a 45 year old male recently diagnosed with chronic phase CML after presenting with symptoms such as fatigue, weakness, and night sweats. He has received treatment with imatinib mesylate (Gleevec) but has not responded to the medication. He has a performance status of 1 and his renal, hepatic, and cardiac functions are adequate. He is not a candidate for allogeneic transplantation and is not currently taking any of the excluded medications. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore potential alternative treatments.

A 32-year-old female diagnosed with Pompe disease for 6 years presents with muscle weakness, respiratory problems, and difficulty swallowing. She has been on a stable regimen of rhGAA for the past 3 months and has not experienced any adverse effects. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 65 mL/min. She is sexually active and agrees to use medically accepted methods of contraception during the study and for 30 days after study completion. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and to comply with all study procedures. She has no history of allergy or sensitivity to study drugs or other iminosugars. The patient has not received any investigational/experimental drug or device within the last 30 days. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not test positive for hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C antibody. The patient has no intercurrent illness or condition that may preclude her from fulfilling the protocol requirements or suggests to the investigator that she may have an unacceptable risk by participating in this study.

The clinical trial is suitable for preterm infants born at a gestation of less than 33 weeks (23+0 to 32+6 weeks) who are admitted to the neonatal unit and require respiratory support with high flow nasal cannula (HFNC). The trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of the Oxygen Assist Module (OAM), an automatic oxygen control system, in reducing the extremes of oxygen saturation in preterm infants. Infants with major congenital or chromosomal anomalies are excluded from the study. This trial can be considered for preterm infants who are experiencing episodes of low oxygen saturation due to their immaturity, which can increase the risk of damage to the eyes and lungs, and contribute to death or disability.

Patient is a 28-year-old Black/African American man who identifies as male and has had sexual encounters with men within the past 24 months. He is currently living in Los Angeles County and is available for the next 12 months to attend study visits. He has experienced discrimination and medical mistrust related to his sexual orientation and race, and is seeking support to cope with these issues. He is willing and able to communicate in written and spoken English, and is excited to participate in a community-based program that will provide a safe space for him to discuss barriers to health care and receive support for his whole identity. He is interested in learning more about evidence-based preventive care, such as cancer and diabetes screening, cardiovascular disease prevention, influenza vaccination, and HIV prevention, and hopes that this intervention will help him to better engage with the healthcare system.

8-year-old female diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) admitted for inpatient treatment with chemotherapy. She has a history of central venous catheter placement and has been receiving treatment for the past 2 months. She has experienced several episodes of fever during her hospitalization and has been treated with antibiotics. No previous history of nosocomial infections. The patient and her parents have provided informed consent for participation in the Oncoped 2006 study.

32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia, currently taking antipsychotic medication at a steady dosage for the past 6 months. Patient reports experiencing auditory hallucinations at least 5 times per day. No significant history of head trauma or neurological disorders. No alcohol or drug abuse. No focal brain lesions on T1- or T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery magnetic resonance images. No history of seizures. No first-degree relative with epilepsy, significant neurological illness or head trauma, endocrine disease, or significant unstable medical condition. Patient is right-handed with an estimated intelligence quotient above 85. Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores are both below 7. Patient is able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity presented to the emergency room with symptoms of COVID-19, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 and admitted to the hospital for treatment. During his hospital stay, he experienced an altered mental status, confusion, and difficulty speaking. A neurological examination revealed abnormal findings, and he underwent a brain MRI, which showed abnormalities. The patient has agreed to participate in the study to further investigate the radiological presentation of brain abnormalities in COVID-19 patients.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman who is 38 weeks and 2 days pregnant has an elective cesarean delivery scheduled due to a previous cesarean delivery. She has a history of seasonal allergies and asthma, but her asthma is well-controlled with an inhaler. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. She has a BMI of 30 and is considered obese. She has no known allergies to any medication or skin sensitivities. She is married and has a support system at home for postoperative recovery. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve postoperative pain management for future patients.

An 80-year-old man was admitted to the ICU for respiratory failure and required mechanical ventilation. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and coronary artery disease. He is 170 cm tall and weighs 70 kg, which gives him a BMI of 24.2 kg/m2. His APACHE II score is 20. He has been on NG tube feeding for the past 48 hours. The medical team has assessed him as being at high nutritional risk based on the mNUTRIC and GNRI scores. He has no known allergies or dietary restrictions. He has been taking his regular medications, including metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin. He has no history of total parenteral nutrition use, fasting for more than 5 days, or brain death.

The patient is a 32-year-old male veteran who was recently admitted to an inpatient psychiatric unit at the VA Medical Center for a significant suicidal crisis. The patient reported current suicidal ideation and has not used the Veterans Crisis Line within the past 12 months. The patient is medically stable and able to provide informed consent. The patient's Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is greater than or equal to 21. The patient speaks English fluently and has no history of receiving or scheduled to receive electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The patient does not have profound psychotic symptoms or cognitive deficits that would prevent them from understanding the content of the intervention and/or assessments. The patient is willing to participate in the study and to be randomized to either the Crisis Line Facilitation (CLF) intervention or the enhanced usual care (EUC) condition.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is 35 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has been experiencing complications in her pregnancy and has been advised by her obstetrician to undergo an emergency caesarean section under general anaesthesia. She has no history of mental health issues and is able to communicate both verbally and in writing in English language. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her consent to be screened for recall of intraoperative events using a standardised questionnaire. She is currently receiving antenatal care and is otherwise healthy. Her medical history is unremarkable and she is not taking any regular medications.

A 60-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on her right forearm. The lesion was excised and resulted in a 3 cm diameter wound. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she is on medications. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is married and has two grown-up children who live in a different state. She lives with her husband who helps her with daily activities. She is able to comprehend and sign informed consent. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol and necessary wound care/follow-up. She does not have any known allergies.

52-year-old female with a history of chronic lower back pain and sciatica, unresponsive to conservative treatment measures such as physical therapy, oral pain medications, and epidural steroid injections. MRI scan showed a large herniated disc at the L4-L5 level causing significant compression of the nerve roots. The patient has agreed to undergo surgical intervention and has signed the consent form. She has health insurance coverage and is available for a 24-month follow-up. The patient is fluent in French and is willing to participate in this study to help improve the understanding and management of spinal disorders.

A 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) comes to the clinic. The tumor is located in the right lobe of the liver and is 7 cm in size with no evidence of extrahepatic metastasis or vascular invasion. The patient is in good general health, with a Child-Pugh score of A and an ECOG Performance Status of 0. The patient has never received immunotherapy or been diagnosed with any autoimmune disorder or interstitial pneumonia. The patient has a past history of hypertension and has undergone angioplasty two years ago. The patient is not on dialysis, has no convulsive disorder, and has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or thrombosis/embolism in the past 6 months. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of pembrolizumab as a neoadjuvant treatment for HCC to prevent the recurrence of the tumor after curative surgery or ablation.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of chronic back pain for the past 5 years. She has been taking opioids for pain management for the past 2 years. She reports experiencing constipation and bloating that began shortly after starting opioid therapy. The patient has tried various over-the-counter laxatives without success. She currently takes oxycodone 10 mg every 4-6 hours for pain relief. The patient reports having bowel movements every 3-4 days, which are often hard and difficult to pass. She has no history of chronic constipation before starting opioid therapy. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to discontinue all pre-study laxative therapy and utilize only study permitted rescue laxatives. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve her bowel function and alleviate the discomfort associated with Opioid-Induced Bowel Dysfunction.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. The patient has been taking metformin at the maximum tolerated dose of 2000 mg per day for the past 3 months. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.5% (69 mmol/mol). The patient's BMI is 28 kg/m^2. The patient has no history of pancreatitis or medullary thyroid carcinoma, and his screening calcitonin value is within normal limits. The patient has no personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2. The patient's liver function tests and renal function tests are within normal limits. The patient has not had any significant cardiovascular events within the past 90 days and his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. The patient has not been diagnosed with any malignant neoplasms in the past 5 years. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of liraglutide versus lixisenatide as an add-on to his current metformin treatment.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been suffering from typical GERD symptoms, including heartburn and acid regurgitation, for the past 12 weeks. She has been taking PPI treatment for the past 8 weeks but still experiences symptoms 3 times a week. The patient has not undergone any surgery in the thorax or upper part of the abdomen, and she has not been treated with SSRI's in the past. The patient has no history of systemic diseases that could affect esophageal motility, and there are no signs of severe erosive esophagitis on endoscopy. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using medically acceptable contraception. The patient is capable of understanding and willing to provide written informed consent. The patient has not used medications that could interfere with the study, such as anticholinergics, tricycle antidepressants, baclofen, and prokinetics. The patient has no significant neurological, respiratory, hepatic, renal, hematological, cardiovascular, metabolic, or gastrointestinal cerebro

The patient is a 28-year-old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 32. She has been struggling with obesity for several years and is interested in participating in a clinical trial related to weight management. She has no significant medical history, no allergies or food intolerances, and is a non-smoker. She does not engage in regular physical activity and her diet consists of mostly processed and high-calorie foods. She has good dental health and no current oral or dental pathology. She is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study results. She is interested in participating in the study to gain a better understanding of the role of mastication and food properties in energy expenditure, and to potentially contribute to the fight against obesity.

A 65-year-old male patient presented at the clinic with complaints of frequent urination and difficulty in starting urination. He was diagnosed with benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH) after a physical examination, digital rectal examination (DRE), and a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test. His prostate volume was found to be 35 cm3. The patient was prescribed AVODART as per the SPC guidelines. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medication that could interfere with the trial. The patient's liver function tests were normal, and he does not have a history of liver failure. He has agreed to participate in the pharmacovigilance study to evaluate the safety of AVODART in subjects with BPH.

A 25-year-old male with cystic fibrosis has been experiencing chronic respiratory infections for the past few years. He has been diagnosed with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in his sputum cultures on multiple occasions. He has an FEV1 of 60% predicted and has been clinically stable with no exacerbations for the past month. He is currently taking ivacaftor and agrees to remain on the same medication for at least 2 months prior to enrollment. He is able to use a nebulizer and provide repeated induced sputum samples. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and available for the duration of the study. He is a non-smoker, has no history of solid organ transplant, and is not currently participating in any other clinical research study. He agrees to use effective contraception during the study, as he is sexually active.

Patient is a 45-year-old man who has been suffering from recurrent kidney stones for the past few years. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has not had any previous surgeries related to his kidney stones. He is generally healthy and has no other significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of flexible ureteroscopy on renal blood flow. He has been referred to a urologist and is scheduled to undergo flexible ureteroscopy and laser lithotripsy according to EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis. He will be asked to sign an informed consent form before the surgery and will undergo pre-operative and post-operative bilateral renal power Doppler US.

32 y/o female diagnosed with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) for 5 years. She has been on treatment with Natalizumab for 7 months and is experiencing a few relapses. She has no history of chronic immune diseases, Crohn's disease, certain cancers, uncontrolled diabetes, certain eye disorders, negative for varicella-zoster virus IgG antibodies, certain hepatic conditions, low white blood cell count, or on certain immunosuppressive medications or heart medications. Her resting heart rate is within normal limits. She has no history of heart conditions or lung conditions, and she is able to undergo MRI scans. The patient is willing to discontinue Natalizumab treatment and participate in the clinical trial.

57-year-old male with a history of ischemic stroke and stable angina who has been taking daily aspirin 325mg for the past 6 months as secondary prevention. He has a documented gastric ulcer within the past 5 years and is at risk for developing aspirin-associated gastric ulcers. He has no history of H. pylori infection and has not had any revascularization procedure in the last 6 months. He has no history of alcoholism or drug addiction within the past year and has no significant psychiatric history. He understands and is able to comply with the study procedures required and is willing to provide written informed consent prior to any study procedures being performed. All other inclusion and exclusion criteria are met.

38F healthy Japanese volunteer with no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 23 and is a non-smoker. The patient has not consumed any alcohol in the last 6 months and her caffeine intake is limited to one cup of coffee per day. She is not currently taking any medications, including over-the-counter, herbal or homeopathic preparations. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of hereditary angioedema.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of stable angina pectoris. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any regular medications. He was referred for an elective coronary angioplasty using a radial approach. He has no previous history of coronary artery disease and his last cardiac catheterization was performed 5 years ago. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and signs the informed consent.

A 45-year-old female patient presented with a history of fatigue, nausea, and abdominal discomfort. She reported her symptoms have been ongoing for the past few months. Upon further investigation, she was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1. She has no prior history of treatment for hepatitis C or any other liver disease. She had no known allergies, and her medical history was otherwise unremarkable. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives. The initial liver function tests showed elevated levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST). The patient was advised to undergo further testing, including a liver biopsy, which confirmed chronic hepatitis C. She was counseled about the available treatment options, and after careful consideration, she decided to participate in a clinical trial investigating RO5024048 in combination with Pegasys and Copegus in patients with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 or 4. She was informed about the study procedures and potential risks and benefits and provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in the clinical trial on caloric stimulation and cerebral blood flow. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disease and is not pregnant or nursing. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has never had any inner ear or pulmonary issues. She is willing to undergo EEG and TCD monitoring for a total of 45 minutes, with 20 minutes of caloric stimulator use. She is able to provide informed consent and is excited to contribute to the study.

A 42-year-old male with a history of obesity, hypertension, and a previous laparoscopic cholecystectomy presents with a large ventral hernia. The patient has noticed a bulge in his abdomen that has progressively increased in size over the past year. He experiences discomfort and pain in his lower abdomen and has difficulty performing daily activities. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use illicit drugs. On examination, a large ventral hernia is noted, measuring approximately 12 cm in diameter with a fascial defect. The patient is scheduled for an abdominal wall reconstruction with component separation. During the preoperative evaluation, the patient is informed about the clinical trial and consents to participate. He is randomized to the study group and receives an unknown solution (solution A or B) of either 30ml of Exparel ((bupivacaine liposome injectable suspension) 1.3% ( 13.3mg/ml)) during the surgery. The patient is provided with Patient Controlled Analgesics (PCA) using Hydromorphone or orally dosed narcotic/acetaminophen combo analgesics for post-operative pain control. The pain scores, dermatomal level of anesthesia, nausea, emesis, return of bowel function, and length of stay are recorded in the electronic medical record. The patient's medical history is entered into a secure database for analysis. Once data collection is complete, the patient is informed which group he was randomized to and all of the data undergoes statistical analysis.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who has a history of hydrocephalus and has had a ventricular shunt placed. Recently, she has been experiencing headaches, vomiting, and lethargy. Her parents suspect that her shunt may be obstructed and take her to the emergency department. She is alert and able to give assent to participate in the study. The doctor suspects shunt obstruction and orders a ShuntCheck-Micro-Pumper test. The patient's shunt crosses the clavicle and is chronically indwelling. The test is performed and the results are compared to other diagnostic tests, including imaging and the attending physician's clinical judgment. The patient is monitored for up to 7 days to determine if the shunt is obstructed or patent. The patient has no other health conditions that would preclude or bias the results of the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl with a history of chronic abdominal pain and gastrointestinal issues. She has undergone previous diagnostic tests, including ultrasound and X-rays, which were inconclusive. Her pediatric gastroenterologist has recommended a diagnostic gastrointestinal endoscopy to further evaluate her symptoms. The patient is generally healthy and has no significant medical history, allergies, or medication use. She is currently at an ASA I-II level of health. Her parents are concerned about the sedation process and have expressed a preference for a sedation method that is both safe and effective. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares sedation with propofol-fentanyl and propofol-ketamine to determine the best option for their daughter. The patient has no respiratory infections or hyperactive airways, and there is no history of serious adverse effects related to anesthetics in her family. She does not suffer from morbid obesity or neuropsychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She has been advised to undergo mastectomy (surgical removal of the breast) as part of her treatment plan. She is concerned about the possible side effects of the surgery, particularly chronic persistent pain. She has experienced pain in the breast area before, but it has always been temporary and associated with menstrual cycles. This pain has never been severe enough to require medical attention. She is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help understand the frequency and presentations of chronic pain after breast cancer surgery, and to contribute to the development of guidelines for managing such pain. She has given consent to be enrolled in the study and agrees to be followed up for up to six months after the surgery.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her BMI is 25 kg/m2. She is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic surgery in a Trendelenburg position. The patient has no history of lung disease and her recent pulmonary function tests are normal. Her EKG and echocardiogram are also normal. She has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to participate. The patient has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 38-year-old female who has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 5 years. She has a history of joint pain, fever, fatigue, and skin rash. She has been treated with steroids and other immunosuppressive agents, and her symptoms have been well controlled. Recently, she has developed an unexplained rise in serum creatinine levels and proteinuria. She was diagnosed with lupus nephritis based on these findings and will undergo a kidney biopsy as part of her standard care of management. She has no history of chronic renal failure, diabetes mellitus, obstructive nephropathy, renal artery stenosis, hypertension, heart failure, hepatic diseases, existing intra renal A-V fistula or renal vein thrombosis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the role of renal resistive index (RRI) as a marker of severity and treatment outcomes in lupus nephritis.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with asthma since childhood. She has been experiencing mild to moderate asthma symptoms, including wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing. She has no history of smoking and no other debilitating systemic or life-threatening diseases. She has not experienced any asthma exacerbations requiring hospitalization in the past 6 months. The patient takes daily inhaled corticosteroids as prescribed by her physician. Despite her current medication regimen, she still experiences some asthma symptoms, which impact her daily activities. She is generally in good health and is not taking any other medications. Her medical history is non-significant.

A 55-year-old woman who was previously healthy now presents with weakness in her arms and legs, difficulty with speech and swallowing, and muscle twitching. She has had these symptoms for the past six months and has been diagnosed with ALS according to the El Escorial World Federation of Neurology revised research diagnostic criteria. She is able to complete assessments either alone or with the help of a caregiver. Her forced vital capacity (FVC) is >50% predicted measured within 30 days of screening. She is not currently taking any approved ALS treatments and her comorbid diseases are well-controlled. She is willing and able to complete all aspects of the study and is capable of taking multiple oral doses of DNL747 in a cross-over design.

This is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with severe preeclampsia during her pregnancy. She delivered a healthy baby girl via cesarean section two days ago and is now hospitalized for postpartum monitoring. She has a history of chronic hypertension and had an abnormal ultrasound finding during her pregnancy, which led to the diagnosis of preeclampsia. She is currently on medication to control her blood pressure and is being closely monitored by her healthcare team. She has agreed to participate in a research study that will evaluate the clinical utility of the Congo Red test GV-005 in following women with a clinical diagnosis of preeclampsia and clinically healthy women in the postpartum period. She will be asked to provide a urine sample daily during her hospitalization, and the Congo Red test GV-005 and a standard urine dipstick proteinuria test will be performed on her samples within 72 hours of collection. The purpose of this research is to evaluate progression of urine congophilia postpartum and to assess the usability and clinical utility of the Congo Red test GV-005.

62-year-old male with a history of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with radiographic evidence of metastatic disease in the bones and lymph nodes, confirmed by biopsy. The patient has been on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with a castrate level of testosterone for the past 8 months. The patient has had two serial rises in PSA from nadir with a minimum PSA of 3 ng/mL, indicating disease progression on ADT. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is currently not receiving any other study agents. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past 4 weeks and has recovered from any adverse events due to agents administered more than 4 weeks earlier. The patient has no history of brain metastases or seizures and is not currently taking any medications known to have seizure potential. The patient has not received prior CYP17 inhibitors or second-generation anti-androgens. The patient must be willing to undergo a needle biopsy of at least one site of metastatic disease. The patient must be able to take oral medications and have normal gastrointestinal function.

The patient is a 42 year old male who was found unconscious in a snow-covered field after being missing for several hours. The patient was known to be an avid skier and had been skiing alone in the backcountry. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient was found to be in hypothermic cardiac arrest with a core temperature of 28°C. Resuscitation efforts were initiated and the patient was successfully resuscitated after 30 minutes of CPR. The patient is now admitted to the ICU for further management. He has a past medical history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. He has no known drug allergies. The patient is married and works as a software engineer. He enjoys hiking and skiing in his free time. His vital signs include a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg, heart rate of 50 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 12 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. His ECG shows sinus bradycardia with prolonged QTc interval. His laboratory values reveal a serum potassium rate of 10 mmol/l.

A 32-year-old Caucasian man who works as a software developer complains of red, itchy, and scaly patches on his elbows, knees, and scalp. He has a history of psoriasis for the past 5 years. He has tried several topical treatments and phototherapy in the past which have provided some relief, but the symptoms have never completely resolved. He does not have any other significant medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He is married and has two children. His Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) score is 12. He is willing to start Enbrel (Etanercept) therapy as per the product monograph.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis for the past year presents with painful lesions on his lower legs. The lesions started as small, red, and painful bumps that gradually became ulcerated and necrotic. The patient reports that the pain is severe and is not relieved by any medication. He also reports that he has lost weight and feels fatigued. He has a history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. On physical examination, his lower legs are swollen, erythematous, and have multiple ulcerated lesions with black eschars. Laboratory results show serum calcium of 10.5 mg/dL, phosphorus of 6.0 mg/dL, and intact parathyroid hormone of 800 pg/mL. The patient is diagnosed with calciphylaxis and is started on wound care, pain management, and aggressive medical management of his calcium and phosphorus levels. He is offered the opportunity to participate in the European Calciphylaxis Registry Network and provides written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been referred for a diagnostic colonoscopy. He has a family history of colon cancer and has never had a colonoscopy before. He has been experiencing occasional abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits over the past few months. The patient has no known history of inflammatory bowel disease or colorectal cancer. The patient has no history of colorectal surgery, and he is willing to undergo the procedure with the initial dose of 2mg of midazolam intravenously. The patient has no known allergies to medications and has been instructed to take bowel prep with macrogolum prior to the procedure. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

This clinical trial is seeking children under the age of 18 with a deficiency of alpha-1 antitrypsin (DA1AT). The children must be included in the DefiAlpha cohort and have a signed informed consent from the patient or parents. The study aims to identify clinical and genetic factors that predispose a patient with DA1AT to liver damage. The study will involve comparing the allele frequencies of certain genetic polymorphisms between a cohort of A1AT deficient patients with hepatic symptoms and a cohort of A1AT deficient patients without signs of hepatic call. Family members of deficient patients who carry the Z/Z genotype but do not have any associated clinical manifestations may also be included in the study. The study will involve blood sampling and the creation of a DNA bank. The study will be conducted over a period of 30 months, and the total number of potentially includable subjects is estimated at about 400 in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has a history of elevated liver enzymes and liver steatosis on ultrasound. She takes medication for her diabetes and hypertension. She is overweight with a BMI of 30 kg/m². She is followed by the endocrinology clinic at Hôpitaux Universitaires de Strasbourg. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent. The patient is affiliated with a social security system. The patient does not consume more than 20g/d of alcohol and does not have a history of chronic viral hepatitis, liver auto immune disease, genetic hemochromatosis, or Wilson disease. She does not have biliary disease, bile duct obstruction, drug-induced liver injury, secondary liver cancer or other active cancer, organ graft, congestive heart failure, AIDS, pregnancy or breastfeeding. The patient is not under guardianship or judicial protection. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is a candidate for screening of NASH.

The patient is a 55-year-old post-menopausal woman with a history of hypertension for the past 2 years. She is currently taking a combination of an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic, which has been stable for the past 3 months. She has a history of smoking but quit 6 months ago. She drinks alcohol occasionally but does not use recreational drugs. She works as a teacher and is physically active, with a regular exercise routine. She has no history of ischaemic heart disease, cardiac failure, cerebrovascular disease, liver impairment, or chronic kidney disease. Her weight is 68kg. She reports occasional headaches and takes paracetamol as needed for pain relief. She has never had an overdose or suicidal ideation. She has no known allergies to medications and is not currently taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatories, oral anticoagulants or corticosteroids. Her most recent average daytime ambulatory blood pressure measurement (ABPM) was 140/90mmHg.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is concerned about her health and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She has a first-degree relative who was recently diagnosed with diabetes and wants to take preventative measures to reduce her risk. She works a desk job and spends most of her day sitting, both at work and during her leisure time. Her BMI is 27, and she is of South Asian descent. She is generally healthy but has noticed that she feels tired and sluggish during the day. She is interested in participating in the study to learn how to reduce her sedentary behavior and improve her overall health.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who has been experiencing recurring constipation for the past few months. He has been to the pediatrician's office twice in the past 3 months for this issue. He is generally healthy, with no known medical problems or chronic conditions. His parents report that he has a well-balanced diet, with plenty of fruits and vegetables, but he does not drink much water. The patient is currently not taking any medications, and has not recently undergone any surgery. The family resides in the city of Indianapolis, IN, and the patient receives primary care at one of the Eskenazi Health system clinics. They are willing to participate in the study to receive additional support for their child's constipation management.

The patient is a 29-year-old HIV-positive woman who has been receiving care and support at TASO Uganda. She is currently on ART and has a partner who is HIV-negative. They are considering having a child but are concerned about the risk of transmission. The patient is interested in learning about safer conception methods and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help improve HIV family planning services. She has no history of pregnancy and is not currently pregnant. She is in good health and has no other medical conditions.

A 65-year-old woman was diagnosed with advanced-stage ovarian cancer and has been recommended to undergo chemotherapy with carboplatin/paclitaxel in combination with Avastin (bevacizumab) as first-line treatment. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it regularly. She does not have any known allergies to drugs or food. She has undergone a hysterectomy in the past and has completed menopause. She is currently not experiencing any major symptoms related to her cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance treatment options for ovarian cancer patients.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a history of coronary artery disease and has previously undergone coronary artery bypass surgery. He was recently diagnosed with end-stage heart failure and was referred for a heart transplant evaluation. He has been on the waiting list for a heart donor for three months and has been experiencing symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a supportive family and has been compliant with his medical treatment. He has agreed to participate in the Heart Transplant Registry of Városmajor and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis, including nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, and early satiety for the past 6 months. Despite making changes to her diet and taking prescribed medications, her symptoms have not improved. Her most recent HbA1c level was 7.5% and her fasting blood glucose level was 180 mg/dL. She has no history of gastric surgery, intrapyloric botulinum toxin, or gastric pacemaker. She has not received acupuncture treatment in the past. She has no history of malabsorptive syndrome, liver or pulmonary disease, and is not pregnant. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol.

N/A - This clinical trial does not require patient enrollment or participation as it is a time-and-motion study comparing nursing and pharmacy time for delivering Xeloda® versus 5-Fluoruracil regimens.

An adult male patient, aged 55, with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presents with symptoms of chest pain and dyspnea. The patient has been experiencing these symptoms for the past two weeks. Upon physical examination, the patient's blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, pulse rate is 85 beats per minute, and respiration rate is 18 breaths per minute. The patient is scheduled for elective cardiac surgery due to severe coronary artery disease. The patient has never been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation or any other supraventricular arrhythmia. The patient's liver function tests and serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. The patient is not currently taking colchicine or any other anti-inflammatory medication. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the effect of colchicine on the incidence of atrial fibrillation in open-heart surgery patients.

The patient is a 38 year-old premenopausal woman who has been experiencing heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding for the past year. She has also been experiencing pelvic pain, bloating and pressure. She has no history of infertility and has had one uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. She has a BMI of 28 and takes occasional over-the-counter pain medication for her symptoms. Pelvic ultrasound revealed multiple uterine fibroids, the largest of which measures 4 cm. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription medication. She is interested in exploring non-surgical treatment options for her uterine fibroids and is willing to participate in the study.

An 80 year old man came to the clinic complaining of low back pain that he has been suffering from for the past six months. He describes the pain as a dull ache that is present most of the time, but becomes more severe with prolonged standing or walking. He has tried taking over-the-counter pain medications but has not found any significant relief. He reports no history of trauma or injury to his back. He walks with a cane due to some balance issues and has been experiencing some difficulty with everyday activities like getting dressed and lifting objects. He is on a stable prescription medication plan and is independent in his daily activities. His Folstein Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28. He is not currently receiving any treatment for his low back pain from other healthcare providers.

55 yo F with a confirmed diagnosis of B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has had 2 failed courses of prior standard chemotherapy and biologic therapy, including Rituxan. She presents with measurable disease and evidence of CD22-positive malignancy, with over 30% of malignant cells from a disease site CD22+ by FACS analysis. She has an indolent subtype of CD22+ B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, specifically follicular lymphoma. She is at stage III-IV of the disease. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and her life expectancy is estimated to be less than 6 months. She understands and has signed the informed consent, and agrees to use an approved method of contraception during the study. She has not undergone a bone marrow transplant, and does not have documented and ongoing central nervous system involvement with her malignant disease. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have plasma containing either a significant level of antibody to CAT-8015 or antibody that neutralizes the binding of CAT-8015 to CD22. She is HIV negative and does not have Hepatitis B surface antigen. She does not have uncontrolled, symptomatic, intercurrent illness or social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. Her liver function, renal function, hematologic function, and pulmonary function meet the eligibility criteria. She has not received cytotoxic chemotherapy, corticosteroids, whole body electron beam radiation therapy, hormonal, biologic, or other standard or any investigational therapy of the malignancy for 3 weeks prior to entry into the trial. She has not had monoclonal antibody therapy (i.e. rituximab) in the past 3 months. She has not received radiation therapy less than 3 weeks prior to study entry. She has not received prior pseudomonas-exotoxin immunotoxin (PE) administration.

A 25-year-old pregnant woman who lives in a rural area with limited access to healthcare came to the clinic for her prenatal check-up at 36 weeks of gestation. She has no significant medical history and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy. She plans to deliver at home with the help of a traditional birth attendant. She has heard of women experiencing excessive bleeding after delivery and is concerned about this possibility. She is willing to participate in a study that provides her with a first aid measure to address excessive postpartum bleeding. She speaks the local language and is able to provide informed consent.

A 54-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer presents with worsening fatigue and shortness of breath. She has previously undergone curative and survival prolonging therapies, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy, but has not responded well to these treatments. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her ANC and platelet levels are within normal limits. Her SGOT and SGPT levels are within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, and her total bilirubin and serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. Her calculated creatinine clearance is 60 ml/minute. She has not undergone major surgery in the past 3 weeks and has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 4 weeks. She has no history of clinically significant arrhythmias, heart block, or prolonged QTc interval on electrocardiogram. She does not have active brain metastases, and is not receiving any drugs that are substrates of cytochrome P450-3A4 (CYP3A4). She is not taking NSAIDs or other potentially nephrotoxic medications. The patient is willing to use effective contraception as she is still of childbearing potential. She is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and has given her signed informed consent.

50 yo M recently diagnosed with stage III Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma (NHL) who is a potential candidate for autologous stem cell transplantation. Patient completed 4 cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy with last cycle completed 4 weeks prior to study drug administration. Patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has recovered from all acute toxic effects of prior chemotherapy. Patient has a white blood cell (WBC) count of 4.2 x 109/L, an absolute neutrophil count of 2.0 x 109/L, and a platelet count of 120 x 109/L on screening laboratory assessments. Patient has a serum creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL, AST and ALT levels within normal range, and total bilirubin level of 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) on screening laboratory assessments. Patient has tested negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Patient has adequate cardiac and pulmonary function to undergo leukapheresis at the Investigator's discretion. Patient is willing to use a double-barrier method of contraception from study Day 1 until 28 days after the last dose of TG-0054. Patient is able to provide signed informed consent.   Note: Additional information, such as patient's medical history, past treatments, and current medications, should also be taken into consideration when selecting patients for this clinical trial.

A 60-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer presents with a rising PSA level. He is scheduled for robot-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy under general anesthesia. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His current medications include aspirin and a multivitamin. His BMI is 25 kg/m2. He has no known allergies to any medication or food. He has normal kidney function with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 80 mL/min/1.73m2. He has read and understood the patient consent form for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing upper gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating and nausea. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m² and is 165 cm tall. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has not had any recent upper gastrointestinal bleeding and has not undergone any prior lower esophageal or gastric surgery. She has fasted for 8 hours prior to the study.

A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of numbness and tingling in her right hand, which worsens at night. She has a history of mild to moderate carpal tunnel syndrome in her right wrist, confirmed by recent electro-diagnostic evidence. The patient reports difficulty in performing daily activities and has noticed a weakness in her right thenar muscles. She has no history of surgical carpal tunnel release and is not currently receiving any treatment for carpal tunnel syndrome. The patient has not been diagnosed with diabetes and has no history of radiculopathy or thoracic outlet syndrome. Her skin integrity is intact, and she has no past history of traumatic events, surgery, or congenital impairments of the forearm, wrist, or hand. The patient is able to understand and sign informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an active splint for the relief of pain due to carpal tunnel syndrome.

The patient is a 63 year old man who suffered a myocardial infarction (heart attack) three years ago. Since then, he has been taking aspirin and clopidogrel as part of his standard of care. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. He also has a family history of heart disease. He does not have any bleeding disorders or abnormalities and has not had any recent surgeries. His most recent platelet count was within normal limits. He is not currently taking any other blood thinning medications and is not pregnant. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if adding vorapaxar to his current standard of care can provide additional benefit in preventing future heart attacks or strokes.

57 yo male with a long history of peripheral arterial disease and uncontrolled diabetes presents with a non-healing ulcer on his left foot. He has already undergone multiple revascularization procedures but continues to experience severe pain and limited mobility. His toe pressure and ABI measurements confirm critical limb ischemia with poor distal artery runoff. He is currently on multiple medications including insulin, aspirin, and statins. Despite his best efforts, his blood sugar levels remain elevated. He is interested in exploring alternative treatment options and is willing to participate in clinical trials.

The patient is a 35-year-old man diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. He has been taking risperidone for the past 6 months but has noticed persistent symptoms of emotional instability, detachment from reality, and hallucinations. The patient is not satisfied with his current treatment and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of flexible-dose of paliperidone extended-release. He is not currently on any other medication and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 6 months. The patient is willing to practice an effective method of birth control throughout the study as he is sexually active. He has never taken clozapine and does not have a history of non-responsiveness to oral antipsychotic treatment. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

52-year-old male with a unilateral transtibial amputation due to a traumatic injury sustained during military service. He has been using a prosthesis for the past year and has been using an unpowered prosthesis for the past 6 months. He is able to walk unassisted for up to 20 minutes at a time before experiencing fatigue. He has no history of orthopedic or neurologic disorders to his intact limb and has no history of cardiovascular disease. He is motivated to improve his physical activity level and is interested in participating in a study to determine the effectiveness of a powered prosthesis compared to his current unpowered prosthesis during extended periods of walking.

A 16-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's disease is experiencing symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. The patient was diagnosed with Crohn's disease two years ago, and he has been receiving medical therapy for the condition since then. He has undergone CT and MRI scans in the past to evaluate the disease extent and activity. The patient is scheduled for a clinically-indicated CT enterography or MR enterography, and his pediatric gastroenterologist has confirmed the presence of active disease. The patient is between the ages of 10 and 18 years and weighs 68kg with a BMI of 23kg/m2. He has no history of allergies to contrast agents, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no history of unstable cardiopulmonary conditions or kidney disease. The patient and his parents have provided written consent for the study and are willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 13-year-old adolescent diagnosed with HIV-1 infection presents with symptoms of depression, anxiety, and social isolation. The patient's primary caregiver is their mother, who is also HIV-positive and receives antiretroviral therapy. The patient has been informed of their HIV status and is struggling to cope with the implications of the diagnosis. The patient and caregiver both speak and understand English. The patient is currently attending school but has difficulty making friends and feels isolated from their peers due to the stigma associated with HIV. The patient's CD4 count is within the normal range, and viral load is undetectable due to antiretroviral therapy. The patient and their caregiver are interested in participating in a life skills intervention program that would help the patient develop coping and communication skills to manage the challenges associated with their HIV diagnosis.

A 28-year-old male presents with a sharp, intermittent toothache in his lower left jaw for the past three days. He reports sensitivity to hot and cold foods and beverages on this tooth. The pain is severe and wakes him up at night. There is no history of trauma, and he has not taken any medication for the pain. The dental examination reveals a large, deep carious lesion on the distal surface of the mandibular left first molar. The tooth is tender to percussion and palpation, and there is no mobility. Radiographic examination shows periapical radiolucency, which is consistent with irreversible pulpitis. The patient has no history of systemic disease or allergies and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old woman who received a kidney transplant three years ago due to end-stage renal disease secondary to lupus nephritis. She has been taking tacrolimus and prednisone with a stable dose for the past three months. Her serum creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dL, and there has been no significant variation in the past three months. She has no proteinuria or history of liver or hematological disease. She has no known allergies to mycophenolate sodium or any other medications. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is an active member of her community. She has no history of cancer or plans to become pregnant in the next year.

This clinical trial is not applicable for generating a patient description as it is designed for a group of athletes who are members of Western University's coed cheerleading team for the 2019 competitive season. It does not involve individual patients seeking treatment for a medical condition.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who underwent a routine check-up and was found to have an abnormal liver function test (LFT) result. He has no history of liver disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, within the normal range. He has no family history of liver disease. He is eligible for the Long-term Follow Up of Patients in the Birmingham and Lambeth Liver Evaluation Strategies (BALLETS) study as he meets the inclusion criteria.

A 52 year old man visited the gastroenterology clinic with complaints of abdominal pain, constipation, and occasional blood in his stool. Upon examination, the doctor recommended that he undergo a colonoscopy for further evaluation. The patient has no history of colonic resection or severe inflammatory bowel disease. He is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. The patient is 5'10" and weighs 180 pounds. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He has never undergone a colonoscopy before and is anxious about the procedure.

The patient is a 5-year-old child diagnosed with retinoblastoma, a form of eye cancer. The diagnosis was made based on imaging exams, including ophthalmoscopic and ultrasound evaluations. The tumor is either bilateral or multifocal unilateral disease, with no metastasis. The child has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The child is generally healthy and has no significant medical history except for the retinoblastoma diagnosis. The child is under the age of 10 and has a good performance status. The parents are aware of the risks and benefits of the study and have given informed consent. The child will be followed up closely by the medical team for a total of 12 years. The child is eligible for this clinical trial to receive carboplatin and vincristine, which are chemotherapy drugs designed to stop tumor cells from dividing and growing. The aim of this study is to assess the effectiveness of this treatment in children with retinoblastoma, estimate the objective response rate and assess the success of this regimen in delaying radiotherapy and eliminating the need for surgery.

A 35-year-old man visited the clinic after being involved in a motor vehicle accident that occurred two weeks ago. He reported experiencing a headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating since the accident. He also had a brief loss of consciousness during the accident. He was not taken to the hospital after the accident and did not receive medical attention until now. He is fluent in English and agreed to take a computerized neurocognitive test battery. He is within the eligible age range for the study.

A 25-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of bipolar disorder who has been admitted to the hospital for psychiatric services related to a first-episode psychosis. He has been prescribed an antipsychotic medication for the first time and is currently taking risperidone. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus, seizure disorders, or mental retardation. He is fluent in English and able to give informed consent. He has never received more than 12 weeks of total lifetime exposure to antipsychotics. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo MRI scans.

A 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma two years ago is looking for alternative treatments as his cancer has become non-resectable and non-responsive to 1st and 2nd line chemotherapy. Due to the toxicity of chemotherapy, he is no longer a candidate for this treatment. He has discussed the option of chemotherapy with his medical team but he prefers to avoid it if possible. He has a good performance status (ECOG 1) and is willing to participate in this pilot study to receive Botox injections in the tumor and the surrounding stomach wall. He does not have any known allergies to the components of Botox and does not have any other cancer disease that is not under control. He is not receiving any other concomitant treatment for cancer and does not have a serious mental illness.

A 58-year-old male patient was diagnosed with chronic heart failure (CHF) three years ago. He is classified as NYHA class II and has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%. He takes medications for CHF regularly and has no other significant medical history. He has no history of diabetes or significant cardiac valve disease. He reports that he experiences shortness of breath during physical activity, but no chest pain or other symptoms. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. His BMI is 28 kg/m2 and he is physically inactive due to his fatigue. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve his condition and contribute to medical research.

60-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer treated with radical prostatectomy several years ago. He has been experiencing biochemical recurrence with PSA doubling time of 6 months. He has not had any prior treatment with androgen deprivation therapy or anti-androgens. He has not received chemotherapy for prostate cancer, and has not had bilateral orchiectomy. He has had adjuvant radiation to the prostate bed only. He has undergone a comprehensive workup for metastasis, including CT/MRI of the abdomen and pelvis, as well as a radionuclide bone scan, all of which were negative. His ECOG performance status is 0. He has normal organ function with serum AST/ALT/bilirubin within normal limits. His serum potassium, creatinine clearance, and platelets are also within normal limits. His serum albumin is 3.5 g/dL.
