He is not on any medication known to lower the seizure threshold. He is willing to use a condom and another effective method of birth control if he is having sex with a woman of childbearing potential or agrees to use a condom if he is having sex with a woman who is pregnant while on study drug and for 3 months following the last dose of study drug. He is eligible for this study.

A 35-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in the GSK2251052 Mass Balance study. He has no significant medical history and takes no prescription or non-prescription medications, vitamins, or supplements. He has not consumed any red wine, grapefruit or grapefruit juice in the past 7 days. He is a non-smoker and has no history of regular alcohol consumption in the past 6 months. His BMI is 24.5 kg/m2 and his weight is 75 kg. He is willing to comply with the study procedures, including the use of contraception during the study and for at least 90 days after the dose of GSK2251052. He has no sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. He is mentally and legally capable of giving written informed consent and is available to complete the study and return for follow-up visits if necessary.

28 year old female with a history of bipolar I disorder diagnosed at age 22. The patient has a history of manic episodes with symptoms of elevated mood, grandiosity, and decreased need for sleep. The patient's current episode is a mixed episode with symptoms of both mania and depression, including irritability, racing thoughts, decreased appetite, and feelings of hopelessness. The patient has previously been treated with lithium and valproate as monotherapy, but has not achieved full remission of symptoms. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to lithium, valproate, or aripiprazole. The patient has not participated in a clinical trial with aripiprazole in the past.

A 26-year-old African American male who identifies as gay came to the clinic concerned about his risk for HIV. He has had sexual intercourse with multiple partners, including males, in the past three months. He is currently sexually active and does not use condoms consistently. He is willing to take an HIV test and identify a friend or relative to participate in the study. He has no known medical conditions and is not on any medications. He lives with his roommate, who is also sexually active and identifies as gay. He is highly motivated to learn more about HIV prevention and to share the information with his social network.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who sustained a left knee injury while playing football. The injury occurred 3 months ago, and he was diagnosed with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury. He underwent physical therapy for the past 3 months and has not undergone any surgical interventions. He reports difficulty with usual activities, including running and jumping, and has significant instability in his left knee. MRI findings revealed a complete tear of the ACL. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. He is interested in participating in the study to determine if he is a candidate for non-surgical ACL treatment.

45-year-old male with a BMI of 38, who has been attending the UCLH Centre for Weight Loss, Metabolic & Endocrine Surgery (UCLH bariatric clinic) for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, and sleep apnea. He has been on Metformin and Losartan for the past year. He is a non-smoker and works as a software engineer. He reports occasional bleeding gums when brushing his teeth and has noticed bad breath lately. He has never received periodontal therapy in the past. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the prevalence and severity of Periodontal Disease (PD) in obese patients. He has voluntarily given written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of Ischemic heart disease who is scheduled to undergo elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. He has been experiencing symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue even with minimal exertion. He has been managing his symptoms with medications prescribed by his cardiologist. He is fluent in Danish and willing to participate in the SheppHeartCABG clinical trial. He has no neurological or orthopedic deficits that may prevent him from participating in the physical exercise component of the intervention. He is aware of the potential benefits and risks involved in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 60-year-old man was admitted to the hospital for a planned surgery to remove his gallbladder. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well controlled with medication. The surgery was successful, and he was discharged after an overnight stay in the hospital. However, during his stay, he had an episode of atrial fibrillation, which resolved spontaneously within 24 hours. The patient is concerned about his risk of stroke due to this episode and has been referred to the ASPIRE-AF trial. His CHA2DS2VASc score is 4, and he meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He has no history of bleeding disorders or other contraindications to anticoagulation. He is willing to participate in the study and understand the risks and benefits of the treatment options. He is compliant with his medications and follow-up appointments.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia presents with a history of nonadherence to oral antipsychotic medication, resulting in frequent relapses and hospitalizations. The patient has a history of at least one inpatient psychiatric hospitalization in the past 4 years and has been managed as an outpatient for the past 4 weeks. The patient has responded to previous antipsychotic treatment and is deemed fit for extended treatment with a long-acting injectable formulation. The patient is able to provide written informed consent, understands the nature of the trial, and is able to follow the protocol requirements. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial with an investigational agent within the past 30 days and has not received electroconvulsive therapy in the past 7 months. The patient has no known history of hypersensitivity to antipsychotic agents or any significant substance use disorder within 3 months prior to screening. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, is sexually active, and commits to utilizing birth control during the trial and for up to 180 days following the trial. The patient has no known medical conditions that would expose them to undue risk of a significant adverse event or interfere with assessments of safety or efficacy during the course of the trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma stage T2, N0. He is currently being evaluated for potential surgical resection. The patient has never undergone any surgical procedures and has no known allergies to fluorescein or drugs. He is able to understand the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient is registered with the French social security regime. The patient has no history of multiple or serious allergic reactions to drugs and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no conditions or diseases that would prevent participation in study procedures. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is not under guardianship.

The patient is a healthy individual between the ages of 20 and 35. They have no neurological impairments, learning disabilities, or psychological syndromes that might affect their executive function performance. They are able to understand English instructions and have no difficulty hearing or seeing stimuli. They have not experienced any serious adverse events during pregnancy or birth and have not suffered from any injuries or major traumas that might affect their current executive function performance or stress responsivity. They are not currently experiencing undue life stress levels and are not taking any medication that affects their thinking, memory, mental clarity, or any other executive function ability. They are not taking any medication that influences circulating gonadal hormone levels or have taken such medications within the preceding four months. They are not smokers, do not use recreational drugs, and have not consumed alcohol within the past 24 hours. For female patients, they have a period that occurs roughly every month and are not pregnant or nursing. They do not have glaucoma, heart conditions, or are anxious, tense, or agitated. They are not taking any medication that might interfere with the study, such as monoamine oxidase inhibitors, pressor agents, coumarin anticoagulants, anticonvulsants, phenylbutazone, tricyclic antidepressants, or cold or allergy medicine that contain decongestants. Finally, they are not allergic to anything in the MPH or Vitamin C capsules.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who suffered a heart attack 6 weeks ago. He was diagnosed with significant coronary artery disease and was recommended for coronary bypass surgery. His ejection fraction is 25%, and he continues to experience shortness of breath and fatigue with minimal exertion. He has no significant past medical history, and his current medications include aspirin, a beta-blocker, and a statin. He has no known allergies. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the safety and effectiveness of implanted skeletal muscle cells from his thigh muscle into the scarred areas of his heart muscle.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma, which has relapsed and has failed to respond to at least one prior course of therapy. He complains of bone pain, fatigue, and weakness. He has undergone radiation therapy in the past for bone pain relief. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 9 g/dl WBC: 4000 /mm3 Plt: 100000 /ml Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy. He is willing to use adequate contraception for the duration of the active treatment phase of the study and for at least 4 months after the last dose of chemotherapy.

A 35-year-old African-American woman with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol presented to the clinic complaining of fatigue, shortness of breath, and difficulty losing weight. On physical examination, she had a body mass index of 35, a waist circumference of 105 cm, and elevated blood pressure (142/90 mmHg). Her fasting blood glucose level was 110 mg/dL, and her lipid profile showed an elevated triglyceride level of 170 mg/dL and a low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol level of 38 mg/dL. She was diagnosed with metabolic syndrome, and her primary care physician recommended lifestyle modifications and prescribed medications to control her blood pressure and cholesterol levels. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effects of nanomicielle curcumin on oxidative stress, inflammation, and other markers associated with metabolic syndrome. She was not taking any weight loss supplements or unusual weight loss plans, and had no other chronic diseases or conditions that would exclude her from participating in the trial.

A 58-year-old male patient who recently underwent elective cardiac surgery for aortic valve replacement is experiencing respiratory distress postoperatively. The patient is experiencing hypoxemia and hypercapnia and requires non-invasive ventilation (NIV) to counter the development of pulmonary atelectasis. The patient is hemodynamically stable and is able to breathe spontaneously. There is no history of chronic obstructive respiratory disease (COPD) beyond stage II. The patient has given prior consent and has social security coverage. The patient is not under legal guardianship or incarceration.

56 F with a history of follicular grade 2 non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma, diagnosed in [**2138-8-15**]. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with rituximab, but unfortunately, her lymphoma has progressed. She is currently experiencing generalized lymphadenopathy, night sweats, and fatigue. PET scan shows diffuse lymphadenopathy with multiple nodes measuring >2 cm in size. Biopsy confirms the presence of CD20 antigen expression. She has adequate renal and hepatic function. She has not received any chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunosuppressants, or cytokine treatment within the past 4 weeks. She does not have active obstructive hydronephrosis, brain or leptomeningeal metastasis, active infection requiring IV antibiotics, and has not had previous allergic reaction to iodine. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, does not have known HIV infection, and is not Human anti-murine antibody (HAMA) positive. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to further treat her relapsed indolent non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma.

55-year-old female presents with recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She has a history of Crohn's disease and has undergone multiple surgeries in the past. Her most recent small bowel imaging showed possible strictures in the distal ileum that could not be fully evaluated with CT enterography. She has previously undergone video capsule endoscopy which showed ulcerations in the small bowel but biopsy could not be performed. She is now being considered for motorized spiral enteroscopy to further evaluate and potentially biopsy the strictures in her small bowel. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent.

Patient is a 6-year-old boy diagnosed with Glucose Transporter Type 1 Deficiency Syndrome (Glut1 DS) confirmed by SLC2A1 mutation. He has been experiencing an average of 4 observable seizures per week (generalized or partial-onset) over the last 24 weeks. Despite being on antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), he is still having seizures. He is not on a prescribed diet plan and has a plasma level of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) ≤ 1 mmol/L (non-fasting) at screening. He is allowed to be on up to 3 concomitant AEDs that have been stable in dose for at least 2 weeks prior to screening. He provides written assent and his parents provide written informed consent for him to participate in the study. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He has not used triheptanoin within 30 days prior to screening and has not used any investigational products within 30 days prior to screening. He is willing and able to complete all aspects of the study and comply with accurate completion of the seizures diary.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is generally healthy and has no history of neurological disorders. He has no history of spine or brain surgery or trauma, and has not had a lumbar puncture within the past month. He is willing to undergo multiple imaging sessions and undergo an LP procedure. He has no claustrophobia and is able to lay still and supine during the imaging sessions. His medical history, physical examination, vital signs, and clinical laboratory values are within normal limits. He has had a normal screening MRI to exclude subjects with a mass, congenital malformation or an abnormal curvature of the spine that could alter CSF flow. He is not pregnant or nursing. He is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the transport kinetics of CNS exposure to gadolinium contrast injected into the lumbar intrathecal space, and to evaluate changes with age.

A 22-year-old college student has been experiencing moderate to severe allergy symptoms when exposed to cats for the past 3 years. The patient is a non-smoker, has no history of illicit drug use, and doesn't have any known chronic illnesses. The allergy symptoms include sneezing, itchy and watery eyes, nasal congestion, and occasional cough. The student tried various antihistamines, nasal sprays, and eye drops, but the symptoms persist. The patient has a positive skin prick test to cat hair and cat dander specific IgE levels of 0.5 kU/L. The patient optionally has controlled asthma with the use of a rescue inhaler as needed. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help manage the allergy symptoms that interfere with their daily life and academic performance.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 8 years ago. She has been receiving treatment with continuous subcutaneous apomorphine infusion for the past year. She reports experiencing skin reactions, including erythema, swelling, and nodular formation, at the infusion site. The skin reactions have been progressively worsening and are causing discomfort and interference with the absorption of apomorphine. The patient has no known history of allergies or hypersensitivity to medications. She is compliant with her medication regimen and has no history of respiratory depression. The patient has no history of Cushing's disease or hypercortisolism. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is willing to use a highly effective contraceptive method during the study if sexually active. The patient is considered reliable and capable of adhering to the protocol, visit schedule, and medication intake according to the judgment of the investigator.

A 42-year-old female patient visited the clinic complaining of an uncomfortable sensation in her legs that always occurred when she was resting or lying down. She described the sensation as a creeping, crawling, or pulling feeling that made her want to move her legs to relieve the discomfort. This condition had been occurring for at least 15 nights in the prior month, making it difficult for her to fall asleep and stay asleep. The patient had no history of sleep disorders or neurological diseases. The International RSL Study Group Diagnostic Criteria were met, and the symptoms were documented for at least 4 of the 7 consecutive evenings/nights during the baseline study period. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ASP8825 for the treatment of restless legs syndrome.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of Type 2 diabetes for five years came to the clinic, complaining of high blood pressure. Her most recent HbA1c was 7.2%, and she was taking metformin and amlodipine for her diabetes and hypertension, respectively. Her average systolic blood pressure over three screening visits was 145mmHg, and her diastolic blood pressure was less than 90mmHg. She has no known food allergies or intolerances and is willing to eat meals provided by the study during the controlled feeding periods. She weighs 180 pounds and is 5'4" tall with a BMI of 30.9. She takes a multivitamin daily and does not use any other vitamin or herbal supplements. She does not consume more than 14 alcoholic drinks per week and is not a smoker. She has no history of heart or kidney disease.

A 25 yo F living in Karachi, Pakistan, presenting with persistent abdominal pain and discomfort. The patient underwent endoscopy and was diagnosed with Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. There is no prior history of H. pylori infection treatment or other significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of an Unani formulation compared to the standard quadruple regimen for H. pylori treatment. The patient is not pregnant and has no known allergies or adverse reactions to medications.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with mandibular prognathism and malocclusion. He is scheduled for elective orthognathic surgery to correct the deformity. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and he has no history of psychiatric, hepatobiliary, or renal disease. He is not taking any monoamine oxidase inhibitors. The patient is experiencing moderate-to-severe pain in the jaw and face due to his condition, and he is otherwise healthy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of perioperative nefopam in reducing postoperative pain.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, and currently takes medication for both conditions. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. His echocardiography results show left ventricular hypertrophy and tissue doppler abnormalities. His NT-proBNP levels are elevated at 250 pg/ml. The patient has not experienced any recent infarctions or severe arrhythmias, but has mild mitral regurgitation. He has agreed to participate in the study to further understand and manage his condition.

This is a 35 year-old male with a history of spinal cord injury resulting in neurogenic bladder. He has been performing intermittent self-catheterization for over a year with the same silicon catheter. He has had no previous issues with urinary tract infections and is interested in participating in a study investigating the safety and satisfaction of re-using catheters for intermittent self-catheterization. He is able to use catheters of size CH12 or CH14 and has not been on antibiotics in the last 4 weeks. He has no known urological or renal anatomical abnormalities that would impact his participation in the study. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer three years ago. She underwent surgery and received six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel as first-line treatment. Unfortunately, her cancer has relapsed and she is now experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating. Her CA-125 level is elevated at 180 U/mL. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise healthy. Her blood work shows: Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL WBC: 4.5 x 10^9/L ANC: 2.5 x 10^9/L Platelets: 150 x 10^9/L Total bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL AST: 20 U/L ALT: 18 U/L Serum creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL She has no history of allergic reactions to carboplatin or paclitaxel. She has not received any PARP inhibitors in the past. She has not received any systemic chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the last 2 weeks. She is willing and able to swallow oral medication. She has a life expectancy of greater than 16 weeks.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been addicted to opioids for the past 4 years. He started using opioids recreationally but eventually became dependent on them. He has tried to quit several times but has been unsuccessful due to the withdrawal symptoms. He is currently not employed and has no stable housing. He has a history of depression and anxiety but has not received any treatment for these conditions. He is willing to attend the clinic 6 days a week for the study and is motivated to quit using opioids. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He is willing to use adequate birth control during the study. His physical examination is unremarkable and his laboratory tests are within normal limits. His urine drug screen is positive for opioids but negative for other drugs of abuse.

A 56-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with stage I non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has never undergone chemotherapy or radiation therapy before. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, meaning he is fully ambulatory but restricted in strenuous activity. He has no evidence of distant metastases or nodal involvement. His tumor diameter is 3.5 cm as assessed by diagnostic CT. He underwent FDG PET/CT of chest within 60 days prior to randomization, and his tumor's SUV max is 7.2. The patient's medical team determined that he is not a surgical candidate, and he agreed to participate in this clinical trial. His liver, kidney, and heart functions are all normal, and his pulmonary function testing showed an FEV1 of 2.5 L and a DLCO of 19.3 ml/min/mmHg. He is willing to use effective contraception throughout the study period and for 5 months after the last dose of atezolizumab.

A 28-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis (positive sweat chloride value ≥ 60 mEq/L) and chronic pulmonary disease is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to cholecystitis. She has a history of recurrent pulmonary infections and has undergone multiple hospitalizations for her CF exacerbations. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any regular medications except for pancreatic enzymes and inhaled bronchodilators. She has no allergies to any medications, and her vital signs are stable. She has a BMI of 22 and oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. She has no current pulmonary symptoms, such as cough or sputum production, and her lung exam is clear. She has no past history of anesthesia-related complications. She is aware of the study and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) two years ago. He participated in the FT500-101 clinical trial and received allogeneic NK cell immunotherapy as part of his treatment. He responded well to the treatment and has been in remission for over a year. He is interested in participating in the FT-003 long term follow-up study to provide long-term safety and efficacy data on his treatment. He has provided informed consent prior to his study participation. He is currently receiving other therapies for his cancer while being followed for long term safety in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with skin phototype III, who has never received botulinum toxin type A (BT-A) injections before. She is interested in improving the appearance of her wrinkles and fine lines on her forehead, glabella, and crow's feet. She has no history of neoplastic, muscular, or neurological diseases, and her medical history and physical examination do not prevent her from participating in the study. She is not pregnant, and her urine pregnancy test is negative. She is currently using an oral contraceptive and has been for the last three months. She has no scars on her face that may interfere with the result of the study. She is willing to adhere to the study protocol and not undergo other cosmetic or dermatological procedures during the study. She understands the study requirements and is willing to attend all six visits throughout the 24-week study period.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a body weight of 70kg and a body mass index (BMI) of 24. He has no history of adalimumab treatment or relevant allergies. He understands the purpose of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent according to the Declaration of Helsinki. He has not participated in any interventional trial within the past three months or donated blood more than 200 mL within the past 12 weeks. He has not used any drugs or traditional Chinese medicine within two weeks prior to administration of the study drug. He has no history of cluster of differentiation 4 antagonist or tumor necrosis factor alpha antagonist use, or use of tumor necrosis factor antagonist within the past three months. He has normal chest radiograph, ECG, and laboratory examinations at screening and baseline. He has no history of opportunistic infection within the past six months and is negative for HIV and hepatitis C virus antibodies. He has no active or chronic hepatitis B virus infection and no history of organ transplant. He has no known immunodeficiency history and has not used a live vaccine within the past three months. He has not abused alcohol or drugs within the past 12 months and is willing to refrain from alcohol during the trial period. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. He has no evidence of clinically significant hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, endocrine, respiratory, hematologic, or neurologic abnormality. He is mentally competent and physically able to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with HIV 10 years ago and has been taking antiretroviral therapy since then. He has a history of alcohol and tobacco use, but he has quit both for over a year. He has also been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago and is currently taking metformin and a sulfonylurea. His most recent hemoglobin A1c level was 8.5%, indicating poor glucose control. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. His most recent blood pressure reading was 140/90 mmHg. He is overweight with a BMI of 27. He has never had any opportunistic infections, but his CD4 count is 420 cells/mm3 and his viral load is undetectable. He has been experiencing symptoms of insulin resistance, including difficulty controlling his blood sugar levels and fat accumulation around his waist. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve his diabetic symptoms.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He is a retired factory worker who smoked for 40 years before quitting 7 years ago. He has experienced occasional exacerbations of his COPD symptoms, but has been clinically stable for the past month. His BMI is 28. He has no other significant medical conditions and is currently not taking any medications for his COPD. He speaks Mandarin Chinese fluently and is able to read and understand the language.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who has been diagnosed with breast cancer-related lymphoedema (BCRL) on her right arm. She underwent a mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection two years ago. She started to experience swelling and tightness in her right arm about six months after the surgery. She also has a feeling of heaviness and discomfort in the affected arm. She tried different conservative treatments for the past year, including complex decongestive physiotherapy (CDP), but she has not been compliant with the compression bandages due to discomfort and inconvenience. She is not currently undergoing any cancer treatments. Her medical history is positive for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any skin diseases or active infections. Her right arm circumference is significantly larger than her left arm, with a difference of 5 cm. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Kinesio® Tex tape (KT) applied to anastomotic regions along with CDP in the management of BCRL.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and a persistent sore throat for the past few months. He has a history of smoking and drinking alcohol regularly, but has cut back significantly in recent years. He also has a history of acid reflux and occasional heartburn. He takes antacids as needed. He is currently employed as a construction worker and enjoys playing golf on the weekends. He is married with two adult children. His father had a history of head and neck cancer. He is willing to participate in the study and provide information about his lifestyle factors, including his smoking and alcohol history, physical activity level, and dietary habits. He is also comfortable answering questions about his sexual history.

The patient is a 14-year-old male diagnosed with Bipolar I Disorder (manic). He has a history of manic episodes characterized by racing thoughts, impulsivity, and decreased need for sleep. He has been previously treated with risperidone, but it was not effective in controlling his symptoms. He is currently not taking any antipsychotic medications and is willing to discontinue all medications during the study period. His past medical history is significant for asthma and seasonal allergies, which are well-controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and antihistamines. He has no history of substance abuse.

The patient is a 56-year-old Korean woman who has been diagnosed with left breast cancer through a biopsy. She underwent a curative resection and is now postoperative. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work, such as office work or light housework. She has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She is willing to use contraception for 6 months after the completion of the radiation therapy. The patient has never received radiation therapy in the chest or neck area before and does not require supraclavicular radiation therapy. The patient does not have any distant metastases and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her breast size is relatively small.

45 yo F with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, currently being managed with metformin. Most recent HgbA1c level was measured at 9.2% within the last 3 months. Patient reports difficulty controlling blood sugar levels despite adhering to dietary recommendations and medication regimen. No known allergies to psyllium or wheat dextrin. Patient is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effect of psyllium vs. wheat dextrin on glycemic control and inflammatory markers in diabetes mellitus type 2. The patient does not currently use any dietary fiber supplements and is willing to refrain from taking any other fiber-containing supplements during the study period. The patient is able to participate fully in all aspects of the study and has access and ability to utilize text messaging or email.

A 2-month-old infant is diagnosed with cyanotic congenital heart disease and is being treated at UC Davis Children's Hospital. The infant has a history of frequent infections and has been exposed to multiple rounds of antibiotics. The baby has been struggling with feeding and has not yet achieved optimal weight gain. The baby's parents are concerned about their child's immune system and the potential long-term effects of the antibiotics. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer an alternative approach to managing their child's health.

26 year-old woman with no significant past medical history who has never used any gynecological formulations. She is currently not pregnant and not breastfeeding. She has not used any anti-inflammatory or immunosuppression drugs in the past month and has not used any topical medications in the region to be treated. She does not have any active cutaneous or gynecological disease that could interfere with the study results. She has no personal history of allergic disease at the area to be treated and no known allergies or atopic

A 50-year-old female with a history of sarcoidosis diagnosed 5 years ago presents with worsening shortness of breath and non-productive cough. She has been on prednisone for the past 2 years, with fluctuating symptoms. She is a non-smoker and has no history of lung infections or lung surgeries. Her pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with a decreased diffusion capacity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the role of bacterial species in sarcoidosis pathogenesis. She is willing to undergo bronchoscopy and provide blood samples for the study. She has not taken antibiotics in the past 90 days and has no history of HIV, HCV, alcohol, or substance abuse.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman, gravida 2 para 1, presented to the hospital for scheduled cesarean section delivery due to a previous cesarean section. She has a history of gestational diabetes during her first pregnancy, which was well controlled with diet and exercise. She denies any history of liver disease, kidney disease, bleeding tendency, abnormal placentation, or preeclampsia. The patient currently takes prenatal vitamins and has no known allergies. The fetal ultrasound revealed a single fetus in cephalic presentation with normal growth and development. The patient is 39 weeks and 5 days gestation. She is fully informed about the study and has given her consent to participate. She meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and inflammation in her gums for the past 6 months. She has noticed that her teeth have become loose and she has difficulty chewing certain foods. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. She has never had any dental treatments before. The dentist has diagnosed her with aggressive periodontitis based on the presence of deep gum pockets, extensive alveolar bone loss, and visible calculus. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to understand the link between inflammation and bone destruction in aggressive periodontitis. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the AP group and will undergo a biopsy of periodontal granulation tissue during her usual treatment. She has no blood disorders or other medical conditions, and has not taken any medications in the past 6 months. She is not pregnant and is willing to follow the study protocol. She hopes that by participating in this study, she can contribute to the understanding and treatment of aggressive periodontitis.

A 55 year old woman visited the clinic for her annual check-up. She has a history of smoking for the past 15 years and her father died of heart attack. Her blood pressure was high (160/90 mmHg) during the exam and her BMI was 28. She has never been screened for AAA before. She is generally healthy and takes medication for hypertension. She is interested in participating in the Female Aneurysm Screening Study to assess her risk of developing AAA.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA) 8 months ago. He underwent the anterior surgical approach for the procedure. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. He has been experiencing some discomfort during weight-bearing activities and is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the kinematics and sound of his hip joint. He reports no previous hip surgeries or dislocations, and his body weight is 220 lbs. His Harris Hip Score (HHS) is greater than 90 and he is able to actively abduct his operated hip against gravity without difficulty. He is willing to sign the informed consent and HIPAA forms.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis B infection. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. She is currently taking lisinopril and metformin. She denies any recent febrile illness or significant changes in her health. She is able to perform her activities of daily living independently and has no significant limitations in her daily routine. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance medical research and improve treatment options for patients with hepatic impairment.

A 32-year-old woman, G2P1, presented with fear of labor and requested induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation. She had a previous vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia and no complications. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she denied smoking or alcohol use. She had regular prenatal care and all antenatal tests were within normal limits. An ultrasound confirmed a single, vertex presentation with adequate fetal growth. The Bishop score was unfavorable, with a score of 4. After counseling about the risks and benefits of induction, she provided informed consent for the study. Amniotomy was performed for induction, and the patient was monitored closely for progression of labor. The delivery was uneventful, and the neonate had Apgar scores of 9 and 10 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient was discharged home with her newborn after 48 hours. The patient completed the Wijma Delivery Expectancy Questionnaire to evaluate her experience of labor.

A 42-year-old female who was diagnosed with osteosarcoma of the left femur two years ago underwent surgical resection of the tumor, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She lives with her partner and two children. The patient reports experiencing fatigue, muscle loss, and weakness since completing her treatment. She has difficulty with activities of daily living, such as walking upstairs and carrying groceries. She is currently not participating in any exercise program and spends most of her day sitting down due to her job as a desk receptionist. She is a non-smoker and doesn't use any illicit drugs. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. She is able and willing to attend weekly video coaching sessions and independently complete weekly resistance training sessions. She has a laptop with internet access and webcam capability. The patient is able to understand and sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester. She was recently diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus during her routine prenatal screening. She is of Caucasian origin and has no known food allergies or restrictions, except for lactose intolerance. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or psychiatric illness. She takes no medication affecting glucose metabolism or cholesterol medication. She is fluent in Finnish and able to effectively communicate with the study team. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her dietary management of gestational diabetes and potentially improve the health of her baby.

A 50-year-old woman has recently been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. She has not had any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy to the head and neck region. She is in overall good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. Her hemoglobin, granulocyte count, and platelet count are all within normal limits. She has had a dental assessment and necessary prophylactic dental extractions carried out. She is not pregnant or nursing and will use effective contraception during the study. She has no connective tissue diseases or active uncontrolled infections. She has normal sleeping habits and has not had any history of psychiatric or neurological disorders that would preclude study compliance. She is willing to participate in the study and will be randomized to receive radiotherapy either between 8 and 10 AM or between 4 and 6 PM daily, 5 days a week for 5-8 weeks, depending on planned total radiotherapy dose. She will be followed for 3 years after treatment.

65 F with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic back pain for the past 10 years. She has tried multiple non-pharmacological approaches for pain management including physical therapy, acupuncture, and chiropractic care, but has not found any significant relief. She has been taking over-the-counter pain medications such as acetaminophen and ibuprofen, but her pain continues to interfere with her daily activities. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore the use of central analgesic drugs for the treatment of her chronic pain. Her labs reveal normal WBC count and liver function tests, but her creatinine clearance is 28 ml/h. She has provided signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). He has been experiencing frequent and sudden motor tics, such as eye blinking, facial grimacing, and shoulder shrugging. These tics have been causing him embarrassment and difficulty in social situations. He has also been experiencing premonitory urges and a sense of relief after the tics occur. He has no known history of other neurological or psychiatric disorders. He is currently not taking any medication for ADHD or tics. His parents have reported that his symptoms have been worsening during stressful situations, such as starting a new school year or during family vacations. They are concerned about the impact of these symptoms on his daily life and overall well-being.

A 32-year-old woman has given birth to a premature baby girl at 28 weeks of gestation. The baby was admitted to the neonatology unit at Rijnstate Hospital in Arnhem due to respiratory distress syndrome. The baby is currently receiving respiratory support and is being monitored for biochemical abnormalities such as calcium, phosphate, and creatinine levels. The parents are informed about the study and are willing to participate. The mother has no history of any medical conditions or allergies. She is a non-smoker and has not taken any medications during pregnancy. The baby's skin in the genital region is intact and there have been no previous urine tests performed on the baby.

A 57-year-old male patient was referred to the clinic for evaluation of uncontrolled hypertension and weight gain. He reports feeling more fatigued than usual and has noticed a significant increase in his waist circumference over the past few months. He has a history of depression and is currently taking sertraline. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance. He has a family history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. He currently works as an accountant and exercises occasionally. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His past surgical history is significant for a cholecystectomy. His physical examination reveals central obesity, moon facies, and a buffalo hump. His blood pressure is elevated at 160/90 mmHg. His laboratory workup shows elevated urinary free cortisol levels. He has no contraindications for MRI and has no history of hypersensitivity to gadolinium.

55-year-old female diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) 5 years ago with a BMI of 30 kg/m^2. She has been on basal insulin therapy for the past 12 months and was started on bolus insulin therapy (Humalog) 6 months ago with a current dose of 70 U/d. She has a glycosylated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) of 8.5%. She is compliant with her insulin regimen and has no history of recurrent hypoglycemia or hypoglycemic unawareness. She has no known allergies and is currently not taking any drugs or supplements that may interfere with the study results. She has no history of significant gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, neurological, renal, genitourinary, or hematological disease. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She has signed and written Internal Review Board-approved informed consent.

Patient A is a 54-year-old male who was diagnosed with clear cell renal cell carcinoma after presenting with abdominal pain and blood in his urine. He underwent a left nephrectomy and was started on targeted therapy with a VEGFR inhibitor which has resulted in stable disease for the last 5 months. Follow-up imaging revealed two metastatic sites, one in his right lung measuring 1.5 cm and another in his liver measuring 2.5 cm. He has not had any previous radiation therapy. His medical history is significant for hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not use any recreational drugs. He is interested in participating in the study to explore additional treatment options for his metastatic RCC.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with HIV for the past 3 years. She has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years and has had no significant side effects. She has a history of abnormal Pap smears and was diagnosed with CIN2 on her last biopsy. She has no other significant medical history, is not pregnant nor breastfeeding, and has no known allergies to any medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive the quadrivalent HPV vaccine to see if it can help improve her response to LEEP treatment of her cervical HSIL. She understands the study requirements and agrees not to participate in any conception process during the study period. She is willing to undergo colposcopy, directed biopsies, and cervical cytology at various time points throughout the study.

67-year-old male with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma, initially treated with androgen deprivation therapy and antiandrogen withdrawal, but now experiencing disease progression despite treatment. The patient has measurable disease progression and an elevated PSA level. The patient has a CALGB performance status of 1 and serum total testosterone level less than 50ng/mL. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. The patient is not currently taking any medications for his prostate cancer and has not received radiation therapy or chemotherapy for androgen-independent prostate cancer. The patient has normal liver and kidney function and no history of adrenal insufficiency or brain metastases. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for his prostate cancer.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who sustained a mild head injury 6 months ago during a car accident. Since then, she has been experiencing persistent symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. She has sought medical attention but has not found relief from her symptoms. Her anxiety levels have also increased since the accident, worrying about the long-term effects of the head injury on her health and well-being. She has completed high school education and is fluent in English. She is not currently involved in any litigation related to the accident.

A 54-year-old male patient came to the clinic with complaints of frequent headaches, nausea, and blurry vision. He works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has a history of smoking but has quit 2 years ago. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is married and has two children. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He has not had any previous surgeries. His family history is negative for any neurological conditions. He is willing to comply with the protocol and is fit to undergo leukapheresis, chemoradiation, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. He has not received any corticosteroid treatment in the past week. His performance status is good and his life expectancy is estimated to be more than 3 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis two months ago. He was hospitalized for two weeks due to severe symptoms and was treated with antibiotics and pain management. After discharge, he experienced persistent abdominal pain and was referred to a gastroenterologist. Imaging studies revealed the presence of a walled-off pancreatic necrosis (WOPN) with a diameter of 5cm. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The gastroenterologist recommended an endoscopic transmural drainage or necrosectomy (ETD/N) procedure to treat the WOPN. The patient has been offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of the AXIOS™ stent versus the conventional approach using double pigtail plastic stents for the treatment of WOPN. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and meet all inclusion criteria.

50-year-old male with a history of metastatic high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma that is not resectable. The patient has undergone two cycles of chemotherapy prior to enrollment. The patient has adequate tissue available for genomic sequencing and ECOG status less than or equal to 2. The patient has no psychiatric illness or social situations that limit compliance. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. The patient does not have small cell carcinoma and does not have an actionable mutation for which guidelines recommend up-front therapy with targeted agents. The patient

A 45-year-old male presents with a 2-year history of progressive muscle weakness, difficulty in speaking and swallowing, and muscle wasting. He was recently diagnosed with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and has been under the care of a neurologist. The patient reports frequent fasciculations in the tongue and appendicular muscles, which cause discomfort and interfere with daily activities. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history or allergies. He is currently taking Riluzole to manage his symptoms. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study. The patient has no history of participating in any clinical study within the last 30 days and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who had a myocardial infarction six months ago and underwent primary coronary angioplasty. He has been diagnosed with periodontitis according to Page's criteria, with a loss of CAL ≥4mm on at least 2 tooth surfaces in the interdental spaces and PD ≥4mm on at least 2 tooth surfaces in the interdental spaces. He experiences bleeding on probing and has signed informed consent for participation in the study. The patient has no history of acute inflammation of the airways or urinary tract, neoplasms, rheumatic or autoimmune diseases, chronic liver disease or chronic kidney failure, stroke or TIA. He has not received antibiotic therapy in the last 12 months or periodontal treatment in the last 6 months. The patient has not participated in any other studies.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 33. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. She has been diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and has elevated levels of liver enzymes. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She exercises for 30 minutes, four times a week. She is scheduled for bariatric surgery due to her obesity. She has the I148I variant for the PNPLA3 SNP rs738409.

A 28-year-old male university student with no history of lower extremity injury or surgery, vestibular or visual conditions, systemic illness, or any other malignancy affecting the lower extremities. He is physically active and participates in intramural sports. He has no known medical conditions and does not take any prescription or herbal muscle stimulants, relaxants, or other medications that could affect balance. He is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo instrument-applied chiropractic manipulative therapy (CMT) to determine its effects on postural control.

This is a 12-year-old girl and her parent who are being invited to participate in a clinical trial aimed at increasing the likelihood of adolescents receiving the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine series. The trial will test the effectiveness of a comprehensive vaccine promotion toolkit that will be implemented in the pediatric healthcare setting. The trial will be conducted through a cluster-randomized trial design, with participating pediatric practices randomized to either the intervention arm or the control arm. If the girl and her parent choose to participate, they will be asked to complete a brief questionnaire at the initial visit, assessing their knowledge, attitudes, and beliefs about adolescent health and protection against infectious diseases. Three months later, they will be contacted again to complete a short follow-up interview on the general health of the girl, her immunization status, and attitudes regarding vaccination. To be eligible for the trial, the girl must be aged 11-12 years and must not have received any previous HPV vaccine doses. It is noted that participants must be English speaking.

A 45-year-old male presents for a routine physical exam. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. He reports no symptoms related to kidney function, such as decreased urine output or swelling in the legs. His family history is negative for kidney disease. His last serum creatinine measurement was within the normal range. He has no known allergies to medications or medical devices. He is interested in participating in clinical research to advance medical knowledge and improve patient care. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study measuring GFR by nasal sensors.

Pt is a 56yo M with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia scheduled to undergo an elective unilateral open inguinal herniorrhaphy with mesh under deep sedation. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status of II. He does not have any pre-existing concurrent acute or chronic painful physical/restrictive condition expected to require analgesic treatment in the postoperative period for pain. The patient is not using opioids for the past 6 months and has not taken any opioids within 24 hours prior to the scheduled surgery. The patient does not have any medical condition that would pose a health risk to the subject or confound the postoperative assessments. The patient has no uncontrolled anxiety, psychiatric or neurological disorder. There is no known or suspected history of drug abuse, positive drug screen on the day of surgery, consumption of 3 or more alcoholic drinks every day, or a recent history of alcohol abuse.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was admitted to the hospital with sepsis. The patient was subsequently transferred to the FMC ICU and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. The patient has been in the ICU for 48 hours and has been responsive to treatment thus far. The patient is able to communicate and has a Richmond Agitation and Sedation Scale Score of -1. The Glasgow Coma Scale Score is 14. The patient is a native English speaker with no hearing impairments. The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is 5, indicating sepsis. The patient has no history of neurological injury or neurodegenerative conditions. The patient is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of outdoor work and sun exposure. He has noticed several rough, scaly patches of skin on his face and scalp, which have been slowly increasing in size and number over the past year. He has been previously diagnosed with mild to moderate actinic keratosis by his dermatologist. The patient is willing and able to do daily applications of topical treatment on his own or has someone available to assist him. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a 5% potassium hydroxide solution versus placebo and a 3% diclofenac gel for the treatment of actinic keratosis. The patient is not currently taking any systemic medications and has no known allergies to any of the ingredients of the investigational products. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 26-year-old woman has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles and weight gain over the past year. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has not been on any oral contraceptives or fertility medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She was referred to a gynecologist where she was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about the impact of lifestyle factors on PCOS. She has completed a pelvic exam within the past year and is willing to undergo an ultrasound scan of her ovaries. She is willing to complete a food frequency questionnaire, a sleep questionnaire, and a physical activity questionnaire. Additionally, she is willing to wear a waist-worn accelerometer to monitor physical activity and a wrist-worn accelerometer to monitor sleep for a week. She is interested in learning about the potential psychosocial factors associated with PCOS and is willing to complete a questionnaire to assess health beliefs. She is not currently taking any medication that may influence reproductive function.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was involved in a car accident resulting in a pelvic fracture and a right leg fracture. He is currently at a level-1 trauma center and has undergone surgery for his fractures. The patient has no history of clots or bleeding disorders. He is not currently taking any medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. The patient speaks English fluently and does not have any cognitive impairment. He is expected to be discharged from the hospital in the next few days and will be followed up for a 3-month period for any VTE events or bleeding complications.

This is a 45-year-old female with a history of knee pain and stiffness. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 years and has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee joint. She has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and oral medications, but has not experienced significant relief. She has been advised to undergo arthroscopic cartilage regeneration facilitating procedure (ACRFP) to treat her condition. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is able to walk without any difficulty. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and agrees to release her medical records for regulatory and research purposes.

As a part of this clinical trial, we are looking for patients who are between the ages of 18 and 70 and have been diagnosed with abnormal renal pathology or have a glomerular filtration rate between 15 and 90 ml/min.1.73 m2, or proteinuria greater than 1 g/24 hours due to any cause. We are also looking for kidney transplant recipients who received their transplant from May 2019 to November 2019. Patients should be able to cooperate with breath-holding and breath-exhaling movements and communicate without any obstacles. Patients with pregnancy or cancer, other serious diseases, or those who are unable to lie down for at least 10 minutes, unconscious, have severe hypoxia, or are in need of rescue are not eligible for the study. Additionally, patients with absolute contraindications of renal puncture, such as obvious bleeding tendency, severe hypertension, psychiatric patients, or non-cooperating operators and isolated kidney, and those with relative contraindications of renal puncture, such as active pyelonephritis, renal tuberculosis, hydronephrosis, or pyonephrosis, renal abscess or perirenal abscess, renal tumors or renal aneurysms, polycystic kidney or renal cyst, kidney position too high, or obesity with severe ascites, are not eligible for the study. If you meet the eligibility criteria, we invite you to participate in this clinical trial to help us establish Ultrasound Integrated Precision Diagnosis Technology with elastography as the core technology to evaluate renal injury and repair comprehensively and accurately.

Sophia is a 3-year-old girl who has been experiencing pain and difficulty walking due to a hip disorder. She has been scheduled for surgical treatment under general anesthesia at Tanta University Hospitals. She is generally healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. Her parents have been fully informed about the procedure and have given their written consent for her participation in this clinical trial. Sophia will be randomized to either receive a real or sham ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block before the onset of the surgery. During the surgery, she will be under general anesthesia and her vital signs will be monitored closely. After the surgery, her postoperative pain score and total morphine consumption in the first postoperative day will be monitored, as well as the time to first request for rescue analgesia. Her parents will be kept fully informed throughout the study and will be able to withdraw her participation at any time.

55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of unresectable pancreatic cancer. The patient has not undergone any prior treatment for the cancer and is currently experiencing moderate to severe pain in the abdomen. The patient has a history of smoking and alcohol use, but has quit both since the diagnosis. The patient has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is willing and able to undergo endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine needle injection of talimogene laherparepvec, and is able to comply with all study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 6-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma. She has undergone chemotherapy, surgery and radiation therapy. Unfortunately, her cancer has not responded well to the treatment and the doctors have recommended enrolling her in a clinical trial. She meets the eligibility criteria for this trial as her tumor has tested positive for GD2. Her parents are willing to participate in the trial and have signed the informed consent form. The girl is in good general health with no significant underlying medical conditions. Her blood counts are within normal limits, and she has not received any chemotherapy or immunotherapy for the past three weeks. Her parents are aware of the investigational nature of this program and are willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who was referred to the ophthalmology clinic due to concerns of poor vision in his left eye. He has no significant medical history and is up-to-date with his routine vaccinations. His parents report that he has been bumping into objects on his left side and squinting his left eye. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist noted a reduced red reflex in the left eye and referred the patient for further testing. The patient will undergo the Red Reflex Test, with and without dilation, as part of a clinical trial investigating the accuracy of this test for early detection of ocular abnormalities in children. Consent will be obtained from the patient's parents and the patient will be de-identified for the purposes of the study. The ophthalmologist performing the test will be blinded to the patient's medical history and will use a standardized survey tool to record the presence or absence of any abnormality in the anterior or posterior segments of the eye. The results of the study will help to determine the sensitivity and specificity of the Red Reflex Test for detecting ocular pathology in the pediatric population.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic pain for the past 5 years due to a work-related injury. The patient has tried various pain management techniques but none have provided long-term relief. The patient has been evaluated and deemed an appropriate candidate for implantation of an intrathecal drug infusion system, specifically the SynchroMed II system. The patient is willing to return to the study center for follow-up visits and is geographically stable. The patient understands the study protocol and has signed an informed consent form prior to any study-related procedures. The patient's estimated life expectancy is greater than twelve months.

25 year old pregnant Marshallese Pacific Islander woman, currently in her first trimester of pregnancy. She has a history of two previous pregnancies, both resulting in preterm births. She is interested in participating in a group prenatal program that is culturally sensitive and tailored to her needs as a Marshallese woman. She is fluent in Marshallese and English and is willing to attend group sessions with other Marshallese women. She is open to learning about new ways to improve her health and the health of her baby.

60 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty walking. He reports a family history of mitochondrial disease in his sister and cousin. He has undergone previous genetic testing that did not identify any deletions or mutations in the 3243, 8344, or 8993 genes associated with mitochondrial disease. He has health insurance and is willing to provide consent for the study.

A 28-year-old female patient with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presented with proteinuria and hematuria. She has been experiencing joint pain, fatigue, and fever for the past few months. She was diagnosed with SLE 2 years ago and was initially treated with hydroxychloroquine and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). However, her symptoms persisted and she was started on a low dose of prednisone. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and recurrent urinary tract infections. Her vital signs were stable in the primary evaluation. Physical examination revealed a butterfly rash on her face and tenderness in her joints. Laboratory tests showed elevated levels of anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, low complement levels, and a urine protein to creatinine ratio greater than 2. A kidney biopsy was performed and revealed ISN Class IV lupus nephritis. The patient was referred to the clinical trial and provided written informed consent. She has no history of previous allergic reactions and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have severe renal impairment and is not currently taking any investigational agents. She is willing to comply with the schedule of protocol requirements.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of colorectal cancer (CRC) who was diagnosed with liver metastases six months ago. He has received multiple lines of chemotherapy but his disease has progressed despite treatment. A recent CT scan shows a 3cm tumor in the right lobe of the liver that is deemed unresectable. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. His hematology and biochemistry results are within normal limits. He has not received any chemotherapy in the last 4 weeks due to intolerance. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders or chronic use of immunodepressants. He has not received any prior gene therapy or participated in any other research protocol involving an IMP within the last 2 months.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of a urinary tract infection for the past few days. She has been prescribed a 7-day course of Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid 875mg BID. She is generally healthy, with a body mass index of 22.5 kg/m2. She has no history of chronic gastrointestinal disorders or other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the trial. She does not have a habit of using pro- or prebiotic products, nor does she have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has given voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study and agrees to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has never received treatment for his chronic hepatitis C. He was diagnosed with the disease 2 years ago after experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. His liver function tests are abnormal, and his hepatitis C viral load is greater than 5 million copies per milliliter. The patient has no history of severe neuropsychiatric disorders, metabolic or hematological disorders, pulmonary or ischemic heart disease, gastrointestinal, neurological, renal, urological, endocrine, or opthalmologic disorders including severe retinopathy, or immune mediated disease. The patient is not pregnant or breast-feeding.

The patient is a 30-year-old man with a history of mild psoriasis on his arms and legs. He has been using Diprosone ointment for the past year, and it has been effective in treating his psoriasis. He has not experienced any adverse reactions to the medication. He does not have any other skin conditions or abnormalities. He is not currently using any other topical medications on his skin. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and he drinks alcohol socially. He is not currently taking any prescription medications. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

A premature baby, born at 31 weeks postmenstrual age, weighing 1.8 kg, is admitted to a National Health Service (NHS) neonatal unit in England. The baby is having difficulty tolerating adequate volumes of milk feeds shortly after birth, and so is given supplemental parenteral nutrition (PN). The doctors are considering whether to continue PN during the first week after birth, as it carries well-established risks, of which the most serious and the most common is sepsis. The doctors are unsure whether continuing PN will improve the baby's survival to discharge from the neonatal unit or affect other important outcomes in the neonatal core outcomes set. The doctors are considering enrolling the baby in a clinical trial to determine whether providing PN in the first week after birth, compared to not providing PN, improves survival to discharge from the neonatal unit in babies born between 30 and 33 weeks postmenstrual age. The baby will be monitored closely for any adverse effects during the trial.

This clinical trial is seeking male soccer players, aged between 22 and 24 years, who are at least 1.80m tall and weigh no more than 72kg. Participants must be training for an average of 2 hours daily, 4-6 days per week, and have at least 8 years of training experience. Participants with heart failure or any lower-limb injuries will be excluded from the study. Additionally, those who have taken antioxidant supplements within the last 3 months prior to the study will also be excluded.

This is a 55 year-old female with a family history of colon cancer. She has previously undergone an optical colonoscopy and was found to have multiple polyps. She is scheduled for a follow-up colonoscopy but is hesitant due to the discomfort and preparation involved. She has been experiencing occasional abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits. She has been referred to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Check-Cap's C-Scan System in providing structural information on colonic polypoid lesions and masses. The subject has provided signed informed consent and is willing to ingest the C-Scan Capsule with some water and contrast media. She is willing to be monitored several times daily by the site clinical study team (or by dedicated external trained medical personnel) to assure her well-being and to monitor for any change or discomfort and for procedure progress. She is willing to ingest daily doses of contrast media and laxadine as recommended by the doctor. She is willing to retrieve the capsule upon excretion and has been provided with a dedicated capsule collection kit.

A 5-year-old male patient with a history of congenital clubfoot and scheduled for corrective surgery is being evaluated for a prospective clinical trial. Medical history reveals no significant past surgeries or anesthesia complications. The patient has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medications. The patient's physical examination was unremarkable and he is classified as ASA physical status class I. Hemoglobin percentage, blood sugar, and coagulation profile have been evaluated preoperatively and are within normal limits. The patient will receive sedation via midazolam (0.2 mg/kg IM) upon arrival to the operating room. Inhalational induction of anesthesia will be achieved by 8% sevoflurane in 100% oxygen, and an appropriate-sized cannula will be inserted. Endotracheal intubation will be performed after which sevoflurane concentration will be reduced to 3%. After hemodynamic stabilization, caudal block will be performed using a beveled needle 18-23 G in the lateral decubitus position by using the loss of resistance technique. The patient will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group D (n=12): Dexmetedomidine group. 0.5 ml of dexmetedomidine (2 μg/kg) added to bupivacaine, Group M (n=12) : Magnesium group.0.5 ml of magnesium sulphate (50 mg) added to bupivacaine, Group C (n=12) :Control group.bupivacaine 0.25% diluted in normal saline with total volume of 1 ml/kg. The patient's hemodynamics will be monitored throughout the surgery, and FLACC score will be assessed at the end of surgery and 12 hours postoperatively to evaluate pain intensity. The patient will be monitored for complications secondary to test drugs or caudal block, and total doses of rescue drugs will be calculated for each group.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with HIV at the Kibera Community Health Centre in Nairobi, Kenya. She has no prior history of HIV treatment and is not yet eligible for antiretroviral therapy (ART). She has access to a cell phone and is able to operate it using simple text-messaging. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She is interested in improving her retention in care and is open to receiving weekly SMS 'check-ins' as part of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with chronic liver disease due to alcoholic cirrhosis. He has been on the waiting list for a liver transplant for several months and has agreed to participate in a research study evaluating the nutritional, functional, and metabolic outcomes of patients undergoing liver transplantation. He has a history of ascites and hepatic encephalopathy, which have been managed with medications including diuretics and lactulose. He has experienced weight loss and decreased appetite in recent months, and his current body mass index is 22.5. His handgrip strength and 6-minute walk test results indicate decreased functional capacity. He is currently on a restricted sodium and protein diet, and his energy balance is negative. He will be evaluated at four time points: before transplantation, and on the 1st to 3rd postoperative day, 5 to 7 days post-transplant, and at discharge from the hospital. After transplantation, he will be monitored for metabolic complications such as hyperkalemia, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus, and the doses of immunosuppressive drugs will be adjusted as necessary. The study aims to evaluate the impact of nutritional status and metabolic disorders on post-transplant outcomes.

A 10-year-old boy is referred for evaluation of developmental delay, coarse facial features, and recurrent ear infections. He is also noted to have short stature and joint stiffness. Family history is negative for similar symptoms. Physical examination reveals some facial dysmorphism, including a prominent forehead, a depressed nasal bridge, and a thickened upper lip. He has limited range of motion in his hips and shoulders. His weight is 30 kg and his height is 120 cm. Laboratory evaluation reveals a leukocyte α-L-iduronidase enzyme activity level of 5% of the lower limit of the normal range of the measuring laboratory, confirming a diagnosis of MPS I. Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) values are within normal ranges. The patient has not previously received Aldurazyme® (laronidase) and is willing to participate in the study. Written informed consent will be obtained from both the patient and the authorized guardian(s) as the patient is under 18 years old.
