The patient is a 40 year old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. She has been taking olanzapine (Zyprexa®) for the past 3 months to manage her psychiatric symptoms. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has been experiencing weight gain since starting the medication. She has no personal or family history of diabetes, but she is concerned about the potential side effects of olanzapine. She has been compliant with her medication regimen and has not experienced any suicidal impulses or intent. She has not had any alcohol or substance abuse for the past 6 months. She has no major medical problems that would interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the potential risks of olanzapine and how it may affect her insulin secretion.

Patient is a 52-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with noninvasive breast cancer. She has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer and is not currently taking any medications for chronic conditions. She has no history of asthma, allergies, or gastrointestinal ulcers. The patient is scheduled for reexcision within 10 days to 6 weeks from the start of the study. She has not taken any celecoxib or rofecoxib within the past month and is not currently taking any anticoagulants or aromatase inhibitors. The patient has no known significant bleeding disorder and is willing to discontinue low dose ASA (160 mg daily) during the study. She has provided informed consent and has enough tissue available for the required research assessments.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). He has previously received treatment for the disease but is now considered to have fludarabine-refractory disease and requires further treatment. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no severe organ dysfunction. The patient has not had any other concomitant or previous neoplasms and does not have autoimmune hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia. He has received up to 5 prior chemotherapy regimens for the treatment of his CLL. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 6 months and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help him overcome his fludarabine-refractory CLL.

32 F, sedentary office worker who spends most of her day sitting. She reports feeling tired and lacking energy on a daily basis. She has a BMI of 28 and has not exercised regularly in the past 6 months. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is interested in increasing her physical activity levels but is unsure of what exercise program would be best for her. She has no history of participation in previous studies from this lab.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and an angiographically intermediate lesion (40-70% diameter stenosis) in a major epicardial coronary artery. He is 175 cm tall and his weight is 86 kg. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of previous myocardial infarction. He complains of shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion. His echocardiogram showed an LVEF of 35%. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 65 bpm. His labs: FBS: 130 mg/dl, HbA1c: 6.5%, TG: 150 mg/dl, Cholesterol: 180 mg/dl, LDL: 110 mg/dl, HDL: 40 mg/dl. He is compliant with his medications and has been advised to make lifestyle changes to improve his condition. He is willing to participate in the study and has no contraindications to adenosine.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing urinary urgency, frequency, and pelvic pain for the past year. She has been previously diagnosed with interstitial cystitis (IC) through cystoscopy and hydrodistension. Despite treatment with oral medications and bladder instillations, she still experiences pain. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help identify potential markers for pain associated with IC. She is able to provide written informed consent and is not currently pregnant.

A 64-year-old male with a history of colon cancer is scheduled to undergo surgery for a resection of a gastrointestinal tumor. He is otherwise healthy with no history of any other major illnesses or surgeries. He is married, retired and spends most of his time gardening and walking his dog. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His performance status is 1. He is able to walk up to one mile without any difficulty. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease. He has no physical limitations and is able to perform a CPET on a cycle ergometer. He is willing to provide consent and participate in the study.

25-year-old female, English-speaking, presenting with bilateral pain in the back of her mouth with difficulty in opening her mouth for two weeks. An oral examination revealed the need for surgical extraction of all four partially impacted third molars. She has no known drug allergies and no history of substance abuse. She has not taken melatonin or any other over-the-counter pain medication in the last month. She is in good overall health, with a BMI of 23. She has no history of chronic pain or psychiatric disease. She has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorder and reports having a good sleep pattern. She understands and speaks English fluently and has no communication barriers. She has never undergone any surgery under local anesthesia. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 27-year-old Chinese male with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m² and a weight of 70 kg is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the evaluation of the safety and pharmacokinetic profiles of HHT201. He has no significant medical history and has never participated in any other investigational drug trial. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not currently taking any prescription medications. He has normal blood pressure and resting pulse rate. His liver and kidney function tests are within the normal range, and he has no detectable protein in his urine. He has no clinically significant ECG abnormalities and has tested negative for HIV, HBsAg, and hepatitis C antibody. He is willing to comply with the food and beverage restrictions and is able to provide written informed consent forms.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or malignancies and has never had severe hypersensitivity reactions or anaphylaxis. He has not received immunosuppressive therapy and has not been infected with HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C. He is not currently pregnant or lactating and is not considered a vulnerable subject. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is within the age range of 18 to 65 years old. The patient is interested in participating in a Phase 1 clinical trial to assess the safety, immunogenicity, and dose response of IC47. The patient is willing to receive three doses of either 30 or 150 μg of IC47 in intervals of 42 days each. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 45-year-old Caucasian female presents to the dermatology clinic with concerns about the appearance of her décolletage region. She has a history of sun exposure and has noticed fine lines, wrinkles, and dryness in this area. She is a non-smoker and has no previous history of skin cancer. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an oral contraceptive for birth control. She has no known allergies to hyaluronic acid or local anesthetics. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effectiveness and tolerability of Restylane® Skinboosters™ Vital for rejuvenation of the décolletage region. She is willing to comply with follow-up and abstain from other treatments in the region during the study period. She has no history of bleeding disorders or treatment with thrombolytics, anticoagulants, or inhibitors of platelet aggregation, and is not using immunosuppressants. She is willing to provide signed and dated informed consent to participate in the study and allow unrestricted use of décolletage images for marketing purposes.

Pt is a 45yo M with ESRD on hemodialysis for the past 2 years with no known complications. The patient has been on bicarbonate hemodialysis for the past 6 months and has not experienced any complications during previous HD sessions. The patient is compliant with their prescribed medication regimen and follows a renal diet. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of different dialysate calcium concentrations on mineral metabolism and hemodynamic stability in standard hemodialysis.

The patient is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma (PTMC) measuring 0.7cm in diameter. Her past medical history is non-significant. She has no family history of thyroid cancer. The patient has undergone fine needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) and a complete radiologic and histologic examination. The biopsy result confirmed PTMC. She has been offered two treatment options: total thyroidectomy (TT: total or near-total thyroidectomy) or less than total thyroidectomy (LT: lobectomy or subtotal thyroidectomy). The patient is concerned about the potential long-term outcomes of both treatment options and wants to make an informed decision. Her surgeon has explained the details of the clinical trial and the potential benefits and risks of each option. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old Caucasian man who has been experiencing abdominal pain and blood in his stool. He has a history of smoking and has smoked a pack a day for the past 30 years. He has also been diagnosed with high blood pressure but is on medication to control it. He has no other significant medical history. His family history is negative for any cancer. He underwent a colonoscopy which revealed a tumor in his right colon. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. CT scan showed the tumor was confined to the colon and there was no evidence of distant metastasis. He is scheduled for surgery and his doctor has recommended him for this clinical trial investigating the radical extent of lymphadenectomy. He has agreed to participate and has signed the informed consent form.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver and unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has undergone transarterial chemoembolization and radiofrequency ablation, and has achieved a complete response. He has a Child-Pugh score of 8 and has been diagnosed with portal hypertension, with a hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) of >5 mmHg. He has not had any more than two ablative procedures prior to enrollment. He has been screened for varices and is on a stable dose of non-selective beta-blockers. He has no history of heart disease or arrhythmias. He is not allergic to sorafenib or any of its components. He has not received any other anti-cancer drugs or investigational agents in the past 30 days. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for at least three months after the last administration of sorafenib. He has signed informed consent.

30F recently diagnosed with CIN III was referred for treatment. She underwent LEEP procedure and the histopathology report confirmed the diagnosis of CIN III. The patient was informed about the follow-up procedures and was asked if she would like to participate in a clinical trial comparing HPV testing to routine colposcopy to identify persistent cervical precancers. The patient expressed her interest in participating in the trial and was given information about the study procedures, available alternatives, and the risks related to the study. She understood the study procedures and accepted voluntarily to participate by signing the informed consent form. The patient is a non-smoker, has no history of cervical cancer or immunodeficiency, and is fluent in English. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and available for follow-up appointments.

This is a 58 year old male with a past medical history of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation. The patient has undergone standard of care front-line therapy but has progressed and exhausted available options with targeted therapy. The patient has refused all other currently available therapeutic options and is allowed to enroll in this study. The patient is expected to have a histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Additionally, the patient must have an ECOG performance status grade of 0 or 1 and meet the study protocol defined laboratory criteria without having a history of red blood cell transfusion, platelet transfusion, or granulocyte-colony stimulating factor support within 7 days prior to the date of the test. Any toxicities from prior anticancer therapy must have resolved to common terminology criteria for adverse events (CTCAE) version 5.0 Grade 1 or baseline level (except for alopecia [any grade], Grade <=2 peripheral neuropathy, and Grade <=2 hypothyroidism stable on hormone replacement therapy). The patient must not have any uncontrolled illness or untreated brain or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases whether symptomatic or asymptomatic. The patient must not have any allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to Lazertinib or their excipients. The patient must be willing to agree not to donate eggs for the purposes of assisted reproduction during the study and for 6 months after receiving the last dose of study intervention.

A 55-year old non-smoker female was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer after experiencing shortness of breath and cough for several weeks. She works as a teacher and lives with her husband and two children. She has no significant past medical history. Her PET-CT scan showed a 2.5 cm mass in the middle lobe of her right lung with no evidence of regional or distant metastases. A biopsy confirmed that the tumor is positive for activating EGFR mutation. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 0. Her cardiac function is normal. Her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She has no active infections. She is not taking any medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She understands the potential benefits and risks of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) for 3 years. She has been taking etanercept 50 mg weekly as a standard dose for the past year and has shown some improvement in her symptoms. She reports experiencing stiffness and pain in her lower back and hips, especially in the morning and after periods of inactivity. She also experiences fatigue and difficulty sleeping due to her AS. She has tried non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and glucocorticoids in the past, but they did not provide significant relief. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no allergies or intolerances to any medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent.

A 50-year-old man with a history of high cholesterol levels visited his primary care physician for a routine checkup. He has a family history of heart disease, and he is concerned about his own cardiovascular health. He has been trying to manage his cholesterol levels by following a healthy diet and exercising regularly, but his recent lipid panel showed a high LDL-C level of 160 mg/dL. He is a non-smoker and has never used oral hypolipidemic therapy. His BMI is 25.5 kg/m2, and his triglyceride levels are within the normal range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of plant sterol-fortified dairy products in reducing cholesterol levels.

45-year-old male with a history of obesity, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with elevated liver enzymes during a routine check-up. Further evaluation reveals a diagnosis of Nonalcoholic SteatoHepatitis (NASH) based on liver biopsy and a NAFLD Activity Score (NAS) of ≥3. MRI determined liver fat fraction is equal to or higher than 7 percent. The patient has been taking metformin for diabetes for the last 4 years and is otherwise stable. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of roflumilast and pioglitazone on transaminase levels and liver fat content in patients with NASH. The patient is aware of the study requirements, including the need for contraception if sexually active and the requirement to maintain a stable dose of Vitamin E and/or pentoxifylline throughout the study. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent form and agrees to comply with the protocol requirements.

A 42-year-old female-to-male transgender patient visited Fenway Community Health for a routine check-up. The patient has not had a Pap smear in the past 4 years since moving to the area and has a history of irregular Pap smear results in the past. The patient is HIV-negative and has a family history of cervical cancer. The patient is a smoker and has a history of heavy alcohol use. The patient identifies as queer and is currently in a monogamous relationship with a cisgender female partner. The patient has a history of depression and is currently taking an antidepressant medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help improve cervical cancer screening rates among underscreened patients like themselves.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was involved in a car accident and suffered multiple injuries, including a traumatic brain injury. She was admitted to the ICU and has been sedated and intubated since then. Her husband has been present at her bedside every day and has been very anxious about her condition. He has expressed interest in participating in her care and has consented to participate in this clinical trial. He speaks and writes French fluently and is available to be present at the patient's bedside at least twice a week. The patient's ICU stay is expected to be longer than a week.

Patient is a healthy male between the ages of 18-35 with no significant medical history, no known allergies to local anesthetics, and not currently taking any medication for pain control or cognition. The patient must be fluent in English or Spanish, able to provide informed consent, and able and willing to attend 5-10 study visits. The patient must be able to come to Boston Children's Hospital for a 24-hour stay. The patient cannot have any acute or chronic pain conditions requiring ongoing treatment or limiting daily activities, alcohol or illicit drug abuse, or be a current smoker. The patient must be willing to undergo subcutaneous injection with a novel prolonged-duration local anesthetic, NeoSTX, and be able to self-report any symptoms experienced during the study. The study will evaluate the systemic and local safety of escalating doses of NeoSTX via sub-cutaneous infiltration in healthy, awake young adult male human volunteer subjects.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of a respiratory infection for the past week. He reports feeling fatigued, having a persistent cough, and experiencing shortness of breath. He has no history of chronic respiratory conditions or immune system disorders. He has not undergone any recent antibiotic treatment. He is currently experiencing a fever of 101°F and reports a loss of appetite. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the efficacy of the antibody diagnostic test kit for the detection of acute phase disease against bacterial and viral infections.

A 68-year-old male presents to the urology clinic with a recent diagnosis of prostate cancer. His PSA level was found to be slightly elevated during a routine check-up and he underwent a biopsy which revealed a low-grade (Gleason 6) tumor involving a single core. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or family history of prostate cancer. Physical examination reveals a normal prostate gland on digital rectal exam. The patient is interested in avoiding the morbidity associated with active treatment and is willing to consider active surveillance as a management option. He is a resident of Israel and is willing to adhere to the follow-up schedule.

A 40-year-old male office worker has been experiencing shoulder pain for several months, which has recently become severe enough to warrant surgical intervention. He has no known allergies and has not taken any antibiotics or used any antibiotic creams or gels in the past three months. He has not had any previous shoulder surgery or radiotherapy. He does not have any active infections and has normal skin in the shoulder area. He is in good health and has no liver or kidney issues. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of different prophylactic antibiotics for skin colonization with P. acnes in primary open shoulder surgery.

A 35-year-old female patient with a history of non-infectious uveitis affecting the posterior segment of her left eye for the past 2 years is seeking treatment at the clinic. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of blurred vision and eye pain, which have been affecting her daily activities. Her last eye exam showed decreased visual acuity in the left eye, and her ophthalmologist suggested that she might benefit from a fluocinolone acetonide intravitreal implant. She is currently not pregnant and has no other medical conditions that may interfere with the study. She is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the implant and improve her quality of life.

6-year-old male diagnosed with autism and meeting the cut off on Autism Diagnostic Inventory-Revised (ADI-R) and the Autism Diagnostic Observation Scale (ADOS). The patient has an IQ of 75 and has been receiving behavioral and psychotropic drug treatment for the past year. The patient's parents are willing to administer subcutaneous methyl B12 injections every three days for the duration of the 12-week study period. There is no clinical evidence of a seizure disorder or cancer, and the patient has not undergone recent surgery or has an active infection with fever. There is no known genetic cause of autism in the patient, and there is no evidence of malnutrition.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of joint pain and stiffness, which have been worsening over the past few months. He has been previously diagnosed with psoriasis and has noticed that his skin condition has been worsening as well. He is currently taking methotrexate for his psoriasis, but his joint symptoms have not improved. He is otherwise healthy, does not smoke, and has no known allergies. He is willing to use acceptable forms of contraception.

A 35-year-old African American male who is a current participant in the U.S. Military HIV Natural History Study presented for his routine follow-up. He was diagnosed with HIV infection five years ago and has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) since then. He is currently asymptomatic and reports good adherence to his medication regimen. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past six months. He denies any history of drug abuse or smoking. He has no current suicidal ideation and is willing to participate in the full neuropsychological battery and questionnaires required for the study. He has no acute medical conditions that may impact his ability to complete the tests. His last ELISA test for HIV was negative, which makes him eligible for the HIV-negative group if he agrees to undergo another HIV test for study enrollment.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old male who has not taken any prescription medications in the past 28 days. He has no history of immunodeficiency or substance abuse. He has not donated blood in the past 6 months and has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products in the past 60 days. He has no history of infection with hepatitis A, B, or C virus or HIV-1. He has not received any investigational drug therapy in the past 60 days. His CBC, electrolyte levels, liver and kidney function, and other laboratory values are within normal limits. He has no significant abnormalities on his 12-lead electrocardiogram. He has not undergone any elective surgery or has any planned during the study period. He is not pregnant or nursing. He is sexually active but has agreed to use an effective method of birth control during the study period. He is willing to forego other forms of experimental treatment during the study period. He has provided written informed consent and is able to complete the follow-up period of 84 days.

A 54-year-old male was admitted to the hospital with a complaint of acute respiratory distress. He is a smoker for the past 20 years and has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He also has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He has no known allergies. His family history is significant for lung cancer in his father. He has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. He denies any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. He is currently on oxygen support and has been experiencing cough and shortness of breath. He is able to speak in full sentences but with some effort. He is afebrile with normal vital signs. His chest X-ray shows signs of consolidation. He is being considered for a MnDCT scan to further evaluate his respiratory distress.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease. He has been receiving treatment for his hypertension for the past year, and his blood pressure has been well-controlled. His most recent serum creatinine concentration was 1.8 mg/dL and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated to be 35 mL/min using the CKD-EPI website. He has not been on any other medication for the past 2 months. The patient has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 75 kg. He is currently not experiencing any symptoms related to his renal impairment. The patient has not taken any creatine supplements, and he does not have any non-standard muscle mass. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of renal impairment on JNJ-56136379.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with moderate-to-advanced chronic periodontitis during her regular dental checkup. She has a history of good oral hygiene practices, but she noticed bleeding gums while brushing her teeth. On examination, her periodontal probing depth was ≥5 mm, and clinical attachment level was ≥4 mm with radiographic signs of alveolar bone loss. The patient reported occasional episodes of mild pain while chewing hard foods. She has no systemic diseases that could influence the outcome of therapy, and she is a non-smoker. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves nonsurgical treatment of chronic periodontitis.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with acromegaly, a hormonal disorder caused by an excess of growth hormone. He presents with symptoms of enlarged hands and feet, facial features, and deepening voice. The patient is on somatostatin analogs for treatment and has a confirmed diagnosis of acromegaly based on oral glucose tolerance test or GH day curve and diagnostic insulin growth factor 1 levels with radiological evidence of a pituitary adenoma. He has not undergone or planned pregnancy and has no known allergies to Lignocaine. The patient has not taken any medication other than the standard treatment for acromegaly and has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo the ULTRADIAN dynamic diagnostics system.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He reports occasional numbness and tingling in his feet, which he attributes to his diabetes. He denies any history of peripheral arterial disease, peripheral neuropathy, or previous lower limb surgeries. The patient is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin for the management of his diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, respectively. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was 7.2%. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to validate the use of Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in measuring the blood supply to the muscles of the leg, and how this changes with exercise and vascular pathology.

14-year-old female diagnosed with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) with a Cobb angle of 45o. She has been experiencing back pain and has noticed a visible curvature of her spine. She is referred to corrective surgery as her condition is severe. She has no known family history of scoliosis. Past Medical History: She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She reports no history of fractures or bone-related problems. She is physically active and enjoys playing basketball and running. She does not follow a specific dietary plan and is not taking any vitamin supplements. She has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Family History: Her parents have no significant medical history, and her siblings are healthy. She has no family history of scoliosis.

A 8-year-old Japanese boy who is in good health and has no known allergies, presents for a clinical trial to test a novel swine influenza virus vaccine. He has not received any adjuvanted influenza vaccine or suspected influenza disease within the past three months, and has not received any other vaccines within the past four weeks, except for a seasonal influenza vaccine within the last week. He has no history of progressive or severe neurological disorders. The boy is willing to participate in the study and has the consent of his parent or legal guardian.

The patient is a 32 year old female who has been trying to conceive for 2 years with her husband. They have been diagnosed with male type infertility and have scheduled IVF treatment with a fresh embryo transfer. The patient has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is considered obese. She has no history of endometriosis or adenomyosis and has not taken antibiotics during IVF treatment or ovum pick-up. The patient is willing to participate in the study to understand the impact of BMI on the endometrial microbiome during IVF treatments. She works as a teacher and enjoys hiking and cooking in her free time.

8-year-old male with a closed lateral condyle humerus fracture, requiring open reduction and percutaneous pinning. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of having a Weiss classification type II and III (>2mm displacement) lateral condyle fracture. The patient has no history of allergies to ropivacaine or oxycodone and does not have developmental delay that would preclude participation in the visual analog Faces Pain Scale-Revised. The patient does not have any other concomitant injuries, vascular or neurologic deficits, or pathologic fractures. The patient's parents have been informed about the study and have provided informed consent for participation. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery at the outpatient surgery center at the Orthopaedic Institute of Children (OIC).

A 42-year-old male presents with complaints of difficulty passing stools for the past 6 months. He reports feeling a sensation of incomplete evacuation and has to strain excessively during bowel movements. He has noticed a decrease in the caliber of his stools and sometimes experiences pain during defecation. He has no history of previous surgeries or significant medical conditions. Physical examination reveals anal stenosis with a diameter of 15 mm. The patient is informed about the nature of his condition and the available treatment options. He agrees to participate in a prospective randomized study comparing three different surgical techniques for anal stenosis. He signs the informed consent form after receiving explanations about the study and its possible risks and benefits. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 62-year-old woman is admitted to the emergency department with sudden onset right-sided weakness and facial droop that started 3 hours ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and she takes medication for both conditions. Upon examination, she has a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 16. Imaging studies reveal an occlusion in the left middle cerebral artery. The patient has already undergone one pass of mechanical thrombectomy with another device but failed to achieve mTICI 2b or better. The patient's mRS score was 1 prior to this stroke. The patient or her legally authorized representative has signed an informed consent form to participate in the study. The patient does not have severe hypertension on presentation and there is no evidence of dissection in the extra or intracranial cerebral arteries.

A 63-year-old male patient is scheduled for an open heart surgery due to severe aortic stenosis. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medication for his conditions such as metoprolol, atorvastatin, and metformin. He is physically active and exercises daily to manage his diabetes. He has no history of chronic pain or bleeding disorders. He has normal renal and hepatic function, and is not on any chronic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications. He is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologist's physiologic state II patient.  He has been informed about the trial and has given his consent to participate.

A 57-year-old male patient presents with abdominal pain and weight loss over the past few months. He has a past medical history of chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis. The patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, the liver is palpable and tender to touch. No other abnormalities are detected. Laboratory findings reveal elevated liver enzymes, alpha-fetoprotein levels, and positive serology for hepatitis B. Imaging studies show a 5 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of HCC. The patient is ineligible for surgery due to the size and location of the tumor. The patient has not received any prior treatment for HCC. The patient's Child-Pugh score is A and ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets all other eligibility criteria.

Patient is a 28yo male with no significant medical history, no current medications, and no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty in understanding the instructions. He is willing to abstain from caffeine, alcohol, grapefruit or grapefruit related citrus fruits 12 hours prior to the administration of study medication. He has a BMI of 23.5 and no history of gastrointestinal or neurological disorders. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or tics. He has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 30 days. He is a non-smoker and has a negative urine test for cotinine. He has no dental or jaw conditions that prohibit gum chewing. He does not have any of the exclusion criteria mentioned in the study.

A 35-year-old male veteran presented to the clinic with symptoms of Military-Related PTSD. He reported experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and intrusive thoughts that have been affecting his daily life for the past 6 months. He has tried various medications and therapies in the past, but none have provided significant relief. He participated in the lead-in study (TNX-CY-P201) and has shown improvement with the TNX-102 SL tablet therapy. He is compliant with the medication (over 60% compliance) and is willing to continue the treatment in the open-label extension study. He has no new or worsening medical conditions that could pose a safety risk or interfere with his participation in the study. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to refrain from the use of specific medications. He is not currently using any medically acceptable methods of birth control.

The patient is a 30-year-old non-smoking female with no history of smoking. She has 28 natural teeth and no diagnosed medical disorders such as diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, immunological and mucocutaneous diseases. She has not used antibiotics, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and immunosuppressive agents within the past 6 months. She has no non-inflammatory destructive periodontal disease and has not received any nonsurgical/surgical periodontal therapy in the past year. She has no restorative and endodontic treatment requirement, no orthodontic appliances or a removable partial denture. She is not pregnant, lactating or postmenopausal. She has been diagnosed with generalized aggressive periodontitis with minimum three teeth apart from the first molars and incisors showing CAL ≥5 mm and PPD ≥6 mm. Radiographic bone loss was ≥30 % of root length affecting ≥3 teeth other than first molars and incisors. She has at least one other family member presenting with or having a history of severe periodontal problems. She will be receiving conventional quadrant scaling and root planning (SRP) under local anaesthesia for 3 weeks as treatment.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with prediabetes. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is concerned about her risk of developing the condition. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the mechanisms of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs in the treatment of obesity and diabetes mellitus. She is currently not taking any medications and has no history of serious medical conditions. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has regular menstrual cycles and uses a barrier method of contraception. She is willing to discontinue any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or antioxidant vitamins for the duration of the study. She is excited to participate in a study that may lead to the development of more targeted therapies for diabetes and obesity.

A 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV infection 3 years ago and has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years. His viral load has been undetectable for the past year, and his CD4 count has been consistently above 500 cells/mm3. However, he has been experiencing intermittent fevers, with temperatures above 101 degrees F, for the past few weeks. He has not been diagnosed with any specific illness yet. He is willing to participate in this study as he wants to know if his fevers are affecting his HIV levels in the body. He is currently enrolled in an ACTG antiretroviral therapy study and has been on a stable antiretroviral therapy regimen for the past 8 weeks. He understands the study's purpose and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 14-year-old male with HIV-1 infection diagnosed at the age of 9. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 5 years and has achieved virologic suppression with an undetectable viral load for the past 2 years. He weighs 50 kg and is affiliated with the local health social security scheme. His parents are willing to provide informed consent for him to participate in the study and adhere to the protocol. He has not received integrase inhibitors for more than 2 weeks, and there is no evidence of resistance to DRV or integrase inhibitors. He is not currently taking any medication that interacts with DRV, RTV, or any once-daily integrase inhibitor. He does not have any intercurrent illness and meets the laboratory criteria for ALT, bilirubin, and creatinine levels. He has no history of tuberculosis, hepatitis B or C co-infection, or allergy to study drugs or their components.

A 65-year-old female with a history of memory loss and difficulty with daily activities over the last 6 months. She has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score of 20, which is two standard deviations below the normative reference value for her age and education level in the Portuguese population. She has a Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Aging and Dementia (CAIDE) Dementia Risk Score of 8 points. She has no medical disabilities that contraindicate physical activity and is able to perform daily activities independently. She is interested in participating in a non-pharmacological strategy that may prevent cognitive decline, including cognitive training, physical activity, nutrition education, adaption to memory loss, and diagnosis and correction of hearing impairment.

As this is a study focused on cricket players, the patient description would be as follows:  This study is seeking male cricket players aged between 18-25 years who have at least one year of experience playing at the domestic (first class) level. The players should not have undergone surgery or had an accident within the last 6 months. The study will involve randomized controlled trial and assessments will be taken at baseline, third week, and sixth week by performing Illinois Agility Run test, T test, and Vertical jump test. The study aims to determine the effects of plyometric training on agility in national cricket players.

A 42-year-old Egyptian man with a history of HCV genotype 4 infection presents with ongoing fatigue, abdominal pain, and yellowing of the skin and eyes. He has a history of intravenous drug use in his twenties and has not received any previous treatment for his HCV infection. He is currently unemployed and lives with his wife and two children. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies current illicit drug use. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory tests show a serum HCV RNA level of 2.4 million IU/mL, serum bilirubin level of 2.5 mg/dl, albumin level of 3.5 g/dl, INR of 1.2, and platelet count of 90,000/mm3. His HbA1c level is within normal range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive daclatasvir-sofosbuvir treatment regimen for his HCV infection.

The patient is a 28-year-old male soccer player who has been experiencing chronic groin pain for the past 6 months. Conservative treatment, including rest, physical therapy, and anti-inflammatory medications, has failed to alleviate his symptoms. He has been diagnosed with sportsman's hernia and referred to your clinic for surgical intervention. The patient has no significant medical history, takes no medications, and has no known drug allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has been playing soccer professionally for the past 7 years and is eager to return to full physical activity as soon as possible.

A 62-year-old female with stage IV pancreatic cancer who is admitted to the inpatient palliative care unit for management of worsening pain and psychological distress. The patient reports feeling hopeless, anxious, and has difficulty finding meaning in her life due to her diagnosis. She reports a score of 8 on the Depression subscale of the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System (ESAS). She has no history of seizures or brain lesions, and is capable of sitting up at a 45-degree angle for the duration of therapy. The patient is able to communicate in English and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no known contraindications to rTMS, including metallic skull plates, clips, or stimulators, pacemakers and other electronic implants, pregnancy, recurrent headaches with no known cause that do not respond to over-the-counter medications, current or previous skull fracture or traumatic brain injury, and previous brain surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) according to the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 2010 criteria. She has been on treatment with adalimumab for the past 18 months and her arthritis symptoms have been well-controlled, with a DAS28 CRP score of 2.4. She is willing to participate in the TAPER trial to investigate whether tapering her medication is safe and effective. She has no history of switching anti-TNF agents in the last 12 months, no recent steroid use, and no planned major surgery. She is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to follow up with the study visits and provide blood samples at the specified time points.

A 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is currently undergoing treatment is looking for ways to improve her mental and emotional well-being. She is married and has two children. Her husband is her primary caregiver. She has no history of severe visual or auditory impairment and is able to read, write, and speak English fluently. She is interested in participating in an arts-based program to help her cope with the stress and anxiety associated with her cancer diagnosis and treatment. She is physically able to participate in the program and is willing to commit to attending all sessions.

A 54-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. Imaging studies reveal a 5 cm mass in the right upper lobe of his lung, consistent with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of autoimmune disease, and is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. He is a surgical candidate for resection of his tumor. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is willing to provide blood samples, undergo leukapheresis, and have excisional or core needle biopsies. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has adequate organ and marrow function. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past 4 months for a different primary tumor or locoregional therapy for the target lesion. He is not receiving any other investigational agents. He does not have metastatic disease for which surgery would not be curative. The patient is negative for HIV and does not have active Hepatitis B.

A 34-year-old female presents with a history of neurotic excoriation characterized by compulsive skin picking resulting in visible skin damage and scarring. The patient reports significant distress and interference with daily functioning due to the condition. The patient has no history of seizures, myocardial infarction, or clinically significant medical illnesses. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraception. The patient has not received previous treatment with Lamictal or any other anti-epileptic medication. She is not currently undergoing psychotherapy or behavior therapy for the condition. The patient is willing to participate in a 12-week open-label study of Lamictal to evaluate its efficacy and safety in the treatment of neurotic excoriation.

A 58-year-old Caucasian female with a history of breast cancer presents with recurrent metastatic disease. She was diagnosed with hormone receptor positive breast cancer and underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy 5 years ago. She was on tamoxifen for 2 years after the completion of radiation therapy but later developed metastatic disease to the bone. She was started on an aromatase inhibitor but had to discontinue it after 2 months due to severe joint pain. She was then switched to a different aromatase inhibitor but developed progressive disease after 6 months. She is currently not on any systemic therapy for her breast cancer and wishes to participate in a clinical trial. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable left axillary lymph node. Laboratory tests reveal no significant abnormalities. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She fulfills the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 25-year-old female was recently diagnosed with high-grade osteosarcoma in her left leg. She has no previous history of cancer or chemotherapy. She has experienced pain and swelling in her leg for several months before diagnosis. Imaging studies show a large lesion in the distal femur with cortical and periosteal involvement. She reports no major medical problems, except for occasional headaches. Her laboratory tests are within normal limits, including liver and kidney function tests. She has no known allergies and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. She is compliant with medications and has a supportive family. She is scheduled for biopsy and if confirmed, she will be randomized to receive either 31 weeks of MAP or 73 weeks of maintenance therapy following MAP. She is excited to participate in the trial and is hopeful for a positive outcome.

This is a 7 year old male with a previous diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder. He was diagnosed at the age of 3 using the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) criteria for autism and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS-G) criteria. He has no known medical cause of autism, such as neurocutaneous syndromes, Fragile X, metabolic disorders, extreme prematurity, congenital rubella and other prenatal or postnatal neurological infections or gross dysmorphology. He is able to communicate verbally but has difficulty with social interactions and exhibits repetitive behaviors. He is currently receiving behavioral therapy and special education services. The patient and the family have agreed to participate in the study to identify genetic variants in selected synaptic genes and establish detailed genotype/phenotype correlations. They have also agreed to provide a blood sample for the generation of induced Pluripotent Stem Cells for further translational studies.

A 54 yo F with a history of breast cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, currently on hormone therapy, who presents with abdominal pain and weight loss. Imaging studies show multiple liver lesions consistent with metastases. Biopsy confirmed non-lymphoma liver metastases. There are 2 liver lesions measuring 3.8 cm and 4.2 cm respectively, and no evidence of other metastatic disease. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. The patient has adequate bone marrow, kidney, and liver function. The patient has not had prior radiotherapy to the liver. The patient is willing to use medically acceptable forms of contraception.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been suffering from osteoarthritis for the past 7 years. She has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and acetaminophen to manage her pain, but she still experiences moderate to severe pain in her right knee. She has difficulty walking and has been told by her doctor that she needs a knee replacement surgery. She is currently on the waiting list for surgery, which could take several months. She has tried taking weak opioids, such as codeine, but they have not provided adequate pain relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new treatment for her pain. She does not have any allergies to fentanyl or its adhesives, and she is not currently being treated for depression or epilepsy. She has not taken any sedative hypnotics, anaesthetics, or muscle relaxants in the past week. She is postmenopausal and is not breastfeeding. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She meets all the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain for more than a year. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee, which has been causing him significant discomfort and limiting his ability to perform daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs and standing for long periods of time. He has tried various medications and physical therapy, but none of them seem to have provided adequate relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial of a new home-based exercise training program with a motion track feedback technology called the Kaia Knee and Hip pain app. He is able to speak and understand English, has access to an iPad and the internet, and has a personal email address. He reports his pain intensity as 6/10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) for knee pain, on average, in the week prior to screening. He is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and use the Kaia Knee and Hip pain app. He is not currently planning to undergo any other treatment for his knee pain in the next 3 months and has no history of substance abuse or inflammatory/rheumatologic diseases.

A 32-year-old female diagnosed with unexplained infertility is seeking treatment for IVF. She has a BMI of 27 and has normal ovarian response with an AFC of 10. She is scheduled for a single embryo transfer and has a normal uterine cavity. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the clinical validation study for a diagnostic test measuring endometrial receptivity 24 hours before embryo transfer. She has no history of recurrent miscarriages or severe male factor infertility.

The patient is a 68-year-old female presenting with a history of transient ischemic attack (TIA) 4 months ago, which resolved spontaneously. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and she is currently taking atorvastatin and lisinopril. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her neurological examination is normal. A carotid ultrasound showed a stenosis of 70% on the right carotid artery. MRI of the brain showed no evidence of acute or chronic infarction. She is considered high risk for adverse events during carotid endarterectomy due to her age and comorbidities. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old nulliparous woman presented to the clinic for an intrauterine device (IUD) insertion. She reported having regular menstrual cycles and no history of sexually transmitted infections. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she was not taking any medications. She denied any allergies to medications or previous surgeries. She had never used any form of contraception before and was interested in the copper IUD. During the consultation, the clinician explained the procedure and possible adverse effects, including pain during insertion. The patient agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of a paracervical block containing 1% lidocaine in reducing pain during IUD insertion. She met all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. She was able to provide informed consent in English and was willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain in his right foot while resting, which has been gradually getting worse over the past few weeks. He also has a non-healing ulcer on his right foot and a history of peripheral arterial disease. The pain is affecting his daily activities, and he has been unable to sleep properly due to the discomfort. He has tried different medications and treatments, but nothing seems to alleviate the pain. Upon examination, the patient has a Rutherford Category 5 diagnosis, and all previous standard revascularization therapies have failed. He is a non-surgical candidate for revascularization as ruled by the investigator and confirmed by the BICR. He is willing and able to maintain compliance with a tolerated medical management regimen for PAD that includes smoking cessation, and may include management of hyperlipidemia, diabetic management, antiplatelet therapy, statin therapy, ACE inhibitor therapy (or ARB therapy), and beta-blocker therapy for control of blood pressure. The patient has poor lower extremity perfusion defined as an ABI ≤ 0.6, foot/ankle SPP ≤ 30 mmHg, or ankle systolic pressure ≤ 60 mmHg or toe pressure < 40 mmHg. The patient has not undergone any prior amputation in the index limb beyond the toe(s) or digits, and there is no systemic infectious symptom associated with the ischemic wound. The patient has written informed consent, and there is no history of neoplastic disease/cancer in the previous three years. The patient is not on renal dialysis or with end-stage renal disease, and the serum creatinine is below 2.5 mg/dl or GFR is above 15 using CKD-EPI equation of National Kidney Foundation.

This is a 35 year old female with a smoking history of 20 cigarettes per day for 10 years. She has a past medical history of hypertension and seasonal allergies. She is currently not on any medications and has no history of psychiatric illness. She is interested in quitting smoking and has provided written informed consent to participate in this study. She experiences at least 4 withdrawal symptoms upon abstinence. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate birth control methods. She does not have a history of myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, sustained or episodic cardiac arrhythmias, symptomatic peripheral vascular disease, or current peptic ulcer disease. She has no medical condition that the physician investigator deems inappropriate for subject participation. She is able to fulfill all scheduled visits and examination procedures throughout the study period.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing heartburn at least three times per week for the past six months. He has been taking omeprazole 20mg once daily for the past two months with sub-optimal symptom control. He has not experienced any weight loss or nausea and has not undergone any endoscopic procedures in the past year. The patient provides informed consent and is willing to complete study questionnaires. He is fluent in English, has no history of Barrett's esophagus, prior esophageal strictures, intolerance, or allergy to study medications. The patient has not undergone upper gastrointestinal surgery and is not taking plavix. He is interested in participating in the study and willing to comply with the optimal dosing regimen of taking omeprazole 30 minutes prior to the first meal of the day.

A 62-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. The electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in leads V2 to V6 and the patient was diagnosed with acute ST-segment myocardial infarction. He underwent successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention within 6 hours from the onset of symptoms. The echocardiography showed left ventricle ejection fraction of 55%. He has no history of significant comorbidities and has good social support. He is a non-smoker and his body mass index is within normal range. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and dyslipidemia. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman with a diagnosis of T1DM for 4 years visited the clinic for a regular check-up of her blood sugar levels. She uses an insulin pump and a CGM for the past 1 year, and her HbA1c level is 8.2%. She is married and does not plan to get pregnant. She has no history of hospitalization for diabetic ketoacidosis or severe hypoglycemia with loss of consciousness. She has no known history of coronary disease or cardiac failure, and her blood pressure is well controlled. She is not taking any medication other than insulin. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She has no known history of adrenal disease or psychiatric treatment. Her liver and renal function tests are normal. She is not experiencing any symptoms of active infectious disease.

A 55-year old man was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes three years ago. He is currently taking metformin 1000 mg twice a day and sitagliptin 100 mg once a day. His HbA1c is 6.5%. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and coronary artery disease. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and lives an active lifestyle. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He occasionally drinks wine with dinner. He doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has no history of alcohol abuse or liver disease. His blood pressure is well controlled at 130/80. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the effects of alcohol on his blood glucose and lipid levels. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and to abstain from alcohol for one month if needed. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking for the past 10 years. She smokes 20 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking in the past but failed. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. She does not use any other tobacco or nicotine-containing products. She is not pregnant and is willing to undergo a blood pregnancy test. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not using any hormonal contraceptives. She has no history of bulimia, organic mental disorder, brain injury, or psychotic disorder. She has not used any non-nicotine substances in the past 6 months and has not been diagnosed with major depression. She has no known allergies to any medication. Her breath carbon monoxide reading is >10 ppm at enrollment. She is competent to provide written informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) two years ago. She underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has since returned and spread to her brain. She has been treated with erlotinib, but her disease has progressed. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a minimum life expectancy of 6 months. She has a single activating EGFR mutation and has measurable extracranial lesions. Her cardiac function is normal, and she has no history of interstitial lung disease or other cardiovascular diseases. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of YH25448.

42-year-old premenopausal woman diagnosed with stage II invasive breast cancer. The cancer is confined to her left breast and nearby lymph nodes. She underwent surgical resection and radiotherapy as appropriate. The patient is currently considering adjuvant treatment options to reduce the risk of recurrence. She is interested in participating in a randomized, multicenter clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of tamoxifen with that of ovarian ablation, and/or combination chemotherapy. She has no other serious illness and no prior invasive malignancy except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old man has a medical history significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease. His nephrologist has informed him that he will need to start hemodialysis within the next few months. The patient is scheduled to have surgery to create a new arteriovenous fistula (AVF) in his left arm. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the function of his AVF. The patient is currently taking medications for his hypertension and diabetes and has been compliant with his medications. He has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 67-year-old male was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) three months ago. He has no significant medical history and is a non-smoker. The patient complained of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss of 10 pounds over the past few months. Laboratory tests revealed leukocytosis with lymphocytosis and elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of CLL. The patient was started on Obinutuzumab plus Chlorambucil (Obi-Clb) regimen as the first line of treatment. After completing six cycles of treatment, the patient experienced a complete response (CR), with no evidence of minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity. The patient did not experience any serious adverse events during the treatment. The patient has agreed to participate in the Real-World Data Study Focused on Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) Patient Treatment Options and Their Effectiveness and has provided informed consent for recording of his data in the CLLEAR registry.

32 yo F, G2P1 at 34 weeks gestation with a history of gestational hypertension in her previous pregnancy, presents to the ED with persistent elevated blood pressure readings (160/105 mmHg) on two separate occasions. She underwent spontaneous vaginal delivery without any complications and is now 48 hours postpartum. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of pre-existing hypertension or other medical conditions, and is able to give informed consent. The primary obstetrician is amenable to starting either study medication in the postpartum period. No other oral antihypertensive medications are being used concomitantly, and there are no absolute contraindications to nifedipine or labetalol such as allergy. The patient does not have significant renal disease, heart failure, moderate persistent or severe asthma, or preexisting diagnosis of chronic hypertension with medical treatment before delivery. The patient is willing to participate in the study and follow all instructions given by the researchers.

62-year-old male with a known history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, genotype 2 or 3, who has not received any previous interferon alpha-based therapy. The patient has no history of decompensated liver disease, hepatitis B virus (HBV) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection, moderate, severe or uncontrolled psychiatric disease, seizure disorder, chronic cardiac disease, preexisting interstitial lung disease, severe lung disease, or immunologically mediated disease. The patient has not undergone organ transplantation other than cornea or hair transplant and has no history of clinically significant hemoglobinopathy or malignancy of any organ system except for localized basal cell carcinoma of the skin. The patient has no history of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, and no known hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or to drugs with similar chemical structures. The patient is not currently addicted to drugs or alcohol and has not received systemic corticosteroids, systemic antibiotics, antifungals, or antivirals for the treatment of active infection, herbal therapies, or investigational drugs within the specified timeframes prior to the Baseline visit. The patient is willing and able to provide signed informed consent (IC) form prior to participation in any study-related procedures.

A 45-year-old female presents with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been on basal/bolus insulin therapy with concurrent use of metformin for glycemic control for the past 2 years. Her most recent HbA1c level was 7.5%. She reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia, but has not had any severe episodes requiring assistance in the past 30 days. She uses approximately 35 units of basal insulin per day and has a stable insulin regimen. Her BMI is 29, and she has no known allergies or sensitivities to skin adhesives. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the use of PaQ™ as a simple patch on insulin delivery device to control her blood glucose levels.

A 56-year-old male with a newly diagnosed squamous cell head and neck cancer presents with complaints of dry mouth and difficulty swallowing. The tumor is located in the right buccal mucosa and has spread to the ipsilateral lymph nodes. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this study, with both parotid glands included in the radiation fields and no distant metastases. He has neutrophils ≥ 2000 / mm, platelets ≥ 100,000 / mm3, creatinine < 130 / mmol.L-1, and transaminase ≤ 3 x upper limit. The patient has not used pilocarpine prophylactically.

A 35-year-old African American woman presented to the UI Health mammography clinic for her annual mammogram. She has a family history of breast cancer with her mother being diagnosed at age 48. She has never been diagnosed with breast cancer herself. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about genetic counseling and how it can impact her risk for breast cancer. She is fluent in English and able to complete the informed consent and survey. She has never had genetic counseling for hereditary breast cancer risk before. She is not a prisoner.

The patient is a 62-year-old female who underwent resection surgery for colon cancer. She was admitted to the surgical intensive care unit postoperatively and requires parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She takes amlodipine, atorvastatin, and acetaminophen as needed for pain. She has no history of deep vein thrombosis or other clotting disorders. She consents to participate in the study and undergoes doppler examination to evaluate for the incidence of thrombosis on the central venous catheter.

The patient is a 32-year-old French-speaking woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia according to the DSM IV criteria. She has been experiencing symptoms of schizophrenia, including delusions and hallucinations, for the past 2 years. Her symptoms have been managed with medication, but she still struggles with cognitive impairments and social autonomy. She has no history of addiction or neurological disease. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the impact of Cognitive Remediation Therapy (CRT) on cognition, social autonomy, symptoms, and brain functioning in patients with schizophrenia. She is able to provide informed consent for the study. If she is selected for the fMRI study, she has no counterindications for MRI.

A 55-year-old male was diagnosed with bladder cancer after experiencing hematuria and lower abdominal pain. He underwent transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT) and cystoscopy, which confirmed the diagnosis of transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of the bladder with muscularis propria invasion. Imaging studies showed no evidence of metastasis. He was deemed operable and met the inclusion criteria for the study. His Zubrod Performance Status was 1, and his complete blood count, serum bilirubin, and serum creatinine levels were within normal limits. He had no prior history of systemic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation therapy. He was willing to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by chemoradiation therapy or radical cystectomy. He provided his informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who lives in an urban area and has been a patient at a community health center for the past two years. She is of Hispanic descent and speaks Spanish as her primary language. She has never undergone colorectal cancer screening and is interested in learning more about it. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are currently well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cancer or gastrointestinal symptoms. She lives alone and is retired. She is able to perform her activities of daily living independently. She has a good understanding of her health conditions and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any exclusion criteria for the study.

45 yo M with chronic low back pain for over a year, with no significant relief with nonsurgical conservative therapy. MRI shows degenerative disc disease at L4-L5. Pain is localized to the lower back and radiates occasionally to the right leg. Patient reports difficulty standing, walking, and sitting for prolonged periods of time. Past Medical History: - Hypertension, well-controlled on lisinopril - Hyperlipidemia, well-controlled on atorvastatin - Former smoker, quit 5 years ago - No history of prior lumbar spine surgery - No known allergies to silicone or barium sulfate - No history of diabetes or autoimmune disease.

A 35-year-old male patient with a spinal cord injury at the T10 level came to the clinic for bladder management. He has been using intermittent catheterization daily for the past 6 months and usually needs to self-catheterize 3-4 times a day. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials recently. The patient is able to self-catheterize and has given written informed consent to participate in this investigation. He has no current symptoms of urinary tract infection.

A 35-year old male was diagnosed with adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN) three years ago. He has been experiencing difficulty in walking, muscle weakness, and stiffness in his lower limbs. He also experiences difficulty in running and has been falling frequently. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he is taking medication. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker and has difficulty performing his job due to his motor deficits. He doesn't have any history of smoking or alcohol use. His MRI scan shows abnormalities in his spinal cord and he has been experiencing spasticity in his lower limbs. He has been on steroid replacement therapy for adrenal insufficiency. The patient is interested in participating in this study and improving his motor deficits.

A 50-year-old female with a BMI of 30 who is scheduled to undergo an elective laparoscopic hysterectomy under general anesthesia. She has no history of difficult airway management or respiratory disease, and does not have any cardiac complications. She is able to lie flat and has a hemoglobin level of 120 g/L. She is not pregnant, and does not have any neuromuscular disorders or cervical spine instability. The patient does not have any allergy to the agents used for induction of general anesthesia, and has no contraindications to the insertion of radial artery cannula or any significant nasal obstruction.

A 58 yo man who underwent coronary bypass surgery 10 years ago using the radial artery as a bypass vessel. He has not had any major cardiovascular events since the surgery and has been following up regularly with his cardiologist. He is willing to attend for coronary angiography and give written informed consent for the RSVP study to evaluate the long-term patency of the radial artery. The patient has no contraindications to coronary angiography and has not participated in any research projects within the previous 60 days.

A healthy 30-year-old male came to the clinic and expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial. He is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 22 kg/m2, and weighs 75 kg. He has no history of cardiovascular, neurological, hematological, psychiatric, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, endocrine, immunologic or renal disease. He has no known allergies to omeprazole, rosiglitazone, desipramine or their constituents. He does not take any prescription or over-the-counter medication, including herbal products, and has not used tobacco or nicotine products for over a year. He is willing to use a condom and spermicide during sexual activity for 90 days after the last dosing of avanafil and is willing to not donate sperm for 90 days after dosing. The subject has not donated blood or plasma in the past 56 days and does not plan to donate during the study. The subject is identified as CYP2D6 extensive metabolizer (determined by genotyping) and is willing to comply with all requirements of study participation.

The patient is a 2-year-old child who has been experiencing cough, fast breathing, and chest indrawing for the past 72 hours. The child's oxygen saturation level is less than 96%. The child is admitted to the Aga Khan University Hospital in Karachi, Pakistan. The child is eligible to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the use of lung ultrasound for acute respiratory infections by community health workers. The trial involves training community health workers on performing and interpreting pediatric lung POCUS to improve pediatric pneumonia outcomes in low-resource settings. The child will undergo lung POCUS by a trained community health worker, and the performance and interpretation of the POCUS will be evaluated. The goal of this trial is to determine if accurate POCUS performance and interpretation can be achieved by non-medically-trained community health workers after focused training, and to develop a novel pediatric pneumonia diagnosis and management algorithm for low-resource settings.

A 65-year-old male patient was recently admitted to the hospital for an ischemic stroke that affected his left hemisphere. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication to manage these conditions. He is married, lives with his wife, and has two adult children. He is retired and enjoys gardening and reading. Since the stroke, he has experienced weakness and numbness in his left arm and leg, as well as difficulty speaking and understanding language. He received treatment in the hospital and is now preparing to return home. He is concerned about his ability to manage his medications and understand the instructions for his recovery. He is open to participating in the clinical trial to receive a pharmaceutical interview to discuss his discharge prescription and improve his knowledge and compliance with treatment.

56-year-old female with a history of breast cancer, status-post right mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, and radiation therapy presents with unilateral upper limb lymphedema. She complains of discomfort, heaviness, and difficulty moving the affected limb. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and is able to ambulate independently. She is willing to participate in the study and provides written informed consent. Her blood serum assessment, including complete blood count (CBC) with differential and comprehensive metabolic panel, is within normal limits. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has a negative pregnancy test within the past 2 weeks. She is not receiving any concomitant treatment for lymphedema and is not allergic to rHUPH20 or any hyaluronidase extracts. She is willing and able to self-administer the subcutaneous experimental drug and maintain a log of the injections. She has no concurrent condition that would make her ineligible for the trial.
