A 57-year-old man was admitted to the hospital for an elective surgery. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of heart disease or diabetes. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 3 times a week. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. He is currently taking lisinopril for his hypertension. After the surgery, he was transferred to the post-operative care unit and was intubated and mechanically ventilated. He is expected to require sedation for at least 2 hours. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologist (ASA) classification of 2.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a soft tissue sarcoma. She has been experiencing pain and swelling in the affected area and has undergone several imaging tests to monitor the progression of her cancer. Her doctor has recommended that she participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET imaging in detecting abnormalities in glucose metabolism in soft tissue sarcomas. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to follow instructions and comply with the protocol. She has a Karnofsky Performance Scale score of 80, indicating that she is able to carry out normal activities with little to no difficulty. The patient has provided written informed consent prior to participation in the study and has been scheduled for a PET scan at the Cross Cancer Oncologic Imaging Department.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has sustained a complete spinal cord injury at the T8 level in a motor vehicle accident. He is currently receiving rehabilitation services and has been experiencing difficulty with erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory dysfunction, and semen abnormalities. He is interested in fathering children in the future and is seeking medical assistance to improve his fertility. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to understand and improve impairments to male fertility resulting from spinal cord injury.

A 56-year-old male with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) 2 years ago presented to the clinic for follow-up. He has been taking aspirin 81mg daily since the time of his MI and has not had any recurrent cardiovascular events. He has no known allergies and his medical history is significant only for hypertension, which is well-controlled on amlodipine 5mg daily. He quit smoking 5 years ago and denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is currently working as a software engineer and lives with his wife and two children. He exercises regularly and has a healthy diet. He has no history of bleeding disorders or gastrointestinal bleeding. His physical examination is normal, and his current blood pressure is 125/80 mmHg. His laboratory tests results including complete blood count, liver function tests and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of smoking for 30 years. He currently smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. He has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and a hoarse voice for the past 2 months. He also complains of a constant sore throat and a lump in his neck. He has no significant medical history, and his physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable left cervical lymph node. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 80 beats/min, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min. His laboratory tests are within normal limits. A biopsy of the cervical lymph node confirms a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. He has not received any previous treatment for this condition. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

12 year old Chinese student residing in Duanzhou District, Zhaoqing city who is currently under home confinement due to the COVID-19 outbreak and enrolled in online learning courses. The student has no history of autism spectrum disorders, pervasive developmental delay or disorder, mental retardation, psychotic disorders, schizophrenia, mania or hypomania disorders, suicidal behavior and/or acute plan that require higher level of care or participation in psychotherapy. The student is in grade 7 and is experiencing digital eye strain and anxiety due to prolonged periods of online learning without adequate physical activity breaks. The student is willing to participate in a randomized control trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a novel digital intervention during recess in reducing anxiety and digital eye strain.

A 28-year-old male software engineer with a history of mild myopia and astigmatism is scheduled for LASIK surgery in both eyes. He has been wearing soft contact lenses for the past 5 years, but he stopped wearing them 2 weeks ago, as advised by his ophthalmologist. He has no history of any systemic illness and is not taking any medication. He has never used any topical eye medication other than the prescribed ones for pre- or post-operative care. He has no history of eye infection, inflammation, or allergy. He is generally in good health, exercises regularly, and follows a healthy diet. He is excited about the prospect of having better vision without the need for glasses or contact lenses. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance the field of ophthalmology and improve the outcomes of LASIK surgery for future patients.

56 year old woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and symptomatic left-sided abdominal pain presents for a distal pancreatectomy. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting despite medical management. The patient underwent several diagnostic tests which revealed a large pseudocyst involving the tail of the pancreas. After discussing the risks and benefits of the procedure, the patient consented to undergo a distal pancreatectomy with the placement of a closed suction drain. The patient is randomized to the suctioning drain group and will be followed up for the development of pancreatic fistula. The patient will be seen in the surgical clinic for follow-up appointments and will undergo imaging studies as part of the study.

A 8-year-old boy with a history of leukemia presents with a single oral temperature of 38.5 degrees C and neutrophil count of 300/cu mm during the course of chemotherapy. He has no known allergies to amikacin or cloxacillin, and his creatinine clearance is within normal limits. He has no central nervous system infection or history of hearing abnormalities. He is not in shock but has mild hepatomegaly. He has not received any aminoglycosides or intravenous antibiotics in the past 14 and 7 days, respectively. His cancer is not newly diagnosed or relapsed.

The patient is a 45-year-old healthy Caucasian female with no known medical history or chronic disorders. She works as an office manager and leads an active lifestyle. She does not have any known allergies or sensitivities to herbal extracts or lactose. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or consume caffeine regularly. Her BMI is within the normal range of 22. She has not participated in any clinical study within the past 60 days and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is willing to provide written and signed informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old, French-speaking woman who is currently 10 weeks pregnant. She has registered with one of the two participating maternity hospitals for prenatal care. She has a good understanding of the French language, and she has internet access at home. She is affiliated with the National Health Insurance Fund of the country within the regional level health insurance. She has no prior history of miscarriage or other pregnancy-related complications. She is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to follow the guidelines set by the study. She is currently employed as a teacher and has a supportive partner who is involved in her pregnancy. She is looking forward to receiving coordinated care from a team of healthcare professionals throughout her pregnancy.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread pain and fatigue for at least 3 months. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by a rheumatologist based on the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Diagnostic Criteria. She has tried various treatments such as physical therapy, massage, and acupuncture, but none of them have provided significant relief. She is currently not taking any medications for her fibromyalgia. Her past medical history is significant for anxiety and depression, which she is taking Sertraline for. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She does not have any history of substance or alcohol abuse. She is willing to discontinue her current medications for this study. She has a BMI of 23 and has no other concurrent diseases. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of high blood pressure. He has been experiencing occasional headaches and dizziness, which prompted him to monitor his blood pressure regularly. He has been taking medication for hypertension for the past 2 years. His current blood pressure readings are averaging around 142/92 mmHg, but he wants to ensure the accuracy of his readings. He is willing to undergo 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to determine the optimal timing and frequency of measurements for a reliable diagnosis of his hypertension. He has no other significant medical history or current symptoms.

A pregnant woman, aged 28, was diagnosed with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) during her 27th week of gestation. She has been admitted to the Fetal Surgery Center for prenatal care and management of the CDH fetus. The prenatal ultrasound showed that the estimated fetal weight (EFW) was within normal limits and the amniotic fluid volume was normal. Doppler velocimetry of the umbilical artery was also within the normal range. The fetal MRI revealed that the observed/expected total fetal lung volume (O/E TFLV%) was 40% and the percentage of liver herniation (%LH) was 30%. The signal intensity of the lung and liver on T2 sequences were normal. The mediastinal shift angle was 10 degrees and the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) on diffusion-weighted sequences (DWI) was normal. The radiographic pulmonary area was calculated and found to be 50% of the normal value. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria. She will be monitored closely throughout the pregnancy, and the investigators will collect data from the prenatal and postnatal course, including details about the FETO procedure, if needed. The patient's neonatal course will be assessed, focusing on the pulmonary hypertensive status, need for ECMO, and deaths. The surgical course will also be recorded, including the type of surgical repair and use of patch. The collected data will be used to develop algorithms that will help predict the patient's outcome accurately.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic neck pain for the last 6 months. She describes her pain as a constant ache in the back of her neck that radiates to her shoulders and upper back. Her pain intensity is 6 out of 10 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS). She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. She has no previous history of neck or head trauma or surgery. She does not have any inflammatory joint disease or systemic conditions. The patient is not taking any medication except occasional pain relievers. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old female with moderate crowding in her lower dental arch. She has all her permanent teeth except for her wisdom teeth, which have not yet erupted. She has an Angle class I malocclusion with normal facial proportions. Her oral hygiene is good, and her periodontium is healthy. She has no relevant medical history and is not taking any regular medication. She has not had any previous orthodontic treatment. Her crowding requires treatment with fixed appliance using the non-extraction approach. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve orthodontic treatment outcomes.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with biliary tract cancer with HER2 overexpression. He has previously undergone first-line chemotherapy which failed to control the disease progression. He has no history of CNS metastases or cancerous meningitis. He has a predicted survival of at least 12 weeks. His ECOG performance status score is 1. He has adequate organ function and meets laboratory criteria for hemoglobin, WBC count, neutrophil count, platelets, total bilirubin, AST, ALT, serum creatinine, and creatinine clearance. He has not undergone major surgery within the last four weeks or received anti-cancer vaccine within the last four weeks. He is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol. He has given voluntary agreement to provide written informed consent. He is not HIV positive, HBsAg positive with HBV-DNA positive, or HCV positive. He has no history of major autoimmune diseases that require systemic treatment. He is not currently experiencing severe, uncontrollable companion diseases. He is not suffering from pleural or abdominal effusion with clinical symptoms that require ongoing treatment.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic headaches for several years. She describes the headaches as a constant dull pain in her forehead and temples, with occasional sharp stabbing pains behind her eyes. The headaches have been interfering with her ability to work and enjoy her hobbies. She has tried various medications, but none have provided lasting relief. She is interested in participating in a behavioral treatment program for chronic headaches that includes an aerobic exercise prescription. She reports that she currently engages in less than 60 minutes of physical activity per week, but is interested in starting a regular exercise routine. She has no history of other medical issues and is physically capable of engaging in exercise. She has regular internet access and is willing to commit to attending regular treatment sessions.

A 65-year-old male patient underwent corneal transplant surgery due to severe keratoconus. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but both conditions are well-controlled with medication. The patient is proficient in instilling eye drops and has no visual or cognitive impairments that could affect compliance with treatment. The patient is able to attend all scheduled visits and is covered by a social security system. The patient has been informed about the study and has signed the consent form.

The patient is a 43-year-old Caucasian woman who has tested positive for a BRCA1 gene mutation. She has a strong family history of breast and ovarian cancer, with her mother and maternal grandmother both diagnosed with ovarian cancer at a young age. The patient has opted for risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (rrBSO) to reduce her risk of developing high grade serous carcinoma (HGSC). She has not had tubal occlusion for sterilization. The patient has no current symptoms of HGSC and is not pregnant. She is mentally capable of providing informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 20-year-old female volleyball player who has been playing the sport for the past 3 years. She currently participates in amateur industry competitions and practices 4 days a week. She has never suffered any major musculoskeletal injuries but has experienced occasional knee pain after prolonged practice sessions. Her BMI is within the normal range and she has no history of neurological, auditory, or vestibular disorders. She has not received any physiotherapy treatment unrelated to the study and is willing to sign the informed consent. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her knee joint stability, balance, and power in the vertical jump.

A 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) a few years ago. He has been treated with imatinib and sunitinib but his tumor has progressed and metastasized. He has not yet received regorafenib. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to access ripretinib, a new drug that has shown promising results in treating GIST. He has no history of allergies or hypersensitivity to medication and is willing to comply with the contraception requirements if necessary. He has adequate organ function and bone marrow reserve as determined by the Investigator at Screening. He is capable of understanding and complying with the protocol and has signed the informed consent form.

A 52 year old woman comes in for her scheduled colonoscopy in the afternoon. She has a family history of colon cancer and has been advised by her physician to get regular screenings. She has never had a colonoscopy before and is feeling quite anxious about the procedure. She reports occasional abdominal pain and bloating, but no other significant symptoms. She is in generally good health with no major medical issues. She has no history of colorectal cancer, FAP or IBD. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing the effect of taking a break during the colonoscopy session on adenoma detection.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has always been in good health. She has no history of chronic or acute medical conditions and takes no regular medications. She maintains a healthy lifestyle, including a well-balanced diet and regular exercise routine. Her medical history is unremarkable, with no significant surgeries or hospitalizations. She has never participated in a clinical trial before but is eager to contribute to medical research.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of high blood pressure is interested in participating in a study to reduce her salt intake. She is currently taking medication to control her blood pressure and has been on a stable diet for the past 3 weeks. She is responsible for her own meals and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of cardiovascular disease, liver or kidney disease, cancer, or substance abuse. She does not have any special dietary needs and is available to sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old female with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) and hypertension. She presents with worsening chest pain and dyspnea on exertion for the past month. She has a history of smoking for 10 years, but quit 15 years ago. She takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin daily. Her physical exam is significant for a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. An electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF. She is diagnosed with stable angina and is scheduled for elective PCI. Her lab studies are as follows: FBS: 110 mg/dl HbA1c: 6.2% Cholesterol: 180 mg/dl TG: 120 mg/dl LDL: 110 mg/dl HDL: 45 mg/dl. She has not been treated with unfractionated heparin prior to PCI and weighs 70 kg.

This is a 32 year old male with a past medical history of acute myeloid leukemia who underwent haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for treatment. The patient has completed the initial post-transplant period and is now considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. The patient has no severe diarrhea or serious infections at the time of evaluation for inclusion. The patient has not been diagnosed with acute GVHD yet.

Pt is a 35yo M with a 10-year history of plaque psoriasis involving more than 20% of his body surface area (BSA) and a PASI score of 12. He has been on a stable dose of ciclosporin for the past 6 months with significant improvement in his symptoms. However, he is concerned about the long-term side effects of ciclosporin and is interested in exploring alternative treatment options. He has no history of other skin conditions or significant medical conditions, and his BMI is within normal limits. He has not received any prior TNF-inhibitor therapy or efalizumab. He is willing to discontinue ciclosporin and start etanercept therapy as part of the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with a neuromuscular disease two years ago. She has been experiencing progressive muscle weakness, which has made it difficult for her to perform daily activities such as dressing and bathing. She relies on a wheelchair to move around and has limited hand and arm movement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve communication for patients with severe disabilities. She has no history of seizures, brain damage, or any other medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. She is able to read and write and has no cognitive dysfunction. She provides informed consent and is willing to participate in the study, which involves testing two different communication devices to determine which one is more effective.

48-year-old male diagnosed with recurrent head and neck cancer with a history of platinum-based chemotherapy with or without radiotherapy presents with progressive disease. Measurable disease is present, with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, an absolute neutrophil count of 2,500/μL, and platelets of 150,000/µL. Total bilirubin is 0.8 mg/dL, and AST/ALT is within normal limits. Creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of allergic reactions related to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to gemcitabine hydrochloride or doxorubicin hydrochloride. The patient has normal cardiac ejection fraction and has undergone echocardiogram or MUGA scan prior to the use of study drugs. The patient is not suffering from any uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient has recovered from prior therapy and at least 3 weeks have passed since prior chemotherapy (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C), at least 30 days since prior experimental agents, and at least 4 weeks since prior radiotherapy for palliation or for the primary tumor. The patient is not receiving concurrent hormones or other chemotherapeutic agents, except for steroids given for adrenal failure, hormones given for non-disease-related conditions, or intermittent use of dexamethasone as an antiemetic. The patient is not receiving concurrent palliative radiotherapy, other concurrent investigational or commercial agents, or therapies.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who underwent a right foot surgery 2 years ago and still suffers from chronic pain in that area. She has tried various pain medications but has not experienced satisfactory pain relief. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and does not take any daily analgesic or opioid medications. Her weight is within a healthy range, and she is not pregnant. She has no neuro-muscular deficits of either femoral nerves or quadriceps muscles. She is willing to have bilateral femoral perineural catheters placed with a subsequent ropivacaine infusion and motor/sensory testing for 6 hours, requiring an overnight stay in the UCSD GCRC/CTRI to allow dissipation of local anesthetic infusion effects by the following morning. She understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 35 year old woman with a clinical diagnosis of schizophrenia. She has been taking aripiprazole for the past 6 months and her dosage has remained stable during this time. Her total PANSS score is currently 70, indicating mild to moderate symptoms. She is not taking any other medications for psychiatric or mood disorders, and has no history of head trauma. She is not currently pregnant, as confirmed by a negative urine hCG test.

The patient is a pregnant woman who is interested in participating in a research study focused on the microbiome of newborns. She is carrying a singleton pregnancy with a non-anomalous, appropriately-grown fetus. The patient has a family history of atopic diseases, such as asthma, allergic rhinoconjunctivitis, or atopic dermatitis, or food allergies in a first-degree relative of the infant to-be-delivered. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the study protocol. The patient has not had any complications during her pregnancy, such as pre-eclampsia, chorioamnionitis, placenta previa, vasa previa, placental abruption, or active vaginal bleeding. The patient has not used any investigational drugs during the third trimester of pregnancy and has not had any current, diagnosed mental illness or current, diagnosed or self-reported drug or alcohol abuse in the mother that, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with the participant's ability to comply with study requirements. The patient is willing to breastfeed and has not had any history of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis within the past year.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent nasal congestion, difficulty breathing, and hearing loss for the past six months. He has also noticed a lump on the left side of his neck that has been gradually increasing in size. After undergoing a biopsy, he was diagnosed with nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The cancer has not spread beyond the nasopharynx and lymph nodes in the neck. The patient will require primary concomitant radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Further testing shows that the patient is positive for PCR-DNA EBV. The patient is in otherwise good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has no prior history of head and neck surgery or chemotherapy within the last 6 months. Blood tests show that the patient's WBC count is within normal range, and serum creatinine level is within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the study-specific consent form.

45-year-old male with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and coronary artery disease with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. He is currently taking metformin and aspirin daily. He does not smoke cigarettes and has a physical work capacity of 60 W. He has a significant coronary stenosis of the LAD artery (>50%) and a stenosis of 20% in the RCX artery. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication, and his LDL-cholesterol level is within normal limits. He has not experienced any ventricular tachyarrhythmias or myocardial infarctions in the past 4 weeks. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his cardiovascular health and is willing to commit to the exercise training program.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who underwent a kidney transplant 6 years ago due to end-stage renal disease caused by IgA nephropathy. He was enrolled in the CTOT-01 study and received noninvasive immune monitoring tests during the first 6 months post-transplant. He has been compliant with his immunosuppressive medication regimen and has had no significant complications since the transplant. He has regular follow-up appointments with his transplant team and has had no episodes of acute rejection. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He occasionally drinks alcohol in social situations. His physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable, and his renal function is stable with a serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL. He has provided consent to participate in this retrospective multicenter study to determine his 5-year clinical outcomes.

A 35 year old woman has been diagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis for 2 years, experiencing frequent flare-ups that require hospitalization. She is currently in symptomatic remission with a modified Partial Mayo score ≤ 2 with a rectal bleeding score = 0. The patient has a history of steroid use and is currently taking a 5-ASA oral medication. She reports that she has trouble adhering to her medication regimen and is worried about the risk of surgery. She is interested in participating in the study as she believes that the home-based kit will be more convenient for her to monitor her condition. The patient is able to use the IBDocTM test kit which requires a smart phone with a camera and internet access to download the CalApp® which interprets the measurement. She is willing to give informed consent to the study protocol and is not currently experiencing a symptomatic flare.

The patient is a 25 year old male of Hispanic ethnicity. He is a non-smoker and a social drinker. He is currently working as a software engineer and enjoys playing video games in his free time. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any prescription medication. He has a body weight within 15% of the appropriate range as defined in the 1983 Metropolitan Life Company tables and weighs 160 lbs. He has no history of mental illness, drug addiction, drug abuse, or alcoholism. He has not donated blood in the past 4 weeks and has never had any difficulty in donating blood. He has not received any investigational drug within the 4 weeks prior to study dosing. He does not use tobacco products. He is not currently in a sexual relationship and is not sexually active. He is interested in participating in the Pravastatin Sodium Tablets 80 mg bioequivalence study under fasting conditions.

A 65-year-old woman presents with a history of cirrhosis due to hepatitis C virus infection. She has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice for the past few weeks. Her medical history also includes type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. She has been on medication for these conditions for several years. Her recent laboratory tests show a serum creatinine level of 1.9 mg/dL and an eGFR of 25 mL/min/1.73 m². She has no documented history of malignancies or other major illnesses. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of copanlisib in subjects with impaired hepatic or renal function.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who was diagnosed with HIV infection 6 months ago. His HIV viral load is 10,000 copies/ml and CD4 count is 250 cells/mm3. He has not received any antiretroviral therapy in the past. The patient has no history of AIDS-defining opportunistic infections or any other significant medical history. He is currently not receiving any systemic chemotherapy or immune modulators. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. He is sexually active and willing to use acceptable methods of contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no history of comorbidities that impair her mobility and her Eastern Co-operative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score is 1. She has a sedentary lifestyle and is concerned about maintaining her physical activity levels during and after treatment. She is willing to wear a commercially available fitness tracker to monitor her activity levels and help her stay motivated to exercise. She is committed to attending all study visits and completing all study requirements.

The patient is a 34-year-old female with moderate-severe melasma on her forehead, cheeks, and upper lips. She has had the condition for the past 2 years and has tried several over-the-counter skin lightening creams with no significant improvement. She is not currently taking any hormone-altering medications and has not had any recent chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or laser treatments. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies to azelaic acid or hydroquinone. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the safety and effectiveness of Azelaic Acid Gel to Hydroquinone Cream in the treatment of melasma.

A 53-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for the past 4 months is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She works as a teacher and her job requires her to stand for long periods of time. She has tried various treatments including pain medication, physiotherapy, and massage therapy but has not found any significant relief. She rates her pain between 4-5 on a scale of 1-10. She does not have any history of back surgery, cardiovascular or rheumatic diseases. She is not pregnant and has not been undergoing any other physical therapy. She is interested in trying the Pilates method to see if it can help alleviate her low back pain.

A 35-year-old female came to the clinic with a history of ear pain and pressure in both ears for the past 3 months. She has been experiencing fullness and popping sounds in her ears, which has been affecting her hearing. She has tried multiple medical treatments including nasal decongestants and antihistamines, but her symptoms have not improved. She was diagnosed with persistent obstructive eustachian tube dysfunction (OETD) through a hearing test and physical examination. She is scheduled to undergo a tympanoplasty procedure to repair a perforated eardrum and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial testing the feasibility of eustachian tube dilation with an endovascular balloon. She has not undergone any prior eustachian tube intervention or radiation to the head and neck. She is willing to follow the protocol for the study and is excited to explore a potential solution to her persistent ear symptoms.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis for the past year. She complains of itching, redness, tearing, and foreign body sensation in both eyes. She has no history of eye surgery or any ocular disease. She does not wear contact lenses and has not used any topical eye drug such as cyclosporine, tacrolimus, interferon-alpha, mitomycin, or any oral or subcutaneous drugs such as antihistamines, anti-leukotrienes, corticoids, immunosuppressants, or biological drugs. She does not have any other disease except for mild rhinitis. She is willing to participate in the study and is available for follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease and renal anemia. He has been receiving Mircera (methoxy polyethylene glycol-epoetin beta) for the past 8 months to manage his anemia. His hemoglobin levels have been fluctuating over the past few months, and his healthcare provider has recommended a retrospective observational study to evaluate the effectiveness of Mircera in managing his anemia over a period of 6 months. The patient has given his written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 3 years. He has been experiencing excessive salivation, which is causing social isolation and embarrassment. He has already tried other treatment options, including anticholinergic medication, with little success. The patient's Hoehn and Yahr stage is 3 and he has a score of 3 on the salivation section of UPDRS, item 6. He is under a stable anti-Parkinson therapy throughout the study. He has no history of hypertension, hyperthyroidism, congestive heart failure, coronary heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, tachycardia or severe bradycardia. He does not have narrow angle glaucoma or shallow anterior chamber and has no history of gastrointestinal obstruction or bladder outflow obstruction. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. The patient is able and willing to comply with the study procedures and provide written informed consent.

A 24-year-old French female presents to the dermatology clinic with a complaint of depigmented patches on her face. The patient reports that the patches have been present for about a year and have not changed in size or color over the last three months. She denies any itching, burning, or pain associated with the patches. She has not received any treatment for this condition in the past three months. The patient has no significant medical history or allergies. She is not currently pregnant and is using contraception. On examination, multiple hypopigmented patches, with a total area greater than 3cm², are seen on her face. The Local Vitiligo Area Severity Index (VASI) score is ≥ 50%. The patient is diagnosed with non-segmental (symmetrical) vitiligo and is offered the opportunity to participate in the VITAC study. As the patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria, she is considered eligible to participate in the study.

35 y/o female who sustained a moderate traumatic brain injury (TBI) 2 years ago following a motor vehicle accident. Currently experiencing post-traumatic headache and seeking relief from ongoing symptoms. Patient is currently under medical supervision for headache management and has not received acupuncture treatment for headaches in the past 6 months. Patient reports a score of 5 on the Patient Health Questionnaire 2 and a raw summed score of 4 on the PROMIS Cognitive Function Short Form v2.0 - Abilities 2a. Patient is community-dwelling, fluent in English, and able to provide voluntary consent. No history of multiple TBIs or diagnosis of PTSD, psychosis, or agitation. No other neurodegenerative disorders or medical/surgical conditions that would prevent travel to participate in the intervention over the study duration. Not pregnant and able to provide informed consent for the research.

A 29-year-old woman who is pregnant with twins was referred to the clinic by her obstetrician. She is currently at 10 weeks of gestation and has had a history of preeclampsia in her previous pregnancy. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any chronic medical conditions. She has not smoked and does not drink alcohol. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has been compliant with her obstetrician's recommendations. She is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about the benefits of low-dose aspirin in twin pregnancies.

25-year-old female who participated in the National Vaccine Evaluation Consortium (NVEC) study conducted between 2009-2011, which evaluated the immunogenicity of the Cervarix and Gardasil HPV vaccines. She received either the Cervarix or Gardasil vaccine 5-7 years ago as part of the study. She is willing and able to give written informed consent for participation in this follow-up study to assess the duration of the humoral immune response elicited by the HPV vaccines. She has no known bleeding diathesis or any other significant condition or circumstance that may put her at risk because of participation in the study, or may influence the result of the study, or her ability to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old female presents to the emergency department with acute onset of chest pain and shortness of breath. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She denies any recent travel or immobilization, and has no personal or family history of clotting disorders. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. On physical examination, she appears anxious and in respiratory distress. Her vital signs are: blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 100 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. Auscultation of the chest reveals decreased breath sounds and crackles in the left lower lobe. The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable. Based on the patient's symptoms and clinical presentation, the emergency physician suspects a possible pulmonary embolism (PE). The patient is considered to have a low clinical pretest probability of PE based on the gestalt. The physician explains to the patient that she may be eligible to participate in a study comparing two different diagnostic strategies for low risk patients suspected of having a PE. The patient agrees to participate in the study and provides written informed consent.

55-year-old female with a history of menopause and complaints of dyspareunia for the past 8 months. The patient reports pain during intercourse with a pain score of 6 on the visual analog pain scale. The patient underwent a gynecological examination and was diagnosed with trophic vagina. She has no history of neurological disorders or urinary tract infections. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of physical therapy intervention techniques in the improvement of dyspareunia in climacteric women.

A 45-year-old Hispanic woman presented with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years, which is well-controlled with Lisinopril 10 mg daily. She has a BMI of 33 kg/m2, and her fasting glucose was found to be elevated at 115 mg/dL on a recent routine blood test. She reports no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and she is a non-smoker. She is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. She is a homemaker and lives with her husband and two children. Her physical examination was unremarkable except for mild obesity. Her laboratory tests revealed a HOMA2-IR index of 2.3, confirming the presence of insulin resistance. She gave informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, immunological or hematological disorders, or renal impairment. She is not taking any anticoagulants or chronic systemic glucocorticoid therapy. She has not participated in any other clinical trial in the last month. She is able to comply with the protocol and has no other factors that would prevent her from completing the study.

A 50-year-old male patient with a history of heavy alcohol intake presents with jaundice, malaise, and loss of appetite. The patient has not been able to work for the past 2 weeks due to his symptoms. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication for the same. He has been diagnosed with alcoholic hepatitis based on his AST:ALT ratio of >2:1 and a serum bilirubin level of 45 mg/dl. He has been started on conventional steroid therapy with Wysolone® 40mg once a day for 7 days but has been non-responsive to the same. He has no history of previous liver disease or liver-related surgery. He denies any history of intravenous drug use or blood transfusions. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He has no history of recent travel or any other infectious disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume non-prescription drugs. He is eligible for the study as he is non-responsive to conventional steroid therapy and is steroid-ineligible.

The patient is a 28-year-old primigravida woman who is currently 39 weeks pregnant. She is experiencing mild to moderate pain in her lower back and abdomen. She has no prior history of chronic pain or any other significant medical conditions. She has a normal BMI and no allergies to medications. She has not received any narcotic medication within the past 3 hours. She is interested in receiving a labor epidural for pain relief during delivery. She is fully informed of the study procedures and has consented to participate. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease with an estimated GFR of 50mL/min/1.73m2. He is part of a high-risk group for developing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is scheduled for a contrast-enhanced CT scan for HCC diagnosis or surveillance. He has no history of congestive hepatopathy or dialysis, and venous access on his forearm is available. However, he has a dental implant and a hip prosthesis, and there may be anticipated beam hardening artifact due to the prosthesis. There are no other relative or absolute contraindications of contrast-enhanced CT except for his chronic kidney disease.

A 52-year-old female patient who underwent bilateral radiotherapy of the neck two years ago due to nasopharyngeal carcinoma. She has been experiencing a reduction of salivation and hyposalivation, with a flow rate of 0.15 ml/min for the past few months. She has been graded 2 on the xerostomy grading scale and has been taking xerogenic medication for the past 6 months. She has a negative history of cancer in the last 2 years and does not have any other diseases of the salivary glands such as Sjögren's syndrome or sialolithiasis. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and has no local infection. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not taking any anticoagulants. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old Thai male who has been using injection drugs for the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for HIV prevention. He has a Thai National Identification Card and has had a non-reactive HIV oral fluid test within the past 2 weeks. His laboratory values are within the required range as follows: Hemoglobin 10 gm/dL, ALT and AST within normal limits, total bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, serum amylase within normal limits, serum phosphorus 2.0 mg/dL, and calculated creatinine clearance 80 mL/min. He is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse or use effective contraception during the trial, and is willing to participate in DOT or monthly follow-up for at least 12 months. He has no history of significant renal, liver, or bone diseases and is not currently taking any prescription medication. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. He is informed about the study and willing to provide consent for participation.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a history of alcohol dependence. He reports a strong craving for alcohol, which often leads to binge drinking episodes. He has tried to quit drinking on his own several times, but has been unsuccessful. He is not currently seeking treatment for his alcohol use and is able to maintain abstinence for two days without the aid of detox medications. He drinks hard liquor/spirits and does not have an aversion to this form of alcohol. He is able to read and understand questionnaires and informed consent. He lives within 50 miles of the study site. He does not have any metal objects in his head or neck and has no history of claustrophobia leading to significant clinical anxiety symptoms, making him eligible for the fMRI imaging sub-study. He does not meet DSM-IV criteria for any other psychoactive substance dependence disorder, and has no history of opiate abuse or a positive urine drug screen for opiates. He has not used any psychoactive substances (except marijuana and nicotine) within the last 30 days, and has not used marijuana within the last seven days. He does not meet DSM-IV criteria for current axis I disorders of major depression, panic disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, bipolar affective disorder, schizophrenia, dissociative disorders, and eating disorders, any other psychotic disorder, or an organic mental disorder. He does not have current suicidal ideation or homicidal ideation, and does not need maintenance or acute treatment with any psychoactive medication including anti-seizure medications. He is not currently using disulfiram, naltrexone, or acamprosate. He does not have any clinically significant medical problems such as cardiovascular, renal, gastrointestinal, or endocrine problems that would impair participation or limit medication ingestion. He does not have a past history of alcohol-related medical illnesses such as gastrointestinal bleeding, pancreatitis, peptic ulcer, hepatic cirrhosis, or alcoholic hepatitis. His SGPT Alanine transaminase (ALT) and SGOT Aspartate transaminase (AST) are within normal limits at screening. He is a male of child-bearing potential who is not pregnant or nursing and is using a reliable form of birth control. He does not have current charges pending for a violent crime (not including DUI related offenses), and has a stable living situation.

This is a 50-year-old male with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. He is currently taking metformin and amlodipine for his medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and is otherwise healthy. He has not had any major illnesses or surgeries in the past 6 months. He has a primary care physician who manages his diabetes and hypertension.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe endometriosis after undergoing laparoscopic surgery. She has a history of chronic pelvic pain that has been unresponsive to previous treatments. Her BMI is 25 kg/m². She is sexually abstinent and willing to use mechanical or sterilization methods of contraception throughout the study. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and has provided written informed consent. She has not used GnRH therapy in the last 6 months and has not used any hormonal contraception, selective estrogen receptor modulators, progestins, estrogens, steroids, or ovulation induction in the 4 weeks prior to inclusion into the study. She has no significant abnormalities in physical or laboratory examination, including renal and liver function. She has no history of venous thrombosis events, stroke, complicated migraine, or documented transient ischemic attack. She has no known hypersensitivity to any ingredient of the study medication and has not been treated with other aromatase inhibitors or other investigational drugs within the past 30 days. She is considered a reliable patient who is likely to comply with medical regimens.

A 35-year-old man with a BMI of 30.5 came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He works as an IT professional and spends most of his time sitting in front of a computer. He is married and has two children. He has no known medical conditions and is not on any medications. He smokes 5 cigarettes a day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has never been diagnosed with any neurological disorder and has no metal in his body. He is right-handed and has no history of eating disorders, depression, or drug addiction. He is interested in participating in the study as he wants to lose weight and start a new exercise regimen. He is willing to exercise but has never participated in a regular exercise program before.

A 45-year-old male office worker has been diagnosed with bladder stones and is scheduled for elective urologic surgery under spinal anesthesia. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control it. He has no history of any psychological or cardiac problems. The patient has never had spinal anesthesia before and is concerned about the potential side effects of intrathecal morphine, specifically pruritus. He has no known allergies to any medications. He does not take sedatives or narcotics. The patient is married and has two children. He is an occasional social drinker and does not smoke. He is generally healthy and physically active, enjoying jogging and cycling in his free time.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer. He has not received any prior chemotherapy treatment for colon cancer. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale and is otherwise healthy, with no history of central nervous system involvement or active neurological disease. He has normal hematological, hepatic, and renal function, with a total bilirubin level within 2 times the upper normal limit (UNL) and AST, ALT, and AP levels within 5 times the UNL. He has signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He does not have a history of radiation therapy, and his medical conditions, including diabetes mellitus and hypertension, are well-controlled.

The patient is a 25-year-old Saudi Arabian woman who has been experiencing fatigue, joint pain, and rashes for the past six months. She has a history of recurrent oral ulcers and hair loss. She has not received a definitive diagnosis for her symptoms but has been told by her primary care physician that it may be lupus. She has no family history of lupus, but her parents are first cousins. She is married, has two children, and works as a teacher. She is interested in participating in this study to gain a better understanding of her condition and contribute to the advancement of lupus research in Saudi Arabia.

49-year-old woman with a history of alcohol use disorder and depression, currently engaged in alcohol treatment. She has experienced multiple relapses in the past and is seeking an intervention that will help her manage her negative emotions and alcohol cravings during early recovery. She has not engaged in regular physical activity in the last 6 months and is interested in exploring exercise as an alternate coping strategy. She has access to a computer connected to the internet and is willing to use a Fitbit device and mobile application to track her progress. She is not currently pregnant or intending to be pregnant in the next 12 weeks.

A 38-year-old male patient was diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome by his physician. He has been experiencing dry mouth and dry eyes for over 6 months. He also has difficulty swallowing and has lost some weight in the past few months. He is not currently taking any medications for his condition. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that studies saliva samples to learn more about how Sjogren's syndrome affects the mouth and salivary glands. He understands that he will undergo saliva collection and that the study will use salivary proteomics to identify multiple proteins in saliva and discover if there are protein patterns unique to specific diseases. The study will also evaluate the possible use of salivary proteomics for early diagnosis and prognosis and treatment of Sjogren's syndrome. He is willing to undergo the required procedures and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 42-year-old male who has been experiencing loud and habitual snoring for more than 6 months, as reported by his live-in partner. He has no history of sleep apnea, and his BMI is within the normal range (25). He speaks fluent English and is able to complete daily neuromuscular stimulation. He does not have any other sleep disorders, tongue or lip piercing, pacemaker, or implanted medical devices. He has not received any treatment for snoring or sleep apnea in the past 6 months, and he has not undergone any oral or pharyngeal surgery other than dental. He does not have any craniofacial skeletal or muscular abnormalities. He has not experienced any driving or other accidents due to sleepiness, and his Epworth score is 10. He is not pregnant, and he does not have any cardiac, pulmonary, renal, neurologic, neuromuscular, or hepatic diseases. He is not taking any medications with sedative or myorelaxant properties, or effects on cardiac or pulmonary function. He does not consume substantial alcohol or use illicit drugs. He does not have any psychiatric disorders other than mild anxiety. During the baseline polysomnography, he snored for more than 20% of the total sleep time.

45 yo F with a history of endodontic failure in the mandibular left first molar leading to caries and tooth fracture. Patient has a regular dental check-up and has a FMPS and FMBS score of less than 25%. She is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic with no known bone metabolic disorders. She has no acute infections at the site of extraction and no history of malignancy, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy. No periapical pathology such as granulomas, cysts, hypercementosis, or ankylosis have been identified in the extraction site. The patient has adequate keratinized tissue to allow for flap management and has adjacent teeth on either side of the extraction site. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no medical conditions that contraindicate surgical interventions. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo socket preservation either with autogenous demineralised dentin(DDM) or bovine derived xenograft(DBM).

35-year-old female with a diagnosis of fibromyalgia according to the ACR 1990 criteria, presenting with chronic widespread body pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances. She has a history of seeking frequent medical attention and has tried various medications for fibromyalgia without significant improvement. She has not taken any fibromyalgia-specific medications for one month and is currently taking only paracetamol 750 mg as needed. She is interested in participating in a 16-week study to evaluate the effectiveness of a supervised resistance muscular exercise (RME) and walking program (WP) on reducing her pain. She will undergo medical and rheumatology evaluations to ensure she is eligible for physical activity and will complete questionnaires to assess her FMS symptoms at baseline, 8 weeks, 16 weeks, and 28 weeks.

A 56-year-old male presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past 2 months. He reports occasional chest pain and weight loss of approximately 10 pounds in the same period. He has a history of smoking for the past 30 years, with an estimated 1 pack per day. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds in the right lung base with no palpable lymph nodes. His vital signs are within normal limits. Blood tests show mild leukocytosis with neutrophilia and anemia. A chest X-ray shows a large mass in the right lung. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for isolating circulating tumor cells for early diagnosis and screening. He is willing to sign the informed consent form.

A 32-year-old female who has been experiencing excessive worry and anxiety for the last 6 months. She reports difficulty controlling her worries and feeling restless and on edge most of the time. She has trouble falling asleep and staying asleep due to racing thoughts. She also experiences physical symptoms such as muscle tension, headaches, and stomach discomfort. She has been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and has been receiving treatment from a primary care physician for the past 3 months. She has not received any previous treatment for anxiety or depression. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at assessing remission rates in patients treated for generalized anxiety disorder in primary and specialized care. She is currently an out-patient and consents to participate in the study.

A 54-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. Computed tomography (CT) scan of the brain showed a large clot blocking the blood flow to the right middle cerebral artery. He was immediately started on tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and transferred to the neurocritical care unit for further management. Due to the severity of the stroke, he required mechanical ventilation and was placed on sedation. He has been in the NICU for 72 hours and is expected to need mechanical ventilation for at least another week. His legal representative has consented him to participate in the MODERNISE trial to compare the safety, feasibility, and potential benefits of moderate vs. deep sedation in patients with severe ischemic stroke. He meets all the eligibility criteria including age, ventilated with expected need of further artificial ventilation for more than 72h, and expected ICU-LOS of more than 5 days. He does not have any exclusion criteria such as pregnancy, severe sepsis, or refractory intracranial hypertension.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing sudden episodes of dizziness and vertigo for the past few weeks. She feels disoriented and unstable during these episodes and has had to take time off from work. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no known allergies. She has no history of head injury or ear surgery. The patient's family history is negative for any ear or balance disorders. Upon physical examination, the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre is positive, confirming a diagnosis of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She has no contraindications to canalith repositioning procedures or betahistine.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing a persistent cough for the past 3 months. She has also been losing weight and experiencing night sweats. Upon testing, she has been diagnosed with multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). She is HIV-negative and has no history of allergies or intolerances to any medication. She has not taken any medication for TB in the past. Her liver enzymes are within normal range, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no previous history of cardiac or syncopal episodes. She is willing to use appropriate contraceptive measures and sign the informed consent form for the study. She lives in an area where the local standard of care for MDR-TB is available, but she is willing to participate in the trial to potentially receive a more effective and less toxic treatment regimen. She is willing to travel to the approved site for blood draws as part of the PKPD sub-study.

The patient is a 3-year-old girl scheduled to undergo elective surgery at Xi'an Children's Hospital. She weighs 12 kg and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of I. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her parents report that she is generally healthy and active, with no known allergies. She has fasted according to the preoperative instructions and has received premedication with intranasal dexmedetomidine. She is accompanied by her parents, who will provide consent for her participation in the study. The anesthesiologists responsible for the procedure have at least one year of experience in inserting supraglottic airway devices in pediatric patients. The patient will be randomly assigned to the appropriate group based on her weight, and the appropriate sized i-gel device will be prepared according to the manufacturer's guidelines. The insertion of the device will be monitored for ease of insertion, oropharyngeal leak pressure, and other relevant outcomes. The patient will be monitored throughout the procedure for any complications or adverse events, and will be followed up after the procedure to assess any postoperative complications.

42 yo F with a history of hallux valgus deformity, experiencing pain and difficulty with walking in shoes, seeks treatment for surgical correction. Past Medical History: - None reported. Current Medications: - None reported. Allergies: - None reported. Social History: - Non-smoker, occasional alcohol consumption. Physical Exam: - Visible hallux valgus deformity with pain and tenderness upon palpation. Patient is otherwise healthy and fit for surgery. The patient has no peripheral circulatory disorders or foot skin lesions and is not allergic to local anesthetics. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the comparative evaluation of two different post-operative analgesia after hallux valgus correction.

A 55-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with esophageal cancer and is scheduled for an elective esophagectomy. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 25. He is concerned about the potential complications and recovery after the surgery and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. At the time of surgery, a jejunal feeding tube will be placed, which will be used for post-operative nutrition.

A 27-year-old female anaesthesia resident in her 2nd year of training is interested in participating in a simulation-based training study. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She denies any history of cardiac disease or endocrine disorder. She does not use beta-blockers or any other medication regularly, except for her hypertension medication. She reports no recent stressful or traumatic life events and is not pregnant. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to improve her skills and knowledge in the field and is willing to undergo the required saliva and performance tests during simulation sessions. She understands the potential benefits and risks of participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

An 70 yo F residing in Lyon or Saint-Etienne cities who is a beneficiary or affiliated with the security social program. The patient should not have any heart rate disorders or a pacemaker, nor be a tobacco user or exposed to second-hand smoke. The patient should not have morbid obesity (BMI > 30), insulin-dependent diabetes, or any chronic disease on treatment or antiarrhythmic treatments. The patient must be willing to sign the information note for the study.

A 42-year-old female with a history of Cushing's disease, who has undergone surgery to remove the pituitary tumor causing her hypercortisolism. Despite achieving biological cure, she has been experiencing persistent symptoms including fatigue, difficulty losing weight, and high blood pressure. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between hypercortisolism and the development of cardiovascular disease. She has no history of myocardial infarction, congenital cardiomyopathy, or adrenocorticotropic hormone-independent hyperadrenocorticism. She is not currently being treated with corticosteroids or insulin. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no specific contraindications to Nuclear Magnetic Resonance imaging. She is able to provide informed consent.

A 45 year old man was admitted to the hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and a family history of coronary artery disease. He is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. Upon admission, he was placed on telemetry monitoring and underwent various tests including EKG, blood tests, and imaging studies. The results showed signs of subclinical critical illness that were not previously detected through conventional clinical predictors. He will be enrolled in the CHAOS study to validate predictive algorithms and identify subclinical signatures of illness to prevent adverse events and provide early, more effective therapies.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been taking an atypical antipsychotic medication for the past year, but still experiences persistent symptoms such as hearing voices and having false beliefs. He lives in an apartment with his roommate and has difficulty with everyday functioning, including managing his finances and maintaining his living space. He has visual and auditory ability intact and reads at the 7th grade level. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past 6 months. He has not received Cognitive Adaptation Training (CAT) in the past 2 years and is not currently being treated by an ACT team. He has moderate delusions and hallucinations according to the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). He is interested in participating in the study to improve both his symptoms and functional outcomes.

A 72-year-old Caucasian man reports feeling weak and tired lately, and has noticed a decline in his ability to walk long distances without stopping. He reports feeling unsteady on his feet and has experienced a few falls in the past 3 months. He is also afraid of falling again. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He lives alone and is retired. He is able to walk independently but is slower than he used to be. He has not been physically active for several years due to his sedentary lifestyle. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his physical function and reduce his risk of falls. His Mini-Mental Status Examination score is 28.

A 55-year-old male presents with moderate urinary symptoms including frequency, urgency, and hesitancy. He has not taken any medication for these symptoms in the past 8 weeks. The patient has no history of cancer or major organic diseases. The patient is able to read and complete the questionnaire and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 12 weeks. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. There is no history of pelvic radiation therapy or pelvic surgery, except for a prostate biopsy three years ago which was negative for cancer. The patient has no history of epilepsy, convulsions, liver or kidney disease, endocrine disease, mental illness, alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has a residual urine volume of less than 250 mL, and the lower urinary tract symptoms are related to prostatic hypertrophy, as determined by medical history.

An 80-year-old woman was admitted to the internal medicine department of a suburban Parisian hospital with complaints of weakness, fatigue, and abdominal pain. She is widowed and lives alone in her apartment. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis and takes medication for both conditions. She has two children who live in another city and visit her occasionally. She has difficulty walking and uses a cane for support. Her vision is impaired due to cataracts, but she refuses to undergo surgery. She speaks French fluently and has no history of cognitive impairment or dementia. She has never been screened for psycho-cognitive troubles before. She has no known allergies to any medications. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is willing to participate in the study and has consented to undergo the screening for psycho-cognitive troubles.

The patient is a 35-year-old premenopausal woman who has recently been diagnosed with early stage breast cancer. She has had at least one menstrual period in the last 12 months and has been pregnant once in the past. She is fluent in English and is capable of participating in the informed consent process. The patient has not yet started systemic treatment, but is planning to start Tamoxifen as her only form of treatment within the next month. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand how cancer treatment may affect her sexual and reproductive function. She is open to having blood draws to assess the impact of treatment on her ovaries and fertility, but understands that this is optional.

A 25-year-old male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 presented with no known medical conditions or allergies. He has not taken any prescription medication in the last two weeks. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is willing to consume a standard FDA specified high-fat breakfast before taking the medication. He has no history of migraines in the past 12 months. He is able to provide informed consent and willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HF-PEF). She has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. She has never had a heart attack or any other significant heart problems. Her recent echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 55%. She is scheduled for catheter ablation of AF and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She does not have any significant valvular heart disease or coronary artery disease. She has not had any coronary interventions or bypass surgery in the past 90 days. She does not have cardiomyopathy, pericardiac disease, or significant pulmonary hypertension. She does not have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or any other non-cardiac condition associated with limited physical capacity. She is not pregnant and does not have any limitations for adequate performance of stress echocardiography. She is willing to undergo left atrial biomarker measurements and periprocedural hemodynamic measurements.

We are seeking adolescents between the ages of 11 and 18 years old who have been diagnosed with spastic cerebral palsy (GMFCS levels I-III). Participants should have a stable health status for 6 weeks prior to screening and the cognitive ability to follow exercise instructions either in written or electronic format. Participants must have access to the internet at home and be able to access the exercise's website/app via Personal computer (PC), laptop, or mobile app. Participants must be able to understand and follow verbal commands in English as the intervention and questionnaires are only available in English. Participants should not have had any other neurological disorders that may cause further decline in balance and walking abilities (head injury, vestibular dysfunction, or Spinal cord injury), or any musculoskeletal condition that would interfere with the safe performance of the exercise intervention or testing protocol. Participants should not have any scheduled surgical operations or castings during study period or be scheduled for intensive rehabilitation during the 8 weeks of intervention. Participants will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group or control group and will receive exercise videos and live consultation sessions or exercise videos only for 8 weeks. All participants will use a HIPAA compliant telehealth provider (Physitrack website/app). Prior approval from parents/guardians is required for participating in this study.

A healthy 3-month-old baby boy who was born at full term is being fed by both breast milk and formula. The baby is growing well and has no known medical issues. His mother is a healthy 32-year-old woman who exclusively breastfed the baby for the first 2 weeks of life before introducing formula into his diet due to work-related reasons. The mother has no known medical issues and is not on any long-term medication. The family has no history of cardiovascular disease or any other chronic illness. The baby's development and growth are being monitored by the pediatrician. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the lipid profiles of infants on different feeding regimens and to assess the correlation between the babies' lipid profiles and their mothers'.

A 42-year-old female with a history of acute myeloid leukemia who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) 4 months ago from an unrelated donor. She was in complete remission at the time of transplantation. The conditioning regimen was myeloablative. She developed extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) involving her skin, mouth, and gut. She has not had any episodes of acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Her current treatment regimen, which includes prednisone and tacrolimus has not resulted in any significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has provided written consent. Her creatinine level is within normal limits and she has no active infections. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 30-year-old African American male presents with a history of sickle cell disease and chronic pain. He reports experiencing pain on most days, with the pain being moderate to severe in intensity. He has been taking daily opioids for pain management for the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore other treatment options for his chronic pain. He is proficient in English and owns a mobile phone. He is married and works as a cashier in a local retail store. He has a supportive family and a close friend network. He desires to learn more about the management of his chronic pain and seeks to connect with other patients with sickle cell disease to share experiences and learn from them. He is motivated to learn new coping skills and techniques to manage his pain and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent a double-lung transplantation 6 months ago due to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and decreased exercise tolerance over the past few weeks. The patient is a former smoker and quit smoking 2 years ago. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. His medications include amlodipine 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and prednisone 10 mg daily. The patient has no known drug allergies. He has been scheduled to undergo a bronchoscopy with transbronchial lung biopsy as part of his routine post-transplant surveillance. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient has a platelet count of 110 K/microL, INR of 1.1, and no known bleeding diathesis. He has not used any anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication within the specified time frames. His estimated glomerular filtration rate is 60 mL/min. He has no evidence of moderate to severe pulmonary hypertension. The patient has not had any previous TBLB-related airway bleeding complications. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria for the application of topical epinephrine.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy Caucasian adults, both male and female, aged between 18 to 50 years old, with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.50 kg/m2 to 30.00 kg/m2. Participants should not be current or ex-smokers and should have no clinically significant diseases or abnormalities in their medical history, physical examination, or electrocardiogram (ECG). Women who are pregnant or lactating are excluded from the study, as well as those with a history of significant hypersensitivity to olmesartan and HCTZ or any related products, significant gastrointestinal, liver, kidney, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, neurological, psychiatric, endocrine, immunologic, or dermatologic disease, or any condition that is known to interfere with drug absorption, metabolism, or excretion. Participants should not have taken olmesartan medoxomil or HCTZ in the 28 days prior to the first study drug administration,

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been struggling with ADHD symptoms for several years.
