Despite medication, he still experiences poor attention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity, which have negatively impacted his academic performance and relationships with peers. He is fluent in English and has an IQ above 80. He has no history of mania, psychosis, or bipolar disorder. He has not undergone electroconvulsive therapy or vagus nerve stimulation and has not been diagnosed with post-concussive syndrome or Autism Spectrum Disorder. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that tests the efficacy of rTMS in reducing ADHD symptoms. His parents are supportive of his participation and have provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing mild to moderate stress urinary incontinence for the past year. She has not undergone any previous pelvic floor exercises or surgery for incontinence or prolapse. Her incontinence severity will be categorized by the four-level Sandvik severity index score (SIS), and her score is 4. She has a wish for treatment and gives her voluntary informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She is not pregnant and has no vaginal bleeding, injuries or infection in the treated area. She is interested in a non-invasive treatment option and is willing to try vaginal laser treatment.

A 26 year old woman is seeking treatment for her Behçet's disease. She has been experiencing recurrent oral and genital ulcers, as well as joint pain and swelling for over a year. She was diagnosed with Behçet's disease 6 months ago after being referred to a rheumatologist for further evaluation of her symptoms. She has tried colchicine and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the past, but her symptoms have not improved. She has not had any major vessel or neurological involvement yet. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She has no history of allergy to immunosuppressive medications. She is willing to use adequate contraceptive measures during the study period and agrees to complete a prophylactic TB treatment course if necessary. She is not currently taking any systemic biologic therapy or cyclophosphamide. She is affiliated with a social security benefit plan.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of depression and anxiety. She has been experiencing involuntary muscle contractions in her left arm and hand for the past year, which have been affecting her daily activities. She has been diagnosed with psychogenic dystonia by her neurologist. The patient has not received any prior treatment with botulinum toxin. She is currently taking sertraline for her depression and anxiety. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study. She has no history of myasthenia gravis, Eaton-Lambert syndrome, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis or any other neuromuscular disorders. She is otherwise healthy and meets all the inclusion criteria of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old female diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 2 years ago. She has been following a diet regimen and her fasting serum glucose levels range from 8-12 mmol/L. Her HbA1c is currently at 10%. She has no history of liver or renal impairment. She has been taking metformin 1000mg twice daily as prescribed by her physician. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or other significant medical conditions. She is willing to give written consent to participate in the study and is able to follow the prescribed medication regimen of taking 3 x 2 ml of the study medication before meals for up to 36 months.

The patient is a healthy male volunteer between the ages of 20 to 45 years old. He weighs over 50kg and is within ±20% of his ideal body weight. He does not have any clinically significant disorders in his liver, kidney, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine or CNS systems, nor does he have a medical history of malignant tumor or psychological disease. He has not had any gastrointestinal or acid restraining surgeries, gastric/esophagus surgeries (excluding appendectomy, hernia surgery) or a history of hypersensitivity to drugs or clinically significant allergic disease. His blood chemistry values are within normal range, with SGOT and SGPT levels being less than 1.5 times the upper normal limit. He has not taken any usual dose prescription drugs within 14 days before treatment or any OTC drugs within 7 days before treatment. He has not participated in another clinical trial within 2 months before enrolling in this study, nor has he donated whole blood within 2 months or component blood within 1 month or donated within 1 month before the treatment. He does not drink more than 21 units of alcohol per week and is able to abstain from alcohol during hospitalization. He has not smoked within 3 months before the treatment. He has not consumed any beverages containing grapefruits within 24 hours before hospitalization, nor will he consume any during hospitalization. He has not consumed any beverages containing caffeine during hospitalization. He is suitable for this study according to the investigatory consideration of the clinical trial specialists.

A 50-year-old woman presents with a new diagnosis of stage II breast cancer. She underwent lumpectomy and is now scheduled to receive breast radiotherapy to 50 Gy. She has fair skin and no history of skin disorders. She currently takes lisinopril for hypertension and a multivitamin. She has no other comorbidities and leads an active lifestyle. She is married and has two adult children. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help protect her skin during radiotherapy.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been suffering from vitiligo for 5 years. She has multiple depigmented patches on her trunk, arms, and legs. Her disease has affected her quality of life and she is very self-conscious about her appearance. She has tried multiple topical treatments in the past but with no significant improvement. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no allergies to medications. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her vitiligo patches have been stable for the past 6 months and she has not received any treatment for vitiligo within the past 4 weeks. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of intralesional corticosteroids in the treatment of vitiligo.

A 25 year old healthy male with no history of medical or psychiatric disorders and not taking any medication comes to the clinic. He is fluent in Portuguese and has not experienced any acute or chronic pain in the past. He has not undergone any neurological surgery or has any metallic implants in the brain. He is interested in participating in the study to investigate the effect of the combination of Melatonin and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on pain threshold and neuroplasticity. He signs the informed consent and is willing to undergo quantitative sensory testing, conditioned pain modulation-task, serum Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) assessment, and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) assessment. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to follow the protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with bipolar II disorder. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past six months, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities he used to enjoy. He also complains of fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and sleep disturbances. He has been taking lamotrigine and quetiapine as mood stabilizers for the past year with no recent changes in medication. He has not experienced hypomania or mania for the past six months. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is currently unemployed and lives with his parents. He has completed high school and has no history of ophthalmic or physical diseases. He is right-handed and willing to participate in the study. His HAM-D score is 22.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with COPD and has a smoking history of more than ten pack-years. He has moderate to severe airway obstruction with an FEV 1 of 60% of predicted normal and FEV1 of 68% of FVC. He has not had an upper respiratory tract infection or COPD exacerbation in the past six weeks. He is currently taking Atrovent® inhalation aerosol (21 mcg per puff) and is able to demonstrate an improvement in FEV1 >=015% within one hour after inhalation of two puffs. He is able to satisfactorily administer the medication, perform pulmonary function tests, and maintain records during the study period as required in the protocol. He has signed an informed consent form prior to participation in the trial. He does not have any significant disease other than COPD, and his baseline hematology, blood chemistry, and urinalysis are within normal limits. He does not have a history of asthma, allergic rhinitis, or atopy, and his blood eosinophil count is below 600/mm³. He does not have a recent history of myocardial infarction or heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia requiring therapy, or chronic daytime oxygen therapy. He does not have known active tuberculosis, cancer within the last five years, or a history of life-threatening pulmonary obstruction, cystic fibrosis, or bronchiectasis. He has not undergone thoracotomy with pulmonary resection. He does not have an upper respiratory tract infection or COPD exacerbation at the time of screening. He is not allergic to anticholinergic drugs, does not have symptomatic prostatic hypertrophy or bladder neck obstruction, and does not have narrow-angle glaucoma. He is not currently taking cromolyn sodium or nedocromil sodium, nor is he taking antihistamines. He is not pregnant or nursing, and he is using a medically approved means of contraception (condoms). He has not taken an investigational drug within one month or 6 half-lives prior to the screening visit, nor is he currently enrolled in another research study. He does not have a history of and/or active alcohol or drug abuse.

A 46-year-old man who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring for the past year. He has been referred to a sleep clinic where he was diagnosed with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and a concomitant patent foramen ovale (PFO). The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control his blood pressure. He has no other significant medical history and is a non-smoker. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the impact of percutaneous PFO closure on his nocturnal hypoxemia and apnea/hypopnea, pulmonary and systemic artery pressure, endothelial function and arterial stiffness. He has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent for study participation.

A 29 year old male veteran who was recently released from prison after serving a sentence for drug-related charges. He has a history of substance use disorder and has been diagnosed with depression and anxiety. He has had difficulty finding employment and stable housing since his release. He has a supportive family and is motivated to make positive changes in his life. He is willing to participate in a program that will assist him in his transition back into society.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who was involved in a minor car accident. He was brought to the emergency department with mild head injury and a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 14. CT scan of his head showed minor injuries, including a subarachnoid hemorrhage measuring less than 2 mm and a linear skull fracture. He is not currently taking any medication or supplements. He has a past medical history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. His family history is negative for any neurological diseases or conditions. He has no history of bleeding disorders and is not currently on any blood thinning medications. He has no other significant injuries from the car accident.

An 68 year old woman has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, lack of energy, and reduced interest in activities she previously enjoyed. She has also been experiencing anxiety and worries frequently. She has no prior history of mental health issues and is not currently taking any medications. She lives alone and has been feeling increasingly isolated since retiring from work. Her primary care physician referred her to a community mental health team for psychological support. She has completed the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) and scored 12 on the depression subscale. She has also scored 9 on the anxiety subscale. She speaks fluent English and is able to travel to the service for one-to-one psychotherapy. She has no significant cognitive deficits, as confirmed by the MoCA administered by the team.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of stage IV non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. She had previously received one line of platinum-based chemotherapy, but experienced disease progression evaluated by RECIST 1.1. She presents to the clinic with worsening fatigue and shortness of breath. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status score is 1. She has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She has at least 3 measurable lesions based on RECIST 1.1, with at least 2 of them being treatable by SBRT. Her laboratory values show an absolute neutrophil count of 1.8x10^9/L, platelets of 100x10^9/L, hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, total bilirubin of 1.2×ULN, AST and ALT of 1.5×ULN, creatinine of 1.0×ULN, and dipstick proteinuria of less than 2+. She has an International normalized ratio of 1.2 × ULN, and normal prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time. She is not postmenopausal and agrees to use an adequate method of contraception. She has no history of inherited bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy that increases the risk of bleeding, uncontrolled hypertension, or clinically significant cardiovascular disease. She has no significant vascular disease and no malignancies other than NSCLC within the past 2 years. She has not received corticosteroid therapy at a dose equivalent to 10 mg prednisone per day or any other systemic immunosuppressive therapy within 14 days prior to randomization. She has no active HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. She has no non-healing wound, active peptic ulcer, or bone fracture. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she does not intend to become pregnant during the study. She has not been treated with any other investigational agent or participated in another clinical trial within 28 days prior to randomization. She has no evidence of ongoing or active infection requiring IV antibiotics or any other disease, neurological, or metabolic dysfunction that would contraindicate the use of an investigational drug or put her at high risk for treatment-related complications.

This is a 38 year old female who was recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer in her family. She underwent a mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection and was found to have metastasis to 11 out of 15 lymph nodes. She completed 6 cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel. A PET scan showed residual disease in the breast and axilla, therefore she underwent a second surgery with removal of residual disease. She has no evidence of metastatic disease. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no comorbid conditions and her LVEF is 50%.

Pt is a 68yo F residing in an urban area of China. She lives alone and has completed middle school education. She reports feeling sad and helpless most days for the past 6 months, with decreased appetite and energy. She denies any suicidal ideation. She is able to communicate effectively and has a MMSE score of 22. She has no history of psychosis or other major medical conditions. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old female who is not planning to become pregnant. She has no history of significant medical or psychiatric illnesses and has not taken any prescription or non-prescription drugs or dietary supplements within the past 7 days. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 5 cigarettes per day. She has no history of substance or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. She has a body weight of 60 kg and a BMI of 22. She is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She has no history of gallbladder disease, megaloblastic anemia or folate deficiency. She has no clinically significant abnormalities as determined by medical history, physical examination, vital signs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECG), and clinical laboratory evaluation. Her veins are suitable for intravenous puncture or cannulation on either arm. She has not taken any moderate/strong inhibitors or inducers of Cytochromes P450 (CYP450) or transporters within 30 days prior to the first dose of study medication. She has not consumed grapefruit, grapefruit juice or grapefruit-related citrus fruits (e.g. Seville oranges, pomelos) within 30 days prior to the first dose of study medication. She has not ingested any poppy seeds within the 24 hours prior to screening. She has not used herbal supplements at least 30 days prior to the first dose of study medication. She has no history or presence of any cardiac conditions and no abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting ECG that may interfere with the interpretation of corrected QT interval (QTc) changes. She has no clinically important abnormalities in laboratory, vital signs or other safety findings. She is capable of fully understanding and complying with the requirements of the study and has signed the informed consent form prior to undergoing any study-related procedures.

50-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 3 years, with a history of poor glycemic control despite treatment with oral hypoglycemic agents. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. She is currently taking metformin and glipizide for diabetes, lisinopril for hypertension, and atorvastatin for dyslipidemia. She has a sedentary lifestyle and struggles with maintaining a healthy diet. She has completed high school education and is willing to attend an educational program for diabetes management. She has no history of chronic complications such as kidney failure, blindness, or limb amputation.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the past year. He frequently experiences a weak urinary stream, difficulty starting urination, and the need to urinate frequently, even at night. He has never sought medical attention for these symptoms but has been using over-the-counter herbal remedies for relief, which has not been effective. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of pelvic surgery, neurologic disease, or urethral obstruction. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 5 ng/ml, which is within normal range. He is willing to discontinue any current medication for BPH-LUTS or PDE5 inhibitors for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 45 year old female with a history of periodontal disease. She has noticed gum recession and increased tooth sensitivity over the past few months. Upon examination, there is a deep pocket with significant bone loss in the lower left molar area. The diagnosis of infrabony vertical defect is confirmed. The patient is otherwise healthy with no systemic diseases and is a non-smoker. She is not pregnant. The study team has explained the potential benefits and risks of the study, including the use of locally injected vitamin D as a non-surgical modality for periodontal regeneration. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. He has been using therapeutic doses of indacaterol, salmeterol, and placebo. He has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit smoking 5 years ago. The patient's BMI is within the range of 18 to 32. He has no significant illness other than respiratory in the past two weeks. The patient has no family history of a prolonged QT-interval syndrome or a prolonged QT-interval at screening. He is physically active, with a history of regular participation in exercise programs. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the study drug or drugs similar to the study drug. He has no history of immunocompromise or drug or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and follow the protocol-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who recently sustained a fracture to his left tibia during a sports activity. He has been experiencing significant pain and swelling in the affected area and is seeking medical attention. The patient has no known history of vascular or circulatory issues. He is not pregnant and is above the age of 16. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the blood supply to the fracture site using Doppler ultrasound.

56-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension who is scheduled to receive a kidney transplant from a deceased donor. He has been on dialysis for the past 2 years and is currently on the waiting list for a transplant. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension and has never undergone a previous transplant or pregnancy. He has not undergone any pre-transplantation desensitization protocols. The patient is willing to participate in the study to determine the impact of HLA-DQ mismatch on acute rejection of his kidney transplant.

A 70 year old woman visits the clinic with a history of knee pain for the past year. She reports that her pain started gradually and has worsened over time. She experiences pain, stiffness, and swelling in her left knee. The pain is aggravated by walking, standing, and climbing stairs. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by her physician. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of heart or lung disease, hypertension, diabetes, stroke, or other neurological or musculoskeletal disease. She is able to perform lower extremity resistance exercise, but her physical activity level has decreased due to her knee pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates chronic muscle disuse in the elderly and the effects of exercise rehabilitation on muscle function.

The patient is a 27 year old African American male who has been diagnosed with drug-resistant epilepsy for the past 5 years. Despite taking multiple anti-epileptic medications, he continues to have seizures on a regular basis, which has significantly impacted his quality of life. He is currently unemployed due to his condition and relies on his family for financial support. He has a history of head trauma from a car accident 10 years ago. His most recent MRI showed evidence of a focal lesion in the left temporal lobe, which is believed to be the epileptogenic zone. He has been referred for surgical evaluation and is being considered for resection of the epileptic focus. He is interested in participating in this study as a non-invasive alternative to intracranial EEG recordings. He is able to complete the necessary study forms and has no contraindications for MRI.

A 34-year-old female nurse working in the emergency department presents with symptoms of fatigue, anxiety, and difficulty sleeping. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and the increased workload and exposure to infected patients. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has not experienced any symptoms of COVID-19 but has been in close contact with several infected patients. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the physical and emotional impact of COVID-19 on healthcare workers. She speaks and understands written English.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer after a biopsy. The pathology report revealed a Gleason score of 4+3=7, placing the patient in a high-risk category. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient has been scheduled for prostate cancer removal surgery and has agreed to participate in this clinical trial. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and lie still for approximately 30 minutes during the 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT or PET/MRI scan. The patient has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to participate. There are no significant acute or chronic medical, neurologic, or psychiatric illnesses that would compromise his safety or ability to complete the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for the past 3 years. She has been managed with various antiarrhythmic medications, but her symptoms have not been well controlled. She experiences episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue that are affecting her quality of life. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in exploring minimally invasive surgical options for the treatment of her atrial fibrillation. She has no history of prior heart surgery and is willing to participate in the study. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including wearing a trans-telephonic monitor for approximately 1 month. She hopes that this study will provide valuable information regarding the efficacy of minimally invasive surgery for atrial fibrillation and potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 40-year-old male diagnosed with HIV infection 3 years ago. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years and is responding well to the treatment. However, he reports experiencing significant fatigue that affects his daily activities. He is fluent in English and has a smartphone and tablet. He has no other medical conditions that cause fatigue and is mentally competent to give informed consent. He does not have active psychosis or dementia, nor does he have suicidal ideation with clear intent. He is not currently dependent on any substances.

A 28-year-old healthy man who works as an engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the safety and tolerability of a new medication. He exercises regularly and has no underlying medical conditions. He has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 and does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively. He has never participated in another clinical trial before and takes no medications. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not recently donated blood. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and is willing to abstain from consuming alcoholic beverages for the duration of the study. He is not surgically sterilized and is not currently in a relationship with a woman of childbearing potential.

A 45-year-old male veteran presented at the VA outpatient clinic with a history of substance use disorder. He has been using opioids and alcohol regularly for the past six years and has attempted to quit multiple times without success. He reported experiencing withdrawal symptoms, such as sweating, shakiness, and nausea. The patient has no known cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent. He is interested in receiving help for his addiction and is willing to participate in a clinical trial exploring the effectiveness of self-help groups (SHGs) for substance use disorders. The patient is available for follow-up appointments at 6 months and 1 year to monitor his progress and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 15-year-old Hispanic female who has not yet received all three doses of the HPV vaccine. She is accompanied by her mother who is also a Hispanic and can converse in both English and Spanish. The patient and her mother report that they have limited knowledge about the HPV vaccine and would like to learn more about it. They are willing to participate in an educational intervention to improve their understanding of the vaccine and make an informed decision about the vaccination. The patient is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is currently in high school and is actively involved in extracurricular activities. She is interested in pursuing a career in nursing. The mother is a homemaker and has two other children who have not yet been vaccinated against HPV. Both the patient and her mother are excited to participate in the study and contribute to improving the health of their community.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD by a specialist child psychiatrist. He has no history of Autism Spectrum Disorder or psychosis, and no significant brain traumas or major medical conditions that would interfere with his ability to complete testing or take psychostimulants. His IQ score is above 80 as per the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC-IV). He is proficient in both English and French. The child is currently undergoing 3 months of treatment consisting of medication and psychological, behavioural, and academic interventions tailored to his individual needs. Following this treatment, he will be randomly assigned to either community follow up or medication monitoring plus tailored case management follow up for two years. The child's parent and teacher will be asked to complete interviews and comprehensive assessments pertaining to ADHD symptoms and various areas of functioning at 6-month intervals during both types of follow-up.

The patient is a 25-year-old Japanese male who is generally healthy and has no history of chronic diseases. He has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. He has not been diagnosed with HIV, HBV, or HCV, nor has he been exposed to SARS-CoV-2. He does not have a history of drug abuse or alcohol dependence. The patient has not undergone any surgeries except for a routine appendectomy. He does not have any symptoms of cardiovascular disease, hematological disorders or gastrointestinal disorders. His liver function tests are within normal range. The patient has not donated blood or plasma recently, nor has he taken any investigational drugs or devices in the last 30 days. He does not use any tobacco or nicotine-containing products. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has given informed consent.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman presents with a blood pressure of 142/92 mmHg and proteinuria of 1+ at 34 weeks of gestation. She was diagnosed with mild preeclampsia and her platelet count is 170,000/mL. She has no relevant medical history or allergies. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated until now, with regular prenatal care and good fetal growth. She is interested in receiving neuraxial analgesia for pain relief during labor and delivery. She is informed that the platelet count needs to be monitored before initiating neuraxial analgesia and that thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100,000/mL) may occur in women with preeclampsia. However, the purpose of this study is to determine the positive predictive value of an initial platelet count greater than 150,000/mL for maintaining a platelet count greater than 80,000/mL during labor and delivery. She is given the option to participate in the study and is informed that her platelet count will be monitored throughout her hospital stay.

A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and angina pectoris was admitted to the hospital after experiencing chest pain while exercising. He underwent a coronary angiography that revealed a significant stenosis in his left anterior descending artery. The patient was scheduled for coronary artery bypass surgery with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass. He has been on a beta-blocker for the past 3 years to control his blood pressure and heart rate. His medication compliance has been good, and his symptoms have been well controlled. He has given his oral consent to participate in the study after being fully informed about the trial's objectives and procedures.

63-year-old Caucasian male with a history of multiple myeloma diagnosed 15 months ago, underwent autologous stem cell transplant 12 months ago, and has been on a maintenance regimen of lenalidomide 10mg daily for the past 10 months. He has not received any other chemotherapy or investigational therapy since transplant. The patient has good performance status (ECOG 1) and no uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses. He has anemia with hemoglobin of 9 g/dL, platelet count of 100,000 cells/mm^3, and an absolute neutrophil count of 1500 cells/mm^3. His calculated creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min, and his total bilirubin, SGPT, and SGOT are all within normal limits. The patient has no grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy or grade 1 peripheral neuropathy with pain per CTCAE. His baseline FDG-PET/CT is positive for residual disease, and he has serum and urine protein electrophoresis within 28 days prior to randomization. The patient is willing to participate in the mandatory Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) program and comply with its requirements. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he agrees to use two acceptable methods of contraception during the study and for at least 90 days after the last dose of protocol treatment. The patient has no known gastrointestinal disease or GI procedure that could interfere with the oral absorption or tolerance of ixazomib or lenalidomide including difficulty swallowing. He has not been on systemic treatment, within 14 days before the first dose of ixazomib, with strong CYP3A inducers or use of St. John's wort.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and is scheduled to undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at the University of Wisconsin Carbone Cancer Center. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He is married, has two adult children, and works as an accountant. He reports having a good support system from his family and friends. He is worried about the potential side effects of the HSCT and the long recovery process, including fatigue, insomnia, and depression. He is interested in participating in a study that may help him manage these symptoms and improve his quality of life after the HSCT. He is willing and able to complete self-report measures and wear an Actiwatch-2 device to objectively quantify his circadian rest-activity patterns. He does not have any contraindications for the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

59-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with chest pain. EKG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. The patient was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and was promptly taken to the catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Blood samples will be drawn at the time of before, immediately after, and 3 days after PPCI. They will be collected in EDTA tubes and centrifuged for 10 min at 2000 g within 0.5 h. Plasma will be stored at -80°C until analysis. Plasma copeptin concentrations will be determined by a commercially available automated immunofluorescent assay (R&D Systems Inc. Minneapolis, USA). Baseline CMR will be performed 3-5 days after PPCI. Follow-up CMR scan will be conducted at 6 months after discharge. The patient will be followed up by phone at 1 month, 3 month, and 12 month after discharge. The purpose of the study is to investigate the prognostic value of copeptin for infarct size and prognosis in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old Chinese woman presented with a history of frequent heartburn and acid regurgitation for the last six months. She described a burning sensation in her chest and an unpleasant sour taste in her mouth after meals, especially at night. She reported that the symptoms were relieved by antacids but would often recur. She denied any dysphagia, odynophagia, or weight loss. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, and she was on medication for this condition. She denied any allergies or other medical conditions. She had a normal physical examination, including a normal abdominal exam, and her vital signs were within normal limits. She had no significant past surgical history. She was literate and able to complete the questionnaire. She had not taken NSAIDs in the past four weeks and had no known hypersensitivity to PPIs. She met the inclusion criteria for the study and was enrolled in the trial.

A 60-year-old male patient complains of constant pain in his right knee for the past 6 months. He reports difficulty in walking and climbing stairs. He was diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the knee based on radiographic evidence of osteophytes and knee pain. He has been taking paracetamol for the pain, but the symptoms have not improved. He has no history of any other musculoskeletal or arthritic conditions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is currently not on any medication other than paracetamol. He has no history of significant injury to the index knee or any lower extremity surgery in the past 6 months. He is married and has two adult children. He has no history of any significant medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with study restrictions. His baseline pain score on the 100mm VAS (WOMAC pain subscale) is 65mm.

The patient is a 50-year-old female smoker who has been smoking for more than 30 years. She has a history of chronic bronchitis and has been experiencing cough and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. She is currently taking inhalers for her symptoms. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, for which she is taking medication. Her family history is negative for cancer. She has no known allergies. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical exam is unremarkable except for mild wheezing in the lung fields. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of celecoxib in preventing non-small cell lung cancer in smokers. She has no history of concurrent use of NSAIDs or liver or renal dysfunction. She is not pregnant and has no other medical conditions that may interfere with the completion of the study.

The patient is a sexually active 25-year-old woman who is in good health and has a normal menstrual cycle. She has no history of adverse reaction to latex or either of the study products. She is willing to use effective forms of contraception and agrees not to participate in other investigational studies during the study period. The patient has had a normal Pap smear result within the last 12 months prior to study entry. She has no history of pathologic bone fracture not related to trauma, gynecologic or genital procedure within 90 days of study entry, or enrollment in other investigational study within 30 days of study entry. The patient has not had nontherapeutic injection drug use within 12 months of screening and does not have any social or medical condition that would interfere with the study. She has normal laboratory values and has no genital lesions, erythema, and/or edema or any other abnormal physical or pelvic exam finding that would interfere with the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not intend to become pregnant during the study period. The patient is willing to comply with study participation requirements, including attendance at all scheduled study visits. She is not using a diaphragm, vaginal ring, and/or spermicide for contraception, acyclovir or valacyclovir, post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV exposure, TDF/emtricitabine, or non-study vaginal products.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 25 weeks pregnant. She presents with a history of depression and is currently experiencing symptoms consistent with a major depressive episode, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and fatigue. Her HRSD(17) score is 16. She reports that her symptoms began during the first trimester of her pregnancy and have persisted since then. The patient is fluent in English and has been receiving prenatal care from an OBGYN practitioner. She has no history of other Axis I disorders and has not received any previous treatment for depression during this pregnancy. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is not currently taking any psychotropic medications or any medication that impacts mood. She is also not receiving any psychotherapy, herbs, or other treatments for depression. She is not currently experiencing any active suicidal potential.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis. He was admitted to the hospital due to severe respiratory distress and high fever. He has been on oxygen support with a respiratory rate of 28/minute and SpO2 level of 92% at room air. His chest x-ray shows bilateral pulmonary infiltrates of about 60%. The patient has elevated levels of CRP (120 mg/L), ferritin (1700 ng/mL), and LDH (480 U/L). He has lymphopenia (600 cells/mm3) and his D-dimer levels are normal. He has no history of other chronic illnesses and has not participated in any other clinical study in the last 30 days. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study. He has not been ventilated and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 46-year-old woman visited the clinic complaining of chronic sinus congestion, nasal discharge, and facial pain for over a year. The symptoms worsen during the winter months and are accompanied by headache and fatigue. She has tried several over-the-counter medications and antibiotics in the past without any significant improvement. She has no history of nasal polyps or asthma. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. She is currently not pregnant and uses a reliable method of birth control. She has not undergone any sinus surgeries or inferior turbinate reduction procedures in the past 2-3 months. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is willing to comply with the clinical trial protocol. She is able to understand and speak the local language fluently.

John is a 56-year-old man who was found unresponsive in his home by his wife. She called 911 and the emergency medical service (EMS) arrived on the scene within 5 minutes. EMS found him in ventricular fibrillation (VF) and immediately initiated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and delivered a shock with an automated external defibrillator (AED). After one defibrillation, EMS established peripheral intravenous (IV) access and randomized John to receive a low cumulative dose of epinephrine (up to 2mg total) as part of the Epinephrine Dose: Optimal Versus Standard Evaluation Trial. John has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has never had a cardiac arrest before and has no known allergies. His physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise. During the resuscitation, he received other medications and interventions as required, including antiarrhythmics and intubation. John was transported to the hospital, where he was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for further treatment. The investigators will follow up with John using a combination of administrative databases and telephone interviews to evaluate the effectiveness of a low cumulative dose of epinephrine compared to a standard cumulative dose of epinephrine during resuscitation from VF or ventricular tachycardia (VT) in adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been feeling down and hopeless for the past few weeks. She has been experiencing a loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy and has been having trouble sleeping. She has no history of depression or other mental health disorders, but has been under a lot of stress at work and in her personal life. She has never received any mental health treatment before and is not currently taking any medication. She has access to a computer and a smartphone and is comfortable using them. She is fluent in Romanian and has access to the internet. She completed the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and scored a 12. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to reduce depressive symptoms with a smartphone app based on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) theory.

A 45-year-old man presents to the dental clinic with a history of gum disease. He reports occasional bleeding when brushing his teeth and has noticed some gum recession over the past year. His medical history includes hypertension and he takes medication for it. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He has good oral hygiene practices, brushing twice daily and flossing once a day. On examination, there is mild gingival inflammation and some areas of recession. The periodontal probing depths range from 3-4mm. The patient is dentulous and has no missing teeth. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his gum health.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis two years ago. She has been experiencing frequent bouts of diarrhea, blood in her stool, and abdominal pain. She has been treated with oral prednisolone, but her symptoms have not improved. She is currently on maintenance medication, but her condition is not well-controlled. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. She has no other significant medical history or ongoing medical conditions. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding or at risk of pregnancy, and is using reliable contraception. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial.

Patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with medulloblastoma with recurrence or progression involving the brain and spine. The patient has undergone previous treatments, including systemic chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has measurable or evaluable tumor as assessed by MRI of the brain and total spine. The patient has an implanted catheter in the fourth ventricle or posterior fossa tumor cavity attached to a ventricular access device. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks in the opinion of the principal investigator. The patient has a Lansky score of 50 or greater, and existing neurological deficits have been stable for a minimum of 1 week prior to study enrollment. The patient has recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior anticancer chemotherapy. Adequate bone marrow function is present, defined by peripheral absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 500/µL, platelet count ≥ 50,000/µL (transfusion independent), and hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 gm/dL (may receive red blood cells(RBC) transfusions). The patient, along with the patient's legal representative, parent(s), or guardian, is able to provide written informed consent.

A 47-year-old female patient presented with a history of irregular menstrual cycles and heavy bleeding. She was diagnosed with uterine fibroids and advised to undergo abdominal hysterectomy. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, which was well-controlled with Lisinopril. She denied any history of renal or hepatic dysfunction, neuromuscular diseases, or use of calcium channel blockers. She had no known allergies to medications. Her vital signs were stable in the primary evaluation. On physical examination, there were no significant findings. She was classified as ASA physical status II. The patient was willing to participate in the study and met the inclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain in the heel of his right foot for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with a plantar calcaneal spur confirmed by X-ray images. The pain has been affecting his daily life, making it difficult for him to walk and complete his daily activities. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known contraindications for physical therapy. He has been randomly assigned to Group 1 of the study and will undergo ultrasound therapy for 10 treatments. The patient will also receive kinesitherapy exercises to strengthen the muscles that bend the plantar and supinated foot to improve the mobility of the feet and maintain the normal longitudinal arch of the foot. He will be evaluated for pain intensity three times: before therapy, after the first week of treatment, and after the second week of treatment using a modified form of the Laitinen pain indicators questionnaire and the Huskisson visual-analogue scale (VAS). The patient is hopeful that the ultrasound therapy will provide relief from his pain and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 15 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis. He is a non-smoker and has never used any illicit drugs. He has been under treatment for CF for several years and is currently taking prophylactic antibiotics. He has a resting awake oxygen saturation of 95% in room air and his FEV1 is 65%. He has never undergone lung transplantation, nor has he been diagnosed with heart disease, immunodeficiency, or methemoglobinemia. He does not have a history of frequent epistaxis or significant hemoptysis. He is currently attending school and is able to comply with the study design. He and his legal guardian have signed the informed consent form to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old man with a history of multiple myeloma presents with relapse after a prior stem cell transplant. He has completed multiple rounds of chemotherapy and has failed to respond to previous treatments. He reports fatigue, bone pain, and weight loss. He has an ECOG score of 2 and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. His neutrophil count is 0.8 X 10^9/L, and his platelet count is 45 X 10^9/L. He has no liver dysfunction, and his bilirubin and transaminase levels are within normal limits. He has no other active neoplasms and no history of ileus paralytic. He is not a candidate for a second stem cell transplant and has no other possible treatment options. He provides written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 49-year-old man who was diagnosed with glioblastoma and underwent radiotherapy and temozolomide treatment 6 months ago. After completion of treatment, he was doing well until he started experiencing symptoms of recurrent glioblastoma, such as headaches and difficulty speaking. His recent MRI scan showed evidence of progressive disease. He is now being considered for a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of cediranib maleate and olaparib to bevacizumab in treating recurrent glioblastoma. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He meets all of the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no existing medical conditions that would make him ineligible. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to release archival tissue samples for research purposes.

A 30-year-old Caucasian female diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 2. She has a history of recurrent chest infections, gastrointestinal issues and has been on long-term oral antibiotics. She is currently taking pancreatic enzyme supplements, inhaled bronchodilators, and mucolytic agents. She has a BMI of 22 and exercises regularly. She denies any history of fractures or bone pain but is concerned about her bone health due to her chronic illness. She is fluent in English and willing to participate in a single study visit that will include a DEXA scan, micro CT, and blood collection. She is also willing to participate in the Denosumab (Prolia) sub-study if she is found to have bone disease.

A 45-year-old male patient who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction symptoms for the past six months and has been undergoing treatment at the outpatient clinic of Urology at the Academic Medical Center in Amsterdam. He is fluent in reading and speaking the Dutch language and has access to a smartphone with an internet connection. He is willing to provide informed consent and has no cognitive problems that could affect his ability to follow instructions. He has not undergone any recent changes in treatment for erectile dysfunction and is fit according to his medical doctor.

We are looking for healthy male or female volunteers aged between 18 to 50 years inclusive, with a Body Mass Index (BMI) between 18.0 and 30.0 kg/m² inclusive. The volunteers should be in good physical and mental health, with blood pressure and heart rate within the normal range. The volunteers should have no known allergy/intolerance to pyrrolidinone derivatives, no abnormalities on EEG recordings, and should not be pregnant or lactating. Volunteers with a history or presence of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, neurological, or psychiatric disorders will not be eligible for this study. Those who are currently on any hepatic enzyme-inducing drug or have an IQ ≤ 80 as determined by Test of non-verbal intelligence or a Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression (CES-D Scale ≥16, will also be excluded from the study.

56 yo M with stage III pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has metastasized to the liver, currently undergoing chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel with stable disease. Has a history of depression and anxiety that has worsened since diagnosis. Has tried various antidepressants and anxiolytics with limited success. Has a high school level of education and is interested in participating in a study that may provide a personally and spiritually meaningful experience. No history of alcohol or drug dependence. Blood pressure readings meet eligibility criteria.

There is no patient involved in this particular clinical trial as it focuses on implementing and testing social-emotional development interventions within the Head Start system. The study will involve a sample of Head Start centers and classrooms, with children who speak both English and Spanish. The inclusion criteria involve having a similar racial/ethnic composition, an equal number of full-day and part-day programs, and a mix of four-year-old-only and mixed-age classrooms. Exclusion criteria include not complying with Head Start Standards, being located in a U.S. territory, only serving migrant children, or already implementing a social-emotional curriculum or participating in another evaluation study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who woke up with sudden onset of dizziness, slurred speech, and left-sided weakness. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. Upon arrival to the emergency department, he was evaluated by a physician and was found to have a clinical deficit consistent with a posterior-circulation stroke. MRI was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO) with an infarct in the brainstem. The patient was found to be eligible for mechanical thrombectomy and underwent the procedure. The total posterior-circulation infarct volume (TPIV) was calculated from the initial MRI and will be used as a predictor of 90-day functional independence and mortality in the clinical trial. The patient's pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 1, indicating he had no significant disability prior to the stroke. The patient is eligible for the trial and will be followed up for 90 days to assess the outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy in ABAO patients.

A 42-year-old female presents with a complaint of dryness, burning, and irritation in both eyes for the past 2 years. She reports that her symptoms are more severe in the late afternoon and evening. She has tried various over-the-counter eye drops without significant improvement. She uses glasses for reading purposes. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medication. On ocular examination, the best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She has moderate conjunctival hyperemia and mild corneal staining. Her Schirmer's test score is 4mm/5minutes in both eyes. She wears soft contact lenses occasionally but can discontinue their use during the study. She has not received any ocular surgery in the last 12 months and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to discontinue the use of any topical ocular medications during the study period.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who is the primary caregiver for her mother with Alzheimer's disease. She spends at least 30 hours a week taking care of her mother's needs, including bathing, dressing, and feeding. Lately, she has been feeling overwhelmed and experiencing mild depressive symptoms. Her score on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale-Revised (CESD-R) is 18. She speaks fluent English and is comfortable using a mobile phone with internet access. She has not participated in any other caregiver intervention programs but is open to trying new ways to improve her well-being. She does not have any terminal illness or severe hypertension, and her cognitive function is intact (MMSE score of 29). She does not receive psychiatric care for any serious mental illness.

Maria is a 32-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is currently planning to undergo adjuvant chemotherapy (epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide). She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has no clinically significant impairments in her cardiac, liver, or kidney functions. Her hematologic, hepatic, and renal functions all meet the requirements for the study, including an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of ≥1.5 x 10^9/L and a blood platelet count (PLT) of ≥100 x 10^9/L. Additionally, her serum creatinine (sCr) is ≤1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), and her total bilirubin (TBIL) is ≤1.5×ULN. Her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) /serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) and/or alanine aminotransferase (ALT)/serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase (SGPT) are both ≤ 2.5 x ULN. Maria's hemoglobin (Hb) is >9 g/dL, and her alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is ≤1.5×ULN. She is expected to comply with the study protocol and has signed the informed consent form. She has a negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test and has no acute infections. She has not received bone marrow or stem cell transplants, has no primary hematological diseases, and has not undergone surgery within three weeks prior to chemotherapy. She has not received G-CSF within four weeks prior to the study and has no known allergies to chemotherapy drugs, recombinant human granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (rhG-CSF), or any other biological products. She is not participating in any other clinical trials at the same time or within four weeks before screening, and does not have any cacoethic addiction such as drug abuse or alcoholism.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, cognitive impairments, and mood changes for the past 6 months. She has consulted various doctors and has undergone multiple tests, but no clear diagnosis has been made. She scores 8 on the Numerical Pain Scale (NPS 0-10) and her pain is constant, making it difficult for her to carry out daily activities. She has been taking pain medications, but they have not provided significant relief. She is literate, lives in the city of Porto Alegre, RS, Brazil, and is willing to participate in the study after the initial evaluation. She is not pregnant, does not have severe mental illness, and does not have any contraindications for tDCS or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to give informed consent to participate.

A 62-year-old man who is a retired construction worker came to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and cough for the past 3 years. He has a history of smoking 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the past 40 years. He has difficulty walking up a flight of stairs and performing daily activities without becoming short of breath. Spirometry was performed revealing a forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) of 50% of the predicted with a ratio of FEV1 to forced vital capacity (FVC) of 0.65. He has been previously diagnosed with moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been using a combination of inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) and long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) therapy. He has experienced exacerbations requiring oral corticosteroids and antibiotics in the past year. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 6 months and has no significant history of heart, renal, endocrine, psychiatric, immunological, or neurological disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment option for his COPD.

A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents for evaluation of cognitive function. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty remembering names and faces. He has undergone several cognitive tests, including the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Logical Memory II delayed recall test, which showed scores of 28 and 12, respectively. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent cognitive decline. He reports that he does not take any omega-3 supplements and has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 30 days. He does not have any serious diseases or use anticoagulants. He is willing to undergo MRI scans and take DHA supplements for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past two weeks. He has a history of uncontrolled diabetes and hypertension. The patient is currently taking oral antidiabetic and antihypertensive medications, but his blood glucose and blood pressure levels are still not well-controlled. Upon physical examination, the patient appears fatigued and his breathing is labored. Lung auscultation reveals crackling sounds in the lower lobes of the lungs. Chest X-ray shows infiltrates in the lower lobes of the lungs. The patient is suspected to have pulmonary mucormycosis and is referred for further evaluation. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman with a history of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and urinary incontinence (UI) who has been using a pessary for the management of her symptoms. She experiences discomfort and pain during pessary removal and insertion, which is affecting her quality of life. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study. She has no known allergies or contraindications to topical anesthetics. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and does not plan on becoming pregnant in the next 6 months.

62 yo M with aortic valve stenosis and moderate mitral regurgitation scheduled for open left heart surgery, specifically aortic valve replacement without concomitant coronary artery bypass. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 Diabetes - Peripheral artery disease - Previous TIA - Previous carotid endarterectomy [**5-20**] - Chronic kidney disease stage 3 - Status post prostatectomy for prostate cancer. Medications: - Aspirin - Atorvastatin - Losartan - Metformin - Clopidogrel. No significant history of pulmonary disease, thoracic or cardiac surgery, or radiation to the chest. No significant pulmonary adhesions to the chest wall or history of internal mammary artery harvesting.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently visited her dentist complaining of tooth sensitivity and discomfort while chewing on the right side of her mouth. She has a history of dental caries and has had several fillings in the past. Her dental exam revealed proximal caries on two posterior teeth, and her dentist recommended composite restorations to fix the issue. The patient is in good general health and has no history of medical problems or allergies. She has a regular dental hygiene routine and visits her dentist for check-ups every six months. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She drinks alcohol occasionally but not excessively. She has no issues with her periodontal health and has all of her teeth present except for her wisdom teeth, which were extracted years ago. She has a stable occlusion and is expected to be available for follow-up appointments.

75-year-old male with end stage renal disease and creatinine clearance of 10 mL/min on hemodialysis three times a week. Patient has a history of atrial fibrillation and was started on warfarin for stroke prevention. Patient has a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding while on warfarin therapy. Patient has been switched to apixaban for anticoagulation therapy. Patient has been on apixaban for at least 1 month. The patient has no prior history of venous thromboembolism but is at high risk due to immobility and comorbidities. The patient has no known contraindications to apixaban. The patient is willing to participate in a retrospective cohort study evaluating the safety and efficacy of apixaban in patients with severe renal impairment.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer six months ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy but the cancer has now recurred and is mostly confined to her peritoneal cavity, as confirmed by imaging and biopsy. She has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating, and her CA-125 levels have been elevated. She has a good performance status and no significant comorbidities. Her liver and kidney functions, as well as her blood counts, are within normal limits. She has no history of prior intra-peritoneal irinotecan therapy. She is willing to use an approved method of birth control during the study period. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options and potentially improve her prognosis.

A 28-year-old healthy female presents with no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m^2 and weighs 60 kg. She does not consume alcohol or smoke. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a non-hormonal contraceptive method. She has not participated in any experimental study or taken any experimental drug in the past 6 months. She takes no prescription or non-prescription drugs or dietary supplements. She has no history of drug abuse, and her urine drug test is negative. Her ECG results show QTc less than 450 msec. She has no known hypersensitivity to ibuprofen or chemically related compounds. She has no history of gastroduodenal ulcer or previous or active gastrointestinal bleeding. She is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 45 yo F with a history of multiple sclerosis presents with symptoms of urinary incontinence and urgency. She has tried various medications and pelvic floor exercises but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of bilateral stimulation of the tibial nerve compared to unilateral stimulation in neurological bladder disorders. She is affiliated to a social security scheme and is over 18 years of age. Her neurological bladder hyperactivity is non-serious and she meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 65-year-old male patient, who has been taking low-dose Aspirin (81 mg) daily for the past 3 years as a preventive measure for cardiovascular diseases, has been scheduled for an elective non-cardiac surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia but has no history of bleeding disorders or previous surgeries. The patient has been advised to continue taking the low-dose Aspirin by his cardiologist but has been instructed to stop taking it by his surgeon. The patient is confused about the conflicting advice and is willing to participate in this study to understand the factors that contribute to the decision to continue or discontinue ASA therapy before non-cardiac surgery. The patient has provided his consent to participate in the study.

A 54-year-old woman has been recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy as part of her treatment plan. She has a supportive husband who is willing to participate in the clinical trial as her caregiver. The patient and her husband are English speaking and have no prior history of malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer. They are eligible for the Navigated Early Survivorship Transition (NEST) intervention which involves survivorship care planning sessions to improve psychosocial well-being, patient and caregiver engagement, and adherence to treatment and follow-up recommendations. They are willing to participate in the trial to help improve survivorship care planning for cancer patients and their caregivers.

Maria is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) 2 years ago. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and jaundice. She has a history of autoimmune diseases in her family, including rheumatoid arthritis and lupus. She takes ursodiol and follows a low-fat diet, but her symptoms have not improved significantly. Her liver function test shows elevated alkaline phosphatase levels. She has not used any investigational agents or systemic antibiotics, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressants for the past 3 months. She is not taking any anti-platelet or anti-coagulant medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use birth control during the study. She does not have any other liver diseases or conditions that would interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for PSC.

This is a 35 year-old female who suffered a severe burn injury on her right thigh and lower leg while cooking at home. She was immediately taken to the hospital where she underwent debridement of the burn wound and was diagnosed with a large area of skin loss. The wound was then covered with a split-thickness skin graft from her left thigh. The wound size was approximately 150cm2. She has no history of immunodeficiency disease, end-stage renal disease, coagulopathy, or radiation therapy. She is otherwise healthy and has no major medical problems. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of negative pressure drainage system with controls (indirect saline soaks) in the coverage of recipient site wounds of split-thickness skin graft.

Patient B is a 65-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU after a fall at home that resulted in a hip fracture. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication regularly. She lives alone and is still able to perform her activities of daily living independently. Upon admission, she was alert and oriented, but complained of pain in the hip area. She underwent surgery to repair the fracture and was transferred to the ICU for post-operative care. Her vital signs upon admission to the ICU were stable, with a blood pressure of 124/78 mmHg, a heart rate of 75 bpm, a respiratory rate of 16 bpm, and an oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. She is able to communicate effectively with the healthcare team and has no known communication problems. She has provided her consent to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old healthy female with a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m^2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing biphasic insulin aspart 30, biphasic insulin aspart 50, biphasic insulin aspart 70, and insulin aspart. She has a normal hemoglobin A1c level and does not smoke. She currently uses an oral contraceptive pill for birth control. She has no history of drug or alcohol dependence and no family history of diabetes mellitus. She has not donated blood or plasma in the past 3 months. She is interested in contributing to medical research and potentially helping to improve the treatment options for diabetes.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with stable coronary artery disease. He has a history of myocardial infarction and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. He is currently taking aspirin 81 mg daily. He has no known allergies or intolerances to cangrelor, prasugrel, or clopidogrel. He has not taken any antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication in the past 30 days. He has no bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. He has no history of stroke or cerebral arteriovenous malformation. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has normal renal function with a glomerular filtration rate of 80 mL/min. He has no significant disease or condition affecting any major organ system. He has not taken any investigational medicinal products or devices in the past 30 days. He has no active pathological bleeding or history of transient ischemic attack.

A 35 year old female with moderate to severe wrinkles in the upper face, including horizontal forehead lines, glabellar frown lines, and lateral canthal lines. She has not received any botulinum neurotoxin treatments in the past 12 months and has not had any facial cosmetic procedures or biodegradable filler treatments in the past year. She has not had any permanent material inserted in her face. The patient has no medical conditions that would put her at increased risk with exposure to NT201. She is willing to participate in a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study to investigate the safety and efficacy of NT 201 for the simultaneous treatment of upper facial lines. She understands that there will be a placebo-control main period followed by an open-label extension period.

Li is a 58-year-old male who has been experiencing bowel habits change, blood in his stool and abdominal pain for the past few months. He went to the local hospital and was diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma. MRI showed that the tumor was located at 5 cm from the anal verge. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are under control with medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has never had any surgical procedures before. He is willing to undergo surgery and participate in the registry study. His physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who suffered a right hemispheric ischemic stroke 4 months ago. He is experiencing right hemiparesis and has difficulty moving his right upper limb. He has been discharged from the hospital and is currently staying at home. He has normal dynamic sitting balance and has at least 120 degrees of shoulder flexion and 45 degrees of shoulder extension by passive range of motion. His active movement is at least stage 3 by Chedoke-McMaster Stroke Assessment and his muscle tone is graded 1-2 by Modified Ashworth Scale in 2 of 3 muscle groups including shoulder adductor, internal rotator or/and elbow flexor groups. He has no cognitive impairment and is right dominant handedness. He has not received any occupational therapy on his upper extremity and has no muscle contracture or pain at the scapula, shoulder, and elbow. He has no history of fracture or surgery at the head, shoulder, scapula, and elbow. He has no other neurological disorders, uncontrolled hypertension, myocardial infarction, seizure or epilepsy, pacemaker or hemodialysis vascular access, and has not experienced cyber-sickness.

32-year-old Caucasian female with a history of episodic migraine headaches since the age of 18. She experiences an average of 3-4 migraine attacks per month with usual migraine pain of 3 on the headache pain severity scale. She has been using NSAIDs for pain relief. She reports no medication overuse headache and has not taken any triptans or ergots in the past 90 days. She has no hemiplegic migraine, migraine with brain stem aura, or other forms of neurologically complicated migraine. She has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack and no concurrent diagnosis of seizure disorder. She is able to differentiate between a migraine headache and other types of headaches. She has no uncontrolled hypertension, severe renal impairment, or liver dysfunction. She does not have positive serology for HIV, Hepatitis B surface antigen, or Hepatitis C antibody. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse in the past year and no neurological or psychiatric impairment that would compromise data collection. She has not participated in any clinical trials involving medication in the past 30 days.

A 10-year-old Hispanic boy with a BMI of 26.5 kg/m² and a family history of type 2 diabetes. The boy is a native Spanish speaker and is currently in the fifth grade. He enjoys playing soccer and video games. The boy has no significant medical history or current medical issues, and he is not taking any medications. The boy's parents and grandparents are also Hispanic and have a history of type 2 diabetes. The boy's mother and father are both overweight and have elevated blood sugar levels. The boy will be participating in a randomized controlled trial of a low-glycemic load diet versus a low-fat diet aimed at reducing insulin resistance and preventing type 2 diabetes in at-risk Hispanic children. The study will involve weekly visits for 12 weeks, monthly visits for 9 months, and 3-monthly visits for 12 months, along with a family-based intervention program that includes behavior modification and increased physical activity. The boy will be randomly assigned to either the low-glycemic load or low-fat dietary plan, and his subjective, hormonal, and metabolic responses will be assessed during a 24-hour admission to the GCRC as part of the study.

A 28-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident two weeks ago and suffered a severe head injury. He was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 7 and has been in a coma since then. He underwent a craniotomy to reduce intracranial pressure and his vital signs have stabilized. He has no previous history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. He is able to breathe on his own but is currently receiving enteral feeding through a nasogastric tube. His family is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was previously treated for leukemia at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital (SJCRH). She has completed her chemotherapy and is currently in remission. She is physically inactive and does not meet the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) physical activity guidelines for children her age. She has internet access and a computer that is compatible with the study device.
