Her medical history is significant for mild asthma, which is well controlled with daily use of an inhaled corticosteroid. She does not have any cognitive impairment and has a Full Scale Intelligence Quotient score of 95. She speaks and writes English fluently. She lives with her parents and two siblings and attends school regularly. She is motivated to improve her physical activity levels and is interested in participating in the study. Her attending physician has approved her participation in the study via email.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is scheduled for elective surgery requiring an arterial catheter. He has no history of chronic obstructive lung disease, bronchial asthma, peripheral artery occlusive disease, or diabetes mellitus. He has a Body-Mass-Index of 28, which is within the eligible range for the study. He is a non-smoker or has smoked less than 5 pack years. His ASA classification is I or II, indicating that he is in good health without any significant systemic disease. He has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is scheduled for coronary artery bypass surgery with CPB. His preoperative echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 45%. He has no history of pacemaker, congenital heart disease or recent open-heart surgery. His body weight is 85 kg, height is 180 cm and waist circumference is 100 cm. The patient reports a history of poor appetite and unintentional weight loss of 5 kg in the past 3 months. His preoperative MUST score is 2, indicating moderate risk of malnutrition. Bioelectrical impedance analysis reveals a fat-free mass index of 19 kg/m² and a phase angle of 5.2 degrees, indicating poor nutritional status. The patient's handgrip strength is 23 kg and his upper third triangle perimeter is 40 cm. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provides informed consent.

The patient is a 34 year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year, but has been unsuccessful. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been diagnosed with thin endometrium after undergoing a hysteroscopic biopsy. She has not undergone any previous treatment for her infertility. She has no known history of tuberculosis or cancer in the reproductive system. She is willing to participate in the study and is in good general health. She does not smoke or consume alcohol and is not taking any medication. She has no known allergies.

John is a 67-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease (PD) five years ago. He suffers from tremors, bradykinesia, and rigidity. John has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He takes medication for these conditions. He has recently been feeling depressed and has had problems with his memory and thinking. John's neurologist ordered laboratory tests that revealed his vitamin D levels were low. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to investigate whether vitamin D repletion can improve his Parkinson's symptoms, mood, and cognitive function. John is able to provide informed consent and is able to complete the study questionnaires and assessments. He is free of active cancer or other serious medical conditions which might reasonably preclude him from completing the 6-month intervention. John is able to complete an 8-meter walk at screening evaluation. He is at H&Y stage III. He has no history of hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, liver failure, end-stage renal disease, or kidney stones within the past 5 years, and has a GFR greater than 15 ml/min.

A 9-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD and impulsive aggression, who previously participated in the 810P301 study, is being considered for this open-label extension study. The patient has been receiving FDA-approved ADHD medication for the past year and has shown some improvement in attention and hyperactivity. However, he continues to exhibit impulsive aggression, which has resulted in multiple incidents of physical aggression towards his peers and family members. His parents report that his behavior is affecting his academic performance and social interactions. The patient has no significant medical history, and his physical exam is unremarkable. His height is 4'8" and weight is 65 lbs, with a BMI in the 75th percentile for his age. His vital signs are stable, and his ECG is normal. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in this study and have provided written informed consent and assent. The patient is currently not experiencing suicidal thoughts or behaviors.

Patient is a 26-year-old female from the United States who comes to the clinic with symptoms of painful urination, frequent urination, and urgency. She reports no history of UTIs in the past year and has never been pregnant. She is currently using a hormonal contraceptive and is in good general health. She has no known allergies or intolerances to any of the study drugs. Her vital signs are stable and her physical examination is unremarkable. Urine analysis shows presence of bacteria and white blood cells.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from recurrent Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) for the past 8 months. Despite receiving standard antibiotic therapy, she has experienced relapse of symptoms within 2 weeks of discontinuing antibiotics. She has been hospitalized twice due to severe diarrhea, abdominal pain and dehydration caused by CDI. The patient is willing and able to comply with all the required study procedures and able to provide informed consent. She has tested positive for C. difficile toxin/gene using PCR within the past 3 months. She has a history of at least 2 recurrent CDI episodes where recurrence is defined as return of diarrhea consistent with CDI within 8 weeks following CDI symptom resolution for at least 24 hours after a minimum of 10-day course of standard antibiotic therapy for each episode and/or ongoing symptoms consistent with CDI despite at least 7 days of treatment using oral vancomycin at a minimum dose of 250 mg four times daily. The patient has not taken any other investigational product and is not actively taking Saccharomyces boulardii or other probiotic. The patient is not currently taking systemic antibiotic therapy for more than 7 days and does not have severe underlying disease that would prevent her from surviving for at least 30 days.

A 43-year-old male with a history of moderate-to-severe psoriasis has been recommended by his physician to start treatment with infliximab. He has been struggling with psoriasis for over a decade and has tried various medications with little improvement. He is willing to participate in the observational study and has signed the written consent. He has no known allergies to any medication and is able to understand and answer a self-administered questionnaire. He is currently not taking any other medication for his psoriasis.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing severe lower back pain for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with a herniated disc in his lumbar spine and has been recommended for spine surgery. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control it. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 28. He has no history of allergies to any perioperative medications. He has not undergone any lumbar spine surgery in the past. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B for the past 5 years. He has been taking lamivudine plus adefovir combination therapy for the past 12 months to manage his symptoms. He has noticed an improvement in his symptoms and his hepatitis B virus DNA levels have been undetectable on two consecutive tests with a 3-month interval. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has no known history of liver disease or malignancy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of switching to tenofovir monotherapy for lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B patients with undetectable hepatitis B virus DNA while on lamivudine plus adefovir combination therapy.

A 25 year old woman with a history of Stargardt disease comes to the clinic for evaluation. She has been experiencing difficulty with central vision, including blurred vision and difficulty reading, for the past year. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/200 in both eyes. She has genetic testing revealing two pathogenic mutations of the ABCA4 gene, consistent with the diagnosis of Stargardt disease. The patient has no other ocular diseases and the ocular media is clear. The patient is able to self-administer oral medication and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant, not lactating, and is willing to practice a medically accepted method of birth control from screening through 30 days after the final dose of study drug.

A 23 year old man came to the clinic with his mother and sister, who have all been diagnosed with diabetes. The patient has had symptoms of increased thirst and urination for the past year, and his fasting blood glucose levels have been consistently high. He has not responded well to treatment with metformin, and his family has a history of early-onset diabetes. Genetic testing has ruled out mutations in known genes associated with MODY (GCK, HNF1A, HNF4A), but the family history strongly suggests a genetic component to their diabetes. The patient is willing to participate in a study to help identify novel genes associated with monogenic diabetes. He is currently not on insulin therapy and has a BMI of 26. He is affiliated with a social protection scheme and is willing to sign an informed consent.

A 68-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a history of major depressive disorder. She has been experiencing symptoms such as persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, insomnia, and fatigue for the last 12 weeks. She has been taking antidepressants for the past 8 weeks but hasn't shown significant improvement. The patient is willing to participate in a long-term study of Brexpiprazole as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder. She is currently taking other medications for hypertension and diabetes, which are well-controlled. The patient is sexually inactive and has no history of electroconvulsive therapy or other mental illnesses. She is capable of giving written informed consent and understanding the contents of the trial.

A 30-year-old female patient scheduled for oral surgery came to the dental clinic with a history of dental anxiety. She has avoided dental treatment for years because of fear and anxiety. She has never received any form of conscious sedation or general anesthesia in the past. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She is not a smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her body mass index is 25 kg/m2. The dental team evaluated her and concluded that intravenous conscious sedation with midazolam would be appropriate for her procedure. The patient was informed about the study and agreed to participate. She was randomized to the study group, which involved capnography monitoring in addition to standard monitoring. The patient was given pre-sedation instructions and was monitored throughout the procedure. The dental team was trained in the interpretation of capnography in relation to respiratory depression, and the capnography monitor was calibrated daily. The patient received midazolam at a rate of one mg per minute until the desired level of sedation was achieved. The capnography monitor provided breath-by-breath information, and any changes in the shape of the capnography waveform and ETCO2 numeric changes were considered as triggers to take measures to avoid desaturation. The patient tolerated the procedure well and was discharged 60 minutes after the last increment of midazolam. She received post-sedation instructions and was followed up to ensure there were no adverse events.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of cellulitis in his right leg. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, and takes oral medications for both conditions. He has no known drug allergies. He reports experiencing fever, chills, and significant pain and redness in his right leg for the past 3 days. On examination, he has an area of erythema and warmth on his right lower leg, with associated swelling and tenderness. He has no signs of systemic toxicity or sepsis. Laboratory studies reveal a white blood cell count of 12,000/mm3 and a C-reactive protein level of 60 mg/L. He is started on intravenous flucloxacillin and admitted to the hospital for further management. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the optimal duration of antibiotic therapy for cellulitis.

A 35-year-old female patient with a recurrent depression diagnosis (ICD-10 F33.0) has been in a heterosexual relationship with her partner for over three years. She experiences symptoms of low mood, loss of interest, and decreased energy, which have been affecting her social interactions and her relationship with her partner. The patient is not currently enrolled in any therapy or group training. She is not pregnant and does not have any severe physical or psychological disorders. She has no history of substance abuse or addiction but is a light smoker, smoking less than 10 cigarettes per day. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve her social interactions and reduce her depressive symptoms.

The patient is a 42 year old woman who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 8 months. She has tried various pain medications and physical therapy but has not seen much improvement. She is currently sedentary due to her pain and has not engaged in regular exercise for the past year. She does not have any history of traumatic, inflammatory, infectious or tumorous etiology related to her low back pain. She has not undergone any spine or lower limb surgery in the past. She is not pregnant and does not have any neurological findings (leg pain). Her recent medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of an exercise program for trunk stabilization performed in stable and unstable surfaces for people with nonspecific chronic low back pain.

The patient is an 8-year-old male child who was diagnosed with a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) after experiencing symptoms such as headaches, vomiting, and difficulty with eye movement. An MRI scan confirmed the diagnosis, and the patient has no history of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or other cancer treatments in the last 5 years. The patient is able to undergo functional MRI (diffusion, perfusion, spectro) and FDG-PET and sestamibi SPECT, and has a life expectancy of more than 8 weeks after the start of study treatment. The patient's Lansky Play Scale score is greater than 50, and the absolute neutrophil count is greater than 1.5 x 10⁹/l, with platelets greater than 100 x 10⁹/l. The total bilirubin is less than 1.5 x ULN, and AST and ALT are less than 2.5 x ULN. The patient's serum creatinine is less than or equal to 1.5 x ULN for age, and there are no current organ toxicities greater than grade 2 according to the NCICTCAE version 4.0. The patient is covered by government health insurance and has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 36-year-old male patient was involved in a car accident and sustained a fractured tibia and fibula. He was admitted to the orthopaedic trauma surgery service at a Level 1 academic trauma center. He speaks fluent English and has no prior history of orthopaedic trauma injuries or relationship with the attending orthopaedic surgeon. He is not visually impaired, intubated or sedated, nor is he intoxicated. He has no significant past medical history, no allergies, and is not on any medications. He is married and works as an accountant. He understands the purpose of the study and has agreed to participate.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to the emergency room with severe sepsis symptoms, including fever, chills, and low blood pressure. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. He is married and has two children. He works as a truck driver and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He had a kidney stone removed 3 years ago and has fully recovered. His medical history includes seasonal allergies and he is currently taking over-the-counter antihistamines for that. He has no known HIV infection and is not pregnant nor breastfeeding.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a body mass index of 32. He has a history of snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness for the past 2 years. He reports frequent morning headaches and difficulty concentrating at work. He sought medical attention for these symptoms and a sleep study revealed moderate to severe OSA with an apnea-hypopnea index of 32 events per hour. He was prescribed CPAP therapy but has been non-compliant due to difficulty adjusting to the mask and discomfort during sleep. The patient is scheduled for a total knee replacement surgery and has agreed to participate in the study to evaluate the impact of CPAP compliance on post-operative outcomes in OSA patients. He will bring his own CPAP unit to the hospital for use during his stay. The patient does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively. He has no known drug allergies and is not taking any medications that could interfere with CPAP therapy. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient has been educated on the importance of CPAP compliance and has agreed to use the device during the post-operative period. He will be monitored for O2 desaturation by using a wrist-watch pulse oximeter at home for one night preoperatively and the first three nights post-operatively at the hospital.

Patient is a 42-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with persistent asthma for the last 5 years. He has been treated with inhaled corticosteroids and a combination of ICS/LABA, but his asthma remains uncontrolled. He has not smoked for over a year and has a smoking history of 5 pack-years. His BMI is 25. He has no history of major surgeries, blood donations, or participation in clinical trials involving investigational drugs. He has not experienced any psychiatric disorders in the past 3 months. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he has agreed to use adequate contraception for the duration of the study. He has no known hypersensitivity or intolerance to inhaled beta-agonists and/or leukotriene inhibitors. He is willing to discontinue or taper asthma controlling medications while receiving Montelukast. After genetic testing, he has the specific genetic marker for clinical efficacy of MK-1029.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B infection. He has been diagnosed with hepatic decompensation with a Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) score of 8, and has been experiencing symptoms such as ascites and mild hepatic encephalopathy. He has not received any treatment for his hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and has been viremic. He has not undergone any solid organ transplant and has no history of malignancy except for basal cell skin cancer which has been treated successfully. He has an estimated creatinine clearance of 60 ml/min and is willing to comply with the dosing instructions for the study drug administration. He is not currently on any of the disallowed concomitant medications listed in the study protocol and is willing to use an "effective" protocol-specified method of contraception during the study. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of Tenofovir Alafenamide in HBV Related Decompensated Liver.

This is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with mycosis fungoides after presenting with a persistent rash on her legs and arms. She underwent a skin biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis. Upon examination, she was found to have stage IA disease. She has no history of PUVA treatment, and her blood work shows normal organ function. She has a Karnofsky performance score greater than 60 and is willing to limit sun exposure on days when she receives PUVA treatment. She has no history of photosensitive or skin cancer syndromes. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

40 year-old woman recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. The tumor is unifocal, measuring between 1-3 cm and has not spread to lymph nodes or other parts of the body. The patient has undergone a sentinel node procedure prior to the start of the study. The patient is in good overall health with no significant medical history or comorbidities. She is able to undergo image-guided preoperative accelerated partial-breast irradiation (PAPBI) followed by surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the study and follow the treatment schedule as outlined.

A 24-year-old male with no history of significant medical conditions or allergies is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of a new drug called PF-06852231. He's a healthy individual with no current use of prescription or non-prescription drugs and has a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2. He is willing to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He is not a smoker and does not consume alcohol. His last physical exam and lab study showed normal results.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer after a radical prostatectomy. The pathology report revealed a Gleason score of 8 and a baseline PSA level of 0.5 ng/ml. The patient has no evidence of metastasis based on a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, and a bone scan. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his laboratory results show a platelet count greater than or equal to 100,000 cells/mm3, hemoglobin level greater than or equal to 10.0 g/dL, and an absolute neutrophil count greater than 1.5 x 10^9/L. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy for prostate cancer, but has undergone LHRH agonist therapy for 3 months prior to the radical prostatectomy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

38-year-old woman with a BMI of 32, residing in the Greater Kansas City area, who is looking to lose weight and maintain the weight loss over time. She is not a smoker and does not have any metabolic disease affecting energy balance. She has not participated in any weight loss or physical activity research projects in the past 6 months. She is not currently on any special diets or medications that affect metabolism or appetite. The patient is willing to be randomized and is able to participate in moderate diet restriction and moderate physical activity. She does not exhibit signs of eating disorders or depression.

A 60-year-old woman had a heart attack a week ago, and she was admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. She underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement in her left anterior descending artery. After the procedure, she was started on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel. She was discharged from the hospital with a prescription for aspirin and clopidogrel with instructions to take them daily. However, she experienced side effects such as headache, dizziness, and gastrointestinal upset with clopidogrel. She returned to the hospital clinic for follow-up and was enrolled in a clinical trial to compare the variability of the antiplatelet effect of prasugrel and ticagrelor. She has no known allergies or contraindications to either medication. Her body weight is 70 kg.

The patient is a 26-year-old healthy female with no history of immunodeficiency or thymus dysfunction. She has not been vaccinated against yellow fever previously and does not have any known allergies to eggs. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the cytotoxicity of yellow fever specific CD8 T cells following YF-17D vaccination. She is not currently taking any immunosuppressants and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no fever on the day of vaccination and is willing to use contraceptives for 4 weeks after vaccination. She meets all the inclusion and exclusion criteria and is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is an 82-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. She lives with her spouse, who is her primary caregiver. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She also has mild osteoarthritis of her knees and hips, which is managed with over-the-counter pain medication as needed. She wears glasses and hearing aids but has no significant impairments in her vision or hearing. She has no history of seizures or any other major medical conditions. She speaks English fluently and has completed high school education. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the combination of cognitive training and transcranial magnetic stimulation can improve her memory function and other mental functions such as language, orientation, and thinking or judgment. She has no metal implants or other medical devices that would exclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar II disorder with two definite periods of hypomania in the last 5 years. She has been on lamotrigine as a mood stabilizer and has been clinically stable for the last 4 weeks. The patient is currently taking lamotrigine and an atypical antipsychotic at therapeutic doses for mood stabilization. She is fluent in English and has a WAIS-IV vocabulary scaled score of 6, equivalent to an estimated IQ of 85. The patient has shown cognitive impairment (-0.50 SD or below) on the Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT) total learning score on trials 1 to 5 or immediate recall at the screening visit. She is a non

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with a herniated disc in his lumbar spine that requires surgical intervention. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control his blood pressure. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient is scheduled for an elective surgery due to high risk of intraoperative blood loss. The anaesthesia team will administer general anaesthesia for the procedure. He does not have a history of respiratory insufficiency, ischemic heart disease, or stroke. He is classified as an ASA class 2. The surgical procedure will be an open laminectomy for the removal of the herniated disc.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman with a history of severe aortic stenosis. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue for the past few months. She has been evaluated by a cardiologist who recommended transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) with a Medtronic CoreValve®. The patient is scheduled to undergo the procedure using the femoral artery as the intended access site for the valve delivery system. She has no prior history of stroke or TIA in the last 12 months, and her carotid and subclavian arteries are free from significant stenosis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with follow-up visits.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has just been admitted to the emergency department with chest pain that started 2 hours ago. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He is a current smoker with a 40 pack-year history. He has no history of myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft. He is alert and oriented and his vital signs are stable. On physical examination, he is diaphoretic with a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg and heart rate of 90 beats per minute. His electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. He is a candidate for thrombolysis, but will undergo angiography to determine the severity of his coronary artery disease. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria for age, transfer to cath-lab, and duration of symptoms. However, he is excluded from the study due to his current smoking status and history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity (BMI=32) was referred to a cardiology clinic for routine follow-up. He reports a sedentary lifestyle due to his job as a desk worker and a lack of motivation to exercise in his free time. He takes medication for his hypertension and dyslipidemia. His blood pressure is well controlled, but his lipid profile is still suboptimal. He has no history of coronary artery disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease. He is interested in improving his health and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that promotes physical activity. He is able to walk without difficulty and has no orthopedic issues that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of rectal bleeding and bowel movement changes for the past 3 months. He underwent a colonoscopy that revealed a tumor located in the rectum, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of stage II rectal cancer. Imaging studies show no evidence of metastasis. The patient is scheduled for a standard trans-abdominal low anterior resection surgery at the University of Virginia. He has no known drug allergies and his medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is willing and able to give written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 62-year-old female with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She was admitted to the ICU due to severe sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). She has been on mechanical ventilation for 24 hours. Her initial vital signs were blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg, heart rate of 95 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 85% on 100% FiO2. She has been started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressors. Her laboratory tests showed elevated white blood cell count (18,000/μL), C-reactive protein (CRP) level (120 mg/L), and procalcitonin level (10 ng/mL). She has no history of smoking, alcohol abuse, or illicit drug use. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m2 and a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which is well-controlled with oral medications. She has no known drug allergies.

This is a 49-year-old male who underwent a bilateral lung transplant in [**10/2019**] due to end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He had a complicated post-operative course with multiple episodes of rejection, which were managed with high dose steroids and anti-thymocyte globulin. Despite these interventions, he was diagnosed with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) in [**5/2021**]. He has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath, cough, and exercise intolerance over the past few months. He is currently on a stable maintenance immunosuppressive regimen of tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of montelukast in slowing down the progression of chronic rejection after lung transplantation. He is able to take oral medication and has signed informed consent. He has no history of retransplantation or multi-organ transplantation.

54-year-old Caucasian male returned from a two-week vacation in Thailand with a fever of 39.2°C and chills. He also reports fatigue, headache, and mild joint pain. He denies any respiratory or gastrointestinal symptoms. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. He takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no known drug allergies. He has no history of travel-related illnesses in the past. He received the recommended vaccinations for Thailand before his trip. He has health insurance and is willing to have his medical records reviewed for the study. He agrees to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of being involved.

A 45-year-old female who has been experiencing dry eyes and discomfort for the past 3 months. She reports that her eyes often feel gritty, itchy and she experiences a burning sensation. She has tried over-the-counter eye drops without much relief. Upon examination, she is found to have meibomian gland dysfunction and evidence of meibomian gland obstruction. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She has no history of glaucoma, ocular hypertension or intraocular pressure. She does not have any corneal abnormalities or disorders that impact normal spreading of the tear film. She has not had punctal plugs or punctal cautery in either eye. She is looking for a new treatment option to alleviate her dry eye symptoms and improve her overall eye health.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. A CT scan revealed a spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage in the right hemisphere of the brain. The patient's NIHSS score on admission was 18. He has no history of epilepsy or antiepileptic medication. The patient is a competent adult and is affiliated with the French National Health Insurance. He has given informed consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have any serious illness that could affect his prognosis within 3 months. He does not have severe renal impairment, lactose intolerance, or any known hypersensitivity to levetiracetam or other pyrrolidone derivatives. The patient is not under measuring socio-legal protection.

The patient is a 53-year-old male who has been diagnosed with liver cancer with a history of cirrhosis. He has been advised to undergo hepatic resection surgery. He has no significant past medical history except for cirrhosis and liver cancer. The patient has not undergone any other surgeries in the past. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and acid reflux. The patient is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic. The patient's body mass index (BMI) is 27.2 kg/m². The patient has a good appetite, but his diet is not well balanced. He has been advised to follow a specific diet to improve his nutritional status before the surgery. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed written consent.

This study is seeking a healthy male participant between the ages of 19-35 years old. The participant should not have taken antibiotics recently and should not have any gastrointestinal diseases, diabetes, psychological diseases, thyroid-related diseases, cardiovascular diseases, celiac disease, or be taking cortisone drugs. The study aims to analyze the gut microbiota using molecular genetic methods and measure stress levels through cortisol levels in saliva and a questionnaire.

The patient is a 52-year-old non-smoking Chinese woman who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer two years ago. She had a biopsy that confirmed the presence of an EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion), and she received first-line treatment with an EGFR-TKI. She had a good response to the treatment, but unfortunately, the cancer progressed after several months of therapy. She underwent a biopsy again, and it was confirmed that she does not have the T790M mutation. She has no history of other cancers or significant medical conditions. She is currently experiencing shortness of breath and cough, and diagnostic imaging revealed several lung nodules, including one that is measurable according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. She has not received any other systemic chemotherapy for her lung cancer, and she has not been on EGFR-TKI therapy for at least two weeks prior to enrollment. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 2 years. He is a former smoker and quit smoking 6 months ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and sputum production. He works as a construction worker and his symptoms have been affecting his work performance. He has been taking bronchodilators but has not noticed much improvement in his symptoms. His CCQ score is 2.5 indicating moderate impairment of health status. His FEV1 is 50% of predicted and his BMI is 28. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who works full-time as a marketing manager. She has been taking care of her mother who has been diagnosed with dementia for the past 6 months. She spends at least 2 hours per day taking care of her mother's daily needs, such as bathing, dressing, and feeding. She lives with her mother and her husband, who is supportive of her caregiving responsibilities. The patient has experienced caregiver burden and feels overwhelmed with her responsibilities. She also reports feeling guilty when she is unable to spend time with her mother due to her work obligations. The patient has access to a telephone and is interested in participating in the HEART intervention to receive support and guidance on how to better care for her mother while maintaining her work responsibilities. She has no other significant medical history and is not pregnant.

60-year-old male diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) or chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) or low-blast acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) with a white blood cell (WBC) count of less than 13,000/microliter (mcL). The diagnosis should be morphologically confirmed. The patient must also have one of the following Prognostic Risk Categories, based on the Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R): Very high (>6 points), High (>4.5-6 points), Intermediate (>3-4.5 points): a participant determined to be in the Intermediate Prognostic Risk Category is only allowable in the setting of >=5% bone marrow myeloblasts. The patient should have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status of 0, 1, or 2. The patient should not have had previous treatment for HR MDS or CMML or low-blast AML with chemotherapy or other antineoplastic agents including hypomethylating agent (HMAs) such as decitabine or azacitidine. The patient should not be eligible for intensive chemotherapy and/or allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The patient should not have either clinical evidence of or history of central nervous system involvement by AML. The patient should not have active uncontrolled infection or severe infectious disease, such as severe pneumonia, meningitis, or septicemia. The patient's prothrombin time (PT) or aPTT should not be >1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN) or active uncontrolled coagulopathy or bleeding disorder. The patient should not have known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) seropositive, known hepatitis B surface antigen seropositive, or known or suspected active hepatitis C infection. The patient should not have known hepatic cirrhosis or severe preexisting hepatic impairment. The patient should not have treatment with strong cytochrome P 3A (CYP3A) inducers within 14 days before the first dose of pevonedist

The patient is a 62 year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer after experiencing urinary symptoms such as frequent urination and weak urine stream. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 7 (4+3). The patient has no significant medical history and his ECOG performance status is 0. Imaging studies showed that the cancer is localized to less than 50% of the prostate gland. The patient has been offered curative-intent HDR brachytherapy boost to external beam radiotherapy and is considering enrolling in the trial to determine if fBT boost (15Gy) to SBRT (35Gy/5) is superior to standard care (whole-gland BT boost 15Gy to RT 37.5Gy/15) in terms of urinary toxicity. The patient is able to understand and sign the informed consent form and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) due to hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on thrice-weekly hemodialysis for the past 8 months. His weight is 85 Kg, and he has no significant medical history other than ESRD. He is compliant with his medications, which include antihypertensives, insulin, and aspirin. He has no known allergies, no history of substance abuse, and does not smoke. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. His physical examination is unremarkable, except for the presence of a fistula in his left arm for vascular access. His laboratory results show a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, serum creatinine of 8.5 mg/dL, and serum potassium of 4.5 mEq/L. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effects of different convective therapies in improving his dialysis outcomes. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and signs the written consent form.

52-year-old male with a history of alcohol use disorder and intravenous drug use presented to the emergency department complaining of fatigue, abdominal pain, nausea, and yellowing of the skin and eyes. He reported having unprotected sex with multiple partners in the past and shared needles with other injecting drug users. He has a history of being incarcerated for drug-related charges. He has not been regularly seeing a healthcare provider and has not been screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) or hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections before. He is admitted to the General Internal Medicine Inpatient Unit at Toronto General Hospital for further evaluation and management. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 35-year-old man presents with a complaint of neck pain that has been bothering him for about 6 months. The pain started gradually and is now described as a constant, dull ache in the neck that radiates down to the shoulders. He reports no history of trauma or injury to the neck. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications but found no relief. He works as an office manager and spends most of the day sitting at a desk using a computer. He denies any other significant medical history, including no history of neurological damage or psychiatric disorders. On physical examination, he has tenderness in the cervical spine and decreased range of motion. The neurological screening checklist is negative. He is diagnosed with mechanical neck disorder (MND) without neurological damage according to the Classification of the Quebec Task Force on Spinal Disorders. He is eligible to participate in the clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of manual therapy (MT) with Electric Nerve Stimulation (TENS) to reduce pain intensity in patients with MND. He provides consent to participate in the study.

32 year old woman with a history of psychological trauma but without the diagnosis of post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or other major mental disorder. She reports experiencing a traumatic event at the age of 14 and has had difficulty coping with the associated memories and emotions since that time. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating closed loop vagal nerve stimulation (VNS) for the treatment of PTSD. She has no history of meningitis, traumatic brain injury or neurological disorder. She denies current or lifetime history of substance abuse or dependence and has no history of schizophrenia or bulimia. She has no major medical or neurological illnesses and her laboratory studies, including CBC, BUN, creatinine, blood sugar, electrolytes, liver and thyroid function tests, urinalysis, and EKG are within normal limits. She is not pregnant and reports regular menstrual cycles.

The patient is a healthy male, between 35 and 55 years of age, with a body mass index between 19 and 30 kg/m2. He should have no history of hematological, renal, urinary/prostatic, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular or other heart diseases, glaucoma, diabetes, hepatic, neurologic, or allergic diseases. He should have a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure of less than 90 mmHg, and heart rate of less than 90 beats/min. The patient must not have a history of psychiatric illness, suicidal or homicidal behavior or attempts, or substance abuse or dependence. The patient should not be using prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements within 7 days prior to the first dose of study medication, unless approved by the investigator and GSK Medical Monitor. The patient should not have a history of sensitivity to any of the study medications or components thereof. Smoking or regular use of tobacco- or nicotine-containing products within 6 months prior to screening will exclude the patient from the study. The patient should not have a cardiac pacemaker or other electronic device or ferromagnetic metal foreign bodies. The patient should be willing to comply with the procedures outlined in the protocol and capable of giving written informed consent.

A 45 year old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer in her right breast. She will be undergoing surgery with axillary lymph node dissection (ALND) for the removal of 10 lymph nodes. The patient has no history of lymphedema and has not received any previous treatment for breast cancer. She is fluent in Danish and able to effectively communicate verbally. She does not have any conditions known to cause swelling and does not have a pace maker. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old premenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with endometrial hyperplasia without atypia. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her menstrual cycle is regular and lasts for 5-6 days. She has no history of infertility or any other gynecological disorders. Her waist circumference is 30 inches and her hip circumference is 36 inches. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. Blood tests showed a fasting blood glucose level of 85 mg/dL, postprandial blood glucose level of 110 mg/dL, and normal levels of sex hormones, liver and kidney function. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy of Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (MPA) with dydrogesterone for the management of her endometrial hyperplasia without atypia. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no history of liver or kidney disease, malignancy, or any other contradictions against progesterone. She is willing to follow the treatment plan and will be able to attend follow-up appointments for the next 2 years.

A 25-year-old male with a history of regular dental checkups and cleanings, and good oral hygiene practices, including twice-daily brushing and daily flossing. He has no significant medical history, takes no regular medications, and does not smoke or use tobacco products. He has no oral conditions that could interfere with the study, such as advanced periodontal disease or oral tumors. He has at least 16 gradable teeth and is willing to refrain from using any non-study oral hygiene products for the duration of the study. He agrees to delay any elective dentistry until the completion of the study and is available to return for all scheduled visits and follow the study procedures.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been experiencing severe tooth pain for the past week. He has tried taking over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not provided any relief. He has a history of dental caries and has had several fillings in the past. His dentist has recommended root canal therapy as the best treatment option to alleviate his pain. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any prescription medications. He has never undergone root canal therapy before and is willing to participate in the study to help identify pre-operative risk factors that may contribute to severe post-operative pain. The patient is able to return for follow-up appointments and is committed to complying with all study requirements.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents with symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. An exercise stress test was performed, which showed ST depression in the inferior leads, indicating myocardial ischemia. The patient is recommended for a SPECT-MPI test to evaluate the extent of the ischemia. He has no history of asthma or COPD, and he is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study drugs. His past medical history is negative for hepatitis B or C, and he has not had a recent history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. His blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial after being informed about the study and its purpose.

A 55-year-old African American man with a family history of prostate cancer is interested in enrolling in a Prostate Cancer Risk Assessment Program. He is currently in good health and has no history of cancer. He is married with two children and works as a teacher. He has a high monitoring style and tends to worry about his health. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no difficulty communicating in English and is competent to give informed consent.

45 yo F with a long history of rheumatoid arthritis who has had limited success with previous treatments, including methotrexate and sulfasalazine. The patient is currently experiencing moderate to severe joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, which is affecting her ability to perform daily activities and work. She has been recommended by her physician to start treatment with adalimumab. Past Medical History: Rheumatoid arthritis, hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Medications: Lisinopril, atorvastatin. Allergies: None known.

A 45-year-old man presents with a history of palpitations and shortness of breath. He is a non-smoker and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age. The physical examination revealed a systolic murmur at the apex, a double apical impulse and S4. The electrocardiogram showed left ventricular hypertrophy and nonspecific ST-T changes. Echocardiography revealed asymmetric septal hypertrophy with a maximum wall thickness of 32mm, left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and diastolic dysfunction. Cardiac MRI revealed extensive fibrosis involving the mid-septum, anterior wall, and apex of the left ventricle. 24-hour Holter monitoring showed multiple episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia. The patient is on beta-blocker therapy and has an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) for secondary prevention of sudden cardiac death. He is motivated to participate in the trial to understand more about his condition and to help others with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

A 47-year-old woman presents with chronic low back pain for the past year. She was diagnosed with lumbar spondylolisthesis by her spine specialty physician based on clinical evaluation and lumbar radiographs. She has no history of lumbar spinal fusion or any procedure resulting in the presence of metallic implants at the level of interest. She is willing to provide written consent to participate in the study and undergo a second MRI approximately 6 months after the first one. She has no history of pregnancy or any condition that would prevent her from undergoing MRI. She is interested in participating in this study to help improve the accuracy of diagnosis and treatment for lumbar spondylolisthesis.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been admitted to the hospital with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has a history of lung cancer and has been receiving chemotherapy for the past 6 months. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past week and his condition has not improved with antibiotics. The attending physician suspects invasive pulmonary aspergillosis

57-year-old male, previously a lifelong endurance athlete, has been competing in triathlons, cycling, and distance running since the age of 25. He has been involved in competitions at regional, national, and international levels and has been training for more than 10 hours per week. He has no history of smoking, diabetes, or cardiopulmonary disorders. He has a healthy diet and abstinence from smoking. He has been experiencing occasional chest pain and has been advised by his physician to undergo further evaluation. He is willing to participate in the Master@Heart Trial, which investigates whether lifelong endurance exercise reduces the incidence of non-calcified plaques (both mixed and soft plaques) as compared to late-onset endurance exercise and a non-athletic lifestyle. He agrees to follow the study protocol, which includes regular exercise, healthy diet, and abstinence from smoking. He is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and has signed and dated the informed consent prior to participation.

A 45-year-old man with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption is diagnosed with stage III anal cancer. He has no other significant medical history and has not received any prior treatment for cancer. He has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform all activities of daily living independently. His blood tests show a white blood cell count of 3,500/mm^3, a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3, and a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL. His creatinine level is within normal limits, and he has no cardiac condition that would contraindicate the use of fluorouracil. He has not received any prior pelvic or inguinal radiotherapy and has no other serious medical or psychological conditions. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks involved.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has been diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis. He has been experiencing symptoms of angina and exertional syncope, and has been deemed ineligible for surgical replacement of the aortic valve due to his high risk. He is a candidate for TAVR and will undergo pre-operative testing, including EKG-gated cardiac Multislice CTA and coronary angiography to evaluate aortic valve anatomy and aortic root dimensions for device sizing. Due to the risk of contrast-induced nephropathy, the patient will also undergo DynaCT during coronary angiography, which utilizes less contrast media. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate is above 40 mL/min/1.73m2 and he does not have any allergies to contrast media. He has given informed consent to participate in the study. After the study has reached its target recruitment, measurements of the major aortic annulus diameter, orthogonal minor aortic annulus diameter, aortic annulus perimeter, maximum ascending aorta diameter at 40mm above the annulus, sinus of Valsalva diameters, sinus of Valsalva heights, and aortic root angulation will be made using both the CTA and DynaCT protocols by a radiologist blinded to patient identity. Based on these measurements, a trained interventional cardiologist will select the appropriate TAVR size in a similarly blinded fashion after the study has reached its target recruitment.

The patient is an 18-year-old individual who has been living with HIV since birth. They have been receiving care at a pediatric/adolescent clinic and are now preparing to transition to adult care within the next 6 months. The patient owns a smartphone and/or tablet and has consistent access to the internet. They are located in either Atlanta, GA or Philadelphia, PA. The patient is willing to participate in the iTransition Development trial to evaluate the effectiveness of the mobile app in improving healthcare transition for youth living with HIV. The patient's medical chart will be reviewed to measure clinical outcomes, including linkage to adult care, care retention, and viral suppression.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with bilateral idiopathic Parkinson's disease three years ago. He experiences rigidity and bradykinesia, with occasional resting tremors. His UPDRS III score is 30 in the meds OFF condition, indicating a significant impact on his daily activities. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and he does not have any significant psychiatric problems, drug or alcohol abuse, recurrent or unprovoked seizures, or terminal illness. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the programming effects of the Boston Scientific Vercise™ PC System using the DBS Directional Lead for bilateral STN DBS in treating his Parkinson's disease symptoms.

The patient is a 47-year-old female who was admitted to the Royal Columbian Hospital neuroscience unit with a diagnosis of traumatic brain injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident. The patient is non-intubated, but dependent on care for all activities of daily living, including oral care. The patient has impaired swallowing and cough reflexes, and is at an increased risk of aspiration. The patient is unable to direct their own oral care and is therefore eligible for the study. The patient has no known allergies or pre-existing medical conditions that would exclude them from the study.

The patient is a 21-year-old male student at Eastern Medical College who is in good general health and has no history of chronic illness or medication use. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the diurnal variation in urinary excretion of paracetamol. The patient will receive a 500 mg oral paracetamol tablet at morning, midday and night in two-week intervals. Urine samples will be collected before and 4 hours after paracetamol administration and will be analysed by HPLC to estimate the concentration of paracetamol in the urine. The patient has no known history of hypersensitivity to paracetamol and has normal renal and hepatic function. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old female presented with a six-month history of nausea, bloating, and early satiety. She reported occasional vomiting, but denied weight loss or significant abdominal pain. She had a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, for which she was taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She had undergone a cholecystectomy five years prior without complications. She denied any history of gastrointestinal malignancy or mechanical obstruction. Her physical exam was unremarkable except for mild epigastric tenderness. Upper endoscopy revealed mild gastritis and no evidence of ulcerations or erosions. Gastric emptying scintigraphy was performed, which showed delayed emptying of solid food from the stomach, consistent with gastroparesis. She was referred to the gastroenterology motility specialty clinic at the University of Florida (UF) for further evaluation and treatment. She met the clinical and radiologic diagnostic criteria for diagnosis of GP and was deemed eligible for the clinical trial. She was not on any medications that would interfere with the study protocol and was not pregnant or nursing. Her EKG did not show any evidence of QT prolongation. She consented to participate in the study and was randomized to either the azithromycin or erythromycin treatment group.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2 is admitted to the ICU with sepsis and respiratory failure. The patient has a history of smoking one pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. He has a BMI of 28. The patient has no history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Upon admission, the patient was started on continuous veno-venous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) due to acute kidney injury (AKI). The patient is scheduled to receive anticoagulant prophylaxis with enoxaparin 40 mg sc. once daily as per the hospital protocol. The patient's platelet count is 120 G/L and prothrombin time is 75%. The patient has not received any antiplatelet drugs prior to admission. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, or allergies to enoxaparin or fondaparinux. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing high levels of anxiety for the past year. She has no known neurological history and is insured under the French social security system. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological or psychological disorders but her anxiety levels were found to be higher than 35 on the STAI-YA scale. She is not currently taking any anxiolytic or benzodiazepine medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is able to give consent. She has no visual, hearing, sensory or motor deficits that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is interested in the study and willing to undergo auditory neurofeedback training sessions and electrophysiological (EEG) and clinical measurements to help with her anxiety.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently found out about her high blood sugar levels during a routine check-up. She has a family history of diabetes and is concerned about developing the disease. Her BMI is 24 and she has no history of debilitating diseases or allergies to beans. She is interested in participating in the Full Plate Diet Study to learn how to increase her fiber intake and potentially improve her blood sugar levels. She is able to attend one weekly session and is committed to making changes in her diet to improve her health.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian female who has moderate to severe sun-damage on her face due to chronic exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light. She has a previous history of retinoid intolerance that was established through a prior history and a 2-week retinoid treatment phase of this study. She is generally healthy and lives within a reasonable driving distance of Ann Arbor, Michigan, and/or can attend all scheduled appointments during the study. She has not used any topical or systemic retinoids in the past 6 months and is not pregnant or nursing. She has no history of non-melanoma skin cancer on her face in the past 5 years, no history of malignant melanoma, and no other skin condition or facial hair that will interfere with the study evaluations. She is not on any special daily skin care regimens that include cleansing with Dove, Olay, Aveeno, or Cetaphil liquid facial cleansers and using facial moisturizers more than twice a day. She is willing to use an accepted form of birth control for the entire duration of the study.

A full-term male neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 29-year-old G1P1 mother. The pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the mother received adequate prenatal care. The Apgar score at 1 minute was 6, and at 5 minutes it was 8. The baby was found to have respiratory distress, and supplemental oxygen was initiated. The baby was noted to be lethargic, with poor feeding and decreased tone. The baby was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit for further management. The baby was diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and was started on hypothermia treatment within 6 hours of age. The mother had given verbal consent for cord blood collection at delivery, and the cord blood was collected and stored. The baby is eligible for the study and will be randomized to receive either autologous cord blood or placebo within 48 hours of age.

54 yo F with a history of Type 2 diabetes for 9 years. She is currently being treated with metformin and a GLP-1 agonist. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.5%. She has a history of hypertension for 5 years, which is controlled with lisinopril. The patient was referred to the study due to her persistent albuminuria, with a UACR of 2500 mg/g and an eGFR of 45 ml/min/1.73m2. She has been on an ACE inhibitor for the past 6 months, but her albuminuria remains high. She has no history of gout or renal transplant. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the investigational drug, TMX-049, will help lower her albuminuria levels.

55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. She lives in a low-income neighborhood and has never participated in the national colorectal cancer screening program. She has limited access to healthcare resources and transportation, and has expressed concerns about the screening process and its potential discomfort. The patient has a family history of colorectal cancer, but has not undergone any previous screening or surveillance for the disease. She speaks French but has limited literacy skills. She has expressed interest in participating in the study and receiving assistance with navigating the screening process.

The patient is a 4-year-old child weighing 20 kg who is scheduled for an elective surgery that will last less than 2 hours under general anesthesia using a supraglottic airway. The child has no history of difficult airway and does not have any risk of aspiration such as gastroesophageal reflux disease or active upper respiratory tract infection. The child's parents have provided informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial.

A 28 year old male who identifies as a transgender woman visits the clinic for a routine checkup. They are HIV-uninfected and currently taking Truvada as PrEP due to their high risk of HIV infection. The patient has a BMI of 23 and reports no history of fragility fractures or kidney stones. They have never taken bisphosphonate therapy or androgenic hormones. The patient currently takes a multivitamin but not a Vitamin D supplement. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the effect of Vitamin D supplementation on bone turnover markers during PrEP in MSM.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and osteoarthritis. She takes multiple medications daily to manage her conditions, including insulin injections for her diabetes. She has a history of falls and has difficulty with mobility, requiring assistance from her daughter for activities of daily living. She has been admitted to the hospital twice in the past year due to complications related to her diabetes and hypertension. She lives alone in a small apartment and has limited social support. She struggles with managing her medications and has difficulty keeping track of her appointments with various specialists. She is interested in participating in a program that can provide her with more comprehensive care and support to help manage her health conditions.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and obesity presents with abdominal discomfort and fatigue. She reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods and sugar. Blood work shows elevated liver enzymes and imaging reveals evidence of liver fibrosis. A liver biopsy confirms the presence of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with fibrosis stage 2. The patient is not on any medications for NASH or related conditions and has not undergone any weight-loss surgeries. She has not been diagnosed with any other chronic liver diseases and does not have a history of significant alcohol consumption. Her BMI is 35 kg/m2. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential treatment for NASH with fibrosis.

Patient A is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is expecting her first child. She and her partner are both Norwegian and speak Norwegian fluently. She is currently in her 20th week of pregnancy and has not experienced any complications thus far. She has a history of depression and anxiety, and is worried about developing postpartum depression (PPD) after the birth of her child. She is interested in participating in The Northern Babies Longitudinal Study, which aims to explore a range of protective and risk factors for PPD, as well as parent-infant interactions and child development. She is particularly interested in the Newborn Behavioral Observation (NBO) as a universal preventive intervention to reduce depressive symptomatology in mothers. She hopes that by participating in this study, she will gain a better understanding of the factors that contribute to PPD and how to prevent it.

14 year old female student with no history of neck pain or other musculoskeletal conditions. The patient is in good overall health and does not participate in regular athletic activities. The patient comes from a middle-class family and attends school regularly. She regularly uses her smartphone for social media and texting. The patient is able to sit comfortably in a chair with her feet on the floor and her elbows slightly flexed. No upper limb or spinal deviations are noted. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help prevent muscle fatigue and pain associated with smartphone use.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 6 months ago. She has been receiving chemotherapy for the past few months and her platelet count has been gradually decreasing. Her current platelet count is 140,000. She has not received VELCADE treatment for the past 2 weeks and has stopped taking aspirin or ibuprofen as instructed. She has no history of heart disease or other serious medical conditions. She is postmenopausal and has no plans for pregnancy. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has given her voluntary written informed consent.

This is a 35 year old female who works as a graphic designer and spends a significant amount of time in front of a computer screen. She complains of eye discomfort, dryness, and occasional itchiness. She has a history of dry eye disease in both eyes and has not used Restasis® in the past 90 days. She has not had any recent eye infections or inflammation, nor has she had any eye surgeries in the last 6 months. She does not wear contact lenses and has not had LASIK in the last 12 months. She is not taking any medication known to cause ocular drying that cannot be discontinued for the trial duration. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy of Restasis® in maintaining visual performance while engaging in electronic visual tasking.

A 62-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with complaints of urinary frequency and hematuria. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is married with two children and works as a teacher. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. His physical examination was unremarkable except for mild suprapubic tenderness. His laboratory tests showed normal renal function and hemoglobin levels. A CT scan revealed a mass in the bladder with no evidence of metastasis. A biopsy confirmed urothelial carcinoma. He is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of having histologically or cytologically confirmed urothelial cancer of the bladder, locally advanced status for planning surgical treatment, age 18 years or older, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1, and adequate organ and bone marrow function for cisplatin-based chemotherapy. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed a written informed consent.

A 25 year old male athlete has been referred to the clinic for an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction surgery. The patient has a history of ACL injury and has been experiencing pain and instability in the knee joint. The patient is in good physical health with an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical status of I. There are no neurological diseases, allergies to drugs or ongoing opioid treatment. However, the patient has been diagnosed with type II diabetes mellitus and requires daily insulin injections. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the continuous infusion or intermittent automatic bolus group.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus 7 years ago. He has been taking metformin and sulfonylurea as prescribed by his personal physician for the last 3 years. His most recent HbA1c value was 8.5%. He has a BMI of 35 kg/m^2. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no known history of severe hypoglycemia or hospitalizations due to poor glucose control. He has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgeries or has no known history of pancreatitis or liver disease. He has no family history of neuroendocrine tumors or multiple endocrine neoplasia. He is willing to undergo magnetic resonance imaging as needed for the trial.

A 57-year-old woman presents with chronic knee pain for the past 5 years. Her past medical history is only significant for hypertension for which she is taking lisinopril (10 mg/day). She has been taking acetaminophen (1000 mg/day) and ibuprofen (400 mg/day) for knee pain for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have not improved. She reports no history of allergies or adverse drug reactions. She reports a history of knee osteoarthritis confirmed by X-ray. The diagnosis was made by her primary care physician based on her clinical symptoms of knee pain and stiffness, and radiological evidence of joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. She reports having grade 3 osteoarthritic changes in her knee based on the Kellgren and Lawrence scale. She has never tried Devil's Claw or any other complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) for her knee pain. She reports that her knee pain is interfering with her daily activities, including walking and household chores. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and to give informed consent. She is not pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.

A 50-year-old male with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma came to the clinic for consultation. He was diagnosed with the disease 6 months ago, and his condition has not improved despite undergoing standard chemotherapy. He has no other underlying diseases and is currently taking acetaminophen for pain relief. He does not have any allergies to any food or drugs. He is married with two children and works as a sales executive. He understands the study's risks and benefits and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 16-year-old male volleyball player who experiences shoulder pain while playing. He reports that the pain has been ongoing for the past month and rates it as a 6/10 on the Visual Analogue Scale. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of shoulder injuries or other musculoskeletal conditions. He trains for 3 hours a week and is an active participant in both training and competitions. His Kerlan-Jobe Orthopedic Clinical Shoulder & Elbow Score is 95/100. The patient is willing to complete all assessments in the study and is able to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI) in a car accident 8 months ago. She has been experiencing severe fatigue, which has greatly impacted her ability to perform daily activities. She has also been feeling sad and anxious since the accident. Her physician has determined that she is physically inactive and is able to stand and walk on a treadmill safely without assistance. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She is not currently on any medications that would influence aerobic capacity or treadmill performance. Her medical history and physical examination will be assessed at baseline, and she will complete questionnaires about fatigue, daily physical activity, sleep quality, mood, and overall quality of life. She will also undergo tests of thinking and a treadmill exercise test. She will then participate in a 12-week treadmill exercise training intervention protocol to improve her physical fitness, fatigue severity, and mood. She will have treadmill exercise training 3 days per week for 12 weeks, and each session will include a check-in, warm-up, treadmill walking at the training heart rate, and cool-down. After completing the exercise training program, she will undergo final testing visits to complete the questionnaires, tests of thinking, and a treadmill exercise test to assess any changes in cardiorespiratory fitness, fatigue severity, and cognitive performance. She will be monitored for any changes in mood reactivity throughout the study. She meets the eligibility criteria for this study and is willing to participate in this research to potentially improve her overall quality of life.

52F diagnosed with UPSC with PIK3CA gene mutation, previously underwent total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and adjuvant chemotherapy. After a year of follow-up, patient presented with recurrent UPSC on imaging. Patient has adequate bone marrow, liver and renal function, and fasting serum cholesterol and triglycerides within normal range. Patient has no prior therapy with mTOR inhibitors and no known intolerance or hypersensitivity to everolimus or other rapamycin analogs. Patient has controlled diabetes mellitus with fasting serum glucose within normal range. There are no severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions such as liver disease, severe lung function impairment, or active bleeding diathesis. The patient is not chronically treated with corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive agents and has no known history of HIV seropositivity. The patient is a woman of child-bearing potential and is willing to use highly effective contraception methods during the study and for 8 weeks after study drug administration. The patient is willing to comply with the treatment plan.

The patient is a 40 year old woman diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 5 years ago. She has been on a stable regimen of medications taken specifically to treat MS for the last 6 months and is willing to continue the same doses and regimens for the duration of study participation. She has been physically active for the past 3 months and is willing to continue without change for the duration of study participation. Her EDSS score during screening is 6.0.
