She has sufficient ambulatory ability to complete two trials of the Timed 25 Foot Walk (T25FW) at the screening visit with a score on each completed screening T25FW test between 10 and 40 seconds, inclusive. She is not taking any medications that could interfere with the study, and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period.

A 35-year-old woman has been experiencing nausea, vomiting, and significant weight loss for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with gastroparesis and has tried dietary changes and oral medications without much relief. She has a history of anxiety and depression and manages it with medication. She is otherwise healthy and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has been referred for endoscopic treatment of gastroparesis for symptom management and is interested in participating in research to improve patient management for this condition.

A 57-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III lung cancer is experiencing breathlessness with a score of 5/10 on the Numerical Rating Scale. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and has an ECOG performance score of 1. She has no history of cognitive impairment, and her estimated life expectancy is greater than 3 months according to her physician. She lives within a 45-kilometer driving radius of Princess Margaret Hospital and has an oxygen saturation of 92% at rest on room air. The patient is available for 8 consecutive weeks and is able to communicate effectively in English. She does not have a history of left heart failure, coronary artery or valvular heart disease, or neuromuscular disease.

The patient is a 65-year-old man recently diagnosed with prostate cancer, with no history of other cancers or significant comorbidities. He has a Gleason score of 7 and is of African-American ethnicity. The patient has a brother who was previously diagnosed with prostate cancer at the age of 60 and is also participating in this study. The patient and his brother are willing to provide blood samples for genomic DNA extraction to be sequenced for single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Akt and mdm-2 genes. They are interested in participating in this study to learn more about changes in DNA that may be related to prostate cancer and contribute to the advancement of prostate cancer research.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and revealed a mutation in the EGFR gene. She was treated with first-generation EGFR-TKI, but after a period of initial response, her cancer progressed. A biopsy confirmed the presence of the T790M mutation, and she was switched to a third-generation EGFR-TKI. She has been on this medication for several months and has shown a partial response with residual oligometastases in the lung and liver. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and is otherwise in good health. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the use of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for her residual oligometastases.

56 year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) presents with recurrent episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. The patient has been on anti-arrhythmic medication but has not been able to achieve adequate symptom control. The patient has been selected for an AF ablation procedure for pulmonary vein isolation. The patient is able and willing to comply with uninterrupted per-protocol anticoagulation requirements, is between the age of 18-75 years, and is able and willing to comply with all pre-, post- and follow-up testing and requirements. The patient has signed the patient informed consent form. The patient has not undergone previous surgical or catheter ablation for AF and is not anticipated to receive ablation outside the PV ostia and Cavo-triscuspid-isthmus (CTI) region. The patient does not have a history of myocardial infarction within the past 2 months or documented thromboembolic event within the past 12 months. The patient has no contraindication to anticoagulation and no history of blood clotting or bleeding abnormalities. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is above 40% and the patient is not experiencing uncontrolled heart failure or New York Heart Association (NYHA) function class III or IV. The patient does not have any significant pulmonary disease or any other disease or malfunction of the lungs or respiratory system that produces chronic symptoms. The patient does not have a significant congenital anomaly or medical problem that would preclude enrollment in this study.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who was previously treated for a hypothalamic tumor. She has been off cancer treatment for six months and has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness for the past three months. The sleepiness is affecting her ability to attend school and participate in social activities. She has no known medical disorders that could be causing the sleepiness and has not had any recent drug treatments. She is proficient in English and able to swallow capsules. The patient and her family have agreed to return to the clinic up to 8 times within 2 months. The patient has not taken methylphenidate or modafinil within the last 14 days and does not have any cardiac disorders or history of substance abuse. She is not currently taking antihistamines, benzodiazepine, anticonvulsants or alcohol. She has not been diagnosed with anemia, untreated hypothyroidism, mononucleosis or narcolepsy. The patient has not been diagnosed with major depression, subclinical depression, or anxiety disorder, and does not have a history of psychosis or mania. She is not experiencing suicidal ideation. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and her total dietary intake of caffeine is less than 500mg per day.

Maria is a 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo cisplatin-based chemotherapy (≥60 mg/m2) as part of her treatment plan. She has no previous history of chemotherapy. Her Karnofsky performance score is 80 and her predicted life expectancy is more than four months. She has no contraindications to cisplatin, granisetron, or dexamethasone. She has never taken 5-HT3 antagonists, Phenothiazines, Benzamides, Domperidone, Cannabinoids, or NK1 antagonists within the last 48 hours, and is not scheduled to receive any other chemotherapeutic agent with an emetogenicity level of 4 or above from Day 2 through Day 6, except on Day 1. She is not scheduled to receive any radiation therapy to the abdomen or pelvis from Day -5 through Day 6. She has not received systemic corticosteroids or sedative antihistamines within 72 hours of Day 1 of the study, except as premedication for chemotherapy. She has no symptomatic primary or metastatic CNS disease, ongoing vomiting, retching, clinically significant nausea caused by any etiology, or a history of anticipatory nausea and vomiting. She has not vomited or had dry heaves/retching within 24 hours prior to the start of cisplatin-based chemotherapy on Day 1 in Cycle 1.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who has been smoking 10 cigarettes a day for the past year. She has expressed her willingness and motivation to quit smoking upon randomization into the study. She has been using an oral contraceptive method for the past 6 months and is willing to continue using it throughout the study period. The patient has good oral health and general health, with no history of heart disease, diabetes, or peptic ulcer. She has not undergone any oral surgery or operative dental work in the past four weeks and has no clinically significant oral pathology. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical study or using any other nicotine replacement therapy. She has no known allergies or intolerance to the study materials or closely related compounds. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse in the past two years and has tested negative on the urine drug screen. The patient fully understands the study procedures and has provided voluntary written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with type 1 diabetes within the past 6 weeks. He participated in the PROTECT study, a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational, multi-center study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of teplizumab, a humanized, anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody. He received two courses of treatment administered 6 months apart and completed the study by finishing the Week 78 visit. He has no known allergies and is currently on daily insulin injections. His blood glucose levels are being monitored regularly by his primary physician. He is accompanied by his mother who has provided written informed consent for him to participate in the PROTECT Extension study, which will collect long-term safety and other clinical data. No study drug will be administered during this extension study. The patient and his mother are willing to return to the study site for assessments once every 6 months through Month 42.

A 58-year-old female patient presented with a history of shortness of breath, palpitations, and occasional dizziness for the past 3 months. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. She denies any history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She reports occasional leg pain while walking, but does not have any history of claudication. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is irregularly irregular at 90 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams are normal. Neurological examination is unremarkable. An electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation. An echocardiogram reveals mild left ventricular hypertrophy, and a normal ejection fraction. The patient is offered enrollment in a clinical trial assessing the prevalence of ankle-brachial index in atrial fibrillation patients. She is informed about the study and signs written informed consent. She is eligible for the study as she has non-valvular atrial fibrillation and is not pregnant or suffering from hyperthyroidism.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl scheduled for an elective surgery under general anesthesia. The child has been experiencing anxiety about the upcoming procedure and has been expressing fear of the operating room. The child's physical health is good, and she has no history of chronic diseases or developmental delays. The child's parents have provided informed written consent for the study. The child has not previously undergone general anesthesia or had any significant medical history. The child does not have any hearing or vision impairments, affective disorders, or history of epilepsy or seizure. The child is eligible for the study and will be participating in the virtual reality tour of the operating room to help reduce preoperative anxiety.

A 32-year-old woman has been smoking cigarettes for the past 10 years. She is a daily smoker and smokes about 10 cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit smoking multiple times in the past, but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in trying novel nicotine products to help her quit smoking. She speaks fluent English and is able to follow verbal and written instructions. She lives alone and has a telephone and address where she can be reached. She is not currently using any other e-cigarettes or smoking cessation medications. She has no history of illicit drug use, but occasionally uses marijuana recreationally. She is not currently taking any medications that are excluded from the study. She does not have any unstable medical conditions and has not experienced any abnormal heart rhythms or cardiovascular disease in the last 3 months. Her blood pressure reading is within the normal range. She has not been diagnosed with major depressive syndrome, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder. She only smokes cigarettes and has not used other tobacco products in the last month. She has not been involved in smoking cessation activities in the past 90 days and is not currently planning to participate in such activities. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using a medically acceptable method of birth control. She is considered suitable for participation in the study by the investigator.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl who is currently enrolled in Compulsory Secondary Education. She does not have any history of musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiological, metabolic, or rheumatic alterations. She is physically active and participates in the sessions of Physical Education regularly. The patient reports occasional episodes of back pain, especially after spending long hours sitting or studying. She has never received any treatment for her back pain. The patient is willing to participate in the study and attend at least 80% of the sessions. During the study, she will be required to perform Pilates exercises as part of her Physical Education sessions for 4.5 months and 9 months. She will be assessed for back pain, quality of life, sagittal spine curvature, hamstring extensibility, BMI, body fat percentage and the waist-hip index. The patient will be included in the experimental group and attend two weekly sessions of Pilates exercises for 10 minutes each, in addition to her regular Physical Education sessions. The exercises will focus on the resistance of the flexor muscles of the trunk, resistance of the trunk extensor musculature, and hamstring extensibility. The patient is expected to attend at least 91.66% of the sessions and complete all assessments throughout the study period.

50-year-old male who sustained a mild traumatic brain injury (TBI) 2 years ago due to a motor vehicle accident. He reports difficulty with memory, attention, and executive functioning, as well as decreased ability to perform daily activities. He denies any history of neurological disease or injury prior to the TBI. He is currently taking stable doses of medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has completed high school and can speak English fluently. He has no history of severe mental illness or untreated alcohol or substance abuse. He is interested in participating in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past year. She works as a nurse and has been finding it increasingly difficult to perform her job due to the pain. She has never taken opioids before and is scheduled for an elective surgery for a herniated disc. She is in good health otherwise with a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is married and has two children. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She does not have any liver disease or recent infections, nor is she on any medications that would prohibit her from participating in the study. She is motivated to participate in the study to potentially reduce any cognitive side effects from opioids and to have a smoother recovery period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male Veteran with a diagnosis of diabetes. He receives his medical care at the Greater LA VA Medical Center. He has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He is compliant with his medication regimen and has no other significant medical history. He is active and engages in regular exercise and a healthy diet. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. He has been undergoing annual retinal photography to screen for diabetic retinopathy. He has not developed any signs of diabetic retinopathy or macular edema so far. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that seeks to identify early biomarkers for the development of hypertension and diabetic retinopathy in Veterans with diabetes.

The patient is a 4-month-old baby girl who has been experiencing breathing difficulties and poor feeding for the past 24 hours. The mother reports that the baby has been coughing and has a runny nose for the past 2 days. The baby was born at full term and has no known medical conditions or allergies. The baby's weight is 6.5 kg. The respiratory rate is at 65 breaths per minute and the oxygen saturation level is at 90%. The baby has a dyspnea with respiratory distress assessment instrument (RDAI) score of 10. The baby is currently breastfeeding but has been taking less food than usual. There is no family history of respiratory or heart diseases. The baby has not been previously diagnosed with any respiratory illnesses.

56 year old woman with a history of ovarian cancer, who has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy, including platinum- and paclitaxel-based regimens. She has been experiencing recurrent disease despite these treatments. She presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. On examination, there is evidence of ascites and palpable abdominal mass. Imaging studies show evidence of disease progression. She is classified as having platinum-resistant disease. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. Her renal function is normal, with a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL and glomerular filtration rate of 70 mL/min. Liver function tests are within normal limits, with AST and ALT levels of 20 U/L and bilirubin concentration of 0.9 mg/dL. Her bone marrow function is also within normal limits, with a neutrophil count of 2.5 x 109/L and a platelet count of 150 x109/L. She has undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. She has no known cardiac disease. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is interested in exploring new treatment options for her recurrent ovarian cancer.

This clinical trial is seeking adult volunteers who are interested in participating in a study to assess the safety and effectiveness of the ivWatch Model 400 device. The study is looking for individuals who are 18 years or older, pass a health screening, and are willing to provide informed consent. There are no specific medical conditions that are required or excluded for participation in this study. The study aims to assess the device's ability to observe non-infiltrated (normal) tissues at common peripheral IV therapy sites. If you are interested in participating in this study, please contact the study coordinator for more information on how to enroll.

A 45-year-old woman has been experiencing neck and arm pain for the past 6 months. She has undergone conservative treatment, including physical therapy and medication, but with no improvement. CT and MRI scans have revealed that she has symptomatic cervical disc disease at one level between C3 and C7, with a loss of disc height and radiculopathy. She has a Neck Disability Index (NDI) Questionnaire score of 35 out of 50. She meets the age requirement of 18 to 60 years old and is mentally and physically capable of following the protocol and complying with the follow-up schedule. She has no prior surgery or fusion adjacent to the vertebral level being treated, and her vertebral bodies at the affected level are not clinically compromised due to trauma. She has no marked cervical instability or facet joint disease, severe spondylosis, or osteoporosis. She is not pregnant or interested in becoming pregnant in the next two years, and she has no active systemic or local infection or known allergy to titanium, polyethylene, cobalt, chromium, or molybdenum. She is not taking any medications or drugs known to interfere with bone or soft tissue healing, nor does she have any neuromuscular disorders or acute mental illness or substance abuse. She has not participated in any other investigational device or drug clinical trials within the past 30 days.

45 year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder type II who has been hospitalized due to a recent manic episode. Her symptoms include elevated and irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, and poor judgement. She has a history of multiple hospitalizations for bipolar disorder and has tried various medications in the past with limited success. She currently lives with her husband and two young children. Her husband has been identified as her primary caregiver and is actively involved in her treatment. He reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed by her recent hospitalization and is interested in learning more about how he can support his wife's treatment and improve their family's overall functioning. Past Medical History: 1. Bipolar disorder type II 2. History of multiple hospitalizations for bipolar disorder 3. Previous medication trials with limited success.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was admitted to the pediatric ward due to respiratory distress. He has a history of asthma and was treated with nebulization and systemic steroids. He is now hemodynamically stable and requires intravenous maintenance fluids. His weight is

The patient is a 36-year-old Singaporean female who works as a full-time office manager at a law firm. She has a 9-year-old daughter who is in primary school. She is concerned about her and her daughter's physical activity levels as they both lead busy lives and spend most of their time sitting in front of a computer or studying. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to increase physical activity levels in both herself and her daughter. She has no major medical conditions but does have a family history of heart disease. She is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to wear a wireless pedometer for 12 months and an accelerometer for 1 week at baseline, month 6, and month 12 assessments. She is excited about the prospect of earning financial incentives for increasing her and her daughter's physical activity levels.

9-year-old male patient who underwent liver transplantation 8 months ago due to biliary atresia. The patient has a history of seasonal flu infection prior to transplantation. The patient is currently on immunosuppressive therapy and has no known allergies to eggs or egg protein. The patient's parents are willing to participate in the study and have signed the informed consent form. The patient does not have any history of Guillain-Barre syndrome, rituximab therapy, or rejection treatment with intravenous steroid bolus or monoclonal antibody. The patient is available for the duration of the study, and the parent or guardian can be reached by phone.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who was diagnosed with HIV at the age of 4. He has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) since diagnosis and has failed first line NNRTI-based therapy and second line PI-based therapy. His most recent viral load was 20,000 copies/ml and his CD4 count was 350 cells/mm3. The patient is currently experiencing intolerance to the current NRTI, NNRTI or PI treatment and needs to receive darunavir, etravirine, tipranavir or raltegravir. The patient is fluent in Thai and has a legal guardian who is willing to provide consent for the patient's participation in the study. The patient does not have hepatic impairment with ALT ≥ 5 upper limit of normal and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 62-year-old man was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer after experiencing difficulty with urination. A biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma and he was classified as high-risk due to a PSA level of 22 and a Gleason Score of 9. His imaging studies showed extra-prostatic extension. He was referred for radiation therapy and is scheduled to receive prostatic and pelvic IMRT with ACCULOC® target localization. The patient has no history of radical prostatectomy or prior pelvic radiation. He is generally in good health with an ECOG Performance Status of 1. The patient is willing and able to sign the informed consent document and participate in the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old right-handed woman with no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders came to the clinic for the Clinical Qualification Study of Electroencephalographic Mobile Equipment for the Capture of Emotions. She reported that she is sensitive to "music chill" and scored above 50 on the Barcelona Reward Music Questionnaire. She agreed to participate in the study and has health insurance coverage. She has no auditory deficits and is not pregnant.

A 25-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential West Nile Virus vaccine. He has no history of chronic medical conditions or allergies to components of the study product. He is sexually active and agrees to use medically acceptable contraception throughout the study period. He is willing to participate for the planned duration of the study which is approximately 14 months. He is able to read, sign, and date the informed consent document. He has not received any experimental agents or blood products in the past 30 days prior to enrollment. He has not donated blood within 56 days prior to enrollment and does not plan to donate blood during the study period. He has not received any inactivated vaccine or allergy desensitization injection 14 days before or after a study vaccination and does not plan to receive any live attenuated vaccine 30 days before or after a study vaccination. He has not attended primary school in Austria, Germany, Japan, South Korea, India, Thailand, Nepal, Vietnam, or Taiwan where tick-borne encephalitis vaccine is given. He has not received any dengue fever vaccine nor has he had dengue fever. He is not currently breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed throughout the study period. He has not enrolled in another clinical trial that could interfere with safety assessment of the investigational product at any time during the study period. He has not received any blood products or immunoglobulin within six months prior to enrollment. He does not have a systolic blood pressure over 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure over 90 mm Hg, and his resting heart rate is between 40 to 100 beats per minute. His oral temperature is less than 38 degrees C (100.4 degrees F) and he has a negative serology for HIV 1/2, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), and antibody to hepatitis C virus (HCV). He does not have any Grade 1 or higher screening clinical lab value. He plans to maintain his current exercise routine throughout the study period.

A 25-year-old female beachgoer who spends a lot of time in the water presents for a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of a jellyfish sting inhibitor sun lotion and protocols for jellyfish sting pain relief. She has fair skin and is prone to sunburns, but she always uses a high SPF sunscreen when exposed to the sun. She has never experienced jellyfish stings before, but she is aware of the risks and wants to participate in the study to potentially help others who may encounter jellyfish in the future. She has no known allergies or medical conditions, and her skin on both forearms is free of any visible skin diseases or excessive hair. She is willing to follow the study's protocols and restrictions, such as avoiding the use of any medical or cosmetic products on her arms for 48 hours before the start of the experiment.

The patient is a 50-year-old Egyptian woman suffering from end-stage liver disease due to primary biliary cirrhosis. She has been on the liver transplant waiting list for 6 months and has now been selected for a living donor liver transplant. Her donor is her 25-year-old son who is healthy and compatible. She has no history of renal failure or diabetes, and her glomerular filtration rate is greater than 60 ml/min. She has undergone all the required preoperative assessments and preparations, including imaging techniques such as abdominal triphasic CAT Scan and liver biopsy. Her MELD score corrected for serum sodium level is 22. Her serum levels of AST, ALT, bilirubin, albumin, ALP, GGT, prothrombin, INR, partial thrombin time, factor V, fasting blood glucose, CBC, CRP, Procalcitonin, urea, creatinine, urinary creatinine clearance, serum electrolytes, urine, and stool analysis have been analyzed, and she has tested negative for HCV and HBV. She will be randomized to one of the three groups based on her preoperative serum taurine level, which will be measured using HPLC four times (preoperative, 7, 14, and 30 days post-transplant). She has given informed consent to participate in the study and will be monitored for primary graft function and any postoperative complications for 30 days after the transplant.

A 38-year-old woman was diagnosed with cervical cancer and underwent a total hysterectomy followed by pelvic radiation therapy. She completed radiation therapy six months ago and has been experiencing vaginal dryness, pain, and discomfort during sexual intercourse, which has negatively impacted her relationship with her partner. She has tried using vaginal lubricants, but found them to be insufficient in relieving her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve women's sexual function after pelvic radiation. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She has no history of major untreated or uncontrolled mental illness.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with worsening heart failure and renal dysfunction. She has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. She has been on furosemide and metolazone for the past 2 years, but her symptoms have been progressively worsening. Her most recent laboratory workup showed an estimated creatinine clearance of 45 mL/min and BNP level of 800 pg/mL. She has been on angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, beta-blockers, and aldosterone antagonist for her heart failure. She is currently not on any dialysis or mechanical circulatory support. She has no history of seizures, stroke, brain tumor, or encephalitis/meningitis. She is not taking any medications that are contraindicated for this study.

There are no specific patient descriptions for this clinical trial as MAPCOG-SEEG is an observational database study that aims to collect brain recordings of cognition performed in clinical routine in patients during the pre-surgical SEEG assessment. However, potential patients who may be eligible for SEEG exploration in the context of presurgical assessment of epilepsy and have drug-resistant focal epilepsy, can be considered for this study if they meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria mentioned in the eligibility section. It is important to note that patients with major legal protection measures or those deprived of liberty due to a judicial or administrative decision, and pregnant women are excluded from the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with bilateral cataracts. She is scheduled for elective cataract surgery under general anesthesia at Mansoura ophthalmology center. She has no significant past medical history and her family history is non-contributory. She is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) II patient. Her parents have provided informed written consent for her participation in the study. She has no gastroesophageal reflux or oropharyngeal pathology and does not have any respiratory or developmental disorders. She has no known sensitivity to the anesthetics that will be used. She has not had any previous surgery on her eyes.

The patient is a 30 year old Hispanic female who has a Fitzpatrick skin type ll. She is a stay-at-home mom with two children and enjoys spending time outdoors with her family. She has no known allergies to sunscreens, cosmetics or toiletries and is in good health. She has never been diagnosed with any dermatologic conditions or any other medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She has not taken any antihistamines or corticosteroids in the past week or any antibiotics in the past two weeks. She is not currently taking any chronic medication that could affect the results of the study. She is not pregnant or nursing at this time. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effectiveness of sunscreens and sun protection on her skin.

The patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with estrogen receptor-positive primary breast cancer five years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy for six months. She was then treated with tamoxifen for two years and has been in remission since then. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. Her physical examination is within normal limits, and her laboratory results show no abnormalities. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive adjuvant treatment with exemestane and help advance breast cancer research.

The patient is a 54-year-old Caucasian man who was recently diagnosed with liver cancer. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss for the past few months. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. His past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He has been taking medication for these conditions. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker and enjoys playing golf. He has been referred to Anhui Medical University for liver resection. The preoperative imaging suggests that both BiClamp forceps hepatectomy and clamp-crushing hepatectomy techniques are feasible. His Child-Pugh score is A. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

55 year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 3, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity with a BMI of 35 kg/m2. She has been struggling with physical activity and has noted a decrease in her quality of life. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently well controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiac failure, motor disorders, or dementia. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help improve her physical activity and obesity.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease 10 years ago. He has been experiencing progressively worsening dyskinesia symptoms and motor fluctuations for the past year, despite being on a stable dose of PD medications. He has had no surgical interventions for Parkinson's disease in the past. He has a Hoehn and Yahr stage of 2 in the ON medication state and a MDS-UPDRS score of 30 in the meds OFF condition. He has been on stable antidepressant medication for the past 6 months, with no significant cognitive impairment as indicated by a MMSE score of 28. He has no history of alcohol or drug dependency, and his cardiac status is stable. He is not currently taking any anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy, nor is he on any drugs known to increase the risk of hemorrhage. He has no history of kidney disease, intracranial hemorrhage, multiple strokes, or seizures within the past year. His brain MRI shows no tumors or intracranial aneurysms requiring treatment or arterial venous malformations (AVMs) requiring treatment. He is willing and able to tolerate the required prolonged stationary supine position during treatment. He has not participated in another clinical trial in the last 30 days.

The patient is a 35-year-old female living in Tanzania. She presents with fever and chills since yesterday. She has no other significant medical history. She is a housewife and has two children. She lives with her husband and children in a rural area in Tanzania. She has not taken any medication for her symptoms yet. She visited the outpatient facility where she was informed about the trial of rapid diagnostic tests for malaria. She has given her consent to participate in the trial and the clinician has decided to request a malaria test for her. She will be randomly assigned to either the hospital slide or the RDT. She will be informed about the test results and will be treated accordingly by the clinic doctor. She will be interviewed after the consultation to collect data on any treatment given or changed as a result of the review of results by the doctor. If she is not satisfied with the assigned test, she may withdraw from the trial and will be offered standard care.

56-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C infection who has undergone previous treatment with full dose PEG-IFN/RBV therapy but did not achieve sustained virologic response. The patient has undergone a liver biopsy within the last 2 years confirming the presence of chronic hepatitis C. The patient is not co-infected with HIV/HBV and has no known intolerance to the study drugs. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential of intravenous silibinin in combination with standard of care for the treatment of hepatitis C.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has tested positive for COVID-19 with RT-PCR test for SARS-CoV-2. He has been experiencing mild symptoms of fever, cough, and fatigue for the past three days. He has no significant medical history, no known allergies, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is currently not taking any medication. He lives with his wife and two children, who have all tested negative for COVID-19. His physical examination is unremarkable, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to practice celibacy during the study period and until 7 days after treatment. He signs the informed consent form and is randomized to the Favipiravir treatment arm. He will receive Favipiravir tablets of 1,800 mg twice daily on day 1, followed by 800 mg twice daily from day 2 onwards for a total of 5 days of treatment. He will be monitored closely for any adverse events and will report any symptoms or changes in his health status to the study team. The aim of the trial is to evaluate the efficacy of Favipiravir in treating mild and moderate COVID-19 infections in Nepal, and he hopes that his participation will help contribute to the development of effective treatments for this disease.

The patient is a 2-year-old baby who has been diagnosed with an initial dental caries lesion on one of their primary molars. The baby's parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the possibility of using silver diammine fluoride (SDF) in arresting enamel caries lesions on occlusal surfaces of primary molars in babies. They are willing to have their child examined and treated in a mobile dental unit, which will temporarily be parked in public schools of Barueri, Sao Paulo, Brazil. The parents are aware that their child will be randomized concerning the treatment in Group A (SDF) and Group B (fluoride varnish) and will be examined at the baseline and followed by 6, 12, 18 and 24 months to determine if there is any caries progression into dentine. They understand that the acceptability reported by parents after treatments, the time and estimated money spent for treating will also be collected, as well as social and biological data that could be related to efficacy of techniques. They consent to the possibility of discomfort, acceptability and costs that may be associated with the clinical trial.

A 55 year old male is admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He is currently on mechanical ventilation and has been for the past 24 hours. He is non-responsive to verbal commands and has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 5. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. His chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates consistent with ARDS. The patient meets the Berlin criteria for ARDS and is therefore eligible for this study. He has no known neurologic disease that may prolong weaning, is not pregnant, and does not have a diagnosis of pulmonary fibrosis. The patient does not have an implanted cardiac pacer/defibrillator and is not a prisoner. The patient is informed of the study and consents to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a family history of colorectal cancer. His father was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 60. He has no personal history of gastrointestinal diseases and no other significant medical history. He has never had a colonoscopy before, but he is concerned about his risk for colon cancer and wants to undergo screening. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. His physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl He has been instructed to follow a low-fiber diet for 2 days before the procedure and to take a bowel preparation kit to cleanse his colon.

The patient is a 70-year-old Japanese male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. His BMI is 24.1 kg/m2, and he is not a smoker. He is retired and lives with his spouse. He does not take any prescription medications or over-the-counter acid controllers. He has not used any other drugs or herbal preparations within the past two weeks. He has no history of drug allergies. He has not been exposed to BMS-708163 or any other investigational drug or placebo within the past 4 weeks. He has no history of blood donation or blood transfusion within the past 4 weeks. He has no history of recent major surgery. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with leprosy 6 months ago. She has been experiencing Type 1 Reactions despite the use of Prednisolone for the past 3 months. Her symptoms include erythematous, painful nodules on her arms and legs, and she has also noticed swelling in her hands and feet. She weighs 55kg, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has no history of tuberculosis or other severe active infections, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Her renal function is normal, and she is not currently taking thalidomide. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and return for follow-up visits.

The patient is a 54-year-old man with a history of HIV infection for the past 10 years. He is currently on efavirenz-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 12 weeks and has been stable on this regimen. He is experiencing symptoms of neuropsychiatric side effects such as depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbances. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the relationship between drug exposure and these side effects, as well as the role of host polymorphisms in drug metabolism. He is able to provide written informed consent and complete the questionnaires in English. He has no history of completion of treatment for any intercurrent acute infection less than four weeks before study entry, major neurologic disease, current delirium or intoxication, drug or alcohol abuse, or any other condition that contraindicates participation. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 10-year-old male with a history of developmental regression, intellectual disabilities, and epilepsy is being evaluated for a possible inherited leukodystrophy. The patient has experienced multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent seizures and has required frequent adjustments to his antiepileptic medication regimen. The patient's parents have noticed a gradual decline in their child's motor and cognitive abilities over the past several years. The patient has had multiple diagnostic tests, including MRI and genetic testing, which have been inconclusive. The family is interested in participating in the Western Leukodystrophy Project to help with diagnosis and treatment options for their child's condition. They are able to travel to Primary Children's Hospital in Salt Lake City, Utah, and are willing to undergo a general physical and neurological exam as part of the study requirements.

A 25 year old woman has had type 1 diabetes for 8 years and has been using an insulin pump for the past 2 years. She has used a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) for 6 months over the last year. Her medication regimen has been stable for the past 2 months. She lives within a 60 minute radius of Massachusetts General Hospital and is willing to spend the night prior to both exercise visits in a hotel and fast overnight prior to exercise. She is willing to wear two steel cannula infusion sets, one Dexcom CGM sensor and change sets frequently. She does not have any history of liver disease or renal failure requiring dialysis. She has never had a hypoglycemic seizure or coma in the last year. She is not using oral or non-insulin injectable anti-diabetic medications. She understands and speaks English fluently and has a mobile phone that she will have access to at all times during the outpatient run-in period for making contact with study staff. She is not pregnant, breast-feeding, planning to become pregnant in the immediate future, or sexually active without use of contraception. She agrees to use acceptable contraception for the two weeks prior to the study, throughout the study, and for the two weeks following the study. Acceptable contraception methods include oral contraceptive pill (OCP), intrauterine device (IUD, hormonal or copper), male condoms, female condoms, diaphragm or cervical cap with spermicide, contraceptive patch (such as OrthoEvra), contraceptive implant (such as Implanon, Nexplanon), vaginal ring (such as NuvaRing), progestin shot (such as Depo-Provera), or male partner with a vasectomy proven to be effective by semen analysis. She has no current alcohol abuse or other substance abuse. She is willing to avoid use of drugs that may dull the sensorium, reduce sensitivity to symptoms of hypoglycemia, or hinder decision making during the period of participation in the study. She has no history of cystic fibrosis, severe pancreatitis, pancreatic tumor, pancreatectomy or any other pancreatic disease leading to diabetes mellitus. She has no history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, TIA or stroke, seizure disorder, pheochromocytoma, untreated or inadequately treated mental illness or electrically powered implants. She is able to completely avoid acetaminophen for the duration of the study. She has no established history of allergy or severe reaction to adhesive or tape that must be used in the study. She has no history of eating disorder within the last 2 years, such as anorexia, bulimia, or diabulemia or omission of insulin to manipulate weight. She is not using benzodiazepines or narcotics or other central nervous system depressants, even if by prescription. She is willing to comply with study procedures and reporting requirements.

30yo female with a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis and symptoms of persistent runny nose, sneezing, nasal itching, and congestion that persists throughout the year. Symptoms are worse indoors and she has noted occasional wheezing and coughing at night. She has previously tried several over-the-counter medications for relief but has not found adequate relief. She has a positive skin prick test to house dust mites, with a wheal diameter of 5mm and a specific IgE level of 3 kU/L. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to understand the information given and complete the daily record card and RQLQ. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a medically accepted contraceptive method. She has not received allergy specific immunotherapy for house dust mites in the last 10 years and has not participated in any clinical study within the last 12 weeks. She does not have any nasal condition that could confound the efficacy or safety assessments.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) six months ago. He has previously tried medication therapy but has not seen any significant improvement in his symptoms, which include progressive exercise intolerance and breathlessness. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and has no history of drug abuse. He is currently retired but was previously employed as a construction worker. The patient is able to perform activities of daily living but feels limited in his ability to participate in physical activities. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the structured exercise training program can improve his exercise tolerance, symptoms, and health-related quality of life. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 44-year-old male patient with a history of chronic kidney disease presents with symptoms of fatigue, decreased appetite, and swelling in his legs. The patient has been diagnosed with CKD stage V and is currently not on dialysis. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has not been diagnosed with diabetes. The patient's fasting glucose level is within the normal range (<6 mmol/l). The patient has not been treated with corticosteroids, insulin, or oral diabetic medications in the past 8 days. The patient has no evidence of significant concurrent illness and has a normal coagulation profile. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the structural and metabolic properties of white adipose tissue in CKD stage V patients. The goal of the trial is to investigate the adipose tissue dysfunction associated with CKD. The patient will be required to undergo a biopsy of abdominal subcutaneous white adipose tissue during an elective urologic surgery (peritoneal dialysis catheter). The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 47-year-old man recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has a family history of myeloid malignancies, as his father was previously diagnosed with AML. His blood work showed decreased red blood cell count, decreased platelet count, and an elevated white blood cell count. He has no history of thrombocytopenia or bleeding propensity. His physical examination is unremarkable, and he has no history of skin pigmentation, oral leukoplakia, unexplained liver disease, lymphedema, atypical infections, or immune deficiencies. He is otherwise in good health and has no other diagnosed medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential genetic predispositions to AML and MDS in families with a history of myeloid malignancies.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with mitochondrial disease due to a deficiency in complex III of the respiratory chain. He experiences muscle weakness, difficulty walking, and frequent episodes of lactic acidosis. Despite being on a special diet, his symptoms have continued to worsen over the past year. He has no history of intractable epilepsy or primary disorders of amino acid or fatty acid metabolism. He has no known allergies to CoQ10 or placebo ingredients. He is willing to discontinue all other medications and supplements for the duration of the study. He and his parents understand the nature of the study and agree to participate.

A 62-year-old female suffered from a massive stroke 2 years ago, which affected her right side. She has been undergoing physical therapy since then, but her ankle remains substantially impaired. Her Fugl-Meyer lower extremity score is 10, and she has minimal hemi-neglect. She has functioning proprioception and can perform a volitional ankle movement in dorsiflexion. She is cognitively and behaviorally capable of complying with the regimen. She has no fractures, spinal cord injury, deep venous thrombosis or peripheral nerve injury. She has no osteoarthritis limiting range of motion or uncontrolled high blood pressure/angina. She is exercise tolerant and has no skin condition intolerant of the device. She has no progressive neurodegenerative disorder or uncontrolled seizure disorder. She has not received Botox treatment within the last 5 months and does not have a Baclofen pump.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who was recently admitted to the hospital for management of acute heart failure. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, for which he takes lisinopril and metformin, respectively. He reports shortness of breath and fatigue upon exertion. Upon examination, he has jugular venous distension, bibasilar crackles, and peripheral edema. His blood pressure is 125/80 mmHg, heart rate is 95 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. His pulmonary wedge pressure is determined to be 20 mmHg by right heart catheterization. He does not have any significant valvular diseases or arrhythmias. His renal and hepatic function are normal. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits associated with the RLX030 infusion.

The patient is a 25-year-old man diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder at the age of 4. He has struggled with social interactions, communication, and repetitive behaviors throughout his life. He has a moderate level of impairment, with a Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) score of 90 and a Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S) score of 5. He is currently not taking any medication for his ASD symptoms but has tried various behavioral therapies in the past with limited success. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of memantine hydrochloride (Namenda®) for cognitive and behavioral impairment in adults with ASD. He is able to swallow pills and is willing to participate in mandatory blood draws. He has no history of severe allergies or multiple adverse drug reactions. He understands the nature of the study and is able to communicate effectively with the investigator and study coordinator.

54yo male with a diagnosis of metastatic melanoma with disease progression after treatment with ipilimumab and pembrolizumab. The patient has multiple metastases to the liver, bone, and brain. He has no significant past medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has undergone radiation therapy to the brain for symptomatic lesions and has completed 3 cycles of chemotherapy with dacarbazine with no response.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of liver cirrhosis diagnosed based on clinical, sonographic, and laboratory findings. He has a history of esophageal varices and has been taking nonselective beta-blockers(NSBB) for the past 6 months. However, his portal pressure has not decreased as expected and he is experiencing poor response to NSBB. He has no history of myocardial infarction in the past 12 months and has no clinically relevant cardiomyopathy or coronary artery disease. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of another primary malignancy within the past 3 years. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient has no active infection, acute renal failure, or poorly controlled hypertension. The patient's serum creatinine level is within normal limits. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to Rifaximin or propranolol and has no dysarrhythmia or any other condition that would make him inappropriate for the study on the investigator's judgment.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, controlled with medication. He is scheduled to undergo elective lower limb orthopedic surgery under spinal anesthesia. He has no known allergies and is otherwise healthy. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 75 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Laboratory results are within normal limits. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria. Therefore, he is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who has been experiencing symptoms of acute upper respiratory infection, including cough, runny nose, and fever for the past three days. The symptoms have not improved with over-the-counter remedies, and her parents are concerned about her condition. She has been diagnosed with qi deficiency wind-heat syndrome by a Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner. The patient's total white blood cell count is within normal limits. She has no history of allergies to medication or serious medical conditions. Her parents have agreed to participate in the clinical trial and have signed the informed consent form.

A 45-year-old non-smoking female presents with a history of chronic cough that has been refractory to multiple treatments. She reports coughing multiple times throughout the day and night, which is affecting her quality of life and causing fatigue. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications currently. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her baseline spirometry shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 75%. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m^2. She is willing and able to comply with all aspects of the protocol and has provided written informed consent. She is a non-smoker and uses two forms of acceptable birth control. Her laboratory tests and ECG are normal, and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

This is a 42-year-old female with metastatic ovarian cancer who has failed to respond to standard therapy. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not undergone radiation treatment encompassing >20% of the bone marrow or major surgery within 3 weeks of study drug administration. She has recovered from all effects of any prior major surgery and has no persistent >Grade 2 toxicity from prior cancer therapy. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the components of niraparib and has not participated in a radioactive clinical study or received an investigational radiolabeled drug within 6 months prior to study drug administration. The patient has undergone a previous computed tomography (CT) scan which confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic ovarian cancer. She is willing to undergo a negative serum pregnancy test (beta human chorionic gonadotropin [hCG]) within 72 hours prior to receiving the first dose of study drug, as required by female subjects of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who underwent a mastectomy for breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a right-sided breast reconstruction using an implant-based approach. She is now scheduled for nipple-areolar complex tattooing. She has a BMI of 26 and is in generally good health. She has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. She has no history of psychiatric disorders. She is an active person and engages in regular exercise. She is a married mother of two children and works as a school teacher. She has expressed concerns about the aesthetic outcome of her breast reconstruction and is interested in participating in a study that may help to improve the assessment of breast reconstruction aesthetics. She has no history of bilateral breast reconstruction or any other type of breast reconstruction other than implant-based reconstruction following mastectomy for breast cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) stage II. She has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit smoking 5 years ago. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past year, which is affecting her daily activities. She is able to perform activities of daily living but experiences shortness of breath when walking uphill or climbing stairs. She is currently using a bronchodilator inhaler for symptomatic relief. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of lower limb impairment or contraindication to cardiopulmonary exercise testing. She is eligible for pulmonary rehabilitation and is willing to participate in the study. The patient's weight is 80 kg. She has never been treated with a heart rate modulator or implanted with a pacemaker/defibrillator.

Patient is a 43-year-old man from the United States who was diagnosed with soft tissue sarcoma six months ago. He has been treated with anthracycline chemotherapy but has experienced disease progression. He has no history of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, or coagulation disorders. His BMI is 27, BP: 118/72, HR: 78/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for anemia (Hb: 9.8 g/dL) and thrombocytopenia (platelets: 90,000/mm3). He has no other significant medical history and is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male recently underwent surgery to remove a tumor from his gastroesophageal junction. The pathology report confirmed that the tumor was HER2+ gastric adenocarcinoma. The tumor was completely removed, and the surgical margins were clear. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no history of cardiac or cardiovascular disease. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not have any known malabsorption syndrome or gastrointestinal bleeding. He has never received any neoadjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He does not have any other malignancies in the last 5 years. His laboratory values are within normal limits, and he is not pregnant or lactating. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo the treatment regimen.

This is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and is being treated at the Rush Cancer Center. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and her physician has recommended Doxorubicin (Adriamycin®) as part of her treatment regimen. The patient is eligible to participate in the study as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to have blood drawn and echocardiograms performed at each of the six study time points. The patient is aware that the study aims to determine if the suPAR biomarker in her blood is causative or predictive of Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy or heart failure. She understands that the data collected will be analyzed using statistical analysis software and the results will be used to gain a better understanding of this relationship. She is willing to participate in the study to help advance medical knowledge and improve future breast cancer treatments.

A 28-year-old nulliparous woman presents to the delivery room at 39 weeks of gestation with regular uterine contractions and cervical dilatation of 4 cm. She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy with no significant medical history. Her BMI is 22 kg/m². Her obstetric history is unremarkable, with no previous miscarriages or abortions. She plans to have a vaginal delivery and has not received any prior opioids or analgesics. She has no known allergies to medications. The fetal presentation is cephalic with normal cardiotocographic recordings. Her American Society of Anaesthesiologists physical status is class I. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the effects of epidural fentanyl on vaginal delivery.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of allergic rhinitis, including sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes for the past few months. She has never used an intranasal steroid before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety of Flixonase. The patient reports that her symptoms are particularly bothersome during the spring and fall months when pollen counts are high, and she has tried over-the-counter antihistamines with limited success. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is willing to have her medical records used for the study and understands that she will be in one of two inception cohorts - either those initiated on Flixonase or those initiated on another intranasal steroid. She is willing to comply with study requirements, including regular follow-up appointments and medication use as prescribed.

A 30-year-old male athlete who has suffered a knee injury is scheduled to undergo knee arthroscopy surgery. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history, and his weight is 70 kg. He has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. He has a Mallampati score of 2 and a thyromental distance of 7 cm. His mouth opening is more than 3 cm. He has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2. He has never had any ENT surgery or laparoscopic surgery. He is able to understand the Study Information Sheet and has provided a written consent to take part in the study. He is willing to be randomized to either the Guardian Laryngeal Mask or the LMA Proseal and is willing to be blinded to the device used during the procedure.

56-year-old male with a history of cervical disc disease presenting with neck and/or arm pain, decreased muscle strength, abnormal sensation, and/or abnormal reflexes in a specific nerve root distribution from C3 to C7. The patient has undergone non-operative, conservative treatment for approximately six weeks but remains unresponsive. Radiographic imaging shows a decrease in disc height, degenerative spondylosis, or disc herniation at two contiguous levels from C3 to C7. The patient has an NDI score of ≥ 30% and is seeking surgical intervention for their symptoms. The patient does not have active systemic infection, prior spine surgery at the operative level, or severe facet joint disease or degeneration at any level. The patient does not have a history of malignancy or autoimmune diseases that affect the musculoskeletal system. The patient is not taking medications known to potentially interfere with bone/soft tissue healing, and has not had an epidural steroid injection within 14 days prior to surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with non-metastatic breast cancer in 2010. She underwent surgery, radiation therapy, and anthracycline-based chemotherapy as part of her treatment. She is currently in remission and has no other significant medical history. She previously led an active lifestyle, but due to her cancer treatment, she has experienced some fatigue and has not been able to exercise as much as she used to. She is interested in participating in this study to determine if aerobic exercise can help her regain her energy and improve her overall health. She is willing to commit to the study's exercise program and follow-up appointments. She has not received Herceptin, and her cancer has not relapsed since her initial diagnosis.

A 62-year-old man diagnosed with rectal cancer 4 years ago underwent radiation therapy and chemotherapy followed by surgery. He had an uneventful postoperative course and remained disease-free for 2 years. However, he recently started experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. He underwent a CT scan which revealed a 4 cm recurrent mass in the pelvis. The mass is adjacent to the sacrum, making it unresectable. He is assessed by a multidisciplinary team who determines that he is not a candidate for surgery and that his only option is reirradiation and chemotherapy. He is fit for reirradiation and chemotherapy, and his target lesion is visible on MR. He has no orthopaedic implants along the proposed MRg-FU beam path, and he is not allergic to MR contrast agents or sedation. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to communicate sensation during MRg-FU treatment.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male, with no significant medical history. He has no chronic medical conditions and is not taking any prescription or non-prescription medications. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. He has a body mass index within the range of 18.5 to 30.0 kg/m2 and weighs between 50 to 100 kg. His blood pressure is within the range of 100 to 150 mm Hg systolic and 50 to 95 mm Hg diastolic. His pulse rate is between 50 to 100 bpm. The patient is a non-smoker and has not participated in a clinical trial within the last 4 weeks. He has not experienced any significant somatic or mental illness in the two weeks preceding the drug administration. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse in the last 3 years. The patient is able to communicate and cooperate with the study investigators and has provided written informed consent. The patient is not currently sexually active, but has agreed to use adequate contraception if he becomes sexually active during the study period. The patient has tested negative for HBV, HCV, HIV, and tuberculosis in the serology examination. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of XG-102.

65-year-old male with a history of COPD, who has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing for the past 3 days. The patient has a 20 pack-year history of smoking and has been using inhalers for the past 2 years. The patient has been admitted to the hospital for acute exacerbation of COPD. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in a study that evaluates the correlation between physical activity and COPD exacerbations.

8-year-old male child with a history of growth hormone deficiency, presenting with a height standard deviation score (SDS) </= 5th percentile for idiopathic isolated GHD participants. The patient has not received any prior recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) treatment and has normal thyroid function tests and complete blood counts within the last 12 months. Physical examination reveals prepubertal (Tanner I) status. The patient has no acute critical illness or uncontrolled chronic illness that may interfere with participation in the study, and no bone diseases such as achondroplasia or hypochondroplasia, intracranial tumor, irradiation, and traumatic brain injury. The patient is not receiving oral or inhaled chronic corticosteroid therapy for other medical conditions and has not required higher doses of corticosteroids for more than 5 days in the last 6 months. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trial or investigation of GH, treatment for growth failure, or treatment with a biologic agent. The patient's epiphyses are not closed, and there is no known hypersensitivity to somatropin, excipients, or diluent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with COVID-19. He has a history of arterial hypertension and diabetes. He is experiencing respiratory symptoms and has been hospitalized due to low blood oxygenation levels. The patient is currently receiving supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula to maintain a SpO2 level above 90%. He has not required mechanical ventilation or vasopressor therapy. The patient is able to comply with inhalation therapy and is willing to participate in the trial. The patient understands the trial's requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

This is a 45 year old female with a history of periodontal disease and multiple missing teeth. She presents with a non-restorable mandibular premolar that requires extraction. The patient has a lack of bone volume for ideal implant placement and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of a socket preservation procedure. The patient is in good health and has no contraindications for surgery. She is willing to undergo the procedure and follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage II lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for the past 30 years and has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). His pulmonary function tests show a FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.65 and a FEV1 of 60% predicted. He is scheduled for a lobectomy via thoracotomy. He is currently taking inhaled bronchodilators and inhaled steroids as prescribed by his pulmonologist. He is willing and able to independently perform incentive spirometry exercises.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling with obesity for over 10 years. She has tried various weight loss plans and diets, but has not been successful in achieving sustained weight loss. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 43 kg/m2 and has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and sleep apnea. She reports experiencing frequent symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux (GER), such as heartburn, regurgitation, and difficulty swallowing. She has not undergone any previous gastric surgeries and does not have any contraindications to pneumoperitoneum. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) on GER symptoms in morbidly obese patients. She is able to provide informed consent and is committed to complying with all study procedures.

45 year old male with a past medical history of ulcerative colitis diagnosis 10 years ago. Patient has undergone regular surveillance colonoscopies for the past 5 years, every 1 to 2 years, due to their increased risk of developing colon cancer as a result of their colitis. Patient has had multiple biopsies taken during previous colonoscopies showing no evidence of dysplasia. Patient is currently asymptomatic and adherent to their medication regimen. The patient has been invited for their next surveillance colonoscopy and has been approached to participate in a feasibility study comparing virtual chromoendoscopy (VCE) to chromoendoscopy (CE) for colitis surveillance. The patient has been informed of the study and its objectives and is willing to participate. The patient is able to provide informed written consent.

A 63-year-old man was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with stage IV disease. He has a history of smoking and is currently experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue, with limitations in carrying out certain activities. He has been offered platinum doublet chemotherapy, but declined due to concerns about potential side effects. His lab work shows normal platelet count, and AST and ALT levels. He has small, asymptomatic brain metastases. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medication, and does not have any autoimmune conditions. He has no history of cardiovascular, hepatic, or renal systemic diseases. He is negative for pregnancy testing and agrees to use effective contraception during the study. He has read and understands the purposes of the study and has signed a statement of informed consent.

55 year old female with a histologic diagnosis of breast cancer and radiologic evidence of brain metastases that are not suitable for surgery or radiosurgery as judged on the basis of the lesion size, number, location and the patient's personal choices. She has controlled systemic disease for >6 weeks and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) of 1. The patient has no prior cranial radiotherapy, measurable lesions by gadolinium-enhanced MRI, and has adequate organ and marrow reserve. She has a hemoglobin level of 11.4 gm/dL, absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/mcL, platelets of 140,000/mcL, total bilirubin of 0.8 x UNL, AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) of 1.5 x UNL, serum creatinine of 1.3 x UNL, PTT of 24.6 seconds, INR of 1.0, and normal serum sodium, calcium, potassium, and magnesium levels. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and sign informed consent. She has no prior cranial RT, hypersensitivity to any of the components of vorinostat, use of Valproic acid or other histone deacetylase inhibitor, or uncontrolled infection. The patient has no co-morbid systemic illnesses or other severe concurrent disease that would make her inappropriate for entry into this study or interfere significantly with the proper assessment of safety and adverse events of the prescribed regimens or limit compliance with study requirements. She has no history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina ≤6 months prior to registration or congestive heart failure (CHF) requiring use of ongoing maintenance therapy, or life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. The patient is able to take oral medications and is not receiving any other investigational agent. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to employ adequate contraception throughout the duration of the study and for 3 weeks after treatment has ended.

A 45-year-old woman presents with persistent pain in her left heel for the past 6 months. The pain is most severe in the morning and gradually subsides as the day progresses. She also reports tenderness in the heel when palpated. She has no history of foot surgery or trauma to the area. She denies any other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 28. There are no visible wounds or infections in the affected area. She has not received any oral or injected corticosteroids in the past 6 months. She has no history of neurological or systemic inflammatory arthritis. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of high-intensity and low-level laser therapy for her Achilles tendinopathy.

Patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has been living independently in the community and has been taking approved medication for Alzheimer's disease for the past 6 months. Her symptoms include forgetfulness, difficulty with language, and confusion. She has a reliable caregiver who is fluent in English and Spanish and is willing to participate in the study with her. She has no evidence of active malignancy, chronic or acute renal, hepatic or metabolic disorder. She has not undergone any major surgery in the past 12 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the subject Informed Consent Form. She is able to read and understand English or Spanish to ensure compliance with cognitive testing and study visit procedures. The patient is postmenopausal for more than a year.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and a family history of kidney cancer. Imaging studies show that he has metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma that can be removed by surgery. His performance status is 1, and his laboratory tests show leukocytes of 4,500/μL, ANC of 2,000/μL, platelet count of 100,000/μL, and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. He is willing and able to undergo nephrectomy and treatment with sunitinib malate. He has not received any prior systemic treatment with sunitinib malate or any concurrent investigational agents. He is not taking any medications or substances that may affect the activity or pharmacokinetics of sunitinib malate.
