A 45-year-old male with a BMI of 38 who has been diagnosed with severe obstructive sleep apnea and is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery. He has a past medical history of hypertension, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of facial abnormalities, cancer, or reconstructive surgery. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. He has been classified as an ASA Class II patient and is between the ages of 18 and 80. There are no other conditions or medications that may interfere with the study.

The patient is a 72 year old male who has been experiencing difficulty with mobility over the past several months. He reports feeling unsteady on his feet and has had several near falls. He is able to walk short distances but often requires a cane for support. He is interested in participating in the "Mind in Motion" clinical trial to help researchers better understand the neural control of mobility in older adults. He is a native English speaker and is willing to undergo all testing procedures. He is available and willing to be enrolled in the study for the duration of the follow-up period, which is between 1.2 to 3.5 years, depending on enrollment date. He meets the inclusion criteria for community-dwelling men and women age 70+ years with SPPB <10 and able to complete the 400 m walk test within 15 minutes without sitting or the help of another person and without a walker (a cane is allowed). He does not have any significant medical events in the past 6 months that could contaminate data being collected, severe visual impairment, metal implants or pacemaker that would prevent him from undergoing MRI, clinically diagnosed vestibular dysfunction, or any of the other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of advanced breast cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. She has already undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has not responded to these treatments. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her Karnofsky Performance Status is 70. She has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, with ANC of 2.0 x 10⁹/L, platelets of 110 x 10⁹/L, Hgb of 11 g/dL, serum total bilirubin of 1.0 x ULN, ALT and AST of 2.5 x ULN, and serum creatinine of 1.0 x ULN. She is willing to use acceptable birth control as she is of child-bearing age. She has not received any investigational agents within the past 28 days, and she has not received extensive radiation therapy within the past 4 weeks. She is not currently taking or has received hormones within 7 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She is not using moderate or strong CYP450 3A4 modulators or prescription or OTC medications that reduce or neutralize gastric acidity. She has not had major surgery within the past 4 weeks, and she does not have any major chronic illnesses other than cancer. She has no major cardiac or neurologic disease and has no history of hepatitis B or C or human immunodeficiency (HIV) infection. She is not required to use granulocyte colony stimulating factors (GCSF) for prophylaxis of neutropenia.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma with inoperable and/or metastatic disease. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status below 1. He has not received any systemic treatment for advanced or metastatic disease before. His labs show that his creatinine clearance is ≥ 60ml/min and his hematopoietic function is within normal limits. He has at least one target lesion with a minimum lesion size as per the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors criteria (at least 1 unidimensional measurable lesion ≥ 20 mm in diameter by conventional CT or MRI scan, or ≥ 10 mm in diameter by spiral CT scan). He has not received prior therapy with Taxotere or Epirubicin. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the treatment regimen.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is scheduled for a hernia repair surgery under general anesthesia. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists score of II and does not have any pre-existing chronic pain treated with opiates. He has given his consent to participate in the GOALDAN study and is affiliated with a social security regimen. The surgery is expected to take less than an hour. The patient has no history of epilepsy, transient attack or stroke, paraplegia, hemiplegia, orthostatic hypotension, or autonomic dysfunction. He is not under tutorship or curatorship, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no arrhythmia or pacemaker, and he is not receiving continuous infusion of vasoactive agents. The patient will arrive at the department the day before the surgical intervention for preoperative assessment and will be offered to participate in the GOALDAN study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). She underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) using a HLA-DPB1*04:01 negative donor. The patient is in complete remission after the transplantation. Her current medication regimen includes cyclosporine and mycophenolate mofetil. The patient is HLA-DPB1*04:01 positive and has no contraindications for mobilization of peripheral blood stem cells using G-CSF. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient has neutrophils ≥1,000 cells/μl and platelets ≥50,000 cells/μl. The patient is affiliated with the National Health Care System and has provided informed consent. The patient is eligible to receive a single infusion of the T cell clone directed against HLA-DPB1*04:01, 4-5 months post-transplantation.

33 yo M with HIV infection and CD4+ lymphocyte count of 250 cells/mm3. The patient has not been on any antiretroviral therapy for the past 6 months. The patient has a history of oral candidiasis and has completed a course of fluconazole. The patient is not currently taking any medications except for prophylaxis for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia. The patient has no known co-existing conditions or symptoms that would exclude him from the trial. The patient has not received any cytotoxic chemotherapy within the past month and has not used any drugs known to induce photosensitivity. The patient does not have Kaposi's sarcoma requiring systemic therapy. The patient does not have active substance abuse.

A 32-year-old woman has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and has been prescribed Betaferon for her treatment. She is an active user of the myBETAapp and has been using it for the past 3 months. She reports experiencing occasional muscle weakness, fatigue, and difficulty with coordination. Despite these symptoms, she has been able to maintain her daily activities and work schedule. She has no history of other significant medical conditions and is not taking any other medications for MS. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided electronic informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who recently had a high PSA level of 8.0 ng/ml during a routine check-up. He has no previous history of prostate cancer or any other serious medical conditions. He has noticed no unusual symptoms apart from mild difficulty in urination. The patient is generally in good health and has a BMI of 26. He is willing to undergo further testing to determine if he has prostate cancer. He has no history of prostate biopsy or prostate surgery. The patient is able to tolerate an MRI and does not have any contraindications for the procedure. He has no claustrophobia and is willing to undergo transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsies. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is above 60 ml/min.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with pneumonia and was prescribed a course of antibiotics. After a week of taking the medication, he started experiencing diarrhea and abdominal discomfort. He visited his primary care physician, who performed a fecal analysis and found the presence of Clostridium difficile toxin. The patient was started on oral metronidazole treatment, but experienced a relapse of diarrhea after a few days. He was then given oral vancomycin treatment, but again experienced a relapse after completion of the course. The patient is now being considered for secondary treatment with cultured gut microbiota rectally or oral vancomycin in sequence. If these treatments fail, he will be given cultured gut microbiota via the upper route or duodenal route. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or immunodeficiency, and is able to accept endoscopic procedures. He has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 70-year-old female diagnosed with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) by a neurologist. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. She has a caregiver, her daughter, who stays with her 5 days a week and can provide necessary information, assist with compliance with study medication, and accompany her to study visits. Her CDR score is 1 and her MMSE score is 18. She has not received any anti-dementia drug therapy within the past 12 weeks. She does not have Parkinson's disease with dementia (PDD) and does not have any serious neuropsychiatric conditions or severe extrapyramidal disorders. Her systolic blood pressure is above 90 mmHg and her pulse rate is above 50 bpm. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of E2020 in treating DLB.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis by a rheumatologist a year ago. He works as a sales representative, and he has been experiencing difficulties in his job due to his condition. He has tried different treatments, but none of them seem to be working effectively. He is fluent in English and has access to a computer, web-cam, headset, and printer. He is willing to purchase any of these items if necessary. He lives in British Columbia and is willing to travel to Vancouver for one visit with an occupational therapist. He is interested in participating in the study to learn how to manage his condition and stay employed.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer with bone involvement. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer 4 months ago after experiencing lower back pain and difficulty urinating. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the prostate, and subsequent imaging studies revealed multiple bone metastases. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications other than pain management medication. His performance status is good, with no significant weight loss or fatigue. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the lower spine with no neurological deficits. His PSA levels have been steadily increasing despite hormone therapy, and bone scintigraphy was performed to assess the extent of bone involvement. The patient has no objections to participating in the study.

54 yo M with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and repeatedly recurring/relapsing reflux oesophagitis, presenting with symptoms of heartburn, regurgitation, and dysphagia. The patient has never been prescribed Nexium before as a maintenance therapy. The patient's past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. The patient is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 28. The patient has undergone an endoscopy and was found to have Grade B reflux oesophagitis according to Los Angeles Classification (Hoshihara's modification). The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Nexium Capsules RE Maintenance Specific Clinical Experience Investigation study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with thoracolumbar and/or lumbo-sacro-pelvic deformity with a Cobb angle of 25° or greater. She has been experiencing back pain, as well as leg pain, weakness, and numbness. She is able to ambulate and stand without assistance for a minimum of 10 seconds. She has not had any major lower extremity surgery or previous injury that may affect gait. Her BMI is within the range of 18.5 to 35. She does not have any neurological disorder, diabetic neuropathy, or other disease that impairs her ability to ambulate or stand without assistance. She is not taking blood thinners and has not had any major trauma to the pelvis. She is not pregnant and does not wish to become pregnant during the study. She is willing and able to attend and perform the activities described in the informed consent within the boundaries of the timelines set forth for pre-, and post-operative follow-up.

52-year-old male diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity with planned treatment of radiotherapy (60 Gy) as part of his post-operative treatment plan. Patient does not have a history of skin rash, ulceration or open wound in the treatment area. Patient is not on high doses of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The patient has no known allergies or systemic skin diseases that would affect the irradiated fields. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and has signed written informed consent. Past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous history of smoking, but he quit smoking upon diagnosis. The patient is otherwise in good health and has no other medical conditions that would interfere with the study results.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with excessive daytime sleepiness and cardiovascular disease. She has been prescribed Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) therapy, but her compliance to CPAP treatment has been less than ideal. She has participated in the ongoing randomized controlled trial (RCT) that assesses the short-term (3-months) efficacy of extended education program, which uses the concepts of Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) and Motivation Interviewing (MI). She has completed the initial phase of the program, but her long-term adherence to CPAP therapy needs to be evaluated. She is able to provide written informed consent for the extended study.

32-year-old female smoker with a 10-year history of smoking, consuming approximately 1 pack per day. She has tried to quit multiple times in the past without success. She has a Fagerström test score of 7, indicating nicotine dependence. She is fluent in French and can read and understand the study procedures. She has no history of intracranial hypertension or any disease causing brain damage. She is not currently taking any medication to stop smoking and has not participated in any other clinical trial in the last 6 months. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any cochlear or ocular implant or cardiac defibrillator. She has no metal in her skull or eczema on her scalp. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the requirements and limitations of the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with locally advanced primary breast cancer. She has no known history of breast cancer or other breast-related diseases. She has a T3, N2 stage disease with no bilateral breast cancer, no high probability for extensive intraductal in situ disease, no clinical fixation to the pectoralis major muscle or skin, and no involvement of the nipple. She does not have inflammatory breast cancer or multicentric disease. Her platelet count is at least 100,000/mm3, and she has no bleeding disorders. Her PT and PTT are less than 1.5 times normal, her INR is less than 1.5 times normal, her bilirubin is no greater than 2.0 mg/dL, and her transaminases are no greater than 2 times normal. She has no coagulopathy, no liver disease, and her BUN is less than 30 mg/dL or creatinine is less than 1.9 mg/dL. She does not have renal insufficiency. She has no clinically significant heart disease or pacemakers/defibrillators. She has no breast implants, prior collagen vascular disease, or concurrent mental condition that would preclude study. She is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She is fertile and agrees to use 2 effective methods of contraception. She has not had prior participation in this study and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial. She has no concurrent anticoagulants. She is able to tolerate prone position and breast compression.

We are seeking healthy adult males between the ages of 20 and 40 years old, with body weight of at least 50 kg and BMI between 18.5 and 25.0, who have no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and no significant health problems. The individual should not have taken any medications or over-the-counter drugs (excluding topical products) or dietary supplements within 7 days prior to the start of study drug administration. They should also not have consumed grapefruit or St. John's wort or any alcohol or caffeine-containing beverages within 3 days prior to the start of study drug administration. They should not have smoked within 90 days prior to the start of study drug administration, or be willing to stop smoking during the study period. The individual should be willing to provide their own written informed consent and comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing visual disturbances in the form of blurred vision and difficulty in reading for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy in his left eye and has undergone laser photocoagulation treatment for the same. However, his vision has not improved significantly. He is a retired government employee and is currently living with his wife. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his time reading books and watching television. He has a BMI of 28 and his blood pressure is under control with medication. On examination, his visual acuity is 6/12 in the left eye and 6/6 in the right eye. There is no other significant finding on ocular examination. His medical history is unremarkable except for diabetes and hypertension. He is willing to participate in the study after understanding the risks and benefits of the procedure.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with bilateral cataracts. She is experiencing difficulty with reading, driving, and watching television. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of ocular surgery or refractive surgery. Her preoperative best-corrected distance visual acuity (BCDVA) is worse than 0.22 logMAR in both eyes. She has no history of glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy or any other ocular pathology. She does not have any amblyopia or color vision deficiencies. Her preoperative regular corneal astigmatism is <1.00 D in both eyes. She is able to comprehend and sign the informed consent form, and is willing to attend all postoperative follow-up visits. She plans to continue her daily activities, including reading and driving, after the surgery.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman who suffered a first-ever unilateral stroke 8 months ago, resulting in moderate to severe movement impairment in her upper limb. She has no excessive spasticity in any of the joints of the affected limb (shoulder, elbow, wrist, fingers). She is able to follow study instructions and perform study tasks. She has not had any upper limb fractures within the last 3 months and has not participated in any experimental rehabilitation or drug studies during the study period. She is willing to provide written informed consent. The patient does not exhibit any major medical problems or poor physical conditions that would interfere with participation, and does not have any excessive pain in any joint that might limit participation.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with silent cerebrovascular disease based on cranial MRI results showing white matter hyperintensity of vascular origin. She has no previous history of stroke and no clinical symptoms, but she experiences occasional episodes of forgetfulness and confusion. She is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels. She is independent in her daily activities, able to stand and walk without assistance, and able to complete cognitive and gait assessments without difficulty. She is willing to participate in the study and able to sign the informed consent. She lives in Shanghai and is willing to undergo follow-up evaluations over the next year.

Maria is a 16-year-old girl who has been living in a group foster care home for the past year. She has a history of running away from home and has struggled with substance abuse in the past. She has had one sexual partner in the past and has engaged in sexual activity without using contraception. She is interested in learning more about safe sex practices and contraception methods, but feels embarrassed and uncomfortable discussing these topics. She has expressed interest in participating in the POWER Through Choices program to gain knowledge and confidence in making healthy choices about her sexual behaviors. Maria is not currently pregnant or parenting.

A 14-year-old girl presents with crowding in her upper and lower arch, and irregularity in her teeth. She is eligible for NHS orthodontic treatment and is planned for non-extraction upper and lower fixed appliance orthodontic treatment. She has not undergone any previous fixed or functional appliance treatment, nor does she have any craniofacial abnormalities or missing teeth due to previous extraction. Her medical history does not include any chronic conditions that require analgesics and she has no known allergies. She has no difficulty with mouth opening or any other contra-indications to intra-oral scanning.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been suffering from nasal congestion, loss of smell, and frequent sinus infections for the past two years. She has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies, for which she takes an inhaler and antihistamines. She has tried various over-the-counter nasal sprays and antibiotics with no significant improvement. She denies any history of aspirin sensitivity or known allergies to medications. She has never had surgery on her sinuses before. On examination, her nasal passages are obstructed with pale, boggy mucosa, and multiple polyps are visible on endoscopy. Her lung function tests show mild obstruction consistent with her history of asthma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates a new treatment for nasal polyps and asthma. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 62 year old man who has been feeling increasingly tired and has noticed a decline in his walking speed over the past year. He also experienced a fall last year, which has made him more cautious about his mobility. He is generally healthy, but has been diagnosed with high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which he is managing through medication. He is not a vegan or vegetarian and is able to undergo an MRI. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his heart health and muscular strength, and is willing to commit to the program and follow the tracking requirements. He does not have any limb fractures or severe arthritis, nor any other conditions affecting his nervous system or cardiopulmonary health. He also does not have any visual or hearing impairments that would prevent him from completing the program.

Patient is a 37-year-old woman with a history of infertility. She has undergone one previous cycle of IVF, which resulted in only 3 mature follicles and 2 oocytes retrieved. Her BMI is within the range of 18 to 30. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve her ovarian response to controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) in IVF cycles.

The patient is a 5-year-old Caucasian girl with a history of dull toothache and swelling in the right mandibular area. The patient's parents reported that the child has been complaining of tooth pain for the past week and has trouble sleeping at night. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, with no known allergies or chronic illnesses. Upon examination, the dentist found a decayed primary second molar with necrotic pulp tissue and purulent discharge when the pulp chamber was accessed. The tooth had no mobility, and the periodontal ligament space was thickened. Radiographic evaluation showed furcation radiolucency not exceeding half of the distance between the furcation and permanent successor. The dentist diagnosed the patient with irreversible pulpitis and recommended root canal treatment using the One Shape single-file system. The parents consented to participate in the clinical trial, and the patient was randomly assigned to Group I. The patient is cooperative and able to follow instructions during the treatment.

The patient is a 65-year-old ex-smoker who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the last 5 years. She is currently using ipratropium and salbutamol to manage her COPD symptoms but is still experiencing frequent wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. She is a retired teacher and spends most of her time at home. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine 5 mg daily. She has no history of heart disease or diabetes. She has not been hospitalized for COPD exacerbation in the last 6 months. Her current smoking status is unknown. Her spirometry values show an FEV1/FVC ratio of 55%, and an FEV1 of 1.4L (45% predicted). She has no history of allergies or asthma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the safety and efficacy of GSK233705 plus salmeterol compared with 2 active comparators and placebo in subjects with COPD.

64-year-old male with a history of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in the right eye 18 months ago. The patient is currently experiencing persistent visual impairment and has been advised to undergo treatment for the same. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial for the treatment of NAION and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient has not received treatment for cancer in the past 12 months, has not undergone surgery requiring general anesthesia with intubation in the past 30 days, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not received any drugs with potential neuroprotective or toxic effects on the optic nerve or retina in the past 6 months and has not participated in any interventional clinical trials in the past 60 days. The patient is not receiving or has not received corticosteroids or immunosuppressive drugs in the past 3 months. Additionally, the patient does not have any medical or psychological conditions that could preclude him from completing the study protocol. The patient's study eye has disc pallor and stable visual acuity, and the participant is able to read at least 20 and at most 66 EVA letters with best-corrected vision. The participant's study eye has a HVF 24-2 SITA Standard visual field using spot size III with mean deviation -5 dB or worse and with a visual field defect compatible with NAION in the study eye.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with >= 10% blasts within the past two weeks. He has previously undergone conventional initial induction chemotherapy and has relapsed within 6 months after first complete remission (CR). He has not had a prior allogeneic or autologous stem cell transplant. The patient has normal cardiac ejection fraction, serum creatinine, and SGOT levels. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has no active or unresolved infections and no evidence of invasive fungal infection. He has not received prior treatment with carboplatin, topotecan, flavopiridol, or sirolimus. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an accepted and effective method of contraception if sexually active.

A 28-year-old woman who is nulliparous and has a history of two early pregnancy losses presented to the clinic with a diagnosis of Asherman's syndrome. She has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years with no success. An intrauterine adhesion was diagnosed on hysteroscopy. The adhesion was surgically removed and a hysterosalpingogram was performed to confirm the patency of the fallopian tubes. The hysterosalpingogram revealed a small cervical canal that will require dilation. The patient was offered the option of using the Aqueduct-100 device as a pre-procedure to intrauterine surgeries. She was counseled on the potential risks and benefits of using the device and agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She has no history of sexually transmitted diseases or infectious diseases.

Patient is a 25-year-old female from the United States who has a clinical history of seasonal allergic rhinitis. She experiences symptoms such as sneezing, itching, and congestion during the ragweed season. She had a positive skin test to ragweed allergen within the last 12 months. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is on an acceptable birth control method. The patient is generally in good health and is willing to attend all study visits. She is capable of following and understanding instructions and is willing and able to provide written informed consent. The patient has not participated in any budesonide study within the last three months and has not participated in any investigational drug trial within the last 30 days. She has no known hypersensitivity to corticosteroids or any of the excipients in the formulation of the investigational drug. The patient has no history of severe respiratory infection or disorder, alcohol or drug abuse, or positive tests for HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. She has not been diagnosed with active asthma requiring treatment with inhaled or systemic corticosteroid and/or routine use of ß-agonists or any controller drugs. She has not used any of the prohibited medications within the identified exclusion periods. She has not used antibiotic therapy for acute conditions within 14 days prior to the Screening Visit and thereafter. The patient has not initiated immunotherapy or dose escalation during the study period. She is not vaccinated nor has she been exposed to or has active infection with chickenpox or measles within the 21 days preceding the Screening Visit. The patient does not have any of the conditions that are judged by the investigator to be clinically significant and/or affect the patient's ability to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman in her 39th week of pregnancy with a singleton fetus. She has no significant medical or surgical history and no known allergies. She is scheduled for an elective lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) under spinal anesthesia due to a previous LSCS delivery. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she is currently not taking any medications. She has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

28yo woman with a diagnosis of SLE for the past 3 years, with a history of recurrent flares despite treatment with hydroxychloroquine, mycophenolate mofetil, and oral prednisone. She has recently experienced an acute flare of SLE with active nephritis and proteinuria of 4 g/day. She has undergone a renal biopsy that confirmed lupus nephritis class III. The patient is currently enrolled in a stable dose of mycophenolate mofetil and oral prednisone and has been on this regimen for the past 30 days. She is ANA positive with a titer of 1:320 and positive anti-dsDNA antibodies. Her BILAG 2004 index score is 17 and her SLEDAI score is 10. Her laboratory test results show a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, platelet count of 200,000 cells/mm³, white blood cell count of 6,200 cells/mm³, and a creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL. The patient does not have any comorbidities and is not taking any antioxidants or biologic therapies. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has been approved by the adjudication committee.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who was admitted to the hospital with a fever of 103°F and severe abdominal pain. She was diagnosed with sepsis and septic shock due to a urinary tract infection. She weighs 70 kg and has no significant past medical history. The patient has no known allergies and has not been on any medication before. She is able to give informed consent and understands English. The patient's serum transaminase level is within the normal range. The patient does not have a history of diabetes, heart disease, or any other serious medical condition that would compromise her participation in the study.

A 68-year-old female with a history of hypertension and unstable angina pectoris presents with chest pain that has been increasing in frequency and intensity over the past week. She has been taking conventional medications for her hypertension and CHD for the past 6 months. The patient has stopped taking traditional Chinese medicine for CHD treatment for at least a week prior to the start of the study. She is willing to participate in a double-blind, randomized, controlled, multi-center study evaluating the efficacy and safety of salvianolate injection in elderly patients with unstable angina pectoris. The patient is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials and does not have any allergies.

The patient is a 22-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 20 weeks of gestation. During a routine ultrasound examination, it was found that she has a short cervical length of 15mm. She is a first-time mother and has no significant past medical history. She has no allergies to medications and is not currently taking any medications. Her family history is unremarkable for any significant medical conditions. She has good communication skills and is fluent in English. She has voluntarily agreed to participate in the clinical trial after having the study explained to her in detail and having all her questions answered. She is willing to comply with all study-related assessments and procedures.

Patient is a 17-year-old Latino male from a low-income family living in the US. He has been experiencing unusual thoughts, beliefs and behaviors in the past 6 months that are concerning to him and his family. He reports hearing voices that others cannot hear, feeling like people are watching him or talking about him, and having difficulty concentrating in school. He has no prior history of mental health concerns and has not been treated for any other medical conditions. Spanish is his preferred language and he is fluent in both Spanish and English. He is not currently using any substances and has no history of head injury. His IQ is in the average range for his age. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to receive treatment for his symptoms and improve his cognitive functioning.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe heart failure. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is ≤ 35%, he is in NYHA III to ambulatory Class IV, and has had at least one hospitalization for decompensated heart failure within the past 12 months. The patient must be on stable, up-titrated medical therapy as recommended according to current guidelines, which minimally includes ACE-inhibitor (ACE-I) and a beta-blocker. The patient must also have cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) and an implanted cardio-defibrillator (ICD) when clinically indicated. The patient has functional limitation due to heart failure as defined by a 6 Minute Walk test of ≥ 175 ≤ 375 meters, measured within 30 days prior to randomization. The patient must understand the nature of the procedure and on-going device therapy, is willing to comply with associated follow-up evaluations, and provide written informed consent prior to the procedure. Exclusion criteria for the patient includes any evidence of either ascending aortic calcification, calcific ascending aortic disease, ascending aorto-coronary artery bypass grafts, history of aortic dissection, Marfans disease, or other connective tissue disorder or repaired aortic coarctation. Additionally, the patient cannot have inotrope dependence or ACC/AHA Stage D heart failure or non-ambulatory NYHA Class IV. The patient must also have a BMI between 18 and 45 kg/m2 and cannot have a suspected or active systemic infection within 14 days prior to randomization.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. He was admitted to the hospital for an elective knee replacement surgery. His fasting blood glucose levels were found to be elevated on admission, and he was diagnosed with hyperglycemia. He is taking Metformin 1000 mg twice daily and has no history of insulin use. His BMI is 27 kg/m2. His past medical history is significant for hyperlipidemia and obesity. His family history is significant for diabetes mellitus in his mother and his brother. He is able to communicate meaningfully with the investigator and is legally competent to provide written informed consent. He is a candidate for the study as his expected length of stay is more than three days.

A 54-year-old male with a history of heart failure diagnosed 2 years ago. He was previously hospitalized with a discharge diagnosis of heart failure 6 months ago. He has been taking ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, and diuretics at optimal doses for the past 6 months. He has been taking digoxin for the past 3 months at a stable dose that results in digoxin plasma levels of 0.5 on 2 consecutive blood tests. His symptoms of heart failure have been stable for the past 6 months, with no increase in shortness of breath or edema. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. He has no history of primary valvular disease, myocarditis, obstructive or restrictive cardiomyopathy, recent myocardial infarction, or stroke. His blood pressure is within the acceptable range for inclusion in the study. He has no history of supraventricular arrhythmia or sustained ventricular arrhythmia. He has no significant pulmonary, renal, or hepatic disease.

A 52 year old woman came to the clinic with a history of stage II colon cancer. She has completed her primary cancer treatment including surgery and chemotherapy 6 months ago. She is overweight with a BMI of 29 and has been struggling to lose weight and maintain a healthy lifestyle. She has access to a computer with high-speed internet and a telephone. She lives in Harris county, Houston and is willing to come to MD Anderson for assessments. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently on a low dose of lisinopril and a statin medication. Her recent lab tests showed that her blood pressure is under control and her lipid profile is within normal limits. She does not have any other pre-existing medical conditions that may prevent her from participating in this study.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male with end stage renal disease who has been on dialysis for the past year. He has been on the transplant waiting list for the past 6 months and has now been informed that he is eligible to participate in a clinical trial. He is interested in participating as he is eager to receive a kidney transplant and hopes to improve his chances of a successful outcome. He has no significant medical history other than his kidney failure and is generally in good health. He is willing to provide written informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study as he is undergoing his first deceased donor kidney transplantation and has a panel reactive antibody frequency of less than 50%. He understands that this is an interventional prospective cohort study and that participation in other randomized prospective interventional trials does not violate the protocol. He is willing to undergo advanced morphological investigation of tissue biopsy life stains and to provide samples for biomarker assessment to derive a general prognostic biomarker panel for functional transplant outcome two years after transplantation. He is also willing to have his medical information shared with the study team and to have follow-up visits to assess the long-term outcome after transplantation.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level was elevated, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. He has no history of other cancers or significant medical problems. He is married and has two grown children. He is currently considering treatment options and has been referred for a research MRI scan to evaluate the extent of the cancer. He is able to lie still for the duration of the MRI scan and is not claustrophobic. He has no metal implants or other contraindications for MRI. He is willing to participate in the study and give informed consent.

A 30-year-old woman visited the dental clinic and expressed her concern about the yellowish color of her teeth. She had a history of coffee and wine consumption, smoking, and had undergone previous dental treatments including fillings and extractions. The patient had no known allergies to dental products or medications. She was otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Upon examination, her central incisors were noted to have a shade of A3. The dentist recommended a tooth bleaching treatment and explained the possible side effects and benefits. The patient agreed and was included in the study. She was randomly assigned to the white diet group and advised to avoid dye-containing food and beverages during the bleaching treatment. The patient was asked to fill out a food frequency questionnaire and color measurements were taken using a spectrophotometer at baseline and six months after the bleaching.

Patient is a 12-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes for 4 years. She lives with her parents who are actively involved in her diabetes management. She has experienced episodes of moderate to severe hypoglycemia in the past which required assistance from her parents. She is currently on an insulin pump and tests her blood sugar levels regularly. She is motivated and willing to participate in the study. She has no intellectual problems that would limit her ability to understand and follow the instructions of the study. She is in good general health with no conditions that could interfere with the study. She is willing to comply with the protocol requirements. She has not consumed alcohol and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of significant hypersensitivity to glucagon or related products.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has been experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath. His disease has progressed despite prior treatments with chemotherapy and radiation. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He reports occasional fatigue and weakness but is otherwise functioning independently. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status is 1. His blood work shows a white blood cell count of 3,500/μL, neutrophils of 2,000/μL, platelets of 120x1000/μL, and hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL. His liver and kidney functions are normal. He has no known allergies or autoimmune disorders. He is interested in exploring clinical trial options for his disease.

A 42-year-old male with a family history of heart disease, who is concerned about his health, is interested in participating in a clinical study. He has no history of coronary artery disease but has a BMI of 32 kg/m2. He has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and his fasting plasma glucose level is 9.2 mmol/L. He does not smoke and has no other major illnesses. His liver function tests, urea and electrolytes, full blood count and creatinine levels are all normal.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who recently started experiencing flu-like symptoms such as fever, sore throat, cough, and fatigue. She is a working professional and has been feeling weak and tired due to these symptoms. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and does not have any allergies to the components of the study medication. She is willing to comply with the observation requirements of the trial and is available for follow-up. She has not participated in any other clinical studies in the past month and is not related to any staff member of the clinical trial site. She is not employed with OOO "NPF "MATERIA MEDICA HOLDING" or any of its subsidiaries. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and agrees to use contraceptive methods during the trial and within 30 days after ending the participation in the trial.

A 27-year-old non-smoking female presented with a history of cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. The symptoms were aggravated by physical exertion and exposure to allergens. The patient had not received any treatment for asthma in the past. The physical examination was significant for expiratory wheezing and decreased breath sounds on auscultation. Spirometry showed a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 75% predicted, with a reversibility of 12% after bronchodilator administration. The chest X-ray was normal. Sputum induction was performed, and the mRNA levels of cytokines in the sputum were analyzed. The patient was diagnosed with non-Th2 asthma, and further classified as Th17 phenotype based on the cytokine profile. The patient was then enrolled in the clinical trial to investigate the response to inhaled corticosteroid treatment for non-Th2 asthma subtypes.

The patient is a 30 year old gay Hispanic male who has been drinking heavily for the past 5 years. He works as a bartender in a popular gay bar and is known for his partying lifestyle. He has never been diagnosed with any psychiatric illness or physical disease but has a family history of alcoholism. He is currently sexually active with multiple partners and is concerned about his drinking affecting his relationships and sexual health. He is willing to reduce his drinking to non-hazardous levels but is not interested in quitting alcohol completely. He is fluent in English and has completed high school education. He is not currently on any medication and has not received any psychotherapy in the past 3 months. He has never been diagnosed with drug dependence or opioid addiction but occasionally uses recreational drugs. He has no history of hypersensitivity to NTX and is considered suitable for receipt of an investigational drug. He is willing to participate in the study and is open to new treatment options to help him reduce his drinking to healthier levels.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with acromegaly. She has noticed an increase in her hand and foot size, as well as a change in her facial features. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, or cancer. She takes medication for thyroid hormone replacement therapy. She has undergone MRI imaging in the past and has no contraindications to MRI imaging. She is willing to participate in the study and has no plans to become pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old Italian male who has been experiencing persistent fatigue and night sweats for the past few months. He also complains of occasional fever and unintentional weight loss. The patient has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. On investigation, he is found to have enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, groin, and axilla. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of grade 3b Follicular Lymphoma. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is scheduled to start front-line Rituximab containing chemotherapy. A histological sample is available for central review according to the trial's criteria. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is an 80-year-old female nursing home resident who has been diagnosed with frailty. She has a history of hypertension, but it is currently well-controlled with medication. She has limited mobility and requires assistance with activities of daily living, such as dressing and bathing. She is participating in a rehabilitative care program aimed at improving her physical function and muscle strength. She has no history of breast or prostate cancer. She has not been diagnosed with any uncontrolled endocrine or metabolic disease, including diabetes, liver disease, or renal disease. She has no history of angina or myocardial infarction within the last 12 months, and her LDL cholesterol is below 200 mg/dL. She has not been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or untreated sleep apnea. She does not have an implanted artificial pacemaker/defibrillator. She has not been diagnosed with any systemic fungal infections, HIV, or active hepatitis. She has not used anabolic steroids within the last 3 months and does not abuse alcohol or drugs. She is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has not been diagnosed with any chronic diseases, has no known allergies, and is not taking any medications. She has not undergone any surgeries or procedures in the past six months. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has not experienced any menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, or vaginal dryness. The patient has not previously been treated with osteoporosis medication and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the bioavailability and pharmacodynamics of oral salmon calcitonin. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. She has a history of recurrent episodes of depression and has been on antidepressant medication for the past year. Despite treatment, she still experiences symptoms of cognitive impairment, such as difficulty concentrating and memory problems. She is currently employed as a marketing manager in a large corporation and finds it challenging to keep up with the demands of her job due to her cognitive symptoms. She lives with her husband and two children and enjoys spending time with her family outdoors. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders other than depression and has never undergone a neurofeedback task before. She is willing to participate in the study to explore alternative treatment options for her cognitive symptoms. She has no contraindications for MRI and is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 45 year old woman has recently been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and has been scheduled for an allogenic stem cell transplantation. She is currently experiencing severe depression but is not on any drug therapy for it. She is mentally and intellectually sound and has expressed interest in complementary medicine methods to help improve her quality of life and reduce side effects associated with the transplantation. She is willing to participate in this study and sign the required forms.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is in good health and does not have any significant medical history. He has no history of substance abuse or smoking, and he is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, herbal remedies, or supplements. He has not consumed any caffeine or alcohol within 48 hours prior to the study drug administration. He is not currently pregnant or nursing, nor does he plan to donate sperm during the study or within 30 days after dosing. He has a body mass index within the range of 18-30 kg/m2, and his blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. He has normal liver function tests, cardiac monitoring, and laboratory tests, and he is between 18 and 50 years of age. The patient has not donated or lost more than 400 mL of blood within 12 weeks of dosing, more than 200 mL of blood within 4 weeks of dosing, or donated any blood within 2 weeks of dosing. He is able to understand and communicate in English, and he has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 55 year-old female who has been experiencing pain and weakness in her right hand for several months. She reports difficulty with gripping and pinching objects, and has noticed a decrease in her ability to perform daily tasks such as opening jars and turning doorknobs. She was diagnosed with trapeziometacarpal osteoarthritis and has been recommended for surgical intervention. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the use of GraftJacket versus tendon interposition for the surgery. She has no history of rheumatoid arthritis and is fluent in German. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

Mrs. Johnson is a 72-year-old retired teacher who lives alone. She has noticed that she has been slowing down lately, feeling more tired than usual, and has had some trouble with daily activities. She has not been diagnosed with any chronic diseases but has a history of hypertension controlled with medication. She is currently not taking any other medications. Her BMI is 25 kg/m2, and her Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA) score is 23. She is an active member of her community, enjoys gardening, and participates in light exercise classes twice a week. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the instructions given.

27 year old woman diagnosed with ulcerative colitis at the age of 23. She has been experiencing frequent flare-ups and has been taking medication to manage her symptoms. She has recently been feeling depressed and anxious, struggling to cope with the impact of her condition on her daily life. She has a PHQ-9 score of 12 and a GAD-7 score of 11. She has access to a computer and internet connection and is interested in participating in a psychological intervention to address her depression and anxiety symptoms. She has not undergone CBT in the past year and is not currently receiving any psychological treatment. She is fluent in English and willing to provide informed consent.

16-month-old girl diagnosed with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy with Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level III. She has difficulty with weight-bearing and limited independent mobility. She is able to sit independently but requires assistance to stand and walk. She has no history of surgery or chronic infectious diseases. Her parents are interested in exploring alternative therapies to help improve her motor development and quality of life. They have provided written informed consent to participate in the pilot study of whole body vibration for children with cerebral palsy.

27-year-old female with no history of ocular or psychiatric disorders. She wears glasses for mild myopia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Refraction Determination Analysis. She presents with no active ocular disease and no history of brain tumor or other contraindications. She is interested in exploring the accuracy of a refraction done over telemedicine compared to a standard refraction.

A 45-year-old male presents with no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not have any known cardiopulmonary or metabolic diseases. He is fluent in German and is able to follow study procedures and instructions. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance research in functional capacity testing. He is able to conduct a 1-minute sit-to-stand test without pain or discomfort. He is of average height and weight for his age and gender, with no physical or intellectual impairments that would preclude informed consent or protocol adherence. He provides informed consent for the study and agrees to participate in the randomized cross-over trial.

A 24-year-old male university student with no history of psychiatric disorders or drug abuse came to the clinic for a clinical trial. He was interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of science. He is currently studying physics and has no significant medical history. He is not on any medications nor does he have any known allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He provided informed consent and scored 30 on the Mini Mental Status Exam. MRI imaging did not reveal any neuro-anatomical lesions. His cardiovascular health is normal, and he has no history of diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, hepatic or renal impairment, seizure disorder, or neurological disorder. His QTc interval is within the normal range. He is literate and has normal vision.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. He was previously treated with interferon-based antiviral therapy but failed to achieve sustained virologic response. He has not received any nucleotide analogue or direct-acting antiviral agents for HCV treatment. He has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and confirmed chronic HCV infection with HCV RNA above 10^4 IU/mL. His HCV genotype is 1, and he has no evidence of cirrhosis. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and follow the instructions for the study drug. He has no exposure to immunomodulators, amiodarone, or ribavirin within the specified time frame. He has no evidence of decompensatory liver function, primary liver cancer, or liver disease of a non-HCV etiology. He meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old Caucasian female who has regular menstrual periods. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m² and does not use any hormonal contraceptive method. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medication. She has no history of neuropsychiatric diseases or epilepsy, and her folate and vitamin B12 levels are within normal ranges. She has not used any potassium sparing drugs or folic acid-containing supplements or medications in the past 2 menstrual cycles. She is willing to use non-hormonal methods of contraception during the trial. She is interested in participating in the study to help investigate and compare the uptake of YAZ (oral contraceptive containing drospirenone and ethinylestradiol) with or without levomefolate calcium (Metafolin) in the body and to examine and compare the uptake of levomefolate calcium with or without YAZ in the body.

The patient is a Latina woman who has been diagnosed with Stage I-III breast cancer and has undergone neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy within the past 12 months. She is centrally obese, with a BMI greater than 30 kg/m2 or body fat greater than 30%, as well as a waist circumference greater than 35 inches. She is currently in breast cancer remission with no detectable disease present. The patient is able to initiate a supervised exercise program and is free from any cardiovascular, respiratory or musculoskeletal disease or joint problems that preclude moderate physical activity. She is also free from any history of chronic disease including uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension or thyroid disease, and has not experienced a weight reduction of 10% or more within the past 6 months. She currently participates in less than 60 minutes of structured exercise per week and does not smoke. The patient is able to speak English or Spanish and self-identifies as Latina. She is willing to travel to the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for necessary data collection and is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 65-year-old female who underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA) for osteoarthritis. She has no history of diabetes mellitus, peripheral vascular disease, or any other significant medical history. The surgery was successful, and she is currently in the hospital recovering from the procedure. She has no current involvement in any other clinical trials. Her vital signs are stable, and she is not experiencing any complications post-surgery. She has given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial and is interested in exploring alternative methods of DVT prophylaxis to reduce her risk of complications during the recovery period.

58 year old man who was diagnosed with advanced colorectal cancer and has developed liver metastases. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past and is now being evaluated for surgical resection of the liver metastases. He has no known allergies and his past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. The patient is able to understand the nature of the clinical trial and is willing to provide written informed consent. He is also able to comply with all the requirements of the study.

A 28-year-old female with a history of traumatic brain injury (TBI) resulting from a car accident two months ago is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. The patient has been experiencing language deficits and sensorimotor impairments as a result of the TBI. She is a native English speaker and meets the inclusion criteria for the TBI group. She has no significant medical or psychiatric illnesses aside from the TBI and meets the general inclusion criteria for the study. The patient is willing to undergo MRI and PET scans as part of the study. She has no pacemaker, aneurysm clips, cochlear implants, shrapnel fragments or any significant history of exposure to small metallic objects that could interfere with the scans. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to help further understanding of speech motor control in patients with TBI.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy diagnosed with bilateral cerebral palsy. He is classified as level II in the Manual Ability Classification System (MACS) and level III in the Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS). The patient has a history of botulinum toxin injections for spasticity management and has not undergone any orthopedic surgeries in the past six months. He has an average cognitive level and can follow instructions. The patient does not have any severe visual impairments, but he has mild difficulty in reading small letters. He is currently receiving physical therapy twice a week and occupational therapy once a week. His parents report that he enjoys playing video games and has good hand-eye coordination.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent surgery. He is fluent in Norwegian and has no cognitive impairments. He reports experiencing difficulty with breathing, fatigue, and occasional pain. He is married and has two children. He works as a carpenter and is concerned about how his cancer diagnosis and surgery will impact his ability to work and provide for his family. He has a strong support system from his spouse and immediate family, but he feels that he could benefit from additional social support. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the postoperative care and support for lung cancer patients like himself.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing for the past few months. He has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and he has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) for several years. He has lost about 15 pounds in the past few months and is feeling fatigued. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has been diagnosed with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma that has spread to other parts of his body. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the tumors have continued to grow. He is currently experiencing pain and discomfort in his chest and abdomen. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to try a new treatment option. His performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance scale. His labs show an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2,000 /mcL, platelets of 120,000/mcL, hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, serum creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL, serum total bilirubin of 1.2 mg/dL, AST of 45 U/L, and ALT of 35 U/L. He is negative for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. He has no history of immunodeficiency or active autoimmune disease. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for 120 days after the last dose of study medication.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who underwent radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer but has been deemed at high risk for early relapse due to a pre-RP prostate specific antigen level of 20 ng/dL and a Gleason score of 9. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 90 and his pretreatment granulocyte count, hemoglobin, and platelet count are within normal range. His serum creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL and his hepatic function is adequate. He has no evidence of metastatic disease or history of other secondary malignancies. He has not received any prior immunotherapy, biological therapy, hormonal therapy or radiation therapy for prostate cancer. He does not have any serious cardiovascular disease, seizures, or active infections requiring parenteral antibiotics. He is willing to use effective contraception while on treatment and for 3 months thereafter. He understands the study visit and follow-up schedule and is able to comply with the procedures.

This is a 70-year-old woman who has been experiencing mild to moderate dementia symptoms for the past year. She has undergone a CT scan within the past 18 months that is consistent with a diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's disease. Her score on the Wechsler Memory Scale - Logical Memory II recall falls below the pre-determined cut-off adjusted for her education level. She has a confirmed apolipoprotein E genotype prior to randomization and has been using medication that corresponds with protocol requirements. Her medical condition, with the exception of dementia, has been stable for at least 3 consecutive months prior to screening. She has no active suicidal thoughts within 6 months of screening and no active history of suicide attempt in the previous 2 years. She has a permanent caregiver who is willing to attend all visits, oversee her compliance with protocol procedures and study medication administration, and report on her status. She resides in an assisted living facility and both she and her caregiver have the ability to read and write in English. She is able to ingest oral medication. She has not used medium-chain triglyceride-containing products within 3 months of baseline and has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to milk or soy products. She has not used any other investigational agent within 60 days prior to screening and has no history of advanced, severe, progressive, or unstable disease that could interfere with protocol assessments or put her at particular risk. She has no medical or neurological condition other than Alzheimer's disease that could explain her dementia. She does not have a history of moderate congestive heart failure, clinically significant ECG abnormalities, or new cardiovascular events within 6 months prior to baseline. She does not have a history of or current psychiatric illness, major depression, insulin-dependent diabetes, clinically significant renal disease or insufficiency, clinically significant liver disease or fasting triglycerides > 2.5 times the upper limit of normal at screening. She is not experiencing clinically significant B12 deficiency within 12 months prior to screening, inflammatory bowel disease, peptic ulcer disease, or irritable bowel syndrome. She has not donated ≥ 2 units of blood within the 2 months prior to screening and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse within 6 months prior to screening. She is not an immediate family member or employee of the clinical site, sponsor or sponsor's agents. She does not have an alternative cause for dementia other than Alzheimer's disease as determined by a required CT or MRI scan within 18 months prior to screening and does not have a history of neoplasm or malignancies within 5 years prior to screening. She does not have clinically significant hypothyroidism as determined by thyroid function testing at screening and does not have a scheduled or expected hospitalization and/or surgery during the course of the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing episodes of chest pain for the past year. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol and has been taking medication for these conditions. He is a retired teacher and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has never had any surgical procedures in the past. During a recent checkup, his physician detected an aortic aneurysm and recommended surgery to repair it. The patient has been advised that the surgery will require deep hypothermic circulatory arrest and that he may require a blood transfusion. He has agreed to participate in this study and is willing to receive autologous platelet rich plasma if it reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusions during surgery. His preoperative platelet count is 180000000000/L and his hematocrit is 35%. He has not taken any anticoagulants in the past 5 days. The patient is generally in good health, but he has some mild osteoarthritis in his knees that limits his mobility.

68 year old female with a history of progressive difficulty in speaking and writing. The patient's husband reports that she used to be able to fluently communicate, but over the past year she has gradually lost the ability to articulate her thoughts. The patient also reports difficulty in finding the right words and has started to rely on gestures to communicate. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. She has undergone a series of cognitive tests, which showed a decline in language ability with no other significant abnormalities. She has been diagnosed with Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA) by her neurologist. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and is referred to the rTMS treatment of PPA study. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent form, and has no contraindications for MRI. Her baseline Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score is 22 out of 30.

4-year-old boy with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) presents to the pediatric clinic with recurrent respiratory infections despite treatment with proton pump inhibitors (PPI). The patient has been experiencing cough, wheezing, and difficulty breathing for the past 3 months. He has been treated with multiple courses of antibiotics and steroids but has not improved. His parents are concerned about the side effects of PPI and are interested in alternative treatments. The patient has no history of neurological disorders or immunodeficiency. The parents provide informed consent for the child to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Lactobacillus GG (LGG) as an adjunct to PPI for reducing the risk of gastrointestinal and respiratory tract infections in children with GERD. The child has not received probiotics within the last 7 days and has not been treated with PPI within the last 4 weeks for at least 2 weeks.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was diagnosed with Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL) two years ago. He received six cycles of chemotherapy with CHOP and achieved a partial response. He did not undergo stem cell transplant due to comorbidities. He has been on surveillance, but he recently developed progressive lymphadenopathy, and biopsy confirmed relapsed MCL. He is experiencing fatigue and weight loss but no night sweats or fever. His performance status is 1, and he has no significant comorbidities. His blood work shows normal renal and liver function, and he has no cardiac history. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and has provided written informed consent.

A 17-year-old male high school student is interested in participating in a clinical trial for acne treatment. He has been struggling with moderate acne for the past 6 months, which has been affecting his self-esteem and social life. He has not used any oral retinoids or antibiotics for acne treatment in the past 2 months. He has no history of diabetes, polycystic ovary syndrome, or drug/alcohol abuse. He does not smoke and is not on any medications. He exercises regularly and has no known allergies. He is willing to adhere to a milk-free and low-glycemic-load diet. He is available to attend all study visits and is comfortable with blood draws.

The patient is a 58-year-old African American male with a history of chronic kidney disease and anemia. He has been receiving Procrit® injections once a week for the past 10 weeks to manage his anemia. His hemoglobin levels have been stable at 11 g/dL over the past 4 weeks. He has no history of self-injecting Procrit® at home and has not received any investigational erythropoietic agents in the past. His estimated GFR is 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. He has no plans to initiate renal replacement therapy in the next year and has an expected life expectancy of more than 1 year. He has signed the written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate subject preference for Aranesp® administered once monthly or Procrit® administered once weekly.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma who has failed to respond to initial multi-agent induction therapy and achieved less than a complete response to one line of salvage chemotherapy. He has not experienced any disease progression but is currently in his first relapse and achieved less than a partial response to one line of salvage chemotherapy. The patient has an HLA-matched donor available and meets other eligibility criteria including WHO performance status 0-1, creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min, serum bilirubin ≤ 1.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), alkaline phosphatase ≤ 2 times ULN, LVEF ≥ 40%, and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has no other malignancy within the past 5 years, except for nonmelanoma skin cancer or stage 0 (in situ) cervical carcinoma. The patient has not received prior high-dose therapy or allograft and has no concurrent serious medical condition that would preclude an allograft. The patient is willing to undergo reduced-intensity conditioning regimen comprising carmustine, etoposide, cytarabine, melphalan, and alemtuzumab followed by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and is willing to be followed up periodically for 3 years after completion of study treatment.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who is pregnant with her second child. She has a history of uncomplicated vaginal delivery with her first child. She is currently at 38 weeks gestation and has been scheduled for an elective secondary lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) due to her preference and previous experience. She has no known medical or surgical complications and has had a healthy pregnancy thus far. Her blood work and ultrasound have been normal throughout her pregnancy. She does not have any allergies to medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help reduce blood loss during her LSCS procedure.

42-year-old male diagnosed with manifest Huntington's Disease with a family history of the disease. The patient has been receiving tetrabenazine for chorea control without significant side effects for the past 6 months. The patient has a Total Functional Capacity score of 7 and is able to swallow medication whole. The patient has provided written informed consent and has a reliable caregiver who interacts with the patient on a daily basis, oversees study drug administration, assures attendance at study visits, and participates in evaluations, as required. The patient is able to ambulate without assistance for at least 20 yards and has sufficient reading skills to comprehend the participant completed rating scales. The patient has no serious untreated or under-treated psychiatric illness or history of suicidal behavior. The patient has no evidence of hepatic or significant renal impairment and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not participated in any investigational drug or device trial other than SD-809-C-15 within 30 days of Screening.

This is a 28-year-old male with a history of cocaine dependence for the past 5 years. He has tried quitting on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is currently seeking treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication called tiagabine. He is in good health with no significant medical history or current medical issues. He reports using cocaine on a daily basis and is motivated to quit. He is willing to undergo regular urine drug testing to confirm abstinence from cocaine. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is able to provide informed consent. He currently does not use any other drugs or alcohol.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. She has a waist circumference of 100 cm, blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, HDL-Chol of 45 mg/dl, Triglycerides of 160 mg/dl, and glucose of 110 mg/dl. She is a nonsmoker and is willing to provide written consent to participate in the study. She has no food allergies and is not currently following any particular diet or using any nutritional supplements other than a daily multivitamin. She maintains a moderate physical activity routine for 30 minutes per day. She has not had any prior cardiovascular disease, myocardial infarction, angioplasty, or bypass surgery, and does not have any known cardiovascular or metabolic diseases such as diabetes. She is not currently using medications to control blood pressure, lipids, or glucose, and is not currently on oral contraceptives. Her hematocrit is above 36 for women.

A 5-year-old Caucasian male child with a history of eczema (atopic dermatitis) and sensitization to grass pollen and house dust mite has completed the previous 18-month treatment period of the EPAAC trial (NCT00152464). The child has not developed asthma yet, and the family is interested in participating in the prolongation of the trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of levocetirizine (LCTZ) in preventing the onset of asthma. The child is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. The family is willing to commit to the 36-month study and follow the prescribed treatment plan.
