This is a 65-year-old man with a history of diabetes and hypertension, who presents with critical limb ischemia in his left leg. He is experiencing ischemic rest pain and has a non-healing ulcer on his foot. He previously underwent an endovascular intervention for this issue, but unfortunately, it was unsuccessful. He is not currently a candidate for further intervention and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new treatment option. He has no history of major surgery in the past 90 days and has not had an endovascular intervention in the past 30 days. He is not currently on dialysis and has never had an above the ankle amputation in his left leg. He understands that he will be randomized to either the treatment arm or control arm and that the primary endpoint measure is freedom from major amputation, arterial intervention below the knee, and death through 12 months. He is willing to participate in this study to potentially improve his quality of life and avoid further complications.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male with a sedentary lifestyle presents at the clinic with slightly elevated blood pressure. His blood pressure readings have been consistently above 130/80 mmHg over the past few weeks. He reports no prior history of hypertension, heart disease, or stroke. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His family history is negative for cardiovascular diseases. His body mass index (BMI) is 28.5 kg/m². His physical exam is unremarkable except for blood pressure readings of 136/86 mmHg. Laboratory tests, including complete blood count, lipid panel, and glucose, are within the normal range. He is diagnosed with stage I hypertension and advised to make lifestyle modifications, including regular exercise and a healthy diet. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial on the effects of hot yoga on vascular function and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 47-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with a brain tumor and is scheduled for surgery at the City of Hope brain and spinal tumor neurosurgical program. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is currently taking medications to manage both conditions. He works as a computer programmer and enjoys hiking and playing basketball in his free time. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. The patient is able to understand the study requirements and is willing to sign a written informed consent to participate in the study.

35 yo female with a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, gas and changes in bowel habits. The patient reports that her symptoms have been present for at least 6 months and have not improved with dietary modifications or over-the-counter remedies. The patient has not taken any antibiotics or analgesics for at least 2 months and has not been treated for intestinal transit. The patient denies any history of diabetes, colic cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, dysthyroidy, Hirschprung disease, anorexia, or excessive consumption of alcohol or tobacco. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical studies and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of fructo-oligosaccharides on IBS symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis two years ago. He underwent pancreatic surgery six months ago and is in a stable condition. However, he is experiencing difficulty digesting his food and has steatorrhea with stool fat excretion greater than 20g/day. He has no history of excessive alcohol intake or drug abuse. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to porcine proteins or pancreatin. He is willing to participate in the study and agrees to stop taking any digestive enzyme preparations before the start of the run-in period.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss in her left ear for the past 8 years. She is highly motivated to improve her hearing and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the best surgical approach for cochlear implant electrode insertion. She has not undergone any prior otologic surgery in the left ear and has no known inner ear malformations or retrocochlear pathology. She has normal cognitive function and is not currently pregnant.

A 55-year-old male patient diagnosed with Chronic Heart Failure (CHF) based on European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines. He has been experiencing symptoms corresponding to New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class II-IV and has a Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) of ≤ 40%. He has been classified as American Heart Association (AHA) stage C or D. He was recently discharged after hospitalization for worsening CHF within the last twelve months. He is fluent in German and has sufficient eyesight to understand and follow the instructions communicated by the Motiva® platform. He is willing and able to use the required hard- and software and maintain a patient diary. He resides within geographical reach of one of the ten study sites and is willing to provide informed consent regarding benefits and risks related to the trial, and to sign a participation agreement for the installation of the telemedicine platform Motiva®. He has not had a myocardial infarction within the past four weeks, heart surgery or any coronary intervention within the past eight weeks, or cardiogenic shock within the past four weeks. He does not have any intended cardiac surgery within the next six months or priority status on a waiting list for organ transplantation. He does not have severe chronic and pulmonary illness with an immediate impact on the main outcome measures, renal failure requiring dialysis, dementia or other severe cognitive impairment, or psychiatric disorders rendering patients unable to participate in the trial. He is not discharged to or living in a geriatric clinic or a nursing home, and is not participating in another clinical trial.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (persistent hydatidiform mole or choriocarcinoma) with a WHO risk score between 0-4. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. The patient has a performance status of GOG 0-2 and meets laboratory examination criteria, including WBC≥3.5×10(9)/L, Granulocyte count≥1.5×10(9)/L, Platelet count≥80×10(9)/L, serum bilirubin≤ 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, transaminase≤ 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, BUN, Creatinine≤ normal. The patient is currently fertile but willing to use effective contraception during and for one year after study entry. She has not been diagnosed with placental-site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) or epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT), and has not received previous MTX treatment for suspected ectopic pregnancy. The patient is able and willing to sign informed consents and abide by the study protocol.

A 35-year-old female presents with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis symptoms including frequent sneezing, runny nose, and nasal congestion. She has never received any treatment for her symptoms and does not have any known drug sensitivities. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of Montelukast and Azelastine in treating her allergic rhinitis.

A 62-year-old male was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma of the colon. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. He is a former smoker and quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally but does not use illicit drugs. He reports feeling fatigued and has lost 10 pounds over the past month. He reports abdominal pain and diarrhea. He has no known allergies. Laboratory testing reveals elevated CEA levels and imaging shows multiple liver metastases. He underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of colorectal adenocarcinoma. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to carry out light work, such as office work. He has adequate organ function, and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive the latest treatment for his condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of advanced melanoma. She has undergone previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy but her disease has progressed. She has also been diagnosed with hypertension, which is currently under control with medication. She has no history of cardiovascular illness or autoimmune disease. Her most recent laboratory results show WBC of 4,000/μL, Neutrophils of 2,000/μL, Platelets of 150x103/μL, Hemoglobin of 10.5g/dL, Creatinine of 1.2mg/dL, AST of 30 IU/L, ALT of 35 IU/L, Alkaline phosphatase of 70 IU/L, and Bilirubin of 1.0mg/dL. She has no active infections or other medical conditions that would make the administration of study drug hazardous. She is willing to comply with all procedures required in the protocol and has signed a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing acute diarrhoea for the past 48 hours with at least three watery stools per 24 hours. She has no other medical conditions and is generally in good health. She has not taken any antidiarrhoeal agents in the past month. She has no history of chronic diarrhoea or irritable bowel syndrome. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the written informed consent. During the screening visit, the patient will provide information on her medical history, demographics, and acute diarrhoea episode including the number of stools, stool consistency, and presence of associated symptoms such as nausea and vomiting. The patient will also be given a diary to record the date and time of bowel movements, stool consistency, and consumption of the study medication. During the 72-hour treatment period, the patient will consume IQP-MM-101 according to the prescribed dosage of one tablet, three times a day dissolved in at least 125mL of water. At the final visit, the patient will undergo a physical examination and provide information on any adverse events, use of concomitant medications, compliance, and a global evaluation of efficacy and safety.

A 65 year old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer 4 years ago and underwent radical prostatectomy with negative margins. His PSA level remained undetectable for 2 years, but now it's increasing gradually up to 1.5 ng/mL. CT scan and bone scan are negative for any metastatic lesions. However, he underwent a NaF PET scan which showed suspicious bone lesions. He is currently not receiving any treatment for his prostate cancer. He has no history of any other medical conditions, and his ECOG performance status is 0. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including hematological and hepatic function. He is willing to participate in clinical trials and has signed an informed consent document.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with end-stage renal disease who has been on dialysis for the past 2 years. He has a history of high blood pressure and diabetes. He has been evaluated for a living donor kidney transplant, and his sister is a compatible donor. His HLA matching is 2/6 with a positive panel reactive antibody (PRA) of 25%. He has been deemed to have moderate immunological risk for kidney transplantation. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing two different immunosuppressive protocols after the transplantation. He is aware of the potential benefits and risks of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

There is no patient involved in this particular clinical trial as it is focused on examining nurses' knowledge about and attitude towards clinical research. Instead, the trial aims to recruit nurses who have graduated and are currently working in a university hospital in Copenhagen, Denmark. The nurses must sign an informed consent form to participate in the trial. However, nurses who are currently participating in another trial similar to the present one will be excluded from participating in the INFO-II trial.

The patient is a 30 year old female who had a stroke 10 months ago. She has mild to moderate hemiparesis in her left upper extremity and has been participating in outpatient rehabilitation for the past 6 months. She is able to comprehend English and is willing to comply with all study procedures. She is a community-dwelling individual who is able to independently operate the gaming system. Her corrected vision is 20/50. She has not received Botox treatment within the last 3 months and does not have any major medical issues that would interfere with study treatments or make intensive rehabilitation difficult to tolerate. She has not participated in any other experimental upper extremity trials.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two years ago. She underwent chemotherapy and achieved complete remission, but unfortunately, her AML came back (relapsed AML). She has undergone additional treatments, but her disease is now considered refractory. She is willing to try new treatment options and has signed informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, meaning she is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities with some difficulty. Her peripheral white blood cell (WBC) count is 25,000/µL, which is slightly above the eligibility criteria, but she is willing to undergo cyto-reduction with hydroxyurea to reduce her WBC count to the required level. The patient has adequate organ function, as evidenced by normal laboratory findings for total bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and creatinine clearance. Her QT-interval corrected according to Fridericia's formula (QTcF) is normal on her electrocardiogram (ECG) at screening. The patient has not received any other concurrent investigational agents, or any investigational agent within one week of registration. She has no history of other malignancies within the preceding 12 months before registration, with the exception of in-situ cancer, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, prostate, basal or squamous cell skin cancer. The patient does not have any life-threatening illnesses other than AML, uncontrolled medical conditions, or organ system dysfunction that could compromise her safety or put the study outcomes at risk. She does not have isolated extramedullary disease, acute promyelocytic leukemia, or AML with active central nervous system (CNS) involvement. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and she does not have any active and uncontrolled infections with HIV, Hepatitis B virus or Hepatitis C virus. She has not undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) within the past 4 weeks.

The patient is a premature infant born at 29 weeks gestational age with a birth weight of 1.2 kg. The infant is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and has been experiencing feeding intolerance, characterized by abdominal distention and vomiting. The infant's residual milk and glucose have been consistently above 55%, and there has been a reduction in the amount of enteral feeding. The infant has not participated in any clinical trials within the past four weeks and does not have pulmonary hypertension, necrotizing enterocolitis, gastrointestinal tract malformation, or congenital heart disease. The infant does not have any pre-existing QT prolongation or risk factors for QT prolongation such as ascites. The infant has not been exposed to any drugs that suppress CYP3A4. The infant is eligible for this clinical trial and will be randomly assigned to one of four groups to receive either 0.2mg/kg/tds domperidone, 0.4mg/kg/tds domperidone, 0.6mg/kg/tds domperidone, or a placebo to determine the most effective dose for the treatment of feeding intolerance.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease. He underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedure with stent placement in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) 2 years ago. He currently experiences chest discomfort during moderate physical activity and is classified as CCS class 2. His medication regimen includes aspirin, clopidogrel, and atorvastatin. He has no allergies and no other significant medical history. He does not smoke but has a history of heavy alcohol consumption, which he has since stopped. His blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 beats per minute. He has no signs of heart failure. His ECG is suggestive of ischemia in the LAD territory. Angiography reveals a 70% diameter stenosis in the stented segment of the LAD. He is deemed eligible for the P E P C A D II clinical trial and agrees to participate.

Patient is a 50-year-old man from the United States who has lost all of his teeth due to periodontal disease. He has a history of controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are managed with medications. He has no known drug allergies. His BMI is 28, BP: 135/85, HR: 80/min. His oral hygiene is acceptable, and he is cooperative with dental procedures. His CBCT scan shows sufficient bone volume for implant placement without the need for grafting, and he has adequate zones of keratinized mucosa (>2mm width) in both arches. He has 6 implants in his maxilla and 4 implants in his mandible, with crown height space of 10mm and 12mm, respectively. He is interested in receiving a fixed full arch screw-retained prosthesis and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing open tray versus digital impressions for the prosthesis.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with no medical history of chronic diseases. He is a non-smoker and has not consumed alcohol or drugs in the past five years. He is willing to avoid pregnancy with his partner during the study and is able to complete the research according to the test plan requirements. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a height of 1.75 m, resulting in a body mass index (BMI) of 22.9 kg/m², which is within the range of 18-28 kg/m². His physical examination reveals normal vital signs with no clinical significance. He has not taken any drugs that affect liver enzyme activity in the past 28 days, and he has not taken any prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, vitamin products, or herbs in the past 14 days. He has not consumed any special diets or vigorously exercised in the past two weeks. His ECG is normal and there are no significant abnormalities in his clinical laboratory results. He has not taken the study drug or participated in a drug clinical trial within the past three months. The investigator deems him suitable for participating in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who attends kindergarten and has been diagnosed with tooth decay. He is otherwise healthy with no major systemic diseases or long-term medications. His parents have given consent for him to participate in the study. The child has at least one tooth with untreated caries that extends into the dentine. The family has limited access to dental care due to financial constraints. The child's oral hygiene habits and use of other fluoride agents will be collected through a parental questionnaire at the baseline and follow-ups. The child is expected to be cooperative during clinical examinations conducted every 6 months over a 3-year period. The study will help determine the most suitable SDF concentration and application interval to arrest caries in children, which can be widely recommended and promoted for caries control in young children or those with difficulty accessing and affording conventional dental care.

A 35-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with Graves' Disease. She presented with symptoms such as jitteriness, palpitations, and weight loss. She has a history of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis and was on Levothyroxine for the past 2 years. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married and has one child. Her occupation is a teacher. She has no known allergies. Her laboratory tests showed high levels of T3 and T4 and low levels of TSH. She was started on Methimazole and advised to follow-up in 6 weeks. Currently, she is taking Methimazole 10 mg daily and her symptoms have improved. She is compliant with her medication, and she has not experienced any adverse effects. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent relapse of her Graves' Disease. She is willing to undergo intrathyroid injection of dexamethasone if randomized to the experimental group.

A 55-year-old male presents with a history of chronic heart failure (NYHA class II) diagnosed 2 years ago. He has been on treatment according to the European Society of Cardiology guidelines and has not been hospitalized for heart failure in the past month. He reports experiencing depressive symptoms such as persistent sadness, hopelessness, and lack of interest in activities he previously enjoyed. He scores higher than 9 points on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. He has difficulty sleeping and often wakes up feeling tired. He has some worries and anxiety related to his health condition. He is interested in participating in an internet-based cognitive behavioural therapy program to improve his depressive symptoms, sleep, and quality of life. He has time to participate in the 9-week intervention and is willing to follow the study procedures. He does not have severe heart failure (NYHA class IV) or any other severe chronic life-threatening illness. He is not currently hospitalized or assessed to need hospital care for his depression.

A 30-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 25 is interested in improving the appearance of her back, flanks, and thighs following liposuction surgery that was performed 8 weeks ago. She has no history of significant concurrent illness and is not taking any anticoagulation medications. She has not undergone any other surgery in the treated areas within the past 9 months and is not currently undergoing any treatment for active cancer. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant and has never had a permanent implant in the treated areas. She is willing to refrain from changes in her diet, exercise, and medication regimen for the entire course of the study. She has no history of immunosuppression/immune deficiency disorders and is not currently using immunosuppressive medications. She has no history of keloid scarring or abnormal wound healing. She is not currently using oral retinoids or anti-cellulite creams. She has no significant skin conditions in the treated areas or inflammatory skin conditions. She is willing to undergo a total of six study treatments to one side of her body at one week intervals and to be followed up at one month after her last study treatment. She understands and is willing to sign an IRB approved informed consent form.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty seeing at night. Upon examination by an ophthalmologist, she has been diagnosed with cataracts and has been scheduled for cataract surgery. She has no known allergies to bromfenac or salicylates. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Bromfenac Ophthalmic Solution in cataract surgery.

The patient is a newborn diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis (CF) by a sweat chloride test that showed a level greater than 60 mEq/L. The infant has two known CF genetic mutations. The study is conducted at the University of Minnesota CF treatment center, and the patient is willing to comply with the study procedures. The parent or guardian of the newborn is willing to provide written consent for participation in the study. There is no presence of vasculitis or rheumatologic disorder. The study will involve the collection of nasal samples by suction at each visit, and nylon swabs will also be used to sample the infant's buccal mucosa. Oropharyngeal swabs will also be obtained, which are considered to be an accurate proxy of lower airway (lung) microbiomes. The study will monitor bacterial trafficking between the oral, nasal, and lung cavities from birth to 3 years of age. The study aims to provide a better understanding of the development of airway bacterial communities and how to promote protective microbiota while restricting the growth of recalcitrant pathogens.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for the last 10 years. She reports experiencing frequent asthma attacks, especially during the winter season. Despite using her prescribed inhaler regularly, she still experiences difficulty breathing and chest tightness. She is generally healthy, with no known cardiovascular disease or other chronic illnesses. The patient has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is considered to have partly controlled asthma, with an ACQ score of 1.3. She has never been pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the link between asthma exacerbations and cardiovascular disease risk. She is willing to undergo pulmonary function testing, vascular function evaluation, and venous blood sample collection before and after being exposed to a bronchoconstrictive agent (either mannitol or methacholine) or a placebo. She also agrees to participate in an exercise regimen to evaluate if it reduces the cardiovascular risk following asthma attacks. The patient understands that the study will be conducted over 3 trials, with each trial separated by a week to allow for washout between tests, and that she will be randomized to either the mannitol or methacholine challenge or the placebo. She is willing to commit to the study protocol and attend all the scheduled appointments.

A 70-year-old man visited the emergency ward with a complaint of pain and swelling in his left leg. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is currently on medication to control his conditions. He is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in regular exercise. He has no history of blood clots or deep vein thrombosis. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having suffered a heart attack at the age of 65. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs.

This is a 45 year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. She has been on insulin therapy for the last 3 years and has a BMI of 25. She has visceral obesity and has been experiencing difficulty with glycemic control despite medication compliance. She has been advised to undergo duodenojejunal or gastric bypass surgery as a potential solution to her diabetes management. She is willing to participate in a prospective observational study to evaluate the effect of these surgeries on her glycemic control. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with pre-operative and post-operative requirements, including oral glucose tolerance tests, insulin and C-peptide level checks, and anthropometric measurements.

The patient is a 28-year-old nulliparous woman who is currently at 39 weeks of gestation. She has been scheduled for a cesarean section under general anesthesia due to concerns about fetal distress. She does not have any history of cardiovascular problems, preoperative pain, or regular analgesic use. She has no allergies to any of the study medications. She is physically fit, with a normal BMI, and reports an uncomplicated pregnancy. She is expecting her first child and is excited to meet her baby. She is concerned about postoperative pain and the potential impact it could have on her ability to care for her newborn. She is willing to participate in the study to help contribute to medical knowledge and potentially reduce postoperative pain.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and fatigue for the past year. She has a history of rheumatoid arthritis and has been taking methotrexate for the past 3 years. Her current medication regimen includes methotrexate, folic acid, and prednisone. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She lives with her husband and two children. Her medical history is also significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has not had any recent infections or coronary events. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of multiple doses of VB-201 on biomarkers.

A 53-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. The cancer is in the early stages and is deemed to be operable. The patient has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to take oral medications and has given his informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He is not receiving any other investigational agents and has no history of allergic reactions to anilinoquinazolins. He is not pregnant or lactating. He is able to comply with study and follow-up procedures.

A 40 year old woman with a history of ulcerative colitis for the past 8 years is experiencing moderate to severe disease activity despite being on adalimumab treatment for the past 12 weeks. She has left side colitis and has a Mayo score of 8 with a Mayo endoscopic sub-score of 3. She is not responding well to the current treatment and is experiencing frequent bouts of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rectal bleeding. The patient has never been treated with a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAK inhibitor) and is affiliated to the national health insurance. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is able to participate fully in all aspects of the trial. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent. The patient does not have any contraindication to vedolizumab treatment but has a contraindication to continuing TNF antagonist due to clinical suspicion of tuberculosis in the past. The patient does not have proctitis, a stoma, or a history of cancer during the past 5 years. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not legally protected. The patient is not currently participating in another interventional study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with advanced pancreatic islet cell tumor. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He presents with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies reveal multiple lesions in the pancreas with metastases to the liver. Biopsy confirms a well-differentiated pancreatic islet cell tumor. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or anti-VEGF angiogenic inhibitors. He is currently not receiving any treatment for his cancer, and his performance status is good. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive either sunitinib or placebo.

62-year-old patient diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for over 10 years. The patient has difficulty with motor function, with predictable motor fluctuations and experiences at least 20% of waking day in the "off" stage. The patient has been on stable doses of levodopa/carbidopa or any other antiparkinson therapy for 2 months prior to the study. The patient has not undergone any intracranial/neurosurgical procedures. The patient has no sensitivity to cyclosporine and is not HIV positive or infected with human T-cell leukemia/lymphoma virus (HTLV-1). The patient does not have any tremors interfering with stereotactic surgery and does not have any clinically significant medical, neoplastic or infectious disease or laboratory abnormality. The patient has no dementia that precludes signing informed consent or scores of less than 24 on Mini-Mental status examination. The patient is willing to undergo 2 separate operations in which the substantia nigra from either 4 fetuses (Group A) or 1 fetus (Group C) will be implanted into the striatum of each side.

35 F with a BMI of 35 and a h/o PCOS with mild hirsutism and irregular menstrual cycles. The patient has attempted various diets and lifestyle modifications with no significant weight loss. She is interested in bariatric surgery but is also willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effects of different weight loss interventions on hormones and glucose control. She does not have any history of diabetes or thyroid disease and does not smoke or use opioids. She is willing to maintain her current level of physical activity throughout the study period.

A 45-year-old male with a history of Lyme disease and antibiotic treatment presents with chronic pain in the musculoskeletal system and clinically troubling sensory hypersensitivity. The patient is able to speak and read English and is willing to not take other than study centrally acting pharmacologic agents prior to MRI and for the duration of treatment with study medications. The patient has no diagnosis of another (not LYME) general medical condition that has a major role in the onset, severity, exacerbation, or maintenance of pain or sensory hypersensitivity. The patient has no DSM-IV Axis I lifetime diagnosis of Pervasive Developmental Disorder, Autism, Psychotic disorder, Bipolar Disorder, Substance dependence. The patient has no current diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder or substance abuse. Additionally, the patient has no history of head injury with loss of consciousness (>5min), neurologic disease, seizures (excluding febrile seizures) or serious unstable medical condition (e.g. cancer, diabetes). The patient has not used opiates for the last month and is willing to be off of centrally active medications or treatment methods for at least 2 weeks prior to MRI and diagnostic visit, except for stable doses of non-benzodiazepines for sleep. The patient has no ferromagnetic implants, metal braces or retainers, or transdermal medicinal patches that cannot be removed. The patient has not given birth at < 37 weeks gestational age and does not have claustrophobia. The patient is not pregnant, lactating, or surgically-sterile, and is using appropriate methods of birth control. The patient is able to reliably rate intensity of pain in response to a fixed thermal stimulus and tolerate sound intensity of fMRI. Finally, the patient has not been successfully treated by medications for their pain, has no history of inability to tolerate treatment with SSRI or SNRI medications or d-cycloserine, and has no renal insufficiency or congestive heart failure or hepatic malfunction Liver Test.

A 20-month-old Caucasian boy with Down syndrome is referred to the study by his pediatrician due to concerns of delayed language development. The child is the first-born child of healthy parents. The pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the child was born full-term via normal vaginal delivery. The child's birth weight was 6 lbs. and 10 oz. The child had no major medical problems and was discharged home with his parents. At six months of age, the child was evaluated by his pediatrician due to concerns of delayed gross motor development. The child was subsequently referred to a physical therapist and started receiving therapy for gross motor delays. The child has been making progress with gross motor development and is now walking independently. The child has also received speech therapy for the past three months but has not made significant progress. The child's parents report that he understands simple commands but does not use words to communicate. The child's family lives in a rural area in Oregon and does not have easy access to specialized language intervention services. The child's hearing has been tested and is within the normal range. The child meets all inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 28.5 kg/m^2 and a waist circumference of 95 cm presents with concerns about her weight and body fat. She reports trying various diets and exercise regimens in the past without significant results. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of red ginseng on decrement of body fat. She is willing to give informed consent and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection two years ago. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and has achieved virologic suppression with a viral load of less than 50 copies/mL. He has a CD4+ T cell count of 700 cells/mm3. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has no known allergies to medications. He has a history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. He has no history of vascular disease or diabetes. He has no history of autoimmune disorders. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 30 days. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has adequate venous access for phlebotomy. He is a non-smoker and does not use any recreational drugs. He is currently employed and has no plans to become pregnant or father a child during the course of the study.

This is a 42-year-old female with short bowel syndrome who has been receiving home parenteral nutrition (HPN) for the past 2 years due to a surgical resection of the small intestine. She has been stable metabolically with an average of 4-5 bowel movements per day and no episodes of dehydration or electrolyte imbalances. She has a benign disease and has not had any recent hospitalizations. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of DPP-4 inhibitors in short bowel syndrome as a potential alternative to the expensive GLP-4 therapy. She meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who is scheduled for laparoscopic non-gastrointestinal surgery under general anesthesia. She has a BMI of 26kg/m2 and an Apfel score of 4, indicating a high risk for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and has not participated in any other clinical studies within the past 3 months. She does not have any skin allergies, damage or infection at the test acupoints and is not allergic to tape. She has no pacemaker implant and is not pregnant or lactating. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to cooperate with the intervention and evaluation.

Pt is a 57yo M with a 10 yr history of Type 2 DM, hypertension, and dyslipidemia, presenting with difficulty controlling his blood glucose levels despite multiple medications. Pt reports difficulty remembering to take all of his medications, and often forgets to monitor his blood glucose levels. Pt also reports feeling overwhelmed with managing his chronic conditions and feels that he would benefit from additional support. Pt is currently taking metformin, insulin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. Pt is able to communicate fluently in English and is willing to participate in a collaborative care model for the management of his diabetes and co-morbidities.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently underwent excision of a skin cancer lesion on her upper arm. The wound measures approximately 10 cm in diameter and is healing slowly. The patient has a history of smoking and has had previous skin cancer lesions removed. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new wound care system for skin cancer excision sites and split thickness skin grafts. The patient is willing and able to follow the study protocol and provide informed consent. She is not pregnant and does not have any allergies to wound care products.

A 68 year old woman was admitted to the Neurology-Neurovascular department of GHPSJ due to sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She was diagnosed with cerebral infarction (CI) through the ICD-10 codes I63.0 to I63.5 and I63.7 to I63.9. She was hospitalized in the NICU as the first hospitalization unit from her home. She stayed in the hospital for more than 3 nights. She is not under guardianship or curatorship, not deprived of liberty, and not under legal protection. She has given consent for the use of her data for this research. She will be included in the study to assess the functional prognosis of patients with CI.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has undergone a mastectomy and is now scheduled to undergo external beam radiotherapy at the Mayo Clinic - Rochester, MN or Mayo Clinic - Eau Claire, WI. She has no history of adhesive or tape allergy, and is able to provide written consent. She is willing to participate in the study and complete questionnaires, as well as return to the Mayo Clinic within 6 weeks post-treatment for assessment. She is also able to initiate thin film usage within the first 3 days of the initiation of treatment. The patient has not had prior radiation therapy to any portion of the planned treatment site, and is not undergoing brachytherapy. She has no active rash or pre-existing dermatitis, lupus, or scleroderma, and there is no gross dermal involvement at initiation of radiotherapy. The patient has not used systemic or topical antibiotics or antifungal medications within 14 days of swab collection, nor has she used systemic or topical steroids, immunosuppressant drugs, or ultraviolet light therapy within 14 days of swab collection. There is no clinical evidence of infection that would interfere with proper assessment of the skin microbiome, and she has not had prior organ or bone marrow transplant. She is not currently lactating and is only undergoing unilateral radiation.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of colon polyps presents for a routine colonoscopy. During the exam, a 1.2 cm polyp is identified in the sigmoid colon. The polyp is located in a difficult-to-reach location, but the endoscopist believes it can be successfully removed with endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any anticoagulant or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications. Her platelet count and coagulation function are within normal limits. She agrees to participate in a clinical trial evaluating a new hemostasis material called EndoClot® absorbable polysaccharide hemostat (PAPH) versus metallic hemoclip. The trial aims to compare the effectiveness of the two methods in controlling intra-procedure bleeding and preventing rebleeding during and after EMR.

A 65-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a history of shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion. The patient was diagnosed with mitral valve regurgitation and underwent transcatheter mitral valve repair six months ago. The patient is currently on medication for hypertension and has no other significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the CSI-Ulm-TMVR clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. The patient's follow-up will be conducted for 10 years to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of the transcatheter mitral valve repair.

A 45-year-old African American woman with a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes visited the clinic. She reported feeling bloated and experiencing abdominal pain. A liver ultrasound scan revealed fatty liver disease. Her ALT levels were elevated, with levels of 45 IU/L. Her BMI was 35 kg/m². The patient reported no history of alcohol abuse. She reported taking metformin for her diabetes and lisinopril for hypertension. The patient provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

14-year-old female with a history of sickle cell disease presents with severe pain in the lower back, hips, and legs. She has been taking oxycodone for the past two weeks but the pain has not subsided. She requires daily, around-the-clock opioid treatment at a dose equivalent to at least 25 mg daily of hydrocodone. Vital signs are stable and hemoglobin oxygen saturation is normal. She is willing and able to swallow medicinal tablets. She has a negative pregnancy test and is using an acceptable method of birth control. She is able to perform study assessments and understand and complete the age-appropriate scale to rate pain intensity. She has no cognitive developmental delay or any other condition that would preclude her from completing the age-appropriate pain scale. She has never had surgery and has no planned surgery during the study. She has no known allergies to hydrocodone or any other component of HYD or any history of allergies to other opioids. She has not received or is expected to receive an investigational drug/therapy during the study drug treatment or follow-up period. She has never had alcohol, medication, or illicit drug abuse or addiction and/or opioid abuse or addiction at any time. She does not have any contraindication to blood sampling.

Patient is a 65-year-old man from the United States who has been suffering from osteoarthritis in his left knee for several years. He experiences significant pain and stiffness in his knee joint, which limits his daily activities and mobility. He has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy, pain medications, and corticosteroid injections, but none have provided significant relief. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has a BMI of 27. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with all follow-up requirements.

A 32-year-old man presents with persistent joint pain and swelling in his knees, ankles, and feet that started about 8 months ago. He reports having had urethritis about a month before the onset of his joint symptoms. He also reports a positive family history of arthritis. The patient has been experiencing stiffness in his back and hips, particularly in the morning, and has also been experiencing pain in his heels. He has not been diagnosed with any other autoimmune or inflammatory disorders in the past. The patient's physical exam shows swelling and tenderness in multiple joints, including his knees, ankles, and feet. The patient has no history of allergic reactions to antibiotics. The patient is willing to use a reliable form of contraception during the study as he has a female partner. The patient is not currently taking any medications that may interact with the study medications. The patient's liver function tests, complete blood count, and pregnancy test are all within normal limits. The patient has not received prolonged antibiotic treatment in the past.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who suffered a stroke 10 months ago resulting in mild to moderate weakness of her left arm and hand. She lives with her husband in their home and is able to perform activities of daily living with some assistance. She is able to walk 10 meters with a cane but requires assistance for longer distances. She has no significant cognitive deficits and has never had epilepsy or any other neurological conditions. She is interested in participating in a home-based rehabilitation program to further improve the function of her affected upper extremity. She has experience using a computer and is open to trying video games as a form of self-training.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who is undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment. She has tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 through PCR testing or has a high suspicion for COVID-19 based on CT scan. The patient is planned for an oocyte retrieval and has signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. There are no other exclusion criteria for this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past year. His pain has been worsening, and he has been experiencing numbness and tingling in his right leg. After being evaluated by a spine specialist, he was diagnosed with lumbar spinal stenosis, which requires surgical intervention. He is scheduled for a laminectomy and discectomy involving 2 adjacent lumbar vertebrae. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any opioid medications. He has no history of previous lumbar surgeries, spinal deformities, or communication difficulties. He has no neurological compromise and his coagulation profile is within normal limits. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who has recently been diagnosed with a benign thyroid condition. He has no history of thyroid or neck surgery and has not experienced any preoperative symptoms related to hypocalcaemia or vocal quality dysfunction. He has no history of hearing or voice problems and has not been diagnosed with gastroesophageal reflux or stomach ulcer disease. He is not on any medications that would contraindicate the use of steroids.

The patient is a 50 year old male with a BMI of 26. He works as a software engineer and enjoys playing golf on the weekends. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not abuse alcohol or drugs. He has no pacemaker or other implanted medical devices. He is able to understand and fulfill all requirements of the study and has provided signed informed consent. He has no current life-threatening medical conditions and has not used systemic corticosteroids recently. He has not engaged in unusually strenuous exercise within the previous 24 hours. There is no medical or anatomical condition that precludes testing of all 62 measurement points.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with colon cancer with clinical (by CT) high-risk T3 and T4 tumors. He experienced abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits for a few months before the diagnosis. He underwent a curative resection of the tumor and is now considered for this clinical trial. He has a performance status of 1 (able to do light work) and has signed the informed consent. He is married and has two grown-up children. He is a retired teacher and enjoys reading books, watching movies, and going for walks. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 27, and his lab tests show normal bone marrow and renal and liver function indices. He has no history of any other malignancy or significant medical condition. He is motivated to participate in this study to prevent the development of peritoneal metastases and improve his chances of long-term survival.

21-year-old female college student who is currently enrolled at the University of Mississippi with an active Facebook account and daily access to a smartphone. She reports experiencing anxiety related to academic stress and social pressures. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to examine the utility of the Transtheoretical Model in influencing anxiety among college students. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders and is not currently taking any medications for anxiety. She is within the eligible age range of 18-35 and has a University of Mississippi email account.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who works as a staff member at the University of Pennsylvania Health System. She is married and has two children, ages 5 and 7. She expresses concern about her family's diet and wishes to make healthier food choices, but struggles with finding fresh and affordable produce in her area. She typically eats dinner out with her family or orders takeout due to her busy work schedule and family responsibilities. She scores below the median (50th percentile) on dinners prepared at home on the screening survey and is therefore eligible for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to see if a CSA membership would help her family make healthier food choices and cook more meals at home.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma. He has no symptoms or signs of active disease, but tests have shown abnormal free light chain ratio, serum M-protein level, and t(4;14) genetic abnormality. Bone marrow biopsy showed 20% plasma cells. He has no lytic lesions or plasmacytomas and normal calcium levels. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. He has not received any prior systemic or radiation therapy for the treatment of myeloma. His blood chemistry and renal function tests are within normal limits. He has no peripheral neuropathy or history of seizures. He has no active, uncontrolled infections or intercurrent illnesses. He has no contraindications to deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophyl

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune disease that affects her skin and internal organs. She has been experiencing skin lesions and severe functional impairment in her hands, which significantly reduces her quality of life. She has undergone medical treatment but has not found any significant relief. She is interested in participating in an innovative cell therapy procedure that involves the reinjection of autologous stromal vascular fraction of adipose origin according to the Celution® system (Cytori Therapeutics, Inc.., United Kingdom) in her hands. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has a functional index of the hand of Cochin upper to 20. She is not participating in any other biomedical research, is not a minor, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no legal protection and is not staying in a sanitary or social establishment.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer with HER2 overexpression. She has no known allergies and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has no history of chemotherapy or trastuzumab therapy for metastatic breast cancer. She has a performance status of 1 and a life expectancy greater than 6 months. She was previously treated with radiation therapy for early stage breast cancer. She has no other non-breast cancer malignancies, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She has no history of neuropathy or other significant medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the trial.

The patient is a 72 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. She has not undergone any previous treatment for this condition. She is in otherwise good health and has no major comorbidities. She is willing and eligible to receive chemotherapy with or without Avastin. She has not participated in any other clinical trials or studies, except for registries.

A 34-year-old woman who sustained a moderate traumatic brain injury (TBI) in a motor vehicle accident presents with cognitive deficits such as difficulty with attention, working memory and processing speed. She has a history of alcohol abuse but is currently sober. She is not currently taking any medications that affect cognition. She is fluent in English and able to comprehend both verbal and written language. She has no history of psychiatric illness and does not have any metal in her body that is not compatible with an MRI scan. She is willing to participate in a study aimed at improving her cognitive abilities through computerized cognitive Speed of Information Processing (SIP) training. She is available to attend two study visits over the course of approximately 13 weeks and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the experimental or control group.

Eligible participants for this clinical trial are full-time nursing students, aged 18 or above, who have been diagnosed with allergic rhinitis for at least two years by a Western medicine and/or Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner. Participants should have a body constitution of Cold and Yang-Deficiency, as assessed by a TCM practitioner, and must understand written Chinese language, particularly the questionnaires used. Exclusion

Patient is a 58-year-old man from the United States who comes to the clinic with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced, unresectable non-small cell lung cancer (Stage III). He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He reports feeling fatigued and short of breath with mild exertion, but denies any other symptoms. His ECOG PS score is 1. He has measurable disease by RECIST and is estimated to have a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. He has not been previously treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy and does not have active autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency. There is no evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, active bleeding diatheses, or active infections including hepatitis B, C and HIV. He has well-controlled hypertension and no evidence of symptomatic congestive heart failure or unstable angina pectoris. He has no unresolved toxicity from prior chemoradiation therapy and has no active or prior documented inflammatory bowel disease.

Patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary node dissection on the right side, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been on hormone therapy for the past two years. She presented with new onset chest pain and shortness of breath. A CT scan revealed a new right upper lobe lung nodule. PET/CT scan was performed to evaluate the lung nodule and to assess for other possible metastases. The PET/CT scan showed increased uptake in the lung nodule with a standardized uptake value (SUV) of 4.2. However, during the injection of the radiolabeled tracer, the patient experienced a moderate infiltration at the injection site. The infiltrate was identified but was not completely resolved before the scan was performed. The patient will now be invited to return for a repeat PET/CT scan with injection performed by specially trained personnel to reduce the risk of repeat infiltration. The two scans will be compared to assess for changes in tumor uptake intensity. The patient is willing to participate in this study and meets the inclusion criteria.

35 y/o female with a history of irritable bowel syndrome, diagnosed 5 years ago. She also recently developed symptoms of constipation, abdominal pain, and flatulence. She has tried multiple medications and dietary changes but has not seen significant improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as a potential treatment option. She has no contraindications to the FMT infusion method such as endoscopy or colonoscopy. She has no other severe diseases and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

45-year-old female with chronic low back pain for the past 2 years. The pain is located in the lower back and radiates to the right leg. The pain is described as sharp and shooting, with a current NPRS score of 7/10. Patient has been prescribed opioids for pain management but is concerned about the potential for dependence and is interested in alternative treatment options. She has tried physical therapy and acupuncture in the past, but did not experience significant relief. The patient is able to ambulate independently and has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of substance abuse or major psychiatric disorders. The patient is willing and able to use the EaseVRx program as directed for 56 days and has access to a compatible VR device at home. She is not planning to have surgery or start any new treatments for her pain in the next 3 months.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic for a routine checkup. He is in good health, has no underlying disease, and his BMI is 24 kg/m2. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is a non-smoker and does not consume recreational drugs. He takes over-the-counter multivitamins regularly but is willing to discontinue their use for the duration of the study. He has no history of mental illness and is not taking any prescription medications. He is willing to use effective contraceptive methods during the study period and for 3 months after study completion. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to follow the study procedures and maintain a consistent diet and lifestyle throughout the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 32nd week of pregnancy. Her Hb level is 11.2g/dL, which is within the normal range. She has never participated in a clinical study before and is willing to participate in this study. She has no history of acute hemorrhage during pregnancy, intolerance to iron therapy, hemolytic anemia, hemoglobinopathies (thalassemia, sickle cell), bleeding tendency, or hypersplenism. She does not have chronic heart failure, Class II-IV heart disease, uncontrolled arterial hypertension, deep vein thrombosis, thrombocytosis, or chronic renal disease. Her renal function and liver function are normal, with no evidence of severe renal failure or liver dysfunction. Her CK level is also within the normal range. She meets all the eligibility criteria and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing mild memory loss and difficulty with problem-solving for the past year. She has no significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. A recent MRI showed mild hippocampal atrophy and mild white matter hyperintensity. The patient underwent a series of tests and was diagnosed with early (prodromal) Alzheimer's disease. She has a global Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR) score of 0.5 and was found to have evidence of amyloid pathology through a positive amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) scan. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m² and is otherwise healthy for her age group. She is not of childbearing potential and has no history of significant depression or any other neurological disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of JNJ-54861911.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman diagnosed with Spina Bifida at birth. She is currently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program in Social Work and is working part-time as a receptionist. She lives with her parents and younger sister in a single-family home. She uses a wheelchair for mobility and has some difficulty with fine motor skills. She enjoys spending time with friends and family, reading, and watching movies. She has never participated in a clinical trial before and is interested in learning more about the impact of Spina Bifida on her daily life. She is fluent in Dutch and able to read and write in the language.

A 45-year old woman was admitted to the hospital with a fever and shortness of breath. She has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is a former smoker. She has been hospitalized several times in the past for COPD exacerbations. Upon admission, blood cultures were positive for a multi-drug resistant gram-negative bacteria. Sputum culture also showed the same bacteria. She was started on colistin for the infection. The patient is currently on supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula and is receiving nebulizer treatments. She is alert and oriented, and her vital signs are stable. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

35 y/o couple residing in the United States, who have 2 children conceived via sperm donation, aged 8 and 10 years. The couple has not disclosed the donor conception to their children and are struggling with the decision of when and how to do so. Both parents are fluent in English and have not received any counseling or education about disclosure to their children. They are interested in participating in the TELL Tool intervention trial to gain access to new tools that could assist them in the disclosure process.

A 45-year-old woman is concerned about her thinning hair and has noticed a significant decrease in hair volume over the past year. She has a family history of hair loss and has been diagnosed with androgenetic alopecia. She has Fitzpatrick Skin Type III and has experienced hair loss in the Ludwig II-2 classification. She is generally healthy and not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of the HairMax LaserComb 2009 12 beam model for androgenetic alopecia in females. She is willing to use the device as directed on three non-concurring days a week for 26 weeks and attend follow-up visits as required.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with her 4-year-old son. The child was found with an open bottle of prescription medication in his hand, and the mother reports that she had left the medication on the kitchen counter while she was on the phone. The child ingested an unknown amount of the medication, and the mother is concerned about his safety. The patient reports that she is the primary caregiver for her son and is responsible for his care 7 days a week. She lives in a single-family home with her son, husband, and two cats. The patient reports that she has never used a medication lockbox, and the medication that her son ingested was stored in its original bottle. The patient reports that she has a history of depression and anxiety but is currently not taking any medications for these conditions. The patient is able to provide consent for herself and her son to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old female scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent gallbladder stones. She has no known allergies to any medications, and her medical history is unremarkable except for a previous appendectomy. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. Her preoperative laboratory values are within normal limits, including a hemoglobin concentration of 13.5g/dl. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 34-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes. She has been on a stable regimen of multiple daily insulin injections, which includes a short-acting as well as a long-acting insulin. She has a BMI within the range of 18.5 to 33.0 kg/m². Her blood pressure, pulse rate, ECG, blood and urine laboratory test results are all acceptable for the study. She has not experienced any episodes of severe hypoglycemia in the past 6 months, which required assistance in treatment by a second party. She has venous access that is sufficient to allow for blood sampling. She has provided written consent and is willing to follow study procedures and commit to the study duration. She is not currently enrolled or has not participated in any clinical trial or any other type of medical research judged to be incompatible with this study. She has not previously completed or withdrawn from this study. She does not have any health problems that, in the opinion of the doctor, could make it unsafe to participate in the study. She has not had blood loss of more than 500 mL within the last month. She is not treated with a continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (insulin pump).

Patient is a 32yo male with a history of mild asthma, confirmed cat hair Felis domesticus allergy, and a current e-cigarette habit of 5 years, smoking 1-2 cartridges per day. He reports occasional wheezing, coughing and shortness of breath with

A 45-year-old male construction worker fell from a height of 10 feet and sustained an open fracture to his left tibia. He was brought to the emergency room and underwent initial wound debridement and stabilization of the fracture. He has no known allergies to detergents or castile soap ingredients. He has no previous history of wound infection or osteomyelitis in the injured extremity. He is currently taking no immunosuppressive medication and does not have any immunological deficient conditions such as HIV. He is willing to undergo the required procedures and has provided informed consent. He has a fixed address and is expected to be available for follow-up visits.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right knee for the last six months. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis in his right knee and has taken some over-the-counter pain medications, but the relief has been minimal. He is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. His BMI is 27 and his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg. Laboratory studies show no abnormalities. He is willing to discontinue all non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or other analgesic medication taken for any condition, including his knee pain. He is willing to abstain from any intra-articular or peri-articular injections to the knee or surgery during the treatment period. He has no history of prior peptic ulcer disease or prior NSAID gastrointestinal complications for the past 5 years.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial. The trial is focused on community health workers in Mali who are already providing iCCM services to children under the age of 5 years with suspected symptoms of pneumonia. The study will evaluate the effectiveness of a self-monitoring tool (ChARM) in improving the accuracy of respiratory rate counting and pneumonia diagnosis by these health workers. Eligible participants are those who have completed the Malian Ministry of Health basic community health care worker training and are currently using a device (a respiratory timer or a cell phone) as part of their basic training package. The trial excludes health workers in conflict-ridden geographical areas, those who do not have a device to support respiratory rate measurement, and those who did not complete the basic training for CHWs provided through the 2016-2020 Strengthening Maternal, Newborn and Child Health program.

53 yo F with a history of recurring dyspeptic symptoms including pain after eating, bloating, and occasional nausea. She has undergone extensive gastrointestinal evaluations, including endoscopy and upper GI series, which were all negative. She has tried various medications and dietary modifications without significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to identify the underlying cause of her symptoms. Past Medical History: - Hypothyroidism - Osteopenia - Depression - Anxiety - Migraines - No history of gastrointestinal diseases or surgeries. Medications: - Levothyroxine - Alendronate - Sertraline - Sumatriptan.

32F, recently diagnosed with HIV, with no prior history of opportunistic infections or AIDS-defining illnesses. She was started on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) regimen 6 months ago and has been adherent with therapy with viral loads ranging from 500 to 1000 copies/ml. Her last CD4 count was 270 cells/mm3. She reports no significant side effects from her current regimen. She has no known history of drug resistance. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of changing HIV therapy at lower versus higher viral loads. She is willing to remain on her current regimen until her scheduled switch and agrees to use two acceptable forms of contraception while on study and for 60 days after going off study. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, does not use drugs or alcohol that would interfere with the study, and has not used any experimental agents or drugs that interfere with the immune system within 45 days prior to entry.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of stage IV colorectal cancer. He has undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor and received adjuvant chemotherapy with capecitabine and oxaliplatin. However, a PET-CT scan revealed metastases to the lungs and liver. The patient is currently asymptomatic and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no history of neuropathy or other neurological disorders. The patient meets all the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the trial. He is not on any other medications or supplements and does not have any allergies to medications. He does not have any significant medical history or comorbidities.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman was diagnosed with colon cancer with liver metastases. She complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She had no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. Her vital signs were stable on presentation. Physical examination revealed diffuse abdominal tenderness. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed a large mass in the sigmoid colon with multiple liver metastases. She underwent a colonoscopy that revealed a large mass in the sigmoid colon. Biopsy of the mass confirmed adenocarcinoma. Her laboratory results were within normal limits except for elevated CEA level (45 ng/mL). She was deemed a candidate for liver resection and enrolled in the clinical trial. She met all inclusion criteria and had no exclusion criteria. She was started on FOLFOX-based therapy and underwent pre-operative treatment. She underwent liver resection after completion of pre-operative chemotherapy. Post-operative FOLFOX-based therapy was started. She tolerated the chemotherapy well with no significant side effects. She completed the therapy as scheduled and has been followed up for 2 years with no evidence of recurrence.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis for the past year. She reports having redness, itching, and tearing in both eyes, with occasional swelling of the eyelids. These symptoms typically occur during the spring and fall months and are triggered by exposure to pollen and other environmental allergens. She has tried over-the-counter antihistamine eye drops in the past, but has not found them to be very effective. She does not wear contact lenses and is willing to avoid any disallowed medications during the study. She has no known allergies to the study medications and is able to read an eye chart from 10 feet away. She is interested in participating in the study to find a more effective treatment for her allergic conjunctivitis.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with a benign tumor in the colon scheduled for a partial colectomy. The patient reports mild to moderate abdominal pain and occasional nausea. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. His BMI is 27. Laboratory analysis is unremarkable, and his ECG is normal. The patient has a history of opioid use for postoperative pain relief after a previous surgery. He is fluent in English and Spanish and willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 17-year-old girl who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two years ago. She received chemotherapy and achieved remission, but unfortunately, her disease has relapsed. She has since undergone two attempts at remission induction with no success. Her current disease state is refractory and there is no known curative therapy or therapy proven to prolong survival with an acceptable quality of life. She has a Karnofsky score of 70% and has recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy. Her platelet count is 25,000/mm^3 and she may receive platelet transfusions. Her serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. She has not received prior exposure to AZD1775 and is willing to use an effective double barrier contraceptive method for the duration of protocol therapy. She is able to swallow capsules whole and is not currently receiving drugs that are strong or moderate inhibitors and/or inducers of cytochrome P450 family 3 subfamily A polypeptide 4 (CYP3A4) or sensitive CYP3A4 substrates and CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic range. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to sign a written informed consent.

This is a 56 year-old Japanese male who presented with persistent cough and chest pain. He was diagnosed with non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after a biopsy was performed. The cancer has spread to his lymph nodes and lungs. He has not received any prior chemotherapy for NSCLC. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Score of 1. He has adequate bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function. He does not have a history of hypersensitivity to paclitaxel or to other drugs formulated with polyethoxylated castor oil (Cremophor). He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of linifanib (ABT-869) in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel as a first-line treatment for his NSCLC.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who was in a car crash 6 months ago and suffered a moderate traumatic brain injury. She has been experiencing fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and occasional depression since the accident. She is currently taking sertraline for depression and zolpidem for insomnia. She has no history of seizures or drug abuse. She works full-time as a teacher and lives with her husband and two children. She reports having difficulty keeping up with her normal daily activities due to her fatigue and sleep disturbances. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand the potential endocrine abnormalities associated with her TBI and to learn about any potential treatments that may improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has not received any prior therapy for the metastatic lesions. He has a history of smoking and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is a retired accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His ECOG score is 1. He has no significant comorbidities and his serum ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. He has undergone surgical resection to obtain tumor tissues. His metastatic lesions occupy less than 50% of liver volume. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or organ transplantation. He has no history of other malignant diseases in the past 5 years. He is not pregnant or lactating. He does not have any acute or chronic infectious diseases. He has no history of allergy or allergic constitutions. He has not received any chemotherapy, radiotherapy or immunotherapy within the last four weeks. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with a severely decayed molar that requires extraction.
