The patient has no history of periapical pathology and maintains good oral hygiene. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any known blood disorders. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in replacing the extracted tooth with a dental implant and is willing to participate in a clinical study evaluating different ridge preservation techniques to improve bone formation and alveolar dimensional stability after tooth extraction.

A 56-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo an elective abdominal surgical procedure under general anesthesia. She has an ASA Class 3 status due to her medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is expected to undergo neuromuscular relaxation with rocuronium for endotracheal intubation and to require at least one maintenance dose of rocuronium. She is also expected to require active reversal of neuromuscular blockade and to recover in the PACU. The patient is sexually active and agrees to use a medically accepted method of contraception through seven days after receiving protocol-specified medication. She has no anatomical malformations that may lead to difficult intubation or neuromuscular disorders that may affect neuromuscular blockade and/or trial assessments. The patient has normal renal and hepatic function with no significant allergies to study treatments or medications used during general anesthesia. She is not taking toremifene or any investigational drug(s) within 30 days of randomization on this study, nor has she participated in any other clinical trial within 30 days of signing the informed consent form of the current trial. The patient or any of her family members are not among the personnel of the investigational or Sponsor staff directly involved with this trial.

This clinical trial is seeking male or female participants who are at least 5 years old and able to provide signed informed consent. Participants should not have taken any medication known to affect body temperature, such as antipyretics, barbiturates, thyroid preparations, or antipsychotics, within 3 hours of the test. Additionally, participants who have been immunized within seven days of the test will not be eligible for this study. The study aims to evaluate the clinical accuracy of the welloStationX, a non-contact thermometer that uses an infrared sensor on the surface of the forehead to screen for fever. If you are interested in participating, please contact the study coordinators for more information.

32-year-old African American male with a history of sickle cell disease presents to the emergency department with severe acute pain. The patient reports a history of frequent ED visits for pain management, with a total of 10 visits in the past year. The patient complains of not receiving adequate pain management during previous ED visits due to the perception among clinicians that he is "drug-seeking." The patient is currently not taking any medication for his sickle cell disease and reports a history of stroke and pulmonary embolism. Past Medical History: - Sickle cell disease - Stroke - Pulmonary embolism.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) based on the Japanese Association for Acute Medicine-defined DIC criteria. The patient has a DIC score of at least 4 and an antithrombin activity of less than or equal to 70%. The patient has given written informed consent or has a guardian who has given consent for participation in the clinical trial. The patient does not have a history of serious drug allergies and has no complications related to liver disorders such as fulminant hepatitis or decompensated cirrhosis. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or possibly pregnant. The patient is not at risk for experiencing bleeding due to the concomitant use of heparin.

A 58-year-old Caucasian female resident of rural Wisconsin with a history of osteoporosis and vitamin D deficiency presents for a clinical trial evaluating the impact of vitamin D supplementation on bone health. She is postmenopausal and has a BMI of 27 kg/m². She reports no history of nephrolithiasis, hypercalcemia or any form of cancer within the past five years. She is currently taking a standard multiple vitamin containing 400 IU of vitamin D once daily. She is willing to avoid cod-liver oil and any non-study vitamin D supplementation during the trial. She is willing to use SPF-15 or higher sunscreen when sun exposure for more than 15 minutes is expected. Her baseline serum 25OHD concentration is 17 ng/ml. She is willing to sign informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in the first chronic phase. He was diagnosed during a routine blood test as he experienced no significant symptoms. The patient has not received any prior treatment for CML. He has a matched related donor available for the study. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The patient has no known drug allergies. The patient has adequate organ function with serum creatinine, total bilirubin, SGOT (AST), and SGPT (ALT) all within normal limits. Echocardiogram shows a shortening fraction of >25%. Pulmonary function tests show DLCO >40%. The patient has no dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and a pulse oximetry >94% in room air. The patient has been fully informed about their illness and the investigational nature of the study protocol and has signed an informed consent in accordance with the institutional policies approved by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The patient is not pregnant.

A 25-year-old male soccer player presented to the orthopedic clinic with a history of twisting his right knee while playing. He complained of pain, swelling, and instability in his knee joint. On examination, he had a positive Lachman test and pivot shift test, indicating a possible ACL rupture. MRI of the right knee confirmed a complete ACL tear with no other significant injuries. He was deemed eligible for the clinical trial and randomly assigned to Group A, which will undergo a single bundle ACL reconstruction surgery. The patient has no significant medical history, is not using any medication, and has no allergies. He is an active athlete with a BMI of 23 and has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has noticed changes in her skin due to chronic sun exposure. She has several actinic keratosis lesions on her face and is concerned about the possibility of skin cancer. She is a non-smoker and has no history of skin cancer or other medical conditions that could interfere with the study. Her Fitzpatrick phototype is III. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the appearance of her skin and reduce the risk of skin cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and no other significant medical history. He presents to the hospital with a fever of 39°C, cough, and shortness of breath for 3 days. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. He denies any recent travel or exposure to anyone with confirmed COVID-19. Upon admission, he is diagnosed with moderate COVID-19 pneumonia based on his symptoms, lab tests, and CT scan findings. He is able to swallow medication without difficulty and agrees to participate in the clinical trial after signing the informed consent form. He has no known allergy to Favipiravir or any of its components. He is currently not on any medication except for antihypertensive medication. He has no history of alcohol, pharmacological, or drug addiction. He has no history of mental pathology. He is willing to use reliable contraceptive methods throughout the study and within 3 months after its completion. He is excluded from the study if he has impaired liver or kidney function or if he needs treatment in the intensive care unit. He will be advised to inform the physician if any new medical condition arises during the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 2 years ago. She is currently using an insulin pump and has been on insulin therapy for the past 2 years. She is an active teenager who enjoys skiing and participating in winter sports. She has no history of diabetic ketoacidosis or hypoglycemic seizure. Her medical history is not significant for any other medical issues. Her family history is negative for diabetes or any other chronic diseases. Her lab studies are as follows: Fasting blood glucose: 120 mg/dl, HbA1c: 7.5%. She is willing to wear a continuous glucose sensor and physiological monitor for the duration of the study and her parents are available for system training and will commit to being the main responsible person for the use of the AP system at home. She is not pregnant and does not have any medical or psychiatric condition that might interfere with the completion of the protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of dental problems. He has been referred to the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery at the University of Jordan Hospital for a non-surgical extraction of one posterior maxillary permanent tooth. The patient is classified as ASA II and is fit for surgery under local anesthesia. He understands the given oral instructions and is willing to participate in the study. The patient does not have acute dento-alveolar infection and is not on anti-inflammatory or recreational drugs. He does not require conscious sedation or general anesthesia. The patient has bilateral symmetrical posterior maxillary permanent teeth referred for extraction under local anesthesia.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with pre-hypertension during a routine check-up. She has a family history of hypertension, as her mother and grandmother both have high blood pressure. Her fasting blood sugar is 110 mg/dL, and her body mass index is 32. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively. She has never experienced any cardiac, cerebral, or vascular events in the past six months. She is not currently taking any beta blockers or ACE inhibitors. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her cardiovascular health and reduce her risk of developing hypertension or other cardiovascular diseases.

A 35-year-old Hispanic woman has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years. She has tried several diets and exercise regimens without success. Her current weight is 135 kg with a BMI of 50 kg/m2. She has been diagnosed with prediabetes and is taking metformin to control her blood sugar levels. Her medical history is unremarkable except for a cholecystectomy 5 years ago. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She works as a teacher and has a sedentary lifestyle. She is interested in undergoing bariatric surgery and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of dietary protein supplementation on her nitrogen balance, body composition, and satiety.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with systemic sclerosis (SSc) for the past 5 years. She reports experiencing Raynaud's phenomenon, skin thickening, and joint pain. She has no history of cancer or chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She has not had any recent infections. She is on a stable regimen of medications for SSc including immunosuppressants and vasodilators. She has not had any recent hospitalizations or surgeries. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the role of circulating cytotoxic lymphocytes in endothelial cell injury in SSc in hopes of contributing to the advancement of knowledge and treatment options for this disease.

55 y/o male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes presents with acute respiratory failure due to community-acquired pneumonia. The patient was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation in pressure-support mode with a PEEP of 8 cmH2O and a pressure support level of 7 cmH2O. The patient has a positive response to antibiotics, and the pneumonia has resolved. The patient's PaO2/FiO2 ratio is >300 mmHg, and the patient is ready to undergo a decremental pressure support trial to evaluate diaphragm function. The patient does not have a diagnosis of COPD, and there is no evidence of circulatory failure.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been experiencing obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors for the past year. He spends several hours a day on repetitive hand-washing rituals and constantly checks that doors and windows are locked. His symptoms have been causing significant distress and interfere with his daily activities such as school attendance and social interactions. He has a total score of 24 on the JCY-BOCS. He is currently not taking any medication for his OCD but has received counseling in the past with limited improvement. His weight is within the standard weight ± 2S.D. based on the standard weight for his age in the School Health Statistical Survey. He does not have a diagnosis of schizophrenia and has not been previously treated with fluvoxamine maleate.

A 50-year-old male patient presents with a history of gastric neoplasm and has been recommended for endoscopic resection. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no previous history of HP eradication or PPI use within the past 6 months. The patient will undergo endoscopy and biopsy to investigate the distribution of HP in the stomach before, during, and after the use of PPI.

The patient is a 32 year-old male who was diagnosed with a soft tissue sarcoma in his right upper arm. The tumor was located between the scapula and arm, and there were no metastases at the time of diagnosis. He underwent limb salvage surgery six months ago and is currently in follow-up care at the Comprehensive Cancer Center, Helsinki University Hospital. He has no other significant medical history and is currently not receiving any other treatments. He is able to perform his activities of daily living without assistance but has noticed some limitations in his range of motion and strength in his right arm. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the understanding of the functional outcomes and health-related quality of life in patients who have undergone similar surgeries.

A 53 year old male patient came to the clinic with a history of glaucoma in his family. He had been diagnosed with early stage glaucoma damage on HVF and currently being treated with eye drops. He has no other ocular or systemic diseases, and his refraction is -1.5 D. His visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. His pupils are reactive to light with no signs of iris abnormalities or neovascularization. He has not undergone any intraocular ophthalmic procedures within the past 30 days. He is willing to sign informed consent and participate in the study.

32 yo M diagnosed with HIV-1 seropositivity and on a stable dose of zidovudine (AZT) for at least 8 weeks with no opportunistic infection for the past 8 weeks. The patient is asymptomatic and has not experienced significant weight loss or fever within the last 3 months. The patient does not have any active drug or alcohol abuse and has no significant cardiac or pulmonary disease (Forced Expiratory Volume > 75 percent). The patient is not on any systemic therapy for opportunistic infection (OI) and has not received any other immunomodulators, corticosteroids, anti-neoplastic chemotherapy, or other experimental therapy within the last 12 weeks. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is available for follow-up visits.

A 65-year-old man presents with a history of elevated prostate specific antigen (PSA) levels during routine prostate cancer screening. He has undergone a prostate biopsy that confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma of the prostate gland with a Gleason score of 7. His PSA level is 12 ng/dL, and he has intermediate-risk prostate cancer according to the T stage (T2b). The patient is scheduled to undergo a radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection within the next few weeks. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and provide informed consent. The patient agrees to use an acceptable form of birth control for a period of 7 days after the Cu-64-TP3805 injection. He has not been administered any radioisotope within 10 physical half-lives before the study drug injection. The patient has no medical conditions or other circumstances that would significantly decrease obtaining reliable data, achieving study objectives, or completing the study, according to the investigator's opinion.

56 yo M with a history of stage IIIB lung cancer. The patient received chemotherapy and radiation therapy within the last 6 months and reports feeling fatigued and weak with no regular exercise regimen in place. The patient is ambulatory but sedentary and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status score of 1 due to some symptoms. The patient is interested in participating in a 12-week exercise program to improve his health outcomes. He has no bone or joint destruction that could be aggravated with exercise and has no severe cognitive impairment. The patient's medical care provider has approved him for participation in the program. The patient speaks and reads English fluently.

A 32-year-old Caucasian male with a history of atopic dermatitis (AD) for the past 5 years complains of persistent itching and redness on his arms, legs, and torso. He has tried various topical treatments, but none of them have provided long-term relief. He has never received systemic therapy for AD. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works from home. He is married and has two children. He reports feeling stressed due to work and family responsibilities. He has a history of seasonal allergies. His past medical history is unremarkable. His family history is negative for any skin problems. His EASI score is 20, and his IGA score is 4.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been suffering from chronic rhinosinusitis for several years. She has tried medical treatment, but unfortunately, it has not been effective. She continues to experience facial pain, nasal congestion, and headaches. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant past medical history. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is scheduled to have endoscopic sinus surgery to alleviate her symptoms. She has health insurance and has given informed consent to participate in the study. She is not taking any antidepressive medications and has no history of coagulation disorders. She is classified as an ASA score 2.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of HIV infection and is currently on stable antiretroviral therapy for over six months. She reports no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or coronary revascularization. She has no symptoms of stable or unstable angina and is not currently being treated for diabetes or actively using cocaine. The patient is not currently taking any exogenous hormones or prescription medication for autoimmune/inflammatory diseases, post-transplant care, asthma, or pain syndromes. She has a calculated eGFR of 85 ml/min/1.73 m2 and no known allergies to iodinated contrast media, dextrans/DTPA/radiometals, or regadenoson/adenosine. The patient has not received significant radiation exposure in the past 12 months and is not currently enrolled in any conflicting research studies. The patient will undergo structural and functional cardiovascular imaging studies, vascular, metabolic/hormonal, and immune phenotyping to assess the relationship between HIV infection, systemic immune activation, inflammation, and cardiovascular pathology.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with no history of bone, joint, muscle or neurovascular disease. He has a BMI of 25 and has no abnormalities in the infraclavicular region. He has not had any injuries, radiation exposure, or invasive procedures in the past. The patient has provided written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with primary hyperparathyroidism. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. She reports feeling fatigued and has bone pain in her lower back. Laboratory tests revealed an elevated calcium level of 11.2 mg/dL (normal range: 8.6-10.3 mg/dL) and an elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) level of 95 pg/mL (normal range: 10-65 pg/mL). Imaging studies showed a single parathyroid adenoma. She was started on cinacalcet 30 mg daily by her endocrinologist and referred to the clinical trial for further evaluation. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She has not used cinacalcet before and does not have secondary HPT or any other known cause of hypercalcaemia.

50 yo male with chronic kidney disease (stage 5) on hemodialysis for the last 2 years, presents with a history of anemia requiring maintenance therapy with darbepoetin alfa for the last 12 weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of smoking. The patient is otherwise stable on his current hemodialysis regimen with no significant past medical or surgical history. Labs show a hemoglobin level of 10.2 g/dL, ferritin level of 200, and transferrin saturation of 25%. The patient has no overt gastrointestinal bleeding or active malignancy. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for the maintenance treatment of anemia in dialysis patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese male who underwent hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 2 years ago. He is currently experiencing chronic graft versus host disease (cGVHD) and is steroid dependent, requiring a daily dose of prednisolone greater than or equal to 0.25 milligram per kilogram per day (mg/kg/day). Despite multiple attempts to taper the dose, his cGVHD manifestations have not improved. He is currently receiving other immunosuppressive therapies in addition to glucocorticoids. His Karnofsky performance status is 70. The patient has not received treatment with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, purine analogs, or other cancer chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks. He has not been vaccinated with live, attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks of the first dose of ibrutinib.

52 yo M who was recently hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and resides in the health care area of the University Hospital of A Coruña. Past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. The patient is able to read and understand the participation sheet in the study and has signed informed consent to participate. The patient possesses and is familiar with operating a smartphone. The patient's LVEF is >30% and has a NYHA score of II.

A 32-year-old Brazilian male with a diagnosed history of schizophrenia presents with symptoms of auditory hallucinations and disorganized thinking, resulting in difficulty maintaining employment and social relationships. The patient has been stable on antipsychotic medication for the past 6 months but continues to experience cognitive impairments, including difficulty with attention and working memory. The patient speaks Portuguese as his primary language, which he learned before the age of 12. He reports no major medical or neurological disorders that would prevent him from participating in the study. The patient has an IQ score of 85 and does not have active substance dependence. The patient is interested in participating in a 40-hour computerized cognitive training program to improve his cognitive functioning, clinical symptoms, and overall quality of life.

A 45-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B infection presents with persistent fatigue and mild abdominal discomfort. He was diagnosed with hepatitis B virus 10 years ago and has been on antiviral therapy intermittently. He is HBeAg positive and HBsAg levels are greater than 250 IU/mL. He has never been diagnosed with cirrhosis. His liver function tests show a mildly elevated AST level of 60 IU/L and a normal bilirubin level. His platelet count is 110E+09/L and his albumin level is above 35 g/L. His INR and AFP levels are within normal limits. He is currently not on any medication for hepatitis B. He is married and works as a sales representative. He has two children and leads an active lifestyle. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo liver biopsy during the screening period and 48 weeks after completion of drug administration.

A 25-year-old woman who works as a nurse is experiencing symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis during the fall season. She has a history of allergies and has been previously diagnosed with SAR. Her symptoms include nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy, watery eyes. She has not used any intranasal corticosteroids or allergy medications for the past 4 weeks. She does not have any significant medical conditions and is not currently taking any prescription medications except for an oral contraceptive. She is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study period. She is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco products. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures and restrictions and can read and comprehend information in English. She has provided an appropriately signed and dated informed consent. She resides in a geographical region where exposure to fall seasonal allergen is expected to be significant during the entire study period and does not plan to travel outside this area for more than 48 hours during the study period.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty achieving and maintaining an erection for the past 6 months. He has a confirmed clinical diagnosis of erectile dysfunction and has been involved in a continuous heterosexual relationship for at least 6 months. He has a low IIEF-EF score (≤ 25) during the screening period. The patient and his female partner are capable of understanding and complying with the requirements of the protocol and have signed the informed consent form prior to participation in any study-related procedures. The patient has no significant or serious cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, haematological, endocrinological, metabolic, neurological or psychiatric disease that would render him unfit to take part in the study. He is not using any medication that is likely to affect his ability to complete the study or preclude his participation in the study. He has no history of radical prostatectomy, severe/uncontrolled diabetes, or postural hypotension, hypotension or uncorrected hypovolaemia. The patient is not taking two or more anti-hypertensives for the treatment of BP, and is not hypersensitive to GTN or to any of the excipients, or has idiosyncratic reactions to other organic nitrates. He is not receiving testosterone pellets, is not taking Alpha blockers, and has not had any penile surgery except circumcision. The patient has no history of operations for Peyronie's disease or primary hypoactive sexual desire or any history of hypogonadism. He is not taking dihydroergotamine or acetyl cysteine, and has no history of migraine or recurrent headache. The patient has not used any investigational product during the 90 days prior to dosing for this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male rubber tapper who has been working in the industry for the past 10 years. He reports experiencing occasional lower back pain after long hours of work, which has been affecting his productivity and quality of life. He has not had any previous significant low back pain or back surgery. He does not have any underlying rheumatologic condition. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of lumbar support for low back pain prevention.

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of laparotomy for appendectomy 4 years ago presented to the clinic with complaints of a bulge in the incisional area that had gradually increased in size over the past few months. Physical examination revealed a reducible incisional hernia with a hernia size of 4 cm. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or chronic illness. He is currently not taking any medication or undergoing any treatment. The patient has a good understanding of the study requirements and is willing to comply with the instructions. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has not undergone any previous mesh implantation at the same site and has no immune competence issues. The patient is not currently participating in any other investigational drug or medical device study.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of propionic acidemia (PA). He was diagnosed at birth through newborn screening and has been on a strict low-protein diet and carnitine supplementation since then. He has been hospitalized several times due to metabolic decompensation and has had a few episodes of seizures. His developmental milestones have been delayed, and he has had some learning difficulties. He complains of frequent abdominal pain and has a history of constipation. The patient is well-nourished and well-dressed, with no apparent physical abnormalities. He is able to communicate well and follow instructions. The patient and his parents are interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about his condition and potentially improve his health outcomes. They are able to travel to the clinic for the required hospital visits.

A 45-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension and diabetes mellitus was referred for kidney transplant evaluation. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years and his current vascular access is an AV fistula in the left arm. His latest labs showed a creatinine level of 7.8 mg/dL and a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine and lisinopril. He does not have a history of cardiac disease and his pre-transplant echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 60%. He is scheduled for a deceased donor kidney transplant surgery in the upcoming weeks. The patient is aware of and has consented to participate in the clinical trial. During the surgery, he experiences distributive shock and needs vasopressor support. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is enrolled in the trial.

A 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic pain and numbness in his lower limbs for more than a year. Despite trying multiple drugs from various categories such as tricyclic antidepressants, anti-epileptic agents, and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, he has not experienced significant relief from the symptoms. He reports that the pain is continuous and has severely impacted his quality of life, causing sleep disturbances and limiting his daily activities. He has been diagnosed with small fiber neuropathy (SFN) and has undergone skin biopsy and quantitative sensory testing to confirm the diagnosis. His medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently on blood pressure medications. He reports no history of drug addiction or alcohol abuse. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial involving Spinal Cord Stimulation (SCS) in combination with the best drug treatment as usual (TAU) to potentially help alleviate his pain and improve his quality of life.

A 38-year-old female presents with unexplained weight gain, facial hair growth, and irregular menstrual cycles. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known family history of osteoporosis, cardiovascular disorders, or thromboembolism. Physical examination shows central obesity, moon face, and buffalo hump. Laboratory testing reveals elevated cortisol levels, and imaging studies confirm the diagnosis of Cushing's disease. She speaks French fluently and is willing to participate in the study. Her life expectancy is normal, and she is not pregnant nor dependent.

8-year-old female with a history of asthma diagnosed at the age of 4. She is currently being treated with an albuterol inhaler and a daily inhaled corticosteroid. She reports experiencing wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath regularly, even with her current treatment regimen. She has had no hospitalizations or emergency department visits in the past year for asthma exacerbations. She is able to perform spirometry and demonstrates 15% airways reversibility. She is not currently taking any medications that would exclude her from participating in the study. Her parents have provided consent for her to participate in the clinical trial.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes for 10 years visited the clinic for a regular check-up. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. She has been experiencing occasional blurry vision and mild eye discomfort for the past six months. She currently takes metformin 1000 mg twice a day and has an HbA1c of 7.2%. Her blood pressure is well controlled at 130/80 mmHg with an ACE inhibitor. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2, and she leads a sedentary lifestyle. She has been receiving routine community care by a family doctor team and has had no previous eye exam. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her manage her diabetes and avoid complications such as diabetic retinopathy.

9 month old baby boy who was born prematurely at 28 weeks and enrolled in Study 20090 to receive treatment for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). He was diagnosed with stage 3 ROP in both eyes and received multiple doses of the investigational drug during the study. The baby has been followed up regularly since the end of the study and is now eligible to participate in this extended study. The baby's parents have provided their informed consent to participate in the study and comply with all the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form and the protocol. The baby does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent his participation in the study or performance of study procedures.

A 22-year-old male college student with a height of 5'9" and a weight of 150 pounds is interested in participating in a clinical trial for cardiovascular disease. He has always been slim and has never had any serious health issues. He has a history of asthma but it is well-controlled with medication. He is not taking any medication currently. He has a healthy lifestyle and exercises regularly. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past. He has growth records available from his childhood.

The patient is a 58-year-old Japanese male who has been suffering from chronic heart failure (CHF) for the past two years. He has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs. He has been taking an ACE inhibitor at a stable dose for the past four weeks. He has also been on a stable dose of a beta-blocker for the past four weeks. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is ≤35%. His NT-proBNP level is ≥600 pg/mL. He has not been hospitalized for HF within the last 12 months. He has no history of angioedema, hypersensitivity or intolerance to ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and no documented untreated ventricular arrhythmia with syncopal episodes within the last three months. His estimated GFR is ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and his serum potassium level is ≤5.2 mmol/L. The patient has no history of acute coronary syndrome, stroke, transient ischemic attack, cardiac or carotid surgery, percutaneous coronary intervention, or carotid angioplasty within the last three months prior to Visit 1. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effect of LCZ696 on delaying time to first occurrence of either cardiovascular (CV) death or HF hospitalization events.

12 year-old boy with a history of congenital heart disease who presents with worsening respiratory distress and hypotension. He was admitted to the ICU and was started on VA ECMO for support. The patient is currently being mechanically ventilated and is receiving nitric oxide and inotropic support. The echocardiogram performed at the time of admission revealed severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 15%. The patient has been on ECMO for 3 days and his clinical status has improved. The patient's heart rate has decreased from 140 beats per minute to 110 beats per minute and his blood pressure has stabilized. The patient is able to tolerate a decrease in the amount of support provided by the ECMO machine. The patient will be enrolled in this study and will undergo multiple echocardiograms at specific time points to assess cardiac function during ECMO support.

The patient is a 35-year-old female respiratory therapist working in the emergency room at an Indiana University Health affiliated facility. She has been in close contact with multiple patients with respiratory symptoms and is concerned about the risk of contracting COVID-19. Despite wearing appropriate personal protective equipment, she is experiencing anxiety and stress related to her exposure risk. She is eligible for the study as a high-risk healthcare worker and has not been previously tested for COVID-19. She will undergo rapid, at-home, point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibody testing to determine if she has been exposed to the virus and to potentially identify her as a candidate for convalescent plasma donation for therapy/prophylaxis.

A 56-year-old woman who had a stroke six months ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial for improving her hand function. She has moderate weakness in her right hand and has difficulty grasping small objects, buttoning her clothes, and writing. She has been working with an occupational therapist for three months, but has not seen much improvement in her hand function. She has no difficulty extending at least 2 fingers in the affected hand 10 degrees at any joint with pain-free passive range of motion at least 50% in all joints below the elbow. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. She has no history of seizures, dementia, or other neurological diseases. She does not have severe pain in her affected upper limb. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves 22 sessions of therapy over 12 weeks, including 8 sessions at home using a non-invasive device called SynPhNe that provides feedback while performing motor tasks with her hand.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patients as it is a physiological study that involves non-invasive ventilation and MRI measurements of the diaphragm. The eligibility criteria are for healthy volunteers without any respiratory or cardiovascular symptoms or contraindications for the placement of a nasogastric tube or MRI. Participants must be over the age of 18 and not employed at the department of intensive care adults or related to staff of the ICU. Therefore, there is no specific patient description for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who had a skin biopsy procedure performed two years ago to remove a suspicious mole on her back. She reports feeling anxious and uncomfortable during the procedure, and is interested in participating in this study to provide feedback to improve the patient experience for future patients. The patient has no known medical conditions and is currently in good health. She is able to provide informed consent and communicate effectively with the investigator.

The patient is a 40 year old Asian woman living in the greater Philadelphia or New York City area. She has not undergone cervical cancer screening in the past three years and has no current diagnosis of cervical cancer. She is interested in participating in a pilot study to test the feasibility of using HPV self-sampling testing to increase cervical cancer screening in under-served Asian women. She is willing to engage with community-based organizations and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease about 4 years ago. He reports difficulty with gait and balance, experiencing freezing episodes and irregular stride lengths. He is currently on a stable medication regimen for the past 3 months. He is able to walk independently but sometimes requires a cane for support. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has not received any previous vibration treatment for gait and balance. The patient is able to communicate effectively and has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score of 25. He has not undergone any surgical procedures that may interfere with the study, and he is not currently in physical therapy for balance or gait. He is willing to attend up to 8 treatment sessions within 5 days at the Virginia Commonwealth University Parkinson's Movement and Disorders Center in Richmond, VA, and provide feedback on the device and therapy sessions. The patient is not pregnant and is not a prisoner.

The patient is a healthy 22-year-old female currently studying at a university. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no balance issues or mobility problems. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not pregnant and has regular menstrual cycles. She has no history of orthopedic problems, traumatic injuries, or surgeries on her lower limbs or lumbosacral region. She does not suffer from tingling or numbness in her limbs. She is not currently participating in any balance training program. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to complete all evaluations.

A 38-year-old male patient was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) six months ago. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy. However, the patient developed recurrent GBM as confirmed by enhanced MRI and magnetic resonance spectroscopy. He did not undergo bevacizumab therapy before enrollment. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score is 1, and he has no known allergies to the administered drugs. The laboratory results showed neutrophil count of 2.5*10^9/L, platelet count of 180*10^9/L, hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, blood urea nitrogen of 0.8 ULN, creatinine of 1.1 ULN, total bilirubin of 0.9 ULN, conjugated bilirubin of 0.2 ULN, ALT of 2 ULN, AST of 2 ULN, and AKP of 1.5 ULN. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 90 days. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 30 yo couple, married for 5 years, is seeking infertility treatment. The female partner has regular menstrual cycles of 28 days with no history of gynecological or medical disorders, and a BMI of 25 kg/m2. The male partner has normal physical health, but his semen analysis showed normal parameters according to the 2010 WHO values. The couple has undergone infertility workup yielding normal results in both partners, and has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility. The couple is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the benefits of Intracytoplasmic Morphologically Selected Sperm Injection (IMSI) in couples with unexplained infertility.

32-year-old male with a history of androgenetic alopecia with vertex pattern IV on the Norwood Hamilton Scale. The patient has tried over-the-counter hair growth products with no significant improvement. He has not used any anti-androgen therapy such as finasteride or minoxidil in the past 6 months. The patient is generally in good health and has no history of folliculitis, scalp psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis or any other inflammatory scalp conditions. He is willing to have a mini dot tattoo placed in the target area of the scalp and maintain the same hair style, color, shampoo and hair products use, and approximate hair length throughout the 16-week study period. The patient is able to give informed consent and comply with the study requirements for the duration of the trial.

23-year-old male college student with a BMI of 22 kg/m² and a stable weight for the past 3 months presents as a potential candidate for a clinical trial investigating the prebiotic effect of xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS) and an inulin-and-XOS mixture (INU-XOS) on endotoxaemia and immune parameters. The patient reports consuming between 13 and 18 g of dietary fiber a day and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is a student on campus at the Institut Polytechnique LaSalle Beauvais and is able to follow the requirements of the study. The patient has no serious pathology, gastrointestinal, vesicular or pancreatic disease, and has not taken any antibiotic or laxative treatment in the last 6 months. The patient has not undergone any surgery of the gastrointestinal tract in the last 12 months and does not have orange juice intolerance. The patient does not have chronic or recurring diarrhea, constipation or abdominal pain and is not taking any drugs known to have an effect on the gastrointestinal, pancreatic, and vesicular function. The patient has not had any recent gastroenteritis or foodborne illness and does not have diabetes. The patient does not consume regularly probiotics- or prebiotics-enriched products and drinks less than 3 glasses of alcohol a day. The patient is not deprived of liberty and is not under judicial protection.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a diagnosis of pancreatic cancer who is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has not had any previous major surgeries and does not have a history of bleeding disorders or other significant medical conditions. The patient has provided consent to participate in the study and is willing to be randomized to either the goal-directed fluid therapy group or the conventional fluid therapy group. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who spends an average of 6 hours per day playing video games. He is an avid gamer and has been playing video games for more than 3 years. He is in good health and has a BMI of 22. He does not take any dietary supplements that may affect cognitive function. He has a history of anxiety but it is well controlled with medication. He agreed to participate in the study and will continue to play his favorite game between study visits. He does not have any allergies to the ingredients in the supplement product. He is willing to maintain his normal sleep pattern and will refrain from consuming caffeine and alcohol for 12 hours prior to each study visit. He will supply his own gaming system and game for the study.

A 30-year-old healthy male software engineer is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He doesn't have any significant medical history and no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. He has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He takes multivitamins and occasionally uses over-the-counter medications for headache relief. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is in a committed relationship and practices safe sex. He is fluent in English and can communicate effectively with the investigator. He is interested in participating in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who underwent clinical coronary CTA 3 months ago due to chest pain. The coronary CTA showed a 50% stenosis in the proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and a 40% stenosis in the mid-right coronary artery (RCA). The patient has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril 10 mg daily. She does not have any allergies to medications or a history of claustrophobia. The patient is willing to participate in this study and give written consent. She does not have any metal fragments in her eyes, brain, or spinal cord and does not have any internal electrical devices. The patient is not pregnant and has no contraindication to use sublingual nitro administration. Her weight is 150 pounds, and she is not taking phosphodiesterase V inhibitors. The patient is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the advancement of non-invasive coronary imaging techniques.

A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with hormone receptor positive breast cancer was receiving anastrozole adjuvant therapy to prevent recurrence of cancer. However, she experienced musculoskeletal disorders that led to her discontinuing the treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that assesses the rheumatologic tolerability of letrozole as an alternative treatment. She has a history of hypertension, which is managed with medication, and no other significant medical conditions. Her blood tests show PNN of 1500/mm3, platelets of 120000/mm3, and Hb of 11 g/dL. She has no hypersensitivity to the components of letrozole. She is fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent for participation.

A 30 year old healthy female came to the clinic to participate in the clinical trial. She has no history of cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, haematological, GI, pulmonary, metabolic-endocrine, neurological or psychiatric disease. She has a normal weight of 60 kg and is not taking any regular medication, vitamins or herbal products. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no known hypersensitivity to the active substance(s) or the excipient of the drug. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of medical research.

A 55-year-old female was acutely admitted to the hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. She has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes multiple medications. She is being treated with atenolol, metformin, simvastatin, lisinopril, and aspirin. She has been hospitalized in the past due to medication errors and is worried about her medications being managed properly during her hospital stay. She is willing to participate in a study to see if a medication review by a clinical pharmacist or pharmacologist can help prevent medication errors during her hospitalization.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a medical history of type 1 diabetes for 3 years. He has been using multiple daily injections (MDI) for his insulin treatment, but has never used continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) or insulin pump therapy. His most recent glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level was 8.2%. He performs at least 4 finger-stick blood glucose measurements per day and is willing to perform required sensor calibrations. He is fluent in English and willing to wear the MiniMed 780G AHCL system continuously throughout the study. He has not used ultra-rapid insulins such as FIASP and has no concurrent illness, laboratory abnormalities, or medications that might affect study participation. He is not currently pregnant and his HbA1c level is below 10%. The patient resides in Poland and is over the age of 26, where he is not entitled to CSII/CGM reimbursement, making him a suitable candidate for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who underwent enterostomy surgery due to inflammatory bowel disease. He has no other serious medical conditions and is generally in good health. He is comfortable using a smartphone and is willing to participate in the survey to help improve the care and support available to patients with enterostomy. He is interested in learning more about self-management and is open to receiving remote guidance from professional colostomy care providers. His main goal is to improve his quality of life and reduce medical expenses associated with his enterostomy care.

This is a 56 year-old female who has not received the Herpes Zoster vaccine or any varicella vaccine previously. She has completed menopause and has no plans to become pregnant. She is in good health and has not been diagnosed with any immunosuppressive or immunodeficient conditions. She has not received any investigational or non-registered products within the past 30 days and is not taking any chronic immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs. She has not received any long-acting immune-modifying drugs within the past six months and does not plan to receive any during the study period. She has not participated in any other clinical study where she has been exposed to an investigational or non-investigational product during the study period. She has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products within the past three months and is not planning to receive any during the study period. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and has provided written informed consent. She is currently not experiencing any acute disease or fever at the time of enrollment. She has no history of any reaction or hypersensitivity likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a chief complaint of a missing permanent canine in his maxillary arch. A clinical evaluation confirmed the presence of an impacted maxillary canine requiring surgical exposure and orthodontic treatment. The patient has not received any orthodontic treatment in the last 12 months and does not have any current systemic diseases. He is not currently on any antibiotic or anti-inflammatory therapy that may compromise the result. The patient has an overall good oral health with no significant dental caries or periodontal disease. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and he is not allergic to any medication. Two CBCT scans will be required for the study, one before the beginning of the traction and the second one after three months. The patient is willing to undergo the treatment and participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma for the past 3 years. She has a history of myopia and hypertension but is otherwise healthy. Her current medications include lisinopril for hypertension and timolol drops for her glaucoma. She reports experiencing difficulties with her vision, including blurry vision and difficulty seeing at night. She also reports that her quality of life has been affected by her glaucoma, including difficulties with daily activities such as reading, driving, and socializing. She is interested in participating in this study as she hopes that it will provide valuable information to help improve the quality of life for people with glaucoma. She speaks fluent English and is able to understand the study requirements. She is available for annual ocular examination and reassessment across a 4-year period.

A 58-year-old male patient presented to the cardiology clinic with a history of ischemic heart disease and angina pectoris. He has been under medical therapy for 2 years with medications including beta-blockers and aspirin, but his symptoms have worsened. He underwent a coronary angiography examination which revealed multi-vessel disease. He was advised to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). His current EF was measured as 35% and he was classified as NYHA class III. He had no history of malignancy, congenital heart disease, stroke, tuberculosis, or hematological diseases. He had no known history of hepatitis B, C, or HIV infection and his liver and renal function tests were within normal limits. The patient had no COPD, coagulopathy, or collagen tissue disease. He had no history of mental or social disabilities. His HbA1c level was measured as 7.5% (58 mmol/mol) and he had no history of type II diabetes mellitus. The patient was not receiving any immunosuppressive therapy.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with a BMI of 38. He is scheduled to undergo general anesthesia for a surgical procedure. He has no history of respiratory disease, smoking or allergies to medications. He is fluent in French and is covered by a health insurance plan. He has given informed and written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old female who underwent primary knee arthroplasty three months ago due to severe osteoarthritis. She has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and has no history of other orthopedic or neurological disorders. She reports difficulty in walking and performing daily activities due to knee pain and stiffness. The patient has been following the standard post-operative rehabilitation program and has been compliant with her physiotherapy sessions. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her functional level and muscle strength. She has no history of revision total knee arthroplasty or any other major surgeries. During the assessment, the patient reports a pain level of 7 on the Numeric Pain Scale and has limited range of motion in the knee joint.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who underwent a kidney transplant surgery two weeks ago. He has a positive EBV serostatus and received his first dose of Nulojix (belatacept) within 14 days of the renal transplant as part of normal clinical care. He has not previously received Nulojix (belatacept) for any other kind of transplant or as part of a clinical trial protocol. He is willing to participate in a prospective study to evaluate the long-term safety of Nulojix (belatacept) in kidney transplant patients.

A 35-year-old woman presents to the gastroenterology clinic with a 6-month history of recurring abdominal pain and constipation. She reports having fewer than three bowel movements per week and has to strain during bowel movements. She also experiences bloating, abdominal distention, and discomfort after meals. She has tried over-the-counter laxatives with little relief. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well controlled with levothyroxine. She has no known drug allergies. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She follows a regular diet and exercises three times a week. On physical examination, the abdomen is soft and non-tender. Bowel sounds are normal. Laboratory tests including a complete blood count, thyroid function test, and metabolic panel are within normal limits. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is interested in participating to address her irritable bowel syndrome with predominant constipation.

The patient is a 1-year-old infant who has a first-degree relative with type 1 diabetes. The family has a history of T1D and has been genetically tested. The infant does not have any islet autoantibodies detected at the time of recruitment. The infant is otherwise healthy and has no other concomitant diseases or treatments that may interfere with the trial or cause immunosuppression. The family is willing to comply with the study requirements and has not participated in any other intervention trials.

The patient is a 40-year-old Chinese man who has been experiencing symptoms of acid reflux for the past 6 months. He reports frequent heartburn, regurgitation, and a sour taste in his mouth. He occasionally experiences throat discomfort and difficulty swallowing, but has no chest pain or vomiting. He has tried taking over-the-counter antacids, but they provide only temporary relief. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He reports a moderate level of stress due to work and family responsibilities. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine combined with omeprazole in treating non-erosive reflux disease. He is able to read and write Chinese, and agrees to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has been experiencing blurred vision and distortion in his left eye, which has been affecting his ability to read and drive. He has never had any eye surgeries or treatments for AMD before. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities.

The patient is a 45-year-old black African woman who has been recently diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma in her left eye. She has no prior treatment for glaucoma in either eye. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. The intraocular pressure in her left eye is currently 22 mmHg. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. She is of reproductive age but is using highly effective contraception and agrees to use it during the study period. She has no contraindications to any of the study interventions. She is able to attend all scheduled study visits.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Cluster 2 personality disorder. She has a history of hospitalization due to personality disorder decompensation. She is currently being treated regularly with psychotherapy and medication, but still experiences occasional episodes of decompensation. The patient is able to read and write fluently and has an active support system. She has not had any suicide attempts within the past month and does not have any urgent need for changes in her medication. The patient does not have a history of drug abuse and does not have an active Axis 1 diagnosis that requires a change in medication. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form.

42 yo F with recently diagnosed infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the right breast on biopsy. Breast cancer was discovered on mammography during a routine screening exam. Patient had no family history of breast cancer, is premenopausal, and has no significant past medical history. Biopsy revealed ER/PR positive, HER2 negative invasive ductal carcinoma. Staging workup including ultrasound of the regional lymph nodes, FDG-PET scan, and MRI of the breast showed no evidence of distant metastases. Patient had no prior radiation therapy or chemotherapy. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 0. Bone marrow function, hepatic function, and renal function are all within normal limits. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Patient has no psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical condition potentially hampering compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule. Signed written informed consent has been obtained.

A 54-year-old woman presents with complaints of hot flashes and night sweats. She has not had a menstrual period for 9 months and has been experiencing these symptoms for the last 4 months. She is a non-smoker with a BMI of 28. She has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of hysterectomy, endometrial hyperplasia or cancer, breast cancer, or any other significant medical conditions. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements, including those containing estrogen or phytoestrogens. She has a history of mild depression that is well-controlled with psychotherapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of black cohosh and red clover for the relief of her symptoms. She is not vegan and gives informed consent to participate in the study.

A 58-year-old female with stage III non-small cell lung cancer who is scheduled to undergo radiation therapy and chemotherapy is being recruited for a clinical trial at M. D. Anderson. She has a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80, has no history of skin diseases, and is physically mobile and independent. She is willing to participate in the study to evaluate whether thermal imaging can be used to check the body's response to cancer therapy. She understands that before beginning thermal imaging, her temperature will be measured with a thermometer and she will be asked to take off all of her clothes in a private room and stand still in front of a thermal imaging camera. She will have thermal imaging sessions several times before the cancer treatment starts and during the therapy course. She will be given detailed instructions on how to prepare for the imaging sessions ahead of time as well as what to expect during the imaging sessions. She feels comfortable with the study's procedures and is excited to contribute to this investigational study.

A 48-year-old male patient arrived at the emergency department with chest pain that radiated to his left arm and jaw. He had a history of hypertension and was a smoker for 20 years. On physical examination, his blood pressure was elevated, and he had a heart rate of 90 beats per minute. The electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. Cardiac biomarkers were elevated, and the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction was made. The patient was a suitable candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and was informed about the study. He provided written informed consent, and the eligibility criteria were met. The patient was randomized to the Stentys self-expanding stent group, and the procedure was performed successfully. The patient was closely monitored for complications and was discharged after 48 hours with an adequate recovery. The patient was advised to continue antiplatelet therapy, and a follow-up evaluation was scheduled to assess the stent's performance.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been experiencing facial redness and sensitivity for several years. She has tried various over-the-counter products for the condition, but nothing seems to provide lasting relief. She has fair skin and has always been prone to sunburns. She has no history of allergies or other medical conditions, and she takes no medications. She works as a teacher and has two young children. She is interested in participating in the study to see if it can improve her symptoms and help her feel more confident in her appearance.

A 62-year-old male smoker visited the oncology clinic for the first time after being diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has never received systemic treatment for his cancer and has no significant medical history. His ECOG PS is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. A CT scan showed a measurable target lesion. His organ function is adequate, and he has no autoimmune disease, HIV, or hepatitis. He has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse. He is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. A pregnancy test was not required as he is a male.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has just given birth to her first child via cesarean section. She is experiencing pain at the site of the surgical incision, with a current pain score of 2 on the Category Numerical Scale (NRS). She is literate, oriented as to time and space, and had spinal anesthesia before surgery. Her incision is of the pfannenstiel type, and there is no history of genitourinary pathology. The patient has no known abnormal sensitivity to clinical examination, demyelinating diseases, spinal cord injury, hemorrhage, infections or fever, anesthetic complications, hypertension, mammary, intolerance, irritation, or strong discomfort at the injection site caused by TENS.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who was diagnosed with nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) 2 years ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy that led to disease remission for 1 year. However, the disease relapsed 6 months ago and the patient is now experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. She has no significant medical history and no family history of cancer. Her current medications include over-the-counter pain relievers. Her physical examination shows an enlarged lymph node in the neck. Her laboratory results are as follows: WBC count of 4,500/mm3, neutrophil count of 2,200/mm3, and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. She has no liver or kidney dysfunction. She has an ECOG status of 1.

A 42-year-old female presented with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath that had started two days prior. She reported no history of recent travel, but had recently been in contact with a family member who had tested positive for COVID-19. She denied any significant medical history, including respiratory illness or smoking. Physical examination revealed mild tachypnea with oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. Chest X-ray was consistent with pneumonia, and a nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2 by RT-PCR. The patient was admitted to the hospital and started on oxygen therapy to maintain oxygen saturation above 92%. Despite treatment with antibiotics and supportive care, the patient's oxygen requirements continued to increase and she developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The patient was deemed eligible for the clinical trial and provided informed consent to receive infusions of cryopreserved allogeneic multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) of the placenta and umbilical cord. The patient received three infusions of MSCs over the course of five days, and was monitored for adverse effects. The patient's oxygen requirements gradually decreased, and she was able to be weaned off of supplemental oxygen after seven days of treatment. The patient was discharged home after a total of 14 days of hospitalization.

A 35-year-old male software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication. He has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. He doesn't smoke and only drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in learning more about the trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has a BMI of 23, which falls within the eligibility criteria. He has no known allergies to medications and has never participated in a clinical trial involving efgartigimod or rHuPH20. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in clinical trials and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. The tumor size is 3.5 cm and there are no palpable lymph nodes. She has no history of breast cancer, but has a family history of breast cancer in her mother. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status is 1. She has undergone a negative axillary ultrasound at Siteman Cancer Center, which showed no evidence of metastatic disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help her determine the best course of action for her treatment, and is willing to undergo either axillary ultrasound or sentinel lymph node biopsy. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no other medical conditions that would make her a poor surgical candidate.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with stage III lung cancer and is scheduled for a surgical procedure. She has no other underlying diseases and is not on any medications. She is able to provide informed consent and has agreed to participate in the study.

32 F, mother to a 4-year-old boy, who is concerned about his weight. The child's most recent well-child exam showed that his BMI is at the 90th percentile. The mother is a stay-at-home mom with access to the internet and is fluent in English. She is motivated to help her child achieve a healthy weight and is willing to attend weekly group sessions with a nurse champion at her primary care office. She is also willing to participate in an interactive web-based intervention and follow the guidelines provided to help her child achieve a healthy weight. The child does not have any developmental disorders or chronic underlying diseases and is not taking any medication that may interfere with achieving a healthy weight.

The patient is a 21-year-old young adult who was diagnosed with HIV infection through behavioral acquisition. The patient has been on ART (anti-retroviral therapy) for 6 months but has been struggling with adherence to medication regimen. The patient has a cell phone and regularly uses text messaging technology. The patient is an English speaker and visits their physician at least every 3 months. The patient has given their assent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to receive daily SMS text message medication reminders for the next 6 months.

A 30-year-old woman with a family history of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) visited the clinic complaining of difficulty in walking and urinary incontinence. She is married and has two children, both of whom are healthy. The patient's father was diagnosed with X-ALD, and she is concerned that she might have inherited the disease. The patient is generally healthy, does not smoke or drink alcohol, and does not take any medications regularly. She reports experiencing mild fatigue and occasional headaches. She works as a teacher and finds it difficult to stand for long periods. She is fluent in English and French and is interested in participating in research to better understand X-ALD and its impact on quality of life.

54-year-old male patient presented with a missing tooth in the anterior maxilla. The patient has a history of trauma to the area resulting in a loss of the tooth and the surrounding bone. The patient is in good health, with no significant medical history. The patient has good oral hygiene and is highly motivated to have the tooth replaced with a fixed prosthesis. Upon examination, the patient was found to have a deficient alveolar bone in the anterior maxilla. The patient is willing to undergo a surgical procedure and follow-up, and has provided informed consent. There is no evidence of any diseases that would compromise bone or soft tissue healing. The patient has not undergone any previous grafting procedures at the designated edentulous ridge.

Patient B is a 15-year-old female high school student who plays soccer. She was injured during a match when she collided with another player and hit her head on the ground. She immediately complained of a headache and was taken out of the game. She visited the emergency department 2 days after the incident due to persistent headache. A concussion was diagnosed, and she was advised to rest and avoid any physical activity. She is an English-speaking student with no history of previous concussions, cervical injuries or neurological issues. She has a normal Glasgow Coma Scale score. She is experiencing headaches with an intensity of 6/10 on a pain scale, and her headaches are occurring frequently (more than 4 times per day) since the incident. She is willing to participate in the study to help find a better solution to manage concussion headaches.

The patient is a 26-year-old male military healthcare beneficiary who sustained a traumatic injury to his right leg during an explosive blast. The wound is a full-thickness wound that has been treated with INTEGRA™ MBWM as part of his standard of care. The wound area is approximately 250 cm2 and is fully engrafted with a viable granulation layer. The patient has no pre-existing conditions that would interfere with wound healing, and he is compliant with study procedures. He has provided voluntary written informed consent and HIPAA authorization to participate in the study. The patient will be assessed for wound healing time, donor site morbidity, and histology during an acute 6-week phase, with follow-up visits at Weeks 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 post-treatment. The patient will continue in the study for long-term follow-up with clinic visits at Week 12 and 24 post-treatment. Aesthetic and functional outcomes of the treated area will be assessed and documented, and subject satisfaction will also be assessed and documented at these two time points.

This clinical trial is not suitable for generating a patient description as it is targeting a specific population - injecting drug users in the prison and probation service who agree to anonymously participate. The trial does not include individual patient recruitment or selection.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent a kidney transplant 10 months ago due to end-stage renal disease. Following the transplant, he developed post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM) and has been struggling to control his blood sugar levels. He was started on insulin therapy, but his glycemic control has been unstable due to fluctuations in his immunosuppressive medication doses. His recent HbA1c was 8.5%, and he has experienced episodes of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia. He has no significant medical history other than end-stage renal disease, and his current medications are tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. Serum creatinine is within normal limits. The patient is willing to learn continuous glucose monitoring and interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his diabetes management.

A 75-year-old retired man with mild hypertension and diabetes comes to the clinic for regular check-ups. He lives alone in a small apartment and has been experiencing occasional forgetfulness. He is fluent in Cantonese and has given consent for sharing his health records in the Electronic Health Record Sharing System (eHRSS) with the Senior Citizen Home Safety Association (SCHSA). He has no hearing difficulties and understands spoken Cantonese. He has not participated in any clinical trials before. He is interested in the Electronic Health Record Sharing System (eHRSS) Encounter Notification Service Pilot Project and is willing to participate if eligible.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was involved in a car accident and sustained a deep laceration on his leg that requires suturing. He is anxious about the procedure and has a history of needle phobia. He has no known allergies to medications and is not currently taking any medications. He has normal vital signs and is otherwise healthy. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

55-year-old female who suffered a left hemiplegic stroke 8 months ago. She is currently able to walk independently with a cane but reports difficulty with balance and a fear of falling. She has no history of other neurological diseases or injuries. The patient is able to follow instructions and has adequate cognition to participate in the study. She is motivated to improve her gait and functional abilities.

A 55-year-old woman who is postmenopausal presents with a history of breast cancer. She is currently not exhibiting any evidence of disease.
