However, she is experiencing vaginal dryness and itching for the past 3 months, which is causing discomfort and a decreased quality of life. She is reluctant to use vaginal estrogen due to concerns about an increased risk of breast cancer. She has a life expectancy of more than 6 months, and she is able to complete questionnaires by herself or with assistance. She is not currently receiving chemotherapy, and she has not used any vaginal preparations in the past week. She has no history of asthma, COPD, CAD, narrow-angle glaucoma, or cholelithiasis, and she is not currently using any anticholinergics or pharmacologic soy preparations. She has occasional PVCs and PACs that do not require treatment. She has not undergone pelvic radiation therapy or radical pelvic surgery, and she does not have a diagnosis of vulvar or vaginal dysplasia, essential vulvodynia, vulvar vestibulitis, vaginal prolapse, Bartholin cyst/abscess, lichen sclerosis, lichen planus of the vulvovaginal region, or desquamative vaginitis.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who recently underwent a colonoscopy for screening purposes. The colonoscopy revealed a 15mm polyp in the sigmoid colon. He has no family history of colon cancer or other gastrointestinal diseases. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study. He has not taken any antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy in the past week, and he does not have a known coagulopathy. He has not been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease and is not currently experiencing any hemodynamic instability. He is not pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 2 years ago. She has been experiencing increasing fever and fatigue for the past 2 weeks. She also reports experiencing a sore throat, headache, and joint pain. On examination, she has splenomegaly and laboratory tests reveal cytopenia involving ≥2 cell lines (Hemoglobin <9 g/dL; platelets <100,000/μL; absolute neutrophil count <1000/μL), hypertriglyceridemia, and serum ferritin ≥3000 ug/L. She is diagnosed with secondary hemophagocytic syndrome and is a candidate for the pilot study of Ruxolitinib. She provides written informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria. She has no history of malignancy, does not have active hepatitis B or hepatitis C or known HIV infection, and her estimated creatinine clearance is >15mL/min.

A 55-year-old man diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) two years ago after presenting with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He underwent standard therapy with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide but relapsed six months after completing treatment. His current laboratory tests show a white blood cell count of 50,000 cells/uL and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. Platelet count is 90,000 cells/uL. The patient has no history of significant infections, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He has no concurrent anticancer therapies and has not received systemic therapy for CLL in the past four weeks. The patient has good renal function with a creatinine level within the normal range. He is willing to use a dual method of contraception to participate in the study.

This is a 28-year-old gentleman with Becker Muscular Dystrophy (BMD) diagnosed at the age of 25. He has noted progressive weakness in his lower extremities and difficulty with ambulation. He has a family history of muscular dystrophy, with his older brother also diagnosed with BMD. He currently takes no medication for his condition. He has no history of hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, or liver disease. His ECG shows no evidence of prolonged QT interval. He is interested in participating in this study to help advance understanding and treatment of BMD.

A 27-year-old female presents with complaints of numbness and tingling in her right arm and leg that started 3 days ago. She reports having experienced similar symptoms in the past, which resolved spontaneously. She denies any recent illness or injury. There is no family history of multiple sclerosis or other neurological disorders. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick in the right upper and lower extremities. Muscle strength, reflexes, and coordination are normal. Laboratory tests including complete blood count, electrolytes, liver and renal function tests, and thyroid function tests are within normal limits. Brain MRI shows multiple T2 hyperintense lesions with gadolinium enhancement in the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial regions, consistent with demyelinating disease. The patient is diagnosed with a demyelinating event and is offered the opportunity to participate in a pilot study assessing the levels of glutamate and aspartate and their impact on clinical and radiological outcomes. She meets the inclusion criteria and signs informed consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a 10yo M diagnosed with velocardiofacial syndrome (VCFS) with a confirmed chromosomal deletion via FISH examination. The patient has a history of developmental delays, speech and language difficulties, and mild facial dysmorphisms. The patient has also exhibited some behavioral issues, including hyperactivity and difficulty with attention and focus. The purpose of this study is to investigate the psychiatric and cognitive phenotypes associated with VCFS, as well as examine the connection to developmental and molecular factors. The study will involve various assessments, including neuropsychological testing, behavioral assessments, and genetic testing. The goal is to better understand the underlying mechanisms of VCFS and develop targeted treatments to improve the quality of life for individuals with this condition. The patient is eligible for participation in this study.

67-year-old male scheduled for elective surgery at UPMC in 3 months for repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease status post-stent placement. He takes aspirin, metoprolol succinate, and atorvastatin. He has no history of diabetes and currently does not take metformin. He is willing to participate in the REMAP trial and meet the inclusion criteria for the SPRY domain. He has a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 3 due to his history of coronary artery disease and hypertension. He is able to take an oral medication in non-crushable pill form. He is post-menopausal and has no allergies to metformin. He does not have any contraindications to metformin therapy and has never had metabolic acidosis or excessive alcohol intake. He has normal renal function with a GFR of 75.

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with low-grade mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon. He underwent a right hemicolectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX. However, he developed peritoneal carcinomatosis 10 months after the initial diagnosis. Imaging studies revealed multiple peritoneal nodules and ascites. He was referred to a tertiary cancer center for further evaluation and management. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no allergies to any medications. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. On physical examination, he has diffuse abdominal tenderness, and the liver edge is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin. Laboratory studies reveal mild anemia and elevated tumor markers, including CEA and CA19-9. A diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the presence of peritoneal carcinomatosis, and multiple nodules were debulked. The pathology report confirmed low-grade mucinous adenocarcinoma. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive further treatment.

10-year-old male with a history of osteosarcoma diagnosed at the age of 8 is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. The patient has received multiple rounds of chemotherapy and surgical intervention, but the disease has progressed. The patient has been experiencing pain and has developed a new mass in the affected area. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions and is taking acetaminophen for pain control. The patient has been compliant with all previous treatments and is eager to try any new options available. The patient lives with his mother and father and has two younger siblings. The patient is in school and continues to attend classes when possible. The patient's parents are willing to participate in the study and have given their consent for their child to participate. The patient is currently not on any other medications and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 4 weeks. The patient is up to date on all vaccinations and has no known history of bleeding disorders or hypercoagulable conditions. The patient's labs are within normal limits, and the patient has a Karnofsky performance status greater than 50. The patient's EKG, echocardiogram, and pulse oximetry are all within age-appropriate levels. The patient's estimated life expectancy is at least 3 months.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 34. She has been struggling with her weight for several years and has tried several weight loss programs without success. She has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. Her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, and her fasting glucose is 6.2 mmol/l. She is a non-smoker and has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or neurological disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of chronic intermittent cold exposure on weight loss. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understand the risks and benefits of the study. She has no claustrophobia and has no ferromagnetic objects in her body that would make MRI imaging contraindicated.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe back pain for several weeks. She reports a history of osteoporosis and has been taking calcium supplements for several years. She has no history of trauma or recent illnesses but has been experiencing a low-grade fever for the past few days. Upon examination, the patient is found to have tenderness over the thoracolumbar region. Imaging studies reveal thoracolumbar spondylodiscitis affecting multiple vertebrae. The patient is scheduled for surgical treatment by posterior approach to address the infection. She has no history of previous spine surgeries and is otherwise in good health.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman experiencing negative mood symptoms such as depression, anxiety, and stress. She is interested in participating in a 10-week training program to improve her interoceptive awareness through either yoga or cardiovascular exercise. She has no history of structural brain disease, mass lesion, stroke, epilepsy, addictive disorder, or significant substance abuse. Additionally, she has no neurological disorders or reversible causes of dementia. She is not currently attending regular yoga or aerobic exercise practice, nor has she participated in more than 6 formal meditation, aerobic, or yoga classes in the past 12 months. She does not report any cognitive impairment or other disorders that may preclude safe participation in the program, including acute major depression, bipolar disorder, or severe personality disorder. She is excited about the opportunity to improve her mental health and well-being through this clinical trial.

John is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and numbness in his left foot for the past few months. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He is a retired carpenter and has been leading a sedentary lifestyle for the past few years. He smokes a pack of cigarettes every day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a BMI of 30 and has not undergone any previous vascular intervention. Upon examination, he was found to have Rutherford Category 4 critical limb ischemia in his left leg, with a lesion in the infrapopliteal crural vessels. His angiography revealed a single atherosclerotic lesion in the target vessel that is 70% or more occluded, with a total length of up to 30 cm. He meets the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the Lower-Limb Adventitial Infusion of DexaMethasone Via Bullfrog to Reduce Occurrence of Restenosis After Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty Revascularization clinical trial and has consented to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of carpal tunnel syndrome, which has been causing her significant discomfort and pain in her right hand. She has no known allergies and her past medical history is unremarkable. Her physical examination reveals mild tenderness and limited range of motion in her right wrist. The patient is scheduled for elective arm surgery, specifically a carpal tunnel release procedure. She has no history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, peripheral artery disease, or any neurological disorders. The patient is willing to undergo brachial plexus blockage and is in good overall health with an ASA score of II. She weighs 65 kg and her BMI is 25.3. She is not pregnant and has no history of trauma or previous surgery in the area scheduled for the block.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is currently undergoing angiographic assessment and percutaneous coronary intervention. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, for which he takes medication. He reports experiencing chest pain during physical activity and at rest on occasion. The patient is generally in good health, with no significant medical history and is not allergic to latex. He is willing to participate in the PERCCAD Study to assess the potential benefits of the gekoTM device on his coronary blood flow. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is motivated to improve his symptoms and overall health.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 2 years. He has been taking oral hypoglycemic medications to control his blood sugar level. He has been experiencing symptoms of diabetic polyneuropathy such as burning, numbness, and pain in his feet for the past 6 months. The pain has become increasingly severe and has started to affect his daily activities. His HbA1c level is 8.5%, and his BMI is 28 kg/m2. He has been referred to this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of Cytoflavin® in treating diabetic polyneuropathy. He has provided informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria, including having a TSS score of more than 5 points and a NISLL score of 2 or more. He has agreed to maintain his current diabetes therapy, diet, and exercise regimen throughout the study. He does not have any significant medical history, allergies or contraindications to the drug Cytoflavin® or its components.

55 year old male with a history of rotator cuff tear and chronic shoulder pain. He has tried conservative management including physical therapy and corticosteroid injections, but has not had significant relief. He is scheduled for an ambulatory arthroscopic rotator cuff repair under regional anesthesia and general anesthesia. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has social health insurance and is able to return home on the evening of his surgery. He understands the objective and constrains of the study and has consented to participate.

45 year-old male with a history of opioid dependence for the past 10 years, currently using heroin intravenously. Has previously attempted methadone and buprenorphine treatments, but has not found them to be effective. Has a history of chronic pain due to a back injury, which has contributed to his opioid dependence. Has experienced legal and financial problems as a result of his drug use. Is interested in participating in a study that may provide a new treatment option for his addiction.

A 2-day-old male neonate was born prematurely at 32 weeks gestation. The baby weighed 1.5 kg at birth and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress syndrome. The baby was intubated with a double-lumen ETT (Uncuffed Tracheal Tube, Mallinckrodt Inc., Chih, Mexico) and started on conventional ventilation. The parents provided consent for the baby to participate in the study. The baby is expected to require ventilation for at least a week and is expected to have at least 3 pairs of blood samples and ETCO2 measurements during the ventilation period. The baby has no other significant medical history or conditions that would interfere with the study.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of fluconazole on the pharmacokinetics of fedratinib. She is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription medications, but she occasionally takes over-the-counter pain relievers for headaches. She has a BMI of 25 and her vital signs are within normal range. She has a negative pregnancy test and agrees to use reliable contraception methods during the study. She has no history of major medical disorders or drug abuse.

This clinical trial is looking for patients who have been diagnosed with Bacillus Species sepsis or meningitis and have experienced a significant change in clinical status. The study is specifically interested in cases where Bacillus Species is the only organism isolated, and excludes cases where Bacillus Species is isolated with other organisms or without clinical change. The trial aims to identify risk factors for severe Bacillus Species infections in immunocompromised patients, particularly preterm infants. If you or your loved one meets these criteria, you may be eligible to participate in this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old Norwegian woman who has been experiencing mild to moderate stress related to the COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting social isolation measures. She has been feeling overwhelmed and anxious about the uncertainty of the situation and the impact it has on her daily life. She is able to read and write Norwegian and is interested in participating in a digital self-guided psychological intervention to help her cope with her stress. She has not received any treatment for mental health disorders in the past and does not have a history of severe mental health disorders.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with locally advanced gall bladder cancer that is not amenable to curative resection. The patient has a history of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past 2 months, and imaging studies revealed a large mass in the gall bladder with liver infiltration and lymph node involvement. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the gall bladder. The patient has no evidence of distant metastasis and has normal hematological and renal and hepatic functions. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effects of neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone versus neoadjuvant chemoradiation and chemotherapy for locally advanced gall bladder cancers in terms of downstaging and overall survival. The patient will undergo Positron emission tomography and contrast-enhanced computerized tomography (PETCECT) scan and staging laparoscopy to rule out metastatic disease before being randomized into one of the study arms.

The patient is a 13-year-old male who has never received a meningococcal vaccine. He has no history of anaphylactic reactions to vaccines or vaccine-related components. He does not have bleeding diathesis or any condition associated with prolonged bleeding time that would contraindicate intramuscular injection. He is not known to have any defects in his immune system that would prevent an immune response to the vaccine or any history of microbiologically proven disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. He has no significant neurological disorder or history of seizures. He is not currently receiving any allergen immunotherapy or blood products, and he is not on systemic antibiotics. He is in good health, and his medical history and physical examination do not show any abnormalities. He is available for the entire study period and can be reached by telephone.

A 40-year-old woman who underwent Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) surgery ten years ago presents with weight regain. She has a history of obesity for more than two years and has failed standard obesity therapy such as diet, exercise, behavior modification, and pharmacologic agents either alone or in combination. She has a BMI of 35 and has experienced no significant weight change (<5% of total body weight) for the last six months. The patient has been deemed a reasonable candidate for general anesthesia and agrees not to have any additional weight loss surgery or reconstructive surgery that may affect body weight during the trial. She has no significant esophageal disease or hiatal hernia, and her Mallampati score is less than 3. She has no history of inflammatory disease of the GI tract or chronic/acute upper GI bleeding conditions. The patient is willing and able to participate in all aspects of the study and agrees to comply with all study requirements for the duration of the study. She is able to fully understand and willing to sign the informed consent. However, the patient has a history of cancer and a life expectancy of less than two years, which disqualifies her for the study.

50 year-old male, who underwent kidney transplant 6 months ago due to end-stage renal disease secondary to hypertension. The donor was a 35 year-old male without any known medical conditions. The patient has been receiving tacrolimus based immunosuppressive therapy since the time of transplantation. His serum creatinine levels have been stable at around 1.5 mg/dL for the past 3 months. He has no history of any episodes of acute rejection. He is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension and atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia. He has no known drug allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

This is a 25 year-old healthy individual with no history of substance abuse or any psychiatric or neurological disorders. The participant has no past or present hematologic abnormality or vascular disease. They have no skin disease and are willing to give informed consent for the study. The participant is interested in contributing to research in the field of neuroscience and is available to participate in up to five testing sessions, each lasting 1 to 2 hours. They are willing to perform tasks of thinking and reasoning during the EEG and NIRS tests, given either separately or together, as well as complete optional tests of thinking and reasoning on paper or on a computer.

55-year-old female with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2 was referred to nephrology for evaluation of proteinuria. On examination, the patient was found to have 2+ proteinuria on dipstick testing. Laboratory investigations revealed serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL and urine protein/creatinine ratio of 2.3 g/g. A renal biopsy was performed which confirmed the diagnosis of monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS) with proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) subtype. The patient has no history of multiple myeloma or lymphoma. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or rituximab therapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. The patient's organ function is normal with leukocytes of 5,000/microliters, absolute neutrophil count of 2,500/mcL, platelets of 150,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal limits, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (SGOT)/alanine transaminase (ALT)(SGPT) ≤2.5 × institutional upper limit of normal, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of isatuximab on kidney function in patients with MGRS.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. He reports difficulty with night driving and reading small print. His vision has been gradually worsening over the past year. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has no other significant medical history and has never undergone eye surgery. He reports no history of eye trauma or injury. His preoperative regular corneal astigmatism is between 1.00 D and 6.00 D. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and stability of AT TORBI 709M 4-haptic toric IOL in cataract surgery.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has not received any prior chemotherapy treatments. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain for the past few weeks. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no other serious medical illnesses or conditions. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of chronic shoulder pain, which has been worsening over the past 6 months. The pain is localized to the posterior aspect of the shoulder and is particularly aggravated during overhead activities. He has tried several non-surgical interventions, including physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but has not achieved significant relief. MRI reveals a partial rotator cuff tear, and the patient is scheduled for arthroscopic surgery. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and he is not taking any medications. He is married, works as an accountant, and enjoys playing golf in his free time. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his pain management during the surgery.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus for 7 years. He has been using continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) for the past 8 months and has maintained acceptable to good metabolic control with an HbA1c level between 5-8%. He exercises moderately for at least 30 minutes, 3 times per week and has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. His daily insulin requirement is within the range of 0.3-1.0 U/kg body weight, indicating normal insulin sensitivity. He has never suffered from microalbuminuria, proliferating retinopathy, or any other chronic complications of diabetes. He has no history of smoking or drug abuse, and his liver and renal function are normal. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 35 year old female diagnosed with schizophrenia, experiencing auditory hallucinations and delusions for the past 2 years. She has been on antipsychotic medication, but experienced multiple relapses due to poor medication adherence. The patient lives with her family and has a telephone line. She is able to give written informed consent and is interested in participating in the study. She has not been hospitalized due to drug intoxication or withdrawal and has not been admitted due to severe self harm. The patient is willing to attend regular outpatient clinic appointments and is not under any forced ambulatory treatment order.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She underwent a complete macroscopic excision of the tumor by breast-conserving surgery. She did not undergo immediate breast reconstruction. She has no requirement for axillary radiotherapy after a Level 1 axillary dissection was performed and only a few lymph nodes were removed. She has not yet received any neoadjuvant or primary medical therapy for breast cancer. She is post-menopausal, has no significant medical history, and has a good performance status. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the eligibility criteria.

Patient is a 52-year-old male with a 20-pack year smoking history and no history of lung disease. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past year, which has been getting progressively worse. He has tried quitting smoking multiple times but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in participating in a study that is examining the changes in immune cells in people who smoke to better understand how smoking causes lung disease. He meets the eligibility criteria for the "current smokers with no history of lung disease" group and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy individual who has no history of respiratory diseases or chronic cough. They are physically active and exercise regularly. They have no family history of asthma or other respiratory diseases. They are a non-smoker and do not have any allergies or sinus problems. They have no history of heart or lung problems and have never been hospitalized for respiratory problems. They have no current medication use or substance abuse. They are willing to participate in the study and are able to provide informed consent.

6-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of progressive diffuse intrinsic pontine gliomas (DIPG) following a worsening of her symptoms of headaches, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies have revealed a tumor in the pons region of her brainstem. The patient's parents have been presented with the treatment options and have agreed to participate in this pilot study of intra-arterial (IA) chemotherapy for the treatment of DIPG. The patient has no known history of hypercoagulable disorders or vasculopathies, and her blood test results are within the acceptable range for this clinical trial. She has not had any previous severe allergic reactions to IV iodinated contrast.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD). She presents with a history of self-harm, suicidal ideation, mood instability, and difficulty regulating her emotions. She has a family history of mental illness, with her mother having been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. She is currently attending high school but has had difficulty maintaining focus and motivation due to her symptoms. She has previously been treated with medication and talk therapy, but has not seen significant improvement. She is willing to participate in a psychotherapy program and is able to understand and comply with instructions. She has no history of psychotic disorders, pervasive developmental disorders, severe somatic or neurological disorders, severe and persistent substance addiction, or elevated risk for complications related to blood sampling.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was involved in a car accident resulting in a fracture of the metacarpal shaft of her right hand's fourth finger. The fracture is isolated and has not affected any other part of her hand or fingers. The patient was treated with closed reduction and a cast was placed for immobilization. The patient has no other medical history and is generally healthy. She does not have any pregnancy or current infection. The patient has no history of previous fractures in her hand or fingers. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will be able to follow up with x-ray imaging for the duration of the study.

A 56-year-old female patient was referred to the clinic with a diagnosis of multinodular goiter. She has been experiencing difficulty breathing and swallowing for the past few months. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well controlled with medications. She has never had any thyroid or parathyroid surgery before. She has no history of vocal cord paralysis. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is not on any medications that may interfere with the study outcomes. She understands the purpose of the study and is willing to participate.

A 24-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5 presents as a healthy volunteer for a clinical trial. She has no significant medical history and has not been taking any prescription or OTC medications for the past 14 days. She is a non-smoker and has not consumed any nicotine-containing products for at least 6 months prior to her participation. She is not pregnant or lactating, and her menstrual cycles are regular. She is not taking any herbal products, vitamin K or food supplements, particularly omega-3-fatty acids, within the 7 days prior to the first dosing. She does not have any known sensitivity or allergy to soybeans, fish, and/or shellfish, as well as compounds related to simvastatin, Epanova®, and aspirin. She has not participated in another clinical trial within 30 days prior to check-in. She voluntarily consents to participate in the study and to follow the restrictions and procedures outlined for the study.

A 48-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) with CD117(+), DOG-1(+), and a mutation in KIT gene. The patient has undergone treatment with imatinib and sunitinib but unfortunately, both treatments have failed due to disease progression and intolerability. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and all toxic effects of prior treatments have resolved to grade 1 by NCI-CTCAE version 3.0. The patient has at least one measurable lesion as defined by RECIST version 1.0. He has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, renal, and other organ functions with neutrophil count of 2,000/mm3, platelet count of 100,000/mm3, and hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL. Total bilirubin is 1.2 x upper limit of normal (ULN), AST/ALT is 2.2 x ULN, and creatinine level is within normal limits. The patient has no history of cardiac disease or impaired cardiac function, uncontrolled infection, pre-existing clinically significant disorder of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, adrenal or thyroid glands, acute or chronic pancreatitis, or malabsorption syndrome. The patient has no history of major surgery within the last 28 days, brain metastases, or alcohol or substance abuse disorder. The patient has not taken any medications that have a potential risk of prolonging the QT interval or inducing Torsades de Points. The patient has never been diagnosed with HIV infection and has no other inhibitor of FGFR except sunitinib. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided a signed written informed consent.

This clinical trial does not involve patients. It is an observational, ambidirectional multicenter cohort study that will compare death rates in nursing homes according to the implementation of recommendations and guidance by the nursing home staff and the severity of the COVID outbreak in the geographic area. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions needed for this study.

A 42-year-old male patient presented to the outpatient clinic complaining of fatigue, decreased appetite, abdominal discomfort, and yellow discoloration of eyes and skin for the past 3 months. He also reported occasional nausea and vomiting. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medication regularly. He has no known allergies. He denies any history of alcohol abuse or illicit drug use. He has a history of unprotected sexual encounters with multiple partners. On physical examination, he appears jaundiced with icteric sclera. His abdominal exam revealed mild hepatomegaly and mild tenderness over the right upper quadrant. No splenomegaly or ascites were detected. Laboratory tests showed elevated liver enzymes with ALT of 170 IU/L and AST of 150 IU/L. His total bilirubin was 4.2 mg/dL, direct bilirubin was 3.3 mg/dL, and alkaline phosphatase was 210 IU/L. HCV antibodies were positive, and HCV RNA was detected by PCR. Abdominal ultrasound showed increased echogenicity of the liver parenchyma and mild splenomegaly. The patient underwent a liver biopsy, and the histopathological examination showed chronic hepatitis with significant fibrosis according to the Ishak scoring system. The patient's BMI is 31, and his hematological and biochemical indices are within normal limits. He is negative for HBsAg and ANA. He does not have any significant cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. His fundus examination is normal. He does not have any history of psychiatric or seizure disorders. He is not currently taking any medication or supplements. He is willing to use proper contraception measures throughout the course of the study and six months later.

Pt is a 2-year-old male attending a nursery program with a history of occasional respiratory and gastrointestinal infections. The patient is otherwise healthy with no chronic or congenital diseases or disabilities. There is no history of active tuberculosis, congenital cardiac defects, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency, chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, celiac diseases, cystic fibrosis, metabolic diseases, malignancy, chronic pulmonary diseases, or malformation of the GI tract. The patient has not taken any antibiotics, pre/pro/symbiotic or immunostimulants within 2 weeks before the study start. The patient is not experiencing diarrhea on admission and is not severely underweight.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with HIV. He has not received any antiretroviral treatment before and is otherwise healthy. His past medical history is non-significant. He takes no medications and has no allergies. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. His physical examination and laboratory results are normal, and he has no signs of acute illness. He has no significant history of cardiac, renal, neurologic, psychiatric, oncologic, endocrinologic, metabolic or hepatic disease. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to practice an effective method of birth control during the study. The patient has voluntarily signed and dated an informed consent form, approved by an Institutional Review Board (IRB)/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC), after the nature of the study has been explained and the subject has had the opportunity to ask questions. The informed consent must be signed before any study-specific procedures are performed. The patient is willing to take all doses of the study drug from the bottles provided by the sponsor and agrees not to take any medication during the study, including over-the-counter medicine, alcohol or recreational drugs without the knowledge and permission of the principal investigator. The patient does not require and agrees not to take any of the following medications for the duration of the study: midazolam, triazolam, terfenadine, astemizole, cisapride, pimozide, propafenone, flecainide, certain ergot derivatives (ergotamine, dihydroergotamine, ergonovine, and methylergonovine), rifampin, lovastatin, simvastatin, and St. John's wort. The patient's plasma HIV RNA level is greater than 400 copies/mL at screening.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with atopy but has not experienced any allergy-related symptoms. He has a family history of asthma and allergic rhinitis. His total IgE levels are 350IU/ml. He is not taking any allergic drugs and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 6 months nor has any plans to participate in any trials during this trial. He is in good health with normal laboratory test results. There is no history of serious clinical conditions or mental disorders. He is not pregnant nor is he a woman of childbearing potential. There is no history of kiwi allergy. He is willing to provide written informed consent before the commencement of the study.

A healthy 22-year-old male non-smoker with no history of cardiovascular diseases or intake of prescription medicine is being sought for a clinical trial studying the effects of Ischemia-reperfusion injury. The study will require the subject to undergo a model ischemia-reperfusion injury on their lower limb and will involve monitoring the expression of markers in both the muscle and blood. The purpose of the study is to measure the damage caused by free radicals and the levels of antioxidants. The results of this trial will help in testing antioxidative intervention.

This clinical trial is not applicable for a patient description as it is specifically looking for healthy NCI-Frederick employees and other NIH staff located at Ft. Detrick to participate as donors for in vitro research. It has exclusion criteria for individuals with chronic illnesses, current acute illness, clotting disorders, anemia, and positive blood tests for exposure to certain viruses. The trial has no direct benefit for patients or participants, and the purpose is to establish a centralized repository for the collection and distribution of samples for in vitro research conducted by NIH investigators.

This is an 80 year old male with a past medical history of osteoarthritis, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. The patient is currently residing in a nursing home due to mobility limitations and requires assistance with activities of daily living. The patient has been experiencing chronic pain for over a year, specifically in the lower back and knees, and has been managed with short-acting opioid medications. The patient has not been taking any medication for pain management other than opioids. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and tolerability of a buprenorphine transdermal system versus placebo on health outcomes. The patient is able to understand and provide informed consent, and has not been taking more than 90mg of oral morphine sulfate per day or more than 50mcg/hr of transdermal fentanyl or its equivalent. The patient does not have cancer-related pain and is not restricted to bed rest.

A 52-year old female was diagnosed with breast cancer six months ago. She underwent surgery and is currently receiving chemotherapy. She reports experiencing pain in her chest and arm, which is being managed by opioid therapy. She also reports feeling anxious, depressed, and overwhelmed by her diagnosis and treatment. She is currently on antidepressant medication. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher but has taken a leave of absence due to her illness. She is interested in participating in a psychological intervention to help manage her pain and improve her psychological well-being. She speaks English fluently and has no history of bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders, or borderline personality disorder. Her estimated survival time is greater than six months, according to her palliative care clinic staff.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with unstable asthma for the past 5 years. She experiences frequent episodes of shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing, especially during the winter months. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and a short-acting bronchodilator as needed. She has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. She works as a teacher and feels that her asthma symptoms often interfere with her ability to perform her job duties. She has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. She lives at home with her husband and has a telephone connection.

A 60-year-old male presented at the hospital with a history of intermittent headaches and blurred vision. He also reported experiencing difficulty with his balance and coordination over the past few weeks. Upon further examination, the patient was diagnosed with primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL). He has no significant past medical history and has never received any anti-tumor treatment before. The patient has no known allergies and has normal organ function. He has a World Health Organization-Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status of 1. A pregnancy test was not necessary as the patient is male. He has agreed to sign the written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

40-year-old female with a history of Lyme Disease diagnosed 6 months ago. Patient was treated with antibiotics for 30 days but continues to experience symptoms including fatigue, joint pain, and difficulty concentrating. Patient reports that these symptoms have negatively impacted daily activities and quality of life. Patient is able to swallow a mixed powder drink and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially alleviate these symptoms. The patient has had a positive Western Blot test and meets the inclusion criteria for this study.

A 52-year-old woman came to the clinic with chronic, intractable pain in her lower back and legs. She has been suffering from this pain for the last 4 years after a failed back surgery. She has tried various pain management treatments, including physical therapy and medication, but nothing has provided long-lasting relief. Her pain interferes with her daily activities and quality of life. Her doctor has recommended Burst-SCS as a potential treatment option. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to speak, read, and understand English. She does not have artificial nails or any impairment that would prevent her from cooperating with clinical testing.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with primary uveal melanoma. She underwent plaque brachytherapy as the primary treatment. The patient is currently experiencing visual symptoms such as decreased vision, blurred vision, and difficulty in reading. The baseline visual acuity is 20/80. The patient's posterior tumor margin is >1.50 mm from the center of the macula and the closest disc margin. The calculated total dose to the center of the macula is > 40 Gy. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosed 3 years ago. She experiences frequent episodes of numbness and tingling in her lower extremities, as well as difficulty with coordination and balance. MRI shows multiple white matter lesions in the brain and spinal cord. She has no history of major systemic diseases, psychiatric disorders, drug or alcohol abuse, or major depression. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no contraindications to MRI and does not suffer from claustrophobia. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at studying the pathophysiological features of MS, including myelination state, amyloid deposition, tau deposition, serum levels of neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP).

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with hypertension during a routine medical check-up. He reports that his blood pressure readings at home are usually normal, but when he visits the doctor's office, his blood pressure readings are consistently high. He denies any symptoms related to hypertension such as headache, shortness of breath, or chest pain. The patient has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medication. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and has a family history of hypertension. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring as well as heart rate variability testing.

A 35-year-old male presents with a positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2, with symptoms of sore throat and mild cough for 2 days. He has no history of chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He has not used any mouthwash or oral antiseptic in the past 24 hours. The patient is able to understand and comply with the study requirements and has given informed consent to participate. He is able to perform mouthwashes and gargles without difficulty. The patient will be randomized to either receive a mouthwash containing 0.07% CPC or a placebo. The patient's saliva samples will be collected before and after the use of the mouthwash to determine the viral load of SARS-CoV-2 in the oral cavity. The patient will be instructed to refrain from eating, drinking, or brushing his teeth, except for water, until the last saliva sample is collected at the 3-hour mark.

A 28-week gestational age preterm infant weighing 1200g was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) due to premature rupture of membranes. The infant is currently receiving standard 3-hour bundled care and wears a breathable diaper. The infant has not been diagnosed with neonatal abstinence syndrome, humidified incubator use, diaper rash, pre-existing or genetic skin conditions, or use of barrier creams. The infant is expected to remain hospitalized for at least 4 weeks.

A 62-year-old woman was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease about 4 years ago. She has been taking levodopa with dopa decarboxylase inhibitor (DDCI) since then. However, she has been experiencing predictable wearing-off and unpredictable ON-OFF fluctuations for the past 3 months. She lives in a low-income area and finds the cost of levodopa therapy to be very expensive. She heard about the potential use of Mucuna Pruriens var. Utilis (MP) powder as a cheaper alternative to levodopa and is interested in participating in this clinical trial. Her medical history includes hypertension, for which she takes medication daily. She has no history of psychiatric illness, addiction disorders or cognitive impairment. She is willing to give written informed consent to participate in the trial. Her Hoehn and Yahr stage is 3 in the medication-OFF state. She is not at risk of pregnancy. She weighs 65 kg and is 165 cm tall. Her last physical exam and lab study was performed yesterday and showed the results below: A wellbeing, well-nourished woman, cooperative and alert Weight: 65 kg Height: 165 BP: 140/90 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 4500/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 35 U/L ALT: 45 U/L Alk P: 120 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl Glucose: 100 mg/dl

25-year-old female with a dental open bite ranging from 3-8 mm and skeletal open bite. She has noticed difficulty in chewing and speaking due to the open bite. She has a full set of posterior teeth from first premolar to second molar, except for one tooth in one quadrant. She has adequate incisal show at rest and on smiling. She has not undergone any orthodontic treatment in the past and has no medical history of any chronic illness. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of maxillary posterior dento-alveolar intrusion versus combined maxillary and mandibular posterior dento-alveolar intrusion in terms of anterior open bite closure.

A 27-year-old woman with classic galactosemia was referred to the clinic due to infertility. She was diagnosed with galactosemia at birth and has been on a galactose-restricted diet since then. She has a history of delayed puberty and has not had a menstrual period for 6 months. Her serum FSH and estradiol levels were elevated, indicating premature ovarian insufficiency (POI). She has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years with no success. She is interested in participating in a research study that investigates the chances of spontaneous pregnancy in women with classic galactosemia and POI. She has no other known medical conditions that would negatively affect pubertal development and fertility.

A 32-year-old male presented with a history of perianal pain and discharge for the last 6 months. The patient reported that he had undergone multiple surgeries for anal fissure in the past, but the condition had not improved. He also complained of difficulty sitting for long periods of time and discomfort during bowel movements. On physical examination, a perianal fistula was identified with an external opening at the 3 o'clock position. The patient was otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. He had a history of occasional alcohol and tobacco use but had quit both approximately 1 year ago. He had no prior history of surgical interventions for any other medical conditions. MRI showed a low simple trans-sphincteric fistula with no evidence of branching anatomy or cavity. The patient was able to provide informed consent and was willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 12 year-old male with a diagnosis of Down syndrome. He has a full IQ of 55 and has difficulty with language, memory and attention. He is currently not taking any medication and has no known allergies. He lives with his parents and siblings and attends a special school for children with developmental disabilities. His medical history is unremarkable and he has no known heart, gastrointestinal, renal, or central nervous system problems that could affect his evaluation or compliance. His hearing and vision are normal. His parents have agreed for him to participate in this 12-month trial and have signed the necessary permit for his participation.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 23. She has no significant medical conditions and is not taking any medications other than occasional mild analgesics. She is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine-containing products. She has no history of anaphylaxis, food allergies, or allergies requiring prescription medication. She does not have any autoimmune disorders requiring more than topical medication and has not had asthma requiring inhaled medication within the past 5 years. She is not pregnant or nursing and agrees to use a medically accepted contraceptive regimen during the study and up to 150 days afterwards. She is willing to follow all study rules and avoid vaccination during the study. She signs an informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man from an arsenic affected area who has been drinking arsenic contaminated water for more than 6 months. He presents with moderate palmer arsenical keratosis on his right hand. He has no other chronic diseases and is not receiving any treatment for arsenicosis. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves taking two probiotic capsules orally per day for 12 weeks. Water sample will be collected before starting the study to confirm the diagnosis. Stool samples will be collected twice, before and after completion of the study, for qualitative and quantitative analysis of anaerobic bacteria. He is aware that similar number of arsenic exposed controls and healthy volunteers from the same area will be included in this study and they will be provided probiotics capsules with similar dosage and duration. He is willing to participate in the trial voluntarily.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a spinal degenerative disease that has been causing him chronic lower back pain that has been limiting his mobility and affecting his daily activities. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year and has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and medication without significant improvement. The patient will require spinal surgery for less than 4 levels to treat his condition. He is affiliated with a national insurance system and has agreed to participate in the Degen Study to receive treatment using MEDICREA's products, including at least PASS LP and/or PASS Degen and/or PASS Tulip implants. The patient is able to sign and understand an informed consent form and complete a self-administered questionnaire. He is also able to undergo X-ray follow-up and attend regular follow-up visits for up to 2 years.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was hospitalized for an acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and underwent an emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at San Filippo Neri Hospital. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history. He presented to the hospital with chest pain that started 4 hours prior to admission. The electrocardiogram (ECG) showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and the troponin level was elevated. The patient underwent an emergent primary PCI, with complete revascularization achieved. The patient is currently stable and recovering in the hospital. He reports feeling anxious and worried about his future health. He is interested in participating in the study to see if short-term psychotherapy (STP) can improve his outcomes after the AMI. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders, cognitive impairment, or other life-threatening conditions.

45-year-old male recreational runner who has been running 3 times per week for the past year. He is able to run 10 km in approximately 40 minutes. He has no history of cardiovascular issues or recent injuries or illnesses. He is not currently taking any multivitamin supplements or anti-inflammatory medications. He is interested in participating in the study as he is looking to improve his exercise performance and recovery.

A 7 year old girl with a history of HIV infection is currently on antiretroviral therapy for the past 8 months. Her CD4 count is 250 cells/mm3 and her viral load is 5,000 copies/mL. She has been compliant with her medications with no changes in her regimen for the past 3 months. She has no known allergies and her medical history is unremarkable. She has not participated in any experimental antiretroviral or HIV vaccine trials. She is currently not taking any IVIG, chemotherapy or any other medication that affects the immune system. She has no history of severe reaction to IVIG. She has no co-existing condition that requires large doses of IVIG or any other condition requiring dosing with IVIG. She is expected to tolerate IV infusions at a minimum rate of 0.02 ml/kg/min.

55F with a history of recurrent infections and fatigue for the past 2 years. She was evaluated extensively by her primary care physician and infectious disease specialist, but no definitive diagnosis was made. Recent laboratory investigations revealed moderate anemia and neutropenia, and a bone marrow biopsy was performed which showed T-cell large granular lymphocytic (T-LGL) leukemia. The patient has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. She is currently not on any medications, including immunosuppressive treatment. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 2 years and is not pregnant. She is willing to use effective contraception if she is fertile. She has not received any previous treatment with methotrexate or fludarabine.

A 42-year-old male presents with fatigue, weakness, and easy bruising that has been ongoing for the past several weeks. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Physical examination reveals mild pallor and scattered ecchymoses on the arms and legs. Vital signs are stable. Laboratory results are significant for a white blood cell count of 15,000/µL, hemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 40,000/µL. A bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of being newly diagnosed with AML and being over 15 years old. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria as he has no severe or uncontrolled medical conditions and his serum creatinine, AST, and ALT levels are within normal limits.

A 62-year-old male presents with stable angina pectoris and non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. He has a past medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are both well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and leads an active lifestyle with regular exercise. He has undergone an invasive coronary angiography and is recommended for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). He does not have any allergies to aspirin, clopidogrel, ticagrelor or prasugrel. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is within normal limits. The lesions in his coronary arteries have been evaluated and found to be tortuous, with angiographically estimated extremely calcified lesions, which makes him ineligible for inclusion in the study. Therefore, he is not a candidate for this clinical trial.

A 30-year-old woman has been experiencing seizures for the past 6 months. Her seizures are focal and occur once every 2-3 weeks. She has tried one anti-epileptic drug, but it did not help her condition. She has no history of head injury or stroke. Her MRI shows a small focal lesion in the left temporal lobe. Her EEG shows focal sharp waves. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any major medical co-morbidities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help identify the best treatment options for her condition.

A 16-year-old Hispanic female adolescent presents with a BMI of 41.2, indicating morbid obesity. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She reports feeling self-conscious about her weight and has been struggling to lose weight on her own. She has tried various diets and exercises but has not been successful in sustaining weight loss. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or surgical interventions. She is currently enrolled in high school and is able to attend biweekly to monthly sessions with the support team. She is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve her health and is willing to adhere to the advised lifestyle changes. Her parents are supportive of her participation in this clinical trial.

Patient is a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with osteoporosis. She has a history of low-impact fractures in her wrist and hip, which were caused by minimal trauma. She is currently taking calcium and vitamin D supplements but her physician has now prescribed Preotact® (parathyroid hormone) to improve her bone mineral density and to prevent any further fractures. Patient is able and willing to self-administer injections of Preotact® using the Pen system. She will be monitored for any adverse drug reactions and will undergo various assessments including the Qualeffo-41 questionnaire to assess the quality of life, VAS score to assess pain, T-Score to assess bone mineral density, and serum levels of calcium and bone resorption markers (DPD, CTX, and NTX) before and after the observational period. The physician will also assess the manageability and functioning of the Pen system for injection of Preotact® through a self-administered questionnaire.

A 60-year-old male patient was referred to the clinic with a history of COPD for the past 5 years. He has been struggling with shortness of breath, especially during physical activities such as walking or climbing stairs. He is a former smoker with a 40 pack-year history and quit smoking 2 years ago. He has been compliant with his medications including bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids. He reports feeling anxious and stressed due to his COPD symptoms which affect his daily life activities. He has a Medical Research Council of Dyspnea Score of 3. He is interested in participating in a program to improve his quality of life and reduce his dyspnea symptoms. He denies any neurological or psychiatric conditions and has no history of active chemical dependency.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastasis to the liver and brain. He received six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy with bevacizumab as part of the ECOG-4599 protocol. He tolerated the treatment well and had a partial response with a reduction in the size of his liver and brain metastases. He is currently in remission and is being monitored for recurrence. He has a history of smoking for 20 years and has quit smoking 10 years ago. His family history is unremarkable for cancer. His most recent CT scan showed no evidence of active disease. He has provided consent for the collection of blood and tissue samples as part of the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, dry cough, and fatigue for the past year. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He was diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) based on a combination of high-resolution computerized tomography (HRCT) pattern and surgical lung biopsy pattern consistent with the disease. His pulmonary function test showed a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 60% predicted of normal and a corrected diffusion capacity (Dlco) of 45% predicted of normal. He is not currently taking any medication for his IPF. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for 6 months. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his IPF.

A 32-year-old man with a history of schizophrenia for 5 years presented with auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech. He had been taking olanzapine 20mg daily for the past 2 years, but the symptoms have not improved. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with amlodipine 5mg daily. He doesn't smoke or use illicit drugs. He is currently unemployed and living with his parents. He has no known drug allergies. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find a better treatment for his schizophrenia.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling to regulate her cholesterol levels despite being on Atorvastatin. She has a history of high triglyceride and low HDL-C levels that have not been successfully managed through medication alone. She has never been diagnosed with fibromyalgia or myopathy, and her creatinine clearance is above 60mL/min. She has not experienced any uncontrolled hypo-thyroidism symptoms and has signed the informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who wears contact lenses daily. She has been experiencing dryness and discomfort during contact lens wear, which has been affecting her ability to wear them for a full day. She has no history of eye surgery or allergies. Her eye exam shows no signs of active inflammation or infection, and her corneal sensitivity is normal. Her tear volume and osmolality will be measured before and after the insertion of collagen punctal plugs, which will be left in place for 3-14 days.

A 62-year-old postmenopausal female with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs) with symptomatic, culture-proven UTIs in the past 12 months. She has been using vaginal estrogen therapy (VET) for at least four weeks prior to the study's day one. She has been diagnosed with a uropathogen susceptible to D-mannose. She is not currently on daily antibiotic UTI prophylaxis and does not have complicated UTIs, incomplete bladder emptying, endometrial cancer, estrogen-sensitive breast cancer, interstitial cystitis/painful bladder syndrome, or urothelial cancer. She is an English speaker and is not enrolled in other clinical trials for UTIs. She is not currently using D-mannose or Methenamine for UTI prevention.

This is a 12 year-old female with a known history of asthma who was admitted to the pediatric ICU at St. John's Children's Hospital with status asthmaticus. Despite receiving one dose of systemic steroid, 1 hour of continuous albuterol (SABA), and 3 doses of ipratropium bromide, her clinical asthma score (CAS) was between 3-8. She is experiencing wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness. The patient's parent has provided written informed consent for her participation in the clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of early initiation of non-invasive NPPV in pediatric patients admitted with status asthmaticus.

A 40-year-old Caucasian woman with a medical history of asthma and ABPA complains of persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. She has been on inhaled corticosteroids and oral prednisone for the past year, but the symptoms are still present. She has a history of seasonal allergies but no known allergies to any medications. She does not smoke cigarettes or use e-cigarettes. She occasionally drinks alcohol but not more than 1-2 drinks per week. She has a BMI of 25. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not had any major surgeries or traumas recently, and she is not currently taking any investigational medications. She is willing to follow the contraception requirements of the study. She has a prebronchodilator FEV1 of 70% predicted normal for her age, sex, race, and height. She has a serum IgE level of 1200 IU/mL at screening. She is able to demonstrate the correct inhalation technique for the use of the delivery device.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman who is not of childbearing potential due to having had a hysterectomy. She has a BMI of 24 and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of gastrointestinal problems or disease, metabolic, endocrine, or chronic diseases, or any allergies to study supplement ingredients or to any food or beverage provided during the study. She agrees to avoid using black or white pepper, turmeric, curcumin, or curry in the preparation of food for 7 days prior to randomization and throughout the study period. She also agrees to avoid Indian and Thai cuisines for the period of the study and to avoid food with yellow dye #E100. She agrees to avoid alcohol, caffeine, and grapefruit and grapefruit juice 48 hours prior to baseline and each subsequent clinic visit. She agrees to consume only low polyphenols in the diet and has given voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study.

A 16-year-old male with a diagnosed pectus excavatum deformity presents with complaints of reduced self-confidence, poor posture and difficulty in social relationships. He feels embarrassed to participate in sports and social activities due to his chest deformity. He has no chronic systemic or musculoskeletal diseases, and no history of psychological diagnosis. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the physical and psychosocial characteristics of patients with pectus deformities compared to healthy controls.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who suffered an ischemic stroke 3 months ago. He has been experiencing right-sided weakness and difficulty with speech since the stroke. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. He has undergone rehabilitation therapy but still experiences significant functional impairment. His MRI shows a relevant ischemic lesion, and his extracranial duplex and transcranial Doppler confirm intra/extracranial arteries permeability. He has a NIH Stroke Scale score of 10. He has never been diagnosed with cancer and is up to date on all age and gender-appropriate cancer screenings. He is willing to maintain contraceptive therapy for the duration of the study. He understands the study and is willing to give written informed consent.

A 32-year-old man arrives at the emergency department with severe pain in his abdomen. He has no history of chronic pain and is an English speaker. He can provide informed consent and is comfortable with the experimental protocol as outlined to him by the research team. He rates his pain as 8/10 on the numerical rating scale. The treating ED attending physician deems him to require IV opioid analgesia. He has an ASA class I or II. He has no neurologic, respiratory, or hemodynamic compromise, and his Glasgow Coma Scale is 15. His pulse oximetry reading is 98%, and his respiratory rate is 18. His SBP is 130 and his DBP is 80. He has no known allergies to ketamine or morphine. He has not used ketamine within 24 hours of presentation, and he has not received conscious sedation in the ED. He has no history of renal or liver failure, stroke, or cardiac disease. He has not had a myocardial infarction, angina, cardiac stents, or bypass surgery.

A 45-year-old male patient presents with gum recession in several teeth, particularly in the lower front teeth. He reports sensitivity when drinking cold and hot beverages and is concerned about the esthetics of his teeth. He has good oral hygiene habits and visits his dentist regularly. He has no history of chronic inflammatory disease or severe systemic diseases. He does not smoke and is not currently taking any medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. A clinical examination reveals multiple Miller class I, II and III gingival recessions in the lower and upper anterior teeth. The patient is interested in undergoing a gingival recession coverage surgery to address his concerns. The treating dentist informs the patient about a clinical trial that is investigating the effect of Coenzyme Q10 spray on early wound healing after gingival recession surgery and asks if he is interested in participating. The patient consents to participate in the trial and meets the eligibility criteria.

A 26-year-old woman presents with irregular menstrual cycles for the past 10 months. She used to have regular periods before. She also reports hirsutism (excessive hair growth on the face, chest, and back), acne, and hair loss from her head. She has gained 10 kg of weight over the past year with a BMI of 29. The patient is married and has no children. Her family history is unremarkable. On pelvic examination, no abnormalities are detected. The transvaginal ultrasound reveals multiple small cysts in both ovaries with a volume of 15 mL. Her laboratory workup shows a high level of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) ratio of 3.5, testosterone level of 70 ng/dL, and normal prolactin and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels. She meets the Rotterdam criteria for PCOS diagnosis. She is eligible for the clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of probiotics, metformin, and their combination therapy in the treatment of PCOS. She will be randomized to one of the three groups and will be followed up regularly in the gynecology OPD of the tertiary care hospital.

A 28 year old woman comes to the clinic expressing her interest in participating in a clinical trial for brain imaging. She is healthy with no history of psychiatric illness or severe systemic disease. She has not had any past brain surgeries or seizure disorders. Her blood pressure is normal and she does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has not been exposed to any radiation from previous clinical trials or medical care in the last year. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not claustrophobic and does not have any metallic implants. She is able to lie flat on her back for up to 2.5 hours. She has tested negative for HIV and is able to provide informed consent. She meets all eligibility criteria for the trial involving (11C)mGlu1 for imaging of brain receptors.

This is a 10-year-old male diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy (CP) with spastic diplegia that affects his lower body function. He is able to walk but has limitations in walking long distances and balancing. He has not yet required the use of mobility devices, but may need them in the future. His spasticity is currently controlled by medication. He is able to follow simple instructions in English and has no skin disorders that would prevent the use of medical-grade adhesive tapes. He will be participating in a clinical trial for Precision Gait Retraining for Children with Cerebral Palsy. The trial will involve testing a novel tethered Pelvic Assist Device (TPAD) with integratable electromyographic (EMG) and inertial (IMU) biofeedback that is uniquely capable of delivering precise, adaptable, multi-degree-of-freedom pelvic control to promote natural intersegmental coupling, restore coordination of upper- and lower-limb movement, and improve normal gait kinematics in children with CP. He will be under the supervision of a physiotherapist while wearing the TPAD device with wearable sensors to receive biofeedback on his gait. He will need to provide informed consent from himself and assent from his parent or guardian.

A 30-year-old female resident of Hillsborough County, Florida who has not experienced any symptoms of SARS-CoV-2 infection. She has no underlying health conditions and has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 previously. She is interested in participating in the study to understand the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 and contribute to filling critical knowledge gaps in the natural history of the virus.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman of South Asian ethnicity who has been diagnosed with diabetes and hypertension. She has had diabetes for 10 years and hypertension for 5 years. She has been prescribed medication but has experienced little improvement in her condition. She experiences frequent headaches, dizziness, and blurred vision. She also has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of commonly prescribed drugs in treating illnesses that cause significant poor health and death in different patient populations in the UK. She is willing to provide biological samples, allow access to her medical records, and complete questionnaires related to her condition.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She underwent a fine needle aspiration which confirmed the diagnosis. The cancer is locally advanced and has not spread to distant organs. She is planning to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery. The patient's hormone receptor status has not been determined. She has no prior history of chemotherapy for any malignancy, and she has not received any biologic, endocrine or radiotherapy treatments. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial which will examine molecular marker profiling of axillary lymph nodes to predict her response to treatment. She will undergo open surgical biopsy of axillary lymph nodes before and after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The axillary lymph node tissue will be examined for molecular and protein markers by immunohistochemistry and fluorescence in situ hybridization. Additionally, she will receive fludeoxyglucose F 18 positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) before and after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. She will then undergo a conventional segmental mastectomy (lumpectomy) with or without needle localization followed by FDG-PET probe-guided surgical resection of any remaining FDG-avid tumor tissue.

A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and swelling in his legs. He reports feeling fatigued and has a rapid heart rate. The patient is concerned as he has experienced similar symptoms in the past but has always been admitted to the hospital. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at identifying high- and low-risk heart failure patients in the emergency department.
