The study involves a digital heart sound recording procedure, medical record review, blood collection, and a brief cognitive assessment. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male presented with a history of chronic plaque-type psoriasis for the past 7 years. The patient reported that his psoriasis flares up intermittently and has been moderately severe for the past 6 months. He has been receiving topical corticosteroids and emollients as maintenance therapy. His medical history was significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia, which were managed with lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He denied any history of heart disease, stroke, diabetes or any other significant medical history. He had no known allergies, and he was currently not on any other medications. The patient was a non-smoker and had no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Physical examination revealed multiple well-demarcated, erythematous, and scaly plaques on his arms, legs, and trunk. The plaque psoriasis area severity index (PASI) score was calculated as 15. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and was willing and able to self-administer subcutaneous injections or have a caregiver available to administer injections.

The patient is a 26-year-old Caucasian woman who is currently 28 weeks pregnant with no pregnancy complications. She has a pre-pregnancy BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no history of substance abuse or eating disorders. She is currently not taking any medications known to influence vitamin D or calcium homeostasis. She has no plans to travel to a lower latitude during the study period and is willing to discontinue tanning bed use and vitamin or mineral supplement use during the study period. She is scheduled to deliver by c-section and is willing to participate in the placental transfer study (Aims 4-6).

This is a 60-year-old male with a history of renal cell carcinoma who has received prior treatment and now presents with progressive disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has been referred to this study by his oncologist. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG Performance Scale and has measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1. He has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent. He has adequate organ function and has a negative urine or serum pregnancy test. He is willing to use two methods of contraception for the course of the study through 120 days after the last dose of study medication. He has a history of diabetes mellitus, but his HgbA1c level is less than 8.5% upon study entry. He has not participated in a study of an investigational agent and is not currently receiving study therapy or using an investigational device. He does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency and is not receiving systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. He does not have active TB or hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or any of its excipients. He has not had a prior anti-cancer monoclonal antibody (mAb) within 4 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 and has not had prior chemotherapy, targeted small molecule therapy, or radiation therapy within 2 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1. He does not have a known additional malignancy that is progressing or requires active treatment and does not have known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a diagnosed advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (unresectable or metastatic) and at least one measurable focus without local treatment. He has Child-Pugh score ≤ 6 points (Child-Pugh A); BCLC staging is stage C, and PVTT classification is combined with PVTT (program classification PVTT ≤ 3), and a single lesion in the liver (or multiple lesions with diameter) ≤ 7cm of primary liver cancer. He is a newly diagnosed patient who has not received targeted therapy or immunotherapy in the past. The patient's liver tumor burden is less than 50% of the total liver volume, and he has not received liver transplantation in the past. The patient's vital organ functions meet the following requirements: The absolute count of neutrophils≥1.5×109/L; Platelet ≥80×109/L; Hemoglobin ≥90 g/L; Serum albumin ≥28 g/L; Bilirubin≤1.5×ULN (within 7 days before the first administration); ALT and AST ≤3×ULN (within 7 days before the first dose); AKP≤ 2.5×ULN; Serum creatinine≤1.5×ULN. The patient has not undergone any surgical sterilization or female patients of childbearing age need to use a medically approved contraceptive method (such as intrauterine device, contraceptive or condom) during the study treatment period and within 3 months after the end of the study treatment period. The patient's ECOG score is 0-1. The patient is willing to participate in the study voluntarily and has signed an informed consent form.

A 25 year old female patient with a recent diagnosis of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) presented for enrollment in this clinical trial. She is currently receiving chemotherapy with augmented BFM. She has no history of fractures or bone loss, and her bone density test showed a T-score of -1.5. She has normal renal function and a calculated creatinine clearance of 90cc/min. Her corrected calcium level is within normal range. She has no known hypersensitivity to risedronate or bisphosphonates. She has not been taking any bisphosphonates, calcitonin, anabolic steroids, or fluoride. She has a 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration of 25 ng/ml. She is sexually active and willing to use contraception. A negative pregnancy test was confirmed. She is able to sit or stand upright for at least 30 minutes. She is interested in participating in the study to prevent the development of osteoporosis caused by the steroid medication used to treat her leukemia.

A 32-year-old woman is experiencing symptoms of moderate to severe allergic rhinitis such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy nose. She has a history of asthma and has been on a daily regimen of inhaled corticosteroids for the past year. She has a positive skin prick test for house dust mites, grass pollen, and animal dander. She has tried various over-the-counter medications but has not found relief from her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate long-term symptom control and satisfaction with immunotherapy. She is fluent in English and has no other medical conditions.

A 55-year old retired teacher was recently diagnosed with stage 3 non small cell lung cancer. She has a history of smoking for over 30 years and quit smoking after her diagnosis. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but is still experiencing persistent cough and fatigue. She has a family history of cancer, with her mother and sister being diagnosed with breast cancer. The patient is married and has two adult children. She is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. She is interested in participating in clinical trials and eager to explore alternative treatments. She is in overall good health and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has no known allergies to medications or food. The patient is willing to comply with the study's requirements and weekly phone calls between office visits.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with localized deposits of adipose tissues in her waist, hips, and thighs that have not responded to diet and exercise. Her body mass index (BMI) is less than 30 kg/m². She is not a diabetic and has no known cardiovascular disease or prior surgical intervention for body sculpting/weight loss. She is not taking any medication known to affect weight levels and/or cause bloating or swelling. She has no medical condition known to affect weight levels and/or cause bloating or swelling. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy prior to study end. She has no serious mental health illness, developmental disability, or cognitive impairment that would preclude adequate comprehension of the informed consent form and/or ability to record study measurements. She has not participated in research in the past 30 days. She is willing and able to abstain from partaking in any treatment other than the study procedure to promote body contouring and/or weight loss during study participation. She is willing and able to maintain her regular diet and exercise regimen without effecting significant change in either direction during study participation.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. He has no family history of the disease, but he has two older siblings who have never been screened for the disease. He is married with two adult children and works in construction. He is generally healthy, but he has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol use. He is interested in participating in this study to learn more about his family's risk for colorectal cancer and to encourage his siblings to get screened.

42-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis for the last 10 years, with a current diagnosis of IBD-associated CRC. He has been treated with mesalamine, budesonide, and azathioprine. He has undergone multiple colonoscopies with biopsies, and the current biopsy showed adenocarcinoma. The patient is scheduled for surgery in the next few weeks. He has no other significant medical history, no allergies, and is currently not taking any antibiotics or undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent to provide fecal samples for the study.

A 28-year-old male was diagnosed with schizophrenia 3 years ago after presenting with auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech. He has been on antipsychotic medication, which has helped to reduce the severity of his symptoms but still experiences difficulties in social situations. He reports feeling anxious and self-conscious, leading to avoidance of social situations, isolation, and a limited social network. He reports spending most of his time at home and has trouble initiating and maintaining conversations. He has had difficulties maintaining employment due to his social difficulties. He speaks English fluently and completed high school with average grades. He has no history of substance abuse or significant medical comorbidities. His current medication regimen has been stable for the last 6 months. He has good insight into his condition and is motivated to participate in interventions that can help him improve his social functioning.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 3 years ago is experiencing active disease despite treatment with methotrexate. She has tender and swollen joints in both hands and feet, with morning stiffness lasting more than an hour. She has also developed fatigue and difficulty performing daily activities. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She has not previously been treated with anti-TNF therapy. She is compliant with folic acid supplementation. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her rheumatoid arthritis.

10-year-old male diagnosed with Tourette Syndrome 2 years ago with motor and vocal tics that have been causing significant impairment in his quality of life. The patient and his family have tried various medications and therapies, but the tics have persisted, affecting his school performance and social interactions with peers. The patient is a native Hebrew speaker and is currently receiving stable doses of medication for his tics. He has no history of substance abuse or developmental disorders, and his FSIQ score is above 80. The patient and his family are interested in participating in a group intervention program to manage his tics and improve his quality of life.

65-year-old female who leads a sedentary lifestyle with no history of smoking or chronic illness. She has a history of normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels. She exercises only occasionally and is interested in participating in the study to improve her cardiovascular health. She has never taken antioxidant vitamins, corticosteroids or anti-inflammatory medications. She is willing to take the MitoQ supplement and will comply with the study protocol. She has no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease. She is postmenopausal and has not received any hormone therapy in the last year.

A 45-year-old man with a past medical history of HIV infection presents with complaints of progressive dysphagia, hoarseness of voice, and difficulty breathing for the past 2 months. His symptoms have been worsening despite being on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the past 6 months. On examination, he has multiple violaceous lesions on the oral cavity, pharynx, and larynx with some of them causing partial airway obstruction. A biopsy of the lesions confirms the diagnosis of Kaposi's sarcoma. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in a clinical trial for the treatment of his localized Kaposi's sarcoma.

A 55-year-old male patient presented with recurrent chest pain and was diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking. He has been on medication to manage these conditions for several years. His recent angiogram showed a narrowing of one of his coronary arteries by 50% and the physiological severity of the lesion is in question. He is currently experiencing stable angina. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test a new technique called the instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) that does not require the administration of drugs for its accurate assessment. The study aims to compare clinical outcomes of patients whose treatment has been guided by iFR to those whose treatment has been guided by fractional flow reserve (FFR). The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is not excluded by any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 1 year with no success. She has a BMI of 25 and has no significant past medical history. She has regular menstrual cycles and has been trying to conceive naturally without any success. She has never undergone any IVF treatment before. She presents to the clinic with a desire to undergo IVF/ICSI treatment to conceive. Her transvaginal ultrasound shows a normal uterine cavity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the pregnancy rates in women with normal uterine cavities and those with corrected uterine lesions. She has no history of poor response to IVF medications and has an AMH level of 2 ng/dl. She is willing to undergo hysteroscopy to detect any uterine lesions and have them treated if necessary.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her right shoulder for the past 6 months. She has tried various conservative treatments including physical therapy and pain medications, but has not seen any significant improvement. An ultrasound imaging revealed medium-sized calcific deposits in her supraspinatus tendon. She has no history of diabetes, coagulation diseases, or anticoagulant therapy, and is not currently pregnant. She has not had any previous shoulder surgeries or been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis or any other connective tissue diseases. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different ranges of energy flux density with Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for the treatment of supraspinatus calcifying tendonitis.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (NET) was referred to our clinic. She had been previously treated with 4 cycles of 200 mCi 177Lu-dotatate, but the last cycle was completed 10 weeks ago. She had multiple liver metastases and was not a candidate for standard therapeutic options such as chemotherapy or surgery. She had no history of brain metastases, spinal cord compression or radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks. Her WHO performance status was 1, and her life expectancy was estimated to be 12 weeks or longer. Her liver disease had at least 3 measurable liver lesions according to the RECIST 1.1 criteria. She had no unresolved toxicity greater than NCI, Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 2 from previous anti-cancer therapy. Her serum bilirubin was within normal limits, and her glomerular filtration rate was 55 ml/min. Her ALT, AST, and ALP were elevated but < 5 x ULN. Her leukocyte and platelet counts were within normal limits. She had no significant cardiac event, and her NYHA classification of heart disease was 1. She was not pregnant or nursing, and she did not have any diseases with an increased chance of liver toxicity. She was using an approved contraceptive implant to prevent pregnancy. She was eligible for the study and consented to participate in the HEPAR PLUS trial to evaluate the efficacy and toxicity of adjuvant 166Ho-radioembolization (166Ho-RE) after systemic 177Lu-dotatate for the treatment of her liver metastases of NET.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty with her vision due to bilateral cataracts. She has had no previous ocular surgery and has good ocular health apart from the cataracts. She is not pregnant nor planning to be during the course of the study. She has a preoperative astigmatism of less than 2.5 diopters. She has no history of corneal disease, diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration, or retinal detachment. She is able to attend postoperative examinations as per protocol schedule and has signed an informed consent form. She has no other protocol-defined exclusion criteria. She is excited for the opportunity to improve her vision and is looking forward to participating in the study.

A 62-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of knee pain that has been progressively getting worse for the past year. He has difficulty walking long distances and getting up from a seated position. He rates his pain intensity at 70 mm on a 100 mm scale. He has been previously diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis and has tried nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but they did not provide sufficient relief. He is physically and mentally able to comply with post-operative rehabilitation and routinely schedule clinical and radiographic visits. He does not have any known tumors or infections in his knee and has not received chemotherapy in the past 12 months. He does not have any known allergies to ozone and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have any significant systemic diseases or history of substance or alcohol abuse.

A 63-year-old retired teacher was recently diagnosed with locally advanced esophageal cancer. He has a history of smoking for 30 years, but quit 10 years ago. He has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and lost weight over the past few months. He lives with his wife and two adult children. He enjoys gardening and taking walks, but his physical activity has decreased due to his symptoms. He is currently scheduled to undergo neoadjuvant chemoradiation. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his nutritional status and overall health. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, well controlled with medication. He is a non-insulin dependent diabetic, also well controlled with medication. He has had no previous surgeries. He is compliant with medications and states he is willing to follow the protocol of the study. He has no known cardiac or pulmonary diseases. He is able to walk and exercise without any problems.

A 25-year-old female diagnosed with major depressive disorder, recurrent, as per DSM-IV-TR criteria, and confirmed by SCID-CT. The patient has a history of taking antidepressants but is currently not on any medication. The patient has a Montgomery-Asberg Depression Scale (MADRS) score of 20 at Screening and baseline. The patient is a non-pregnant, non-lactating female of childbearing potential who agrees to use medically acceptable forms of birth control (hormonal contraception, abstinence, diaphragm with spermicide, condom with spermicide, or intrauterine device) from Screening until the end-of-study. The patient has the ability to understand the purpose and risks of the study and provides signed and dated informed consent, authorizing the use of protected health information in accordance with national and local patient privacy regulations.

A 4-year-old boy is referred to the department for a VCUG procedure due to frequent urinary tract infections. The boy is generally healthy but has a history of bedwetting and daytime incontinence. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. The parents are concerned about the radiation exposure during the procedure and are interested in any options to reduce it. They are open to participating in the clinical trial and learning more about the urinary sensor. The child is cooperative and able to follow instructions.

A 35-year-old woman visited the hospital with complaints of recurrent headaches that persisted for over a year. She described her headache as a dull, aching pain that is often associated with tightness or pressure around her forehead and temples. She reported a throbbing pain occasionally and feels discomfort in her neck and shoulders. She has a history of stress and anxiety and works in a high-pressure job. She has tried various medications but doesn't get adequate relief from the pain. Upon physical examination, the doctor found tenderness points on the upper part of her trapezius muscle. She was diagnosed with tension-type headache and was offered to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of Kinesio taping on upper trapezius muscle on the reduction of pain and emotional state. She was between the ages of 30-45 and met all the inclusion criteria. She agreed to participate in the study and was randomly assigned to the study group where she received KT and stretching exercises.

A 28-year-old male athlete who participates in high-impact sports, such as soccer and basketball, complains of knee instability and pain after a traumatic injury while playing soccer 13 months ago. He reports anterior knee pain, swelling, and a sensation of knee giving out during pivoting movements. The patient has tried conservative treatments such as physiotherapy and knee bracing, but he still experiences knee instability during sports activities. Physical examination confirms a grade 2 pivot shift test and positive Lachman test. He does not have any history of knee surgeries or any other significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 23. He is currently not taking any medications or supplements. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of combined ACL and ALL reconstruction with isolated ACL reconstruction in individuals with a high risk of ACL re-rupture.

58-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) for the past year. The patient has experienced at least two episodes of PAF, with one episode documented by electrocardiography (ECG) within the last 12 months. The patient has failed treatment with at least one anti-arrhythmic drug (AAD Type I or III) due to effectiveness and intolerance. The patient is mentally and linguistically able to understand the aim of the trial and is willing to follow the trial protocol. The patient has been informed of the risks and benefits of the cryoballoon ablation system or standard RF ablation technique and has consented to the trial. The patient is between 18 and 75 years of age, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not participating in any other clinical trial. The patient has no history of prosthetic valves, previous LA ablation or surgery, cardiac surgery or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within the last three months, unstable angina pectoris, myocardial infarction within the last three months, symptomatic carotid stenosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with detected pulmonary hypertension, or any condition contraindicating chronic anticoagulation. The patient has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack within the last six months, LV dysfunction with EF < 35%, or LA thrombus. The patient has no laboratory abnormalities such as thrombocytosis, thrombocytopenia, untreated or uncontrolled hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism, or severe renal dysfunction.

A 25-year-old female presented to the clinic with a history of mild asthma since childhood. She currently works as a teacher and has no history of smoking or vaping. She is not pregnant or nursing. She exercises regularly and only experiences asthma symptoms during exercise or when exposed to triggers such as pollen or dust. She uses an inhaler as needed and has not had an asthma exacerbation or change in treatment within the past four weeks. She has no major chronic cardiorespiratory disease or significant comorbid condition. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in a clinical trial. Her asthma is treated according to level-1 of the British Thoracic Society treatment guidelines. She is not participating in any other clinical trial of an investigational medicinal product. She has no known hypersensitivity to mannitol, gelatin or strong anaphylactic response in the past. She speaks English fluently. Her FEV1 is 2.6 liters or 85% predicted value.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing fatigue and muscle weakness over the past few months. She reports a history of a Western diet and limited sun exposure due to her office job. Blood workup reveals a plasma 25(OH) vitamin D level of 30 nmol/l. The patient is in good overall health and has no known gastrointestinal diseases or diabetes mellitus. She does not take any lipid-lowering medications, supplements, or have any relevant food allergies/intolerances. The patient has not visited a solarium or been to the mountains for skiing within the past 4 weeks, and does not plan to during the study. She is interested in participating in the study to increase her vitamin D levels and improve her overall health.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension who is currently taking medication to manage it. He has no history of heart failure, cancer, heart attack, stroke, transient ischemic attack, angina pectoris, CABG, or PCI. He is not taking any vitamin D or fish oil supplements currently and is willing to forego their use during the trial. The patient is not allergic to fish or soy. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits for up to five years.

A 32-year-old female patient presents to the hospital with a history of intermittent right upper quadrant pain for the past 2 weeks. The pain is dull and aching in nature, and it is associated with nausea and vomiting. She feels better after vomiting. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of any systemic diseases, cardiovascular, respiratory, hepato-renal, neurological, endocrinal or hematological disorders, drug or alcohol addiction, or psychiatric diseases. Her BMI is 26. She has no history of motion sickness and has not taken any antiemetic medication within 24 hours before surgery. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She is not menstruating, and her pregnancy test is negative. She consents to undergo elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallstones. She is randomized to the study group and receives ramosetron as prophylactic medication for post-operative nausea and vomiting. She is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or sensitivity to the study drug. She is monitored for 48 hours for nausea, vomiting, pain, adverse effects, and post-anesthetic discharge score.

35 year old female diagnosed with femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and acetabular dysplasia presenting with persistent hip pain accompanied by mechanical symptoms refractory to nonoperative management lasting at least 3 months. The patient has undergone radiographic imaging including radiography, computed tomography with 3-dimensional reconstruction, and magnetic resonance imaging, which have all confirmed the diagnosis of FAI and Hip Dysplasia. Joint-space width is greater than 3 mm on all views of plain radiography and 3-dimensional computed tomography. The patient is scheduled to undergo hip arthroscopy for the treatment of FAI, Hip Dysplasia, or the combination of the two by the Principal Investigator, who has modified and improved two devices for hip arthroscopy - the hip capsule side fixed slotted cannula for continued access to the hip joint and the bone graft delivery tool set for grafting subchrondral cysts arthroscopically during hip arthroscopy procedure. The patient is between the ages of 18 and 60 years and is fluent in English.

An 80-year-old male retiree who is generally in good health, with no significant medical history, is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a standardized Centella asiatica water extract product (CAP) on the elderly. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has never used illicit drugs. He has no history of psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is cognitively healthy with a MMSE score of 29 and Geriatric Depression Scale-15 score of 8. His BMI is 24.5. He is able to speak and understand English fluently, and has sufficient vision and hearing to complete all required tests. He is willing to discontinue all botanical dietary supplements for one week prior to and during each study visit, and to comply with a 48-hour low plant diet for each study visit. The patient is enthusiastic about participating in the study and contributing to the advancement of scientific knowledge.

32 year old HIV-positive woman who has sex with men presenting with abnormal anal cytology test results. The patient was diagnosed with HIV 6 years ago and has been on anti-retroviral therapy since then. She has a past medical history of herpes simplex virus and occasional vaginal yeast infections. She has a history of sexual contact with multiple partners and inconsistent condom use. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help reduce her risk of developing anal cancer. She meets the inclusion criteria for this trial, including having a negative pregnancy test, normal laboratory values, and a recent anal cytology result. She has not received the HPV vaccine in the past and is willing to receive either the vaccine or a placebo as part of the trial. The patient understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the follow-up visits and procedures.

A 70-year-old man presents with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild cognitive impairment. He requires surgery for a colon malignancy and has been referred to participate in a clinical trial comparing manual versus automated anesthesia. He lives independently and has a preoperative MOCA score of 26/30. He has no history of stroke, Alzheimer's, or Parkinson's disease. The patient has no known allergies to propofol or remifentanil, and his creatinine level is within normal range. However, he has a hearing deficiency that requires the use of hearing aids. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent form and participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who leads a sedentary lifestyle and works in an office environment. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or lung disease. She does not smoke and is not pregnant. Her BMI is within the normal range. She occasionally engages in mild aerobic exercise such as walking or light jogging but is not involved in any structured endurance training. She is fluent in English and able to understand and follow instructions. She has no history of hypertension, valve disease, coronary artery disease, or cardiac conduction abnormalities. Her spirometry is within predicted limits and her VO2 max is between 84-120% predicted using Wasserman reference equations. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her exercise performance and is willing to undergo the training protocol in a hyperbaric-hyperoxic environment.

A 45-year-old male with hospital-acquired pneumonia caused by Gram-negative bacteria is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. He was admitted to the hospital with a high-grade fever, cough, and shortness of breath. A chest x-ray revealed evidence of pneumonia, and sputum culture confirmed the presence of Gram-negative bacteria. The patient has no known allergies to antibiotics or any other medication. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. The patient has normal renal function and no history of epilepsy. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

The patient is a 21-year-old college student who has no history of neurological or orthopedic disorders. She is 170 cm tall and weighs 60 kg. She has no vision or hearing problems that would affect the balance tests. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She enjoys running and yoga. She has no prior experience with balance assessment tests but is willing to participate in the study. She is interested in contributing to the development of a new balance assessment system that could help individuals assess their balance quantitatively. She has no known health issues and is not taking any medications. Her blood pressure is normal, and she has a BMI of 20.8. She has no prior experience with balance assessment tests but is willing to participate in the study. She is committed to following the study plan and completing the specified tests.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. She has undergone several chemotherapy treatments but has not responded well to standard therapies. Her cancer has metastasized to her liver and lungs. She has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG Performance Scale. She has no history of heart disease but has hypertension that is controlled with medication. She has a history of smoking but quit several years ago. She has no psychiatric disorders or substance abuse history. Her past medical history is significant for hyperlipidemia and hypothyroidism. She is currently taking atorvastatin and levothyroxine. Her tumor has been tested and found to have a normal copy of the KRAS gene and a mutation within the PIK3CA gene, making her eligible for this study. She is willing and able to swallow capsules and has no surgical or anatomical condition that would prevent her from taking oral medication. She has given written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who was referred to the pulmonary hypertension clinic at the institution. He has a history of progressive shortness of breath and chest pain for the last 6 months. He is a current smoker with a pack-year history of 20. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Upon evaluation, he was found to have an elevated systolic pulmonary artery pressure of 55 mmHg by echocardiogram. He was scheduled for a right heart catheterization as part of his diagnostic workup for pulmonary hypertension. His laboratory results were within normal limits, with a creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. He underwent the right heart catheterization, which revealed an elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure of 40 mmHg and a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 12 mmHg. He was then referred for a pulmonary CT angiography, which will be performed as part of the clinical trial to assess lung perfusion using dual-energy computed tomography.

A 38-year-old woman presents with a history of difficulty swallowing solid food and has been experiencing this symptom for at least two weeks. She reports a feeling of food getting stuck in her throat, which makes it difficult to swallow. She has also been experiencing heartburn, chest pain and nausea. The patient has been diagnosed with Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE) by endoscopy prior to the screening. She has a history of allergic rhinitis, but no history of hypereosinophilic syndromes or Churg-Strauss vasculitis. She has not participated in any dupilumab (anti-IL-4R) clinical trial before. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not planning to become pregnant during the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old Asian male who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) six months ago during a routine check-up. The patient has no significant past medical history, but he has a family history of liver disease. His most recent lab results show HBsAg+ serology and elevated ALT levels (2.5 times the upper limit of normal). The patient has not received any treatment for CHB in the past 6 months. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is interested in participating in the NASVAC Phase-III trial in CHB patients to explore alternative treatment options to antiviral drugs. He has no history of other hepatic diseases of different etiology, immune suppressive disorders, or administration of immune suppressive-immune modulator drugs. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to provide voluntary informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who works as a software engineer and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She reports occasional discomfort in her upper back and neck region, which she attributes to poor posture and lack of physical activity. She has no history of spinal or thoracic pathologies, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her spine and thoracic mobility and potentially prevent future pain and discomfort.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who had a renal transplant three weeks ago. She was diagnosed with end-stage renal disease secondary to lupus nephritis. She had received induction therapy with basiliximab and maintenance immunosuppression with tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. She had a positive crossmatch with her donor but underwent desensitization therapy with plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) before the transplant. She had an uneventful postoperative course until she developed a fever and worsening serum creatinine levels. A repeat biopsy showed features of antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) with positive C4d staining and donor-specific antibodies (DSA) detected by Luminex® system. She has no history of malignancy, hepatitis or HIV infection. She is not actively taking any investigational drug, and she understands the purpose and risks of the study. She is willing to comply with the required contraception methods during the study and for three months following discontinuation of assigned treatment.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl with a formal diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). She was diagnosed at age 5 by a developmental pediatrician and has since been receiving speech therapy and occupational therapy twice a week. She is currently enrolled in a mainstream school but has difficulty with social communication and interaction with peers. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her parents will be participating in the study as she is under 18 years old. Both parents are fluent in English and have compatible smartphones with the GuessWhat app installed. They are willing to commit to playing the game with their daughter three times a week for four weeks. They are excited to try a new therapy option and hope it will help improve their daughter's social communication skills.

A 68 year old man was recently diagnosed with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after initial treatment with androgen deprivation therapy. He underwent 6 cycles of docetaxel-based chemotherapy with a cumulative dose of 325mg/m2 and achieved disease stabilization without any evidence of progression on imaging according to PCWG2 and modified RECIST 1.1 criteria. His PSA levels were not elevated ≥ 25% and were at least 2 ng/mL above the nadir since start of docetaxel treatment. He is non-surgically castrated and agreed on ongoing use of GnRH analogues (agonists). He has a WHO performance status of 1 and a total testosterone level ≤ 50 ng/dL. His potassium, neutrophils, and platelets are within normal limits, and he has normal kidney and liver function. He has no history of myocardial infarction, thromboembolic events, or arrhythmias of Grade ≥ 3. He has no other malignancy within the last 2 years and has no known hypersensitivity to trial drug or hypersensitivity to any of its components. He is able and willing to swallow study drug as whole tablet and comply with the protocol. He has completed the baseline QL questionnaire and agreed to practice effective barrier contraception or to completely abstain from intercourse. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess the impact of maintenance orteronel on disease progression and its effect on his quality of life.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is currently working as a healthcare worker in a hospital in Paris. He is concerned about contracting COVID-19 due to his exposure to patients with the virus. He is a non-smoker and non-vaper, and has never used any nicotine replacement therapy. He has no history of COVID-19 infection or symptoms suggestive of COVID-19 in the past 14 days. He has not been vaccinated against COVID-19 infection. He does not have any addiction problems to alcohol or other substances. He is not currently taking any medications that would be contraindicated for the use of nicotine patches. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no history of stroke, myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndrome, or any of the other conditions listed as contraindications for the use of nicotine patches. He has a smartphone and is willing to be followed for the duration of the study. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of nicotine in preventing COVID-19 infection.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 4 years ago. He has been treated with two prior lines of therapy but has experienced relapse. His disease is measurable, and he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. He is in good overall health and has no known serious illnesses or medical conditions. He has not received any of the excluded treatments within the specified time frame. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and has agreed to undergo all necessary tests and evaluations. He is not currently taking any investigational agents and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of haemophilia B with a FIX activity below or equal to 2% and a history of at least 150 exposure days to other FIX products. He has been scheduled for major surgery and is currently seeking a safe and effective treatment option to manage his condition during the procedure. The patient has no known history of FIX inhibitors and does not take any immune modulating or chemotherapeutic medication. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of NNC-0156-0000-0009 during surgical procedures.

A 45 year old woman has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C of genotype 4. She has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain and loss of appetite for several months. Her HCV RNA level is over 10,000 IU/mL at screening. She has never been treated with any direct acting anti-HCV agent before. The patient has no history of hepatic decompensation, and no other significant comorbidities or liver disease of non-HCV etiology. She has no co-infection with HIV-1 or HIV-2, and is negative for hepatitis-B-surface-antigen. The patient understands the study requirements and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis for the past 4 years. She is fluent in French and has no cognitive impairment or aphasia. She does not have any substance addiction or psychiatric troubles except for a history of major depression which is currently being treated under the supervision of a psychiatrist. She does not have any other severe neurological or somatic disease, and she is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She reports mild difficulty with mobility and activities of daily living, but still able to perform most tasks independently. She has a supportive family and social network, and she is actively engaged in her profession. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the relationship between disability, perceived social support, and quality of life in multiple sclerosis.

A 55-year-old woman who has recently had a stroke presents with hemiparesis of the upper limb. She is currently hospitalized at Loma Linda East Campus Rehabilitation Hospital. She is able to speak English and manual muscle testing shows at least 2/5 in 3 or more muscle groups in the affected upper limb. She has no active neck pain, headaches, or vertigo that would limit her ability to tolerate a Virtual Reality Head Mounted Device. She has not undergone hemicraniectomy and has no current uncontrolled seizures or active infections requiring contact precautions. She is cognitively able to participate and has no vision loss that would limit her participation in VR therapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) six months ago. She reports experiencing sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping. She has a history of MDD with a previous episode two years ago, which was treated with medication and psychotherapy. She is not currently receiving any treatment for her depression. She is not currently taking any psychotropic medication, herbal preparations, or melatonin. She has no history of substance or alcohol abuse or dependence. She is not currently undergoing psychotherapy. She is using effective contraception and is willing to continue doing so throughout the study. Her CGI-Severity score is 5 at Screening and Baseline. She meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

This is a 32 year old female who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 3 years ago. She presents with symptoms of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and bloody stools. She has tried mesalamine and sulfasalazine in the past without significant improvement. She has no history of colon resection or infectious colitis. She has a history of hypertension and mild osteoporosis, which are being managed with medications. She has no history of cancer or other inflammatory or bleeding disorders of the colon and intestine. She is currently not pregnant and is willing to use effective birth control during the study. She has provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

Pt is a 78yo F with no significant medical history, non-smoker, non-alcoholic who is interested in participating in a study to determine protein requirements in elderly females. She has no history of diabetes, cancer, liver or kidney disease, HIV, acute cold or flu, hypo or hyperthyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis treated with anti-inflammatory medications or other chronic illnesses that could affect protein and amino acid metabolism. The pt reports no significant weight loss in the past month, is not on weight reducing diets, and has no issues with tolerating the diet or having blood drawn from a venous access. The patient does not consume more than 2 cups of coffee per day or more than one drink of alcohol per day. The pt is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV 5 years ago. She has been receiving HIV care at a local clinic and has been adhering to her medications. However, she reports struggling with alcohol use and acknowledges that her drinking has increased during the pandemic. She reports drinking 5-6 drinks per week, usually on the weekends. She reports feeling guilty and ashamed about her drinking and is interested in receiving treatment for it. She has a history of depression, but has been stable on her current medication regimen. She is fluent in English and is not currently experiencing any acute psychiatric symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her reduce her alcohol use and improve her overall health outcomes. Her AUDIT-C score is 6.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of rheumatoid arthritis presents with complaints of shoulder pain and limited mobility. The patient has been diagnosed with RA based on the 1987 revised criteria and has a disease activity score (DAS) of 4.5. There is no history of shoulder trauma or rotator cuff disorders, and the patient has not received any shoulder injections. The patient does not have cervical spondylosis with nerve root compression or cervical symptomatic disc syndromes. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of anterior shoulder ultrasound for assessment of glenohumeral joint synovitis.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision in her left eye for the past 6 months. She has a medical history of hypertension and is currently taking medications for it. She has never had any eye surgeries before and has no history of ocular trauma. Her visual acuity is 20/80 in the affected eye, and the fundus examination shows a stage 3 macular hole. OCT imaging confirms the diagnosis, and the duration of symptoms is within the inclusion criteria. She has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate. Her refractive error is within normal limits, and there is no evidence of any other ocular disease affecting visual function.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. He received first-line platinum-based chemotherapy but relapsed after treatment. The patient has multiple metastases in the lungs and bones, which cannot be re-irradiated or re-operated. He complains of persistent pain in the chest and back and has difficulty breathing. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80 and is able to perform most of his daily activities independently. He has no significant medical history other than smoking for 30 years. The patient is willing to participate in clinical trials and has given informed consent. The laboratory tests show that the patient meets the eligibility criteria, including normal liver and kidney function and adequate bone marrow function. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no history of allergy to recombinant human endostatin.

The patient is a 45-year-old active woman who works as a personal trainer. She has been experiencing pain in her left shoulder for the past 6 months, which has worsened over time. She has difficulty lifting weights and performing overhead activities. She visited her primary care physician, who diagnosed subacromial bursitis and tendinitis. The physician prescribed physical therapy and recommended subacromial corticosteroid injections to relieve the pain. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial comparing two doses of corticosteroid injections as she wants to explore her treatment options and contribute to advancing medical research. She has no history of rotator cuff tear or osteoarthritis and is not pregnant.

47-year-old male with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia. He underwent standard chemotherapy with daunorubicin and cytarabine, but did not achieve complete remission after the first cycle of chemotherapy. He was then diagnosed with core binding factor (CBF) positive AML and was referred for further evaluation. The patient is in good general health with normal vital signs and laboratory results. He has no significant medical history, except for a smoking history of 20 pack-years. The patient has provided consent for the study and has a stored bone marrow specimen available for analysis.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID19. He has moderate symptoms including fever, cough, and body aches. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He has not traveled outside of the country in the past year and has not been in contact with anyone known to have COVID19. His physical exam shows mild tachycardia with a heart rate of 100 bpm and mild tachypnea with a respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. His chest X-ray shows mild bilateral infiltrates. His laboratory studies show a WBC count of 8000/mm3, a platelet count of 200,000/mm3, and a creatinine level of 0.8 mg/dL. He is eligible to participate in the study's main group and will be prescribed favipiravir as part of his treatment regimen.

A 28-year-old female patient visits the dentist complaining of dental sensitivity and gum recession on both sides of her mouth. She is concerned about the appearance of her teeth and wants a solution that will improve the aesthetics of her smile. She has a history of good oral hygiene and has been seeing the dentist regularly for routine check-ups. She is not a smoker and does not have any systemic diseases. Her medical history is unremarkable and she is not taking any medications. A dental examination reveals Miller class I or II recession defects without any signs of periodontal disease. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help improve her condition and is willing to comply with all study-related procedures. She understands the nature of the proposed surgery and is willing to provide a signed informed consent.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (pNET) that has progressed on both everolimus and sunitinib. He has been diagnosed with pNET 2 years ago and has undergone Whipple procedure followed by systemic chemotherapy. Despite the treatment, the disease has progressed with liver and lung metastases. He has also received palliative radiation therapy for bone metastasis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He used to smoke 1 pack of cigarettes per day but quit smoking 6 months ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently retired and lives alone. He has an ECOG performance status of 1.

A 7-year-old girl with a birthmark on her left cheek presents for evaluation and treatment. The birthmark has been present since birth and has gradually increased in size over the years. The patient has expressed concern about the appearance of the birthmark and its impact on her social interactions with peers. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for their child to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a Pulsed Dye Laser treatment for port-wine stain birthmarks.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with early stage breast cancer. The cancer is operable and has been confirmed by cytological examination. She is suitable for breast-conserving surgery and is over the age of 45, making her eligible for the TARGIT clinical trial. She has no history of previous breast cancer or radiation therapy. The patient's medical history is unremarkable for any severe concomitant disease that may limit her life expectancy. She has no known BRCA2 gene mutations, and no concomitant medical treatments are being considered. She is willing and available for regular follow-up visits for at least ten years. The patient has no gross nodal disease, and the cancer is not considered clinically malignant or proven cytologically or by scanning. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets all inclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old non-smoking female diagnosed with Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer which has progressed after prior treatment with erlotinib (Tarceva®). The patient has no history of any other malignancy. She has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale and a life expectancy of at least three months. The patient has no active CNS metastases and has not received major surgery, chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks. She has no severe alterations in serum fasting cholesterol or triglycerides. The patient has not received any investigational drug within the last 4 weeks before the start of therapy. She has no known hypersensitivity to BIBW 2992 or Sirolimus. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 28-year-old female was diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) three years ago. She has been experiencing kidney inflammation and has been taking Prednisone and Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) concurrently since her diagnosis. Despite her current medication regimen, she still experiences fatigue, joint pain, and swelling. She is not pregnant and does not have any underlying medical conditions. She exercises regularly and has a healthy diet. She has no allergies to any food or drugs. She is interested in participating in this study to explore alternative treatment options that may reduce the side effects of Prednisone.

The researchers are looking for participants for a clinical trial examining the effects of aerobic exercise on neuroplasticity in depression. They are seeking individuals aged 18-50 years old who can provide informed consent. Participants with depression must meet the criteria for unipolar depression assessed using the Mini-international Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) and have a Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score of 20 or greater. They must be psychoactive drug free or have maintained a stable dose of up to one antidepressant medication for four weeks prior to study participation. Control participants must not meet criteria for unipolar depression assessed using the MINI, have a MADRS score of 6 or less, and no history or previous diagnosis of depression. Exclusion criteria include primary diagnosis of another Axis 1 disorder, secondary diagnosis of a psychotic disorder, cognitive disorder, substance-related disorder, or obsessive-compulsive disorder, illicit drug use or alcohol abuse, current smoker, history of seizures, other diagnosed neurological or musculoskeletal disorder/injury, uncontrolled cardiovascular or metabolic disease, resting blood pressure > 200mmHg systolic or 100mmHg diastolic, electronic or metal implants, current participation in a structured exercise program, and pregnancy. If you meet these criteria and are interested in participating, please contact the research team for further information.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the tumour has relapsed. The patient is experiencing pain and discomfort in the affected area. The patient's parents are concerned about the limited treatment options available and are willing to explore alternative options. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. The patient is alert, cooperative, and well-nourished. The tumour has been confirmed through pathology and a blood sample has been taken for central germline BRCA testing. The patient is able to swallow tablets and has adequate organ and marrow function. The patient's weight is suitable for obtaining blood samples for safety laboratory assessments and PK analysis. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV infection. He has never received antiretroviral therapy before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare different drug regimens for the initial treatment of HIV infection. He has a viral load of 5,000 copies/ml and is willing to use acceptable means of contraception. He has not taken any NNRTIs or 3TC before and is not currently experiencing peripheral neuropathy of Grade 2 or higher. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not used immunomodulators, vaccines, or investigational therapies within 30 days of study entry. He has no hypersensitivity to components of the study drug formulations and is not currently using drugs or alcohol that would interfere with adherence to study requirements. He is in good overall health and is interested in contributing to HIV research.

A 25-year-old male with a BMI of 22 kg/m², no history of chronic diseases, and not taking any medication presents for a clinical trial examining the effect of human nasal insulin on the dopaminergic system. He gives informed consent and reports no allergies or contraindications for MRI investigation. His HbA1C level is 5.3% and his clinical routine blood parameters are within normal ranges. He is advised that he may be informed of any unexpected clinically relevant findings. He is unaware of the study's randomization and is willing to participate in the trial, which will include fMRI measurements to investigate insulin sensitivity of the central nervous system.

A 56-year-old man was diagnosed with stage III colon cancer and has undergone surgery to remove a tumor. He is now receiving adjuvant chemotherapy treatment. His wife, a 52-year-old woman, has been his primary caregiver since his diagnosis, helping him manage his medications, accompanying him to medical appointments, and providing emotional support. She has been experiencing stress and anxiety related to her husband's illness and treatment, and has noticed changes in her own quality of life. She is fluent in both spoken and written French and has agreed to participate in a study evaluating the burden of care on spouses/partners of patients with colon cancer. She lives with her husband and is available for a one-hour interview.

A 25-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He has no current symptoms or complaints and is not taking any medications or supplements. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 90 days or received any investigational products in the past 5 half-lives or 90 days, whichever is longer. He has not been exposed to more than 4 new chemical entities within the past 12 months. He has no history of hypertension, significant cardiac disease, liver disease, renal disease, bleeding diathesis, or coagulopathy. He does not consume alcohol regularly and is willing to abstain from alcohol for 48 hours prior to the study and throughout the study. He is a non-smoker and has not used any tobacco or nicotine-containing products in the past 3 months. He has no known allergies or sensitivities to any medication or component thereof. His BMI is within the range of 18 to 30 kg/meter-squared, and he weighs more than 50 kg (110 pounds). He has no history of a positive test for hepatitis C antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen, or HIV antibody. His serum creatinine, glomerular filtration rate, albumin to creatinine ratio, and blood in urine levels are within the normal reference range. His Fridericia's QT correction formula is less than 450 milliseconds (msec). He is a male without female partners of child-bearing potential or vasectomy with documentation of azoospermia, and he agrees to meet the contraception requirements from the time of the first dose of study treatment until the last follow-up visit.

A 25-year-old female who exercises regularly presented with a history of experiencing muscle soreness after moderately strenuous exercise. She has no known medical conditions and is in good general health with a BMI of 25. She is sexually active and agrees to use medically acceptable birth control throughout the study and for 30 days following the end of study participation. She is able to read, comprehend, and sign the informed consent form. She reports developing muscle pain/soreness within 24-48 hours of the end of the exercise regimen and has a baseline muscle pain/soreness with movement of 7 on the NRS scale and is rated as "moderate" on the categorical scale. She has no history of allergy or intolerance to any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), aspirin, or acetaminophen. She does not work out or exercise the upper extremities with weights or gym equipment regularly during the past 6 months and does not have a job that requires regular heavy lifting or involvement of the upper extremities. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has not taken any analgesic medication within 5 half-lives of performing the exercise regimen during the run-in period or completing the baseline assessment. She is able to swallow whole or large tablets or capsules and is willing to remain at the study center for the 6-hour inpatient observation period.

A 32-year-old male farmer residing in Magude district, Southern Mozambique, presents with a history of fever, chills, and body aches for the past 3 days. He reports no significant medical history and denies any history of travel outside the district. He has not taken any anti-malarial drugs in the past month. He is married with two children and works in his farm every day. His wife is not pregnant. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. On physical examination, he has a fever of 38.5°C and has mild splenomegaly. A rapid diagnostic test (RDT) is positive for Plasmodium falciparum. His weight is 65 kg. He agrees to participate in the study and is eligible for inclusion.

The patient is a 45-year-old American woman who has been hospitalized with symptoms of COVID-19 for the past 48 hours. She has a confirmed diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection through PCR test. Her oxygen saturation levels are low and she requires supplemental oxygen. She has no significant past medical history or allergies to any study medication. She has not received more than five doses of remdesivir prior to screening, and she has not received monoclonal antibodies targeting cytokines, T-cells or B-cells in the past four weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she agrees to use contraception if needed. She is willing to comply with the planned study procedures and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study. She is willing to be randomized to receive any one of the active arms or placebo. She has not participated in any other blinded clinical trial for the treatment of COVID-19 through Day 29. She is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study drugs. She is eligible for the trial based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 68 year old woman who is in good health and is able to live independently. She has never been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis, cancer, renal disease, COPD, cardiac arrhythmias or decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, lactose or gluten intolerance, inflammatory bowel disease, hyper/hypothyroidism or dementia. She has not suffered from any bone, muscle, tendon or joint injuries that would compromise her ability to participate in exercise regimens. She has not had any implanted magnetic devices that would be incompatible with MRI scanning. She consumes less than 21 units of alcohol per week (1 unit equals 4 g of ethanol) and has not been taking any medication other than acetylsalicylic acid, paracetamol, or thyroid function hormones. She has been exercising for less than 1 hour per week, but has not been engaged in any light activities such as stretching/gymnastics, bike-riding/walking as transportation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to counteract age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian woman who noticed a pigmented lesion on her left upper arm about a month ago. The lesion is 4 mm in diameter and has not changed in size or color. She has no personal or family history of melanoma or other skin cancers. She has fair skin, light eyes, and blonde hair, and has had several sunburns in her lifetime. She works primarily indoors and uses sunscreen when outdoors. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. There is no evidence of trauma or bleeding in the lesion, and it is accessible to the MelaFind hand-held imaging device.

A 67-year-old woman visited the clinic with pain and numbness in her right leg. She is a retired nurse with a history of smoking for 30 years. She quit smoking 5 years ago, but her symptoms started 2 years after quitting. She reports that the pain is worse when walking and improves when she rests. She also reports that her foot feels colder than the other one. The symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few months. She has no history of heart attack or stroke. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are well controlled with medications. She has no history of diabetes. During the physical exam, she had a weak pulse in her right foot. The ankle-brachial index (ABI) was 0.65 on the right and 1.0 on the left. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has a Swedish personal identification number.

Maria is a 62 year old woman who was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer three weeks ago. She underwent surgery for the removal of the tumor and is now following a fast-track recovery program. She has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She currently lives alone but has a supportive network of family and friends. She is fluent in Swedish and has no cognitive dysfunction. She is motivated to be involved in her own health care and is interested in learning more about her recovery process. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help improve patient care for others with similar conditions.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for the past 3 months. She has a family history of colon cancer, with her mother being diagnosed at age 55. She has no personal history of gastrointestinal diseases or cancer. She is not currently taking any medications and does not have any allergies. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no significant medical history and her vital signs are stable. Her bowel movements are regular and she has not experienced any recent changes in bowel habits. She has been scheduled for an endoscopy by her gastroenterologist and is interested in participating in the study.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia presents with difficulty concentrating and retaining information. He struggles with social interaction and has difficulty maintaining relationships. He has been stabilized on an atypical antipsychotic medication for the past 3 months and has not been hospitalized in the past 6 months. He has no history of neurologic illness, traumatic brain injury, or substance dependence. He is able to communicate in English fluently. His IQ is within the normal range. He is seeking intensive outpatient clinical care for his symptoms and is interested in participating in a cognitive remediation study that focuses on improving cognitive function and community function.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is currently on the kidney transplant waitlist. She has been waiting for a kidney transplant for the past 6 months and is very interested in learning more about living donation and kidney paired donation (KPD) as a potential option for receiving a kidney transplant. She speaks both English and Spanish fluently and has completed the initial health screening required for living donation. She has not undergone donor evaluation before and has not participated in any other study to increase her knowledge about living donation or KPD. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about the risks and benefits of living donation and KPD and to make an informed decision about her options for kidney transplantation.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with end-stage kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis. She has been on hemodialysis for the past 3 years and has been experiencing anemia for the last 6 months. Her hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL, and her ferritin level is 600 mg/dL. She has been taking oral iron supplements with no improvement in her anemia. Her current ESA dose is 1000 IU twice a week. She has no known allergies to iron supplements. She has not received a blood transfusion in the last 4 weeks. She is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to try a different form of iron supplementation.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty achieving and maintaining erections during sexual activity. He has had this problem for the past 6 months and it has been causing him significant distress. He has not taken any phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5) inhibitors such as sildenafil citrate, vardenafil or tadalafil within the past 4 weeks. The patient is generally healthy, does not smoke, and has no significant medical history. He is sexually active and has a regular partner. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of sildenafil citrate on the hardness of his erections.

A 57-year-old Caucasian male presents with abdominal discomfort and unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds in the last 3 months. He has no history of gastrointestinal disorders or surgeries. He is a non-smoker and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass in the epigastrium. CT scan of the abdomen shows a 2.5 cm solid mass in the pancreas. He is referred to the University of Arkansas Medical for Sciences for an EUS-guided biopsy of the mass. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of two different needles for EUS-guided biopsy of solid mass lesions. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 30-year-old Japanese man with no significant medical history. He is currently not taking any prescription drugs or supplements, including St. John's Wort. He has no history of alcohol abuse, and reports consuming alcohol only occasionally, with an intake of less than 10 units per week. He has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and a resting pulse and heart rate within the normal range. He is able to read and understand the informed consent form for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55 year old African American male with a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion for the past 6 months. He visited his primary care physician and underwent a stress test which revealed reversible ischemia. He was referred to a cardiologist who performed additional testing including coronary angiography and confirmed the diagnosis of microvascular angina. He has been experiencing symptoms despite medical therapy and is now considering enrollment in a clinical trial. He is a retired construction worker and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He is married and lives with his wife in a suburban area. He is interested in participating in the trial to help advance medical knowledge and potentially improve his own symptoms.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD). She has been taking an antidepressant for several months with limited success in managing her symptoms. She experiences feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She also has difficulty sleeping and concentrating on tasks. She is currently an outpatient and is seeking additional treatment options to help manage her symptoms. The patient has no history of bipolar disorder, psychotic disorder, or post-traumatic stress disorder. She has no history of suicide attempts or significant risk of suicide or homicide. There is no known history of renal insufficiency or impairment, and she has no conditions that could affect absorption or metabolism. The patient is willing to provide informed consent before starting any study-related procedures.

A 29-year-old woman in her 23rd week of pregnancy was referred to the obstetrics clinic with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. She had no significant medical history and was not on any medications. Physical examination revealed pallor and tachycardia. Laboratory investigations showed a hemoglobin level of 9.8g/dL and ferritin level of 10 ng/dL, consistent with iron deficiency anemia. She was diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia and was recommended to participate in a clinical trial comparing lactoferrin versus ferrous sulphate for treatment. She is carrying a single fetus and has no history of chronic medical disorders, bleeding disorders or anemia requiring blood transfusion. She is not hypersensitive to iron preparations nor has any haemoglobinopathies. She is willing to participate in the study and is currently in her 23rd week of pregnancy.

A 32-year-old female diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) is seeking to participate in a clinical trial examining the effects of treadmill walking exercise training versus stretching-and-toning activities on learning and memory outcomes, hippocampal volume and resting-state functional connectivity, and cardiorespiratory fitness in fully-ambulatory individuals with MS who have impairment in learning new information. The patient is fully-ambulatory with an EDSS score of 2.5, indicating some difficulty with walking but able to do so unaided. She has demonstrated a significant impairment in learning new information based on open-trial Selective Reminding Task scores at least 1.5 standard deviations below the normative score for healthy controls. The patient is relapse-free and has not taken corticosteroids for at least 30 days. She has no history of major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder I or II, or substance-abuse disorders, and is not taking medications that can affect cognition. The patient is right-handed and has corrected vision better than 20/80. She has no known cardiovascular, metabolic, or renal disease and is asymptomatic. The patient has scores on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) of 25, indicating no decisional impairment. She is on a stable disease-modifying therapy regimen and has a low risk for contraindications for MRI. The patient is not pregnant and is not engaging in ≥ 150 min of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week, nor is she actively engaging in cognitive rehabilitation or participating in regular brain fitness activities. Her systolic blood pressure values are < 200 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure values are < 110 mmHg at rest.
