57 year old male admitted to the Medical ICU with a diagnosis of sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The patient has been intubated and started on mechanical ventilation. Enteral access has been established via a nasogastric tube for nutritional support. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. The patient's current medications include insulin, metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. The patient's BMI is 30, indicating obesity. The patient's estimated caloric needs based on the Harris-Benedict equation is 2200 kcal/day. The patient has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

A 45-year old female diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma two years ago. She received chemotherapy as her primary treatment, which initially showed a good response. However, the cancer relapsed after six months of completing chemotherapy

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been experiencing radiating pain in his right upper limb for the past 4 months. The pain started as a dull ache in his neck and shoulder, but gradually progressed to a sharp, shooting pain down his arm. He also experiences tingling and numbness in his fingers and has difficulty gripping objects. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy but has not noticed any significant improvement. He has a positive Spurling's test, indicating cervical nerve root compression. He has no history of traumatic injury to his upper limb or cervical spine and does not have any circulatory disturbances in his upper extremity. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of neural mobilization with or without soft tissue mobilization in cervical radiculopathy.

A 68-year-old man presents with a recent diagnosis of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in his left eye. He has experienced a significant decline in his vision, making it difficult for him to perform daily activities such as reading, driving, and recognizing faces. His ophthalmologist has recommended EYLEA treatment to improve his vision and overall quality of life. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has agreed to provide informed consent and is registered to the Special drug use investigation of EYLEA for AMD (Trial Number 15858). The patient will be evaluated using the Japanese version (v.1.4 - interviewer administered format) of National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire-25 (NEI VFQ-25) at baseline and at the 6 and 12 months after the start of EYLEA treatment to assess the effect of the medication on his quality of life.

The patient is a 31-year-old woman who has been struggling with cocaine abuse for the past year. She reports using smoked cocaine at least twice a week and spending approximately $100 per week on the drug. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has never been diagnosed with a seizure disorder or heart disease. She is willing to comply with study procedures and agrees to practice an effective form of contraception. She has no current or recent history of significant violent or suicidal behavior. She is not pregnant or lactating. Her clinical laboratory tests are within normal limits.

Mr. Johnson is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and quit smoking two years ago. He has noticed increased coughing, wheezing and shortness of breath over the past few months. He is currently on maintenance therapy with an inhaler but continues to experience symptoms. He has no other significant medical history, is not taking any other medications, and has not been hospitalized in the past year. He is able to walk a few blocks before becoming short of breath. Mr. Johnson is interested in participating in the study to help improve his symptoms and reduce his risk of cardiovascular disease. He is able and willing to attend all required visits and comply with the study requirements. He speaks English fluently and is able to give informed consent.

A 9-year-old girl was diagnosed with leukemia 6 months ago and has been receiving high-dose methotrexate treatment. She experiences frequent physical and emotional distress during the treatment, which has affected her quality of life. The girl's legal guardians are concerned about the efficacy of symptom relief and the child's overall wellbeing. The healthcare professionals in charge of the child's care are also interested in finding better ways to assess and manage the child's symptoms. The girl is able to understand a numeric rating scale (NRS) and has a cognitive level of approximately five years. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates a new digital communication tool for children undergoing cancer treatment, which aims to decrease the child's self-reported distress and increase person-centredness during treatment. The family has been informed about the hybrid design of the study, where the child will participate twice, once as a control and once with the e-health support Pictorial support in Person-centered care for children (PicPecc). The girl's legal guardians and healthcare professionals will also be involved in the study, providing feedback on the process evaluation.

A 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with liver cancer and is scheduled to undergo hepatectomy at the main campus of the University of Texas (UT)-MD Anderson Cancer Center. The patient has a history of mild cognitive impairment and is currently being treated with a neuropsychiatric medication. The patient is an English speaker and is able to provide informed consent as determined by his attending physician. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve the assessment of mental capability in patients undergoing liver surgery.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female, with a BMI of 22. She has no known medical conditions and takes no regular medication. The patient has not participated in any clinical studies in the past 3 months or taken any marketed drugs in the past 30 days. She has no history of Raynaud's disease or peripheral vascular disease. The patient does not have any symptoms of postural hypotension or suicidal ideation. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient is a non-smoker and has negative results for HIV and Hepatitis B and C, as well as a negative urinary drug screen. She does not have any allergies to clonidine or any of its excipients or milk or milk derivatives. She is available to attend all study visits and will comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male who works as an office manager. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and is not planning to participate in any other clinical trials during the present trial period. He is not known to have any chronic illness or history of anaphylactic reaction or asthma. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive therapy or long-term systemic corticosteroid therapy. He has not received any blood or blood-derived products in the past 3 months. He is not known to have seropositivity for HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C, and has normal platelet counts. He is not living in a household with children <5 years of age. He is willing to use an effective method of contraception or abstain from sexual activity for at least 4 weeks prior to the first vaccination until 4 weeks after the last vaccination, as he is a man of child-bearing potential. He has not received any pneumococcal vaccine in the past 5 years and has no history of pneumococcal infection within the same period. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures.

26 yo F with regular menstrual cycle and stable body weight. No history of dietary supplement use containing iron or folic acid within the past month. No history of acute or chronic inflammatory disease or connective tissue disease. Non-smoker, non-drinker, and no history of drug abuse. Not on a vegetarian diet. No current pregnancy or lactation. Patient has expressed interest in participating in the study to help contribute to scientific research on the bioavailability of iron and folic acid during simultaneous supplementation. Consent has been obtained and the patient is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits.

A 45-year-old female was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 10 years ago. She has been using the Omnipod for the past 5 years and is currently on Humalog insulin. She has a history of severe hypoglycemia in the past 6 months, but it was related to an intercurrent illness. She is fluent in English and has no unresolved skin conditions in the area of sensor or pump placement. She is willing to wear the system continuously throughout the study and is willing to use the Dexcom App on the Omnipod Horizon™ PDM as the sole source of Dexcom data. She is able to sign the Informed Consent Form and has no plans to participate in another clinical study using an investigational drug or device other than Omnipod Horizon™.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic cancer. He underwent diagnostic imaging which showed a 5 cm tumor involving the pancreatic head and encasing the celiac artery, as well as involvement of several peripancreatic lymph nodes. He has no history of other malignancies and has not received any prior treatment for pancreatic cancer. His physical exam is unremarkable except for mild epigastric tenderness. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. His laboratory values, including CBC, liver function tests, and renal function tests, are normal. He has no contraindications to chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study. He is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. He is interested in exploring all possible treatment options for his cancer.

58-year-old female with a history of ischemic stroke six months ago resulting in mild to moderate weakness in her right arm and leg. She is currently undergoing physical therapy twice a week but has not seen significant improvement in her motor function. She has no history of epilepsy or major health conditions, and is not taking any alcohol, recreational drugs, or medications that would contraindicate tDCS. She has no metal in her head and is able to understand and complete behavioral tasks required for the study. She is not pregnant and does not have a pacemaker.

The patient is a 68-year-old man with a medical history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease. He was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding, including abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and bloody stools. The patient's hemoglobin level was low, and he was transferred to the endoscopy unit for further evaluation. The endoscopy identified a bleeding gastric ulcer, and the medical team decided to use Hemospray® to achieve hemostasis. The patient was treated with Hemospray®, and immediate hemostasis was achieved. He was monitored for rebleeding and discharged after his condition stabilized. The patient's current medication includes amlodipine and lisinopril for hypertension, and he is compliant with his medication regimen. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide informed consent.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of recurrent urothelial bladder cancer that has metastasized to her liver. She has already undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with platinum-based drugs, but the disease has progressed despite treatment. Her tumor has been confirmed to be HER2-positive, with immunohistochemistry showing that at least 30% of the tumor cells overexpress HER2. She reports pain in her right upper abdominal quadrant and has lost significant weight in the past few months. A recent CT scan has confirmed the presence of multiple liver metastases, and a biopsy of one of the metastases has been taken for confirmation of HER2 overexpression. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant cardiac history. Her LVEF is currently at 55%. She has no history of brain metastasis or other significant comorbidities. She understands that there are no standard treatment options available for her at this point, and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore other options.

A 58 year old male smoker presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for 3 months. Imaging studies reveal a right lung mass that is biopsy-proven to be non-small cell lung cancer. Further staging workup reveals stage IIIA disease with no distant metastasis. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy to the chest, immunotherapy, or biologic therapy. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, including adequate hematologic, renal, and liver function. The patient is willing to participate in the study and signs the informed consent.

A 57-year-old man was diagnosed with liver carcinoma after experiencing abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and weight loss for several weeks. The patient underwent imaging tests that revealed several hypervascular liver tumours and an α-fetoprotein level of 450 ng/ml. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of liver carcinoma. The patient is not eligible for surgery, liver transplantation, local ablation techniques or chemoembolisation. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, adequate organ function, and a Child Pugh score of A. The patient has not been exposed to anti-IGF-1R class compound and is not eligible for sorafenib therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed an approved informed consent form.

Maria is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is a non-smoker and her BMI is 29 kg/m2. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She has been scheduled for an elective breast cancer surgery, and her surgeon has recommended she participate in a clinical trial to assess the function of her heart preoperatively.  Maria has provided informed consent and will undergo a preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) to assess biventricular function, left ventricular filling pressures, and level of venous return. Additionally, her Troponin T, NT-proBNP, and ECG will be collected as part of the trial.  Maria is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that the results will help improve the understanding and management of hypovolemia and heart failure in non-cardiac surgeries.

This is a 65 year-old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled to undergo a robotic prostatectomy. Due to his medical history, he is considered to be at a high risk for aspiration during the procedure. He has no history of gastroesophageal reflux disease or any other gastrointestinal disorder. The patient is currently taking tamsulosin for his benign prostatic hyperplasia. He has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient B is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and changes in bowel movements for the past 6 months. She has a family history of colon cancer, and her doctor recommended that she undergo a colonoscopy. She has never had a colonoscopy before and feels anxious about the procedure. She works as a teacher and enjoys spending time with her family and pets. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her BMI is 27 and she does not take any analgesics or opioids on a daily basis. She is able to complete the questionnaire and has given her written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 65-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and swelling in her legs. She has a history of chronic heart failure and is currently on oral diuretics. She reports that her symptoms have been getting progressively worse over the past week, despite taking her medication as prescribed. On examination, her jugular venous pressure (JVP) was elevated and she had bilateral lower extremity edema. Chest X-ray showed pulmonary congestion. She was started on IV diuretics and her electrolyte levels were monitored twice daily. She has type 2 diabetes and her HgA1C is 7.5%. She has been diagnosed with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and is currently taking an ACE inhibitor, beta-blocker, and aldosterone antagonist. Her serum sodium level on admission was 136 mmol/L and her serum potassium level was 4.2 mmol/L. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate is 45 mL/min/1.73m². She has had two hospitalizations for heart failure in the past year. She is eligible for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria of having acute decompensated heart failure and actively being diuresed, and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with melasma for the past year. She has irregular light brown to dark brown patches of hyperpigmentation on her face, particularly on her cheeks and forehead. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and serums but has not seen any significant improvement. She is not pregnant and is not currently taking oral contraceptives. She has no history of hypertrophic scars or keloids and has never had herpes infection. She is mentally capable of giving informed consent for the clinical trial. She is hopeful that this trial will provide effective treatment for her melasma.

A 28-year-old male athlete presents with a history of chronic hip and groin pain that has been troubling him for over three months. He describes the pain as a dull ache that worsens during activity and is accompanied by stiffness and a limited range of motion. He also reports experiencing anterior and/or medial groin pain during the FADIR test with a pain severity of ≥2/10 on NRS. The patient has been previously diagnosed with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAIS) based on radiological findings of cam morphology defined as alpha angle >55° on a lateral view. The patient is excluded if he has inguinal-related groin pain diagnosed according to Doha Agreement or pubic-related groin pain diagnosed according to Doha Agreement. The patient must not have evidence of pre-existing hip osteoarthritis, defined as a joint space width <3 mm at the lateral sourcil on anterior-posterior pelvic radiograph. The patient must not have previous hip pathology such as Perthes' disease, slipped upper femoral epiphysis, hip dysplasia defined as a Lateral Center Edge Angle <25°, or avascular necrosis. Other causes of hip and groin pain identified by the orthopedic surgeon during the clinical examination, such as stress fracture of the femoral neck, referred pain from the facet joint, referred pain from the sacroiliac joint, or other competing diagnosis (rheumatoid arthritis, cancer etc.) are also excluded. The patient must not have previous hip injury such as acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral neck fracture, nor undergone previous intra- or extra-articular hip surgery. The patient must not be pregnant and must not have had an intra-articular steroid hip injection during the preceding 3 months. The patient is an ideal candidate for this clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of 12-weeks of semi-structured and supervised physiotherapist-led treatment on self-reported hip and groin function in patients with FAIS with and without intra-articular hip pain. The patient will undergo an ultrasound-guided intra-articular anesthetic hip injection to determine if intra-articular hip pain is present before commencing treatment. The primary outcome measure is the between-group (intra-articular pain vs. no intra-articular pain) difference in mean change of the HAGOS sport subscale from baseline (week 0) to follow-up (week 12).

Siri is a 4-year-old girl living with her parents in Nakhon Pathom province, Thailand. She attends a daycare center and enjoys playing with other children. Her parents reported to the center that they have concerns about her weight as she seems to be gaining weight rapidly. Siri's diet consists of rice, vegetables, and meat. She drinks milk and water regularly. She has no known chronic diseases, and her parents reported no ongoing medical treatments that could affect her body composition. Siri's height and weight measurements fall under the study protocol, and she is selected as a participant for the study. The study aims to investigate the quality and quantity of dietary intake in preschool children and assess their body composition using the deuterium dilution technique. Siri's nutritional status falls under the overweight/obese category, and the study hypothesis is that she will have more fat mass compared to children with normal nutritional status.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who experienced a stroke 9 months ago resulting in severe hemiparesis of the right hand. She has been experiencing spasticity and difficulty controlling the movement of her affected hand. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in a new rehabilitation approach to improve her condition. She has not received botulinum toxin injections or any new anti-spasticity medication within the past 6 months. The patient does not have hemispatial neglect or apraxia and has no history of seizure disorder or other major health impairment. She is willing to make several visits per week to the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago to participate in the treatment sessions and evaluations.

The patient is a 46-year-old female who has been married to her husband for 15 years. Her husband, who is 48 years old, has recently been diagnosed with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). She reports that her husband snores loudly during the night and frequently wakes up gasping for air. As a result, she has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has noticed an increase in irritability and fatigue during the day. She has not been diagnosed with OSA herself and does not use any specific treatment for sleep disorders. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively and is not taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the impact of three months of treatment with nasal CPAP or nasal strips on her cardiovascular function, sleep duration, and sleep quality. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all follow-up appointments.

A 52-year-old woman from Piedmont, Italy, received an invitation letter to participate in a clinical trial comparing Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) versus conventional Digital Mammography (DM) in a population-based screening program. She has a family history of breast cancer, but no personal history of the disease or breast implants. She is asymptomatic and regularly attends the regional breast cancer screening program. She is interested in participating in the trial to learn more about the diagnostic performance of these screening methods and contribute to the advancement of breast cancer detection. She has no terminal illness and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been treated with insulin for the past 5 years, with no previous hypoglycemic episodes. He has also been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (eGFR of 33 ml/min) and is on medication for hypertension and dyslipidemia. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He lives alone and works as a truck driver. He has no known allergies. The patient has experienced occasional palpitations and shortness of breath, but no syncope or chest pain. His electrocardiogram (ECG) showed sinus rhythm with no significant abnormalities. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male veteran who served in Iraq. He is currently experiencing prolonged grief disorder (PGD) after losing his close friend during a combat mission. The patient reports feeling persistent sadness, guilt, and a sense of disbelief about his friend's death. He also experiences intrusive thoughts and memories of the traumatic event, which has significantly impacted his daily functioning. He has tried various treatments for depression and PTSD in the past, but none of them have been effective in addressing his PGD symptoms. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the efficacy of an experimental treatment (BATE-G) for PGD in Veterans with the current standard of care treatment.

As a clinical trial specialist, I must inform you that this study is looking for elite weightlifters who have been training for at least five sessions per week with 90 to 120 minutes per session and have more than 3 years of experience in Olympic weightlifting. Participants should not have used any antioxidants or anti-inflammatory medications during the experimentation period and one month before, and should not have had any injuries during the experimentation period and one month before. If you meet these criteria and are interested in participating in this study, please contact the research team for further information.

A 52-year-old woman visited the clinic with a complaint of eye discomfort. She reported experiencing a burning and gritty sensation in her eyes for the past month, especially in the evening. She also noted that her eyes felt tired and sensitive to light. She had no history of eye surgery and had not used contact lenses in the past month. She denied having any eye infections or inflammation but reported using artificial tears occasionally. She had no known allergies to cornstarch or Dacron. She had not used any topical ophthalmic medications, including artificial tears, for at least 2 hours before the appointment. She had not taken any oral doxycycline, corticosteroids, or immunomodulators in the past month. She had no history of uveitis or blockage of the lacrimal drainage system. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the InflammaDry device for detecting dry eye.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of fatigue, abdominal discomfort and nausea for the past 3 months. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. Her BMI is 32. She has never been pregnant and is using a reliable method of contraception. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and her heart rate is 75 beats per minute. Her physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory investigations reveal elevated liver enzymes (ALT: 70 U/L, AST: 60 U/L) and a positive HCV antibody test. Further testing confirms the presence of HCV genotype 4 and a viral load of 1.2 million IU/mL. A liver biopsy shows mild portal inflammation and mild fibrosis (stage F1). She has no evidence of other liver diseases or co-infection with HIV or HBV. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, alcohol or substance abuse. She is willing to participate in the trial and follow the treatment protocol.

Patient is a 28-year-old male who recently returned from a trip to Thailand. He has been experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea for the past 2 weeks. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His BMI is 22, BP: 118/72, HR: 82/min. Stool test results show the presence of B. hominis and no other pathogenic micro-organism. He has no fever, bloody diarrhea, or weight loss. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 10-month-old baby boy was referred to the clinic for tympanostomy tube insertion as a treatment for Chronic Otitis Media with Effusion (COME). He has been experiencing recurrent ear infections since he was 3 months old. He is bottle-fed and has a normal birth weight. He sleeps in a crib in his own room and wakes up once at night for feeding. He has no history of snoring or sleep disordered breathing (SDB). He has no chronic medical conditions and is not referred for TTI and adenoidectomy/tonsillectomy. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. His parents are both in good health and have no history of sleep disorders.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia two years ago and received an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) from a geno-identical family donor. After a period of remission, the patient has recently experienced a molecular relapse of the disease. The patient's previous DLI has brought a total dose of 6.5 x 10^6 CD3+/kg, however, it was ineffective in controlling the disease. The patient has not developed acute GVHD or extensive chronic GVHD since the first DLI and is not receiving immunosuppressive therapy for the treatment of GVHD or any other reason. The patient has a good performance status, with an OMS score of 1. The patient has no history of severe infection and is not under legal protection. The patient has given informed consent to the study and is insured by a social security system. The patient's donor is the initial HSC donor, a geno-identical family donor, who weighs more than 20kg and has no contra-indications for donating blood. The donor has negative serology for HIV1-2, HBV, HCV, HTLV 1 and VDRL/TPHA in the 30 days prior to apheresis, and has given an oral non-opposition to the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has recently suffered from a stroke caused by bleeding in the central nervous system. He has noticed a sudden onset of symptoms such as weakness on one side of his body and difficulty speaking. The symptoms started about 5 hours ago. Prior to the stroke, he had no history of chronic illness or significant medical conditions. He was fully functional and independent. The patient is alert and cooperative, but has some difficulty communicating due to slurred speech. There is significant weakness on his left side, and he has difficulty moving his left arm and leg. The patient is not unconscious and is able to understand and follow instructions. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is not known to have any severe kidney disorder, alcohol or illicit drug abuse, or dependence. He is willing to participate in the study and meet all the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

A 50 year old woman has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is scheduled for a cardiac surgery. She has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy with no significant medical or psychiatric conditions. She has never participated in a clinical study before and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is post-menopausal and has no child bearing potential. She is willing and able to attend follow-up visits as needed per protocol. The surgeon has determined that she is at risk for poor hemostasis and may benefit from the ArterX surgical sealant as a hemostatic agent.

A 45 year old male was brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident with multiple injuries. He was intubated due to respiratory distress and admitted to the Trauma/Surgical Intensive Care Unit. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no previous surgeries. The patient is currently receiving mechanical ventilation and is following the institutional sedation protocol. He is expected to receive sedation for more than 24 hours after randomization. The patient has not been treated per the institutional traumatic brain injury protocol and has not received continuous infusion of a neuromuscular blocking agent. His heart rate and mean arterial pressure are stable with no need for vasopressors. The patient has not received other alpha-2 agonists within 24 hours of randomization. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible for enrollment.

A 45-year-old African American woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 10 years, on hydroxychloroquine therapy for the past 5 years, came to the ophthalmology clinic for a routine screening appointment. She had no complaints regarding vision or ocular symptoms. Her systemic lupus erythematosus had been stable, and she was currently on a maintenance dose of hydroxychloroquine (400 mg/day). Her past medical history was also significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were well controlled with medications. She had no known drug allergies. She had never had any ocular surgeries and had no family history of ocular disease. Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes, and anterior segment examination was unremarkable. Her dilated fundus examination revealed mild perifoveal parafoveal retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) changes bilaterally. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed normal macular thickness with a preserved foveal contour. She was enrolled in this clinical trial to assess the ocular toxicity in patients on high dose hydroxychloroquine.

A 35 year old man came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has a normal BMI, with no history of any significant medical conditions. He has no family history of diabetes or any other metabolic disorders. His liver and renal function tests, as well as his blood count, are all within normal ranges. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the role of KP-10 on insulin secretion in healthy men. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

Patient B is a 35-year-old female who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis five years ago. She has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, numbness, and tingling sensations in her limbs, as well as difficulty with coordination and balance. She has been receiving treatment with interferon beta-1a injections for the past two years. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. Her current EDSS score is 5.5. She is able to read and comprehend information written in English and is willing to provide a venous blood sample for genetics research and in vitro ligand binding assay. She is of non-childbearing potential and is willing to follow contraception guidelines. She has not participated in any previous research or medical protocol involving nuclear medicine, PET, or radiological investigations with radiation exposure. She has no family history of cancer and does not have any physical abnormality or functional disability that prevents her from acquiring a suitable position for scanning. She is willing and able to follow all procedures outlined in the protocol.

A 45 year old woman complains of burning, tingling and shooting pain in her feet for the past 6 months. She was previously diagnosed with peripheral neuropathy following a peripheral nerve injury. She has been taking painkillers, but the pain is still moderate in intensity (NRS 4). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new therapy for her pain. She has not used a lidocaine patch in the test area in the last 6 months and has no contraindications for capsaicin application. She speaks German fluently and is able to understand the study protocol.

The patient is a 60 year old man who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome. He underwent cardiac catheterization which revealed triple vessel disease and he subsequently underwent coronary artery bypass graft surgery. He is currently recovering in the medical ICU and is intubated and mechanically ventilated. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and insulin. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg and his heart rate is 80 bpm. He is alert and oriented and able to communicate via writing. He has no known history of reactive airway disease or congestive heart failure.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF) diagnosed five years ago. He has been on oral anticoagulation therapy (OAC) for the past two years due to his high CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3. He has had no history of stroke or systemic embolism (SE). Recently, he has been experiencing recurrent episodes of AF despite being on OAC therapy. His cardiologist has recommended catheter ablation for AF as a treatment option. The patient has agreed and is scheduled for the procedure in two weeks. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history.

A 68-year-old man with a clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease visited the clinic for this clinical trial. He had a CT scan within the last year, which showed no significant changes in his brain. He has been taking donepezil for the past 6 months, and the dose has been stable for the last 3 months. He has no history of cerebrovascular disease or myocardial infarction in the last 6 months. He is married for 45 years and lives with his wife. He has two children who live in a different state. He was an engineer and retired 5 years ago. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no history of allergies or any other significant medical conditions. He is excited about participating in this study and hopes that it will help him and others who suffer from Alzheimer's disease.

A 30-year-old Chinese woman visited the clinic with symptoms of depression. She has had these symptoms for the past 6 months, including feelings of sadness, loss of interest in pleasurable activities, difficulty sleeping, lack of energy, and suicidal thoughts. She has no history of psychiatric illness, and this is her first episode of depression. She is currently not on any medication and has not received any treatment previously. She is married, has no children, and works as a teacher. She has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 57-year-old female who has been diagnosed with lung cancer and requires a pulmonary resection by open thoracotomy. She has an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical status of II and has no history of shoulder pain on the operative side. The patient has no known allergies to NSAIDs, sulfonamides, or parecoxib, and has no history of hepatic or renal impairment. She is not currently experiencing any gastrointestinal symptoms, fluid retention, or congestive heart failure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to understand the numeric rating scale despite preoperative coaching.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who is scheduled to undergo a surgical procedure under general anesthesia. He has a body-mass index of 26 kg/m2 and his ASA Physical Status is 2. He has no history of serious skin lesions or vascular disease in the arms, and he is not currently experiencing any fever or infection. The surgery is expected to be performed in a supine and neutral position.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty with digestion and has been referred for further evaluation. He has no prior history of gastrointestinal disease and has an average bowel movement frequency of at least once every 48 hours. He has no history of tobacco or alcohol use within the past 24 hours. He has a BMI of 29, showing he is overweight but not obese. He has no allergies to the components of the test meal. He is in otherwise good health and is able to comply with the requirements of the study. The trial is suitable for his age group, and he is willing to participate in the study to receive a diagnosis and potentially guide his medical treatment.

This is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. She has been on stable CPAP therapy for the past six months and has been compliant, averaging over 4 hours of use nightly. Her diagnostic polysomnogram showed an apnea hypopnea index of 25/hour of sleep, with a sleep efficiency of 82%. She has no other primary sleep disorders, allergies to mask materials or contraindications as listed on product labeling. She is willing to give written informed consent and is able to adhere to the visit schedule. She has no other medical conditions that would render her participation at risk.

A 68-year-old German-speaking man recently diagnosed with prostate cancer is scheduled for an elective radical prostatectomy. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril for it. He does not have any history of cerebrovascular disease or preexisting cognitive impairment. He is retired and lives with his wife who will provide support during his recovery. He is able to independently perform activities of daily living and is physically active, regularly going for walks and participating in light exercise. He reports occasional forgetfulness but denies any other cognitive issues. He is looking forward to the surgery and hopes to return to his normal routine as soon as possible.

A 52-year-old male patient was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of chest pain that started 6 hours ago. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no prior history of myocardial infarction. The ECG revealed ST-segment elevation in leads V1 to V3 and he was diagnosed with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient was given aspirin, heparin, and ticagrelor and underwent emergent coronary angiography. The angiography showed a single vessel disease in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery with thrombus formation and TIMI flow grade 0. The patient was deemed eligible for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and enrolled in the clinical trial. The patient is able to verbally confirm their understanding of the risks, benefits, and treatment alternatives of receiving intracoronary abciximab and/or aspiration thrombectomy. The patient has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to any of the medications used in the trial. The patient's hemogram shows Hb>10g/dL and PLT count >100,000/μL. The patient has no history of bleeding diathesis or known coagulopathy and is willing to receive blood transfusions if needed. The patient has not experienced any gastrointestinal or genitourinary bleeding within the last 3 months and has not undergone major surgery within the last 2 months. The patient does not have severe LV systolic dysfunction or cardiogenic shock. The patient does not have any non-cardiac co-morbid conditions with a life expectancy less than 1 year or that may result in protocol non-compliance. The patient is not actively participating in another drug or device investigational study that has not completed the primary endpoint follow-up period.

The patient is a 55-year-old Taiwanese woman diagnosed with breast cancer 6 months ago. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She reports difficulties sleeping at night and feels fatigued during the day. She has a history of hypertension and is taking medication for that. She is able to understand Mandarin Chinese and is interested in participating in the study. She has a good understanding of the study's intent and gives informed consent to participate. She scores 29 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and has a score of 50 on the Berg Balance Scale test. She is able to walk and does not refuse to participate.

9-year-old girl with a diagnosis of polyarticular-course juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) based on International League of Associations for Rheumatology classification. She has been on methotrexate (MTX) therapy for the past year, but her symptoms have not been well controlled. The treating physician has recommended switching her to tocilizumab (TCZ) therapy. The patient is afebrile and has no history of active systemic infection. She has no history of reactivation or new onset of a systemic infection within the last two months of her screening visit. The patient does not have active uveitis at screening. She has normal hematologic, renal, and liver function. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during study conduct as she is of childbearing potential. She is not wheelchair-bound or bedridden and has no history of alcohol, drug, or chemical abuse within the last six months.

A 54-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She had a history of endometrial cancer and had undergone surgery and chemotherapy. However, her cancer recurred and she received one line of platinum-based systemic chemotherapy. Imaging studies revealed metastasis to the liver and lungs. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. She has adequate hepatic, renal, heart, and hematologic functions, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2.5×109/L, platelet count of 90×109/L, and hemoglobin of 110 g/L. Her total bilirubin is within 1.5×the upper limit of normal, and her serum transaminase is ≤2.5×Upper Limit Of Normal. Her serum creatine is ≤1.5 x Upper Limit Of Normal, and her creatinine clearance rate is ≥50ml/min. Her International Normalized Ratio is <1.5 x Upper Limit Of Normal, urinary protein is ≤（+）and Thyroid stimulating hormone is ≤ 1.5 x Upper Limit Of Normal. She has not been exposed to any anti-tumor drugs within the past 4 weeks or any anti-PD1 antibody drugs. She has no history of psychiatric drug abuse, dysphrenia, or central nervous system diseases, and her digestive system is functioning normally. She has no active ulcers, intestinal perforation, intractable intestinal obstruction, or history of digestive tract perforation within 28 days prior to enrollment. She does not have uncontrolled hypertension or severe cardiovascular disease, and she has not experienced artery/venous thromboembolic events within the past 6 months. She is negative for active infections such as HIV/AIDS or other serious infectious diseases. She has no active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease and is not receiving systemic hormonal therapy or immunosuppressive therapy. She is willing to use appropriate methods of contraception during the trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has undergone surgery for appendectomy. He is being discharged from the hospital with a prescription for opioid medication. The boy has never taken opioid medication before and his parents are concerned about how to safely manage his pain at home. The family speaks English fluently and is filling the prescription for the opioid medication at Shoppers Drug Mart at The Hospital for Sick Children. They are willing to participate in a study that aims to understand how long children need to use opioid medication after surgery and how to provide safe pain management at home. The follow-up will take place 28 days after discharge from the hospital. The patient has no history of chronic pain and is not being discharged to a rehabilitation facility.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who was born with clubfoot. He underwent casting and corrective surgery at BC Children's Hospital and has since started walking. He is compliant with the treatment protocol and has been attending follow-up appointments regularly. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no allergies or chronic conditions. He lives with his parents and has two older siblings. During the assessment, the child will be asked to stand on the pedobarograph mat and walk across it at his ordinary pace. The assessment is expected to take about 20 minutes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse. He presents with severe abdominal pain and is diagnosed with acute pancreatitis. His serum lipase level is elevated at 4 times the upper limit of normal, and a CT scan confirms the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. He also meets the criteria for SIRS with a temperature of 37.5°C, heart rate of 105 beats/minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths/minute, and WBC count of 13,500/mm3 with 11% of band forms. He has a SpO2 of 95% on room air. He has no evidence of pancreatic necrosis on CECT performed within the last 18 hours. He has no history of cholangitis or any other concurrent clinical condition that would pose an unacceptable health risk while participating in the study. He is not currently receiving any chemotherapy or immunotherapy for any malignancy or autoimmune disease. He has no known history of hepatitis B or C or HIV. He has never undergone organ or hematologic transplant. He has no

The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a known history of sickle cell disease (SCD) with HbSS genotype. She has been experiencing episodes of vaso-occlusive pain crisis frequently for the past few months. She presents with severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever. She was admitted to the hospital for the management of pain and dehydration. Her medical history includes hypertension, asthma, and hypothyroidism. She does not smoke or drink. She is married and has two children. Her medications include hydroxyurea, folic acid, and albuterol inhaler. Her physical examination is remarkable for diffuse abdominal tenderness and decreased bowel sounds. Her laboratory tests show elevated white blood cell count (15.5), hemoglobin level of 8.2, and elevated serum creatinine level (1.5). Her urine output is monitored, and she is started on intravenous fluids and analgesics for pain control. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial and provides informed consent for daily blood and urine collection during her hospital stay and follow-up clinic visits.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old male with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He has no history of congenital or chronic disease and does not present any pathologic symptoms during physical examination. He has not taken any medication that may induce or inhibit drug metabolizing enzymes within the last 30 days, nor has he taken any medication within the last 10 days before the first dose. He has not consumed any abnormal diets, such as grapefruit juice, that may influence the ADME of drugs. The patient has no clinically significant allergic disease, alcohol abuse, or drug hypersensitivity. He has not donated whole blood within the last 60 days, nor has he participated in any other clinical trial within the last 90 days. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is fully informed about the study procedures.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with HIV and tuberculosis. She has a history of heroin use and is being treated for substance use disorder. She is a native of Irkutsk and lives with her partner. She is currently hospitalized for tuberculosis treatment and is awaiting antiretroviral initiation. Her CD4+ cell count is 210 and her viral load is 80,000. She has no other medical comorbidities aside from HIV and tuberculosis. She has no prior history of tuberculosis. She reports occasional alcohol use but has not used heroin since her hospitalization. She is willing to use a mobile phone for research purposes and will be trained on how to use it. She is alert and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of heartburn and acid reflux for the past 3 years. She has tried over-the-counter antacids and H2 receptor antagonists without significant improvement. She experiences a burning sensation in her chest and throat after eating or when lying down. She has not had an upper endoscopy but would like to participate in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options. She has no known allergies or other medical conditions and is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years. He has a recent diagnosis of Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastases to the liver, bones, and lungs. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and he has no history of interstitial lung disease or other active malignancy. The patient has no prior treatment with chemotherapy or EGFR TKI therapy. Genetic testing reveals that the patient has an EGFR exon 19 deletion. The patient has no brain metastases and has not undergone any recent surgical procedures. The patient has adequate hematological, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception as he is fertile. He is able to swallow the formulated product and has no significant bowel resection. The patient consents to participate in the study and is enrolled.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy scheduled for a tonsillectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis. He has a history of mild asthma, which is well-controlled with an inhaler. He has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. The patient is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. He is accompanied by his mother who has given informed consent for the study. The patient has been fasting for 8 hours prior to the surgery as per standard guidelines. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his airway examination shows no abnormalities. The patient is classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I.

This is a 27-year-old female who presented to the emergency room with a fever, headache, and muscle pain. She reported that she had been exposed to stagnant water while on a camping trip in Martinique. Upon further evaluation, she was diagnosed with leptospirosis based on a positive PCR test within the first five days of onset of symptoms. She has agreed to participate in the upcoming clinical trial that aims to study the decreasing kinetics of the leptospiremia during antibiotic treatment of leptospirosis in Martinique. She has national insurance and is willing to comply with the proposed follow-up schedule. She understands the risks and benefits of participation in the study and has given her informed consent.

62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of decreased vision in his left eye presented to the ophthalmology clinic. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled with medications. He reported no history of diabetes, smoking or alcohol use. On evaluation, his visual acuity was 20/40 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. His intraocular pressure was normal bilaterally. On fundus examination, he was found to have epiretinal membrane in the left eye. After discussing the available treatment options, he opted for vitrectomy surgery. He was prescribed NSAIDs for pain control before the surgery. He has no known allergies to any medication. He was instructed to discontinue the use of any other pain medications. He has no history of ocular surgery in the past.

A 10-year-old child diagnosed with de novo ALL who is currently receiving systemic induction chemotherapy with a corticosteroid, vincristine, and a single dose or multiple doses of asparaginase, with or without daunorubicin. The child has a functioning Central Venous Access Device and is able to tolerate oral medication or have it administered via an Nasogastric tube (NGT) or GT tube. The child has not had more than 3 lumbar punctures over the course of the study treatment period and has no prior history of documented DVT or PE in the past 3 months. The child has no known inherited bleeding disorder or coagulopathy and has not undergone major surgery (excluding Central Venous Access Device replacement and bone marrow aspiration and non-open biopsy) within the last 7 days prior to enrollment that may be associated with a risk of bleeding. The child does not have uncontrolled severe hypertension or extreme hyperleukocytosis with WBC counts over 200 x 109/L (200,000/microL) at the time of enrollment. The child has normal liver and renal function and INR and aPTT within the acceptable range. The child has no history of allergy to apixaban or Factor Xa inhibitors, no significant adverse reaction or major bleeding related adverse reaction to other anticoagulant or antiplatelet agents, and no significant drug allergy.

A 28-year-old female who reports feeling extremely anxious and uncomfortable in social situations, especially when meeting new people or being in large groups. She often avoids social events and has difficulty making friends. She has been diagnosed with social phobia according to the DSM-IV criteria. She does not currently suffer from depression or suicidal ideation. She has no history of surgery in the heart or brain, no metals implanted in her body, no dental braces or bridge, and no piercings that can't be taken out. She has no tattoos on her shoulders, arms or back, but has one on her leg which is small enough to not interfere with fMRI scanning. She is willing and able to lie still for about an hour during the scanning process. She is not pregnant and has no history of neurological diseases. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to provide saliva samples for genotyping.

The patient is a 35-year-old Zimbabwean woman who was recently diagnosed with HIV through a routine screening test. Her CD4 count is 80 cells/mm3 and she has not started antiretroviral therapy (ART) yet. She reports feeling generally well but has had occasional headaches and mild fatigue. She lives in a rural area about 40 km from Harare and has reliable transportation to the study site. She is able to provide written informed consent and has no history of clinical symptoms suggestive of meningitis. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to use contraception while on high dose fluconazole therapy. She has no previous allergy or other reaction to amphotericin B and/or fluconazole. She is a suitable candidate for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with tracheal stenosis caused by intubation, which has been causing breathing difficulties. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for the past six months. He has a history of smoking and has been trying to quit for the past year. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he has no signs of heart or lung disease. He is able to perform activities of daily living but has difficulty with physical exertion. He has been referred to the interventional pulmonology clinic for treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently suffered a supination-external rotation type IV injury to his ankle while playing football. He is experiencing significant pain and swelling in his ankle and has difficulty bearing weight on it. He has no prior history of ankle fractures or significant medical conditions. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. He has a physically demanding job as a construction worker and is concerned about the impact of his injury on his ability to work. His X-ray shows a posterior malleolar fracture. He is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 31-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has been diagnosed with male factor infertility due to her partner's low sperm count and motility. The couple has opted for Intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) as a treatment option. The patient has no significant medical history, and her gynecological exam is normal. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to undergo laser-assisted ICSI and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and has given her informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

45-year-old female with a previous history of cholecystectomy presents with complaints of severe abdominal pain and fever. CT scan shows evidence of a small bowel perforation. The patient is taken to the OR for an exploratory laparotomy and small bowel resection. Post-op, the patient is admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of severe sepsis. The APACHE II score is 20. The patient's legal guardian consents to prophylactic antifungal treatment. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with head and neck cancer. He has been a smoker for the past 20 years and currently smokes a pack of cigarettes a day. He has attempted to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is in a committed relationship and has two children. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to make a concerted effort to quit smoking prior to his surgery. He has no history of psychiatric or medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study. He is willing to attend counseling sessions and use nicotine replacement therapy as part of the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired man who recently suffered a stroke about 3 months ago. He was hospitalized for a week due to weakness on his right side and difficulty speaking. He was able to regain full control of his right side but still experiences difficulty speaking. He is married and lives with his wife. He has a history of hypertension, high cholesterol and has been a smoker for 30 years. He quit smoking after his stroke. He is currently taking medications for his hypertension and cholesterol. He has no known allergies. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disease. He has not experienced any severe perceptual or cognitive deficits but has difficulty finding the right words to express himself. He has no visual agnosia or limb apraxia. He is motivated to improve his communication skills and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male suffered a heat stroke while working outdoors in the summer. He was hospitalized and treated for dehydration and heat exhaustion. He has no past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has been working outdoors for the past 10 years and has not experienced any heat-related illness before. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He is not taking any medications or supplements. He has recovered from the heat stroke and has been cleared by his physician to participate in the study.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with prediabetes during his annual check-up. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m² and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He works as an office manager and spends most of his time sitting at his desk. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes, and his father was diagnosed with it at the age of 55. The patient has never smoked or consumed alcohol. He is currently not taking any herbal supplements or medications. The patient is concerned about his health and is motivated to make lifestyle changes. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of BGG on glucose metabolism and other markers of metabolic syndrome.

8 year old boy brought to the emergency room after a bicycle accident. He was not wearing a helmet and was found unconscious by his mother. Upon arrival, he was found to have a Glasgow Coma Scale of 7. CT scan showed a large right temporal lobe contusion with midline shift. He was intubated and transferred to the pediatric intensive care unit for further management. The neurosurgeon decided to place a catheter for intracranial pressure measurement. The patient has no prior history of ocular or neurological disease. The patient's parents have agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo an elective surgery for the removal of a benign tumor in the abdomen. She has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification of I. She has a body mass index of 28 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. She has no history of chronic cough or recent upper respiratory infection. There is no suspected difficult airway, and she has not had any prior surgeries involving the oral cavity, neck, or thoracic region. The estimated operative time is 90 minutes. She has no known allergies to lidocaine or any other medications.

A 45-year-old woman, diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 10 years ago, has been experiencing chronic pain for the past 2 years. She reports pain in her hands, wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees, and ankles. She describes the pain as a constant dull ache, which is exacerbated by movement and activity. She reports difficulty sleeping due to the pain, and has been experiencing insomnia for the past 6 months. She has been taking naproxen and tramadol to manage her pain, but finds that they are not providing adequate relief. She has no history of benzodiazepine or neuroleptic use, alcohol abuse, psychiatric disorders, Restless Legs Syndrome, or Obstructive Sleep Apnea. She is currently hospitalized in the department of rheumatology at the Nîmes University Hospital.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and elevated fasting triglycerides. She has an abdominal circumference of 38 inches and her fasting blood glucose is 102mg/dL. She has been taking medication for her hypertension for the past 6 months. Her medical records show no history of coronary artery disease, diabetes mellitus, congestive heart failure, familial hypercholesterolemia, or any other major chronic medical condition. She is not pregnant and does not plan to get pregnant during the duration of the study. The patient reports that she does not engage in any physical activity other than her daily chores at home. She is interested in learning more about lifestyle modifications to improve her health and reduce her risk of heart disease.

A 5-year-old boy who is currently attending kindergarten and has been struggling with his weight. His parents have noticed that he has been gaining weight steadily and his BMI is now in the overweight range. They are concerned about his health and want to help him develop healthier habits. The boy is generally active and enjoys playing outside with his friends, but his parents feel that he could benefit from a more structured exercise program. They are also interested in learning more about healthy eating habits and how to encourage their son to make better food choices. They believe that participating in this clinical trial would be a great opportunity to help their son and contribute to the research that could benefit other children in similar situations.

A 72-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis and is being considered for transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease, for which he underwent percutaneous coronary intervention 3 years ago. He has had no neurological symptoms or evidence of cognitive impairment. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The screening anesthesiologist has cleared the patient for the procedure. There is no history of active neurodegenerative disease. The patient is randomized to receive either sedation or general anesthesia during the procedure. The study will monitor the patient's cerebral oxygen saturation using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) and measure cerebral biomarkers to monitor cerebral hypoxia during the "rapid pacing"-period during valvuloplasty.

A 65-year-old man with hearing impairment in both ears is seeking a solution to improve his hearing ability. He has a history of noise exposure due to his previous occupation as a construction worker. He currently wears hearing aids but finds them ineffective in noisy environments. He has no history of surgical procedures in his outer ear and is able to fill in a questionnaire conscientiously. He is willing to attend weekly appointments and able to describe his listening impressions and experiences with the hearing aid accurately. He doesn't have any known hypersensitivity or allergy to the investigational product. He has no significant mobility or dexterity issues and has reliable hearing test results. He doesn't have any known psychological or central hearing disorders, and he is not color-blind.

A 24-year-old Indian male, who works as a wildlife ranger, was bitten by a wild dog two days ago while on duty. He immediately washed the wound with soap and water and received first aid from the healthcare center nearby. He has no past medical history and is in good health. He has no known allergies to any medicines or vaccines. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written consent. He is not on any medications or antibiotics. He is not suffering from any acute or chronic infectious disease, and his body temperature is normal. He has not received any other vaccines in the past 28 days or blood products in the past 12 weeks. He is available for all the visits scheduled in the study.

31-year-old obese female, currently 25 weeks pregnant, diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) at 16 weeks gestation. She has a BMI of 35 and a family history of type 2 diabetes. She has been monitoring her blood glucose levels daily, and her A1c at diagnosis was 6.4%. She has not required insulin therapy, and has been able to manage her GDM with diet and exercise modifications. She will be delivering at St. Mary's Health Center and has agreed to participate in a retrospective data review investigating the correlation between glucose variability and maternal and neonatal outcomes in diabetic pregnancies.

A 19-year-old unmarried woman from a low-income area in Mumbai, India presents with concerns regarding her sexual and reproductive health. She is sexually active and is interested in learning more about contraception and other related topics. She has never received any formal education or counseling regarding sexual and reproductive health. Her family is conservative and she feels uncomfortable discussing these topics with them. She has visited a local healthcare facility in the past but felt that the providers were not knowledgeable or sensitive to her needs. She is interested in participating in a pilot study that provides adolescent-friendly services and education to young women like herself. She is willing to provide consent to participate in the study and is excited to learn more about her sexual and reproductive health in a safe and supportive environment.

A 46-year-old male presents with symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) and end-stage heart failure. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 32% and he is classified as NYHA class III. He has a dual chamber ICD with home monitoring capabilities already implanted due to primary prevention. He has not undergone any left heart ablation procedures for AF in the past. His left atrial diameter is 5.5 cm as measured by parasternal long-axis view. He is eligible for heart transplantation due to his end-stage heart failure. He has no contraindication for chronic anticoagulation therapy or heparin. He has not experienced any acute coronary syndrome, cardiac surgery, angioplasty or cerebrovascular accident in the past 2 months. He has no untreated hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism. He has not enrolled in any other investigational drug or device study. He has no indication for cardiac resynchronization therapy. He is not a woman currently pregnant, breastfeeding or not using reliable contraceptive measures during fertility age. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol and has provided written informed consent. He has sufficient GPRS-network coverage in his area.

The patient is a 58-year-old male veteran who recently visited the VA hospital for a routine check-up. He has a family history of diabetes, with both of his parents having been diagnosed with the disease in their 60s. He is overweight with a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 29.5 and has a history of high blood pressure. The patient reports feeling tired and thirsty more frequently than usual, and he has noticed that he has been urinating more frequently.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's disease in remission, presented with symptoms of fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. He has a history of recurrent episodes of anaemia and is currently experiencing symptoms of IDA. The patient's Hb level is 11.5 g/dL, and CRP level is within the normal range. His ferritin level is below 100 µg/L. He is currently taking mesalazine for his Crohn's disease. He has a history of allergic rhinitis and is currently not taking any medications for it. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of liver disease or chronic infections. He weighs 70 kg and is willing to participate in the study after signing informed consent.

A 35-year-old male patient presented with a sharp pain in his lower left jaw. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of dental procedures or trauma. Upon examination, the dentist found that the tooth in question is a mandibular premolar with a single canal. The patient has no allergies to any food or drugs and does not take any medications. He has not consumed any preoperative medication, such as analgesics, non-steroidal or steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, within 12 hours before treatment. The patient has not had any antibiotics over the past two weeks preoperatively. He does not have bruxism or clenching. He has no other teeth in the same quadrant or opposite quadrant that require endodontic treatment. He is not pregnant and has no significant systemic disorders. The patient is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided.

The patient is a 43-year-old female with a primary diagnosis of breast cancer. She is a native Russian speaker and has been living in Almaty, Kazakhstan for the past 10 years. She is fluent in both Russian and Kazakh languages. She has not been diagnosed with depression or anxiety in the past and is not currently taking any antidepressants. She is interested in participating in the study as she believes that it will help improve the understanding of depression and anxiety in breast cancer patients and improve the quality of care provided to them. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who does not suffer from any significant disease or known hypersensitivity to any of the drugs used in the study. He is not on regular medication, including birth control pills. He is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand possible drug interactions with CYP2C9 substrates. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements, including taking the study drugs and providing urine and blood samples as required. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participation in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 10 years. He has a chronic diabetic foot ulcer on his left foot that has been present for the past 6 months. Despite regular wound debridement and dressing by a surgeon, the ulcer has not healed and measures approximately 2 cm in diameter. The patient has no evident local infection or gangrene, and his C-reactive protein level is negative. He has no history of end-stage organ failure, hepatic or renal failure, or thrombocytopenia. He is not currently taking anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents, and he is not on steroid therapy. The ulcer is not deeper than 2 cm and has no ischemia present, as confirmed by the detection of distal limb pulsations with an ankle-brachial index > 0.9. The patient is interested in exploring new therapeutic options for his diabetic foot ulcer and is willing to participate in a clinical trial.

A 65-year-old Caucasian man was referred to the cardiology clinic for evaluation of aortic stenosis. He had a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which were well-controlled with medication. He denied any chest pain, shortness of breath or syncope. On physical examination, he had a harsh systolic ejection murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border. Echocardiogram revealed severe aortic stenosis with a peak velocity of 4.2 m/s and mean gradient of 45 mmHg. Coronary angiography revealed mild coronary artery disease with no significant stenosis. The patient was scheduled for an elective surgical aortic valve replacement with possible concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting. He was randomized to receive either placebo or methylprednisolone 15mg/kg intraoperatively. As part of the study protocol, CSF and blood samples were collected the day before and after surgery for analysis of inflammatory markers, neuronal damage and blood brain barrier function. The patient was closely monitored for any adverse events related to the study drug.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male with a history of recurrent Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is being treated by a psychiatrist at a private clinic. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 2 years, including feelings of sadness, lack of interest, and hopelessness. He was previously treated with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and cognitive-behavioral therapy but did not show significant improvement. His psychiatrist prescribed Seroquel XR as an adjunct treatment for his MDD. He has been taking Seroquel XR for the past 6 months and reports some improvement in his symptoms. He has no significant medical history, does not smoke or drink alcohol, and has no family history of mental illness. He has provided informed consent to participate in the drug utilisation study, and his medical records will be used to collect data for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a history of sickle cell disease. He experiences frequent episodes of vaso-occlusive pain crisis, and reports shortness of breath and chest pain with exertion. He has also experienced episodes of dizziness and fainting. His medical history includes a diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension (high blood pressure in the lungs) based on an echoc

The patient is a 35-year-old African American female who was diagnosed with HIV infection 3 years ago. She is currently taking antiretroviral medication and has a CD4 count of 400 cells/mm3. She complains of occasional diarrhea and abdominal discomfort. She has no history of gastrointestinal pathology or inflammatory bowel disease. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She has not received oral antibiotics in the past 3 months. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing the efficacy of a synbiotic supplement in improving intestinal function and immune system overactivation in HIV-infected individuals.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and stable angina presents to the hospital for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. The patient has previously undergone a coronary angiography that revealed significant stenosis in multiple coronary arteries. The patient is scheduled for CABG using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) support. The patient has been informed about the study and has given informed consent.
