The patient will undergo a comprehensive transesophageal echocardiogram before and after CPB support to measure myocardial deformation parameters using two different echocardiographic techniques: Doppler tissue imaging and Speckle tracking. The aim of the study is to compare the accuracy and efficacy of these two techniques for the detection of regional myocardial deformation in patients undergoing CABG surgery. The patient will be monitored closely throughout the surgery and postoperative period. The patient will be assessed for cardiac output using the thermodilution method via a pulmonary artery catheter. The study will be conducted in the Department of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care, Advanced Cardiac Centre, Post Graduate Institute Medical Education Research, Chandigarh.

68 yo M with a 40 pack-year smoking history and a diagnosis of COPD according to GOLD criteria. He reports chronic cough, sputum production, and shortness of breath with exertion. The patient has a history of hospitalizations for COPD exacerbations and is currently in a clinically stable state. He is able to communicate via touch-tone telephone and reads and speaks English. He has access to a computer and is willing to interact with a computer screen, mouse, and keyboard. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. Past Medical History: COPD, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, and a remote history of colon cancer.

55-year-old male diagnosed with early-stage prostate cancer within the past 9 months. The patient is currently maintaining a high-fat, low-vegetable, low-fruit diet and is not meeting the goal for moderate physical activity for at least 150 minutes per week. The patient is able to speak and write in English and has no other malignancy within the past 5 years except nonmelanoma skin cancer. The patient has not received any biologic, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, radiotherapy or surgery as part of their cancer treatment.

The patient is a 45 year old non-smoking woman who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stage IIIA. She has completed platinum-based concurrent chemoradiation therapy (cCRT) and has not progressed following the therapy. She has an ECOG score of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She has not received prior anti-cancer treatment, including anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2 or anti-VEGF treatments, as well as therapeutic anticancer vaccines. She is willing to provide tumor histological specimens required for this study. She has adequate organ and marrow function required for the trial. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use adequate contraception for the course of the study through 90 days after the last dose of study medication. She has provided signed informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old African-American woman who presented with two keloids on her left shoulder and upper arm. She has a history of keloids on her chest and back as well. The keloids have been present for several years and have caused discomfort, itching, and occasional pain. She has not received any treatment for these keloids in the past. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. She is not currently taking any medications. The patient is willing and able to participate in the requirements of the study and has signed the informed consent. The keloids are between 0.5 and 2 cm in length and the investigator believes that they can be excised in a similar manner and closed properly with the two techniques. The investigator has determined that the keloids could benefit from surgical procedure. The patient does not have excessive body hair in the area and does not have any conditions that would put her at heightened risk or limit the study evaluations required by the protocol.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who underwent a total hip arthroplasty for end-stage hip osteoarthritis 3 years ago. He has been experiencing pain in his right hip for the past few months, which has been gradually worsening. He also reports difficulty in walking and standing for prolonged periods. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. Upon examination, he has tenderness and swelling around his right hip joint with limited range of motion. X-rays show a periprosthetic femur fracture, according to Vancouver classification. He is planned to undergo surgical treatment for the fracture as part of this clinical trial.

Sophie is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS). She has an EDSS score of 6.5 and has been experiencing occasional episodes of fatigue, numbness, tingling, and weakness in her legs. Sophie is currently taking corticosteroids for her MS symptoms, but she has not used any other immunomodulatory treatments in the past. She has no history of heart disease or metal implants, and her urine pregnancy test at screening was negative. Sophie has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and she has not used any investigational drugs for the treatment of MS in the past 30 days. Her lab results are within normal ranges, and she has no known allergies. Sophie is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance research in the treatment of MS.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma five years ago. She has received two rounds of chemotherapy and one stem cell transplant but has recently relapsed. Her performance status is good (ECOG 1) with no other significant medical conditions. Her laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count of 1,800/mm^3, platelet count of 80,000/mm^3, creatinine of 1.8 mg/dL, bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dL, ALT of 40 U/L, and AST of 35 U/L. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to thalidomide or lenalidomide. She has not received lenalidomide treatment within the last six months and has not received any experimental drugs or corticosteroids in the last four weeks. She is willing to use two methods of highly effective contraception if she is fertile. She is interested in participating in the study and willing to comply with the protocol.

An 80-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer presents with symptoms of bone pain and fatigue. He was initially diagnosed with prostate cancer 7 years ago and has been treated with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). However, he has recently developed castration-resistant prostate cancer, and his PSA levels have started to rise. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment. He is currently on medications for these conditions, including metformin, lisinopril, and donepezil. The patient has a WHO performance status of 3, indicating that he is capable of only limited self-care and is confined to bed or chair for more than 50% of waking hours. He has a PSA level of 17 ng/mL, and imaging studies reveal metastatic disease to the bones. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this study as he is aged 75 or older, has histologically proven prostate adenocarcinoma, and has metastatic disease refractory to castration. He is classified as "vulnerable" or "frail" according to the SIOG criteria and has a WHO performance status of 3. The patient has neutrophils greater than or equal to 2.109/L, platelets greater than or equal to 100.109/L, and hemoglobin greater than or equal to 9 g/dL, meeting the study's eligibility criteria. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent according to local regulations.

This clinical trial is seeking patients who have received or are currently receiving treatment with the NUsurface® meniscus implant. This implant is designed to replace a damaged or deteriorated meniscus, which is a common injury among athletes and active individuals. The purpose of the study is to further understand the long-term safety and effectiveness of the implant in a real-world setting. Patients who meet the inclusion criteria and provide informed consent will be eligible for enrollment. There are no specific exclusion criteria for this study, meaning that all patients who meet the inclusion criteria can participate in the registry. If you have received the NUsurface® meniscus implant and are interested in contributing to the understanding of its long-term safety and effectiveness, this study may be right for you.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 3 years ago. She has been on metformin 2000 mg/day for the last year and has been following a strict diet and exercise regimen. Despite the treatment, her HbA1c levels remain high, with a current value of 9.2%. She experiences occasional episodes of hyperglycemia with glucose levels around 240 mg/dl (13.3 mmol/dl). She has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or transient ischemic attack. Her liver and renal function tests are normal. She has not had any gastrointestinal surgery and is not currently on any anti-obesity medication. She is not currently receiving treatment with systemic steroids or any other medication for diabetes except metformin. She is interested in participating in the trial to help manage her diabetes more effectively.

Patient is a 60-year-old male who underwent left heart valve replacement surgery due to severe aortic valve stenosis. After the surgery, the patient developed tricuspid regurgitation and right heart failure with symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and fluid retention. The patient is currently taking a diuretic but is still experiencing fluid retention. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of tolvaptan in improving fluid retention and mid-term prognosis. The patient has no hypersensitivity to the study drug and is not anuric or hypernatremic. The patient does not have any malignant tumor and does not have serious hepatic or renal failure. The patient is otherwise deemed appropriate for inclusion in the study by the investigator.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the surgeon with a large ventral hernia in the midline of his abdomen. He states that he has had the hernia for several years, but it has been gradually increasing in size and causing him discomfort. He denies any recent weight loss, fevers, or chills. He is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago, and drinks alcohol occasionally. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals a large, reducible ventral hernia measuring approximately 10 cm in diameter. The patient is deemed to have a Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG) grade 3 hernia. He is advised that a biologic mesh will be required for repair due to contamination and comorbidities precluding the use of synthetic mesh. The patient is informed of the study and agrees to participate. Informed consent is obtained, and the patient is randomized to receive either Strattice or XenMatrix for his hernia repair.

The patient is a 19-year-old male with a history of Atopic Dermatitis for the past 2 years. He has mild to moderate eczema with a current IGA score of 2 and treatable BSA of 10%. The patient has not been on any systemic treatment for AD in the past 4 weeks and is not currently using any topical steroids or immunomodulators. He has no other significant medical conditions and is not taking any medications. The patient is willing to use effective contraceptive methods throughout the course of the study and has a negative urine beta-human chorionic gonadotropin hormone (hCG) pregnancy test at Day 1. The patient is able to understand and provide signed informed consent. The patient is expected to be normally active and in good health by medical history and physical examination.

The patient is a 54-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with high-risk endometrial cancer. She underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy within the past 56 days. Pathology revealed grade 3 adenocarcinoma with >50% myometrial invasion (stage IIA). She has Zubrod performance status of 0-1 and no evidence of metastatic extrauterine disease, gross or residual disease, or distant metastases. Her absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 1,800/mm^3, platelet count is 120,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin is 12 g/dL. Her total bilirubin is 1.3 times upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are within normal limits, and serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL. Her urine protein:creatinine ratio is 0.4, indicating no significant proteinuria. She has no serious, active comorbidity and no history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy, stroke/cerebrovascular event, or arterial thromboembolic events within the past 12 months. She has no abdominal fistula, GI perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within the past 6 months, and no other invasive malignancies within the past 3 years. She has no mental status changes or bladder problems that would preclude the ability to comply with bladder-filling instructions and has no mental or psychiatric illness that would preclude giving informed consent. She has no known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or other recombinant human antibodies and no prior allergic reaction to bevacizumab, cisplatin, carboplatin, or paclitaxel. She has no concurrent erythropoietin, St. John's wort, therapeutic anticoagulants, aminoglycoside antibiotics, or amifostine and has no prior organ transplantation. She has no prior external-beam radiotherapy to the pelvis resulting in overlapping of radiotherapy fields, no prior systemic chemotherapy for uterine cancer, and no prior therapy with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) compounds. She is not currently on concurrent warfarin at doses > 1 mg/day but prophylactic low molecular weight heparin is allowed.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been experiencing chest pain with exertion for the past 6 months and has failed to respond to medical management. The patient underwent a cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe diffuse multivessel atherosclerotic coronary artery disease (CAD) and was subsequently referred for coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG). A recent echocardiogram showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 40% (Simpson's rule). The patient reports Class III angina (Canadian Cardiovascular Society) despite maximally tolerated medical therapy. He has undergone multiple cardiac scintigraphy and magnetic resonance imaging tests, which have shown abnormal myocardial perfusion. The patient is not a candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) due to extensive and diffuse lesions, and he is also not a candidate for complete CABG due to the severity and extension of the disease with diffuse small vessel involvement, according to an expert panel. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, end-stage renal disease requiring maintenance dialysis, neoplasia, or a life expectancy below 2 years. The patient has not participated in any cell therapy trial in the past 2 years.

A 24-year-old woman is pregnant for the first time and is currently 10 weeks gestation. She resides in Dar es Salaam and plans to stay there until delivery and for at least 6 weeks thereafter. She has tested negative for HIV. She has a history of anemia and has experienced mild symptoms of malaria in the past. She has no known allergies or medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help reduce the risk of placental malaria and its associated adverse pregnancy outcomes.

The patient is a 62-year-old Chinese postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with estrogen-receptor positive (ER+) locally advanced breast cancer three years ago. She underwent surgical resection followed by adjuvant therapy with letrozole for one year. However, she experienced a recurrence of the breast cancer with bone metastasis and was treated with anastrozole for six months, but experienced disease progression. The patient is now seeking alternative treatment options and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no history of diabetes mellitus or other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to give written informed consent.

A 7-week-old baby boy, born full-term with a birth weight of 3.1 kg, was brought in by his parents to participate in a clinical trial for a new rotavirus vaccine. The baby has received all the recommended EPI vaccines (OPV, BCG, and Hep B) at birth and is in good health as confirmed by a medical history and clinical examination before entering the study. The parents have given their informed consent and are willing to remain available in the area during the study period. The baby has not had diarrhea or vomiting in the previous 72 hours and does not have a fever on the day of enrollment. The baby is not known to have any medical condition that would compromise his health or result in non-conformance to the protocol. The baby has not received any immunoglobulin therapy and/or blood products since birth, and has not been administered corticosteroids or any immunosuppressants. The baby does not have any history of neurologic disorders or seizures. The parents are excited to participate in the study and contribute to the development of a new vaccine that might help prevent childhood diarrhea caused by rotavirus.

A 8-year-old girl who is generally healthy and active. She enjoys playing outside with her friends and participating in after-school sports programs. She does not have any known chronic medical conditions and does not take any regular medications. Her BMI is within the normal range for her age and sex. She is able to walk and run without difficulty and does not have any known motor disabilities.

Pt is a 45yo M with a history of loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness. He was referred to Sleep Disorder Program at the University of British Columbia for a sleep study to rule out obstructive sleep apnea. The sleep study revealed moderate to severe OSAH with an AHI of 30 events per hour. The patient was prescribed CPAP by his sleep physician, but he has struggled with compliance due to discomfort and inconvenience. The patient is willing to accept a trial of CPAP and has provided a telephone number that would allow contact during regular office hours if necessary. The patient has access to a telephone line in their bedroom that can be used to transmit data with the modem. The patient has no active cardiopulmonary or psychiatric disease and has not been previously treated for OSA. The patient resides in the greater Vancouver area.

45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and previous myocardial infarction presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient was admitted to the adult inpatient ward at HUG during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The patient underwent cardiac catheterization and was found to have significant coronary artery disease requiring coronary artery bypass grafting. The patient was treated successfully with surgery and discharged home. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Previous myocardial infarction - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 diabetes - History of smoking - No known drug allergies.

The patient is a 48-year-old man who recently tested positive for COVID-19. He has mild symptoms including a dry cough, fever, body aches, and fatigue. He has not been hospitalized and is currently isolating at home. He has no known risk factors for severe COVID-19 disease such as heart or lung conditions and is not taking any medications for COVID-19. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of Artesunate in adults with mild symptoms of COVID-19. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no known exclusion criteria.

A 32-year-old female presents with a history of right ovarian cyst measuring 5cm in diameter. She has been experiencing mild pelvic pain for the past few months. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. She is nulliparous and is not currently using any contraceptive method. She has been referred for a laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing 2D versus 3D laparoscopy for this procedure. She is able to understand Cantonese, Putonghua or English and is willing to participate in the study after it has been explained to her. She has no other contraindications for the study.

The patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman who is attending an ob-gyn practice in Colorado. She is currently in her second trimester and has concerns about receiving the influenza and pertussis (Tdap) vaccines during pregnancy. She has heard conflicting information about the safety and effectiveness of these vaccines and is unsure of whether or not she should get them. She has no known allergies to any vaccine components. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to improve provider communication about maternal immunizations and increase vaccine uptake among pregnant women.

Mrs. Lim is a 72-year-old retired teacher who has been diagnosed with colon cancer. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue and has lost some weight recently. Her family history is positive for colon cancer in her father and diabetes in her mother. She is currently on medication for hypertension but has no other significant medical history. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise. Her hemoglobin level was found to be 10.5 g/dL, which is below the normal range for her age. She was informed that she meets the eligibility criteria for a clinical trial that aims to investigate the impact of preoperative anemia on postoperative complications in elderly patients undergoing major open abdominal surgery. She was given detailed information about the study and the risks and benefits involved. She has agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 58-year-old non-smoking woman who has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and occasional chest pain for the past 3 months. She recently underwent a chest X-ray and CT scan that revealed a mass in her left lung. Biopsies confirmed the presence of non-small cell lung cancer. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore gene mutations in NSCLC cells and is a candidate for systemic treatment such as EGFR-TKI or chemotherapy. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 3 months and is willing to provide written informed consent for the study.

A 58-year-old man presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with stable angina pectoris. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and is a smoker. He has been on anti-hypertensive medication and lipid-lowering medication for several years. He has no history of diabetes or other major medical illnesses. Coronary angiography revealed a significant de novo lesion (>70% stenosis) in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). The reference vessel diameter was 3.0 mm. He is considered for coronary revascularization and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has no contraindications to anti-platelet agents and his creatinine level is normal. He has not been treated with any drug-eluting stent (DES) within the past year, and has no severe hepatic dysfunction or complex lesion morphologies. He does not have a target lesion in a vein graft and his reference vessel diameter is within the range of 2.5-3.5mm. He is willing to undergo intravascular optical coherence tomography (OCT) to evaluate the neointimal coverage and malapposition at 3 months after stent implantation with either Endeavor resolute or Xience. He understands the study procedure and has given informed consent.

A healthy 52-year-old male with a BMI of 28 kg/m² who does not exercise regularly is needed for a clinical trial investigating the effects of acute exercise on gene expression in human skeletal muscle. The patient must not have a history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease and should not be taking medications that can interfere with gene expression in the muscles, such as statins or fenofibrate. The patient should not have diabetes mellitus type 1 or 2 and should not abuse drugs or alcohol. The patient should not have any (chronic) injuries of the locomotor system that can interfere with the intervention. The study requires a single exercise bout that consists of one hour of one-legged cycling on an adapted recumbent cycle ergometer at a submaximal rate. The non-exercising leg will serve as control for the exercising leg. The patient will be asked to provide a blood sample and muscle biopsy before and after exercise to assess changes in gene expression and blood plasma levels of selected proteins.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been hospitalized for second-degree burns on her left arm and leg. She has a history of anxiety but has never been diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder. The patient is able to communicate verbally in English and has an IV access already in place. She has no head or neck injuries that could interfere with the use of Virtual Reality equipment. The patient is interested in participating in the study to alleviate pain during the burn care procedure. She is capable of filling out study measures and complying with the questionnaires. The patient is alert and cooperative and has no known allergies to ketamine or any other medication.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a history of recurrent plantar warts. He reports experiencing moderate to severe pain during previous wart removal procedures, which has led to anxiety and fear of undergoing further procedures. He presents to the dermatology clinic with multiple plantar warts on both feet, requiring liquid nitrogen application for removal. He is interested in participating in a study that explores the use of virtual reality technology for pain control during the procedure. The patient has no history of vertigo, inner ear diseases, or seizures. He is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

25 yo M seeking treatment for cannabis use disorder. He reports using cannabis daily for the past year and has been unsuccessful in quitting on his own. He has no significant medical or psychiatric history, and is not currently taking any medications. He is employed full-time but is willing to take time off work to participate in the inpatient phase of the trial if necessary. He is in a stable relationship and reports no issues with contraception. He has no allergies or hypersensitivity to benzodiazepines, and has not previously taken benzodiazepines. He does not have a history of significant violent behavior, and is not on parole or probation.

A 6-year old girl was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) six months ago. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings. Her father works as a software engineer and her mother is a stay-at-home mom. The family has no history of cancer. The patient has been undergoing chemotherapy and has experienced several hospitalizations due to complications from her treatment. She has experienced hair loss and fatigue but has maintained a positive attitude throughout her treatment. Her mother has been her primary caregiver and has had to take time off from work to care for her. Her younger siblings have also been affected by her illness, with changes in routine and increased stress in the household. Her family is concerned about the impact of her illness on their own health and well-being.

55-year-old woman diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and scheduled for a lumpectomy at UH GMC Seidman Cancer Center. The patient has no history of lymphedema or prior radiation treatments to the breast or axilla areas. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the follow-up call 3 months post-surgery. The patient has a good understanding of written, verbal, and/or recorded survey questioning in English. She is interested in learning more about the risk factors and symptoms of lymphedema and is open to receiving written and verbal education on the topic.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with thyroid cancer. She is otherwise healthy and is not taking any medications or supplements. She underwent total thyroidectomy and is in the euthyroid state. She has no history of neck surgery or irradiation, and is not pregnant. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of routine calcium and vitamin D supplementation in preventing postoperative hypocalcemia. She is willing to take oral supplements of 1,500 mg/day elemental calcium and 1,000 IU/day cholecalciferol for 2 weeks after surgery, if she is randomized to the routine calcium group. She understands that if she develops symptomatic hypocalcemia, she will receive intravenous calcium supplementation followed by oral calcium and vitamin D supplements. She is willing to undergo laboratory tests and follow-up visits as required by the study protocol.

A 15-year-old male presents with a history of persistent nasal congestion, sneezing, itching, and rhinorrhea. He reports experiencing these symptoms for more than four days per week and for more than four consecutive weeks per year. He has a positive skin-prick test to multiple allergens, including dust mites, grass pollen, and tree pollen. He has been using nasal decongestants and antihistamines with minimal relief. He reports no history of anaphylaxis or severe local reactions to skin testing with allergens. He is not currently sexually active and has no history of pregnancy. He has never participated in an investigational study and has not used any drug or device in an investigational protocol in the 30 days prior to the visit. He is willing and able to adhere to dose, visit schedules, and meet study requirements.

A 35-year-old female with no history of lactation or gestational risk is needed for a clinical trial evaluating the safety of the gynecological formulation in normal and usual usage condition of Dermacyd Tina Gel Sweet Flower. The patient should not have used any anti-inflammatory or immunosuppression drugs in the past month and should not be using any topical medication in the region to be treated. The patient should not have any active gynecological disease or cutaneous disease that may interfere with the study results. Additionally, the patient should not have a personal history of allergic disease at the area to be treated or any allergies or atopic history. The study requires an integral skin test in the region, and the patient should be willing to undergo gynecological follow-up.

A 60-year-old male suffered from a subcortical stroke about 8 months ago, resulting in decreased range of motion in his left index finger. He has been undergoing physical therapy since then, but has only seen limited improvement. He has no history of seizures or epilepsy, but does have a pacemaker. He is able to understand the study goals and follow simple directions. He is excited to participate in the study to potentially improve his hand function.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with a brain tumor and is scheduled for surgery in an awake condition. She has been experiencing headaches, dizziness, and difficulty with coordination for the past few months. MRI revealed a tumor in the right frontal lobe of the brain. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is able to communicate effectively and has no sensory or motor deficits. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the interest of ultra-high frequency Doppler ultrasound in the surgical management of patients operated in an awake condition for a cerebral tumor. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and has given informed consent.

Kate is a 28 year-old woman who is currently 16 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has been experiencing increasing feelings of stress and anxiety since she found out about the pregnancy. She has trouble sleeping at night and often wakes up feeling fatigued. She is also concerned about her ability to cope with the changes that come with motherhood. Kate has a history of depression and anxiety, and has previously received therapy for these conditions. She is currently not taking any medication for her mental health. She is fluent in English and has access to the internet. Kate plans to deliver her baby in Singapore. She is not experiencing any severe psychiatric, medical, or obstetric complications, and there is no known fetal abnormality. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her psychological well-being during pregnancy.

This is a 40 year-old female with a history of rosacea. She has tried various topical treatments with little to no improvement. She is Fitzpatrick Skin Type II and does not have any significant medical history. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is willing to refrain from using any topical or systemic corticosteroids or retinoids on the treated area for the duration of the study. She is willing to adhere to the treatment and follow-up schedule and post-treatment care instructions. She is willing to use a sunscreen of SPF 50 or higher on the face every day for the duration of the study, including the follow-up period. She is willing to have digital photographs taken of the face. She has not had any previous laser or light-based procedures for the face within 6 months of study participation. She is not taking any medications that increase sensitivity to light, such as tetracycline. She is not undergoing systemic chemotherapy for the treatment of cancer. She is not taking any systemic use of retinoid such as isotretinoin and/or corticosteroid within 6 months or topical use of retinoid and/or corticosteroid within 4 weeks of study participation. She is not excessively tanned in areas to be treated or unable/unlikely to refrain from tanning during the study. She is not a current smoker or history of smoking within 12 months of study participation. She has not participated in a study of another device or drug within 6 months prior to enrollment or during the study.

Patient A is a 26-year-old female who is pregnant with her first child. She has a history of good health and has not undergone any previous surgeries. The patient is at term and is scheduled for a transverse lower segment cesarean section. She has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy and has no history of postoperative fever. She is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial to compare the use of barbed sutures versus conventional sutures for incision closure during her cesarean section. The patient has provided written consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with malignant melanoma cutis with a Breslow tumor depth of 3.5 mm. He is scheduled to undergo a combined re-excision and sentinel node biopsy (SNB). He feels generally healthy and has a WHO Performance Status of 1. He has no known allergies to oligodeoxynucleotides. He has no active auto-immune disease requiring disease-modifying therapy. He has not been diagnosed with any loco-regional or distant metastasis. He has no other primary malignancy except for the melanoma. He has not been diagnosed with any active systemic infections requiring antibiotics. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to use effective contraceptive methods from screening until at least 90 days after the IMO-2125 administration. He has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 38-year-old pregnant woman who is expecting her first child. She is currently at 38 weeks of gestation and is scheduled for an elective cesarean section in two days. She has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications or pre-existing medical conditions. She has not received any steroid treatment during her pregnancy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of dexamethasone before elective cesarean section in reducing neonatal respiratory distress syndrome. She is willing to receive four intramuscular injections of 6 mg of dexamethasone 48 hours before the scheduled cesarean section. She understands the potential benefits and risks of the treatment and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

72 year old female with a BMI of 25 kg/m2, non-smoker, and currently taking no medications. She has a regular and normal Dutch eating habit consuming three main meals per day. She has veins suitable for cannulation. She has no history of medical or surgical events that may significantly affect the study outcome. She has no known gastrointestinal disorders or allergies to dairy or acetaminophen. She does not consume protein supplements and has not had unexplained weight loss or gain in the past month. She has not had recent blood donation and is willing to give up blood donation during the study. She has a general practitioner and is willing to accept information-transfer concerning participation in the study, or information regarding her health, like laboratory results and eventual adverse events to and from her general practitioner.

John is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV melanoma 3 months ago. He underwent multiple surgeries and chemotherapy, but his lesions have progressed and are now deemed inoperable. He has a large melanoma skin lesion on his back that is causing him pain and discomfort. He has no history of heart disease, but he is a former smoker and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. His ECOG performance status is 2, meaning he is ambulatory and capable of all self-care, but unable to carry out any work activities. He has no significant medical history of autoimmune disease or other chronic illness, and his organ function is normal. He is aware of the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing headaches, seizures, and difficulty with speech and memory for the past few months. She has undergone an MRI scan which revealed a large mass in the left temporal lobe of the brain. Biopsy results have confirmed a diagnosis of glioblastoma multiforme. She has not previously received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work, but is unable to perform any strenuous activities. She has adequate bone marrow and liver function, with normal levels of creatinine and albumin. She is willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control during the study. She has no history of disorders of urea metabolism or insulin-dependent diabetes. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed a document of informed consent indicating her understanding of the investigational nature and the risks of the study.

45-year-old male, diagnosed with gastric cancer, is scheduled to receive radiotherapy within the next 3 weeks. The total dose of at least 2,000 cGy will be delivered in at least 15 fractions, 1 fraction per day, 5 days per week. The treatment field will include an area of at least 80 cm2 in the anterior/posterior direction encompassing the upper abdomen. The patient is at risk of developing radiation-induced emesis and has not experienced emesis (retching and/or vomiting) or nausea with severity greater than 2 within the past week. His performance status is ECOG 1, and his life expectancy is not specified. He has no specific hematopoietic or renal issues, no active peptic ulcer, and no lactose intolerance. He has no concurrent condition or illness that contraindicates corticosteroids, serotonin antagonists, or prochlorperazine. He has no prior unusual or allergic reaction to a serotonin antagonist (ondansetron, dolasetron, or granisetron), corticosteroid, or prochlorperazine. He is able and willing to complete diary and quality of life questionnaires in English. He is able to swallow and has not taken any medication with antiemetic intent in the last 2 days.

A 9-year-old male child diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency (GHD) for the last 3 years. He has been receiving daily Genotropin injection for the last six months with a stable dose. He is 124 cm in height and weighs 28 kg. He has no history of cancer, radiation therapy or chemotherapy. He has no psychosocial dwarfism, or any other chronic medical or psychiatric condition. He is not born small for gestational age (SGA) and has no chromosomal abnormalities. He is not currently on any other regular injectable medications. He has no known hypersensitivity to the components of the medication. He has no history of drug, substance, or alcohol abuse. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding or a fertile male. He has no closed epiphyses. The patient and the parent/legal guardian are willing and able to understand and follow the written and/or verbal instructions on the proper use of growth hormone injection devices.

A 42-year-old male who works as a construction worker has been experiencing plantar heel pain for over a year. He has tried various conservative treatments, including resting, stretching, and wearing orthotics, but they have provided only temporary relief. He is otherwise healthy and does not smoke. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help him with his long-standing plantar fasciitis. He has no history of fractures or ankle surgeries, and he has not had any previous local painful episodes. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has a long-standing history of asthma and allergic rhinitis. She has a positive allergy testing for cat allergen and experiences worsening of her symptoms, including shortness of breath and runny nose, upon exposure to cats. She is not currently experiencing a respiratory tract infection and does not have any other lung disorder. She is not currently taking any medication for her asthma or allergic rhinitis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the protective effect of an approved medication on her symptoms upon exposure to cats. She is available to attend all study visits for a duration of 2 weeks.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic hip pain and functional impairment for the past 3 years. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the hip by his physician and has tried various pain medications, including acetaminophen, NSAIDs, and opioids, but has not experienced satisfactory relief. He is scheduled to undergo a hip replacement surgery for his affected joint but wishes to participate in this clinical trial to help manage his pain until the surgery. He is willing to receive a single injection subcutaneously once every 4 weeks for up to 16 weeks and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study. He is also willing to comply with all study requirements, including blood sample collections and safety evaluations throughout the study. He is currently not pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant, and does not have any unstable or progressive neurologic disorders.

12 year old girl with history of severe sepsis and septic shock requiring ICU admission for 2 weeks. The patient was intubated for 8 days and required pressor support for 4 days. She was diagnosed with sepsis secondary to pneumonia which was treated with antibiotics, and subsequently developed severe acute kidney injury requiring initiation of renal replacement therapy. The patient was recently discharged and has been recovering well with no residual symptoms. She has no history of chronic kidney disease or other chronic illness. The patient and her parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the long-term impact of pediatric acute renal injury in severe sepsis.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who underwent an open cholecystectomy for gallstones. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are managed with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies. He has a BMI of 30 and exercises regularly. He has never had abdominal surgery before and has no history of wound healing complications. His surgical incision is approximately 10 cm in length and is closed with staples. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in follow-up visits.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis at the age of 28. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and rectal bleeding. She has been prescribed various medications including mesalamine, prednisone, and infliximab. Despite the treatment, she continues to have symptoms and has noticed that she feels fatigued and weak most of the time. She has been recently diagnosed with anemia and her hemoglobin levels have been consistently below the normal range. She is concerned about the impact of anemia on her quality of life and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the prevalence and pathogenesis of anemia in IBD patients in Italy. She is willing to undergo screening to investigate the mechanism of anemia and participate in follow-up evaluations to assess the treatment of anemia, fatigue, and quality of life.

Mary is a 58-year-old woman who has struggled with weight issues for most of her adult life. She is 5'5" and currently weighs 210 pounds, giving her a BMI of 35. She has been sedentary for the past year but is willing to become more active. She has been diagnosed with hypertension with a blood pressure of 155/90 mmHg. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol, but her current levels are within normal range. She has never had a heart attack or stroke, and has no history of respiratory, endocrine, or neurological disease. She has not been taking any medications for her hypertension, but is willing to be randomized to treatment or placebo. She is interested in learning about ways to improve her health and is willing to participate in the study if approved by her doctor.

A 45-year-old African American man presents with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He has been on medication for these conditions for the past 5 years. He reports feeling tired during the day, snoring loudly, and having difficulty sleeping at night. He has never been evaluated for sleep apnea. His BMI is 32, and his waist circumference is 42 inches. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He is currently employed as a construction worker, and his job requires him to work long hours. He has limited access to healthcare due to his work schedule and financial limitations. He is interested in learning more about sleep apnea and improving his overall health. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old male Army Veteran from the United States who served in Iraq for two tours. He is currently experiencing symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) including nightmares, flashbacks, and hypervigilance. He is seeking treatment for PTSD at the Boston VA and has been diagnosed with the disorder. He lives with his wife and two children who are supportive of his treatment. His wife is willing to participate in a brief family intervention to enhance his treatment. The patient has no current diagnosis of unstable bipolar disorder or substance dependence, past or present psychosis, or organic mental disorder. He does not present any clear and current suicidal risk and is not currently participating in family/couples therapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been suffering from severe knee pain for the past 5 years. The pain has been progressively worsening and has started to affect her daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and even standing for extended periods of time. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been advised to undergo a primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) surgery. She has no history of fractures in her thigh or leg, and has not undergone any previous high tibial osteotomy. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to determine the best position of soft tissue repair (flexion versus extension) in post-operative range of motion and functional outcome after TKA surgery.

A 46-year-old man with a history of hypertension and high blood sugar visited the clinic complaining of abdominal obesity. He has a BMI of 29 and has been struggling with weight loss despite having tried several diets and exercise programs. His fasting plasma glucose levels have been above 100 mg/dL, and his triglyceride levels are above 150mg/dL. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high, with systolic blood pressure above 130mmHg and diastolic blood pressure above 85mmHg. He is not currently using any investigational medication and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ALS-L1023 in treating abdominal obesity of metabolic syndrome.

The patient is a premature baby boy born at 26 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 800 grams. He was admitted to the NICU on the first day of his life due to respiratory distress and is currently on mechanical ventilation. His mother has been expressing breast milk and he has been receiving it through a nasogastric tube. He has not yet had any enteral feedings. He has no known congenital anomalies or other health issues. His parents are both in their early thirties and are highly motivated to provide the best care for their son. They live in a nearby town and visit the NICU every day. They have no other children. The baby's mother is a teacher and his father works in IT. They have a good support system from their extended family. The baby's head circumference and length are both below the 10th percentile for his gestational age, but his weight is maintaining at around 900 grams. He has not shown any signs of feeding intolerance

The patient is a 30-year-old woman seeking dental treatment for a lower first molar. She has no significant medical history and is in good overall health. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of buffered articaine as a local anesthetic. She is not allergic to articaine and has not taken any CNS depressants, including alcohol, within the last 48 hours. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She will be asked to report any postoperative pain or discomfort on a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for three days following each appointment. The dentist and patient will be blinded about which anesthetic is being used during the appointments. The patient's participation in the clinical trial will help to determine the effectiveness of buffered articaine and improve dental procedures for patients in the future.

A 42-year-old man diagnosed with HIV infection for the past year comes to the clinic. He has been on HAART and has a CD4+ cell count ranging from 300 to 500 cells/mm3. The patient has not experienced any opportunistic infections or HIV-related malignancies. He has no history of serious hypersensitivity to tetanus toxoid or any vaccine components. The patient is not a drug or alcohol abuser. He had not received any pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine or tetanus toxoid booster within the last 5 years. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effect of thalidomide on immune responses to vaccination with polyvalent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine and tetanus toxoid in HIV-infected patients.

A 60 year old male patient arrived at the clinic with a painful right hip. The X-ray revealed an unstable pertrochanteric fracture of the femur. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is an active person who enjoys walking and hiking. He is currently retired but was previously employed as a construction worker. He has a BMI of 28 and is a nonsmoker. He was prescribed the TFNA for his surgery and is allowed for immediate weight bearing as tolerated. He has agreed to participate in the study and wear the sensor insole in his shoes for up to 3 months after surgical treatment. He understands the content of the patient information/informed consent form and is willing and able to participate in the study according to the clinical investigation plan. He has signed and dated the ethical committee approved written informed consent according to the local regulations.

A 52-year-old male visited the clinic with a history of abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past six months. He also complained of early satiety and occasional vomiting. He had a significant weight loss of approximately 10 kg in the last three months. Upper GI endoscopy revealed a large, ulcerated mass in the gastric antrum. Biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. CT scans showed no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient had an ECOG performance status of 1, and his laboratory workup was within normal limits. The patient provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 60-year-old man visited the clinic with complaints of knee pain and stiffness that has been bothering him for the past year. He is a former smoker and has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. His current medications include an ACE inhibitor and a statin. X-ray imaging showed degenerative changes in the knee joint, confirming the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis. His pain intensity, as measured by the visual analog scale, was 6/10. He has no history of ulcers, asthma or allergic reactions to NSAIDs, kidney disease, or recent myocardial infarction. His blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg, and his blood tests showed normal liver and kidney function with a platelet count of 180 x 10^9/L.

Patient B is a 13-year-old female who has been diagnosed with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). She has been undergoing conservative treatment for the past year but her scoliosis has progressed to a primary Cobb angle greater than 30°. She is considered skeletally immature with a Risser grade of 1 and a skeletal age of 13.5 years. She has not undergone any previous spine surgery and does not have any musculoskeletal or neurologic conditions responsible for the cause of her spine curvature. She has a non-rigid curve and her scoliosis is of all Lenke types. She has no known allergies or intolerance to any device materials and is not obese. She is willing to undergo a minimal invasive non-fusion double rod bipolar posterior spinal implant (Nemost growing domino) to correct her scoliotic curve.

The patient is a 40 year old woman who has been experiencing recurrent pain in the upper right quadrant of her abdomen for the past 6 months. She has been evaluated by her primary care physician and has undergone an ultrasound which revealed the presence of gallbladder polyps. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has been referred to a surgeon for further evaluation and treatment. The surgeon has determined that a cholecystectomy is medically necessary and has offered her the opportunity to participate in a research study comparing single port laparoscopic cholecystectomy versus four port laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has consented to surgery and study participation.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and choking during sleep for the past year. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 38 and has never smoked. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of cardiovascular disease, malignancies, or thyroid disorders. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes and is not taking any medications that could affect hormone secretion. She has not received any sleep apnea treatment. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the influence of nCPAP on metabolic consequences associated with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS). She will be required to undergo a polysomnography to confirm the diagnosis of OSAS and to evaluate plasma inflammatory cytokines, insulin resistance index, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, and overnight cortisol suppression test with 0.25 mg of dexamethasone. She will be randomly assigned to either the nCPAP therapy group or the control group. If assigned to the nCPAP therapy group, she will receive nCPAP therapy for three months and will be re-evaluated for changes in heart rate, cortisol suppression, insulin resistance, blood pressure values, and adipokines.

A 55-year-old man with a history of major depression was referred to the clinic by his psychiatrist. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months, including loss of appetite, insomnia, and feelings of worthlessness. He has been on various antidepressants, but none have been effective. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies. He is not taking any medications currently. He has no history of cardiac problems or arrhythmias. He has no family history of cardiac disease. He is eager to participate in the study as he hopes it will help improve his depression symptoms.

A 30-year-old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital in a COVID-19 hotspot came to the clinic for a routine blood test. She had experienced mild flu-like symptoms, including fever and cough, a month ago, but did not get tested for COVID-19 at that time. She has since recovered and has been feeling well for the past two weeks. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. She has not traveled outside the country in the past six months. Her last menstrual period was two weeks ago. She has no known allergies to any food or medications. She has tested negative for COVID-19 via PCR testing.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who was diagnosed with a desmoid tumor in the abdominal area two months ago. The tumor was initially detected after a routine ultrasound and was confirmed by biopsy. The patient has no significant medical history and has not undergone any treatment for the tumor yet. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. The physical examination shows no abnormalities, and her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. Her liver enzymes, bilirubin, and serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 58-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma with peritoneal metastasis. He underwent surgery, but the cancer was deemed inoperable due to its advanced stage. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy for other diseases except for gastric cancer. His performance status is 2, and he has no other major medical conditions such as infection, diabetes, hypertension, acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina, liver cirrhosis, intestinal pneumonia, or pulmonary fibrosis. His laboratory tests show adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 43-year-old individual scheduled for elective surgery in two weeks. The patient is in good general health and able to provide informed consent for the study. The patient has no known allergies to mupirocin or CHG and is not currently on antibiotic therapy. The patient is willing to complete the study decolonization protocol, which involves an at-home five-day regimen of nasal mupirocin ointment, chlorhexidine gluconate mouth rinse, and CHG pre-operative bathing. The goal of the study is to determine the efficacy of this decolonization protocol in eradicating SA carriage pre-operatively in surgery out-patients, compared to the current standard of care. The patient will be admitted from home the day of the surgery or have the surgery done on an outpatient basis. The study also aims to obtain data on screening requirements, assess treatment adherence and cost-effectiveness, and identify risk factors for SA carriage.

This is a 34-year-old female who is in good general health and does not have any history of hemochromatosis or polycythemia. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the World Mosquito Program Noumea project, which aims to control the spread of mosquito-borne illnesses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya in the community. She has given her written consent to participate in the study and for the collection of a blood sample. She understands that her blood sample will be used for mosquito feeding to generate, maintain, and amplify Aedes aegypti Caledonian lineages carrying the Wolbachia bacteria for the planned insect release program in Noumea. She has been informed that participation in this study does not involve any treatment or medication, and she will not receive any personal benefit from the study. She has also been informed that she will be excluded from the study if she tests positive for arboviruses or if her blood donation is deemed invalid.

32 year-old woman in her first pregnancy at 39 weeks gestation, presenting to the labor and delivery unit with contractions every 10 minutes. The patient has a history of obesity but is otherwise healthy. She desires pain relief during labor and is interested in participating in the study. She has no known allergies to opioids and has not received any other analgesics during labor. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo an intrathecal injection.

A 54-year-old male patient was diagnosed with recurrent renal cell carcinoma (RCC) 6 months ago. He had undergone a nephrectomy for the primary tumor 3 years ago. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril 20 mg daily. His last physical exam and laboratory studies were performed yesterday and showed the following results: BP: 130/80 mmHg HR: 78 beats/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 12.2 g/dL WBC: 7500 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 30 U/L ALT: 35 U/L Alk P: 99 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dL Cr: 0.9 mg/dL Urine dipstick: negative for proteinuria. The patient has measurable disease with multiple pulmonary and hepatic metastases. The patient has no history of hematologic malignancies or active CNS metastases. The patient has not received any systemic treatment for RCC, and his performance status is 80%. The patient has given written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing increased stress for the past 6 months due to her job and personal life. She reports feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and having trouble sleeping. Her stress levels have been consistently high, with a perceived stress score of 60 on the visual analog scale. She is otherwise healthy with no chronic illnesses or mental health disorders. She is fluent in German and able to provide informed consent. She is not currently undergoing any psychotherapeutic treatment or participating in any other stress management programs. She is interested in trying hypnotherapy as a means of coping with her stress.

55-year-old Cantonese-speaking Chinese woman who has been diagnosed with normal-tension glaucoma and is attending a university-affiliated glaucoma clinic in Hong Kong. She has been experiencing visual field defects with normal intraocular pressure (<21 mmHg) over a period of twenty-four hours, and normal chamber-angle anatomy. She has consented to participate in a study to identify the prevalence of psychopathology in patients with normal-tension glaucoma in Hong Kong. She has no history of psychoses, psychiatric conditions that require hospitalization, or any other acute or chronic diseases. She is not taking any medication.

A 45-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician due to persistently elevated serum aminotransferases. She has a history of hypobetalipoproteinemia, which was diagnosed in her early 20s. She had no previous symptoms and was asymptomatic during the initial diagnosis. She was not treated with any medication, as she had no dyslipidemia or cardiovascular disease. Her family history is significant for hypobetalipoproteinemia in her father and brother. She is currently not taking any medication and has no significant past medical history. Her physical examination was unremarkable, except for mild hepatomegaly. Laboratory tests showed elevated serum aminotransferases and decreased LDL-cholesterol and Apolipoprotein B levels. Genetic testing revealed two novel truncating mutations in the Apolipoprotein B gene. She was offered to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the outcomes of these mutations. Her family members, who do not carry the mutations, were also invited to participate as the control group.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 5 years ago. She presents with cough, fatigue, and shortness of breath. Her physical examination is remarkable for diminished breath sounds on the right side of the chest. Her CT scan showed a mass in the right lung with mediastinal lymphadenopathy. She has no history of EGFR or ALK mutation. Her performance status is 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group criteria. Her weight has been stable for the past 6 months. She is currently taking vitamin D and calcium supplements. She has no known allergies to any medications or supplements. She has signed the informed consent and is willing to comply with the study treatment and follow-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis. She has a score of 3 on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS). She has no history of epileptic seizures and is free from dementia as determined by the Mini Mental State Exam (MMSE>=24). She can walk on the treadmill without partial body weight support harness for 5 minutes at her preferred walking speed. She is currently taking MS-specific drugs and her medication regime is stable. She has adequate hearing and vision capabilities. She is willing to commit to the treadmill training program and participate in all of the assessments. She provides informed written consent and is willing to be randomized to any of the 2 study arms. She is not participating in any other intensive exercise program, and she does not use any walking aids.

The COPD patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease for the past 2 years. She has a history of smoking for 35 years and quit smoking 2 years ago. She has mild symptoms of cough, expectoration, and shortness of breath. She takes inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids daily. She has no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, hematological, endocrine, or neurological diseases other than COPD. She has clear consciousness and can communicate with others normally. She understands the full study protocol and has high adherence. She has signed the written informed consent herself.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) who is still able to walk independently. He has been experiencing difficulty in running and climbing stairs since the age of 5. He has a positive family history of DMD, as his older brother was also diagnosed with the disease and lost his ability to walk at the age of 11. The patient has no history of other chronic illnesses or previous use of steroids. The patient's parents are interested in exploring alternative treatment options for DMD and are willing to participate in a clinical trial. They have been informed about the potential benefits and risks of Tamoxifen treatment and have provided signed informed consent. The patient will undergo a medical evaluation to determine eligibility for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced breast cancer. She has had several rounds of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery, but the cancer has spread to other parts of her body. She is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and pain in her bones. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She lives alone and is retired. She enjoys reading, watching TV, and spending time with her grandchildren. She has never participated in a clinical trial before, but she is willing to undergo pre- and post-treatment biopsies. Her tumor has been confirmed to overexpress EphA2, making her eligible for the trial. She is not currently on any hormonal therapy, and she understands that she cannot receive any other investigational agents or therapies for her cancer while participating in the trial. She is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study and for at least 3 months after completion of EphA2 siRNA-DOPC therapy. She has no known allergies to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to DOPC, Magnevist, or fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG). She has no history of bleeding disorders, coagulopathy, or any tumor involving major vessels. She has not had a cerebrovascular accident (CVA, stroke) or subarachnoid hemorrhage within the past 6 months. She has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease, and her blood pressure is well-controlled. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to undergo MRI and PET scans as required by the trial protocol.

A 32-year-old woman, who is gravida 2 para 1, presented to a tertiary women's hospital in Singapore for the delivery of her second child. She has a history of iron-deficiency anaemia and was prescribed iron therapy during her antenatal visits. During the delivery, she experienced heavy bleeding and was given a red cell transfusion. She delivered a healthy baby boy without any complications. She is now eligible to participate in a retrospective survey of obstetric red cell transfusion at the hospital.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy female who has recently given birth at full term. She is currently in the first six months of lactation and has not experienced any lactation problems. She has a healthy dietary intake, consuming a mix of vegetarian and omnivore foods. She is willing to donate breast milk samples and has agreed to consume 8oz. of pomegranate juice daily for a week leading up to the second collection. She has no history of any medical conditions, allergies or surgeries. She has a normal body mass index (BMI) and is not taking any medications or supplements.

This study is looking for individuals who are candidates for a kidney transplant at the National Institutes of Health Clinical Center. The ideal candidate should not be on any immunosuppressive drug therapy at the time of or 2 months prior to enrollment. They should also not have any active malignancy or any history of a hematogenous malignancy or lymphoma. Patients with primary, cutaneous basal cell or squamous cell cancers may be enrolled providing the lesions are appropriately treated prior to transplant. The candidate should not have any significant coagulopathy or requirement for anticoagulation therapy that would contraindicate protocol allograft biopsies. The platelet count should be more than 100,000/mm(3). The individual should not have any known immunodeficiency syndrome or any history of cardiac insufficiency, major vascular disease, symptomatic coronary artery disease, systemic or pulmonary edema, or any condition that would likely increase the risk of protocol participation or confound the interpretation of the data. They should not have any history of sensitization to rabbits or extensive exposure to rabbits. The ideal candidate should be willing to comply with protocol monitoring and therapy, including, among others, a history of compliance, circumstances where compliance with protocol requirements is feasible and access to urgent medical services or access to anti-rejection drugs after the research protocol is completed.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male presented with abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation. He reported a history of colon cancer in his mother and father, both of whom were diagnosed in their 60s. He underwent a colonoscopy, which revealed a 3 cm adenocarcinoma in the ascending colon. Pathology confirmed the diagnosis of stage III colon cancer, with T3N1M0 disease. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. His physical exam is unremarkable. He has no peripheral neuropathy and his liver and renal function tests are normal. His performance status is 1, and his ECOG score is 1. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is willing to participate in the study and give written informed consent.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with stage IIB mycosis fungoides (MF) with multiple skin lesions, who has failed at least one prior standard therapy. The patient has a skin lesion of at least 2 cm in size, which is amenable to radiation and at least two additional measurable skin lesions distant from the radiation site. The patient is currently receiving romidepsin and has documented stable disease or partial response. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of over 6 months. The patient has normal organ and marrow function with leukocytes of 3,000/mcL, absolute neutrophil count of 1,200/mcL, platelets of 80,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal limits, AST/ALT within 2.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal, and creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the last 4 weeks or topical therapy within the last 2 weeks. The patient is not receiving any other investigational agents and has no known history of pre-existing autoimmune disease or allergy to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition. The patient is not receiving systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications. The patient must agree to use adequate contraception and must have the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent document.

A 26-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy is eligible for this study. She must have enrolled in prenatal care before 20 weeks gestation and should have a negative CMV IgG serological testing indicating CMV seronegative status or a non-primary CMV infection. She should not have any known major fetal anomalies or demise and should not be planning to terminate the pregnancy. The patient should not have any maternal immune impairment, such as HIV infection or be on anti-rejection medications due to organ transplant. The patient should not have any pre-enrollment ultrasound suggestive of established fetal CMV infection or positive fetal CMV results from culture or PCR. Additionally, the patient should have no intention of delivering outside of the University of Alabama at Birmingham hospital. If the patient meets these eligibility criteria, she may be recruited for this study which aims to prevent maternal CMV infections during pregnancy through a brief prenatal clinic-based CMV risk-reduction behavioral intervention.

The patient is a 49-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer that has metastasized to the brain. Her past medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled by medication. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the breast cancer diagnosis and testing showed HER2-positive status. A recent MRI revealed brain metastases that are measurable by RANO-BM criteria. The patient has not received any treatment for the brain metastases yet. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80 and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1. Her left ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. She has not received any investigational agents in the last 28 days and has no history of malignancy other than breast cancer. She has not undergone any major surgery in the last 4 weeks and has no indication for immediate local therapy. She has no history of leptomeningeal involvement and has not received any other anticancer therapy, including radiation therapy or chemotherapy, in the last 3 weeks. She has a life expectancy of at least 3 months and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraception.

This is a 42-year-old woman who is a frequent smoker and has a history of smoking for over 15 years. She is coming to the Vancouver General Hospital Emergency Department with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she is stable at this time. She has been smoking about a pack a day and has tried to quit smoking multiple times in the past, but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in quitting smoking and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help her quit. She speaks English and is able to provide a telephone number for follow-up.

This clinical trial is a non-interventional study that is open to male or female patients aged 18 years or older who are undergoing varicose vein procedures, lower limb amputation or lower limb bypass surgery. The patient in question is a 50 year old man who has been experiencing varicose veins in his legs for the past 6 months. The veins are unsightly and have caused him some discomfort, but he has not experienced any other symptoms. He has been referred to a vascular surgeon for treatment of his varicose veins. The surgeon has explained to him about the clinical trial and the opportunity to participate in the study. The patient has agreed to participate and has given his informed consent.

A 48 year old female is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic nephrectomy for kidney cancer. She has no significant past medical history and does not take any long-term medications. She has no history of diabetes mellitus or neuritis. Her BMI is 26 kg/m2. She has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in the affected area for the past few weeks. She has been informed about the intravenous PCA for postoperative pain control and agrees to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old female presents with abdominal discomfort, bloating, and occasional nausea. She reports a history of gastritis and has been diagnosed with chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) through a biopsy. She has tested negative for Helicobacter pylori infection.
