The patient has no history of upper gastrointestinal surgery, peptic ulcers, GERD or esophageal stricture. She has no history of malignant diseases or drug allergies. She is not currently pregnant, nursing, or using birth control. The patient has not participated in any other investigational studies within the past four weeks. She does not have any other medical conditions such as heart failure, liver disease, renal disease, hypertension or diabetes that are exclusion criteria for this study. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Gastropyloric Complex Capsules in the treatment of chronic atrophic gastritis.

A 55-year-old woman was referred to the outpatient endocrinology clinic for evaluation of suspected Cushing's syndrome. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and osteoporosis. She is postmenopausal and has not had a menstrual period for 5 years. She is currently taking anti-hypertensive medications and metformin for diabetes. She has no history of steroid use or chronic inflammatory disease. She has not been hospitalized for any infectious disease in the past 3 months. Her serum creatinine level is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome.

A 12-year-old child is brought to the clinic by his parents with complaints of fever for the past 24 hours. The child has a history of malaria infection in the past. On examination, the child has an axillary temperature of 38.5 degrees Celsius and a Plasmodium falciparum density of 5000 asexual forms per cubic millimetre. The child weighs 30 kg and is a resident of the area covered by the investigating centre. The child has no signs of severe malaria, no history of repeated convulsions or respiratory distress, and is able to drink and eat normally. There is no history of allergies or serious concomitant diseases. The child has not taken any antimalarials in the past seven days.

A 3-month-old healthy Chinese infant boy is being brought by his parents to participate in the study. He was born at full term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. He has no history of neurological disorders, chronic diseases or convulsions. He is currently not taking any medication, and his weight is within the normal range for his age. His parents have agreed to adhere to the study regimen and are willing to complete the

The patient is a 45 year old Japanese man who has been diagnosed with hypercholesterolemia. He has a family history of high cholesterol and has been previously treated with lipid-lowering drugs. His most recent lipid profile showed a total cholesterol level of 250 mg/dL and LDL cholesterol level of 160 mg/dL. He has normal liver function tests and is generally in good health. He is currently not taking any medication for his cholesterol and is willing to participate in a 52-week observational study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Zetia as a monotherapy or in combination with other lipid-lowering drugs. He understands that this study is non-interventional and will not involve any changes to his current treatment plan. He agrees to attend regular follow-up visits and provide information about his cholesterol levels, as well as any adverse events that may occur during the study.

62F with a history of chronic knee pain and stiffness for the past year. The patient reports pain with walking, climbing stairs, and standing for long periods of time. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, physical therapy, and weight loss, which have provided minimal relief. She reports no prior knee injuries or surgeries. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial and lateral joint lines, crepitus with passive range of motion, and mild swelling. Knee X-rays show mild to moderate osteoarthritis with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. The patient has no significant medical history, is not taking any medications, and has no allergies. She is able to walk independently with a cane. The patient is interested in non-surgical treatment options and is willing to receive intraarticular injections.

As this clinical trial is focused on establishing comprehensive thyroid tissue and data banks to understand the consequences of the Chernobyl accident, a patient description is not applicable. This trial is seeking patients who have already been diagnosed with thyroid tumors and have undergone thyroid operations. The inclusion criteria states that patients must have been born after 26th April 1967 and be from the contaminated oblasts of Belarus, the Russian Federation, or Ukraine. The trial is not seeking new patients for treatment or diagnosis.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is bothered by the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines. She has never undergone any type of aesthetic treatment or procedure for glabellar lines before and is interested in a long-term solution. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the protocol. She is not currently pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy during the study. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to Dysport or its excipients and does not have any infections at the proposed injection sites. She is not diagnosed with myasthenia gravis, Eaton Lambert syndrome or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and does not have any contraindications for the use of Dysport.

A 30-year-old male presents with fever, chills, and headache for the past two days. He recently returned from a trip to Sarawak, Malaysia, and visited a rural area where malaria is endemic. He reports taking malaria prophylaxis medication as recommended, but still developed symptoms. On physical examination, the patient has a temperature of 38.5°C, and mild splenomegaly is noted. A blood smear is taken and sent for microscopy, which is inconclusive. The patient provides written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the sensitivity, specificity, and practical value of new molecular diagnostic assays for detection of Plasmodium knowlesi. The patient is eligible for the study, and further testing will be done to determine the presence of P. knowlesi.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of chronic alcoholism, who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate liver impairment. He has had multiple hospitalizations for hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, and variceal bleeding. He is currently stable on his medications, including lactulose and rifaximin. He has not had any recent alcohol intake and has been compliant with his medications. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the effects of conivaptan in subjects with mild and moderate liver impairment versus subjects with normal liver function, as he is interested in potentially improving his liver function and overall health.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of lung cancer diagnosed four months ago. He has completed first line doublet chemotherapy and had a stable disease at the initial evaluation scan. He is currently receiving maintenance therapy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him manage his symptoms and improve his prognosis. He has access to the internet, a mobile phone, and the Danish digital secure mail system (E-boks) and is willing to fill out weekly questionnaires to monitor his symptoms. He has a performance status of 1 and has given his written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 45-year-old male with a family history of colon cancer presents with a recent change in bowel habits and mild abdominal discomfort. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical exam is unremarkable. Colonoscopy is recommended for further evaluation. The patient has no known allergies and is between the ages of 20 and 80, meeting the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial comparing polyethylene glycol and sodium picosulfate alone or combined. He has no history of colon resection, gastrointestinal obstruction, ileus, intestinal perforation, toxic megacolon, or active stage of inflammatory bowel disease. He also does not have congestive heart failure, acute cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled arterial hypertension, severe liver cirrhosis, or renal failure.

The patient is a 45-year-old Latina woman who has recently completed treatment for breast cancer. She has been experiencing fatigue, anxiety, and sleep disturbance since her treatment ended. She has a supportive spouse who is willing to participate in the study as her caregiver. She speaks both English and Spanish fluently. She is interested in improving her overall health and adhering to the ACS guidelines for cancer prevention. She is willing to participate in a 12-week intervention that integrates telephone coaching and printed materials about healthy lifestyle behaviors. She is excited to learn more about how to manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

Mrs. Johnson is a 60-year-old widow who has been experiencing feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has also been drinking more frequently and heavily, especially since the death of her husband six months ago. She reports drinking at least six drinks per day, and often more on weekends. She does not have a history of drug abuse or dependence but has struggled with alcohol addiction in the past. She has never received formal treatment for either her depression or alcohol dependence. She has no history of psychosis or opioid or cocaine abuse. She is interested in participating in the study as she wants to address both her depression and alcohol use. She is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and has a history of hypothyroidism. She lives alone but has regular visits from her adult children.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who works at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and has been selected to participate in a clinical trial for SARS-CoV-2 detection. She has not tested positive for the virus before and is generally in good health. The trial aims to determine the accuracy of using saliva samples only or a combination of saliva and midturbinate swabs for detection of SARS-CoV-2 compared to the standard nasopharyngeal (NP) swab. The patient will be required to provide 1 or 2 saliva samples and 1 or 2 nasal swabs alongside their NP swab when they undergo routine staff screening. If the NP swab result is positive, the participant will be required to have another NP swab, and provide 1 or 2 saliva samples and 1 or 2 nasal swabs at the same time. If the NP swab result is negative, they will provide 1 or 2 saliva samples and 1 or 2 nasal swabs the next time they undergo NP swab screening. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have any issues with providing saliva samples or midturbinate swabs.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. She has no curative treatment options and is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to swallow and retain oral medication. She has measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 criteria present and has experienced radiologically confirmed progression on prior therapy. Her platelets are 120,000/uL, hemoglobin is 11.5 g/dL, and absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 2,500/uL. Her total bilirubin is within institutional upper limit of normal (ULN), and her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are both within 2.5 x institutional ULN. Her creatinine is within ULN, and she has no history of serious mood disorders or cardiac events. She has not received prior immunotherapy with anti-PD1/PDL1 therapy for the mTNBC. She is willing to undergo a biopsy and has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or any drugs administered on the protocol. She understands the investigational nature of the study and is willing to sign an Independent Ethics Committee/Institutional Review Board approved written informed consent form prior to receiving any study-related procedure.

A 68-year-old female presented with a complaint of blurred vision in her left eye for the past few months. She had a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which were well controlled with medications. She denied any other ocular or systemic symptoms. On ophthalmologic examination, her visual acuity was 20/60 in the left eye, and 20/20 in the right eye. Dilated fundus examination revealed the presence of wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in the left eye. She was diagnosed with neovascular AMD and was started on ranibizumab, receiving three consecutive induction treatments. Following the induction phase, the patient was assessed for the time to recurrence of neovascularization and will be followed for a year. The patient has no other ocular or systemic diseases that could affect the visual acuity of the studied eye.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has a body mass index (BMI) of 42 and is scheduled for laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery at the Royal Victoria Hospital. The patient has a history of obstructive sleep apnea and is currently using a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine at night. Due to the patient's obesity and obstructive sleep apnea, the anesthesiologist has recommended an awake intubation for the surgery. The patient has no other significant medical history and is able to communicate fluently in both English and French. The patient has consented to participate in the clinical trial and will be randomized to either the fiberoptic bronchoscope or video assisted laryngoscopy group for the awake intubation.

A 10-year-old boy was diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis at the age of 5. He has been on prednisone for the past 3 years with a dose of 0.5 mg/kg/day. He had one vertebral compression fracture at the age of 8. His past medical history is significant for mild asthma and eczema. He is allergic to penicillin. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He attends school and is in the 4th grade. He is an active child and likes to play soccer and basketball. He takes daily calcium and vitamin D supplements. His height is at the 60th percentile for his age, and his weight is at the 50th percentile. He denies any pain or discomfort in his back or limbs. His laboratory tests are within the normal range. His bone age is 8.5 years old.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents to the urology clinic with complaints of difficulty in passing urine. She reports that she has to strain and push hard to empty her bladder and is unable to completely empty it. She also complains of a weak urinary stream and occasional urinary incontinence. The patient reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, and they have been progressively worsening. She denies any history of urinary tract infections or kidney stones. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals a distended bladder with a palpable suprapubic mass. Her bladder scan shows a post-void residual urine volume of 80cc, and her maximum flow rate is 10cc/sec. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets the inclusion criteria. She is otherwise healthy with no contraindications for Tamsulosin or Prazosin.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with severe COPD two years ago. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years, and he quit smoking after his diagnosis. He has been hospitalized twice in the last year due to exacerbations of COPD. He has been on home oxygen therapy for the past six months. He lives with his wife, who helps him with his daily activities. He has difficulty walking and gets out of breath easily. He has a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of less than 50% of theoretical. He has two or more moderate or severe exacerbations per year, separated by at least 4 weeks after the end of previous treatment or 6 weeks from the start in cases that have not been treated. He is considered clinically stable for the past six weeks since his last exacerbation of COPD. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis (UC) for the past 3 years. She has been experiencing recurring episodes of inflammation limited to the mucosal layer of the colon, which have been managed with medication. She has been considering surgical options for her condition and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a new technique called Close Rectal Ileo Pouch Anal Anastomosis (CR-IPAA). She is willing to undergo the CRD procedure and has provided written informed consent. She is matched for age, sex, and disease with a control group of UC patients who have undergone the conventional Ileo Pouch Anal Anastomosis (C-IPAA) procedure. She has no history of malignancy or psychiatric disease and is able to assess follow-up.

The patient is a 68-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are currently under control with medication. He lives alone and reports a decreased interest in food lately. He admits to skipping meals and has lost about 5 kg in the past 2 months. He also complains of a decreased sense of smell and taste. He reports that he used to enjoy cooking and eating spicy foods, but now everything tastes bland. He denies any allergies or respiratory disorders. His cognitive function is intact, as evidenced by a Folstein test score of 27. He has no acute illnesses at the time of the test, and his life expectancy is greater than 6 months.

67 year old woman with a history of ischemic stroke presenting with complaints of difficulty with visual tasks, particularly involving reading and driving. Patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. On examination, the patient has a right homonymous hemianopsia with sparing of fixation in the left eye. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial testing the Functional Outcome Measure for those with visual field defects. The patient is able to provide consent and has no contraindications to visual stimulation. The patient speaks and reads English fluently and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no severe cognitive impairment, complete blindness, or physical limitations. The onset of visual field defect occurred more than 3 months prior to enrollment.

39 yo F living in a malaria-endemic area of Ethiopia. She presents to the local health center with fever, chills, and headache. She is diagnosed with uncomplicated malaria and is treated with artemether-lumefantrine (AL). As part of the study, she is asked to provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. After providing consent, she is asked to complete a short questionnaire to collect information on her demographics, travel history, access to malaria interventions, and other risk factors for malaria. She is also asked to participate in a cross-sectional household survey, which will measure malaria prevalence in her community and assess household and individual risk factors for malaria. She is randomly assigned to the targeted mass drug administration (tMDA) arm of the study, which means that she will receive a single round of mass drug administration with chloroquine (CQ) and primaquine (PQ) within a 100-meter radius of the passively detected index case. She is not excluded from the study based on any of the exclusion criteria, and she is not phenotypically G6PD deficient or pregnant, so she is eligible to receive primaquine. Over the course of the study, she will be monitored for any adverse events and will be asked to report any symptoms she experiences. She will also be asked to participate in follow-up surveys to assess the acceptability of tMDA in her community and to provide cost data. By participating in this study, she is contributing to the evaluation of tMDA as a potential strategy for malaria elimination in Ethiopia.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been receiving treatment for the disorder for several years now, but with little success. He has been taking two antipsychotic medications for the past month, but his symptoms have not improved. He has a history of hospitalization due to severe episodes of psychosis. He is unemployed and lives with his parents. He is single and has no children. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies and has never participated in a clinical trial before. His BMI is 28. His lab results show no significant abnormalities. He is considering participating in a clinical trial to try and improve his symptoms.

32F with T6 ASIA C paraplegia due to a motor vehicle accident 4 years ago. She reports chronic pain in both legs and lower back, with a pain intensity of 7/10 on a numerical rating scale. The pain interferes with her daily activities, especially with sitting for long hours in her wheelchair. She has been on various pain medications, including opioids, but has not found significant relief. She has also tried physical therapy and acupuncture, but the benefits were short-lived. She reports feeling depressed and frustrated due to her pain and its impact on her life. She is interested in the study and has access to a computer with a webcam and microphone. She speaks fluent English and has no history of mental health problems or drug/alcohol dependence. She has not undergone previous treatment with CT or hypnosis for pain. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent headaches and episodes of confusion. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is otherwise healthy. He has been evaluated by a neurologist who suspects that he may have primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS) and has referred him to participate in a clinical trial. He has been informed about the study and has given his consent to participate. He will undergo a lumbar puncture to exclude potential alternative diagnoses and will be evaluated with MRI and high-resolution intracranial vessel wall imaging. The aim of the study is to determine the utility of these imaging techniques for the diagnosis and disease activity assessment of intracranial vasculitis. The patient will receive up to 4 imaging examinations at predefined intervals as part of this study. The imaging findings will be correlated with clinical and any available laboratory or pathologic data. The target accrual is 10 patients for this pilot study.

A 45 year old male patient with a history of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis and large hepatocellular carcinoma was referred to the hospital for liver resection. The patient had no other significant medical history and had not undergone any prior surgeries. Upon examination, it was determined that the patient was a candidate for open liver resection. The target bleeding site was identified as a generalized bleeding that persisted on the cut surface of the liver, which could not be controlled by conventional methods. The patient was willing and able to complete the clinical trial procedures and signed a written informed consent to participate in the trial. The patient was not suffering from any coagulation disorder, Klatskin tumour, cirrhosis, re-hepatectomies, or biliary resections. The patient had not participated in any concurrent clinical trial with a medical device or medicinal product or with interfering endpoints. The patient had not received any concurrent or previous therapy with systemic pharmacologic agents promoting blood clotting. The patient had no known allergy or hypersensitivity to any component of the investigational treatments Hemopatch® , riboflavin, or proteins of bovine origin. The patient was not pregnant or breastfeeding and was able to understand the nature and extent of the trial and the procedures required. During surgery, there was no evidence of an infected wound area or persistent major bleeding after primary hemostasis.

A 25-year-old female with no history of dental restorations or bleaching procedures presented to the dental school clinic at the Federal University of Goias located in Goiania. She expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and dental sensitivity associated with Combined Bleaching Technique. The patient has upper and lower anterior teeth of A2 or darker shade compared to the Vita Classical. She has no carious lesions or non-carious lesions such as abfraction, erosion, or abrasion. The patient has no visible cracks or defects on the dental enamel surfaces of her upper and lower anterior teeth. She is not currently using fixed orthodontic appliances and does not have any parafunctional habits. The patient is not a smoker and is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of severe dental dimming or any oral pathology. The patient will undergo a dental prophylaxis with pumice and water to remove extrinsic stains two weeks prior to the beginning of the tooth whitening procedure.

A 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with moderate to severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and has not received CPAP therapy before. His AHI is above 15 events per hour of sleep. He has a body mass index less than 30kg/m2 and does not take ARBs or angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors for blood pressure control. He does not have a history of heart failure, myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, stroke, or diabetes mellitus. He has normal renal function and does not have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma. He has not smoked within the past year and has normal blood pressure. He is not taking any over-the-counter supplements that affect the cardiovascular system. He is a male of non-childbearing potential. He is interested in participating in a study to improve his 24-hour blood pressure in OSA and is willing to undergo CPAP therapy as prescribed by his doctor.

A 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22.5 presents for a Phase I clinical trial. He has no prior history of significant disease or disorder and has suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture. He is willing to comply with study procedures and restrictions, and has provided signed and dated, written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures. The subject is sexually active and agrees to use barrier contraception during the study. He has no known history of allergy or hypersensitivity to carbapenem or cephalosporin antibiotics or any other investigational product to be administered as part of the study. The subject has not experienced any clinically significant illnesses, medical/surgical procedures, or trauma within 4 weeks prior to the first administration of investigational product. The subject has normal physical examination, ECG, clinical chemistry, haematology, and urinalysis results as judged by the Investigator.

The patient is a 50-year-old French woman who had a sudden onset of severe headache and vomiting about 24 hours ago. She was brought to the emergency department with a decreased level of consciousness and right-sided weakness. A CT scan showed a large intracerebral hemorrhage in the left temporal lobe. She has a past medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She is not on any antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy. Her vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 145/90 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. Her temperature is normal and her blood glucose level is within the normal range. She has no history of alcohol abuse. The Glasgow Coma Scale score is 6. The family has been informed about the poor prognosis and the possibility of organ donation after brain death. They have agreed to the withholding of therapy and the patient will be included in the study to validate the predictive score of brain death in severe stroke patients.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of sickle cell anaemia (HbSS). The patient has been experiencing albuminuria, as confirmed by three positive urine samples taken one day apart, with a value of albuminuria assessed by ACR over 3 mg/mmol and inferior to 100 mg/mmol. The patient has not received hydroxycarbamide treatment in the past 6 months and has not received chronic blood transfusion or transfusion in the last 3 months. The patient has no history of hypertension treated with antihypertensive agents belonging to the pharmacological class of RAS inhibitors. The patient does not have any symptoms suggestive of urinary tract infection or gross haematuria. The patient is not known to have any primary kidney disease and does not have any systemic conditions that could result in a glomerulopathy not related to SCD (e.g. diabetes mellitus, active hepatitis B or C infections, HIV infection, systemic lupus erythematosus, inflammatory arthropathies). The patient does not have chronic kidney disease with an eGFR < 60 mL/min per 1.73 m2 or eGFR ≥ 140 ml/min/1,73m². The patient is not requiring long-term treatment with drugs potentially nephrotoxic or ACE inhibitors or ARBs within the 3 months before inclusion regardless of the indication. The patient does not require long-term treatment with non-steroid anti-inflammatory drugs or any treatment that can modify kidney function in the last 3 months. The patient is not known to be infected with HIV and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has agreed to use a highly effective form of contraception during the trial and for 3 months after hydroxycarbamide discontinuation. The patient has signed and dated the Informed Consent Form and is covered by an insurance scheme according to local regulatory requirements.

A 60-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years presented with a chronic cough and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with COPD and was prescribed bronchodilators and inhalers. He has been experiencing dyspnea, especially when he is active, and his mMRC Dyspnea Scale Score is 2. He has been referred for regular inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation. His current medications include albuterol, ipratropium, and fluticasone/salmeterol. He has no history of heart disease or implanted cardiac devices. His ECG and echocardiogram are normal. His oxygen saturation levels are within normal range without supplemental oxygen. His spirometry results indicate hyperinflation with residual volume (RV) of 150% of the predicted value. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old boy who had a liver transplant 2 years ago due to biliary atresia. He is currently taking tacrolimus as part of his immunosuppressive regimen. His last SD of tacrolimus levels was 2.5, indicating variability in medication adherence. He and his guardian both speak English fluently and are able to understand the study procedures. He has been seen regularly in the transplant center's clinic for follow up care. He has no history of biopsy-proven rejection within the last six months, and has not been diagnosed with Hepatitis C. He is not actively psychotic or severely disoriented, and is medically stable.

A 32-year-old woman and her husband have been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. They have no children and no history of infertility. The woman has regular menstrual cycles and no known medical conditions. Her husband has no known fertility issues, and his semen analysis shows more than 15 million motile sperm. They have undergone a fertility workup, which showed bilateral tubal patency. They have consented to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of vaginal progesterone after COH with IUI on pregnancy rates. The woman has no allergies to prescribed vaginal progesterone. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up appointments. She is between the ages of 21 and 43.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been the primary caregiver for her husband with Alzheimer's disease for the past two years. She has been experiencing increased stress and emotional distress as her husband's condition has worsened, and she is worried about how she will cope when he eventually passes away. She has a history of depression and anxiety, which has been managed with medication and therapy. She currently takes sertraline and attends counseling once a week. She lives with her husband in a long-term care facility and visits him daily. She is interested in participating in a group therapy program to help prepare for her husband's eventual death and to mitigate the risk of complicated grief.

A 16-year-old male with a history of cystic fibrosis presents to the clinic with complaints of bloating, abdominal pain, and diarrhea for the last 6 months. He has lost about 7 kg during this time. He has a history of chronic lung disease and has been on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy for the last 3 years. He complains that his symptoms have not improved with the current dose of enzyme replacement therapy. He has no history of recent respiratory exacerbation. He denies any significant medical history other than cystic fibrosis. He is currently on a high-calorie diet and has been compliant with his medications. He is a nonsmoker and does not use any illicit drugs. On examination, the patient is thin, and his BMI is 18.3. He has diffuse abdominal tenderness with no rebound. His bowel sounds are hypoactive. Laboratory evaluation reveals a low serum albumin level, and stool elastase is less than 50 μg/g stool. The sweat test confirms the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. The patient is compliant with his medications but still has significant symptoms. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Creon N and Creon® on fat digestion.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been struggling with cocaine addiction for several years. He primarily smokes cocaine and has tried to quit several times but has been unsuccessful. He has not sought drug treatment but is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him overcome his addiction. He is currently not taking any medication for his addiction or any other mental health condition. He has no history of autoimmune disease, immune deficiency or hypersensitivity to vaccines. He is HIV negative and does not use drugs intravenously. He is in good overall health and has no abnormal laboratory test results. He is able to give informed consent and is committed to complying with the study protocol. He meets all of the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

55-year-old female with a history of chronic fatigue, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss presented to her primary care physician with complaints of abdominal discomfort and jaundice. She was referred to a gastroenterologist who performed a liver biopsy which revealed the presence of granulomas. She was subsequently referred to the Lyon Hepatitis Granulomatous (LHG) study at the Croix-Rousse Hospital in Lyon, France. The study aims to better characterize granulomatous hepatitis and severe hepatic sarcoidosis in terms of etiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. The patient meets the eligibility criteria as she has a diagnosis of granulomatous hepatitis and is being followed by the Hepato-gastroenterology department at Croix-Rousse Hospital. She has consented to participate in the study and will be included in the analysis of the 596 patients who had a liver biopsy showing granulomas. The LHG study will provide a better understanding of the disease and may contribute to the development of more effective treatments.

A 52 year old female from Jordan, who has recently been diagnosed with non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the prevalence of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in participants with NSCLC. She has not participated in any other clinical trials involving investigational agents within the past 30 days. The patient is willing to provide informed consent to participate in this non-interventional, local, multicenter, cross-sectional study. She has no history of any other primary malignancies and has not had a fine needle aspiration sample.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of fatigue, shortness of breath, palpitations, and chest pain. He has been to several cardiologists and has undergone multiple tests, including echocardiography, electrocardiogram (ECG), and blood work, but the results were inconclusive. The patient was referred to undergo a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) test for suspected inflammatory cardiomyopathy. He has never undergone any cardiovascular surgery or intervention in the last 90 days. He is not diagnosed with any other heart diseases such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy. He is currently not on any medication for heart disease or any other condition. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His occupation is an accountant, and he leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is able to provide informed consent and is above 18 years of age.

This is a 56 year-old male with a longstanding history of diabetes and diabetic retinopathy. He has been managed with multiple laser treatments and intravitreal injections in both eyes, but unfortunately, he developed a vitreous hemorrhage in his left eye. The decision was made to proceed with pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in his left eye. During the surgery, the corneal epithelium was debrided to obtain a better view of the surgical field. Postoperatively, the patient experienced delayed corneal epithelial healing, which led to recurrent corneal epithelial defects. The patient was referred to the ophthalmology service for further management. He was approached to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of autologous serum eye drops for promoting corneal epithelial wound healing in patients undergoing PPV for diabetic retinopathy. The patient was eligible for the study and agreed to participate.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman presented with moderate to severe hot flashes associated with sweating and palpitations. She had a history of irregular menstrual periods and had not menstruated for the past 8 months. She denied any history of breast or ovarian cancer. She currently takes tamoxifen for the treatment of breast cancer, which was diagnosed two years ago. She has completed her chemotherapy and radiation therapy and is on a stable dose of tamoxifen for at least 8 weeks. She reported an average of 10 hot flashes per day, which interferes with her daily activities and sleep quality. She has no history of hypertension or suicidal tendency. She does not take any herbal or dietary supplements. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including completing a VMS episode event log (patient diary). She provided written informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer that was diagnosed 2 years ago. She underwent a left breast lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the lungs 6 months ago and started on hormonal therapy with an aromatase inhibitor, but her disease progressed after 3 months. She was recently started on bicalutamide and her serum tumor markers showed a slight decrease. Her HER2 status was negative, and her AR expression was ≥ 10%. She has no other significant medical history and her performance status is good. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and her pregnancy test was negative within the last 7 days. She is willing to undergo PSMA-based PET imaging using 18F-DCFPyL to evaluate the expression of PSMA in her metastatic breast cancer.

The patient is a 24-year-old female with Fitzpatrick skin type II. She has no history of severe reactions from exposure to sunlight but experiences mild sunburn on occasion. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to adhesives in patches and is able to evaluate the skin in and around the test sites. She does not have diabetes requiring medication or any significant skin disease. She has no history of asthma or other severe respiratory disease, nor does she have any known immunological disorders such as HIV, AIDS, lupus, or rheumatoid arthritis. She has no history of skin cancer or mastectomy involving removal of lymph nodes draining the test sites. She does not have epilepsy and is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not used systemic antihistamine medication within 14 days of screening or anti-inflammatory drugs within 2 days of Screening Visit 1. She is not currently receiving allergy injections or using immunosuppressive drugs. She has not used any topical drugs at the test site within 7 days of Screening Visit 1 and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial or patch test for irritation or sensitization. She has not used any investigational drug therapy within 4 weeks of study start.

The patient is a 30-year-old mother of a 6-year-old boy living in a low-income community in Hong Kong. She struggles to make ends meet and feels overwhelmed by the daily stressors of her life. Her son has been showing signs of behavioural problems and difficulty with attention and emotional regulation. The family is interested in participating in a mindfulness-based intervention to learn strategies for reducing stress and improving their overall well-being. The mother is willing to commit to attending regular sessions with her son, and they both have no physical disabilities or mental health disorders that would preclude their participation in the program.

N/A - This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment or enrollment. It utilizes a bank of biological specimens and clinical information collected by the investigators prior to their joining the intramural program. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

The patient is a 65 year old male with a history of lower extremity arterial occlusive disease. He has been experiencing significant pain and difficulty walking due to decreased blood flow to his legs. His doctor has recommended vascular surgery to improve blood flow to the affected areas. The patient is otherwise generally healthy with no significant medical history, and is not on any chronic medications or immune modulators/suppressors. He is willing and able to follow all study protocols and sign informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has a history of cystic fibrosis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has been on mechanical ventilation for the past 6 months due to respiratory failure. Despite maximal medical therapy, his respiratory function has continued to deteriorate, and he is unable to perform activities of daily living. His pulmonary function tests show severe airflow obstruction, and he has a low diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). He has been evaluated by a lung transplant team and has been deemed a suitable candidate for bilateral sequential lung transplantation under extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support. He has no significant comorbidities and has been compliant with his medical therapy. He has given his informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 45-year-old woman who has been smoking for the past 20 years is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the palatability of experimental cigarettes. She smokes an average of 15 cigarettes per day and is able to inhale when smoking. She has not had any major health issues in the past year, and her carbon monoxide (CO) level is above 8 ppm. She is currently not pregnant, lactating, or trying to become pregnant. She does not suffer from bipolar disorder, general anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, or major depressive episodes. She has not used any nicotine replacement products or medications like bupropion or varenicline in the past 3 months, and she is not planning to reduce or quit tobacco use in the next 30 days. She has not used any other forms of tobacco in the past 30 days.

56M with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on maintenance hemodialysis for the past 5 years. No history of active infection or chronic liver disease but has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has a stable vascular access, anticoagulation, and hematocrit of 32%. The patient is currently not participating in any other clinical trials and is medically stable. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is male and has no history of active hepatitis or any other medical conditions that may interfere with the study.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman from Brazil who is currently 25 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is married and works as a part-time accountant. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has never been diagnosed with dengue fever. She has a healthy lifestyle, does not smoke or drink alcohol, and exercises regularly. Her BMI is 22, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min. Her laboratory study is unremarkable. She has social security coverage and is interested in participating in the study to help contribute to the understanding of the risks of symptomatic dengue on pregnancy.

A 54-year-old male with a history of primary autonomic failure and symptomatic nOH came to the clinic seeking treatment options. He was previously enrolled in Study 0170 and had completed the 26-week treatment period with ampreloxetine. He reported significant improvements in his symptoms during the treatment period and is willing to continue on long-term treatment with ampreloxetine. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and high cholesterol, but has no known allergies. He is able to understand the study and has provided written informed consent. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders that may interfere with his ability to give informed consent or participate in the study.

A 55-year-old man recently underwent surgery to remove a thymoma in his chest. The pathology report revealed that he has Masaoka stage II-III B type thymoma. He is feeling well and has a Zubrod-ECOG-WHO status of 0. He has no serious comorbidities and has not received any previous cancer treatments. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his prognosis.

The patient is an 8-week-old infant who is healthy and residing in The Gambia. The infant's parents are willing to comply with the requirements of the study and have provided informed consent. The infant has not received any investigational or non-registered products within the past 30 days, nor has he/she received any chronic administration of immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within the past six months. The infant has not received any vaccination against S. pneumoniae, and there are no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient conditions based on medical history and physical examination. The infant has no major congenital defects or chronic illnesses, no history of neurologic disorders or seizures, and no acute disease or fever at the time of enrollment. The infant has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products within the past three months and has no contraindications to any co-administered vaccine. The infant will be evaluated for the impact on nasopharyngeal carriage, safety and immunogenicity of GSK Biologicals' pneumococcal vaccine 2189242A given as a 3-dose vaccination course and co-administered with other routine pediatric vaccines.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and is currently on hemodialysis. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is scheduled to undergo renal transplantation from a deceased donor. The patient has no known allergies to any medications and is compliant with his current medication regimen. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided signed IRB-approved informed consent. The patient's platelet count, white blood cell count, and lipid levels are within normal limits. He has not had any recent infections requiring IV antibiotics and has not experienced any biopsy-confirmed acute rejection since his transplant. His baseline CAC score is greater than 100 at baseline reading.

Patient is a 9-year-old girl with biopsy-proven neuroblastoma who is planned to undergo a 123I-MIBG imaging. She has completed 3 cycles of chemotherapy and is scheduled for surgical resection of the primary tumor. The treating physician is interested in comparing the results of her 123I-MIBG scan with a 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT scan to investigate the feasibility of using the latter in the future. The patient and her parents have been informed about the study and have provided signed informed consent. The patient has no history of other cancers in the past 5 years and is medically stable to undergo the scan.

The patient is a 53-year-old male who presented with chest pain, arm pain, and shortness of breath that began 2 hours ago. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but has never had a heart attack before. On examination, the patient is diaphoretic and in distress, with a blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg and a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. An electrocardiogram (ECG) is obtained, which shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. The patient is diagnosed with an anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and is taken to the cardiac catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The angiogram shows an occluded proximal left anterior descending (LAD) artery with TIMI 2 flow. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the INFUSE - Anterior Myocardial Infarction (AMI) Study and is randomized to one of the treatment arms.

Patient B is a 17-year-old female who is receiving gynecological care at the Maternal Fetal Care Center. She is a student in high school and is currently in good health. She has never received the Gardasil vaccination and is interested in learning more about it. She has a cell phone and is willing to accept any texting charges that may occur for receiving the reminder text. She has no known allergies to the HPV-4 or HPV-9 vaccine. She is not pregnant and is within the age range of 9-26 years old as per the manufacturer's recommendation. She agrees to participate in the study and consents to receiving the Gardasil vaccination series and the reminder texts for follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer six months ago. She has undergone chemotherapy and has been responding well to the treatment. However, she recently experienced headaches and blurred vision, which led to the discovery of new brain metastases. MRI confirms the presence of two lesions, with the largest one measuring 30 mm in diameter. She has no history of brain metastasis treatment and her ECOG performance status is 1. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is currently taking letrozole and palbociclib for breast cancer treatment. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to travel to the study site for visits.

A 47-year-old female presented with a complaint of urinary frequency, urgency, and pain for the past 6 months. She described her pain as a constant dull ache in her lower abdomen that is intensified by urination. She also reported that the pain sometimes radiates to her lower back. She denied any history of urinary tract infections or sexually transmitted infections. She has never been pregnant and is not sexually active. She is a current smoker, smoking approximately 10 cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. She has no known allergies and her medical history was otherwise unremarkable. On physical examination, there was tenderness in the suprapubic area and the bladder was palpable. Urine analysis showed mild hematuria and pyuria. She was diagnosed with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) based on her symptoms and physical examination findings. She was offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial to determine whether Platelet Activating Factor (PAF) is stable in urine and if cigarette smoking contributes to changes in the bladder indicative of or predisposing to IC/BPS. She provided informed consent and agreed to donate urine samples for the study.

A 48-year-old postmenopausal woman was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the bone, liver, and lungs. She has undergone three lines of chemotherapy including paclitaxel and docetaxel, but her cancer has progressed despite treatment. Her hormone receptor status is positive for estrogen and progesterone, but HER2 neu is negative. She has a performance status of 2 due to fatigue and shortness of breath. She has a history of hypertension and Type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has been informed about the potential benefits and risks of receiving biweekly docetaxel. She is willing to undergo imaging studies every 2 weeks and has provided informed consent for the trial.

Maria is a 35 year old woman who works as a nurse and was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies but is otherwise in good health. She began experiencing symptoms such as fever, cough, and shortness of breath about a week ago and was admitted to the hospital for treatment. She has been receiving supplemental oxygen and is being monitored closely by medical staff. Maria is able to communicate effectively with her healthcare providers and is willing to participate in the study. She has not been enrolled in any other clinical trials and is willing to provide written informed consent.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from China who was diagnosed with locally advanced gastric cancer. He has no significant past medical history and currently takes no medications. He reports some abdominal discomfort and indigestion. On physical examination, there are no palpable masses or lymphadenopathy. His laboratory studies are within normal limits. CT scan shows a tumor in the upper third of the stomach, with no distant metastases. He has an ASA score of II and an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male with a medical history of advanced prostate cancer presents to the clinic for a screening visit. He has been diagnosed with prostate cancer three years ago and has been receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy. His most recent PSA (prostate-specific antigen) level was 9 ng/mL. He reports no other significant medical history, and he is not taking any other medications. His vital signs are within the normal range. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities except for a palpable prostate gland. Laboratory results show normal hematological, renal, and hepatic function. Serum phosphate and calcium levels are within the normal range. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to identify plant-derived phytochemicals that can safely reduce systemic inflammation in patients with advanced cancer. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is scheduled for further evaluation.

A 34-year-old female has a history of spring rhinitis hay fever, and whenever she eats fresh apples, she experiences an itchy and swollen mouth. She has also experienced similar symptoms after consuming other plant-derived foods known to be involved in the pollen-food syndrome. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She has a history of mild asthma controlled on a regular inhaler. She doesn't smoke or use illicit drugs. She is generally fit and healthy, with no significant medical conditions. She has never undergone previous immunotherapy with birch pollen extract. She is currently not using contraception as she and her husband are trying to conceive their third child. She is willing to attend all the required injections and follow-up visits for the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male presents to the gastroenterology clinic with a long history of GERD symptoms, including heartburn, regurgitation, and difficulty swallowing. Despite taking medication for GERD, his symptoms persist, leading to a reduced quality of life. He has undergone endoscopy which showed no distinct hiatal hernia, dysphagia or esophageal strictures. His preoperative evaluation showed pathological values in the functional parameters. He is in good physical status (ASA score II) and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in exploring alternative treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing laparoscopic antireflux surgery versus endoscopic full-thickness gastroplication for GERD.

54 year old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 15 pack-year smoking history presents with rectal bleeding and was found to have a 4 cm adenocarcinoma on colonoscopy with biopsy. CT imaging revealed T3N0 disease with no evidence of metastasis. The patient underwent preoperative chemoradiation and is now being considered for surgical resection. He is interested in participating in a randomized prospective trial comparing laparoscopic and open resection for locally advanced rectal cancer after preoperative chemoradiation. The patient is currently in good health, with a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, WBC count of 5,500/mm3, and platelet count of 170,000/mm3. His creatinine level is 0.9 mg/dL and he has adequate cardiopulmonary function. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the trial.

52-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C and alcohol-induced cirrhosis. Recently, he has been experiencing increasing abdominal pain and distension. An ultrasound revealed portal vein thrombosis with a velocity of 12 cm/s. Laboratory findings showed low levels of AT-III (<70%) and a platelet count of 75,000/uL. He is currently classified as CPT Class A cirrhosis. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders, major surgeries, or malignancies. He is not currently taking any medications that increase the risk of thrombosis or antiplatelet medications, except for aspirin 81 mg once daily. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the trial.

A 46-year-old woman presents with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 years. She has been taking methotrexate (20mg weekly) for the past 4 months but still experiences joint pain and stiffness. She has also been taking omeprazole for the past 6 months for acid reflux. She reports persistent pain in her right wrist, both knees, and both ankles, along with swelling in her fingers and toes. She has difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing, grooming, and cooking due to the pain and stiffness. She denies any recent infections and has not taken any other medications for RA in the past 3 months. Her CRP is found to be elevated above the upper limit of normal. MRI of her right wrist reveals synovial hypertrophy and joint effusion. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to find out if BMS-582949 can help improve her symptoms.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She had a normal pregnancy with no complications until she developed high blood pressure during the third trimester. She was diagnosed with pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) and was closely monitored until her delivery. After delivery, her blood pressure remained elevated, and she was diagnosed with persistent postpartum hypertension. She has no history of hypertension before pregnancy and has no significant medical history. She is currently breastfeeding her infant and taking no medications except for prenatal vitamins. She has a supportive partner and a good social support system. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow-up appointments. Her blood pressure at hospital discharge was 160/100 mmHg. She is otherwise healthy and has no contraindications to Nifedipine or Labetalol.

The patient is a 7-month-old infant living in a rural area who has missed one or more routine vaccinations. The child is brought to the mobile team for vaccination and is eligible for the study. The infant is otherwise healthy with no known medical conditions and has not received vitamin A supplementation in the past month. The parents are willing to participate in the study and have given informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with early rheumatoid arthritis. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications for RA or any other medical condition. She has experienced joint pain and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and feet for the past 6 months. She has not had any respiratory symptoms, but has a history of occasional cough and mild shortness of breath with exertion. She is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 25. Her physical exam is significant for synovitis in her hands and wrists, but no lung findings are present. Her recent labs show positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies. She speaks and understands English fluently and is willing to participate in all study related tasks, including returning to NJH every 6 months for an 18 month period of time. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old Japanese male who was diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis. He had previously been treated with hydroxyurea and interferon-alpha but showed no significant improvement in his symptoms. He complains of fatigue, night sweats, and abdominal discomfort. On physical examination, he has hepatosplenomegaly with a spleen palpable 8 cm below the costal margin. His Eastern Collaborative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He has no other active malignancy and is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study drug. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

28-year-old male with a BMI of 26 kg/m2, non-smoker, and generally healthy is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating postprandial fatigue. The study aims to evaluate if severity of postprandial fatigue is driven by IL-1. The patient typically eats breakfast and lunch and is willing to use contraceptive measures to prevent pregnancy during the study. The patient owns a smartphone and is able to download and use the sleeping app, Sleep cycle, prior to the study days. The patient must not have a history of sleep disturbances, clinical signs of infection in the week before inclusion or history of infection during the last 2 months, hematologic disease, kidney disease, liver disease, heart disease, pulmonary disease, inflammatory disease, history of carcinoma, history of tuberculosis, alcohol consumption >40g/d, smoking, known allergy towards Kineret, known allergy to ingredients of the test meal, current treatment with any drug in the week before inclusion, including vitamin supplementation (especially vitamin C and E), or use of any investigational drug within 30 days prior to enrolment or within 5 half-lives of the investigational drug, whichever is longer. The patient must also be willing and able to give written informed consent.

A 50-year-old Hispanic woman with a history of cirrhosis secondary to non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) presents to the emergency department with confusion and disorientation. She is complaining of difficulty concentrating and is unable to remember simple tasks. Her medical history also includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both well controlled with medications. She denies any history of substance abuse or alcohol consumption. On physical examination, she has asterixis and bilateral hand tremors. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and an elevated ammonia level. A diagnosis of grade 2 hepatic encephalopathy is made. The patient is admitted to the hospital and started on lactulose therapy. Despite treatment, her symptoms continue to persist. The patient is then approached to participate in a clinical trial comparing polyethylene glycol (GoLYTELY®) to lactulose for the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy. She is interested in participating and meets all eligibility criteria, including having a legally authorized representative who is able and willing to comply with all protocol procedures and consent on her behalf.

A 42 year old woman with a BMI of 28.5 has been struggling with her weight for the past year. She has tried various diets and exercise programs without success. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares two different diets for weight loss. She has no history of serious medical conditions and has clearance from her primary care physician to participate in the study. She is willing to be randomized to one of two diet strategies for weight loss and is able to independently shop for and prepare meals. She is not currently taking any medications that significantly influence weight and has not undergone any CT, PET, fluoroscopic, or nuclear medicine studies in the past year.

A 3-month-old infant, born full term with no significant medical history, is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the post-marketing use and safety of Prevnar (13v). The infant has not yet received any pneumococcal vaccines, including Prevnar 13. The parents understand the study requirements and are willing to have their child vaccinated according to the indicated dosage and administration schedule. The infant has no history of anaphylaxis to any of the vaccine ingredients or diphtheria toxoid, and is currently in good health with no signs of fever or acute illness.

This is a 49-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C (CHC) based on a detectable viral load as measured by a serum HCV RNA test. He has been living with CHC for at least 6 months and is currently in a stable condition with compensated liver disease as per the results of his recent screening laboratory assessment. He weighs 68 kg and has no history of immunologically mediated disease or interstitial lung disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of albinterferon alfa 2b (alb-IFN) single dose for the treatment of CHC.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who was diagnosed with Stage III ovarian cancer 6 months ago. She has already undergone surgery and chemotherapy, but she is still experiencing physical and psychological distress. She is a married mother of two children and works as a nurse. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious about her cancer diagnosis and the impact it has on her daily life. She does not currently practice mindfulness meditation but is open to trying it as a potential coping mechanism. She speaks English fluently and has access to a personal computer and internet. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative methods of managing her distress.

A 9-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents with a history of difficulty in paying attention, impulsiveness, and hyperactivity. He has had these symptoms for the past few years, and they are affecting his academic performance and social interactions. He has been evaluated by a psychiatrist and diagnosed with ADHD combined subtype. He is currently functioning academically at age-appropriate levels and is capable of following classroom instructions. He has no other comorbid psychiatric diagnosis except for occasional oppositional defiant behavior. He has no allergies or intolerance to the active treatments or tricyclic antidepressants. The parents are concerned about their child's academic performance and are willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the behavioral effects of ADDERALL XR versus STRATTERA under controlled conditions utilizing the SKAMP deportment scale.

Patient is a 50-year-old African American man who works as a construction worker. He comes to the clinic with a complaint of chronic pain in his lower back and knees for the past 6 months. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications such as acetaminophen and ibuprofen but they have not been effective in managing his pain. He is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. He is not taking any prescription medications or supplements. Laboratory study is unremarkable.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy for 6 weeks. She then started taking non-platinum-containing chemotherapy for 6 cycles. Her hemoglobin level at baseline was 10.2 grams per deciliter. She has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and dizziness. She was recently diagnosed with anemia due to her cancer and chemotherapy. She has no history of high blood pressure, seizure, or iron, folate, or Vitamin B12 deficiency. She has not received any transfusions or radiotherapy in the last 2 weeks, nor has she had any surgery within the last week. She is not planning to use steroid drugs during the study. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if epoetin alfa can reduce the need for transfusions and improve her anemia and quality of life.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been experiencing persistent and severe mood swings for the past year. His parents have noticed that he has been extremely irritable, impulsive, and easily agitated. He has also been experiencing periods of euphoria and grandiosity, followed by sudden crashes into depression. The patient has been diagnosed with bipolar I disorder by a licensed mental health professional. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of serious or unstable medical illness. The patient and his parents have consented to the use of medication to treat his symptoms. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive treatment and help researchers learn more about the safety and effectiveness of ziprasidone for children and adolescents with bipolar I disorder.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing hearing loss for several years. She has tried several hearing aids but has not been able to obtain significant benefit. She has difficulty understanding conversations, especially in noisy environments, and often has to ask people to repeat themselves. She is fluent in English and has no known cognitive impairments. She is willing to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study. She has been diagnosed with moderate to profound hearing loss in the low frequencies and severe to profound hearing loss in the high frequencies, bilaterally. Her low-frequency PTA is greater than 40 dB and her high-frequencies are not better than 65 dB (3000 Hz - 8000 Hz). She has a sensorineural hearing loss, demonstrated by an air-bone gap of less than or equal to 10dB. Her CNC word score in quiet is 60% or less in the ear to be implanted and 70% or less in the non-implanted ear. She has not used hearing aids within the last year and is willing to participate in a 30-day hearing aid trial prior to enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who suffered from an ACL injury while playing soccer. He has been experiencing knee instability and pain for the past few months. His past medical history is non-significant, and he takes no medications. He has no other known injuries or health conditions. The patient underwent ACL and anterolateral ligament reconstruction surgery using an anatomic technique and flexor tendon graft. The surgery was successful, and the patient is now ready to begin rehabilitation. He is motivated to regain his knee function and return to playing soccer. His physical examination shows limited range of motion in the knee joint and mild swelling. There is no evidence of any other injuries or abnormalities. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial and will be enrolled in the rehabilitation protocol for ACL and ALL reconstruction surgery.

Patient is a 56-year-old woman from Canada who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago and underwent lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. She is postmenopausal, has no prior history of osteoporosis, and is not currently taking any medications. Her BMI is 26, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. She reports occasional joint pain but is otherwise healthy. Her laboratory study is unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her bone health.

A 10-month-old male infant was brought to the emergency department with symptoms of fever, cough, and difficulty breathing. The infant was born at term and had no significant medical history. The parents reported that the infant had been experiencing these symptoms for about 3 days and his condition had been worsening. On physical examination, the infant was tachypneic, with a respiratory rate of 52 breaths per minute. His heart rate was 128 beats per minute, and his oxygen saturation was 90% on room air. The infant appeared to be in moderate respiratory distress, with intercostal retractions and nasal flaring. Lung auscultation revealed scattered wheezing, with decreased breath sounds in the lower lobes. The infant was diagnosed with moderate acute bronchiolitis and was admitted to the ICU with supplemental oxygen therapy. The infant met the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial, and the parents agreed to the infant's participation in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage osteoarthritis of the bilateral knees. The patient has been experiencing severe pain, stiffness, and difficulty in walking. The patient has tried several non-surgical treatments including physical therapy, medications, and injections, but the symptoms have not improved. The patient is generally healthy with no significant medical history. The patient has Medicare insurance and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has no prior operations involving the extensor mechanism, patellar thickness is more than 18mm, and no serious deformity. The patient is capable of cooperating and following the instructions for the study. The patient is a good candidate for total knee arthroplasty and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 75-year-old man was admitted to the hospital following a fall that resulted in a proximal femur fracture. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking metformin and lisinopril. He is an ex-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is independent in activities of daily living and has no cognitive impairment. He is scheduled for surgical internal fixation of the femur. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical knowledge and potentially improve outcomes for future patients.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who has been admitted to the hospital for a category 2 pressure ulcer on her sacrum. She has a history of diabetes and has been wheelchair bound for the past 6 months due to a recent leg injury. She is able to give consent and is fluent in English. She has no known peripheral vascular disease or tissue damage in her feet, and is not hypersensitive to fixation tape. She is well enough to attend the lab without any attachments and is able to transfer to bed with the assistance of one person. She is interested in participating in the study to help prevent future pressure ulcers.

45 year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and recent exacerbation requiring hospitalization. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation for 48 hours. He has been successfully treated for his exacerbation and is now ready for weaning from mechanical ventilation. He meets weaning criteria, including adequate cough and no excessive respiratory secretions. His primary pathology has been resolved and he is clinically stable, with a heart rate of 120 bpm and systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg. His oxygenation is adequate, with a saturation of 94% on a FiO2 of 0.4. His ventilatory pattern is also adequate, with a respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, maximal inspiratory pressure of -15 cmH2O, tidal volume of 500 ml (10 ml/kg), and a respiratory rate/tidal volume ratio of 40 breaths per minute/liter. He is fully conscious and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with aspirin exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) characterized by asthma, eosinophilic rhinosinusitis and intolerance to aspirin and NSAIDs. He has been experiencing symptoms of chronic rhinosinusitis, including nasal congestion, facial pain, and headaches, which have not responded well to current treatments. He has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorders or psychiatric conditions. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the impact of nasosinusal surgery on his sleep quality, quality of life, and symptoms.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was labeled as penicillin allergic by her primary care physician during childhood due to hives and itching after taking amoxicillin for a urinary tract infection. She has never undergone formal allergy testing for penicillin allergy. Her past medical history is only significant for seasonal allergies and occasional migraines for which she takes antihistamines and ibuprofen as needed. She has no history of beta-lactam associated toxic epidermal necrolysis/Stevens Johnson syndrome, Drug induced Eosinophilia with Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), autoimmune hepatitis/interstitial nephritis, or hemolytic anemia. She is not currently pregnant and has no history of poorly controlled asthma or heart disease. She is willing to discontinue her antihistamines for at least 5 days prior to allergy testing.

A 56-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. His chest X-ray showed infiltrates in the lower lobe of the right lung, and his white blood cell count was elevated at 12.5 x 10^9/L with 18% immature neutrophils. He was diagnosed with moderate to severe community-acquired pneumonia and admitted to the hospital. He has not received any antibiotics for the current illness. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent form. He is willing to use contraception during the study period as he is married. His ECG showed no prolongation of the QT / QTc(F) interval, and his liver and kidney function tests were within normal limits. He has no history of tendon disease, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, or epilepsy.
