The patient does not have known HIV-positive status or AIDS, and he has not received quinolones or fluoroquinolones within the last two weeks.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue for the past six months. She has a history of lung problems in her family, but she herself has never smoked. Her doctor has been suspecting sarcoidosis and has performed various blood tests and imaging studies to confirm the diagnosis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to develop a new, non-invasive diagnostic tool for sarcoidosis using exhaled breath. She is excited to contribute to the advancement of medical science and hopes that the results of the study will help other patients with sarcoidosis in the future.

This is a 6-year-old male who was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit with severe respiratory distress due to an asthma exacerbation. The patient was intubated within 6 hours of admission and started on mechanical ventilation. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and has been hospitalized multiple times for asthma exacerbations in the past. The patient is classified as ASA 2. The patient is not currently taking any medications other than those required for his hospitalization. The patient will be part of the ICU group in the study aimed at determining if there are differences in the oral flora bacteria in children admitted to the ICU who require intubation compared to healthy children undergoing anesthesia for their dental caries. The patient meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with follicular center grade 2 lymphoma 5 years ago. She underwent treatment with chemotherapy and radiation therapy and achieved complete remission. However, her disease relapsed 2 years later, and she was treated with rituximab and bendamustine. She achieved partial remission but experienced disease progression 8 months later. She was then treated with ibrutinib and achieved stable disease for 10 months before experiencing disease progression again. Her current imaging studies show diffuse lymphadenopathy with involvement of multiple nodal groups and splenomegaly. She has no significant medical history and has not undergone any major surgeries in the past 4 weeks. Her current medications include aspirin and amlodipine for hypertension. She has no history of porphyria or G6PD deficiency. She has not received any radioimmunoconjugate therapy or prior exposure to murine antibodies other than rituximab. She has not undergone stem cell collection previously. The patient is willing to use effective contraception and has a negative pregnancy test.

The patient is a 18-month-old girl who has been experiencing mild to moderate atopic dermatitis with cow milk allergy. Her parents have noticed that her skin has been itchy, red and dry with occasional flare-ups. She has been avoiding cow milk products and has been receiving alternative sources of calcium and protein. Her medical history includes eczema in her family, but no other significant health issues. She has not been on systemic steroids or immune-suppression medications in the past 6 weeks. Her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have provided their consent. The severity of her atopic dermatitis will be assessed using the modified SCORAD index. She has not experienced anaphylaxis, angioedema or severe allergic reactions to cow milk and does not have chronic diarrhea.

A 28-year-old female with a history of opioid use disorder presents to the clinic. She has been using opioids recreationally for the past 6 months and has noticed increased difficulty controlling her drug use. She has no significant medical history and is not currently pregnant. She is interested in participating in a survey about a wearable device that can detect and respond to opioid overdoses. She has been living in the Kensington Neighborhood in North Philadelphia for the past year and is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

Patient is a 58-year-old woman with a history of metastatic breast cancer to the liver and lungs. She has previously received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy to the chest wall and mediastinum. The patient has been experiencing progressive disease despite treatment and is now interested in exploring clinical trials. Imaging studies show multiple measurable lesions in the liver and lungs. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her lab values meet eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to undergo pre- and post-vorinostat tumor biopsies. She has no history of cardiac failure, long QT syndrome, ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation, or seizures. She has not received anthracycline exposure and is not currently on any concurrent chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, or investigational agents for primary disease. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception during and for 6 months after completion of study treatment.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who is generally in good health. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m2, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not taken any proton-pump inhibitors, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or vitamin supplements in the past two weeks. She has not taken any antibiotics in the past three months. She has never had abdominal surgery. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not donated blood in the past three months. She is not HIV-positive. She has not had any side effects from prebiotic supplements in the past. She has no history of gastrointestinal complaints or major illnesses. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of pectin on gut health in older adults.

35 yo F with Type 1 diabetes for 12 years, on insulin pump therapy with poor glycemic control, BMI of 26, non-smoker for over a year, and stable kidney function. Despite insulin therapy, the patient experiences frequent hypoglycemic episodes and struggles to maintain blood glucose levels within target range. The patient has been identified as a potential candidate for islet cell transplantation to achieve insulin independence. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial testing the effect of sitagliptin on islet graft function following transplantation and is interested in participating. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to sitagliptin and meets all other inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 48-year-old woman with partial edentulism in the posterior mandible is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She had a lower right molar extracted due to caries 3 months ago and now wants to replace it with an implant. She has no untreated caries or periodontal disease in her residual dentition. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. The physical examination reveals a healthy, well-nourished woman with no abnormalities. She has good oral hygiene, and her occlusion is stable. She is willing to return for follow-up visits for the duration of the study. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old woman presents with persistent facial pain for the past 6 months. The pain is poorly localized and radiates beyond the trigeminal nerve distribution. The patient reports a dull, aching, or nagging quality of pain that occurs daily for more than 2 hours a day. The patient has seen a neurologist, ENT specialist, and maxillofacial surgeon, and all available treatments such as anticonvulsants and antidepressants have failed to provide adequate relief. The patient rates the average pain intensity as 6 out of 10 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NRS) on the affected side during the 4-week baseline period. The patient has undergone dental investigations which did not reveal any pathology. The neurological examination is normal, but the patient reports paresthesia. The patient has no history of neurological disorders or any other related systemic diseases that can explain the pain. MRI and CT examinations did not reveal any intracranial pathology. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or using inappropriate contraception. The patient confirms that she is not abusing medication, drugs or alcohol. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to botulinum toxin type A or to any of the excipients. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old male with keratoconus complains of blurred vision, halos around lights, and frequent changes in his eyeglass prescription. He has been diagnosed with keratoconus and has been wearing rigid contact lenses for the past 2 years. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for any eye or vision problems. His visual acuity is 20/60 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. His corneal thickness is 450 microns in both eyes. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve his vision and stabilize his corneal profile.

A 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia presents for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating precision drug use strategies based on pharmacogenomics compared with traditional drug use strategies for cardiovascular-related chronic diseases. He is a permanent resident of Da-jie town in Da-ming County and can provide reliable information related to drug treatment and efficacy evaluation. He has been diagnosed with primary hypertension and is currently taking medication but has not achieved adequate blood pressure control. His systolic blood pressure is consistently above 140 mmHg and his diastolic blood pressure is above 90 mmHg. He has also been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has an HbA1c level above 7.0% despite taking medication. Additionally, he has a history of hyperlipidemia and has been treated with or without medication prior to enrollment. He does not have any infectious diseases or serious life-threatening conditions such as malignant tumors, nor does he have severe liver or kidney function damage that would affect the choice of treatment drugs. He is willing to provide real and reliable information for the study evaluation.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy of Asian descent, diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. He has a history of severe behavioral problems, including frequent tantrums and aggressive behavior towards family members and schoolmates. His irritability subscale score on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist (ABC-I) is ≥18 at screening and baseline. He has a mental age of 6 years and is currently taking no other medication for his condition. He weighs 25 kg and has no history of significant medical conditions. His parents have consented to his participation in the study and are able to comply with the protocol requirements. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trial within the past 4 weeks.

Mr. John Smith is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with NYHA Class III heart failure. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema in his lower extremities for the past few months. Despite being on optimal medical therapy, his symptoms have not improved. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He is willing and able to visit the clinic frequently during the 6 months following implantation and perform all follow-up procedures. He is not pregnant and has no plans to get pregnant during the study. He does not have tricuspid or pulmonic stenosis, pulmonary stents, right-sided mechanical heart valves, or any other conditions that are listed in the exclusion criteria. He is not suffering from an active infection and has no known intracardiac mass. He has not been implanted with a VAD and is not a candidate for listing for heart transplantation. He has not had a lead implanted at the heart right side of the heart within the last 6 months. He does not have any terminal illness or a life expectancy of less than 6 months. He is able to lie flat for the duration of the procedure and operate the home unit. He has not undergone pneumonectomy and is not treated with oral anticoagulants with INR > 1.5 prior to catheterization. His creatinine level is less than 2.5 mg/dl and he has not suffered from acute myocardial infarction within the three months prior to the study. He has not undergone open heart surgery within 4 weeks prior to the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old African-American woman who has been living with HIV for over 5 years. She is currently taking antiretroviral medications, which have been causing her significant nausea and fatigue. She also experiences occasional pain and anxiety. She is currently single and lives alone, but has a close support network of friends and family. She works as a nurse in a hospital and is generally in good health, except for her HIV diagnosis. She is fluent in English and has a high school education. She does not have any substance abuse issues and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant within the next 3 months. She is interested in participating in the trial as she would like to find ways to reduce the side effects of her antiretroviral medications and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who presented with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the last two months. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but she is otherwise healthy. A chest X-ray revealed a large mass in the right upper lobe of her lung, and subsequent imaging showed evidence of locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis, and she is now a candidate for first-line palliative therapy with nab-paclitaxel and carboplatin. She has no known contraindications to this treatment regimen.

53 yo woman with a 5-year history of ET affecting both upper extremities with a moderate to severe postural and action/intention tremor. The patient has tried propranolol, primidone, and topiramate but has not achieved significant tremor reduction. She has no other significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is willing to abstain from alcohol consumption for at least 24 hours prior to each study visit. The patient is in good general health and has a negative urine drug screen and blood alcohol test at screening. She is willing to discontinue all other tremor-reducing medications and is able to follow the washout procedure and restrictions described in the protocol prior to randomization. The patient has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, major depressive disorder, or drug or alcohol abuse within the past year.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with glioblastoma 2 years ago. She underwent surgery followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide. She has been in remission for the past 18 months but recently had a recurrence of the tumor. The patient reports headaches, confusion, and difficulty with balance. Imaging studies showed a recurrence of the glioblastoma in the same location. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial involving a new schedule of radiation therapy for recurrent glioblastoma. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including having a single recurrence of glioblastoma and being an appropriate candidate for re-irradiation. The patient has not received more than one prior course of radiotherapy to the local site of the progressive disease and has not received prior radiotherapy to the local site of progressive disease within 3 months of the anticipated start of re-irradiation. The patient is not receiving concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy or concurrent immunotherapy but may receive sequential chemotherapy before or after radiation without limitation. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication.

The patient is a 47-year-old female who had been experiencing severe pain in her left foot for several months. She was diagnosed with arthritis and was recommended to undergo a surgical procedure for joint arthrodesis. The patient was informed about the Shark Screw® transplant and was willing to participate in the study. She has no other significant medical history and did not have any allergic reactions to previous surgeries. The patient was operated on in November 2017 and received the Shark Screw® transplant. After surgery, the patient visited the clinic for follow-up examinations at 6 weeks and 12 weeks. At the 6-week examination, the patient reported significant improvement in pain and mobility. The wound and bone healing process was found to be satisfactory by the surgeon. At the 12-week examination, the patient reported full recovery and no complications or adverse events were observed. The patient's records will be included in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the Shark Screw® transplant in hand and foot surgery.

The patient is a 72-year-old Caucasian woman who fell down while walking and sustained a hip injury. She reports severe pain in her hip and difficulty walking. She has no history of hip fracture or any other major orthopedic injuries. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has no other significant medical history. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She lives alone and is independent in her activities of daily living. She is able to perform basic household tasks and enjoys gardening. She is generally in good health and is physically active. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help contribute to research and improve treatment options for others with similar injuries.

A 50 year old Chinese woman was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) 2 years ago and has been managing the condition through dietary modifications. She has been experiencing difficulty maintaining stable glycaemic control and has a HbA1c level of 8.5%. She is not on any medication for T2DM and has no other significant medical conditions, including cardiovascular disease, cancer, or renal impairment. She is willing to comply with study procedures and adhere to meal plans, as well as undertake blood glucose monitoring and continuous glucose monitoring. She is able to prepare at least two meals at home per day and has not had any significant changes in weight or diet over the past 6 months. She is not allergic or intolerant to any of the ingredients or food items in the intervention diet or to paracetamol/ acetaminophen. She meets the eligibility criteria for the DIDM clinical trial and is willing to participate.

A 50-year-old male patient with a history of chest pain on exertion and shortness of breath on climbing stairs for the past 6 months came to the clinic. He has no other significant medical history, such as diabetes or hypertension. Physical examination was unremarkable. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment depression in the inferior leads. Coronary computed tomographic angiography revealed intermediate degree of stenosis (50% stenosis by visual estimation) in the right coronary artery (RCA) and left anterior descending artery (LAD). Invasive coronary angiography showed a normal left main coronary artery, and intermediate lesions in the LAD (60% stenosis) and RCA (50% stenosis). The fractional flow reserve (FFR) values were 0.89 and 0.88 in the LAD and RCA, respectively. The patient has given consent to participate in the IMPACT-FFR registry study, which aims to assess the risk of atherosclerotic plaque progression and clinical events in deferred lesions with or without microvascular disease, defined as physiological classification. Invasive imaging techniques and physiologic assessments, such as intravascular ultrasound, optical coherence tomography, coronary flow reserve, index of microcirculatory resistance, and fractional flow reserve, will be used to evaluate the coronary stenosis. The patient is willing to undergo any study-related procedures and is able to understand the risks, benefits, and treatment alternatives of invasive physiologic or imaging evaluation. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate is >30 mL/min, and he has no contraindication to medications like statin, ezetimibe, heparin, aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel, and ticagrelor. Non-cardiac co-morbid conditions are absent, and the patient's life expectancy is >2 years.

A 36-year-old female presented with right eye pain, redness, and decreased vision for 2 weeks. She denied any history of trauma, fever, headache or other systemic symptoms. Her medical history was significant for asthma and Hashimoto's thyroiditis. She did not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history was unremarkable. On examination, her visual acuity was 20/40 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. Slit-lamp examination of the right eye showed 2+ anterior chamber cells and flare and 1+ vitreous cells. Fundus examination showed mild optic disc swelling and retinal vasculitis. Her intraocular pressure was normal in both eyes. She was diagnosed with chronic non-infectious uveitis and was started on prednisolone acetate eye drops and topical cyclosporine eye drops. However, her symptoms persisted despite treatment. She was referred to a uveitis specialist who recommended enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of two different treatment regimens of EYS606.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and acne. She has noticed that she has gained weight over the past year and has difficulty losing it. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She has been diagnosed with PCOS by meeting three of the Rotterdam criteria. Her thyroid function is well-stabilized with medication. She has no history of metabolic syndrome, endometriosis, primary hyperprolactinemia, or continuously elevated 17-OH-P. The patient is willing to participate in the study to help researchers better understand the relationship between PCOS and diabetes.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with end-stage liver disease and was recommended for liver transplantation (LT). He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been sober for the past 6 months. He has lost 15 pounds in the past 3 months and has decreased appetite. His laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and low albumin levels. He underwent LT surgery and is currently recommended for total parenteral nutrition (TPN) due to prolonged fasting after the surgery. He has no known history of renal dysfunction and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 85 mL/min/1.73 m2. He has no known history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of SMOFlipid supplement in TPN for LT patients.

63-year-old female diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with a history of smoking and a performance status of 1. She has undergone chemotherapy for 6 months and has received pembrolizumab monotherapy as a standard of care for her treatment. The patient has demonstrated partial response by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and is currently in the maintenance phase. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she has received pembrolizumab monotherapy treatment for at least 6 months and is in need of further treatment. The patient has no active or untreated brain metastasis and has not received major surgery within 14 days prior to starting protocol treatment. She is willing and able to follow protocol requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

This clinical trial is seeking children between the ages of 5-18 who have experienced a mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). The child must have been evaluated in the emergency department, urgent care, or primary care setting within 72 hours of the injury and discharged home. The child must not have a known severe developmental delay or psychiatric history, a known prior severe brain injury, or have had an mTBI within the past 3 months. The child must be able to provide verbal informed telephone consent/assent. The study is looking for healthcare providers who are actively practicing in the CHOA system, with primary practice in either ED, UC, and/or PCP. Providers must be able to complete study training/education requirements and provide written/electronic informed consent.

A 55 year old female was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and underwent chemotherapy with cisplatin and etoposide. However, her disease progressed after the chemotherapy. She is now experiencing a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. She has no other underlying diseases except hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She had no major surgery or radiotherapy within the past 4 weeks. Lab results show normal liver, renal and bone marrow function. A biopsy of her lung tumor was performed and confirmed positive for EML4-ALK fusion gene by RT-PCR. She has no history of psychiatric or substance abuse disorders, and she is not a regular user of illicit drugs. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to conceive or father children. She is willing to participate in the study and able to swallow capsules.

58-year-old woman with a history of COPD and frequent exacerbations requiring hospitalizations. The patient was admitted to the medical service due to increased shortness of breath and decreased oxygen saturation. The patient is currently receiving nebulizer treatments and is being considered for discharge on an MDI. The patient speaks English fluently, but has expressed difficulty in understanding and remembering how to properly use her inhaler in the past. The patient is interested in participating in a study that could improve her understanding of how to use her inhaler correctly to prevent future exacerbations. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is expected to be discharged within the next few days.

Patient is a 34-year-old male veteran who was diagnosed with Hepatitis C virus (HCV) 6 months ago. He is interested in receiving treatment for HCV and resides within a 2-hour drive of the clinic. The patient has no known co-infection with HIV or Hepatitis B and has not received IFN treatment in the past 6 months. He is willing to undergo treatment with PEG-interferon and ribavirin and is motivated to self-administer the medications and attend regularly scheduled appointments. The patient has no active malignancy, autoimmune disease, or active alcohol or intravenous drug use. He also has no history of seizures or severe psychiatric illness. The patient's partner agrees to observe strict contraception to avoid pregnancy during and up to 6 months after treatment completion. The patient is willing to participate in the cognitive therapy and stress-reducing techniques training program and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

A 28-year-old non-smoking healthy male volunteer with no significant medical history presents for a pharmacokinetic study. His body mass index is within the normal range, and his haematology and chemistry parameters are normal. He has a negative urine test for selected drugs of abuse and a negative hepatitis panel and HIV antibody screens. He is willing to use an effective contraceptive method during the study and for at least 3 months after the last study drug administration. He is able to comprehend and willing to sign an Informed Consent Form (ICF). His lung function test shows a Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) ≥ 90% of predicted value, and his height is between 170 and 190 cm.

A 45-year-old male patient presented to the primary care clinic for a routine check-up. He reports a history of HIV infection, which was diagnosed 6 years ago. His HIV is well controlled on a stable antiretroviral therapy regimen with no history of CNS-related HIV disease. He reports no history of alcohol or substance abuse and no history of traumatic brain injury. The patient's medical history is notable for hypertension, which is well-controlled through medication. He reports no other significant medical history. The patient's neurological exam is within normal limits. He is able to comprehend and read English and is willing to participate in the study procedures. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or chronic neurological illnesses. His current CD4 count is 600 cells/mm3, and his viral load is undetectable. The patient is considered eligible for the study as an HIV-positive participant.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy with a confirmed diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and is currently experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms, such as constipation, diarrhea, or abdominal pain. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate social deficits, as per the Social Responsiveness Scale-2. The child has no major psychiatric illnesses and is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. The child's family history is unremarkable, and there is no history of allergies or GI diseases. The child has not used any probiotics or oral antibiotics/anti-fungal in the last 60 days. The child is available for the study and willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of metastatic colon cancer that has spread to her liver. She has undergone chemotherapy and surgery in the past but the cancer has recurred. The patient is experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss. She has been referred to the clinical trial for personalized functional profiling in metastatic gastrointestinal cancer patients in Luxembourg. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including a confirmed diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the colon and liver, having received previous cancer treatment for metastatic gastrointestinal cancer, and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has no active infections or medical conditions that would prevent her from complying with the protocol, and is willing and able to sign the informed consent form. She is hopeful that personalized functional profiling will provide her with a more effective treatment option and improve her quality of life.

35 y/o male seeking treatment for an alcohol use disorder. He drinks approximately 25 drinks per week and reports drinking on 80% of days in the past 90 days. He has a stable living situation and a current postal address. He has a Body Mass Index of 24 and is in good physical and mental health with no history or laboratory evidence of diabetes. He meets the DSM-5 criteria for a current Moderate Alcohol Use Disorder. He is not currently attending any self-help treatment group such as AA, but is willing to attend for the duration of the study. He does not meet the exclusion criteria for the study and is willing to comply with the protocol.

62-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C and cirrhosis presented with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and weight loss. A CT scan of the abdomen revealed a 4 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver with evidence of arterial enhancement and early washout consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient underwent a liver biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. He received treatment with sorafenib but experienced intolerable side effects and discontinued therapy. The patient now presents for evaluation for enrollment in the clinical trial evaluating the safety and pharmacokinetics of oral Artesunate in patients with advanced HCC. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and Child Pugh class B7. He has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing to use adequate methods of contraception as he is not surgically sterile but has no plans for further children. The patient has provided written informed consent indicating that he understands the purpose of and procedures required for the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 55 year old non-smoking woman who has recently been diagnosed with Stage 3B non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. She presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. Imaging studies reveal a large mass in the lung, as well as additional lesions in nearby lymph nodes. The patient has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She is able to perform light activities but experiences fatigue easily. Blood tests, including renal and liver function tests, are within normal limits. The patient has not received any previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy for lung cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

56-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension presents with rectal bleeding and abdominal pain. Colonoscopy revealed a large mass in the rectum, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. CT scan showed no evidence of metastasis. The patient is scheduled for colorectal cancer surgery and is being considered for participation in a clinical trial comparing laparoscopic surgery and epidural anesthesia to traditional open surgery under general anesthesia. The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any medications that would exclude him from participation.

45 yo F with a history of frequent sun exposure and outdoor activities. She has noticed multiple rough patches on her face and scalp that have been slowly increasing in size and number over the past year. She was diagnosed with actinic keratoses by her dermatologist and was recommended for treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. She has no history of skin cancer, is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant, and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She has fair skin (photo type II) and has not undergone any tanning in the past 4 weeks. She has not used any topical or oral medications that may cause fragile skin or impaired skin healing in the past 3 months. She has not undergone any prior treatments for actinic keratoses including ablative laser, any laser or photo-dynamic therapy, cryotherapy or electrodessication, systemic retinoid therapy or topical treatment with 5-Fluorouracil cream and/or imiquimod cream and/or diclofenac gel and/or ingenol mebutate gel in the past 6 months. She has no tattoos or permanent makeup in the treated area and has not suffered from any skin conditions or injuries that would prohibit treatment. She is willing to undergo 1-3 treatments (as determined by clinical improvement) and attend follow-up visits as required by the study.

Patient is a 65yo man who was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum after presenting with rectal bleeding and weight loss. The tumor is classified as clinically T3b, with a largest diameter of 4.5 cm and is located 3 cm from the anal verge. The patient is deemed operable and has no comorbidities that would prevent treatment. He has read the information note and has signed the informed consent. The patient has health care insurance and follow-up is possible. The patient has not had pelvic irradiation previously and has no evidence of metastasis. MRI staging shows that the tumor has not invaded external anal sphincter and is not within 1 mm of the levator muscle. The patient is able to receive CXB or CRT. The patient is not on any other clinical trial using an investigational anti-cancer treatment within 28 days prior to the first dose of study treatment.

25 year old healthy female with no significant medical history. Non-smoker, with no prescription drug or over-the-counter medication use within the past 2 weeks. No history of acute or chronic bronchospastic disease, GI bleedings/cerebral hemorrhage, or immunocompromised status. Negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and Hepatitis C. Not nursing an infant. Able to communicate well with the investigator and comply with the requirements of the study. Interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of food on the relative bioavailability of a single dose of imatinib (STI571) given as a 800 mg modified release tablet, MR2 compared to twice-daily doses of 400 mg film-coated imatinib tablets. Willing to participate in a single center, four-treatment, four period, crossover study with a 10 day wash out phase between treatments and a 1 week safety period at the end of the study.

30-year-old female with a history of drug dependence as per DSM-IV criteria who has been enrolled in drug treatment for over 30 days. The patient is currently unemployed and expresses interest in finding employment. She has a basic understanding of English and is willing to participate in a 12-hour job-training program to develop the necessary skills to secure a job and set vocational goals.

A 55-year-old German-speaking man who had a left-sided stroke six months ago is experiencing difficulty with word retrieval and has been diagnosed with aphasia with anomia. He is right-handed and has no history of medication/drug abuse or premorbid depression or psychosis. He does not have any severe hearing disability, and he is not currently taking any anticonvulsive medication or medication with dopamine agonists or antagonists. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves daily administration of levodopa and several hours of language training every day to improve his naming abilities. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

Patient A is a 35-year-old individual who has been diagnosed with Gaucher disease with glucocerebrosidase deficiency confirmed by enzymatic or molecular assay. They have at least three organ systems affected, including anemia, thrombocytopenia, organomegaly, bone deterioration on radiograph, and pulmonary compromise. The patient experiences symptoms that compromise their daily activities and risk their longevity. They do not have any neurologic disease. The patient is interested in participating in a Phase II study of glucocerebrosidase enzyme therapy to evaluate its efficacy and toxicity in patients with Gaucher disease. They understand that they will receive intravenous glucocerebrosidase every 2 weeks, and the dose will be based on the clinical severity of their disease and their response to therapy.

The patient is a 3-month-old infant weighing 6 kg, who has been diagnosed with an inguinal hernia. The infant is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The parents have been informed about the benefits and risks of spinal anesthesia as an alternative to general anesthesia for their child's surgery. They have provided informed consent for their child to participate in the clinical trial that will evaluate the use of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to spinal anesthesia. The surgery is anticipated to take less than 1 hour, and the infant meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial. The medical team will closely monitor the infant's vital signs and ensure that the infant remains comfortable throughout the procedure.

A 40 year old woman comes to the clinic concerned about her weight. She has been struggling with her weight for several years and has tried multiple diets and exercise programs without success. Her BMI is 29.5 kg/m2 and she has a central body fat distribution. She is motivated to reduce her weight and improve her health. She has not used any weight loss medications or participated in a weight loss program within the past 30 days. She is not currently taking any supplements known to affect weight. She has not had weight fluctuations of 20 pounds or more in the past 6 months. She does not have an implanted device in the targeted area of LLLT. She does not have an active untreated clinically significant psychiatric condition. She has not used an investigational drug within 30 days of study enrollment. She does not have a recent history of alcohol or drug abuse or dependence. She is not currently pregnant, lactating, or likely to become pregnant during the medication phase and is willing to use a reliable form of contraception. She does not have a history of any major cardiovascular events or current uncontrolled hypertension documented on 2 separate occasions. She does not have clinically significant acute or chronic progressive or unstable neurologic, hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, lymphatic, respiratory, or metabolic disease. She has not had prior surgical intervention for body sculpting/weight loss, such as liposuction, abdominoplasty, stomach stapling, lap band surgery, etc. She does not have medical, physical, or other contraindications for body sculpting/weight loss. She is not currently using medication(s) known to affect weight levels/cause bloating or swelling and for which abstinence during the course of study participation is not safe or medically prudent. She is not concurrently taking a serotonergic drug.

Pt is a 35yo F with a history of asthma for the past 10 years. She reports symptoms of wheezing, coughing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, which are not well controlled on her current medication regimen. She is currently on a daily dose of fluticasone propionate (250mcg) via a Diskus inhaler, but still experiences frequent asthma exacerbations. She has been using her rescue inhaler (albuterol) frequently, and has had to visit the emergency room for asthma exacerbations in the past year. She is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. She has been compliant with her asthma medications and has not used any investigational drugs in the past 30 days. She is willing to comply with study requirements, including study visits and procedures. She has given informed consent to participate in the study and agrees to take contraceptive precautions (including abstinence) which are adequate to prevent pregnancy during the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stage II squamous cell carcinoma in the upper right lobe of his lung. He has a history of smoking at least 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is currently scheduled to undergo radiation therapy for his cancer and has been referred to the Department of Radiation Oncology in Rochester, MN. He is willing to participate in a tobacco use intervention program and is able to return for all 5 sessions. His Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score is 80, indicating that he is able to carry out normal activity with some difficulty. He does not have any history of psychiatric disorders and is not currently enrolled in any formal behavioral tobacco cessation program.

A 42-year-old woman presents with fatigue, night sweats, and fever for the past 2 weeks. She has also noticed a loss of appetite and weight loss of 10 pounds in the past month. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. Her physical examination showed pallor, and her spleen was palpable 1 cm below the costal margin. Blood tests revealed a white blood cell count of 28,000/μL, hemoglobin of 7.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 40,000/μL. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) (according to 2008 WHO diagnosis criteria of AML). She is willing to participate in a clinical trial aiming at assessing the efficacy and safety of Idarubicin at different doses of 8mg/m2 and 10mg/m2 combined with cytarabine as induction therapy for newly diagnosed AML. She satisfies the inclusion criteria of the study, and there is no evidence of severe malfunction of liver, lungs, kidneys, or heart. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 2. She is fully informed about the trial and has provided written consent to participate.

This is a 52 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily to manage his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. He is generally in good health and has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2. He does not have a history of stroke or major neurological disease, and is able to rise from a seated to standing position without difficulty. He does not have a history of bleeding or clotting disorders, and has never had cancer. He does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol or caffeinated beverages. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a new medication for hypertension.

The patient is a 36-year-old male living in the municipality of Oppegård. He has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep for the past two months. He reports feeling tired and irritable during the day due to lack of sleep. He has tried over-the-counter sleep aids with no success. He has no history of mental illness, but he does have a family history of depression. He works as a computer programmer and does not handle heavy machinery. He does not have any known somatic sleep disorders. He has never been diagnosed with epilepsy or bipolar disorder. He has not had any recent falls or accidents. He is generally healthy and not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a study to receive treatment for his insomnia.

This is a 6 year-old female who was born prematurely at 28 weeks gestation and weighed 1.2 kg at birth. She was diagnosed with apnea of prematurity and was randomized at birth to receive either caffeine or placebo as part of the Caffeine for Apnea of Prematurity (CAP) trial. She was followed up until the corrected age of 18 months and was found to have reduced rates of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and cerebral palsy (CP) with no effect on mortality. She is now being recruited for the Caffeine for Apnea of Prematurity-Sleep (CAP-S) Study, which aims to examine the impact of methylxanthines on neurocognition and behavior. Her parents have given informed consent for her participation in the study.

A 28 year old pregnant woman, at 36 weeks of gestation, has tested positive for Group B Streptococcus (GBS) during routine vaginal screening. She has no prior history of GBS colonization or any other underlying medical condition. She has received all necessary information about the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She is fluent in French and affiliated with an insurance plan. She will be included in the study group for women who have tested positive for GBS during routine screening. At the time of delivery, she will undergo vaginal swabs for GBS detection by both real-time PCR and conventional bacteriological techniques. A blood sample of 5 ml will be taken from her at the time of the implementation of the IV line. Her newborn will also be tested for GBS colonization in the stools and the pharynx prior to returning home. The mother will provide 3-5 ml of breast milk for sample collection when breastfeeding. She will be followed up at day 21 and day 60 post-delivery and vaginal swabs will be collected for analysis of GBS colonization.

Pt is a 75yo M retired teacher who has been living in a residential facility for the past year. He enjoys playing cards and socializing with other residents, but he has been struggling to maintain an active lifestyle due to his sedentary hobbies. He reports feeling stiff and achy when he gets up in the morning and has noticed a decrease in his stamina and overall energy level. He is interested in participating in the Residential MapTrek trial as a way to increase his physical activity level and improve his overall health. He is able to walk without any limitations and is excited to take part in the team-based walking races with other residents. He is also comfortable using technology and is eager to learn how to use the Fitbit and participate in the MapTrek game.

A 35-year-old female presents with no significant past medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the in vivo response to 13C-Spirulina meals that contain different levels of protein. She is a non-smoker and consumes a balanced diet. She is currently not taking any medications and has not taken any medication that may alter gastric motility within the past two days. She has no history of abdominal surgery except appendectomy. She is not pregnant and has no allergies or intolerance to any component of the Gastric Emptying Breath Test meal. She is willing and able to eat the test meal and provide breath samples. She is not on hormone replacement therapy and has no history of neurologic or psychiatric disorder.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented with a 6-month history of intermittent lower abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He reports no history of weight loss, fever, or night sweats. He has a past medical history of hypertension and occasional heartburn for which he takes over-the-counter antacids. He has no family history of colon cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, or other significant gastrointestinal diseases. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. A colonoscopy was performed and revealed colonic diverticulosis with macroscopic signs of inflammation, including erythema, friability, and ulcerations of the inter-diverticular mucosa in the sigmoid colon. Biopsies were taken from the affected mucosa and the adjacent normal mucosa, and also from the colon proximal to the diverticular area and the rectum to exclude chronic inflammatory bowel disease. The patient is willing to sign informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

This is a 57-year-old male who works as an accountant and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which he manages with medications. He reports feeling tired and sluggish throughout the day and has noticed that he has gained some weight over the past year. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to reduce sedentary behavior and improve his overall health. He is able to attend all four measurement visits and is willing to wear the study device for 21 days. He is able to read and write in English and has provided written informed consent. He does not have any chronic conditions that would limit his ability to stand.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer three years ago. He underwent a radical prostatectomy followed by radiotherapy. However, his PSA levels have been increasing despite the treatment. He has a history of high blood pressure which is well-controlled with medication. He does not have a history of heart disease, stroke or any other major medical conditions. He has no known allergies to any medication. He is able to perform most daily activities without assistance and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has a partner but she is past childbearing age. He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He has not been treated with sunitinib or any other antiangiogenic agents before. He has received only one line of docetaxel-based chemotherapy which was discontinued due to toxicity. He has no brain metastasis or carcinomatous meningitis, or spinal cord compression. He has no other medical or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with the study.

A 50-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a BMI of 27 kg/m² is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of high-intensity interval training on cardiac function and glycemic control in diabetic cardiomyopathy. He has been diagnosed with diabetes for 7 years and is currently on stable medication for the past 4 months. He has no history of iron deficiency anemia or heart diseases such as CAD, ischemia, valvular diseases or congenital heart diseases. He has never been diagnosed with neurological, pneumological, oncological, or orthopedic disorders. He has no complications associated with diabetes such as renal diseases or retinopathy. He exercises 3 times a week for 30 minutes but has not tried high-intensity interval training before. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol and attend all study visits.

This is a 55 year old male with a history of idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) who has been on bosentan for over 3 months. Despite being on bosentan, he still experiences shortness of breath and exercise intolerance. He is currently able to walk 200 meters in 6 minutes. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications for his pulmonary hypertension. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if adding inhaled iloprost to his current treatment regimen will improve his symptoms and quality of life.

Pt is a 55yo M with a PMH of chronic low back pain and radiculopathy, presenting with worsening back pain and bilateral leg pain. MRI of the lumbar spine revealed a large disc herniation at L5-S1. The patient has no known drug allergies and is otherwise healthy, with a BMI of 30. His labs were unremarkable, and his preoperative EKG was normal. He was scheduled for a single-level laminectomy/discectomy. The patient has no history of opioid use, obstructive sleep apnea, psychological disorders, hepatic or renal failure. He is ASA physical status 2, and his pain is currently managed with NSAIDs.

A 30-year-old Caucasian woman visited the clinic for treatment of her acne scars, which have been bothering her for years. She has Fitzpatrick skin type II and is willing to comply with all study procedures. Her acne scars are depressed and atrophic, with a diameter of less than 4 mm according to the SCAR-S score of 3 categories moderate. She has never had icepick scarring or atrophic scars with a diameter of 4 mm or greater covering more than 25% of her face. She has not used isotretinoin or topical substances containing retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, alpha-hydroxy acid at a concentration above 10% or beta-hydroxy acid at a concentration above 2% or antibiotics within four months of the baseline visit. She has not used anti-inflammatory agents, anticoagulant therapy, inhibitors of platelet aggregation, Omega-3, vitamin E, or had a history of bleeding disorders. She has not had a history of radiation or skin tumors, collagen diseases or autoimmune diseases, previous hypersensitivity to HA, lidocaine or other amide-type anesthetics, or previous tissue augmenting therapy or revitalization treatment in the treatment area with HA or collagen within 12 months of the baseline visit. She has not had laser or other facial light therapy, chemical peeling, or surgery in the treatment area within 12 months of the baseline visit. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any medical condition that would make her unsuitable for inclusion. She is excited to participate in the study and hopeful that Restylane Vital Lidocaine will help improve her acne scars.

This is a 32-year-old woman who has a family history of peanut allergy. She is currently pregnant with her first child and is concerned about the risk of her child developing a peanut allergy. She has discussed this concern with her obstetrician who has referred her to participate in the iREACH clinical trial. She is eligible to participate in the trial as she plans to deliver at a participating hospital and intends to bring her child for 4- and 6-month well-child visits to a participating pediatric practice. She understands that the trial aims to assess and improve pediatric clinician adherence to the 2017 NIAID Prevention of Peanut Allergy (PPA) Guidelines and explore the end-goal of reducing peanut allergy incidence by age 2.5 years in the intervention vs control group. She is willing to provide informed consent for herself and her child to participate in the trial and understands that data will be collected from her and her child's pediatric clinician through EHR data extraction and surveys. She also understands that the trial aims to identify common barriers/facilitators for PPA Guideline adherence among pediatric clinicians and caregivers and is willing to provide feedback through surveys.

The patient is a 43-year-old man who was diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) two years ago. He has been on dialysis ever since. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He wants to receive a kidney transplant but has been unable to find a suitable donor. He has several family members who are willing to donate a kidney, but they cannot afford to take time off work for the evaluation, donation surgery, and post-operative recovery period. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if lost wage reimbursement for living donors will increase his chances of receiving a living donor kidney transplant. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is capable of providing informed consent.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing blurred and distorted vision in his right eye for the past six months. He reports difficulty reading and driving due to the visual impairment. The patient has no positive history of ocular inflammation, diabetic retinopathy, hypertensive retinopathy, and retinal vasculitis. The patient has no media opacity that would influence visual acuity or preclude acquisition of clear spectral domain optical coherence tomography images. The patient has no history of intraocular surgery other than uncomplicated cataract surgery, retinal detachment, or other ocular diseases that may influence the macular microstructure or visual function. The patient's ocular examination revealed the presence of idiopathic epiretinal membrane in his right eye, and he is scheduled for epiretinal membrane removal. The patient has no measurable fovea location on the spectral domain optical coherence tomography image due to severe retinal contraction, and his intraretinal structure on spectral domain optical coherence tomography images is indistinct. The patient has not undergone combined epiretinal membrane removal and cataract extraction and has a follow-up of more than six months after epiretinal membrane removal.

A 32-year-old Caucasian male with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) was diagnosed a year ago. He initially responded well to chemotherapy but relapsed after 6 months. He underwent a bone marrow transplant but relapsed again after 2 months. His current condition is not stable, and he is experiencing fatigue, fever, and night sweats. He has a history of smoking, but he quit after he was diagnosed with cancer. He is currently not working and is living with his parents. His family history is negative for cancer or any other hematologic disorders. His Hgb level is 8.2, and he is transfusion-dependent. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he is aware of the limitations of the current treatments and is hopeful for a successful outcome.

A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and a 5.5cm abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) was referred for endovascular AAA repair. He underwent successful endovascular repair with an EndoSure Wireless AAA Pressure Sensor implanted for long-term follow-up. The patient has been stable and asymptomatic since the procedure. The physician recommends regular follow-up visits to monitor the aneurysm sac size and endoleaks. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to collect and compare EndoSure and EndoSure s2 Wireless AAA Pressure Sensor measurements with measurements from CT scan imaging, ultrasound, and other tests used to measure the AAA sac size and endoleaks following AAA repair. The patient also agrees to comply with the site-specific follow-up requirements of the investigator.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been recently diagnosed with Stage 1 invasive breast cancer. Her tumor is hormone receptor-positive and HER2-negative, and she underwent breast conserving surgery with clear margins of excision. The patient has no evidence of nodal involvement and her Oncotype-DX RS score is 16. She is willing to take endocrine therapy for at least 5 years and is a candidate for either an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen. She has undergone breast imaging within the past 6 months, which shows no evidence of disease beyond the site of the primary tumor in the ipsilateral breast or in the contralateral breast. The patient has Zubrod performance status of 1 and is willing to participate in the study after signing the informed consent form. She has not received prior radiation therapy to the breast region and has no previous history of invasive malignancies.

The patient is a 14-year-old male who was diagnosed with peanut allergy at the age of 8 after experiencing anaphylaxis during a family gathering. He has avoided peanuts and all peanut-containing products ever since. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of asthma or other medical problems. He takes seasonal allergy medications and uses an inhaler occasionally for exercise-induced wheezing. He enjoys playing soccer and video games and has good grades in school. His parents are concerned about his peanut allergy and have enrolled him in this clinical trial to better understand his immune response and to potentially build tolerance to peanuts. He weighs 45 kg and has a hematocrit of 0.37. He is excited to participate in the study but is a little nervous about the food challenges.

62-year-old male diagnosed with colon cancer who is scheduled to undergo colectomy surgery in two weeks. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is physically active, walking approximately 30 minutes per day and attending a weekly yoga class. He owns a smartphone and is comfortable using technology. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his postoperative recovery and prevent readmissions. He lives with his spouse and has a supportive social network of friends and family. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to wear the wearable device and participate in the gamification intervention.

52 yo female with a history of seasonal allergies and allergic rhinitis presents with symptoms of runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes. Her symptoms are worse in the spring and summer months when grass pollen is prevalent in the air. She has previously been diagnosed with grass pollen induced rhinoconjunctivitis and has a positive skin prick test. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess whether the Grazax® treatment compliance can be improved by use of a compliance device (Memozax®). She has not previously received treatment for grass pollen allergen.

A 6-year-old boy who has been struggling with his weight is brought to the pediatrician by his mother for evaluation. He has a BMI that is greater than the 85th percentile for his age group. His mother reports that he is an only child and spends a lot of time watching television and playing video games. She also notes that he frequently requests sugary snacks and fast food. The patient's past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any medications. The pediatrician informs the family about the clinical trial and explains that the purpose of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a low-intensity treatment program for childhood obesity. The family agrees to participate, and the patient is enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) for over a year. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of bruising and petechiae, and her platelet count has been consistently below 30,000. She is currently taking corticosteroids to manage her symptoms, but her parents are concerned about the potential side effects of long-term steroid use. The patient is otherwise healthy and active, with no other significant medical history. She enjoys playing soccer and spending time with her friends. Her parents are interested in exploring alternative treatments, such as traditional Chinese medicine, to manage her ITP symptoms. They are willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of TCM in improving their daughter's quality of life and reducing the need for conventional medications.

32-year-old pregnant woman from Tanzania attending antenatal care for the first time. She is currently in her second trimester and has not received any antenatal care in her previous pregnancies due to financial constraints. She is HIV-negative but has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. She is currently employed as a primary school teacher and lives with her husband and two children in a rural village. She is interested in learning more about antenatal care and how to improve her pregnancy outcomes. She speaks Swahili and has some basic knowledge of English. She is willing to participate in the group antenatal care program and hopes to meet other pregnant women in her community.

A 47-year-old female diagnosed with coeliac disease for over 2 years with blood test and biopsy confirmation. She has been on a gluten-free diet for more than a year. She has a history of lactose intolerance and has been avoiding lactose-containing foods. The patient is generally in good health, not taking any regular medication, and has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. The patient has no history of any major medical conditions or surgeries. She is willing to participate in the study and able to attend all 6 appointments and donate blood, urine, and faecal samples before and after bread intake. She is able to read and understand the informed consent document and provide written informed consent for participating in the study.

A 28-year-old woman who has just delivered her first child. During the pregnancy, she developed high blood pressure and proteinuria in the third trimester which was diagnosed as preeclampsia. She was closely monitored during her delivery and was given magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis. After delivery, she was discharged with instructions to follow up with her obstetrician within a week. Her blood pressure remained elevated at her follow-up appointment and she was diagnosed with postpartum hypertension. She has been referred to the clinical trial to evaluate if antihypertensive treatment in the postpartum period can decrease postpartum hypertension and its associated maternal morbidity, including risk of readmission and healthcare utilization in comparison with no treatment. She will be randomized to either initiate antihypertensive treatment or standard of care. All subject's blood pressures will be monitored per standard postpartum protocols. As per standard practice, all patients with preeclampsia will be asked to return at 7-10 days for a blood pressure check and then again at 6 weeks for a complete postpartum assessment. She will be allowed to continue routine antenatal, intrapartum and postpartum care with her primary obstetrician.

45-year-old male recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme, with a Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) of 80%. Completed >80% of the prescribed radiation therapy and concurrent temozolomide according to the Stupp regimen without grade 3 or 4 hematologic toxicity. No prior therapy other than standard chemoradiation according to Stupp et al and Gliadel has been received. No known allergy to mebendazole or benzimidazole. Not taking metronidazole and no benzimidazole has been taken within the last 3 months. No anti-convulsant medication

The patient is a 16-year-old female who is currently 20 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is living with her parents and is currently attending high school. She has a history of seasonal allergies and has been taking over-the-counter antihistamines as needed. She does not have any other significant medical history or chronic illnesses. She reports having a healthy diet and does not take any supplements. Her BMI is within the normal range, and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is a non-smoker and does not use any drugs or alcohol. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet the inclusion criteria. She has no history of eating disorders, malabsorption diseases, diabetes, hypertension, or substance abuse. She is not taking any medications that can affect calcium or vitamin D status, and she has not been diagnosed with elevated blood lead concentrations during childhood.

A 42-year-old male with a history of left transtibial amputation due to a motorcycle accident three years ago is interested in improving his balance ability. He has been using a prosthetic leg independently for two years and is able to stand for up to 10 minutes without any discomfort. He reports experiencing occasional falls due to balance issues and has developed a fear of falling, which has limited his social participation. He is fluent in English and is able to travel to the university campus for data collection sessions. He has not used the Nintendo Wii or a similar system for structured balance training before. He is currently not taking any medication that may affect his balance. He is interested in participating in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant who was admitted to the hospital with Acute Respiratory Failure. He was brought in by his parents who noticed that he was having difficulty breathing, with increased respiratory rate and use of accessory muscles. He has no major medical history and is not taking any medications. He was born full-term and had no complications during birth. He is exclusively breastfed and has been gaining weight appropriately. On physical examination, he is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 50 breaths per minute. His oxygen saturation is 89% on room air. He has mild intercostal and subcostal retractions. Lung auscultation reveals diffuse bilateral crackles. His chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates. His arterial blood gas test shows a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 250 mmHg. A nasogastric catheter was inserted and transesophageal electromyography was used to assess the Electrical Activity of his diaphragm (EAdi). He was found to be a suitable candidate for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing blurry vision and eye redness for several weeks. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He denies any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. On physical examination, he has bilateral uveitis with no other significant findings. Laboratory tests reveal mild elevation of serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) levels and a positive chest x-ray for bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. He is referred to the internal medicine department at the Croix-Rousse hospital in Lyon, France, for further evaluation and management of his sarcoid uveitis.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a diagnosis of unresectable biliary tract carcinoma. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past few months. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. His physical exam reveals mild jaundice and an enlarged liver. His laboratory tests show an elevated bilirubin level of 4.0 mg/dL, AST of 150 IU/L, and alkaline phosphatase of 250 IU/L. His absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mm^3, and his platelet count is 120,000/mm^3. His creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his cancer. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a family history of colorectal cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at the age of 45 and her grandmother had also been diagnosed with colorectal cancer at a young age. Genetic testing confirmed that she has hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC) or Lynch syndrome. She has no symptoms but is concerned about her increased risk for developing colorectal cancer. She has never had a colonoscopy before and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new colonoscopic viewing technique called narrow band imaging (NBI) that may help detect precancerous areas that are difficult to see with conventional colonoscopy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating to help improve the detection and prevention of colorectal cancer in patients with HNPCC.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread body pain, fatigue, and stiffness for several years. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by her rheumatologist according to the classification criteria of the American College of Rheumatology. Her pain is rated at 7 out of 10 on the visual analogue scale (VAS) and she reports difficulty in performing daily activities due to her symptoms. She has no history of regular exercise, but is motivated to try a new approach to managing her fibromyalgia symptoms. The patient has no uncontrolled hypertension, decompensated cardiac disease, history of syncope or exercise-induced arrhythmias, decompensated diabetes, or severe psychiatric illness. She is willing to participate in a 12-week program of either stretching exercises or strengthening exercises using the Swiss ball. The patient is between the ages of 20 and 65 years old and is interested in improving her quality of life and reducing the impact of fibromyalgia on her daily activities.

A 68-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe pain in her left hip after a fall. Imaging reveals an intertrochanteric hip fracture, and the on-call orthopedic resident or research coordinator obtains informed consent from the patient for enrollment into a clinical trial. The patient has no history of anticoagulant use or significant bleeding events, and is not allergic to tranexamic acid. She has no history of thromboembolic events, cirrhosis, or renal dysfunction, but has a prior diagnosis of coronary artery disease and has received coronary stents. The patient does not have color blindness. The hospital's Investigational Pharmacy randomizes the patient into one of two cohorts, and the patient receives either 1g of intravenous tranexamic acid or a placebo injection upon presentation to the emergency department and again at the time of surgical incision. The patient is treated surgically with a long trochanteric femoral nail and is monitored for the need for blood transfusion, calculated perioperative blood loss, length of stay, cost of inpatient care, and any adverse events, including DVT, PE, infection, MI, cerebrovascular event, need for re-hospitalization or re-operation, and 30 day mortality. The patient is followed at regular intervals and reports any adverse events that occur since the last visit. The safety of the study is monitored by an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a ruptured brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM), which caused significant neurological deficits. The patient initially presented with a sudden onset of severe headache and vomiting, followed by the development of left-sided weakness and difficulty with speech. Imaging studies revealed a ruptured brain AVM. She received surgical intervention to evacuate the hematoma and to embolize the AVM. Despite the intervention, the patient continued to experience significant neurological deficits, including left-sided weakness and difficulty with speech. She was referred to the TOBAS study for further management. The patient is currently stable and without any further neurological deficits, but is at risk for future hemorrhage or other neurological events related to the AVM. The patient is eligible for the TOBAS study and will be randomized to receive either interventional therapy or conservative management. The primary objective of the study is to determine the best management strategy for patients with brain AVMs, in terms of long-term outcomes, despite the presence of uncertainty. The patient will be followed up for 10 years to assess the occurrence of disabling stroke or death, and to determine the morbidity and mortality related to therapy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male scheduled to undergo a supratentorial craniotomy for the removal of a brain tumor. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control it. He does not have diabetes or any coronary heart diseases. He has a BMI of 25. The patient is not currently taking beta-blockers and does not have a history of coagulopathy, severe liver disease, or renal disease. He has been informed about the study and has given his consent to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and complains of excessive daytime sleepiness and snoring. He has tried continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy but found it uncomfortable to wear during sleep. He is interested in alternative treatment options and is considering participation in a clinical trial that tests the efficacy of the LinguaFlex Tongue Retractor (LTR) device for the treatment of OSA and snoring. The patient has no known allergies, bleeding disorders, or impaired immunity. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to read, understand, and sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He underwent a biopsy after an abnormal prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test result. The biopsy revealed prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 7 (3+4). He is currently in good health and has no significant medical history. His PSA level is 8.2 ng/mL, and his digital rectal exam (DRE) is consistent with a mildly enlarged prostate. He has not received any treatment for his prostate cancer yet. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help researchers study prostate cancer and find better ways to diagnose, prevent, and treat it. He has read and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He has a smoking history of 30 pack years and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He has been using an inhaled bronchodilator and inhaled corticosteroid for the past year. He reports shortness of breath with exertion and has difficulty walking long distances. He denies any chest pain or coughing up blood. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication regularly. He is able to perform spirometry and plethysmography maneuvers without difficulty. He has no history of any implanted devices or metal in his body. He understands the study procedures and is willing to participate in the study as indicated by signature on the informed consent. He is able to perform a breath hold for 16 seconds and is judged to be in otherwise stable health on the basis of medical history.

A 32-year-old non-menopausal woman presented to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m² and a waist circumference of 85 cm. She has no history of chronic illness and her laboratory parameters are within the normal range. She is a non-smoker and does not engage in intense physical activity.
