She reports a habitual low intake of whole grain foods and is willing to eat breakfast cereals. She has not undergone any weight loss or gain that exceeds 3kg within the last 3 months. She has not received any medication or undergone any surgery that could interfere with the evaluation of the studied parameters. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known allergies to cereals. She has consented to participate in the study and is covered by Health Insurance System and/or in compliance with the recommendations of National Law in force relating to biomedical research. She has also registered in the national file of volunteers participating in biomedical research.

42-year-old female with a history of hypertension presents to the cardiology clinic for evaluation of her cardiac function. She has no previous history of heart disease, but reports occasional palpitations and shortness of breath. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates a new device for monitoring cardiac function. She is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension and has no other medical conditions. The patient has no wounds or surgical incisions at the site of sensor placement and meets all inclusion/exclusion criteria for the trial.

16 yo F with a history of depression and anxiety presenting with worsening mood and decreased interest in activities. The patient has tried multiple medications in the past with minimal improvement in symptoms. The patient is currently not taking any medication for depression but is seeing a therapist once a week. The patient is interested in non-pharmacological options to improve mood and willing to participate in a clinical trial. Past Medical History: -Depression -Anxiety -Migraines -Seasonal allergies -GERD -IBS. Medications: None. Allergies: NKDA. Family History: Maternal grandmother with depression, father with anxiety. Social History: Lives with parents and younger sister, attends high school, participates in extracurricular activities, no current drug or alcohol use.

Sophie is a 14-year-old girl who is going to high school. She is in good health and has completed all routine childhood vaccinations against diphtheria, tetanus and pertussis diseases, according to the recommended vaccination schedule at the time. She has no history of any allergic reactions to vaccines. She is not pregnant and has agreed to use adequate contraceptive precautions for 30 days prior to vaccination and for two months after completion of the vaccination series. She has not participated in any other clinical study and has not received any investigational or non-registered product within 30 days preceding the first dose of study vaccine. She is not on any chronic immunosuppressive drugs or any other immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to the first vaccine dose. She has no known history of cancer or autoimmune disease under treatment. She has no history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine or following any other tetanus toxoid, diphtheria toxoid or pertussis-containing vaccine. She has no history of encephalopathy within seven days of administration of a previous dose of pertussis vaccine that is not attributable to another identifiable cause. She has no history of progressive neurologic disorder, uncontrolled epilepsy or progressive encephalopathy. She has not had a temperature of >= 105°F within 48 hours of receipt of a prior dose of diphteria-tetanu-pertussis (DTP) vaccine, not due to another identifiable cause. She has not experienced seizures with or without fever within three days of a prior dose of DTP vaccine. She has not had severe Arthus-type hypersensitivity reactions following a prior dose of tetanus toxoid within the previous 10 years. She has no previous history of Guillain-Barré syndrome. She has no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition. She is not currently suffering from any acute disease.

A 45 year old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with multiple metastases to her liver, lung and bone. She has been treated with one prior regimen of cytotoxic chemotherapy and her disease has progressed. She complains of fatigue, loss of appetite, difficulty breathing and bone pain. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. She has a performance status of 1 on ECOG scale. Her labs are as follows: Hemoglobin: 10.5 g/dL Platelets: 170,000 /cu.mm Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL AST: 42 IU/L ALT: 38 IU/L Bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL. She has no other concurrent malignancy and is willing to comply with contraceptive measures.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and is scheduled for surgical resection. The patient has a history of smoking and has been experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past few months. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has consented to participate in the study after receiving clear and loyal explanations. The patient has no history of previous abdominal surgeries in the upper part and does not have peritoneal carcinomatosis. The aim of the study is to demonstrate the existence of independent pancreatic segments following the lymphatic drainage of the gland, which may lead to better outcomes for pancreatic resections. The patient will undergo peri-operative exploration of the peri-pancreatic lymphatic pathways during the surgical resection. This study aims to improve the lymph-node dissection and prevent leakage from the pancreatic duct stump, which may lead to a lower rate of postoperative complications such as fistula formation.

33 y/o female who had a vaginal delivery 14 months ago, currently experiencing lumbopelvic pain and incontinence. She has been diagnosed with diastasis recti and her inter-rectal distance is measured at 2.5cm above the umbilicus. She is interested in participating in a research study that evaluates the success of a 4-week group exercise class specifically designed to address diastasis recti closure. She has no history of cardiovascular problems or abdominal surgery other than her cesarean section.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with posterior vaginal wall prolapse. She has been experiencing pelvic pressure and discomfort during intercourse for the past year. Her medical history includes hypertension and hypothyroidism, for which she takes medication. She does not have any known allergies to local anesthetics. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but drinks alcohol socially. She speaks and understands Danish fluently and is able to give informed consent. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her postoperative pain management.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after her routine mammogram showed a lump in her breast. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of triple negative breast cancer. She had received adjuvant chemotherapy with anthracycline and taxane and completed the treatment 2 years ago. However, her cancer has come back and has now spread to her lungs and liver. She is experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial for treatment. She has no history of CNS metastasis or prior exposure to gemcitabine or mTOR inhibitors. Her lab results show adequate hematopoietic, hepatic, and renal function. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is willing to comply with the protocol.

52-year-old male with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease status post percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) who was admitted to the ICU with acute decompensated heart failure. He has a history of smoking and alcohol use. On admission, he presented with dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam revealed bilateral crackles in the lung fields and elevated jugular venous pressure. He was started on intravenous dobutamine and noradrenaline to support his blood pressure and cardiac output. He has been on mechanical ventilation since admission. His laboratory studies showed elevated levels of BNP and troponin. He has been receiving diuretic therapy and his fluid status has been closely monitored. He is currently hemodynamically stable on inotropic support but has not been weaned off mechanical ventilation yet.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through routine liver function tests. The patient has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and chronic hepatitis B infection. CT scan revealed a 5 cm liver mass without vascular invasion. The patient underwent liver resection and TACE therapy as a primary treatment for HCC. The patient has an ECOG performance score of 1 and Child-Pugh rating of A. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency, or any disease process requiring immunosuppressive therapy. The patient has no history of congestive heart failure, unstable angina, or thrombosis requiring anticoagulation. The patient has no primary cancers of any kind or location other than HCC. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed a voluntary informed consent form.

A 20-year-old male college student, who is a varsity basketball player, presents for a study on the effects of exercise and non-concussive bodily contact on eye-tracking scores. The patient has no history of neurological conditions, psychiatric disorders, or significant eye-sight abnormalities. He has 20/20 vision with corrective lenses. He is fluent in English and has been playing basketball since high school. He is physically fit and has no current complaints or concerns. He currently takes no medications and denies any history of substance abuse. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of research in sports medicine.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) for the past 2 years, and is currently on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion over the past few months. His recent echocardiography revealed moderate pulmonary hypertension with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) of 45 mmHg. He has been scheduled for a right heart catheterization (Swan-Ganz) to confirm the diagnosis and establish the severity of PH. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will explore the correlation between non-invasive pulmonary blood pressure readings and Swan-Ganz results. He does not have a history of asthma or any other significant pulmonary disease. He is not on any ventilator support, long-term oxygen therapy or CPAP/BPAP. He has not had any chest surgery or pacemaker implantation in the prior 6 months. He does not have any significant primary valvular disease or major cardiovascular event within the prior 3 months. He is a non-smoker and does not have any diagnosed respiratory tract infection or airway or lung disease in the prior 3 months. He does not have any unexplained muscle weakness and is able to comfortably lie down for 30 minutes. He is not currently hospitalized due to CHF deterioration, and his BMI is less than 40 kg/m2. He is able and willing to sign informed consent.

72-year-old female with a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in her left eye with a primary or recurrent subfoveal choroidal neovascularization (CNV) lesion. She has a classic CNV component that is >=50% of the total lesion area with a total lesion size >=5400 um in greatest linear dimension. Her best corrected visual acuity, using ETDRS charts, is 20/80 in the left eye. She has not received treatment with verteporfin in her left eye less than 3 months preceding Day 0. She has not participated in any studies of investigational drugs within 1 month preceding Day 0 (excluding vitamins and minerals studies). She has no subretinal hemorrhage in the left eye that involves the center of the fovea, if the size of the hemorrhage is either >=50% of the total lesion area or >=1 disc area in size. She has no subfoveal fibrosis or atrophy in the left eye. She has no CNV in either eye due to other causes, such as ocular histoplasmosis, trauma, or pathologic myopia. She has no retinal pigment epithelium tear involving the macula in the left eye. She has no concurrent intraocular condition (e.g., cataract or diabetic retinopathy) that, in the opinion of the investigator, either could require medical or surgical intervention during the 24-month study period to prevent or treat visual loss that might result from that condition, or if allowed to progress untreated, could likely contribute to loss of at least 2 Snellen equivalent lines of best corrected visual acuity over the 24-month study period. She has no active intraocular inflammation (grade trace or above) in the left eye. She has no vitreous hemorrhage in the left eye. She has no history of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment or macular hole (Stage 3 or 4) in the left eye. She has no history of idiopathic or autoimmune-associated uveitis in either eye. She has no infectious conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, or endophthalmitis in either eye. She is able to comply with study or follow-up procedures. She has signed informed consent and authorization of use and disclosure of protected health information. She meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

A 62-year-old male patient presented at the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with a suspected myocardial infarction. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes for which he takes oral hypoglycemic medication. He is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of bleeding disorders or known allergies to medication. He has not participated in any other clinical trials before.

A 31-year-old pregnant woman in her 32nd week of gestation presented with preterm rupture of membranes. She has no significant medical history and no history of preterm birth. She reports no fever, chills, abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart rate is regular at 140 beats per minute. Her cervix is closed upon examination, and there are no signs of inflammation or infection. Initial inflammation markers, including vaginal IL-6 and cervical swab samples for atypical bacteria and direct microscopy, are taken. The physician decides that the patient is eligible for the clinical trial and randomly assigns her to receive either azithromycin-ampicillin or sulbactam-ampicillin treatment. The patient receives her treatment and continues her routine follow-up. When delivery occurs, cord blood is taken, and inflammation markers such as procalcitonin, CRP, and complete blood count are examined. The baby's neonatal inflammation status is determined and compared to the initial inflammation values. The routine neonatal intensive care follow-up of the baby is continued, and the effectiveness of the treatment in terms of early neonatal sepsis is determined.

50-year-old man with a history of metastatic colorectal cancer who has completed a previous Amgen-sponsored conatumumab study without disease progression. The patient has been on chemotherapy and conatumumab for the past 6 months and has tolerated the treatment well. He has no significant medical history, with the exception of hypertension that is well-controlled with medications. The patient is not planning to become pregnant or father a child in the near future and is willing to use adequate contraceptive precautions as specified in the exclusion criteria. The patient is available for protocol required study visits and is willing to continue the treatment with conatumumab and/or ganitumab.

58-year-old male smoker with a history of COPD for the past 5 years. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing on exertion. His current medications include tiotropium inhaler and albuterol inhaler as needed. He has a smoking history of 20 pack years. His FEV1 is 60% of the predicted normal and post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC is 0.6. He has no history of asthma or respiratory tract infection within the past 6 weeks. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of glycopyrronium bromide in comparison to his current medication.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of epilepsy secondary to neurocysticercosis. He has experienced at least one spontaneous seizure within the past 6 months and has been diagnosed with intraparenchymal NCC with fewer than 20 active cysts. The patient is willing to be hospitalized for a minimum of 2 weeks for the study and is willing to use acceptable forms of contraception during the study and for at least 1 month after albendazole therapy. He has tested PPD negative and does not have subarachnoid or ventricular NCC. The patient has not received previous therapy with albendazole or praziquantel within 2 years of study entry. He does not have intracranial hypertension, history of status epilepticus, focal neurological defects, or cysts in critical regions such as the brainstem or eyes. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not hypersensitive to albendazole, antiepileptic drugs, or contrast. He is willing to undergo CT or MRI and has no other CNS processes that may interfere with study assessments.

56 year old man with a history of non-small cell lung cancer diagnosed 6 months ago. He underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy for the primary tumor and is currently in remission. However, he now complains of severe pain in his mid-back which has been worsening over the past 2 months. Imaging studies revealed multiple spinal bone metastases. He is currently on bisphosphonate therapy for the bone metastases. He reports difficulty with walking due to the pain and is seeking further treatment options. He has a Karnofsky performance score of 80 and has given his consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was recently diagnosed with oral cancer. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and had a neck dissection. He is experiencing shoulder dysfunction and has limited range of motion in his left shoulder. He is a retired teacher and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He is an avid reader and enjoys watching movies. He is currently living with his wife and adult son. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has no history of shoulder pain or known shoulder pathology prior to his cancer diagnosis. He is fluent in Chinese and able to communicate well. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the instructions given.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been living with diabetes for 8 years and has been taking metformin 1500 mg/day and gliclazide 120 mg/day without achieving adequate glucose control. His HbA1c is 9.2% and he complains of frequent episodes of hyperglycemia and polyuria. He is obese with a BMI of 32 and has a sedentary lifestyle. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his time sitting in front of a computer screen. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled by lisinopril 20 mg/day. He denies any history of cardiovascular disease or retinopathy. His serum creatinine is 0.9 mg/dl and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 75 ml/min/1.73m2. He has no known drug allergies. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his diabetes control and to reduce his body weight.

The patient is a healthy adult volunteer, aged 25, who wishes to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of intravenous Lactated Ringer Solution on measured serum lactate levels in healthy individuals. The patient does not have any history of acute symptoms or clinical conditions associated with fluid overload, such as congestive heart failure, renal or hepatic failure. The patient is not pregnant or currently breastfeeding, and has not been a prisoner. The patient's baseline serum lactate level is less than 2.2mmol and their baseline creatinine is less than 1.5 mg/dL. The patient will be required to sign a written consent form approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) and will be instructed to provide their weight in the consent form. The patient will receive an 18-gauge IV in one antecubital fossa and will be randomized to either the Lactated Ringer's group or the Placebo group. The exact amount of fluid bolus will be determined based on the patient's weight in kilograms multiplied by 30, rounding the final figure to the nearest 100ml for simplicity. After the intravenous fluid treatment, a serum lactate level will be drawn to determine if there is a significant rise in lactate levels. The patient will be monitored continuously during the procedure and will be assessed by an attending and/or resident physician should any adverse effects occur.

A 28-year-old Canadian woman who has been recently diagnosed with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) or relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) according to McDonald criteria. She has an EDSS score of 5.5 or less and is experiencing features of a first typical optic neuritis within 21 days of recruitment. She has a baseline 25(OH)D level below 80 nmol/L and is not currently taking vitamin D3 supplements. She is willing to use a reliable form of contraception during the active treatment phase of the trial, which is the first 90 days of being provided with the study drug. She has no contraindications to high-dose vitamin D supplementation. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 64-year-old female who recently underwent testing and was diagnosed with low grade endometrioid type adenocarcinoma. She has no history of cancer in her family and has never undergone radiation or chemotherapy for cancer. She has been treated with hormonal therapy for early endometrial neoplasia in the past. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove the uterus and/or cervix (hysterectomy) to treat her cancer. She has no evidence of deep invasion or peritoneal disease based on preoperative imaging. She is in good overall health and has no medical conditions that would make surgery unsafe. The patient is willing to participate in the study and have sentinel lymph node mapping performed to see if the cancer has spread. She understands that this study will involve the collection of tissue for molecular testing before and after surgery, as well as blood samples for tumor marker analysis.

The patient is a healthy male between the age of 20 and 30, with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.0 and 32.0 kg/m2. He has no history of any metabolic, allergic, dermatological, hepatic, renal, hematological, pulmonary, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, neurological, respiratory, endocrine, or psychiatric disorder. The patient is willing to sign an informed consent form and abide by the study restrictions. He has a history of a minimum of one bowel movement per day. The patient is not known to have any hypersensitivity to saroglitazar magnesium or other PPAR agonists, or excipients in the saroglitazar magnesium formulation. He has not undergone stomach or intestinal surgery or resection that would alter absorption and/or excretion of orally administered drugs. The patient has no history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse within the past year. He consumes less than or equal to 14 units of alcohol per week, and has a negative urine drug screen at Check-in. He has no positive hepatitis panel or human immunodeficiency virus test. The patient has not participated in a clinical study involving administration of an investigational drug in the past 90 days prior to dosing or 5 times the t1/2 (whichever is longer). He is not using any medications/products known to alter drug absorption, metabolism, or elimination processes, and is not using any prescription medications/products, slow-release medications/products, or nonprescription medications/products, including vitamins, minerals, and phytotherapeutic/herbal/plant-derived preparations within the respective time frames. He has not used tobacco- or nicotine-containing products within 3 months prior to Check-in, and has not received blood products within 2 months prior to Check-in. The patient has no poor peripheral venous access, and has not previously completed or withdrawn from this study or any other study investigating saroglitazar magnesium. He has not been exposed to significant diagnostic or therapeutic radiation or current employment in a job requiring radiation exposure monitoring within 12 months prior to Check-in. The patient has not participated in a radiolabeled drug study within the previous 4 months prior to admission to the clinic for this study or participated in a radiolabeled drug study where exposures are not known to the Investigator within the previous 6 months prior to admission to the clinic for this study.

32-year-old female who has been internally displaced due to a natural disaster in Leogane, Haiti. She currently lives in a temporary tent or camp and is interested in learning more about HIV/STI prevention. She is capable of providing informed consent and is willing to participate in group sessions led by a trained community health worker. She has no medical history of HIV/STIs and has not received any previous HIV/STI prevention education.

Sophia is a 10-year-old girl who suffered from burns on 35% of her total body surface area due to a kitchen accident. She was admitted to the hospital within 4 days of the injury and her attending physician believes she is likely to survive. Her parents have given their informed consent and Sophia has provided her assent to participate in the study. There is no history of anticonvulsant or glucocorticoid use, gastric/bowel resection, parathyroid disease, liver disease, chronic renal failure or prior pharmacologic vitamin D use (>1000 IU/D). Physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise.

55-year-old female with a history of obesity, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with upper abdominal pain and elevated liver enzymes. Abdominal ultrasound reveals evidence of fatty liver disease. The patient is diagnosed with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and is recommended for a liver biopsy to assess the degree of liver steatosis and staging liver fibrosis. The patient agrees to participate in the non-invasive diagnostic method for liver biopsy, which includes the Transient Elastography (TE) combined with the Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP). The patient will undergo regular follow-up visits, and blood routine, blood biochemistry, abdominal ultrasound, and the non-invasive diagnostic method will be detected during the follow-up. The patient has signed an informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 19-year-old female college freshman who has gained weight since starting college. She is currently not exercising and has a BMI of 28, which is considered overweight. She has a family history of obesity, hypertension, and diabetes. She is not currently on any medications and has no known allergies. She reports feeling self-conscious about her weight gain and is interested in learning about ways to improve her body composition and overall health. She lives in a dormitory on campus and has a meal plan through the university. She reports consuming fast food and sugary drinks frequently due to the convenience of these options on campus. She is willing to participate in a 10-week intervention to improve her physical activity and eating habits.

45-year-old female with a history of borderline elevated total cholesterol levels for the past 2 years presents for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the effect of plant oils on blood lipids and metabolism. She has no prior history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, hypertension, or any other chronic diseases. She reports occasional bloating and constipation but denies any known gastrointestinal disease. She has no history of acute or chronic inflammatory conditions, liver or kidney dysfunction, or drug or alcohol abuse. She is not currently taking any lipid-lowering, anti-inflammatory, antidepressant, or blood pressure medication. She has not taken any antibiotics or probiotics in the last three months. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the role of polyunsaturated fatty acids in improving blood lipid levels and reducing the risk of cardiovascular disease.

The patient is a 32 year old man who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has a history of auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions. He has been stable on his current medication regimen for the past 6 months, with no medication changes during this time period. He has a stable Positive and Negative Symptom Score (PANSS) score over a period of 2 weeks. He understands the purpose of the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate. He does not have any history of substance or alcohol abuse. He has not had any seizures in the past 6 months and has not suffered from any clinically significant brain trauma documented by CT or MRI. He is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is a high school graduate and is currently unemployed. He lives with his parents and is not involved in any particular hobbies or interests. He is not on any other medications besides those prescribed for his schizophrenia.

32 F with a history of ulcerative colitis diagnosed at age 18. She has been in clinical remission for the last six months as assessed by an adapted disease activity index and a CRP level of less than 10. However, she continues to experience functional abdominal symptoms such as bloating, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. She also reports high perceived stress levels with a Levenstein perceived stress score of 0.6. She has not used steroids or made any changes to her medication in the last month. She does not have an ileostomy or colostomy and does not have any history of cognitive impairment, psychosis or substance misuse. She has not received any previous psychological interventions and is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of high protein and cereal grain intake and low fruit intake. He reports consuming less than 2.5 servings of fruit per day. He has no history of diabetes, thyroid or parathyroid disease, cirrhosis, or unstable heart disease. He has not had gastric bypass surgery and is able to chew dried fruit adequately. He is willing to avoid potassium supplements, antacids other than Pepto Bismol, and medications that alter appetite during the study. He is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated for the study. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore the effect of dried fruit intake on his acid-base balance.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year with her partner. She has no significant medical history and her BMI is within the normal range (23 kg/m2). She is a normoresponder and will be undergoing an antagonist protocol with agonist trigger for ovarian stimulation. Her partner has no known fertility issues with fresh autologous ejaculates of at least 5 million/ml. The patient has opted for only ICSI as the insemination technique. Prior to the start of the IVF cycle, the patient will undergo PGT-A using NGS in blastocysts. The patient has a normal karyotype and has primary infertility. She is interested in participating in the study to investigate whether there is a correlation between telomere length (TL) in the first Polar Body (PB) and TL in the corresponding Cumulus cells (CC) to gain information about oocyte competence.

A 55-year-old man was referred to the hepatology department for further evaluation of his liver disease. He has a past medical history of alcohol use disorder and was diagnosed with alcoholic liver disease by his primary care physician. He reports drinking about a pint of whiskey daily for the past 20 years. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 3 weeks and currently experiencing symptoms of withdrawal, including tremors and anxiety. His laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, and his imaging studies show evidence of cirrhosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the safety of acamprosate in individuals with liver disease to help him maintain sobriety. He has no history of kidney disease or congestive heart failure and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

An 18-year-old girl, with a BMI at the 95th percentile for her age, presents with concerns about her weight. She has been struggling with her weight for several years and has tried various diets without much success. She is generally healthy and physically active, but she has not been able to lose much weight. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not taking any medication or supplements for weight control. She meets the eligibility criteria for this study and is interested in participating in a 12-week combined exercise program to explore the effects on ghrelin O acyl transferase, acylated ghrelin, and desacylated ghrelin levels. She is excited to potentially learn more about her body and how exercise can impact her overall health.

The patient is a 32-year-old full-time nurse working in a hospital in Israel with routine direct hands-on contact with patients. She has been a member of Clalit Health System health plan for more than a year. She has no history of chronic illness and is generally in good health. She has received the current season's flu vaccine within the last 48 hours and is willing to participate in the study by completing blood draws and providing respiratory specimens when experiencing acute respiratory illnesses. She is interested in learning more about the effectiveness of the flu vaccine in preventing illness and reducing exposure to patients.

The patient is a 27-year-old man who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder II. He has experienced multiple episodes of depression and hypomania over the past 5 years. He has a history of suicide attempts and has been hospitalized in the past due to severe depression. He is currently under the care of a primary care physician who prescribes his medications. He has a stable medication regimen, which includes a mood stabilizer and an antidepressant. However, he still experiences residual symptoms of depression, including low mood, loss of energy, and decreased motivation. He is interested in participating in an online psychotherapy program for bipolar disorder, as he would like to learn new skills to manage his symptoms and improve his overall quality of life. He has access to a broadband internet connection and a telephone, and is fluent in English. He is not currently receiving specialty mental health services and is not experiencing active suicidal ideation.

A 67-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is scheduled for an elective surgical procedure. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disease and is not currently taking any medications known to affect cognitive function. She is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no history of reduced level of consciousness and is generally healthy except for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with obesity for several years. She has a BMI of 42 and has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past two years. She has been trying to lose weight through diet and exercise, but with little success. She has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job, which limits her physical activity. She is married and has two children. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her diet consists of high-calorie and high-fat foods. She is interested in bariatric surgery to help her lose weight and improve her diabetes control. She is open to either laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery or laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, as recommended by her physician. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help advance understanding of the factors that may affect liver function after bariatric surgery.

A 62-year-old woman is seeking medical attention for knee pain that has been bothering her for the past year. She reports pain that is worse with weight-bearing activities and after prolonged sitting. She also experiences stiffness in the morning that lasts for about 30 minutes. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers and physical therapy, but they have not provided significant relief. She has no history of trauma or injury to her knee. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medications. She denies smoking, drinking alcohol, or using illicit drugs. On examination, there is tenderness on palpation of the medial and lateral joint lines of the right knee. There is also mild effusion present. The range of motion of the knee is limited due to pain. X-rays show evidence of primary knee osteoarthritis. The doctor has recommended her to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of methotrexate in decreasing pain and inflammation in symptomatic knee OA.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. He was initially started on adefovir treatment, but his viral load has not decreased significantly despite six months of treatment. His medical records show that he is HBeAg positive and has no history of other viral infections. There is no evidence of decompensated cirrhosis, and his liver function is compensated. The patient has no history of pancreatitis or chronic renal insufficiency. He has no current or past abuse of illegal drugs or alcohol. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. His serum alanine aminotransferase level is less than 10 times the upper limit of normal at screening. He is not currently taking any nucleoside/nucleotide analogues other than adefovir. The patient has not received any prior therapy with nucleoside or nucleotide analogue antiviral agents with activity against hepatitis B or any experimental anti-HBV antiviral therapy or any China Traditional Medicine. He has not received therapy with interferon, thymosin alpha, or other immunostimulators within 24 weeks of randomization. The patient does not require chronic administration of medications that cause immunosuppression or that are associated with a high risk of nephrotoxicity or hepatotoxicity.

A 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic non-malignant pain for the past 3 years. She has been referred to the Interdisciplinary Pain Center Zealand University Hospital Koege, Denmark, after seeking treatment from multiple specialists without success. She reports that her pain is affecting her quality of life and ability to work. She has a history of anxiety and depression and is currently taking medication for both. She is married and has two children. She has completed vocational training but has been unable to work due to her pain. She speaks and understands Danish fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with moderate renal impairment. She has a medical history of hypertension, managed with medication. She is currently not on any other medications. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys hiking and cooking. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance knowledge about renal impairment and drug safety.

A 42-year old woman was diagnosed with stage 2 breast cancer six months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She is currently taking hormonal therapy. She is married and has two children. She works as a school teacher. The patient complains of difficulty remembering things, such as the names of her students, and is easily distracted. She is also experiencing difficulty concentrating on tasks and finds herself becoming mentally fatigued more quickly than usual. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or substance abuse. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study. She is an alert and cooperative woman who wants to improve her cognitive function after cancer treatment.

A 25-year-old female with a history of good dental hygiene and no smoking habits presented to the dental clinic with complaints of sensitivity in her teeth. She has four non-carious cervical lesions (NCCLs) with margins in enamel and dentin, and the largest area is in dentin. The patient has no known medical issues and is not under orthodontic treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of self-etching adhesive systems for restoring these lesions. The patient is willing to undergo selective enamel etching if necessary and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 29-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of vaginal itching, burning, and discharge. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year and has been diagnosed with Candida vaginitis multiple times. She complains of discomfort during sexual intercourse and has noticed that her symptoms worsen after taking antibiotics. She has tried over-the-counter antifungal creams and suppositories, but the symptoms keep returning. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of allergies or chronic medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find a more effective treatment for her recurrent Candida vaginitis.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19 and is currently under mechanical ventilation due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He has no significant medical history and no prior lung disease. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 90/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and D-dimer levels. He has been receiving standard care for COVID-19 and is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial comparing two ventilation strategies for ARDS caused by COVID-19.

A 10-year-old boy was referred to the orthodontic clinic by his dentist for evaluation of his malocclusion. His parents reported that he has difficulty chewing and often experiences jaw pain. Upon examination, he was diagnosed with skeletal Class II malocclusion with an ANB angle greater than 5 degrees and a retrognathic mandible. His overjet was measured to be greater than 5mm and he had minimal crowding in his dental arches. He did not have any previous orthodontic treatment, and his lower incisors were on average inclination. He was determined to be in stage II based on the modified cervical vertebral maturation stages (CVMS) according to Bacetti et al. He did not have any congenitally missing or extracted permanent teeth and did not present with posterior crossbites or severe maxillary transverse deficiency. He did not have any severe facial asymmetry or systemic diseases that may affect orthodontic treatment results.

A 33-year-old healthy, non-smoking male with a BMI of 25 is being sought for a clinical trial to determine the effect of morning versus evening administration of Empagliflozin. The patient should not have any gastrointestinal, renal or cardiovascular diseases, nor any abnormal laboratory values. Additionally, the patient should not have any prior history of sensitivity to medicinal products or excipients, nor any surgeries of the gastrointestinal tract that may interfere with drug absorption. The patient should not have any endocrine or autoimmune disorders, nor have a history of drug, alcohol or solvent abuse. The patient should not have donated blood or participated in a drug study within 6 weeks preceding the start of the study. The patient should be willing to participate, give their consent and be available for the study procedures.

Patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. He has received two prior treatment regimens, including both a proteasome inhibitor and an immune-modulatory drug, but has experienced relapse and/or progression of the disease. He has measurable disease, with a serum M protein level of 1 g/dl measured by serum protein electrophoresis. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He has an indwelling central venous catheter. He has not received any anticancer treatment for at least two weeks prior to visit 1 and has not received a therapeutic antibody for at least six weeks prior to visit 1. He has not undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation or solid organ transplantation. He has not received corticosteroids for at least two weeks prior to visit 1 unless the dose was <= 10 mg/day prednisolone or equivalent. His AST and ALT levels are within normal limits, and his total conjugated bilirubin is not higher than 1.5 x upper limit of normal. His absolute neutrophil count is >= 1.0 x 10^9/L (without growth factor support) and his platelet count is >= 25 x 10^9/L (without transfusions). His calculated GFR is >= 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault Formula). He has no clinically relevant concurrent medical disease or condition that would compromise his safety or interfere with the evaluation of the safety of the test drug. He has no chronic or ongoing infectious disease requiring treatment at the time of enrollment or within the previous two weeks. He has no active hepatitis B or C, laboratory evidence for a chronic infection with hepatitis B or C, or HIV infection. He is willing to use a highly effective method of birth control during the trial until one year after the last dose if he is a woman of childbearing potential or a male patient with partners of childbearing potential. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no known or suspected active alcohol or drug abuse, and has not been treated with another investigational drug within the past four weeks before start of therapy or concomitantly with this trial. He has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the study drug. He has no other malignancies within 5 years at time of screening (except basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ treated with curative therapy). He has no known autoimmune diseases requiring systemic treatment in past 5 years and interfering with evaluation of study drug. There are no pre-existing disorders of the central nervous system.

A 46-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 comes to the clinic seeking surgical intervention for weight loss. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and osteoarthritis of the knee. She has tried various diets and exercise programs to lose weight but has been unsuccessful. She has been evaluated by the bariatric multidisciplinary team and found to be a suitable candidate for the study. She does not have a history of H. Pylori infection or chronic diarrhea and has not undergone any previous bariatric or extensive abdominal surgeries. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the post-operative care plan.

A 40-year-old woman presents with redness, pain, and decreased vision in her left eye. She reports a history of uveitis that has been refractory to previous treatments including corticosteroids and immunosuppressive agents. Her medical history is significant for rheumatoid arthritis and she is currently taking methotrexate for this condition. She denies any recent infections or exposure to sick contacts. On examination, visual acuity is 20/200 in the affected eye with anterior chamber cells and flare and vitreous haze. Slit lamp exam reveals posterior synechiae and keratic precipitates. She meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial of infliximab for uveitis and is interested in participating.

A 60-year-old Japanese female who has been diagnosed with advanced breast cancer and has completed a double-blind study with either letrozole or fadrozole therapy. The patient must be postmenopausal and not have experienced intolerable toxicity during the double-blind study. Additionally, the patient must not have had confirmed progressive disease during the double-blind study and must not have received concurrent anti-cancer therapy. The patient must be willing to participate in an extension study to investigate the safety of letrozole monotherapy at a dose of 1.0mg/day or fadrozole monotherapy at a dose of 2.0mg/day.

A 56-year-old man with a medical history of hypertension for the past 8 years, despite treatment with multiple antihypertensive medications, presents to the hypertension consultations for evaluation. His most recent blood pressure reading was 158/90 mmHg. He has a family history of hypertension and cardiovascular disease. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and he exercises regularly. He has no known allergies or other medical conditions. He has been taking medication for hypertension, but his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. He underwent an ambulatory measure of the arterial pressure during 24 hours before the pre-inclusion visit which confirmed his essential hypertension. The patient is interested in participating in the Stendo pulsating suit clinical trial to help improve his blood pressure control.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who have been diagnosed with schizophrenia, schizophreniform or schizoaffective disorder, and are stable outpatients or partial hospitalization. The participant must have a normal IQ (>70) and not currently taking the antipsychotic clozapine. They must be able to speak and understand English fluently to complete cognitive tasks and provide valid informed consent. Participants with pacemakers, implanted electrical stimulators or defibrillators, metallic implants, skin damage or skin conditions, hair styles hindering the placement of electrodes, cranial pathologies, head trauma, epilepsy, mental retardation, any known history of neurological disorders, autism, uncorrected vision problems, pregnancy, substance dependence in the past six months, or substance abuse in the past month are excluded from the study.

A 35-year-old male patient is presenting to the dentist with a complaint of a painful tooth on the lower left side of his mouth. The patient has a history of dental caries and has had several fillings in the past. Upon examination, the dentist discovers that the tooth has decayed beyond repair and requires a crown. The patient is informed about the clinical trial and agrees to participate. The patient has no known allergies and is not pregnant or lactating. The tooth in question is a lower molar and is vital and asymptomatic at the start of the study. The patient is able to attend all recall appointments and is eager to participate in the study to improve the quality of his dental care.

65 year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. Currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin daily. The patient has no symptoms of carotid stenosis or stroke, but is considered at risk due to his medical history. He is interested in participating in a screening program to detect any potential issues with his carotid arteries and reduce his risk of stroke. The patient is able to travel to the physician's office or central screening location for the screening.

A 19-year-old male student who has recently been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder is interested in participating in research on autism and other neurodevelopmental disabilities. He was diagnosed with autism at the age of 12 and has been receiving therapy and support ever since. He is currently taking medication for anxiety and has no known allergies. He is an avid reader and enjoys playing video games. He has no history of extreme prematurity, genetic disorders related to autism, or recent diagnosis of psychosis. He does not have any metal implants or permanent retainers.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the Nephrology department of the Besançon University Hospital Center with acute kidney injury (AKI). The patient's serum creatinine level has increased by more than 50% compared to the baseline level. The patient does not have chronic kidney disease. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus but is currently not on any medication. The patient reports feeling fatigued and has decreased urine output. On examination, the patient is afebrile and has normal vital signs. Focal tenderness is observed during palpation of the lower back. Blood and urine tests have been ordered to assess kidney function. The patient is a candidate for inclusion in the clinical trial investigating the development of a prognostic score for intra-hospital mortality in ARI. The patient will be followed up for the duration of their hospital stay to assess their prognosis.

A 45 year old female patient is admitted to the hospital with a stage 2 pressure ulcer on her sacrum. She has been bedridden for the past two weeks due to a lower back injury. The patient has a history of diabetes and hypertension. She is currently taking medication for both conditions. The patient has normal mental status and is able to communicate well. She is not allergic to any wound products. The wound is measured to be 2 cm in diameter and has a depth of less than 5 mm. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the lower oesophagus. He presented with difficulty swallowing, chest pain, and weight loss of 8% in the past six months. He underwent an endoscopic ultrasound and CT scan, which showed a T3 N1 lesion. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. He has never undergone radiation therapy or chemotherapy for any other condition. His performance status is 1, and he weighs 80kg. He has no known allergy to any medications.

A 45-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His medical history was unremarkable except for a recent diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) confirmed by biopsy. He had been previously treated with rituximab and an anthracycline-based chemotherapy, but his cancer has returned. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His life expectancy is more than 6 weeks. His recent lab results showed normal absolute neutrophil count and platelets, with total bilirubin levels within normal limits. His creatinine and AST/ALT levels were also within normal limits. He has never received any anti-cancer therapy for his primary relapsed/refractory DLBCL except for palliative radiation therapy (RT). He is HIV negative and has no active clinically significant cardiovascular disease. He is willing to use adequate contraception methods for 90 days after the last dose of study drug.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been experiencing pelvic pain for the past 6 months. The pain is moderate to severe and is associated with her menstrual cycle. She also experiences pain during intercourse and bowel movements. She has been diagnosed with endometriosis based on laparoscopic findings. Her menstrual cycles are regular, lasting approximately 5 days. She has no history of abnormal cervical cytology or HPV infection. She is willing to use standardized rescue pain medications and not use any prophylactic pain medication during the study. She is in good general health except for findings related to endometriosis. She has no history of osteoporosis or low trauma fracture. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has no contraindications for elagolix or the standardized rescue medications. She has not had a hysterectomy or bilateral oophorectomy. She has no underlying diseases requiring regular use of pain medication. She has no history of or current anxiety or depression. She has not participated in another clinical trial with investigational medicinal product(s) in the past 3 months. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol, including taking the study intervention as complete units.

We are seeking healthy subjects between the ages of 20 and 40 years old to participate in a clinical trial evaluating changes in heart rate in response to heat pressure and neural stimulation. There will be no harm or tissue damage inflicted during the thermal pain induction, which will be performed using an authorized protocol. The trial aims to develop and apply novel signal processing tools to ECG signals for the first time, with the potential to provide better insight into the basic components of the signal and their relation to pain. Participants will be monitored using VAS and ECG before, during, and after the thermal pain induction. Patients with cardiovascular diseases, taking cardiovascular medications, or with neurological disorders will be excluded from the trial.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and underwent a reduced intensity allogeneic stem cell transplantation from a 7/8 HLA-matched unrelated donor. The patient has had a mixed chimeric state since the transplant and has also experienced disease persistence. The patient's performance status is ECOG PS 1. The patient has had a stable disease state for

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been admitted to the hospital with a positive test for COVID-19. He has been experiencing symptoms for the past 7 days, including fever, cough, and fatigue. The patient has been having difficulty breathing and his SpO2 levels have been consistently below 93%. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. His blood ALT/AST levels are within the normal range. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction. He is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy diagnosed with advanced neuroblastoma. He has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy, but the tumor has not responded to the treatment. He has a solid mass with definable dimensions on the left side of his abdomen. His past medical history is significant for asthma, which is well-controlled with inhalers. He has a normal body mass index, and his growth and development are appropriate for his age. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He enjoys playing soccer and video games. He complains of abdominal pain and decreased appetite, but denies any other symptoms. He has never smoked or used any illicit drugs. His parents are willing to participate in the study and have signed the consent form.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has a history of recurrent fever, fatigue, and muscle pain. She also experiences pain and weakness in her arms and legs, and sometimes experiences dizziness and shortness of breath. She has been diagnosed with Takayasu arteritis (TA) based on the ACR and/or Ishikawa modified Sharma criteria. She has been on glucocorticoids for the past year but has not achieved complete remission of her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and tolerance of Tocilizumab in TA. She is willing to use an effective means of birth control throughout the study. She has not been on any immunosuppressive treatment or biologics other than steroids for the past 4 months. She does not have evidence of an active infection, HIV, hepatitis C, or a positive hepatitis B surface antigen. She has no history of malignant neoplasms except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or solid tumors treated with curative therapy and disease-free for at least 5 years. She is able to provide informed consent and has no cytopenia, insufficient liver function, or insufficient kidney function. She has a negative tuberculin skin test and/or negative Quantiferon and no radiographic evidence suggestive of tuberculosis. She has no contraindication to or precaution in the use of Tocilizumab according to the summary product description, and she is not pregnant.

The patient is a 65-year-old postmenopausal female who has been diagnosed with actinic keratoses on her posterior scalp, ears, neck, lips, arms, hands, and face. She has been using sunscreen regularly but still experiences frequent sun exposure due to her outdoor gardening hobby. She has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. The patient is willing to comply with the prescribed treatment regimen and return to the study site for designated follow-up visits. She has no known allergies to any of the ingredients in the test drug formulations and is not pregnant or lactating. She has not used any other topical agents for the treatment of actinic keratosis in the designated treatment area within the past 5 months and has not had liquid nitrogen treatment for AKs within the past 4 weeks. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to help improve her skin condition and reduce the risk of developing skin cancer.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosed 10 years ago. He is currently taking metformin and sitagliptin for diabetes control. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction three years back. His current blood pressure and lipid profile are well controlled. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He is currently working as a computer programmer and is physically active. The patient has no known drug allergies. His current HbA1c is 7.2% and fasting blood sugar is 145 mg/dl. The patient has undergone a coronary CT angiogram which showed calcium score of 50. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his cardiovascular health. He understands the requirements of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 52-year-old male patient, who is a smoker, came to the clinic with a history of cough and shortness of breath for the past 3 months. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. A chest x-ray revealed a 2 cm nodule in his right lung. A CT scan confirmed the presence of the nodule and showed no signs of metastasis. The pulmonologist recommended a biopsy of the lung lesion using the superDimension™ Navigation System Version 7.2 with Fluoroscopic Navigation Technology. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient is over 18 years of age and is a candidate for the elective ENB procedure. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and has never participated in an investigational drug or device research study within the past 30 days.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been suffering from migraines with or without aura for several years. She experiences at least one migraine attack every 6 weeks, as defined by the International Headache Society criteria. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate contraception. She is able to take study medication as an outpatient and is willing to record the effects. The patient has no history of frequent non-migrainous headaches, atypical migraine that had not previously responded to therapy, migraine with prolonged aura, familial hemiplegic migraine, basilar migraine, or migrainous infarction.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is scheduled for an elective robot-assisted thyroidectomy. She has a BMI of 28 and has no history of arrhythmia, valvular heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, peripheral artery occlusive disease, lung disease or right heart failure. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 33 kg/m2 was recently diagnosed with hypertension. She has a history of unsuccessful dietary attempts to lose weight. She does not have diabetes mellitus, and her body weight has been stable for the past 3 months. She does not have obesity induced by other endocrinologic disorders or monogenetic or syndromic forms of obesity. She has no history of pancreatitis, medullary thyroid carcinoma, or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2. She does not have a significant active or unstable major depressive disorder or other severe psychiatric disorder within the last 2 years. She has never attempted suicide. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about maintaining body weight or adding to weight loss after an intensive lifestyle modification program with the use of tirzepatide.

A 45-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a history of chronic facial pain for the past year. The pain is intense, spontaneous, and can also be evoked by light touch to the facial skin. She has been taking multiple medications for pain control, but none of them have provided satisfactory relief. The patient reports a minimum average pain score of 6 (severe) on the visual analogue scale (VAS). The pain is unilateral and affects the orofacial allodynic region to mechanical and thermal stimulation. She has no history of systemic disorders or any other chronic pain disorder. She has not undergone any recent orofacial surgery or trauma. The patient is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant. She is willing to undergo neuroimaging techniques and non-invasive brain stimulation to investigate factors associated with chronic pain in patients with Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain (TNP).

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who requires an elective surgery under general anesthesia in combination with regional anesthesia. He is classified as ASA 1, without any severe underlying medical conditions or disabilities. He has no history of general anesthesia within the last 3 months before or 4 weeks after the procedure. He has not received prophylaxis with droperidol and has no contraindications for the medications used in the study. He has no known mental or behavioral abnormalities. He is healthy and has no known allergies. The patient and his parents have given informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who has not engaged in regular exercise for the past six months. He has no history of any diseases or injuries in the past six months and has not taken any medication during this time. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and works in an office environment. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to investigate the joint effect of air pollution and exercise on cognitive function. He has no history of professional sports or regular exercise in the past six months. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the exercise intervention program, which includes high intensity intermittent exercise, moderate intensity of aerobic exercise, and stretching control groups.

55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking presented with pain in his left leg when walking 300 meters which disappears after resting for 5 minutes. He reports that this pain has been present for the last year and it has been gradually increasing in severity. He denies pain at rest, numbness, and tingling in the lower extremities, and has no history of trauma, surgery or lower extremity ulcerations. He reports that he has not been very active due to his work schedule and is overweight, with a BMI of 30. He is currently taking amlodipine and atorvastatin for his hypertension and dyslipidemia, respectively. He has no known allergies to medications. He is married and works as a truck driver. He understands the importance of exercise but due to his busy schedule, he has not been able to exercise regularly. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his symptoms and quality of life. He is willing to attend supervised exercise sessions 3 times a week and comply with the protocol.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who are currently employed within the police force and have access to a smartphone or tablet that can run the Bupa Boost app. The study will explore the feasibility and acceptability of using wearable fitness technology to increase physical activity levels among police officers and staff, with the aim of improving health and wellbeing and reducing stress levels. Participants will be required to wear a Fitbit Charge 2™ activity monitor and use the Bupa Boost app to set specific physical activity goals and engage with the motivational strategies provided by the app. The study will involve completing online questionnaires at four different time points, and some data will also be collected from staff occupational health records. The duration of the study is approximately 12 months, and a small pilot study will be undertaken to ensure the data collection methods are acceptable. This study has the potential to provide valuable insight into the effectiveness of mobile fitness technology in a specific workplace setting, and inform future larger scale trials.

A 56-year-old man with a history of hepatitis B virus infection and cirrhosis of the liver. He was diagnosed with liver cancer and was scheduled to receive proton beam therapy as a treatment option. The patient has no history of other malignancies and has not received any previous radiation therapy to the liver. He has a performance status of 1 and is able to carry out light work, such as office work or household chores, but is unable to perform any physically demanding work. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and understands the benefits and risks associated with proton beam therapy.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been experiencing severe pain and stiffness in his right hip for the past year. He has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried various treatments, including physical therapy and medications, but they have not provided significant relief. His mobility has been significantly affected and he has difficulty performing daily activities. He has been scheduled for an elective primary total hip replacement surgery to improve his quality of life. He has no history of bleeding disorders or significant bleeding events. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. His medications include aspirin for prevention of heart attack and high blood pressure medication. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 30-year-old healthy male with no history of orthopedic, musculoskeletal, or neurological pathology is being sought for a clinical trial investigating the effect of a custom-made biomechanical perturbation platform on kinetics, kinematics, and electromyography in healthy subjects. The participant should have a similar anthropometric profile, including weight, shoe size, height, and dominant leg, to ensure consistency in the trial. The participant will be required to walk on the platform under 16 different settings while being analyzed by a three-dimensional motion analysis system, ground reaction force analysis using force platforms, and an electro-myography system. The aim of the study is to evaluate the influence of specific biomechanical challenges on the lower limb's kinetics, kinematics, and electromyographic activity. The trial will be conducted in a controlled setting, and the participant will be required to follow all instructions provided by the research team.

A 37-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV three years ago and has been receiving care at a clinic affiliated with a university medical center. Despite her initial commitment to her medical care, her attendance has been inconsistent over the past year due to a variety of issues such as transportation, child care, and housing. She has missed several appointments over the past 12 months and has not been seen for HIV primary care at least once in each of two consecutive 6-month periods. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent for the study. She has no plans to move out of the area in the next 12 months. The study's interventionists may be able to provide assistance with some of the barriers to care she faces, and she is willing to participate in the study to try to improve her attendance and overall health outcomes.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been addicted to opioids for the last 2 years. She has a history of heroin and codeine abuse and has been in and out of the correctional facility for the last year. She is currently enrolled in Norway's national OMT program and is scheduled to be discharged within the next 30 days. She has voluntarily agreed to participate in this clinical trial after learning about the study from her treatment provider. Her past medical history is significant for opioid dependence and she has never been pregnant or breastfed. She has no known allergies or intolerances to any medications. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up visits.

The patient is a 35-year-old biological mother of an 8-year-old child who has no history of any significant medical conditions. The mother has normal, healthy skin with no pre-existing or dormant dermatologic skin conditions. She is willing to use only the provided cleansing product during the washout time period and refrain from using any other topical skincare products such as moisturizers, lotions, sunscreens, oils, or tanners throughout the study. She is also willing to avoid swimming, hot tubs, excessive sun exposure, or tanning beds during the course of the study. The mother is interested in participating in this study to assess the predominant microflora and skin physiology of her child and herself.

Patient is a 40-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with severe right-sided flank pain. CT scan revealed a 5mm stone in the right ureter causing hydronephrosis. The patient was diagnosed with renal colic and prescribed NSAIDs for pain management. However, due to a history of gastrointestinal ulcers, NSAIDs were not an option. The patient was then given paracetamol and opioids for pain management but experienced side effects such as nausea and dizziness. The patient is now being considered for a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of Heat Wrap for Renal Colic. The patient has no known allergies to heat tapes and is willing to try an alternative treatment with little potential for side effects.

A 25-year-old woman who recently graduated from college is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a toothbrush. She has always used a manual toothbrush and has never had any dental issues. She is in good physical health and has no known allergies. She has a regular menstrual cycle and does not smoke. She has not had any dental work, including prophylaxis, in the past year. She has 28 natural teeth with no significant dental restorations. She is not currently taking any antibiotics or using any chlorhexidine mouth rinse. She has no oral appliances or piercings, and no history of seizures or cancer. She is willing to follow all study procedures and attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who received a kidney transplant 9 months ago due to end-stage renal disease. She has been taking a calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppressant therapy since then. Her past medical history includes hypertension, which is now well controlled, and obesity. She is married and has two teenage children. She works as a teacher and has been struggling with fatigue and lack of energy, which has been affecting her daily activities and quality of life. She used to enjoy walking and hiking, but she has not been able to engage in physical activity as she used to. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her current medications include amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, and the calcineurin inhibitor. She is interested in participating in clinical trials that could potentially improve her quality of life.

59-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic bronchitis and emphysema presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. He reports a 40 pack-year smoking history and has never been prescribed Salmeterol or Flixotide or similar compounds. Spirometry confirms the presence of moderate COPD with an FEV1 of 45% predicted and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 52%. He denies any history of asthma, lung cancer, or bronchiectasis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the mechanisms of action of Seretide in COPD.

A 2-year-old female toddler, presented to the Pediatric Emergency Department with a history of vomiting and diarrhea for the past 24 hours. She was diagnosed with mild dehydration secondary to gastroenteritis. A nasogastric tube placement has been prescribed by the attending physician to initiate enteral rehydration. The child's mother is present and has consented to participate in the study. The child has no known history of intolerance to nitrous oxide. There are no other exclusion criteria for the patient.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has a history of a right breast lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy 5 years ago. She is currently experiencing mild to moderate pain in the left chest and back area, and her oncologist has ordered a PET/CT scan which revealed metastasis to the liver and bones. She has no significant past medical history except for mild hypertension which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. Her laboratory values show adequate liver and renal function, and she has no evidence of CNS metastases. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer, and she has not undergone any major surgeries or experienced any significant traumatic injuries in the past 28 days. She does not have any pre-existing peripheral neuropathy and has not been taking aspirin or anticoagulants. She does not have uncontrolled hypertension or clinically significant cardiovascular disease. She has no active peptic ulcer or bone fractures and does not have a history of thrombotic disorders within the last six months.

32-year-old female delivered a healthy baby girl via C-section two days ago. During her pregnancy, she developed gestational hypertension and her blood pressure was monitored closely. After delivery, her blood pressure remained elevated with two readings over 140/90 taken four hours apart. The patient has no prior history of hypertension or other significant medical conditions. She is interested in participating in the study and using the Honeywell Genesis Android Touch Bluetooth System to help monitor her blood pressure and weight at home.
