She has a smartphone and is comfortable with technology. She is available for video telehealth visits at 48 hours and 7 days after discharge. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 59-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) six months ago. She has been treated with chemotherapy, but the tumor has continued to grow. The patient is a non-smoker and has no significant past medical history. She is married and has two adult children. The patient is currently experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and cough. Her performance status is 1, meaning she is able to carry out activities of daily living, but is limited in physically strenuous activities. The patient has positive NY-ESO-1 expression, as determined by analysis at the trial central laboratory. She is willing to undergo tumor biopsies before starting therapy and after the 3rd CDX-1401 injection. Additionally, she is willing to consent to a third tumor biopsy to be performed after the 3rd MPDL3280A infusion. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or CNS metastases. Her hematologic and end-organ function are adequate. She does not have any known infections or intercurrent illnesses. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to use highly effective contraception during and for 6 months after the last dose of trial therapy.

The patient is a 19-month-old child residing in Guinea-Bissau. The child's height and weight are within the normal range for his/her age. The child has received the BCG vaccine at birth and has a visible scar at the injection site. The child has not been diagnosed with any illness or medical conditions. The child's parent/guardian has consented to the study and is willing to participate in the follow-up visits for up to 5 years. The child has no history of adverse reactions to vaccines or any other medical procedures. The child will undergo a tuberculin skin test to determine eligibility for the study, and if the PPD reaction is less than 15mm, the child will be randomized into either the revaccination group or the non-revaccination group. The child will be monitored for any adverse effects, including morbidity and mortality, during the study period. The study aims to examine whether revaccination with BCG reduces childhood mortality after 19 months of age by 30%.

A 31-year-old woman presents with a history of preterm labor at 32 weeks of gestation. She gave birth to a male infant weighing 2200 grams at the secondary hospital of Aga Khan University Hospital. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress and low birth weight. The infant's mother had a normal prenatal course with no significant medical or obstetrical history. The mother is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent. The infant has no congenital abnormalities or brain hemorrhage. The mother is not suffering from severe depression, sickness with intensive care requirements, or any other condition that would exclude her from participating in the study.

This is a 65 year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent a prostatectomy but recurrence was noted with metastasis to the bones. He underwent chemotherapy with docetaxel but due to adverse effects such as neuropathy, he was switched to cabazitaxel. Despite the change in chemotherapy, there was no significant improvement in his condition. He is now experiencing worsening pain in his bones and has difficulty with ambulation. His PSA level has continued to rise despite treatment. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

A 24-year-old woman has been experiencing obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) symptoms for the past 5 years. She has persistent, intrusive thoughts that cause anxiety and compulsive behaviors that temporarily relieve the anxiety. She has tried several medications in the past, but has not achieved remission. She is currently on clomipramine, but her symptoms have only partially improved. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. She is physically healthy, not currently pregnant, and able to provide informed consent. She has no history of schizophrenia, violence, severe depression, eating disorders, or substance abuse. She is not enrolled in cognitive-behavioral therapy at this time. She is willing to undergo a medication washout if necessary to participate in the trial.

A 64-year-old male smoker presents with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a family history of lung cancer. He has been smoking a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has never been diagnosed with lung cancer but is concerned about his risk due to his smoking history and family history. His physical examination is significant for decreased breath sounds and wheezing on lung auscultation. A chest X-ray is negative for any masses or nodules. The patient has been advised to participate in this clinical trial to help with early detection of lung cancer.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has a history of unprotected sexual intercourse with multiple partners in the past year. He had a negative ELISA test initially, but a confirmatory Western blot test was positive. His viral load is >10,000 copies/mL by RT-PCR. He is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. He has never received any antiretroviral therapy before. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo leukapheresis at baseline and at months 6 and 12 after initiating antiretroviral therapy. He understands the risks and benefits of the study, and is willing to make follow-up visits to the clinic. He is not pregnant.

Maria is a 68-year-old woman who recently suffered an ischemic stroke about 2 weeks ago. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking medications for these conditions, including metformin and lisinopril. Upon admission to the hospital, she was found to have an elevated blood glucose level of 220 mg/dL, which was subsequently managed with insulin therapy. Her neurological exam showed mild right-sided weakness and slurred speech, with a score of 3 on the Glasgow Outcome Scale. Imaging studies revealed a small embolic infarct in the left middle cerebral artery territory. Maria is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would help prevent future strokes.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. She has a history of malnutrition due to limited access to nutritious food and lack of knowledge about proper nutrition during pregnancy. She is currently underweight, with a BMI of 18.5, and has experienced nausea and vomiting throughout her pregnancy, which has further impacted her ability to consume adequate amounts of food. Despite her best efforts, she struggles to maintain a healthy and balanced diet. The patient has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. This is her first pregnancy, and she is eager to learn more about how proper nutrition can impact the health of her baby. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her microbiome and pregnancy outcomes.

Patient A is a 32-year-old female who has been struggling with infertility for the past year. She has been diagnosed with an autoimmune disease and is currently undergoing fertility treatment. She has no history of abnormal FSH levels, antral follicle counts, genital infections, endometriosis, tubal occlusion, or polycystic ovarian syndrome. She is fluent in the language used in the study and is willing to provide endometrial tissue and blood samples for cytokine profiling. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study group and is eager to participate in the study to help advance knowledge in this area.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obesity presents to the clinic complaining of fatigue, shortness of breath, and difficulty with exertion. His weight is 110 kg, and his height is 5'9". His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, and his heart rate is 88 bpm. His laboratory results show elevated triglycerides of 200 mg/dL and low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) of 30 mg/dL. He is diagnosed with Metabolic Syndrome and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of LaFlavon in lowering triglycerides and raising HDL. The patient is willing to take the study nutritional supplement once a day for three months. He denies any allergies to milk, soy, or whey.

The patient is a 10 year-old child who is overweight and meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. The child has a BMI above the 85th percentile for their age and gender and often eats in the absence of hunger. The child does not have any major psychiatric disorders and is not taking medication that can affect cognitive functioning. The child's parent is willing to participate in the study and attend all meetings and can read at least at a 5th grade level in English. The family does not have any restrictions on the types of food due to allergies or religious or ethnic practices. The child does not have an active eating disorder and the parent does not have any major psychiatric or eating disorder. The family resides in the San Diego community and is willing to commit to attending all treatment sessions and assessments.

35F healthy female with no known medical conditions, living in the United States and interested in participating in vaccine trials. She has not been vaccinated against H5 influenza or "bird flu" in the past. She is willing to undergo blood draws, physical exams, and medical history reviews as part of the study. She understands and signs the consent form for the study and meets all pre-screening qualifications for the DMID study. She is eligible for the main monovalent subvirion H5 vaccine trials (DMID studies 04-063 and 04-076) and has agreed to the extra blood draws for the cell-mediated immunity (CMI) sub-study. She has no known allergies to vaccines and is not currently taking any medications that may interfere with the study outcome.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who lives in a filariasis-endemic area and has been diagnosed with lymphedema in her right leg. She has been enrolled in the lymphedema treatment program at the Ste. Croix Hospital in Leogane, Haiti, and has received training in self-care techniques. She experiences frequent acute bacterial infections in her leg, which significantly affect her physical health and quality of life. She is seeking a treatment that can prevent these infections and improve her condition. She lives within a 10-km radius of the hospital and is able to adhere to the treatment protocol, particularly hygiene. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves the use of antibacterial soap to determine its effectiveness in reducing the incidence of acute bacterial infections in patients with filarial lymphedema.

This clinical trial does not involve individual patients and instead focuses on evaluating the impact of an antimicrobial stewardship program in nursing homes. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable in this case.

33-year-old male diagnosed with hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) due to bi-allelic mutations in CSF2RA. Patient has experienced persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue for the past year, with worsening symptoms over the past 3 months. Patient has not responded to conventional therapy for PAP including whole lung lavage and corticosteroids. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of asthma or other reactive airways diseases. The patient is willing and able to give written informed consent to participate in the trial.

10-year-old boy diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 3 months ago. He has already undergone induction chemotherapy and 2 cycles of consolidation chemotherapy, but his disease is refractory to conventional therapy. He has an ECOG performance status of 90%. He has a WBC count of 25,000/mm^3 and platelet count of 40,000/mm^3. He has no history of seizures or CNS toxicity. His liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. He has not received any biologic agents in the past week and has not undergone any radiotherapy in the past 6 weeks. He is not currently on any medications that induce cytidine deaminase or deoxycytidine kinase. The patient and his parents have been informed of the risks and benefits of the study and have provided written informed consent.

56-year-old female diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension and diabetes mellitus. She has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years and is now being evaluated for kidney transplantation. The patient has a history of hypertension for which she takes lisinopril 20mg daily and amlodipine 5mg daily, and diabetes mellitus for which she takes metformin 1000mg twice daily and insulin glargine 40 units at bedtime. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her current BMI is 31. She has no history of previous transplantation, and her panel reactive antibodies (PRA) are less than 20% of IgG anti-T. Her crossmatch T in cytotoxicity and / or flow cytometry is negative, and she has no active infections or diarrhea. She has a negative pregnancy test and is willing to use effective contraception throughout the study and 6 weeks after the end of the study. She has no known allergies or intolerances to tacrolimus, macrolide, corticosteroids, or mycophenolate mofetil. She has no history of de novo malignancy prior to transplantation, and she is not currently participating in another clinical study. She is able to understand and communicate with the investigator and his representatives and is willing to give her signed informed consent form.

Patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia based on DSM-IV-TR criteria. He has a history of chronic negative symptoms and cognitive deficits that have greatly affected his social functioning and quality of life. He has been on stable medication for the past four weeks and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve his symptoms. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse within the last month or the criteria for DSM-IV TR alcohol or substance dependence within the last 6 months. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use adequate contraception for the duration of the study. The patient is able to take oral medication and is likely to complete the required evaluations. He has no relevant ICD 10 organic brain disease or neurological diagnoses and is not planning to relocate in the next 12 months. The patient is fully informed and willing to give informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) by polysomnography (PSG). He has been prescribed continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy to manage his OSA. However, he has difficulty adhering to the treatment schedule and often removes the mask during sleep. He complains of loud snoring, choking or gasping during sleep, and abnormal daytime sleepiness. He has no history of substance abuse but has been diagnosed with mild depression. The patient is currently taking an antidepressant medication and has not had any changes to his medication in the past three months. He has no past treatment for OSA. The patient's sleep physician believes he would respond well to CPAP therapy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his adherence to CPAP therapy.

A 40-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic constipation for more than 3 months. She reports having less than 3 bowel movements per week and has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating. She has tried increasing her fiber intake but has not seen much improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates a new product for constipation. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or complications. She has not had any abdominal surgeries except for an appendectomy. She does not have any neurologic diseases or chronic illnesses that would affect gut motility. She is not currently taking any medication that may impact gut motility. She is able to understand the study instructions and has access to a smartphone device to complete the study e-Diary. She has not participated in any other constipation trials in the past year and is physically and mentally fit to participate in the trial.

62-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer treated with radical prostatectomy three years ago. He is currently under surveillance with a rising PSA level of 4.5 ng/mL. He is asymptomatic with no history of metastasis, no bone pain, weight loss, or any other symptoms. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled on medications. He has no allergies to medications or contrast agents. He has no history of renal or liver disease. He is a non-smoker and non-drinker. He is able to comply with study procedures and able to remain still for the duration of the imaging procedure. He is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been deaf in her left ear since birth. She received a cochlear implant in her right ear 2 years ago, which has greatly improved her ability to communicate and understand speech. However, she continues to struggle in noisy environments and when people speak to her from her left side. She has tried using a hearing aid in her left ear, but did not find it helpful. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new device, the Naída CROS, which may help her hear better from her left side. She has been using the Naída CI processor for over a year and is comfortable with its use. The patient reports no other medical problems and is proficient in French, the language of the study. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes it will improve her ability to communicate with others.

The patient is a 45-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with her-2 positive invasive ductal carcinoma in her left breast. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with a trastuzumab based regimen and had a lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy. The pathological review showed no evidence of residual disease in the tumor bed, and the tumor bed was no larger than 5 cm in size. The fibrotic area of the prior tumor was located at least 3mm away from surgical margins. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and wishes to be placed in Arm A to omit radiation therapy. The patient has no history of inflammatory breast cancer and has not been diagnosed with metastatic disease. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status between 50% to 100%. The patient will be recommended to complete a full year of trastuzumab therapy after surgery as standard of care under the clinical management of her medical oncologist.

The patient is a 35-year-old man with no systemic diseases and no history of dental treatment for his mandibular first molar with an asymptomatic periapical lesion. He reported no sensitivity to percussion and had no spontaneous pre-treatment pain. He is not currently taking any analgesics, antibiotics or corticosteroids. He is not allergic to NaOCl and has no intolerance to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The tooth can be isolated with rubber dam and is suitable for further restoration. The patient has no severe periodontal disease or root canal calcification or resorption. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the postoperative pain assessment protocol.

This clinical trial is not applicable for patients as it is a study focused on evaluating the effects of relaxation breathing coupled with biofeedback on the performance and stress of residents during high-fidelity simulation scenarios in medical training programs. Therefore, there are no specific patient characteristics required for this study.

56 year old male with a 10 year history of type 2 diabetes. He is currently on metformin and sulfonylurea but has been unable to achieve his glycemic target. His last A1C was 8.5%. He has no prior history of insulin use and has no known hepatic or renal dysfunction. He has mild gastrointestinal symptoms but no history of gastroparesis or other severe gastrointestinal diseases. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve his blood sugar control. He is compliant with his medication regimen and is willing to adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with low grade neuroendocrine carcinoma. The biopsy was taken from his small intestine. He has been experiencing diarrhea, flushing, and wheezing despite being treated with octreotide. His CT scan showed multiple liver metastases and he was advised that his cancer was unresectable. He has never received any chemotherapy treatment before. His performance status is 1 according to ECOG criteria. His lab results are within normal limits. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of atiprimod treatment.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who works as a software developer. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in any regular exercise routine. He has no history of any neuromuscular disorders, diabetes or prior injuries or surgeries of the back, neck, or limbs. He takes no medication other than occasional non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents for headache relief. He has no history of caffeine or nicotine use within 8 hours of testing. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as a volunteer for research purposes. He has no known allergies and has never undergone any nerve conduction studies before.

A 12-year-old boy with spastic cerebral palsy (GMFCS level III) is being considered for participation in this clinical trial. He has a history of difficulty with upper limb movements, including reaching and grasping, and experiences muscle stiffness and tightness. He has been receiving physical therapy for the past 3 years, which has helped to improve his motor function to some extent. The patient does not have any other underlying medical conditions, such as chromosomal abnormalities or cardiovascular disorders. He is able to understand and follow commands during an examination, and his parents have given their consent for him to participate in the trial. The patient is excited to try out new treatments that could help improve his upper limb functions and quality of life.

This is a 27 year-old female who is currently 8 weeks pregnant and has been taking prescription opioids for chronic pain management for the past 2 years. She has tried to stop using opioids during pregnancy but experiences severe withdrawal symptoms, which affects her ability to function and care for her other children. She has a history of depression and anxiety and struggles with negative emotions related to her chronic pain condition. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers an alternative to traditional opioid addiction treatment and may help her better manage her chronic pain during pregnancy.

A 67-year-old Caucasian man presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and cough for the past week. He reports that he has been feeling more fatigued than usual and has had difficulty breathing when lying down. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He quit smoking 10 years ago after smoking for about 30 years. He takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. His blood pressure is 148/92 mmHg, and his heart rate is 92 beats per minute. His respiratory rate is 24 breaths per minute, and his oxygen saturation on room air is 90%. Physical examination reveals elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral crackles on lung auscultation, and pedal edema. An echocardiogram shows preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF > 45%). He is diagnosed with acute heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFPEF) and is admitted to the hospital. He is asked to participate in a study examining the electrical and echocardiographic characteristics and prognosis of consecutive patients with HFPEF.

A 45-year-old non-smoking man with a non-restorable anterior tooth that requires extraction and future implant restoration. The patient has a treatment plan for ridge preservation and implant procedure at Tufts University School of Dental Medicine. The patient has good oral hygiene and no history of systemic diseases that affect bone metabolism. The patient has not undergone radiation therapy or chemotherapy and is not currently taking corticosteroids or bisphosphonates. The patient has no known allergies to research-related materials and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with polymyositis for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue, making it difficult for her to perform daily activities. She has undergone several clinical exams and muscle biopsies to confirm her diagnosis. She has been prescribed various medications to manage her symptoms, but she has not seen significant improvement. The patient is willing to participate in this registry to help physicians better understand the clinical outcomes of myositis patients treated with Acthar. She is capable of providing informed consent and complying with the treatment regimen. She has no history of scleroderma, osteoporosis, systemic fungal infections, ocular herpes simplex, or any other co-morbid condition that would make completion of the trial unlikely. She is not currently pregnant or breast-feeding and is willing to use appropriate birth control if of childbearing age.

The patient is a 32-year-old African American female who was recently diagnosed with cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) after presenting with a rash on her face, chest, and arms. She reports experiencing significant discomfort and embarrassment due to the visible nature of the rash. She has no family history of lupus or other autoimmune disorders. She avoids sun exposure as much as possible to avoid exacerbating her rash and has been using sun protection regularly. She reports no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about her vitamin D status and potential benefits of supplementation for her skin disease. Her 25(OH)D levels will be evaluated and if found to be less than 30 ng/ml, she may be eligible for the interventional arm of the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He has been taking L-dopa medication for the past 2 years, but has not been able to achieve adequate disease control. He reports experiencing tremors, stiffness, and difficulty with movement on a daily basis, which is affecting his ability to perform activities of daily living. He has not participated in any other clinical trials for Parkinson's disease and does not have any significant medical conditions other than his Parkinson's disease. He is willing to use a clinically accepted form of birth control if he is a woman of child-bearing potential.

This is a 45-year-old male with a history of recently diagnosed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He presented with complaints of fatigue, night sweats, and a 3-month history of painless lymph node enlargement in the neck, axilla, and groin. Biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of low-grade B-cell NHL, and he has not received any prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy. CT scans have confirmed measurable tumor size, and he has positive expression of CD20. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate renal, bone marrow, and liver function. He has completed a patient informed consent form and is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control to avoid pregnancy for the duration of the study and for at least 3 months thereafter. He meets the inclusion criteria for this study and he does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 10-year-old child with sickle cell anemia who has experienced three or more painful events in the past 2 years and required treatment with parenteral narcotics, equianalgesic dose of oral narcotics, or parenteral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The patient has also had two or more episodes of acute chest syndrome with a new infiltrate on chest radiograph and/or a perfusion defect demonstrable on a lung radioisotope scan. The patient has abnormal cerebral MRI and MRA and has experienced a clinically significant neurologic event lasting more than 24 hours. The patient has been diagnosed with beta thalassemia major and requires eight or more red blood cell transfusions a year and iron chelation therapy. The patient has adequate physical function with left ventricular ejection fraction at rest greater than 40% and improving with exercise, and shortening fraction greater than 26%. The patient's serum creatinine is within the normal range for age.

This is a 62-year-old Caucasian male who has a history of extensive sun exposure due to his occupation as a farmer. He has noticed several rough, scaly patches on his face and scalp, as well as his arms. He has been previously diagnosed with actinic keratosis (AK). He has tried cryotherapy for these lesions in the past, but they have not responded well. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new gel medication called LEO 43204. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial as he has at least 15 clinically typical, visible, and discrete AKs on his face, scalp, and arms within a contiguous area of approximately 250 cm2 of sun-damaged skin. He is willing to shave his face if needed for the trial. He is a non-smoker and is not taking any medications that would interfere with the trial. He understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman with a BMI of 38 kg/m2 who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past 2 years. The pain has been affecting her daily activities, including her job as a nurse, and has been worsening over time. She has been diagnosed with degenerative disc disease and spinal stenosis, and her surgeon has recommended posterior lumbar fusion surgery with or without interbody fusion. The patient has no prior history of lumbar spine surgery and is able to provide informed consent. She has been informed of the risks associated with the surgery, including the risk of wound complications due to her obesity. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and will be randomized to either receive standard of care or Closed-Incision Negative-Pressure Therapy (CINPT) to decrease post-operative wound complications. She will receive standard pre-operative prophylactic antibiotics and will be prepped with alcohol and either duraprep, chloraprep, or betadine. After the procedure is complete, a subfascial and subcutaneous closed suction drain will be placed in the wound prior to closure. In the CINPT group, a CINPT dressing will be placed and attached to a compact portable negative pressure unit to deliver 125mmHg continuous pressure for 5 to 7 days. The patient will receive standard wound care instructions before hospital discharge and will return to the clinic in 6±1 days for a wound check and removal of the CINPT. The primary endpoint for this trial is the occurrence of a wound complication, which may include a local inflammatory reaction, wound dehiscence, skin blistering/necrosis, stitch abscess or Incision and drainage for hematoma seroma, deep or superficial infection.

57 year old man diagnosed with Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) in the left lobe of the liver. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and hepatitis B. He has undergone previous liver surgery for a benign lesion in the right lobe of the liver. The patient's KPS score is 80 and his liver function is classified as Child-Pugh A. The tumor has been staged as AJCC stage II. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is willing to sign the informed consent form and is able to comply with the follow-up requirements of the trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl enrolled in a public middle school in Baltimore City. She complains of feeling overwhelmed and stressed on a daily basis due to the high-pressure academic environment and the constant exposure to violence and crime in her neighborhood. She reports difficulty sleeping, frequent headaches, and feeling irritable and anxious. She has no history of mental health problems or substance use. Her parents are supportive and concerned about her wellbeing and have agreed to have her participate in a 12-week school-based program that teaches mindfulness-based stress-reduction techniques.

The patient is a Japanese man or woman who is at least 55 years old and of first-order Japanese descent. The patient may have a clinical diagnosis of either amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) or probable Alzheimer's disease (pAD). For those with aMCI, the patient has an MMSE score of 27 to 30 (inclusive) and a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) of 0 to 0.5. For those with pAD, the patient meets National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke; Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association (NINCDS-ADRDA) criteria for clinical pAD and Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV]), 4th Edition, criteria for AD (DSM-IV criteria, American Psychiatric Association 1994). The patient must have a score of =< 4 on the Modified Hachinski Ischemic scale and an appropriate caregiver capable of accompanying them on all study visits if necessary and applicable according to local regulations. They should have an MRI image as part of the screening visit consistent with the diagnosis of aMCI or pAD and of sufficient diagnostic quality for volume of interest (VOI) definition and partial volume correction. The patient must not have any significant neurological or psychiatric disorder other than pAD that may have affected cognition, or a previous history of clinically evident stroke or significant cerebrovascular disease on brain imaging. Finally, the patient must not have participated in a clinical trial using an investigational medicinal product (IMP) within 30 days of dosing.

An 68-year-old woman visits the clinic with a chief complaint of feeling sad, hopeless, and fatigued for the past month. She reports difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in her hobbies. She denies any suicidal thoughts, but admits to feeling like a burden to her family. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence, and no history of manic episodes, psychotic disorders, or bipolar disorder. She is not currently taking any medications or undergoing any psychotherapy. She has a Mini Mental State Examination score of 28, indicating no cognitive impairment. She meets the criteria for major depressive disorder based on the DSM-IV, with a baseline HAM-D17 score of 18. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of DVS-233 SR for the treatment of depression in elderly outpatients.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy and was prescribed tamoxifen. After two years of treatment, she developed metastases in the liver and bones. She is currently undergoing treatment with fulvestrant and has received two lines of chemotherapy. The patient is postmenopausal and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has no history of cardiac or gastrointestinal disorders, and her organ function is adequate. The patient has not received prior treatment with GDC-0810 and has not undergone any major surgery or radiation therapy in the past 2 weeks. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with type 2 diabetes. He has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 10 years and has been experiencing proteinuria with albumin levels of 200 mg/24h for the past year. His HbA1c is 8.5% and he is currently on metformin and insulin therapy. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no history of chronic end-stage renal disease or significant diseases other than diabetes. He does not abuse alcohol or drugs and has no history of HIV or hepatitis. The patient is fluent in Italian and able to understand the study protocol.

This is a 25 year old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential HIV drug called GSK1349572. He has no past medical history and is not taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements. He does not consume alcohol, tobacco or nicotine-containing products. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5 kg/m2. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form. He has no pre-existing conditions that interfere with normal gastrointestinal anatomy or motility, hepatic and/or renal function. He is not pregnant or lactating. He does not have a history of cholecystectomy, significant cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic diseases. He has a normal blood pressure and heart rate. He is eligible to participate in the study and is willing to use one of the contraception methods listed in Section 8.1 during the study period.

27-year-old Somali refugee seeking treatment for symptoms of PTSD and khat addiction. The patient has been living in a refugee camp in Kenya for the past five years and has experienced multiple traumatic events, including witnessing the murder of family members and living through a terrorist attack. The patient reports using khat as a coping mechanism for the symptoms of PTSD, including flashbacks, nightmares, and anxiety. The patient has attempted to quit using khat in the past but has been unsuccessful. The patient speaks Somali as their primary language and has limited English proficiency. The patient has no history of severe psychotic disorder or suicidality, but reports occasional depressive symptoms. The patient is willing to participate in psychotherapeutic treatment to address their PTSD and khat addiction.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been having trouble sleeping for the past year. She often wakes up in the middle of the night and has difficulty falling back asleep. She has tried various sleep aids and relaxation techniques, but nothing seems to work. She reports feeling anxious and stressed most of the time and has been diagnosed with mild depression. She works as a graphic designer and spends a lot of time sitting at her desk. She is generally healthy, with no known medical conditions, but admits to drinking two cups of coffee per day. Her BMI is 22, and her blood pressure is 115/75 mmHg. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the PS128 supplement can help her improve her sleep quality and reduce her anxiety and depressive symptoms. She has not taken any probiotic products or sleep medications in the last two months.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m². He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His fasting plasma glucose level is 5.5 mmol/l and his glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) level is 38 mmol/mol. He has normal haemoglobin levels (9.5 mmol/l). He has no first-degree relatives with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. He has no history of nephropathy, liver disease, or active or recent malignant disease. The patient has provided informed and written consent to participate in the study.

47 year-old female diagnosed with stage II breast cancer with no known metastasis. She recently started receiving anthracycline-containing chemotherapy as part of her treatment regimen. She has no significant medical history, but reports occasional headaches and mild hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has not had any previous heart-related issues or procedures. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the cardioprotective effects of ketotifen in patients receiving anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. She meets all eligibility criteria and is randomized to the Ketotifen Group. She will be taking one tablet of ketotifen (1 mg/tablet) orally three times daily, before and during the chemotherapeutic cycle for 6 cycles of treatment. Blood samples will be obtained, and echocardiography will be performed at baseline and after 6 months to evaluate the prophylactic effect of ketotifen against cardiotoxicity induced by anthracycline therapy.

32-year-old female with a diagnosis of stable moderate to severe asthma for the past 5 years. She has not had any asthma exacerbations in the past 6 months and her lung function tests (FEV1 and PEF) are within the range of 60% to 80% of predicted values. She has no history of smoking and does not have any cardiopulmonary diseases. The patient is able to understand verbal commands and has consented to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and does not have any contraindications for the use of noninvasive ventilation.

Patient is a preterm infant born at 30 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1200 grams. The infant is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit and is scheduled for a retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) examination. The infant is on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) with an FiO2 of 30%. The infant has not had any significant medical complications and is tolerating feeds well. The parents have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis five years ago. She has been taking methotrexate (20 mg/week) for the past three years, but it is no longer controlling her symptoms effectively. She has persistent swelling, tenderness, and stiffness in her joints, particularly in her hands and feet. She has been experiencing fatigue and difficulty doing everyday tasks. She has not received etanercept therapy before and is interested in participating in the CAMEO study to evaluate the efficacy of this treatment option. She is not pregnant and has been using adequate contraception for the past year. She has no history of tuberculosis, HIV infection, multiple sclerosis, congestive heart failure, hepatitis B or C, cytopenia, prior or current use of cyclophosphamide, or malignancy. She is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up assessments.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension, currently on lisinopril. He works as an office manager and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies and takes no other medications. His family history is positive for hypertension (father and maternal uncle). He has no history of cardiac arrhythmias, pacemaker, or implanted metal devices. He has not undergone any recent surgeries. He has no skin breaches or sensitivity to adhesives. He has not had axillary node dissection. His limb size circumference is 20 cm. He is willing to wear the Investigational Device (ID) for 24 hours and participate in the clinical investigation to validate the performance and safety of the device for measuring blood pressure.

35 yo female with a history of GERD and heartburn for the past 10 years. She has been taking PPI's for the past 4 weeks and reports improvement in her heartburn symptoms, but she continues to experience mid-upper abdominal discomfort characterized by postprandial fullness, early satiety, and bloating. She reports that these symptoms are bothersome and impacting her quality of life. She denies any history of intestinal obstruction, symptomatic gallbladder disease, or abdominal adhesions. She reports that her dyspeptic symptoms are not relieved by defecation and are not associated with a change in frequency or stool form. She is interested in participating in the study to assess the safety and efficacy of tegaserod use in patients with dyspepsia who are being treated with PPI's for heartburn. Past Medical History: - GERD - Heartburn - Anxiety - Depression - Migraines - Asthma - Allergic Rhinitis

A 25-year-old male patient was brought into the emergency department after a motorcycle accident. He has severe pain in his right ankle and foot with a visual analog scale (VAS) score of 80mm. He has no known allergies and is not on any chronic medications. He denies any history of drug addiction or pregnancy. His vital signs at presentation include a systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg, respiratory rate of 20 per minute, and Glasgow coma scale of 15. His right leg is swollen and tender to palpation. Plain radiographs reveal a displaced fracture of the distal fibula and a comminuted fracture of the calcaneus. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets the inclusion criteria for severe pain and leg, ankle or foot injury. There is no evidence of local infection, nerve or vascular pathology, or coagulation disorder. He has not used opioids within the past 6 hours.

The patient is a 30-year-old Native American woman living on the Cheyenne River Sioux Indian Reservation in South Dakota. She has a history of high-risk drinking behavior, consuming an average of 9 drinks per week and episodes of binge drinking at least once a month in the past 90 days. She is sexually active with a male partner and not currently using effective contraception. She is not currently pregnant and is able to become pregnant. Her past medical history is non-significant for infertility or any other chronic medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the Native CHOICES study and attend 2 motivational interviewing sessions plus 1 contraceptive counseling session over 4 weeks, with supportive electronic messaging for 3 months to modify her drinking behavior and increase contraception effectiveness. She does not live in a household with anyone who is already enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 48-year-old Hispanic woman presenting with a history of diabetes for 5 years. She has been managing her diabetes with diet and exercise alone, but her recent HbA1c levels have been between 7.5% and 10.0%, indicating poor glycemic control. Her BMI is 29 kg/m^2, and she has a fasting C-peptide concentration of 1.2 ng/mL. She is not taking any antidiabetic medication and has not received any investigational drug in the past 90 days. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. She is not currently taking any excluded medications and has no history of hypersensitivity or allergy to alogliptin, other DPP-4 inhibitors, metformin or related compounds. She has not undergone any gastric surgeries for diabetic gastric paresis, gastric banding or gastric bypass surgery. She is willing to monitor her own blood glucose concentrations with a home glucose monitor and complete patient diaries throughout the study. She is a sexually active female and agrees to routinely use adequate contraception from Screening throughout the duration of the study. She meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was previously diagnosed with multiple myeloma and has undergone 2 lines of therapy. He has been experiencing a relapse of the disease, with worsening symptoms of bone pain, fatigue, and anemia. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1 and he has measureable disease based on central laboratory assessment. His lab values are acceptable prior to starting study treatment. The patient has not previously received treatment with panobinostat or carfilzomib. He has not undergone an allogeneic stem cell transplant and does not have graft versus host disease. The patient is not receiving any other concomitant anti-cancer therapy, except for bisphosphonates which were commenced prior to the start of the screening period. The patient does not have any intolerance to dexamethasone or contraindication to carfilzomib or dexamethasone, and does not have unresolved diarrhea ≥ CTCAE grade 2 or a medical condition associated with chronic diarrhea.

Patient B is a full-term neonate with a prenatally diagnosed left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The infant was delivered by a planned C-section at 38 weeks gestation due to the prenatal diagnosis. On admission, the infant was intubated and mechanically ventilated. The chest x-ray showed a left-sided diaphragmatic defect with herniation of bowel and liver into the left chest. Echocardiogram revealed no structural heart disease but showed evidence of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN). On the most recent blood gas sample, arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) was 45 mmHg, arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) was 45 mmHg, and oxygenation index (OI) was 20. The infant is currently receiving inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) for PPHN. The infant's birth weight was 3000g, and the postnatal age is 3 days. The infant meets all eligibility criteria for the study, and there are no exclusion criteria present. The parents have given informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who presented to the emergency room with a severe headache and blurred vision. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which has been poorly controlled despite taking medication. He reports occasional alcohol use and is a current smoker. His blood pressure at the time of presentation was 180/110 mmHg. He was diagnosed with hypertensive urgency and was enrolled in the study. The patient's baseline characteristics include a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2, a systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 180 mmHg, and a diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of 110 mmHg. He has no history of kidney disease, diabetes, or cardiovascular disease. The appropriate cuff size was used to measure his BP, and three readings were taken at 30-second intervals with the patient in a sitting position after five minutes of rest. The average of three BP measurements was used for analysis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

A 35-year-old man suffered a traumatic brain injury 9 months ago as a result of a motor vehicle accident. He has experienced difficulty with balance, coordination, and gait since the injury. He has not received outpatient therapy in the past month but has tried various treatments including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy. He weighs 80 kgs and is medically stable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at improving his functional ability and is available for intensive rehabilitation robotic gait training.

The patient is a 28-week-old male neonate who was born prematurely weighing 2.3 pounds. He was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress syndrome and was started on nasal CPAP on a fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) of 0.25. He has been receiving CPAP for 72 hours and his respiratory status is stable. His parents have given their consent for him to participate in the study. He has no known congenital anomalies or genetic/chromosomal abnormalities. He has not undergone any surgeries and has no neurologic abnormalities. His medical history is significant for a 3-day course of antibiotics for suspected sepsis, which was later ruled out. He is being fed via a nasogastric tube and has been tolerating feeds well.

55 year old female, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 3 months ago after presenting with increased thirst, frequent urination, and blurred vision. She has a past medical history of hypertension and is currently on lisinopril. Her HbA1c level was 8.6% at the time of diagnosis. She denies any micro- or macroangiopathy such as nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, or peripheral vascular disease. She is not on any medications for these conditions. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is compliant with her diabetic diet and exercise regimen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between plasma irisin level and endothelial dysfunction in type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently had a routine blood test that showed she has high cholesterol levels. She has a family history of heart disease, as her mother had a heart attack at age 60. The patient exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet, but her cholesterol levels have remained elevated. She has no history of liver disease or any other medical conditions. She is currently taking no medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help find a more effective treatment for her high cholesterol levels.

The patient is a 6-year-old child who recently completed treatment for an acute infection at an outpatient clinic in Turkey. The child has no history of primary or secondary immunosuppressive states and has never had abdominal or gastrointestinal tract surgery. The child has not used probiotics or prebiotics in the last month or antibiotics in the last month. The child is not experiencing any accompanying gastrointestinal symptoms and is not currently using anti-acid medication. The child's parents have provided consent for the child to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past 2 years. His most recent blood pressure reading was 140/90 mmHg. He has never experienced any major cardiovascular events, but has a family history of heart disease. He is a retired accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. His lab results are as follows: HbA1c: 7.2%, total cholesterol: 200 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol: 120 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol: 50 mg/dL, triglycerides: 150 mg/dL, creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL, and estimated GFR: 50 mL/min/1.73m². He meets the eligibility criteria for the OPTIMAL-DIABETES trial as his SBP is between 130 and 180 mm Hg and he has a high cardiovascular risk due to his diabetes and hypertension. He has no exclusion criteria and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 27 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD) after seeking help for her emotional instability and difficulty maintaining relationships. She has a history of self-harm and suicidal ideation, and has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to suicidal attempts. She is currently receiving psychotherapy and taking medication for her symptoms. She reports experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations, which she has been reluctant to disclose to her therapist due to fear of being labeled as "crazy". She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand her symptoms and potentially receive more targeted treatment. She is fluent in French and able to read and write in the language. She does not have any history of head trauma, stroke, Parkinson's disease, dementia or autism. She is not currently incarcerated and is able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 58-year-old woman was diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis (OA) 2 years ago. She has been struggling with her weight for many years and has a body mass index (BMI) of 33. She was enrolled in the CAROT study (NCT00655941) a year ago, where she received group therapy with a low-energy diet. During the study, she lost 10% of her initial body weight and reported significant improvement in her knee OA symptoms. She is now eligible for the Long-term Intervention with Weight Loss in Patients with Concomitant Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis (LIGHT) study, which aims to maintain the weight loss achieved during the CAROT study through a continuation of the dietary intervention. She is willing to participate in the study and is looking forward to continuing her weight loss journey to improve her knee OA symptoms even further.

A 35-year-old Japanese male with a BMI of 22.1 kg/m2 presents for a Phase 1 clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetic bioequivalence of DMB-3113 and adalimumab. He has no significant medical history and does not currently take any medications. He underwent a screening test within the last 4 weeks and had no clinically abnormal findings. He has no history of tuberculosis, demyelinating disease, congestive cardiac failure or any known allergies. His cardiac, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and hematological function are all normal. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and comply with all study procedures.

52 yo F with a history of chronic hepatitis B and mild cirrhosis presents for screening for a clinical trial evaluating the safety and pharmacokinetics of MEK162. She is currently on antiviral therapy and has not had any recent episodes of hepatic decompensation. Her most recent liver function tests showed an elevated total bilirubin level of 2.5 mg/dL, which is above the upper limit of normal. Her ALT, AST, GGT, and alkaline phosphatase levels are all within normal limits. She denies any symptoms of encephalopathy or ascites. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. Her creatinine clearance is 90 mL/min, and her serum creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL. She has not used tobacco or consumed alcohol within the past 7 days. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to be confined to the facility for 5 days for monitoring.

A 45-year-old woman visited the gastroenterologist with a history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain and bloating for the past year. The pain is intermittent, but she notes that it is more severe after eating fried and fatty foods. She has no nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, well-managed with medication, and is a non-smoker. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has a BMI of 28. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen without rebound or guarding. There are no palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory tests are normal except for a slight elevation in bilirubin levels. An abdominal ultrasound shows multiple gallstones with no evidence of choledocholithiasis. The patient is diagnosed with cholecystolithiasis and is offered the option of laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial and is randomized to receive either single port transumbilical approach or three-trocar laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

The patient is a 64-year-old former smoker with a 35 pack-year history of smoking. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has not used inhaled corticosteroids before. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. She does not have a history of lung cancer or asthma. She has no known allergies and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use the study drug twice daily regularly and undergo a bronchoscopy. She has not donated blood recently and does not have any planned hospitalization or travel that would preclude her from participating in the study.

54-year-old male resident of northern Taiwan diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) in 2013. Histologically confirmed incident case of NPC with no prior history of cancer. The patient is a non-smoker and does not chew betel nut. The patient has a history of consuming salted fish and other nitrosamine containing preserved foods. The patient has been exposed to formaldehyde and wood dust in his occupation as a furniture maker. The patient has not undergone any treatment for NPC as part of this protocol. The patient is willing to participate in a risk factor interview and provide biological samples for the study.

A 32-year-old female is diagnosed with major depressive disorder and has a baseline HAM-D score of 18. She has never used any nicotine products and reports fewer than 10 lifetime uses of nicotine. She is not currently taking any psychotropic medication and has not taken any in the past 2 weeks. She has no history of substance abuse or cardiac problems, and her blood pressure is within normal range. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 200 mg of caffeine per day. She speaks English fluently and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old male with severe congenital protein C deficiency presents at the hospital with symptoms of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his left leg. His medical history includes multiple episodes of DVT in the past, for which he has received anticoagulation therapy. Upon examination, a DVT is confirmed by ultrasound, and the patient is started on anticoagulant therapy. However, due to his severe congenital protein C deficiency, the treating physician decides to treat the patient with protein C concentrate under an Emergency Use Investigational New Drug Application (IND). The patient or his legally authorized representative has provided written informed consent. The patient will be followed up for dosing and treatment outcome data as part of a data collection study.

54-year-old male with a history of stroke and left-sided hemiparesis, referred for swallowing assessment at the Forcilles' Hospital due to suspected dysphagia. The patient reports difficulty in swallowing both liquids and solids, and occasional coughing or choking episodes during meals. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is on multiple medications, including aspirin, statins, and antihypertensive agents. He is a non-smoker and reports occasional alcohol use. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provides oral consent. The patient is not pregnant, does not have a cognitive disorder that would prevent him from understanding instructions, and is not under guardianship or curatorship. The patient has not undergone previous laryngectomy surgery and is not subject to judicial health protection.

56 yo F with multiple missing teeth and significant bone loss in the mandible. Patient reports multiple failed attempts at denture use and is interested in dental implants. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Osteopenia - No history of smoking or alcohol use. The patient has read, understood, and signed the Form for Patient Information and the Informed Consent. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements, including follow-up visits and data collection. The patient is not currently experiencing any untreated systemic disease and is cleared for implant surgery. The patient is a good candidate for dental implant surgery and is interested in participating in the study.

A 45-year-old male worker in a quarry comes to the clinic with a persistent cough, weight loss, and a history of tuberculosis treatment 5 years ago. The chest X-ray shows fibrotic changes in both upper lobes. Sputum test for acid-fast bacilli is negative, but a chest CT shows small nodules in both lungs. A diagnosis of silicosis is made based on his occupational history and imaging findings. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial for TB prevention. He has no known allergies to the study drugs and has not taken any rifamycin or INH in the past 2 years. His liver function tests and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He is not infected with HIV and has no history of hepatitis B/C or liver cirrhosis. He has never received immunosuppressants or biological agents.

Patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been wearing complete dentures for the past 6 months due to the loss of all her teeth. She reports good general health with no significant medical history. Intraoral examination reveals a satisfactory condition of the edentulous high ridge, classified as Atwood's Class I. The patient reports no signs or symptoms of temporomandibular dysfunction. She is able to chew and swallow without difficulty but is interested in exploring options for improving her masticatory efficiency with her complete dentures.

The patient is an 11-year-old Hispanic girl who lives with her mother in a low-income neighborhood. The girl is currently enrolled in the sixth grade, attends school regularly, and has no history of substance use. The mother is a single parent who works full-time as a housekeeper and has limited education. The mother is concerned about her daughter's future and wants to learn how to prevent her daughter from using drugs. The girl and her mother have a good relationship, but they struggle to communicate effectively. The girl has expressed interest in participating in extracurricular activities at school, but her mother cannot afford to pay for them. The girl has a history of low self-esteem and has expressed concerns about her body image. The girl and her mother have access to a private computer and are willing to participate in a family-based intervention to prevent substance use.

25-year-old female with no prior history of ear surgery or TM condition, presenting with mild hearing loss in her left ear. The patient has no known sensitivity or allergic reactions to lidocaine HCl, tetracaine, epinephrine, or any local anesthetics of the amide type. She has never had an ear iontophoresis procedure before and does not have any conductive hearing loss or history of familial insensitivity to local anesthetics. The patient's tympanic membrane is intact, and she does not have significantly atrophic, retracted, bimeric, monomeric or atelectatic tympanic membrane. She does not have perforated tympanic membrane, otitis externa, or damaged/denuded skin in the auditory canal. The patient is able to read and understand English and is willing to comply with the protocol and attend all study visits. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any health conditions that would present undue risk to the subject.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is generally healthy and not taking any medications. She has no history of neuromuscular disease, epilepsy, or cardiovascular disease. She has never had any traumas or surgeries affecting her upper limb, shoulder girdle or cervical area, and she has no osteosynthesis material in her upper limb. She does not have diabetes or cancer. She does not have any tattoos or other external agents introduced to the treatment or assessment area. She is not pregnant. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical knowledge and is willing to undergo the necessary procedures and assessments.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 42 kg/m². She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes that is poorly controlled with medication. She has tried various diets and exercise programs to lose weight, but has been unable to achieve significant weight loss. She is interested in undergoing laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery as a means of achieving long-term weight loss and improving her overall health. She has no history of bariatric surgery and is not currently pregnant. She is able to comply with the study protocol and proposed follow-up visits. She has read and signed the informed consent form.

This trial is looking for healthy individuals to participate in a study comparing the effectiveness of acupuncture and modulated electroanalgesia in managing cold-induced pain. Therefore, patients with any history of disease or medical conditions will not be eligible to participate in this study. If you are a healthy individual interested in exploring non-pharmacological methods of pain management, this might be the right clinical trial for you.

The patient is a premature infant, born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1.3 kg. The infant has been diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) based on symptoms such as vomiting, regurgitation, and difficulty feeding. The infant has undergone a 24-hour intra-esophageal pH monitoring and multi-channel intraluminal impedance (MII) test, which confirmed the presence of GERD. The infant has also undergone an upper GI contrast radiograph to evaluate for associated congenital gastrointestinal anomalies, which showed no abnormalities. The infant is currently receiving medical therapy for GERD, but the symptoms persist. The infant is over 2 kg, making them eligible for anti-reflux surgery (fundoplication). There is no history of intra-abdominal surgery, and the infant is considered a surgical candidate. The infant is less than 1 year old at the time of the initial evaluation of GERD.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic with chronic low back pain that has been affecting his daily life for the past 2 years. He works as a construction worker and has a history of heavy lifting and repetitive bending. He has tried various non-operative therapies including physical therapy, chiropractic treatment, and medications, but none of them provided long-term relief. He has been diagnosed with degenerative disc disease (DDD) at the L4-L5 level on MRI and CT scan. He has no history of prior spine surgery, tumors, or traumatic injuries. He has never smoked and has no known allergies to titanium or cobalt chrome. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol, including follow-up visits and imaging. He is currently not involved in any spinal litigation and has no current mental or neuromuscular disorders that would interfere with the study. He has a BMI of 26 and no other significant medical history. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his back pain and regain his ability to work without discomfort.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with epilepsy at the age of 18. His seizures are uncontrolled despite trying multiple seizure medications. He experiences about two seizures per month, which usually last for 1-2 minutes and are followed by a postictal period of confusion and fatigue. He is currently under the care of a neurologist and is being monitored with video EEG. He is interested in participating in this study to help develop better tools for predicting and managing his seizures. He lives alone in a small apartment and is able to follow instructions and comply with the study requirements. He has no major psychiatric co-morbidities and does not have psychogenic non-epileptic seizures.

56 year old woman with a history of breast cancer and known bone metastases presents for evaluation of recent increase in bone pain. Her breast cancer was diagnosed 3 years ago and she underwent lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation. She was then started on endocrine therapy with tamoxifen. She was found to have bone metastases on a routine imaging study 6 months ago and was started on denosumab. On physical exam, there is tenderness over her thoracic spine and right hip. She reports the pain has been worsening over the past month and is now requiring increasing doses of analgesics. She is scheduled for a biopsy of her thoracic spine lesion next week. The patient is approached regarding participation in the study and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) for the past 2 years. She reports irregular menstrual cycles, excessive hair growth, and acne. She has tried various treatments for her symptoms, including birth control pills and topical creams, but has not seen significant improvement. She has a BMI of 27 and has been struggling with weight gain. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no significant medical history and is not using any medications. Her family history is negative for cardiovascular disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effects of inositol on some cardiovascular risk factors in PCOS patients.

This clinical trial does not involve living patients and instead involves post-mortem analysis of liver and bone tissue in individuals who have died of non-metabolic causes. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this trial.

A 54 year old female with a history of gastric cancer presents with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite. She has previously undergone a total gastrectomy with adjuvant chemotherapy. A recent CT scan showed diffuse infiltrating gastric lesions and retroperitoneal lymph node involvement, indicating disease progression. She has received one prior systemic treatment with cisplatin and capecitabine. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no evidence of brain metastases. Her liver, kidney, and hematologic function are adequate. She has no history of another primary malignancy within the past 3 years.

A 45-year-old man with a history of grade IV glioblastoma multiforme who has undergone surgical resection and radiation therapy but has experienced recurrence of the tumor. He is currently experiencing headaches, seizures, and cognitive decline. He is currently on a stable dose of anti-seizure medication and is able to swallow pills. He has recovered from toxicity of prior therapies and has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80%. He has no chronic or active viral infections of the central nervous system and is not allergic to 5-FC or 5-FU. He has no serious medical or psychiatric illness that would interfere with the completion of the treatment. He is willing to sign a written informed consent document and agrees to use an effective method of contraception while participating in the study as he is sexually active. He is not currently enrolled in another treatment clinical trial. His MRI shows evidence of recurrent supratentorial tumor(s) and he needs a craniotomy for tumor resection or a stereotactic brain biopsy for the purpose of diagnosis or differentiating between tumor progression versus treatment-induced effects following radiation therapy +/- chemotherapy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently underwent a breast biopsy and was diagnosed with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the left breast. The patient is currently considering treatment options and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help further research on DCIS. She has no history of breast cancer in her family, and she has never had any prior breast surgeries or treatments. The patient is in good health, with no significant medical history or chronic conditions. She does not smoke or use any recreational drugs, and only drinks alcohol occasionally. She is an active individual, who enjoys hiking and yoga regularly. She works full-time as a marketing manager for a small firm, and is married with two children. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to provide breast tissue samples for the study.

A 35-year-old woman with phototype III skin presents with brown spots (solar lentigo) on both hands, with a diameter of ≤ 6 mm. She has not undergone any aesthetic care on her hands, such as exfoliants, scrubs, or self-tanning, in the month prior to the study. She has not applied any depigmenting products on her hands in the last month. She has not undergone any aesthetic care at a dermatologist, such as laser, IPL, peeling, depigmenting creams, or cryotherapy, on her hands in the last 6

A 72-year-old female patient presented to the Prince Philip Dental Hospital for her routine dental check-up. She reported that she had received cobalt chromium metal framework removable partial dentures (RPDs) five years ago. The patient was in good health, with no history of systemic disease. She had no known allergies and was not taking any medications. The patient was a non-smoker and did not consume alcohol. She lived independently in her own home in the community. The patient was willing to participate in the study and met the inclusion criteria for the trial. She was randomized into one of the three groups for denture hygiene intervention. The patient was instructed to follow the prescribed denture cleaning regimen for one month and return for a follow-up evaluation.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or adrenal pathology. His performance status according to the WHO scale is 1. He has a family history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy. He has given informed consent to participate in this study.

Baby J is a 4-month-old infant who was diagnosed with a congenital heart disease (CHD) during routine prenatal screening. After birth, multiple diagnostic tests confirmed the presence of a ventricular septal defect (VSD) and pulmonary stenosis (PS). Baby J underwent cardiac surgery to repair the VSD and relieve the PS at Children's Mercy Kansas City. Post-surgery, Baby J has been experiencing hemodynamic changes and pain responses, which have been challenging for the medical team to manage. Baby J weighs 9 kg and has been in the hospital for 3 weeks. The parents are looking for ways to help their baby during this difficult time and are interested in exploring the use of the SNOO Smart Sleeper bassinet by Happiest Baby INC, which they have heard about from other parents. Baby J meets the eligibility criteria for the SSSH Study: SNOO Smart Sleeper Use in Post-Operative Infants with Congenital Heart Disease and the parents are willing to give parental permission for participation in the use of the SNOO.

The patient is a 65 year old African American male with a history of prostate cancer. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago and has been undergoing continuous treatment with orchiectomy. Despite the treatment, his PSA levels have been rising, indicating castrate-resistant disease. His current PSA level is 20 ng/mL. He has no evidence of metastatic disease on bone or CT scan. His serum testosterone level is <50ng/mL. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He is not on any immunosuppressive agents and has no evidence of immunosuppression. He has not discontinued LHRH agonist treatment within 6 months prior to study entry. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements with known hormonal effects. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his family and gardening. He is willing and able to undergo two leukapheresis procedures for the study.
