The patient is a 50-year-old man who works as a healthcare worker in the emergency department of Hospital Nacional Hipolito Unanue (HNHU) in Lima, Peru. He has been experiencing a persistent cough for the past few weeks and has a history of exposure to TB patients at his workplace. He is concerned about the potential risk of contracting TB and transmitting it to his family members. The patient has never been diagnosed with TB in the past and has no known allergies to medications. He is willing to participate in the study and provide a sputum sample and/or exhaled breath test sample for evaluation. The patient understands that the study aims to find and treat unsuspected and resistant TB cases to reduce transmission in the hospital setting. He hopes that his participation in the study will help improve TB infection control measures and protect healthcare workers and patients from the transmission of TB.

This is a 63-year-old woman who has been suffering from Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy for the past three years. She has been experiencing progressive vision loss, and her best corrected visual acuity has decreased to 20/200. She has been advised by her ophthalmologist to undergo corneal transplantation to improve her vision and quality of life. She has no other ocular comorbidities except for cataract. She has not undergone any previous corneal transplantations and is willing to complete the follow-up for the duration of the study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to determine the most effective and cost-effective corneal transplantation technique for patients with Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy.

65 year old female with a history of osteoarthritis and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). She is currently taking rabeprazole 20mg/day for her GERD symptoms and has been prescribed naproxen for her joint pain. She also takes a low dose of lorazepam for anxiety. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has never had any adverse reactions to medications in the past. She is compliant with her medication regimen and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety of rabeprazole in polymedicated patients to ensure that her current treatment plan is safe and effective.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. His biopsy results have confirmed that he has adenocarcinoma of the prostate. His PSA level is 35 ng/mL, and he has a Gleason score of 9. Digital rectal examination revealed a hard nodule in the right lobe of his prostate. He has not undergone any prior treatment for prostate cancer. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no evidence of metastatic disease or other malignancy. He has consented to participate in the study and is willing to provide biopsies as required. His baseline organ function is adequate with serum creatinine at 1.2 mg%, T. bilirubin at 1.8 mg%, ALT and AST levels within normal limits, platelet count at 150,000/mm3, ANC at 2000/mm, and Hemoglobin level at 11 gm%. He does not have a history of allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the components of the proposed regimen. He is able to swallow food and has no condition of the upper gastrointestinal tract that precludes administration of oral medications. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study but does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of advanced heart failure who has received implantation and VAD care at Northwestern Memorial Hospital (NMH). He is currently being cared for by his wife, who is his primary caregiver. The patient has struggled with managing his VAD device at home and has experienced several VAD-related infections and re-hospitalizations. He and his wife are both fluent in English and are interested in participating in a study that could improve their self-management skills and reduce the risk of future infections and hospitalizations. They are willing to undergo training using medical simulators as part of the study. The patient does not have any mental retardation or mental incompetence that would prevent him from giving informed consent.

This is a 52 year old male who presented with right-sided weakness and headache. Imaging revealed a mass in the left frontal lobe consistent with glioma. The patient underwent resection and was subsequently diagnosed with WHO grade III anaplastic astrocytoma. He completed radiation therapy and is currently on maintenance chemotherapy with temozolomide. The patient has no significant medical history other than hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. His current medications include amlodipine and lisinopril. His performance status is Karnofsky >= 80 and ECOG <=1. The patient has no history of diabetes, heart failure, or liver disease. His blood work is within normal limits, and he has no contraindications to MRI scanning.

An 68-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo an elective surgical procedure under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cerebrovascular disease and her Mini Mental status score is 28. Her preoperative laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient has given her informed consent to participate in the study. She will be monitored intraoperatively for cerebral perfusion and her blood will be tested for anticholinergic activity. Her cognitive function will be assessed preoperatively and at 1 week and 3 months postoperatively. She has no cardiac or neurosurgical history, and her medical history and medication lists have been reviewed to ensure eligibility for the study.

A 35-year-old male office worker presents with a complaint of low back pain that has been recurring for the past two years. He describes the pain as a dull ache that worsens with prolonged sitting and standing. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medications and stretching exercises, but the pain keeps coming back. He rates his pain as a 6 out of 10 on the visual analog scale (VAS). The patient has no history of trauma, fever, or weight loss. He has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. His physical exam reveals tenderness on palpation over the lumbar paraspinal muscles, but no neurological deficits. The patient has access to a mobile phone and knows how to send text messages. He speaks proficient Swedish and rates himself as "definitely improved" after the fourth visit. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effectiveness of chiropractic maintenance care for persistent or recurrent low back pain.

The patient is a 62-year-old Italian man who has been experiencing abdominal pain and loss of appetite for the past few months. He has also noticed that he has been losing weight rapidly. He has no history of pancreatic cancer in his family. The patient underwent diagnostic procedures such as CT scans and biopsy, and the results showed that he has pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The patient is now scheduled to have his first visit with the doctor to discuss the diagnosis and treatment options. He is fluent in Italian and able to read and write. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given full, written informed consent. The patient has an ECOG status of 1, meaning he is able to carry out light physical activities. He is a retired teacher and enjoys reading and spending time with his grandchildren.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is concerned about the health of her teeth. She works as a graphic designer and has no history of systemic diseases except for her controlled diabetes. She is a non-smoker and has no allergies to any drugs. She was referred to the clinic by her dentist due to the presence of Grade II furcation on her permanent first and second molars in the mandible. She has at least 2 millimetres probing depth horizontally and at least 5 millimetres probing depth circumferential. She is compliant with adequate oral hygiene protocols and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has not received any periodontal regenerative therapy within the past 12 months, is not lactating or pregnant, and has no tooth mobility greater than grade II. Her medical history is unremarkable except for her controlled diabetes. She is willing to comply with the hygiene protocols in Phase I therapy and is not taking any medications that can interfere with the healing outcomes of the periodontal wound.

A 14-month-old infant girl has just started daycare and her parents are concerned about her contracting hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). She has never had the disease before and has not received the vaccine against enterovirus 71 (EV71). She has no known allergies to any medications or food. She was born full-term and had a normal birth weight. She has no known medical history of seizures or neurological disease. She has not received any immunodepressant or corticosteroids in the last 6 months, nor any blood products in the last 3 months. She has not received any other research medicines in the last 1 month, nor any attenuated live vaccine in the last 28 days, such as pneumococcal vaccine. She has not been diagnosed with any bleeding disorder or significant bruising or bleeding difficulties with IM injections or blood draws. She is in good health and has no acute infections in the last 7 days. Her parents are willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and are able to understand and sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman diagnosed with idiopathic epilepsy at the age of 16. She has a history of generalized tonic-clonic seizures and has been on anti-epileptic medications since her diagnosis. Despite medication, she has been experiencing frequent seizures, with at least two emergency department visits in the past 12 months. Her current medications include carbamazepine and lamotrigine. She has an upper arm circumference of 20 cm and is able to tolerate wearing the device on her arm. The patient speaks and understands English and is able to read and follow study procedures. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to adhesives or electrode patch components.

A 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes presented to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath and chest discomfort. The patient reports experiencing these symptoms for the past two weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He currently takes metformin and lisinopril for his diabetes and hypertension, respectively. The patient has never undergone a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR). He denies any history of heart failure, malignancy, or renal or liver dysfunction. The patient has no clinical detectable angiopathy. His BMI is 28.5 kg/m², and he is a non-smoker. The patient is currently employed as a software engineer and reports no exposure to occupational magnetic fields. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand the impact of CMR on endothelial function in patients with type 2 diabetes.

John is a 35-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his jaw for the past few months, especially when he chews or talks for an extended period. He has also noticed that he is clenching his teeth more frequently during the day and grinding his teeth at night. He consulted his dentist, who diagnosed him with myofascial pain syndrome with trigger points in his masseter muscle. He was referred to the clinic to receive injection treatment for the trigger points in the masseter muscle. John has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and has a healthy diet. He has no known allergies to any medications. John is excited to participate in the clinical trial and hopes to find relief from his jaw pain.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman of Caucasian ethnicity. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and reports sitting for more than 8 hours a day with less than 60 sit-to-stand transitions and less than 20 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per day. She is ambulatory and medically stable without any health conditions that would inhibit standing or physical activity. She is able to give informed consent, read, communicate, and write fluently in English, and can travel to study visits. She has not menstruated for more than a year and is not currently participating or planning to participate in a physical activity or weight loss program or research study. She does not have any mental state that would preclude complete understanding of the protocol or compliance. She does not have type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes using insulin, poorly controlled hypertension, chronic illness associated with weight change, anemia, personal or first-degree relative history of venous thrombosis, weight instability in the past 3 months, regular use of vasodilator medication, or high risk of stroke and/or heart attack. She is not a regular user of immunosuppressant or corticosteroid medication and has not donated blood less than 56 days prior to the screening visit. She does not smoke cigarettes or use tobacco products including e-cigarettes, and has not been diagnosed with orthostatic hypotension.

52-year-old female who is the primary caregiver for her mother, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. The patient reports feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and stressed due to the demands of caregiving. She has noticed that her mood has been impacted and she has decreased interest in activities she once enjoyed. She reports that she has been feeling this way for the past few months. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine if a telephone-based Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) intervention will reduce her anxiety and improve her overall well-being. She is willing to commit to at least 12 months of caregiving and is able to provide informed consent. She has a GAD-7 score of 14, indicating clinically-significant anxiety. The patient is not enrolled in any other ADRD caregiver intervention studies or programs.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She is 5'6" and weighs 210 pounds, with a body fat percentage of 37%. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or other major health issues. She works a sedentary job in an office and does not engage in regular physical activity. She has tried various diets and weight loss programs in the past, but has not been able to sustain weight loss. She has some concerns about her self-esteem and body image due to her weight. She is interested in participating in a study that will help her lose weight and improve her overall health and well-being. She is willing to commit to a three-month exercise program, with three sessions per week, and is open to both endurance training and endurance-strength training. She does not have any conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

A 3-year-old girl with symptoms of acute gastroenteritis, including vomiting and diarrhea, is brought to the emergency department by her mother. The girl has been vomiting for the past 4 hours and has had 2 or more episodes of vomiting during that time. Upon examination, the healthcare provider determines that the girl is mildly to moderately dehydrated and decides to begin intravenous (IV) fluids. The healthcare provider approaches the mother about enrolling the girl in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of IV fluids alone versus IV fluids with the addition of the medication ondansetron to treat dehydration caused by vomiting in children with gastroenteritis. The mother agrees to participate in the study and provides informed consent. The girl meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 47-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding for the past year came to the clinic for a check-up. She is currently using combined oral contraceptives to regulate her periods but has not noticed any significant improvement. She has no history of endometrial polyps or cancer. She is married with two children and is not planning any more pregnancies. She has no known drug allergies and is not taking any medications other than the oral contraceptives. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has never had a hysterectomy. She has no history of abnormal Pap smears or gynecological surgeries. She is willing to participate in the study to help find better diagnostic and treatment options for endometrial polyps.

A 7-year-old boy was diagnosed with CLN3 Batten disease after experiencing a gradual decline in his motor and cognitive abilities over the past year. He experiences difficulty walking independently and has a UBDRS physical impairment score of 5. He has no history of seizures. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has not received any investigational medications in the past 30 days. He does not have any immunologic diseases or contraindications for intrathecal administration of the product or lumbar puncture. He does not have poorly controlled seizures, corneal or intraocular surgery, or a history of organ transplantation. He has not received any chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or other immunosuppression therapy within the past 30 days. He is not pregnant, and his family is willing to disclose his study participation with primary care physicians and other medical providers.

The patient is a 45-year-old female scheduled for elective surgery for a femur fracture. She has no significant past medical history and is an ASA grade I patient. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her vital signs are as follows: BP: 120/70 mmHg, HR: 80 bpm, RR: 16/min, and O2sat: 98%. Her BMI is 23. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has no history of thyroid disease, Parkinson's disease, dysautonomia or Raynaud's syndrome. She is not currently taking any sedative-hypnotic agents or vasodilators. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The ideal patient for this clinical trial is a healthy male or non-childbearing potential female, light smoker or non-smoker, 18 years of age or older. The patient should not have any clinically significant illnesses or surgeries within 4 weeks prior to the administration of the study medication. They should also not have any clinically significant abnormalities found during medical screening, abnormal laboratory tests, or positive testing for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV at screening. The patient should not have a BMI ≥30.0kg/m2 or a history of significant alcohol or drug abuse. They should not have any clinically significant history or presence of any clinically significant gastrointestinal pathology, unresolved gastrointestinal symptoms, liver or kidney disease, or other conditions known to interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of the drug. The patient should not have any clinically significant history or presence of clinically significant neurological, endocrinal, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, immunologic, psychiatric, or metabolic disease. They should not be using prescription medication or over-the-counter products (excluding topical products without systemic absorption) within 14 days prior to administration of the study medication. The patient should be able to swallow study medication and not have any food allergies, intolerances, restrictions, or special diets that could contraindicate their participation in the study. They should not have a clinically significant history of renal, hepatic, or cardiovascular disease, tuberculosis, epilepsy, asthma, diabetes, psychosis, glaucoma, or angioedema. Additionally, the patient should not have a history of known presence of volume-depletion or hypotension, collagen-vascular disease and/or renal disease, ischemic heart disease, congestive heart failure, or cerebrovascular disease. Breastfeeding subjects and those with positive urine pregnancy tests at screening are also excluded.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for the past 2 years. Despite being on anti-arrhythmic medication, he still experiences episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath and chest discomfort. He has no history of structural heart disease or heart failure. His echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular function with no significant valvular abnormalities. He is scheduled to undergo a cardiac ablation procedure with an irrigated ablation catheter to treat his arrhythmia. He understands the nature of the study and has provided informed consent to participate in the measurement of intracardiac pressures and pressure waveforms using both an irrigated ablation catheter and a 'gold standard' balloon tipped pulmonary artery catheter placed for this study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been on the waiting list for a kidney transplant for over three years. He has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease due to an unknown cause. His cPRA level is 98%, indicating that he has a high level of HLA antibodies, making it difficult to find a compatible donor. He has undergone several rounds of desensitization without success. The patient has no history of allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past six months. He has no current infections or active neoplasia. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception for up to three months after the end of the trial. He has given informed consent and is affiliated with a social security regime. He is not currently under duress psychiatric care or admitted to a health or social institution. He is eager to participate in this clinical trial as he hopes to have a successful kidney transplant and improve his quality of life.

32 yo F with an uncomplicated pregnancy at 28 weeks gestation, presenting for evaluation of fetal biomagnetism with the atomic magnetometer. No history of chronic medical conditions or surgeries. No current use of medications or supplements. No history of metal plates, screws or devices. No history of chronic or acute illnesses. No history of substance abuse or alcohol use. Willing and able to sit or lie still for 5 minute periods during data acquisition. Willing and able to wear metal-free clothing and laser eye protection goggles. English-speaking.

The patient is a healthy 32-year-old woman who has received the first dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. She works as a nurse in a hospital and has been at high risk of contracting the virus due to her exposure to COVID-19 patients. She has not experienced any side effects from the vaccine and is willing to participate in this study to help evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the vaccine under real-world conditions. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is able to provide written informed consent.

A 65 year old woman with no significant medical history would be a good candidate for this clinical trial. She is mentally competent and willing to provide written informed consent prior to study entry. She is in good health, as determined by the outcome of medical history and physical examination. She has not received any vaccines in the last 4 weeks and is not planning to receive any vaccines for the next 4 weeks. She has not received any blood/blood products and/or plasma derivatives or any parenteral immunoglobulin preparation in the past 12 weeks and for the full length of the study. She has not experienced any fever (i.e., axillary temperature ≥ 38°C) within the last 3 days of intended study vaccination. Her BMI is within the acceptable range for the study.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of advanced solid malignancy and cerebral metastases presents for evaluation of treatment options. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. She underwent surgery and whole brain radiotherapy for cerebral metastases 6 months ago, but imaging studies now show evidence of progressive disease. She has refused further radiation therapy and is not a candidate for surgery. Her Karnofsky performance status is 70. Laboratory values such as ANC, platelet count, hemoglobin, BUN, serum creatinine, total and direct bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and alkaline phosphatase are all within normal limits. A life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks is expected from her disease outside the CNS. She gives written informed consent and meets all eligibility criteria for the study. She is currently taking medication for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her bidimensionally measurable disease in the brain is documented on gadolinium magnetic resonance imaging (GdMRI) scan of the brain performed within 14 days prior to enrollment in the study. She has not received systemic therapy for the past 4 weeks, and all clinically significant toxicities (other than hair loss) have resolved. She has no concurrent primary malignancies at other sites and has negative serum pregnancy test. She is willing to use an effective method of contraception. She is an alert female with no acute distress. Her BP: 130/75, HR: 80/min, and BMI: 25. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The neurological examination shows no focal deficits.

A 43-year-old male with a history of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) presents with symptoms of muscle weakness, fatigue, difficulty swallowing, and shortness of breath. He has been previously treated with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and immunosuppressive therapy. He has no other significant medical history and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He participated in the MOM-M281-004 study and did not have any major eligibility deviations or other major protocol deviations or did not meet any of the stopping criteria or discontinue study drug for any reason other than the need for rescue therapy as specified in the MOM-M281-004 study. He is interested in continuing treatment with M281 to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of the drug.

60-year-old male patient, Mr. Smith, has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. He has been receiving care at Intermountain Medical Center for several years and has been diagnosed with a higher than typical risk for cardiovascular events. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. His family history is positive for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is able to understand and sign a written informed consent form and is willing to undergo a blood draw for SomaSignal Tests. He is also able to provide access to his electronic health records. Mr. Smith is not pregnant and is willing and able to comply with any virtual or in-person follow-up visits, tests, and schedule of evaluations.

The patient is a 14-year-old female diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma with residual disease after receiving standard therapy. She has completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but still has measurable residual disease on imaging studies. She is currently experiencing fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss. Her vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 110/70, pulse of 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. Her physical examination is significant for abdominal distension and tenderness. Her lab results show a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, platelet count of 150,000/uL, and white blood cell count of 8,000/uL. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial, including having a suitable adult family member donor available for NK cell donation. She has not received any biological therapy, systemic chemotherapy or radiation therapy for at least two weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has recovered from all acute NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade II-IV non-hematologic acute toxicities resulting from prior therapy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who lost a molar tooth due to decay. She has two remaining posterior teeth adjacent to the missing tooth. The patient has good oral hygiene habits and does not require any acute conservative or periodontal treatment. She reports no known allergies to dental materials and does not have a history of bruxism or missing antagonist teeth. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to provide written consent for the study. She does not have any severe systemic diseases and has no untreated carious lesions or untreated periodontitis. The patient is expected to be compliant with the study requirements.

This is a 35-year-old woman who has struggled with weight management for several years. She has a BMI of 35 and has tried various diets and exercise programs without much success. She is interested in participating in a weight management program that can offer her support and accountability. She has not lost more than 4.5 kg in the past six months and does not have any medical conditions that would limit her ability to participate in physical activity. She is not planning to relocate from the area in the next 12 months and is willing and able to attend weekly group sessions. She understands that she may be randomly assigned to either a large or small group and is willing to accept this.

A 55-year-old retiree who has noticed a decline in her memory and is concerned that it may be affecting her daily life. She has no history of stroke, cognitive impairment, major psychiatric illness, alcoholism, or substance abuse. She is proficient in reading, comprehending, and speaking English and is able to participate in tasks involving motor abilities such as using at least one arm and hand. She is interested in participating in the cognitive screening and training portion of the study to improve her cognitive abilities and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 39-year-old woman who was recently admitted to the hospital due to symptoms of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She tested positive for SARS-CoV2 by RT-PCR on a nasopharyngeal swab. The patient has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies, and she takes an inhaler as needed. She has no other significant medical history, and she has not been hospitalized in the past year. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits, and she is currently receiving oxygen therapy. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. The patient is a resident of France and is affiliated with a hospital within the GABRIEL network. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old Caucasian male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of vertigo and ataxia for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with episodic ataxia type 2 (EA2) and has been treated with acetazolamide, but has not responded well to the medication. He experiences at least three episodes of ataxia per month, which significantly impact his daily life, including his ability to work. He is a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of the computer. He has no significant medical history other than EA2 and is not taking any other medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol regularly. He lives with his wife and two children and is eager to find a treatment that can help him manage his symptoms. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to maintain a daily log of his ataxia episodes using an Interactive Voice Recording System (IVR). He understands the study requirements and is committed to complying with them.

A 32-year old female office worker is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She is in good health, has no known gastrointestinal disorders, and is not currently taking any medications. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. Her diet is not particularly focused on any specific food group, but she tries to eat a balanced diet. She doesn't have any allergies or food intolerances. She exercises 3-4 times a week and is generally active. She is interested in contributing to the study as she believes in the importance of maintaining a healthy diet and is curious about her omega-3 fatty acid intake.

The patient is a 14-year-old female who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) two years ago. She completed standard chemotherapy regimen but unfortunately relapsed 6 months ago with bone marrow involvement. She was refractory to conventional therapy and has no evidence of extramedullary involvement. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 2 months. Her liver function tests are within normal limits and her creatinine clearance is 80 mL/min. She has not received biologic therapy for 7 days and has recovered from any prior chemotherapy treatment for at least 2 weeks. She is not currently on corticosteroid therapy and has not received paclitaxel or docetaxel before. She is not pregnant, and she will use effective contraception during the study.

45-year-old male with a history of gallstones presents with abdominal pain and jaundice. He underwent an ERCP with sphincterotomy for stone extraction. Post-procedure, he developed bright red blood per rectum and was diagnosed with post-sphincterotomy bleeding (PSB). He was treated with epinephrine-injection into the papilla and had no further bleeding. He is now being considered for a retrospective study comparing the efficacy of epinephrine injection versus insertion of a plastic stent for the treatment of PSB. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with non-valvular atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic kidney disease according to KDIGO definition. She has been on stable RAS background treatment for the past year. Her HbA1c is currently at 8%, and her UACR is below 3000. She has no history of renal transplant, immunosuppressant therapy, hematologic disorders, or connective tissue diseases. She has not been diagnosed with any cancer or undergone any major surgical interventions within the last 3 months. She has not experienced any clinically relevant bleeding events within the last 3 months, nor has she had any acute coronary syndrome, PCI, or CABG within the last 12 months. She has not had any hemorrhagic stroke within the last 12 months, nor has she experienced any organ damages from clinically relevant bleeding within the last 6 months. She has not had any major trauma or craniocerebral trauma within the last 30 days. Her hypertension is currently controlled with antihypertensive treatment. She has no history of CHF III-IV functional class, ischemic stroke within the last 14 days, or persistent use of drugs with potential nephrotoxic effects. She has no need for anticoagulation treatment for any other disease except for AF. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. Her creatinine clearance is above 30 ml/min (by Cockroft - Gault equation), and her platelet count is above 100 *109 /л. She has no history of hepatic failure B and C by Child-Pugh score, psychiatric disorders, or background poor compliance. She has no known hypersensitivity to dabigatran, warfarin, or their components. Her life expectancy is estimated to be more than two years.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents with chest pain and is diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome. He is scheduled to undergo percutaneous coronary angioplasty. He has no known allergies and is currently taking aspirin and a statin. He is a non-smoker but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a sedentary lifestyle and is overweight. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg and his heart rate is 80 bpm. His lab studies show elevated cardiac enzymes and lipid levels. He has undergone a stress test and echocardiogram which both show evidence of ischemia. He is considered eligible to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety of high-dose tirofiban during coronary angioplasty.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She does not have any medical conditions and is not on any medications. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. Her blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, and her heart rate is 70 beats per minute. Her recent lab tests showed normal serum potassium levels and estimated GFR. Her hemoglobin A1c, LDL, and triglycerides levels are within the normal limits. She has never been diagnosed with depression, anxiety, or post-traumatic stress disorder. She has no metal in her body and has not been exposed to shrapnel or metal filings. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the effect of a moderately low blood sugar stress on the nervous system.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who suffered a complete tear of his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) during a soccer game. He has been experiencing significant knee pain and instability, limiting his ability to participate in sports and even perform daily activities. He has no history of any major medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He has been referred to the orthopedic surgeon for primary ACL reconstruction with hamstring grafts. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial assessing the outcomes of celecoxib administration versus placebo following ACL reconstruction. He is willing to attend appropriate follow-up and meet all the inclusion criteria. He has no bilateral ACL injuries, no need for revision ACL reconstruction, no meniscus repair, no multiple ligament injuries, no gross osteoarthritis, no significant clinical malalignment, and no history of esophageal, gastric, or duodenal ulceration, hepatic disease, renal disease, hypertension, hypersensitivity to Celecoxib, known allergic-type reactions to sulfonamides, known allergies to ASA or other NSAIDS, inflammatory bowel disease or hyperkalemia.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IIIc epithelial ovarian cancer two years ago. She underwent optimal cytoreductive surgery followed by six cycles of intravenous carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. After completion of chemotherapy, she was in remission for one year. However, during a follow-up visit, she complained of abdominal distension and discomfort. Imaging studies revealed recurrent disease in the pelvis and peritoneal cavity. She underwent another debulking surgery followed by three cycles of liposomal doxorubicin chemotherapy. However, her disease progressed again, and now she is experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and loss of appetite. Imaging studies show disease progression in the pelvis and liver. She is now a candidate for the Abraxane/Bevacizumab clinical trial. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, normal organ function, and no history of allergic reactions to either study drug. She is willing to provide written informed consent and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male who recently underwent cardiac surgery and is now experiencing hemodynamic instability. Despite receiving standard medical therapy, his hemodynamic situation has not improved. He is currently receiving a stable infusion of one high-dose inotrope and two medium dose inotropes for the past 24 hours. His cardiac index is low and he has elevated filling pressures, PCWP, and PA. The patient has no history of renal or hepatic dysfunction. Imaging studies do not show any evidence of LV or RV thrombus. The patient is within 48 hours of being weaned from a cardiopulmonary bypass system, and the surgeon has determined that implantation of the IMPELLA RECOVER LP/LD 5.0 left ventricular cardiac assist device is necessary to support his hemodynamic status.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer. He underwent a prostatectomy 3 years ago and radiation therapy 2 years ago. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level has been rising steadily for the past few months, and his recent biopsy confirmed the recurrence of a soft tissue tumor in the prostate fossa. Surgery is not an option for him, and radiation therapy is not indicated at this time. His tumor size is less than 5 cm in its largest diameter, and it does not encompass the rectal wall or the external urethral sphincter. He is in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He is able to undergo an MRI and is willing to participate in the MR-guided cryoablation clinical trial. He does not have a pacemaker or defibrillator.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the cardiosurgical and vascular intensive care unit of the University Hospital Zurich after undergoing aortic valve replacement surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. His post-operative course has been uneventful, and he is expected to stay in the ICU for at least 24 hours. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He has an invasive CBT measurement (blood temperature from a pulmonary catheter) as part of his clinical standard monitoring. The patient does not have any acute medical contraindications against the measurement of the non-invasive wearable device, and he is not comatose or pregnant. He does not have any implanted pacemakers or other implanted life-sustaining devices.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She has a history of opioid misuse and has been referred for treatment through outpatient services. She is highly motivated to recover from addiction and be a good mother to her child. She reports struggling with responsive parenting due to the challenges of managing her addiction and the demands of caring for a newborn. She is interested in participating in a parenting intervention that could help her improve her parenting skills and support her recovery. She has custody of her child at least half-time each week and is committed to attending all study visits and participating fully in the intervention.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma in both eyes. She has a family history of glaucoma and has been experiencing blurry vision, headaches, and eye pain. She has been taking eye drops for the past year to manage her condition but has noticed that her eye pressure has been fluctuating. She is willing and able to attend all study-related visits and is open to staying overnight at the clinical site for the study assessments. She has no history of severe eye trauma, ocular surgery, or ocular infections within the past few months. She has no other medical conditions that would preclude her from safely participating in the clinical trial. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate birth control. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the new medication Simbrinza™ will help manage her glaucoma more effectively.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with acute heart failure. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. His echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 35% and left ventricular hypertrophy. His N terminal-pro-brain natriuretic peptide level was 1800 pg/ml. He was treated with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers and was subsequently discharged from the hospital. A recent blood test showed that his plasma CA125 level was 55 U/ml. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of a CA125-guided management strategy versus standard therapy on the composite endpoint of 1-year all-cause mortality or readmission for AHF. He is able to understand and sign an informed consent form.

A 28-year-old woman gave birth to a healthy baby boy at a hospital in Mumbai. The baby was born at 39 weeks of gestation and weighed 3.2 kg at birth. The mother had a normal vaginal delivery without any complications. The baby has been exclusively breastfed since birth and is otherwise healthy with no reported medical conditions. The family lives within 5 km of the hospital and has given informed consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial. There is no history of gross congenital malformation or need for resuscitation at birth. The family is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been struggling with bulimia nervosa for the past year. She reports bingeing and purging episodes at least three times per week and has noticed that her alcohol consumption has increased over the past few months. She drinks about four to five drinks per day and has tried to quit but has been unsuccessful. She is currently not taking any medications for her bulimia or alcohol use. She is fluent in English and has a weight above 80% of her ideal weight. She has no significant medical or psychiatric conditions and is not pregnant. She does not have a history of neurological disorders or substance abuse or dependence other than alcohol. She is interested in participating in the study to gain a better understanding of the relationship between her bulimia and alcohol use and to receive treatment that addresses both disorders.

45-year-old male patient diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea and prescribed continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. However, the patient has been non-compliant to the therapy due to high pressure intolerance. The patient has not used bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP) therapy before and is otherwise in good health. The patient is interested in participating in a prospective cohort study to evaluate the effectiveness of BiPAP therapy as a second-line treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. The patient is willing to commit to the study protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her knee joints for the past six months. She has been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis and has mild deformity with no varus or valgus deformity and no crepitus. Her radiographic assessment shows Kellgrane-lawrance type II-III, and a minimum baseline medial tibiofemoral JSW of _2 mm. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent. She has not received intra-articular treatment of the signal joint with any product (corticosteroids in the previous 2 months, or glycosaminoglycans/hyaluronic acid in the previous 6 months) or undergone joint lavage and arthroscopic procedures in the previous 6 months. She has no contraindication for using diacerein and glucosamine and is not currently using or has previously used oral SYSADOA, anti-depressants, tranquillisers, antacids or antibiotics known hypersensitivity to diacerein, to similar compounds, to the excipients or to paracetamol.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with non-metastatic, hormone-naive prostate cancer. He underwent prostatectomy and started androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) as per the NCCN guidelines. His PSA level at the time of screening was 0.05 ng/ml. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and he is eligible to receive castration therapy for 12 months. The patient has a serum total testosterone level of 250 ng/dl. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or any other significant medical condition. The patient is able to swallow enzalutamide and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient is able to complete a baseline cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) and muscular strength test. He has a life expectancy of more than 12 months. The patient uses condoms during sex with his wife, who is of childbearing potential, and is willing to use two acceptable methods of birth control throughout the study period and for three months after the final study drug administration. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who is scheduled for an elective surgery under general anesthesia. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is 178 cm tall and weighs 85 kg. The patient has no known difficult airway history, and he has never had any ear, nose, or throat (ENT) surgeries. He reports no symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux or nausea. The patient has provided informed consent for the study and is willing to participate. He has no language problems, psychological disorders, or dementia that would prevent him from following the procedures of the study. He has not previously enrolled in the study and is not related to the investigator or any of the study staff.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who is in good health with no significant medical history. She has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic diseases. She is not pregnant or nursing and is of non-childbearing potential. The patient is undergoing regular monthly menstrual cycles without any irregularities. She is currently not taking any medication, including hormonal contraception. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is available to participate in the study for the required duration. The patient's physical examination, including blood pressure and heart rate measurement, 12 lead ECG and clinical laboratory tests, show no clinically relevant abnormalities.

The patient is a 22-year-old dental student who has been experiencing tooth sensitivity and discomfort while eating and drinking cold or hot beverages. She has a history of dental caries and has been diagnosed as a high caries risk patient after undergoing caries risk assessment using CAMBRA. She brushes her teeth twice a day with a regular toothpaste and does not use any additional fluoride products. She has a sweet tooth and consumes sugary snacks and drinks on a daily basis. Her medical history is non-significant and she has no periodontal disease or occlusion problems. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the preventive program as directed by the dental team.

The patient is a 36-year-old female who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) by her psychiatrist. She has been experiencing symptoms such as persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed, fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and difficulty concentrating. Her HAMD17 score is 21. She has been taking antidepressant medication for the past 4 weeks, which has stabilized her symptoms to some extent. However, she is still experiencing significant impairment in her daily functioning and is interested in exploring alternative treatment options. The patient has no history of brain surgery, head injury, stroke, or neurodegenerative disorder. She has a history of mild anxiety but no history of substance dependence or abuse. She is not currently taking any antiepileptic or benzodiazepine medication. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with study procedures and visits, including 4 weeks of daily TBS treatment and concurrent fNIRS measurements.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who is completely edentulous and has an opposing natural dentition. She has proper amount of attached gingiva (≥2 mm) and no history of bruxism. She does not have any medical condition that absolutely contraindicates implant placement and her glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) is less than or equal to 6.4 percent, indicating controlled diabetes. She is a non-smoker and is willing to go through the proposed interventions. She currently wears a complete upper denture and is interested in getting implant-supported restorations for better stability and retention.

20-year-old female with moderate to severe acne on both sides of her face. She has a history of using multiple over-the-counter acne treatments, including salicylic acid and benzoyl peroxide, with little improvement. She has not used any prescription medications for acne in the past 4 weeks. The patient is not currently taking any oral retinoids or systemic corticosteroids. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a mid-infrared laser treatment for her acne. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and sign an informed consent form.

A 55-year-old female caregiver is caring for her 70-year-old husband who has been diagnosed with dementia. He requires assistance with basic activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing and grooming. He also has two dependencies in instrumental activities of daily living, such as cooking and cleaning. The caregiver reports that her husband often displays difficult behaviors, which makes it challenging for her to provide care. They live together and she provides care for at least 2 hours per day, and has been caregiving for 8 months. The caregiver has no major health issues and is 45 years of age. The care recipient has a diagnosis of dementia, but is not confined to bed most of the day and is responsive to touch and the environment.

2-year-old male, weighing 12 kg, presented to the emergency department with a fever, cough and difficulty breathing. The patient was diagnosed with severe pneumonia based on WHO criteria and admitted to the hospital. The patient's oxygen saturation level on room air was 88% by pulse oximetry, and SpO2 did not improve with administration of supplemental oxygen via a standard nasal cannula. The patient's parent/guardian provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has no history of hypercapnia, acidosis or lactic acidosis, and has not previously been intubated or required positive-pressure ventilation. The patient's hemoglobin level is within normal range, and there are no facial abnormalities or traumas precluding use of the novel mask (nasal reservoir cannula) or standard nasal cannula. The patient is not suspected to have pneumothorax, and has a SICK score of 2.0. The patient does not have any hemodynamic instability based on clinician judgment, and the SpO2 level on oxygen is 93% at the start of the enrollment.

52-year-old female with a history of essential hypertension for the past 7 years. She has been taking candesartan cilexetil 16mg once daily for the past 6 months, but her blood pressure remains elevated at 150/95 mmHg. She has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding amlodipine besylate to her current treatment regimen. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with Cushing's disease in 2005 and has been intermittently followed up in a university center in the West of France since then. She had a history of weight gain, easy bruising, muscle weakness, and depression. Her past medical history was significant for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and osteoporosis. She underwent transsphenoidal surgery twice in 2005 and 2008, respectively, and had a recurrence in 2012. She received medical treatment with ketoconazole and later with pasireotide, and had a radiation therapy in 2014. Her current medications include levothyroxine, calcium, vitamin D, alendronate, amlodipine, metformin, and insulin. She reports experiencing fatigue, mood swings, and decreased libido. She is willing to participate in the study and share her medical history and complete the questionnaire.

55 yo F with newly diagnosed ovarian adenocarcinoma, FIGO stage III, underwent primary chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. Tumor sample from diagnostic biopsy is available. Patient has no significant comorbidities, good performance status, and has not undergone previous cancer treatment. The patient has consented to the trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has a history of endometriosis and has undergone laparoscopic surgery in the past to remove the adhesions. She has been taking oral contraceptives for the past 6 months to manage her symptoms but has stopped taking them in order to attempt to conceive. She and her partner have been trying to conceive naturally for the past 6 months but have not been successful. She has a regular menstrual cycle and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is a non-vegetarian and has no known allergies. Her BMI is 22 and her blood pressure is normal. She has undergone fertility testing and her AMH levels are normal, her FSH levels are within normal limits, and her antral follicle count is over 6. She has never undergone IVF or ICSI treatment before. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has medical insurance and is willing to undergo any experimental treatments that may be required as part of the study.

8-year-old male patient with a history of asthma and pneumonia presented to the emergency department with respiratory distress, tachypnea, and hypoxia. The patient was admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit and was placed on mechanical ventilation due to severe respiratory failure. The patient is currently sedated with intermittent boluses of fentanyl and midazolam at the discretion of the attending physician. The patient is unable to follow commands or communicate due to sedation. The patient's current FLACC score is 6 and COMFORT score is 18. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the sedation and ventilator weaning protocol clinical trial.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who works as an engineer. He has not received any booster dose containing a tetanus- and diphtheria-containing vaccine in the last 20 years. He has no history of pertussis disease in the last 10 years and is not currently on any medication or vaccine that may interfere with the study assessments. He has no febrile illness or moderate to severe acute illness/infection. He is not pregnant, and there is no history of Guillain-Barre syndrome or brachial neuritis following previous vaccinations. He has no history of encephalopathy of unknown origin within 7 days after immunization with a pertussis-containing vaccine or neurological disorders. He has no known or suspected immune dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, bleeding disorder or anticoagulants contraindicating intramuscular vaccination. He has no chronic disease or intercurrent illness that might interfere with study assessments.

6-month-old male infant diagnosed with sickle cell anemia (HbSS) with no history of hospitalizations for SCA complications. Medical records show that the steady-state absolute reticulocyte count was obtained between 2-6 months of age. The infant is not currently receiving hydroxyurea or monthly blood transfusions and has not participated in the preliminary study. The infant's parents are concerned about their child's risk for future SCA complications and are interested in participating in a study that could potentially identify the highest risk patients and target therapy accordingly.

67-year-old female admitted to the ICU with septic shock secondary to pneumonia. On admission, she was hypotensive and required vasopressor support. She was started on antibiotics and received aggressive fluid resuscitation. Her clinical status improved over the next 24 hours and she was weaned off vasopressors. However, she remained in the ICU for continued management of her pneumonia. She is currently alert and oriented, with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is not pregnant and does not have any finger, hand, or forearm anomalies or diseases that may interfere with attaching a pulse oximeter sensor. She is not wearing nail polish, nail gel, or nail decorations.

The patient is a 70-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been recently diagnosed with invasive breast adenocarcinoma. The tumor is clinically T2 and measures more than 1 cm on echography. The biopsy confirms that the tumor is estrogen receptor-positive, with more than 10% of the tumor cells positive. The patient has no prior history of breast cancer or any other malignancies within the past 5 years, except for nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She has no contraindications to tamoxifen citrate or letrozole. The patient has no mental incapacitation that would preclude consent, and no cardiac function that could contraindicate surgery or medical treatment (e.g., radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy). She is not currently on hormone-replacement therapy or any other treatment for menopause. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo treatment with either letrozole or tamoxifen citrate before undergoing surgery for breast cancer.

A 54-year-old male presents to the ophthalmologist with blurry vision and redness in his left eye. He reports that he has a history of corneal transplantation in his left eye due to keratoconus several years ago. The patient has also noticed that his eye gets easily irritated and that his vision has decreased in the last few months. On examination, there is corneal neovascularization in the temporal and superior quadrant of the cornea. The neovascularization extends beyond 1.0 mm over the limbus. The patient's intraocular pressure is within normal limits, and there is no evidence of inflammation in the anterior chamber. The patient has no other medical problems and does not take any medication. He has never been treated with anti-VEGF medication. He denies any history of heart disease, stroke, or bleeding disorder. He is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and has no history of drug abuse. He is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II low-grade serous ovarian cancer. She underwent bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and maximal upfront cytoreductive surgery. The pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of low-grade serous ovarian cancer with nonaberrant p53 IHC result. She has no history of neoadjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy for the treatment of this disease. She doesn't have any known hypersensitivity to letrozole or carboplatin/paclitaxel therapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, which allows for moderate physical activity, such as carrying groceries, but not strenuous exercise, such as running. Her labs show an ANC of 2,000/mcl, platelets of 150,000 cells/mcl, creatinine of 1.2 x upper limit of normal (ULN), bilirubin of 1.0 x ULN, ALT and AST of 2.5 x ULN. She has no history of severe cardiac disease or central nervous system metastases. She is not known to be HIV-infected nor does she have any active systemic infections. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is willing to take per oral (P.O.) medications.

25 year-old male who recently underwent surgical extraction of third molars and is experiencing post-operative dental pain. He is in generally good health with no serious medical conditions and has been medically cleared to participate in the study. He does not have an acute localized dental infection at the time of surgery. He is not pregnant or lactating and is not of child-bearing potential.

59-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) of French American British (FAB) subtype except M3. The patient has a history of relapsed or refractory AML with NPM1 genetic mutation detected by molecular assay. The patient is medically unfit for or resistant to standard intensive induction chemotherapy. The patient is Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) 1. The patient has a total bilirubin level of 1.1 mg/dL, ALT and AST levels of 25 U/L and 30 U/L, respectively, and a calculated creatinine clearance of 57 mL/min. The patient is postmenopausal for more than 1 year before the screening visit. The patient agrees to practice 2 effective methods of contraception from the time of signing the informed consent form through 90 days after the last dose of study drug. The patient has no significant uncontrolled infection or active infection. The patient is not diagnosed with any other malignancy within 2 years before study enrollment or previously diagnosed with another malignancy and have any evidence of residual disease. The patient does not have ≥ grade 3 peripheral neuropathy, or grade 2 with pain on clinical examination during the screening. The patient has not participated in other clinical trials, including those with other investigational agents not included in this trial, within 21 days of the start of this trial and throughout the duration of this trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a cleft lip and palate. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as a software engineer and is physically active. He has one missing tooth in his upper jaw, which has compromised bone support for installation of dental implant(s). He has adequate interdental arch space for dental implant restorations and bony continuity between cleft segments. His medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications. He has normal renal and hepatic functions, as well as normal laboratory values for blood count, serum, and metabolic bone diseases. He is willing to follow the study procedures and instructions and has read and signed the informed consent form. He is eligible for the study and will be randomly assigned to receive either traditional autogenous bone grafting or cell therapy (ixmyelocel-T) for the regeneration of bone in the area of the jaw where an implant will be placed.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial as it does not involve patient participation. The study is focused on collecting DNA samples from African-American sib-pairs and other family members with hypertensive end-stage renal disease in order to identify genes causing the condition.

Pt is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach with metastasis to the liver. He has undergone a total gastrectomy and has completed neoadjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX six months ago. Imaging studies reveal disease progression, and the patient is now presenting for possible enrollment into the Her+XELOX clinical trial. The patient is HER2-positive as determined by IHC with a score of 3+. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least three months. The patient has no physical integrity problems of the upper gastrointestinal tract, and the malabsorption syndrome has been ruled out. The patient does not have active gastrointestinal bleeding, and there are no residual toxicities from previous therapy. The patient has no other malignancies within the last five years, and neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits. The patient has no significant liver or kidney dysfunction, and LVEF is above the minimum threshold for enrollment. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who recently visited the emergency department due to injuries caused by intimate partner violence. She has been in a relationship with her partner for the past 5 years and has two young children. The abuse started a few months ago and has been gradually getting worse. The patient reports being hit, pushed, and kicked by her partner. She also suffers from psychological abuse, including verbal insults and threats. The patient has bruises on her arms and legs, and her face is swollen. She complains of severe pain and difficulty moving. The patient has a low level of education and has been unemployed for the past year. She has a history of exposure to violence during her childhood. The patient speaks French fluently and has no verbal opposition to inclusion in the study. The investigators will assess her level of incapacité totale de travail (ITT) to determine the severity of her injuries sustained.

A 40-year-old male with a history of chronic Hepatitis-C (CHC) who has previously been treated with daclatasvir-based therapy in combination with other HCV direct acting antivirals (DAAs) for at least 8 weeks. The patient must have completed the treatment within the last 12 months or within 6 months of protocol availability at the clinical site for subjects treated in the AI447036 or AI447114 studies. The patient must be willing to enroll in this study and must be 18 years of age or older at initiation of prior DCV-based therapy.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with mitral valve stenosis and tricuspid valve regurgitation. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He reports occasional shortness of breath and chest discomfort during exertion. Preoperative evaluation showed that he has pulmonary hypertension with a mean pulmonary artery pressure (MPAP) of 35 mmHg on right-sided catheterization. Echocardiography also confirmed the presence of pulmonary hypertension with a systolic pulmonary artery pressure (SPAP) of 45 mmHg. The patient is scheduled for elective valvular cardiac surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass (ECC). He is eligible for the study since he meets the inclusion criteria for preoperative pulmonary hypertension. The patient will be recruited the day before surgery and randomized using computerized cards by the pharmacy department.

The patient is a 67 year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure and cirrhosis. He presents with a serum sodium level of 127 mEq/L and has been experiencing fatigue, confusion, and headaches. He has a history of alcohol abuse and currently smokes a pack of cigarettes daily. His current medications include furosemide and spironolactone for his CHF and lactulose for his cirrhosis. He denies any recent changes in diet or fluid intake. On physical exam, he has pitting edema in the lower extremities and ascites. His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg and heart rate is 90 beats per minute. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his hyponatremia.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) after experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He underwent first-line treatment with chemotherapy and radiation therapy but unfortunately, the cancer did not respond well to the treatment and he experienced relapse after completing the therapy. He currently has measurable disease by RECIST criteria and his ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for his ANC which is 1.2 × 109/L. He has no history of HIV infection, cardiac disease, or other malignant tumors. He does not have any motor or sensory neuron lesions/symptoms of NCI - CTC AE > 1 nor does he have any serious active infections. He has no allergies to ifosfamide or liposomal doxorubicin. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28 year-old female who presented to the Emergency Department with a chief complaint of headache. She describes the headache as a throbbing pain on the right side of her head that started about 3 hours ago. She rates the pain as 8 out of 10 on the pain scale. She has a history of occasional headaches that she usually manages with over-the-counter pain medication, but those have not been effective this time. She has no history of head trauma or other medical conditions. She is not pregnant and has no allergies to medications. She speaks Turkish fluently and is able to comply with the study requirements. She has not taken any analgesic drugs in the last four hours.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who was diagnosed with IgE-mediated wheat allergy one year ago. She experienced an allergic reaction after consuming wheat products, which included hives, itching, swelling of the face, and difficulty breathing. She has a positive skin prick test and wheat-specific IgE test results. She has not had any recent reactions to wheat products. She lives with her parents and has no significant medical history or allergies to any other foods. She has not been on any specific immunotherapy or other biological agents. The study will be conducted at the Department of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, 2nd University Pediatric Clinic of "Panagiotis & Aglaia Kyriakou" Children's Hospital, Athens, Greece. The patient and her parents will be trained in the use of self-injectable epinephrine in case of severe allergic reactions. The parents will provide signed written consent for their child's participation in the study.

45 y/o male with a history of lower back pain and leg pain, who underwent decompression/discectomy for lumbar disc herniation at L5-S1 level a year ago. The patient reports that the pain improved following the surgery but returned with the same intensity after a few months. MRI shows recurrent lumbar disc herniation at the same level. The patient reports radicular leg pain that worsens with movements, and the pain is relieved with rest. The patient is not diabetic, has no history of fractures, and no autoimmune diseases. The patient has no history of psychological/psychiatric problems that could compromise the reliability of their results. The patient is not on any other medication that may interfere with the interpretation of efficacy and safety data during the study. The patient has undergone flexion and extension x-rays that demonstrate an absence of sponylolisthesis or spondylolisthesis with less than 3 mm of movement.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has a medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has never undergone general anesthesia before. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her body mass index is within normal limits. The patient has no history of gastroesophageal reflux or high-grade obesity. She has been informed of the study and has provided written consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a history of stage IV colorectal cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not achieved complete remission. Her most recent CT scan revealed stable disease with no new lesions. She presents with fatigue and abdominal discomfort. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of pulmonary disease or major surgery in the past four weeks. She meets the inclusion criteria for the THINK study and is interested in participating in the Phase I dose escalation segment to assess the safety and clinical activity of multiple administrations of autologous NKR-2 cells. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to undergo apheresis and up to three cycles of NKR-2 therapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2. She has no history of hypersensitivity to aspirin or any other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. Her pregnancy test is negative, and she uses a medically acceptable form of birth control. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She is willing to participate in all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other trial procedures according to the clinical protocol.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with schizophrenia 5 years ago. She has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past 3 years and her symptoms have been stable. She works part-time as a bookkeeper and lives with her husband and two children. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and her medical history is unremarkable. Her current medications include risperidone 2 mg/day and benztropine 2 mg/day. Her most recent blood work showed normal levels of cholesterol and triglycerides, and her liver and thyroid function tests were within normal limits. She has no history of pancreatitis, thyroid axis alterations or cataracts. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to sign informed consent. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve her cognitive function and quality of life.

A 63-year-old male smoker was diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) four years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue even when performing light activities. His most recent pulmonary function test showed a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 1.5 L (45% predicted) and a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 2.8 L (60% predicted). He was diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension due to COPD (PH-COPD) and was enrolled in the randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, adaptive study 'A Phase 3, Randomized, Placebo-controlled, Double-blind, Adaptive Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Inhaled Treprostinil in Patients with Pulmonary Hypertension due to Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (PH-COPD)' (RIN-PH-304). After completing all scheduled study visits during the Treatment Period of Study RIN-PH-304, he has been invited to participate in the open-label study to evaluate the safety of continued therapy with inhaled treprostinil. He has agreed to participate and is willing to reinitiate inhaled treprostinil at 3 breaths (18 micrograms [mcg]) 4 times daily (QID) during waking hours.

45 y/o female diagnosed with malignant pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, metastatic to the liver and lungs. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the tumor has progressed despite treatment. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is HLA-A2 positive. The patient has a life expectancy of > 6 months as judged by her treating physician. The patient is not currently receiving dexamethasone or any other immunotherapy treatment. The patient has not been previously exposed to EO2401. The patient has no history of solid organ transplantation or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The patient does not have a history or presence of tuberculosis, human immunodeficiency virus, or potentially active hepatitis B virus/hepatitis C virus infection. The patient has not received live or attenuated vaccine therapy used for prevention of infectious diseases including seasonal (influenza) vaccinations within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug. The patient does not have a history of hypersensitivity to any excipient present in the pharmaceutical forms of the study treatments.
