The patient is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures indicated in the protocol. The patient has received the information sheet and has provided written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures.

Pt is a 55yo F with a recent diagnosis of stage I invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast, with a unifocal lesion measuring 2.5 cm diameter. She underwent breast-conserving surgery with clear margins of at least 2 mm in all directions. Histopathology revealed that there was no lymph invasion (L0) and no hemangiosis (V0). A sentinel node biopsy was negative for cancer cells. She has no history of any other malignancy or significant medical history. She is currently not pregnant or lactating. The patient has been informed about the option of external beam irradiation (EBI) after BCS or modified dose of pulsed-dose-rate (PDR) and high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy alone as Accelerated Partial Breast Irradiation (APBI) in a defined low-risk group of invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial with signed study-specific consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old female smoker who has been smoking an average of 15 cigarettes per day for the past 10 years. She has tried to quit smoking multiple times in the past, but has been unsuccessful. The patient is in good overall health with no history of cancer or heart disease. She has no known allergies to adhesive tape or latex. She is currently not pregnant or nursing, and is using an effective form of contraception. The patient is able to communicate effectively in English and has resided in the geographic area for over 6 months. She is not currently receiving treatment for depression or substance abuse. The patient is willing to participate in a smoking cessation study involving counseling and nicotine replacement therapy.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 2 years ago. She has been treated with a combination of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) that includes methotrexate (MTX) and hydroxychloroquine. Despite this treatment, she continues to experience moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness. She has tried different nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and analgesics, but they provide only temporary relief. Her RA symptoms have significantly impacted her daily activities, and she is interested in exploring other treatment options. She doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of intolerance to anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha agents or tocilizumab. She hasn't received any biologic therapy for the treatment of RA within the last 3 months. Her current dose of oral corticosteroids is 5 mg/day of prednisone, which she has been taking for the last month. She has no other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of sirukumab in reducing the signs and symptoms of RA and inhibiting radiographic progression.

A 50 year old woman who has been wearing multifocal contact lenses for the past 6 months seeks to participate in the study. She has no known active ocular disease or infection and has had a full eye examination in the past year. She reports being able to wear contact lenses for at least 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. She has refractive astigmatism of -0.50DC and is presbyopic with a reading addition of +1.25D. She has no known sensitivity to diagnostic sodium fluorescein and is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy at the time of enrollment. She has not undergone any refractive error surgery or intraocular surgery.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presented to the clinic with concerns about her health and body composition. She reported experiencing hot flashes, night sweats, and difficulty sleeping, which were affecting her quality of life. She was interested in improving her health through exercise and dietary supplements. The patient had no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, renal pathologies or hypertension, and was not a smoker. She was physically able to practice exercises on treadmill and weight exercises. The patient was not using hormone therapy or isoflavones nor any drugs that interfere with lipid and antihypertensive metabolism. She was interested in participating in the clinical trial that evaluated the effects of isoflavone supplementation associated with physical exercise in postmenopausal women.

A 55-year-old woman came to the clinic with a complaint of headache and jaw pain for the past week. She also reported experiencing fatigue, malaise, and weight loss over the past month. Her medical history included hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were both under control with medications. Upon physical examination, her temporal arteries were tender to palpation, and her CRP levels were elevated. She was suspected of having giant cell arteritis (GCA) based on her symptoms and imaging results. The patient agreed to participate in the study and had not undergone temporal artery biopsy before. She was willing to undergo color Doppler imaging of temporal arteries and cervicocephalic axes as part of the study protocol. The patient was not currently receiving a corticosteroid dose of 20 mg or more and had no history of GCA. She was not pregnant or breastfeeding and was using effective contraception. She met all the inclusion criteria and did not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 62 year old woman was admitted to the hospital due to sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. A brain CT scan revealed a spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage in the right basal ganglia. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no history of atrial fibrillation or anticoagulant use. Her initial National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 18. She was started on blood pressure-lowering medications and transferred to the stroke unit for further management. Her family reports that she was independent in her activities of daily living prior to the stroke. She is willing to participate in the longitudinal cohort study on ICH care.

A 45-year-old Japanese man was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1. He has never received interferon treatment and is looking for a treatment option. He has no history of liver cirrhosis, ascites, or hepatic encephalopathy. He has no other medical conditions that would contraindicate the use of pegylated interferon alfa-2b and ribavirin. He works as an office manager and enjoys playing golf on weekends. He has no history of co-infection with HIV or hepatitis B. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of vaniprevir in combination with pegylated interferon alfa-2b and ribavirin compared to treatment with pegylated interferon alfa-2b and ribavirin alone.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was prescribed a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) for the treatment of atrial fibrillation. After several weeks of taking the medication, he experienced a severe episode of gastrointestinal bleeding, resulting in hospitalization. The patient was previously healthy, with no known medical conditions or history of bleeding disorders. He is currently stable and has provided informed consent to participate in this retrospective study, which aims to evaluate if Cipherome's algorithm could have predicted the serious adverse drug reactions he experienced while on DOAC therapy.

The patient is an 18-year-old male with severe congenital neutropenia (SCN). He was diagnosed with SCN at the age of 2 and has been receiving granulocyte-colony stimulation factor therapy for the past 16 years. Despite this treatment, he continues to have frequent bacterial infections and has required hospitalization several times. Genetic testing has revealed an unfavorable mutation of an SCN gene, indicating a high risk of malignant transformation. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no family history of immunodeficiency disorders. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally with friends. His physical exam and lab studies show neutropenia and no other abnormalities. He has a matched unrelated donor for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and has consented to participate in the clinical trial.

52 year old female with congenital abnormalities affecting her ears since birth. She has significant hearing loss in her left ear and moderate-severe hearing loss in her right ear. She has been using traditional hearing aids for several years with limited benefit. She is interested in exploring other options and has been recommended for BAHA implantation. Her hearing thresholds and speech perception will be evaluated to determine if she meets criteria for a high gain super-power processor. She is a native English speaker and is excited to participate in this study to potentially improve her hearing outcomes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 15 years. He is experiencing chronic cough and sputum production for the past 2 years. He has no history of asthma or allergies. He works as a construction worker and is exposed to dust and fumes at work. He has never been diagnosed with any lung disease before. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril 10 mg daily. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath at rest. He has a BMI of 28. His physical examination is unremarkable except for coarse breath sounds. His vital signs are within normal limits. His labs: FBS: 95 mg/dl, TG: 120 mg/dl, Cholesterol: 180 mg/dl, LDL: 100 mg/dl, HDL: 35 mg/dl. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine whether his smoking and chronic bronchitis have caused any significant changes in his pulmonary function.

The patient is a generally healthy 32-year-old male with a body mass index of 24. He has never donated blood or plasma in the past month and has never donated more than 500 mL within the past 3 months. He is a non-smoker and is willing to refrain from smoking and using nicotine gum or transdermal nicotine patches during the inpatient period.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease stage 3. He was recently diagnosed with hyperkalemia and had to discontinue the previous medication due to adverse reactions. His i-STAT potassium value is between 3.5-6.2 mmol/l inclusive. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not received any other treatment for hyperkalemia while participating in the previous study ZS-004 (NCT 02088073). He is able and willing to provide written informed consent and start dosing in ZS-004E (NCT 021070920) within two (2) days after the last dose of investigational product in ZS-004. He is not on dialysis, and he has no history of diabetic ketoacidosis. He is not severely physically or mentally incapacitated and can perform the tasks associated with the protocol. He has no known hypersensitivity or previous anaphylaxis to ZS or to its components. He is not currently on any drug or device other than ZS.

65 year old woman with primary open angle glaucoma diagnosed 5 years ago. She is currently prescribed topical hypotensive medications but her intraocular pressures remain uncontrolled. Her last recorded IOP was 24 mmHg in both eyes. She has no history of any prior glaucoma surgeries, neovascular glaucoma, or clinically significant corneal disease. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new implant for glaucoma treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old right-handed woman who suffered an ischemic stroke six months ago, resulting in hemiparesis of the arm. She has residual movement of at least 15 degrees of shoulder flexion or adduction and 15 degrees of active elbow flexion and extension. She is not claustrophobic and does not have any neurological or psychiatric disorders. She is able to understand instructions and complete tracking tasks. The patient is not depressed and is willing to participate in the full protocol of the study. She has no history of synkinetic or mirror movements and does not have shoulder or joint pain during movements. The patient has no allergies to goretex or conductivity gel.

A 35-year-old male with a history of synovial cell sarcoma presented with progressive abdominal pain and swelling. Imaging studies revealed multiple liver and lung metastases. The patient underwent biopsy confirming recurrent synovial cell sarcoma. He was referred to the clinical trial for vaccine therapy and sargramostim for advanced sarcoma. The patient has HLA A*0201 positive by genotyping and meets all other eligibility criteria.

56 year old man with a recent coronary artery calcium score (CACS) of 450, who has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on a statin, ACE inhibitor, and metformin. He has no history of prior revascularization procedures, and is a non-smoker. He has no known contraindications to MRI, and has a resting heart rate of 68 beats per minute. He has never been pregnant or lactating, and has a BMI of 28. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 54 year-old male with a BMI of 30 kg/m2. He was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and is currently being treated with metformin. He has no evidence of impaired renal function and is in generally good health. He has no history of heart disease, hepatitis B or C, or any other significant medical or psychiatric disorder. He is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study. He has not been exposed to insulin and is not currently taking any exclusionary concomitant medications.

A 68-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of osteoporotic hip fracture is being recruited for a clinical trial evaluating the contribution of quantitative computed tomography (QCT) image analysis in predicting the risk of osteoporotic hip fracture. She has a history of low bone mineral density (BMD) and has been on bisphosphonate therapy for the past 2 years. She reports no significant medical history, except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has been exercising regularly for the past year under the supervision of a physical therapist. She is married and lives with her husband. She has 2 adult children who live nearby. She has undergone dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in the past, which confirmed low BMD. She has provided her consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo QCT imaging of the proximal femur.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who has struggled with obesity for several years. He has previously attempted various dietary and nutritional treatments but has not seen significant results. He was not eligible for bariatric surgical treatment due to failing neuropsychological tests. He will be participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the olfactory-gustatory aspects and blood patterns of subjects undergoing a 6-month period of Fasting Mimicking Diet (FMD) compared to a group of subjects observing their own eating habits. The patient will be randomly assigned to either Group A or Group B, and will either follow the FMD for the first 6 months followed by eating habit observation for the next 6 months, or vice versa. Before and after each period, the patient will undergo olfactory and taste tests, as well as provide blood samples for analysis. The patient has no history of mental or psychiatric illness, drug or alcohol addiction, or visual impairment that would affect completion of neuropsychological tests.

The patient is a 36-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her second trimester. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has received routine prenatal care and has undergone ultrasound scans that showed no abnormalities. However, she is concerned about the risk of chromosomal abnormalities in her baby and has opted for invasive prenatal testing. She is able to read and understand both Chinese and English. The patient is well-informed about the options of conventional cytogenetics and aCGH and is willing to participate in the study. She is aware that the use of aCGH may provide a higher resolution analysis of chromosomal aberrations in a shorter period of time, but may also have limitations in the interpretation of certain copy number variants (CNV). She is willing to complete the questionnaire survey on knowledge and acceptance on the application of aCGH in prenatal diagnosis.

56 F with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a positive family history of CAD. She presented to her primary care physician with complaints of exertional chest pain and dyspnea on exertion. She was referred for cardiology evaluation and underwent a stress test which revealed evidence of reversible myocardial ischemia. She was then scheduled for a CZT-SPECT MPI to further evaluate the extent and severity of her CAD. She is able to complete exercise treadmill testing and has a resting heart rate of 80 beats/min with no significant arrhythmia. She does not have severe aortic stenosis or any other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled for an elective interventional neuroradiology procedure that requires general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She denies any history of heart disease, kidney disease, or diabetes mellitus. She does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is currently not taking any medications other than her blood pressure medication. She has never had a previous surgery or anesthesia. She has been informed about the study and has given her oral agreement to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The patient has been scheduled to receive a bone marrow transplant and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to identify specific antigens that can be used for cellular immune therapy. The patient has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. The patient is willing to undergo additional testing and procedures to identify personalized antigens for potential future treatment options.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) and has been taking warfarin to prevent stroke. However, he has experienced a stroke despite taking the medication. The patient is now contraindicated to long-term oral anticoagulant therapy. He does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study. The patient is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule and able to provide written informed consent. His CHA2DS2-VASC score is 2, indicating a moderate risk of stroke, and his HAS-BLED score is 2, indicating a moderate risk of bleeding. His LAA anatomy accommodates a device per the sizing guidelines. He has not been exposed to any other investigational products and has not had a left atrial appendage closure device implanted previously.

The patient is a 12-year-old male with a diagnosis of hemoglobin SC disease and has had at least one painful crisis in the past. He weighs 40 kg and is 150 cm tall. He is in good general health with no other significant medical history. Laboratory results are as follows: hemoglobin level of 9.8 g/dL, total bilirubin level of 2.3 mg/dL, and reticulocyte count of 7.5%. He is not currently taking any medication that contains magnesium. He is able to swallow the Mg pidolate preparation. The patient and their parent/guardian have provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient will be required to attend 21 clinic visits during the 16-month study period and keep a diary of any pain episodes or changes noticed. The patient has been randomized to receive either magnesium or placebo during the first 24 weeks of the study and will receive the opposite treatment during the second 24 weeks of the study, with an 8-week washout period in between.

A 32-year-old male was admitted to the burn center after suffering from a major burn injury on his upper body and limbs caused by a workplace accident. The patient is conscious and has no history of chronic disorders or organ dysfunctions. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient's burns cover approximately 25% of his total body surface area, and he is in stable condition. He has no inhalation injury. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he is breathing without the need for oxygen support. The patient is able to communicate well and has no cognitive or communication impairments. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is HIV-negative and has a CD4 count of 550 cells/mm3. He has no history of immunodeficiency, chronic illness, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. He has never received an HIV-1 vaccine or participated in a previous HIV vaccine trial. He has not used any experimental agents within the past 30 days or received live attenuated vaccines within the past 60 days. He has not received any medically indicated subunit or killed vaccines within the past 2 weeks. He has not had any blood products or immunoglobulin within the past 6 months. He reports no history of injection drug use within the last 12 months prior to enrollment and does not meet the criteria for AVEG Risk Groups C or D. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the safety and immunogenicity of the HIV-1 pseudovirion vaccine. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with hematemesis and coffee ground emesis. He was admitted to the ICU for further management. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. He takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. He has no known allergies to medications. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has not received any prokinetic medication in the last 48 hours and does not have a history of cardiac arrhythmia or QT prolongation.

The patient is a 17-year-old female with a history of keratoconus. She has been experiencing progressive visual impairment and difficulty wearing contact lenses due to the irregular shape of her cornea. She has no known allergies to riboflavin ophthalmic solution or any of its components. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has a stable refraction and her manifest refraction spherical equivalent and average K (Km) on the Pentacam do not differ by more than 0.75 D from the respective measurements taken at the second exam. She has a BSCVA of 60 letters on ETDRS chart in her right eye and 70 letters in her left eye. Her corneal pachymetry at the thinnest point measured by Pentacam in the eye to be treated is 450 microns. She does not have a history of corneal surgery or insertion of Intacs in the eye to be treated, nor has she had a previous Limbal Relaxing Incision (LRI) procedure in the eye to be treated. She has no clinically significant corneal scarring in the cross-linking treatment zone that is not related to keratoconus or, in the investigator's opinion, will interfere with the cross-linking procedure. She has not used Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) supplements within 1 week of the cross-linking treatment. She has not used any investigational drug or device within 30 days of the study, nor is she concurrently enrolled in another investigational drug or device trial within 30 days of the study. She understands and agrees to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old Hispanic woman who was diagnosed with HIV during her pregnancy. She has a 6-year-old daughter who is HIV-negative. She is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and has a viral load of less than 50 copies/ml. She reports feeling overwhelmed with the demands of parenting while managing her HIV, including taking her medication and attending medical appointments. She has a history of depression and anxiety and reports feeling isolated from her community due to the stigma associated with HIV. The patient is fluent in both English and Spanish. Her daughter is also fluent in English and attends a local elementary school. The patient has no history of cognitive or intellectual impairment and does not report any current symptoms of psychosis. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her parenting and self-care skills and hopes that it will lead to better health outcomes for both herself and her daughter.

54-year-old male with a history of Parkinson's disease for 10 years, treated with Carbidopa/Levodopa (Sinemet) with gradually increasing doses. The patient has been experiencing tremors and rigidity which have been unresponsive to medication. The patient has been evaluated and approved by a neurosurgeon for Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery. The patient has no history of other neurological, psychiatric or medical conditions that could interfere with the study. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and able to attend follow-up visits for at least 12 months.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with varicocele after being evaluated for infertility. He has been trying to conceive with his partner for the past year without success. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is anxious about the surgery but willing to undergo it to improve his chances of conceiving. He has no prior surgeries at the inguinal level. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial, and has given informed consent in accordance with national and Declaration of Helsinki guidelines. He is physically fit and has no comorbidities. His varicocele has been evaluated and found to have complexity and tortuosity of the veins at inguinal level, making separating and ligation of the vein could lead to artery injury. Therefore, he is a suitable candidate for Combined Mini-incision Microscopic Varicocelectomy.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with stage III colorectal cancer and underwent curative treatment consisting of surgery, radiation therapy, and adjuvant chemotherapy between March 2014 and December 2018. He has not experienced any cancer recurrence since then. However, he has been experiencing significant fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) and worries about the possibility of the cancer coming back. He has been feeling anxious and depressed since his diagnosis and has difficulty in focusing on his daily activities. His Fear of Cancer Recurrence Inventory score is 25, indicating that his FCR is clinically significant. He is fluent in Danish and has access to the internet. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to reduce his FCR and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been completely edentulous for the past five years. He has been wearing a conventional full denture for the past two years but he is experiencing difficulty with retention and stability of the denture. He has been complaining of discomfort and sore spots caused by the denture. He is in good general health and has no history of systemic or neurological diseases. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is cooperative and willing to participate in the study. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the single implant-retained mandibular overdenture treatment and has given his written informed consent. He is able to attend all follow-up appointments and is committed to maintaining good oral hygiene. He has no allergies to any medications or materials used in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old Japanese man who has been diagnosed with hypertension and renal dysfunction. He has been on medication for hypertension for the past year, but his blood pressure is not well-controlled. He reports feeling tired and short of breath with minimal exertion. He has a history of smoking and quit 5 years ago. He has no other significant medical history. His blood pressure at the screening visit was 150/90 mmHg, and his eGFR was 40 mL/min/1.73m^2. He is not on dialysis. He is willing to participate in the study and has no history of angioedema. He lives alone and is retired. He enjoys gardening and walking in the park. He is compliant with his medication and is willing to follow the study protocol.

An 68-year-old woman with a history of memory complaints presented to the clinic for evaluation. She has noticed a decline in her memory over the past year, with difficulty remembering names, appointments, and daily tasks. She has no personal or family history of dementia or neurological disorders. She lives alone in her apartment and is independent in her activities of daily living. She is able to manage her medications and finances without assistance. Her MMSE score is 29, and her CDR score is 0.5. She has no sensory defects and is not currently using any psychotropic medications. She has no history of seizures or epilepsy. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her memory and maintain her independence.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who suffered a mild stroke three months ago. He lives alone in his apartment and has been experiencing feelings of social isolation, depression and reduced satisfaction in his daily life since the stroke. He is able to communicate effectively and has a Barthel ADL-index score of 18 out of 20 and MMS score of 27 out of 30. He is able to perform most of his activities of daily living on his own, but requires assistance with some tasks. He is interested in participating in a group intervention program that may help him improve his social participation and overall well-being.

This is a 55 year-old female who was diagnosed with HER2-positive locally recurrent breast cancer. She had undergone neoadjuvant and adjuvant trastuzumab-containing chemotherapy but showed radiological evidence of disease progression while on trastuzumab. Complete radiology and tumor assessment within 4 weeks prior to randomization showed measurable disease per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) guidelines. The patient has undergone up to 2 prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens for treatment of metastatic or locally recurrent breast cancer. She has a negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days prior to randomization and agrees to appropriate method of pregnancy prevention. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction assessment (2-D echocardiogram or Multiple Uptake Gated Acquisition Scan(MUGA) scan) performed within 6 weeks prior to randomization showed a LVEF value > 50%. She has no history of prior Histone Deacetylase(HDAC),Deacetylase(DAC), Heat Shock Protein 90 (HSP90) inhibitors or valproic acid for the treatment of cancer. The patient has no prior chemotherapy or investigational agent within the last 4 weeks prior to randomization. There is no unresolved diarrhea ≥CTCAE (National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) grade 1. The patient has no history of cardiac dysfunction and has no concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions that could cause unacceptable safety risks or compromise compliance with the protocol. She is willing to use a double barrier method of non-hormonal birth control.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who gave birth to her first child 3 months ago. During her pregnancy, she was diagnosed with preeclampsia with a blood pressure of 150/100 mmHg and proteinuria of 600 mg in 24 hours. She was treated with antihypertensive medication and delivered via caesarean section at 36 weeks of gestation. Her blood pressure has been stable since delivery, and she is not taking any medications currently. She has no history of chronic hypertension, kidney disease, diabetes, or any other endocrine disease. Her past medical history is non-significant. She is willing to participate in the study and understand the importance of ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in the post-partum period.

The patient is a 22-year-old African American woman who resides in Detroit, Michigan. She has been diagnosed with moderate to severe persistent asthma and has been prescribed daily controller medications. She has had a history of asthma attacks, which have resulted in emergency room visits. She struggles with medication adherence due to forgetfulness and has been seeking ways to better manage her asthma. She speaks English fluently and owns a cell phone. She currently works part-time at a retail store and attends community college. She has no history of thought disorder, suicidality, or mental retardation. She does not have any other chronic health conditions or pregnancy requiring ongoing medical intervention.

A 52-year-old female patient recently diagnosed with breast cancer is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She underwent a biopsy after a routine mammogram, which revealed a new lesion. She has never been diagnosed with cancer before and has not received any treatment for cancer in the past five years. The patient fasted for at least 6 hours before the blood sample was taken. She has not taken any medication on the day of investigation. Her plasma glucose concentration is normal, measuring below 200 mg/dl. She is eager to contribute to the study and help with the development of a diagnostic indicator for cancer.

A 32-year-old woman visited the gynecologic clinic due to abnormal Pap smear results showing LSIL. She has been sexually active with multiple partners and does not use condoms regularly. She has a history of smoking and has been smoking a pack a day for the past 10 years. She is not currently pregnant and has never had a history of CIN. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the natural history of HPV infection and its correlation with pathologic changes. She has read and understands the informed consent form and is willing to sign it.

A 45-year-old female presented with a history of chronic constipation for the past 6 months. She reported having less than 3 bowel movements per week, and often had to strain with lumpy or hard stools that were difficult to pass. She also experienced a sensation of incomplete evacuation after bowel movements. She denied any abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or blood in her stool. She had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications. The patient underwent a colonoscopy as per the AGA criteria, which revealed no clinically significant findings. Physical exam, 12-lead ECG, and clinical laboratory tests were also performed and showed no abnormalities. She met the protocol criteria for chronic constipation and demonstrated continued constipation during the Pretreatment Period. She was compliant with the IVRS. She did not have a history of loose or watery stools or symptoms of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). She had no structural abnormalities of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract or any disease or condition that could affect GI motility. She had no protocol-excluded or clinically significant medical or surgical history that could confound the study assessments.

56-year-old male with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, who has received standard chemotherapy treatment in the past, but has progressed with new metastatic lesions. Patient has a KPS score of 80%. CT scan shows multiple measurable metastatic tumors per RECIST v1.1 criteria. Patient has acceptable liver function with bilirubin, AST, ALT, and alkaline phosphatase within normal limits. Serum creatinine is within normal limits. Hemoglobin, platelet count, and granulocyte counts are within normal limits. Patient has no history of cardiac disease, myocardial infarction or unstable arrhythmias, and has a normal ECG. Patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to comply with study procedures.

55 year-old male with a recent diagnosis of metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status and is able to provide tumor tissue for the study. The patient has not previously received systemic treatment for advanced disease and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient's organ function is adequate and is willing to use adequate contraception for the course of the study through 120 days after the last dose of study medication or through 180 days after last dose of chemotherapeutic agents. The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis that required oral or IV glucocorticoids to assist with management. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not expecting to conceive or father children prior to 120 days after the last dose of study medication or through 180 days after last dose of chemotherapeutic agents. The patient has not participated in a study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks prior to administration of pembrolizumab. The patient is excluded from the study if the patient has predominantly squamous cell histology NSCLC, is currently receiving study therapy, has received prior systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy for metastatic disease, has received antineoplastic biological therapy, or has had major surgery less than 3 weeks prior to first dose.

A 32-year-old Chinese woman with a BMI of 25 presents with infertility and is seeking treatment at a reproductive center. She has both ovaries and is interested in undergoing IVF/ET. The patient has no history of drug sensitivity to lignocaine, fentanyl, midazolam, diazepam, or pethidine. She has at least three dominant follicles present, and the TUGOR will be performed on both ovaries. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent for the non-inferiority randomized double-blinded trial comparing fentanyl and midazolam vs diazepam and pethidine in terms of pain levels and post-operative side effects of TUGOR.

A 56-year-old male patient was diagnosed with advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma after presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath for several weeks. He has previously undergone one course of combination chemotherapy, which contained a platinum agent, but it failed to cure the disease. The patient has an accessible tumour lesion for a fresh biopsy, which is formalin fixed and paraffin embedded. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has no history of other malignancies except for a curatively treated non-melanoma skin cancer. He has no known brain metastases and has no history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to PF-03446962. The patient has not received concurrent treatment with other anti-cancer therapy or other investigational anticancer agents. He has no cardiovascular findings that could exclude him from the trial. The patient is willing to provide tissue and blood samples for banking and correlative science evaluation.

A 45-year-old male presents with fatigue, generalized weakness and easy bruising for several weeks. Blood tests reveal low red blood cells, low platelets and high white blood cells. A bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has already undergone standard chemotherapy treatment but unfortunately, the disease has relapsed. He is otherwise healthy with no history of any other significant medical conditions. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to participate in clinical trials and has signed informed consent. His ECOG performance status is 1. His clinical laboratory values are within normal limits. The patient has no CNS involvement by leukemia and no uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses. He agrees to use acceptable contraceptive methods for the duration of the study and for at least one month after the last drug administration.

A 56-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetic nephropathy has been on hemodialysis for the last 6 months. She is scheduled to receive her first kidney transplant from a deceased donor. The estimated donor organ cold ischemia time is less than 30 hours, and she meets the BMI criteria of less than 40 based on dry weight. She has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. The patient has no history of active bacterial infection, malignancy, or participation in an investigational drug or medical device study within the past 30 days. She has no donor-specific antibodies or positive cross-matches requiring desensitization prior to transplantation. She has not received a kidney preserved by normothermic pulsatile machine perfusion. The patient is eligible for the study and can begin receiving the study drug within 30 hours after restoration of blood flow to the engrafted kidney.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of Type 1 Diabetes for the past 4 years presents with well-controlled blood sugar levels. She has been on a stable treatment regimen for the past 6 months, which includes insulin injections, and has not experienced any significant changes in her treatment regimen. Her HbA1c levels are consistently under 7.0%. She has tested positive for GAD65 auto-antibodies and has a peak C-peptide level of >100 pM following IV injection of 1 mg glucagon. Her BMI is 23 kg/m2, and she is willing to maintain her current doses/regimens of vitamins and dietary supplements throughout the study. She has no history of recent infections or tuberculosis and has tested negative for Hep B surface antigen (HBsAg), Hep C virus (HCV), and HIV. She has no history of foot, leg, or decubitus ulcers and is not currently on any immunosuppressive treatment. She has no history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions, asthma requiring systemic corticosteroid therapy, or coronary intervention within the past 12 months. She has no history of congestive heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV) or a coronary event within the past 12 months. She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, recently delivered, or breastfeeding. She has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years and has not received a live (attenuated) vaccine within the past 3 months.

A 56-year-old male with a diagnosis of metastatic colon cancer complains of persistent abdominal pain and constipation. He underwent surgery for colon cancer 2 years ago and received chemotherapy for 6 months. However, his cancer has metastasized to his liver and lungs. He has previously been treated with FOLFIRI and FOLFOX but has not responded well to the treatments. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical or surgical history. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and is still able to work full-time. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including a creatinine clearance of 65 ml/min. His most recent CT scan shows multiple liver and lung metastases.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been undergoing hemodialysis for end-stage renal disease for the last 3 years. He has a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hyperphosphatemia. The patient is currently taking a phosphate binder medication and has been on a stable regimen for the past month. His serum phosphate level has been above 3.0 mmol/L for the past 2 months. The patient is willing to abstain from taking any phosphate binder or oral magnesium-, oral aluminum- or oral iron-containing products and preparations other than the study medication. He is willing to have at least three meals per day if required to take >6000 mg/day of fermagate. The patient is able to comply with the study procedures and medication and has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 44-year-old female is admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory failure. She has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been a smoker for the past 20 years. She was intubated and is currently on pressure support ventilation with a sedation agitation score (SAS) of 3. She has an arterial line in place to monitor her blood pressure. The patient is alert and oriented and able to communicate with the healthcare team. She has no contraindications to insertion of a nasogastric tube, no history of heart or lung transplantation, no neuromuscular disease, and is not currently being treated with neuromuscular blockers. Her mean arterial blood pressure is stable without the need for vasopressors or inotropes. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and her next of kin is available to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. She has no history of ocular inflammation, previous intraocular surgery or age-related macular degeneration. She has controlled hypertension and no other significant medical history. She is scheduled to undergo uncomplicated cataract surgery at UNC and may be eligible for a clinical trial studying the effect of nepafenac ophthalmic suspension 0.1% in preventing post-operative macular swelling. She will undergo pre-operative Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) vision measurement and pre-operative OCT testing in both eyes. Depending on the results, she may be randomized into two groups. Group 1 will receive standard post-operative cataract management, while Group 2 will receive standard post-operative cataract management plus topical nepafenac for one month. Post-operative macular thickness will be studied by analyzing the visual acuity and OCT measurements at two months post-surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer a year ago and underwent external-beam radiotherapy as a treatment. However, he has been experiencing erectile dysfunction (ED) since then. He is currently in a stable relationship with his wife and they have sexual intercourse on average once a week. He is willing to participate in the study and make regular attempts at sexual intercourse during the study period. He has not used any other ED treatment for at least four weeks before the initial dose of the study drug. He has no history of pelvic surgery or penile implant, and no evidence of clinically significant renal insufficiency or hepatobiliary disease. He does not have any significant cardiac or neurological conditions that could interfere with the study. He is willing to provide informed consent and comply with study instructions.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain during physical exertion. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has undergone a coronary artery bypass graft surgery 5 years ago. Her echocardiogram shows an aortic valve area of 0.8 cm², mean gradient of 45 mmHg, and an ejection fraction of 55%. Her computed tomography (CT) scan shows aortic annulus diameter of 23mm. She has been deemed high-risk for surgical aortic valve replacement due to her age and co-morbidities. Her STS score is 10%. She has not undergone any percutaneous coronary or peripheral interventional procedures in the past 30 days. She has no active infections, bleeding disorders, or other significant medical conditions that could preclude her from participating in the study. She has been informed of the nature of the study, agrees to its provisions, and has provided written informed consent. She and her treating physician agree that she will return for all required post-procedure follow-up visits.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 3 years ago. He has undergone treatment with lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, but his disease has relapsed. His current symptoms include fatigue, bone pain, and difficulty sleeping. He is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His labs show: creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, ALT 25 U/L, AST 20 U/L, albumin 4.0 g/dL, calcium 9.2 mg/dL, hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, platelets 150,000/mcL, white blood cells 4,500/mcL. The patient has not previously received venetoclax or pomalidomide. He has not had any stem cell transplant. The patient's t(11;14) status is negative.

A 65-year-old man was recently diagnosed with heart failure and left ventricular systolic function. He also has a history of metabolic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking medication to manage his heart failure symptoms, but still experiences exercise intolerance and occasional congestion. He has not had any recent major systemic diseases or active malignancies, and is estimated to have a life expectancy of over three months. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 50-year-old male with a history of peripheral artery disease in his left leg presented to the clinic complaining of intermittent claudication and pain in his left calf. He has been diagnosed with PAD for the last 3 years and has been taking aspirin and clopidogrel daily. He has no other medical conditions, no allergies, and does not smoke. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance medical research and improve his own condition.

A 28-year-old woman with a diagnosis of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) has been experiencing progressive and symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas (PN). She has had the condition since childhood and has been receiving treatment for many years. The patient has exhausted all available approved therapies as appropriate for NF1 with inoperable progressive/symptomatic PN. The PN is inoperable, which means that it cannot be surgically removed without the risk of substantial morbidity. The patient has been experiencing pain and discomfort in the affected area. She has no further treatment options and is not eligible for clinical trials. She has a body surface area (BSA) of 1.65 m2 and is able to swallow whole capsules. Her cardiac function is normal, and she has no history of heart disease. She has normal blood pressure and has no ophthalmological conditions. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no evidence of any other significant clinical disorder or laboratory finding that, as judged by the treating physician, makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the study. She is interested in participating in this intermediate access protocol and has provided a signed informed consent prior to any protocol-specific procedures.

25-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 22.5, non-smoker, and non-drinker interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has no history of hepatic, renal, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, epileptic, hematological or psychiatric condition, nor hypo or hypertension requiring pharmacological treatment. He has not been hospitalized in the past eight weeks, nor has he participated in any experimental trial or used any experimental drug in the past six months. He has not donated or lost more than 450 mL of blood in the past three months, nor has he consumed grapefruit or any food or beverages containing grapefruit in the past seven days. He has read and understood the nature and objective of the trial, including the risks and adverse effects, and has agreed to cooperate with the investigator and to act according to the requirements of the whole assay.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) for the past 2 years. He has been on guideline directed heart failure therapy including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and aldosterone antagonists for the past 6 months. He has a BMI of 35 kg/m². The patient has not experienced any major cardiovascular surgery or stroke in the past 90 days. He has not had acute decompensated heart failure requiring IV diuretics within the past 12 weeks. The patient has a history of mild liver dysfunction but has not had any significant hepatic, pancreatic, or biliary tract disorders. He has never been diagnosed with malignancy and has had age-appropriate cancer screenings. The patient's LVEF is 30% and NT-ProBNP levels are 500 pg/mL. The patient is willing to follow contraceptive requirements as he is married but does not plan to have children.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is currently 9 weeks pregnant. She presents to the emergency department with a chief complaint of vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 days and they have been progressively getting worse. She denies any fever, chills, or nausea. The patient reports that she has had a previous pregnancy that ended in a miscarriage at 12 weeks, and she is concerned that this may be happening again. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She has no known drug allergies. On physical examination, the patient appears uncomfortable but is in no acute distress. Her vital signs are stable. Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the lower quadrants. Pelvic examination shows a closed cervical os with no visible blood or discharge. Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an intrauterine pregnancy consistent with 9 weeks gestation. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets all inclusion criteria for the study. She is able to provide written informed consent and speaks English fluently.

A 6-month-old male infant who was born prematurely at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 900 grams, and has had a complicated neonatal course. He had a prolonged hospital stay due to respiratory distress syndrome, patent ductus arteriosus, and sepsis. He was discharged on home oxygen therapy and has been readmitted twice for respiratory distress. He was recently diagnosed with invasive candidiasis and has been receiving fluconazole therapy for 2 weeks without improvement. He now requires central line placement for total parenteral nutrition and has been enrolled in this clinical trial to receive posaconazole therapy for his invasive fungal infection.

28-week gestational age male preterm infant born via cesarean section due to maternal preeclampsia. The infant was intubated at birth and started on prophylactic antibiotics. The infant was transferred to the NICU and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. On day 2 of life, the infant developed sepsis and was started on empiric antibiotics. The central line was placed for total parental nutrition, and a non-impregnated polyurethane umbilical venous catheter (UVC) was inserted. The infant continued on antibiotics for the next 7 days. On day 10 of life, the infant was randomized to receive an AgION-impregnated UVC. The catheter remained in place for 14 days. During this time, the infant did not develop any signs of infection or sepsis. The infant was discharged home on day 40 of life, weighing 1.5 kg.

The patient is a healthy pregnant woman aged between 18 to 45 years, in her third trimester of pregnancy, and expecting to give birth to a healthy single full-term infant. She has an Hb level more than 105 g/L and an omnivorous diet. She has an intention to breastfeed for at least four months, and not more than one bottle or 10% of total milk intake daily as formula. She has no intention to take multivitamin supplements, DHA supplements, lutein supplements, or any combination of the aforementioned after giving birth except for iodine and iron. She has tested seronegative for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C at screening. She is willing and able to participate in all scheduled visits, adhere to the study plan, laboratory tests, and all other study-related procedures according to the clinical protocol. She has provided a personally signed and dated informed consent to participate in the study and to adhere to all study procedures, including the assessments done to the infant, indicating that she has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the trial and that she understood and accepted these, prior to admission to the study.

A 48-year-old male with a history of hypertension and aortic valve replacement 6 years ago due to aortic stenosis, presents with fever and chills for the past 3 days. He has also been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and a dry cough. On examination, he has a temperature of 38.3°C, a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. A new holosystolic murmur is heard on cardiac auscultation. Blood cultures are drawn, and the patient is started on empiric antibiotic therapy for suspected infective endocarditis (IE). Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) reveals a large vegetation (15 mm) on the aortic valve with no evidence of perivalvular extension. The modified Duke criteria confirm the diagnosis of left-sided IE. The patient is eligible for the EARLY study, and after providing informed consent, he is randomized to the early surgical strategy arm.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse for the past 15 years. He presents to the hospital with jaundice, ascites, and confusion for the past 3 days. His laboratory studies show elevated bilirubin, elevated liver enzymes, and evidence of coagulopathy. The patient is diagnosed with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) and hepatic encephalopathy (HE) grade 2. The patient is currently on lactulose therapy for HE management. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are being treated with medication. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol on a daily basis. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets all the eligibility criteria.

This is a 50 year old male with no significant past medical history who reports occasional morning fatigue and mild difficulty with concentration. He has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and does not smoke or use any tobacco products. He is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription medications or drugs of abuse. He has not worked irregular day and night hours, regular night work, or rotating shift work for the past six months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of Vitamin C to counteract morning cardiovascular risk markers.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe arthritis pain in her left knee for the past two years. She has tried several non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), but her pain has continued to worsen. She has decided to undergo total knee arthroplasty surgery at Hahnemann University Hospital to alleviate her pain and improve her mobility. She has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication to control it. She does not have a history of substance abuse or chronic pain. She is currently not pregnant or nursing. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to follow the study restrictions. She is ASA physical status II.

The patient is a 72-year-old male with a history of smoking for 40 years. He has been experiencing occasional leg cramping and numbness when walking for the past year. He is otherwise healthy, with no known cardiovascular or neurological disease. He is able to walk independently and has no difficulty with activities of daily living. The patient has been recommended for screening for peripheral arterial disease and has agreed to participate in this study. The patient is able to give informed consent and can lie supine for at least 15 minutes. The patient has not had any prior laboratory studies showing non-compressible vessels with an ABI greater than 1.3 on either side.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with symptomatic heart failure due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF<35%). He has undergone cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) implantation recently. He is a retired engineer and lives alone. He complains of shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty with activities of daily living. He reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is taking angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, beta-blockers, and diuretics. He does not smoke or drink. He has a BMI of 29. He is able to perform a peak exercise test and willing to give informed consent. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or angina pectoris symptoms limiting exercise tolerance. His imaging quality is reliable. He is not taking calcium channel blockers (CCBs).

This clinical trial is not applicable to individual patient participation as it is a cluster randomized controlled trial targeting Grade 8 high school students in South Africa, their educators, and parents/caregivers. The trial aims to develop and evaluate a multi-faceted school-based intervention to prevent intimate partner violence among Grade 8 high school students in South Africa. Therefore, the trial does not involve individual patient participation or enrollment.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is slightly overweight with a BMI of 26 kg/m2. She is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She has a desk job and does not engage in regular exercise. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of calorie restriction on metabolism in non-obese individuals. She does not have a history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, eating disorders, or any other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or on any medications or supplements that may interfere with the study. She is a never-smoker and does not have any magnetic metallic objects in her body. She is willing to adhere to the strict dietary restrictions and the data collection schedule required by the study. She is excited to participate in research that may contribute to the understanding of the long-term effects of calorie restriction on metabolism and overall health.

55 year old male with a history of colorectal cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. He now presents with a CT scan that shows retroperitoneal lymph node metastases below the level of the renal vein. The patient is in good general health and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no history of heart disease, epilepsy, or mental disorder. His blood work meets the criteria for participation in the study. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has struggled with attention and focus for as long as she can remember. She has difficulty finishing tasks and following through with plans. She often feels restless and fidgety and has trouble sitting still for long periods of time. She has a history of impulsivity and has made impulsive decisions that have had negative consequences in her personal and professional life. She is currently employed as an administrative assistant but has had difficulty keeping jobs in the past due to her inability to stay focused and organized. She has never been formally diagnosed with ADHD but has been wondering if it could be the cause of her struggles. She has no history of significant medical or psychiatric problems and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if she meets the criteria for ADHD and to receive a formal diagnosis and potential treatment options.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 18 and 60. They do not have a history of insomnia, narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, abnormal sleeping patterns, or restless leg syndrome. They have not used any psychoactive medications or medications that may affect brain function within the past two weeks (four weeks for fluoxetine). They do not have a current or past diagnosis of a psychiatric disorder, substance use disorder (except for nicotine/caffeine), or alcoholism/dependence. They do not have major medical problems that can impact brain function, including problems of the CNS, cardiovascular disease, metabolic, autoimmune, or endocrine disorders. They have not experienced head trauma with loss of consciousness for more than 30 minutes. The patient has negative test results for controlled substances and is not pregnant. They do not have any ferromagnetic objects in the body that are contraindicated for MRI of the head and do not have a fear of enclosed spaces. The patient is able to lie comfortably flat on their back for up to 3 hours in the MRI scanner and does not weigh over 250 kg. They have not consumed alcohol on the day of the MRI.

33 yo M with no significant past medical history, currently taking no medications and not using any psychoactive or psychotropic substances, interested in participating in a study exploring the effects of osteopathic cranial techniques on the nervous system. The patient reports having slept for at least 6 hours the night before the experiment and denies any recent headaches or use of nicotine or alcohol in the past 24-12 hours, respectively. The patient is willing to undergo EEG recording during the study interventions and understands the study procedures and potential risks.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with primary colon cancer. The tumor measures 5 cm and is located in the ascending colon. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or previous abdominal surgery. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is scheduled to undergo a tumor resection procedure. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about how colon cancer affects muscle gene expression, body composition, muscle function, and muscle metabolism.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis due to alcohol abuse. She has been on the waiting list for liver transplant for the past 6 months. The patient has a history of heavy alcohol consumption for over 10 years, but has been sober for the past 4 months. She complains of abdominal discomfort and fatigue. She has lost 10 pounds in the past month. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and she takes lisinopril. She is not currently taking any other medications. She lives alone and works as a teacher. She reports occasional episodes of diarrhea and flatulence. She has never taken probiotics before. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

52 yo M with relapsed multiple myeloma, having received prior therapy and now indicated for 2nd or 3rd line Lenalidomide/Dexamethasone (Len/Dex) treatment according to the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC). The patient has provided voluntary written informed consent to participate in this multicentre, prospective, observational, open-label, single arm, post-marketing study, which aims to assess the real-life safety of Len/Dex in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (rrMM). The study will evaluate adverse events of special interest, including infections, gastrointestinal events, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, and thromboembolism. The study will also assess Len/Dex safety and effectiveness by patient frailty groups. The patient is eligible for the study as he is 18 years or older and meets the inclusion criteria. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the active substance or any of the excipients. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to comply with the contraceptive measures stated in the SmPC. The patient is not participating in any other clinical trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been struggling with obesity for the past 5 years. He is 180 cm tall and his weight is 110 kg, giving him a body mass index of 34.0 kg/m2. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, and is currently taking medication for both conditions. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has not been able to achieve sustained weight loss. He has no history of diabetes or other serious medical conditions. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him achieve long-term weight loss and improve his overall health.

The patient is a 50-year-old Caucasian male who presented with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of coronary artery disease and underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement in the past. He is currently on aspirin, clopidogrel, and a statin. He has been compliant with his medications and has not had any major adverse events. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has no other significant medical history. His current complaint suggests a possible coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR). His recent angiography shows 2 ISR lesions, one in the right coronary artery and the other in the left anterior descending artery. The lesions are <35mm in length and have a reference vessel diameter of >2.5mm. His serum creatinine level is within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

A 60-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 4 years ago. He experiences tremors and stiffness in his hands, difficulty in initiating movements, and trouble with balance. He is currently taking carbidopa-levodopa, which provides some relief from his symptoms. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to understand the changes that occur in the brains of people with Parkinson's disease. He is willing to undergo different ways of brain imaging and brain chemical testing to contribute to the study's findings. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to visit the National Institutes of Health Clinical Center every 18 months or 3 years for up to 9 years.

A 54-year-old female, who works as a bank teller, presents to the emergency department with severe right upper quadrant pain that started a few hours ago. She has never experienced this type of pain before. She also complains of nausea and vomiting. She denies any significant past medical history, except for a diagnosis of hypertension that is well controlled on medication. She has never had surgery before. On physical examination, she has tenderness in the right upper quadrant and a positive Murphy's sign. Her laboratory investigations show leukocytosis and elevated liver enzymes. An abdominal ultrasound confirms the presence of gallstones and signs of acute cholecystitis. She is informed that she needs surgery for this condition and may be eligible for a clinical trial that aims to compare the outcomes of patients with AC who receive accelerated surgery (i.e., as soon as possible with a goal of surgery within 6 hours of diagnosis) with those who receive standard care. She is interested in participating in the trial and meets the eligibility criteria. She provides written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who recently had an incomplete colonoscopy due to difficult anatomy. She is interested in completing the procedure to ensure her colorectal health is optimal. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is able to provide informed consent and is currently hemodynamically stable.

The patient is a 28-year-old African American woman who was diagnosed with HIV two years ago. She has a history of alcohol abuse and reports consuming more than seven drinks per week and three or more drinks in a single occasion in the past three months. She has also engaged in unprotected vaginal and anal sex in the last 12 months. She is currently not pregnant and does not have any active mental health issues that would prevent her from participating in the computer-delivered brief intervention. She can understand English and read at a 5th-grade level. She has a phone and can receive text messages.

The patient is a 35-year-old Pakistani woman who was diagnosed with head and neck cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy at Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi. She is currently in remission and is interested in participating in the study to evaluate her resilience and quality of life after cancer treatment. She is fluent in both Urdu and English and is willing to complete the questionnaire and other assessments for the study. She has no other physical or psychiatric illnesses and is not taking any anti-depressants. The patient resides in Pakistan and is a Pakistani national.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who lives alone in her apartment. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, and she is taking medication to manage these conditions. She enjoys going for walks in the park and gardening, but recently she has noticed that she is becoming more tired and her balance is not as good as it used to be. She is worried that she may fall and not be able to get up. She is looking for ways to maintain her independence and improve her overall health. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how technology can help her monitor her health and provide personalized recommendations to improve her functional ability. She is able to walk independently, but sometimes she needs support from a cane. She has a basic understanding of technology and is willing to learn how to use the online monitoring platform. She is excited to have the opportunity to work with a health care professional to develop a personalized plan to promote a healthier lifestyle.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who underwent surgery for breast cancer six months ago. She experienced a sharp, burning sensation in her right breast and upper arm, which she describes as a constant pain that has persisted since the surgery. She reports difficulty sleeping and performing daily activities due to the pain. The patient has no known allergies and her medical history is unremarkable. She is not pregnant and does not have diabetes. The pain is localized to the breast and upper arm, and she has not received any other treatment for this pain. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the 8% capsaicin patch.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with malignant melanoma with brain metastases. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. She is currently experiencing headaches, dizziness, and blurred vision, which prompted her to seek medical attention. Imaging studies have revealed 2 brain lesions, confirmed to be BRAF V600 mutated. The largest of the two lesions is approximately 3 cm in diameter. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80 and has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has no clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities. The patient has not received prior treatment with a BRAF inhibitor or MEK inhibitor, and has not had any systemic anti-cancer treatment in the last 2 weeks. The patient meets all laboratory requirements and is not currently taking any prohibited medication. The patient has no history of Hepatitis B or C virus infection, and no history or current evidence of cardiovascular risk or retinal vein occlusion or central serous retinopathy. The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease or active pneumonitis.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with a pituitary adenoma. He has been experiencing headaches, vision problems, and fatigue for several months. The patient has no family history of endocrine tumors. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help researchers better understand the genetics of this disease and potentially develop new treatment options.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who has been experiencing heartburn and acid reflux for the past year. He has tried over-the-counter antacids and proton pump inhibitors but has not seen significant improvement. He underwent upper endoscopy which revealed the presence of Barrett's esophagus. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has a BMI of 32 and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his condition and to potentially avoid the risk of stricture formation associated with thermal ablation. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who recently suffered from a transient ischemic attack (TIA) and is currently undergoing medical management for his condition. He presents with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. He is currently taking medications for his conditions including aspirin, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has no history of allergy to vitamin supplements. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of vitamin supplements on preventing stroke and other major atherothromboembolic vascular events, dementia, and depression in patients with recent stroke or TIA. He is willing to take the study medication and has no plans to take any other vitamin supplements during the study period. He is geographically accessible for follow-up and provides written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing dryness, irritation, and a gritty feeling in her eyes. She has been using artificial tear products for the past few months but has not found them to be effective in relieving her symptoms. She has a history of mild nearsightedness and wears glasses for distance vision. She has not undergone any recent eye surgeries, and she does not wear contact lenses. She has not experienced any recent eye infections or inflammation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of Refresh Optive® Gel Drops in treating her dry eye disease.

55 year old man with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic prostate cancer with positive bone scan and elevated PSA levels who has failed androgen deprivation therapy.
