The patient has no measurable disease but has documented osseous progression. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. The patient has not undergone chemotherapy for prostate cancer and has not received any investigational immunotherapy. The patient has not received any systemic corticosteroids for at least 4 weeks prior to the start of the clinical trial. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease except for a resolved case of psoriasis. The patient has no history or radiologic evidence of central nervous system metastases. The patient has no significant cardiovascular disease, HIV, or other immunodeficiency disorder. The patient has a normal laboratory profile including an ANC ≥ 1500/μL, Bilirubin < 1.5 x ULN, Hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL, PSA ≥ 2 ng/mL, Platelets > 100,000/μL, AST and ALT < 2.5 x ULN, Creatinine clearance ≥ 60mL/min, and Testosterone < 50 ng/dL. The patient has not undergone prior treatment with ipilimumab or prior CD137 agonist or CTLA 4 inhibitor or agonist. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception for the duration of study participation, and for three months after discontinuing therapy.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of smoking for the past 15 years and has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She is married to a 50-year-old man who also smokes and has a history of heart disease. Both of them are concerned about their health and want to quit smoking. They have been married for 10 years and have two children. The patient has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. They are both fluent in English and are willing to participate in the family consultation intervention. There are no signs of mania or psychosis in either partner, and the patient is not pregnant. The patient is excited to participate in this study and hopes that this intervention will help her quit smoking for good and improve her overall health.

This is a 32-year-old female who presents with complaints of jaw pain and stiffness, headaches, and teeth clenching. She reports that her symptoms have been present for the past 6 months and have been progressively worsening. She also reports a history of bruxism and lip biting. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation at the temporomandibular joint and increased muscle tension in the masseter, anterior temporalis, sternocleidomastoid, and upper trapezius muscles. The patient has a Helkimo index of III and is diagnosed with myogenic temporomandibular disorder. She has no history of surgery or trauma in the orofacial region or any systemic or degenerative diseases. The patient is not currently undergoing any odontological, psychological, or physical therapy treatments.

34-year-old Caucasian female G2P1 at 9 weeks of gestational age presented to the obstetrician's office with vaginal bleeding and mild cramps for the past 24 hours. The bleeding started suddenly and was bright red in color with clots. She had no fever, chills, or abdominal pain. She had a history of an uneventful pregnancy and delivery for her first child. She has no known medical conditions and her only medication is a prenatal vitamin. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has a BMI of 25 and exercises regularly. She has no history of assisted reproductive technology or previous treatment with progesterone. She has a singleton intrauterine pregnancy, and the gestational age was confirmed by ultrasound at her first prenatal visit. She has no significant medical or surgical history, and there is no family history of pregnancy-related complications. She has no known allergies.

The patient is a 48-year-old Japanese woman who was diagnosed with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) three months ago. She has not undergone balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) or pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) due to the organized thrombosis localized in the peripheral regions. She has been treated with anticoagulation agents for the past 90 days. She has no history of allergies or any other medical conditions. She is not pregnant and uses appropriate contraceptive methods. Her WHO functional class is III, and her 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) measured during the screening period was 325 m. Her resting mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) is 32 mmHg, pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) is 12 mmHg, and resting pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is 450 dyn*sec/cm5. She has no known factor or disease that may interfere with treatment compliance or full participation in the study.

A 60 year old man with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease was referred to the hospital for open-heart surgery. He is scheduled for a mediastinotomy incision to access the heart. He has never had a sternotomy before and has no known allergies to skin adhesives or keloid formation. During the physical examination, he was found to be in stable condition with no signs of infection or inflammation. The patient has also been advised about the possibility of experiencing pain, redness, swelling, and infections post-surgery. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and to undergo the 3M TM S Surgical Skin Closure System.

A 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of glioblastoma (Grade 4 astrocytic tumour) and MGMT promoter methylation will be eligible for this clinical trial. The patient should have a Karnofsky performance status of ≥ 70% and should be able to use intranasal administration. The patient should have histological material available for the possibility of revising histological verification. The patient should not have a history of hypersensitivity to TMZ or any of its excipients, inherited bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy with the risk of bleeding, or suffered a stroke according to the results of the first MRI upon admission. The patient should not be currently receiving other anticancer agents and should have fully recovered from the effects of prior chemotherapy (haematological and bone marrow suppression effects). The patient should not have received more than 1 cycle of Irinotecan and Temozolomide as previous relapse therapy. The patient should be willing to abide by the study protocol and cooperate fully with the investigator or designee.

A 14-year-old male patient presents with a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis (SAR) for the past two years. He reports experiencing nasal congestion exacerbations during the study season, which significantly impact his daily activities. The patient has a positive skin prick test response to an appropriate seasonal allergen at the first visit. He is currently experiencing clinical symptoms at the screening and baseline visits. The patient has not had a severe local reaction or anaphylaxis to skin testing. He has not had an upper respiratory tract or sinus infection that required antibiotic therapy within the last 14 days before the screening visit. The patient has not used any drug in an investigational protocol within the last 30 days before the screening visit. He is not participating in any other clinical studies, nor is he part of the staff personnel directly involved with this study. The patient is not a family member (parent, spouse, or sibling) of the investigational study staff. He is not a female subject who is breast-feeding, pregnant, or intends to become pregnant. The patient has not been previously randomized into this study, and he does not have a family member (parent, spouse, or sibling) currently enrolled in this study.

Patient is a 28-year-old female nurse who works in a busy hospital in the United States. She has been experiencing high levels of stress due to the demands of the job and the COVID-19 pandemic. Her BMI is 25, BP: 120/80, HR: 80/min. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in finding new ways to manage her stress and improve her overall well-being.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years. He has been treated with insulin for the past 6 months. The patient has a history of hypoglycaemic episodes, with one severe episode in the last year, requiring external assistance for recovery. He has moderate renal impairment, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate value of 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The patient has known hypoglycaemic unawareness, as indicated by the investigator according to Clarke's questionnaire question 8 at screening. He has been treated with basal insulin for the past 3 months, along with metformin and a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor. The patient's HbA1c level is 8.5% (69 mmol/mol) at screening. His body mass index is 30 kg/m^2. The patient has no history of uncontrolled or potentially unstable diabetic retinopathy or maculopathy. He is willing to wear a sensor on the back of his upper arm to monitor his blood sugar level during the study. The patient is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period.

42-year-old male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B 2 years ago. The patient was started on antiviral therapy (Tenofovir) and has been compliant with the treatment regimen. The patient has had no significant side effects from the medication. The patient's past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with Lisinopril. The patient denies any history of alcohol or substance abuse. The patient's viral load has been undetectable for the past 12 months, and the patient has been adhering to the APASL guideline. The patient is interested in participating in a study to investigate off-treatment sustained response in chronic hepatitis B patients and is willing to undergo regular follow-up visits to monitor for any potential relapse.

Patient is a 70-year-old man who has not engaged in any resistance exercise in the last 12 months. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, or cognitive malfunctioning. He does not have severe knee or hip problems. The patient is interested in participating in a 12-week exercise intervention to improve his rapid force production and functional capacity.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe knee pain and stiffness for the past year. She reports that the pain is worse with activity and has been limiting her ability to perform daily tasks such as walking, climbing stairs, and getting in and out of her car. She has tried conservative treatment measures such as physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections, but has not experienced significant improvement. She is interested in undergoing total knee replacement surgery to alleviate her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She has no history of hardware involving her hip, knee, or ankle. She is able to walk independently with the use of a cane, but reports significant difficulty with stairs and uneven surfaces. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would preclude her from undergoing surgery.

A 42-year-old woman has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia, which causes her pain and fatigue. Despite her condition, she works full-time in an office job and has been struggling to manage her symptoms while at work. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to provide support and resources for workers with chronic physical health conditions. She is able to read and speak English fluently and is available to attend group workshops after working hours. She is not planning to retire or make any major career changes in the next 12 months.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been smoking for the past 10 years. She smokes approximately 10 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking twice in the past three years but was unsuccessful. She has no history of major psychiatric disorder or chronic pain syndromes. She is motivated to quit smoking and is interested in participating in a non-invasive smoking cessation program using self-administered auricular acupressure. She is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study and has no known allergies to plaster.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain and digestive issues. She has been advised by her gastroenterologist to undergo a gastroscopy procedure under sedation with propofol. The patient is generally healthy, with no history of coagulation disorders or nose bleeding tendency, congestive heart failure, severe aortic or mitral stenosis, cardiac surgery, acute myocardial infarction, acute arrhythmia, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has no history of increased intracranial pressure, and her ASA score is below III. The patient is not currently experiencing any mouth, nose, or throat infection, nor does she have a fever. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is not in need of an emergency procedure. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the feasibility and safety of high-flow nasal cannula oxygenation in reducing hypoxia during the gastroscopy procedure.

60-year-old male with a history of severe tricuspid regurgitation confirmed by echocardiography. He is currently experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs, which are classified as NYHA Class III. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 45%, and has been treated for coronary artery disease and mitral regurgitation for the past 30 days. The patient has undergone a 6-minute walk test and has covered a distance of 70 meters. The Heart Team, consisting of an interventional cardiologist, cardiothoracic surgeon, and heart failure cardiologist, has deemed him an acceptable candidate for the Cardiovalve System. The patient has no significant intracardiac shunt or congenital structural heart disease, and has not experienced a cerebrovascular event in the past 3 months. The patient's systolic pulmonary arterial pressure is 45 mmHg, and he has no known life-threatening non-cardiac disease that would limit his life expectancy to less than one year. The patient has no history of mitral/tricuspid endocarditis or primary coagulopathy or platelet disorder, and has an eGFR of 65 ml/min/1.73m². The patient is not on dialysis, has no contraindication or known allergy to the device's components or anti-coagulation therapy with vitamin K antagonists, and is not currently unsuitable for implantation because of thrombosis of the lower venous system or presence of a vena cava filter. The patient has no contraindication against a transesophageal echo (TEE) during the procedure, and has not suffered from an acute myocardial infarction (AMI) within the past month. The patient does not have hepatic insufficiency, is not a female patient of child-bearing potential, and does not have psychiatric or behavioral disease including known alcohol or drug abuser that is likely to impair compliance with protocol. The patient has not required antibiotic treatment within the last 48 hours, and his cardiac anatomy is deemed suitable for the Cardiovalve Implant.

A 35-year-old Hispanic woman who has been diagnosed with psoriasis for 5 years presented to the dermatology clinic. She has tried various treatments including topical corticosteroids, vitamin D analogs, and phototherapy with limited success. She has difficulty attending regular follow-up appointments due to her busy work schedule and long commute. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her better manage her psoriasis. She has access to a smartphone and uses WhatsApp to communicate with her family and friends. She is fluent in both English and Spanish. She is excited about the prospect of receiving individualized communication from her healthcare provider and being able to take and upload pictures of her skin for remote assessment. She is willing to commit to the 3-month study period and is happy to provide informed consent.

A 46-year-old female of Caucasian ethnicity presented to the oncology clinic with a recent diagnosis of advanced ovarian cancer. She had a history of endometriosis and had undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 5 years ago. The pathology report revealed clear cell carcinoma of the ovary, and the patient underwent adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She was disease-free for 4 years and then developed recurrent ovarian cancer with multiple peritoneal metastases. The patient received several lines of chemotherapy, including bevacizumab, but her disease continued to progress. She was then referred for this clinical trial and met the eligibility criteria. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and measurable lesions by RECIST v1.1. Her laboratory studies showed adequate organ function, and she is able to take oral medications. She is a non-smoker and has no significant past medical history other than the previous cancer diagnosis. She has no history of HIV or hepatitis B or C. She has no active autoimmune disease or a known history of MDS or AML. She has not previously received treatment with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent or a known PARP inhibitor. She has a heart-rate corrected QT interval (QTc) of 420 msec at screening.

Patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease stage III on the Hoehn and Yahr scale. He has been on an optimized oral therapy regimen that includes levodopa/carbidopa inhibitors and a direct acting oral dopamine agonist for the past 6 months. The patient has been experiencing off events despite the optimized oral therapy and has been receiving apomorphine subcutaneous injections for rescue therapy for the past 4 months. He has been receiving an average of 3 doses per day over the past week. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol dependency in the past year and has not been treated with experimental agents in the past month. He has no clinically significant disease of cardiovascular, hematologic, hepatic, renal, metabolic, respiratory, gastrointestinal or endocrinological systems or neoplasm within the past 3 months. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing fevers above 38.5°C for the past two weeks. She has also noticed fatigue and a loss of appetite during this time. She has visited her primary care physician and undergone standard check-up, which did not reveal any definitive diagnosis. Her CRP level was found to be 7mg/L. She has no known history of immunosuppression or cancer and is not currently taking any medications. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and is able to provide written consent.

58-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with decreased vision in her left eye for the past 3 months. She reports no significant ocular history or previous intraocular surgery. On examination, her visual acuity is 20/200 in the left eye with a stage III idiopathic macular hole according to the classification proposed by Gass. No evidence of severe cataract or exudative age-related macular degeneration is found. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the anatomical and functional outcomes of different dyes used for internal limiting membrane peeling in macular hole surgery.

This clinical trial is focused on newborn infants born to women residing in rural northern Bangladesh in the Gaibandha/Rangpur area. The trial is nested within the JiVitA-1 maternal supplementation study, which involves under 5-weekly pregnancy surveillance conducted by village-based field staff. The trial aims to determine whether a 50,000 IU oral dose of vitamin A delivered to newborn infants within the first days of life reduces six-month infant mortality by at least 15%. The trial will also evaluate whether the survival impact of newborn vitamin A dosing is modified by concurrent weekly, routine maternal vitamin A or beta-carotene supplementation during pregnancy through three months postpartum, gestational age, and birth size. Infants born to women enrolled in the maternal supplementation trial, alive and less than 30 days of age during a newborn dosing visit are eligible to participate in this trial.

A 60-year-old male presents with chronic knee pain and limited mobility. He has a history of non-inflammatory degenerative joint disease, including osteoarthritis, and has tried various non-surgical treatments with no improvement. He is a suitable candidate for a UKA procedure using CORI and a S+N Knee compatible implant system. He is considered skeletally mature and is willing to consent to and follow the study visit schedule. He plans to be available through one year postoperative follow-up. He understands the language used in the Informed Consent Form. He does not have a history of post-traumatic arthritis, active infection or sepsis, morbid obesity, or neuromuscular disorders that would pre-empt his ability or willingness to participate in the study. However, he has a history of moderate renal insufficiency and takes medication to manage it. He is not a prisoner and does not meet the definition of a Vulnerable Subject per ISO 14155:2011 Section 3.44.

A 32-year-old male patient with a history of infertility is seeking medical assistance after being diagnosed with azoospermia. He has been trying to conceive with his partner for the past two years, without success. He has no history of sexually transmitted infections or other medical conditions that may affect fertility. The patient underwent a semen analysis which showed the absence of sperm cells in the ejaculate. The patient will undergo a testicular biopsy to determine the cause of his azoospermia. The patient will be included in the clinical trial if the biopsy confirms the presence of azoospermia and there are no sperm cells found in the sample. The patient will be excluded if any sperm cells are found in the biopsy.

A 46-year-old Asian female with a history of advanced solid malignant tumor presents for enrollment in a Phase I clinical trial. The patient has previously received standard therapies for her cancer with no success. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, with no deterioration over the previous 2 weeks. The patient has no history of interferon treatment for HBV and HCV or prior liver transplantation. She has no evidence of interstitial lung disease on baseline high resolution computerized tomography (HRCT). Bone marrow reserve and organ function are adequate based on laboratory values. The patient is willing to undergo paired biopsies for histological or cytological confirmation of her cancer. She meets the inclusion criteria for Part A and C of the trial, and is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of AZD1480 (JAK2 inhibitor) for her advanced solid malignant tumor.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who received the first dose of GSK Biologicals' hepatitis B vaccine in the primary vaccination study approximately five years ago. She has a history of being healthy with no allergies or chronic diseases. She has no history of hepatitis B infection or vaccination prior to the primary study. She understands the purpose of the long-term follow-up study and is willing to participate. The patient has provided written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle accident two days ago. He was the driver of the car and was hit from behind by another vehicle while he was stopped at a red light. He was wearing his seatbelt and the airbags were deployed. He was taken to the hospital where he was diagnosed with a mild traumatic brain injury (TBI) and was discharged home with instructions to rest and take pain medications as needed. He is experiencing headaches, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, and memory problems. He reports feeling anxious and worried about his ability to return to work and his normal activities. He has no history of psychiatric illness and is not taking any medications. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He is eager to participate in the study to receive early intervention and improve his symptoms.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was admitted to the ICU due to sepsis. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on insulin therapy for diabetes management. Upon admission, he required mechanical ventilation and was started on vasopressor support. A central venous catheter was inserted for administration of medications and blood draws. The patient has no known allergies to any medications or dressings. The site of the catheter insertion is on the patient's right subclavian vein. The patient has intact skin in the area and no active lesions are present. He is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 30-year-old woman with fair skin type (II) presents with a history of recurring acne breakouts on her upper back. She has no history of skin cancer or other skin conditions. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any tattoos, moles or scars in the treatment area. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the potential of different pretreatments to enhance the effectiveness of photodynamic therapy for acne. The patient is willing to undergo microneedling, sandpaper, curettage, ablative fractional laser, and non-ablative fractional laser treatments on 17 different areas of her upper back in a randomized sequence. She is willing to have her skin evaluated for PpIX accumulation after 3 hours incubation with methyl aminolevulinate (MAL), and to report on any pain or skin reactions during treatment.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been experiencing recurring episodes of oral thrush and vaginal yeast infections over the past year. He has a history of diabetes mellitus and has been taking insulin for the past 5 years. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, malaise, and occasional fever for the past few weeks. A blood culture was positive for Candida albicans, confirming the presence of a systemic candida infection. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the diagnostic value of candida-specific IgG, IgM, and Mn levels in candida infection.

A 58-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, who has been receiving haemodialysis for 3 years due to end-stage renal disease. He is 1.73m tall and weighs 70 kg. His blood pressure is well controlled with amlodipine 5mg daily. His fasting blood sugar is controlled with insulin. His dialysis is done three times a week, and the last session was 24 hours before screening. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgeries or malignancies. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 120 days or received any medication within seven days before dosing of the investigational drug. He understands the study requirements and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain and cramping in his right calf while walking for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He quit smoking three months ago. His ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.6 on the right side. Duplex ultrasound showed an 8 cm long stenosis in the proximal segment of the right superficial femoral artery (SFA). The patient is eligible for the study because he has a flow-limiting lesion after POBA/DCB interventions and is in Rutherford class 3. He is able to understand the nature of the study and is willing to participate. The patient has no contraindication to interventional treatment. He has no history of allergy to any medication. He has a good support system at home and will be able to comply with the study protocol. The patient has no other significant medical conditions that would interfere with the study. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 months.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and has scheduled a C-section delivery due to a breech presentation of her baby. She speaks English and is in good general health with no history of opioid, other illicit substance, or alcohol use disorder either before or during pregnancy. She has no allergies or contraindications to study medication. The planned Pfannenstiel skin incision and lower uterine segment transverse hysterotomy make her eligible for the trial. She is able to provide informed consent and has no severe renal or hepatic impairment. She will be invited to participate in the trial and will be randomized to receive either a combination of acetaminophen and ibuprofen or ibuprofen alone on a scheduled basis for pain management after her C-section delivery. The trial will assess the efficacy of the combination regimen in reducing opioid consumption and improving quality of life after discharge.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who presented to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss for the last 3 months. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the pancreas, which was confirmed by biopsy to be pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or target therapy. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and adequate organ function as defined by study-specified laboratory tests. He has no history of heart, liver, kidney, lung, neurological, immune, or other medical conditions. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and has signed the informed consent form. He has no history of alcohol or drug dependence and no intercurrent illness that would affect his ability to comply with study visits and procedures. He is not currently taking systemically active steroids and has not received another investigational product within 28 days prior to receiving study drug. He has not undergone major surgery or significant traumatic injury in the last 28 days prior to receiving study drug. He has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B, or C at screening. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 29-year-old woman who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and has not been diagnosed with any major medical illness nor taking any chronic medication. She does not have any thyroid disease and has not been using any iodine-containing dietary supplements or medication in the last year. She is a non-smoker and has been residing at the study site for more than 12 months. The patient is carrying a singleton pregnancy and is generally healthy. She is interested in participating in the study to help monitor her iodine status and ensure that her baby is not affected by iodine deficiency.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who was diagnosed with T-lymphoblastic lymphoma three years ago. He has undergone several courses of chemotherapy and radiotherapy, but unfortunately, the tumor has relapsed. He has no significant medical history, no allergies, and does not smoke nor drink alcohol. His ECOG rate is 1 and he is expected to survive for more than 3 months. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the study requirements. His hemoglobin level is 110 g/L, absolute neutrophil count is 1.8 x 109/L, and platelet count is 120 x 109/L. His ALT and AST levels are within normal limits, as well as his serum bilirubin and creatinine levels. He has no contraindications to chemotherapy. He has at least one measurable lesion and his cardiopulmonary function is normal. He has not undergone any other antitumor therapies, including Chinese medicine, immunotherapy, or biotherapy. He is not pregnant, and he is willing to adopt reliable contraceptive methods during the study period.

Pt is a 65yo F who is physically underactive and currently not engaging in regular physical activity. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her physical activity habits and overall health. She has no evidence of any major psychological illness and is currently residing within 20 miles of the study site with no plans to move within the next 12 months. She reports no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes and has not experienced any falls within the past year. She consumes less than 14 drinks per week and is fluent in English. She has no severe hearing or sight impairments that would interfere with her participation in the study.

This is a 57 year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with stage III colorectal cancer. He has undergone surgery and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. Despite the treatment, the patient is still experiencing symptoms and has been recommended for participation in the clinical trial involving autologous antigen-activated dendritic cells. The patient is in good general health and does not have any other major medical conditions. The patient is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the trial and is interested in participating in the study to improve his chances of recovery.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with recurrent pituitary adenoma. The patient underwent prior treatments including surgery and radiation therapy, but the tumor has returned. The patient's current Karnofsky performance status is 80%. The tumor measures 1.5cm in maximal diameter on MRI Brain. The patient has normal organ and marrow function with a platelet count of 120 × 109/L, hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, WBC of 4 × 109/L, and ANC of 2.0 × 109/L. The patient has no history of immunodeficiency or deficient dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase activity. The patient has not received prior temozolomide and/or capecitabine therapy for treatment of the pituitary tumor. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to take contraceptive measures for the duration of treatment and at least 6 months after the last dose of chemotherapy. The patient has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

A 45-year-old male with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation came to the clinic complaining of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He had been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and they have been affecting his daily life. He was scheduled for pulmonary vein isolation ablation procedure in the next few weeks. He does not have any known anxiety or depression. He has a sedentary lifestyle and is overweight with a BMI of 28. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently taking a beta-blocker and a blood thinner prescribed by his cardiologist.

A 32-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes for 5 years and a recent diagnosis of depression. She has been struggling to manage her diabetes and has experienced frequent high blood sugar levels. She has tried various diabetes management techniques, including insulin pumps and glucose monitoring, but has not been able to achieve optimal control. Her depressive symptoms have also been affecting her ability to manage her diabetes. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious about monitoring her blood sugar levels and following a strict diet. She is interested in participating in the DIA-LINK study to gain a better understanding of the relationship between her diabetes distress, depression, and poor glycemic control. She has a smartphone and speaks fluent German.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She had an uneventful pregnancy and delivery, and was discharged from the hospital two days ago. The patient reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious since coming home with the baby, and has been having difficulty sleeping and eating. She has a past history of anxiety and depression, and is currently not taking any medications for these conditions. The patient owns a smartphone and is able to use it proficiently. She is fluent in English, and has no hearing or vision impairments that would prevent her from using the app. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to receive additional support for her mental health during the postpartum period.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with multiple myeloma one year ago. She has already received one line of prior therapy, which didn't show any significant improvement. She has evidence of measurable disease and is now experiencing relapsed disease. She has adequate bone marrow reserve and is not suffering from intracranial disease or epidural disease. She has not received any anti-cancer medications or investigational therapy in the past 28 days. She is willing to participate in the study to see if the oral Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2)-inhibitor (Ruxolitinib; INBC018424) can help treat her relapsed multiple myeloma.

The patient is a neonate who was born prematurely at 33 weeks gestation and is currently receiving treatment for a suspected bacterial infection. The neonate is receiving amoxicillin as part of their routine clinical care and is expected to continue the treatment for at least 7 days. The neonate has a birth weight of 2.1 kg and is otherwise healthy with no known medical conditions or allergies. Blood and cerebrospinal fluid samples will be collected during the course of the treatment as part of routine care, and these will be used for the pharmacokinetic analysis. The neonate's parents have given their consent for the baby to participate in this study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who received BCG vaccination within the first month of life. He has no history of exposure to tuberculosis and is generally in good health. He is currently attending elementary school and has no known immunodeficiency or recent use of steroids or immunosuppressants. He has not received any live vaccines within the past 6 weeks. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo the PPD test and ELISPOT assay to detect T cells specific for M. tuberculosis antigens. His parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old heterosexual male who has been in a committed relationship for the past year. He reports experiencing premature ejaculation during sexual activity, with an intravaginal ejaculation latency time (IELT) of less than 2 minutes. He has not received any treatment for this condition in the past six months nor has he been diagnosed with diabetes or a history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that utilizes an exercise app in combination with an electronic device designed to treat premature ejaculation. He is willing to commit to an 8-week treatment period and is able to give informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with HIV infection for 3 years. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is undetectable. He has a CD4+ T cell count of 550 cells/mm3. He is in good health and reports no significant medical history or allergies. He does not have any other immune diseases and has not undergone chemotherapy within the past year. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help develop a vaccine against HIV. The patient understands the risks and benefits associated with participation and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including blood draws.

A 56-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of metastatic pancreatic cancer. He had undergone 2 cycles of gemcitabine hydrochloride treatment, but his condition did not improve. He had a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He didn't have any other significant medical history. His performance status was 1 according to ECOG. His blood tests showed a normal absolute neutrophil count and platelet count, INR, bilirubin, creatinine, and AST or ALT. His hemoglobin level was 11.2 g/dL. He had no history of CNS or brain metastases, and radiographically measurable disease was not required. He is not using contact lenses and has no history of any serious systemic disease. He gave informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

9-year-old child with a BMI above the 85th percentile for their age and gender. They live within 50 miles of the treatment site and speak English at a second-grade reading level. At least one of their parents is overweight with a BMI above 25.0. The child has no conditions known to promote obesity, is not currently participating in another weight control program, and is not taking weight-affecting medications. The child and their parent have no disability or illness that would preclude them from engaging in at least moderate-intensity physical activity, and have no current or prior diagnosed eating disturbance, thought disorder, suicidality, or substance abuse disorder.

A 28-year-old woman has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection and is currently taking antiretroviral drugs for the past 6 months. She is on oral contraceptive pills and has no history of significant vaginal pathology, hysterectomy or conization. She has not had any abnormal Pap smear in the past year and does not have any clinical symptoms suggestive of genital infection. She has not taken any systemic antibiotics or immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory treatment in the last six months, nor has she taken corticosteroids (> 20 mg / day for 5 days) in the last 3 months. She has no history of Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, gonorrhea, Trichomonas, Candida albicans or Syphilis. She is affiliated to a social security system and has signed the informed consent. She is willing to participate in the MUCOVAC study that aims to study the immunity at the genital mucosa of HIV-1 infected and healthy women. The study involves two visits and will include the collection of blood samples and cervicovaginal samples for immunological and transcriptomic analysis.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with oral pain and discomfort for the past six months. She reports burning sensation and difficulty eating, especially when consuming spicy or acidic foods. She also mentions that the symptoms have affected her quality of life and sleep. The patient has a medical history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She denies any other systemic diseases or medication use that could cause lichenoid reaction. The patient has been diagnosed with oral lichen planus by a dermatologist and oral medicine specialist, and the diagnosis has been confirmed by biopsy according to WHO's clinic-pathological diagnostic criteria for LP. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will provide informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old HIV-positive male who has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years. He was diagnosed with HIV when he presented with fever, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy. His CD4 count at diagnosis was 150 cells/μL and his viral load was 60,000 copies/mL. He was started on a combination of tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz and has been adherent to his medication regimen since then. His most recent CD4 count is 400 cells/μL and his viral load is undetectable (<20 copies/mL). He has no history of opportunistic infections or AIDS-related illnesses. He has no known allergies, takes no other medications, and does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is married and has two children. He has been tested for hepatitis B and C, and both tests were negative. He has never been exposed to a chemokine receptor 5 antagonist. He has no history of liver or kidney disease.

A 65-year-old man came to the clinic with severe pain in his right knee due to end-stage osteoarthritis. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it regularly. He also has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He does not have any allergies. He underwent a total joint replacement surgery for his knee and is now experiencing post-operative pain. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that could provide better pain relief after surgery. He is able to understand and respond to the questionnaire and is willing to attend outpatient clinic follow-up. His ASAI status is II. He does not have any liver cirrhosis, chronic renal insufficiency, heart disease or arrhythmia, insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, or previous narcotic abuse history.

The patient is a 28 year old male who has been using prescription opioids for chronic pain management after a car accident that left him with multiple fractures. He reports taking the medication as prescribed but has developed a tolerance and now feels like he cannot function without it. He has tried to quit multiple times but experiences severe withdrawal symptoms including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, sweating, and intense cravings. He has been advised by his healthcare provider to consider other options for pain management and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new earpiece that may help alleviate his withdrawal symptoms. He is in good overall health, does not have any history of seizures or neurological diseases, and is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of overactive bladder for the past 6 months. She feels a sudden and strong urge to urinate frequently throughout the day and night, which has been interfering with her work and social life. She has also been experiencing occasional leaking of urine when she laughs or sneezes. She has no history of urinary tract infections and has not been diagnosed with any other bladder or urinary conditions. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and has a healthy diet

A 62-year-old female non-smoker presented to her primary care physician with shortness of breath and coughing up blood. She had no significant past medical history and no known family history of cancer. She underwent a chest X-ray, followed by a CT scan, which showed a mass in the upper lobe of her

60-year-old male with a histologically confirmed diagnosis of carcinoma of the prostate and current objective evidence of metastatic disease to the bone. The patient is currently receiving 1st line hormonal therapy with LHRH agonists. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to zoledronic acid or other bisphosphonates. The patient has no other nonmalignant disease that would confound the evaluation of primary endpoints or prevent the patient complying with the protocol. The patient has a corrected (adjusted for serum albumin) serum calcium concentration of 8.2 mg/dl (2.05 mmol/L). The patient's WBC is 4.5x1'000'000'000, ANC is 2000/mm3, Hgb is 11.5 g/dL, and platelets are 200 x 1'000'000'000/L. The patient's liver function tests and serum creatinine are within normal limits. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 3-year-old girl is referred to the trial due to her parents' concerns about her swallowing function. She has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been diagnosed with cerebral palsy. She is currently fed orally, but her parents have noticed that she has difficulty swallowing certain foods and liquids. They report that she often chokes, coughs, and gags during mealtimes. The girl is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. Her parents are willing to participate in the trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer. He has a history of smoking and quit 10 years ago. His lung function is good, and he is otherwise healthy. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. Upon further examination, he was found to have a mass in his lung. His doctors have recommended that he undergo a lobectomy or anatomical segmentectomy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the videothoracoscopic (VATS) approach versus the robotic approach for the surgery. He has been informed that the study will involve a randomized assignment to one of the two procedures, and that the primary endpoint is a combination of conversion and complication rate. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including being over 18 years old, having early-stage lung cancer, and being in good overall health (ASA-1-2-3). He does not have any severe heart disease, alcohol abuse, or renal impairment.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of dental caries. She has previously had fillings in her molars and premolars. She has no systemic diseases and is not taking any medications. The patient has no allergies and is a non-smoker. The patient has good oral hygiene practices and visits her dentist twice a year for routine cleanings. On examination, there are three cavities on the left mandibular posterior teeth, including one class I, one class II and one class V. There is no evidence of periapical pathology or pulp exposure. The occlusion is stable, and there is no evidence of bruxism. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the trial and is available for the required post-operative follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with breast cancer and scheduled for a unilateral modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and is not taking any major centrally acting drugs. She has no history of opioid dependence or substance abuse. She is in good general health with no severe cardiopulmonary, renal, or hepatic diseases. She has not experienced any extensive myocardial ischemia or unstable angina. She does not have any intracranial metallic devices, pacemakers, or any other device that may interfere with the transcranial direct current stimulation.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on assessing the usual practice and levels of pain, sedation, physical restraints, and delirium in Spanish intensive care units. The study will evaluate all adult patients who were admitted to the participating units at the time of the audit and had a minimum stay of 24 hours in the unit.

Patient is a 64-year-old woman who underwent multifocal intraocular lens (IOL) implantation for age-related cataract. She reports persistent vitreous floaters that significantly affect her daily activities and quality of life. The patient has no history of glaucoma, retinal abnormalities, diabetes mellitus, steroid or immunosuppressive treatment, or connective tissue diseases. The patient's central endothelial cell count is greater than 2000 cells/mm2 and her intraocular pressure is within normal limits. She has not been diagnosed with amblyopia. The patient is seeking a solution to her disabling vitreous floaters and is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of 25-gauge transconjunctival sutureless vitrectomy (TSV).

A 55-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis due to non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is being evaluated for liver transplantation. He presents with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and unintentional weight loss. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. He does not have a history of alcohol or intravenous drug use. His fasting serum glucose and thyroid function tests are normal. However, he has evidence of malnutrition as quantified by low triceps skinfold thickness and mid arm muscle area. He has also been diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy and is currently being treated with lactulose. He is identified as a potential candidate for the Mechanisms of Malnutrition in Cirrhosis with Portosystemic Shunting study, which aims to examine the expression of myostatin and its receptor in the skeletal muscle and mesenteric adipose tissue in cirrhotic patients undergoing liver transplantation. The study will also evaluate his nutritional status using anthropometry, dual energy x-ray absorptiometry, and bioelectrical impedance analysis. If he meets the inclusion criteria, he will be enrolled in the study and undergo rectus abdominis muscle tissue and omental fat tissue harvesting during the liver transplantation surgery.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was involved in a motorcycle accident three years ago resulting in irreversible damage to his radial nerve. Since the accident, he has been unable to extend his fingers and wrist, and has lost the ability to grasp objects with his right hand. He underwent radial nerve repair surgery but it was unsuccessful. He has no history of vascular injuries or other medical conditions that may affect the outcome of the surgery. He is willing to undergo tendon transfer surgery to restore the lost function of his hand.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male who recently had an MRI scan due to chronic headaches. The MRI revealed a mass in his brain, and upon further testing, he was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). The patient had no prior history of brain tumors or neurological disorders. The patient underwent surgical resection of the tumor, and the pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of GBM. The patient has unmethylated MGMT promoter as determined by Methylation-specific polymerase chain reaction (MGMT(+) tumor). The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and no significant medical history. The patient has normal blood pressure and all required blood work within 14 days prior to registration. The patient is eligible for standard concurrent chemoradiation with Temozolomide. The patient's liver function is normal, and there is no evidence of bleeding or pathologic condition that carries a high risk of bleeding. The patient has not undergone prior radiation therapy to the brain, chemotherapy, or anti-angiogenic therapy. The estimated life expectancy of the patient is at least 6 months. The patient is willing to sign a written informed consent document and is able to understand the details of the study.

The patient is a 15-year-old female living in a rural area in Oregon. She is enrolled in the Oregon Health Plan (OHP) and assigned to receive dental care from Advantage Dental Plan. She has been experiencing tooth pain and sensitivity for the past few weeks and is in need of dental treatment. Her family has limited financial resources and has difficulty accessing dental care due to their location. She is eligible for this clinical trial as a low-income individual living in a rural area, and will receive primary preventive care in non-conventional community settings, such as WIC and Head Start, as well as seamless, timely, and appropriate evidence-based care in Advantage dental clinics. This trial aims to reduce disparities in access and oral health for low-income mothers and children like her.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, followed by radiation therapy. She completed adjuvant endocrine therapy with tamoxifen for two years. However, she was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has progressed on her previous chemotherapy regimen of docetaxel and carboplatin. She has not received any prior treatment with capecitabine or vinflunine. Her ECOG performance status is 1 and she has adequate organ function. Her baseline labs show a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL, platelet count of 120 x 109/L, and ANC of 2.0 x 109/L. She has measurable disease with multiple liver and bone metastases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

A 50-year-old woman with advanced cervical cancer complains of persistent abdominal pain and bloating. She was diagnosed with cervical cancer (Stage II) two years ago and underwent cisplatin-based chemo-radiation as an initial treatment. She did not receive any other treatment for her cancer following the chemo-radiation therapy. She has been experiencing abdominal discomfort for the past few weeks, and her CT scan showed the progression of the cancer to the liver and lungs. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled on medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has one child and is post-menopausal. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her physician has suggested enrolling her in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options.

A 34-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a severe traumatic brain injury. He was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 8 and remained in the hospital for several months. He is now admitted to Craig Hospital for inpatient rehabilitation for TBI. The patient's testosterone levels were found to be below the assay normal range during the screening process for this clinical trial. He is fluent in English and his attending physician has approved him for study participation. The patient has no history of prior psychiatric illness requiring hospitalization or testosterone therapy. He has not been diagnosed with any hormonally dependent cancer and has no known hypersensitivity to T gel ingredients. The patient's BMI is within the normal range. The patient has given consent to participate in the study.

The patient is an 8-month-old male infant who has been diagnosed with Type I Spinal Muscular Atrophy. He has never achieved independent sitting and his symptoms started to manifest before he was 6 months old. The patient has a confirmed homozygous deletion of the SMN1 gene. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials for experimental drugs and does not require continuous respiratory support. The patient does not have any known hematological disorders or severe systemic disorders.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) 2 years ago. She has previously experienced pneumothorax and chylothorax and has been struggling with progressive loss of lung function. Her past medical history includes a diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) and she has been experiencing difficulty breathing, which has been affecting her daily life. Her BMI is 22, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help stabilize or improve her lung function. She has never been pregnant and is willing to use adequate contraception throughout the trial period.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was diagnosed with a central nervous system tumor that requires radiation therapy. The patient's parents are concerned about the potential cognitive side effects of the treatment and are interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially reduce the impact of radiation therapy on her memory and thinking. The patient is able to use a computer for cognitive assessment and has normal serum creatinine, total bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels. The patient has no prior history of intracranial radiation and does not have any contraindications or allergies to memantine. The patient has occasional sleep disturbances but is not currently taking any short-acting benzodiazepines. The patient has no uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses or significant psychiatric illness that would limit compliance with study requirements.

The patient is a 8-year-old child who has been diagnosed with Henoch-Schönlein purpura nephritis (HSPN). The child has been experiencing symptoms such as joint pain, abdominal pain, and skin rash. The child has been receiving Western medicine treatment for the past few weeks but has not seen significant improvement in symptoms. The parents are interested in alternative treatment options and have agreed to participate in a clinical trial that explores the effectiveness of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) on HSPN. The child is able to understand and follow instructions, and the parents are able to provide detailed information and complete a follow-up. There is no history of renal insufficiency or serious complications such as respiratory, digestive, hematological or liver diseases. The child has not had any allergic reactions to TCM in the past. The family is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

Sophie is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 29 weeks of gestation. She has a history of premature delivery of her first baby. Her obstetrician has prescribed her a course of antenatal steroids after identifying her as at risk for preterm delivery. She received her first course of antenatal steroids 15 days ago. Sophie has a history of smoking, but she stopped smoking during her pregnancy. She has no history of any underlying medical condition. Her vital signs and laboratory studies are normal. She is informed of the potential benefits and risks of the study and has provided informed consent. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and has agreed to participate.

A 40-year-old female with a 14-year-old daughter diagnosed with anxiety disorder and depression is seeking help for her own major depressive disorder. She is struggling to cope with her daughter's illness and feels overwhelmed and hopeless. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and poor appetite. She is currently not taking any antidepressant medication and has not received any psychotherapy in the past 6 months. She lives with her daughter and is responsible for her care. She is fluent in English and willing to comply with study requirements. Her daughter is also willing to participate in the study and meets the inclusion criteria for mentally ill children.

The patient is a 62 year old man who was recently diagnosed with localized adenocarcinoma of the prostate. He has undergone treatment on clinical trial NCI-00-C-0154 and has consented to the use of his collected blood cells for future research. He has completed his treatment and is currently in remission. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is willing to participate in this study and provide blood samples for analysis.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection 5 days ago. He developed symptoms of fever, cough, fatigue, and headache. He has no known comorbidities and is not currently taking any medications. He has not been hospitalized for COVID-19, nor has he participated in any other clinical trials for COVID-19 treatment or prophylaxis. He has no history of ventricular arrhythmia, Long QT syndrome, kidney disease, ischemic or structural heart disease, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, or porphyria. He is not taking any medications that can prolong QT intervals or increase the risk for QT prolongation, except for loop diuretics which he stopped taking 30 days ago. He is not allergic to HCQ or azithromycin. He has experienced symptoms of fever, cough, shortness of breath, sore throat, body pain, muscle pain, fatigue, and headache for less than 10 days. He agrees not to participate in any other clinical trial for the treatment of COVID-19 or SARS-CoV-2 during the study period up until reaching hospitalization or 20 days, whichever is earliest, and not to obtain study medications outside of the A5395 study.

A 2-month-old male infant presents with persistent yellow skin and sclera, pale-colored stools, and hepatomegaly. The infant has elevated serum bilirubin levels dominated by direct bilirubin (>60%) and liver enzyme abnormalities. Ultrasound confirms poor gallbladder filling and signs of liver fibrosis. Radionuclide imaging confirms obstructed biliary excretion. The infant is scheduled for a Kasai procedure and is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the effects of sevoflurane on hepatic blood flow and hepatic arterial buffer response in infants with obstructive jaundice. The infant has no concomitant cardiovascular or abdominal organ malformations.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He is scheduled to undergo elective cardiac surgery for coronary artery bypass grafting. His past medical history includes a myocardial infarction 2 years ago, for which he underwent angioplasty and stent placement. He is compliant with his medications, which include aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a grade II/VI systolic murmur at the apex. His preoperative laboratory results are within normal limits, including a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL. The patient has no known allergies, and he has not participated in any clinical studies in the last 3 months. He has provided informed consent to participate in this study.

Patient A is a 44-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stage IV melanoma with metastases to the liver, lungs, and bones. He has not received any systemic treatment for his cancer and is generally in good health. He works as a high school teacher and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. His performance status is ECOG 1 and his life expectancy is not specified. His lab tests are within normal limits, with a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, a neutrophil count of 3,500/mm3, and a platelet count of 150,000/mm3. His liver function tests are normal, with a bilirubin level of 0.8 mg/dL, an alkaline phosphatase level of 70 U/L, and transaminases within normal limits. His creatinine level is 1.3 mg/dL, and he has no history of cardiovascular disease. He has no concurrent infections or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. He has not undergone any prior systemic therapy for his cancer and has not received any experimental drugs in the past four weeks. He is not taking any concurrent medications that are contraindicated for E7070. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and use effective contraception during the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with gallstones and underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He works as a construction worker and has a history of occasional lower back pain. He does not smoke or drink alcohol regularly. He has a wife and two children and enjoys spending time with his family. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. He speaks Mandarin and Taiwanese fluently and has agreed to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing severe menstrual cramps and heavy bleeding for the past year. She was diagnosed with moderate-severe endometriosis and underwent conservative surgery to preserve her uterus and ovary. After surgery, her CA125 levels were found to be elevated. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for maintenance therapy of levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) to prevent the recurrence of symptomatic endometriosis after conservative surgery. She has not taken any endometriosis treatments in the past 2 months and does not have any concomitant diseases that can be a cause of chronic pelvic pain or anemia. She is not planning to get pregnant in the next 3 years. She is willing to be evaluated every month for 24 weeks, and at 3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24 months after the end of medical treatment. She understands that this trial involves two groups of patients, one group receiving LNG-IUS for 5 years and GnRH agonist (triptorelin 3.75 mg, sc q28day) for 24 weeks, and the other group receiving GnRH agonist (triptorelin 3.75 mg, sc q28day) alone for 24 weeks. The primary outcome measure of this trial is the recurrence rate of endometriosis, defined as elevation of CA125 or endometriosis lesion in sonography or symptoms suggesting endometriosis including menorrhagia or dysmenorrhea. She understands that the trial requires a follow-up period of 2 years after the end of GnRH agonist medical treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who has been diagnosed with HIV infection and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for more than a year. His viral load has been controlled (<50 copies/ml) but his CD4+ cell count is less than 350/mL, indicating an immunological discordant response to the therapy. He has not experienced any opportunistic infections in the last 12 months, and his liver function tests are normal. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use a contraceptive method throughout the duration of the clinical trial. He has not received any steroids, immunomodulators or chemotherapy in the last 12 months, and his AIDS Clinical Trials Group scale is grade 1 or 2. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment with MSCs or placebo.

A 23-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5 presented to the clinic with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and denies any use of illicit drugs. She is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. She has normal vital signs, ECG, and laboratory results within the normal range. She has a negative urine pregnancy test and is using a reliable method of contraception. She has no history of psychiatric disorder, alcohol abuse, or exposure to other substances of abuse. She has not participated in any experimental drug study in the last 8 weeks. She has not donated or lost blood equal to or exceeding 500 mL in the last 8 weeks. She has no diagnosis of hypertension, and her resting pulse rate is within the normal range. She has no significant liver disease or history of hypersensitivity to trazodone or related drugs. She is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and has signed the statements of informed consent for the screening and phase-related procedures.

Patient is a preterm infant with gestational age ≤ 32 weeks and birth weight ≤ 1500 grams. The infant is currently undergoing screening for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). The screening procedure is known to be painful and uncomfortable, and topical anesthetics have not been effective in completely suppressing the painful responses. The infant will be enrolled in a prospective observational study at a tertiary-care neonatal intensive care unit to compare the efficacy of oral ibuprofen and oral paracetamol in reducing pain during the ROP screening. The primary outcome measure will be pain assessed by the Neonatal Pain, Agitation, and Sedation (N-PASS) scale. Secondary outcome measures will include tachycardia, bradycardia, desaturations, and crying time. The infant must have a gestational age of ≤32 weeks and a birth weight ≤1500 grams to be eligible for the study. Exclusion criteria include major congenital abnormalities, neurological dysfunction, infants who were mechanically ventilated and/or sedated, hemodynamically unstable infants, infants > 32 weeks of gestational age, and infants whose parents denied consent.

A 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no known medical conditions and has never been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. He does not smoke or drink alcohol and has no history of seizures or psychiatric disorders. He is currently taking no medications and has no history of previous surgeries or gastrointestinal procedures. He is willing to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 14-year-old male with a history of chronic musculoskeletal pain that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. Despite multiple consultations with various specialists and treatments, including physical therapy and medications, the pain has persisted and has significantly impacted his daily activities and school attendance. He reports a pain intensity level of 8/10 on the visual analog scale. He has no prior history of psychological or behavioral issues, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is accompanied by his parents who are supportive and engaged in his care. They are seeking options for pain management and improvement in his overall functioning.

The patient is a 54 year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with Stage IV squamous non small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking cigarettes for 30 years, with a 20 pack-year history. He presented with a 2-month history of cough, shortness of breath, and unintentional weight loss. CT scan revealed a 6.5 cm mass in the right upper lobe of the lung, pleural effusion on the right side, and multiple pulmonary nodules. A biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma. Brain MRI revealed no evidence of metastases. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, meaning he is ambulatory and able to carry out light work, but is limited in physically strenuous activity. He has no known autoimmune diseases. He has been advised to undergo treatment with paclitaxel and carboplatin and is considering participation in a clinical trial comparing Ipilimumab versus placebo in addition to paclitaxel and carboplatin.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian man who works as a bartender in a local casino. He has been playing casino games for the past 3 years and has been experiencing a loss of control in his gambling behavior. He spends most of his free time at the casino and has been borrowing money from friends and family to finance his gambling. He has been diagnosed with pathological gambling according to the DSM-IV-TR criteria. He is right-handed, aged between 18-60 years, and is not currently on any psychotropic medications. He has no history of visual or hearing problems. He has no other addictions except for occasional tobacco use. He has no current psychiatric comorbidity and has not started or changed any psychotropic medications in the past month.

A 56-year-old male who has been experiencing increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, and persistent cough for the past few months. He has a history of exposure to asbestos due to his former occupation as a construction worker. After undergoing diagnostic tests, he was diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma. The doctors have recommended a pleural biopsy to determine the stage and prognosis of his cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that is testing a new method for determining cancer stage and estimating prognosis prior to surgery or another treatment. He is willing to undergo pleural biopsy as part of the study and is 18 years of age or older.

Patient is a 35yo male who has been using intravenous cocaine for the past 2 years. He reports using cocaine on a weekly basis and has a history of positive urine drug screens for cocaine within the past 6 weeks. The patient does not report any adverse reactions to cocaine or other psychostimulants. He does not have any current Axis I psychiatric disorders other than drug abuse or dependence. The patient denies any history of dependence on opiates, benzodiazepines, alcohol, or other sedative-hypnotics. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of tacrine on cocaine self-administration and pharmacokinetics.

52 year old female with a history of COPD and frequent exacerbations, presenting with shortness of breath and wheezing. She reports increased difficulty breathing with minimal exertion, and has been using her rescue inhaler more frequently. She also notes decreased exercise tolerance and has had to decrease her daily activities. She has been previously hospitalized for exacerbations of her COPD and is currently on maintenance inhalers, but has not been able to achieve adequate control of her symptoms. She is a non-smoker and has no other significant medical history. She is able to communicate effectively in the local language and has no known mental or cognitive disorders.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who had a stroke 1.5 years ago. She experiences weakness in her right leg and has difficulty standing and walking without assistance. She has been receiving physical therapy for the past year to improve her muscle strength and mobility. She is able to walk short distances with a cane but needs a wheelchair for longer distances. She has no history of other neurological disorders, muscle diseases, or injuries to her lower extremities. Her current medications include aspirin and a blood pressure medication. She lives alone and relies on her family for support with daily activities. She is motivated to participate in the study to improve her muscle strength and functional abilities.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer three months ago. He has received one line of chemotherapy, but his disease has progressed. He is experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and occasional cough. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform routine activities of daily living without assistance. He does not have any significant past medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not sexually active and has no plans for future fertility. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 10 g/dl WBC: 6000 /mm3 Plt: 200000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with lung cancer and is scheduled to undergo elective thoracotomy surgery. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of respiratory illness or surgery. She is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies. Her preoperative laboratory test results are within normal limits. She is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension and has no other medications. She understands the study requirements and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease and has been on oral levodopa therapy for the past 3 years. He experiences wearing-off phenomenon and has an "ON" score of at least 20% better than the "OFF" score as measured by the MDS-UPDRS motor score. His daily "OFF" time duration is at least 2 hours per day. The patient is in Hoehn-Yahr stage less than 4 and is able to walk without the use of an assisted device. He is currently receiving levodopa at least TID with a minimum of 100 mg levodopa administered with each dose. The patient is willing and able to not change his Parkinson's Disease medications or dosages during the up to 2-week study therapy period. He is willing to provide Informed Consent to participate in the study and is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and required availability for study visits. The patient does not have cognitive dysfunction defined by a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score <24, moderate levodopa-induced dyskinesias as indicated by a score >2 on items 4.1 and/or 4.2 in the MDS-UPDRS Part IV, or clinically significant depression as determined by the Beck Depression Inventory-II score >15. The patient has not been diagnosed with any other medical or psychiatric comorbidity that can compromise participation in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 months. She has been on methotrexate for the past 6 months and has at least 6 swollen and tender joints. She has no history of other inflammatory disorders or major health issues such as diabetes, cancer, HIV or active infections.
