The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not been diagnosed with any cardiac conduction disorders, hepatic/renal insufficiency, active depression/anxiety/psychosis/schizophrenia or convulsions. She is willing to continue taking methotrexate throughout the study and is interested in participating in the trial to determine the efficacy of the new drug AD 452 in treating her RA symptoms.

48-year-old female with a history of chronic neck pain for the past 8 months, rated at 7/10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), despite physical therapy, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and acetaminophen. She reports the pain as a constant dull ache that worsens with movement and is associated with occasional headaches. MRI of the cervical spine shows mild degenerative changes in the facet joints at C4-C5 and C5-C6. She has no history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy and is not taking any antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication. She is willing to participate in the study and complete the follow-up questionnaires. Ultrasound imaging of the cervical spine shows clear visualization of the targeted structures. She is scheduled for unilateral cervical medial branch block as part of her usual care.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of myocardial infarction (MI) that occurred 6 months ago. He presents with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. His past medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity. He has been on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and clopidogrel for the past 3 months. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. His most recent laboratory values show an HbA1c of 7.5%, a creatinine clearance of 50 mL/minute, a platelet count of 150x106/mL, and a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL. He is a candidate for the study investigating the pharmacodynamic effects of vorapaxar in addition to standard DAPT with aspirin and clopidogrel, as well as in combination with clopidogrel only following aspirin withdrawal.

12-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis with one CFTR gating mutation. The patient has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been experiencing difficulty with maintaining a healthy weight, despite aggressive nutritional intervention. The patient has been recommended by their CF Care Team to begin treatment with Ivacaftor due to their specific genetic mutation. The patient is otherwise in a usual state of good health and has no other significant medical history. The patient and their family have committed to the 3-month study protocol with two, 3-4 day visits to Children's Hospital of Philadelphia's Clinical Translational Research Center. The patient's FEV1 is greater than 40% predicted and they are not currently on any medications that inhibit or induce cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any other illnesses affecting growth or nutritional status. They are not receiving total parenteral nutrition.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and hypertension. The patient has been experiencing uncontrolled hypertension with an office blood pressure (BP) reading of 150/95 mmHg despite being on antihypertensive medication. The patient has no history of secondary causes of hypertension such as pheochromocytoma or primary aldosteronism. The patient has not been hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina or acute ischemic stroke within the past 3 months. The patient is currently not undergoing hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. The patient has a BMI of 30 kg/m2. The patient is willing to provide informed written consent to participate in the study.

A 8-year-old girl is scheduled for two dental appointments for restorative treatments, including fillings and pulp treatment. She has no history of dental anxiety, but her parents express concern about her behavior during dental treatment. She is generally healthy and has no underlying medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications.

Patient is a 31-year-old pregnant woman who is scheduled for an elective caesarean section at 38 weeks of gestation. She has a singleton fetus and an American Society of Anesthesiologist Physical status of 1. Her body mass index is 27kg/m². The patient has never been diagnosed with any mental illness or allergic reaction to medication. She has no history of diabetes, bleeding, coagulation disorders, hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, respiratory disease, or neuropsychiatric disorders. The patient is not receiving any anticonvulsants or antidepressants. She does not have pregnancy-induced hypertension, intrauterine growth restriction, or fetal compromise. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

52yo male with a history of stable angina and hypertension presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. Coronary angiography reveals an intermediate lesion in the left anterior descending coronary artery with visual diameter stenosis of 50%. The patient is a former smoker with a pack-year history of 20 and no other significant medical history. The patient has not undergone coronary artery bypass grafting or had any significant valvular disease. The patient does not have obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma bronchial but has moderate calcification in the coronary arteries. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates physiological patterns of coronary artery disease.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent and excessive worry for the past few months. She describes feeling anxious and overwhelmed much of the time, and finds it difficult to focus on tasks because her mind is constantly preoccupied with worry. She has not sought treatment for her symptoms, but is interested in participating in a study to learn coping strategies. Her Penn State Worry Questionnaire score is 70, indicating high levels of worry. She does not have a history of psychosis or mania, and denies any current or past substance abuse. She is not currently receiving psychological treatment or taking psychotropic medications. She has never taken benzodiazepines regularly, and does not currently take them on a daily basis. She is interested in participating in the Attention Training Technique study to learn how to better control her worry and improve her attention.

A 37-year-old man with a history of psoriasis and joint pain complains of pain, swelling, and stiffness in his joints, especially in his fingers, toes, and lower back, for the past 2 years. He reports difficulty in performing daily activities due to joint pain and stiffness. He has taken DMARDs for the past 3 months, but the symptoms are still present. His corticosteroid dose is stable at 5mg QD. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has a history of chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 5 years. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is unremarkable. His family history is negative for any autoimmune disorders. His current Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) score is 10. His rheumatologist has recommended him for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with intermediate-risk acute myeloid leukemia. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer except for 5 days of hydroxyurea. He is generally in good health with a WHO performance status of 1. His kidney and liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no active uncontrolled infections or HIV positivity. He is not pregnant or nursing. He does not have any concurrent severe uncontrolled cardiovascular disease. He has no history of malignant disease other than his current diagnosis. He is willing to use effective barrier contraception during and for at least 3 months after completion of study treatment.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at the age of 2. He has spastic diplegia and walks with a noticeable limp. His parents have noticed that he has trouble performing activities that require balance and coordination, such as running and jumping. He has received two previous Botulinum Toxin-A injections in his lower limbs to improve muscle tone and mobility. He has also undergone physical therapy and wears ankle-foot orthotics to aid in walking. His parents have noticed some improvement in his gait and overall mobility, but they are interested in exploring additional treatments to further improve his quality of life.

Pt is a 67yo M with a history of esophageal cancer who underwent esophagectomy and chemotherapy. He has been struggling with oral intake and has lost significant weight over the past few months. The patient is scheduled to undergo PEG tube placement for long-term enteral tube feeding. The patient has no history of gut usage in the past 2 weeks and is able to tolerate semi-solid feeds. The patient has consented to participate in the trial to assess the effect of semi-solid feeding after PEG on the incidence of aspiration pneumonia and postoperative length of stay.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing leg pain, numbness, heaviness, or vague discomfort in part or all of both legs when walking or standing for more than three months. She has difficulty walking and has to stop frequently due to the pain. Her Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) for pain is at least 6 out of 10 when asked to rate the worst leg and lower back pain she experienced during walking last week. She has undergone an MRI or CT scan that shows at least one level of lumbar spinal stenosis within the past year. The patient does not have any significant medical illnesses, and her cognitive function is intact. She is not allergic to oxymorphone hydrochloride, propoxyphene, or acetaminophen. She is not currently taking any long-acting opioid or regularly-scheduled use of a short-acting opioid. She is not suspected to have paralytic ileus, moderate or severe hepatic impairment, or major conduction abnormality on ECG or cardiac stress test. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

A 25-year-old female patient with a known diagnosis of beta-thalassemia major since childhood presented with a history of chronic fatigue, weakness, and pale skin. She has been receiving regular blood transfusions every month since the age of 5, along with desferrioxamine therapy (50 mg/kg) for iron overload management. Her serum ferritin levels were noted to be between 1000-5000 ng/mL at the last follow-up. The patient is negative for CRP and has no history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, chronic renal or heart failure. She is not currently on any other iron chelating therapy. The patient has a BMI of 22.1 and is otherwise healthy with no significant medical or surgical history. She is compliant with her medications and follows a healthy diet and lifestyle. She has consented to participate in the clinical trial and has been randomized to receive silymarin tablets (140 mg) three times a day along with her current desferrioxamine therapy. She will be monitored for the next 6 months for any changes in iron status and liver function.

The patient is a 12-year-old male who is slightly overweight and has a history of picky eating habits. He is generally healthy and active, but his parents are concerned about his nutrient intake and want to ensure he is getting adequate vitamins and minerals for optimal health. He has not been diagnosed with any diseases and is not currently on any medications or supplements. He has not participated in any other clinical studies in the past 4 weeks.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman from China who has been diagnosed with metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). She has received several courses of chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past, but unfortunately, the cancer has progressed and spread to her liver and lungs. The patient is experiencing symptoms such as cough, shortness of breath, and weight loss. Her current PS score is 2. The biopsy results confirmed that her cancer is EBV-positive. The patient's creatinine level is within normal limits, and her liver function tests are slightly elevated but lower than three times the ULN. She has no contraindications for leukocyte collection. The patient has undergone a reliable method of contraception and understands the trial and has signed an informed consent. She has not been diagnosed with any other uncontrolled diseases that interfere with the trial. The patient has no history of mental illness that is difficult to control. Researchers have deemed her appropriate to participate in the trial. She has not been pregnant or nursing and has no plans for pregnancy within two months of treatment or after the end of treatment.

32-year-old Tunisian male diagnosed with treatment-resistant schizophrenia and currently prescribed clozapine is invited to participate in a clinical trial. The patient must have good adherence to the current treatment and not be taking any additional medications that may affect the pharmacokinetics of clozapine. Patients with gastrointestinal disorders that may disturb the absorption of clozapine are excluded from the study. The study aims to investigate the influence of genetic (CYP1A2 and CYP2C19 polymorphisms) and non-genetic factors on Clozapine pharmacokinetics. The patient will be required to provide genetic material for the analysis of CYP1A2 and CYP2C19 polymorphisms. The study will be conducted in Tunisia and aims to investigate the impact of these SNPs in the southern Mediterranean populations. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the study.

This is a 50 year-old female diagnosed with early stage breast cancer (Stage I) who underwent a lumpectomy followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy. She has reported experiencing memory lapses and difficulty concentrating since her treatment ended. She also reports feeling more fatigued, stressed, and depressed than usual. She is fluent in English and able to operate a computerized test without difficulty. She is interested in participating in this study to help others who may experience similar cognitive difficulties after breast cancer treatment. She has no history of psychiatric impairment or other significant medical conditions.

Pt is a 52yo M with a history of COPD and frequent respiratory infections. He has been on oxygen therapy for the past year and has been placed on the lung transplant list. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 14-year-old male with known hereditary angioedema (HAE) Type I, presenting with acute symptoms of abdominal pain and swelling. He has a past medical history significant for multiple HAE attacks requiring treatment with C1 esterase inhibitor replacement therapy. He is currently not using hormonal contraception or androgen therapy. He has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational products within the last 30 days. He is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study, and his parent or legal guardian will also sign informed consent.

A 42-year-old man, who recently had a tooth extraction, is interested in dental implants to restore his smile. He has never received any dental implants before. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no known systemic pathologies or conditions that may affect oral surgical procedures. He speaks fluent English and is willing to comply with all the steps of the study. He is a patient at the UAB School of Dentistry and is excited to participate in this trial to improve his dental health.

55 year old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presenting with chest pain and diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction. No previous history of diabetes mellitus. He is scheduled to undergo primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Past Medical History: Hypertension Hyperlipidemia Gout Obesity (BMI 32) Current Smoker No history of diabetes mellitus

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been diagnosed with cholecystolithiasis and requires laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no significant medical history and has an ASA physical status of I. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She does not have any known psychiatric disorders and has not taken any painkillers within the 24 hours before the operation. She has no history of respiratory tract infections within the last 2 weeks and has no known allergies to local anesthetics. She is not currently taking any opioid medications for pain management.

32yo female administrative assistant who works full-time at Brigham and Women's Hospital. She reports being sedentary and typically only walks around her office building during the day. She is interested in increasing her physical activity level but has struggled to find motivation. She has no known medical conditions and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to wear a Fitbit Flex accelerometer and complete occasional questionnaires for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing allergic rhinitis symptoms for over a year. She presents with symptoms such as sneezing, nasal congestion, and itchy eyes during the grass pollen season. She has a history of positive skin prick test for Phleum pratense and documented positive specific IgE against grass pollen (IgE ≥ Class 2) within the last 5 years. She has not received any immunotherapy treatment for grass allergen extracts in the past. She is willing to comply with the trial protocol regimen and has no contraindications for immunotherapy as established by the IT subcommittee of the EAACI or in the Summary of Products Characteristics of GRAZAX®. She is not pregnant and is not an immediate family member of the investigator or trial staff. She has no mental condition that would render her unable to understand the nature, scope, and possible consequences of the trial, and demonstrates a cooperative attitude. She has no plans to move or travel for extended periods of time during the trial period. She has not used any investigational drug within 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longest, prior to screening.

The patient is a 35-year-old English-speaking male smoker who has been smoking Marlboro Red cigarettes for over a year. He smokes at least 15 cigarettes per day and has not attempted to quit smoking in the last month nor plans to do so in the next month. He is in good general health with no significant medical conditions, psychiatric illness, or substance abuse. He has not used non-cigarette nicotine delivery products, such as e-cigarettes or marijuana, in the past week. He is willing to provide blood and urine samples and is comfortable with the study procedures. He is not currently pregnant or nursing and is taking steps to avoid pregnancy. He plans to stay in the local area for the next month. He is interested in participating in a compensated short-term study to determine the short-term effects of switching to tobacco products that deliver low levels of nicotine or reactive oxygen/nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) on smoking behavior and biomarkers of tobacco smoke exposure and oxidative stress.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who is generally active but has noticed some decline in her mobility and cognition in recent months. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the effects of lifestyle-related interventions on her health. She is able to walk 50 meters unassisted and is classified as non-frail or pre-frail according to the Fried frailty phenotype. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological disorders but has noticed some forgetfulness and difficulty with spatial working memory. She has not had any lower limb surgery or vestibular impairments. She does not have a seafood allergy and has not regularly consumed multivitamin/fish oil supplements within six months prior to baseline measurements. She is willing to commit to a 24-week dietary supplementation and aerobic exercise regimen and is excited to potentially improve her mobility and cognitive function.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of chronic liver disease. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate hepatic impairment and is stable under medical management. He has a body weight of 80 kg and a BMI of 28. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently on any chronic treatment medication and has not made any significant changes to his medication regimen within the last 14 days. His creatinine levels are within the normal range. His vital signs and laboratory parameters are acceptable for his condition. He has no history of hepatocarcinoma or acute hepatitis. He is willing to use double contraception methods during the study period as he is sexually active.

55 year old man with a history of Type 2 Diabetes diagnosed 8 years ago. He has been on insulin treatment for the past 3 years and has been struggling to achieve good glycemic control. His HbA1c level has been consistently above 9% despite multiple adjustments in his insulin regimen. He requires daily home nursing care for his insulin injections and glucose monitoring. He lives with his wife who is able to provide support and has a nearby caregiver who can provide assistance if needed. His total daily insulin dose is 0.8 U/kg. He has had a recent fundus examination that showed no proliferative retinopathy. He has a good understanding of the benefits and harms of the automated insulin delivery system and is willing to participate in the study. He has healthcare insurance coverage and has received verbal and written information about the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 15yo male student attending a public secondary school in Barcelona, Spain. He has no prior history of mental health disorders but has noticed feelings of anxiety and stress related to schoolwork and social pressures. His parents have also expressed concerns about his behavior and mood swings. The patient is able to understand and communicate fluently in Spanish and Catalan. The patient is interested in participating in the "EspaiJove.Net" study to learn more about mental health and how to cope with stress and anxiety. He is willing to sign the informed consent form and commit to attending the intervention program sessions.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian man who was admitted to the ICU after a severe car accident resulting in multiple fractures, including a broken pelvis and ribs. He was intubated and sedated with a combination of hypnotics and opioids to manage his pain. He has been in the ICU for 2 days and is currently calm and alert with a RASS score of -1. He has no history of cognitive disorders and his Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28 out of 30. He has social security coverage and has given his informed consent to participate in the study. He has no known neurodegenerative diseases and is not pregnant. His family members are supportive of his participation in the study. The patient is not delirious, and the results of the Confusion Assessment Method in ICU (CAM-ICU) are negative. The patient is currently receiving sedatives and analgesics to manage his pain. The study investigators will assess the patient's decision-making capacity using the Johns Hopkins adapted cognitive examination (ACE) and observe the impact of sedatives on his decision-making capacity.

The patient is a 41-year-old man who was diagnosed with COVID-19 and is currently admitted to the ICU due to severe pneumonia. He is experiencing shortness of breath and rapid breathing, with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute. The patient has a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of less than 200 despite receiving oxygen therapy for at least 15 minutes at an FiO2 of 0.50 or higher. He has an intact airway protective gag reflex and is able to follow instructions. The patient has not been intubated during this hospital admission and has not experienced cardiopulmonary arrest. He has a Glasgow coma scale of 14 and no tracheostomy or upper airway obstruction. The patient is not pregnant and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials that prohibit co-enrollment. He is a candidate for the helmet non-invasive ventilation trial for COVID-19 patients.

Patient is a 25-year-old male from the United States who is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications and has no history of hormone disorders. He has a normal BMI and reports a balanced diet and regular exercise routine. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that examines the effectiveness of a standardized 1µg adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test, and salivary cortisol concentration during the test. He has no clinical suspicion of hypoadrenalism and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

A 58 year old male smoker with a history of COPD presents with worsening dyspnea, cough and sputum production for the past couple of months. He reports feeling more fatigued and has experienced a decrease in exercise tolerance. His medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently taking amlodipine. Physical examination is significant for decreased breath sounds and wheezes on auscultation. Pulmonary function tests were performed and reveal a FEV1/FVC ratio of 45%. The patient has no contraindications for non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (NPPV) or inspiratory muscle training (IMT). He is willing to participate in a clinical trial exploring the potential benefits of the new rehabilitation method of "IMT - NPPV sequential".

35 yo F with history of IBS diagnosed 3 years ago with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating and constipation. Patient has undergone endoscopy to exclude organic lower gastrointestinal pathology. Despite trying different medications, including antispasmodics and laxatives, patient still suffers from IBS symptoms. Patient's physician has prescribed Progut (1 capsule per day) as a new treatment option. Patient has no known allergies and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Patient will be followed up for up to 12 weeks while taking Progut to assess its tolerability and effectiveness in improving her IBS symptoms.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF = 35%). She has been diagnosed with NYHA Class III symptoms (fatigue, shortness of breath, and limited physical activity). Her medical history also includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and loop diuretics. She has not been hospitalized for heart failure in the past 12 months. Her most recent NT-proBNP level was 1500 pg/mL. She has not had a myocardial infarction, coronary artery bypass graft surgery, or other major cardiovascular surgery in the past 90 days. She has not had a stroke or TIA in the past 90 days. Her blood pressure at Visit 2 was 140/80 mmHg. She has no known liver disease or impaired renal function. She has never used a SGLT-2 inhibitor. She is willing to participate in the EMPEROR-Reduced trial and has provided signed informed consent.

25-year-old female with regular menstrual cycles and no history of polycystic ovary syndrome presents for participation in a clinical trial. She is fluent in both English and Spanish and is willing to provide written informed consent. She reports using condoms as her method of birth control and agrees not to attempt to become pregnant during the study. She has negative pregnancy test results and normal laboratory values. She is willing to remain in the clinic overnight for pharmacokinetic assessments. She denies using any hormonal products or narcotics, and is not currently taking spironolactone. She has no history of liver disease and her liver enzymes are within normal limits. She does not have an intrauterine device in place and has not used oral contraceptives in the last two weeks. The patient has no significant abnormal findings on screening examination and she is deemed eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) 3 years ago due to non-inflammatory degenerative joint disease. She received the EVOLUTION® TKA system with cruciate sacrificing inserts. She has been experiencing mild discomfort and occasional stiffness in her knee, but overall she reports improved function and mobility compared to before surgery. The patient is willing and able to complete required study visits and assessments and plans to be available for the 10-year postoperative follow-up visit. She has no history of substance abuse or emotional or neurological conditions that would pre-empt her ability or willingness to participate in the study. Her body mass index (BMI) is 29.4. She is currently not enrolled in another clinical investigation and is willing to sign the approved Informed Consent document.

55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with decreased vision in his left eye. Fundus examination revealed macular edema involving the center of the macula in the left eye. Retinal thickness as assessed by OCT is above 300 um in the left eye. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) ETDRS letter score of 60 (20/63) in the left eye. The patient has not had any previous treatment with anti-angiogenic drugs in either eye. The patient is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures, and is willing to provide a signed informed consent form. The patient has no history of ocular inflammation, vitreoretinal surgery, or laser photocoagulation in the left eye within 90 days of Day 1. The patient does not have high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy in the left eye. The patient does not have any other ocular condition that could compromise VA or require medical or surgical intervention during the study period. The patient has no history of systemic anti-angiogenic agents administration within 180 days before Day 1. The patient has controlled blood pressure and diabetes mellitus, defined as systolic <160 mmHg, diastolic <95 mmHg, and Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) < 10%. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to practice adequate contraception during the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and a persistent cough for the past few months. She has no significant past medical history and does not smoke. She underwent a chest x-ray and CT scan that revealed numerous bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. A biopsy of the lung tissue was performed, and the diagnosis of sarcoidosis was confirmed. She has not received any immunosuppressive therapy in the last six months and is willing to participate in the study procedures, including undergoing venipuncture and/or bronchoalveolar lavage. She is not pregnant and has no contraindication to undergo the study procedures.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with mild traumatic brain injury (TBI) two years ago. Since then, she has experienced cognitive dysfunction, including difficulty with memory and concentration, as well as behavioral problems, including irritability and mood swings. She has not responded well to previous treatments and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to try a new medication, tolcapone. She is fluent in English and is able to come to Sheppard Pratt Towson for the baseline evaluation and testing and for the duration of the protocol. She has a stable medication regimen and has not participated in any other investigational drug trials in the past 30 days. She does not have any active alcohol or substance use disorders, nor does she have any history of cardiovascular disease or liver disease. She is not currently taking tolcapone or any other medications that can interact with tolcapone. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period. The patient has a recent structural neuroimaging (within 1 year or since the time of the onset of cognitive complaint)-noncontrast head CT or MRI-to rule out any gross lesion inconsistent with the diagnosis of MCI (e.g. subdural hematoma, normal pressure hydrocephalus, demyelinating lesion, infarct, or mass lesion).

The patient is a 60-year-old male veteran who was recently diagnosed with low-risk prostate cancer during a routine screening. His PSA level was 9.5 ng/mL, and a prostate biopsy revealed a Gleason score of 6 (3+3). He has opted for active surveillance and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of vitamin D3 supplementation in preventing the progression of his cancer. He has no history of any other malignancy, sarcoidosis, or lithium use. His serum creatinine, phosphate, and calcium levels are within the normal range.

A 32-year-old female diagnosed with major depressive disorder 2 years ago. The patient presents with depressed mood, loss of interest, and pleasure in most activities, fatigue, hypersomnia, decreased appetite, and weight loss. She feels hopeless and helpless most of the time and has suicidal thoughts at times. She denies any history of mania or hypomania. She has been treated with SSRIs in the past with minimal improvement. She has no history of psychotherapy. She is currently not taking any medication for depression. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence. She is a single mother of a 5-year-old daughter, and she is currently unemployed. She has an undergraduate degree in English literature. She has mild anxiety, no history of psychotic symptoms or bipolar disorder. She speaks German fluently, and her cognitive and physical abilities are adequate for participating in the study.

The patient is a 3-year-old girl brought to the emergency department due to diarrhea and vomiting for 2 days. Her parents noticed that she has decreased urine output and poor oral intake which led them to bring her to the hospital. Upon physical examination, she appears to be dehydrated with a capillary refill time of 4 seconds. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her lungs are clear. She is planned to have a nasogastric tube inserted for rehydration as part of her management. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has no known allergies.

A 42 year old man with a history of alcohol dependence presents to the clinic seeking treatment for his addiction. He has been drinking heavily for the past 10 years and has attempted to quit on his own several times but has been unsuccessful. He is currently experiencing withdrawal symptoms such as tremors, anxiety, and insomnia. He lives within commuting distance of the treatment program and has a reading level of at least 6th grade. He is willing to provide consent to participate in the study. He has not received treatment for alcohol use disorder in the past 12 months. He does not have any current organic mental disorder or psychotic disorder.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy with limited success. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, meaning he can carry out light work, but is restricted in physically strenuous activity. He has no known autoimmune diseases and his organ and marrow function are within normal range. He is currently not undergoing any other concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.

A 55 year old male patient has recently undergone lobectomy for lung cancer and is now in the process of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. He is generally in good health, but has been largely sedentary due to his cancer diagnosis and treatment. He has no history of ar-rhythmia or atrial fibrillation, nor is he currently taking beta-blockers. He is able to perform cycling exercises without difficulty, and has no musculoskeletal problems that would impede his participation in the study. He is generally compliant with instructions from trainers and has no cognitive or emotional problems that would affect his ability to follow the protocol.

A 32-year-old female who underwent liver transplant 3 years ago due to cryptogenic cirrhosis. She has been experiencing recurrent autoimmune hepatitis with no improvement in her liver function despite previous treatment with steroids and other immunosuppressive agents for the past month. She has no known allergies and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to commit to the complete treatment protocol at Duke and is able to read and understand English. Her EBV serology tests were positive when she was first diagnosed with cirrhosis.

A 68-year-old woman has been diagnosed with bilateral OAH with mild to moderate symptoms. She has been experiencing pain, stiffness, and restricted mobility in her hips, which has been affecting her quality of life. She has not undergone any arthroplasty in her lower limbs yet and is currently awaiting primary THR. She has no personal history of chronic inflammatory arthritis (such as rheumatoid arthritis) or cognitive, psychiatric, or neurological disorders that may interfere with the study. She is able to read, understand, and respond to questionnaires and perform functional tests. She has no other comorbidities, and her symptoms do not significantly interfere with the functions of attention, memory, or logical reasoning. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the guidelines provided by the professionals.

A 10-month-old infant with no known health issues is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. The infant has not yet received any influenza vaccine and is otherwise up to date on their routine vaccinations. The parents are willing and able to attend all scheduled study visits and comply with all study procedures. The infant's insurance coverage meets the requirements for participation in the study. The parents have no plans for the infant to participate in any other clinical studies during the study period. The infant has not received any vaccines in the 30 days preceding the first study vaccination. The parents report no known allergies to any vaccine components. There is no history of Guillain-Barre Syndrome in the family. The infant does not have any chronic illnesses that would interfere with the study conduct or completion. The parents are interested in enrolling their child in the study to contribute to a better understanding of the efficacy of high-dose quadrivalent influenza vaccine compared to standard-dose quadrivalent influenza vaccine in young children.

A 25-year-old healthy male who works in an IT firm, and has been wearing hydrogel daily disposable brand contact lenses for the past 2 years. He has no known allergies or history of ocular infections. He has a spherical contact lens prescription of -3.50 D in each eye and refractive cylinder of 0.25 D in each eye. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in each eye. He has no history of ocular surgeries, binocular vision abnormalities or strabismus. He has not participated in any contact lens or lens care product clinical trial within 14 days prior to study enrollment. He has no systemic diseases or autoimmune diseases and is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with contact lens wear. He is willing to adhere to the instructions set forth in this clinical protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been experiencing severe pain and discomfort in his lower back, hip, and leg for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with sciatica by his physician after presenting with severe pain, numbness, and tingling sensations in his lower back and leg. Despite undergoing physical therapy and taking pain medications, his symptoms have not improved significantly. He is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options and improve his quality of life. The patient has no known allergies or coagulation disorders and expresses no fear of needles.

A 55-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis of the knee for 5 years, reporting worsening pain and stiffness in her knee. She has tried various medications, including acetaminophen and NSAIDs, but has not found significant relief. She is otherwise healthy with no known comorbidities and is not pregnant. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new potential analgesic medication for osteoarthritis of the knee.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male volunteers to participate in a study investigating the effects of atazanavir-induced hyperbilirubinemia during human endotoxemia. The participant must not have a history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, hypotension, renal impairment, or liver enzyme abnormalities. They must also not be taking any medication or anti-oxidant vitamin supplements, or have a positive HIV serology or any other obvious disease associated with immune deficiency. The participant must not have had a febrile illness in the week prior to the LPS challenge and must not have participated in a drug trial or donated blood within the past three months. Smoking and history of allergic reaction to atazanavir are also exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 28yo pregnant woman in her third trimester who has recently been diagnosed with cytomegalovirus (CMV) seroconversion during her pregnancy. She is experiencing stress and anxiety due to the lack of information and understanding about the virus and its potential effects on her unborn child. The patient has not experienced any symptoms related to CMV and has undergone ultrasounds that have not shown any criteria of severity. She has been referred to the 3 DAN centers for further monitoring and support. The patient is willing to participate in this study to help improve the care and support of future mothers who may experience similar situations. She has no other concurrent infections or medical conditions that would exclude her from participation in this trial.

A 54-year-old man was diagnosed with stage IV renal cell carcinoma six months ago. The primary tumor was in the right kidney and has metastasized to the lungs and liver. He has undergone two lines of treatment with targeted therapy (sunitinib and pazopanib) with partial response followed by disease progression after both treatments. His current ECOG performance status is 1 and his LDH is elevated (3 times the upper normal limit). His last physical exam and lab study was performed yesterday and showed the results below: Weight: 80 kg Height: 175 BP: 130/80 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 11.8 g/dl WBC: 5200 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 3500/mm3) Plt: 220000 /ml AST: 30 U/L ALT: 36 U/L Alk P: 110 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl ESR: 50 mm/hr The patient has not had any previous surgeries for the removal of tumor tissue, but is eligible for the study as the primary tumor can be surgically removed. He has no history of cerebral metastases or widespread bone metastases. He has no significant toxicities or side effects from previous treatments (CTC ≤ 1). He has no severe allergies or medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study. He is willing to comply with the study protocol procedures and restrictions.

An 80-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis is admitted to the hospital under a geriatrician for acute exacerbation of her arthritis pain. She reports a decreased appetite and unintentional weight loss of 5% in the past month. On examination, she is found to have mild dehydration and oral thrush. Her BMI is 19.7 kg/m². She speaks English fluently and is mentally competent to participate in the study. The expected length of stay is more than 72 hours, and she is not enrolled in the study during her previous admission. The patient is eligible for the malnutrition screening study in acute aged care.

The patient is a pregnant woman living in the catchment area of EPI centres with good accessibility to Agogo Presbyterian Hospital in Ghana. The woman is over 18 years of age and has no history of positive HIV status. She is willing and able to give informed consent. The patient will be recruited during antenatal care visits in her last trimester and will be followed for 12 months after the birth of her child. The purpose of the study is to investigate the development of immunity against malaria in neonates and infants, specifically looking at the impact of parasite diversity, endothelial cell activation, and the influence of microbiota, as well as behavioural and socio-economic risk factors. The study aims to address the high malaria morbidity and mortality in young children in resource-poor countries and to better understand anti-malarial immunity development. The patient will be required to provide biological samples and participate in questionnaires and follow-up visits for the first year of her child's life.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing dry eye symptoms for the past year. She reports a sensation of grittiness, burning, and itching in her eyes, especially after prolonged periods of computer use. She has tried over-the-counter artificial tears, but they only provide temporary relief. She wears glasses for reading and has no significant medical history. She is not currently taking any prescription medications and has never had eye surgery. She is interested in participating in this study to help find a better solution for her dry eye symptoms. She has no current eye disease, infection, or inflammation and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to spend time for the study and understands the time commitment involved.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and occasional alcohol use was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury. Upon arrival to the hospital, he was unresponsive with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 8 and was intubated for airway protection. A CT scan of the head revealed a right-sided subdural hematoma with midline shift. The patient was admitted to the ICU for management of his TBI and subsequent polytrauma including multiple rib fractures and left femur fracture. He underwent surgical evacuation of the subdural hematoma and was started on a standardized treatment protocol for TBI. The patient remains intubated and sedated for airway protection and neurologic monitoring. He has not yet met criteria for a tracheostomy and remains on mechanical ventilation. The patient's family has been informed of the severity of his injuries and has provided consent for his participation in this clinical trial.

22-year-old male who did not attend college and is not currently enrolled in high school. He reports consuming alcohol heavily in the past month, with a minimum of two episodes of 4/5+ standard drinks per occasion. He has no history of substance use treatment and does not consume more than 40 drinks per week. He is interested in participating in a brief personalized feedback intervention to reduce his risk of alcohol-related harms.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years. Despite being on antihypertensive medication for the past 3 years, his blood pressure is not consistently controlled, with a mean sitting diastolic blood pressure of 105 mmHg. He has no history of stroke, hypertensive encephalopathy or heart attack. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is under control with medication. His current medications include candesartan 32 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. He has not had any adverse reactions to these medications, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of aliskiren plus hydrochlorothiazide in patients with moderate hypertension. He is also open to participating in the optional study extension with triple therapy with amlodipine 5 mg and aliskiren 300 mg plus HCTZ 25 mg if eligible.

42 yo F presents with pain in the right TMJ that has been worsening over the past 6 months, rated as a 7/10 on a VAS scale, with associated stiffness and difficulty opening mouth to eat. Patient reports no prior surgeries or trauma to the TMJ. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the right TMJ and a limited range of motion with a maximal mouth opening of 30mm. Patient is diagnosed with TMJ arthralgia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the effectiveness of corticosteroid administration following arthrocentesis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known allergies to medications or history of pregnancy.

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus (DM) presented to the emergency room with complaints of excessive thirst, frequent urination, and abdominal pain for the last 24 hours. The patient reported that he has been non-compliant with his insulin regimen for the past week due to financial constraints. He denied any history of recent illness, trauma, or surgery. The patient's vital signs were within the normal range. Upon examination, the abdomen was soft and tender, with no guarding or rebound tenderness. Blood glucose levels were found to be 500 mg/dL, and serum bicarbonate levels were low, indicating diabetic ketoacidosis. The patient was admitted to St. Mary's Medical Center for further management of DKA. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the study and was enrolled for the evaluation of the DKA protocol.

A 42-year-old female patient presents with a history of ovarian cancer. She underwent surgical and chemotherapy treatments for her cancer and has been disease-free for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing psychosexual distress since her cancer diagnosis and is reluctant to discuss her concerns with her doctors. She has been feeling isolated and alone in her struggles and is interested in finding a support group to connect with other women who have gone through a similar experience. She has access to a computer and the internet and is fluent in English. She is willing to discuss her psychosexual concerns and is interested in participating in the GyneGals online support group intervention. She has no major psychiatric illness and is not acutely suicidal. She provides informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, scheduled for elective open colonic surgery due to colon cancer. The patient has been compliant with medications and has not experienced any recent hospitalizations or complications related to his comorbidities. Preoperative evaluation revealed no significant abnormalities in laboratory values or physical examination. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided independent consent to participate.

A 30-year old woman who works as a graphic designer is currently 8 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a history of a healthy lifestyle, exercises regularly and eats a balanced diet. She has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. She is married and lives with her husband in a small apartment in Munich. She speaks fluent German and is excited about her pregnancy. She is concerned about gaining too much weight during pregnancy and wants to maintain a healthy lifestyle for herself and her baby. She is willing to participate in a lifestyle intervention program that focuses on diet, physical activity, and weight monitoring during pregnancy to ensure the best health outcomes for her and her baby.

55 year old male who underwent a heart transplant 5 years ago and is currently being followed up at Marie Lannelongue Hospital. The patient has a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease which led to a heart transplant. The patient is in good overall health and has been compliant with follow-up appointments and medication regimen. The patient has undergone routine endomyocardial biopsies during the first post-operative year but is now eligible for the "no biopsy approach" for follow-up. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo echocardiography to detect early acute allograft rejection. The patient understands the potential benefits and risks of the study, including reduced risk of complications associated with endomyocardial biopsy and improved quality of life.

A 42-year-old woman with a history of Crohn's disease affecting her small intestine, specifically the ileum, presents to the hospital for a laparoscopic ileo-caecal resection. She has never undergone abdominal surgery for Crohn's disease before. The patient is currently not on corticosteroids and is not pregnant. She speaks French fluently and has no hearing impairments. The patient has no prior knowledge or experience with self-hypnosis.

A healthy 30-year-old woman who enjoys outdoor activities and frequently goes on hikes is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of a tick repellent. She has no known allergies or skin disorders affecting her forearms where the product will be applied. She does not smoke and is willing to refrain from smoking for 24 hours prior to and during each test. She is able to understand and comply with the study procedures and is willing to provide informed consent. She is not pregnant, nursing, or intending to become pregnant during the time period of the study. She has no serious cardiac or respiratory disorders, and her immune system is not compromised. She is willing to have hair clipped from her wrist area (3cm upwards from wrist line) and can stand unsupported for periods of at least 5 minutes. She has no known history of tick bite allergies or phobia of ticks or tick bites. She is not an employee or spouse of an employee of the Study Sponsor (Citrefine Inc.) or arctec, and is not a student of Professor James Logan or any other faculty members involved in the study.

A 30-year-old woman in her 32nd week of pregnancy presents with a headache, nausea, and blurred vision. Her blood pressure is elevated at 160/100 mmHg, and a urine test reveals proteinuria. She is diagnosed with severe preeclampsia and is admitted to the hospital for close monitoring. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has not had any complications during her pregnancy prior to this point. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to participate in research studies related to her condition to help improve understanding and treatment options for preeclampsia.

42 year old man diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) ten years ago. He has undergone various treatments, including psychotherapy and medication, but has not experienced significant improvement in his symptoms. Two years ago, he received deep brain stimulation (DBS) in the bilateral bed nucleus of stria terminalis (BNST), which has helped him manage his OCD symptoms. He is now willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating unilateral stimulation of the left BNST to assess its efficacy. He experiences compulsive behavior related to cleanliness and washes his hands excessively. He is able to provoke this behavior within a clinical setting. He does not report any personality changes or cognitive impairment due to chronic DBS.

A 45-year-old female patient who was diagnosed with Triple Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) six months ago is seeking treatment options. The patient has undergone one regimen of chemotherapy for her metastatic disease, but her cancer has progressed. She has no history of cardiovascular impairment, serious marrow suppression, or intercurrent illness. Additionally, the patient has no history of any psychiatric disorders or altered mental status. She is willing to comply with the study protocol for the duration of the study and has agreed to use adequate measures of contraception in the opinion of the Investigator. The patient is seeking participation in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of the AR-inhibitor bicalutamide for AR-positive TNBC.  The patient is also willing to make available the paraffin-embedded tissue or slides from the diagnostic biopsy or surgical specimen for confirmation of diagnosis.

This is a 62-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent pain and limited mobility of her right shoulder due to osteoarthritis. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and corticosteroid injections, but has not found relief. After consulting with her orthopedic surgeon, she has decided to undergo a total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) with subscapularis repair. She meets the eligibility criteria for the RESTOR study, which is investigating whether the use of Regeneten implant can improve rates of subscapularis healing and clinical outcomes. She is willing to participate in the study and will be randomized into either the standard subscapularis repair group or the group that receives standard repair with Regeneten augmentation. She will be assessed pre-operatively and post-operatively at specific time points for one year to evaluate subscapularis repair integrity and healing.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who presented with rectal bleeding, changes in bowel habits, and abdominal discomfort. A colonoscopy revealed the presence of a rectal adenocarcinoma. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not have any known allergies. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is physically active and has no difficulty performing his daily activities. The patient has no history of previous surgeries. His family history is significant for colon cancer in his father. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 68-year-old retired male with a valid Ontario driver's license is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication. He is healthy, has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, and does not take any psychoactive medications. He drives at least three times a week and is comfortable using technology such as driving simulators. He exercises regularly and has no history of substance abuse or sleep disorders. He takes daily multivitamins and anti-hypertensive drugs. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He lives in Toronto and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a family history of colon cancer. He has been experiencing occasional abdominal pain and bloating. His primary care physician has recommended a colonoscopy for further evaluation. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, colonic resection, or other gastrointestinal disorders. He has a body mass index of 28 and is in good overall health. The patient has no history of adverse reactions to bowel preparations and is able to give informed consent. He agrees to participate in the study and is willing to follow the low residue diet prescribed the day before the colonoscopy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been suffering from peripheral arterial disease in the femoropopliteal artery. He has been experiencing symptoms such as pain, cramping, and numbness in his legs while walking or climbing stairs. The patient has been advised to undergo endovascular intervention to relieve his symptoms and has been given the option to participate in the MIMICS-3D study to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and device performance of the BioMimics 3D Stent System. The patient has provided written informed consent for participation in the study and meets all inclusion criteria. He has no known hypersensitivity to nickel-titanium and is willing to comply with site standard of care procedures and follow-up visit schedules.

Patient A is a 35-year-old female who has been smoking cigarettes for the past 10 years. She has tried to quit smoking several times in the past but has been unsuccessful. She is currently working as a customer service representative and lives with her partner and two children. She has noticed a decline in her overall health and quality of life and is interested in receiving support to quit smoking and improve her health. She speaks English fluently and is interested in participating in clinical trials that could help her quit smoking. She is generally healthy and has no major medical conditions.

A 48-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast, HER2 negative, ER/PR positive, stage IIb, with no lymph node involvement, scheduled to receive adjuvant TAC chemotherapy. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has a body mass index of 24 kg/m2 and a performance status of 1. Her renal function is normal, and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of diabetes mellitus or other serious illnesses. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 10-year-old female was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and underwent allogeneic stem cell transplant (HSCT) at a medical center. The patient received conditioning chemotherapy prior to transplant and engrafted with no complications. However, a few weeks after the transplant, the patient developed autoimmune cytopenias, including hemolytic anemia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia, which did not improve with standard treatments such as corticosteroids, rituximab, IVIG, and plasmapheresis. The patient has been receiving daily GCSF at 10 mcgs/kg/day for autoimmune neutropenia despite 2 weeks of treatment, and transfusions of packed red blood cells or platelets 3 times weekly for 2 weeks despite continued treatment. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is being considered for treatment with Bortezomib, an investigational drug that has been used in children with certain types of blood cancers. The patient has not had any documented anaphylaxis to bortezomib and does not have ongoing life-threatening infections, failed engraftment, relapse of primary malignancy, or a transplant from a ≥6/8 matched or haploidentical donor.

As this study is an ancillary to the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study, residents of four geographically defined areas are eligible to participate. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 56-year-old man with a diagnosis of advanced prostate cancer that has spread to his bones. He has been undergoing treatment for the past year, but his disease has progressed despite multiple therapies. His Karnofsky Performance Status is 80%, and his liver function tests and total bilirubin are within normal limits. His calculated creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min, and his serum calcium is normal. He reports occasional tingling in his feet and hands but denies any other significant neuropathic symptoms. He has no history of hepatitis or HIV infection. He has not received any transfusions or radiation therapy in the past 4 weeks, and he is not taking any medications that have inhibitory or inducing activity for CYP 3A4. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate how ketoconazole affects the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of Velcade.

The patient is a 55-year-old Korean man who was diagnosed with essential hypertension two years ago. Despite taking amlodipine, his blood pressure has not been adequately controlled, with readings consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He has no history of allergies to medications or dihydropyridine derivatives. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. He has no other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is interested in making lifestyle modifications to help control his blood pressure and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been suffering from psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has tried various topical treatments and UVB therapy but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She is now considering biological treatment for her psoriasis and has been informed about a clinical trial investigating miRNA and mRNA expression before and during biological treatment. She is interested in participating in the trial as it may provide insights into the underlying mechanisms of psoriasis and could potentially lead to individualized treatment options. She meets the eligibility criteria of the trial and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

A 6-month-old male infant was brought to the emergency department by his parents due to a seizure episode that lasted for about 2 minutes. The parents mentioned that the baby had been febrile for the past 2 days, and they had been giving him acetaminophen for the fever. The baby had no previous history of seizures or any neurological disorders. He was born full-term via normal vaginal delivery, and his birth weight was 3.2 kg. The baby was exclusively breastfed and had no known allergies. On physical examination, the baby was febrile, tachycardic, and tachypneic. The neurological examination was unremarkable, and there were no meningeal signs. The laboratory analysis showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia. A lumbar puncture was recommended per current guidelines, and the results showed normal cerebrospinal fluid parameters. The baby was diagnosed with a febrile seizure and was discharged home with instructions to continue acetaminophen for fever management.

Maria is a 28 year old Latina woman who lives in Harlem. She has struggled with her weight for several years and her BMI is 30, which categorizes her as obese. She has tried various diets and exercise plans in the past, but has not been able to sustain significant weight loss. She speaks fluent English and is able to participate in physical activity. She is not currently pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the next year. She does not have a history of bulimia or surgery for obesity. She does not have any severe comorbid diseases that can lead to unintentional weight change, including cancer, HIV/AIDS, or congestive heart failure. She is not currently participating in another weight loss program or trial and is not on medications for obesity. She is excited to participate in the SCALE study and hopes to achieve a sustained weight loss of 7% or more over 12 months by making small changes in her eating behavior and increasing her physical activity.

This is a 46-year-old female who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer with brain metastases. MRI brain imaging showed the presence of 2 brain metastases with a maximum diameter of 3.5 cm. She had previously undergone taxane-based chemotherapy with anthracyclines. A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue block was made available for biomarker evaluation. Prior to enrollment in the study, she provided signed and dated informed consent, and expressed willingness to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1. She has not received whole brain radiation therapy and does not have leptomeningeal disease. She has not been previously treated with antiPD-1, antiPD-L1, antiPD-L2, antiCD137, or antiCTLA-4 antibody. She has no known autoimmune disease or interstitial lung disease that may interfere with the detection or management of suspected drug-related pulmonary toxicity. Her medical history does not indicate any condition that would increase the risk associated with study participation or study drug administration or that would interfere with the interpretation of safety results. She has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or study drug components.

The patient is a 25 year old male who is a regular gym-goer and likes to engage in recreational physical activities such as soccer and basketball. He is currently pursuing a degree in business administration and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He has no history of cardiovascular, musculoskeletal or metabolic disease and is a non-smoker. He is interested in maintaining his physical health and is looking for ways to improve his vascular function and muscle strength. He is willing to commit to an 8-week intervention period and is open to the idea of receiving heat therapy, moderate-intensity cycling training, or both. He is looking forward to learning more about his body's response to different training modalities and

The couple is a 32-year-old female and a 33-year-old male who are both carriers of a genetic mutation of cystic fibrosis. They have been trying to conceive for over 2 years with no success. The couple has undergone genetic counseling and has decided to undergo IVF with preimplantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) to avoid transmitting the genetic mutation to their offspring. The couple has confirmed the presence of the genetic mutation through a laboratory report from a CLIA certified laboratory. The female partner has a regular menstrual cycle and has never been diagnosed with any significant medical conditions. The male partner is in good health and is willing and able to provide a semen sample. Both partners are willing to undergo confirmatory testing through CVS/Amnio once pregnancy occurs. The female partner's FSH level is 8.5, which indicates good egg quality and a high likelihood of successful egg stimulation during the IVF cycle.

John is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma based on biopsy results. He has undergone allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) from an HLA-identical unrelated donor based on high-resolution typing using Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center (FHCRC) matching. He had no prior exposure to brentuximab vedotin. The post-transplant donor CD3+ chimerism of > 50% in sorted peripheral-blood CD3+ cells was documented. John is currently enrolled in an FHCRC non-myeloablative allogeneic transplant protocol. He is at least 28 days out from the transplantation and no more than 60 days out from the procedure. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant hepatic dysfunction. His absolute neutrophil count is > 1,000 cells/mm³, and his serum creatinine is within normal limits. John has no history of moderate/severe peripheral neuropathy, HIV, or hypersensitivity to brentuximab vedotin. He is willing and able to use an effective method of contraception during the study and for at least 30 days after the last study dose of brentuximab vedotin. John is able to give informed consent.

This is a 42-year-old female patient who was previously diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and completed the standard Anti-tuberculosis treatment course. However, she has now developed a relapse of her tuberculosis symptoms, with persistent cough and sputum production, and is acid-fast bacilli smear positive by microscopy. The patient is considered unfit for DOTS and is not currently pregnant. She does not have any clinical signs of concomitant diseases such as diabetes mellitus or acute renal failure, nor has she had any infectious diseases including TB/HIV or HIV positive status. The patient has not taken any alternative therapies in the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effect of homeopathy as an adjuvant to Anti tuberculosis treatment on sputum conversion and clinical outcomes.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has a personal history of major depressive episode. She has been in clinical remission for the last year, taking antidepressants and attending regular psychotherapy sessions. She has no history of cognitive impairment, substance abuse, or bipolar disorder. Her family history is negative for bipolar disorder. She has no current psychiatric symptoms and her BDI-21 score is 5. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of depression and its treatment. She has no contra-indications to MRI and is not currently pregnant. She agrees to be informed of any abnormal findings during the MRI scan.

A 35 yo healthy female who does not smoke and has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 presents for a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of AG-881 on the pharmacokinetics of a single dose of lamotrigine. She has no history of significant medical conditions, and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has undergone bilateral tubal ligation and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She agrees to use contraception during the study period. She understands the study procedures outlined in the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the protocol. She has not used any drugs, including prescription and non-prescription medications, herbal remedies, and vitamin supplements, for 14 days prior to the first dosing and throughout the study. She has not been on a diet incompatible with the on-study diet within the 30 days prior to the first dosing and throughout the study. She has not participated in another clinical study within 30 days prior to the first dose.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy adult with no history of major chronic diseases such as coronary heart disease, angina, myocardial infarction, stroke, diabetes, congestive heart failure, and cancer. They are interested in participating in a study that explores the associations between diet quality and leukocyte telomere length. The patient is willing to comply with the dietary requirements and restrictions of the study and is within the age range of 20 to 65 years.

The patient is a 28-year-old male living in Colombia. He owns a mobile phone and is fluent in Spanish. He works as a sales representative for a local company and enjoys playing soccer in his free time. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication regularly. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the accuracy of noncommunicable disease risk factor surveys.

A 44-year old office worker presented with a painful right inguinal hernia that has been noticeable for a few months. He has no past medical history of note, except for high blood pressure which is treated with medication. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and is overweight, with a BMI of 30. He has never undergone surgery before and he is nervous about it. The patient is an English speaker and is able to read and understand the language used in the registry's questionnaires. He has been scheduled for a hernia repair procedure with a synthetic mesh implantation using an ETHICON mesh product. He has been informed about the registry and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 53-year-old Japanese man who was diagnosed with follicular lymphoma 3 years ago. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiotherapy but unfortunately, the cancer has recurred. He currently has measurable disease with a diameter of 3 cm. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and weighs approximately 68 kg. He has no history of plasma cell neoplasm or major surgery within the last 4 weeks. The patient has not received any immunotherapy, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or experimental therapy within the last 4 weeks. There is no evidence of central nervous system involvement. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (Btk) Inhibitor PCI-32765 for patients with recurrent mature B-cell neoplasms.

A 34-year-old male construction worker presented to the clinic with pain and swelling in his left ankle. He had a history of ankle sprain two weeks ago while on the job. The pain had persisted, and he was unable to bear weight on the affected ankle. On examination, the ankle was swollen, tender to touch, and had limited range of motion. The attending physician recommended an arthrocentesis to relieve the pressure and obtain synovial fluid for analysis. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or comorbidities, and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for two years. She has been experiencing hand pain and swelling for the past six months, which has been interfering with her daily activities. She has tried various medications but has not found significant relief. She is willing to wear Isotoner three-quarter length gloves and attend a review appointment four weeks after glove provision. She is able to give informed consent and is interested in taking part in the study to find out if the arthritis gloves will work for her.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy woman who works as a graphic designer. She wears contact lenses and has no history of eye diseases. She has never tried any visual diagnostic device before. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the research and learn more about her eye health. She has no allergies or sensitivity to pupil dilation ophthalmic solutions. She has no history of glaucoma or cardiac dysrhythmia. She has never been diagnosed with light sensitivity or photosensitive epilepsy. She is willing to get her pupil fully dilated for the research study. She has no history of any medical conditions that could affect her participation in the study.

55 yo M with a history of Stage 4 venous insufficiency, peripheral neuropathy, and obesity. Patient has had multiple venous leg ulcers in the past, but has recently healed from an ulcer with intact epithelium. Patient reports experiencing pain and discomfort in the lower legs and ankles, particularly after standing or sitting for prolonged periods of time. The patient is able to perform the required protocol activities and is willing to make the necessary study visits. The patient is English-speaking and has access to phone, email or mail communication. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, but does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

Pt is a 67yo F postmenopausal with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, currently well controlled on medications. Patient reports feeling fatigued and less physically active in recent months, and experiencing occasional chest discomfort with exertion. Patient had a recent EKG that showed no significant abnormalities but was referred to the study by her primary care physician due to her high risk of HFPEF. She reports willingness to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. She is not on loop diuretics and has not had a recent MI, stroke, angina, or atrial fibrillation. Her glucose levels are controlled and her renal function is normal. She is excited to participate in the study and hopeful for potential improvement in her cardiac and skeletal muscle health.

A 48-year-old female was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma and has undergone one course of prior chemotherapy. After a few months, the disease relapsed, and she is currently experiencing significant fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss.
