She has no other significant past medical history and reports no allergies. She is a non-smoker and social drinker. Her family history is negative for cancer. Her physical examination reveals generalized lymphadenopathy, and her laboratory tests show elevated lactate dehydrogenase levels. She has a Zubrod performance status of 1. She has undergone screening for HLA-matched allogeneic stem cell transplantation and found to have a 6 out of 6 HLA A-, B-, and DR- identical sibling donor. She is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She is HIV negative, and her cardiac and pulmonary functions are within normal limits. She has a life expectancy of more than six months. She is willing to use effective contraception during the trial.

Patient is a 25-year-old male from Nigeria who has been diagnosed with sickle cell trait. He is currently not experiencing any sickle cell crises and has no known medical problems. His past medical and drug history are unremarkable. His BMI is 22, BP: 118/72, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for normal renal and liver function, blood count within normal limits, and negative for syphilis, hepatitis B and C, HIV, and HTLV-1. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, cancer, or cardiovascular disease. He has no allergies to G-CSF or bacterial E. coli products. The patient has no history of G-CSF administration or leukapheresis.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, swollen legs, and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes a day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a carpenter and is physically active at work. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

67-year-old Caucasian male with a history of smoking (30 pack-years) was diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastasis to the liver and bones. He received four cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy followed by immunotherapy, but progressed on therapy. Currently, he is experiencing moderate fatigue and shortness of breath with minimal exertion. He has no history of brain metastases or other significant medical problems. His ECOG PS score is 1. His laboratory studies show normal hematopoietic function, liver enzymes, and renal function. He has no active infections or other contraindications to the study drugs. He has no history of allergies to any of the agents or any of the ingredients. He is willing to take contraceptive measures during the study and within 6 months after the study. He is able to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of liver disease and recurrent ascites requiring large volume paracentesis (LVP) every month for the past 6 months. The patient has been experiencing low blood pressure with a systolic reading consistently below 100 mmHg. The patient has not undergone liver transplant, TIPS, or evaluation for multiple organ transplant. There is no history of malignancies, primary renal diseases, or chronic kidney disease. The patient has not experienced grade 3 or 4 encephalopathy, and the patient's Child C cirrhosis or model for end stage liver disease (MELD) score is not greater than 20. The patient is not actively using recreational drugs or alcohol. The patient is experiencing discomfort and inconvenience due to the frequent LVP and is looking for an alternative treatment option. The patient is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effectiveness of midodrine in reducing the frequency of LVP and improving symptoms associated with ascites.

A 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing sudden, overwhelming feelings of fear and anxiety for the past few months. She often feels like she is losing control or having a heart attack. These panic attacks frequently occur without any apparent trigger and are accompanied by physical symptoms such as sweating, trembling, palpitations, and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of depression and has been previously treated with fluoxetine, which was discontinued due to sexual side effects. She currently has a HAM-A score of 21 and has not used any medication for the past 3 months. She is currently not using any illicit drugs or alcohol. She has no history of OCD, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or bipolar mood disorder. She is not taking any antipsychotic medication and has not changed her antidepressant or mood stabilizer dosing in the past 2 months. She has no history of adverse reactions to risperidone or paroxetine.

60-year-old male with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing dialysis three times a week for the past 6 months. The patient has a sedentary lifestyle due to fatigue, limited mobility, and lack of motivation. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and peripheral neuropathy causing numbness and tingling in the feet. The patient is overweight and has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m². The patient has not undergone any regular physical activity programs and is interested in improving his quality of life and overall health. The patient is able to walk unassisted for short distances but has limited endurance. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide signed informed consent.

A 38-year-old female, with no history of medical problems, has been diagnosed with CIN 2 and will require a conization procedure. She has been referred to the anesthesia team at Grenoble Mutualist Hospital group (GHM) for consideration of hypnosis as an alternative to general anesthesia (GA). The patient is anxious about the procedure and is concerned about the potential risks and side effects of GA. She is interested in hypnosis as a potential alternative to reduce anxiety and improve her overall experience. The patient is affiliated with social security and has no legal guardianship or trusteeship.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. He describes the pain as constant and moderate in intensity, which requires him to modify his daily activities. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications without much relief. He has no history of back surgery, trauma, or spinal pathology. He is able to walk without assistance but does experience some difficulty with balance. He has no history of other significant medical conditions and is currently taking medication for hypertension. He scores a 26 on the Folstein Mini-Mental State Examination and has no significant visual or hearing impairment. He does not have a pacemaker and does not experience significant pain in other parts of the body. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his low back pain and overall function.

A 62-year-old male diagnosed with localized T1a renal cell carcinoma with a maximum tumor volume of 20 mL. He has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy, with a performance status of 1. The patient has adequate marrow, liver, and renal function, and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to comply with all requirements, including adequate method of birth control.

A 9-year old boy named Jack has been diagnosed with ADHD. He is in the fourth grade and has been having difficulty with concentration and impulsivity, which has resulted in a significant decrease in his academic performance. Jack's parents have tried behavioral interventions, but they were not effective. Jack's medical history is significant for seasonal allergies, but he is otherwise healthy. Jack is currently taking 40 mg of methylphenidate daily, but his symptoms have not improved as expected. Jack's parents are interested in enrolling him in this clinical trial to potentially improve his symptoms. Jack is a bright and active child who enjoys playing sports and video games. He is friendly and cooperative during his medical appointments.

A 42-year-old man was diagnosed with schizophrenia 2 years ago. He has a history of impulsive aggression towards others and himself. His aggression episodes have caused him to be hospitalized multiple times, and he has had involvement with the criminal justice system. He is currently taking risperidone and lithium to manage his symptoms. He has completed high school and was previously employed as a construction worker. He has no significant medical history or current medical conditions. He speaks and reads English fluently, and his auditory and visual acuity are adequate to complete cognitive tests. His Mini Mental Status Exam score is 28 at screening. He has agreed to participate in the study and has the capacity to give consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman residing in French Guyana. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes for which she takes medication regularly. She presents to the hospital with sudden onset of weakness and numbness on the right side of her body, along with difficulty speaking. She is diagnosed with a suspected first symptomatic CVA and undergoes a cerebral imaging examination (CT-scan and/or MRI) to confirm the diagnosis. She is able to answer questions personally and provides informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of prior symptomatic CVA and does not have any other severe evolutive disease that could cause death in the weeks following the CVA. She is reachable by phone and agrees to follow up at 1 month.

The patient is a 51-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IIIC ovarian cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been cancer-free for a year and a half and is currently taking medications for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. Her last follow-up visit with her oncologist was six months ago, and she has been experiencing some physical and emotional symptoms such as fatigue, anxiety, and pain during intercourse. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand her quality of life and identify any potential issues that can be addressed. She is able to understand and fill out questionnaires and is willing to provide written informed consent according to ICH/GCP and national/local regulations.

52 y/o male who underwent kidney transplant 3 months ago with a calculated creatine clearance of 40 ml/min and a serum creatinine level of 1.5. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis, with a T-score of -2.5 at the spine and -2.8 at the hip on DXA scan. The patient has not experienced any vertebral or non-vertebral fractures in the past two years. The patient is currently taking calcium with Vitamin D supplements. The patient has no abnormalities of the esophagus and is able to stay upright for 30 minutes. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is using an effective form of birth control. The patient does not have hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia. The patient has not been treated with bisphosphonates within the past year. The patient is able to undergo DXA testing. The patient does not have cancer.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with several chronic conditions, including heart failure, hypertension, and osteoarthritis. She has been receiving care from a Home Nursing Care Services SSIAD for several months, but has had multiple hospitalizations due to complications from her conditions. She has expressed interest in participating in the study and her family caregiver has also agreed to participate. She is able to understand and respond to study questionnaires and evaluations with the assistance of her caregiver. She lives in the territory of activity of the SSIAD participating in the assessment and has social coverage. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who recently returned from a trip to the Peruvian Amazon. She presents with fever and chills and reports a history of headache, nausea, and body aches. The physical examination reveals an axillary temperature of 38.5°C, and a rapid diagnostic test for malaria is positive for Plasmodium falciparum. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history, and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to follow-up visits for a period of 42 days. She has no known allergies to any of the drugs used in the study. The patient is willing to be hospitalized for the first 72 hours of the study for close monitoring and administration of artesunate. She has no contraindications for the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old man was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after experiencing headaches and vision changes. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor within the last 28 days and has recovered well from the procedure. He has no prior history of cancer and has not received any prior treatment for brain tumors. He is willing to forego cytotoxic and non-cytotoxic drug therapy against the tumor while being treated with lenalidomide. He is in good overall health with no significant medical illnesses that would compromise his ability to tolerate the treatment. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and is willing and able to comply with all study requirements. He will begin partial brain radiotherapy 4-7 days after beginning lenalidomide, and within 35 days of the surgical procedure that established the diagnosis. He has no metastases below the tentorium or beyond the cranial vault and has no history of hypersensitivity or development of a desquamating rash while on thalidomide. He is HIV negative and has no active infectious hepatitis or chronic hepatitis. He has no serious concurrent medical illness and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to practice adequate contraception during the trial.

Patient A is a 40-year-old female who is interested in maintaining a healthy lifestyle. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and is currently not pregnant or post-menopausal. She has no history of liver or kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension, stroke or myocardial infarctions, thyroid disease, celiac/gastrointestinal disease, HIV positive or AIDS. She does not have any chronic use of medications or fibre, nor any swallowing difficulties. Patient A has no allergies or sensitivities to any of the test meals. She is normotensive with a systolic blood pressure of 120mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 80mmHg. Patient A is interested in participating in the study to help improve her understanding of the effects of incorporating soluble fibre into refined carbohydrate foods on postprandial blood glucose levels. She is willing to complete both the sensory evaluation and acute crossover RCT in order to provide valuable data to the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old man with a history of chronic liver disease, specifically cirrhosis, and has been experiencing symptoms of decompensation such as fatigue, loss of appetite, and jaundice. He has been under the care of a gastroenterologist and has been on treatment to manage his liver disease. He has not experienced any infectious complications thus far. His liver function tests have been abnormal with elevated levels of bilirubin, AST, and ALT. He has not undergone liver transplantation or any other invasive liver procedures. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further the understanding of the disease and to potentially benefit from any new treatment options that might arise.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing a dull, persistent pain on the outside of his elbow for the past six months. The pain is exacerbated when he lifts objects or performs repetitive motions with his right arm. He has tried pain relievers and ice packs, but the pain persists. Upon examination, he was diagnosed with chronic lateral epicondylalgia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options and improve his condition. He is in good overall health and has no other conditions affecting his right arm. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent form.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing severe asthma symptoms for the past 6 months. She has been treated with a fixed combination of fluticasone propionate/salmeterol at a dose of 250/50 mcg twice daily for the past 3 months. Despite this treatment, she has had uncontrolled asthma with an asthma control questionnaire (ACQ-7) score of 2.0. She has a documented physician diagnosis of severe asthma consistent with global initiative for asthma (GINA) step 4 clinical features. She has a pre-bronchodilator FEV1 of 65% of predicted and has shown airway obstruction proven to be reversible by an improvement of FEV1 of 15% and 300 mL after inhalation of a short-acting bronchodilator. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no history of allergies or idiosyncrasies to roflumilast or montelukast. She is willing to use acceptable contraceptive methods during the study. She has provided written, informed consent and meets all other inclusion/exclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of dry eyes for the past 6 months. She reports a sensation of burning, stinging, and itching in her eyes, especially after spending time in front of a computer screen or in an air-conditioned room. She also complains of redness and occasional blurred vision. She has tried over-the-counter artificial tears without much relief. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist notes the presence of corneal and conjunctival staining. The patient has not had any ocular surgery or trauma in the past 4 months, nor has she had punctal plugs or punctal occlusion. She does not wear contact lenses and is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment for dry eye syndrome.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has a BMI of 22. She reports good overall health and is not taking any medications or supplements known to affect the study outcomes. She has no known history of diabetes, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cardiovascular, peripheral vascular, cerebral vascular, pulmonary, or renal disease. She has no allergies. She exercises regularly and has been instructed to maintain her regular physical activity level during the study. She lives with her partner and has a full-time job. She has no dietary restrictions and consumes a balanced diet. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and undergo imaging and blood draws for research purposes. She has no active smoking habits.

A 32-year-old man with a history of HIV infection has been receiving treatment at the Medical Faculty Associates Infectious Diseases clinic for the past 4 years. He has been experiencing symptoms of fatigue and weight loss lately and suspects that his viral load may have increased. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy but has missed a few doses in the past month due to forgetfulness. He is aware of the importance of adhering to his medication regimen and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He is married and has two children. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. He is currently unemployed but has been actively seeking employment. He is interested in participating in the study as he believes it may help in the development of a more efficient and cost-effective diagnostic tool for HIV detection.

25-year-old pregnant woman who has attended her first antenatal care visit at a health facility in Maseru district, Lesotho. She knows her HIV status and is willing to participate in a study to improve maternal and child health outcomes. She resides in an area around the study facility and is able to provide informed consent. The woman does not have any significant medical or psychological conditions that would preclude active study participation.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with PVR grade C in the left eye. He experiences a sudden onset of floaters, flashes and blurred vision in his left eye. The patient has undergone two surgeries for the same condition in the past, but both were unsuccessful. He is otherwise in good health and has no other ocular or systemic disease. Visual acuity in the left eye is counting fingers at 1 meter. He has no known drug allergies. Examination of the left eye reveals a total retinal detachment with a large retinal tear at 10 o'clock position. The intraocular pressure, anterior segment, and right eye examination are normal. OCT shows macular edema. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of repeated methotrexate injections for PVR grade C.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 6 months ago. After induction chemotherapy, she underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation from an HLA-matched unrelated donor. However, 2 months after the transplantation, she developed acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) involving the skin, gut, and liver. She was treated with high-dose corticosteroids, but her aGVHD remained unresponsive. Despite the added treatment of DLI, her aGVHD became progressive. She was then referred for consideration of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy. The patient has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate. Her physical exam and lab study results were performed yesterday and showed the following results: A tired looking woman, icteric, cooperative, and alert. Weight: 65 kg, Height: 167 cm, BP: 110/70, HR: 90/min, RR: 20/min. Hgb: 10 g/dl, WBC: 4500 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 2000/mm3), Plt: 60,000 /ml, AST: 80 U/L, ALT: 120 U/L, Alk P: 150 U/L, Bill total: 5.5 mg/dl, CMV PCR: Negative, EBV PCR: Negative.

This is a 56 year old male with a past medical history of stage IV pancreatic adenocarcinoma, diagnosed 9 months ago. The patient underwent a Whipple procedure followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. Despite the initial response, there was a progression of disease with the development of liver and peritoneal metastases. The patient was then treated with folfirinox chemotherapy but had to discontinue due to neuropathy. The patient is currently receiving palliative care, but has expressed interest in participating in clinical trials for potential treatment options. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health with no significant comorbidities. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and undergo blood sampling for pharmacokinetic and pharmacogenetic analysis. The patient has acceptable safety laboratory values with WBC of 4.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count of 150 x 10^9/L, serum bilirubin within normal limits, ALT and AST levels within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal and creatinine less than 150μmol/L. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has no psychological, familial, sociological or geographical conditions that could hamper compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer two years ago. He underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy and was declared cancer-free after six months. However, routine MRI scans revealed the presence of two small, asymptomatic brain metastases measuring 0.5 cm each. The patient has no neurological symptoms, and his Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score is 90. He is currently taking targeted therapy for his lung cancer. The patient has no history of other medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. He is interested in participating in the observation registry to avoid unnecessary treatment for his brain metastases.

48yo male with a history of type 2 diabetes for 10 years, currently managed with metformin 1000mg twice daily, with a most recent HbA1c of 9.2%. He has a history of hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and obesity with a BMI of 32. Despite his current medication regimen, he reports difficulty controlling his blood glucose levels and has experienced intermittent episodes of hypoglycemia. He also reports symptoms of fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and joint pain. He is a native English speaker and is registered on kp.org. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better prioritize his care during upcoming visits with his primary care provider.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with metastatic renal cell adenocarcinoma. He has multiple metastatic sites, including lung, bone, and abdominal lymph nodes, and has a Karnofsky score of 80%. He has no prior history of systemic chemotherapy, organ transplantation, or cytokine therapy. The patient has a creatinine level of 1.5 mg/dL, hematocrit of 35%, WBC count of 6,500/mm^3, and platelet count of 130,000/mm^3. His bilirubin level is within normal range, and his LVEF is 55%. He is not pregnant or nursing, and has tested negative for HIV and hepatitis B surface antigen. He has no severe lung, liver, or kidney conditions that would preclude study treatment, nor any severe neuropsychiatric condition, epilepsy, or serious thromboembolitic disorder. He has no other concurrent primary malignancies. The patient is willing to comply with the study treatment and follow-up schedule and has no geographical, psychological, or familial condition that would preclude study participation.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of right above knee amputation due to a traumatic injury. He has been using a prosthesis for the past 8 months and has been experiencing discomfort and difficulty with walking on uneven surfaces. He is currently classified as a K2 ambulator and is interested in improving his mobility and comfort. He does not have any history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. He is not currently experiencing any pain or discomfort in his residual limb or other foot. He is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He is married with two adult children and works as a software engineer. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve his prosthesis fit and function.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is concerned about his weight and overall health. He is 5'11" tall and weighs 220 pounds, giving him a BMI of 30.7. He has no history of diabetes and is not taking any medications known to impact glucocorticoid metabolism. He has not used any glucocorticoids within the last 6 months. He has been experiencing some difficulty with weight loss and has noticed that his energy levels have decreased over time. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the role of an enzyme called 5-alpha reductase (5αR) in regulating how the body handles sugar and fat. The patient is motivated to make changes in his lifestyle to improve his health and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 27-year-old healthy male from Ghana, who is currently pursuing a degree in computer science, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a preventive vaccine for Lassa Fever. He is in good health with no significant medical history. He has no allergies to any medications or food. He is negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), Hepatitis C antibody and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) antibody. He has no history of immunosuppressive therapy. He exercises regularly and has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He has a regular menstrual cycle and uses condoms as his chosen method of contraception. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the follow-up visits.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to sepsis caused by a urinary tract infection. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, and is currently on medication for both conditions. The patient is unable to eat and will require enteral feeding within the next 48 hours. She is conscious and able to provide written consent for the study, or alternatively, her next of kin can provide consent on her behalf. The patient does not have any severe gastrointestinal or metabolic diseases and is expected to survive for more than 6 days. She has not participated in any drug trials in the past 4 weeks and does not have any other exclusion criteria. The patient will be randomized to receive either Intestamin plus Fresubin or Fresubin alone, and her inflammatory parameters, catecholamine need, and maximal enteral delivery will be monitored after 10 or 14 days.

A 20 year-old female university student with mild to moderate anxiety and depression symptoms for at least six months. She has been feeling anxious most days of the week and has difficulty sleeping. She also feels sad and hopeless at times and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication for her symptoms. She is willing to participate in an 8-week study comparing the effects of physical activity and cognitive behavioral therapy on anxiety and depression. She is able to perform moderate to vigorous physical activities and is willing to increase her physical activity level to one hour daily, 5 days per week for 8 weeks. She understands the study requirements and is willing to attend weekly cognitive behavioral therapy sessions if assigned to group B.

The patient is a 13-month-old male infant scheduled to undergo elective inguinal herniorrhaphy. He was born at full term via uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has no significant medical history. He has received all recommended vaccinations and his growth and development are appropriate for his age. He is not allergic to any medications and has no known family history of adverse reactions to anesthesia. His weight is 9.5 kg and he is in good general health. The parents have provided informed consent for their child to participate in the study, and they are willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The anesthesiologist has determined that the patient is an ASA class 1. The study will involve the administration of a caudal block with ropivacaine prior to the surgical procedure to evaluate the efficacy of preemptive analgesia in pediatric pain management.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes two years ago. She has been using an insulin pen with a 12 mm needle for insulin administration. Her HbA1c level is currently 8.5%, indicating poor blood sugar control. She reports experiencing occasional hypoglycemic events and pain during insulin injection. She is currently taking metformin and glipizide for her diabetes, but her blood sugar levels remain high. She has a BMI of 28 and no significant medical history. She lives alone and works full time as a teacher. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effect of insulin injections using a 5 mm needle with her usual 12 mm needle, in hopes of improving her blood sugar control and reducing the pain and discomfort during injection.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia who is a daily cigarette smoker. She has been smoking for 10 years and currently smokes 10 cigarettes per day. She is aware of the health risks associated with smoking but finds it difficult to quit due to her addiction. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the views and attitudes regarding health risks of cigarette smoking, smoking patterns and motivators for cessation in smokers who suffer from schizophrenia compared to a sample of smokers without a major psychotic disorder. She is willing to participate in a 2-hour visit and answer clinical and demographic information as well as a semi-structured interview. She is not actively trying to quit smoking at the time of the interview.

The patient is a 24-year-old first-time mother who is at 39 weeks of gestation. She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy and has been attending regular prenatal check-ups. She has a BMI of 24 and is physically active, going for a brisk walk for 30 minutes every day. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and she has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use recreational drugs. She has completed high school and works as a receptionist in a law firm. She lives with her partner, who is supportive of her pregnancy and plans to be present during her labor and delivery. She has been experiencing regular contractions for the last few hours and has been admitted to the hospital with cervical dilation of 3 cm. She has not received any pain relief medication yet and is willing to participate in the study.

A 68-year old retired teacher who lives alone and is participating in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA). Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She can walk without assistance and is able to perform her activities of daily living independently. She complains of difficulty in remembering recent events and misplacing her belongings. She has noticed that it takes longer for her to complete her crossword puzzles and her reaction time is slower compared to before. She denies having any history of stroke, head injury, or any psychiatric illness. She has never been diagnosed with dementia or Alzheimer's disease. She takes lisinopril and atorvastatin for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has been participating in the BLSA for over 10 years and is willing to continue with the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old female swimmer who trains regularly at a swimming team in the 4th Region of the State of São Paulo. She has been practicing swimming for the past 4 years and has no significant medical history. She does not smoke, consume alcohol or take any medication regularly. She has not experienced any episodes of muscle-tendon or osteoarticular injuries in the last six months. The patient is currently in good health, with a normal BMI and blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg. She will be able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old male adolescent who is generally in good health with no significant medical history. He has not received any meningococcal serogroup B vaccine before and is not scheduled to receive any HPV vaccine during the study period. He is not currently on any medication, including systemic antibiotics or immunosuppressive therapy. He does not have any known or suspected defects of the immune system or any significant neurological disorder. He has not received any investigational vaccines, drugs, or devices within 28 days before the first study vaccination. The patient will be required to have a negative urine pregnancy test if female.

A 45-year-old man, who works as a delivery driver in a disadvantaged community in Queens, New York, visited his primary care physician for a routine check-up. His BMI is 27 and he has been informed by his doctor that he has pre-diabetes. He is a father of two and spends 6 days a week on his job. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He speaks and reads English fluently and is interested in participating in a diabetes prevention program.

The patient is a 52-year-old Chinese man who was diagnosed with Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer in December 2013. The initial diagnosis was based on a biopsy of a lung mass that was identified during a routine chest X-ray. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which he takes medication. He is married with two children and works as a sales representative. He has a history of smoking two packs of cigarettes per day for 30 years. He has been treated with chemotherapy and radiation therapy at a selected hospital in China. He has been hospitalized twice for his treatment and is routinely followed up as an outpatient. He reports experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and coughing. His performance status is 2. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/85 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl

A 7 year old girl with a history of complex heart problems and surgery is eligible for this clinical trial. She has been receiving regular medical care for her heart condition and has not had any interventions in the past 6 months. She speaks English fluently and is accompanied by her parents to her clinic visits. She does not have any identified cognitive or emotional health disability. She is experiencing some difficulty coping with stress and anxiety related to her medical condition and her parents have reported some behavioural and social problems. The family is interested in participating in the study to help their daughter cope better with the stress associated with her health condition.

Mrs. Lee is a 52-year-old woman who was recently hospitalized for pneumonia complicated by sepsis. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics including carbapenems due to her sepsis. Despite the treatment, she developed a fever and her blood cultures were positive for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE). Her physicians are concerned about the limited treatment options available for her infection and have decided to enroll her in a clinical trial evaluating a novel individualized treatment strategy for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria infections. Mrs. Lee is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria.

This is a 35 year old male who has been diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency and is currently receiving treatment with Norditropin® SimpleXx (somatropin). He has a history of delayed puberty and growth retardation during childhood. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He has been compliant with his treatment regimen and is interested in participating in a study to help further understand the efficacy and safety of somatropin in adults with growth hormone deficiency.

As this is not a clinical trial involving patients, a patient description is not applicable. Instead, I can provide a description of the target participants for this study. The study is seeking nurse managers who are currently working in Finland and are fluent in Finnish. They must be willing to participate in the Ethics Quarter (EQ) educational intervention and provide consent for their data to be collected for the study. The participants must meet the inclusion criteria of working as a nurse manager, while the exclusion criteria include being unwilling to provide consent. The study aims to improve the ethical activity profile of nurse managers and promote ethical management of nursing.

Patient is a 65-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing severe hip pain for the past year, which has been limiting his daily activities. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. X-rays reveal that he has osteoarthritis in his right hip joint. He has been recommended to undergo a total hip arthroplasty (THA) surgery.

Pt is a 35yo M who sustained frost damage to his lower extremities after being exposed to extreme cold weather conditions for several hours. The patient has been diagnosed with frost damage grade III and will need surgical intervention to remove the dead tissue. The patient presents within 24 hours of the injury and is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of heart or lung diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has been randomized to receive hyperbaric oxygen treatment as adjuvant therapy for the frost damage. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male smoker who has recently been diagnosed with small cell lung cancer. He presented with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. Imaging studies revealed a mass in his right lung and biopsy results confirmed a diagnosis of SCLC. He has no history of other malignancies and is otherwise healthy, with no significant comorbidities. He has not received any previous chemotherapy for his SCLC. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the SCOT Registry.

Pt is a 35yo M scheduled for elective surgery in Mulago Hospital. He has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA I. He has not taken any medications or supplements in the past 24 hours. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he has no fever. He has provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 32-year-old woman who was previously enrolled in the East Jakarta Cohort Study is eligible to participate in this follow-up study. She has a healthy 3-year-old child who was born during the initial study. The woman lives in the same neighborhood as the other participants and is willing to participate voluntarily. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The woman is willing to provide blood samples for biomarker assessment and to answer a structured questionnaire regarding her socioeconomic status. She understands the importance of the study and is committed to completing all necessary assessments.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl with intermittent exotropia confirmed by a comprehensive eye examination. She presents to the clinic with a history of occasional drifting of her eyes outwards, especially when she is tired or focusing on near tasks such as reading or writing. Her parents noticed this when she was 7 years old, and it has been gradually worsening over time. She has no history of previous eye surgeries, office-based vision therapy, or regular use of ocular or systemic medications known to affect the accommodation or vergence system. She has no medical history of developmental disability, ADHD, or learning disability. Her birth weight was 3.5 kg, and she was born at 38 weeks gestational age. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and her near stereoacuity is 60 arcsec by the Preschool Randot stereotest. Her cycloplegic subjective refraction spherical equivalent (SE) refractive error is +1.00 D in both eyes. She wears updated refractive correction (spectacles) for the past 2 months. Her distance exodeviation is 14 prism diopters, and her near deviation is 10 prism diopters by prism and alternate cover test (PACT). She meets all inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who was previously diagnosed with cervix cancer and has undergone surgery and chemotherapy. However, her cancer has recurred and she is now experiencing symptoms such as vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain. She has undergone additional testing which has confirmed the recurrence. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive a combination treatment of Niraparib and Dostarlimab. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. The patient has measurable lesions by RECIST v1.1 and has adequate organ function. She has received at least one prior systemic treatment regimen and is able to take oral medications. The patient agrees to not donate blood during the study or for 90 days after the last dose of study treatment. She has a negative pregnancy test within 7 days prior to taking study medication and agrees to use contraception from enrollment through 180 days after the last dose of study treatment. The patient does not have any known active central nervous system metastases or carcinomatous meningitis and has no known history of myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia. She is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding or expecting to conceive children within the projected duration of the study and is not diagnosed with immunodeficiency or receiving systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of study treatment. The patient has not participated in a study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of treatment. She has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent and has not received a live vaccine within 14 days of planned start of study therapy. The patient has not received prior treatment with a known PARP inhibitor and does not have a known hypersensitivity to Niraparib or Dostarlimab components or excipients. The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman who has a history of early stage breast cancer with no more than 4 involved axillary nodes. The patient is not currently experiencing any evidence of the disease. The hormone receptor status is positive, negative, or unknown. The patient has not had any prior malignancy except basal cell skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. The patient has not been diagnosed with porphyria or any other serious disease that would prevent compliance or greatly limit life expectancy. The patient has not undergone any prior randomization into trials comparing effects of chemotherapy and bilateral oophorectomy in premenopausal women. The patient has not been on any concurrent hormonal therapy for breast cancer except tamoxifen or toremifene. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized, open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the safety of hormone replacement therapy in terms of risk of recurrence in women with previously treated, nonrecurrent stage 0-II breast cancer. The patient is willing to be randomized to one of two treatment arms and receive treatment for 2 years in the absence of disease progression. The patient is willing to be assessed for quality of life, gynecological health, and breast cancer at specified intervals during the study period.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese woman who is in good health and has a normal body weight. She is not currently taking any medication and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has not participated in any clinical trials for an investigational drug before. She has no history of suicidal ideation, transient ischemic attack or stroke, epilepsy or seizures. She has no significant skin hypersensitivity or active skin disease. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use double contraceptive barrier method during the study period. She has no medical or psychiatric conditions that could compromise her ability to participate in the study. She has a normal heart rate, blood pressure and pulse rate. She does not smoke or consume more than 3 cups of caffeinated beverages per day. She has no clinically relevant allergy and has not made a blood donation or had a comparable blood loss.

A 45-year-old woman, with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presented with chronic abdominal pain and was diagnosed with gallstones. Due to the severity of the symptoms, it was decided that she would undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient's BMI was calculated to be 32.1, placing her in Group II of the study. She was advised of the study and provided written consent to participate. The surgery went smoothly, and the patient was extubated and moved to the recovery room, where the morphine PCA treatment was started according to her adjusted body weight. The patient's VAS values were recorded in the first 48 hours, and when VAS values exceeded 4, 10 mg/kg Paracetamol IV was used as an escape treatment. Delivery and Demand of the PCA and additional need for analgesics were also recorded during this time. The patient did not have any complications and was discharged after 48 hours.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy from the United States who comes to the clinic with a history of atopic dermatitis. He has been experiencing persistent itching, redness, and dry skin on his arms and legs for the past 3 months, which has been affecting his daily activities and sleep. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. His BMI is within the normal range, and his vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory results are not required for this study.

A 56-year-old female patient who was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory insufficiency requiring mechanical ventilation (MV). She has no history of severe organ dysfunction, active cancer, or acute or chronic organ transplant rejection. The patient has all four limbs intact and mobile and is eligible for and able to participate in physical therapy. Her pre-admission Barthel Index is greater than 70. The patient has no acute kidney injury with a glomerular filtration rate of less than 30 ml/min. The patient does not have high mechanical ventilator settings or alternative modes of mechanical ventilation. She is not on high dose vasopressor agents. Liver function tests were within normal limits. She does not have chronic dementia or cognitive impairment. The patient is able to provide written or witnessed verbal informed consent in English or has a legally authorized representative to provide consent.

55-year-old female with a 6-month history of a white lesion on the left side of the tongue. She is a former smoker who quit 10 years ago and reports occasional alcohol use. The lesion was biopsied and showed mild dysplasia. She underwent surgical excision of the lesion but the pathology report showed moderate dysplasia at the margins. The patient is concerned about the risk of developing oral cancer and is interested in participating in a study that uses new imaging techniques to better detect and monitor potentially malignant oral lesions. She is willing to undergo frequent imaging and brushing procedures to help improve surveillance and diagnosis of her condition.

This is a 35 year old female who has had issues with constipation for several months. She typically has difficulty evacuating and feels a sense of incomplete evacuation after bowel movements. She has tried increasing her fiber intake and fluid intake but has not seen much improvement. She has not taken any laxatives or medications for constipation. She has no known allergies or intolerances to dairy products. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of diabetes or gastrointestinal disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effect of consumption of dairy products with probiotics on constipation. She would be willing to consume 150 ml of milk drink a day, with breakfast or morning snack, for a period of 60 days. She understands that she may be randomized into either the group that receives milk drink with probiotics or the group that receives a probiotic milk drink without. She is willing to attend regular check-ups and fill out questionnaires related to her bowel habits.

57-year-old male recently diagnosed with locally advanced gastric carcinoma that is considered operable. Biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma of the stomach. CT scan and peritoneal lavage revealed no distant metastases or peritoneal carcinomatosis. He has a performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. He has adequate hematopoietic, hepatic, and renal function within limits to allow for treatment with cisplatin. He has no unstable cardiac disease requiring treatment, no significant arrhythmias, and no myocardial infarction within the past 6 months. Ejection fraction is greater than 50% on cardiac sonography. He has no other serious concurrent illness or medical condition that would preclude study therapy. He has no history of significant neurologic or psychiatric disorders. He has not received any prior treatment for gastric carcinoma and is not currently receiving any other experimental or anticancer therapy.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing droopy upper eyelids for the past few years, which has been causing her discomfort and affecting her self-esteem. She has never had any previous eyelid surgeries. During her consultation with the oculoplastic consultant, she was informed about a clinical trial that aims to reduce pain during the administration of local anesthesia in upper eyelid surgeries. She is interested in participating in the trial and has given fully informed consent. She will undergo bilateral upper eyelid surgery under local anesthesia. The patient is generally healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. Her current medications include a multivitamin and an occasional ibuprofen for headaches.

This is a 5 year-old female who has been experiencing tooth pain for the past few weeks. On examination, it was discovered that she has caries in one of her primary mandibular molars that requires pulpotomy and restoration treatment. She has no previous experience of hospitalization or dental visits and has no systemic diseases or developmental disorders. Her parents have agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effect of filmed modelling versus tell-show-do technique on the anxious and cooperative behavior of children during dental practice. The child will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups and will undergo the dental procedure in two separate sessions, with heart rate measurements and behavioral ratings recorded by the attending dentists.

A 9-year-old male, accompanied by his mother, presents with a history of intermittent abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea for the past 6 months. The symptoms have not responded to dietary changes, and he has lost 4 pounds in the past 2 months. The family history is unremarkable. The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. On physical examination, the patient appears healthy and vital signs are within normal limits. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, and there is no hepatosplenomegaly or palpable masses. Laboratory results show no abnormalities. After discussing the options with his healthcare provider, the patient's mother is considering gastro-endoscopy for her son. She is a native English speaker with adequate health literacy. The patient is eligible for the trial and his mother has consented to participate.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who is generally healthy and active for his age. He takes a daily multivitamin and has never smoked or consumed alcohol. He has no history of major medical conditions and takes no prescription medications. He engages in regular exercise, including walking and light weightlifting. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research and potentially improve health outcomes for the elderly population. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with study procedures and requirements. The patient understands that there may be potential risks associated with the study drug and is willing to discuss any concerns with the study team.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is specifically looking for healthy adult males between the ages of 18 and 50 who meet certain criteria. Therefore, any specific patient description would not be appropriate.

A 50-year-old woman who has been in a stable relationship with her husband for the last 20 years is experiencing a decrease in sexual desire over the last few years. She has no personal or family history of psychiatric or chronic medical conditions. She has never experienced any sexual abuse, and she does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. She is currently not taking any medication except for an occasional paracetamol for headaches. She is fluent in German and is willing to answer questionnaires about her sexual function and give a blood sample. She has not had any hormonal contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy in the past year. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to understand the possible genetic factors contributing to the decline in her sexual desire.

A 60-year-old man, who has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee, has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in his knees for the past 3 months. Despite being on paracetamol and NSAIDs at therapeutic doses for the past 2 weeks, the pain has not subsided. He is under the care of a rheumatologist in a private practice. His knee osteoarthritis has been confirmed by x-ray, and it is at stage 3 according to Kellgren and Lawrence. The pain has been interfering with his daily activities, and he is looking for alternative treatments. He is affiliated with social security insurance and is willing to try actiTENS as a non-medicinal analgesic treatment for his pain. He owns a smartphone and is able to download the actiTENS application. He has no allergy to actiTENS electrodes and has no history of neuropathic pain or other painful conditions that could interfere with the study's evaluation.

A 35-year-old Hispanic female presented to the emergency department with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She reported a recent history of exposure to a colleague who tested positive for COVID-19. The patient underwent an RT-PCR test for SARS-CoV-2, which was positive. Within 48 hours of the RT-PCR test, a frontal CXR was performed. The CXR showed infiltrates in both lungs. The patient was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help with the development of an AI algorithm for the detection of COVID-19 pneumonia on chest radiographs.

The patient is a 29-year-old male living in a rural area of Mississippi. He identifies as gay and has multiple sexual partners. He has never been tested for HIV and is interested in learning more about his risk of contracting the virus. He is concerned about the cost of PrEP medication and the distance he would have to travel to access PrEP care at an academic medical center. He is open to receiving PrEP care through telemedicine at a local community-based organization. He is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent. He does not have a known HIV infection.

A 50 year old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia and low HDL-C levels presents at the clinic. He has been taking statins for the last 3 months but his lipid profile remains unchanged. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his lipid levels. He has no history of liver or kidney disease, and is not taking any other medications that interact with CYP3A4. He is willing to comply with the medication and dietary restrictions defined in the protocol, and is not planning on getting a flu shot during the study. He is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are under control with medications. He is an active individual who enjoys running and cycling for exercise. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He owns an iPhone 11 and is comfortable using technology. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about how wearable devices can help manage his condition. He is willing to wear either the Apple Watch Series 6 or the Withings Move for the study period and is willing to use the Hugo mobile health platform. He has a primary care physician at Yale-New Haven Hospital and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital due to an acute exacerbation of her chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She is a smoker and has a history of multiple hospital admissions for respiratory distress. She lives alone in her apartment but has a close friend who visits her regularly. She has difficulty moving around due to her shortness of breath and reports needing assistance to turn in bed. She also has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She can follow simple commands and has no signs of dementia or mental disability. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study. Her chest is clear on auscultation, but she has decreased air entry bilaterally with prolonged expiration. She is on nebulized bronchodilators and systemic steroids. She has no known tape allergy or sensitivity to EKG leads or similar types of adhesives used in common medical products. She agrees to have an area of hair on her chest be clipped or shaved, if needed for patient sensor adhesion.

The patient is a 2-month-old infant living in Korea, who is in good health and has not received any pneumococcal, diptheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio or Hib vaccines in the past. The infant is available for the entire study period of 14 months. The parents of the infant are willing to give their consent for the child's participation in the study.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who loves playing outside and going to the beach with her family. She has fair skin that burns easily and has experienced sunburns in the past. Her parents are concerned about the long-term effects of sun exposure and want to ensure that their daughter is protected during outdoor activities. The family resides in a sunny region and spends a lot of time outdoors. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus 7 years ago. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He has been taking insulin for the past 6 years and is currently on a stable insulin regimen. His total insulin dose is less than 1.2 IU/kg/day. He has never participated in a clinical trial before. He has no history of cancer or severe allergies to drugs or foods. He is generally healthy but occasionally experiences hypoglycemia. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use drugs. He is sexually active but uses condoms as a contraceptive method.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman with a BMI of 22. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. Her family history is negative for diabetes, heart disease, or any other significant medical conditions. She has no allergies or food intolerances. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is willing to participate in a 6-week inpatient study to test the relationship between frequency of meals and hepatic fat content and insulin sensitivity. She understands the study requirements and is able to give informed consent. She has no contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and has not undergone any surgical procedures involving metallic implants, neuromuscular-skeletal stimulators or internal orthopedic screws or rods.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past 6 months. The pain is most pronounced in her knees and elbows, and she has noticed difficulty with mobility due to the pain. She has not been diagnosed with any specific arthritis condition, but her doctor suspects early stage oligoarthritis. She has never been treated with DMARD therapy or oral, intra-muscular, or intra-articular steroid treatment. She is currently taking NSAIDs for pain management, but the dosage has remained unchanged for the past 28 days. She is willing to comply with the terms of the study

The patient is a 68 year old Hispanic male with a past medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and heart failure. He has been admitted to the hospital numerous times in the past year due to exacerbations of his heart failure. He lives alone and has difficulty managing his medications, leading to non-adherence and worsening of his condition. He has also been experiencing shortness of breath and edema in his lower extremities. He is retired and used to work as a construction worker. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a daughter who lives in another state and visits him occasionally. He has been identified as a high-risk patient for readmission and is eligible for referral to the Carolinas HealthCare System's Transition Services (CHS-TS) program, which aims to improve patient outcomes through innovative approaches that leverage analytics and technology, while bridging care coordination and communication gaps. The patient will be randomized into either the CHS-TS or usual care group as part of the Aiming to Improve Readmissions Through InteGrated Hospital Transitions (AIRTIGHT) study. The study seeks to evaluate the effects of the CHS-TS services for patients at high risk for a 30-day readmission. The patient's primary outcome variable will be a 30-day all-cause readmission.

A 34-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis presents with concerns about managing her relapses. She has experienced two relapses in the last year, including numbness and tingling in her arms and legs, and difficulty walking. She has some experience using the internet and feels comfortable navigating websites. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would provide her with a web-based relapse management program. She is willing to commit to at least 12 months of follow-up and is eager to learn more about her condition and how to manage it more effectively. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is willing to sign informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with Non-small Cell Lung Cancer through a non-incisional biopsy. He has not received any previous treatment for lung cancer, and his physician has certified him for a PET scan. He has an Eastern Co-operative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance rating of 1. He is postmenopausal and has no history of sexually transmitted diseases. He reports clinical symptoms consistent with NSCLC and has a fasting blood glucose of less than 200 mg/dL. The patient is able to tolerate SPECT/CT and PET/CT imaging, and is able to make the scheduled appointments within the designated time windows. His safety laboratory values are within normal range. He understands and provides signed informed consent. He has no known hypersensitivity to EC-DG or FDG or similar compounds including any of the inactive ingredients. He has not been exposed to any investigational agent within 30 days prior to the screening visit or participating in an ongoing clinical study.

A 16-year-old female patient with a history of anorexia nervosa is admitted to the ISL unit at Melrose Institute for treatment. The patient has a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes and is currently using an insulin pump. The patient's BMI is 16, and she has a history of self-injurious behavior, but it is currently under control. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent. She is able to communicate in English and has no regular use of acetaminophen or acetaminophen-containing medications. The patient is willing to utilize the CGM system and perform required calibrations using self-monitored blood glucose.

A 25-year-old female came to the clinic complaining of itching, redness, and dryness on her skin. She mentioned that she has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few months and have tried using over-the-counter creams without much success. She was diagnosed with atopic eczema according to Hanifin and Rajka criteria. The affected areas are two comparable lesional areas of 20 - 50 cm2 with a distance of at least 5 cm, with clinical condition of atopic eczema mild to moderate. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is using a medically accepted contraceptive regimen. She has not participated in another clinical study involving pharmaceutical products in the 28 days preceding or during the study. She is not known to have any allergic reactions to components of the study preparation and the comparator. She has not been treated with systemic or locally acting medications which might counter or influence the study aim within two weeks before the beginning of the study.

A 65-year-old man presents with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He has been on medication for both conditions for the past 5 years. He also has a history of dyslipidemia with LDL-cholesterol levels consistently above 160 mg/dL despite treatment with statins. His fasting glucose levels range between 110 and 130 mg/dL. He is currently overweight with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and has a sedentary lifestyle. He reports occasional constipation and bloating, but no other relevant digestive symptoms. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has no history of psychiatric disorders and has good cognitive function. He is interested in improving his quality of life and achieving a healthier lifestyle. He is able to follow scheduled visits and is willing to comply with the dietary intervention. He reports no food allergies or intolerances.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been referred for an abdominal ultrasound due to suspected gallstones. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, respectively. The patient denies any significant abdominal pain or discomfort but has been experiencing occasional nausea and vomiting. She has no known allergies to medications or imaging contrast agents. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial and is interested in learning more about the potential uses of ultrasound technology in medical education and patient care. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to complete a questionnaire to provide feedback on her experience with the ultraportable ultrasound technology.

An 8-year-old boy fell off his bike and injured his elbow. The elbow was swollen and painful, and the parents took him to the hospital. X-rays revealed a dislocated fracture of the Epicondyles ulnaris. The fracture was more than 5 mm, and the doctors recommended operative treatment with screw fixation. The boy has no relevant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is able to follow the procedures of the study, and his parents have provided informed consent. He has not been enrolled in the current study before, and he meets all the inclusion criteria. The boy does not have any of the applicable absolute and relative contraindications listed in the MAGNEZIX® CBS and CSc 4.8 mm instruction for use.

Patient A is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a complex aortic aneurysm. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. His aneurysm measures 6.5cm in diameter and has grown 6mm within the last 6 months. He has been advised by his physician that he is eligible for an elective repair of TAAA with BEVAR and has been given the option to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and performance of the BGP+ balloon expandable covered stent Graft System implanted as bridging stent in BEVAR. Patient A has a landing zone in his target vessel of at least 20mm and the coverage/wall adaptation of the BGP+ stent should be obtained for at least 12mm. The access vessel for introduction of the sheath through which the BGP+ will be advanced is 5mm. Patient A has no early important division branch from the target vessel with risk of coverage and no dissection. His renal arteries, superior mesenteric artery, and celiac trunk have a diameter between 6 and 8mm. Patient A understands the nature of the procedure and has provided written informed consent prior to enrollment in the trial. He has a projected life-expectancy of at least 12-months and is willing to comply with specified follow-up evaluations at the specified times. Patient A has not been previously implanted with a stent in the target vessel and does not have a renal artery with >100° cranial orientation. He is not currently participating in another investigational drug or device trial that has not completed the entire follow-up period.

The patient is a 12-year-old African American girl who was diagnosed with persistent asthma at the age of 6. She has been taking daily controller medication since then and has had several exacerbations over the years. She currently uses a combination inhaler with fluticasone and salmeterol twice a day. She has a history of allergies to dust mites and pets. Her past medical history is unremarkable and she has no other chronic illnesses. She has access to a smartphone with iOS operating system and is fluent in English. Her parents have given their consent for her to participate in the study.

43-year-old male with a history of lower back pain following a lumbar discectomy surgery 1 year ago. The patient has tried multiple conservative treatments including physical therapy, pharmacological therapy, and interventional pain procedures but has not seen any significant improvement in their pain. The pain is localized to the lower back and rated 80 mm on the VAS scale. The patient is willing and able to comply with the follow-up schedule and protocol and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient has no active infections or coagulation disorders and is not currently using any anticoagulants. The patient has not had corticosteroid therapy or radiofrequency treatment of an intended target DRG in the past 30 days and does not have any active implantable devices. The patient has not been diagnosed with cancer in the past 2 years and does not have any anatomical spinal abnormalities that are anticipated to require further surgery.

A 52-year-old male patient was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the lung with brain metastases. The metastases are unresectable according to the neurosurgeon. The patient is currently undergoing radiation therapy with palliative intent. The patient has a Karnofsky performance score of 80 and extracranial metastases. The patient's hemoglobin is 11 g/L, and his serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL with a 24-hour creatinine clearance of 75 mL/min. The patient's liver function tests are within normal limits. The patient's body weight and composition have been stable for the last month. The patient has no history of treatment for brain metastases or primary brain tumors. The patient does not have any hematologic malignancies or solid tumors of germinal origin. The patient is not allergic to L-arginine.

A 27-year-old female with epilepsy has been on treatment for the past year with a stable dosage regimen of carbamazepine. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and has a serum 25(OH)D level of 25 ng/ml indicating hypovitaminosis D. She has no history of hypercalcemia, nephrolithiasis, fractures, hepatic disease, kidney disease, or granulomatous disease. She is not currently taking any vitamin D supplements. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effect of different doses of vitamin D3 supplementation on serum 25(OH)D levels. She will be randomized to receive either 1000, 3000 or 6000 IU of vitamin D3 once daily for 16 weeks. She will attend clinic visits at 8 and 16 weeks to monitor her serum 25(OH)D levels.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing progressive loss of vision and is currently at the Light Perception (LP) level in both eyes. He has no significant medical history apart from his RP diagnosis. He is retired and lives with his wife who helps him with daily activities. He has no history of smoking or drug use. His visual acuity in the eye to be implanted is poor, but he has a history of reading vision in that eye. The patient has undergone a pseudophakia surgery three months ago. His fluorescein angiogram shows retinal vascular perfusion in all four quadrants of the macula. The patient has evidence of inner retinal function (ganglion cells and optic nerve function) by the EEP test, which has identified the ability to elicit phosphene thresholds. His ERG shows rod and cone non-function. He is willing and able to give written informed consent and participate in ongoing follow-up. The patient has no ophthalmic conditions other than RP with relevant effects upon visual function. He has no other ocular disease that affects the retina and/or optic nerve function. There is no opacification of ocular structures that prevents clear image transmission. He does not have nystagmus or cystoid macular edema within the target region for implantation shown via Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). His retina is not detected as too thin as shown via OCT (<100 μm) to expect required functionality of inner retina, and OCT shows layering of the inner retina in the central region. There is no scar tissue (e.g., epiretinal, intraretinal, subretinal, macular pucker) within the target region for implantation. There is no heavily clumped pigmentation at the posterior pole that would interfere with image transmission to the vision chip. There is no anterior segment pathology that interferes with clear visualization of the retina (e.g., presence of cloudy or scarred cornea and/or papillary membrane) that cannot be resolved prior to entrance into the study. The patient has no history of amblyopia reported earlier in life for the eye to be implanted. He has no systemic diseases that might imply considerable risks with regard to the surgical interventions and anesthesia (e.g., cardiovascular/pulmonary diseases, severe metabolic diseases). The patient has no condition and/or allergic contraindication to pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative medication. There are no health problems where general anesthesia is contraindicated. There is no disease or condition that would probably limit life expectancy to less than 1 year from screening. There is no orbital deformity that would interfere with surgical implantation that could not be resolved prior to entrance into the study. The patient has no plastic intra-ocular lenses, or other materials that would interact with silicone oil. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use a medically acceptable means of birth control for the duration of the study. The patient has no neurological and/or psychiatric diseases (e.g., Parkinson, epilepsy, MS, depression, or severe anxiety). The patient has cognitive and emotional ability (e.g., no depression or severe anxiety) enabling participation as assessed by psychiatric evaluation. The patient has not participated in another interventional clinical trial within the past 30 days. The patient does not need regular administration of anticoagulants, platelet aggregation inhibitors, or analgesics containing acetylsalicylic acid. The patient does not have a disease or condition that likely requires regular use of MRI or other similar imaging technology that emits electromagnetic radiation. The patient is willing to avoid participating in vigorous sports or activities with a high risk of a head injury. The patient is willing to avoid security-scanning devices that would result in a full body, manual search. The patient has the ability to perceive form or motion under optimal conditions (largest size, brightest lighting, highest contrast, etc.) of form and motion testing as tested by BaLM, BaGA, and Landolt C.
