The patient does not have hearing deficits and cochlear implants, nor will he be implanted with cochlear implants in the near future. The patient is not undergoing or requiring medical treatments generating induced currents in the area of the implant such as electrosurgery, diathermy, neurostimulation, electroconvulsive therapy, ionizing radiation therapy, therapeutic ultrasound. The patient has an active immunization status against organisms causing meningitis.

54F with a history of breast cancer diagnosed in 2014, status post lumpectomy, radiation therapy and currently on hormonal therapy with no evidence of disease. Patient was referred to oncology for evaluation of multiple liver lesions on imaging. Biopsy confirmed metastatic breast cancer. Patient has been treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy but has progressed on all of them. Patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. A recent MRI showed multiple liver lesions, the largest measuring 4.5cm. Patient is willing to participate in clinical research and has signed informed consent. Prior to study enrollment, patient will undergo baseline laboratory testing, imaging and a tumor biopsy. Patient has no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, no history of immunodeficiency, solid organ transplant, or tuberculosis. Patient is willing to use highly effective methods of contraception during the study.

A 30-year-old healthy female presents for the clinical trial of GSK Biologicals' NTHi candidate vaccine. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. She has not participated in any clinical trial in the past 30 days nor does she plan to in the future. She is of childbearing potential, but uses adequate contraception and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements. She has never received any vaccine containing NTHi antigens. She has no known immunodeficient condition or any clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic or renal functional abnormality. She is not pregnant or lactating, nor is she planning to become pregnant or discontinue contraceptive precautions during the study period. She does not have any history of chronic alcohol consumption or drug abuse. Her laboratory screening tests are within normal limits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has noticed fine lines and wrinkles on her face and neck. She has Fitzpatrick skin type III and has never had any cosmetic treatments on her face or neck. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses an acceptable method of contraception. She has no known allergies to facial or general skin care products and does not have an active systemic or local skin disease that may affect wound healing. She has not had any recent significant trauma to the areas to be treated and does not have significant scarring or cystic active and clinically significant acne in the treatment areas. She is willing to withhold aesthetic therapies to the areas of the face and neck being treated or judged to potentially impact results by the Investigator. She is willing to cooperate and participate by following study requirements for the duration of the study and to report any changes in health status or medications, adverse event symptoms, or reactions immediately. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to read, speak, write, and understand English.

Patient is a 46-year-old male from the United States who has been receiving home parenteral nutrition for the last 18 months due to complications from intestinal surgery. He has a central venous catheter in place for the administration of the nutrition. His past medical history is significant for Crohn's disease and he is currently on immunosuppressive therapy. His vital signs are stable, and he reports no recent infections or complications related to the catheter.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who recently tested positive for hepatitis C virus (HCV) through nucleic acid testing. He has not yet developed HCV antibodies. He is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He denies any history of drug use or needle sharing, but had a blood transfusion after a car accident about 6 months ago. He is currently experiencing mild fatigue and occasional stomach discomfort, but otherwise has no symptoms. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form. He is fluent in English and meets all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who presents with symptoms of urinary frequency, urgency, and urge incontinence for the past six months. She has tried behavioral modification techniques and anticholinergic medications with no improvement in her symptoms. She has a history of urinary tract infections but currently does not have an active infection. She has no history of bladder tumors or previous urinary tract surgeries within the last six months. She has normal renal function and is not undergoing hemodialysis. She has no history of heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, or severe neurological disease. She has not used Botox in the past year. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study requirements.

The patient is a 52-year-old Indian male who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 6 months. He has been taking Acupil® for the past 4 weeks with no significant side effects. He has a history of smoking and consumes alcohol occasionally. His blood pressure at Week 0 visit was 150/90 mm of Hg. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has provided a personally signed and dated informed consent document to participate in the study.

Pt is a 35yo M with a history of a minor burn injury to his right forearm. He presents to the hospital for a scheduled excision and grafting procedure on the burned area which is less than 15% of his total body surface area. The procedure will require the removal of a piece of skin from a non-dependent body surface area to cover the burned area. He has no systemic abnormalities and is not taking any medications that can compromise wound healing. The burn does not involve the harvesting area, and he has not previously undergone any skin grafting procedures. The patient agrees to participate in follow-up evaluations.

A 52-year-old male patient was diagnosed with esophageal cancer and underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, the cancer has metastasized to other organs, and the patient's condition has worsened. The patient is experiencing severe fatigue, difficulty swallowing, and weight loss. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is expected to live for at least three more months. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial for a new treatment option and is able to provide informed consent. The patient has no history of blood-borne infectious diseases or immune diseases, and is not currently taking immunosuppressants or steroids. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use effective contraception if applicable.

A 60-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for 5 years. He is currently on medication for his diabetes, hypertension, and lipids. His current HbA1c level is between 7.5-10%. He is capable of giving informed consent and completing the study. He is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials and has not taken antibiotics in the last 3 months. He is not on insulin therapy and does not have any known food allergies. He is not currently eating dates or raisins and can be washed out for 4 weeks. He is not pregnant or nursing and does not plan to become pregnant in the next 3 months.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who has been experiencing urinary symptoms such as difficulty starting and stopping urine flow, weak urine stream, and frequent urination for the past few months. He is also complaining of lower back pain and discomfort in the pelvic area. He has a family history of prostate cancer, as his father was diagnosed with the disease when he was in his 70s. The patient has never been diagnosed with prostate cancer before and has not undergone a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Upon examination, his prostate is enlarged and firm. His PSA level is elevated (10.2 ng/mL) and a biopsy confirms the presence of metastatic prostate cancer. The patient has no history of connective tissue disorder, and his performance status is good (ECOG PS 1). He is willing to undergo radiation therapy and has a life expectancy of more than 2 years based on his current health status.

63 year old female with a 6 year history of Parkinson's disease, characterized by unilateral tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia. The patient has been on levodopa/carbidopa 25/100 mg three times daily, pramipexole 1.5 mg twice daily, and rasagiline 1 mg daily with good symptom control. The patient has also reported chronic constipation for the past 2 years, with decreased stool frequency (less than 3 bowel movements per week), and has tried multiple over-the-counter laxatives with no improvement. The patient has no history of dementia and is able to provide reliable answers to the questionnaire. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials at the time of the visit.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with sepsis-induced acute lung injury. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well controlled with medication. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation upon admission. His chest X-ray showed bilateral opacities consistent with pulmonary edema. He met the inclusion criteria for the trial within 24 hours of admission. The patient has no known allergies to medication and is willing to participate in the trial. His liver function tests, thyroid function tests, and cardiac enzymes are all within normal limits. He has not received any statin medication within 48 hours prior to randomization. The patient has no history of intraparenchymal CNS bleed or myocardial infarction within the past 6 months. He is willing and able to utilize the ARDS network 6 ml/kg predicted body weight ventilation protocol. The patient is conscious, alert, and able to provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who suffered chest trauma due to a car accident. He had three rib fractures and a small hemopneumothorax that was treated with chest tube placement. He is a smoker with a 20-pack-year history and has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. He complains of severe pain in his chest and difficulty breathing deeply. He does not have any other significant medical history or allergies. On physical examination, he has tenderness and bruising over the chest area, but there are no other significant findings. His vital signs are stable, and his oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. His chest x-ray shows the presence of rib fractures and a small residual pneumothorax. He has been started on pain medication and is receiving conventional chest physiotherapy. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effect of Positive Expiratory Pressure (PEP) breathing on his recovery.

Maria is a 58 year old post-menopausal woman who presented to the clinic with vaginal itching and discharge. She reports mild discomfort and odor. She is sexually active with her husband and uses condoms as a form of birth control. She has no history of vaginal infections and is not currently taking any antimicrobial therapies or medications that would interfere with the outcome of the study. Her physical exam reveals erythema of the vulva and vagina with a moderate amount of yellow-green discharge. She has no fever, abdominal pain or dysuria. All other laboratory values are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the study to find an effective treatment for her symptoms.

This is a 32 year-old female who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has regular menstrual cycles, normal pelvic examination, and evidence of ovulation by transvaginal ultrasound and/or normal mid-luteal serum progesterone. Her partner has also undergone a normal semen analysis according to WHO guidelines. She has no history of pelvic surgery or pelvic inflammatory disease, and is not currently using hormonal contraception or an IUD. She does not have a history of endometriosis or any pelvic pathology such as uterine fibroids or ovarian cysts. She has no general medical disorders and does not smoke. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with sudden onset severe headache and vomiting. He had no history of hypertension, diabetes or smoking, and he was not taking any medications. His neurological examination revealed no focal deficits, and his Glasgow coma scale score was 15. A non-contrast CT scan showed a diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage with no evidence of intracranial hematoma. He underwent a cerebral angiogram, which showed a small aneurysm in the anterior communicating artery. The patient was scheduled for endovascular coiling of the aneurysm. He has never taken a statin before and has no known liver dysfunction. His Hunt-Hess scale score is 2.

A 48-year-old Japanese male was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath for several weeks. The patient underwent biopsy, which revealed anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive NSCLC. He was started on chemotherapy but experienced severe side effects and had to discontinue the treatment. The patient is currently seeking alternative treatment options and has expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial. He is in otherwise good health, with no significant medical history or comorbidities. His current medication regimen consists of over-the-counter pain relievers and occasional use of an inhaler for his respiratory symptoms. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up assessments.

A 62-year-old male patient visited the clinic with symptoms of abdominal pain, weight loss, and jaundice. He had been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 months. He reported no history of smoking or alcohol intake. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were controlled with medication. His family history was non-contributory. After undergoing various imaging studies, he was diagnosed with a suspected pancreatic malignancy. His endosonographer deemed the target lesion safe and feasible for the necessary study passes. He agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent. He is scheduled to undergo EUS-FNA with equal cytological samples to be examined by digital image analysis and conventional cytology respectively. The investigators will compare the efficacy of DIA and conventional cytology in diagnosing pancreatic cancer. A blood sample will also be collected for advanced study.

54-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma in the oral cavity. She has no history of cancer and is otherwise healthy with no significant comorbidities. She is scheduled for definitive radiotherapy with curative intent with or without concomitant chemotherapy. The patient is willing and able to give full written consent according to the protocol approved by the Regional Ethics Committee. She has adequate renal function with a Creatinine clearance of 80 ml/minute. The patient has no general contraindications for MRI and no serious comorbidities that would compromise her ability to complete the study or interfere with the evaluation of the study objectives. She is committed to participating in the study and has no plans to withdraw for any reason during the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is currently undergoing androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). He is experiencing moderate to severe fatigue, which is affecting his daily life and ability to work. He has not received any therapeutic touch, Reiki, Polarity Therapy, or professional massage therapy during the prior four weeks. He is able to read English and is willing to participate in the study. He understands the potential benefits and risks of the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not scheduled to receive surgery, chemotherapy, radium 223 therapy, abiraterone, enzalutamide, Sipuleucel-T, or radiation therapy during the next 10 weeks. He is not taking erythropoietin or darbepoetin for anemia. He does not have a bleeding disorder, blood clot, previous neck/back injury, or any other medical condition that would, in the estimation of his physician, preclude him from having massage therapy.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who was previously diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme. She underwent a right frontotemporal craniotomy with gross total resection followed by adjuvant radiation therapy with concurrent temozolomide. She completed a total of six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide and has been clinically stable for the past six months. She is currently being evaluated for eligibility in National Cancer Institute research protocols. The patient has no significant past medical history other than the glioblastoma multiforme and has no history of tobacco or alcohol use. She is currently taking levetiracetam for seizure prophylaxis. MRI of the brain shows no evidence of recurrent tumor.

A 45-year-old female patient with recurrent ovarian cancer presents for consideration in a Phase 1 clinical trial for oral metronomic topotecan and oral pazopanib to treat recurrent/persistent gynecologic tumors. She was initially diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer and underwent surgical resection followed by chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. After completing treatment, she was in remission for 14 months before the cancer recurred. She then received second-line chemotherapy with gemcitabine and carboplatin but experienced disease progression after 5 cycles. She underwent debulking surgery followed by a third-line chemotherapy regimen consisting of liposomal doxorubicin, but her CA-125 levels continued to rise. She is now seeking alternative treatment options and is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has a Gynecologic Oncology Group performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least six months. She has adequate bone marrow, liver, renal, and cardiac function as assessed by the study's criteria. She has measurable disease according to RECIST version 1.0. She has not had more than two prior treatments for her recurrent ovarian cancer, including chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, investigational therapy, radiation therapy, etc. She has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up. She is not pregnant and agrees to use adequate contraception. She has no history of central nervous system metastases or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.

The patient is a 35 year old female who visited her dentist for a routine check-up and was found to have two decayed molars. She has no significant medical history and no known allergies to dental materials or local anesthetics. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not received any restorative treatment on her teeth in the last 12 months. She is willing to provide voluntary written informed consent and is in good medical health to tolerate the dental procedures. She has no abnormal oral soft tissue findings and does not have any condition affecting salivary flow. She is willing and able to have dental radiographs and photographs taken of her dentition and soft tissues. The two decayed molars are in occlusal function and are in contact with the neighboring tooth on at least one surface. The buccal to lingual/palatal width of both teeth is equal to or greater than 1/3 the distance from buccal to lingual/palatal cusp tips. The study teeth are vital and do not exhibit clinical signs of periapical pathology. She is eligible to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who recently had a dental consultation for a non-molar tooth that requires extraction and replacement with a dental implant. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. Her oral hygiene is excellent, and there is no evidence of infection or inflammation in the area of the affected tooth. She has no known allergies to any materials or medications used in the study. She is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent approved by the University of Louisville Human Studies Committee.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who underwent a single lung transplantation due to end-stage lung disease. He is currently in stable condition and will be discharged from the hospital soon. As part of his post-operative treatment, he will be required to perform daily spirometry tests at home to monitor his lung function. He has access to a cell phone and is able to use it to transfer his spirometry recordings to the transplant center. He has no history of long-term care dependency or restricted ability to communicate. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve post-operative treatment for future lung transplant recipients.

This is a 28-year-old female who is sexually active with a man and is interested in helping researchers develop new products that can protect against HIV and other sexually transmitted infections. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to explore women's thoughts and opinions on vaginal products and their application. She is not currently pregnant and has no intention of becoming pregnant during the course of the study. She reports negative or unknown HIV status and has no known allergies or sensitivities to vaginal contraceptive film or nonoxynol-9. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and is excited to be a part of a project that may help other women in the future.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has not received any anti-HER2 therapy before. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss. Her medical history includes hypertension and she is currently taking medication for it. She does not have any history of other invasive cancers. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use two forms of acceptable contraception during the study and for at least 7 months after the last administration of study treatment. She has not received any systemic anti-cancer chemotherapy, small molecule, biologic, hormonal agent, or immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy from a previous treatment regimen or clinical study within 21 days prior to the first dose of U3-1402. She has adequate organ function and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to undergo pre-treatment biopsy and on-treatment biopsies, and is available for the required follow-up visits.

Emily is a 25-year-old woman who delivered a healthy baby girl 7 months ago. She lives in the Tuscaloosa county area with her husband and their newborn daughter. She has no history of CMV infection and is in good health. Emily is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help prevent CMV infection between pregnancies. She has discussed the study with her healthcare provider and understands the requirements and potential risks involved. Emily is willing to attend all study visits and use effective contraception throughout the trial. She does not have any chronic medical conditions or immune disorders, does not use steroids or other immunosuppressive medications, and has never received a CMV vaccine before. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is willing to provide blood and urine samples, and allow her infant daughter to be checked for CMV infection.

A 25 year old female with no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial to validate an in-ear temperature sensor. She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and duration. She is available for at least 2 visits for ear molds and study conduct. She is not pregnant and is not currently trying to conceive. She has not had any recent surgeries, respiratory conditions, heart or cardiovascular conditions, or any other known health conditions. She is not taking any medications, including antipyretics, and has not recently received any immunizations. She is interested in contributing to the advancement of medical technology through research participation.

A 42-year-old man diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma has been recommended to undergo radiation therapy to the head and neck area. He has no history of head and neck malignancies or prior radiation therapy to the head and neck region. He is a non-smoker and does not have any other medical conditions. He is currently not taking any medications nor has any known allergies. He has agreed to participate in the study and understands that he will be randomly assigned to either receive amifostine or radiation therapy alone. He is willing to complete quality-of-life questionnaires and follow-up visits at the designated intervals.

A 29-year-old woman presents with a history of irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty conceiving. She has been diagnosed with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) based on the Rotterdam ESHRE/ASRM criteria, which includes a combination of at least two of the following three criteria: cycle disorder, clinical hyperandrogenism, and/or biological, and account antral follicles > 24. The patient is within the age range of 18-38 years with a BMI of 28 kg/m². She has no known allergies and has not participated in any interventional biomedical research with treatment administered that may disrupt ovarian stimulation. The patient is seeking infertility treatment through IVF and is interested in participating in the clinical trial testing the use of myo-inositol as adjuvant therapy to reduce the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). She is able to understand the protocol and has signed an informed consent.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of colorectal cancer who has developed liver metastases. He has previously undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor and received chemotherapy with irinotecan and oxaliplatin. Unfortunately, he has had a failure outcome with chemotherapy and is no longer a candidate for surgery due to the extent of his liver lesions. He has not received any intervention therapy for his liver lesions in over a year. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a Child-pugh's grade of A. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his liver metastases.

A 6-year-old boy with a diagnosis of cerebral palsy, mental retardation, and cortical visual impairment is being evaluated for a clinical trial investigating the effect of enhanced visual and cross-modal environments on visual attentiveness. He has difficulty with visual tracking and often appears to be visually unresponsive. He has a history of seizures and is on anti-convulsant medication. He is non-verbal and communicates primarily through vocalizations and gestures. He has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and is followed by a pulmonologist. He is currently attending a special education program and receives physical and occupational therapy. He is able to sit independently but has limited mobility. No other significant medical history is reported.

A 9-year-old girl is scheduled to undergo an appendectomy due to acute appendicitis. She weighs 25 kg, with a BMI of 20. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies or sensitivities to opioids. She is currently not taking any medication. She will be an inpatient post-surgery for at least 24 hours, and her pain will be managed with a short-acting opioid analgesic. She is able to provide pain assessment evaluations using an age-appropriate instrument provided in the protocol. Her legally responsible parent has given informed consent, and the subject has provided assent in accordance with IRB requirements. She has a line in place for blood sampling.

A 50-year-old female with a diagnosis of recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The patient has already been treated with two lines of prior standard therapy, including R-CHOP and high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation, but the disease has relapsed. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has measurable disease. She has resolved all prior treatment-related toxicities to ≤ Grade 1 per NCI CTCAE, Version 4.03 or clinically stable and not clinically significant. She has adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic function. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to comply with the contraception measures defined by the protocol. She has no active central nervous system or leptomeningeal metastasis and has not had a prior malignancy other than the current diagnosis. She has not had major surgery within 3 weeks prior to enrollment and is not taking medications that are known potent or moderate inducers/inhibitors of CYP3A4. She is able to take oral medications and has no uncontrolled gastrointestinal condition that might impair the bioavailability of IP. She has not had any bleeding within 1 month prior to beginning therapy and does not have a clinical history of alcohol or illicit drug use that would interfere with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with a rectal adenoma after a routine colonoscopy. The tumor has been identified as non-invasive and is between 2 and 6 cm in diameter. The patient is in generally good health, but has an ASA score of III. The tumor is located at least 2 cm from the anal verge and at least 15 cm from the upper edge. The patient is not currently on antiplatelet or anticoagulation therapy and is able to undergo general anesthesia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and cost of 2-D high definition vision systems versus conventional 3-D in transanal endoscopic surgery.

32 yo F with primary infertility, diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) and male factor infertility. She has been trying to conceive for over 3 years and has been referred to the Kasr Alainy Assisted Reproduction Unit for ICSI. She has regular menstrual cycles, no history of thyroid dysfunction or hyperprolactinemia, and no contraindications for pregnancy. She has not taken any medication known to alter prolactin levels. She has been on ovulation induction protocol with gonadotropins and her ultrasound showed multiple follicles. She is scheduled for ovum pick up and embryo transfer. She has provided informed consent for all blood samples to be taken during the procedure.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. She had a vaginal delivery with her first child and did not experience any complications during the delivery. She is currently at 36 weeks of gestation and has a cephalic presentation. The patient has no history of uterine myoma, postpartum hemorrhage in previous pregnancies, placenta previa, polyhydramnios, or fetal macrosomia. She has a normal hemoglobin level of 11g/dL and has not been diagnosed with preeclampsia or uterine anomalies. The patient is not currently receiving anticoagulant therapy and does not have a suspected coagulopathy. She has not previously experienced any allergic reactions to oxytocin.

A 42-year-old man with a history of chronic renal insufficiency and end-stage renal disease is scheduled to undergo living-donor kidney transplantation. He has been accepted by the organ transplantation conference and registered by ET (Euro Transplant). He is willing and able to participate in The ONE Study IM and HEC Subprojects. The patient has signed and dated the written informed consent. He has no prior history of organ transplantation or contraindication to protocol-specified treatments or medications. He is not genetically identical to the prospective organ donor at the HLA loci. His Panel-Reactive Antibody (PRA) grade is less than 40%, and he has not received any desensitization procedure. He has no concomitant malignancy or history of malignancy within 5 years before the study entry. He has no significant local or systemic infection, and he is not HIV-positive or suffering chronic viral hepatitis. He has no significant liver disease or malignant or pre-malignant hematological conditions. He has no uncontrolled medical condition or concurrent disease that could interfere with the study objectives. He has not received any systemic immunosuppressive drugs at study entry. He is not participating in any other clinical trial during the study or within 28 days prior to planned study entry. He is a male patient and not of childbearing potential. He has no psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical factors potentially hampering compliance with the study protocol and follow-up visit schedule. He has no form of drug or alcohol abuse, psychiatric disorder, or other condition that may invalidate communication with the Investigator and/or designated study personnel. The patient is able to freely give his informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been admitted to a regional community hospital for a planned elective surgery. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a retired accountant and lives alone in a single-story house in the suburbs. He is able to perform activities of daily living on his own and has a good support system of nearby family and friends who can assist him if needed. He is fluent in English and has no known cognitive impairment. He plans to return home after his surgery and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old male presents to the ED with a complaint of chest pain that started suddenly while he was at work. He describes the pain as a tightness in his chest that radiates to his left arm. He rates the pain as a 6 out of 10 in severity. He has no history of heart disease but has a family history of heart attacks in his father and paternal grandfather. He is a smoker, and his BMI is 30. The patient is currently taking medication for hypertension. Upon examination, the patient's vital signs are stable, and his ECG is normal. His blood tests, including troponin, are negative. His HEART score is calculated to be 2. The patient is concerned about his chest pain and is worried that it might be a sign of a heart attack. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

65 y/o male with a history of moderate to severe COPD, referred to pulmonary rehabilitation at West Park Healthcare Centre. The patient reports chronic pain associated with osteoarthritis and osteoporosis. He has no recent history of acute exacerbation and is clinically stable. The patient is able to provide his own informed consent and has no known cognitive impairment that would interfere with completing surveys. He has no cardiac, neurological, or orthopedic conditions that would prevent him from safely undertaking exercise. The patient will be enrolled in the study as part of the pain group.

A 12-year-old girl was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician for uncontrolled asthma symptoms. She has a history of asthma since she was 6 years old, experiencing episodic wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. Her symptoms have been worsening over the past few months despite using her inhaler regularly as instructed. Her school attendance has been affected due to this. She lives with her parents and two siblings in a suburban area, and they have a landline phone connection at home. She has no other respiratory health problems or allergies. She is currently using an albuterol inhaler as needed and fluticasone 100 mcg/salmeterol 50 mcg, one puff twice daily as prescribed. Her spirometry test shows an FEV1 of 70% of the predicted. Her parents are supportive and willing to participate in a nurse-led telemonitoring programme to manage her asthma.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who is caring for her husband who suffered from a stroke 2 years ago. She expresses difficulty in managing her husband's symptoms and is concerned about her own quality of life due to the demands of caregiving. She has access to a telephone and is willing to participate in 9 calls from a nurse and 5 data collection calls at designated timepoints. Her husband's stroke occurred within the past 3 years. She speaks fluent English and has no serious medical illness that would limit her ability to participate. She is not pregnant and is not a prisoner or on house arrest. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating in the ANSWERS-VA intervention to acquire new skills and enhance her remaining strengths as a caregiver.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman with a diagnosis of advanced/metastatic ovarian cancer, fallopian tube cancer or primary peritoneal cancer (FIGO Stage IIIb, IIIc and IV) according to routine clinical practice. She has been prescribed to receive bevacizumab, or is already receiving treatment with bevacizumab for her condition. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in this study, and is expected to be followed until death, withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, or study closure. The patient does not have any medical conditions or other factors that would make her ineligible for treatment with bevacizumab according to the local prescribing information.

The patient is a 65 year old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. His recent ECG and echocardiogram show evidence of atrial fibrillation and left ventricular hypertrophy. He has been advised to undergo an open-heart cardiac surgery for the management of his condition. He is willing to participate in the CAREBANK study and has provided written informed consent.

A 4-year-old African American boy named Marcus has been diagnosed with asthma. His parents are both employed but have limited incomes, and they struggle to afford Marcus's asthma medication and to manage his symptoms effectively. Marcus often experiences wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, which can interfere with his ability to participate in preschool activities. Despite their best efforts, Marcus's parents have difficulty knowing when to administer his medication and how to respond when he has an asthma attack. They are interested in participating in the A+ Asthma early intervention program, which they hope will provide them with more information and support to manage Marcus's asthma effectively. Marcus's preschool is a Head Start site, and the staff have expressed an interest in participating in the program as well. Marcus's parents are hoping that the program will not only help them manage Marcus's asthma but also reduce the number of days that he has to miss preschool due to asthma-related symptoms.

A 35-year-old woman has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia for the past year. She experiences widespread pain and fatigue that prevent her from performing daily tasks. She has tried different medications and therapies, but none of them have been effective in relieving her symptoms. She is not currently on any medication for fibromyalgia. She reports having a sedentary lifestyle due to her condition and feels discouraged about her ability to be physically active. She does not have a history of heart disease, neurological disease or severe osteoarthritis. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to understand the effects of exercise on fibromyalgia symptoms.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing increased bladder sensation and urgency for the past 6 months. She reports having to go to the bathroom frequently, including multiple times during the night, which is affecting her sleep. She has also noticed occasional urine leakage when she coughs or sneezes. She has not received any previous pharmacological treatment for these symptoms. She has no history of neurogenic bladder, acute urinary infection, pelvic floor surgery, congenital urological malformations, or pelvic radiotherapy. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no other chronic conditions or allergies. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands that she will be randomly assigned to either the control group or the group receiving medium frequency electrotherapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The aneurysm has grown to 6.5 cm and is causing discomfort and pain. The patient has no history of rectal bleeding or obstruction. The patient has been advised to undergo a catheter-based stent procedure to repair the aneurysm. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. The patient's rectum is patent, and the patient meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. He is a smoker and has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He has not had any prior episodes of atrial fibrillation. His ECG shows evidence of NSTEMI and he is diagnosed with stable angina requiring revascularization therapy. He is not currently taking any medications for his conditions. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially reduce his risk of stroke and other adverse outcomes. He is willing to comply with the treatment plans and follow-up appointments. However, he is concerned about the potential side effects of oral anticoagulation treatment and would like to discuss his options further with the healthcare provider.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder and prior psychiatric hospitalization. She was recently diagnosed with Stage III breast cancer and has had a medical oncology consultation at the MGH Cancer Center within the past 8 weeks. She is currently experiencing anxiety and depression related to her cancer diagnosis and is having difficulty coping with the added stress. She has a supportive partner who accompanies her to appointments and helps with daily tasks, but they both feel overwhelmed with managing her mental health needs and cancer treatment. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in a study that connects her to a psychiatrist and case manager at the cancer center to help coordinate her care and provide support.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who recently had a mammogram that showed a highly suspicious mass in her left breast. A biopsy was performed and revealed an invasive ductal carcinoma. She is scheduled to undergo a contrast-enhanced breast MRI for further evaluation. She has no prior history of breast cancer or any other significant medical history. She takes a daily multivitamin and has no known allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has three children and breastfed all of them. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the sensitivity of Positron Emission Mammography and Contrast-enhanced Breast MRI in detecting breast cancer.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who lives in Southeast Minnesota. He has participated in the Mayo Clinic Biobank and has no history of myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, or other atherosclerotic medical conditions. He is not currently taking any statins or lipid-lowering medications. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack in his early 60s. The patient is concerned about his own risk of heart attack and is interested in participating in the MI-GENES study to better understand his risk based on genetic information. He is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including blood lipid level testing and lifestyle modifications.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male with a history of schizophrenia diagnosed 10 years ago presented to the clinic for follow-up with his treating psychiatrist. He has been taking clozapine for the last 6 months with no significant improvement in his symptoms. He has also been experiencing cognitive symptoms such as difficulty with memory and attention, which are negatively impacting his daily functioning. He reported no history of substance abuse or dependence and denied any suicidal or homicidal ideations. He has no known allergies to any medications or a history of adverse reactions to clozapine. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. He is living alone and is unemployed. He has a supportive family who is willing to participate in his treatment. He is able to understand the nature of the study

A 30-year-old woman with a history of uveal melanoma and basal cell carcinoma was referred to a cancer genetics clinic for evaluation of hereditary cancer risk. Her mother had a history of mesothelioma and her paternal grandmother had a history of renal cell carcinoma. Genetic testing revealed a germline BAP1 pathogenic variant. The patient's sister and father were also found to have the same variant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the clinical phenotype of BAP1 hereditary predisposition syndrome and to help with the development of screening and prevention strategies for individuals with the syndrome. She speaks fluent English and is able to read and understand the study materials.

56 year old woman with a history of breast cancer diagnosed 5 years ago, who underwent mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. The patient subsequently underwent adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy, and was found to be free of disease on follow-up imaging. However, the patient presented with a new diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer with multiple bone, liver and lung metastasis. The patient is symptomatic with diffuse bone pain and the liver lesions are causing abdominal discomfort. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and has no contraindications for proton therapy and immunotherapy. The patient has a KPS score of 80 and is able to understand and sign the informed consent. The patient is postmenopausal and has no history of other malignancies or significant comorbidities.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has been diagnosed with severe peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD) at stage IV according to the Lèriche-Fontaine classification. He is experiencing intractable pain and has not received any opioid treatment. He has no history of renal failure or congestive heart failure, and is not taking digoxin or calcium channel blockers. He has no known neuromuscular diseases or chronic diarrhea. He has not undergone successful interventional angiography, Fogarty embolectomy or surgical revascularization for acute limb ischemia. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial aimed at assessing the efficacy of oral magnesium supplementation in controlling severe pain in patients with advanced PAOD.

A 50-year-old mother brings in her healthy 2-month-old daughter for a routine check-up. The daughter was born full-term and has no history of any medical conditions. The mother reports that the daughter has been feeding well and has been having regular bowel movements. The daughter has not received any prior vaccinations. The mother is interested in enrolling her daughter in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of concomitant administration of RotaTeq® and inactivated poliomyelitis vaccine in Chinese infants. The mother understands the study procedures and provides written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman who is currently six weeks postpartum and has been diagnosed with HIV during her pregnancy. She is currently taking antiretroviral therapy (ART) and has had no adverse reactions to the medication. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of depression since the birth of her child, including feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping. She has never taken antidepressant medication before and has no known allergies or contraindications to sertraline. The patient is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of suicidal ideation or attempts. The patient resides in Lusaka, Zambia, and is able to travel to the study clinics for follow-up visits.

A 7-year-old boy is scheduled to undergo an open surgical procedure that is expected to result in at least moderate pain based on an age-appropriate scale. He is in generally good health and has no known allergies or sensitivities to ketorolac or ethylene diamine tetraacetic acid (EDTA). He is not taking any medications regularly and has never used Toradol (ketorolac tromethamine) before. His parents are willing and able to assist him in completing the study procedures and pain scales and to communicate meaningfully with the study personnel. They are willing to refrain from using non-study analgesics for the duration of the study, from the day of surgery up to post-operative Day 4. The patient assents to participation, and his parents are willing and able to sign the informed consent approved by the IRB. The patient does not have a history of nasal-septal injury or surgery, peptic ulcer, gastro-esophageal reflux, or gastrointestinal bleeding. He is not at risk of pregnancy, has never had renal impairment, and has no bleeding diathesis or other disorder affecting coagulation. He is not currently using any CNS-active drugs for pain or any antihypertensive agent or diabetic regimen at a dose that has not been stable for at least 30 days.

A 40-year-old female who has been diagnosed with lupus nephritis by American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria. She has suffered from active renal disease in the past and has active renal disease now. Her spot urine protein/creatinine ratio is ≥1.0 and she has more than 5 RBC/HPF, more than 5 WBC/HPF, and columnar cells. She has been taking immunosuppressive agents, steroids, and anti-Malarials (hydroxychloroquine) in a certain capacity to manage her condition, and will maintain the same capacity before the 4-week screening. She has consented to participate in the study in writing by herself or her legal representatives. She has a HLA-haplo-matched bone marrow donor who is less than 70 years old. She is not hypersensitive to antibiotics including penicillin and streptomycin, and does not have a systemic infection at screening. She does not have uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes, and has not had a myocardial infarction or angina on ECG at screening, or received stent procedure or bypass. She has not been administered another study drug 3 months prior to the study, and has not previously received stem cell therapy. She does not have severe mental disease (for example, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, etc.). She is expected to comply with the proper method of contraception during the clinical trial.

A 60-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis of the liver is referred to the liver clinic at PGIMER, Chandigarh, for a follow-up visit. He was diagnosed with cirrhosis 6 months ago after presenting with jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal distention. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption for the past 20 years but has abstained from alcohol for the past 6 months. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes medication. He has no history of neurologic diseases or psychiatric disorders. His physical examination is remarkable for mild ascites and hepatosplenomegaly. His laboratory tests reveal mildly elevated liver enzymes, hypoalbuminemia, and thrombocytopenia. An ultrasound confirms the presence of cirrhosis. He also had a previous episode of overt hepatic encephalopathy (HE) for which he was hospitalized and treated with lactulose. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to prevent recurrence of HE in patients with cirrhosis of the liver.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. The baby is being treated in the neonatal intensive care unit due to complications at birth. The patient is committed to exclusively breastfeeding her child during their stay in the NICU and has been keeping a daily log of milk expression since the birth of their child. She speaks fluent English and is able to answer a written survey in English. She has no medical contraindications to breastfeeding and intends to keep her baby in her legal custody. The patient has not been separated from her baby due to legal custody issues. At 7 days postpartum, the patient is eligible to participate in the study.

A 28-week-old male premature infant with a birth weight of 1300 grams is currently in the NICU receiving respiratory support via noninvasive ventilation. The infant was started on daily caffeine therapy for apnea and is currently stable with no signs of acute sepsis or increased intracranial pressure. The infant has no history of meningitis or seizures and no cyanotic heart defects or clinically significant congenital heart disease. The parents are English-speaking and are willing to provide informed consent for the infant's participation in the study.

25-year-old female with a history of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) for the past 8 months. She has been taking H1-antihistamines but has found little relief from her symptoms of itching and hives, which have persisted for at least 6 consecutive weeks. She has a UAS7 score of 20 and an HSS7 score of 10, indicating that her symptoms are inadequately controlled despite treatment. She has no history of allergic reactions to drugs or their excipients. She is willing and able to complete a daily symptom eDiary and adhere to the study visit schedules. She has no other skin diseases or conditions that might influence the study evaluations and results. She has not been exposed to ligelizumab or omalizumab in the past, and she has not used any H2 antihistamines, LTRA, or H1 antihistamines at greater than approved doses since Visit 1. She gives her informed consent to participate in the study.

A 50-year-old man presents with a history of high cholesterol levels for the past 2 years. He has been trying to control his cholesterol levels through diet and exercise but has not been successful. His most recent lipid profile shows a total cholesterol level of 240 mg/dL and an LDL cholesterol level of 160 mg/dL. His triglyceride levels are within normal limits. He has no history of cardiovascular disease and his 10-year cardiovascular risk is estimated to be less than 10%. His BMI is 25 and he does not have any thyroid, liver or kidney problems. He does not consume alcohol excessively and is not taking any lipid-lowering drugs or supplements. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effects of vitaminized corn oil on lipid profile, endothelial function and PCSK9.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of colorectal cancer presents to the clinic for the trial. She had previously undergone surgery for colon cancer and had received oxaliplatin combined with fluorouracil chemotherapy. A recent CT scan revealed metastases to the liver and lungs. She has not been exposed to apatinib before. The estimated survival time is longer than 3 months. Her ECOG score is 1. The CT scan shows a measurable lesion in the liver (longest diameter>10mm) and two lesions in the lung (longest diameter>10mm). Blood tests showed Hb 10.5 g/dL, Absolute neutrophil count 2.2 × 109 /L, and Platelet count 120 × 109 /L. Serum bilirubin is within normal range. ALT&AST are within normal range. Creatinine clearance rate by Cockcroft-Gault formula is 75 mL/min. She had a negative pregnancy test and is willing to use appropriate methods of contraception during the trial. She is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 9-year-old African American male who resides in Southwest Detroit presented to the clinic with symptoms consistent with persistent asthma (mild). He has a history of recurrent wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, especially during the night and early morning. His mother reports that his symptoms have been worsening over the past few months despite using his prescribed inhaler as directed. He has no known allergies or other medical conditions. He lives with his mother, father, and two younger siblings in a two-bedroom apartment. His bedroom is located in the living room, which is adjacent to the kitchen. They do not have air conditioning or air filters in their home. His mother reports that they live in an area with high pollution levels. The family speaks English and has access to transportation. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial that will provide them with air filters and air conditioners to help manage his asthma symptoms.

A 45-year-old male patient diagnosed with ulcerative colitis has been experiencing symptoms for the past 6 months, including frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He has been receiving treatment with oral corticosteroids but still has a Mayo endoscopy score of ≥ 2. He has no history of malignancy within the last 5 years, bleeding disorder, or hypercoagulable disorders. His liver function, renal function, absolute neutrophil count, and hemoglobin are all within normal limits. He has not received any investigational therapy or investigational biologics in the past 8 weeks. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the pharmacokinetic profile of LYC-30937 in patients with active ulcerative colitis.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with colon cancer that has spread to her peritoneum. She underwent a colon resection surgery and received 6 cycles of FOLFOX chemotherapy, but her cancer has progressed to her abdomen. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, including her renal function parameters. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She is willing to undergo placement of an intraperitoneal (IP) catheter and a Port-A Cath, if not already present. She has no known allergies to chemotherapy drugs.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who has been living in a residential care facility for the past year. She suffers from hypertension, osteoporosis, and type 2 diabetes. She takes a total of 8 medications to manage her conditions, including blood pressure medication, insulin, and calcium supplements. Her cognitive function is mildly impaired, but her family has designated her daughter as the decision maker for her medical care. Her attending GP has agreed to participate in the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided consent through her daughter.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic knee pain for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has been taking pain medication to manage her symptoms. Despite the medication, her pain has been getting worse and is now rated at a VAS score of 60 mm while walking on a flat surface. She has also reported neuropathic pain, with a PainDETECT score of 16. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage it. She has not undergone any knee surgery or taken part in any clinical trials within the past year. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her informed consent. She undergoes an MRI examination to determine the structural changes in her knee joint that may be associated with her neuropathic pain.

The patient is a 7-year-old Caucasian girl diagnosed with Mucopolysaccharidosis type VI disease. She has been receiving Enzyme Replacement Therapy (ERT) for the past 18 months with no significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient's parents are concerned about the long-term efficacy of ERT and are interested in exploring alternative treatments. The patient has normal growth and development milestones but has been experiencing corneal clouding, cardiac valve disease, and skeletal dysplasia. The patient has no history of anaphylactic reactions to Naglazyme. The patient's parents are willing to adhere to the protocol and required long-term follow-up and have provided written informed consent for the trial. The patient is not currently receiving systemic corticosteroid therapy or other immunosuppressive/immunomodulating drugs. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and the parents are willing to use effective contraception for at least one year post- IMP administration. The patient does not have detectable serum neutralizing antibodies against AAV8 vector.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma. During the surgical resection of the primary tumor, the surgeon observed a rupture of the tumor inside the peritoneal cavity, indicating a high risk of developing peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC). The patient received standard systemic adjuvant chemotherapy with the Folfox 4 regimen for 6 months, which was well-tolerated. At the end of the chemotherapy, the patient did not present any signs of tumor recurrence. The patient is in overall good health, with a performance status of WHO <2 and a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient has no major comorbidities and the necessary hematological and liver and renal functions are within normal limits. The patient is considered operable and has grade 2 peripheral neuropathy. The patient has been informed about the trial and has signed the consent form to participate in the study.

A 23-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a complaint of abdominal pain that started in the periumbilical region and migrated to the right lower quadrant. She also reported nausea, vomiting, and a decrease in appetite. She denied any history of fever, diarrhea or constipation. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she was not taking any medication. On examination, there was tenderness in the right lower quadrant, with guarding and rebound tenderness. There were no signs of peritonitis. Blood tests showed a mild leukocytosis, with a white cell count of 12,000/μL. An abdominal ultrasound was performed, which showed a thickened appendix with peri-appendiceal fluid collection, consistent with acute appendicitis. The patient was scheduled for an emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy and was informed about the option of participating in a clinical trial comparing two methods of closing the stump of the appendix during the surgery. After providing informed consent, the patient was randomly allocated to the polymer clips group for stump closure. The operation was successful, and the patient was discharged after a few days without any complications. She was informed about the need for follow-up within 30 days to assess any potential readmission.

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of alcohol dependence and current abstinence is seeking treatment for his addiction. He has been abstinent for the past three months and is motivated to stay sober. He reports that he has been drinking heavily for the past 10 years and has tried to quit several times without success. He is currently employed as an engineer and lives with his wife and two children. He reports that his family is supportive of his decision to quit drinking. He has been diagnosed with severe alcohol addiction according to DSM-5 criteria. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, and is not taking any psychotropic drugs. He has normal vision with glasses and understands the note of information and has signed the consent form. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo the neuropsychological tests and social cognition test. His MoCA score is 28/30.

The patient is a 45 year old male scheduled for hand surgery under supraclavicular brachial plexus blockade. He has a history of hypertension but is currently on medication and his blood pressure is well controlled. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics or dexamethasone, and has a BMI of 30. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or peptic ulcer disease. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who has received treatment with AA4500 for Dupuytren's contracture in his right hand. The patient had a fixed-flexion contracture measurement after treatment with AA4500. He is willing and able to comply with the yearly assessments outlined in the protocol. The patient has voluntarily signed and dated an informed consent agreement approved by the Institutional Review Board/Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC). The patient has no medical history of any chronic illnesses or any allergies to medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has no history of drug abuse or addiction. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old female who has been diagnosed with stable angina pectoris of coronary heart disease (CHD) and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. She has a history of myocardial infarction and coronary angiography showing more than 50% coronary stenosis. She has been experiencing symptoms for the past three months and has had an attack in the recent one month. She has been diagnosed with phlegm and blood stasis syndrome of the traditional Chinese medicine. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication and she has no other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the agreement paper voluntarily.

42-year-old female with a history of anxiety disorder and scheduled for elective low limb orthopedic procedure under spinal anesthesia. She has no known cardiovascular, central nervous system, or autonomic nervous system disease. She does not take any medication for anxiety or pain management. She is able to communicate effectively and is willing to cooperate with the experimenter. She is classified as an ASA II patient.

70 yo M with a history of BPH, presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms, including nocturia, urinary frequency, urgency, and weak stream. The patient has not responded to medical management with alpha-blockers and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors. The patient has no history of neurological diseases or previous surgery on the lower urinary tract. The patient is willing to undergo surgery and is eligible for inclusion in the clinical trial. The patient will undergo HoLEP performed by two experienced surgeons with more than 1000 procedures performed (FM; GB) at a single academic center. The patient's pre-operative data will include prostate volume as assessed with trans-rectal prostate ultrasound, uroflowmetry parameters, total PSA, baseline hemoglobin, and creatinine level. The patient will also complete psychometric validated questionnaires assessing pre-operative urinary and sexual function, including the International Prostatic Symptoms Score (IPSS), the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF), the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF), and the Overactive Bladder Questionnaire (OABq). The patient will be assessed for UC at 1 week after surgery and will undergo a first uroflowmetry evaluation at 3 months after surgery, with a final assessment at 1 year after surgery.

60-year-old male patient diagnosed with acute respiratory failure was admitted to the ICU and intubated. The patient has a past medical history of COPD, hypertension, and coronary artery disease. Upon examination, the patient is alert, oriented, and cooperative with a RASS score of 0. The patient is currently undergoing weaning from mechanical ventilation and is hemodynamically stable. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient does not have any contraindication for nasogastric catheter insertion. The patient is fluent in English and is able to communicate effectively.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His PSA level is elevated at 35 ng/mL and biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma of the prostate. He has no history of previous pelvic radiation or surgery for prostate cancer. Clinical examination reveals a hard nodule on the right side of the prostate. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, and he is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. He is able to undergo gold seed insertion and MRI. The patient has not received any hormonal therapy in the past 14 days and has not taken finasteride in the past 180 days. The patient agrees to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 52 year old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease comes to the clinic for a routine checkup. She has been on angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and/or an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) for the past 6 weeks with a stable dose. Her eGFR is between 15.0 and 45.0 mL/min/1.73 m2. Her BMI is between 18.5 and 45 kg/m2. Her mean systolic blood pressure (SBP) is ≤ 160 mmHg and ≥ 105 mmHg and mean diastolic blood pressure (DBP) is ≤ 90 mmHg during screening. She has not had acute dialysis or acute kidney injury within 24 weeks prior to Study Day -1. She has no clinical signs and/or symptoms of uremia and is not expected to need renal replacement therapy within 12 weeks following Study Day -1. She is willing to practice methods of birth control from screening through Study Day 84. She is non-pregnant and non-lactating and has a negative serum pregnancy test result prior to enrollment in the study. She is willing and able to give written informed consent for study participation and cooperate with all aspects of the protocol. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 10-year-old Thai girl who has been diagnosed with HIV. She was infected through vertical transmission from her mother who is also HIV positive. The patient has been taking antiretroviral therapy (ART) based on non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) for the past 3 years. Her ART regimen hasn't shown optimal efficacy in controlling the viral load, and she has developed drug resistance to NNRTI. The patient has never taken protease inhibitor (PI) therapy before. She weighs 30 kg and has a good appetite. Her last CD4 count was 450 cells/mm3, and her viral load was 11,000 copies/mL. She has a history of mild elevation of ALT but no other significant medical history. She is currently attending school and has an interest in drawing and painting. Her parents are both alive and are her primary caregivers. They have given informed consent for the patient to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is willing to take capsules but may need assistance with swallowing.

A 25-year-old woman with a history of Hodgkin lymphoma presents with relapsed cancer. She has received at least two prior cytotoxic regimens for her condition, and has failed autologous stem cell transplant. The patient has measurable disease, as defined by the International Harmonization Project. Her performance status is good, with a Karnofsky score of 90%. She has normal organ and marrow function, including an absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/mcL and platelets of 100,000/mcL. The patient has a normal total bilirubin level and AST/ALT levels within normal limits. She has no history of pericardial effusion or cerebral/meningeal involvement by lymphoma. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use adequate contraception. She has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past 3 weeks and has recovered from any adverse events from prior treatments. The patient has not received any other investigational agents and has no known allergies to similar drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is aware of the potential risks associated with the study.

Patient A is a 5-year-old boy who is scheduled for a tonsillectomy under general anesthesia. He has a history of recurrent tonsillitis and his parents have opted for surgery as a treatment option. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He weighs 22 kg and has a body mass index of 18 kg/m2. The patient is currently fasting and has not eaten or drank anything since midnight the night before the surgery. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for their child to participate in the study. The patient does not have any cervical spine pathologies or peripheral neurologic deficiencies, malformations of the upper airway or head, anamnestic hiatus hernia or esophageal reflux, or a history of stomach or esophagus surgery. He also does not have any recurrent respiratory infections or obstructive airway disease.

52-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of ALS by El Escorial Criteria with progressive muscle weakness, difficulty speaking and swallowing, and muscle wasting. He is currently taking Riluzole and has been on a stable dose for the past 6 months. He has no significant medical history or allergies, and is not currently taking any other medication. He is able to understand and complete questionnaires and is willing to comply with the trial protocol. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study. He is not in the manic phase of bipolar disorder and has no active suicide ideation. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using appropriate contraception. He has normal liver and kidney function, and normal thyroid function. He has no history of ventricular arrhythmias, heart block or myocardial infarction. He is not taking any medication that interacts with the active substances and their excipients according to the SPCs.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl attending primary school in China. She is in good health and has no history of chronic illnesses or mental or physical handicaps. She enjoys a balanced diet and is willing to maintain her current dietary habits throughout the study. Her parents have given their informed consent for her to participate in this study and she has given her oral consent. She is willing to consume the test product and perform all measurements required, including cognitive testing, blood drawing, urine samples, anthropometry and questionnaires. She has not suffered any major life events in the past six months and does not take any medications that interfere with study measurements.

This is a 55 year old male with a 20 pack-year smoking history and occasional shortness of breath. A chest X-ray showed a suspicious mass in the lung and a CT scan confirmed a 3 cm nodule in the right upper lobe. The patient is scheduled for a diagnostic bronchoscopy to further evaluate the nodule. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidemia 3. Occasional shortness of breath 4. No prior history of cancer except for a basal cell carcinoma on the nose.

A 32-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of schizophrenia was referred to the clinical trial by his psychiatrist. He has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past 2 years with no hospitalizations in the past 3 months. He lives with his parents and works part-time as a cashier at a grocery store. He has a history of smoking cigarettes and marijuana use, but has not used any illicit drugs in the past 30 days. He has no history of immune disorders or any other significant medical conditions. His baseline hsCRP level is 0.8 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his cognitive function and quality of life. He has read the informed consent form and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled visits.

A 56-year-old male patient with a history of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) diagnosed 6 months ago. He underwent a radical nephrectomy and is currently receiving sunitinib as a standard of care treatment for RCC. He is experiencing severe fatigue, which is affecting his quality of life and causing dose reductions. In addition to sunitinib, he is taking medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no history of psychiatric illness or substance abuse. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. He is physically active and exercises regularly. His latest lab studies show a normal range of hemoglobin, platelet count, total bilirubin, and creatinine. His cardiac ejection fraction by MUGA scan is also above 50%. He understands the purpose of the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He has no contraindications for the scintigraphy scan and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 35 year-old male who has been in a stable sexual relationship with the same woman for the past 5 years. He has a history of premature ejaculation for the past 6 months, with intravaginal ejaculatory latency time (IELT) of less than or equal to 2 minutes in at least half of events. The patient has a PEDT score of 12 and 6 domains of International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF) score of 22. He has no significant medical history affecting ADME in the past 3 years and no clinically significant disorders in ophthalmic, gastro-intestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, autoimmune systems or malignant tumor. He has no history of psychological or allergic disease and is not hypersensitive to TCA or SSRIs. The patient has not taken dapoxetine within the past 3 months, is not using any other forms of therapy for the treatment of PE and has not taken another investigational drug within the past month. He has no history of drug abuse. The patient and his partner agree to attempt sexual intercourse at minimum intervals specified in the protocol, and his partner has a negative urine pregnancy test at the time of screening.

A 45-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent a lumpectomy. She was advised to undergo a mastectomy as a preventive measure to avoid recurrence. She underwent the mastectomy 1 month ago and is now considering breast reconstruction. She is generally healthy with a BMI of 30. She is a non-smoker and has no history of bleeding disorders or diabetes. She has never had any back or axillary surgeries. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that uses the Da Vinci Robotic Surgical System in procedures that harvest the latissimus dorsi muscle for reconstructive procedures. The study doctor or a member of the research team has reviewed her medical information and asked her questions about her medical history and demographic information.
