She has undergone a physical exam and has been evaluated by a Physical Therapist to test her range of motion and strength. She has completed a questionnaire about pain, as well as her shoulder, arm, and hand range of motion. She has agreed to follow-up examinations out to 6 months post-treatment.

A 48-year-old man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years came to our clinic for routine medical surveillance. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of heart disease or other serious health problems. He takes daily metformin and glimepiride for his diabetes. His blood glucose levels are usually well controlled. He has no known allergies to food or medication. He exercises occasionally but not on a regular basis. He is interested in participating in research studies that may help improve his condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been undergoing hemodialysis treatment for the past 18 months due to end-stage renal disease. He has been experiencing a reduction in his quality of life and physical activity due to the frequency of hemodialysis sessions. He has expressed interest in participating in a physical activity program during his hemodialysis sessions to improve his cardiovascular health and overall wellbeing. He is a French-speaking patient and is affiliated with the French social security scheme. He does not have cancer, hepatitis, stage 4 arterial disease, arteritis or amputation of a limb. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not considered a vulnerable person under article L.1121-6 of the CSP. He is able to give his consent to participate in the study.
N/A - Since this is a laboratory-based study to generate dendritic cell precursors from cord blood stem cells, there are no specific patient criteria or descriptions needed for this clinical trial.

65F with ESRD on hemodialysis for the past 2 years, presents with a complaint of chronic fatigue, insomnia, and itching. Patient reports feeling drained after each dialysis session, which persists for the rest of the day. The patient also reports experiencing moderate to severe itching all over her body during and after dialysis, which has persisted for the past 6 months. She reports no history of pruritus prior to hemodialysis initiation. The patient is compliant with her medications, which includes erythropoietin and phosphate binders. The patient is otherwise healthy, with a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of trauma to her upper front tooth resulting in its loss. She is in good health and maintains good oral hygiene. She has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. The patient has sufficient bone volume to accommodate an implant with minimum dimensions of 3.6 mm diameter and 10.0 mm length. The patient has healthy soft tissue at the future implant site. The patient has no history of bruxism or parafunctional habits and has a stable posterior occlusion. She has not undergone head and neck radiation. The patient is seeking implant treatment for the replacement of her missing tooth and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of bone grafts on facial gingival profile in maxillary anterior single tooth replacement.

A 10-year-old boy with cerebral palsy and right-sided upper limb hemiparesis is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. His caregiver is his mother who is fluent in English. The boy is stable on his current medications and has no other neurological conditions affecting his hemiparetic arm. He is able to follow 3-stage commands and has some active movement of his paretic arm to position his hand for table-top task practice. His Box & Blocks Score on his weaker side is less than 90% of his stronger side score. He is able to hear and respond to auditory cues. He does not have any cardiac pacemaker or any other implanted electronic systems. He has not received any intramuscular Botox injections in any upper extremity muscle in the last 3 months. He is not pregnant. He and his mother are willing and able to attend weekly sessions and assist with home treatment.

Pt is a 29yo pregnant female who was diagnosed with HIV during her antenatal care visit. She was initiated on ART therapy in accordance with Option B+ PMTCT guidelines. She delivered a healthy baby girl through a planned c-section and both were discharged home with follow-up scheduled for 6 weeks postpartum. However, the patient failed to show up for her follow-up appointment and has been deemed lost-to-follow-up (LTF) by the Safe Generations study protocol. The study team will attempt to contact her via phone or community outreach to administer a questionnaire and learn about her reasons for disengaging from care. The patient will be eligible for inclusion in the study as she was enrolled in PMTCT at a Safe Generations study site after the transition to Option B+.

A 35-year-old man with a history of closed head injury 9 months ago presents with moderate-severe irritability and aggression. His family reports that he has been prone to outbursts and mood swings since the injury. The patient is medically stable and has no other neurological issues. He is willing to participate in the study and has a reliable informant who is able to provide daily observations of his behavior. The patient is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study and has not taken carbamazepine in the month prior to enrollment. He is able to communicate effectively with his caregiver and has no signs of active infection or liver/renal failure. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use birth control if sexually active. The patient also does not have Asian heritage.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who is scheduled for a venipuncture due to a routine blood test. He has no history of medical problems or cognitive/developmental impairments. He is accompanied by his mother who is anxious about the procedure and has a fear of needles. The patient has expressed fear and anxiety about the procedure in the past and has had previous negative experiences with venipuncture. The family is Italian-speaking and is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce the child's distress and pain during the procedure.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) that has progressively worsened over the past year. She has minimal movement and is unable to communicate effectively using natural speech. She has been using a speech generating device for communication, but it does not meet her daily communication needs. She is interested in participating in the study to test a new AAC-BCI device that may provide her with more effective communication options. She is a native English speaker, able to read a standard computer screen and follow instructions. She does not have a history of photosensitive epilepsy, open sores on the scalp, or uncorrectable hearing loss. She is available to participate during the times scheduled for the study.

45-year-old male with a history of heart failure due to non-ischemic etiology with an implanted cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) device for the past 2 years. The patient has been clinically stable for the past 6 weeks with no change in medication for the past 3 months. The patient reports experiencing dyspnea in activities of daily living and fatigue perception. The patient's comorbid conditions, including hypertension and diabetes, are well-controlled. The patient has no history of acute myocardial infarction, cognitive disorders, complex arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension, stroke or transient ischemic attack within the last six months prior to the study, angina pectoris, recent viral infections (six months prior to study), significant valvular disease, orthopedic problems or rheumatologic diseases.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who is a non-smoker and has a normal ECG. He is not a shift worker, vegetarian, or a person who frequently travels long distances. He is not currently participating in a psychology or psychiatry course. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of GSK561679 on part of the body's system that controls the balance of many hormones, including cortisol.

Thomas is a 37-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent back pain for the past year. He has tried physical therapy and pain medications, but they have been ineffective. He has been diagnosed with lumbar spinal stenosis and his surgeon has recommended corrective spinal procedures with MEP monitoring. Thomas has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and occasionally drinks alcohol. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his day sitting. He is able to provide informed consent for the study and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 66-year-old woman who is generally healthy and physically active. She exercises regularly, eats a balanced diet, and takes multivitamins daily. Her BMI is 24 kg/m² and she does not smoke. She has no history of major illnesses or injuries, and is not currently taking any medications or supplements that may interfere with the study results. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the combined orange- and pomegranate extract supplement can improve her physical fitness and quality of life. She has no known allergies to citrus fruits or the test product/placebo.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She has been feeling sad, hopeless, and has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has difficulty sleeping at night, often waking up in the middle of the night and finding it hard to fall back asleep. She has tried various over-the-counter sleep aids, but they have not been effective. She works as a teacher and feels that her depression is impacting her ability to perform well at work. She has not had any prior experience with acupuncture, but is willing to try it as a treatment option. She has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder by a psychiatrist and has a HAMD score of 25. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including having a PSQI score of 9 and is willing to wear the Actigraphy during the trial. She does not have any alcohol abuse or drug dependence issues, and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has given her consent to participate in the trial and is looking forward to seeing if electroacupuncture can improve her symptoms of depression and insomnia.

A 55-year-old Chinese man presents to the clinic with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He has been taking metformin 1000mg twice daily and amlodipine 5mg daily for the past 2 years. His blood pressure is usually around 145/90mmHg and he has been experiencing occasional episodes of nocturia. In his latest laboratory results, his urinary albumin excretion rate was found to be 180ug/min, indicating microalbuminuria. He denies any significant past medical history, including cardiovascular disease or renal disease. He has no known allergies or intolerances to any medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only occasionally. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his diabetes and hypertension, and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 22-year-old woman complaining of severe menstrual cramps that interfere with her daily activities. She has been experiencing dysmenorrhea for the past year and has tried over-the-counter pain relievers with little relief. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for dysmenorrhea. She has read and understood the informed consent document and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 35-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained multiple fractures in both lower extremities. The patient underwent emergency surgery, which included four compartment fasciotomies on his right leg. He has no significant past medical history, does not smoke, and has no known drug allergies. The patient is currently admitted to the hospital and is receiving care from a multidisciplinary team. The wound is being managed with standard wet to dry dressing changes. The patient is experiencing moderate pain at the surgical site, which is being managed with analgesics. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to determine the utility of wound vacuum assisted closure (VAC) compared to conventional saline dressing changes in treating lower leg fasciotomies.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been diagnosed with colorectal cancer and is scheduled to undergo elective colon surgery by laparotomy. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has adequate time to complete preoperative bowel preparation and is expected to be hospitalized for 3-5 days post-surgery. The patient is physically active and does not have any physical limitations that would prevent her from participating in the study.

55-year-old female breast cancer survivor who completed radiation therapy and is currently not receiving active treatment. She reports experiencing sleep issues, including difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep. She scores 8 on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. She owns an iPhone and is comfortable using a mobile application for assessment purposes. She is fluent in English and able to read and write. She does not have a history of chronic insomnia or other co-morbidities related to poor sleep and fatigue. She is not currently taking any pharmacological sleep aids.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has a past medical history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She reports mild shortness of breath during exercise and has been told that she has mild-to-moderate pulmonary dysfunction. She is scheduled for elective open thoracic surgery and has been identified as a potential candidate for this clinical trial. She is an ASA physical status II patient. She is an active individual who enjoys hiking and gardening. She is married and has two children. She is willing to participate in this study and has provided informed written consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old high school student who has been struggling with feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and irritability. She has had thoughts of self-harm and suicide in the past and has been diagnosed with depression by her primary care physician. She is currently receiving treatment for depression and has been prescribed medication to help manage her symptoms. Her parents are supportive of her treatment and are involved in her care. She is able to communicate effectively in English and is willing to participate in the study assessments and measures. She is available to complete the scheduled visits and has a reliable means of contact. She is hoping that by participating in this clinical trial, she can help other teens who are struggling with similar mental health issues.

A 35-year-old female patient with no significant past medical history is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic hysterectomy due to uterine fibroids. The patient is physically and mentally able to give full informed consent to participate in this study and complete all study assessments within the timeframes required. She has never received any investigational drug within 30 days prior to EXPAREL administration, nor has she planned administration of another investigational product or procedure during her participation in this study. The patient has no chronic condition requiring use of opioids for treatment of a medical condition for 2 weeks or more prior to surgery. She is not confirmed pregnant at the time of enrollment or breastfeeding. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reactions to amide-type local anesthetics. The patient is not taking any selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), gabapentin, pregabalin (Lyrica®), or duloxetine (Cymbalta®) at the time of enrollment. She is willing to return the diary after POD 4 by mail or upon follow up visit. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

10-year-old female with a history of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and uveitis, currently under the care of a pediatric rheumatologist. The patient has been on adalimumab for the past year with no recurrence of uveitis during that time. She is compliant with her medication and has no contraindications to continue adalimumab. Her arthritis is well-controlled and she has no other medical conditions that would interfere with the study. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and understands the need for highly effective contraception if she were to be of reproductive age. She has no history of intraocular surgery within the past 90 days, nor does she have any chronic hypotony or severe cataract that would prevent a clear view to the posterior pole in both eyes. Her lab values are within normal limits, and she has not had oral corticosteroids or intraocular corticosteroid injection within the last 12 months. She is not currently using NSAID eye drops and has not had acute anterior uveitis characterized by redness and symptoms, including but not limited to floaters, pain, and light sensitivity. The patient’s parents are fully informed of the study and have given their consent for their child to participate.

A 62-year-old woman has been diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia and has undergone treatment with fludarabine. However, the treatment has not been successful, and her disease has relapsed. She has been experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss over the last few months. Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and she has no other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding, and she has agreed to use two effective birth control methods during the study. Her laboratory tests show that she has adequate blood counts, normal liver and kidney function, and negative for HIV and infectious hepatitis. She has never been treated with lenalidomide or dasatinib before, and she has no known hypersensitivity to thalidomide. She is willing and able to take oral medication and agrees to discontinue St. John's Wort while receiving dasatinib therapy. She does not have a significant bleeding disorder or a cardiac condition that would exclude her from the study. She understands and voluntarily signs a written informed consent including a HIPAA form according to institutional guidelines.

50 year-old male with a history of routine dental visits presents with a toothache and sensitivity to hot and cold in the lower right quadrant. Clinical examination reveals a large carious lesion in the distal surface of tooth #46 with pulp exposure. The diagnosis is reversible pulpitis. The patient is informed about the clinical trial for direct pulp capping and is interested in participating. He has no history of systemic diseases and is not taking any medications. He agrees to sign the consent form and will be randomized into one of the two experimental groups for the direct pulp capping procedure. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled for 1 week, 3 months, and yearly thereafter.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes three years ago. He has been taking metformin for the past year, but his blood glucose levels are not well controlled. He is 170 cm tall and weighs 90 kg. He has a sedentary lifestyle and his job requires him to sit at a desk for long hours. He reports feeling tired and sluggish throughout the day. He has a family history of diabetes, with his mother and two of his siblings also having been diagnosed with the disease. His lab results show an FPG level of 170 mg/dL and an HbA1c level of 8.5%. He has no history of diabetic complications or any other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is interested in participating in the trial as he is looking for alternative treatments that may help him better manage his diabetes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) three years ago. He has been experiencing symptoms including fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty with coordination. His EDSS score is 4.5. He has been taking medication for his MS and has not experienced any relapses in the last three months. He is currently employed as a software engineer and works from home. He has no known allergies or medical conditions, and he does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is able to come to the outpatient clinic 2-3 times per week for the next three months. He has no contraindications for MRI, and his medical examination and ECG are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the intermittent hypoxia intervention will help improve his MS symptoms.

48-year-old male with a history of rheumatoid arthritis presents with severe elbow pain and stiffness. He has failed conservative management with physical therapy and corticosteroid injections. He is enrolled in the Discovery Elbow Multi-Center Prospective Study and has undergone a Discovery™ Elbow Replacement surgery. At his two-year follow-up appointment, he consents to participate in the Discovery Elbow Long-Term Survivorship Study. The patient reports significant improvement in pain and function since his surgery and is interested in contributing to the long-term data collection for the study. His past medical history also includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and depression. He takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and sertraline daily. His physical exam is notable for moderate synovitis and tenderness over the elbow joint. He has full range of motion and 4/5 strength in his affected arm. Laboratory studies reveal a mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, consistent with his rheumatoid arthritis.

This clinical trial is not suitable for individual patients as it involves studying genes, environment, and prostate cancer risk in patients with or without prostate cancer and their first-degree relatives. The trial is looking to recruit a total of 2,250 participants, including 750 probands (patients with or without prostate cancer who previously participated in Dr. Shannon's Diet and Prostate Cancer Risk study and consented to future studies) and 1,500 first-degree relatives. Probands can also be referred to the Portland VA Medical Center urology clinic for a prostate biopsy. First-degree relatives (siblings, parents, or offspring) of probands can participate if they are introduced to the study by a proband or found to be related to a proband who is part of a homogenous high-risk subgroup after completing the family history of cancer analysis. The trial will collect blood and saliva samples for fatty acid, DNA, and polymorphism analyses and review medical records for demographics, history and course of disease, and clinical laboratory test results. Participants will also complete questionnaires related to genetic risk, diet history, and environmental risk factors.

A 50 year old male came to the clinic with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) for the past 5 years. He is currently on stable treatment with metformin and DPP-IV inhibitors. His latest HbA1c was 7.6%. He is obese with a BMI of 35 kg/m2. The patient is hypertensive with a blood pressure reading of 150/90 mm Hg. He has a history of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) 8 months ago and had undergone coronary artery revascularization 3 months ago. He also has a history of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). The patient has no history of MRI contraindications, volume depletion or congestive heart failure. He is not on insulin, GLP-1 or any other oral antidiabetic drugs except metformin and DPP-IV inhibitors. His creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min (estimated with Cockroft-Gault formula), and his liver function tests show AST and ALT levels within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of dapagliflozin on tissue specific insulin sensitivity in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

A 35-year-old female presents to the clinic with a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in her left leg three years ago. She was treated with blood thinners and the clot resolved. Recently, she has been experiencing pain and swelling in the same leg and is concerned that the clot may have returned. She has no other significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is willing and able to give informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old patient diagnosed with end-stage renal disease requiring peritoneal dialysis (PD) is eligible for this clinical study. The patient has been on PD for the past 6 months and is currently using an automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) system. The patient is concerned about the unwanted glucose absorption during APD and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates an optimized bi-modal treatment regimen that may reduce glucose absorption. The patient does not have severe heart failure (NYHA III or IV), is not pregnant, and has not experienced catheter malfunction or peritonitis within the past 3 months. The patient is willing to receive both a standard 6 x 2L 1.36% glucose regime and an optimized 7 x 2 L 2.27% glucose + 5 x 2 L 0.1% glucose regime in a crossover fashion as part of the study.

42-year-old male with a history of neuroendocrine tumor of the lung origin. The patient has been treated with various chemotherapy agents and radiation but still experiences disease progression. He has a WHO performance status of 1, ANC of 1.7 x 10^9/L, platelets of 120 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 11 g/dL, serum bilirubin of 1.2 x ULN, ALT of 2.3 x ULN, AST of 2.4 x ULN, INR of 1.1, and serum creatinine of 1.3 x ULN. He has no uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and fasting serum glucose is within normal limits. He has no uncontrolled hypertension and is on antihypertensive medication. He has no history of HIV or hepatitis. He has no history of severe or uncontrolled medical conditions. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has signed the informed consent form.

For this clinical trial, we are seeking participants of different age groups, including healthy adults, adolescents, toddlers, and infants. Participants need to be aged between 10 and 25 years (US) or 42 to 89 days or 12 to 18 months or 10 to 50 years (EU). They should be covered by health insurance, able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures. They must be overtly healthy as determined by medical evaluation, including medical history, physical examination, and judgement of the Investigator.   Female participants who are of childbearing potential must have a negative highly sensitive pregnancy test and agree to use an effective contraceptive method or abstinence from at least 4 weeks prior to the first study intervention administration until at least 4 weeks after the last study intervention administration. Participants must not have any known or suspected congenital or acquired immunodeficiency or any bleeding disorder contraindicating intramuscular vaccination.  Participants must not have a history of any Neisseria meningitidis infection or be at high risk for meningococcal infection during the trial. They must not have known systemic hypersensitivity to latex or any of the vaccine components or a history of a life-threatening reaction to the vaccine(s) used in the trial or to a vaccine containing any of the same substances.  Participants must not have self-reported thrombocytopenia or laboratory-confirmed thrombocytopenia, contraindicating intramuscular vaccination. They must not have a history of intussusception or receipt of any vaccine in the 4 weeks (28 days) preceding the first trial vaccination or planned receipt of any vaccine 4 weeks before to 4 weeks after each trial vaccination.  Participants must not have received immune globulins, blood, or blood-derived products in the past 3 months or since birth for infants and toddlers or oral or injectable antibiotic therapy within 72 hours prior to the first immunogenicity blood draw. They must not have participated in another clinical trial investigating a vaccine, drug, medical device, or medical procedure at the time of study enrollment or planned participation during the present trial period.  Participants must not have a chronic illness that, in the opinion of the investigator, is at a stage where it might interfere with trial conduct or completion or a moderate or severe acute illness/infection, according to the investigator's judgment. They must not have a history of Guillain-Barré syndrome or any neurologic disorders, including any seizures and progressive neurologic disorders.

The patient is a 20-year-old male with a history of cleft lip and palate. The patient presents with a sunken midface and malocclusion, causing difficulty with chewing and speaking. The patient requires maxillary advancement of 6mm to correct the deformity. The patient is not syndromic and has not yet reached skeletal maturity. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the use of orthognathic surgery and distraction osteogenesis for the treatment of cleft lip and palate.

A 12-year-old boy was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) when he was 8 years old. He has been on a TID insulin regimen (morning and bedtime NPH) for the past 3 years. He has no other significant medical history, and his current medications include insulin, levothyroxine, and albuterol as needed for his asthma. He has a BMI of 21. His most recent HbA1c level was 7.2%. The patient has not experienced any episodes of severe hypoglycemia in the past year, but he reports occasional mild hypoglycemic symptoms, especially in the morning. He has been using a blood glucose meter to monitor his blood sugar levels regularly. The patient and his parents have been informed about the study, and they expressed their willingness to participate. The patient will be asked to wear a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS) for 3 days while continuing his usual insulin regimen. During this time, he will also be required to test and record self-monitored blood glucose readings at designated time periods and if he has symptoms of hypoglycemia. The patient and his parents will be asked to complete a survey assessing their satisfaction with the CGMS.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and morning headaches for the past year. He underwent a sleep study and was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea/hypopnea index (AHI) of 30. The sleep physician prescribed CPAP therapy as the primary treatment for his OSA. The patient has been using CPAP for 3 months but has been having trouble adhering to the treatment schedule. He reports that he removes the mask during sleep and also forgets to use it on some nights. He does not have a history of substance abuse or any other serious medical conditions. He is not currently taking any antidepressant medication and has not made any changes to his medication regimen in the past 3 months.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 7 years is looking to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments. She complains of persistent pain and swelling in her joints, especially in her hands and feet. She has tried several treatments, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), but her symptoms have not improved. She has no history of ongoing infections or significant cardiac or pulmonary diseases. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to use an effective contraceptive method while on the trial. She is fluent in Mandarin Chinese and has no history of significant cognitive impairment. She is eager to participate in the study and contribute to the advancement of rheumatoid arthritis treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing epigastric pain and bloating for the past few weeks. She has a past medical history of gastroesophageal reflux disease and has been on proton pump inhibitors for the last year. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any antibiotics. She has no significant family history of gastrointestinal disease. She is being referred for gastroscopy due to her symptoms and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

A 25-year-old, right-handed woman with no history of neurologic disorders or psychiatric conditions is interested in participating in a research study investigating the effects of cooling on the brain. She does not take any medications and does not smoke or use substances. She is willing to abstain from caffeine for 24 hours before the last three session visits. She does not have any surgically implanted metallic foreign bodies or any other conditions that might be physically hazardous during TMS or MRI. She has a normal neurological exam and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who recently gave birth to a healthy baby girl via vaginal delivery. She is experiencing postpartum fatigue and depression, which is making it difficult for her to care for her newborn. She has been feeling exhausted, irritable, and has a lack of motivation to complete daily tasks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of exercise on reducing her fatigue and depression levels. She has no previous history of obstetrics and gynecological conditions, sexually transmitted diseases, or any physical or mental illness.

A 42-year-old female was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 3 years ago. She has been experiencing mild to moderate symptoms with an Ulcerative colitis clinical activity index (UCAI) score of 6. She has been taking mesalamine 2.4g/day (Asacol) for the past year with no improvement in her symptoms. She has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives. She is willing to comply with the protocol and provides consent to participate in the study. Her liver function tests and renal function are within normal limits. She has no systemic infections and is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant.

A 35-year-old male patient comes to the hospital with symptoms of chronic pharyngitis and recurrent episodes of tonsillitis. He has a history of seasonal allergies and has been taking antihistamines for the past few years. He is generally healthy and follows a balanced diet, but he is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical examination reveals enlarged tonsils with white patches, and his throat swab culture is positive for group A Streptococcus. His medical history shows no chronic diseases, and he has no family history of respiratory illnesses or genetic disorders. He consents to participate in the clinical trial to have his tonsil tissue samples analyzed for the expression of ACE 2 and the serine protease TMPRSS2.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse for the past 6 months. She has noticed a bulge or pressure sensation in her vaginal area, especially when standing or lifting heavy objects. She has also experienced urinary incontinence and constipation. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. She has never had surgery on her reproductive organs. She has agreed to undergo a vaginal hysterectomy for her condition and has met the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. She is a Mayo Clinic patient and is at least 18 years old. She has no history of a recognized classic connective tissue disease.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital due to a recent stroke. He has a medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking medications for these conditions, including metformin and lisinopril. He has no known allergies. He has never had a urinary tract infection before, but he has been catheterized during past hospitalizations. He is currently on bed rest and is expected to require a urinary catheter for at least 48 hours. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. She has undergone a previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) through the right forearm transradial access (fTRA). She is currently on aspirin, clopidogrel, and a statin. Her physical exam is unremarkable, and her electrocardiogram shows ST depression in the inferolateral leads. Coronary angiography is recommended, and the patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing distal radial artery access (dTRA) for cardiac catheterization to standard forearm transradial access (fTRA). She is able to provide informed consent and willing to complete a 90-day post-PCI radial artery ultrasound. She has not undergone previous cannulation of the left forearm radial artery for coronary angiography and/or PCI.

This clinical trial does not involve direct participation of patients, but rather clinicians and consumers with severe mental illness who are receiving IMR intervention at participating agencies. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this study.

As this is a feasibility study for primary care patients with vague and non-specific abdominal symptoms, the patient to be included in this trial is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past 4 weeks. She has no history of abdominal cancer or any other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant, and she has not been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal disorders. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not experienced any significant weight loss, and her bowel movements have been normal. She is currently not on any medications. She has not been referred to a cancer patient pathway (CPP) for alarm symptoms. She lives in the municipality of Silkeborg and is registered with a general practitioner (GP) who has been invited to participate in the study. She is willing to provide written informed consent and participate in the study for up to 6 months.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus infection 10 years ago. He has been undergoing regular monitoring and treatment for the condition. Recently, he has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and abdominal discomfort. He has been referred to a liver specialist who has diagnosed him with hepatocellular carcinoma based on biopsy and imaging studies. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of other liver conditions or viral infections. He is willing to participate in the study and provide blood samples for genetic analysis.

55-year-old male patient with severe resorption in the maxilla and total edentulism complains of difficulty in chewing and speaking. He has no known allergies or systemic diseases, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol regularly. His oral hygiene is good, and he has been using a removable denture for the last 5 years. He has no complaints of sinusitis or nasal congestion. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive GM Zygomatic implants and abutments to improve his quality of life. He agrees to undergo the surgical placement of GM Zygomatic implants and abutments according to the standard routine in daily practice, as specified by the manufacturer's instructions for use. He understands the risks and benefits and has signed an informed consent form.

25-year-old male with a history of muscle weakness and difficulty with daily activities such as climbing stairs and lifting objects. Genetic testing revealed a mutation in the dysferlin gene, confirming a diagnosis of LGMD2B/MM. Muscle biopsy showed dysferlin-deficiency. The patient is currently not on any steroid treatment and has not been confined to a wheelchair. There are no other neurologic or internistic diseases present. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and side effects of deflazacort in dysferlinopathy patients.

30-year-old female with a history of social anxiety disorder and panic disorder. She has been experiencing symptoms for the past 5 years, including sweating, trembling, and heart palpitations in social situations, as well as sudden panic attacks. She has previously undergone cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) with a therapist but did not complete the treatment due to scheduling conflicts. She is currently not taking any medication for her anxiety disorders. She has access to a computer with internet connection and is fluent in Swedish. She is interested in participating in a study that allows her to be more actively involved in her own care and decision-making process. She is willing to commit to the study's treatment protocol and follow-up assessments. She does not have any other significant medical or psychiatric comorbidities.

Pt is a 57yo male with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma, who has progressed after one line of chemotherapy with a fluoropyrimidine and platinum agent. The patient has not received prior treatment with cabozantinib or pembrolizumab. The patient has no known brain metastases or cranial epidural disease, and has not received radiation therapy for bone metastasis within the past 2 weeks or any other radiation therapy within the past 4 weeks. The patient has adequate organ and marrow function and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. The patient has no history of severe hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or cabozantinib and/or any of their excipients. The patient is not currently receiving any other investigational agents or any type of small molecule kinase inhibitor. The patient is willing to comply with study and follow-up procedures and is not pregnant or nursing.

Pt is a 10-day-old male neonate weighing 2.8 kg, admitted to the Neonatal Unit with suspected sepsis. The baby was born at term via normal vaginal delivery with no complications. The baby was started on intravenous antibiotics after culture samples were taken. The baby responded well to antibiotic therapy by day 5, and the treating physician has decided to enroll the baby in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of 7-day versus 14-day antibiotic therapy for neonatal bacterial sepsis. The baby meets the eligibility criteria for randomization, including a positive blood culture other than Staphylococcus aureus, no signs and symptoms of sepsis from day 5 through day 7 of starting sensitive antibiotics, and no diagnosis of meningitis, septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, or abscess. The baby's parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have provided their consent to participate. The baby will be randomized on day 7 of antibiotic therapy to receive either a 7-day course of intravenous antibiotics or a 14-day course, and will be followed up for a 35-day period after randomization to assess the primary outcome of treatment failure.

This clinical trial is seeking female patients who are 30 years old or younger and meet institutional criteria to be an oocyte donor. The patient should be willing to donate oocytes for research purposes and agree to the study protocol. Patients who are 18 years old or younger or who have been diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) will be excluded from the study. The patient should have no known medical conditions that would prevent them from undergoing ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval. The patient should be willing to undergo cryopreservation of their oocytes with either liquid nitrogen or slush nitrogen and follow the study protocol for intracytoplasmic sperm injection and embryology outcomes tracking. The patient's ovarian reserve will be taken into consideration, but no specific ovarian reserve cutoffs will be required.

A 55-year-old male who suffered from a heart attack three months ago and underwent angioplasty with stenting. He has never been on cholesterol-lowering medication before. His current lipid profile shows high levels of LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. He is a non-smoker and has no history of liver, renal disease, or myopathy. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of Rosuvastatin in reducing his coronary artery disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of smoking for 30 years and has recently quit smoking. He experiences shortness of breath, especially with physical activity, and has been diagnosed with COPD. He has a family history of respiratory disease, as his father had emphysema. He is interested in participating in research to help find better treatments for COPD and ultimately a cure. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to share his health information over several years.

A 65 year old man comes to the clinic with complaints of forgetfulness and difficulty in remembering things. He has a history of Parkinson's disease and has been on medication for it for the past 2 years. He reports frequent episodes of confusion and forgetfulness which have been affecting his daily activities. He also reports difficulty in concentrating and completing tasks. The patient is a French speaker and is interested in taking part in a clinical trial that validates a french version of the 5-minute Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) as compared to the full french version of the test. He meets the inclusion criteria as a patient suffering from Parkinson's disease and will be submitted to the full version of the MOCA during a face to face procedure. Thirty to forty days later, he will be submitted to the short version of the test through a phone call performed by an independent rater.

A 25-year-old woman who is a healthy oocyte donor and meets the requirements of the Spanish law for oocyte donation has been selected for this clinical trial. She is currently undergoing a controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) following a flexible antagonist protocol and stimulation with recombinant follicular stimulating hormone. She has signed the informed consent for the study. The woman does not have a history of hormonal disorders or other medical conditions that could interfere with the study. She is not pregnant, and there is no evidence of luteinizing hormone surge before triggering. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to research that can potentially benefit women's health.

A 28-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. He exercises regularly and has a BMI of 25. His medical history is unremarkable and he is not taking any medications. He is willing to follow the contraception requirements of the study. He has no history of long QT syndrome and his ECG is normal. His liver function tests, serum creatinine and total bilirubin levels are within normal range. He has not participated in any clinical trials involving receipt of an IMP within the past 90 days. He is interested in learning more about the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

This is a 9 year-old male who was admitted to the PICU due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) following a severe asthma attack. He is currently receiving mechanical ventilation and has been stable for 48 hours. Upon admission, his STRONGkids score was 4. He has no known food allergies or dietary restrictions. He has not been previously enrolled in any randomized controlled outcome studies. The patient's parents have been informed about the study and have provided consent for their child to participate.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a known diagnosis of Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS) caused by genetic mutation. The patient has been conservatively managed and has not received any treatment for WAS. The patient experiences recurrent infections, bleeding episodes, and eczema. The patient's parents are the primary caregivers and are willing to participate in an audio-recorded, telephone, or video conference interview session to share their experiences of living with WAS and its impact on their quality of life. The patient and his parents are fluent in English and meet all the inclusion criteria for this study.

A 48-year-old male with chronic genotype 1 HCV infection is seeking treatment for his condition. He has no history of clinical hepatic decompensation or use of immunosuppressive agents. He is HCV treatment-naive and has HCV RNA levels greater than 10,000 IU/mL at screening. He has no history of hepatitis B virus infection, and he is not currently taking any antiretroviral medications for HIV. He has no other clinically significant illnesses or medical disorders that may interfere with his treatment or compliance with the protocol. He is sexually active and will use two effective methods of contraception during the study.

A pregnant woman between the ages of 18 and 40 years, who has completed 37 weeks of pregnancy and is scheduled for an elective cesarean section, may be eligible for this clinical trial. The patient must have a singleton pregnancy and must not have any history of analgesic administration or intake during the past 24 hours. The patient must have an ASA physical status class I or II and must not have morbid obesity with BMI > 35 kg.m-2 at the initial hospital visit. Additionally, the patient must not have any history of chronic use of steroid therapy or any possibility of anticipated difficult intubation. The trial is conducted at Ain shams University maternity Hospitals in Cairo, Egypt and will last for 4 months from 1st December 2019 to 1st April 2020. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: magnesium sulphate group (M), dexamethasone group (D) or placebo group (C). The aim of the study is to compare the efficacy of single low dose of intravenous MgSO4 versus intravenous dexamethasone as adjuvants to ultrasound guided TAP block for prolongation of postcesaren analgesia. All participants will be monitored all through the surgery by standard monitors including, electrocardiogram, the pulse oximeter, non-invasive blood pressure, and capnography. After the surgery, each patient will receive ultrasound guided bilateral ultrasound guided TAP blocks. The patient will be transferred to the recovery unit and will be monitored for stable vital signs, pain score less than or equal to 2, no nausea or vomiting, calm and alert patient before discharge.

The patient is a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with osteoporosis. She has been taking oral bisphosphonates for the past 6 months to prevent further bone loss. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and is in good health overall. She has no known allergies to blosozumab or its constituents, and has not previously used teriparatide. She has no history of breast carcinoma or long bone fractures within the past year. Her electrocardiogram (ECG) is normal. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further research on osteoporosis treatments.

A 57-year-old male presents with a history of moderate to severe central sleep apnea for the past 3 years. He has been on optimal medical management for the past 6 months, which includes medication and breathing mask-based therapy. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg once daily, atorvastatin 20 mg once daily, and aspirin 81 mg once daily. His BMI is 31 kg/m², and he reports excessive daytime sleepiness despite good adherence to medical management. His recent polysomnography showed an Apnea/Hypopnea Index (AHI) of 32, Central Apnea Index (CAI) of 60% of all apneas, and an Oxygen Desaturation Index (OAI) of 18% of the total AHI. His baseline oxygen saturation is 95% while awake and on room air. He is medically stable for 30 days prior to all baseline testing, and his medications have remained stable during this period. He is expected to tolerate study procedures, therapy titration, and the sensation of therapy. He is willing and able to comply with all study requirements and has signed the Institutional Review Board approved informed consent.

42-year-old sedentary female with a waist circumference of 88 cm, concerned about her risk for metabolic complications. She has no medical conditions that may affect the study measurements, metabolism or distribution. She has a fasting blood glucose level of 5.2 mmol/L (93.6 mg/dL) and is not taking any medication currently, except for occasional use of paracetamol. She consumes fewer than five servings of moderate activity per week and drinks less than 14 units of alcohol per week. She has no known allergies or intolerances to tea extract or rice.

The patient is an 70-year-old male diagnosed with mild to moderate stage Alzheimer's disease. He is able to walk independently and has not engaged in regular exercise in the past 6 months. He has no major orthopedic, neurological or cardiopulmonary issues that restrict his functioning. He is not suffering from non Alzheimer's disease dementia and has no visual impairment.

A 35-year-old male with a BMI of 27.5 kg/m^2 presents with no significant medical history. He is generally healthy and currently not taking any prescription or non-prescription medications, herbal products, or vitamins, except for occasional use of paracetamol. He does not smoke or use tobacco or nicotine products. He consumes an average of 15 units of alcohol per week. He is proficient in both English and Dutch. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the different solutions used to inject drugs under the skin, specifically the excipient solutions used to ensure the stability of the drug product. The purpose of the trial is to determine if there is a difference in the injection site pain experience after an injection under the skin with 12 different study products. The study will be conducted in healthy male and female volunteers aged 18 to 69 years, with a BMI equal to or above 25.0 and below 30.0 kg/m^2. The patient meets all the eligibility criteria and is interested in participating in the trial.

56-year-old male with a history of ocular hypertension and open-angle glaucoma in both eyes. He has been on topical medications, including prostaglandin analogues, for the past year with good IOP control. He has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. He has had a visual field test and OCT within the past 3 months, which were both normal for open-angle glaucoma. He has not had any ocular infections or inflammation in the past 3 months. He does not wear contact lenses and has not undergone any ocular surgeries in the past 6 months. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the clinical trial and is able to provide signed informed consent.

35-year-old male, diagnosed with HIV and pulmonary tuberculosis, with a history of tobacco and alcohol abuse. The patient presented with a cough, fever, and weight loss. Sputum microscopy and culture confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The patient is currently hospitalized and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. He has agreed to participate in the study and has given informed consent. The patient has a good venous access and is able to perform the collection of sputum or tracheal aspirate for microbiological confirmation. The patient has no extra-pulmonary TB and no evidence of resistance to Mtb. The patient's ALT is within normal limits. The patient has agreed to adhere to the proposed treatment for the duration of the study.

A 34-year-old woman has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, cramping, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. She has previously tried other medications for her condition, but they were either ineffective or caused intolerable side effects. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to mesalazine, salicylates, or any excipient. She has no history of severe liver or renal function damage. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety profile of Pentasa slow release tablets 500mg in patients with ulcerative colitis.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and pain for the last 12 months. She has noticed a change in her stool frequency and appearance, which worsens during periods of stress. She has tried various over-the-counter treatments with limited success. She has no known medical history and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She speaks English fluently. Her abdominal pain is not continuous or severe but causes her significant discomfort and affects her daily activities. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for her symptoms.

The patient is a 55 year old man who was recently diagnosed with a biopsy-proven cutaneous SCC lesion on his right cheek. The lesion measures approximately 7mm in diameter and is growing rapidly. He is concerned about the possibility of disfigurement and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to treat the lesion. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history and no current medications. He works as a construction worker and spends a lot of time outdoors. He is married with two adult children and enjoys spending time with his family and gardening in his free time. He has no history of skin cancer in his family. He is willing to apply the topical remetinostat gel 1% three times daily for 8 weeks and cover it with an occlusive bandage. He understands that he will need to avoid using certain topical or systemic therapies during the study and agrees to comply with the study requirements. He has signed and dated the informed consent document and is willing to use acceptable methods of contraception to avoid pregnancy.

A 46-year-old female presented with a 6-month history of widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and depression. She denied any history of trauma or injuries. She reported taking medications for hypertension and antidepressants. She had tried physical therapy, massage therapy, and acupuncture in the past with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She reported difficulty with daily activities such as household chores, work, and social activities due to pain and fatigue. She was interested in participating in a study to help manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She is proficient in English and willing to participate in an 8-month intervention study. She has no contraindicated medical conditions and is not pregnant.

A 32-year-old man was diagnosed with Crohn's disease three years ago. He has been experiencing moderate to severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloody stools. He has tried several conventional therapies, including oral locally acting steroids, intravenous corticosteroids, and immunosuppressants, but has not achieved adequate relief of his symptoms. In addition, he has tried biologic therapies, but had to discontinue them due to insurance reasons. He has been on a stable dose of methotrexate for the past six months. He has normal screening laboratory results. He is willing to meet the contraception recommendations if he enrolls in the study. He wants to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of upadacitinib as an induction therapy for his CD.

A 9-year-old Hispanic male child with a BMI at the 94th percentile presents to a federally-qualified health center for a routine check-up. The child is accompanied by his mother, who is fluent in both English and Spanish. The child's medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. He is currently not taking any medications. The child's vital signs are within normal limits, and he appears to be in good health. The physical examination reveals the presence of excess adipose tissue, particularly around the abdomen. The child's weight is 75 lbs, and his height is 4 ft 8 in. Laboratory results show a fasting glucose level within the normal range. The child is diagnosed with obesity and referred to participate in a pediatric weight management intervention (PWMI) trial. The mother agrees to participate in the study and is willing to follow study procedures for one year.

A 55-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure for the past 10 years presents with complaints of shortness of breath and difficulty sleeping at night. He reports waking up in the middle of the night gasping for air and feeling very tired during the day. His current medications include lisinopril, furosemide, and spironolactone. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies any drug use. His BMI is 29. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 30%. He underwent a sleep study and was diagnosed with central sleep apnea requiring ASV therapy. He is interested in participating in the FACE study to help advance research on the management of his condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with ovarian clear cell carcinoma (OCCC) with confirmed mutations in one of the SWI/SNF genes (SMARCA4, ARID1A). She has received at least one prior regimen in the recurrent or advanced setting and is not a candidate for other potentially curative treatment options. She has no history of immunodeficiency or chronic systemic steroid therapy. She is not currently participating in or has participated in a study of an investigational agent or has used an investigational device within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. She has no known additional malignancy that is progressing or has required active treatment within the past 3 years. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive within the projected duration of the study, starting with the screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of trial treatment. She provides written informed consent and has measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1. She has provided archival tumor tissue sample or a newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of a tumor lesion not irradiated. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status of 0 to 1 and adequate organ function. She has not received prior therapy with LSD1 targeted agents including monoamine oxidases for cancer therapy. She has not received radiotherapy within 2 weeks of start of study treatment. She has not received a live vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She has no diagnosis of severe hypersensitivity (≥Grade 3) to pembrolizumab and/or any of its excipients. She has no active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years (i.e. with use of disease modifying agents, corticosteroids or immunosuppressive drugs). She has no history of (non-infectious) pneumonitis that required steroids or has current pneumonitis. She has no active infection requiring systemic therapy. She has no known history of HIV, Hepatitis B, or known active Hepatitis C. She has no known history of active TB. She has no clinically significant, uncontrolled heart disease and/or cardiac repolarization abnormality. She is not currently receiving any substances that cannot be discontinued 14 days or 5 half-lives for CYP inhibitors (whichever is shorter) prior to Cycle 1 Day 1.

A 25-year-old male presents with a recurring pain and swelling in the skin at the top of his buttocks. He reports that he has had this issue for the past 2 years and has had multiple abscesses drained in the past. The patient reports that he has had to miss work and school due to the pain and the wound care required. On physical examination, there is a small pit in the skin with surrounding erythema and tenderness. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat his pilonidal disease and wants to explore new options for a permanent solution.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been experiencing excessive sleepiness during the day for the past year. He is diagnosed with narcolepsy based on clinical history and nocturnal polysomnogram (NPSG) results that ruled out other sleep disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea/hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) or periodic limb movement with sleep (PLMs). The patient has a mean sleep latency (from 4 naps) of less than 10 minutes and/or a Clinical Global Impression of Change (CGI-C) rating for excessive sleepiness (ES) of 4 or higher. The patient's blood pressure is within the 5th and 95th percentiles for his age, and he is in good health as determined by a medical and psychiatric history, physical examination, ECG, and clinical laboratory tests. The patient does not have a seizure disorder, history of psychosis or clinically significant head trauma, or past neurosurgery. The patient is not at suicidal risk and has not attempted suicide in the past. The patient does not have an average of 5 or more apneic/hypopneic episodes per hour of nocturnal sleep as assessed by NPSG at the baseline visit. The patient has not shown a clinically significant drug sensitivity to stimulants such as amphetamine, dextroamphetamine, methylphenidate, or pemoline; and/or modafinil or any of its components. The patient has not used any prescription or nonprescription medications, including dietary supplements with psychoactive or sedating properties, within 1 week of the baseline visit, except for medications for the treatment of cataplexy, which have been stable for at least 1 month. The patient has not used any MAO inhibitors or SSRIs within 2 weeks of the baseline visit, unless used for cataplexy. The patient has not received any investigational drug within 4 weeks of the baseline visit. The patient does not have any disorder that could interfere with drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion, or any active, clinically significant gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, hematologic, neoplastic, endocrine, neurologic, immunodeficiency, pulmonary, or other major clinically significant disorder/disease. The patient's physical examination, ECG findings, and clinical laboratory test results are within the normal range(s). The patient does not have an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) below the lower limit of normal at the screening visit. The patient's seated pulse is within the range of 60 through 115 bpm after resting for 5 minutes. The patient does not have a history of alcohol, narcotic, or any other substance abuse or dependence as defined by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of the American Psychiatric Association, 4th Edition (DSM IV) criteria. The patient's total daily intake of caffeine is less than 250 mg per day. The patient is not pregnant or lactating/nursing. The patient has not had a clinically significant illness within 4 weeks of the baseline visit and is not symptomatic for any clinically significant illness at the screening or baseline visit.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of recurrent abdominal pain, discomfort and bloating for the last 6 months. Endoscopy showed a gastric ulcer and biopsy confirmed H.pylori infection. The patient has no known allergies to any of the study medications and is not taking any other medications that are contraindicated for the study. The patient has not taken any PPI or antibiotics for the past 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant, lactating and is not a reproductive-aged woman. The patient has controlled diabetes and hypertension. The patient has no history of digestive malignancy, gastrectomy or esophagectomy. The patient has no known hereditary diseases such as Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactose deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption. The patient understands the conditions of the clinical trial and agrees to participate by signing the informed consent form.

A 22-year-old male with Asperger's disorder has recently graduated from college and is struggling to find employment. He has difficulty with social interactions and has a limited understanding of workplace norms and expectations. He lives independently in an apartment and enjoys playing video games and reading science fiction novels. He has no history of neurological disorders or major mental illness. He is interested in participating in a program that can help him improve his social skills and increase his chances of finding a job.

The patient is a 55-year-old Korean male with a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia with LDL-C levels between 100 to 250 mg/dl. The patient has no history of diabetes, myocardial infarction, coronary artery bypass surgery, or angioplasty within the past 3 months. He is not experiencing congestive heart failure and has not been diagnosed with any uncontrolled endocrine or metabolic disease that is known to influence serum lipids or lipoproteins. The patient is currently taking medications to control hypertension, and he understands and agrees to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with angina pectoris. She experiences chest pain frequently, and it has started to impact her daily activities. Her angiogram shows a bifurcation lesion in her left anterior descending artery (LAD) and diagonal branch, with the diameter of the main vessel estimated to be greater than 2.5mm, and the diameter of the side branch estimated to be greater than 2.0mm. She has no history of ST-elevation Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) within the last 24 hours, and her expected survival is greater than 1 year. She has no known allergies to Aspirin, Clopidogrel, or Ticlopidine or sirolimus/paclitaxel. She has been informed about the study and has signed the consent form to participate.

38-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with major depressive disorder and has been experiencing suicidal ideation for the past week. He has a history of substance abuse but has been sober for the past two months. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the study. He has no history of psychotic disorders, and his urine drug screen is negative for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). He has no medical conditions that would preclude his participation in the study.

Patient is a female caregiver, aged 28 years, living in The Gambia with a child under 5 years of age. She will be living in the compound of one of the peer health educators participating in the study. The patient is open to learning and willing to participate in the peer health education programme about malaria prevention and treatment. She has some basic knowledge about malaria and its transmission but is interested in learning more about the disease and how to prevent it. The patient is willing to be interviewed 10 weeks and 6 months after the start of the programme to evaluate the impact of the malaria messages on her knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding malaria prevention and treatment. She understands that participation in the study is voluntary and that she can withdraw at any time without any negative consequences.

54 y/o female with no prior history of breast cancer or breast symptoms. She underwent routine Full-Field Digital Mammography (FFDM) which showed one or more abnormalities, including calcifications, and was referred for diagnostic work-up within 4 weeks. She is post-menopausal, with documentation of cessation of menses for greater than one year. She has no breast implants or reconstructed breasts. She is surgically sterile (with documentation of bilateral oophorectomy and/or documented hysterectomy). She has a compatible breast size with the dimensions of 24x31 cm of the image detector. She is in sufficient good health to be able to undergo an examination on mammography equipment as determined by the Investigator. She is able to provide written informed consent or have a legally authorized representative provide written informed consent. She has not undergone radiotherapy or chemotherapy and has no history of prior radiotherapy treatment on the side of the targeted breast. She has not been previously enrolled in this study and has not participated in another trial of an investigational product.

A 35-year-old woman who has struggled with weight gain and difficulty controlling her blood sugar levels, despite medication, comes to the clinic for a consultation. She has a BMI of 32 and has been weight stable for the past 6 months. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or psychiatric disorders. She is not currently taking any medication that may affect energy metabolism, gastrointestinal function, body weight, or appetite. She has not experienced any recent weight changes in the past 3 months or any fever or upper respiratory infections. She currently engages in light exercise, such as walking, but does not regularly perform high-intensity exercise. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not plan to become pregnant in the near future. She does not smoke or use any illicit substances. She does not experience claustrophobia in confined spaces and has not donated blood within the past 3 months. She is able to comprehend the study protocol and does not experience migraines.

32-year-old male, BMI of 29, with a history of prediabetes and interest in improving his glucose control through lifestyle changes. He is currently taking metformin and has no known dermatologic conditions on his upper arms. He has health insurance and is willing to wear a continuous glucose monitor for 12-14 days on both arms. He has no implanted medical devices and is not critically ill or on dialysis. He has no planned magnetic resonance imaging screening or high-frequency electrical heat treatment during the study period. He is willing to comply with the fasting requirements of the study and maintain once daily email responses. He is not pregnant, planning pregnancy in the next 30 days, or breastfeeding. He has no active eating disorder and is not taking any medications that have an increased risk of hypoglycemia. He has not completed a specialized diet in the past 2 weeks and has no history of adverse events during prior fasting experiences. He is within the age range of 18-65 years.

As this study is focused on postmortem analysis of patients who were poisoned with paraquat, there are no specific patient descriptions needed for eligibility criteria. The study aims to analyze the histo-pathological findings in all patients who were confirmed to have paraquat poisoning through dithionate test postmortem. However, it is important to note that this study is not recruiting living patients for any intervention or treatment.

This is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing jaw pain and tightness for the past year. She has noticed that she grinds her teeth at night and sometimes during the day when she is stressed. She has also experienced headaches, limited opening of her mouth, and clicking sounds when she opens her jaw. She has tried using a mouth guard at night but has not noticed much improvement. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the exercises and techniques being studied can help alleviate her symptoms. She is able to make mental evaluations, has no major health problems, and is willing to commit to the training program. She has provided her informed consent to participate in the study.

28 yo F with a long-standing history of anorexia nervosa, extreme weight loss and malnutrition, and previous hospitalizations for AN. The patient is currently medically stable for outpatient treatment, and has no significant physical or medical conditions that would influence eating or weight. She has not previously received cognitive remediation therapy or cognitive behavioral therapy for AN. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of cognitive remediation therapy in improving treatment retention in people with anorexia nervosa. Past Medical History: - Anorexia nervosa with a BMI of 15.5 - Previous hospitalizations for AN - No other significant medical or surgical history.

Unfortunately, as this is a retrospective study using archived tissue samples, no patient description is needed for this particular clinical trial. The study will be conducted on tissue samples from patients who have already been diagnosed with either endometrial cancer, endometrial hyperplasia, or normal endometrium.

A 56-year-old Spanish-speaking woman presents with hearing loss that has been slowly progressing over the past few years. She reports difficulty understanding conversations, especially in noisy environments, and frequently asks others to repeat themselves. She has not previously sought treatment for her hearing loss. She has a communication partner, her daughter, who is willing to attend the program with her. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and has no cognitive impairment.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it is not recruiting patients. The study is focused on testing interventions aimed at improving antimalarial stewardship in the retail sector in Nigeria. The study will involve a cluster-randomized controlled trial using private medicine retail outlets as the unit of randomization. The participants in the study will be customers leaving participating shops who will be interviewed about their demographics, symptoms of their current illness, whether they had a malaria diagnostic test at the outlet or elsewhere, how much they paid for the test, the results of the test, and the drug(s) they purchased. There are inclusion and exclusion criteria for this study, but they are related to the individuals who will be interviewed during the exit interviews and not to patients being recruited for a clinical trial.

9 yo F with persistent asthma, on Fluticasone and Albuterol PRN, and BMI at 95th percentile for age and gender norms. Child and parent live together and speak English.
