No history of musculo-skeletal condition that limits walking, heart condition, chronic lung diseases limiting physical activity, or current participation in commercial weight loss program. No use of antipsychotic agents, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, systemic corticosteroids within 3 months, or prescription weight loss drugs within 6 months. Parent is aged 35.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who is generally healthy and has a normal body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2. She doesn't have any chronic diseases or gastrointestinal disorders. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is not a competitive athlete and doesn't have any drug dependencies. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of traditional Greek meals on glycemic responses. She enjoys trying new foods and is willing to follow the dietary instructions provided by the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was diagnosed with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma after undergoing a surgical resection. The tumor was confirmed to be stage IIIB with a histologic grade of G3 according to AJCC TNM (8th edition, 2017). There is no evidence of extrahepatic metastases. Preoperative assessment showed Child-Pugh A and ECOG performance status 1. The patient has chronic HBV infection with HBV-DNA <500 IU / ml. The patient has not received any anti-tumor treatment for the intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma before surgery. The patient's vital organ function indicators meet the study requirements: neutrophils ≥1.5*109/L, platelets≥50*109/L, hemoglobin≥90g/l, Alanine aminotransferase （ALT） and Aspartate aminotransferase （AST） ≤ 2.5 times ULN, total bilirubin≤1.5 ULN, International standardized ratio (INR) ≤2.3ULN, creatinine ≤1.5 ULN. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or clinically significant heart disease. The patient has not received a live vaccine within 4 weeks of the first dose of study medication. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has been deemed suitable for the clinical trial by the principal investigator or physician-in-charge.

A 23-year-old female who received a single dose of quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine 5 years ago and is interested in receiving a booster dose to maintain protection against meningococcal disease. She is in good health and has no history of meningococcal infection or vaccination with a meningococcal B vaccine. She is not pregnant or lactating and is of non-childbearing potential. She has not received any other vaccines in the past 4 weeks and is not planning to receive any other vaccines during the study period, except for influenza vaccine, which she may receive at least 2 weeks before the investigational vaccine. She has no history of immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive therapy and is not at high risk for meningococcal infection during the trial. She has no known hypersensitivity to any of the vaccine components and has not had a life-threatening reaction to any vaccine. She is willing and able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male with a history of chronic periodontitis presents with a chief complaint of gum recession and loose teeth. The patient reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few months. He has been using a soft-bristled toothbrush and flossing regularly, but still experiences bleeding gums and bad breath. The patient denies any history of smoking or drug abuse. He is not currently taking any medications that affect the number or function of platelets. The patient has a normal platelet count and no history of immunologic diseases. He has not undergone any periodontal therapy in the last 6 months. The patient has a mandibular infrabony pocket measuring ≥ 6mm with radiographic evidence of intrabony defect. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Supercell glue (PRFM and PBMSCs) as a regenerative material in comparison with PRFM alone in human mandibular periodontal intraosseous defects.

60-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction requiring coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) in [**2010**]. The patient is now scheduled for a repeat CABG due to a high-grade stenosis in one of his grafts. He reports occasional heartburn but denies any other gastrointestinal symptoms. He is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. He has no history of dysphagia or voice changes. On physical exam, he has no obvious cranial nerve deficits and his lungs are clear. His cardiovascular exam is notable for a regular rate and rhythm with a grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left sternal border. His current medications include aspirin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He is willing to participate in two research testing sessions to assess his swallowing function and vocal fold mobility before and after his CABG surgery.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a BMI of 24. She leads an active lifestyle, exercises regularly and follows a balanced diet. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications or natural health products. She has no known history of liver or kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension, stroke, myocardial infarctions, thyroid disease, gastrointestinal disease, or AIDS. She is interested in participating in a research study that aims to investigate the effects of Salba and Flax on postprandial glycemia and appetite. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with gastric cancer. He underwent a D2 resection, and the pathology reports confirmed stage IIIB adenocarcinoma. The patient has a Karnofsky performance score (KPS) of 80, indicating that he is able to carry out normal activities with some difficulty. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or other anti-cancer therapies. His blood counts are within normal limits, and he has no prior history of allergic reactions to Fluorouracil or Platinum drugs. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. There are no concurrent malignancies, malabsorption syndromes, or symptoms of peripheral neuropathy. The patient has no uncontrolled medical conditions and is free from severe postoperative complications such as anastomotic leakage.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a nurse at the Military Health Schools of Lyon-Bron. He has been actively involved in providing care to patients during the COVID-19 pandemic. He reports that he has not experienced any symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath. However, he is concerned about the possibility of having been exposed to the virus during his work at the health schools. He has not been tested for COVID-19 before, and he is willing to participate in the study to determine the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among the personnel of the health schools. He understands that the study will involve a blood sample collection for serological testing and that the results will help to better understand the epidemiological dynamics of the virus in the population of the Military Health Schools of Lyon-Bron. The patient has no contraindications to blood sampling and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

28 year-old pregnant woman at 12 weeks gestation with no prior history of NIPT. She is currently receiving prenatal care and has no significant medical history. The pregnancy is singleton and she is willing to provide informed consent for the collection of a whole blood sample. She has not had any invasive prenatal diagnostic procedure, transfusion of blood or blood components in the past 8 weeks, or preimplantation genetic screening. She does not have a history of transplant or malignancy.

Patient is a 9yo male who was not breast-fed during infancy. He is right-hand dominant and attending school at an appropriate grade level with a normal body mass index (BMI). He has no current general medical or psychiatric illnesses and is medication-free. His intelligence is normal as assessed by the Kaufman Brief Intelligence Test. He and his biological parent are willing and able to provide assent and informed, written consent. He has no pacemaker, cerebral aneurysm clip, cochlear implant, or metal fragments lodged within the eye. He does not have claustrophobia and does not require sedation. He has not lost consciousness for more than 10 minutes in duration. The patient has not been adopted. The study aims to determine if 8-week dietary treatment with the omega-3 fatty acid docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) improves attention performance and associated cortical activity and metabolism in 8 - 10 year old males that were not breast-fed during infancy. The patient is eligible for the study and will be evaluated for inclusion.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and is recommended to receive adjuvant radiation therapy. She reports experiencing moderate to severe fatigue during her treatment and has a qualifying Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI) score of 6. She is not anemic and is not currently taking medication to manage her fatigue or pain. She does not have clinical evidence of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism and has not used erythropoietin to control anemia. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ALC in treating her fatigue.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing severe urinary disturbances associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) for the past 6 months. He reports frequent urination, difficulty initiating urination, weak urine flow, and incomplete emptying of the bladder. His International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) is 23 and his Quality of Life (QoL) score is 4. The patient has not been treated with silodosin, an α1A-adrenoceptor selective antagonist, or any other α1A-adrenoceptor blocker in the past one month. He has not been prescribed antiandrogens or undergone any prostatectomy, intrapelvic radiation therapy, transurethral microwave hyperthermia, or transurethral needle ablation. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. The patient does not have any renal or hepatic impairment, orthostatic hypotension, or any other medical condition that may affect urine passing. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 8 weeks and has a PSA level of less than 10ng/mL.

The patient is a 25-year-old male smoker who has been smoking for the past 5 years. He smokes about 10 cigarettes a day and has no known medical history of pulmonary or cardiovascular disease. He has a normal body mass index (BMI) and is generally healthy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the acute effect of smoking on the distribution of ventilation/perfusion ratio in the lung. He is aware of the risks associated with smoking and is willing to quit smoking if necessary. He has no family history of malignant hyperthermia or neuro-muscular disorders, and he is not hypersensitive to any of the inert gases or substances administered. He has never experienced postoperative nausea and vomiting, and he is not currently pregnant. The patient is enthusiastic to participate in the study to contribute to the greater understanding of the acute effects of smoking on lung function.

A 63-year-old man with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with complaints of tingling, pain, and numbness in his feet. He is a retired construction worker who has always been active, but his symptoms have begun to limit his mobility. The patient reports taking metformin and glipizide as prescribed by his physician. On physical examination, the patient has decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick in a stocking-glove distribution. He has no history of amputation, and his mental health is stable. The patient has not previously received biofeedback treatment, and he does not have a history of alcohol abuse. He is interested in participating in the study to find alternative treatment options for his diabetic neuropathy.

A 8-year-old male patient was referred to the Otto Heubner Center in Berlin, Germany with a history of recurrent seizures and developmental delay. The patient was diagnosed with epilepsy at two years of age and has been treated with multiple anti-epileptic drugs with partial response. The patient has also been noted to have global developmental delay and motor deficits. The patient's family history is significant for a paternal uncle with a similar history of seizures and developmental delay. The patient's physical exam was significant for microcephaly, hypertonia, and hyperreflexia. The patient's brain MRI was normal. The patient has undergone multiple diagnostic procedures including metabolic testing, chromosomal microarray, and targeted gene panel sequencing, all of which were negative. The patient's parents are available for blood draw and have provided informed consent for genetic testing as part of a clinical trial. The family is interested in participating in the MENDEL-study to potentially obtain a diagnosis and improve their child's quality of life.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) at the age of 23. She is married and has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. Her menstrual cycles are irregular, ranging from 30 to 45 days. She is overweight with a body mass index (BMI) of 32. She has a history of acne and excessive hair growth on her face and body. She has no history of diabetes or hypertension. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no known drug allergies or chronic medical conditions. Her family history is negative for diabetes or hypertension. She is fluent in English and has no language barrier. She is keen to participate in the study to improve her chances of having a healthy pregnancy in the future.

A 57 year old female with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia presents to the emergency room with shortness of breath, cough, fever, and fatigue. Imaging reveals a left lower lobe infiltrate consistent with community-acquired pneumonia. Blood cultures are drawn and the patient is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Despite treatment, the patient's condition worsens and she develops acute kidney injury and liver dysfunction. She is diagnosed with sepsis and meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial. The patient consents to participate in the study and is randomized to receive different dosages of Allocetra-OTS. She is followed closely for efficacy and safety for the duration of the study.

A 55-year-old female with a history of presbyopia and no significant medical history is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of three different topical ophthalmic solutions. The patient must be in good general health and have no history of allergic reactions to any of the study drugs or their components. The trial is designed to test the effectiveness of the study drugs against each other in treating presbyopia, and the patient will be randomly assigned to one of the three treatment groups. The patient should be willing to participate in a double-masked crossover study and be available for follow-up visits.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a background in resistance training for the last 2 years. He is currently not taking any fish oil supplements and is interested in improving his muscle mass and function. He has no history of metabolic, cardiovascular, or pulmonary diseases, and is not experiencing any chronic inflammatory conditions, neurological conditions, or sexually transmitted diseases. He is a non-smoker and has not been diagnosed with hypertension, hypercholesterolemia or dyslipidemia. He is not taking any medications to manage cholesterol, blood lipids, blood pressure, or diabetes, and has not used performance-enhancing drugs or anabolic agents. He is not currently taking oral contraceptives, and is not pregnant or intending to become pregnant while enrolled in the study. The patient's fasting blood total cholesterol concentration is 190mg/dl and fasting blood glucose concentration is 90mg/dl, within the range of the eligibility criteria. He will participate in a six-week study that involves fish oil or placebo supplementation alongside his current resistance exercise training regimen. He will be randomly assigned to either the fish oil or placebo group, and will be monitored throughout the study for adherence to the intervention and dietary recommendations.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of prostate cancer confirmed by biopsy. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He underwent an in-house MRI with contrast medium, which showed a suspicious lesion in the prostate gland. The imaging was followed by a biopsy, which confirmed the presence of prostate cancer. The patient is scheduled to undergo a radical prostatectomy at the same institution. He has no history of other malignancies or significant medical conditions, and he is not taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to extract accurate and reliable quantitative biomarkers for prostate cancer diagnosis using radiomics.

The patient is a 11-year-old girl who was referred to the orthopedic clinic due to a mild curvature of her spine. She complains of occasional back pain and feels self-conscious about her posture. The doctor diagnosed her with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) in the early stage with a primary Cobb angle of 18 degrees. She has not started her menstrual period yet. She is physically active and enjoys playing tennis and swimming. She has no other musculoskeletal or developmental illnesses. She has never had surgery or orthotic treatment for AIS. She is fluent in English and has no psychiatric disorders. She has not experienced any recent trauma or traumatic events. She is willing and able to comply with the posture correction girdle protocol.

The patient is a 58 year old male who has been experiencing abdominal pain and nausea for the past two months. He has lost approximately 10 pounds during this time and feels fatigued. He has seen his primary care physician who ordered an upper endoscopy and biopsy which revealed adenocarcinoma of the stomach. The patient has no history of other malignancies and has never received radiation therapy. He is married and has two adult children. He is retired and enjoys gardening and playing cards with his friends. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his laboratory tests show adequate hepatic, renal, heart, and hematologic functions. His platelets are 110×10^9/L, neutrophil count is 3.5×10^9/L, serum creatinine is 1.2mg/dl, total bilirubin is within normal limits, and serum transaminase is 1.5×the ULN. He has no significant comorbid conditions and has never had coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction.

A 56 year old Turkish man with a clinical diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes presents with difficulty in managing his blood sugar levels. He has been struggling with his diet and exercise regimen, and has not been able to maintain a consistent routine. His blood sugar levels have been fluctuating, and he has been experiencing fatigue and difficulty with concentration. He is able to read and write Turkish, and is motivated to improve his diabetes management. He has had no history of cancer or mental disorder.

A 38-year-old female was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis two years ago. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloody stools, and fatigue. She has tried different medications including mesalamine, sulfasalazine, and corticosteroids but her symptoms have not improved. She has lost weight and avoided social gatherings because of her condition. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher but has had to take a leave of absence due to her illness. She is eager to try new treatments and is willing to undergo a leukapheresis. She has no history of major illnesses or allergies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help researchers find a new treatment for ulcerative colitis.

A 40 year old woman with a history of preeclampsia during her first pregnancy, which was complicated by severe hypertension and proteinuria. She has since then been diagnosed with hypertension and is on medication to control it. She is otherwise healthy, with no known history of cardiovascular disease. She is fluent in Danish and has no physical or mental disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about her risk of developing cardiovascular disease and to potentially prevent it.

The patient is a 20-year-old male diagnosed with Angelman Syndrome (AS) with molecular confirmation. He completed the OV101-15-001 study up to the end of study (EOS) and is currently under stable doses of anti-epileptic medication, gabapentin, clonidine, and melatonin for at least 4 weeks prior to baseline. The patient has a caregiver who is capable of providing informed consent and attending all scheduled study visits. The patient is able to swallow study drug capsules or ingest the contents of study drug capsules after sprinkling the capsule contents onto 1 spoon of applesauce or low-fat yogurt. The patient has been sexually abstinent from the first day of screening until 30 days after the last dose of study treatment. The patient has not posted any personal medical data or information related to the study on any website or social media site. The patient has not discontinued from the OV101-15-001 study due to safety reasons causally related to OV101. The patient does not have any concomitant disease or condition that could interfere with the conduct of the study or that would pose an unacceptable risk to the subject in this study. The patient has no poorly controlled seizures or clinically significant clinical laboratory abnormalities or vital signs at the time of screening. The patient has not used benzodiazepines, zolpidem, zaleplon, zopiclone, eszopiclone, barbiturates, or ramelteon for sleep within the 4 weeks prior to Day 1. The patient has no history of suicidal behavior and is considered suitable for enrollment by the investigator. The patient has not enrolled in any clinical trial or used any investigational agent or device, or has participated in any investigational procedure, within the 30 days before screening or does so concurrently with this study. The patient is not a family member of the investigator or of study site staff.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing gradual vision loss in both eyes due to cataracts. He has no other ocular diseases or prior surgeries that may affect the quality of his vision. His potential visual acuity is estimated to be 20/25 in both eyes, and his pupillary dilation is at least 7mm. He requires IOL power in the range of 18-22 diopters. He has no known allergies to any medications or materials. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and attend follow-up appointments for up to 3 years.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with difficulty in losing weight despite making significant lifestyle changes. She has a BMI of 30 and a waist circumference of 36 inches. She reported having a sedentary lifestyle and consuming a diet high in refined carbohydrates and saturated fats. Her fasting blood glucose was 98 mg/dL and her HOMA-IR was 3.2 indicating insulin resistance. She denied having any history of smoking, alcohol consumption or fish/shellfish allergy. Her medications included lisinopril and atorvastatin. Her physical examination revealed no significant findings. She was interested in participating in the study to better understand the effects of dietary omega-3 fats on insulin sensitivity in adults.

This study does not involve patient recruitment as it is an observational study or registry designed to collect data on the use of Xydalba® in daily clinical practice in Germany. Therefore, no patient description is required.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents with a diagnosis of advanced, metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has exhausted all standard-of-care treatments and has shown resistance to established therapies. He has multiple measurable tumors as outlined by modified RECIST v1.1. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 3 months. He is otherwise healthy, with acceptable liver and renal function, hematologic and coagulation status, and no known infections with HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. He has not undergone any significant surgery to the gastrointestinal tract that could impair absorption or result in short bowel syndrome with diarrhea due to malabsorption. He is willing to comply with procedures required in this protocol and has read and signed the Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved informed consent form (ICF) prior to any study related procedure. He has not received treatment with radiation therapy, surgery, chemotherapy, or investigational therapy within 28 days or 5 half-lives, whichever occurs first, prior to study entry (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or Mitomycin C). He is non-fertile or agrees to use an adequate method of contraception. He has not exhibited allergic reactions to a similar structural compound, biological agent, or formulation. He is not currently receiving any other investigational agent. He is not exhibiting any of the exclusion criteria listed in the study protocol.

A 58-year-old current smoker who has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain for the past 3 months. The symptoms have progressively worsened, and they have been accompanied by weight loss and fatigue. The patient has a history of hypertension, and his family history is unremarkable. The chest X-ray revealed a large mass in the left lung, and the CT scan confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. Biopsy results showed adenocarcinoma, and the patient has been staged as IIIB. The patient is considering participating in a clinical trial that will test the safety and efficacy of two drugs, Afatinib and Dasatinib, that will be used together to treat his lung cancer. The patient is aware of the potential side effects and understands the importance of close monitoring by the medical team. He has no history of significant cardiac, hepatic, or renal disorders, and he is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated in the study. The patient is motivated to participate in the trial and hopes to contribute to the development of new treatments for lung cancer.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with a mild head injury after falling down a few steps. She has no loss of consciousness, vomiting or seizure. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and she takes lisinopril daily. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her vital signs are stable, and her neurological exam is unremarkable. The patient is concerned about her injury and asks if she needs a CT scan. The physician explains that the use of CT scans may not always be necessary and that there are guidelines to help determine if a CT scan is necessary. The physician informs the patient about

An 75-year-old Caucasian man presented with exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and chest discomfort. He had a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He underwent a coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) 8 years ago. He had been taking lisinopril, amlodipine, and aspirin. In the physical examination, his blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg, heart rate was 76 beats per minute, and respiratory rate was 18 breaths per minute. He had a grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard best at the second right intercostal space with radiation to the carotid arteries. His electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. His echocardiogram revealed severe aortic stenosis with a peak gradient of 78 mmHg and a mean gradient of 50 mmHg. His aortic valve area was 0.7 cm². His left ventricular ejection fraction was 60%. His coronary angiogram showed patent grafts and mild stenosis in the proximal left anterior descending artery. He was referred for aortic valve replacement surgery.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with advanced-stage ovarian cancer. She has undergone a partial oophorectomy and chemotherapy treatment without much improvement. She is now looking for alternative treatment options and is interested in participating in clinical trials. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. She is able to perform daily activities without assistance and has an ECOG performance status score of 1. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and undergo study-specific procedures for the JAB-3068 clinical trial. She has no known serious allergies to experimental drugs and has not been diagnosed with brain or spinal metastases. The patient is seeking a new treatment option to help improve her quality of life and potentially extend her life expectancy.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who previously participated in the double-blind study C1538/3027/NA/MN or C1538/3028/AP/MN. He has a diagnosis of narcolepsy or OSAHS according to the criteria established by the International Classification of Sleep Disorders (ICSD) manual of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM). The patient is in good health as determined by a medical and psychiatric history, ECGs, physical examination findings, serum chemistry, hematology, and urinalysis. The patient's blood pressure is within the 5th percentile and 95th percentile on the National High Blood Pressure Education Program guidelines for blood pressure levels for boys and girls ages 6 through 16 years. He has not been diagnosed with any other major clinically significant disorder/disease and has no history of sensitivity to stimulants such as amphetamine, dextroamphetamine, methylphenidate, or pemoline; and modafinil or any of its components. The patient is not taking more than 500 mg of caffeine per day and is not pregnant or lactating/nursing. The patient's parent or legal guardian has provided written informed consent and the patient has given written assent.

A 42-year-old woman has been experiencing daily lower back pain for the past 6 months. She rates her pain as a 6 out of 10 on the pain scale, and it is dominating over any pain she may have in her legs or other joints/muscles. She has not had any previous back surgeries, nor does she have any history of cancer, inflammatory disease, or pregnancy. She is generally healthy and takes no medications. She works a desk job and has not engaged in regular physical activity for the past few years due to her back pain. She is interested in participating in the study to find ways to alleviate her pain and improve her quality of life.

A 58-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He underwent coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery during his current hospitalization. His ejection fraction (EF) was measured at 30% following the surgery. The patient was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy as well. Given his high risk for sudden cardiac death (SCD), his healthcare provider prescribed him a wearable defibrillator (WD) to wear following discharge. The patient is willing to wear the WD and agrees to be contacted at 90 days. He is able to properly interact with the device and has no physical conditions preventing electrode contact. He does not have an active ICD or unipolar pacemaker. The patient understands the potential benefits and risks of the device and consents to participate in the LifeVest Post-CABG Registry study.

A 23-year-old female diagnosed with Anorexia Nervosa and admitted to the hospital due to severe malnutrition. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 15.5 kg/m2 and is experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue. She has a history of restricting food intake, excessive exercise and is obsessed with body weight and shape. She is currently undergoing treatment for her eating disorder and has been cleared by her medical team to participate in the physiotherapy program aimed at increasing muscle strength and quality of life. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with the sudden onset of severe headache, nausea, and vomiting. The patient has a history of hypertension and smoking. The CT scan showed a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) secondary to ruptured aneurysm in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory. The patient underwent endovascular coiling of the aneurysm and was started on oral nimodipine for vasospasm prophylaxis. Despite maximal medical management, the patient developed symptomatic vasospasm with a decrease in level of consciousness and focal neurological deficits. A CT angiogram confirmed severe vasospasm in the left MCA territory, with >50% narrowing of the vessel diameter. The patient meets all inclusion criteria for the Vesalio NeVa VS for Symptomatic Cerebral Vasospasm Following aSAH (The VITAL Study) and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her right shoulder for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain started gradually and has progressively worsened, and she attributes it to a fall she had while carrying groceries. The patient states that the pain is most severe when she lifts her arm above her head or when she tries to reach for something behind her back. She has difficulty sleeping at night due to the pain and reports taking over-the-counter pain medications for relief. MRI and ultrasound scans have confirmed a partial thickness rotator cuff tear. The patient has not received any recent pharmacotherapy with NSAIDs during the last month, and she has not undergone any shoulder surgeries. Her orthopedist has recommended physiotherapy, and she is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has no history of open wounds, skin diseases, neoplastic diseases, or collagen diseases. She also does not have a pacemaker or any serious cardiovascular conditions.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of heartburn and regurgitation of food for the past 6 months. She also experiences chest pain and coughing. She has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) for the past 3 years. Despite taking PPIs, her symptoms have persisted. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes medication. She has no history of abdominal surgeries. She is currently not pregnant or nursing and uses medically acceptable methods of contraception. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months. She understands the nature of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is scheduled to undergo a routine colonoscopy. She is in good health with no history of chronic medical conditions. She has no known allergies to propofol or fentanyl. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25. She is able to read, speak, and understand English. She has never participated in any other investigational device or drug study within 30 days of enrollment. She has no history of sleep apnea, gastroparesis, or any other physical or psychological conditions that would impair her trial participation.

A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with septic shock due to a urinary tract infection. Despite receiving antibiotics and vasopressors, his condition worsened and he was transferred to the medical ICU. He is conscious but confused and requires mechanical ventilation. His blood pressure is unstable and he has developed disseminated intravascular coagulation. He meets the inclusion criteria for this study and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 9-year-old child diagnosed with chronic liver disease. The child has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and nausea for the past few months. Blood tests indicate elevated liver enzymes, and an ultrasound revealed signs of liver damage. The child's medical history includes no significant illnesses or surgeries. The child is currently taking medication to manage the symptoms of chronic liver disease. The child's parents are concerned about the child's health and would like to explore non-invasive diagnostic options to monitor the progression of the disease and prevent life-threatening complications. They are interested in participating in clinical trials that explore new techniques for diagnosing portal hypertension in children.

A 45-year-old male patient is admitted to the hospital with a medical history of chronic liver disease for the past 10 years. The patient has been experiencing recent symptoms of jaundice, abdominal pain, and fatigue. The patient has not undergone any liver transplantation or any other surgical procedure in the past. Upon admission, the patient is diagnosed with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) with acute kidney injury (AKI). The patient's AKI has progressed to stage 2 with no response to volume repletion and diuretic withdrawal for 12 hours. The patient has no history of coronary artery disease, ischemic cardiomyopathy, peripheral vascular disease, or ventricular arrhythmia. The patient is not on renal replacement therapy (RRT) and has no history of known chronic kidney disease (CKD) or obstructive uropathy. The patient has not experienced any intolerance or side effects to terlipressin or albumin in the past. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

57-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the clinic with a complaint of frequent urination and lower extremity edema. His blood pressure was 136/84 mmHg and laboratory workup revealed an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 60 ml/min/1.73m² and urine albumin/creatinine ratio of 30 mg/g. The patient was diagnosed with early chronic kidney disease and was advised to avoid foods with phosphorus additives. After a few weeks, the patient was enrolled in the SODA-POP study to investigate the effect of higher vs. lower phosphorus intake on albuminuria and fibroblast growth factor 23. The patient has not been using phosphorus binders, phosphorus supplements, or high-dose vitamin D.

A 25-year-old healthy male presents to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new asthma medication. He reports no history of asthma, allergies, or any other respiratory conditions. He has a BMI of 22, and his medical history and physical examination are unremarkable. He denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not taken any medications or herb medicine in the past 4 weeks. He is a non-smoker and has not had any vaccinations in the past 3 months. He has not donated blood in the past 3 months and reports negative results for Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and HIV antibody tests. He has been informed of the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the requirements. The patient will receive training to ensure the correct use of the investigational products before participation in the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old male who is a non-smoker and has a stable weight for the past 2 months. He has a BMI of 23 kg/m^2 and does not consume caloric or artificially sweetened beverages in excess of 1L/week. He also does not consume alcohol in excess of 7 drinks/week. The patient has not undergone any antibiotic treatment in the past two months and has not had any chronic or acute illnesses. He has not undergone any previous abdominal surgery. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of drinking-water pH on the gut microbiota.

A 62-year-old retired teacher has been diagnosed with advanced colorectal cancer that cannot be completely removed by surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She lives with her husband and has two grown-up children. The patient complains of abdominal pain, constipation, and occasional rectal bleeding. She has lost 10 pounds over the past three months and feels fatigued most of the time. She has no history of blood clots or bleeding disorders. Her current medications include amlodipine and atorvastatin. A recent CT scan showed multiple metastases to the liver and lungs. Her SWOG performance status is 1. Her laboratory tests showed normal liver and kidney function. She is negative for pregnancy and uses adequate contraception. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment. She agrees to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has undergone chemotherapy but has not achieved complete remission. He is considered to be at high risk for regimen-related toxicity associated with a high-dose transplant, and also has a HCT-comorbidity index (CI) score of 1. He is willing to undergo donor peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) transplant with a related or unrelated donor. The patient has no history of HIV infection, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use contraception during and up to 12 months following treatment. He has a Karnofsky score of 70 and his pulmonary function tests show a corrected diffusion capacity of carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 65%, total lung capacity (TLC) of 60%, and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 55%. The patient has no history of liver disease or poorly controlled hypertension. He is currently taking imatinib for his AML. The patient's donor is a mismatched unrelated volunteer donor who is heterozygous at the mismatched HLA class I locus and allele matched for HLA-DRB1 and HLA-DQ.

A 50-year-old Caucasian male presents with progressive dyspnea that started 6 months ago. The patient has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for 20 years but quit 2 years ago. He reports a dry cough that started a month ago. He has no history of exposure to environmental toxins or occupational hazards. His medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension that is controlled with medication. He has no family history of pulmonary fibrosis or any other pulmonary disease. Physical examination reveals bilateral basal crackles. Pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with decreased forced vital capacity (FVC) and decreased diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO). High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest shows honeycombing with basal and peripheral predominance. The patient is diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). He is eligible for the study and will undergo bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) to determine the presence of pepsin in the recovered fluid.

A 48-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of fatigue, shortness of breath, and a lump in her left breast. She has a history of breast cancer and has received both an anthracycline and a taxane as part of her previous chemotherapy regimen. She has been diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer and has not received treatment for it yet. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she takes medication. She has no history of brain or leptomeningeal metastases and has no Grade 2 or worse neuropathy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and learn more about her condition.

A 56-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer, previously treated with bilateral orchiectomy, is now experiencing progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. He has a history of a right hip replacement and osteoarthritis, for which he takes ibuprofen as needed. His ECOG performance status is 1. Biopsy of the metastatic site confirms neuroendocrine-like prostate cancer, with no evidence of small cell histology. He has no significant family history of cancer, no known allergies, and no other significant medical history. He is currently taking no other medications apart from ibuprofen.

The patient is a premature infant born at 29 weeks gestational age. The baby was delivered via emergency C-section due to preeclampsia in the mother. The baby weighed 2.2 pounds at birth and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The baby was diagnosed with patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) on the second day of life and it was decided to treat it with Ibuprofen. The baby has not received any other treatments that could affect renal function. The baby has not had any complications since birth and is currently stable. The parents have given their consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate renal function maturation in very premature infants and to determine whether Ibuprofen treatment for PDA would alter renal function maturation at short term and up to 28 days of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent heartburn, regurgitation, and chest pain for the past six months. She has been taking over-the-counter antacids but has not had any significant relief. She recently visited her gastroenterologist who recommended a 24-hour pH monitoring or impedance measurement to diagnose gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). She has no history of dental problems and regularly visits her dentist for routine check-ups. She does not smoke and has not consumed alcohol in the past year. She is not currently taking any medications, including proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), and is willing to discontinue their use for at least one week before study participation. She is able to provide written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who recently experienced an episode of sudden vision loss in his left eye. He was diagnosed with optic neuritis after undergoing an ophthalmologic examination and a brain MRI that did not meet the MS criteria. The episode lasted for less than a month, and the patient has no history of optic neuritis in the past. He does not have any ophthalmologic comorbidity in the ipsilateral eye and is not pregnant or lactating. He has no contraindications to MRI.

This is a 30-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and underwent a modified radical mastectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. She is currently on her third cycle of chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide. She presents with a fever of 38.5°C and an absolute neutrophil count of 300/mm3, consistent with low-risk febrile neutropenia. She has no history of hypersensitivity reactions to antibiotics and has not received antibiotics within 24 hours prior to enrollment. She has no clinical signs of focal infection or sepsis and her organ function is normal. She has a MASCC score of 25, indicating low risk for complications. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using effective contraception.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with no known medical conditions. The patient has no history of seizures, facial nerve palsy, migraine or recurrent headaches, glaucoma or neuropathies. The patient has not undergone any carotid surgery, and has not experienced any episodes of syncope. The patient has no known arteriosclerosis and has not been diagnosed with any intracranial abnormalities observed by MRI or MRA. The patient also does not have any metal implants such as cochlear implants, pacemakers, or metal prostheses. The patient has normal audiometry chart and neurological examination at the time of inclusion. The patient is not currently breastfeeding or pregnant, and has not had any acute or chronic medical conditions. The patient's intraocular pressure is within normal limits. The patient is within the age range of 20 to 40 years.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing balance and gait disorders for the past year. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has never smoked or used any other substances. She has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. She is able to walk short distances with the use of a cane, but has difficulty with stairs and uneven surfaces. She is interested in participating in a rehabilitation program that could improve her mobility and reduce her risk of falls.

A 32 year old woman is seeking treatment for her multiple sclerosis diagnosis. She has been experiencing relapses, with two relapses over the past two years. She is still ambulatory with an EDSS score of 4.0. She has not had a relapse in the past 60 days and has been clinically stable without the use of ACTH or systemic steroid treatment for the past 30 days. She has no other significant medical conditions and is not pregnant or nursing. She has not used cladribine, mitoxantrone, or other immunosuppressant agents such as azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, methotrexate, or mycophenolate before enrolling in the study. She is willing to participate in a 128-week study to evaluate the effect of teriflunomide on the frequency of relapses and accumulation of disability in patients with multiple sclerosis.

A 29-year-old woman presents with a history of opioid use disorder for the past 3 years. She has previously tried to quit on her own but was unsuccessful. She is currently seeking treatment for her opioid addiction and meets the DSM-5 criteria for moderate opioid use disorder. She has no other chronic medical conditions requiring opioid treatment and is a suitable candidate for opioid partial-agonist treatment. Her BMI is 25, within the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial. She has not received medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder in the past 90 days and has not used opioids, barbiturates, benzodiazepines, methadone, or buprenorphine in the past 30 days. She is not undergoing court-mandated treatment for opioid use disorder and has no history of recent suicidal ideation or attempts. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help manage her opioid addiction and is willing to regularly visit the clinic for laboratory tests and assessments.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been discharged from the hospital after experiencing a myocardial infarction (heart attack) 6 weeks ago. He is currently attending cardiac rehabilitation classes and is concerned about the possibility of experiencing another heart attack. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse, but has quit both since his heart attack. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works at a desk job. He has no known allergies or medical conditions other than his recent heart attack. He is willing and able to give written informed consent for the study. He has no thoracic metal implants or pacemaker/defibrillator. He speaks fluent English and is able to understand the informed consent process. He is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who is generally healthy but has a history of hypertension and occasional migraines. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol in moderation. He has not received any vaccinations in the past month and is not scheduled to receive any other vaccines during the study period. He is not currently on any immunomodulator therapy or systemic antibiotics. He has never had invasive meningococcal disease or received meningococcal vaccination. He is able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures. He has signed the informed consent form approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB). He is not pregnant or nursing. He does not have a bleeding disorder or any other chronic disease that would interfere with his ability to participate fully in the study or interfere with the evaluation of the vaccines. He is not currently on a tapering dose schedule of oral steroids. He is not allergic to latex or any of the components of either Menactra® vaccine or Menomune® vaccine. He has not had Guillain-Barré syndrome in the past. He is not deprived of freedom by an administrative or court order, or in an emergency setting, or hospitalized without his consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive with her partner for the past 2 years. She has been diagnosed with subfertility due to unexplained causes. The couple has opted for In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF) and Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) cycles as a treatment option. The patient has no history of previous surgeries or medical conditions that may affect her fertility. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has not used any hormonal medications in the past 6 months. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has been informed of the study and has agreed to participate. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to follow the protocol for the IVF/ICSI cycle and the intrauterine injection of hCG before Embryo Transfer (ET).

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been suffering from migraines for the past 6 months. She is overweight with a BMI of 30 and is interested in participating in a study that can help her manage her migraines. She is a mother of two children and works as a receptionist. She is married and lives a sedentary lifestyle due to her job demands. She reports experiencing 4-5 migraine headaches per month, with each episode lasting for 2-3 days. She has tried several medications and lifestyle changes, but the relief is temporary. She does not have a history of substance abuse or diabetes. Her blood pressure is within normal limits with a reading of 120/80 mmHg. She is interested in making dietary changes and is willing to follow a low carbohydrate or low-fat diet for the duration of the study. She is motivated to improve her overall health and reduce the frequency of her migraines.

A 25-year-old first-time expectant mother who is currently in active labor is eligible for this clinical trial. She must have a singleton pregnancy and be between 37-42 weeks gestation. She must have an arrested labor progress with a need for oxytocin to stimulate further progress. The patient should not have any maternal or fetal chronic or pregnancy-related conditions. The patient should not have any previous birthing experience beyond this being her first delivery. The patient should not have any non-cephalic presentation, multiples, fetal chronic or pregnancy-related conditions, IUFD, or premature delivery before 37 weeks gestation. The patient should be willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial and be open to receiving either bicarbonate or no bicarbonate treatment during the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male scheduled for a thoracotomy surgery due to lung cancer. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He has never had any previous surgeries and has no known allergies to medications. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. His BMI is within the range of 18-25 kg/m2. He has been experiencing mild to moderate pain in the chest area for the past few weeks. His doctor has prescribed him with painkillers, but they have not provided sufficient relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the effectiveness of dexmedetomidine as an adjunctive analgesic, used in ultrasound-guided continuous thoracic paravertebral blocks for post-thoracotomy pain syndrome (PTPS). He is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the study.

A 60-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer after a routine check-up. He has no history of prostate cancer in his family. The biopsy revealed that he has a low-risk cancer with a Gleason score of 6. His PSA level is 8 ng/ml, and the MRI shows only one target tumor on a maximum of 2 contiguous sextants. The tumor is positioned so that a safety distance of at least 9 mm from the external sphincter can be defined during HIFU-FOCAL treatment in prostate tissue around the target. The patient is in overall good health, with no other significant medical history. He has spoken with his doctor about the pros and cons of active surveillance versus focal HIFU therapy and has decided to participate in this clinical trial. He is willing to be randomized to either the active surveillance group or the HIFU treatment group. He understands that the trial involves regular follow-up appointments and assessments, including imaging and blood tests, and he is committed to complying with the study requirements. He has health insurance and is a suitable candidate for the trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who underwent surgical repair for a congenital heart defect involving the atrioventricular canal. The procedure was performed using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). She is currently admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) for postoperative care. The patient has no history of kidney disease and her preoperative creatinine lab value is available. She has been closely monitored for any signs of acute kidney injury (AKI) and will continue to be monitored throughout her stay in the PICU. Her parents have provided informed consent for her participation in this retrospective study.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been diagnosed with severe hemophilia A. He has been treated with ADVATE for the past 8 years and has had no issues with his current treatment plan. He is currently employed as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He lives with his partner in a one-bedroom apartment. He does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. He reports having an average of 2-3 bleeding episodes per year, which typically require factor infusions. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the requirements of the protocol. He is proficient in English and is able to use the SPACE eDiary. He is seeking to better understand the relationship between his activity level and bleeding episodes in order to better manage his condition.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who attends a public school in Barueri-SP, Brazil. He has no significant medical history and is in good health. His parents have noticed some cavities in his teeth and have expressed concern about his dental health. The boy has a sweet tooth and enjoys eating candies and sugary snacks. A dental exam revealed that he has at least one cavity in a primary molar tooth that involves the dentin. The parents have consented to him participating in a clinical trial comparing two different restorative techniques. The boy is cooperative and does not have any severe behavioral issues. There is no evidence of a fistula or abscess near the selected tooth, and there is no pulp exposure or mobility in the tooth.

A 45-year-old woman has been battling B-cell lymphoma for the past 3 years. She has received several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but the disease has progressed despite treatment. She has now been diagnosed with recurrent or refractory B-cell malignancy and is seeking alternative treatment options. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and Karnofsky 80%. She has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. Her WBC, granulocyte count, and platelet count are within normal limits. She has no significant medical complications and is HIV negative. She is not pregnant, and her pregnancy test is negative. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves radiolabeled monoclonal antibody, combination chemotherapy, and peripheral stem cell transplantation as a potential treatment option. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to comply with all study-related procedures.

A 62-year-old male diagnosed with stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue. Following surgery, the patient will undergo radiation therapy for curative intent. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker and is in overall good health. The initial lesion was 3 cm in diameter, and the biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. The patient is eligible for the trial and has provided informed consent.

A 50 yo F with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency room with sudden onset right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The symptoms started 4 hours ago. The patient is currently alert and oriented, but has a NIHSS score of 12. CT scan of the brain shows no evidence of hemorrhage. The patient is unable to provide consent due to the severity of the symptoms and is accompanied by a family member who consents to the research.

A 10-year-old Hispanic boy with a history of asthma presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing, especially at night. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past six months, and his condition has been worsening over time. He has been on a long-term controller medication for asthma for the past year but still experiences frequent symptoms. He has had one asthma-related overnight hospitalization in the last six months. He lives in an urban area of Baltimore and is exposed to multiple environmental allergens such as dust mites, cockroaches, and furry pets. He has a positive skin test to dust mites, cockroaches, and cats. He does not have any other significant medical history, and his family history is negative for asthma. His medications include a long-term controller medication, a rescue inhaler, and nasal steroids. He lives with his parents and two siblings in a rented apartment, and they have a dog and a cat. His insurance covers prescription medications.

A 32-year-old female patient presents with a history of joint pain, fatigue, and dry mouth. She reports that her symptoms have been present for the past 6 months and have been gradually worsening. She denies any fever, rash, or cough. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. On examination, the patient appears fatigued, and there is tenderness on palpation of multiple joints. The patient also reports dry eyes and mouth. Laboratory analysis reveals a positive ANA and anti-SSA/Ro antibodies, and a decrease in the CD4+ T-cell count. The patient is referred to the study for further evaluation of her lymphocyte subpopulations.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has a mild to moderate infected diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) for the past 3 weeks on his left foot, which is painful and has caused difficulty in walking. The wound area measures around 4 cm2. He has been receiving oral Ciprofloxacin for the past week with no improvement in the wound. He is looking for alternative treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. The patient has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and has a BMI of 32. His HbA1c level is 8%. He has no known allergies to medications. He is able to read and speak English and is willing to comply with

62-year-old male with chronic stroke (>6 months post-stroke) and able to stand independently without upper-limb support for >30 seconds. The patient has some difficulty with balance control, especially when standing on one leg or walking on uneven surfaces. The patient reports feeling fatigued easily and has not been able to exercise as much as they would like due to lack of time and motivation. The patient has no other neurological conditions that could affect balance control (e.g., Parkinson's disease) or lower extremity amputation. The patient is able to follow instructions and has no significant cognitive, language or communication impairments. The patient has not had any recent (last 6 months) significant illness, injury or surgery, and does not have severe osteoporosis, uncontrolled hypertension, or uncontrolled diabetes. The patient is not currently attending in- or out-patient physiotherapy that includes aerobic training, balance training or strength training for lower limbs. The patient's current physical activity levels do not meet the recommended guidelines (at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous or at least 75 minutes of vigorous physical activity/week).

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic HCV infection based on a history of positive serum anti-HCV antibody and/or HCV RNA. He was diagnosed with HCV Genotype 4 during the screening visit. He had undergone initial treatment using peginterferon-alfa and Ribavirin therapy with a starting dose of 1.5 μg/kg/week PEG-Intron and 1000 mg/day ribavirin. He reports that he was at least 80% compliant during the initial peginterferon/ribavirin therapy. He had undergone a liver biopsy within the past 3 years which indicated a fibrosis score of F2. He experienced a partial response after 12 weeks of treatment as a therapy-naive patient with one course of peginterferon alfa-2a (PEGASYS) and Ribavirin. He denies having any severe neuropsychiatric disorder, significant metabolic, hematological, pulmonary, ischemic heart disease, gastrointestinal, neurological, renal, urological, endocrine, ophthalmologic disorders including severe retinopathy, or immune-mediated disease. He is not known to be HIV positive. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have any underlying autoimmune disease.

The patient is a 64-year-old female diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She underwent a surgical resection, followed by chemotherapy. The patient has a 40-pack-year smoking history and is currently a non-smoker. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes amlodipine as well as a daily multivitamin. The patient is currently in good health and has no complaints of shortness of breath or cough. She has been recommended by her medical team to undergo thoracic radiation therapy as part of her treatment plan. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is capable of giving written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with myelofibrosis with myeloid metaplasia. She is experiencing anemia with a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, palpable splenomegaly, and leukoerythroblastosis. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. Her performance status is ECOG 1, and her absolute neutrophil count is 1,200/mm^3, platelet count is 300,000/mm^3, and WBC count is 25,000/mm^3. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for at least 4 weeks after the study. She has not received interferon, pirfenidone, anagrelide, epoetin alfa, hydroxyurea, or other chemotherapy in the past month. She has no peripheral neuropathy and no concurrent condition that would preclude study participation.

The patient is a 62 year old male who was diagnosed with heart failure 2 years ago. He presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no previous cardiac surgeries. On echocardiogram, he has an ejection fraction of 30%. He has been on guideline-directed medical therapy, including a beta blocker and an ACE inhibitor, but continues to have symptoms. His cardiologist has recommended cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) with a CRT device and left ventricular lead placement. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the safety and effectiveness of epicardial versus transvenous left ventricular lead placement.

35-year-old male diagnosed with partial seizures. He has been experiencing at least three seizures per month for the past two years, despite being treated with multiple anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs). His latest AED regimen includes carbamazepine, clonazepam, and levetiracetam. He does not have a history of generalized seizures or status epilepticus within the last year. The patient has been stable on his current dose of anti-depressants for the past 8 weeks. The patient has no history of psychotic disorders or suicidal attempts. The patient has no significant active hematological disease and his liver function tests are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the maximum tolerated dose of E2007 as an add-on to his current AED regimen.

Pt is a 45yo M smoker with a history of poor oral health, including gum disease and occasional bleeding. He has been trying to quit smoking for several years but has had difficulty quitting completely. He has a BMI within the range of 20-35 kg/m2 and is not currently taking any medications that inhibit clotting or using prescribed oral rinses. He has no known allergies to strawberries, corn, or wheat products and has consumed these products in the past. He is willing to abstain from purple and red colored foods and beverages and to avoid the use of any mouth washes during the 6 week study period. He is willing to consume a standardized vitamin and mineral supplement and to avoid other nutritional, dietary, or alternative medications/supplements for the duration of the study. He is not currently receiving or in need of dental treatment during the study period and has no noticeable open lesions or sores that have not healed for more than 3 months or any active oral lesions or maladies within the last month. He is able to swallow without difficulty or pain and does not have salivary gland dysfunction or xerostomia. He is willing to submit to a 24 hour urine cotinine test to determine his smoking status and meet the criteria for habitual smoking at least 10 cigarettes/day with a urine cotinine level of >1000 ng/mL. He does not have any active metabolic or digestive illnesses or any history of pituitary hormone diseases that currently require supplemental hormonal administration or other endocrine disorders requiring hormone administration. He has not had significant loss of gastrointestinal organs due to surgery and does not have altered immunity such as chronic inflammatory disease, autoimmune disorders, cancer, anemia, hemophilia, and blood dyscrasias. He has not consumed more than 15 glasses of alcohol weekly. He has not used antibiotics in the last 6 months or on medications that will accelerate or decrease bowel motility.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was previously diagnosed with urothelial carcinoma and has undergone chemotherapy with platinum-based agents. However, the cancer has progressed, and the patient is now experiencing symptoms such as pain during urination, frequent urination, and blood in the urine. The patient is diagnosed with metastatic or locally advanced unresectable disease and is seeking a second-line therapy. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST criteria and has not received prior taxane therapy for metastatic disease. The patient's peripheral neuropathy is less than or equal to grade 1 by NCI-CTC criteria, and the calculated creatinine clearance is above 40 ml/min (Cockcroft & Gault formula). The patient is willing to give informed consent and employ adequate contraception for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently admitted to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medication for these conditions. The patient has experienced chest pain before, but this time it is more severe and persistent. The patient is initially treated with aspirin and given a loading dose of an approved P2Y12 receptor blocker. His electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in two contiguous leads, indicating a diagnosis of ST segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (STE-ACS). He is eligible for enrollment in the European Ambulance Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) Angiography Trial since he meets all the inclusion criteria. However, he is excluded from the trial due to his estimated body weight being over 120 kg. The patient is offered standard anti-thrombotic therapy other than bivalirudin, which includes treatment with unfractionated heparin and optional glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor. The patient is alert and cooperative, and he agrees to participate in the trial after receiving detailed information about the study.

A 50-year-old male with a history of multiple myeloma presents with relapsed/refractory disease as defined by the IMWG criteria. He has received prior therapies, including chemotherapy and stem cell transplant, but has experienced disease progression. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and good bone marrow function. He is willing to undergo leukapheresis for the study and has adequate organ function. The patient has not received any experimental therapy in the past 14 days and is willing to use adequate contraception. He does not have any uncontrolled medical or psychiatric disorders that would preclude participation in the study. However, he does have a history of pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis, but these conditions are currently under control with medication. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore potential new treatment options for his relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 7 months pregnant. She has a history of gingivitis and is seeking treatment for her inflamed gums. She has noticed bleeding and tenderness when brushing and flossing her teeth. She is not currently taking any medication and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has not used any anti-inflammatory or antimicrobial medication in the past 6 months. She is not currently breastfeeding and has not had her menstrual period for several months due to her pregnancy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the relationship between stress and gingival inflammation in pregnant women. She is willing to undergo non-surgical periodontal therapy and provide samples of gingival crevicular fluid and saliva for analysis. She is aware that the study will involve measurements of probing pocket depth, clinical attachment level, gingival index, and plaque index using a periodontal probe. She understands that the study will require her to return for follow-up appointments after three weeks to repeat the clinical measurements and sample collection. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and provide informed consent for participation.

This is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer approximately one year ago. She has been treated with aromatase inhibitors but has not responded well to this therapy. She has also not received any prior chemotherapy, except in the adjuvant setting. She is still able to perform her activities of daily living and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no history of congestive heart failure or ventricular arrhythmia requiring therapy. Her platelet count is at least 100,000/mm^3 and her creatinine is no greater than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal. She has no active infection or other concurrent medical condition that would preclude her from participating in the trial. She is willing and able to swallow oral medication. She has not received any prior epidermal growth factor receptor or HER2 blockers and is not currently receiving concurrent hormonal therapy for breast cancer. She is not taking any medications that are known to interact with the study drugs. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore other treatment options and potentially improve her disease outcome.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma that has relapsed after receiving one prior line of therapy. He is currently suitable for treatment with lenalidomide and dexamethasone. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. He has acceptable neutrophil and platelet counts and adequate kidney and liver function. He has not experienced peripheral neuropathy greater than CTCAE grade 1 and does not have any significant GI function impairment or GI disease. He has not undergone major surgery within the last 4 weeks and has recovered from any side effects of prior therapies. He is willing and able to sign informed consent and comply with the protocol.

A 26 year old female arrives at the clinic with severe itching due to contact dermatitis caused by a new detergent that she used to wash her clothes. She has been experiencing itching and redness on her arms and legs for the past two days, and the condition is getting worse. She has tried using over-the-counter anti-itch creams but they have not provided any relief. She has a history of eczema and has used various topical steroids and antihistamines in the past for the same. She has not taken any other medications in the past month. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new topical spray that promises to provide quick relief from itching.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with COVID-19 and is hospitalized due to pneumonia. He is experiencing shortness of breath and his oxygen saturation level is below 93% while at rest in ambient air. He has no known allergies to medications. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed written consent. He is able to take medication by oral route. He is not currently receiving invasive mechanical ventilation, but he may need oxygen therapy or non-invasive mechanical ventilation. He does not have a history of tuberculosis, hepatitis B or C, deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. His creatinine clearance is above 30 ml/min, and his ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. His neutrophil count is above 1000/mmc, his platelet count is above 50,000/mmc, and his hemoglobin level is above 8g/dl. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have bowel diverticulitis or perforation. He is not currently receiving immunosuppressants or anti-rejection drugs.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metastatic colorectal carcinoma. He has undergone multiple chemotherapy treatments in the past, but his cancer has progressed despite the treatments. He experiences symptoms such as fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2, meaning he is able to carry out his normal activities, but with some difficulty due to his symptoms.
