He has measurable metastases and a recent radiological evaluation confirmed the progression of his disease. He has no other active cancer, but he has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. His complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the study to explore new treatment options for his cancer. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent. He is willing to adhere to monthly visits to the oncology unit for evaluation.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was referred to the clinic by his neurologist for further evaluation of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. He reported symptoms of weakness in his legs and feet, as well as difficulty with balance and coordination. He has a family history of the condition, as his father was also diagnosed with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. His genetic testing has confirmed the diagnosis. He is currently using orthotics to help with his mobility and is interested in participating in the study to help further the understanding and management of the disease. He is otherwise healthy and has no other peripheral neuropathy caused by trauma, immunity, or toxicosis.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a BMI of 32. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has struggled with weight gain for the past 5 years. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. She does not smoke and has no history of alcohol abuse. Her blood pressure is within normal limits. She has no known allergies to any food and is not on any medication except for birth control pills. She does not follow any special diets but has a preference for vegetarian food. She has no history of pregnancy or lactation and has no plans for pregnancy in the next 18 months. She has not experienced any significant weight fluctuations in the past 2 months.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who suffered a stroke 6 months ago. He is ambulatory with the help of an ankle-foot orthosis and can walk 10 meters with or without supervision. He has a Functional Ambulation Category score of 4. He has no previous history of stroke or other neurological disorders. He has no complications from other health conditions, such as cardiovascular or musculoskeletal conditions. He has no contracture or muscle tonus ≥ 3 according to the Modified Ashworth Scale. He has no severe osteoporosis. He has no cognitive deficits preventing him from

A 15 year old girl who has been experiencing irregular sleep patterns and changes in social routines for the past year. Her mother has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and she is concerned about her own risk of developing the illness. She has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any medications. She is fluent in English and has at least a 3rd grade literacy level. She lives with her mother and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old Caucasian female presents to the clinic with a history of asthma for the past 10 years, which has been difficult to control despite maximal medical therapy. She has a history of frequent exacerbations requiring systemic corticosteroids, with the most recent one being two months ago. She is a non-smoker and has no significant past medical history other than asthma. Her current medications include inhaled corticosteroids, long-acting beta-agonists, and leukotriene receptor antagonists. Physical examination is remarkable for wheezing and decreased breath sounds. Pulmonary function tests reveal mildly obstructed airways with FEV1 of 65% predicted. She has no known allergies, and her serum liver function tests are within normal limits. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has acceptable contraceptive methods.

50-year-old female with a history of hypertension and recent admission to the ICU for respiratory distress secondary to pneumonia. The patient has been intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. A central venous catheter has been placed for medication administration and monitoring. The patient is alert and oriented but requires continuous monitoring and management of her respiratory status. She has no known allergies to chlorhexidine.

25-year-old male, non-smoker, with a body mass index of 24.5 and a physically active lifestyle, is being invited to participate in a clinical trial to study the effects of caffeine on hydration and energy metabolism. He does not consume more than 100 mg of caffeine per day and has no history of major diseases. He is interested in participating in the study and agrees to follow the study protocol for a period of 4 days. He understands that he will be randomly assigned to receive either a moderate dose of caffeine or placebo through capsules, and that he will undergo evaluations at baseline, end of condition 1, and end of condition 2. The evaluations will include measurements of total body water and its compartments, total energy expenditure, and physical activity energy expenditure. He will also be required to wear an accelerometer during the study to measure the intensity of his physical activities. He confirms that he is not taking any medication or dietary supplements that may interfere with hydration status, body composition, or energy expenditure regulation.

The patient is a newborn infant with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) who is being treated with surfactant therapy. The infant was born prematurely at 32 weeks gestation and has been intubated since birth. The infant's mother had a history of pre-eclampsia during pregnancy. The infant's birth weight was 1.8 kg and the Apgar scores were 7 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The infant's oxygen saturation levels have been fluctuating between 85-90% despite oxygen therapy. The infant has not been diagnosed with any congenital malformation, inherited metabolic abnormality, intrauterine infection, Rh/Rh incompatibility, pneumonia, pulmonary hypertension, meconium aspiration syndrome, or asphyxia. The infant's medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 58-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma after experiencing symptoms such as weight loss, night sweats, and fatigue. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of low-grade lymphoma. She has no prior treatment for this condition and is otherwise healthy. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and her blood tests show a normal ANC and platelet count. Her creatinine, bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. She has no known hypersensitivity to thalidomide and has not developed erythema nodosum while taking thalidomide or similar drugs. She has no active infections or other serious medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is registered in the RevAssist® program and is willing to comply with its requirements.

A 42-year-old female with a BMI of 39.5 kg/m2 who has struggled with obesity for most of her adult life. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She has tried multiple diets and exercise programs but has been unable to achieve substantial weight loss. She is interested in bariatric surgery and has been referred to the study by her doctor. She has not taken antibiotics in the past 2 months and does not regularly take proton pump inhibitors. She has never had surgery on her gastrointestinal tract. She is motivated to participate in the study to better understand the role of gut microbiota in obesity and metabolic syndrome.

A 2-year-old boy living in Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has African nationality and has resided in Burkina Faso since birth. His parents have given informed consent for his participation. The child is in good health with no chronic or acute severe illness requiring specialized medical care. He has no known allergies to any components of the vaccine and has not received a pneumococcal vaccine outside the context of the trial. His weight is greater than the 5th percentile of Burkinabe children, and the blood draw at the first vaccination visit was successful. The child will receive a single dose of PCV13 and have IgG and OPA assessments pre-vaccination and 1 month post-vaccination.

The patient is a 25-year-old African American male smoker who has been smoking five cigarettes daily for the past year. He has no interest in quitting smoking in the next 6 months and is willing to use e-cigarettes. He is in good physical health with no unstable medical or mental health conditions and no contraindications for e-cigarette use. He has not used any tobacco or nicotine products other than regular cigarettes in the past 30 days and has not participated in a smoking cessation program in the past 30 days. He is not pregnant or nursing. The patient will be enrolled in a clinical trial to determine changes in biomarkers associated with the use of electronic cigarettes among African American menthol and non-menthol smokers. The trial will last for 24 weeks and will involve using e-cigarettes as per the study protocol. The patient will be required to attend follow-up visits at 8 weeks and 24 weeks post-enrollment to determine changes in biomarkers of smoking exposure.

72 F with no significant past medical history who has been referred to the clinical trial. She is interested in participating in the study to help contribute to the understanding of how elderly individuals recover from general anesthesia. The patient has no allergies or hypersensitivity to drugs, and she is able to read and understand English. She is not pregnant and is not currently nursing. She has not been diagnosed with any chronic inflammatory conditions or diabetes mellitus. She has no visual or auditory disorders, and her BMI is within normal limits. She does not have any metal implants in her body nor is she a current smoker. She is excited to participate in the study and is eager to share her experience with the research team.

Maria is a 52 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is married and has two teenage children. She works as a teacher at a local high school. She has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she has been treated in the past. She is currently not taking any medication for her mental health. She has a support system of family and friends who are helping her through this difficult time. Maria will be receiving radiotherapy treatment for her cancer and is interested in participating in any research that may help her and other cancer patients. She can read and speak Dutch fluently and is willing to complete questionnaires.

The patient is a 26-year-old male volleyball player who has been experiencing pain in his patellar tendon for the past 6 months. He has a history of patellar tendinopathy and has not undergone any lower extremity surgery or suffered any fractures. He has been playing volleyball for the past 10 years and trains for at least 2 hours every day. He describes his pain as a dull ache that worsens during jumping and landing movements. He has been managing his pain with rest, ice, and over-the-counter pain medications. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help better understand the biomechanics of landing and fatigue in athletes with a history of patellar tendinopathy.

A 13-year-old Latina girl and her mother are interested in participating in the study. The girl attends a local middle school and is involved in various extracurricular activities. She has a group of close friends, some of whom have experimented with alcohol and drugs. The mother is concerned about the peer pressure her daughter may face and wants to ensure that she has the skills and knowledge to make informed decisions. The family speaks primarily Spanish at home, but the daughter is bilingual and proficient in English. They are excited to participate in the study and learn more about how to prevent substance use in their community.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently taking medication for both conditions. He is a smoker and has been smoking for the past 20 years. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. He has no history of heart attacks or other cardiovascular events. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits associated with it. He has no other significant medical conditions and is mentally capable of giving informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman has been smoking for 10 years and has tried to quit smoking multiple times without success. She smokes an average of 10 cigarettes per day and is motivated to quit smoking. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to any substances. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She has not used ENDS or any medications such as nicotine replacement therapy, varenicline or bupropion to aid in smoking cessation within the last 3 months. She has a valid phone number and email address and is willing to attend the clinical visits required for the study. She gives informed consent to participate in the ESTxENDS trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been experiencing pain in her legs while walking for the past year. She has been diagnosed with symptomatic claudication and has been experiencing rest pain as well. She has undergone angiography, which has confirmed the presence of de novo and/or restenotic lesions in her common and/or external iliac artery. The patient's target lesion is between 5 and 12mm in diameter and less than 110mm in length. She has a patent profunda or superficial femoral artery (SFA) in the target limb. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to adhere to the required follow-up visits and testing through month 36. Additionally, she is able and willing to adhere to the required follow-up medication regimen. The patient has no other non-target ipsilateral arterial lesions requiring treatment within 30 days post-procedure. She has no adjacent, acute thrombus and her target lesion is not highly calcified or previously treated with a stent. The target lesion does not involve the internal iliac artery and there is no presence of abdominal aortic aneurysm contiguous with the iliac artery target lesion. The patient has no pre-existing target iliac artery aneurysm or perforation or dissection of the target iliac artery prior to initiation of the iCAST implant procedure. She has no post-surgical stenosis and anastomotic suture treatments of the target vessel, no vascular graft previously implanted in the native iliac vessel, and no tissue loss (Rutherford-Becker classification category 5 or 6). The patient has no contrast agent hypersensitivity, no hypersensitivity to stainless steel, expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE), and no intolerance to antiplatelet, anticoagulant, or thrombolytic medications. The patient has no history of neutropenia (WBC <3,000/mm3), coagulopathy, or thrombocytopenia (platelet count <80,000/ μL) that has not resolved or has required treatment in the past 6 months. The patient has normal laboratory values including platelet count, prothrombin time (PT)/partial thromboplastin time (PTT), and serum creatinine level. The patient does not require general anesthesia for the procedure and is not pregnant. The patient has no co-morbid illness that may result in a life expectancy of less than 1 year and is not participating in an investigational study of a new drug, biologic or device at the time of study screening.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with HER2-positive invasive breast cancer following a mammogram and biopsy. She underwent breast-conserving surgery to remove the tumor and received anthracycline-based chemotherapy. The tumor was found to be node-positive with a size of 3.5 cm and was negative for estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor. Her left ventricular ejection fraction measured by echocardiogram was 60%. She has no history of other malignancies or breast cancer in the past. She has not received any prior systemic anti-cancer treatment, including chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, or hormonal therapy. She is not pregnant and is not lactating. She is willing to use highly effective non-hormonal contraception or two effective forms of non-hormonal contraception. She has not received any chronic immunosuppressive therapy. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed HER2-positive adenocarcinoma of the breast. Further imaging studies showed that the tumor is 3 cm in size and has spread to one lymph node in her axilla. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, or radiation therapy for cancer. She has normal liver and kidney function and has an echocardiogram with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) within normal limits. The patient is premenopausal and has a negative pregnancy test. Her peripheral neuropathy is grade 1. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male who has never been exposed to tuberculosis or received a BCG vaccination. He has no history of skin disorders, allergies, or any other medical conditions. He is not taking any medications and has no known history of drug or alcohol abuse. His physical examination is normal and his laboratory tests are within normal limits. He has agreed to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial.

This is a 22 year old male diagnosed with ADHD in childhood. He has a history of two driving collisions and has received citations for driving violations. He has a valid driver's license and has been driving for five years. He is not currently taking any medication for his ADHD. He has access to a car of which he is the primary driver. He has no current history of depression or anxiety. He does not have any medical conditions that might impair his driving or be contraindicated for the use of methylphenidate. He is not pregnant or intending to get pregnant for the duration of the study, and is not breastfeeding or intending to breastfeed for the duration of the study. He has no skin allergies or skin conditions that could be exacerbated by wearing the medication patch. He has no documented allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to methylphenidate or the Daytrana® adhesive backing. He has no history of seizures, liver or renal disease, glaucoma, chronic skin conditions or contact sensitivities, or current symptoms suggestive of cardiac disease. He has no current diagnosis of psychosis, bipolar disease, anxiety disorder, substance use disorder/substance abuse disorder. He is capable of driving the simulator without experiencing simulation sickness.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with lumbar spinal stenosis and has been treated with conservative measures such as physical therapy and pain management without significant relief. The patient has moderately impaired physical function as determined by a baseline score >2.0 in the physical function (PF) domain of the Zurich claudication questionnaire. He underwent X-STOP surgery and received the X-STOP implant(s) intact under the IDE. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and return to the clinic for clinical evaluations or complete study questionnaires without a clinic visit. He did not participate in the Pivotal Trial as part of the X STOP group, but he is an active CAP/COS participant who has not completed a 24-month follow-up visit in his CAP/COS study. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria and is eligible to participate in the LTOS program.

Patient is a 48-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 1 infection. He has already received at least one course of treatment without response. His viral load has been above 1 x 105 UI/mL for more than 6 months and has not been treated for at least the last two months. He has a METAVIR score lower than F4. He has no history of alcohol intake greater than 20 g/day or immuno-suppressive therapy. His BMI is 28 and he does not have diabetes or require specific therapy for dyslipidemia. He has no liver cirrhosis or carcinoma, no HIV or HBV co-infections, no other liver diseases, and no major organ failures. He is not receiving therapy with cytochrome P450 metabolized drugs.

32-year-old healthy non-smoking female with no significant medical history, looking to participate in a clinical trial to assess the potential cardiovascular benefits of reducing personal particulate air pollution exposure by wearing a facemask. She has no significant occupational exposure to air pollution and is not on any regular medications (except for oral contraceptive pill). She is interested in contributing to research that helps understand the effects of air pollution exposure on cardiovascular health and is willing to wear a facemask as part of the study.

A 55 year old woman with a biopsy-confirmed diagnosis of stage IIIB cervical cancer. She reports no significant past medical history and is currently experiencing some lower back pain that she attributes to her active lifestyle. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work and is able to walk for more than half of her waking hours. Laboratory results show that her ANC is 2,300/mcl and her platelet count is 150,000/mcl, indicating adequate bone marrow function. Her creatinine level is within normal limits at 1.2 mg/mL, indicating adequate renal function. She has not been diagnosed with any other malignancy tumors except papillary or follicular thyroid cancer or skin cancer. She does not have metastatic lymphadenopathies in her inguinal, paraaortic, supraclavicular, or mediastinal nodes, nor does she have distant organ metastasis. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 8-year-old boy who suffered a traumatic brain injury 6 months ago as a result of a car accident. He has been undergoing rehabilitation at Sheba Hospital's Pediatric Rehabilitation Department. He has difficulty with daily living activities such as dressing and eating, and has limited movement of his left arm. The patient's parents have agreed for him to participate in a clinical trial to test the usability of a Virtual Reality (VR) Video Capture Projected System in children with acquired brain injury. The trial will include experiencing 3 different virtual environments and performing 3 different tasks as a part of the trial group. The patient will also be evaluated using the PEDI, Melbourne Assessment, and TEA-ch tests to evaluate his functional abilities and attention abilities. The patient does not have any significant visual limitations or developmental disorders.

A healthy 30-year-old woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 who is a non-smoker and has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 30 days may be eligible for this study. She has never used insulin products for therapeutic purposes in the past and has not used any prescription drugs within the last three weeks, except for her oral contraceptive pill that she has been taking without difficulty for at least three months. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past five years and has no known allergies to trial products or related products. She is willing to provide informed consent and has no language barriers that may preclude adequate understanding or cooperation. She has no significant cardiovascular disease, anemia or hemoglobinopathy, and her liver enzymes and renal function are within normal range. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is using adequate contraceptive measures.
N/A - This clinical trial does not require a patient description as it is evaluating the accuracy of a medical device rather than testing a new treatment or intervention on human subjects.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced metastatic breast cancer. She has undergone one chemotherapy regimen in the past and her cancer has progressed since then. She has measurable disease, but no brain or leptomeningeal involvement. Her performance status is WHO 1, and her life expectancy is at least 3 months. Her hemoglobin level is 11.5 g/dL, neutrophil count is 2,200/mm3, and platelet count is 120,000/mm3. Her bilirubin level is 10.5 mg/dL, and AST/ALT levels are within normal limits. Her creatinine level is 1.4 mg/dL. She has no active uncontrolled infections or concurrent nonmalignant systemic diseases. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception. She has not had any prior malignant disease, except for curatively treated carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She has undergone radiotherapy at least 4 weeks prior to the study and has recovered. She has not undergone any concurrent experimental therapy.

As a 27-year-old male, you have been an Army Reserve soldier for the past three years. You have received orders to deploy to a hazardous area in the Middle East for the next 12 months. You have never been deployed before. You have no current medical conditions and no history of any chronic illnesses or injuries. You have a high school diploma and some college credits. You are single and have no children. You live with your parents and have no major financial obligations. You are physically fit and enjoy running and weight-lifting. You have no allergies to medications or food. You are a non-smoker and drink alcohol occasionally on social occasions. You have been informed about the study and are willing to participate.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in his neck. His tumor has not yet spread, and he is a candidate for radical radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. He is in good physical condition and has no history of respiratory illness. He has never undergone MRI scanning before. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He enjoys playing golf in his free time. He has no known allergies to any medication. He is willing to participate in this study and has signed the informed consent form.

35 year-old male diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) 2 years ago. The patient received 6 cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy and achieved a partial response, but relapsed 6 months later. The patient received salvage chemotherapy with DHAP and achieved a partial response followed by an autologous stem cell transplant. The patient again relapsed 12 months after transplant, and received salvage chemotherapy with ICE with a minimal response. PET/CT scan revealed disease progression in multiple lymph nodes and bone marrow infiltration. A biopsy of the most accessible site showed CD19-positive DLBCL. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate organ function. The patient has not received any prior CAR T-cell therapy. The patient is willing to undergo leukapheresis procedure for T-cell collection and agrees to use appropriate contraception.

A 62-year-old woman presents with severe knee pain and stiffness that has been affecting her daily activities for the past 3 years. She was diagnosed with severe osteoarthritis of the knee joint and was advised to undergo total knee arthroplasty. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she is taking lisinopril 10mg daily. She has no known allergies to any medication. Her vital signs are within normal range, with a BP of 130/80 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 bpm. On examination, there is marked tenderness and swelling in the right knee. X-ray shows severe degenerative changes in the right knee joint. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, with a creatinine clearance of 60 ml/min. She has never experienced any seizures or thromboembolic events in the past. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the most effective regimen of administration of tranexamic acid to improve clinical outcome among patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent herniorrhaphy surgery six months ago. He is experiencing severe pain in the inguinal region, with an average daily pain intensity of 8 on a numerical rating scale (NRS) of 0-10, both during rest and movement. The pain has persisted despite various pain medications and physical therapy. The patient has no known allergies to amide local anesthetics or vehicle ingredients in the patches. He is not taking any class I antiarrhythmic drugs and has no history of severe cardiac or hepatic disorder. He has no inflamed or injured skin at the application site. His renal function is normal and there are no signs of cognitive impairment or drug or ethanol abuse during the last 2 years. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the analgesic and sensory effects of a lidocaine patch for inguinal post-herniorrhaphy pain.

Samantha is a 28-year-old woman who works as a graphic designer. She has no history of any medical condition and takes no daily medications except for oral contraceptives. She has an average height of 5'5" and weighs 60 kg. Her family history is negative for migraine or any other primary headaches. She has never experienced a migraine or any other primary headaches in the past. She has not been exposed to radiation within the last year. She has no history of hypertension, hypotension, respiratory or cardiac disease. She has not had any headaches within the last 24 hours before the start of the trial. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in the trial to further scientific research on headaches and their treatments.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who works as a laboratory technician in a research facility. He has no notable medical history and has never been vaccinated for the plague. He is physically active and enjoys playing soccer with his friends on the weekends. He has no allergies to any medications or vaccines. He has not donated blood or blood products for at least 4 weeks prior to the study. He drinks alcohol occasionally and has never used illicit drugs. He has never participated in any clinical trials or been treated with an investigational drug in the last 30 days. He is willing to use barrier methods of contraception if his partner is using an acceptable form of contraception for at least 3 months after each dose. He understands the informed consent form and other documents required to be read by the subject and is willing to give signed informed consent. He meets the inclusion criteria of the study as a healthy male aged between 18-55 years with a BMI of 18-35. He has a negative urine pregnancy test prior to each dosing as required by the study protocol. He has no tattoos that cover or partially cover the upper arm, which could limit adequate assessment of the injection site.

A 42-year-old woman who has been on sick leave for 3 months due to chronic back pain and depression. She works as a nurse in a hospital and has been struggling with her symptoms for over a year. She has tried several treatments, including pain medication and psychotherapy, but none have been successful in getting her back to work. She is married with two children and lives in a suburban area. She has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. She reports feeling isolated and disconnected from her coworkers and has difficulty sleeping. Her current treatment plan includes acceptance and commitment therapy and physical rehabilitation at Hysnes Rehabilitation Centre. She is motivated to return to work and has set a goal to be back within 3 months. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help others who may be struggling with similar issues.

The patient is a 30 year old female who has been diagnosed with primary Sjögren's syndrome based on the 2016 American College of Rheumatology-European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) Classification Criteria. She is seropositive for anti-Sjögren's syndrome antigen A antibody. She is otherwise healthy with no significant acute or chronic medical illness. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She is willing to follow specific methods of contraception if applicable. She is able to tolerate venipuncture and has adequate venous access. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, drug levels, and drug effects of BMS-986325.

A 30-year-old Caucasian male with seasonal affective disorder (SAD) experiences extreme anxiety when speaking in public. He avoids social situations whenever possible and has difficulty performing his job duties which require him to interact with clients. He has tried cognitive behavioral therapy in the past, but it did not provide significant improvement. He has never taken any medication for his anxiety. He has a history of seasonal depression and experiences a decrease in mood during the winter months. He is currently not taking any medications. He is employed as an accountant and is married with no children. He does not drink alcohol or smoke. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and agrees to use acceptable methods of birth control. His blood tests and ECG findings are normal. He meets the DSM-IV criteria for social phobia.

This is a 54 year-old female with a history of hypertension and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who presents to the emergency department with palpitations and shortness of breath. Her vital signs are stable with blood pressure of 132/78 mmHg, heart rate of 160 beats per minute and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. She is alert and oriented with no evidence of chest pain, pulmonary edema or altered mental status. She denies any history of asthma or allergy to any of the study medications. She is a good candidate for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 28 year old woman in her 26th week of pregnancy. She had a normal pregnancy and delivery with her first child, who is now 3 years old. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 29, and her prenatal screening test revealed that her one-hour glucose challenge test (GCT) value was 155 mg/dL. She underwent a diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test (GTT) and was diagnosed with gestational diabetes. She has been receiving dietary counseling and performing capillary glucose monitoring at home. However, >20% of her recorded home glucose values are in excess of the target range despite appropriate diet, and she has agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She has no known allergies to medications and is not taking any herbal or nutraceutical supplements. She has no history of diabetes or other underlying medical conditions that could affect fetal growth or drug clearance. She plans to deliver at the participating medical treatment facility. She has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver. He presents with mild symptoms of hepatic encephalopathy, such as mental slowing and impaired reaction times while driving and operating machinery. The patient has no history of previous episodes of overt HE without a clear precipitant, recurrent excessive alcohol consumption or known myopathy or myositis. He has not suffered any trauma to his lower extremities within the last three months. The patient has normal renal function with serum creatinine levels within the normal range. He has no ferromagnetic implants, cerebrovascular disease, or pre-existing neurological conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume excessive alcohol. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial for the evaluation of the Brain Muscle Axis During Treatment of Hepatic Encephalopathy With L-ornithine L-aspartate.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has never undergone a colonoscopy before. She has no current symptoms of gastrointestinal disease, but she has a family history of colorectal cancer in her maternal grandfather. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She takes no other medications and has no known allergies. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her laboratory studies are within normal limits. She has never had a positive fecal occult blood test. The patient is willing to participate in the National CT Colonography Trial and has signed the informed consent form.

33 yo F with bilateral lower extremity swelling, pain and tenderness. Patient reports that the swelling and pain have been present for several years and have progressively worsened over time. The patient has been previously diagnosed with lipedema and has tried various conservative treatments with minimal improvement. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the treatment protocol.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). He signed a voluntary informed consent form to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of allopurinol sustained-release capsules in improving coronary plaque stability. The patient had a history of hypertension and was taking medication for it, but no history of smoking or diabetes. His liver and kidney function tests, platelet count, and hemoglobin level were all within normal range. He has never been diagnosed with gout or thyroid dysfunction, and he was not taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, steroid hormones, immunomodulatory or chemotherapeutic drugs during the study period. He was not allergic to allopurinol or any excipients, and his HLA-B5801 gene test was negative. The patient was informed that he would receive either allopurinol or placebo, and he agreed to participate in the study.

27-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with early stage endometrial cancer and desires to preserve fertility. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has not received any prior cancer treatments. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for pelvic examination which revealed a slightly enlarged uterus. Blood tests including routine blood tests, hepatic and renal function tests, and thyroid function tests are normal. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, autoimmune disease, or tuberculosis. She is negative for hepatitis B and C. She has no history of other malignant tumors or acute infectious disease. She is willing to undergo three hysteroscopies before, 3 months after, and 6 months after treatment. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the PD-1 inhibitor combined with progesterone clinical trial.

55 yo male presents with elevated PSA levels and abnormal uptake in the prostate on PET imaging. He has never had a prostate biopsy before and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new, molecular image directed, three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound guided biopsy system. He is able to provide informed consent and has not had any prostate biopsy in the past 2 months to decrease false positive uptake from inflammation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with stage III cervical cancer. She has a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain for several months. The diagnosis was made after a biopsy of her cervix showed the presence of squamous cell carcinoma. She is in good overall health and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided her written, voluntary informed consent. She is accessible for follow-up and management in the treatment center. Her hematological, renal, and hepatic functions are adequate, meeting the inclusion criteria for the study. She has no active infections or serious underlying medical conditions that would impair her ability to receive the planned treatment. She is not suffering from dementia or altered mental status that would prohibit her from understanding and providing informed consent.

The patient is a 35 year old female who has noticed a receding gum line on multiple teeth, particularly on the lower front teeth. She is concerned about the esthetic appearance and is willing to participate in the study. She has good oral hygiene practices and a full mouth plaque score of less than 20%. She is a non-smoker and has no untreated periodontal conditions. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and does not have any medical conditions that would preclude elective surgery. She is not being treated with any medication known to cause gingival hyperplasia and does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. The teeth in question have Miller's class I, II or III or combined recession defects. The patient is between the ages of 18-55 years.

72F living at home with her husband, with a clinical diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, on multiple daily injections of insulin was referred to endocrinology for management of blood sugars. She reports multiple episodes of hypoglycemia and struggles with maintaining blood sugar control. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis. She is able to perform basic activities of daily living but reports occasional difficulty with mobility due to joint pain. She has mild hearing loss but is able to communicate effectively. She denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has not used real-time CGM in the past 2 years and her A1c is between 7-10%. She is willing to participate in the tasks needed for the study during the run-in period. She does not have severe vision or hearing impairment that could interfere with study tasks. She does not need to use acetaminophen on a regular basis. She is not living in an institutional setting and does not have terminal diseases with life expectancy less than 1 year. She has no severe comorbidities that would prevent completing outcome measurements. She is not on dialysis and does not have end-stage renal insufficiency.

Pt is a 28yo M who is in good health with no significant medical history. He does not take any medications or supplements, and his blood magnesium level is within the normal range of 0.75 mmol/L. He has no known allergies and his vital signs are normal. He is a non-smoker and drinks only moderate amounts of coffee and tea. He has no history of drug addiction or excessive alcohol consumption. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has given written consent. He is affiliated with the French social security system and is willing to be registered as a volunteer participant in research.

The patient is a 62-year-old female who has been diagnosed with hypercholesterolemia. She has been taking lipid-lowering drugs for the past 4 months. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. She is a retired teacher and lives alone. She enjoys cooking and gardening in her free time. She has experienced some side effects from her medication, including mild muscle pain and weakness, but they have not been severe enough to cause her to stop taking her medication. She has not had any changes to her lipid-lowering medication for the past 8 weeks. She has given consent for the study and has had her blood sample taken for lipid profile and glucose within the last 5 days. She is willing to participate in the study to help with the evaluation of the efficacy of hypercholesterolemia treatment.

45-year-old male with a history of psoriasis, currently on a daily dose of 10mg prednisone for the past 6 months. The patient has been experiencing some side effects such as weight gain, insomnia, and mood changes. The patient is interested in participating in the TOASSTtrial and has no history of primary adrenal failure, systemic depot glucocorticoid treatment, or incapability to administer glucocorticoid cover treatment in situations of stress. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and will use medically reliable contraception throughout the study duration. The patient is compliant with medication and able to follow the procedures of the study.

50-year-old female with a history of narrow-angle glaucoma and scheduled to undergo a Peripheral Laser Iridotomy. The patient has previously undergone cataract surgery without complications and has not had any adverse reactions to steroids or Euphrasia drops in the past. The patient does not currently have any inflammation in the anterior chamber of the eye. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of prednisolone acetate eye drops and Euphrasia D3 eye drops in reducing intraocular inflammation in the post-operative period after a Peripheral Laser Iridotomy. The patient is willing to follow the post-operative instructions and attend follow-up appointments with the resident ophthalmologist.

A 42-year-old man with chronic low-back pain that has been bothering him for the past 8 months. He works as a construction worker and his job requires him to lift heavy objects frequently. His Hanover functional ability questionnaire (FFbH-R) score is less than 70% and he has been diagnosed with chronic lumbar ischialgia with radicular radiation. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and has not taken lymphdiaral basistropfen medication in the past 3 months. He is not pregnant or lactating and is capable of understanding the study. He has never had any fractures of the spine, Bechterew's disease, or neurological disorders. He has no allergies to any of the ingredients or excipients of the study drugs or to composite plants in general. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

57-year-old female admitted to the Neurointensive care unit at Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden with a diagnosis of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. The patient has a history of hypertension and migraines but no known cardiac arrhythmias or pacemaker use. She was admitted to the hospital after experiencing a sudden, severe headache and vomiting. Upon arrival, a CT scan revealed blood in the subarachnoid space, confirming the diagnosis of subarachnoid hemorrhage. The patient underwent an emergency craniotomy to clip the aneurysm and is currently recovering in the neurointensive care unit. The patient has consented to participate in the study and will have continuous heart rate variability monitoring during her stay, with the aim of evaluating whether specific patterns could be found in patients developing delayed cerebral ischemia after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

The patient is a 40-year-old Norwegian woman with a BMI of 45, who has been considering bariatric surgery for some time. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking ramipril for the past 2 years. Her blood pressure has been well controlled on this medication, but she has experienced some side effects such as dizziness and dry cough. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the pharmacokinetic effects of bariatric surgery on ramipril. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no history of significant medical problems other than her hypertension. She is not taking any other medications at the moment. She is a citizen of Norway and is planning to undergo either gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy in Central Norway.

44-year-old female with a history of multiple abdominal surgeries presents with a recurrent ventral wall hernia. The hernia is causing moderate to severe pain and discomfort, with a noticeable bulge in the abdominal wall. The patient has tried conservative management with a support belt but has not experienced any relief. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat her hernia and is willing to undergo either "Mesh Only Repair" or "Posterior Component Separation with Transversus Abdominis Muscle Release."

A 29-year-old female who works as a graphic designer is interested in participating in the Toric Contact Lens Performance Study. She has a history of astigmatism and has been wearing soft contact lenses for the past two years. Her last eye exam was six months ago, and her corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She spends at least 8 hours a day working on her computer and experiences occasional eye strain and headaches. She has no history of ocular pathology or surgery, and she does not wear gas permeable lenses. She is eager to participate in this study to see if toric contact lenses can improve her digital reading performance and alleviate her symptoms of asthenopia.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who is currently 35 weeks pregnant. She was diagnosed with preeclampsia during a routine check-up, as she presented with high blood pressure and protein in her urine. She has no significant medical history and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far. She is currently being managed with bed rest and medication to control her blood pressure, but her condition has not improved. The clinic care team has recommended magnesium sulfate treatment, but it is limited or not available at the current site. Therefore, the patient has been given the option to participate in this study, which offers the administration of magnesium sulfate with the Springfusor pump. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with HIV infection 10 years ago. The patient has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 8 years and has a history of treatment failure with Kaletra as their second protease inhibitor-based HAART. The patient has demonstrated reduced susceptibility to lopinavir and has had two consecutive viral loads above 1,000 copies/mL while on Kaletra therapy. The patient's Kaletra regimen is their second protease inhibitor-containing regimen and does not contain any other PIs. The patient is currently on ART and has not been treated for an active opportunistic infection within the last 30 days. The patient is not receiving systemic chemotherapy and does not have a history of acute or chronic pancreatitis. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol and is not currently using any investigational drugs. The patient is eligible for the study and is at least 18 years of age.

A 46 year old woman who has never had a mammogram and is scheduled for a routine physical examination with a non-resident PCP in the next few weeks. She does not have a history of breast cancer or a BRCA mutation and is not currently receiving any breast cancer prevention medications. She is fluent in English and has not had any breast enlargement or reduction surgeries. She is interested in learning more about her breast cancer risk and is open to participating in the study to assess the personalized risk-based approach for breast cancer screening and prevention.

A 62-year-old woman presented to the hospital with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with COVID-19 infection and hospitalized for supportive care. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled with medication. She reported no previous history of heart disease or arrhythmias. However, during her hospitalization, she developed episodes of palpitations and had a transient episode of syncope. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial examining the relationship between COVID-19 infection and the development of cardiac arrhythmias. She understands the study's purpose and has provided informed consent to participate. The patient is able to cooperate and follow instructions for continuous ECG monitoring during her hospital stay.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing atopic dermatitis for the past 5 years. She has tried multiple treatments including topical steroids and antihistamines, but has not achieved satisfactory improvement in her symptoms. She currently has an IGA score of 3 and AD affecting approximately 10% of her total Body Surface Area (BSA). The patient is generally in good health with no significant medical history or conditions that may impact the validity of the study results. She is not currently taking any immunosuppressive or systemic (cortico) steroid therapy, nor has she used phototherapy or tanning beds in the past 6 weeks. The patient is willing to practice acceptable birth control methods during the study period and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 20-year-old sexually active woman who recently had unprotected sex with her new partner. She has a history of bacterial vaginosis (BV) and has experienced the symptoms before, such as vaginal discharge and odor. She is concerned about the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and wants to participate in a clinical trial for screening and treatment of BV to prevent STIs. She lives in a major city in the United States and has access to a healthcare facility. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and understands the importance of regular screening and treatment for BV. She has no allergies to metronidazole and is not currently taking any antibiotics or medications that may interact with metronidazole. She is not pregnant and is willing to abstain from alcohol for one week if required for the study. She has more than two risk factors for STIs, including a history of BV, regular douching, and having multiple sexual partners in the past year. She is able to swallow pills and does not have any active medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

17F with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 and a history of failed conservative treatment for obesity, including dietary modifications and physical activity. She has been struggling with her weight since childhood and has a family history of obesity. Despite efforts to lose weight, she has not been successful in achieving a healthy weight. She has experienced bullying and social isolation due to her weight, which has led to low self-esteem and decreased quality of life. She has no known comorbidities related to her obesity but is concerned about the negative impact her weight may have on her future health. She has been evaluated by a psychologist and has been deemed psychologically fit for surgery. She is in Tanner stage 4-5 of puberty, and her parents have given their informed consent for her to participate in the study. She is willing to undergo laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery as a potential solution to her obesity and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 5 years ago. She reports experiencing pain, swelling, and stiffness in multiple joints, including her hands, wrists, and knees. She has been prescribed various medications to manage her symptoms, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). Despite these treatments, she continues to experience pain and stiffness on a daily basis. The patient also reports feeling anxious and depressed due to the impact of RA on her daily life, including difficulty with work and household tasks. She is interested in participating in the SARA study to explore new ways of managing her symptoms and improving her mental health. She is not currently taking cyclical estrogen replacement therapy and does not have a diagnosis of lupus.

A 70-year-old woman who fell from a standing height and fractured her tibia is scheduled to undergo surgery. She reports no history of adverse reactions or side-effects to melatonin. She has no history of delirium or cognitive impairment. The patient is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively. She lives independently and does not require assistance with activities of daily living. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she is in good general health. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help prevent post-operative delirium.

The patient is a fluent German speaker and does not have a history of major depression. The patient is not currently taking any psychotropic medication or any drugs within the last two weeks. The patient has not consumed alcohol within the last twelve hours. The patient does not have any allergies to capsaicin or sesame oil. The patient is not a third year or older student in medicine, pharmacy, or psychology.

The patient is a 24-year-old female who is sexually active and at risk for pregnancy. She has been using condoms as her only method of birth control but is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an oral contraceptive. She reports having regular menstrual cycles and no history of gynecological issues. She is a non-smoker and does not have any medical conditions that would contraindicate the use of oral contraceptives. She is willing to use the study oral contraceptive therapy as her only method of birth control during the study period. She understands the requirements of the study, including completing a daily diary and attending regular physical and gynecological exams.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who has been experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past few weeks. She has been diagnosed with depression in the past and has been prescribed medication for it. She is currently taking sertraline 50mg daily. She has no history of substance abuse or other mental health conditions. She is fluent in English and is comfortable using the internet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help with her depression symptoms.

A 42-year-old woman with a BMI of 34.5 kg/m2 was referred to the clinic for hypertension management. Her blood pressure was found to be 142/92 mm Hg during the initial visit. She reported occasional headaches and dizziness. Physical examination revealed a waist circumference of 104 cm. She was diagnosed with metabolic syndrome and has been on a low-calorie diet and exercise program for the past 6 months. She is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg daily for hypertension control. Her last lab results showed: HgbA1c: 5.7%, Fasting glucose: 101 mg/dL, LDL: 128 mg/dL, HDL: 48 mg/dL, Triglycerides: 205 mg/dL, TSH: 3.8 milli-International unit/mL. She is not taking any medications affecting glucose metabolism or hormonal contraceptives. She is a non-smoker and has no history of psychiatric or medical conditions including diabetes, liver or kidney disease, obesity syndromes or active periodontal disease.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her first pregnancy, currently in her second trimester, is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no prior history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes or any other chronic medical condition. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker with no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. She has been regularly attending prenatal check-ups and has had a normal ultrasound scan with no abnormalities detected. She plans on exclusively breastfeeding her baby after delivery. She is proficient in English and is capable of understanding and providing informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Barrett's Esophagus with Intestinal Metaplasia and Low Grade-Intraepithelial Neoplasia. He has undergone endoscopic BE ablation treatment and is now due for follow-up procedure to evaluate the efficacy of the treatment. He has less than 2cm of circumferential BE and less than 5 total islands of BE on prior to last ablation. He is over 18 years of age and has the ability to provide written, informed consent. He does not have complete eradication of BE documented by biopsies and does not have any allergies to fluorescein.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and has been receiving treatment according to NCCN panel recommendation. He has recently developed spinal metastasis and has been experiencing back pain and weakness in his legs. He has a history of heavy smoking for over 30 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. His performance status, as measured by the Karnofsky Performance Scale (KPS), is 60%, indicating he is able to care for himself but has significant limitations in his daily activities. He has no significant medical history, except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of any other tumors, and his follow-up has been regular. The patient is interested in learning more about his prognosis and potential treatment options.

The patient is a 35 year-old man who has been struggling with alcoholism for the past 5 years. He has had multiple unsuccessful attempts at quitting on his own and has experienced several relapses. He drinks an average of 20 alcoholic beverages per week and has had several instances of binge drinking, with at least 5 drinks in one sitting. He has been sober for the past 10 days and has not experienced any significant withdrawal symptoms. He has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, bulimia/anorexia, or dementia. He is currently not taking any medication for a psychological disorder, but has received therapy in the past. He is willing to attend mutual help groups but not seek additional psychotherapy during the first 6 months of the study. He is able to read and write in German and is willing to sign a declaration of informed consent. He has no significant medical disorders but has elevated ALT levels due to his alcohol consumption. He is currently not pregnant or nursing, and uses a reliable contraceptive method.

A 45-year-old male patient presented with symptoms of excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and witnessed apneas by his partner. He reports waking up several times at night gasping for air. He has noticed decreased energy levels, irritability, and difficulty concentrating at work. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient's BMI is 32, indicating that he is overweight. He has no history of respiratory disease, such as asthma, COPD, or bronchiectasis, and has not had an upper or lower respiratory tract infection within the past 6 weeks. He is not currently pregnant and has no history of malignancies or serious medical illness. The patient has been referred for a sleep study under the Division of Respiratory Medicine, Prince of Wales Hospital, and has been recruited for the study upon admission.

A 58-year-old male patient with COPD GOLD/ATS of 3, without any major co-morbidity, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been experiencing shortness of breath for the past 5 years and is currently taking bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids as prescribed by his pulmonologist. He has never participated in any pulmonary rehabilitation program. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and he performs light exercises for 30 minutes a day. He has not had any exacerbation in the past month and is covered by social insurance. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements and procedures involved.

A 65-year-old woman was diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica and prescribed a systemic corticosteroid therapy with Prednisone for at least one year. She has no history of previous cataracts and her lens autofluorescence is normal at inclusion. She has never used eye drops other than artificial tears and has no history of ocular disease or elevated intraocular pressure. She does not have diabetes or atopic dermatitis. She has not had protracted corticosteroid therapy in the past and is not taking any medications known to be associated with an increased risk of cataract. She is willing to participate in the study and attend follow-up appointments as required.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents to the clinic with chest pain and shortness of breath during exercise. He has a past medical history of coronary artery disease and has undergone angioplasty with stenting in the past. His current medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin. His family history is significant for coronary artery disease in his father and brother. He is a smoker, with a 30 pack-year history. His physical exam is significant for a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 bpm. His lab work shows a total cholesterol level of 220 mg/dL and a LDL level of 130 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial for crossing chronic total occlusions in coronary arteries.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with papillary thyroid cancer after a suspicious nodule was found during a routine physical examination. The nodule was biopsied and confirmed as cancerous. She has no history of thyroid problems or any other medical conditions. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has never had surgery before. On ultrasound, there was no evidence of cervical lymph node metastases. She is able to read and write in English and has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a healthy male or female between the ages of 40 and 80 years old, with a body mass index of 18.0 to 30.0 kg/m2. The patient has normal lung function, with a percent predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second ≥ 80% and forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio ≥ 70%. The patient is able to produce a peak inspiratory flow rate of at least 30.00L/min using the investigational device attached to an electronic flow meter. The patient must not have smoked within 12 months before admission and should not have a history of clinically relevant respiratory disease, diseases affecting respiratory function, E.N.T. diseases, or lung surgery. The patient should not be pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the study period or within 3 months after the last dose of study treatment. The patient should also be willing to use appropriate contraception measures from time of screening until 3 months after the last dose of study drug.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on understanding the underlying biological principles of granulation and fibrotic responses limiting the effectiveness and longevity of BELVR treatment with EBVs. Therefore, the trial does not involve patient recruitment.

37-year-old female with a history of non-infectious, non-necrotizing anterior scleritis (nodular) presents to the clinic for evaluation. She reports experiencing pain, redness, and discomfort in her right eye for the past few weeks. She has tried several over-the-counter eye drops without any significant improvement. She has no history of ocular surgery, ocular trauma, or any other ocular conditions. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and mild hypertension. On examination, the patient has conjunctival injection and a nodular scleral lesion in the right eye. The left eye is normal. The intraocular pressure is within normal limits. She is not taking any systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressants. She provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with all study-related instructions. She is not currently pregnant or nursing, and agrees to use an acceptable method of contraception during the study. She has no other significant illnesses or conditions that would interfere with the study parameters or put her at significant risk.

The patient is a 45 year old male who presented to the emergency department with acute onset of shortness of breath and chest pain. He has a history of smoking and hypertension, but no prior history of pulmonary embolism (PE). CT pulmonary angiography confirmed the diagnosis of submassive PE with evidence of right ventricular strain on echocardiography. The patient has been admitted to the hospital and is currently receiving systemic anticoagulation therapy. He meets the eligibility criteria for catheter-directed thrombolysis for submassive PE and has consented to participate in the study. The patient does not have any known bleeding disorders or other contraindications to thrombolysis. He is currently stable and not requiring any supplemental oxygen or vasopressor support. The patient is married, works in construction and enjoys playing basketball with friends on weekends. His BMI is 28 and his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg.

A 63-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with recurrent colorectal cancer. He has undergone surgery for colorectal cancer in the past and is scheduled for curative surgery again. He has no other history of malignancies, and all laboratory values are within normal range. He is currently not taking any medication and has no known allergies. He has no history of HIV, HBsAG or HCV. He is not currently sexually active and is not planning to have children. He has provided a negative urine pregnancy test and is willing to practice adequate contraception for 30 days prior to administration of investigational product and 30 days after completion of injection.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) four years ago. She has been receiving oral antispasticity medication for the last three years and has been stable for the past 30 days. She experiences frequent muscle spasms that interfere with her daily activities and quality of life. She has not used cannabis or cannabinoid-derived products for medicinal or recreational purposes within the past 30 days and is willing to abstain during the trial. She is not currently using botulinum toxin injections for spasticity relief and is willing to abstain during the trial. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using a highly effective method of birth control. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse or dependence within the last year and has no known hypersensitivity to cannabinoids or any of the excipients of the IMP.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. He is currently undergoing treatment at a local hospital and is interested in participating in the pilot study for digital follow-up. He speaks fluent Dutch and is willing to complete the weekly questionnaire for the intervention arm of the study. He has a supportive family and is motivated to participate in the study to help improve the care for future lung cancer patients. He works as a software developer but has had to take a leave of absence due to his diagnosis. He does not smoke or drink alcohol and maintains a healthy lifestyle. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has no significant comorbidities.

This is a 65 year old right-handed male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing mild cognitive impairment, mainly in the area of memory, for the past year. He has not been receiving any treatment for this impairment. He is able to perform his activities of daily living without assistance and has no significant motor impairments. He has not been diagnosed with depression and his score on the Beck Depression Inventory is 4 out of 63. He is not taking any centrally active drugs and has no history of epilepsy or epileptic seizures. He is not pregnant and does not have a pacemaker or any other metal parts in his body.

The patient is a 58-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension. He presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past few months. Upon further examination and imaging, he is diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He has no history of ototoxicity or peripheral neuropathy. His laboratory tests show a WBC count of 4,500/mm^3, absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3, and platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. His bilirubin level is normal, and his AST and ALT levels are within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. His creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. He has no history of cardiac or gastrointestinal disease. He is not pregnant or nursing, and his pregnancy test is negative. He uses effective barrier contraception. He has no history of c-kit-targeted therapy or other malignancy within the past 5 years. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands and signs the informed consent document.

Unfortunately, as this clinical trial is seeking healthy participants, I cannot provide a patient description for this study. It is important to recruit participants who meet the specific inclusion criteria of the trial in order to accurately study the immunological responses to SARS-CoV protein in different age groups.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who is struggling with obesity, with a BMI of 35 kg/m^2. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has been finding it difficult to lose weight through diet and exercise alone. She has no known health conditions and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke and has no history of drug use. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential treatment for obesity.

The patient is a 22-year-old female diagnosed with asthma by her general practitioner. She is experiencing difficulty in breathing, chest tightness, and frequent coughing episodes. She is currently on daily ICS/LABA therapy with a stable total daily dose of > 250 micrograms per day. However, her asthma is inadequately controlled, as her ACT total score is less than 20. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will compare the effectiveness and adherence of single inhaler triple therapy (SITT) of FF/UMEC/VI with the Connected Inhaler System (CIS) as compared to multiple inhaler triple therapy (MITT) of the combination of FP/SAL plus TIO without CIS. She has her own Android mobile device and is willing to download the app and keep it turned on for the duration of the study. She is a non-smoker and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is capable of giving a signed informed consent. She is eligible to participate in the study if she meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing itchiness and redness on her skin for the past six months. The symptoms are localized to the skin on her arms, legs, and trunk. She has tried various over-the-counter medications but has found no relief. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. Upon examination, the doctor noticed skin lesions that are consistent with primary cutaneous lymphoma. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide the required information for the registry.

There is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is a retrospective study that will evaluate the clinical performance of posterior multi-surface amalgam and resin composite restorations placed by dental students over a five-year period. The study will not involve any patient recruitment or require the participation of any specific individual. The eligibility criteria for the study only involves the type of restorations placed by dental students over a five-year period.

A 35-year-old male with a history of intermittent explosive disorder (IED) for the past 5 years, presented to the psychiatric clinic for management of his aggressive behaviors. He reported frequent outbursts of anger and aggression towards others that are often unpredictable and difficult to control. He has had several legal issues due to his aggressive behavior, including physical assault and property damage. He has tried several medications with no significant improvement in his symptoms. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He is a social drinker but denies any history of drug use. His family history is significant for a paternal uncle with a history of bipolar disorder. He has no history of suicidal ideation or attempts. On physical examination, he is alert and oriented, with no signs of acute distress. His vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory tests and electrocardiogram (EKG) are normal. He meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial of SRX246 in adults with IED. He is willing to sign the informed consent and follow the study requirements.

A 32-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of recurrent panic attacks for the last six months. She has a history of anxiety and depression, which was treated with medication and therapy two years ago but she discontinued both treatments. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She has no history of substance abuse. She is currently not on any medication. Her past surgical history is unremarkable. She experiences anticipatory anxiety, agoraphobia avoidance, and fear of body sensations during the panic attacks. She is interested in trying cognitive-behavioral therapy with medication to treat her panic disorder.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with three-vessel coronary artery disease. He experiences chest pain during physical activity and has been advised to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking medications for these conditions. He has never had any surgery before and is anxious about the procedure. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about the different types of grafts that will be used during the surgery.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of shoulder pain and weakness for the past six months is scheduled for elective shoulder arthroscopy under general anesthesia. He reports no significant past medical history, although he has a family history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He is currently not taking any medications except for occasional over-the-counter pain relievers. His BMI is 27.3. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of different nerve blocks for postoperative pain management. The patient has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders, and he is not currently taking any psychotropic or opioid medications. Physical examination of the patient reveals tenderness, weakness, and limited range of motion of the right shoulder. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.
