56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency room with a deep laceration on his right wrist after accidentally cutting himself with a sharp knife while working in the kitchen. The patient reported immediate loss of sensation and function in his right hand. The physical examination revealed a clean-cut transection injury of the median and ulnar nerves with no signs of crush injury or vascular compromise. The patient was referred to a hand surgeon for further evaluation and management. The patient was deemed eligible for the clinical trial comparing primary versus secondary repair of the nerves based on electrodiagnostic assessment and clinical examination. The patient provided informed consent and was enrolled in the study.

A 45-year-old woman noticed a small lump on her left forearm. The lump has been slowly growing over the past few months and is now about the size of a marble. It is soft to the touch and not painful. She has no history of trauma or injury to the area. She visited her primary care physician who referred her to a specialist to further evaluate the lump. Upon examination, the specialist noted a well-defined, mobile, soft mass located just below the skin surface. An ultrasound was performed which showed a hypoechoic mass with some internal vascularity. The patient has not undergone any previous operations at the same site and the mass is not recurrent. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to further evaluate the nature of the mass using Doppler ultrasound.

The patient is a 50 year old woman diagnosed with Rheumatoid arthritis for 5 years. She is currently in remission and taking Methotrexate for her RA. She has been experiencing numbness and tingling in her right hand for the past few months, with worsening symptoms at night. She also reports difficulty gripping objects and weakness in her hand. On physical examination, she has positive Tinel's sign and Phalen's maneuver. Nerve conduction studies and ultrasound parameters confirm the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome. She is right-handed and works as a data entry clerk for a local company. She has no history of diabetes or other peripheral nerve disorders. Her BMI is 25 and her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her symptoms and avoid surgery.

65-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with a history of ischemic stroke 6 months ago. He has residual left-sided weakness and difficulty walking, but is able to ambulate at least 10 feet with minimal to moderate assistance. He has no history of transient ischemic attack, cerebral aneurysm or any other serious terminal illnesses. He has no cognitive decline or dementia. The patient reports that he has not been very active since his stroke due to his physical limitations. He is overweight with a BMI of 29. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is interested in participating in a study to improve his recovery after stroke. He is able to travel to the intervention site on a weekly basis. The patient is aware that the study involves lifestyle changes, including exercise, nutrition, stress management, education, and group support. He is willing to participate in the study and to have blood drawn at baseline, week 6, and week 12. The patient is determined to improve his physical abilities and quality of life.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. She has a 2-year-old daughter at home and is concerned about the risk of congenital infections during pregnancy. She is interested in learning more about how to reduce the risk of CMV infection during pregnancy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test an educational intervention. She is a non-smoker and does not use any drugs. Her pregnancy to date has been uneventful and she has had no complications. She has a history of mild asthma, which is well-controlled with an inhaler. She is not currently taking any medications. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and her blood pressure is within normal range. Her labs: FBS: 90 mg/dl, Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dl, WBC: 8.2 x 10^3/uL, Platelets: 250 x 10^3/uL. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that her involvement will help prevent congenital infections in future generations.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. She has no history of other cancers and has not received any prior radiation therapy for pancreatic cancer. Imaging studies have confirmed the presence of measurable disease that is suitable for treatment with chemotherapy. The patient has an ECOG functional status of 1, indicating that she is ambulatory and able to carry out light work, but is restricted in physically strenuous activity. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to Thiazolidinedione (TZD) therapy. She has no history of heart failure, HIV, or bladder cancer. The patient has undergone recent liver function tests, which indicate that she has adequate hepatic function. Her total bilirubin level is within normal limits, and her AST and ALT levels are below 2.5 x ULN. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

A 35 year old woman presents to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of redness and discharge in her left eye for the past 3 days. The patient reports mild pain and itching in the eye. She has no previous history of eye problems or surgeries. The visual acuity in both eyes is 20/20. On examination, the left eye shows mild erythema and conjunctival discharge. The right eye is normal. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to avoid all disallowed medications for the appropriate washout periods. The patient has not previously participated in a conjunctival biopsy study and is not currently enrolled in an investigational drug or device study.

The patient is a 42 year old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 41 kg/m² who has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years. She has hypertension and sleep apnea syndrome, which have been difficult to manage with conventional treatments. She is interested in undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery to address her obesity and associated health problems. She is not currently taking any medications other than vitamins, and does not have any allergies to the drugs used in the study. She is willing to participate in the three 12-hour studies at different time periods following her surgery and understands the risks and benefits associated with the study. She resides in France and has French social security.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer three years ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy and had a good response to treatment. However, her cancer has now relapsed and she is experiencing a rise in CA 125 levels. She reports mild abdominal discomfort but no other significant symptoms. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. Her hemoglobin is 11.5 g/dL, WBC count is 5,800/mm^3, and platelet count is 140,000/mm^3. Her creatinine level is within normal limits, as well as her AST/ALT and bilirubin levels. She is not pregnant or nursing and is not currently taking any hormonal therapy. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

Pt is a 29yo F with a history of allergic reactions to certain foods, including shellfish and peanuts. She presents to the emergency department with acute urticaria and itching after consuming shrimp at dinner. She has no known history of chronic urticaria or hereditary angioedema. The urticaria is widespread and accompanied by mild facial swelling. She has no history of narrow angle glaucoma or prostatic hypertrophy. She has not taken any antihistamines within the past 4 hours or received steroids, epinephrine, or H2 antagonists within the past 12-48 hours. She is able to provide informed consent and meets all other inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 78-year-old woman who lives alone and has been recently diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and diabetes. She has also suffered from chronic heart failure (CHF) in the past. She experiences shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing as well as difficulty controlling her blood sugar levels. She often forgets to take her medication and has trouble keeping up with her self-care routine. She feels weak and experiences fatigue on most days, and her mobility is limited. She has a history of falls and is afraid of falling again. She has been recommended to join the CareWell clinical trial, where she can receive comprehensive multidisciplinary integrated care programmes using ICT platforms and communication channels. She is willing to participate in the study and is capable of understanding and following instructions. She lives independently and does not require assistance in her daily activities.

A 52 year old woman with a diagnosis of breast cancer is scheduled for an elective mastectomy. She has no history of allergies or contraindications to local anesthetics or ropivacaine. She has no history of severe cardiovascular disease, renal or liver failure, neurologic or psychological disease. She is not currently being treated with any analgesics. This patient has not undergone a previous mastectomy or thoracic surgery. She has an ASA score of 2.

A 45-year-old female diagnosed with cervical cancer after abnormal Pap smear and cervical biopsy. The patient has no history of cancer in her family. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker and has no history of any major illnesses. The patient is currently experiencing vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain. She underwent a CT scan, which demonstrated cervical mass measuring 6 cm, with no evidence of metastasis. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a normal organ function. She has not received any prior treatment for cervical cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study participation.

The patient is a 60 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with early idiopathic Parkinson's Disease. He experiences tremors in his left hand and has some difficulty with coordination on that side. He has been on a stable dose of a single dopamine agonist for the past 24 weeks as part of a previous clinical trial. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies. He is willing to use an adequate method of contraception if necessary and is able to provide written, informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who has been diagnosed with opioid dependence according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR) criteria. He has been receiving maintenance treatment with Subutex at doses ranging from 4 mg to the maximum dose permitted by country labeling requirements, but not exceeding 24 mg/day, for at least one month prior to screening. He reports not having injected opioids more than four times in the month prior to screening and has an opioid-negative urine drug screening (UDS) result prior to randomization. He confirms that he is practicing adequate contraception. He is willing to participate in the study and adhere to dose and visit schedules. He is a candidate for transfer from Subutex to Suboxone as required in the protocol. He is not participating in any other clinical study in which medication(s) are being delivered and does not have serious untreated Axis I DSM-IV-TR psychiatric comorbidity, unauthorized and significant benzodiazepine use requiring medical detoxification, or alcohol dependence requiring medical detoxification. He is not treated with generic buprenorphine.

A 31-year-old male smoker who has been smoking at least 10 cigarettes per day for the past 5 years is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new vaccine aimed at reducing nicotine addiction. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric illness, and is generally in good health. He is right-handed and has no known immunodeficiency. He does not currently use any psychoactive medications and does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol. He is interested in participating in the study as he is motivated to quit smoking and believes that the vaccine could be a helpful tool in achieving his goal. He is willing to undergo medical screening and fMRI scanning as part of the study.

A 42-year-old woman is experiencing frequent urination at night, with an average of 3-4 times per night. She wakes up feeling tired and has trouble concentrating throughout the day. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. She has no history of genitourinary tract pathology, urolithiasis, or diabetes insipidus. She is not pregnant and has no history of cardiac or liver failure. She has no known allergies to desmopressin or any other substances. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. She will be given a prescription to buy Minirin Melt 60µg at the local pharmacy and will take it in the evening before going to bed for 30 days. She will fill out a frequency/volume chart for the first 14 days, and blood and urine samples will be taken on day 3 and day 7 for safety control. On day 30, another blood sample will be taken.

Lin is a 25 year old Taiwanese man who works as a software engineer. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2. He has no history of any major medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for any metabolic or cardiovascular diseases. He has no known allergies to medications or any history of drug or alcohol dependence. His physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise. He was informed about the study and provided his consent to participate.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has a history of hypersensitivity reactions to intravenous iron infusions. She was diagnosed with iron-deficient anemia during her pregnancy and received intravenous ferric carboxymaltose (Ferinject) infusion. However, during the infusion, she experienced a hypersensitivity reaction of grade II, characterized by urticaria and mild dyspnea. She was treated with antihistamines and the infusion was discontinued. She has a past medical history of seasonal allergies and asthma, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids for her asthma. She has no other significant medical history or co-morbidities. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on hypersensitivity reactions to intravenous iron infusions.

A 38-year-old German-speaking woman has been suffering from severe unipolar major depression for over 10 years. She has had at least four episodes of the disorder and has failed to respond to primary antidepressants from at least three different classes, as well as augmentation and combination therapies, ECT, and psychotherapy. Her HDRS24 score is currently above 20, and her GAF score is below 45. She is drug-free and has no medical comorbidities, but she smokes occasionally. She is interested in participating in the DBS clinical trial and is able to give written informed consent. She has no history of substance abuse, personality disorders, or nonaffective psychotic disorders.

A 7-year-old male child presents with a fever of 39°C and chills that started 2 days ago. He complains of headache, fatigue, and muscle pain. The patient lives in Kilifi District, Kenya, and has a history of malaria episodes in the past. On physical examination, he has a palpable spleen, and his blood smear reveals mono-infection with P. falciparum with a parasitaemia of 15,000/µl asexual forms. His weight is 22 kg, and his height is 118 cm. He is able to swallow oral medication and has no underlying chronic diseases, and he is not taking any medication that may interfere with the study protocol. His parents provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

There is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial as the study is evaluating the feasibility of a novel strategy for preventing the spread of infection in nursing homes. However, eligible participants must be aged 18 years or older and reside in a participating nursing home. Exclusion criteria include being identified by nursing home staff as combative or having behavioral problems that could lead to agitation if approached by project staff.

32 yo F with a history of schizophrenia diagnosed at the age of 25 presenting with symptoms of anxiety, paranoia, and auditory hallucinations. The patient has been on stable doses of antipsychotics for the past 2 years, but still experiences occasional breakthrough symptoms. The patient is currently taking 15mg of aripiprazole daily with some reduction in symptoms but still experiencing significant anxiety and paranoia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of Bifeprunox. The patient's weight is 160 lbs, and she is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is compliant with medications and has no history of substance abuse or suicidal ideation. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

54 yo F with history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 10 years and diabetic nephropathy for 2 years. The patient is being treated with angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) and has microalbuminuria (30-40 mg/24 h urine) on two samples collected over the past month. The patient's HbA1c is 8.2%. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 ml/min. The patient has no other renal impairment and blood pressure is well controlled at 140/80 mmHg. No other significant medical history or medication use. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has given written informed consent.

This is a 35 year-old male with a history of cocaine and opiate dependence. He has been maintained on methadone for the past 3 months and has been stable on a dose of 80mg/day. He reports using cocaine sporadically, but has been unable to stop on his own. He has tried various treatment methods in the past, including outpatient counseling and 12-step programs, but has not been successful in maintaining abstinence. He is in good overall physical health, but reports occasional anxiety and depression. He does not have any significant medical or psychiatric history other than his substance use disorders. He is currently employed part-time and lives with his partner and two children. He expresses a strong desire to stop using cocaine and is willing to participate in a research study to explore new treatment options.

Pt is a preterm infant born at 32 weeks gestational age referred for a videofluoroscopic swallow study (VFSS) due to suspected pharyngeal phase dysphagia. The infant weighs 2.5 kg and has been in the neonatal intensive care unit for 4 weeks. The infant is currently being fed breast milk via a nasogastric tube. The infant has no known allergies or medical conditions other than being born prematurely. The parents have consented to participation in the study.

A 45-year-old female patient underwent lumbar spinal stenosis surgery with posterolateral fusion at the Traumatological Institute of Santiago due to severe back pain that limited her daily activities. She has no history of previous surgeries, is not overweight or underweight, and has not experienced any postoperative complications. Her preoperative Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score was 8 out of 10, and her Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score was 60%. She is motivated to participate in the study and has no history of inability to exercise. She is willing to commit to the follow-up visits and comply with the exercise program. She is currently taking acetaminophen for pain management as prescribed by her physician. She has been cleared by her surgeon to participate in the study.

A 56 year old man visits the dental clinic with complaints of missing two teeth in the posterior mandibular region. His medical history is unremarkable and he is a non-smoker. On clinical and radiological examination, he is diagnosed with partial edentulism and is deemed eligible for implant placement. The patient's bone quantity and band of keratinized mucosa are deemed adequate for the insertion of 4.3 mm diameter implants. The patient is not suffering from active periodontal disease and has proper oral hygiene with bleeding on probing scores (BOP) and plaque indices (PI) less than 15%. The patient is informed about the study and signs an informed consent form. The patient is then included in the randomized clinical trial, which involves the placement of two implants, one with a PEEK healing abutment and the other with a Ti healing abutment. The patient is prescribed antimicrobials, analgesics, and 0.2% chlorhexidine solution and undergoes the surgical procedure for implant placement under local anesthesia. Postoperative care is given and the patient is scheduled for a follow-up 3 months after the implant surgery for the placement of larger diameter healing abutments and to collect soft tissue specimens for histological examination.

25 yo F who is in good health and is a non-smoker. She has a BMI of 21.5 kg/m2 and has no history of significant acute or chronic illness. She is not currently breastfeeding nor is she of childbearing potential. The participant's renal function is normal, with a Glomerula Filtration Rate of 90 mL/min/1.73 m2. She has no history of cardiac arrhythmias, autonomic instability or pulmonary, renal or liver disease. The participant has no history of Gilbert's Syndrome, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency or any other congenital hemolytic anemias. The participant has not had major surgery within the last 4 weeks. She has no known or suspected autoimmune disease and has never had active tuberculosis requiring treatment, documented latent TB within the previous 3 years, or evidence of a past TB infection without documented adequate therapy. She has agreed to follow instructions for method(s) of contraception for the duration of treatment with BMS-986205 and for a total of 110 days after the last dose of BMS-986205.

A 55-year-old Hispanic woman presents to the clinic with a medical history of CKD and hyperphosphatemia. She has been on thrice-weekly hemodialysis for the past 6 months and is currently receiving stable doses of treatments affecting serum phosphorus. She reports experiencing fatigue and difficulty concentrating during hemodialysis sessions. The patient has a history of uncontrolled hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine and losartan. She denies any hospitalization for cardiac disease in the past 3 months, but reports having chronic constipation for which she takes over-the-counter laxatives. She denies any history of liver disease or abnormal liver function tests. Her AST and ALT levels are within normal range. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the safety and efficacy of EOS789 in patients with CKD and hyperphosphatemia on hemodialysis. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to discontinue her current treatments affecting serum phosphorus.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl with craniosynostosis, Philadelphia type, which was diagnosed shortly after birth. She has cranial malformations and webbing of the fingers and toes. She has no other medical conditions or allergies and is not taking any medications. Her family has a history of craniosynostosis, and she is a member of a large family that has been previously referred to the study. She is willing to provide informed consent or assent, and her primary physician, a trained medical geneticist, will be informed of the results of the study. She will have 1 to 2 teaspoons of blood drawn for genetic studies and may have her medical records reviewed. She understands that the results are preliminary and must not be disclosed to the patient or included in the medical record without repeat testing in a CLIA-approved lab. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that her contribution will help other families in the future.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was diagnosed with retinoblastoma at the age of 2. He underwent several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, and his treatment was completed 20 years ago. He has been in remission ever since. He has noticed some changes in his vision in the affected eye in recent years, but otherwise, he is in good health. He is interested in participating in this study to help improve the care and follow-up for future children with retinoblastoma.

Patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes who presents with fatigue, back pain, and weight loss of 10 pounds over the last 2 months. Imaging studies reveal a 7 cm mass in the left kidney and multiple lung nodules, consistent with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis. The patient has no prior therapy for metastatic disease and is deemed appropriate for first-line treatment with sunitinib malate. The patient has no history of heart failure, chronic unstable disease, or long QT interval. The patient has no history of another primary cancer and no severe, uncontrolled acute infection, hypertension or psychological disorder. The patient is affiliated with the French Social insurance and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has a history of coronary heart disease and was hospitalized for decompensated heart failure with shortness of breath, peripheral edema, and rales. He had undergone PCI for myocardial revascularization 8 months ago. His current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, bisoprolol, and spironolactone. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol abuse. His medical records show a previous diagnosis of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no known allergies or intolerances to medications. On physical examination, he has jugular venous distension, bibasilar crackles, and peripheral edema up to the knees. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 80 bpm, and BMI is 28. An echocardiogram reveals an LVEF of 35%. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent document.

63-year-old Caucasian male with a history of frequent sun exposure and a previous diagnosis of nodular basal cell carcinoma on the face. The lesion was previously treated with curettage and cautery/electrodessication (C&C) and has since recurred. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. On exam, there is a well-defined, primary, nodulo-cystic BCC measuring ≤1cm in diameter on the right cheek. The lesion is not close to any vital structures and is suitable for C&C followed by the application of Imiquimod cream to the base. The patient is considered compliant and physically able to apply the treatment. The patient is willing to participate in this pilot study as an alternative treatment option to reduce the recurrence rate of nodular BCCs on the face.

The patient is a 57-year-old Caucasian male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced esophageal cancer. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. He complains of difficulty swallowing and occasional chest pain. He has lost about 8kg in the last 2 months. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1 at the time of screening. He has no other significant medical history or ongoing medical conditions. His blood tests and imaging studies show no evidence of metastatic disease. He is willing and able to complete the fatigue and quality of life questionnaires. His BMI is 23, and his nutritional status SGA rating is A. He is currently not taking any medications or supplements. He is married and has three adult children. He works as a manager in a construction company. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his quality of life during preoperative chemoradiation therapy and to contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) through genetic testing. She has been experiencing muscle weakness and difficulty with mobility since the age of 2 years. She has been treated with physiotherapy and support devices such as braces and a wheelchair. She has not received any disease-modifying therapy for SMA. She is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the metabolome of patients with SMA before and after treatment with nusinersen to identify parameters that reflect the state of the disease and predict the response to gene therapy.

As this is a clinical trial for screening plasma pools from source plasma donors, there are no specific patient descriptions required. The study will be conducted on a minimum of 100,000 individual donor samples who fulfil criteria for plasma donation and are healthy adults aged between 18-65 years. There are no exclusion criteria mentioned other than not fulfilling criteria for plasma donation.

7-year-old male child who has difficulty with coordination and balance, often bumping into objects and tripping while walking or running. He has been diagnosed with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) and has difficulty with handwriting, buttoning clothes, and tying shoelaces. He is enrolled in a mainstream school and has no intellectual disabilities. The child is able to follow instructions and does not demonstrate excessive disruptive behavior. There is no history of neurological, musculoskeletal, or cognitive disorder that affects test performance. The child scores below the 16th percentile on the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2 (MABC-2). The parents have consented to the child participating in the clinical trial to investigate the effects of K Tape on walking pattern, muscle activity, and motor performance in children with DCD and typically developing children.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy with a history of atopic eczema that has been unresponsive to conventional therapies. He presents with dry, itchy, and flaky skin on his arms, legs, and face. His parents have tried various topical corticosteroids with little success. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. The patient's family history is significant for atopic conditions, including asthma and hay fever. The patient is generally healthy and active, with no known allergies or sensitivities. His parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial to try a new treatment for his eczema.

The patient is a 4-year-old male diagnosed with Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS) at the age of 1 year. He has experienced frequent infections, eczema, and thrombocytopenia. The patient has undergone multiple blood transfusions and immunoglobulin therapy. The patient's clinical score is 4, indicating severe disease. Molecular confirmation of the diagnosis has been made through WAS gene DNA sequencing. The patient has no HLA-genotypically identical bone marrow or 10/10 antigen HLA-matched unrelated donor or cord blood after a 3-month search. The patient's parents have signed informed consent for participation in the study. The patient is willing to return for follow-up and has no contraindications to leukapheresis or bone marrow harvest. The patient is not HIV positive.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who needs to undergo a surgical procedure that is expected to last around 30 minutes. She is generally healthy, but she has a history of mild hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is not allergic to any medications and has never experienced any adverse reactions to anesthesia. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married and has two children. She works as a nurse and is physically active, regularly engaging in moderate exercise. She has never experienced any back pain, and she has not had any neurological symptoms. Her height is 165 cm, and her weight is 70 kg (BMI: 25.71). She has no cognitive impairments, and her laboratory results are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the incidence of TNS between lidocaine and bupivacaine for spinal anesthesia.

The patient is a 25-year-old right-handed man who is fluent in English. He is in good health and has no history of heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has never been diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder and is not currently taking any medication for such conditions. He has no history of neurological or medical illness. He has not consumed any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the past two weeks or fluoxetine in the past five weeks. He does not have any metal in his body. He is interested in participating in the study to help further understand the effects of oxytocin on social processes. He understands the study requires an fMRI scan and administration of intranasal oxytocin or placebo. He is excited to contribute to the study and is willing to comply with all of the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a mastectomy and received adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Unfortunately, the cancer has returned and has now spread to the liver and bones. She is experiencing pain in her bones and has difficulty moving around. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new chemotherapy drug. She is in good general health, able to perform most activities of daily living and has no known allergies. She is not pregnant, nursing or planning to become pregnant. Her blood counts and liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. She has not received more than 2 prior chemotherapy treatments and has not had radiotherapy to the target lesion. She is willing to undergo daily oral medication and follow-up visits every 3 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who underwent a kidney transplant 4 years ago due to end-stage renal disease caused by systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). She has been on immunosuppressive therapy since then to prevent transplant rejection. She received the Pandemrix™ vaccine during the H1N1 pandemic in 2009 and has also received seasonal influenza vaccinations annually. She has had no prior episodes of solid organ transplant rejection since her transplant surgery. The patient is currently being followed up at a transplant clinic and her medical records are available in the Clinical Practice Research Datalink GP Online Database (CPRD GOLD). She has provided written informed consent to participate in this study.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of advanced colon cancer presents with a complaint of fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past year. He reports no significant medical history other than colon cancer. He drinks alcohol occasionally and has never smoked. He has no history of thromboembolic disease. His ECOG performance status is 1. His most recent CT scan shows the progression of the disease. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

45 yo F with a recent diagnosis of unifocal ductal carcinoma in situ of the left breast with no invasive component. The patient underwent complete microscopic excision with a minimum radial margin of 1 mm by specimen x-ray within the past 2 months. The maximum microscopic tumor diameter is 20 mm and the tumor grade is 2. The patient is planning to receive adjuvant tamoxifen for 5 years. Hormone receptor status is Estrogen receptor positive with more than 10% tumor staining for the receptor. The patient has no prior history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolus and there is no contraindication to full-dose radiotherapy to the breast. No other cancer has been reported within the past 5 years. The patient is not on concurrent anticoagulants.

The patient is a 25-year-old Japanese male with a BMI between 18 and 27 kg/m^2. He is in good general health with no history of chronic or acute illnesses. He has not consumed alcohol within the last 48 hours and does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. He does not smoke more than 10 cigarettes per day and is willing to refrain from smoking during the 3 days prior to dosing and during the confinement period. He has no known allergies to the trial product or related products. The patient has not tested positive for Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibodies, or HIV antibodies. He has no clinically relevant abnormalities of physical examination, laboratory values, vital signs, or ECG findings at the screening. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to help advance medical research and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 56-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) came to the clinic seeking treatment options. He has a history of smoking and has already undergone two prior therapies, including platinum doublet and immunotherapy, but was refractory to both. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a predicted life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has measurable disease as defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) criteria (Version 1.1, 2009). He is currently taking anti-hypertensive drugs and has no known allergies to any medications. He is willing and able to comply with required scheduled visits and study procedures.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who presented with a persistent cough, fever and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with Covid-19 based on a positive SARS-CoV-2 test and was admitted to the Västerås Hospital Intensive Care Unit due to severe respiratory distress. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled on medication. He has never smoked and does not consume alcohol. The patient's oxygen saturation levels have been fluctuating and he has required increasing amounts of oxygen support. He is currently being treated with antiviral medication and corticosteroids. Despite treatment, the patient's condition has not improved and he is currently in critical condition. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and provide consent for the collection and analysis of his data.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman scheduled for elective total knee replacement surgery. She has a history of hypertension, but her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. She has no history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. The patient has not had a myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke within the last 6 months prior to randomization. She does not have a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or allergy to heparins. She has not experienced intracerebral or intraocular bleeding within the last 6 months prior to randomization. She has not had any gastrointestinal disease with gastrointestinal bleeding within the last 6 months prior to randomization. The patient does not have a history of an impaired absorption of the study drug. She has not had an amputation of one leg. She does not have heart insufficiency NYHA III-IV, congenital or acquired haemorrhagic diathesis, thrombocytopenia, macroscopic hematuria, allergy to contrast media, severe hypertension, impaired liver function, impaired renal function, active malignant disease, presence of active peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal disease with increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding, body weight less than 45 kg, or drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is not currently receiving therapy with oral anticoagulants, fibrinolytic therapy or therapy with acetylic salicylic acid or other thrombocyte aggregation inhibitors. She is not on any other drugs influencing coagulation. The patient is not planning to receive planned intermittent pneumatic compression during the active treatment period or planned epidural anesthesia with indwelling epidural catheter. She is not currently participating in another clinical trial or study.

A 35-year-old female presented with a history of recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, and irregular bowel movements for the last 2 years. She reported alternating episodes of diarrhea and constipation with the frequency of 3-4 bowel movements per day. She also reported increased symptoms during stressful periods. She has tried a low FODMAP diet, probiotics, and over-the-counter medications with minimal relief. She denied any rectal bleeding, weight loss or fever. Physical examination was unremarkable. She was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) based on Rome III criteria. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or previous abdominal surgeries. She was not on any antibiotics, probiotics or laxatives in the last 4 weeks. She was scheduled for colonoscopy examination as part of the study. She signed the informed consent and agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who suffered from a stroke 6 years ago. Since then, he has been experiencing difficulty in walking and performing daily activities due to weakness and spasticity in his right leg. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He is a retired engineer and spends most of his day sitting at home. He has not been able to participate in any physical activities due to his condition. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 28. He has been attending stroke support groups and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve his physical and cognitive abilities.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been hospitalized with COVID-19 pneumonia. He presents with shortness of breath, cough, fever, and fatigue. The patient has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is currently single and has no children. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written consent. His chest X-ray and CT scan indicate the presence of pneumonia. The patient has no record of HIV or AIDS, liver cirrhosis, or any other serious chronic disease. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is above 30 ml/min. His QTcB or QTcF is within the normal range. He has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 3 months. The patient is eligible for diagnosis/evaluation to chest X-ray or chest CT.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and is currently experiencing a depressive episode. She has been taking an antidepressant medication for the past 4 weeks at a therapeutic dose, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She does not have a history of bipolar disorder or current psychotic symptoms, and has not been diagnosed with substance or alcohol dependence. She reports occasional thoughts of suicide, but does not have a HAM-D item 3 score of ≥ 3. She has never been treated with tricyclic antidepressants or monoamine oxidase inhibitors. She does not have Diabetes Mellitus. She is willing to participate in the 6-week clinical trial and agrees to regularly enter information on symptom severity and functional impairment into a handheld computer.

This clinical trial is not applicable for patient recruitment as it's a registry study and does not involve direct patient participation. It aims to gather data on patients who require ECMO in Australia and New Zealand to identify best practices and improve patient outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing auditory verbal hallucinations for the past 3 years that have not responded to antipsychotic medications. She has a history of alcohol and opiate abuse but has been sober for the past year. She completed elementary school and is currently unemployed. She has no history of stroke, heart failure, head injury, infection, or brain tumor. She does not have neurological focal deficits such as hemiparesis and cranial nerve paresis. Her cognitive function is within normal limits (MMSE score of 28). She has normal hearing and has no history of mental retardation. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and sign the informed consent document.

A 12-year-old Hispanic boy was referred to the Clinic with a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis, which was confirmed by a biopsy. He has been experiencing diarrhea, abdominal pain, and bloody stools for the past 6 months. He has been previously treated with Mesalamine, but he has difficulty complying with the multiple doses a day regimen due to school activities. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history. He is able to swallow tablets without difficulty. The patient and his parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial that would allow him to take Mesalamine once a day, to see if it is as effective as the multiple doses a day regimen in preventing clinical relapse of ulcerative colitis.

A 45-year-old male patient is admitted to the emergency room of FEMH with complaints of shortness of breath and cough. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a smoker and has been smoking for the past 20 years. On examination, he is found to be tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min and his oxygen saturation is 85% on room air. His chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates suggestive of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The patient is started on invasive mechanical ventilation and transferred to the medical intensive care unit. The patient's family is informed about the clinical trial and they provide their consent for the patient's participation. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who suffered a brain injury due to a car accident 2 years ago. The injury affected subcortical brain regions, resulting in difficulty in regulating emotions, as well as cognitive and motor deficits. Despite undergoing rehabilitation therapy, the patient still experiences difficulty in processing information and has occasional mood swings. The patient is fluent in English and has no hearing impairment. There are no implanted metal devices or cardiac pacemaker. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to explore the potential benefits of tDCS on subcortical brain functioning.

A 26-year old woman in her 28th week of gestation was admitted to the hospital with signs of preterm labor. She had no past medical history and was a non-smoker. She is married and lives with her husband. This is her first pregnancy. She had a normal prenatal course until her admission to the hospital. She was given tocolytic therapy and was monitored for any further signs of labor. The patient's condition worsened, and she delivered a baby boy at 28 weeks gestational age. The infant was intubated and received mechanical ventilation. The infant was diagnosed with Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) and required surfactant therapy. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Curosurf and Survanta in improving lung function and survival rates and reducing the complications of prematurity in very premature infants < 30 weeks gestational age at birth.

Patient is a female aged 25 who has not had a cervical cytology specimen collected within the last 4 months, has not had a prior complete or partial hysterectomy involving removal of the cervix, and has not had any chemical compounds applied to the cervical area 24 hours prior to study entry. The patient has not undergone any conization, Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), cervical laser surgery or cryosurgery on the cervix in the last twelve months and has not been enrolled in a cervical disease diagnostic trial since 2007. The patient is willing to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple blunt force injuries. Upon arrival to the emergency department, the patient presented with a drop in hematocrit of more than 10 points, requiring transfusion of 8 units of packed RBCs. The patient's injury severity score was 17 and serum lactate was 4 mmol/L. The patient was also hypotensive with a mean arterial blood pressure of 55 mmHg and systolic arterial blood pressure of 85 mmHg. The patient has no known pre-existing medical conditions and is not pregnant. The patient was admitted to the emergency department within 4 hours after the onset of trauma. The patient has provided consent to participate in the study.

Maria is a 55 year old woman who has a history of hypertension and diabetes. She is scheduled to undergo cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) due to aortic valve stenosis. She is currently taking metformin and lisinopril for her medical conditions. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 ml/min. Her family history is significant for cardiovascular disease, but negative for kidney disease. She has no known allergies to medications. Four hours after the CPB procedure, her urinary [TIMP-2]*[IGFBP7] level is 0.5. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing memory problems and difficulty in performing daily activities for the past year. He is married and has two children. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He previously worked as an accountant and has a high school education. He speaks English fluently and has no difficulty in communication. He has no history of significant medical or neurological illnesses. His physical examination, laboratory tests, vital signs, and ECG are all within normal limits. He has not undergone any investigational medicinal product within the last 30 days. He is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who experiences pain and stiffness in her hands, especially in the morning. She reports difficulty with gripping and carrying objects. She has been previously diagnosed with hand osteoarthritis by her primary care physician. She has no known history of rheumatic disease or active gastrointestinal ulcers. She is not allergic to analgesic drugs. She is currently using over-the-counter pain relievers to manage her symptoms with moderate success, but is interested in trying a new treatment option. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol requirements.

Patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of multiple myeloma. He has had three different lines of therapy with previous exposure to PI, IMiDs, and a CD38 antibody. He is currently experiencing relapsed/refractory disease and has been refractory to his last line of therapy. He has measurable disease and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has no history of central nervous system disease, adequate liver and renal function, and adequate bone marrow function. He has no active infections within the last 72 hours and no significant co-morbid conditions that would place him at undue risk or interfere with the study. The patient has not had a bone marrow transplant, has not received gene therapy-based therapy for cancer, or BCMA-targeted therapy. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of plasma cell leukemia, active plasma cell leukemia, Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia, POEMS, or clinically significant amyloidosis.

Mary is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her right knee for the past year. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried various non-surgical treatments such as physiotherapy, painkillers, and corticosteroid injections without any significant improvement. She works as a teacher and her job requires her to stand for long periods of time. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history or allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no family history of arthritis or joint replacement. She is willing to participate in the fast-track surgery program and is able to provide informed consent. She has no contralateral knee arthroplasty and has no plans of becoming pregnant during the study period. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

50-year-old male with a history of locally advanced rectal cancer with threatened circumferential resection margin (CRM) or recurrent rectal cancer. The tumor has been clinically diagnosed as T3 or T4. The patient has no history of other malignancies in the past five years and has not been diagnosed with peritoneal metastases or distant metastases. The patient is willing and able to practice effective contraception during the study and for at least 30 days after their last dose of study treatment. The patient has no laboratory abnormalities that would exclude them from the trial and is willing and able to give signed informed consent before study-specific procedures. The patient has not received previous administration of SGM-101.

45-year-old male diagnosed with bronchiectasis for the past 3 years. He has had recurrent chest infections, shortness of breath, and cough with sputum production. He has been on inhaled bronchodilators, inhaled steroids, and antibiotics intermittently. He is a non-smoker and has no other known medical problems. He reports difficulty with physical activity and daily tasks due to his symptoms. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the potential benefits of yoga training on his functional capacity and quality of life. He has not had an acute exacerbation in the past 3 weeks and does not have any known systemic, orthopedic or neurological disease.

The patient is a 22-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 29. He has a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in saturated fat and processed foods. He is looking to improve his metabolic health and reduce his risk for future disease. He has no history of diabetes or cardiovascular problems, but his blood pressure is slightly elevated (130/80 mmHg). He does not smoke or consume alcohol heavily. He is proficient in reading English and is able to ingest the supplement or placebo.

John is a 62 year old man who has been diagnosed with advanced head and neck cancer. He has completed the previous late phase 2 study (CA139-388) and his treating physician has determined that he should continue therapy with paclitaxel. He has undergone prior treatment with radiation therapy and chemotherapy. He has a history of smoking and alcohol use, but has since quit both. He reports occasional difficulty swallowing and hoarseness. Physical exam shows a mass in his neck and enlarged lymph nodes. Lab studies show elevated tumor markers. Despite prior treatment, the cancer has progressed and he is seeking access to paclitaxel therapy through this clinical trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is scheduled to undergo non-urgent PCI for coronary artery disease. He weighs 80 kg and has a measured creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min. He has not received a clopidogrel loading dose in the last 30 days and is not currently taking any thrombolytic agents, fondaparinux, or oral anticoagulants. He has no history of bleeding disorders or known intracranial vascular malformation. He is able to read and give written informed consent and has signed an informed consent form approved by the Investigator's IRB/IEC.

63 year old male diagnosed with rare cholangiocarcinoma with metastases to the liver and bones. He was initially treated with chemotherapy and achieved partial response. However, he developed progression in one of his liver metastases and a new lesion in his left femur. A biopsy of the femur lesion confirmed metastatic cholangiocarcinoma. The patient has an ECOG score of 1 and a life expectancy estimated to be greater than 6 months. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial with a total of 2 oligometastases (1 in liver and 1 in bone). The radiation oncologist believes that he is a suitable candidate for SBRT to both sites of disease, and the patient has agreed to participate in the trial after being provided with informed consent according to ICH/GCP regulations.

A 72-year-old woman who is currently residing in a long-term care facility is experiencing incontinence-associated dermatitis. She has been incontinent for the past few months and has been using moisture barrier pastes to protect her skin, but her skin remains red and painful. She has severe Category 2 Incontinence-Associated Dermatitis (IAD) with skin erosion and denudation, which is affecting her buttocks and thighs. She is willing to have photographs taken of her skin and permit the use of the photographs in potential publication. The woman is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any known allergies to acrylates or cyanoacrylates. She is willing to sign an Institutional Review Board-approved informed consent/assent document and authorize the use and disclosure of protected health information. She has not received antifungal powders or cyanoacrylate-based skin protectant in the area affected by IAD within 24 or 72 hours prior to the screening visit, respectively. Her caretakers are willing to discontinue the use of Dimethicone-containing wipes and Chlorhexidine Gluconate wipes on the area where the skin protectant product will be applied. Her medical condition does not exclude her from participating in the study.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of chronic hepatitis C and liver cirrhosis presents for screening in this clinical trial. She reports a long history of alcohol abuse, but she has been sober for the past year. She takes medications for hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She has no other significant medical history and reports no recent hospitalizations. She has not had any major bleeding episodes in the last 6 months and has had no recent antibiotic use or Clostridium difficile infection. She is willing to abstain from alcohol and limit nicotine use for the study. Her hepatic impairment has been classified as moderate (Child-Pugh score of 8). She has a platelet count of 40,000 × 10^9/L and has no active bacterial infection or hepatopulmonary or hepatorenal syndrome. She has not participated in a clinical trial within the last 30 days and has not taken gepotidacin in the last 12 months. She is able to provide informed consent and agrees to comply with all study procedures.

A 27-year-old male comes to the clinic with a complaint of severe pain in his lower jaw after a road accident. He has a history of good oral hygiene and no medical or surgical history. Physical examination reveals severe tenderness over the anterior mandible with the presence of an obvious step deformity. There is no other facial injury or neurosensory deficit. Radiographs show a displaced anterior mandible fracture without any other facial bone fractures. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no systemic disease. He is willing to undergo surgery for fracture fixation.

A 10-year-old male patient presented with persistent episodes of painful crises in the lower extremities and hands, which started 2 years ago. The episodes occur every 2-3 months and last for several days. The patient also complains of burning sensations in the hands and feet, fatigue, and difficulty exercising. The patient has a past medical history of proteinuria and recurrent urinary tract infections. The family history is significant for Fabry disease in the patient's maternal grandfather. Physical examination reveals acroparesthesia, telangiectasia, and angiokeratoma on both lower extremities. No neurological deficits, heart murmurs, or hepatosplenomegaly were identified. Laboratory tests reveal low levels of alpha-galactosidase A in the serum and leukocytes, and genetic testing confirms a pathogenic mutation in the GLA gene. The patient has not received any enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in the past.

A 55-year-old woman living in Bologna has been diagnosed with primary coxarthrosis and is currently waiting for total hip arthroplasty. She reports a severe pain level that is rated at an 8 on the Numeric Rating Scale. She has been experiencing pain for several months and it has been affecting her daily activities such as walking and standing for extended periods of time. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore non-surgical options to manage her pain and improve her functional performance before and after the surgery.

A 43-year-old male patient is admitted to the emergency department with multiple fractures after a motorcycle accident. The patient reports a history of chronic lower back pain and has been taking oxycodone 30 mg every 4 hours for the past year. Upon admission, the patient reports a pain score of 8 out of 10 and has received 80 mg of oxycodone in the first 24 hours. The patient reports occasional recreational use of marijuana but denies habitual or chronic usage. The patient is willing to divulge marijuana usage and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient has no known allergies to drugs and is not on a pain management agreement. The patient is not NPO and has not received or is not expected to receive neuraxial/locoregional blocks for pain within the next 48 hours. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not incarcerated.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III colorectal cancer. She has undergone a radical operation to remove the tumor and is now scheduled to begin postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy. The patient reports feeling tired and weak, and has lost weight over the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medications for both conditions. The patient reports that she has always been relatively healthy and active, but has struggled with maintaining a healthy diet since her cancer diagnosis. She is interested in participating in the trial to explore the effect of nutrition support in colorectal cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. The patient is able to give informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman with hormone receptor positive breast cancer who has failed prior treatment with letrozole or anastrozole. She presented with a breast lump and biopsy confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma. She underwent breast-conserving surgery and sentinel lymph node biopsy, which showed no evidence of axillary nodal involvement. She received adjuvant radiation therapy and was started on adjuvant letrozole. However, after 6 months, she developed progressive disease in the form of multiple liver metastases. She underwent liver-directed therapy and was started on everolimus, but developed stomatitis and had to discontinue the medication. She is now being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial to receive real-time pharmacokinetic therapeutic drug monitoring to prevent stomatitis from developing while maintaining the effectiveness of everolimus to treat her cancer. She is in good general health with ECOG performance status 1, and has adequate bone marrow, renal, and liver function. She has signed informed consent and is willing to use adequate birth control during the study and for 8 weeks after the end of treatment.

The patient is a 25 year old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help understand and prevent infectious diarrhea caused by Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC). She has no significant medical history and no clinically significant physical examination findings or laboratory abnormalities. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to participate after informed consent is obtained. She is available for the entire study duration and can attend all planned follow-up visits. She has not received any vaccinations or investigational products within the last 30 days and has not had a confirmed ETEC infection or cholera infection in the last 3 years. She has not handled ETEC or Vibrio cholerae in her occupation currently or in the past 3 years. She has not experienced symptoms consistent with Travelers' Diarrhea concurrent with travel or planned travel to countries where ETEC infection is endemic. She is not currently taking any medication known to affect the immune function and is not allergic to ciprofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, or amoxicillin.

A 10-day-old Chinese male infant was referred to the hospital due to uncontrolled seizures that started shortly after birth. The seizures manifested as sudden, jerky movements of the limbs and face, and lasted for several seconds to minutes. The infant had no previous history of seizure disorder, and the pregnancy and delivery were unremarkable. The infant was born at full term with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. The infant is currently being breastfed and is growing well. The family has no history of seizure disorder or other neurological diseases. The infant was diagnosed with neonatal seizure by EEG and is eligible for participation in the epidemiology study on neonatal seizure. The parents have provided their consent for their infant's participation in the study.

The patient is a 55 year old man with a history of coronary artery disease and previous stent placement. He presents with recurrent chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. His cardiac workup reveals in-stent restenosis and he is deemed eligible for interventional therapy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of paclitaxel-eluting PTCA-balloon catheter versus paclitaxel-eluting stent Taxus® Liberte for the treatment of coronary in-stent restenosis. He has not experienced a myocardial infarction within the last week and does not have severe congestive heart failure or valvular heart disease. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including follow-up visits and clinical assessments. The patient is currently taking aspirin and clopidogrel and has not experienced any adverse reactions to these medications. He meets the lesion criteria for the study, with a stenosis diameter of ≥70% or ≥50% accompanied by ischemia and a target lesion >10mm in length. The patient does not have any other co-morbidities that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer. She was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 3 years ago and underwent lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. She completed endocrine therapy with tamoxifen for 2 years and was switched to an aromatase inhibitor. She was doing well until she started experiencing cough and chest pain. Her chest X-ray revealed multiple lung nodules, and a biopsy confirmed metastatic breast cancer. She was treated with first-line chemotherapy with docetaxel and trastuzumab for 6 months, which was stopped due to disease progression. She then received second-line chemotherapy with capecitabine for 3 months, which was also stopped due to disease progression. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her metastatic breast cancer. Her performance status is 1, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets all the eligibility criteria except that she received prior sunitinib for a different cancer.

A 30-year-old woman who is a first-time mother gave birth to a healthy baby girl yesterday. She has decided to breastfeed her baby and has been doing so since then. She has no history of medical problems and has had a normal pregnancy with no complications. The baby has been healthy since birth and has been feeding well. Both the mother and baby are expected to be dismissed from the hospital together in the next 24 hours. The mother is willing to participate in the study to help identify any potential risk factors related to breastfeeding that may affect her baby's health.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer approximately 18 months ago. He underwent a Whipple procedure and adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. However, his cancer has progressed and he is now experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. He has a performance status of 1 and is still able to perform his daily activities, but with some difficulty. He is married with two children, and works as a small business owner. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in any potential treatment options that may improve his prognosis and quality of life.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has a history of kidney disease and has been on long-term glucocorticoid treatment for the past 2 years. He presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and a fever that has lasted for the past 5 days. He also complains of chest pain when breathing deeply. He has a weak immune system due to his medical condition and treatment. He has never smoked and reports no alcohol consumption. He has no significant family history of lung or infectious diseases. Upon physical examination, his oxygen saturation is low, and his lung sounds are diminished. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. His blood pressure is normal, and his heart rate is slightly elevated. His chest X-ray shows signs of pneumonia. His laboratory tests reveal low lymphocyte counts and elevated levels of CD55, HBP, and CD64. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to validate the predictive effects of these markers on severe pneumonia and to explore new diagnostic and treatment strategies to improve patient outcomes.

A 42-year-old male patient was diagnosed with neuroendocrine tumour (NET) of the small intestine. He has been on a stable dose of lanreotide Autogel 120mg every 28 days for the past 6 months to manage his carcinoid symptoms. He is in a committed relationship and his partner has agreed to administer the injections during the self-administration period. He has no history of hypersensitivity to the Investigational Medicinal Product or drugs with similar chemical structure. He has no other medical conditions that might jeopardize his safety or the chance of obtaining satisfactory data for the study. He is competent in injection technique, as judged by the investigator. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a long history of coronary heart disease and severe angina. He experiences chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue during physical activity, which limits his ability to perform daily tasks. He has tried multiple medications to alleviate his symptoms, but they have been ineffective. He has an ejection fraction of 30% and is not a candidate for direct coronary revascularization methods such as CABG or PCI. He has no history of bleeding disorders, arrhythmias, or implanted pacemakers or defibrillators. He is willing to undergo surgical procedures and general anesthesia. He is able and willing to adhere to the study tests and procedures and authorize the use of his PHI.

28-year-old female with no significant medical history, non-smoker, with no alcohol or drug abuse history, presents as a healthy volunteer for the clinical trial. The patient has not participated in any other investigational drug trial for at least 2 months prior to the administration. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, hormonal, or central nervous system disorders. The patient has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to BIBV 308 SE or any of its excipients. The patient is not taking any medication that might influence the results of the trial or drugs with a long half-life (> 24 hours) for at least 1 month prior to administration. The patient has normal blood pressure, pulse rate, and ECG findings during the medical examination.

This is a 29 year-old female who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28-30 days and has never been pregnant before. Her BMI is 24 kg/m2 and she has no known medical conditions. Her FSH levels are within normal limits (5 IU/l). She has never been diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome or endometriosis. She has never undergone IVF before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may increase her chances of conceiving.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a history of coronary artery disease and severe left ventricular dysfunction. He has been experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue with minimal exertion for the past few months. His ejection fraction (EF) is 35%. He is a retired construction worker who used to smoke but has quit for the past 10 years. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father and two brothers having experienced heart attacks in their 50s. He is currently taking aspirin, a beta-blocker, and a statin drug. He has no other significant medical history and does not have any allergies. He is considering undergoing revascularization and has been informed about the possibility of participating in a clinical trial comparing on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting by ventricular assist.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing allergic reactions after consuming certain types of food. She has a history of seasonal allergies and asthma. She presents with symptoms such as itchy skin rashes, hives, and difficulty breathing. Her recent allergy tests reveal that she is allergic to several types of nuts, wheat, and soy. She has never consumed hemp seeds before, but her work as a farmer exposes her to hemp plants. She is curious about the potential benefits of consuming hemp seeds and wants to know if she has any allergies to them. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo prick-tests to determine her sensitivity to hemp seeds. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is fluent in French and able to provide informed consent.

62-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with blurry vision in her left eye for the past few months. She denied any trauma or history of ocular surgery. Upon examination, the patient was found to have a full-thickness macular hole in her left eye with a visual acuity of 20/200. OCT imaging revealed a stage 3 macular hole. The patient was scheduled for surgery for idiopathic macular hole (MH) and was enrolled in the clinical trial. She was randomized to the small extent group and underwent a standard 3-port pars plana vitrectomy with a 23-gauge vitrectomy system. The internal limiting membrane (ILM) was peeled in round shape with the radius of 0.75-disc diameter centering at the center of the MH. The patient maintained a face-down position for at least 5 days postoperatively. Postoperative measurements of BCVA and M-score were conducted at 2- and 6-month follow-up visits by independent masked observers, and OCT scans were conducted at follow-up visits 2 and 6 months postoperatively.

A 56-year-old male presented to the emergency department with chest pain and was diagnosed with non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). He had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and was on medication for both conditions. He had never experienced chest pain before and denied any family history of cardiovascular disease. His electrocardiogram showed ST segment depression in leads V2-V6 and cardiac biomarkers were elevated. He underwent a baseline coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) as part of the Incident COronary EveNts Identified by Computed Tomography (ICONIC) trial. He was enrolled as a case in the study due to his NSTEMI diagnosis and the presence of baseline CCTA. He has not undergone any previous coronary artery revascularization procedures or had a prior history of myocardial infarction. He was not excluded from the study due to his medical history and met all inclusion criteria.

50-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction, who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement. The patient now presents with angina, which has been increasing in frequency and severity over the past few weeks. The patient is scheduled for a coronary angiogram which shows a chronic total occlusion (CTO) in a non-infarct related coronary artery. The patient has previously undergone failed attempts to cross the CTO with a conventional guidewire. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of renal or liver disease, and no known allergies to contrast agents or antiplatelet agents. The patient has a BMI of 28 and a left ventricle ejection fraction of 50%. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a novel device called NovaCross that may help cross his CTO lesion.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of persistent asthma for the past 5 years. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) at a stable dose for the past 30 days. She has no history of life-threatening asthma exacerbations, hospitalizations or systemic corticosteroid use for the past 30 days. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements, including withholding rescue medication for at least 6 hours before spirometry is performed in each visit. The patient has a BMI within the 5th and 97th percentiles for her age and gender, with a weight of 130 pounds. She has no known hypersensitivity to any corticosteroid or salmeterol. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past 2 years. The patient is capable of understanding the requirements, risks, and benefits of study participation and has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old Korean male with a history of glioblastoma, who has already undergone the standard Stupp regimen (temozolomide-radiation therapy followed by adjuvant temozolomide) and is now experiencing recurrent/ refractory glioblastoma. The patient has a confirmed methylated MGMT promoter and a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 70%.
