The patient has not received any chemotherapy for at least two weeks and has adequate hematological, liver, and renal functions. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient does not have any evidence of active infection or leptomeningeal metastasis and is able to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl studying in a medium urbanization school in the north region of Taiwan. She has no history of any ocular disease and is not using orthokeratology. Her parents have no history of myopia or any other ocular disease. She is willing to participate in the study and complete all the screening procedures. She has no known allergies and is in good general health.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. He has been experiencing bowel movement accidents and has not achieved continence. His caregivers have tried various interventions in the past, but none have been successful. He has no history of intestinal surgeries or concurrent enuresis. The patient's gastroenterologist has cleared him for the use of glycerin suppository, bisacodyl suppository, and senna. The caregiver is willing to give consent/assent for the study.

A 62-year-old male presents with a history of urothelial carcinoma involving the ureter and renal pelvis. He has previously undergone endoscopic treatment, but residual or recurrent cancer has been confirmed. He is ineligible, unwilling or refusing to undergo surgical management by resection of involved kidney or ureter. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 60%. He is currently taking prophylactic anticoagulation but his treating physician believes it is safe to temporarily withhold anticoagulation during the study. His organ function is within normal limits, with a calculated creatinine clearance of 55 ml/min, total serum bilirubin of 1.2 mg/dL, and AST/ALT within normal limits. He is able to provide written informed consent. The patient is a non-smoker and has not received any systemic therapy (including chemotherapy, biologic therapy, or immunotherapy) ≤4 weeks prior to treatment. He is willing to use contraception while on the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with metastatic colon cancer confirmed by biopsy. She has been on chemotherapy treatment for the past year with no significant improvement in her condition. She experiences abdominal pain, bloating, and frequent diarrhea. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. Her family history is negative for any cancer. Her current medications include oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin. She has no known allergies. She is willing to provide extra blood samples during her routine blood draws for the purpose of this clinical trial. She signs the informed consent form and is ready to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was diagnosed with melanoma that has spread to other parts of her body. She has already received treatment with ipilimumab and adjuvant anti-PD1 therapy but did not respond well. She has not previously been treated with BRAF inhibitors (vemurafenib, dabrafenib, encorafenib), MEK inhibitors (selumetinib, trametinib, binimetinib, cobimetinib), and/or anti-PD1/PDL1 monoclonal antibodies for metastatic or unresectable disease. She has a measurable disease, defined as at least one lesion

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain in her neck and back for the past 6 months. The pain is rated as a 7 out of 10 on a pain scale and has been impacting her daily life. She has tried taking over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided relief. She has no history of cancer or other medical conditions that would limit her life expectancy. She owns an Android smartphone with a data plan and is able to read and speak English. She has not tried more than 3 analgesic medications for her pain. She is willing to collaborate with her clinician to try personalized pain treatments using the Trialist app to find a more effective treatment.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 5 years ago. He has undergone a radical prostatectomy and adjuvant radiation therapy but has since developed metastatic disease with rising PSA levels. He has been treated with docetaxel chemotherapy and abiraterone but has now progressed with rising PSA levels. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no other significant medical history. He has a serum PSA level of 50 ng/ml and is eligible for this clinical trial. He will undergo pre-study assessments including CT scans, bone scans, and blood tests. Mitotane will be administered to him starting at 1.5g daily and escalated to a maximum of 5g daily based on serum levels and tolerability. He will be monitored for toxicity and response to therapy throughout the course of the trial. The aim of the trial is to assess the feasibility, safety, and response rate of mitotane treatment in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

Maria is a 48 year old woman who is in the late peri-menopausal period. She has been experiencing vaginal dryness for the past six months, which has led to discomfort and pain during intercourse. She has not had any vaginal bleeding or discharge. Maria has a body mass index of 26. She is sexually active and uses a lubricated condom as a contraceptive. She has never used any hormonal therapy for menopause. Her medical history is unremarkable with no known allergies. She is not currently under any medication and has not participated in any clinical study or used any investigational agents in the past 30 days. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and sign the informed consent.

Patient is a 12-month-old boy who is currently up-to-date on all his routine vaccinations. He is being seen at the study site during the study period of Nov. 1, 2011, through March 31, 2012, and will receive trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (TIV) and 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) concomitantly. His parent has a cell phone with text messaging capabilities and speaks English. The patient has not received any antipyretics in the 6-hour period prior to vaccination, and there is no stated intent to use prophylactic antipyretics at the time of vaccination before the development of a fever. The patient has not received trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (TIV) or 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) in the seven days prior to enrollment date.

A 32-year-old Caucasian male, 5'10" tall, and weighs 190 pounds will be screened for eligibility for the clinical trial. He is generally healthy and has no history of chronic medical conditions. He reports no known allergies to medications or any history of autoimmune disorders. He is not on any medications, and he does not have any ongoing infections. The patient denies any history of cancer or blood disorders requiring immunosuppression. His family history is negative for any autoimmune or blood disorders. He has no history of splenomegaly or abdominal tenderness. He has no signs of cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, or pulmonary disease. The patient does not have any latex allergy. He has never had a reaction to Filgrastim, lidocaine, or any other numbing agent. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

Pt is a 55yo M with a confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis, based on positive RT-PCR and a highly suggestive thoracic CT scan. The patient is experiencing severe hypoxemia and requires intensive care for acute respiratory failure. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known comorbidities. The patient is currently receiving standardized care for COVID-19, including ventilation, sedation, and antimicrobial treatment. The patient will be enrolled in a clinical trial to assess the longitudinal immune response to the virus and its potential association with disease outcomes. The study will involve a series of blood tests to monitor the patient's innate and adaptive immune response, including the number and function of monocytes and lymphocytes, as well as their ability to be stimulated by SARS-CoV-2 viral proteins.

A 35-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia with high-risk cytogenetics. She has completed several cycles of chemotherapy with no significant response. Her performance status is 1, and she is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Her family members have been tested for HLA match, and her sister was found to be a 6/6 match. Her sister is a healthy 28-year-old female with no significant medical history. She has agreed to donate stem cells for the transplant procedure. The patient will undergo induction chemotherapy with fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, etoposide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone for several cycles. She may also receive rituximab if she has CD20+ malignancies. Conditioning chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine will be given before the infusion of stem cells. Methotrexate and cyclosporine will be used to prevent graft-versus-host disease. The patient will be monitored closely for several weeks after the transplant and will have frequent follow-up visits

The patient is a 60 year-old male who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been recommended to undergo Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) surgery. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has a history of smoking and is trying to quit. He is able to walk for short distances but experiences chest pain and shortness of breath upon exertion. He has no history of diabetes or other significant medical conditions. He has agreed to participate in the study to help develop a method for converting Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain and mobility scores to EuroQol-5Dimensions-3Levels (EQ-5D-3L) answers. He will undergo the CABG surgery with the use of a vein segment for conduit. He will be asked to complete the EQ-5D-3L questionnaire postoperatively to evaluate his quality of life.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He underwent successful electrocardioversion and is now interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent recurrence of atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not excessively. He is not currently taking any supplements or following a special diet. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. He is willing to comply with the diet recommendations and follow-up requirements of the study.

A 28-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is experiencing mild depression and anxiety symptoms characterized by feelings of sadness, loss of interest, and excessive worry. He is currently taking medications for CF, including pancreatic enzymes, bronchodilators, and antibiotics. He has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been hospitalized twice in the last year due to respiratory exacerbations. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has completed high school and is currently employed in a customer service role. English is his primary language. He reports feeling overwhelmed with managing his CF treatments and has difficulty managing his emotions related to his chronic illness. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a cognitive-behavioral therapy intervention to help manage his depression and anxiety symptoms.

80-year-old male with a history of hypertension and mild cognitive impairment was diagnosed with chronic subdural hematoma after a fall resulting in a minor head trauma. The patient underwent a unilateral burr-hole craniostomy and is now scheduled for postoperative treatment. The patient has the ability to take medication on his own and has no known allergies. The patient has been informed of the study and is willing to participate.

A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman was recently diagnosed with hormone receptor positive breast cancer. She underwent surgery for the breast cancer and completed chemotherapy four weeks ago. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating some limitations in her daily activities. Her blood work shows adequate haematological, renal, and hepatic function. She has no evidence of metastasis. She has not undergone metachronous bilateral breast cancer and has not been diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer. She has not received any hormone therapy or hormonal replacement therapy within the previous four weeks, except for Estring, Vagifem, or Estrogen Cream. She has not had gastrectomy, small bowel resection, malabsorption syndrome, or dysphagia. She has estrogen and/or progesterone receptor-positive breast cancer.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with a history of acute onset right lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He was diagnosed with acute appendicitis and is scheduled for a Lanz incision appendectomy. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He denies any allergies. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any recreational drugs. His vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is informed about the study and has given consent to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who came to the emergency department with a superficial laceration on her forearm that requires suturing. She has a history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She denies any known allergies to medications. She is conscious, alert, and oriented to person, place, and time, with no distracting pain in other locations. She is not intoxicated or comatose and is not under guardianship. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she confirms that she is using adequate contraceptive measures. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

John is a 28 year old male who works as a construction worker. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of drug addiction. He has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2. He has no history of alcoholism or serious gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic or cardiovascular disease, tuberculosis, epilepsy, asthma, diabetes, psychosis or glaucoma. John has not donated blood or plasma in the last thirty days and has not taken any investigational drug within the same time period. He is not pregnant and is unable to become pregnant. He has undergone a general physical examination within the last 28 days and has been found to be in good health. His blood pressure and other clinical laboratory tests are all within the normal range. John is interested in participating in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who is scheduled for elective Hypospadias repair. The patient's past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known allergies to medications. The patient is in good general health with an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I. The patient's parents have been fully informed of the trial and have given written consent for their child's participation. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and is able to follow instructions. The patient has no coagulation disorder, major malformations of the lower spine or meninges, or any cutaneous or subcutaneous lesion at the site of injection.

A 65-year-old male patient is scheduled for an elective endovascular repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He is currently taking aspirin, a beta-blocker, and a statin. The patient has undergone a preoperative CT angiogram which revealed a 5 cm AAA. The patient is willing and capable of providing informed consent for the trial. The patient's glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is greater than 60 mL/min/1.73m2 and has no contraindication to intravenous contrast. The patient's CT angiogram was performed at BIDMC with the standard EVAR protocol and within 4 months of the operation. The patient has no disability or previous implants that may preclude adequate visualization on rotational imaging. The patient is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial that involves overlay of 3D scans on live fluoroscopy for endovascular procedures in the hybrid OR.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with stage T2 nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He has undergone biopsy and imaging tests to confirm the diagnosis. The patient does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past three months. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he is not currently under treatment with other similar drugs. The patient has no severe hypocalcemia or dysfunction of heart, lung, liver, kidney or hematopoiesis. He has no severe neurological, mental, or endocrine diseases. Additionally, the patient has not participated in any clinical trials of other drugs in the last three months. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Score is 80, and his expected survival is more than three months. The patient has no previous allergic reaction to the drug.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been on maintenance hormonal therapy for the past year and has been responding well to the treatment with no evidence of disease progression. She has a performance status of 1 and is able to carry out her daily activities without any difficulty. She has been regularly followed up with imaging tests and blood tests to monitor for any recurrence of the cancer. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of new analysis methods for detecting circulating tumor cells, circulating endothelial cells, and circulating tumor DNA.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and fatigued most of the time, with a loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has also been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has lost her appetite. She has a history of depression and has tried various antidepressants in the past, but has not found any significant relief. She is not pregnant and is using a reliable method of birth control. She has no history of seizure disorder or any other medical conditions that would put her at risk for seizures. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who underwent an emergency laparotomy due to a perforated appendix. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. She was hospitalized for 7 days post-surgery and experienced some post-operative complications including wound infection and urinary tract infection. She has since been discharged and is recovering at home. She reports some discomfort and difficulty with daily activities such as getting up from a chair and walking short distances. She is interested in participating in a study that will assess her quality of life and ability to return to her normal activities following her surgery.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who has been experiencing moderate acne for the last 3 years. He has tried various over-the-counter acne products but has not seen much improvement. He has no other medical conditions and is generally healthy. The acne is mostly located on his cheeks and nose, with a total of 20 inflammatory lesions in the designated application area. The patient has not used any acne treatments for at least 3 weeks prior to enrolling in the study, except for topical benzoyl peroxide pre-treatment. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with hypertension and borderline high LDL-cholesterol. She has a family history of cardiovascular disease and is concerned about her risk of developing these conditions. She is overweight and has been struggling to lose weight through diet and exercise alone. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the effects of purple vegetables on cardiovascular disease risk factors. Her current medications include amlodipine and atorvastatin. She is a non-smoker and not currently pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) for 10 years. He has been taking eye drops regularly to control his intraocular pressure, but they are no longer effective. His ophthalmologist has recommended a Molteno 3 glaucoma drainage device implant surgery to reduce the pressure in his eye. The patient has no known allergies and has never had any prior surgeries on his eyes. He understands the risks and benefits of the surgery and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and safety of KeraSys and Tutoplast patch grafts for covering the Molteno 3 tube shunt during the surgery. The patient does not wear contact lenses and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who presents to the hospital with a fever of 39°C and leukocytosis of 12.5 K/microLiter. She reports feeling weak and fatigued for the past few days, as well as experiencing chills and night sweats. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and takes medications for both conditions. Upon examination, she is found to have crackles in her lung fields and is diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia. She is started on antibiotics and admitted to the hospital for further management. Blood samples are collected upon admission and again after she has recovered from the infection. The samples are used to investigate the involvement of the translation initiation factors (eIF4E and eIF4G) in the process of recovery from acute infection in elderly patients. The study aims to identify protein translation regulation mechanisms that enable the rapid activation or termination of synthesis of specific proteins required for inflammation or its resolution. The study will help to determine if these mechanisms function differently in elderly patients and if so, how they may be manipulated to improve clinical outcomes.

A 35-year-old female with a diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL) in complete remission 2 (CR2) after treatment with induction chemotherapy is being considered for participation in a clinical trial for donor bone marrow transplantation. The patient has no HLA-matched, sibling donor available for bone marrow transplantation. She has no history of CNS disease or more than two episodes of active CNS disease, and no active serious infection. Her LVEF is at least 45%, and she has no active congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, or angina pectoris. Her pulmonary function tests show an FEV1 and FVC of at least 50% predicted. The patient is HIV negative and not pregnant, and is willing to use effective contraception. She has not had any prior malignancy except curatively treated skin cancer. The patient has not undergone any prior autologous or allogeneic bone marrow transplantation and has not received any transfusions from a donor. She is willing to undergo high-dose chemotherapy and donor bone marrow transplantation, and is willing to comply with the protocol for follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who sustained a traumatic spinal cord injury from a motor vehicle accident 15 years ago. He is currently classified as ASIA Scale B, meaning he has some sensory function but no motor function below the level of injury. He reports no history of heart disease or symptoms such as chest pain or shortness of breath. He is not being treated for high cholesterol but reports a family history of heart disease. He is able to communicate and understand the testing procedures and is willing to provide voluntary informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. He underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy for approximately 6 months. Three months after completing the treatment, he started experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. His primary care physician referred him to a cardiologist who diagnosed him with chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy (CHIC). He is currently taking medications for his heart condition, including a beta-blocker and a diuretic. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father experiencing a heart attack in his 50s. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His physical examination revealed a regular heart rhythm with a heart rate of 80 beats per minute and blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. His lungs are clear, and he has no swelling in his abdomen. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed a left bundle branch block (LBBB) with a QRS duration of 160 ms. An echocardiogram revealed a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30%. He is interested in participating in research to improve his heart function and quality of life.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who enjoys playing sports such as basketball and soccer. He recently experienced a Grade II meniscus injury to his right knee while playing basketball. He has been experiencing pain and limited function in his knee even after 3 months of nonoperative treatment, including physical therapy and pain medication. He has no history of lower limb fractures or intra-articular drug injection. He does not have any severe coagulation disorders, cardiopulmonary failure, or other serious medical conditions. He is not currently pregnant or nursing. He does not have any electronic implants such as pacemakers in his body. He has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis, and syphilis. He does not consume alcohol or use drugs. He has no vestibular or balance disorders and has normal cognitive function. He is willing to sign an informed consent form and participate in the clinical trial.

This clinical trial is specifically designed for Pre-K teachers working in Early Education Centers in New York City. The trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ParentCorps in high-poverty Early Education Centers in New York City. The trial will include 158 Pre-K teachers from 23 Centers, out of which 12 Centers will receive Thrive Professional Learning plus ParentCorps, and 11 Centers will receive Thrive Professional Learning only. The trial will involve self-report surveys and interviews of the participating teachers over a two-year period. The trial will also collect observational data and semi-structured interviews from the teachers in the sites randomized to ParentCorps to evaluate their experiences with implementation. The trial does not involve any families or students, and only Pre-K teachers from the 23 Centers are eligible to participate. Leaders and other school staff from the Centers are excluded from the study.

This is a 35 year-old female with a BMI of 30. She has been struggling with weight loss for several years and has tried various diets and exercise programs without success. She is currently not taking any weight loss or appetite regulation medication and has not lost more than 5% of her body weight in the past 6 months. She is physically able to walk for 2 blocks without stopping and has no major psychiatric or medical conditions that would limit her participation in the study. She is willing to consume meal replacements and is committed to losing at least 8% of her body weight during the 4-month weight loss phase of the study. She understands that she will be randomly assigned to either a low-ED prescription or an energy balance prescription for the weight loss maintenance phase and is willing to comply with the assigned dietary prescription for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing urinary incontinence for the past 6 months. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has been advised by her doctor to undergo reconstructive pelvic surgery to address her incontinence. The patient has consented to participate in a clinical trial that aims to prevent catheter-associated urinary tract infection in women undergoing incontinence or reconstructive pelvic surgery. The patient will require catheterization for more than 24 hours following surgery. The patient is fluent in English and does not have any known allergies to sulfonamides or trimethoprim. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or suffering from severe renal impairment. The patient is not taking dofetilide, methenamine, procaine, warfarin, procainamide, or methotrexate.

A 30-year-old healthy female who has not received an influenza vaccine in the past 6 months is being recruited for a study on the immune response to the FluMist vaccine. The study will involve a single dose of the nasal spray vaccine, and the patient will be required to keep a diary of any health changes and daily temperatures for 21 days after vaccination. Blood and nasal swab samples will be collected from the patient before and after vaccination to analyze changes in protein biomarkers reflective of the immune response. The patient will participate in the study for approximately 1 month and must be available to attend all scheduled visits and comply with study procedures. The patient must also be willing to use an adequate method of birth control for at least 1 month after vaccination and have a negative pregnancy test at the time of enrollment. The patient should not have any acute or chronic medical conditions that would render vaccination unsafe or interfere with the evaluation of responses. The study is being conducted at the Glennan Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology at Eastern Virginia Medical School.

A 42-year-old female presented with complaints of unpleasant sensations in her legs that occurred mainly at night, causing an irresistible urge to move them. The symptoms had been present for the past year and had worsened over time. The patient reported that the sensations were relieved by moving her legs and that she had trouble falling asleep due to the discomfort. She denied any history of peripheral neuropathy, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, dyskinesias or dystonias. She had a body mass index of 29 kg/m2 and was not taking any medication that could affect the sleep/wake cycle or RLS. She had no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient was diagnosed with primary restless leg syndrome based on the International Restless Legs Syndrome Study Group (IRLSSG) diagnostic criteria. The patient had an International Restless Legs Scale (IRLS) Total severity score of 20 (moderate severity) and had significant sleep disturbance on item 4 of IRLS. She was willing to participate in the study and met all other inclusion criteria. The patient was informed about the study and provided informed consent.

42-year-old female with type 1 diabetes who has been on continuous subcutaneous insulin therapy for 5 years. She has been using an Accu-Chek insulin pump with a Luer lock infusion set for the last 3 years. She has adequate infusion sites and is diligent in measuring her blood glucose levels at least 4 times per day. She has no history of catheter abscesses or plaster allergies. She does not have any chronic diseases other than diabetes and is not on any immuno-modulatory medication or chemotherapy. She is able and willing to comply with study procedures and is interested in participating in the study to evaluate and compare the perception of insertion pain with Accu-Chek FlexLink and FlexLink Plus infusion sets.

A 45-year-old woman who works from home as a freelance writer is interested in participating in a weight loss study. She has a BMI of 32 and has struggled with her weight for several years. She lives in the Chapel Hill area and has access to a computer and the internet. She exercises regularly, but has difficulty sticking to a diet plan. She has no history of major health conditions, including psychiatric or eating disorders, and is not currently taking any weight loss medications or participating in any structured weight loss program. She has never had surgery for weight loss and has not lost 5% of her body weight and kept it off within the past 6 months. She is willing to be randomized to either group and able to attend data collection visits at the UNC Weight Research Program Center.

The patient is a 55 year old African American male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer. He has failed treatment with both irinotecan-based and oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy regimens. He is currently experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform daily activities with some difficulty. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married with two adult children and works as a mechanic. He has not undergone any major surgeries in the past 3 months and has not received radiation therapy in the past 6 weeks. His screening laboratory values are within normal limits, with a hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, WBC count of 5,000/mm3, neutrophil count of 2,500/mm3, and a platelet count of 150,000/mm3. His creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL and creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. He understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 17-year-old female high school student has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad most of the time, has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, and has trouble sleeping. She also reports feeling anxious and worried about her academic performance and social relationships. She has no history of suicidal ideation or attempts. She does not have any ongoing psychological treatment and is not taking any psychiatric medication. She has not had any recent changes in her medication during the last 4 weeks. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive tailored internet-administrated cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) for her depressive symptoms.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer. She has been receiving hospice care at home for the past 2 months. She has been experiencing pain, anxiety, and depression, which have been impacting her quality of life. She is currently taking opioids for pain management, but they have been causing her to feel drowsy and disoriented. She is interested in exploring complementary therapies to help manage her symptoms and improve her overall well-being. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from receiving either massage or music therapy. Her caregiver, her daughter, is available and willing to participate in brief interviews and complete questionnaires on her behalf.

A 20-year-old male NCAA division I varsity basketball player with a history of exercise-induced asthma, presented with cough and wheezing during sports training. He has been treated with inhaled albuterol and fluticasone for the past 2 years. His symptoms have been well controlled with occasional use of albuterol inhaler, but he has noticed decreased athletic performance in the past few months. He is a non-smoker with no known allergies. The patient has no other significant medical history or family history of asthma. He is actively training 6 days a week and drinks plenty of water. His physical exam is significant for bilateral wheezing and mild tachypnea. His lung function test results indicate a mild obstruction with a FEV1/FVC ratio of 65%. The patient has been identified as a potential candidate for the study and has consented to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who lost his right leg below the knee due to a motorcycle accident. He is currently using a traditional prosthetic leg, but he experiences discomfort and difficulty with mobility. He works as a farmer and needs to be able to walk and stand for long periods of time. He lives in rural Kenya and has limited access to prosthetic services. He speaks English fluently and is interested in trying out new technology that can improve his quality of life. He weighs 80kg and has a residual limb length of 20cm and a distal circumference of 40cm. He is in good overall health and has no known complications or open wounds.

A 25-year-old non-smoking male, weighing 70 kg, has no known medical conditions and takes no medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, and safety of phencynonate hydrochloride tablets. His urinalysis and laboratory evaluations are within acceptable range, and he has normal ECG and chest x-ray results. He has not taken any medications within the past 14 days and has not donated blood in the past 3 months. He has no history of drug or alcohol addiction or abuse.

45-year-old female who sustained a T12 spinal cord fracture 6 weeks ago due to a motor vehicle accident. She has been stable medically and has no other significant injuries. She has been receiving physical therapy and is able to ambulate with a walker. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial as she is concerned about the potential for bone loss due to her injury. She has no history of vitamin D deficiency, hypocalcemia, renal insufficiency, abnormal thyroid hormone status or abnormal mental status. Her most recent dexa scan showed no evidence of osteoporosis at the hip or spine. She is willing and able to return for follow-up visits at 6 and 12 months.

Patient is a 28-year-old male from the United States who was recently involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a traumatic, closed, depression fracture of the proximal tibia (AO type B2). He is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical or surgical history. He is a non-smoker and does not use any medications. He has no known allergies. His diagnosis was confirmed by X-ray imaging. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 15. She has been treated with multiple daily insulin injections (MDI) since then. She is concerned about managing her blood glucose levels and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the long-term effects of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in patients with type 1 diabetes treated with MDI. She is 165 cm tall and weighs 65 kg. Her HbA1c level is 7.5%. She works as a graphic designer and leads an active lifestyle. She exercises regularly and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and camping. She has never been pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant during the study duration. She has no known cognitive dysfunction or allergy to any of the CGM materials or adhesives in contact with the skin. She is willing to participate in the trial and provide written informed consent.

A 42-year-old woman with a BMI of 40 kg/m^2 presents with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) for the past 5 years. She has been on a stable dose of metformin for the past 12 weeks and has tried to control her diabetes with diet and exercise, but has not seen significant weight loss results. Her Hemoglobin A1c level is 8.2% at screening. The patient reports no history of secondary causes of obesity such as Cushing's disease/syndrome. She has not been diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes mellitus, diabetic ketoacidosis, pancreatitis, or pancreatectomy. Fasting C-peptide level is 1.1 ng/mL at screening. Her fasting fingerstick glucose is 190 mg/dL on Day 1. The patient is currently not on any thyroid hormone replacement therapy and has no history of inadequately controlled thyroid disorder. She is willing to adhere to the specific prohibitions and restrictions outlined in the study. The patient is postmenopausal and is not currently sexually active.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer that has spread to her liver and lungs. She has previously undergone two rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has continued to progress. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. Her absolute neutrophil count is 1,600/mcL and platelet count is 105,000/mcL. Her liver function tests are within normal limits and her creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min/1.73 m^2. She has completed and recovered from the effects of prior chemotherapy with only grade 1 toxicity. She has no history of brain metastases or allergic reactions to the study drugs. She is not receiving any other investigational agents, is not pregnant, and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She has measurable or evaluable disease at one site and has not received prior therapy with dinaciclib. She is excluded from the study if she has a history of organ allograft, requires immunosuppressive therapy, or has a history of New York Heart Association class 3 or 4 heart failure, myocardial infarction, unstable angina or cerebral vascular accident (CVA) within 6 months of protocol registration. Her LVEF is normal and she has no history of PR prolongation or atrioventricular (AV) block.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and is scheduled for elective outpatient adenotonsillectomy at Memorial Hermann Hospital. She has a history of snoring and restless sleep, and her parents have reported episodes of breath-holding during sleep. Her sleep study confirmed a diagnosis of OSA with increased end tidal CO2 levels during sleep. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, or renal disease. She has not been diagnosed with any congenital syndromes, sickle cell disease, or seizures. She is not receiving theophylline. Her parents have given written informed consent for her participation in the study, and she has provided child assent.

A 45-year-old woman with a T10 spinal cord injury due to a car accident 3 years ago comes to the clinic for follow-up. She has been experiencing back pain and has been diagnosed with low bone mineral density (BMD) with a T-score of -2.5 at the lumbar spine. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of heart disease, stroke or other significant medical conditions. She is currently taking calcium and vitamin D supplements, but her BMD has continued to decline. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate a new treatment for low BMD in patients with spinal cord injury. She meets the study criteria, including having a BMD T-score of -2.0 or lower at the lumbar spine, total hip or femoral neck, and having a spinal cord injury of at least 24 months but less than 7 years duration. She is willing to receive either monthly romosozumab injection or one-time zoledronic acid infusion for 12 months and undergo regular bone mineral density and biochemical marker testing.

The patient is a 58 year old male diagnosed with advanced gastric adenocarcinoma, confirmed by biopsy. He has undergone first-line treatment with fluoropyrimidine and platinum, but has progressed on this treatment. He is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, nausea, and loss of appetite. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light physical activity. He has no known active central nervous system metastases and has not received prior therapy with taxanes or anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies. He has no active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease, no clinically significant cardiovascular or cerebrovascular diseases, and his blood pressure is well controlled with medications. His recent blood work has shown no coagulation abnormalities. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60 year old male who has been recently diagnosed with chronic glaucoma. He has noticed a gradual loss of peripheral vision over the past year and has a family history of glaucoma. He wears glasses for presbyopia but has good visual acuity. His intraocular pressure (IOP) has been consistently elevated at 25 mmHg in both eyes despite using latanoprost drops for the past 6 months. On examination of visual field and optic disc, glaucoma damage has been detected. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in a randomized double-masked clinical trial of memantine for the treatment of glaucoma.

54 yo M with acute myeloid leukemia in complete remission (CR) and preparing for his first hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). The patient will receive a peripheral blood graft from a matched unrelated donor with a 10/10 human leukocyte antigen match. He will undergo a myeloablative preparative regimen and receive post-transplant GVHD prophylaxis consisting of a calcineurin inhibitor (CSA) and methotrexate. The patient has a Glutamate Pyruvate Transaminase (GPT) level that is below 3 times the upper normal limit (UNL) and creatinine levels that are ≤ 1.4 mg%. The patient is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 60-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was recently diagnosed with moderate to severe mitral valve regurgitation and has been advised to undergo a surgical repair. He has no history of endocarditis or valve calcification. He is willing to return to the hospital where the implantation will occur as part of the standard practice of care. He is not currently participating in any other investigational device study and has a life expectancy of greater than one year.

A 67-year-old male with a history of hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and a previous myocardial infarction was admitted to the hospital due to shortness of breath, leg swelling, and fatigue. The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease with a baseline serum creatinine level of 1.3 mg%. Upon admission, his serum creatinine level was 1.8 mg% and he was diagnosed with cardiorenal syndrome type 1 (CRS1) due to acute decompensation of heart failure. The patient is conscious and oriented, able to provide informed consent, and has no contraindications for bio-impedance measurements or hand-held echocardiography. The patient is not on dialysis, nor is he mechanically ventilated. He has no anemia, bleeding, or signs of a new myocardial infarction. The patient's BMI is within the normal range. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no history of hypothyroidism or Addison's disease.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with hypertension. She has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past year. She has a family history of hypertension and heart disease. She has a sedentary lifestyle and her diet is high in sodium and low in calcium. She does not take any calcium supplements. She has no history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, chronic renal disease, hypercalcemia, or nephrolithiasis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of calcium-D supplement on hypertension.

The patient is a 58-year-old man diagnosed with stage II prostate cancer. He is married and has been with his spouse for over 10 years. His PSA level was elevated during a routine check-up and subsequent biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications except for over-the-counter supplements. He has been referred to the John and Carol Walter Center for Urological Health for further management. During his initial visit, he expresses interest in participating in a research study that explores the effects of mindfulness-based stress reduction on health-related quality of life. He is fluent in English and has no known hearing or vision impairments. He provides informed consent and is enrolled in the 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course. After completing the course, he is randomized to receive weekly mindfulness-specific text or email messages related to course teachings for 4 months. He completes PRO and bio-marker assessments at 8, 6, and 12 months post-course completion.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who suffered a stroke six months ago, resulting in hemiplegia of the right arm. She has completed traditional rehabilitation therapy but still has limited mobility and function in her affected arm. She has no history of Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, or other upper limb disabilities. Her Mini Mental State Examination score is 26, indicating no significant cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in a new rehabilitation program using music therapy and hand tracking sensors to improve her arm function. She has not undergone any previous rehabilitative treatments that involved music therapy.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease who has been on regular hemodialysis for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. She presents for her scheduled hemodialysis session with a blood pressure of 145/90 mmHg and a heart rate of 78 beats per minute. She complains of occasional dizziness during dialysis and her medical team suspects that this may be related to hemodynamic changes during the procedure. She has no history of Raynaud's disease or peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD). She has intact skin on her wrists and fingers where the non-invasive hemodynamic monitor will be applied. She consents to participate in the study and agrees to have her hemodynamic parameters and fluid removal measured during the next hemodialysis session.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman who got married a year ago. She is currently trying to conceive her first child. She lives in a rural area in Northern Bangladesh with her husband and in-laws. She is a homemaker and spends most of her day taking care of household chores. She has completed her secondary education and can read and write in Bengali. Her diet primarily consists of rice, lentils, vegetables, and occasional fish or meat. She has never taken any vitamin supplements before. She has no known medical conditions and has never been hospitalized. She has regular menstrual cycles and has been trying to conceive for the past 3 months. She is aware of the risks associated with pregnancy and childbirth in her community and is interested in participating in a study that could potentially reduce these risks.

50 yo M with a history of hypercholesterolemia and coronary heart disease (CHD). He has been on a stable dose of atorvastatin for the past 3 months but his LDL-C levels have remained elevated. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if adding anacetrapib to his current statin therapy can further improve his cholesterol levels. The patient reports no significant past medical history except for a remote history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled on losartan. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His current medications include atorvastatin 40mg daily, losartan 50mg daily, and aspirin 81mg daily. He denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse and has no significant psychiatric history. His recent labs show an LDL-C level of 130 mg/dL and HDL-C level of 45 mg/dL. He has no history of ileal or gastric bypass surgeries and has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 3 months. The patient is interested in participating in the study and willing to adhere to the protocol requirements.

A 55-year-old male with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) diagnosed two years ago presents with complaints of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has received chemoimmunotherapy with fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab (FCR) in the past without any significant side effects. He was recently started on ibrutinib therapy and has been experiencing mild diarrhea and occasional headaches. He is also being treated for hypertension and dyslipidemia with lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He works as a computer programmer and is able to access the internet from home. He is proficient in English and is willing to use a web-based portal to report any symptoms he experiences. He has not experienced any recent ED visits or hospitalizations related to his CLL. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the use of patient-reported outcomes and supportive care plans in the management of CLL.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with no significant medical history. He has a normal BMI of 22 and weighs 70 kg. He does not smoke or consume any tobacco-containing products and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has never been diagnosed with any cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematological, gastro-intestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurological or psychiatric disease. He does not have any allergies to drugs or any drug chemically similar to the drug. He is not currently taking any medications, including over-the-counter products and vitamins. He is in a monogamous heterosexual relationship, and his partner is currently using a highly effective contraceptive method. He has no difficulty in swallowing tablets, and his forearm veins are accessible for cannulation or blood sampling. He consents to abstain from food for at least 10 hours prior to drug administration and for at least 4 hours post-dose in each period. He is willing to abstain from fluid for at least 1 hour prior to and 1 hour post each dose except for a 20% glucose solution given after dosing. He is able and willing to provide written informed consent and is available to participate in the study for the duration of the trial.

This study is seeking children between the ages of 2 and 7 who have been referred due to language delay, behavioral issues, or attention/hyperactivity problems. Both genders are eligible to participate, with parental consent. The child must have an ECBI score greater than 120, but cannot be receiving any other form of therapeutic intervention during the study. Parents must be biological and have a minimum education level of high school, with sufficient proficiency to fill out questionnaires. Parents cannot have psychosis or serious drug abuse. The objective of this study is to determine the efficacy of parent-based intervention in Pakistan using Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) in treating behavior and language problems due to behavioral disturbances in young children. The study will involve translating assessment tools and applications into Urdu and measuring the impact of PCIT on parenting relation, parenting stress, and children's compliance.

The patient is a 56-year-old non-smoking Caucasian male who has been experiencing difficulty in swallowing and hoarseness for the past three months. He also noticed a mass on the right side of his neck. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications. The physical examination reveals a 3 cm mass in the right tonsil and palpable cervical lymph nodes. The biopsy confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. The CT scan shows no distant metastases. The patient has a WHO performance status of 0 and meets all the inclusion criteria. The laboratory investigations show hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, WBC 8,500/µL, platelets 220,000/µL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, AST 25 U/L, ALT 30 U/L, and bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who is in good health and has no history of any clinically significant disorder. She has a body mass index of 23 kg/m2 and is not currently taking any medication. She does not smoke, use any tobacco-containing or nicotine-containing products within 6 months, and does not consume alcohol-containing, grapefruit-containing, or caffeine-containing foods or beverages, or foods or beverages with high levels of tyramine. She is not pregnant, lactating, or breastfeeding. The patient has agreed to use an effective method of birth control during the study if necessary. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of TR-701.

A 45-year-old male with a history of leukemia was admitted to the hospital with a fever of 38.5 C and an absolute neutrophil count of 200/microL. He has been receiving chemotherapy for the past month and has developed febrile neutropenia. He has no history of allergic reactions to antibiotics, and his liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has not been treated with systemic antibacterial therapy for the past two weeks. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial comparing ciprofloxacin with cefepime for the treatment of febrile neutropenia.

Li is a 65-year-old Mandarin-speaking man who has been experiencing persistent decline in cognitive function compared to his previous normal status. He has concerns associated with his memory complaint and worries about it. Li has received a normal age-, gender-, and education-adjusted performance on standardised cognitive tests. He does not meet the criteria for mild cognitive impairment or dementia. He has no history of stroke or other central nervous system diseases. Li has not been diagnosed with major depression (Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score < 24 points). He has not suffered any traumatic brain injury or systemic diseases such as thyroid dysfunction, syphilis, or HIV. He has no history of psychosis or congenital mental growth retardation.

This is a 56 year-old female who has been diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She underwent colonoscopy, which revealed a mass in the ascending colon, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has been scheduled for a minimally invasive right hemicolectomy with the creation of an anastomosis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially benefit from a quicker return of bowel function and earlier discharge. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets all of the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old woman presents with chronic pelvic pain with suspected endometriosis. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. She reports no allergies and does not smoke. She has regular menstrual cycles and denies any recent pregnancies. On physical examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender with no palpable masses. Pelvic examination shows mild tenderness on the right adnexal region. Pelvic ultrasound shows a 4 cm endometrioma on the right ovary. She is scheduled for a laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy under general anesthesia. She has provided written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial studying the effects of carbon dioxide with and without oxygen on CO2 absorption during laparoscopy. She meets all eligibility criteria and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 35-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital was involved in a car accident three months ago, which resulted in her experiencing severe physical injuries and witnessing the death of a fellow nurse who was in the vehicle with her. Since the accident, she has been experiencing intrusive memories, nightmares, and flashbacks related to the traumatic event. She also avoids driving or being a passenger in a car and has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed. Her symptoms have been negatively impacting her work and home life, and she feels like she is unable to cope with her emotions. She has been diagnosed with PTSD as a primary diagnosis and has agreed to withdraw from any psychotropic medication for the duration of the study. She does not have any extensive dissociative symptoms, current psychosis, suicidal risk, substance or alcohol abuse, or ongoing trauma.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was admitted to the hospital due to severe pneumonia. He has a past medical history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. He works as a sales executive and travels frequently for work. He recently returned from a business trip to Asia and developed fever, cough, and difficulty breathing upon his return. He was diagnosed with pneumonia and admitted to the hospital for treatment. He is currently receiving antibiotics and supportive care for his pneumonia. The patient has no known history of sepsis or any other serious medical conditions. He is scheduled to be monitored with the Morley Medical Sepsis Software Device as part of a clinical trial evaluating its efficacy in predicting sepsis using AI machine learning algorithms.

8 yo F diagnosed with Ewing's sarcoma with planned high dose chemotherapy and autologous transplant. The patient has completed initial rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with residual tumor still present. She has adequate performance status with a Karnofsky score of 80. Laboratory values show that she has an absolute neutrophil count of 1.5 x 10^9/L and a platelet count of 75 x 10^9/L. Her calculated creatinine clearance is 90 mL/min/1.73m^2. The patient has recovered from all acute significant toxic effects of prior chemotherapy. The patient and her parents have agreed to participate in the clinical trial and have provided informed consent. The patient has no history of cardiac abnormalities or arrhythmia. The patient is not on any investigational drugs and does not have any co-morbid conditions that would put her at high-risk from treatment complications. The patient is eligible for inclusion in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) three years ago. He has been taking imatinib but is experiencing resistance to the medication. He has a history of smoking and alcohol use but has quit both since his diagnosis. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He has no significant comorbidities and is otherwise healthy. His HLA typing shows that he is A0201, B0801 positive. He has tested positive for BCR-ABL b3a2. His current white blood cell count is 60,000/μL, and his hemoglobin and platelet counts are normal. He has no blast crisis. He is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to undergo the conditioning protocol and prophylactic infusion of cytotoxic T cells.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is generally healthy and resides in the United States. She is currently using adequate contraception and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of a superfoods nutrition supplement on health related quality of life. She does not smoke and does not have any underlying chronic health conditions. She has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has not participated in any interventional clinical studies in the past 31 days. She is willing to comply with study procedures and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35 year old Nepalese woman who has been living in a temporary shelter since the 2015 earthquake that devastated her village. She is married and has three children aged 5, 8 and 10 years old. She has been experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness since losing her home and belongings in the earthquake. She has also been struggling to perform daily tasks such as cooking and cleaning due to the limited resources available to her in the shelter. She has not received any formal mental health treatment before. She reports occasional drinking but denies any alcohol use disorder. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her improve her well-being and cope better with the challenges she is facing.

The patient is a 43-year-old male who received a kidney transplant 5 years ago due to end-stage renal disease caused by diabetic nephropathy. The patient has been on maintenance immunosuppressive therapy with tacrolimus for the past 5 years. However, the patient developed chronic active antibody-mediated rejection, which is causing gradual deterioration of kidney function. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and decreased urine output. The patient's renal biopsy showed Banff histological criteria for chronic active antibody-mediated rejection. The patient has no significant medical history other than diabetes and hypertension. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to follow study instructions and participate in all study assessments and visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic sinusitis with nasal obstruction and recurrent sinus infections for several years. Despite multiple rounds of antibiotics and nasal sprays, her symptoms have not improved. She has scheduled to undergo nasal and/or paranasal sinus surgeries under general anesthesia. She has no medical history of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, leukemia, lymphoma, or other neoplasias under chemotherapy treatment, and is not currently taking any nonsteroid anti-inflammatory drugs. She has no history of adenoidectomy or tonsillectomy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy of different pharyngeal packing during routine rhinologic surgery in the prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting, and to evaluate the influence of pharyngeal packing on postoperative throat pain.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma after presenting with a painless lump on his neck. He underwent 6 cycles of R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone) chemotherapy and achieved a partial response. However, a follow-up PET scan revealed residual disease in his abdomen. He is now being considered for an allogeneic stem cell transplant. He has a brother who is a HLA-compatible donor. He has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. His performance status is 90% according to the Karnofsky scale. He has normal kidney and liver function tests. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is willing to undergo pre-transplant chemotherapy and radiation therapy.

25-year-old male, non-smoker, with no significant medical history, BMI 21.5, weight 70 kg, presents to the clinical trial center for participation in the study evaluating the effects of food intake on the pharmacokinetic profiles of Z-338. He has not taken any investigational new drug within 120 days of the study and has not received any medical treatment drugs within 7 days of the study. He has not donated blood before the study. He is in good health and has no known allergies. He does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse. He reports a regular diet and is willing to follow the dietary restrictions provided during the study. He has no history of gastrointestinal or metabolic disorders. He has no known history of previous surgeries or medical procedures. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 45-year-old male with an advanced stage of solid malignant tumor that has not responded to standard therapies or for which no standard therapy exists. He has a WHO performance status of 1 and is post-menopausal. He has moderate liver function and is otherwise healthy. He has not received any investigational agents or study drugs in the last 30 days, as well as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or anticancer agents in the last 3 weeks. He has no severe cardiac conditions and has stable respiratory and cardiac conditions.

The patient is a 26-year-old university student who spends an average of 6 hours per day in front of the computer. She has been experiencing neck pain for the past 2 weeks, which radiates to her shoulders and upper back. The pain is described as a dull ache and is aggravated by prolonged sitting and typing. She has not undergone any recent traumas, surgeries or physiotherapy treatments. She takes occasional over-the-counter pain medications to alleviate the pain, but it does not offer long-term relief. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her neck pain.

The patient is an adult aged 18 or older, who has recently enrolled in one of the 22 HIV care and treatment clinics in Botswana. The patient is HIV-infected and has not started antiretroviral therapy (ART) yet. The patient's past medical history includes a previous positive TB test, but the patient has not received treatment for TB in the past. The patient is experiencing symptoms such as cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats. The patient is not currently incarcerated. The patient has consented to participate in the study and is willing to provide sputum samples for TB testing. The patient will be followed for six months after HIV clinic enrollment to monitor TB and ART-related outcomes. The patient will receive the Xpert MTB/RIF assay for the GeneXpert platform (Xpert) for TB diagnosis, as part of the stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial to evaluate the impact of the Xpert package on TB case finding among HIV-infected persons. The patient will also be assessed for all-cause mortality during the first six months of ART.

60 year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the hospital with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has been feeling unwell for the past 3 days with a worsening of his symptoms over the last 24 hours. He has no known exposure to COVID-19, but his wife was recently diagnosed with the virus. He is admitted to the hospital with confirmed COVID-19 infection via positive nasopharyngeal RT-PCR. He is currently not requiring mechanical ventilation or vasopressors. His ECG shows a corrected QT interval of 420 milliseconds. He has no history of retinal disease or G6PD deficiency, and is able to take oral medications. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the TEACH study and is randomized to receive either hydroxychloroquine or placebo for 5 days. The primary endpoint is severe disease progression, and secondary outcomes include 30-day mortality, hospital length of stay, noninvasive ventilator support, and cytokine release syndrome grading scale.

A 52-year-old male presents with a history of hematuria and lower back pain. Imaging studies show a mass in the left kidney and multiple metastases to the lungs and bones. A biopsy confirms renal cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. He has no history of significant cardiovascular disease. His ECOG performance status is 1. Blood tests show hemoglobin of 12.5 g/dL, neutrophil count of 3,500/µL, platelet count of 200,000/µL, serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, ALT and AST of 30 U/L, and INR of 1.1. The patient has no history of brain metastases and has normal brain MRI. He has at least one measurable lesion using the RECIST criteria. He has no proteinuria confirmed by urinary dipstick test. He has no history of other malignancies. He is not pregnant or lactating. He gives signed written informed consent and is affiliated with a healthy security insurance.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who suffered a sudden cardiac arrest while at home. Emergency medical services were immediately called and the Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) team arrived at the scene. Despite their efforts, the patient did not regain consciousness before the arrival of the HEMS team. The HEMS team initiated resuscitation attempts, including defibrillation and drug administration. During the resuscitation process, the HEMS team performed a differential diagnosis including ultrasound and blood gas analysis to determine the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. The patient was transported to the hospital, but unfortunately, he did not survive. The HEMS team filled out a form detailing the execution of the protocol and noted that it took approximately 10 minutes to complete. The cause of the cardiac arrest was not identified during the differential diagnosis.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing seasonal allergies for the past 3 years. She presents with typical symptoms of birch pollen allergy, including sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes. She has a positive result on skin prick testing and a high level of birch-specific IgE in her blood. She has not been diagnosed with asthma and does not have any other allergies to animal dander, mites, or other types of pollen. She is willing and able to comply with the treatment regimen and has provided written consent to participate in the study. She is not currently pregnant and is not taking beta-blockers or oral corticosteroids.

This is a 10 year-old boy diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). He struggles with attention and has difficulty focusing on tasks for extended periods of time. He is currently receiving support in the form of medication and behavioral therapy. His parents are interested in finding alternative ways to help him improve his attention capacity and have consented to him participating in this study. The boy enjoys playing on digital devices and is excited to participate in the study.

28 yo F Japanese with no significant medical history, BMI of 22.0 kg/m^2, who is sexually active with a nonsterilized male partner and agrees to use routinely adequate contraception. She has not received any investigational compound or seasonal influenza vaccine within the past 6 months, and has no history of influenza infection within 6 months prior to the initial injection of study vaccine. She has not been vaccinated with TAK-850 before. She is not a study site employee or in a dependent relationship with one. She has no uncontrolled, clinically significant manifestations of neurological, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, metabolic, gastrointestinal, urologic, endocrine or other disorders, no immune deficient condition, no immune compromising condition or disease, and is not currently undergoing any form of treatment that can be expected to influence immune response within 30 days prior to the initial injection of study vaccine. She has not received antipyretics within 4 hours prior to the initial injection of study vaccine. She has no history of Guillain- Barré Syndrome, demyelinating disorders (including acute disseminated encephalomyelitis [ADEM] and multiple sclerosis) or convulsions, functional or surgical asplenia, rash, other dermatologic conditions or tattoos which may interfere with the evaluation of injection site reaction, and no history of, or is infected with the Hepatitis B Virus (HBsAgs), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) or Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). She has no known hypersensitivity to any component of TAK-850, no history of severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis, drug abuse (defined as any illicit drug use) or a history of alcohol abuse within 1 year prior to the initial injection of study vaccine. She has not received any blood products or vaccines within the specified time frames prior to the initial injection of study vaccine. Her laboratory values are within normal limits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with advanced melanoma. She has a history of severe sunburns during her childhood and adolescence, and she noticed a new mole on her back that rapidly grew in size and started to bleed. Imaging studies confirmed multiple metastases to her lungs and liver. She underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor, but the disease continued to progress despite adjuvant therapy with ipilimumab and nivolumab. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and she has no significant comorbidities. She has a measurable lesion on her chest wall, and her laboratory tests show adequate organ function. She has not received any prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137 antibody, or anti-CTLA-4 agent. She has not participated in any other clinical trial within the past 30 days, and she has not received any chemotherapy, targeted small molecule therapy, radiotherapy, or biological cancer therapy within the past 4 weeks. She is willing to use contraception during the trial and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known hypersensitivity to the components of the study drug or another monoclonal antibody.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been experiencing severe pain in her back and abdominal region for the past few weeks. She has been diagnosed with a kidney stone after undergoing a CT scan. The stone is located in her right kidney and is approximately 10mm in size. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is not currently taking any medications. The patient is willing to undergo the percutaneous nephrolithotomy procedure to remove the stone. She has no allergies to anesthesia or any other medications. The patient has a guardian who is willing to provide consent for her participation in the study. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been actively trying to conceive for the past 6 months. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has been tracking her ovulation using an ovulation predictor kit (OPK). The patient has no known medical conditions that would prevent her from becoming pregnant. She has been taking prenatal vitamins for the past month and has been following a healthy lifestyle, including a balanced diet and regular exercise. The patient has been researching different methods to increase her chances of becoming pregnant and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will validate the instructions for the Conception Kit. She has read the information provided on the website and feels confident that she can follow the instructions to use the Kit at home. The patient is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that it will increase her chances of conceiving.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of ER-positive, stage II breast cancer. She has completed four years of adjuvant endocrine therapy and is considering continuation of the therapy beyond five years. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a family history of breast cancer. She has undergone a lumpectomy and radiation therapy, followed by adjuvant endocrine therapy with tamoxifen for four years. The patient is currently asymptomatic and has a good performance status.
