She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the decision-making impact of the Breast Cancer Index (BCI) in recommending extended adjuvant endocrine therapy. She is able to provide informed consent and has a life expectancy of greater than five years.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to a viral illness. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fever for the past five days. Her oxygen saturation levels have been dropping, and she is now requiring a high flow of oxygen to maintain her levels. She has no history of respiratory illness or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Her chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates. She has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) and is being closely monitored. She has not been intubated yet but is at risk of requiring it if her condition worsens. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the requirements of the protocol.

The patient is a 6-month-old boy diagnosed with unilateral ureteropelvic junction obstruction. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. A recent scintigraphy has shown partial renal function of 50% in the affected kidney. The renal pelvis diameter is 15 mm, and there is a urodynamically relevant decrease in renal drainage. The patient is asymptomatic and has a healthy contralateral kidney. The patient has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions and has not undergone any previous surgeries.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock caused by a kidney infection. He has no significant past medical history, but he is a smoker with a history of heavy alcohol use. He has a BMI of 29 and is obese. He is lethargic and bedridden due to his critical illness. He has no significant muscle weakness or complaints of pain. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication to control it. His family history is significant for diabetes and heart disease. He has a CT scan of his abdomen performed within 24 hours of his admission to the ICU as part of his clinical workup. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male SCUBA-diver who has experienced decompression illness (DCI) due to a patent foramen ovale (PFO). He has a history of occasional joint pain and occasional headaches, but otherwise is in good health. He is an experienced diver and has been diving for over 10 years, with an average of 20-30 dives per year. He is currently not taking any medications and does not have any allergies. His blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and his heart rate is 70 beats per minute. His physical examination is unremarkable. He has agreed to undergo catheter-based PFO-closure as part of this clinical trial to reduce his risk of DCI in the future.

A 48-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer is planning to undergo a bilateral mastectomy with immediate two-stage prosthetic breast reconstruction. She is a non-smoker and has never had radiotherapy. Her BMI is within the normal range. She has no history of prior sternotomy. She has not received neoadjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced breast cancer, and preoperative axillary lymph node metastasis is not present. She is not planning to undergo direct-to-implant reconstruction. The mastectomy weight is less than 800 grams, and there is adequate mastectomy skin perfusion. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare two different surgical techniques for breast reconstruction.

A 30-year-old female presents with a history of recurrent anal fistulas for the past 6 years. She has tried multiple treatments including antibiotics and drainage procedures but has not achieved complete healing. She has also experienced fecal incontinence and discomfort during bowel movements. She has been diagnosed with complex anal fistulas confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging. A seton has been placed 6 weeks prior to the study to prevent abscess formation. The

This is a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with osteoporosis and has been taking alendronate once daily for the past 6 months. She has not experienced any adverse effects from the medication but has expressed difficulty adhering to the daily dosing regimen. She is interested in exploring a monthly dosing regimen and has been identified as a candidate for the BONCURE study. She is able to stand or sit in an upright position for at least 60 minutes and does not have any abnormalities of the esophagus. She is otherwise in good health and willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old African American man who has been receiving care at a VA healthcare site for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with hypertension (HTN) for the past 3 years and has been taking medication for it. His last two BP readings were 145/95 mmHg and 150/100 mmHg. He has been experiencing some dizziness and headaches lately. He has a family history of hypertension and heart disease. He works as a truck driver and spends most of his time on the road, making it difficult to manage his health. He has a cell phone and is willing to receive text messages for the next 6 months. He is interested in learning more about how to manage his HTN and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been referred to the ophthalmology department of El-Minia university hospital for evaluation of her high myopia. She has a history of wearing glasses since childhood and has noticed that her vision has been progressively deteriorating over the past few years. On examination, her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in both eyes. Her intraocular pressure is within normal limits and there are no signs of any ocular abnormalities. Her axial length measurement is greater than 26.5 mm, confirming her diagnosis of high myopia. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the macular microvascular network alterations in high myopic eyes using optical coherence tomography angiography. She meets the inclusion criteria for group B and has no exclusion criteria. She has been advised about the study protocol and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who is scheduled for an elective surgery due to a sports injury. He is generally healthy with no history of chronic medical conditions. His BMI is within the normal range. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies to medications. His vital signs are within normal limits. He has never undergone general anesthesia before. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is an ASA 1 patient between 18-65 years old scheduled for elective surgery. He does not meet the exclusion criteria as he has no history of heart failure or COPD.

The patient is a 54-year-old male diagnosed with stage III follicular lymphoma. He was initially treated with chemotherapy, followed by radiation therapy. However, he had a relapse of the disease a year later, and his lymph nodes have been progressively increasing in size. He has an ECOG performance score of 1 and has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not sexually active, and his last colonoscopy was normal. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. His bone marrow function is adequate, and his renal, hepatic, and coagulation function is within normal limits. He has not undergone any stem cell transplant or received any anti-cancer therapy within the last 14 days. He has tested negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C infections.

A 65-year-old retired teacher was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, cough, and swelling in her legs. She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She takes metformin and lisinopril for her medical conditions. She denies any chest pain, dizziness, or fainting. She mentioned feeling more tired than usual in the last few days. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her family history is significant for heart disease, with her father having a heart attack in his late 60s. She lives with her husband and has two adult children. Upon physical examination, the patient is breathing rapidly, has crackles in her lungs, and pitting edema in her lower extremities. She is awake, alert, and oriented to person, place, and time. Her blood pressure is 160/90 mm Hg, and her heart rate is 98 beats per minute. She is diagnosed with acute heart failure and is admitted under the care of a cardiologist.

A 59-year-old male patient with a history of ischemic heart disease is scheduled to undergo cardiac surgery. He has a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well controlled with medication. His left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 45%. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently not on any steroid therapy or antibiotics. He gives informed consent to participate in a randomized controlled double-blind study, which aims to identify whether fluid resuscitation using hypertonic saline results in less fluid administered in patients following cardiac surgery. The study intervention involves the patient receiving 5ml/kg body weight of 7.3% NaCl or 0.9% NaCl by infusion pump over 60 minutes upon admission to the ICU after the surgery. If necessary, fluid resuscitation will thereafter be performed with Ringer's lactate to normalize peripheral perfusion and to allow weaning of vasopressors. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is enrolled as a participant.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female volunteer who has been using oral contraceptives for the past three months. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days and a body mass index of 22 kg/m2. She has no history of polycystic ovary syndrome or thyroid dysfunction. She has never been diagnosed with any malignant disease and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has not participated in any clinical trial in the past three weeks and has no foreseen inability to attend scheduled study visits. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has signed an informed consent form and is willing to practice effective barrier methods for birth control during the study.

A 52-year-old man has been diagnosed with colon cancer and requires primary elective implantation of a Totally Implantable Access Port. He has no history of allergies to contrast agents and is mentally and physically capable of complying with the study requirements. He has not participated in any other clinical trials that could interfere with the primary endpoint of this study.

A 42 year old Japanese male patient was referred to the clinic with a history of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He had undergone several treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his condition has relapsed and is refractory to standard treatment. His latest PET-CT showed FDG avid lymph nodes in the neck, axilla, mediastinum, para-aortic, and pelvic regions. He is experiencing night sweats, fever, and weight loss. His performance status according to the ECOG scale is 1. He has not undergone autologous stem cell transplant and is not eligible for it. He has one measurable lesion on PET-CT. He has no history of another primary malignancy, no active bleeding diathesis, and no active respiratory, skin, mucosal, renal, neurological, or ocular disorder of grade > 1. He is willing to provide a portion of bone marrow aspirate and biopsy during the study.

A 29-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) 5 years ago is looking for options to manage her symptoms. She has been on corticosteroids for the last 3 years and hydroxychloroquine for the last year. Despite the medications, she still experiences symptoms such as joint pain, fatigue, and skin rashes. She is willing to try new treatments that may provide relief. She is currently single and not planning to have children in the near future. She has no significant medical history other than SLE. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She works as a graphic designer and can take time off from work for the required hospitalization. She is interested in learning more about the clinical trial and is willing to undergo the required tests and evaluations to determine her eligibility.

The patient is a teenage girl who has reached menarche and has a BMI at the 95th percentile for her age and sex. She is not currently taking any oral contraceptive pills, diuretics, or anticonvulsant medications. She has no history of diabetes or other endocrine or acute or chronic medical illnesses. She was previously identified as vitamin D deficient through an existing study and received standard therapy for vitamin D deficiency. She self-reports that she has taken the treatment for vitamin D and therefore qualifies for this study. She will undergo evaluation with measurement of serum 25 OH D level, PTH, and oral glucose tolerance test to assess for improvement in glucose-insulin sensitivity dynamics once the serum 25OH D level has been normalized.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl who is generally healthy and does not have any emotional, behavioral, or learning problems. She weighs 60 kg and is currently in the early stages of puberty. She enjoys eating pizza but is not a picky eater and does not have any dislikes for foods that will be included in the study. The patient's parents have given informed consent for her to participate in the study. The patient has not experienced any recent weight changes and has no history of eating disorders.

The patient is a 32-year-old female diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for over 2 years. The patient has experienced disease flares in the past 1 year with prednisone dosage of more than 20mg/day. The patient has a score of 6 or less on the SLEDAI scale, and does not have any British Isles Lupus Assessment Group (BILAG) A or more than one B. The patient currently takes prednisone (15mg/day), hydroxychloroquine (200mg/day), and mycophenolate mofetil (1g/day). The patient's BMI is 28.2 kg/m². The patient has a history of elevated liver enzymes, with ALT and AST levels being twice the upper normal limits. The patient has not been exposed to metformin in the past 30 days and does not have a history of intolerance to metformin. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been undergoing hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to end-stage renal disease. He has a stable vascular access and is clinically stable without any episodes of hypotension or other complications during dialysis sessions. He has no history of chronic inflammatory diseases, liver cirrhosis, or malignancies. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressant or anti-inflammatory medications. He is dialyzing through a permanent arteriovenous fistula and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his survival.

55 year-old male who will undergo elective abdominal surgery for a suspected tumor. The patient reports a decreased appetite over the past few months, unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds in the last 3 months, and generalized fatigue. The patient has no known allergies and takes no medications. The patient has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years and consumes alcohol socially. The patient reports no history of previous surgery or medical conditions that would affect nutritional status. The patient consents to participate in the study and undergoes preoperative nutritional assessment to determine their nutrition risk. Based on the results of the assessment, the patient may receive preoperative nutritional support which will be recorded along with the clinical outcomes after the surgery.

This is a 5-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with a speech delay. She has been evaluated by a speech therapist and her score on the Preschool Language Scale was more than 1 standard deviation below her age level. Her parents have noticed that she has difficulty communicating her needs and wants, and often becomes frustrated when she is not understood. They have sought out this clinical trial to see if Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT) can help improve their daughter's communication skills and reduce their stress as caregivers. The child has no other significant medical issues and her parents are committed to bringing her to all study visits and accurately reporting the services she receives.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who came to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain. After initial assessment, it was determined that he has acute appendicitis and will require surgery. The patient is expected to be admitted to the hospital for the surgery and post-operative care. The patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent based on his current mental status. There is no indication that the patient is pregnant or a prisoner. The patient doesn't have any history of psychiatric illness or cognitive impairment that may affect his ability to comprehend the informed consent. He has access to a smartphone and is comfortable with using audio-visual telemedicine. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his consent to be randomized into either the standard face-to-face consent group or the telemedicine consent group.

A 31-year-old woman visited the clinic with complaints of chronic nasal congestion, headache, and post-nasal drip for the past 6 months. The symptoms have been affecting her daily life, causing difficulty in breathing and sleeping. She has tried various medications, including nasal sprays and antihistamines, but the relief was only temporary. She has a history of nasal trauma during her childhood from a fall. She has never had any nasal surgery before and has never received radiotherapy to the head and neck region. She works as a teacher and finds it difficult to concentrate during classes due to her symptoms. She doesn't smoke and has no other significant medical history. Physical examination revealed a deviated nasal septum. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the two techniques of relieving nasal obstruction, and its efficacy in the relief of headache, hyposmia, and post-nasal drip, and nasal synechiae formation following each technique of surgery.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the disease has progressed despite treatment. He presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and frequent bowel movements. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis confirms the presence of multiple liver and lung metastases. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. His recent laboratory results are within normal limits, and he has no significant medical history aside from his cancer diagnosis. He has not received any anti-cancer treatment within the past 4 weeks and has not participated in any other clinical trials involving investigational drugs within the past 2 weeks. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

A 10-year-old boy named Jack was diagnosed with hemiplegia after a brain injury that occurred 6 months ago. He is able to use his unaffected arm normally, but has limited movement in his affected arm. He is able to attend school and participate in most activities with some assistance. He enjoys playing video games and has good hand-eye coordination. There are no other medical or social issues that preclude his participation in the study. He has not received botulinum toxin or intrathecal baclofen in the last 3 months, and does not have any implanted neuromodulatory or electronic device.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 42 complains of significant weight gain over the past 5 years. He has tried different diets and exercises but has not been successful in losing weight. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obstructive sleep apnea. He is currently taking medications for these conditions, and his blood sugar levels and blood pressure are well-controlled. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He is interested in losing weight but is not comfortable with the idea of surgery. He does not have any history of inflammatory bowel disease, gastroparesis, or peptic ulcer disease. He has a normal upper endoscopy, and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He does not have any history of aortic pathology, peripheral arterial disease, or renal insufficiency. He does not have any active infections or autoimmune diseases. He does not have any history of a major psychiatric disorder or an eating disorder. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the procedure.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy woman living in the United States. She works as a teacher and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and camping. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to any medications or vaccines. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and is willing to abstain from alcohol intake for 24 hours prior to each study visit. She is willing to have samples stored for future research, including genetic research. She is of childbearing potential but agrees to practice effective contraception or abstinence for 4 weeks prior to study initiation through 12 weeks after the second vaccine administration. She is willing to keep a symptom diary for 7 days after each vaccine and to record her temperature and any redness around the injection site. She is also willing to document and, if possible, photograph any mosquito bites she gets. She is excited to participate in this clinical trial and hopes that the vaccine will help prevent mosquito-borne diseases and reduce the spread of these diseases worldwide.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with HIV infection within the past 6 months. She is currently asymptomatic and has no history of AIDS-defining condition. Her CD4 count is above 300 cells/mm3. She is not taking any immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory drugs, chronic nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, or bone marrow suppressive drugs. She has no history of malignancies or mucocutaneous herpes infection requiring systemic treatment. She had a negative PPD test within the past month. She has no inflammatory bowel disease, peptic ulcer disease, obesity combined with insulin-requiring diabetes, liver disease, or chronic renal disease within the past 6 months. She tested negative for HBsAg or hepatitis C antibody within the past 2 weeks. She had a chest radiograph within the past 60 days that showed no evidence of cavity disease, infiltrates, or scars from prior disease that would preclude diagnosis of a new infectious process or drug-induced pneumonitis. She is not currently taking zidovudine or lamivudine. She does not have a history of alcohol abuse.

This is a 58-year-old male with a past medical history of primary open-angle glaucoma and hypertension. He underwent phacoemulsification plus trabeculectomy surgery on his left eye in June 2017 due to uncontrolled intraocular pressure despite medication. His preoperative baseline values showed astigmatism of 2.5 diopters in the left eye. The patient has no history of corneal diseases and is not currently experiencing any acute or chronic corneal issues. He is compliant with his medications and has regular follow-up visits with his ophthalmologist. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study to help further understand the effects of the surgery on corneal astigmatism.

This is a 33-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic gastrointestinal symptoms for the past 5 years. She reports bloating, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, and gastroesophageal reflux. She has tried eliminating gluten from her diet but has not noticed a significant improvement in her symptoms. She has since been diagnosed with non-celiac wheat sensitivity (NCWS) and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the prevalence of lactose intolerance and cow's milk protein allergy (CMPA) in NCWS patients with self-reported gastrointestinal symptoms related to milk and/or milk derivatives ingestion. She reports occasionally consuming milk and cheese but has noticed that it tends to worsen her symptoms. She is willing to participate in lactose breath tests and DBPC cow's milk protein challenges to diagnose lactose intolerance and CMPA, respectively. She is not currently taking steroids or antihistamines and has no other organic cutaneous or gastrointestinal diseases. She hopes that participating in this trial will help her better understand the relationship between her symptoms and lactose intolerance and CMPA.

A 43-year-old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 2 years ago. She currently experiences pain and swelling in multiple joints including her hands, wrists, and knees. She is taking methotrexate (20mg/week) for the past 6 months, which has improved her symptoms but still experiences occasional flare-ups. She has no other significant medical history, including no history of malignancy or tuberculosis. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore a potential new treatment option.

A 50-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus has been taking glimepiride for the past year, but his glycemic control remains inadequate with an HbA1c of 8.2%. He is intolerant to metformin and has not taken any other anti-diabetes medication (oral or injection) in the past 12 weeks. He has no history of acute metabolic conditions such as ketoacidosis or lactic acidosis within the past 6 months. He has been taking sulfonylurea for less than 5 years and has no known hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or to drugs with similar chemical structures. He is not pregnant and has no other medical conditions that may interfere with his participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has previously undergone a successful percutaneous coronary intervention for bifurcation disease. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medication to manage these conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not use recreational drugs or alcohol. He is physically active and engages in regular exercise. He is currently asymptomatic but is concerned about the long-term prognosis of his condition. His last cardiac catheterization showed restenosis involving the bifurcation, and he is interested in participating in the LATINA registry to better understand his prognosis. He has a good understanding of the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

45-year-old female with a history of obesity and multiple pregnancies presents with a symptomatic umbilical hernia that has been gradually increasing in size over the past year. Physical exam reveals a reducible umbilical hernia with a defect size of 1.5 cm. The patient is a non-smoker and has no prior history of abdominal surgeries. She has provided written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of non-absorbable sutures versus mesh repair for small umbilical hernias. She has no comorbidities and is otherwise healthy.

56 y/o South Asian Canadian with a history of type 2 diabetes and CAD. The patient has been on maximally tolerated statin therapy but still has LDL levels above 2.0 mmol/L. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and provide written consent. The patient has not made any changes to their current lipid-lowering therapy in the last 12 weeks and does not have uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c < 0.10) or significant hepatic or renal disease (ALT < 2x ULN and eGFR > 30 mL/min/1.73 m²). The patient's triglyceride levels are below 5.0 mmol/L. The patient is of South Asian ethnicity and has at least 3 of 4 grandparents born in a South Asian country (i.e. India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Bhutan).

The patient is a 3-month-old healthy infant with no significant past medical history. The infant's parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have provided informed consent. The infant has not received any poliomyelitis vaccine before. The infant's temperature is within the eligible range of <=37.0°C on axillary setting. The infant has no known allergies or other medical conditions that would exclude them from participating in the trial. The parents are willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and are able to understand and sign the informed consent.

80 year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. The patient is scheduled for elective knee replacement surgery under general anesthesia. He has no history of delirium or neurological disorders. He is able to communicate effectively and has no language barriers. Echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. The patient has no history of sinus bradycardia or atrioventricular block. His renal function is normal and he is not on dialysis. The patient is expected to survive for more than 24 hours after surgery.

A 47 year old woman is diagnosed with cervical cancer. She has a history of heavy smoking and is currently on medication for hypertension. She has been experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding for the past few months along with lower back pain and abdominal discomfort. Upon examination, a biopsy of the cervix is taken and she is found to have adenocarcinoma of the uterine cervix. An FDG PET scan is performed, and it shows positive pelvic lymph nodes but no evidence of metastatic disease outside of the pelvis. Her Karnofsky Performance Status is 70. Blood work shows WBC of 5,000/mm3, platelets of 130,000 mm3, BUN of 22 mg/dl, creatinine of 0.9 mg/dl, and bilirubin of 1.2 mg/dl. She has not had any prior malignancies or chemotherapy, and she has not undergone pelvic radiation therapy. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 30-year-old man has a history of cocaine addiction for the past 5 years. He has been trying to quit for the last 2 years but with no success. He has been experiencing symptoms of ADHD such as difficulty in paying attention, impulsiveness, and hyperactivity. He finds it hard to focus on a task for an extended period and has a short attention span. He is also forgetful and has trouble remembering things. He is currently not taking any medications for ADHD or any other psychiatric disorder. He has never had any brain surgery, seizures, or epilepsy. He is in good physical health and has no history of any significant somatic illness. He has been abstinent from cocaine for 15 days and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 47-year-old man with a history of ulcerative colitis for the past 12 years. He currently takes mesalamine and has had several colonoscopies in the past to monitor his condition. His last colonoscopy showed mild inflammation with no evidence of dysplasia. He has a first-degree relative with a history of colon cancer. He has been referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of chromoendoscopy to improve the detection of dysplasia in patients with chronic inflammatory bowel disease. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 30 year old Chinese woman who is in good health with no history of serious medical conditions. She has a body mass index of 22 kg/m2 and her serum LDL-C concentration is between 1.8 mmol/L and 4.9 mmol/L. She is willing to maintain her current regular diet and physical activity, and is willing to comply with protocol required visit schedule and visit requirements. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using effective contraception. She has no history of allergic reactions or previous anti-PCSK-9 treatment. She is not currently taking any medications, herb, vitamins or nutraceuticals that could alter serum lipids. She has not consumed any alcohol or caffeinated beverages within 72 hours prior to the trial. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of IBI306.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is currently in good health. She has a BMI of 22.8 kg/m^2 and has no history of any significant medical conditions, including disorders in the digestive system, neuropsychiatric system, endocrine system, liver, and cardiovascular system. She has the ability to comprehend the objectives and contents of the study and has expressed willingness to sign the informed consent form in writing. The patient is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety of HIP1701.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been using short-acting opioids for the past 5 years. He reports using an average of 100mg of morphine equivalent daily and has not used any opioids for at least 12 hours prior to screening. He has physical dependence on opioids and meets the DSM-IV-TR criteria for opioid addiction. His clinical opioid withdrawal scale (COWS) score is 12. He is in good general health and has no history of suicidal ideation or behavior. He has not used any long-acting opioids in the last 72 hours and has not participated in any other clinical trials involving investigational drugs or devices in the last 30 days. He has no known hypersensitivity, allergy or intolerance to buprenorphine, naloxone or related drugs.

Patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) diagnosed 2 years ago. He has been treated with rivaroxaban for the past 8 months and has been compliant with the medication. The patient has no history of prosthetic heart valves or severe valvulopathies. He has no known cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent. The patient has no chronic infections or systemic autoimmune diseases. He has no history of active cancer or liver insufficiency. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend all required study visits.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He is scheduled to undergo an elective pancreatectomy. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of significant heart or lung disease, and his kidney and liver function tests are within normal limits. He does not have any known allergies to gelofusine or human albumin. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 30 year old healthy male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He works as an office clerk and exercises regularly, maintaining a healthy lifestyle. He has no known allergies and has never participated in a clinical trial before. His blood pressure, heart rate, and clinical laboratory test results are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research and is willing to comply with study related constraints.

A 60-year-old woman was referred to the hospital for evaluation of chest pain and shortness of breath. She experienced these symptoms at rest and during physical activity for the past week. She has a medical history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She takes amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg daily. She had a previous myocardial infarction 5 years ago and underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). She quit smoking 2 years ago after smoking for 30 years. Her family history is significant for coronary artery disease (CAD), with her father having a myocardial infarction at age 50. She is postmenopausal and had a hysterectomy at age 45. She had a negative pregnancy test at screening. She has never had an MRI or SPECT, but had a quantitative coronary angiography (CXA) 3 months ago, which showed a 50% stenosis in her left anterior descending artery. She is currently not lactating or pregnant. She was not previously included in this study and has not received any investigational product in the past 30 days or is scheduled to do so. She does not have any known allergies or contraindications to the investigational product. She is conscious and able to comply with study procedures and provided written, informed consent. She is suspected of having CAD due to her clinical signs and symptoms and was referred for a SPECT for a functional evaluation of myocardial perfusion, which she underwent 2 weeks ago. The findings of SPECT were not taken into account for inclusion purposes. She did not have any other stress examination or MRI contrast medium in the past 24 hours or scheduled in the next 24 hours. She does not have lactating, pregnancy, clinically active, serious, life-threatening disease, with a life expectancy of less than 1 month, or a bypass graft. She does not have second or third-degree atrioventricular block, sick sinus syndrome or a symptomatic bradycardia, asthma, bronchospasms, or obstructive pulmonary disease, severe hypotension (<90 mm Hg systolic), unstable angina pectoris, or a decompensated congestive cardiac failure. Her ECG does not show a prolonged QT interval, and she does not have a contra-indication for MRI according to clinical guidelines, local regulations, or manufacturer's recommendations. She did not consume coffee, tea, coke, chocolate, or other caffeinated beverages in the last 24 hours before the adenosine administration.

A 72-year-old male retiree who lives independently came to the clinic for a check-up. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has a BMI of 26. He is able to complete 180 meters during the 6-minute walk test without an assistive device. His SPPB score is 8. He has no history of neurological or neuromuscular diseases that cause impaired muscle function or mobility. He has not participated in any interventional clinical study or has been treated with any investigational drugs within 30 days or 5 half-lives whichever is longer, prior to the initiation of screening. He exercises minimally and has not participated in any resistance training program before. He is willing and able to sign the IRB approved informed consent form. He is not an employee of the Astellas Group or vendors involved in the study.

A 53-year-old man was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. The diagnosis was made after he noticed a painless lump in his neck that did not go away after two weeks. He went to his primary care physician who referred him to a specialist for further evaluation. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of cancer. The patient underwent a thorough evaluation by a head and neck cancer specialist and was found to have no distant metastasis. He was scheduled for a continuous course of intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and concurrent cisplatin chemotherapy. His treatment plan involves a cumulative radiation dose of 66 Gy over six weeks. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension that is well controlled on medication. His blood pressure is 130/80, pulse rate is 75, respiratory rate is 16 and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a palpable lymph node in the neck. His laboratory results show adequate bone marrow, hepatic and renal function. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent.

As this is a clinical trial for a study on middle school students, there is no need for a patient description. However, to clarify, the trial is not recruiting patients, but rather middle school students who meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been walking for exercise for the past 6 months. She walks for 30 minutes at a moderate pace, three times a week. She is interested in increasing her physical activity level and maintaining it over the long-term. She has participated in the National Walkers' Health Study in the past and has internet access. She is looking for a supportive and engaging platform to track her progress and connect with others who share similar goals. She is motivated to work towards completing the virtual transcontinental route and earn awards for her achievements.

35-year-old male with a Quetelet index of 29.5 kg/m2 was referred to the clinical trial for the comparison of the effects of homogenized, unhomogenized, and skimmed milk on postprandial metabolism. He has no history of lactose intolerance, smoking, familial hypercholesterolemia, or drug abuse. He has a stable body weight with no weight gain or loss of more than 3 kg in the past three months. He has no severe medical conditions that might interfere with the study, such as epilepsy, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, inflammatory bowel diseases, and rheumatoid arthritis. He has no active cardiovascular disease, congestive heart failure, or recent event (acute myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident). He has not used an investigational product within the previous 1 month and is willing to stop the consumption of vitamin supplements, fish oil capsules, or products rich in plant stanol or sterol esters 3 weeks before the start of the study. He is willing to give up being a blood donor (or having donated blood) from 8 weeks before the start of the study and during the study. The patient has no difficulty with venipuncture as evidenced during the screening visits.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who has been suffering from osteoarthritis in his right knee for the past 5 years. He has tried various non-surgical treatments including physical therapy, pain medications, and injections, but has not experienced significant relief. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical or surgical history. He has a BMI of 28 and is a non-smoker. He is motivated to undergo knee replacement surgery and is interested in the Oxford Partial knee arthroplasty.

The patient is a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse for the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She has no history of vaginal bleeding and has not been on hormonal replacement therapy in the past three months. Her recent mammogram and oncotic cytology were normal. She has not had any renal or hepatic disease and does not have porphyria. She has never had venous thromboembolism and her prolapse is not ulcerated. Ultrasound showed that her endometrium measures less than 5mm. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the difference of three vaginal estrogens creams comparative with placebo on improvement of hormonal cytology, local and systemic climacteric complaints, as well as its endometrial security.

This study is an extension study, so no new subjects will be enrolled. The study will evaluate the persistence of immune response in Chinese female subjects who received three doses of the HPV-16/18 vaccine in the HPV-058 study. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with high-risk stage II breast cancer with 8 positive lymph nodes. She has undergone lumpectomy and axillary dissection followed by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and hormonal therapy. Her most recent CT scan and bone scan showed no evidence of disease. She is currently taking adjuvant hormonal therapy and has been advised to continue for the next 5 years. She has a history of peripheral neuropathy, for which she has been receiving medical treatment for the past 2 months. She has no other significant medical history, is not pregnant, and is using adequate contraception. She understands and is willing to sign the informed consent document to participate in the study.

A 45 year old woman complains of tingling, numbness, and pain in her right hand and wrist. The pain is described as a burning sensation that radiates from her wrist up to her forearm. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 8 weeks and they have been steadily worsening. The patient works in a factory and performs repetitive tasks with her hands for many hours each day. She reports that the pain and numbness are most severe at night and often wakes her up from sleep. Physical examination reveals positive Tinel's sign and Phalen's test. Nerve conduction studies show mild to moderate severity of median nerve lesion. The patient has no history of surgery or steroid injections in the upper extremity and reports no other systemic diseases or traumas in the affected area. She is not pregnant and has no contraindications for exercise.

A 58-year-old woman has recently been diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia. She completed induction chemotherapy and is now in remission. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. Her blood work is within normal limits, and she has no evidence of cardiac, hepatic, or renal dysfunction. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. She is a haploidentical 1st-degree relative and has a donor who is 50 years old and in excellent health. The donor performed well on the medical and psychosocial evaluation and is 4/6 HLA-matched at HLA-A, -B, or -DRB1. The patient has not received systemic anti-neoplastic therapy or radiotherapy within 14 days of study treatment. The patient has not had a positive pregnancy test and is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception during the entire study treatment period and through 6 months after the last dose of lenalidomide. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the REMS® program. She has no history of active hepatitis B or C and is not HIV-positive. She is not taking thalidomide or lenalidomide and does not have known hypersensitivity to these drugs. She does not have significant cardiac disease and has not had a cerebrovascular event with persistent neurologic deficit. She has no history of erythema nodosum or ataxia, cranial or peripheral neuropathy. She has not had a systemic infection requiring IV antibiotic therapy within 7 days preceding the first dose of study drug or other severe infection. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer. She has been receiving chemotherapy for the past 3 months and has noticed a decline in her functional mobility. She experiences pain in her joints and muscles and has difficulty performing daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. She has a life expectancy of more than 6 months and is fluent in English. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to improve her functional status through collaborative targeted case management. She has a working phone to communicate with the study team and is capable of completing questionnaires by herself or with assistance. She provides informed written consent to participate in the study.

A premature male infant born at a gestational age of 32 weeks with a birth weight of 1.8 kg. The infant was intubated immediately after birth and has been on mechanical ventilation for the past 3 weeks due to respiratory distress syndrome. The infant is stable now and ready for extubation. The parents have given their consent to participate in the study. There is no history of any malformations or clinical/surgical conditions that would prevent the infant from being positioned in either prone or supine position after extubation.

The patient is a 30 year old woman with no history of skin diseases or allergies. She has Fitzpatrick skin type II and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of a new health care product. She has no skin marks or injuries in the test region and is willing to adhere to the study procedures and requirements. The patient has no current or recent use of immunosuppressants, antihistamines, non-hormonal anti-inflammatory drugs or corticoids, nor has she received any vaccinations in the past 3 weeks. She has not participated in any clinical trial within the past 21 days and is not a professional involved in the conduct of the protocol.

The patient is a 24-year-old European American female who occasionally drinks alcohol. She has no significant medical history and is in good health as determined by medical history, physical exam, and laboratory tests. She is able to read and comprehend eighth-grade English and can hear and comprehend verbal instructions. She does not wear eyeglasses and can resolve 2 dots, each 2 mm in diameter with centers placed 5 mm apart on a card placed 20 inches from the bridge of the nose. She has no current or prior history of any serious disease, including head trauma causing loss of consciousness, cancer, CNS, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, endocrine, or alcohol or drug dependence, but has a history of alcohol abuse. She has not consumed more than 0.10 standard drinks per liter of total body water on any one occasion in the last month. She is not currently pregnant and has no intention to become pregnant. She has not used medications known to interact with alcohol within 2 weeks of the study.

A 27-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 22 presents for a bioequivalence study. She is in good health and has no history of psychiatric, gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal diseases. She is not on any oral contraceptives and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has a normal QTc interval and is willing to participate in the study procedures.

45 yo F with recent diagnosis of metabolic syndrome according to NCEP ATPIII criteria, referred for potential enrollment in clinical trial investigating the effects of fluvastatin on metabolic syndrome. PMH includes obesity with BMI of 32, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Her medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She reports having difficulty controlling her blood sugar levels despite adhering to her medications and diet. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her overall health and help with her diabetes management. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with COVID-19 three months ago. Although he has recovered from the virus, he still experiences physical limitations and significant fatigue. His overall health history is unremarkable, except for his recent COVID-19 infection. He has not been diagnosed with any cardiac condition that would prevent him from participating in an exercise program. He is not on any medications that would influence exercise performance. He is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine products. He is fluent in English and able to understand and sign a written informed consent document. He is willing and able to complete all study procedures.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has no history of hand musculoskeletal disorders. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and has a body mass index (BMI) between 20 and 25. He is between 170 and 179cm tall and has no neurological or orthopedic disorders. He is able to understand and follow instructions and has consented to participate in the study. The patient has no Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) contraindications and does not suffer from claustrophobia.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of occasional acne breakouts on her forehead and chin. She has fair skin with no significant pigmentation issues. She is generally healthy with no known allergies to any medications or products. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not participated in any investigational drug or device research study within the past 30 days. She has not used any topical corticosteroids or retinoids on her face for at least 1 week and has not used any systemic treatments for at least 4 weeks. She does not have any current sunburn, eczema, atopic dermatitis, perioral dermatitis, rosacea, or other topical conditions on the area to be treated. She does not anticipate any unprotected and intense UV exposure during the study period. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the informed consent process.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a BMI of 22 and is a non-smoker. He is physically active and enjoys hiking and skiing. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He has given written consent to participate in a study investigating the influence of breathing in an air-pocket during a simulated avalanche scenario on physiological parameters. The study aims to better understand how oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through snow, and how rebreathing of CO2 in addition to mild hypoxia influence physiological measures such as ECG, continuous invasive blood pressure, cerebral oximetry, and continuous pulse oximetry. The study may have clinical implications for better outcomes for victims of avalanches by providing additional air or oxygen close to the patient. The patient is excited to participate in the study to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge and potentially help save lives.

The patient is an 75-year-old retired accountant who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. She has been forgetting names, appointments and where she has placed certain items. She is concerned that her memory is getting worse and that she may be developing dementia. She is in good health otherwise, with no history of serious medical conditions, such as liver or kidney disease, nor is she taking any medication that could interfere with the cognitive function. The patient is fluent in English and has a study partner who is willing to participate in the study. She is willing to comply with study procedures and give written consent. She has not taken omega-3 dietary supplements containing >200 mg DHA per day during the last 6 months, nor has she received a physician prescribed vitamin B12, B3 or vitamin B-complex in the past 3 months. She has not participated in another clinical study in the previous month and is not currently participating in another study. The patient is willing to undergo PET scan and MRI-scan if selected for the subset group.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer three years ago. He has been receiving treatment with napabucasin in combination with chemotherapy in a Boston Biomedical-sponsored study and has shown a significant clinical benefit. He has experienced some mild side effects, including nausea and fatigue, but they have been manageable with medication. He is otherwise healthy, with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are well controlled with medication. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty swallowing or retaining orally administered medications. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not currently participating in any other interventional clinical studies. He has signed the consent form to participate in this rollover study to continue receiving napabucasin in the same dose and regimen as in the parent study. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and will be accessible for treatment and follow-up.

This is a 10-year-old boy who was involved in a motor vehicle collision while riding his bike. The car was traveling at a speed of 35 mph and hit him directly on his abdomen. He was wearing a helmet but did not have any other protective gear. He was immediately taken to the emergency department where he complained of abdominal pain and tenderness. His vital signs were stable, and his Glasgow Coma Scale score was 15. Physical examination revealed no other injuries except for the abdominal trauma. He meets the inclusion criteria for this trial as he has blunt torso trauma resulting from a significant mechanism of injury. He will be randomized to either the initial evaluation strategy with abdominal ultrasound or a strategy without abdominal ultrasound for the evaluation of children with blunt abdominal trauma. The trial aims to compare the rate of abdominal CT scanning, time to emergency department disposition, rate of missed/delayed diagnosis of intra-abdominal injury, and the costs between the two strategies.

The patient is a 16 year-old male with Marfan syndrome diagnosed by revised Ghent criteria. His echocardiogram showed a dilated aortic root with no dissection. His primary cardiologist has cleared him for exercise. He has a history of mild scoliosis but no back pain or other musculoskeletal complaints. He is currently not engaged in regular exercise and spends most of his time playing video games. He feels anxious about his diagnosis and is interested in learning more about how exercise can benefit his health. He lives with his parents and has no significant medical history or family history of Marfan syndrome.

A 48-year-old female diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma and failed anthracycline-containing regimen is currently seeking treatment options. She has also failed second-line treatment, which included chemotherapy and rituximab. Radiological studies have been performed, and a unilateral bone marrow biopsy was done within four weeks before the start of treatment. She has acceptable tumor burden, and the lymphoma requires treatment. Bone marrow reserve is likely to give a harvest of at least 2x10 6 peripheral CD34+ stem cells or the existence of such a harvest or a corresponding central harvest. Her total bilirubin level is within the acceptable limit, and her GFR is measured by Cystatin C of 50 ml/min. Her HIV, Hepatitis B, and C status are known, and she has a life expectancy of at least three months. She has no known CNS involvement, bone marrow involvement at harvest as measured by biopsy and flow cytometry, or prior radiation to a field that includes over or equal 25% of their red marrow, liver or lung, or to both kidneys. She has not received prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the last four weeks, and she is not pregnant or nursing. There is no significant pulmonary involvement, and liver involvement of lymphoma is not present.

14 yo M with a BMI of 32.6 kg/m2 (98th percentile for age and gender) presenting with concerns about his weight and difficulty controlling his blood sugar levels. The patient had a recent episode of hyperglycemia that was treated with insulin. He denies any history of endocrinopathy or medication use that may alter glucose metabolism. The patient speaks English and is interested in participating in a study investigating the relationship between adipocyte cell and lipid turnover in obese adolescents. Past medical history is notable for remote history of otitis media and appendectomy. Family history is significant for obesity and dyslipidemia in both parents.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of Sezary syndrome. He presented with erythroderma, which is a diffuse, red, scaly rash covering almost the entire body. He has noticed the rash for the past few months, and it has progressively worsened. He has been experiencing itching, fatigue, and weight loss. A skin biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Sezary syndrome. He has not received any prior systemic therapy for his disease. He is otherwise in good health with no significant medical history. His laboratory work is remarkable for mild leukopenia and lymphopenia. He is currently not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has been informed about the study.

The patient is a 35 year old male who sustained a spinal cord injury at the C5 level in a motor vehicle accident 2 years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath that has been gradually worsening over the past few months. He reports feeling like he cannot get enough air, especially when lying down or during physical activity. He has not been diagnosed with asthma or any other chronic pulmonary disease. He is a former smoker, having quit over a year ago, and reports occasionally using vaping products. He is currently employed as a graphic designer and works from home. He is able to sit upright in a chair or wheelchair for extended periods of time. He is interested in participating in this study to better understand the mechanisms of his dyspnea and to potentially improve his breathing pattern.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with prediabetes after a routine blood test. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes, with her mother and two siblings currently living with the condition. She works as an office administrator and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has noticed increased fatigue and difficulty losing weight, despite efforts to eat a healthy diet and exercise regularly. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but she drinks alcohol socially on the weekends. She has never participated in a research study before but is interested in learning more about her condition and potentially contributing to finding new treatments for diabetes.

A 19-year-old college student who is currently receiving mental health services at their university counseling center due to symptoms of depression and anxiety. The student speaks English as their primary language and is able to provide informed consent. They have no history of communication disorders and do not have any serious medical or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with their ability to complete the study. The student has no intellectual disability that would be deemed a barrier to participation by their therapist. They are willing to participate in the study to help optimize the smartphone-based algorithms for the early detection of mental health and suicidal risk in a student population.

This clinical trial is not applicable for patient description as it does not involve recruiting patients. It is an observation study that compares the outcomes of medical augmented reality glasses and general monitors in endoscopic diagnosis for early gastric cancer. The participants will be patients with early gastric cancer who are scheduled for endoscopic submucosal dissection and have voluntarily agreed to participate in the study. They must be at least 19 years old and provide written informed consent. The exclusion criteria is limited to patients with poor general medical condition that prevents them from understanding and consenting to the study.

This clinical trial is an expanded access program for IFx-Hu2.0, which may be considered for adult patients aged 18 years and above with stage III through IV cutaneous melanoma, advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), or advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) who have failed all available treatment options. The eligibility criteria are not specified, but interested patients can contact the responsible party for more information.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 8 years. She has been on methotrexate (MTX) treatment for the past 6 months and has shown some improvement but still experiences joint pain and stiffness. She has tried other disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in the past, but none have been effective. She works as a part-time accountant and has difficulty completing her job due to her RA symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. At screening, she has 10 tender joints and 8 swollen joints. Her CRP level is elevated. She has no ongoing infections or wounds. She has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 12 weeks. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her RA symptoms and quality of life.

A 56-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was measured to be 30%. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the "MEtabolomics and MicrObiomics in caRdIovAscular diseases Mannheim (MEMORIAM)" trial to identify disease-specific metabolic and microbiomic patterns in high-risk cardiovascular patients.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who worked in construction for over 20 years, where he was regularly exposed to asbestos. He is a former smoker who quit 10 years ago, but has a history of heavy tobacco use. He presents with a persistent cough, occasional chest pain, and shortness of breath. His medical history is significant for high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which are both well-controlled with medications. He denies any other significant medical conditions or surgeries. He lives alone and is retired. He has heard about the study and is interested in participating in the screening program. The patient is able to provide informed consent and participate in the study procedures.

32 yo F with a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing flares every few months despite being on medication. Her symptoms include joint pain, fatigue, and a rash on her face. She is currently married and has a supportive spouse who is willing to participate in the study as her caregiver. She has no significant history of psychiatric disorders or alcohol/drug abuse. She is fluent in English and has access to the internet. She is interested in participating in the study to see if mindfulness-based interventions can help improve her symptoms and overall quality of life. She passed the initial MRI screening and is currently participating in The University of Toronto Clinic and Database Research Program - Prognosis and Genetic Studies in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit 5 years ago. He presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. CT scan and PET scan showed a tumor in the right lung and spread to nearby lymph nodes. He has no history of other cancers or significant medical problems. His performance status is good, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1. His blood work shows normal liver and kidney function with no evidence of infection. He is not pregnant or lactating, nor is he attempting to conceive. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study participation. He is interested in participating in the trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 50-year-old African American man who lives in a low-income neighborhood. He works as a custodian and has health insurance through his employer. He has a history of smoking and drinking but quit both 10 years ago. He has a family history of colon cancer, and his doctor recommended him to get screened for colorectal cancer. He has been reluctant to get screened due to fear and anxiety related to the procedure. He also has difficulty navigating the healthcare system and understanding the screening process. He has a BMI of 31 and reports occasional constipation. He has not had any symptoms of colon cancer. He is interested in learning more about the screening process and receiving support in navigating the healthcare system.

This is a 45-year-old female with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) on maintenance hemodialysis. She has evidence of Chronic Kidney Disease Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD) and is currently receiving Erythropoietin Stimulating Agents (ESA) for management of her anemia. Her hemoglobin levels are between 10.0-11.5, and her iPTH levels are between 300-600 pg/ml. She has been on dialysis via artero-venous fistula and has a Kt/V greater/equal than 1.2. She has signed informed consent to participate in the study aimed at improving anemia management in ESRD patients with CKD-MBD. She will be randomized (1:1) to either the control group receiving standard care with an iPTH target of 300-540 pg/ml or the optimal CKD-MBD control group with an iPTH target of 150-300 pg/ml achieved with a therapeutic algorithm. She will receive a flexible dose of any active vitamin D available in Italy (calcitriol and paricalcitol-"Zemplar®") and cinacalcet("Mimpara®") to achieve iPTH, serum phosphorous, and serum calcium control.

Patient A is a 70-year-old female who recently fell and fractured her hip. She has a history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy and active. She is able to walk independently and has no neurological or musculoskeletal disorders. She underwent surgical fixation of her intertrochanteric hip fracture with an intramedullary nail according to the current international guidelines. She has provided written informed consent to participate in this study which aims to evaluate gait and mobility after surgical fixation of intertrochanteric hip fractures in elderly population with Gait Analysis in combination with clinical and radiographic information. She will undergo follow-up appointments at 6- and 12-months where gait parameters will be measured and recorded in the Gait Analysis Laboratory. Additionally, her clinical outcomes will be assessed according to the Harris Hip Score (HHS) and Western Ontario and Mc Master University (WOMAC), and dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) will be acquired at 12-months follow-up to collect T-score data.

A 57-year-old Caucasian male with a history of indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (FL grade 2) complains of persistent fatigue and night sweats. He was diagnosed with lymphoma 2 years ago and has received 1 prior systemic regimen. His most recent PET-CT scan showed disease progression. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is married and has two children. He is retired and spends most of his time reading and watching TV. His ECOG performance status is 1. His recent laboratory tests show normal renal and liver function. He is not taking any chronic immunosuppressants or systemic steroids. His baseline QTcF is within normal limits.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been the primary caregiver for her husband with dementia for the past 6 years. She has been feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and depressed lately, often feeling guilty for not being able to take care of her husband as well as she thinks she should. She has not sought any psychological intervention in the past year. She spends at least 3 hours a day taking care of her husband and has been doing so for the past 3 months. She scores 18 on the Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Scale (CES-D) and 14 on the Tension-Anxiety subscale from the Profile of Mood States scale (POMS). She also scores 20 on the Caregiver Guilt Questionnaire (CGQ). She is eligible for the study and is willing to participate in the intervention.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking who recently experienced chest pain and was diagnosed with triple vessel coronary artery disease (CAD). He is scheduled to undergo primary isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery with at least one left anterior descending (LAD) site and another anterolateral target. He has no previous history of CABG surgery and provides written informed consent to participate in the AMI-PONT trial. His left internal mammary artery (LIMA) is usable, and he has no concomitant cardiac procedures associated with CABG. He has no contraindications to cardiopulmonary bypass or Multi-Slice Computed Tomography (MSCT) graft assessment. He is not pregnant nor lactating, and he has no history of severe hypersensitivity to iodinated contrast agents or known or suspected pheochromocytoma. He has an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) greater than 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; therefore, he does not have moderate to severe renal impairment. He has no history of chronic atrial fibrillation or any other cardiac rhythm that precludes reliable ECG triggering. He is not in severe congestive heart failure, New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV, despite coronary revascularization and maximal medical treatment.

55 year old male with a 7 year history of type II diabetes mellitus presents to the hospital outpatient clinic. The patient reports inconsistent glucose control despite compliance with his medication regimen and diet. He reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia and complains of fatigue, polyuria and polydipsia. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and obesity with a BMI of 33. He is a smoker with a 20 pack-year history and reports occasional alcohol use. He has no known history of microvascular or macrovascular complications. The patient speaks Dutch fluently and is willing to participate in the study. There are no indications of pregnancy or a life expectancy less than one year.

Leilani is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer a year ago. She completed initial regional and systemic treatment 2 months ago and is currently living on Oahu. She has been feeling tired and lethargic since her cancer diagnosis, and she hasn't been able to engage in any physical activity due to her treatment. Her physician has cleared her to participate in the trial, and she is interested in trying hula as a form of physical activity. She has no history of any other major medical conditions and is generally in good health. She is excited to participate in the trial and is looking forward to seeing the biological and psychosocial effects of hula as a form of physical activity for female cancer survivors.

The patient is a 45-year-old American man who has been struggling with alcohol dependence and abuse for the past 5 years. He has attempted to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is now seeking formal help and has been admitted to an alcohol treatment center. He has a stable medical history with no significant physical or mental health issues. His family history is positive for alcohol abuse in his father and grandfather. He works as a construction worker and is married with two children. During the baseline interview, he expressed a strong desire to quit drinking and improve his relationship with his family.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has been taking metformin and insulin to manage his blood sugar levels. He reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia and has a BMI of 30. He does not have any significant past medical history or allergies. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not exercise regularly. He has not experienced any complications related to diabetes, such as peripheral neuropathy or retinopathy. He does not have any known liver diseases or iron overload disorders. He has not participated in any clinical trials previously. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 10-year-old boy with a history of HIV-1 infection since birth presents to the clinic with his mother for a routine check-up. The boy has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 3 years and has been virally suppressed with no detectable viral load. He is otherwise healthy, with no complaints of fever, cough, or weight loss. His mother reports good adherence to his medication regimen. The boy and his mother express an interest in participating in a clinical trial to help advance HIV research. After a thorough screening process, he is found to meet the eligibility criteria for Arm B of the study, as he has no or moderate immune suppression at the time of study entry as defined by CDC classification and has been on antiretroviral treatment for more than 7 weeks. He is scheduled to receive 10 units of HIV-1 Immunogen intramuscularly at 0, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. His antiretroviral therapy will continue as usual, and any changes to his regimen will be made in accordance with the study protocol. The boy and his mother are fully informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for the past 5 years. She has been on intensive insulin therapy with a combination of a basal, long-acting insulin and insulin rapid analog before each meal. Despite her efforts to manage her diabetes, her HbA1c levels have remained above 8% for the past 12 months. She has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is able to use a PDA-Phone and is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant nor is she a prisoner. She is excited to participate in the study in hopes of improving her blood glucose control and overall quality of life.

A 72-year-old man was brought to the emergency department after falling from a ladder while cleaning the gutters of his house. He landed on his right hip and was unable to get up. He was diagnosed with a trochanteric hip fracture (AO 31-A2) and scheduled for surgery with a sliding hip screw (SHS) with or without a trochanteric support plate (TSP). He is able to walk independently with the use of crutches and has consented to participate in the clinical trial. He has no previous history of hip fractures or surgeries with retained metal work in the same hip. The patient has no concomitant diseases that would shorten his life expectancy.

The patient is a 30-year-old Black man who has had sex with both men and women in the past 12 months. He is concerned about his risk of contracting HIV and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help him reduce his risk of acquiring and transmitting the virus. He is committed to attending six counseling sessions with a trained counselor and is willing to undergo behavioral risk assessments and HIV and STD testing at three different time points during the study. He understands the importance of the study in providing targeted HIV prevention interventions to Black MSM/W and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He does not inject drugs and has engaged in recent unprotected sex.

A 34-year-old female patient was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 2 years ago. She has a history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She has been treated with different medications, including corticosteroids, aminosalicylates, and antibiotics.
