However, she developed multiple draining enterocutaneous fistulas in the last few months that did not respond to medical therapy. She has no other significant medical history and is a non-smoker. Her physical examination reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen and multiple draining fistulas in the perianal area. Laboratory tests show an elevated CRP level and leukocytosis. Stool culture is negative. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of fistulizing Crohn's disease and is willing to receive infliximab infusions every 8 weeks.

27-year-old nulliparous woman, currently 38 weeks pregnant, with no significant medical history, presents to the hospital in labor. She requests epidural analgesia for pain management during labor. She is eligible for inclusion in the study as she meets the age criteria and is having a spontaneous vaginal delivery. She has no history of multiple gestation or neonatal ICU admission, so she is not excluded from the study. The duration of epidural infusion and total micrograms of fentanyl delivered will be recorded for this patient, along with her breastfeeding behavior and duration of hospital stay post-delivery.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure. He was recently admitted to the hospital due to an episode of acute decompensation of his condition. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently on a medication regimen that includes lisinopril, metoprolol, furosemide, aspirin and atorvastatin. The patient lives alone, has a home telephone line and is able to use basic technology. At the time of hospital discharge, the patient was classified as NYHA class III. He has previously experienced anxiety and depression due to his condition. The patient has no history of dementia or confusion that would interfere with the use of the HomMed telemonitoring equipment.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a glioblastoma multiforme brain tumor approximately 10 months ago. The patient underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by a course of radiation therapy of 60 Gy in 30 fractions. She is currently not receiving any adjuvant chemotherapy or other treatments for the brain tumor. She reports experiencing fatigue, cognitive impairment, and subjective confusion since undergoing radiation therapy, which have negatively impacted her quality of life. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of allergies, and her only current medication is amlodipine for her blood pressure. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Status is 80, and she has no significant neurological deficits. The patient is not currently taking any dementia drugs, cognitive enhancers, neuroleptics, or anti-parkinsonian agents. She is not hypersensitive to donepezil and is not currently taking Ketoconazole or Quindine. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to give informed consent to participate in the study, including signing the consent form. The patient has a telephone and is able to complete self-reported questionnaires at baseline and 12 and 24 weeks.

This is a 63-year-old female with a diagnosis of locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She presented with a 2-month history of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. CT scan revealed a 4 cm mass in the head of the pancreas with encasement of the superior mesenteric artery and vein. She underwent an EUS-guided biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She was deemed to have unresectable disease due to the extent of vascular involvement. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and stable pain controlled with analgesics. Her blood work is within normal limits, including her creatinine, bilirubin, and alkaline phosphatase. She has no other medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. She has not received any prior abdominal radiation or systemic chemotherapy. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is interested in exploring treatment options for her cancer.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman with a history of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) that has relapsed after two cycles of induction chemotherapy. The patient has undergone lymphodepleting chemotherapy and is currently experiencing recurrent disease in the bone marrow identified by immunohistochemistry. The patient is eligible for this trial as she has CD22 expression on malignant cells at relapse. The patient has adequate vital organ function with a creatinine level of <1.6 mg/dL, ALT/AST level of ≤ 3x upper limit of normal range, and total or direct bilirubin level of ≤ 2.0 mg/dL. The patient has a left ventricle ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 40% confirmed by ECHO/MUGA. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no contraindications for leukapheresis. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is agreeable to using acceptable birth control methods. The patient does not have active hepatitis B, active hepatitis C, HIV infection, class III/IV cardiovascular disability according to the New York Heart Association Classification, clinically apparent arrhythmia, active acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) requiring systemic therapy, planned concurrent treatment with systemic steroids or immunosuppressant medications, CNS3 disease that is progressive on therapy, or a known history or prior diagnosis of optic neuritis or other immunologic or inflammatory disease affecting the central nervous system.

This clinical trial is not applicable to an individual patient as it is a study to develop and evaluate a web-based gardening game to teach nutrition and combat obesity in 3rd to 5th grade children and their families. Therefore, there is no specific patient description required.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 3 years. She has been experiencing frequent flare-ups and has been on various medications including corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, but with limited success. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient has been experiencing weight loss and has been struggling with her appetite due to nausea and abdominal pain. She currently has a BMI of 19.5 and her nutritional status has been assessed as moderate to high risk. She has been referred for the standardized nutritional therapy trial and has given informed consent to participate. Her family history is negative for any gastrointestinal disease. She is otherwise healthy, alert, with no acute distress, and is eager to participate in the trial to improve her quality of life and long-term prognosis.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who recently immigrated to Geneva, Switzerland from a high TB incidence country. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. She has been identified as a close contact of a person diagnosed with active TB and has consented to participate in the study. She reports no symptoms of TB and has not received the BCG vaccine. Her medical records show no history of HIV infection or previous TB treatment. She is willing to undergo both the TST and the T-SPOT.TB blood test for the purpose of this study.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa and has been experiencing significant vision loss over the past few years. She has received a RETINA IMPLANT Alpha AMS and has been using it for the past 6 months. She is willing and able to give written informed consent to participate in the post-market clinical follow-up (PMCF) study to monitor the safety, lifetime and efficacy of the implant. She has no other medical conditions and is motivated to participate in the study to help improve the understanding of the effectiveness of the RETINA IMPLANT Alpha AMS.

A 10-year-old female student who has been experiencing myopia for the past 2 years. The patient's myopia is between -1.00D to -3.00D, with-the-rule astigmatism not more than 1.50D, and the difference between the eyes is no more than 1.25 spherical equivalent. The patient's best corrected visual acuity is equal to or better than 0.10 in logMAR scale (Snellen VA 6/7.5 or better) and eyes are straight at distance and near with best subjective correction. The patient has not undergone any prior myopic treatment, refractive surgery or progressive lens wear for myopic control before and during the study period. The patient has no abnormal ocular and general health and has no history of rigid contact lenses (including orthokeratology lenses) wearing. The patient has no systemic condition that might affect refractive development, such as Down syndrome or Marfan's syndrome, and no ocular conditions that might affect the refractive error, such as cataract or ptosis. The patient is willing to be randomized and wear the study spectacles according to the instructions from the practitioner and come back for follow-up in the Optometry Clinic during the study period.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who has given birth to her first child vaginally with the help of a vacuum extractor. She experienced a first-degree perineal tear during delivery and received epidural analgesia for pain management. The patient is fluent in French and is affiliated with a national insurance scheme. She has no history of contraindications to local anesthetics and is not currently experiencing severe arterial hypotension. The patient has given written consent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to have her pain levels monitored at various times over the course of the immediate postpartum period.

28-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with major depressive disorder and has a history of suicidal ideation. She has been prescribed medication but has experienced adverse side effects and is reluctant to continue taking it. She has a part-time job and lives alone. She has a supportive family and has been attending therapy sessions regularly. She owns an iPhone and is comfortable using it for daily tasks. She is interested in participating in the study to help find alternative ways to manage her symptoms and potentially prevent future suicidal thoughts.

47-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who is undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at the Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Center of the "Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein". The patient has a history of smoking and moderate alcohol consumption. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiotherapy and has been experiencing oral changes such as mucositis, xerostomia, and dysgeusia. The patient has no known history of periodontal disease or other infectious foci prior to transplantation and has normal chewing, swallowing, and phonation functions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will be able to attend all laser therapy sessions.

The patient is a 40-year-old male diagnosed with urticaria, a condition characterized by red, itchy bumps on the skin. The symptoms have been persisting for the last 6 months and are affecting his daily routine. He has not received any treatment for the condition so far. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of chronic illnesses or allergies. His blood tests and physical examination are normal. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the use of genetic screening for HLA-B*1301 to determine the risk of dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome (DHS) associated with dapsone treatment. The aim of the trial is to evaluate if genetic screening for HLA-B*1301 can reduce the incidence of DHS in patients receiving dapsone treatment. The patient is dapsone-naïve and meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial. He is willing to complete the 6-week observation period and undergo the epicutaneous patch test (EPT) assessment if he experiences any suspected DHS during the study. He understands the benefits and risks of participating in the trial and has given his written informed consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who has been diagnosed with an extra cranial non seminomateous malignant germ cell tumor (NSMGCT). He has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss. The tumor was discovered during routine imaging for unrelated abdominal pain. The patient has no significant medical history or allergies. He is a high school student and enjoys playing basketball and video games. The patient is accompanied by his parents who are supportive of his treatment and have given their consent for him to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is willing to comply with the study procedures and is scheduled to start treatment soon.

The patient is a 45 year old male residing in the Philippines. He presented to the hospital with a fever, persistent cough, and shortness of breath for 7 days. He underwent a COVID-19 test and the result came back positive. He was subsequently admitted to the hospital for further management of his COVID-19 disease. During his hospitalization, he developed new-onset neurological symptoms including confusion, disorientation, and ataxia. His medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently taking amlodipine for his blood pressure. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a construction worker and has been unable to work since the onset of his symptoms. He was treated with remdesivir, dexamethasone and convalescent plasma for his COVID-19 disease and his neurological symptoms were managed with supportive care. He was discharged from the hospital after 2 weeks of hospitalization and is currently recovering at home.

A 25-year-old healthy female who is not pregnant or nursing and has a body weight of 55 kg with a BMI of 22.5 is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and has not consumed alcohol regularly. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days. The patient must agree to use two effective methods of contraception from the date of Screening until 90 days after the last dose of EDP 938. She is willing to sign an informed consent document and is of any ethnic origin between the ages of 18 and 55 years, inclusive. She does not have any clinically relevant evidence or history of illness or disease and has not had a febrile illness within 7 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She does not have any condition that may affect drug absorption and has not undergone gastrectomy or cholecystectomy.

A 45-year-old female presents with fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats for the past 2 months. She also reports enlarged lymph nodes in her neck and armpits. Biopsy of the lymph node revealed large B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, CD20 positive. The patient is scheduled to receive R-CHOP chemotherapy treatment, but it has not yet started. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has no history of lymphoma or any other type of cancer. Her performance status is good, and she is able to tolerate the PET/CT procedure. She is not pregnant, as determined by urinary β-HCG and blood test. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo the four PET/CT exams as described.

56-year-old male presenting to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath for the past 3 hours. The patient has a medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and the patient is diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient is eligible for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and is enrolled in the study investigating the efficacy of thrombus aspiration using Export Aspiration Catheter (Medtronic Corporation, California, USA) during primary PCI in acute myocardial infarction. The patient has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and is not pregnant. The patient is not known to have any hypersensitivity or contra-indication to contrast agent. The patient does not have left main disease or in-stent restenosis lesion, graft vessels lesion, or chronic total occlusion lesion. The patient's creatinine level is within normal limits, and there are no contraindications to aspirin, clopidogrel or cilostazol. The patient has not had prior PCI or bypass surgery and has not experienced an old myocardial infarction.

A 32-year-old female presents with a history of allergic rhinitis for the past 6 years. She reports experiencing symptoms such as nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes during the spring and fall seasons. She has been using over-the-counter allergy medication as needed but has not been prescribed any prescription medication for her symptoms. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and weighs 60 kg. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and she has a normal 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). She is comfortable with self-administration of intranasal medication and has no anatomical or medical conditions that may delay delivery or absorption of the study medication. She is currently not taking any prescription or non-prescription medication within the last 14 days before the first scheduled dose of the study drug. She is sexually active and practicing an effective method of birth control. She has no significant psychiatric or medical illness, and she has not undergone any facial reconstruction or surgery in the previous 2 years. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided.

A 68-year-old male diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease and with a study partner will be eligible for this clinical trial. The patient is required to be an English speaker and should not have any serious medical conditions such as type 1 diabetes, cancer, or recent cardiac events like heart attack or angioplasty that may confound the study. The patient must also not have any contraindications to oxaloacetate (OAA) intake. The study aims to examine the pharmacokinetics and safety of OAA in Alzheimer's patients, and the patient will be monitored for any potential side effects throughout the one-month study period.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. She has been taking metformin and glipizide for diabetes management. The patient underwent a coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery 3 years ago and is currently on aspirin therapy (75 mg/day) since then. She has no history of bleeding disorders or any other significant medical conditions. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication and is within normal limits. Her BMI is 27. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her recent lipid profile shows high LDL and low HDL levels. Her hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is 7%. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her platelet function and reduce the risk of future cardiovascular events.

There are two patient descriptions that can be generated for this clinical trial, one for SPMS patients and one for normal control volunteers.  SPMS Patient Description: The patient is a male or female between 25 and 65 years old who has been diagnosed with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS) and has an EDSS score between 3 and 7. The patient must weigh between 130 and 200 pounds. They must not have received previous treatment with DMF for disease management. They must not have had a relapse within the past 90 days prior to screening or not stabilized from a previous relapse prior to screening. The patient must not have a clinically significant brain MRI finding other than those related to MS. They must not have any contraindications to having a brain MRI or a lumbar puncture. They must not have any autoimmune diseases other than MS, or any chronic active infections requiring systemic treatment. They must not have been pregnant or breastfeeding, or males of fathering potential or females of childbearing potential who are unwilling or unable to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for at least 28 days after the last dose of DMF. They must not have had a history of drug or alcohol abuse within 2 years prior to screening.  Normal Control Volunteer Description: The patient is a male or female between 25 and 65 years old who does not have multiple sclerosis or any autoimmune diseases. They must weigh between 130 and 200 pounds. They must not have any contraindications to having a lumbar puncture. They must not have any chronic active infections requiring systemic treatment. They must not have been pregnant or breastfeeding, or males of fathering potential or females of childbearing potential who are unwilling or unable to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for at least 28 days after the last dose of DMF. They must not have had a history of drug or alcohol abuse within 2 years prior to screening. They will serve as a normal control group for comparison to SPMS patients.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman diagnosed with multiple myeloma 6 months ago. She has been receiving bortezomib at a dose of 1.3mg/m2 SQ weekly as part of her chemotherapy regimen. She presents to the clinic complaining of tingling and numbness in her hands and feet, which have been worsening over the last few weeks. She has no history of peripheral neuropathy before starting the treatment, and her National Cancer Institute (NCI)-Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v4.03 criteria score is <2. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. She takes a multivitamin tablet once daily, and she has no known allergies. Her lab study is as follows: FBS: 110 mg/dl HbA1c: 5.8% Cholesterol: 170 mg/dl TG: 90 mg/dl LDL: 100 mg/dl HDL: 50 mg/dl. She has no history of seizures or mood disorders. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 46-year-old man with end-stage renal disease who is scheduled to receive a kidney transplant from a living or deceased donor is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. He has no known contraindications to the administration of tacrolimus or other macrolides and study drug excipients. He agrees to use a highly reliable method of birth control. His donor-recipient negative cross match test is compatible with AB0 blood type. He is able to swallow tablets and capsules. He has not had a previous kidney transplant, and his anti-HLA Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) levels are not higher than 30%. He is not currently abusing drugs or alcohol. He is capable of understanding the purpose and risks of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol. He has not been treated with any other investigational agent in the 30 days prior to enrollment, and he is not positive for HCV, HBV, or HIV. He does not have a current diagnosis or history of malignancy within the past 5 years except basal or non-metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the skin successfully treated. He does not have any uncontrolled concomitant infection, systemic infection requiring treatment or any other unstable condition that could interfere with study objectives. He does not have severe diarrhea, vomiting, active peptic ulcer or GI disorder that may affect absorption of tacrolimus. He is not known to have hypersensitivity to tacrolimus or other macrolides and study drug excipients. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he is willing to use reliable methods of contraception.

50-year-old male diagnosed with sigmoid colon cancer, scheduled for laparoscopic surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension, well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and has not had any previous surgeries. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able to understand and provide written consent for participation in the study. The patient is affiliated with the national social security system and has no contraindications for anesthesia or surgical resection.

An 70-year-old retired telecommunications professional who is an associate of ASASTEL and has access to the internet at home is interested in participating in a cognitive training program. The patient reports occasional memory lapses and difficulty with word recall. They have no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and are currently not taking any medications that may affect cognitive function. The patient is proficient in accessing and navigating the internet and is willing to be evaluated and followed by the professional team. They score 30 points on the Mini Mental State Examination (MEEM). The patient is excited to improve their cognitive function and maintain their mental abilities as they age.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer 3 years ago. She has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy, hormone therapy, and radiation therapy, but her disease has progressed despite treatment. She has no history of heart disease, stroke, or thromboembolic events. Her performance status is 1 according to the ECOG scale, and she is able to carry out light or sedentary work. She has no active infection or inflammatory bowel disease. She is currently not taking any medications except for painkillers. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. She has been informed about the investigational nature of the study protocol and has given her consent to participate.

32 F with a history of Cushing's disease diagnosed 2 years ago. She underwent transphenoidal pituitary surgery, but her disease remains biochemically active with elevated cortisol levels. Pathology revealed a corticotroph adenoma. She has suffered from fatigue, easy bruising, and muscle weakness. She denies any recent weight gain. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension which is well controlled on lisinopril. She has no known drug allergies. She is not pregnant or lactating and is not planning to become pregnant in the near future.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese male who has been diagnosed with colon cancer and is scheduled for elective gastrointestinal surgery under general anesthesia. He has no history of cognitive difficulties or mental illness. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to cooperate with the researcher's requirements. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past month. The surgery is scheduled during the daytime, therefore he is not eligible for this study as night surgery is an exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis caused by chronic hepatitis B. He has had a history of alcohol abuse for the past 10 years and has stopped drinking for the past 6 months. He has been experiencing episodes of abdominal pain and fatigue for the last few months. He has a history of esophageal varices, which were discovered during a previous gastroscopy. He is currently taking medications for his liver cirrhosis and has been advised to undergo regular check-ups to monitor his condition. He is married and works as a construction worker. He is a non-smoker and has no history of drug abuse. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 bpm. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the diagnosis of bleeding in patients with liver cirrhosis.

30-year-old female with a history of myopia presents for a routine eye exam. She reports difficulty seeing distant objects clearly and has been experiencing eye strain, headaches, and eye fatigue. Her medical history is unremarkable and she takes no medications. Her visual acuity with current glasses is 20/40 in both eyes. Refraction reveals a spherical equivalent of -2.75 diopters in both eyes with no significant astigmatism. Autorefraction confirms the findings. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new method of refractive error correction and is deemed eligible based on her visual acuity and refractive error.

The patient is a 13-year-old boy who was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) two years ago. He has received multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but had a relapse of the disease six months ago. Despite further treatment, his cancer has become refractory, and his condition has deteriorated. He is now experiencing severe fatigue, weakness, and recurrent infections. The patient's parents are willing to enroll him in an experimental clinical trial that involves GC022 CAR-T cell immunotherapy for relapsed or refractory B-ALL. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and the medical team has explained the potential benefits and risks of the treatment. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent and are willing to comply with the planned visits, research, treatment planning, laboratory, and other test procedures.

56 yo M, retired Army veteran, with a history of smoking for over 30 years, admitted to the Portland VA Health Care System for evaluation of a newly diagnosed pulmonary nodule. The patient is currently an active smoker with a 1-pack per day history. The patient has expressed a desire to quit smoking but has not been successful in previous attempts. The patient is eligible for the TeaM OUT clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of having a newly diagnosed pulmonary nodule with a plan for surveillance and receiving care at the Portland VA Health Care System. The patient will be randomly assigned to either the TeaM OUT intervention group or the enhanced usual care group. The TeaM OUT intervention will consist of a letter describing the nodule and the importance of cessation related to the pulmonary nodule and notification that a Proactive IVR Quit Line will initiate contact, followed by call(s) from the Proactive IVR Quit Line which will offer smoking cessation resources and help connect the patient to those resources. The enhanced usual care group will receive a letter that provides information about how to contact the IVR Quit Line. The IVR system will track referrals to cessation services, and additional information about smoking status and use of cessation resources will be collected from the electronic health record and surveys.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer. He has undergone several treatments, including chemotherapy and hormone therapy, but his cancer has continued to progress. He has a family history of cancer, with his mother and sister both having had breast cancer. He is interested in learning more about genetic testing and is willing to participate in this clinical trial. He understands that the study will involve providing basic demographic information, family cancer history, and treatment history, completing patient-reported outcomes questionnaires, and providing a saliva sample. He is willing to undergo genetic testing and is open to receiving phone-based genetic counseling. He hopes that the study will provide him with more information about his cancer and help guide his treatment options.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who sustained a burn injury in a house fire. He was brought to the emergency department with a 30% Total Body Surface Area (TBSA) burn on his face, chest, back, both arms, and both legs. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. He smokes a pack of cigarettes a day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He was intubated due to inhalation injury and started on mechanical ventilation. He was admitted to the burn unit and underwent escharotomy and wound debridement. His burn injury was classified as a second-degree burn with some areas of deep partial-thickness burns. He was started on fluid resuscitation with lactated ringers solution and received a total of 5 liters in the first 24 hours. His urine output was 50 cc/hour, and he required vasopressors to maintain his mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg. The physician decided to use albumin on the second day of admission due to persistent hypotension despite adequate fluid resuscitation. The patient received one dose of 25 grams of albumin. His urine output improved, and vasopressors were tapered off. He was extubated on day 4 and started on oral nutrition. His wound care was managed with topical agents and dressings. He was discharged home on day 14 with close follow-up in the burn clinic.

A 25-year-old healthy male who is living in a non-endemic area for dengue and hepatitis A virus. He has no known allergies to any of the vaccine components or excipients. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive therapy, steroids or immunoglobulins, and he has not received any blood products or immunostimul

Pt is a 60yo male with a history of non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnosed 2 years ago. He received standard-of-care platinum-based chemotherapy and an immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) for his metastatic disease, which showed initial response but then progressed. Archival tumor sample showed carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule (CEACAM) 5 expression of ≥2+ in at least 50% of the tumor cell population. The patient is currently experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. CT scan shows progression of his disease in the lung and liver. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has a measurable lesion as determined by RECIST v1.1. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has agreed to use highly effective contraceptive methods during and for at least 6 months after the last dose of study intervention. The patient has no history of untreated brain metastases, significant concomitant illnesses, or invasive malignancy within the last 3 years. The patient's bone marrow, liver, and kidney functions are good, and he has no known hypersensitivity or allergies to any of the study interventions or components thereof.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who weighs 70 kilograms and has a body mass index within the range of 19-30 kg/meter (m)^2. She has no significant medical condition and has not had any regular alcohol consumption or tobacco use within the past 2 months. She has not participated in any clinical trial or taken any prescription medication within the last 30 days. She is not pregnant, lactating or of reproductive potential. She is able to communicate in German or the native language of the site. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of GSK1795091 in healthy subjects.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury due to a motorcycle accident two years ago. He is classified as ASIA A and has no voluntary movement or sensation below the level of his injury, which is at the eighth thoracic vertebrae. He has intact reflexes below his level of injury. He has no history of psychiatric problems, joint contractures, or spasticity medication use. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He is willing to use acceptable contraception methods if necessary. He has a BMI of 24.5 and weighs 75kg. He has no coagulopathy or significant cardiac or medical risk factors for surgery. He has no history of frequent hypotension, hypertension, or autonomic dysreflexia. He has no implanted medical devices which are not MRI-compatible. He has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cardiac failure, or heart arrhythmia.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has a history of gestational diabetes that was managed with diet and exercise. She has no history of chronic medical conditions and has not had any complications during her pregnancy. She plans to have a vaginal delivery and is interested in receiving epidural analgesia for pain management during labor. She is currently in her 36th week of pregnancy and has no contraindications for labor epidural analgesia. She is able to understand and communicate with the study team and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of heart disease. The patient has been implanted with a Medtronic Model 4195 LV lead for at least 181 days and is now indicated for left ventricular lead removal as per physician discretion. The patient has provided consent to participate in the Attain StarFix® 4195 Lead Extraction Study and is willing to comply with the protocol. The patient is 18 years of age or older and has no other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who presents to the emergency department with a complaint of abdominal pain and fever. He reports that the pain started about 2 days ago and has been persistent since then. The pain is localized to the right lower quadrant and is associated with nausea and vomiting. He also reports having a fever for the past 24 hours. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. On physical examination, the patient appears uncomfortable and his vital signs are as follows: blood pressure – 126/82 mmHg, heart rate – 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate – 18 breaths per minute, and temperature – 38.5°C as measured by an ear thermometer. The patient's abdomen is tender to palpation in the right lower quadrant, and there is no rebound tenderness or guarding. The patient is enrolled in the study and both ear and rectal temperature measurements are taken at the same time by the research team.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of carpal tunnel syndrome. He has no significant past medical history, and he does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his lab studies are within normal limits. His BMI is 24. He is scheduled for an elective surgery on his hand, and he has been informed about the option of receiving ultrasound-guided axillary plexus anesthesia with a reduced dose of local anesthetic prilocaine. He has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with fibrovascular proliferation and vitreo-retinal adhesions in 3 or more sites but not extending beyond equator in more than one quadrant. The patient underwent pars plana vitrectomy for diabetic fibrovascular proliferation between June 2008 and December 2008. Complete removal of the visible posterior preretinal membrane was done during surgery, and the patient has attached retina postoperatively. She has not had rhegmatogenous detachment, silicone oil infusion, or post-operative moderate to dense cataract. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to follow-up regularly. Data on her age, gender, systemic diseases, study eye, types and duration of diabetes mellitus, intraoperative diagnosis, and additional surgical procedures such as cryotherapy, scleral buckling, or internal gas are recorded. The patient will undergo postoperative standard 6 mm 6-line OCT study centered on the macula and fundus photography between 7 months to 15 months after surgery. The patient's morphological macular changes detected by OCT will be categorized, and correlations with postoperative visual outcome will be conducted. The patient is aware that levels of statistical significance are set at P<0.05.

A 30-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with schizophrenia presents with frequent auditory hallucinations, occurring more than 5 times per day. He has been on antipsychotic medication for the past 6 weeks, which includes an atypical antipsychotic medication. The medication has been stable for 4 weeks prior to the commencement of the study. The patient is competent to give informed consent. He has no history of seizure disorder or recent head injury. He denies any acute suicidality or alcohol/substance abuse. The patient does not have any implanted pacemakers or metal in the head or neck. The patient is not pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in reducing auditory hallucinations related to his schizophrenia.

65 yo F with newly diagnosed breast cancer detected on routine mammogram. Biopsy confirmed ER+ HER2 negative breast cancer. Patient reports menopause at the age of 52 and denies previous use of hormonal replacement therapy. The histologic grade of the cancer is intermediate. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, with no significant comorbidities. Baseline laboratory values, including hematological, renal and hepatic function, are within normal limits. The patient is able to take oral medication and has adequate tissue for diagnosis, biomarkers and Ki67 assays. The patient has not received any previous treatment for this cancer and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that may help in determining the response to estrogen therapy prior to surgery. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was hospitalized due to COVID-19 infection. He tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 PCR and has evidence of pulmonary involvement on CT scan. He experienced shortness of breath within the previous 5 days and has a fever. He has a history of arterial hypertension and is obese with a BMI of 31 kg/m2. He does not have a history of cardiovascular disease, chronic pulmonary disease, or chronic renal disease. His C-reactive protein level is 40mg/L and oxygen saturation at rest in ambient air is 92%. He has no contraindications to the class of drugs under study (C1 esterase inhibitor). He has not received tocilizumab or another Il-6R or Il-6 inhibitor before enrollment and has no history or suspicion of allergy to rabbits. He is not currently admitted to an ICU or receiving invasive or non-invasive ventilation. He is able to provide informed consent. He has no concurrent illness that would put him at greater risk or limit compliance with the study requirements. He is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 55 year old Hispanic male who is uninsured and has been receiving healthcare at the John Peter Smith (JPS) Health System for the past year. He works as a construction worker and has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. He has never undergone colorectal cancer screening and has not experienced any symptoms related to colorectal cancer. He lives alone in a small apartment and does not have any family members nearby. He speaks English fluently and has basic knowledge of Spanish. He has a phone number and address on file at JPS. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive screening for colorectal cancer and is willing to follow the instructions provided in the mailed invitation kit.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has recently noticed a hard lump in her right breast. The lump is painful, and she has also experienced nipple inversion and skin thickening. She has a history of using oral contraceptive pills for the past 2 years and has been breastfeeding her 1-year-old child. She is concerned about the possibility of breast cancer and seeks medical attention. A mammogram and ultrasound reveal an irregular hypoechoic finding that connects with a tubular hypoechoic area and parenchymal heterogeneity. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of idiopathic granulomatous mastitis. She is still breastfeeding her child and is hesitant to undergo surgery due to her concern about the impact on her breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options that could avoid the need for surgical intervention.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl diagnosed with neurofibromatosis type 1. She has a history of difficulty in making and maintaining friendships with peers at school. Her parents have reported that she struggles with initiating conversations, joining group activities, and dealing with social anxiety. The patient has shown an interest in improving her social skills and is motivated to participate in the PEERS program delivered via Telehealth. She has reliable internet access and is fluent in English, which is the main language spoken in her home. The patient does not have any cognitive or developmental difficulties that would impact her understanding of treatment material. She has not undergone any major surgery in the past 6 months and does not have any other comorbid medical conditions. She has not participated in any social skills group treatment or the PEERS program in the past 6 months.

A 60-year-old male presents to the emergency department with chest pain radiating to his left arm. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. He is immediately taken to the catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The angiogram reveals a 90% occlusion in his left anterior descending artery, which is successfully treated with stent placement. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is measured at 45% by echocardiogram. He is currently taking aspirin, clopidogrel, and a statin. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the long-term benefits of beta-blocker therapy after his STEMI. He has no contraindications to beta-blocker therapy and does not have an implantable cardioverter defibrillator. He has been informed of the risks and benefits of participation in the study and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

50 yo M diagnosed with prostate cancer through a biopsy. The cancer has not spread beyond the prostate gland (clinical T2 or less in the TNM classification). Patient is a regular at the Methodist Urology clinic in Indianapolis, IN and has been referred to the clinic's LRP registry and database study. Patient has no major abdominal surgery that would preclude a safe laparoscopic approach. Additionally, patient has no bleeding diathesis or anticoagulation, and no medical disease that would preclude general anesthesia/laparoscopy. Patient has not undergone radiation therapy to the pelvis and is not morbidly obese. Patient is able to give informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 10-month-old infant living in South-Benin. The parents brought the child to the clinic due to fever and general malaise that started 6 hours ago. The infant weighs 7 kg and has no known underlying chronic disease. Blood tests reveal that the infant has Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia of 2,500 trophozoïtes/µL. The parents provide informed consent for the infant to participate in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) to two compact artemisinin-based therapies (ACT): artemether-lumefantrine and the amodiaquine-artesunate coformulation. The infant meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is enrolled.

A 37-year-old male diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD) presenting with a history of heavy alcohol consumption for the past 10 years, with frequent binge drinking episodes. He has been recently admitted to a detoxification program at an alcohol inpatient clinic in Germany. The patient has a history of depression and anxiety, which he has been treated for with antidepressant medication for the past 2 years. He is fluent in German and has no sensory or motor deficits that would affect his participation in the study. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is currently enrolled in standard treatment and is expected to complete detoxification within the next two weeks. The patient does not meet the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer that has relapsed after one prior chemotherapy regimen. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing and fatigue. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. He has normal bilirubin levels and his AST/ALT levels are within the normal range. His platelet count is above 100,000/mm³ and his hemoglobin level is above 9 g/dL. He has no known hypersensitivity to bendamustine. He has no other concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or anti-tumor hormonal therapy. He has no cardiac disease but has a history of hypertension. He is not pregnant or nursing, and he will use effective contraception before, during, and for at least 3 months after completing the study therapy.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory problems and difficulty with daily activities such as cooking and managing finances. Her family has noticed a decline in her cognitive abilities over the past year, and they have become increasingly concerned. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, and her medical history is significant only for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She currently lives at home with her husband who is her primary caregiver. Her husband has expressed concerns about the impact of her condition on his daily life and mental health. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given permission for her caregiver to complete the questionnaire regarding caregiver burden.

The patient is a 60-year-old Japanese man who was diagnosed with ischemic heart disease. He is eligible for treatment with XIENCE PRIME SV Everolimus Eluting Stent. He has provided informed consent for registration in the post-marketing surveillance study. He is able to return for the 8-month follow-up visit for angiogram and the 1-year clinical follow-up. He will be treated with XIENCE PRIME SV during the index procedure. He does not have any other planned staged procedures or additional revascularization procedures as a part of adverse event treatment. He has not been treated with other drug eluting stents. He has only one target lesion that will be treated with XIENCE PRIME SV.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who frequently uses grocery coupons to save on her food purchases. She lives with her husband and they both have full-time jobs. She enjoys cooking and often prepares meals at home. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medications. She has a BMI of 27 and is concerned about her weight. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effects of grocery coupons on her diet and weight. She is open to the idea of incentivizing healthy food purchases and is willing to follow the study protocol for a duration of 3 months. She has no dietary restrictions or medical conditions that would affect her food intake or weight.

A 42 year old woman has been experiencing widespread pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances for the past 5 years. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by an expert and has been stable on her current treatment regimen for the past 6 months. She has no other medical conditions and does not have a history of psychotic disorder or drug abuse. She demonstrates an understanding of the study and is willing to participate as evidenced by voluntary written informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma in her colon. She underwent a colonoscopy and biopsy after experiencing persistent abdominal pain and changes in bowel movements. The biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma, and a CT scan revealed that the cancer has spread to her liver. Her medical history includes hypertension and coronary artery disease, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and normal hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has not received any previous treatment for her cancer and is willing to undergo surgery to remove the tumor.

The patient is a 28 year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is currently at 36 weeks gestation and is experiencing regular contractions. She has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications or pre-existing medical conditions. She has had regular prenatal care and all her ultrasounds have been normal. She does not smoke or consume alcohol and has a healthy diet. She is planning for a vaginal delivery and has not had any previous surgeries. She is not taking any medications except for prenatal vitamins. She has no known family history of pregnancy complications.

72 year old man with a recent diagnosis of a disabling stroke resulting in left sided hemiparesis. He is currently medically stable and has completed his acute hospitalization. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. Prior to his stroke he was independent with activities of daily living and lived with his spouse. He is interested in participating in a study that will compare hospital-based rehabilitation care with transitional subacute rehabilitation in order to determine the best option for his recovery and long-term independence.

A 25-year-old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5 kg/m2 presents for participation in a pharmacokinetic study. She is a non-smoker and has not used e-cigarettes or nicotine replacement products in the last 12 months. She has never been pregnant or lactated and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception with her partner throughout the dosing period and for at least 30 days after the last follow-up visit. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 2 years and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She has no history or family history of meningococcal infection, cholecystectomy or gallstones, and has not experienced any clinically significant allergy requiring treatment. Her laboratory, vital sign, and ECG results are all within normal limits. She is willing and able to communicate and participate in the entire study and provides written informed consent.

This is a 56-year-old female with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer. She was first diagnosed with breast cancer 5 years ago and underwent a lumpectomy, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Despite initial treatment, she was recently found to have metastatic disease to the liver and bones. She was started on a regimen of palbociclib in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as per the national basket of health services in Israel. She has been on this treatment for 8 months and has been experiencing stable disease. She has been continuously enrolled in the Maccabi Healthcare Services plan for the past 10 years and has no history of prior HER2 inhibitor treatment.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman with a Port wine stain birthmark on her left cheek. The birthmark has been present since birth and has caused her significant emotional distress due to its prominence on her face. She has tried various treatments in the past, including pulsed dye laser, but has not seen significant improvement. She is interested in participating in this pilot study to see if the Matrix Radiofrequency device can provide better results. She is in good overall health and has no other medical conditions.

A 60-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Room complaining of chest pain, shortness of breath, and sweating. He had a history of hypertension, diabetes, and high cholesterol levels. His electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. He was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and immediately taken to the catheterization lab for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). He is not allergic to any medication, has not had major surgery in the last 6 weeks, and is not currently taking any antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications. He has a platelet count of 170x10^9/l and hemoglobin level of 12 g/dl. He has given informed written consent to participate in the RAPID study.

45 year old female scheduled for spinal fusion surgery due to severe low back pain and radiating leg pain. The patient has tried conservative treatments including physical therapy, medications, and injections without relief. MRI showed significant disc herniations and spinal stenosis at L4-5 and L5-S1 levels. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, no known allergies, and no history of spine infections. The surgeon plans to use closed suction drains post-operatively due to the expected amount of fluid discharge. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been wearing spherical soft contact lenses for distance correction for at least 5 days per week and 8 hours per day for the past 3 months. She has a Best Corrected Visual Acuity of 20/25 or better in each eye. She has not worn the investigational verofilcon A or delefilcon A contact lenses before. She does not wear her contact lenses in an extended wear modality (i.e., she does not sleep in her lenses for at least 1 night per week). She is willing to attend 7 office visits as required by the study protocol.

The patient is a 29-year-old male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection. He has been HBsAg positive for more than six months, with an HBV DNA level of more than 2000 IU/mL. He has not received any antiviral treatment in the past, including interferon-alpha or pegylated interferon-alpha. He is willing to comply with the study drug regimen and all other study requirements. He has no history of decompensated liver cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma. He does not have any laboratory signs of co-infection with HIV or HCV, HDV. He has no hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or to drugs with similar chemical structures or their excipients. He has not used any other investigational drugs within 30 days or 5 half-lives of enrollment. He has no concurrent medical or social condition that is likely to preclude compliance with the schedule of evaluations in the protocol, or likely to confound the efficacy or safety observations of the study. His laboratory values during Screening meet the requirements specified in the exclusion criteria. He is not currently abusing alcohol or illicit drugs. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with congestive heart failure for the past year. He has a history of hypertension, diabetes, and obesity. He takes medications for his conditions, including metformin and lisinopril. He reports experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a diet high in processed foods and sodium. He has a family history of heart disease and has never received any nutritional counseling. He is interested in learning more about the role of nutrition in managing his condition.

A 6-year-old girl has been diagnosed with tyrosinaemia. She lives with her parents and two siblings. The patient is currently prescribed nitisinone and follows a strict low protein diet. Her parents have reported difficulty in ensuring that she is receiving adequate protein intake, which has led to concerns about her growth and development. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She enjoys playing with dolls and drawing. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and are willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 32-year-old mother of two from rural South Central Montana is concerned about the safety of her children while travelling in their car seats. She has had difficulty installing the car seats properly and has noticed that the restraints are not always secure. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy of parents installing restraints with guidance from a remotely-located technician using interactive virtual presence. She is able to communicate in English and drives a vehicle with one or more car seats present. She is willing to install a car seat into the vehicle and is excited to participate in the study to improve the safety of her children while driving.

Patient is an 80-year-old man who fell down and got injured his hip. He is currently hospitalized and requires surgery for hip fracture. His past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and arthritis. He is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. His BMI is 25, BP: 140/80, HR: 80/min. Orthopedic POSSUM scoring system reveals that he is in moderate risk status before surgery. He has no known allergies to anesthesia drugs.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with Stage II breast cancer. She is currently undergoing daily radiation therapy for 6 weeks at M. D. Anderson. She is able to read, write, and speak English fluently. She had a lumpectomy followed by axillary lymph node dissection. Pathology revealed that the tumor was ER/PR positive and HER2 negative. She has no history of formal thought disorders, bone metastases, or active/non-canalized deep vein thrombosis. She underwent surgical treatment for her cancer about a month ago and has not practiced yoga or taken any yoga classes in the year prior to her diagnosis. She has not been diagnosed with lymphedema at baseline. She does not have extreme mobility issues and is able to get in and out of a chair unassisted. She is interested in participating in a yoga program as an adjuvant to her radiation therapy to help improve her fatigue and sleep disturbances. She has no contraindications for the study and is willing to attend 3 sessions of yoga or stretching each week for 6 weeks.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who has been diagnosed with moderate-to-severe COPD. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and has a 20 pack-year smoking history. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty breathing for the past 6 months. He has been using a SABA inhaler for relief of symptoms but has noticed that it is not as effective as it used to be. The patient has not used any inhaled or oral steroids for the past 3 months. He is able to use an Accuhaler device and is willing to comply with the study protocol. The patient is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant during the study duration.

50-year-old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of poor glucose control is interested in participating in a study evaluating a new screening test for diabetic neuropathy. The patient reports occasional burning and tingling sensation in both feet and hands, but denies any numbness or pain. He currently takes metformin and a low dose of amlodipine for hypertension, with no known allergies. The patient has not previously been diagnosed with neuropathy, and is not currently being treated for any other health conditions. The patient does not have a history of alcoholism or use of psychoactive substances. He is interested in participating in the study as he hopes to improve his overall management of diabetes and reduce his risk of complications. The patient understands the study's eligibility criteria and is willing to undergo screening to determine if he is eligible to participate.

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of Parkinson's disease presents with functional disorders in the upper extremities and difficulty in performing daily activities. He reports experiencing tremors and stiffness in his arms, which makes it difficult to perform routine tasks like opening jars, buttoning shirts or brushing his teeth. His symptoms have been progressing over the past year despite medication. The patient has no significant medical history apart from hypertension, which is well managed with medication. He is independent in activities of daily living, but requires occasional assistance with housekeeping and cooking. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his upper extremity function and quality of life.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago. She had a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been doing well with no recurrence until recently when she noticed a small lump on her right side under the armpit. Biopsy confirmed metastatic breast cancer with no evidence of spread to other organs. CT scan and PET scan showed that there are three small metastases (two in the lungs and one in the liver) and one metastasis in the right axilla. The patient is a candidate for a pilot study of stereotactic ablative body radiosurgery (SABR) treatment (20Gy/1#) and a PD-1 antibody, MK-3475. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial, is 18 years of age, and has a performance status of 0-2 on the ECOG Performance Scale. She has demonstrated adequate organ function and has a life expectancy of more than 12 months. She is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including treatment, attending assessments, and follow-up. She has had no prior high dose radiotherapy, no evidence of visceral metastases in liver or brain, and has not received any chemotherapy agent within +/- 3 weeks of SABR. She does not have evidence of spinal cord compression, spinal instability neoplastic score greater than or equal to 7, or lytic metastases in a long bone that which erodes the cortex. She has not participated in any study of an investigational agent or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of treatment. She does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. She has not had a prior monoclonal antibody within 4 weeks prior to study Day 1 or who has not recovered from adverse events due to agents administered more than 4 weeks earlier. She does not have a known additional malignancy that is progressing or requires active treatment. She has no known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis. She does not have an active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within the past 3 months or a documented history of clinically severe autoimmune disease, or a syndrome that requires systemic steroids or immunosuppressive agents. She does not have evidence of interstitial lung disease or active, non-infectious pneumonitis. She does not have an active infection requiring systemic therapy. She has no history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the trial, interfere with the subject's participation for the full duration of the trial, or is not in the best interest of the subject to participate, in the opinion of the treating investigator. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive or father children within the projected duration of the trial, starting with the pre-screening or screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of trial treatment. She has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, or anti-Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) antibody (including ipilimumab or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint pathways). She does not have a known history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C. A 42-year-old female with a history of major depression for the past 12 years came to the clinic seeking treatment for her persistent symptoms. Despite multiple trials of different antidepressants and combination therapies, she has not experienced significant relief from her symptoms. She has a Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS24) score of 24 and a Global Assessment of Function (GAF) score of 40. She has had at least four episodes of depression and has been chronically depressed for the past 3 years. She has tried electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) in the past, but it did not provide significant relief. She is currently drug-free and has not used any illicit substances in the past 2 years. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo deep brain stimulation (DBS) to improve her symptoms. She is a German speaker and is able to provide written informed consent. She does not have any medical comorbidities or significant abnormalities on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

The patient is a 25-year-old man who identifies as a gay male. He reports engaging in high-risk sexual behaviors with multiple partners and has a history of problematic stimulant use. He has been prescribed PrEP to reduce his risk of contracting HIV. However, he struggles with remembering to take his medication consistently, and this has led to missed doses. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him improve his adherence to PrEP. He is comfortable with using a digital pill to monitor his PrEP use and is willing to attend monthly study visits to assess his adherence and receive substance use disorder counseling. The patient speaks fluent English and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with mild hemophilia A. He has a baseline FVIII level of 20%. He has a history of occasional nosebleeds and bruises that take longer than usual to heal. He has never developed an inhibitor to FVIII. He is currently not on prophylactic treatment and only uses on-demand treatment when he has a bleeding episode. He is in good health and has no other medical conditions. He lives with his parents and two siblings and is a student in the 7th grade. He is an active child who enjoys playing basketball, soccer, and video games. He has a BMI of 24 and is in good physical shape. He has never had a surgery or major injury in the past. He is willing to participate in the Stimate/DDAVP challenge as part of the study. He has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to monoclonal antibody therapies. He is able and willing to comply with the scheduled visits, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. His parents are supportive of his participation in the study and are willing to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy in the upcoming weeks. She is fluent in Spanish and has basic phone skills. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, traumatic brain injury, or previous cancer diagnosis or chemotherapy. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is concerned about the impact of chemotherapy on her cognitive abilities, as she has noticed some difficulties with memory and concentration in the last few months. She is interested in participating in a study that could help prevent chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment and improve her quality of life during treatment. She is open to receiving occupational therapy through videoconferencing and is willing to commit to a 12-week program.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with mycosis fungoides, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, a year ago. She has undergone one line of systemic treatment with PUVA therapy, which was not successful in controlling her disease. She is now experiencing extensive lesions requiring systemic treatment. The patient has a past medical history significant for asthma and is currently on inhaled corticosteroids. She is married and has two children. She is currently employed as a teacher. She reports her symptoms as itching, redness, and skin lesions covering more than 50% of her body. Her physical examination shows erythematous plaques with scale, and scattered papules on her trunk, arms, and legs. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her laboratory results show normal platelet count, normal liver and kidney functions. She has negative pregnancy tests and is willing to comply with study requirements. She has not had neuropathy of grade 2 or higher. She has not received HDAC inhibitors or brentuximab vedotin for more than 8 weeks, and was not progressed while on treatment. She has not had any allergic reactions to monoclonal antibodies.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 6 months. She presents with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. The patient currently takes lisinopril, simvastatin, and metformin. Her most recent laboratory values show a hemoglobin A1c of 7.9%, serum creatinine of 7.8 mg/dL, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 6 mL/min/1.73m2. She has no history of psychiatric illness or suicidal ideation. The patient has no significant medical history other than ESRD and her current medications. She has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 3 months and has not been exposed to more than four new chemical entities within the past 12 months. She has no known allergies to any of the study medications or components thereof. The patient has given written informed consent and is willing and able to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of knee osteoarthritis. He works as a construction worker and spends most of his day on his feet, lifting heavy objects and performing physical labor. He complains of pain in his knee which worsens during the day and affects his ability to work efficiently. He has tried various pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. He is interested in participating in a study that will explore the use of wearable technology to monitor his physical activity level and provide feedback to optimize his physical activity at work. He is able to do physical activity and is proficient in Swedish language.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with essential hypertension 2 years ago. She has been taking candesartan 16 mg daily for the past year, but recently her blood pressure has been fluctuating and she has been experiencing occasional headaches. She has no other significant medical history, but she does smoke 10 cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol on weekends. Her blood pressure readings have been consistently above 140/90 mmHg despite her medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to monitor her compliance with candesartan treatment and to potentially receive a combination therapy with hydrochlorothiazide.

A 45-year-old woman presented at the clinic with a history of chronic neuropathic pain for the past 2 years. She was diagnosed with fibromyalgia and has been taking high-dose opioid therapy (120 mg/day MED) for the past 6 months, along with other non-opioid pain management treatments. She reported difficulty in carrying out her daily activities due to the persistent pain, which was localized mainly in her lower back and legs. She was willing to undergo an opioid taper and was in good physical and mental health, as confirmed by her physician. The patient was able to understand the purpose and instructions of the study and provided informed consent, as approved by the University of Pennsylvania IRB. She did not have a history of substance use disorder, neurological or psychiatric illness, heart disease, stroke, or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer that has metastasized to his liver and bones. He has already undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his cancer has continued to progress. He is experiencing significant pain and fatigue, and his quality of life has deteriorated. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than those prescribed for his cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial using white blood cells from healthy donors to treat solid cancers. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment and has signed the informed consent form. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including having a life expectancy of at least 4 months, measurable disease, and adequate organ function. He has no history of stem cell transplantation or fludarabine therapy. The patient will receive granulocytes from approximately 4 to 6 donors, and each donor will be HLA-mismatched to avoid engraftment of the granulocytes and any transfusion-related GVHD. The infusions will take place over a 1 to 2 week period, and the timing of which will be dependent on both the patient's tolerance and the availability of the donors. The patient will be monitored carefully for possible adverse events, and response status will be evaluated between Days +90 to +100 after the last infusion. The patient is hopeful that this treatment will improve his quality of life and possibly even extend his life.

32 year-old woman who has been referred for colposcopic directed biopsy (CDB) after an abnormal pap smear result. She reports experiencing significant pain and discomfort during previous colposcopic examinations and is anxious about the upcoming CDB. She has no known allergies to medications and has no history of peptic ulcer disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or bleeding disorders. She does not have any known cardiovascular, hepatic or renal impairment, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of drug abuse or cervical/vaginal infection. She is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effect of Celecoxib in reducing pain associated with CDB.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male patient is scheduled to undergo the FAST dental implant surgery procedure for both maxillary and mandibular repair with at least 4 upper and 4 lower teeth to be extracted. He has a history of tooth decay and gum disease, and his dentist has recommended the dental implant procedure to replace the missing teeth. He reports experiencing moderate to severe pain after dental procedures in the past, and he is concerned about the use of opioids for pain management. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and he is currently not taking any medications. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or opioids. He is married and works as a software engineer. He has a good understanding of the English language and can communicate via telephone. He is willing to provide informed consent, participate in the study, and comply with the study protocol.

A 58-year-old man had a stroke 2 months ago, resulting in cognitive impairment. He was diagnosed with cerebral infarction by CT examination. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are currently well-controlled with medication. He has no history of allergies to any medication or food. He is married and lives with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He has no history of smoking or drinking alcohol. He is able to take care of his daily needs but needs help with complex tasks. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has no other serious complications that could affect the treatment. He is able to comply with the treatment and follow-up visits. He has signed informed consent for the trial.
