A 60-year-old male with a history of smoking for 40 years was recently diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. He has not yet received any systemic treatment for his cancer. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and able to swallow pills. He has measurable disease as defined by RECIST v1.1. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has not had any major surgical procedures within 28 days prior to enrollment and does not anticipate needing any during the course of the study. He has not received any investigational therapy with therapeutic intent within 28 days prior to enrollment. He has not received any live attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks before enrollment or doesn't anticipate needing one during the study. He has not received prior treatment with CD137 agonists or immune checkpoint blockade therapies, anti-PD-1, and anti-PD-L1 therapeutic antibodies. He has not received systemic immunosuppressive medications within 1 week prior to enrollment. He has no history of severe allergic, anaphylactic, or other hypersensitivity reactions to chimeric or humanized antibodies or fusion proteins. He has no known hypersensitivity to biopharmaceuticals produced in Chinese hamster ovary cells or any component of the atezolizumab formulation. He has no history of allergic reactions to carboplatin or etoposide or to any of its excipients (etoposide). He has no known hypersensitivity to venetoclax or to any of its excipients.

The patient is a 45-year-old male Gulf War veteran who has been experiencing unexplained chronic fatigue and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) for the past 10 years. He has no significant medical history other than his military service during the Gulf War campaign. He has been on medication for PTSD for the past 5 years, including benzodiazepines and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). His physical examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no abnormalities noted on cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, or neurological examination. His laboratory tests are within normal limits, including complete blood count, metabolic panel, thyroid function tests, and lipid profile. He has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions that could explain his symptoms. The patient has no contraindication for the study, and he has agreed to withdraw from his medications before participating in the study.

27-year-old female asylum seeker from Syria who has been living in the UK for the past 2 years. She has a diagnosis of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) and is on the waitlist for trauma-focused therapy at Woodfield Trauma Service. She has been experiencing intrusive memories of traumatic events in the past two weeks, as assessed by scoring 1 or above on question 1 of the PCL-5. She is able to communicate with the researcher, with or without an interpreter, and has a fixed abode. She is committed to attending regular appointments and keeping an intrusion diary throughout the duration of the study. She does not have a current diagnosis of schizophrenia or bipolar disorder type 1 and has an IQ above 80. She does not have acute suicide risk or substance dependence and has been able to complete the routine questionnaires given to new patients in the service at assessment.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who works outdoors in construction. He has a history of frequent sun exposure without sunscreen use. He has noticed the appearance of several rough, scaly patches on his face and scalp that sometimes itch and burn. He was diagnosed with actinic keratosis by his dermatologist after a biopsy was performed. He has tried other topical treatments in the past, but they have not been effective in treating his lesions. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find a new treatment option for his condition. He has no other significant medical history and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old man presents with a bulge in his abdomen that is causing discomfort and occasional pain. The patient has been previously diagnosed with an abdominal hernia and is interested in exploring surgical repair options. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient is willing to participate in a long-term registry study to track outcomes following hernia repair with mesh. The patient understands that this study involves the collection of medical data and self-reported outcomes over an extended period of time and agrees to participate.

25-year-old male contact lens wearer with a history of seasonal allergies to grass pollen. No significant past medical history or current medications for allergies or eye disease. The patient experiences symptoms of itchy, red, and watery eyes during the grass pollen season and usually avoids contact lens wear during this time.

The patient is a 32-year-old female experiencing frequent abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel movements for the last 6 months. The symptoms are interfering with her daily activities and causing significant discomfort. She has previously consulted with her primary care physician and undergone a colonoscopy, which were both unremarkable. She has not taken antibiotics, proton-pump inhibitors, H2-antagonists or dietary supplements containing Lactobacillus reuteri within the last 2 weeks. She meets the Rome IV criteria for moderate to severe irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and has a baseline GSRS-IBS score (Spanish/LA version) indicative of moderate to severe IBS. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 27 and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of L. reuteri DSM 17938 and L. reuteri ATCC PTA 6475 as an adjuvant to reduce the severity of symptoms in adults with moderate to severe IBS.

A 32-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of eczema is interested in participating in future dermatology clinical research projects. She has experienced chronic symptoms and has tried various treatments with minimal success. She is currently managing her condition with topical corticosteroids and emollients. She is interested in learning about potential research studies that may offer alternative treatment options for her condition. She is in good health, does not smoke, and has no significant medical history. She is married and has two children, both of whom are healthy. She works full-time as a graphic designer and enjoys hiking and camping with her family on weekends. She is fluent in English and has reliable access to the internet. She is excited to potentially participate in a clinical trial that could offer new solutions for her eczema.

55-year-old male with a history of symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for the past 2 years, despite treatment with anti-arrhythmic medications. The patient was referred for catheter ablation with a plan for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) only. The patient has a history of hypertension, well-controlled with medications, and no other significant medical history. He is currently not on any anti-coagulation therapy. Echocardiogram showed a left atrial diameter of 48 mm and normal left ventricular function with an ejection fraction of 60%. The patient is able and willing to comply with all protocol requirements and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is excluded from the trial if he has any history of prior left-sided catheter or surgical ablation for AF, planned for left atrial ablation beyond PVI, uncontrolled heart failure or NYHA Class III or IV heart failure, left ventricular ejection fraction < 35%, left atrial size > 55 mm diameter, severe pulmonary hypertension, reversible causes of AF, poor candidate for general anesthesia or deep sedation, anticipated survival < 1 year, MI or CABG within 3 months, significant congenital anomaly or medical condition that may affect the integrity of study data, women who are pregnant or breastfeeding, active enrollment in another investigational study involving a drug or device.

This is a 54 year-old male with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. He has been on various anti-hypertensive medications but his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. Despite increasing his medication dosage, he continues to have systolic blood pressure readings above 160 mmHg and diastolic readings above 90 mmHg. He is compliant with his medication regimen, but he has also modified his lifestyle with a low sodium diet and regular exercise. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers a potential alternative to his current treatment plan. He is willing to undergo invasive procedures if necessary, but is seeking a non-surgical alternative.

This clinical trial does not involve recruitment of individual patients, as it is a genetic study of families who have already participated in the Framingham Study. Therefore, there is no specific patient description needed.

Patient B is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent external beam radiotherapy and his PSA levels had been stable until recently. In his last check-up, his PSA level showed a rise of 2.5 ng/mL above the nadir level. He has no history of brachytherapy or hormonal therapy. He has a good performance status and is fit for local anesthesia. He has no contraindications to MRI and has not undergone previous MRI-guided biopsy. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided informed consent. His ECOG performance score is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 10 years.

A 29-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 23.5 presents for screening for a phase I clinical study. He has no history of congenital or chronic diseases within the last three years and no evidence of clinically significant blood, kidney, endocrine, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urinary, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurological or allergic disease. He has never participated in other clinical trials within two months and has not donated blood or undergone apheresis donation within the last two months. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is not taking any medication, prescription or nonprescription, and has not taken any medication of drug-metabolizing enzymes within the last 30 days. He is willing to comply with the lifestyle described in the protocol. He signs the IRB-approved consent form and agrees to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with oral hypoglycemic agents. He was diagnosed with uncomplicated age-related cataract in his right eye and scheduled for phacoemulsification with single-piece hydrophobic acrylic intraocular lens implantation. The patient has no history of glaucoma, high myopia, pseudoexfoliation, traumatic cataract, or subluxated cataract. He has not undergone any ocular surgeries in the past and is not allergic to dilating drops. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is willing to return for postoperative follow-up visits at 1 month, 1 year, and 4 years.

45-year-old male with a history of metabolic syndrome, including large waist circumference (105 cm), hypertension (140/90 mmHg), dyslipidemia with high triglycerides (180 mg/dL), reduced HDL cholesterol (35 mg/dL), and elevated fasting blood sugar (110 mg/dL). He has been taking medication to control these conditions but has noticed that his symptoms have not improved. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of interval hypoxy-hyperoxic training (IHHT) on the arterial stiffness and elasticity of the liver tissue in patients with metabolic syndrome. The patient is able to come to the hospital 5 days per week for 3 weeks and is willing to undergo laboratory and instrumental examinations, including arterial stiffness measurement, measurement of liver tissue elasticity and fibrosis, and laboratory analysis. The patient does not have cirrhosis of the liver, chronic kidney disease, or positive serological reactions to hepatitis B and C, and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 58-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage IV colorectal cancer that cannot be radically resected. She is experiencing cancer-related fatigue (CRF) with symptoms of deficiency of qi and blood. She has not received chemotherapy yet but has been evaluated to tolerate intravenous targeted therapy. Her expected survival period is more than 3 months. Her fatigue score evaluated by visual analogue fatigue scale is 6 and her Karnofsky scale score is 70. She has good compliance and is willing to sign an informed consent before the test. She has not participated in other intervention studies within the last 30 days. She does not have any significant trauma injuries in the past month, severe bleeding or systemic infection diseases that have not been completely controlled. She does not have tangible proofs of marrow or central nervous system metastasis. She has not received erythropoietin or blood transfusion within 1 month before the test. She does not have hypersplenism, hyperthyroidism, desmosis, tuberculosis, and other diseases that have not been completely controlled. She does not have serious diseases such as cardiovascular or cerebrovascular system diseases, active hepatitis, disfunction of liver or kidney. She has not eaten EJiao products in the past 2 weeks and does not have an ileus or severe malabsorption or other diseases that affect gastrointestinal absorption. She is able to understand, read and fill in the self-rating scale due to her level of knowledge or intelligence. She is not pregnant or nursing, or childbearing female that are inadequate contraception. The investigators have determined that she is appropriate to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who recently had a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stenting due to a significant blockage in her coronary artery. She has been prescribed clopidogrel (Plavix) by her cardiologist to prevent blood clots and reduce the risk of future heart attacks. She has been taking clopidogrel for two weeks and has noticed some mild side effects such as stomach upset and occasional headaches. She has no known allergies to aspirin and is not pregnant or nursing. She is interested in learning more about personalized medicine and pharmacogenomics testing to see if it can help optimize her clopidogrel therapy and reduce the side effects she is experiencing. She is able to complete the study materials and is proficient in English.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and has undergone a coronary angiogram which revealed significant stenosis in two of his coronary arteries. The patient has been recommended by his doctors to undergo elective primary coronary bypass surgery. He has no history of renal insufficiency or chronic atrial fibrillation. The patient has provided written informed consent and has legal capacity to participate in the CABY1 clinical trial. He is not participating in any other interventional trial and has no known hypersensitivity to therapeutic apheresis. He will be excluded from the study if he experiences any acute coronary syndrome, or if he shows signs of an acute infectious disease with a body temperature greater than 38.0°C. The patient will undergo standard anesthesia with isoflurane and will be placed on a heart-lung machine with antegrade Bretschneider cardioplegia and mild hypothermia. The patient will be monitored for any changes in ECG during the bypass surgery. The patient will not receive any intraoperative antithrombotic therapy or off-pump surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer stage III a year ago. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and cytoreductive surgery of macroscopic lesions. However, during her follow-up visits, she was diagnosed with peritoneal carcinomatosis. The patient's current symptoms include abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue. She is scheduled to undergo Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (HIPEC) as a part of her multimodal treatment approach. The patient has no significant past medical history and she is not taking any medications. Her family history is negative for any cancer. Her vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with non-infectious intermediate uveitis. She has been experiencing eye pain, redness, and sensitivity to light for the past 2 months. She has been taking oral prednisone 10mg daily to control the inflammation and maintain inactivity of the disease. She has no history of infectious uveitis or any other eye diseases. She has not been exposed to anti-TNF therapy or any biologic therapy that has a potential therapeutic impact on non-infectious uveitis. She is not on any concomitant immunosuppressive therapy except for methotrexate, which she has been taking for the past 6 months. Her best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in both eyes is 20/20, and she has no corneal or lens opacity that precludes visualization of the fundus. She has no history of scleritis or any other disease that precludes her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe headache and vomiting. The initial CT scan reveals a spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) that measures 18cc. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, respectively. He is a smoker, with a 20 pack-year history, and drinks alcohol socially. He is currently unemployed and lives alone. His baseline Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is 11. He is admitted to the Neuro-ICU and requires mechanical ventilation for airway protection. His medical team has discussed the severity of his condition with him and his family, and they have decided to proceed with any necessary interventions to improve his outcome. He has no history of DNR orders or other advance directives.

The patient is a premature neonate with a birth weight of less than 1750 grams. The infant has been diagnosed with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) based on the results of an abdominal x-ray that showed dilated loops, bowel wall edema, and possibly even pneumatosis. The infant's parents have provided consent for participation in the study. The baby does not have any other significant medical conditions or complications. There is no history of abdominal perforation. The infant will be randomly assigned to either the treatment group, which will receive IV pentoxifylline, or the placebo group, which will receive an equal volume of ½ normal saline. The study aims to evaluate the potential therapeutic value of pentoxifylline in the treatment of NEC in premature neonates by improving microcirculation and decreasing TNF alpha levels associated with sepsis.

As this clinical trial is not related to patient medical conditions, there is no need for a patient description. Instead, the eligibility criteria are focused on the group of participants - members of RODA and Association for Patients' Rights, who are women. Male members of these organizations are excluded from the study.

A 60-year-old man with a diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer presents with ongoing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss despite receiving multiple lines of standard therapy including chemotherapy and radiation. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has adequate hepatic, renal, heart, and hematologic functions. He has at least one measurable lesion larger than 10 mm in diameter by spiral CT scan. The patient has no history of VEGFR inhibition and is not currently on any anticoagulant therapy. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He has not participated in any clinical trials within the last 4 weeks and has no evidence of CNS metastasis or uncontrolled intercurrence infection. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and his proteinuria is less than 2+. He has no uncontrolled hemorrhage in the gastrointestinal tract, and he has not experienced any arterial/venous thromboembolic events or acute myocardial infarction within the past 12 months. The patient has no bone fractures or wounds that have not healed and no coagulation dysfunction or hemorrhagic tendency.

This is a 60 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) who has undergone a previous transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) guided prostate biopsy which was negative for prostate cancer. However, he has been experiencing persistent elevated PSA levels and has been recommended for a repeat biopsy. On a recent multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) of the prostate, a discrete lesion was identified with a PI-RADs score of 4. He has an understanding of the English language sufficient to understand the written and verbal information about the trial and has signed informed consent. He has not taken any hormones within the last 6 months and does not have any irreversible coagulopathy predisposing to bleeding. He is able to undergo transrectal ultrasonography and has not had any previous radiation therapy to the pelvis or any other treatments to the prostate except for transurethral resection or vaporization for BPH. There is no evidence of metastatic or nodal disease outside the prostate on bone scan or cross-sectional imaging.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma since childhood. She experiences mild to moderate symptoms of asthma, including shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness, which are usually triggered by exercise, changes in weather, or exposure to irritants such as smoke or dust. She is currently taking a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid and a short-acting beta-agonist as needed. She has not had an asthma exacerbation in the past 4 weeks and has not changed her medication dosage in the past 4 weeks. She is a non-smoker and is not pregnant. She is able to perform normal daily activities without significant limitations due to her asthma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve the delivery of asthma medications and potentially improve her asthma control.

A 68-year-old male presents with pain and limited function in both knees. He reports that the pain started gradually and has been present for several months. The pain is located in the anterior aspect of both knees and is aggravated by prolonged walking, standing, and climbing stairs. He rates the pain as 6/10 on a visual analog scale. He denies any history of trauma or surgery to the knees. On physical examination, there is tenderness over the patella and medial joint line of both knees. There is no effusion or crepitus. The range of motion of both knees is limited, with a flexion of 90 degrees and extension of 10 degrees. The muscle strength of the lower limb is reduced. He is diagnosed with primary knee osteoarthritis and is eligible for a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of a therapeutic exercise program and dry needling in the treatment of knee osteoarthritis in older adults. He is randomized to receive either therapeutic exercise program and dry needling or the same therapeutic exercise program and sham dry needling. He is willing to attend the proposed course of intervention and follow-up schedule.

A 62-year-old man with a history of complete atrioventricular block presents with symptoms of bradycardia. He has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and dizziness. An ECG shows a paced QRS duration of 190 ms. An echocardiogram reveals a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. The patient is being considered for a permanent pacemaker. He has no history of acute coronary syndrome or recent coronary artery bypass surgery. He has not received a heart transplant and is expected to have a life expectancy of more than one year. He meets the eligibility criteria for the Left Ventricular Pacing to Avoid Cardiac Enlargement Study and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old recreational athlete who exercises at least 3 days a week for 30 minutes each time. They have no history of heart or blood pressure abnormalities, and are considered low risk according to ACSM risk stratification guidelines. The patient is interested in participating in a study examining the acute responses in arterial and muscle tissue oxygenation during incremental exercise in normobaric versus hypobaric hypoxia. The patient is not currently taking any prescription drugs, except for female contraceptives, and is between the ages of 19 and 45. They are willing to participate in all three trials (normobaric normoxia, normobaric hypoxia, and hypobaric hypoxia) in a randomized counter-balanced order. The patient understands that the study will involve rating of perceived exertion, heart rate, blood oxygenation, respiration rate, muscle tissue oxygenation, and whole body gases analyses during the trials. They are willing to travel to different locations for the trials and understand that there is no follow-up as a part of this study.

A 6-year-old boy was diagnosed with developmental delay at the age of 2 years. He had difficulties with communication, social interaction, and repetitive behaviors. He was evaluated by a pediatric neurologist and was found to have motor and cognitive delays. He started receiving speech therapy, occupational therapy, and physical therapy at the age of 3 years. Despite frequent therapy sessions, his language and social skills remained limited. He was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) at the age of 4 years. Genetic testing was performed, revealing a CTNNB1 mutation. The boy's parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to help learn more about this rare genetic mutation and its effects on their son's health and wellbeing. They hope that this study will help develop new treatment options for their son and other patients with CTNNB1 mutations.

The patient is a 52 year old male who has recently been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has never received any hypoglycemic agents and his current glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level is 9.5%. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2 and is capable of using wearable devices and mobile apps. He is willing to follow the study protocol and data collection. He has no history of type 1 diabetes or specific types of diabetes. He has no allergic reactions or intolerance to medicine used in the study. He has no acute diabetic complications and no severe diabetic microvascular complications. His glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is above 50 ml/min and his ALT and bilirubin levels are within the normal range. He has no significant macrovascular disease and his blood pressure is well controlled. He has no history of regular blood transfusion, chronic cardiac dysfunction with NYHA grade III or above, or use of medicines that affect blood glucose for a cumulative time of more than 1 week within the prior 12 weeks. He has no serious systemic disease or malignant tumor, chronic diarrhea, or uncontrolled abnormality in endocrine glands. He is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant and is not currently lactating.

The patient is a 28-year-old Black woman who has been diagnosed with HIV. She has experienced physical, sexual, and psychological abuse by a former intimate partner. She owns a smartphone with internet browsing capabilities and is fluent in English. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to develop and pilot test a culturally tailored smartphone app, called LinkPositively, for Black women living with HIV/AIDS who have experienced interpersonal violence. She wants to learn coping skills to overcome barriers and navigate the challenges of living with HIV, and she wants to receive peer support through a social networking platform. She is willing to participate in a randomized control trial to assess the feasibility and acceptability of the intervention and its preliminary effects on HIV care outcomes, such as retention in care, ART adherence, and viral suppression. She hopes to contribute to the advancement of HIV prevention science and improve the lives of Black women living with HIV/AIDS.

A 40-year-old Hispanic/Latino woman presented to the clinic with a history of uncontrolled blood sugar levels for the past year. She reports a family history of type 2 diabetes with both her parents and two siblings also diagnosed. Her BMI is 30, and she does not currently take insulin as treatment for diabetes. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand the impact of behavioral and psychological factors on the risk of progression of T2D and responses to existing and new therapies. She is willing and able to adhere to the protocol and participate in the video-recording part of the study. She has access to a compatible smartphone and is comfortable with using digital health technologies. She does not have any active clinically significant disease or disorder that could interfere with the study. She is not pregnant and does not have a history of substance use disorders, bipolar disorder, schizoaffective disorder, schizophrenia, or antisocial personality disorder.

A 35-year-old male patient visits the Tufts University School of Dental Medicine complaining about gum recession in his upper front teeth. He has been experiencing sensitivity and discomfort while brushing his teeth. The patient has never undergone any periodontal treatment before and maintains good oral hygiene practices. Upon clinical examination, two adjacent teeth were noted to have gingival recession with a height of more than 2mm and less than 4mm. The recession defects were classified as Miller class I or II. The affected teeth are anterior teeth including incisors, canines or premolars, except the mandibular central and lateral incisors. The patient has a full-mouth plaque index of less than 1 and a gingival index of less than 1, indicating good oral hygiene. The patient has no known allergies, has not undergone any gum surgery, and is not currently undergoing immunosuppressive therapy. The patient does not smoke more than five cigarettes per day and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is scheduled to undergo an elective cesarean section due to a breech presentation. She has no known allergies to any of the study drugs and has not undergone previous cesarean sections or elective tubal ligation. She has no contraindications for the use of the study drugs. She has a history of occasional headaches and takes over-the-counter ibuprofen for pain relief. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than prenatal vitamins. She plans to breastfeed her baby after delivery.

55 yo male with complete edentulism of maxillary and mandibular arches, who is considering dental implant treatment. He is generally in good health and has no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and has no known para-functional habits. He has adequate keratinized attached mucosa and interarch space between the maxillary and mandibular ridges. The patient has been informed of the two treatment options: fixed (screw-retained) or removable telescopic retained implant supported prosthesis. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has been randomized to receive either the fixed or removable prosthesis. The patient will be asked to complete the OHIP-14 and a patient satisfaction questionnaire at 2 weeks, 3, 6 and 12 months post-prosthetic insertion. The patient understands the purpose of the study and has given informed consent.

A 9-year-old girl, who is generally healthy but prone to getting colds during the winter months, wants to participate in a clinical trial aimed at preventing viral respiratory tract infections. She has no known allergies or underlying medical conditions, and her parents have given written consent for her participation in the study. The family has access to a computer and is proficient in German language. The girl has not participated in any clinical studies in the past 30 days and is not taking any medications including antimicrobial, antiviral or immunosuppressive agents. She has not had any surgical interventions in the past 3 months or planned interventions during the observation period. She does not have diabetes mellitus, atopy, asthma, cystic fibrosis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, COPD, immunosystem diseases, metabolic or resorption disorders, liver or kidney diseases, or any serious health problems such as neurological problems. She is excited to participate in the study and hopeful that it will help her stay healthy during the upcoming winter season.

A 40-year-old male with a history of hypogonadism, documented by two previous visits with total testosterone levels below 300 ng/dL. He has no known allergies to sesame or testosterone products and is in good general health. He has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and has no history of breast or prostate cancer, abnormal digital rectal examination or elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) for age. He has a stable psychiatric illness and does not have obstructive uropathy of prostatic origin. He has well-controlled diabetes and no history of congestive heart failure. He has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or endovascular procedures, and has not had any surgeries for peripheral vascular disease. He has no history of thromboembolic disease and has not used adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or oral/depot corticosteroids within the last 6 weeks. He has no history of severe, untreated sleep apnea, drug or alcohol abuse, and has no skin conditions in injection sites that could confound injection site assessments. He has not used estrogen, gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), or growth hormone within the last 12 months and has not used other androgens or anabolic steroids. He is not scheduled for any surgical or dental procedures associated with blood loss ≥500 mL during the study and has not donated plasma or blood within the last 56 days.

28 yo female with a history of good oral hygiene and regular dental cleanings. She has no visible caries lesions or periodontal disease. Her recent dental visit indicated moderate to high counts of salivary mutans streptococci (>104 CFU) as estimated with the Dentocult SM chair-side test. The patient reports no history of smoking or taking antibiotics within the last two months. She is currently seeking to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of probiotic lactobacilli on plaque lactic acid production in vitro and in vivo.

A 29-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child is looking for a highly effective contraceptive method. She is interested in intrauterine devices (IUDs) and has discussed this option with her healthcare provider. She is considering either LCS12 or Mirena but is unsure which one to choose. She has no history of pelvic inflammatory disease or ectopic pregnancy, and she has never had an IUD before. She is currently breastfeeding and has not had a menstrual period since giving birth. She is willing to participate in an active surveillance study to help evaluate the safety and efficacy of the IUD she chooses. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study as a woman under the age of 40 who is having a new IUD inserted and is willing to participate in active surveillance. She does not meet the exclusion criteria as she is not currently enrolled in an interventional trial on IUD use.

A 60-year-old female patient with a history of osteoarthritis, diagnosed by a rheumatologist based on clinical examinations and laboratory tests. The patient has been experiencing pain and stiffness in both hips and knees for the past 6 months, which has been limiting her daily activities. The patient has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief, but has not experienced significant improvement. The patient has no other acute or chronic underlying disease and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effect of crucumin on her immune system and osteoarthritis symptoms.

A 36-year-old woman presented with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. She has been smoking for 10 years and is currently smoking a pack of cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit smoking multiple times but has been unsuccessful in her attempts. She is motivated to quit smoking and wants to participate in a clinical trial to help her quit. She reports no history of illicit drug use or psychiatric illness, and is not taking any medications other than an occasional over-the-counter pain reliever. She does not have any significant medical or neurological illness. Her blood pressure is within normal range. She is willing to engage in two practice quit attempts and is willing to forgo other medication-based treatments during the trial.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 29.5 complains of not being able to lose weight despite trying various diets and exercise programs. He is a software engineer who works long hours and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and has one child. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day but is willing to quit if necessary for the study. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He consumes three main meals a day but often snacks on unhealthy foods. He expresses a desire to lose weight and is committed to adhering to the diet recommendations and avoiding the use of other weight loss products during the study period. He understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply.

A 44-year-old female presented with a lump in her right breast. The lump was painless and was noticed by the patient about 2 months prior to presentation. The patient had no family history of breast cancer or any other cancer. She was not on any medication and had no significant past medical history. She was a non-smoker and did not drink alcohol. Physical examination revealed a 3 cm firm, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast. No axillary lymph nodes were palpable. Mammogram and ultrasound confirmed the presence of a 3 cm mass in the right breast. A core biopsy of the mass showed invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR-positive, Her2-negative. CT scan of the chest, abdomen and pelvis showed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient was diagnosed with stage IIB breast cancer and was referred for neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The patient meets the inclusion criteria, has not received prior chemotherapy or more than 3 months of neoadjuvant hormone therapy, is Her2-negative and has a performance status of 1 by the ECOG scale. She is willing to use adequate methods of birth control during the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old Taiwanese woman who has a family history of high cholesterol levels and premature coronary artery disease. She was recently diagnosed with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) based on the revised Taiwan FH diagnostic criteria. Her total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels are significantly elevated, and she has tendon xanthomas. She has not been previously treated for FH. She has no secondary causes of hyperlipidemia, no significant valvular or congenital heart disease, and no history of any life-threatening malignancy. She is not taking any immunosuppressive agents. She is willing to participate in a national FH registry to improve the diagnosis, management, and reduction of unnecessary cardiovascular events in the FH population in Taiwan.

30-year-old female, with a history of previous pregnancy loss, presents to the prenatal diagnostic clinic at Ysan Yuk Hospital for routine scan at 12 weeks' gestation. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The ultrasound shows a possible fetal anomaly and she is referred to the study for further evaluation with 3D/4D ultrasound using the XI VOCALTM technique for volumetry measurement. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is informed of the potential benefits of the new modality in prenatal diagnosis and screening. She is also informed of the risks and possible complications associated with invasive procedures and the potential of reducing these risks with non-invasive volumetry measurements. She meets the inclusion criteria for objective 1 and 2 of the study and is enrolled in the study. She provides written consent for her data to be used for the study and agrees to follow-up visits as required.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who is the primary caregiver for her 68 year old husband who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. Her husband has been living with her at home for the past year and she has been struggling to balance her caregiving responsibilities with her job as a part-time teacher. She has been feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the demands of caregiving and has been experiencing sleep disturbances and fatigue. She has been receiving some support from her adult daughter who lives nearby, but she feels that she needs more help. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the computer-assisted care management system can help her identify and address her unmet needs as a caregiver. She is able to provide written consent and is comfortable using a tablet PC to complete the self-administered questionnaire. Her husband is able to participate in the study as well and is willing to have a care manager visit their home to provide support. They live in the study region and are available for follow-up assessments after 6 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes who has been experiencing chronic foot ulcers for the past year. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a former smoker and has quit smoking for the past 2 years. He has undergone multiple revascularization procedures, including angioplasty and bypass surgery, but these have been unsuccessful in improving his foot perfusion. His foot ulcer is classified as grade III and stage C according to the Texas University Classification System. His TcpO2 value is less than 30 mmHg, indicating inadequate perfusion. He is not a candidate for further surgical intervention due to his comorbidities. He has signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and meets all the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 29-year-old man who presented with a two-week history of asymmetrical oligoarthritis. He had a recent history of urethritis and had been treated empirically for chlamydia infection with a single dose of azithromycin. He also reported a sore throat and a history of unprotected sexual contact. On examination, he had tender, warm, and swollen ankles and knees bilaterally, with limited range of motion. There were no signs of conjunctivitis or uveitis, and no skin or mucosal lesions were noted. Laboratory testing showed a normal complete blood count and mildly elevated C-reactive protein levels. Joint fluid analysis was consistent with a non-inflammatory effusion. Radiographs of the affected joints were unremarkable. A diagnosis of reactive arthritis was made, and the patient was started on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

The patient is a 25-year-old non-smoking female who is in good health and has no known medical conditions. She has a history of seasonal allergies and experiences hay fever symptoms during the spring and fall. She does not use any medication to manage her allergies. She is not pregnant and does not use any illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and immunological effects of two subcutaneously administered mistletoe preparations. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled visits.

A 28-year-old man with a history of heart murmur was referred to the echocardiography laboratory for further evaluation. He reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion and palpitations, but denies any chest pain or syncope. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His family history is negative for any cardiovascular disease. Physical examination showed a grade 2/6 systolic murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border. Echocardiography confirmed the presence of a bicuspid aortic valve with no significant stenosis or regurgitation, and normal left ventricular function. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about his condition and potential risks.

A 55 year old male patient with severe mitral valve prolapse without any history of atrial fibrillation and planned for mitral valve repair surgery without the Cox MAZE procedure. The patient has no history of prior cardiac surgery, implanted pacemaker, or use of antiarrhythmic agents. The patient has no active inflammatory or infectious disease, malignancy, autoimmune disease or sensitivity to sorbitol or acidic juices such as orange juice. The patient is a non-smoker with no comorbidities such as congenital or cardiac re-operation. The patient is willing to consume Tart Cherry Concentrate and participate in the study to evaluate its impact on post-operative atrial fibrillation and related outcomes.

Patient is a 14-year-old male who has been diagnosed with major depression for the past 6 months. Despite being on a high dose of an SSRI medication for the past 6 weeks, his symptoms have not improved. His mood is consistently low and he has lost interest in activities that he used to enjoy. He also has trouble sleeping and concentrating in school. His parents have noticed a significant change in his behavior and have reported that he has become increasingly irritable and withdrawn. The patient will undergo physical examination, blood tests, and intelligence and memory evaluations. He will also be asked standardized questions and tasks that involve looking at pictures, remembering things, testing reaction times, and making simple choices. The patient will spend time in a mock MRI scanner to become comfortable with the procedure. The patient and his parents will meet weekly for 2 weeks with a psychologist or psychiatrist for sessions. If the patient remains depressed after these two sessions, he will begin study medication. As he is currently taking an SSRI, he will be randomly assigned to receive either lithium or a placebo (non-active pill) in addition to the SSRI. Treatment will continue for 8 weeks, during which the patient and his parents will meet with the doctor once a week and complete written and oral evaluations. Blood will be drawn before medication begins and at the end of the 8-week treatment. Additional blood tests might be needed later on to ensure that the dose is correct. The patient will continue treatment at NIH until responsibility for his care can be assumed by an outside physician if he improves after 8 weeks. Program staff will help in facilitating referrals to physicians who will monitor the medication after the patient leaves the study.

A 17-year-old male was diagnosed with Ewing's sarcoma after experiencing persistent pain in his right leg for several weeks. He underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy for six months but his cancer has progressed despite treatment. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use recreational drugs. His vital signs are stable and he appears to be in good physical health. His performance status is good and he is able to perform daily activities without assistance. He has measurable disease and is willing to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study. He has obtained prior approval from his insurance company to receive oral temozolomide for the duration of the study. If he meets all eligibility criteria and agrees to participate in this research study, he will undergo some screening tests and procedures to confirm that he is eligible. These tests and procedures may include a medical history, complete physical examination, tumor assessment, EKG, blood tests, and a biopsy to provide tumor tissue for research tests. He will be given the investigational drug olaparib in combination with temozolomide and/or irinotecan for the study duration. He will be monitored closely through regular clinic visits, physical exams, blood tests, EKGs, and CT scans or MRIs to measure his tumor. He will be asked to return study drug bottles and any unused study drug at the end of the study. The investigators will keep track of his medical condition for as long as he allows by either calling him on the telephone or following him at clinic visits every 3 months.

Sarah is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing unusual fatigue and easy bruising for the past few weeks. She visited her physician who performed a complete blood count and found abnormal levels of white blood cells and platelets. A bone marrow biopsy revealed a diagnosis of de novo acute myeloid leukemia. She has no history of any other medical conditions or surgeries. Her family history is negative for any cancer or hematological disorders. She is a non-smoker and drinks occasionally. She is currently not on any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for the study evaluating the role of high dose ara-c plus idarubicin and mitoxantrone consolidation followed by maintenance in the setting of high total cumulative anthracyclines dose(720-660 mg/m2).

A 50 year old man presented to the clinic with a history of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and had undergone balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) treatment. His mean pulmonary artery pressure was 27 mmHg, and cardiac output was 3.2 L/min/m2 at the last angioplasty session. He had completed an incremental cardiopulmonary exercise test and showed exercise-induced dyspnea with a peak oxygen consumption of 15 ml/kg/min. He is affiliated with the French social security system, and he gave his signed informed consent for the study. He is able to perform a 6-minutes walking test, 3-minutes chair raising test, and rehabilitation. He has access to the internet and is capable of connecting for remote monitoring and/or telerehabilitation. He has not participated in a rehabilitation program in the last 6 months, and he has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been using the etonogestrel-releasing implant for the past 3 months. She has a history of prolonged uterine bleeding, with her current bleeding/spotting episode lasting for more than 10 consecutive days. The patient's BMI is 24.5, and she reports no history of chlamydia infection or use of hepatic enzyme-inducing medication. She is not currently pregnant and is willing and able to swallow pills. The patient has no significant medical conditions and is not on any anticoagulant drugs. Her speculum examination reveals no anatomic source of bleeding. She is not in the first 6 months of delivery and is not on any concurrent hormonal contraceptives or DMPA interruption. The patient is literate and has a mobile phone. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to alleviate her prolonged uterine bleeding associated with the etonogestrel implant.

A 57-year-old man was referred to a neurologist for evaluation of muscle weakness, muscle atrophy, and fasciculations in his arms and legs. He reported difficulty with grasping objects, buttoning shirts, and walking. The symptoms started about 9 months ago, and they have been gradually worsening. He also reported mild slurring of his speech and difficulty swallowing. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He doesn't smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He works as a computer programmer. On examination, he has significant muscle wasting of the upper and lower extremities, fasciculations, and spasticity. His muscle strength is 4/5 in the upper and lower extremities. His reflexes are brisk with bilateral ankle clonus. The sensory exam is normal. The neurologist ordered an EMG which showed widespread chronic denervation and reinnervation consistent with ALS. The patient was offered to enroll in the HEALEY ALS Platform Trial, Regimen D Pridopidine.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and is concerned about the impact of her treatment on her future fertility. She is an English speaker and has the ability to consent to participate in the study. She is interested in learning more about fertility preservation options and the potential long-term effects of her cancer treatment on her reproductive health.

A 54-year-old male with a history of smoking and a family history of colorectal cancer came to the clinic for a routine screening for colorectal cancer. He reported occasional constipation and abdominal discomfort but no other gastrointestinal symptoms. He has never had a colonoscopy or any other screening for colorectal cancer. Physical examination was unremarkable. His latest FOBT was negative, but his physician recommended further testing due to his risk factors. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and provide a fecal sample for both FOBT and fecal RNA test.

A 55-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) due to hypertension was started on hemodialysis three months ago. He has been receiving thrice-weekly hemodialysis sessions for a total of 12 hours per week. Despite the dialysis sessions, his blood pressure remains elevated, and he has been prescribed multiple antihypertensive medications. He reports feeling dizzy and lightheaded during hemodialysis sessions, and his nurse has had to intervene a few times due to intra-dialytic hypotension. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if a new biofeedback system, the Hemocontrol system, could improve his dialysis experience and help lower his blood pressure. He is willing to measure his blood pressure at home and sign an informed consent form. He does not anticipate any changes in his renal replacement therapy or transfer to another center during the trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing acute pain in his left knee for the past 10 days. He reports that the pain is worse during daily activities and rates his average pain intensity as 7 on an 11-point scale. He has not taken any analgesic medications for the past 12 hours. The patient has no history of systemic inflammatory disease, surgery, or other conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is not currently taking any medications contraindicated for this study and has not participated in any investigational drug studies in the past 30 days. The patient has been informed about the nature of the study and has provided written informed consent.

Pt is a 35yo F who has undergone significant weight loss through diet and exercise. Despite her success, she still has excess skin around her abdomen and is seeking an abdominoplasty with umbilical reconstruction. She has no prior history of umbilicoplasty or keloid formation. She is a non-smoker and her BMI is 27. She has provided a signed informed consent form and is interested in participating in the trial to help determine which of the five conventionally used umbilical reconstructive techniques will offer superior aesthetic results.

54 yo F with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with measurable disease. Patient has a known BRCA-associate genetic mutation and a personal history of breast cancer diagnosed at age 42. The patient underwent modified FOLFOX-6 treatment with partial response but developed progressive disease after 3 months. The patient is currently considering the ABT-888 with modified FOLFOX-6 trial as a potential treatment option. Past Medical History: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, BRCA-associate genetic mutation, breast cancer diagnosed at age 42.

50-year-old man with a history of chronic low back pain and recent onset of right leg pain, which has been progressively worsening over the past 2 weeks. MRI shows a herniated disc at L5-S1. The patient has tried physical therapy, stretching, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with minimal relief of his symptoms. He is scheduled for a transforaminal epidural injection to help manage his pain. The patient is computer-literate and has access to email.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The patient was diagnosed with AML two years ago and has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with no success. The patient has relapsed after achieving complete remission once. The patient is experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and bone pain. The patient has undergone leukapheresis and is medically able to tolerate the process for harvesting natural killer cells. The patient has a related donor who is HLA-haploidentical with the patient and meets the criteria for donor viral screen. The patient is in good health and meets the eligibility requirements for the clinical trial. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to sign an informed consent document. The patient does not have any uncontrolled bacterial or viral infections, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of ≥50%. The patient meets the criteria for the phase I portion of the study.

This is a 70-year-old woman who lives alone and receives in-home services from a home care agency. She has been struggling with maintaining her physical activity due to limited mobility and fear of falling. She is able to sit independently for at least 15 minutes but requires assistance with transferring to a chair. She is fluent in English and has adequate cognitive function to follow directions and respond to survey questions. Her primary care physician has been informed of her participation in the study and is supportive of her engagement in a physical activity program. She is excited about the opportunity to improve her physical function and well-being through this safe physical activity program, led by her home care aide, who she trusts and has a good rapport with.

John is a 35 year old male who has been diagnosed with chronic plaque psoriasis. He has had this condition for over 10 years and has tried several topical treatments without much success. His Psoriasis Activity and Severity Index (PASI) score is 20 and at least 30% of his plaques are considered severe. He has a body surface area (BSA) involvement of 10%. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the combination therapy with etanercept and narrow-band (NB) UVB phototherapy can improve his psoriasis symptoms. He is sexually active and agrees to use medically acceptable form of contraception during the study. He has no history of prior phototherapy or treatment with any tumor necrosis factor (TNF) antagonist. He has no other skin conditions that would interfere with the study. He has no active infections or history of immune compromised health. He does not have any contraindications according to the ENBREL(r) Package Insert. He is willing and able to commit to all the assessments required by the protocol.

A 50 year old woman was diagnosed with rectal cancer and underwent an open colorectal resection with diverting loop ileostomy surgical procedure in 2016. She has been experiencing complications related to the defunctioning stoma since then, including frequent blockages, skin irritation and difficulty with stoma care. She has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort, along with frequent visits to the hospital for stoma-related issues. The patient is willing to participate in a retrospective study to evaluate the incidence and type of surgical complications occurring in patients who have a defunctioning stoma after LAR for rectal cancer. She has medical records available for a postoperative visit occurring 12 months after the LAR surgery.

A 26-year-old African American woman, who works as a nurse, is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no family history of diabetes and has not experienced any major health issues in the past. She takes a daily multivitamin and exercises regularly for 45 minutes a day. She has no known allergies to any food or drugs. She is not currently pregnant and has not been pregnant in the past year. She is willing to undergo routine blood tests and physical examination as part of the screening process.

Patient A is a 17-year-old female who has been smoking daily for the past year. She is currently smoking half a pack of cigarettes per day and expresses interest in reducing her smoking. She is otherwise healthy and does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is fluent in English and able to understand study procedures. She is not currently pregnant and does not have any current suicidal ideation. She meets the breath carbon monoxide criterion of 6 ppm or higher for inclusion in the study. She is interested in participating in the study to help her reduce her smoking habit and learn more about the effects of very low nicotine content cigarettes.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with an EGFR activating mutation. She has been taking osimertinib (80 mg daily) for the past 6 months, but has recently experienced progression of her CNS (Central Nervous System) disease. She is currently experiencing headaches, confusion, and difficulty with balance. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is currently taking a low dose of prednisone to manage her symptoms. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She underwent radiation therapy to her brain 2 months ago and had a good response, but has since developed new lesions. Her lab results are within normal limits, and her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 65 mL/min as determined using the Cockcroft-Gault formula. Brain MRI with contrast shows progressive CNS disease. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and will be available for the duration of the study. She has not previously received temozolomide or any other investigational drug or chemotherapy within the past 3 weeks or ≤ 5 half-lives of first dose of study treatment. She is not taking any prohibited medications listed in section 6.4.

A 25-year-old female university student who enjoys experimenting with different flavors and is interested in the impact of taste on the body. She has no known issues with salivation, taste, or smell and is not taking any medications other than birth control. She is a non-smoker and has not used any tobacco products or electronic cigarettes in the last 30 days. She agrees to maintain her current diet throughout the intervention and to inform the researchers if there are any changes in her medication use during the study. She is willing and able to taste and consume samples and take pictures to document the use of the flavor during the intervention. She is excited to participate in the study and contribute to the research on the relationship between salivary proteins and flavor sensation.

The patient is a 55-year-old obese female with a body mass index of 35 kg/m2, diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. She has undergone a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy for breast cancer treatment in the past. The patient had been taking hormonal therapy for the past 6 months, which was discontinued due to the progression of the disease. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1. She has no liver metastases and her serum bilirubin level is within normal limits. Her creatinine clearance is estimated to be 70 mL/min/1.73 m2. She has no history of brain metastases and is not on any medications for it. The patient is not pregnant, and her last menstrual period was two years ago. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient has not received any systemic chemotherapies or targeted therapies for the past three weeks or radiotherapy for the past two weeks. She has no significant gastrointestinal tract conditions that would affect oral medication absorption. The patient is willing to sign a written informed consent document and participate in the study.

A 56 year old male with a history of follicular lymphoma who has been treated with rituximab on ECOG-E4402. The patient's PBMCs and FFPE tumor samples have been banked and are available for analysis. The patient has not received any other concurrent therapy and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently asymptomatic with a Karnofsky Performance Status of 90.

A 50-year-old Caucasian man with end-stage renal disease due to hypertension is on hemodialysis thrice weekly for the past 6 months. He is on the waitlist for a cadaveric renal transplant for the past 2 months. He has no history of previous renal transplant. His comorbidities include type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. He is compliant with his medications, including metformin, insulin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and amlodipine. He has no history of malignancy or any infections in the past 6 months. His vital signs are stable. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild peripheral edema. His lab reports show HbA1c of 6.8%, LDL-C of 70 mg/dL, and serum creatinine of 9.8 mg/dL. His viral serology for HIV, HCV, and HBV is negative. He is willing to use effective contraception during the trial period.

A 62-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with heart failure a year ago. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. She has been taking medications for her heart failure and her blood sugar. She is married and has two children. She used to be active with walking, gardening, and volunteering in her community. But she has been limited in her activities because of her heart failure symptoms. She is currently at NYHA Class III. She has never had an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) or a cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) system. She is able to walk for 300 meters in the 6-minute hall walk test. She is willing to undergo echocardiogram, exercise stress testing, and complete a quality of life questionnaire. She has not participated in any clinical investigation in the last 30 days.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer. He has been experiencing severe pain in his chest and back, which is making it difficult for him to sleep and carry out daily activities. He has never taken any strong opioids before and is currently not on any pain medication. He has a life expectancy of at least one month and is willing to participate in the study. He has no history of psychiatric or mental illness, dementia, or chronic renal failure. He is not currently undergoing antalgic radiotherapy or radio-metabolic therapy and is not starting a first-line chemotherapy during the study. He is willing and able to attend regular follow-up visits at the clinic.

A 42-year-old female with a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 2 years, with moderate to high disease activity, and functional class II as per the American College of Rheumatology classification. She has been on methotrexate for the past 6 months at a dose of 15 mg/week orally, and the dose has been stable for the past 4 weeks. She has not been taking any other basic antirheumatic drugs except methotrexate. The patient has been experiencing pain and swelling in 10 or more joints, including the hands, wrists, and knees, with an ESR of 34 mm/hour and CRP of 9.5 mg/dL. She has not taken any NSAIDs for the past

This is a 56 year-old female with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus who underwent an intra-abdominal surgical intervention for gallbladder stones. She was admitted to the intensive care unit of National Hepatology & Tropical Medicine Research Institute (NHTMRI) for post-operative care. She has a Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score of 4 on admission. The duration of surgery was 2 hours and blood loss during the surgery was approximately 500 ml. She did not require any blood transfusion intra-operatively. Upon admission to the ICU, a baseline lactate level and ScVO2 were obtained. The patient will be randomly assigned to either group A (ScVO2) or group B (lactate clearance) for fluid management. The patient will receive maintenance fluid in the form of crystalloid e.g. Ringer or Ringer acetate (in a dose of 30-35 ml/Kg/day) plus replacement with crystalloid e.g. Ringer, Ringer acetate or saline 0.9%, 500 ml over 10-30 min. that will be administered in boluses [7] guided by ScVO2with target value ≥ 70% versus lactate clearance (LCR) with target value ≤ 2mmol/L (or decline ≥ 10%) by the end of the study in group A & group B respectively with close regular clinical monitoring/30min., CVP limits 12-16 cmH2O & mean arterial pressure (MAP) 65-90mmHg. The patient's hemodynamics, fluid balance, blood gases (base excess, PH), hypoxic index (PaO2/FIO2 ratio), and laboratory investigations will be monitored at regular intervals during treatment on 0, 2, 6, 12, 24 & 48hours. Post-operative medical or surgical morbidities will be followed during ICU & hospital stay e.g. weight gain, impairment of hypoxic index (P/F ratio), pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, need for mechanical ventilation, paralytic ileus, renal impairment& intra-abdominal bleeding. The patient will be followed-up for 28 days for mortality.

A 55-year-old male presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain that started 45 minutes ago. He rates the pain as 9/10 in intensity, and it is not relieved by rest or nitroglycerin. He has a history of hypertension, but no prior history of heart disease. He doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. He works as a computer programmer and is married with two children. Upon arrival at the hospital, an ECG shows ST-elevation in the inferior leads, and he is diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction. He is immediately taken to the cath lab for primary PCI. The patient is hemodynamically stable with a blood pressure of 138/86 mmHg and a heart rate of 78 beats per minute. The patient has no contraindications for PCI, and the treating physician determines that he meets the eligibility criteria for the study. The patient signs the informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

32 yo woman with a sedentary lifestyle and a desk job reports a sudden onset of neck pain while working at her computer. She describes the pain as a dull ache in the cervical region, rated as 6 out of 10 on a visual analog scale (VAS). The pain is constant and worsens with movement, especially with prolonged sitting or standing. She denies any radiation of pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness in the upper extremities. There is no history of trauma, fever, or recent upper respiratory tract infections. She has no significant medical history or surgery. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but has not found relief. The patient is referred to an outpatient physical therapy program, and is enrolled in a clinical trial investigating the use of ThermaCare heat wraps and ibuprofen as an adjunct to physical therapy for neck pain.

35-year-old female with a BMI of 24.5 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the accuracy of a new non-contact respiration rate (RR) sensor. She has no history of respiratory or cardiac conditions and is not currently taking any medication. She has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past six months. She is available to attend the testing sessions and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She is interested in contributing to scientific research and hopes that her participation will help improve the accuracy of future medical devices.

John is a 53 year old man who has been diagnosed with multi-vessel coronary artery disease (blockages in more than one vessel bringing blood to the heart). He is being considered for Hybrid Coronary Revascularization [HCR] (combination of surgery and catheter procedures to open up clogged heart arteries) or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention [PCI] (catheter procedures to open up clogged heart arteries). He has given his consent to participate in the Hybrid Revascularization Observational Study, which will collect information about the medical care he receives during his planned procedure(s) and how well he does following the procedure(s). John's clinical characteristics and multi-vessel disease are amenable to both PCI with DES and Hybrid as adjudicated by one interventional cardiologist and one cardiac surgeon. He is able to tolerate and has no plans to interrupt double platelet therapy for ≥ 12 months. He is willing to comply with all protocol required follow-up. John has never had a previous coronary stent within 6 months prior to enrollment for DES. He has no evidence of in-stent restenosis of a DES or BMS. He has never had previous cardiac surgery of any kind, chronic total occlusion (CTO) in LAD or ≥ 2 CTOs in major coronary territories that are considered targets for revascularization, left main disease ≥ 50% stenosis or presence of fresh coronary thrombus. John has no need for concomitant vascular or other cardiac surgery during the index hospitalization (including, but not limited to, valve surgery, aortic resection, left ventricular aneurysm, carotid endarterectomy or stenting, etc). He has never had previous STEMI within 30 days prior to randomization, previous stroke within 6 months prior to randomization, previous thoracic surgery involving the left pleural space, acute decompensated heart failure within 30 days prior to randomization, ejection fraction < 30%, creatinine clearance ≤ 50 ml/min within 24 hours prior to randomization or hemodynamic instability at the time of screening. John's body mass index is within normal range, and he has no extra-cardiac illness that is expected to limit survival to less than 3 years. He has no participation or planned participation in another investigational intervention study within 60 days prior to randomization. He is able to give informed consent and has no potential for noncompliance with the study protocol due to psychiatric illness, organic brain disease, dementia, current alcohol abuse, mental retardation, language barrier, or geographical inaccessibility. John is not pregnant at the time of screening or intention to become pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old male athlete who has been experiencing patellar malalignment for the past year. He has a history of playing basketball and running frequently. The pain is located in the front of his knee and is aggravated by activities that require squatting or bending the knee. He reports no history of knee surgery or fractures, and he is not pregnant. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study. On physical examination, there is tenderness over the medial facet of the patella and crepitus with knee flexion. He has full range of motion and no evidence of instability. He is able to bear weight on the affected extremity during the CT scan.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with a central nervous system tumor. He is scheduled to receive a new therapy including surgery, chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy. He has been experiencing frequent headaches and dizziness for the past few months, which led to the diagnosis. He is currently in good spirits and is looking forward to starting treatment to fight the tumor. He lives at home with his parents and younger sister. He enjoys playing video games and watching movies. He attends school regularly and has many friends. He is a bit nervous about the upcoming treatment but is determined to fight the tumor and get better. His physical exam is unremarkable except for a slight weakness in his left leg.

This is a 55 year-old Hispanic female with a history of type 2 diabetes and obesity. She was diagnosed with Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease during a routine check-up and subsequent liver biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NASH. She experiences mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort but is otherwise asymptomatic. She has been managing her diabetes with diet and exercise but has not seen significant improvement in her liver function tests. She is interested in participating in the UTHSCSA NASH trial to potentially improve her liver health and gain a better understanding of her condition. She does not have any other significant medical history or medication use that would exclude her from participation.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has never experienced any urological problems or lower urinary tract symptoms. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the detectability of the bladder in healthy subjects by ultrasound monitoring with an early prototype of a future bladder sensor. She has no active implants that can be affected by electromagnetic interference, no symptoms of constipation or diarrhea, and no known allergies or intolerances to any of the study product components. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is willing to follow the requirements of the protocol and laboratory safety. She is also willing to conduct a urine pregnancy test and to use a reliable method of contraception with a failure rate of a Pearl-Index less than 1% per year when used consistently and correctly, as required by the study. She understands the subject information and has provided conscious informed consent for study participation and data protection regulations.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who is married with two children. Her husband has recently been diagnosed with acute leukemia and is currently receiving intensive chemotherapy at the Department of Hematology, Rigshospitalet. She is a homemaker and has been taking care of her family for the past 10 years. She is emotionally and physically drained from taking care of her husband and two children, and is struggling to cope with the stress and burden of being a caregiver. She has no prior experience caring for a loved one with cancer and feels overwhelmed by the amount of information and responsibilities that come with it. She is fluent in Danish and can read and write in the language. She has no cognitive or psychiatric disorders, and is generally in good health.
