She is interested in participating in a peer-to-peer support program for caregivers of patients with hematological malignancies, and hopes that this program will help her manage her stress and improve her overall quality of life.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with stage IV breast cancer that has metastasized to the bone and liver. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not seen any significant improvement in her condition. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. Her absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 1,200/mL and platelets are 80,000/mL. Her creatinine clearance is 45 ml/min and total bilirubin is 1.5 X upper limit of normal (ULN). Her fasting lipid profile shows cholesterol at 330 mg/dL and triglycerides at 380 mg/dL. Her corrected calcium is 9.0 mg/dL and phosphorus is 2.7 mg/dL. She has no active infections and is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of hypersensitivity to anakinra, denosumab, or everolimus. She is willing to use adequate contraception throughout the study and is able to understand and sign the informed consent document.

A 27-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy is seeking to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of physical activity during pregnancy on the cognitive function of the newborn. She has a pre-pregnancy BMI of 22, is a first-time mother, and has no known health issues. She has been taking folic acid as recommended by her healthcare provider. She is a non-smoker and does not use alcohol or illegal drugs. She is willing to exercise a minimum of 20 minutes, 3 times per week, at a minimal intensity of 55% of her maximal aerobic capacity. She plans to breastfeed her newborn and is committed to a healthy lifestyle during her pregnancy.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who has been experiencing episodic migraines with aura for the last 5 years. She typically experiences 1-2 migraines per month, each lasting 24-48 hours. During her migraine attacks, she experiences sensitivity to light and sound, nausea, and vomiting. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological diseases and does not have any skin diseases that may cause abnormal skin sensation. The patient has not taken any acute pain medication within the last 12 hours prior to allodynia testing. She is able to read and understand the informed consent form and study procedures.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a history of gallstones. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and nausea for the past year. She has been advised by her physician to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has normal body mass index and no allergies to medications. She has been scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy and has agreed to participate in the study. She has given written informed consent and has been randomized to undergo the operation with either coag or blend modes. Skin biopsies will be performed at three different port sites during the operation to assess for thermal injury at the site of the active electrode and the non-active electrode.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with heart failure 8 months ago and has been hospitalized for heart failure once in the past 6 months. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 35% and he is classified as NYHA class III. He is currently being treated with a diuretic, beta-blocker, and ACE inhibitor. He has an Android smartphone and lives in an area within Verizon cellular coverage. He sleeps in the same bed at least 5 days per week and is willing to complete the required surveys, measurements, and study activities. He has not been diagnosed with any form of cancer, is not undergoing active treatment or on a heart transplant list. He is not on home oxygen or chronic dialysis, and he is not living in a skilled nursing facility or undergoing palliative care. He is not planning on having surgery/procedure or an extended trip away from home in the next 3 months. He is willing to consent and follow the requirements of the study.

52F with a history of dyspepsia and occasional epigastric pain presented to Chulalongkorn Hospital for an esophagogastroscopy. She has been taking omeprazole 20mg daily for the last 3 months to relieve her symptoms. She has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding, gastric surgery, or gastric cancer. She denies any recent use of bismuth or antibiotics. The patient has no coagulopathy, with an INR of 1.1 and a platelet count of 165,000. Upon review of her medication history, the patient has not taken any NSAIDs in the last 4 weeks. She has no history of iron deficiency anemia or any signs of previously bleeding gastric ulcer. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 40-year-old male with a BMI of 45 has been struggling with morbid obesity for several years. He has tried various diets and exercise programs, but none have been successful in helping him achieve sustainable weight loss. He has recently been referred to the Weill-Cornell Weight Loss Surgery program and is considering laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery as a treatment option for his obesity. He has no history of ulcer disease or chronic acid suppression medication use. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol, including taking daily proton pump inhibitors in the early post-operative period if assigned to the treatment group.

14-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's Disease 6 months ago. He has been experiencing mild disease activity, with occasional abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue. He has been adhering to his medication regimen and following a strict diet, but still experiences discomfort and anxiety related to his condition. He speaks English fluently and has normal cognitive development. He is comfortable using a smartphone and has daily access to one. He is interested in trying complementary therapies to improve his quality of life and is willing to participate in the study. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that is estrogen and progesterone receptor positive. She has undergone surgery and radiation therapy but has developed resistance to endocrine therapy. She has not yet received treatment with Palbociclib. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has two children and works as a teacher. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with bilateral open-angle glaucoma, specifically primary glaucoma. She has a history of latanoprost monotherapy for the past 6 months but has not achieved adequate control of her intraocular pressure with a recorded pressure of 25 mm Hg at 8:00 AM. Her visual acuity in both eyes is 20/20. She has no contraindications to the study medications and is not anticipated to have any changes or modifications to her systemic hypertensive therapy during the trial. She has no previous history of failure to respond to topical beta-blockers.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with triple-negative breast cancer six months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and surgery, but the disease has progressed and metastasized to her lungs. She has completed one line of systemic chemotherapy for metastatic disease and is now eligible for this clinical trial. Her ECOG performance status is 0, and she has normal organ and marrow function. She had an echocardiogram within the last month, and her left ventricular ejection fraction is normal. She is willing to undergo tumor biopsies if required for the study. She is able to tolerate oral medications and has agreed to use effective contraceptive methods during the study period. She understands the requirements of the study, has provided written informed consent, and will comply with study restrictions. She has archival tumor tissue available for analysis. She has no active infections or bleeding, uncontrolled hypertension, or history of congestive heart failure, stroke, or myocardial infarction. She does not have any other serious medical or psychiatric illness or require therapeutic doses of any anti-coagulant. She has no CNS metastases, and no medical condition that would impair the administration of oral agents.

A 26-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of urea cycle disorder presents with symptoms including nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She has a history of multiple hospitalizations due to hyperammonemia and has been managed with a low-protein diet and medication. She is currently stable with her current treatment regimen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the effect of KB195 on her nitrogen metabolism. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any antibiotics, probiotics, or prebiotics. She is compliant with her treatment regimen and is able to comply with the study requirements. Her legal guardian has given permission for her to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been suffering from hip osteoarthritis for the past few years. She experiences pain in her left hip that has severely limited her ability to perform daily activities. Her pain is rated as a 7 out of 10 on a visual analog scale. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. She lives with her husband and they have two adult children. She used to enjoy going on walks and gardening before her hip pain became severe. She is seeking treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to manage her postoperative pain after total hip arthroplasty. She has not been taking any opioids for her pain. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with study procedures. She is scheduled for a primary total hip arthroplasty with anterior (Smith-Peterson) approach.

This is a 62 year-old postmenopausal woman with a recent diagnosis of early stage breast cancer. She underwent conservative surgery with clear margins and placement of 6 clips in the surgical bed. Tumor size was 1.5 cm and lymph nodes were negative on sentinel node biopsy. The cancer was ER and PgR positive. She has no history of thoracic radiation therapy or autoimmune disease. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has given written informed consent.

A 57 year old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath and cough. He is admitted to the intensive care unit with a diagnosis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and is placed on mechanical ventilation. Despite receiving sedatives, the patient is experiencing significant sleep disruption, which is causing agitation and anxiety. The patient is eligible to participate in a clinical trial investigating the short-term effects of sedation with sympatholysis on sleep and inflammation in critically ill patients with ALI/ARDS. The patient fulfills the inclusion criteria for the trial, including age range, acute hypoxemia, and ventilatory parameters. The patient has no exclusion criteria, such as acute myocardial infarction, active seizures, or renal failure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided signed and dated informed consent.

The patient is a 58 year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and confusion. Blood cultures grew gram-negative bacteria and he was diagnosed with sepsis. His condition rapidly deteriorated and he developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and acute kidney injury (AKI) within 48 hours of the onset of sepsis. He has no history of hematologic or advanced malignancies, but does have a history of heavy alcohol use and liver disease. He is currently intubated and sedated with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 8 out of 15. There are no therapeutic limitations and he has no contraindications to aPC administration.

A 68-year-old man with a history of non-small cell lung cancer came to the clinic for his routine check-up. He was previously treated with platinum- and docetaxel-based therapy but did not show any significant improvement. He has no other significant medical history and has never smoked. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive EKB-569 as a second-line treatment for his non-small cell lung cancer.

Patient A is a 65-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with a 3-month history of increasing dyspnea on exertion, fatigue, and lower extremity edema. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago. On physical examination, he was found to have bilateral rales, jugular venous distension, and pitting edema up to his mid-thighs. His blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg, heart rate 85 bpm, respiratory rate 20, and O2 saturation 95% on room air. His laboratory results showed creatinine clearance of 50 ml/min, hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL, and serum potassium of 4.5 mEq/L. Echocardiography showed left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 30%. He has not had any episodes of decompensated heart failure in the last 3 months and has been on stable doses of an ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker for the last month. He is not on any nitrates or alpha blockers, and he has not had any episodes of unstable angina or myocardial infarction in the last 3 months. He has no history of intrinsic renal disease, peritoneal or hemodialysis, or renal artery stenosis. He is not on any investigational drugs and has no known allergy to iodine.

43 year old male diagnosed with stage III rectal cancer based on histology. The patient will receive neoadjuvant treatment using Folfox. The patient has a history of hypertension, but otherwise has no other significant medical history. The patient has no known allergies to medications. The patient is able to understand the study protocol and has signed a written informed consent document. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 3 months. The patient has no severe inflammation or coagulation disorders.

The patient is a 28-year-old African American woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She presents with signs of preterm labor including regular contractions and cervical dilation at 32 weeks of gestation. There is no evidence of infection or fetal anomalies. She has a history of hypertension and is being treated with antihypertensive medication. She has no history of preterm delivery or other obstetric complications. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She will be monitored closely for changes in gene expression levels using microarray technology.

Patient A is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing cognitive decline and forgetfulness. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has been struggling to maintain her weight. She has never been diagnosed with diabetes or cardiovascular disease, but she has a family history of both. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs, and she only drinks alcohol occasionally. She takes a multivitamin every day but doesn't take any medication for blood pressure, lipid, or glucose metabolism. She has never had an MRI and is not aware of any medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She is willing to give up being a blood donor for the duration of the study and for 4 weeks after completion. She is right-handed and does not have any difficulty with venipuncture. She is interested in participating in a 36-week study to evaluate the effects of NWT-03 on cognitive performance and brain vascular function.

A 21-year-old man who identifies as gay and lives in Tampa is interested in participating in a clinical trial to support HIV/STI testing and uptake of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among young men who have sex with men (YMSM). He has been sexually active with male partners for the past 2 years and has had multiple partners during that time. He reports inconsistent condom use during anal intercourse and has never been tested for HIV or STIs. He owns an iPhone and is willing to download the LYNX app onto his phone. He is comfortable with using technology and is excited to participate in a study that will help him learn more about his risk for HIV/STIs and how to protect himself. He is in good health and has no medical, psychiatric or social conditions that would make his participation in the study unsafe. He is able to understand, read, and speak English fluently.

A 22-year-old healthy male athlete who engages in regular physical activity and has no known medical conditions presents to participate in a clinical trial evaluating localized muscular endurance. He agrees to participate in the study and signs a statement of informed consent. He reports no recent illnesses or injuries and has not engaged in any intense physical activity in the past 24 hours. He understands the test and is willing to comply with the protocol. He is not taking any medications or supplements that could interfere with the study. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other conditions that would prevent him from engaging in physical activity. The eligibility criteria are met, and he is enrolled in the study.

A 45-year-old male patient came to the clinic with a recent diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The patient underwent surgery for the primary tumor two weeks ago and has now completely recovered from the procedure. His Zubrod performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His peripheral granulocyte count is 2,000 cells/mm3, and his platelet count is 150,000/mm3. His total bilirubin level is 1.5 mg/dl, and his SGOT and SGPT levels are within the normal range. His serum creatinine level is 0.9 x upper limit of normal. He signed an informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial.

Patient is a 30yo non-smoking, non-drinking, non-drug abusing female with no history of systemic conditions or periodontal treatment within the last 12 months. She presents with a probing depth (PD) of ≤ 3mm and bleeding on probing (BOP) of less than 10%. There is no clinical evidence of gingival recession, clinical attachment loss or radiographic evidence of alveolar bone loss. The patient has not had any prior history of contagious disease. She is considered periodontally and systemically healthy and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

This is a 35 year old female who has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for the past 2 weeks. She reports feeling tired and irritable during the day and has noticed a decline in her productivity at work. She has no prior history of sleep disorders and has not received any psychological treatment for insomnia in the past 6 months. She does not work night shifts or have frequent cross-time flights. She is in good health and takes antihypertensive medication for mild hypertension. She owns a smartphone and is willing to comply with the intervention.

4-week-old male infant presented to the pediatric clinic with a 2-week history of projectile vomiting after feeds. The vomiting has become more frequent and forceful in the past few days. He has not had a bowel movement in 24 hours, and his parents report that he appears to be losing weight. He has no history of fever, diarrhea, or blood in his stools. The infant was born at full term via normal vaginal delivery and weighed 3.5 kg at birth. He has been exclusively breastfed and has not had any other medical issues. On physical exam, the infant is alert and active, with a heart rate of 140 beats per minute and a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg. Abdominal examination reveals a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant, and peristaltic waves are visible. A diagnosis of pyloric stenosis is suspected, and an ultrasound confirms the diagnosis. The infant is eligible for the clinical trial comparing open and laparoscopic pyloromyotomy for treatment of pyloric stenosis.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with diabetes 5 years ago and has been taking metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. He has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and weighs 90 kg. He has no history of smoking or use of tobacco or nicotine-containing products. He has no history of pulmonary disease and his pulmonary function tests and ocular examination are normal. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than metformin. He reports occasional seasonal allergies but is currently asymptomatic. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance research in the field of diabetes management.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has not used any contraception methods in the past. The patient has undergone hormonal assessment, which revealed normal levels of thyroid function, prolactin, and androgen. Her partner has also undergone semen analysis, which showed normal results. The patient has undergone hysterosalpingography and transvaginal ultrasound examination, which showed no abnormalities in the uterus or fallopian tubes. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility following standard World Health Organization criteria. The patient has no history of uterine malformations or pathologies and no presence of infections, including hepatitis, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), TORCH, Chlamydia trachomatis, or Mycoplasma. There is no presence of anti-sperm antibodies in her serum. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test for anti-Helicobacter pylori antibodies (IgG) in serum to investigate their possible association with unexplained infertility.

This is a 45 year-old male who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 by Reverse Transcriptase-Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) assay using a respiratory tract sample (nasopharyngeal swab) collected within 48 hours of randomization. The patient is currently hospitalized and presenting with moderate COVID-19 symptoms with a score of 6 on the 10-point ordinal scale of clinical status used by WHO in the SOLIDARITY trial at baseline assessment. The patient has blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) of 93% at rest on room air at sea level and requires supplemental oxygen. The patient is able and willing to provide informed consent and understands the trial requirements and comply with trial medications and assessments in the opinion of the Investigator. The patient has not received any investigational treatment from participation in another clinical trial within 30 days prior to randomization in the current trial and agrees not to participate in other clinical studies during the entire study period. The patient does not have any critically ill condition and has not used interferon beta 1-a (IFN-β-1a) preparations or drugs with reported anti-viral action against SARS-CoV-2 (hydroxychloroquine sulfate, chloroquine phosphate, lopinavir-ritonavir combination drugs, ciclesonide, nafamostat mesylate, camostat mesylate) within 8 days after development of fever (≥37.5°C). The patient's alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels are within normal range.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who works as an office manager and spends most of her day sitting at her desk. She has a history of obesity and has been struggling with her weight for several years. She is interested in participating in the study because she wants to improve her overall health and learn more about the interplay between her gut microbiome and her endocannabinoid system. Her diet consists mostly of processed foods and she rarely exercises due to her busy schedule. She has never been diagnosed with any intestinal pathologies and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not completed any antibiotic treatments or experienced significant weight variations in the past six months. She does not consume alcohol over the recommended limits. She speaks and understands French fluently and has access to a computer and the internet.

72yo male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 30%, presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. He is admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of acute decompensated heart failure and is treated with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers. As part of his discharge plan, he is referred to the Congestive Heart Failure Disease Management Program at Saint Francis Hospital and Medical Center (SFHMC). He is informed about the study and consents to participate. The patient is followed for 90 days post-discharge with clinic visits, homecare agency and visits, and heart failure education class attendance, as well as tracking dates of hospital readmission. The patient is excluded from the study if he is discharged to a skilled nursing facility.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her right hip for the past two years. She has difficulty walking and performing daily activities. She has been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the hip and has been recommended for total hip arthroplasty. She has no history of inflammatory arthritis or any other medical comorbidities. She is an ASA class 2 patient with a BMI of 28. She has no history of previous hip surgery and is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study. She has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and has been randomly assigned to the ERAS protocol group.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian female with no significant medical history. She leads a healthy lifestyle and has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She does not smoke, use recreational drugs, or consume multi-vitamins. She is not pregnant and has not experienced menopause. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to study products or ingredients. She is willing to participate in the study and able to provide written informed consent. She has not donated blood within the past three months and has not participated in any other clinical studies within the past four weeks.

N/A - As this is a study on the effectiveness of a machine learning model in recognizing out-of-hospital cardiac arrest during emergency calls, there is no patient eligibility criteria or patient involvement in the trial.

This is a 45-year-old gentleman who has a previous history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was found unresponsive at home and was brought to the emergency department after receiving CPR from his spouse. He was diagnosed with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and had sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after 25 minutes of CPR. Upon arrival to the ED, his lactate level was found to be 4.2 mmol/L. He meets the eligibility criteria for the Thiamine as a Metabolic Resuscitator After Cardiac Arrest clinical trial and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He will be randomized to receive either intravenous thiamine or placebo and will be monitored for changes in lactate level, cellular and global oxygen consumption, and biomarkers of neurologic injury over the course of the study.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 23, no significant medical history, and not currently taking any hormonal contraceptives. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 1-2 cups of coffee daily. She is willing to abstain from smoking, (methyl)xanthines, and alcohol-containing beverages for the duration of the trial. The patient is not pregnant and is not breastfeeding. She has not participated in an investigational drug trial or donated blood in the past 90 days. The patient has easy venous accessibility and is willing to use non-hormonal contraceptives during the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old non-smoking woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer with an EGFR 19 mutation. She has never received any systemic anticancer therapy before. She has a measurable lesion according to RECIST that has not been previously irradiated. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than three months. She does not have any intrapulmonary metastasis, atelectasis of an entire hemithorax, pleural dissemination, or contralateral hilar lymph node metastasis. She does not have severe heart disease, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, or active infection. She does not have an active concomitant malignancy, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her prognosis.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant female with a singleton gestation of 38 weeks. She has a history of mild asthma and seasonal allergies, but otherwise, her past medical history is non-significant. Her current pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and there are no signs of fetal distress or abnormalities. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. Her height is 165 cm. The patient has elected to have an elective cesarean section under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia. She has no cardiac disease, thrombocytopenia, or coagulation abnormalities. She is not taking any antihypertensive medication during pregnancy. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She speaks fluent English and does not have any communication or language barriers.

A 13-month-old male infant with no significant past medical history presents to the clinic with his mother. The child is up-to-date with all routine vaccinations and has no known allergies. The mother reports that they live in a canine rabies endemic area and are concerned about the risk of rabies exposure. The child is currently not experiencing any symptoms of illness and has not been on any medications recently. The mother reports that the child has not received any previous rabies or Japanese encephalitis vaccinations. The child is alert and responsive with normal vital signs. Physical examination is unremarkable. The mother provides written informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial. The child is eligible for the study and is randomized to receive the Purified Chick Embryo Cell Vaccine (PCECV) in a 3-dose Full-IM (1mL) regimen in combination with two doses of Japanese Encephalitis (JEV). The child will receive a booster dose of PCECV and JEV concomitantly one year after primary vaccination. The child will be monitored for safety after each injection and blood will be drawn at various time points to evaluate rabies and JE virus neutralizing antibodies.

The patient is a 49-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries, including a fractured pelvis, rib fractures, and a lacerated spleen. He underwent surgery to repair his pelvis and spleen and is currently being treated in the surgical intensive care unit. The patient has been receiving enteral nutritional support since admission to the ICU and is expected to require nutritional support for at least another week. He has no significant history of chronic organ failure or malnutrition prior to admission. The patient has been deemed appropriate for protein supplementation according to the study guidelines and is eligible to participate in the trial. He has no history of intestinal discontinuity, short bowel syndrome, bowel obstruction, enterocutaneous fistula, intestinal ischemia, or massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and enteral access is obtainable. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 42-year-old woman presents with chronic low back pain for the past 6 months, with a pain score of 7/10 on the NPRS scale. She has not undergone any physical therapy intervention or surgery for her condition. The patient does not have any neurological, musculoskeletal, or sensory affectations, nor evidence of an infectious process, fever or hypotension. She does not have any metallic implants in the low back area or treated area. However, she is taking antidepressants for depression. The patient has been informed about the study and has signed the informed consent form. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided.

This study is looking for healthy male or female volunteers between the ages of 18 and 55 years old. The participant must be able to swallow and retain oral medication, and have adequate organ systems function. Female participants must be non-childbearing potential or using acceptable contraceptive methods. The study requires subjects who understand and are likely to comply with the protocol requirements and instruction to complete the study. Exclusion criteria includes having a clinically relevant abnormality, medical condition, or circumstance that makes them unsuitable for the study per the study doctor, history of drug or other allergies, use of an investigation drug within 28 days or 5 half-lives, blood donation in excess of 500mL within 56 days prior to dosing or intends to donate within 30 days of the post-treatment follow-up visit, presence of or suspected iron deficiency, positive stool for occult blood, female subject who is lactating, positive urine drug screen, positive for HIV antibody, hepatitis C antibody or hepatitis B surface antigen, use of tobacco-containing products within the past 12 months prior to screening, history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependence within 6 months of screening, history or presence of uncontrolled emesis, and positive purified protein derivative (PPD) skin test for tuberculosis.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a diagnosis of prostate cancer. He has undergone bilateral orchiectomy and is currently receiving gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist therapy. He is experiencing hot flashes with a score of 6 per day that interfere with his daily activities and affect his sleep. He has no history of other significant medical problems, and his physical exam and lab studies were normal, except for the expected side effects of androgen deprivation therapy. He has not taken estrogen or progestational drugs in the last 4 weeks and is not taking gabapentin or antidepressants. He is interested in alternative therapies to help him manage his hot flashes and improve his quality of life. He is willing to undergo acupuncture therapy twice weekly for 4 weeks and then once weekly for an additional 6 weeks. He is aware that this is a randomized clinical trial and he may receive placebo acupuncture. He understands that the study will assess the impact of acupuncture therapy on the frequency and intensity of his hot flashes, as well as his quality of life. He is willing to complete questionnaires at baseline, weeks 2, 4, 6, and 10, and then at 6 weeks after completion of study treatment. He is also willing to provide blood and urine samples for analysis of serotonin, 5-HIAA, calcitonin gene-related peptide, and MHPG levels. He understands that tongue diagnosis will be used as a traditional Chinese clinical assessment method to predict clinical and biological changes.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years, presented to the clinic with uncontrolled blood sugar levels despite oral hypoglycemic medications. His latest HbA1C level was 9.5%, and his fasting blood glucose level was 250 mg/dL. The patient has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are currently well controlled with medications. He is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. The physician has decided to start insulin therapy and has selected NovoMix® 30 as the insulin of choice. The patient has not received insulin therapy before and has not used NovoMix® 30 in the past 4 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the observational study to document the effectiveness of NovoMix® 30 in routine clinical practice.

A 38-year-old woman has been struggling with cellulite on her thighs and buttocks for several years. She has tried various creams and treatments with no significant improvement. She has a BMI of 28 and has not had any recent hormonal changes. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new treatment option for cellulite. She has not had any previous surgery in the treated area and is not currently undergoing any medical or cosmetic treatment for cellulite. She is committed to following medical directions during the study and has signed the informed consent form.

25yo healthy male who exercises 0-5 hours per week with no history of cardiovascular or metabolic disease. He is a non-smoker and has never used performance-enhancing drugs. He is interested in participating in a study on the effects of micro-dose and low-dose rhEpo on mitochondrial function and cognitive performance.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic diarrhea for the past year. She has been diagnosed with IBS diarrheal variant (IBS-D) and has tried various diets to alleviate her symptoms, but has not found much relief. She currently takes a probiotic supplement and has been on a low-lactose diet for the past month. Her medical history is non-significant, and she takes no other medications. She is willing to change her current diet and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the efficacy of a low-FODMAPs diet compared to specific dietary advice for IBS-D. She has no history of serious cardiac, hepatic, neurological or psychiatric diseases, and has not been diagnosed with any other GI diseases that could explain her symptoms.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with grade IV Glioblastoma multiforme. He has undergone surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. However, the tumor has recurred and has grown in size. The patient has no other medical conditions and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He is well-dressed and well-nourished, with a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. His blood work shows a WBC count of 4,500/mm^3, absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3, platelet count of 150,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin of 12 g/dL. His bilirubin level is 0.9 mg/dL and SGOT level is within normal limits. His creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL. He has no history of unstable angina or congestive heart failure, and no myocardial infarction in the last 6 months. He has no significant alcoholism or substance abuse, and is HIV negative. He has no active infection or other severe disease that would preclude study. The patient has had only one relapse after prior chemotherapy for his glioblastoma. He has not received temozolomide or irinotecan before, and has not received any other anticancer chemotherapy for more than 4 weeks. The patient is currently not taking any drugs that would preclude study. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study-related tasks.

This is a 45-year-old female who underwent surgery for stage II breast cancer approximately 8 months ago. She has completed her primary treatment and has been in remission for the past 4 months. She is interested in maintaining a healthy lifestyle to improve her quality of life and prevent cancer recurrence. However, she has been struggling to adhere to a regular exercise routine and a healthy diet. She is currently not meeting the recommended daily intake of vegetables and fruits. She has access to the internet and a mobile phone and is willing to participate in a web-based program to help her achieve her health goals. She has no history of heart or breathing problems, and her BMI is within the healthy range. She is motivated to make positive changes in her lifestyle and willing to commit to the program.

A 34-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of sickle cell disease without any vaso-occlusive crisis in the last two weeks. She has been medically stable and is able to speak and understand English to complete assessments and scales. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol dependence/abuse within the past 5 years or cigarette smoking. She has not used tranquilizers, steroids, or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents three or more times per week. The patient does not have any clinically significant medical conditions that will confound the analysis of factors associated with sickle cell pain, such as chronic inflammatory disease, diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled hypertension, or known malignancies. The patient is willing to participate in the study, undergo weekly clinic visits, provide blood samples and keep a pain diary for 4 weeks after the first visit. The patient is also willing to undergo one session of quantitative sensory testing.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been caring for her husband, who was recently diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer. She has been struggling with feelings of anxiety and depression, as well as fatigue from the demands of caregiving. She has access to an Internet-connected device and is interested in participating in a study that could provide her with support and resources to improve her quality of life and decrease her psychological distress. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past and is willing to commit to the time and effort required for the study.

A 58-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure (CHF) is seeking to participate in the RoC-HF study. The patient has been diagnosed with CHF for 3 years and is currently receiving treatment according to the current Heart Failure Guidelines of the European Society of Cardiology. The patient reports NYHA class II-IV symptoms and has a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 50%. The patient has not been hospitalized for CHF in the past month and has not undergone any surgical procedures within the past 3 months. The patient has no significant valve disease and has not received any organ transplant. The patient is willing and able to provide signed informed consent prior to participation in any study-related procedures.

The patient is a healthy 22-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) vaccine. She has no history of autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency, bleeding disorders, or significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use highly effective contraception throughout the study period. She has not received any live attenuated vaccinations within the past 30 days or blood products within the past 120 days. She has not had any febrile illness within 14 days of the first dose of vaccine. She does not have a history of serious reactions to vaccines, hereditary, acquired or idiopathic forms of angioedema or idiopathic urticaria within the past year. She has no history of asthma, diabetes mellitus type 1 or type 2, thyroid disease, hypertension, bleeding disorder, significant bruising or bleeding difficulties with IM injections or blood draws, malignancy, seizure disorder, asplenia, functional asplenia, or history of Guillain-Barre Syndrome. She has a normal BMI and has not taken any systemic immunosuppressive medications or immunomodulating therapy within the past 180 days. She has not received any investigational research agents within the past 30 days and is not planning to receive any investigational products while on study. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and willing to allow storage of blood and saliva for future research.

A 40-year-old male diagnosed with low-risk prostate cancer 18 months ago, treated with brachytherapy, and currently under observation. The patient is concerned about the potential impact of radiation therapy on his fertility and is interested in participating in a study to assess the effect of radiation therapy on semen quality and fertility. The patient has no prior history of infertility, has not undergone a vasectomy, and has not received LHRH therapy or anti-androgens in the last 6 and 3 months, respectively. The patient has not taken finasteride or dutasteride in the last 4 months and has not used alpha blockers within 7 days of specimen provision.

This is a 55 year-old female with a history of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) who has been diagnosed with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with fibrosis stage between F0 and F3. She is homozygous for the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing 3 (PNPLA3) 148M risk allele. She has a body weight of 67 kg with a BMI of 30 kg/m². The patient has agreed to follow the protocol-defined contraceptive procedures and is willing to provide mandatory genetic PNPLA3 I148M determination genetic/biomarker for inclusion/exclusion in the clinical study. She has not undergone liver transplant nor is on a liver transplant list. She does not have any history or presence of hepatic disease other than NAFLD and NASH. The patient has a negative result for serum hepatitis B surface antigen and human immunodeficiency virus. She does not have a history of renal disease or cardiovascular event within the last 6 months prior to the screening visit. She has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 pneumonia or any significant findings from pulmonary imaging tests. The patient has not undergone bariatric surgery or initiated a weight loss diet within the last 6 months and has not experienced changes in any concomitant medication that may impact the study readouts.

A 62-year-old man has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right knee for the past several months. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate osteoarthritis of the knee by his primary care physician. He has no history of knee instability or systemic inflammatory arthropathy. He has not had any recent intra-articular intervention on his knee. He has not been diagnosed with anemia or coagulopathy, nor is he currently taking any blood thinners. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effects of hyaluronic acid to platelet-rich plasma injections for the treatment of osteoarthritis in the knee. He is willing to undergo blood draws and synovial fluid aspirates for analysis of pro- and anti-inflammatory markers. He understands that he will be randomized to receive either the hyaluronic acid or platelet-rich plasma injections, and that the study is double-blind, meaning that neither he nor the primary research team performing analysis will know which treatment he received. He is willing to limit the use of his leg for at least 24 hours after the injection and use cold therapy/icing for discomfort. He is willing to rest or perform mild exertion activities during the treatment period, followed by gradual return to sports or recreational activities as tolerated.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His biopsy results showed Gleason score of 8, and his PSA level was above 20. He has been experiencing urinary symptoms such as frequent urination, difficulty starting and stopping the flow of urine and blood in the urine. He has no history of cancer or any other significant medical issues. His performance status score is 1. He has undergone a negative bone scan and no distant metastasis has been detected. He is willing to participate in the study and sign the consent form. He has no severe psychiatric or medical problems that could affect his participation in the study. His liver function tests are normal. He is available for treatments and follow-up visits.

A 25-year-old female presents to the clinic with symptoms of acute bronchitis, including cough, chest congestion, and shortness of breath. She has had these symptoms for the past 3 days and reports feeling generally unwell. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon physical examination, the patient has a bronchitis severity score of 6 points. She is otherwise healthy and able to comply with the requirements of the clinical trial. The patient provides written consent to participate in the trial and is randomized to receive either DW1601, DW16011, or DW16012 for the treatment of her acute bronchitis. She does not have any severe respiratory diseases or hemostatic disorders that would interfere with the study assessment.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection six years ago. She has been on ART for the past four years and her viral load has been undetectable (less than 50 copies/ml) for more than a year. Her current medication regimen includes abacavir, lamivudine, and efavirenz. The patient has a history of asthma and hypertension, both well-controlled with medication. She works as a teacher and lives alone. She is sexually active with her partner and uses condoms consistently. She has no history of opportunistic infections or drug allergies. Her CD4 count at screening was 500 cells/mm3, and her hemoglobin, platelet count, and renal function are all within normal limits. She does not drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. She is interested in participating in the study to see if adding raltegravir to her current ART regimen will further reduce her viral load.

Patient is a 35-year-old sedentary female who works in an office and spends most of her leisure time watching TV or browsing social media. She is concerned about her health and intends to be physically active but finds it challenging to start an exercise routine. She has access to a mobile phone and is fluent in English. She has no known medical conditions that require special attention during an exercise program, has not planned any trips abroad during the study period, and has not had a baby in the last 6 months. Her BMI is 32.0 kg/m2. She is not currently participating in any lifestyle modification programs or research studies that may confound the results of the study. She has not had bariatric surgery and has no plans to have it in the next 12 months.

A 9-year-old girl is admitted to the pediatric clinic for treatment of pneumonia. She has never had a catheter-related infection before and has no history of systemic infection or immunological disease. She is not currently on any antibiotics, and she does not have any scar tissue in the catheterization area. She has no chronic skin diseases or history of allergies. The medical staff needs to place a peripheric intravenous catheter to provide her with the necessary intravenous treatment. The clinical trial team will evaluate the effectiveness of using sodium bicarbonate as a skin antiseptic in preventing catheter-related infections and compare it with other commonly used antiseptic agents.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) after experiencing abdominal discomfort and fatigue. The patient is overweight with a BMI of 31 and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol but has a family history of diabetes and high blood pressure. He is currently taking medication for hypertension. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of probiotics on NAFLD. He has not taken antibiotics for more than a week and has not lost more than 10% of baseline body weight during the study period. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend follow-up visits.

A 30-year-old female presents with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 5 years. She has been treated with corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and azathioprine, but has not achieved remission. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has no significant allergies or previous surgeries. She experiences symptoms of joint pain, fatigue, and rash. She meets at least 4 of 11 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Classification criteria for SLE. She has failed corticosteroids and azathioprine for mucocutaneous disease, and is unable to be weaned from prednisone to less than 0.5 mg/kg/day for more than 6 months. She has obvious cushingoid habitus. Her recent biopsy was negative for malignancy. Her baseline laboratory values are as follows: WBC: 4,200/mm3, Hgb: 11 g/dL, platelets: 180,000/mm3, creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL, AST: 25 U/L, ALT: 22 U/L, ANA: positive. She is able to give informed consent. She is not HIV positive and has no ongoing malignancy or active infection. She has no known hypersensitivity to E Coli derived proteins. She is willing to pursue effective means of birth control and understands the risk of irreversible sterility as a side effect of therapy.

A 42-year-old female with a history of hypertension and migraines presents to the nephrology clinic with a recent diagnosis of end-stage renal disease. She has no family history of renal disease and has never had any previous kidney issues. She reports taking over-the-counter analgesics for her migraines, specifically ibuprofen and acetaminophen, on a regular basis for the past 5 years. She is currently undergoing dialysis three times a week and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the association between non-phenacetin-containing analgesics and end-stage renal disease. She meets the inclusion criteria for cases in the SAN trial and is willing to be interviewed about her lifetime exposure to analgesics and potential renal risk factors.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. She has never been a smoker and has no significant past medical history. Her symptoms include persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. She underwent radiological imaging that showed multiple lung nodules and pleural effusion. A biopsy was attempted but was unsuccessful. A subsequent liquid biopsy revealed an activating EGFR mutation (L858R) from circulating tumor DNA. She has not received any prior treatment for her cancer. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has no significant comorbidities and her organ function is normal. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers a targeted therapy option for her cancer. She is willing to undergo regular monitoring and follow-up visits for the study.

A 26-year-old right-handed female with normal vision and no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders came to the clinic to participate in an early phase clinical trial on temporal interference brain stimulation. She has no medical history of fainting spells, seizures or any systemic illness. She is not taking any medication except for birth control. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She underwent a comprehensive screening process, including MRI and retinotopic mapping, and met all the inclusion criteria for the study. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in up to 6 study visits, including the TI stimulation sessions. She will be monitored for any adverse effects throughout the study.

This clinical trial is not recruiting individual patients, as it is a community-wide study aimed at evaluating the effectiveness of oral azithromycin in controlling trachoma in rural areas of Egypt. Therefore, there is no patient description required.

A 64-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis and hip pain for the past 10 years presented to the clinic for evaluation of total hip replacement surgery. She has been taking over-the-counter pain medication but has not obtained significant relief. She is married and lives with her husband. She has no other significant medical history and does not smoke. She exercises regularly but has stopped due to the hip pain. She does not have any known allergies to medications or food. She has consulted with her primary care physician and has been referred to the orthopedic surgeon for further evaluation.

32F with a BMI of 27.5 kg/m2 who has struggled with weight loss attempts in the past. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She has no known allergies to food and has not used any nutritional or sport supplements. She is not currently pregnant nor trying to become pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a study that will help her achieve her weight loss goals and she is committed to following a dietary intervention plan.

This is a 43-year-old male with a history of spinal cord injury resulting in neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD). The patient experiences urinary urgency with or without incontinence and voiding dysfunction that severely impairs his quality of life. The patient has tried antimuscarinics and alpha-blockers for at least 4 weeks each, but has not seen significant improvement in their symptoms. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS) for NLUTD. They have had a urethro-cystoscopy and bladder washing cytology within 1 year before inclusion and a urodynamic investigation within the last 6 months with no change in bladder medication since then. The patient is able to demonstrate a motor response by TTNS stimulation in at least one leg. They are willing to refrain from changing or starting any new medications or treatments for their LUTD during the entire study period. The patient does not have any contraindications to the investigational product and is not currently undergoing any neuromodulation treatment for urological indication, nor have they had botulinum toxin injections in the detrusor and/or urethral sphincter in the last six months. They are not pregnant or breastfeeding and have no intention to become pregnant during the course of the study.

52-year-old male diagnosed with chronic HCV infection with genotype 1a. The patient has no history of cirrhosis and has not been treated with any antiviral agents before. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He presents with fatigue, mild abdominal discomfort, and elevated liver enzymes. The patient's laboratory result confirms hepatitis C viral (HCV) genotype (GT) 1a infection. The patient has no other significant comorbidities and meets the specific human leukocyte antigen (HLA) allele requirements for the study. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or diagnosed with HBsAg or anti-human immunodeficiency virus antibody (HIV Ab) positive immunoassay.

The patient is a 2-month-old male infant with a diagnosis of inguinal hernia. He is scheduled for an elective surgery at KKH. He was born at full term and his birth weight was 3.5 kg. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has no known allergies. His parents report that he is feeding well and has normal bowel movements. His physical exam reveals a reducible right inguinal hernia. The infant is otherwise healthy, with no signs of respiratory distress or other medical issues. The parents have been informed about the study and have given their consent for their child to participate. The infant meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and there are no exclusion criteria.

Pt is a 70yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. He reports occasional difficulty with balance and has had a few falls in the past year. He is able to ambulate independently with a cane. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his balance and reduce his risk of falls. He has no significant visual or cognitive impairments. His medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and acetaminophen as needed for pain.

50-year-old female diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with high-risk features, including dual expresser status and testicular involvement. No evidence of central nervous system involvement on initial staging. Performance status is 0. Renal function is normal. The patient is not pregnant and agrees to use contraception during the study. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent. No significant comorbidities are present in the investigator's judgment.

A 62-year-old man presented to the emergency department after a fall down the stairs. He hit his head on the railing and was experiencing a headache and dizziness. He was taking aspirin and clopidogrel for a history of stroke. A CT scan was performed and showed no evidence of hemorrhage. He was admitted to the emergency department observation unit for 24 hours and then discharged home with instructions to follow up with his primary care physician. He was contacted by phone at 2, 7, 15, 30, 60, and 90 days after his ED visit to assess for any new symptoms or complications related to his head injury.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman from the United States who has been diagnosed with interstitial lung disease (ILD) associated with connective tissue disorder (CTD) 6 months ago. She has been on conventional therapy for 6 months, but there has been no evidence of improvement. She has a history of Raynaud's phenomenon, joint pain, and fatigue. She is currently taking prednisone (10mg/day) and hydroxychloroquine (200mg/day). She has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. Her BMI is 25, BP: 120/75, HR: 80/min. Her laboratory study is remarkable for CRP: 2mg/dl, ESR: 28mm/h, ANA: 1:640, RF: 35 IU/ml, and anti-SSA: positive.

A 10-year-old boy with a primary diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and anxiety disorder, who has been receiving treatment for the past 2 months but has not shown significant improvement. He has a supportive family and is motivated to try new therapy options. He has no history of other psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any psychiatric medications. He enjoys playing video games and is comfortable with technology. His parents are willing to participate in the study and provide support during the VR exposure therapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who has no significant medical history or current health concerns. He has a body weight of 80 kg and a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2. He has no history of Helicobacter pylori infection or gastrointestinal disorders. He is not currently taking any prescription drugs, herbal medicines, or over-the-counter drugs. He has not participated in any other clinical studies or bioequivalence studies within the past three months. He is a non-smoker and does not consume excessive amounts of caffeine or alcohol. He agrees to abstain from grapefruit-containing foods and caffeine-containing foods during the hospitalization period. He is willing to use a medically acceptable method of contraception throughout the study. The patient provides written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension was recently admitted to the Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA) for complications related to his diabetes. He is currently taking multiple medications for his conditions, but he reports difficulty remembering to take them as prescribed. He has a history of smoking and drinking alcohol but has recently quit both. He has a literate caregiver who assists him with his medications. He speaks and reads Portuguese fluently and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with follicular lymphoma three years ago has undergone two lines of treatment with combination chemoimmunotherapy, including R-bendamustine and R-CHOP, with little success. The patient has measurable disease and no known presence or history of central nervous system involvement by lymphoma. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and adequate renal, hepatic, pulmonary, and cardiac function. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use birth control from the time of consent through 6 months following chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell infusion. The patient is available to undergo leukapheresis and conditioning chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine for 3 days to prepare for the infusion with axicabtagene ciloleucel. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the experimental product, which is made from the patient's own white blood cells, can help fight the cancer and improve the patient's condition.

A 58 yo F with past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and a previous stroke is being considered for participation in a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of antiplatelet therapy in patients with cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA). The patient has been stable on aspirin therapy for the past year, but her physician is concerned about the potential risks of combining antiplatelet therapy with CAA. The patient is able to swallow tablets and has no known allergies to aspirin or clopidogrel. She has not participated in any other experimental device or drug study in the past 30 days and is willing to comply with the trial requirements. The patient has no history of surgical thrombolysis, arteritis, aneurysms, arterial trauma, tumors, infections, fever, inflammatory diseases, post-embolization bleeding, peripheral vascular thrombosis, or hemophilia. The patient is considered medically stable by her physician and is not expected to need to change or discontinue her current medication regimen during the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastases to the liver, adrenal glands, and bones. She has already received first-line treatment with chemotherapy and has shown progression. She is currently experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and weight loss. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. Her lab reports show adequate renal, hepatic, and hematologic functions. She is willing to provide recently acquired (within 90 days) tumor tissue from an unresectable or metastatic site of disease for biomarker analyses. She has no active brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases. She has no known autoimmune diseases, and her medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has had a negative test for Hep B/C, HIV, and pregnancy.

55F with a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 5 years ago on Metformin, presents to the clinic for a follow-up appointment. The patient reports poor blood pressure control despite being on multiple antihypertensive medications. The patient also reports occasional episodes of nocturia and fatigue. The physical examination revealed a blood pressure of 150/95 mmHg, BMI of 30 kg/m2, and bilateral pedal edema. The laboratory workup showed a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL, HbA1c of 7.5%, and albuminuria/proteinuria with a urinary albumin creatinine ratio (UACR) of 600 mg/g. The patient was assessed to have microalbuminuria/proteinuria and deemed eligible for the clinical trial to assess the effects of valsartan on albuminuria/proteinuria in hypertensive patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient met all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria, and expressed interest in participating in the study after receiving a thorough explanation of the study procedures and its potential benefits and risks.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with atopic asthma by her physician. She has a history of positive skin tests for common allergens like dust mites, pollen, and pet dander. Her asthma symptoms are well controlled on a daily regimen of inhaled corticosteroids and beta-agonists. She has never been exposed to omalizumab before. She has a BMI of 23, and she is not currently taking any prescription medication other than her asthma medication. She has no history of drug abuse or significant psychiatric disease. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance medical research and potentially benefit others with asthma.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has not received any previous antiretroviral therapy. His plasma HIV-1 RNA levels are ≥ 5,000 copies/mL. He has no history of hepatitis B or C infection, and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He has a CD4+ cell count of 200 cells/µL. His estimated glomerular filtration rate is 90 mL/min according to the Cockcroft Gault formula. He has normal thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and serum amylase levels. He has no history of malignancy or active serious infections. He is not currently taking any medications contraindicated for use with emtricitabine or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. He is willing to use highly effective contraception methods during heterosexual intercourse throughout the study period and for 90 days following discontinuation of investigational medicinal product. He is able to understand and sign a written informed consent form.

10-year-old male patient presented to the pediatric gastroenterology clinic with a history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for the past 6 weeks. He has lost 5% of his body weight over the past month. He has no history of fever, vomiting, or joint pain. No family history of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) was reported. Physical examination revealed mild abdominal tenderness without palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly. His height and weight are at the 50th percentile. Initial laboratory tests showed elevated inflammatory markers with a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 12 mg/L and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 30 mm/h. Complete blood count revealed a mild anemia with hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL and platelets of 350,000/μL. Stool studies were negative for bacterial and parasitic infections. Colonoscopy showed diffuse erythema, friability, and ulceration throughout the colon with a Pediatric Ulcerative Colitis Activity Index (PUCAI) score of 45. Histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. The patient is planned to receive 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) induction treatment but will be enrolled in a clinical trial for complementary therapy with curcumin. The patient and his legal guardians agreed to participate and provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman with a history of diabetic macular edema. She has been receiving intravitreal injections of bevacizumab every month for the past 3 months. She has not been diagnosed with glaucoma or any other ocular disease. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. She has no history of ocular surgery or laser procedures. She wears contact lenses but will remove them prior to the study visits. She is able to participate on site over the multi-visit study period. Her lab tests show FBS: 120 mg/dl HbA1c: 7.1%, cholesterol: 180 mg/dl, TG: 120 mg/dl, LDL: 100 mg/dl, HDL: 50 mg/dl. She is able and willing to give informed consent and attend the study visits.

A 60-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with localized prostate cancer after undergoing a biopsy. He has no prior history of cancer, except for a basal cell carcinoma on his forehead that was treated with surgical excision. The patient has no known history of hepatic or renal disease, and his lab values are within normal limits. He has an omnivorous diet and does not consume a lot of soy products. He currently takes a multivitamin and is not taking any nutritional supplements that contain soy or soy isoflavones. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 due to mild fatigue, but he is otherwise healthy. He has no history of allergic reactions to soy isoflavones or other compounds similar to Novasoy 400®. He is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent. The patient is scheduled for prostatectomy within the next 3-6 weeks and is willing to take two capsules of either purified isoflavones or placebo daily for the duration of the study.

A 42 year old male patient was diagnosed with thymic carcinoma after presenting with chest pain, cough, and shortness of breath. A CT scan showed a large mass in the anterior mediastinum. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of thymic carcinoma. The patient has no significant past medical history and has never smoked. The patient is married with three children and works as an accountant. He is physically active and enjoys jogging and swimming. His blood work and other diagnostic tests revealed that he is otherwise healthy. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial in hopes of improving his chances of complete resection and preventing recurrence. He understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to undergo the combined chemotherapy and radiation therapy prior to surgery.

A 52-year-old man presented with knee pain and stiffness that has persisted for the past year. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs as prescribed by his physician. He has no history of major illness or surgery, and he is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications or any other substances. He works as a teacher and is physically active, but his knee pain has limited his mobility and ability to engage in physical activity. His damaged cartilage area is approximately 5 cm2. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo a planned cesarean section delivery due to a history of previous cesarean section. She has no known allergies or intolerances to local anesthetics or steroids. She has an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) classification of II, with mild systemic disease due to her pregnancy. The patient is currently at 35 weeks gestation and has no significant medical history. She has no pre-existing neurological or anatomical deficits that would preclude a regional block. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. She will receive neuraxial anesthesia with spinal anesthesia intraoperatively, which is the standard of care at the institution for cesarean section deliveries. The patient is not classified as an emergency case and will not require general anesthesia or epidural anesthesia. She has a BMI of 28.7, which is within the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has suffered from atopic dermatitis for the past 10 years. She experiences severe itching and redness on her face and neck, which have a significant impact on her quality of life. The patient has tried various topical treatments, including corticosteroids, but they have not provided complete relief. She has no history of other skin conditions, but she has experienced mild allergic reactions to certain medications in the past. The patient is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She is willing to take oral ivermectin once a week for 4 weeks and monitor her symptoms for 8 weeks. The patient is able to read and speak English fluently and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She has signed and dated the informed consent document and is willing to use effective birth control during the study period. The patient does not have any medical conditions or laboratory abnormalities that would put her at risk or interfere with the study results.

A 52 year old man was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) 2 years ago after presenting with fatigue and enlarged lymph nodes. He received 6 cycles of bendamustine and rituximab with a partial response. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He has no history of significant allergic reaction to antibody therapies or active secondary malignancy. He has been HIV and HCV negative, and has no history of central nervous system involvement with CLL. There is no active infection requiring treatment with antibiotic, antiviral or antifungal agents. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who lives at home and has been experiencing signs of frailty, such as decreased mobility and difficulty completing daily tasks. He is able to walk inside his home with the assistance of a mobility aid, but has difficulty walking longer distances. He communicates in Finnish and is interested in participating in a study that could help him maintain his independence and avoid institutional care. The patient has not been diagnosed with severe neurological, heart, or musculoskeletal diseases that would prevent him from participating in long-term physiotherapy. Additionally, he does not have a terminal illness that would diminish his estimated home-dwelling time to less than two years. The patient does not have severe mental problems or problems with hearing or eyesight. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the intervention protocol for 12 months, which includes home-based physiotherapy (physical exercise) twice a week. The patient will be randomized into either the intervention group or the control group and will have measurements taken at his home at baseline, and after 3, 6 and 12 months. The study will also collect register data on living and housing conditions, use and costs of social and health care services, and mortality at the end of the follow-up (24 months since the beginning of the study).

A 59-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B presents with abdominal pain, jaundice, and significant weight loss over the past few months. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the liver and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The patient has no evidence of metastatic disease, and surgery is not an option due to the location and size of the tumor. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and normal organ function. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is interested in potentially receiving hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) of chemotherapy to treat the cancer. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was brought to the emergency department due to chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. Upon arrival, the patient was found to have a blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on room air. The patient is alert and oriented, with no signs of confusion or altered mental status. The patient is in moderate distress due to his symptoms. The emergency medicine team has decided that the patient requires arterial line placement for continuous blood pressure monitoring and repeated arterial blood gas sampling.
