The patient is considered a candidate for the clinical trial comparing landmark vs ultrasound guided arterial line placement by emergency medicine interns. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 68 year old man who has recently been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and is scheduled for elective surgical treatment. He has a history of smoking, but quit 10 years ago, and has been diagnosed with hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He reports feeling anxious and worried about the upcoming surgery, and feels like he does not have enough information about the procedure and what to expect postoperatively. He is fluent in Swedish and is able to communicate effectively with healthcare providers. He does not have any visual or hearing impairments, and has not been diagnosed with dementia or any other medical conditions with a limited life expectancy. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially receive additional support and information during his surgical treatment for AAA.

A 25-year-old female student who was diagnosed with ADHD at the age of 10. She has tried various medications to manage her symptoms, but none have been effective. She experiences ongoing inattention and impulsivity that negatively impacts her academic performance and daily life. She has no history of epilepsy, head trauma, or comorbid psychiatric disorders. She is not taking any renin angiotensin aldosterone inhibitors or other potassium elevating agents. She has a normal IQ and no mouth lesions. She is willing to undergo the lidocaine effectiveness test and participate in the study.

An 72-year-old man fell from a ladder while cleaning gutters around his house. He experienced severe pain in the right hip, and he was unable to stand or move his right leg. He was brought to the emergency department by ambulance. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which is well controlled with medication. He had no prior history of hip fractures or surgeries. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. The vital signs are within normal limits. The examination revealed right hip tenderness, inability to bear weight, and shortened leg. Radiography showed a displaced femoral neck fracture. The patient is eligible for hemi-arthroplasty as per the algorithm used at the University hospital Basel. The patient wishes to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

As this is a clinical trial focused on college students, there is no specific patient description required. However, the target population for this study is incoming college students aged 18-21 at the University of Minnesota who engage in heavy drinking or are at risk for high-risk alcohol use and associated negative consequences.

A 55 year old male patient visited the clinic with the complaint of recurrent painless hematuria for a month. He also reported having urinary frequency and urgency. The patient underwent cystoscopy and biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder with stage T2. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The latest lab results showed that his WBC count was 6,000, and platelet count was 200,000. His creatinine level was 1.2 mg/dL and bilirubin was within normal range. The patient is not pregnant and uses adequate contraception. The patient's performance status is Karnofsky 80%. The patient has no other active malignancy.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and moderate renal impairment with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 ml/min/1.73m2. She is currently on metformin, lisinopril, and amlodipine for her diabetes and hypertension management. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not smoke. Her current weight is 160 lbs, and her BMI is 32 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of the pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of MNTX in patients with impaired renal function. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including abstaining from grapefruit or grapefruit juice consumption for seven days prior to the administration of study medication. She does not require hemodialysis and is in generally good health, aside from her CKD.

8-year-old male scheduled for outpatient tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis and obstructive sleep apnea. He weighs 45 kg and is between the 5th and 95th percentile for weight. He is able to self-report pain and will complete a pain diary with assistance from his mother. He does not require pre-anesthesia medication for anxiety and does not need an interpreter for verbal or written communication. He does not have significant obstructive sleep apnea that would disqualify him from outpatient surgery. He does not have ongoing oxygen dependence, pulmonary hypertension, or an elevated risk of regurgitation. He has no history of seizures or chronic pain disorders requiring medication. He does not have any developmental or cognitive disabilities. He has no history of adverse reactions to components of liquid gabapentin or placebo.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). He has no prior history of cancer and has never received any systemic therapy for his condition. He is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel habits. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no other significant medical history. His liver, kidney, and bone marrow function are all within normal limits. He has at least one measurable lesion according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. He has not received any prior therapy with monoclonal antibodies or small molecule inhibitors against Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) or VEGF receptors, including Avastin® or Avastin® biosimilar. He has not had any spinal cord compression or brain metastases and has no unresolved toxicity from previous anticancer therapy. He has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and has not experienced any thrombotic or hemorrhagic events within the last 6 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive BI 695502 in combination with leucovorin/5-fluorouracil/oxaliplatin (mFOLFOX6) and as maintenance therapy (when applicable) to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the treatment, as well as the efficacy parameters including progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (proportion of patients with complete response [CR] plus partial response [PR]), overall survival (OS), duration of response (DOR), and time to progression (TTP).

25-year-old Indigenous woman residing in a remote community in Darwin, currently in her third trimester of pregnancy with an uncomplicated pregnancy. The patient has not received the 23 valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (23vPPV) in the last three years and has not received a previous dose of dTPa. The patient intends to deliver her child at the Royal Darwin Hospital and has given informed consent to participate in the PneuMum clinical trial. The patient does not have HIV and does not have a history of severe allergy, uncontrolled asthma or splenectomy.

The patient is a 35 year old male with a BMI of 35.9 who has struggled with weight loss for several years. He has tried various diets and exercise programs without significant success. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SR147778 on weight loss. He is willing to follow a hypocaloric diet and has no history of significant medical conditions. He is able to follow verbal and written instructions and can comply with the double method of birth control if applicable. He has not used any anti-obesity drugs or herbal preparations for weight reduction within the past 3 months. He is willing to participate in the study for 24 weeks and is willing to undergo physical examinations, laboratory evaluations, and 12-lead ECGs throughout the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in complete remission. He is scheduled to undergo a myeloablative conditioning regimen followed by allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. His donor is a matched unrelated donor. He has no history of psychosis or bronchial asthma. He is not currently using any drugs or alcohol. He is married and has no children. His past medical history is significant for seasonal allergies and a broken arm in childhood. He is currently taking multivitamins and omega-3 supplements. He is physically active and enjoys running and weightlifting. His HCT-CI score is 0.

Unfortunately, as this is a study using an existing data set, there is no need for a patient description. However, I can provide general information about the study. The study will be examining the relationship between parental feeding styles and the quality of dinner meals in low-income Hispanic and African-American families with children enrolled in Head Start programs. The goal is to use the Healthy Eating Index to assess the overall quality of the dinner meal served and consumed, based on the different feeding styles used by the parents. Parents who were responsible for feeding the child while the child was not in Head Start and their oldest child enrolled in Head Start were included in the study, while children with dietary restraints or food allergies were excluded.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a diagnosis of limited systemic sclerosis/scleroderma. The patient has been experiencing ulcers on the fingertips of both hands for the past six months. The ulcers have been causing significant pain and discomfort, and have been interfering with the patient's ability to perform daily activities. The patient has no history of sympathectomy, and the ulcers are not due to any other conditions such as PVD, DM, or Thromboangiitis obliterans. The patient is not currently taking any antibiotics or Prostanoids, and has not received Bosentan therapy in the past. The patient has no history of severe liver or renal insufficiency or severe cardiac-pulmonary diseases. The patient's blood pressure is well-controlled and there is no evidence of untreated or therapy-refractory hypertension. The patient is compliant with medical treatment. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

A 55 yo F with a recent diagnosis of early stage endometrial cancer, grade 1 or 2, who has undergone a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy for endometrial cancer nor pelvic radiation. The patient must not have a history of another invasive malignancy, except for non-melanoma skin cancers or tumors curatively treated with no evidence of disease for ≥ 5 years. The patient must not have abnormal p53 and/or mismatch repair deficiency on immunohistochemistry without pathogenic POLE mutation. Finally, the

A 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes is currently hospitalized due to a suspected Staphylococcus aureus infection. The patient has a previous history of MRSA colonization. He is being treated with vancomycin for the infection. The patient's weight is 80 kg and his height is 180 cm. His serum creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL. His baseline laboratory results are within normal limits. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been suffering from unexplained muscle weakness, fatigue, and muscle pain for the past few years. He has seen several doctors and undergone multiple tests, but the exact cause of his symptoms remains unknown. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or family history of genetic diseases. He is willing to undergo genetic testing to help diagnose his condition and potentially receive personalized treatment. He has not undergone Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) or panel analysis previously.

The patient is a 52-year-old Chinese man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 2 years ago. He has been treated with multiple daily insulin injections for the last 8 months. He has no allergies and takes multivitamins daily. He has a positive family history of diabetes (his father and both grandparents). He is married and has one child. He works as a teacher and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He has no history of surgery or trauma with significant blood loss in the last 3 months. He is a smoker but is willing to refrain from smoking during the in-patient period. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve diabetes treatment in Chinese people.

The patient is a 12-18 month old toddler who has completed routine childhood vaccinations with two doses of Haemophilus influenzae type b outer membrane protein (Hib-OMP) containing vaccine OR three doses of diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis and Haemophilus influenzae type b (DTPa/Hib) containing vaccine at least 6 months before the start of the study. The toddler is in good health, with no history of major congenital defects or serious chronic illness. The toddler has not received any investigational or non-registered product (drug or vaccine) other than the study vaccine(s) within 30 days preceding the first dose of study vaccine, and has not been administered any immuno-suppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to vaccination. The toddler's parent or guardian has provided written informed consent to participate in the study, and the investigator believes they can and will comply with the requirements of the protocol.

A 45-year-old Indian man was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been experiencing symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. He has been prescribed other anti-diabetic medications but his condition has not improved. His treating physician has recommended treatment with liraglutide and he is interested in participating in this study to evaluate its safety and effectiveness. He understands the study requirements and is able to give study-specific signed informed consent before any collection of information. He does not have a history of hypersensitivity to liraglutide or any of its excipients. He is not currently participating in another clinical trial and does not have the intention of becoming pregnant within the following 6 months.

34-year-old female with a history of infertility, undergoing IVF/ICSI embryo transfer. She has a BMI of 28 and no significant medical history. The patient's endometrial cavity is visualized adequately via ultrasound. She has previously undergone two failed cycles of embryo transfer, one fresh and one frozen. She has no history of ectopic pregnancy or multiple gestations. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two-dimensional and three-dimensional ultrasound for embryo transfer guidance to improve her chances of a successful pregnancy.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with colon cancer and needs to undergo elective surgery for ileo-colo-rectal resection with anastomosis. She has an American Society of Anesthesiologists' (ASA) class II and has agreed to participate in the study. She has no history of stoma before or at operation, and is not planning to undergo hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy for carcinomatosis. She has no contraindications for laparoscopic/robotic/open/converted surgery. She has no known allergies or comorbidities that would affect her eligibility for the study.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who recently underwent a surgical procedure at the Clinical Care Center/Wallace Tower Surgical Center. He has a history of chronic back pain and is currently taking opioids for pain management. His BMI is 27 and he has a history of high blood pressure which is well controlled with medication. He lives with his wife and two children. He is concerned about the potential for accidental ingestion of his unused opioids by his young children and wants to ensure proper disposal of any unused medication.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is scheduled for elective surgery for a herniated disc in her lower back. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Her physical exam is unremarkable. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her lab results are within normal limits. She has no history of recent anesthesia or any central neurological disorder. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the study.

18-month-old male with a history of mild to moderate Atopic Dermatitis (AD) and dry skin. His parents have tried various over-the-counter creams and ointments, but they have not been effective in relieving his symptoms. He has not had any signs or symptoms of AD within the last month prior to enrollment. The child has Fitzpatrick skin type III. The parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of a new modified Diprobase formulation for the treatment of AD in infants and children under physician's control.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of Type 2 diabetes. She has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 10 years and has been managing her blood sugar levels through medication and diet. She is fluent in English and able to comprehend and follow instructions. She is interested in participating in the study to determine the accuracy of her self-reported blood glucose levels versus those measured by a Blood Glucose Meter. She is willing to complete all study procedures and has no history of bleeding disorders or cognitive impairments. She is not pregnant and is not currently using a continuous glucose monitoring system. She is not an employee of any competitive medical device company.

Pt is a 35yo F with a 6-year history of IBS-D subtype. Her symptoms include abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, urgency, and occasional fecal incontinence. She reports that her symptoms have affected her quality of life and ability to work. She has tried several medications, including antispasmodics, antidiarrheals, and probiotics, with little improvement. She has no other relevant medical history, and she is not taking any other medications. She meets the Rome III criteria for IBS diagnosis. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain for the past 6 months. She works as a nurse and has a busy work schedule, which makes it difficult for her to find time for exercise. She is 5'5" tall and weighs 165 lbs, giving her a BMI of 27.5. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis based on the ACR criteria, with a Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grade of 2. She has been taking NSAIDs to manage her pain but is willing to try other options. She reports a score of 70/100 on the KOOS Pain subscale. She does not have any other known medical conditions and does not smoke or use drugs. She has not had any knee surgery or steroid injections in the past 6 months and does not have any planned for the next 6 months. She is able to ambulate without an assistive device and has not had any joint replacements or osteotomies. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn about other options for managing her knee pain.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl who lives with her mother and father. Both of her parents are smokers and smoke at least three cigarettes a day inside the house. The patient has never smoked and has no history of respiratory illness, asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has no unusual sensitivity to environmental odors or history of allergic reactions to foods or chemicals. She is not diabetic and is not currently taking any medication, except for occasional over-the-counter pain relievers for headaches. She has a healthy diet and a normal body weight. She enjoys sweet foods and drinks, but her preferences have not been measured before. She has no history of addiction or substance abuse. She and her parents have consented to provide saliva samples for genomic DNA analysis.

32 yo F with a history of knee pain, seeking treatment for a chondral defect. The patient is currently using a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) for pain management. Past Medical History: None. The patient has not had any prior surgeries, and is not currently taking any prescription medications other than the NSAID. The patient has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Physical Examination: The patient has moderate pain on palpation of the medial femoral condyle. There is no evidence of effusion or instability. The patient has full range of motion and no signs of crepitus. MRI findings: The MRI shows a 2 cm^2 chondral defect on the medial femoral condyle. The patient meets all of the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial, and has no exclusion criteria. The patient has been informed about the trial and has voluntarily signed the informed consent form.

A 28-year-old healthy female came to the clinic for a routine physical exam. She is a non-smoker, works as a nurse, and exercises regularly. She has no history of allergies. Her BMI is 23 kg/m2. She has regular menstrual periods and uses oral contraception. She has never been pregnant. She has no history of neurological or cardiovascular disorders. She has not used any psycho-active medication, illicit drugs, or alcohol in the past 2 years. She has not participated in any clinical trial within the last 3 months. She has normal ECG and laboratory values. She is not currently breastfeeding nor trying to conceive. She understands the trial procedures and is willing to follow instructions. She has provided written informed consent. She has not donated blood in the past 3 months. She has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 nor tested positive for it.

A 26-year-old female presents with recurring headaches and vision loss. She has been diagnosed with Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) and has tried multiple medical treatments, including acetazolamide and topiramate, with little success. Her visual field test shows moderate to severe visual function loss. Her MRI results indicate bilateral transverse sinus stenosis with a 50% reduction in the sinus lumen diameter. She is seeking alternative treatment options and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for venous sinus stenting. She is willing to undergo the procedure and follow-up appointments for evaluation of long-term efficacy.

62 year old male with a history of coronary artery disease and previous myocardial infarction, who underwent implantation of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) in 2010. He has had regular follow-up appointments with his cardiologist but has expressed concerns about his understanding of the device and how to identify if it has been recalled. He is fluent in English and is able to read and comprehend written materials. He has no significant hearing, sight, or reading impairments that would hinder his ability to complete written surveys. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with bilateral age-related cataracts. He has no preoperative corneal astigmatism or regular corneal astigmatism ≤2.5D. He has no history of corneal surgery or any abnormality, disease, or condition of the cornea that would clinically contraindicate the implantation of a toric IOL. He is willing and able to understand and sign an Informed Consent and attend post-operative examinations as per protocol schedule. He is planning to undergo cataract removal via phacoemulsification with implantation of an IOL and is available to undergo second eye surgery within 6 weeks of the first eye surgery. He is able to read and understand one of the following languages: Dutch, French, German, Italian, Spanish, English, or Catalan. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy during the course of the study. He meets all other protocol-defined inclusion criteria and does not meet any protocol-defined exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45 year old male of South Asian descent who presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has a family history of diabetes and heart disease, and has been experiencing occasional shortness of breath and chest discomfort during physical activity. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. His BMI is 29, indicating he is overweight. He has no history of malignancy, neck cancer, radiation therapy, and/or surgery. His fasting glucose level is measured to be 120 mg/dL during his visit. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about his cardiovascular risk and potential metabolic syndrome.

A 7-month-old baby boy was born with a ventricular septal defect and underwent a successful surgical repair at 3 months of age. However, he still experiences shortness of breath and fatigue during feeding. His cardiologist has recommended a corrective surgical repair using cardiopulmonary bypass. His parents have been informed about the potential risks associated with the surgery, including lung injury. They have also been informed about the clinical trial investigating whether pre-operative administration of Sildenafil can reduce lung injury. They are willing to enroll their child in the study and understand the potential risks and benefits of the trial. The baby boy has no known organ dysfunction, and his parents are fluent in English. He has not taken Sildenafil before, but the parents report no history of vomiting or intolerance to oral medication.

A 55-year-old Hispanic man presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past month, and they have been progressively getting worse. He denies any chest pain or palpitations. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. He also has a history of smoking, but he quit 2 years ago. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. He is married and has 2 children. He is able to understand and follow instructions in English. He has not had any major adverse cardiovascular events or surgeries in the past 6 weeks. He does not have a pacemaker, chest wall disease or pectus excavatum. He is not a candidate for heart or lung transplant. He is not pregnant, and he does not have end-stage renal or liver disease. His echocardiogram shows that he has heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). His ejection fraction is 35%.

A 45 yo Black F with a BMI of 28, a history of gestational diabetes, and a CDC diabetes risk assessment score of 7. She has been struggling with weight loss and has tried various diets and exercise programs with little success. She lives within driving distance of a participating church and is interested in participating in a community-based lifestyle intervention to improve her health and prevent the onset of diabetes. She has no known contraindications to moderate physical activity and is committed to making lifestyle changes to improve her health.

50 year old male with a history of smoking and hypertension. Imaging studies have revealed a mass in the kidney, suspected to be renal cell carcinoma. The patient has agreed to undergo surgery or biopsy for further diagnosis. The patient does not have Parkinson's disease or any allergies to the substances used in the study. The patient has normal renal function with a GFR of 80. The patient is not taking any of the excluded medications and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no history of mental illness or language difficulties.

A 32-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). She was diagnosed with SLE 4 years ago and has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, joint pain, and rash. Her medical history is significant for Raynaud's phenomenon and antiphospholipid syndrome. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and mycophenolate mofetil for SLE. Despite the medications, she still experiences flares and has difficulty in performing her daily activities. She has no history of malignancies or opportunistic infections. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of BENLYSTA for SLE. She understands the study requirements and provides written informed consent. Her physician confirms that she meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and agrees to enroll her in the BENLYSTA cohort.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with vulval cancer. The diagnosis was made after she noticed a painful lump on her genital area that has gradually increased in size. A biopsy confirmed the presence of cancer cells, and further tests showed that the cancer has not spread beyond the vulva. Her treatment plan includes surgical excision of the tumor and bilateral groin node dissection. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of PlasmaJet in reducing postoperative complications such as wound breakdown, lymphocyst and lymphedema formation following BGND for vulvar cancer. She is willing to provide informed consent and is not pregnant, lactating or planning pregnancy during the course of the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman with a history of hypertension for 5 years. She presents to the clinic complaining of palpitations and shortness of breath. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes mellitus, significant heart valve disease, hyperthyroidism, renal failure, malignancy, acute infection, recent thoracic or abdominal surgery, or current therapy of Vit D3. Her current medications include lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension management. She reports no family history of atrial fibrillation or cardiovascular disease. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for an irregularly irregular heartbeat with a pulse rate of 100 beats per minute. An electrocardiogram confirms the diagnosis of atrial fibrillation. Laboratory studies show that her serum vitamin D level is 20 ng/mL, which is below the normal range. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of vitamin D on new-onset AF in hypertensive patients.

A 62-year-old male with a history of Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS) is seeking treatment options after failing prior therapies. The patient has been diagnosed with MDS by World Health Organization criteria and is classified as intermediate-2 risk or high risk. The patient has undergone 4 cycles of hypomethylating agent therapy with no response, loss of response, or progressive disease/treatment intolerance. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 2 or lower and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has a renal glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of at least 60 ml/min and meets the screening laboratory values, including Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) / Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 3.0 times upper limit of normal, and Bilirubin < 1.5 times upper limit of normal. The patient is not HIV positive and has no active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C infection. The patient is not using chemotherapeutic agents or experimental agents for MDS within 14 days of the first day of study drug treatment. The patient is not using erythroid stimulating agents, Granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF), or Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) within 14 days of the first day of study drug treatment, or during the study. The patient does not have any cardiac abnormalities and has a mean triplicate heart rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) of less than or equal to 500 msec. The patient has no serious or uncontrolled medical disorder, and has not had prior malignancy within the previous 3 years except for local cancers that have been cured. The patient has not used other investigational drugs within 30 days of study drug administration, undergone major surgery within 4 weeks of study drug administration, or received a live-virus vaccination within 30 days of study drug administration. The patient is willing to use study-specified contraception if sexually active and is not breastfeeding. The patient is eligible for inclusion in the SX-682 Treatment in Subjects With Myelodysplastic Syndrome Who Had Disease Progression or Are Intolerant to Prior Therapy clinical trial.

This study is looking for newborn infants whose mothers were recruited for the SCOPE Ireland study at 15 weeks gestation. The study will monitor the growth and development of the infants from early pregnancy for the first two years of life. The study will investigate the effects of intrauterine growth restriction, the incidence and prevalence of food allergy and eczema in early childhood, and the incidence and effects of maternal and infant vitamin D status on the growth and health of Irish children. The study will also establish a biobank of maternal and fetal plasma, serum, and DNA. The eligibility criteria for this study include liveborn infants whose mothers were recruited to the SCOPE Ireland study at 15 weeks gestation, and singleton pregnancies with no previous history or risk of pre-eclampsia. Stillbirths or mothers who do not consent to pediatric follow-up will be excluded from the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been diagnosed with myopia and is interested in exploring surgical options for correction. She wears contact lenses for most of the day and has a prescription of -4.50 D sphere in both eyes. She has never had any previous eye surgeries or complications and has had a stable refraction for the past year. Her corneal topography is normal and she has a minimal corneal thickness of 500 microns. She does not have any other ocular or systemic health conditions and is not taking any medications that would affect wound healing. She is willing and able to comply with all scheduled follow-up appointments for 24 months after treatment. She has read and understands the informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical investigation for the Vedera KXS for the correction of her myopia.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who had a hysterectomy 5 years ago. She is experiencing bothersome bulge symptoms, feeling something falling out, and sensation of bulging. The patient desires surgical treatment for post-hysterectomy vaginal prolapse. She has not had any previous synthetic material or biologic grafts to augment pelvic organ prolapse repair. She has no known adverse reaction to synthetic mesh or biological grafts. She has no unresolved chronic pelvic pain, no abdominal or pelvic radiation, and no contraindication to any of the index surgical procedures. The patient is willing to be available for up to 60 months of follow-up.

A 40-year-old woman has been taking care of her husband who was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. She has two young children and a full-time job. She has been experiencing high levels of distress related to her caregiving role and has a score of 7 on the Distress Thermometer. She also reports high levels of worry and rumination. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have a history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or schizoaffective disorder. She is not a regular smoker or heavy drinker. She does not work night shifts and is not engaged in ongoing psychotherapy.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. The cancer has spread to his liver and lungs. He has not received any prior systemic treatment for his cancer. He has a target lesion in his liver that measures 4 cm in diameter. His liver function tests and complete blood count are within the normal range. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet the eligibility criteria.

A 25 year old male college student came to the clinic for the clinical trial. He is a non-smoker with a BMI of 23. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. His last checkup was six months ago, and all his laboratory results were normal. He has no history of diabetes, liver disease, kidney disease, or thyroid disease. He is interested in participating in the study to gain more knowledge about the release of gut hormones after oral versus intravenous amino acids.

A 35-year-old female presents to the emergency department with chest pain. The patient denies any history of coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, or percutaneous intervention. She reports occasional smoking, but no other significant medical history. Her initial troponin level is within the normal range for the hospital. The patient does not report any use of cocaine in the previous 14 days. The ECG performed by the attending emergency physician is unremarkable. The patient is able to consent for the study and her admitting attending physician agrees to randomization into either study arm. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been experiencing delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized speech for the past 6 months. He has not been taking any antipsychotic medication for the past 2 weeks. The patient has no history of mental retardation, epilepsy, or head trauma. He has no history of substance use disorder that explains the majority of his psychopathology. He is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy adults aged 18 or older who are medically and psychiatrically healthy and enrolled in another study (01-M-0254) evaluating participants with mood and anxiety disorders and healthy volunteers. Participants should not have any current Axis I diagnosis, clinically significant laboratory abnormalities, or have had recent exposure to radiation related to research that, when combined with this study, would be above the allowable limits. Participants should not have a history of neurologic illness or injury with the potential to affect study data interpretation, be unable to have an MRI scan or lie flat on camera bed for at least two hours. Pregnant or breastfeeding women and those with current substance use disorder based on DSM-5 or current use of psychiatric medications will not be eligible to participate. NIMH employees/staff and their immediate family members will be excluded from the study per NIMH policy. This study will involve brain PET imaging using 18F-PF-06445974 and an arterial line to assess quantitation of PDE4B. A total of 30 healthy volunteers will be enrolled.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, presents to the emergency department with chest pain that started 2 hours ago. The patient was at home watching TV when he started to feel a pressure-like sensation in his chest that radiated to his left arm. He also felt short of breath and nauseous. He took aspirin and called the ambulance. The 12-lead ECG showed ST-segment elevation in inferior leads, and he was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He was brought to the cardiac catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The patient was randomized to the STEMI-RADIAL trial and underwent radial approach PCI. He has no history of bleeding disorders or previous cardiac interventions. His vital signs are stable, and he is able to sign written informed consent.

74yo male with a confirmed diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease as per the DSM-IV criteria. He has been experiencing mild to moderate symptoms and has a FAST score of 4 or 5. The patient has not used Aricept within the last 3 months and has no history of hypersensitivity to any ingredients of Aricept or piperidine derivatives. The patient is seeking treatment for his Alzheimer's Disease and is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the clinical safety and effectiveness of donepezil hydrochloride administration.

54-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and aortic insufficiency presents for elective cardiac surgery. He has undergone two previous cardiac surgeries, including aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting. His current medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a 20 pack-year history of smoking. He is currently on aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. His preoperative laboratory studies are within normal limits. He has no known allergies and no history of seizures or thromboembolic events. He has not received antifibrinolytic or thrombolytic therapy in the past 5 days. He has no coagulation disorders or liver disease but has a mild renal insufficiency with a creatinine clearance of 48 mL/min. He is not a Jehovah witness.

A 7-year-old male child with congenital hypothyroidism diagnosed through neonatal screening program in Egypt, currently receiving L-thyroxine (L-T4) since diagnosis. The child was born full-term, with a birth weight of 3 kg. There was no history of perinatal asphyxia or birth trauma. The parents are healthy and non-consanguineous. The child is growing at a normal rate, but the parents are concerned about his final height. The child's thyroid function tests have been within the normal range since starting L-T4. The child is compliant with taking the medication and has regular follow-up appointments at the clinic. The family history is unremarkable for any endocrine disorders. The child's medical history is significant for occasional upper respiratory tract infections, which were treated with antibiotics. The child has no history of any bone-related disorders or fractures. The child's height is currently at the 50th percentile for age, and his weight is at the 25th percentile. The child's bone age is consistent with his chronological age.

A 35-year old woman was diagnosed with asthma at the age of 20. She has been under the care of her primary care physician for asthma and is currently taking a daily inhaled corticosteroid medication through a metered dose inhaler (MDI) at least twice a day. She speaks English fluently and is in good general health. She works as a graphic designer and enjoys hiking in her free time. She reports occasional asthma symptoms such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath but is able to manage them with her medication. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has no history of mental health disorders and is not currently taking any medications for such conditions. She is interested in participating in this study to help improve patient care for those with asthma.

A 25-year-old male who recently tested positive for HIV after having unprotected sex with multiple partners. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He reports experiencing mild flu-like symptoms, including fever, headache, and muscle aches, for the past week. He does not have any significant medical history or past surgeries. He is currently employed as a waiter and does not have any known drug allergies. The patient is worried about the long-term implications of HIV infection and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive aggressive anti-HIV therapy as soon as possible to prevent disease progression. He is willing to comply with study requirements and attend all scheduled follow-up visits. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 35 year-old male who has been smoking 1 pack of commercially-manufactured cigarettes daily for the past 5 years. He is in good health and has no history of significant medical conditions. He routinely smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of awakening in the morning. He is willing to refrain from smoking during the confinement period of the study and agrees not to use any other tobacco products during the study. He is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow study restrictions.

The patient is a 58-year-old female diagnosed with congestive heart failure (CHF) three years ago. She has been on optimal conventional heart failure therapy, including a beta-blocker and an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB), for the past 6 months. Her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 33% as measured by radionuclide angiography. She has symptoms of New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III CHF, experiences shortness of breath with exertion, and fatigue. She has poor venous access due to repeated hospitalizations and multiple IV administrations. She has no history of thyroid disease, valvular disease, obstructive/hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pericardial disease, amyloidosis, or primary pulmonary hypertension. She has not undergone cardiac surgery or bi-ventricular resynchronization procedure or listed for transplantation. She has never had a myocardial infarction. She is not taking any study prohibited medication, and her serum potassium level is within normal limits. She is not pregnant, lactating or planning to become pregnant during the study. She is willing to change from an ACEI to an ARB. She has not participated in any clinical drug or device trial in the last 90 days. She is able to complete the 6-minute walk test and the Kansas City Congestive Heart Failure Quality of Life Questionnaire (KCCQ). She is interested in participating in the study and giving written informed consent.

A 56-year-old woman, diagnosed with COPD, came to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath during physical activity, chronic cough, and wheezing. She had a history of smoking for 20 years, quit smoking 5 years ago. She was prescribed bronchodilators and corticosteroids but did not experience significant improvement. She was referred to a respiratory rehabilitation program where she completed the program successfully. She has consented to participate in the clinical trial investigating the effects of respiratory rehabilitation by gender in COPD patients.

A 35-year-old woman, diagnosed with opioid dependence, has been prescribed buprenorphine/naloxone (bup/nal) medication. She has been on the medication for the past 6 months and has been experiencing difficulty in managing it in the prescribed manner. She has missed doses in the past and is concerned about negative health outcomes due to poor adherence. She owns an Android smartphone and is able to speak and read English. She is willing to provide written informed consent prior to study entry and is able to understand the study. The patient is concerned about her addiction and wants to take a more active role in managing her medication to prevent relapse.

32-year-old male with a history of opioid dependence and seeking treatment for the same. He has previously undergone opioid therapy for chronic pain, but is not currently on any medication for it. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2 and normal ECG findings at screening. He has not donated blood or plasma in the last 30 days and has not participated in any other clinical trials recently. He has not taken buprenorphine in the last 30 days and has no history of allergic or adverse reactions to buprenorphine or the ATRIGEL Delivery System. He is willing to cooperate with study procedures and provide written informed consent prior to start of any study procedures. He meets Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR) criteria for opioid dependence and is seeking opioid-dependence treatment with methadone. He does not have any significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, oncologic, or psychiatric diseases or any other conditions that, in the opinion of the study physician, would jeopardize the safety of the subject.

65-year-old male with bilateral age-related cataracts and no previous ocular surgery or complications presents for evaluation of second eye refinement cataract surgery. He reports progressive blurred vision, difficulty reading and driving at night, and a decrease in visual acuity over time. His ocular history is significant for mild dry eye syndrome and he wears glasses for presbyopia. His medical history is notable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis, all well-controlled with medications. He denies smoking, alcohol, or drug use. On examination, his visual acuity is 20/50 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Slit-lamp examination reveals bilateral age-related cataracts, with no significant corneal or retinal abnormalities. Intraocular pressure is within normal limits. Pentacam HR examination reveals adequate cooperation and no significant corneal astigmatism. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating to potentially improve his refractive outcomes.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who are 18 years or older and have been diagnosed with stage IV or recurrent non-squamous non-small cell lung carcinoma with activating EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R point mutation) and concurrent TP53 mutations. Patients who have not received previous palliative chemotherapy or biological or immunological therapy for the condition may be eligible. Patients must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance-status score of 0 or 1, a life expectancy of at least 3 months, and adequate organ function. Patients with known severe hypersensitivity to Osimertinib, carboplatin, or pemetrexed, or with a history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial disease, radiation pneumonitis, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease, are not eligible. Patients must not have any unresolved chronic toxicity from previous anticancer therapy, nor any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic disease. Pregnant or breastfeeding women are not eligible.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She had a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, and now she is going to receive adjuvant weekly paclitaxel for 12 cycles. She has no history of diabetes mellitus, and her blood tests showed adequate bone marrow, liver and renal function. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has not received vitamin B1, B6, B12, adjuvant analgesic agents, or any other medications for neuropathic pain. She has no known hypersensitivity to N-acetyl cysteine. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effect of N-acetyl cysteine in combination with paclitaxel on the clinical outcomes of patients with peripheral neuropathy.

A 65-year-old man with a diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's disease (AD) is seeking to participate in the TOAD clinical trial. He has a CDR score of 1 and a MMSE score of 17 at his last visit to the University of Kansas Alzheimer's Disease Center (KU ADC). He has a study partner, his wife, who is willing to accompany him to all study visits and monitor his compliance with study medication administration. He has been on a stable dose of his current medication for the past 4 weeks. He has no history of diabetes or cancer, and no recent cardiac events. He is fluent in English and has no metal implants or pacemaker. He is willing to use contraception throughout the trial if needed.

A 30 yo F with a history of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD) with sleep disturbance, despite inadequate response to topical medications, is being sought for a clinical trial. The participant should have applied skin emollients (moisturizers) and medium potency topical corticosteroids (TCS) on all active AD lesions at least 7 days before screening. The individual should be willing and able to comply with all clinic visits and study-related procedures and provide signed informed consent. Participants with known hypersensitivity to Dupixent, clinical depression, drug abuse history, sleep problems not related to AD, irregular sleep pattern, active/acute infections, severe medical conditions, laboratory abnormalities, any condition that may present unreasonable risk to patients or interfere with study assessment, or any severe concomitant illness(es) that would adversely affect the patient's participation in the study, and contraindications of topical corticosteroids will be excluded from the study. At baseline, presence of any conditions listed as criteria for study drug discontinuation will also be excluded. The trial will evaluate the effect of dupilumab on sleep quality in adult patients with moderate to severe AD and the effect of dupilumab on objective and subjective quantitative sleep parameters, AD related outcomes, and daytime consequences of sleep deprivation. The safety and tolerability throughout the study will also be assessed. Duration per participant is up to 28 weeks.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of a spinal cord injury (SCI) resulting in motor complete SCI (AIS A-B). He has no history of pressure ulcers, chronic infections, lower extremity muscle contractures, deep vein thrombosis, bleeding disorder, recent limb fractures, or any comorbid disease known to affect bone metabolism. He is not taking any anti-osteoporosis medications or vitamin D supplements, nor is he on metformin or any other medication for diabetes. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of high and low frequency active-resisted stance on skeletal muscle gene regulation, systemic markers of metabolic health and bone turnover, and quality of life in patients with SCI.

The patient is a 43-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to her lungs and liver. She has previously undergone anthracycline and taxane therapies, but her cancer has progressed despite these treatments. The patient has HER2-negative and hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has at least one target lesion as defined by RECIST 1.1 that allows for evaluation of tumor response. Her absolute neutrophil count is 2000/mm3, platelet count is 120 x 109/L, and hemoglobin is 10 g/dL. Her serum creatinine is 1.2 times the upper limit of the normal range, total bilirubin is 1.5 mg/dL, and AST/ALT is within the normal range. The patient has no remaining grade 2 or higher toxicity from prior cancer therapies. She has not received chemotherapy for at least three weeks. The patient is willing to use an acceptable contraceptive method for the duration of the study and for 30 days following the last dose of study drug, and has a negative urine pregnancy test within 2 weeks prior to beginning treatment on this trial. The patient has no history of inadequate renal function, ventricular fibrillation, sinus node or AV nodal disease, Wolff Parkinson White Syndrome, hemodynamically significant or life-threatening cardiac arrhythmia. She has no uncontrolled cardiac disease, congestive heart failure, angina, or hypertension. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 2 months of treatment. She has no known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, chronic active Hepatitis B or C, or active clinically serious infection > CTCAE (version 4.03) Grade 2. The patient has not had a thrombotic or embolic event such as a cerebrovascular accident including transient ischemic attacks within the past 6 months. She has not experienced a pulmonary hemorrhage/bleeding event ≥ CTCAE Grade 2 within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug or any other hemorrhage/bleeding event ≥ CTCAE Grade 3 within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug. The patient has no serious non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture. She has not undergone major surgery or significant traumatic injury within 2 weeks of the first study drug. The patient is willing to complete the informed consent process and adhere to the protocol treatment plan and follow-up requirements. She does not have concurrent severe illness such as active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit safety and compliance with study requirements. The patient is not currently on anticoagulation therapy with Coumadin, and does not have symptomatic untreated brain metastasis or leptomeningeal metastases or treated but still symptomatic requiring the use of steroid within the past two weeks. The patient is not receiving any other investigational agents and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is scheduled to undergo elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery at Barnes-Jewish Hospital. He has no history of diabetes, smoking, or alcohol use. He reports occasional chest pain with exertion and shortness of breath. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. His physical examination is significant for a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, a regular heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and a body mass index of 28. Laboratory testing shows a normal complete blood count, normal electrolytes and renal function. His preoperative electrocardiogram shows evidence of prior anterior myocardial infarction.

A 16 year old female is being treated for schizophrenia with risperidone for the past six months. She has gained 10% of her pre-drug body weight and is currently residing in an in-patient psychiatric facility. She is experiencing excessive weight gain which is causing her to become self-conscious and depressed. She is willing to participate in an 8-week open label trial to test the hypothesis that daily vitamin D supplementation will reduce her weight gain and associated metabolic complications. She has no history of diabetes, liver or kidney disease, and no known disorders of vitamin D metabolism. She is not on any weight loss medications, nor on any medication that might affect glucose levels. She is able to take the prescribed vitamin D by mouth. Her 25-hydroxyvitamin D level is < 32 ng/mL. She is eager to participate in the study as she hopes it will alleviate her depression and improve her overall health.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV three years ago. She has been receiving antiretroviral therapy and has been doing well with her treatment. However, she has been experiencing anxiety and depression due to her diagnosis and has been turning to alcohol to cope. She reports drinking four or more drinks on some days in the past 30 days. She is referred to a study MI counselor by clinic staff as needing an intervention for her drinking. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She speaks fluent English and does not have any hearing impairments. She does not have any plans to leave the greater New York metropolitan area during the study period. Her cognitive function is normal and she is able to complete the Halstead-Reitan Trails (A) without any difficulties.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He has no history of exposure to radiation for professional or medical reasons in the past year. He has not participated in any investigational study involving radioactivity. He has a consistent bowel movement habit of approximately once per day within the past 30 days. His blood pressure is between 90 and 140 mmHg systolic, inclusive, and no higher than 90 mmHg diastolic. He has normal cardiac conduction and function. He has no history of cardiac arrhythmias or other cardiac disease, hematologic disease, coagulation disorders, lipid abnormalities, significant pulmonary disease, including bronchospastic respiratory disease, diabetes mellitus, renal or hepatic insufficiency, thyroid disease, neurologic or psychiatric disease, or infection. His hematology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis values are within normal limits. He has no significant abnormal physical examination, vital signs, or 12-lead electrocardiogram at screening or at admission to the study center. He has no clinically significant ocular deficits, including retinal disorders. He is willing to participate in the study and adhere to the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol.

A 46 yo male who has been diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma on his forehead. The lesion was removed surgically and he is now in remission. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent the recurrence of his skin cancer. He is in good health with no significant medical history, and he is not currently taking any medications. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma originating from the esophagus. She received a platinum-containing regimen for two months but had disease progression. The patient underwent genetic testing and was found to have a somatic mutation in the HR pathway gene BARD1. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and has completed her prior cancer treatment 3 weeks prior to registration. She has adequate organ function and has no known history of myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia. The patient has measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 and has not received prior therapy with a PARP inhibitor. The patient understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with them for the entire length of the study. She is willing to abstain from heterosexual activity or use adequate contraception from the time of informed consent until 30 days after treatment discontinuation. She agrees to not donate blood during the study or for 90 days after the last dose of study treatment.

The patient is a 25-year-old male living with HIV for the past 2 years. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 8 months. The patient reports experiencing fatigue and decreased energy levels, which has been affecting his daily activities. The patient has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and is physically active, engaging in moderate exercise for at least 30 minutes, 3 times per week. He has no known history of other chronic diseases or endocrine disorders. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. The patient has no known drug allergy. The laboratory values of the patient show the following results: CD4+ cell count: 560 cells/mm3, Viral Load: Undetectable, Fasting glucose: 92 mg/dL, Total cholesterol: 180 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol: 55 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol: 105 mg/dL, Triglycerides: 120 mg/dL. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his energy levels and overall health status.

The patient is a 45 year old African-American male who resides in the metropolitan Washington DC area. He is married with two children and works as a bus driver. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease (CVD) with his father experiencing a heart attack at the age of 50. The patient is overweight with a BMI of 32 and has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years. He reports occasional chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity. He has tried to improve his diet and increase physical activity but has been unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of stroke, heart attack or heart failure. He is interested in participating in the GENE-FORECAST study to better understand his risk for CVD and to potentially help future generations of African-Americans.

4-year-old male diagnosed with cerebral palsy at 18 months of age. He was born 10 weeks premature and spent 6 weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit due to respiratory distress syndrome. He has spastic quadriplegia with hypertonicity in all limbs, predominantly in the lower extremities. He is unable to walk without assistance and has limited fine motor skills. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and is currently taking prophylactic antibiotics. He has a gastrostomy tube for feeding due to difficulty swallowing and has a history of aspiration pneumonia. He has received multiple injections of rhEPO as part of his treatment plan. He is regularly followed by a pediatric neurologist and receives physical, occupational, and speech therapies.

A 55-year-old retired military service member presents with a history of cataracts in both eyes. He has been experiencing blurred vision, glare, and difficulty reading. He has a history of hypertension, but it is currently well-controlled with medication. The ophthalmologist diagnoses him with cataracts and astigmatism in both eyes with corneal astigmatism of 2.5 D in the right eye and 1.8 D in the left eye. The patient is interested in correcting his astigmatism and improving his overall vision. He is advised that he may be a candidate for a toric intraocular lens (TECNIS IOL) combined with a capsular tension ring device to improve the stability of the lens. The patient is eligible to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of the capsular tension ring device on rotational stability of the implanted toric intraocular lens following cataract surgery. The patient is an active-duty military beneficiary, aged 55 years or older, with corneal astigmatism of at least 1.0 D, and is undergoing cataract surgery. He has no observed zonular or capsular problems prior to, or at the time of, capsular tension ring insertion. The patient is randomized into the treatment group, which involves a toric intraocular lens plus capsular tension ring device.

A 26-year-old woman came to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is sexually active and uses condoms as a method of contraception. She has no history of TBEV vaccination or infection. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand the procedures involved in the trial. She has no plans to travel to areas that require immunisation against Japanese B encephalitis or yellow fever during the study period. She is willing to abstain from vaginal intercourse for 12 hours prior to cervico-vaginal secretions sampling. She understands that she will receive TicoVac vaccine either in her right deltoid muscle or right anterolateral thigh. She will need to attend follow-up visits and provide blood samples and cervicovaginal secretions for immunological measures. She is willing to abstain from donating blood during and for three months after the end of her participation in the trial.

The normal volunteer is a 32-year-old non-smoking female who works as a teacher. She has a history of seasonal allergies and mild asthma, but she has not required any medication for the past year. She has no other significant medical history and takes no medications regularly. She has normal lung function, with FEV1 of 85% of predicted and FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.80. She has negative allergy skin test and methacholine inhalation challenge. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with a history of developmental problems and severe epilepsy. She was diagnosed with glucose transporter 1 deficiency syndrome (GLUT1DS) at the age of 4 years. She has been on the ketogenic diet for the past 6 years with good compliance, but unfortunately, it has not had a positive effect on her epilepsy. She experiences frequent clinical seizures and epileptic discharges on EEG. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no known allergies or medication use. She lives with her parents and is attending school. Her parents are aware of the study and have given their informed consent. Her serum sodium level is within normal range. She has no known panic disorders or history of panic attacks.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has had recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) for the past year. He has had 5 episodes of CDI with each episode defined as 3 or more unformed stools in 24 hours associated with positive Clostridium difficile test, each occurring within 3 months of each other. His symptoms are under control with 2 unformed stools in 24 hours for the past 10 days. He is generally healthy and does not have any other medical conditions. He is not taking any regular medications. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or irritable bowel syndrome. He is willing to provide informed consent and agrees to use effective contraception for the duration of the study. He has no chronic diarrhea, ileus or small bowel obstruction. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant within 3 months. He has not had chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 6 months. He has no active infection requiring antibiotics. He is willing to take capsules for the study.

50 year-old male with a history of rheumatic heart disease and mitral valve prolapse presents to the hospital with complaints of fever, chills, and fatigue for the past week. Physical examination reveals a new systolic murmur, and blood cultures are positive for Streptococcus viridans. Transthoracic echocardiography shows a vegetation attached to the mitral valve. The patient is diagnosed with infectious endocarditis and meets the inclusion criteria for the EPEI study. Past Medical History: 1. Rheumatic heart disease 2. Mitral valve prolapse 3. Hypertension 4. Hyperlipidemia

The patient is a 26 year old male who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 6 months ago during a routine screening. He is asymptomatic and has not been on any anti-retroviral therapy. His viral load is between 3,000 and 100,000 HIV-1 RNA copies/mL and his CD4+ T-cell count is above 400/mm3. He is currently working as a software engineer and is in a stable relationship with his partner, who is also HIV-1 positive. He has a history of smoking but has quit for the past 2 months. He occasionally drinks alcohol on weekends with friends but does not engage in any other substance abuse. He has no history of hepatitis B or C infection, and has not participated in any investigational drug/vaccine study in the past 30 days. He is interested in participating in the TUTI-16 clinical trial to help advance the development of potential therapeutic vaccine for HIV-1.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl with a diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 3 years. She has been followed by a care provider at the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto, Canada since her diagnosis. The patient is fluent in English and has no developmental disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the mindfulness program. She is willing to consent to the study and is able to attend in-person mindfulness meditation sessions at Sickkids. The patient has been experiencing some difficulty managing her diabetes, and her recent HbA1c levels have been higher than the recommended range. She is interested in participating in the study to learn new strategies for managing stress related to her condition. Her parents are supportive of her participation and will ensure that she attends all the required sessions.

35 F with a history of Hypophosphatasia (HPP) confirmed through genetic testing. She reports persistent musculoskeletal pain and a history of multiple fractures. Her alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels have been consistently low, measuring at 30 U/L over multiple tests. She has not been treated with any medications that affect bone metabolism, including oral corticosteroids, anti-osteoporosis drugs, or sex steroids. She does not have any skin infections or allergies to Lidocain. She has submitted informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. His vital signs show a temperature of 38.2°C, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. His physical exam reveals tenderness in the chest wall and decreased breath sounds in the left lower lung field. A CT scan of the chest confirms the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism in the left lower lobe. The patient has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He is not currently taking any antibiotics and has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and signs the consent form.

The patient is a 45 year old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is in need of a renal allograft. He has been on dialysis for the past year and is awaiting a transplant. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of malignancy or active infections. He is willing to comply with the use of contraception if applicable. His white blood cell count and platelet count are within normal limits. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 30 year old woman who works as an office assistant has been experiencing stress and anxiety lately. She has been feeling overwhelmed with her workload and has trouble sleeping at night. She has tried various relaxation techniques, but nothing seems to work. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effectiveness of laying-on-of-hands therapy in reducing stress and anxiety. She is willing to receive the therapy for 30 minutes or more from the investigators and is able to self-evaluate the change of her symptoms. She is also competent to answer the Japanese questionnaires and meets the age requirement of 16 years or older. She does not have any other medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing anxiety and panic attacks for the past year. She is a teacher and has been finding it difficult to manage her work and anxiety symptoms. She has not used recreational cannabis in the past 4 weeks and does not have a history of daily cannabis use or cannabis use disorder. She has never been diagnosed with any other psychiatric disorders, and her physical exam and laboratory findings are normal. She is currently taking an antidepressant that has been stable for the past 8 weeks. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future and is using medically accepted forms of contraception. She has no history of adverse reactions to cannabis. She is willing to abstain from recreational cannabis use for the duration of the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for her anxiety and panic symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes. He was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) following a motor vehicle accident and required intubation and mechanical ventilation due to multiple rib fractures and pulmonary contusions. He has been ventilated for the past 3 days and is now stable enough to undergo a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) to assess his readiness for extubation. However, he failed his first T-piece trial and is at high risk for extubation failure. He has no history of neuromuscular disease or other exclusion criteria. The patient is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22kg/m2. He has no history of any chronic medical conditions or allergies to medications. He has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medications in the past 2 weeks and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 8 weeks. He has been informed of the investigational nature of the study and voluntarily agrees to participate. He is of Korean ethnicity and understands English fluently. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow the instructions provided by the study staff.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been suffering from chronic trunk and limb pain for the past 5 years, which has significantly impacted his quality of life. His pain is not adequately managed with medication and he has been advised to consider spinal cord stimulation (SCS) therapy by his pain specialist. He has undergone a trial of SCS and has found significant pain relief, leading to the permanent implantation of a Medtronic Intellis™ neurostimulation system. He is now being considered for conversion to Differential Target Multiplexed (DTM®) programming, which has shown superior efficacy to conventional programming parameters in a randomized controlled trial. The patient has an iPhone and has access to regular internet access, which will enable him to complete the web-based participant self-reported questionnaires via SMS text or email. The patient is eager to participate in the UPGRADE registry study to collect long-term, real-world outcomes data on the effect of DTM® programming on the management of his chronic pain. The patient does not have any medical, social, or psychological conditions that would limit his ability to participate in the clinical investigation or to comply with follow-up requirements.

A 30-year-old woman who experiences an overwhelming fear of being judged, embarrassed or humiliated in social situations. She often avoids social gatherings and has difficulty making friends. She has been diagnosed with Generalized Social Anxiety Disorder and her Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS) score is above 50. She is currently taking medication but has not found it to be completely effective. She is fluent in Hebrew language and has no history of primary Axis I or Axis II disorder other than SAD. She does not have any suicidal ideation or substance dependence within the past three months or current substance abuse. She also does not have any mental retardation or another pervasive developmental disability. She has never been diagnosed with current or past schizophrenia or psychosis, current bipolar disorder or organic brain syndrome.

A 55 year old woman was recently diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma after experiencing symptoms of abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits. She underwent abdominopelvic CT and liver MRI for initial staging before any treatment. The CT showed no evidence of distant metastasis, but multiple liver lesions were identified. She has no past or concurrent malignancy other than colorectal adenocarcinoma. She has not had a precontrast abdominopelvic CT or precontrast liver MRI, and the interval between the CT and liver MRI was less than 4 weeks. The patient has not had any liver MRI using contrast other than extracellular agent or gadoxetic acid. The patient has no suspected multiple hepatic metastases (> 10) on CT and no distant metastasis other than liver.
