The patient has provided consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo both Gd-EOB-MRI and ECA-MRI for evaluation of her focal hepatic lesions.

26-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 who is not a smoker, does not use any medications except for oral contraceptives, and does not consume any pre- or probiotic supplements or foods. She has no chronic illnesses such as hyperlipidemia, diabetes, or inflammatory diseases, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is moderately active, engaging in exercise for about 4-5 hours per week.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The diagnosis was confirmed through a biopsy of a liver lesion. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy for pancreatic cancer within the last 5 years and has not undergone radiotherapy for pancreatic cancer. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has at least one measurable lesion. The patient has no history of brain metastasis and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no known hypersensitivity or allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to gemcitabine, nab-paclitaxel, capecitabine, cisplatin, or irinotecan. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and has no clinically significant wound or serious medical risk factors involving any of the major organ systems. The patient is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial.

A 65-year-old male patient presents with severe osteoarthritis in his right knee joint. He has been experiencing significant pain and stiffness in his knee joint for the past year, which has significantly affected his ability to perform daily activities. He has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and medications, but they were not effective in providing long-term relief. After consultation with his orthopedic surgeon, he has opted for a primary total knee arthroplasty surgery. He meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of local infiltration of liposomal bupivacaine versus use of an indwelling femoral peripheral nerve block in controlling early postoperative pain in primary total knee arthroplasty. He has no history of allergy or adverse reaction to local anesthetics and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, abdominal distension, and mild discomfort in the right upper quadrant. He has a history of a positive HCV antibody test and has been confirmed to be HCV RNA positive. His liver function tests (ALT and AST) are elevated, and he is experiencing occasional episodes of nausea. The patient has no history of clotting disorders, is not currently taking any anti-coagulant or anti-aggregant medications, and has not undergone any surgery for brain aneurysm. He does not have a history of hepatocellular carcinoma or any other cancer. The patient does not have a pacemaker or defibrillator, and he has no ocular metal foreign body. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the noninvasive evaluation of hepatic fibrosis in chronic hepatitis C.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who has been receiving hemodialysis treatment for the past year. He has been experiencing frequent hospitalizations due to complications related to his condition. He has expressed concerns about his end-of-life care and wants to discuss his options with his family. He speaks fluent English and has a designated surrogate, his wife, who is willing to participate in the study. He is not enrolled in hospice and is not too ill or cognitively impaired to participate, according to his clinicians.

A 45-year-old woman was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock caused by an abdominal infection. She was transferred from the emergency room where she had presented with abdominal pain, fever and chills. She was hypotensive (mean arterial pressure of 62 mmHg) and tachycardic (heart rate of 120/min), and was started on intravenous fluids and vasopressors immediately. Blood cultures were drawn and she was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. A CT scan showed a perforated appendix with abscess formation, which was subsequently drained by interventional radiology. She required intubation due to respiratory failure and was started on mechanical ventilation. Her laboratory results showed leukocytosis (white blood cell count of 18,000/mm3) and elevated lactate levels (4 mmol/L). She has been in the ICU for 12 hours and has received 2 liters of crystalloid and norepinephrine to maintain her blood pressure. She is currently hemodynamically stable with a mean arterial pressure of 75 mmHg and a heart rate of 95/min. She is alert and oriented and able to provide informed consent. She has no history of bowel surgery or contraindications for enteral nutrition. Her BMI is 26.5 and her baseline laboratory results are as follows: Hgb: 12 g/dL, WBC: 7,000/mm3 (Neutrophil: 4,000/mm3), Plt: 200,000 /ml, Cr: 1.0 mg/dL, BUN: 25 mg/dL.

The patient is a 43-year-old female scheduled for a breast surgery under general anesthesia. She has no significant medical history and takes no regular medications. She has no recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms and is not currently using post-operative patient-controlled analgesia. She has not had any surgeries in the head and neck area, and she has not been using a nasogastric or orogastric tube before the surgery. She is not known to have any allergies to medications or anesthesia. The patient is classified as ASA I and is aged between 20 and 70 years old. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past month. His chest pain is typically brought on by physical activity and relieved with rest. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are managed with medications. He has never had a heart attack or any other significant cardiovascular event. He is a non-smoker and does not use recreational drugs. He is able to perform all of his activities of daily living without difficulty. He was recently diagnosed with stable angina pectoris and is scheduled to undergo a coronary catheterization procedure to assess the extent of his coronary artery disease. He has agreed to participate in the AtheroRemo-IVUS study, which will involve a blood sample for biomarker measurements and genetic analyses prior to the procedure. After the procedure, he will undergo intravascular ultrasound in a non-culprit coronary artery to evaluate the presence of vulnerable plaque. He understands that he will be followed up for long-term incidence of major adverse cardiac events. The patient is willing and able to comply with the specified follow-up evaluation and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 16-year-old female with a history of major depression, who has been previously treated with a combination of psychotherapy and sertraline, presents with symptoms of sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping. She has not experienced any manic or hypomanic episodes and denies any history of substance abuse. She has no significant medical history, is not pregnant, and has never been treated with sertraline for depression. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the potential benefits of continuing treatment with sertraline to prevent a recurrence of her depression.

Patient is a 45yo woman who has been diagnosed with invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast by core needle biopsy. The tumor size is approximately 3 cm, and there is evidence of involvement of at least one lymph node. The patient's hormone receptor status is known, and she has been confirmed to have HER2-positive disease by fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH). The patient has no definitive clinical or radiologic evidence of metastatic disease, and there is no history of invasive breast cancer. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 0-1 and meets the other eligibility criteria for the trial, including normal blood counts and liver and kidney function. The patient has no history of cardiac disease that would preclude treatment with epirubicin hydrochloride or trastuzumab (Herceptin), and has no sensory or motor neuropathy greater than grade 2. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and has agreed to use an effective non-hormonal method of contraception during therapy. The patient has not had prior therapy for this breast cancer, and has not received anthracyclines or taxanes for any malignancy. The patient is eligible for the trial, and will be randomized to one of two treatment arms.

The patient is a healthy adult with a valid driver's license who is fluent in English and literate. They have not been using daily medication for any chronic conditions, and they do not have acute narrow angle glaucoma. They have never had an adverse experience with the study drugs, and they do not experience motion sickness in response to driving simulators. Their BMI is within the normal range, and they are not pregnant, lactating, or planning on becoming pregnant. They do not use tobacco products or have a current substance use disorder. They have no clinically significant ECG abnormalities and are not currently experiencing any ongoing psychiatric disorders.

This clinical trial is a retrospective review of charts and echocardiograms of patients with Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection (TAPVC) between January 1, 2002 and November 26, 2006. The patient in question is a child who was diagnosed with TAPVC during this time frame and has medical records at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and Sibley Heart Center Cardiology. The child's medical history will be reviewed to determine if they meet the inclusion criteria for the study, which includes a total of approximately 40 patients with TAPVC. The study will evaluate the presence of descending aortic flow reversal and other associated cardiac anomalies as potential predictors of poor prognosis in TAPVC. The patient's clinical charts will also be reviewed to evaluate for serious co-morbidities and mortality, with outcome measures including mortality, chronic lung disease, continued oxygen requirement, recurrent respiratory infections, listing for transplantation, cardiopulmonary arrest or requirement for ECMO.

A 38-year-old woman presents with primary amenorrhea for the past 6 months. She has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles and no significant past medical history. She has never been pregnant before. She is interested in participating in the Inovium Ovarian Rejuvenation Trial to explore alternative fertility treatments. She has both ovaries and is willing to undergo IVF as part of the experimental protocol. She is not currently taking any anticoagulant medication, has no history of substance abuse, and has no known mental health disorders. She is willing and able to comply with all study requirements and will report any pregnancy to the research staff immediately. She has reviewed and signed the informed consent form.

This is a 45 year-old female who was diagnosed with breast cancer that has already spread to other parts of her body, known as metastatic breast cancer. The patient is currently undergoing anthracycline-based chemotherapy which has been successful in stabilizing the disease. The patient is expected to have a survival of at least one year. The patient has less than two visceral organ involvement and does not have multiple liver metastases with deranged liver function tests. The patient does not have any ulceration, fungation or bleeding that would require surgery. The patient is expected to be eligible for loco-regional treatment and would be a good candidate for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old Japanese man who has been recently diagnosed with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medications regularly. He has no history of stroke or other cardiovascular events. His current symptoms include occasional palpitations and fatigue. He is retired and spends his free time gardening and taking walks around his neighborhood. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His blood pressure is well-controlled, with a reading of 130/80 mmHg. His creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min, and his liver function is normal. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to receive treatment with rivaroxaban. He is not allergic to any of the ingredients in the medication and has not experienced any significant hemorrhagic events. He is not taking any HIV protease inhibitors or oral or injectable formulations of azole antifungal drugs.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian woman who has a history of myocardial infarction (heart attack) in the past three years. She has had a previous heart bypass surgery and angioplasty with a stent. The patient has blockages in at least one of her arteries in her heart, resulting in 50% or more blockage. She has mild to severe gum problems, and at least six natural teeth present in her mouth. The patient has no major illnesses requiring hospitalization, and her serum creatinine level is within the normal range. She has not undergone any organ transplant and is not currently undergoing any chemotherapy. The patient does not require any surgery in the next three years and has no history of head and/or neck radiation or liver dysfunction. She has no class IV congestive heart failure and does not have a pacemaker or AICD/defibrillator. The patient is willing to participate in the study to determine if treating her periodontal infection will lead to fewer heart problems.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been struggling with binge eating disorder for the past year. He reports having 5-6 episodes of binge eating per week, where he feels a loss of control and eats large quantities of food in a short period of time. This has led to significant weight gain, and his body mass index (BMI) is currently 30 kg/m2. He has tried cognitive behavioral therapy in the past but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He is literate and right-handed. There is no history of pregnancy or bariatric surgery. He has not undergone any treatment for weight loss in the last 30 days. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and receiving nutritional counseling associated with transcranial direct-current stimulation to reduce his binge eating episodes.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He was initially treated with sorafenib-based therapy, but unfortunately, his disease has progressed despite treatment. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and Child-Pugh class A liver function. He has no history of brain or leptomeningeal metastases or upper gastrointestinal bleeding within the last year. He has at least one measurable tumor according to RECIST version 1.1, that has not been treated with any local procedure. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive lenalidomide as second-line treatment for his HCC.

A 16-year-old Hispanic woman who is currently pregnant with her first child is interested in participating in a study to improve her knowledge and skills in breastfeeding. She is in her second trimester of pregnancy and plans to keep her newborn after delivery. She has a high school diploma and speaks fluent English. She has access to a telephone and is willing to receive telephone calls and visits from peer counselors and lactation consultants. She has no history of any medical conditions that may affect her ability to breastfeed. She is not pregnant with twins and has no history of premature birth. The pregnancy has been uneventful so far, and she has not experienced any complications during labor and birth. She is excited about participating in the study and hopes it will help her provide the best care for her newborn.

This is a 58-year-old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes approximately 7 years ago. She has been on metformin for the last 5 years and has been struggling to keep her blood sugar levels in the target range. Her most recent HbA1c level was 8.6%. During a routine check-up, it was discovered that she has albuminuria and her UACR is > 100 mg/g. She has been on a maximal tolerated dose of an angiotensin II receptor blocker for the last 4 weeks. She does not have any history of cancer or cardiac disease. Her eGFR is ≥ 30 ml/min/1.73 m² and her body mass index is 26 kg/m². She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the renal effects of treatment with empagliflozin alone or in combination with semaglutide. She is able to communicate with the investigator and understands informed consent.

A 25-year-old female patient presents to the orthodontic clinic at the University of Malaya with a chief complaint of crowding in her upper teeth. She has never received any orthodontic treatment before. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medications. Intraoral examination reveals mild crowding in the upper arch, with a need for extraction of the maxillary first premolars. Her oral hygiene is good, and there are no signs of periodontal disease. She is interested in receiving orthodontic treatment and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the conventional method of Transpalatal Arch (TPA) fabrication to a new method using 3D reconstructed models. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and signs a written consent form. The orthodontic postgraduates involved in the study will provide treatment for her, and she will be randomly assigned to either the conventional TPA group or the 3D TPA group. She will be given questionnaires to assess her oral health-related quality of life before receiving the TPA and at 1- and 3-month intervals after TPA insertion. Pain levels will also be assessed, and her progress will be recorded. She will also participate in a focus group discussion with other patients and clinicians to evaluate their preferences between the two methods of TPA fabrication.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II follicular lymphoma. She presents with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in her neck and groin. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes revealed follicular lymphoma. The patient has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. The patient has not received any treatment for her lymphoma yet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study the prognosis of follicular lymphoma through a prospective collection of data. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is over 18 years of age.

A 65-year-old Caucasian male presents with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in his left eye. He complains of blurred vision and difficulty reading. His ocular media is clear, and his pupil dilates well. His best-corrected visual acuity in the left eye is 70 letters (20/40 Snellen equivalent). The lesion area in his left eye is less than 30 mm2, and he does not have any other ophthalmic conditions that affect central vision. His right eye has a BCVA of 80 letters (20/25 Snellen equivalent). He has no history of intraocular surgery, laser photocoagulation, or any other treatment for AMD in the past 6 months. He does not have any vitreous hemorrhage or retinal detachment in either eye. He has no history of retinal pigment epithelial tear, rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, or macular hole in his left eye. He has no history of systemic immunological diseases or uncontrolled medical conditions. He is willing to provide written informed consent and participate in the study.

62-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal failure on hemodialysis for the past year. The patient has a left arteriovenous fistula (AVF) for hemodialysis access. The patient reports persistent swelling and discomfort in the left arm with the fistula. The patient also reports decreased sensation in the left hand and fingers. The patient's primary care physician has noted decreased pulse and fremitus in the anastomotic astium during routine physical examinations. The patient's blood flow rate at the access site has decreased to less than 200 mL/min. The patient has not undergone endovascular recanalization with stent or graft placement. The patient does not have any contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) examination. The patient's platelet count is above 60*10^9/L and international normalized ratio (INR) is below 1.5. The patient does not have any significant organ function failure or other serious illnesses. The patient reports no known allergies to antiplatelet drugs, anticoagulant drugs, anesthetic drugs, or contrast material.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer three years ago. She underwent cytoreductive surgery followed by chemotherapy with paclitaxel in combination with carboplatin. The treatment was initially successful, but the cancer has relapsed twice since then. The patient has completed two rounds of chemotherapy and is now experiencing persistent abdominal pain, bloating, and digestive difficulties. Her CA-125 levels are elevated, and her CT scan shows evidence of recurrent disease. She is considering participating in a clinical trial that will assess the effectiveness of a chemoresponse assay in predicting the success of chemotherapy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study, having only received one or two prior chemotherapy regimens for her ovarian cancer and has completed prior chemotherapy regimens at least 3 weeks prior to tissue extraction. She has an estimated life expectancy of greater than six months, as determined by her physician, and requires chemotherapy. She has signed an approved consent form to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old boy with a known diagnosis of Marfan syndrome presents at the clinic for his routine follow-up visit. His parents have been diligent about bringing him in for his check-ups every six months since he was diagnosed at the age of 5. The patient is currently asymptomatic, and he denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. He is not on any medication, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient's weight is 35 kg, and his height is 140 cm. His blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 bpm. The physical examination reveals a thin build, arachnodactyly, pectus carinatum, and pes planus. There is no evidence of joint laxity or scoliosis. The cardiac exam is unremarkable. The echocardiogram shows an aortic root diameter of 3.2 cm, which is within normal limits for the patient's age. The patient's parents express concern about the cost and burden of traveling to the specialized center every six months for follow-up visits. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that could offer tele-visits and home echocardiograms to monitor their child's condition.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). He is being treated according to the NOPHO ALL2008 protocol, which includes asparaginase treatment. The patient has completed the induction phase of treatment and is now in the consolidation phase. He has experienced some mild side effects from the asparaginase treatment, including nausea and vomiting, but has not had any severe adverse reactions. His parents are concerned about the potential for asparaginase-associated toxicities and the possibility of asparaginase treatment being truncated. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. The patient's blood counts and chemistry panel are within normal limits, and he is currently in remission. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for him to participate in this clinical trial.

28-year-old female with Hb SS sickle cell anemia, who has had multiple hospitalizations for pain crises and acute chest syndrome over the past 2 years. The patient has a history of bilateral leg ulcers and osteonecrosis of multiple bones. She has previously failed treatment with hydroxyurea and is interested in exploring alternative treatment options. The patient has no active sickle cell crises or acute chest syndrome, no active uncontrolled infection, and no allergies to E. coli derived products. She has no significant comorbid conditions, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use contraception during the study. The patient is able to give informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the efficacy and safety of recombinant-methionyl human stem cell factor in the treatment of sickling disorders.

55-year-old male who has been experiencing dizziness for several months. The dizziness is associated with neck stiffness and pain. He has not found relief with medication and physical therapy. The patient has a hypomobility of the upper cervical spine. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of traction manipulation on dizziness intensity, range of motion of cervical spine, and quality of life. The patient has no contraindications for traction manipulation. He understands and is able to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer three years ago. He underwent radical prostatectomy and adjuvant radiation therapy. His PSA level remained undetectable for over two years, but it has recently risen to 1.2 ng/mL. A biopsy confirmed biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer. The patient has not received any prior treatment for biochemical recurrence. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not have any other significant medical history. The patient has no known allergies to any medication.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma (MM) six months ago. He has been receiving chemotherapy but has experienced significant side effects, including fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. He has difficulty walking and has lost a significant amount of weight. He has several comorbidities, including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and osteoarthritis. He is currently taking several medications for these conditions. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and tolerability of lower dose lenalidomide and dexamethasone. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study, including having symptomatic MM based on standard CRAB criteria and measurable disease. The patient has been classified as frail based on the R-MCI scoring system due to his reduced physical function and comorbidities. He meets the clinical laboratory criteria with ANC ≥ 1,000/mm3, platelet ≥ 50,000/mm3, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, and calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 30mL/min or creatinine < 3mg/dL. The patient has not received previous treatment with anti-myeloma therapy and does not have any significant medical diseases or conditions that may interfere with protocol adherence.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with a hernia and requires surgery. He has no history of psychotropic or neuropsychiatric medications and has an American Society of Anesthesia (ASA) physical status class I. His body mass index is 23 kg m-2. He has a class II Mallampati airway and a mandible-to-hyoid distance of greater than three fingerbreadths. He is between the ages of 18-75 years. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to determine the effect of neuromuscular blockade on the Composite Variability Index (CVI) during laryngoscopy. The patient will be randomized into one of four doses of rocuronium, and the study anesthesiologist will perform a laryngoscopy to monitor the CVI, entropy, and hemodynamic responses before and after the laryngoscopy. The patient will be monitored for three minutes before and after the laryngoscopy.

N/A - This is not a clinical trial that involves patient enrollment or interaction. It is a genetic research study that aims to identify blood pressure quantitative trait genes (BPQTGs) that influence blood pressure levels in the population and determine if they can predict the occurrence of essential hypertension or coronary artery disease. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions needed for this study.

A 62-year-old man is scheduled for a lobectomy due to a lung cancer diagnosis. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He is a smoker and has been smoking for over 30 years. He has never had any lung surgeries before. He has no known allergies to medications or bovine-derived products. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not excessively. He is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

48 y/o male recently diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on a metformin regimen and follows a strict antidiabetic diet. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He is looking for additional treatment options to help manage his diabetes and is interested in participating in clinical research studies. The patient has no history of other significant medical conditions and is not a woman of childbearing potential.

A 9-year-old boy has been experiencing headaches and dizziness for the past 3 weeks. His parents noticed that he has been having difficulty walking and has been complaining of blurry vision. Upon further evaluation, he was diagnosed with a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), a type of brainstem tumor. He has no significant past medical history and has not received any prior treatment except for dexamethasone. He is able to walk with assistance but has difficulty maintaining his balance. He has a Karnofsky score of 50% and is able to attend school for a few hours a day. His laboratory results show normal kidney and liver function, with a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, platelet count of 120,000/uL, and an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200/uL. He is not on any anticonvulsants and has no history of seizures. He is able to swallow capsules and liquids without any difficulty. MRI of the spine did not show any evidence of disseminated disease. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of stage III breast cancer. She has completed one standard chemotherapy regimen and has confirmed HER-2/neu protein overexpression in her tumor. Her WBC count is greater than 3,500/mm3, and her platelet count is greater than 100,000/mm3, with no evidence of liver or renal dysfunction. She has no history of anergy and is non-fertile. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves receiving a vaccine made from the HER2/neu antigen plus sargramostim (GM-CSF) as an adjuvant to build an immune response to kill tumor cells. She is willing to receive serial intradermal vaccinations and participate in immunologic evaluations every 2 months to monitor the potential toxicity associated with sequential immunizations. She is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 12 months.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was admitted to the hospital due to acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. He was diagnosed with pneumonia and required orotracheal intubation for respiratory support. Despite treatment, his arterial oxygen tension (PaO2) remained below 60mmHg with a venturi mask and FiO2 of 0.5, and his arterial carbon dioxide tension (PaCO2) remained below 45mmHg. He met standard criteria for weaning readiness but failed a spontaneous breathing trial. He does not have a tracheotomy and his percentage of cuff leak volume in tidal volume is above 15.5%. He is able to spontaneously clear secretions from his airway and does not have recent oral, nasal, facial, or cranial trauma or surgery. He does not have recent gastric or esophageal surgery, active upper gastro-intestinal bleeding, or severe abdominal distension. He is cooperative and does not have chronic respiratory diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, or interstitial lung disease. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial assessing the efficacy of noninvasive positive pressure ventilation for early extubation of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

A 35-year-old male with a history of recurrent renal calculi confirmed by plain X-ray KUB and ultrasound KUB/CT scan Abdomen is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The size of the calculi ranges from 4mm-9mm, and the patient is willing to participate and give written informed consent. The patient is not suffering from any acute condition of renal calculi, systemic disease requiring other medications or surgery for calculus condition. The patient does not have any complicated cases of Renal Calculi requiring surgical condition or any chronic or current infectious disease. The patient has controlled diabetes and hypertension without any symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, and urogenital disorders. The patient has normal liver and kidney functions with no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is willing to cooperate and give consent for the trial and comes for regular follow-up. The patient is willing to use reliable means of contraception throughout the study participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for the past year. She has tried pelvic floor muscle training in the past but has not seen significant improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new outpatient therapy using laser treatment for SUI. At the screening visit, she performs a standardised 1-hour pad test and her pad weight is found to be 8g. Her medical history is checked, and she undergoes a clinical and vaginal examination, pregnancy test and dipstick urinalysis which are all normal. At the baseline visit, she completes a standing and supine cough test and questionnaires including the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Short Form (ICIQ-SF) and Pelvic Organ Prolapse/Urinary Incontinence Sexual Function Questionnaire (PISQ-12). She is then randomly assigned to either the active treatment or sham treatment group, and undergoes 3 outpatient treatment visits at 1-month intervals receiving the Incontilase laser treatment. At each visit, she is asked about any deleterious effects since her last appointment and completes the ICIQ-SF and Patient Global Impression of Improvement questionnaire. She also undergoes a dipstick urinalysis and pregnancy test at each treatment appointment. She is invited to attend follow-up visits at 6 and 12 months after the 3rd treatment and asked to complete ICIQ-SF, PISQ-12 and PGI-I symptom questionnaires and undergo a clinical examination. She is also asked to perform a cough test supine and standing, and a 1-hour pad test at 6 and 12 months. She is eligible for the trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of having a clinical and UDS diagnosis of SUI, SUI on 1-hour Pad weight test between 2g and 25g, and no significant improvement in urinary incontinence from at least one previous conservative treatment such as pelvic floor muscle training. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 67-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral arterial disease. He presents with chronic ischemic limb pain in his left lower extremity that has been worsening over the past few months. He has tried conservative management but has not found any significant relief. His ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.6, and he has a non-healing ulcer on the medial aspect of his left foot. He is scheduled for peripheral angioplasty under monitored anesthesia care. He has no history of allergies or contraindications to local anesthetic drugs or sedative drugs. The expected timing of the procedure is less than 3 hours. He is able to cooperate with the staff and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and is not taking any medications. He has no history of smoking or drug use. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. His height is 180 cm and his weight is 75 kg. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is interested in participating in clinical trials to contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) six months ago. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He has never undergone AF ablation therapy before. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol requirements. He has no planned surgical or endovascular intervention within 30 days before or after the index procedures. He has no clinical evidence of active coronary ischemia, significant valvular heart disease, or hemodynamically significant congenital cardiac abnormality. He has not experienced a myocardial infarction (MI), stroke (CVA), or transient ischemic attack (TIA) or other neurological disturbances. He does not have a pacemaker, and no thrombi have been detected in his heart. His estimated life expectancy is greater than 12 months. He has no known severe renal insufficiency or allergy to iodine.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who presents with fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and elevated liver enzymes on routine blood work. She has a history of obesity with a BMI of 33 and type 2 diabetes that is well-controlled with oral hypoglycemic agents. Her alcohol consumption is less than 10 g/day. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Abdominal ultrasound revealed increased echogenicity of the liver suggestive of fatty liver disease. A liver biopsy was performed within the last 6 months and confirmed the diagnosis of NASH. She has no other significant medical problems and is not taking any medications known to cause steatosis. Her vital signs are stable and physical exam is unremarkable.

42 year old male with a BMI of 31.5 kg/m2 and a waist circumference of 97 cm, presenting with sedentary lifestyle and no regular engagement in physical activity. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, but no known cardiovascular or metabolic disease. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of substance abuse or engagement in uncommon eating practices. The patient is not taking any prescription or non-prescription medication or supplements that may influence normal metabolic responses. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and restrictions and has provided voluntary written informed consent. The patient has not had more than 3 muscle biopsies obtained from the thigh quadriceps region within the past 5 years.

A 70-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation is being considered for the PLUG Dementia Trial and MRI PLUG Dementia Sub-Study. He has a CHADS2 score of 3 and has received a left atrial appendage closure device within the past 3 months. He has no history of dementia and is able to complete a mini-mental status evaluation and quality of life and dementia questionnaires independently. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 24 months and is willing and able to comply with the prescribed follow-up tests and schedule of evaluations. He has not participated in any other clinical trials involving an investigational or marketed drug within the past 30 days. The patient does not have a nonconditional cardiac implantable device, history of metallic implants, shrapnel, neurosurgical clip placement or severe renal dysfunction. Additionally, he does not have any other conditions that may increase his risk or compromise the quality of the trial. The patient is interested in participating in the MRI PLUG Dementia Sub-Study and is willing to undergo a cranial MRI at baseline and at the 2-year follow-up visit.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis affecting multiple joints. She has been receiving conventional therapy for the past 6 months but has not responded well to the treatment. She is experiencing frequent joint pain, swelling, and stiffness which have significantly affected her ability to perform daily activities and participate in school activities. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has not been diagnosed with any other comorbid conditions and is not taking any other medications. She has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. Her parents are actively involved in her care and are willing to provide consent for her participation in the study.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) five years ago and has been receiving nilotinib treatment in a Novartis-sponsored Oncology Clinical Development & Medical Affairs study for the past two years. The patient has been responding well to the treatment with nilotinib, as judged by the investigator, and has demonstrated compliance with the parent study protocol requirements. The patient has not experienced any unacceptable toxicity and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, and any other study procedures. The patient has provided written informed consent to enroll in the roll-over study to allow continued use of nilotinib. The patient is not currently receiving treatment with any medications that have the potential to prolong the QT interval or inducing Torsade de Pointes, and is not pregnant, nursing, or of child-bearing potential.

The patient is a 24-year-old man who works as a bartender and enjoys socializing with friends on weekends. He drinks alcohol regularly and often exceeds the recommended daily limit. He has no history of neurological, psychiatric, or medical disorders. He is physically fit and able to read and write in English. He does not take any prescription or non-prescription medications, including psychoactive or herbal supplements. He is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to conceive in the next six months. He is willing to provide voluntary, written informed consent and is comfortable with undergoing Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging. He has no contraindications for MRI and is not claustrophobic or sensitive to metal. He is not a "low binder" for the rs6971 polymorphism.

The patient is a 12-year-old Syrian refugee girl living with her parents in Lebanon. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety, depression and behavioural problems for the past 6 months. Her parents have noticed that she is often tearful, irritable and lacks interest in activities that she used to enjoy. She also has difficulty falling asleep and has nightmares. Her parents have tried to comfort her but her symptoms have not improved. They are concerned about her well-being and have requested mental health services. The family has been identified as eligible for the study based on the inclusion criteria. The patient and her parents have agreed to participate in the study and have provided informed consent and assent. They have been randomised to receive t-CETA, a version of Common Elements Treatment Approach (CETA) adapted to be delivered over the telephone. The treatment will take approximately 8-16 weeks and will involve therapy sessions 1 or 2 times per week for up to 30 minutes per session. They will also complete assessments at baseline, immediately after treatment, and at three months follow-up. The family will be closely supervised by an experienced clinical psychologist and will have access to case manager-led care, involving initial assessment by a case manager, with intervention then provided by a case manager, and/or referral to a psychotherapist or psychiatrist as necessary. The family will also receive independent assessments conducted over the phone (or face-to-face if phone assessment is not possible) by trained assessors who are independent of the treatment team and are blind to treatment condition. The patient and her family will have access to a visual aids booklet to assist them in responding to questionnaire items. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of t-CETA in treating common mental health problems in 8-17 year old Syrian refugee children living in Lebanon.

A 24-year-old female diagnosed with cystic fibrosis with an F508del mutation who is being treated at the Adult CF Program at National Jewish Health has been recommended to start a CFTR modulator as part of her clinical care. She has been experiencing an increase in cough and sputum production over the past few months and has had multiple exacerbations of her disease in the past. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and provide written consent. She has the ability to perform reproducible Pulmonary Function Tests. The patient has no other medical conditions that would compromise her safety or the quality of the data. She will be enrolled in the study and biological samples will be collected at two different time points prior to treatment initiation, and at least one month after starting treatment. The study assessments will continue up to 2 times a year, including during pulmonary exacerbations, in order to document longitudinal effects of therapies and changes in inflammatory biology over time.

Patient is a 30-year-old male residing in India who has been experiencing itchy, red rashes in the groin area for the past two weeks. He has not received any treatment for this condition and has been avoiding scratching the affected area. He presents with a clinical diagnosis of Tinea cruris and is prescribed itraconazole at 200 milligram/day orally for the treatment of Tinea cruris. He has not been diagnosed with any other dermatoses and does not have a history of ventricular dysfunction or liver or renal insufficiency. He is willing to practice a highly effective method of contraception if he is a woman of childbearing potential and agrees to wear a condom during sexual activity if he is a male participant.

62 yo M with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and stable angina presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath. Cardiac workup demonstrated an acute non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction requiring urgent coronary angiography. On exam, the patient is alert and oriented, with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. His labs reveal a normal renal function with an eGFR of > 60 ml/min/1.73 m2. The patient's Mehran's risk score for contrast-induced nephropathy is >11. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign the informed consent form. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial testing the hypothesis that fenoldopam, in addition to standard treatment, reduces the occurrence of contrast-induced acute kidney injury in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing urgent/emergency coronary angiography and/or percutaneous coronary intervention.

The patient is an 18-year-old student who is enrolled in the First Year Initiative Courses titled "Balance" or "Constructing Health" at Beloit College. They have no known medical conditions that would prevent them from participating in a 30-day wellness intervention program that combines exercise, mindfulness, sleep, social connectedness, and nutrition. They are willing to commit to the program and are not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the next 30 days. They are excited to participate in the study to improve their overall health and wellness.

45F with a history of migraines and dizziness, referred to neurology for further evaluation. The patient reports experiencing episodes of vertigo accompanied by migraines for the past year. The vertigo episodes are described as a spinning sensation that lasts for several minutes, and are often triggered by sudden head movements. The patient reports experiencing nausea and difficulty with balance during these episodes. She denies any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear pain. She has tried various migraine medications with limited success. On exam, the patient has no nystagmus at rest, but there is a mild horizontal nystagmus present during head impulse testing. Audiometry shows normal hearing thresholds. The patient is able to stand and walk without difficulty, but reports feeling unsteady on her feet during vertigo episodes. The patient is diagnosed with vestibular migraine and is offered participation in a clinical trial comparing pharmacological management options and vestibular rehabilitation programmes.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries, including a fractured femur, a lacerated spleen, and a head injury. He was transported to the trauma center and is currently stable but requires immediate resuscitation. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications. The patient is not pregnant, a child, a psychiatric patient, or a prisoner.

56-year-old male diagnosed with chronic phase chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) with hematologic resistance to imatinib mesylate. He has been treated with imatinib mesylate for 3 months but failed to achieve complete hematologic response (CHR). He has a WBC count of at least 10,000/mm^3 and rising on at least two consecutive measurements obtained at least 14 days apart with at least one of these measurements greater than 15,000/mm^3, indicating acquired hematologic resistance. His CD4^+ T-cell count is at least 350/mm^3, and he is in good general health with an ECOG performance status of 0-1, and a life expectancy of at least six months. He has no significant hepatic or renal dysfunction, and his potassium, magnesium, and serum calcium or ionized calcium levels are normal. He has tested negative for pregnancy and is using effective contraception. He has not received interferon, cytarabine, or hydroxyurea for more than 14 days, and other investigational or antineoplastic agents for more than 28 days. He has not received imatinib mesylate for more than 7 days. He has not taken medications that inhibit platelet function, anticoagulants, or drugs known to cause torsades de pointes for at least 5 days or 5 half-lives. He has no history of significant bleeding disorder unrelated to CML, acquired bleeding disorder within the past year, congenital bleeding disorders, uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction, clinically significant ventricular arrhythmias, diagnosed or suspected congenital long QT syndrome, prolonged QTc interval on pre-entry EKG, heart rate less than 50/minute on pre-entry EKG, uncontrolled hypertension, vasculitis, gastrointestinal tract bleeding within the past 6 months, connective tissue disorders, other serious uncontrolled medical disorder or active infection, dementia or altered mental status that would preclude giving informed consent, evidence of organ dysfunction or any clinically significant deviation from normal in physical examination, vital signs, EKG, or clinical laboratory determinations unrelated to CML, and is not currently taking concurrent drugs accepted to have a risk of causing torsades de pointes, other concurrent treatment for CML, dolasetron or droperidol, anticoagulants, or medications that inhibit platelet function.

The patient is a 40 year old male who works as a construction worker. He has been experiencing persistent pain in the bottom of his right foot for over 6 months. The pain is worse in the morning and improves slightly with activity, but he still experiences discomfort throughout the day. He rates his pain as a 5 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) during activity. He has tried over-the-counter pain relievers and rest, but has not found any significant relief. He has no prior history of foot or ankle injuries, and is otherwise healthy. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a BMI of 28 and his blood pressure is within normal range. He enjoys playing soccer on the weekends and is frustrated that his foot pain is limiting his ability to participate in physical activities. He is fluent in Norwegian and is willing to participate in the trial to receive treatment for his plantar fasciopathy.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who presents with a history of cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with pleural effusion of unknown etiology and is being evaluated for possible tuberculosis. He has no significant past medical history and currently takes no medications. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He denies any history of smoking or drug use. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds on the right side of his chest. He is able to exhale through the E-nose device without difficulty. He has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with follow-up visits.

Patient is a 65-year-old right-handed woman who has been experiencing mild to moderate cognitive impairment consistent with dementia of the Alzheimer type. She has not been treated with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and has no motor impairments that affect her daily life. The patient has no history of epilepsy and has not been diagnosed with depression. She is not currently taking any centrally active drugs and has no contraindications for MRI, such as a pacemaker or metal parts in her body. The patient has insurance coverage and has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old non-smoking woman who has been recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. Her CT and PET scans reveal no evidence of cancer spread to other parts of the body, but there is a suspicion of cancer in the mediastinal lymph nodes. She reports occasional shortness of breath and cough, but no chest pain or weight loss. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. Her family history is negative for lung cancer or any other cancers. She is willing to participate in the trial and has given written informed consent.

John is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing severe pain in his left hip joint for the past year. He has difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to this pain. He has no history of any major illnesses or surgeries in the past. He is generally healthy and has no known allergies. He works as a carpenter and has physically demanding work. His X-ray shows severe osteoarthritis in the left hip joint. He has been recommended for a total hip arthroplasty surgery, and his doctor has suggested the DELTA Multihole TT cup. John has provided informed consent to participate in the retrospective study evaluating the clinical and radiographic early outcomes of total hip arthroplasty and revision hip arthroplasty with DELTA Multihole TT cup. He meets the inclusion criteria of the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx and is currently scheduled for biopsy and/or resection. The patient's tumor tissue sample is available from the Head and Neck Tissue Repository and Clinical Database of Vanderbilt University. The patient has not received any prior concurrent therapy. The patient's HPV status is positive, and their tumor tissue sample will be used for DNA analysis in the laboratory to identify biomarkers related to cancer. The patient will be included in the study if they meet the eligibility criteria and give their consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent cough for several months, with occasional hemoptysis. He has a history of smoking, with a 40 pack-year history. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He reports a productive cough with yellowish sputum, and has experienced fatigue and weight loss. Imaging studies reveal a left upper lobe mass, and biopsy confirms a diagnosis of non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR activating mutations. The patient's physician has prescribed Tarceva (erlotinib) as first-line treatment. The patient is willing to participate in the observational study to evaluate the patterns of disease progression in patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC harbouring EGFR activating mutations receiving Tarceva as first-line treatment. The patient meets all of the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45 year old male with Type 2 Diabetes mellitus diagnosed one year ago. He has been on NPH insulin treatment along with one oral anti-diabetic medication for the past 6 months, but his blood glucose levels have been difficult to control. His HbA1c level is between 6.5% and 9%. He has been measuring his blood glucose levels at home for the past 3 months. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m² and waist circumference of 105 cm. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, allergies or other significant medical conditions. His blood chemistry is normal except for an hsCRP level of 8 mg/l. He has never been treated with GLP1-analog or Thiazolidinediones (TZD). He is willing to give written informed consent and allow his family physician/diabetologist to be informed of his trial participation.

Patient is a 5-year-old boy who recently visited the dentist for a routine check-up. During the examination, the dentist noticed atypical cavities on two of his deciduous molars. The boy has no known medical conditions and is in good general health. He is able to cooperate during the examination and has no orthodontic apparatus in place. The parents have consented to their child's participation in the study. The teeth with pulp exposure, spontaneous pain, mobility, swelling or fistula close to the tooth, and furcation or cervical injury will be excluded. The dentist will randomly select one of the atypical cavities to be treated with chemically activated composite resin Alkasite, while the other cavity will be treated with resin-modified glass ionomer cement. Follow-up examinations will be performed at 6 and 12 months to evaluate the efficacy of the treatments and patient-centered outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. He has been on a stable dose of antipsychotic medication for the past 6 months. He has a history of substance abuse, but has been sober for the past year. He is currently unemployed and lives with his parents. He has no significant medical history aside from his psychiatric diagnosis. He complies with his medication regimen and attends regular appointments with his psychiatrist. He has no history of seizures, dementia, or other neurological disorders. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in cognitive remediation exercises as part of the study. He understands the importance of using appropriate birth control measures during the study if female and fertile.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to a severe respiratory infection. He presents with a high fever, shortness of breath, and coughing up blood. The patient has no history of heart, liver, or kidney diseases and is not currently taking corticosteroids. The patient is receiving nutrition through a nasogastric tube. The patient has not previously taken any glutamine supplements. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is between the ages of 18 and 60.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy woman who works as a software engineer. She has no history of chronic medical conditions, hospitalizations, or hospitalizations in the past year. She is not taking any medications or supplements. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has never received an influenza vaccine and is seronegative to at least one of the strains included in the seasonal vaccine against influenza for 2011. She is currently not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use an acceptable method of contraception throughout the study period. She is willing to adhere to the visit schedule and protocol requirements and be available to complete the study. She has no known hypersensitivity or allergies to any drug or vaccine and has never had Guillain Barré Syndrome in the past. Her hematology, chemistry, and urinalysis values are within normal limits. She has not been immunized with any vaccine within the last 30 days before the screening visit. She is willing to sign the consent form and participate in the study.

This clinical trial is not applicable for generating a patient description as it is an open label roll-over extension protocol for participants who have completed a Novartis trial with secukinumab and have been judged by the investigator to benefit from continued treatment with secukinumab. Therefore, the patient description would depend on the previous Novartis trial that the participant completed.

The patient is a 4-month-old infant diagnosed with primary congenital glaucoma. The baby's parents noted that their baby had cloudy eyes and excessive tearing since birth. The ophthalmologist confirmed the diagnosis of congenital glaucoma after measuring the intraocular pressure which was found to be above 25 mmHg in both eyes. The baby has an enlarged corneal diameter of 12 mm, and corneal edema is also observed. The optic disc appears to have mild cupping. The baby has no significant medical history, and no previous interventions have been done. The parents have been informed about the risks and benefits of the combined trabeculotomy-trabeculectomy with Ologen collagen matrix implant implantation procedure, and they have provided written consent for their child's participation in the study.

A 45-year-old female came to the clinic with a surgical wound on her lower leg that has not healed properly for the past three weeks. She had undergone a surgical procedure to remove a non-cancerous growth from her leg. The wound is approximately 4 cm in diameter and has been oozing pus. She has also been experiencing pain and discomfort in the area. The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes, which is well controlled with medication. She does not have any other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study. She is able to comply with the study procedures and is willing to sign the informed consent form. Her TcPO2 evaluation showed tissue hypoxia in the periwound region, indicating a reading of 15 mmHg. Her ankle brachial index (ABI) is 0.9, which is consistent with normal blood flow to the lower extremities. Her pre-albumin levels are within normal range. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not pregnant or lactating.

Patient is a 28-year-old male cyclist from Denmark, who has been competing at an elite level for the past 3 years. He trains for 15-20 hours per week, focusing mainly on endurance exercise. His VO2max is measured at 70 ml/kg/min. He does not have any history of chronic medical conditions or injuries that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is willing to incorporate 5 days per week of low-intensity training with heat exposure into his regular training routine for a period of 5 weeks. He understands that the study may involve additional testing and monitoring of his blood characteristics and muscle function, and agrees to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy living in India with no known chronic medical conditions. He has never received an influenza vaccine before. His family lives in a crowded area with multiple generations living in the same household. He attends school and interacts with other children regularly. He has no known allergies to eggs or any other components of the vaccine. His parents are willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. They understand that their child may receive either the TIV or IPV vaccine and will be closely monitored for any adverse reactions. They are willing to participate in the surveillance arm of the study, which involves monitoring for any influenza-like illness in the household throughout the study period.

8yo male with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and a recent diagnosis of pneumonia with sepsis. The patient presented to the emergency department with fever, shortness of breath, and cough. His respiratory rate was elevated and he was tachycardic. Blood cultures were drawn and he was started on antibiotics. He was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit for further management of sepsis. The patient will be enrolled in a nation-wide observational study to evaluate the specificity/sensitivity of new biomarkers for pediatric sepsis in combination with usual diagnostic markers for sepsis with a focus on early identification of sepsis, severe sepsis, and septic shock. The patient will have inflammation markers and full blood count parameters measured at the time of admission and on 3rd, 5th, and 7th day of stay in intensive care to evaluate the organ dysfunction score.

The patient is a 34-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for 8 years. He has been taking clozapine for the past 2 years and has been compliant with his medication. He has been experiencing significant weight gain, and his blood sugar levels have been elevated. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past 6 months. He is currently unemployed and lives with his parents. He has no significant medical history other than schizophrenia and has never received any radiation or chemotherapy treatments. He is willing to practice appropriate birth control methods during the study. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if aripiprazole could help alleviate the side effects of clozapine that he is experiencing.

A 65-year-old female with primary bilateral knee osteoarthritis that has been refractory to conservative treatment, including physical therapy, medication, and steroid injections. She has experienced significant pain and difficulty with mobility, which have had a negative impact on her quality of life. She has no history of malignancy, is not morbidly obese, and has no significant cardiac or systemic inflammatory diseases. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and accept randomization to either the two-surgeon or single-surgeon group. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

12-month-old male infant living in a rural area of Vietnam, with no history of Japanese Encephalitis vaccination, presents for routine vaccination. The child is in good health, with no chronic or acute diseases, and has not received any immunocompromised treatment within 4 weeks of enrollment. The parents consent to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form. The child has no family history of immunocompromised conditions, no history of febrile seizures, and is not allergic to any vaccine components. The child has not had a fever (>38 Celsius degree) within 3 days before vaccination or at enrollment, and is not malnourished. The child has no history of blood disorders or use of unlicensed vaccines within 7 days before enrollment in this study.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia (WM) two years ago. She has received chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past but her disease has relapsed. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she takes medication. She has no known allergies. She is retired and lives with her husband. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for mild splenomegaly. Her lab results show total bilirubin levels of 1.8 mg/dl and AST levels within normal limits. She is not pregnant and not currently breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

30-year-old woman diagnosed with neuromyelitis optica (NMO) for 4 years, with recurrent attacks of optic neuritis and transverse myelitis. She has been on high-dose steroid therapy with only partial control of symptoms. MRI shows widespread inflammation and demyelination in the brain and spinal cord. She has no significant medical history, and her vital signs are stable. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who has been admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) due to respiratory failure caused by severe pneumonia. The patient requires mechanical ventilation and vasopressors (dopamine and norepinephrine). The patient's family is available to discuss informed consent criteria and provide informed consent. The patient has no preexisting conditions in which there is impaired glycogen stores or counter regulatory response. The patient is not diagnosed with type I diabetes mellitus presenting to the ICU in diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). The patient will be screened for hyperglycemia as part of the study's inclusion criteria. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a glycemic control protocol on at least 250 children with hyperglycemia in different critical care units. The study is supported by an R21 Grant from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK).

This clinical trial is not applicable to a patient description. It is a study seeking to investigate factors associated with well-being in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic, and is not recruiting patients for a specific intervention or treatment.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of chronic coronary syndromes. She had undergone CCTA three months ago which showed at least one site with stenosis ≥ 50% of the lumen in a large coronary artery of ≥ 2 mm diameter. She is currently on standard treatment for chronic coronary syndromes with no dosage modification required within at least 4 weeks before the enrolment. The patient has no history of acute coronary syndrome, revascularization, or coronary obstruction confirmed by CCTA or invasive coronarography. She has no history of haemodynamic abnormalities of the valve or surgical correction of the defect or CABG. The patient has no second-degree or third-degree atrioventricular block, sinus node dysfunction, QTc > 450 ms, or prolonged QTc. Her LVEF is > 35% found in an echocardiogram performed within the last 6 months. Her BMI is 30. She has no clinically apparent infection or thrombocytopenia below 100.000/mm3. The patient does not have active neoplastic disease (apart from basal cell carcinoma and carcinoma in situ) and other conditions that, in the investigator's opinion, significantly affect their life expectancy. The patient has no other significant conditions, infections, addictions, or psychological or social factors that may affect their ability to participate in the trial or significantly affect their safety.

A 55-year-old male patient underwent a thoracotomy procedure for lung cancer. He has a medical history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. His vital signs are stable, and he is conscious. He has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for 24 hours and is now eligible for the physiotherapy program. He is experiencing some pain and discomfort in his chest, but it is manageable. He is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to perform the physiotherapy exercises. His oxygen saturation levels have been normal, and he has not experienced any neurological complications or posttraumatic injuries that would prevent him from exercising. He has a fever of 37.5 degrees Celsius.

Mary is a 54-year-old woman who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor and received adjuvant chemotherapy. Her disease has progressed and she has now been started on immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. She has a solitary pulmonary nodule measuring 20 mm in the longest diameter, which has been confirmed as recurrent NSCLC on biopsy. She has no other significant medical or surgical history and her performance status is 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) criteria. She is a non-smoker and has no history of other malignancies. Her laboratory and imaging studies were normal otherwise. She has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the protocol-specified follow-up evaluations.

45 year-old male with a history of hypertension and occasional snoring presents with excessive daytime sleepiness and morning headaches. He reports feeling tired even after a full night's sleep and has difficulty concentrating during the day. His spouse reports loud snoring and pauses in breathing during the night. He denies any history of major diseases or surgeries. His BMI is 32 kg/m2. He has not had any prior evaluations for sleep apnea.

The patient is a 72-year-old retired teacher who has been living in the same Montreal neighbourhood for the past 20 years. She lives alone in a small apartment and is generally in good health. She is interested in participating in the Montreal Neighbourhood Networks and Healthy Aging Panel study as she believes that social networks and neighbourhood environments play an important role in maintaining good health and well-being as one ages. She is fluent in both French and English and has no history of institutionalization. She is excited about the opportunity to contribute to longitudinal research that could benefit older adults in her community.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her knees for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse when she walks or stands for long periods of time. She has no history of trauma to her knees or other joints. She has been taking over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not provided much relief. Her BMI is 28, and she has controlled hypertension. She does not take any other medications or supplements. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new treatment for her osteoarthritis.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. He is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine-containing products. His urine drug and alcohol breath tests were negative. He is sexually active and willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. He is willing to consume a non-vegetarian high-fat and high-calorie breakfast. He has no known allergies to the study drug ingredients and has not experienced any significant allergic reactions to any medication in the past. He is not currently taking any medications except occasional paracetamol. He has no history of hepatitis or immunosuppressive conditions. His liver and renal function test results were within normal limits. He has no clinically relevant abnormalities detected on ECG or vital signs. He does not have any dietary requirements that preclude participation in the study. He has not consumed large quantities of caffeinated coffee or tea. He has not participated in any drug or drug/device investigational research study and has not participated in a previous study with the same compound (GLPG1690).

As this is a clinical trial to evaluate the knowledge level of healthcare professionals regarding COVID-19 guidelines, there is no need for a patient description. Instead, the study will be recruiting healthcare professionals such as physicians, nurses, physiotherapists, and nutritionists. The study will be open to those with clinical practical experience and currently working in hospitals or any health institution. However, employees outside the health area, health professionals who do not work in any health institution, and employees who do not have a bachelor's degree will be excluded from the study.

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of difficulty losing weight despite multiple attempts at dieting and exercise. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, and her BMI is 31 kg/m². She is currently taking medications for hypertension and cholesterol management. She has not participated in any other clinical trials and is not currently hospitalized. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with follow-up visits. She understands the study requirements and provides informed consent.

A 25-year-old Chinese male visited the clinic for a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His vital signs were within normal limits and he has a BMI of 22. He has no respiratory symptoms and his chest X-ray was normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to support the development of a new inhalation powder for respiratory conditions. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and understands the risks and benefits of participation.

The patient is a 28-year-old Hong Kong resident who has been smoking for the past 6 years. She smokes an average of 8 cigarettes per day, but has been struggling to quit smoking on her own. She is aware of the health risks associated with smoking and is motivated to quit, but has not been successful in her previous attempts. She is fluent in Cantonese and willing to participate in a community-based smoking cessation program. She is currently not following any other smoking cessation programs. Her exhaled carbon monoxide (CO) level is assessed to be 6 ppm. She works as a salesperson and is concerned about the impact of her smoking habit on her health and work performance. She is looking for an effective and sustainable way to quit smoking with the help of a supportive community.

John is a 65-year-old man who served in the Vietnam War as a combat infantryman. He has been experiencing chronic pain and limited mobility in his right shoulder and right knee for several years. He is currently receiving disability benefits from the VA but has been told that his case needs to be re-evaluated through a C&P examination. He is scheduled for an appointment at the VA TVHS for a C&P examination of his right shoulder and right knee. John has no other significant medical history and takes no medication for his joint pain. He has a supportive family and is eager to participate in this clinical trial to help improve the quality of veteran care.

A 56-year-old man with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and undergoing hemodialysis for the past 6 months visits the clinic.
