He has been experiencing pain in his legs, especially during walking, for the past few weeks. He reports having high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels. The patient has agreed to participate in the research study to investigate the role of the interaction between advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and their receptor RAGE in the development and progression of the uremic vasculopathy of hemodialyzed patients. The investigators will measure vascular calcifications by X-ray and tomodentimetry, as well as AGEs accumulation in the serum and non-invasively in the skin. The patient will also undergo genetic polymorphism testing and measurement of soluble forms of RAGE to analyze factors influencing RAGE activation. The patient has no known diabetes and is affiliated to a social security scheme. He is eligible for the study unless he has pigmented skin, an abdominal aortic aneurysm, or a progressive neoplastic disease.

A 52-year-old male with a history of advanced prostate cancer that has failed to respond to standard therapies. He has not received any prior chemotherapy. The patient is able to understand and follow study requirements and has signed a written informed consent form. He is post-menopausal and agrees to practice two effective methods of birth control during the study period or completely abstain from heterosexual intercourse. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and meets laboratory test standards for bone marrow function, liver function, blood pressure, and renal function. He has no history of another cancer diagnosed or treated within the past 3 years and has no severe cardiovascular, thyroid, or bleeding issues. He has not had any serious wounds, ulcers, or bone fractures that do not heal. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no illnesses or conditions that may affect his ability to participate in the study. The patient has not participated in another clinical study or post-marketing clinical study within 4 weeks prior to the start of this trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and vomiting for the past 12 hours. On examination, he has diffuse abdominal tenderness and guarding with rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. Blood tests reveal leukocytosis and an elevated Neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Imaging studies show signs of acute appendicitis with suspicion of perforation. He is diagnosed with acute appendicitis and scheduled for emergency laparotomy. The patient has no known history of COVID-19 infection and has not been exposed to anyone with confirmed COVID-19. He agrees to participate in the study and undergoes regular follow-up assessments for 30 days post-surgery to evaluate outcomes including mortality, length of stay, respiratory complications, sepsis, and ICU admission.

A 19-year-old English-speaking individual who has been diagnosed with HIV and is currently receiving care at the adolescent outpatient clinics at Johns Hopkins Children's Center (JHCC). The patient is on anti-retroviral therapy (ART) but has struggled with medication adherence. They have experienced stress and difficulties with self-regulation and coping due to their diagnosis. The patient is interested in participating in a mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) program to help improve their medication adherence and overall well-being. Past medical history includes occasional depressive symptoms but currently stable on medication. No history of substance abuse or major psychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who fell off the monkey bars at school and hurt her wrist. She is experiencing moderate to severe pain in her wrist, and her parents brought her to the Emergency Department for evaluation. The patient is able to speak and communicate effectively in English. She is accompanied by her mother, who speaks both English and Spanish fluently. The patient has no history of traumatic brain injury, developmental delay, autism, or chronic pain. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. She is in first grade and enjoys playing on the playground at school. In her free time, she likes to read books and draw pictures. Her BMI is within normal limits for her age and height, and her vital signs are stable. There is no visible deformity or swelling in her wrist, but she complains of pain when it is touched or moved.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has a history of melanoma. He has a palpable skin lesion on his back that has not been biopsied yet. He is interested in participating in a pilot study of infrared imaging of cutaneous melanoma. He has fair skin, brown hair, and blue eyes. He works as a construction worker and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and fishing. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. He has no known allergies to adhesive skin markers or water-soluble ink. He understands the study requirements and is willing to give informed consent.

A 32-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia presents to the outpatient clinic. He reports experiencing auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions for the past 6 months. The patient has been previously treated with antipsychotic medications and has a history of noncompliance with medications. His family has noticed a decline in his overall functioning and he has been unable to maintain employment due to his symptoms. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible to participate.

50 yo F with a long-standing history of fibromyalgia syndrome with moderate to severe pain in the neck, shoulders, and lower back for the past 6 months. She has tried multiple medications over the years, including NSAIDs, opioids, and gabapentinoids, but has not experienced significant relief. Her symptoms have been affecting her daily activities, including work and household chores. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and improve her quality of life. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has no other uncontrolled medical conditions.

A 70-year-old male with a history of localized prostate cancer treated with radical prostatectomy 5 years ago presented with rising PSA levels of 8 ng/mL. He underwent radiation therapy and was started on intermittent androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for 6 months. His PSA levels decreased to 0.2 ng/mL after 6 months of ADT. The patient has been off ADT for 2 months and his PSA levels have risen to 6 ng/mL. He is otherwise healthy with no history of other medical conditions. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance (ECOG) performance status is 0. Bone scan and CT scan were performed within the last 12 months and showed no evidence of distant metastases. His hemoglobin, platelet count, total bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are within normal limits. He is not on any other medications or investigational agents. He has not received any glucocorticoids or anabolic steroids within the last 3 months. He has not received chemotherapy or hormonal therapy within the last year. He has not had any drug or alcohol abuse within the last 12 months. He is willing to use condoms if sexually active and is able to swallow and retain oral medication. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the full study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was referred to the cardiology department for evaluation of chest pain. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He is a smoker and has been smoking for 20 years with a 10 pack-year history. He has no family history of coronary artery disease. He presents with chest pain that is exertional, relieved with rest, and associated with shortness of breath. He has normal vital signs and no other significant physical exam findings. His ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with no ST-T changes. He has never had an echocardiogram before. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the study.

Sarah is a 52-year-old woman who visited the dental clinic with bleeding gums and bad breath. She reported that she had noticed bleeding from her gums during brushing and flossing for the past 6 months. She had also been experiencing bad breath and sensitivity in her teeth while eating hot and cold foods. She had not received any treatment for her periodontal disease before. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it daily. She has no history of any other systemic diseases. She is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. Her oral examination revealed generalized gingival inflammation with deep pockets and mild bone loss. She is diagnosed with stage 3, grade B and generalized periodontitis. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

55-year-old male with end-stage kidney disease due to hypertension, currently on hemodialysis three times a week. History of myocardial infarction and peripheral vascular disease. No active inflammation or malignancy. Able to understand and speak Dutch fluently. Has no cognitive disorder. Willing to participate in the study by undergoing different tests to identify potential biomarkers for dialysis adequacy and quality of life. Has no history of non-compliance with dialysis treatment.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who has been experiencing headaches, nausea, and vomiting for the past few weeks. She has also noticed changes in her vision, such as blurriness and double vision. Upon further examination, it is discovered that she has a newly diagnosed glioblastoma multiforme, a grade IV astrocytoma. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial, including being able to undergo serial MRIs, having adequate bone marrow, liver, renal, and metabolic function, and having a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of at least 60. She has not received any prior treatment for her GBM, except for surgical resection and/or corticosteroid therapy. She is willing to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures including receiving daily external beam radiation therapy in a radiation treatment facility. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraceptive measures for the duration of treatment and for 4 weeks following discontinuation of study treatment. She has no history of prior cardiotoxic chemotherapy exposure or thoracic irradiation involving cardiac tissue.

The patient is a 61-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer three years ago. He underwent surgery and radiation therapy, followed by hormone therapy. Recently, his PSA levels have risen despite hormone therapy. He presents with fatigue and difficulty urinating. His past medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no known allergies. His family history is significant for prostate cancer in his father and uncle. He is not currently taking any other medications besides his anti-hypertensive medication.

A 45-year-old man has been experiencing chronic pain in his right knee and was referred to an orthopedic surgeon for evaluation. He was diagnosed with a torn meniscus and has scheduled a surgical procedure to repair it. He has no known allergies or medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has a sedentary lifestyle and his BMI is within normal range. The surgeon has informed him about the risk of surgical site infections and the importance of perioperative infection control measures. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial.

This is a 29-year-old male construction worker with a history of occasional lower back pain after prolonged periods of standing and lifting heavy objects. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medication. He works in construction and has to perform tasks that involve lifting, carrying, and shoveling heavy construction materials. He is right-handed and has no prior injuries or chronic pain in the last 6 months. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to walk and lift heavy objects without pain or discomfort. He has no pacemaker, breast implants, or removed axillary lymph nodes. He is not pregnant and not using blood thinning medications. He will be asked to wear four types of commercial Back support exoskeletons (BSEs) during simulated concrete work tasks while his postural data will be recorded. He will be asked to provide feedback on the effectiveness, usability, and acceptability of the BSEs after completing each work task. The study will require approximately 3 hours of his time.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with acute onset chest pain and shortness of breath 4 hours ago. His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but he is not on any regular medications. On physical examination, he appeared in moderate distress, with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, a heart rate of 104 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. Cardiac auscultation revealed normal heart sounds with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. His electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. He was diagnosed with a first ST-elevation myocardial infarction and scheduled for an emergency angioplasty. After meeting the eligibility criteria, he was enrolled in the clinical trial and randomized to receive either thromboaspiration followed by angioplasty or angioplasty alone. The infarct size and severity will be assessed by ce-MRI and rest Tc99m-mibi gated SPECT performed during initial hospital stay (5th-8th day). A control MRI will be performed at 6-month follow-up to analyze the evolution of left ventricular volumes.

A 62-year-old female came to the clinic with complaints of difficulty walking and freezing of gait (FOG), which has become more frequent over the past year. She has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (PD) for 7 years and has been on levodopa therapy with good response. Despite the medication, she has difficulty with walking, especially when initiating steps or turning corners. She also experiences FOG, where she feels like her feet are glued to the ground and cannot move. She has fallen several times due to FOG and has become increasingly dependent on her husband for daily activities. She has tried physical therapy and occupational therapy, but her symptoms have not improved. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or psychiatric illness. She is not taking any anticoagulants or immunosuppressive medications. She is willing to participate in the study and to undergo minimally invasive spinal cord stimulation (SCS). She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is able to provide informed consent.

Patient A is a 27-year-old pregnant woman currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. She has been attending antenatal care (ANC) visits at a Level 3 government-owned health facility in Kenya. She has not had any previous complications during her pregnancy and has been following a healthy diet and lifestyle. She is HIV-negative and has not had any previous exposure to malaria. She has been enrolled in the IMPROVE trial and has been randomly assigned to receive either intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP) with or without azithromycin or the current policy of IPTp with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) to prevent malaria, sexually transmitted and reproductive tract infections. She has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate. During her ANC visit, she will receive the appropriate intervention according to the arm allocated to her health facility. She will be asked to complete follow-up interviews to assess the acceptability and feasibility of the intervention. Additionally, she will be asked to participate in a home visit to assess her adherence to the treatment regimen. Overall, Patient A is an eligible participant for this clinical trial and her participation will provide valuable information to assess the effectiveness and feasibility of different interventions to prevent malaria and sexually transmitted infections during pregnancy.

The patient is a 12-year-old male with a history of Crohn's disease. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past few months. His doctor has recommended a CT or MR enterography to evaluate the bowel lumen and bowel wall. The patient has previously undergone this type of imaging and has received the standard-of-care oral contrast material (VoLumen). However, he experienced difficulty in tolerating the taste and texture of the contrast material. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to oral contrast agents. The patient is able to drink liquids without difficulty and is not currently taking any medications that may interfere with the imaging studies. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in this study to compare the newly available oral contrast material (Breeza) to the standard-of-care oral contrast material (VoLumen).

52 yo F with history of metastatic BRAF+ melanoma, currently on dabrafenib and trametinib combination therapy. She has previously received immunotherapy with anti-PD-1 and anti- CTLA-4 inhibitors. The patient presents with persistent fever (grade 2) for two days, along with nausea and mild headache. Lab work shows elevated CRP levels. The patient has an ECOG score of 1 and has provided informed consent for the study. She has no history of autoimmune disease or known allergies to tocilizumab.

54-year-old male with alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) within the Milan criteria is being considered for liver transplantation. His MELD score is 20, and he has been on the waiting list for 6 months. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not have a history of diabetes or any other significant medical conditions. He has been informed that he may be eligible for a clinical trial involving the use of a hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) technique for liver transplantation with extended criteria donor (ECD) grafts. He is interested in the trial and willing to provide written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedure. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. His BMI is 28, and his liver biopsy shows mild macrosteatosis (10%). He is affiliated with the French social security system and is willing to undergo primary liver transplantation using an ECD graft from a brain-dead donor.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of relapsing-onset multiple sclerosis (MS) presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up. She has been on first-line disease modifying therapy (DMT) with glatiramer acetate for the past 7 years and has not experienced any relapses or new lesions for the past 5 years. The patient reports no significant side effects from the medication and has been adherent to the treatment regimen. She is interested in exploring the possibility of discontinuing the medication to avoid long-term exposure to potential side effects. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess whether it is safe to discontinue treatment and the potential impact on her quality of life. She has not switched between first-line DMTs and has not been tested positive for neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) for interferon-beta. The patient is willing to undergo blood collections to assess the possibility of predicting inflammatory activity with biomarkers such as neurofilament light (NFL) and provide informed consent for the use of protected health information (PHI) in accordance with national and local privacy regulations.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of acid reflux and occasional abdominal discomfort. He has been scheduled to undergo an upper endoscopy for further evaluation. He has not experienced any respiratory symptoms or fever in the last 2 weeks and has not been in close contact with any known COVID-19 positive individuals. He lives with his wife and two adult children who are healthy and asymptomatic. He has not traveled outside of the country in the last 6 months. He wears a mask when he goes out in public and practices social distancing. He has not been tested for COVID-19 previously. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he does not take any chronic medications. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he denies any recent weight loss or changes in bowel habits. He agrees to participate in the study and undergoes a telephone triage with a pulmonologist to screen for COVID-19 symptoms. He then undergoes serological testing for IgG and IgM antibodies against COVID-19. After testing negative, he undergoes the scheduled endoscopy with strict adherence to the protocol, including isolation in an individual preoperative and recovery room, and the use of PPE by the endoscopy staff.

Patient B is a 9-year-old female who was diagnosed with acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes (AOMT) in her left ear. She has been experiencing ear pain, fever, and difficulty hearing for the past 2 days. She has no history of hearing loss or immunodeficiency disease. Her caregivers are willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all study visits. She is currently not taking any medication for her AOMT. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions.

55 year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus type 2 who was recently admitted to the ICU due to sepsis. He has been receiving insulin therapy for the management of his hyperglycemia but has experienced episodes of hypoglycemia in the past. He has been informed about the GlucoClear CGM System clinical trial and has given his written informed consent to participate. The patient is expected to stay in the ICU for at least 72 hours and has an APACHE II score of 12. He has hyperglycemia with a blood glucose level of 180 mg/dl upon admission to the ICU. The patient has large peripheral veins and is not participating in any other investigational interventional study. He does not have any end-stage pre-existing medical conditions that would preclude him from completing up to 72 hours of glucose monitoring and follow-up. The patient does not have any skin conditions or existing medical instrumentation that would preclude placing the peripheral IV catheters. He has not participated in any other drug, device, or biologic study within the last 30 days that may interfere with this study. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is interested in learning more about cancer prevention and early detection measures. She is an Arkansas resident and is currently enrolled in ARResearch. She has access to a personal cell phone and/or computer. She has no significant medical history, does not smoke, and has no family history of cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and provide feedback on the online module or application. She understands the purpose of the study and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 38-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with prediabetes. She has a history of obesity and has been struggling to lose weight despite following several diets and exercise programs. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2 and her fasting blood glucose level is 115 mg/dL. She has no history of liver or kidney insufficiency, allergies to tomatoes, or other malabsorptive disorders. She does not smoke, and her alcohol consumption is limited to one drink per week. She is not taking any anti-inflammatory drugs, carotenoid-containing or metabolism-altering supplements. She has not been on a special diet or taking nutrient supplements, pre- or probiotics for the past 3 months. She has never been a habitual consumer of salmon or other astaxanthin-rich foods. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if increased consumption of salmon as a whole food and its bioactive compound astaxanthin can help reduce inflammation and improve her metabolic health.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has recently experienced a significant life change, such as a breakup or job loss, which has left her feeling depressed and anxious. She spends a lot of time on her computer and is comfortable using web-based technologies. She has a stable Internet connection and access to a desktop computer. The patient is a native English speaker and is interested in trying new techniques to manage her symptoms. She is open to participating in an online study and is available to commit to the three-week duration of the intervention.

The patient is a 50-year-old female veteran who receives primary care at the Miami Veterans Affairs Healthcare System. She is fluent in English and willing to participate in the study. She has experienced symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, mood swings, and vaginal dryness, for the past year. She is interested in learning more about menopause and its management options. She is willing to register and become authenticated in the patient health portal, MyHealtheVet, and able to use read, understand, and respond to secure messages using the patient health portal. She has no history of any medical condition that would exclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. He presents with a non-healing ulcer on the plantar surface of the right foot for the past 8 weeks. The ulcer is about 1.5 cm2 in size and requires debridement. There are no signs of infection. The patient is currently on insulin and oral medications for the control of blood glucose levels. He is willing and able to make all required study visits and follow the dressing changes at home or with the help of a caregiver. He is willing to use an appropriate off-loading device to keep weight off of the foot ulcer. The patient has an ankle brachial index (ABI) of 0.85, indicating adequate arterial blood flow. The patient has not participated in another clinical trial within the last 30 days and does not have any bleeding disorder that would preclude sharp debridement during the study. He has no contraindications or hypersensitivity to the use of clostridial collagenase or products containing silver. Additionally, the patient's blood counts and blood chemistry values are within normal limits. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial to test the efficacy of SANTYL in the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers.

The patient is a 30-year-old laboratory worker who has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She is in good health as determined by medical history, physical examination and clinical judgment of the investigator. She is not pregnant or nursing (breastfeeding). She is currently using oral hormonal contraceptives as a birth control measure. She has no history of any serious chronic or progressive disease or any impairment/alteration of the immune system resulting from immunosuppressive therapy, immune deficiency disorder, or known HIV infection. She has not received any meningococcal B vaccine before and has not had any known or suspected disease caused by N. meningitidis. She is able to comprehend and follow all required study procedures for the whole period of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 3 years. She has tried multiple antidepressants in the past without success. Her current depressive episode has lasted for approximately 6 months and is characterized by low mood, lack of energy, and feelings of hopelessness. She is currently not taking any psychiatric medication. She lives with her partner and works as a freelance graphic designer. She enjoys spending time with her friends and family but has found it increasingly difficult to engage in activities she once enjoyed. She has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She is willing to be voluntarily admitted to an inpatient research unit at the New York State Psychiatric Institute for baseline PET imaging and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), ketamine infusion, and repeat PET imaging. She is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control during study participation. She does not have any unstable medical or neurological illness, significant electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormality, prior ineffective trial of or adverse reaction to ketamine, or a history of bipolar disorder or current psychotic symptoms. She has not used ketamine in the past. Her weight is within the allowed limit for MRI scanning.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works as a firefighter. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control it. He has been experiencing symptoms of COVID-19 for the past 5 days, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He tested positive for COVID-19 and was admitted to the hospital due to respiratory distress. His X-ray showed radiological evidence of pneumonia. He has no known allergies and has never received immunosuppressant or immunomodulatory therapy. His neutrophil count is within normal range and his platelet count is above 50,000/microliter. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with bilateral knee pain that has worsened over the past year. She describes the pain as a dull ache that is present most of the day and is aggravated by walking, standing, and climbing stairs. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. On physical examination, there is tenderness and crepitus on palpation of both knees with no erythema or warmth. Range of motion is limited due to pain. X-rays of both knees show joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation consistent with osteoarthritis. The Kellgren-Lawrence X-ray grade is 3 for both knees. She reports no history of gastrointestinal disorders or electrocardiogram abnormalities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to examine the pain relief of PH-797804 alone or with naproxen in subjects with osteoarthritis of the knee.

45-year-old male with a history of stage III melanoma, who underwent surgical resection within the last 90 days, with no prior treatment for melanoma other than surgery or regional irradiation. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and has not used biologic response modifiers within 60 days of the first dosing. The patient has no history of other malignancy within the past 5 years except for melanoma. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent the relapse of melanoma and is willing to undergo further evaluation to determine eligibility.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a 5-year history of active rheumatoid arthritis that has not responded adequately to methotrexate (currently on 15mg/week). The patient has a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 15mg/L. The patient has not received any biologic therapy in the previous 12 months and does not have active tuberculosis or any other clinically significant concurrent medical condition. The patient is willing to participate in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ALD518 and able to attend all 11 visits over the course of approximately 16 weeks (excluding the screening period).

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and recommended to undergo coronary artery bypass graft surgery. He has no history of allergies, smoking, or any illicit drug abuse. The patient is in good health, with no significant comorbidities, and has a normal baseline laboratory test. He has been informed about the study and has consented to participate. The patient will be undergoing sternotomy for the coronary artery bypass graft surgery, which makes him eligible for the study. The patient will be followed up for a period of 3 months after surgery to monitor for the occurrence of surgical site infections. The patient will receive standard antibiotic prophylaxis before and after the surgery. The study will evaluate all risk factors before, during, and after surgery to identify specific factors that may contribute to surgical site infections in cardiac surgery. The patient will be informed about the study and given regular updates on the results.

A 30-year-old Japanese man who has been living outside of Japan for the past 5 years came to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is healthy and has no history of significant medical conditions. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 75 kg, giving him a BMI of 24.5 kg/m^2. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not donated sperm in the past 3 months and does not plan to do so during the clinical trial. He is not currently taking any medications, and his medical history is unremarkable. He has no allergies and has not had any recent illnesses. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing severe pain and stiffness in his right hip joint for the past year. He has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried various conservative treatments, including physical therapy and pain medications, but has not experienced significant relief. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of inflammatory or renal diseases. He has never had a hip replacement or any other cobalt-chromium implants. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his quality of life and is willing to provide informed consent. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is randomized into the ceramic-on-metal group. The patient is scheduled to undergo a conventional cementless total hip replacement with a 36mm bearing, and his metal ion serum concentrations and cytokine production will be monitored throughout the study period. Follow-up data of his clinical and radiographic examinations will also be collected.

57-year-old male presented with rectal bleeding and constipation for the past few months. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. He has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. He has no family history of colon cancer or any other malignancy. The patient underwent colonoscopy which revealed a large mass in the rectum at 7 cm from the anal verge. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies including pelvic MRI and CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of metastatic disease, and the tumor was considered to be locally advanced. The patient is scheduled for neoadjuvant chemoradiation therapy prior to surgical resection. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, and understands the written informed consent document and is willing to sign it. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 65 mLs/min.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of thyroid cancer. The patient has a family history of thyroid disease but has not experienced any symptoms until recently. She underwent a thyroid ultrasound which revealed a nodule and a subsequent biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of thyroid cancer. The patient is scheduled to undergo a thyroidectomy and cervical node dissection to remove the cancer. She is currently taking thyroid hormone replacement therapy for hypothyroidism. The patient is in good health with no other medical conditions and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has never participated in any clinical trials before and is interested in participating in this study to potentially reduce the risk of post-surgical complications.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago. She underwent an autologous stem cell transplant, but unfortunately, she experienced a relapse. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is currently taking lenalidomide and dexamethasone. Her lab results show that her creatinine level is within normal range, as well as her liver function tests. She reports no gastrointestinal symptoms and is able to swallow oral medication without difficulty. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the feasibility of MLN9708 as maintenance therapy following allogeneic stem cell transplant in patients with multiple myeloma. She understands the nature of the study and is willing to give written informed consent.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is in her 38th week of pregnancy. She has had a healthy pregnancy and has no history of high-risk pregnancy. She plans to breastfeed her newborn and has no nipple abnormalities. She is excited to participate in the study that aims to explore the relationship between the onset of maternal and child skin contact and the relationship between neonatal milk, mother's willingness to breastfeed and parent-child attachment. Her baby's estimated weight is between 2500-4000 grams. She has no major bleeding during production and her baby has no neonatal life signs abnormality or neonatal oral structure abnormalities. She is willing to be randomized into either the control group or the experimental group and is committed to completing the study.

The patient is a 50 year old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two months ago. He underwent myeloablative conditioning and received an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from his younger brother as a donor. He is currently being treated at a hematology department in Paris. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are managed with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two children, both of whom are in college. He works as an accountant in a small firm and is currently on sick leave due to his treatment. He is fluent in French and English. He has given his written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 63 year old woman who has been postmenopausal for 5 years. She has a BMI of 25 and weighs 70 kg. She is in generally good health and takes no regular medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol regularly. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. She has no history of diabetes, renal or hepatic disease, myocardial infarction, or any other major medical conditions. She has not donated blood in the past 56 days. She is willing and able to give written informed consent and understands the requirements of the study. She is interested in participating in clinical research to help advance medical knowledge.

Samantha is a 35 year old woman who was diagnosed with bipolar I disorder three years ago. She has been taking prescribed medication for the past year and has had stable mood swings. Samantha is fluent in English and has an 11th-grade education. She has no known allergies and is not pregnant or lactating. She does not have any neurological disorder or HIV. Her current Young Mania Rating Scale Score is 8 and her Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale Score is 6. Samantha is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve cognitive abilities in persons with bipolar disorder. She is willing to provide informed, competent and written consent for the trial.

56 year old woman residing in a rural area with limited access to mental health care. She presents with a history of depression for the past 6 months, with symptoms including persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, difficulty sleeping, and feelings of worthlessness. She has not received any treatment for her depression and does not have an on-site mental health specialist available to her. She has access to a telephone and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have a history of bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders, drug or alcohol dependence, cognitive impairment, or terminal illness. She is not currently being treated by a mental health specialist and does not have a court-appointed guardian. She speaks English fluently.

A 32-year-old female with a long history of refractory partial onset epilepsy presents with a complaint of persistent seizures despite being on multiple anti-epileptic drugs. She has been experiencing an average of 2 seizures per month for the past 6 months. She is fluent in English and has no known history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is not pregnant and is using a reliable form of contraception. She has no prior history of psychiatric disorders requiring hospitalization, suicidal thoughts or intent in the last 6 months, or use of antidepressant, anxiolytic, or antipsychotic agents. She has not suffered from any traumatic brain injury in the last 6 months and has no history of cardiac arrhythmia. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and cooperate fully with the neuropsychological testing.

35 year old male diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) for 5 years who experiences joint pain and stiffness in the spine and peripheral joints. He has difficulty with activities of daily living, such as dressing and bathing, and has been relatively sedentary due to pain and fatigue. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate his physical performance through the Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test (KPET) and to better understand his limitations in comparison to the control group. The patient has no history of cardiac disease, stroke, asthma or COPD, deformities that may prevent exercise, hypertension, or other conditions that would preclude his participation. He is enthusiastic about participating in the study and is eager to learn more about his physical capabilities.

A 55 year old man with a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease presented with stiffness, tremors and difficulty in walking. His symptoms are in the early stages (Hoehn & Yahr stage 2). His medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He is currently taking levodopa-carbidopa, pramipexole and metformin. He is physically active and enjoys swimming and hiking but has noticed a decline in his physical abilities. He has no cardiovascular contraindications to aerobic exercise and is not reliant on a walker or wheelchair. He is willing to participate in a supervised exercise program and is looking for ways to improve his overall health and quality of life.

32-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester with a diagnosis of fetal intrauterine growth restriction, currently receiving prenatal care. She has no history of preterm labor or preterm delivery. She speaks fluent English and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no contraindications for fetal heart monitoring and has not been taking any selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) during pregnancy.

A 42-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with infiltrative breast cancer through a core biopsy. She is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove the sentinel lymph node (SLN). The aim of this study is to evaluate the performance of a double labelling method using isotope and methylene blue dye injection to precisely localize the SLN. This will involve the injection of methylene blue dye and lymphoscintigraphy prior to surgery to locate the SLN. After surgery, the SLN will be analyzed through serial analysis and immunohistochemistry. The study aims to compare the two methods and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the complete procedure. The patient will need to meet the eligibility criteria which includes approval and informed consent. She should not have received chemotherapy or locoregional radiotherapy and should not have a prevalent axillary lymph node.

A 54 year old woman presents with severe headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty with balance. She has a history of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, which was previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation. MRI and lumbar puncture confirm the diagnosis of recurrent brain lymphoma with lymphomatous meningitis. Pathology analysis of the tumor tissue shows that the tumor cells are CD20+. The patient has an Ommaya reservoir (ventricular access device) and has recovered from any reversible toxicities caused by prior treatment. She has sufficient baseline hematologic function with granulocyte count of 2,000 and platelet count of 80,000 per ul. She has not had whole brain or craniospinal irradiation or intrathecal chemotherapy within the past 4 days. She does not have HIV infection.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who underwent a craniotomy for a left-sided subdural hematoma following a fall. He is currently being managed in the neurosurgical intensive care unit and requires mechanical ventilation. The patient has an intracranial pressure monitoring device in place and is hemodynamically stable. The patient has no known history of pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum. The patient has no known coagulopathies or thrombocytopenia. The patient has no known esophageal or nasopharyngeal pathology that would preclude placement of an esophageal balloon catheter. The patient has no known planned change in the external ventricular drain set point during the pre-intervention, intervention or post-intervention periods. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who has been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa and is currently enrolled in residential-level treatment at The Emily Program. She has a BMI of less than 18.5, and has been experiencing symptoms related to her eating disorder. She has no history of substance abuse or neurological disorders. The patient speaks English fluently and is able to comprehend testing procedures. She has not undergone any craniotomy or other surgery that would prevent her from undergoing tDCS or MRI scans. She has not recently been discharged from a residential treatment setting due to medical need for inpatient-level care. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

Patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Huntington's Chorea, a rare genetic disorder that causes uncontrollable movements and psychiatric symptoms. He has been experiencing involuntary jerking movements of his limbs and face, difficulty with balance and coordination, and mood swings. He has been taking medication to manage his symptoms, but they have not been effective. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive bone marrow derived autologous mononuclear cells (MNCs) to improve his symptoms. He is willing to undergo the therapy and is able to comprehend the protocol and give informed consent. He is also able and willing to make regular visits to the hospital for protocol procedures and follow-up. The patient has no history of immunodeficiency, allergies, or immune-mediated reactions. He is not a heavy drinker or drug user and does not have any severe skin infections. The patient's diabetes is well-controlled with insulin and he does not have any neurological disease caused by autoimmune or genetic factors.

A 54-year-old man with end-stage renal disease is scheduled for kidney transplantation from a living-unrelated donor. He has been on hemodialysis for 2 years and has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is non-smoker and non-alcoholic. His BMI is 28.4 kg/m². His panel reactive antibodies (PRA) are 25%. He has no history of autoimmune disease. His serum creatinine level is 8 mg/dL, and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 5 mL/min/1.73m². He has no history of acute rejection or opportunistic infections. He is currently on a lipid-lowering medication and insulin. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

A 14-month-old boy from a rural community in Limela, Machinga District, Malawi, was brought to the local clinic by his mother for a routine check-up. He is the youngest child of a family of five, and his mother is a subsistence farmer. The child was born at home and has had all of his vaccinations up to date. He is exclusively breastfed by his mother, but he has recently started showing interest in solid foods. The child's mother reports that he has had occasional diarrhea and has been slow to gain weight. The child's weight-for-age Z-score (WAZ) is -2.5, and his height-for-age Z-score (HAZ) is -1.8. The child does not have any signs of severe acute malnutrition or edema. The mother is willing to participate in the study and return for follow-ups.

A 45 yo F diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 5 years ago. She has been on methotrexate with minimal improvement in her symptoms. She has 8 tender and 9 swollen joints currently. Her CRP level is 2.1mg/L. She has been taking hydroxychloroquine and methotrexate for the last 3 months at a stable dose. She is currently on a stable dose of 5mg prednisone for the last 2 weeks. She is interested in starting a biologic agent for RA and has been prescribed Enbrel by her physician. She is able and willing to wear a wrist actigraphy band to measure her rest-activity circadian rhythms. She has no medical conditions that would prevent her from completing the study.

This is a 45-year-old female who has a history of high blood pressure but is currently well-controlled on medication. She has no history of diabetes and her HbA1C levels are within normal limits. She is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine-containing products. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is not taking any medications that alter peripheral vascular control. She has no history of allergies to latex or investigative substances. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of cheese consumption on blood vessel function. She is willing to undergo four 8-day controlled feeding periods where she will consume either cheese or no cheese along with a low-sodium or high-sodium base-diet. She will also undergo microdialysis experiments and brachial artery flow-mediated vasodilation tests to assess the function of her blood vessels before and after each feeding period.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of severe coronary artery disease. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is scheduled to undergo coronary artery bypass surgery due to severe blockages in his coronary arteries. He is taking several medications including aspirin, metformin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild bilateral ankle edema. His lab results are within normal limits except for an elevated HbA1c of 7.5%. He is willing to participate in the study and allow a small biopsy to be taken from his heart during surgery.

A 45-year-old male kidney transplant recipient is experiencing reduced exercise tolerance and general wellbeing. His ferritin level is ≤100 ug/L and transferrin saturation is ≤20%. He has been on immunosuppressive therapy since his transplant surgery and takes several medications to manage his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. He has a history of smoking but has quit since his kidney transplant surgery. He is generally in good health, with no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve his exercise tolerance and quality of life.

The patient is a 35 year-old female who is considering abdominoplasty to address excess skin and fat in her abdominal area. She has no known medical conditions that affect wound healing and has not undergone any previous abdominoplasty or bariatric surgery. She has a BMI of 26, which is within the eligibility criteria for the study. She has never had keloid formation or hypertrophic scarring, nor is she taking systemic steroids or immunosuppressive agents. She does not smoke and has not used any nicotine products within the past 30 days. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and schedules and is available for follow-up evaluations for the duration of the study. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is willing to follow instructions for incision and drain care.

Patient is a 9-year-old child who has been admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with suspected staphylococcal or streptococcal infection. The child has a systolic arterial pressure below the 5th percentile for their age and has been unresponsive to fluid resuscitation. There is a strong suspicion of toxic shock syndrome (TSS) based on the CDC criteria, including the presence of at least one sign of hypo perfusion. The child has no known hypersensitivity to any of the components of the study treatment or placebo and has health coverage. Consent to participate in the study will be obtained from the child's parents or legal guardian. The child has not had any signs of shock for more than 24 hours and does not have any known immunodeficiency or is not taking any immunosuppressive drugs.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been visiting the same dental practice for the past five years. She has had several cavities filled during that time and is concerned about the continued progression of tooth decay. She has a history of diabetes, but it is well-controlled. She takes medication for high blood pressure but has no other significant medical conditions. Her dental habits include brushing twice a day and flossing regularly, but she admits to occasionally snacking on sweets throughout the day. She is interested in participating in the study to see if her dental health can be improved through the use of CAMBRA principles. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and protocol and is excited to learn more about how she can prevent further dental decay.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 3 years ago. She has been on insulin pump therapy for 2 years and currently using insulin lispro. She has experienced several episodes of hypoglycemia in the past 6 months but has not had any seizures or loss of consciousness. She has no history of heart disease, altitude sickness or chronic pulmonary conditions. She is currently taking no other medications. She is willing to wear a continuous glucose sensor and physiological monitor for the duration of the study. She has not had a febrile illness in the past 24 hours and is not pregnant. She is able to travel to the ski resort for the 72-hour ski admission and attend the 5 study visits over about 2 weeks.

Pt is a 45yo M with a 9-month history of progressive weakness and muscle atrophy, initially noticed in his right hand and now involving his right arm and shoulder. He also reports occasional twitches in his arms and legs. He denies any sensory symptoms or bowel/bladder dysfunction. He has a family history of ALS, with his father being diagnosed at age 55. On exam, he has significant weakness in his right arm, with decreased muscle bulk and fasciculations. He has brisk reflexes and upgoing toes bilaterally. He is able to walk without assistance, but with a slightly wide-based gait. His speech and swallowing are normal. EMG/NCS studies showed evidence of chronic and active denervation in his right upper and lower extremities, with a decreased recruitment pattern. He has normal sensory studies. MRI of the brain and cervical spine are unremarkable. He meets the El Escorial criteria for possible ALS.

The patient is a 45-year-old office worker who complains of chronic neck pain for the past year. The pain is described as a constant dull ache with occasional sharp stabbing pain that radiates to the shoulders and upper back. The pain is intensified by prolonged sitting and computer work. The patient reports a score of 15 on the NDI (Neck Disability Index) and 5 on the NPRS (Numeric Pain Rating Scale). The patient experiences restricted movements of the neck and has difficulty turning the head to the right and left. The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of rheumatic disease, cervical myelopathy, tumors, vertebrobasilar insufficiency, or neurological disorders. There is no history of major trauma, fracture, or surgery in the neck, shoulder, or upper limb. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of vertebral manipulation and pain education on chronic neck pain.

A 25-year-old male patient diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus at the age of 16. The patient is currently on a multiple daily injection (MDI) insulin regimen and has been struggling with poor glycemic control. The patient's latest Hemoglobin A1C (A1C) reading was 9.5%, indicating that the current insulin regimen is not effectively controlling blood sugar levels. The patient is willing and able to perform self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) and keep a study diary. The patient has not used any SGLT inhibitors in the past 8 weeks and has no history of severe hypoglycemic events or diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in the past 6 months. The patient has given written informed consent and is willing to use an adequate method of contraception if female. The patient is excited about participating in the study to potentially improve glycemic control and manage their diabetes better.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure. He has been experiencing symptoms of heart failure, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his ankles, for the past year. He has been treated with diuretics for the past 6 months and has been hospitalized twice for heart failure in the past year. His latest BNP value was 200 pg/ml in normal sinus rhythm. He has been managed with guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for the past 4 weeks without any significant changes in his medication regimen. His latest echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 45% within the past 3 months. He has not had any recent myocardial infarction or percutaneous cardiac intervention within the past 3 months. He has not had cardiac resynchronization therapy initiated within the past 6 months. He is not on the cardiac transplant waiting list. He is able to perform a 6-minute walk test with a distance of 350 meters. He does not have any significant valve disease or untreated carotid artery stenosis that would require intervention. His estimated-GFR is 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 by CKD-Epi equation.

We are seeking healthy adults, COPD-like patients, and patients with COPD to participate in a study investigating respiratory performance. For those who are COPD-like or have COPD, symptoms such as coughing, sputum production, and dyspnea must have been present for at least 3 months and for more than 2 years. Participants must be aged 20 years or older and not currently undergoing treatment for any comorbidities related to COPD. Additionally, participants must not have any postural asymmetries, chronic nonspecific lumbopelvic pain, gynecological or abdominal surgery in the previous year, neurological or inflammatory disorders, or any conditions that may interfere with data collection. Participants will undergo body composition measurements, pulmonary function tests, and assessments of respiratory muscle force and voluntary cough performance. We hypothesize that there will be significant differences between the three groups in terms of respiratory performance and that correlations between various variables will be further investigated.

10-year-old female diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in the last month. Cytogenetic analysis confirmed the presence of the translocation t(9;22)(q34;q11) and the patient is currently in the chronic phase of CML. She has not received any prior treatment for CML except for hydroxyurea, which was discontinued one week before beginning treatment with imatinib mesylate. She has no extra-medullary disease except for mild hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. She has a Lansky score of 80 and effective contraception is in place as she is pre-pubertal. The patient and her family have provided written informed consent for participation in the study. She has no other significant medical history and no significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, or neurological conditions of grade >2 (WHO). She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is expected to be compliant with the study follow-up requirements. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with heart failure and has a history of life-threatening ventricular tachyarrhythmias. He is scheduled to undergo implantation of a St. Jude Medical SJ4 system as per ACC/AHA/HRS guidelines. The patient is willing to participate in this study and able to comply with the prescribed follow-up test and schedule of evaluations. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with the study, and he is not currently participating in any other clinical investigation with an active treatment arm.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with severe congenital haemophilia A with less than 1% activity of Factor VIII. He has a documented history of at least 150 exposure days to other FVIII products. He weighs 70 kg and is 5'11" tall. He is not HIV positive, and his CD4+ count is normal. He does not have any other congenital or acquired coagulation disorders. His platelet count is within normal laboratory ranges. His ALAT and creatinine levels are normal. He is not on any immune modulating or chemotherapeutic medications. He is willing to participate in the trial and comply with study procedures.

A 38-year-old woman presents with a history of psoriasis vulgaris affecting her trunk and limbs for the past 5 years. Her past medical history is only significant for seasonal allergies and she is not on any medication for it. She has a family history of psoriasis in her mother and two siblings. She has tried various topical treatments in the past including corticosteroids and emollients, but the effectiveness has been limited. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Her physical examination reveals erythematous, scaly patches on her trunk and limbs. Her BP: 120/80, HR: 75/min and BMI: 25. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness or organomegaly. The lower extremities are normal with no edema. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different treatment regimens for psoriasis vulgaris.

A 4-year-old Caucasian male with no significant past medical history presents to the clinic for a scheduled tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy procedure due to recurrent tonsillitis and sleep apnea. He is generally healthy with no upper respiratory symptoms or signs of mental retardation. He has no known allergies to any medications, and his physical exam is unremarkable. He is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologist physical status I. The patient's parents have been informed about the study and have given their consent for their child to participate. The child will be randomized to receive either sevoflurane and remifentanil or a different inhalation agent and remifentanil to determine if the lower minimum alveolar concentration of sevoflurane will reduce the incidence of emergency agitation during the procedure.

A 35-year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 42.5 kg/m2 presented to the bariatric surgery clinic for evaluation. She had a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea, all of which were poorly controlled despite multiple medications. The patient had attempted various weight loss diets in the past but was unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. She was scheduled for a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery and was advised by her healthcare provider to follow a very low-calorie liquid diet for two weeks prior to the surgery. The patient was initially hesitant as she had never tried a liquid diet before and was concerned about the feasibility and efficacy of such a diet. However, after discussing the potential benefits of pre-surgical weight loss, she agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She had no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She had no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She was counseled by a registered dietitian and provided with a sample meal plan that included three liquid meal replacements and one healthy solid meal per day, totaling to 800 kcal/day. She was instructed to drink at least 64 ounces of water per day and to avoid any solid foods, sugary drinks, and high-fat foods during the study period. The patient was closely monitored by the healthcare team throughout the study period to ensure compliance and to monitor for any adverse effects.

Sarah is a 13-year-old girl with Down syndrome who loves reading books and spending time with her family. She has a receptive language age estimate of 5 years as measured on the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test- 4th Edition (PPVT-IV; Dunn & Dunn, 2006) and is currently attending middle school. Sarah has some difficulty with communication and relies on an aided AAC system to supplement her spoken communication. She is able to navigate her communication device with some assistance and enjoys using it to communicate her thoughts and ideas. Sarah has no history of uncontrolled seizures or any significant sensory or peripheral impairments that might affect her performance. Her parents are excited about the opportunity for Sarah to participate in this study and are willing to bring her to all the required appointments.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer six months ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection, followed by adjuvant radiation therapy. Her tumor was found to be HER2-positive, and she was started on trastuzumab for the adjuvant treatment, which she completed three months ago. Unfortunately, she has now developed metastatic disease with multiple lung and liver lesions detected on imaging. She has no significant past medical history, no known allergies, and is currently using birth control pills. Her performance status is 1, and she has a life expectancy of at least 12 months. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer, and she meets the inclusion criteria for the trial.

52-year-old female diagnosed with mild pre-perimetric glaucoma with cataract formation in her left eye. The patient has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is seeking cataract surgery to improve her visual acuity and quality of life. The patient has been informed of the option to undergo minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) during the cataract surgery and has agreed to participate in the study. She is willing and able to comprehend informed consent and complete the 4-6 month post-op visit. The patient has a potential postoperative best corrected distance visual acuity (BCDVA) of 20/20 or better in each eye, as assessed by the investigator. She meets all other inclusion criteria, and does not have any exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of chronic heart failure (CHF) and has been admitted to the hospital multiple times for episodes of decompensated CHF. She has been referred to the Heart Failure Nursing Service (HFNS) and is eligible for referral for cardiac rehabilitation. The patient is able to communicate in spoken English and is willing to give informed consent. She does not have any contraindications to participating in cardiac rehabilitation as detailed in the ESC consensus statement. The patient is currently living independently but has reported difficulty with daily activities due to her CHF symptoms, such as shortness of breath and fatigue. She has a supportive family member who is willing to participate in the study as a caregiver. The patient has not previously been recruited for this study.

An 84-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presents to the cardiology service with shortness of breath and chest pain. She has been previously hospitalized for heart failure and has undergone coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The patient lives independently but requires assistance with activities of daily living. She takes multiple medications including lisinopril, atorvastatin, furosemide, and aspirin. Upon admission, she is found to have elevated troponin levels and an electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression. She is diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome and is scheduled for coronary angiography. The patient has expressed willingness to participate in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). She has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and night sweats for the past few months. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which are both well-controlled with medication. She lives alone but has a supportive network of family and friends who help her with daily activities. She is able to perform most activities of daily living independently, but has noticed a decline in her physical function over the past few months. She is interested in participating in the study to help determine the best treatment option for her based on her frailty status. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to be randomized to either Arm A or Arm B.

Lila is a 32 year old woman who has been struggling with opioid addiction for the past 4 years. She has recently undergone inpatient detoxification and is now looking to engage in Buprenorphine/Naloxone (B/N) treatment to help manage her addiction. Lila is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to use the MySafeRx mobile application to help with her daily supervised dosing of B/N. She has a stable living situation and is interested in continuing her treatment after the detox program. Lila is fluent in English and has no cognitive impairment or medical contraindications to B/N. She is not pregnant and is not currently incarcerated or court-ordered to participate in any treatment programs. Lila is excited to be part of the study and hopes that it will help her successfully manage her addiction and prevent future overdoses.

Identical twin sisters, both 25 years old, are interested in participating in a clinical trial studying the genetic control and immune system function in twins with and without allergic disease. One sister has a history of seasonal allergies and the other sister has no known allergies. They are both in good health, have no chronic medical conditions, and have not had any recent surgeries. They are willing to provide blood samples for research purposes.

Emily is a 32 year old woman who is 18 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a naturally conceived, single pregnancy, and her pre-conception BMI was 32. She recently had a new OB complete blood count (CBC) which showed that she is at risk for iron deficiency anemia (Hb 11.0 - 12.0 g/dL in the first trimester) and has fluency in English to provide consent and complete study procedures. She doesn't have any history of IDA requiring high dose supplemental iron or any allergy to milk proteins or wheat. She is not a vegan and has no history of bariatric surgery or any inflammatory bowel disease. She is not a regular smoker or alcoholic and doesn't use any illicit drugs. She doesn't have any hematologic disorder or trait carrier and doesn't use any regular medication that may interfere with nutrient absorption. She owns a smartphone and is willing to comply with the interventions.

28 yo female, primigravida, with a diagnosis of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) at 32 weeks gestation presents to the clinic for enrollment in a clinical trial. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She denies tobacco, alcohol or drug use. She has no contraindications to MRI. She understands the study and has signed the informed consent form. She will be randomized to either the treatment group, consisting of daily intake of 8 oz of pomegranate juice, or the placebo group, consisting of daily intake of 8 oz of pomegranate-free juice placebo that matches taste, calories, and appearance to regular pomegranate juice but lacks polyphenols. She will keep a daily diary documenting her compliance and will be followed up on a weekly basis to assess compliance. A detailed diet history will be collected at the time of enrollment, midway through the 3rd trimester and at the time of delivery. Cord blood will be collected upon delivery and sent for ellagic acid, a polyphenic component. All placental material will be sent for formal pathological exam and analyzed for markers of placental injury. If clinically stable, the infant will receive MRI evaluations to evaluate for possible brain injury.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has been a smoker for 25 years. She presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. CT scan reveals metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with bone metastases. The biopsy confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has no history of autoimmune diseases, and her performance status is 1. Her lab study results show: CEA: 72 ng/ml, CRP: 2.1 mg/L, LDH: 465 U/L, hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL, platelets: 220,000/mm3, creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL, and albumin: 3.5 g/dL. She has no history of prior systemic treatment for advanced non-small cell lung cancer. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. Her social security is compliant with the French law (Loi Jardé). She has signed and dated written informed consents prior to any study specific procedure.

A 35 year-old female with a history of asthma presents with recurrent exacerbations within the last year that required oral corticosteroid treatment for at least 3 days. She has a current blood eosinophil level of 600/μl and airway reversibility of 20% to beta-agonist administration. She has an ACQ score of 2.2 at the screening and baseline visits. She is currently taking inhaled fluticasone at a dosage of 1100 μg daily and has been on a stable dose of oral corticosteroids (prednisone 10mg/day) for the past 2 months. The patient is surgically sterile and has a negative pregnancy test. She provides written informed consent and is in good health except for her asthma. She has no other significant medical conditions that would interfere with the study schedule or procedures. She has not participated in any other investigative drug or device study within the last 30 days and has not participated in any investigative biologics study within the last 6 months.

A 60-year-old Caucasian man with a history of follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma complains of recurrent symptoms despite previous chemotherapy. He has a history of palpable nodes on the neck and groin, and a recent PET scan showed enlarged nodes in the chest and abdomen. He has no history of cardiac disease, hepatitis, or HIV. He is married with two adult children and works as a teacher. He reports fatigue, night sweats, and occasional fevers. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He had previously received anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and interferon alpha, but the disease progressed. His Hb is 12.5 g/dL, WBC is 5.5 x 10^9/L, and platelet count is 150 x 10^9/L. He has a performance status of 1 according to the WHO criteria. He has frozen biopsy material available for central pathology review and molecular biology studies. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to try a new treatment regimen.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of ischemic heart disease and recurrent episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia. He has been implanted with an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) for sudden cardiac death prevention. Despite receiving antiarrhythmic therapy, he continues to experience recurrent episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia, which has led to multiple activations of the ICD. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 30%, and he has been referred for a 3D mapping and radiofrequency ablation of the ventricular tachycardia myocardial substrate. The patient is willing and able to undergo the procedure and understands and signs the informed consent. He meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 10 years ago. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. She is currently taking metformin and amlodipine for her diabetes and hypertension, respectively. She has been hospitalized for pneumonia and will be staying for at least 5 days. She has never received insulin treatment and is not currently prescribed any rapid-acting insulin. She is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 32-year-old female with a history of occasional wheezing and shortness of breath. She has never been diagnosed with asthma but has experienced these symptoms intermittently for the past year. She does not have a history of smoking or exposure to environmental pollutants. She has not used any asthma medications in the past. Her most recent spirometry showed an FEV1 of 85% predicted post bronchodilator and a PC20 methacholine of 6 mg/ml indicating airway hyperresponsiveness. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study small airway disease and hopes to gain a better understanding of her symptoms.

We are seeking healthy male and female volunteers aged 18 to 55 years old, with suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture, and a body mass index between 19 and 30 kg/m2. Females must have a negative pregnancy test and be of non-childbearing potential. Male volunteers should be willing to use barrier contraception during the study period. Participants must not have a history of gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of drugs. Additionally, participants must not have a history of psychiatric disorders, depression, bipolar disorder, use of psychoactive medication or electroconvulsive therapy in the 6 months prior to dosing, or a history of seizures or severe dystonic reaction to other drugs. Participants must not have a history of syncope, fainting, vasovagal reactions, arrhythmias, or postural hypotension. Participants must also not have a positive result on screening for serum hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
