If you meet these criteria, you may be eligible to participate in this single ascending dose study to assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of AZD4451.

A 42-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with HER2-positive invasive breast carcinoma after feeling a lump in her left breast. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and imaging studies showed no evidence of metastatic disease. She has no significant medical history and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is normal as determined by echocardiography. The patient has signed informed consent and has adequate organ function with an absolute neutrophil count >1500/mm3, Hgb >9.0 g/dl and platelet count >100,000/mm3. Total bilirubin, creatinine, serum glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase(SGOT)(AST), serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase(SGPT)(ALT), and Alkaline Phosphatase are all within the range allowing for eligibility. She has not received prior chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, biologic therapy, investigational agent, targeted therapy or radiation therapy for her breast cancer. She has no history of previous or current malignancy at other sites, with the exception of adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. She is over 18 years old and has a negative serum pregnancy test performed within 7 days prior to the start of treatment. She agrees to use adequate contraception (barrier method of birth control) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation.

This is a 52 year old male who presented with progressive weight gain, central obesity, hypertension, and easy bruising. Laboratory tests revealed elevated 24-hour urine free cortisol levels and low-dose dexamethasone suppression test results consistent with Cushing’s disease. MRI revealed a pituitary microadenoma that was confirmed with a subsequent pituitary gland biopsy. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He reports mild difficulty with memory and concentration which has been worsening over the past year. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand the effects of cortisol on brain structure and function and hopes to contribute to advancing knowledge on the role of cortisol in cognitive dysfunction.

A 56-year-old Japanese male who suffered a cerebral infarction within the last 14 days to less than 1 year with a stable nervous system for more than 24 hours. The patient has no history of cerebral hemorrhage, transient ischemic attack, progressive stroke or cardiogenic cerebral embolism. The patient is willing to complete all study-related procedures and adhere to dosing and visit schedules. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the study drug, is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use a medically accepted method of contraception. The patient's platelet count is above 100,000/mm^3, and the patient has no history of bleeding diathesis or evidence of active abnormal bleeding within 30 days before obtaining consent. The patient's renal and hepatic function is normal and there is no known impairment. The patient is not scheduled to have any contraindicated procedures or combination therapy during the study period.

A 34-year-old Caucasian woman has been diagnosed with papular-pustular rosacea for the past 2 years. Despite various treatments such as systemic antibiotics and topical therapy, she has been resistant to standard therapy for the past 3 months. She presents with at least 10 papules and/or pustules on her face, with some redness and flushing. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraceptive methods throughout the study duration. She has no known hepatic impairment or history of hypersensitivity to isotretinoin. She has no known allergies to soy oil and is not taking tetracycline. She is not currently participating in any other study and is able to comply with the study requirements. She is seeking treatment for her rosacea and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of isotretinoin.

A 23-year-old healthy female who works as a nurse and has no history of chronic or acute medical conditions. She is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant during the study duration. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses oral contraception. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and does not use any illicit substances or nicotine products. Her BMI is within the range of 18 - 30 kg/m2. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, drug allergies or sensitivity to ibuprofen. She has not donated blood in the past 3 months and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 4 months. She has not used any over-the-counter drugs, herbal remedies, or supplements in the past 7 days and is willing to continue avoiding them during the study period. She has normal serum biochemistry, haematology and urine examination values. She has no clinically significant abnormality in the 12-lead ECG. She is fluent in English and able to communicate well with the investigator. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. He has undergone several months of chemotherapy and there has been no detectable spread of his tumor on imaging studies following the chemotherapy course. The patient is currently in good condition with Zubrod performance status 1. He has no distant metastasis based on the minimum diagnostic workup including an abdominal/pelvic CT scan and chest CT scan. The patient has not received any prior invasive malignancy except non-melanomatous skin cancer. He is not currently on any medication that would interfere with the study. The patient is willing to receive radiation therapy and concurrent chemotherapy, with the ability to swallow oral medications. He must have had at least 4 months of prior systemic chemotherapy. The patient must provide study-specific informed consent prior to study entry. He is not currently pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study. The patient must practice adequate contraception if sexually active. The patient has not undergone any major surgery within the past 28 days prior to study entry. He has no severe active co-morbidity, which includes any unresolved bowel or bile duct obstruction. The patient is not currently participating in another clinical treatment trial while on study.

Pt is a 28yo M or F, who is a non-treatment-seeking alcohol-experienced volunteer (to include military service members, veterans and/or civilians) with no history of substance use disorders other than alcohol or nicotine. Pt must score <10 on the revised clinical institute withdrawal assessment for alcohol scale (CIWA-Ar) assessed in the context of a blood alcohol level (BAL) ≤ 0.02% to demonstrate that they do not need medical detoxification. Pt must have blood laboratory test results within acceptable limits (normal range as noted per protocol). Pt must also have normal vitals (heart rate 60-100 bpm, systolic blood pressure 90-140 millimeter of mercury (mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure 60-90 mmHg); a baseline electrocardiogram (ECG) that demonstrates clinically normal sinus rhythm

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with breast cancer and scheduled for breast surgery at the National Cancer Institute, Cairo University. She has a history of hypertension, for which she takes medication daily. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She does not have any allergies to medications. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2, and she does not have any coagulopathies. She is not currently taking any opioids for chronic pain. She has no history of chronic pain or any other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She has been informed about the study procedures and has provided written informed consent. She will be randomized into one of the two analgesic groups (ESP block or PECs block type II) and will be assessed for postoperative pain intensity and opioid consumption within 24 hours after the surgery. She will be given medications for nausea or vomiting if needed. The primary objective of the study is to evaluate the total morphine consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours, and the secondary objectives include duration of analgesia, postoperative pain scores up to 24 hours postoperative, and occurrence of postoperative nausea and vomiting.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who is scheduled to undergo outpatient surgery for an ear surgery at Nationwide Children's Hospital. She has a history of recurrent ear infections and has been experiencing severe pain and discomfort for the past few months. She has been prescribed opioids for pain management after the surgery. Her parents are concerned about the safe storage and disposal of the unused opioids at home after her recovery. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a novel opioid disposal mechanism, the Deterra® drug deactivation system, to increase proper opioid disposal by families of children undergoing outpatient surgery. They are willing to track their child's pain medication use and complete a follow-up survey to help improve the safe disposal of opioids in the community.

Patient is a 30-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 25. She has no history of chronic illness and does not take any medication. She has a blood pressure of 120/80 mm Hg and no allergies to medicated mouthwash or ingredients in oral products. She has good oral hygiene and no history of periodontal disease or chronic oral complaints. She has not taken antibiotics within the last 3 months, and has no fixed or removable oral appliances or xerostomia. She does not excessively consume alcohol and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to change her dental hygiene routine and avoid using mouthwash during the study. She is available to participate in the study for 20 weeks and is willing to consume up to 70 ml of beetroot juice or a matched volume of placebo beetroot juice daily for 8 weeks. She is comfortable providing a spot urine sample, a stool sample, and a blood sample during the study visits. She is willing to fast overnight before each baseline study visit and refrain from strenuous exercise and alcohol during the study period.

5.5-month-old female infant living in Lungwena area, Mangochi District, rural Malawi. The infant's parents have given their informed consent to participate in the study. The family is a permanent resident of the area and will be available during the period of the study. The infant has no history of peanut allergy and is not currently participating in another clinical trial with intervention to the child. The infant has not been diagnosed with severe illness warranting hospital referral and does not have a weight-for-height z-score below -2.0 or presence of oedema.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been a smoker for more than 20 years. He has a history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of heart disease, stroke, or any other significant medical conditions. He is married and lives with his wife in a suburban area. He works as a retired accountant and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He has received an invitation to participate in the English AAA Screening Programme and is considering whether to participate. He has not had any previous screening for AAA and is unsure about the benefits and risks of the screening. He is generally in good health and has no significant concerns about his health, but is open to participating in the study if it can provide more information about the safety and feasibility of a targeted approach to AAA screening.

The patient is a 32 year old man who has been suffering from allergic rhinitis (AR) for the past 5 years. He experiences sneezing, itching, and congestion in his nose and throat, and his eyes become red and watery. The symptoms are worse during the spring and fall seasons. He has tried over-the-counter allergy medications, but they provide only temporary relief. He recently consulted an allergist who recommended allergen immunotherapy (AIT) as a treatment option. The patient is married and works as an engineer. He has two children, aged 4 and 6 years, and enjoys spending time with them on the weekends. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not exercise regularly. His medical history is unremarkable, and he takes no medications other than occasional antihistamines for his AR symptoms. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance scientific knowledge about the effectiveness of AIT in treating AR.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 6. She lives in a low-income neighborhood with her mother and two younger siblings. Her mother works long hours and struggles to make ends meet, leading to food insecurity and difficulty accessing healthcare. The patient has a history of poor glycemic control with a Hemoglobin A1c of 10.5% at the time of enrollment. She has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to diabetic ketoacidosis and has missed several appointments. The patient attends a local public school and has difficulty managing her diabetes during school hours. She is currently on an insulin pump and takes insulin injections regularly. Despite education and counseling on diabetes management, her mother struggles to help her daughter manage her diabetes due to her own limited health literacy and lack of resources. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and hopes to receive additional support to help her manage her diabetes and avoid hospitalizations.

A 53-year-old female presents with no history of smoking and no previous medical history of cancer, radiotherapy or chemotherapy. She has been living in Tianjin for the past 20 years and has not traveled outside of the region. She has no family history of lung cancer. She is currently asymptomatic and has no complaints. She has not experienced any significant weight loss or changes in appetite. She is a homemaker and is married with two children. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on lung cancer in the Tianjin population.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of psoriasis for the past 10 years. He experiences flares of red, scaly patches on his scalp and nails, as well as in folds of his skin. He has not been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis but has been experiencing some joint pain and stiffness in his hands and feet. He has not had any joint trauma or other significant health issues. He is currently not taking any medications for his psoriasis, but he has used topical creams in the past. He leads an active lifestyle and enjoys playing basketball and hiking. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He has no history of inflammatory or microcrystalline disease, osteoarthritis, or any other rheumatic disease. He has no physical or mental incapacity and is willing to participate in the study.

This is a 55 year old male who recently underwent laparotomy for a ruptured appendix. He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and has no history of lung disease. He is able to understand and follow directions for maximal expiration for measurement of peak expiratory flow meter. He has no known allergies to medical equipment or devices. He has no current pregnancy or plans for pregnancy. He is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo surgery for the removal of the tumor. She has no known allergies and no significant medical history. Her BMI is within the normal range, and she is not insulin-dependent. She has not received neoadjuvant chemotherapy and will not undergo immediate breast reconstruction procedures. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of prophylactic antibiotics in breast cancer surgery to prevent surgical site infections. She has been randomly assigned to the cefazolin group and will receive 2g of cefazolin diluted in 0.9% saline by endovenous. She understands the study's risks and benefits and is willing to provide informed consent. She will be closely monitored for any signs of infection postoperatively.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of metastatic prostate cancer, currently under active medical oncology care. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and has failed or refused all approved lines of therapy for his condition. The patient has progressive disease as evidenced by bone scan, CT, MRI or serum PSA, and a serum prostate specific antigen level of 3 ng/ml at baseline. The patient has no prior history of PSMA radioligand therapy or hemi-body irradiation. He has no impaired organ function as evidenced by laboratory values, and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months as judged by the investigator. The patient is able to tolerate the physical requirements of two PET/CT scans, including lying for up to 30 minutes.

A 45-year-old female patient is scheduled for an elective urological surgery. She has been diagnosed with a recurrent urinary tract infection and her urologist has recommended a surgical intervention. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She denies any history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, substance abuse or hearing loss. She is fluent in German and has given her written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is classified as ASA status II and is within the age range of 18 to 65 years. The patient has not participated in any other clinical investigations and is not taking any centrally acting medication. She is eligible for the study and will be monitored using mid latency auditory evoked potentials during general anesthesia.

The patient is a 42-year-old Chinese male who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis and has been taking a conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drug for the past 3 months, but has had inadequate response to the treatment. He has active arthritis as indicated by 6 tender/painful and 4 swollen joints. He also has active plaque psoriasis, and has not been diagnosed with any other autoimmune rheumatic disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of tofacitinib in treating his condition.

A 25-year-old female of Taiwanese/Chinese ethnic background presenting with symptoms of major depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has a family history of depression and has previously tried multiple antidepressant medications without much success. She is not currently pregnant and agrees to use effective contraception during the study. She does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 6 months, has no active suicidal ideation, and has no allergies to antidepressants. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

58-year-old male with a history of metastatic renal cell carcinoma with clear cell histology and a previous treatment with sunitinib. Despite receiving 14 doses of sunitinib therapy, the patient has experienced radiographic evidence of disease progression defined by RECIST. The patient has been off sunitinib for 14 days prior to day 1 of treatment on the protocol. The patient has been diagnosed with unidimensionally measurable disease based on RECIST criteria, with at least 1 measurable lesion. The patient has an ECOG Performance status of 1. The patient has no history of prior treatment with bevacizumab and has not received systemic therapy other than sunitinib within 4 weeks of starting the study treatment. The patient has no significant vascular disease, bleeding diathesis, or coagulopathy. The patient has no significant psychiatric illness or social situation that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient is willing to undergo the study procedures, including medical history review, vital signs, physical exam, urine analysis, EKG, and CT scan.

A 29-year-old man was recently diagnosed with a brief psychotic disorder and has been experiencing positive symptoms such as delusions of grandeur and suspiciousness. He has been experiencing these symptoms for less than a year and has a PANSS score of 4 or above for delusions, grandiosity, and suspiciousness. He has no history of neurological disorders or intellectual disability. He is currently being followed up in one of the participating hospitals in the study. He is single and lives with his parents. He has a bachelor's degree in engineering and was previously employed in a reputable company before his symptoms started. He is currently not employed due to his illness. He has no history of substance abuse. He is willing to participate in the study and understands that he will be randomly assigned to either the Meta-Cognitive Training (EMC) group or the control group.

A 42-year old woman was diagnosed with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) after experiencing recurrent nosebleeds and shortness of breath. She has a family history of HHT, with her mother and one sibling also being diagnosed with the condition. The patient has previously undergone embolization for AVMs in her lungs and is currently being managed with regular blood transfusions to manage her anemia. She has also experienced gastrointestinal bleeding and has undergone multiple endoscopies to treat the telangiectasias in her stomach and intestines. Despite these interventions, she still experiences symptoms and complications related to her HHT. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She is concerned about the impact of HHT on her quality of life and is interested in participating in research that may help improve treatments for the disease.

A 28-year-old woman with sickle cell disease (SCD) presents with a history of taking hydroxyurea for the past 2 years, which has effectively managed her SCD symptoms. She is currently pregnant and has continued taking hydroxyurea during her pregnancy, despite the contraindication label. She is interested in participating in a study that will document the effects of hydroxyurea exposure during pregnancy and lactation for women with SCD and their babies. She has a history of a previous miscarriage and is determined to have a healthy pregnancy this time around. She is married and has a supportive family. She is currently in her second trimester and has no complications with her pregnancy so far. She plans to breastfeed her baby after delivery and wants to understand the effects of continuing hydroxyurea exposure during lactation. She has access to her medical records and is willing to provide any necessary information for the study.

A 35 year old woman who is a nonsmoker, with a BMI of 23, and no history of alcohol consumption or allergies presents for the study. She has no ocular diseases or recent infections within the last year. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her overall health and immune function. She reports a generally healthy diet and lifestyle with regular exercise. She has not taken any vitamins or food supplements containing lutein for the past 2 months. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the dietary instructions given by the investigators.

The patient is a 29-year-old female who has been experiencing high myopia since she was a teenager. She has been wearing glasses and contact lenses for years, but finds them inconvenient and uncomfortable. She is currently not pregnant, nor is she planning to become pregnant during the course of the trial. She has no preexisting ocular diseases or conditions other than myopia, and no evidence of connective tissue disease or other systemic diseases that may confound the results of the study. Her best spectacle-corrected visual acuity is 20/30 and her refractive error is -6.50D in both eyes. She has a clear central cornea, normal anterior chamber depth of at least 2.8 mm to endothelium, and endothelial cell density more than 2000 cell/mm2. Her pupil diameter is smaller than 7.0 mm under mesopic condition. She has discontinued wearing her soft contact lenses for one week as advised by her ophthalmologist to prepare for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve her vision and quality of life.

This is a 56 year old male with a history of smoking and alcohol use who presented to the ER with difficulty swallowing and weight loss. An endoscopy revealed a large mass at the gastroesophageal junction with biopsy confirming adenocarcinoma. CT scans showed no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient was diagnosed with locally advanced gastroesophageal junction cancer and deemed unresectable due to the extent of the tumor. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for esophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancer. Past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled on medication. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to swallow and retain oral medication. Hematologic, liver, and renal function are all within normal limits. The patient is willing to undergo chemoradiotherapy and has provided archived tumor tissue for biomarker analysis.

A 70-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of pain in both knees, which has been persistent for the last 3 months. She reports difficulty in walking and performing her daily activities due to the pain. She has no history of injury to the knee joint. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication regularly. She denies any history of diabetes, cardiac or respiratory illnesses, and neurological disorders. The patient has not undergone any surgery or treatment for knee pain in the past. On examination, there is tenderness and swelling over the knee joint with reduced range of motion. X-rays show Kellgren and Lawrence score of 3. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her knee osteoarthritis.

An 11-year-old boy with molar incisor hypomineralisation (MIH) was referred to the clinic by his dentist. He has no history of tooth decay or filling on his anterior teeth. He is not undergoing any orthodontic treatment and has no periodontal diseases. He is in good health, and there are no cognitive or behavioural problems. His parents report that he brushes his teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and has a healthy diet. The MIH lesions are located on the labial surface of his permanent central teeth. The boy and his parents are willing to participate in the study and give their informed consent.

A 35-year-old male presents to his rheumatologist with complaints of joint pain and stiffness, which has been present for the last 3 months. He reports that the pain is worse in the morning and improves with activity throughout the day. He also reports intermittent psoriasis for the last 5 years. He has no history of joint pain or swelling in the past. He is a non-smoker and doesn't drink alcohol. On examination, there is swelling in the proximal interphalangeal joints, distal interphalangeal joints, and metacarpophalangeal joints of both hands. There is also tenderness over the lateral epicondyle of the left elbow. Laboratory investigations reveal elevated ESR and CRP. X-ray of the hands shows erosions in the proximal interphalangeal joints and metacarpophalangeal joints. The patient meets the Classification Criteria for Psoriatic Arthritis (CASPAR) criteria for PsA. The patient has not been previously treated with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDS), and therefore, he is eligible for the clinical trial.

A 13-year-old male adolescent, previously participated in a clinical trial in 2007-2008, came to the clinic for follow-up evaluation. He lives with his parents and siblings in a low socio-economic urban area in East Jakarta. He is currently attending junior high school and has no known medical conditions. He has no history of chronic or congenital diseases, tuberculosis, or allergic diseases. He is not taking any medication, including antibiotics, and has not participated in any clinical trials for the past two months. He is willing to participate in the follow-up study and able to give informed consent. He has not been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes and is not taking any cholesterol-lowering drug, anti-diabetic drug, or oral corticosteroid for more than two consecutive weeks in the last three months.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing bilateral eyelid twitching and difficulty opening her eyes for the past year. She reports that the symptoms are worse when she is under stress, anxious, or exposed to bright lights or wind. She has tried botulinum toxin injections in the past, but the effects were short-lived and the symptoms returned. She is willing to undergo surgery to improve her condition. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married and has two adult children. Her occupation is a teacher. She has no history of mental health problems. Her ophthalmologist referred her to participate in this clinical trial to compare two different surgical methods for the treatment of blepharospasm.

40-year-old male with a BMI of 35, who has a history of insulin resistance and is planning to undergo vertical sleeve gastrectomy (VSG) for weight loss. He has no history of diabetes, stroke, or epilepsy. He has no known psychiatric illnesses, nor has a history of alcohol or substance abuse. He is willing to undergo cognitive testing and MRI scans before and after the surgery.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing hair loss for the past 7 months. She has a clinical presentation compatible with alopecia areata and is diagnosed with moderate to severe alopecia areata with a current episode lasting for 7 months. She has a SALT score of 60 indicating that she has lost more than 50% of her scalp hair. She has tried different over-the-counter hair growth products, but none of them have been effective. She has no active inflammation, psoriasis, or seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, but she does have mild dandruff that she treats with a medicated shampoo. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to comply with the dosing schedule and study procedures required for the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old man has been diagnosed with colon cancer and scheduled for a laparoscopic right hemicolectomy. He has a history of hypertension, but otherwise, his medical history is unremarkable. He doesn't smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. The surgery lasted for 3 hours, and the patient was discharged on the 5th postoperative day. The patient had an uneventful postoperative course, and he didn't experience any significant pain or complications. However, he complained of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension, and he didn't pass stool for 3 days after surgery. The patient was diagnosed with postoperative ileus (POI) and received intravenous fluids and electrolytes. He was also started on prokinetic agents and underwent physiotherapy. The patient's symptoms gradually improved, and he was able to pass flatus and stool on the 4th postoperative day. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the use of the SmartPill® to assess the severity and duration of POI after abdominal surgery. He has an estimated operation time of 2 hours and a negative serum pregnancy test. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent, and his ASA score is II.

A 45-year-old man with a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease. He has never been treated for high cholesterol before but was recently diagnosed with LDL-C concentration of 160 mg/dL. He has no history of liver or muscle disease. He is currently not taking any medications for any other condition. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not more than 10 units per week. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is not planning to relocate during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) within the last 5 years. He has a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 70% predicted normal and a partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (PaO2) of 65 mmHg on room air. His hemoglobin-corrected diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 50% predicted normal. He has not had any IPF exacerbations in the past 14 days and has completed any previous treatments for exacerbations. He has no history of connective tissue disease or drug toxicity as the likely cause of interstitial disease. He has not had any clinically significant environmental exposure to known causes of pulmonary fibrosis. He does not have a FEV1/FVC ratio < 0.70 post-bronchodilator and the extent of emphysema on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) is not greater than the extent of fibrosis. He is willing to provide informed consent for study participation.

Patient is a 30yo healthy non-smoking female with a BMI of 24. She has no history of significant medical conditions, surgeries or allergies to medications. She is not currently using any prescription or over-the-counter medications, and has not consumed alcohol or xanthine-containing products in the past 48 hours. She has not had an abnormal diet in the past 30 days and has not participated in an investigational drug study or donated more than 100 mL of blood in the past 30 days. She is willing to remain abstinent or use double-barrier contraception during the study period as she is of childbearing potential. She has provided clinically acceptable results from the screening procedure including blood pressure, heart rate, ECG, physical exam, medical history, hematology, biochemistry, urinalysis, and infection screen. She has signed the written consent form (Research Subject Information and Consent Form) prior to study entry.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past year. She was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) six months ago and has been on stable doses of methotrexate (MTX) for the past three months. She has seropositive RA with a plasma rheumatoid factor level of 30 IU/ml and an anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody level of 60 IU/ml. She has at least 10 swollen joints and 12 tender joints, and her serum C-reactive protein level is elevated at 30 mg/L. She has no history of other autoimmune diseases or complications of RA, and her screening laboratory values are within normal limits. She is not currently taking any other disease-modifying non-biologic anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), but she has been taking low-dose corticosteroids (5 mg/day) and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief. She is postmenopausal and does not plan on becoming pregnant during the study. She has no history of major psychiatric disease, infections, or cardiac disease, and is not taking any medication that may interfere with the study drug. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

57 year old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, status post percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with in-stent restenosis within a "limus"-eluting stent (LES) presenting with recurrent chest pain and dyspnea on exertion. Cardiac catheterization showed significant restenosis of the previously implanted stent. The patient is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy and statin therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to optimize treatment of his in-stent restenosis. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Dyslipidemia - Status post percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with in-stent restenosis within a "limus"-eluting stent (LES) - Chronic kidney disease (Stage 3) - Type 2 diabetes mellitus - Former smoker - No history of malignancy or severe comorbid conditions

A 24-year-old female who is right-handed, healthy, and has been taking oral contraceptives for at least 3 months is eligible for this clinical trial. She has no tattoos on her head or neck, and does not have any non-removable metal on or in her body. She does not abuse alcohol, smoke more than 3 cigarettes per day, or play videogames more than 2 hours per week. She is not a professional athlete and has not taken part in another study involving motor learning or medication in the last 3 months. She does not suffer from migraines, heart rhythm disorders, hypertension, calcium or magnesium deficiency, neurological disorders, chronic metabolic disorders, liver or kidney diseases, immunodeficiency, endocrine disorders, psychiatric disorders, tumors, or injuries to the head and brain.

47-year-old male with a history of knee pain and a recent diagnosis of a meniscal tear. The patient has been scheduled for an arthroscopic menisectomy to alleviate symptoms. He currently takes over-the-counter pain medications as needed for his knee pain. He has no known allergies to medications and has never taken opioids before. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any prescription medications. He reports occasional heartburn but has never been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal issues. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits.

40-year-old woman with a history of chronic depression presents to her psychiatrist with continued social functioning impairment despite adequate medication management. The patient reports feeling sad and hopeless most days, with decreased energy and motivation to perform daily activities. She endorses feelings of worthlessness and guilt, and has difficulty sleeping and concentrating. Despite being on an adequate dose of antidepressant medication for more than 4 weeks, she continues to have difficulty finding employment and feels socially isolated. She reports avoiding social situations and feels like she is missing out on meaningful activities. She has no history of psychotic or eating disorders, bipolar disorder, or substance abuse. She is willing to participate in a brief psychotherapy approach to improve her social and occupational functioning.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and cholesterol. He is a retired accountant and spends most of his day sitting in front of the computer. He has never smoked and only drinks alcohol socially. He is concerned about the risk of stroke associated with atrial fibrillation and is willing to participate in the study to assess his thrombotic status. He is able to understand the patient information sheet and has provided informed consent. He has agreed to comply with the drawing of blood samples for the assessments. He is currently undergoing standard medical therapy for his atrial fibrillation and has been enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B infection for the past 10 years. He was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with multiple nodules and vascular invasion. He is not a candidate for liver transplantation or surgical resection due to the advanced stage of the disease. His Child-Pugh score is A, and he has no evidence of extrahepatic tumor spread or complete portal vein thrombosis. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control it. He has not received any prior transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) or experimental therapies for HCC. He has no history of variceal bleeding or oesophageal varices. His blood tests show normal haematology and biochemistry results. He has a life expectancy of more than three months. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the protocol. He has agreed to use effective means of contraception during the study period. He has not undergone any major surgical procedure or experienced any significant traumatic injury in the past 28 days. He is not currently taking full-dose oral or parenteral anticoagulants. He does not have any serious cardiovascular disease, and his physical examination has not revealed any contraindications to Sorafenib/TACE treatment.

A 55-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse presented to the hospital with abdominal pain and distension. The patient was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis and ascites. A diagnostic paracentesis was performed, and the ascitic fluid analysis showed a PMN count of 200/mm3 and an ascitic protein level of 1.2 g/dL. The patient was prescribed norfloxacin 400mg per day for the prevention of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). After 3 months of treatment, the patient complained of nausea and diarrhea, and the medication was discontinued. The physician is considering switching the patient to ciprofloxacin 750 mg once weekly. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial comparing the efficacy of norfloxacin 400mg per day and ciprofloxacin 750mg once weekly for the prevention of SBP. The patient has no history of antibiotic treatment within the past 2 weeks and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 34-year-old man who was previously diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) and underwent radiation therapy and temozolomide chemotherapy. The patient experienced a recurrence of the GBM and underwent another surgery. The pathology report confirmed the recurrence of GBM. The patient is now seeking alternative treatments and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 80 and no significant medical history, except for hypertension treated with medication. The patient's laboratory values are within normal limits, and the most recent MRI scan shows a recurrent tumor. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 30 days and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient has no known allergies to any compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to ONC201 or its excipients. The patient is willing to comply with study requirements and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 10 year old boy who presented with a painful abscess on his leg. The abscess was drained and a culture was taken, which tested positive for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Additional cultures from his axilla, anterior nares and groin area also tested positive for MRSA, indicating that he is both infected and colonized with the bacteria. The boy is otherwise healthy and has not been hospitalized or received dialysis in the past year. He has not used chlorhexidine or mupirocin in the past month, is not pregnant, and does not have any known immunodeficiency. The boy and his family are willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of decolonization measures for MRSA.

32F with a history of HIV-1 diagnosed 5 years ago, currently on efavirenz (EFV) and emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (FTC/TDF) combination therapy with an undetectable viral load. The patient has been using condoms as the primary method of contraception. She is interested in switching to the contraceptive implant as a more reliable method of family planning. She has no known allergies and is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient reports regular menstrual cycles with no history of abnormal vaginal bleeding or thromboembolic disease. She has not been pregnant in the last six months and is not currently breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, laboratory tests, and follow-up procedures. The patient has provided informed consent and meets all eligibility criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old female patient is seeking dental treatment for a lower right back tooth. She is in good health, without any systemic medical conditions, and is a non-smoker. She frequently forgets where she puts things and struggles to remember names of people she recently met. She has been feeling anxious and frustrated with herself. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She lives with her husband who helps her with daily activities. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is fluent in French and has no sensory deficits. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially receive an early diagnosis and treatment. She regularly attends her medical check-ups and is open to cognitive testing.

A 35-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past 6 months. His oncologist recently recommended allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) as the next step in his treatment plan. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the onset and course of immune-mediated disorders after stem cell transplant. He has no significant medical history aside from his AML diagnosis. He has no history of autoimmune disorders or inherited immunodeficiencies. He has not had a previous stem cell transplant. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and has signed informed consent.

This is a 63 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was diagnosed with advanced urothelial carcinoma (transitional cell carcinoma) after presenting with hematuria and was found to have metastatic disease involving the liver, lung, and bones. He received four cycles of standard first line chemotherapy with gemcitabine and cisplatin which resulted in a partial response. He is now being considered for participation in a clinical trial evaluating the drug SUO11248 (SUTENT) for maintenance therapy. He has no history of major surgeries or bleeding disorders, and has not received prior antiangiogenic therapy for this stage of the disease. He is willing to be randomized into either the treatment or placebo arm of the trial and understands the need for close follow-up and monitoring throughout the trial.

A 42-year-old man was admitted to the ICU due to severe sepsis caused by a urinary tract infection. He required endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure. He has no history of neurological disease or COPD. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He has a history of occasional alcohol consumption and smoking. His family authorized his inclusion in the study. He is expected to require mechanical ventilation for more than 72 hours.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a BMI of 24. She is generally healthy with no known medical conditions. She enjoys trying different types of coffee and drinks it regularly. She does not have any known food allergies or intolerances. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol moderately. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. She is willing to participate in a study to investigate the effects of coffee roasting on postprandial glucose response. She is interested in learning more about how her coffee consumption may affect her health. She has not participated in any scientific studies in the past month.

Patient A is a 55-year-old Japanese male who was diagnosed with follicular lymphoma 3 years ago. He has received treatment with chemotherapy and immunotherapy but has experienced a relapse. He is currently experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and swollen lymph nodes in his neck and groin. He has not received any treatment for his lymphoma for the past 4 weeks. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and has undergone baseline laboratory tests, including a negative serum pregnancy test for female participants of childbearing potential. The participant is willing to use protocol-specified method(s) of contraception if he engages in heterosexual intercourse. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of idelalisib in Japanese participants with relapsed or refractory indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (iNHL) or chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

The patient is a 59-year-old female who had a stroke 10 months ago. She has right-sided hemiplegia and experiences difficulty with walking and daily activities. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medications. She is married and lives with her husband. Her highest education level is high school. She has no history of falls since her stroke, but she does have a fear of falling. She uses a cane to assist with walking. She has some spasticity on her right side, but it does not cause her significant discomfort. She has been attending physical therapy twice a week for the past 6 months. Her Berg Balance Scale score is 35/56, and her Functional Ambulation Classification score is 3/5. She has a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 26/30. The patient speaks Turkish as her primary language.

This is a 45-year-old male patient who has been admitted to the ICU due to respiratory failure secondary to pneumonia. He has been intubated and is currently on mechanical ventilation (IMV) for more than 48 hours. He is sedated and has a Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale (RASS) score of -4. His respiratory parameters are stable with a FiO2 of 40% and PEEP of 8 cmH2O. He has no history of lung disease or pulmonary parenchyma damage. He has a central venous catheter in place for hemodynamic monitoring, but is not on hemofiltration. He is not in a strict dorsal decubitus position and does not have any high-risk respiratory infections. He is able to participate in the study and is willing to undergo chest physiotherapy twice daily. He has not received mechanical in-exsufflation treatment before and is eligible to be included in this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old Chinese woman who has been experiencing recurrent headaches for the past year. She has noticed that she has difficulty focusing and completing tasks at work, and has also experienced some forgetfulness. She visited her physician and underwent an MRI that revealed moyamoya disease (MMD). She has not had any previous surgical intervention for this condition. She is currently taking daily aspirin therapy. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She works as an accountant and has a stable job. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand her condition and to potentially improve her cognitive function through surgical revascularization. She lives in close proximity to the study site and is available for follow-up visits.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with esophageal cancer. He has a history of smoking and alcohol use. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy for his cancer but has not responded well to the treatment. His current condition is such that he is unable to eat solid food and requires a feeding tube. However, his upper gastrointestinal tract has tight stenotic malignant lesions that make routine pull PEG placement difficult without dilatation/bougeinage of the UGI tract. He is not currently receiving any systemic antibiotics and does not have any contraindications to PEG. However, he is allergic to Ceftriaxone antibiotics. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with Fibromyalgia a year ago. She has been experiencing widespread pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances which are affecting her daily physical activity. She has tried various treatments but has not been able to find relief from the symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves dance therapy as she believes it could help improve her mobility and reduce her pain levels. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not on any medications. She is able to walk independently and does not require any aids for balance, hearing or visual problems.

A 60-year-old male patient was referred to the cardiology clinic after experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker and quit 10 years ago. A cardiac catheterization was performed, and a stent was implanted in the left anterior descending artery due to a significant blockage. The patient returned to the clinic 6 months later with recurrent chest pain, and a repeat cardiac catheterization showed reocclusion of the stent. The patient reports a history of skin sensitivity to metals, including jewelry and belt buckles. He has never been tested for metal allergies but suspects that he may be allergic to the nickel used in the stent.

Lisa is a 48-year-old postmenopausal woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication called BIIB061. She is in good health, with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2, and has normal vital signs. Lisa has never been exposed to BIIB061 before and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She has not used any over-the-counter products, including herbal or alternative health preparations, in the last 14 days. Lisa has not participated in any interventional clinical study in which an investigational drug, biologic, device, or approved therapy for investigational use was administered or used within the last 30 days. She has not had any live or attenuated immunization/vaccination within the last 30 days and has not donated blood in the last 30 days. Lisa has not had any surgery in the last 3 months. She is willing to practice effective contraception during the study and to refrain from sperm donation for at least 3 months after receiving the study treatment. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman whose mother was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at the age of 58. She has two siblings, both older than her. She does not have any symptoms related to the digestive system. She is generally healthy and takes no medications. She has never had a colonoscopy or any other type of colon screening. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if colon capsule endoscopy is a viable screening option. She does not have a personal history of adenoma or colorectal cancer, does not have any known hereditary conditions, and has not had any gastrointestinal surgeries. She is willing to sign the informed consent form and is committed to following the study protocol. She is not pregnant and does not have any known allergies or contraindications to the medications used in the study.

48-year-old female with a BMI of 36 and a history of endometrial cancer is scheduled to undergo a hysterectomy via a vertical abdominal incision. She has no prior history of abdominal surgery, hernia repair, or radiation therapy to the abdomen or pelvis. She is fluent in spoken English and is able to provide informed consent. She has no planned concurrent plastic surgery procedures, and is not currently pregnant or incarcerated. She has consented to participate in the study to evaluate a quality improvement intervention to reduce wound separation rates in obese gynecologic oncology service patients undergoing abdominal surgery.

A 15-year-old male high school student with a diagnosis of ADHD and has been prescribed medication for the condition. Despite medication treatment, he continues to experience significant symptoms of ADHD such as inattention, disorganization, and difficulty concentrating. He has expressed interest in participating in a study aimed at improving his ADHD symptoms through the use of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). The participant is motivated to learn skills for organization and planning, attention, and mood that will help him better manage his ADHD symptoms. He is able to travel to Boston or another study location in the Greater Boston area for 4 assessment visits and 12 weekly therapy visits. The participant does not have any exclusion criteria such as substance abuse, conduct disorder, or other conditions interfering with consent or participation.

A 60 year old postmenopausal woman with a history of breast cancer and currently taking anastrozole (1mg) daily, presenting with moderate to severe arthralgia in the hands and wrists, which she believes is caused by her aromatase inhibitor. She reports difficulty with everyday tasks due to the pain and stiffness. The pain has been present for the past 6 months, and she has tried over-the-counter pain medications with no relief. She has a BMI of 25, and her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to medication. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and complete the required questionnaires. She is able to comply with study visits and follow-up. Her laboratory values are within normal limits.

A 26-year-old male patient with beta-thalassemia/Hb E disease came for a routine check-up at the clinic. He was diagnosed with beta-thalassemia/Hb E disease when he was 6 months old. He has been regularly taking folic acid supplements and has not received any blood transfusions or iron chelator treatment for the past 3 months. His hemoglobin level during the screen visit was 8.2 g/dL. He has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. He works as an accountant and leads an active lifestyle. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve his health condition.

A 56-year-old man, living in a rural area of Vermont, is interested in learning more about cancer research studies and clinical trials. He has a family history of cancer and has concerns about his own cancer risk. He is a retired school teacher and enjoys spending time outdoors, hiking and fishing. He has no known cognitive impairments and is able to provide informed consent. He has access to a computer and the internet and is comfortable with technology. He has no history of cancer, but has been experiencing occasional shortness of breath and coughing. He is a former smoker, quit smoking 10 years ago, and has been screened for lung cancer with a negative result. He is interested in participating in a study to learn more about cancer research studies and clinical trials, and potentially enroll in one.

A 29-year-old female has been experiencing redness, itching, and irritation in both eyes for the past 3 weeks. She wears contact lenses regularly but has discontinued their use for the past week. She has no known allergies to medications and has not been diagnosed with any cardiovascular, liver, or kidney disorders in the past. She has not used any investigational drugs or devices in the past 30 days. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who presented to the hospital with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and flushing. She has a history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) and has undergone surgical resection of a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (NET) 5 years ago. She has been receiving octreotide therapy since her surgery but has been experiencing increasing symptoms over the past few months. Her blood tests revealed elevated levels of chromogranin A and 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA). A CT scan of her abdomen showed a small NET in her small bowel. She is currently asymptomatic and able to lie still for up to 50 minutes. She is not pregnant or lactating.

As this is a clinical trial that involves healthy volunteers, there is no patient description needed. However, if a potential participant were to inquire about the trial, they would need to meet the inclusion criteria listed, including being between the ages of 18 and 67, passing a medical examination similar to a standard aviation medical examination, and being affiliated with a social security system or holding a European Health Insurance Card. They would also need to be willing to participate in the study and provide written consent. Individuals with a medical history of claustrophobia or contraindications to MRI, as well as pregnant women, would be excluded from the study.

A 45 year old woman is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy surgery. She has no significant medical history and no known allergies to latex or silicone. Her body mass index is 25 and she has a normal mouth opening of 3 cm. She has not had any recent upper respiratory tract infections and has no history of gastro-oesophageal reflux or any upper airway pathology. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the new LMA Protector device for airway management during her surgery.

The patient is a 28 year-old premenopausal woman who has had recurrent fatigue and difficulty with exercise. She reports regular menstrual cycles and no history of anemia. Her BMI is 22 kg/m2. Her serum ferritin level was found to be 12ug/ml on a routine blood test. She exercises approximately 2 hours a week, mostly through jogging and yoga. She is not currently using any contraception but is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. She has no known allergies to iron carboxymaltose, iron sucrose or iron sulfate. She has not taken any iron preparations or multivitamins containing iron in the past 8 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease, orthopaedic or rheumatologic disease, or muscle disease. She reports no acute or chronic infections, inflammation or malignancies. She has no known mental disorders or depression. She is not taking any concurrent medications except for oral contraceptives. Her CRP, TSH, and CK levels are within normal range. She has no concurrent medical conditions that would prevent compliance or participation in the study. She has not participated in any therapeutic trials in the past month.

68-year-old retired airline pilot who participated in the "Age-Related Longitudinal Changes in Aviator Performance" study and is willing to participate in this new MRI study. The participant has a history of hypertension, which is currently well controlled with medication. The participant has no history of major neurological disease and has no metal prosthesis or cardiac pacemaker. The participant reports no history of severe claustrophobia or poorly controlled back pain. The participant is able to safely and comfortably complete the scanning session. The participant is interested in contributing to the research efforts to understand the changes in the brain that occur with aging and its impact on complex tasks such as flying a plane.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is at 38 weeks of gestation with her second pregnancy. She has a history of gestational hypertension in her first pregnancy, but it resolved after delivery. Her current pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and she has attended regular antenatal check-ups. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is 160 cm tall. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is a homemaker and is married with one child. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is scheduled for a non-elective Caesarean section due to fetal distress. She has been counselled about the study and is willing to participate. She is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has recently undergone menopause. She complains of elevated systolic blood pressure and experiences occasional dizziness and shortness of breath. She is currently taking anti-hypertensive medications but is interested in alternative interventions that can help lower her blood pressure. She has no history of alcohol abuse or smoking. She has no known chronic clinical disease except hypertension. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to accept random assignment to the study condition. The patient has not had any significant weight changes in the past 3 months and is willing to remain weight stable throughout the study. She has not been diagnosed with neurological disorders or diseases that may affect motor/cognitive function. A graded exercise test will be performed to ensure that the patient is fit to participate in the study.

30-year-old female with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency department with a twisting injury to her left ankle while playing basketball. She reports immediate onset of pain and swelling around the ankle. The patient is able to bear weight, but experiences significant discomfort. On physical examination, there is moderate swelling and tenderness over the lateral malleolus, but no obvious deformity or neurovascular deficit. The patient is affiliated to the national health insurance and agrees to participate in the study. She provides written informed consent. The patient has not had any X-ray performed prior to her visit to the Emergency Department. She is not pregnant and does not have any mental disorder or excessive alcoholization. She is cooperative and willing to follow the study protocol.

25-year-old M diagnosed with first-episode psychosis and currently receiving treatment from the Fraser Health Early Psychosis Intervention (EPI) program. He expresses a strong desire to return to work and has been on a stable therapeutic dose of anti-psychotic medication for the past 6 months. He has a good command of the English language and is interested in participating in a vocational support program to enhance his chances of finding and maintaining employment. He has no history of substance abuse and has completed some college coursework.

The patient is a 63-year-old male diagnosed with MDS, classified as Intermediate 2-risk according to the international prognostic scoring system (IPSS). He has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising for the past few months. His platelet count is < 75 x 109 /L and he has been receiving regular platelet transfusions. He has no history of cancer other than MDS or sAML/MDS with systemic chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy within the last 2 years. He has no history of liver cirrhosis, thrombophilic risk factors, or active and uncontrolled infections. He is currently not on any investigational drug treatment. His ECOG status is 1. He is able to understand and comply with protocol requirements and instructions. He has signed and dated informed consent. His total bilirubin, ALT and AST, and creatinine levels are within normal limits. He is practicing an acceptable method of contraception as he is sexually active.

Pt is a 58yo M with a history of hypertension and chronic renal disease presenting with persistent albuminuria exceeding 20 mg/24h for the last three months. Despite being on antihypertensive medication, his blood pressure is not adequately controlled and he has not responded to previous treatment. His serum creatinine concentration is 1.7 mg/dL and his calculated glomerular filtration rate is 40 mL/min/1.73 m2. He has not had any recent myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, or peripheral vascular disease. His total cholesterol level is 180mg/dL and he is on statins. He has not had any treatment with corticosteroids, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or immunosuppressive drugs. He has not been on angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers in the last month. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for the last 3 months. He has a significant weight loss of around 10 pounds in the last month, and he feels tired and weak. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he doesn't have any other specific complaints except the respiratory symptoms. A chest X-ray is ordered, which shows a mass in the right lung. A CT scan is performed, and it reveals a 4 cm mass in the right upper lobe, along with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. A biopsy of the mass confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Further investigations, including brain MRI and PET scan, show no evidence of distant metastases. The patient is scheduled for radical surgery of the lung cancer.

A premature baby boy weighing 1200 g was born at 28 weeks gestation. He was intubated and admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). The baby has been gradually weaned off the ventilator and is now on non-invasive ventilation. The baby has been tolerating enteral feeds well and has reached 100 ml/kg/day of oral feeds by day 14 of life. The baby's mother is willing to participate in the study. The baby has no major congenital anomalies or Rh hemolytic disease.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who underwent allogeneic hematologic stem cell transplantation three months ago. He presents with chronic ocular graft versus host disease with worsening of dry eye symptoms for the past month. He has been using over-the-counter and prescription eye drops for dry eye symptoms for the past month but has not experienced any significant relief. During the ophthalmic examination, corneal fluorescein staining score of 3 was observed in one region and 1 in the other region. The total lissamine green conjunctival staining score, according to a modified National Eye Institute grading system, was 4. The patient has no history of using topical ophthalmic cyclosporine within the last 45 days, and no use of any topical ophthalmic steroid or autologous serum eye drops within the last two weeks.

A 35-year-old woman presents with symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath, and recurrent infections for the past month. She has a history of allergies and asthma but is otherwise healthy. Physical exam reveals pallor and mild hepatosplenomegaly. Lab results show a white blood cell count of 150,000/uL with 90% lymphoblasts. Bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of T-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (T-ALL). The patient has no severe comorbidities and is eligible for treatment with Hyper-CVAD chemotherapy regimen. The healthcare team will recommend allogeneic stem cell transplantation if the patient has high-risk disease.

The patient is an 80-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and chest pain. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. She underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for an acute myocardial infarction (MI) 3 years ago. She has been compliant with her medications, which include aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. On admission, her vital signs were stable, and her physical examination revealed crackles in the lungs bilaterally. Lab studies showed elevated troponin levels, and an electrocardiogram showed ST segment depression in the inferior leads. She was diagnosed with acute decompensated heart failure and admitted to the medical intensive care unit (MICU) for further management. During her hospitalization, she required mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure and received inotropic support for hemodynamic instability. She was discharged from the hospital on day 14 with continued medical management of her heart failure. At the time of discharge, she was able to ambulate with assistance and required home health services for continued physical therapy and monitoring of her chronic medical conditions. The patient and her family have been informed about the clinical trial and have expressed interest in participating.

This is a 42-year-old male of Caucasian descent who is scheduled for bariatric surgery due to his BMI of 35 kg/m2. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has not experienced any adverse effects from the atorvastatin but is concerned about the possibility of drug interactions. He does not have a history of liver or kidney problems or any other major medical conditions. He does not smoke or use any illegal drugs but does drink alcohol occasionally. He is fluent in English and has no issues with reading, speaking, or understanding the language.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with retinal detachment in his right eye. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has bilateral phakic lenses and has not undergone any previous ocular surgeries. His best-corrected visual acuity in his right eye is 20/40. He has noticed a gradual decrease in vision over the past few months, which prompted him to seek medical attention. Upon examination, his left eye was found to be normal. He has been advised to undergo a vitrectomy in his right eye to address the retinal detachment. He has been informed that this surgery may increase his risk of developing cataracts in the future. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to objectively measure the progression of lens opacification after his vitrectomy surgery. He understands that the study will involve repeated measurements of the opacity of his lens using innovative objective techniques and that he will need to attend regular follow-up visits. He meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

75-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of glioblastoma/gliosarcoma. He has not had any previous treatment for this cancer. His past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently able to perform most activities of daily living independently and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 (ECOG 1). His laboratory values are within normal limits, and he has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He has not had any other malignancies in the past 5 years and is willing to participate in the study.

This is a 7-year-old female patient who recently lost a primary molar in the mandibular left quadrant. She has a healthy dentition with no abnormal dental conditions such as crossbite. Her oral hygiene is good, and she has no medically compromised conditions. She has sound and healthy buccal and lingual surfaces of the abutment teeth. The patient's parents are interested in the possibility of using a 3D printed space maintainer to replace the missing tooth and prevent any future dental issues.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who recently experienced persistent headaches and vision changes, leading to a diagnosis of a high-grade glioma (WHO grade III). He has no history of other primary malignancies or severe lung infections. His Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score is 80, and his expected survival period is estimated to be at least three months. Blood routine examination shows normal levels of hemoglobin (100 g/L), ANC (2.0 x 10^9/L), and PLT (120 x 10^9/L). His liver and kidney function tests are also normal. The patient has no history of myocardial ischemia or infarction, arrhythmia, or cardiac insufficiency, and his blood pressure is controlled with medication. He is able to swallow medications and has no chronic diarrhea or intestinal obstruction. His coagulation function is normal, and he has no history of hemorrhagic tendencies or treatments with thrombolysis or anticoagulation. The patient has not experienced any pulmonary or other organ hemorrhages in the past four weeks, and he has no history of arteriovenous thrombosis in the past six months. He is not currently taking any medications that would significantly affect oral drug absorption. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and meet all other inclusion criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the combination of TMZ and apatinib in newly diagnosed high-grade glioma.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl diagnosed with type 1 diabetes when she was 10 years old. She is currently attending a diabetes clinic for routine check-ups and management of her condition. She has been experiencing difficulty in managing her blood glucose levels, which has caused her to feel frustrated and overwhelmed. She has missed a few appointments with her healthcare provider and has been inconsistent with her medication and dietary regimen. She is generally compliant with her treatment plan but often struggles with motivation to maintain a healthy lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the trial of motivational interviewing to see if it can help her improve her management of diabetes and overall quality of life.

A 30-year-old Chinese male presents as a healthy individual with a body mass index of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of metabolic diseases such as diabetes or hypertension, and his fasting blood glucose level is within normal limits. He does not take any prescription medications, and he is not involved in sports at a competitive or endurance level. The patient reports no allergies or intolerances to any test foods and does not intentionally restrict his food intake. He does not smoke and has normal blood pressure readings. The patient is interested in participating in a research study that aims to determine the effect of glycaemic index on 24 hour blood glucose profiles and energy regulation in Asians when fed a normal diet modulated with sweeteners.

A 55-year-old male patient was diagnosed with melanoma and underwent surgery to remove the primary tumor and sentinel lymph node. The pathology report confirmed the presence of cancer cells in the sentinel lymph node. The patient has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and has never smoked. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a good performance status and is able to carry out his daily activities without any assistance. The patient has adequate archived paraffin-embedded tissue and freshly removed sentinel lymph node tissue available for laboratory assays. Clinical data and date of last follow-up on tumor stage and status are available.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a long-standing history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Despite being treated with two different mechanisms of action, the patient still experiences moderate to severe RA symptoms, including pain, swelling and stiffness in at least 4/28 tender and 4/28 swollen joints. The patient has been taking conventional DMARDs regularly for at least 12 weeks, with a non-changing dose for at least 8 weeks prior to screening. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol.
