The patient has no history of psychiatric illness or substance abuse, active infection requiring treatment with antibiotics, uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes, or any condition that precludes participation in the study. The patient is willing to use a double barrier method of contraception throughout the study as the patient is a woman of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 45 year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV infection three years ago. He has been on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) including Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and a ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitor (r/PI) for the last 6 months. He has no prior PI genotypic resistance and his plasma HIV RNA has been less than 50 copies/ml for the past 3 months. He was recently diagnosed with low bone mineral density (BMD) after a dual energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan revealed a spine or neck of femur t-score ≤ -1.0 (i.e. WHO-defined osteopenia). The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials and is not using oral corticosteroids or inhaled fluticasone. He has no fragility fractures and is not receiving therapy for low BMD or hypogonadism. He is not breastfeeding and is not pregnant. The patient has no secondary, endocrinological cause of low BMD and has no contraindication to Raltegravir therapy.

A 52-year-old female university professor is experiencing symptoms of dizziness over the past few weeks. She has been experiencing vertigo episodes, especially when she stands or moves her head suddenly. She has no history of head injury or neuropsychiatric disorders. She takes medication for hypertension and has a history of migraines. She speaks fluent English and is willing to stand with a strap on her head for an hour. She is not currently pregnant and has not had any ear operations besides myringotomy and tube placement in the past.

A 34-year-old male with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections is scheduled to undergo elective ureteroscopy. He reports difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep for the past 6 months. He states that he wakes up feeling tired and unrefreshed. He denies snoring or observed apneas during sleep. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has a desk job. His BMI is 25. His preoperative assessment is normal, and he is classified as ASA physical status I. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and signs the written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old African American man with a history of Type 2 diabetes. He has been experiencing symptoms of gastroparesis, including nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral neuropathy. He is currently on metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. His most recent HbA1c was 8.5%. He is a retired construction worker and is married with three adult children. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is willing to discontinue his current treatment for diabetic gastroparesis and avoid all medications specified by the protocol for the duration of the study. He is able to read and understand English and is willing and able to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He has not received any previous treatment for HCV and is currently experiencing fatigue, joint pain, and occasional abdominal discomfort. He has been diagnosed with fibrosis stage F3 or greater, as indicated by acceptable tests. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has tested negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen (HbsAg) and anti-HIV antibody. He does not have a history of solid organ transplant or any clinically significant abnormalities or co-morbidities. However, he has been taking medication for high blood pressure for the past year.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who lives in one of the villages in the Nice hinterland that was devastated by the Alex storm that hit France from September 30, 2020 to October 3, 2020. During the storm, her family's home was severely damaged and they were forced to evacuate to a nearby shelter. They were without electricity and water for several days, and the girl experienced prolonged stress due to the fear of another storm and the uncertainty of when they would be able to return home. She was seen by the medico-psychological emergency unit between October 3 and October 30, 2020 and was assessed by a child psychiatrist trained in emergency and pediatric psychological trauma. The assessment sheet specific to her developmental age was used to assess her immediate symptoms. Her parents have consented to the processing of her data for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing pain in his joints and muscles for the past year. He takes L-DOPA and dopamine agonists to control his Parkinson's symptoms. He rates his pain as 6 out of 10 on a scale, with 10 being the most severe. He has no history of epilepsy and is not currently under any treatment for chronic pain. He is affiliated with a social protection program and has given his informed consent to participate in the study. He has no personal or familial history of epilepsy. He is not suffering from any other pathology causing chronic pain, such as rheumatic disease or orthopedic pathologies. He is not suffering from cancer, and he does not have any neuroleptic treatment. He is able to fulfill the scales of the study. He is not under tutelage, curatella or law protection, and he is not included in any other clinical study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of partial onset epilepsy for the past 7 years. She is currently taking two concomitant antiepileptic drugs, but experiencing regular seizures despite her medication. She has a history of hypersensitivity to certain medications, but not to lacosamide. She is motivated to try a new medication to improve her seizure control, and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no history of generalized epilepsy or status epilepticus within the last 12 months. She has not experienced any non-epileptic events, including pseudoseizures or conversion disorder. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and has never attempted suicide. She has been diagnosed with progressive cerebral disease and is therefore interested in exploring additional treatment options. The patient is not currently taking felbamate or vigabatrin. She is not under legal protection.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with low grade B-cell lymphoma two years ago. She underwent chemotherapy with rituximab and achieved complete remission. However, her disease relapsed after 6 months of remission. She received another chemotherapy regimen as salvage therapy and achieved partial response. She is now eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a minimum life expectancy of 6 months. Her HIV, HBV, and HCV serologies are negative. She has no history of cancer except for her lymphoma. Her bone marrow reserve is good with neutrophils of 2.5 G/l and platelets of 150 G/l. Her renal and hepatic functions are normal. She is not pregnant and is able to give informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman with two children visited the health center in her village, seeking counseling for her experiences of domestic violence. She reported that her husband frequently used physical and emotional abuse to control her, causing her stress and anxiety. She has at least one score from the Conflict Tactics Scale 2 (CTS2) questionnaire, confirming the presence of domestic violence. She has completed secondary education and is fluent in Persian. She is an Iranian citizen and married. She is not pregnant or postpartum and does not take any psychedelic, anti-anxiety or anti-depressant medications. She does not have any history of hospitalization in a psychiatric ward or incurable physical disease such as cancer or malignant tumors. She has not experienced any severe stress such as divorce, accident, or bereavement of relatives in the last six months. She is not participating in any other counseling courses with content similar to the present intervention. She has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to attend the 8 sessions of 90 minutes each week, either as part of the intervention group or control group.

A 28-year-old first-time mother with a 6-month-old daughter residing in Pelotas, Brazil, is concerned about her daughter's oral health. The mother has a high school education and works as a part-time cleaner. She reports that her daughter is solely breastfed and has not yet started any solid foods. The mother has no history of dental caries and brushes her teeth twice a day. The daughter does not have any teeth yet. The mother is interested in participating in a study that can provide her with information and guidance on how to prevent early childhood caries. She is willing to attend educational sessions and follow oral hygiene instructions provided by the study. She understands that her daughter must not have any teeth in her mouth at the time of enrollment to be eligible for the study.

The patient is a 56 year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. He was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx two years ago and underwent radiation therapy and surgery. However, the cancer has recurred and metastasized to his lungs. He has not received any prior systemic treatment for his recurrent or metastatic disease. He has a performance status of 2 due to fatigue and dyspnea on exertion. His laboratory parameters are within normal limits except for mild anemia (Hb 8.5 g/dl) which is being monitored by his physician. He has no evidence of central nervous system involvement or lung fibrosis. He has no history of other malignancies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

25F with myopia up to -5.50 D sphere and -2.50 D astigmatism, stable refraction for the past 2 years, currently wearing contact lenses. Best Spectacle Corrected Visual Acuity (BSCVA) 20/20 in both eyes. No history of ocular disease or surgery. No systemic medications that may affect wound healing or tissue repair. No dry eye syndrome or nystagmus. Not pregnant or planning a pregnancy during the course of the study. Willing to comply with the schedule for follow-up visits. Signed informed consent document.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced breast cancer that has metastasized to her pelvic bones, causing severe pain that is refractory to palliative care. She has been experiencing pain with a numerical rating scale (NRS) of 8/10 and has undergone three palliative care evaluations. She has provided informed consent to participate in this study and is able to complete assessment forms. She meets the inclusion criteria of having unilateral pain below the shoulder level due to cancer. She does not have uncorrectable coagulopathy, a large intracranial mass, or a morphine allergy. Her life expectancy is estimated to be more than one month.

A 40-year-old female patient with a history of breast cancer was recently diagnosed with metastasis to the liver. She has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past 3 months and is experiencing significant side effects, including hair loss, fatigue, and nausea. She has been married for 15 years and has two children. She has been hesitant to discuss the impact of her cancer treatment on her sexual health with her healthcare team, but is interested in participating in a program that provides support and guidance in this area. She is open to receiving counseling from a nurse, esthetician, and sexologist to help her navigate the physical and emotional changes she is experiencing.

Patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with multiple myeloma that has relapsed after prior chemotherapy. He has measurable disease with plasmacytosis in bone marrow and elevated immunoglobulin levels in serum and/or urine. He does not have known CNS involvement and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his absolute neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits. His bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are all within two times the upper limit of normal, and his creatinine level is below 2 mg/dL or creatinine clearance is above 40 mL/min. He is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. He is able to swallow pills and does not have a history of seizures or allergic reactions to study agents. He does not have sensory or motor neuropathy greater than grade II, and he does not have any uncontrolled illnesses or conditions that would limit his ability to comply with the study requirements. He has not received therapy for multiple myeloma in at least 2 weeks, and he is not receiving any other concurrent investigational or commercial agents or therapies for this malignancy.

A 65-year-old male diagnosed with aortic valve stenosis is scheduled for cardiac valve replacement surgery. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but has been managing them with medication. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or any other heart arrhythmia. His preoperative troponin levels are within the normal range, and his lipid profile is normal. He does not have any underlying metabolic or renal diseases, nor does he have any history of psychological disorders. He is not currently taking any anti-arrhythmic medications or lipid-lowering therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare the antiarrhythmic and cardioprotective effects of Atorvastatin versus Magnesium Sulfate after cardiac valve replacement surgery.

Pt is a 30yo F who presents with missed miscarriage at 9 weeks gestation confirmed by ultrasound. She has a history of one prior pregnancy resulting in a live birth. She has no significant medical history or allergies. Pelvic exam reveals a uterus consistent with a 9-week gestation. She is not hemodynamically unstable and has no evidence of sepsis. She has not had a previous failed medical or surgical evacuation. She is not using an intrauterine contraceptive device and does not have a suspected or proven ectopic pregnancy. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding and cramping after a missed period. She reports a history of irregular menstrual cycles but denies any previous pregnancies. Upon examination, the patient's uterine size is estimated to be less than 12 weeks LMP, and the cervical os is open. The patient is willing to provide contact information for follow-up and is over 18 years old. She has no history of ectopic pregnancy, and there is no intrauterine device in place. The patient is in good general health with no signs of infection or anemia. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to be treated with 400mcg sublingual misoprostol as first-line treatment.

Patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, presenting with symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has been diagnosed with aspirin and clopidogrel resistance based on laboratory results. He has been recommended for coronary angiography and possible percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The patient has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or bleeding disorders. He is not currently taking any GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist, anticoagulation, or lytic therapy. His serum creatinine level is within normal limits, and he has no ongoing bleeding or bleeding diathesis. The patient has no contraindications for anticoagulation and has not undergone any major surgery or trauma within the last six weeks. His platelet count and hemoglobin levels are also within normal limits. The patient has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35 yo F with a history of mild to moderate asthma for the past year, currently using a short-acting beta-agonist for relief/rescue of asthma, and with demonstrated FEV1 reversibility of at least 12% (and 200ml) or greater within 15-30 minutes following administration of 4 inhalations of albuterol. The patient is between the ages of 18 and 65 years, has no history of lung cancer, COPD, or other co-morbidity associated with irreversible narrowing of the airways, and has no abscess, infection or lesion (including lymphadenopathy) at the AlphaCore™ treatment site. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use an accepted form of birth control. The patient is not currently implanted with any electrical and/or neurostimulator device, and has not had carotid endarterectomy or vascular neck surgery on the right side. The patient has not experienced recent clinically significant changes in blood pressure, has no uncontrolled high blood pressure, and is not presently receiving pressors to maintain blood pressure.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. She has been on multiple daily injections (MDI) of insulin since her diagnosis. She checks her blood glucose levels at least three times a day using a conventional Self Measurement of Blood Glucose (SMBG) device. She experiences frequent hypoglycemic episodes, especially during the night. She has a history of severe hypoglycemia requiring hospitalization. Her HbA1c is 8.5%. She is a graduate student and has a part-time job. She has no known allergies or other significant medical history. She is willing to commit to the study protocol and wear the flash glucose monitoring system (FGMS) for at least 6 months. She speaks, reads, and writes Chinese fluently. She does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. She has not participated in any other investigational studies in the past 30 days.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who has been suffering from chronic tinnitus for 5 years. She describes her tinnitus as a high-pitched ringing sound that is present in both ears and is constant. She also reports a gradual hearing loss in both ears over the past 10 years. She has tried various treatments including medications and sound therapy, but none of them have provided significant relief. She has no history of neurological diseases and is not currently taking any medications affecting the central nervous system. She has no evidence of dementia, and no clinical diagnosis of depression. She is interested in participating in this study to explore the potential benefits of transcranial magnetic stimulation and transcranial direct current stimulation in the treatment of her tinnitus.

A 32-year-old female patient was diagnosed with HIV two years ago and started on ART. She lives in a rural area outside of Kampala, Uganda with her husband and two children. She works as a farmer and has limited access to healthcare facilities. She struggles with remembering to take her medication at the correct time and often forgets to attend follow-up appointments due to her busy schedule. She has limited knowledge about HIV and how to manage her symptoms. She speaks Luganda as her primary language and has basic cell phone literacy. She has expressed interest in participating in the clinical trial to improve her quality of life and better manage her HIV.

25 yo F nulliparous with no significant medical history, not currently using hormonal contraceptives and willing to participate in a clinical trial. The patient has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2, weighs 125 pounds and has a hematocrit of 39%. The patient has no known allergies and has not experienced any adverse reactions to previous medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent and comply with the study requirements.

A 45 year old woman visited her physician for a routine mammogram, which showed an abnormality in her left breast. She underwent a stereotactic biopsy that confirmed the presence of a small mass that was suspicious for cancer. A biopsy marker was placed during the biopsy, which is visible under ultrasound. The mass is less than 6 cm from the skin when lying supine, and is a discreet surgical target in which the center/focal area is defined. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient has not undergone previous open surgical biopsy, lumpectomy, or mastectomy in the operative breast, nor does she have a prosthesis/implant in the operative breast. The patient does not have a cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator device, and is not contraindicated for surgery. The patient is not pregnant.

Patient is an elderly male or female over the age of 65 who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders and is currently being treated at the University Memory Center of Angers University Hospital. The patient should be able to walk without any walking aid for 15 meters and have a Mini-Mental Status Examination score greater than 10. The patient should not have any history of cerebrovascular accident or other cerebro-spinal pathology, and should not have poor workmanship of the written or oral French language. The patient should not use walking aids such as walking frames with wheels or tricycles, and should not have had any acute medical or surgical disease in the past 3 months. The patient should not refuse to participate in the study or have near visual acuity less than 2/10.

A 26-year-old pregnant woman at 38 weeks gestation presented to Ayder Referral Hospital in Mekelle, Ethiopia, in labor. This is her first pregnancy, and she has had an uncomplicated prenatal course. The patient has no significant medical history and no allergies. During her antenatal care, she received routine screening for gestational diabetes and hypertension, which were negative. Her prenatal ultrasound examinations have been within normal limits. Upon admission, she is monitored with electronic fetal monitoring (EFM) for intrapartum management. As per the current protocol at Ayder Referral Hospital, she is designated as "high risk" due to nulliparity, and she receives EFM. EFM is performed using a live feedback of fetal heart rate, but without the ability to interpret fetal heart rate pattern due to depleted paper supplies. The patient is considered eligible for inclusion in this study as she is receiving EFM for intrapartum management. She is approached by the study team regarding participation in a study comparing EFM with and without pattern interpretation. The study team explains that the purpose of the study is to evaluate whether cesarean delivery rates can be decreased without compromising neonatal outcomes. The patient is informed that she will be randomly assigned to receive EFM with or without pattern interpretation. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old female with a history of migraines and a seizure disorder presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe headache and confusion. Imaging showed a cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM) which has not been previously treated. The patient underwent an angiogram, which confirmed the diagnosis of a ruptured AVM. The patient was offered endovascular treatment with SQUID™ liquid embolic agent and provided informed consent. The patient is scheduled for the endovascular treatment and will be followed up for 6 months after the procedure to assess the safety and efficacy of the treatment. The patient does not have any renal insufficiency and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is a registered nurse working at a hospital in the United States. She has been working in the healthcare industry for about 10 years and has been actively involved in treating COVID-19 patients for the last 6 months. She has a husband and two young children, and she is the primary caregiver for her family. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the increased workload and the fear of contracting COVID-19 and infecting her family. She has noticed that her sleep patterns have been affected, and she often feels anxious and irritable. She has no prior history of mental health conditions and has not sought any counseling or psychiatric treatment in the past. She is able to use electronic devices and is willing to participate in the study to help contribute to the understanding of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on healthcare workers' mental health.

We are seeking healthy individuals aged between 25-45 years old who are willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effects of lower limb immobilisation with cast and orthosis on blood flow and microcirculation in the lower limbs. The study aims to measure the blood flow and tissue oxygen saturation in the right popliteal and lower limbs respectively, before, 30 and 60 minutes after the application of a cast or orthosis. The orthosis, called VACOped, is a weight-bearing orthosis with an adjustable range of motion of the ankle used in patients operated for Achilles tendon rupture. The orthosis will be set to allow for ankle plantarflexion restricted between 15 and 30 degrees. Participants should not have any severe cardiovascular or renal disease causing pitting oedema, nor any previous operation in the lower limbs affecting the vascular or lymphatic system. Women who are pregnant are also excluded from this study. Ten healthy individuals will be recruited for this study. If you are interested in taking part in this clinical trial, please contact us for more information.

A 25 year old healthy female with a BMI of 24.5 presents for a pharmacokinetics study of an herbal supplement. She has no underlying medical conditions and is not currently taking any prescription medication or herbal supplements. She is able to read and understand English and has active health insurance coverage. The participant has undergone a screening procedure and has met all inclusion criteria. She has signed the informed consent form and is fully aware of the study's procedures and restrictions. The study will involve a single-dose administration of the study agent and will take place within 21-28 calendar days of her selection as a subject. Blood and saliva samples will be collected at pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 24 hours to estimate the plasma concentration of four key constituents of the herbal supplement. The participant is willing to fully comply with the study procedures and restrictions.

The patient is a 57-year-old man with a long-standing history of diabetes. He has been taking metformin for the past year to control his blood glucose levels. He has no known allergy to any medication. He has not received a pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine in the past. He regularly fills his prescription at a Kroger pharmacy in the Richmond area. He is willing to participate in the study and receive education on the pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine. He understands that the study aims to improve the vaccination rates in patients with diabetes and is willing to provide feedback through a brief survey after the pharmacist's education.

32-year-old male with a medical history of Von-Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease with multiple retinal capillary hemangiomas (RCH) in both eyes, which have been growing despite previous laser treatments. The patient has noticed a progressive decrease in visual acuity in the left eye over the past several months. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of cardiac disease, stroke or diabetes mellitus. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a combination of two investigational treatments, E10030 and ranibizumab, which have the potential to slow the growth of RCH and improve vision. The patient meets all the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to undergo serial intravitreal injections and follow-up evaluations for 104 weeks.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and is overweight. He is 5'10" tall and weighs 220 pounds. He has a history of mild high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. He has never had any liver issues but has been experiencing some abdominal pain and discomfort lately. He drinks alcohol occasionally but never to excess. He is interested in participating in the FLIP pilot study to monitor his liver fat content and potentially detect any issues early. He is fluent in English and has no metal or electronic implants. He is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of dry eye, including burning, itching, and redness in both eyes for several weeks. He has used over-the-counter artificial tears but has not found significant relief. He has no history of ocular surgery or serious trauma and has not been diagnosed with Sjogren's syndrome. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any systemic medications. The patient is willing and able to follow study instructions and agrees to discontinue his contact lens wear for the duration of the study. He has no known allergies to any of the components of the study medications. The patient's best corrected visual acuity is 0.2 logMAR in each eye as assessed using an ETDRS chart at Visit 1. The patient reads, signs, and dates the informed consent document and HIPAA privacy document.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has been admitted to the hospital due to respiratory distress. The patient has been on mechanical ventilation for 24 hours and has evidence of increased inflammation as assessed by hsCRP and elevated levels of fibrinogen. The patient's PaO2 / FiO2 ratio is < 300, indicating ARDS. The patient is capable of giving informed consent and has provided it for this study. The patient has a history of hypertension but is otherwise in good health. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials for COVID-19 and is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medications. The patient is not pregnant and does not have a history of nephrolithiasis. The patient has agreed to undergo treatment with PF-06650833, an investigational drug, in addition to standard-of-care treatment, as part of this clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and has never been pregnant. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs but occasionally drinks alcohol at social events. She is sexually active with her long-term male partner who has undergone a vasectomy. Her medical and surgical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any prescription medications or over-the-counter drugs (including herbal supplements). She has not participated in any clinical studies in the past 30 days and has not received any immunosuppressive agents, coal tar, and/or radiation therapies within the past 30 days. She has not donated blood or plasma in the past 6 weeks and has negative screens for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. Her estimated creatinine clearance is > 80 mL/min using the Cockcroft-Gault equation, and her QTcF interval is < 450 msec at screening. The patient is willing and able to consume standardized meals and comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He presented with complaints of cough, blood in sputum, and shortness of breath. A chest X-ray showed a mass in the right lung, which was confirmed on a subsequent CT scan. The biopsy of the mass showed non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has no significant past medical history, and he is a non-smoker. His physical examination was unremarkable except for decreased breath sounds over the right lung. The patient's laboratory studies revealed normal renal and hepatic function, leucocyte count of 6,000/mcl, hemoglobin level of 12 mg/dL, and platelet count of 200,000/mcl. The patient has clinical stage IV lung cancer, and his ECOG functional status is 1. The patient has been referred for chemotherapy, and he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the association between the number of circulating tumor cells and response to treatment in non small-cell lung cancer patients.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has been diagnosed with colorectal cancer and needs to undergo a radical resection surgery. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He has no other significant medical history. He is able to communicate and understand the study procedures. The patient is able to complete the pain VAS evaluation and cognitive function assessment. The patient has signed the informed consent form to participate in the study.

62 yo M with a long-standing history of osteoarthritis of the knee, currently experiencing severe pain in the right knee with a Kellgren Lawrence Grade IV diagnosis. The patient has completed the AP-003-C Main Study and is willing to participate in the Open Label Extension study to assess the safety of long-term treatment with Ampion ™. The patient is ambulatory, able to provide written informed consent, and willing to comply with all study requirements and instructions of the site study staff. The patient has moderate to moderately-severe OA pain and function in the study knee, with a rating of at least 1.5 on the WOMAC Index 3.1 5-point Likert Pain and Function Subscales. The patient has a WOMAC A, 5-point Likert pain subscale <1.5 in the contralateral knee and is able to discontinue NSAID ± 72 hours before/after injections (in-office visits). Low-dose Aspirin (81 mg) is allowed during the study but must not be taken at least 24 hours prior to in-office visits. The patient has not taken any analgesia (including acetaminophen [paracetamol]) 24 hours prior to an efficacy measure. Moreover, the patient has no known clinically significant liver abnormality, history of allergic reactions to human albumin or excipients in 5% human albumin, presence of tense effusions, inflammatory or crystal arthropathies, acute fractures, history of aseptic necrosis or joint replacement in the affected knee. The patient is not suffering from isolated patella femoral syndrome or any other disease or condition interfering with the free use and evaluation of the index knee for the duration of the trial, and has not experienced any major injury to the index knee within the last 12 months. The patient is not suffering from severe hip osteoarthritis ipsilateral to the index knee or any pain that could interfere with the assessment of study knee pain. The patient is not taking any pharmacological or non-pharmacological treatment targeting OA and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study. Finally, the patient is not using IA injected pain medications in the study knee during the study, no analgesics containing opioids, and no topical treatment on the study knee during the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been living with HIV for the past 10 years. He works as a librarian and spends most of his day sitting at his desk. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and has been clinically stable for the past 6 months with an undetectable viral load. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels but is not currently taking any medication for these conditions. He reports mild memory and concentration difficulties, which have been affecting his work performance and quality of life. He is fluent in English and lives independently in the Atlanta area. He does not engage in any structured exercise program and exercises less than 3 times a week for a minimum of 30 minutes. He does not participate in any weight loss program and has not been hospitalized in the last 60 days. He is willing to participate in the study and has a screening MOCA score of 22, indicating mild cognitive impairment. He does not have any medical or physical condition that would preclude him from participating in the exercise component of the study. He is not on corticosteroids and does not have any current opportunistic infection. He is not pregnant and does not have any severe learning disabilities, intellectual disabilities, or psychotic disorders that may affect his participation in the trial.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis seven years ago. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of weakness and numbness in her legs, as well as bladder and bowel dysfunction. Despite receiving treatment with interferons and other immunomodulatory drugs, her symptoms have been progressively worsening, and she has had two severe relapses during the past year. Her EDSS score is currently 5.5, and she is resistant to further drug therapy. She has no history of cytotoxic or immunomodulatory drug treatment during the past three months. She is not pregnant and has not had a relapse in the past 30 days. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the safety and feasibility of autologous mesenchymal stem cell transplantation for multiple sclerosis.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman, with no significant medical history except for mild hypertension, presents to the clinic with complaints of difficulty maintaining balance and fear of falling. She reports that her balance issues have worsened in the past few months and she has had a few near-falls. She is able to walk independently but feels unsteady at times. She denies any history of falls or fractures. She is currently not taking any medications that affect balance. She has never undergone any regular exercise program in the past. She is a non-smoker and reports social alcohol consumption. She has no history of neurological, muscular, or rheumatologic disease. She is not using an assistive walking device or any hearing aids. Her BMI is 27. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of PNF and Frenkel's exercises on balance, fall risk, and quality of life in postmenopausal women.

25-year-old healthy male with no history of HIV infection, currently living in the United States. The patient has access to a participating HIV Vaccine Trials Network (HVTN) clinical research site and is willing to be followed for the planned duration of the study. He is able and willing to provide informed consent and demonstrates understanding of the study. The patient has good general health, as shown by medical history, physical exam, and screening laboratory tests, and is at low risk for HIV infection. He has a hemoglobin level of 14.5 g/dL, a white blood cell count of 7,000 cells/mm^3, and a normal chemistry panel. The patient has not received any blood products or investigational research agents within the past 120 days and has not received any live attenuated vaccines other than influenza vaccine in the past 30 days. He has not received any non-HIV experimental vaccines within the past 5 years and does not have any immune system disorders or clinically significant medical conditions. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently on any immunosuppressive medications. He is willing to receive HIV test results and to discuss HIV infection risks and amenable to HIV risk reduction counseling. The patient is sexually active and agrees to consistently use effective contraception for sexual activity that could lead to pregnancy from at least 21 days prior to enrollment through the last required protocol clinic visit. He is willing to be contacted annually after completion of scheduled clinic visits for a total of 3 years following initial study injection.

10-year-old female with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment. She presents with a fever of 101.5°F and an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 200/microliter. She has been on broad-spectrum antibiotics for the past 4 days with no improvement in her fever. Her treating physician suspects a fungal infection and recommends empirical therapy with an intravenous anti-fungal agent. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial comparing MK0991 and liposomal amphotericin B for empirical therapy in febrile, neutropenic pediatric patients.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 14 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a family history of allergies, including eczema, asthma, and rhinitis. She has never been a regular consumer of oily fish, consuming less than two portions per month, and is not currently taking any fish oil supplements. She has no history of diabetes, autoimmune diseases, or mental health problems. She is willing to have essential identifiable information stored for tracking purposes during the study. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that by increasing her salmon intake during pregnancy, she can help reduce the risk of her child developing atopic diseases.

The patient is a 52-year-old female of Hispanic origin, who was found unconscious by her family in the morning. She was immediately brought to the hospital, where the initial evaluation revealed signs of left-sided weakness and difficulty in speaking. The CT scan showed an acute ischemic stroke involving the right middle cerebral artery territory. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently on medications including lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. The vital signs are stable, with blood pressure of 140/80 mmHg and heart rate of 80 beats per minute. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her informed consent.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant living in Berekum District, Ghana. He weighs 7 kg and is 67 cm long. He is currently attending well baby clinic and is suspected to be at risk for anemia. His mother reports that he has been exclusively breastfed, but he has recently started eating porridge made from maize flour. His mother has been advised to bring him back to the clinic every two months for check-ups. The baby is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions or history of hospitalization. He is not known to be G6PD deficient.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with moderate to severe inflammatory acne vulgaris. She has a history of acne since her teenage years and has been using various topical and systemic treatments with limited success. She currently has 35 facial inflammatory acne lesions and 15 comedos. She has no nodular cystic lesions. She is not pregnant and has a regular menstrual cycle. She has no known hypersensitivity to any components in Tazarac gel or to any tetracyclines. She has not used any systemic antibiotics or topical anti-acne medication in the past 30 days. She is not currently participating in another drug or investigational study. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with neoplastic disease in the left colon. He has been scheduled for a left laparoscopic colectomy and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists Classification (ASA) score of I. He resides less than 30 minutes away from La Rochelle hospital and will have a companion with him from the anaesthesia consultation onwards. He has a good understanding of outpatient care, his pathology and the surgical procedure, as does his companion. He has been informed of the study and is willing to participate. He is not currently taking any anticoagulant treatment and has not experienced any anaphylaxis or difficult intubation during previous procedures. He agrees to close monitoring by a home care nurse twice daily after his discharge on the same day as his surgery.

Patient is a 26-year-old male who suffered a lateral ankle sprain while playing basketball a year ago. Since then, he has experienced recurrent episodes of giving way, swelling, and pain in his ankle. He has been diagnosed with chronic ankle instability by a physician and has been advised to seek further treatment to improve his postural control ability. He is otherwise healthy with no history of neurological or vestibular disorders. He is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the reliability and validity of a smart-phone based system in postural control ability assessment.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman with a recently diagnosed stage II breast cancer. She has undergone a lumpectomy and is scheduled to start her first round of chemotherapy next week. She lives alone and works as a teacher at a local high school. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are managed with medication. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is fluent in English and has no trouble communicating. She is not pregnant and has never had a tracheostomy. She is concerned about the potential side effects of chemotherapy and is interested in participating in a study that may help her manage them better.

The patient is a 56-year-old Hispanic man with a history of hepatic cirrhosis of unknown etiology. He had a previous variceal bleeding episode that was treated with endoscopic eradication therapy 3 weeks ago. He has a history of alcohol abuse, but he has been sober for the past 6 months. He is not using any drugs or smoking. His medical history is positive for hypertension that is well controlled with lisinopril 20mg daily. His family history is negative for any liver disease or bleeding disorders. His physical examination reveals mild ascites and splenomegaly. His laboratory tests reveal a total bilirubin of 2.0 mg/dL, creatinine clearance of 75 mL/min, platelet count of 90,000/uL and INR of 1.3. His Child-Pugh score is 10 and his MELD score is 16. His HVPG measurement is 15 mmHg.

A 35-year-old woman has been struggling with severe depression for several years. She has tried multiple antidepressants, augmentation agents, and even electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) but has not seen any lasting improvement. She has a history of multiple suicide attempts and has been hospitalized several times due to her depression. She has undergone trials of psychotherapy and other interventions lacking definitive evidence of efficacy in severe depression. She is currently drug-free and has good general health. She is willing to comply with the operational and administrative requirements of participation in the study, including undergoing preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and an awake operation. She is not pregnant and is using effective contraception. She is not participating in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who recently underwent an elective orthopedic surgical procedure for the definitive management of a fracture. She is being discharged from Children's Hospital in London, Ontario with a prescription for pain medication to manage post-operative pain. She has no known allergies to any medications and has never taken ibuprofen or morphine before. Her parents are willing to have her participate in a clinical trial that will compare the effectiveness of oral morphine versus ibuprofen for post-operative pain management in children. She is able to communicate and understand English fluently and has no known medical conditions that would exclude her from the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing moderate to severe chronic pain in his lower back for the past year. He has been prescribed Tylenol® #3 (acetaminophen 300mg with codeine phosphate 30mg) by his primary care physician to manage his pain. He is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He has not been diagnosed with HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C. He does not have a history of allergic or adverse response to codeine sulfate or any comparable or similar product. He is not currently taking any enzyme-altering drugs. He is willing to participate in the study to assess the comparative bioavailability of codeine from Roxane Laboratories' Codeine Sulfate 30mg tablets to Tylenol® #3 under fasted conditions.

A 35-year-old woman underwent a cesarean section delivery 6 months ago and developed a hypertrophic scar at the incision site. The scar is about 5 cm2 in size, red, and causes severe itching and discomfort. She tried various over-the-counter creams and ointments, but none have provided significant relief. She has no history of intralesional injections for the scar. She has no known allergies to Botulinum toxin type A or steroids. She is not immunocompromised and has no current systemic infections. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially alleviate her symptoms and improve the appearance of her scar.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with ovarian cancer six months ago, and despite undergoing standard therapy, her cancer has progressed. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She complains of fatigue, abdominal pain, and bloating. She underwent a biopsy, which confirmed HER2-positive refractory ovarian cancer. Her ECOG score is 1, and she has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1. She has no history of brain metastasis, active infection, or other systemic illness. Her QT interval is normal, and she is not pregnant or lactating. She has never received lapatinib in the past.

A 65-year-old man came to the clinic for a follow-up appointment for his osteoarthritis pain. He has been taking naproxen 500mg twice a day for the past 6 months, but he finds that the pain is still not well-controlled, especially during the night. He has no history of substance abuse or addiction. The patient has mild hypertension, which is controlled with lisinopril 10mg daily. He has no history of any other significant medical problems, allergies, or adverse reactions to medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is not scheduled to have any surgery or dental procedures during the study period.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 4 months. He has experienced symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He has tried various medications, including mesalamine and corticosteroids, however, they have not provided significant relief. He started on infliximab 14 weeks ago, but has not achieved remission. He has not had any prior surgeries related to his ulcerative colitis and does not have any other underlying medical conditions. He is currently not using any form of contraception and is sexually active. He is willing to use two forms of contraception during the study period. He has no history of sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. He is not currently taking any other medications or participating in any other clinical trials.

A 56-year-old male with a history of advanced solid tumor that has metastasized to his liver, lungs, and bones is eligible for this clinical trial. He has already undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but his condition has not improved. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no history of brain metastasis, spinal cord compression or carcinomatous meningitis. He has not undergone any major surgery within the last month and his surgical wounds have fully healed. He has good organ function but has a history of peptic ulcer disease. He has not received abdominal radiotherapy and has not received high cumulative doses of anthracycline. He is not currently undergoing any other anticancer therapy.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather endoscopists accredited to perform colonoscopies within the Dutch Nationwide colorectal cancer screening program. Therefore, there is no patient description needed for this trial.

Patient B is a 14-year-old female who has just completed orthodontic treatment with fixed orthodontic appliances. She had a non-extraction treatment plan and had moderate crowding in her mandibular arch with an irregularity index of 4mm. She had Class II molar relationship at the beginning of her treatment. She has no missing teeth, impacted teeth, or other dental anomalies. She does not have any congenital anomalies or syndromes. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend all follow-up appointments for up to 5 years.

A 64-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. He has had a history of back pain and was found to have multiple vertebral fractures. The patient has been treated with vertebroplasty for two of these fractures. He reports that he has been feeling better since the procedure. He is currently receiving chemotherapy and has completed radiation therapy for a previous rib lesion. He does not have any neurological deficits or loss of sensation in his limbs. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His family history is unremarkable. The patient's medications include dexamethasone and lenalidomide. He has been experiencing fatigue, but otherwise, he is able to perform his daily activities. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. MRI scans of his spine will be done to measure vertebral bone marrow fat fraction and assess the correlation with bone fragility represented by a severity score of vertebral fractures.

A 28-year-old woman presents at 39 weeks of gestation with her second pregnancy. Her first delivery was a vaginal delivery with epidural anesthesia. She reports regular contractions every 5-7 minutes since last night. She has not experienced any complications during the pregnancy and her prenatal visits have been unremarkable. She is married and has a supportive partner who will be present during labor. She is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. She expresses concerns about pain management and anxiety during labor. She is interested in participating in clinical trials that could help improve her labor experience. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study as a multiparous woman in spontaneous active labor with a cephalic presentation. She has no known psychiatric disorders and her labor is not induced. Her dilation at admission is 4cm. The fetus has no prenatally diagnosed anomalies and is expected to be discharged normally.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage 3 colon cancer. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both well-controlled with medication. He is currently receiving chemotherapy treatment and requires parenteral nutrition due to difficulties with eating and digesting food. He has been recommended to undergo the placement of an implantable catheter for his infusion therapy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to prevent infections related to the catheter. He is not currently receiving any other preventive measures for catheter-related infections and is not allergic to citrate or taurolidine. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and is willing to sign the consent form.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. He has already received androgen deprivation therapy, but his cancer has progressed, and he is now asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic. He will be starting treatment with either abiraterone acetate or enzalutamide. He has not received any chemotherapy or cytotoxic agent for the treatment of his mCRPC before, and he is not currently receiving any investigational treatment for prostate cancer. He is able to complete patient surveys and has signed the participation agreement or informed consent form per local regulations. He is not currently included in any other observational studies with abiraterone acetate sponsored by Janssen.

This is a 48-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer six months ago. She underwent surgery and is currently receiving chemotherapy. She has been experiencing emotional distress and has been having trouble sleeping since her diagnosis. She was approached by phone to participate in a clinical study that aims to evaluate the feasibility and impact of group interventions on breast cancer patients' well-being. She was given a choice between three group interventions: cognitive-behavioral therapy, yoga, and self-hypnosis. She chose to participate in the yoga group intervention. Before starting the intervention, she completed a baseline assessment including self-reported measures. She attended all six sessions of the intervention and completed follow-up assessments at 1 week, 3 months, and 9 months after the end of the intervention. The study aims to evaluate the benefits of the intervention on emotional distress, quality of life, sleep quality, and mental adjustment to cancer. The patient did not have any diagnosed psychiatric disorder or dementia and had the ability to read, write, and speak French.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of smoking for the past 40 years. He has been experiencing respiratory symptoms for the past week, including cough, shortness of breath, and chest tightness. He has not been on any long-term maintenance therapy for his COPD. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. He denies any history of asthma, cystic fibrosis, bronchiectasis, interstitial lung disease, or pulmonary thromboembolic disease. He has not had any significant cardiac events in the past six months and has no history of tuberculosis or severe respiratory infections requiring hospitalization. He is able to independently read and understand English and has no visual impairment that would prevent him from completing the required questionnaires and electronic diary. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to inhale medication from the HandiHaler® device and metered dose inhaler (MDI).

45 year-old male with a single implant-supported crown placed in 2009 due to tooth loss resulting from trauma. He is an English-speaking professional who maintains a busy work schedule. He reports brushing twice a day with a manual toothbrush and using dental floss occasionally. He has not seen a dentist in the past year but reports no pain, bleeding, or swelling in his mouth. He has never been diagnosed with periodontal disease, diabetes, or any other systemic diseases. He does not smoke or use any tobacco products. He has no history of radiation therapy or drug abuse. He is interested in learning more about how to maintain good oral hygiene practices and take care of his dental implant to ensure its longevity.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU for severe shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was previously healthy and did not smoke. The patient reports that the symptoms started approximately 5 days ago and have progressively worsened. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated. The chest X-ray showed bilateral opacities. The arterial blood gas analysis showed a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 150. The patient meets the Berlin definition of moderate to severe ARDS. The patient is not pregnant, has no history of COPD, is not on immunosuppressive therapy, and does not have onco-hematological disease or HIV. The patient has social insurance and has provided informed consent signed by his next of kin. The patient is a good candidate for the ARDS-Markers of Inflammation-Strain clinical trial.

56 y/o with end-stage renal disease on nocturnal in-center hemodialysis three times per week. The patient lives in close proximity to Stanford University and VA Palo Alto for easy access to the clinical trial site. The patient has not recently used antibiotics and does not have any gastrointestinal disease. The patient is seeking to improve their overall health and is willing to participate in the clinical trial designed to test the effects of a new method to improve the removal of protein-bound solutes during dialysis.

16-year-old female who is obese with a BMI of 32.5 (95th percentile for age) and has a history of prediabetes. She has been attending the ADOBE clinic at the University of Missouri for the past year for weight management. She takes a standard multi-vitamin preparation that contains 400 IU of vitamin D daily. Her 25OH vitamin D level was checked within the past three months and was found to be 20 ng/mL. She has no history of hepatic or renal disorders, hypercalciuria, or hypercalcemia. She is not currently taking any medications that interfere with vitamin D metabolism and is not undergoing UV radiation as medical therapy. She is not pregnant and does not smoke or use tanning beds. She is not currently taking any antihyperglycemic medications. She is interested in participating in the study and has obtained assent from her parent.

An 80-year-old Mexican American woman comes to the clinic for her routine check-up. She mentions that she has been experiencing mild joint pain and difficulty sleeping. She reports having a history of using various herbal remedies, including chamomile tea, for her sleep problems and arnica cream for her joint pain. She also mentions using other traditional remedies such as eucalyptus oil for congestion and aloe vera for skin irritations. She has been using these remedies for several years and finds them helpful. She has no significant medical history, no chronic illnesses, and takes no prescription medications. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the use of complementary and alternative medicine among older Mexican Americans.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with an ovarian cyst during a routine ultrasound examination. The cyst is between 3cm and 10cm in size and needs to be removed by cyst enucleation. She has regular menstrual cycles with a cycle length between 25 and 35 days. She has not undergone any previous ovarian surgery and there is no suspicion of malignancy. She has not reached menopause and has not used oral contraceptive drugs, GnRH agonist /antagonist, or other drugs related to ovarian function in the last 3 months. The patient has agreed to be enrolled in the study to investigate the impact on ovarian reserve after single-port, two-port, or four-port access laparoscopic ovarian cyst enucleation based on serum anti mullerian hormone change. Serum anti mullerian hormone will be measured at preoperative and postoperative 1 week, 1 and 3 months to evaluate ovarian reserve change.

The patient is a 45-year-old male from a township in Cape Town, South Africa. He presents to the primary health care clinic with symptoms of cough for the past three weeks, accompanied by fever and night sweats. He reports a weight loss of 5 kg in the last three months. The patient has no positive history of drug allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient has not received any TB treatment in the past 90 days nor has he received any immune suppressive therapy. His hemoglobin level is within normal limits. He is willing to give informed consent and undergoes HIV testing. He has a permanent address in the study area and has been living there for more than three months.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has a history of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. He underwent a cardiac evaluation which revealed significant blockages in his coronary arteries. He is currently on medications for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. He has a history of smoking and quit 10 years ago. He is retired and lives with his wife in a suburban area. He enjoys gardening and walking in the park. He has no history of peripheral vascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, or renal insufficiency. His creatinine level is within the normal range. His ejection fraction is 50%. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical knowledge and improve outcomes for patients with coronary artery disease.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who enjoys cooking and experimenting with different flavors in her meals. She is generally in good health and has no known taste abnormalities. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She works as a graphic designer and spends her free time trying out new recipes or going to farmers' markets. She has no known allergies to food or medications. Her physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable. She is interested in participating in this study to help improve the understanding of the taste of fatty acids in food.

A 55-year-old female with a history of Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) comes to the clinic with a complaint of worsening cough and shortness of breath. She was previously treated with erlotinib but her disease progressed after 6 months. A tissue biopsy confirmed the presence of an EGFR mutation and T790M mutation within the EGFR gene. The patient has not received any further treatment and is currently chemotherapy naive. She has a World Health Organization (WHO) performance status of 1 and has at least one measurable lesion that has not been previously irradiated. The patient is eligible to receive treatment with the selected doublet-chemotherapy and has been confirmed to have T790M+ mutation status through central confirmation. The patient is willing to provide a biopsy for central confirmation of T790 mutation status following confirmed disease progression on their first line EGFR-TKI treatment. The patient meets all other inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has not met any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been receiving treatment for diabetes with metformin and insulin injections. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease, with his father and grandfather both having had heart attacks in their 50s. He has undergone haptoglobin genotyping and has been found to have the Hp 2-2 phenotype. His HbA1c levels have been difficult to control, despite changes in his medication regimen and adherence to dietary and exercise recommendations. He has never experienced a cardiovascular event, but his primary care physician is concerned about his increased genetic susceptibility for such events and wants to enroll him in this clinical trial to investigate the associations between diabetes care and haptoglobin genotype on outcomes. The patient is willing to participate and has provided informed consent for the ICARE study and registry.

32-year-old Korean female with a BMI of 31.5 kg/m² who has been struggling with weight loss for several years. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She has no known comorbidities or allergies to medication. She has agreed to follow a low-calorie diet during the trial and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use proper contraception during the study period. She does not have a history of smoking cessation within the last 3 months and is not currently smoking irregularly. She does not have endocrine diseases associated with weight gain, such as hypothyroidism, Cushing's syndrome, etc. She has no history of heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes, severe renal or liver disability, or any other medical conditions that preclude her from participating in the study. She is not currently taking any medication that can affect her weight or is contraindicated for the trial. She has no history of eating disorders or other psychological conditions that may affect her participation in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old Chinese man who was diagnosed with a pancreatic pseudocyst after experiencing severe abdominal pain and bloating. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. He is currently unemployed and lives with his wife and two children. He has a BMI of 28.5 and has been trying to lose weight by changing his diet and exercising regularly. His lab results show elevated levels of amylase and lipase. The pseudocyst has a diameter of 7cm and is located in the tail of the pancreas. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially avoid surgery and seek a minimally invasive treatment. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to comply with all follow-up evaluations. He does not have any coagulation disorders or abnormal anatomy that would preclude the delivery of the stent. He does not have any other medical conditions that would interfere with the endpoints of the study.

54-year-old male diagnosed with nasopharyngeal cancer, scheduled to undergo IMRT at MD Anderson. He has anatomically intact parotid and submandibular glands and a Karnofsky performance status of 70. The patient is right-handed and has no history of xerostomia prior to radiation therapy or underlying systemic illness known to cause xerostomia. He has not received prior head and neck radiation treatment and has no suspected or confirmed physical closure of salivary gland ducts. The patient has no known bleeding disorders, is not taking warfarin or heparin, and has no upper or lower extremity deformities that could interfere with accurate acupoint location. He has no local skin infections or active systemic infection. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident or spinal cord injury. His mental status is normal, and he has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient has not received acupuncture for any condition and has no prior experience with acupuncture.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who had a heart attack two years ago. She has since then undergone a cardiac rehabilitation program and has been advised to exercise regularly to improve her heart health. She speaks German fluently and is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative exercise options. She has no severe pneumatological or psychiatric disorders, but she does have mild cognitive impairment. She is currently taking medications for hypertension and high cholesterol, and her cardiologist has approved her participation in the study. She enjoys gardening and walking in her free time.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who was admitted to the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) ACE unit with an admitting diagnosis of congestive heart failure. He lives within 30 miles of UTMB and is able to walk across a small room with or without the aid of an assistive device. He can stand without assistance at the time of pretesting and presents no medical contraindication to wearing a loose fitting velcro strap for the accelerometer on one ankle

A 45-year-old woman came to the Emergency Room with severe neck pain that started 3 days ago. She describes her pain as aching and dull, with a pain scale of 7 out of 10. She has no history of trauma or other medical conditions. She took over-the-counter painkillers with no significant relief. She is a teacher and spends long hours grading papers and using the computer. Her physical examination reveals tenderness in the cervical spine with a limited range of motion. X-ray showed no structural abnormalities. She has not received chiropractic treatment in the past. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to fill out questionnaires about her pain levels and anxiety. She understands the nature of the study and is willing to sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 58 year old male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of hematuria (blood in urine) for the past 2 months. He visited his urologist and underwent a cystoscopy which revealed a superficial bladder tumor. Biopsy confirmed the presence of transitional cell carcinoma. He has no significant past medical history and is currently taking only a multivitamin supplement. He does not have any history of smoking or alcohol consumption. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness over the suprapubic region. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 90%. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including serum creatinine, liver function tests, and complete blood count. He has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of gemcitabine. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form. He is available for follow-up visits and resides within a reasonable distance from the study site.

A 65-year-old man with a history of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia (CLL) according to International Workshop for Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (IWCLL) 2008 criteria documented in medical records. He has undergone at least two prior treatment regimens for CLL including at least 4 cycles of chemo-immunotherapy containing a CD20-targeting monoclonal antibody, i.e. at least 4 doses of a monoclonal antibody and at least 4 doses of a cytotoxic AND a B-cell receptor pathway inhibitor. He has a clinically quantifiable disease burden defined as either Absolute Lymphocyte Count (ALC) >10x10^9/L, or measurable lymphadenopathy (at least one node > 2 cm on Computed Tomography (CT) scan) or quantifiable bone marrow infiltration documented in a bone marrow biopsy during screening if applicable. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score is 1. He has resolved all clinically relevant acute non-hematologic toxic effects of any prior antitumour therapy to Grade <=1 with the exception of alopecia or neurotoxicity (Grade 1 or 2 neurotoxicity permitted) prior to the first dose of venetoclax. He is a male patient of full age (according to local legislation, usually >= 18 years) at screening. He is ready and able to use highly effective methods of birth control per International Conference on Harmonisation (ICH) M3 (R2) that result in a low failure rate of less than 1% per year when used consistently and correctly. He has signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with International Conference on Harmonisation - Good Clinical Practice (ICH-GCP) and local legislation prior to admission to the trial.

Pt is a 10yo male who presents to the Emergency Department with a non-life-threatening injury. Pt is accompanied by biological mother and is stable as per triage. Pt has no prior history of behavioral health concerns or diagnoses. The study team will approach the family to participate in a study to determine the prevalence of unidentified mental health issues in the pediatric population that visits the Emergency Department. The study will involve completing a questionnaire, the DISC Predictive Scales, Version IV (DPS-IV), to assess for emotional issues in children and adolescents. Additionally, for children aged 9-17, the study will assess families' readiness to seek care when a problem is indicated.

The patient is a 67-year-old man who recently noticed that his vision in his left eye is not as sharp as it used to be. He has a history of high blood pressure, but otherwise, he is in good health. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. His family history is negative for eye diseases. His best-corrected visual acuity in the left eye is 20/60. An ophthalmic examination revealed a well-demarcated area of geographic atrophy in the macula of his left eye, measuring approximately 2 disc areas in size. The lesion is secondary to age-related macular degeneration, and there is no evidence of choroidal neovascularization. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of microperimetry and SS-OCT in assessing the natural changes of retinal sensitivity and anatomy in the perilesional zone of geographic atrophy areas.

A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman comes to the clinic complaining of heavy and prolonged bleeding after menopause. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. The patient underwent a biopsy which showed endometrial cancer. She is scheduled for an MRI to assess the extent of the cancer. However, due to her claustrophobia, she is unable to complete the MRI scan. She is offered participation in a clinical trial that will assess the use of 3D ultrasound as an alternative to MRI to assess myometrial invasion in endometrial cancer. The study will involve an additional 1-2 minutes of ultrasound scan time to obtain 3D ultrasound images. The patient is deemed eligible for the trial and agrees to participate. The saved 3D ultrasound images will be analyzed and compared to the gold standard test (histological examination) to assess the depth of spread of the cancer. The results of the 3D ultrasound will be compared to the MRI report and final histology. The aim of the study is to assess the diagnostic accuracy of 3D ultrasound compared to MRI and final histology with respect to myometrial invasion of endometrial cancer.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman who is currently 38 weeks and 5 days pregnant with a singleton, vertex presentation is seeking epidural anesthesia for pain relief during labor. She has no contraindications to neuraxial analgesia and is willing to provide informed consent. She has no history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reaction to local anesthetics or opioids. She is in good health with no significant medical conditions. She is currently at 4 cm cervical dilation and is experiencing mild to moderate pain. She has no risk factors significantly increasing the need for Cesarean delivery or anticipated fetal abnormalities. She is an ASA 2 patient and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old African American woman who has recently been diagnosed with a lung tumor. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and occasional coughing for the past few months. She is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago after smoking a pack a day for 20 years. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and she is otherwise healthy. Her vital signs are stable and within normal limits. She has been referred to the Department of Radiation Oncology for further evaluation and treatment planning. She is able to lie flat on her back for extended periods of time without difficulty. She has been advised of the study and has provided consent to participate. She will undergo 4D CT scans with audio and visual biofeedback to improve the accuracy of radiation treatment for her lung tumor.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is in good health, has no history of chronic illnesses, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has had regular prenatal care and all her ultrasounds have been normal. She is currently at a gestational age of 30 weeks and is scheduled for a planned C-section due to her baby's breech position. The C-section is planned to take place in a tertiary care hospital with a neonatal intensive care unit. The patient has given written consent to participate in a clinical trial that aims to assess aldosterone resistance in preterm infants. The trial will involve collecting urine samples from her newborn within the first 24 hours of birth, as well as on day three, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months postpartum. Blood samples will also be collected from the umbilical cord at birth and during the Guthrie test at day three. The trial will include 240 newborns, classified into four groups based on gestational age, and the patient's newborn will be included in the group with a gestational age of 28 - < 33 weeks.
