The aim of the trial is to evaluate the intensity of aldosterone resistance in preterm newborns and to determine normal values of urinary aldosterone concentration in each group. The patient's newborn will be closely monitored throughout the first year of life, and plasma and urinary electrolyte concentrations, as well as aldosterone and renin concentrations, will be measured in the hospital laboratory. The trial will provide new insights into the mechanisms of hormonal regulation of sodium balance in preterm newborns and may open new perspectives for therapeutic management of water and sodium waste in premature infants.

The patient is a 23-year-old healthy male who regularly engages in physical activities such as running and weightlifting. He is 178 cm tall and weighs 75 kg. He has no history of musculoskeletal injuries or neurological diseases. He is a university student majoring in physical education and has a keen interest in optimizing his physical performance. He reports that he typically warms up for physical activity by performing static stretching exercises, but is open to trying dynamic stretching if it is found to be more effective. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the prescribed stretching regimen.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing headaches and visual disturbances for the past six months. He visited his primary care physician and was referred to a neurologist for further evaluation. An MRI of the brain revealed a large pituitary adenoma with a Ki67 labeling index greater than 3%. The patient underwent surgical resection of the tumor at Tohoku University Hospital. Post-operative pathology confirmed the diagnosis of an atypical pituitary adenoma. The patient has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. He is interested in participating in this study to help contribute to the understanding of this rare and aggressive type of pituitary adenoma, and to potentially help future patients with this condition.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who works as a teacher in a secondary school in Tunisia. He has a family history of heart disease, and his father had a heart attack at the age of 60. The patient is overweight with a BMI of 31. He has a sedentary lifestyle and rarely exercises. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not been diagnosed with any chronic diseases but has high blood pressure that is being treated with medication. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about his risk for cardiovascular disease and to contribute to the national effort to prevent heart disease.

A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease presents to the clinic with symptoms of heart failure, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and orthopnea. He is currently on guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and diuretics. The patient reports a history of a myocardial infarction 2 years ago and has had 2 hospitalizations for heart failure in the past year. His most recent NT-proBNP level is 1,200 pg/mL, and his echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 40%. The echocardiogram also confirms moderate aortic stenosis with an aortic valve area of 1.2 cm2 and a mean gradient of 30 mmHg. He is otherwise stable and able to perform activities of daily living. He has a BMI of 29 kg/m2. He is willing to participate in the study and provides independent informed consent.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy with a diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). He has a history of hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention, which has caused difficulty in school and at home. He is currently being treated with a medication for ADHD, but his symptoms are not well-controlled. He has no significant medical history, and no history of cardiac or other major illnesses. He has no cognitive impairment or other psychiatric diagnoses. He is a well-nourished and alert child who is cooperative during the evaluation. The patient and his family are willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of new medication NT0102 for the treatment of ADHD. The patient is not taking any disallowed medications, and there is no evidence of positive drug test.

56-year-old male with a newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer with mediastinal nodal involvement. He is scheduled to undergo radiation treatment with a minimum of 45 Gy. The patient has no history of esophageal motility disorders but does have a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease treated with proton pump inhibitors. He has no current symptoms related to his esophagus. The patient is able to understand and comply with swallowing instructions for the esophageal manometry procedure. He is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III serous epithelial ovarian carcinoma. She underwent primary cytoreductive surgery, during which macroscopic cytoreduction was achieved. She is currently undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is platinum-sensitive. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her performance status is good, with a Karnofsky index of 80%. She has no major cardiac or respiratory disease, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is highly motivated to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 30-year-old female who recently experienced a sudden onset of low back pain while lifting a heavy object at work. The pain has been persistent for the past three days despite taking over-the-counter pain medications. The patient is currently unable to stand or sit for long periods of time and has difficulty walking without support. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment for acute low back pain. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study assessments scheduled in the protocol.

A 19-year-old woman was admitted to the obstetrics ward at 25 weeks of gestation with the complaint of lower abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is a primigravida with no significant medical history. The ultrasound revealed a single live fetus with a gestational age of 24 weeks and 5 days. The fetal biometric measurements including biparietal diameter (BPD), head circumference (HC), abdominal circumference (AC), and femur length (FL) were within normal range. The patient was treated for threatened preterm labor and discharged with strict bed rest and follow-up appointments. At 26 weeks and 4 days of gestation, she delivered a preterm male infant with a birth weight of 960 grams. The infant had no congenital anomalies, and Apgar scores were 6 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The anterior lens capsule vascularity (ALCV) of the infant was measured using a smartphone ophthalmoscope within 24 hours of delivery. The parents provided written informed consent for the infant's participation in the study. The infant will be followed up for biophysical parameters appropriate for gestational age and ALCV-based gestational age estimates.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding for the past few months. She has a medical history of hypertension and is otherwise healthy. After undergoing several tests and examinations, her gynecologist has recommended a total abdominal hysterectomy to address her condition. The patient has been booked for the procedure at Southern Health and has been offered the opportunity to participate in a randomized control trial comparing the use of traditional clamp and suture technique versus the newer electrocoagulation forceps, specifically the gyrus open seal forceps, curved. The patient will receive detailed information about the study and will have the option to provide consent for participation. The trial aims to determine if using the newer electrocoagulation forceps will lead to a reduction in operating time, intra-operative blood loss, and post-operative pain compared to the traditional technique. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility for the trial based on her medical history and the presence of suspected benign pathology.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with evidence of progressive, locally advanced or metastatic disease. The patient has received prior chemotherapy that included a platinum agent and has demonstrated tumor progression. The patient has at least one measurable lesion outside the field of any prior radiotherapy. The patient has no symptomatic brain metastases or other concurrent severe or uncontrolled underlying medical disease that would compromise patient safety and study outcome. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 0-2 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has recovered from prior chemotherapy and radiotherapy and has not undergone any major surgery in the past four weeks. The patient is not currently receiving any other anticancer treatments and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has normal hematopoietic, hepatic, renal, and cardiac function. The patient is willing to use effective contraception if fertile and has no psychiatric disorder that would preclude giving informed consent or following study instruction.

The patient is a 27-year-old female diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) at the age of 14. Despite her efforts to adhere to a strict insulin regimen, her blood glucose levels have remained poorly controlled with an HbA1c of 8.5% for the past year. She has been attending regular follow-up visits with the Endocrinology department, with an average of 5 visits each year. She is currently using insulin pens for her insulin administration. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the impact of an electronic device called Insulclock on her glycemic control and treatment compliance. She is willing to learn how to use the device and the mobile application, and to fill in the questionnaires required by the study protocol. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse or acute infection. The patient is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that the study would help her improve her glycemic control and overall quality of life.

A 45 year old man with genotype 1 hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is seeking treatment for his condition. He has not received any previous treatment with interferon or ribavirin. The patient shows willingness to participate in the study and agrees to comply with its procedures by signing a written informed consent. He has a serum TNF-alpha level >300 pg/mL (single measure at Pre-Screen Visit). The patient has a liver biopsy within 24 months of enrolment demonstrating Stage 0-3 fibrosis (Metavir System). He has compensated liver disease with normal hematological, biochemical, and serological criteria at the screen visit. The patient is a non-pregnant male and does not have any past or present psychiatric condition that could interfere with the subject's participation in and completion of the study. He is not using any illicit drugs and is willing to record, study medication compliance, concomitant medications, and adverse events accurately and consistently in a daily diary. The patient is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control if applicable.

A 5-year-old boy is scheduled for an elective hernia repair surgery on his lower abdomen. He has no significant medical history, and his parents report no allergies or adverse reactions to medications or anesthesia. The child is developmentally appropriate for his age and is able to follow simple instructions. He has no history of bleeding disorders or cardiac, neurological, renal or hepatic diseases. The patient's parents have given informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old female with a history of primary liver cancer. She has been diagnosed with a single tumor measuring 4 cm in diameter, which is in contact with the right hepatic vein at the caval confluence. Her liver function tests are within normal limits, and she has no other significant medical history. She is scheduled for hepatic resection of the right hepatic vein and intraoperative ultrasound exploration for the detection of communicating veins between adjacent hepatic veins. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 15-year-old female high school student who attends a school in the Vulindlela School Circuit in rural KwaZulu-Natal. She is currently in Grade 10 and is willing to participate in the study. She reports being sexually active and has had multiple sexual partners in the past. She is aware of the risk of HIV transmission and wants to learn more about how to protect herself from getting infected. The patient is willing to provide locator data for home visits if necessary, and she is willing to be finger-printed to verify her identity for study purposes. She has no plans to move to another school or relocate in the next 36 months. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to complete all study procedures. She has no cognitive impairments that would prevent her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease five years ago. She has been treated with Humira® for the last two years and has achieved partial remission. Her previous medical history is significant for surgery to remove a small bowel stricture. She is currently not smoking and not using any co-immunomodulatory drugs or corticoids. She is fluent in Flemish and English. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide signed informed consent.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her right knee for several years. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried conservative treatments such as physiotherapy, medication, and corticosteroid injections, but they have not provided long-term relief. Due to the severity of her symptoms, the patient has been scheduled for total knee arthroplasty surgery. She is in generally good health and has no significant medical history or allergies. The patient is able to read and write and has no cognitive dysfunction. She is a citizen of the country where the clinical trial is taking place.

25-year-old college student with no history of neurological or cognitive disorders, no family history of Alzheimer's disease or dementia, and no current prescription or dietary supplement use for memory or cognitive function. The patient is fluent in English and willing to participate in the trial for 30-35 days, including taking a placebo. The patient follows a healthy diet and is willing to continue with their current diet and refrain from taking any new nutritional or herbal supplements during the study. The patient is able to understand and write in English.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, weighing 75 kg and with a body mass index of 24.5 kg/m2, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has normal vital signs, blood pressure, pulse rate, and ECG results, and his clinical laboratory tests are within normal reference ranges. He has no gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, hormonal, neurological or psychiatric disorders, and has no history of seizures, stroke, orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. He has no known allergies or hypersensitivity. He is interested in participating in the study and is able to provide written informed consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice and local legislation.

The patient is a 53-year-old Caucasian male who has been on maintenance hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to chronic kidney disease. He has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking lisinopril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He has no history of myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular event within the past 3 months. He has not had any active infectious diseases within the past month and has not undergone any immunosuppressive therapy in the past month. He has no history of active connective tissue disease or advanced liver disease. He has no history of gastrointestinal dysfunction requiring parental nutrition. He has no history of active malignancy excluding basal cell carcinoma of the skin. He has a normal ejection fraction and is not anticipated to undergo a live donor kidney transplant. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have childbearing potential. He is compliant with his hemodialysis and medical regimen. He has no metallic implants, permanent tattoos, or retained foreign metallic bodies that are contraindicated in magnetic resonance imaging. He is able to provide consent.

A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, and a history of snoring and witnessed apneas during sleep visited the clinic. He takes metformin and pioglitazone daily to control his blood sugar levels. He has a body mass index of 32 kg/m2 and has been struggling with excessive daytime sleepiness. He has never received treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. He has no history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, or arrhythmia. He is retired and does not operate heavy machinery or drive public transport. He has no known allergies.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been previously diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer that has recurred after multiple rounds of chemotherapy. She is currently in remission and has responded to platinum-based chemotherapy, however, the response has not lasted more than 12 months. The patient has a high-grade (Grade 2 or 3) serous features or a serous component and a positive TA-MUC1 status confirmed through immune-histological testing. The patient has received at least 2 but not more than 5 lines of chemotherapy prior to the start of maintenance treatment and has recovered from all chemotherapy-related toxicities to Grade 1 or Grade 0 according to the NCI-CTCAE Version 4.0, with the exception of alopecia (any grade) and peripheral neuropathy (≤Grade 2). The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is ≤1 and they have an expected life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, has no allergy to the components of the test product and is willing to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old woman with a positive family history of colon cancer came to the clinic for a colonoscopy. She has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or inflammatory bowel disease. She takes anti-hypertensive medication and has well-controlled hypertension. She has no known electrolyte abnormalities and her laboratory results are within normal limits. She has not used laxatives or colon motility altering drugs in the last month. She is not pregnant and is using an acceptable form of birth control. She has no known allergies or drug intolerances. She has not taken antibiotics within the past 7 days. She is mentally competent to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 5-month-old baby boy diagnosed with Down syndrome. He was born full-term and is the first child of his parents. He has been receiving early attention therapy since birth and is in good health with no other associated pathology. His parents have agreed to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of infant massage on the maturation of babies with Down syndrome. They have been assigned to the experimental group and will receive training on infant massage techniques during the study period. The baby will be evaluated twice, at the beginning and end of the five-week intervention period, using the Scale of Psychomotor Development Early Childhood Brunet-Lézine-Revised. He is expected to grow and develop differently from typically developing children, and this study aims to provide insight into how infant massage can support his development.

55 yo female, with a history of multiple basal cell carcinomas on her face, presents to the dermatologist for evaluation of a new growth on her nose. Biopsy confirms the presence of a nodular basal cell carcinoma, which is excluded from the ongoing randomized trial comparing surgical excision with curettage. The patient is offered participation in the observational study measuring the cosmetic result and recurrence rate of all BCCs excluded from the randomized trial. Local anesthesia is administered, and the tumor is surgically excised. The patient is followed up at 12 and 48 months post-operation and assessed for esthetic outcome and suspicion of recurrence of BCC. The patient is excluded from the study if she receives treatment other than 3D-histology or shave excision.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of Major Depressive Disorder is seeking treatment for her symptoms. She has previously been treated with paroxetine and has responded well to the medication. Her depression rating scale score is currently above 18, indicating a need for further treatment. She is not currently using any other psychoactive medications except for zolpidem as needed for insomnia. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any serious medical conditions that would preclude the administration of paroxetine. She has never had a history of seizure disorders and is not currently taking any medications that would interact with paroxetine. She does not have a history of substance abuse or dependence but has undergone formal psychotherapy in the past.

A 26-year-old Hispanic female presented to the clinic for a routine follow-up visit for her HIV diagnosis. She was diagnosed 3 years ago and has been on efavirenz (EFV)-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) since then. Her CD4 count is 650 cells/mm3, and her viral load is undetectable. She is currently sexually active with one partner and uses condoms as her contraceptive method. She reports regular menses lasting 4-8 days at 28-day intervals. She denies any history of abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge, pelvic pain, or dyspareunia. Her past medical history is significant for depression for which she is taking sertraline. She denies any history of thromboembolic disease, liver tumors, or sex hormone-dependent neoplasia. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method and is willing to explore the use of the etonogestrel (ENG) implant. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She is informed of all pertinent aspects of the study and signs the informed consent document.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing intense itching and discomfort in her genital area for several months. She has a history of lichen sclerosus and has tried various topical corticosteroids with little relief. She has also noticed some changes in the appearance of her vulva, including white patches and thinning of the skin. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She is sexually active with one partner and uses contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to follow the treatment regimen. She is not currently using any medications or treatments for her lichen sclerosus.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who recently visited a dentist for a routine check-up. The dentist diagnosed her with two approximal caries lesions that require restoration. She does not have any significant medical history and is in good general health. Her periodontal status is healthy, and she has never had any behavioral issues during dental appointments. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to dental research and improve her oral health. She has a flexible work schedule that allows her to attend all follow-up appointments. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products, and she drinks alcohol occasionally. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her vital signs are within normal limits. Her BP: 115/70 mmHg, HR: 80 bpm, RR: 16 breaths per minute.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the upper abdomen and is often associated with nausea and vomiting. She has visited several physicians and underwent various tests (including x-rays, ultrasounds, and blood work), but no clear etiology for the pain has been identified. She has no significant medical history, but she admits to feeling anxious and stressed lately due to work-related issues. She is married, has two children, and works as a teacher. She denies any history of allergies or previous surgeries. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She consents to participate in the study and gives informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision in her left eye for the past few months. She has been diagnosed with high myopia and has been wearing corrective lenses for many years. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of significant medical problems or allergies. Her best-corrected visual acuity in the study eye is 56 ETDRS letters. The ophthalmological examination reveals the presence of choroidal neovascularization (CNV) in the subfoveal area of the left eye, secondary to pathologic myopia. She has no history of prior treatment with anti-VEGF or verteporfin PDT in the study eye. Her blood pressure is normal, and she is not currently taking any medications. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements, including regular visits to the clinical center for assessments and treatments.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired teacher who is concerned about her memory and ability to complete daily tasks. She has been experiencing forgetfulness and difficulty with organization for the past year. She is fluent in English and has an available informant who can complete surveys. She lives alone and is independent in her daily activities. She enjoys reading, gardening, and spending time with her grandchildren. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. She has no known neurological condition or severe psychiatric illness. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her memory and daily functioning.

The patient is a 60-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with unresectable gastric adenocarcinoma. He underwent first-line chemotherapy with cisplatin and fluorouracil but unfortunately had disease progression. His ECOG PS score is 1. His medical history is significant for hypertension that is well controlled with a single anti-hypertensive medication. His physical examination is unremarkable, and his laboratory tests show adequate bone marrow and liver function. He has no history of bleeding, gastrointestinal perforation, or fistula. He has not received any immunotherapy or experimental treatments within the last 28 days, and he has not received any live vaccinations within the last 4 weeks. He is willing to comply with the study protocol, swallow pills, and provide hematology and histology samples. He is fertile and agrees to use effective contraception during the study period and within 6 months after the end of the study period. He has no autoimmune disease, HIV infection, or other active malignant tumors. He has no history of interstitial lung disease, tuberculosis, or uncontrollable systemic diseases. He has no significant cardiovascular risk factors or history of corticosteroid use.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) 2 years ago. She has had intermittent flare-ups of the disease, but currently, her UC is in remission with SCCAI score of 3. She has been experiencing symptoms of iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) such as fatigue, headache, and cognitive impairment for the past few months. Her haemoglobin (Hb) levels have been decreasing steadily and are currently at 10 g/dl. Her ferritin levels are also low, indicating iron deficiency. She has previously taken oral ferrous products (OFP) to treat her IDA, but she was intolerant to the medication and experienced nausea, epigastric discomfort and constipation. Due to the failure of OFP, she is now seeking an alternative treatment option. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial for ST10-021, an oral ferric iron preparation, to treat IDA in subjects with non-active UC. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to comply with study requirements. She is not pregnant and is willing to use a reliable method of contraception.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation for the past year. She reports that her symptoms worsen during periods of stress and after consuming certain foods, such as dairy products and fatty foods. She has no significant medical history and has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past. She has not been diagnosed with any inflammatory bowel diseases or malignancies. She is currently not taking any medications for her symptoms. She has agreed to undergo a colonoscopy to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the role of neurotrophic factors, tight junction proteins, and cytokines in IBS.

56F with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis that has been unresponsive to treatment with methotrexate for the past 6 months. She has active RA consisting of more than 6 swollen joints and more than 6 tender joints, and a CRP level above the upper limit of normal. She meets the American College of Rheumatology criteria for RA and has an ACR functional class of II. The patient is currently taking 15mg of methotrexate weekly and folic acid daily. She is willing to maintain a constant, weekly dose of methotrexate and folate throughout the study. The patient is able to store the patient kit/cooler containing the drug in a refrigerator at home. She understands, signs, and dates the written, voluntary informed consent form at the screening visit prior to any protocol-specific procedures being performed. She is willing to comply with study visits and procedures per protocol. The patient is a sexually active woman of childbearing potential and agrees to use a medically acceptable means of birth control during the study and for 4 weeks after the last dose of the study drug.

We are seeking healthy male volunteers between the ages of 18-40 with a BMI between 19 and 28 to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of amino acids and 3-hydroxybutyrate on muscle protein metabolism. Participants must be willing to provide written consent before the study starts. Individuals with diabetes or allergies to egg or soy are excluded from the study. The study will involve insertion of catheters in the femoral artery and vein under local anesthesia. Participants will undergo a 3-hour basal period followed by a 3-hour period with hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp. Samples of arterial and venous blood and 4 muscle biopsies will be obtained during the test. The intervention will include continuous saline infusion compared to either amino acids (Vamin) or 3hydroxybutyrate solution FFa-3OHB. This study aims to elucidate the direct effects of amino acids and ketone bodies on muscle protein metabolism in humans and contribute to the further development of nutritional therapy in human catabolic states.

The patient is a 65 year old man who has been experiencing severe pain in his right knee joint for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief. However, the pain has become unbearable and has started to interfere with his daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs and even sleeping. He has been advised to undergo total knee arthroplasty (TKA) by his orthopedic surgeon. The patient has no history of any major medical conditions and is otherwise fit and healthy. He is a retired school teacher and enjoys gardening and reading books. He has a BMI of 30 and has normal blood pressure and heart rate. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is looking forward to finding a better alternative to manage his postoperative pain with minimal side effects.

A 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) two years ago is interested in participating in this study. She is currently working as a part-time nurse and is experiencing mild disability due to her MS, including fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty with balance. She lives with her husband and two children, and her husband provides her with support and assistance as a caregiver. The patient has not participated in any other clinical study and is not living in an institution. She is able to answer questionnaires and does not have severe cognitive dysfunction. She is interested in participating in this study to help researchers better understand the economic burden of MS on patients and caregivers in France.

Elizabeth is a 65-year-old woman who was admitted to the ICU due to sepsis. She was brought to the hospital by her daughter after experiencing fever, chills, and confusion for 3 days. Upon examination, she was found to have an elevated heart rate, low blood pressure, and a high temperature. Blood tests revealed an elevated white blood cell count and elevated levels of inflammatory markers. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressors to support her blood pressure. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no known allergies and is not taking any supplements. She is able to receive enteral nutrition and has not received Omega-3 supplements in the past week. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the effect of enteral Omega-3 fatty acid in septic critically ill patients.

The patient is a 2-month-old infant who is in good health and has no history of abdominal disorders or problems with the immune system. The infant has not had a fever at the time of immunization and has not received a rotavirus vaccine in the past. The infant has had no known prior rotavirus disease, chronic diarrhea, or failure to thrive. The infant is currently meeting all developmental milestones and is being raised in a stable home environment. The parents are fully informed about the study and have given their consent for the infant to participate.

The patient is a 62-year-old male smoker who presented with a persistent cough for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. A chest X-ray revealed a small, peripheral lung lesion measuring 2 cm in diameter. Further imaging with a CT scan confirmed the presence of the lesion and ruled out any evidence of metastasis. The patient was referred for further evaluation with bronchoscopy, but initial attempts with conventional fluoroscopic assisted bronchoscopy (FBS) in combination with rapid on site evaluation (ROSE) failed to provide a definitive diagnosis. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial, which will evaluate the use of Electromagnetic navigation (ENB) in combination with ROSE to improve diagnostic accuracy in patients with small peripheral lung lesions. The patient is a suitable candidate for surgical intervention if deemed necessary.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female who has not experienced regular menses for the past 24 months due to achieving postmenopausal status. She has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease. She does not have any drug allergies, but has seasonal allergies which are currently asymptomatic. She is interested in participating in a Phase I clinical trial investigating the safety and tolerability of PF-06412562.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian male with a newly diagnosed high-grade glioma. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and is now scheduled to receive radiation and temozolomide treatment. His lymphocyte count is low (ALC 500/mcL) and his Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) is 80%. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has no allergies and does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. He is married with two children and works as a lawyer. He is fluent in English and able to provide written informed consent. He has no autoimmune disease or active viral infection requiring systemic treatment. He has not received any live attenuated vaccines within the past 30 days.

60 year old woman with a history of coronary artery disease and a recent myocardial infarction (MI) who has been admitted to Saint Etienne university hospital for cardiac rehabilitation. The patient underwent coronary artery bypass surgery following her MI and has since been prescribed medications to manage her condition. She has been experiencing difficulty with her daily occupational activities including household chores and work duties. The patient has expressed interest in improving her overall quality of life and would like to participate in a study that focuses on occupational therapy as part of her cardiac rehabilitation. She is willing to attend all sessions of the cardiac rehabilitation protocol and is motivated to make positive changes in her lifestyle. The patient has no contraindications for the study and has given her informed consent to participate.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She underwent debulking surgery, during which the surgeon was not able to remove all of the tumor. She also has a malignant pleural effusion, which makes her a high-risk patient. Her performance status is ECOG 1, and she has a life expectancy of more than 2 months. Her blood work shows a WBC of 4,500/mm3, an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. Her bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, SGOT, and SGPT levels are all within normal limits. Her creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL, and her creatinine clearance is 50 mL/min. She has no evidence of infection and no peripheral neuropathy grade 2 or greater. She has not had any prior cytokine therapy for epithelial tumors of mullerian origin. She has had one prior chemotherapy regimen for ovarian cancer. It has been more than 3 years since she had any other prior chemotherapy, and she has not had any pelvic radiotherapy.

A 32-year-old woman has been diagnosed with a right ovarian cyst and has been scheduled for elective laparoscopic cystectomy. She reports no significant medical history and is currently taking only oral contraceptives. She has no known allergies and does not smoke. Her physical examination shows no abnormalities and her vital signs are within normal limits. Her preoperative lab work shows the following results: Hgb 12.5 g/dL, WBC 6.8 x10^3/µL, Platelets 250 x10^3/µL, BUN 10 mg/dL, Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, and electrolytes within normal limits. She has received complete information regarding the study and has given her informed consent to participate in it.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease by his physician. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 19. He has been taking donepezil for the past 6 months and his dose has been stable. He has no history of significant psychiatric or medical problems but takes medication for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His liver function tests and bilirubin levels are within normal range. He has not participated in any investigational drug studies in the last 3 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help find a new treatment option for Alzheimer's disease.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who had a fall while skiing, resulting in a painful right wrist. She was diagnosed with a distal radius fracture Frykman type II at the emergency department. The fracture is considered unstable based on Lafontaine's criteria and the fracture line is more than 1cm from the joint line. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is willing to undergo surgery within 72 hours of the trauma and has agreed to participate in this clinical trial after signing the informed consent.

A 55-year-old Danish man with a history of ischaemic heart disease has been referred to elective coronary artery bypass graft surgery. He has been experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He is married and has two children. He works as a carpenter and enjoys fishing and gardening in his free time. He is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. He has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses. He takes medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He speaks and understands Danish and has given his written consent to participate in the trial.

A 14-year-old male with newly diagnosed acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) presents with no evidence of fungal infection at randomization. He is currently undergoing induction chemotherapy and is hemodynamically stable with no pneumonia on chest X-ray. He has not received any systemic antifungal therapy within 7 days before randomization. His laboratory results show no significant hepatic or renal dysfunction. The patient and his parents have signed informed consent forms to participate in a prospective, randomized, concealed, single institutional study comparing oral Voriconazole and IV low dose Amphotericin B as antifungal prophylaxis during induction of acute leukemia in pediatric patients. The patient will be evaluated twice weekly for the duration of the study and at completion of the study. If the patient develops fever during induction chemotherapy, he will be evaluated by clinical examination, hemogram, biochemistry, chest X-ray, blood and urine culture for fungus and bacterial for three consecutive days. If there is evidence of chest infection or if the patient is febrile even after receiving appropriate antibiotics for 5 days, full dose therapeutic antifungal will be started earlier. The patient will be started on oral Voriconazole in a dose of 6mg/kg 12 hourly on day 1 then 4mg/kg 12 hourly daily or IV Amphotericin B 0.5mg/kg/day weekly thrice. The study aims to assess the efficacy of oral Voriconazole as antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric acute leukemia during induction, with less toxicity and more convenience compared to intravenous Amphotericin B.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who recently suffered an injury to her knee while playing soccer. She experienced a popping sensation in her knee followed by immediate pain and swelling. She was unable to bear weight on her affected leg and had to be carried off the field. Examination revealed instability of her knee, with a positive anterior drawer test, and an MRI confirmed a complete tear of her ACL. The patient is scheduled to undergo an ACL reconstruction surgery and will be enrolled in this clinical trial to evaluate the clinical, functional and morphological results of the intervention. She has a history of good health and no previous knee injuries or surgeries. She is highly motivated to return to her previous level of activity and is willing to participate in the rehabilitation program prescribed by the surgeon.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of hypertension for 20 years, type 2 diabetes mellitus for 15 years, and end-stage renal disease. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 5 years. He is scheduled for an elective angiogram with intravascular administration of iodinated contrast material at Maastricht UMC+. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is less than 30 mL/min/1.73m2 in the absence of dialysis. He is currently taking lisinopril, metoprolol, insulin, and calcium carbonate. He has no history of previous contrast administration within the last 30 days. He is able to complete follow-up and is not in emergency or intensive care status.

A 10-year-old boy diagnosed with X-linked hypophosphatemia at the age of 6. He has a history of recurrent bone pain, muscle weakness, and fatigue. The patient has been receiving conventional therapy with phosphate and calcitriol supplements, but he has been showing a poor response. He has been experiencing frequent episodes of hypercalcemia and has developed nephrocalcinosis. His laboratory findings reveal hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and elevated parathyroid hormone. He has been referred to the clinical trial for burosumab treatment. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with a prior history of glioblastoma, who has undergone first-line therapy with surgery, radiation, and temozolomide. However, he has experienced disease progression, and his MRI shows an enhancing lesion consistent with recurrent glioblastoma. He is planned for carboplatin monotherapy and has no prior toxicity with carboplatin chemotherapy. He has no known sensitivities or contraindications to ultrasound contrast agents or perflutren. His cardiac function is normal, and he has no history of hypertension or bleeding disorder. He has no active drug or alcohol use disorders. His renal function is satisfactory, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent/assent and able to communicate verbally.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a gynecologic tumor that requires surgical resection. She has no history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or hypercoagulability. She has never taken a statin before and has no known allergies to medications. She has normal renal and liver function, and no history of alcoholism. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not currently taking any medications that significantly affect cytochrome P450 3A4. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers determine if high-dose perioperative statins can reduce inflammatory responses and prevent DVT formation.

45F with a history of varicose veins in her left leg for the past 6 years. She reports aching pain in her leg, particularly after prolonged standing or sitting. She denies any swelling, redness, or warmth in the leg. She has tried compression stockings and elevating her leg, but has not noticed significant improvement in her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. On physical examination, she has visible varicose veins in her left leg, with no signs of inflammation or ulceration. An ultrasound showed a diameter of the great saphenous vein in the left leg of 5mm. She has a CEAP classification of C2. She was referred to participate in this clinical trial and has voluntarily agreed to participate after signing the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who came for a routine check-up at her primary care practice. She has no known history of cardiovascular disease and her AGLA/GSLA risk score indicates a low risk for stroke and heart attack. She is generally in good health, with no major medical conditions or chronic illnesses. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol moderately. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has no family history of cardiovascular disease. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has given written informed consent. She will undergo ultrasound screening of both common and proximal internal carotid arteries and both common femoral arteries to assess for the presence of atherosclerotic plaques. The screening will be performed by a certified medical doctor using a Toshiba Nemio XG ultrasound system with probe 7.5 MhZ. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria and is eligible to participate in the study.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman with a BMI of 32 kg/m² who has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles for the past year. She reports that her periods occur every 35-40 days and are often heavy and painful. She has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months without success. She has no history of chronic diseases affecting hormone production or metabolism, and her prolactin and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels are within normal range. The patient does not use any medications known to alter or interact with reproductive hormones and does not engage in excessive exercise. She has not used any hormonal contraceptives within the past three months and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand why obesity may be affecting her fertility.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian male who has been recently diagnosed with anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC). He has had a history of hypothyroidism and has been taking levothyroxine for the past 10 years. He has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He presented with a rapidly growing mass in his neck and has already undergone surgery and radiation therapy, but the tumor has continued to progress. He has not received any prior chemotherapy for his ATC. He has an ECOG Performance Score of 1 and his blood work shows adequate bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function. He has no known hypersensitivity to any of the drugs being used in the study. He does not have any clinically evident brain metastasis or any other comorbidities that would exclude him from the trial. He has given informed consent and is willing to undergo the screening procedures necessary for enrollment in the trial.

The patient is a 68 year old woman who participated in the iStent Inject IDE clinical trial for the treatment of open-angle glaucoma. She underwent iStent Inject implantation in both eyes and completed the 24-month follow-up period without any adverse events. She is now being invited to participate in a continuation post-approval study to monitor the long-term safety and stability of the iStent Inject. The patient is able to understand the study requirements and is willing to attend scheduled follow-up exams for 5 years post-operatively. She is also willing to provide written informed consent on the IRB approved Informed Consent Form. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoarthritis, which are well-controlled with medication.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been struggling with her weight for the past few years. She has a BMI in the obese range and has been experiencing difficulty with physical activity due to joint pain. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. Her parents are concerned about her bone health and have enrolled her in this study to better understand the relationship between her body fat and bone development. She is able to comprehend the study protocol and has provided assent, and her parents have provided informed consent. She is otherwise healthy and active, and her family has no history of bone disorders.

The patient is a 50-year-old Hispanic male who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years. Despite taking three different anti-hypertensive medications at the highest tolerated doses, his blood pressure has remained elevated with systolic blood pressure averaging 170 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure averaging 100 mm Hg. He has no prior history of heart attack, stroke, or other cardiovascular disease. He has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years and drinks alcohol moderately on weekends. He has no history of diabetes or kidney disease. He works as a construction worker and is physically active on a daily basis. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. He has suitable renal artery anatomy and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 60 ml/min/1.73m^2. He has no contraindications for anticoagulant, analgesic, or anxiolytic medications. He is not currently enrolled in any other investigational study and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

62 year old male diagnosed with gastric cancer and has undergone gastrectomy. Hemoglobin levels are above 10 g/dL, and he is able to communicate in Mandarin. He is able to walk on his own and has no lower limb disability. He has no suspected or confirmed bone metastasis but has a history of poorly controlled hypertension and diabetes. His systolic blood pressure is greater than 160mmHg and his diastolic blood pressure is greater than 100mmHg when at rest. His HbA1C is greater than 9% and his blood sugar is higher than 250mg/dl. He does not have a history of regular exercise above moderate intensity in the past three months.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of a positive fecal occult blood test (FOBT). Further diagnostic work-up with colonoscopy revealed a sessile polyp measuring 1.5 cm in size in the ascending colon. The polyp is laterally spreading, as defined by Paris Classification type II. The patient has no personal or family history of inflammatory bowel disease or colorectal cancer. Laboratory tests reveal normal coagulation parameters with INR less than 1.5. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

This is a 28 year old male with no significant past medical history. He is HIV-negative and has a CD4 count of 550 cells/mm3. He has a normal physical exam and a negative ELISA and Western blot for HIV. He has normal urine dipstick with esterase and nitrite. He has a low-risk sexual behavior. He has no co-existing conditions such as hepatitis B surface antigen positive, medical or psychiatric condition (such as recent suicidal ideation or present psychosis) that precludes compliance, active syphilis, and active tuberculosis. He is not allergic to egg products or neomycin. He has no history of immunodeficiency, chronic illness, autoimmune disease, or use of immunosuppressive medications. He has no history of anaphylaxis or other serious adverse reactions to vaccines. He has not received prior immunization against rabies or HIV. He has not received live attenuated vaccines within 60 days prior to study entry. He has not received experimental agents within 30 days prior to study entry. He has no identifiable high-risk behavior for HIV infection, such as injection drug use within past 12 months, or higher or intermediate risk sexual behavior.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic knee pain for the past 5 years. The pain has progressively worsened, limiting his ability to perform daily activities. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been recommended for elective unilateral total knee arthroplasty. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies and his BMI is within the normal range. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male scheduled for an elective surgical procedure. He has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA physical status I. He has been instructed to fast for the surgery and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have a history of difficult airway management or hypersensitivity to drugs used for general anesthesia.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of metastatic colon cancer. He has previously received first and second-line therapy regimens and is stable on his current treatment. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. His organ function is adequate, and he is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control during the study and for 28 days after the final dose of study drug. He has signed an informed consent form and is willing and able to comply with study procedures. The patient has no history of heart, liver, kidney, lung, neurological, immune, or other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He has not used systemically active steroids or any investigational product within 28 days prior to receiving study drug. He has not undergone major surgery or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to receiving study drug, nor has he undergone chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal, or biological cancer therapy within the same time frame. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing and able to comply with study procedures.

A 22-year-old male diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 2. He has a history of chronic pulmonary infections with Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. He is a non-smoker and currently not on CFTR modulators. He has had previous hospitalizations for pulmonary exacerbations and is currently admitted to the hospital for treatment of a PEx. He is able to produce sputum and willing to comply with study procedures. He has provided written consent to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old boy is scheduled to undergo a tonsillectomy surgery. He has a history of recurrent tonsillitis and snoring. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. He is in the 5th grade and enjoys playing soccer and video games. His parents are concerned about the pain associated with the IV placement and induction of anesthesia. They are interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the Synera patch can help decrease the pain for their son. The patient is excited about the prospect of participating in a research study and hopes that his experience can help other children in the future.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who experienced chest pain and shortness of breath while mowing the lawn. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking medications for these conditions, including atorvastatin, lisinopril, and metformin. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. Upon arrival at the hospital, an electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads, and he was diagnosed with STEMI. Coronary angiography revealed significant disease in three vessels, including the culprit left anterior descending (LAD) artery, which was successfully treated with primary PCI. However, the patient still has significant blockages in other arteries, and the treating team is considering further intervention. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. His renal function is within normal limits, and he is not currently experiencing any symptoms.

The patient is a 27-year-old Caucasian male who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at birth. He has a history of chronic respiratory infections, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He has been receiving treatment for his lung infections with Tobramycin TOBI® Inhalation Solution for the past 6 months. However, he has been experiencing recurrent infections and worsening lung function. His FEV1 is currently at 30% of predicted value. He has not had any major complications of his lung disease in the past 8 weeks, and he has not experienced any hemoptysis in the past month. He has no history of Burkholderia cepacia infection, tuberculosis, or non-tuberculous mycobacterial lung disease. He does not require continuous oxygen supplementation or nighttime supplemental oxygen. He does not smoke tobacco or any substance. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 9-year-old male with a history of amblyopia associated with anisometropia and intermittent exotropia presented to the ophthalmologist with complaints of difficulty seeing things clearly with his right eye. On examination, visual acuity in the right eye was 20/60, while the left eye was 20/20. The inter-eye acuity difference was 3 logMAR lines. The patient was prescribed single vision spectacles, which he has been wearing for the past 16 weeks. However, his visual acuity in the right eye remained at 20/60. The patient has no known allergies to patch or bandage adhesives, and his family has access to a computer on a daily basis. The patient has not undergone any previous vision therapy or orthoptics, nor has any family member been enrolled in this study.

38-year-old female presents with sudden hearing loss in her left ear and visual disturbances in the form of flashing lights and blurred vision in her left eye. She also experiences confusion, forgetfulness, and difficulty concentrating. She has no significant medical history and currently takes no medication. On examination, the patient is found to have a retinal artery branch occlusion in her left eye and audiogram confirms sensorineural hearing loss in her left ear. Brain MRI shows scattered areas of restricted diffusion that are most consistent with microinfarcts. The patient is diagnosed with SUSAC's Syndrome and is offered to participate in a clinical trial to better understand the disease. She provides written informed consent and undergoes a medical examination beforehand. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is enrolled as a participant.

23-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2 who is a non-smoker and has no significant medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications or herbal remedies and has not participated in another study with an experimental drug within the last 8 weeks. He has no history of psychiatric disorders, alcohol or substance abuse, bronchial asthma, convulsions, porphyria, cardiac arrhythm

The patient is a 39-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with one or more uterine fibroids confirmed by ultrasound in study M99-144. She completed the initial 12 weeks of treatment with asoprisnil 10 mg daily in study M99-144 and has not had any interruptions in dosing. She is otherwise in good health and has not had any significant abnormal laboratory results. She has no history of severe reactions to or current use of hormone therapy, nor a history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is interested in participating in the long-term safety study of asoprisnil to further evaluate the treatment's effectiveness and safety.

45-year-old female with chronic neck and shoulder pain for the past year, who has been under the care of a pain management specialist for 6 months. The patient has tried various treatments and medications with minimal improvement in pain interference and quality of life. She is motivated to improve her pain management and has a goal to increase her daily activity level. The patient has no major medical conditions or changes in pain management and owns a smartphone. She does not have low back pain requiring surgical intervention, severe psychiatric illness, ongoing substance abuse, or pain related to malignancy. The patient is willing to travel to the clinic and participate in the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU with severe shortness of breath and oxygen saturation of 80%. He was intubated and diagnosed as having acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 150. Despite optimal mechanical ventilation and use of rescue therapies, the patient's oxygenation index did not improve over the next 24 hours. The patient meets all the criteria for inclusion in this clinical trial. He has no history of malignancy, is not pregnant or lactating, and has not had any end-stage respiratory disease. The patient has not had a deep venous thrombus or pulmonary embolism in the past three months, and he is not experiencing cerebral hernia. The patient has been on invasive ventilation with PEEP ≥8 cmH2O and has bilateral infiltration in lung CT scan. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

A 25-year-old healthy male with no significant past medical history presents to the study clinic for participation in a COVID-19 vaccine trial. He is currently employed as a software developer and has been working from home since the start of the pandemic. He reports no symptoms of COVID-19 and has not been tested for the virus. He has not received any other vaccine in the past month and plans to receive the influenza vaccine in the next few days. He does not have any known allergies to vaccines or vaccine components. He is not currently taking any medications, including immunosuppressive agents, and has not received radiation therapy or chemotherapy in the past 6 months. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to conceive in the next 12 weeks. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures, including attending all scheduled visits. He has signed the informed consent form and is committed to effective contraception throughout the study period.

62 year old male with a 10 year history of COPD, who presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath and an increased respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute. He is hypoxic with an SpO2 of 86% despite supplemental oxygen. Arterial blood gas analysis reveals a pH of 7.28 and a PaCO2 of 55 mmHg. He is alert and oriented with a GCS of 14. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, but is otherwise in good health. He consents to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension. Her symptoms include shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain. Her medical history is non-significant for any other chronic illness. She is not taking any experimental or study medication and is not allergic to iron. Her blood tests reveal a transferrin saturation level of 15% and serum ferritin level of 80 ug/l, indicating iron deficiency. She is willing to take ferrous sulfate tablets orally for 3 months as part of the study. She has no history of hemochromatosis, active infection, malignancy or bleeding.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with severe aplastic anemia. He presents with symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath, and bruising easily. His blood tests show pancytopenia, with an absolute neutrophil count of 400/microL, platelet count of 15,000/microL, and reticulocyte count of 30,000/microL. Bone marrow biopsy shows a hypocellular marrow with less than 30% cellularity. He has no history of Fanconi anemia or other underlying immunodeficiency states, and his cytogenetics are normal.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been a smoker for the past 10 years. He has not had a dental visit in the past year and has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath. Upon evaluation, he has 18 teeth and multiple interproximal sites with clinical attachment loss (CAL) greater than 4 mm and pocket depth greater than 5 mm. He has no history of periodontal surgery in the past five years. His overall health is good, with no significant medical history. His blood pressure is within normal range, and his BMI is 25. He is willing to participate in the study and commit to maintaining good oral hygiene practices as instructed. He has a flexible work schedule which enables him to attend education sessions and follow-up dental appointments.

55 yo F with a 10-year history of COPD, currently using oxygen therapy at home, and a former smoker (quit smoking 5 years ago). Patient reports feeling sad and anxious most of the time, but has never received any treatment for these symptoms. Patient is currently taking albuterol as needed and tiotropium daily for COPD management. She has a history of hypertension, well-controlled with medication, and mild osteoarthritis. She reports difficulty with daily activities due to shortness of breath and feeling fatigued. The patient reports that she is interested in participating in this study because she would like to learn new ways to manage her symptoms and improve her mental health. She scores a 20 on the Beck Anxiety Inventory and a 16 on the Beck Depression Inventory II. She is able to read and understand English and has no history of cognitive impairment. She is not currently participating in any other studies and has no history of psychotic disorders, non-nicotine substance use disorders, bipolar disorders, or suicidal intentions.

A 9-year-old boy is scheduled for a diagnostic colonoscopy in the next month. He has a history of constipation and abdominal pain, which has been ongoing for the past year. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He attends school regularly and enjoys playing soccer with his friends. He has no known allergies to any food or medications. His parents have been thoroughly informed of the study procedures and have provided written informed consent for his participation. The boy has been explained the study procedures and has provided informed assent.

A 35-year-old female, married and mother of two children, presented to her primary care physician complaining of persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of energy over the past 3 months. She also reported difficulty sleeping and loss of appetite. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric illness. She has not sought treatment previously for her depressive symptoms. Physical examination and laboratory tests were within normal limits. She was diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder by DSM-5 and scored 12 on the Patient Health Questionnaire. The patient has good computer skills and easy access to internet at home. She is fluent in Spanish and willing to participate in a psychological intervention for depression. She provided informed consent and has no exclusion criteria. She is interested in participating in a brief psychological intervention for depression and is open to the option of either face-to-face or online intervention. She is willing to receive usual medical treatment and is willing to be part of a study to test the effectiveness of a mindfulness-based intervention for depression in primary care.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of hereditary angioedema (HAE). He has previously participated in CINRYZE Study 0624-200 and completed the subcutaneous therapy period in that study. He has experienced less than 1 HAE attack per month on average during the 3 consecutive months prior to screening, which required treatment with C1 INH therapy or other blood products. The patient agrees to avoid his known HAE triggers during the study to the best of his ability. He has not received any C1 INH therapy or any blood products for treatment or prevention of an HAE attack within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug. He has not received any ecallantide, icatibant, or antifibrinolytics within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug. He has not had any change in androgen therapy within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug. The patient is not taking any hormonal contraceptive regimen or hormone replacement therapy. He has no history of abnormal blood clotting or allergic reactions to products containing C1 INH or other blood products. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not received an investigational study drug within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug.

A 24-year-old female from Thailand presented to the emergency department with a history of fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, and body ache for the past 5 days. She also complained of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for the last 2 days. She had no significant past medical history, and her vaccination status was up to date. On examination, she was febrile with a temperature of 38.5°C and had a pulse rate of 100 beats/min. Her blood pressure was 110/70 mmHg, and her respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min. She had petechiae on the upper limbs and mild hepatosplenomegaly. Her laboratory investigations revealed thrombocytopenia (platelet count of 70 x 109/L), elevated liver enzymes, and a positive NS1 antigen test for Dengue virus. She was diagnosed with Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever (DHF) Grade II and was started on standard replacement therapy. However, despite receiving the standard treatment, her platelet count continued to drop, and she developed persistent bleeding from her gums and nose. She was then screened for eligibility for this clinical trial, and it was found that she met the inclusion criteria. She was provided with detailed information about the trial, and after obtaining informed consent, she was enrolled in the trial to receive activated recombinant human factor VII (rFVIIa) to achieve haemostasis.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic neck pain for the past 5 months. She rates her pain as an 8 out of 10 on a visual analogue pain scale and it has been interfering with her daily activities. She has not received spinal manipulative treatment in the past two years and has not had any adverse reactions to manipulative treatment or benzodiazepines. She is not a regular user of benzodiazepine medications and is not currently enrolled in an ongoing physical therapy program. The patient is taking ibuprofen for pain relief. She does not have any significant cardiac or pulmonary disease and has no plans to relocate during the course of the study. She will be evaluated by a trained and experienced manipulative practitioner for the presence of lesions that would be amenable to manipulation and by a medical physician for the absence of any contraindications to manipulative treatments.

Patient B is a 65-year-old female who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and needs to undergo non-emergent coronary and/or valve surgery that requires cardiopulmonary bypass. She has moderate chronic kidney disease with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) between 30 and 60 ml/min/1.73m2 and has one additional risk factor for developing cardiac surgery associated-acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI), which is preoperative anemia with hemoglobin less than 11g/dl. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She does not have a history of diabetes, cancer, or organ transplantation, and she is not dialysis-dependent. She has not received contrast media within 24 hours prior to cardiac surgery and does not have cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability within the 24 hours prior to surgery. She has not received mechanical ventilation, intra-aortic balloon counter-pulsation (IABP), left ventricular assist device (LVAD), or other forms of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) within seven days prior to cardiac surgery. She has not had cardiopulmonary resuscitation within 14 days prior to cardiac surgery. She is not pregnant or lactating and is not on immunosuppressant drugs or prednisone over the dose of 20 mg per day. She does not have any congenital coagulation disorders and is not known to have active human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, Hepatitis B (HBV), or Hepatitis C (HCV) infection. She is not on any investigational drugs or participating in any interventional trials within 60 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. Patient B meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

A 62-year-old man was admitted to the critical care unit due to sepsis secondary to pneumonia. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He is a nonsmoker and rarely drinks alcohol. On admission, he was found to have acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. He has been receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics, and his sepsis has been improving. However, his nutritional status has been declining, and he has lost about 10% of his body weight since admission. His laboratory tests showed hypoalbuminemia and anemia. He has not been able to tolerate enteral nutrition due to gastrointestinal intolerance. The critical care team has decided to start him on parenteral nutrition to provide adequate nutrition and prevent further decline in his nutritional status. The patient has consented to participate in the clinical trial comparing enteral and parenteral feeding in critically ill patients.

26-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23, who does not have any known allergies or hypersensitivity to bupropion, and has not consumed grapefruit or grapefruit juice during the 7 days prior to the study initiation. The patient has not used any prescription drugs during the 14-day period before the study initiation, and does not smoke more than 25 cigarettes per day. The patient is reliable and capable of understanding his responsibility and role in the study, and has provided written informed consent. The patient does not have any clinically significant laboratory abnormalities or any history or clinical evidence of autoimmune, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, hematological, hematopoietic, hepatic, neurological, ongoing infection, pancreatic, renal, or other diseases, conditions, or surgeries that would interfere with the conduct or interpretation of the study or jeopardize his safety. The patient does not have serious psychological illness, and has not had a positive urine drug screen or saliva alcohol screen, or a positive HIV-l, or hepatitis B or C screen. The patient is able to refrain from the use of alcohol or xanthine-containing foods or beverages during periods beginning 48 hours prior to study drug administration and ending when the last blood sample has been taken in each study period. The patient is also able to refrain from the use of all concomitant medications during the study.

A 35-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for two years came to the clinic seeking help for her infertility. She has no history of endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome or neoplasia. She has a normal menstrual cycle every 28 days and her last menstrual period was two weeks ago. Her anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) level is 2 ng/ml. She has not undergone any assisted reproductive techniques in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her conceive naturally or through assisted reproductive techniques.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with high blood pressure (HBP) for over a year but has not been able to control it. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes mellitus. His systolic blood pressure is consistently above 140 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure above 90 mmHg. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve hypertension control through an educational intervention. He lives in Madrid and is willing to visit a primary healthcare clinic for regular check-ups and to receive the educational intervention. He is between 40 and 65 years old and is willing to have his blood pressure checked regularly over a period of one year.
