He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last month and is not taking any medication that could interfere with his participation in the trial.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who has noticed a decline in her memory and thinking abilities. She has difficulty recalling recent events and often forgets important information. These symptoms have been ongoing for the past 6 months. She has a past medical history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She takes lisinopril 10mg daily and ibuprofen as needed for pain. She has not been previously diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, but her family history is significant for her mother having the disease. The patient has completed up to 15 years of education and has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score of 24. She has been referred to Emory University for evaluation and possible participation in a clinical trial investigating the effect of Montelukast on mild cognitive impairment and early Alzheimer's disease. She has no history of liver or renal disease, and has not been diagnosed with any neurological or psychiatric disorders that affect cognition. She is not currently taking Montelukast or any other leukotriene receptor antagonist. She is able to undergo MRI and lumbar puncture for study purposes.

The patient is a 25-year-old African American woman. She is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand how alpha globin deletions in healthy people affect blood vessels. She is willing to provide a saliva sample for the research. She has no history of sickle cell disease in her family. She is able to give informed consent and is available for follow-up studies if needed.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman in her 39th week of gestation, scheduled for an elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She has no medical history of hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, or heart disease. She has no known allergies and takes no regular medications. Her body mass index is 27. She is well-nourished and well-dressed, and she is alert and cooperative. She has no history of peripheral edema or deep venous thrombosis. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated, and her fetal ultrasound has shown no abnormalities.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia at the age of 8. She received anthracycline chemotherapy (daunorubicin and doxorubicin) as part of her treatment regimen. She completed her chemotherapy treatment at the age of 11 and has been in remission since then. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is unremarkable for heart disease. She is currently not taking any medications. She reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activities. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and her heart rate is 80 beats per minute. There are no significant findings on cardiovascular or respiratory examination. She is willing to participate in the study and provide consent for all the investigations involved.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired engineer who is in good overall health. He has not been diagnosed with any chronic medical conditions and takes no prescription medications. He has a history of seasonal allergies and occasional colds. He has no history of COVID-19 infection, and he is not currently experiencing any symptoms suggestive of COVID-19. He has had no previous exposure to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. He is affiliated with a social security system and is able to comply with study procedures. He understands that he will receive two doses of Moderna mRNA-1273 vaccine, and he is willing to be monitored for 24 months to assess the vaccine's effectiveness and safety. He understands that he may receive a placebo instead of the vaccine, and that he will not know which he receives. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials, and he has not received any investigational Ig, investigational monoclonal antibodies or convalescent serum within the last three months. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he has an effective contraception plan.

A 57-year-old male patient with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is scheduled to undergo an AF ablation procedure in the coming weeks. He owns an iPhone 4S and has a data plan. He is willing to use the AliveCor iPhone case for monitoring his heart after the procedure. He has no known allergies or other underlying medical conditions, and he is currently not taking any prescription medication. He exercises regularly and has a healthy lifestyle. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the monitoring and management of atrial fibrillation.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was diagnosed with liver cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice. He underwent several diagnostic tests including CT scan and liver biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of a left lateral hepatic sectionectomy. He is generally in good health, with no significant medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He is able to understand the nature of the study and willing to participate in the clinical trial. His BMI is within the range of 18-35, and he falls under the ASA II category. He is interested in both laparoscopic and open surgery options and is willing to be randomized to either of the two groups, or to be included in the registry arm if he has an explicit preference for the type of surgery.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia underwent a colonoscopy 4 years ago at Brigham and Women's Hospital, which revealed the presence of adenomatous polyps that were removed. He was advised to undergo a repeat colonoscopy in 5 years as per the American Gastroenterology Association guidelines. He has not undergone any colonoscopy since then. He is married and retired from his job as a teacher. He has two adult children who live out of state. He denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. He exercises daily by taking a brisk walk for 30 minutes. He has no significant symptoms or complaints. He is compliant with his medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is due for a repeat colonoscopy according to the guidelines but has not scheduled one yet. His primary care physician is a member of Harvard Vanguard Medical Associates.

A 32 year old female with history of second-degree burns covering 20% of her body surface area, sustained in a house fire. The patient has been admitted to the burn unit and is scheduled for excision and grafting of the affected areas. She has a history of mild asthma and is currently on albuterol and inhaled corticosteroids. The patient reports moderate pain in the affected areas, which is currently being managed with oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen. No history of drug abuse or addiction. The patient has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic neck and back pain for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with facet joint disease and has tried various treatments such as physical therapy, medication, and steroid injections, but none have provided long-lasting relief. The pain has greatly impacted his quality of life, making it difficult to perform daily activities and work. The patient is willing to explore other options and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient has no history of cancer or any other major medical conditions. He lives with his wife and two children and is able to adhere to the visit schedules for the study. He has had an MRI done in the past for his condition and is willing to undergo pre and post imaging for the trial. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

46-year-old male with a history of advanced stage lung cancer that has not responded to previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has also undergone surgical removal of the tumor but has had recurrence of the cancer. The patient has experienced increasing fatigue, shortness of breath, and weight loss in the past few weeks. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, a WBC count of 4,500/mm3, and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. The patient has a history of hypertension, but no significant cardiac or pulmonary disease. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and willing to use effective contraception.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian woman who has been struggling with severe rosacea for the past 2 years. She reports having at least 20 inflammatory lesions (papules and pustules) on her face, which have been a source of constant embarrassment and discomfort. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and ointments but has not seen any significant improvement. Her rosacea has been rated as 4 on the Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score. She is not pregnant and is using a highly effective method of contraception. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to any of the components of the investigational or non-investigational products. She is willing to participate in the study to find a more effective treatment for her severe rosacea.

A 65-year-old male diagnosed with severe emphysema is scheduled to undergo lung volume reduction surgery. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no other significant medical history and is currently a non-smoker. He has been informed of the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

57-year-old male with a laboratory-supported probable diagnosis of ALS made 18 months ago. The patient reports difficulty with ambulation and progressing weakness in both upper and lower extremities over the past 12 months. The patient's ALSFRS-R score is 28, indicating mild to moderate functional impairment. The patient's slow vital capacity (SVC) is 75% of predicted. The patient has been taking a stable dose of Riluzole for the past 9 months. The patient has no history of autoimmune or other serious diseases, malignancy, or immune deficiency. The patient has not received any stem cell therapy or experimental agents within the past 30 days. The patient has not used RADICAVA (edaravone injection) within the past 30 days and has no plans to use it during the study. The patient does not use non-invasive ventilation, diaphragm pacing system or invasive ventilation (tracheostomy) and does not have a feeding tube. The patient is a permanent resident of the United States and is able to travel to a US site for all follow-up study visits.

55 year-old man recently diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. He has previously been treated with one line of systemic therapy (sunitinib) with disease progression. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. The patient has measurable disease and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. He has not received any investigational agents and is not currently receiving valproic acid. The patient has undergone a head CT/MRI within the past 28 days which did not reveal any untreated central nervous system (CNS) metastases. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study period. The patient does not have any medical conditions that would preclude adequate evaluation of the safety and toxicity of the study combination. He has no history of allergy to entinostat or other medications that have a benzamide structure. The patient is not pregnant and is not breastfeeding. He is HIV-negative and is not currently receiving combination antiretroviral therapy. The patient has no serious or non-healing wounds, ulcers, or bone fractures, and has not undergone major surgical procedures, open biopsies, or significant traumatic injuries within the past 28 days.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa for the last 5 years. Despite receiving treatment from a specialized team, she has found it challenging to overcome her eating disorder. She has a BMI of 15.2 and experiences severe anxiety related to food and weight gain. She has no history of seizures or epilepsy but has experienced occasional blackouts in the past. She has no known brain pathology or physical illnesses that may affect her cognitive abilities, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to understand the nature, purpose, and methodology of the trial. She has signed the informed consent and has an effective means of contraception. She is affiliated with a social security scheme.

The patient is a 45-year-old non-smoking female who lives within 50 miles of the School of Dentistry, University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio. She has a single rooted tooth that needs to be extracted and desires a dental implant to replace the missing tooth. The patient has adequate restorative space for a dental implant-retained restoration and at least 10mm of alveolar bone height, without impinging on the maxillary sinus or inferior alveolar canal. She also has a dehiscence of the buccal or lingual bony plate of the tooth socket extending no more than 50% of the total depth of the socket. The patient is a former smoker who quit smoking more than a year ago. She has no history of disease entity, condition, or therapeutic regimen which decreases the probability of soft tissue and bony healing. The patient is not pregnant and has no positive medical history of endocarditis following oral or dental surgery. The patient is willing to attend a minimum of 6 visits over a 4-5 month period as required by the study protocol.

A 17-year-old boy was diagnosed with high-grade osteosarcoma after presenting with severe bone pain in his left leg. Imaging showed a large mass in the proximal femur with cortical destruction and a pathologic fracture. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of osteosarcoma. He underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin, doxorubicin, and high-dose methotrexate followed by surgical resection with limb-salvage surgery and reconstruction with a modular endoprosthesis. Unfortunately, postoperative imaging showed residual disease, and he was deemed refractory to chemotherapy. His oncologist recommended participating in a clinical trial of famitinib and camrelizumab. The patient and his family agreed to participate in the trial, and they provided consent. Tumor tissue samples were collected before starting the study drugs and after the first progression. The patient also provided frozen samples of normal tissue and blood. The patient is not pregnant, and he does not have any other concurrent malignancy or serious medical illness.

88 year old woman diagnosed with moderate Alzheimer's disease who has been residing in a care home for the past year. She has been experiencing increased agitation and restlessness in the evenings and has had some episodes of verbal and physical aggression towards staff and fellow residents. She has a history of being a professional pianist and has always had a great love for music. She has been previously involved in music therapy sessions with positive outcomes, including improved mood and decreased agitation. She is currently taking donepezil for her Alzheimer's disease. She has a keyworker who has been working with her for the past 6 months and is familiar with her needs and behaviours.

A 52-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with abdominal pain and jaundice. Imaging reveals a mass in the head of the pancreas, and a biopsy confirms pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The patient is scheduled for a pancreatoduodenectomy and is eligible for inclusion in the study. The patient will be asked to participate in the study and sign an informed consent as part of their preoperative evaluation. The patient has no other ongoing oncological diseases and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has been informed about the purpose of the study and the potential benefits and risks of participating.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is 38-41 weeks pregnant and has a history of acquired or congenital heart disease with NYHA class I or II. The patient has a singleton gestation with cephalic presentation. She has not had a previous cesarean section, does not have primary pulmonary hypertension, Eisenmenger syndrome, Marfan syndrome, or left heart obstruction. The patient has not had a prior cardiac event or arrhythmia, and the fetus does not have any known malformations. Her hemoglobin level is above 7g/dl. She does not have any obstetrical indications for induction of labor and is not on anticoagulation therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is aware of the risks and benefits associated with both elective induction and spontaneous labor.

A 43-year-old woman complains of chronic pain in her muscles and joints, especially in her neck and jaw. She experiences headaches and difficulty opening her mouth. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia and temporomandibular joint dysfunction (TMD) by her doctor. The patient has been taking antidepressants and painkillers for several months with little improvement. She has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient understands the procedures and is willing to follow the guidelines. She has signed the consent form and is ready to receive the assigned treatment. She does not participate in any regular exercise program and does not have any orthodontic treatment. The patient is classified as Class I of angle.

Maria is a 67-year-old woman who has been suffering from severe back pain for the past two months. She was recently diagnosed with two vertebral compression fractures in her lumbar spine due to her osteoporosis. Maria has tried various pain management techniques, including medications and physiotherapy, but none have provided significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially alleviate her pain and improve her quality of life. Maria has healthcare insurance and is willing to sign the informed consent form. She does not have any bleeding disorders or infections but has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or under guardianship. Maria is fully cooperative and has a good understanding of the study requirements.

The patient is a 35 year old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia for 5 years. She has been taking antipsychotic medications for the past 2 years. She has no history of fractures or bone diseases. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Her serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels are within normal limits. Her fasting blood sugar is also normal. However, her prolactin levels are elevated. She does not take any medication that affects bone metabolism. Her creatinine levels are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand the effects of antipsychotic medications on bone metabolism.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past 4 months. On physical examination, decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion were noted over the right lung field. A chest X-ray revealed a mass in the right upper lobe of the lung. Further evaluation with CT scan and PET scan revealed mediastinal lymph node metastases. The patient has a performance status of 1 and is medically fit for protocol therapy, including possible surgery. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy. His medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He has no significant neurologic or psychiatric disorders, active uncontrolled infection or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. He is a non-smoker and has no history of other malignancies. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

65 year old woman with a diagnosis of advanced stage cervical cancer with extensive pelvic involvement. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She has undergone surgery to remove the tumor, but it was found to be inoperable due to the extent of the disease. She has been experiencing severe pain in the pelvic region and difficulty with urination and bowel movements. She has been receiving palliative care and is currently taking morphine for pain management. The patient has not received any prior radiation therapy to the pelvic region. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to participate to alleviate her symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years who presents with a persistent cough and difficulty breathing. A CT scan reveals a suspicious pulmonary nodule that requires further investigation. The patient has no other significant medical history, and his physical examination is largely unremarkable. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is able to understand the study requirements, provide written informed consent, and agree to abide by the study restrictions and return for the required assessments. Additionally, he is willing to use an acceptable form of contraception if applicable. The patient has not previously been exposed to OTL38 and does not have any medical conditions that could potentially jeopardize his safety in the study. He does not have a history of anaphylactic reactions to folate or any of the components of OTL38, including folic acid. The patient's renal and liver function are within normal limits, and he has not received any investigational agents in another investigational drug or vaccine trial within 30 days prior to the administration of the study drug. He also does not have a known sensitivity to fluorescent light.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 2 years ago. She is currently participating in the CARE MS I study and has been receiving alemtuzumab treatment. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other autoimmune diseases or significant allergies. She has been compliant with her current medication regimen and has not experienced any significant adverse effects. She is willing to participate in this exploratory study to investigate the potential reparative and regenerative effects of alemtuzumab in RRMS patients.

A 42-year-old male patient presents with a body mass index (BMI) of 52 kg/m2. He has a medical history of hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea, which is currently being treated with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. He has been scheduled for an elective laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy under general anesthesia. The patient has no known disorders affecting neuromuscular blockade (NMB) and has not experienced any adverse reactions to narcotics, rocuronium, neostigmine, or other medications used during anesthesia. He has no renal, pulmonary, cardiac, and/or hepatic dysfunction, and no history of malignant hyperthermia. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has been informed of the study and has provided written consent to participate.

42-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) for 3 years, presented with recurrent infections despite receiving intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG) every 4 weeks. He had an episode of pneumonia and sinusitis within the past 3 months. The patient has a history of hypothyroidism and a remote history of alcohol use disorder, which is in remission. He is currently taking levothyroxine and has no known drug allergies. He reports no significant family history of immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease. His BMI is 25.3, and he is a non-smoker. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for the presence of sinusitis. Laboratory investigations show a normal complete blood count and serum chemistry panel, including renal and liver function tests. His immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM) are low, and his trough IgG level is 3.5 g/L. He is compliant with his IVIG treatment and has no history of thrombotic events or significant adverse reactions to IVIG. He has not participated in any other clinical trials involving an investigational product in the last 30 days.

A 8-month-old Chinese infant is brought in by his parents for a clinical trial for an inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccine. The infant is in good health and has never received any Japanese encephalitis vaccine before. His parents report no medical or family history of allergies, seizures, epilepsy, brain or mental disease. The infant's medical record shows no history of congenital or hereditary immunodeficiency, thrombocytopenia, blood coagulation disorder or bleeding difficulties. He has not received any immunodepressant or corticosteroids in the past 6 months or blood products in the past 3 months. He has also not received any research medicine/vaccine in the past 30 days or any attenuated live vaccine in the past 30 days. The infant's temperature is normal and there is no evidence of acute or serious infection. The parents are able to comprehend and sign the informed consent and are willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

45 yo F with a recent diagnosis of ALS, confirmed by EMG and clinical presentation of progressive muscle weakness in the upper and lower extremities. She has had difficulty with swallowing and speech over the past few months. Her slow vital capacity is 70% of predicted value. She is currently taking riluzole and has been on a stable dose for the past 2 months. She has no significant past medical history, no known allergies, and is not currently on any other medications. She is able to travel to Stony Brook for medical care and has a family member who can serve as her monitor for the duration of the trial. She is interested in participating in this study to explore potential treatment options for her ALS.

60-year-old woman who has been experiencing some memory loss and forgetfulness over the past year. Her family members have also noticed her repeating things and having difficulty remembering names and places. She has no significant medical history and takes only a daily multivitamin. She reports no current symptoms of depression or anxiety. She has completed high school education and one year of college. She is right handed and has no significant hearing or visual impairments. She is willing and able to undergo an MRI examination. She has been referred by her primary care physician for further evaluation of her cognitive complaints.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease. He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stenting six months ago. He is currently on aspirin (81mg/day) and clopidogrel (75mg/day) therapy to prevent thrombotic events. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has no history of bleeding disorders or prior stroke. His renal function is normal, and he has no known allergies to any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the pharmacodynamic effects of dabigatran in patients on dual antiplatelet therapy.

A 35-year-old woman is bothered by the appearance of cellulite on her thighs and buttocks. She has tried various creams and diets but hasn't seen any significant improvement. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve the appearance of her cellulite. She has completed the double-blind study EN3835-201 and is willing to apply sunscreen before sun exposure. During the observation phase, she had no adverse reactions to the treatment. She meets the inclusion criteria for the treatment phase as she has at least 1 quadrant with a moderate or severe score on the Photonumeric Cellulite Severity Scale and a Cellulite Severity Scale score no greater than 13. She is using an effective contraception method and has a negative pregnancy test. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to see an improvement in the appearance of her cellulite.

A 28-year-old female presents to the optometrist's office for a routine eye exam. She has been wearing toric soft contact lenses for the past 6 months and is interested in trying out new daily disposable toric contacts. Her past medical history is unremarkable and she reports no eye-related issues. Her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with a spectacle prescription of -2.50D in the right eye and -2.75D in the left eye. She has refractive astigmatism of -1.25D in her right eye and -1.50D in her left eye, with the cylinder axis between 155 to 25 degrees. She is a habitual contact lens wearer and has no issues with wearing the lenses for at least 12 hours a day, 7 days a week. She is willing to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule. She has not participated in any concurrent clinical or research study and does not have any active ocular disease or infection. She is not using any systemic or topical medications that may affect contact lens wear or a study outcome variable. She is not sensitive to the diagnostic sodium fluorescein used in the study and is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy at the time of enrollment.

A 48-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer after a routine mammogram. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis, and she is scheduled to start chemotherapy with pyrotinib and apatinib. She has no prior history of cardiovascular disease and is physically active, exercising regularly. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has two children and works as a nurse. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has no known systemic diseases and has normal laboratory and imaging results. She has not received any prior systemic anti-cancer therapy for advanced disease. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She has no contraindications to cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 60 ml/min/1.73 m2.

The patient is a 57-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The cancer has spread to other organs and is not amenable to surgery or radiotherapy with curative intent. The patient has received prior weekly irinotecan, fluorouracil, and leucovorin calcium chemotherapy regimen but the disease has progressed within the last three months. The patient has at least one measurable lesion that is at least 20 mm in at least one dimension. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status between 0-2 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has an absolute neutrophil count greater than 2,000/mm3 and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm3. The bilirubin level is no greater than 0.5 mg/dL above the upper limit of normal (ULN), AST is no greater than 5 times ULN, and creatinine is no greater than 1.5 times ULN OR creatinine clearance is greater than 60 mL/min. There is no evidence of unstable angina, symptomatic congestive heart failure, or serious uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia. The patient has no active or uncontrolled infection or other serious illness. There is no other malignancy within the past 5 years except adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer or noninvasive carcinomas. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, has a negative pregnancy test, and is using effective contraception. The patient has received no more than one prior chemotherapy regimen for advanced colorectal cancer, and prior adjuvant chemotherapy is allowed. The patient has received no prior radiotherapy to more than 25% of bone marrow and at least 4 weeks have passed since major surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently underwent surgery for a fractured leg. He is currently immobilized and on bed rest. He has a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) and is unable to take anticoagulant medications due to a recent gastrointestinal bleed. His primary care physician has recommended the placement of an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter to prevent the migration of potentially dangerous blood clots from his legs to his lungs. The patient has been referred to the UCSF Department of Interventional Radiology (IR) for the placement of the IVC filter. The IR physician has informed him about the ODEN Trial and asked if he would be interested in participating. The patient has given his consent and has undergone screening procedures to confirm his eligibility. He is currently waiting for his IVC filter placement procedure and is willing to participate in the follow-up visits and filter removal if medically appropriate.

The patient is a 34-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection 3 years ago. He has a positive Hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) status. He has no history of coinfection with immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C virus (HCV) or hepatitis D virus (HDV). He has no other forms of liver disease such as alcoholic, autoimmune, or biliary disease. He has not received any nucleoside or nucleotide analogue antiviral agents for the past 12 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patients are a set of 2-year-old identical twin boys, whose parents are interested in participating in a research study on early brain development. The boys were born at term without any major medical or obstetrical complications. They have met all their developmental milestones on time and are growing and developing normally. The boys are generally healthy and have no history of neurological disease or developmental delay. The family is eager to participate in this study to help advance the understanding of the role of genes and environmental factors in early brain development. The family is willing to bring the boys for regular MRI scans and developmental assessments over the next few years, as part of their participation in the study.

Patient is a 25-year-old male with sickle cell disease who receives regularly-scheduled blood transfusions as part of existing medical care. He has been experiencing recurrent painful crises and is interested in exploring treatment options beyond symptomatic care. He meets the eligibility criteria for this non-randomized pilot safety and feasibility single-center study, which will treat subjects with SCD with plerixafor, followed by collection of peripheral hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) by apheresis. The study requires bone marrow aspirate before and after plerixafor administration to compare HSPCs and their bone marrow niche in SCD patients. The primary objective of this study is to assess safety and feasibility of plerixafor in SCD patients, and to increase knowledge of HSPCs and their bone marrow niche in SCD patients. The secondary objective is to assess the effectiveness of plerixafor in mobilizing HSPCs in SCD patients. The patient will undergo laboratory testing, history, and physical exam prior to plerixafor administration. The patient must be taking hydroxyurea, which will be stopped 14 days prior to planned day of apheresis. The patient will be admitted to the Hematology service at Boston Children's Hospital for plerixafor administration and apheresis, and will remain overnight for observation. The patient will return for outpatient visit and labs on Days +3, +7, +14 after apheresis.

A 28-year-old female who leads a sedentary lifestyle and works at a desk job has been experiencing tightness and discomfort in her hamstrings. She has no previous history of lower extremity surgery or physical therapy and rehabilitation in the last 6 months. She is not pregnant and does not have any diagnosed medical condition. She is interested in participating in a study to improve her hamstring flexibility and range of motion. She is willing to receive any of the three interventions: instrument assisted soft tissue mobilization, dry needling or static stretching. She understands that there may be some unexpected side effects associated with the interventions and is willing to stop the application immediately if she experiences any.

56-year-old Hispanic male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. Despite being on several oral antidiabetic medications, his most recent HbA1c value was 8.5%. He resides in a rural area of Central Texas and has limited access to diabetes education and support services. He has a high school education and works as a farm laborer. He reports difficulty with monitoring his blood sugar levels at home due to lack of resources and knowledge. He has also struggled with maintaining a healthy diet and increasing physical activity. He is willing to participate in a 24-month diabetes self-management study and is able to attend regular follow-up visits. He speaks English at a basic level but may require additional support in understanding intervention protocols. He is motivated to improve his diabetes control and quality of life.

A 48-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of a brain tumor is being evaluated for a craniotomy. She reports moderate to severe headaches, which have been increasing in frequency and severity over the past few weeks. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine, and vitamin D deficiency. Her 25(OH)D level was recently measured at 15ng/dL. She has no history of kidney disease or nephrolithiasis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She is not currently involved in any other clinical trials and is not pregnant or lactating.

A 47-year-old male with a history of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) presents to the clinic with recurrent symptoms. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80% and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient has had a pathologically documented, and definitively diagnosed recurrent GBM. He has undergone maximum safe surgical resection and standard adjuvant radiation/temozolomide treatment. However, he has had recurrence or progression of disease confirmed by MRI and measurable by RANO criteria. He has received no more than one other therapeutic regimen other than the standard of care therapy. The patient may be receiving steroid therapy at the time of enrollment (stable dose of ≤ 4 mg/day of dexamethasone or steroid equivalent). The patient has a bi-dimensionally measurable disease measured using contrast enhanced MRI. Hematological, renal, and hepatic function are normal. Serum phosphate levels are within normal limits. The patient has not had central nervous system bleeding within 6 months of enrollment and has no evidence of acute intracranial/intra-tumoral hemorrhage, except for stable grade 1 hemorrhage. The patient has no history of coronary artery disease, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, or cardiac arrhythmias requiring anti-arrhythmic therapy. The patient has no active infection requiring treatment. The patient has no history of other malignancies, except for adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer or other malignancies curatively treated with no evidence of disease for ≥ 2 years. The patient has no known positive test for human immunodeficiency virus infection (HIV), or active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection. The patient has not received therapies or procedures prior to the first dose, as listed in the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman with diabetes and impairments in mobility. She has been taking four or more long-term medications for her diabetes and comorbidities, including hypertension, hypercholesteremia, and peripheral vascular disease. She lives at home and has difficulty walking and standing for long periods of time. She has experienced adverse effects from some of her medications in the past, including dizziness and nausea. Despite her health conditions, she tries to maintain an active lifestyle and enjoys spending time with her grandchildren. She has a family doctor who manages her medications but has expressed interest in receiving additional support and guidance to better manage her health.

A 24-year-old man was referred to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial for HIV. He was diagnosed with HIV six months ago through routine screening and has never been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) before. He has been experiencing no symptoms related to HIV or any other medical conditions. He is currently not taking any prescription or non-prescription medications, vitamins, herbal or dietary supplements. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is sexually active with men and uses condoms inconsistently. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and restrictions. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. His medical history is unremarkable including gastrointestinal anatomy and renal function. His blood pressure, heart rate and ECG results were within normal limits during the screening visit. He understands the risks and benefits of participation in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

This clinical trial is for children between the ages of 2 and 17 years who have been diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) with gp91 phox or p22 phox deficiency. The patients who are currently free of active infection, have a history of at least one life-threatening infection or a family member with CGD and a history of at least one life-threatening infection are eligible for this study. Patients with HLA-matched related donors that meet donor selection criteria or patients without an eligible HLA-matched related donor can participate in this study. The study will compare the efficacy of a novel approach to allogeneic stem cell transplantation designed to promote partial or complete donor stem cell engraftment with reduced transplant-related morbidity and mortality. Stem cells from the donor will be infused after a low-intensity bone marrow conditioning regimen, and cyclosporine will be given to help prevent rejection of donor cells. The primary end points of this study are to demonstrate reduced incidence of CGD-like infections in the transplanted patients compared to the controls with acceptable incidence of acute and chronic graft versus host disease and transplant-related mortality. Patients enrolled in the control arm who complete a 24-month follow-up period may enroll in the transplant arm should an eligible, consenting donor become available. Written informed consent/assent conforming to institutional guidelines will be obtained from patient and parent. The patients must have adequate organ function for enrollment. Female patients who are pregnant or lactating or have ECOG performance status of 2 or more or less than 50 percent on the Lansky scale for ages 0-10 are not eligible. The donor must be related to the patient and HLA-phenotypically identical with the patient for HLA-A, B, and DRB1 alleles, and written informed consent from the donor must be obtained.

A 32-year-old woman and her partner have been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. She has regular menstrual cycles of 28 days and reports no history of sexually transmitted infections or gynecological issues. The patient's body mass index (BMI) is 24 kg/m2, and her partner's semen analysis reveals a sperm concentration of 35 million/mL with 60% motility and 5% normal morphology. The patient has no prior history of infertility treatments. Her AMH levels were measured and found to be within normal limits for her age. The couple is interested in pursuing IVF and has been recommended the Freeze all strategy. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the blastulation rate in women under the age of 40 years following this strategy.

A 16-year-old Hispanic female presented with a history of marijuana use for the past year, with daily use in the last six months. She reported that she started using marijuana to cope with school-related stressors and anxiety. She denied any history of alcohol or other substance use. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she was not on any medications. Her vital signs were within normal limits, and her physical examination was unremarkable. She is currently living with her parents and two younger siblings in a low-income household. Her parents are concerned about her marijuana use and have agreed to participate in the study. The patient is willing to participate and understands the study procedures. She has no contraindications for MRI and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in her breast and neck area, which is affecting her daily activities and quality of life. She is currently admitted to the hospital for pain management and has not used the self-reported pain scoring tool before. She is able to understand and answer the pain scoring tool questions. The patient is aware of the importance of managing her pain and is willing to participate in the study. She is otherwise healthy with no cognitive impairments. The patient is cooperative and motivated to help improve pain management for herself and other cancer patients.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with hypertension during a routine check-up with his primary care physician. He has a family history of hypertension and has been overweight for most of his adult life. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He is not taking any medication for his hypertension. The patient will be required to collect 24-hour urine and wear a 24-hour blood pressure monitor. They will be asked to follow a 'no added salt diet' for 6 weeks.

48 yo F with high-frequency hearing loss in both ears. She had been using hearing aids for the past 5 years but had limited improvement in speech discrimination. Speech audiometry showed significant benefit from the use of high-frequency amplification. She opted for a cochlear implant and underwent surgery with a long electrode array insertion. Post-operatively, she had a significant improvement in her ability to understand speech in noise. However, she also reported a decrease in low-frequency hearing in her implanted ear. CT imaging showed that the electrode array was located in the scala vestibuli. The patient is now being considered for a second cochlear implant in the contralateral ear and has been approached to participate in this clinical trial to determine the optimal surgical placement of the electrode array to avoid loss of low-frequency hearing.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial, as patients were not recruited for nor enrolled in this study. This is a retrospective observational study, where data from medical records or insurance claims databases are anonymized and used to develop a patient cohort. All diagnoses and treatment are recorded in the course of routine medical practice.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his left knee for several years. He has been previously diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has been taking over-the-counter pain medications to manage his symptoms. He reports difficulty with walking and getting up from a seated position. The patient is otherwise healthy and does not have any other chronic medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate a proprietary cherry juice blend for the treatment of his knee osteoarthritis.

The patient is a 59-year-old male who has been experiencing unexplained weight loss, fatigue, and abdominal discomfort for the past few months. He has undergone various diagnostic tests, including blood work, imaging scans, and endoscopic procedures, but the primary site of his cancer remains unknown. His biopsy results show poorly differentiated carcinoma, and he is considered to have a poor prognosis. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent for this trial and is at least 18 years of age. He has documented measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1 through computerized tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He is willing to use two methods of birth control if he is of childbearing potential. The patient has adequate organ function as defined in the eligibility criteria. He has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent, and he does not have a known history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). The patient does not have known active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C. The patient has not received a live vaccine within 30 calendar days of planned start of study therapy.

A 45 year old woman with a recent diagnosis of stage IVA squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. She has no history of any other malignancies and has not received any prior treatments for her cancer. She has a performance status of 1 and her blood work shows a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL, leukocytes of 6,500/mm3, and platelet count of 100,000/mm3. Her liver function tests are within normal limits and her renal function shows a creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. She has no bilateral hydronephrosis. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.

50-year-old female with a history of multiple myeloma that has not responded to previous treatment regimens, including chemotherapy, bone marrow transplantation, biologic therapy, radiotherapy, and interferon therapy. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and has no other concurrent malignancies within the past 5 years. The patient has quantifiable M-components of IgA and kappa light chain excretion. The patient has an absolute granulocyte count of 1,200/mm3 and a platelet count of 60,000/mm3. The patient's bilirubin and SGOT/SGPT levels are within normal limits, and the patient's creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. The patient has not received thalidomide therapy for more than 3 months and has no preexisting peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1. The patient is willing to use two methods of effective contraception for 4 weeks before, during, and for 4 weeks after the study. The patient is interested in participating in a randomized phase III trial to compare the effectiveness of combination chemotherapy with or without thalidomide in treating refractory multiple myeloma.

A 55-year-old man has been suffering from moderate to severe hearing loss for several years. He has difficulty understanding conversations, especially in noisy environments. He has been using hearing aids, but they are not providing sufficient benefit. He has a history of chronic otitis media that was treated with antibiotics. He has no history of cholesteatoma, vertigo, or Meniere's syndrome. He has normal tympanic membranes and middle ear anatomy. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He is a native English speaker and uses hearing aids in both ears, with the left ear being the one to be implanted with the Esteem® Hearing Implant. He has undergone audiological testing and has an unaided maximum word recognition score of 50% with recorded delivery using a phonetically balanced word list at Speech Reception Threshold (SRT) + 40 dB. His air-bone gap is less than 10 dB at 4 of the 5 frequencies tested (500, 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz). His pure tone air-conduction threshold levels are within the limits of a Hearing Aid (HA). He has had a fine cut temporal bone CT scan to ensure adequate space for the Esteem® System implant. He has normal eustachian tube function and is not known to have any psychological, developmental, physical, or emotional disorders that would interfere with the surgery or follow-up testing. He has no known medical conditions that would affect healing and is not undergoing any treatments that would interfere with the trial. He has signed the Subject Informed Consent Form and is willing and able to comply with specified follow-up evaluations.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II cervical cancer. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She has two children and works as a teacher. Her physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any other abnormalities. She was recommended to receive definitive chemoradiation including brachytherapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve the treatment planning and outcome of the procedure. She has no implanted devices or medical conditions that preclude MRI acquisition. She is willing to undergo MRI-guided internal radiation therapy applicator placement. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to sign an informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has a history of recurrent infections, including frequent sinus infections and pneumonia. She has also been diagnosed with autoimmune thyroid disease and Raynaud's phenomenon. She has been seen at the University of Virginia Asthma, Allergy, and Immunology clinics in the past and had an undetectable serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) level noted during her last visit. Her serum immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, and IgM) are within normal or high levels. She is interested in participating in a study to investigate whether an undetectable serum IgE level is a biomarker for the development of immune deficiency. She is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits and study procedures.

This is a 62 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He had a myocardial infarction 2 years ago and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with placement of two drug-eluting stents in the left anterior descending artery. He is on a statin and aspirin therapy for secondary prevention of cardiovascular events. He denies any symptoms of claudication or stroke. He is interested in participating in a research study to improve knowledge about Lipoprotein(a) in patients with established cardiovascular disease.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) and has previously received one course of rituximab therapy. The patient has not responded to the therapy and has not received any other treatments for the condition. The patient's lymphoma is CD20 and CD22-positive and is either follicular or diffuse large B-cell NHL. The patient has measurable disease but is not a candidate for potentially curative therapies. The patient has not undergone a bone marrow transplantation within the last 6 months and has not received previous radioimmunotherapy.

A 32-year-old man was diagnosed with classical Hodgkin's lymphoma two years ago. He has been treated with ABVD chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. However, after six months, he developed a palpable mass in his left supraclavicular region. The biopsy of the mass confirmed relapsed classical Hodgkin's lymphoma. He received ICE chemotherapy and achieved partial remission. A PET-CT scan done after ICE chemotherapy showed residual metabolic activity in the left supraclavicular mass. He was told that his disease is refractory to chemotherapy, and high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation is not a curative option. He is currently asymptomatic, works full-time, and has a performance status of 1. His laboratory results are within the normal limits except for a mildly elevated AST level. His absolute neutrophil count is 1,300/mm^3, and his platelet count is 170,000/mm^3. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy. He is not taking any medications, and he has no other medical problems. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks of participating.

A 62-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with COPD five years ago. She is a former smoker and quit smoking 10 years ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She lives alone in a single-story house and has three adult children who live nearby. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for several months. She has been using a rescue inhaler, but it doesn't seem to be helping as much as it used to. She reports having had two exacerbations in the past year, requiring hospitalization. She is interested in participating in this study to help improve the management of her COPD and reduce the frequency of exacerbations.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder Type II. She has been experiencing a lack of motivation and interest in activities that she used to enjoy, which has been affecting her quality of life. She is currently taking medication for her mood disorder and is proficient in English. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce her anhedonia symptoms. She has no history of psychosis or suicidal ideation that would preclude her from receiving outpatient treatment. She is not currently pregnant and does not have any cognitive impairment. She is not currently in psychotherapy and is not living in the United States on a VISA.

57F with a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type 2, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with symmetrical painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The patient reports a burning sensation in both feet, which has been gradually worsening over the past few months. The pain is described as constant and moderate to severe in intensity. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medication, but it has been ineffective in relieving her symptoms. On examination, the patient has decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick in both feet. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity, allergy, or contraindication to opioids and acetaminophen. The patient does not have any confounding painful conditions, significant vascular disease, history or risk of seizure, chronic disease that might affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient denies any history or evidence of alcohol, medication, or drug abuse.

This is a 34-year-old female with a history of Type 1 diabetes for the past 12 years. Despite her best efforts, she has had difficulty controlling her blood sugar levels, often experiencing hypoglycemic episodes and requiring hospitalization for ketoacidosis. She has a low arginine-stimulated C-peptide level of 0.1 ng/mL, indicating minimal insulin production by her pancreas. She has no history of smoking or malignancy, and her BMI is within the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. She has no significant cardiac or arterial issues, and her creatinine clearance is above 60 ml/mn. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially alleviate her dependence on exogenous insulin therapy and improve her quality of life. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis according to the current 2011 American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society/Japanese Respiratory Society/American Latin Thoracic Association (ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT) guidelines. The patient has had symptoms of shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue for the past 6 months. Pulmonary function tests showed a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 60% of predicted value and carbon monoxide diffusing lung capacity (DLCO) corrected for hemoglobin of 40% of predicted value. The patient is a former smoker with a 20 pack-year history and quit smoking 2 years ago. The patient has no history of significant respiratory disorders other than IPF and does not require 24 hours of oxygen therapy or have oxygen saturation <88% after 10 minutes breathing ambient air at rest. The patient has not used any cytotoxic/immunosuppressive agent including but not limited to azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, and cyclosporine within 4 weeks prior to screening. The patient has not used any investigational drug within 1 month of screening or 5 half-lives, if known, or within 12 weeks for stem cell therapy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of SAR156597 in the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who has recently been diagnosed with developmental coordination disorder (DCD). He has difficulties with planning and executing motor coordination activities like dressing and sports. He has no other neurodevelopmental diagnoses, except for a suspicion of ADHD. He has not received any rehabilitation services for DCD in the public health care system. He scored at or under the 16th percentile for the global score at the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2 (MABC-2) and at or under the 5th percentile for one of the 3 subscales of the MABC-2. His parents are interested in participating in a teleintervention study to increase their capacity to manage their child's needs. They have access to the internet and are willing to participate in a 3-month randomized feasibility trial to determine the feasibility of using the internet to build parents' capacity to manage their child with DCD.

An 11-year-old boy named Jack is brought in by his parents to participate in a clinical trial on the effects of active video games (AVGs) on body composition, cardiometabolic risks, and cognitive functions among overweight/obese children. Jack has been struggling with his weight for several years and is currently in the 90th percentile for BMI. He is an active child but has difficulty maintaining regular exercise routines due to his busy school schedule. Jack is fluent in English and loves playing video games, particularly Xbox. He has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study. His parents are supportive of his participation and are excited to see the potential benefits of AVGs on his health.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread pain, fatigue, and stiffness for at least 3 months. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by a rheumatologist and has a Widespread Pain Index (WPI) score of 14 and a Severity Scale (SS) score of 5. She has not engaged in regular physical activity for more than 6 months and spends most of her time sitting or lying down due to pain and fatigue. She does not have any significant cardiac or respiratory conditions that would contraindicate the practice of physical activity. She speaks and writes French fluently and is willing to participate in a supervised physical activity program. She does not have any geographical, social, or psychological barriers that would prevent her from participating in the program or undergoing regular medical monitoring. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs and is not currently pregnant. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 13 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

A 45 year old woman diagnosed with dumping syndrome complains of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and palpitations after meals. She has undergone partial gastrectomy and has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. Despite following a diet of six small meals a day with low concentrations of mono- and disaccharides, her symptoms have not improved. She has not been treated with Somatuline or Sandostatine LAR in the past. She does not have cholecystolithiasis, diabetes mellitus, coeliac disease, giardia, untreated severe oesophagitis, or untreated gastric and duodenum ulcers. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use barrier contraceptive precautions throughout the trial. She has not had any hypersensitivity reactions to lanreotide or any of its compounds.

The patient is a 70-year-old male diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, with mild to moderate memory loss and difficulties in thinking. He is currently living in his own home and has been on a stable dose of acetylcholine esterase inhibitor for more than three months. His vital signs are stable, and he has no significant medical history, except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of alcohol abuse or any other substance abuse. He has a devoted caregiver who can ensure regular medication and supplement intake. The patient has not been treated previously with omega-3 fatty acids, NSAIDs, or warfarin. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the protocol.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of recurrent major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 5 years. She has tried five different oral antidepressant treatments in the current episode of depression, but none have been effective (less than or equal to 25% improvement). Her depression symptom severity is high, with a Week 1 Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score of 32. She has been on a different oral antidepressant treatment (escitalopram) for the past 2 weeks at or above the minimum therapeutic dose. She is in good health, with no history of psychotic disorders or substance abuse. She does not have any suicidal or homicidal ideations. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to switch to flexibly dosed intranasal esketamine (56mg or 84mg) plus a newly initiated oral antidepressant as part of the study. She is willing to participate in the 4-week double-blind treatment phase to evaluate the efficacy, pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of the treatment.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer. He underwent radical prostatectomy 5 years ago and was on hormone therapy for 3 years after the surgery. However, his PSA levels have been rising steadily for the past year, and he has been diagnosed with bone metastasis based on an X-ray. He has not received any previous bisphosphonate therapy. The patient is in good health otherwise, with no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare MER-101 20mg tablets to Zometa 4mg IV infusion for the treatment of his bone metastasis.

50-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, currently controlled by diet or metformin alone, with a body mass index of 31 kg/m2. HbA1c levels between 6.0% to 9.5% (42mmol/mol to 80mmol/mol). No history of major psychiatric disease, eating disorders, drug or alcohol abuse. No known sight-threatening retinopathy, renal impairment, or abnormal liver function tests. No history of ischaemic heart disease, heart failure, or stroke. No known history of porphyria or allergy to trial product or related products. Not currently taking anti-diabetic therapies other than metformin. Not currently receiving oral steroid treatment. No known malignancy or any other condition that would affect the patient's ability to participate in the protocol. The patient must not have received any investigational trial drug within 3 months prior to participation in the current trial.

Sarah is a 56 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). She has never had any major medical issues in the past and has no significant family history of cancer. She underwent a CT scan that showed a tumor measuring 4 cm in diameter in her right lobe of the liver. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. Sarah is currently being evaluated for treatment options and her doctor has suggested the use of the Surefire Precision Infusion System with DEB-TACE. She meets all of the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate to help advance research on this new treatment modality. Sarah understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and is able to provide informed consent.

A 43-year-old female with a history of cholecystitis is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no known drug allergies and has never undergone general anesthesia before. Her past medical history includes hypertension that is well-controlled with lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia that is managed with atorvastatin. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. She reports occasional headaches but denies any neurologic disorders or neuromuscular diseases. Her preoperative evaluation indicated normal magnesium levels and she is not taking any medications that contain calcium channel blockers or magnesium. She has normal renal and hepatic function and no respiratory or cardiovascular dysfunction. She is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologist physical status II. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the impact of magnesium pre-treatment on intubation conditions during general anesthesia.

Patient is a 42-year-old woman from Canada who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy and is currently in remission. She reports fatigue and lack of energy, and is interested in finding ways to improve her physical and psychological well-being. She has completed an ACE baseline class and exercises regularly at home. She has access to a laptop with a video camera and internet connection. Her BMI is 25, BP: 115/75, HR: 70/min. She does not have any active infections or bowel obstructions and does not suffer from cognitive impairment. She speaks English fluently.

We are seeking healthy male volunteers between the ages of 25 and 55 years old to participate in a clinical trial investigating a new drug for the treatment of Parkinson's disease. The study will require you to take a single oral dose of V81444 and undergo PET and MRI scans to assess the effects of the drug on brain activity and blood flow during cognitive function tests. The study aims to determine the best dose of V81444 to use in future trials and to assess the safety and tolerability of the drug after dosing. To be eligible, you must be in good general health, take no regular medication, and have no significant medical conditions or history of such conditions. You should have a confirmed medical history from your general practitioner. You should also be willing to abstain from caffeine and have no contraindications or cautions for MRI scanning.

45-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) based on the presence of characteristic cystic changes on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest. The diagnosis was confirmed by histopathological confirmation by biopsy. The patient has been on sirolimus for the treatment of LAM for at least 20 weeks and has demonstrated evidence of disease stabilization with two stable values of serum VEGF-D post-initiation of sirolimus drawn at least 12 weeks apart from each other. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other clinical drug trials for LAM and is willing to comply with pulmonary function tests and follow-up visits. The patient is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the next six months and is not currently breastfeeding. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to resveratrol and is able to provide informed consent. The patient does not have any clinically significant medical disease that is associated with an expected survival of less than 2 years or is likely to impact the ability of the patient to participate in the study in the opinion of the investigator or impact the study efficacy or safety assessments.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus at the age of 18. She has been managing her diabetes with insulin therapy since the diagnosis. Recently, she experienced vision problems and was diagnosed with non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy in her right eye with an ETDRS score of 45. She is otherwise healthy with no history of photosensitive skin rash or myositis. Her thyroid function test, liver function test, and creatinine phosphokinase level are all within normal limits. Her fasting triglycerides level is 4.9 mmol/L. She has no history of pancreatitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or cancer. She is not currently taking any investigational drugs and has not undergone any organ transplantation. She is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including treatment, assessment, and clinic visit attendances. She has read and understood the Participant Information and Consent Form and has provided written, signed, and dated informed consent to participate in the study.

35 year old female with a BMI of 38.2, presenting with a history of obesity-related co-morbidities including hypertension, sleep apnea, and joint pain. The patient has tried multiple diets and exercise regimens with limited success in weight loss. Due to her worsening health and difficulty in daily activities, she has opted for laparoscopic surgery to help achieve weight loss goals. She currently takes medication for hypertension and has a history of smoking, but has quit for the past year. The patient is willing to participate in research studies related to her condition and is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve her overall health.

The patient is a 60-year-old African American male who was diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma. He has been experiencing progressive visual field loss and increased intraocular pressure despite using multiple eye drops. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a mechanic and enjoys spending time with his family and friends. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his condition and prevent further vision loss.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for over a year. She has been experiencing an exacerbation of her asthma symptoms, including increased wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. She has been seen in the outpatient setting at a clinic and is able to comprehend English and provide informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent pain in her left shoulder for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse during activities that require overhead reaching or lifting, and she has difficulty sleeping at night due to the discomfort. She has tried taking over-the-counter pain relievers and applying heat to the area, but the pain persists. On physical examination, there is tenderness over the left shoulder joint and limited range of motion. The patient also reports a history of occasional instability in her shoulder joint. Plain X-ray shows some signs of shoulder instability. The patient has not undergone any previous surgical interventions on her shoulder joint and has no history of fracture repaired with metal plates or screws. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the use of high-resolution ultrasound in the evaluation of shoulder pain guided by MRI.

The patient is a 22-year-old female college student who has recently noticed that her feet seem to be "flatter" than usual. She reports no pain or discomfort, but is concerned about the appearance and potential long-term effects of her pes planus. She has a body mass index of 22 and is generally active, participating in regular exercise classes and sports activities. She has no history of foot or ankle trauma or surgery, and has no neurological or orthopedic diseases affecting her lower extremities. She is interested in participating in a study on foot core training to improve the strength and function of her feet, as she wants to maintain her active lifestyle and prevent any future foot-related issues.

50 yo F with a history of chronic HCV infection presenting for evaluation for liver transplantation due to increasing symptoms of fatigue and jaundice. She has been on antiviral therapy with interferon and ribavirin in the past without sustained virologic response. She has no history of renal failure or HIV/HBV co-infection. Workup for liver transplantation reveals that she is a good candidate with no contraindications. She is approached to participate in a pilot study examining the role of Nitazoxanide (NTZ) in the prevention of HCV reinfection after liver transplantation. She meets the eligibility criteria and agrees to participate in the study. She will receive NTZ immediately prior to liver transplantation and for 3 days thereafter. The primary endpoint is the number of patients who remain HCV RNA-negative at day 7 after LTx.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired teacher who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease six years ago. She has been experiencing persistent motor complications despite receiving treatment with available anti-Parkinsonian medications. Her symptoms are inadequately controlled on this optimized treatment, and she is experiencing a minimum of 3 hours per day of "Off" time during a continuous 16-hour interval, including the portion of the day during which she is awake the majority of the time. She is able to recognize her "Off" and "On" state and has been confirmed by UPDRS Part III (in both "On" and "Off" states) and by the Parkinson's Disease Diary©. She is diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease according to the United Kingdom Parkinson's Disease Society (UKPDS) Brain Bank Criteria and has a modified Hohn and Yahr (H & Y) classification of disease severity of 4. She has no history of neurosurgery for the treatment of Parkinson's disease or other parkinsonian syndromes such as secondary Parkinsonism or Parkinson's-plus syndromes. She has no primary psychiatric diagnosis of acute psychotic disorder or other uncontrolled primary psychiatric diagnoses, and no significant cognitive impairment or dementia. Her B12 levels are normal. She is interested in participating in the study to assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of ABT-SLV187 monotherapy in subjects with advanced Parkinson's disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. He is scheduled for a left heart catheterization with possible percutaneous coronary intervention.
