He has no known allergies and is not taking any anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications. He has never had a catheterization before and is nervous about the procedure. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his vital signs are stable. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. His lab work is within normal limits, including his platelet count and coagulation profile. His creatinine clearance is >60 ml/min. He has no known bleeding disorders or vascular abnormalities.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with lung cancer and requires thoracic surgery for one lung ventilation. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. He has no difficulty with breathing or ventilation. The surgery is scheduled in advance, and it is not an emergency operation.

35-year-old male with severe hemophilia (factor activity level < 1%) and chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He has not been previously treated with interferon. He has no history of hepatitis B virus (HBV) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. He does not have chronic liver disease caused by any other disease besides HCV. He has no presence of Bethesda inhibitor nor any current evidence of or history of portal hypertension.

A 40-year-old female tennis player presented with complaints of pain in her right arm for the past 6 weeks. She had been experiencing tenderness and pain over the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, along with grip weakness. The pain increased with activities that involved repetitive use of her wrist and strong grip. The patient denied any other significant medical history or prior elbow injuries. She reported no history of diabetes, neuropathy, or arthritis in the upper extremities. She had never received any injections or physical therapy for lateral epicondylitis in the past three months. She denied any allergies to tape. Upon physical examination, tenderness and pain were noted over the lateral epicondyle of her right humerus. Provocation of the lateral elbow pain was observed with the resisted middle finger extension (Maudley's test) and passive stretch of wrist extensors (Mill's test). She was diagnosed with lateral epicondylitis and was deemed eligible for the study.

The patient is a 17-year-old female who seeks orthodontic treatment to correct the rotation of her lower incisors. She has good oral hygiene and has not had any previous gingivitis or untreated caries. She has a 2 mm keratinized tissue band and at least two rotated lower teeth with a degree of rotation between 30º-50º. She has a normal periodontal condition and does not have any interproximal bone loss or thin gingival biotype. She is not currently undergoing root canal treatment, and she is not pregnant. She does not have any systemic diseases or medications that alter bone metabolism. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares two treatments for the rotation of lower incisors after arch wire removal. The trial will randomly assign her to receive either Er,Cr:YSGG laser-aided circumferential supracrestal fiberotomy or conventional circumferential supracrestal fiberotomy. The trial will measure the degree of lower incisor rotation relapse after one month of arch wire removal and the probing depth and gingival margin position. Pain will also be evaluated using the visual analogue scale at baseline, 24, 48, and 72 hours after the clinical intervention.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has recently sustained an acute laceration wound on his right forearm due to an accident at work. He does not have any history of chronic illnesses or allergies to medications. He does not consume tobacco or alcohol. He is seeking treatment in an outpatient setting and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The wound is approximately 5 cm in length and is located on the upper extremity. The patient has not received any prior treatment for the wound and does not exhibit any signs of infection.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding for the past 3 months. She has no prior history of abnormal pap smears or pelvic pain. She has never been pregnant and her menstrual cycle is regular. Her past medical history is unremarkable and she is not taking any medications. She has no known allergies. She is sexually active with one partner and is using condoms as her preferred method of contraception. Physical examination reveals a nulliparous cervix without any obvious abnormalities. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is willing to undergo a vaginoscopic office hysteroscopy procedure to determine the cause of her abnormal bleeding. She has been provided with information regarding the potential for pain during and after the procedure and has consented to participate in the study to compare the pain associated with two different diameter rigid hysteroscopy procedures. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus. He is currently on mechanical ventilation and receiving vasopressor therapy to maintain his blood pressure. His urinary output has decreased to less than 0.5 mL/kg/hour for the past 2 hours. His heart rate is elevated at 105 beats per minute. His lactate level is elevated at 6 mmol/L. He has skin mottling on his extremities. He is not pregnant and does not have any chest tubes with air leak, abdominal compartment syndrome, or clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia. His Transthoracic echogenicity is suitable for measuring velocity-time integral of aortic blood flow (SVI). He is not a prisoner and does not have clinical brain death. His PEEP is currently set at 10 cmH2O.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of type 2 diabetes complains of persistent abdominal pain and discomfort. He has been diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) with a Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP) of 270 dB/m. His HbA1c level is 7.5%, and he has been on metformin monotherapy for the past 12 weeks. He does not drink alcohol or smoke. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He has no history of liver disease or any other major illnesses. His family history is negative for any liver or metabolic disorders. He is willing to use proper contraception during the study period. His serum creatinine level is 1.1 mg/dL, and his creatinine clearance is 75 ml/min.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer one year ago. She underwent surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has a good support system from her family and friends. Her current treatment regimen includes trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and docetaxel for metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer. She is experiencing some fatigue, but otherwise tolerating the treatment well. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the cardiotoxicity of this regimen and the usefulness of troponin I (TNI) and Brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in identifying patients at risk for cardiotoxicity and predicting LVEF recovery. She understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with secretory multiple myeloma with myeloma markers at levels defined in the protocol. He has received at least 3 prior regimens and was responsive to at least 1, but refractory to most recent prior therapies, which included an immunomodulatory imide drug, proteasome inhibitor, alkylator, CD 38 monoclonal antibody, and glucocorticoid as separate lines or a combined line of therapy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is HLA-A*02:01, HLA-A*02:05, and/or HLA-A*02:06 positive. He has confirmed sufficient expression of NY-ESO-1 and/or LAGE-1a as determined by a designated central laboratory. He has not received anti-programmed death (PD)-1, anti-PD-ligand (L)1, or anti-PD-L2 inhibitor in the past. He has not previously participated in Merck pivotal trial NCT02576977. He has no history of allogeneic stem cell transplant or myelodysplasia. He has adequate organ function and cell counts as described in the protocol. The patient has previously undergone radiotherapy and chemotherapy, but can meet the washout periods for these prior therapies.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining swallowing sounds of different textured foods and viscous liquids in healthy subjects. She is a student at a local university and has no history of swallowing disorders, neurological deficits, or cancer of the mouth, neck, or brain. She reports being able to sit upright with or without back support of a chair. She has no other diseases that affect swallowing function. She has a BMI of 21.2, and her height and weight will be measured upon acceptance and consent to participate. She is able to sign the informed consent after the whole study is explained to her. The study will take 2 hours for each section, and there will be 2 sections to complete the entire process. The PI and faculty advisor of the research team will be present during the recording session.

57-year-old male diagnosed with refractory Hodgkin's Lymphoma with previous treatment history of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has a performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of over 3 months. The patient has no significant comorbidities and has normal organ and bone marrow function. Measurable lesions are present for evaluation. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and comply with the study protocol. The patient has not been previously exposed to any drug targeting CD47 or SIRPα. No major surgery has been performed within 4 weeks of the first administration of the drug. The patient has not received any live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks of the first administration of the drug. The patient has no history of other primary malignant tumors in the past 5 years. The patient is negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. The patient has no active or suspected autoimmune diseases. The patient is a male and is not of childbearing potential. The patient has no known history of hemolytic anemia or severe allergic reactions to monoclonal antibody.

A 30-year-old female marketing executive is interested in non-invasive liposuction of her abdomen and flanks. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet but has had difficulty losing stubborn fat in these areas. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated in the study. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the treatment/follow-up schedule. She uses reliable birth control methods and has a negative urine pregnancy test at baseline. She has no significant skin conditions or inflammatory skin conditions in the treatment area.

65 F with subacute non-specific low back pain for the past 3 months. Pain is primarily located in the lumbar region and radiates to the right hip and leg. Pain is rated as 7 out of 10 on the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). The patient has good comprehension of written and spoken Italian Language and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. No specific pathologies or neurologic signs have been noted on examination. The patient has not undergone any surgical interventions in the last six months and does not have osteoporosis.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who was referred for a brain MRI due to headaches and dizziness that started a few weeks ago. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. On examination, he is alert, oriented, and cooperative. His vital signs are within normal limits. There are no focal neurological deficits, and cranial nerves are intact. The patient denies any recent trauma, seizures, or loss of consciousness. His family history is non-significant for any neurological disorders. MRI of the brain is scheduled for further evaluation of the headache and dizziness. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial as he is already scheduled for a brain MRI at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta at Scottish Rite for reasons other than tectal plate glioma evaluation. The patient does not meet the exclusion criteria for the trial.

Unfortunately, as this is a healthy volunteer trial, we cannot provide a patient description as participants must meet the specific eligibility criteria outlined in the study protocol. The study is seeking healthy men of Northern European descent with a BMI of 19-25 kg/m2 and stable body weight in the last three months. Additionally, participants cannot be currently taking medication or dietary supplements that cannot be paused for 12 hours, have a history of liver or renal disease, severe heart disease or failure, low blood count, or be participating in other clinical experiments with medication. First-degree relatives with diabetes or any other disease/condition that may interfere with participation in the experiment are also excluded.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was diagnosed with high-grade glioma a year ago. Despite undergoing conventional therapy, her tumor has progressed and she is currently experiencing worsening headaches, nausea, and vomiting. MRI shows measurable disease and her performance status is Lansky 90%. She has an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200/mm^3 and a platelet count of 110,000/mm^3. Her hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL, bilirubin level is within normal limits, and her SGPT and SGOT levels are less than 2 times the upper limit of normal. Her creatinine clearance is 80 mL/min and her echocardiogram shows a shortening fraction of 30%. She has no history of dyspnea at rest or exercise intolerance and her pulse oximetry is 98%. The patient has no active graft-versus-host disease, uncontrolled infection or allergy to azoles. She has recovered from prior immunotherapy and it has been more than 7 days since she received antineoplastic biologic agents. She has not received autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplantation and has not received any growth factors in the past month. She is currently taking dexamethasone to control increased intracranial pressure. She has recovered from prior radiotherapy and it has been more than 3 months since she received craniospinal radiotherapy. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is not taking any medications that interfere with CYP3A4.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has not had a mammogram in the last 12 months or any breast study in process. She is interested in participating in the personalized breast cancer screening trial to understand the feasibility and acceptability of such a program. She has no history of breast cancer or any clinical indication for genetic counseling. The patient is fluent in both Catalan and Spanish and has no cognitive or physical disabilities that would prevent her from undergoing a mammogram. She is willing to sign the informed consent form for the trial.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been suffering from seasonal allergies for the past 5 years. She often experiences redness, itching, and tearing in her eyes during pollen season, which makes it difficult for her to go about her daily activities. She has been diagnosed with allergic conjunctivitis in the past and has a positive skin test reaction to cat hair, cat dander, grasses, ragweed, and trees. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in each eye as measured using the ETDRS chart. She has no known contraindications or sensitivities to the study medication or its components, and does not have any ocular conditions that could affect the trial parameters. She is willing to participate in the trial and is committed to adhering to the study protocol.

A 14-year-old male with moderate hemophilia A presents with a history of recurrent joint bleeding and documented high titer inhibitor (>5 BU/mL) on emicizumab prophylaxis. The patient has received immune tolerance induction (ITI) therapy with concomitant bypassing agent (BPA) prophylaxis with no success. The patient has no history of thromboembolic disease or clinically significant hypersensitivity associated with monoclonal antibody therapies or components of the emicizumab injection. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient and their parent/guardian have provided written informed consent and are willing to participate in a prospective safety study investigating the use of a personalized dose of aPCC during acute bleeding events or prior to procedures. The patient is expected to undergo minor and major procedures over the next 2 years, making them an ideal candidate for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old female smoker with a history of chronic cough and shortness of breath upon exertion for the past 2 years. She has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medication. She denies any history of previous respiratory illnesses or hospitalizations. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Spirometry shows a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.68 and an FEV1 of 65% predicted. The patient is able to walk up one flight of stairs without stopping but experiences significant dyspnea with more strenuous activity. She has not used antibiotics in the last two months. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial and provides informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of heart failure, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs. She was diagnosed with NYHA class III heart failure and had a BNP level of 350 pg/mL. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medications for these conditions. She has no known allergies or other medical conditions. She is able to walk short distances but gets easily winded and has difficulty with stairs. She is willing to participate in a research study to evaluate predictors of cardiovascular outcome and reverse remodeling in patients with heart failure. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old boy visited the clinic with complaints of recurrent stomach pain, bloating, and occasional vomiting. He had a history of taking antibiotics for upper respiratory tract infections several times in the past year. The physical examination was unremarkable, but endoscopy revealed Helicobacter pylori infection in the gastric mucosa. The patient has not taken any acid-suppressing medications or antibiotics in the past 4 weeks. He has no known allergies and has no history of liver or kidney disease. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the study and have provided written consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and chest pain for the past few months. He underwent several diagnostic tests, including an endoscopy, which revealed a tumor in his esophagus. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. The tumor is considered unresectable due to its size and location. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80 and is otherwise in good health. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is a candidate for the Definitive Radiochemotherapy Plus/Minus Cetuximab in Unresectable Locally Advanced Esophageal Cancer clinical trial. The patient has provided a signed informed consent and meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 62 year old woman was diagnosed with severe osteoarthritis of the right knee and has scheduled an elective total knee replacement surgery. She has been experiencing significant pain in her right knee for several months and has difficulty walking and performing daily activities. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and is not taking any regular medications. She is able to provide informed consent and is expected to require inhaled oxygen concentrations less than 25%. She is looking forward to the surgery and hopes that it will improve her mobility and quality of life.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with castration resistant prostate cancer. He has received at least one but not more than two cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens for metastatic CRPC. He has experienced prostate cancer progression as assessed by the investigator with PSA progression according to Prostate Cancer Working Group 2 (PCWG2) criteria. The patient has ongoing androgen deprivation with serum testosterone <2.0 nM and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of ≤2. His platelet count is ≥100,000/μL and serum albumin is ≥30 g/dL. Serum creatinine is <1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) or a calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 60 mL/min and serum potassium is ≥3.5 mmol/L. The patient has not received abiraterone or MDV3100 in the past. He has no serious or uncontrolled co-existent non-malignant disease and no abnormal liver functions. He has no uncontrolled hypertension, clinically significant heart disease, brain metastasis, or history of gastrointestinal disorders that may interfere with the absorption of the study drug. The patient is willing to sign informed consent and meet all other inclusion criteria.

This is a 27-year-old female who sustained second-degree burns on her arms and legs after an accident at home with boiling water. She has been receiving wound care treatments for the past week and has been experiencing significant pain during the procedures, despite the use of pain medication. She has no history of psychiatric disorder or traumatic brain injury, and is able to communicate verbally in English. She is interested in participating in this study to explore additional methods to reduce her pain during wound care. She has no face/head/neck injuries that would interfere with the use of Virtual Reality equipment and does not have a history of extreme susceptibility to motion sickness or seizures.

A 16-year-old adolescent with sickle cell disease is experiencing frequent episodes of vaso-occlusive crises that require hospitalization. She has a confirmed diagnosis of sickle cell disease and her hemoglobin level is between 5.5-10 g/dL. She has been taking hydroxyurea for the past year, but her symptoms have not improved. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and uses reliable contraception. She has not received any blood transfusions or cellular-based therapy in the past. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He sustained a traumatic spinal cord injury due to a fall from a height of 20 feet during work. He was initially diagnosed with complete paralysis and loss of sensation from his waist down. He was brought to the emergency department within 4 hours of the injury. His vitals are stable, and he is responsive to the doctors' questions. He can speak and understand English fluently. He has no prior neurological issues, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He does not have any allergies to medications or foods. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period.

The patient is a 32-year-old African American woman with a history of asthma. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of shortness of breath, chest tightness, and wheezing, despite being on daily controller medications. She works as a nurse and is married with two children. She has a history of allergies and has been diagnosed with allergic asthma. She has had to visit the emergency department multiple times in the past year due to asthma exacerbations. She has access to a telephone and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any other chronic respiratory conditions such as cystic fibrosis or COPD. She is motivated to improve her asthma control and is interested in participating in a study that focuses on the specific challenges faced by African American women with asthma.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female. She is not pregnant and not currently breastfeeding. She has no known allergies to eggs, ovalbumin, chicken protein, neomycin, polymyxin, or any components of the vaccine. She has not received any influenza vaccinations in the past six months. She is sexually active and using a medically accepted contraceptive regimen. She is willing to comply with study requirements and attend all scheduled visits. She has no history of significant medical conditions and has not shown any signs of active infection.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness for the past year. She has not been previously treated with methotrexate or aminopterin. She has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis based on the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria, with a score of 7 out of 10. She has more than 6 swollen and tender joints and is classified as Class II functional according to the ACR 1992 revised criteria for the classification of global functional status in RA. She has no history of hepatitis, HIV infection, or interstitial lung disease, and her screening laboratory blood tests are within normal limits. She is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study drug or have drug interactions with aminopterin. She has been using NSAIDs occasionally for pain relief. She has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study period as she is sexually active. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of persistent allergic rhinitis for the past 2 years. She suffers from nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, nasal itching, sneezing, and ocular symptoms for more than 4 days a week and for more than 4 weeks per year. She has a history of allergies and has undergone a CAP or prick test within the last 12 months which showed sensitization to allergens that cause her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with its procedures. She understands the dosing and visit schedules, and agrees to record symptom scores, NPIF measurements, adverse events, concomitant medications and intake of rescue medication accurately and consistently in a daily diary. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using an acceptable method of birth control. She has not used any investigational product within 30 days prior to enrollment or any investigational antibodies for asthma or allergic rhinitis in the past 90 days. Her medical history is unremarkable except for her allergies. She is not currently experiencing any other upper or lower respiratory tract disease and has normal nasal patency. She has no significant cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, neurologic, psychiatric or autoimmune disease, no tumor or conditions that may interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of the study medication. She has no history of hypersensitivity to the study drug or its excipients.

The patient is a 55-year-old post-menopausal woman who has been diagnosed with lipedema. She has significant subcutaneous fat above her knees, as determined by a circumference of 55cm. She has tried various conservative measures, including compression garments and exercise, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She has no significant medical history, is not taking any medications, and has no known allergies. She has a normal blood pressure and fasting glucose levels. She has no history of primary or secondary immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease, or use of immunosuppressive drugs. She is willing and able to adhere to the visit schedule and protocol requirements. She does not have any wounds, tattoos, or infections in the treated area. She has not undergone any invasive treatments such as surgery or injectable drugs in the area to be treated with RZL-012.

The patient is a 10-month-old female infant who has not received any previous vaccinations. She is in good health with no known or suspected immune system impairments or serious diseases. Her parents are willing to have her participate in a clinical trial testing the safety and efficacy of an MF59C.1-adjuvanted subunit influenza vaccine compared with a conventional subunit vaccine. She has not received any influenza vaccines in the past or had any documented suspected cases of influenza disease.

A 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years, controlled on metformin therapy, and with a body mass index of 29 kg/m2, presents to the clinic. He reports occasional difficulty controlling his blood sugar levels and is interested in new treatment options. He has no history of smoking and is generally healthy, with normal thyroid function and no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has not been diagnosed with any cardiovascular disease or other coexisting conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to adhere to the dosing schedule, visit schedule, and phone follow-up assessment. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old Caucasian female with a history of irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty conceiving presents to the clinic. She has been trying to conceive with her partner for over a year with no success. She reports having mild acne and excessive hair growth on her face and body. Physical exam reveals a BMI of 32 and evidence of hirsutism. Transvaginal ultrasound shows multiple small ovarian follicles bilaterally. Blood work reveals elevated testosterone levels and AMH levels. She meets the Rotterdam criteria for PCOS and has not responded to clomiphene citrate treatment. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the mechanisms of anovulation in PCOS. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She signs the informed consent before being enrolled in the study.

This is a 54 year old female with a history of breast cancer who had undergone mastectomy and chemotherapy 3 years ago. She had been in remission since then but had developed a new lesion in the liver on routine surveillance imaging. Biopsy confirmed metastatic breast cancer to the liver. She had been started on systemic chemotherapy but had developed severe nausea and vomiting which led to poor tolerance and discontinuation of treatment. She is now considering participation in a clinical trial for an oral formulation of gemcitabine hydrochloride. She has no known allergies to gemcitabine and meets the eligibility criteria including adequate liver and kidney function. She has a performance status of 1 and is willing to comply with the study requirements. Her current medications include ondansetron and lorazepam for nausea and vomiting. She has no history of cerebrovascular disease or gastrointestinal surgery that could interfere with oral therapy absorption.

This is a 27-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with HIV. She is currently 24 weeks pregnant and seeking antenatal care at a community health center in rural South Africa. She is eligible for this clinical trial, as she has a primary male partner and is over 18 years of age. The trial aims to test the effectiveness of a behavioral intervention to increase Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV (PMTCT) protocol uptake among South African HIV positive pregnant women. The intervention will utilize a combination of both gender-concordant groups and individual or couples counseling strategies, before and after birth. The participant will attend six sessions during the antenatal and postnatal periods that address the barriers to PMTCT, such as stigma, disclosure, intimate partner violence, communication, infant feeding practices, and safer conception. The aim is to help the participant and her partner increase adherence to ARV/PMTCT protocols, including breastfeeding and family planning, to reduce infant HIV incidence.

A 45-year-old man was recently diagnosed with a brain tumor after experiencing seizures and headaches. Imaging studies have shown a mass in the left temporal lobe of the brain that is suspicious for a glioma. The patient has no significant past medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 1. A neurosurgical procedure, either biopsy or resection, is planned as part of routine clinical care to confirm the diagnosis and determine the best course of treatment. The patient will be undergoing surgery at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN and has expressed willingness to participate in the study. He has been informed about the risks and benefits of the procedure and has provided written informed consent. The patient has no history of vulnerable populations and does not have any concurrent illness that would make him an unsuitable candidate for surgery.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of biliary obstruction, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain. He was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma after undergoing an MRI and biopsy. He has been deemed inoperable due to the extent of the disease and his age. He has undergone endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) and had a stent placed to relieve his biliary obstruction. He has a performance status of 1 and is capable of completing quality of life questionnaires. He has signed the consent form to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment. He is not currently receiving any chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his cancer. His bilirubin level has decreased by more than 50% after stent insertion compared to the baseline level. He has no clinical or laboratory signs of biliary infection or extrinsic biliary compression. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception if female and of childbearing potential.

Patient B is a 42-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and her basal follicular stimulation hormone (FSH) level was measured to be 14 mIU/ml. She underwent one cycle of IVF in the past, with only two oocytes retrieved and no successful pregnancy. She has a BMI of 25 and has no history of metabolic or autoimmune disorders. Ultrasound and biochemical tests did not show any signs of polycystic ovary syndrome or endometriosis. She has not taken any infertility medications for the past two months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of different IVF protocols in poor responders.

A 42-year-old male patient diagnosed with low-grade neuroendocrine tumor located in the pancreas. The patient has been experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, nausea, and occasional diarrhea. The tumor has shown progression after completion of prior systemic therapy. The patient has undergone surgery to remove part of the pancreas, but the tumor is still present. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has no history of allergic reactions to vatalanib or octreotide injections. His blood tests show normal hematopoietic function with an absolute neutrophil count of 1500/mm³, platelet count of 100,000/mm³, and hemoglobin of 12.0 g/dL. His liver function tests show normal bilirubin and AST levels. His creatinine levels are within normal range. He has no history of ulcerative disease, bowel obstruction, or other gastrointestinal tract disease. He is not pregnant or nursing and is using effective contraception. He is able to swallow tablets and receive contrast-enhanced CT scans. He has not received anti-vascular endothelial growth factor agents or therapeutic warfarin.

A 25-year-old female cancer survivor who lives in North Carolina is interested in participating in a telemental health intervention study. She was diagnosed with stage 2 breast cancer and completed treatment a year ago. She has been experiencing health-related anxiety and distress in the last 3 months due to the pandemic. She is fluent in English and has a computer with audio and visual capabilities. She has no history of inpatient hospitalization, psychiatric hospitalization, or psychotic processing in the last 3 years. She has not been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, eating disorders, or substance abuse. She is interested in learning coping skills to manage her mood during these challenging times.

28 year old male with a medical history of severe nodulocystic acne and no other significant medical conditions. The patient has at least 10 nodular lesions on the face and/or trunk. The patient weighs between 40 and 110 kg and is able to swallow pills. The patient has not used any topical or systemic acne treatments for at least 2 and 4 weeks respectively prior to baseline. The patient has no history of prostatic disease or surgery on the prostate. The patient has no skin disease or condition that might interfere with the evaluation of nodular acne. The patient is not allergic to finasteride or any other ingredients in the study medications. The patient is willing to use a medically acceptable form of barrier-method contraception or practice abstinence during the study. The patient has not used any investigational drug within 90 days prior to Day 1. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs an IRB-approved informed consent prior to performing any of the screening procedures.

A 46-year-old male patient has been intubated for 2 days following an exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The patient has a history of heavy smoking for the past 30 years and was previously diagnosed with severe COPD, which requires regular use of bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids. The patient has been receiving mechanical ventilation in the ICU and is currently in the weaning phase with PEEP of 7 cmH2O and support of 10 cmH2O. The patient is responsive and alert with a Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale score of 0. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to assess the correlation between two methods for cough peak flow measurement in intubated patients. The patient has no history of bronchospasm, and the FiO2 is currently at 40%. The patient has not undergone any recent surgeries or suffered from any thoracic injuries within the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with no prior medical history, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and has not used any tobacco or nicotine containing products for at least 6 months. Her BMI is 22. She has not had any surgery or significant blood loss in the past 90 days. She is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, except for occasional use of acetaminophen. She has not consumed any alcohol, grapefruit/oranges or caffeine/xanthine within the restricted time frame prior to dosing. She has undergone sterilization procedure and has no plans for pregnancy. She is willing to comply with the protocol and assessments of the study, including all restrictions. She understands the study procedures and has provided written informed consent.

A 75-year-old male patient is admitted to the emergency department with complaints of abdominal pain and vomiting blood. The patient has a history of peptic ulcer disease and has undergone surgical intervention for the same previously. The patient also has a history of hypertension, diabetes and chronic kidney disease. On examination, the patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg and pulse rate is 110 beats per minute. The patient is pale and has signs of dehydration. Hemoglobin levels are found to be low, and the patient is diagnosed with bleeding peptic ulcer. The patient is treated with therapeutic endoscopy and primary hemostasis is achieved. The patient is then enrolled in the study to validate the CU prediction model for predicting mortality in patients with high risk bleeding peptic ulcers. The patient provides informed consent for the study and will be monitored for any adverse events such as rebleeding, need for surgery or hospital stay. The accuracy of the prediction model will be analyzed to validate its applicability for the patient population from different Asian countries.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male, with no known allergies or medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco products. The patient has not taken any drugs known to induce or inhibit hepatic drug metabolism or any systemic prescription medication in the 14 days prior to period I dosing. The patient has not donated blood or plasma within the last 30 days prior to period I dosing, and he has not received any investigational drug within the last 30 days prior to period I dosing. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and will be available for both confinement periods. The patient is practicing an acceptable method of birth control or has been surgically sterilized.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV three years ago. He has been attending regular HIV outpatient clinic appointments and has been taking antiretroviral medication since his diagnosis. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has not been diagnosed with any cardiovascular disease or risk factors. His most recent HIV viral load was undetectable and his CD4 count was 650 cells/microliter. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in the study to further understand the cardiovascular risk associated with HIV and its treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has been admitted to Hackensack University Medical Center due to complications related to the disease. She is experiencing severe dyspnea, with a respiratory frequency of 35/min and blood oxygen saturation of 91%. She has been judged by her healthcare provider to be at high risk of progression to life-threatening disease. The patient is willing to provide informed consent or has a healthcare proxy who can provide informed consent on her behalf. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and may be eligible to receive investigational convalescent plasma as part of the expanded access program.

A 68-year-old man was diagnosed with wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in his right eye. He has been a smoker for over 30 years, smoking a pack a day. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago and controls it with medication. He also takes anti-coagulants for a previous heart condition. He underwent three intra-vitreous injections of ranibizumab as the first intra-vitreous treatment between January 2016 and December 2020. His visual acuity was measured before the start of the injections and after the series of three injections (4 to 8 weeks after the last injection). He is a patient at CHU Brugmann Hospital.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. She has a history of smoking for over 30 years and was diagnosed with COPD after experiencing recurrent episodes of cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath. She has been hospitalized twice in the past year for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. She is currently on bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids to manage her symptoms. She is able to perform activities of daily living with some difficulty, but reports feeling tired and breathless after walking short distances. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control her blood pressure. She lives alone and has limited support from family and friends. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if tele health monitoring can help manage her COPD symptoms and prevent future hospitalizations.

45-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident presents to the hospital with multiple, severely displaced rib fractures. He has been experiencing respiratory distress, pain, and poor cough since the injury. The patient is currently receiving the best medical management, but his pain is not well controlled, and his respiratory function is continuing to deteriorate. The medical team is considering surgical stabilization of rib fractures as an option in addition to the standard medical management. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial, which aims to investigate the efficacy of SSRF, as compared to non-operative management, for hospitalized patients with non-flail, severe rib fractures. The patient is not excluded by any of the exclusion criteria, and the surgery is anticipated to be performed within 72 hours from the injury. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to undergo randomization to either surgery or medical therapy only.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with H. pylori infection. She has a history of gastric ulcers and has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for several months. She has not received any H. pylori eradication treatment before. The patient is not currently experiencing any upper gastrointestinal bleeding or any other acute mucosal lesion. She does not have any history of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, gastric acid hypersecretion disorders, or any hepatic or renal impairment. She has not undergone any surgery that affects gastric acid secretion. The patient is not allergic to TAK-438, PPIs, penicillin antibiotics, macrolide antibiotics, or antitrichomonal agents. She is generally healthy and does not have any organic disease of the brain or spinal cord. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is available for follow-up visits.

A 32-year-old woman named Sarah is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to test whether restricting the timing of energy intake can improve fuel utilization patterns and enhance circadian rhythms in metabolic tissues for optimal health. Sarah is currently overweight and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She leads a fairly sedentary lifestyle with less than 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity per week. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and has not been pregnant in the past 6 months. She typically consumes food over a window of more than 12 hours per day. Her sleep-wake cycle involves going to bed between 2200 and 0100h and getting up between 0600 and 0900h with more than 7 hours and less than 9.25 hours in bed. She has a regular sleep-wake schedule and is willing to keep it for the duration of the study. She owns a smartphone and is willing to install and utilize the meal timing application. Sarah has not participated in any other research study that would influence her safe participation in this study. She does not have any conditions affecting weight or lipid metabolism, and her blood chemistry and hematology are within the normal range. She does not have a history of systemic, psychiatric, neurological disease, or drug and alcohol abuse. She is a non-smoker and does not have any clinically significant allergies. Sarah is interested in improving her metabolic health and is willing to follow the control diets at imposed times for 1 week prior to the inpatient CTRC visits.

57-year-old female with a history of gradually progressive bilateral upper and lower limb weakness for the past 2 years, along with fasciculations and cramps. She has also noticed difficulty in swallowing and speaking. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She denies any family history of neuromuscular disorders. On examination, she has bilateral upper and lower limb muscle wasting, fasciculations, and weakness. Her reflexes are brisk, and there is bilateral extensor plantar response. Sensory examination is normal. She is diagnosed with definite ALS based on the revised EL Escorial criteria for Airlie House. She can eat and move with herself alone but needs assistance in everyday life. She is less than 3 years from the onset of ALS, and her condition has not deteriorated significantly during the 12 weeks before administration. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use contraception during the study period. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within 12 weeks. She is judged to be adequate to participate in this study by her physician.

Pt is a 30yo healthy female with no significant medical history, not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and willing to use a consistent form of double-barrier birth control. She is interested in participating in clinical research studies and understands the risks and benefits associated with participation.

47 yo F with no significant past medical history presenting as a healthy volunteer for the EyeControl device safety and feasibility study. She is fluent in Hebrew and has understandable speaking communication. She does not wear glasses or contact lenses and has no known eye conditions such as Ptosis, Strabismus or Crossed Eyes. She has no history of epilepsy or any other medical condition that would prevent her from complying with the requirements of the study. She is not pregnant or lactating.

A 55-year-old male who has a history of high cholesterol levels and has been diagnosed with thickening of the walls of the arteries in the neck. He is a non-smoker and has no history of coronary artery disease, angina, myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack, symptomatic carotid artery disease, stroke, coronary artery bypass graft, percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty, peripheral arterial disease, or abdominal aortic aneurysm. He is not currently taking any lipid-lowering medications and has a fasting low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level between 120-190 mg/dL. The patient is willing to take part in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating.

Patient A is a 10-year-old female who was diagnosed with Proteus syndrome at the age of 2. She has a documented mutation in the PIK3CA gene and her condition has been assessed by her treating physician as severe. She has undergone several surgeries to manage the overgrowth of her right leg, which has resulted in severe functional impairment. She is also experiencing chronic pain and recurrent infections. Her physician has deemed treatment necessary and she has been treated with alpelisib for the past 6 months. Patient A's medical chart is available for review during enrollment in the Novartis MAP, and her parent has consented to her participation in the study.

There is no patient involvement in this clinical trial, as it is focused on investigating the ability of anaesthesiologists to locate airway structures in a healthy subject using different methods including ultrasonography. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this particular trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old male diagnosed with progressive keratoconus in both eyes with a recent increase in corneal curvature. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His visual acuity in both eyes is 20/40 with correction. His intraocular pressure is normal in both eyes. His corneal thickness is measured at 450um in both eyes. The patient has no history of corneal scarring or other ocular disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no allergies to any medication or topical anesthetics. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has metastasized to the bones, liver and lungs. Despite undergoing several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, the patient's cancer has continued to progress rapidly. The patient is currently experiencing severe bone pain, fatigue and loss of appetite. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate bone marrow function. The patient has no history of leukemia or other bone marrow disorders, and has not received any cancer treatment within the past 21 days. She is willing to use effective methods of contraception throughout the study period. The patient has normal renal and hepatic function, and no evidence of electrolyte imbalance. She is not currently receiving any other test drugs or anticoagulation/antiplatelet treatment. The patient has no severe or uncontrolled medical conditions that could affect her participation in the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who has been admitted to the University Hospital of Amiens for an uncomplicated bone and joint infection. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medications. He denies any allergies to medications. He has no history of liver or biliary injury. His vital signs are stable. He is able to perform activities of daily living, but he reports mild pain and stiffness in the affected joint. His blood tests reveal a mild elevation in inflammatory markers. The treating physician has recommended oral switch to ofloxacin for the treatment of his infection. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the knowledge of the optimal dosing of ofloxacin in the elderly population.

56 yo F with a history of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) diagnosed 6 weeks ago. The patient completed 6 cycles of first-line standard chemotherapy with platinum combined with etoposide, achieving partial remission (PR) according to recist1.1 standard. The patient's ECoG score is 1. Imaging (CT) showed that the distance between the tumor focus and the large blood vessel is greater than 5 mm, and there is no central tumor invading the local large blood vessel or any obvious cavitary or necrotic tumor in the lung. The patient has not received chest radiotherapy before and has no history of central nervous system metastasis or pathological fracture in bone metastasis of small cell lung cancer. The patient has not used vasotargeted drugs or immunosuppressive agents before. The patient is willing to participate in this trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory difficulties and a decline in cognitive function for the past year. She reports difficulty concentrating and has noticed a decrease in her mental capacity. She has also been feeling down and has been experiencing some mild depressive symptoms. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is unremarkable. She is not currently taking any medications for her symptoms and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months. She is able to read and write and is willing to provide consent for participation in the study. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no known infectious diseases. She is a candidate for the study and will undergo a psychometric test to evaluate her cognitive function.

45-year-old male with a history of grass pollen allergy, presenting with symptoms of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and occasional asthma exacerbations during the grass pollen season. He reports a positive skin prick test and Immunoglobulin E test to grass. He has no other overlapping allergies during the grass pollen season. His asthma is well-controlled with a daily inhaled corticosteroid and bronchodilator, and his FEV1 is above 70%. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing and able to comply with study requirements and provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

A 27-year-old healthy male presented to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 23. He has no history of liver disease, liver abnormalities, or biliary abnormalities. His QTcF interval is 420 msec. He is not taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs and does not consume alcohol or tobacco. He does not have any sensitivity or allergies to the study medication or its components. His creatinine clearance is 85 mL/min. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and has not been exposed to more than four new chemical entities in the past 12 months. He has not donated blood or blood products in excess of 500 mL in the past 56 days. He is willing to follow the highly effective methods of contraception and has agreed to comply with all the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form and protocol.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is currently studying for a postgraduate degree. She is generally healthy and exercises regularly. Her body mass index is 22 kg/m² and she has no history of chronic health conditions or surgeries related to weight loss. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her current medication includes only oral contraceptives. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the thermogenic effect of ginger as she is open to natural methods of weight management. She provides consent to participate in the study after reviewing the informed consent form and discussing the study with her physician.

This is a 29 year old female who gave birth to a healthy term newborn at 39 weeks gestation. The baby was born with neonatal jaundice and bilirubin levels increased to 350 µmol/l, which requires phototherapy treatment. The mother has expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of home phototherapy treatment compared to hospital treatment. She speaks fluent Swedish and is expected to be able to handle the home phototherapy equipment. She has no history of any severe diseases, ongoing infections or weight loss greater than 10%. She is willing to answer questionnaires both at the time of discharge and 4 months after discharge. She is motivated to contribute to the scientific community and improve the outcomes of newborns with neonatal jaundice.

Patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man who has been suffering from chronic urticaria for the past 6 months. He reports experiencing rashes and itching all over his body on a daily basis. He has tried several over-the-counter antihistamines without relief. He has no known allergies or medical history. He works as an office clerk and is otherwise healthy. His physical exam is unremarkable except for the presence of erythematous wheals on his arms and legs. He has no history of physical urticaria, cholinergic urticaria, or contact urticaria.

A 35-year-old male patient is scheduled for a surgical procedure that requires general anesthesia. He has no significant medical history and is in good health with an ASA physical score of I. He does not smoke and does not use any anti-inflammatory drugs. He is not allergic to any medications. He has no known history of difficulty with anesthesia or airway management. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the use of topical chlorobenzene spray to reduce hemodynamic response and postoperative throat and ear pain, swallowing difficulty, voice anxiety, and soft LMA removal.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been a smoker for the past 20 years. He was diagnosed with emphysema 3 years ago and has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue. He has tried different medications and pulmonary rehabilitation programs but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He stopped smoking 1 year ago. His CT scan shows homogeneous emphysema. He has no significant history of respiratory infections. His vital signs are within normal limits. He is able to walk for 6 minutes without stopping. He has no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in this study and has read and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who has been experiencing severe premenstrual symptoms for the last three months. Her symptoms include breast swelling and tenderness (level 8), bloating, depression, and fatigue. She has also noticed a decrease in productivity at work and has avoided social activities due to her symptoms. She has not been on any hormonal contraception for the last 6 months and is currently using a reliable non-hormonal contraceptive method. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has no serious health problems and has not been treated with hormones in the past. She is not pregnant or lactating and her menstrual cycle is regular. She is currently experiencing her premenstrual symptoms and is within the 14 day window prior to the onset of her menstrual flow.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male who has not had any history of flavivirus infection or vaccination. He has not traveled to an area with active flavivirus transmission or Zika cautionary areas in the past 4 weeks. He has no chronic active hepatitis B or C virus infection, and no HIV infection. He has not received any live-attenuated vaccines within the past 28 days or inactivated, subunit, or conjugate vaccines within the past 14 days before the planned study vaccine administration. He is willing to provide verifiable identification and agrees not to donate bone marrow, blood, and blood products from the first study vaccine administration until 3 months after the last study vaccine administration. He is physically healthy and all clinical laboratory tests performed at screening are within normal reference ranges. He is willing to participate in the study and follow all instructions provided by the investigator.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who is scheduled to undergo a non-emergent, non-cardiothoracic surgical procedure under general anesthesia in 2 weeks. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 5 years ago. He also has a history of mild asthma and seasonal allergies, but he does not require daily medications for these conditions. His preoperative assessment revealed an ARISCAT score of 30, indicating an intermediate risk for postoperative pulmonary complications. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He has access to the internet and is fluent in English. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has no history of tracheal stoma or ventilator dependency, and he is not pregnant. He does not have any motor or visual impairment that will prohibit the utilization of the device or instructional video and handout.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with a fibroadenoma in her left breast. The fibroadenoma is about 20mm in diameter as determined by ultrasound imaging. She has no history of breast cancer or radiotherapy to the target breast. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not currently participating in any other studies using drugs or medical devices. The patient is able to understand the nature and extent of the study and the procedures required, and is willing and able to complete the screening and study procedures. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. The pain is moderate to severe and is affecting his ability to perform daily activities. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis in his lower back. He has tried different types of pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. The patient has no history of mental illness or cognitive impairment. He has not been admitted to a psychiatric facility in the past two years and does not have any life-threatening medical conditions such as cancer. He is interested in participating in a mindfulness-based intervention to help manage his pain and improve his quality of life. He is willing to attend the six group meetings and practice the mindfulness meditation techniques on a daily basis. He is not planning to use any other alternative interventions during the course of the study.

A 25-year-old male patient who has been addicted to heroin for the past 2 years and has been using the drug intravenously. He has no history of any chronic systemic illnesses or major psychiatric disorders. The patient has been on methadone maintenance treatment for the past 6 months and does not use any other drugs or alcohol. He has not been diagnosed with any infectious diseases and has not had any symptoms of illness in the past 4 weeks. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 47 year-old female with a long-standing history of knee pain and stiffness due to osteoarthritis. She has tried conservative management including physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with minimal relief. She was referred to an orthopedic surgeon who recommended a corticosteroid injection. She is hesitant to undergo the injection and has expressed interest in exploring other treatment options. She is a native English speaker with no known allergies or adverse reactions to corticosteroids. She is able to read and understand the consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman presented to her gynecologist with vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain for the past 2 weeks. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She has no history of gynecologic malignancies in her family. She underwent a pelvic examination, which revealed an enlarged uterus with no palpable adnexal masses. An endometrial biopsy was performed, which revealed endometrial adenocarcinoma. She has no comorbidities other than hypertension and is otherwise in good health. She is willing to participate in the study and agrees to undergo the recommended surgical treatment for her endometrial cancer. She understands the nature of the study and gives informed consent to participate. She is fluent in English and is able to communicate effectively with the study staff. She is 52 years old and meets the eligibility criteria for part 1 of the study.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath for the past 2 months, despite regular brushing and flossing. She has otherwise been in good health and is not currently taking any medications. She has a total of 28 teeth and has never undergone any nonsurgical or surgical periodontal therapy. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not have any known systemic diseases. The patient has no allergies to any materials used for the study, and is not a smoker or an alcoholic. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and provide written informed consent.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with chest pain that has been going on for several months. She describes the pain as a pressure or tightness in the chest, which is brought on by physical activity or emotional stress, and relieved by rest or nitroglycerin. She has no other symptoms and no significant past medical history. She is a non-smoker, and her family history is negative for cardiovascular disease. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination is unremarkable except for mild obesity with a BMI of 29. Laboratory test results show no abnormalities. She undergoes a coronary angiography which shows no significant stenosis in her coronary arteries, but impaired coronary microvascular function is detected with a Transthoracic Doppler Echocardiography measured CFVR of 2.2. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating comprehensive treatment of angina in women with microvascular dysfunction. She consents to participate in the study and is randomized to receive the intervention.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and IgA nephropathy. He was diagnosed with IgAN four years ago after presenting with proteinuria and hematuria. Renal biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and showed evidence of mesangial IgA deposition. He has been taking angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) and fish oil supplements (FOS) to control his blood pressure and reduce proteinuria. Despite this treatment, proteinuria has been persistently high. The patient has not previously been treated with mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) or azathioprine. He is otherwise in good health and has no other known medical conditions.

62-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the liver and bones. The patient has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy and is currently experiencing significant pain as well as fatigue. She lives with her daughter who provides the majority of her care. The patient is able to speak and understand English and has estimated survival of 2 years or less. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve her quality of life and symptom management, as well as to receive support for her daughter who is her primary caregiver. The patient does not have a history of severe mental illness or dementia and has not been involved with palliative care services within the last year. She is willing to participate in the biomarker sub-study if eligible.

42-year-old female with a history of invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast with mastectomy, chemotherapy, and radiation. She is now interested in bilateral breast reconstruction using implants. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke. Her BMI is 28. She has no history of prior breast surgery or radiation. The patient is willing to undergo subpectoral tissue expander placement with acellular dermal matrix and is willing to have the single drain removed on the first post-operative day. She is willing to have weekly office visits for transcutaneous fluid aspiration until expansion is complete and/or the amount of fluid aspirated is less than 10cc. She is willing to complete a 7 item multiple-choice questionnaire regarding her attitudes about her breast reconstruction.

A 64 year old man came to the clinic with a history of advanced non-squamous and non-small cell lung cancer. He has undergone two lines of chemotherapy including EGFR-TKI but was unresponsive. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. A CT scan revealed at least one measurable lesion that has not received radiotherapy and is larger than 10mm in diameter. His ECOG performance scale is 1. His hemoglobin level is 110g/L, platelets are 120×10^9/L, and neutrophils are 2.5×10^9/L. His total bilirubin is within the normal range, serum transaminase is within 2.5× the ULN, serum creatinine is 1.2 x ULN, and creatinine clearance rate is 60ml/min. He has signed and dated an informed consent for the study and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He has no history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, or heart failure. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is not taking any medications that may influence the usage of oral administration. He does not have any abnormal PT, APTT, TT, or Fbg. He is not receiving therapy for thrombolysis or anticoagulation. He has not experienced pulmonary hemorrhage or other hemorrhage greater than CTCAE class 2 within 4 weeks prior to starting the study. He does not have any long-term untreated wounds or fractures. He has not experienced any artery/venous thromboembolic events within 6 months prior to starting the study. He is not currently using anticoagulants or vitamin K antagonists. He does not abuse alcohol or drugs. He has not participated in any clinical trials within the last 4 weeks. He has not been treated with VEGFR, PDGFR, or sSRC-TKI before. He does not have a history of any second malignancies within 3 years except for cured basal cell carcinoma of skin and carcinoma in-situ of uterine cervix.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who has been struggling with her weight for the past few years. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and abdominal obesity with a waist circumference of 95 cm. She has no history of cardiovascular events, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, or dyslipidemia. She is not taking any medication for these conditions. Her thyroid function tests are within normal limits. Her creatinine and AST/ALT levels are also within normal limits. She is not currently pregnant or lactating.   Patient B is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of green tea on body weight and gut microbiota. She is willing to commit to a 12-week treatment duration and is willing to comply with the lifestyle and drug compliance diary. She is excited to potentially see positive changes in her body weight and metabolic parameters.

A 30-year-old healthy male with no acute or severe chronic diseases is needed to participate in a clinical trial investigating metabolic changes induced by genetically modified potatoes. The study aims to test starches from genetically modified potatoes that differ in terms of amylose, amylopectin, and phosphate content. If you are interested in participating, please contact the research team for further information.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22. She has no significant medical history and is a non-smoker. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives as a method of birth control. She has never been pregnant and is willing to use acceptable and effective methods of contraception during the study. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has never had any nasal problems or surgeries, and no history of drug or alcohol addiction. She is fluent in English and able to communicate well with the investigators and staff. She is willing to fast for the study and tolerate venipuncture. She has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational medicinal products within the last 30 days.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has noticed dark discoloration in her underarms for the past year. She reports that the discoloration has been persistent and has not responded to over-the-counter topical creams. She is of Hispanic descent and has a skin type IV. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or medications. She has never been pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. The patient reports no history of obesity or endocrinological diseases. She has not received any treatment for her axillary hyperpigmentation in the past 2 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the depigmenting effect of topical niacinamide versus desonide. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol, including the daily application of the assigned topical cream and the required clinic visits for evaluation. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participation in the trial and has provided informed consent.

A 34-year-old male Army veteran who served in Operation Enduring Freedom. He was honorably discharged and is currently working as a security guard. He has been experiencing symptoms of PTSD, including intrusive thoughts, nightmares, and avoidance behavior. He is currently taking sertraline and has been on a stable dose for the past 6 months. He reports that his symptoms have improved, but he feels that he needs additional help. He is physically active and exercises regularly, mostly jogging and weightlifting. He has no history of medical problems and is not on any medical profile. He speaks English fluently, and he is willing to commit to an 8-week program to explore the role of exercise in the treatment of PTSD symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 2 years. He has been taking metformin 1000mg twice daily for the past year to control his blood sugar levels. However, his HbA1c level is still above 7%. He does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has gained about 10kg in the past year. He drinks alcohol occasionally and smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. He has been advised to quit smoking and increase his physical activity. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve his diabetes control. His HbA1c level is 7.5%.

The patient is a 28-year-old primiparous woman who had a normal pregnancy with no complications. She had a vaginal delivery of a healthy baby boy weighing 3.5 kg two hours ago. She had a blood loss of 550 ml after delivery and her uterus is not contracting well. She is currently experiencing heavy bleeding and her blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse rate is 90 bpm, and her temperature is 37°C. She has no history of hypertension, preeclampsia, cardiac, renal or liver diseases, or epilepsy. She is not allergic to Carbetocin. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent.

A 20-year-old Caucasian male student has been experiencing hearing sounds that are not there, feeling emotionally detached from self and others, and troubles with memory and learning. He has not been diagnosed with any mental health disorder but has a family history of schizophrenia. He is currently studying at a university and is involved in regular physical activities such as jogging and weightlifting. He has no history of brain injury or neurological disease, and no other physical disorder that could affect brain functioning. He is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has never been treated with antipsychotics, and there are no contraindications for him to be in an MRI scanner. He meets criteria for a prodromal syndrome based upon the Structure Interview for Prodromal Syndromes (SIPS) interview. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of cardiovascular exercise in promoting brain health and improving related symptoms, cognitive difficulties, and every day social-occupational functioning in youth at imminent risk for developing a psychotic disorder such as schizophrenia.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been in a minimally conscious state for the past 6 months following a traumatic brain injury in a car accident. He has been stable with no significant changes in his level of consciousness. He is able to open his eyes spontaneously but does not follow any commands, and his responses to stimuli are inconsistent. He has normal body temperature, stable vital signs, and is breathing spontaneously without extra oxygen supply. He does not have a tracheotomy or any other surgical implants that may interfere with magnetic resonance scans. The patient's family has provided written informed consent for him to participate in the clinical trial.
