The patient will undergo fMRI and EEG evaluations before treatment and will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: DBS, TMS, or Control. The patient will undergo the assigned treatment and will be evaluated again three months later to assess any changes in his level of consciousness and prognosis.

A 45-year-old female with a history of persistent asthma for the past 10 years, who is currently using an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) with a short-acting, beta2-receptor agonist (SABA) for the past 12 weeks, presents to the clinic for a clinical trial. She has a pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 65% of predicted and has demonstrated the presence of reversible airway disease during the screening visit. She is a non-smoker and has not used any inhaled tobacco products in the past 12 months. Her body weight is 68 kg and her body mass index (BMI) is 22. She has no evidence of significant abnormality in the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) performed at screening. Her AST and ALT levels are within the normal range. She is able to give written informed consent and is capable of satisfactorily using the novel dry powder inhaler. She has no history of life-threatening asthma within the last 5 years, and no culture-documented or suspected bacterial or viral infection that is not resolved within 4 weeks of screening. She has not had any asthma exacerbation requiring oral corticosteroids within the past 12 weeks and has no clinically significant, uncontrolled condition or disease state that would put her safety at risk through study participation. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not participated in any clinical trial or received any investigational product within the past 30 days. She is willing to follow the procedures outlined in the protocol.

A 56-year-old African American male with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years presents with complaints of blurry vision and difficulty reading. He was diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy and referred to an ophthalmologist. He had a successful laser treatment a year ago. His HbA1c is 8.5%, and his blood pressure is under control with medication. He is taking metformin and lisinopril for diabetes and hypertension, respectively. He has a history of dyslipidemia and takes atorvastatin 20 mg daily. He quit smoking 2 years ago and drinks alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is married and has two daughters. He works as an accountant in a private firm. He has no known liver or kidney disease. His last eGFR was 65 mL/min/1.73m2. He has no history of gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, or myopathy. His ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements.

The patient is a 8-year-old Egyptian boy who is visiting the dentist due to complaints of sensitivity in his molars and incisors. He has no known systemic health problems and has not undergone any dental trauma. He has no orthodontic bands or dental appliances. His parents report that he brushes his teeth twice a day and has a healthy diet. He has no history of cavities. His second primary molars and permanent incisors and molars are all present. His medical and drug history is unremarkable. His HSPM and MIH status will be evaluated in this clinical trial.

48-year-old female admitted to the ICU due to sepsis with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. She has a history of obesity, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Patient is cooperative and responsive to verbal commands with a Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale (RASS) of -1. Her arterial line is in place for hemodynamic monitoring. The patient is able to understand and communicate fluently in Greek language. She has not had any previous psychiatric disturbances and has no hearing impairment. The patient is not receiving neuro-muscular blockers and is not confused. She does not have any universal conduct precautions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been struggling with moderate facial acne for the past year. She has tried various over-the-counter treatments without much success. Her acne has been affecting her self-esteem and causing her to avoid social situations. She has been prescribed EpiduoTM gel by her primary care physician and has been instructed on the proper use of the medication. Despite her physician's instructions, she has been inconsistent with her medication regimen and has missed several doses. The patient is interested in participating in the PEAce study to receive additional education on adherence to her acne treatment and hopes to improve her medication adherence and overall satisfaction with her treatment. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy during the study.

26 yo healthy male with no known medical problems with a BMI of 22 and a weight of 70 kg. He has never smoked and does not use nicotine in any form. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he is interested in contributing to medical research and also feels comfortable with the eligibility criteria. He has no history of taking any prescribed or non-prescribed medication. The patient has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of participating in this study and has provided written consent to participate.

Patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C infection. He presents with worsening renal function and is diagnosed with hepatorenal syndrome type 1. He has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma, active bacterial infections, or significant cardiac or respiratory disease. He has no history of peripheral artery disease, ischemic heart disease or hypersensitivity to terlipressin or albumin. He is not pregnant or in lactation. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to use adequate contraception since at least 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug until 14 days after the last. The patient is at least 18 years old and has no chronic renal failure.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe dry eyes for the past year. She has tried multiple forms of ocular lubricants, including drops, gels, and ointments, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has also been treated for other potential sources of ocular surface disease but has not seen any improvement. The patient has no physical disabilities that would prevent her from performing needlestick blood sampling. She has no concurrent ocular infections or known blood-borne infections. The patient is willing and able to consent to participate in the study and is between the ages of 18-100 years.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been successfully wearing soft contact lenses on a daily wear basis for the past 4 years. She wears her contact lenses for at least 8 hours per day and has vision correctable to 20/20. She has normal eyes and has not used any topical ocular medication in the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of two marketed multi-purpose solutions on the corneal epithelium after soft contact lens wear.

55-year-old male with a history of diverticulitis and recurrent episodes of constipation presents with worsening abdominal pain, bloating, and nausea. He is scheduled for elective colorectal resection surgery. The patient has no known allergies and is not pregnant. He has not been diagnosed with any bowel obstructions or planned stoma formation. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has discontinued all laxatives and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of liver cirrhosis. He has been experiencing low-grade fever, abdominal pain, and recent onset fatigue for the past few weeks. Abdominal ultrasound revealed the presence of a portal vein thrombus (PVT). The patient underwent a triphasic CT scan, which did not fulfill the criteria of malignancy, but the nature of the PVT was not clear. The patient has not received any anticoagulation treatment or suffered from any coagulopathy. He has not taken any medications that inhibit platelet aggregation. He has no contraindications for sedation. The patient's platelet count is within normal limits. He has not been diagnosed with any malignancy by the triphasic CT. There is no indication of extrahepatic metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient's Child-Pugh classification is stage B. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the role of EUS-guided FNA in the diagnosis and staging of HCC-related PVT.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 8 months. He is currently taking one oral diabetes medication to control his blood sugar levels, but his HbA1c level is still at 7.5%. He has a BMI of 38 and has been struggling with weight loss for the past few years. He has well-controlled hypertension and dyslipidemia, but he does suffer from sleep apnea. He has not had any previous bariatric or reconstructive surgeries and is willing to refrain from any such surgeries for the next 2 years. He is committed to using contraception to avoid pregnancy. He has no known allergies to nickel or titanium. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent documents for the study.

As this is a study that focuses on high school-based relationship education, there is no patient description required. Instead, eligible participants would be students currently enrolled in designated classes at the 14 participating high schools in Colorado.

The patient is a 16-year-old boy with secondary dystonia resulting from cerebral palsy. He has difficulty with both gross and fine motor skills, and his dystonia has been resistant to standard pharmacologic treatments including baclofen and diazepam. He is currently receiving botulinum toxin injections every 3 months, but the effects of these injections are limited and temporary. He has had no prior intracranial surgeries or interventions, and his thalamic anatomy is intact on MRI. He does not have any major comorbidities or uncontrolled epilepsy, and his blood pressure and blood glucose levels are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of infections or immunosuppression. His parents are supportive of the idea of DBS as a potential treatment option for his dystonia. He is able to give informed consent for the study and is willing to comply with all follow-up visits.

A 65-year-old male patient was diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) 6 months ago. He has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking medications for these conditions. His most recent echocardiogram showed a left atrial diameter of 4.8 cm and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 50%. He has tried one anti-arrhythmic drug, but it was ineffective in controlling his symptoms. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. He has no history of recent cardiac events or structural heart disease, and his NYHA class is II. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he does not have any bleeding diathesis or suspected pro-coagulant state. He is capable of complying with the study protocol requirements and is willing to adhere to the specified follow-up scheme.

25-year-old female, working as an administrative assistant, reported taking over-the-counter (OTC) analgesics for pain on at least 5 days in the last month. She has been experiencing headaches and menstrual cramps and has been using Aleve 24 Hour to manage the pain. She reports having had pain at least once in the last 3 months lasting longer than 12 hours or that she believes would have lasted longer than 12 hours if she had not treated it. She is able to read and understand English and has provided written informed consent. She purchased the investigational product, Aleve 24 Hour, and is willing to comply with the daily dose label instructions. She has never participated in a trial involving OTC analgesics in the last 6 months, and she or anyone in her household does not work for a market research company, advertising agency, public relations firm, pharmaceutical company, healthcare professional, or as part of a healthcare practice. She has no known allergies to NSAIDs and no history of heart surgery in the last 60 days or plans for heart surgery in the next 60 days. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis. She has been prescribed disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and is being monitored after starting the treatment. She experiences joint pain and stiffness, especially in her hands and feet. The pain affects her daily activities such as walking, cooking, and cleaning. She has no history of allergies and does not smoke. She lives with her husband and has two children. Her family history is negative for rheumatoid arthritis. She has been seeing a rheumatologist for her treatment and is now being offered the opportunity to receive follow-up care from a clinical nurse. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the care given by a nurse specialist is effective and acceptable. She is able to give informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who works as a teacher. She is in good health with no known medical conditions and is not currently taking any medication. She has a BMI of 24.7 kg/m^2. She has never participated in a clinical trial before and has no known allergies. She is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She does not use any herbal supplements or over-the-counter medication. She has not had any recent infections or vaccinations and has not been exposed to a live vaccine in the past 12 weeks. She has not had any symptomatic herpes zoster or herpes simplex infection within the past 90 days.

55-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of high-risk melanoma after a biopsy of a mole on her back. She is currently being evaluated for surgical resection and has been referred to this clinical trial by her oncologist. She has no previous history of melanoma or any other malignancies. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to medications. Physical examination reveals a 1.5 cm pigmented lesion on her back with no palpable lymphadenopathy. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She is interested in participating in the trial and willing to undergo the required tumor tissue biopsies.

A 32-year-old female presents with complaints of difficulty swallowing, chest pain, and occasional vomiting. She has a history of food allergies and asthma. She underwent endoscopy and biopsy, which revealed eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) with 20 eosinophils/hpf. She has been experiencing symptoms within the last month prior to enrollment. She is able to understand and provide informed consent. She is not pregnant and agrees to use FDA-approved methods of birth control for the duration of the study. She has not participated in any investigative drug study within 6 weeks prior to study entry. She is capable of completing study procedures, including endoscopy, and does not have any luminal strictures that would prevent passage of the EST. There are no other medical problems that would interfere with the study requirements or impact the quality or interpretation of the data obtained from the study. She is willing to follow the recommended four food elimination diet (FFED) and subsequent food reintroductions as outlined in the study.

A 54-year-old woman with Type 2 diabetes for 10 years, currently on insulin therapy for the past year. She self-monitors her blood glucose levels 5 times a day and has an HbA1c level of 8.5%. She is technically capable and willing to use the Abbott Sensor Based Glucose Monitoring System. She has no known allergies to medical grade adhesives and is not currently participating in any other device or drug study that could affect glucose measurements or glucose management. She has not used a Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) device in the past 4 months and is not planning to use it during the study. Her total daily dose of insulin (TDD) is 1.5iu/kg at entry to the study. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She does not receive dialysis treatment and has not experienced any acute myocardial infarction or severe hypoglycaemia requiring third party assistance in the past 6 months. She has no other concomitant disease or condition that may compromise her safety. She is willing to modify her diabetes management and is considered suitable for inclusion in the study.

As this is a retrospective national registry study, patient recruitment is not required. Data from patients who have been diagnosed with rectal cancer and underwent curative treatment between 2007-2018 in Sweden will be collected for analysis. Therefore, no patient description is necessary for this clinical trial.

A 13-year-old female patient with a history of scoliosis is scheduled for multilevel thoraco-lumbar spine surgery with instrumentation and fusion. She has been experiencing significant pain and discomfort due to her condition and is currently not on any pain medications. The patient has no other underlying medical conditions and has not undergone any previous surgeries. She has no known allergies to medication and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 31-year-old healthy, non-smoking female with a body mass index of 24 has volunteered to participate in this clinical trial. She has no significant medical history and has not taken any drugs that are moderate to potent inhibitors of CYP3A4 or CYP1A2. Her laboratory and ECG results are normal. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she has not used any investigational drugs or procedures within the last 30 days. She has no history of drug or alcohol addiction, and her alcohol intake is less than 2 units per day or 14 units per week. She has not donated or lost over 500 mL of blood in the past 3 months, and her test results for HIV, Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C, and drugs of abuse are negative. She is willing to tolerate multiple venipunctures and can fast or eat the standard meals provided. She has not used tobacco or nicotine-containing products in the past 90 days.

45 yo F with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, stage II, who has not received any prior treatment. The patient has an ECOG performance score of 1 and is in otherwise good health. Laboratory results show adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient has no history of allergies to arsenic and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has no history of cardiac arrhythmia, myocardial dysfunction or seizure disorder. The patient has no history of confusion or dementia or neurological condition that could mask a potential adverse response to the Study Drug. The patient is willing to use effective contraception from Screening through 30 days after the last dose of study drug and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient is eligible to receive CHOP alone and has no previous history of anti-cancer treatment.

The patient is a 32 year-old woman who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. She has a history of migraines and has had frequent headaches since becoming pregnant. She has tried acetaminophen for relief but has found it to be ineffective. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has not had any complications during this pregnancy and has a normal prenatal ultrasound. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is currently employed as a teacher and has been experiencing increased stress due to the pandemic. She is seeking relief from her headaches so that she can continue her daily activities and responsibilities.

This is a 52-year-old woman who has a family history of colon cancer. Her father was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 60. She has been diligent with her annual check-ups and has always had normal colonoscopies. However, her last FIT test came back positive for blood in her stool. She has not been experiencing any symptoms such as abdominal pain, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits. She underwent a colonoscopy which revealed a small adenoma. She has been referred to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of the fecal DNA methylation test compared to FIT and colonoscopy. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the detection rate of adenoma and colorectal cancer for herself and others who may be at risk.

A 22-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes mellitus after experiencing symptoms of increased thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the genetic factors that contribute to the development of this disease. She has no prior history of other autoimmune diseases or malignancies. She is generally healthy and does not take any immunosuppressive medications. She is willing to have up to three blood samples drawn over the course of less than a year.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian woman who has recently been diagnosed with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and an ejection fraction (EF) of 30%. She has been prescribed the wearable cardioverter defibrillator (WCD) for 3 months and has worn it for less than 14 days. She has no known contraindications or intolerance to beta-blocker therapy and is not pregnant. She has had occasional palpitations and feels tired frequently. The patient is not currently taking any medication for her cardiomyopathy. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the need for continuous heart rate monitoring to optimize beta-blocker dosage. The patient is committed to wearing the WCD for at least 15 hours per day to ensure her eligibility for the continuation phase of the study.

The patient is a 28 year-old non-smoking male with no history of respiratory or cardiovascular conditions. He has a BMI of 24 and is of Caucasian race. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and duration. He has no known clotting disorders or severe contact allergies to standard adhesives, latex or other materials found in pulse oximetry sensors, ECG electrodes, respiration monitor electrodes or other medical sensors. He does not have colored nail polish or non-clear artificial nails on his test digits. He has no history of bleeding disorders or personal history of prolonged bleeding from injury. He is not taking any blood thinners such as prescription medication or daily use of aspirin.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic renal insufficiency (pre-dialysis) for the past 3 years. She has a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. Her creatinine clearance is below normal, and her parathyroid hormone levels are elevated, indicating secondary hyperparathyroidism. She has not had a heart attack in the last 3 months and is not pregnant or nursing. She is interested in participating in the study to explore new treatment options for her condition.

A 72-year-old retired teacher visited the clinic for a routine check-up. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of stroke or heart attack. She has noticed that she walks slower and feels unsteady on her feet lately, but she has no pain or numbness in her legs. She has had no falls, but she is afraid of falling. She lives alone and is independent in her daily activities. She has no history of cognitive impairment, depression, or anxiety. She wears glasses for presbyopia and has normal hearing. She has no history of Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, or other neurological diseases. She has no history of osteoporosis or arthritis. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent.

This is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 38 weeks pregnant with a healthy singleton fetus in cephalic presentation. She has been experiencing regular contractions and has been admitted to the labour ward for monitoring of the active phase of labour. She has no prior history of pre-eclampsia or antepartum hemorrhage. She has not had any previous cesarean sections and is not scheduled for an elective cesarean section. She is eligible to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of a wind-up, handheld Doppler fetal heart rate monitor to the current practice of using a Pinard horn to monitor fetal heart rate during labour. The trial aims to assess the impact of the Doppler on rates of intrapartum stillbirth and neonatal deaths within 24 hours, and to compare the quality of partographs completed using the Doppler versus the Pinard horn. The patient will be randomly assigned to either the Doppler or the Pinard horn group for fetal heart rate monitoring during labour. The trial will take place at the San Raphael of St Francis Hospital Nsambya Hospital in Uganda, where the patient will receive routine care during her labour and delivery.

A 42-year-old male was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 6 months ago. Following chemotherapy, he underwent a non-myeloablative allogeneic stem cell transplant (ASCT) using a 6/6 human leukocyte antigen (HLA) matched sibling donor. The engraftment of donor cells was successful, and he was discharged from the hospital. However, he experienced acute graft versus host disease (aGvHD) with a severity of grade II. He has been receiving immunosuppressive therapy, and his aGVHD is well controlled. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and he has an estimated survival of at least 8 weeks. Currently, he does not have measurable disease. He meets all the inclusion criteria for this pilot study, and he is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of natural killer (NK) cell infusion following nonmyeloablative ASCT from matched donors.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and in her 11th week of gestation. She has no known risk factors for Down syndrome and is seeking prenatal care at a local clinic in Rhode Island. She is interested in participating in the DNAFirst study to explore the use of maternal plasma circulating cell free DNA (ccfDNA) as a primary screening test for Down syndrome. She is fluent in English and has agreed to be contacted by telephone for a survey regarding her experience with the test. She is not currently experiencing any complications with her pregnancy and is excited to learn more about this new screening technology.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic shoulder pain and limited range of motion for the past 3 years. She has tried various conservative treatment options including physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications, and corticosteroid injections, but none have provided significant relief. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She has no known allergies and is a non-smoker. Imaging studies reveal severe glenoid bone loss, and she is considered a candidate for reversed total shoulder arthroplasty with the patient-specific Glenius Glenoid Reconstruction system. She is willing to cooperate with the post-operative therapy and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

40-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that is refractory to chemotherapy, is currently in remission, and is eligible for haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). He has no suitable HLA identical related or unrelated hematopoietic stem cell donor available, and his partially HLA-mismatched (haploidentical), first-degree related donor is over 50 years old. However, he has two potential donors, one who is a young non-first-degree HLA haploidentical donor and the other is an older first-degree HLA haploidentical donor. The patient has adequate end-organ function, an ECOG performance status of 1, and no other contraindications for HSCT. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

Pt is a 50yo M with a history of locally advanced rectal cancer. The patient has undergone neoadjuvant treatment with FOLFOX for 2 months followed by TME surgery. The patient's postoperative stage was ypT4N1M0. The patient is now eligible for the clinical trial that compares mFOLFOXIRI versus mFOLFOX6 as adjuvant chemotherapy. The patient has an ECOG PS of 1, and there are no distant metastases after surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has no history of significant cardiovascular disease or unresolved toxicity higher than CTCAE v.4.0 Grade 1 attributed to any prior therapy/procedure. The patient has no known allergies to the study drugs or any of its excipients. The patient is not currently on any other investigational drug or participating in any other investigational study. The patient is not breastfeeding or pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study.

A 28 year old woman presents to the clinic for intrauterine device insertion. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has never been pregnant. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She reports mild anxiety about the procedure but has not taken any analgesics or anxiolytics in the last 24 hours. The patient has no contraindications to intrauterine device placement. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has given her consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with pelvic organ prolapse. She has been experiencing symptoms such as vaginal bulging, vaginal pressure, constipation and urinary incontinence. She is not interested in surgical management and has opted for non-surgical management with a pessary. She has no history of vaginal erosion with prior pessary use. She has no history of breast cancer or any pathology of the female reproductive organs. She is not currently using vaginal

63F with a history of coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction presented to the cardiology clinic with symptoms of heart failure, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema. She currently has a standard ICD implanted for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death. Her echocardiogram demonstrated a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% and significant dyssynchrony. Given her symptoms and LVEF, the cardiologist recommended that she undergo an upgrade to a cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) device. She has agreed to participate in this clinical trial, which will involve a pre-CRT cardiac MRI, pre-CRT/post-CRT echocardiography, and pre-CRT/post-CRT cardiopulmonary exercise testing. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has no history of claustrophobia or metal implants that would be contraindications to MRI.

52-year-old female diagnosed with stage II breast cancer after undergoing a lumpectomy. The patient has no prior history of cancer or psychiatric treatment for a serious disorder. She is fluent in English and has not yet started adjuvant therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a study to learn coping skills and improve her psychosocial and physiological adaptation to breast cancer.

A 38-year-old male with a confirmed HIV-positive diagnosis is asymptomatic and has no history of opportunistic infections. He has been taking zidovudine (AZT) for the last 6 months with no adverse effects. He has not taken any other antiretroviral drugs or investigational drugs in the last 30 days. He is willing to sign the informed consent and undergo a single oral dose of 3'-deoxy-3'-fluorothymidine (FLT) in a liquid formulation. He has no history of oral candida infection, malignancy other than cutaneous basal cell carcinoma or cervical carcinoma in situ, or significant chronic underlying medical illnesses. His neurological exam is normal, and he has no unintentional weight loss, unexplained temperature > 37.8 C, or unexplained diarrhea within the last 2 months.

A 32-year-old female presents to the dermatology clinic with concerns regarding hair loss. She has noticed an increasing amount of hair shedding in the shower and while brushing her hair. She reports no significant medical history except for a previous diagnosis of alopecia by her primary care physician. She has not used any topical or oral medications for hair growth in the past 4 weeks. The patient is interested in non-invasive treatments for her hair loss and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the potential of platelet rich plasma (PRP) injection for treatment of hair loss. She is able to understand and carry out instructions and has no personal medical history of bleeding disorders or platelet dysfunction syndrome. She is not currently on any anti-coagulation therapy or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, who weighs 75 kg and has a BMI of 21, has volunteered for a clinical trial to assess the pharmacokinetic characteristics of Lodivixx Tab. 5/160mg. He does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively nor does he take any prescription or over-the-counter medications, including oriental medication. His blood pressure is within normal limits, and he has no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatologic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, immunologic, dermal, neurologic, or psychological diseases. He has not donated blood or received blood transfusion in the past month. He has no known hypersensitivity to S-amlodipine, amlodipine, valsartan, or dihydropyridine derivatives. He does not have any clinically significant allergic disease, and his laboratory test results are within normal limits. He is willing to comply with the institutional standard meal and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 52-year-old Hispanic female who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 10 years. She has noticed a gradual decrease in vision in her right eye over the past year, which has been confirmed by an eye exam. The best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in her right eye is 20/60, while the BCVA in her left eye is 20/20. The central subfield thickness (CST) in her right eye is 340 μm. She has been receiving anti-VEGF injections in her right eye for the past 6 months, but there has been no improvement in her vision. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. She has no history of ocular pathology, vitreous hemorrhage, or recent intraocular surgery. She is not currently on any topical NSAIDs or topical steroids. She has never been treated with any intravitreal steroid. She has never received panretinal photocoagulation or focal grid macular photocoagulation. She is currently not using any antiglaucoma agents. Her hemoglobin A1C is well-controlled at 7.2%. She has no history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, anterior segment neovascularization, or retinal neovascularization. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her vision loss caused by diabetic macular edema.

Patient is a 62-year-old male from the United States who is experiencing knee pain and difficulty walking due to osteoarthritis. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He has not undergone any recent surgeries or procedures related to his knee. He has tried various pain medications and NSAIDs to manage his symptoms, but they have not provided sufficient relief. He has not undergone any physical therapy or used knee braces. He is willing and able to provide informed consent, comply with study requirements, and attend all study visits. His BMI is 29.5.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with breast cancer that has metastasized to her lungs. She is experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain, and a chest X-ray has revealed the presence of a malignant pleural effusion. Her oncologist has recommended that she participate in a clinical trial to determine the most effective treatment for her condition. She has no history of chylous effusion and requires drainage of the effusion with a chest tube. She has a performance status of ECOG 1 and her blood work shows WBC greater than 2,000 and platelets greater than 50,000. Her creatinine level is less than 2.5 mg/dL or creatinine clearance is greater than 40 mL/min. She is not pregnant or nursing and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study. She has not received any prior sclerosing agents on the affected side or intrapleural therapy, and her systemic therapy has not been changed for at least 2 weeks prior to randomization. She has not received systemic bleomycin therapy in the past, but systemic chemotherapy is allowed after pleurodesis.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who lives with her husband in a suburban area. She has a history of cognitive decline and memory impairment that has been gradually worsening over the past few years. Her husband reports that she has become more forgetful and has difficulty completing tasks that previously were easy for her. The patient has also started experiencing difficulty with planning, organizing, and problem-solving. She has become more withdrawn and has lost interest in her hobbies. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has never been diagnosed with dementia, but her husband is concerned that she may have Alzheimer's disease. She is currently receiving care from her primary care physician, who has referred her to a specialist for further evaluation. She has agreed to participate in the study to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of dementia.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease two years ago. He has been experiencing extreme fatigue, which has been affecting his daily life for the past six months. He is fluent in English and has a mean VAFS score of 6. He is currently taking carbidopa-levodopa and pramipexole for the management of his Parkinson's Disease symptoms. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse or any significant medical conditions. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Droxidopa for fatigue in patients with Parkinsonism.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of memory impairment for the last year. His family members have observed forgetfulness, difficulty in recalling recent events, and difficulty in following conversations. He is aware of his memory impairment and has sought medical advice. The neurological examination is unremarkable. The neuropsychological test battery revealed significant memory impairment, particularly in short-term memory. MRI of the brain showed mild atrophy, which is consistent with Alzheimer's disease. The amyloid PET scan revealed amyloid deposition in the brain. He is married and has two children who are willing to accompany him to the office visits. He has no history of claustrophobia or any other contraindications for MRI. He has not been exposed to radiation recently and has no history of intracranial hemorrhage or any other significant medical conditions.

35 F with a BMI of 37.5, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, presented to the bariatric surgery clinic for potential surgical treatment of obesity. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and sleep apnea. Her fasting blood glucose level was 8.5 mmol/l, and her HbA1c level was 8.9%. She had previously tried lifestyle modification but was unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. The patient is interested in participating in a study on the genetic factors associated with obesity and diabetes and is willing to undergo laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery. She has signed the consent form and is willing to provide biological samples for research purposes.

A 65-year-old retired teacher was recently implanted with an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) after experiencing a sudden cardiac arrest. She is a widow and lives with her daughter. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She is currently taking medications for hypertension, high cholesterol, and diabetes. The patient is concerned about the shock that ICD can administer and is experiencing anxiety and depression related to her recent diagnosis. She is aware of the device and its function. She can read and write and has no history of cognitive impairment or neurological disorders. She is willing to participate in the study to learn more about the ICD and its effects on her quality of life. She does not have any other medical conditions that would interfere with the study.

A 38-year-old male presents with symptoms of major depressive disorder, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities he once enjoyed. He reports difficulty sleeping and a lack of energy. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders and is currently not taking any medication. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient undergoes an auditory evoked Event Related Potential (ERP) test to measure the N100 amplitude slope. The test reveals that he falls within the aberrant N100 response outlier criteria with a N100 slope of 1.8. The patient is randomized to receive either Quetiapine XR adjunctive therapy or SSRI monotherapy for a duration of six weeks. He has no hearing impairment and does not have any medical conditions that would affect the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of the study treatment. He has not participated in any drug trials within the past four weeks and is not currently taking any cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors or inducers. The patient has no substance or alcohol dependence and has not abused opiates, amphetamine, barbiturate, cocaine, cannabis, or hallucinogens within the past four weeks. The patient does not have unstable or inadequately treated medical illness and has a complete blood cell count within the normal range. He has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2.5 x 1,000,000,000 per liter, indicating he is eligible to participate in the study.

This is a 60 year old male with a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction (AEG type II). He underwent endoscopic ultrasound which showed a 4 cm mass involving the gastroesophageal junction with extension beyond the muscularis propria. Biopsy confirmed a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis did not show any evidence of distant metastasis. He was evaluated by a multidisciplinary team and deemed a candidate for surgical resection. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing esophagogastrectomy versus extended gastrectomy for AEG type II. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidemia 3. Gout 4. Chronic low back pain 5. Osteoarthritis 6. History of kidney stones.

The patient is a 65-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2. He has no history of dyslipidemia and is not taking any medications that could interfere with lipid metabolism. He does not smoke and has never smoked more than ten cigarettes per day. His glycaemic and lipid parameters are normal. He has no significant medical history and is able and willing to comply with study procedures. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance scientific understanding of the metabolic pathway of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) in the human body.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 0, with a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days. She has no significant medical history, and her family history is negative for any genetic disorders. She is currently in her 10th week of pregnancy and desires to undergo comprehensive screening for Down Syndrome and other aneuploidies. She does not have a multiple gestation. She speaks fluent English and has no difficulty in understanding the study details. She has been provided with informed consent and understands the study's purpose and procedures.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been experiencing knee joint pain due to chondromalacia for the past year. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. His Kellgren-Lawrence grade is 2, and his pain score on the 100mm VAS pain scale is 60mm. He does not have any significant pathological tests at his screening visit, and his medication is confirmed to be stable within one week of his study enrollment. He is willing to follow the guidelines of the investigators during the study and to visit the hospital five times, including for screening. The patient does not have any autoimmune disease, hypersensitivity to grafting materials or porcine protein, inflammatory arthritis, gout, or calcium pyrophosphate disease. He has not undergone radiation therapy or cancer treatment within the past two years and does not have diabetes. He also does not have any serious health conditions that may affect the study results. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, nor is he planning to become pregnant. He has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who is scheduled for upper extremity surgery under general anesthesia. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of bleeding diathesis or anticoagulant treatment. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics or opioids. The skin at the site of the needle puncture is intact and there is no evidence of infection. He is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

52-year-old woman with a diagnosis of Type II diabetes for 5 years, currently on metformin and glipizide, presenting with poor glycemic control (HbA1c of 9.5%). The patient resides in a rural area and has limited access to endocrinology specialists and diabetes education programs. She reports difficulty managing her blood glucose levels, despite taking her medications as prescribed and following a recommended diet. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. She speaks and reads English fluently. The patient does not have a diagnosis of dementia or mental retardation, is not a resident of a personal care home, assisted living, or long-term care facility, and does not have a history of significant drug or alcohol abuse. She does not have an active malignant process or steroid-induced diabetes, and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 30 year old female experiencing significant pain and discomfort in her right shoulder. The pain has been present for the past 4 weeks and is interfering with her daily activities. She rates her pain at a 4 on the Wong-Baker scale. The pain is localized to the infraspinatus muscle and occasionally refers to her upper arm. She has not taken any NSAIDs or muscle relaxants in the past 48 hours. She has never had any injections or dry needling in the cervical region or shoulder girdle. She has no history of fractures, dislocations, or neurologic diseases. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to metals. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing dry eyes, blurred vision, and eye fatigue for the past few months, especially during long hours of computer work and exposure to air conditioning. She has never been diagnosed with any eye diseases and does not wear contact lenses. She has tried using over-the-counter eye drops with no relief. Her eye exam shows mild to moderate tear film dysfunction syndrome, with a TBUT of 7 seconds, Schirmer test of 10 mm, and corneal staining of grade II on the Oxford scale. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any medications or supplements. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness and safety of preservative-free ophthalmic solution PRO-087 versus Systane ® Ultra and Ultra Preservative Free in treating her condition. She is able to attend all follow-up appointments and comply with the study protocol.

This is a 35 year old male who is an avid runner and has been experiencing pain on the lateral aspect of his right ankle for several months. He noticed swelling and discomfort with activities such as running and jumping. MRI showed a partial tear of the peroneus brevis tendon in Zone 2. Conservative treatment was attempted with physical therapy, ankle bracing, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication, but his symptoms persisted. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a novel surgical technique that utilizes cryopreserved Human Amniotic Membrane (C-HAM) graft to reduce inflammation and adhesions after surgical repair of the peroneal tendon. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including restrictions on pre and postoperative anti-inflammatories except for ecotrin 325 mg QD for DVT prophylaxis during the postoperative immobilization period.

The patient is a 50-year-old man diagnosed with KRAS 4MUT+ pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has received standard chemotherapy, but his cancer has progressed. The patient has confirmed HLA types HLA-A11:01 and HLA C08:02. He has measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by the local site investigator/radiology. He has an evaluable archival tumor sample to submit for analysis. The patient has adequate organ function and a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. He does not have a history of interstitial lung disease or active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years. The patient has not fully recovered from any effects of major surgery or has evidence of detectable infection. Surgeries that required general anesthesia must be completed at least 2 weeks before the first study treatment administration. The patient has not had chemotherapy, definitive radiation, or biological cancer therapy within 4 weeks (2 weeks for palliative radiation) prior to the first dose of study therapy, non-cytotoxic small molecule therapeutics within 5 half-lives (or 2 weeks, whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of study treatment, or has not recovered to Common Toxicity Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade 1 or better from any adverse events that were due to cancer therapeutics administered more than 4 weeks earlier. The patient has not received a live-virus vaccine within 30 days of planned treatment start. Seasonal flu vaccines that do not contain live virus are permitted. The patient is not currently participating in or has participated in a study of an investigational agent or has used an investigational device within 28 days prior to the first dose of study intervention. The patient does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of study drug. The patient does not have a known additional malignancy that is progressing or has required active treatment within the past 2 years. The patient does not have known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis. The patient does not have a known history of Hepatitis B, active Hepatitis C virus infection, or HIV. The patient does not have a known psychiatric or substance abuse disorder that would interfere with cooperating with the requirements of the study. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive or father children within the projected duration of the study, starting with the screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of study intervention. The patient has not had an allogenic tissue/solid organ transplant.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer that has not responded to previous treatments. She has undergone surgery and chemotherapy but the tumor has continued to grow. She is currently experiencing pain in her chest and back and has difficulty breathing. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is alert and oriented, and appears well-nourished. Physical examination shows a palpable mass in her left breast, as well as enlarged lymph nodes in her left axilla. CT scan confirms the presence of metastatic disease in her lungs and liver. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is aware of the potential risks and benefits. She is not currently pregnant or nursing, and agrees to use effective contraception during the trial. She has no known hypersensitivity to SR-45023A analogs and meets all other eligibility criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with metastatic gastric cancer that has progressed after treatment with available therapies. She presents with abdominal discomfort, bloating, and decreased appetite. Imaging studies reveal multiple liver metastases and peritoneal carcinomatosis. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has no history of autoimmune disease or HIV infection. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no known allergies to medications. She has not received any anticancer medications or investigational drugs within the protocol-defined intervals before the first administration of study drug. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 59-year-old male who was diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) two years ago. He received fludarabine as his first-line treatment and achieved a partial response. He was then treated with ibrutinib, which he received for more than a year before he progressed. His disease is now relapsed and he is experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His bone marrow function is adequate with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,500/mm3, platelets of 80,000/mm3, and hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL. His coagulation, renal, and hepatic functions are also adequate. He has no history of drug-induced pneumonitis or inflammatory bowel disease. He has not received any anti-cancer or investigational therapy within 14 days prior to initiation of study treatment. He has recovered from the toxicities of his previous treatment except for alopecia. He is negative for HIV and hepatitis B or C. He is willing to use medically accepted forms of birth control for the duration of the study treatment and for at least one month following completion of venetoclax and/or idelalisib, or 12 months following rituximab, whichever occurs later. He has a comprehensive understanding of the trial and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

10-year-old male diagnosed with Ataxia Telangiectasia (A-T) characterized by progressive ataxia, conjunctival telangiectasia, and respiratory infections. The patient has low lymphocyte counts, IgA and IgG subclass deficiency, and is at risk of malignancies due to the mutation in the ATM gene on chromosome 11. The patient has not received IgG treatment and is willing to participate in the clinical trial investigating the prevalence of respiratory infections in A-T patients compared to healthy controls. The patient and their legal guardian have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the past year. He reports difficulty in initiating urine flow, weak stream, and the need to urinate frequently, especially at night. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been on alpha-blockers for the past 6 months with little improvement. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications apart from the alpha-blockers. He has a BMI of 27 and a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. He is retired and spends most of his time at home with his wife. He enjoys reading and watching movies. He has no known allergies or contraindications for the AQUABEAM system or hemostatic agents. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to find a more effective treatment for his symptoms.

A 16 year old female with a Class II division 1 malocclusion and mild crowding requiring maxillary first premolar extractions and canine retraction. No previous history of orthodontic treatment or periodontal problems. Good oral and general health. No systemic diseases or regular use of medications that could interfere with orthodontic treatment. No blocked out or impacted maxillary canines. Complete permanent dentition excluding third molars.

A 60-year-old male presents to the ophthalmology clinic with a history of glaucoma. He has been on treatment for the past 4 years, but his intraocular pressure (IOP) has been fluctuating between 24-27 mmHG despite being compliant with his medication. He has no history of ocular surgery or inflammation. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes. The anterior chamber angles are open in both eyes with no evidence of peripheral anterior synechiae. The optic nerve head shows a cup-to-disc ratio of 0.8 in the right eye and 0.7 in the left eye, with thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer. Central corneal thickness is within normal limits. The patient is currently taking timolol 0.5% twice daily and latanoprost 0.005% once daily. He has no known allergies to any ocular medication. The patient is willing to discontinue his current medications and participate in the study to evaluate the efficacy of Xalacom in lowering his IOP.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with invasive breast carcinoma. She has undergone preoperative pathology confirmation and is clinically T1 or T2 with a maximum tumor diameter of ≤5cm. She is clinically ALN negative and has no clinical or imaging evidence of distant metastasis. The patient is scheduled to receive skin sparing mastectomy or nipple sparing mastectomy. She has a BMI less than 35 and has no or mild mastoptosis. The prosthesis to be implanted is less than 500ml. The patient is able and willing to sign the Informed Consent Form (ICF). She has no history of smoking or diabetes.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis two years ago. She experiences intermittent bouts of fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty with balance. She has a history of optic neuritis in the right eye, which resulted in blurred vision for several weeks. She has no other neurological or medical conditions. She is currently taking disease-modifying therapy for multiple sclerosis. She is able to walk independently for at least six minutes without rest. She is a stay-at-home mother of two children and does not engage in regular exercise. She reports experiencing fatigue during her daily activities, especially in the afternoon. She enjoys reading and watching movies in her free time. Her BMI is within the normal range, and her blood pressure and heart rate are normal. She has no significant physical findings on examination. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) six months ago. He has already undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not achieved a complete remission. His recent PET-CT showed persistent disease in the mediastinum, abdomen, and pelvis. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. His creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has a CD34+ stem cell count of 7 x 10^6/kg. He understands the study protocol and has provided informed consent. The patient is willing to complete the required follow-up visits after the study treatment.

The patient is a 60-year-old active woman who has noticed difficulty hearing conversations in noisy environments. She has not previously used hearing aids but is interested in exploring options for improving her hearing. She has no history of middle ear issues or any other medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. Her hearing loss is mild to moderate, with her better ear having a PTA1/2/4 of 45dB. She is fluent in English and has no language difficulties. She is willing to participate in the trial and is available for a three-hour visit to the AMC.

A 57-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain that started while he was resting. He described the pain as a heavy, crushing sensation with a feeling of tightness in his chest. He also complained of shortness of breath and sweating. His medical history includes hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. On admission, he had an ECG which showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. The patient was diagnosed with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction and was immediately transferred to the coronary care unit.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with leiomyosarcoma of the uterus that has come back or persistent. She has undergone one prior cytotoxic therapy and currently has measurable disease. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other invasive malignancies except for non-melanoma skin cancer. The patient's baseline laboratory values are within normal limits, including leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, serum creatinine, bilirubin, AST/ALT, and alkaline phosphatase. She has signed an informed consent and authorization permitting release of personal health information. The patient is able to take oral medication, maintain a fast for 2 hours before and 1 hour after alisertib administration, and has not taken agents that affect gastric pH within 4 days (any proton pump inhibitor), or 1 day (any histamine-2 antagonist) of the planned start of therapy. She is able to avoid all other types of antacids for 2 hours before and 2 hours after each dose of MLN8237. The patient's performance status is 1.

A 60-year-old woman who lives in Belgium visited her ophthalmologist for her annual eye exam. She has no significant history of eye disease or surgeries. She has been experiencing difficulty reading small print and has noticed a decrease in her vision at night. She has no history of smoking, but does drink alcohol occasionally. She has not taken any nutritional supplements containing vitamin D or trace nutrients in the past 4 months. She has a STARS® score of 12, indicating moderate-to-high risk for AMD. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if she needs nutritional supplementation for her eye health. She has no known allergies to any medications or food. She exercises regularly and has no significant medical history.

Pt is a 32yo F with a BMI of 31 kg/m², presenting with a history of overweight and a desire to lose weight. She has no known gastrointestinal illness or history of bariatric surgery. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not currently taking pro or prebiotics or antibiotics. She is not participating in any other clinical studies and is enrolled in the French national healthcare system. She has not undergone any weight loss programs or diets within the last 3 months. The patient has signed the informed consent for the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) after a routine ultrasound screening. He denies any history of alcohol consumption exceeding 20 g/day or any metabolic diseases. He is not currently experiencing any acute illnesses or untreated conditions that require treatment. He is willing to use an effective form of birth control if needed. The patient has no history of impaired hepatic or renal functions. He is willing to participate in the study and fill out a TCM syndromes questionnaire. The patient has no history or presence of any condition that would endanger his safety or affect the study result.

Patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no history of heart disease, hypertension, renal or hepatic diseases, glaucoma, hyperthyroidism, or any medical conditions contraindicated for the study. The patient is not currently on any psychotropic medication and has not been diagnosed or treated for Axis I disorders including major depression, bipolar affective disorder, schizophrenia, and panic disorder within the past year. The patient does not have a current dependence on alcohol or drugs or treatment for drug or alcohol addiction within the past 5 years. The patient is willing to use acceptable birth control methods if female and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing memory loss, difficulty with language, and confusion for the past year. He was diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease and has been taking medications to manage his symptoms for the past six months. He has had an MRI in the past which confirmed the presence of beta-amyloid brain pathology. The patient is generally in good health, but has high blood pressure that is managed with medication. He is married and lives with his wife who provides him with support and assistance. The patient is able to understand and sign the written informed consent, and has committed to using effective contraception as he is of child-bearing potential. The patient is willing to undergo PET imaging with the investigational imaging agent [18F]PI-2620 at a radioactive dose of 185 MBq, one with high specific activity (≤ 5 µg tracer mass dose), another one with low specific activity (40-50 µg tracer mass dose). The patient is also willing to commit to the study procedures and assessments, and is able to cooperate with the study team.

A 56-year-old male diagnosed with a gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEP-NET) and currently being treated with somatostatin analogues (SSA) for the past 6 months. The patient has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy with no other ongoing treatments. The patient has experienced some side effects from the SSA treatment, including occasional diarrhea and abdominal pain, but has not had any significant complications. They have provided consent to participate in this study and are willing to provide information about their treatment experience and quality of life.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with severe alcohol use disorder according to DSM 5. He reports heavy drinking, consuming more than 60g of alcohol per day, at least 5 days a week. He is right-handed and has normal vision. He has not taken any psychotropic medication in the last 14 days and does not have any severe withdrawal symptoms (CIWA-Ar score <= 4). He is not currently intoxicated, with a breath alcohol concentration of less than 0.3 ‰. He has no contraindications to the prescription of nalmefene. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the written informed consent.

This is a 65-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with malignant pleural effusion. She has not received any previous treatment and has undergone testing for driver genes (EGFR/ALK/ROS1). She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial, including being between the ages of 18 and 80, having an ECOG score of 0 to 2 or a KPS of ≥70, and having metastatic lesions in the distant area that do not affect lung function. She has no contraindications for radiotherapy, EGFR-TKI, or chemotherapy. She will receive primary tumor radiotherapy with IMRT technology and a planned dose that includes 100% GTV and 90% of the prescribed dose that includes 98% to 100% of PTV. Additionally, her normal lung (full lung volume minus GTV volume) V20 ≤ 32%, MLD≤20Gy, and metastatic tumor radiotherapy will be a three-dimensional radiotherapy technique. She has no major organ dysfunction or laboratory test indicators that fall outside of the normal range. She has given informed consent for the treatment and follow-up and is expected to have good compliance with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing eye dryness for the past 6 months. She has been using artificial tears several times a day, but has not experienced significant relief of her symptoms. She wears glasses and is willing to discontinue their use during the study period. She has no significant medical history or allergies, and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to withhold the use of artificial tears during the study period. She has no history of contact lens use.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been suffering from chronic pain for the past five years. He reports pain in his lower back, hips, and legs that is constant and interferes with his daily activities. He has tried various treatments, including physical therapy, medications, and injections, but has not found significant relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a novel approach to treating chronic pain called Floatation REST. He has no previous experience with floating and is willing to give written informed consent. He has no acute illnesses that may exacerbate his chronic pain condition and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is physically able to participate in the study and has no clinical conditions that may prevent him from floating. He understands the protocol requirements, instructions, and study-related restrictions, as well as the nature, scope, and possible consequences of the study.

A healthy male or female volunteer aged 18 years or older is needed for this clinical trial. The volunteer must have a BMI within 20% of the Desirable Weights for Adults-1983 Metropolitan Height and Weight Table. The volunteer must not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse and must not be currently smoking. The volunteer must have normal laboratory test results and be free from any clinically significant disorder involving the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal, immunologic, hematologic, endocrine, or neurologic system(s) or psychiatric disease. Female volunteers must not be pregnant or breastfeeding and must be practicing an acceptable method of birth control. Volunteers must not have taken any drug known to induce or inhibit hepatic drug metabolism in the 28 days prior to Period I dosing and must not have taken any systemic prescription medication in the 14 days prior to Period I dosing. The volunteer will be required to complete a screening process including a physical examination, blood and urine tests, and an electrocardiogram. The study involves taking a single oral dose of either 5 mg Glyburide/500 mg Metformin Hydrochloride Tablets by Purepac Pharmaceutical Co. or 5 mg/500 mg CLUCOVANCE® Tablets by Bristol-Myers Squibb Company under fasting conditions. The purpose of the study is to compare the relative bioavailability of the two tablets.

A 47-year-old woman with a history of triple negative breast cancer presents to the oncology clinic with relapsing metastatic disease. She has already undergone chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and immunotherapy but has not seen significant improvement in her condition. Imaging studies show a 3 cm injectable lesion in her right axilla and a distant non-injected measurable site in her left lung. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and all laboratory values are within normal limits. She has no history of auto-immunity, severe eczema, or ongoing inflammatory skin conditions. She has no significant cardiac disease and is not taking any anticoagulant or anti-platelet medication. She is willing to comply with study visits and procedures and has medical insurance coverage. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use double barrier methods of contraception during the treatment period and for up to 6 weeks after the last Pexa-Vec administration. She is eligible for the study.

The patient is a 12 year-old girl who has been experiencing episodes of rapid heartbeats and palpitations for the past year. She has no prior medical history and takes no medication. She has a family history of heart disease, with her mother having had a heart attack at age 45. She has undergone several diagnostic tests which revealed that she has an atrioventricular accessory pathway. Her legal guardians have been informed of the ablation procedure and have given written consent. The patient is willing and able to comply with the follow-up evaluations.

A 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented to the hospital for elective surgery to remove his gallbladder. He was taking metformin and lisinopril for his medical conditions. The patient had no known allergies. During the surgery, the patient experienced a drop in blood pressure to 90/60 mm Hg, which was a 25% drop from his preoperative baseline. The anesthesiologist administered a bolus of cafedrine/theodrenaline to treat the hypotension. The patient remained stable for the remainder of the surgery and was monitored closely for the next hour. The patient consented to participate in the study, and his data was recorded. The patient was assigned to Cohort A due to his age, pre-existing comorbidities, and elective surgery. The patient's blood pressure was monitored every two minutes for the first 15 minutes after the medication was administered and then every 5 minutes thereafter. The patient did not experience any adverse effects from the medication, and his blood pressure remained stable.

A 6-year-old boy was referred to the clinic by his school nurse due to his difficulty in reading and writing. During the exam, it was revealed that he had amblyopia in his right eye with a visual acuity of 20/100. The examination also showed a hyperopic error in his right eye and an anisometropia of 2.5D between the two eyes. He started wearing glasses and patching treatment for 2 hours daily after the diagnosis. After 5 months of treatment, his visual acuity improved to 20/60. However, the improvement stopped, and amblyopia is still present. Therefore, he is a candidate for the clinical trial to increase his patching treatment from 2 to 6 daily hours. He is eligible for the study as he is between the ages of 3 to < 8 years old and has a visual acuity of 20/40 to 20/160 in the amblyopic eye with an inter-ocular difference of >2 lines. His parents are willing to participate in the study and able to comply with the prescribed treatment.

A 57-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. He has an FVC greater than 40% predicted and DLCO greater than 30% predicted. He has no history of acute coronary syndromes, atrial fibrillation, coronary angioplasty, or stenting within the past 24 weeks. He has no Class II, III, or IV heart failure and his left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 50%. He has no uncontrolled hypertension or a history of conditions that could increase the risk of complications from hypertension. He is not currently experiencing an IPF exacerbation or current upper or lower respiratory tract infection. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol abuse. He is not currently taking Pirfenidone or have received Pirfenidone within the previous 30 days. He is able to refrain from the use of prohibited prescription or non-prescription drugs. He has no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications, or components thereof or a history of drug or other allergy that, in the opinion of the investigator or GSK Medical Monitor, contraindicates their participation.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been struggling with breast enlargement for the past few years. She complains of back pain, shoulder pain, and difficulty finding clothes that fit properly. She wears a cup size of D and has ptosis of 6 cm. She is a non-smoker and not currently on any anti-coagulants. She has good quality thick skin and is interested in breast reduction to improve her quality of life. She is affiliated with a social security scheme and has signed a free and informed consent form. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and hopes to achieve a reduction in breast enlargement without any visible scarring.

A 45-year-old Chinese male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) with a stable estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 30 ml/min/1.73 m². He has been under the care of a nephrologist for the past two years and has been managed with blood pressure control, low-protein diet, and phosphate binders. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or hypertension. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the relationship between bone metabolic markers and kidney function progression, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, and bone loss in patients with CKD G3-5ND. He is willing to communicate through a mobile platform to monitor and manage his complications. He understands that the study requires at least two measurements of serum creatinine with a minimum interval of three months and that he cannot participate if he is currently under any interventional clinical trial, undergone organ transplantation, or currently receiving renal replacement therapy.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of major depression presents with symptoms of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities that were previously enjoyable to her. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, and they have been affecting her daily life and work. She has tried various antidepressants in the past, but none have provided sustained relief of her symptoms. She is currently not taking any medications and is willing to participate in a clinical trial for a new antidepressant.
