She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use a reliable method of birth control during the study. Her HAMD score is 22, indicating moderate to severe depression. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence and has no significant medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She has not used any psychotropic drugs within the past 3 days and is willing to forgo their use throughout the study. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with them.

The patient is a 17-year-old male with a history of Ewing's sarcoma. He has undergone surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. Unfortunately, his cancer has returned and he has failed one prior therapy. He has an evaluable tumor lesion by RECIST criteria version 1.1. He has available tissue for protein and genomic analysis. He is currently on opioid pain medications for his pain. His Lansky score is 80%. He has normal cardiac function with a shortening fraction of 31%. He had a negative β-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) pregnancy test and is using a barrier method of contraception. He has given written informed consent/assent prior to any study-specific procedures. He is able to swallow a tablet. He has recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior therapy to ≤ grade 1 before entering this study. He has not received systemic chemotherapy or biologic therapy within the last 2 weeks and radiation therapy outside the central nervous system ≤ 14 days prior to the start of neratinib. He has no radiation to the central nervous system within the last 12 weeks. His absolute neutrophil count is 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets 120 x 10^9 /L, hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, total bilirubin 0.9 ULN, AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) 2 X ULN, serum creatinine 0.9 X ULN, and creatinine clearance > 60mL/min/1.73m^2. He has no symptomatic or unstable brain metastases. He has no clinically active cardiac disease, including prolonged QTc interval ≥ 481ms. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. He is not being actively treated for a concurrent malignancy. He has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness, significant chronic gastrointestinal disorder with diarrhea, known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)-related disease, known history of hepatitis C or known active hepatitis B infection, or hypersensitivity to any component of the investigational product.

Patient is a 48-year-old man from the United States with a history of colorectal cancer. He has undergone previous treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He is scheduled for cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) due to peritoneal carcinomatosis. The patient is in good general health with an ASA Class II status. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and has a BMI of 27. He has no history of significant comorbidities or systemic disorders.

A healthy 16-year-old Asian-American male with no history of ocular diseases, ocular surgeries, or chronic or recurrent severe ocular inflammatory disease. The patient has not had any ocular infections or inflammation within the past three months and has no history of clinically significant or progressive retinal disease such as retinal degeneration, diabetic retinopathy or retinal detachment. The patient has not been diagnosed with ocular hypertension or glaucoma or any other ocular disease. The patient has no history of intraocular surgery, ocular laser surgery, or any abnormality preventing reliable tonometry of either eye. Additionally, the patient has not experienced any hypersensitivity or allergy to beta blockers and sulfa drugs, severe, unstable or uncontrolled cardiovascular, hepatic or renal disease, bronchial asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The patient has not worn contact lenses and is willing and able to discontinue contact lens wear if necessary. The patient is between the ages of 15 and 18 and will be participating in the study as part of the adolescent group to determine the effect of age and ethnic background on ocular aqueous humor dynamics and biometric parameters.

45F diagnosed with asthma since childhood, currently taking high-dose ICS and LABA, with at least one additional controller medication for 12 months. Has a history of recurrent asthma exacerbations requiring oral corticosteroids (OCS) at least twice a year. Patient has a documented blood eosinophil count of 400 cells/microliter in the last 12 months. Patient has been on stable asthma therapy for the past 12 months and has recorded baseline data in medical records or questionnaires for 12 months. Patient has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchiectasis, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency, or malignancy of any kind. Patient has not been on any biologics for asthma for at least 4 months and has not been on omalizumab for at least 1 month. Patient has no acute or chronic condition that may limit their ability to complete questionnaires or participate in the study. Patient is willing and able to read and comprehend written instructions, and complete the questionnaires required by the protocol.

10-year-old male diagnosed with ADHD and currently taking methylphenidate as a treatment. The patient presents with symptoms of inattention, impulsivity and hyperactivity that interfere with academic and social functioning. The patient's parents report that he has difficulties in recognizing and interpreting facial expressions, which may affect his social interactions with peers and adults. The patient has no history of neurological or mental conditions other than ADHD and is not suffering from asthma. The patient is cooperative and able to complete computerized tasks that examine recognition and memory of facial expressions. The patient's social function will be examined by questionnaires filled by parents and teachers. The patient and their family have consented to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old female presents to the clinic with a BMI of 32.5 kg/m2 and a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and sleep apnea. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for weight loss. She is ambulatory, able to perform moderate exercise, and between 18 and 60 years of age. She provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with all aspects of the protocol. She has not been treated with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) in the last 14 days or any time prior to randomization. She does

A 35-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (HBeAg negative) 5 years ago. He had no history of other chronic diseases or medication use. The patient underwent an Omnibus study and completed it without any adverse events. The patient's most recent HBV DNA PCR test showed an undetectable viral load in the past 12 months. The patient is willing to participate in this study and provide written informed consent. The patient has no plan to become pregnant, and he is not currently breastfeeding. The patient has no co-infection with HCV, HDV, or HIV. The patient has not received any other anti-HBV treatment during the Omnibus study or the study's screening period. The patient's laboratory values are within normal limits, and no abnormality was found that would exclude him from the study. The patient has no evidence of renal insufficiency or drug abuse. The patient is not enrolled or planning to enroll in another clinical trial of an investigational agent while participating in this study.

An 68-year-old retired man was referred to a hematologist for evaluation of persistent anemia. The patient reported feeling fatigued, weak, and short of breath with minimal exertion for several months. He also reported occasional night sweats but denied any fever, weight loss, or bleeding. His past medical history was significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of prostate cancer, treated with radiation therapy. The patient did not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. On physical examination, he appeared pale and had mild hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory tests showed normocytic anemia with a hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dL, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia. The peripheral blood smear showed dysplastic changes in all three cell lines. The bone marrow biopsy revealed trilineage dysplasia with no evidence of blasts, and the cytogenetic analysis showed normal karyotype. The patient was diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). He was offered a clinical trial comparing low-dose decitabine with standard supportive care.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who is currently on hemodialysis. He has been on statin therapy for the management of his high LDL-C levels. The patient has a BMI of 27 kg/m² and has not received Evolocumab (AMG 145) or any other investigational therapy directed against PCSK9. He has no history of statin intolerance or hypersensitivity or allergic reaction to mammalian-derived drug preparations. The patient has not used any illicit or licit drugs in the past 12 months. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of evolocumab after a single 140 mg subcutaneous (SC) dose in adults with normal renal function or severe renal impairment or ESRD receiving hemodialysis.

A 28-year-old male patient with a spinal cord injury above the C8 level presents with decreased hand and arm function following a motor vehicle accident that occurred two years ago. The patient has an ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS) classification level of D and has some active intrinsic hand muscles in at least one UE and active extrinsic hand muscles in both UE. The patient reports difficulty with daily activities such as bathing, eating, and writing due to decreased hand function. The patient is able to follow multiple step commands and communicate pain or discomfort. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo the testing. The patient does not have any implanted metallic devices in the head or a pacemaker, no history of seizures, and no severe contractures of UE that would limit participation in FTP. The patient has not received Botulinum toxin injection in the tested UE in the last 3 months and is not pregnant.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been scheduled for a surgical procedure. She has been referred for pre-assessment and has been approached to participate in a pilot study evaluating an online preoperative assessment tool called MyPreOp. She has a good command of the English language, is lucid and able to provide written responses. She has no significant medical history that would preclude her from participating in the study. She has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to complete both the MyPreOp assessment and the nurse-led pre-assessment process as per standard practice. She has access to a computer device at the hospital and is willing to complete the satisfaction questionnaire about her experience of using MyPreOp.

63F with a history of breast cancer diagnosed 4 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy with axillary lymph node dissection and adjuvant radiation. She was found to be ER+ and PR+. She received adjuvant chemotherapy with no evidence of disease until she presented with shortness of breath and was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the lungs. She was started on hormonal therapy with an aromatase inhibitor but developed arthralgias and had to discontinue. Further imaging showed additional bone and liver metastases. She was started on Faslodex and has completed 2 cycles. She reports feeling more fatigued and has noted some mild hot flashes. She is otherwise tolerating the medication well. She is interested in participating in this study and willing to complete the questionnaire. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 6 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling with fecal incontinence for the past year. She has tried various treatment options including dietary changes, medication, and pelvic floor exercises, but none of them seem to provide significant relief. She works as a nurse and her condition is affecting her job and personal life. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial as a potential solution for her fecal incontinence. She has no history of anorectal surgery, autoimmune disease, or infectious diseases. She is not currently pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study period. Her Wexner's fecal incontinence score is 7, indicating moderate severity. She has no history of abuse of alcohol or drugs. She is willing to sign the informed consent and undergo the injection of autologous cultured adipose-derived stem cells for the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with end-stage renal disease who requires hemodialysis. He has been referred by his nephrologist for the creation of a primary vascular access. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or stroke. His medications include lisinopril, amlodipine, metformin, and insulin. He reports no history of previous surgery on his arms. Clinical examination reveals a cephalic vein at the distal third of his forearm, radial pulse, and ulnar pulse. The Allen test shows patent palmar arches. Arterial and venous duplex ultrasound examination shows a patent cephalic vein, ≥2mm in diameter at the distal 1/3 of the forearm, free from stenosis, and ≥15cm in length, a patent dominant radial artery, ≥2mm in diameter at the distal 1/3 of the forearm, free from stenosis and major calcifications, and a patent ulnar artery, free from stenosis and major calcifications. Digital pressure is >50mmHg when occlusive compression is made on the radial artery and digital/brachial ratio is >0.5. The patient is not under guardianship.

The patient is a 77-year-old woman who has been a member of the PROOF cohort for the past 10 years. She has not undergone any surgery or aesthetic treatments in the past, and she does not have any neurological disorders. She has a history of non-insulin dependent type 2 diabetes, which is managed with metformin. She is not currently taking any corticosteroids or retinoids. The patient reports that she has noticed changes in her skin over the years, including increased dryness and wrinkles. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the aging process of her skin and how it can be managed. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to undergo the various skin evaluations as part of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She complains of postpartum pelvic girdle pain that started during pregnancy and has persisted for several weeks after delivery. The pain is localized in the sacral region and is aggravated by physical activities such as walking or bending. She rates the intensity of her pain as 6 out of 10 on a visual analogue scale. The patient has no history of nerve root affection in the lumbo-sacral spine, inflammatory disease with pelvic bone and/or spinal manifestation, endometriosis, gynecologic cancer or ongoing malign disease, previous surgery of the lumbar spine or incapacity to complete the questionnaires. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of low level laser therapy and pelvic stabilization exercises on postpartum pelvic girdle pain. She understands that the study involves 12 sessions over six week's period by 2 sessions per week and that she will be randomly assigned to one of the three groups: low-level laser therapy and pelvic stabilization exercises, low-level laser therapy only, or pelvic stabilization exercises only. She is willing to provide informed consent and undergo all necessary assessments and treatments.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory loss and confusion for the past year. She has difficulty remembering names and faces, and often forgets where she put things. She has a family history of Alzheimer's disease, as her mother also suffered from the condition. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, and takes medication for both conditions. She has never smoked, but drinks alcohol occasionally. She is currently under the care of a neurologist and has been diagnosed with dementia.

A 58-year-old male with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. He has been taking antihypertensive medications for the last 7 years but has not achieved adequate blood pressure control. He has a family history of hypertension, but no history of diabetes, heart disease, or renal disease. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28. He complains of occasional headaches and dizziness. His current blood pressure readings at the clinic are consistently above 150/90 mmHg despite being on three different antihypertensive medications. He has undergone a 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, which revealed an average systolic blood pressure of 142 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 87 mmHg. The patient has two main renal arteries, with diameters of 4.2 mm and 4.5 mm and lengths of 25.0 mm and 27.0 mm, respectively. The patient is willing to undergo all study procedures and provide written informed consent.

A 26-year-old male patient presents with a history of hearing voices and seeing things that others do not. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 years and they have been progressively worsening. He reports feeling paranoid and anxious most of the time. His family has also noticed that he has been neglecting his personal hygiene and daily routines. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has been diagnosed with schizophrenia by a psychiatrist and has been referred to UMC Utrecht for participation in a clinical trial investigating changes in brain activation patterns in patients with schizophrenia before and after treatment. He has not received any neuroleptic medication for at least 2 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to perform a working memory task, a language task, and a motor task while lying in the scanner. He understands the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his cancer has progressed despite these treatments. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He is willing to provide written consent for the clinical trial and has archival tumor tissue available for retrospective biomarker analysis. He has not received any prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (anti-CTLA-4) antibody, or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or immune checkpoint pathways. He meets the inclusion criteria for the expansion cohort, with histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of stage IV NSCLC with high (> 50%) PD-L1 tumor expression as determined by immunohistochemistry (IHC) without epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) sensitizing (activating) mutation or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) translocation. He has not had any prior malignancy active within the previous 2 years except for locally curable cancers that have been apparently cured, such as basal or squamous cell skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix or breast, or localized prostate cancer. He has a neutrophil count of ≥ 1000/μL, platelets of ≥ 75,000/μL, hemoglobin of ≥ 9.0 g/dL, creatinine of ≤ 1.5×upper limit of normal (ULN), AST of ≤ 2.5×ULN (Except with liver metastasis, AST ≤ 5×ULN), ALT of ≤ 2.5×ULN (Except with liver metastasis, AST ≤ 5×ULN), and bilirubin of ≤ 1.5×ULN (except patients with Gilbert's syndrome, who must have total bilirubin < 3.0 mg/dL). He does not have any active or suspected autoimmune disease or a documented history of autoimmune disease, or history of a syndrome that required systemic steroids or immunosuppressive medications, except for patients with vitiligo or resolved childhood asthma/atopy. He has not received live, attenuated vaccine within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP and does not have any other condition that may increase the risk associated with study participation or may interfere with the interpretation of study results.

A 35-year-old HIV+ male patient with a CD4 count of 250 cells/mm3 and no significant medical history is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. He has been taking antiretroviral medications (zidovudine, zalcitabine, stavudine, and lamivudine) for the past 6 months without any change in dosing. He has no history of drug allergies or drug hypersensitivity. He denies any current or past history of intravenous drug abuse, alcohol, or substance abuse. He is currently not taking any macrolide antibiotics, azole antifungals, cimetidine, rifampin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, protease inhibitors or non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor compounds. He has not received any investigational drugs or antineoplastic agents within the past 12 weeks. The patient is informed that he will be receiving clarithromycin orally for 32 days and nevirapine orally for 28 days. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and provides informed consent to participate.

A 40-year-old male of African American descent presents with a history of fever, nasal congestion, pressure, and facial pain for the past week. He has no prior history of sinusitis. The symptoms have not responded to over-the-counter (OTC) medications. He denies any allergies, persistent cough, or chest pain. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril daily. His vital signs are stable, and his physical examination reveals tenderness over the maxillary sinuses bilaterally. No nasal polyps are noted. Laboratory analysis is within normal limits. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the sinuses reveals evidence of acute bacterial sinusitis. The patient weighs 80 kg and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He agrees to adhere to the dose and visit schedules and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 29 year-old male who has been experiencing psychotic symptoms for the past 3 years. He reports hearing voices that tell him to harm himself and others. He also has paranoid thoughts that people are watching him and plotting against him. He has been diagnosed with schizophrenia by a psychiatrist and has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past year. He has a history of marijuana and alcohol use, but has been abstinent for the past 6 months. He has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. He is able to understand the nature and consequences of the trial and is willing to participate. He is not currently pregnant or lactating.

A 65-year-old man who is generally healthy and active. He enjoys spending time with his grandchildren and traveling with his wife. He has never received the influenza vaccine before, but he is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of influenza virus vaccine. He has provided written informed consent and is available for the duration of the trial. He is not a resident of a nursing home or long-term care facility, does not have any signs of renal insufficiency, and does not have any pre-existing disease that requires a change in therapy or hospitalization within 12 weeks before receiving the study vaccination. He does not have any known or suspected diseases of the immune system or receive immunosuppressive therapy. He has no history of hypersensitivity to egg or egg protein or any other component of the vaccine. He has not received any live virus vaccine within one month prior to vaccination or expected to receive another live virus vaccine within one month of vaccination in this study. He has not received any influenza vaccine in the 6 months prior to enrollment or intends to receive a non-study influenza vaccine after enrollment. He is excited to potentially contribute to the development of a new influenza vaccine.

Karen is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe hip pain that has significantly impacted her quality of life. She is scheduled to undergo elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). Karen has no known allergies to local anesthetics or chlorhexidine. Her weight is 70 kg. Karen has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and osteoarthritis. She takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. She has no known allergies to opioids. She has no history of substance abuse but intermittently drinks alcohol socially. Karen is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the difference in postoperative opioid consumption when subjects receive a quadratus lumborum (QL) or lumbar plexus (LP) block preoperatively for THA. She has been educated on the role of regional anesthesia in postoperative analgesia and will consider the study until the day of surgery. If she chooses to participate, she will be enrolled on the day of surgery in the preoperative holding area. After discussion regarding risks and benefits of both the lumbar plexus and QL block, Karen will be consented if she chooses to participate.

Patient is a 30-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new drug called ASC41. She has no history of thyroid disease or intolerance to beta blockers and her thyroid function indicators are within normal range. She has never fainted or experienced fainting during blood draws. She has no history of liver disease and her liver function tests (ALT, ASL, and direct bilirubin) are within normal range. Her Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), Hepatitis C virus antibody (HCV Ab), HIV antibody (HIV Ab) and syphilis antibody tests are negative. She has not taken any special diets or consumed alcohol in the past 2 weeks. She is a non-smoker and does not consume caffeine or xanthine-containing foods or drinks. She has not donated blood or lost more than 400ml of blood in the past 3 months. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period and for one month after the end of the study. Her fasting low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is between 110mg/dl and 190mg/dL during the screening period. She voluntarily signs the informed consent and is interested in participating in the ASC41 clinical trial.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who has been experiencing recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) over the past year. She has been treated with antibiotics multiple times, but the infections keep coming back. Her urologist has recommended a cystoscopy to investigate further. The patient is nervous about the procedure and is concerned about experiencing pain during the procedure. She has no history of chronic pain and is not currently taking any medication for pain. This will be her first cystoscopy and she has not undergone any other interventions concurrently. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to potentially reduce any pain or discomfort during the procedure.

Patient is a 21-year-old male from the United States who is currently enrolled as an undergraduate student at a local university. He reports experiencing occasional stress and anxiety related to academic and social pressures. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to promote mental health in university students through brief and cost-effective interventions teaching emotion regulation techniques.

67-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presents to the cardiology clinic for evaluation of a slow heart rate. He reports feeling fatigued and short of breath with minimal exertion. He denies chest pain, syncope, or palpitations. His medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. His physical exam is notable for a heart rate of 40 beats per minute with regular rhythm and a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. His lung exam is clear and there is no peripheral edema. An electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals sinus bradycardia with first-degree atrioventricular block. An echocardiogram demonstrates preserved left ventricular function with an ejection fraction of 50%. The patient is referred for a dual-chamber pacemaker implantation due to symptomatic bradycardia. He meets the inclusion criteria for the Optimize RV study, as he is expected to be paced in the right ventricle greater than 90% of the time and has an ejection fraction greater than 40%. He is a candidate for a dual-chamber pacemaker and will be implanted with a market released dual chamber Medtronic pacemaker and 3830 SelectSecure Lead in the ventricle. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old man presents to the hospital for a scheduled surgery for a herniated disc in his lumbar spine. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Physical examination reveals a well-nourished individual with normal vital signs and no significant findings in the neurological exam. Preoperative laboratory values including CBC, electrolyte, liver function tests, and coagulation profile are within normal limits. Anesthesia is induced and a tracheal intubation is performed with the use of a neuromuscular blocking agent. Acceleromyography is used to monitor the neuromuscular blockade throughout the surgery. The patient is randomized to the study group and double burst stimulation is applied. The interval between the moment when DBSs are visually identical and the T4/T1 ratio is > 0.9 is recorded. The patient is monitored until an optimal recovery is achieved. The data collected will contribute to the calculation of the optimal recovery time for 95% of patients.

A 42-year-old male presented to the dermatology clinic with complaints of red, scaly patches on his elbows, knees, and scalp. The patient reported that the patches have been present for the past 6 months and are accompanied by itching and burning sensation. He had previously used topical corticosteroids and moisturizers with no significant improvement. The patient has a past medical history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years, which is controlled with metformin 1000mg twice daily. He has no history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or cardiovascular disease. His family history is significant for his mother having psoriasis. On physical examination, there were erythematous plaques with silvery scales on his elbows, knees, scalp, and sacral region, with the largest plaque measuring 5 cm in diameter. The rest of the physical examination was unremarkable. The patient was diagnosed with psoriasis vulgaris and started on topical calcipotriol and betamethasone dipropionate ointment. The patient was referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating the correlation between glucose transporter type 1 (GLUT1) expression and psoriasis with type 2 diabetes. The patient met the inclusion criteria and agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing for several weeks. He has a history of smoking for over 20 years and consumes alcohol regularly. Upon medical evaluation, he was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. The cancer is potentially resectable and does not involve malignant celiac nodes or cervical esophageal carcinoma. The patient has no other significant medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 1. His blood work reveals an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. His bilirubin level and AST are both within normal limits. His creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL and his creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min. He has not undergone any prior chemotherapy or thoracic radiotherapy for esophageal cancer. The patient understands and agrees to the use of effective contraception during and for at least 3 months after the study, as he is fertile.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, which is being treated with antiviral therapy. He was recently diagnosed with a liver tumor, which was confirmed to be hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by American Association for Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) guidelines. His Childs-Pugh score is A and he has no clinically significant portal hypertension. The tumor is measurable according to the standard Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. The patient has never received chemotherapy or immunotherapy, and has no history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to nivolumab or yttrium-90 (Y-90). He has a performance status of 1 and his organ and bone marrow functions are adequate. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of other primary malignancies within 2 years. He has no history of autoimmune disease, toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), or Stevens-Johnson syndrome. He has not received live vaccines within 28 days of registration. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is not a prisoner or involuntarily incarcerated. He is willing and able to provide informed consent prior to registration on the study.

52-year-old male veteran who lives in a rural area in Iowa, and receives primary care from the Iowa City VAMC or Coralville Clinic. He has been smoking cigarettes on a daily basis for over 30 years and is willing to make a quit attempt in the next 30 days. He reports having experienced depressive symptoms and concerns about weight gain in the past, which have made it difficult for him to quit smoking. He has access to a telephone (land line or cell phone) and has a stable residence. He is willing to participate in the study and is capable of providing informed consent. He does not have any terminal illness or unstable psychiatric disorder.

A 70-year-old Hispanic man who lives alone and has been recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, but they are well-controlled with medications. He is retired and receives social security benefits. He has limited access to transportation and struggles with reading and understanding medical information. He has never been screened for cancer before and is apprehensive about discussing it with his doctor. He has no family history of cancer. He is interested in participating in a program that will help him become more knowledgeable about cancer prevention and screening and make him a more effective participant in his health care.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and numbness in her right hand and wrist for several months. She works as a computer programmer and spends most of her day typing and using a mouse. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers but has found little relief. She has no known allergies and is in overall good health. She is not currently taking any medications. She has a family history of diabetes, but she has not been diagnosed with the condition. She is able to give informed consent and speaks English fluently. She has never had carpal tunnel surgery before.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with brown irises and no history of ocular disease. She wears contact lenses occasionally, but is willing to discontinue use during treatment visits. She is in good health and able to comply with all protocol mandated procedures and attend all scheduled office visits. The patient is willing to give written informed consent to participate in this study. Her medical records show no clinically significant systemic diseases, ocular infections or inflammation, or recent ocular trauma or surgery. She has never been diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy or any condition affecting the pupil or iris. She has no known allergies or contraindications to any components of the mydriatic agents or the vehicle formulation. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, planning a pregnancy, or using any form of birth control. She has a resting heart rate and blood pressure within normal range.

A 30-year-old male with a history of opioid use disorder has had several overdoses in the past year. He has expressed a desire to stop using opioids but has been unsuccessful in maintaining sobriety without assistance. He has no other underlying medical conditions and is willing to participate in a study to help with his addiction. He speaks English fluently and is willing to sign an informed consent form. He is not currently physiologically dependent on alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other drugs of abuse that require immediate medical attention. He has no known sensitivity to buprenorphine or naloxone.

The patient is a 45 year-old office worker who spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She reports that she doesn't have time or motivation to engage in physical activity after work due to various personal and professional commitments. She has tried to incorporate more physical activity into her daily routine, but has found it difficult to achieve. She has a BMI of 28, indicating that she is overweight, and has a history of hypertension. She does not have any known contraindications to moderate-intensity physical activity. She is interested in participating in a research study on sedentary behavior reduction and is willing to make changes to her lifestyle to become more physically active.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. She has skin phototype IV and is willing to perform a minimum of 8 finger sticks and 8 optical measurements per day for 30 days in her home. She is able to understand and read English and has no conditions that would interfere with the accuracy of the interstitial glucose measurements, such as extensive skin changes or tattoos on the probe application site. She is not currently undergoing dialysis treatment and is not receiving glucocorticoids or other medication/topical agents that increase photosensitivity. She is willing to provide written, signed, and dated informed consent and is not currently enrolled in any other study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with congenital hemophilia A and has inhibitors to coagulation factors VIII. He has been experiencing frequent bleeds requiring haemostatic drug treatment for the past year. The patient has a history of joint pain, swelling, and stiffness due to repeated bleeds in his ankles, knees, and elbows. He reports difficulty in performing daily activities such as walking, standing, and even simple tasks like buttoning a shirt. The patient is married and has two children, and works as a computer programmer. He is seeking a better treatment option that can help him manage his condition and reduce the frequency and severity of bleeds. The patient is generally in good health, with no history of arterial thrombotic events or deep venous thrombosis. He is compliant with his current medication regimen and is looking forward to participating in the trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of congenital hemophilia A with inhibitors.

A 38-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of ALS (less than 2 years). The patient reports experiencing progressive weakness, muscle atrophy, and fasciculations. He has difficulty speaking and swallowing, but his breathing remains normal. He is currently taking Riluzole (Rilutek) with minimal improvement. The patient has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, and no other systemic illnesses. His FVC is greater than 40% and his ALS-FRS score is 28. He has not received any corticosteroids, Ig, or other immunosuppressive treatments in the past year. He is willing to undergo bone marrow aspiration and intraventricular injection of mesenchymal stem cells as part of the clinical trial. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 52-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, cough, and fever. He tested positive for COVID-19 (SARS-CoV2) and was diagnosed with acute hypoxemic respiratory illness. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient was initially placed on oxygen therapy, but his respiratory distress continued to worsen over the next several hours. He was transferred to the ICU and intubated for mechanical ventilation. After several days on a ventilator, the patient's condition began to improve, and he was extubated. He was transferred to the ward and is currently receiving oxygen via a nasal cannula. The doctor presents the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of intravenous L-citrulline to delay and potentially prevent the need for invasive mechanical ventilation for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) illness. The patient is interested in participating and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

Patient is a 32-year-old male from the United States who has been smoking since he was a teenager. He smokes "every day" and has smoked over 100 lifetime cigarettes. He is currently looking for ways to quit smoking and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of pictorial warning labels on cigarette packages. He is a US resident and has never had a history of not smoking cigarettes.

A 32-year old female diagnosed with schizophrenia presents with a history of delusions of control over her thoughts and actions. She reports experiencing the feeling of being controlled by external forces and having her thoughts and actions influenced by others. She also reports hearing voices that tell her what to do and feeling compelled to follow their instructions. She is currently taking risperidone and reports that her symptoms have improved, but she still experiences occasional episodes of delusions of control. The patient lives with her parents and is currently not employed. She completed high school and some college courses but has not been able to complete a degree due to her illness. She denies any history of substance abuse or other medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 38-year old woman was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 6 years ago. She experiences severe spasticity in her lower extremities, which has not been well controlled with oral baclofen. She has tried various doses and combinations of oral baclofen, but has not been able to achieve adequate relief from her spasticity. She is also experiencing intolerable side effects from oral baclofen. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher, but has had to take a leave of absence due to her spasticity. She is otherwise healthy and has no allergies to medications or materials used in the Prometra Programmable Pump System. She is willing to undergo the implantation of the pump and is able to comply with all study requirements. She has had a successful trial of Lioresal® for the management of her spasticity. She does not have any contraindications for the use of Lioresal®. She has not had any systemic infections or renal insufficiency. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using effective birth control. She is not participating in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease and angioplasty. He has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. His cardiologist has recommended further testing to evaluate his myocardial perfusion and perfusion reserve using non-invasive imaging methods. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided informed consent. He has no history of claustrophobia or contraindications for MRI. He has normal kidney function and is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study. The patient has agreed to refrain from consuming caffeine for at least 12 hours prior to each study.

A 55-year-old woman presents with partial edentulism, requiring removable denture prosthesis. She has been missing her lower left molar for the past 6 months, which has resulted in difficulty in chewing and speaking. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She has no known allergies. She has had prior denture experience and is willing to participate in the study. Her dental examination shows that she has lost teeth number 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, and 23. Her oral hygiene is good, and there is no evidence of oral diseases such as periodontitis or caries. The remaining teeth are in good condition, and the occlusal plane is stable. The maxillary and mandibular arches are well-formed with adequate ridge height and width. There are no maxillofacial defects. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 57-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of chest pain that occurs after walking for a few blocks or climbing stairs. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, high cholesterol, and he is a smoker. His ECG showed signs of ischemia and his stress test was positive for inducible ischemia. He was diagnosed with chronic stable angina pectoris and was prescribed a beta-blocker and a calcium-channel blocker. Despite the medication, his symptoms persist. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication that may help relieve his chest pain.

45-year-old HIV-positive woman with a history of ARV medication for more than 1 year, with demonstrated HIV RNA <50 copies/ml for a period of 1 year. The patient reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating. The patient is willing to utilize 2 effective contraception methods and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Laboratory parameters are within normal limits. HIV DNA within peripheral blood mononuclear cells is >100 copies/mL. The patient has not received Maraviroc as part of ARV regimen. The patient does not have any history of seizure disorder, myocardial infarction, angina, congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, angioplasty, or cardiac surgery. The patient does not have any other chronic illnesses including diabetes, autoimmune diseases, and endocrinopathies. The patient is not currently receiving immunomodulator, HIV vaccine, or investigational therapy. The patient is not currently undergoing acute therapy for other AIDS-defining illness or other serious medical illnesses. The

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). He underwent surgery to remove as much of the tumor as possible, but residual tumor was still present. The patient is scheduled to undergo standard fractionated radiation therapy and temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy. He has a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80, indicating that he is able to carry out normal activities with some effort. The patient has no history of renal or psychiatric conditions, and is not allergic to any compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to FMISO. He is willing to undergo MRI and PET scans using FMISO to assess tumor hypoxia. The patient has no implanted medical devices or metallic objects in his body and his weight is less than 350 lbs. He has no history of sickle cell disease or chemotherapy or radiotherapy sources such as wafers of polifeprosan 20 with carmustine. The patient is able to provide written informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

57 year old male with a solid pancreatic lesion detected on CT scan during routine surveillance for chronic pancreatitis. The lesion is suspicious for malignancy and a biopsy is indicated. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He has a family history of pancreatic cancer in his father who was diagnosed at the age of 68. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent.

Pt is a 10yo M with a history of congenital heart disease and AV valve regurgitation. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activity. An echocardiogram was performed within the last 6 months and noted audible AV valve regurgitation on clinical exam. The patient is scheduled to undergo a clinically indicated CMR study and is able to hold still within the scanner for imaging. There are no contraindications to the CMR scan. The patient does not have a common AV valve or corresponding semilunar valve regurgitation that would preclude use of stroke volume comparison as a second means of assessing AVV regurgitation by CMR.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She was diagnosed with severe preeclampsia prior to delivery and was closely monitored by her healthcare provider during her pregnancy. She had elevated blood pressure and protein in her urine, but she did not develop any of the severe features associated with the disease. She delivered a healthy baby via cesarean section at 37 weeks gestation. Her blood pressure has normalized since delivery, but she is still at risk for complications related to preeclampsia in the postpartum period. She is eligible to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of low-dose aspirin in improving endothelial function and reducing the severity of preeclampsia in the postpartum period. She will be randomized to either receive low-dose aspirin (81mg) or placebo to take daily for up to 3 weeks post-delivery. She will be closely monitored by her healthcare provider and will undergo flow-mediated dilation (FMD) testing to assess her endothelial function. She must not have any contraindications to taking aspirin, such as a history of gastric or duodenal ulcers, bleeding disorders or diathesis.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy with a history of hemophilia A. He has had multiple episodes of bleeding in his knees, elbows, and ankles, which have resulted in frequent emergency department visits. He has been receiving on-demand or low-dose prophylaxis with human coagulate factor or recombinant factor VIII. He has not developed any inhibitors and has no family history of inhibitors. He has regular clinical visits and accessible data. His parents are willing to provide informed consent for his enrollment in the study. The patient is currently attending kindergarten and enjoys playing with his friends. He is active and enjoys outdoor activities. He has no other bleeding disorders or systemic disorders. His physical exam is unremarkable except for some joint swelling and tenderness in his knees and elbows.

A 55-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis in her left knee for the past 5 years presents with complaints of moderate pain in her left knee. She reports difficulty walking and performing activities of daily living due to the pain. She has no history of upper gastrointestinal tract ulceration or inflammatory joint disease. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She has no significant hepatic or renal disease. She has not taken any NSAIDs in the past 2 weeks. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old premenopausal woman with a new diagnosis of non-metastatic (stage II) estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. She is scheduled to start chemotherapy with dd-AC-T regimen. She works as a teacher and is concerned about how the treatment will affect her appearance, especially hair loss and skin changes. She has no history of alopecia or scalp disorders and is not currently taking any medications that could affect her hair. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study.

A 26-year-old female with a BMI of 23 kg/sq m comes to the Clinic as a potential participant in the study. She has no history of tobacco use, diabetes or uremia, and is not a vegetarian. She exercises 2-3 times a week for an hour. She confirms that she is not taking any dietary supplements other than those given in the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Her laboratory results show normal liver function, CBC, and thyroid values. She reports no history of gastrointestinal diseases or soy or garlic allergies. She is willing to maintain her normal exercise and activity patterns and avoid cruciferous vegetables and garlic and related foods for one week before and two weeks during the study for a total of three weeks. She is given a detailed explanation of the study and agrees to participate.

A 25-year-old woman who is generally healthy and interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has no previous cardiac disease or history of atrial fibrillation. She is able to provide written informed consent prior to the study procedure.

28-year-old pregnant woman at 25 weeks of gestation with a history of allergic rhinitis and eczema. Her father has a history of asthma and her older sibling has a history of food allergy. She has no known allergies to soy or fish and is not currently taking any anti-coagulation medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effects of omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LCPUFA) supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on the development of allergic disease in her child. She has not been taking any commercial omega-3 supplements at this time.

A 35-year-old woman presents with blurry vision, headache, and redness in both eyes. She has no significant medical history and denies any chronic illnesses. The patient reports no recent ocular trauma or surgeries, and she is not currently taking any medications or health care products. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist observed bilateral serous retinal detachment, which was confirmed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA). The patient was diagnosed with acute VKH disease and was referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating immune profile changes during the course of treatment. The patient is willing to participate in the study, and her blood sample will be collected to observe major immune cells' number, functional and membrane molecular changes. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial as she is within the age range of 18 to 50 years old and has no history of severe cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, allergies to steroids or contrast agents, ocular trauma or surgeries within the past 3 months, vaccination, infectious or hereditary diseases, immune system correlation, neuroendocrine, and digestive system diseases. The patient also reports no heavy alcohol or tobacco addiction.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who is a former smoker with a 30-pack year history. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) associated with chronic bronchitis. He has a productive cough on most days for a minimum of three months per year for at least two successive years. His current medications include albuterol and tiotropium inhalers. His post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) is 45% predicted and his post-bronchodilator FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio is 65%. He has no lactose intolerance and is not currently on any medication that may interfere with the study procedures or evaluation. He has never taken astemizole, cisapride, pimozide, or terfenadine, nor is he currently taking an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who recently suffered a fall resulting in an acute osteoporotic vertebral fracture. He reports experiencing significant low back pain and difficulty moving around. The pain is a constant ache that is exacerbated with movement or changes in position. The patient has no history of spinal surgery or other major spinal conditions. X-rays confirm the presence of an acute vertebral fracture. The patient is not currently taking any medications for osteoporosis or other related conditions.

The patient is a 46-year-old male who underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallstones. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and occasional episodes of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). He smokes half a pack of cigarettes a day and drinks alcohol socially. He woke up in the post-anesthesia care unit with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. His blood pressure is 90/50 mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. He is feeling anxious and is unable to take deep breaths due to pain. He is currently receiving oxygen via a nasal cannula at 4 liters per minute and his pain is being managed with intravenous morphine. The patient appears to be confused and disoriented. The nursing staff is concerned about his low blood pressure and hypoxemia and decides to perform a point-of-care ultrasound to assess his cardiac function and lung status.

The patient is a 16-year-old overweight adolescent girl with irregular menstrual cycles. She has been experiencing hirsutism (excessive hair growth), acne, and weight gain for the past year. She is not diabetic and has no history of liver disease. She is not taking any medication that affects insulin sensitivity. Her BMI is above the 90th percentile for her age and gender. She is not currently engaging in more than 3 hours of moderate exercise per week. She has been menstruating for the past 3 years. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is negative for any metabolic disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating liver and fat regulation in overweight adolescent girls.

The patient is a 42-year-old Hispanic man diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and asthma. He has been managing his conditions with medication and regular check-ups. He has a family history of leukemia, with his mother being diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia. He has experienced fatigue, bruising, and recurrent infections over the past few weeks, leading to his diagnosis. His bone marrow biopsy confirmed the presence of abnormal promyelocytes, and a karyotype analysis showed the t(15;17) translocation. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he is over 15 years old and has acute promyelocytic leukemia with PML/RAR alfa.

A 70-year-old woman who lives independently but has been experiencing difficulty with standing balance, walking speed, and chair-rise time, will be a suitable candidate for this clinical trial. She has a score between 4 and 10 on the Short Physical Performance Battery. She is mentally alert with a score of 28 on the Folstein mini-mental status exam. She is able to climb stairs independently. She has no unstable acute or chronic disease or any neuromusculoskeletal impairment interfering with independent stair climbing. She has no history of abdominal aortic aneurysm or exertional angina or symptomatic valvular heart disease. She is willing to provide informed consent and is ready to meet three times per week for 30-60 minutes per session at a research exercise gym for 16 weeks. She will be under the direct supervision of research staff.

The patient is a 55 year old male of Asian descent who has a history of hypercholesterolemia. He has been on a lipid-lowering drug treatment for the past 6 months and has not experienced any significant side effects. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has a BMI of 30. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. His most recent LDL-C level was found to be above the target range according to the Third Joint European Task Force guidelines, despite being on medication. He is interested in participating in the Pan-European Survey on the Under Treatment of Hypercholesterolemia to help improve the management of his condition and to contribute to the research on this topic.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman with a history of autoimmune disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis and lupus. She was diagnosed with warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (WAIHA) six months ago and has failed treatment with corticosteroids and rituximab. Her current hemoglobin level is 8 g/dL, and she experiences fatigue and shortness of breath with minimal activity. Her direct antiglobulin test (Coombs) is positive for IgG and C3. She has evidence of active hemolysis with an elevated lactate dehydrogenase level and low haptoglobin level. She has a total IgG level of 800 mg/dL. She has no history of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for WAIHA.

50 year-old male with a history of inoperable locally advanced gastric cancer, who has been experiencing upper abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting and fatigue for the last few months. A CT scan revealed the presence of a large gastric tumor with metastasis to the liver, and a biopsy confirmed the adenocarcinoma diagnosis. The patient has not received any previous chemotherapy for advanced/metastatic disease. Upon further testing, it was found that the patient's tumor is HER2-positive. The patient has no history of cardiac disease or dyspnoea at rest, and is able to perform daily activities without oxygen therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for HER2-positive advanced gastric cancer.

The patient is a 42-year-old Chinese man with a history of high myopia. He has been wearing glasses since he was 10 years old and has an equivalent spherical of -8D. He has no history of ocular surgery or laser treatment. His best corrected visual acuity is 6/9 in both eyes. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his time in front of a computer screen. He has no family history of glaucoma and does not have any other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in a long-term study to investigate the natural course of myopic optic neuropathy in high myopia population in China.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with cervical cancer. She has undergone surgery and chemotherapy but there is still evidence of disease on imaging studies. She is scheduled to receive 6 weeks of chemoradiation therapy. Her WHO performance status is 1 and she has no history of myocardial infarction or hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol. She has not developed any significant peripheral neuropathy. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials to explore more treatment options and improve her chances of survival.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was recently admitted to the hospital with a psychotic episode. He has a history of methamphetamine use and tested positive for the drug on admission. He is experiencing delusions and hallucinations that are causing him distress and interfering with his daily activities. He has no prior history of primary psychotic disorders or use of antipsychotic medication. He does not have any chronic medical conditions and is generally healthy. He works as a construction worker and lives with his girlfriend. He does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

Patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis for the last 5 years. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her joints, especially in her knees and hands, which has been affecting her daily activities and quality of life. The patient has tried various pain medications in the past, including acetaminophen and ibuprofen, but they have not provided sufficient relief. She has no known allergies to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and has not experienced any adverse reactions to them in the past. The patient does not have any active peptic ulceration, severe hepatic failure, or severe renal insufficiency, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in this study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Mobic® intramuscular injection for the management of her osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

63-year-old female diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the left knee presented to the clinic with complaints of pain, stiffness and limited range of motion. She reports that the pain has been present for the last 6 months and has been worsening over time. She has tried physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) without significant relief. She denies any history of knee trauma, surgery or infection. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and osteoporosis. She is an ex-smoker and has a family history of osteoarthritis. On physical examination, there is tenderness on the medial and lateral joint lines and crepitus with movement. She has a range of motion of 0-110 degrees with pain at the end of range. X-rays show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 osteoarthritis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effects of hyaluronic acid injection and platelet-rich plasma injection on her knee pain and function. She is able to provide informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old female with a history of Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has undergone previous cycles of chemotherapy, which caused severe nausea and vomiting, leading to discontinuation of treatment. She is scheduled to receive a new chemotherapy regimen that includes cisplatin, but is concerned about experiencing similar side effects. She has a Karnofsky score of 80 and a predicted life expectancy of more than 6 months. She has not undergone stem cell rescue therapy.

A 30-year-old healthy male presents with no significant medical history. He is physically fit and exercises regularly. He has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is sexually active with his female partner and uses condoms as his preferred method of contraception. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. He has not undergone cholecystectomy or surgery of the gastrointestinal tract. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test how BI 730357 is processed by the body. He has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

52-year-old male who sustained a traumatic brain injury due to a motor vehicle accident. He has a history of depression and anxiety, and is currently on medication for both. The patient has difficulty with short-term memory and executive functioning, as well as difficulty with verbal communication. He is able to speak English fluently and is interested in participating in the study to help improve his perceived self-efficacy in coping with his brain injury.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of smoking for the last 25 years. He has been experiencing difficulty in swallowing food for the last 6 months, along with chest pain and weight loss of 15 pounds. He has visited a general practitioner who referred him to a gastroenterologist. An endoscopy was performed, which revealed a tumor in the esophagus, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. He has no significant past medical history, and his family history is unremarkable. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. Imaging studies have shown that his cancer is unresectable and has metastasized to the lymph nodes. He has not received any previous systemic treatment for his cancer. His liver function tests and renal function tests are within normal limits. His blood counts are also normal. He is willing to provide archival or fresh tissues for PD-L1 expression analysis. He is not currently taking any Chinese traditional medicines with anti-cancer indications or immunomodulators. He is not on any immunosuppressants. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of sintilimab or placebo with chemotherapy as first-line treatment in subjects with unresectable, locally advanced recurrent or metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been diagnosed with early proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) in his right eye, with no vitreous hemorrhage observed. His best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in the study eye is greater than 20/400. He is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures. He has not received any prior systemic anti-VEGF or IVT anti-VEGF treatment in the study eye. His SD-OCT central subfield thickness measurement is less than or equal to 320 µm in the study eye. He does not have evidence of infectious ocular infection at the time of screening, and has no history of vitreoretinal surgery or prior panretinal laser photocoagulation in the study eye. The patient has no current vitreous hemorrhage obscuring retinal imaging in the study eye. He has not undergone cataract surgery in the study eye within 4 weeks of Day 0. His blood pressure is well-controlled and stable at < 180/110 mm Hg systolic/diastolic. He has no significant renal disease and has not been treated with corticosteroids (intravitreal or peribulbar) in the study eye within 12 weeks of screening. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is a sexually active man who is willing to practice adequate contraception during the study.

We are looking for participants to enroll in a clinical trial studying the inflammatory and mitochondrial responses in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) of healthy controls, heavy drinkers, and patients with alcoholic hepatitis. We are looking for individuals who meet the following criteria: healthy controls without liver disease, heavy drinkers who have been consuming alcohol for a minimum of 6 months with an average of >40 g/day or >280g/week for women and >60 g/day or >420 g/week for men, and patients with alcoholic hepatitis diagnosed by imaging, biochemical values or liver biopsy with a drinking history. Participants must be willing and able to sign informed consent, and cannot have cancer or autoimmune diseases that may confound study data. Control subjects (drinking and non-drinking) must have INR levels <1.4 and total bilirubin levels <3, with no prior history of known alcoholic liver disease or hepatosplenomegaly. If you meet these criteria and are interested in contributing to the study of alcoholic hepatitis, please consider participating in our clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with Acute Myelogenous Leukemia (AML) secondary to myelodysplastic syndrome. He has received several rounds of chemotherapy, but the disease has relapsed. His Eastern Oncology Cooperative Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and he is expected to complete at least 4 weeks of therapy. He has no history of heart disease or diabetes, and his total cholesterol level is within normal limits. His white blood cell count is 60,000/mm3 (60x10*9/L) at baseline. He is currently not on any other medications. He is married and has two children, aged 12 and 15. He works as a sales representative at a pharmaceutical company and enjoys playing golf on weekends. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his AML.

A 45 year old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes for 7 years has developed a non-healing wound on her left foot. She has no previous history of foot ulcers or amputation. She reports occasional numbness in her feet but denies any pain. Her most recent A1c result from 4 months ago was 8.5%. She has not had any major surgeries in the past year and is not currently on any medications that would impact wound healing. She has no psychiatric disorders, cancer, or HIV. Her pulses are present on palpation and she has no pallor on elevation. She has no trophic skin changes and her ankle brachial index is 0.9. The wound is located on the forefoot and is less than 1 inch in diameter with a pink wound bed. She is interested in participating in a study to determine the most efficient and cost-effective way to heal her diabetic foot ulcer.

A 35-year-old man diagnosed with moderate-to-severe psoriasis and is starting methotrexate treatment for the first time. He has no history of chronic alcohol abuse and is not allergic to methotrexate. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo FibroScan and FibroSURE™ testing. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the effects of food additives on phosphorus metabolism. He is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and exercises regularly. He has no family history of kidney disease or any other significant medical condition. He has a BMI of 24, and his urinalysis is normal. His blood work shows normal levels of phosphorus, calcium, and hemoglobin. He is not taking any medications or supplements that may affect phosphorus metabolism. He is willing to follow a specific diet during the study period and is committed to attending all study visits.

A 13-year-old male patient accompanied by his mother presented to the orthodontic department with a chief complaint of protruding upper front teeth. He had no history of previous orthodontic treatment. Medical history revealed no systemic disease or growth disorder. The patient was in the active growth period with a normal or mildly prognathic maxilla and retrognathic mandible. The initial cephalometric analysis showed a Class II skeletal pattern with an increased overjet of 7 mm and a retruded mandible. The patient had a horizontal to average growth pattern and a positive pretreatment visual treatment objective. The dental arches had minimum crowding, and no permanent teeth had been extracted. The patient was eligible for the study and gave informed consent.

The patient is a 50 year old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for 10 years. He has HbA1c levels above 7% and is under treatment with oral hypoglycemic agents. He has a history of smoking for 10 years but quit 2 years ago. He occasionally drinks alcohol. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has a BMI of 30 and his blood pressure is within normal range. He has a history of periodontitis with generalized moderate to severe chronic periodontitis affecting his gum and teeth health. He has at least 10 permanent teeth. He is a registered LLU patient and follows good oral health habits. His oral health habits include daily brushing and flossing, and regular dental check-ups. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) as adjunctive therapy to Scaling and Root-planing in the management of Periodontitis in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.

A 55-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of fatigue, bone pain, and weight loss. He has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma after a bone marrow biopsy. He had received initial treatment with combination chemotherapy but had a partial response. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial of combination immunotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation for myeloma. He has measurable disease and has not received prior autotransplant or allogeneic transplant. His ECOG performance status is 1 due to bone pain. His laboratory studies showed normal liver function tests, negative HIV or HTLV-1/2 serology, and no evidence of active bacterial, viral, or fungal infections. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has given written informed consent. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally.

Maria is a 35-year-old laboratory technician who has been experiencing pain in her neck and shoulders for the past 6 months. She rates her pain as 6 out of 10 on the pain scale and experiences it at least 4 days a week. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but has not found significant relief. Maria has no history of any serious illness or pregnancy. She is otherwise healthy, but does not engage in regular physical exercise due to her demanding work schedule. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effect of physical exercise at the workplace on her musculoskeletal pain.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain upon exertion for the past six months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and does not have diabetes. A stress test has revealed evidence of ischemia, and a subsequent angiogram has shown a chronic total occlusion in a major coronary artery. The patient has been advised to undergo revascularization and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing bioresorbable vascular scaffolds to stents in this setting. His physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable except for mild obesity (BMI 31 kg/m2) and a blood pressure of 140/80 mmHg.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms for the past year. He reports waking up several times during the night to urinate and has difficulty starting the stream. He denies any pain or hematuria. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His prostate-specific antigen level is within normal limits. He has no history of prostate or bladder cancer. His prostate size measured by transrectal ultrasound is 120 mL. He is mentally capable and willing to sign a study-specific consent form. He is available to attend all required visits and follow study instructions. He meets all inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian woman who has been actively trying to conceive for the past 6 months without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle, typically lasting 28 days, and uses no form of contraception. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and exercises regularly. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is negative for any reproductive disorders. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the impact of lifestyle factors on reproductive aging.
