She is willing to travel to Oklahoma City to participate and undergo a transvaginal ultrasound exam and skin autofluorescence measurement. She has no prior ovarian surgery or any ovarian pathology. She is willing to provide informed consent and complete a structured interview to obtain information regarding oral contraceptive, ethanol, tobacco use, and socioeconomic status. She is excited about the potential to improve our understanding of female reproductive aging and to help develop better models for assessing and predicting reproductive lifespan.

Pt is an 80yo M admitted to a geriatric service with suspected coronary heart disease. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He presented to the emergency department with chest pain, which resolved with nitroglycerin. ECG showed sinus rhythm with nonspecific ST-T wave changes. Troponin levels were within normal limits. He is currently on aspirin and metformin. He has no history of coronary artery disease or previous cardiac interventions. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 60-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of bilateral knee pain, stiffness and difficulty in walking. She had been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis in both knees and had undergone conservative treatment for a year with no significant improvement. She was advised to undergo total knee replacement for her left knee, which was causing more discomfort. She was referred to this study to evaluate the effect of intra-articular injection of Diprospan into her right knee, which was planned for surgery after a few months. She had no history of allergies or active infection and was not pregnant. She was willing to participate in the study and randomized to the intervention group, receiving 2ml Diprospan diluted in 10 ml Bupivocaine injection into her right knee.

A 35-year-old woman visited the clinic, complaining about her chocolate cravings. She has a history of binge-eating chocolate, especially during stressful periods. She is generally healthy, with no underlying medical conditions. She is married and has two children. She does not smoke, drink or use any psychoactive drugs. She is currently on a low-calorie diet and exercises regularly. Her BMI is 23.5 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in the study to reduce her chocolate cravings and improve her overall well-being.

The patient is a 8-year-old boy who attends a government school. He has no previous history of dental caries and has never received any dental sealants. During his last dental check-up, deep pits and fissures were observed on his lower permanent first molars. The patient is in good health and has no known allergies. He has no developmental anomalies and his teeth are not hypoplastic. The patient and his parents have given consent for him to participate in a clinical trial comparing the retention and caries preventive effect of glass-ionomer fissure sealant and resin-based fissure sealant. The patient will be randomly assigned to receive one type of sealant on each side of his lower permanent first molars. The patient will be recalled for sealant retention and caries prevention assessments at intervals of 3, 6 and 12 months.

42 yo F with a history of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) with nasal polyps, worsening symptoms despite maximal medical therapy, and scheduled for functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism, both well-controlled with medications. No history of chronic pain or opioid use in the past two weeks. No history of seizures or alcohol/drug abuse. No known allergies to acetaminophen. No history of end-stage renal or liver disease. She has no history of depression or anxiety. She is scheduled for a 3-hour FESS procedure involving at least 3 sinuses. She has been advised of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with mantle cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma 3 years ago. He has received standard chemotherapy but has experienced a relapse of the disease. He presents to the clinic with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in his neck, chest, and groin. He has no history of HIV or CNS involvement by lymphoma. His medical history includes hypertension, which is being managed with medication. He takes daily vitamins and supplements but is not currently taking any other medications. His lab results show a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, white blood cell count of 8.0 x 10^9/L, and platelet count of 150 x 10^9/L. His creatinine level is within normal limits, and his total bilirubin level is slightly elevated at 1.8 mg/dL. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 70% and is willing to use birth control if of reproductive potential. He has not received any investigational drugs in the last 3 weeks and has frozen tumor tissue available from his last prior therapy for analysis.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with fever and chills. Blood cultures revealed methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia. He has no significant past medical history, but he suffers from hypertension and is taking lisinopril daily. He has no known allergies. He is a candidate for the SAFO trial, a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of cloxacillin and fosfomycin combination with cloxacillin monotherapy in patients with MSSA bacteremia. The patient will be randomized to one of the two groups: standard treatment group, receiving intravenous cloxacillin 2g/4h for the duration of 7 days IV treatment, or combination therapy group, receiving intravenous cloxacillin 2g/4h and fosfomycin 3 g/6h for the duration of 7 days treatment. After the first week, the antibiotic treatment and duration will be decided by the responsible clinician. The primary endpoint is the treatment success measured at day 7 of treatment. The patient will be monitored for up to 12 weeks after randomization to evaluate the treatment success at Test of Cure visit (TOC). The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the SAFO trial and is willing to participate.

A 20 year old Japanese female student who is sexually active has come to the clinic for a routine Pap smear. She is concerned about the risk of cervical cancer and wants to take a vaccine to prevent it. She has had only one sexual partner and is using condoms as a form of contraception. She has no history of abnormal PAP smear or biopsy showing CIN. She has never had genital warts or tested positive for HPV. She is generally healthy and has not received any immunosuppressive medications or blood products in the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of quadrivalent HPV vaccine.

A 7-year-old male child weighing 20 kg presented with fever, chills, and vomiting for the past 3 days. The patient was diagnosed with P. falciparum malaria with a parasitemia of 12,000 parasites/microL on initial blood smear. The child's parent/guardian have provided written informed consent for participation in a Phase II clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of 2 intravenous artesunate dosing regimens in children with severe P. falciparum malaria. The child will be hospitalized for at least 4 days and will be randomized to receive either artesunate 2.4 mg/kg initially and at 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours or artesunate 4.0 mg/kg initially and at 24 and 48 hours. The study will also evaluate the pharmacokinetic profile of artesunate in pediatric patients. The child is eligible for the study and will be monitored for efficacy and safety throughout the study.

This is a 35 year old female with PMH of anxiety and depression who presents to the psychiatric day hospital for treatment. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety, including racing thoughts and palpitations. She has been on medication for anxiety and depression for several years, but has had difficulty managing her symptoms. She is able to perform a coloring and answer a questionnaire without severe deterioration of her general condition, according to the investigator's assessment. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate. She has not had any recent hospitalizations and is generally in good health.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has struggled with obesity for many years. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 42 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed with insulin resistance, with a fasting serum insulin level of 70 pmol/L. He has been stable in weight for the past 6 months, with a fluctuation of +/- 3 kg. He takes medication for hypertension and has no other significant medical history. He has been advised to undergo bariatric surgery, specifically the bilio-pancreatic diversion (BPD) procedure, and has consented to participate in this study. He exercises moderately 2-3 times a week, does not have a history of drug addiction or alcohol use, and has not donated blood in the past 12 weeks. The patient will be required to provide informed consent and is aware that the study aims to identify plasma proteins or peptides that may be involved in the restoration of insulin sensitivity after BPD surgery.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. She has been taking amlodipine for the past year to control her blood pressure. Her BP readings at the clinic have been consistently above 120 mmHg systolic. She has no history of congestive heart failure or myocardial infarction. She has no evidence of proteinuria or nephrotic syndrome. Her BMI is 29. She has no evidence of liver or kidney dysfunction. She is not taking any hormonal contraceptives and is not pregnant. She has not participated in any clinical trial involving investigational products in the past 3 months. She is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 30.5 kg/m2 who has been struggling with weight loss for several years. She has no significant medical history, but she has tried multiple weight loss interventions including diet and exercise with little success. She is interested in the Endoscopic Vertical Gastroplasty or Fogel Gastroplasty (FG) procedure as a potential solution. She is willing to participate in the study and attend all follow-up appointments. The patient has no previous history of gastrointestinal tumors, gastric cancer, bariatric surgery, or any other exclusion criteria. She is generally in good health and has no significant esophageal or gastric issues that would preclude her from the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the rectum. The cancer is at the T3 stage and has not spread to other parts of the body. The patient has not received any prior treatment for this cancer. Laboratory results show that the patient's hematological condition is normal with neutrophils ≥ 1500 G / L and platelets ≥ 100 000 G / L. The patient's lactatemia is within the higher standard of the sampling laboratory. The patient is otherwise in good health with a performance status (WHO) of 1. The patient is not diabetic and has not received any antidiabetic treatment in the past. The patient is not hypersensitive to capecitabine or to any of the excipients or to fluorouracil. The patient does not have any history of severe and unexpected reactions to a fluoropyrimidine therapy. The patient does not have a known deficiency to the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD). The patient is not hypersensitive to metformin or to any of the excipients. The patient does not have renal failure or impaired renal function with creatinine clearance < 60 ml / min. The patient does not have any severe infection or acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia such as heart or respiratory failure or recent myocardial infarction (< 6 months). The patient does not have hepatocellular insufficiency, acute alcohol intoxication, or alcoholism. The patient is mentally competent to give consent. The patient is not under tutorship or guardianship. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 45-year-old male patient admitted to the ICU following a motor vehicle accident with multiple fractures and severe pain requiring opioid-based analgesia. The patient has not had a bowel movement in the past 72 hours despite other interventions to manage opioid-induced constipation. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal issues or surgeries within the last 8 weeks. The patient is expected to stay in the ICU for more than 3 days. The patient has no other contraindications for the use of methylnaltrexone. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

This is a 54 year-old male with end stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to polycystic kidney disease. He has been on hemodialysis for 3 years and has been awaiting a kidney transplant for the past year. He has no history of HIV, Hepatitis B or C, and has no clinically significant liver disease. His calculated pre-transplant reactive panel (cPRA) is 60% and his estimated post-transplant survival (EPTS) index is 70%. He has no living donor available and has been listed for a kidney transplant. He has been selected to participate in a clinical trial for the utilization of Hepatitis C positive kidneys in negative recipients. The trial requires him to take DAAs therapy post-transplant and agree to abstinence from alcohol for at least 6 months post-transplant. He has agreed to participate in the trial and is willing to receive a kidney from HCV positive donors with KDPI<85%. He understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 67-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer six months ago. He has been undergoing anti-androgen therapy for the past three months. His PSA level has remained stable for the past month. He presents with a loss of appetite and difficulty eating solid foods. He reports feeling bloated and constipated. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are currently well-controlled with medications. He denies any food allergies or significant gastrointestinal symptoms. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the trial. He has a performance status of 1 and is expected to live longer than 6 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with lung cancer and is scheduled for urgent thoracic surgery. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is currently well controlled with medication. He has no history of bleeding disorders. The patient is currently taking aspirin for prophylaxis of potential cardiovascular events. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient has been provided with a detailed explanation of the study and has provided informed consent to participate. He is willing to undergo blood tests and is expected to require platelet transfusion during or after the surgery. The patient is able to communicate effectively and is expected to be able to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 32-year-old female complaining of redness, itching, and discharge in her left eye for the past 3 days. She wears contact lenses and has stopped using them since the onset of symptoms. She denies any trauma or injury to her eye. The patient has no known systemic diseases and is otherwise healthy. She has no history of ocular surgery, corneal erosion, or immune compromise. She has not used any ocular or systemic medications for this condition. The patient is willing to comply with all treatment and follow-up/study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled for elective surgery for a hernia repair. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no family history of bleeding disorders or anaemia. During his pre-operative evaluation, his haemoglobin levels will be measured using both the standard central laboratory method and the non-invasive SpHb method. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 30-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) based on the results of molecular biology tests. He is a nonsmoker with no significant medical history. He is not taking any medications and has never been treated for tuberculosis before. His chest CT scan confirms the presence of pulmonary lesions. He has signed informed consent and agreed to follow-up. His kidney function and liver function tests are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has no history of cardiovascular diseases or active viral hepatitis. He is willing to take oral drugs and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the treatment and follow-up.

Patient A is a 63-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after presenting with chronic cough and shortness of breath. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NSCLC, and further imaging showed no evidence of metastases. She underwent curative-intent surgical resection of the lung primary, which included a lobectomy and systemic lobe-specific nodal sampling. Pathology revealed a close margin of 1 mm with no extracapsular extension and no nodal involvement. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history, no smoking history, and no significant family history of cancer. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially reduce the risk of recurrence and side effects from radiation therapy. She understands the investigational nature of the study and is willing to comply with all protocol requirements.

A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 7 years. Despite taking methotrexate for the past 6 months, her RA symptoms have not improved, and she experiences frequent joint pain, stiffness, and swelling. She has no history of other inflammatory arthritis or autoimmune diseases. She has never been diagnosed with tuberculosis, pro-thrombotic disorder, venous thrombosis, substance abuse, or serious psychiatric condition. She has never had any allergy or hypersensitivity to aspirin or non-steroidal cyclooxygenase inhibitors, or Staphylococcal protein A. She has no history or presence of malignancy, and her diabetes is well-controlled. She does not have any systemic autoimmune diseases other than RA, and her HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C antibody tests are negative. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has normal hepatic, renal, and hematologic function. She has not received any live vaccines within the past 5 weeks. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of PRTX-100 in combination with methotrexate to treat active rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is in otherwise good health and has no known coagulation disorders. The tumor is localized and is considered operable, and surgical treatment has been recommended by her medical team. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the use of a regular electric scalpel versus an argon plasma coagulation scalpel for the surgical treatment of her breast cancer. She has been fully informed about the study and has given her consent to participate.

A 5-year-old girl who was noted to have early onset breast development and pubic hair growth by her parents. She has also been experiencing an increase in height and has gained weight rapidly over the past year. Her bone age is advanced by 1 year compared to her chronological age. The patient has not been treated with any medication that would affect her hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The patient and her guardians have given written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who underwent coronary artery bypass surgery due to severe coronary artery disease. He was discharged from the hospital six days ago and is currently recovering at home. He reports feeling fatigued and experiencing occasional chest discomfort. He also reports having difficulty sleeping at night due to anxiety about his recovery. He has been taking his prescribed medications as directed, including aspirin, beta blockers, and statins. He has no history of stroke or other neurological deficits. The patient is scheduled for his first outpatient review six weeks after hospital discharge, as per current practice. The patient has been provided with a questionnaire to complete at home and bring to the appointment, which includes questions about any complications, unplanned hospital visits or admissions, and level of satisfaction with the current follow-up practice. The data collected from the questionnaire will be used to determine the postoperative mortality and morbidity rates in the 6-week interval between hospital discharge and the first planned specialist review after cardiac surgery, and to assess the level of patient satisfaction with current practice. The study aims to determine if six weeks is too long for the first outpatient review after cardiac surgery.

This is a 42-year-old woman who has been living with HIV for 8 years. She is a smoker and currently smokes 15 cigarettes per day. She has expressed a motivation to quit smoking within the next 6 months and has a score of 6 on the Abrams and Briener Readiness to Quit Ladder. She is currently receiving HIV treatment at a participating HIV clinic and is able to read and speak English. She does not have any current moderate or severe alcohol or substance use disorder, as established by the MINI drug and alcohol sections. She is not currently pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She has not had any allergic reactions or hypersensitivity to Varenicline in the past. She is not currently using any medication that would interfere with the protocol and does not have moderate to severe renal impairment. She does not have any unstable cardiovascular disease, dementia, or recent use of Varenicline in the past 3 months. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 24-year-old female has been experiencing excessive sweating in her underarms, hands, and feet. She has tried multiple over-the-counter antiperspirants and has even changed her diet to try and reduce the sweating, but nothing seems to work. She has never been diagnosed with any medical conditions related to the sweating. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to understand how patient characteristics affect the response to primary hyperhidrosis treatments. She is willing to have non-invasive measurements of her sweat production taken during clinic visits and is comfortable answering electronic and telephone surveys about her disease and treatment. She is able to provide informed consent for study participation. She has never received botulinum toxin injections, aluminum chloride, iontophoresis therapy, or oral systemic anticholinergics for her condition, and has not undergone surgical intervention, suction and curettage, microwave thermolysis, or ultrasound therapy for her condition prior to baseline gravimetrics.

A 45-year-old woman has been diagnosed with advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. She has a germline BRCA mutation and has previously been treated with PARP inhibitors for 4 months before disease progression. She is estrogen receptor positive and has progressed on prior endocrine therapy. She has a good performance status (ECOG 0-1) and an estimated life expectancy of at least 16 weeks. Her hemoglobin, absolute neutrophil count, and platelet count are within normal limits. She has no history of brain metastases, spinal cord compression, or symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease. She is not currently receiving any investigational agents and has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the past 3 weeks. She has no known allergies to compounds similar to olaparib, cediranib, or AZD6738. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study and has measurable disease that can be accurately measured at baseline. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using highly effective contraception.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was recently diagnosed with epilepsy. She experienced her first seizure six months ago and was seen at a hospital-based emergency department. She was referred to a specialized epilepsy team that will be participating in this study. She has been experiencing seizures at a frequency of 2-3 times per month. She has not had any changes in her antiepileptic drug treatments in the months preceding the neuropsychological and psychiatric evaluations. She is able to attend school and has no cognitive impairments. She has never been diagnosed with any psychiatric disorders. Her legal guardians have agreed to sign the written consent form and she is willing to participate in the study. The epilepsy team has diagnosed her with focal idiopathic (genetic) epilepsy.

The patient is a 10-month-old baby boy who was born prematurely at 32 weeks of gestation. He was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at 6 months of age due to his delayed motor development. His parents have noticed that he has difficulty sitting and reaching for toys. The baby is able to maintain head control and visually focus on objects for a few seconds. He has no major medical complications except for occasional reflux which is controlled with medication. The baby's family is committed to participating in the study and is willing to follow the intervention protocol for 3 months. They do not have any plans to move out of the local area within one year.

The patient is a 24-year-old nulliparous woman who is currently pregnant with a single fetus. She is in her 26th week of gestation and has been receiving prenatal care since the beginning of her pregnancy. She has no history of chronic medical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, or asthma bronchial. She is not HIV positive and has not experienced any bleeding or premature labor. The patient is not currently in psychotherapy and does not engage in any physical activity more than once a week. The patient has been approached to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a program for preparation of pregnant women for delivery. The program includes physical and educational activities that will be performed at each prenatal consultation and will also include orientation on exercises that can be done at home. The patient will be randomized into either the study group where she will participate in the program or the non-interventional group where she will follow the regular prenatal care routine offered at the service. The patient will be asked to sign an informed consent form before being allocated into the study group.

62 yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes presents to his primary care physician's office for a follow-up appointment. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. During the visit, he is prescribed a new medication for his hypertension. He reports that he sometimes forgets to take his medications, and he is concerned about the potential side effects of his new medication. He is primarily responsible for administering his own medications and has a mobile phone. He speaks fluent English and is interested in learning more about how to safely take his medications.

A 28-year-old male with a diagnosis of schizophrenia spectrum disorder is seeking treatment for his symptoms. He has been experiencing auditory hallucinations and delusions for the past 3 years, which have negatively impacted his ability to work and socialize. He has been hospitalized once in the past year due to worsening symptoms. The patient is able to read and write in Hebrew and has the ability to provide informed consent for the study. There are no co-morbid neurological conditions. The patient is interested in participating in the Metacognitive Reflection and Insight Therapy (MERIT) study to improve his metacognitive abilities and increase his sense of agency and meaning in life.

45-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a current diagnosis of pneumonia. He was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after respiratory distress and received mechanical ventilation support for more than 24 hours. The patient is able to communicate using non-verbal approaches such as paper and pencil. He has no history of dementia or psychiatric illness, nor has he experienced drug or alcohol intoxication/overdose or withdrawal. The patient does not have severe or uncorrected hearing impairment and is not in a coma status after cardiac arrest or hypothermia treatment. He is not expected to die within the next 24 hours and has no history of delirium during this admission. The attending physician and healthcare team have approved and agreed to the patient's participation in the study.

32F with recent travel history to Singapore developed fever (37.9°C) with headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia and rash on the second day. She was diagnosed with dengue fever and confirmed positive for NS1 strip assay. She is otherwise healthy with no known comorbidities. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide written informed consent. She is able and willing to be an inpatient from Study Screening to Study Day 5 and to return to hospital on study Days 14 and 28. She is also willing to keep a study diary from Study Day 5 to Day 14. She has no signs of severe dengue and meets all inclusion criteria. She is not pregnant and is willing to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 65 days after the last dose of study drug.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who is currently experiencing symptoms of heart failure, specifically shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his lower extremities. He has been sedentary for the past few months, with structured exercise occurring less than twice a week. He has a history of hypertension and has been treated for it for the past two years. He also has a history of smoking but quit five years ago. He has no family history of cardiovascular disease. His recent echocardiogram showed preserved systolic function with LVEF > 50% but diastolic dysfunction with E/é > 15. He has been clinically stable for six weeks and optimized on his medical treatment. He is willing to participate in a study that aims to assess the optimal exercise intervention to improve peak oxygen uptake and diastolic function in patients with HFpEF. The patient has never participated in any clinical trials before and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy Muslim male who lives in Bangkok, Thailand. He follows his religious duties and fasts during the ninth month of Islamic lunar calendar called Ramadan. He maintains a healthy lifestyle and has no known metabolic-related diseases. He does not smoke or drink alcohol and does not take any medication or dietary supplements. He is interested in his health and is willing to participate in a study to determine the effect of Ramadan fasting on body composition, metabolic profile, serum leptin and adiponectin levels. He is aware that his dietary intake and physical activity will be recorded during Ramadan in a food record booklet. He is willing to provide fasting blood samples at the beginning and end of the fasting period for metabolic profile measurement. He is willing to undergo anthropometry and body composition measurements to assess his weight, BMI, and percent body fat mass. He understands that his participation in this study will contribute to understanding the effect of Ramadan fasting on metabolic health in healthy men.

A 38-year-old woman presents to Ataturk University Hospital for a scheduled cesarean section at 39 weeks of gestational age. Her pregnancy was uncomplicated, and prenatal ultrasounds did not reveal any congenital anomalies. She has no significant past medical history and denies smoking, alcohol, or drug use. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she feels well. The cesarean section is performed without any complications, and a healthy male newborn is delivered. The newborn is ≥34 weeks of gestational age and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The mother consents to participate in the study, and the newborn is enrolled for screening of critical congenital heart disease and to establish normal values of oxygen saturation and perfusion index at high altitude.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has a history of diabetes and has undergone a recent surgery to remove a tumor from his abdomen. The wound from the surgery is approximately 6 inches long and is located on his lower abdomen, just above the pubic bone. The wound is difficult to close due to the patient's excess body fat and loose skin. The patient is cooperative and willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 32 year old female with a history of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and recurrent GI infections. She has been experiencing frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloating. She has been on several medications for IBD including mesalamine, prednisone, and azathioprine. She has no history of adverse reactions to fluorescein, ICG, dextran or PEG. She has not taken antibiotics within the previous four weeks. She is able to give informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to help improve our understanding of leaky gut and develop better treatments for IBD.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman in her 39th week of gestation. She has no significant medical history and is currently experiencing a healthy pregnancy. The patient has been selected to participate in a clinical trial that compares the use of ultrasound to traditional palpation techniques for identifying a specific area of the neck. This will involve a non-invasive examination of the neck using ultrasound technology. The study aims to determine which method is more reliable and easier to perform in pregnant women at term. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study.

This is a 9-year-old male living in Burkina Faso who presents with symptoms of fever and chills. Upon examination, he is found to have a confirmed monospecific infection by P. falciparum with a parasitaemia between 2000-200,000/μl. He has a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dl and is able to take oral medication. The child's parents are willing to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study and have provided their consent for participation. The child has not previously received complete antimalarial treatment with an ACT within the last two weeks and has no history of hypersensitivity to any of the drugs being tested. The child has not participated in a malaria vaccine clinical trial before.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IVb head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) six months ago. He underwent definitive chemo-radiotherapy (CRT) and has no evidence of disease (NED) on clinical and radiographic examinations. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work, such as light housework or office work. The patient has no prior history of treatment with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-targeted small molecules, EGFR-targeted antibodies, or any investigational agents for HNSCC. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack years, and his primary tumour site was his larynx. The patient has no known pre-existing interstitial lung disease (ILD). The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

32 yo M with a history of HIV-1 infection, currently on a stable HAART regimen for 12 weeks, presenting with a viral load of 340 copies/mL. The patient reported some difficulty with adherence to his current regimen due to side effects, including nausea and vomiting, and expressed interest in simplifying his regimen. The patient has previously received etravirine and demonstrated sensitivity to the medication. The patient is willing to practice safe sex practices during the study period. The patient has not experienced any active AIDS-defining illnesses and has not taken any non-ARV investigational agents within the past 90 days. Liver function tests were within normal limits. The patient is interested in enrolling in the study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of etravirine in combination with other ARV agents.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with severe cough, fever, and shortness of breath. Upon examination, the patient was diagnosed with influenza A (H3N2) virus infection. The patient has a history of hypertension and has not received a pneumococcal vaccine. The patient is hospitalized due to the severity of his symptoms and complications arising from the influenza infection. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate major depressive disorder. He has been taking antidepressants for four weeks at therapeutic doses, but he still experiences symptoms of depression, including sadness, loss of interest in activities, and sleep disturbances. He has a history of hypertension, but his cardiovascular disease has been stable for the past 12 months. He has no history of neurological disease or seizures, and he has not been diagnosed with dementia. He is able to hear and follow verbal instructions and can sit comfortably for 45 minutes. He lives alone and has a history of social isolation. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs but consumes alcohol occasionally. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing intermittent toothache in her molar tooth for the past few weeks. She noticed sensitivity to hot and cold food and drinks that subsides after a few minutes. She has not sought dental treatment for this issue before. On clinical examination, there is deep decay in the molar tooth that is close to the pulp but the pulp is still vital. There is no swelling or sinus tract. The patient is cooperative and willing to participate in clinical trials. She has no history of systemic diseases or disabilities.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain for several months. He was diagnosed with tropical calcific pancreatitis (TCP) based on his symptoms and imaging tests showing pancreatic ductal dilatation and intra-ductal stones. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption but denies any current alcohol use. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He has been experiencing malabsorption and nutritional deficiencies due to his condition. He has been taking oral vitamin D3 supplements as recommended by his doctor but has not noticed any significant improvement in his vitamin D levels. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of high dose intramuscular (IM) vitamin D3 supplementation in normalizing his vitamin D levels. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with study requirements.

Mary is a 52 year old woman who was diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma six months ago. Despite receiving platinum based chemotherapy and a second-line chemotherapy, her cancer has continued to progress, leading to metastatic disease. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. Her recent CT scan confirms measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 criteria. She is willing to provide a newly obtained or archival tumor tissue sample. Her blood count, liver and renal functions are all within normal limits. She has no history of autoimmune disease or interstitial lung disease. She has not received any anticancer vaccine within the past 3 months and has not participated in another clinical trial within the past month. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate contraception during the course of the study and through 6 months after the last dose of study medication. She voluntarily agreed to participate by giving written informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman came to the Pain Clinic complaining of chronic abdominal pain for the past 4 months. She describes the pain as a constant, dull ache that is located in the lower right quadrant of her abdomen. The pain is worse with activity and is not associated with any specific food or drink. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not provided any relief. Upon examination, she has a positive Carnett's sign and an identifiable abdominal trigger point. She has no history of abdominal surgery or hernias. Her BMI is 27. She does not have any chronic psychotic disorder or dementing illness. She has no active abdominal visceral disease contributing to the pain.

A 6-year-old boy was diagnosed with HIV infection at birth. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years, including Zidovudine, Stavudine, Didanosine, and Lamivudine. He lives with his mother and three siblings. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. He enjoys playing with his siblings and attending school. His recent laboratory results showed a CD4 count of 650 cells/uL and an undetectable viral load. The patient's mother is willing to provide informed consent for her child's participation in the clinical trial. She is committed to ensuring her child receives the best possible care and treatment for his HIV infection. The patient has never experienced any adverse reactions to his current antiretroviral therapy.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient enrollment as it is a feasibility study for new MRI hardware and software for radiation therapy planning and assessment. Therefore, there are no specific patient descriptions required for this trial.

42-year-old male with a history of heavy alcohol use and smoking presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He was diagnosed with severe acute pancreatitis based on Ranson Criteria > 2, elevated CRP levels (>100 mg/L), and necrosis of the pancreas on CT scan. The patient has no known coagulation disorders and no skin infections in the vertebral region. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. The patient has never had a pancreatitis episode before and is concerned about his prognosis. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his clinical outcome.

A 69-year-old retired teacher presented to the clinic with a 2-year history of gradual memory decline. Her family has noticed that she is forgetting appointments, repeating herself, and misplacing items. She has also become less involved in social activities and seems withdrawn. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She has completed 16 years of education and scored 22 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) at screening. Her Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) score is 3. She is currently taking donepezil for Alzheimer's disease, which she has been on for the past 6 months. Her previous medical history is unremarkable. MRI of the brain shows evidence of mild to moderate atrophy.

32F, a social media enthusiast and a regular Facebook user, is a smoker who has been trying to quit smoking for the past 6 months without much success. She has a history of tobacco use for the past 10 years and has tried nicotine patches and gum in the past without much success. She is interested in participating in a study that would help her quit smoking through an online platform. She is a resident of the United States and has entered the UbiQUITous Facebook Application, confirming her smoker status. She is excited to be part of a study that could help her quit smoking and improve her health.

A 68-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of vision loss in her left eye. She reports that the vision loss has been gradual over the past few months and she is no longer able to read or watch TV with her left eye. She has a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in both eyes and has been receiving treatment for the past year. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist diagnoses her with geographic atrophy (GA) in her left eye. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of ANX007 in patients with GA secondary to AMD. Her GA lesion has well-demarcated borders and measures 5 mm2. Her best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 70 letters using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) charts. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a highly effective contraceptive method. She has not had any prior intravitreal treatment for AMD and has not had any surgical or laser intervention for the condition. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if ANX007 can slow down the growth rate of her GA lesion.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of vulvar cancer presents with concerns about her quality of life and unmet needs after treatment. She underwent surgery for vulvar cancer and received adjuvant therapy. She reports experiencing pain, discomfort, and difficulty with sexual function. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help assess her quality of life, treatment-related morbidity, unmet needs, and satisfaction with care after treatment for vulvar cancer. She is able to understand and complete the questionnaire and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 58-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction 11 days ago. He had a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction 7 years ago. The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and was discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel, beta-blockers, and statins. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metoprolol succinate. The patient has no history of heart failure, arrhythmia, or syncope. His ECG on admission showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. His peak troponin level was 12 ng/mL. His echocardiogram on day 5 after the infarction showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the IRIS trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in her left eye. She reports experiencing a gradual loss of central vision and distortion in that eye over the past several weeks. The patient has no significant past medical history and has not undergone any ocular surgeries or laser treatments. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in her left eye and 20/20 in her right eye. On examination, she has drusen and subretinal fluid in the macula of her left eye, and no abnormalities in her right eye. She is deemed an appropriate candidate for intravitreal injections of bevacizumab or ranibizumab to treat her wet AMD. The patient is willing and able to sign an informed consent and is able to return for scheduled follow-up visits. She does not have any other significant ocular or medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

A 20-year-old male college athlete who plays basketball and suffered a complete tear of his ACL during a game. He underwent primary ACL reconstruction surgery 6 months ago and has completed his physical therapy. He reports that his knee feels stable and he has been following his rehabilitation program religiously. He has been slowly increasing his activity level but is still hesitant to return to playing basketball at full capacity. His coach has been pressuring him to return to the team, but he wants to make sure he is fully recovered before doing so. He has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate his readiness to return to sports following ACL reconstruction.

A 25-year-old woman is seeking treatment for recurrent and severe menstrual pain that has been affecting her daily life for the past 2 years. She reports having regular menstrual cycles of 28-30 days and a menstrual period lasting for 5-6 days. The pain is located in the lower abdomen and radiates to her lower back and thighs. The pain is accompanied by nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fatigue. She reports missing school or work for 1-2 days every month due to the pain. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications such as ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but the pain relief is inadequate. She has no history of pregnancy, lactation, or delivery within the past year. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She has no history of liver, kidney, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, nervous, immune or blood system disorders. She is not currently taking any medications, and she has not participated in any clinical trials within the past month. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo treatment for 5 consecutive menstrual cycles.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy but still experiences significant pain. Her pain is described as burning, tingling and shooting in her tongue and jaw, and is rated at 7 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). She also reports that the pain interferes with her ability to eat, drink and speak. She has no previous history of opioid use and is currently not taking any pain medication. She has a history of hypothyroidism, which is well controlled with levothyroxine. She is currently not pregnant and uses contraception. She is able to read and fill in the questionnaires. She is willing to participate in the study to find a better pain management option.

A 55-year-old breast cancer survivor has completed the VOLUME study 6 months ago. She works as a school teacher and is married with two children. She experiences permanent/persistent chemotherapy-induced alopecia (CIA) after cancer treatment. Her hair diameter at 6th month after chemotherapy had not recovered to baseline level. She has tried a few anti-hair loss treatments but did not feel any improvement. She has never had hair transplants. She is physically and psychologically able to participate in the study. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to the components of CG428. She is willing to commit to the study treatment and follow the protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has suffered from bunions for several years. He experiences significant pain and discomfort when walking or standing for extended periods of time due to the condition. The patient has no prior history of opioid or non-opioid pain medication use, and is not currently taking any medication. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of peripheral vascular disease, diabetes, or hepatitis. The patient is able to take oral medication to assess opioid regimen postoperatively. He has a BMI of 30. The patient has provided signed and dated informed consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study. He meets the inclusion criteria for forefoot surgery, including bunionectomy +/- digital surgery. The patient is not currently taking prescription for SSRIs, gabapentin, duloxetine within 3 days of surgery, and has no known allergic reactions to components of the bupivacaine injectable or other amide anesthetics.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing constant tingling and numbness in her left hand for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome and her physician recommended an elective carpal tunnel release surgery. She has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medications. She works as a graphic designer and spends a lot of time typing on her computer. She has been experiencing difficulty in completing her work due to the persistent numbness and tingling in her hand. The surgery will be performed in an outpatient setting and she has consented to participate in the clinical trial. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to be randomized to either receive Bupivacaine or Lidocaine local anesthesia.

45 year-old male with no significant past medical history presents to the hospital with shortness of breath and a cough. He was tested positive for COVID-19 and has been admitted to the COVID-19 ward team. He is able to read and speak English and has access to his own functioning smartphone in the hospital room. He has no acute issues such as deep venous thrombosis or unstable fractures, and is not receiving more than 6 liters per minute of supplemental oxygen. He has no history of lung transplant or dementia. He is willing to participate in the study and follow instructions on how to safely self-prone position.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with non-squamous cell, non-small cell carcinoma of the lung. She has stage IV disease (includes M1a, M1b stages or recurrent disease) according to the 7th edition of the TNM classification system. She has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She has a Life Expectancy of greater than 12 weeks and an ECOG performance status 0 or 1 (Karnofsky > 70%). Her organ and marrow function are normal with an absolute neutrophil count >1,500/mcL, platelets > 100,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal institutional limits, AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) < 2.5 X institutional upper limit of normal, creatinine ≤ 1.5 X institutional upper limit of normal, and urine dipstick for proteinuria of < less than 1+. She has an INR < 1.5 and a PTT no greater than upper limits of normal within 1 week prior to randomization. She has no history of gross hemoptysis and is not receiving chronic daily treatment with aspirin or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents known to inhibit platelet function. She is not receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. She has not received any other investigational agents. She has no serious non-healing wound ulcer, or bone fracture, or major surgical procedure within 21 days prior to starting treatment. She has no uncontrolled brain metastasis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is HIV-negative. She agrees to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation. She has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who has been experiencing pain in his legs when walking for several months. He also has a history of smoking for 30 years and has recently quit. He has a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medication for these conditions. He has a BMI of 28 and is physically active, engaging in daily walks. He presented to the vascular medicine department with complaints of pain in his legs and foot ulcers. He underwent an endovascular revascularization procedure for Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease in the vascular medicine department in December 2015. He has been followed up regularly by the vascular medicine department since then. He speaks French fluently and has given consent for the use of his data for this research.

A 47-year-old man who is undergoing colectomy due to a diagnosis of colon cancer has been identified as a potential participant for this clinical trial. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication to manage it. He does not have any allergies to food or medication. He is able to give informed consent and understands the purpose of the clinical trial. His medical history shows that he has no other significant medical conditions.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic with persistent ankle pain due to a previous injury. He has a history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of infections, tumors, open fractures, burns, or varicose veins. His ankle pain has not responded to conservative management, and he is scheduled for ankle surgery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the use of tourniquets during surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a smoking history of 20 pack-years. He quit smoking 5 years ago. He has a history of seasonal allergies but no other significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) vaccine. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. He is not currently participating in any other clinical study and has not received any investigational or non-registered product within 30 days prior to the first dose of study vaccine. He has not received any vaccine containing NTHi-antigens in the past. His FEV1 is 85% of predicted normal value and he has no diagnosed respiratory disorder. He has no history of immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease, or malignancy within the previous 5 years. He is not pregnant or lactating, and is willing to practice adequate contraception during the entire treatment period and for 2 months after completion of the vaccination series.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with stomach cancer that has spread to his liver and lungs. He had experienced abdominal pain, bloating, and feeling full after eating a small amount of food for the past few months. He has lost 10 pounds in the last 3 months. On examination, his abdomen was distended and tender on palpation. Laboratory tests showed anemia, thrombocytosis, and elevated liver enzymes. CT scan revealed a large mass in the stomach with multiple metastases to the liver and lungs. The largest liver lesion was 5.5 cm in diameter. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. The patient received one cycle of chemotherapy with cisplatin and 5-FU with no response. He did not receive any prior topoisomerase I inhibitors. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1, and his Karnofsky score is 80%. His blood counts, renal function, and electrolyte levels are within normal limits. The patient has no history of seizures or psychiatric illness. He is not taking any medications except for over-the-counter antacids. He has no other malignancies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and does not have any pre-existing cystitis.

This is a 42 year-old female with a history of gallstones and recurrent biliary colic. She has been scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. She is otherwise healthy, with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no history of glaucoma. She has not used any sedative drugs in the past month and has an ASA physical status of I.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Friedreich's ataxia. He has been experiencing clumsiness and uncoordinated movements for the past 5 years. He also has a family history of the same condition. His body mass index is 22. He has not taken any dietary supplements or over-the-counter medications with an antioxidative effect within the last week. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or caffeine-containing beverages. He is willing to adhere to the protocol-defined schedule of assessments and procedures. He is informed of the nature of the study and has provided written informed consent before any study-specific procedures are performed. He does not have any clinically relevant medical or surgical condition that could interfere with the administration of study drug, interpretation of study results or compromise the safety or well-being of the subject. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to follow an acceptable method of birth control as determined by the Investigator, from the screening visit through 2 months after the last dose of study drug. He is able to swallow capsules whole. He has not participated in any investigational drug trial within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug on Day 1. He has an International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) mean total score of ≤75. His C-SSRS score is 2.

The patient is a 67-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory failure. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and was intubated for mechanical ventilation. He has been in the ICU for more than 48 hours and has developed a fever and purulent sputum. His chest x-ray is normal, but a CT scan is ordered to rule out pneumonia. The CT scan shows no evidence of pneumonia, but he is diagnosed with tracheobronchitis. He has leukocytosis and fever. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is a former smoker and quit 10 years ago. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He is randomized into the intervention group and receives 7 days of treatment with Piperacillin/Tazobactam.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently on inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting bronchodilators. She has also had multiple episodes of pneumonia in the past. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for pandemic influenza A (H1N1) vaccine for elderly and immunocompromised patients. She has never had an allergic reaction to the seasonal influenza vaccine in the past and has not received any other vaccines within the last two weeks. She is able to understand and provide informed consent for her participation in the study. The study team will ensure that her COPD is stable and that she does not have any acute infectious disease prior to vaccination.

A 57-year-old man with a previous history of urothelial carcinoma comes to the clinic complaining of abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. He had undergone surgery and chemotherapy but was found to have metastatic disease on follow-up imaging. He has failed first-line systemic treatment and was started on second-line therapy but did not respond. The patient has no other significant medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient's recent imaging showed progressive disease with measurable disease per the RECIST guidelines, Version 1.1. The patient has adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient's tumor has been evaluated and prospectively identified as having FGFR 1, 2, 3, or 4 genetic alterations. The patient has not received adequate prior treatment with a highly selective FGFR inhibitor. The patient has no other major uncontrolled medical conditions such as recent myocardial infarction, stroke, diabetes, or active hepatitis. The patient has not received prior systemic anticancer therapy ≤ 3 weeks prior to study start, and does not have a primary neoplasm of the brain or known uncontrolled metastases to the central nervous system (CNS).

A 70 year old woman came to the clinic complaining of persistent sadness, loss of appetite and lack of energy. She has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and is currently not taking any antidepressant medications. Her Hamilton Depression Scale score is 18. She has never been diagnosed with psychotic disorder or bipolar spectrum disorder. She does not have any neurocognitive disorder or cognitive disability. She has not had any history of substance use disorder and does not have any clinically implicable personality disorder. She has not experienced any brain injury and is not claustrophobic. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with diffusion tensor imaging and amyloid Positron Emission Tomography (PET) to evaluate the specific deposition in the brain. She will also undergo peripheral proteinomic evaluation with platelet BDNF level and other pro-inflammatory cytokines.

The patient is a 65-year-old American woman who is scheduled to undergo major non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia. She has a history of peripheral vascular disease and has been diagnosed with diabetes, which is currently being managed with oral anti-diabetic medication. Her eGFR is 25 m/min, indicating chronic renal failure. She has never received beta-blocker medication within the past 30 days and is considered beta-blocker naïve. She has an ASA risk status of III and a Revised Cardiac Risk Index score of 3, which puts her at high risk for perioperative cardiac adverse events. She has no history of stroke or heart failure, but has a heart rate of 60 bpm. She does not have second or third degree AV block without a pacemaker, and does not have active asthma or COPD. Her hemoglobin level is within normal limits at 11 g/dL. She has no known allergy to beta-blockade drugs. She is willing and able to provide consent for participation in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who sustained a burn injury to his left forearm while cooking at home. He presented to the emergency department within 2 hours of injury and was initially treated with topical ointments. On day 3 post-injury, the burn wound appeared to be healing but there was still uncertainty regarding the depth of the burn. The treating clinician decided to enroll the patient in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of laser Doppler imaging (LDI) in burn care. The patient meets the eligibility criteria as he has a burn of indeterminate depth and is being treated in one of the three Dutch burn centers. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient will be randomized into either the 'new diagnostic strategy' group, where LDI will be used to assist in the diagnosis and treatment decisions, or the 'current diagnostic strategy' group, where clinical assessment alone will be used. The patient's wound healing time, diagnostic and therapeutic decisions, and costs will be observed as part of the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with head and neck cancer. He is currently being treated at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, where he will undergo planned surgery to remove the tumor. The patient is interested in participating in a research study that collects and stores tissue, saliva, and blood samples to study cancer in the future. He understands that his participation in this study may help advance cancer research and improve future treatments for cancer patients. The patient is willing to provide tissue samples and undergo blood sample collection at baseline and every 2-6 months thereafter. He is also willing to contribute buccal swabs, mouthwash samples, and saliva samples as requested. The patient has no prior history of cancer and has no known cancer risk factors. He is in good overall health and has not undergone any concurrent therapy for his cancer. The patient is motivated to contribute to cancer research and hopes that his participation in this study will benefit future cancer patients.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of chronic back pain due to degenerative disc disease. He has been experiencing worsening symptoms over the past year, including numbness and tingling in his legs, difficulty walking, and weakness in his lower extremities. MRI showed significant spinal cord compression at the level of L4-L5. The patient has been scheduled for complex spine surgery to alleviate the compression and improve his symptoms. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of neurologic, hepatic or renal impairment, or cardiovascular disease. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve the safety of his anesthesia during surgery.

Looking for individuals aged 50-80 years old who have been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Participants must have an Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score between 18 and 28, and a Modified Hachinski Ischemia Scale (MHIS) score of ≤4. Participants must have a reliable study partner/informant who accompanies them to study visits and participates in assessments, and be willing to provide a blood sample for Apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotyping. Participants must not have a clinically relevant neurological disorder other than AD, a history of stroke or vascular dementia, or a history of multiple episodes of head trauma or serious infectious disease affecting the brain. Additionally, participants must not have an unstable psychiatric disorder, a recent or ongoing, uncontrolled, clinically significant medical condition, or a history of cancer. Participants must not have a relative contraindication to donepezil. Participants must have a negative urine drug screen (UDS) prior to randomization, and have not undergone neuropsychological testing or cognitive remediation in the past 4 weeks. Participants must not be investigational site or Sponsor staff directly involved with this study

A 30-year-old healthy woman visited the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for studying the immune response to the flu virus and comparing the immune cell responses to FDA-licensed flu vaccines. She has no history of allergies, asthma, or any chronic disease. She is willing to participate in the study for up to 5 years. She has not received any flu immunization in the past year and has only one prior season of flu immunization with IIV. She has no history of blood dyscrasias, renal disease, or hemoglobinopathies requiring regular medical follow up or hospitalization during the preceding year. She has not taken any influenza antiviral medication within 48 hours prior to the study vaccination. She is not pregnant and not breastfeeding. She has no history of Guillain-Barre syndrome. She is willing to complete the informed consent process and is available for follow-up for the planned duration of the study.

Patient A is a 50-year-old female who has been diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that has relapsed or is refractory following at least one multi-agent systemic treatment regimen. She has undergone previous chemotherapy but has not been treated with loncastuximab tesirine or R-GemOx. Her medical history includes high blood pressure, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis, and no evidence of active autoimmune disease or motor neuropathy of autoimmune origin. She has no evidence of CNS involvement of the lymphoma. Her most recent CT scan shows measurable disease. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has adequate organ function, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2000/μL, a platelet count of 100000/μL, ALT, AST, and GGT within normal limits, a total bilirubin of 0.8 × ULN, and a calculated creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min. She has negative beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) pregnancy test, and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during treatment. She has a formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue block available for testing. She meets all eligibility criteria and is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the efficacy of loncastuximab tesirine combined with rituximab compared to standard immunochemotherapy for her relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

The patient is a 14-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with skeletal Class II malocclusion due to mandibular deficiency. She has a moderate to severe overjet of 7 mm and complains of difficulty biting and chewing food. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has not had any previous orthodontic treatment. She has good oral hygiene habits and no clinical signs or symptoms of temporomandibular disorders. She is in the maturity stage of MP3-I, and all her permanent teeth have erupted except for the third molars. She is generally healthy, active, and enjoys playing basketball. She is willing to participate in the study and understand the requirements of the treatment.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic with concerns about her facial appearance. She had a history of a car accident 2 years ago that resulted in severe facial trauma, causing contour deformities on her face. In addition, she had developed hyper pigmentation over the deformities, which made them more noticeable. The patient had tried several de-pigmentary creams, but none of them had provided significant improvement. She was interested in exploring alternative treatment options and was excited to learn about the mesenchymal stem cell enriched adipose tissue grafting clinical trial. She met the eligibility criteria for the trial as she had contour deformities associated with pigmentary changes on her face and had not used any de-pigmentary creams for the past 3 months. The patient was hopeful that this novel approach would provide a reliable and long-term solution to her cosmetic concerns. She was willing to participate in the trial and undergo adipose tissue grafting with or without mesenchymal stem cells to improve her pigmentation and contour deformities.

Patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of opioid dependence who has been on methadone maintenance treatment for the past 6 months. He has a history of cocaine abuse and has been using it intermittently. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help him better understand his drug cravings and use patterns. He is willing to use handheld data-collection devices (electronic diaries) to report his drug use and moods in real-time. He understands that he will receive daily methadone and weekly drug counseling sessions that will continue throughout the study. He is willing to participate in a voucher-based program to encourage abstinence from heroin and cocaine. He is willing to carry a global positioning system (GPS) unit to record his locations during the study and complete questionnaires about his stress levels at specific intervals during the study. He understands that the study will last 28 weeks and that he will have the choice of transferring to a community clinic or undergoing an 8-week taper from methadone at the end of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with mild to moderate essential hypertension. She is currently taking one antihypertensive medication but is still experiencing elevated blood pressure with a trough mean sitting diastolic blood pressure of 95 mmHg and a systolic blood pressure of 145 mmHg. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the effects of aliskiren, an inhibitor of the renin-angiotensin system, on retinal vasculature. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she does not have any other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses adequate contraception. She lives with her husband and has two children. She is willing to attend all study visits as planned in the protocol and perform routinely self-home blood pressure measurements throughout

A 29-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester, expecting her first child, is concerned about the possibility of developing preeclampsia. She has no history of hypertension or diabetes and has never experienced preeclampsia in previous pregnancies. She has a BMI of 23 and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a family history of hypertension and cardiovascular diseases. She is otherwise healthy and excited about her pregnancy. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about her risk of developing preeclampsia and to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has a history of smoking for the past 40 years. He recently started experiencing persistent cough with blood in sputum and shortness of breath. His chest x-ray and CT scan showed a mass in the left lung with mediastinal lymph node involvement. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer Stage III. He has no other significant medical history and is currently not on any medications. He has a good performance status of 1 and is able to perform his daily activities without any difficulty. His blood tests showed adequate hematological parameters and his lung function reserve is acceptable for the trial. He has not received any previous chemotherapy and thoracic radiation for non-small cell lung cancer. The patient does not have any distant metastases. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is looking for new treatment options to improve his condition.

A 30-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history came to the clinic for the study. He works as a software engineer and has a BMI of 23. He has never smoked and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. His blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, and his laboratory results are within normal limits. He has no known allergies, and he understands the requirements of the study and has voluntarily consented to participate.

The patient is a 75 year old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and chest pain for the past few months. He was diagnosed with esophageal cancer at a local hospital and was referred to the clinical trial center for treatment options. He has never received any treatment for cancer before. He lives with his wife and adult son who provides him with support. He has a history of smoking and quit 10 years ago. He does not drink alcohol. He has a history of hypertension which is controlled with medication. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his family and gardening. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore more treatment options for his cancer.

The patient is a 15-year-old African American adolescent who is currently experiencing symptoms of depression, such as sadness, irritability, and a lack of interest in activities that used to bring them joy. The patient's parent(s) are also African American and have noticed these changes in their child's behavior. The family is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand how African American families identify and treat emotional and behavioral concerns associated with depression in their adolescent youth. The patient and their parent(s) have demonstrated the cognitive ability to understand participation and have provided consent and assent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing excessive worry and anxiety for the past 6 months. She has difficulty controlling her worry and it interferes with her daily activities.
