She reports feeling restless and on edge, and has difficulty falling asleep due to her constant worrying. She denies any history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders, and is in overall good health. At the screening visit, her HAM A score was 22, Covi Anxiety Scale total score was 12, and Raskin Depression Scale total score was 5. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her symptoms and be part of a research study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has recently received a reminder to attend cervical cancer screening. She is married and has two children. She works as a nurse and is interested in learning more about the HPV vaccine. She has never received the vaccine before and is willing to participate in the study questionnaire and receive the HPV vaccine if eligible. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is fluent in English and is willing to provide informed consent for both the study questionnaire and HPV vaccine administration.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension. She was diagnosed two years ago and has been on a stable regimen of medications for the past year. She has mild shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion, but is otherwise able to perform her daily activities. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new treatment option for PAH and has a 6-minute walk distance of 400 meters. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes. His diabetes was diagnosed 5 years ago, and he has been taking oral medications to control his blood sugar levels. He has a BMI of 40 and has struggled with weight loss despite various attempts at diet and exercise. He has a sedentary job and spends most of his free time watching TV or playing video games. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes, and his father passed away from complications related to the disease. He has well-controlled hypertension with a blood pressure of 130/80 and his HbA1C level is 7.5%. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if gastric bypass surgery can help him achieve remission of his diabetes. He is not currently on insulin, antidepressants, DPP-4 inhibitors or thyroid medication.

A 28 year old woman has a history of seasonal grass pollen-induced allergic rhinoconjunctivitis. She often experiences symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes during the grass pollen season. She has positive skin prick test (SPT) response with a wheal diameter of 4mm and positive specific IgE against Phleum pratense with an IgE titer of class 3. She has not received immunotherapy for grass pollen allergen or any other allergen within the previous 5 years. She is not affected by any other allergies or medical conditions. She is willing to comply with the treatment regimen and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a device that could potentially improve adherence to treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma two years ago. He underwent chemotherapy and achieved a complete remission. However, six months ago, he experienced a relapse and received salvage chemotherapy, which resulted in a partial remission. He is now experiencing a second relapse and is seeking additional treatment options. He has no major organ dysfunction or intercurrent disorder. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not pregnant or nursing.

This is a 72-year-old female diagnosed with probable Alzheimer's disease. She has been experiencing significant symptoms of agitation, including verbal aggression and physical outbursts, which have been difficult for her primary caregiver to manage at home. She is able to attend outpatient clinic visits with her caregiver. She has no medical conditions that would make her ineligible for study participation.

A 26-year-old woman arrived at the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a compound on mood and cognitive function. She has no history of psychiatric, medical, or neurological illness or substance abuse. She is currently healthy and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She has a Bachelor's degree in Psychology and works as a research assistant in a university laboratory. She is interested in learning more about the effects of different compounds on cognitive and emotional processes. She is a non-smoker, does not use illicit drugs, and occasionally drinks alcohol socially. She has no allergies to medications and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

67 year old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and mild-to-moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The patient has been experiencing blurry vision and noticed a cataract developing in his left eye. He is scheduled to undergo cataract surgery with implantation of a posterior chamber intraocular lens. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of ocular iontophoresis with dexamethasone phosphate ophthalmic solution compared to placebo. The patient is able to comply with all study-related instructions and is not using any topical ocular medication in either eye, other than tear substitute for dry eye.

55 year old woman who is cognitively normal and has a family history of Alzheimer's disease. She has no history of medical, psychiatric or neurological illnesses and is not currently taking benzodiazepines or sedating antihistamines. She has undergone genotyping and has been identified as an APOE e4 carrier. She has a score of at least 28 on the MMSE and a score of less than 10 points on the HAM-D-17. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the impact of lorazepam on cognition in APOE e4 carriers. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

N/A (As this is a feasibility study focused on measuring the evolution of operation time during the start-up phase of robotic-assisted surgery for the treatment of umbilical hernias, there is no need to generate a patient description for this trial.)

A 57-year-old male presents with rectal bleeding and change in bowel habits for the last 2 months. He has no significant past medical history and no family history of colorectal cancer. The colonoscopy revealed an ulcerated mass in the rectum, and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. CT scan showed no evidence of metastasis. The tumor is located 8cm from the anal verge, and an anterior resection is recommended. He is married with two children and works as a sales representative. He is physically active and has no significant comorbidities. He has never had surgery before and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore a new technique to facilitate the transection of the rectum during the laparoscopic anterior resection.

A 58-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic low-grade neuroendocrine tumors. She had a history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and flushing for several months, which prompted her to seek medical attention. Imaging studies revealed multiple liver lesions, confirming the diagnosis of metastatic neuroendocrine tumors. She underwent biopsy and was found to have a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her performance status is Karnofsky 90%, and she is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 3 months. Laboratory studies revealed normal renal and hepatic function, with a white blood cell count of 4,000/mm^3, absolute neutrophil count of 2,200/mm^3, and platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. She is not pregnant or nursing, and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing to use 2 forms of effective contraception during and 4 weeks before and after the study. She has no history of grade 2 or greater neuropathy, and no other clinical circumstances that would preclude study participation. She has not received prior thalidomide or interferon, and has not undergone concurrent chemotherapy or radiotherapy. She had one prior systemic therapy regimen more than 4 weeks ago. She qualifies for the study and may benefit from treatment with thalidomide.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 3 weeks. The pain is described as a dull ache that is present throughout the day and worsens with prolonged sitting or standing. The patient has not received any previous chiropractic or acupuncture treatment in the past month. The patient has no history of low back surgery, osteoporosis or spondylolisthesis. The patient is not taking any anticoagulant or systemic corticosteroid medication. The patient has no progressive unilateral lower limb muscle weakness or symptoms of cauda equina syndrome. The patient does not have any severe concurrent illness or known pregnancy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to find relief from his low back pain.

Patient B is a 50-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. She has never been treated for her HCV before and is seeking a new treatment option. She has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and occasional nausea. Her medical history is significant for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. She has not had any previous organ transplants or evidence of hepatic decompensation. She is willing to follow contraception requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in this clinical trial. Her screening laboratory values and physical exam are within acceptable ranges. Her HCV genotype is 1 and her HCV RNA is detectable. She is excited to potentially participate in a new treatment option and is willing to abide by the study restrictions.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who is scheduled for an elective surgery that requires general anesthesia. He is in good health with no history of respiratory disorders, lung surgery, or implants in his body. He has no facial or thoracic deformities and is not at risk for reflux or aspiration. He is not pregnant. He has a history of occasional smoking but does not currently smoke. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is an American Society of Anesthesiologist (ASA) physical class I. The patient is fully informed about the study and has given his consent to participate.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of competitive triathlon performance for the past 5 years. He has participated in at least four competitive triathlon events within the past 2 years and is currently in regular training for triathlon events. His personal best time for a standard ½ Ironman race is 5 hours and 45 minutes. He is experienced in using carbohydrate supplementation, such as gels, bars, and drinks, during training and racing. He has no known fructose intolerance or wheat intolerance, and he does not have any precluding food or packaging-related allergies. He has no chronic injuries that may affect his ability to complete the races. The patient is willing to participate in the study, complete all study requirements, and is available to compete in the ½ Ironman events. He has obtained his informed consent and is willing to take part in the familiarization sessions. The patient is not currently participating or has not participated in another clinical study during the last four weeks prior to the beginning of this study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who woke up this morning and noticed that he was having difficulty moving his right arm and leg. He also complained of difficulty speaking and understanding others. These symptoms have persisted for the past 3 hours. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking lisinopril and metformin. He has no known allergies. Upon arrival at the emergency department, he was noted to have a right facial droop, right arm and leg weakness, and difficulty with speech. His NIHSS score is 8. A head CT showed no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air.

A 52-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia who is currently undergoing chemotherapy. He is receiving antifungal prophylaxis due to chemotherapy-related immunosuppression. He has no known allergies to azole compounds and his liver function tests and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He is not receiving any medications that are contraindicated with the use of voriconazole.

A 40-year-old woman has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain for more than three months. The pain is present on both sides of her body and above and below the waist. The pain is described as a deep ache and is associated with tenderness in multiple areas. She also reports fatigue, sleep disturbances, and stiffness in the morning. The patient has tried various medications for fibromyalgia, but none have provided significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV squamous cell lung cancer three months ago. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but experienced a relapse with metastasis to his liver and lymph nodes. He underwent biopsy, and the results showed a positive cell cycle gene alteration. He is in good general health with no significant comorbidities. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable for any other abnormalities. He has no history of cardiac disease, hepatitis, or uncontrolled infection. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1. He is willing to use effective contraception as he is of reproductive potential. He is informed of the investigational nature of the study and has signed the written informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with HIV. He is from Southeast Asia and has a history of travel to rural areas. He has not started antiretroviral therapy yet and his CD4 count is 80 cells/mm3. He is currently asymptomatic and has not experienced any opportunistic infections. He works as a teacher and is married with two children. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. He has a history of hypertension and is taking medication to control it. His labs: FBS: 100 mg/dl, TG: 125 mg/dl, Cholesterol: 170 mg/dl, LDL: 85 mg/dl, HDL: 45 mg/dl. His cardiac assessment and joint ROM are normal. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to attend regular clinic visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 5 years. She has tried several treatments, including steroids and immunosuppressive drugs, but has not experienced any significant improvement in her symptoms. She experiences frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. She has lost weight and feels fatigued most of the time. She is currently not taking any medication for her condition. She has no history of neoplasm or hematological disease. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and she has no history of any cardiac or respiratory problem. Her BMI is 28 Kg/m2. She has no history of deep venous thrombosis, stroke or myocardial infarction. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced solid tumor. She has undergone several previous treatments, but her tumor has progressed. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the relative bioavailability of ARQ 197 tablet formulation with capsule C formulation as a reference. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and meets the eligibility criteria for adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient has not undergone any previous mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor (c-MET) inhibitor therapy. The patient is not pregnant and has a negative serum pregnancy test result. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits.

This is a 26-year-old male who was diagnosed with psychosis approximately 1 year ago. He has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past 6 months, which has helped to control his symptoms. However, he still experiences some delusions and hallucinations, which affect his ability to function well in daily life. He has a history of frequent cold sores on his lips, which he has been treating with over-the-counter medication. He is interested in participating in the Vancouver-Victoria Valacyclovir Trial for Early Psychosis, as he has been previously exposed to herpes type 1 and believes that his symptoms may be related to this virus. He is otherwise healthy, has no significant medical history, and is able to understand and communicate well with the study coordinator. He is willing to participate in cognitive testing and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl living in the 3rd arrondissement of Marseille, France. She has a body mass index of 34 and is considered medically obese. She lives with her mother and two younger siblings in a small apartment in a vulnerable neighborhood in Marseille. Her mother works long hours as a cleaning lady, leaving the patient responsible for taking care of her siblings and managing the household. She often eats fast food and snacks because it is easier and more convenient for her to prepare. The patient has expressed feelings of low self-esteem and has been bullied at school due to her weight. She has also experienced binge eating episodes, but has not received any medical care for it. She is currently not involved in any extracurricular activities and spends most of her free time watching TV or using her phone. Her EPICES score is 34, indicating social precariousness. She is interested in participating in the program to improve her health and self-esteem.

40 yo F with no significant past medical history, presenting to the ophthalmology clinic for a routine eye exam. Denies any problems with vision or eye discomfort. Patient has no known history of amblyopia, eye movement disorders or double vision. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Visual acuity with best correction is 20/20 in both eyes. She has no known allergies to medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the validity of input methods for Landolt Cs. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and has none of the exclusion criteria.

55 year-old male with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and an ejection fraction of 30%. The patient has been experiencing fatigue with minimal exertion and shortness of breath with activities of daily living. The patient is currently on maximal tolerated doses of evidence-based medical therapy for the past 6 months. The patient has no history of coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, or congenital or primary valvular heart disease. The patient has no evidence of persistent atrial fibrillation, chronic lung disease, advanced renal or liver disease. The patient is able to perform bicycle ergometry and has a functional capacity of NYHA class II. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of n-3 PUFAs on left ventricular systolic function in patients with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

The patient is a 46-year-old man who has been diagnosed with primary hemochromatosis, which is the most frequent hereditary condition in Scandinavia. He has been experiencing fatigue, joint pain, and abdominal pain, which are common symptoms of the condition. He has a homozygous C282Y mutation and has ferritin levels higher than 300 micrograms/L. He is eligible to participate in a controlled clinical trial that will compare erythrocyte apheresis and traditional phlebotomy as treatments for hemochromatosis. The trial will follow the decline of ferritin levels and transferrin saturation, as well as discomfort during the therapeutic procedure and any changes in blood cell counts or albumin and CRP levels. The patient meets the requirements to participate in the trial, as he has a body weight higher than 65 kg and an initial hemoglobin level higher than 12 g/dL. He has provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 50-year-old male patient with a genetic confirmation of myotonic dystrophy type 2 (DM2) presents to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. The patient has a history of progressive proximal muscle weakness and wasting, combined with axial and anterior neck muscles involvement, myotonia, muscular pain, fatigue, and cataracts. He is currently not participating in any other clinical trial and has no other invalidating diseases. The patient is able to read and speak fluent German and provide informed consent. He is willing to complete a battery of patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and clinical outcome measures (OMs) for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been experiencing recurring episodes of abdominal pain for the past few months. He was diagnosed with cholecystitis and advised to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history. He does not smoke, drink or use any drugs. His body mass index is 26. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics or any other drugs used in the study. He has no history of bleeding disorders or mental impairment. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He is classified as ASA class II. He is currently not experiencing any infections in the block area.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who experienced his first episode of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction two weeks ago. He was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. ECG showed ST elevation in leads II, III, and AVF. The patient received thrombolytic therapy and was transferred to the cardiac care unit for further management. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. The patient's echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent. He does not have any contraindications for ARB use and has not participated in any other pharmacological study within the past 2 months.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been experiencing symptoms of allergic conjunctivitis for the past 2 years. She reports itching, redness, and tearing of the eyes, particularly during the spring and fall months. She has previously been treated with topical ocular anti-allergy medications twice daily, but has found the regimen to be inconvenient and disruptive to her daily routine. She wears contact lenses but is willing to avoid them during the study visits. Her ocular health is within normal limits and she has no history of recurrent corneal erosion syndrome. She is not currently pregnant or nursing.

This clinical trial is seeking a male or female patient between the ages of 20-65 who is undergoing elective craniotomy surgery. The patient must be willing to provide informed consent for participation in the trial. They must not have a history of HIV, hepatitis, or other CNS infections. Additionally, they must not have any history of dementia, Alzheimer's disease, or other neurodegenerative diseases. The patient should have been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and be willing to undergo transplantation of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells derived from human brain.

This is a 28-year-old male who has a history of recurrent knee pain for the last 2 years. An MRI showed a meniscal tear and he is scheduled for knee arthroscopic surgery. He has a BMI of 25 and no anatomical anomalies of vertebrae. He has no known drug allergies or medical conditions. He is currently not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the accuracy of two landmarks (Tuffier's line and tenth rib line) for application of spinal anesthesia. He understands that the trial involves the use of ultrasonography during the procedure to ensure accuracy and that he will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups. He has been provided with all the necessary information about the trial and has given his informed consent to participate.

Patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22. He has no history of any chronic illnesses or organ dysfunction. He is not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medications or supplements. He has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is not currently smoking or using any tobacco products. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the guidelines for the duration of the study.

An 65-year-old Caucasian male is scheduled to undergo elective major surgery for prostate cancer. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has never had any surgery before. He has no history of schizophrenia, epilepsy, or Parkinson's disease. He has normal hearing and vision, and no language barriers. He has no history of traumatic brain injury. His electrocardiogram shows normal sinus rhythm. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He has been experiencing motor fluctuations over the past year, with periods of "off" time where his symptoms worsen despite medication. He has been taking levodopa/carbidopa and entacapone to manage his symptoms but has not seen significant improvement. He has no history of atypical Parkinsonian syndrome, surgical intervention for Parkinson's disease, or participation in other studies involving investigational drugs. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his motor fluctuations.

A 25-year-old Caucasian female presents with facial acne that started about a year ago. She has tried over-the-counter products but has not seen any significant improvement. She has no history of any other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She does not have any allergies. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions on her face. Laboratory tests are normal. She is willing to adhere to all study procedures and is able to provide written informed consent. She is not pregnant and is willing to use medically acceptable contraception if sexually active.

A 35-year-old male manual worker who has been employed in a municipal workplace for the past 3 years is experiencing low back pain for the past few weeks. He has no history of any chronic disease or significant health issues. He exercises occasionally but mostly leads a sedentary lifestyle outside of work. He has never received any formal education or training regarding low back pain. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about managing his symptoms and preventing further injury.

47-year-old female with a history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) secondary to sarcomeric gene mutation presents with dyspnea on exertion and chest pains during exercise. The patient is currently on beta-blocker therapy and has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. The patient is a non-smoker and not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not been diagnosed with any other cardiac pathology reducing life expectancy. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the relations between endothelial and venous dysfunctions and symptomatic left ventricular outflow-tract obstruction in HCM patients. She is willing to undergo additional testing, including air venous plethysmography, upper member arterial Doppler echography with analysis of Flow Mediated Dilatation (FMD), and endothelial function biomarkers blood sample tests. The patient is able to provide signed informed consent and is affiliated with the national social security system.

The patient is a 32 year old female who has been experiencing pain in her bladder for the past year. She describes the pain as a constant burning sensation that is worse when she urinates. She has been to several doctors and has been diagnosed with interstitial cystitis. She has tried several different treatments, including medications, but has not found any relief. She is currently working as a sales representative and spends a lot of her time on the road. She enjoys spending time with her family and friends but has had to cancel plans due to the pain she experiences. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if intranasal oxytocin can help relieve her pain. She is not pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. She has no history of significant cardiac or pulmonary disease and has not undergone any procedural interventions related to her interstitial cystitis in the past month. Her blood pressure is within the normal range. She is willing to complete the questionnaires and follow-up visits required for the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with Rett Syndrome, diagnosed according to the 2010 criteria and confirmed to have a MECP2 mutation. She is currently in the post-regression stage, having lost her spoken language and motor skills 9 months ago. She has a Clinical Global Impression - Severity (CGI-S) score of 5. She is currently taking a stable regimen of two antiepileptic drugs, which have been unchanged for the last 30 days. She is receiving educational and behavioral interventions, which have been continuous for the last 90 days and will remain unchanged during the study. She does not have any known hypersensitivity to any of the excipients contained in the study drug or placebo formulation. She is willing to participate in the study and her parent/caregiver/LAR has provided written informed consent. She has no history of liver disease, clinically evident neurologic or psychiatric conditions, or other clinically significant abnormality on physical, neurological, laboratory, or electrocardiogram examination. She is not taking any other investigational drugs or potent CYP 3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors and inducers.

This is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with advanced prostate cancer that has shown resistance to standard hormonal therapy and chemotherapy. He has a histological diagnosis of adenocarcinoma and has been determined to have HLA-A*2402. Despite undergoing previous treatments, his cancer has continued to progress. He currently has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that he is still able to function independently with some limitations. His blood work shows a WBC count of 8,500/mm³, hemoglobin level of 11.2 g/dl, and platelet count of 180,000/mm³. His liver function tests show AST and ALT levels within normal limits, and his total bilirubin levels are 0.8 mg/dl. His renal function is normal with a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dl. He has a PaO2 level of 85 mmHg, indicating normal oxygen levels. The patient has a life expectancy of more than two months and is willing to participate in the study, having given valid written informed consent.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of smoking came to the clinic with a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has no other serious concurrent medical illness and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient is scheduled to undergo a continuous daily course of radiation therapy with or without chemotherapy. The patient has no prior history of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and has an absolute neutrophil count of 1000/mm3 and a platelet count of 70,000/mm3. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has access to refrigerated storage for the Whole Food Intervention. The patient has no ongoing alcohol or drug abuse and is not undergoing treatment for HIV with HIV medications. The patient has no allergies or food intolerances relevant to the ingredients of the Whole Food Intervention and is able to swallow.

A 14-year-old female diagnosed with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) with a Cobb angle of 60 degrees is scheduled for a posterior spinal fusion surgery to correct the curvature. The patient has no history of chronic pain or narcotic medication use. The patient is otherwise healthy with an ASA physical status of 1. Informed consent has been obtained from the patient's legal guardian and assent from the patient. The patient is able to use the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) for pain assessment. The patient has no known allergies to standard of care drugs used in the study.

Patient is a 6-year-old boy who has been experiencing symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) for at least 3 months prior to screening. He has previously been on proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy but had a failed attempted withdrawal of the medication with a return of symptoms upon withdrawal. The patient has a medical history of hurting or burning in the stomach, chest, or throat on at least 3 of any 7 consecutive days during the Screening Period. The patient is male and aged between 1 to 11 years. He is a candidate for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of the study. The patient's parents will be asked to record any time the patient has heartburn symptoms in an electronic diary. The overall time to participate in this study is up to 16 weeks, which includes up to 4 weeks to screen for the study. The patient will make multiple visits to the clinic, plus a final phone call 5 to 10 days after last dose of study drug for a follow-up assessment.

50-year-old male with end-stage liver disease due to alcoholic cirrhosis, with a MELD score of 22, is scheduled for an elective living donor liver transplantation. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently on lisinopril. The patient has no history of neuromuscular disease or severe cardiopulmonary diseases. The patient has not received any transfusions in the past 24 hours. The patient has not taken any drugs that influence the metabolism of vecuronium. The graft to recipient body weight ratio is within the acceptable range for transplantation. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old male patient was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil. He underwent left tonsillectomy and left selective neck dissection, revealing a T2N2b tumor. The patient has no history of other malignancies, and his past medical history is unremarkable. The patient has no allergies, and he is not taking any medications. The patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has no significant family history of cancer. The patient's performance status is good, with a Karnofsky score of 80. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and overweight with a BMI of 30 kg/m2. He has been stable in treatment for 6 months with metformin (1.5 g) and a GLP-1 receptor agonist. He does not have any gastrointestinal, liver, or kidney diseases, nor does he have a history of anorexia, bulimia, or binge eating disorder. He is a non-smoker and is not taking any other glucose-lowering drugs besides the prescribed ones. He has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

As a retrospective study, there will be no patient contact in this clinical trial. The study will be collecting data from Sheffield Children's Hospital Accident and Emergency Department and Jessop Hospital for the past 10 years. The study will be focused on children up to the age of 2, both term and preterm, who have had either accidental or inflicted fractures and are otherwise healthy. The study will not include children who have sustained fractures from other causes such as post-surgery, post-resuscitation, metabolic bone diseases or have any significant metabolic bone condition or received any medication known to affect vitamin D metabolism 3 months before enrollment such as oral glucocorticoids, anticonvulsants, etc. The study will be collecting data on age, sex, gestation, ethnicity, and diagnosis of the patients.

A 32-year-old woman who has been suffering from migraines for the past 10 years came to the clinic for a consultation. She has been experiencing 2-3 migraine attacks per month, which are characterized by throbbing pain on one side of the head, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound. She has been using injectable sumatriptan for the past 6 months, which has been effective in relieving her migraine symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate an investigational auto-injector system for delivering sumatriptan under the skin for a single migraine attack. She has no history of seizure disorders, coronary artery disease, cardiac dysrhythmia, high blood pressure or autoimmune disease. She is not currently pregnant and has not used any other investigational drug product within 30 days prior to treatment visit. She is capable of using a migraine self-injection auto-injector and distinguishing between migraine and other headache types.

The patient is a healthy, full-term, 7-day-old baby boy with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. His mother is unable to breastfeed and has agreed to enroll him in the study. The baby has no known medical conditions and has not received any antibiotics or other drugs in the last three days. His family has no history of allergies to cow's milk. The parents have agreed to exclusively feed the baby with the study formula until he reaches 16 weeks of age and participate in the study up to 9 months of age. They have also agreed to fill out the infant's diary and parent questionnaires during the study period. The baby meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old Korean male who has been diagnosed with actinic keratosis. He has noticed rough, scaly patches on his face and scalp that have not improved with over-the-counter treatments. He has fair skin and a history of sun exposure due to his outdoor occupation. He is in good health with no significant medical history. He is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for the duration of the trial. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with recurrent or metastatic HPV16 positive oropharyngeal cancer. He has already undergone platinum-containing chemotherapy but experienced disease progression. His tumors express PD-L1 (Combined Positive Score [CPS] ≥1) and he is a candidate for first-line therapy with a PD-1 blocking antibody. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, measurable disease by computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) per RECIST 1.1 criteria and has completed previous radiation therapy at least 4 weeks prior to study drug administration. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory testing, and other requirements of the study. He has not received prior treatment with an anti-PD-1 antibody or therapeutic anti-HPV vaccines including ISA101 or ISA101b. He has no known brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases and has no serious or uncontrolled medical disorder that may increase the risk associated with study participation or study drug administration.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with melanoma on his left lower leg five years ago. He underwent several surgeries and was enrolled in a clinical trial for talimogene laherparepvec treatment. He received a total of 6 doses of talimogene laherparepvec and completed the clinical trial successfully. He has been in remission for the past 3 years and has been receiving regular follow-up appointments with his oncologist. He is interested in enrolling in this registry study to help advance research on the long-term safety and effectiveness of talimogene laherparepvec.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester, currently enrolled in the Oportunidades program. She lives in a rural area with her husband and two young children. Her pregnancy has been relatively healthy so far, with no complications reported. However, she has a history of anemia and is currently taking iron supplements as recommended by her healthcare provider. She is interested in participating in a study that could potentially improve the health outcomes for her and her unborn child. She is willing to try different nutritional supplements as part of the study and is willing to discontinue any other supplements she is currently taking. She is able to attend regular study visits and follow all instructions provided by the study staff.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who presented to the hospital with complaints of shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue. Further evaluation revealed severe mitral regurgitation due to degenerative disease. The patient has been advised to undergo mitral valve repair surgery. He has no prior history of cardiac surgeries or chest deformities that would prevent robotic-assisted or minimally invasive video-assisted surgery. His femoral arteries diameter is greater than 6mm. His left ventricular systolic function is normal. He is willing to participate in the study and complete the follow-up. He has signed the informed consent form for participation and data management. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) at the age of 23. Her current pregnancy was achieved with the help of ovulation induction therapy. She is currently at 28 weeks and 4 days of gestation. She has been experiencing regular and painful uterine contractions for the past 24 hours, with an average of 4 contractions per hour. She has not experienced any vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage. She has a cervical length of 25mm on transvaginal ultrasound. She has no history of cervical cerclage, multiple gestation, preterm rupture of membranes, chorioamnionitis, cervical dilation greater than 3cm, placenta previa or abruptio placentae, intra-uterine growth restriction, pre-eclampsia, or any other maternal or fetal pathology. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She is able to attend all follow-up visits as required.

Patient is a 62-year-old man from the United States who was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) 5 months ago. He has completed first-line therapy with irinotecan and platinum-based chemotherapy, but the disease has progressed. He reports fatigue, shortness of breath, and coughing up blood. He has no significant past medical history, and his laboratory tests show normal renal and hepatic function. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no active brain or leptomeningeal metastases. His only other medication is a blood pressure medication, which he has been taking for 5 years. He is willing to participate in clinical trials and understands the potential risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of chest pain and a positive stress test. He has been diagnosed with a >70% coronary artery stenosis and is scheduled to undergo coronary angioplasty or stenting procedure. He has not been on a Hmgcoa-reductase inhibitor or a stable statin dose for at least four weeks prior to the procedure. He has no history of recent coronary intervention, treatment with abciximab antagonist, thrombolytic therapy within 48 hours, or MI within 2 months. He has no recent infections and has not undergone general anesthesia within 3 months. He has normal renal function and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents with severe shoulder pain and stiffness that has been worsening for the past year, affecting his sleep and daily activities. He has been diagnosed with a rotator cuff tear and scheduled for surgery. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He takes lisinopril for hypertension and atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia. He has no known allergies. On physical examination, there is tenderness and weakness in the affected shoulder, with limited range of motion. He has no other significant medical history, and no family history of shoulder problems. The patient is able to give written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

45 yo M with a history of chronic shoulder pain and limited range of motion in the right shoulder. The patient reports difficulty with overhead activities and has been taking over-the-counter pain medication for symptom relief. The patient was referred to Radiology for an ultrasound of the shoulder to evaluate for any underlying structural abnormalities. The patient has no known history of previous shoulder surgeries or injuries. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - No known allergies

A 25-year old office worker is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of influenza. She reports being in good health with no major medical conditions. She has no history of autoimmune disease, lower respiratory tract infection, or frequent nosebleeds. She is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. She has not been vaccinated for influenza virus since 2006. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has not had any nasal or sinus surgery within the past 6 months. She has no history of autonomic dysfunction or significant allergies. She is not a healthcare worker and does not anticipate having patient contact within 2 weeks of viral challenge. She is willing to discontinue any asthma medications she may be taking.

Patient 1: The patient is a 14-year-old girl diagnosed with congenital hyperinsulinism. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of hypoglycemia, despite appropriate treatment with medications and dietary modifications. Her treating physician has recommended 18F-DOPA PET/CT imaging to evaluate the extent and location of abnormal insulin secretion in her pancreas. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prohibit her from participating in the study.  Patient 2: The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with neuroblastoma. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, and his treating physician has recommended 18F-DOPA PET/CT imaging to evaluate the effectiveness of his current treatment regimen. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prohibit him from participating in the study.  Patient 3: The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of carcinoid tumor of the small intestine. She has been experiencing symptoms of carcinoid syndrome, including facial flushing and diarrhea, despite treatment with somatostatin analogues. Her treating physician has recommended 18F-DOPA PET/CT imaging to evaluate the extent and location of her tumor. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prohibit her from participating in the study.  Patient 4: The patient is a 60-year-old man with a clinical suspicion of Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia, and his treating physician has recommended 18F-DOPA PET/CT imaging to evaluate the extent and location of dopaminergic dysfunction in his brain. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prohibit him from participating in the study.  Patient 5: The patient is a 25-year-old woman with a primary brain tumor. She has undergone surgical resection and radiation therapy, and her treating physician has recommended 18F-DOPA PET/CT imaging to evaluate the extent and location of residual tumor. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prohibit her from participating in the study.

A 55-year-old male stroke survivor with left hemiparesis presents to the Kırıkkale University Faculty of Medicine Physical Therapy clinic for rehabilitation. The patient has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of falls after his stroke and has completed eight weeks of stroke rehabilitation. The patient is cognitively intact and able to communicate effectively. He weighs 75 kg and has a Modified Ashworth Scale score of 2 for spasticity in his affected leg. The patient has no open wounds under the soles of his feet and is able to stand independently for more than 20 seconds. He has no history of thoracolumbar surgery or spinal canal stenosis. The patient has no vision problems, and his Mini Mental Test score is above 24. He volunteers to participate in a clinical trial investigating the immediate effect of plantar vibration on fall risk and postural stability in stroke patients.

A 32-year-old male, diagnosed with cocaine dependence as per DSM-IV criteria, is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at reducing stress and cue induced cravings. The patient has never been treated for cocaine dependence before but has attempted to quit in the past with limited success. He currently smokes cigarettes and drinks alcohol socially but is willing to abstain from all drugs of abuse during the study. The patient is in good health and has no significant medical history. He is currently taking no prescription medications and has no known allergies. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the guanfacine or placebo group. He is also willing to be randomly assigned to the stress or no-stress subgroup. The patient has no history of psychotic disorder, bipolar affective disorder, or major depressive disorder. He is not taking any psychotropic medications, opiates, or opiate antagonists. The patient has a BMI of 25 and is not grossly obese. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and attend all follow-up visits.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has not undergone any previous endocrine treatment for prostate cancer and is currently seeking treatment options. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) score of 1 and a serum PSA level of 4.5 ng/mL at screening. He has no history of poorly controlled asthma, anaphylactic reactions, or severe urticaria or angioedema. Additionally, he does not have hypersensitivity to mannitol. He has a normal QT/QTc interval and does not have a family history of QT prolongation syndrome. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of ASP3550 to goserelin acetate for the treatment of prostate cancer.

30 year old woman who is expecting her first child and planning to receive neuraxial labor analgesia. She is fluent in English and able to read and comprehend the language, as the study requires the completion of several questionnaires. She has identified her partner as her primary support person and is over the age of 18. She has no contraindications to receiving any of the medications routinely used in the placement of a labor epidural catheter. This is her first pregnancy and she is currently admitted to the Labor and Delivery ward at Prentice Women's Hospital.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who presents with a history of bloody stool and constipation for the past 6 months. She initially ignored the symptoms, but they have now progressed and are causing her significant discomfort. On examination, a rectal mass is palpable, and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis of rectal cancer. Further evaluation reveals that the tumor is T3 and N+. The patient is a non-smoker, has no significant past medical history, and is in overall good health. She is deemed eligible for the clinical trial, and neoadjuvant chemoradiation is planned. The patient receives pelvic irradiation by 50.4 thousands grays together with radio sensitization by 5-FU. Eight months after completion of neoadjuvant chemoradiation, the patient is assessed clinically and radiologically. It is found that the patient has achieved complete clinical response and has the split scar sign in her pelvic MRI. The patient will undergo total mesorectal excision 8-11 weeks after completion of neoadjuvant chemoradiation, and postoperative pathology will be assessed to determine the effectiveness of the neoadjuvant therapy.

This is a 32 year-old woman who is pregnant with twins and is scheduled for an elective cesarean section at 38 weeks gestation. She has a history of gestational diabetes but it is well-controlled with diet and exercise. She has not had any complications during her pregnancy and has been regularly attending her prenatal appointments. She has no known allergies to medication and has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male with a body weight of 75 kg and a BMI of 25. He does not smoke and has no history of regular alcohol consumption. The patient has normal PT, aPTT, and TT laboratory values. He has no known allergies to acetylsalicylic acid, other salicylates, clopidogrel, thienopyridines (eg, ticlopidine, prasugrel), apixaban or dabigatran. The patient has not been diagnosed with any coagulation abnormality or had any major bleeding episodes. He has never had peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics profile of multiple doses of LT3001 drug product and drug interactions with potential concomitant medications.

A 50-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of leg pain and swelling. He has a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his right leg five years ago, which was treated with anticoagulants. He has been experiencing occasional pain and swelling in his leg since then, but it has become more frequent and bothersome recently. He works as a construction worker and spends most of his day standing and walking. He has no other underlying medical conditions and takes no medication regularly. He has no allergies to any food or drugs.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who is generally healthy and has not smoked or used any nicotine-containing products for at least 6 continuous months. He has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18 and 32. He does not have any significant medical history, including cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, gallbladder or biliary tract, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic or psychiatric disease. He has not consumed any alcohol-containing beverages for 3 days prior to the study and has agreed to abstain from taking any dietary supplements or non-prescription drugs (except for multivitamins or as otherwise authorized by the Investigator and Medical Monitor) for 14 days prior to the study. He has agreed to abstain from consuming caffeine- or chocolate-containing products from CRU admission through discharge. He is not positive at screening for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B surface antigen, or hepatitis C virus. He has not participated in another clinical trial within 90 days prior to dosing. He has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years, with the exception of successfully treated non-metastatic basal cell or squamous cell carcinomas of the skin and/or localized carcinoma in situ of the cervix. He has adequate venous access for repeated venipuncture and his hemoglobin is >/= 11.5 g/dL. He has voluntarily provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her jaw joint for the past 6 months. She reports feeling a clicking or popping sensation when she opens her mouth wide or chews food. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided relief. In addition to her jaw pain, she has a history of osteoarthritis in her knees and takes naproxen for pain management. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find alternative treatment options for her jaw pain. Her lab results are within normal limits, and imaging studies show evidence of disc displacement. She meets the inclusion criteria for the Celecoxib study and has not undergone any TMJ surgery within the past 6 months. She is willing to keep a pain diary twice a day and complete written questionnaires about her jaw condition. She is also interested in the Etanercept study, but she does not meet the inclusion criteria for this study as she has not tried non-surgical TMD therapy yet. She is willing to participate in either study and is looking forward to finding relief for her jaw pain.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with hypertension during a routine checkup. Her blood pressure readings were consistently high, ranging between 160/100 mm Hg and 170/110 mm Hg. She has no history of diabetes, coronary artery disease, or any other significant medical conditions. She has never been treated for hypertension and is not currently taking any antihypertensive medication. She has no known secondary hypertension of any etiology. Her bloodwork results from the last three months show a serum creatinine level of 100 µmol/L, AST and ALT levels within the normal range, and serum potassium levels of 4.0 mEq/L. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is not planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is able to adhere to the study protocol and follow-up visits.

This is a 55-year-old African-American male with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been taking antihypertensive medications for the past 3 years and has had difficulty keeping his blood pressure under control. Despite taking his medications regularly, his most recent clinic blood pressure reading was 150/95 mm Hg. He reports occasional headaches and dizziness but denies any chest pain, shortness of breath or palpitations. He smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently employed as a truck driver and has a sedentary lifestyle due to his job. He has a family history of hypertension and stroke. He is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has struggled with her weight for most of her adult life. Her BMI is currently at 38. She has tried multiple diets and exercise programs but has not been able to achieve sustained weight loss. She is now seeking medical or surgical management for her severe obesity and is referred to the Arras Hospital Nutrition Unit for consultation. She has no history of psychiatric conditions or eating disorders, but she does admit to frequently overeating and feeling out of control around food. She is willing to participate in the OSCAR study to better understand her eating habits and potentially uncover any underlying eating disorders. She is able to read and write and is not under guardianship or deprived of liberty. She is affiliated with the social security scheme and consents to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a constant dull ache that is worsened with prolonged sitting or standing. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and hot/cold therapy, but these treatments have only provided temporary relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate different physiotherapy treatments for her low back pain. She has no history of cardiac pacemaker, osteosynthesis or prostheses, and has not received any spinal injection in the last six weeks. She is willing to sign the consent form and commit to attending 20 sessions of treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who had a heart attack in the past five years and undergone coronary revascularisation. He has completed a minimum of eight supervised cardiac rehabilitation sessions and exercises at least once a week for a minimum duration of thirty minutes. He is conversational in English and has a recent experience of at least one month using any mobile app. He displays capacity for self-monitoring and entering data. The patient has a documented ejection fraction of at least 40%. He has experience using a smartphone for at least 6 months. The patient does not have any abnormal physiological response during exercise. The patient is willing to participate in a study to explore the usability of the "Heart-track" app to improve his cardiac rehabilitation experience.

40-year-old female with a 3-year history of rheumatoid arthritis, currently experiencing mild-to-moderate disease activity with swelling and tenderness in multiple joints, particularly in the hands and feet. The patient has tried two conventional synthetic Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs (csDMARDs) with inadequate response. She is not currently taking any medication for her RA. She has no significant comorbidities, is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of bleeding or coagulation disorders. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of sacral nerve stimulation (SNS) for the treatment of her RA symptoms.

52-year-old male with a history of alcoholism and alcoholic liver cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class B) diagnosed by liver biopsy. He has stopped drinking for the past 6 months and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma, infectious diseases such as HIV, HBV, or HCV, and any other incurable malignancy. He has no history of previous stem cell therapy. He is currently on medications for hypertension, and his liver function tests show elevated levels of ALT and AST. He has no history of significant complications related to cirrhosis, such as ascites or hepatic encephalopathy. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of bone marrow-derived autologous mesenchymal stem cell therapy for hepatic failure caused by alcoholic liver cirrhosis.

A 62-year-old male patient is scheduled for a primary, unilateral knee replacement surgery. He has been experiencing severe pain and stiffness in his knee joint that limits his ability to perform daily activities. The patient has a BMI of 28 and no history of renal insufficiency. He does not have any chronic opioid use or abuse. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has a caretaker who will remain with him from home discharge until catheter removal. During the study, he will receive perineural local anesthetic infusion through a tiny tube next to the nerves in his knee for five days following the surgery. He will be able to control the infusion pump himself and will be given pain pills if needed. Physical therapy will also be provided to the patient, and he will be checked to see if he is ready to go home. After hospital discharge, the patient will be contacted by a research nurse for five nights to assess his comfort level and satisfaction. He will also be contacted at 7 days and then 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 months following the surgery to assess his pain levels, stiffness, and joint functional ability.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has been hospitalized due to COVID-19 infection. He was initially diagnosed with fever, cough, and breathing difficulty and was later confirmed positive for COVID-19 through testing. He has been in the hospital for 5 days and is currently in the COVID-19 overflow area of the hospital. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 3 years. He also has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit smoking 5 years ago. The patient has been experiencing some chest pain and the healthcare provider has ordered a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) to evaluate his heart. The patient has been informed about the new software program that guides non-sonographers to take the best possible pictures of the heart and has consented to participate in the study. The patient is able to lie flat for the study and is willing to give consent.

45-year-old male with a BMI of 38 kg/m2, scheduled for bariatric surgery in 2 weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. The patient reports a family history of obesity and has struggled with weight loss for many years, attempting various diets and exercise programs with limited success. The patient reports no current neurologic or psychiatric conditions and does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient has been cleared for surgery by his primary care physician and has no contraindications for bariatric surgery. The patient is right-handed and willing to participate in the study to help advance the understanding of taste physiology in obese individuals.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer 3 years ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy treatment for the cancer, but it has since returned. She is experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. Her CA-125 levels are elevated. She has previously received platinum-based chemotherapy for her cancer and has not received any non-cytotoxic therapy for her recurrent disease. She has a performance score of 1 and adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. She has no other concurrent medical conditions that could cause unacceptable safety risks. She has not received regorafenib before and has not used any investigational drugs, biologics or devices in the past 28 days. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has a normal blood pressure. She has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and has not had any significant bleeding events in the past 4 weeks. She has no symptomatic metastatic brain or meningeal tumors and does not have ongoing infections. She is willing to participate in this study to try to improve her cancer prognosis.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. His echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 40%. He has been advised to undergo elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) under cardiopulmonary bypass. He has not had any previous heart surgeries and has agreed to participate in the study. The patient is able to read and understand the informed consent document and has signed it. He has normal serum creatinine, ALT/AST levels and does not require intra-aortic balloon pump pre-operatively. He has not had a stroke or atrial fibrillation in the last 3 months and does not have heart conduction problems or a pacemaker. The patient does not have HIV and does not have any contraindications to pulmonary artery catheter insertion.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who was recently released from incarceration after serving a 2-year sentence for drug possession. He has a history of drug abuse and has undergone treatment for drug-related problems in the past. He is currently on parole and is required to participate in substance use treatment as a condition of his parole. He is at moderate-to-high-risk of drug relapse and/or recidivism as determined by a Lifestyle Criminality Screening Form (LCSF) score of 8. He is fluent in English and has no psychotic features. He has no parole or probation conditions that prohibit him from participating in the protocol. He is interested in participating in a study that examines whether improved integration between the community supervision system and outpatient addiction treatment system can improve treatment adherence, drug use, and public safety outcomes among drug-involved inmates re-entering the community.

A 6-year-old boy with a history of asthma and eczema is scheduled to undergo an allergy prick skin test to determine the cause of his recurrent episodes of wheezing and itching. He is accompanied by his mother, who reports that he is generally anxious about medical procedures and has difficulty sitting still. The boy is alert and oriented and appears to be in good health. His vital signs are within normal limits for his age. On physical examination, he has mild eczema on his arms and legs. The nurse explains the procedure to him and his mother and offers to apply either a topical anesthetic cream or have a medical clown present during the procedure. The boy expresses a preference for the medical clown, as he finds them funny and entertaining. The medical clown arrives and begins interacting with the boy, using humor and magic tricks to distract him. The nurse applies the allergen to his volar aspect of the arm, and he reports feeling a slight sting. However, he is able to remain calm and cooperative throughout the procedure. Afterward, he receives a sticker from the medical clown and a lollipop from the nurse. He reports feeling very happy and not at all anxious about the procedure.

A 25 year old male gym enthusiast, who exercises 3 times per week, is interested in participating in the study. He has no history of cardiovascular, musculoskeletal or metabolic diseases. He is a non-smoker, and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is within the normal range (22.4 kg/m²). He has no regular medication or supplement use. He is willing to come to the lab for a total of 3 visits and follow the instructions given for each visit. He is comfortable with the use of ultrasound imaging and blood sampling.

This is a 32 year-old male who has been struggling with alcohol use disorder (AUD) for the past 5 years. He has tried to quit drinking multiple times but has been unsuccessful in maintaining sobriety. Recently, he has been admitted to the 12-week inpatient program at the Clinic Südhang to receive treatment for his AUD. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 6 weeks and has shown a strong motivation to stay sober. He is mentally competent and able to provide informed consent. He has no other main psychiatric diagnosis except for AUD, and has no severe substance use disorder apart from nicotine addiction. He does not have any neurocognitive problems and is physically fit to participate in the study. He is able to read and understand the participant's information and is willing to participate in the study. The study team has explained the potential risks and benefits of the study to the patient and he has agreed to sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%) six months ago. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg daily. He presents with mild dyspnea on exertion (NYHA class II) and reports occasional episodes of orthopnea and lower extremity edema. He denies chest pain, syncope, or palpitations. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 75 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. Physical examination is notable for bilateral basal crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure, and pitting edema up to mid-shin. Laboratory tests show an elevated BNP level of 600 pg/mL and a stable creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. His current dose of lisinopril is 5 mg/day, and he has not been prescribed a beta-blocker yet. He is interested in participating in a study that may help his primary care physician uptitrate his medications to improve his heart failure management.

A 16 year old female presents with a history of brief psychotic symptoms, including hearing voices and paranoia, that resolved spontaneously within one week. She also reports a decline in her academic and social functioning in the past year. She has no previous history of mental illness or substance abuse. Her family history is significant for psychosis in her maternal grandfather. She is not currently taking any medications and has no medical conditions that might interfere with the trial. Her laboratory values are normal. She meets the criteria for ultra-high risk of psychosis as determined by the Comprehensive Assessment of At-Risk Mental States (CAARMS) and is interested in participating in the study.

24F with a 9-month-old male infant, residing in a rural community in a low-income country. The infant's birth weight was 3.5 kg, and he was born full-term via normal vaginal delivery. The infant is breastfed exclusively and has started complementary feeding. The mother reports that the infant has had multiple episodes of diarrhea in the past month, with an average duration of 3 days per episode. The infant has not been hospitalized for any of these episodes. The mother reports that the infant has not been given any micronutrient supplements previously. The mother herself reports good health, with no chronic illnesses or medication use. She is willing to participate in a study on preventing zinc deficiency and treating diarrhea in young children. She plans to stay in the community for the next year.

The patient is a 4-year-old male child who has been suffering from intense snoring, which has been causing sleep disturbances. The parents have noticed that the child's snoring is loud and frequent, and he has episodes of gasping and choking during sleep. The child is otherwise healthy, with no history of chronic illnesses or surgeries. The child's parents have signed the informed consent form and are covered by the National Health Insurance Program. The child is eligible for the study and will be required to undergo a home polysomnography test to diagnose the possibility of Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome (OSA).

The patient is a 62-year-old man who underwent cardiac surgery for coronary artery bypass grafting 2 years ago. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and chronic kidney disease stage 3. His current medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and a low dose of aspirin. He presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and chest pain on exertion. His physical examination is significant for bilateral crackles on lung auscultation, hypertension with a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, and a regular heart rhythm with no murmurs. His laboratory results show an elevated troponin level at 3.4 ng/mL (normal range <0.03 ng/mL) and a glomerular filtration rate of 40 mL/min/1.73 m². He is scheduled for further evaluation to determine the cause of his symptoms and to assess his cardiac function. He is a potential candidate for the clinical trial investigating the prognostic value of postoperative troponin in patients with renal dysfunction undergoing cardiac surgery.

45 yo F with a history of chronic sinusitis that has not responded to medical management. The patient has been experiencing nasal congestion, facial pain, and pressure for over 12 weeks. The patient is scheduled for sinus surgery due to the severity of symptoms. The patient has no history of cystic fibrosis, vasculitis, or nasal tumors and is not currently receiving immunosuppressant therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide both nasal and peripheral blood samples before and after surgery. The patient understands that the study aims to identify biomarkers associated with CRS disease severity and is willing to complete quality of life symptom scoring.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with classical Hodgkin's disease with mediastinal involvement. Upon diagnosis, a chest X-ray showed enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum. She is currently asymptomatic and has no prior history of lung disease. She is a non-smoker and works as a teacher. The patient is scheduled to receive bleomycin-based chemotherapy with or without chest radiation therapy as part of her standard cancer treatment. She has no allergies to any medications and is currently taking a multivitamin and calcium supplement. The patient has no previous history of chest radiation therapy or refractory or progressive disease on treatment. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the pulmonary function tests and CAT scans.

A 35-year-old male patient with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis is being considered for participation in a pilot study. He has been experiencing exacerbations of his symptoms and is initiating treatment with interferon beta-1a subcutaneous injections with a minimal dosing of 22mcg. He is between 18-60 years of age and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has a stable dose of concomitant medications and is willing to maintain steady doses of these medications for the duration of the study. He has no history of hypersensitivity to interferon beta 1a and is able to administer subcutaneous injections. He has no history of diabetes mellitus type I or II, hepatitis B or C, or seropositivity for HIV. He has no implanted devices or metal which would contraindicate MRI. He has no clinically significant abnormalities in CBC or CMP and has a MMSE score of 27. The patient is interested in participating in the study to determine if there is a correlation between serum leptin levels and serum nitric oxide levels during a clinically observed increase in disease activity.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) for the past 5 years is experiencing cognitive problems. He has a history of relapsing-remitting MS and currently takes interferon-beta-1a injections. He has no other significant medical conditions and is physically active with regular walking and light stretching exercises. He reports difficulty with memory, concentration, and attention in his daily life, which is affecting his job performance and social interactions. He is able to ride a recumbent cross trainer and is willing to participate in the exercise program. He has not undergone chemotherapy or natalizumab treatment and has a screening score of less than 50 on the PASAT.
