He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his cognitive function and overall quality of life.

A 24-year-old woman with a history of osteosarcoma presents with relapsed, non-resectable disease that has progressed after first-line treatments. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has undergone biopsy and has been diagnosed with high-grade osteosarcoma. Imaging studies reveal measurable disease as defined by RECIST criteria vs. 1.1, and the baseline evaluation has been completed within 28 days prior to enrolment. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her estimated life expectancy is at least 3 months. She is over 18 years old and meets the eligibility criteria for adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. Hemoglobin is 10 g/dL, Absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mm3, and Platelet count is 150,000/μl. Total bilirubin is 1.0 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT and AST are <2.5xULN (<5xULN for patients with liver involvement of their cancer), PT-INR/PTT<1.5xULN, Serum creatinine is <1.5xULN. She is willing to give written informed consent. She has no history of dementia or significantly altered mental status that would prohibit the understanding or rendering of informed consent and compliance with the requirements of this protocol. She has no severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions that could cause unacceptable safety risks or compromise compliance with the protocol. She is not pregnant or breast-feeding and has a negative pregnancy test performed within 7 days of the start of treatment. She is willing to use adequate barrier birth control measures during the course of the trial and 8 weeks after the last dose of study drug.

Patient is a 70-year-old Indonesian male who is currently in a fit (robust) or pre-frailty state. He has no known history of liver cirrhosis or severe liver dysfunction, and his serum ALT levels are within normal limits. His BMI is 22.5 Kg/m2, indicating that he is not malnourished. He has no history of acute illnesses during the inclusion period, such as pneumonia, pain due to acute arthritis, stroke attack, crisis hypertension, or severe cardiac or pulmonary dysfunction. His Abbreviated Mental Test (AMT) score is 9, indicating that he is capable of understanding and carrying out instructions. His Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) score is 5, indicating that he is not experiencing significant depression. He is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about his frailty status and quality of life.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital in Denmark. She has a history of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) and tends to experience depressive symptoms during the winter season. She reports feeling tired, sad, and unmotivated during this time of year, and has noticed a decrease in her overall well-being. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the role of vitamin D supplementation in preventing depression symptoms during the winter season. She has no history of sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, bipolar affective disorder, schizophrenia, hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperparathyroidism, or reduced kidney function. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The ideal participant for this clinical trial would be a healthy adult between the ages of 19 and 30 who is right-hand dominant and has normal or corrected-to-normal vision. They should be planning to move to a high altitude environment within the next month or have long-term residency in a low altitude area. The participant should not have a history of intravascular thrombosis in the upper limbs and should not have severe hepatic or renal dysfunction, hemostatic disorder or coagulation dysfunction, or any cardiac disease that would interfere with participation. Additionally, the participant should not have any existing neurological or psychiatric disease that would confound the neurological or functional evaluations and should be available for follow-up for at least 3 months. The participant should not have a contraindication for RIC such as severe soft-tissue injury, fracture, or peripheral vascular disease in the upper limbs.

A 52-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with a solid tumor in his left kidney. He underwent a CT scan, which revealed a 4.5 cm mass in the kidney. The patient has no significant medical history, except for hypertension that is well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The urologist recommends an ultrasound-guided biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and determine the treatment plan. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial that will measure the pressure and stiffness inside the tumor using a Millar Mikro-tip catheter and shear wave elastography. The patient understands the study procedures and signs the informed consent form.

A 32-year-old female presents with chronic neck pain that has been bothering her for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the back of her neck and is described as a constant ache that increases with movement and palpation of the neck muscles. The patient reports no history of trauma or injury to the neck. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but the pain persists. The patient is able to read and fill out the informed consent form, and has no cognitive impairments. She has no history of psychological pathologies, such as depression or anxiety. The patient has not received any manual treatments for her neck pain in the past two months. She has not been recommended by a physician or anesthetist to receive any type of analgesic, anti-inflammatory or neuromodulator medication. She is not afraid of vertebral manipulation in the upper cervical area and tests negative for the Klein test and other integrity tests of the vertebral artery, cervical instability test, and Spurling test (foraminal compression test). The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of different techniques for suboccipital inhibition in chronic mechanical neck pain.

The patient is a 65 year old male with a history of coronary artery disease and has undergone two coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgeries in the past. He presents with recurrent chest pain despite optimal medical management and has been diagnosed with refractory angina. He reports experiencing chest pain at rest or with minimal exertion and is unable to perform daily activities without experiencing chest pain. He has tried multiple medications and has undergone several procedures including angioplasty and stenting, but his symptoms persist. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has two grown-up children who live in different states. He enjoys gardening and watching sports on TV. He reports feeling frustrated and limited by his symptoms and hopes to find relief through participation in the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old woman who is 36 weeks pregnant with a single fetus was scheduled for an elective caesarean delivery due to previous caesarean section. She has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA I. She does not have any history of heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, or pre-eclampsia. Her BMI is 29. She has no known allergies to medications and is not on any medications. She has a normal pregnancy with no complications. She has been informed about the study and has provided written and informed consent to participate.

56-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and a clinical diagnosis of diabetic nephropathy as described in the Family Investigation of Nephropathy and Diabetes Protocol, with a baseline creatinine clearance of >30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and proteinuria of ≥1.0 g/day. Blood pressure at baseline is <150/95 mm Hg and adequate hepatic function. The patient is currently taking ACE inhibitors and/or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), but dos

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease. She lives alone and has limited in-person social interactions due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The patient reports feeling isolated and lonely, and is interested in participating in a study that investigates the impact of social interaction through communication technologies on cognitive performance. She is fluent in English and has access to a computer and smart phone. The patient has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy and currently takes medication to manage her blood pressure. She has never been diagnosed with depression or any other neurological disorder, and her corrected vision is 20/20. The patient scored a 29 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and performed above 80% correct on the speech discrimination test from the Boston Diagnostic Aphasia Examination. She is enthusiastic about the study and willing to participate for the full duration of the intervention and control phases.

56 yo female with a history of smoking presents with a persistent cough and dyspnea. CT chest reveals a right hilar mass and biopsy confirms small cell lung cancer. She undergoes treatment with cisplatin and etoposide and achieves a partial response, but eventually develops progressive disease despite additional chemotherapy. Molecular testing reveals RICTOR gene amplification. The patient is currently asymptomatic and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. She has not participated in any other clinical trials with investigational products in the past 21 days and has not received any chemotherapy, biological therapy, radiation therapy, or other anticancer agents within 21 days. She has not undergone major surgery in the past 4 weeks and has no spinal cord compression or brain metastases. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and undergo treatment and scheduled visits and examinations.

45 y/o female diagnosed with stage 2 breast cancer, without any metastasis except for axillary nodes. She has agreed to participate in this study and receive Lymphoscintigraphy of upper extremity. She has no history of axillary lymph node resection. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have inflammatory breast cancer. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with twins. She is at 28 weeks of gestation and has been diagnosed with preterm labor. She has no significant medical history and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy until now. She is currently hospitalized and is being given medication to stop the contractions. The babies are both in breech position. The obstetrician has discussed the risks and benefits of delivery at this gestational age and the possibility of complications such as respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage, and sepsis. The patient has given informed consent for the trial and is willing to participate.

A 30-year-old software engineer who primarily works from home and has a good understanding of the English language is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is right-handed, has no history of cardiovascular disease, and is not taking any medications that affect cardiovascular function. The patient regularly uses a smartphone and has access to one for the duration of the study. He is motivated to participate and has the availability to participate in the study. There is no history of color blindness.

The patient is a 55-year-old Norwegian man diagnosed with prostate cancer. He is currently waiting for a radical prostatectomy at the University Hospital of North Norway. He has never smoked and has a BMI of 26. He works as an office manager and his physical activity is limited to occasional walking and light exercises due to his busy work schedule. He has no history of heart failure, angina pectoris, or respiratory disease limiting possible intervention. He is not using physical supportive devices to aid movement. He is living in the Tromso region and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial that involves moderate/high intensity aerobic exercise program for four to five weeks. He has given his informed consent to participate in this study.

A 24-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history and no known allergies to fruits, dairy or pectin. She is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant within 1 month of vaccination. She is not breastfeeding. She has not received any experimental vaccines or devices within the past 6 months nor is she currently enrolled in any other clinical trials. She does not have any chronic viral infections, demyelinating disease, significant renal disease, oxygen-dependent chronic lung disease, or insulin-treated diabetes mellitus. She is not taking oral or parenteral steroids, high-dose inhaled steroids, other immunosuppressive or cytotoxic drugs, or radiation therapy within six months prior to vaccination. She has not used OTC or other 'herbal' immune suppressant or stimulants within the 6 months prior to vaccination. She does not have a history of active neoplastic disease or hematologic malignancy in the past 5 years. She does not have any clinically significant structural abnormality of the nasopharynx or acute respiratory disease at the time of enrollment. She has not had a febrile illness with temperature greater than or equal to 38 degrees Celsius within 72 hours prior to enrollment. She does not have a history of drug abuse or alcohol abuse in the five years prior to enrollment.

A 28-year-old female presents with difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from a seated position. She has a history of muscle weakness and wasting, which has been gradually progressing over the past several years. Genetic testing revealed biallelic alterations in the FKRP gene, confirming a diagnosis of Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy 2I (LGMD2I). The patient is able to walk and run 10 meters but experiences significant fatigue and weakness after physical activity. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient expresses interest in participating in a clinical trial for LGMD2I and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study and meets all eligibility criteria, including adequate hepatic and renal function, normal iron content estimate on liver MRI, and ability to comply with the protocol instructions for the entire duration of the study. The patient has not undergone any major surgical procedures within the past 6 weeks and has no history of cognitive impairment or behavioral issues that would impede her ability to provide informed consent or follow study instructions. She has not received treatment with another investigational product within the past 30 days and has not undergone corticosteroid treatment within the past 3 months. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use highly effective methods of contraception during sexual activity for the duration of the study.

45-year-old female diagnosed with node-positive breast cancer requiring surgical intervention for primary tumor removal and axillary dissection. Sentinel lymph nodes tested positive during surgery. The patient has a BMI within the eligible range for the trial and does not require immediate breast reconstruction surgery. She is not receiving anticoagulation therapy or has any coagulation disorders. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is not on steroid therapy. The patient has not received chest radiotherapy and has not received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The patient is willing to sign an informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old healthy woman who is interested in participating in a dietary study to improve her overall health. She is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. She is a vegetarian and consumes a balanced diet, but she is interested in exploring the potential benefits of methionine and cysteine restriction. She is a full-time student and is currently maintaining a healthy weight with a BMI of 21 kg/m2. She does not take any medications or dietary supplements that could interfere with the study's biomarkers of interest. She has no known allergies to eggs, wheat, nuts, soy, or latex. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to gain insight into how dietary restriction can impact her overall health and longevity.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic hormone-resistant prostate cancer 2 years ago. He has undergone surgery and drug castration, and his testosterone levels have been consistently below 50 ng/dL. He has received two taxane-based chemotherapy regimens and has failed both due to radiological progression. He has also received novel endocrine therapy, including enzalutamide, apartamide, abitelone, and shr3680. He has experienced disease progression within the last 6 months, with a PSA level of 5 ng/mL and new bone metastases. The patient has adequate hepatic, renal, heart, and hematologic functions and is willing to comply with scheduled visits and laboratory tests. He has not received any prior MEK inhibitors, and he is willing to stop any other anti-tumor treatment during the trial period. He has no radiological confirmed tumor foci in the brain, severe bone injury caused by tumor bone metastasis, or history of epilepsy. His blood pressure is within the normal range, and he has no active heart disease. He is able to swallow and has no chronic diarrhea or intestinal obstruction. He has no history of retinopathy or glaucoma. He has no active HBV or HCV infection or history of immunodeficiency or organ transplantation. The patient is willing to take effective contraceptive measures during the whole study period and within 6 months after the last administration.

A 22-year-old woman with no history of pneumococcal vaccination has volunteered for a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a multivalent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. She is a healthy individual with no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only occasionally. She is sexually active and uses a hormonal contraceptive method to prevent pregnancy. She has no known allergies to vaccines or any other medications. She has not received any vaccinations containing diphtheria, pertussis, or tetanus in the past year and has no plans to receive any during the study period. She has undergone a thorough medical history review, physical examination, and laboratory screening, and has been deemed eligible for the study by the investigator. She has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 32-year-old female with a history of schizophrenia presents with persistent symptoms despite being on antipsychotic medication for the past 8 weeks. She has been diagnosed based on DSM-V criteria and has a PANSS score of 85 with a score of 5 on the delusions and unusual thought content items. Her Clinical Global Impression-Severity score is 4. She is fluent in English and has provided written informed consent. She has no history of renal insufficiency, congestive heart failure, cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction, liver cirrhosis, guanidinoacetate methyltransferase deficiency or herpes. She is not on any medication that affects NO-mediated vaso-relaxation, and she is not on any antihypertensive, antidiabetes or anticoagulant/antiplatelet medications. She has not taken any investigational drug or participated in any clinical trial in the past 30 days. She has not been diagnosed with alcohol or substance use disorder in the past 3 months and tested negative for urine drug screen. She does not have any known history of phenylketonuria or hypersensitivity reactions to L-arginine and/or BH4. She is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and restrictions.

A 35-year-old male with a history of food impaction and dysphagia presents to the gastroenterologist's office for evaluation. He reports difficulty swallowing solid foods and has experienced frequent episodes of food getting stuck in his throat. He has tried over-the-counter antacids and proton pump inhibitors without relief. Endoscopy with biopsy has been recommended to evaluate for Eosinophilic Esophagitis, a condition he has never been diagnosed with before. The patient is able to swallow pills and capsules and provides informed consent for participation in the SECM capsule validation study.

45 y/o female with a history of symptomatic gallstones and referred for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy by her GP. She has been experiencing right upper quadrant abdominal pain for the past 6 months, which is associated with nausea and vomiting. The patient also reports bloating and belching after meals, which has been affecting her quality of life. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. The patient is able to read and communicate in English without the presence of a translator and has access to a computer, tablet, or multimedia phone. She is willing to engage with the multimedia process and is interested in learning more about her condition and the necessary surgery.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of smoking presents with a diagnosis of Stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx. He underwent a radical neck surgery, which involved the removal of multiple lymph nodes, and he was found to have microscopic positive tumor cell margins. He has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The patient's performance status is 80 on the Karnofsky Performance Score. He has provided written informed consent and is able to communicate effectively with the investigator. The patient has no other malignancies and has not participated in a clinical trial with another investigational drug or treatment in the past 30 days. The patient's platelet count and prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time are within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to utilize a medically acceptable method of contraception.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. He has a history of smoking, and his BMI is 32. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high, with a mean sitting systolic blood pressure (msSBP) of 165 mmHg. He has been prescribed a low-dose diuretic and an ACE inhibitor, but his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. He is also taking metformin for his glucose intolerance, and his fasting glucose levels have been fluctuating between 102 and 120 mg/dL. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. His waist circumference is 105 cm, and his HDL-cholesterol levels are 38 mg/dL. His triglyceride levels are 170 mg/dL. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate new treatment options for his condition.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with malignant melanoma. She underwent a biopsy that revealed a Breslow score of 1.5 mm and the presence of ulceration. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not undergone any previous chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or surgery to the lymph nodes of interest. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the accuracy of lymph node identification in skin malignancy cases. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 40-year-old premenopausal female with a BMI of 32 and a waist circumference of 97 cm is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating the effects of dietary fatty acids on inflammation in obesity. She is currently not pregnant, lactating, or taking any birth control medication. Her fasting LDL-cholesterol and triglyceride levels are within the acceptable range, and she does not have any chronic medical conditions or surgical procedures for cardiovascular, renal, liver, rheumatoid arthritis or immune disorders, or cancer in the last 5 years. She does not have any neurological or gastrointestinal disorders, and has not undergone any gastrointestinal or bariatric surgeries, liposuction, or experienced migraines. She does not smoke, consume more than 15 alcoholic beverages per week, or take medications for inflammation, pain, or blood glucose management. She is willing to maintain a stable level of activity and refrain from consuming omega-3 supplements, omega-3 rich foods, and anti-inflammatory natural health products during the study. She is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and procedures and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer after an elevated PSA level was detected during a routine check-up. The biopsy confirmed the presence of localized prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 6. The patient has declined alternative treatment options and has opted to undergo High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for focal ablation of prostate tissue as his standard of care treatment method. His PSA level is 12 ng/mL, and his prostate volume is 50 cc. He is able to tolerate general anesthesia and has no medical contraindications for follow-up mpMRI or prostate biopsy. He is willing to complete informed consent forms and participate in this observational study.

A 28-year-old male who sustained a T10 complete spinal cord injury (SCI) 2 years ago during a motocross accident is interested in participating in the study. He uses a manual wheelchair as his primary means of mobility and has difficulty with daily activities such as transfers, pushing over uneven terrain, and negotiating curbs. He is currently employed as a software engineer and wants to improve his wheelchair skills to be more independent at work and in his personal life. He has no cognitive impairment and is highly motivated to participate in the study.

The patient is a pregnant female between the ages of 18 and 45 who has had a previous preterm birth due to spontaneous preterm labor or preterm premature rupture of membranes between 16 0/7 and 36 6/7 weeks gestation. She must be less than 22 weeks pregnant at the time of enrollment. The patient must have a singleton gestation and not have any known fetal anomalies or chromosomal anomalies that may affect gestational age at delivery. The patient must be able to give informed consent and undergo all study procedures, including a single seven-day pharmacokinetic study, which requires daily venipunctures and answering questions about side effects and discomfort at each study visit. She must not have a malformation of the uterus, medical or obstetrical complications that may affect gestational age at delivery, or a history of thrombosis or thromboembolic disorders. She must also not have known or suspected breast cancer, other hormone-sensitive cancer, or a history of these conditions. The patient must not have moderately severe depression with a PHQ-9 score of ≥15, EPDS score of >13, or suicidal ideation.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy with special needs who is currently not using any form of augmentative alternative communication (AAC). He has difficulty communicating with others and is often frustrated when he cannot express his needs and wants. He attends the Step to Learn School, where he participates in group activities with other children. His parents report that he has been making slow progress in his communication skills and are interested in exploring AAC options for him. He has no other co-morbid conditions. A pre-assessment will be conducted to establish his baseline communication skills, and he will be enrolled in the AAC intervention program for 6 weeks, attending 3 days a week. The intervention will include the use of objects, picture cards, and choice boards to help him make choices during group activities. The aim of the study is to determine the efficacy of AAC in improving functional communication in group activities for children like him who are not currently using any AAC options.

The patient is a 35 year old woman presenting with chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain and bloating for the past 6 months. She has previously been diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea subtype (IBS-D) and has tried various medications with no significant improvement. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a Chinese Medicine JCM-16021 for IBS-D. She is willing to provide written informed consent and meet the inclusion criteria of the trial. She has no history of constipation-predominant, mixed or unsubtyped IBS, severe diseases on heart, liver and kidney, hematology or cancer which is diagnosed by traditional Chinese medicines, medical history of organic gastrointestinal diseases or systemic diseases which could affect gastrointestinal motility diagnosed by traditional Chinese medicines, or current concomitant medication with effects on gastrointestinal function. She has not had abdominal surgery, drug or food allergies, is not pregnant or breast-feeding, does not have any medical history of neurological diseases or psychiatric disorders and is not currently participating in another clinical trial. She has not taken IBS treatment drugs within the past week.

A 29-year-old woman was diagnosed with Crohn's disease six months ago after experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. Her diagnosis was confirmed by a colonoscopy and she was started on a treatment regimen by her gastroenterologist. Despite treatment, her symptoms have persisted and she has been experiencing frequent flare-ups. She is currently seeking alternative therapies and has been referred to participate in a clinical trial for QBECO induction treatment. She is generally healthy with no known allergies or medical conditions, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She understands the study requirements and is willing to practice effective contraception if necessary. She has not undergone any major surgical interventions for Crohn's disease and has not been previously treated with any Qu Biologics' Site Specific Immunomodulators (SSIs).

A 58-year-old female with a history of knee pain for the past two years, which has worsened in the last six months. She reports pain in both knees, which is present most of the time and increases during physical activity. She has difficulty with activities of daily living such as going up and down stairs, walking long distances, and standing for prolonged periods. She is obese with a BMI of 35 and has been struggling with weight management for the last five years. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She works full-time as a nurse and has three children. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She reports a history of knee injections six months ago, which provided temporary relief. She has not undergone any knee surgeries. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help manage her knee pain and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cancer and is undergoing chemotherapy. She is experiencing significant weight loss and has a MUST score of 2. She reports feeling weak and fatigued, and has difficulty eating due to nausea and vomiting. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She reports no known allergies or intolerances to any foods. The patient has been prescribed oral nutritional supplements in the past, but has had difficulty tolerating the taste and texture of the products. She is interested in trying the new supplement, 'CARDIFF', to see if it is more tolerable and acceptable for her. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with rumination syndrome. She experiences discomfort in the stomach during and immediately after meals, which is causing her to regurgitate undigested or partially digested food from the stomach and rechew it. She is not currently on any medication that may affect vagal tone or gastrointestinal motility, and has never performed diaphragmatic breathing (DiaB) as a therapy for rumination syndrome. The patient has no other major comorbidities, no history of GI surgeries apart from appendectomy, and no known allergies to ECG electrodes or latex. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study requirements.

A 62-year-old male patient who underwent surgery for a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm is admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) postoperatively. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20 pack-year smoking history. The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. His expected length of ICU stay is more than five days, and his expected survival is more than seven days. He has no contraindications to enteral nutrition (EN) and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has a nasogastric tube in place, and EN is started within the first 24 hours of admission. On the third day of admission, the patient's energy intake is less than 60% of predicted energy needs despite adequate EN. The patient is randomized into either the "Control group" (EN alone) or the "SPN group" (EN + PN) to reach 100% of their predicted energy needs. Tight glycemic control will be achieved according to local practice by insulin administration. The primary outcome is to determine if the combined administration of SPN and EN will reduce the rate of nosocomial infections (CDC criteria) in ICU patients. The secondary outcomes are to determine the duration of mechanical ventilation, the length of ICU and hospital stay, antibiotic-free days, ICU complications (extra-renal epuration, neurological, cardiac and respiratory complications), energy and protein balance, and 28 days clinical outcome.

Patient A is a 28-year-old male who lost both hands in a traumatic accident. He has undergone extensive rehabilitation but still faces difficulty in performing basic daily activities. He is right-handed, and the loss of his dominant hand has had a significant impact on his quality of life, including his ability to work and take care of himself. He has been evaluated by the University of Michigan interdisciplinary evaluation team and has been deemed appropriate for listing for hand transplantation. He is currently taking pain medication for residual pain in his upper limbs and is willing to participate in the study to track his experience from pre-operative care through surgery and post-operative care. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the procedure and has provided informed consent.

A 30 yo F with a BMI of 24.5, presenting with irregular menstrual cycles, acne, and hirsutism. She has previously been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and has not made any significant changes to her diet or exercise routine in the past 6 months. She does not take any oral contraceptives and has not used any weight-loss medications. Her labs show elevated levels of free testosterone and normal fasting blood glucose, liver and kidney function, TSH and FT4 levels, and serum prolactin. She typically wakes up between 6:00 am and 7:00 am and goes to sleep between 10:00 pm and 11:00 pm. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medication. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of two isocaloric diets with different meal timing distribution on insulin resistance and hyperandrogenism in lean PCOS women.

10 year-old boy who has a history of seasonal allergies with hay fever symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and throat, and nasal congestion during the peak of the grass pollen season. He experiences these symptoms every year, typically starting in late spring and lasting through the summer months. He also reports occasional wheezing and chest tightness, which are mild and usually relieved with over-the-counter allergy medication. He has not been formally diagnosed with asthma, but his parents report that he sometimes has trouble breathing during exercise or when he has a cold. The patient has been tested and shown to be sensitized to grass pollen. He has no other known allergies and is otherwise healthy. The patient will be monitored for changes in exhaled breath temperature during the pollen season and will be randomized to receive either grass-pollen sublingual immunotherapy or a placebo control.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl with obesity diagnosed a year ago. She presents with a history of abdominal pain, nausea, and fatigue. Blood tests show elevated liver enzymes. An ultrasound reveals the presence of fatty liver disease. She has no history of alcohol consumption or other chronic liver diseases. Her past medical history is non-significant. Her family history is significant for obesity in her mother and diabetes in her grandfather. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will use a non-invasive imaging technique to diagnose and assess the degree of fibrosis in her liver.

A 35-year-old woman presents to the dermatology clinic with a complaint of hyperpigmentation on her cheeks and forehead for the past 6 months. She reports that the hyperpigmentation worsens with sun exposure and has tried various over-the-counter creams with no improvement. The patient denies any previous history of skin diseases or surgeries. She has no allergies, and her past medical history is unremarkable. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. On examination, the dermatologist notices brownish macules on both cheeks and forehead. The rest of the skin examination is unremarkable. The dermatologist makes a diagnosis of melasma and explains the study to the patient. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and agrees to participate in the pilot study.

A 22-year-old female presents with no history of shoulder pain or discomfort within the past 6 months. She has no previous diagnosis of any shoulder or upper extremity condition. She is a right-handed individual and has no history of traumatic injury to her upper extremities. She has never received any shoulder injection or surgery. She has no known history of rheumatoid arthritis or autoimmune disease. She is willing to participate in the study to help establish the reference norm of spatial frequency analysis parameters in those without obvious tendon degeneration or injury. She understands that she will undergo bilateral shoulder ultrasound imaging and that the study aims to investigate the differences in spatial frequency analysis parameters between different age groups and different equipment. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

An 80-year-old retired teacher, who lives alone, has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past few months. She feels lonely and isolated, and finds it difficult to engage in activities that used to bring her joy. She has no history of depression, but she has a family history of mental health disorders. She has not sought treatment for her symptoms before. She has no cognitive impairment or serious loss of sight or hearing. She is not taking any antidepressant medication or participating in any other therapeutic project or individual psychotherapy. She has no substance abuse history. She is able to use virtual reality technology and has no contraindications for virtual therapy.

45-year-old male with a medical history of hemophilia B, with a history of recurrent elbow bleeds and limited range of motion (ROM) of the right elbow joint. The patient reports frequent episodes of elbow pain, especially during activities that require the use of the affected arm. He has been receiving prophylactic factor IX concentrate infusions for the past 10 years to prevent bleeding episodes. Despite this, he still experiences pain and stiffness in the right elbow joint. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of physiotherapy in the hemophilic arthropathy of the elbow. He is willing to commit to the required treatment sessions and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

This clinical trial is seeking young, healthy volunteers who are willing to participate and have no history of skin disease or damage on the measurement sites. Participants must not have used corticosteroids or immunomodulators in the month prior to the trial or during the trial, and must not have used emollients for at least three days prior to the trial. Exposure to artificial UV radiation, pregnancy, and lactation are also exclusion criteria. All participants must provide written informed consent and be willing to adhere to the trial protocol.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who has been struggling with depression for the past 5 years. He has tried multiple antidepressant medications and has undergone talk therapy without much success. He feels hopeless, lacks energy, and has difficulty sleeping. He is not currently taking any medications for his depression. He is an engineer by profession and is married with two children. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. Lab study is reported bellow: Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 8000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 20 U/L ALT: 18 U/L Alk P: 48 U/L Bill total: 0.5 mg/dl Na: 138 mEq/l K: 4.1 mEq/l Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl ESR: 15 mm/hr. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores new treatments for depression. He is willing to undergo regular ketamine treatments and follow the protocol as an outpatient. He is willing to sign the informed consent document and is using a medically accepted means of contraception.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently hospitalized for heart failure. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes. He was diagnosed with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and is classified as NYHA class III. He has been discharged and is receiving home health care services. He is able to stand on a scale and his weight is within the range of 100 to 500 lbs. He has a working landline phone at his residence and is able to hear and see. He does not have severe ischemic heart disease, MI, or CABG in the last 6 weeks. He also does not have severe uncorrected valvular disease, home inotropic therapy, severe lung disease, active cancer, uncorrected thyroid disease, AIDS, or end-stage renal disease on dialysis. He is eligible for the trial and may be randomly assigned to either the telemonitoring or usual care group.

This study does not involve patient recruitment or intervention. The study will be conducted using human lower lid skin and lashes derived from lateral tarsal strip dissected routinely in ectropion repair surgery. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions required for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 78-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest discomfort for the past several months. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She also has a history of smoking, having smoked a pack a day for over 30 years before quitting 15 years ago. She has been under the care of a cardiologist for several years and has been diagnosed with severe symptomatic degenerative aortic valve stenosis. She has been evaluated by a multidisciplinary team and has been deemed a high-risk candidate for open surgical aortic valve replacement due to her age, co-morbidities, and frailty. She has been selected as a suitable candidate for TAVI with the JenaValve according to the instructions for use. Her echocardiogram shows a mean aortic gradient of 40 mmHg, an aortic valve area of 0.7 cm², and an ejection fraction of 50%. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary hypercholesterolemia. She reports a family history of high cholesterol and is currently taking atorvastatin 20mg daily. Her LDL-C levels are between 130 and 190 mg/L, which places her in Category I for this study. She has no history of coronary heart disease or diabetes. Her BMI is 25, and she exercises regularly. She is compliant with her current medication and has no other medical conditions that could interfere with her participation in the study. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the co-administration of MK0524B will further improve her lipid levels.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) based on American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria 1997 with at least 4 criteria documented, one of which is a positive anti-dsDNA antibody or a positive antinuclear antibody (ANA). She has been diagnosed with Lupus Nephritis Class III or IV (International Society of Nephrology (ISN)/Renal Pathology Society (RPS)-2003 classification) with active or active/chronic disease, co-existing class V is permitted, proven by renal biopsy within 3 months prior to screening or during screening if induction therapy has not yet been started. She has proteinuria of at least 1.0 g/day [(Uprot/Ucrea) ≥ 1]. The patient is willing to use two reliable methods of birth control, one of which is highly effective as assessed by the investigator. She has not received induction therapy for Lupus Nephritis within the last 6 months prior to randomization except induction with Mycophenolate Mofetil and high dose steroids started within 6 weeks prior to randomization. She has not been treated with any biologic B-cell depleting therapy (e.g. anti-CD20, anti-CD22,) within 12 months prior to randomization, abatacept within 12 months prior to randomization, tacrolimus or cyclosporin within 4 weeks prior to randomization, cyclophosphamide within 6 months prior to randomization, or any investigational drug within 6 months or 5 half-lives, whichever is greater before randomization. She does not have chronic or relevant acute infections, including but not limited to HIV, Hepatitis B and C and tuberculosis, active or suspected malignancy or history of documented malignancy within the last 5 years before screening, except appropriately treated carcinoma in situ and treated basal cell carcinoma. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant while in the trial. She has normal hepatic function, defined as serum Aspartate Transferase/Alanine Transferase, bilirubin or alkaline phosphatase levels ≤ 2 x Upper Limit of Normal. Further eligibility criteria apply.

We are looking for individuals who have been diagnosed with prediabetes and have a BMI of 25-34. You must have a cellphone to participate in the study. You cannot have fasting blood glucose levels ≥ 126 at the beginning of the intervention, terminal chronic diseases, major cardiovascular problems such as angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, or cerebrovascular accident, severe psychiatric pathology, or any other pathology that can be a contraindication to participate in the program. Pregnant women and individuals belonging to the private health system (called ISAPRE) are excluded from this study. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a multi-component remote care model (telephone-based) to modify unhealthy eating practices and increase physical activity in adults who have prediabetes and are over-weight/obese. The intervention will last 6 months, and the counseling intervention is the core of the multi-component tele-care model, which also includes counseling-through text messages, supply of Educational material, and self-monitoring equipment (pedometers and measuring tape for patients to check their waist circumference). If you meet the eligibility criteria and are interested in participating in this study, please contact us to learn more about the study and how to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). He has been on optimized medical therapy for COPD for the past 6 months. He reports experiencing breathlessness, leg discomfort, and reduced exercise capacity, which has led to a decrease in daily physical activity levels. The patient has a history of anxiety and depression, with a Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) score of 10. He is interested in improving his physical activity levels and quality of life. The patient does not have any orthopaedic or neurological conditions that significantly impair normal biomechanical movement patterns. He has not experienced a moderate or severe COPD exacerbation or myocardial infarction within the past 6 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 35-year-old male, working as an accountant, has been a daily smoker for the past 10 years, smoking approximately 10-15 cigarettes per day. He has attempted to quit smoking several times in the past, but has not been successful. He has access to the internet and regularly checks his email. He lives in the United States and is comfortable taking surveys in English. He does not currently use any pharmacotherapy, quitline, or quit smoking program or support group for smoking cessation. He has not participated in any research study about smoking cigarettes or using other tobacco products in the last 3 months. He is willing to complete three 20-minute surveys during the study and able to complete surveys in the morning for 15 days.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a family history of breast cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 45 and her grandmother also had breast cancer. She is concerned about her own risk and is interested in participating in studies focused on inherited cancer predisposition. She is able and willing to provide informed consent and wishes to learn more about the ICARE registry. She has no personal history of cancer but wants to take proactive steps to manage her risk. She is currently in good health and has no significant medical history. She is willing to complete questionnaires and provide medical records/tumor releases as applicable. She prefers to receive correspondence through email.

A 54-year-old Caucasian man who has been experiencing neck and arm pain due to cervical radiculopathy for the past 3 months is recommended to undergo a cervical epidural block. He has tried pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain is still persistent. He has no history of allergy to local anesthetics, contrast dye, or steroids, and is not taking any anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication. He does not have any infections or neurological or psychiatric disorders. He has not undergone any prior spine instrumentation. He is married and works as an accountant. He exercises regularly and does not smoke or drink alcohol. His past medical history is unremarkable. His family history is negative for any spine-related problems. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 52-year-old office worker was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes four years ago. He is married and has two children. He has a sedentary lifestyle and admits to not exercising regularly. His BMI is 32 kg/m2. He is currently taking Metformin 1000 mg twice a day and Gliclazide 80 mg once a day. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. He has no history of cancer or end-stage liver or renal disease. He has not taken any GLP-1 or DPP-IV inhibitors in the past. He has been referred to a primary care center in Sweden for treatment with liraglutide or sitagliptin. He is willing to participate in a retrospective database assessment of clinical effectiveness study to evaluate the efficacy of liraglutide in treating his type 2 diabetes.

Pt is a 25yo F with a 3-year history of seasonal allergic rhinitis to grass pollen. She reports symptoms of sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes during the pollen season. She has never received immunotherapy for her allergies and is not currently taking any medications for her symptoms. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses contraception. She is willing to adhere to the visit schedules and follow the study protocols. She does not have any purulent secretions in her nasal cavity, and her septum is normal. She does not have asthma and does not suffer from claustrophobia. She is interested in participating in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 25-year-old female who works as a nurse is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is generally in good health, with no known medical conditions or allergies. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. In her latest physical exam, her blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg, and her heart rate was 80 bpm. Her laboratory tests showed no abnormalities in hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic or psychiatric functions. She has not had any surgeries, including gastrectomy, and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the importance of following the instructions provided by the researchers.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who sustained a traumatic injury to his right arm in a motor vehicle accident. He was brought to the emergency department with a fractured humerus and required immediate surgery. During the surgery, the orthopaedic surgeon used Vivigen Cellular Bone Matrix allograft as a bone graft substitute to promote bone healing and fusion. The patient will be followed up at hospital discharge, 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months, and 24 months after treatment to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the bone graft. The patient is fluent in both English and Spanish and is able to provide informed consent for the study. He does not have any history of dementia or mental/psychiatric diagnoses that would preclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with both hepatitis B and C virus infection. He has been seropositive for HCV antibody and HBsAg for more than 6 months and has positive serum HCV RNA. His HBeAg test came back negative, and his serum ALT levels are between 1-10-fold of the upper limit of normal (ULN). He has never received treatment for hepatitis B or C in the past. He does not have any signs of decompensated liver disease and has a Child-Pugh score of less than 7. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any other known diseases that would make him unsuitable for Peg-IFN therapy.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring hemodialysis for the past 5 years. He reports compliance with his medication regimen, including phosphate binders, but has been struggling to maintain serum phosphorus levels within the target range. His most recent laboratory data within the past month showed a serum phosphorus level of 5.2 mg/dL. He denies any new medical problems or changes in his diet or medication regimen. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of niacinamide in reducing serum phosphorus levels. He understands the trial involves taking either niacinamide or a placebo for a period of 21 weeks, with weekly monitoring of his phosphorus levels. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is capable of giving informed consent.

A 40-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 4 years ago is currently taking combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) for the past 2 years. He has a CD4+ T-cell count of 550/µL at screening. He is currently employed as a software engineer and lives alone. He has a history of smoking 1 pack per day for the past 10 years, but he quit smoking 1 year ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally, but not in excessive amounts. He has no history of drug abuse. He has no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and able to give informed consent. He is currently not taking any immune therapy or immunosuppressant medication. He has not used any antibiotics within the last 2 weeks prior to randomization. He has no known HBV or HCV infection. He is not currently experiencing any acute bacterial infection or undiagnosed febrile condition. He is willing and able to use barrier contraception during sexual intercourse for the entire study period.

We are seeking children and adolescents who have been diagnosed with acute liver failure or chronic liver disease or those who have undergone a liver transplant for this clinical trial. Patients must be stable to participate in the study. Liver disease in childhood and adolescence can present as chronic liver disease (CLD) or acute liver failure (ALF), with different interim stages, and with the possibility of a presentation with acute on chronic liver failure as well. This study aims to provide clinicians with better diagnostic tools for assessing liver function in these patients, in order to determine the optimal timing for potential liver transplantation and differentiate those who may recover without a transplant. The study will involve a variety of diagnostic tests, including imaging, blood and urine sample collection, and analysis of the microbiota. We hope that this study will help clinicians more accurately diagnose and predict outcomes for children and adolescents with liver disease.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who sustained a 30% total body surface area burn injury from a house fire. She was admitted to the hospital within 2 hours after the injury occurred. She has a history of asthma and is a non-smoker. She has no other chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She weighs 70 kg and is 5'6'' tall. The vital signs on admission were as follows: BP 110/70, HR 90 bpm, RR 18/min, and temperature 98.6°F. The initial laboratory workup showed a hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, a white blood cell count of 10,000/mL, and a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL. The burn injury is located on her chest, abdomen, back, and both arms. She is conscious and alert, and able to provide informed consent. She is willing to participate in the study and is expected to require intravenous fluid resuscitation for at least 24 hours after injury.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer. The cancer has metastasized to her lungs and liver, and she has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient's cancer has progressed despite these treatments, and she is now considered to have relapsed or refractory advanced tumors. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has no concurrent hematological malignancies. The patient is willing and able to practice contraceptive methods. She has adequate bone marrow reserve, renal, and hepatic function. She is not currently receiving any other anticancer therapy, aside from supportive care. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore potential new treatment options for her cancer.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) two years ago. He has been taking coumarin derivates to manage his condition, with a target INR between 2.0 and 3.0. He has experienced recurrent episodes of AF despite multiple antiarrhythmic medications. His CHA2DS2-VASc score is 2, indicating a moderate risk of stroke. He has no history of ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. He has never undergone pulmonary vein ablation. His left atrial size is within normal limits (44 mm), and his ejection fraction is 55%. He has no contraindications for anticoagulation therapy, diffusion-weighted MRI, or transesophageal echocardiography. He has no implanted cardiovascular devices or valvular heart disease. He has no history of acute coronary syndrome or heart failure. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and participate in neurocognitive assessments. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he does not plan to become pregnant during the study. He has no limitations to contractual capability and is not participating in any other study.

A 30-year-old female with a 2-year history of myofascial pain syndrome (MAS) is seeking treatment options. She experiences muscle spasm, tenderness, limited range of motion, stiffness, fatigue and accompanying pain caused by trigger points in the tense bands formed in the muscles. She has no history of cervical disc hernia, radiculopathy, myelopathy, tumoral, infectious, psychiatric, systemic disease or bleeding diathesis. She does not have stage 3-4 osteodegeneration or kyphoscoliosis. She has not been diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome and is not pregnant. She has not had previous brain, neck or shoulder surgery, and has not received treatment for MAS in the last 6 months. The onset of her symptoms is more than 3 months ago and she has not used analgesics for any reason. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of dry needling and balneotherapy for the treatment of MAS.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who has been referred for abdominal MRI. He has a history of asthma, but it is well controlled with albuterol and fluticasone inhalers. He does not have any cardiac, hepatic, or renal pathology. He has no known allergies or contraindications to MRI. His BMI is within normal limits. He is enrolled in a social security plan and has signed an informed consent form. He has undergone a preliminary medical examination, and there were no significant findings. He does not have any implantable devices or metallic foreign bodies in his body. He is not claustrophobic, and he is not morbidly obese. He is not pregnant, and there is no risk of pregnancy. He is not under any measure of legal protection.

67-year-old female with a 2-year history of memory impairment and difficulty with spatial orientation was referred to a neurologist for further evaluation. The patient reports that she gets lost easily when driving and has difficulty remembering appointments, conversations, and recent events. She has a family history of Alzheimer's disease (AD) with her father having been diagnosed with AD in his 70s. The patient denies any history of stroke, head trauma, or psychiatric illness. She has mild hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. On examination, the patient has mild impairment in attention, calculation, and recall of recent events. Her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 24/30. She has no signs of depression or anxiety. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed mild atrophy, but no evidence of stroke or significant white matter disease. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed elevated amyloid-beta levels consistent with the presence of amyloid pathology. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) three years ago. He has undergone surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy but continues to experience recurrence of the tumor. The patient is currently experiencing headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty speaking. He presents to the clinic for evaluation and possible enrollment in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerated dose of transiently opening the blood-brain barrier (BBB) using the NaviFUS system. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2, a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) of 80, and normal hepatic, renal, coagulation, and hematopoietic function. He has been on a stable dose of steroids for 10 days prior to screening. The patient has not received any investigational drugs or participated in a research study within the past month. The ROI for FUS exposure is located close to the cortex with at least 20 mm distance beneath the skull bone and the ROI is not in the deep center brain with crucial brain functions. The patient has no history of arteriovenous malformation (AVM) or cerebral aneurysm. He is not currently using any recreational drugs or has a history of drug addiction. The patient is not pregnant or breast-feeding. He does not have any known sensitivity/allergy to MRI contrast agents, CT contrast agents, SonoVue®, or any of its components. His baseline findings are normal and he does not have hemorrhage or cyst within the ROI.

An 80-year-old male patient was admitted to Saint Marys Hospital at Mayo Clinic following a car accident. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He has not experienced any urinary tract infections in the past year. The patient does not have any known allergies. On admission, he complains of pain in his right leg, and a CT scan reveals a fracture of the right femur. The patient is being treated with pain medication and has undergone surgery for his fracture. He is currently bedridden and requires a urinary catheter for bladder drainage. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo additional testing for detecting subclinical UTIs.

This clinical trial is not looking for patients, but rather participants who have had a stroke and healthy controls. However, if we were to generate a description for a potential participant with a history of stroke, they would need to meet the following criteria:  - They have had a stroke resulting in hemiplegia  - They are currently a patient at UZ Pellenberg  - They have a Functional Ambulation Category score of two or less  - They are able to sit independently for two minutes  - They are able to understand and follow simple instructions  - They do not have any musculoskeletal or neurological disorders that could interfere with the protocol  - They do not have severe communication, memory, or language disorders that could impact their ability to understand the research protocol  - They have provided signed informed consent.

The patient is a 59-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (PD) six years ago. He has been experiencing difficulty swallowing for the past year, including coughing and choking while eating and drinking. He has also noticed some changes to his voice, which has become hoarse and strained. He has been referred to participate in a clinical trial that aims to assess laryngopharyngeal function in patients with PD, multiple system atrophy (MSA), and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and related 4repeat tauopathies. The study will involve a flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES) while performing a structured task protocol, and if available, laryngeal electromyography (EMG) results will also be recorded. Along with the examination results, demographic and disease-specific data will be collected, and two questionnaires, the Swallowing Disturbance Questionnaire for Parkinson's Disease (SDQ-PD) and the swallowing specific Quality Of Life Questionnaire (SWALQOL), will be administered. The patient is within Hoehn and Yahr Stage I-V and is eligible for the trial.

A 28-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history and no current medications is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is surgically sterile and willing to comply with scheduled visits and confinement. She has not experienced any febrile illness within the past 5 days and has tested negative for any illicit drugs. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days.

A 32-year-old female patient who has been experiencing mild to moderate depression symptoms for the past 3 months is looking for alternative treatment options. She has never been diagnosed with depression before and has no family history of mental health disorders. She works as a graphic designer and has been feeling overwhelmed and fatigued lately, with a lack of motivation and interest in her work. She has been experiencing trouble sleeping, difficulty concentrating, and a loss of appetite. She has tried therapy in the past but has not found it effective. She is currently not taking any medication for depression. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to take the Phytostandard® Rhodiola-Saffron supplementation for 6 weeks. She has read and understood the eligibility criteria and has no history of severe depression, suicidal tendencies, or other psychiatric disorders. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not taking any medication that may interfere with the treatment. She is motivated to find relief from her symptoms and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

32 yo male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 2 years ago during routine screening. He was not symptomatic at the time of diagnosis and was referred to an infectious disease specialist for further management. His CD4 count was 650 cells/mm3 and his viral load was 12,000 copies/mL at the time of diagnosis. He has never been on antiretroviral therapy and has not used chronic anti-HSV therapy for the past 6 months. He is currently asymptomatic and has been compliant with his regular follow-up appointments. His most recent CD4 count was 800 cells/mm3 and his viral load was 20,000 copies/mL. He has been counseled regarding the importance of adherence to regular follow-up visits and safe sex practices. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to delay the need for initiating HAART among HIV infected individuals who neither use nor require HAART, and who have not used chronic suppressive anti-HSV therapy for at least the 6 months prior to study initiation. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

45 yo F with a history of chronic shoulder pain and limited range of motion for the past 6 months. MRI revealed a small full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon, less than 3cm in the anteroposterior dimension, unresponsive to conservative therapy for >3 months. The patient has no previous history of rotator cuff repair surgery, preoperative stiffness, subscapularis tear, neurologic disorder affecting the ipsilateral upper extremity, cervical pathology, or arthritis. The patient is English-speaking and able to understand consent. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different postoperative immobilization methods - abduction shoulder brace versus simple arm sling - following rotator cuff repair surgery.

A 47-year-old woman diagnosed with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer in 2018. She has no family history of breast cancer, and she is a nonsmoker. She underwent lumpectomy with axillary lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She achieved complete remission for 1 year before disease recurrence in the liver, lungs, and bones. She received first-line treatment with letrozole combined with palbociclib and achieved partial remission for 12 months. The patient experienced disease progression with new liver metastasis confirmed by biopsy. The patient received second-line treatment with a combination of fulvestrant and ribociclib for 8 months before experiencing disease progression. The patient has no significant medical comorbidities and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her complete medical history is available, and she meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

An 68-year-old woman presents with mild cognitive impairment, as assessed by a MMSE score of 24. She lives alone in her own apartment and has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She has an informal caregiver, her daughter, who visits her daily to assist with daily activities. She takes medications as prescribed and is able to manage her own medication use. She has good eyesight and has no known physical limitations that would prevent her from using the TV-AssistDem platform. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has provided written consent. She has not been diagnosed with depression and scores below 11 on the Geriatric Depression Scale.

5 year-old girl with cerebral palsy who is non-ambulatory (GMFCS-E&R IV) and has limited opportunities for structured physical activity due to her mobility impairments. She is otherwise healthy with no other neurological, metabolic, or orthopedic disabilities, asthma, heart disease, or cognitive impairments. Her parents are interested in finding ways to improve her health and well-being through exercise and have consented to her participation in this clinical trial. She will be using the robotic medical device Innowalk to participate in tailored training programs of either high intensity interval training (HIIT) or steady state training (SST) for 16 weeks, with a washout period in between, and her physiological responses will be monitored through indirect calorimetry and blood samples. Additionally, her adherence to the exercise program and factors that facilitate or hinder her participation will be studied through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews with her and her family. The goal is to develop an improved individualized exercise program that will increase her health and well-being, and ultimately decrease the use of medications and healthcare.

A 63-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with a history of a minor head injury. He had no loss of consciousness and no neurological symptoms at the time of the injury. However, he started experiencing headaches, dizziness, and nausea a few days later. A CT scan of the head was performed which revealed the presence of a chronic subdural hematoma. The patient was scheduled for surgery to remove the hematoma. He has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. The patient is able to have a normal conversation and has a Glasgow Coma Scale (Verbal Response) score of 5. He has been informed about the study and has signed a written informed consent. The patient has no shunt or other foreign object implanted in the brain. He is not participating in any other clinical study that could interfere with the results of this study.

This clinical trial is not recruiting patients, as it is focused on analyzing existing samples and data from a subset of 494 men and women from 4 European countries (Germany, Greece, Italy and France) who participated in the European Prospective Investigation on Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC) Calibration Study. The study is looking for healthy adults between the ages of 30 and 70 who have donated one 24-hr urine sample and blood serum, and have filled out one 24-hr dietary recall (24HDR) and food frequency questionnaire (FFQ). There are no specific patient characteristics necessary for this study, as it is not recruiting new patients.

This is a healthy 3-year-old girl who has received a complete three-dose primary vaccination with diphtheria-tetanus-acellular pertussis (DTPa) vaccine and inactivated poliovirus (IPV) vaccine in the first six months of life, in line with recommendations in the United Kingdom (UK). She has also received a first dose of a live attenuated measles-mumps-rubella vaccine within the second year of life, in line with recommendations in the UK. Her parents have given written informed consent for her to participate in the study. She has no chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She has not received any other vaccines within 30 days preceding the booster dose of the study vaccine and is not planned to receive any other vaccines during the study period. She has not participated in any other clinical trials involving investigational or non-investigational products during the study period. She has no known exposure to measles, mumps, or rubella within 30 days prior to the study start and has no history of adverse reactions to any of the vaccine components. She is not experiencing any acute illnesses or fever at the time of enrollment or within 24 hours of study vaccine administration.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian woman who was recently diagnosed with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) after a routine mammography. She has no history of breast cancer or any other cancer. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications. She has a performance status of 1. She is married and has two children. She is currently going through menopause. She lives in a suburban area and has easy access to healthcare facilities. She is affiliated with the social health system and has health insurance. She is willing to comply with study treatment and follow-up. She has no known psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical situations that preclude compliance with study treatment and follow up. She is not currently participating in any other therapeutic trial. She is available for long-term follow-up and has a life expectancy of greater than 5 years.

A 62-year-old female patient was admitted to the Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center ICU due to complications related to advanced breast cancer. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. She underwent a mastectomy and was receiving chemotherapy. The patient was admitted to the ICU due to fever, shortness of breath, and altered mental status. The patient is currently intubated and sedated due to respiratory failure. Her family reports that she has been confused and disoriented, and they are concerned about her mental state. She is unable to provide consent at this time. The patient's medical team suspects that she may be experiencing delirium and would like to implement a delirium screening and treatment protocol to improve her outcomes. The patient's medical team will seek consent from her family members to participate in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old English-speaking woman who has been diagnosed with diabetes for over 5 years. She has been prescribed a statin medication for the past year but has been struggling with adherence, with a medication possession ratio of less than 70%. She denies any side effects from the medication. She has a close friend who has agreed to serve as her Medication Adherence Partner (MAP) for the trial. She is insured by Humana and is willing to participate in a 90-day trial using an electronic pill bottle (GlowCap) to store her statin medication. She is interested in improving her adherence to her medication and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old male with a history of stable angina presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. He has undergone previous PCI to his right coronary artery with a drug-eluting stent.
