On evaluation, he is found to have two de novo lesions in separate epicardial vessels, one in the left anterior descending artery and one in the left circumflex artery. The lesions have

Patient is a 54-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of recurrent malignant glioma, specifically anaplastic astrocytoma. She has previously undergone surgery to remove the original tumor and has received chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, her disease has progressed and there are no other treatment options of higher priority. The patient has measurable disease that can be assessed for tumor response based on radiographic assessment following Macdonald criteria and Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST). She has sufficient hepatic, renal, and hematological function, and her performance status is ≤2 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. She has discontinued all previous cancer therapies for at least 30 days prior to study enrollment and has recovered from the acute effects of therapy. The patient is able to swallow tablets and capsules and is willing to use an approved contraceptive method during and for 3 to 6 months after the study. She has not received prior nitrosourea (including lomustine) therapy.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Her chest X-ray revealed a pulmonary infiltrate, confirming a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. Upon admission, her Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) and CURB-65 scores were calculated. She was started on an appropriate antibiotic regimen and received respiratory support. Her condition improved over the following days, and she was eventually discharged from the hospital. She has no history of HIV infection or AIDS, anti-tumor treatment, or immunosuppressive therapy. She has not received radiation therapy, and she has not undergone a bone marrow transplant. She does not have cystic fibrosis or active tuberculosis.

A 45-year-old male patient was diagnosed with a brain tumor and scheduled for supratentorial craniotomy. He has a history of hypertension and occasional headaches but no other significant medical history. The patient provided signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He has a good understanding of the procedure and the potential side effects of the analgesics used for postoperative pain management. The patient scored 28 points in the Mini Mental State Examination and has no disabilities that could hinder the postoperative clinical assessment. He is willing and able to cooperate with the Acute Pain Unit during the postoperative period.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with fever and shortness of breath. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension. He has smoked for 30 years and currently smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. He works as a construction worker and has been exposed to dust and fumes on the job for the past 20 years. His physical exam shows tachypnea, tachycardia, and hypotension. His oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. He is diagnosed with sepsis based on the clinical suspicion of acute infection and the presence of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS). Blood cultures are positive for a gram-negative bacteria. He is admitted to the ICU and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. His condition is stable but he remains in the ICU for further management. He is approached about participating in a clinical trial investigating measures of zinc status in relation to oxidative stress and inflammation in patients with sepsis. He consents to participation in the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who recently tore her ACL while playing soccer. She reports feeling a sudden "pop" in her knee and experiencing immediate pain and swelling. She has been using crutches to ambulate and has not been able to participate in any physical activity since the injury. MRI imaging confirmed a complete tear of the ACL. Upon physical examination, the patient has a positive Lachman test and pivot shift test. She has no other ligament instability or associated injuries. The patient has a BMI of 22.1 and has never had any previous knee surgeries. She is highly motivated to return to her previous level of activity and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the single-bundle and double-bundle ACL reconstruction techniques.

65-year-old male with a history of smoking, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with a 5cm abdominal aortic aneurysm. He complains of occasional abdominal pain and discomfort. CT scan confirms the presence of the aneurysm and surgical intervention is recommended. The patient has no known allergies and is willing to participate in the study. Past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease with a previous myocardial infarction and a previous open heart surgery for coronary artery bypass grafting. The patient is currently on aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. He has a 40-pack year smoking history and quit smoking 10 years ago. He has a BMI of 28 and exercises regularly. The patient understands the nature of the study and has provided informed consent.

Unfortunately, as this is a study focused on the implementation of evidence-based nursing recommendations in nursing homes, there is no specific patient description required for this trial. The study aims to improve the care and outcomes for all female nursing home residents with urinary incontinence through the implementation of evidence-based nursing recommendations.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking medications for these conditions. He has never had any heart surgeries before. He experiences occasional palpitations but has never been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has a normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and normal thyroid function. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has a history of schizophrenia and was hospitalized for psychiatric treatment twice in the past. She came to the MGH Cancer Center for a second opinion after receiving a diagnosis of breast cancer from her primary care physician. She is married with two children and works part-time as a librarian. She reports experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations, delusions, and occasional suicidal ideation. She is currently taking antipsychotic medication and has been stable for the past six months. Her cancer diagnosis was confirmed through a biopsy, and she is scheduled to start treatment in two weeks. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study. She has no history of traumatic brain injury or dementia, and her cognitive function is within normal limits. Her vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. She is slightly overweight, with a BMI of 27. Her recent lab results are within normal limits.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during her prenatal care visits. She has no significant medical history, and her pregnancy has been otherwise unremarkable. Her gestational age is 38 weeks, and she gives birth to a healthy female infant with an APGAR score of 9 at 5 minutes. The infant weighs 3.2 kg and has no medical complications. The mother and infant are enrolled in the Well Baby Nursery (WBN) program and meet the eligibility criteria for the study. The mother is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend a one-time Family Nurture Intervention (FNI) session with her infant. The study aims to assess the impact of FNI on neurodevelopmental outcomes in at-risk infants, such as those born to mothers with GDM. The mother and infant will be compared to a control group of infants who did not receive FNI to evaluate the efficacy of the intervention. The study will assess developmental milestones such as cognitive and motor development, memory, attention, and emotion regulation at 6 and 15 months of age. The goal of the study is to improve developmental trajectories in at-risk infants and improve their overall health outcomes.

The patient is a 7-month-old healthy baby boy who was born full term with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. He has been exclusively breastfed and has had no significant medical history. His parents are both healthy and there is no family history of pneumococcal disease. The baby has not received any vaccinations yet. He is up-to-date with his well-baby check-ups and has been growing and developing normally. His weight is in the 50th percentile for his age and his head circumference is in the 75th percentile. He has no known allergies and no history of seizures or convulsions. He has not been administered any blood products or medications in the past 3 months. His parents are willing to provide proof of identity and sign informed consent for their child to participate in this clinical trial. They are able and willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and understand the nature of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is currently not taking any medications and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past six months. She weighs 60 kg and has a BMI of 24 kg/m2. She has no gastrointestinal diseases or past history of gastrointestinal surgeries. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has not donated blood or blood components in the past two months. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to medical research and understand more about the safety and pharmacokinetics of DWP14012 tablet A and tablet B.

A 50-year-old Taiwanese male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and high cholesterol presents to the clinic complaining of fatigue, shortness of breath and occasional chest pain. His diabetes has been managed with metformin 1000mg twice daily for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension and has been on lisinopril 10mg daily for the past year. He reports a previous myocardial infarction and angioplasty with stent placement 3 years ago. He reports occasional smoking, around 5 cigarettes a day for the past 10 years, and consumes 2-3 alcoholic beverages per week. His BMI is 30, and he has a family history of diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia. His most recent lab results show an LDL-C level of 150 mg/dL, HbA1c level of 8.5%, and triglyceride level of 300 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of atorvastatin in patients with diabetes and high cholesterol.

25 year-old woman who recently chose Nexplanon as her contraceptive method. She has no known allergies and has not been pregnant before. She does not smoke and has no known medical conditions. She received the Nexplanon implant from her healthcare provider who completed the Nexplanon Clinical Training Program. She is able to understand the study and complete the self-administered questionnaire in English. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She will be followed up at regular intervals to assess any insertion-, localization- or removal-related events and clinically significant consequences thereof.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who underwent kidney transplantation 2 years ago due to end-stage renal disease. He has been taking tacrolimus as an immunosuppressive agent since the transplant surgery. His medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking amlodipine, atorvastatin, metformin, and insulin as prescribed by his primary care physician. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written informed consent. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the Envarsus XR treatment. He is able to speak, write, and understand English. He has not participated in any Envarsus XR clinical study before and has no history of organ transplant other than kidney transplant. He is not pregnant or nursing, and is practicing a defined SOC method of contraception.

A 58 year old man, who had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presented to the hospital with sudden onset of weakness in his right arm and leg. MRI and CT scan revealed an ischemic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery territory. The patient was admitted to the hospital within 24 hours of stroke onset. Upon admission, the patient had a NIH Stroke Scale score of 10 and exhibited severe weakness in his right arm and leg. He was able to make a minimal isometric voluntary contraction of his affected limb. The patient was randomized into the vibration group and received Repeated Muscle Vibration (rMV) treatment for the upper and lower limbs on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd day after admission. The patient also received physiokinesitherapy every day. The patient will be re-evaluated after 4 ± 1 days to assess the effects of rMV on motor recovery.

A 40-year-old man, who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the last 5 years, is currently taking an ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) once daily to manage his blood pressure. He is in good general health, with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He has been experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms, including abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea for the last 2 months. Gastroenterologist recommended him to undergo gastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy to investigate the cause of these symptoms. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgery, alcohol or drug abuse or any other chronic illness. His blood pressure is well controlled, and he has no other medication except lisinopril.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) according to the Rotterdam criteria. She has no other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She has not used hormonal contraceptives for at least two months and does not have any contraindications to hormonal contraception. She does not smoke regularly or consume excessive amounts of alcohol. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has never been diagnosed with migraine with focal aura, thrombosis, cancer, estrogen-dependent tumor, or any abnormal liver function. She experiences irregular menstrual cycles and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of long-term use of oral and vaginal contraceptives on androgen secretion, insulin and glucose metabolism, lipid profile, and serum levels of SHBG and hs-CRP in women with PCOS. She understands the study requirements and is willing to participate voluntarily.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who presents with acute onset of severe, colicky pain in her right flank. She has a history of recurrent kidney stones and has previously undergone lithotripsy for a stone in her left kidney. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. On examination, she is in significant distress, with tenderness to palpation over her right flank. She has no fever or signs of infection. Imaging studies reveal a 5mm stone lodged in her right ureter, causing hydronephrosis. She is a candidate for placement of the PercSys MicroStent device to alleviate her symptoms and facilitate the passage of the stone. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 50-year-old man with a history of hypertension presents with complaints of fatigue, decreased appetite, and difficulty sleeping. Routine blood work reveals elevated creatinine levels and a subsequent renal function test confirms a mild to moderate impairment in kidney function. The patient is not currently receiving any prescription or non-prescription medications. He has a body mass index within the range of 18-40 kg/m2 and his total body weight is greater than 50 kg. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the blood levels, safety, and tolerability of PF-00734200 in subjects with impaired kidney function and normal kidney function.

A 65-year-old man was recently diagnosed with stage I prostate cancer after a biopsy. His Gleason score is 6 and his PSA level is 10. He has no other prior history of cancer except for nonmelanoma skin cancer. He is currently not taking any hormonal therapy or radiotherapy, and has not participated in any other clinical trials involving medical, surgical, nutritional, or lifestyle intervention in the past 30 days. He has a life expectancy of more than 5 years. He is willing to take selenomethionine or placebo for 8-9 weeks immediately prior to undergoing prostatectomy or brachytherapy. He is not taking any concurrent dietary supplementation with selenium at doses > 60 mcg/day, including multivitamin supplements or any hormonal therapy, including 5-alpha reductase inhibitors, anti-androgens, or luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonists.

An 80-year-old female resident of a nursing home has been selected to participate in a clinical trial on buccodental teleexpertise for oral care. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, but these conditions are well-managed with medication. She has also had several teeth extracted in the past due to decay and gum disease. The patient has experienced some difficulty with oral care in the past due to arthritis in her hands. She has given her free, informed, and signed consent to participate in the study. The medical team has approved her participation, and she is a member of a social security scheme. She is not in a period of relative exclusion from another protocol and is not deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision. She has no plans to change nursing homes within the next 6 months. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopes that it will improve her overall oral health and quality of life.

No patient description is needed for this clinical trial as it is a safety study and does not involve patient interventions or recruitment. The study will collect data on adverse drug events or adverse drug reactions in 30,000 patients who have already been prescribed Kudiezi(Yueanxin) injection in selected hospitals in China from 2012 to 2014.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a non-restorable maxillary anterior tooth that needs to be extracted. The patient has sound adjacent teeth and intact thick biotype gingival tissue with at least 2mm band of keratinized tissue. The patient's buccal bone thickness is 1mm or less with good apical bone, and the root position is sagittal type 1, as described by Kan et al. The patient has good oral hygiene and is willing to provide informed consent. The patient does not smoke and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient does not have any active infections related to the site of implant/bone graft placement or untreated active periodontal diseases. The patient does not have any medical contraindications for the surgical procedure, such as uncontrolled diabetes, bisphosphonate injection treatment for osteoporosis, active cardiac diseases, or undergoing radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The patient does not have any parafunctional habits.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled for an elective hernia repair surgery. He has a history of occasional alcohol use and currently takes over-the-counter ibuprofen for occasional joint pain. He has no known allergies and no significant medical history. He lives with his wife and two children and works as a construction worker. He has never had a TAP block before and has no history of opioid use disorder. His surgery is scheduled for mid-morning and he is not the first case of the day. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

Maria is a 26-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a Norovirus GI.1/GII.4 bivalent Virus-Like Particle Vaccine. She is in good health and has not experienced acute gastroenteritis within the past 14 days. Maria has never been exposed to an experimental Norovirus vaccine and has not received any inactivated vaccines within 14 days or any live vaccines for 28 days prior to enrollment in this trial. She is willing to comply with trial procedures and is available for the duration of follow-up. Maria's body weight is greater than or equal to 50 kg and her BMI is less than 35. She does not have any known hypersensitivity or allergy to any of the NoV vaccine components (including excipients). Maria has no history of progressive or severe neurologic disorder, seizure disorder or neuro-inflammatory disease. She does not have any known bleeding diathesis or any condition that may be associated with a prolonged bleeding time. Maria is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is willing to use an acceptable contraceptive method for at least 2 months prior to trial entry and through to 6 months after receipt of the investigational vaccine. Maria is excited to potentially contribute to the development of a Norovirus GI.1/GII.4 bivalent Virus-Like Particle Vaccine.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who suffered a left hemisphere ischemic stroke 8 months ago. He has residual left hemiparesis affecting his arm and leg. He is currently undergoing physical therapy to improve his upper extremity function. He has some ability to grasp objects with his affected hand, but he is unable to release them voluntarily. He has difficulty performing daily activities that require the use of both hands and has been relying on his unaffected hand for most of his activities. He is living with his wife who is his primary caregiver. He has no history of dementia or any other neurological disorders. He is able to follow verbal instructions and has no difficulty standing for more than 2 minutes. He is not currently participating in any other experimental rehabilitation or drug studies. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his upper limb function and regain independence in his daily activities.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer. She has undergone surgery and multiple lines of chemotherapy with no success. She has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She has no major surgeries in the past 3 weeks and has not received any investigational therapy in the past 4 weeks. She does not have any known hypersensitivity to the components of niraparib, everolimus, rapamycin analogues, or the excipients. She has not received any transfusion in the past 4 weeks. She does not have current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the study or interfere with her participation for the full duration of the study treatment. She is a non-smoker, and her BMI is 25. She is post-menopausal and has no plans to conceive children. She is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study and for at least 180 days after the final dose. She is able to understand the study procedures and agrees to participate in the study by providing written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic nausea and vomiting for the past 6 months. She has tried multiple over-the-counter anti-nausea medications, including ginger and peppermint supplements, with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She has also noticed that her symptoms are worse when she moves her head quickly or when she changes positions, such as getting up from a sitting or lying down position. She reports feeling dizzy or off-balance at times, and she has had a few instances of falling or nearly falling due to this. On examination, the patient has a positive modified Fukuda stepping test, with rotation greater than 90 degrees from midline while marching in place for 60 seconds. She also has mild nystagmus on gaze testing. The patient is not pregnant and is able to complete the questionnaire survey.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II colon cancer during a routine colonoscopy. She has no significant past medical history and is generally in good health. She reports occasional constipation and mild abdominal discomfort, but denies any significant weight loss, anemia, or rectal bleeding. She is a retired schoolteacher and lives with her husband. She has two adult children who live in another state. She is willing to participate in clinical trials and has no prior history of cancer. Her surgery is planned in the next few weeks, and her physician has discussed the possibility of adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery. She is concerned about the potential side effects of chemotherapy and wants to know if there is a way to determine if she truly needs it.

Patient is a 58-year-old man who presents with a history of transient ischemic attack (TIA) 3 months ago. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus, all of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no significant past surgical or medical history. He is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 28, BP: 140/85, HR: 72/min. The patient has undergone a carotid ultrasound which revealed a 70% stenosis in the right internal carotid artery. The study team has recommended carotid revascularization with the MicroNet-covered stent system, and the patient has agreed to participate in the study. The patient has signed informed consent and has agreed to undergo clinical and ultrasonographic follow-up.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs). The patient has been experiencing frequent episodes of painful urination, urinary urgency, and lower abdominal discomfort. The patient reports having to use a catheter intermittently to relieve his symptoms. The patient has been on antibiotics multiple times for his UTIs, but the symptoms keep recurring. The patient is married, retired, and lives with his wife. He does not have any history of allergies or chronic illnesses. The patient has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to see if the Camstent coated catheter can help reduce his symptoms and improve his quality of life. The patient understands and is willing to comply with the study procedures and visits.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe headache, confusion and left-sided weakness. A CT scan revealed a spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) with a volume of more than 30 ml. He has a history of hypertension and has been on antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years. He is currently taking lisinopril and amlodipine. He has no other medical conditions and is not on any other medications. His blood pressure on admission was 180/100 mmHg. He has a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 7 at presentation. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. His family history is not significant for any neurological or cardiovascular diseases. His lab work shows a fasting plasma glucose level of 6.2 mmol/L and normal clotting function. The patient and his family are willing to participate in the study and have signed informed consent.

53-year-old female with a history of low-grade B-cell lymphoma involving the cervical lymph nodes, diagnosed 6 months ago. She has no prior history of cancer and has not received any prior treatment for her lymphoma. She reports mild fatigue and occasional night sweats. On physical exam, there is palpable cervical lymphadenopathy on the left side, measuring approximately 3 cm in diameter. CT scan of the neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis confirms the presence of left cervical lymphadenopathy and right axillary lymphadenopathy. There is no evidence of disease involvement in other organs. The patient has a Performance Status of 1 and adequate bone marrow, renal and hepatic function. She is not on any immunosuppressive drugs and has no active autoimmune disease. She has a life expectancy of greater than 4 months. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 52-year-old Japanese man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus two years ago. He has been trying to control his blood sugar levels through diet and exercise but has not been able to achieve the clinical target of glycemic control (HbA1c less than 7.0%). He takes metformin and an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor regularly. He has no history of renal dysfunction or hepatic insufficiency. He does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol and is not on loop diuretics. He has not previously taken dapagliflozin or participated in any other clinical trials. He is able to communicate and comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV prostate cancer that has metastasized to his bones. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy without significant improvement. The patient's current prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 200 ng/mL. The patient has a performance status of 1 and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient's absolute neutrophil count is 2.5 x10^9 /L, platelet count is 80 x 10^9 /L, and creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. The patient has a serum bilirubin level of 0.9 x the institutional upper limit of normal and SGOT (AST) and SGPT (ALT) levels that are within the institutional upper limit of normal. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient has no history of torsades de pointes type ventricular arrhythmia or prolonged QT interval. The patient has not received any radiotherapy or chemotherapy within the past three weeks and has recovered from the acute effects of any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient has no uncontrolled electrolyte imbalance and is not undergoing therapy with other investigational agents. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of hypersensitivity to pamidronate or other bisphosphonates. The patient has not been previously treated with arsenic trioxide.

70-year-old male with newly diagnosed advanced stage Hodgkin Lymphoma, presenting with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He has not received any prior treatment for his lymphoma. Laboratory workup reveals adequate organ function, with ANC of 1.8 x 109/L, hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, and platelets of 120 x 109/L. AST and ALT are within normal limits, and bilirubin is 1.2 x ULN. Creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL. The patient is able to perform activities of daily living with an ECOG performance status of 1. He agrees to practice effective barrier contraception during the entire study period and through 6 months after the last dose of study drug. The patient is enrolled in the study after providing informed consent.

52 yo female with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in complete remission after undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation (related donor) presents for a clinical trial. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medication. She reports a history of occasional shortness of breath with exertion but denies any chest pain or palpitations. She is currently in good physical condition and is able to perform activities of daily living without significant difficulty. She is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve her quality of life and overall physical functioning post-transplant. She provides written informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

28-year-old G1P0 woman at 40 weeks gestation with a history of gestational diabetes and hypertension. The patient has been carefully monitored throughout her pregnancy, and her blood sugar and blood pressure levels are well-controlled with medication. The patient has no history of uterine surgery and has a clinically adequate pelvis. The patient has a modified Bishop's score of 4 and a reactive non-stress test. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

71-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease with an MMSE score of 19 and CDR 1 at the screening visit. He is currently taking donepezil and has been on a stable dose for 9 months. He lives with his wife who serves as his reliable caregiver. Past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a history of prostate cancer that was treated with surgery and radiation therapy. The patient has no significant history of neurologic disease or psychiatric illness. He has not had significant hearing loss and has no history of seizures. He has not had a recent myocardial infarction or unstable angina and has no significant cardiac arrhythmias. He has normal renal and hepatic function. He has not received active amyloid or tau immunization at any time. He is willing to participate in the 26-week randomized, double-blind treatment with ATH-1017 and comply with all study procedures.

A 42-year-old woman, who works as a nurse in a hospital, is experiencing severe anxiety and fear around contracting COVID-19. She has a history of anxiety and phobias, specifically related to germs and illness. Her symptoms have worsened since the start of the pandemic, and she is finding it difficult to cope with her daily life. She is not currently infected with COVID-19, but worries constantly about the possibility of contracting it at work. She is willing to participate in the study and give written consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who is struggling with her weight and has a BMI of 27. She admits to consuming at least 3.5 oz of chocolate per day and has noticed an increase in cravings for chocolate. She is right-handed and has no medical contraindications to exercise. She is currently not pregnant and does not have any known risk factors for heart disease. She is interested in participating in a research study that investigates whether a single high-intensity interval exercise can help reduce her addictive behavior towards chocolate. She is willing to complete a three-day chocolate diary, abstain from chocolate on the fourth day, and record everything she eats and drinks before the study. She is also willing to complete two stress-inducing tasks followed by either 26 minutes of HIIE or a seated resting condition on two separate days. She is willing to complete mood and craving questionnaires and a task that measures the amount of attention she pays to chocolate.

A 45-year-old woman has been living with multiple sclerosis for the past 10 years. She uses a wheelchair to move around and is unable to walk for more than a few steps without stopping. She has been struggling with her weight for the past year and has a BMI of 28 kg/m squared. She has wireless internet access in her home and is interested in participating in a weight loss program that she can do from home. She has not participated in any structured weight loss or exercise program in the previous 6 months and is not currently exercising more than 3, 30-min bouts of planned exercise per week. She is willing to be randomized and has no plans for pregnancy or lactation in the next 18 months. She has no serious medical risks or psychiatric illnesses that would prevent her from participating in the study. She has no cognitive, visual, or hearing impairments that would interfere with her compliance to the study protocol. She does not adhere to any specialized diets, and has no history of binge eating or other eating disorders. She lives alone and does not share her household with another study participant.

The patient is a 70 year old male who lives alone in his apartment. He fell down from the stairs and was admitted to the hospital with a displaced femoral neck fracture. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has never undergone any major surgeries before. He is mentally competent and has no concurrent joint disease or previous fracture in the lower extremities. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks of both total hip arthroplasty and internal fixation for his fractured femoral neck. He has a Harris hip score of 100 before the injury and is eager to regain his mobility and independence. He is physically active and enjoys walking and gardening as his hobbies.

A 32-year-old woman seeks treatment for her trichotillomania, which has significantly impacted her daily life. She has been pulling her hair out for the past 5 years and has tried various treatments without success. She has no history of mental illness, but has been diagnosed with trichotillomania by her primary care physician. She is fluent in English and currently an outpatient. She is not currently taking any medications for her trichotillomania, and agrees not to alter the dosage of any psychotropic medication throughout the course of the study. She does not eat her hair after pulling, and has not been diagnosed with gastrointestinal blockage due to hair pulling. The Massachusetts General Hospital Hair Scale score for her is greater than 12, indicating moderate to severe hair pulling. She has a Wechsler Test of Adult Reading score greater than 85, indicating adequate intelligence to participate in the study. She is willing to participate in the 12-week study and follow-up assessments for 6 months. She has not received psychotherapy for trichotillomania or any other psychiatric condition prior to study participation.

45 y/o male diagnosed with schizophrenia according to DSM-IV criteria, currently receiving treatment in an outpatient psychiatric department. The patient has no history of alcohol abuse or dependence but is a light smoker, consuming less than 1 pack of cigarettes per day. The patient is not currently using mood stabilizers or beta-blockers. The patient has a history of positive and negative symptoms of schizophrenia, including auditory hallucinations, delusions, social withdrawal, lack of motivation, and emotional blunting. The patient also has a history of obesity and metabolic syndrome. The patient has been previously treated with risperidone for schizophrenia. The patient is able to complete written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) for the past 5 years. She has been using a CPAP machine but has not been able to tolerate it due to discomfort and claustrophobia. She reports feeling tired during the day and has difficulty concentrating at work due to her sleep disturbances. She has a BMI of 27 and has no history of narcotic dependency. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in a 30-day open-label trial of the therapeutic treatment THX-110 (a combination of Dronabinol and PEA) for the treatment of OSA. She is interested in exploring alternative treatment options for her sleep apnea and hopes that THX-110 will provide relief from her symptoms.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain during physical activity for the past 6 months. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father experiencing a heart attack at the age of 60. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past year. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. He has undergone a stress test, which has shown borderline results, and his Cardiologist has referred him to participate in this clinical trial to determine the extent of his coronary artery disease. The patient has not undergone any prior diagnostic imaging studies for his chest pain. His serum creatinine level is within normal range, and he does not have any significant co-morbidities. The patient is able to provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

This is a 6 year-old female with a history of frequent headaches for the past 2 months. The headaches are described as throbbing in nature and last for several hours. The patient was seen by her primary care physician who prescribed acetaminophen for the headaches, but they have not improved. The patient's mother brought her to the pediatric emergency room due to concerns about her daughter's worsening headaches. The patient has no history of trauma, no significant medical history, and no family history of neurological conditions. A brain CT scan was ordered by the emergency room physician to rule out any potential serious underlying conditions.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a solid tumor that has metastasized and is not responsive to standard treatments. She has undergone previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not experienced significant improvements. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is expected to live for at least 3 months. Her leukocyte count is 4,000/mcL, absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mcL, platelets are 150,000/mcL, and hemoglobin is 12 g/dL. Her total bilirubin is within normal range, and her AST and ALT levels are not more than 2.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal. Her creatinine levels are within normal range, and her fasting serum glucose and triglycerides are below 130 mg/dL and 300 mg/dL, respectively. She has an evaluable or measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past four weeks and has recovered to =< grade 1 toxicity or previous baseline for each toxicity. She has a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within seven days and agrees to practice effective contraception during and for 90 days after the last dose of study drug. The patient must have the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent document and swallow oral medications.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been admitted to the hospital with sudden onset right-sided weakness and slurred speech. He reports that the symptoms started about 4 hours ago while he was at home. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. An initial CT scan shows that he has an anterior large vessel occlusion in the left middle cerebral artery. He is a candidate for mechanical thrombectomy and will be randomized to receive either standard blood pressure management or individualized blood pressure management during the procedure. He is able to provide informed consent and is affiliated with social security assurance. His baseline mRS score is 0, indicating no pre-existing neurological disability. He has no contraindications to iodinated contrast agents.

A 56-year-old male presents with a history of high-risk prostate cancer. He underwent radical prostatectomy within the last 3 months and was found to have pathological stage T3b disease with a Gleason score of 9. His pre-operative PSA level was 28ng/mL. He has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy for prostate cancer. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0 and is able to swallow the study drug. His testosterone level is above 50 ng/dL, and his baseline post-prostatectomy PSA level is less than 0.4 ng/mL. He has normal organ and marrow function, with a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mcL, and platelet count of 150,000/ìL. He has no known history of HIV, CNS metastases, or active unresolved infection. He has no history of Mobitz II second degree or third degree heart block without a permanent pacemaker in place, and his blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. He is not taking any herbal products that may interfere with the study drug, and he has not used 5-alpha reductase inhibitors within 7-14 days prior to enrollment. He has no clinically significant gastrointestinal disorders affecting absorption, and he agrees to use adequate contraception during the study and for 6 months after usage of enzalutamide. He meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is eligible to participate.

The patient is a 65-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of Hodgkin's Lymphoma. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis. The CT scan revealed a bulky mediastinal mass (> 1/3 maximum transverse thorax diameter) and involvement of 2 lymph node areas. Her ESR was > 50 mm/hour and she experienced occasional B-symptoms. The patient has no previous history of cancer and is in otherwise good health. She is able to perform daily activities without assistance and has a good performance status (ECOG 0-1). The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

An 85 year old woman was brought to the hospital by her daughter after falling in her home. She was diagnosed with an undisplaced intracapsular fracture of her hip. She has a history of osteoporosis and hypertension, but her medications are well-controlled. She is independent in her activities of daily living and still enjoys her daily walks around the neighborhood. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial comparing fixation versus arthroplasty for her fracture. She understands the potential benefits and risks of both procedures and is willing to be randomized to receive either reduction and internal fixation of the fracture with a screw and plate device or replacement of her femoral head with an artificial hip replacement (hemiarthroplasty). She has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and in chemo-sensitive remission is eligible for a phase 1 clinical trial of AB-205. He is scheduled to undergo high-dose therapy and autologous stem cell transplantation with the BEAM conditioning regimen. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical conditions and has adequate organ function. The patient is willing to comply with the scheduled visits, drug administration plan, and other study procedures. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to use a recommended method of contraception throughout the study period.

The patient is a 30 year old male who presents to the clinic complaining of a fractured central incisor tooth due to a recent sports injury. On examination, it is found that the tooth is non-restorable and requires extraction. The patient is concerned about the esthetic appearance of his smile and wishes to have a dental implant placed. He has good oral hygiene and no periapical lesions. The patient has sufficient bone (5 mm) below the tooth to allow for primary implant stability and adequate medio-distal and labial bone. He has a sufficient band of keratinized mucosa. His medical history is unremarkable and he does not have any systemic conditions that would be considered an absolute contraindication for implant placement. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any parafunctional habits such as bruxism. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the accuracy of selective laser sintered computer guided stents versus digital light processing stents for implant placement.

The patient is a 14-year-old male diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with t(9;22) chromosomal abnormality in first remission. He did not respond well to initial induction therapy and has less than 15% blasts at the time of registration. He meets eligibility criteria for the clinical trial that involves undergoing an allogeneic stem cell transplantation (AlloSCT) with stem cells selected utilizing α/β CD3+/CD19+ cell depletion. The patient has no documented uncontrolled infection at the time of study entry and has a Karnofsky/Lansky performance score of 80. The patient and his family have been informed of the experimental nature of the study and its potential risks, and have signed an Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved written informed consent form indicating such an understanding.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy diagnosed with neurogenic bladder. He has been using clean intermittent catheterization (CIC) daily to empty his bladder. He has a recent history of fecal incontinence within the last three months, and he has experienced more than two episodes of urinary tract infection and/or pyuria within the last six months. He has not undergone bladder augmentation surgery, and he completed toilet training. He has no anatomical abnormalities of the bladder neck and no known intractable origin of bacteriuria such as urolithiasis or nonfunctional renal segment. He has not received any of the treatments diagnosed according to Peristeen® product safety guidelines. He is willing to perform transanal irrigation twice weekly for 12 weeks as part of this study.

Patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma. The patient has been managing his condition with combination drop therapy for the past year. The patient's glaucoma is considered severe, with a grade 4 Shaffer-Etienne scale rating. The patient has no history of uveitis, cystoid macular edema, or cornea edema. The patient has not undergone any intraocular surgery or had any cornea/refractive surgery in the past 6 months. The patient's visual acuity in the non-study eye is the same as the study eye. The patient is currently taking a prostaglandin analogue as part of their drop therapy. The patient is willing to discontinue drop therapy in the study eye and continue it in the contralateral eye. The patient is not experiencing any uncontrolled infection in the eye.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past year. She has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue despite being on antiarrhythmic medication. She has a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) to monitor her AF burden. Her glycated hemoglobin level is within normal range and her estimated glomerular filtration rate is above 30 mL/minute/1.73 m2. She is scheduled to undergo catheter ablation for her AF in the next few weeks. She has no history of type 1 diabetes mellitus or diabetic keto-acidosis. She has no history of liver disease or left atrial diameter of 60 mm or greater. She is not currently pregnant, planning to become pregnant within the next year, or breastfeeding. She has not been on therapy with an SGLT2 inhibitor. She is willing and able to cooperate with the protocol and is willing to sign the consent for participation. Her life expectancy is greater than 1 year after consenting for the trial.

A 35-year-old female patient presented with symptoms of itching, pain, and discharge in her left ear for the past 2 weeks. She has previously experienced ear infections and had been diagnosed with otomycosis in the past. Physical examination revealed erythema, edema, and discharge in the left external ear canal. The tympanic membrane was intact, and there was no evidence of middle ear involvement. The patient has no history of allergy or sensitivity to any medication. She is not pregnant and has not used any systemic antifungal therapy or immunosuppressive drugs in the past 28 days. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 28 days. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the treatment of otomycosis with miconazole oil and meets the inclusion criteria.

A 28-year-old woman came to the emergency department complaining of abdominal pain and difficulty breathing. She reports feeling anxious and depressed lately, and has been having trouble sleeping. She is currently in a relationship with her partner, who she reports has been physically and emotionally abusive towards her. She has not sought help for the abuse, but expresses a desire to leave the relationship. She speaks English fluently and is able to read. She is not acutely intoxicated or too ill to participate in the study. She meets the inclusion criteria and is willing to participate in the mental health symptoms and intimate partner violence screening.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently hospitalized for an acute myocardial infarction (AMI) with ST elevation. He underwent a primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and was discharged from the cardiology department of the Leiden University Medical Center. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He is fluent in both English and Dutch and is willing to participate in the study. His body mass index is 27 kg/m2. He has a smartphone and is comfortable using technology. He has no other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

A 45-year old female was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. She is currently taking metformin and sitagliptin to manage her blood sugar levels. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is being controlled with medication. She has a BMI of 31 kg/m2. She has no history of diabetic complications such as retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy or gastroparesis. She has not had any recent severe hypoglycemic episodes or hypoglycemic unawareness. She does not have any psychological or emotional problems that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is currently not taking any non-oral antihyperglycemic agents or thiazolidinediones. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers evaluate the safety and efficacy of JNJ-38431055 in managing blood sugar levels in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

50 year old man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He has been managing his diabetes with metformin and a low-carb diet. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.2% indicating a need for intensified glucose-lowering therapy. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no history of cardiovascular disease but has a family history of heart disease. The patient is willing to start treatment with empagliflozin and participate in the study to assess its effects on glucose metabolism, weight, blood pressure, and cardiac function.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is dissatisfied with the appearance of her nasolabial folds. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has not undergone any facial tissue augmenting therapy with non-permanent filler or aesthetic facial surgical therapy within the last 9 months. She has no permanent implants in the NLF area and no evidence of scar-related disease. She is not pregnant or lactating and has never received semi-permanent fillers anywhere in the face or neck. She has no scars at the intended treatment sites and no history of keloid formation or hypertrophic scars. She has no infections or unhealed wounds on the face and no allergies to natural rubber latex, lidocaine, or any amide-based anesthetic. She has not taken aspirin or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs within the last week and is not currently taking any anticoagulant therapy, antiplatelet therapy, or history of bleeding disorders. She has not received any investigational product within the last 30 days and has no facial tattoo that may interfere with diagnosis. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study, including refraining from seeking other treatment for this condition during the study.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who has been experiencing severe shoulder pain and limited mobility for several years. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and a non-repairable rotator cuff tear in his right shoulder. He has tried various non-surgical treatments including physical therapy, pain medication and corticosteroid injections, but they have not provided significant relief. His BMI is 30. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or any other medical condition that would interfere with his ability to participate in the study. He is willing and able to comply with the follow-up schedule and evaluation outlined in the protocol. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 75 year old woman diagnosed with probable Alzheimer's disease, who has been living in an Adult Family Home (AFH) for the past 6 months. Her family reports that she experiences frequent sleep disturbances, including difficulty falling asleep, waking up frequently during the night, and getting up very early in the morning. She often wanders around the home at night and has fallen several times. She has no previous diagnosis of a primary sleep disorder such as sleep apnea or restless legs syndrome. She is currently taking donepezil for her Alzheimer's disease and has no other significant medical issues. She is able to walk with assistance and perform most activities of daily living with help. The owner and staff of the AFH are willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old mother who brought her 3-year-old daughter to the Children's Hospital of Wisconsin for treatment. She speaks fluent English and is the primary caregiver for her daughter. The family uses their car for transportation. The child was brought in for a mild fever and cough. The triage nurse assessed the child as a level 3 and she was asked to wait in the waiting room for further evaluation. The mother is expected to spend at least 30 minutes in the waiting room before being seen by a healthcare provider.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been receiving methadone maintenance therapy for the past two years. He is currently on a stable dose of methadone and has been for the past six months. He reports experiencing chronic back pain, which has been affecting his quality of life. He is a smoker and reports consuming alcohol occasionally. He does not have any history of sexual dysfunction or osteoporosis. He has not been diagnosed with congestive heart failure and reports no illicit drug use. He is willing to participate in the study and is competent in English. The patient is interested in learning more about the potential side effects of methadone therapy and is motivated to take steps to improve his overall health.

The patient is a 6-year-old male child who is attending a well-child visit with his primary care provider. He is generally healthy and has no medical history of chronic illnesses or developmental delays. His parents are both non-smokers and do not allow smoking in their home. The child's mother is a stay-at-home mom and his father works as an accountant. The family lives in a suburban area and the child attends a local elementary school. The child is up-to-date on all of his vaccinations and has no known allergies. He is at a healthy weight for his age and height and is meeting all of his developmental milestones. The parents are interested in participating in the study and learning more about how they can promote their child's health.

A 65-year-old retired man came to the ophthalmologist's office complaining of blurry vision and difficulty reading his favorite newspaper. He was diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes with a lens opacity classification of grade III. He has no significant medical history, but he takes medication for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He wears glasses for distance vision correction but is interested in being spectacle independent for both distance and near vision. He has not had any previous ocular surgeries or trauma, and he does not have corneal opacities, fundus abnormalities, glaucoma, uveitis, or amblyopia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will compare two different multifocal intraocular lenses to determine which one provides better near vision.

A 54-year-old man was admitted to the ICU at Peking University Third Hospital due to COVID-19. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes for 5 years, controlled with medications. He presented with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath for 2 days before the admission. His symptoms worsened rapidly, requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. He is currently on a ventilator and receiving enteral nutrition support through a feeding tube due to difficulty swallowing. His APACHE II score and SOFA score were calculated at admission, and he was diagnosed with COVID-19 based on clinical and radiological findings. He is expected to have a prolonged ICU stay due to the severity of his illness. The medical team is considering enrolling him in a clinical trial to validate the NUTRIC nutritional risk assessment tool to determine the most effective nutrition support therapy for critically-ill COVID-19 patients.

The patient is a 22-year-old woman who has been naturally thin her whole life. She has a BMI of 17.2 and has maintained this weight for the past 6 months. She has no history of eating disorders or significant medical conditions. She is not a vegetarian and has no lactose intolerance. She occasionally drinks alcohol but never more than 2 glasses of wine per week. She does not smoke and has never been diagnosed with depression or any other psychiatric condition. She has never undergone any significant surgery and is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study parameters. She has agreed to gain up to 2 kg of weight for the study. She is a beneficiary of a social security system and has signed consent forms for participation in the study and genetic analysis. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical study.

A 3-month-old Caucasian male infant with 2 cutaneous hemangiomas on his right arm and left leg. His mother noticed these lesions when he was born, and they have continued to grow in size. The infant is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or family history of hemangiomas or liver disease. The infant is not taking any medications and has no known allergies. The infant's weight is in the 60th percentile for his age, and he is meeting all developmental milestones. The mother is interested in participating in the study to determine if her child has hepatic hemangiomatosis and to identify any potential risk factors. The mother understands that the study involves hepatic ultrasound imaging and agrees to follow-up visits as needed.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He has no significant medical history or psychiatric illness that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He is not a female of childbearing potential, pregnant, or breastfeeding. He has not been exposed to an investigational drug or used any prescribed systemic or topical medication within 30 days or 5 terminal half-lives prior to the first dose administration. He has not used any non-prescribed systemic or topical medication within 14 days prior to the first dose administration. He has not used CYP3A and/or CYP1A2 inducers and/or inhibitors within 30 days prior to the first dose administration. He has no surgical or medical condition possibly affecting drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. He has not donated blood or plasma within 8 weeks before the first dose administration to a blood bank or blood donation center. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within 2 years before the first dose administration. He is a non-smoker and has not received immunization with a live or live attenuated vaccine within 2 months prior to administration of the first dose of IP or is planning to receive immunization with a live or live attenuated vaccine for 2 months after administration of the last dose of IP. He is not part of the clinical staff personnel or a family member of the clinical site staff.

The patient is a premature infant born at 31 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1500 grams. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit and is currently receiving enteral feeding of 80 ml/kg/day of donor breast milk. The infant's parents have provided consent for the infant to participate in a clinical trial comparing targeted and standard fortification of human milk. The infant has not experienced any complications related to feeding or other health issues. The infant has not received any formula or parenteral nutrition. The infant has not been diagnosed with any congenital abnormalities that increase the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis. The infant is stable and meeting milestones appropriate for gestational age.

32 year-old man with a history of snorted/sniffed cocaine dependence presents with symptoms of cocaine withdrawal including fatigue, depression and anxiety. He has been using cocaine for the past 5 years and has been unsuccessful in multiple attempts to quit. He is currently unemployed and living with his parents. He reports a history of occasional alcohol use but no other substance abuse. He has no significant medical history and denies any current medical conditions. He is aware of the study's requirements and is willing to participate. He is not on any current medication and has no known allergies. He is sexually active with his girlfriend and is willing to use effective contraceptive measures during the study.

A 35-year-old woman with a long-standing history of asthma, currently treated with inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists, who participated in one of the three predecessor studies for benralizumab. The patient has reported frequent asthma exacerbations, despite treatment with current medications, and has experienced adverse effects from previous asthma medications. She has no history of other significant medical conditions and is not currently taking any other medications. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including the use of effective birth control, and is able to provide informed consent.

A 10-month-old baby boy was brought to the pediatrician's office with a history of cough, runny nose, and difficulty breathing for the past 3 days. The baby was born full-term with no complications and is up-to-date on all vaccinations. The mother reports that the baby was otherwise healthy and had no significant medical history. The baby is breastfeeding and has started on solid foods. On physical examination, the baby has a respiratory rate of 42 breaths/minute with mild subcostal retractions. Lung auscultation reveals scattered rhonchi and coarse breath sounds. The baby is afebrile and has no signs of dehydration. The pediatrician diagnosed the baby with bronchiolitis and recommends supportive care. However, the mother is concerned and requests additional tests and treatments, such as antibiotics and bronchodilators. The pediatrician discusses with the mother the potential harms and benefits of these interventions and explains that they are not evidence-based or recommended for bronchiolitis. The mother agrees to follow the pediatrician's recommendations and the baby is managed with supportive care.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with unresectable melanoma with KIT mutations. She has previously received anti-PD-1/L1 mAb therapy, but has experienced disease progression. The patient has not received any prior treatment with KIT inhibitors. She presents with a measurable lesion on CT and MRI scans, and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has a history of well-controlled hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine 5mg daily. She has no known history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, or autoimmune diseases that have required systemic treatment in the past 2 years. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an adequate method of contraception during the study period. Her laboratory parameters are within the protocol-defined range, including a white blood cell count of 3,800/mm^3, platelets of 120,000/mm^3, hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL, AST and ALT levels of 45 IU/L and 30 IU/L respectively, bilirubin level of 1.0 mg/dL, and serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL. The patient has no history of pneumonitis or active infections. She is willing and able to provide written consent before starting therapy.

An 86-year-old female with a history of congestive heart failure and COPD presented to the hospital with shortness of breath and fatigue. Imaging studies showed worsening of her left ventricular ejection fraction to less than 25%. She has been admitted to the hospital several times in the past year due to respiratory failure. She lives alone and has no family members living nearby. She has expressed concerns about end-of-life care but has not yet engaged in advanced care planning (ACP) activities. She speaks English fluently and has no cognitive impairment. The patient has agreed to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of ACP in elderly patients at high-risk for dying.

A 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV-1 infection five years ago presents for his routine follow-up visit. He has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past three years with a combination of tenofovir/emtricitabine and efavirenz. His viral load has been undetectable for the past year with a CD4 count of 450 cells/mm3. However, he has been experiencing side effects related to efavirenz, such as insomnia, headaches, and vivid dreams, which affect his daily functioning. He has no history of drug resistance to ART. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication and a family history of diabetes. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma 3 years ago. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but unfortunately, his disease relapsed and became refractory to treatment. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His physical examination reveals multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axilla, and groin regions. The patient's laboratory results show that he has an elevated lactate dehydrogenase level, indicating active tumor burden. He has also developed mild anemia and thrombocytopenia. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. He has undergone autologous stem cell transplantation in the past, but unfortunately, it did not provide long-term disease control. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the eligibility criteria, including being between the ages of 10 and 80 years old, having measurable target lesions, and having no effective treatment options available. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage IVb squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He has a history of heavy smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has noticed difficulty swallowing and hoarseness for the past few months, and a biopsy confirmed the cancer diagnosis. He has not received any treatment for the cancer yet. He has no history of sleep apnea, but he has noticed that he snores loudly at night. He is willing to participate in the study and has no problem operating the home sleep study device. His ECOG performance status is 1. He does not have a tracheostomy or require the assistance of a ventilator.

A 52-year-old non-smoking woman presents with a history of exertional dyspnea and dry cough for the past 6 months. She reports feeling fatigued and has lost about 5 kg of weight. The physical examination reveals fine inspiratory crackles on pulmonary auscultation. Chest X-ray reveals interstitial lung disease. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest shows sub-pleural and basal predominant reticulations and honeycombing. Pulmonary function test reveals a restrictive ventilatory defect with reduced diffusion capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO). She has no history of exposure to occupational dust or environmental pollutants. She has never been diagnosed with any other chronic medical condition. She is currently not taking any medication. She has no known allergies. She is married and has two children. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 55-year-old male presents with several scaly, rough patches of skin on his face and balding scalp that have been present for several months. He is concerned about the appearance and discomfort caused by these lesions. He has a history of sun exposure and has used tanning beds in the past. The patient is in good general health and does not have any significant medical history. He is not taking any medications regularly. The patient is willing to discontinue the use of tanning beds and sun parlor for the duration of the study. He agrees to use an effective method of contraception during the study and one month after its completion. The patient has 6 clinically typical, discrete, non-hyperkeratotic, non-hypertrophic AK lesions located within a contiguous 25 cm2 treatment area on his balding scalp. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions.

32 year-old woman who has been struggling with absolute uterine factor infertility for the past 5 years. She has a twin sister who has completed childbirth and is willing to donate her uterus for transplantation. The patient has a BMI of 28 and has no history of any systemic disease. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial in hopes of achieving a successful pregnancy and fulfilling her dream of starting a family.

A 32-year-old male patient diagnosed with schizophrenia has been admitted to the psychiatric ward. He has been struggling with the symptoms of the disorder for 5 years and has been hospitalized twice before. He speaks fluent German and has completed high school education. He lives alone in an apartment and is unemployed. He is currently taking antipsychotic medication as prescribed by his psychiatrist. He has expressed interest in being involved in his treatment decisions but feels uncertain about how to communicate his preferences effectively.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. She has been taking levodopa and pramipexole with a good response. However, she has recently developed swelling in her lower legs and feet, which has become bothersome to her. She also reports occasional hallucinations, but maintains insight. She has not experienced any impulsive behaviors. Upon examination, she has resting tremors, bradykinesia, and rigidity. Her cognitive function is intact. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures and give informed consent. She is not currently participating in any other clinical drug trials and does not have any medical problems that are unstable or uncontrolled. She has no history of melanoma and is not currently taking any MAO-A or B inhibitors, meperidine, tramadol, methadone, propoxyphene, dextromethorphan, or mirtazapine.

A 28-year-old man with a history of cocaine and amphetamine use disorder presents to a substance abuse clinic seeking treatment. He reports using stimulants daily for the past 2 years, and has attempted to quit multiple times without success. He currently lives with his partner and is employed as a restaurant cook. He reports experiencing significant negative affect such as depression and anxiety, which often lead to relapse. He has no current medical conditions and is not taking any medications. The patient speaks fluent English and is able to provide informed consent. He is willing and able to participate in all study procedures.

This is a 60 year-old female who has not had a colorectal cancer screening in the past 10 years. She has a family history of colon cancer in her father and her sister. She is currently asymptomatic and has no significant medical history. She is not homeless and has no severe co-morbidities limiting life expectancy. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she falls within the age range of 50 to 75 years of age and has not had a polyp requiring colonoscopic surveillance.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 25 weeks of gestation. She was diagnosed with hypertension during pregnancy and has been closely monitored by her healthcare provider. She has a history of pre-eclampsia in her previous pregnancy. She does not have any other significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to assess endothelial function in pregnant women with and without hypertension. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

A 48-year-old woman with a history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis underwent a single lung transplantation 6 months ago. Despite initial good recovery, she has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath and decreased exercise tolerance for the past 2 months. Her pulmonary function tests show a decline in FEV1 and DLCO. A transbronchial biopsy has been recommended by her physician to investigate allograft dysfunction. She has no history of malignancy, active infections, or bleeding disorders. She is currently taking tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone for immunosuppression. She is married and employed as a nurse. She is interested in participating in the study to improve diagnostic accuracy and potentially avoid unnecessary treatments.

Patient A is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing moderate to severe lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the past 6 months. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been on medical therapy, but has not seen significant improvement. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and has no other significant medical history. He has not had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) in the past. His prostate is larger than 40 cubic centimeters and his Qmax is below 15 mL/s. He is willing and able to provide written, informed consent. He has no known malignancy and his serum PSA is less than 10 ng/mL at screening. He has had a pelvic examination within the past 6 months and has no large bladder diverticula or bladder stones. He is not allergic to bovine collagen and has no contraindications related to performing an MRI. He has not received any experimental therapy in the past 4 weeks and has normal coagulation profile.

The patient is a 27-year-old Japanese male with a BMI of 24. He is in good health with no history of significant medical conditions or surgeries.
