He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He has suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture. He is sexually active and willing to use barrier contraception, such as condoms with spermicide, from the first day of dosing until 3 months after the last dose of the investigational product. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the compound AZD7687, as well as how his body handles and responds to the drug following single and multiple dosing over 7 days.

A 30-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester with a BMI of 32kg/m2 is eligible for the Walking in Pregnancy (WiP) clinical trial. She has no known risks or complications and is able to walk. She is interested in maintaining a healthy pregnancy and is willing to participate in a feasibility study aimed at increasing physical activity during pregnancy. She is comfortable with using technology and social media and is able to commit to wearing a Fitbit pedometer and joining a closed Facebook group. She is motivated to improve her physical activity level and reduce the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with confusion, altered mental status, and seizures. His family reported that he had been experiencing behavioral changes and mood swings for the past few weeks. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. Initial blood work showed elevated inflammatory markers, and a lumbar puncture revealed abnormal levels of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid. The patient was diagnosed with auto-immune encephalitis and underwent an MRI scan. The MRI scan was available for this study and showed diffusion-weighted abnormalities. The patient has provided consent for the use of his medical records and imaging for research purposes.

The patient is a 25-year-old female presenting with a 2 cm laceration on her non-dominant hand that occurred while she was cooking. The laceration is located on the dorsal aspect of her hand, just proximal to her fifth metacarpal bone. She reports no previous medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to medications or adhesives. Upon examination, there is no involvement of tendons, arteries or any other structures. Hemostasis is achieved within 10 minutes of pressure application. She consents to participate in the study and is willing to comply with follow-up visits.

Pt is a 58yo M with a history of sun exposure and a recent diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma and actinic keratosis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient has not undergone any previous treatment for these conditions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet all inclusion criteria. There is no evidence of morphea form or pigmented form of basal cell carcinoma.

32 F with a h/o MVC 2 years ago, resulting in a whiplash injury. Since then, she has had chronic neck pain and headaches which has had a significant impact on her quality of life. She has tried various treatments including physiotherapy and pain medication, but has not experienced significant relief. She has been diagnosed with WAD II-III and has trigger points in the back of her head and neck. She has experienced some pain relief with local anesthesia towards the painful areas. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effects of neurolysis and physiotherapy on her symptoms. She does not have any history of mental illness or drug/alcohol abuse, and understands and reads the Swedish language. She has not had any previous surgery in the back of her head.

45 yo female with no significant medical history and a BMI of 24. She is a non-smoker and reports no allergies or adverse reactions to food. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She has not undergone bariatric surgery or been diagnosed with any metabolic disorders. She has not been treated for cancer in the last 3 years and is not currently using any medications or supplements that may interfere with the study objectives. She is willing to give informed consent and communicate with study staff. Overall, she meets the inclusion criteria for the Measuring Daily Grain Intake Study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with liver cancer. He is scheduled for a major hepatic resection at the Department of General Surgery, Medical University of Vienna. The patient has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medication. He has been informed about the two different hepatectomy methods, CUSA and stapler hepatectomy, and has given informed consent to participate in the randomized controlled trial. The patient's preoperative imaging shows that both methods are feasible. The patient is not infected with Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, or HIV and does not have any autoimmune diseases or inflammatory conditions of the bowel such as Crohn's Disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic lower back pain. He has been experiencing symptoms for the past 3 years and has been taking pain medication to manage his condition. He has a BMI of 26 kg/m² and has never undergone surgery before. He works as a construction worker and leads an active lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and his medical history is unremarkable. He has no prior history of respiratory, cardiac, renal, or liver disease. He does not have any ongoing infections and is not allergic to voluven. The patient is scheduled for a prone position spine surgery, and the mini-fluid challenge method will be used to predict fluid responsiveness during the procedure.

A 30-year-old female with a history of Crohn's disease (CD) diagnosed based on established clinical, endoscopic, radiologic, and histologic criteria. She is scheduled for an ileocolonoscopy and has agreed to undergo a colonic capsule endoscopy (CCE) procedure within a week after the ileocolonoscopy. The patient has not had surgery of any segment of the colon or terminal ileum, and does not have non-colonic CD. She is not at high risk for capsule retention and does not have stenosis of the colon or ileum that cannot be passed by the colonoscope. Additionally, she has not received anti-TNF or biotherapy treatment after the ileocolonoscopy and before the CCE procedure. The patient has had small bowel imaging (Small Bowel Follow Through, Magnetic Resonance Enteroclysis, or Computed Tomography Enterography) performed in the last 12 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent a mastectomy on her right breast and had lymph node dissection, which resulted in lymphedema in her right arm. She has been experiencing swelling and pain in her right arm for the past year. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is managed with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently not undergoing any cancer treatment. Her grip strength in the affected arm is weaker than her non-affected arm, and she has noticed a decrease in muscle mass. She is interested in participating in the study to assess the potential benefits of complete decongestive therapy on her lymphedema and muscle strength.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing cough, fever, and shortness of breath for the past 5 days. She went to the hospital and was tested for COVID-19 using RT-PCR, but the results are still pending. She underwent a CT scan to evaluate the extent of the lung involvement. She has no underlying medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has no history of smoking or exposure to environmental toxins. Her family history is negative for COVID-19. Her CT scan shows bilateral ground-glass opacities with some consolidations in the lower lobes of the lungs. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial for the use of her CT data in the development of deep learning-based solutions for diagnosis, quantification, and prognostic estimation of COVID-19. She understands the study's purpose and gives her consent for the use of her data.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who requires an elective surgery under general anesthesia. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. Her vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 bpm, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98%. The attending anesthesiologist has determined that endotracheal intubation is necessary for the procedure. The operator assigned to intubate the patient has previously performed more than 10 intubations using the GlideScope videolaryngoscope. There are no contraindications for the use of the GlideScope in this patient.

A 50-year-old man presented to the hospital with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He has a history of gallstones and was diagnosed with choledocholithiasis. Imaging revealed an impacted stone at the ampulla of Vater. The patient is in good general health, but has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He is not allergic to any medications and does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient has not had any recent surgeries or serious medical conditions.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with acute peripheral arterial occlusion (PAO) in the left leg. He has been experiencing sudden onset of ischemic rest pain in his left foot and toes, and has difficulty walking due to lifestyle-limiting claudication. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He does not smoke and does not have any allergies to contrast agents. He has not had any endovascular or open vascular surgery in the past 30 days. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is available for follow-up assessments. He is not currently on any thrombolytic therapy and has not participated in any alfimeprase trial in the past. He is willing to undergo contrast angiography to confirm the diagnosis and eligibility for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is scheduled to receive adjuvant dose-dense anthracycline plus taxane-based chemotherapy, including paclitaxel, for a total of 12 doses. She has no history of diabetes or peripheral neuropathy and is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of head trauma, stroke, or other neurological disorders. She is not currently taking any medications that could cause facial spasms. On examination, there is visible twitching of the right facial muscles, and the patient reports discomfort during the spasms. The rest of the neurological examination is unremarkable. MRI imaging shows evidence of neurovascular compression of the facial nerve at the root entry zone. The patient is otherwise in good health and has no contraindications for MRI or other study procedures.

55-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus, who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery 10 years ago. He recently presented with chest pain and was found to have accelerated coronary artery disease with blockages in two of his bypass grafts. He is scheduled to undergo redo CABG surgery. He has no history of stroke or peripheral vascular disease. He is on medical therapy for his hypertension and diabetes mellitus. He has no allergies to medications or latex. He has no known contraindications to blood transfusions. He has a good performance status and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. He has provided informed consent for the study.

A 68-year-old man who had a stroke 6 months ago presents with persistent shoulder pain rated 6/10 on the numerical rating scale. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has no history of heart disease or other significant medical problems. He is a retired teacher and lives with his wife. He is right-handed and had a left-sided stroke that affected his right shoulder. He received physical therapy following the stroke and has made some progress with his mobility, but his shoulder pain has not improved. He reports that the pain is worse with any movement of his arm, especially with abduction and external rotation. On examination, he has limited passive range of motion of the shoulder due to pain. He is able to follow simple commands and is cognitively intact. He has no history of seizures or implanted electrical devices.

A 30-year-old healthy female with no history of chronic diseases or pathological symptoms is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and her BMI is within the range of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m^2. She has no history of gastrointestinal resection that may affect drug absorption. She has normal values for hematology and biochemistry tests of blood and urinalysis, with an eGFR greater than 80 ml/min/1.73 m^2 and normal Creatinine. She has no known hypersensitivity to the ingredients of the study intervention or Biguanides. She is not taking any medication that may affect the outcome of the study and has not participated in any other clinical studies where the last administration of previous study medication was within 6 months. She is willing to undergo venous puncture and has negative screening results for Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis B Virus antibody, Hepatitis C Virus antibody, Human Immunodeficiency Virus antibodies, and Rapid Plasma Reagin Antibody. She meets all the eligibility criteria for the GXR RM 500 mg Korea BE Study.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman from the United States who was diagnosed with endometrial cancer 18 months ago. She underwent one line of chemotherapy as adjuvant therapy and experienced progressive disease. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and her BMI is 25. Her laboratory studies are within normal limits, and she has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no history of brain or other central nervous system metastases, and her bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function are adequate. She is able to understand and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 53-year-old man who was previously diagnosed with non-ST-segment acute coronary syndrome and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug-eluting stent. He is currently taking aspirin and clopidogrel for the management of his condition. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure but is otherwise in good health. The patient has been experiencing occasional chest discomfort and shortness of breath with exertion. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study and has demonstrated endothelial dysfunction with percent flow-mediated dilation values lower than 7% at baseline. The patient is eligible for the study and will be randomly assigned to receive either ticagrelor or clopidogrel for 30 days. He will undergo flow-mediated dilation tests and blood sampling before the first dose of study drugs and at the end of the 30-day treatment period. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and follow medication guidelines throughout the study period.

40 year-old Hispanic woman who was born in Mexico and currently lives in the United States. She is overweight with a BMI of 28. She has no major medical, psychiatric or chronic problems except for controlled hypertension. She does not participate in any other weight loss treatment programs and does not plan to for at least 12-16 months. She has internet access at least once per week and is able to engage in light activity such as walking. She is interested in participating in the MiDieta eHealth portal study to help her lose weight and improve her health.

A 35-year-old female patient is scheduled for an elective gynecological surgery for the removal of uterine fibroids. She has a history of dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia. She does not have any known spinal pathologies or history of low back pain. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She has never undergone any surgeries before and has no known allergies. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to sign an informed consent form.

This is a 45 year-old male who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. MRI showed spinal canal stenosis at L4-L5 level. He has tried physical therapy, chiropractic care, and multiple medications but has not had significant relief of his pain. The patient is scheduled for a decompressive lumbar laminectomy for spinal canal stenosis. The patient has no history of renal, liver or heart disease, and is not taking any medications that would contraindicate participation in the study. The patient is willing to participate in a study evaluating the efficacy of a continuous perioperative lidocaine infusion for postoperative pain control and is able to comply with follow-up visits.

A 52-year-old woman has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. She has been experiencing insomnia, depression, and anxiety, which are affecting her quality of life. She is able to read and write Vietnamese and has a Karnofsky score of 90. Her Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score is 13 and her anxiety and depression scores, as measured by the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), are both above 8. She is not receiving any other cancer treatments and is not participating in any other research studies. She is interested in exploring alternative treatments for managing her symptoms and is willing to practice self-acupressure at home for four weeks.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during a routine antenatal checkup. She is of Middle Eastern descent and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She has no history of diabetes or any other significant medical conditions. She is currently employed as a teacher and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She is married and has one child. She has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders. She speaks Finnish fluently. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

60 year-old male with a history of knee pain and stiffness for the past month. The pain is most prominent when walking, standing, or climbing stairs. The patient also reports having difficulty bending and straightening the knee. The pain has been unresponsive to over-the-counter pain relievers. The patient has bony enlargement and has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis by his primary care physician. The patient has not participated in other clinical studies in the past 3 months and is willing to comply with study regulations. The patient has no history of allergies to similar constituents or chemical components of the drug, and no history of limited liver and kidney function, hematopoietic system disease, diabetes, Cushing's syndrome, severe heart and brain disease, or low immunity. The patient is not a woman during pregnancy or lactation.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who suffered from a distal humerus fracture in her right arm 5 months ago. She underwent surgery and had plates and screws inserted. Although the fracture has healed, she has been experiencing elbow limitation in flexion and extension. She feels pain in the elbow when performing daily activities such as carrying groceries or typing. She has not received any physiotherapy for her elbow limitation. She works as a graphic designer and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has no history of cardiovascular or neurological diseases, rheumatic diseases or psychiatric diseases. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. Her physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of progressive muscle weakness and proximal muscle wasting. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 5 years, with no family history of neuromuscular diseases. The patient has undergone multiple diagnostic tests, including EMG, nerve conduction studies, and muscle biopsy. She was diagnosed with a myopathy, but the specific cause could not be determined. Recently, she underwent NGS testing, which identified a potentially pathogenic variant in the TTN gene. She has consented to participate in the present study, which aims to perform functional studies to evaluate the effect of TTN variants on the transcripts and protein in order to improve the diagnostic approach and to perform correlation studies with the modes of inheritance and the phenotypes. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and has previously undergone muscle biopsy.

Patient is a 52-year-old woman from the United States who has been diagnosed with recurrent endometrial cancer that is not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy. She has undergone radical surgery in the past for this condition but is now experiencing a recurrence of the cancer. She has never received chemotherapy or anti-estrogen therapy for her endometrial cancer in the past. Her performance status is good (Karnofsky 90%) and she is postmenopausal. Her laboratory studies are within normal limits, with a granulocyte count of 2,000/mm3, platelet count of 120,000/mm3, and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. Her bilirubin level is 1.2 times normal, and her ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. Her creatinine level is also within normal limits. She has no other primary malignancy within the past 5 years.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy with a high risk of dental caries due to poor oral hygiene habits, a diet high in sugar, and a family history of dental caries. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would affect his eligibility for the study. He has at least two pairs of molars with initial enamel lesions in the pits and fissures or suspected dentine caries that have not been highlighted by usual clinical and radiographic examinations. He does not have any molars that are inaccessible, closed, sealed or decayed and does not require local anesthesia for the dental procedures. He has attended regular dental check-ups and is affiliated with the Social Security program.

A 58-year-old man was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer after a biopsy procedure. He has no previous history of radiation therapy or hormonal treatment for prostate cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve the accuracy of prostate cancer detection. He has no allergies to latex and has no metal implants or other conditions that may distort the magnetic field. His doctor has recommended magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) to further evaluate his condition. He is willing to undergo two MRSI studies, one with air and one with perfluorocarbon (PFC), to compare the quality of the images. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

58 year-old man with a history of prostate cancer, status post prostatectomy, now presents with abdominal pain and bloating. CT abdomen and pelvis reveals a 7 cm soft-tissue mass in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen, which appears to be involving the left adrenal gland. CT-guided biopsy of the mass confirmed metastatic prostate cancer. He has been treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his disease is no longer responsive to these treatments. He reports moderate pain in the abdomen that is not relieved by over-the-counter pain medications. He has a performance status of 1 and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He is able to provide written informed consent and has adequate hematologic, hepatic and renal functions. He has no history of diabetes and is not taking steroidal or hormonal therapy. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no known allergies to monoclonal antibodies or other therapeutic proteins. He is not an employee of the investigator or study center with direct involvement in this study or other studies under the direction of the investigator or study center and has no family members who are.

The patient is a 58-year-old female diagnosed with arterial fibrillation (AF) and started on oral anti-coagulation therapy (NOAC) with Eliquis® (apixaban) 8 months ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. She has no known allergies and has never had any adverse reactions to medications. Her current medication regimen includes Eliquis® (apixaban) 5mg twice daily. She reports occasional forgetfulness in taking her medication on time and has missed a few doses in the past. The patient lives alone and is able to manage her own medication regimen. She has no significant physical disabilities or impairments that would affect her ability to use the ReX-C device. She is able to read and understand the Informed Consent Form and has given her consent to participate in the study. The patient is receiving treatment at home and her medication dose has been stable for the past 3 months.

32 yo F with a history of HIV infection for 4 years. The patient was diagnosed with HIV after being tested during a routine check-up at a community health clinic. The patient has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 3 years and has maintained an undetectable viral load. She reports a history of unprotected sex with her partner who is HIV-positive. She has had no sexually transmitted infections in the past year. Her last gynecologic exam was normal. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the levels and types of HIV found in the blood compared to the female genital tract. She is willing to follow the study protocol which includes regular visits for blood and genital tract collections. The patient is aware that she may need to change her antiretroviral regimen during the study and she is willing to comply with the study requirements. She meets the inclusion criteria for Group 2 of the study as her viral load is undetectable and she has not failed an antiretroviral regimen.

A 27-year-old healthy female volunteer with a body mass index of 22 kg/m² and normal hemoglobin levels is suitable for this clinical trial. She has no history of smoking, regular medication use or abuse of alcoholic beverages and drugs. Her medical history and physical examination are normal except for a history of mild iron deficiency anemia, which was successfully treated with oral iron supplements. She is not currently taking any iron supplements or food supplements containing iron. She has no history of hypertension, pathologic hyperglycemia or hyperlipidemia, and her serum AST and ALAT levels are normal. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past three weeks and is willing to attend all scheduled study visits. She has signed informed consent and is willing to practice effective barrier methods for birth control. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who works in the tech industry. He has a history of anxiety and panic attacks, for which he has been prescribed alprazolam extended-release tablets 3 mg (generic version). He has been taking this medication for the past 6 months and finds it helpful in managing his symptoms. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he does drink alcohol occasionally at social events. He is not currently taking any other medications, including hormonal contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy. He is in good overall health and has not experienced any recent significant changes in his dietary or exercise habits. He weighs 70 kg and is within 5% of his ideal body weight. He has never been institutionalized and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has no known allergies to any of the study medications or inactive ingredients. He has not donated or lost a significant volume of blood or plasma within the past 28 days. He has not consumed grapefruit or any grapefruit-containing products within the past 7 days.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He works as a construction worker and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a family history of stroke and heart disease. He has not experienced any prior stroke symptoms. He noticed sudden onset of weakness in his left arm while at work and quickly called for emergency medical services. The paramedics arrived within 10 minutes and assessed him with an AVPU scale, which showed he was alert. He was then diagnosed with acute stroke and his blood pressure was noted to be elevated (systolic BP >160mm Hg). He is transported to a hospital that is a PIL-FAST trial site. The patient is able to give verbal consent to participate in the study. He does not have any allergies or contraindications to lisinopril or any other ACE-inhibitor medication. He is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial. His pulse is within normal range, and he is not experiencing any seizure activity or hypoglycemia. He is able to walk independently prior to the stroke.

This is a 28-year-old female with no known medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help assess the bioequivalence of Epanutin Infatabs® 50 mg sourced from Germany and Dilantin Infatabs® 50 mg sourced from Australia. She has signed the informed consent document and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient has no evidence or history of clinically significant abnormalities and has not undergone gastrectomy. She falls within the age range of 21 to 55 years, inclusive, and is in good health.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who is interested in participating in a clinical trial on cognitive training. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently being treated with medication. He has no history of stroke, diabetes, major surgeries, or psychiatric disorders. He is a native speaker of English and has completed high school education. He is in overall good health and does not have any cognitive impairment. He is physically active and enjoys going for walks and doing light exercises. He is interested in participating in the reasoning-trained group of the study and is willing to undergo brain imaging to evaluate any changes in brain function. He is excited about the possibility of this study contributing to the development of non-pharmacological interventions to prevent mental decline and maximize cognitive brain health in seniors.

Patient is a 55-year-old resident of Texas who has been diagnosed with stage III rectal cancer and has completed treatment within the last year. They are able to read, speak and write English and are 18 years or older. The patient has expressed distress and scored a T score >63 on the Global Severity Index (GSI) of the Brief Symptom Inventory (BSI) or a T score >63 on any two primary dimensions of this measure. They reside within one hour of M.D. Anderson Cancer Center and are willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old right-handed female with no history of neurological or psychiatric disease. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no cognitive deficits that would restrict understanding of the tasks. She is not under guardianship, curator or any other administrative or judicial measure of deprivation of rights or liberty. The patient is not currently participating in any other study. She has no history of cardiac electrostimulation or defibrillator, cardiac prostheses, intracranial clips or clamps, cerebrospinal fluid disorders, metal particles in the eyes, metal dental or articular prostheses, diffusion pomp, or other infusion system. She does not suffer from claustrophobia and does not have any head tattoos, make-up, or hair gel. She is using a non-copper intrauterine device (IUD). She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

This is a 25 year-old male from Tajikistan who recently arrived in St. Petersburg, Russia to work as a construction worker. He is currently living in a crowded apartment with several other labor migrants from his home country. He speaks limited Russian but is able to communicate in Tajik. He has heard about HIV but has limited knowledge about how it is transmitted and how to protect himself. He is single and looking for a girlfriend in Russia. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written consent.

Alice is a 30-year-old woman who works as a graphic designer. She lives in California with her partner and their two cats. Alice has been experiencing stress and difficulty focusing at work lately, which has been affecting her productivity. She has tried different relaxation techniques in the past, but hasn't found one that works for her. She owns a smartphone and uses it regularly for communication and social media. Alice is interested in participating in the MINEs study to see if any of the five interventions (gratitude journaling, mindfulness meditation, random acts of kindness, physical activity, and laughter therapy) can help improve her stress levels and cognitive focus. She is fluent in English and is excited to try out the different activities to see if they work for her. Alice has no pre-existing cardiovascular disease and is cleared by her physician to engage in new types of physical activity.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 5 years. She participated in the ADDRESS II core trial (NCT01972568) and completed the 24-week treatment period. She did not meet any of the discontinuation criteria and was invited to participate in this long-term extension (LTE) study (NCT02070978) to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of atacicept. She is a woman of childbearing potential and has had a negative pregnancy test. She does not have any active neurological symptoms of SLE that are deemed severe or progressive, nor has she been diagnosed with any demyelinating disease such as multiple sclerosis or optic neuritis. She is not pregnant and does not have any active clinically significant viral, bacterial, or fungal infection. She is willing to participate in this study to help further the understanding of the long-term safety and tolerability of atacicept in the treatment of SLE.

54F with a history of dry eye symptoms for several years, including ocular discomfort, burning, and redness. She has been using over-the-counter lubricating eye drops without significant relief. She reports no history of ocular infection or surgery. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hypothyroidism, all well-controlled with medications. On examination, her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and intraocular pressures are within normal limits. Slit lamp examination reveals mild punctate epithelial erosions and mild conjunctival injection. She is willing to comply with all study procedures, including the use of study eye drops and follow-up visits. She has signed the informed consent and has no known allergies to the test article or its components.

45-year-old female with a history of metastatic breast cancer that has progressed on standard of care therapy. She has also been diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer that has progressed on or after standard of care therapy. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and meets all laboratory parameters required for the study. The patient has evaluable or measurable disease by RECISTv1.1. The patient has not received chemotherapy, biological or investigational therapy in the past 14 days. She does not use any medication known to result in a prolongation of the QT/QTc interval or any medication that is a strong inducer or substrate of cytochrome P450 3A. The patient does not have any central nervous system metastases or a known history of leptomeningeal metastases. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C infection. The patient has no history of clinically significant cardiovascular abnormalities, and her blood pressure is controlled. She has no serious active infection at the time of treatment, or any other serious underlying medical condition that would impair the ability of the patient to receive protocol treatment. The patient is willing to provide tumor tissue (archival preferred) prior to study entry and agrees to use adequate contraception throughout the study and for at least 30 days following the last dose of PMD-026.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been smoking an average of 10 cigarettes per day for the past 5 years. He recently suffered a knee injury and has been referred to an orthopaedic specialist for management. He is a native English speaker and currently not receiving any smoking cessation medications or counseling. He does not have any impairments and is not a user of other tobacco products. He lives alone and does not have any family members who smoke. He is interested in quitting smoking and has expressed a desire to participate in a clinical trial that could help him achieve that goal.

55-year-old male with relapsed multiple myeloma after receiving one prior line of therapy. He has not been refractory to prior lenalidomide and did not discontinue lenalidomide due to a Grade ≥ 3 related adverse event. The patient has not participated in elotuzumab studies CA204-004, CA204-006 or CA204-009. He has no active plasma cell leukemia or significant cardiac disease, and is negative for HIV and hepatitis A, B, and C. The patient has undergone prior myeloma therapy but has adequately recovered from it. He has no medical conditions that would impose excessive risk to him and is not hypersensitive to lenalidomide, dexamethasone, any excipients in the elotuzumab formulation, or recombinant protein. The patient is willing to participate in the expanded access program and is seeking access to elotuzumab in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone.

A 50-year-old male smoker with a history of locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer that has progressed after first-line therapy with taxane. The patient has no clinically apparent CNS metastases or carcinomatous meningitis and is amenable to radiologic imaging techniques. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, and normal hematopoietic and renal function. The patient has no other severe disease, infection, or comorbidity that would preclude study participation and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has not received any investigational agents in the past 4 weeks and is not on any concurrent anticonvulsants or high-dose acetaminophen.

We are looking for healthy male or female volunteers between the ages of 18 to 50 years old (for young healthy volunteers) or between the ages of 65 to 80 years old (for elderly healthy volunteers), who have a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2. Participants should have normal findings in a medical examination, including blood pressure, pulse rate, and electrocardiogram. Participants should not have any laboratory values outside the reference range or any evidence of a concomitant disease judged as clinically relevant by the investigator. Additionally, participants should not have any gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. Participants should not have a history of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts, or any chronic or relevant acute infections. Further exclusion criteria may apply. Participants must provide a signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study in accordance with good clinical practice (GCP) and local legislation. Female participants who are surgically sterilized or postmenopausal (defined as at least 1 year of spontaneous amenorrhea) may also be eligible to participate.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. He underwent several rounds of chemotherapy but did not achieve remission. The medical team recommended hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and the patient's parents agreed. The patient will undergo allogeneic HSCT using stem cells from an unrelated donor. The patient has no known allergies and has not experienced any infections during his treatment. He will receive prophylactic antimicrobial treatment post-transplantation. The patient's family has no history of autoimmune diseases.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a family history of congenital vertical talus (CVT). She has been experiencing foot pain and difficulty walking since childhood. Her mother and younger sister also have foot deformities and experience similar symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is married and has two children. The physical examination reveals bilateral vertical talus, rigid hindfoot valgus and forefoot abduction, rocker-bottom deformity and a prominent talar head. X-rays of her feet confirm the diagnosis of CVT. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to identify the genes responsible for this inherited disorder in hopes of finding better treatments for herself and her family members.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired teacher who is scheduled to undergo an elective surgical procedure for a hernia repair. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with Lisinopril 20 mg daily. She has also been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and takes ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain. The patient has never had surgery before and is anxious about the procedure. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of asthma, chronic pulmonary diseases, glaucoma, diabetes, neurological or psychiatric disorders, Parkinson's disease, or disorders of the gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as she is over 60 years of age, has an ASA physical status of I-III, and is scheduled for general anesthesia for her surgery. She does not meet the exclusion criteria and may be eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male who works full time in a shared laboratory environment with at least 3 other employees. He has not experienced any symptoms of SARS-CoV-2 infection, such as fever, cough, sore throat, or shortness of breath. He is fully able to consent to the study and its procedures and is available to participate in the study for the full duration of the trial. He works on-site at least 3 full working days a week and is interested in contributing to the understanding of the epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2. He has not participated in any other clinical trials involving exclusion periods.

A 55-year-old male patient who has been a smoker for about 30 years is experiencing shortness of breath and coughing. He is a construction worker and spends most of his workday outdoors. He has been experiencing these symptoms for about 6 months and has not sought medical attention yet. He has a history of high blood pressure, for which he takes medication regularly. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. He speaks English fluently and has not seen a pulmonary specialist in the past 3 years. He is willing to be part of the study and does not plan to move away from the city in the next year.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman with a history of irregular menstrual cycles, acne, and excessive hair growth on the face and body. She has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and is currently overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m^2. Her weight has been stable for the past three months. She is currently using non-hormonal methods of contraception. She has not had a menstrual period in the past 30 days. She does not have any medical conditions that may significantly alter the absorption, metabolism, or excretion of the study drug. She has not been pregnant or nursing in the past 6 months. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

Patient is a 26-year-old pregnant woman in her 16th week of gestation. She resides in Dhaka, Bangladesh and plans to remain in the city for the duration of the study. The patient has a history of regular prenatal care and has not experienced any complications in her current pregnancy. She does not have a history of severe anemia and her hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about prenatal micronutrient supplementation. She is open to trying different delivery vehicles for the supplement and is committed to regularly consuming the supplements as directed.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male participants who have no history of significant medical conditions or compromised immune status. Participants must have a body mass index between 18.0 to 32.0 kg/m2 and weigh at least 50 kg. They must not have any history or risk for tuberculosis (TB) or any acute or chronic bacterial, fungal, or viral infection within the 3 months prior to screening. Participants must not have a history of or active liver disease, known or suspected autoimmune disorder, or any history of known or suspected congenital or acquired immunodeficiency state or condition. Additionally, participants must not have received live vaccines within 60 days before screening. Other protocol defined inclusion/exclusion criteria could also apply. For more information, interested individuals can visit www.BMSStudyConnect.com.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with Fitzpatrick skin type III. He has 6-7 mild to moderate grade actinic keratosis lesions on his forehead and scalp which are non-hypertrophic and non-hyperkeratotic. He has not used any prohibited medications for the past 60 days and is willing to use contraception during the study period. He has not participated in any other clinical research study in the past 60 days and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He does not have any autoimmune, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, hematological, hepatic, neurologic, pulmonary, or renal disease. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant. He has not undergone any cosmetic or therapeutic procedures, such as laser or peeling, within 2 weeks and within 2 cm of the selected treatment area. He has no other skin conditions within the selected treatment area and has not used sun lamps or tanning beds or booths during the past 14 days, nor does he plan to use them during the study. He has not undergone any systemic cancer therapy within the past 6 months.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and no significant past surgical history, who is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient has no known allergies and is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension. The patient's height is 5'7" and weight is 68 kg, with an ASA physical status classification of II. No other significant medical history was reported.

John is a 62-year-old man who is a retired teacher. He has been a smoker for 30 years and currently smokes 10 cigarettes per day. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. Recently, he has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He underwent a series of tests and was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). His cancer was confirmed to be Stage IIA by chest computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET) scan. Due to his medical conditions, he cannot undergo thoracic surgery, so he has decided to receive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) as definitive therapy. John has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive SBRT plus pembrolizumab (MK-3475) as he hopes it will prolong his overall survival. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the study, including having adequate organ function and not having received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 agent. However, he has not participated in any study of an investigational agent or used an investigational device within the past four weeks.

75yo male with a diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's disease for 2 years, receiving treatment with a cholinesterase inhibitor, with a MMSE of 18. Patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and a remote history of smoking. The patient lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus or hypoglycemia. The patient is able to swallow oral medications and has no evidence of hepatic or renal insufficiency. The patient is fluent in English and has no history of major mental illness, seizure or head trauma with disturbance of consciousness within the past two years. The patient has not used any investigational drug within the past two months. The patient is not currently using any of the excluded medication.

55 year-old man diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He underwent surgical biopsy that confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma. CT scan showed metastasis to the liver and lungs. He received gemcitabine as first line therapy but his disease progressed. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or active infection requiring antibiotics. His Karnofsky performance status is 80 and he understands the purposes and risks of the study and has signed a written informed consent form approved by the investigator's IRB/Ethics Committee. He is willing to use effective means of contraception from entry into the study through 6 months after the last dose. His laboratory test results show hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL.

A 65-year-old woman presents with decreased vision in her left eye for the past 3 months. She has a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and has been receiving intravitreal injections of ranibizumab in her left eye every 4 weeks for the past year. However, her vision has continued to decline despite treatment. On examination, her left eye has a best-corrected visual acuity of 55 letters, and spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) shows evidence of fluid and swelling in the macula. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study, including the presence of active choroidal neovascularization (CNV) lesions in the central subfield of the study eye confirmed by fluorescein angiography, intra- and/or subretinal fluid affecting the central subfield of the study eye at Screening/Baseline, and a BCVA between 83 and 23 letters in the study eye. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including having poor quality of OCT-A and SD-OCT images at Screening/Baseline, atrophy or fibrosis involving the center of the fovea in the study eye, and history of malignancy of any organ system within the past 5 years. She is willing to attend the mandatory study visits and provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old male patient, weighing 80 kg, was admitted to the hospital with a severe headache and neck pain. He was diagnosed with a brain tumor and required a CT scan followed by MRI. He has no history of spine fracture and is able to move his limbs. He is accompanied by his wife, who is his primary caregiver. They have signed the informed consent and are willing to participate in the study. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. He works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is eager to participate in the trial to help improve the safety and comfort of patient transfers for both himself and the nursing staff.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic headaches for the past year. She reports that the headaches occur at least once a week and last for several hours. She describes the pain as a dull ache that is located on both sides of her head. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but they only provide temporary relief. She has no history of cognitive or neurological disorders. She is married and works as a teacher. She enjoys spending time with her family and friends, reading, and practicing yoga. She speaks Turkish fluently and is willing to participate in a study to help improve the understanding and treatment of headaches in her community.

The patient is a 45-year-old Asian male with a body mass index (BMI) of 35. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are both controlled with medication. He has tried various weight loss programs and diets in the past, but has been unable to achieve sustained weight loss. He is interested in bariatric surgery as a potential solution to his obesity and related health issues. He does not have a history of myocardial infarction, angina pectoris or ischemic stroke in the past month, and his congestive heart failure is classified as less than class IV based on the New York Heart Association classification. He does not have any malignancies or other conditions with poor prognosis, and his pulmonary and renal function are normal. He is compliant with medical treatment and is able to attend follow-up appointments. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

This clinical trial does not involve patients directly, but rather emergency nurses who will receive an educational and organizational intervention to improve the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction in patients. Therefore, no patient description is required.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma based on the presence of M-protein in the serum and radiographic evidence of osteolytic lesions. The patient has been receiving conventional-dose chemotherapy as initial therapy but has not achieved complete remission. The patient has a genotypically identical sibling donor and is eligible for the study. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and the LVEF is greater than 40% at rest. The patient has no significant history of cardiac or pulmonary disease but has a history of corticosteroid use. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and the patient is willing to use effective contraception if fertile.

A 16-year-old male diagnosed with B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) with high-risk features. He has undergone treatment with standard chemotherapy regimens, including 4-drug induction, BFM consolidation, and interim maintenance with high-dose methotrexate. However, the patient remains MRD positive at end of consolidation (EOC) and is therefore eligible for this trial. The patient has a Lansky performance status of 80% and adequate organ function, including normal renal, hepatic, and pulmonary function. The patient has not received previous anti-CD19 therapy or gene or engineered T cell therapy. The patient's bone marrow MRD will be assessed by central laboratory analysis prior to screening.

Smith is a 62 year old man who was brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, he was noted to have right-sided hemiparesis and facial droop. National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 15. A CT scan of the head showed a left middle cerebral artery stroke. Smith was immediately started on tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and admitted to the stroke unit for further management. His blood pressures were controlled with intravenous antihypertensive medication. He is conscious and cooperative with the medical staff. He will be informed about the study and will be given the option to participate.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic back pain due to degenerative disc disease. He is scheduled for an upcoming orthopedic surgery to treat his condition. The patient is ASA physical status II and has no known allergies to medications. He has not used any narcotic medications for his back pain in the last 6 months. The patient has no history of bleeding disorder, cardiovascular disorder, liver or renal failure, or neurologic disorder. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 40-year-old female with a history of recurrent epigastric pain and elevated liver function tests, underwent ultrasound which showed gallstones with evidence of common bile duct stones. She was scheduled for an ERCP procedure to remove the stones. She has no significant past medical history and is currently taking no medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her physical exam is unremarkable, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 58 year-old female with a recent diagnosis of metastatic lung cancer. She reports experiencing shortness of breath that started after her cancer diagnosis. She has been receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy as treatment for her cancer. She does not have any chest wall deformities or neuromuscular disorders. She denies any history of congestive heart failure, sarcoid disease, pneumonia, or obesity. She is currently experiencing moderate to severe shortness of breath that interferes with her daily activities. She has no prior experience with acupuncture. Her life expectancy is at least 4 weeks. She is interested in exploring alternative treatments to manage her symptoms.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pelvic pain and menstrual cramps for several years. She has been diagnosed with deep endometriosis after undergoing clinical examination, MRI, and surgery. She has been recommended to undergo surgery to remove the endometriosis with or without endometriomas. She has a BMI of 26, which falls under Class II according to the classification by the HAS. She has breastfed her two children in the past. She has no known allergies and is not currently pregnant. She has consented to the collection of omental and/or parietal adipose tissue samples for the study.

A 35-year-old female presented with a history of recurrent episodes of cold-induced pain, numbness, and tingling in her fingers and toes. She also reported experiencing these symptoms during times of emotional stress. She was diagnosed with Raynaud's syndrome by her primary care physician and referred to a specialist for further evaluation and treatment. She had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications at the time of the evaluation. She reported occasional alcohol consumption and denied tobacco use. On physical examination, she had no signs of peripheral vascular disease and her neurological exam was normal. She reported having 2-3 vasospastic attacks per week, which typically lasted for 10-15 minutes. She rated the severity of her attacks as moderate, with a pain score of 5 on a scale of 0-10. Her baseline quality of life score was 70 out of 100. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for her condition.

This is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 29 weeks pregnant with a history of preterm labor. She has been closely monitored by her obstetrician and has been receiving antenatal steroids to promote fetal lung development. She presents to the hospital in active labor and gives birth to a baby boy at 31 weeks and 3 days gestational age. The baby requires stabilization with VPP and is enrolled in this study. The baby weighs 1430 grams and has no congenital malformations or chromosomal aberrations. The Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes are 6 and 8, respectively. The cord blood pH is 7.25. The baby is randomized to Group 1, where the parameters of lung mechanics would be visible to the rescuer. The baby is closely monitored during the intervention, and blood gases are obtained. The parents have provided informed consent for the baby's participation in this study.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who presented with persistent right shoulder pain and weakness. MRI revealed a full-thickness rotator cuff tear involving the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons. He underwent DEXA scans and was found to have osteoporosis with a T-score of -2.7 at the lumbar spine and -2.5 at the hip. However, the BMD of the GT of the affected proximal humerus was within normal limits. He has no history of fractures or surgeries on the affected shoulder and has never been diagnosed with glenohumeral osteoarthritis or shoulder instability. He does not have any neurologic or systemic diseases affecting the shoulder joint. He does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is willing to undergo primary arthroscopic repair and follow-up for a minimum of 2 years after the surgery.

32-year-old male with cystic fibrosis, diagnosed at age 3. He has a history of recurrent pulmonary exacerbations and decreased lung function, with a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 45% predicted. He has been experiencing symptoms of hyperglycemia, such as increased thirst and urination, and was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis related diabetes (CFRD) 6 months ago. He is currently managed with insulin therapy and dietary modifications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the pathophysiology of CFRD and how it relates to altered metabolism in people with cystic fibrosis.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pelvic pain for the past year. She describes the pain as a constant dull ache, which occasionally becomes sharp, and it occurs mostly in the lower abdomen and pelvic region. She has already undergone several diagnostic tests, including ultrasound, MRI, and CT scan, which have not provided any conclusive findings. She has no history of endometriosis or any other chronic medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications, and she has not undergone any surgery in the past. She is sexually active with regular menstrual cycles and no history of sexually transmitted infections. She has a BMI of 27 and has no major comorbidities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help identify the source of her pelvic pain and possibly find a less invasive treatment option.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male with a confirmed diagnosis of cervical dystonia. He has had symptoms for the past 3 years, which started gradually and then worsened over time. The patient reports having difficulty turning his head to the right, which has caused him significant pain and discomfort. He also reports that his voice has become hoarse and his head tilts to the left. He has been treated with botulinum toxin injections in the past, which have helped to alleviate his symptoms. He is currently not taking any medication for depression or anxiety. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no family history of dystonia or other neurological disorders. He is fluent in English and has no claustrophobia. MRI screening form shows no metal in any part of his body, and he meets the weight requirements for MRI safety. He is not pregnant nor has a history of serious medical illness. He is willing and able to participate in the study.

A 12-year-old patient with Class II division 1 malocclusion, retrognathic mandible, and increased overjet of 6mm is being considered for orthodontic treatment. They have normal or mildly prognathic maxilla, horizontal to average growth pattern and no severe crowding in dental arches. The patient has never undergone any orthodontic treatment before and has no history of systemic disease affecting bone or growth. The patient's parents have given their informed written consent to participate in a controlled clinical study comparing the treatment effects of PowerScope2 and Forsus Fatigue Resistant Device in patients with Class II division 1 malocclusion. The patient will be randomly allocated to receive either PowerScope2 or Forsus Fatigue Resistant Device as part of their treatment. CBCT scans will be taken before and after the functional phase of treatment to evaluate changes caused by the appliance. Regular follow-up appointments will be scheduled until Class I molar relationship is achieved.

A 44-year-old woman with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 came to the clinic concerned about her weight. She has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. She has tried to lose weight in the past but has been unsuccessful. She does not have a history of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or psychiatric problems. She is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her lose weight and improve her health.

52-year-old male with a history of recurrent meningioma. The initial diagnosis was a grade II chordoid meningioma, and the patient underwent resection and radiotherapy in 2015. In 2018, a new lesion was found on imaging, and the patient underwent a second surgery followed by radiotherapy. The patient has been experiencing progressive neurological symptoms, including headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty with coordination. The most recent MRI shows a 30% increase in the size of the recurrent tumor, and the patient has been deemed ineligible for further local therapy. The patient has not received any prior systemic anti-neoplastic therapy for meningioma. The patient's performance status is 1 according to the WHO criteria, and the patient has adequate liver, renal, and hematological function, as well as normal cardiac function. The patient has no history of serious illness or medical conditions, but has a history of hypertension, which is being managed with medication. The patient is willing to undergo a highly effective method of birth control during the study treatment period, as defined by the investigator. The patient has been informed of the study protocol and follow-up schedule and has given written informed consent according to ICH/GCP and national/local regulations.

The patient is a 25 year old male who works as a bartender. He reports using opioids recreationally on a semi-regular basis for the past year, typically on weekends with friends. He has never been diagnosed with substance dependence or sought treatment for drug abuse. He reports occasional marijuana use but denies any recent use of other illicit substances. He has no history of sleep apnea or positive results for Hepatitis B or C and HIV on screening. He is interested in participating in the study to help further research on the abuse potential of opioids.

The patient is a Danish individual diagnosed with Fabry disease, a recessively inherited disorder caused by the lack of the lysosomal enzyme α-galactosidase. They have not yet started enzyme substitution therapy and have undergone baseline eye examination. The patient may have experienced symptoms such as angiofibroma or painful acro-paresthesias. They may also have ophthalmic findings such as cornea verticillata, brown-yellow Bowman membrane related corneal deposits, and teleangiectatic conjunctival vessels. Fundus vessel tortuosity may also be observed, though best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is usually normal. The patient must have no missing values for eye examination at baseline or follow-up to be eligible for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has a history of painful menstrual cycles and pain during intercourse. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not take any medications or supplements. She has regular menstrual cycles with a duration of 5-7 days and moderate flow. Her BMI is within the normal range. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has not undergone any fertility treatments in the past. She has been diagnosed with endometriosis based on symptoms and laparoscopic findings. She has not received any hormone replacement therapy or used oral contraceptives in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the relationship between telomerase activity and endometriosis-related infertility.

A 35-year-old woman has been suffering from atopic dermatitis for the last 10 years. She has tried several topical treatments, but they only provided temporary relief. She has also experienced worsening of her condition in the last few months. Her medical history is remarkable for asthma, for which she is prescribed a daily inhaler. She smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no known drug allergies. On examination, there are erythematous, scaly, and lichenified lesions on the flexural surfaces of her elbows, knees, and neck. The affected areas are itchy, and she has been scratching them, causing excoriations. Her body surface area involvement is about 20%. She has an Investigator Global Assessment score of 3, Eczema Area and Severity Index score of 25, and Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale score of 7. She is willing to discontinue current AD medications and use contraception during the study.

The purpose of this clinical trial is to investigate the impact that chronic kidney disease (CKD) and its treatments have on an individual's life, specifically their psychosocial well-being. The study aims to get insight into the perceptions of individuals at advanced stages of CKD (stages G4 and G5) and those undergoing different forms of renal replacement therapy (RRT) including in-centre haemodialysis (ICHD), home haemodialysis (HHD), peritoneal dialysis (PD), and transplantation. Participants must be over 18 years old, fluent in English, and able to provide written informed consent. Exclusion criteria include individuals with neurological or psychiatric diagnoses, those who have commenced RRT within three months of the study start date, and transplant patients being seen in clinic more than once every fortnight. If you have advanced CKD or are undergoing different forms of RRT and are interested in sharing your experiences, please consider participating in this study. Your participation can help improve the understanding of the impact of CKD and RRT on individuals' lives and lead to better interventions to improve individuals' psychosocial well-being.

Patient is a 68-year-old male from the United States. He is retired and enjoys playing golf and gardening as hobbies. He reports occasional pain in his right thumb, but has not sought care for it from a hand surgeon. He has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. He is fluent in English and has good literacy skills.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman diagnosed with osteoarthritis (OA) in both knees. She reports experiencing pain that worsens with weight support, morning stiffness, and after periods of inactivity. She has a BMI of 30, indicating she is overweight. The patient is currently undergoing clinical treatment for OA, but has not undergone any previous knee surgeries or infiltrations in the knees within the last 6 months. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders or inflammatory diseases in the gastrointestinal tract. Her creatinine clearance is greater than 60 ml/min/1.73m2, indicating normal kidney function. She has no personal history of cognitive, psychiatric, or neurological disorders that could interfere with the assimilation of given guidelines. The patient is able to read, understand, and respond to questionnaires, and is willing to attend scheduled appointments and perform tasks as instructed by professionals.

The patient is a 22-year-old male who presents with bilateral impacted mandibular third molars, causing him pain and discomfort. His medical history is unremarkable, and he is a non-smoker with good oral hygiene. He has not taken any medications or drugs for the past 10 days, and his radiographic examination shows no signs of associated inflammatory or osteolytic pathologies. He has a high extraction difficulty index of >7 according to Pederson's scale and a degree of IV on a modified version of Parant's scale, indicating that the procedure will be complex. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his informed consent.

A 50-year-old male was referred to the clinic for evaluation of his worsening kidney function. He was diagnosed with Stage 3 CKD two years ago and his kidney function has gradually declined since then. He has no significant medical history, but he takes medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. His estimated GFR is 30 ml/min and his serum ferritin levels are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore potential new treatments for his condition.

45 yo female with a history of Raynaud's phenomenon for the past 10 years presenting with recurrent episodes of cold-induced numbness and pain in her fingers and toes. Her symptoms have been unresponsive to current treatments including calcium channel blockers and vasodilators. She has previously tried multiple non-pharmacological interventions such as hand warmers and protective gloves but with minimal relief. She is currently on no medications for Raynaud's. She is a non-smoker and has no history of upper extremity vascular surgery or allergy to abobotulinum toxin A. She has health insurance and is able to read and speak English. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her Raynaud's symptoms. Past Medical History: - Raynaud's phenomenon - Hypertension - Migraines - Seasonal allergies - Anxiety

The patient is a 27-year-old female who is a non-smoker and has no history of chronic medical conditions. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and is physically active, exercising at least 3 times a week. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or any other cardiovascular disease risk factors. She does not take any medications or supplements that affect endothelial function. She presents to the clinic for the clinical trial on leptin and endothelial function. She is interested in participating in the study and has no concerns about the potential risks or side effects of the study medication. She understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with the protocol. She is able to provide written informed consent and agrees to attend all study visits as required. Her baseline vascular studies and blood tests are normal.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has recently been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). He has been enrolled in COG-9900, COG-C1991, COG-AALL03B1, COG-AALL05B1, COG-AALL08P1, or other current COG or legacy trials for ALL and has consented to submit blood and marrow samples for biological research studies. The patient has had blood and/or marrow samples collected on or after Day 28 of remission indication therapy or at the time of ALL diagnosis. The patient has no known genetic history of cancer and does not have any other significant medical history. The patient will be contributing to research that may help identify biomarkers related to cancer and predict how well patients will respond to treatment.

Patient is a 45-year-old Thai male who has been diagnosed with alcohol dependence for the past 5 years. He reports a history of binge drinking, with a typical pattern of drinking 6-8 standard drinks per session, 3-4 times per week. He has a family history of alcoholism with his father and grandfather also having alcohol use disorders. The patient reports experiencing withdrawal symptoms such as sweating, tremors, and anxiety when he tries to cut back on his alcohol consumption. He has never received any formal treatment for his alcohol use disorder but is motivated to quit drinking. He denies any history of major psychiatric disorders, suicidal ideation or attempts. He is currently not taking any other medications, and denies using other substances except for tobacco. He has no history of medical diseases or cognitive impairment, and his laboratory tests are within normal limits. He is not allergic to gabapentin. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 40-year-old man presents with a BMI of 36. He has a family history of obesity-related comorbidities such as diabetes, hypertension and heart disease. He reports difficulty in losing weight despite previous attempts at diet and exercise. He is motivated to learn weight management strategies and is willing to undergo indirect calorimetry testing. He is not taking any weight loss medication and has not had bariatric surgery. He has no history of diabetes or thyroid disorder. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is married and has two children. He works as a desk-bound accountant and reports a sedentary lifestyle. He is willing to adhere to the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol.

The patient is a 67 year old female who has recently been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath and frequent infections. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Laboratory results show anemia and thrombocytopenia. A bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of acute myeloblastic leukemia (AML) according to WHO 2008 classification. She has not been previously treated for AML and is willing to participate in an observational study aimed at estimating the incidence, typology, and evolution of patients aged 60 years or older with AML. She meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. She has signed informed consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a 45yo F who is concerned about the appearance of her mid-face due to aging. The patient reports a history of facial fillers in the past with no complications. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of significant medical problems. The patient reports no allergies to lidocaine, amide anesthetics, hyaluronic acid, or any components of the device to be used in the study. The patient is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of ANIMERS Chiara LA and JUVÉDERM VOLUMA® for aging mid-face. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of age 30-60 years and midface volume deficit scale of 2-5. The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria listed for the trial.

This is a 32-year-old female who has been suffering from heavy menstrual bleeding for the past year. Her menstrual periods are usually very heavy, and she experiences them for an average of seven days. She has tried taking over-the-counter pain medication, but it has not helped much. She has also tried using pads and tampons, but still experiences significant bleeding. She has not been diagnosed with any structural or organic pathology as an underlying cause of her heavy menstrual bleeding. She has not been treated with dydrogesterone or any other medication for her condition. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if dydrogesterone can help reduce the severity of her bleeding and improve her quality of life.
