She is not nursing, has no history of liver disease, and is not taking any NSAIDs.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with multiple myeloma. She has no previous history of cancer and is currently experiencing bone pain, fatigue, and weight loss. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1, meaning that she is able to perform most activities, but experiences some fatigue. She has not previously undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and is ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant (Auto-SCT) due to her age. She has measurable disease and has not received any prior therapy with anti-programmed cell death 1 receptor (anti-PD-1), anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (anti-PD-L1), anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, or anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) antibody. She has no known Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C infection. She is willing to undergo thromboembolic prophylaxis and is not lactose intolerant. The patient is a good candidate for this clinical trial as she meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 25-year-old male football player who plays for a local club is interested in participating in the Lyske Trial. He has been playing football for the past 10 years and has never sustained any groin injuries. He is physically fit and exercises regularly. He has no history of any chronic illnesses or surgeries. He is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to commit to the training program and follow the study protocol. He is excited to participate in the study and help contribute to the improvement of football player health and well-being.

A 25 year old male was involved in a severe motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries, including a head injury, multiple fractures, and internal bleeding. He was admitted to the hospital and intubated due to respiratory distress. His injury severity score (ISS) is greater than 15, and he is expected to require mechanical ventilation for at least 48 hours. He is not on any other research protocols or anti-infective treatments. He is participating in a social security scheme and is willing to participate in the study. He does not have any contraindications to the head-up position.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) four years ago. She has mild cognitive impairment with a score of 27 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). She reports difficulty with walking and balance, especially when performing dual tasks such as walking while talking. She has not experienced a relapse in the past 60 days and is not currently undergoing any corticosteroid therapy. She has not had any changes in disease-modifying treatment in the past 90 days. She lives with her husband and two children and works part-time as an accountant. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and depression, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She wears glasses but has no hearing problems. She has not undergone dual task training or any other interfering physical or cognitive therapy in the past six months. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her cognitive and mobility functions.

5 year old male with a history of undescended testicles presenting for surgical intervention for cryptorchidism. The patient had no known medical history and no medications. The patient underwent surgical intervention and a congenital anomaly of the epididymis or vas deferens was discovered incidentally during the procedure. Photographs of the anomaly were taken and the patient was included in the study.

A 27-year-old woman who is currently experiencing regular menstrual cycles and is not pregnant or nursing, who is right-handed, and who is willing to abstain from all drugs of abuse (except for nicotine) for three days prior to the study. She has no significant hematological, endocrine, cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal, or neurological disease, and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of Addison's disease, Cushing's disease, or other diseases of the adrenal cortex. She has no history of or current psychotic or bipolar affective disorder. She is not receiving synthetic glucocorticoid therapy, any exogenous steroid therapy, or treatment with other agents that interfere with HPA axis function within one month of the time of testing. She is not taking opiates, opiate antagonists, or benzodiazepines. She is not pregnant, nursing, or of childbearing potential and not practicing an effective means of birth control. She is willing to maintain abstinence from alcohol and other drugs of abuse (except nicotine) for three days prior to the stress task procedure. She does not have ferrous metal implants or pacemaker since fMRI will be used. She is not claustrophobic. She is not currently dependent on cocaine or any other substances, and she does not meet DSM-IV criteria for past or current substance dependence (other than nicotine).

A 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, productive cough and fever. The patient was admitted with a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia and started on empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, including ceftriaxone and azithromycin. On day 2 of admission, the patient's clinical condition improved, and repeat chest X-ray showed improvement in infiltrates. The patient was intubated due to worsening respiratory distress and was started on mechanical ventilation. The patient's clinical course was complicated by the development of hypotension, which was successfully managed with fluid resuscitation and vasopressor therapy. On Day 3 of admission, the patient was evaluated for de-escalation of antibiotic therapy based on microbiological results obtained from Unyvero® testing. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the study and provided informed consent to participate. The patient was randomized to the intervention group and had antibiotic therapy de-escalated based on the results of the Unyvero® test. The patient's clinical condition continued to improve, and he was successfully extubated on Day 5 of admission.

This is a 26 year old male patient diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 22. He has a family history of schizophrenia with his brother and mother also diagnosed with the disorder. The patient is currently on antipsychotic medication and has been stable for the past 6 months. He has no significant medical history or substance abuse history. The patient has no hearing impairment and is not currently pregnant. He has not experienced any head trauma or functional impairment due to head trauma. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 24-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician for uncontrolled asthma. She had been experiencing symptoms for the past 7 years, including coughing, wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, especially during the summer and fall seasons. She currently takes inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting beta-agonists daily as needed. She has a positive skin prick test for grass mix and dust mites, and a positive response to inhaled methacholine. Her FEV1 is 85% of predicted, and FEV1/FVC is 75%. She is a non-smoker and has not had any respiratory tract infection within the past four weeks. She has no history of other respiratory diseases or significant medical issues. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of surfactant protein D on pulmonary immune cells derived from bronchoalveolar lavage after segmental allergen challenge in patients with asthma. She understands the protocol requirements and restrictions and is available to complete all study measurements. She is using a highly effective method of contraception during the entire study period.

25-year-old university student currently enrolled at the University of Fribourg with a good understanding of French. The patient is right-handed, has no history of endocrinological conditions or neurological disorder or brain injury. The patient is not currently taking any psychotropic drugs and has no presence of a mental disorder. The patient has never participated in any psychological intervention before and is not currently participating in any other psychological intervention or longitudinal study. The patient does not have claustrophobia and is not pregnant. The patient does not have any metal in their body, such as pacemakers, aneurysm's clips, metallic prosthesis, or cochlear implants. The patient is interested in participating in a multidimensional stress prevention program to improve their psychological and physical well-being.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has a history of ragweed allergy. He participated in the Ragweed-SPIRE study and completed at least 6 out of 8 treatment visits. The patient has not received any allergen immunotherapy or prohibited therapies since completing the study. He has not experienced any significant side effects from the previous treatment and is willing to participate in the follow-on study. The patient has no significant medical history and is able to understand the study requirements and communicate clearly with the investigator.

The patient is a 47-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 4 years. She has been prescribed multiple medications, including opioids, benzodiazepines, and antidepressants to manage the pain and discomfort associated with RA. She has been experiencing severe joint pain, stiffness, and swelling in her hands, wrists, and knees, which have limited her ability to carry out daily activities. Her current medications include oxycodone, alprazolam, and sertraline. She recently started taking adalimumab, which is a biologic agent used to treat RA. Her physician recommended the medication due to her worsening symptoms, and she started the medication a month ago. She is now being evaluated to determine the effectiveness of the medication on her symptoms and whether there has been a change in her use of opioids, benzodiazepines, and antidepressants since starting the adalimumab. The patient has been compliant with her medication regimen and has not experienced any adverse effects from the adalimumab. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her informed consent.

A 58-year-old male with a 30 pack-year smoking history, diagnosed with moderate to severe COPD and stable airway obstruction as per the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease guidelines. The patient has not been hospitalized for an acute COPD exacerbation in the past three months and has not had any respiratory tract infections or COPD exacerbations in the past six weeks. The patient does not have any clinically significant respiratory conditions other than COPD and does not have a clinical history suggesting asthma instead of COPD. The patient does not use oxygen therapy for more than 15 hours per day and does not have any clinically significant cardiovascular conditions. The patient has not had any hypersensitivity reactions to inhaled anticholinergics, beta-2 agonists, sympathomimetic amines, or inhaled medications.

The patient is a 25 year-old male with sickle cell disease who has been experiencing bone pain and discomfort. He has a history of recurrent vaso-occlusive crises (VOC) and has been hospitalized multiple times for pain management. His current medications include hydroxyurea and folic acid. He denies any history of heart, renal, or liver failure. He has not taken any medications that influence bone metabolism in the past two years. He has no history of traumatic vertebral fracture, hypo/hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, osteomalacia, Paget disease, or malabsorption diseases. He is not currently pregnant or trying to conceive. He has not had any history of cancer.

30 yo non-smoking female with no significant medical history presents for consideration in a clinical trial. She is interested in participating in research studies that could help improve health outcomes for others. The patient is currently not pregnant and reports no history of asthma or other respiratory conditions. She is otherwise healthy and meets the study's inclusion criteria.

As this is a retrospective study, patient descriptions are not needed. The study will analyze medical records and electronic medical records of all patients who were followed in the intensive care unit between January 1, 2015, and January 1, 2016, regardless of their age, sex, and medical history.

67 year old male with a 20 year history of smoking and a diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) GOLD stage IV. The patient has a history of two hospitalizations for acute exacerbation of COPD in the past year. He reports difficulty walking more than a few steps and has been using oxygen at home for the past six months. The patient experiences shortness of breath even at rest and reports frequent coughing with expectoration of yellowish phlegm. He has been unable to participate in any physical activity due to his symptoms. The patient is currently on triple inhaler therapy (inhaled corticosteroid, long-acting beta-agonist, and long-acting muscarinic antagonist) and short-acting bronchodilators as needed. The patient has no history of cardiovascular disease or other significant comorbidities. The patient is willing to try new interventions to improve his quality of life and is interested in participating in this study.

Samantha is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer two years ago. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy with cisplatin and carboplatin, but unfortunately, her cancer has returned and spread to other parts of her body. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. Her CA-125 antigen titers have been consistently elevated, indicating that her cancer is still active. She has been referred to this clinical trial to receive high-dose chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide, carboplatin, and mitoxantrone, followed by an autologous bone marrow transplant. Samantha is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She has no hearing loss and no active infections. She has a negative pregnancy test and is HIV negative. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo the necessary procedures.

Patient is a 28-year-old HIV-positive woman with normal menstrual cycles and no gynecological issues. She is currently using an oral contraceptive for birth control. She has been on zidovudine (ZDV) for the past 6 months and is responding well to the treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of different methods of birth control on the drug actions of ZDV in HIV-positive women. She is willing to switch to Depo-Provera as her birth control method for the clinical trial. The patient has no history of cancer or chronic high blood pressure, thrombophlebitis, or pulmonary emboli. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with them.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with vitiligo on her arms and legs. She has had the condition for several years and has tried various treatments with no significant improvement. She is frustrated with the appearance of the white patches on her skin and is interested in trying new treatments. She has no known allergies and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is able to attend treatment sessions regularly. She has stable vitiligo, and the affected areas are symmetric.

The patient is a 50 year old male who received dental implant therapy between the years of 1999-2005 at The Specialist Clinic Skanstull in Stockholm, Sweden. He has been living with the implants for over 10 years and has experienced no complications or issues related to the implants. He is in good overall health and currently employed as an engineer. He enjoys playing golf and spending time with his family in his free time. His BMI is within normal range and his blood pressure is stable. He is fluent in Swedish and English and is willing to participate in the study to help advance dental implant treatments for future patients.

A 58-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has no history of any other cancer. He has been experiencing cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. He has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently, but with some difficulty. He has no history of heart attack, unstable angina, or congestive heart failure. He is not currently taking any medications or undergoing any treatments for cancer. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has no known allergies to any medications.

A 40-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and underwent autologous stem cell transplantation 120 days ago. He has completed all standard chemotherapy and radiation therapy. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies. His performance status is good, with no evidence of disease progression. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. His hemoglobin, neutrophil count, and platelets are all within normal limits. He has no cardiac symptoms, is not pregnant, and is not breastfeeding. He is willing and able to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study period and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug. The patient has no known bleeding disorders, no history of significant toxicity to dasatinib or any other medication, and is not using any prohibited treatments or therapies. He is currently not taking St. John's Wort and agrees to discontinue it if needed. He is able to take oral medication and understands the study procedures and requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hypertension and is struggling to control his blood pressure with medication alone. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30, indicating he is overweight. He has a history of a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in salt and processed foods. He is willing to make dietary changes to improve his health and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no history of chronic kidney disease, liver disease, or chronic inflammatory bowel disease, and has not been diagnosed with any tumors.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl diagnosed with Aicardi Goutieres Syndrome (AGS) with clinical features of early-onset encephalopathy resulting in severe intellectual and physical handicap. She has been experiencing recurrent seizures and has shown evidence of neurologic disease on neuroimaging including intracranial calcifications and leukoencephalopathy. There is also evidence of skin involvement

The patient is a 52 year-old female with a history of end stage renal disease, maintained on regular hemodialysis for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing persistent bone pain, fatigue, and pruritus despite medical treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Her intact parathormone hormone levels have been consistently elevated at greater than 600 pg/mL and her serum calcium and phosphorus levels have been difficult to control. She has no history of primary hyperparathyroidism or kidney transplantation. She has not undergone repeated parathyroidectomy in the past. She has no history of other significant comorbidities and is compliant with her hemodialysis treatment. She is willing to undergo surgical parathyroidectomy if deemed necessary by her physician.

52-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes (1999 WHO diagnosis criteria) for the first time without drug therapy. The patient has been diagnosed with diabetes for less than 10 years and has not accepted insulin in the past 3 months. The patient's fasting plasma glucose (FPG) is greater than or equal to 11.1 mmol/L or glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) is greater than or equal to 9%. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient does not have any obvious heart, liver or kidney function failure, severe acute or chronic complications, associated diseases or other diseases that should not use oral hypoglycemic drugs. The patient is not a woman in pregnancy or planning to get pregnant.

A 55-year-old man presents with a history of leg pain and cramping that has been progressively worsening over the past year. He reports difficulty walking more than a block without stopping to rest. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He reports no history of smoking or diabetes. Physical examination reveals decreased pedal pulses and coolness in the lower extremities. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) testing shows an ABI of 0.7 on the right and 0.8 on the left. An arterial duplex ultrasound reveals a significant stenosis in the superficial femoral artery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of drug-coated balloons for the treatment of peripheral artery disease. He meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including being over the age of 20, having claudication or critical limb ischemia, and having a vessel diameter of 4-6mm. He has not previously undergone atherectomy, laser, cryoplasty, scoring, cutting, or balloon angioplasty.

28-year-old G2P1A0 female with a history of uncomplicated vaginal delivery 4 years ago presents for routine prenatal care at 22 weeks gestation. She reports no significant medical history, allergies, or surgical history. She denies any history of hypertension, diabetes, or other chronic medical conditions. The patient reports no abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge, no abdominal pain, and no contractions. Fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks gestation was normal. Second-trimester screening test was low-risk, and anomaly screening was negative. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for placenta previa management and meets the inclusion criteria. She is scheduled for a vaginal ultrasonography and MRI on her 32nd week of gestation and will be followed up until delivery.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has smoked a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications currently. He has a family history of lung cancer, as his father passed away from the disease at age 65. He is a resident of the Tuscany region of Italy and is registered with a participating general practitioner for the ITALUNG trial. He received a letter explaining the study and completed a questionnaire about his smoking history and general health information. He provided his consent to be randomized and was centrally randomized into the active arm of the trial. He was contacted by phone to schedule his first low-dose CT screening test and provided written consent to be enrolled in the biomarkers collateral research project. He was also invited to a free smoking cessation program. He completed his baseline screening test and received the results within three weeks. The test was negative, and he was scheduled for annual repeat screening tests. He has been followed up for the past 9.3 years since randomization for cause-specific mortality, overall mortality, and lung cancer incidence. He has also had blood and sputum samples stored in the Italung Biomarker study Biobank.

Maria is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for several months. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and has been on medications for both conditions for the past 3 years. She also smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not undergone any cardiac interventions in the past. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal except for her elevated blood pressure and cholesterol levels. She was diagnosed with multi-vessel coronary artery disease (CAD) and her treating physician recommended coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) as the optimal revascularization mode. After discussing the benefits and risks of the procedure, she agreed to participate in the clinical trial that aims to assess the use of iFR measurement during coronary angiography to determine the level of damage to the coronary arteries before CABG surgery. She understands the study procedures and has signed the informed consent document. She will continue on optimal medical therapy and undergo echocardiography and CT coronary angiography at 3 and 12 months respectively to assess graft patency. She will also complete a quality of life questionnaire at 3 months during the follow-up appointment.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to the intensive care unit following a severe infection with Acinetobacter baumannii. The patient has a history of hypertension, but otherwise, he is generally healthy. The patient received colistin empirically and subsequently tested positive for carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacilli. He is currently receiving colistin as a microbiologically documented case. The patient's urine output has been stable and consistent throughout his stay in the ICU. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help researchers understand the effectiveness of different dosing strategies for colistin in critically ill patients.

Patient A is a 54-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, for which he takes medication. He is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies. The patient has been on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor for 6 months after the PCI and has not experienced any cardiovascular events or bleeding episodes. The patient is considered for randomization in a clinical trial comparing 6 months versus 12 months of DAPT after DES implantation in STEMI. If the patient meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria, he will be randomized in a 1:1 fashion to receive either single (aspirin) or dual (aspirin plus P2Y12 inhibitor) antiplatelet therapy for an additional 6 months. The patient will be assessed for the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality, any myocardial infarction, any revascularization, stroke, stent thrombosis, and bleeding (TIMI) at 18 months after randomization. The patient will also be included in a registry studying the safety outcomes of Bivalirudin and Prasugrel combination and Bivalirudin and Ticagrelor combination at 2 and 30 days, as well as a report assessing the clinical outcomes after primary PCI for treatment of STEMI with the new Resolute Integrity stent at 30 days and 6 months.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was diagnosed with congestive heart failure (NYHA III) three years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema in his legs. He was hospitalized last month due to an episode of acute decompensation of heart failure (NYHA IV) and underwent medical recompensation. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with multitasking. He has no history of dementia or other neurological conditions. He has completed high school and worked as an accountant before retiring. He is willing to participate in a study investigating cognitive impairment in patients with heart failure, and he is able to attend multiple neuropsychological testing sessions. He is not currently experiencing major depression or psychosis, and he has not undergone reanimation or received assist device systems. He has an ejection fraction of 30%.

The patient is a 48-year-old male with a history of sleep apnea and hypertension. Despite taking three different antihypertensive medications, his blood pressure remains uncontrolled. He has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness and snoring, and a polysomnography confirmed the presence of obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea-hypopnea index of 20. He has been using a CPAP machine for the past two months with good adherence. However, his blood pressure is still not well controlled. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines CPAP treatment with a physical activity program to optimize his blood pressure control. He has no history of acute hepatic failure, biliary cirrhosis, cholestasis, or acute hypertension.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who gave birth to a premature baby boy at 28 weeks of gestation. The baby is currently admitted to the NICU and expected to stay there for several weeks. The mother is married and has a 5-year-old daughter. She works as a teacher and is currently on maternity leave. She has a history of postpartum depression after her first pregnancy and is currently on a low dose of antidepressants. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. Her husband is also involved in the care of their baby and is willing to participate in the study as well. They live close to the hospital and have access to transportation.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with non-nasal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NKTCL) based on histopathology examination. He has already received 3 regimens of chemotherapy but did not achieve remission. His disease has progressed or relapsed after remission. He has at least one measurable focus with a long diameter of more than 1.5cm and a short diameter of more than 1.0cm or at least one evaluable focus. His body weight is 70 kilograms, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His estimated survival is more than 3 months, and he is willing to sign the written consent before the trial. He has normal blood-routine tests, except for lymphoma-related abnormalities. He has not received symptomatic treatment for bone marrow toxicity within 7 days prior to enrollment, has no active hemorrhage, and has no history of thrombosis, embolism, cerebral hemorrhage, or cerebral infarction. He has no active infection or continuous fever within 14 days before enrollment. He has not had major organ surgery within 6 weeks prior to enrollment, and his liver and renal function tests are within the normal range. He has not received Chidamide treatment before, and his disease progression did not occur within 6 months afterward. He has no history of hemophagocytic syndrome, central nervous system diseases, mental disorders, or drug abuse.

9-year-old male from a rural area in Morocco was stung by a scorpion while playing outside. The parents immediately brought him to the local hospital where he was evaluated by a physician. The sting site was edematous and erythematous with severe pain. The child also complained of abdominal pain and had some diaphoresis. The physician classified the envenomation as Class II B and initiated standard supportive care. The child was then referred to a tertiary care center where he was considered for enrollment in the clinical trial. He met all eligibility criteria and the parent provided informed consent for enrollment in the trial. The child was randomized to receive either the equine F(ab')2 antivenom or placebo and was monitored for 4 hours to evaluate for improvement in the severity of envenomation.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with advanced breast cancer that is estrogen receptor positive and Her-2 negative. She has undergone surgery and radiation therapy, and has been treated with an aromatase inhibitor, however, her disease has progressed. She is currently experiencing bone pain and has been taking pain medication to manage it. She has no history of diabetes or other significant medical conditions, and her blood tests indicate acceptable glucose control, bone marrow, liver and kidney function. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and agrees to avoid foods or drugs that are known inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4.

This clinical trial is only open to subjects who have previously received a dTpa booster vaccination in a previous clinical study (NCT01267058). Therefore, no patient description can be generated for this trial as new recruitment is not being performed.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and drinks approximately 2-3 alcoholic beverages per day. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has gained weight in recent years. He has no history of heart disease or myocardial infarction, but has been on antihypertensive medications for the past 5 years. His blood pressure is currently well-controlled. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy to the treatment field. He has a platelet count of 160,000/mm3, WBC count of 5,200/mm3, and hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL. His renal function is normal with a creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. He does not have any known allergies to medications. He is willing to use effective contraception as he is sexually active and fertile. He is eligible for PEG gastrostomy if necessary.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been struggling with weight gain for the past few years. She has a BMI of 35 kg/m2 and a waist circumference of 98cm. She has tried several diets in the past with little success. She is generally healthy, but has a family history of heart disease and diabetes. She takes medication for high blood pressure, but it is well controlled. She does not have any gastrointestinal or thyroid problems, and is not a heavy drinker. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her lose weight and improve her overall health. She is willing to follow a low-calorie diet for the first phase of the trial and is excited to try a healthy Nordic diet to help maintain her weight loss. She understands that there may be some restrictions on what she can eat during the trial, but is willing to make the necessary changes to her diet. She is committed to improving her health and reducing her risk for heart disease and diabetes.

The patient is a 58 year old Asian male who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to his liver and bones. He is currently experiencing fatigue, weight loss and shortness of breath. He has a history of smoking for over 20 years and has quit smoking 5 years ago. He is married, living with his wife and two children. He is an engineer by profession and works full-time. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. His previous treatment with immunotherapy was discontinued due to the progression of his disease. He is now planning to start systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy along with pembrolizumab. He meets the inclusion criteria for cohort 2 in the CITaDeL clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study to assess the changes in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) following the initiation of treatment.

A 28-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a history of injury to her right wrist after falling from her bike. She is an avid cyclist and was not wearing any protective gear at the time of the injury. The patient reports pain and swelling in her right wrist, which is preventing her from performing routine activities of daily living, including typing on her computer and lifting heavy objects. She has no other significant medical history and is a non-smoker. Physical examination reveals tenderness and swelling over the right wrist with no obvious deformity. X-ray imaging confirms a distal radius fracture. She is provided with a splint and advised to follow up with an orthopedic surgeon. The patient is approached to participate in a clinical trial investigating the impact of keeping a personal recovery diary on upper extremity disability. She is fluent in English and has no difficulty with reading and writing. She provides informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old woman who is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2 and does not plan to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She is willing and able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all study procedures. She has no history of neoplastic disease or hematological malignancy within the past 5 years, and has no known congenital or acquired immunodeficiency or chronic active hepatitis B or C infection. She has not received immunosuppressive therapy or long-term systemic corticosteroid therapy within the past 3 months. She meets the laboratory criteria defined in the protocol within 12 days before Day 1. She is willing to be randomized to a single vaccination with 1 of 5 doses of ExPEC4V or placebo and is willing to participate in the long-term follow-up phase of the study for up to 3 years.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male, retired and living in the greater Vancouver area, has no previous history of cancer, except for non-melanoma skin cancer. He is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves blood draws, medical exams, and PET-CT scans. He is in good health and able to donate three tubes of blood. He has an email address and is willing to share medical data related to the test, imaging scans, and follow-up with the study investigators for the following year. He has no immunocompromised status or bleeding disorders. He is able to have blood work in the greater Vancouver area and has no contraindications to MRI or PET-CT.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory loss for the past year. She has noticed that she forgets things more easily and has trouble recalling recent events. Her family has also observed that she repeats herself and forgets important dates. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She is able to perform her daily activities without difficulty, but has noticed that it takes her longer to complete tasks than it used to. She has no history of stroke or thyroid disease. Her vision and hearing are normal. She is right-handed and is willing to undergo MRI examination. Her cognitive impairment is confirmed by her husband, who is her informant. Her general cognitive function is near-normal, but her CDR score is 0.5, indicating a borderline level of cognitive impairment. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and may be a suitable candidate for the construction of the diagnosis system for early AD based on multi-modality MRI technology.

A 64-year-old man was referred to a neurology clinic by his primary care physician for complaints of memory loss, difficulty with complex tasks, and increased anxiety over the last 4 months. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he was on a stable dose of medications for memory loss including cholinesterase inhibitors (rivastigmine). He denied any history of seizures, epilepsy or family history of epilepsy. He also denied any history of neurological disorders other than dementia, such as stroke, multiple sclerosis or intracranial brain lesions. He does not have any current diagnosis of major psychiatric disorder with the exception of depression. He scored 22 on the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) and has a Clinician Dementia Rating (CDR) of 0.5. His amyloid status was confirmed by a cerebral spinal fluid biomarkers study. His neurological exam was unremarkable. He is not currently taking any medication which could alter cortical excitability. His MRI and TMS results were normal. He has no history of head trauma resulting in prolonged loss of consciousness, fainting spells of unknown or undetermined etiology that might constitute seizures or any metal in his body. Based on his eligibility, he was enrolled in the study as a participant with early Alzheimer's Disease (AD).

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic hip pain for the past year. He is scheduled to undergo a primary elective total hip replacement surgery in 2 weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg daily. He also takes over-the-counter ibuprofen occasionally for his hip pain. The patient reports no known drug allergies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient weighs 80 kg and is in good overall health. He does not have any bleeding disorders, renal or liver disease, alcohol or drug misuse, or history of malignancy. The patient has not been on any other study drug in the past month.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with mild renal impairment, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 55 ml/min/1.73m2. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and is currently on standard anti-diabetic therapy. He has a BMI of 35 kg/m2 and is able to communicate well with the investigator. He has no history of liver disease, malignancy, or active substance abuse. He is a non-smoker and agrees to continue his anti-diabetic therapy throughout the duration of the study. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and comply with the requirements of the study.

This is a 65 year-old female who has been diagnosed with early to moderate atrophic age related macular degeneration (AMD). She has noticed a decrease in her visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, and photostress glare recovery. She has no history of advanced glaucoma, diabetes, or any other ocular or systemic disease that could affect her macular function. She has clear non-lenticular ocular media and has not undergone any recent cataract or retinal surgery. She has not taken any lutein or zeaxanthin supplements in the past six months and is not currently taking any photosensitizing drugs such as phenothiazines or chloroquine. She is interested in participating in the Zeaxanthin and Visual Function Study to evaluate if zeaxanthin supplementation can improve her visual function.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman of Asian ethnicity, who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 4 years. She has been on oral anti-diabetic medication but is now requiring insulin therapy due to poor glycemic control. She also has a history of asthma for the past 10 years and is currently on inhalers for symptom control. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2. Her HbA1C is 9.5%. She has not smoked for the past 2 years. She has no other pulmonary diseases except asthma. She has no history of severe hypoglycaemia or any complications related to her diabetes. She does not have proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell cancer that has been treated with at least one platinum-containing regimen. The patient has been diagnosed with HPV associated HNSCC by a p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay. The patient has failed previous treatments and has no curative treatment options. The patient is in good general health with no significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study including follow-up evaluations. The patient has not received any prior immune-mediated therapy and has no active autoimmune disease. The patient is not currently receiving any other cancer treatments or immunosuppressive medication. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 25-year-old healthy male from the United States who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. His BMI is 22, BP: 115/70, HR: 70/min. He has no significant past medical or drug history. He does not smoke and does not drink alcohol. He is aware of the study requirements and is willing to comply with the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently 12 weeks pregnant and seeking a surgical abortion. She has a history of painful menstrual cramps and chronic headaches. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The patient is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent. She has no allergies or sensitivities to gabapentin and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of gabapentin in reducing perioperative pain during her uterine aspiration procedure. She is willing to comply with all study requirements, including taking the study medication as prescribed, keeping a pain diary, and attending all scheduled follow-up visits.

Patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He has been undergoing hormone therapy for the past 2 years, but his cancer progressed despite treatment. He was enrolled in the CALGB-9480 clinical trial and received suramin treatment. However, his prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels continued to rise, indicating that his cancer was still growing. The patient has agreed to participate in this laboratory study, which will collect plasma and urine samples to better understand biomarkers associated with advanced hormone-refractory prostate cancer. The samples will be collected and shipped appropriately, and Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval will be obtained. The study aims to correlate plasma and urine biomarkers, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), chromogranin A, interleukin-6, and human Kallikrein 2, with survival duration in patients with advanced hormone-refractory prostate cancer. The goal is to identify biomarkers that can help predict treatment response and overall patient survival.

The patient is a Korean male between the ages of 20 and 45 years old. He weighs over 55 kg and has an ideal body weight between -20% and +20%. He has no history of drug abuse and has not participated in any clinical studies within the past two months. He has no known hypersensitivity to drugs, including naftopidil. He has no clinically significant history or presence of liver or kidney disease, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, musculoskeletal, neurological/psychiatric, urinary, hematological, or oncological pathology. The patient understands the purpose of the study and has given written informed consent to participate.

A 9-year-old boy with no known medical conditions who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new respiratory monitor. He has no history of breathing difficulties and is able to follow verbal instructions. The boy is comfortable with wearing the bands around his chest and abdomen and is willing to perform breathing exercises with a resistive element. He is excited to help with the development of a new non-invasive respiratory monitor.

A 28-year old male was recently diagnosed with primary HIV-1 infection after experiencing flu-like symptoms that persisted for weeks. He is a graduate student and lives with his partner. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He is a non-smoker and does not use drugs. He is very concerned about his condition and is eager to start treatment. He reports no allergies to any medications. He is fluent in French and is willing to comply with all the study requirements for one year. He is currently not on any antiretroviral treatments and has not taken any pre- or post-exposure prophylaxis in the past 4 weeks. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has effective contraception methods in place. He is willing to participate in the trial and undergo additional tests and sub-studies. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who has noticed a decline in his cognitive function over the past year. He has difficulty remembering names, places, and events. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, and he does not take any medication that might affect cognitive function. He has a normal body mass index and a relatively healthy diet. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of omega-3 fatty acids and blueberry supplementation on cognitive function in older adults. He is willing to comply with the research protocol and provide written informed consent. He has no allergy to shellfish or seafood, and he does not currently supplement with fish oil or consume fish more than once per week. He is able to comprehend and comply with the research protocol. He meets the inclusion criteria for age-associated cognitive decline and has a Geriatric Depression Scale score of less than 16.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of primary open-angle glaucoma in his left eye. He has been on topical medications for the past 5 years, including prostaglandin analogs and beta-blockers. His intraocular pressure (IOP) has been well-controlled, ranging from 16 to 18 mm Hg. However, he has noticed a gradual decline in his visual function, including difficulty with night vision and reading. His visual acuity in the affected eye is 20/50. His most recent visual field test shows moderate glaucomatous damage, with a mean deviation of -12 dB. He has no known allergies and no significant medical history. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently taking any systemic medications. He has not had any recent eye surgeries or injections in the affected eye. He has no plans for pregnancy and is not currently nursing.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who attends a public school in Bogalusa, Louisiana. She has a family history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol. She is generally healthy and active, but her parents are concerned about her risk for cardiovascular disease in the future. The patient has participated in the Bogalusa Heart Study since she was 5 years old and has had her blood pressure and cholesterol levels measured on multiple occasions. The patient and her parents have given consent for genetic testing to investigate the effects of genetic variants on the course of CVD risk factor development over time. The patient is willing to continue participating in the study and is committed to attending follow-up appointments as necessary.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past few weeks. She has a history of chronic pancreatitis and has been hospitalized multiple times for pancreatitis-related symptoms. She reports a history of heavy alcohol consumption in the past, but has been sober for the past 6 months. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. On physical examination, there is tenderness in the epigastric region and a palpable mass is felt. CT scan reveals a 7 cm pseudocyst in the head of the pancreas. She has increasing size of the cyst within the last 6 weeks. Her platelet count and PTT are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old male scheduled to undergo elective abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. He has no history of airway disease or difficult intubation and has never experienced a sore throat following anesthesia. His BMI is 24 kg/m2 and he is classified as ASA class I. The surgery is expected to last more than two hours. He has not undergone any similar procedures in the past and is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study. He has been informed of the study and has provided written consent to participate.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of metastatic melanoma. The patient has previously been treated with BRAF and MEK inhibitors, but has shown resistance to these treatments. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for new anti-melanoma compounds and is willing to undergo further testing and treatment. The patient has no known allergies to any medications and has not participated in any other clinical trials for melanoma treatment. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility and if eligible, will be enrolled in the trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. A colonoscopy performed 2 weeks ago revealed a mass in the sigmoid colon, and a biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. The patient is scheduled for surgery to remove the tumor next week. He has no family history of hereditary CRC or any other known genetic predisposition to cancer. His physical examination is unremarkable, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He has no signs of metastasis, and his blood work is within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient is a 56-year-old male from Mexico City who has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). He has a history of smoking and has worked as a construction worker for the past 30 years. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He reports occasional shortness of breath and a persistent cough for the past few months. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the upper lobe of the right lung. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Tissue samples were collected for biomarker studies, including ALK rearrangements. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials to potentially improve his treatment outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has given birth to her first child 6 months ago. She is scheduled for a routine gynecological exam and Pap smear. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections or other vulvar or vaginal conditions. She is not menopausal and is not using hormone replacement therapy, and has no history of chronic pelvic pain or dyspareunia. The patient is able to read and speak English.

Patient is a 70-year-old man with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) who is scheduled for a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP). He is in generally good health, with no significant medical history, except for controlled hypertension with medications. He is not taking any sedatives or antidepressants. The patient has given informed consent to undergo spinal anesthesia for the procedure. He is willing to participate in the study to determine the optimal dose of dexmedetomidine for sedation during the procedure. The patient has no history of allergy or intolerance to any medications, and there is no evidence of local infection at the site of operation. The patient is classified as ASA class II.

Ms. Johnson is a 56-year-old woman who was rushed to the hospital after experiencing sudden weakness and numbness on the left side of her body. She also had difficulty speaking and understanding language. Upon physical examination, her blood pressure was found to be high, and her left eyelid drooped. She was immediately diagnosed with a cerebral infarction in the middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory. A cerebral MRI was conducted within 24 hours of her admission to the hospital, and a magnetic susceptibility sequence (SWAN) was also performed. The sequence revealed a brush sign, indicating the presence of deoxyhemoglobin in the affected area. Ms. Johnson was hospitalized for further management of her stroke and received medicinal and endovascular revascularization treatment. The investigators conducting the BRUSH Sign clinical trial approached her to request her participation in the study, and she agreed to have her medical information used for the study's retrospective analysis.

A 45-year-old male who received his first renal allograft 3 weeks ago and is currently maintained on conventional immunosuppression. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and is not pregnant or nursing. His current urine output is averaging 20 ml/hr over the last 4 hours since the end of surgery. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance research in renal allograft rejection prevention.

The patient is a 28-year-old female diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 6. She underwent a lung transplantation six months ago due to chronic respiratory failure. She is currently on immunosuppressive medication, including anticalcineurins. Her medical history includes chronic kidney disease, and her current glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is greater than 30 ml/min, as measured by technical radionuclide. She is willing to participate in a study that evaluates the predictive value of PIIINP urinary for the development of chronic renal failure in patients with cystic fibrosis after lung transplantation. The patient is not pregnant and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with atrial flutter. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. He has never undergone any previous CTI ablation procedures. He works as an accountant and leads a relatively sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from undergoing the ablation procedure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 57-year-old Caucasian male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. He complains of fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss of approximately 5 kg over the past month. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with enalapril 10mg daily, and occasional alcohol use. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. His performance status is 1. He underwent a partial nephrectomy for a 6 cm renal mass 3 years ago, but a recent CT scan showed metastatic disease in both lungs and liver. He has not received any systemic therapy for renal cell carcinoma. He has a normal EKG and no history of brain metastases. He is married, has two adult children, and works as a sales representative for a pharmaceutical company. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 5 years ago. He underwent prostatectomy and radiation therapy. However, his cancer has now become resistant to hormone therapy and his PSA levels have been steadily rising. He is experiencing fatigue and weakness, and has lost some weight over the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He is a non-smoker and doesn't drink alcohol. He is retired but used to work as an engineer. His family history is negative for any cancers. His ECOG performance status is 1. His blood tests show that his ANC is 1,200/mm³, platelet count is 90,000/mm³, and hemoglobin level is 11.2 g/dL. His serum creatinine is 1.5 mg/dL, AST level is 50 U/L, and total bilirubin level is 1.8 mg/dL. His corrected calcium level is within normal limits. He has not received any chemotherapy or investigational agents in the past 28 days. He is not taking any medications or supplements that contain additional calcium.

The patient is a 65 year old man who was diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) 3 years ago. He has received multiple lines of therapy for his MCL, including chemotherapy, immunotherapy and stem cell transplantation, but has not achieved a complete response or maintained a stable disease. He is currently experiencing symptoms of fatigue, night sweats and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 1. His most recent therapy was completed 4 weeks ago. He has not received prior treatment with ibrutinib or other Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitors. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is within normal range. He is not currently pregnant, breast-feeding or planning to become pregnant.

A 55-year-old male patient comes in with a history of relapsed multiple myeloma. He has been undergoing treatments, but the cancer has returned. He has measurable disease with a serum monoclonal protein of 1.5 g by protein electrophoresis. He is not a candidate for stem cell transplantation or has undergone prior stem cell collection. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient's life expectancy is estimated to be more than three months. His absolute neutrophil count is 1,200/microliter, and his platelet count is 85,000/microliter. His hemoglobin levels are 9.5 g/dL, which is low but still above the minimum requirement. His total serum bilirubin is within the normal range, and his aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. His creatinine levels are 1.5 mg/dL. He is not pregnant or nursing. He has undergone four prior therapies, including stem cell transplantation and preceding induction therapy. He has no history of anthracycline exposure or central thoracic radiotherapy that included the heart in the radiotherapy port. He has no history of serious ventricular arrhythmia or corrected QT interval (QTc) prolongation. He has well-controlled hypertension. He has no condition that impairs the ability to swallow and retain sunitinib malate tablets. He has no preexisting thyroid abnormality. He has no active malignancy, except for multiple myeloma. He has no concurrent uncontrolled illnesses or ongoing or active infections. He has recovered from adverse events of prior therapy. He has not undergone chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the last four weeks. He is not taking nonmyelosuppressive agents. He has not taken any prior antiangiogenic agents. He is not taking high-dose corticosteroids or concurrent therapeutic doses of coumarin-derivative anticoagulants. He has no concurrent agents with proarrhythmic potential, any other concurrent investigational agents or anticancer therapy.

A 35-year-old woman has been experiencing widespread pain and fatigue for the past year. The pain is often described as a dull ache and is present in multiple areas of her body, including the neck, shoulders, back, and hips. She also experiences frequent headaches and difficulty sleeping. She has seen multiple doctors and has undergone several tests, but there is no clear diagnosis. She is frustrated with the lack of answers and is looking for alternative treatment options. She speaks fluent Spanish and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating pain response in fibromyalgia. She has no history of diagnosed psychiatric or rheumatic pathology.

Pt is a 14yo male patient who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and is scheduled for his first cytotoxic chemotherapy cycle. He is at intermediate risk of tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) and has no access to rasburicase. The patient has no known allergies, with normal renal and hepatic function. Given the potential risks associated with TLS, the patient has been enrolled in the FLORET study to receive oral administration of febuxostat at a dose of 80 mg/day. The study will assess the efficacy of febuxostat in preventing TLS in pediatric patients like the patient. The patient and his family have provided informed consent and are willing to participate in the study.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has a history of ovarian cancer that has recurred after previous treatment. She has been diagnosed with platinum-resistant disease and has not received any platinum or taxane agents within the past 6 months. Her last chemotherapy was more than 4 weeks ago. She is in overall good health with a performance status of 1. Her bone marrow function is adequate, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/uL, hemoglobin of 10 g/dl and a platelet count of 120,000/uL. She has normal renal function with a serum creatinine level of 1.0 mg/dL and normal hepatic function with serum total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL and AST/ALT levels within normal limits. She has not had prior whole abdomen or pelvic radiation, nor has she had more than 6 cycles of an alkylating agent or more than 450 mg/m2 of doxorubicin. She has recovered from the effects of prior surgery and chemotherapy. She is able to read and understand the informed consent and is willing to use an effective form of contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of study medication. She does not have any active infections or extra-abdominal metastases, nor does she have active CNS metastases. She has no known hypersensitivity to any of the components of docetaxel or oxaliplatin. She has peripheral neuropathy grade 1.

32 yo F with a recent diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis confirmed by clinical and laboratory-supported criteria. The patient has an EDSS score of 2.5 and is currently treatment-naïve. She has a history of seasonal allergies but no history of severe allergic reactions or hypersensitivity to interferons or any of its components. She is in overall good health with no significant medical conditions or psychiatric illness not due to MS that would interfere with therapy. The patient is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study, and has no history of malignancy or uncontrolled seizures. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and is interested in participating in the study to better understand the therapeutic response and immunomodulatory effects of Avonex in MS patients.

A 62-year-old male patient was referred to the clinic for cardiac surgery due to severe aortic stenosis. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a retired teacher and was previously physically active but has had decreased exercise tolerance due to his heart condition. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath at rest but reports exertional dyspnea and fatigue. He quit smoking 10 years ago and does not consume alcohol. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. His echocardiography showed a severely calcified aortic valve with an area of 0.7 cm² and a mean pressure gradient of 50 mmHg. His left ventricular ejection fraction was 55%. He was scheduled for aortic valve replacement surgery and agreed to participate in the registry for perioperative data.

A 45-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital due to persistent fatigue and easy bruising. Her medical history includes hypertension and hypothyroidism, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of bleeding disorder. Her physical examination showed multiple bruises on her arms and legs, and laboratory tests revealed that her platelet count was 60 x109/L. She is able to give informed consent and has not received a platelet transfusion or undergone surgery or trauma in the past 14 days or 7 days, respectively. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study and is eligible to participate.

The patient is a 68 year old woman who was diagnosed with stomach cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. She has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy but has not responded well. Her HER2 status is positive, as confirmed by HER2 IHC 3+. She has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1. She is in good general health with an ECOG performance status score of 1. She has no history of hypersensitivity to any medications. She has not received any cancer treatments or surgeries within the last 4 weeks. She has no history of major surgery within the last 4 weeks or any live virus vaccinations within the last 4 weeks. She is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol. She is postmenopausal and agrees to use two forms of highly effective contraception. She has adequate organ function and a predicted survival of more than 12 weeks. She is expected to be compliant with the requirements of the protocol.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by her rheumatologist. She is in stage 2 of the condition according to Kellgren-Lawrence criteria. She has not undergone any prior knee surgeries nor does she have any known malignancies or circulation disorders. She is not pregnant and has no diagnosis of mental disorders. She has some scar tissue on her knee from a previous injury, but it does not cause any complications. She does not have any metal implants. She experiences discomfort and swelling in her knee, which sometimes restricts her movement. She is willing to try new treatments to alleviate her symptoms.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who recently lost a molar tooth in the posterior area of her lower jaw. She has good oral hygiene and healthy gums, with no signs of periodontal disease or bone loss around the adjacent teeth. She does not suffer from bruxism and is a non-smoker. The patient is systemically healthy and willing to comply with study procedures. She has been selected to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of cement residues on the microbiota and inflammation of peri-implant tissues. The trial requires a two-piece dental implant to be placed and restored with both a cemented and a screw-retained single crown. The patient will be randomized into two groups and will receive either a screw-retained crown or a cemented crown, which will be removed and replaced with the other type of crown after 16 weeks. Microbiological samples will be collected every 8 weeks and analyzed for bacterial content, as well as two host markers. Clinical parameters for inflammation and probing depths will be obtained after each 16-week period. The patient is eligible to participate in the trial as she meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder. She has been taking conventional alprazolam tablets for the past six months, and although they have helped her anxiety, she finds it difficult to swallow the tablets due to the size. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. She lives alone and works full-time as a graphic designer. She has no significant medical history, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She is currently taking a dose of 0.5 mg of alprazolam twice a day as prescribed by her physician. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess her preference for the orally disintegrating tablets compared to conventional tablets.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who was diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) two years ago. He has been receiving treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), but has not achieved remission. He participated in a previous study of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) as a treatment for depression (HREC 07305) but did not reach remission at the end of the trial (defined as a MADRS score of ≤ 10). He is interested in participating in this new trial of tDCS using alternative electrode montages to see if it can improve his depressive symptoms. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependence, and there are no neurological disorders or insults that would place him at risk of seizure or neuronal damage with tDCS. He is not currently pregnant and is not sexually active.

A 26-year-old female presents for a clinical trial of influenza vaccines. She is in good health and has not had any recent illnesses. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has not participated in any previous influenza vaccine trials. She is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with them. She has not received any live licensed vaccines within the past 4 weeks or inactivated licensed vaccines within the past 2 weeks. She is available by telephone for follow-up and is able to complete the 180-day follow-up period. She is judged to be capable of understanding and complying with the study requirements.

The patient is a healthy, full-term newborn baby boy, born at 40 weeks gestational age, weighing 7 lbs 2 oz. He was delivered vaginally without any complications. The baby has no known medical conditions and is exclusively breastfed by his mother. The mother intends to participate in the study and switch to the study formula for the duration of the study. The baby's parents confirm that they will not administer any vitamin or mineral supplements, solid foods or juices to the baby during the study. The baby has not received any antibiotics or probiotics since birth. The baby's parents have signed the informed consent form and are willing to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 28-year-old sexually active woman who has been in a monogamous relationship with her male partner for the past year. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles occurring every 28 days and is seeking to avoid pregnancy for the duration of the study. She is willing to use the study drug as the sole form of contraception and understands the risk of pregnancy. She has no history of IUD complications, such as perforation, expulsion, or pregnancy with IUD in place, and has not used ParaGard IUD within the past 3 months. She has no plans to use any non-contraceptive estrogen, progesterone or testosterone during the 60 months of study participation. She is not exclusively breastfeeding and has had 2 normal menstrual periods prior to enrollment. She has no history of unexplained abnormal uterine bleeding or significant abnormal Pap smear requiring evaluation or treatment. She does not have any congenital or acquired uterine anomaly that may complicate study drug placement. She is not currently participating or planning future participation in a research study of an investigational drug or device during the course of this investigational study. She has no known or suspected alcohol or drug abuse within the past 12 months and has no general health, mental health or behavioral condition that would render her less likely to provide the needed study information. She is not using corticosteroids.

A 35 year old male patient suffered a traumatic brain injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident and is confirmed to have brain damage through imaging. It has been a month since the injury and he has been experiencing pain in his left shoulder with a score of 6 on the numerical scale (NRS). He has a clear cognitive function and scored 20 points on the mini mental state examination (MMSE). He has not received any injection treatments in the past two weeks and is not experiencing severe coagulopathy. He has agreed in writing to participate in the study and comply with the precautions.

A 52-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo a hysterectomy surgery under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. The patient has no known allergies and does not smoke. She has never had any previous surgeries, and there is no history of difficulty with intubation. The patient reports no recent sore throat or upper respiratory infections. She has good oral hygiene and does not have any missing or friable teeth. Her Mallampati score is 2. She has provided informed consent for the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

A 12-year-old boy with a BMI above the 90th percentile is eligible to participate in the Danish Childhood Obesity Biobank. He has been struggling with weight gain for the past few years and has been advised to seek treatment for his obesity. He is an only child and lives with his parents who are both overweight. He enjoys playing video games and watching TV in his free time. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. He has no known allergies. He has been previously diagnosed with prediabetes and his parents are concerned about the potential long-term health consequences of his obesity. They are interested in participating in the biobank to contribute to the research that could help their son and other children like him.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who was diagnosed with asthma at the age of 8. She has been using an inhaled corticosteroid with a long-acting beta2 antagonist and inhaled albuterol sulfate as rescue medication. However, her asthma control has been suboptimal with frequent exacerbations in the past year. She is willing to discontinue all other rescue medications and replace them with the study provided Albuterol multidose dry powder inhaler with integrated electronic module (eMDPI). She is fluent in English and familiar with using smart devices and downloading and using apps. She has no other clinically significant medical conditions and has not been hospitalized for severe asthma in the last 30 days. She is a non-smoker and has never been treated with systemic corticosteroids or biologics for asthma.

A 6-year-old child is brought in for a routine check-up by their parent who is their primary caregiver. The child's BMI is above the 85th percentile, but not yet at the 99th percentile. The child attends one of the four TCPA clinics and is a Texas Children's Health Plan member. The parent is willing and able to participate in the study, including attending the 6-month intervention sessions and 3 measurement time points over 14 months. The child does not have any medical consequences of obesity that require treatment and is not currently taking any medications that can affect their weight status. The parent and child are able to participate in counseling sessions in either English or Spanish. This study is an opportunity to help them learn about lifestyle changes that could improve the child's weight status and overall health.

50-year-old male with a history of oropharyngeal cancer diagnosed 2 months ago, currently scheduled for definitive radiation therapy. The patient has no reported history of skin diseases or sensitivities. No significant medical history other than hypertension, managed with medication. The patient has no tattoos in the neck region and does not have a beard. The patient is mentally competent to provide informed consent and complete self-assessment questionnaires.

45 year-old man who is 5'8" and weighs 220 pounds with a BMI of 33.5. He has been struggling with weight loss despite attempts at diet and exercise. He does not have any history of high blood pressure, psychiatric disorder, stroke or heart disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him lose weight and improve his overall health.

As this clinical trial is focused on middle school students, no patient description is necessary. The trial aims to enroll all 7th and 8th grade students in participating schools, and there are no exclusion criteria.
