The patient is a 3-year-old girl who lives in a rural area in Kenya. Her parents brought her to the Bondo District Hospital because she has been experiencing a fever for the past 24 hours. She weighs 12 kg and is currently at the 50th percentile for weight on Kenya growth charts. Upon examination, her axillary temperature is 38.5º C, and a slide-confirmed infection with P. falciparum is present. Her parasitemia is 10,000 asexual forms per μl. The child has no signs or symptoms of severe disease and has not been enrolled in the IPTi trial. Her parents are willing to bring her for follow-up visits as needed.

50-year-old male admitted to the intensive care unit with severe pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring mechanical ventilation. The patient has a past medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He has been receiving enteral nutrition via a nasogastric tube since admission to the ICU. On the morning of day 5, the patient's protein intake for the first four days was calculated to be 0.7 g/kg/day. The patient has no known allergies to protein supplements. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets all inclusion criteria for the REPLENISH study.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presented with complaints of difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep, as well as excessive daytime sleepiness. She reported feeling tired throughout the day and often found herself dozing off during work meetings. She had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications. She denied smoking or drinking alcohol. She had tried various sleep tracking devices in the past but found them to be unreliable. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial that compared the accuracy of popular sleep tracking devices to the "gold standard" Polysomnography (PSG). She met the inclusion criteria for the study as she was scheduled to undergo a PSG to evaluate her sleep disorder. She did not meet the exclusion criteria as she did not have severe sleep apnea, severe insomnia with less than two hours of sleep per night, epileptiform activity or electrical status epilepticus of sleep. She was enthusiastic about participating in the study as she hoped it would provide insight into the accuracy of sleep tracking devices and help her better understand her sleep patterns.

14-year-old male with a history of physical and emotional abuse, presenting with symptoms of major depressive disorder (MDD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), including nightmares, flashbacks, and social withdrawal. The patient has a CGAS score less than 60 and has not responded to previous talk therapy. The patient is not currently on any antidepressant or benzodiazepine medication and does not have any medical conditions that increase the risk for MRI or fluoxetine treatment. The patient and their parent/guardian are willing to provide written informed consent/assent and have an IQ greater than 70. The patient does not have a pacemaker or any metallic foreign material in their eye, is not pregnant, and does not currently abuse or depend on alcohol or drugs.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a history of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. He has had the condition for the past 10 years and has tried various topical treatments with limited success. He currently has a BSA of 12% and a PASI score of 15. He has no other significant medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of tuberculosis or other infectious diseases. He is willing to use approved contraceptive methods if he engages in activity in which conception is possible. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his psoriasis.

Pt is a 45-year-old woman recently diagnosed with breast cancer and recommended for conservative surgery. She is interested in improving the aesthetic outcome of the surgery and maintaining a good quality of life post-treatment. She has no other significant medical history and is currently not on any medications. She has good compliance with medical appointments and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She does not have multicentric tumors or tumors larger than 5cm, is not in stage IV, and does not require mastectomy. She understands the terms of the study and agrees to participate.

The patient is an 80-year-old woman who resides in a Nursing Home located in a medical desert. She has been living in the Nursing Home for the past six months due to her chronic heart disease and difficulty in performing daily activities. She is currently taking medications for high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and heart failure. She has a history of stroke and has suffered from a few falls in the past. She is able to communicate and is aware of her surroundings. She has a legal representative who is her daughter and visits her regularly. She has signed the consent form for the study and is covered by social security. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past two days and her nurse has filled her symptoms on the Artificial Intelligence/Telemedicine device for analysis by a distant medical doctor.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with toning and strengthening her arms, lower limbs and oblique muscles. She exercises regularly and follows a balanced diet, but has been unable to achieve the desired results. She is motivated to participate in this clinical trial, as she is interested in exploring alternative methods for achieving her fitness goals. The patient reports no history of cardiac pacemakers, implanted defibrillators, implanted neurostimulators, or electronic implants. She also reports no history of pulmonary insufficiency, metal implants, drug pumps or malignant tumors. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not undergone recent surgical procedures that may impede the healing process. The patient has no known allergies to latex and is not suffering from any fever or injuries that may impair muscle function. She is willing to abstain from any treatments other than the study procedure to promote body contouring during the study participation. The patient has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and is willing and able to maintain her regular diet and exercise regimen without effecting significant change in either direction during study participation. She has voluntarily signed the informed consent form and is committed to following the study protocol.

30-year-old female with a BMI of 27. She has no medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of smoking or tobacco use, and she agrees to refrain from nicotine use during the in-house period(s). She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders or symptoms of gastrointestinal disorders. She has not undergone any major surgical procedures involving the stomach potentially affecting absorption of trial products. She has no personal or first-degree relative(s) history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid carcinoma. She doesn't have a history or presence of pancreatitis. She is willing to comply with the study criteria and understands the importance of completing the study according to the protocol.

A 45-year-old man presented to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and blood in his stool. He had a colonoscopy that showed a Stage II colon cancer. He underwent surgical resection and had no residual or metastatic disease. His CEA levels were within normal limits after the surgery. He does not have any history of radiation therapy or chemotherapy, and he has not had any prior malignancy of any type. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any other significant medical history.

The patient is a 60 year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled for a radical prostatectomy. He has no history of urinary or fecal incontinence, nor does he have any neurological conditions affecting his bladder. He has not had any previous pelvic surgeries. He is generally in good health and is able to perform daily activities without difficulty. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications regularly. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the assigned rehabilitation program.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and cramping in his legs while walking for the past few months. The pain is located in the calf muscles and is relieved by rest. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication for these conditions. He has never undergone any endovascular or surgical intervention for his arterial disease. Upon physical examination, the pulses in his feet are weak, and there is evidence of decreased circulation in the lower extremities. Imaging studies reveal significant stenosis in the superficial femoral and popliteal arteries. The patient has been recommended endovascular revascularization with the use of AcoArt drug-coated PTA balloon catheters carrying the CE Mark per current Instructions for Use as per the institution's standard practice. The patient is willing to participate in the post market clinical follow-up trial and has provided written informed consent. His Rutherford Clinical Category (RCC) is 3, and he meets all other eligibility criteria.

Patient B is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain, frequent loose stools, and urgency of defecation for the past six months. She has undergone several tests and investigations to rule out other gastrointestinal disorders such as inflammatory bowel disease and celiac disease. She has been diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D) based on the Rome IV criteria. She has been taking loperamide to reduce bowel frequency but has not experienced any relief from her abdominal pain. She is currently seeking alternative treatments and is interested in participating in the TReatment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Diarrhoea Using Titrated ONdansetron Trial. She is willing to use medically acceptable forms of contraception during the study and for 90 days after completion of study drug. She has a weekly average worst pain score of 35 on a 0 to 100 point scale and has stools with a consistency of 6 or 7 on the Bristol Stool Form score for 4 days a week. She has not undergone gastrectomy or intestinal resection and does not have any other known organic GI diseases. She has not taken Ondansetron or any other medication with contraindications to it. Her pulse, blood pressure, FBC or LFTs are within normal ranges according to the site's local definition of normal. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not currently taking SSRIs or tricyclic antidepressants and is not taking any of the restricted medications. She meets the eligibility criteria and is a suitable candidate for the study.

This is a 45 year-old male who was diagnosed with malignant melanoma stage III after undergoing a surgery to remove a melanoma on his back. He has been prescribed Intron A therapy as an adjuvant treatment and has started the therapy within 60 days of his surgery. He has no history of other malignancies or previous Intron A therapy. He is currently using proper contraception and his female partner is also using proper contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

This is a 32-year-old female with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who has recently been diagnosed with lupus nephritis. She was found to have a urine protein/creatinine ratio of 1.5 and hematuria on routine screening. A renal biopsy confirmed Class III/IV±V lupus nephritis (ISN/RPS 2003). She has positive anti-dsDNA antibodies and is currently on prednisolone 15 mg/day. She has no other significant medical history and is not pregnant. She has not received any other immunosuppressive therapy in the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of tacrolimus versus mycophenolate in the treatment of lupus nephritis.

42-year-old Taiwanese female diagnosed with polycythemia vera in 2018 after presenting with fatigue, headache, and dizziness. Her initial workup showed hemoglobin of 20 g/dL, hematocrit of 60%, and JAK2 V617F mutation positive. She was started on phlebotomy and low-dose aspirin and has been regularly followed up by her hematologist. She has no history of thrombotic events or bleeding. She has been interested in participating in a registry for patients with MPNs in Taiwan to contribute to the understanding of the disease and its management in her country.

68F, postmenopausal, reports symptoms of vaginal dryness and discomfort during intercourse. She has not had a menstrual period for 2 years. She is not currently using estrogen replacement therapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, osteoporosis, and hyperlipidemia, all of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of gynecological surgeries or cancer. She is interested in trying a natural remedy to alleviate her symptoms and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of sea buckthorn oil on mucous membranes.

Patient is a 24-year-old healthy female from the United States who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of a plant-based ingredient on glucose response. She has no history of diabetes, hyperglycemia, or any other glucose metabolism disorders. Her BMI is 23. She is a non-smoker and does not consume any alcoholic drinks. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders and is not on any medication or supplements. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is willing to refrain from drinking alcohol on and one day before the blood withdrawal. She has never participated in any nutritional or biomedical trial in the past 3 months. She is not allergic or intolerant to any food products and is willing to consume the food products provided during the study. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period.

A 20-year-old male college student who does not smoke and is not on any medication came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial. He has no history of atopic dermatitis, hypercholesterolemia, or arteriosclerotic disease in his family. He is interested in contributing to medical research and is willing to give oral and written informed consent. He has no known arrhythmias and his baseline HRV recording was normal. He is in good health and exercises regularly.

The patient is a 65-year-old female who was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease 2 years ago. She completed study 3133K1-3001 (NCT00676143) and had a brain MRI scan consistent with the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. Her Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE) score is 14 at screening. Her caregiver is available to attend all clinic visits with her. She has no significant medical or psychiatric contraindication that would increase the risk associated with her participation in this study or preclude the evaluation of her response. She has not used any investigational drugs or devices, other than bapineuzumab, within the last 60 days prior to screening. She is willing to participate in this study and receive bapineuzumab for the next 4 years.

25-year-old healthy male with a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5, and weighing 140 pounds. The patient has no significant medical history and has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medications in the past 7 days, excluding vitamins or herbal supplements. He does not smoke or consume alcohol, caffeine, grapefruit beverages or foods, or xanthine beverages or foods. The patient is not currently lactating or pregnant, and he has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), and hepatitis C antibody at screening. He is willing to provide written informed consent and is available for the entire study period. The patient is eligible to participate in this clinical trial as a healthy volunteer.

26 F who is sexually active and seeking reliable contraception. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles without any significant abnormalities. The patient has no significant past medical or surgical history and is currently not taking any medications. She has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m². She is willing to use the investigational product as the primary method of contraception for 13 consecutive cycles and is able to comply with the study requirements, including completing diaries and questionnaires. The patient provides written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any exclusion criteria, and her physical and mental health are good based on medical, surgical, and gynecological history, physical examination, gynecological examination, clinical laboratory, and vital signs.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and has undergone a lumpectomy and radiation therapy. She has also received chemotherapy with a partial response, but has now developed cutaneous metastases on her chest wall. The largest lesion is approximately 2 cm in diameter and is causing discomfort and pain. The patient has been offered other treatments such as surgery and systemic chemotherapy, but is not interested in pursuing these options due to concerns about potential side effects and impact on her quality of life. She has been informed about the calcium electroporation clinical trial and is interested in participating. The patient is in good overall health with no significant medical history or comorbidities. She is currently taking tamoxifen as part of her breast cancer treatment. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has provided informed consent to participate. She is willing to undergo regular follow-up examinations for 12 months and is committed to complying with the study protocol.

This is a 44 year old male with a past medical history of ENKTL-NT diagnosed 3 years ago. The patient was treated with L-asparaginase-based regimen and achieved complete remission, but has since relapsed with multiple new lesions at the primary location and other sites. The patient is now considered to have refractory ENKTL-NT. The patient has undergone radiotherapy for stage I/II disease. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) score is 1. The patient has signed the informed consent form (ICF) and is able to comply with the scheduled follow-up visits and related procedures required in the protocol. The patient is between the ages of ≥18 to ≤70 years and has a life expectancy of ≥12 weeks. The patient has taken effective contraceptive measures since the last dose of treatment. The patient has adequate organ and bone marrow functions with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1.5×10^9/L, platelets (PLTs) count of 80×10^9/L, and hemoglobin (HGB) of 9.0 g/L. The patient has normal thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) at baseline. The patient has not been exposed to any anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies in the past. The patient has not received any investigational drug within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. The last dose of radiation or anti-tumor therapy was received over 3 weeks ago. The patient has not received immunosuppressants within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. The patient has not received any live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. The patient has not undergone any major surgery within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. The patient does not have any active autoimmune diseases, primary immunodeficiency diseases, or pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient is not allergic to any ingredients of monoclonal antibodies. The patient does not have any uncontrolled concurrent diseases. The patient is negative for HIV. The patient does not have any acute or chronic active hepatitis B or C. The patient has no history of GI perforation and/or fistula within 6 months prior to enrollment. The patient does not have interstitial lung disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hyperlipidemia and has been on atorvastatin therapy for the past 6 months. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and has been keeping a healthy lifestyle by exercising regularly and following a low-fat diet. She is currently not pregnant and uses adequate contraception. She is willing to participate in the study and to return for all clinic visits. Her medical history does not include any myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndrome, angina, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, or cardiac revascularization. She does not have congestive heart failure and has not consumed more than 1 quart of grapefruit juice per day. She has not been previously exposed to any therapeutic or investigational biological agent within 30 days of screening and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past year. She is able to read and sign the informed consent form.

42-year-old female with a history of hallux valgus deformity, experiencing moderate to severe pain in the big toe that is interfering with her ability to walk and stand for prolonged periods of time. She has tried conservative treatments such as shoe modifications, physical therapy, and NSAIDs, but her symptoms have not improved. Imaging studies have revealed a significant deformity and an osteotomy procedure is recommended. The patient is otherwise healthy and does not have any medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. She has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with the research protocol.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic with a complaint of tooth pain in the upper left molar region. She reports the pain started a few days ago and has been increasing in severity. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. Upon examination, the dentist finds that the patient has symptomatic irreversible pulpitis in tooth #14. The tooth has a slight widening in the periodontal ligament space on radiographs. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial and agrees to participate. She will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group (pulpotomy using Biodentine) or the control group (pulpotomy using MTA). She will be given a pain diary and will be asked to rate her pain level at specified times. The patient will attend recall appointments and provide written consent.

This is a 56 year old female diagnosed with breast cancer with metastases to the bones. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and has a bone lesion located in the upper end of the femur. The lesion is 18mm in size and has caused significant pain and limited mobility. She has not received any targeted treatment at the lesion site, such as radiotherapy or surgery. She has been receiving systemic bone therapy for the past 2 months with monthly pamidronate injections. She is willing to participate in the MEKANOS study which aims to evaluate the mechanical strength of the pathological bone using a numerical simulation model. A CT scan focused on the target lesion has been performed within the required time frame for the study. She understands the study requirements and has provided written informed consent for participation in the study.

28 yo female, primigravida at 30 weeks gestation with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2, presents with a history of healthy eating habits and regular physical activity. No history of gestational diabetes. Currently taking prenatal vitamins and has no significant medical history. Plans to exclusively breastfeed her infant for at least 2 months postpartum. Fluent in English and willing to complete up to 3 clinic visits at Pennington Biomedical Research Center. Intends to enroll her infant in the study after delivery. Willing for study staff to contact the primary care doctor who is providing prenatal care for the current pregnancy and to obtain information from the prenatal medical records, the labor and delivery records and the medical records of the infant at birth.

The patient is a 26-year-old pregnant woman living in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. She was recently diagnosed with HIV during antenatal care and has been initiated on lifelong ART. She is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and has no significant medical history. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not currently breastfeeding but plans to do so after delivery. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 11.5 g/dl WBC: 9000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl Beta hcg: positive for pregnancy

33yo female presenting with irregular menstrual bleeding and severe dysmenorrhea for the past 6 months. She reports heavy bleeding with clots and pain that is not relieved with over-the-counter pain medication. She has completed her family planning and is not interested in becoming pregnant. She has no history of hormonal treatment for the past 6 months, including contraception such as IUD. On physical examination, an enlarged uterus is palpated. Pelvic ultrasound shows diffuse adenomyosis with no focal lesions or adnexal masses. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing the efficacy of dienogest in the treatment of symptomatic adenomyosis.

7-year-old male student in an inner-city elementary school with a history of asthma and a recent episode of wheezing in the past 12 months. He experiences frequent asthma symptoms, including coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity and exposure to allergens. He is prescribed a daily controller medication and a rescue inhaler to manage his symptoms. He spends the majority of his day in one classroom and has experienced asthma exacerbations during school hours. His parents are concerned about his health and are interested in learning more about potential exposure risks specific to the classroom environment.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which is well-controlled on medication. She is married and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and is currently on medical leave. She complains of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and has noticed blood in her stools. She has undergone surgical resection of the primary tumor and has received one line of chemotherapy, which was not effective in controlling the disease. Her current ECOG performance status is 1. She is willing to undergo a biopsy of a liver metastatic lesion to assess putative biomarkers. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in this study and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential. She has adequate bone-marrow, liver, and renal function. She has no history of or currently known brain metastases. She has no known hypersensitivity to regorafenib or its excipients. She is able to swallow oral medications. She is willing to provide informed consent and understands that she may withdraw from the study at any time.

The clinical trial is seeking male or female Korean infants between 6-12 weeks of age who are in good health and have not received any investigational or non-registered products within 30 days preceding the first dose of the study vaccines. The study aims to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine GSK 1024850A compared to Prevenar™ when co-administered with a Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine during the first 6 months of life. The infant must have been born after a gestation period of 36 to 42 weeks inclusive, with a birth weight of at least 2.5 kilograms. They must not have any history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccines, neurological disorders, seizures, major congenital defects, or serious chronic illness. The infant must not have any acute disease at the time of enrolment, and study entry should be delayed until the illness has improved.

A 35-year-old male patient with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV infection presents with severe pain in his extremities, which he describes as burning, tingling, and shooting. The patient reports that the pain is affecting his daily activities and his quality of life. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and acupuncture, but the pain persists. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus or any other neurological disease. His current medications include AZT, cimetidine, and aspirin. He has no history of cardiac disease or allergy to tricyclic antidepressants, mexiletine, or benztropine. The patient abstains from drug and alcohol abuse. The patient is eligible for the study and is randomized to receive either amitriptyline, mexiletine, or benztropine mesylate as an active placebo. The patient's pain intensity is rated twice daily, and neurologic exams are performed at the beginning and end of the treatment. The patient is followed up for 10 days after completely tapering off the drug.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of periodontitis and tooth loss. She has good general health and is not currently taking any medications that affect inflammation or periodontal status. She does not have any gross oral pathology, neoplastic disease, renal failure, or chronic liver disease. Her HbA1c is within the ideal control range for diabetes. She is a non-smoker with good oral hygiene practices. She is interested in dental implant treatment and is willing to follow study procedures and instructions. She has no history of non-compliance or unreliability. She is available for the 18-month duration of the clinical trial and has read, understood, and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 16-year-old female with a BMI above the 85th percentile. She has no significant medical history and takes no medication. She lives with her parents and has two siblings. She attends high school and is in her sophomore year. She reports feeling self-conscious about her weight and has tried various diets without success. She has no known contraindications for physical activity and is able to participate in moderate exercise. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and are willing to attend the informational meeting.

A 30-year-old female patient with cystic fibrosis is diagnosed with CFRD during her annual CF studies. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Her BMI is 22, and she reports no significant weight changes. She reports occasional episodes of coughing and shortness of breath, but her pulmonary function tests are stable. The patient's fasting glucose level is found to be elevated, and she is diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia. The patient has no history of macrovascular complications, but she reports mild neuropathic symptoms such as numbness and tingling in her toes. She has no history of retinopathy or kidney disease. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of the prevalence of microvascular complications in CFRD patients with and without fasting hyperglycemia.

A 9-year-old female student from Al Salamania in Central Sudan is eligible for this clinical trial. She has been attending school for the past year and has not received any treatment for Schistosoma haematobium infection. She is in good health and has no known allergies or underlying medical conditions. Her parents have given consent for her participation in this study.

The patient is a 12-year-old child who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 4 years ago. They currently weigh 15 kg and have been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past year. However, their recent viral load test showed a viral load of greater than 1000 copies/mL, indicating that their current ART regimen is failing. The child's parents are willing to participate in the study and provide consent. The child has not been enrolled in any clinical or cohort trials within the past 30 days and does not have any active clinically significant diseases, such as tuberculosis or cardiac dysfunction. The child has not taken any investigational medications or vaccines within the past 30 days. The child's medical history and physical examination was unremarkable, and they have not been diagnosed with any non-HIV encephalopathy or WHO Clinical Stage 4 conditions. The child's life expectancy, according to the investigator's judgment, is greater than 6 months.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who presented with abdominal pain and bloating. Imaging studies revealed a cystic mass in the pancreas, which was further confirmed by biopsy. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has never been pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. The patient has been advised to undergo surgery for the pancreatic cystic neoplasm and has provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who had a surgery for rectal cancer and had a temporary ileostomy placed 3 months ago. He is now in the process of preparing for the reversal surgery. He is concerned about the possibility of developing a hernia after the stoma reversal surgery. He has no history of hernia or other abdominal surgeries. He is a retired accountant and lives with his wife. He exercises regularly and has a healthy diet. He is in good physical condition and has no chronic illnesses or conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent herniation and improve his quality of life after the stoma reversal surgery. He meets all the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. He is willing to provide informed consent and follow the study protocol.

A 52-year-old man, who works as a construction worker, has been experiencing severe knee pain for a few years. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis in both knees and was referred to Dr. Gregory Golladay, who recommended a total knee replacement surgery. The patient exercises regularly to manage his pain and has no underlying health issues. He takes over-the-counter pain medication as needed. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. He is fluent in English and understands the instructions given by health care providers. He has no hearing impairments.

A 56-year-old male diagnosed with stage A chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) is invited to participate in a clinical trial to study immune responses to influenza vaccination. He has not yet received any treatment for CLL. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for its control. He has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to flu vaccination. The patient is generally in good health, with no history of recent infections or hospital admissions. The patient is a non-smoker and exercises regularly. The trial investigators explain to the patient that the study aims to improve the immune response rate to flu vaccination in patients with CLL. They explain that the trial involves a new cream called Imiquimod, which may help boost the immune system's response to the flu vaccine. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provides informed consent.

A 55-year-old male patient was diagnosed with late-stage pancreatic cancer and has been receiving palliative care at home from a specialized palliative home care team. He lives in the catchment area of SPHC and wishes to live at home as long as possible. His general practitioner is involved in his care, and he is registered with Spitex care. He is able to read and understand German and fill out questionnaires with minimal assistance. The patient's expected survival time is approximately six months or less. He has agreed to participate in the PROAKTIV study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old former smoker who quit smoking 5 years ago. He has a 30-pack-year history of smoking and has been experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past 2 months. He also reports fatigue and unintentional weight loss of 10 lbs in the past month. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of cancer or other significant medical conditions. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds in the right lung base, and chest X-ray shows a suspicious mass in the right upper lobe. CT scan confirms a 2.5 cm mass in the right upper lobe with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. The patient is referred for EBUS-TBNA to evaluate the extent of the cancer and the presence of metastasis. He is willing to sign the consent form to participate in the trial.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy who has a history of dental caries and has been identified as being at high risk for developing further caries. He has fully erupted first permanent molars with deep and/or intermediate pits or fissures. His dental caries status is at least two decayed, filled, or missing teeth due to caries (dft ≥ 2). He has not received any topical fluoride application in the last six months. The patient does not have any systemic disease that may affect dental health.

A 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease presents with shortness of breath, fatigue and palpitations. The patient has been diagnosed with chronic atrial fibrillation and is currently taking amiodarone and metoprolol. The patient has a history of CHF with an ejection fraction of 30%. The patient's symptoms have been gradually worsening, and he is currently classified as NYHA Class III. The patient has undergone several cardioversions but has failed to maintain sinus rhythm. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate whether AVJ ablation followed by BiV pacing can improve his functional status and exercise capacity. The patient is able to walk 300 meters in 6 minutes and is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other clinical studies and is willing to give informed consent for study participation.

Mrs. Johnson is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with lung cancer. She has been scheduled for thoracotomy surgery in the next two weeks. She has a history of hypertension and mild depression, which is well controlled with medication. She has never used opioids before and is concerned about the risk of addiction. She has a family history of substance abuse and is worried about becoming dependent on pain medication. She has no significant history of neurological disease or psychiatric disorders. She speaks fluent English and has no vision or hearing impairment. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of non-invasive brain stimulation for pain relief. She is able to commit to the study visits and follow-up phone calls. She has no contraindications for MRI or TMS and is comfortable with these procedures.

This is a 35 year old female with a history of patella instability and trochlear dysplasia Dejour type B. She has experienced recurrent patella dislocations with associated pain and swelling, limiting her ability to perform daily activities and exercise. She underwent a lateral trochlear lengthening osteotomy two years ago to address her condition. She does not have any neurological disorders that may affect lower extremity muscle strength. She is interested in participating in this study to help evaluate the functional and clinical outcome of this new osteotomy and potentially improve treatment options for future patients with similar conditions.

8-year-old male with no known food sensitivities or allergies, no dietary restrictions, and no health, learning, emotional, or behavioral problems. Born full-term within the normal weight range for his age and height. Participates in regular physical activity and has no current or recent medication use.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 7 years. She has been taking medications for diabetes management and her HbA1C is well controlled below 9%. She has been experiencing neuropathic pain in her feet for the past 2 years, which is affecting her daily activities and sleep. She has tried different medications including anticonvulsants and analgesics, but the pain relief is not satisfactory. She has no history of psychiatric or medical illness and is not pregnant or lactating. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no allergies or sensitivity to the study medication or its components. She will be able to comply with study directions and complete the entire study course. She is willing to give written informed consent and participate in the study.

A 37-week pregnant woman is admitted to the hospital in labor. During labor, the fetal heart rate drops and the baby is delivered by emergency cesarean section. The baby is diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) due to inadequate blood flow and oxygen delivery to the neonatal brain. The medical team determines that the baby is eligible for the pilot study on umbilical cord milking for neonates with HIE. The parents agree to participate in the study and give their consent. The baby is included in the study and will receive umbilical cord milking to investigate the feasibility and safety of this intervention. The medical team will closely monitor the baby's condition and assess the short-term outcomes to determine the potential benefits of umbilical cord milking for neonates with moderate and severe HIE.

A 40-year old female resident of a rural village in the Vientiane municipality, Lao PDR, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for predicting the prevalence of diabetes in her community. She is married with two children and works as a farmer. She has no known medical history of diabetes, but her father was diagnosed with diabetes when he was in his 50s. She does not smoke, but she admits to being physically inactive due to her work on the farm. She has a BMI of 27.5, and her waist circumference measures 90 cm. She reports having no history of dyslipidemia or gestational diabetes. She is willing to participate in the physical exam, blood pressure measurement and fasting glucose test to help in the development of risk scores for predicting the prevalence of diabetes in her community.

Pt is a 16yo M/F who is generally healthy and fluent in English. They are experiencing increased stress and anxiety due to the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact on their daily life, including social distancing measures and remote learning. They have not had any prior mindfulness training or practice with typically sitting meditation or yoga in the past 60 days. They are not currently taking any psychotropic medication and do not have any MRI contraindications or pregnancy. They are willing and able to give written informed assent, and their legal guardian/representative is also willing and able to provide written informed consent. They are interested in participating in a randomized controlled feasibility study to test the effectiveness of TARA intervention in improving their emotional well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic.

48 yo male presents to the emergency department with chest pain radiating to his left arm and shortness of breath. He has a history of smoking, hypertension, and high cholesterol. EKG shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads and troponin levels are elevated. The patient is diagnosed with an acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and is taken for emergent cardiac catheterization with successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to the left anterior descending artery. Patient is stable and able to consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the use of Levosimendan for post-conditioning in patients with acute STEMI. No previous myocardial infarction or bypass surgery. No known heart valve disease. MRI is not contraindicated. Onset of symptoms was within 6 hours. There is no evidence of respiratory failure or unstable hemodynamics.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer five years ago. After undergoing multiple rounds of chemotherapy and surgery, she has since been in remission. However, during her most recent follow-up appointment, her doctor discovered that the cancer had returned. The patient is now experiencing abdominal pain and bloating, along with fatigue and nausea. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. She is currently not taking any other medications or supplements. She is willing to undergo tissue biopsy for research purposes and is open to participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a newborn infant who was born at 38 weeks gestation. The baby had a low Apgar score of 4 at ten minutes after birth and required tracheal ventilation for 20 minutes after birth. The baby also had an umbilical cord pH of 6.8 at birth. The baby was diagnosed with moderate hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) based on altered state of consciousness, hypotonia, and abnormal reflexes. The baby is currently intubated, ventilated, and sedated, and is being treated with cooling therapy. The baby is less than 5 hours old and weighs more than the 2nd centile for gestational age. The baby has no major congenital abnormalities, bowel obstruction, or chromosomal anomalies. The baby's mean arterial pressure is greater than 40mmHg, and the oxygen requirement via mechanical ventilator is less than 40%. The baby's PEEP requirement is less than 8cm H2O, and the arterial/capillary/venous pCO2 is within the acceptable range (<7kPa). The baby's postnatal age is less than or equal to 5 hours. The baby has not had any seizures for at least 30 minutes and is considered to be a good candidate for additional inhaled xenon therapy.

A 45-year-old male patient presents to the ophthalmologist with complaints of eye pain, redness, and blurred vision. On examination, the ophthalmologist diagnoses him with a corneal ulcer and recommends subconjunctival antibiotic and antifungal injection. The patient is informed that the injection may cause some discomfort and pain. The patient has no history of allergies to local anesthetics, antibiotics, or antifungal drugs. He has not taken any NSAIDs or weak opioids in the last 24

The patient is a 30 year old male who was recently exposed to carbon monoxide in a poorly ventilated workspace. He has been experiencing headaches, nausea, and dizziness for the past few days. He went to the emergency department where he was diagnosed with carbon monoxide poisoning and received treatment. His carboxyhemoglobin levels were measured, and he was found to have a level of 20%. He is now stable but is being monitored closely to ensure that his condition does not worsen. He is an electrician and works long hours in construction sites. He is a smoker and has a history of alcohol abuse. He is living alone and has no significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of carbon monoxide poisoning.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing tingling, numbness, and pain in his hands and feet for the past 3 years. He has a family history of the same symptoms, and his father was diagnosed with Familial Transthyretin-Mediated Amyloid Polyneuropathy (FAP) at the age of 55. The patient has been diagnosed with FAP and has been experiencing Stage II symptoms (polyneuropathy disability [PND] IIIa). His NIS score during screening is 60, and nerve conduction studies (NCS) score is 4. He has a mutation consistent with ATTR-PN confirmed by genotyping obtained at Screening prior to randomization. The patient has an anticipated survival of more than 2 years and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He has not had a liver transplant, and he is not planning to undergo liver transplantation during the study period. The patient does not have sensorimotor or autonomic neuropathy not related to ATTR-PN, for example, autoimmune disease or monoclonal gammopathy, malignancy, or alcohol abuse. He has Vitamin B-12 levels within the normal range. He does not have clinical evidence of untreated hyper/hypothyroidism, leptomeningeal TTR amyloidosis, Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes, active hepatitis B or C, or known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. His NYHA heart failure classification is Class II. He has not had any malignancy in the last 2 years, except for basal or squamous cell carcinoma. He is not currently undergoing treatment for ATTR-PN with patisiran, inotersen, or other gene silencing agents, marketed drug products lacking a label indication for ATTR- PN, natural products or derivatives used as unproven therapies for ATTR-PN within 14 days, or 90 days for patisiran and 180 days for inotersen prior to dosing. Prior to screening, tafamidis, if already prescribed to potential subjects as part of their established background therapy, is allowed at the labeled dosage and administration of 20 mg/day for the treatment of ATTR-PN with, in the opinion of the Investigator, evidence of disease progression while on tafamidis treatment. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial of AG10.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with complaints of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. The patient's CT imaging showed findings consistent with Covid-19 pneumonia, and the PCR test result was positive. The patient has no known comorbidities and is not on any medication. He has no history of chronic inflammatory disease, autoimmune disease, cancer, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The patient is a non-smoker and is not pregnant. He has no known history of kidney or liver failure, acute pulmonary embolism, or cerebrovascular disease. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has given written consent.

A 25-year-old healthy woman who works as a nurse is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new drug. She has no underlying medical conditions and takes no medication other than occasional over-the-counter pain relievers for menstrual cramps. Her body weight is 50 kg and her BMI is within the range of 18 to 30 kg/m^2. She has never had any history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, seizures, or significant medical conditions. She has never used any investigational drug or tobacco products. She has a normal blood pressure and has not experienced any significant back pain or headaches. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in a first-in-human study.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. He reports difficulty walking and standing up from a seated position. He has been previously diagnosed with mild-to-moderate knee osteoarthritis (mKOA) by his primary care physician. The patient's Kellgren-Lawrence grade is 2 and his Western Ontario and McMaster Universities (WOMAC) Osteoarthritis Index (Likert version 3.1) pain subscale is 12. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of acute fracture, rheumatoid arthritis, gouty arthritis, traumatic arthritis or inflammatory arthritis. He is not allergic to HA or lidocaine and has not received any HA or corticosteroid injections to the target knee in the past 6 months. The patient has not undergone any surgery on the target knee in the past 6 months and does not have OA of the target knee with K-L grade 4. The patient does not have active liver and renal disease, cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial and provide written informed consent.

A 32-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder with psychotic features (DSM-IV 296.24) is eligible for this clinical trial. She has already completed an 8-week study of Corlux versus placebo (an inactive pill) and has experienced a significant improvement in her symptoms. Her medical history reveals that she has no major medical problems and has no history of an allergic reaction to CORLUX. She is 18 to 75 years of age and is able to provide written informed consent. She is willing to participate in the study and receive additional courses of treatment with Corlux periodically if a psychotic episode should reappear during a period of one year.

Patient is a healthy, non-smoking 25-year-old woman who is not currently taking any medications or oral contraceptives. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently menstruating. Her BMI is within normal range (less than 30). She does not have any chronic conditions requiring regular treatment or medical follow-up, bleeding disorders, or current infections. The patient is interested in participating in a study examining and comparing the rehydration effect of different types of bottled water on various health markers following exercise-induced dehydration in a controlled environment.

A 54-year-old man came to the clinic with complaints of persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath that had been present for the last month. He is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history of smoking. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking anti-hypertensive medication for the past 5 years. He has not had any surgeries or major injuries in the past 6 months. His physical examination shows decreased breath sounds on the right side of his chest. A chest x-ray revealed a mass in the right lung. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of small cell lung cancer with extensive-stage disease. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. His bone marrow function and organ function are normal. He does not have any brain metastases, and he has not received any previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his cancer. He has been informed of the investigational nature of this study and is willing to participate.

75-year-old male participant of the DANCAVAS study, asymptomatic, with no known history of diabetes, hypertension or hypercholesterolemia. The patient is able to give written informed consent and has a BMI between 20 and 35. The patient has no known history of CAD or Apoplexia and is not currently experiencing symptoms of CAD. The patient has not been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation or other tachyarrhythmia that would prevent CCTA analysis. The patient has an estimated Glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥ 45 ml/min and no known contrast allergy. The patient has not been diagnosed with untreated hyperthyroidism.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Raynaud's Phenomenon for the past 2 years. She experiences regular attacks of acral cyanosis and pain in the fingers when exposed to cold temperatures or when under stress. The patient has tried several conservative and pharmacological treatments but has not experienced significant relief of her symptoms. She does not have any skin alterations such as scars, ulcers or gangrene in the examined area. The patient does not suffer from upper limb entrapment syndrome, central nervous system polyneuropathy, Hypothyroidism, renal failure, cerebral or cardiac ischemic disease. She has not abused drugs or alcohol and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not use vibratory tools nor does she have any tumor process. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent document.

A 25-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of chronic lower back pain. She had a previous history of a motor vehicle accident resulting in a spinal injury. She has been prescribed opioids for pain management but is concerned about developing an addiction. She is looking for alternative ways to manage her pain and is interested in learning more about non-pharmacological methods. She is also interested in learning about addiction treatment options in case she develops a dependence on opioids. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that would provide her access to a helpline with trained counselors who can provide her with educational materials and support to manage her pain safely and reduce her dependence on opioids. She is open to referral to treatment programs if needed.

55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 10 years, presents with moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy and cataracts. The patient has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. The patient does not have a history of glaucoma, active proliferative diabetic retinopathy, neovascularization of the iris, tractional retinal detachment, or any prior ocular surgeries. The patient’s renal function is within normal limits. The patient has no history of cerebrovascular accident or uveitis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of intravitreal injection of triamcinolone combined with cataract surgery on diabetic macular edema and diabetic retinopathy. The patient will undergo a complete eye examination, OCT, FAG, and color photography 2 weeks prior to the operation. After being divided into a control group (Phyco, PCIOL) and a triamcinolone treatment group (Phaco with PCIOL+IVT), the patient will receive cataract surgery and will be followed up for 6 months. The patient will undergo regular examinations to monitor any progression of diabetic retinopathy and any complications such as increased intraocular pressure or endophthalmitis.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IIB cervical cancer after experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain. She is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove pelvic and abdominal lymph nodes to determine the extent of the disease. She has never smoked, drinks alcohol moderately, and exercises regularly. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cancer in her family. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study glycoprotein and glycan in tissue and blood samples of patients with cervical cancer to improve the understanding of the disease and identify potential biomarkers.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been struggling with alcohol addiction for the past 5 years. He has tried several times to quit drinking, but has relapsed each time. He has experienced physical and emotional consequences due to his alcohol use, including liver damage, job loss, and strained relationships with family and friends. He is highly motivated to quit drinking and has sought help from addiction treatment centers in the past. His current abstinence from alcohol is 3 weeks. He reports that he experiences intense cravings when he is exposed to alcohol-related cues, such as the smell of alcohol or seeing someone drinking. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that uses transcranial direct current stimulation supported cue exposure therapy to help prevent relapse in alcohol dependency. He does not have any history of epilepsy, acute psychotic episodes, or other substance use disorders besides nicotine dependency.

A 35-year-old woman presented to the gastroenterology clinic with complaints of abdominal pain, frequent bloody diarrhea, and weight loss. She was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) 5 years ago and has been on various medications including oral 5-aminosalicylate, oral corticosteroids, and azathioprine. However, her symptoms have not been well-controlled. Her colonoscopy revealed moderate to severe inflammation and a Mayo score of 8. She met the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial as she has moderately to severely active UC and is willing to undergo genetic testing to determine the likelihood of response to golimumab treatment. She has not received any biologic therapy targeted at tumor necrosis factor alpha in the past and is not currently taking any prohibited medications. She has no history of viral or bacterial vaccination within the past 8 weeks. Her physical exam and laboratory results were unremarkable except for mild anemia. She is interested in participating in the study and signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with a history of non-infectious uveitis that has been unresponsive to topical medications. She has previously been treated with methotrexate for six weeks without improvement. The patient has not received any previous biologic medications for uveitis and has not had any intraocular steroid injections or ophthalmologic surgeries within the past three months. She has no history of trauma or intraocular surgery related to her uveitis. The patient is able to provide informed consent, and her parent/guardian is also able to provide consent. She is sexually immature and not currently sexually active. The patient is able to cooperate for a non-sedated slit lamp exam and visual acuity examination. Her PPD test was negative and her screening laboratory tests all met the inclusion criteria. The patient has not had any serious infections or opportunistic infections within the past three to six months. She has no history of lymphoproliferative disease or malignancy. The patient does not have any signs or symptoms of severe, progressive, or uncontrolled renal, hepatic, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, pulmonary, cardiac, neurologic, or cerebral disease. She has not used any investigational drug within the past 30 days. The patient has not received a solid organ transplant.

This is a 28-year-old female who has been using cannabis regularly for the past 5 years. She reports experiencing anxiety and depression, as well as occasional psychotic symptoms such as hearing voices and paranoid thoughts. She has tried to quit using cannabis in the past but has been unsuccessful. She has no history of other drug use or neurological damage. She is not pregnant and is HIV negative. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effects of psychological and pharmacological treatment on regular users of cannabis and psychostimulants in a treatment center in Israel. She is willing to undergo psychological evaluation before and during treatment and follow up at 4 months. She is also willing to undergo brain imaging of the dopamine receptor D2 using [I123] IBZM in Single Photon Emitted Tomography (SPECT) before and after treatment in order to evaluate the effects of treatment on dopamine turnover in the brain.

A 58-year-old female was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in 2011, after presenting with cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. A biopsy confirmed the presence of EGFR mutation (19 exon) and contrast CT showed at least one measurable lesion with the longest diameter >10 mm. She was started on first-line treatment of erlotinib, an EGFR-TKI, and had a partial response after 3 months of therapy. However, she experienced disease progression after 10 months and was switched to second-line therapy of afatinib, another EGFR-TKI, which led to a partial response for 7 months. She then had a second progression and was switched to chemotherapy. A retrospective analysis of her medical records will be conducted to evaluate her treatment strategy and progression-free survival 2 (PFS2) will be assessed. The patient did not receive EGFR-TKI concurrently with chemotherapy or other anti-tumor drug, and her evaluated lesions were not previously treated with radiotherapy. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study as she had taken EGFR-TKI as first/second line therapy and has an appraisable disease.

39-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis diagnosed at the age of 26. She has been on mesalamine for the past 13 years with occasional flares requiring short courses of oral steroids. She reports occasional abdominal pain, urgency, and loose stools with blood. She denies any extra intestinal manifestations of the disease. She has never been tested for Helicobacter pylori infection and has no history of proton pump inhibitor or antibiotic use within the past eight weeks. She is a non-smoker with no other significant medical history or medication use. She presents to Assiut University Hospital to participate in the cross-sectional study to detect the prevalence of H. pylori among patients with inflammatory bowel disease.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 8 weeks. She reports that the pain is primarily located below the L5 vertebra and is accompanied by tenderness overlying the sacroiliac joint(s). She has also noticed increased pain with certain movements and positions, such as crossing her legs or standing for prolonged periods of time. She rates her average pain level over the past week as 7 out of 10. The patient has not received prior sacroiliac joint injections and has no history of inflammatory spondyloarthropathy or untreated coagulopathy. She is not allergic to contrast dye or bupivacaine. The patient is willing to undergo sacroiliac joint injection for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 73-year-old man who underwent a routine health check-up and was found to have an elevated PSA level of 25 ng/ml. He has no symptoms related to his prostate and his digital rectal examination was unremarkable. An ultrasound of the prostate revealed an enlarged gland with an indeterminate lesion in the right lobe. Therefore, a transrectal ultrasound guided biopsy of the prostate is recommended to rule out prostate cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the standard method of prostate biopsy with a non-invasive "liquid biopsy" model, which uses blood and urine biomarkers and an algorithm to predict the presence of aggressive prostate cancer. He meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to provide informed written consent.

A 12-year-old boy presents with progressive neurological symptoms, including difficulty in coordination, slurred speech, and frequent falls. He has a history of developmental delay and was diagnosed with Niemann-Pick Type C1 disease after genetic testing revealed two NPC1 mutations. The patient has difficulty walking independently and requires assistance. He is currently taking medications for his symptoms, but they do not seem to be effective in slowing the progression of the disease. The patient and his parents are interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the potential protective effect of lithium carbonate on the brain in patients with Niemann-Pick Type C1 disease. The patient's liver and kidney function are normal, and he does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the trial. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study and are willing to follow the protocol and attend all required visits.

A 56-year-old woman presents with bothersome urinary symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and occasional urge incontinence. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and they have a negative impact on her daily life. She reports having at least 4 episodes of urge incontinence per day, which are associated with moderate to severe urgency. She also reports a mean frequency of urinary voiding events per day of more than 10 times, as recorded in the baseline 3-day voiding diary. The patient has not taken antimuscarinics, anticholinergics or beta-3 agonists for the past 2 weeks. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to follow all study-related procedures. The patient is ambulatory and able to use the toilet independently. She is not pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding. The patient is not diagnosed with stress urinary incontinence as the most bothersome type of urinary incontinence. She does not have an abnormal post-void residual urine volume, abnormal serum creatinine levels, or history of chronic kidney disease. The patient is not diagnosed with diabetes with peripheral nerve compromise or severe uncontrolled diabetes. She does not have known polyuria, peripheral arterial disease, the presence of a urinary fistula, bladder stone or interstitial cystitis, diagnosis of prostate, urethral, or bladder cancer, clinically significant urethral stricture disease or bladder neck contracture, or morbid obesity. The patient is not currently using, or has used in the past 3 months, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) in the pelvic region, back, legs, or feet. The patient has not been treated with onabotulinumtoxinA in the past 9 months, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, or pelvic floor muscle stimulation. She does not have a clinically significant peripheral neuropathy or a history of pelvic pain as a primary diagnosis in the past 12 months (VAS score of >4 (scale of 0 to 10)). The patient does not have neurogenic bladder (i.e. Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's, Spinal Cord Injury) and has not used an investigational drug, biologic, or medical device in the past 4 weeks.

The patient is a 62-year-old retired teacher who was diagnosed with dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in both eyes two years ago. She has experienced slow progressive vision loss, which has affected her daily activities such as reading and watching television. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She has previously received intraocular injections for her condition, but due to their high cost, she is unable to continue with the treatment. She is interested in alternative treatments and agrees to participate in this study, which involves acupuncture and periocular massage.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been suffering from major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 6 months. She experiences feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities that she used to enjoy. Additionally, she often experiences anxiety and worries about the future, which has been affecting her daily life. She has not received any treatment for her condition and does not have a history of psychotic or bipolar illness. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs and does not have any known allergies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl born with profound sensorineural hearing loss. The patient has been using hearing aids since the age of 1 but has not shown significant improvement in her hearing ability. The patient's parents have decided to opt for cochlear implant surgery to improve their daughter's hearing ability and communication skills. The patient has undergone cochlear implant surgery and is currently in the post-operative period. The patient has no history of other medical conditions or surgeries. The patient and her parents have expressed interest in participating in the Cochlear Implants Registry in Thailand Project to help improve the outcomes of cochlear implant surgery for future patients.

A 52-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of stage 2 breast cancer is looking for alternative methods of axillary staging. She has a family history of breast cancer, and her mother is currently in remission after undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Her oncologist has recommended primary systemic therapy (PST) before surgery to shrink the tumor and the lymph nodes before surgery. However, the patient is concerned about the potential side effects of surgery and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will compare the accuracy of Sentinel Node Biopsy (SNB) vs. PET/MRI in detecting axillary lymph node macro-metastases. She has positive axillary lymph nodes at diagnosis, confirmed by cytology. She is a nonsmoker and has no significant past medical history. She is not pregnant and has no contraindication to PET or MRI. She is willing to undergo PET/MRI prior to PST and is willing to undergo axillary surgery after PST per the study protocol. She has signed informed consent and is committed to attending all study visits.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing infertility issues. She has no history of multiple abdominopelvic surgery and her BMI is within the range of 18-35kg/m2. She is scheduled for ambulatory laparoscopic surgery with a precise indication. The procedure will be either exploratory or diagnostic, an exploration of infertility, performing a tubal permeability test, performing a salpingectomy, realization of a tubal sterilization, realization of a tubal plasty, performing an ovariectomy, or performing a simple ovarian cystectomy. She has been informed about the procedure during her preoperative consultation and has signed the consent in a free and informed manner upon admission to the hospital. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and she is able to receive informed information and give consent. She is not a person deprived of liberty. The patient is not undergoing emergency surgery, and the procedure is not carcinological surgery or complex surgery of endometriosis or removal of a large cyst from the ovary.

This is a 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus who has been diagnosed with mild to moderately severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) and has no clinically significant diabetic macular edema (CI-DME) at baseline. She has a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20 in both eyes and is willing to wear a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) device. She has not been initiated on intensive insulin treatment in the past 3 months and is not planning to do so in the next 3 months. She has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to any component of fenofibrate or fluorescein dye. She has not been treated with a prescription fibrate medication within the past 12 months and has no current use of medications that are excluded from the trial. She has no evidence of definite neovascularization, no current CI-DME, and no history of major ocular surgery within the prior 4 months or anticipated within the next 6 months following randomization. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and meet all other eligibility criteria for the study.

A 19-year-old male was diagnosed with osteosarcoma in his right femur and underwent surgical resection followed by chemotherapy. However, the tumor has recurred and is refractory to treatment. A biopsy confirmed the recurrence of osteosarcoma. The patient has good performance status and is otherwise healthy. He has no history of allergic reactions to any drugs. He has not participated in any other clinical trial within the past 2 weeks. He is not sexually active and has no plan to have children in the near future.

The patient is a 58 year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 10 years ago. He has been treated with a combination of levodopa and dopamine agonists, but has experienced motor fluctuations and dyskinesias. His physician has recommended Duodopa/Duopa therapy via percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy-with jejunal extension (PEG-J) to better manage his symptoms. The patient has no history of deep brain stimulation or other PD surgeries, and is not currently receiving continuous subcutaneous apomorphine infusion. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 26 and is able to understand and complete study questionnaires. He has no history of participation in concurrent interventional clinical trials.

25 year old male, healthy with no known medical conditions, currently not on any medication, non-smoker, and non-alcoholic. He is able to understand study procedures and willing to sign informed consent. He has no history of constipation or severe diarrhea within the past 14 days and has not undergone any gastrointestinal procedures or treatments in the past year. He is not currently participating in any other investigational trial and has no known allergies to the study drug or placebo. He is reachable in case of emergency.

The patient is a 26-year-old man who has been using methamphetamine intravenously for the past 2 years. He has a history of depression and has been hospitalized once for suicidal ideation. He is not currently seeking abstinence-focused treatment. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs other than methamphetamine. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial for the treatment of methamphetamine dependence. He is fluent in English and weighs 80 kg. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his laboratory tests are within normal range except for liver function tests, which are slightly elevated but less than 3 times the upper limit of normal. He has no history of asthma or chronic respiratory illnesses.

The patient is a 57 year old male diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) in complete remission after undergoing chemotherapy. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, renal or hepatic dysfunction, and is on medication for hypertension that is well controlled. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife of 30 years. He has two adult children who live in a different state. He exercises regularly and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could improve his chances of survival following an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with head and neck cancer six months ago. He underwent radiation therapy and chemotherapy and is currently in remission. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication daily to manage it. He has noticed swelling and tightness in his neck in the past few weeks and has been experiencing difficulty swallowing. He is able to speak and eat but finds it uncomfortable. He speaks English fluently and is able to read and write. He lives with his wife and they have two adult children who live nearby. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that can help him manage his symptoms and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who has a history of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. She is currently at 33 weeks of gestation and her HBV DNA level is higher than 200,000 IU per milliliter. She has never received any antiviral treatment for HBV infection, and her alanine aminotransferase and total bilirubin levels have been normal (less than 40 U/L and less than 17.1 μmol/L, respectively) during the pregnancy. The patient has no evidence of other liver diseases or coinfection with hepatitis C, D, E, or human immunodeficiency virus. She has no history of genetic diseases or fetal deformities in a previous pregnancy. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and adhere to the trial protocol. She has not received any treatment to reduce alanine aminotransferase and total bilirubin levels. She has no clinical signs of threatened miscarriage and her ultrasound examinations have not shown any evidence of fetal deformities.
