The patient is not concurrently taking any other drugs, including nephrotoxic drugs, immune modulators, cytotoxic drugs, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or steroids. Her hemoglobin level is greater than 80 g/L, her neutrophil count is greater than 1.0 × 10^9/L, and her albumin level is greater than 30 g/L. She is eligible for this clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide to prevent perinatal transmission of HBV.

A 50-year-old woman presents with history of early stage breast cancer (stage IIA) that was surgically removed and treated with radiation therapy. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is currently on hormonal therapy (tamoxifen) as per her oncologist's recommendation. She is married and has two children. She is a homemaker and lives a sedentary lifestyle. Her BMI is 32 and she admits to consuming high amounts of alcohol (around 100g/d). She is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the intervention. She has no digestive disease or allergies to the key foods of the intervention.

The patient is a 37-year-old female physician working at Mayo Clinic. She has been practicing medicine for 10 years and has a full-time position. Her work schedule is often stressful and involves long hours. She reports experiencing frequent fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and high levels of stress related to her job. She does not currently practice mindfulness training on a regular basis and has not participated in any clinical or research programs that intervene on her quality of life or stress levels in the past 3 weeks. She is generally healthy and has no contraindicated comorbid health conditions that would interfere with the proper use of the Muse-S™ system. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and complete all aspects of the trial. She has access to a smartphone or tablet device.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic constipation for the past 2 years. Despite dietary modifications and the use of laxatives, he has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He has no known gastrointestinal conditions and has not used laxatives in the past 2 years. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and does not have diabetes or any food intolerance. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a non-invasive method for assessing colonic motility. The participant is willing to undergo an electro-entero-graphy (EEnG) procedure, which involves placing surface electrodes on his abdomen to measure electrical activity in the colon. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is an adult with a suspected functional colonic motility disorder that has been diagnosed previously. He does not have any exclusion criteria, such as the presence of an intestinal stoma or use of continuous tube feeding. The participant understands the study requirements and is willing to complete questionnaires assessing the burden of the EEnG procedure.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III epithelial ovarian cancer. The cancer was detected during a pelvic exam after she experienced abdominal bloating and discomfort. The patient underwent surgery and was found to have residual disease. The patient has no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. She is married and has two adult children. The patient works part-time as a teacher's assistant at a local elementary school. She enjoys gardening, baking, and spending time with her family. She is in good overall health, with a BMI of 23, and her blood pressure and labs are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and understands the risks and benefits associated with it. She is committed to complying with all study requirements and has a good support system in place. She has not received any live vaccines within the last 30 days and is not currently taking any immunosuppressive therapy. The patient is excited about the possibility of receiving a novel treatment that could improve her chances of survival.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who is a smoker and also uses multiple substances. He currently lives in Ottawa or Toronto and has been smoking an average of 15 cigarettes per day for the past year. He is interested in participating in an initiative that will help him improve his quality of life and connect him with opportunities for education, short-term work, and volunteer positions. He is open to participating in life-skills workshops, training, and accessing health services for testing and treatment for HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis-C. He is looking for support to reduce his smoking and other substance use and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled cross-over trial to help others in similar situations. He is available for follow-up for the next 12 months and is not currently enrolled in any other smoking cessation program or addiction treatment program.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is physically active and enjoys running and weightlifting. She has a BMI of 24 and has no chronic diseases or medical conditions that could affect the study outcomes. She is a non-smoker and is not taking any prescription medication. Her VO2max is 56 mL/min/kgLM, which meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand the proteome signature dynamics and remodelling in human skeletal muscle induced by exercise training.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic knee pain. He has been scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and has been classified as ASA I. He does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not currently receiving any anxiolytic or antipsychotic treatment. He has not been taking any opioids or soporifics for his chronic knee pain. The patient will be discharged on the same day of the surgery and will have a responsible adult to follow him at home for 24 hours. The patient is fluent in Danish and has provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia and recurrent urinary tract infections. The patient's urologist has recommended a radical prostatectomy due to the presence of prostate cancer on biopsy. The patient has an ASA score of I and has not had any major surgeries in the past. The patient does not have a known allergy to hydroxyethyl starch and has normal renal function with a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. The patient does not have any significant hepatic disease and has normal liver function tests. The patient does not have any coagulation disorders with an INR of 1.1. The patient agrees to participate in the study and follow the protocol for infusion of hydroxyethyl starch solutions during the urologic surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis six months ago. She has been experiencing moderate to severe joint pain, stiffness, and swelling in at least three joints. She has been treated with adalimumab and methotrexate combination therapy for the last three months, but she has not responded well to it. Her condition has worsened, and she has lost a satisfactory response to the combination therapy. She is currently not taking adalimumab and has been off it for the last two weeks. She has no history of hepatitis B or C and has tested negative for both. She is not pregnant and is willing to take a serum and urine pregnancy test before starting the study drug. She has been taking 15 mg of methotrexate weekly for the last 12 weeks and has had a normal chest X-ray within the last three months. She has tested negative for tuberculosis. She has no other significant concurrent medical conditions and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 30-year-old male diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) and an EDSS score of 4.5 was referred to the physical therapy department for lower extremity strength testing. He has had two episodes of MS exacerbation in the past year, for which he received treatment with intravenous steroids. He is currently on disease-modifying therapy (DMT) with interferon beta-1a. He reports mild difficulty in walking long distances and climbing stairs. He has no history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. He denies any pain or orthopedic conditions affecting his lower extremities. He has no history of other neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS or Parkinson's disease. He is not pregnant, and he has no cognitive deficits. He is willing to participate in the strength testing for the study.

This is a 42-year-old female who had a left transtibial amputation due to a traumatic injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident a year ago. She currently wears a prosthesis and is able to ambulate independently with the help of a cane. She has no other neurological or orthopedic problems that affect her posture or gait. She is motivated to participate in the study and understands the commands given to her. She has no history of mental illness or cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the biomechanical changes that occur after an amputation and contribute to the development of better prosthetic devices.

A 5-year-old boy named Max has been experiencing difficulties with his balance and gait since he was 2 years old. The symptoms have been progressing over time and he now has trouble walking, running, and climbing stairs. Max's parents have taken him to several doctors and specialists, but a diagnosis was not made until recently when he was diagnosed with metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) after undergoing genetic testing. Max is an active child who enjoys playing with his friends and participating in sports. He has no other significant medical history and his family has no history of MLD. Max's parents are eager to participate in this study to help further research on MLD and to better understand the natural history of the disease.

A 30-year-old female with a BMI of 29.8 kg/m2 presents with a history of occasional episodes of mild dizziness and fatigue. She reports a healthy diet with occasional indulgences in sweets and desserts. She is a low consumer of tea and coffee and is willing to refrain from both during the 48 hours prior to the test days and on the test day. Her fasting blood glucose level is 5.5 mmol/l via capillary finger-stick blood sample using a SureStep glucometer (Lifescan, Milpitas, CA). She is not taking any medications known to affect glycemia, lipid metabolism or appetite, nor is she taking any vitamin or other supplements. She is a non-smoker and has no history of acute or chronic disease. The patient is willing to consume all test foods and is interested in participating in the study to better understand the impact of grape juice on postprandial glycemic response and cognitive function.

The patient is a premature infant born at 28 weeks gestational age with a birth weight of 900 grams. The infant has no known chromosomal, structural, metabolic, endocrine or renal abnormalities. The infant is currently less than 18 hours old and is expected to survive past 72 hours. The parents have given informed consent for the infant to participate in this clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department complaining of lower abdominal pain for the past 24 hours. The pain is constant, crampy, and located in the left lower quadrant. The patient describes his pain as a 7/10 in severity. He has had no bowel movements in the past 24 hours and has had decreased appetite. He denies any fevers, chills, or night sweats. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which he controls with medication. He denies any allergies to medications. Physical examination reveals left lower quadrant tenderness and guarding with no rebound tenderness or palpable masses. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory studies show an elevated white blood cell count of 14,000/µl with a left shift, and an elevated C-reactive protein level of 40 mg/l. A contrast enema shows evidence of sigmoid diverticulitis. The patient has not received any antibiotics in the past 2 weeks. He agrees to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has a medical history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and chronic heart failure. He has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. He has been classified as NYHA class III. He has been on a combination of medications for his heart failure, including diuretics and ACE inhibitors. His recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 40%, which places him in Group B of the study. He has been compliant with his diabetes medication, which includes metformin and insulin. He has no significant valvulopathies or history of cardiac surgery within the past year. His kidney function is normal. He is willing to participate in the study and attend periodic clinical evaluations and echocardiographic exams.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male patient presented to the hospital with a history of acute myeloid leukemia. He underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) 10 days ago. He had a good performance status before the transplantation. However, he started experiencing abdominal pain, jaundice, and ascites 5 days after the HSCT. His liver function tests were elevated, and an ultrasound showed hepatic vein thrombosis consistent with VOD. He was started on standard therapy with ursodiol and diuretics. However, his condition continued to worsen, and he developed multi-organ failure. The transplant team discussed the use of defibrotide as a compassionate use option. After obtaining informed consent, the patient was started on defibrotide therapy. He showed significant improvement in his liver function tests, ascites, and overall clinical status. He was discharged from the hospital after a 3-week stay and continued to receive defibrotide therapy as an outpatient.

50-year-old female patient diagnosed with stage II squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue, currently undergoing radiation therapy to the head and neck region. Patient is experiencing grade 2 oral mucositis based on WHO criteria, with painful ulcers and erythema present in the oral cavity. Patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or systemic diseases. Estimated survival is greater than 6 months. Patient is willing to participate in the study and able to comply with the instructions for using the 5% Dexpanthenol mouthwash three times daily.

Maria is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). She underwent a thorough workup including serum hematology, biochemistry, antibodies against Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) viral capsid antigen (VCA) and early antigen (EA), and imaging studies such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). She has no history of thyroid disorders, pituitary disorders, prior thyroid surgery, or drug history of thyroxine (T4) or triiodothyronine (T3). She has not undergone any radiation therapy to other areas. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Maria is planned to receive only one course of radical intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) with or without adjunct chemotherapy for her NPC as curative treatment. She will be monitored closely for any biochemical and clinical hypothyroidism after the treatment.

A 63-year-old male was admitted to the ICU after a severe motor vehicle accident. He sustained multiple injuries, including chest trauma. The patient required mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. Chest X-ray showed a pleural effusion on the right side. The patient is being managed with a sedation and pain regimen, and is receiving prophylactic antibiotics for ventilator-associated pneumonia. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is alert and oriented, but is unable to communicate due to the endotracheal tube. His vital signs are stable, and he is tolerating intermittent suctioning. The patient is not on any anticoagulant therapy. The patient's family has been updated about his condition and has given consent for the insertion of a pleural drain if deemed necessary by the attending clinician.

A 10 month old male infant with a history of occasional diarrhea who is experiencing watery stools for the past 24 hours with no signs of dehydration. The infant is otherwise healthy and has no history of chronic illnesses. The parents are available throughout the study period and are able to give written informed consent to participation in the study. The infant has not received any probiotics or antibiotics in the previous 2 weeks before recruitment. The family is interested in participating in the study to help improve their child's symptoms of acute gastroenteritis.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with peripheral artery disease. She is scheduled to undergo an elective catheter-based procedure via the common femoral vein using a 6 to 12 Fr inner diameter introducer sheath. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. Her body mass index (BMI) is within the normal range. She has two femoral venous access sites and is anticipated to have prolonged bedrest after the procedure. She is able to walk independently and has no history of bleeding diathesis, coagulopathy, or thrombophlebitis. She is not taking any medication that would impact her immune system or blood clotting. She is willing to participate in the trial and meet all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 14 year old male who was referred to the hospital due to chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of viral infection and was treated with antibiotics for pneumonia. His symptoms persisted and he was diagnosed with myocarditis by his pediatrician. He was referred to the hospital for further evaluation and management. He is currently not on any medication and has no known drug allergies. He lives with his parents and siblings and is in the 9th grade. He enjoys playing basketball and video games. His parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the MYKKE registry.

The patient is a 16-year-old female high school student who started smoking cigarettes with her friends a year ago. She now smokes approximately 10 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit on her own but has been unsuccessful. She reports experiencing irritability, depressed mood, and anxiety when she tries to quit smoking. She is generally in good health, weighs around 120 lbs, and has an IQ of 95. She is not currently taking any medications or substances and does not have any known cardiac, CNS, or severe psychiatric disorders. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help her quit smoking and improve her overall health.

A 34-year-old woman was diagnosed with classic paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) one year ago. She had a history of unexplained anemia and fatigue for several months, and her urine turned dark red or even black sometimes. She was diagnosed with PNH after a positive Ham's test and flow cytometry. She has been on cyclosporine A treatment for 6 months but has not shown significant improvement. Her blood counts remain low, and she still experiences frequent episodes of hemoglobinuria. She has no history of significant infections, epilepsy, or mental illness. Her liver and kidney function tests are normal. She is not pregnant or lactating. She completed levamisole study for 8 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with uveal melanoma in his left eye. He underwent enucleation surgery and was found to have a T3 tumor with chromosomal abnormalities on CGH array testing. He has no previous history of cancer and is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical or psychological conditions. He is covered by French social insurance and is able to comply with the schedule of visits and blood samples required for the study. He has signed the informed consent form for the SALOME study and is willing to participate in the study to receive a personalized risk-adjusted surveillance schedule for the early detection of liver metastases.

A 35-year-old male office worker complains of persistent pain and stiffness in his neck and shoulder on the right side. He describes the pain as a dull ache that worsens after prolonged sitting or working on the computer. He has no history of trauma or previous injuries. He has tried physiotherapy and massage therapy but has not experienced significant relief from his symptoms. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of major medical conditions. He has not used any analgesics or anti-inflammatory medication for the past 48 hours. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

Patient must be 18 years or older with a histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of cancer not amenable to curative therapy. Patients who have a diagnosis for which a PD-(L)-1 inhibitor has been approved must have previously received treatment with one of these therapies. Patients with melanoma must have histologically confirmed metastatic melanoma (ocular melanoma not included) which has progressed on or after treatment with a PD-(L)1 inhibitor. Patients should have at least one lesion accessible for intratumoral injection and biopsy. Patients must have Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status ≤2. Patients must meet the laboratory criteria set forth in the eligibility section. Women of childbearing potential and men must agree to use effective contraceptive methods from Screening throughout the study treatment period and until at least 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug. Patients must be willing and able to provide signed informed consent and comply with the study protocol. Patients must not have received prior therapy with a TLR agonist. Patients must not have received experimental vaccines or immune therapies other than PD-(L)1 or cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) inhibitors within the past 6 months prior to enrollment. Patients with known hypersensitivity to any oligodeoxynucleotide that cannot be adequately managed with appropriate prophylaxis, active autoimmune disease requiring disease-modifying therapy, or requiring concurrent systemic steroid therapy higher than physiologic dosage (>10mg/day of prednisone or equivalent) are excluded. Patients with another primary malignancy that has not been in remission for at least 3 years, active infections requiring systemic treatment, known to be hepatitis B surface antigen positive, known diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, pregnant or breastfeeding women, or with known central nervous system, meningeal, or epidural disease are excluded. Patients with impaired cardiac function or clinically significant cardiac disease or have not recovered (to baseline or Grade ≤1) from toxicity associated with prior treatment are also excluded.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who presents with a history of worsening shortness of breath and cough over the past year. She underwent a high resolution computerized tomography (HRCT) which revealed extensive pulmonary fibrosis. Pulmonary function tests showed a restrictive pattern with a diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 45% predicted. The patient denies any history of connective tissue disorders, tuberculosis, cystic fibrosis, sarcoidosis, amyloidosis or other pulmonary diseases except for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). She reports no significant past medical history, no current medications or allergies. She has never smoked and has no significant environmental exposure. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a potential new treatment for her IPF.

A 42-year-old female diagnosed with relapsed and refractory Hodgkin's lymphoma is being considered for autologous stem cell transplantation. She underwent 6 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy with partial response but developed recurrent disease after 3 months of completing the last cycle. PET-CT scan at the time of recurrence showed multiple lymphadenopathies and splenomegaly. She underwent a biopsy of a lymph node which confirmed the recurrence of Hodgkin's lymphoma. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and her creatinine clearance (Ccr) is 65 ml/min. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. Her cardiac function is normal and pulmonary function tests are satisfactory. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to practice contraception during the study period. She has no history of prior stem cell transplant, viral infections or severe complications. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

45-year-old female with a history of gallstones and scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. She has no significant medical history and her BMI is within normal limits. She has not taken any antihistamines or antiemetic drugs in the last three days and has no history of reflux, gastrointestinal disease, or epilepsy. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to the drugs in the protocol.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) with metastases to the lungs and lymph nodes. He had previously undergone treatment with cisplatin, fluorouracil, and cetuximab. His medical history was significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. The patient is a former smoker, having quit 2 years ago, with a history of 20 pack-years. He has not consumed alcohol for the past 3 years. He reports no significant family history. Physical examination revealed multiple palpable lymph nodes in the neck and axilla. A CT scan of the chest showed multiple pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases. A biopsy of one of the pulmonary nodules confirmed HNSCC. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his bone marrow and organ function are adequate for the study. He has no history of brain metastases, autoimmune or allergic disorders, or active infections. He has not undergone radiotherapy within the past 6 weeks. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial and is eligible based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 29 year-old female who is concerned about her weight and body composition. She has a BMI of 31 kg/m2 and has struggled with weight gain since college. She does not smoke and is a moderate alcohol and caffeine consumer. She does not drink tea and has not used any probiotics or antibiotics in the past 6 months. She is not on any medication except for oral contraceptives. She has no allergies to any of the food items that will be used in the study. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the long-term effects of green tea on gut flora, fat absorption, resting energy expenditure and body composition.

The patient is a 11 year old female from Europe with Turner Syndrome. She was diagnosed with Turner Syndrome during infancy due to her short stature and delayed development. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is not taking any regular medication. She has had regular endocrinology follow-ups and her thyroid function is normal. Her current height is below the 50th percentile for her age in Dutch children. She has not yet started puberty and is not experiencing any symptoms related to puberty. She is excited to participate in this clinical trial to potentially increase her height and improve her overall growth.

A 55-year-old man who has a history of smoking for at least 30 years came to the clinic with complaints of persistent coughing, shortness of breath, and wheezing. He was diagnosed with COPD at a local hospital two years ago. He has been using inhalers and corticosteroids to manage his symptoms. He is married and has two children. His weight is within normal limits, and he has no significant medical history other than COPD. He has no known allergies to food or drugs. He does not drink alcohol or smoke anymore. His last pulmonary function test showed GOLD Stage IIA COPD with an FEV1 of 63%. He has not had any exacerbations in the past month and has not been on antibiotics or steroids in the past year. CT scan of his chest showed evidence of emphysema.

The patient is a 32-year-old Danish citizen who lives in one of the 10 municipalities in the Capital Region of Denmark. The patient is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. The patient has not been pregnant in the past year and is not currently pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in the Health2016 study and is available for a health examination, including measurements of anthropometry, lifestyles, symptoms and diagnoses of diseases, blood pressure, resting heart rate, muscle strength, fitness, lung function, allergy tests, and biochemistry. The patient understands the purpose of the study and is willing to provide informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 14-day-old term infant who was born at 40 weeks gestational age. The infant was delivered via uncomplicated vaginal delivery and had no birth complications. The infant has been feeding well and is currently receiving formula feeding. The infant has no history of chronic disease, congenital malformation or feeding difficulties. The parents have given their consent to participate in the study and are willing to follow the instructions for feeding and monitoring their infant's growth and development.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She has been experiencing fatigue, pain, and a decline in her quality of life, which has led to feelings of depression and anxiety. She is currently undergoing palliative chemotherapy and has a life expectancy of at least three months. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and has at least one measurable lesion as assessed by CT-scan or MRI. She has identified an accompanying partner who is willing to participate in the Adapted Physical Activity (APA) program. She has no history of cerebrovascular accidents or myocardial infarctions in the last 6 months, but she does have controlled hypertension. She has no severe cardiovascular or respiratory diseases, cognitive or psychiatric disorders, or motor and/or sensory neuropathy. However, she does have a history of rheumatologic problems, and the study team will evaluate if they are contra-indicated for physical exercises. She has provided a signed and dated informed consent and is registered in a National Health Care System.

Maria is a 65 year old woman who has been experiencing gradual vision loss in both eyes over the past year. She has been diagnosed with age-related cataracts and has been referred to a specialist for possible surgery. She has no other ocular comorbidities, glaucoma, uveitis or any other eye-related conditions. Her vision is corrected with glasses and she has no difficulty with her activities of daily living. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoarthritis. She takes lisinopril and ibuprofen for her conditions. She has no known allergies and is a non-smoker. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/50 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Her intraocular pressure is within normal limits bilaterally. Her slit lamp examination reveals only the presence of cataracts in both eyes. She has no other ocular abnormalities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing outcomes following phacoemulsification with 1.8 and 2.2mm incisions.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic gallstone disease for several years. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of right upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea, and has been diagnosed with cholecystitis. After discussing the risks and benefits of surgery with her surgeon, she has decided to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is able to understand and follow instructions and has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer with wild-type RAS. He has already undergone surgery and chemotherapy but has not yet received EGFR-targeted therapy. He is eligible for anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody therapy as a single agent or in combination with other approved therapies or investigational agents as part of an IRB-approved clinical trial. He has archived tissue from his primary tumor that can be used for RNA-seq gene analysis. He has undergone or is scheduled to undergo CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 28 days of the investigational 11C-glutamine PET/CT and 18F-FSPG PET/CT scans. He has measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1, with at least one lesion larger than 2 cm in diameter to be measurable according to PERCIST v1.0. He weighs 180 pounds and has no disabilities that would prevent the imaging protocol from being performed. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman who is 38 weeks along is scheduled for a planned caesarean section delivery. She has a history of motion sickness and has experienced nausea and vomiting during her previous pregnancy. She has no known allergies and is in overall good health. Her BMI is 26. She is not currently taking any antiemetic medications or opioids. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological or cardiac disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of PC6 electroacupuncture in reducing the incidence of intraoperative and postoperative nausea and vomiting in caesarean section patients who undergo spinal anesthesia.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He is currently taking metformin and insulin to manage his blood sugar levels. He has a BMI of 32 and has struggled with weight loss in the past. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or comorbidities. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively. He is able to walk without any assisted device and has no major psychiatric disorder. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his diabetes and potentially lose weight.

A 63-year-old man visited his urologist for a regular check-up. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has been married for 35 years and has two children. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies. He underwent a transrectal ultrasound guided prostate biopsy 3 months ago where he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. His Gleason score is 8 and his prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 8.5 ng/mL. He has no history of hormonal management of prostate cancer, radiation therapy to the pelvic area, or any other malignancy within the last five years. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 due to mild fatigue.

A 65-year-old Hispanic male was admitted to the hospital with complaints of fatigue, shortness of breath, and anemia. His physical exam revealed pallor, and he had a moderate splenomegaly. His laboratory studies showed a hemoglobin level of 7.5 g/dL, WBC count of 3.0 × 109/L, and a platelet count of 60 × 109/L. The bone marrow biopsy showed myeloid blasts comprising 70% of nucleated cells, consistent with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The cytogenetic analysis showed a complex karyotype with multiple chromosomal abnormalities, which placed him in the non-favorable risk group for AML. The patient underwent standard chemotherapy and achieved complete remission after one cycle of consolidation chemotherapy. However, he was not eligible for allogeneic stem cell transplantation due to his age and lack of a suitable donor. Therefore, he was offered participation in a clinical trial that investigates the use of pembrolizumab to reduce the risk of relapse in AML patients who are not eligible for transplant.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing sleep problems for the past few years. He has noticed that he frequently wakes up during the night and feels tired during the day. He is a smoker and has a BMI of 28. He is not currently being treated for any medical conditions and has never been diagnosed with sleep apnea. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about his sleep problems and potential risks associated with them. He has a history of occasional alcohol use but denies any drug use. He works in the IT industry and exercises a few times a week. He has normal blood pressure and his lab results indicate no known cardiovascular risk, respiratory diseases, neoplastic pathology, or chronic inflammatory disease. He is affiliated with the French social health care system and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old woman presented to her primary care physician with complaints of abdominal pain and yellowing of the skin. She underwent imaging studies that showed a mass in the bile duct, and a biopsy confirmed cholangiocarcinoma. She is now being referred to a specialized center for further evaluation and treatment. She is otherwise healthy with a history of hypertension, and has no known allergies. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for her disease, and has no active Hepatitis B or C or history of an HIV infection.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure for the past 10 years. He has been taking furosemide regularly for the past 2 years with a daily dose of 120 mg. The patient is also taking an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker, and the doses have been stable for the past 6 months. His ejection fraction is 35%. The patient experiences frequent episodes of fluid retention and swelling in the legs. His serum creatinine is 1.5 mg/dL, and his AST and ALT levels are within normal limits. He does not have any known allergies or adverse reactions to diuretics. The patient is willing to participate in the study and sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has a BMI of 46 and has been struggling with obesity for most of her adult life. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea. She is currently being evaluated for Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass or Sleeve Gastrectomy as a treatment option for her obesity and associated comorbidities. She reports occasional alcohol use, but no history of substance abuse. She has a history of depression and anxiety, but reports that they are currently well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is not currently taking any medication that is known to affect the gut microbiome, nor has she taken any antibiotics or pre/pro biotics in the past month. She is willing and able to engage in physical activity and dietary monitoring. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with moderate asthma for the past two years. She experiences wheezing, coughing and shortness of breath during physical activity or when exposed to allergens. She has been taking inhaled corticosteroids and a rescue inhaler as needed. She lives with her parents and younger sister in a suburban area. She attends school and enjoys playing with her friends. She has not participated in any organized physical activity programs before. She has had no hospitalizations or emergency room visits for her asthma in the past year. She is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and her parents have given their consent.

A 55-year-old man presents with high levels of LDL cholesterol and diagnosed with dyslipidemia. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. He is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 28. He has no history of heart disease, stroke, or diabetes. He has been prescribed rosuvastatin as a part of his treatment plan. He has a smartphone and is comfortable using interactive smartphone applications. He is able to read, understand and write Chinese. He has not taken any statins in the last 4 weeks prior to enrollment. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. He is not allergic to rosuvastatin or any of the excipients and has no active liver disease or severe renal impairment. He is not currently pregnant or lactating and is using appropriate contraceptive measures. He has no significant medical or psychological conditions that would compromise his safety or successful participation in the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who presents to the pediatric emergency department with status epilepticus. She has a known history of epilepsy and has previously been treated with phenobarbital and valproic acid. She is currently not taking any anti-epileptic medications. The seizure began 30 minutes ago and has not stopped despite administration of lorazepam and midazolam. She has no past medical history of any other neurological or psychiatric disorders. She has no allergies to any medications. The patient's parents have given informed consent for her participation in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy of phenytoin with levetiracetam for the management of children with status epilepticus.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and mild endothelial dysfunction. She is currently taking losartan for her blood pressure and has been advised to maintain her current level of physical activity and diet throughout the study. She has abstained from coffee at least 14 hours before blood pressure measurement and physical exercise at least 4 hours before blood pressure measurement. The patient has no history of significant cardiac issues such as myocardial infarction, coronary angioplasty, or bypass grafts. She has not been diagnosed with Type I diabetes or any other unstable medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. She has not abused alcohol or drugs in the last 6 months and has not participated in any clinical research trials within the last 30 days. The patient has given voluntary, written, and informed consent to participate in the study.

13-year-old female patient with a history of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) diagnosed by a child psychiatrist a year ago. The patient is currently experiencing moderate to severe depressive symptoms including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities that she previously enjoyed. She also reports experiencing fatigue, changes in appetite, and difficulty sleeping. The patient has not responded well to previous treatment with psychotherapy and other antidepressant medications. She is currently on a break from school due to her depression and is being homeschooled. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is willing and able to participate in the study and has provided informed consent, along with her parent or guardian. The patient's CDRS-R score is greater than 40 at the screening and study day -1 (baseline) visits and her CGI-S score is greater than or equal to 4 at the screening and study day -1 (baseline) visits, meeting the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 9-year-old Hispanic boy who has been struggling with obesity for the past two years. His BMI-for-age is more than +2SD according to the WHO growth chart 2007. The patient and his parents have reported that they have tried various weight management programs, but none of them have been successful. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus, psychiatric disorder or other serious medical conditions. His medications list is only including antihistamines for seasonal allergies. The patient is known to be a picky eater and prefers high-calorie foods. He also spends most of his time playing video games and watching TV, and he has no interest in any physical activity. The patient's parents are highly motivated to find a solution for their child's obesity and are willing to participate in any program that might help their child.

A 41-year-old man who has been experiencing migraines for over a year. He has been diagnosed with chronic migraine by his neurologist. He has been experiencing migraines on average 4 or more days per month over the past 3 months. He has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational products within the last 30 days or within 5 half-lives (whichever is longer). He has not been exposed to galcanezumab or any other CGRP antibody. He has no known hypersensitivity to drugs, monoclonal antibodies or other therapeutic proteins, or to galcanezumab. He does not have a history of persistent daily headache, cluster headache or migraine subtypes including hemiplegic (sporadic or familial) migraine, ophthalmoplegic migraine, and migraine with brainstem aura (basilar-type migraine) as defined by IHS ICHD-3 beta. He is interested in participating in a safety study of galcanezumab and is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits.

A 55-year-old man with a family history of colon cancer was referred for a screening colonoscopy. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He denies any gastrointestinal symptoms, including abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation. His bowel preparation was adequate, and the procedure was unremarkable. The colonoscopist detected one small adenoma in the sigmoid colon and removed it successfully. The patient is now eligible for the clinical trial to test the impact of active nurse participation on adenoma detection during routine colonoscopy.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years. He presented with a cough that has been ongoing for the past 3 months, dyspnea, and chest pain. A chest X-ray and a CT scan revealed a mass in the right lung with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has no history of other malignancies in the past 5 years, excluding basal cell carcinoma. He has no pleural or pericardial effusion and no central nervous system involvement. The patient has a performance status of WHO 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 6 months. His hematopoietic, hepatic, and renal functions are within normal limits. He has no uncontrolled hypertension, arrhythmia, or active infections requiring IV antibiotic therapy. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for NSCLC and is not currently on any experimental medications. He is not pregnant or nursing, and he is willing to use effective contraception during the study.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman living in Tallahassee, Florida. She has a body mass index of 23.2 kg/m2 and does not take any medication that interferes with metabolism or oxygen delivery/transport. She does not smoke, vape, or chew tobacco, and she refrains from using dietary supplements throughout the entire study. She is willing to spend two overnight visits on the Florida State University campus. She has not traveled to areas that are more than 1,200 m (~4,000 feet) or have lived in areas that are more than 1,200 m for five days or more within the last two months. She has no metabolic or cardiovascular abnormalities, gastrointestinal disorders, or any condition that interferes with metabolism or oxygen delivery/transport. She has no prior diagnosis of apnea or other sleeping disorders, high-altitude pulmonary edema, high-altitude cerebral edema, anemia, or sickle cell anemia/trait. She does not have any present condition of alcoholism, anabolic steroid, or other substance abuse issues. She is not pregnant, lactating, planning to become pregnant, or have had an irregular menstrual cycle in the past six months. She has no allergies or intolerance to foods included in the standardized or ad libitum meal.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years. He is currently on medication for hypertension and his blood pressure is well controlled. He has been experiencing erectile dysfunction for the past 8 months, as defined by the NIH Consensus statement. He has been in a stable sexual relationship with his partner for over a year. He has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke or life-threatening arrhythmia within the past 6 months. He is not currently on nitrate therapy.

35-year-old female with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding for the last 6 months with no definable organic cause presents for enrollment in the clinical trial. She has had failed medical therapy for her bleeding and has a Menstrual Pictogram (MP) score of 170. She has a uterine sound measurement of 8.5 cm (external os to fundus) and is premenopausal with an FSH level of 25 IU/L. She is not pregnant, has no desire to conceive, and agrees to use a reliable form of contraception during the study. She is literate and able to provide written informed consent. She has not had any prior uterine surgery or endometrial ablation procedure. She is not currently on medications that could thin the myometrial muscle or anticoagulants. She has a normal shaped uterine cavity as confirmed by transvaginal ultrasound scan +/- hysteroscopy. She does not have an intrauterine device (IUD) or an implantable contraceptive device.

A 35-year-old female patient with a history of leiomyosarcoma presented to the clinic with symptoms of recurrent and metastatic disease. She had undergone surgical resection of the primary tumor two years ago and had undergone chemotherapy as well. However, she had developed lung metastases and was deemed unresectable. The patient had an ECOG performance status of 1 and had received two prior systemic therapies in the metastatic setting. She had a measurable disease on CT scans as defined by RECIST 1.1, and had at least one site of accessible disease for pre- and post-treatment core biopsies. The patient was willing to provide and had available archival tissue for PD-L1 testing. Her organ function was adequate, and she had a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient had not received prior systemic therapy targeting PD-1: PD-L1 axis, and did not have active autoimmune disease or a documented history of autoimmune disease or syndrome that requires systemic steroids or immunosuppressive agents. The patient was not pregnant or nursing/breastfeeding and did not have a known hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or another mAb. The patient was willing to use an effective method of birth control from providing signed consent and for 120 days after the last study drug administration. The patient was eligible for enrollment into the soft tissue sarcoma group of the SARC028 study.

A 56-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo elective cholecystectomy due to recurrent gallstone-related pain. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. She has never undergone any surgical procedures before. She has no known allergies to medications, including benzodiazepines. She has no history of liver or kidney disease. She is able to communicate effectively and has no hearing or language disorders. She does not use any sedative, analgesic or anxiolytic drugs on a long-term basis. She meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 30-year-old HIV-positive male who was diagnosed with HIV one year ago. He has been receiving anti-HIV treatment for the past 6 months, and his most recent CD4 count was 120 cells/mm3. He has a history of CD4 counts under 50 cells/mm3 in the past. He has not had MAC disease in the past and has no known allergies to azithromycin. He is currently taking anti-HIV medications and is in overall good health. He is expected to live for at least 6 months. He has no history of drug abuse, alcoholism or any other significant disease. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with it.

29 year old female who presented to the gynecology outpatient clinic with irregular menstrual cycles and hirsutism. She was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) based on the Rotterdam criteria. She is nulliparous and has no history of endocrine disorders or anabolic drug usage. She has been experiencing occasional urinary incontinence and is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effect of PCOS on pelvic floor structure and function. She will undergo perineometry and anogenital distance measurement, as well as complete the ICIQ-SF questionnaire to evaluate pelvic floor function.

50-year-old female with a history of metastatic breast cancer, confirmed by pathological analysis, is being evaluated for a clinical trial. The patient has previously been treated with trastuzumab and chemotherapy four weeks ago. Immunohistochemical analysis of HER-2/neu expression on paraffin-embedded specimens was positive, with 3+ indicating the strongest positivity. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 70%. The patient has never been treated with vinorelbine before. The patient has adequate hepatic, renal, and hematologic function. Cardiac function is adequate, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55% documented by echocardiogram. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any known hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived proteins, filgrastim, or any component of the product. The patient has given written informed consent indicating they are aware of the investigational nature of this treatment, as well as the risks and benefits of this protocol.

A 16-year-old female adolescent diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and experiencing symptoms such as anhedonia, lack of motivation, and feelings of sadness and hopelessness. The participant must be fluent in English and have a personal cell phone for Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA). The participant must be right-handed and in the follicular phase of their menstrual cycle during the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study session. The participant must not have a history of head trauma with loss of consciousness, seizure disorder, serious or unstable medical illness, history of stimulant use or use of dopaminergic drugs, history of electroconvulsive therapy, or be pregnant. An additional exclusion criterion for the MDD sample is major depressive disorder diagnosis secondary to another disorder. The participant will need to attend four sessions, including diagnostic interviews, assessments, and questionnaires, and complete surveys on their cell phone during the week following each session. The second session will include an fMRI brain scan at the McLean Hospital Imaging Center.

This is a 68-year-old female who has noticed a decline in her hearing ability over the past year. She has not used hearing aids before and is interested in exploring her options. She speaks English as her primary language and has no history of middle-ear conductive pathology, dementia, Parkinson's disease, or any other neurological disorders. She is able to read 18-point font without difficulty. She is willing to purchase hearing aids and is open to participating in a clinical trial to compare different hearing-aid delivery models.

The patient is a 7-month-old infant who lives in an urban slum area in Vellore, south India. The infant was born full term with a birth weight of 3 kg and has been exclusively breastfed for the first 6 months of life. The infant has not had any history of significant illness or hospitalizations, and has been meeting all developmental milestones appropriately. The family is willing to participate in a clinical trial to prevent rotavirus gastroenteritis using a food supplement. They understand the study procedures and are available for a follow-up period of one year. The infant does not have any atopic conditions or gross congenital anomalies, and has no serological evidence of HIV infection.

A 32 year old woman presents with persistent cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats for the past 4 weeks. She has no history of tuberculosis and has not been vaccinated against tuberculosis. She denies any recent travel or exposure to someone with tuberculosis. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion over the right lower lung field. Chest x-ray shows consolidation in the right lower lobe. Sputum smear microscopy for acid-fast bacilli was positive. She does not have any other serious health problems.

12-year-old male patient with a history of burn injury sustained from a house fire 2 months ago. The patient is currently undergoing burn rehabilitation and is scheduled for an elective surgical procedure. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has been complaining of fatigue during the day, affecting his ability to participate in rehabilitation activities. The patient has no history of anoxic brain injury, head injury within the last year, pre-existing seizure disorder, pre-existing neurological disorder, pre-existing blindness, known hypersensitivity to melatonin, anticoagulant use or aspirin therapy, antihypertensive medication use, diabetes mellitus or other endocrine disorders, autoimmune disorders, schizophrenia, or intellectual disability. The patient has access to the internet and is able to follow directions. The patient and their parents have provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy from a rural area in Ethiopia. He presents with fever, chills, headache, and body aches for the past two days. His axillary temperature is 38.5°C. He lives with his parents and five siblings in a small house with no access to clean water. He attends school but has missed several days due to his illness. He has no known medical history or allergies. He weighs 25 kg and has no signs of severe malnutrition. His physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. A blood smear confirms a diagnosis of P. falciparum with a parasitemia of 8,000 asexual forms/ μl. The patient and his caregiver agree to participate in the study and the patient is considered eligible for enrollment.

A 60-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer is scheduled to start pelvic radiation therapy in the next 2 months. He has no history of allergies, dietary intolerances, or other concurrent medical conditions that would preclude study compliance. He has a performance status of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He is not receiving any concurrent chemotherapy but is undergoing hormone therapy. He has not had any previous colectomy, inflammatory bowel disease, or enteric support, and is not taking any glutamine or fiber supplements. He is willing to participate in a randomized clinical trial to compare a low-residue diet with no dietary intervention to treat diarrhea caused by radiation therapy. He will be interviewed to obtain a baseline grade of diarrhea, dietary history, and Fecal Incontinence Quality of Life (FI-QOL), and will be monitored weekly for up to 6 weeks to monitor dietary intake, bowel symptoms, diarrhea events, FI-QOL, and changes in CTC scores.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male who is fluent in German. He has a BMI of 25, with a body weight of 85 kg. His vital signs are normal, with a pulse rate of 75 bpm, systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg, and diastolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg. He has no history of chronic viral infections, systemic illness, or any relevant medical conditions. He does not smoke or use any nicotine-containing products and has not consumed alcohol or illicit drugs in the past three months. He has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medications or herbal supplements in the past 14 days. He has not donated blood or experienced significant blood loss in the past 30 days. He is willing to comply with the study's protocol requirements and agrees not to donate blood until one month after receiving the study drug. He is willing to forgo sunbathing and strenuous exercise during the study period. He has no known allergies to any of the study drug's excipients. He is a potential candidate for the clinical trial.

There is no specific patient involved in this clinical trial as it is a study to evaluate the performance of a diagnostic test using archived confirmed ZIKV positive and confirmed ZIKV negative human serum samples from various geographical locations and ages. The study will include both retrospective (archived) and prospective human serum samples, and will exclude samples that are not de-identified.

A 62-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) three years ago. He received six cycles of Fludarabine, Cyclophosphamide, and Rituximab (FCR) chemotherapy, which resulted in a complete response. However, his CLL relapsed six months ago. He is currently asymptomatic except for mild fatigue. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled on medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He lives with his wife and has two grown-up children. He enjoys reading and going for walks. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. His blood counts are as follows: WBC 18.5 x 10^9/L, Hb 11.5 g/dL, and platelets 150 x 10^9/L. His renal and liver function tests are within normal limits. He has not received any prior treatments with bendamustine or GA101. He is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the study protocol procedures.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and limited mobility in his right shoulder for the past year. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis at a nearby hospital and was referred to this clinical trial for possible treatment options. He reports that the pain is always present and worsens with movement, especially when he tries to lift things. He has been taking over-the-counter pain medications, but they provide only temporary relief. He has no history of shoulder surgery or trauma. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His family history is negative for shoulder problems. He has no neurologic disorders and is able to follow directions. His X-rays show moderate joint destruction and some bone loss in the right shoulder. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is willing to comply with all requirements. His HAM-D score is 2.

The patient is a 42-year-old asymptomatic individual who has not experienced any of the CDC COVID-19 symptoms listed in the exclusion criteria. They are able to read and write English fluently and are willing to try the rapid COVID-19 test and self-collect a nasal swab sample in both nostrils. The patient has not suffered any nasal trauma such as a nosebleed and has not received a nasal rinse/wash/aspirates in the past 12 hours. They are interested in participating in the study to help evaluate the performance of the Lucira COVID-19 All-In-One Test Kit and are available to attend one study visit for collection of nasal swabs at a community-based location with trained medical staff oversight.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer three years ago. Since the diagnosis, he has been undergoing chemotherapy and radiation treatments. Despite the treatments, he still experiences significant symptoms such as pain, fatigue, and anxiety. He has been feeling isolated and helpless since his diagnosis, and he wants to find ways to cope with his symptoms and improve his quality of life. He has a supportive spouse and children who are helping him manage his illness, and he is willing to participate in a telephone-based mindfulness-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy intervention to learn new coping skills. He is fluent in English, has no visual or hearing impairments, and is physically able to engage in the telephone sessions and study materials. He is willing to commit to 4 weekly 50-minute telephone sessions with a study therapist and practice skills learned in session at home. He hopes that this study will help him manage his symptoms and improve his overall well-being.

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic with a BMI of 31. She was referred by her primary care physician for a weight loss program. She was diagnosed with pre-diabetes and she is not taking any medication at the moment. She is married with two young children and works as an accountant. She complains of feeling tired and stressed most of the time. She speaks fluent Hebrew and is interested in participating in a health coaching program to improve her lifestyle. She has no significant medical history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. Her blood pressure was 130/86 and her fasting glucose was 110 in the latest lab study. She is motivated to attend the sessions and make lifestyle changes.

A 16-year-old teenage boy diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder is eligible for participation in this clinical trial. The boy has normal intellectual abilities (Full-scale IQ ≥ 70) and has not experienced seizures within the last year. He has no metal implants in his head and is not contraindicated for fMRI. The boy struggles with making and keeping friends and has expressed a desire to improve his social skills. He is willing to participate in a 14-week training program that involves interacting in small groups and learning social skills. The boy is also willing to receive either active brain stimulation or non-active stimulation (placebo) during the program. He understands that before and after the training, MRI scans will be taken to see whether the active brain stimulation made a difference in brain activation.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. She has been on continuous antiretroviral therapy for more than 48 weeks and has a CD4+ cell count of 300/mm3. Her most recent HIV-1 RNA test was negative. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has a history of high triglycerides and low HDL-C levels, with an HDL-C level of 38 mg/dL. She has a history of smoking, but quit 3 years ago. She does not have a history of diabetes, cancer, or other serious illnesses. She is not currently taking any lipid-lowering drugs or antihypertensives. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use reliable contraception while receiving study drug and for 6 weeks after stopping study drug, as she is a woman of reproductive potential. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with an ascending aorta aneurysm and is scheduled for surgical correction. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but has been on medication to control these conditions for the past 5 years. He reports occasional chest discomfort and shortness of breath with exertion. He is a non-smoker and does not have any family history of CAD. He is willing to participate in the study and has no known allergy to contrast material. He has not had any previous coronary angiogram or CT-AS done in another hospital. He has no known arrhythmia and the time between the two exams will be less than 6 months.

46-year-old male recently hospitalized for acute coronary syndrome. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. The patient has been on moderate-intensity statin therapy for the past four weeks, but his LDL-C levels have remained above 90 mg/dL. The patient has no known allergies to the medications required for this study and is able to understand the research requirements and sign informed consent. The patient has not been treated with evolocumab or other PCSK9 inhibitors in the past. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate is above 30 ml/min/1.73m² and the patient does not have active liver disease or liver dysfunction. The patient is not currently receiving systemic steroid or cyclosporine treatment and has no known infections, hemorrhages, or metabolic disorders. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to assess the effects of evolocumab added to moderate-intensity statin therapy on LDL-C lowering and cardiovascular adverse events.

The patient is a 12-year-old female who was diagnosed with Friedreich's Ataxia (FA) 2 years ago. She experiences difficulty with walking, coordination and balance, and has had a recent increase in the frequency and severity of falls. She also has mild dysarthria and complains of occasional tingling in her feet. She is currently on a treatment regimen consisting of physical therapy and occupational therapy. She has no history of diabetes or cardiomyopathy. She lives with her parents and attends school regularly. Her parents have provided consent for her participation in this clinical trial. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical examination is notable for mild pes cavus (high arches) and mild scoliosis. Her family history is negative for FA, and she has no known allergies or medical conditions.

A 42-year-old male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in the MRI Assessing Clinical Usability of STrategically Acquired Gradient Echo on Human Participants clinical trial. He is literate in English and has no contraindications to MR. He is not claustrophobic and has not had any major surgery in the past eight weeks or scheduled surgery within the next 30 days. He does not have chronic back pain or a history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has a BMI of 25 and weighs 190 lbs. He is not a direct employee or student of the PI and does not belong to any vulnerable group.

A 65-year-old man with a history of smoking for 40 years has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He was hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation 2 months ago and was prescribed supplemental oxygen. He has been using oxygen at home since then. His resting saturation on room air is 92%. He is currently taking inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids for his COPD. He reports shortness of breath with exertion and difficulty walking for more than a few minutes. He has not experienced any hospitalization or exacerbation of COPD within the last 30 days. He is willing to participate in a virtual video visit for follow-up assessments and to stop oxygen if randomized to the intervention group. He speaks and understands English and is able to provide written informed consent. He does not have any cognitive issues that would preclude participation.

52-year-old male with a long-standing history of difficulty swallowing, regurgitation of food, and occasional chest pain. He was initially diagnosed with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and was treated with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) for several years with no improvement. He recently underwent an esophageal manometry study which was consistent with the diagnosis of achalasia. His symptoms have been progressively worsening and he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand and help direct the treatment for patients with achalasia. He has no previous history of pneumatic dilation, Heller myotomy, or botulinum toxin injection to the distal esophagus. He has no medical conditions that preclude safe performance of barostat. He is able to read and comprehend English.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) three years ago. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy but has had multiple relapses and is currently in refractory state. He is experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and recurrent infections. His Karnofsky Performance Status is 60%. He has not received any biologic antineoplastic agents for the past seven days and has not received any treatment for graft-versus-host disease for the past 30 days. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. He has a history of excised and cured non-melanoma skin cancer. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his treatment outcome.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently 30 weeks pregnant with twins. Her pregnancy has been complicated by preterm labor, and she is at risk for preterm birth. She has not received any prior doses of antenatal corticosteroids but has received the first dose of 12 mg intramuscular betamethasone within the past 24 hours. She has no contraindications to receiving corticosteroids, and all fetuses are alive and without compromise as per ultrasound or fetal heart monitor. She is capable of giving informed, written consent in English. She has no history of chronic corticosteroid use due to medical conditions and is not pregnant with twins that are monoamniotic/monochorionic (Mono/Mono).

This trial is not suited for any particular patient as it is designed for healthy volunteers without any significant medical history or current medical conditions. Participants in this trial must have a BMI between 17.5 to 30.5 kg/m2 and a total body weight of over 50 kg. They should not have any history or evidence of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease, including clinically significant drug allergies. This is a single-dose study, and the purpose is to evaluate the safety and tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of a new drug. Therefore, this trial does not require patients with any specific condition.

A 45-year old woman was diagnosed with lichen planus three years ago. She has been experiencing intense itching, pain and discomfort on her skin and mucosal surfaces. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with levothyroxine. She is a non-smoker and doesn't use any illicit drugs. She is married and has two children. The patient has tried several treatments for her lichen planus, including topical corticosteroids and oral antihistamines, but has not had significant relief from her symptoms. She has been advised to use systemic therapy due to the severity of her symptoms but has been hesitant due to concerns over potential side effects. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer new treatment options with fewer side effects. She is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not currently using any topical cyclosporine, tacrolimus or pimecrolimus. She has a baseline laboratory results within the required parameters and has tested negative for HIV and hepatitis C. She is not pregnant or lactating and is practicing successful contraception. She has no other significant medical conditions that may interfere with the study.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with end-stage ankle arthritis and has been experiencing joint pain, tenderness, and limitation of movement for the past two years. He is ambulatory, speaks English and is cognitively intact. He has elected to undergo surgical correction for end-stage ankle arthritis, and has chosen to participate in this clinical trial at the VA Puget Sound Health Care System in Seattle, WA. He has no history of rheumatoid arthritis or any other systemic arthritis, and does not have any other diseased lower extremity joints or traumatic lower extremity injury that grossly inhibits normal gait. The patient is willing to undergo Musculoskeletal Function Assessment (MFA), SF-36 general health survey, and biomechanical domain assessment through instrumented gait analysis. The patient is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the surgery, as well as the clinical trial, and has given informed consent to participate.

Patient is a 28-year-old healthy male from the United States who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has a BMI of 23 and has no significant medical history or drug allergies. He does not smoke, drink alcohol excessively or consume tobacco products. At the screening visit, his laboratory tests, vital signs, and medical history are unremarkable. He understands and speaks English fluently and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form and protocol.

A 65-year-old man was admitted to Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen University Hospital with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He was hospitalized due to shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and COPD. He is a former smoker, with a 20 pack-year history. On admission, his vital signs were stable, with a blood pressure of 140/85 mmHg, heart rate of 95 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. The patient received a blood transfusion during hospitalization for severe anemia due to gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient's weight is 85 kg, and his height is 175 cm. The patient has no known drug allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and tremor came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for deep brain stimulation (DBS). He has been on medication for the past 5 years but is experiencing side effects and is looking for an alternative treatment. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders other than Parkinson's. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has never undergone DBS surgery before and is open to trying the "asleep DBS" technique under general anesthesia without the use of microelectrode recordings (MER) with the portable head CT scanner. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that could affect the surgery.

65 F with a h/o hypertension, coronary artery disease, and COPD who presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and cough productive of white sputum. She was found to have bilateral infiltrates on chest x-ray and was diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The patient was subsequently intubated and started on mechanical ventilation. She remained on mechanical ventilation for 48 hours with a PEEP of 5 cm H2O. Repeat arterial blood gas showed persistent hypoxemia with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 150. The patient was deemed eligible for the study and will undergo evaluation with different levels of PEEP to determine its effect on gas exchange and dead space. The patient remains hemodynamically stable and has no evidence of barotrauma.
