Patient is a 65-year-old female with a history of uncomplicated phacoemulsification cataract extraction with implantation of posterior chamber intraocular lens (IOL/PC). She has no history of glaucoma or other ocular diseases. She is scheduled to undergo neodymium: yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Nd:YAG) laser posterior capsulotomy due to posterior capsule opacification (PCO). She is not currently taking any medications known to affect intraocular pressure (IOP), and has no known allergies or contraindications to the medications being tested. Her baseline IOP is within normal limits. She has no history of respiratory or cardiovascular disease, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it does not involve human participants. The study will use pig jaws as the samples to measure soft tissue thickness by CBCT. The eligibility criteria are related to the condition of the pig jaws and teeth, rather than the characteristics of human patients.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of breast cancer. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She reports experiencing feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and anxiety over the past few weeks. She rates her depression and anxiety symptoms as 7 out of 10 on a self-reported scale. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any antidepressant medication. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent. Her serum bilirubin, creatinine, AST, and ALT levels are all within normal limits. She is expected to live for greater than 6 months. She has no history of liver or allogenic stem cell transplant and does not have any known cognitive or psychological impairments other than her current depressive and anxiety symptoms.

This is a 26 year-old female who recently underwent dental extraction of three third molars due to impaction. She is experiencing moderate to severe pain and is seeking relief. She does not have any known allergies to acetaminophen or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and is able to swallow whole large tablets or capsules. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and has a BMI within the range of 18 to 30.

A 67-year-old male patient was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of uncontrolled diabetes and pressure ulcers on his left hip and sacrum. He has been bedridden for the past month due to a fracture in his left femur. His blood glucose levels are frequently above normal range and he has been prescribed insulin. His medical history is significant for hypertension and coronary artery disease. He is not on any blood thinners or antiplatelet medications. He has no known allergies to medications or food. He has not received any prior treatment for pressure ulcers. The ulcers are rated as stage II and have an area of approximately 15cm2. He has no discomfort during treatment and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of persistent anal pain and bleeding for the past 3 months. The pain is described as sharp and occurs during bowel movements, and the bleeding is associated with the pain. He has noticed that the pain is worse when he is constipated. He denies any history of inflammatory bowel disease, previous anal surgery, or any other anorectal disease. He has not used any topical agents for the treatment of his symptoms. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Physical exam reveals an anal fissure at the posterior midline with no other remarkable findings. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial and gives his consent for randomization to either group I or group II.

A 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Stage 2 breast cancer 3 years ago is seeking Reach to Recovery services from the American Cancer Society. She is currently sedentary and does not meet the recommendations for moderate-intensity physical activity. She is able to walk unassisted and has access to a telephone. She does not have any medical or psychiatric problems that may interfere with protocol adherence. She is fluent in English and is willing to provide consent for medical chart review to extract disease and treatment variables. She will obtain medical clearance from her physician before enrolling in the trial.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) with metastasis to the liver, bones, and brain. The patient has tried standard therapy but has not responded to treatment. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has not received any prior therapy with an anti-Programmed cell death protein (PD)-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, anti-Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) agents, or IDO1 inhibitor. The patient is not currently participating in another study with an investigational compound or device within 4 weeks, or 5 times half-life of the investigational compound, whichever is longer, of initial dosing on this study. The patient has at least one measurable lesion by computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging per Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. The patient has provided tissue for programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1)/ Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) expression evaluation from an archival tissue sample or newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of a tumor lesion not previously irradiated. The patient is not expected to require any other form of systemic or localized anti-neoplastic therapy while on this study. The patient does not have active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis. The patient does not have symptomatic ascites or pleural effusion. The patient does not have an active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment. The patient is not receiving systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 1 week prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient does not have an active infection requiring systemic therapy. The patient does not have history of (non-infectious) pneumonitis that required systemic steroids or current pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach after experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss for several months. She underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of gastric cancer. The tumor was deemed surgically resectable and the patient was evaluated for metastases. Pathological examination revealed peritoneal metastases, but no distant metastases were detected. The patient has a WHO performance status of 1 and an ASA score of 2. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant. She has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to undergo cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy with cisplatin. The patient has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 42 year old male who was admitted to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and fever. He was diagnosed with fecal peritonitis and underwent an emergency laparotomy. During the surgery, it was found that there was a perforation in the large intestine which was causing the peritonitis. The surgeon performed a damaged control surgery, and placed a urine bag temporarily over the abdomen to allow for a second relook laparotomy after 24-48 hours. The patient was managed in the ICU, and after the second relook laparotomy, the abdomen was washed with normal saline and any missed pathology was identified and controlled. The patient required multiple washouts and dressing, and the abdominal content was covered again with the urine bag. The patient was discharged after complete recovery with the final closure of the abdominal wall using deep tension suture. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial as he was diagnosed with fecal peritonitis and required a relook laparotomy.

55-year-old female diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma in partial remission after two prior chemotherapy regimens. She has no 6/6 or 5/6 HLA-matched related, 10/10 matched unrelated donor, or unrelated donor available within the time frame necessary to perform a potentially curative stem cell transplant. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no cardiac, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, or neurologic disease. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no active infections or HIV antibody. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial involving unrelated cord blood transplantation using tacrolimus and sirolimus.

A 28-year-old female visits the clinic for a routine dental check-up. She reports good oral hygiene practices and has no known history of periodontal disease or any other systemic diseases. She does not smoke and has not taken antibiotics or anti-inflammatory drugs in the past three months. Upon examination, her gingival index score is ≤1, and there are no probing depths over 3mm or approximal attachment loss greater than 2mm. She has no untreated caries lesions or local retention factors and does not suffer from allergies. The patient has not previously taken any probiotic supplements in her diet. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the effects of probiotic yogurt on the development of gingival inflammation.

A 25-year-old African American male presents with a history of sickle cell disease (SCD) and has been receiving treatment at Duke University Medical Center's Day Hospital for acute painful episodes for the past year. He reports having frequent painful episodes that have disrupted his daily activities and caused him to miss work. Despite taking pain medications as prescribed, he has not been able to manage his symptoms effectively. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his quality of life. He owns a smartphone and is familiar with using mobile applications. He is currently not receiving chronic RBC transfusions and has had less than 20 acute care visits within the past year. He is willing to give informed consent and comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with twins. She is in her 20th week of pregnancy and is experiencing occasional contractions. She has a history of preterm delivery in a previous pregnancy. The twins are dichorionic and are developing normally with no major malformations or complications. The patient has not had a cerclage placed and her cervix length is within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent preterm delivery and is willing to use vaginal progesterone gel.

The patient is a 50 year old man admitted to the hospital for chest pain and shortness of breath. Medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. The patient has been placed on telemetry for continuous ECG monitoring due to the high risk of sudden cardiac arrest. The physician has determined that the patient is eligible for the Hospital Wearable Defibrillator Inpatient Study, as they are at risk of sudden cardiac arrest during the hospitalization period. The patient is able to interact with and wear the device, and has no active implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or other medical conditions that would prevent participation in the study. The patient has provided consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced esophageal cancer. A biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. The patient has no history of prior chemotherapy, thoracic radiotherapy or prior surgical resection for an esophageal tumor. The patient is in generally good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has no known distant metastases and is deemed eligible for potentially curative treatment. The patient has adequate organ function and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no prior history of psychiatric or addictive disorders, and is not expecting to conceive or father children.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. After undergoing a series of tests, including an electrocardiogram and echocardiogram, she has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and requires a percutaneous cardiovascular procedure. She has no significant medical history and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials.

46 y/o male with a history of hypertension and no previous antihypertensive medication. BP at recent office visits has been ranging from 150-170/90-100 mmHg. The patient has a family history of hypertension and no significant past medical history. The patient has no history of cardiovascular conditions, diabetes, or other significant medical conditions. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

No patient description is needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on testing the effectiveness of an antimicrobial agent on hospital scrubs worn by nurses during patient care. It does not involve direct patient participation.

65-year-old male with a history of stage IV prostate cancer with radiographic evidence of regional or distant metastases. He has undergone standard hormonal therapy and docetaxel-containing chemotherapy, but his disease has progressed, as evidenced by rising PSA levels and new lesions. He has not undergone orchiectomy and his serum testosterone level is less than 50 ng/dL. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. Laboratory studies show an absolute neutrophil count of 2,200/mm³, a platelet count of 150,000/mm³, a creatinine level of 1.1 times the upper limit of normal, a bilirubin level of 1.2 times the upper limit of normal, and AST and ALT levels of 1.5 times the upper limit of normal. He has no known or suspected brain metastases and no significant cardiovascular illness. He has not

A 45-year-old male with a history of non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis presents with an exacerbation of symptoms including increased sputum production and shortness of breath. He reports a productive cough with yellow-green sputum and has a fever of 101°F. His medical history is significant for recurrent bronchitis and pneumonia. He is a non-smoker and works as a teacher. He has not been hospitalized for his respiratory condition in the past year. Sputum culture shows the presence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. He does not have any medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new drug. He has no significant medical history, and his weight is 70kg with a BMI of 23. He is a non-smoker, and he does not drink alcohol frequently. The patient has not taken any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, herbal supplements, or nutritional supplements within the past two weeks. He has no history of drug abuse or continuous alcohol intake exceeding 21 units/week. The patient expresses his consent to participate in the trial and is willing to follow the diet restrictions (grapefruit, caffeine) and use contraceptive measures that are allowed for the clinical trial. Based on the eligibility criteria, the patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. The patient is deemed eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 25-year-old female college student who is interested in receiving fillers for her lips. She is in good health and has never had any cosmetic procedures before. She has no medical history of note and is not currently taking any medications. She is aware of the risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to participate in the study. She has no known hypersensitivity to hyaluronic acid.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no history of major medical conditions. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. He is a non-smoker and does not use any drugs or alcohol. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and weighs 70 kg. He has no known allergies to any medications or food. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 3 months. He is willing to comply with the study requirements, including the use of an effective form of contraception for the duration of the study. He does not use any prescription medications, proton pump inhibitors, or H2-receptor antagonists. He has not received any vaccinations or immunizations in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to consume high-fat meals during the study. He is not a vegetarian and is able to consume all types of food. He is not currently pregnant or nursing.

A 64-year-old male patient presents with a history of COPD and a smoking history of 30 pack-years. He has been using inhalers as the mainstay of his COPD treatment for the past year. He complains of persistent coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. His post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio is 0.62 and FEV1 is 55% of predicted normal value. He is not currently taking any medication for HIV, chronic hepatitis B or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, theophylline, warfarin, or any other xanthine medication. He has not had an acute exacerbation of COPD within the previous 60 days or during the washout period of the study. He has no history of organ transplant, cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the previous 3 months, or known neuromuscular disorder from clinical history (e.g. myasthenia gravis, Parkinson's disease). He has no known significant renal, hepatic, or hematological impairment. He is willing and able to comply with all study visits and procedures. He is eligible to participate in this study.

The patient is a premature infant born at 35 weeks of gestation at Soroka University Medical Center. The infant does not have any chromosomal, neurological, muscular, cardiac or respiratory anomalies that would affect the absorption and/or metabolism of Vitamin D. The infant's family has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that aims to assess the effect of Vitamin D administration on respiratory morbidity in premature infants. The infant will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group, which will receive 800 IU of Vitamin D once daily, or the control group, which will receive 400 IU of Vitamin D once daily. The infant will be followed up for one year after randomization to assess serum Vitamin D levels and respiratory morbidity. The family is insured by "Clalit" HMO.

This is a 45 year-old female who was diagnosed with RA 5 years ago. She has been on methotrexate for the past 3 years and has been tolerating it well. She participated in Study MRA213JP and received MRA for her RA. She did not experience any safety concerns during the study and wishes to continue treatment with MRA. She has not been administered drugs such as infliximab, etanercept, and leflunomide within the past 12 weeks and has not undergone any surgical interventions in the past 4 weeks. She is available for follow-up visits and is willing to participate in the long-term safety and efficacy study of MRA for RA.

A 17-year-old female who has been smoking 8-10 cigarettes a day for the past year is interested in quitting smoking. She reports trying to quit on her own several times, but has been unsuccessful. She has a family history of smoking and a few close friends who also smoke. She reports feeling anxious and depressed at times but has never sought professional treatment for these symptoms. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. She is fluent in English and has the support of her parents who are willing to participate in the intervention. She is willing to try nicotine replacement therapy if offered as an option. She lives within an hour of the study site and is able to attend all study assessments and participate in the intervention. She is able to provide informed assent and her parents are willing to provide informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with colon cancer during a routine colonoscopy. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. The biopsy showed adenocarcinoma of the descending colon. He is scheduled for elective surgical resection of the colon. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness over the left lower quadrant. His laboratory tests are within normal limits. He has no known allergies to medications, including iodine. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) for the past two years. Despite being on stable doses of medication for UC for the preceding three months, he is still experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea and rectal bleeding. His Mayo score is 8 and sigmoidoscopy subscore is 3. He has not received antibiotic therapy in the last three months nor probiotic or prebiotic therapy in the last month. He has no history of Crohn's disease or indeterminate colitis. He is not pregnant nor lactating. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and adhere to the protocol for six months.

A 42-year-old male with a history of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis that has been unresponsive to previous treatments such as PUVA, methotrexate, and retinoids. The patient has a normal organ and marrow function and is HIV negative. The patient is currently not on any systemic, intralesional, or phototherapy treatment for psoriasis and has not used cyclosporine or any other immunosuppressive medication within the past 6 months. The patient is willing to be followed and monitored regularly on a weekly basis for up to 30 weeks and is able to provide informed consent. The patient is not currently pregnant and agrees to use appropriate contraception during the study.

A 29-year-old woman has been struggling with binge eating for the past 5 years. She has been diagnosed with binge eating disorder by a mental health professional and is currently receiving psychological treatment. She reports that the urge to eat large amounts of food comes unexpectedly and results in feelings of guilt, shame, and anxiety. She has experienced weight fluctuations and feels that her eating disorder has a negative impact on her overall quality of life. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to explore the feasibility of a computerised training to reduce her approach to high energy-dense foods. The study will involve completing a food-specific go/no-go task using a mobile app called FoodT. She is willing to complete the training for 4 weeks and complete questionnaires at baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including being fluent in English and having a BMI ≥ 18.5. She does not have a diagnosis of psychosis, visual impairment that cannot be corrected by glasses or lenses, cognitive or neurological impairment, or drug or alcohol abuse.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is focused on investigating the learning curve of novice practitioners in visual estimation of LV ejection fraction through echocardiographic videos. The study is being conducted at the academic emergency department of a tertiary urban hospital and is recruiting EM residents who have no prior experience of echocardiography.

An 80-year-old woman is admitted to the medical ward with pneumonia. She requires assistance with mobility due to her recent history of falls and weakness. She is expected to stay in the hospital for at least three days and is planned for discharge home. The patient is fluent in English and can follow commands. She has no contraindications to exercise and can exercise with the assistance of one person. The patient is not in need of active palliative care and does not require full isolation for a contagious infection.

A 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of probable ALS experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion, especially while lying down or sleeping. He has been using BiPAP for the past 3 months, but he struggles to tolerate the expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) setting of 4 cm H2O. He reports that he feels like he is suffocating when the EPAP is turned on, and he frequently removes the mask during the night. He is married and lives with his wife. He has two adult children. He is retired and spends his time reading, watching movies, and spending time with his family. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has a history of snoring but has not been formally diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea. His forced vital capacity (FVC) is 46% predicted, and his maximal inspiratory force is 55 cm/H2O. His transition dyspnea index (TDI) score is 6, and his EuroQol Visual analogue scale(VAS) score is 60.

A 38-year-old woman was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) about 3 years ago. She is currently experiencing fatigue that affects her daily activities and quality of life. She has tried various treatments, including medication and lifestyle changes, but the fatigue persists. She is motivated to participate in a clinical trial that may help alleviate her fatigue. She is not currently practicing high-intensity training but is willing to participate in supervised training twice a week. She speaks fluent Swedish and is able to understand and communicate effectively. She is otherwise in good health and has no other medical conditions that may interfere with the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. He has bidimensionally measurable disease but no clinical evidence of CNS metastases. His performance status is Karnofsky 80% and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 6 months. His hematopoietic profile shows hemoglobin of 12.0 g/dL, WBC of 5,000/mm3, and platelet count of 150,000/mm3. His hepatic profile shows normal PTT and bilirubin level of 0.8 times the upper limit of normal. His renal function is normal with a creatinine level of 1.2 times the upper limit of normal. He has no abnormal cardiac function by resting ECG and his pulmonary function tests show FEV and FVC at least 80% predicted and SaO2 of 95% by pulse oximetry. He has no other concurrent ongoing active malignancy and no serious recent nonmalignant medical complication. He has no organ grafts or prior documented asthma or systemic allergic reaction within the past 5 years. He has not had a history of seizures, CNS disorders, or psychiatric disability that would preclude study compliance. He has no active peptic or esophageal ulcer disease and no prior peptic or esophageal ulcer disease with a history of bleeding. He has not received any immunotherapy or chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks. He is not currently on any systemic antimalignancy therapy and has no concurrent beta blockers or clonidine.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman diagnosed with Williams syndrome (WS) at the age of 5. Her parents are available to participate in the study and provide medical information. She has not undergone any weight loss surgery or liposuction. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of WS and its impact on metabolic and bone abnormalities. She is currently not pregnant, and she does not have any other secondary causes of obesity or abnormal fat distribution. She is able to travel to Massachusetts General Hospital for in-person participation in the study.

Pt is a 38yo M with a history of bipolar depression for the past 10 years. He has been on various antidepressants and mood stabilizers, but continues to experience moderate to severe depressive symptoms with a HAM-D score of 20. Pt has no history of substance dependence or physical illnesses that could interfere with the study. He has not had any intracranial surgeries or metal foreign bodies. Pt is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore potential alternative treatments for his depression.

The patient is a 55-year-old American man who was diagnosed with Type II diabetes five years ago. He has been managing his condition with metformin and lifestyle modifications. His most recent HbA1c was 7.5%. His BMI is 30 kg/m² and his body weight is 90 kg. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications other than metformin. His family history is positive for diabetes in both parents. The patient has normal lab test results for serum magnesium, potassium levels, and lactate dehydrogenase, CK values. His estimated glomerular filtration rate is 65 mL/min/1.73 m². The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 54-year-old woman was admitted to the intensive care unit with severe respiratory distress. She had a history of hypertension and was a smoker for 20 years, but quit 5 years ago. She had been experiencing cough, fever, and shortness of breath for the past 10 days. Her symptoms worsened rapidly, and she was referred to the hospital. A nasopharyngeal swab test was performed, and the result was positive for SARS-CoV2. Upon admission to the ICU, her oxygen saturation level was 80% on room air, and she required immediate intubation and mechanical ventilation. She was started on a regimen of antivirals and steroids. Her condition remained critical, and she required a prolonged stay in the ICU. This patient meets the inclusion criteria for the French Single Centre Experience of Critically Ill Patients With Covid 19 clinical trial.

A 55-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease was referred for peritoneal dialysis (PD) due to a failed kidney transplant. She has been receiving PD for the past 6 months and has been experiencing secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) with an intact PTH level of 450 pg/mL. Despite receiving vitamin D and phosphate binders, her corrected calcium level is 9.5 mg/dL. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is not pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. She has not undergone parathyroidectomy in the past 3 months and has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 30 days. She has not received cinacalcet therapy previously. She is willing to participate in a study that compares the efficacy of a cinacalcet-based regimen with unrestricted conventional care for achieving the stringent National Kidney Foundation Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative targets for dialysis patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty with her vision for the past few months. She reports difficulty seeing objects on her left side, and has noticed a gradual decrease in her visual acuity in her left eye. She has no history of glaucoma or optic nerve anomalies. Her visual acuity is measured at 20/20 in both eyes. Her refractive error is within the study criteria. She has a temporal field defect in her left eye. The patient is well-nourished, well-dressed, and appears alert and cooperative. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the detection and management of her condition.

56 yo male veteran with a clinical diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with a BMI of 30.2 kg/m2 and an HbA1c of 8.5%. The patient is currently on medication for diabetes and has received medical clearance from his physician. He reports being sedentary but is interested in exercising. The patient denies any history of peripheral neuropathy, active psychosis or substance abuse in the last 6 months, severe brain dysfunction, abnormal ECG, or orthopedic related limitations. The patient speaks fluent English and has direct access to a telephone.

The patient is a 55-year-old healthy male who has not been hospitalized in the past year. He has no history of any allergies, autoimmune diseases, or chronic illnesses. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. He has not participated in any clinical trial in the past 28 days and does not plan to participate in any other clinical trial during the study period. He is willing to comply with the study protocol requirements and return for follow-up visits. He has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products in the past 3 months and does not plan to receive any during the study period. He is not taking any immunosuppressive or immune-modifying drugs and has not taken them for more than 14 days in total in the past 6 months. He has normal hematological and biochemical values, as per local laboratory normal values. He has no family history of congenital or hereditary immunodeficiency. He does not have any acute or chronic disease, as determined by physical examination or laboratory screening tests. He has not had any malignancies in the past 5 years, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer and lymphoproliferative disorders. He is not planning to move to a location that will prohibit him from participating in the trial until study end. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who is concerned about her weight and has a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m2. She has been enrolled in the Jenny Craig® Rapid Results™ program for weight loss. She has access to a tablet or smartphone with internet access and a camera. She is able to use a glucometer and Levl device to measure breath acetone. She is not currently using any medications for weight management or treatment of diabetes or psychosis. She does not have any serious allergies to corn, corn products, gluten, milk, soy, wheat, peanuts, or tree nuts. She does not have celiac disease, is not currently being treated with hemodialysis, and has not had bariatric surgery in the past 3 years. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an acceptable method of contraception. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who has recently undergone a kidney transplant from a deceased donor due to end-stage renal disease. The patient is currently taking Prograf® twice daily to prevent the body from rejecting the transplanted kidney. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication, LCP-Tacro™, which is a tablet containing tacrolimus, the same active ingredient as Prograf, but with a longer release period that only needs to be taken once a day. The study aims to determine the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of LCP-Tacro™ compared to Prograf® in the first 2 weeks after kidney transplantation. The patient must be over 18 years of age and must have received their first dose of randomized study drug within 48 hours of the transplant surgery. The patient cannot have received a kidney from a non-heart beating donor, have been treated with any other investigational agent in the 30 days prior to enrollment, be seropositive for HIV, have a current malignancy or a history of malignancy (within the past 5 years), or have any form of current substance abuse or psychiatric disorder that may invalidate communication with the investigator. The patient must also be willing to use a double-barrier method of contraception throughout the duration of the study if they have reproductive potential.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a diagnosis of B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) confirmed by immunophenotyping and immunohistochemistry. He is in functional stage 1, according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale, with a creatinine depuration of 70 ml/min measured by the CKD-EPI formula. His liver function is normal, with total bilirubin levels of 0.9 x upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT levels of 2.5 x ULN, and AST levels of 2.0 x ULN. He has no TP53 mutation and/or del(17)p. The patient has received one line of treatment that did not include the drugs in the study scheme, making him eligible for cohort 2. He has no active systemic infections, including viral, bacterial, or fungal infections, and is negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He has no history of hepatitis B or C infection or significant cardiovascular diseases. He has not been diagnosed with any malignancies within the past two years, and is not currently on any anticoagulant therapy with acenocoumarol or warfarin. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident or intracranial hemorrhage within the past six months, and has not experienced any severe allergic reactions to humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies. He is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old native Arabic-speaking man who suffered a stroke about 9 months ago. He has been experiencing difficulties in expressing himself verbally and has been struggling with naming objects and actions. He has also been experiencing difficulty in word fluency. He has been receiving standard speech-language therapy but has not seen significant improvement. He is right-handed and has no hearing or vision impairments. He is married and has three children. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. His medical history includes hypertension, type II diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking medications for these conditions. He has no history of psychiatric conditions. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has been attending his physical therapy sessions as prescribed. He has no contraindications for tDCS. His GACAT score for auditory verbal comprehension is 60 out of 100, and his naming score is 40 out of 100. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to sign the consent form.

Pt is a 45yo female with a recently diagnosed locally advanced breast cancer. She has opted for neoadjuvant therapy and is currently receiving chemotherapy. She has no history of radiation therapy to the thorax and has not participated in any prior breast clinical trials that gave additional radiation dose. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and understands the study constraints. She does not have any physical limitations that would prohibit resting prone on the exam table. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is of any ethnicity and is over 18 years old.

The patient is an 8-year-old male with a family history of Hemophilia A. He has not received any previous treatment with FVIII concentrates or any other blood products containing FVIII. He was diagnosed with severe Hemophilia A when he was 6 months old, based on frequent episodes of spontaneous joint bleeding and easy bruising. The patient has no other coagulation disorder and has no history of liver or kidney disease. He is not currently receiving any systemic immunosuppressive drugs.

A 14-month-old baby boy is brought into the clinic by his mother for a routine check-up. He was born full term and has had no significant health issues so far. He has completed the three-dose infant series of PCV13 and has not had any adverse reactions to the vaccine. He weighs 10 kg and is up to date on all his routine vaccinations. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. His mother is able to read, understand and complete study questionnaires, and is willing to comply with the study procedures. She has access to a telephone and agrees not to enroll her son in any other interventional studies while participating in this one.

A 42-year-old female with a BMI of 32, who has been struggling with weight loss for several years. She has a history of unsuccessful attempts at weight loss through various diets and exercise programs. She does not have any known significant medical history, and her thyroid function tests are within the normal range. She is motivated to participate in a clinical trial to help her achieve her weight loss goals and maintain her muscle mass. She has no history of eating disorders or psychological instability.

This is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of invasive breast cancer, and her tumor was found to be HER2 negative. She has not received any prior treatment for her breast cancer, including chemotherapy, hormonal therapy or radiation therapy. Her ER and PgR status by immunohistochemistry are known. She has a diagnosis of stage T2N1M0 breast cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of cisplatin versus doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (AC) chemotherapy prior to removal of her breast cancer. She may undergo an optional research biopsy so the study team can obtain tissue samples. She has a life expectancy of greater than six months and will use an effective means of contraception. She does not have a history of peripheral neuropathy of any etiology that exceeds grade 1, significant hearing loss, or uncontrolled diabetes. She also does not have renal dysfunction, a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to study drugs, uncontrolled intercurrent illness, or any condition that would prohibit administration of corticosteroids. She is not HIV-positive and is not on combination antiretroviral therapy.

The patient is a 30-year-old individual with a history of high triglyceride levels and episodes of postprandial abdominal pain, malaise, blurred vision, and dizziness. The patient has been diagnosed with lipoprotein lipase deficiency (LPLD) and has a homozygote or compound heterozygote for a LPL-gene mutation. The patient is willing and able to adhere to the protocol specifications and has signed an informed consent document indicating their understanding of the purpose of the study. The patient has not been diagnosed with overt cardiovascular disease, liver or renal disease, or uncontrolled thyroid disorder. The patient is not currently taking any medication that affects lipid or carbohydrate metabolism, except for statins, metformin, and other antihypertensive agents that can be safely interrupted. The patient does not smoke and does not consume more than two alcoholic beverages per day. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is seeking orthodontic treatment to improve the esthetics of her smile. She has a full set of permanent teeth with no dental or craniofacial anomalies. The patient has bimaxillary-dentoalveolar protrusion with a molar Class I occlusion. The overjet and overbite are within normal range. The orthodontic treatment plan includes the extraction of four 1st premolars and retraction of anterior teeth using maximum anchorage mechanics. The post-treatment goal is to achieve a canine 1 relation and molar Class I occlusion. The patient has not undergone any previous orthodontic treatment that does not meet the inclusion criteria for this retrospective cohort study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a BMI of 32, who has been struggling with weight loss for the past few years. She was recently diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) after an MRI showed her liver fat was above 5%. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medication. She has no known history of liver cirrhosis, portal hypertension or chronic liver disease. She does not have diabetes or any other significant endocrine disease. The patient has not previously participated in any clinical trials. She is willing to follow a carbohydrate-restricted diet (<20 g/day) for two weeks to determine the time-course of hepatic fat loss in NAFLD subjects.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing knee pain and stiffness for the past two years. He has been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis and has been told that he needs a total knee replacement (TKR) on his right knee. He also has knee flexion contractures (KFlCs) in both knees, which make it difficult for him to move around and perform daily activities. He is not on any medication for the osteoarthritis. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not excessively. He is married, lives at home with his wife, and works part-time as a security guard. He has no other medical conditions that affect joint range of motion. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided by the researchers. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty communicating. He has no history of previous knee surgery or septic arthritis.

This clinical trial is seeking parents or legal guardians of children between the ages of 5 and 17 to participate in the study. The parents or guardians must be able to read Turkish and willing to attend the study. The child's participation in home, school, and community activities will be assessed using the Participation and Environment Measure for Children and Youth (PEM-CY). The study aims to examine the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the PEM-CY. There are no specific medical or health-related criteria for this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is right-handed and has a body mass index of 23 kg/m2. He is in good health, with no significant medical history. He has not smoked or used nicotine-containing products for the past 3 months. He is willing to comply with all the trial requirements and allow his general practitioner to be notified of his participation. He has no contraindications to MRI scanning and is able to tolerate it. He responds to topical capsaicin by attaining a pain score of 5/10. He has no personal or family history of psychiatric disorders or chronic pain conditions. He has never had any surgery or blood donation in the past 4 weeks. He has no history of significant allergies or anaphylactic reactions to drugs or food. His estimated creatinine clearance is 100ml/min based on the Cockcroft-Gault equation. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to give informed consent.

This is a 54 year-old male who was diagnosed with COVID-19 and is currently hospitalized with moderate respiratory illness. He has confirmed positive test results for SARS-CoV-2 virus infection by PCR. His qSOFA score is ≥1 and he has evidence of lower respiratory disease by clinical assessment and chest X-ray. His SpO2 is ≥94% on room air at sea level. He is able to swallow 5 capsules of the study product at dosing time points. He has not demonstrated previous intolerance of 5-ALA and/or SFC by topical or oral administration (except for photosensitivity). He is not pregnant, nursing, or of reproductive potential. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent or has a legal representative who can provide informed consent. He is not participating in any other clinical trial of an experimental treatment for COVID-19.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has a history of shortness of breath and fatigue. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year and they have been getting progressively worse. He has been diagnosed with hypertension and is taking medication for it. He is a smoker and has been smoking for the past 30 years. He works as a construction worker and his job involves a lot of physical activity. He has noticed that he gets more breathless while working, especially while climbing stairs or carrying heavy objects. He has never been diagnosed with any lung disease in the past. He has been referred to a specialist for further evaluation of his symptoms. He underwent right heart catheterization in the past and was diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). He is scheduled for a thorax CT with dynamic contrast-enhanced DE-CT protocol as part of this clinical trial. He has no known allergies to contrast material and has not received a CT scan in the past six months. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

50-year-old female office worker complaining of non-specific chronic neck pain for over 6 months. She reports limited range of motion in the neck and difficulty with prolonged sitting and computer work. She has not received physical therapy for the past 3 months and is not currently taking any medication for her neck pain. She reports a sedentary lifestyle and a score of 7/50 on the Neck Disability Index (NDI) and a score of 3 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) for pain. She has no history of neck surgery or whiplash injury, and no dizziness or headaches. She is able to understand, write, and speak Spanish fluently.

A 60-year-old male patient presents with a history of colon cancer diagnosed 2 years ago, for which he underwent surgery, adjuvant chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. The patient reports that he has been experiencing abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue for the past 2 months. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass in the patient's abdomen, and laboratory tests show elevated levels of CEA and CA 19-9. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals multiple hepatic and peritoneal metastases, consistent with disease progression. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of >12 weeks. He has not received any other treatments for this cancer in the past 28 days, and his hematological, renal, hepatic, and respiratory functions are adequate. The patient agrees to present archival tumor tissues to the sponsor or undergo a pre-treatment biopsy. He is a potential candidate for the study of combination therapy with Mogamulizumab and Nivolumab in subjects with advanced solid tumors.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of diabetes for 10 years. He complains of blurred vision and was referred to an ophthalmologist. He has a history of poor glycemic control for the past 6 months with an HbA1c level of 10.5%. The patient complains of difficulty in reading small print and has a best corrected visual acuity of 20/80 in his right eye and 20/60 in his left eye. Fundoscopy reveals neovascularization in both eyes with active neovessels present. Fluorescein angiography shows a total area of active retinal neovessels of 5 mm2 in the right eye and 6 mm2 in the left eye. The patient has not received any previous treatment for his diabetic retinopathy. The patient has a history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. He does not have any known allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent. The patient is able to comply with the study and follow-up procedures.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma (MM) 2 years ago. He has received prior treatment with 2 lines of therapy and has recently experienced a relapse/progression of the disease. His performance status is good with an ECOG score of 1. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no significant history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. His laboratory tests show a serum monoclonal protein level of 1.5 g/L and an abnormal ratio of serum free light chains. His hemoglobin level is 11.2 g/dL, platelet count is 120 x 10^9/L and absolute neutrophil count is 1.5 x 10^9/L. His liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no significant non-hematologic toxicity from previous treatments. The patient has given written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using effective contraceptive methods. He has not received concomitant anti-myeloma therapy within 14 days prior to Day 1 of Cycle 1.

A 33-year-old mother of a 4-year-old child with a confirmed community diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is seeking help to cope with the stress associated with raising a child with ASD. She reports experiencing high levels of stress that affect her ability to manage her child's behavior and daily routines. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that tests the efficacy of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) as an intervention to reduce parenting stress, lessen parental reactivity and negativity, and decrease child externalizing behaviors. The patient is willing to participate in laboratory assessments at baseline and immediately post-treatment, as well as at 6 months and 12 months post-treatment. She understands that the MBSR intervention includes eight weekly 2.5-hour group sessions, a day-long (6hr) meditation retreat on the weekend during week six, 45 minutes of daily home practice guided by instructional audio CDs, and an MBSR parent workbook. She is willing to commit to the daily home practice and is open to learning more about mindfulness techniques to improve her coping skills. The patient has an Abbreviated Battery IQ (ABIQ) score above 35 on the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales 5th Edition ABIQ, ensuring task validity. She has no history of active parental psychosis, substance abuse, or suicidality, and is not currently participating in an auxiliary mental health treatment or support group.

Patient is a 45yo man with a history of hypertension and severe aortic stenosis. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. His echocardiogram shows aortic valve stenosis with a mean gradient of 45mmHg and an aortic valve area of 0.75cm2. He has been scheduled for aortic valve replacement surgery with extracorporeal circulation. The patient has given consent to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the potential differences between a minimal extracorporeal circuit (MECC) and a conventional cardiopulmonary bypass (MOPS) system.

A 45-year-old Caucasian man presented to the clinic with a history of HIV infection for 5 years. He has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and dolutegravir for the past 2 years with good adherence and viral suppression. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently employed as a software engineer and has a stable job. He has no history of CNS diseases or recent head injury. He reports occasional episodes of fatigue and mild difficulty in concentration but no major depression or psychosis. He has no significant family history of neurological diseases. He is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the MARCH CNS substudy.

A 35-year-old male who had a spinal cord injury in a car accident two years ago is experiencing neuropathic pain that is not relieved by his current therapy. He rates his pain as a 6 out of 10 on the Numerical Rating Scale during the last seven days of the baseline period. His neurology has been stable for the past six months, and he has been on a stable medication regimen for the past four weeks. He has not used cannabinoids in the past seven days and is willing to abstain from their use during the study. He has no history of schizophrenia, other psychotic illness, severe personality disorder, or any significant psychiatric disorder other than depression associated with his underlying condition. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, severe cardiovascular disorder, autonomic dysreflexia, or epilepsy. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. He has no significant renal or hepatic impairment and is not scheduled for any elective surgery or other procedures requiring general anesthesia during the study. He does not have a terminal illness and is considered appropriate for placebo medication. He has no known hypersensitivity to cannabinoids or any of the excipients of the study medications, and he has not previously been randomized into this study.

A 52-year-old female with a clinical diagnosis of probable ALS and a disease duration of 3 years since symptom onset. She has been on a stable dose of Rilutek® (riluzole) for the past 6 months. The patient has noticed a decline in upper extremity strength and has difficulty with activities of daily living such as brushing her hair and teeth. She has grade 4 or better strength in 8 of 10 testable upper extremity muscle groups. The patient is non-lactating and surgically sterilized. She has given informed consent approved by the appropriate Institutional Review Board (IRB).

50 year old woman with a history of diabetes, hypertension and myopia presenting with floaters and decreased vision in her left eye. Fundus examination revealed the presence of epiretinal membrane and macular edema. She has no previous history of vitrectomy surgery. Her current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial comparing 23G versus 27G vitrectomy. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in severe trauma, with an ISS score of 18. The patient was admitted to the ICU and underwent surgical intervention for multiple fractures and internal injuries. The patient has no known history of diabetes, alcohol or nicotine abuse, and is fluent in German. The patient's vital signs are stable, with a pH of 7.3, lactate of 2.5mmol, and Basedeficit of 5mEq/L. The patient's GCS was 10 at admission and has since improved to 14. The patient has no severe heart or liver injuries. The patient is being monitored for the development of trauma-induced sepsis, and their serum protein levels will be monitored as part of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy and is currently in remission. However, she has been experiencing symptoms of anemia such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and dizziness. Her most recent hemoglobin level was measured at 9.8 g/dL. She is not currently receiving any chemotherapy or radiotherapy. She weighs 125 lbs and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore treatment options for her anemia.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who has a history of allergic rhinitis with moderate response to grass pollen. She has been experiencing symptoms such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy eyes during pollen season. She has tried several over-the-counter allergy medications in the past, but they did not provide much relief. She does not have any structural nasal abnormalities, nasal polyps, or history of frequent nose bleeding. She is a non-smoker and has no history of respiratory tract infections or exacerbation of asthma. She is currently not taking any medications for allergies or asthma. She is willing to stay in an Environmental Challenge Chamber for 6 hours to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is using a highly effective method of contraception. She is able and willing to give written informed consent and complete all study measurements.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who suffered from an ischemic stroke about 6 months ago. He is currently on medication to manage his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. He has a history of smoking but has quit for the past year. He complains of excessive daytime sleepiness and snoring. A polysomnography test showed that he has moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 20. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30, indicating he is overweight, and he reports having difficulty sleeping on his back. He has good cognitive function and is able to understand and follow instructions. He is willing to participate in the study and wear the positional device as recommended. He has no other medical conditions that would interfere with the study.

A 28-year-old male presents to the hospital with a history of hepatitis B and alcohol abuse. He has been experiencing symptoms of jaundice, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for the past week. Upon physical examination, he is found to have hepatomegaly, ascites, and encephalopathy. Laboratory investigations reveal elevated liver enzymes and coagulopathy. He is diagnosed with acute liver failure and is not a candidate for liver transplantation due to lack of a suitable donor. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is an 18-year-old female who has been experiencing a persistent feeling of sadness and lack of energy for the past two weeks. She has also been experiencing changes in her sleep patterns and has lost interest in activities that she used to find enjoyable. Her mother has a history of depression and she also experienced a depressive episode two years ago following a breakup with her boyfriend. Her CES-D score is 16. She is interested in participating in a program that can help her prevent depression and improve her mental health. She denies any current suicidal ideation and is not currently undergoing treatment for major depression. She is willing to talk with her primary care physician and complete an online workbook as a part of the program.

A 25-year old single mother gave birth to a premature baby girl who is currently in the NICU at Children's Memorial Hermann Hospital (CMHH). She has a history of substance use, including marijuana and cocaine, and had a positive urine drug screen during pregnancy. She denies any current substance use and is motivated to enter substance abuse treatment. She has a past medical history of depression and anxiety for which she takes sertraline. The patient lives with her mother and two siblings, and has a history of domestic violence with her ex-partner who is the father of her baby. She reports that she does not want to have any more children until she is able to provide the best care for her current baby. She is fluent in English and has access to a telephone.

A 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma by a medical specialist is interested in participating in the Asthma Inflammation Research [AIR] Translational Program. She experiences occasional wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, which are relieved by the use of her inhaler. Her FEV1 is within acceptable limits. She has no history of diabetes, milk or coconut allergies, and her BMI is within normal limits. She does not smoke and has no significant respiratory or cardiac disease. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic options for asthma.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic for a routine colonoscopy. He has no significant medical history, no family history of colon cancer, and he does not smoke. He has been experiencing occasional abdominal pain and bloating, and his primary care physician recommended a colonoscopy to rule out any potential issues. He is currently taking no medications and has no allergies. He is generally in good health, with a BMI of 27. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve bowel preparation for colonoscopy.

A 33-year-old female patient with a history of uterine fibroids is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic myomectomy under general anesthesia. She has been experiencing heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding for the past 6 months, which has significantly impacted her quality of life. She has no other significant medical history and is classified as ASA II. She is not currently taking any medications and has no known drug allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no contraindications to the use of oxytocin. She is eager to participate in this clinical trial to help advance medical knowledge and improve patient care.

A 25 year old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis has been experiencing chronic sputum production for the past year. She is currently on a home therapeutic regimen that includes daily bronchial drainage therapy (BD) performed at least 2 times daily, along with concomitant use of an inhaled mucolytic and inhaled bronchodilator. Her lung function parameters have been stable for the past 4 months with no greater than a 10% variation. She has been evaluated at the University of Minnesota CF Center 4 times in the past 12 months

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with myocardial infarction (MI) and was hospitalized within 24 hours of the onset of symptoms. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medication for both conditions. The patient is a non-smoker and has a moderate alcohol intake. He is able to understand and communicate in the local language and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. The patient is willing to participate in this study and is committed to attending all follow-up appointments throughout the 2-year period.

32 yo woman with a history of severe obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) diagnosed by polysomnography with an AHI of 42 events/hour, presents to the clinic for participation in a research study investigating pulmonary disorders during exercise in patients with OSAS. She reports sleepiness during the day, loud snoring, and frequent choking or gasping during sleep. The patient has no history of clinical asthma or chronic lung disease. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 31 kg/m2. She is not currently experiencing any respiratory tract infection symptoms and has no exercise contraindication due to cardiovascular disease. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol as required.

Pregnant or postpartum women experiencing obstetric hemorrhage with blood loss greater than 500 mL (1000mL at RH), SBP less than 100 mm Hg, and pulse greater than 100 bpm are eligible to participate in this study. The patient must be willing and able to participate, able to sign or mark a consent form, and speak one of the languages into which the consent form has been translated, including English, Nyanja, and Bemba in Zambia and English, Shona and Ndebele in Zimbabwe. Patients with current viable third trimester intrauterine pregnancy that can be delivered in the next 20 minutes after hemorrhage begins and/or current bleeding sites above the diaphragm are excluded from the study. Patients with a history or current clinical evidence of mitral stenosis or congestive heart failure (CHF) are also excluded from the study. Women suffering obstetric hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock who have no detectable vital signs (non palpable pulse and BP) at the time of their arrival at the RH and have not responded to resuscitation attempts after 30 minutes and more than three hours have elapsed between the start of hemorrhage and the beginning of her treatment are ineligible for enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with persistent non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF). He has a history of high blood pressure and diabetes. His CHADS score is 2. He is eligible for long-term warfarin, but he experiences frequent falls due to his age and is concerned about the risks associated with taking the medication. He has no contraindications for aspirin or clopidogrel. He has been advised to consider Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) occluders after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation as an alternative treatment option to reduce his risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and cardiovascular death. The patient is considering participating in this clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of this treatment option.

A 25-year-old male with a history of acute leukemia that has not responded to standard chemotherapy. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and has no excessive hepatic or renal dysfunction. The patient has no clinically-evident cardiac or pulmonary dysfunction. The patient and donor have both signed informed consent. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

56yo man with newly diagnosed prostate cancer with a CAPRA score of 8, planned for primary radiotherapy. Patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild COPD. He is currently on lisinopril, atorvastatin, and tiotropium. Patient has no known allergies. He presents with urinary frequency and urgency, and mild lower back pain. His PSA is 12ng/mL. Biopsy results show Gleason score 8 (4+4) with involvement of 6 out of 12 cores, including bilateral involvement. MRI of the pelvis is negative for extraprostatic extension. Patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive PSMA PET/CT guided intensification of radiotherapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who has been HIV positive for the past 3 years. He has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the past 2 years. He has a recent CD4 count of 250 cells/mm3. He has been complaining of numbness and tingling sensation in his feet and hands for the past few months. He denies any pain or weakness. He has no history of diabetes or peripheral neuropathy. He has never had spinal surgery or any nerve condition unrelated to HIV infection or antiretroviral therapy. He has not had any alcohol-related complications in the past 6 months. His vitamin B12 levels are normal. He is willing to participate in the study to determine the factors that increase nerve damage in people with HIV who have taken drugs for treatment of HIV disease. He understands that he will undergo various nerve exams to evaluate the progression of peripheral neuropathy and the risk factors associated with it.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5 who is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not participated in any clinical research study within the past 90 days. She has not been diagnosed with any significant medical conditions and has no history of cancer or adrenal insufficiency. She is currently not using any glucocorticoids and has not used any systemic glucocorticoids in the last 12 months or inhaled products in the last 3 months. She is willing to adhere to the contraception requirements of the study and is able to consume a high-fat breakfast that includes pork. She has a body weight of 60 kg, which is below the maximum weight limit of 102 kg for this trial.

The patient is a healthy male volunteer aged between 30 and 55 years with a BMI between 18.5 and 30 kg/m2. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. He does not have any diseases of the central nervous system or psychiatric disorders, neurological disorders, or history of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells or blackouts. He has not had any chronic or relevant acute infections, drug allergies, or drug abuse. He is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 60g of alcohol per day. He has not donated blood or engaged in any excessive physical activity in the week prior to the screening visit. He does not have asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, urinary tract obstruction, or occupational exposure to antimuscarinic substances. He is willing to provide written informed consent prior to admission to the study and is available to participate in the multiple rising inhalative doses of BEA 2180 BR.

A 56-year-old male patient presented to the hospital with a history of abdominal pain and discomfort. Further diagnostic tests revealed that he required abdominal surgery due to a condition that required immediate intervention. The patient was over 40 years of age and met the inclusion criteria for the APOLLO study, which aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of fondaparinux in preventing venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing abdominal surgery at increased risk for VTE. The patient did not have active, clinically significant bleeding or any documented congenital or acquired bleeding tendency/disorders. He did not have a recent intracranial hemorrhage or recent brain, spinal, or ophthalmologic surgery. The patient was not using any contraindicated drugs that could not be combined with the injection of contrast medium. His creatinine level was below 2.0 mg/dL (180 μmol/L), and he did not have any documented hypersensitivity to contrast media. The patient was able to undergo IPC and wear Elastic Stockings. He provided written informed consent to participate in the study and was randomized to receive either fondaparinux or placebo in conjunction with IPC.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who is interested in losing weight and improving her body composition. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is able to swallow capsules without difficulty. She has tried various diets and exercise plans in the past but has not achieved her desired results. She is motivated to participate in this study and is willing to follow the study protocol for a period of 60 days. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any abnormalities. BP: 120/70 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl.

A 65-year-old male with a long history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents with worsening shortness of breath, cough, and difficulty with daily activities. The patient has been diagnosed with GOLD stage III COPD with a post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1s (FEV1)/forced vital capacity < 0.7 and FEV1 < 50% predicted. The patient has no history of recent exacerbations, infections, embolisms, pneumothorax, or thoracic or abdominal surgery. The patient also does not have any cardiologic conditions such as myocardial infarction, heart failure, or severe angina. The patient is able to perform the exercise training and understand the instructions required to carry out the tests and assessments planned. The patient is interested in participating in a low-load eccentric exercise training program to improve muscle function and quality of life.

A 39-year-old woman has been experiencing low sexual desire for the past year. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and lives a healthy lifestyle. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. She reports feeling tired and stressed from her daily routine, and that her lack of desire has been causing strain in her relationship with her husband. She is interested in participating in the study to explore treatment options for her HSDD. She has never taken Flibanserin before and is willing to participate in the study to determine whether the medication can help increase her sexual desire. She is right-handed and has no history of neurological disorders, seizures, or substance abuse. She is not currently taking any medications that may interact unfavorably with Flibanserin.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who is generally in good health. He has no history of cardiac disease, but has a family history of heart problems. He is physically active, and enjoys swimming and hiking. He has never had CPR training, but is interested in learning how to perform CPR in case of an emergency. He speaks English fluently and has no difficulties following instructions. He has no musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, or pulmonary conditions that would preclude him from performing moderate exercise. He has not had any recent surgeries or illnesses. He is willing to give informed consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old Hispanic man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain that he had been experiencing for the past few days. The patient had a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus. Further investigations revealed that the patient had significant atherosclerotic disease with triple vessel coronary artery disease. The patient was scheduled for a coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery with aortic valve replacement. The patient's preoperative echocardiography showed a mildly dilated left atrium with a diameter of 4.5 cm. The patient had no history of atrial fibrillation (AF) or other preoperative rhythm abnormalities, and his ejection fraction was 50%. The patient agreed to participate in a prospective cohort study to evaluate the predictors of postoperative AF after CABG. The patient was monitored for AF during his postoperative ICU stay with continuous ECG monitoring and daily 12-lead ECG recording. Serum potassium and magnesium levels were regularly measured postoperatively, and other parameters such as valve replacement, CHA2DS2-VASc score, and postoperative inotropic support usage were recorded.

25 yo F with a history of myopia and daily wear soft contact lenses. The patient reports experiencing dryness and discomfort with her current contact lenses. She has tried using different brands of contact lens solutions and artificial tears, but her symptoms persist. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate her tear film evaporation and potentially find a better contact lens option. Past Medical History: Myopia.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection. He has been experiencing episodes of hepatic encephalopathy (HE) in the past, which were managed with lactulose therapy. He is now scheduled to undergo a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) procedure to manage his portal hypertension. He has been advised to follow a vegetable-based diet and has been randomized to receive either lactulose or rifaximin therapy in addition to the diet, as part of the clinical trial. He has no history of alcohol or psychoactive drug use and has no unrelated neurological disease. His bilirubin and creatinine levels are within normal limits and his Child-Pugh's score is 8.

A 55-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer, currently undergoing adjuvant chemotherapy, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has been struggling with maintaining a healthy weight and has noticed a decrease in her quality of life. She is interested in learning more about nutrition and wants to make healthy changes in her diet. She is open to trying new recipes and learning how to cook healthier meals. She is motivated to participate in the cooking workshop and hopes to improve her metabolic indexes and control her weight.
