The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his vital signs are within normal limits. His labs show a normal serum magnesium level. He has been advised by his oncologist to receive therapy with an inhibitor of the EGFR pathway as part of his treatment plan. He has agreed to participate in this pilot study to help doctors understand the effect of EGFR inhibitors on magnesium levels in the body. He is willing to undergo blood and urine sample collection at baseline and at 2, 4, and 8 weeks during treatment. He understands that he will be followed periodically for up to 10 weeks after finishing treatment.

32F with a history of chronic low back pain for more than 6 months. The pain is at least 5 on the VAS scale and has not responded to non-operative care such as physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medication. The patient's pain is primarily in the back and is worsened by sitting. MRI shows evidence of single-level degenerative disc disease. The patient has not had any surgical interventions in the last 3 months and disc height is at least 50% of adjacent control disc. Patient does not have evidence of compressive radiculopathy with predominant leg pain, nucleus pulposus herniation, or disc bulges greater than 5mm. The patient has no prior lumbar surgery of any kind and no evidence of concordant cervical or thoracic pain. The patient does not have symptoms or signs of lumbar canal stenosis or structural abnormality at the symptomatic level. The patient does not have chronic severe conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis or fibromyalgia, and does not have pending workers compensation claim, litigation, or disability income remuneration. The patient has no psychological issues and has a Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score of less than 20. The patient is not pregnant, has no systemic infection, and is not allergic to contrast media or any medication to be used in the procedure. There is no history of traumatic spinal fracture, coagulopathy, unexplained bleeding, progressive neurological deficits, opioid abuse, free disc fragments on MRI, immunosuppression, or participation in another investigation within 30 days of signing informed consent. The patient has a BMI less than 30 kg/m2 and is willing to consent to the study.

Pt is a 56yo M with a long history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis of the liver. He presents with abdominal pain, ascites, and diarrhea. His past medical history is significant for hepatic encephalopathy and several episodes of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). During his most recent episode of SBP, he required hospitalization and treatment with intravenous antibiotics. His current medications include lactulose, rifaximin, and spironolactone. The patient is scheduled to undergo elective endoscopy as part of the AMBIC trial and has no known allergies to fluorescein. He is willing and able to provide blood samples and samples of ascitic fluid, and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has been classified as Child-Pugh class C due to his extensive liver disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a spinal fracture. She is experiencing significant pain in her lower back and has difficulty standing and walking. The patient has a medical history of osteoporosis and has previously undergone a spinal fusion surgery. She is currently taking calcium supplements and vitamin D to manage her osteoporosis. Her physician has recommended a minimally invasive surgery to stabilize the fracture. The patient has been informed of the potential benefits and risks of using Target Tape during the procedure, which include improved accuracy of incision placement and a potential reduction in the use of fluoroscopy. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided consent for the use of Target Tape during her surgery. The patient does not have any known allergies to medical skin adhesives, medical skin inks or copper metal. The medical practitioner will use Target Tape during the spinal surgery to assist in the localization of the incision site. The patient will be monitored post-surgery for any adverse effects related to the use of Target Tape.

Patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She is currently undergoing radiation therapy for her breast cancer and has completed 3 weeks of the treatment. She is fluent in English, understands written and spoken English, and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her health-related quality of life during her radiation therapy treatment.

56-year-old female diagnosed with Stage IV metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. The patient has relapsed from standard therapy and there is no therapy available that would be curative or provide significant benefit. The patient is also intolerant to standard chemotherapy and is interested in receiving experimental therapy. The patient has measurable disease and an ECOG performance status of 1, as assessed before the first dose of PBI-05204. The patient has a predicted life expectancy of at least 3 months and adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study and comply with all study requirements. The patient is capable of swallowing study drug capsules whole. The patient has not undergone major surgery or received cancer-directed therapy within the past 4 weeks or 5 half-lives of the agent, whichever is shorter. The patient has not been previously exposed to PBI 05204 and does not have a history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar composition.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was admitted to the hospital 2 days ago after testing positive for COVID-19. He was experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fever for about a week before hospitalization. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He lives with his wife and two children in a suburban area and works as a software engineer. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is currently on oxygen therapy and is being monitored in the hospital. His chest X-ray showed infiltrates consistent with COVID-19. His oxygen saturation level is 92% on room air. On laboratory testing, his ferritin level is 500 ng/mL, LDH is 350 U/L, and CRP is 45 mg/L. He is interested in participating in the study to help find a treatment for COVID-19.

62 year old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion for the past few months. He was evaluated by a cardiologist and was diagnosed with coronary artery disease. His coronary angiogram showed significant stenosis in two of his coronary arteries. He was advised to undergo coronary artery bypass graft surgery. He is fluent in Turkish and has no history of severe cognitive impairment or end-stage organ failure. He is willing to participate in the study and is excited to potentially contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired Caucasian male who lives alone. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is currently well-controlled with medications. He has not engaged in regular physical activity for the past year and spends most of his time sitting or watching TV. He reports occasional joint pain in his knees and lower back, but otherwise, he is in good health. He is independent in all activities of daily living and is able to transfer from his home to the exercise facility. He enjoys spending time with his grandchildren and hopes that participating in this study will help him stay active and healthy enough to continue doing so.

Pt is a 48yo M recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma after experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss. He completed standard therapy with R-CHOP±RT and is currently in complete remission. He has an intermediate IPI score and is otherwise healthy. He has no history of prior malignancies and meets all laboratory criteria for the trial. He has not received any other experimental drug or therapy within 28 days of baseline and does not have a diagnosis of deep vein thromboses in the preceding 3 months of study enrollment. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the Revlimid REMS® program. He has no known hypersensitivity to thalidomide and has not previously used lenalidomide. He is negative for HIV and infectious hepatitis.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 24 weeks pregnant with her second child. She reports experiencing physical violence from her partner during the current pregnancy, which has caused her significant distress and fear for her safety and that of her unborn child. She speaks English fluently and has expressed interest in receiving information about a study related to women's safety during pregnancy. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

Maria is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing melasma for the past year. She has had one pregnancy 2 years ago and had no issues during the pregnancy. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has tried various topical creams and home remedies, but has not seen any significant improvement in her condition. She has no history of skin cancer, liver or thyroid diseases. She has a healthy lifestyle and exercises regularly. Her hemoglobin levels and platelet counts are normal. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 42-year-old man was recently diagnosed with essential hypertension with systolic blood pressure between 140-179mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure between 90-109mmHg. He works a stressful job and has a family history of hypertension. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He is not currently taking any medications and is otherwise healthy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his hypertension and improve his overall health.

34-year-old male smoker who smokes at least 10 cigarettes per day for the past 8 years. He has no known liver or kidney disease and his most recent blood work showed normal liver and kidney function. He is not currently taking any medications or dietary supplements and has no known allergies. He has not consumed alcohol for the past 2 weeks and is willing to abstain from alcohol for the duration of the study. He has no history of gastric bypass surgery, bowel resection, or malabsorption syndromes. He is not currently taking antibiotics and has not had any problems with drug or alcohol use in the past year. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to provide informed consent. He is willing to take kava supplement as instructed and willing to abstain from all medication and dietary supplements for 3 days prior to kava administration, continuing until a minimum of 7 days after kava administration.

A 15-year-old adolescent with a history of social isolation, academic stress, and family conflicts resulting in low mood and occasional crying spells. No history of formal psychological/psychiatric treatment. The adolescent has no history of anxiety or mood disorders but has some risk factors for developing emotional disorders like anxiety and depression. The adolescent has a low to medium score on the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale and does not meet the cut-off score for the Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale-30. The adolescent and their legal guardian have provided written informed consent to participate in PROCARE, a selective prevention transdiagnostic intervention for at-risk adolescents. The adolescent is able to attend prevention modules on their own and is competent in the language of the intervention. The adolescent meets the inclusion criteria for the study as they have been identified as at risk for developing emotional disorders and have no contraindications that would prevent attendance at prevention modules.

This is a 68-year-old female who has a history of a hip fracture from a fall at home. She was referred to home health care upon discharge from the hospital and was subsequently diagnosed with osteoporosis. She has been receiving home health care services for the past month and is currently receiving physical therapy to help regain strength and mobility. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. Her primary care physician has prescribed a medication for her osteoporosis, but she has been hesitant to take it due to concerns about side effects. She currently takes a daily calcium and vitamin D supplement. She has expressed interest in learning more about osteoporosis and how to manage it effectively.

This is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) since childhood. He has tried various medications in the past but has not found one that effectively manages his symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves PET scanning and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to study brain function and nerve cell communication involving phospholipids. He is a non-smoker and has no past or current medical conditions that would interfere with brain function. He understands that the study requires overnight stays and multiple visits to the Clinical Center in Bethesda over a one-year period.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been wearing glasses since the age of 12. She has a history of myopia and has a current prescription of -3.50 diopters in both eyes. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Her recent eye exam revealed a corneal thickness of 530 micrometers, a refractive power of 43 diopters, and an axial length of 24.5 millimeters. She has no history of ocular surgery or inflammation and does not have any known ocular or systemic diseases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that is studying the choroidal thickness in myopes using SSOCT.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is currently not on any medication, and his BMI is in the range of 19 to 32. He does not have a personal or family history of cardiac arrhythmias or uncontrolled hypertension. He does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly. He is employed as an accountant and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. His blood pressure and vital signs are within normal ranges. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and understands the protocol restrictions. He is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs, vitamins, herbal, or dietary supplements. He is willing to stay at the research unit from the day before the first dose of the study drug until the day after the last dose of the study drug of each period. He is willing to wear a Holter monitor to record heart rate and rhythm continuously on days 1 and 3.

A 42-year-old female administrative assistant has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She has no history of spinal injuries or surgeries. Her pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting and standing, and she reports postural dysfunction. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and stretching exercises with little relief. She has no known allergies to any food or drugs. She has never participated in static or dynamic endurance exercise before. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to find relief from her back pain and improve her overall quality of life.

A 45-year-old Spanish woman has been experiencing subacute neck pain for the past three weeks. The neck pain has been consistent and has not improved with any over-the-counter pain medication. She has not been diagnosed with any inflammatory rheumatologic disease, fibromyalgia, or cancer in the past five years. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form. She is able to complete the questionnaires without any difficulty. The patient has no history of illiteracy or dementia.

65 year-old male with a history of open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension, currently taking TRAVATAN Z® solution and AZOPT® suspension to manage his intraocular pressure. He presents with concerns about potential side effects and inconvenience of using two different eye drops, and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new fixed combination of Travoprost/Brinzolamide ophthalmic suspension that may simplify his medication regimen. He is able to understand and sign an informed consent form and meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including having a mean IOP within the protocol-specified range at both the Eligibility 1 and 2 Visits and no recent history of ocular trauma, infection, or inflammation. He is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the study period, and is using adequate birth control methods to prevent pregnancy throughout the study. He has no history of hepatic or renal disease that would preclude the safe administration of a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (CAI) and is not currently using high dose (> 1 g daily) salicylate therapy or any additional topical or systemic ocular hypotensive medication. He has been on a stable dosing regimen for his other medications for at least 30 days prior to the Screening Visit and has not used any other investigational agent within 30 days prior to the Screening Visit.

A 60-year-old male diagnosed with coronary artery disease and scheduled for non-emergent coronary artery bypass grafting surgery is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. The patient is in good physical health and weighs 85 kg with a height of 170 cm. The patient has no history of alcohol, narcotic or illicit drug abuse and has not participated in any clinical trial within the past 30 days. The patient is not currently taking any narcotic analgesics or perioperative stress-dose steroids. The patient has no chronic non-cardiac pain requiring narcotic analgesics. The patient has normal liver and renal function tests and has no known allergies to amide-type anesthetics. The patient is able to provide informed consent and understands how to use pain rating scales and operate the patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) machine.

52-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal failure and currently undergoing hemodialysis for the past 6 months, presents with an elevated creatinine level. She denies any symptoms of cough, fever, or weight loss. She has no known history of tuberculosis or exposure to individuals with tuberculosis. The patient has previously received BCG vaccination as part of routine immunization in her country of origin, and she is a non-smoker. She has never had a tuberculin skin test before. The patient has provided written informed consent and agreed to participate in the study for the detection of latent tuberculosis infection. She will undergo chest X-ray and simultaneous testing with the tuberculin skin test according to the Mantoux technique, and with the T-SPOT. TB and QuantiFERON Gold in tube Interferon-gamma release assays to compare the performance of these tests for detection of latent tuberculosis infection.

The patient is a male or female diagnosed with haemophilia A in Japan. They have decided, along with their physician, to initiate treatment with commercially available NovoEight®. They must be willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study and have no known or suspected allergies to the study product or related products. They should not have previously participated in this study and have no mental incapacity, unwillingness, or language barriers that would preclude adequate understanding or cooperation. The patient's age can range from 0 years and above.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus during her pregnancy in 2008. She gave birth to a healthy baby girl and has been managing her blood sugar levels since then. She is now interested in participating in the Tianjin Gestational Diabetes Prevention Program (TGDPP) to reduce her risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes in the future. She has a 4-year-old son who will also be eligible to participate in the study. The patient has no significant medical history other than her previous GDM diagnosis. She is willing to commit to the lifestyle intervention program and attend the required consulting sessions with a dietician. She understands that the study will involve testing for metabolic traits and cardiovascular risk factors for both herself and her children. She is excited to potentially improve not only her own health but also her children's health through this intervention.

56-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component. The patient has received first-line treatment with an immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy (antiPD1, anti-PDL1, or antiCTLA4) but has progressed. Measurable disease has been confirmed per RECIST 1.1 by the investigator. The patient has not undergone any surgical treatment, radiotherapy, or combined treatment with curative intent. Toxicities related to any prior treatments have recovered to ≤ Grade 1 CTCAE v.4.03, and the patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (PS) of 0-2. Blood pressure is adequately controlled with antihypertensive medication to maintain a BP <150/90 mmHg before the start of study treatment. The patient has adequate marrow function with an ANC ≥ 1500/mm3 (≥ 1.5 GI/L), platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3 (≥ 100 GI/L), and hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL (≥ 5,6 mmol/L). Liver function is adequate, with ALT and AST < 2.5 × ULN and total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN). Kidney function is adequate with a calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 30 mL/min (≥ 0.5 mL/sec) using the Cockroft-Gault equation, and proteinuria is <2+ on urine test strip. Life expectancy is >3 months, and the patient is able to ingest study drug and meet study follow-up requirements. The patient is using medically accepted methods of contraception and is not pregnant at screening. The patient has not had previous treatment with sunitinib and has not undergone major surgery within 3 weeks of patient inclusion. Radiation therapy or embolization has not been performed within 2 weeks of the first dose of sunitinib. The patient has not undergone previous treatment with immunosuppressive drugs such as cyclosporine, tacrolimus, azathioprine, or long-term oral glucocorticoids taken prior to (3 months) patient inclusion. The patient has not undergone prior high-dose chemotherapy requiring hematopoietic stem cell rescue, and is not currently undergoing treatment on another clinical trial. The patient is not currently undergoing treatment with known potent CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers or that prolong the QT interval, within 7 days prior to the inclusion. There is no evidence of uncontrolled brain metastases, spinal cord compression, carcinomatous meningitis, or leptomeningeal disease. Any gastrointestinal malabsorption disorder or any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, may affect the absorption of sunitinib or increase the risk of bleeding or perforation is absent. There is no presence of an unhealed wound or active ulcer, and diarrhea grade III/IV in the screening period is not present. The patient does not have a diagnosis of any second malignancy within the last 3 years, except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. Clinically significant cardio-cerebrovascular disease within 6 months prior to initiation of treatment is absent, as is ongoing cardiac dysrhythmias of NCI CTCAE grade ≥2, atrial fibrillation of any grade that require treatment. Corrected QT interval (QTc) interval ≤ 500 msec. Active hemoptysis within 6 weeks prior to initiation of study treatment is absent, as is evidence of active bleeding or hemorrhagic diathesis. Presence of endobronchial lesions and / or lesions that infiltrate large vessels is absent. Current treatment with therapeutic doses of Coumadin (low dose Coumadin up to 2 mg PO daily for deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis is allowed). Other clinically significant alterations such as known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, presence of an uncontrolled active infection, presence of uncontrolled or symptomatic hypothyroidism, moderate-severe liver disease (Child Pugh B-C), requirement for hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, and history of solid organ transplantation are absent.

32F with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at age 14 years. She has been on insulin therapy since then, currently on basal-bolus therapy with insulin glargine and insulin aspart. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.5% and has been consistently elevated despite adherence to insulin therapy and regular monitoring of blood glucose levels. She reports frequent episodes of hypoglycemia and difficulty achieving optimal glucose control. Her BMI is 24 kg/m2. She has no history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, pancreatic surgery, or chronic pancreatitis. She has not taken any non-insulin antihyperglycemic agents or GLP-1 receptor agonists within the past 2 months. She has not taken metformin or thiazolidinediones within the past 2 months. She has not had hospital admission for glycemic control or diabetes ketoacidosis within the past month. She has not had frequent episodes of severe hypoglycemia or glucagon therapy administered by a third-party individual within the past month. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 45-year-old female patient presented to the clinic complaining of constipation symptoms for the past 3 years. She reported having a bowel movement every 4-5 days and had to use laxatives to assist with it. She has tried various medications, including fiber supplements, stool softeners, and laxatives, without success. She also reported abdominal discomfort, bloating, and distension. She denied any rectal bleeding, weight loss, or fever. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, and she is currently taking hydrochlorothiazide. She has no known drug allergies. She has no family history of gastrointestinal disorders. Her physical examination was unremarkable, except for a distended abdomen. Laboratory workup, including complete blood count, electrolytes, creatinine, and thyroid function tests, was within normal limits. A barium enema examination revealed no megacolon, and colonoscopy showed no organic lesions. Colonic transport tests showed that the opaque X-ray markers remained more than 20% after 72 hours. She expressed a strong desire for surgery and was willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of total or subtotal colectomy for slow transit constipation. She met all the inclusion criteria and had none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a 29-year-old female who recently gave birth to her first child via normal vaginal delivery. She is currently on her 7th postpartum day and is able to read and write in Turkish. She has no history of psychiatric illness and is not currently taking any psychiatric medication. Her newborn had a normal birth weight and an APGAR score of 9. The patient has not experienced any postpartum complications and is interested in participating in the study to receive tele-education to help manage any potential postpartum depression, anxiety or attachment issues during the COVID-19 pandemic. She understands that participation in the study is voluntary and is willing to provide informed consent.

Patient is a 45yo male who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain and weight loss. The patient resides in Japan and is able to read and understand Japanese. The patient has not yet started any treatment for HCC and is interested in learning more about the available treatment options. The patient is willing to participate in this non-interventional online survey to provide their preferences regarding descriptions of HCC treatments and to rank various treatment characteristics. The patient hopes that their participation in this survey will help them and their physician make a more informed decision regarding the best treatment option for their HCC.

The patient is a 13-year-old African American girl who has been diagnosed with persistent asthma for the past 2 years. She has been prescribed a daily inhaled steroid medication, but her adherence to the medication has been inconsistent. She lives in an inner-city neighborhood and has limited access to healthcare facilities. She has experienced several asthma exacerbations in the past year, which have resulted in emergency department visits and hospitalizations. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her manage her asthma better. She is a straight-A student, active in her school's basketball team, and enjoys listening to music. She has a close group of friends, but none of them have asthma. She is willing to participate in a peer support program and is excited about the possibility of using technology to help her manage her asthma. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and are willing to provide transportation to study visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has a history of smoking for over 20 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath during physical activities, such as walking up stairs or carrying groceries. He also has a cough with sputum production. The patient has a post-bronchodilator Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 60% of predicted normal and post-bronchodilator FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) of 60%. He reports a modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) score of 2, indicating that he becomes short of breath when walking at his own pace on level ground or when hurrying on level ground. The patient is able to walk 350 meters during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) and has a modified Borg score of 5 at the end of the test. He is willing and able to use the RESPIMAT Inhaler and metered dose inhaler, perform pulmonary function tests (spirometry), and complete the 6MWT as required by the study protocol. The patient has no significant comorbidities and meets all other eligibility criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and has been diagnosed with opioid dependence. She has been receiving buprenorphine maintenance therapy and is enrolled in a parent study. She has expressed a desire to breastfeed her infant after delivery. The patient is in good general health and has not experienced any major complications during her pregnancy. She is willing to comply with the study procedures, including providing breast milk and plasma samples at specific times after delivery. The patient has no history of major psychiatric illness, congenital malformations, or medical conditions that would make lactation inadvisable. The patient plans to deliver at the institution affiliated with the protocol and has no medical complications that would impair her ability to feed her infant after delivery.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse. He underwent a chemoradiation treatment, but unfortunately it did not work for him. He has a measurable lesion according to the RECIST1.1 criteria. His ECOG performance status is 1, and his life expectancy is more than 12 weeks. He has not been treated with any molecular targeted drugs. He has normal organ function. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. He has no known allergies to anlotinib and its excipients. His blood pressure is under control, with a systolic pressure of 130 mmHg and a diastolic pressure of 80 mmHg. He has no history of myocardial ischemia, myocardial infarction or malignant arrhythmias, and has a normal LVEF. He has no gastrointestinal bleeding tendency or bleeding tendency with INR and APTT within normal limits. He has no active brain metastasis, cancerous meningitis, spinal cord compression or other concomitant diseases that could seriously endanger his own safety or affect the completion of the study according to the investigator's judgment.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from moderate to severe atopic dermatitis for the past 10 years. She has tried various treatments such as topical corticosteroids and antihistamines but her symptoms persist. She experiences intense itching, pain, and swelling with areas of crusting over and dryness. The affected areas involve at least 10 percent of her body surface area. She has no other skin disorders and has never been diagnosed with severe heart, liver, kidney, or lung diseases. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of tacrolimus ointment. She has given informed consent and has met the washout requirements before the study. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of hypersensitivity to macrolides or any excipient of the ointment.

Samantha is a 42 year old woman who has been struggling with rosacea for the past five years. She has a history of moderate to severe papulopustular rosacea with at least 10 inflammatory lesions above the mandibular line. She has tried several treatments in the past, including topical antibiotics and steroids, but with little success. She is in good physical and mental health and is willing to comply with the protocol. She does not have any other skin diseases or conditions that would complicate the evaluation of the rosacea. She has not used any topical or systemic antibiotics, retinoids or steroids in the past 30 days. She is not currently using any physical modalities that could benefit rosacea. She is willing to sign an approved informed consent form for the study and HIPAA authorization.

A 56-year-old female was diagnosed with lung cancer with metastases to the liver and bones. She has a history of smoking for 25 years and quit 10 years ago. She has been experiencing persistent cough, fatigue, and weight loss for the past 6 months. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled on medications. She underwent a biopsy of the lung lesion and was found to have adenocarcinoma. A PET-CT scan revealed multiple liver and bone metastases. She is currently receiving chemotherapy and has responded well to treatment. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance research in lung cancer with metastases.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 23 kg/m^2. He works as a software engineer and has no history of any significant medical illness. He is not currently taking any medication or supplements. He has no allergies or hypersensitivity to any medications. He is sexually active with a woman of childbearing potential and is willing to use two effective methods of contraception during the study and for at least 90 days after receiving the last dose of study drug. He has no history of clinically relevant heart rhythm disturbances, unusual T wave morphology, or electrolyte abnormalities. He has not had any thoracic surgery or breast implants. He understands the purpose of the study and is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements. He signs the informed consent form indicating his willingness to participate in the study.

A 48-year-old man was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of septic shock due to pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia for which he is taking medications. He also has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. On admission, he was started on norepinephrine infusion for hypotension, which was gradually increased to maintain a mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65mmHg or more. Despite adequate fluid resuscitation, his lactate levels remained elevated at 3.5mmol/L with persistent hypotension, indicating catecholamine resistance. He was intubated due to respiratory failure and was under sedation with midazolam. His family has given informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been struggling with OCD for several years. Despite trying multiple treatments, including SRI therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy, he has not experienced significant relief from his symptoms. His Y-BOCS score is currently 22, indicating severe OCD symptoms. He has no history of liver disease, psychosurgery or seizure disorder. He is not currently using any illicit drugs or alcohol. He has no significant medical problems or psychiatric diagnoses other than OCD. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to try N-Acetylcysteine as an augmentation agent to his current treatment.

A 68-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with worsening headaches and confusion. He has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit 15 years ago. A brain MRI shows a large mass in the left frontal lobe with surrounding edema. He undergoes a biopsy, and the pathology confirms a diagnosis of glioblastoma. His KPS score is 60-70. He is started on steroids and antiepileptic medication. His MGMT promoter methylation status is tested and found to be positive. He is eligible for the trial and signs the informed consent. The patient is randomized to receive the biomarker-guided treatment arm and will receive TMZ monotherapy. The dose will be calculated using the body surface area (BSA) method. He will receive TMZ at a dose of 75 mg/m2 daily for 15 days on weekdays (Monday through Friday). This will be followed by six cycles of TMZ according to the standard 5-day schedule (days 1-5) every 28 days. The dose will be 150 mg/m2 for the first cycle and increased to 200 mg/m2 beginning with the second cycle, so long as there are no hematologic adverse events. He will be followed every 3 months for 2 years and every 6 months for years 3-5. Response and progression will be evaluated using the new international criteria proposed by the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology working group (RANO).

A 28-year-old woman has been suffering from Atopic Dermatitis since her teenage years. She has been experiencing frequent flare-ups of the disease, and despite using various topical medications and corticosteroids, the disease has not been well controlled. Her symptoms include severe itching, redness, scaling, and thickening of the skin on her face, neck, and limbs. Her objective SCORAD score is 38, indicating mild to moderate Atopic Dermatitis. She is interested in participating in the KM110329 clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition. She is generally healthy and has no known allergies to the ingredients of the investigational product. She is not pregnant, lactating or planning a pregnancy. She is willing to use proper contraception during the trial period. She has not taken any systemic photochemotherapy or immunosuppressive drugs in the past four weeks. She is excited to participate in the trial and contribute to the advancement of Atopic Dermatitis treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with severe asthma for the past 10 years. He reports experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing on a daily basis. He has been prescribed multiple asthma medications including inhalers, nebulizers, and oral medications. Despite these treatments, he continues to experience asthma symptoms that impact his daily life, limiting his ability to carry out physical activities and work. He reports having missed several days of work due to his asthma symptoms. He is a non-smoker and has no other respiratory diseases. He is interested in participating in this study in the hopes that it will improve his respiratory function, quality of life, and exercise tolerance. He is able to attend all study visits and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 35 year old male patient visited the dental clinic with a complaint of missing teeth in the upper jaw. He had a history of a car accident where he lost his upper right second premolar and second molar. His maxillary first molar was extracted due to caries. The remaining alveolar bone height was only 5 mm which made it difficult for dental implant placement. He had no history of any systemic disease and was physically fit and healthy. He is a non-smoker and has a normal BMI. He had a blood test and all the results were within normal limits. He was willing to follow the study procedures and provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with a liver tumor. Imaging studies show that he requires a right or extended right hepatectomy, but the future liver remnant volume (FLRV) is less than 25%. He has no significant medical history and has a WHO performance status of 1. The patient is able to comply with protocol requirements and has given written informed consent.

28 year old female who sustained a minor burn to her right forearm while cooking at home. The burn affects approximately 1% of her total body surface area. She has no history of significant medical conditions or allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has a BMI of 24.1 and is physically active, exercising 3-4 times a week. She has no history of malnutrition or eating disorders. She speaks fluent Swedish and English and is mentally able to understand and participate in the study. She has provided oral and written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman diagnosed with primary immunodeficiency. She has been receiving subcutaneous injections of immunoglobulin at home using an automatic pump for the past six months. She experiences fatigue, recurrent infections, and fever. The patient is compliant with her treatment regimen but has experienced some discomfort and inconvenience while administering her injections using the pump. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate subcutaneous injections of Gammanorm® 165 mg/mL administered with two different delivery devices: injections using pump or rapid push. She is willing to use either method of delivery during the trial and is looking forward to the possibility of improved quality of life and greater satisfaction with her treatment. The patient is not currently pregnant and is willing to practice reliable contraception throughout the duration of the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has recently suffered from a stroke resulting in left hemiparesis. The patient is currently admitted to the inpatient neurological rehabilitation unit with an estimated length of stay greater than 5 days and less than 5 weeks. The patient speaks English as their first language and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has intact skin integrity of the arms and has commercial insurance. The patient does not have a pacemaker, left ventricular assist device, or ventilator support. The patient is able to comply with wearing a heart rate tracking device during their full admission. The patient does not have multiple sclerosis, brain tumors, or degenerative neurological disorders.

Samantha is a 54-year-old woman who has been experiencing rectal bleeding, abdominal pain, and changes in bowel habits. She was referred to Carolinas Medical Center for further evaluation, where she was diagnosed with colorectal cancer. She is scheduled to undergo surgical resection of the tumor in two weeks. Samantha is married and works as a teacher. She has two adult children who live out of town. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or chronic conditions. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. However, she is feeling anxious about her upcoming surgery and has expressed concerns about her ability to manage her recovery at home. She is interested in participating in the preoperative education class to learn more about what to expect during and after her surgery, and to help alleviate her anxiety.

Maria is a 52-year-old woman who has been receiving hemodialysis for 6 months due to end-stage renal disease. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is controlled with insulin therapy. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.5%. She has a functioning arteriovenous fistula for dialysis access and has been on a stable dose of Paricalcitol for the last 4 weeks. Her iPTH value is 600, Ca is 9.6, and PO4 is 3.8. She has no acute inflammatory disease and is medically stable. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand the relationship between Vitamin D, insulin resistance, and inflammation in end-stage renal disease.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis. The procedure was successful and the patient was discharged home after a few days. The patient is currently on the standard antithrombotic medication prescribed by the hospital which includes aspirin and clopidogrel. The patient complains of occasional chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. The patient is well-nourished and well-dressed. The physical examination is unremarkable. The patient's electrocardiogram shows sinus rhythm. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the incidence and predictors of reduced leaflet motion and valve thrombosis after TAVI procedure using multimodality imaging strategy comprising cardiac CT, transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 56-year-old male patient diagnosed with colorectal cancer is scheduled for an elective colorectal surgery involving resection, with no stoma formation, that includes at least 1 incision that is > 10cm (target incision). He has no preoperative infection or is receiving any antibiotic therapy in the past 1 week prior to randomization, besides prophylaxis or antibiotic for the treatment of the disease that consists the indication for surgery. He is hemodynamically stable, male, and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception consistently and correctly for the duration of the study since he has a female partner. He is 56 years old, and he meets all study requirements. He has no known allergy to Doxycycline and/or to the tetracycline family of drugs or to the D-PLEX's excipients. He is not diagnosed with CVA within the past 6 months prior to randomization, and he has not undergone any abdominal surgery, and the current planned surgery involves re-opening the scar of a prior abdominal surgery performed within the last 5 years. He has no active malignancy or with malignancy that has not been in complete remission for at least 3 years. He has no other concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical condition that could compromise participation in the study. He is not a chronic alcoholic or drug abuse subject. He has no psychiatric or any other disorder that compromises ability to provide Informed Consent Form for participation in this study. He is willing to participate and meet all study requirements.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it does not involve enrolling patients or conducting any interventions. It is a protocol for the storage and use of human samples and data collected from participants who were previously enrolled in terminated NIH studies. The eligibility criteria are related to the type of study being conducted, which is a data analysis study. Therefore, participants may be enrolled in this protocol regardless of their age, gender, medical history, or current health status, as long as they meet the criteria for the type of study being conducted.

This is a 35 year old male with a past medical history of psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis diagnosed 2 years ago. He has tried multiple disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) with minimal improvement in his symptoms of joint pain, stiffness, and swelling. He reports difficulty with daily activities and has had to take time off work due to his symptoms. He is currently taking NSAIDs and low dose oral corticosteroids for pain management. He has not tried any biologic tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers yet. He is not currently pregnant nor is he planning to become pregnant during the study period. He is willing to use contraception during the study period. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is generally in good health with no significant medical history. He has a body mass index of 22.5 kg/m2. He reports no history of allergies or intolerances to drugs or food. He has not had any stomach or intestinal surgery or resection. The patient's liver function tests are within the normal range. He is interested in participating in the study to investigate the absorption, metabolism, and excretion of [14C]-BGB-3111 in healthy males. The patient is willing to fast for at least 8 hours prior to the administration of [14C]-BGB-3111. He understands that the study is open-label and non-randomized and involves the evaluation of the pharmacokinetics of [14C]-BGB-3111 when administered in healthy male subjects following at least an 8-hour fast from food (not including water). The patient is willing to undergo medical history, physical examination, 12-lead ECGs, and clinical laboratory evaluations to determine his eligibility for the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients directly, but rather focuses on developing and testing a new electronic health record (EHR)-based health information technology (IT) intervention to improve the management of Otitis Media (OM) in primary care and ENT physicians working within an integrated physician network that uses a common EHR. Therefore, there are no specific patient eligibility criteria.

A 35-year-old man presents with a history of chronic hepatitis B for the past 8 months. He has been diagnosed with HBeAg-positive hepatitis B virus with HBV DNA levels of 1.5 x 10^6 copies/mL. He has not been on any anti-viral agents, including interferon or pegylated interferon. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no significant family history of liver disease. He reports occasional alcohol intake but denies any tobacco or drug abuse. On physical examination, he appears well and has no signs of acute distress. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his abdomen is soft with no tenderness or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory investigations reveal elevated liver enzymes, including ALT and AST. His total bilirubin levels, prothrombin time, and serum albumin levels are within normal limits. His creatinine clearance is 75 ml/min. His alpha-fetoprotein levels are normal. The patient expresses interest in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Baracle Tab.® versus Baraclude Tab.® in HBeAg chronic hepatitis B.

The patient is a 19-year-old female college student who has been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) by a psychologist. She has been registered with Student Disability/Accessibility Services at her post-secondary institution due to her ADHD symptoms. She often struggles with maintaining focus and organization, and has difficulty with working memory tasks. She has tried medication in the past, but has experienced negative side effects and is currently not taking any medication for her ADHD. She is interested in participating in the Engage Study to improve her working memory capacity and potentially reduce her ADHD symptoms. She is comfortable using a computer and is willing to commit to daily training sessions for the duration of the study. She has no major neurological dysfunction or perceptual handicap that would prevent her from using the computer program.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman who is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic surgery for removal of an ovarian cyst. She has a BMI of 22.5 and has an ASA physical status of II. She has no known history of neuromuscular disease, hepatic or renal dysfunction, or glaucoma, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study. However, she has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently taking medication for it. Therefore, she may not be eligible for the trial due to the exclusion criteria for patients with COPD or taking medication that might influence the effect of NMB agents.

The patient is a 3-year-old girl with no history of illness or hospitalization in the last four weeks. She has no family history of kidney stones and is not currently taking any vitamins. She is being recruited to participate in a clinical trial to establish the reference interval of oxalate for the Pakistani population. Her parents have been informed about the study and provided with a container for urine collection. The urine sample will be stored at -30 ºC until analysis. The study will help determine the normal range of urinary oxalate to creatinine ratio in healthy children under six years of age.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. Her most recent HbA1c level was 8.2%. She has a total of 20 natural teeth but complains of bleeding gums and bad breath. Her dental examination reveals moderate to advanced periodontal disease, with pockets ranging from 4-6 mm and localized bone loss. She is not currently under the care of a periodontist and has not received antibiotic treatment in the past 3 months. She denies any allergies to iodine or antibiotics. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and there is no evidence of cognitive or communication impairment. She has a cardiac pacemaker but her cardiologist has cleared her for dental treatment. She is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study. She is available for follow-up visits and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 4-year-old Hispanic girl living in the South Bay area of Southern California. She has 4 caries-free primary molars with no occlusal pre-cavitation and no restorations. Her parent/guardian is able to provide consent in English or Spanish, and the child is cooperative and behaviorally suited for the clinical trial interventions. The family is registered at the San Ysidro Health Center Inc. The child has no health conditions or special needs that would prevent them from completing the required number of visits during a 36-month follow-up period.

Patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 18 and 50 with no current Axis I diagnosis, history of psychotic symptoms, or suicide attempt. They must be able and willing to give written informed consent. The patient should not be routinely taking prescription medications, except birth control pills, and should agree not to take any medication, prescription, or over-the-counter one week before and one week after receiving tariquidar. The patient should not have a history of head trauma resulting in a period of unconsciousness lasting longer than 10 minutes or a history of seizures. They should not have a recent exposure to radiation (i.e., PET from other research) which when combined with this study would be above the allowable limits. The patient should not be pregnant or breastfeeding and should have a negative urine drug screen. They should be able to tolerate small, enclosed spaces, as in the MRI. The patient should not have metallic foreign bodies that would be affected by the MRI magnet or fear of enclosed spaces likely to make them unable to complete an MRI scan. They should also have a negative HIV status and be able to lie flat on the camera bed for about 2 hours.

The patient is a 45 year old man with a history of colorectal cancer that has metastasized. He has received only one prior chemotherapy regimen for his metastatic disease and has not received irinotecan for treatment of his metastatic disease. His performance status is good with an ECOG score of 1. He has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has normal organ and marrow function, including leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, hemoglobin, platelets, total bilirubin, AST/SGOT and ALT/SGPT, alkaline phosphatase, INR and aPTT, and creatinine. The patient must have had a prior hysterectomy or have a negative serum pregnancy test and be using adequate contraception prior to study entry and must agree to use adequate contraception from study entry through at least 6 months after discontinuation of study drug. He is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient is not receiving any other investigational agents or anti-cancer therapy. He does not have brain metastases, uncontrolled seizure disorder or active neurologic disease. The patient does not have a significant allergic reaction attributed to humanized or human monoclonal antibody therapy. He does not have significant intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. He does not have known HIV infection, bleeding disorder or coagulopathy, or clinically significant gastrointestinal disease including, but not limited to, inflammatory bowel disease. The patient is in New York Heart Association Classification I, and his blood pressure is within normal range. He does not have tumors that are currently involving the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract. The patient does not have current evidence of cardiac ischemia or heart failure within the last 6 months, and he is not receiving any medications for cardiac ischemia. The patient does not have ECG evidence of ischemia or ≥ Grade 2 ventricular arrhythmia, and he does not have a history of acute myocardial infarction within 6 months, or unstable angina.

The patient is a 28-year-old primigravida who is currently at 34 weeks of gestation. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. She was diagnosed with mild preeclampsia at her last prenatal visit due to elevated blood pressure, proteinuria, and edema. Her current blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and she has gained 4 kg in the past month. She reports occasional headaches and blurry vision, but denies any abdominal pain or contractions. Her laboratory results show elevated liver enzymes and low platelet count. She has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use. Her pregnancy has been otherwise uncomplicated, and she has been receiving regular prenatal care. She has signed the informed consent to participate in the study investigating the relationship between severity of preeclampsia and maternal heavy metal levels.

35F with a history of alcohol dependence and recent binge drinking was referred to an alcohol treatment center seeking help for withdrawal symptoms. On examination, she appears anxious and restless, with mild tremors and sweating. She reports a history of alcohol use for the past 10 years with attempts to quit in the past but has relapsed each time. She has no history of delirium tremens or withdrawal seizures. Her past medical history is significant for depression, for which she is currently on medication and under psychiatric supervision. She denies any other substance abuse except nicotine. She is currently employed and has a supportive family. She is interested in participating in a detoxification program and is willing to undergo either an inpatient or outpatient program.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis confirmed by positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibody tests. She has been on methotrexate for the past 3 years and has had good control of her disease activity. She has not been diagnosed with any cognitive impairment or dementia. She is enrolled in Medicare Part A, B, and D, and has no HMO coverage for 365 days prior to and including the cohort entry date. She has not used tocilizumab or abatacept before. She has not been admitted to a nursing home in the past 365 days.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, diagnosed six months ago. He is currently using insulin therapy, taking one injection per day, but his A1C levels are still above 8%. He is experiencing difficulty managing his glucose levels and has been admitted to the hospital for glucose management. He is willing to participate in the study and follow all study procedures. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to insulin or insulin infusion sets. His random blood glucose levels are within normal range. He is not currently using real-time CGM therapy or insulin pump therapy. He is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. He does not have any systemic disease or medical condition that may interfere with the safety of the patient and efficacy of the study treatment, according to the physician's discretion. He is willing and able to provide informed written consent personally or by legal proxy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath and chest pain for the past few weeks. He has a history of smoking for the past 30 years, with a pack-a-day habit. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. Upon examination, his vital signs are stable, and he has a BMI of 28. The chest X-ray revealed a mass in his left lung, and a biopsy confirmed non-squamous cell lung cancer. He has not received any prior treatment for his lung cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and improve his chances of survival.

This clinical trial is specifically looking for healthy volunteers to participate in the study. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable in this case. However, it would be important to inform potential participants about the eligibility criteria and exclusion criteria mentioned above to determine if they meet the requirements to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35 year-old woman who underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for acute myeloid leukemia in 2008. She is fluent in Dutch and has completed high school education. She currently works part-time as a sales associate at a department store. She reports no social isolation and has a supportive family and friends. She experiences occasional pain and takes over-the-counter pain medication as needed. She is compliant with her medications and has received influenza vaccination yearly since transplantation. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She drinks alcohol occasionally and follows a healthy diet. She engages in moderate physical activity on a regular basis. She reports normal sexual function and feels satisfied with her couple life. She has no history of depression or anxiety and feels spiritually fulfilled. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the knowledge of long-term effects of allogeneic transplantation.

The patient is a 62-year-old retired non-smoker who was diagnosed with COPD 2 years ago. The patient has been attending pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) sessions for the past 6 months, which has helped to improve their breathing and exercise tolerance. Despite this, the patient still finds it difficult to socialize and engage in physical activities due to their condition. They have mentioned feeling isolated and lonely, which has resulted in a decline in their mental health. The patient is fluent in spoken English and has the capacity to make their own decisions. They are interested in finding ways to improve their social interactions and support network outside of the health service. The patient has no history of allergies or other medical conditions that would interfere with their participation in the study.

16 year-old male with moderate Hemophilia A diagnosed at age 4. He has a history of recurrent joint bleeding, with frequent hospitalizations for factor infusions. He is currently transitioning to self-infusion in the home setting and has been assigned responsibility for monitoring his bleeding logs. However, he has been inconsistent with maintaining accurate records of each bleeding episode and its treatment. He has missed several entries in his log over the past month, which has made it difficult for his healthcare providers to assess the efficacy of his treatment regimen and detect early signs of target joint bleeding. He has expressed interest in better understanding the importance of maintaining accurate records and improving his adherence to his treatment regimen. His past medical history is significant for mild asthma, treated with albuterol as needed. He takes no prescribed medications other than factor VIII for his Hemophilia A.

32-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 2 years ago and under the care of an HIV physician. He is ART-naïve and has never received ART after diagnosis. His viral load level is 20,000 copies/mL at screening and CD4 count is 600 cells per mm3. He is in good general health with no other significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. He works as a teacher and is not involved in any high-risk behaviors. He has no history of autoimmune disease or malignancy. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 68-year-old male who presented with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and occasional palpitations. He has a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with a previous myocardial infarction and percutaneous coronary intervention. He is currently on amlodipine, metoprolol, aspirin, and atorvastatin. His physical examination is significant for a regular heart rhythm with a heart rate of 70 bpm, blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, and no edema. His ECG shows a prolonged PR interval of 240 ms. Echocardiogram revealed normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 50% with mild diastolic dysfunction. He has been referred for pacemaker implantation due to symptomatic intermittent third-degree AV block. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the potential benefits of biventricular pacing compared to single stimulation of the right ventricle.

A 17 year old high school student who recently obtained his driver's license and has been driving for less than 6 months. He has no history of claustrophobia, migraine headaches, or motion sickness. He is not pregnant, and English is his primary language.

A 35-year-old obese man with a BMI of 32 kg/m2 comes to the clinic for a weight loss program. He has a history of hypertension that is controlled with medication. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and unhealthy eating habits, including frequent fast food and soda consumption. His family history is significant for type 2 diabetes in both parents. His blood glucose level is 5.5 mmol/L, C-peptide level is 2.2 nmol/L, and HbA1c level is 5.7%. His serum creatinine is 90 micromol/L, and liver enzymes are within normal limits. He denies any history of gout, alcohol or drug abuse, or smoking cessation within the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of a medication for weight loss in obese men with hyperinsulinemia.

The patient is a 32-year-old office worker who spends most of their day sitting at a desk. They work full-time and have access to a work telephone and desktop computer with internet. They have no history of cardiovascular or metabolic disease and are not currently taking any medication. They are not pregnant and do not plan to be absent from work for more than one week during the trial. They are interested in participating in the study to explore whether a sit-stand workstation can reduce their sitting time at work and improve their health over an 8-week period. They are willing to attend University laboratories for individual assessments of other stated outcomes at baseline and 8 weeks, and to keep ecological momentary assessment (EMA) diaries at baseline, 4 weeks (mid-intervention), and 8 weeks (end-intervention) to assess their office-based behaviours. They are excited to potentially contribute to research that may help improve the health and well-being of office workers.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or coffee. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is not currently taking any medications or undergoing any treatments for any health conditions. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has read and signed the Informed Consent Form. He has no history of allergic reactions to any drugs or foods. He has not received any isotope treatment or examination before screening, or received X-ray examination more than three times within one year. He is not currently undergoing any other clinical trials and is available to complete the trial according to the regulations.

A 42-year-old man who has been struggling with depression for the past year. He has been receiving treatment from a psychiatrist, but has not found much relief from his symptoms. He has tried multiple medications and therapy, but has not achieved remission. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he hopes an AI-powered clinical decision aid will help guide him and his physician towards a more personalized treatment plan. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to use contraception if necessary. He does not have a diagnosis of bipolar disorder.

The patient is a premature infant who was born at 31 weeks gestation, with a birth weight, length and head circumference between the 5th and 95th percentiles for gestational age. The infant has been in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for the past 2 weeks and is currently stable. The infant has not had any major congenital anomalies, complex cardiac defects, severe CNS injury, hypothyroidism, inborn errors of metabolism, or difficulty establishing full enteral feeds. The parents have given consent for the infant to participate in the study and the infant has been randomized to receive either developmental massage therapy or a SHAM control. The study will track the infant's growth and development over the next 6 months, including multiple measurements and developmental testing.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with heart failure six months ago. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue, limiting her ability to do daily activities. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She lives with her husband who is her primary caregiver. She reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, but denies any history of dementia or neurological disorders. She speaks fluent English and does not have any active substance abuse. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the relationship between her cognitive function and her ability to manage her heart failure symptoms. She is willing to complete the required tests and questionnaires and to be contacted in 90 days to report any hospitalizations.

The patient is a newborn male infant, born at 38 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery to a 27-year-old mother. The mother had a healthy pregnancy and no complications during delivery. At birth, the infant had signs of moderate to severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Seattle Children's Hospital. After evaluation, the infant was started on therapeutic hypothermia for 72 hours to prevent brain damage. Mechanical ventilation was initiated, and the infant was intubated. The treating physician deemed the infant to be a candidate for the study, as he is anticipated to require continuous sedation and/or treatment to prevent shivering. The infant has a central line and a peripheral arterial line in place. The parents have voluntarily signed the informed consent document approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB)/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC). The infant does not have any chromosomal anomalies or known cyanotic congenital heart defects. He has not received DEX prior to enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and has completed locoregional treatment. He has a history of elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels in his serum. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker and is in overall good health. He has no history of allergies or chronic medical conditions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His HLA-A2.1 status is positive. He has a normal hemoglobin level, platelet count, and ANC. His liver function is Child-Pugh Class A. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore adjuvant therapy for HCC. He is willing to follow the contraception requirements as he is sexually active. He is able to provide informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman has been struggling with infertility for the past 5 years due to congenital absence of the uterus. She is interested in uterine transplantation to achieve a pregnancy. She has no significant medical history, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She currently takes prenatal vitamins and has no known allergies. She has been approved for the study and will be undergoing a uterine transplant procedure in the upcoming weeks. As part of the study, she will be providing non-invasive samples such as blood, smears, and biopsies for analysis to understand the mechanisms of rejection in uterine transplantation and to search for non-invasive markers of rejection. She is excited to be a part of this groundbreaking research that may help other women in the future.

32-year-old female diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes for over 5 years, currently treated with an external insulin pump for the past 2 years. Her last HbA1c was 9.5% measured in the analysis laboratory medical 3 months ago. She requires a daily dose of insulin of 35 units. She lives with her husband and has a nearby neighbor who has the key to her residence and access to a phone. She has a GSM connection in her area and does not plan to travel outside of France during the trial. She is not pregnant nor planning to be. She is affiliated to social security and has agreed to participate in the study and signed an informed consent form. She has no other serious illnesses that may impair study participation and is not taking any medication that may significantly interfere with glycemia.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has had a persistent cough for over a year that does not respond to standard treatments. She has undergone medical investigations but no underlying trigger has been identified. She has no significant findings on chest imaging within the past year and her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) is above 80% of the predicted normal value. At screening, she scores more than 40 millimeters on the Cough Severity Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). She weighs more than 50 kilograms and has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18 to 40 kilograms per meter square (kg/m^2). She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding but is capable of giving informed consent. She has no serious or clinically significant gastrointestinal, renal, endocrine, neurologic, hematologic, or other conditions that would make her unsuitable for the study. She has not had a history of chronic productive cough, acute coronary syndromes, coronary angioplasty, or stenting within the past 6 months. She has no active ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding and has not had a history of stroke or seizure disorder within the past 5 years. She has not had a respiratory tract infection within the past 6 weeks. She has no evidence of serious suicide risk or any history of suicidal behavior or ideation. Her ALT and bilirubin levels are normal, and she has no current or chronic history of liver disease or known hepatic or biliary abnormalities. Her QT interval corrected (QTc) is less than 450 milliseconds (msec). She is not using any prohibited medication within the restricted timeframe relative to the first dose of study treatment and has not been exposed to more than 4 new chemical entities within the past 12 months. She has not participated in any clinical study involving an investigational study treatment within the past 3 months. She has no known sensitivity to any of the study treatments or components thereof, or drug or other allergy that contraindicates participation in the study.

A 32-year-old male veteran presented to the clinic complaining of persistent flashbacks, nightmares, and anxiety. He had been diagnosed with PTSD by a mental health professional and was undergoing treatment with psychotherapy and medication, but his symptoms persisted. He had no history of substance abuse, cardiac pacemaker implant, epilepsy, neurosurgery, or brain trauma. He had no other chronic medical conditions. The patient was informed about the study and gave written informed consent. He will be randomly assigned to one of the four groups and will receive rTMS treatment with or without traumatic stimuli. The patient will be assessed at four time points-before TMS (baseline), at day 5, at day 10, and at day 24 (14 days after the intervention). The PTSD Checklist, the Treatment Outcome PTSD Scale, the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression, and the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale will be used to evaluate the efficacy of the treatment.

A 52-year-old male presents with worsening headaches and seizures over the past month. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications. He denies any recent head trauma or family history of brain tumors. Neurological examination reveals mild right-sided weakness and difficulty with speech. Imaging studies reveal a large mass in the left frontal lobe consistent with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). The patient is scheduled for neurosurgical resection of the tumor and is being considered for the combined approach of 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) and intraoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to improve the precision of the resection.
