The patient has no known allergies to 5-ALA or porphyrin and does not have porphyria. He is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and has been receiving treatment for the past 3 years. She was recently admitted to the inpatient psychiatric unit due to a manic episode with psychotic features. She has a history of non-compliance with her medication regimen and has been known to abruptly stop taking her medications in the past. She is currently prescribed lithium and risperidone, and her preadmission dosing regimen was 600 mg of lithium twice daily and 2 mg of risperidone once daily. She has a history of alcohol and substance abuse but reports being sober for the past 6 months. She has a supportive family and is motivated to adhere to her medication regimen during her hospital stay. Her plasma levels of lithium and risperidone will be monitored and compared to the expected plasma levels based on her preadmission dosing regimen.

A 45-year-old man presents with a history of HIV mono-infection for the past 6 years. He has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 2 years, which includes tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz. He reports occasional alcohol consumption but denies any drug abuse. He has a history of high cholesterol and hypertension, for which he is taking atorvastatin and lisinopril. His physical exam is unremarkable, with no significant findings on abdominal exam. His BMI is 28. His most recent laboratory tests show a CD4 count of 650 cells/mm3 and an undetectable HIV viral load. His liver function

Patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of heart failure for the past 2 years. He has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. His heart failure is classified as NYHA Class III. He lives with his wife, who has been his primary caregiver and support system throughout his illness. The patient is interested in participating in a research study that aims to improve his and his spouse's health and well-being. He has access to a device with a camera and is willing to participate in Zoom sessions. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is reachable by telephone/email. He does not have any major hearing or cognitive impairments and is not currently enrolled in any other trials.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 kg/m2. She has a history of obesity-related co-morbidities, including type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She has been considering weight loss surgery and has been advised by her physician that she is a candidate for either standard laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) surgery. She has no history of prior bariatric surgery and is willing to comply with the study protocol and proposed follow-up visits. She has reviewed and signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in this observational registry to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the easyEndoTM Universal Linear Cutting Stapler during her RYGB surgery.

The patient is a 62-year-old man recently diagnosed with prostate adenocarcinoma. He has a Gleason score of 7 and his cancer is in stage II. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is scheduled for radical treatment and will be enrolled in Group 2 of the study, which involves blood sampling before and after the start of hormonal therapy. He has not received any antibiotic treatment in the past two months and has not undergone any previous hormonal treatments for advanced disease. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old active man who recently sustained an acute ACL injury while playing soccer. He is 175 cm tall and his weight is 80 kg. He is complaining of knee instability and is unable to participate in his regular physical activities. He is currently employed as a software developer and does not smoke or use any drugs. He has no prior history of knee injuries or surgeries. He enjoys sports and exercise and is motivated to get back to his normal activities as soon as possible. His BP: 120/80, HR: 70/min and his BMI is: 26.12. His labs are within normal limits. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the best treatment option for his ACL injury.

38-year-old female with a history of biopsy-confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. The tumor size was measured at 3.8 cm by ultrasound and MRI, and there was no evidence of axillary lymph node involvement based on preoperative imaging evaluations. The patient has not undergone neoadjuvant therapy and does not have distant metastases. She is currently planning to undergo breast-conserving surgery followed by adjuvant radiation therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo axillary surgery and pathological testing, including sentinel lymph node biopsy, if required. She does not have any history of diabetes mellitus or any known allergies to the tracer used in LymphPET.

A 54-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. The patient underwent a mediastinoscopy, which revealed ipsilateral mediastinal lymph node involvement. A CT scan confirmed the presence of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes and PET scan showed the same lymph nodes to be positive. The patient's performance status is 1 according to SWOG criteria. The patient's laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count of 2.0 x 10(9)/L, platelet count of 150,000 x 10(9)/L, Serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, calculated creatinine clearance of 60mL/min, serum bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, SGOT of 25 IU/L, SGPT of 30 IU/L and alkaline phosphatase of 80 IU/L. Pulmonary function tests show an FEV1 of 2.5L and DLCO of 60% predicted. Brain imaging ruled out brain metastases. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for any malignancy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided signed informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with insulin-dependent diabetes and end-stage renal disease. He has been on hemodialysis for the past year and has been recently listed for a simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplant. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral vascular disease. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has no history of malignancy and is not on any investigational drugs. His physical examination is significant for peripheral edema and reduced pedal pulses. His lab study shows a fasting blood sugar level of 190 mg/dL, HbA1c of 7.5%, creatinine of 8.5 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate of 8 mL/min/1.73m², total cholesterol of 220 mg/dL, LDL of 140 mg/dL, HDL of 35 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 200 mg/dL. He has signed and dated informed consent, and has no evidence of any active systemic or localized major infection.

Patient is an 8-year-old boy from the United States with no significant past medical history, who is scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia. The surgery is expected to last for 2 hours. He is not on any vasoactive medications, and has normal sinus rhythm. There is no history of neck surgery or carotid interventions. His physical examination is unremarkable.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who has been struggling with addiction to opioids for the past two years. He started using opioids recreationally after a sports-related injury, but the addiction quickly took over his life. He has tried to quit several times but has not been successful. He is currently on a medication-assisted treatment program and attends therapy sessions regularly. He has a history of depression but has not had any symptoms for the past year. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs other than opioids. He is not currently employed but is actively seeking a job. He has a supportive family who is involved in his treatment. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate.

72-year-old male patient with a history of ischemic stroke that occurred 8 months ago is seeking a rehabilitation program to improve his upper extremity motor function. His medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are currently well controlled with medication. He underwent formal rehabilitation programs immediately after the stroke, but he still experiences mild paresis of his right upper extremity, with a score of 3 in the Medical Research Council Scale for Muscle Strength. He has no major language or cognitive deficits affecting comprehension and his Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28. He has no other neurological or psychiatric comorbidities, or musculoskeletal conditions affecting upper extremity motor function. He is interested in participating in a rehabilitation program that involves playing musical instruments and is willing to attend weekly group sessions for 10 weeks, in addition to a home-based self-training program using an app for electronic tablets.

The patient is a 10-year-old male with a history of intellectual disability and severe dental caries. The patient's parents have noticed that he has been experiencing pain while eating and sleeping and is having difficulty maintaining good oral hygiene due to his disability. The patient will be recruited from the GA unit in the department of pediatric dentistry at the faculty of oral and dental medicine, Cairo University. The patient will undergo a comprehensive clinical dental examination and full dental rehabilitation under general anesthesia. The study will assess the impact of the dental treatment on the patient's oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) using the early childhood oral health impact scale (ECHOIS). Anthropometric measurements such as height, weight, and BMI will also be recorded before and after the dental treatment. The patient's parents will be asked to complete the ECHOIS questionnaire before and after treatment, with follow-up after 3 and 6 months to assess the patient's OHRQoL and overall growth parameters. The study excludes healthy children, children with physical special needs, and those with serious medical conditions or transmissible diseases. The patient's parents have given their consent for their child to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of septic shock. He presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of fever, chills, and productive cough. On exam, he was found to have a temperature of 39°C, heart rate of 120 beats/min, blood pressure of 85/55 mmHg, and respiratory rate of 24 breaths/min. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and given fluid resuscitation with crystalloids. Despite these measures, his blood pressure remained low, and he required vasopressors for hemodynamic support. He has been on vasopressors for less than 24 hours. Sequential serum samples will be collected to examine cytokine responses and correlate them to clinical manifestations of disease as well as the patient's response to antibiotic therapy and resuscitation efforts.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rectal cancer after experiencing rectal bleeding and abdominal pain for several weeks. She underwent MRI and endorectal ultrasound, which confirmed the tumor is located 10cm from the anal verge and is clinically staged as cT3N1M0. The patient is in good overall health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. She has no history of prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy, and her laboratory results show normal hematologic, liver, and renal function. The patient has no clinically significant cardiac disease or peripheral neuropathy. She has no other cancers and is negative for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 2-year-old girl who was diagnosed with complex congenital heart disease and has undergone cardiac surgery. She lives with her parents and older brother in Nord-Pas-De-Calais, France. She is currently being followed by the Pediatric Cardiology Department of Lille University Hospital for her cardiac condition. Her parents have noticed that she is not reaching the same developmental milestones as her older brother did at the same age. She has difficulty with fine motor skills, such as picking up small objects, and with gross motor skills, such as crawling and walking. She has also had difficulty with feeding and swallowing since birth. She has no other significant medical history or developmental concerns. Her parents are interested in participating in the study to help better understand the risk factors for neurodevelopmental disorders in children with congenital heart disease and to potentially receive specialized care for their daughter's developmental delays.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who was diagnosed with hepatitis C virus (HCV) six years ago. He has tried the standard of care treatment (pegylated interferon and ribavirin) twice but did not respond to either of them. He is currently in good physical health and has no other major health concerns. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He doesn't smoke or use any drugs. He drinks alcohol socially. His labs: HCV viral load: 1,500,000 IU/mL, AFP: 35 ng/mL, Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL, platelet count: 140 x 10^9/L, and white blood cell count: 4.5 x 10^9/L. His baseline AST and ALT are elevated at 80 U/L and 90 U/L, respectively. He is willing to use two reliable forms of contraception during the trial.

This is a 34 year old male who presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain that started 2 days ago. The pain is described as sharp and constant, with a score of 8 out of 10 on the pain scale. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. An ultrasound showed a gallbladder with multiple stones and he was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis. The attending ED physician has decided to administer intravenous opiates to manage his pain. This patient is eligible for the clinical trial comparing different dosing regimens of morphine in patients with moderate to severe pain. He meets the age criteria and the inclusion criteria for pain duration and need for opioid analgesia. He does not have any exclusion criteria, as he is not taking any opioids or tramadol within 7 days, his systolic blood pressure is above 90 mm Hg, and his weight is less than 100 kg.

A 68-year-old retired teacher presents with concerns about her memory. She reports that she often forgets where she has placed her belongings, has difficulty remembering people's names, and sometimes struggles to find the right words during conversations. She also reports feeling more anxious and worried than usual and has noticed a decline in her mood. She is eager to participate in the Neurotrack Virtual Cognitive Health Study. She has access to a desktop computer, video-teleconferencing, and reliable internet connection, and is highly motivated to use a daily coaching program. She has no significant history of mental illness, substance abuse, learning disability, or neurologic conditions. She is not pregnant and is not currently participating in a formal cognitive-training coaching program.

A 25-year-old female was diagnosed with ADHD during her college years. She has been prescribed mixed amphetamine salts for the past 3 years and has been adhering to her medication regimen. She reports difficulty with focus and concentration, and has a history of impulsivity and restlessness. She does not have any other psychiatric disorders or significant medical illnesses, and is not currently taking any other medications. She has no metallic devices that preclude magnetic resonance imaging and is willing to withhold her medication for 72 hours prior to the MRS scan. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the neurobiology of ADHD and the effect of stimulant treatment on neurotransmitter levels in the brain.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with hypertriglyceridemia. She reports a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease, with her father having a heart attack at age 55. The patient has been trying to manage her condition through lifestyle modifications, including dietary changes and exercise. However, despite her efforts, her triglyceride levels have remained elevated, ranging from 180 mg/dL to 200 mg/dL. She has never been prescribed lipid-lowering medications and has no history of diabetes mellitus. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates postprandial lipid metabolism in patients with hypertriglyceridemia and normo-lipidemic controls. She is willing to comply with the study protocol, which includes an oral fat challenge using different types of fats (saturated fatty acids, mon-unsaturated fatty acids, and medium-chain fatty acids). She understands that she cannot participate in the study if her LDL-cholesterol levels are greater than 190 mg/dL or if she is taking lipid-lowering medications. She hopes that participating in this trial will provide her with a better understanding of her condition and help her manage her triglyceride levels more effectively.

25-year-old Caucasian male with no significant medical history, weighing 75 kg and with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2. The patient reports no allergies or adverse reactions to any medications or excipients of clinical significance. He has never participated in more than three clinical studies of a new chemical entity in the previous year or a clinical study of any investigational medicinal product within 12 weeks or five half-lives of the IMP before the administration of the IMP in this clinical study. The patient has no clinically relevant abnormal medical history, physical findings, or laboratory values that could interfere with the objectives of the study or the safety of the subject, as judged by the Investigator. There is no previous medical history of tuberculosis or recurrent medical history of cold sores, pharyngitis, urinary tract infection, diarrhea/dysentery, chest infections, or fungal infection. The patient has not received any prescribed systemic or topical medication within 14 days prior to administration of the IMP(Day 1). The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 55 year old woman was diagnosed with multiple system atrophy (MSA) a year ago. She has been receiving drug treatment for the disease. She experiences respiratory symptoms such as stridor and sleep-related respiratory disturbances. Recently, she has been feeling weak and experiencing difficulty breathing. She has no history of respiratory disease or occupational exposure that could affect her respiratory system. She does not have any physical or mental disability that could prevent the implementation of tests. She scored 27 on the Mini Mental State Examination. She has never been diagnosed with neuromuscular disease other than MSA, psychiatric illnesses or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the respiratory muscle strength in MSA patients.

The patient is a premature infant born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1100 grams. The baby was diagnosed with patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) via echocardiogram. The infant has been receiving respiratory support via nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and is tolerating feeds of 15 ml every 2 hours. The baby has no other congenital anomalies and has no significant medical history. The infant's laboratory values are within normal limits, with a platelet count of 100,000/mm3, creatinine level of 0.4 mg/dL, and bilirubin level of 3 mg/dL. The infant has no signs of intestinal abnormality or necrotizing enterocolitis. The baby's parents have been informed of the study and have given their consent for their child's participation.

This is a 42-year-old female who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis three years ago. She is currently being treated with subcutaneous biologic DMARDs (Tocilizumab) and has been experiencing some side effects, including injection site reactions and fatigue. Despite these side effects, she is committed to managing her condition and is interested in learning more about her treatment options. She is fluent in French and willing to participate in a study aimed at improving her knowledge and safety skills related to subcutaneous bDMARDs. She is scheduled to attend a rheumatology appointment and is open to meeting with a pharmacist for an educational interview just before her consultation. She is eager to learn more about her medication and how to manage any potential side effects.

45 yo F with a history of metastatic melanoma to the liver, lungs, and brain. She has previously been treated with Vemurafenib/Cobimetinib and Nivolumab with limited response. MRI showed progression of brain metastases and PET-CT demonstrated new lung lesions. Biopsy confirmed metastatic melanoma. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. She has no history of immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease or organ allograft. The patient has adequate organ function and meets radiographic criteria with measurable lesions in multiple organs. She is willing to use barrier methods of contraception or abstain from heterosexual activity during the study. The patient has been off systemic therapy for melanoma for at least 1 week and all side effects of previous treatments have resolved to grade 1 or better. The patient is willing to undergo hypofractionated palliative radiation therapy to target up to 2 metastases per treated organ separated by more than 5 cm of normal tissue. She has sufficient archival tissue block material and/or newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of tumor tissue. She is able to understand and provide voluntary written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with an aortic aneurysm. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking medications for both conditions. She has never had any surgery before. She is married and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and enjoys gardening and hiking. She is concerned about the risks of surgery and potential complications, particularly related to renal function. She has completed all preoperative testing and has been cleared for surgery. She is scheduled for ascending aorta and aortic arch surgery with use of hypothermic cardiopulmonary bypass and circulatory arrest. She has been advised that she may be randomized to receive either Aprotinin or Amicar during her surgery to reduce bleeding. She is willing to participate in the study and hopes that her participation may help improve outcomes for future patients.

42-year-old male with a history of COVID-19 infection, who has noticed a loss of the sense of smell for the past three months. He has tried different therapies with no improvement. He has no history of sinonasal disease, and his nasal endoscopy and CT scan are normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of NAC nasal spray for the treatment of his anosmia. He has no known sensitivity to NAC or severe asthma.

A 49-year-old Japanese man with a history of liver cirrhosis presented with increasing abdominal distension, fatigue, and decreased urine output. He was diagnosed with hepatorenal syndrome type 1 as his serum creatinine value (SCr) doubled at 2.8 mg/dL within 2 weeks. He has no history of diabetes or hypertension. He is married and works as an office clerk. He is a non-smoker and has a social history of occasional alcohol consumption. His medications include lactulose and spironolactone for hepatic encephalopathy and ascites, respectively. His physical examination showed a distended abdomen with shifting dullness, mild pedal edema, and no signs of encephalopathy. He was started on albumin and diuretics, but his SCr continued to increase, indicating a poor response to therapy. He was deemed eligible for the study and provided consent to participate.

A 45-year-old woman presented with a history of menorrhagia and lower abdominal pain. She was diagnosed with uterine fibroids and advised to undergo an open total abdominal hysterectomy. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, which was well controlled with medication. She was a non-smoker and did not consume alcohol. Her vital signs were within normal limits, and she was physically fit to undergo the surgery. She had no known allergies to medications. She was mentally and physically able to participate in the study and provided fully informed consent after demonstrating a good understanding of the risks and benefits of the TAP. She was not on chronic pain medication and had not received any investigational drug within the past 30 days.

A 27 year old mother just gave birth to her first child and is currently hospitalized at Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on pain management during infant immunizations. She is fluent in English and is rooming with her infant on the postnatal ward. She has no significant psychiatric conditions and is excited to learn more about pain management strategies to help her child during immunizations. She hopes to gain more knowledge and confidence in managing her child's pain during these procedures.

A 43-year-old man was diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma in 2010. He underwent radiation therapy and chemotherapy as a primary treatment, and achieved complete remission. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of other malignancies. He has regular follow-up visits at the clinic and all of his clinical data is available. He has not received any prior radiation therapy to the head and neck region.

This is a 22 year old male university student who is currently enrolled in a full-time program. He has been struggling with his weight for the past year and has a body mass index of 29. He owns a smartphone (Android) and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him become more physically active and lose weight. He does not take any medications and has no significant medical history. He is able and willing to attend four pre-specified visits during the study period. He has not used any activity tracker device in the last three months. He is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve his health and is excited to participate in the study.

Patient is a 35 year old male with a family history of heart disease. He is interested in learning more about his genetic risk for heart disease and has given informed consent for genetic testing. He has no renal replacement dependency, is not pregnant and does not have active cancer disease. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent for both genetic testing and study participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo a minor gynecologic surgery in KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH). She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history other than a history of mild hypertension and asthma, which is well-controlled. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is generally active, but she does not engage in any regular exercise routine. She has never undergone surgery before and is feeling nervous about the upcoming procedure. She is open to non-pharmacological interventions to help manage her pain and anxiety in the perioperative period. She is able to read and understand the hospital anxiety questionnaire and has no hearing impairment. She is classified as an ASA 2.

A 45-year-old male smoker who has been smoking for 30 years with a smoking history of at least 1 pack per day. He is generally in good health with no significant medical history. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He has experienced occasional sinusitis and nasal congestion in the past. He is willing to limit alcohol consumption to no more than 2 drinks per day during the study period. He is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document. He is willing to refrain from using any non-study ASA or NSAIDs during the study period. He is willing to limit use of leukotriene antagonists and glucocorticoids during the study period. He has no history of allergic reaction to aspirin or NSAIDs and no history of gastric intolerance attributable to ASA or NSAIDs. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. He is able to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 55-year-old male veteran presents with chronic low back pain that has been ongoing for over a year. He receives care at the local VA hospital and has been prescribed various pain medications, but has found little relief. He reports difficulty with daily activities such as bending, lifting, and even sitting for extended periods of time. He has also been experiencing fatigue and some symptoms of depression. His BMI is 27 and he does not have any coexisting medical or psychiatric illnesses. He has not practiced yoga before but is willing to attend a yoga program if assigned to the intervention group. He speaks fluent English and is willing to complete 4 assessments throughout the study period. He has not started any new pain treatments or medications in the past month and is willing to not change his pain treatments during the 12-week intervention period unless medically necessary. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

62-year-old postmenopausal female with a history of breast cancer diagnosed 2.5 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant therapy with tamoxifen 20 mg/day. She has been receiving tamoxifen continuously for the past 2 years and 1 month and is still free of disease. Her last mammogram and breast exam were negative for any signs of cancer. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She takes lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, and calcium with vitamin D supplements. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and tolerability of exemestane versus continued tamoxifen for the prevention of breast cancer recurrence.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with obesity based on her body mass index (BMI) of 35. She has a sedentary lifestyle, works long hours sitting at a desk, and often eats fast food due to her busy schedule. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has not been able to maintain a healthy weight. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and wearable technology to promote healthy habits and lifestyle changes. She is tech-friendly and willing to receive feedback through her smartphone, email, and wearable devices. Her past medical history is non-significant, and she does not have any severe psychiatric disturbances or visual difficulties. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the trial and has provided written informed consent to participate.

32-year-old female patient scheduled for surgical removal of impacted third molars at the Discipline of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Traumatology of the Dental School of Araçatuba, São Paulo State University, Brazil. The patient is in good general health and has no systemic disorders, known hypersensitivity to any of the study medications, pregnancy, nursing, or local contraindication to surgery as judged by the oral surgeon. The patient has not used any analgesic agent 24 hours before surgery. The patient has been informed about the study purposes and procedures and has signed an informed consent form prior to enrollment.

Maria is a 45 year old woman who recently underwent ureteroscopy and had a 6/26 ureteral stent placed due to a large kidney stone. She is experiencing moderate to severe discomfort and pain in her lower abdomen and back. She has no history of urinary tract infections or other urogenital disorders. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any liver or kidney dysfunction. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is not currently taking any herbal supplements or participating in any other clinical trials. She is willing to use reliable contraception during the study period. She is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 4-year-old boy is brought in by his mother for a routine check-up. The boy is in good health, has no significant medical history, and is up to date on all immunizations. He is in the 50th percentile for height and weight on the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) growth charts. The boy is able to understand instructions provided during the cognitive testing, and English is the primary language in the home. He has no family history of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). His mother reports that he does not consume more than 3 oz. of fish more than 2 times per week and is not taking any dietary supplements or foods containing or fortified with omega-3 fatty acids. The boy has not received any investigational product within the past 30 days and does not have any medical condition that would preclude a successful response or outcome.

A 10-year-old male patient was diagnosed with a brain tumor located in the occipital lobe. He underwent proton radiation therapy for a total of 6 weeks at the MGH Francis H. Burr Proton Center. The patient received baseline neurocognitive testing at MGH before the radiation therapy. He is currently in the 5th grade and is experiencing some difficulties with reading comprehension and attention during class. The patient's parents report that he is easily distracted and has difficulty focusing on his school work. He does not currently receive any special education services. The patient has no history of radiation exposure or chemotherapy prior to this treatment. He has no known medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the study and have completed the initial questionnaires sent to them through the mail.

45 year-old male with a recent diagnosis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) after presenting with symptoms of persistent nasal congestion, headaches, and hearing loss. Biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated NPC, which was further staged as T3N2M0. He has no prior history of chemotherapy, radiotherapy or immunotherapy for NPC, and he has good organ function (liver, renal, hematologic). Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He is otherwise in good health with no significant comorbidities, and he is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his NPC, and he meets the eligibility criteria for this study.

Mrs. Jackson is a 56 year old woman who underwent colonic resection through laparotomy due to colon cancer. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She also had a hysterectomy 10 years ago. She is currently in the ICU for monitoring and recovery. She has been experiencing postoperative pain and has been using PCA (Patient Controlled Analgesia) as a pain control method. The pain has been interfering with her ability to sleep and eat. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the TAP block can help reduce her pain and opioid use. She has no known allergies to local anesthetics and is able to provide written informed consent. Her lab studies show normal renal and liver function.

A 45-year-old woman who recently underwent a kidney transplant from a cadaveric donor is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has given her written informed consent for the study. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no history of participation in any other studies in the past 3 months. Her physical examination is normal, and her blood test shows normal blood count, creatinine, and BUN levels. She is currently on a cyclosporine-based immunosuppressive regimen along with mycophenolate and prednisone. She will be randomly assigned to either continue her current regimen or switch to a rapamycin-based regimen after one month from her transplant. She will be monitored for the next 2 years with regular visits at 1, 6, 12, and 24 months post-transplant. At each visit, her physical examination, blood pressure, and blood test will be performed, and a blood sample will be collected for evaluation of regulatory T cells.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with heroin addiction for the past 3 years. He has tried to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is currently unemployed and has a history of previous incarceration due to drug-related offenses. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive optimized intervention for his addiction. He is able to take methadone and is motivated to attend psychotherapy sessions. He does not have any physical disabilities that would prevent him from attending the sessions. The patient has no history of schizophrenia or mood disorders.

A 52-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage III breast cancer and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. She has been on chemotherapy for the last 4 weeks and has experienced tingling pain in her hands and feet, which is affecting her daily activities. She has no prior history of diabetic, anatomical or regional neuropathies (except pre-existing CIPN). She is capable of understanding the investigational nature, potential risks, and benefits of the study, and is able to provide valid informed consent. She has no known medical, surgical, or psychiatric condition that may interfere with the conduct of the study or be detrimental to the donor in the opinion of the PI or caring physician. She has agreed to participate in the study and provide a blood sample, information about her symptoms during chemotherapy, and past medical history.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion for the past few months. She also reports occasional palpitations and fatigue. Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a family history of heart disease. She is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. She is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Cardiovascular examination reveals normal heart sounds and no murmurs. Her lungs are clear to auscultation. An electrocardiogram (EKG) shows normal sinus rhythm with no evidence of ischemia. A chest x-ray is normal. Based on her symptoms and medical history, the patient is referred for further evaluation at the Cardiology Branch of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma in both eyes. She reports that she has been experiencing blurry vision and difficulty seeing at night for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine 5mg daily to manage her blood pressure. The patient reports no allergies to medications and has never had any ocular surgeries. She currently uses timolol maleate in both eyes to manage her glaucoma. Her baseline intraocular pressure is 28 mm Hg in the right eye and 26 mm Hg in the left eye. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/30 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye. The patient is willing to discontinue use of all ocular hypotensive medications or switch to another for the purposes of this clinical trial. She is highly motivated to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

64-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and underwent a radical cystectomy with extended pelvic lymph node dissection. Pathologic examination revealed a pT3 tumor stage with the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The patient had <10 lymph nodes removed and no lymph node involvement was found. However, the surgical margin was positive. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and has a good performance status. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of adjuvant external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) to prevent local and lymph node recurrence and improve disease-free and overall survival. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to undergo radiation up to a median dose of 50 Gy in 25 fractions with intensity modulated arc therapy (IMAT) to the pelvic lymph node regions with a simultaneous integrated boost to 64 Gy to the positive lymph nodes if detected.

The patient is a healthy term infant, born at full term and weighing 7 pounds and 6 ounces. The infant was exclusively fed a new infant formula for the first two months of life, as part of the previous phase of the clinical trial NCT04218929 "Evaluation of Growth, Safety, and Efficacy of an Infant Formula for Healthy Term Infants". The infant had no adverse reactions to the formula and had normal growth and development during the first two months of life. The infant is now eligible to participate in the follow-up study to continue to monitor growth, safety, and other health outcomes for an additional two months. The infant's parents have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in this study.

We are looking for individuals between the ages of 50 and 90 who have been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease according to current McKhann et al. criteria. Patients must have a CDR global score of 0.5 or 1, and speak English as their primary language. Participants should have a study partner who is willing to cooperate with the study procedures. We are seeking individuals who have not had medication changes within the past 30 days. Patients cannot reside in a nursing home or dementia special care unit and must be able to control their diet. Participants should not have a serious medical risk, including insulin-requiring diabetes, cancer requiring chemotherapy or radiation within the past 5 years, or a recent cardiac event. Patients should not be participating in another clinical trial or using an investigational drug or therapy within 30 days of the Screening Visit. Individuals with a history of renal stones are excluded from this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with persistent atrial fibrillation for the past year. Despite trying different antiarrhythmic medications, she has not experienced any improvement in her symptoms. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no prior history of cardiac surgeries or procedures. She is currently taking metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. She is willing to undergo either endoscopic ablation or irrigated radiofrequency current ablation to treat her persistent atrial fibrillation. She is compliant with anticoagulation therapy and has no contraindications for the procedure. She is not pregnant and does not have any intracardiac thrombi.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on evaluating the sustainability of a health promotion program for older adults and involves the participation of provincial partners, provincial coordinators, activity coaches, and older adults who have recently completed the Choose to Move program.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with PTSD after being involved in a car accident 6 months ago. She has been experiencing intrusive thoughts, nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance of driving or being in a car since the accident. She has sought treatment from a therapist and has been prescribed medication for anxiety but has not seen significant improvement. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence and is not currently taking any medication other than the prescribed anxiety medication. She has no history of bipolar or psychotic disorder, and her cognitive function is normal. She has no metal implants and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. His body mass index (BMI) is 34 kg/m², and he is a smoker. The patient has a history of heavy drinking in his twenties but has been sober for the past 10 years. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, lethargy, and occasional abdominal pain in the past few months. His primary care physician has ordered a liver biopsy to determine the possible causes of his symptoms. The patient has agreed to participate in the Quantification of Liver Iron Overload and Steatosis Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging study. The patient has no history of heart or respiratory issues and has no contraindication to MR imaging. The patient has provided written informed consent for the study.

45-year-old male diagnosed with non-keratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) 2 years ago. The patient has received two prior lines of chemotherapy containing platinum drugs such as Cisplatin and Carboplatin. The NPC has recurred at locoregional and distant sites and is not amenable to potentially curative radiotherapy or surgery. The patient has adequate organ reserve with neutrophils >1.5x109/L, platelets ≥100 x109/L, hemoglobin ≥9 g/dL, serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) < 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) and serum bilirubin < 2.5 x ULN. The patient has measurable disease as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST ver 1.1). The patient has not received chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or investigational treatment within 4 weeks of enrollment. The patient does not have diabetes or risk for hyperglycemia. The patient does not have a baseline QTcF > 450 msec (male) or QTcF >470 msec (female) or other cardiovascular issues. The patient is willing to give written informed consent.

This is a 57 year-old female who was diagnosed with CLL last year. She has had previous treatment for CLL and is currently experiencing progressive disease with symptomatic CLL, including drenching night sweats and extreme fatigue. She has a minimum threshold peripheral lymphocyte count of > 5 x 10^9/L and immunophenotypic demonstrations of a population of B lymphocytes (as defined by CD19+) which are monoclonal. She has been screened for CD52 expression by CLL cells and is willing to provide mandatory biospecimen samples for research studies as required by the protocol. Her ECOG Performance Status is 1 and she has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to employ adequate contraception during the study. She does not have any major comorbid conditions such as heart disease, recent myocardial infarction, active infection with HIV/AIDS or hepatitis B/C, or active autoimmune hemolytic anemia, immune thrombocytopenia, or pure red blood cell aplasia. She has not had any major surgery in the past 4 weeks and is not receiving concurrent investigational drug therapy. She is not currently using any of the following CYP3A4 strong inhibitors: Clarithromycin, Nefazodone, Telithromycin, Aprepitant, Indinavir, Nelfinavir, Diltiazem, Borisonazole, Itrazonazole, Ritonavir, Erythromycin, Ketoconazole, Saquinavir, or Fluconazole. She does not have a known bleeding diathesis and does not have severely impaired lung function. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is eligible to participate.

A 42-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has a history of smoking but quit after her diagnosis. The patient reports feeling fatigued and experiencing pain in her left breast and underarm. She has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past two months and has noticed a decrease in her overall quality of life. The patient is interested in participating in an activity program to help improve her physical and emotional well-being. She has clearance from her doctor to participate in the program. The patient resides in West Philadelphia and is excited to have the opportunity to engage in activities and socialize with other women who have experienced similar difficulties.

The patient is a 56 year old man who has been experiencing chest discomfort and shortness of breath during physical activity for the past few months. He was diagnosed with stable angina pectoris and has been prescribed aspirin and clopidogrel for secondary prevention. He is a smoker and has a history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is currently well-controlled with medications. He is overweight with a BMI of 29 and admits to a sedentary lifestyle. He works as an office manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has no history of bleeding disorders or recent major surgeries. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve his own health outcomes and contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past month. He is a smoker with a 30-pack-year history of smoking. He has a history of hypertension but it is well-controlled with medication. A chest X-ray revealed a small lesion in his left lung. Further examination showed that the lesion was a ground-glass opacity (GGO) measuring 2cm in diameter with GGO of 30%. Biopsy results confirmed the lesion as minimally-invasive adenocarcinoma. The patient was offered both sublobar resection and lobectomy.

54 year old woman with a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 3 years. She has been on various medications including methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine with little improvement in her symptoms. Her physician has decided to begin treatment with infliximab and has explained the potential benefits and risks of the treatment to the patient. The patient has consented to the treatment and has signed the informed consent form. She has not been previously exposed to infliximab. She reports joint pain and stiffness, particularly in her hands and feet, which has limited her ability to perform daily activities. She also reports fatigue and occasional fevers. She is interested in participating in this study to learn more about her disease characteristics and potentially improve her treatment outcomes.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and has undergone chemotherapy treatment. She is experiencing symptoms of genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) including dryness, irritation, and dyspareunia. On examination, clinical findings of vaginal atrophy are present, including thin, dry, and pale vaginal tissue. She has not had a menstrual period in over a year and has had a normal Pap smear within the last three years. She is not currently using any topical estrogen treatments and has not had any previous vulvar, vaginal, or cervical dysplasia or cancer. The patient is interested in exploring non-hormonal treatment options for her GSM symptoms.

A 25-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a persistent cough, fever, and night sweats. She works as a teacher and has had no prior diagnosis of HIV or TB. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently not taking any medication but takes daily multivitamins. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of mental illness or drug use.

This is a 25-year-old female who suffered a spinal cord injury (SCI) due to a motor vehicle accident. She is currently admitted to the acute inpatient rehabilitation (AIR) facility and has been diagnosed with non-progressive SCI. She has a good upper extremity strength and is able to manage walking aid (front-wheeled walker, platform walker or crutches). She is able to follow directions and has no skin integrity issues in areas that would contact the device, or that would likely be made worse by device use. She does not have any uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions, orthostatic hypotension, or any form of progressive SCI as defined by the physician. She is fluent in English and is able to give informed consent for the clinical trial. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who suffered a lacunar stroke 3 months ago. He has been experiencing difficulties with his memory and focus, as well as some mild weakness on his left side. He has been diagnosed with small vessel disease and has white matter hyperintensities on his MRI. He takes aspirin and atorvastatin daily. He does not have any other significant medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. He has a useable TCD window to record MCA waveform on at least one side. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not a woman of childbearing age not taking contraception. He is not suffering from any major neurological or psychiatric conditions interfering with the study design. He does not have any other causes of stroke such as luminal stenosis, cardioembolic source of embolism, or other specific causes of stroke. He does not have large vessel occlusion on MRA or CTA. He has a Modified Rankin Score of 2. He is able to swallow and does not have renal impairment or significant biochemical abnormalities. He has a life expectancy of over 2 years. He does not have any contraindications to active agents and is not using an alphablocker or regular use of nitrate. He does not have heart failure or severe aortic stenosis. He is not suffering from any uncontrolled arrhythmias or previous priapism. He does not have any anatomical deformation of the penis, recent myocardial infarction, or unstable angina. He has not had non-arteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy in the past. His blood pressure is not below 90/60 and he does not have any haemodynamically significant aortic/mitral valve disease. He does not have sickle cell disease, myeloma, leukaemia, or uncontrolled hypertension. He has not participated in another research study involving an investigational product in the past 12 weeks and is not using an anticoagulant. He does not have a predisposition to intracerebral haemorrhage or intraocular haemorrhage. He is not allergic to constituents of medications or components of placebo/overencapsulation. He is not using CYP inducers that interact with study medications. He is able to transfer to the MRI scanner, does not have an active respiratory illness, and is not claustrophobic or have any contraindication to MRI scan.

The patient is a 55-year-old former smoker who quit smoking 3 years ago after smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the last 20 years. He has a history of moderate COPD with cough and sputum production for at least 3 months in each of the last 2 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing frequently with mucus production. He has been using a short-acting bronchodilator as his rescue medication for the last 2 years. He works as a construction worker and has difficulty performing his job due to his symptoms. He has a CAT score of 15 at screening and randomization visit. He has no history of asthma or angina. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is currently not taking any medication that is prohibited by the protocol. He is interested in participating in the study and has given his written consent after understanding the purpose and nature of the investigation.

A 13-year-old adolescent is experiencing nasal congestion due to rhinitis. The symptoms have been present for a week and are causing discomfort, difficulty sleeping and difficulty breathing through the nose. The adolescent has no history of allergies or other medical conditions. The adolescent's mother is supportive of the study and willing to ensure that the protocol is followed. The adolescent has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past year. The adolescent has not used any intranasal corticosteroids or systemic medications within the appropriate time frame. The adolescent is a non-smoker and does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse.

A 54-year-old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss of 10 pounds in the last month. She also reports feeling fatigued and experiencing loss of appetite. She has a history of smoking and has a family history of pancreatic cancer. A CT scan confirms the presence of metastatic disease in the pancreas. Biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma. She has not received any prior treatment for her metastatic disease except for immunotherapy. She has a performance status of ECOG 1 and meets all the other eligibility criteria for the clinical trial. She is willing to participate in the study and is interested in exploring treatment options to manage her condition.

A 64-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with ischemic heart disease based on her ECG and echocardiogram findings. She is currently on metformin and glipizide for her diabetes and simvastatin for her hypercholesterolemia. Her blood glucose levels are well-controlled with an HbA1c level of 6.5%. Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and her BMI is 28. She reports occasional numbness in her feet and legs but denies any other symptoms of peripheral arterial disease. She has no history of stroke, DVT or pulmonary embolism. She has undergone an angiogram, which revealed stenosis of two coronary arteries. She underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent placement for the stenotic lesions. Following the procedure, she has been advised to attend the cardio-metabolic clinic at the Heart Hospital for optimal metabolic and hemodynamic control. She has consented to participate in the Qatar Cardiometabolic Registry and has agreed to allow her clinical information to be added to the registry database.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when he was 6 years old. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his cancer has relapsed and is now refractory to treatment. His parents are interested in exploring alternative treatment options and are willing to participate in a clinical trial. The patient has measurable disease on CT scans and has a Karnofsky performance status score of 80. He has fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of his previous treatments and has normal organ function. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study and agree to use an effective contraceptive method for the duration of study therapy and for 3 months after the last dose of GD2Bi-aATC. The patient is not pregnant or breast-feeding and does not have an uncontrolled infection. The patient is eligible to participate in the phase II expansion cohort of the study.

75-year-old female with a history of osteoporosis, diagnosed with moderate kyphosis, and a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She lives independently in the community and is able to perform activities of daily living with some difficulty due to her kyphosis. The patient reports occasional back pain and has not had any recent fractures. She is able to follow simple commands and is willing to participate in the study. The patient does not have any other medical conditions that would affect her participation in the study.

32-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a new influenza vaccine. She has not received any influenza vaccination within the past 6 months and is willing to follow study procedures. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using appropriate contraceptive methods. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m² and is reliable and willing to make herself available for the duration of the study. She does not have any known infectious diseases or immunodeficient conditions, and has not received any investigational or non-registered drug or vaccine within the past 3 months. She is a non-smoker and does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is willing to complete an e-diary and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial.

35 yo F with a history of chronic headaches for the past 3 years. She reports having at least 2 headaches per week, which last for several hours and are often accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried various over-the-counter pain medications and prescription drugs, but they only provide temporary relief. She has not tried acupuncture before and is interested in exploring it as a treatment option. Past Medical History: - Migraine headaches - History of anxiety and depression, treated with medication - Allergies to penicillin and sulfa medications.

A 54-year-old Caucasian male presents with lumbar radicular pain due to spinal canal stenosis causing neuropathic pain. He reports pain in his lower back and left leg that is sharp, shooting, and burning in nature. The pain is present most of the day and has been ongoing for the past year. He has tried physical therapy, chiropractic care, and over-the-counter pain medications, but none have provided significant relief. He does not have a history of diabetes or alcohol/drug abuse. He has no significant psychiatric history and is not on any antidepressants. He does not have fibromyalgia or chronic fatigue syndrome. He is married and works as a carpenter. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies to medications. His current pain score on a 0-10 scale is 8.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been struggling with cocaine addiction for the past two years. She has tried multiple forms of treatment, including therapy and medication, but has not been able to maintain long-term abstinence. She is currently not using cocaine but reports significant cravings and triggers that make it difficult for her to stay sober. She has no history of brain trauma or organic brain disease. She is willing to participate in the study and is looking for new methods to help her overcome her addiction. She does not have any metallic cerebral implants or severe somatic disease. She has not been diagnosed with any other psychiatric disorder.

This is a 42-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus who has been taking insulin for the past year due to inadequate control of her blood sugar levels with oral medications. She owns and is able to operate an iPhone. She has been struggling with maintaining consistent blood glucose levels and has experienced occasional hypoglycemic events. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will assess the effectiveness of a mobile phone telemedicine intervention in managing her diabetes. She is willing to attend an initial/baseline visit and a three-month clinical visit at the Diabetes Center.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a benign ovarian cyst and requires laparoscopic surgery. She has a history of motion sickness and has experienced nausea after previous surgeries. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She does not smoke and does not have any known allergies. Her BMI is within the normal range. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the importance of strict adherence to PONV guidelines for her recovery.

Pt is a 50yo Japanese male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 2 years. He has been on an oral antidiabetic drug (OAD) monotherapy with a stable daily dose of a sulphonylurea (SU) for the past 6 months. His HbA1c (glycosylated haemoglobin) is 8.5% (69 mmol/mol). He has never been treated with once-weekly glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) or once weekly dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor. He has no history of pancreatitis, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) within the past 180 days prior to the day of screening and randomisation. He has no family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN 2) or medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). He has no history of major surgical procedures involving the stomach potentially affecting absorption of trial product. He has no proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy requiring acute treatment. He is willing and able to sign written informed consent. He is available for follow-up visits and is compliant with the protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who recently suffered a deep laceration on his upper thigh while working with power tools. The wound became infected and, despite treatment with antibiotics, it has not fully healed. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgical debridement of the wound followed by VAC therapy. The healthcare provider will take samples of the wound prior to debridement, immediately following initial debridement, after 2 days of VAC veraflo therapy, and at the time of repeat operative debridements, if needed. The goal of the study is to compare the microbiologic burden and need for further operative debridement of patients undergoing primary surgical debridement of infected tissue, soft tissue abscesses, or traumatic wounds of the upper and lower extremity. The patient will be monitored for the number of operative debridements required prior to reconstruction, number of days until final reconstruction, number of days until decision is made by surgeon that further debridements are no longer necessary, length of hospital stay, and wound surface area from enrollment through when the veraflo is removed. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 42-year-old female physician who has been smoking for the past 15 years is motivated to quit smoking. She smokes about 20 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking several times in the past but without success. She is currently in good health and not taking any medication. She has no history of any major metabolic disease, renal or hepatic disease. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has a normal dental status and chewing ability. After 15 smoke-free minutes, her carbon monoxide level is 12 parts per million (ppm). She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other trial procedures. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not participating in any other clinical trials. She has personally signed and dated the informed consent form indicating that she has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the trial. She is interested in using Nicorette® gum 2 mg or Nicorette® patch 5 mg/16 h to assist her in quitting smoking. She is open to receiving brief telephone consultation and SMS as behavioral supports during the study.

Pt is a 9yo M scheduled for a tonsillectomy under general anesthesia with LMA flexible. The patient has no significant past medical history and is generally healthy. The patient's vital signs are stable with no significant arrhythmia or hypotension. The patient has no facial deformity and is not at high risk of aspiration. The patient has no recent history of upper respiratory tract infection. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible to participate.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a lump in her left breast that was discovered during a routine mammogram. Biopsy results showed invasive ductal carcinoma, which is estrogen receptor positive, and the tumor size is 1.8 cm. The patient has no family history of breast cancer and is in good health otherwise. She has not undergone any neo-adjuvant treatment, radiotherapy, chemotherapy or hormone therapy. The gland exeresis margins are ≥ 2 mm, and there is no inflammatory breast cancer, associated peri-tumoral lymphatic emboli or extensive intra-ductal component, invasive lobular carcinoma, pure ductal carcinoma in situ, sarcoma, or lymphoma-type non-epithelial tumor. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergoes a combination extended tumorectomy with axillary dissection (sentinel lymph node) in addition to 20 Gy of per-operative partial irradiation at the tumor site. She will be followed up for 5 years after the treatment.

As this is an observation only study involving participants already enrolled in the CHAT trial, no patient description is required. Participants will be selected based on their eligibility as outlined in the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

As this is a clinical trial focused on organ donation, no specific patient description can be generated. Patients are not directly involved in this trial, but rather organ donors and lung transplant recipients. The trial is focused on testing the effectiveness of nebulized albuterol in reducing pulmonary edema and improving donor oxygenation in brain dead organ donors, as well as developing a blood test to predict primary graft dysfunction in lung transplant recipients. Therefore, the eligibility criteria for this trial is limited to brain dead individuals above the age of 14 who have consented to lung donation and donor research, and have been released by the coroner or medical examiner.

45-year-old male with a history of liver cirrhosis due to alcohol abuse presents to the hospital with fever, chills, and abdominal pain. Blood cultures confirm a diagnosis of invasive candidiasis, with Candida albicans identified in the bloodstream. The patient has no known allergies, is not currently taking any medications, and has no history of abnormal blood clotting. The patient is currently hospitalized and is being treated with standard dosing of an antifungal drug. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a higher-dose regimen of the same antifungal drug.

Patient is a 28-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with active Crohn's disease. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past 6 months. He has not received any treatment for Crohn's disease before and has not been on any medications for the past 6 months. His Crohn's disease activity index score is between 220 and 450 points. He has no known allergies to any medications.

A 35-year-old healthy male presents for a clinical trial investigating the recovery, excretion, and pharmacokinetics of [14C]-GSK2140944 administered as a single intravenous (IV) dose (Period 1) and a single oral dose (Period 2). The patient has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He has a body weight of 75 kilograms and a BMI of 25. He has no history of liver disease, alcohol consumption, or sensitivity to heparin, quinolones, or any of the study medications. His urinalysis is negative for protein and glucose, and his serum creatinine value is within normal limits. He has not used tobacco or nicotine-containing products for the past 6 months and has a negative drug/alcohol screen. His ECG is normal with no evidence of previous myocardial infarction or conduction abnormality. The patient is willing to commit to avoiding excessive exposure to sunlight from the first dose up to and including discharge. The patient has given written informed consent and agrees to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

The patient is a 24-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the ketogenic potential of different dietary supplements. She reports no significant medical history, no use of tobacco or recreational drugs, and no regular use of medications. She has had no recent illnesses or infections and does not have a history of diabetes or prediabetes. She has normal blood pressure and thyroid function. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 47-year-old male diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) with persistent or recurrent molecular residual disease (MRD) after at least one year of tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. He has been on TKI therapy for at least 6 months prior to enrollment, and at minimum goal doses of Imatinib 300mg PO daily, Dasatinib 70mg PO daily, Nilotinib 200mg PO BID, Bosutinib 300mg PO daily, or Ponatinib 30mg PO daily. His BCR-ABL transcripts measured by RT-PCR at a CLIA-approved laboratory show a value of >0.01% within 28 days prior to study enrollment. He has been diagnosed with non-blast phase CML by standard definition, with a confirmed presence of the Philadelphia chromosome or variants of the (9;22) translocation by cytogenetics, FISH or with a positive RT-PCR for BCR-ABL. His performance status is ECOG PS 0, 1, or 2. He is a woman of childbearing potential and is willing to use 2 highly effective methods of contraception while receiving study treatment and for an additional 3 months after the last dose of protocol-specified therapy. Male who has a female partner of childbearing potential, and is willing to use 2 highly effective forms of contraception for at least an additional 3 months after the last dose of protocol-specified therapy. He has not been on other investigational agents for CML within 4 weeks of study enrollment, and has a platelet count of ≥50,000/mm3, ANC ≥500/mm3, and hemoglobin ≥ 7.5 g.dL. He does not have abnormal screening laboratory values as defined in the exclusion criteria. He has not been diagnosed with other major medical or psychiatric illnesses, which the treating physician feels, could seriously compromise tolerance or compliance to this protocol. He has not been diagnosed with prior immunodeficiency or organ transplant requiring immunosuppressive therapy, and does not have any of the following in the previous 6 months: myocardial infarction, severe/unstable angina, coronary/peripheral artery bypass graft, symptomatic congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular accident, transient ischemic attack, deep vein thrombosis, or symptomatic pulmonary embolism. He does not have known prior or suspected hypersensitivity to study drugs or any component in their formulations, and does not have active autoimmune disease that might deteriorate when receiving an immunostimulatory agent. He has not been diagnosed with any other malignancy within 3 years, except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, carcinoma in situ of the breast or of the cervix, low grade prostate cancer on surveillance without any plans for treatment intervention, or prostate cancer that has been adequately treated with prostatectomy or radiotherapy and currently with no evidence of disease or symptoms. He is not currently on immunosuppressive medications at the time of study enrollment and within 2 weeks of any study treatments, except for intranasal, inhaled, topical steroids, or local steroid injection, or systemic corticosteroids at physiologic doses ≤10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent, or steroids as premedication for hypersensitivity reactions at physiologic doses ≤10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who works as an administrative assistant at a local government office in a rural county in Southwest Georgia. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 6 years and has been struggling to manage her blood glucose levels with her current medication regimen. She has reported feeling overwhelmed and frustrated with her condition and is interested in finding new ways to manage her diabetes. The patient is interested in participating in a program that will help her better manage her chronic disease and improve her overall health. She reports that she is physically active, but struggles with maintaining a healthy diet and managing stress. She is willing to participate in a six-week program that is designed to help individuals better manage their chronic disease and its many complications. She hopes that this program will provide her with the knowledge and tools to better manage her diabetes and improve her quality of life. The patient is excited to participate in this clinical trial and looks forward to the potential benefits it may provide.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing pelvic organ prolapse symptoms, including a vaginal bulge, for the past year. She has previously attempted conservative management with pelvic floor exercises and pessary, but with no significant improvement. She has no significant medical history, is not on any medication, and has not had any pelvic surgery in the past. Pelvic examination reveals stage III prolapse on the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification System Assessment (POP-Q). The patient desires surgical intervention and is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia 5 years ago. He has undergone several treatments, but the disease has relapsed and is refractory to treatment. He experiences fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His previous treatment included chemotherapy and monoclonal antibodies. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. His bone marrow function, renal function, and hepatic function are adequate. He has measurable disease by CT scan. He has no history of prolymphocytic leukemia or Richter's transformation. He has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease, no history of stroke or intracranial hemorrhage, and no severe or debilitating pulmonary disease. He has no active fungal, bacterial, or viral infection requiring systemic therapy. He has no known central nervous system involvement by leukemia or lymphoma, no history of severe bleeding disorder or spontaneous bleeding requiring blood transfusion or other medical intervention. He has no moderate or severe hepatic impairment. He has not undergone major surgery within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug. He has not received prior treatment with a BTK inhibitor. He has not recently been vaccinated with a live vaccine. He is not pregnant or lactating. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meet all other inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been on chronic hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to end-stage renal disease. He has a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2, and hyperlipidemia. He has been compliant with his hemodialysis and medications. He reports a decreased appetite and has lost some weight over the past few months. His serum albumin level is 3.2 g/dL, and his daily protein intake is around 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight.
