He is interested in participating in the study to improve his nutritional status and learn more about the impact of different protein diets in hemodialysis patients. He is able to comply with the diet plan and is willing to follow the study protocol. He is not suffering from any active infections or severe illnesses. He is married and lives with his wife. He has two children who are currently studying abroad. He works as an office clerk and enjoys reading and gardening in his free time. His BMI is 26, and his blood pressure is well controlled at 130/80 mmHg. There is nothing remarkable in his physical exam.

25-year-old female who is HIV+ and currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. She resides in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and plans to exclusively breastfeed her infant. She has no known allergies to any of the components of the protein-calorie supplementation (PCS) or the micronutrient supplement (MNS) being studied. The patient has not been diagnosed with any other high risk pregnancy conditions such as diabetes or pre-eclampsia. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of doing so. She is committed to complying with the study protocol and will remain in Dar es Salaam for the duration of breastfeeding. The patient hopes that by participating in this study, she can improve the health outcomes for herself and her infant.

The patient is a 68-year-old French-speaking woman who was recently diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment. She has completed at least a Junior Secondary School Diploma and has no difficulty with vision. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disease, alcoholism or brain injury. She has not been prescribed any psychotropic medication in the past week. She is affiliated with social insurance and is able to sign the informed consent form. She will be participating in the study's control group of individuals without Alzheimer's disease or related disorders.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with carcinoma of the urothelium. He underwent a transurethral resection of the bladder tumor, which revealed lymphovascular invasion. The staging CT scan showed no evidence of disease outside the pelvis. The patient has no significant medical history and his performance status is 1. His lab results show: Creatinine clearance: 60 mL/min Hemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL Platelets: 224,000 /mm3 Total bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL AST: 22 U/L ALT: 28 U/L Alkaline phosphatase: 70 U/L His ECG and echocardiogram show an ejection fraction of 55%. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by cystectomy.

A 25-year-old male university student who has been using synthetic psychoactive cannabinoids for the past 6 months. He is otherwise healthy and has completed his bachelor's degree in computer science. He is able to provide written consent for the study. He has no history of claustrophobia or metal implants that would exclude him from undergoing an MRI.

The patient is a 75 year old woman with a diagnosis of dementia established by her primary care physician. She lives at home with her husband who is her primary caregiver. Her husband speaks English and has a phone. She has a primary care provider who is willing to partner with the study. She is not currently enrolled in hospice and does not plan to move out of the area within the coming year. Her husband is willing and capable of providing self-reported outcome measures for 18 months. She is not currently participating in another dementia intervention study.

A 58-year-old male patient with a history of diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years presents with a non-healing foot wound that has been present for the past 6 months. The wound is located on the plantar surface of the left foot and measures approximately 2 cm in diameter. The patient reports intermittent pain and a foul odor emanating from the wound. He has been treated with various topical ointments and antibiotics, but the wound has not shown any significant improvement. The patient has no history of peripheral arterial disease but has a history of hypertension which is well controlled with medication. The patient is otherwise in good health and is able to perform his activities of daily living independently. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the use of 3% Sodium pentaborate pentahydrate hydrogel for wound treatment.

25-year-old female with a medical diagnosis of asthma and a history of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. The patient currently uses an albuterol inhaler as needed for symptom relief, and has had no recent exacerbations or respiratory infections. The patient does not smoke and is not pregnant. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent and understands the study instructions. The patient's baseline FEV1 is above 70% predicted. The patient has no history of anaphylaxis, cardiovascular disease, or injuries that would prevent exercise on a cycle ergometer. The patient is not currently taking oral corticosteroids and has no history of blood borne disease. The patient will be able to attend four study visits at the Brunel University London campus, Uxbridge.

Patient is a 25-year-old, sexually active, English-speaking female who is HIV-negative and has been receiving healthcare services at the Delgado Personal Health Center. The patient has been previously diagnosed with Trichomonas vaginalis (TV) infection and has received treatment for the same. The patient has been asymptomatic for the last 2 weeks and is willing to participate in a study aimed to determine the duration of time for TV DNA to clear from the vaginal cavity post-treatment. The patient has no history of any other sexually transmitted infection or any chronic medical condition. The patient has consented to participate in the study and will be screened weekly using culture and Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) to determine how long TV DNA is detectable post-treatment. The patient will also be examined for potential confounders to clearance such as bacterial vaginosis. The outcome of interest will be a negative PCR result indicating that TV DNA has cleared.

A 30-year-old female with a diagnosis of Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) according to the McDonald criteria and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) of 2.5 is seeking to participate in this clinical trial. She has a history of occasional fatigue and muscle weakness, but overall has been managing her symptoms well with the use of disease modifying therapies. She is interested in participating in an exercise intervention to improve her overall health and potentially reduce her risk for cardiovascular disease. She has no other significant medical history or current comorbidities. She is an active individual and regularly engages in low to moderate intensity exercise, but has not yet attempted high intensity interval training. She is able to provide written informed consent and is available for the complete study course.

45-year-old male with a history of Bell's palsy diagnosed 2 years ago. He reports a sudden onset of left-sided facial paralysis that progressively worsened in the first few days. He has been treated with corticosteroids and antiviral medications without significant improvement. The patient reports social and psychological distress due to the facial asymmetry and inability to control his facial expressions. He is motivated to participate in the study to potentially improve his facial function. Past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. No history of malignancy or severe neurological diseases. The patient is willing to participate and provide informed consent.

A 40-year-old female with a diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma in her right breast is scheduled for a unilateral breast surgery. She has no history of local anesthetic allergy or chronic pain. Her body mass index is within normal limits, and she has no history of severe organ failure, neurological deficits, or psychiatric diseases. She is classified as ASA II and is between the ages of 18-65 years. She has provided approval for the study and is not pregnant.

A 57-year-old male patient was diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled for oncological inpatient rehabilitation at the Rehabilitation Center Walenstadtberg. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He is fluent in German and has signed the informed consent form. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He reports feeling fatigue and has difficulty with mobility due to the cancer treatment. His MMSE score is 25, and his HADS score is 6 at the baseline.

A 31-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetic interactions of telmisartan and chlorthalidone. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medication currently. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of significant illnesses or drug/alcohol abuse. He smokes 3-4 cigarettes per day. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to medical research and is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

Pt is a 45yo F with a history of ER/PR negative, HER2/neu positive (3+ by IHC) invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast diagnosed 4 years ago. She underwent left breast lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (AC) followed by paclitaxel and concurrent trastuzumab. She received adjuvant radiation therapy to the left breast and chest wall. She has been on trastuzumab every 3 weeks since the end of her chemotherapy. Despite her therapy, she developed liver and bone metastases a year ago and has been on letrozole 2.5 mg daily for the past 6 months. However, she continues to have bone pain despite this treatment. She presents with worsening bone pain and increasing serum alkaline phosphatase level. Imaging studies reveal progression of the bone metastases with new liver involvement. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has never had oxaliplatin, and her LVEF is normal.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who lives in an urban area with her parents. She has been diagnosed with asthma and has had two or more visits to any combination of the outpatient, ED or hospital setting in the past year for asthma exacerbations at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP). She and her parents have a smartphone and the patient has been prescribed an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) medication for daily use. The parents are willing to participate in a six-month intervention with a six-month follow-up period to improve the patient's adherence to the ICS medication. The study intervention will include daily automated medication reminders (either via text message or push reminder) and an app to track daily medication use. The patient will also receive nominal incentives to promote daily controller use. The researchers will affix electronic monitors to the inhalers to measure inhaled controller medication adherence and rescue medication use. During the study, the patient and her parents will be asked to complete surveys to assess factors associated with differential adherence. The efficacy outcomes will include change in parent-reported asthma control and mean adherence to ICS between study arms during the experiment interval and the observation interval. The patient will be considered enrolled when she fulfills the requirements of the Run-in period (sensor data uploaded to research platform AND text message receipt confirmed by caregiver) and is subsequently randomized.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl with a history of premature birth at 30 weeks gestation. She was born weighing 2.2 pounds and spent 8 weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. She attends preschool and is able to communicate effectively with her peers and adults. Her parents have given their informed consent for her to participate in the study. There is no history of neurodevelopmental disorders in her family. The child will undergo behavioral evaluations as a part of the study.

A 62-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. His current medications include metformin and glipizide, but his HbA1c levels are still not well controlled. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m² and has been stable at this weight for the past 6 months. He has no history of severe hypoglycemia or other major diabetes-related complications. He had a colonoscopy 2 years ago, which was normal. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and walking for exercise. He is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

60-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer, recently underwent chemotherapy and radiation treatment. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He currently experiences fatigue and shortness of breath and is required to use a supplemental oxygen tank. He lives with his wife who acts as his primary caregiver and surrogate decision-maker. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident, transient ischemic attack (TIA), seizure disorder, dementia or traumatic head injury with loss of consciousness. He is fluent in English and able to read a computer screen without difficulty. He is willing to participate in the study and his wife is also willing to enroll as his surrogate.

A 28 year old female patient presents to the clinic for an upcoming elective diagnostic gynecological laparoscopic surgery. She has a medical history of mild asthma but is otherwise healthy. She reports no allergies to medications and is not taking any medications currently. She has never had any cardiac, diabetes mellitus, thyroid or endocrine diseases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent brad arrhythmia induced by repeated succinylcholine during the surgery. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is willing to be randomly assigned into one of the groups to receive either atropine sulfate or normal saline solution. She is fully informed about the study and provides consent to participate.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who has been experiencing frequent upper respiratory infections, with more than four infections per year for the past 2 years. He lives in a crowded home with six other family members and has been exposed to other family members who have had upper respiratory infections. He is otherwise in good general health and has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. The patient has not used any nicotine or nicotine-containing products for the past year and has tested negative for drugs of abuse and alcohol. He has no history of significant medical or surgical problems, and his laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has been fully informed of the nature of the study. He has read, signed, and dated an IRB-approved informed consent/assent form for subjects to participate in the study.

The patient is a 46-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 7 years. Despite being on methotrexate for the past 6 months, the patient is still experiencing moderate to severe active symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis including joint pain, stiffness, and swelling. The patient has not received any prior treatment with tumor necrosis factor (TNF) antagonists or any other monoclonal antibody therapies. The patient has no positive history of other rheumatic autoimmune disease and inflammatory joint disease other than rheumatoid arthritis. The patient has not been pregnant or lactating in the past year and has no plans to get pregnant during the course of the study. The patient has no history of allergic reactions or intolerance to rituximab, MabionCD20, or any of their components. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with no history of significant medical problems. She is interested in improving the appearance of her skin and has noticed a decrease in skin elasticity and firmness, particularly in her facial area. She has not undergone any facial resurfacing or injectable filler treatments in the past 6 months and does not plan to do so during the study period. She is willing to use the study cream as directed and attend all study visits. She has normal skin sensitivity and no known allergies to any of the ingredients in the study cream.

A 42-year-old female with a history of ileostomy for more than a year visited the clinic to participate in a clinical trial investigating the impact of a newly developed adhesive on peristomal skin. The patient has intact skin on the area used in the evaluation and the ileostomy has a diameter up to 35mm. She has given her written informed consent and has full legal capacity. The investigating scientist has assessed that the patient has a peristomal area accessible for application of patches/adhesive strips. The patient is not receiving or has not received radio- and/or chemotherapy within the past 2 months, nor has she received topical steroid treatment in the peristomal skin area or systemic steroid (tablet/injection) treatment within the past month. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any dermatological problems in the peristomal or abdominal area, as assessed by the investigating scientist. The patient is not participating in any other interventional clinical investigations nor has she previously participated in this evaluation.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no history of gynecological or reproductive disorders. Her partner has a normal semen analysis. The patient has undergone initial fertility workup, which revealed no abnormalities. She has been advised to undergo IVF/ICSI treatment in order to achieve a pregnancy. The patient has more than 10 follicles with a diameter of ≥10 mm the day before the follicular puncture, and is therefore eligible to participate in the study. She does not have a history of preimplantation genetic diagnosis treatments, which is an exclusion criterion for this study.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is in overall good health. His complete blood count, hepatic function, and renal function are all within normal limits. He has not received previous radiotherapy and has no history of any other type of malignancy. He is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any allergies to S-1. He does not have any obvious dysfunction of liver, renal, cardiac, or lung function and has no uncontrolled infection. He does not have systemic or distant metastasis and does not have severe gastrointestinal diseases or mental disorders that would affect patient participation in the trial. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) combined with S-1 concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for his condition.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman from the United States who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is married and has two children. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of breast cancer. She has undergone a mammogram, ultrasound, and core biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of breast cancer. She is scheduled for breast-conserving surgery, and her physician has recommended that she participate in this study to evaluate the role of high-resolution positron emission mammography (PEM) imaging and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in pre-surgical planning. She has no contraindications to breast MRI and has never had a breast implant. She understands the study requirements and has signed the study-specific consent form. She has agreed to undergo follow-up MRI or PEM at 6 months if needed based on the results of the MRI or PEM examination.

13-year-old male with a history of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) diagnosed by a pediatric gastroenterologist based on laboratory/radiological studies and gastrointestinal histology. The patient is currently on a stable dose of sulfasalazine for the treatment of IBD and is in remission with a PUCAI score of 24. The patient has been compliant with medication for the past 3 months and is able to swallow study medication. The patient has not experienced an increased gastrointestinal symptom in the last 3 months. The patient and their parent/guardian are able to attend study visits at screening, baseline, and weeks three, six, and nine. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or planned surgery during potential study participation time. The patient is not currently using any excluded medications or treatments and has no other serious medical conditions.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with no history of chronic pain conditions. She is currently not using any pain medications, including opioids, NSAIDs, or acetaminophen. She is medically healthy with no neurological or medical disorders that may affect brain function. She has no comorbid DSM-V diagnosis of alcohol or substance abuse in the prior three months. She is willing to commit to the study protocol and able to provide written informed consent. She has no history of suicidal or homicidal ideation. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use reliable means of contraception. She has an adequate comprehension of English to complete the study materials. She has not tested positive on a urine toxicology test for any substance, including CBD. She has no current acute or chronic pain conditions. She has not detected any abnormal liver function tests or CBC.

The patient is a 65-year-old female who recently completed chemoradiation treatment for stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. She is experiencing difficulty swallowing and requires tube feeding for the last 4 months. She has been diagnosed with pharyngeal phase dysphagia, incomplete UES opening, and post-deglutitive aspiration. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She is otherwise healthy and able to comply with the protocol mandates, willing to perform the exercise programs, and attend study sessions. The patient has no history of cervical spine injury, neuromuscular disorders, or other medical conditions that would exclude her from participation in the study. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to return to oral feeding soon.

A 35-year-old male presented to the urology clinic with complaints of pain in the lower abdomen, perineum, and suprapubic area for the past 6 months. The pain gets worse during and after urination and ejaculation. The patient reports frequent urination, urinary urgency, and nocturia. He has no history of sexually transmitted infections. He denies any history of hematuria, fever, or chills. The patient has a sedentary lifestyle and has been experiencing stress at work. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, the prostate gland is mildly enlarged and tender to palpation. His urine analysis and urine culture are negative for any bacterial infection. The patient was diagnosed with chronic non-bacterial prostatitis and was recommended for a clinical trial investigating the effect of pumpkin seeds oil phonophoresis. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no known hypersensitivity to pumpkin seeds oil or contraindication to ultrasound treatment.

The patient is a 28 year old male who sustained a traumatic injury to his neck in a motor vehicle accident. He is currently experiencing paralysis and loss of sensation in his arms and legs. The injury occurred at the C5 level and he has been diagnosed with an AIS Grade A or B spinal cord injury. He is scheduled to undergo decompression and stabilization surgery within the next five days. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study protocol, including follow-up visits. He has not participated in any other clinical trials for acute spinal cord injury. The patient does not have a history of bleeding or immunodeficiency disorders, and has not recently used heparin or thrombolytics. He is not currently breastfeeding and has not had a positive pregnancy test. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. The patient does not have any clinically significant pre-existing neurological, cardiac, respiratory, hepatic, or renal diseases.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent upper abdominal pain, early satiety, and postprandial fullness for the past 6 months. She reports that her symptoms are worsened by stress and seem to be unrelated to any specific food or drink. She has tried over-the-counter antacids and proton pump inhibitors without relief. She denies any history of gastrointestinal surgery, bleeding, obstruction, or cancer. She has no known allergies or medical conditions and is currently not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DWJ1252 in the treatment of functional dyspepsia.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is scheduled for an ambulatory knee arthroscopy under general anesthesia. She has never been prescribed opioid medication before and has no history of psychiatric disease. The surgery is expected to take less than 60 minutes. The patient is able to use the Visual Analogue Scale-100 for pain intensity measurement and has given informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have any local or systemic infections. The patient has no prosthetic or damaged cardiac valves and is able to understand the consent form.

This is a pair of 30 year-old identical twin sisters, one of whom has been diagnosed with asthma, while the other does not have any history of respiratory illness. Both sisters have agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the variation in individual responses over time after controlled immune activation following influenza vaccination of monozygotic twins. The study aims to provide unprecedented molecular (omics) data on the molecular dynamics of immune response to vaccination, and novel insight into the flu response. The investigators will infer novel networks and pathways and as well as the dynamics of genes and mechanisms involved in asthma, flu vaccination, and individual responses, and correlate them to evaluated personalized genetic risks in the same study. The study involves following responses in blood and saliva components after influenza vaccination. Two annual vaccinations will be considered, one per year for 2 years, and at 8 time points samples will be collected. The study involves a simple blood draw, saliva collection, standard FDA-approved influenza vaccine administration and Spirometry. Both sisters meet the eligibility criteria for the study and have no allergies or medical conditions that could affect their participation in the study or its results.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia six months ago. She has received two rounds of chemotherapy but her cancer has relapsed. She is now experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and bone pain. She has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no history of drug abuse. She has no known allergies. She has a supportive family and lives at home with her parents. On physical examination, she is pale, tachycardic, and has hepatosplenomegaly. Her laboratory results show pancytopenia and elevated serum LDH. Her bone marrow biopsy confirms the presence of ALL lymphoblasts with CD52 expression on at least 10% of the cells. She is mentally competent and willing to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 9-month-old infant who was diagnosed with single ventricle physiology at birth. The infant underwent stage I Norwood reconstructive surgery within the first week of life. The infant has been experiencing difficulty sleeping, snoring, and gasping for breath during sleep. The parents have noticed that the infant's oxygen saturation levels are dropping during sleep. The infant has been experiencing episodes of cyanosis, especially during feeding and sleep. The infant has been hospitalized for monitoring and management of his condition. The infant's parents are fluent in English and are willing to participate in the clinical trial. The infant is currently stable and not experiencing any other health issues.

The patient is a 9-month-old female infant who is scheduled for elective surgery to correct a congenital hip dislocation. She has no significant medical history and her physical exam is unremarkable. The infant is alert and responsive with no signs of respiratory distress. Her weight is 8 kg and her height is 67 cm. The parents have given informed consent for their child's participation in the study. There is no history of difficult intubation or abnormal airway. The infant has not previously undergone any anesthesia or surgical procedures. The anesthesia team will consist of a pediatric anesthesia attending or fellow, or an anesthesia resident.

A 32-year-old woman with no history of mental illness, closed head injury, or drug/alcohol dependence is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) on the brain. She has no metallic implants or substances within her body and is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription medications with psychotropic effects, except for birth control. The patient is willing to give informed consent and is compatible with the size requirements for the fMRI scanner. She has not had any first-degree family members with a history of epilepsy and does not have any serious neurological illnesses or medical conditions that could compromise brain function. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to scientific research and learn more about the potential effects of TMS on cognitive control.

This is an 81-year-old woman who has been experiencing a persistent cough and fever for the past few days. She was admitted to the hospital due to suspicion of an upper respiratory tract infection. She has a history of hypertension, but her other medical history is unremarkable. She is currently living in a nursing home and has not traveled recently. She has not received any vaccinations in the past year. After a thorough examination, it was determined that she meets the WHO Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) case definition. She has also been diagnosed with bacteremia with positive blood culture. The patient is affiliated with social security insurance and has signed the informed consent form. She is eligible for the study as she is hospitalized, is 65 years or older, and meets the inclusion criteria. She will be followed up via phone calls for three and six months after the hospitalization.

25 yo F with no significant past medical history and no current medications seeking participation in a clinical trial focused on evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of NasoVAX. The patient is in good physical condition, has adequate venous access, and is willing to comply with all aspects of the study. The patient has a negative drug and alcohol screen and is willing to practice a highly effective method of contraception for 28 days after receiving NasoVAX. The patient has not received any investigational product or vaccine within the past 30 days and has not received any influenza vaccine within the past 6 months. The patient has not smoked or used tobacco products within the past 30 days and has no known allergies to the ingredients in the vaccine formulation. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and does not live with or care for pregnant women, children under 5 years of age, or immunocompromised individuals.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been struggling with alcohol dependence for the past three years. He has tried to quit on his own several times but always relapses within a few days. He drinks heavily every day, consuming at least 10 standard drinks per day. He has a stable job as a software developer, but his drinking has started to affect his job performance. He lives alone in a one-bedroom apartment and has no family nearby. He is generally in good physical health and has no history of psychiatric disorders, including PTSD. He is fluent in English and has no planned absences during the six-week active treatment period. He is willing to provide informed consent and attend weekly check-ins with the study psychiatrist. He is not currently taking any psychiatric medications or opiates, and his urine is negative for opioids. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He is not currently experiencing any signs or symptoms of alcohol withdrawal.

A 35-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting MS for the past 3 years complains of foot drop on the left side, which makes walking difficult. She states that she feels unsteady and has fallen twice in the past month. She has been using a cane for the past week. She has no other neurological symptoms. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She exercises regularly by swimming and doing yoga. She has no other medical conditions and is not on any medication. She is married and has one child. She works part-time as a graphic designer. Her EDSS score is 4.0.

A 40-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) not otherwise specified presents with relapsed or refractory disease after two or more lines of systemic therapy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living without assistance. He has a caregiver who is willing and able to provide 24-hour care for the first 30 days after CAR-T cell infusion. He lives within a 30-minute distance from the cancer center and has access to a wifi network. He and his caregiver have attended the education session for outpatient CAR-T and have demonstrated competency to collect vital signs with equipment provided. He is fluent in English and is willing and able to sign an IRB-approved informed consent document.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of heart failure. He presents with shortness of breath at rest and with activities of daily living. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. His physical exam reveals a heart rate of 78 beats per minute, blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, and an irregular rhythm. He has bibasilar crackles on lung exam. His ECG shows left bundle branch block with a QRS duration of 150 msec. His echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% with severe mitral regurgitation. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial on response to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure: role of arterial stiffness.

A 45-year-old male who has been on omeprazole for several years due to chronic GERD symptoms. He recently underwent an upper endoscopy for evaluation of his symptoms and was found to have a fundic gland polyp in his stomach. The polyp was removed and sent for pathology, which confirmed its benign nature. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to examine the correlation between PPI use and the development of fundic gland polyps. He is able and willing to sign the informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has noticed small, raised, pink or flesh-colored bumps in the genital area. She reports discomfort during sexual intercourse and itching. She has no history of any sexually transmitted diseases or infections. She is sexually active with one partner and uses condoms inconsistently. The patient is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with it. She is not pregnant and is not too frail or ill for a gynecological examination. She has provided informed consent for the study. The patient is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial investigating the typing of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) from female genital warts.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who presents with a history of dyslipidemia. He has a family history of heart disease (father and grandfather). He currently takes a low dose of atorvastatin (10 mg) daily and follows a healthy diet but has not achieved target lipid levels. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days. He has no history of liver disease, cancer, or endocrine disorders affecting lipid metabolism. He has no clinically significant food allergies and has not had any gastric bypass surgery or surgical procedures for weight loss. He is willing to comply with the recommended, standardized diet. His fasting LDL cholesterol levels are between 3.36 mmol/L and 5.6 mmol/L and triglyceride levels are less than or equal to 4.52 mmol/L. He is willing to use adequate contraception if sexually active and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has been on insulin therapy for the past 2 years, taking insulin NPH and regular human insulin. She has a BMI of 30 and has a history of hypertension, but no previous cardiovascular events. She takes medication for hypertension and regularly monitors her blood glucose levels. She has experienced occasional episodes of hypoglycemia in the past. She is currently able to self-medicate and is compliant with her medication regimen. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her metabolic control and cardiac function.

The patient is an 82-year-old man who has been diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but has been otherwise healthy. He presents with symptoms of shortness of breath and chest pain. After being evaluated by a cardiologist, he is deemed a candidate for a transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Edwards Sapien XT valve. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and has no contraindications to the procedure. He is willing to undergo a comprehensive geriatric assessment to evaluate his overall health and determine the best course of treatment.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of acute lower respiratory tract infection, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of smoking and has had a previous episode of pneumonia. The patient was not prescribed oseltamivir or zanamivir at the time of admission. The patient has signed an informed consent form to participate in the Rapid Empiric Treatment with Oseltamivir Study (RETOS). The patient will be randomized to either Group A, which will receive standard clinical care, including empiric antibiotics and anti-influenza drugs at the clinician's discretion, or Group B, which will receive oseltamivir within 24 hours of admission, ideally within 8-12 hours of admission, plus empiric antibiotics. The patient will be enrolled from one of four hospitals in Louisville, KY during the influenza season, which is defined as December 1st until May 1st. The patient's diagnosis of influenza will be based on nucleic acid amplification through polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The patient's management will be different only in regard to early empiric anti-influenza therapy. The study nurse will facilitate receipt of early oseltamivir treatment for the patient in collaboration with the hospital pharmacies. The time of oseltamivir administration will be recorded for the patient.

A 45-year-old man who has chronic low back pain for at least three months came to the clinic. He works as a truck driver and has a sedentary lifestyle. His pain level ranges from 5-7 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale, and he sometimes experiences radiating pain at his left leg. He has never used custom-made orthotics before and has not received any ongoing active conservative care for his low back pain. He has no history of litigation for any health concern and is fluent in English. He does not have any brain disorders or chronic pain other than low back pain. He has no spinal pathology or fracture and no history of lumbar spine surgery. He does not have any peripheral neuropathy or skeletal deformity of the foot. He has no contraindications to orthotic use or chiropractic spinal manipulations.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing pain in his lower abdomen and back for the past week. He visited his doctor and was diagnosed with a 7 mm kidney stone. His doctor recommended ureteroscopic treatment with laser lithotripsy. The patient has no known pathology of the upper urinary tract and no untreated infection. He has never had this procedure before and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

30 y/o female with confirmed COVID-19 infection presenting with mild symptoms including cough, fatigue, and loss of taste and smell. No significant past medical history or chronic medical conditions. No recent travel or close contact with known COVID-19 positive individuals. Currently taking no medications. No known drug allergies. No recent hospitalizations or surgeries. No history of smoking or substance abuse. No history of pregnancy.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female who does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no known allergies to any medications or food products. Her BMI is 23 kg/m², which falls within the eligible range for the study. She is not currently taking any prescription medications, but occasionally takes over-the-counter pain relievers for headaches. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study. She has no history of abnormal bleeding or coagulation disorders. Her blood pressure and pulse rate are within normal limits. She has no history of significant cardiovascular disease or myocardial infarction. She consumes 1-2 cups of coffee daily but does not consume excessive amounts of caffeinated beverages. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to medical research and learn more about potential drug interactions.

A 35-year-old female presents with chronic low back pain that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a constant ache in the lower back that worsens with prolonged sitting or standing. She denies any radiating pain to the legs, but reports occasional stiffness and discomfort in her hips. She has tried over-the-counter pain relief medications without significant improvement. She has no history of significant trauma, surgery, or neurological conditions. Vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination reveals mild restriction of lumbar spine movement with tenderness on palpation. She is diagnosed with non-specific chronic low back pain and is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the effects of High-Velocity Low-Amplitude (HVLA) manipulation on H-reflex responses. She meets the inclusion criteria of the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. She is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

33-year-old F with a deep-partial thickness burn injury to her right forearm and hand due to accidental contact with hot oil while cooking in her home kitchen. She was admitted to the burn unit within 48 hours of the injury, and the burn site was diagnosed as non-infected by the attending physician. The total body surface area burned was estimated to be 10%. The patient has no history of developmental disability or significant psychological disorder, nor does she have any history of active alcohol or substance abuse. She is not pregnant, nursing, or actively lactating. The burn site on her right forearm is large enough to accommodate placement of control and microsurfaced cadaveric grafts at the same location. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study protocol for evaluation of the effectiveness of Microsurfaced vs Control cadaveric grafts on wound healing.

A healthy 25-year-old male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in the clinical trial for Schistosomiasis. He has no history of schistosomiasis or any other significant medical condition. He is not taking any medication known to interact with praziquantel, artesunate or lumefantrine metabolism. He weighs 70 kg and has a BMI of 22. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and he is willing to refrain from blood donation throughout the study period. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to abide by the procedures of the study. He is reachable by mobile phone from week 3 to week 12 of the study period and agrees to use adequate contraception for the duration of the study.

58-year-old male with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon that has progressed after initial treatment with FOLFOX and FOLFIRI regimens. The patient has also undergone radiation therapy to the pelvis for palliation of bone metastasis. The patient reports mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort, but is otherwise able to perform activities of daily living. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of at least 16 weeks. The patient is interested in exploring additional treatment options and has not had prior treatment with doxorubicin or PARP inhibitors. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive AZD2281 in combination with liposomal doxorubicin.

A 28-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 22 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of repeated dosing of PF-05175157 on the pharmacokinetics of a single dose of Simvastatin. The patient has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, ocular, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease. Additionally, the patient has not previously experienced any intolerance to simvastatin or other statins. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and is available for the duration of the study.

57 yo M with newly diagnosed advanced NSCLC after presenting with cough, dyspnea, and weight loss. Biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. Staging CT revealed multiple mediastinal lymph nodes and liver metastases. The patient received 6 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy and had a confirmed response (partial response) on imaging. MRI of the brain was negative for metastases. The patient is in good general health with ECOG performance status of 1. He has no history of brain surgery or radiotherapy. He has normal renal, hepatic, and hematological function. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 diabetes mellitus - History of smoking (40 pack-year history) - No history of seizures or brain disease

A 57-year-old male with a history of diabetes and hypertension presents with unexplained bone pain and fatigue. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past three months. He also complains of weight loss without any change in his diet. He has no history of smoking or drinking. His family history is negative for any hematologic disorders. He underwent a bone marrow biopsy, which revealed smoldering plasma cell myeloma with high-risk features. He is asymptomatic and has an ECOG performance status of 1. His platelet count is 120,000/uL, and his ANC is 1,500/mm^3. His AST and ALT are within normal limits, and his total bilirubin is 0.8 x ULN. His calculated CrCl is 70 mL/min per 24-hour urine collection, and his T-Spot test for tuberculosis is negative. He has no evidence of end-organ damage attributable to the underlying plasma cell proliferative disorder. He has not received any prior treatment for smoldering multiple myeloma. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and has signed a written informed consent.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of iliac vein thrombosis. She was diagnosed with the condition two years ago, after experiencing sudden and severe pain in her left leg. The pain was accompanied by swelling and discoloration of the leg. Duplex sonography confirmed the presence of a blood clot in the iliac vein. The patient was treated with anticoagulant therapy for six months and has remained asymptomatic since then. She has no other known medical conditions and does not take any medications. The patient reports no family history of blood clotting disorders or other thromboembolic events. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help researchers better understand the causes and risk factors for iliac vein thrombosis.

A 48 year old man visits the clinic with the complaints of severe pain in the back and side of the abdomen. He also experiences nausea and vomiting. The pain started suddenly and is colicky in nature. He has a history of kidney stones and has had similar episodes in the past. Physical examination showed an elevated temperature of 38.3°C and a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. The abdomen is tender to palpation in the right flank area. Urinalysis showed red blood cells and leukocytes, suggesting the presence of urinary tract infection. The patient is diagnosed with kidney stones and RIRS is recommended. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the clinical trial comparing multiple-, single-, zero-dose of ciprofloxacin prophylaxis in RIRS. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus or allergy to quinolone. He has an ASA score of 1 and the size of the kidney stone is less than 2.5 cm. He does not have a positive preoperative urine culture or pyuria. He has not received antibiotics treatment for UTI in the past 4 weeks and is not immunocompromised. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is randomly assigned to receive multiple-dose prophylactic antibiotic of 200mg intravenous ciprofloxacin, 30 minutes before surgery and within 12 hours after surgery.

A 55-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with invasive carcinoma of the breast. Her tumor size is less than 3.0 cm in diameter and she is axillary node negative. She underwent prior breast-preserving surgery with complete microscopic resection of the tumor. She has not undergone neoadjuvant or adjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy, and her hormone receptor status is not specified. She is not on any other concurrent therapy. She is  postmenopausal and has a good performance status with a life expectancy of over 5 years. She is willing to use effective contraception if she is fertile. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the effectiveness of radiation therapy in treating localized breast cancer.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who suffered a traumatic spinal cord injury resulting in high tetraplegia. He has been ventilator-dependent since the injury and has undergone a surgical implantation of Diaphragmatic Pacing System (DPS) in 2010. He has been under the management of the SCI center since then and has been followed up regularly. He has not had any major surgeries or hospitalizations since the implantation of DPS. He has been able to use the DPS system for an average of 8 hours per day without any significant issues. He is willing to participate in a long-term follow-up study to help improve the understanding and outcomes of DPS use in patients with high tetraplegia.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient recruitment as it is an experimental study, and the participants will be healthy volunteers rather than patients with a specific condition. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history. She is currently not taking any prescription medications and is able to safely discontinue any over-the-counter medications for the duration of the study. She has no known allergies to nitroglycerin and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She has a negative pregnancy test and agrees to use effective contraception throughout the study. She has not recently experienced any myocardial infarction, uncontrolled congestive heart failure, unstable angina, uncontrolled hypotension, or uncontrolled hypertension. She has not participated in a study of an investigational drug within two weeks of visit 1. Her screening lab values are within range and not considered clinically significant by the investigator. She has not had major abdominal, thoracic, or vascular surgery within the past 6 months. She does not have any non-epithelialized skin lesions or interfering skin conditions in the area where the study medication is to be applied.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of asthma and recurrent sinus infections. She has been experiencing symptoms of EGPA for the past year, including persistent cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath, as well as numbness and tingling in her hands and feet. Blood tests have shown elevated levels of eosinophils, and a biopsy has confirmed the presence of eosinophilic vasculitis. Despite receiving standard corticosteroid therapy, her symptoms have persisted and she has experienced several relapses within the past 6 months. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. She has provided written informed consent and is committed to consistent and correct use of an acceptable method of birth control for the duration of the trial and for 4 months after the last study drug administration.

This clinical trial is focused on preschool children aged three to five years who are enrolled in preschool or daycare in Campina Grande, Brazil. The study aims to evaluate the perceived impact of dental caries and dental pain on the oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) among these children and their families. A total of 843 preschool children will be included in this cross-sectional study. Parents/caregivers will be required to answer a questionnaire on socio-demographic information, their child's general/oral health, and history of dental pain. The Brazilian version of the Early Childhood Oral Health Impact Scale will be administered to determine the perceived impact of caries and dental pain on OHRQoL, and the children will undergo an oral examination. The study will be conducted in compliance with Resolution 196/96 of the Brazilian National Health Council and received approval from the Human Research Ethics Committee of the State University of Paraíba. Children who are three to five years old, enrolled in preschool or daycare, and free of any systemic disease according to parents'/caregivers' reports will be eligible to participate. Parental authorization will be required, and exclusion criteria include children who do not accept clinical examination or have mental illness.

65 year old man who has been experiencing shortness of breath and a persistent cough for the past 6 months. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 10 years ago. He has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) through a lung biopsy. He is currently taking oxygen therapy and has been advised to avoid exposure to pollutants and irritants. He has no other known medical conditions and has not participated in any clinical trials for IPF treatments.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with elevated M30 antigen levels (300 U/L) and hepatic steatosis on ultrasound. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, which are currently well-controlled with metformin and lisinopril, respectively. His BMI is 32 kg/m2 and he leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of alcohol abuse or liver disease unrelated to NASH. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He has no known food allergies or intolerances. He works as a desk job and has a family history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore the benefits of nutritional counseling versus nutritional supplements for the treatment of NASH.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep for the past 6 months. She reports that it takes her over an hour to fall asleep and that she often wakes up in the middle of the night and struggles to fall back asleep. She has tried various over-the-counter sleep aids, but they have not been effective. She does not have any significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is interested in participating in the study to try a new medication that may help her sleep better.

A 52-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with a fever, chills, and rapid breathing. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a construction worker and has been exposed to dust and chemicals at his job site. Upon admission, he was diagnosed with sepsis caused by a bacterial infection. He is currently receiving intravenous antibiotics to treat the infection. His blood pressure is low, and his heart rate is elevated. He is also experiencing shortness of breath and confusion. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Biomarker Analysis of Stress clinical trial at the Wadsworth Center.

58 year old female from Vietnam with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. She is currently under treatment with metformin and has been visiting her local diabetes center regularly for the past year. She is able to comply with the study protocol and is willing to sign the informed consent form. She has not participated in this study previously and is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman with a clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes who has been using daily insulin therapy for over a year and an insulin infusion pump for over 6 months. She has internet access for periodic upload of study data and has experience using the Medtronic pump and CGM, which she uses on a near-daily basis. She has experienced nocturnal hypoglycemia meeting the criterion of having one or more nights with a sensor glucose value of <=70 mg/dL during the most recent 15 nights with CGM glucose data. Her HbA1c level is <=8.0%. The patient has not had diabetic ketoacidosis in the past 3 months and has not had a hypoglycemic seizure or loss of consciousness in the past 6 months. She has no history of seizure disorder (except for hypoglycemic seizure), coronary artery disease, heart failure, cystic fibrosis, ongoing renal disease (other than microalbuminuria), liver disease, or any medical or psychiatric condition that might interfere with the completion of the protocol. The patient is not pregnant and will be required to have a negative urine pregnancy test if she is premenopausal and not surgically sterile.

A 20-year-old female presents with a history of irregular periods and facial hair growth. She has noticed an increase in her body weight over the past year and currently has a BMI of 25 kg/m*m. She reports having acne and occasional headaches but no other medical problems. She has not been on any medications for the past three months. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes in her mother and grandmother. She has not been pregnant before. Physical examination reveals excess hair growth on her face, chest and back. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute and her respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute. Her waist circumference is 90 cm and hip circumference is 100 cm. Laboratory results show elevated levels of luteinizing hormone (LH) and testosterone, with a LH/FSH ratio of 3.5. Her thyroid and prolactin levels are within normal range. She is diagnosed with PCOS according to the modified Rotterdam criteria and is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating Taichi for overweight/obese adolescent and young women with PCOS.

The patient is a 36-year-old male who was diagnosed with psoriasis vulgaris over a year ago. The patient has a history of psoriasis involvement on the trunk and limbs, scoring at least 4 in total by the Investigator's Assessment of Severity of the Target Lesion/Location. The patient's psoriasis vulgaris involves 15% of the body surface area (BSA) excluding psoriatic lesions of genitals and skin folds. The patient has not received any systemic treatment with biological therapies, corticosteroids, retinoids, methotrexate, ciclosporin, or other immunosuppressants within the last 4 weeks prior to Visit 1. The patient has not undergone psoralen combined with Ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy within the last 4 weeks prior to Visit 1, nor Ultraviolet B (UVB) therapy within 2 weeks prior to Visit 1. The patient does not have severe and/or extensive scalp psoriasis which requires treatment with potent or super-potent corticosteroids. Also, the patient has not used antidepressant medications or any other medication known to affect cortisol levels or HPA axis integrity within 4 weeks prior to baseline.

Patient A is a 60-year-old female who has been diagnosed with late-stage solid cancer (with or without lung involvement). She has failed or refused anti-cancer treatment and is currently experiencing symptoms such as pain, dyspnea, and decreased performance status. Her medical history shows no significant comorbidities and she is currently not taking any medications other than conservative treatment for her symptoms. She has an ECOG performance status of 2 and a Karnofsky performance status of 70. Her blood test results show normal levels of hematology and biochemistry variables, with WBC, platelet count, and hemoglobin within the acceptable range. Her albumin corrected serum calcium level is also within the normal range. Her 25(OH)D serum level is above 20 ng/mL. She has not received any acute anti-cancer therapy in the last 2 weeks and does not have brain metastases or spinal cord compression. She is not pregnant. She is eligible for the study and will be administered with AMOR powder and AMOR Inhaled Double Pack 1% ACC in 8 ml suspension to improve her function and welfare.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing solid food for the past couple of months, accompanied by intermittent chest pain. He has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). He recently underwent an endoscopy, which revealed a mass in his esophagus. Biopsy results indicated that he has stage II esophageal adenocarcinoma. He has no previous history of chemotherapy, thoracic radiotherapy, or surgery for an esophageal tumor. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL. His absolute neutrophil count is 2000/mm^3, platelet count is 150,000/mm^3, and his creatinine level is within normal range. His bilirubin level is 1.2 x ULN, and his AST/ALT is within normal limits. He is able to take oral tablets without difficulty. He has not received any investigational agents within the last 4 weeks, and he is not currently undergoing any other active malignancy that requires systemic intervention. He has no grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy. He is willing to use highly effective contraceptive methods as he is of child-bearing potential. The patient fully understands the nature of the study and has signed the informed consent form prior to receiving any study related procedure.

A 25 yo healthy female with no significant medical history, currently working as a research assistant in a laboratory, is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She weighs 65 kg and has a body mass index of 22 kg/m2. She has not participated in any clinical studies in the past year and has no known endocrine, thyroid, hepatic, respiratory, gastrointestinal, neurological, renal, cardiovascular diseases or significant psychiatric/psychotic illness disorder. She is excited to contribute to medical research and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis as per the American College of Rheumatology and European League Against Rheumatism criteria. He has been taking Methotrexate (MTX) treatment (10mg/week) for the past 3 months but has not been adequately responding to the treatment. He has no history of other connective tissue disorders or chronic or recurrent infectious diseases. However, he has a past history of congestive heart failure, for which he is currently taking medication and is under the care of a cardiologist. He has never been diagnosed with tuberculosis nor has he been in close contact with anyone who has been diagnosed with tuberculosis. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate a new treatment option for his rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 62-year-old man diagnosed with stage III pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has not received any prior systemic therapy and is ineligible for or refused chemoradiotherapy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is expected to live for more than 3 months. His white blood cell count, absolute neutrophil count, and platelet count are within normal limits. His bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are within acceptable limits. He does not have any prior exposure to EGFR-inhibitors and is not taking any concurrent drugs that are known to be strong inducers or inhibitors of the CYP450 enzyme system. He is not taking any concurrent investigational or commercial agents or therapies with the intent to treat his malignancy.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of hypertriglyceridemia. She has been diagnosed with this condition for 5 years and has been taking medication to manage her triglyceride levels. She reports a family history of heart disease and has been advised by her physician to maintain a healthy lifestyle, including a low-fat diet and regular exercise. She is currently taking fenofibrate and has not made any recent changes to her medication or diet. Her fasting triglyceride level is 280 mg/dL during screening. She has a body mass index of 25.5 kg/m2 and is in overall good health. She has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. She is willing and able to undergo the scheduled study procedures and understands the study procedures, signing forms documenting informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for stenotic coronary arteries. He has been taking both aspirin and clopidogrel as part of his cardiovascular disease treatment. He has a past history of peptic ulcer disease without complications and has previously taken aspirin and clopidogrel before enrolling for his current CV disease. He has no contraindications to antithrombotic or antiplatelet therapy and has no clinical severe thrombocytopenia. He has no history of disabling or hemorrhagic stroke or intracranial hemorrhage, and has stable hepatic, renal, and pulmonary function. He has no progressive malignancy and no epigastralgia or positive occult blood in stool. He has not received surgical intervention due to PUD complication in the past and has not received a GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor fewer than 3 days before randomization. The patient will be randomly assigned to receive aspirin (100 mg/day) plus clopidogrel (75 mg/day) with PPI (lansoprazole-Takepron@ 30 mg/day) or aspirin (100 mg/day) plus clopidogrel (75 mg/day) with placebo (antacid 1 table/day) for 3 months. He will be followed as an outpatient, with visits every one month, checking blood hemoglobin as well as stool occult blood for 3 months. He will be asked to report to gastroenterologist if he has persistent ulcer symptoms (epigastric pain, dyspepsia) and to report to the emergency room if he has evidence of GI bleeding or ulcer complications (melena, hematemesis, or sudden onset of severe epigastric pain). Endoscopy will be undergone to document any gastroduodenal ulcers with or without ulcer complications. The patient will not be eligible if he experiences any of the exclusion criteria during the course of the study.

A 28-year-old male came to the clinic for a routine checkup. He has no history of neurological or orthopedic conditions. He works as a computer technician and is physically active. He enjoys playing basketball on weekends with his friends. He has no previous experience with any kind of robotic devices. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve motor adaptation in healthy individuals. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and is not taking any medication. His BMI is 23.

The patient is a 45-year-old female of African-American descent who has recently been diagnosed with Philadelphia chromosome positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). She has been on imatinib at full dose (600mg) for the past 6 months, but her disease has progressed despite the treatment. She has not undergone stem cell transplantation yet. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is in good general health, with no significant medical conditions other than CML. Her performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is able to take daily oral capsules/tablets reliably.

This is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has seen her primary care physician and has been prescribed an antidepressant medication, but has not yet started treatment. She is familiar with the use of mobile phones and is able and willing to carry one. She speaks and reads English fluently and is at least 18 years of age. She does not have any visual, hearing, voice, or motor impairments that would prevent her from completing study procedures or using a mobile phone. She does not have a history of psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, dissociative disorder, current substance dependence, or any other diagnosis that would make her ineligible for the trial. She is not severely suicidal and does not have any ideation, plan, or intent. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her depression symptoms and receive personalized, guideline-congruent care.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with COVID-19 three days ago and was admitted to the hospital for treatment. He is currently experiencing mild respiratory symptoms, including shortness of breath, coughing, and mild fever. His oxygen saturation level is 93%, and he is currently receiving oxygen therapy via nasal cannula. He has no previous history of neurological or cognitive disorders. He is alert and able to participate in training with a score of 4 points on the Riker scale. His current medications include antipyretics and antibiotics. He has no contraindications for non-invasive cerebral stimulation.

This is a 30-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and is in overall good health as assessed by the investigator. He has never been diagnosed with a congenital or acquired long QT syndrome or cardiovascular disease, and he has no personal or known family history of these conditions. He does not consume alcohol or use drugs/chemicals. He is able to comprehend the study requirements and is willing to sign informed consent. He has no plans to father children in the near future and is willing to use required barrier contraception during the study period.

20-year-old female football player, part of a team registered in the federated league, training for 4 and a half hours a week or more, and competing and training in regulatory fields with artificial grass. She has a qualified technician on her team who is registered and in possession of the corresponding validated license. She must have a valid federal license signed by the competent medical authority and sign the informed consent. She should not have suffered a lower limb injury at the start of the study. The purpose of this clinical trial is to design and carry out a physiotherapy program based on the prevention of modifiable risk factors to prevent lower extremity injuries in female football players. The study will have two groups, the first being the experimental group, which will be made up of female players from the football team called CD Oliver (CDO), and the second being the control group, which will be made up of female players from the first team SD Huesca (SDH). The study will evaluate data on variables of injury incidence, muscle length, and torque.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman diagnosed with Turner Syndrome, confirmed by karyotype analysis. She has been experiencing short stature and infertility since puberty. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and provides informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. She has been informed of the results of the medical examination prior to the trial. The patient does not have any comprehension difficulties and does not have any contra-indications for MRI examination, such as a pacemaker or automatic defibrillator, implanted pump, or intraocular metallic objects. The patient does not suffer from claustrophobia and has a morphotype allowing access to MRI. The patient is not under judicial protection, guardianship or trusteeship, and is not pregnant at the time of inclusion in the trial.

The patient is a 9-year-old Chinese boy who is currently in grade 3. He was referred to the clinic by his school teacher for exhibiting symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity. His parents also reported that he has difficulty making friends and often prefers to play alone. He has no known chronic medical conditions and has not been diagnosed with any neurodevelopmental disorders before. He is an only child and his parents are highly educated with no known family history of psychiatric disorders. His current medication includes multivitamins and probiotics. The vital signs are within normal limits. His parents have agreed to participate in the study and will be completing the SRS, AQ, and ASRI questionnaires. The child will also be completing the SRS, AQ, and SNAP-IV questionnaires. He will be assessed by a board-certified child psychiatrist to confirm the diagnosis of ADHD or ASD, if any.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who works as a software engineer. She has been wearing Avaira sphere contact lenses for the past 1 year with a spherical prescription of -4.00 in both eyes. She wears contact lenses for around 8-10 hours a day during weekdays and occasionally on weekends. She has no history of ocular or systemic disease and has not undergone any corneal refractive surgery. She has a spectacle cylinder of -0.50D in each eye, and her best-corrected spectacle distance visual acuity is 20/20 in each eye. She has no history of contact lens-related complications and follows good personal hygiene practices. She is willing to comply with the wear schedule and visit schedule of the study. She has read, understood and signed the information consent letter. She is excited to participate in the study and contribute to the advancement of contact lens technology.

A 28-year-old female gave birth to a male infant at 32 weeks of gestation, weighing 1700 grams. The delivery was by cesarean section due to premature rupture of membranes. The mother had an unremarkable pregnancy except for gestational diabetes that was well controlled. The baby was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to prematurity and placed on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). The baby was started on total parenteral nutrition (TPN) and gradually advanced to enteral feeding over the course of 2 weeks. The baby tolerated feeds well and was discharged from the NICU after 4 weeks. However, the baby was readmitted to the NICU at 6 weeks of age with signs of sepsis, including fever, tachycardia, and respiratory distress. Blood cultures were positive for gram-negative bacteria, and the baby was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. The baby's condition improved after 7 days of antibiotic therapy, and he was discharged home after 10 days. The parents were informed about the clinical trial and have agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of actinic keratosis (AK) on his face and scalp. He has no previous history of skin cancer. He is in good general health and not taking any systemic medications. He is willing to comply with study instructions and commit to all follow-up visits. The patient has at least four, but no more than eight visible and discrete non-hyperkeratotic, non-hypertrophic AK lesions, each at least 4 mm in diameter, within a contiguous 25 cm2 treatment area on the face and scalp. The patient has not used any topical creams, lotions, or gels of any kind within the selected Treatment Area within one day prior to entry into the study. He has not used any topical therapy for actinic keratosis within 2 cm of the selected contiguous 25 cm2 Treatment Area within eight weeks of Visit 1/Baseline. The patient has not had cryodestruction or chemodestruction, surgical excision, curettage, dermabrasion, chemical peel, or laser resurfacing on the Treatment Area (i.e., face or scalp) within two weeks prior to Visit 1/Baseline. He has no skin pathology or condition that could interfere with the evaluation of the test article or require the use of interfering topical, systemic, or surgical therapy. The patient understands the study requirements and has provided written informed consent.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. He has been on oral hypoglycemic agents and has controlled his blood glucose levels well. He has a history of hypertension for 2 years and is currently on antihypertensive medication. He has not had any cardiovascular events or renal complications so far. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He works in an office and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no family history of cardiovascular diseases or renal complications. His most recent blood tests showed HbA1c of 6.8%, fasting blood glucose of 120 mg/dL, total cholesterol of 180 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol of 100 mg/dL and triglycerides of 150 mg/dL.
