His blood pressure was measured at 130/80 mmHg. He has no symptoms related to cardiovascular or renal diseases. He is willing to participate in the study to investigate the relationship between albuminuria and arterial stiffness in diabetic patients.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). She has been managing her condition with diet and exercise, but has recently been experiencing microalbuminuria. She has never used a thiazolidinedione (TZD) medication or insulin, and does not have any significant renal or hepatic disease or anemia. She does not have unstable or severe angina or coronary insufficiency, and her blood pressure is within normal range. She is currently taking a single oral antidiabetic agent and is compliant with the medication regimen. She has not previously received combination oral antidiabetic therapy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the consent form.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of first stroke onset. He has a history of hypertension and smoking for the past 20 years. He has been married for 25 years and has two adult children. He is currently unemployed and lives with his wife. He is able to communicate effectively and is willing to complete questionnaires as part of the study. He has no other major diseases such as cancer.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Bipolar II Disorder two years ago after experiencing a major depressive episode. She has been prescribed an atypical antipsychotic medication for the past three months and has been compliant with her treatment plan. She does not have any comorbidities and is not currently experiencing a hypomanic, manic, or mixed episode. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant in the near future. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 24-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia who has been experiencing auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking for the past 2 years. He has been taking antipsychotic medication but is still experiencing symptoms. He has no known serious medical conditions and is able to visit the doctor's office for the next 7 months as scheduled. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of ovarian cancer, who has completed platinum-based therapy and has had a first or second peritoneal recurrence of epithelial adenocarcinoma or carcinosarcoma of ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal origin. The patient has measurable disease in the peritoneal cavity and has a progression-free interval (PFI) of more than 6 months from any platinum therapy, meeting the platinum-sensitive criteria. The patient is a reasonable candidate for laparoscopy and IP platinum regimen with no prior evidence of clinically significant intra-abdominal adhesions, persistent abdominal wall infections, renal toxicity, or bowel obstruction. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 1 and adequate organ function. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the trial.

A 12-year-old girl with a history of atopic dermatitis since the age of 3 years old. She has been prescribed topical steroid and emollient treatment by her dermatologist, but despite regular use, her skin condition has not improved. Her parents report difficulty in adhering to the treatment regimen due to the complexity of the treatment, the time required for its implementation and the cost of the products. The girl has been experiencing itching, dryness, and rashes on her arms, legs, and face, which often interfere with her daily activities. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of allergies or other chronic medical conditions. She is currently not taking any medication and has no known drug allergies. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to use a computer to complete the PO-SCORAD questionnaire between consultations. Her parents will be responsible for applying the topical treatment.

A 30-year-old woman, currently in her third trimester of pregnancy, presents with complaints of difficulty falling and staying asleep at night. She reports feeling restless and anxious, with racing thoughts that prevent her from getting a good night's rest. She has tried various sleep aids, but they have not been effective and she is concerned about the safety of taking medication during pregnancy. The patient speaks fluent Danish and is a first-time mother. She does not have a history of psychiatric disorders, sleep disorders, or postnatal depression. She does not work night shifts and is not currently taking any sleep medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of music as a treatment for pregnancy-related insomnia.

A 45-year-old male veteran with a spinal cord injury was admitted to the hospital due to complications related to urinary retention. He is dependent on a Foley catheter for the drainage of his urinary bladder. In the physical examination, he had no signs of periurethral inflammation or infection. He is able to read and understand the protocol requirements, and has given his informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has not had a symptomatic urinary tract infection in the past 2 weeks and his urine culture shows less than 1,000 Colony Forming Units/mL. The patient is able to accommodate a size 14,16, or 18 French Foley catheter.

A 42-year-old woman with persistent asthma is seeking to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new technology for identifying different inflammatory asthma phenotypes. She has been diagnosed with asthma for ten years and has been using an inhaler to manage her symptoms. She experiences shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing several times a week, but these symptoms are usually manageable with her current treatment. She has never had a respiratory tract infection or asthma exacerbation within the last 30 days and is not currently taking oral steroids or immunosuppressive treatments. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve the diagnosis and management of asthma.

A 25-year-old woman who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy and resides in one of the study counties (Laoting, Mancheng, Fengrun, Xianghe, Yuanshi). She has not given birth previously and is not anemic (hemoglobin levels are above 10 g/dl in the first trimester and above 9.5 g/dl in the second trimester). She can follow instructions and is able to swallow pills. She is not currently taking any iron or other vitamin or mineral supplements, except for folic acid. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to take a daily prenatal supplement to help reduce the risk of perinatal mortality.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and cough. He has been experiencing fever and chills for the past week. On examination, he is found to have bilateral lung crackles, and his oxygen saturation is 87% on room air. Arterial blood gas analysis shows hypoxemia with a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of 140. Chest x-ray shows bilateral infiltrates consistent with ARDS. The patient is started on mechanical ventilation with a tidal volume of 6 ml/kg predicted body weight (PBW) and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 12 cmH2O. However, the day-1 driving pressure is found to be 15 cmH2O, indicating an increased risk of mortality. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial investigating enhanced lung protective ventilation with ECCO2R during ARDS.

A 42-year-old veteran who suffered a closed-head traumatic brain injury (TBI) a year ago presents with symptoms of affective lability such as mood swings, irritability, frustration and anxiety. In addition, he has been using alcohol as a coping mechanism for his mood problems. He has no history of bipolar disorder or anxiety disorder prior to the TBI and has not had any skull opening either surgically or traumatically. He has no history of stroke or major psychosis, and is not currently experiencing any suicidal or homicidal ideations. He has no active liver disease, no history of seizure disorder, and no evidence of the alcohol amnesic syndrome. He does not have any medical conditions that would constitute contraindications to treatment with divalproex sodium.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who is scheduled for an elective surgery. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. He also has a history of smoking, but he quit 2 years ago. He has no history of lung disease, sleep apnea, or any other respiratory conditions. He is 6 feet tall and weighs 220 pounds. His airway examination reveals that he has a Mallampati score of III and is predicted to have a difficult airway. He is able to understand and follow instructions, and he has given his informed consent for the procedure. He has no contraindications for the procedure and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. He is married with two children and has a busy job as a sales manager. His BMI is 33, BP: 140/90, HR: 80/min. He has a family history of diabetes and heart disease. He has been trying to lose weight and improve his diet, but has not been successful so far. His laboratory study shows evidence of insulin resistance with an HgA1C level of 6.5% and a fasting glucose level of 110 mg/dl. He also has a waist circumference of 105 cm, triglycerides level of 180 mg/dL, and HDL level of 35 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including consuming only study food and drink and avoiding certain foods and medications.

A 68-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents to the emergency department with a fever of 102°F, productive cough, and shortness of breath for the past 4 days. He also complains of dysuria and frequency for the past 2 days. He denies any chest pain or palpitation. He has been on home oxygen therapy for the past 2 years. His vital signs are: temperature 102°F, blood pressure 94/56 mmHg, heart rate 120 bpm, respiratory rate 28 bpm, and oxygen saturation 88% on 2L/min. of supplemental oxygen. Physical examination reveals decreased air entry in the right lower lobe of the lung, and suprapubic tenderness. Laboratory investigations show leukocytosis (WBC 14,000/uL), lactate level is 2.5 mmol/L, and endotoxin activity assay is 0.7 units. Chest X-ray shows right lower lobe infiltrate. He is diagnosed with severe sepsis secondary to pneumonia and urinary tract infection.

A 10-year-old child with cerebral palsy presents with non-ambulatory and scoliosis. The child has difficulty maintaining their sitting posture due to pelvic obliquity and sliding from the sitting floor. The child's parents report that their child has been experiencing back pain and discomfort when sitting for extended periods. The child is classified as Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) Level IV. The spinal curvature measured by Cobb angle is between 10-40 degrees. The child does not have a history of spinal surgery, and their parents are not considering surgery as an option. The child does not have any contractures in the lower extremities to prevent sitting. The parents agree to participate in the intensive therapy program and stop therapeutic interventions for scoliosis and lower extremities during the 3-month follow-up period. The child does not have any history of epileptic seizures, bone operations for hip joints, or comorbidity unrelated to cerebral palsy.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of high cholesterol levels and triglycerides in the past year. He has been advised to modify his diet to help control his lipid levels, but he has found it difficult to stick to a low-fat diet. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2, and his fasting plasma triglyceride concentration is 4.5 mmol/l while fasting plasma LDL cholesterol concentration is 4.2 mmol/l. His fasting plasma HDL cholesterol concentration is 0.9 mmol/l. He lives within a 40 km radius of St. Michael's Hospital. He is not taking any cholesterol-lowering medications, but he does take antihypertensive medication for high blood pressure. He has no known food allergies, and he is not a smoker or heavy drinker. He has no history of diabetes, liver disease, or gastrointestinal disease.

A 45-year-old female presents with a BMI of 32. She has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication, and dyslipidemia that is currently untreated. She reports stable weight over the last three months, with no significant fluctuations. Her labs reveal a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL, ALT and AST levels within normal limits, and bilirubin within normal range. Her fasting plasma glucose is 5.8 mmol/L (104 mg/dL). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing the safety and effectiveness of JNJ-28431754 in promoting weight loss. She is willing to comply with the study diet and exercise non-drug therapy, and to visit the study site regularly for 12 weeks to have her weight and other safety and effectiveness tests recorded. She understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive either the study drug or a placebo, and that neither she nor the investigator will know which treatment she is receiving. She is willing to undergo two oral glucose tolerance tests as part of the study protocol. She has no history of hereditary glucose-galactose malabsorption or primary renal glycosuria, and does not have an established diagnosis of diabetes mellitus or treatment with glucose lowering drugs. Her fasting triglyceride level is within normal limits. She is excited to potentially contribute to research that may lead to effective non-drug therapies for weight loss in overweight and obese patients.

A 56-year-old man was diagnosed with multiple myeloma six years ago. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and an autologous stem cell transplant, but his cancer has relapsed and is now refractory to further chemotherapy. He is married and has two adult children. He is retired and spends his time reading and traveling. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly by walking for 30 minutes a day. He has no known allergies and has never had surgery before. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the CAR T-cell therapy can help him fight his cancer.

A 32-year-old woman presents with symptoms of major depressive disorder for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad and hopeless most days, with difficulty sleeping and concentrating. She also reports a history of childhood sexual abuse before the age of 18. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is seeking outpatient psychotherapy treatment at a community mental health center. Upon initial screening, she meets DSM-IV criteria for unipolar major depressive disorder and is eligible for the study. She is randomized to receive either interpersonal psychotherapy or individual psychotherapy. During treatment, she attends weekly 50-minute sessions with a therapist and focuses on current interpersonal stressors in her daily life. She also works on examining the relationship between her mood changes and interpersonal problems. She completes evaluations at mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 3 months after treatment.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with Fanconi anemia, which was diagnosed when he was 10 years old. He has a history of recurrent infections, bleeding episodes, and bone marrow failure. He has had several blood transfusions and is currently on a regimen of androgens and G-CSF. He has never had any cancer diagnosis, but a recent MRI revealed a suspicious mass in his left thigh. A biopsy confirmed the presence of a malignant solid tumor, which is thought to be a sarcoma. The patient and his family have agreed to participate in this study, which involves the collection and storage of his tumor tissue for future molecular studies and the development of cancer cell lines. The patient is otherwise in good health and has no known drug allergies. He is a high school student and enjoys playing soccer and video games in his free time.

Patient is a 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for pulse oximetry. She has no history of hypertension, seizures, significant respiratory disease, or previous injury or trauma to fingers or hands. She has never had altitude sickness or sickle cell disease/trait. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and has a negative urine pregnancy test. She has no history of transient ischemic attacks, carotid artery disease, myocardial ischemia, angina, myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, or cardiomyopathy. She also has no history of chronic renal impairment or recent arterial cannulation. She does not currently use blood thinners and has no known allergies to lidocaine or heparin. She is willing to undergo a physical examination, including a 12 lead ECG, medical history review, and blood test.

A 32-year-old man presents with a history of HIV infection for the last 5 years. He has been on an initial HAART regimen consisting of 3TC/ZDV and a boosted PI for the last 2 years. He has been compliant with his medication, and his viral load has been undetectable (<400 copies/ml) for the last 2 years. However, in the last 2 months, he has noticed a gradual increase in his viral load, and his most recent test showed a viral load of 7,500 copies/ml. His CD4+ count is 90 cells/mm3. He has never taken abacavir or tenofovir before. He has no history of any AIDS-defining illnesses in the last 30 days, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no specified viral genotypes upon screening. The patient is concerned about his increasing viral load and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an investigational regimen combining FDA approved HIV drugs for antiretroviral-experienced patients experiencing early virologic failure.

A 50-year-old male with a history of mantle cell lymphoma or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma who has previously undergone anthracycline-based treatment is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient must have confirmed pathology diagnosis at the National Cancer Institute, National Institutes of Health (NIH) and recurrent measurable disease. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status must be 2 or better, and major organ function, such as absolute neutrophil count, platelet count, creatinine, serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase (SGPT), and bilirubin, should be within the normal range. The patient should not have HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, or active central nervous system lymphoma. The patient should have fully recovered from any toxicity caused by prior therapy, and systemic cytotoxic or experimental treatments should have been avoided for at least four weeks before treatment. The patient must be willing to use adequate contraception methods or completely abstain from heterosexual intercourse while on protocol treatment.

The patient is a 58-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). She has noticed a gradual decrease in her vision over the past few months and is concerned about the impact this will have on her quality of life. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. Her best corrected visual acuity in the study eye is between 20/32 and 20/400. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with all study assessments for the full duration of the trial. She has clear ocular media and adequate pupillary dilation to permit good quality fundus imaging. She does not have subretinal hemorrhage involving the center of the fovea that is either > 50% of the total area of the lesion or > 1 disc area (2.54 mm2) in size, nor does she have subfoveal fibrosis or atrophy in the study eye. She is not currently being treated for any other ocular or systemic conditions.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with acute anterior circulation ischemic stroke due to a large vessel occlusion (LVO) through CT or MR angiography. Her NIHSS score is 10 and her ASPECTS is 8 on NCCT or 7 on DWI-MRI. She has not yet received endovascular mechanical thrombectomy (TBY) or intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) but is likely to receive TBY. She has a pre-stroke mRS of 1 and can provide written informed consent for the trial. The patient is not currently breastfeeding and has no history of chronic pulmonary diseases or severe allergies to contrast medium. Her baseline blood glucose is 110 mg/dL and her body temperature is 37.2°C. She has no history of acute myocardial infarction or acute bilateral stroke. She is not currently participating in any other interventional studies and has not previously participated in the PROOF trial.

A 28-year-old healthy male who weighs 75 kg and has no significant medical history is being sought for a clinical trial. The trial is for a new autoimmune therapeutic agent, HL237, for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. The patient must be willing to use proper contraception during the trial period and must have no history of clinically significant neurological, psychiatric, cardiovascular, respiratory, kidney, endocrine, hematologic, digestive or central disease. The patient must also have no history of gastrointestinal disorders that may affect the absorption of pharmaceuticals for clinical trials or gastrointestinal surgery, except for simple cecal surgery or hernia surgery. The patient must be willing to participate voluntarily after hearing the detailed explanation of the clinical trial and must sign an agreement. The trial will assess the maximum oral dose of HL237 and evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic characteristics for each dose group.

Pt is a 28yo F with a history of fibromyalgia for the past 4 years, presenting with severe pain and fatigue that has not responded to current treatment regimen of amitriptyline, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, and tramadol. The patient has a BMI of 30 and has been participating in an active rehabilitation program for the past year. The patient's FIQ score is 85 and her IGF-1 serum level is 140 ng/mL. The patient has no major psychiatric conditions or history of rheumatic disease. Additionally, the patient has no history of malignancies, intracranial space-occupying lesions, or adrenal gland disease. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A premature baby boy was born at 28 weeks gestation, weighing 1.2 kg. The infant was delivered by emergency C-section due to maternal preeclampsia. The baby was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for respiratory distress syndrome and received surfactant therapy. After 2 days in the NICU, the medical team diagnosed the infant with intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) grade 3 based on brain ultrasonography. The baby is now 5 days old and meets the inclusion criteria for the Phase 1 Clinical Trial of PNEUMOSTEM® Treatment in Premature Infants with Intraventricular Hemorrhage. The baby's parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have given their consent for their baby to participate. The baby is stable and his vital signs are within normal limits.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic heart failure. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs for several months. She has been diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and has been on standard therapy for the condition for the past 3 months. Her echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 35% and she has elevated levels of NT-proBNP. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication (135/80 mmHg) and her kidney function is stable with an eGFR of 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2. She has not received any SGLT2 inhibitors in the past and has not been hospitalized for heart failure in the past 4 weeks. She has not had any recent major cardiac events or procedures and is not planning any cardiac surgeries or interventions in the near future. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of chronic kidney disease, anemia, and hypertension presents to the clinic for evaluation of his condition. The patient reports feeling fatigued and experiencing shortness of breath with minimal exertion. He has been on erythropoietin stimulating agents (ESA) for the past 6 months and has been stable on a dose for the last 4 weeks. His central laboratory hemoglobin level is 10 g/dL and his serum ferritin level is 80 ng/mL with a transferrin saturation (TSAT) of 25%. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an investigational intravenous (IV) iron, ferric carboxymaltose (FCM), compared to IV iron sucrose (Venofer) in patients with impaired renal function and iron deficiency anemia (IDA). The patient has no known history of hypersensitivity reaction to any component of FCM or Venofer, and has not previously been randomized in a clinical study of Ferric Carboxymaltose (FCM). The patient is not on dialysis and has an estimated life expectancy of greater than 6 months.

This is a 26 year old male with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) who completed a pre-employment training program and has an IQ between 60 and 90. He has been experiencing difficulty maintaining steady employment and is interested in participating in a specialized employment support program aimed at improving employment outcomes and overall quality of life (QoL) for individuals with ASD. The program he is interested in is the Neurodiversity at Work (NaW) Program at Stanford University. He is able to travel to work independently and has no significant current psychosocial stressors per history. Past Medical History: 1. History of ASD 2. No other significant psychiatric disorders.

A 60-year-old woman presents with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. She has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has undergone a previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement. She is currently on aspirin and a beta blocker. She has no history of hemodynamic instability, ventricular arrhythmias, or ongoing angina. Her target lesion is located in a native coronary artery with a reference vessel diameter (RVD) of 2.5mm. She is a suitable candidate for either PCI or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). She has no lesions in the left main coronary artery, and her target lesion is not located within 3mm of the origin of the LAD or LCX coronary artery. She has no lesions located in a saphenous vein graft or arterial graft, and her target lesion will not be accessed via an SVG or arterial graft.

A 3-year-old Tanzanian boy named Hassan, who is at risk of iron and vitamin A deficiency, is eligible to participate in the Micronutrient Fortified Food Aid Pilot Project (MFFAPP) Tanzania Efficacy Study. Hassan's hemoglobin level is 9.8 mg/dl and his weight-for-height z-score is -2.5. His mother is willing to travel to the health facility for the study and is committed to ensuring Hassan consumes the fortified-blended food product provided during the study period. Hassan is not currently enrolled in school and there are no plans for the family to relocate during the study. He has no known allergies to the ingredients of the fortified-blended food product.

A 45-year-old female patient with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years is seeking treatment for her disease. She has been under the treatment of metformin with a stable dose of 2000mg/day for the past 6 months. She also follows a strict diet and exercise regime to manage her condition. The patient has a BMI of 32.5 kg/m^2 and her glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels at the screening visit were 8.5%. The patient has no history of long QT syndrome or QTc prolongation. She has not been treated with any glucose-lowering agents other than metformin in the last 3 months. The patient has no history of pancreatitis, pancreatectomy, or weight loss surgery. She has no personal or immediate family history of medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) or genetic conditions that predispose to MTC. The patient has not been exposed to drugs belonging to the class of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists/GLP-1 analogs. The patient is willing to be tested for pregnancy and is protected by a highly-effective method of birth control.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman with a BMI of 39. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are currently controlled with medication. She has been struggling to lose weight through diet and exercise and has decided to undergo bariatric surgery. She is scheduled to undergo elective bariatric surgery next week and has consented to participate in a clinical trial studying the effect of alveolar recruitment maneuvers on postoperative pain. She has no active pulmonary disorder and her cardiovascular disease is well-controlled.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of knee pain and stiffness, particularly in the medial compartment of his right knee. He has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis and has tried various treatments, including medication and physical therapy, but has not seen significant improvement. He rates his knee pain as a 7 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale. He is able to walk intermittently for 30 minutes without significant discomfort. He does not use any gait aids, and he has not undergone any knee surgery or intraarticular injections in the past 6 months. He is not currently on any corticosteroid injections, and he has no history of joint replacement surgery or high tibial osteotomy. He does not have any inflammatory arthritic conditions or any other conditions that may affect his gait or ability to participate in an aerobic exercise program. He is willing and able to attend all required appointments for the study. He fits into the available sizes of sensorized shoes, which range from US women's size 5 to men's size 13.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who works as a full-time administrative assistant. She has no history of significant medical conditions and is not taking any medication. She has regular menstrual cycles and is currently not sexually active. She underwent hysteroscopic sterilization six months ago and has official documentation of the procedure. Her physical examination, vital signs, and clinical laboratory tests obtained within the last 28 days are all within normal limits. She has no history of abnormal ECG results and her blood pressure and heart rate are within the ranges specified in the eligibility criteria. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 48 year old man diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He has been receiving chemotherapy and his treating physician has recommended high dose therapy and autologous transplantation. He is currently not taking thalidomide, any cytotoxic agents, or high doses of prednisolone or Dexamethasone. He is taking regular bisphosphonate therapy for his multiple myeloma. His absolute neutrophil count is between 1.5 and 10 x 109/L and his ECOG performance status is 2. He has a life expectancy of at least 2 months. He has not used any vitamin A preparations in the past 30 days, including oral supplements or topical preparations. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to take adequate measures to prevent conception during the trial. He has no significant non-malignant disease, including HIV infection, uncontrolled hypertension or unstable angina. He does not have any known allergies to E.coli-derived products and is not currently being treated with tetracycline antibiotics. He has given his written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 55-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation was referred to the clinic for catheter ablation. The patient has been diagnosed with NVAF for the past six months and has been taking Rivaroxaban to reduce the risk of blood clots. His medical history is remarkable for hypertension, for which he takes amlodipine. He denies any history of stroke, heart attack, or bleeding disorders. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is otherwise healthy and physically active. He has been instructed to continue taking Rivaroxaban until the day of the procedure.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22. She does not have any significant medical history and is a non-smoker. She has not taken any prescribed or over-the-counter medication, including herbal remedies, in the past 14 days. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and her alcohol consumption is within the recommended limits. She is not pregnant or lactating, and her urine and serum pregnancy tests are negative. She has suitable veins for multiple venepunctures/cannulation. Her clinical chemistry, haematology and urinalysis are within normal limits. She has no history of allergy requiring treatment, and she is able to swallow capsules without difficulty. She is willing and able to communicate and participate in the whole study and has provided written informed consent. She agrees to adhere to the contraception requirements defined in Section 9.4. In the investigator's opinion, she is able to understand the nature of the study and any risks involved in participation and is willing to cooperate and comply with the protocol restrictions and requirements. She does not have a history of cholecystectomy or gall stones.

The study is seeking healthy volunteers over the age of 18 with no history of bleeding disorders. Female participants must be post-menopausal, have had a tubal ligation, or hysterectomy. Interested volunteers will be screened and those who meet the eligibility criteria will be randomized into two groups. The study will compare the effectiveness of posterior tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) vs a sham treatment for overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms. Participants will receive 15 minutes of stimulation during one session. All participants will be blinded to the therapy they receive. This study is important in determining if the PTNS treatment is effective or if it is due to a placebo effect.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and was found unconscious at the scene of the accident. He was quickly transported to the hospital by paramedics who are participating in the clinical trial. Upon arrival at the hospital, the medical team evaluated his condition and found that he had multiple injuries, including a severe head injury and a broken leg. The patient is eligible for the trial because he requires prehospital intervention and admission to a hospital involved in the trial. The patient will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group. If he is assigned to the intervention group, his prehospital TICCS score will be calculated and, if necessary, he will receive the STTTOPPP bleeding protocol. If he is assigned to the control group, he will receive standard local care. The trial aims to evaluate the impact of early identification of patients who require Damage Control Resuscitation (DCR) and the potential benefits on mortality and cost-effectiveness. The patient will be monitored throughout his stay at the hospital, and data will be collected anonymously to evaluate the effectiveness of the trial.

A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic for her annual check-up. She has a history of hyperlipidemia and has been taking statins for the past year. She reports no adverse effects from the medication. She does not smoke, and her alcohol consumption is limited to occasional social drinking. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. Her blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, and her BMI is 28. Her lipid profile shows total cholesterol of 240 mg/dL, LDL of 160 mg/dL, HDL of 50 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 150 mg/dL. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, and her family history is unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of lipid-modifying drugs on HDL function.

A 56-year-old Caucasian female presented to the emergency department with a fever of 102°F, chills, and confusion. She reported feeling weak and short of breath for the past 2 days. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and obesity. She was taking oral hypoglycemic agents and antihypertensive medication. On examination, she was hypotensive with a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg and a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. She had tachypnea with a respiratory rate of 25 breaths per minute and an oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. The patient was confused and agitated. Laboratory tests revealed a white blood cell count of 22,000/mm3, a platelet count of 60,000/mm3, and an elevated lactate level of 5.5 mmol/L. A chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with pneumonia. She was diagnosed with septic shock and was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluids. The patient was randomized to the low-dose hydrocortisone group and will be monitored for coagulation function during her hospital stay.

A 32-year-old Hispanic woman presented to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, fever, and easy bruising for the past two weeks. Physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly and petechiae on the skin. Blood tests showed a low red blood cell count, low platelet count, and high white blood cell count with blasts. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of acute myeloblastic leukemia. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She is willing to undergo chemotherapy and has consented for the study. She has an ECOG performance status of 1.

This is a 35 year old male who has been using Electronic Assistive Devices (EADs) for the past 6 months, due to a spinal cord injury resulting in complete paraplegia. He has been experiencing difficulties in completing his Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) and is looking for a tool to assess his satisfaction in using EADs to perform these daily tasks. He is able to read and comprehend English instructions and is willing to participate in an online research platform for the duration of the study. He has no history of cognitive impairment and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old Hispanic woman with a family history of diabetes and hypertension was recently diagnosed with impaired fasting glucose during a routine check-up. She has a BMI of 31 and reports feeling fatigued and having difficulty losing weight. Her blood tests showed low levels of vitamin D (25-OHD level of 25 ng/ml). She has no history of major psychiatric, hematological, hepatic, or renal disorders, heart disease, or substance abuse. She does not take any medications, including diabetes medications or glucocorticoids. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of vitamin D supplementation in delaying the development of diabetes in minority populations with prediabetes and low vitamin D levels.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with indolent prostate cancer. His biopsy revealed that at least 12 cores had positive cancer cells, but none of them had a tumor length greater than 3 mm. His PSA levels are less than 10 ng/ml, and he has a Gleason score of less than 7. He has accepted the principle of active surveillance and is willing to participate in the study for a minimum of 15 months. The patient has not received androgen deprivation therapy in the past 6 months and has no known allergies to any components of leuprorelin or Casodex. He has a life expectancy of more than 5 years and is expected to attend all control visits.

A 62-year-old male patient with a history of high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes presents with recurrent bone pain, fatigue, and difficulty walking for the past two months. He reports a significant weight loss of 7 kg in the past three months without any significant changes in his diet. The patient denies any history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or illicit drug use. On examination, the patient appears tired, and his gait is unsteady. There is tenderness over the sternum and the lower back. Laboratory tests show elevated serum creatinine levels, hypercalcemia, and anemia. Further investigations reveal the presence of multiple osteolytic lesions on the spine and pelvis, and a bone marrow biopsy confirms a diagnosis of multiple myeloma. The patient's performance status score (ECOG) is 2. He has been on analgesics and supportive care for the past two months, but there is no significant improvement in his symptoms. As he is not a candidate for stem cell transplantation, he is eligible to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the quality of life in non-transplant candidate patients with multiple myeloma treated with early bortezomib. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent document.

A 46-year-old HIV-positive man who was diagnosed 5 years ago and has never been on antiretroviral therapy. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse but quit both 2 years ago. He has a history of mild hypertension and is currently on amlodipine 5mg daily. His CD4 count is 450 cells/mm3 and HIV viral load is 12,000 copies/mL. He has no known allergies to iodine/seafood and does not have thyroid disease. He is able to swallow pills and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of dietary algae on his immune system and HIV viral load.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on peritoneal dialysis. She has been experiencing fatigue, pallor, and shortness of breath lately. Her most recent bloodwork shows hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL which is lower than her previous results. She has a history of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) and has been on oral iron supplements for the past 2 months but her hemoglobin levels have continued to decline. Her TSAT is 30% and ferritin level is 80 ng/mL. She is a candidate for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria. The patient has no known allergies to intravenous (IV) iron and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including the use of effective birth control measures.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She presents with complaints of polyuria, polydipsia, and occasional blurred vision. Her fasting plasma glucose level is 140mg/dl and her HbA1c level is 8.5%. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medication for diabetes. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes, with her father and maternal aunt both having the condition. She has a BMI of 27 and is generally in good health.

The patient is a 43-year-old male who has been suffering from Crohn's disease for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss despite being on various medications. His gastroenterologist has recommended that he undergo an exploratory laparotomy and stoma formation to manage his symptoms. He has not had any previous abdominal surgeries or peritoneal dialysis. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently sexually active and has no significant medical history other than Crohn's disease. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

Patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IIIA lung adenocarcinoma and underwent lobectomy and systematic lymph node dissection. The patient received platinum-based double-drug adjuvant treatment post-surgery. The patient has potential dynamic tumor biomarkers and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating neoantigen tumor vaccine as adjuvant therapy. The patient has no history of immunodeficiency disease or autoimmune disease and is willing to participate in long-term follow-up for up to 3 years. The patient understands the study requirements and is able and willing to give witnessed, written informed consent form prior to receiving any study related procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and weight loss for the past 3 months. She has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. She presents to the clinic with jaundice and elevated liver enzymes, and a CT scan reveals a mass in the head of her pancreas. A biopsy confirms pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and she is diagnosed with stage III pancreatic cancer. She has not received any neoadjuvant treatments and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. Her Karnofsky Performance status is 80, and her life expectancy is estimated to be more than 6 months. Her platelet count is 120,000/mcl, and her INR is 1.2. Her renal function is adequate with a creatinine level below the threshold, and her bone marrow function is normal with a WBC count of 4,000. She is willing to express her consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic with a lump in her left breast that has been growing for the past 6 months. She also reported a rash and swelling of the breast with associated tenderness, pain, and warmth. The patient has no previous history of breast cancer, and she is otherwise healthy. Her biopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), which is HER2-negative. She is eligible for the clinical trial that aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of pembrolizumab in combination with standard chemotherapy for neoadjuvant treatment of IBC. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, and she is affiliated with the national "Social Security" regimen. She has not received any prior therapy for breast cancer, and she meets the inclusion criteria for the trial. She is willing to provide written informed consent, and she will be followed up for 12 months after the last dose of pembrolizumab.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman suffering from chronic back pain for the past 5 years. She has tried physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medications, and other therapies, but has not experienced any significant reduction in her back pain. She has been diagnosed with chronic neuropathic pain of trunk and limbs and is currently eligible for and participating in a spinal cord stimulation trial of a commercially available SCS trial system. Her back pain score on a Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) is 7, while her leg pain scores are 3 and 4 respectively. She is not a candidate for revision surgery and is willing to adhere to the warnings associated with the DISCSS™ system. The patient is capable of providing written informed consent, and is able to comply with the requirements of study visits, follow-up phone visits, and self-assessment questionnaires. She does not have any untreated major psychiatric comorbidity or serious drug-related behavioral issues. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is using adequate birth control. The patient is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old male undergoing maintenance hemodialysis three times a week due to end-stage renal disease. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years. Recently, he has been experiencing hyperphosphatemia, despite taking a phosphate binder agent. He complains of frequent muscle cramps and weakness. His blood tests indicate that his serum phosphorus level is higher than the normal range. He is not allergic to any medications and does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, for which he takes medication. He has no history of gastrointestinal or hepatic disorders. He has not experienced any pronounced brain or cardiovascular disorders. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

A 28-year-old male with a history of beta-thalassemia major presents with symptoms of fatigue, abdominal pain, and joint pain. He has been receiving multiple blood transfusions since childhood and has been diagnosed with iron overload. His serum ferritin and transferrin saturation levels are both elevated. He has tried chelation therapy with limited success and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any calcium channel blockers or medications that could potentially interact with nifedipine. He has a primary care physician who will continue to manage his medical care throughout the trial. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent. He is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no history of significant cardiac disease. He has normal kidney function and albumin levels. He is willing to avoid certain foods and medications in preparation for the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old G2P2 woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding along with painful cramps for the past year. She also reports a sensation of pressure in her lower abdomen. She has a history of hypertension for the past 5 years and has been taking medications to control her blood pressure. Her vital signs are within normal limits, with blood pressure readings consistently around 140/90 mm Hg. She has no other significant medical history or current complaints. Pelvic examination reveals a palpable mass in the uterus, and an ultrasound confirms the presence of a large myoma. She is a suitable candidate for hysterectomy, and she consents to participate in the study to evaluate the effect of myoma removal on her blood pressure and erythropoietin level.

A 28-year-old woman from Zambia gave birth to a healthy baby boy 8 months ago. She is currently breastfeeding and plans to continue for the next few months. She has no history of chronic health conditions and her hemoglobin levels are within the required range. Her infant received 100,000 IU vitamin A at 6 months of age. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her and her son's vitamin A status.

25 yo F with type 1 diabetes diagnosed at age 16. Reports recurrent hypoglycemic episodes with decreased awareness for the past year, as evidenced by CGM data. No history of erythropoietin treatment or other exclusion criteria. On insulin pump therapy with current HbA1c of 7.2%. No history of heart failure, ischemic heart disease, epilepsy, thrombocytosis, or vision disturbances. Informed consent obtained. No current pregnancy or plans for pregnancy in the next year. No recent surgeries or cancer diagnoses. Willing to abstain from rigorous exercise, alcohol, and psychoactive drugs for the duration of the study. Willing to attend multiple study visits and undergo cognitive function testing, hypoglycemic clamps, and EEG monitoring.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with preterm pre-eclampsia during her current pregnancy. She has been hospitalized for the past week due to elevated blood pressure and proteinuria. She is currently 32 weeks pregnant and her obstetrician has decided to deliver the baby via c-section within the next few days to prevent further complications. The patient has a history of gestational diabetes in a previous pregnancy, but she has no other significant medical history. She takes no medications at the moment, and has no known allergies. Her vital signs are stable and she is not experiencing any symptoms at the moment. Her laboratory results show elevated blood pressure, proteinuria, and an elevated sFlt:PlGF ratio. Her creatinine level is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

A 30-year-old woman presents with active ulcerative colitis (UC) for the past year. She has a history of two UC flares in the past, both of which were treated with mesalamine. She is currently on vedolizumab (300mg IV infusion) therapy for the past 3 months to manage her UC symptoms. Her medical record shows previous positive fecal calprotectin levels as well as ulcerations in the sigmoid colon. She is breastfeeding her 6-week-old infant and has no history of breast implants, breast augmentation, or breast reduction surgery. She is committed to continuing breastfeeding throughout the duration of the study. She is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 22. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness or masses. She has no history of alcohol or illicit drug abuse. Her blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, and her heart rate is 80 beats per minute. She has a history of seasonal allergies and is currently taking antihistamines as needed.

A 4-year-old female patient with a history of regular dental check-ups and no previous dental treatment. The patient has multiple white spot lesions on the smooth enamel surface of the upper anterior primary teeth, with units of fluorescence (UF) ranging from 11-20 as determined by DIAGNOdent. The patient is attending the Paediatric Dentistry Postgraduate Program's Clinic for the treatment of these lesions. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to any of the compounds of the pastes and has no enamel hypoplasia or compromising systemic diseases. The parents have given their signed informed consent for the child's participation in the study.

62-year-old man diagnosed with Siewert Type II adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction. He presents with dysphagia, regurgitation, and weight loss over the past several months. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type II diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no previous history of esophagectomy or gastrectomy. CT scans and endoscopic biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma with no evidence of distant metastasis or invasion of surrounding organs. The patient has an ECOG score of 1 and an ASA score of II. Pulmonary function tests showed an FEV1% of 70% of expected value. The patient provides informed consent and is willing to undergo transthoracic single-hole assisted laparoscopic radical gastrectomy for the treatment of Siewert Type II adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction.

The patient is a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with hormone-receptor positive breast cancer. She underwent lumpectomy and was prescribed anastrozole, but has not started taking it yet. She will need radiation therapy as part of her standard care. She is a non-smoker and does not use nicotine in any form. She has a history of hypertension, well-controlled with medication, but does not have diabetes or high cholesterol. She had a gastric surgery 10 years ago for an ulcer and has not taken weight-loss medication since then. She is physically active and follows a healthy diet. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effects of anastrozole on her cardiovascular risk factors.

A 52-year-old woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a new drug called ONO-5788. She has no significant medical history, no allergies to medications, and she is not taking any prescription medications. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and her vital signs are normal. She underwent a routine physical examination, laboratory tests, and an ECG, which did not show any abnormalities. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. In the past two years, she has not suffered from alcoholism or drug abuse. She has never been diagnosed with gallstones, cholangitis, cholecystitis, pancreatitis, hypothyroidism, diabetes, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, thrombocytopenia, inflammatory bowel disease, or vitamin B12 deficiency. She has not had any abdominal surgery. She has normal serum electrolyte levels and her blood pressure is within the normal range. She does not engage in strenuous physical exercise regularly. She has not donated blood or plasma recently. She has not tested positive for HIV, HBsAg, or HCV.

A 35-year-old female patient with a history of anxiety and depression for the past 5 years came to the CHU Brugmann Hospital for treatment. The patient reported a persistent feeling of sadness, loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and recurrent thoughts of death or suicide. The patient also reported experiencing frequent panic attacks, with symptoms such as palpitations, sweating, and shortness of breath. The patient has no significant medical history, and she is not currently taking any medication for her condition. The physical examination was normal, and laboratory tests did not reveal any abnormality. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial as she was interested in finding out more about her condition and how she can manage it better.

A 16-year-old girl presented to the clinic with a BMI of 42. She has a history of obesity for the past 7 years and has tried various diets and weight loss programs with no success. She is experiencing difficulty with physical activity due to her weight and has been bullied at school because of her size. She has no history of any congenital or acquired anomalies of the GI tract and has no previous history of any psychiatric problems. She is motivated to lose weight and has the support of her family. Her pediatric psychologist has confirmed that she is emotionally mature and has adequate family support to comply with the study protocol. She is interested in participating in the study to receive the Lap-band system to help her achieve her weight loss goals.

Mrs. Rodriguez, a 38-year-old Hispanic mother of a 7-year-old child, is seeking help for her daughter's learning difficulties at school. Her daughter was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia two years ago and underwent chemotherapy treatment, which is now completed. However, since then, her daughter has had difficulty catching up with her peers in terms of school functioning and learning. Mrs. Rodriguez speaks only Spanish and would prefer a bilingual therapist for any intervention program. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on improving their daughter's learning and school functioning.

Pt is a 56yo M with a history of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring mechanical ventilation for > 48 hours. He is currently in the ICU and has a cuff leak volume (CLV) < 110 mL. The patient meets the weaning criteria: temperature ≤ 38°C for > 8 hours, discontinuous use of sedatives, heart rate ≥ 70 and ≤ 130 /min, systolic blood pressure (SBP) ≥ 80 mm Hg in the absence of vasopressors, fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) ≤ 0.6, PaO2 ≥ 60, and partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2)/FiO2 ratio > 200, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) ≤ 5 cm H2O, rapid and shallow ratio of frequency to tidal volume (f/VT ≤ 105), minute ventilation ≤ 15 L/min, and pH ≥ 7.3. The patient's supplemental oxygen is being maintained to keep his oxygen saturation > 95% as measured by a pulse oximeter. The patient has not received corticosteroids in the past 7 days. The patient has not had more than one tracheal intubation during his hospital stay and is hemodynamically stable with no profound recalcitrant hypoxemia. The patient is able to provide informed consent or a relative can provide consent on his behalf.

Patient is a 65-year-old man who was admitted to the emergency room with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. He was diagnosed with acute ischemic stroke and treated with intravenous thrombolysis (rtPA) within the recommended time frame. The patient was then transferred to the stroke unit for observation and rehabilitation. The treating physician decided to include the patient in the Cerebrolysin REGistry study in Stroke, and the patient provided informed consent. The patient had a pre-morbid mRS score of 1, indicating that he was independent prior to the stroke. He is expected to have successful follow-up for the maximum duration of 100 days. No exclusion criteria were met.

This is a 28 year old male who sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI) 8 months ago while playing football. He was tackled from behind and hit his head on the ground. He was initially unconscious but regained consciousness quickly after. He was taken to the emergency department where a CT scan was performed, which showed a small subdural hematoma. He was admitted to the hospital and observed for 24 hours. He was discharged with a diagnosis of mild TBI and told to follow up with his primary care doctor. Since the injury, he has had persistent headaches, difficulty with attention and memory, and fatigue. He has not been able to return to work as a construction worker due to his symptoms. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders prior to the injury. He is not currently taking any medications. He speaks English fluently and is able to undergo MRI scanning. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his symptoms.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with a chronic bone infection in his left ankle. He has been experiencing pain, swelling, and limited mobility for the past six months. He underwent surgical management of the infection and is currently on postoperative IV antibiotic therapy for 10 days. The bacterium causing the infection is a susceptible anaerobe in skin flora that is susceptible to clindamycin and rifampin. The patient has no known allergies to lincosamides or rifamycins. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has a normal liver function and a creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min. He weighs 80 kg and is 170 cm tall. He is willing to participate in the study and has consented to it. He is not currently under guardianship and is entitled to French National Health Insurance.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of Tourette syndrome, diagnosed at the age of 8. He presents with multiple motor tics, including eye blinking, facial grimacing, and throat clearing. He also complains of frequent vocal tics such as barking and grunting, which have interfered with his social and professional life. Additionally, he has experienced rage attacks, anxiety, and depression. He has tried various medications in the past, including antipsychotics and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), but has not found significant relief. He has not received any behavioral treatments for tics. He is currently not using any cannabis-based medications or CBM, and has not used them in the past 30 days. He does not have any allergies to cannabis, cannabinoids, or sesame oil. He has signed written informed consent and is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up procedures. He is not an employee of the sponsor or an employee or close relative of the investigator.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer in her left breast. She has no significant past medical history and is currently undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy with anthracyclines and taxanes. Her mammogram and ultrasound show a unifocal tumor with no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient's tumor is negative for c-erbB2 by immunohistochemistry. She has measurable disease by ultrasound and is willing to undergo positron emission tomography (PET) using 3'-deoxy-3'-(18F) fluorothymidine (^18F-FLT) to assess her response to chemotherapy before surgery. The patient has a normal ECOG performance status, hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. She is not pregnant or nursing, and if fertile, she agrees to use effective contraception during the study. The patient has no history of alcohol dependency or prior reaction to ethanol injection. She is not participating in another concurrent therapeutic study with an experimental drug.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. She has a family history of heart disease, with her father having a heart attack in his early 60s. The patient is a non-smoker, with no history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes. She is currently taking no medications and has no known allergies. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle, exercising 3-4 times per week. Her recent physical examination and electrocardiogram (ECG) were unremarkable. She has never had any cardiac imaging tests before. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and efficiency of CT angiography and stress testing in the diagnosis of suspected coronary artery disease.

A 56-year-old Caucasian man presented with a history of coronary artery disease with recurrent angina pectoris in the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with hypertension 10 years ago and is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. He has a history of smoking cigarettes for 25 years but quit 5 years ago. He is currently working as a truck driver and reports a sedentary lifestyle. He has had no previous history of myocardial infarction, stroke or peripheral vascular disease. He is not aware of any family history of cardiovascular disease. He has been on stable medical therapy for the past 3 months, including aspirin 81mg, atorvastatin 40mg and metoprolol 50mg twice daily. His most recent ECG shows sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. His echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 45%. He reports chest pain during moderate exertion and occasionally at rest. His most recent Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) angina class is III.

The patient is a 27-year-old Caucasian female diagnosed with cystic fibrosis. She has been experiencing recurrent respiratory exacerbations and is currently stable, with no evidence of respiratory exacerbation within a month of enrollment. Her FEV1 is greater than 45% predicted as calculated by Wang reference equations. She is willing to adhere to the prescribed treatment regimen and is competent in performing spirometry. She has no diagnosis of Allergic Broncho-Pulmonary Aspergillosis or a persistent culture for B.cepacia complex within the previous 1 year period, nor is she on active treatment for non Tuberculous Mycobacterium. She has not used intravenous antibiotics within the previous 14 days of enrollment, nor has she initiated or changed maintenance therapy within 14 days of enrollment. She has not used systemic corticosteroids within 14 days of enrollment. She is not concurrently participating in another study that could potentially affect the present study. She has not experienced haemoptysis of over 20 mls on more than 2 occasions within the previous 30 days from enrollment, nor has she experienced a pneumothorax in the six months preceding the study. She does not have any condition or abnormality that would compromise her safety or the quality of the data.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment or intervention. It is an observational study that will use data from the Whitehall II cohort study of British civil servants. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this trial.

A 58-year-old man presents with chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. He has a history of smoking, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Upon evaluation, he is found to have significant blockages in his coronary arteries. He is recommended for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the use of the SeQuent® SCB. He has no known allergies to sirolimus or any of the components of the coating. He is not pregnant or lactating, and does not have any bleeding disorders or other disorders that would restrict the use of platelet aggregation inhibitor therapy and anti-coagulation therapy. His ejection fraction is normal and his vascular reference diameter is within the eligible range for treatment with the SeQuent® SCB. He is willing and able to comply with the necessary medication regimen and follow-up appointments. He is enrolled in the clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of the SeQuent® SCB for the treatment of his coronary artery disease.

A 35-year-old female was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) three years ago. She had received chemotherapy and had achieved complete remission, but unfortunately, she relapsed one year ago. She received a second round of chemotherapy but did not achieve complete remission. She was referred to the clinical trial for the combination chemotherapy and alemtuzumab. She has no history of hepatitis B, any bacterial or fungal infections, or any other malignancies. Her performance status is 2, bilirubin and creatinine are within normal limits, and she is HIV negative. She is not pregnant, and she is using effective contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with kidney cancer and is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic nephrectomy surgery. He has no other medical conditions and is in overall good health. The patient is experiencing moderate to severe pain in the abdominal and back area due to the cancer, but is otherwise compliant with treatment and medications. He is able to provide informed consent and understands the risks and benefits of the proposed study. The patient has a BMI of 25 and is expected to stay in the hospital overnight after the surgery. He has not used opioids for more than 3 months prior to surgery and has no history of chronic pain. The patient is eligible for the study and can be enrolled in the pilot randomized control trial to evaluate ESP blockade for laparoscopic nephrectomy surgeries.

A 55-year-old male smoker presents with a persistent cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing. A chest X-ray revealed a mass in the left lung. A CT scan confirmed the diagnosis of stage IIIB squamous NSCLC. The patient has no history of allergies or severe medical conditions. He has a history of smoking 1 pack per day for the past 35 years and quit smoking 6 months ago. His vital signs are stable, and his ECOG performance status is 0. The patient has not received any prior systemic therapy for lung cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has agreed to use contraception during the study. The patient's laboratory tests show normal values for liver and kidney function. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient has not received denosumab for bone metastases. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma six months ago. She already received gemcitabine-based chemotherapy, but it was not effective. She has lost significant weight over the past few months and is now experiencing fatigue, weakness, and loss of appetite. She has a BMI of 21 and weighs 65 kg. She has no history of major surgery recently and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to perform double-barrier contraception during the study. Her expected life expectancy is more than three months. She has no other significant medical conditions and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl who has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation. She was diagnosed with bronchiolitis and has been receiving standard treatment for the condition. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has no known allergies. The patient's weight is 18 kg and her height is 100 cm. The parents have voluntarily signed the informed consent document for the clinical trial. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for Group I, which includes subjects ages ≥2 through <6 years old. She is expected to require continuous intravenous sedation for at least 6 hours. The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain in her right hand due to carpal tunnel syndrome. She has been advised to undergo minor hand surgery by her orthopedic surgeon to relieve the pain. She has no history of narcotic use in the previous 3 months and is not allergic or intolerant to hydrocodone or acetaminophen. She is not pregnant and has no acute trauma or post-operative complications. She is able to provide personal consent to the procedure and the research. She is interested in participating in the study and has agreed to be randomized to receive either 10 or 30 tabs of 5 mg hydrocodone/325 mg acetaminophen following her surgery.

45 yo F with previous diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, status post distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy, with recent follow-up MRI showing suspicious lymph node involvement. Patient is currently asymptomatic and has no significant medical history other than the NET. The patient is currently not on any somatostatin analogues or other anti-tumor treatments. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for imaging using DOTATATE peptide labelled with the 64Cu tracer to accurately detect the presence and extent of her NET disease. The patient has previous experience with OctreoScan imaging and is familiar with the diagnostic process. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to provide written consent to participate.

34 yo female with a history of major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 10 years presents with persistent symptoms of low mood, loss of interest and pleasure, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating despite being on sertraline 100mg daily for the past 3 months. She reports a past history of non-response to fluoxetine and citalopram. She denies any suicidal ideation, self-harm, or psychotic symptoms. She has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric hospitalizations. She is currently employed as a teacher and reports difficulty with concentration and low energy affecting her job performance. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy of a new medication as an augmentation therapy to her current antidepressant.

The patient is a premature infant born at 32 weeks gestational age and admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Marmara University. The infant was diagnosed with apnea of prematurity (AOP) and received caffeine therapy for 4 weeks with a loading dose of 20 mg/kg and a maintenance dose of 5 mg/kg/day. The infant did not have perinatal asphyxia, intraventricular hemorrhage grade 3 or higher, retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) of stage 3 or higher, or any major congenital anomalies. The infant did not receive any sedative or anticonvulsant drugs during data collection. The infant will be followed up for sleep architecture and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 6 and 12 months corrected age. The sleep and activity behavior of the infant will be recorded by actigraphy, sleep diary, and polysomnography. Neurodevelopment will be assessed by neurological examination defined by Hammersmith, Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ-2), and Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development at 6 and 12 months corrected age.

A 50-year-old male patient with a previous diagnosis of multiple myeloma underwent a single autologous stem cell transplantation 90 days ago. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has recovered from the toxicity of previous chemotherapy, except for grade 1 neurotoxicity and hematological toxicity. His creatinine level is within normal range of 1.8 mg/dL. His absolute neutrophil count is 1200/uL, platelet count is 90,000/uL, and hemoglobin is 10.5 g/dL. He has no history of myocardial infarction or uncontrolled heart failure. He has no active malignancy requiring therapy, except for multiple myeloma, and has not undergone an allogeneic bone marrow/peripheral blood stem cell transplant. He is willing to return to the enrolling institution for follow-up and provide bone marrow and blood samples for correlative research purposes. His measurable disease of multiple myeloma at the time of baseline values for disease assessment is defined by serum monoclonal protein of 1.5 g/dL. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 28 days after stopping treatment. He has no known allergies to any of the components of the investigational treatment regimen or required ancillary treatments.

4-year-old child weighing 15kg, recently diagnosed with uncomplicated malaria, will be enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of two oral antimalarial drugs commonly used in Mozambique: artemether-lumefantrine (AL) and Amodiaquine-Artesunate (AQ-AS). The child must have a microscopically confirmed mono-infection of Plasmodium falciparum in blood, with a parasite density between 2,000 and 200,000 asexual parasites per microliter of blood, and an axillary temperature of at least 37.5°C or a history of fever in the previous 24 hours. The child must not display any signs of severe or complicated malaria, as defined by the WHO, nor have any other chronic or serious illnesses. The child must be able to swallow the medication and have a haemoglobin level of at least 5.0 g/dL. The child must be a resident of the study area and have the ability to attend follow-up visits for a period of 28 days. The child must not have a history of hypersensitivity to study medications or be taking any medication that may interfere with the pharmacokinetics of antimalarials. The child must not have taken antimalarial drugs or drugs with antimalarial activity in the past 7 days, nor be receiving continuous prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole if they are HIV positive. A written informed consent from the parent, guardian or caregiver must be provided.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory loss for the past year. She has difficulty remembering recent events and has lost track of conversations. She has also been experiencing difficulty completing daily tasks and needs assistance to manage her finances. She was diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease and has been on AchE inhibitors for the past 6 months, with no significant improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new treatment and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She has no history of CNS disease and is not taking any protein therapeutics targeting Abeta.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad most of the day, nearly every day, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy.
