She has difficulty sleeping and has experienced a significant decrease in her energy levels. She has no history of suicidal intent/ideation, psychotic illness, or alcohol/drug misuse. She has not received psychological treatment for her depression symptoms and is currently not on any medication. She owns an iPhone 8 and is interested in participating in a study that investigates the use of a smartwatch as a tool to support an internet-delivered Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) based intervention for depression. She sees this as an opportunity to monitor her mood in the moment, and keep track of her daily sleep and activity level. She is willing to complete questionnaires regarding the technology at three time points.

A 21-year-old male patient who is a member of a Military Organization in Bento Gonçalves, southern Brazil, is seeking dental care. He reports brushing his teeth twice a day, but he has no specific oral hygiene routine. He has no history of periodontal disease, and his general health is good. He has all his permanent teeth, and he has no dental implants, dental caries, or restorations at the cervical buccal surfaces. He does not wear orthodontic appliances. He has no deleterious habits such as smoking, alcohol consumption, or drug use. He is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the incidence and behavior of gingival fissures in young adults using soft and medium toothbrushes. He understands that the study is a randomized clinical trial and that he will be assigned to one of the two groups according to the toothbrush bristle stiffness. He agrees to attend the follow-up appointments and return the toothbrushes used at the end of each experimental phase.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who has been experiencing fever, headache, and joint pain for the past 2 days. He lives in a tropical region and is frequently exposed to mosquitoes. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a BMI of 23. His NS1 strip test confirmed dengue virus infection, and his symptom onset was within the last 48 hours. He is willing to use two forms of contraception until three months after receiving the last dose of study drug. He has not taken any steroids or immuno-suppressive therapies. His laboratory test results are within the normal range, except for the ones associated with dengue infection. He has no history of HIV or any autoimmune disease. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

Pt is a 45yo male who has just experienced a sudden cardiac arrest at his workplace. The event was witnessed and bystander CPR was initiated immediately. Emergency medical services were called and arrived within 5 minutes. Upon arrival, they found the patient in ventricular fibrillation, and they began advanced cardiac life support procedures. The patient received a total of 3 shocks and multiple rounds of epinephrine and amiodarone with no return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). The patient was then transferred to the hospital. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient had a pulseless ventricular tachycardia and received an additional 3 shocks with ROSC achieved. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial to verify the accuracy of the Sherlock algorithm of Philips MRx monitor/defibrillator in identifying shockable rhythms during chest compressions. He meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 28 year-old female who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 4 years ago. She participated in the previous studies 461/PO and 901 and received all doses of the study medication according to protocol. Her MMTT stimulated C-peptide concentration is ≥ 0.20 nmol/L, indicating clinically significant residual beta-cell function. She is not currently pregnant, does not intend to become pregnant during the study period, and is willing to use effective contraception. She has no clinical evidence of any diabetes-related complications, severe allergies, or immune deficiency. She is currently managing her diabetes with insulin therapy and regular exercise.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has noticed a significant loss of elasticity in her neck skin. She is in good health with a BMI of 25 and has no known allergies or medical conditions. She has never undergone any cosmetic surgeries on her neck or face. She is willing to comply with the protocol requirements, including returning for follow-up visits and abstaining from exclusionary procedures for the duration of the study. She is of childbearing potential and agrees to have a negative urine pregnancy test result at Visit 1 and to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to see an improvement in her submental volume and cervicomental angle.

A 7-year-old boy named Ali was referred to the pediatric surgery department at Mayo Hospital Lahore for the treatment of his hernia. He has had a bulge in his right groin area for the past few months, which sometimes causes discomfort and pain. He has no history of any underlying disease, and his parents report that he is otherwise healthy. He has no known allergies, and he is not taking any medications. The examination reveals a reducible right inguinal hernia, and he fulfills the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

A 25-year-old male college student presents with persistent anterior knee pain that began three months ago. He reports that the pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting, running, and squatting. He denies any history of knee surgery or injuries. He is physically active and participates in sports. He has no significant medical history and takes no medication. On physical examination, tenderness is noted over the patella with no evidence of swelling, crepitus, or instability. He is diagnosed with anterior knee pain and is eligible for participation in the joint position sense clinical trial.

Pt is a 57yo M who underwent a radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer 6 months ago. He has been experiencing urinary incontinence since the surgery, with a frequency of 5-6 episodes per day. The patient has been using pads, but they have not been effective in controlling his incontinence. He is motivated to find a solution to his incontinence to improve his quality of life. The patient has no history of neurological degenerative chronic diseases or implantable cardioverter defibrillators, and he does not have any iatrogenic metals in the pelvic region. He understands the proposed instruments and is willing to participate in the research study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled to undergo a biopsy. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage his blood pressure. The patient has no known allergies or adverse reactions to medications. He is able to give written informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is not part of any vulnerable population or a child.

The patient is a 28-year-old Japanese female who presents to the clinic with abdominal pain, fever, and nausea for the past 3 days. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She denies any recent travel or exposure to sick individuals. A physical examination reveals tenderness in the lower abdomen with rebound tenderness. Blood tests show elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein levels. A CT scan of the abdomen shows evidence of intra-abdominal infection. The patient is diagnosed with intra-abdominal infection and is eligible for the clinical trial. She has no known allergies to metronidazole or ceftriaxone sodium. Her creatinine clearance is within normal limits, and she has no evidence of hepatic dysfunction. She is willing to provide a specimen for bacteriological efficacy assessment.

The patient is a 56 year-old woman who was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer six months ago. She has completed all primary treatments except for hormone therapy. She is post-menopausal, having had no menstrual periods for 2 years. She is currently taking hormone therapy. Her weight is 70 kgs and her ECOG status is 1. Her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 6 months. She currently performs less than 150 minutes of structured moderate-intensity or strenuous intensity exercise per week and has exercise intolerance as defined by a VO2peak below that predicted for sedentary age and sex-matched individuals. She is willing to be randomized to one of the study arms and is able to complete an acceptable baseline CPET. She has no absolute contraindications to cardiopulmonary exercise testing and no other condition or intercurrent illness that would make her a poor candidate for the trial. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve her physical fitness levels and quality of life.

A 48-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and cough. He had been feeling unwell for the past week and experienced worsening symptoms over the past two days. On arrival, he was hypoxic with an oxygen saturation of 85% on room air. His respiratory rate was 32 breaths per minute, and his heart rate was 110 beats per minute. On auscultation, there were bilateral crackles on lung examination. An arterial blood gas showed a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 60 mmHg. A chest X-ray revealed diffuse bilateral infiltrates consistent with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The patient was started on non-invasive ventilation, but his condition continued to deteriorate. He was subsequently intubated and started on mechanical ventilation. Despite aggressive management, including high levels of PEEP and prone positioning, the patient's oxygenation remained poor, and he was transferred for veno-venous ECMO. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is enrolled in the study to determine whether an ultra-protective multimodal strategy can reduce the lesions induced by mechanical ventilation compared to usual protective ventilatory management during ECMO.

A 60-year-old man came to the clinic with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of coronary artery disease for 5 years and underwent a coronary angioplasty 3 years ago. He has been experiencing chest pain on exertion and shortness of breath on and off for the past month. He is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history and has a family history of heart disease. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 8 years. His medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, metformin, and losartan. His blood pressure is 138/86 mmHg, and his heart rate is 78 bpm. His BMI is 30 kg/m2. He has no history of alcohol abuse or use of immunosuppressive drugs.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of heartburn on 2 out of the last 7 days. She has a history of GERD but has not been diagnosed with erosive esophagitis. Her Body Mass Index is within the limits specified in the protocol. She has no history of esophageal, duodenal or gastric surgery, and no history of severe liver disease. She is not currently experiencing any other significant disease or pathology that would be judged to be clinically significant by the investigator.

The patient is a 35 year old male who has been recently treated for drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis. He is HIV-negative and has completed at least 5 calendar months of TB treatment on Study Day 0. He is a resident of South Africa and is willing to be enrolled in the clinical trial. He is working as a laborer in a construction company and spends most of his time on physical activities. He is married and has three children. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His physical examination is unremarkable and he has no history of previous TB or any other chronic illness. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to complete the full course of TB treatment as well as the clinical trial.

55-year-old Chinese male with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The patient has undergone bilateral orchiectomy and/or androgen deprivation therapy with effective GnRH analogues. The patient has evidence of metastatic lesions in the bone and CT. The patient has had progressive disease despite castration and meets the criteria for PSA progression, soft tissue disease progression, and bone progression. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and laboratory tests that meet the inclusion criteria. The patient has an estimated life expectancy of greater than 6 months. The patient has not participated in any other clinical drug trials within the past month and does not have any brain metastases. The patient has not been on any medication that lowers the seizure threshold, 5α-reductase inhibitors, estrogen, or cyproterone within the past 4 weeks. The patient has not been previously treated with investigational or approved medications that inhibit testosterone synthesis or target testosterone receptors, except for bicalutamide and flutamide. The patient is not known to have any hypersensitivity to the study drugs and does not have any history of medication or drug abuse.

A 25-year-old healthy male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He works in a tech company and has no underlying disease. He does not smoke or use any nicotine products. His BMI is 23. He has no significant medical history, and his physical examination, laboratory profiles, vital signs, and ECGs are normal. He is not taking any medications, supplements, or herbal remedies. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. He has no history of allergy to any food or drugs. He has no family history of QTc prolongation or unexplainable sudden death at less than 50 years of age. He has no history of cardiac arrhythmia or conduction abnormalities. He is not lactose intolerant and has no significant food allergy. He has not participated in another clinical study within the last 90 days.

A 60-year-old male patient presents with severe pain and difficulty in walking due to osteoarthritis in his right hip. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are being managed with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient has undergone several imaging tests, including X-rays and MRI, which have confirmed the need for a total hip arthroplasty (THA) anterior approach. The patient has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and has given written consent. The patient is currently not experiencing any skin problems or allergies to acrylic. He does not have any open wounds or psoriasis. The patient does not have an active tumor site or lymphedema present before surgery. He does not have circulatory disorders such as phlebitis. The patient speaks English fluently and is able to understand and follow instructions.

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of episodic cluster headache that started when she was 28 years old. She experiences excruciating pain around her right eye and temple that lasts for 30-45 minutes, up to 8 times a day during a cluster period that lasts for 6-8 weeks. She also experiences nasal congestion, tearing, and drooping of her right eyelid during these attacks. She has tried multiple medications, including triptans, oxygen therapy, and verapamil, but with limited success in preventing or aborting the attacks. She has not tried any medications targeting the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) pathway. She has no significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and does not use illicit drugs. She has no history of psychiatric illness, cardiovascular disease, or other significant pain syndromes. She reports having at least one typical cluster headache attack per day for the past week. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of a new treatment for episodic cluster headache.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has struggled with obesity for most of her life. She has a BMI of 42 kg/m2 and suffers from hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea. She has tried various diets and exercise programs with limited success. She has been accepted for bariatric surgery and is eager to make long-term lifestyle changes to improve her health. She owns and frequently uses a smartphone and is comfortable with using different apps. She does not have any physical disabilities that would prevent her from walking on a daily basis. She has a good understanding of the Swedish language and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease. He has no significant family history of neurological disorders. He is currently taking levodopa for his symptoms, which have been affecting his daily activities and quality of life. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand his disease and the potential genetic factors involved. He is fluent in English and is able to understand and provide informed consent. He has no history of blood transfusions, hematologic malignancies, or bone marrow transplant. He is able to perform study activities and complete surveys either online, in-person, or on paper.

A 4-year-old male child presents with bilateral severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss. His parents noticed that he was not responding to sounds and was not developing language skills at the expected rate. The child was born at term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. There is no family history of hearing loss. The child has not received any hearing aids or cochlear implants before. A hearing evaluation confirmed the diagnosis of severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss in both ears. The child is prelingually deaf. The family is interested in exploring options for hearing rehabilitation, and the child is considered eligible for the clinical trial for vestibular cochlear implant in hearing-impaired children. The child has no other pathologies affecting balance and has no orthopedic problems. The child will be implanted with a cochlear implant in one or both ears, depending on the results of vestibular assessments to ensure preservation of vestibular function. The child will be followed up closely to monitor any postoperative vestibular symptoms or changes in vestibular function.

Patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman with no history of cardiovascular disease. She has all 12 anterior teeth present and speaks English fluently. She has no clinical role at the University of Illinois College of Dentistry and is not taking aspirin, other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or statins. She is not pregnant or nursing, not taking birth control pills, and not using any hormone released birth control device. She has not taken antibiotics within two weeks of the data collection appointment and has not experienced xerostomia, any illness, infection or tissue injury within two weeks of the data collection appointment. She does not have arthritis, lupus, or any other chronic inflammatory conditions or syndromes, and has no allergies to dyes or over the counter products. She has all anterior teeth present, with no missing teeth or visible decay or staining in the anterior region. She has not had a dental prophylaxis or any new restoration placed anywhere in the oral cavity within 30 days of the data collection visit. She is willing and able to commit to two 30-minute appointments, which must be 1 month apart, and is interested in testing a toothpaste to reduce plaque and inflammation.

Patient is a 30-year-old male with a diagnosis of HIV and hepatitis-B co-infection. The patient has not been previously treated for either condition and currently has detectable HBV viremia. The patient is willing to start antiretroviral therapy and is over 18 years of age. The patient has the ability to sign the consent form and is interested in participating in the trial.

A 25-year-old male patient presented at the clinic with chronic sacrococcygeal pilonidal disease. He has been experiencing pain, discomfort, and embarrassment for several months, which has affected his daily activities and caused him to miss work. He has a history of hirsutism and has tried various treatments, including topical ointments and antibiotics, but they have not been effective. He has no underlying medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke and exercises regularly. He has no known allergies, and his surgical history is unremarkable. He is willing to undergo

A 55-year-old woman has been experiencing chest pain at rest for the past 2 days, with episodes lasting for at least 10 minutes. She has a prior history of cardiovascular disease and is currently taking aspirin. She is planning to undergo an invasive strategy after receiving the study drug for 12 to 96 hours. She has no history of stroke, central nervous system damage, bleeding disorders, or major surgery. She is willing and able to give informed consent and comply with study procedures and follow-up through 1 year. She is not currently on renal dialysis and does not have any serious illnesses or any conditions that would pose a significant hazard to her if investigational therapy was to be initiated.

34-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of Behcet's disease based on the international criteria for BD. The patient has a history of recurrent oral and genital ulcers, as well as skin lesions. She has been experiencing joint pain and swelling, as well as occasional episodes of uveitis. The patient has been off immunosuppressive therapy for the past 6 months and has not had any recent flares. She has no history of infection, malignancy, other connective tissue disease, chronic liver or kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, hypertension or hyperlipidemia. The patient is willing to undergo laboratory assessments and carotid intima media thickness measurements as part of the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 28 kg/m² and a waist circumference of 90 cm. She is currently enrolled in the RNPC weight reduction program and has been struggling with weight loss for the past year. She works from home due to the Covid-19 pandemic and has been experiencing increased stress and anxiety levels, which have led to compulsive food intake and lack of physical activity. Her sleeping pattern has also been disturbed, and she frequently wakes up in the middle of the night feeling anxious. She drinks alcohol occasionally, but not in excessive amounts. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the impact of confinement on her weight loss journey and to receive additional support during this challenging time.

A 28-year-old healthy male living in or near Dar-es-Salaam with no history of malaria infection in the past five years is being sought for a controlled human malaria infection study using intradermal injection of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites. The volunteer must be in good health and not suffering from any chronic illness, including HIV/AIDS, with no plans to travel outside the Dar-es-salaam or Coast Region in the first month of the study. The volunteer must be willing to undergo HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests, and to stay in the hospital during parts of the study, including overnight after challenge, up to 15 days during follow-up, and 3 days of Coartem® treatment. The volunteer must be reachable by mobile phone 24/7 during the whole study period and agree not to donate blood during the study period. The volunteer must be willing to undergo a Pf sporozoite challenge and take curative treatment for malaria (Coartem®) and any other medication which may be prescribed by a study doctor during the study period. The volunteer must be available to attend all study visits and agree not to participate in another study during the study period. The volunteer must sign the informed consent form and answer correctly 15 out of 15 questions demonstrating their understanding of the meaning and procedures of the study.

The patient is a 52 year old man with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are controlled with medication. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father suffering a heart attack at the age of 58. He is currently overweight with a BMI of 31 and has a waist circumference of 108 cm. His recent blood work showed a total cholesterol level of 6.5 mmol/L and an HDL cholesterol level of 1.1 mmol/L. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of alcohol abuse. He does not take any supplements or medications other than his prescribed hypertension and cholesterol medication. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of different dietary fats on blood vessel elasticity and other risk factors for heart disease.

32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year, with a history of regular menstrual cycles lasting between 24 and 35 days. She has no history of infertility medication use in the past month and has a BMI between 17.5 and 38.0 kg/m^2. She has no known endocrine or metabolic abnormalities, and no known tumors. She has a regular male partner with adequate semen analysis for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). She has never been an oocyte donor or embryo recipient, gestational or surrogate carrier. She has not had more than two previous controlled ovarian stimulation cycles for IVF/ICSI. She also has no known history of recurrent miscarriage or active thromboembolism or severe thrombophlebitis. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to any active ingredient or excipients in the medicinal products used in the trial. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

32 year old male seeking orthodontic treatment for cosmetic reasons. He has no significant medical history and is in good overall health. He speaks fluent Dutch and is able to understand and follow instructions. He has been self-conscious about his crooked teeth and believes that having straight teeth will improve his confidence and self-esteem. He has no previous experience with orthodontic treatment and is motivated to improve the appearance of his teeth. He has realistic expectations and is willing to comply with the necessary orthodontic procedures.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired teacher living in Montreal, Canada. She was admitted to the Jewish General Hospital's cardiovascular unit due to chest pain and shortness of breath. She has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes, all of which are well-controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. She reports feeling tired and weak lately and has noticed a decline in her ability to perform daily activities like cooking and cleaning. She has no history of falls or fractures. Upon assessment with the Essential Frailty Toolset, her score was 2/5, indicating pre-frailty. She speaks fluent English and has given informed consent to participate in the TARGET-EFT trial. She is using a walker for mobility during her hospital stay. Her vital signs are stable, and she is clinically stable. She is expected to be discharged in 4 days.

The patient is a healthy male or non-pregnant female who completed either the LIPO-202-CL-18 or LIPO-202-CL-19 study. They are capable of providing written consent and willing to adhere to the study procedures and schedule. They are not currently pregnant, and if female, are using adequate birth control methods. They do not plan on starting a weight loss or exercise program during the study, nor do they plan to enroll in another investigational drug or device study. They are likely and able to adhere to the study visit schedule.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with IgA nephropathy. He has a history of proteinuria, with levels greater than 1.0 g/day confirmed on two separate occasions within the past 6 months. He has been taking ACE inhibitors for at least 3 months for his hypertension. His eGFR is 45 mL/min/1.73m^2. He is married and works as a construction worker. He is a non-smoker and does not use any recreational drugs. He enjoys playing basketball on the weekends. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 28 days. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old female who has been experiencing bleeding and swelling of the gums for the past few months. She has noticed that her teeth feel loose and she has bad breath. She has a history of smoking, but she quit 6 months ago. She has no known systemic diseases and does not take any medications regularly. She has a total of 26 natural teeth excluding third molars. Upon clinical examination, she has at least two non-adjacent sites per quadrant with a probing depth (PD) of ≥ 5mm and clinical attachment level (CAL) of ≥ 5mm. Radiographical examination reveals alveolar bone loss affecting more than 30% of her teeth. She is diagnosed with periodontitis and is willing to participate in the study to investigate IL-32 isoforms levels in GCF and plasma before and after nonsurgical periodontal treatment.

Pt is a 28yo F, currently 20 weeks pregnant with her first child, and has been attending regular prenatal visits. She has no history of chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of Pilates on reducing the incidence of pelvic floor dysfunction during pregnancy and has given her written consent to participate. She is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 25. She has no history of physical activity intolerance or physical limitations. She will be assigned to either the intervention group, which will participate in the Pilates program, or the control group, which will maintain their usual monitoring of pregnancy. She will be evaluated for eligibility by filling out the international physical activity questionnaire (IPAQ) during her initial visit.

A 45-year old male was recently diagnosed with hypertension during a routine check-up. He has a past medical history of high cholesterol levels and is currently on medication to control it. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He works in an office and spends most of his day sitting. He is overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m2. He has never engaged in regular physical exercise before. He reports feeling tired and lethargic most of the time. He is married with two children and is motivated to improve his health. He is compliant with his medications and attends regular follow-up appointments with his primary care physician. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effects of aerobic and strength training on his blood pressure and overall cardiovascular health.

The patient is a 7-month-old Aboriginal baby boy living in a remote community in the Northern Territory of Australia. He has received one dose of RV1 vaccination and is due for his second dose. He has had no previous medical history of note and is currently well with no symptoms of gastroenteritis. His parents are willing for him to participate in the study and have given informed consent. They are aware of the requirements of the protocol and are willing for their child's participation in the trial to be recorded within the Northern Territory Immunisation Register. They are also willing for the study team to obtain a vaccination history and medical history from hospitalisation and laboratory databases, the disease notification register, the participant's electronic medical records and/or from the participant's primary care provider for the period from enrolment to age 36 months. The baby boy has no contraindications for RV1 vaccination and is eligible for enrolment in the trial.

This is a 52-year-old female who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy five years ago. Her menopausal symptoms have been managed with hormone replacement therapy, but she reports a significant decrease in her sexual desire and arousal. She has tried other treatments for HSDD including counseling and behavioral therapy, but has not seen any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for LibiGel 300mcg to help improve her sexual function and quality of life. She reports no history of allergic reactions to androgens, topical alcohol, or any component of the formulation. She has no systemic skin diseases or local skin abnormalities in the area of application, and no other primary female sexual dysfunction. She has no medical condition that could affect or interfere with sexual function, and is not currently using systemic transdermal gel or cream estrogen therapy. She is motivated to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

This is a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing symptoms of pelvic organ prolapse, including a bulging sensation and discomfort. She has not had any prior surgical repair for her prolapse and is planning to have a total hysterectomy as part of her pelvic reconstructive surgery. She is between 1 and 10 years postmenopausal and has not received any estrogen replacement therapy in the last month. She is physically capable of daily application of vaginal cream. She does not have a history of connective tissue disease or vaginal radiation, and does not have any contraindications for estrogen replacement therapy, such as a history of deep vein thrombosis, stroke, coronary artery disease, or breast or endometrial cancer. She is not currently using steroid cream for Lichen sclerosis and has not had a recent history of vaginal infection or vaginitis. Her BMI is less than 35.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant female in her last trimester residing in Karachi, Pakistan. Her past medical history is non-significant and she has no underlying complications or co-morbidities. She lives less than 30 kms away from the study clinic and has resided there for at least 1 year. The patient has indicated that she will not move from her current residence for the 5 months after the birth of the child (study period). She is carrying a singleton full-term pregnancy with no underlying complications, and the baby has an APGAR score of 7 or higher 5 minutes after delivery. The patient is willing to participate in a double-blinded two-arm randomized placebo-controlled trial that aims to assess the effectiveness of lactoferrin in increasing mucosal and serum immunity in children following administration of poliovirus vaccines. The patient will be followed up through 6 months of age. The patient is compliant and willing to administer all vaccinations according to the routine immunization schedule.

A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. The patient has been on antihypertensive medications for the past 3 years but has not been able to achieve adequate blood pressure control. She reports a blood pressure of 145/95 mmHg at the last visit to her primary care physician. The patient expresses interest in alternative therapies such as acupuncture to manage her hypertension. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities and is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of electroacupuncture as a complementary treatment for hypertension. Her blood pressure at the screening visit is 150/100 mmHg.

Patient is a healthy 18-year-old with no history of eye problems or diseases. They have clear vision and have never worn glasses or contacts. They will participate in a study to examine the characteristics of the crystalline proteins in pristine young normal lenses using a method called dynamic light scattering (DLS). The DLS device uses a very dim laser light to study the lens of the eye, detecting proteins in the lens and identifying early changes that may make the device useful in future cataract studies. The patient will undergo a medical history and an eye examination with dilation to measure visual acuity and examine the front of the eye and retina. They will then have DLS measurements taken of their lenses, which will be used for comparison with aging and cataract DLS measurements to obtain normative data for future lens

A 43 yo F with a history of peripheral T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma was initially diagnosed 3 years ago and underwent multiple lines of chemotherapy, resulting in a partial response. Over the last 6 months, she has noticed an increase in her lymph nodes and has experienced fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. A biopsy of her lymph nodes confirms relapsed disease. She has not received any radiation therapy, stem cell transplant, or allogeneic stem cell transplant. She has measurable disease based on CT scan and bone marrow involvement. Her Zubrod performance status is 1, and her laboratory values are adequate for enrollment in the study. She has no other active malignancies and is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing watering from her left eye for the last year. She reports discomfort and irritation in the eye due to the constant watering. She has tried using eye drops and ointments, but they have not provided any relief. Her ophthalmologist diagnosed her with ectropion of her left eyelid and referred her for surgery. The patient has no other significant medical history and takes no medication regularly. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the two surgical methods for eyelid ectropion and improve her quality of life.

32 year old healthy female with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m^2 presenting for a clinical trial to study insulin sensitivity. She has never smoked or used any nicotine products. She is currently on oral contraceptives for birth control and has been on the same regimen for 3 months. She is willing to avoid regular exercise from screening through the end of the treatment period. The patient denies any history of diabetes, glaucoma, or substance dependence. She has not had any serious infections or vaccinations in the past 3 months. The patient denies any chronic use of NSAIDs or acetaminophen, except for low-dose Aspirin. She has not used any antipsychotic medications in the past.

The patient is a 45 year old female diagnosed with primary pulmonary hypertension (PPH) with WHO functional class III symptoms. She has not been previously exposed to an endothelin receptor antagonist (ETRA) such as sitaxsentan, bosentan or ambrisentan. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, fatigue and dizziness for the past 6 months. She is currently on oxygen therapy and taking diuretics and calcium channel blockers to manage her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of adding sildenafil to her current treatment plan.

The patient is a 35 year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia according to the criteria of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th edition (DSM IV). He has a history of non-adherence to oral antipsychotic medications due to forgetfulness and lack of insight into his condition. He has been living independently for the past year and has a supportive family. He currently takes no medications and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. He has no major medical conditions and is in generally good health. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to receive long-acting injectable risperidone every two weeks for at least one year. He is not currently pregnant or nursing and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity, who presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has no known exposure to COVID-19. He was found to be positive for COVID-19 on a nasal swab RT-PCR assay. On examination, his respiratory rate is 32 cycles/minute, oxygen saturation is 88% on 8L/min of oxygen via nasal cannula. CT scan shows bilateral infiltrates >30%. Laboratory values show CRP of 120 g/dL, lymphocytes of 500 /mm3, D-dimer of 1.5 L, and Ferritin of 600. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is randomized to receive either dexamethasone or tocilizumab. He provides informed consent for treatment with off-label agents and participation in the study.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) that were detected based on 68Ga-DOTATOC/DOTATATE scan. She has a history of carcinoid syndrome with symptoms of flushing, diarrhea, and wheezing for the past 6 months. She underwent surgery to remove the primary tumour in her small intestine but had multiple metastases to the liver. She was started on octreotide therapy but experienced minimal symptom relief. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is stable on octreotide. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new imaging technique to detect NETs. She does not have any history of allergies or other medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study.

We are seeking individuals who have been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and have at least two of the following symptoms: resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, asymmetrical onset of symptoms, and symptomatic response to L-dopa. Participants must not have undergone previous thalamotomy on the implanted side, have significant brain atrophy or structural damage seen on CT or MRI, marked cognitive dysfunction, active psychiatric symptoms, or concurrent neurological or other uncontrolled medical disorders. This study aims to identify genetic variants associated with Parkinson's disease through genetic analysis of exome-sequencing data of familial cases and controls. The ultimate goal is to generate a diagnostic tool for the identification of genetic risk profiles. Participants will undergo clinical evaluation and genetic testing as part of the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been a smoker for 40 years. He was diagnosed with emphysema 5 years ago and has been treated with inhaled medications and steroids, but his symptoms have persisted and his exercise capacity is limited. He experiences shortness of breath when walking short distances and has difficulty performing daily activities. He has no significant heart, kidney or liver disease. He is willing and able to tolerate bronchoscopy. He has not undergone any Lung Volume Reduction Surgery or Lung Transplantation. His screening test results indicate that he is a suitable candidate for the Aeris Bronchoscopic Lung Volume Reduction System.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking. He has been smoking for 30 years and currently smokes 1 pack per day. He has not been vaccinated against COVID-19. The chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates, and the COVID-19 test is positive. He was diagnosed with moderate to severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) according to the Berlin criteria. He is currently on invasive mechanical ventilation in controlled mode with VC, adjusted to Vt≤8 mL/kg, Ppl <30 cmH2O, and minimum PEEP of 8 cmH2O. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical study and has not received any cell therapy product in the last 5 years. The patient has no known history of alveolar hemorrhage or hemoptysis, states of hypercoagulability, or DVP or PE in the last 6 months. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 29-year-old Caucasian female office worker with a BMI of 24.5 is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She is generally healthy and does not have a history of chronic diseases. She is physically active, engaging in at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week. She reports eating a balanced diet, but does not consume dairy products regularly. She does not take any supplements containing vitamin D. Her most recent serum 25(OH)D concentration was measured six months ago and was found to be 65 nmol/L. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant in the next six months. She has no history of intestinal malabsorption, cirrhosis, renal insufficiency, or hypercalcemia. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in this study to learn more about vitamin D supplementation.

A 57-year-old male patient came to the clinic complaining of difficulty swallowing solid foods for the past 2 months. He has lost 5 kg in the last 6 weeks. He has a history of smoking for 30 years, but quit 5 years ago. His physical examination was remarkable for cervical lymphadenopathy. His CT scan revealed a 5 cm mass in the middle thoracic esophagus with involvement of adjacent lymph nodes. His biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior treatment for this condition. His performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. His hemoglobin (HGB) is 105 g/L, white blood cell (WBC) count is 6.2 × 109/L, neutrophil count is 3.0 × 109/L, platelet count is 170 × 109/L, total bilirubin (TBil) is 0.9 upper normal limitation (UNL), creatinine (Cr) is 1.2 UNL, alanine aminotransferase (ALAT) is 1.8 UNL, and aspartate aminotransferase (ASAT) is 1.7 UNL. He has a normal electrocardiogram result and no history of congestive heart failure. He is willing to comply with the clinical trial protocol and follow-up requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer six months ago. She has undergone previous treatments with chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the disease has progressed despite the treatment. She has no known CNS metastases. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 12 weeks. Her hemoglobin level is 10 g/dL, WBC count is 4,500/mm3, granulocyte count is 2,300/mm3, and platelet count is 110,000/mm3. Her bilirubin level is within the normal range, ALT and AST levels are 2 times ULN, and alkaline phosphatase level is 3 times ULN. Her creatinine level is within the normal range, and her creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she is willing to use effective contraception. She has no history of other serious medical conditions. She has not received any biologic therapy for at least 4 weeks, chemotherapy for at least 4 weeks (6 weeks since mitomycin or nitrosoureas), or hormonal therapy for at least 4 weeks. She has not received any extended field radiotherapy for at least 4 weeks. She has not undergone any surgery since her diagnosis.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer during a routine checkup. He underwent radical prostatectomy via the robotic-assisted laparoscopic approach at William Beaumont Hospital. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of urinary or bowel problems prior to the surgery. His pre-operative PSA level was 7.2 ng/mL, and his biopsy showed a Gleason score of 7 (4+3). The surgery lasted for 4 hours, and there were no intraoperative complications. The patient was discharged home on postoperative day 2 after demonstrating adequate pain control, no signs of infection, and the ability to eat and ambulate without assistance. He has since returned for follow-up visits, and his urinary and bowel function are improving gradually. He reports no sexual function at this time.

A 32-year-old woman, Caucasian, with no known medical history, presented to the imaging center for a routine breast evaluation. The results of the evaluation showed that she has a suspicious mass in her right breast, categorized as ACR BI-RADS Category 4. The physician recommended further follow-up, including a biopsy. The patient agreed to participate in this clinical trial, which aims to evaluate a laboratory developed test that measures multiple breast cancer-specific biomarker proteins in blood samples. The patient is within the age range of 25 to 50 years, and her breast evaluation results meet the inclusion criteria. The patient will be required to provide a blood sample (35 mL or 2 1/2 tablespoons) during two visits, which will take approximately 1 hour each. The first visit will include a blood sample collection, and the second visit will be a follow-up visit at 6 months. The patient will also undergo a follow-up breast evaluation. The samples will not be labeled with her name but a unique identification code. The test results will not be reported back to the study doctor and will not be used to determine or change her treatment. The patient will not receive the results of these tests.

72-year-old female with a medical history of knee osteoarthritis, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with chronic knee pain. The patient reports that the pain has been progressively worsening over the past year and has been limiting her ability to perform daily activities such as walking, standing, and climbing stairs. She reports no recent falls or injuries to the knee. The patient has tried pain medications and has received physical therapy, but there has been no significant improvement. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and is able to walk without the use of crutches or other assistive devices. Radiographic imaging confirms a diagnosis of Grade 2 knee osteoarthritis. The patient does not have any neurological or cognitive disorders, rheumatoid arthritis, electronic implants, or any other cardiorespiratory, neuromuscular, or metabolic disease that would be a contraindication to the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months without success. She has regular menstrual cycles and her last period was 5 days ago. Her BMI is 24 kg/m² and her blood tests show FSH levels of 8 IU/l, estradiol levels of 60 pg/ml, and progesterone levels of 1.2 ng/ml on day one of the cycle. She had a hysterosalpingography 2 months ago, which showed normal results. No history of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or endometriosis. She is considering intrauterine insemination (IUI) as a treatment option and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the use of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) versus spontaneous luteinizing hormone (LH) in IUI cycles. She is open to the use of donor sperm if needed.

A 45-year-old man visited the clinic with complaints of heartburn, nausea, and stomach pain. He was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease and prescribed a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) for daily use for one month. He has no history of kidney disease and his renal function tests were normal at the time of diagnosis. He does not smoke, and he is not diabetic. He is not taking any other medications except for occasional analgesics. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of prolonged PPI therapy on renal function.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing chronic pain and stiffness, as well as fatigue and depression. She has been taking medications for pain management and has also tried physical therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on her symptoms. The patient does not have any contraindications for TMS and has not received any TMS treatment before. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and has signed an informed consent form. She is willing to continue her current drug therapies during the trial.

A 56-year-old man with a history of pancreatic cancer presents with recurrent metastatic disease despite receiving multiple lines of chemotherapy. He has been experiencing significant pain and weight loss. Imaging studies reveal multiple liver and lung metastases. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has no significant comorbidities and has normal organ function. He has not received any investigational agents within the past 4 weeks. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use appropriate contraception during the study period. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 32-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 24.5 kg/m^2 and has never participated in any clinical trial before. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. He has never undergone any surgery of the gastrointestinal tract. He has no history of seizures or stroke, and no other relevant neurological or psychiatric disorders. He has not experienced any fainting spells or blackouts in the past. He has no chronic or acute infections and no known allergies to medication or its excipients. He does not take any medications that might reasonably influence the results of the trial. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study, in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. He reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. He is currently taking lisinopril, metformin, and atorvastatin. On physical examination, he is found to have a jugular venous pressure of 8 cm, bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation, and peripheral edema. Echocardiography reveals an ejection fraction of 35% with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He reports being unable to walk more than a block without experiencing significant dyspnea. He is willing to participate in this clinical study and meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 38-year-old female who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. She has a family history of Down syndrome, and her recent prenatal screening test showed an increased risk for aneuploidy. She has decided to undergo an amniocentesis procedure to confirm the diagnosis. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has had a routine prenatal care and has had no complications so far in her pregnancy. She is aware of the risks associated with the procedure and has provided a signed and dated informed consent. She is willing to provide a 30-50mL blood sample for the noninvasive screening test for fetal aneuploidy. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially help develop a new maternal plasma marker for noninvasive prenatal screening.

Patient is a 35-year-old female presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms, including urgency, frequency, and occasional urinary incontinence. The patient has undergone urodynamic studies to evaluate her symptoms. The patient has kept a bladder diary documenting the frequency and urgency of her urinary symptoms. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study to identify the best parameter of the bladder diary that correlates with the volume at strong desire to void of filling cystometry. The patient is able to follow instructions for keeping a bladder diary and is available for follow-up visits as required by the study protocol.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) diagnosed 3 years ago. She has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity which suggests exercise-induced ischemia. Her past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hypothyroidism, all of which are well-controlled on medications. She is not taking any cholesterol-lowering medication at present. Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and her BMI is 30 kg/m2. She has no signs of peripheral edema or jugular venous distension. Her electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF during treadmill exercise. The echocardiogram shows mild left ventricular hypertrophy, and there is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities or valvular disease. She does not have a history of unstable angina or myocardial infarction in the past month. She has not undergone any coronary arterial surgery. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, as defined by the protocol.

Patient is a 28yo woman who is 16 weeks pregnant with her first child. She was diagnosed with chronic hypertension (CHTN) during routine prenatal care. Her blood pressure ranges from 145-155 systolic and 90-100 diastolic. She is currently not taking any antihypertensive medication. She has no significant past medical history and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated thus far. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness and safety of pharmacologic treatment for mild CHTN during pregnancy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP) Project and has no known exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 36-year-old female diagnosed with schizophrenia according to DSM-IV-TR criteria. She has a history of tolerating aripiprazole as determined by her psychiatrist. She is not currently experiencing an acute relapse of schizophrenia and is not considered treatment-resistant to antipsychotic medications. She is not using any CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers and has not participated in any clinical trial involving a psychotropic medication within the past month. She is willing to receive multiple-dose administrations of aripiprazole intramuscular (IM) depot in the deltoid muscle for a period of 113 days with a 28 day follow-up period. She is between 18 and 64 years old at the time of informed consent.

62-year-old female diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (stage 3) and moderate anemia presents with fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath on exertion. Her hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL, serum iron is low, and ferritin levels are significantly reduced. The patient has been receiving oral iron supplements for the past few months with no significant improvement in her hemoglobin levels. The patient is not receiving erythropoietic agents and is not on dialysis. The patient has no known sensitivity to Ferrlecit® or its components and is clinically stable. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of Ferrlecit® versus oral iron in treating anemia and iron deficiency in chronic kidney disease.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance. He is 180 cm tall and weighs 96 kg, giving him a BMI of 29.6. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes, with his father and two uncles having been diagnosed in their 50s. He has tried to lose weight in the past by dieting, but has been unsuccessful. He is currently not taking any medications and has no other chronic health conditions. His most recent lab results show an HbA1c of 6.2%, fasting glucose of 106 mg/dL and a 2-hour postprandial glucose of 170 mg/dL. He has been enrolled in a diabetes prevention program and has been following a low-calorie diet and increasing his physical activity. Despite his efforts, his glucose tolerance has not improved. He has not received any prior treatment with insulin or cortisone.

8-month-old infant brought to pediatric emergency department with symptoms of fever, irritability, and poor feeding. The infant has not yet acquired walking. The pediatrician suspects a urinary tract infection and needs a urine sample for diagnosis. The infant does not exhibit any signs of vital distress. The parents have given their consent for the infant's participation in the clinical trial. The infant is affiliated to social security. Clinical examination shows no abnormalities other than the suspected UTI. The investigator will attempt bladder stimulation to obtain a urine sample.

The patient is a 64-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma last year. He has been treated with oral agents as well as intravenous therapy. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history and no history of any other primary cancer diagnosis. He is currently not on any other medications except for those related to his hypertension and diabetes. He is married and retired from his job as an accountant. He has a good support system and is able to attend all of his medical appointments. His healthcare provider referred him for this study to evaluate the cost and resource utilization of his treatment.

A 9-year-old boy with a history of medulloblastoma came to the clinic for a recurrent brain tumor. He has already undergone radiation therapy and two chemotherapy regimens. He is currently taking dexamethasone for his neurological deficits. His Karnofsky performance score is 70%. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. His platelet and hemoglobin counts are transfusion independent. His creatinine, bilirubin, SGPT and SGOT levels are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 35-year-old woman called 911 due to severe nausea and vomiting. She reported feeling dizzy and had vomited three times before the paramedics arrived. She had no significant past medical history and was not taking any medications. She denied any recent travel, exposure to sick contacts or ingestion of any known toxins. She had a normal blood pressure, pulse and respiratory rate on exam. Her physical exam was significant for dry mucous membranes, and she was slightly tachycardic. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial and provided verbal consent. She was randomized to receive either 70% isopropyl alcohol or ondansetron. The paramedic provided her with the assigned treatment according to the study protocol. Her nausea score was recorded at baseline, upon arrival at the emergency department and 15 minutes after treatment. The paramedic evaluated the treatment as very easy to use and the patient reported feeling better after the treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a BMI of 45 kg/m2. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol only occasionally. She has not undergone any gastric bypass surgical procedure. She has never experienced any significant hypersensitivity reaction to oseltamivir. Her liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. She is currently not pregnant and is using an effective method of contraception. She is willing to abstain from sex during the study period and one week following the study period. She is comfortable with venipuncture and multiple blood draws. She has no significant clinical illness requiring pharmacological management. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for her BMI. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand the pharmacokinetics of oseltamivir in morbidly obese individuals.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with bipolar disorder 3 years ago. He experienced manic episodes and was hospitalized several times for his condition. He has been on mood stabilizers (lithium and valproate) for the past year, but still experiences manic episodes despite his medication. He is currently not employed due to the impact of his condition on his work. He is single and lives alone. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a history of drug abuse, but has been clean for the past year. He has no history of seizures or sensitivity to the medications being used in the study. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he hopes to find a more effective treatment for his manic episodes. He is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all the requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies or skin conditions. She has not been diagnosed with asthma or hay fever. She occasionally experiences mild headaches and muscle soreness but does not take any analgesics for these symptoms. The patient is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the development of new analgesics. She is willing to abstain from smoking for 24 hours prior to each iontophoresis treatment and limit smoking to no more than 5 cigarettes per week during the study. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

60-year-old African American male with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years presented to the primary care clinic for his regular follow-up appointment. He reports that he has been taking his prescribed anti-hypertensive medication regularly but his blood pressure readings have been fluctuating. He also mentions that he sometimes forgets to take his medication and has difficulty managing his medication schedule. His past medical history includes hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis, and benign prostatic hyperplasia. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 and is currently unemployed. He denies any history of smoking, alcohol or drug use. He lives alone and has a limited social support system. He has difficulty with transportation to the clinic due to financial constraints. His family history is positive for hypertension and diabetes. His physical exam was normal except for elevated blood pressure readings of 150/90 mmHg. He is currently taking lisinopril and amlodipine for hypertension.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. She has been diagnosed with preeclampsia, a serious pregnancy complication characterized by high blood pressure and damage to organs, typically the liver and kidneys. She has no history of autoimmune diseases or previous thromboembolic disorders. Her prenatal care has been uneventful until the onset of preeclampsia, which occurred at 34 weeks of gestation. She is currently being closely monitored by her healthcare provider and is being treated with medication to manage her blood pressure. Her baby is also being closely monitored for growth and well-being. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help researchers better understand the prevalence of positive antiphospholipid antibodies among women with preeclampsia and to potentially improve outcomes for future mothers and babies.

52F with no previous history of gastric cancer who has been invited to participate in the National Cancer Screening Program and receive an upper endoscopy. She reports occasional abdominal discomfort, bloating, and dyspepsia. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, well controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. She has no known family history of gastric cancer. On physical examination, she is found to be in good health. She is willing to sign an informed consent form and participate in the study. She has not received H. pylori eradication therapy in the past.

An 80-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with epilepsy, which she has been experiencing for at least 12 months. During the past 4 weeks, she has had at least two partial-onset seizures, including subtypes of simple partial, complex partial, and/or partial seizures evolving to secondarily generalized. She is currently being treated with one or two anti-epileptic drugs (excluding oxcarbazepine) in a stable dosage regimen for a minimum of 4 weeks prior to screening. She has agreed to participate in an open-label study investigating the safety and efficacy of eslicarbazepine acetate as adjunctive therapy for partial seizures in elderly patients. Despite her age, she is willing and able to comply with all trial requirements, according to the investigator's judgment. She has not experienced any primarily generalized seizures or seizures of non-epileptic origin. She has not had any history of status epilepticus or cluster seizures within the 3 months prior to screening. She has no major psychiatric disorders or history of suicide attempts. She has not been previously treated with ESL or participated in a clinical study with ESL. She does not have known hypersensitivity to other carboxamide derivatives (e.g. oxcarbazepine, carbamazepine) or to any of the excipients. She has no uncontrolled cardiac, renal, hepatic, endocrine, gastrointestinal, metabolic, haematological, or oncological disorders or abnormalities in the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) as determined by the investigator. Her clinical laboratory results are within normal limits. She has not received an investigational drug (or a medical device) within 3 months of screening or is currently participating in another trial of an investigational drug (or medical device) trial.

50-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension for the last 5 years. The patient has been managing his conditions with medication and lifestyle changes but has been experiencing difficulty in managing his physical activity due to his busy work schedule. He has been experiencing fatigue and a decline in his overall quality of life. The patient lives in a remote area and has difficulty accessing rehabilitation services due to transportation issues. The patient is interested in participating in a study that uses new technology to help him manage his conditions and improve his physical activity level. The patient has good verbal communication skills and is in a stable period in terms of his chronic conditions. The patient's blood sugar levels are currently under control with medication.

This is a 62 year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COPD in stage GOLD III. He is currently receiving optimized medical treatment and is on long term oxygen therapy. The patient has not received treatment with Non-invasive Ventilation (NIV) in the last 4 weeks and is willing to participate in this trial. He has no intolerance to perform NIV and has not experienced any acute exacerbation at baseline or during pulmonary rehabilitation. The patient's pCO2 level is within normal range and he is able to perform a 6 minute walking test.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American male who has been diagnosed with sickle cell disease. He has been experiencing moderate to severe pain related to his SCD over the past year, which has required him to visit the emergency department or be hospitalized. He is scheduled for continuing care at the University of Illinois at Chicago Sickle Cell Clinic. Although he has been taking medication to manage his pain, he is still experiencing pain on a regular basis. He speaks and reads English and is willing to participate in a study that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a computer-based pain management tool called PAINRelieveIt. The study will assess whether this tool can help manage his pain and provide him with better education on his role in pain management. The study will also evaluate the effectiveness of a decision-making support tool for doctors that provides personalized pain medication therapies based on the patient's pain level.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been feeling sad and hopeless for the past few months. She has been struggling to get out of bed in the morning and has lost interest in activities that she used to enjoy. She has also been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has lost her appetite. She works as a graphic designer and has been finding it hard to concentrate on her work. She has no prior history of depression, but her family has a history of mental illness. She has not sought treatment for her depression, but her friend recommended that she talk to her primary care physician about it. She visits her GP and after a brief assessment, she diagnoses the patient with mild major depression. The GP recommends active monitoring as a non-pharmacological treatment option and explains the study to the patient. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

Patient is a 25-year-old female who has been wearing Acuvue 2 contact lenses for the past 2 years. She uses a multipurpose solution to clean and store her contact lenses. She has not undergone any corneal refractive surgery in the past 6 months. She does not have corneal ectasia and is not currently using Restasis. She is willing to refrain from using her contact lenses on the day of examination for the study. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the corneal staining after contact lens instillation with two different multipurpose solutions.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was recently admitted to the hospital for shortness of breath and fatigue. She has a history of hypertension and was diagnosed with heart failure with an ejection fraction of 40% by echocardiography. Her symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few months, and she has been experiencing frequent hospitalizations due to heart failure exacerbations. On physical examination, she has bilateral pitting edema up to her knees and crackles in her lungs. Laboratory tests reveal a low hemoglobin level and low serum iron levels, suggestive of iron deficiency. She denies any recent blood loss or changes in her diet. Her medications include furosemide, spironolactone, and lisinopril. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She lives alone and is able to perform her activities of daily living with some difficulty due to her heart failure symptoms. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life.

A 45-year-old male with a history of heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) presents with documented coronary artery disease (CAD) and LDL-C levels of 230 mg/dL. Despite being on maximum statin therapy and lifestyle modifications, his LDL-C levels have remained elevated for the past year. He has been attending LDL apheresis sessions twice a month for the past six months and his LDL-C levels have improved to 150 mg/dL. He has given consent to participate in this clinical trial to assess the effects of LDL apheresis on inflammatory and lipid markers. He has no history of renal or hepatic disease, malignancy, amyloidosis, or rheumatoid arthritis. His bone health is normal based on recent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan. He is eager to participate in the study and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in the management of FH.

The patient is a 56-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II triple-positive breast cancer. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. The patient underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the estrogen receptor (ER) is positive (90%), progesterone receptor (PR) is positive (20%), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is positive (2+). The patient has a KPS score of 80 and her bone marrow function, liver and kidney function, cardiac function, and electrolyte levels are all within the normal range. She can swallow medication without any difficulty and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has not received any anti-tumor treatment in the past and has not participated in any clinical drug trials in the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraceptive measures throughout the study period. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up appointments.

A 32-year-old woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of AZD9056 on retinal function. She has no history of neurological or ophthalmological diseases and is not currently taking any medications. She has 6/6 vision and an intraocular pressure of 15mmHg. She passed the test for narrow angle glaucoma risk and the color blindness test. She is willing to undergo the electroretinography assessments required for the study.

A 35-year-old African American woman was diagnosed with epilepsy at the age of 20. She has been taking anticonvulsant medications with no significant improvement in seizure control. Her seizures occur at least twice a month despite taking her medications regularly. She has never been on a ketogenic diet before. She has no history of metabolic or mitochondrial disorders that may preclude the use of medium chain triglycerides (MCT) and the ketogenic diet. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and no history of dysphagia or gastroesophageal reflux. Her cholesterol and triglyceride levels are within normal limits. She has not used Betaquik before and is willing to participate in the study. She has given her informed consent and is able to comply with the study protocol and keep written records. She is hoping to improve her quality of life by participating in this study.

A 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage I breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and had negative margins on surgical evaluation. The tumor size was 1.8 cm and was ER/PR positive and HER2 negative. She has no history of prior radiation therapy to the chest, neck, or axilla. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to provide informed consent. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She is currently using hormonal therapy to prevent recurrence of breast cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of hypofractionated radiation therapy in treating breast cancer.

A 62-year-old man with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-negative acute lymphoblastic leukemia presents with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has a performance status of 2 and has mild elevation of AST and ALT levels. He is not pregnant and is willing to use an effective method of contraception.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with actinic keratosis on her upper extremity. She has noticed the lesions for the past 6 months and has not sought medical attention until now. She is generally healthy and takes no medications. She has no known allergies.
