The patient is post-menopausal and has not had a menstrual period in over a year. She is willing to use high effective methods of contraception during the trial period. The patient is able to follow instructions and is likely to complete all trial requirements. She has signed the written informed consent form.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male who regularly participates in endurance athletics for leisure. He has no known drug allergies and is currently not taking any medication. His ferritin levels are above 35 ng/mL and transferrin saturation is above 20%. He has no history of acute or chronic medical or psychiatric conditions and has not been enrolled in any registered testing pool for anti-doping purposes. He is willing to provide urine and blood samples for the study. He does not have a history of bleeding or bone marrow aplasia, and does not have any blood or iron disorders. His hemoglobin concentration and hematocrit are within the normal range. He does not have chronic kidney disease, HIV, cancer, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or any planned surgeries during the study. He is not diabetic and does not have a history of cardiac or hepatic disease or drug abuse.

A 42-year-old man was diagnosed with Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type I (CRPS I) three months ago and has been experiencing a VAS pain score of 7. He has not been on Gralise or gabapentin for at least one month. He is currently taking ibuprofen for pain management. He works as an accountant and sits at a desk for long periods of time. He has no history of suicidal thoughts or behavior and has never had a seizure disorder. He has no allergies to medications and has never tested positive for illicit drugs.

A 25-year-old female patient with Fitzpatrick skin type III came to the clinic with severe acne scarring on her face. She had been dealing with acne since her teenage years and had tried multiple treatments, including over-the-counter products and prescribed medications, with little success. She had never undergone any procedures for her acne scarring before. She has no history of keloidal scarring, immunodeficiency disorders or connective tissue disorders. She is not pregnant or nursing and has not used isotretinoin in the past 6 months. She has no allergies to lidocaine, tetracaine or valacyclovir.

22-year-old female US Army recruit who has just begun basic combat training at Fort Jackson, South Carolina. She has no known history of kidney stones, kidney disease, amenorrhea, endocrine disorders, bone modifying disorders, or anemia. She is not currently taking or have taken glucocorticoid drugs in the 2 years prior to study participation. The patient has no known allergies to any component of the snack bar. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol as instructed by the investigators.

The patient is a 52 year-old male with a history of obesity, hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He presents with a 3-day history of cough, dyspnea and fever (38.5°C) and is admitted to the hospital. On physical examination, he is tachypneic (respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute) and hypotensive (blood pressure of 95/60 mmHg). Chest X-ray reveals bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Laboratory results show elevated inflammatory markers and lymphopenia. The patient is started on supplemental oxygen and broad-spectrum antibiotics. He requires mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. He has not been hospitalized within the last 3 months and does not have any known immunodeficiency disorders. The patient is affiliated with social security.

A 68-year-old Caucasian man has been experiencing gait difficulties, urinary incontinence, and memory problems for the past 6 months. He has fallen a few times and has difficulty walking on uneven surfaces. He reports that his thinking is slow, and he has difficulty remembering things that just happened. He has had no previous history of neurological problems. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild osteoarthritis. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. He takes medications for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His physical examination reveals a wide-based gait and difficulty with tandem walking. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 22. An MRI of his brain revealed ventriculomegaly out of proportion to his age. The patient meets the criteria for probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) according to the NIH guidelines. He is planned for shunt surgery and is willing to participate in the computerized neuropsychological test battery study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is generally healthy and physically active. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has a BMI of 23 and has no history of liver disorders. His ferritin levels are below 50ug/l and his transferrin saturation is below 20. He has never donated blood in the past six months and is not a high-level athlete. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the impact of iron injection on blood donation markers. He is willing to attend regular blood sampling and donate 500mL of blood for the study. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form. He is available to attend all study appointments and is willing to follow the study protocol.

A 55-year-old male patient came to the clinic complaining of loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few months and they have been affecting his work performance. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. His BMI is 32, indicating he is overweight. He has never been diagnosed with any cardiac disease and does not smoke. A polysomnography test revealed an apnea-hypopnea index of 10, indicating he has obstructive sleep apnea. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the impact of obstructive sleep apnea on left atrial volume and function.

A 45-year-old Hispanic male with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with fever, chills, and malaise for the past 3 days. He reported a productive cough with thick yellow sputum, shortness of breath on exertion, and pleuritic chest pain. He denied any recent travel, sick contacts, or exposure to tuberculosis. On physical examination, he was febrile with a temperature of 39°C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. Blood pressure was 98/60 mm Hg. Lung examination revealed crackles over the left lower lobe. Laboratory studies revealed a leukocyte count of 14,000/mm³, serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, and a lactate level of 3.8 mmol/L. Chest radiograph showed left lower lobe consolidation. The patient was diagnosed with severe sepsis and admitted to the intensive care unit. He received 1 liter of normal saline and was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics.

A 40-year-old Polynesian male who had been diagnosed with bronchial dilation and had been followed by the Centre hospitalier de Polynesie Francaise for the past 5 years. The patient had a history of recurrent respiratory infections and had undergone multiple chest CT scans and pulmonary function tests. The patient's family history was significant for similar respiratory problems in his mother and two siblings. The patient had no expressed refusal to participate in the study and was willing to provide retrospective data for the period between Jan 1, 2010, and Dec 31, 2020.

A 32-year-old man was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from a HLA-matched related donor 2 years ago. He achieved complete remission (CR) after the transplant, but he recently experienced a relapse. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the recurrence of CD19+ B cell malignancy. He is currently receiving chemotherapy but has not achieved a second CR. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of donor T cells engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) targeting CD19 after allogeneic transplant. The patient's donor is a family member who is CMV seropositive and HLA-A*0201 positive. The patient is HIV seronegative and has no significant medical or psychological conditions that would make him unsuitable for T cell therapy. He is willing to use contraception during and for 12 months after the protocol enrollment. The patient's donor is also willing to participate in the study and has no significant medical conditions that would make him unsuitable as a T cell donor. The patient is aware that he will receive one intravenous infusion of CMV/CD19 or EBV/CD19 bi-specific CD8+ T cells at least 30 days after HCT.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who works as an administrative assistant at a large company in Leeds. She has a BMI of 30 and has been struggling with weight loss for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs, but none have been successful in helping her achieve her weight loss goals. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a weight loss smartphone application and is willing to commit the necessary time and effort. She is able to read and write in English and has access to the internet. She has not had any previous weight loss surgery and is not taking any medications that would exclude her from participating in the trial. She is motivated to make lifestyle changes and is willing to be randomized to one of the three study groups.

A 32-year-old woman is currently pregnant with her second child. Her previous delivery was by cesarean section with a Pfannenstiel incision due to fetal distress. The surgery was uncomplicated, and she recovered well. She is now at 38 weeks of gestation and scheduled for a repeated cesarean section due to concerns over the size of the baby. She has no known allergies and is in good general health. Her BMI is 27, and she has no medical disorders that could affect wound healing. She has no previous history of keloids or transversal suprapubic scars. The area to be studied is free of infections and tattoos. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study, and her surgical incision will be closed using either tissue adhesive or staples.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and bloody stools. He underwent surgery to remove the primary tumor and was started on a first-line treatment regimen consisting of oxaliplatin and bevacizumab. Unfortunately, after several months of treatment, his cancer progressed and he was deemed a suitable candidate for the study. He has a liver metastasis that is accessible for biopsy. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension that is well-controlled on medication. He has never been on aflibercept or any other anti-angiogenic therapy. He is willing to undergo a needle core biopsy of his liver metastasis and provide blood samples during treatment. He understands the investigational nature of the study and has provided written consent.

35 yo F with a history of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m2 presenting to the gynecological outpatient clinic for examination. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, and elevated androgen levels. She is currently not on any hormonal medications, including birth control pills, and has not been using any metformin treatment in the last 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to examine the effects of motivational interviewing on weight loss in women with PCOS. She is able to read and understand Danish and does not require a translator. The patient will be randomized into either the treatment group or the control group and will receive the usual PCOS treatment. However, the treatment group will also receive individual motivational interviews by a nurse every 14 days for a period of six months. The patient will be required to fill out questionnaires and have hair samples taken during the course of the study. She will also undergo blood tests and scans of the ovaries at the beginning of the study and after six months. The patient is hopeful that participation in this study will help her lose weight and improve her quality of life.

This clinical trial does not involve patients or their medical conditions. Instead, it involves medical students and their ability to diagnose and treat acute otitis media in children. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this trial.

The patient is a male or female aged 18 years or older, diagnosed with Gaucher disease type 1 confirmed by a documented deficiency of acid β-glucosidase activity by enzyme assay. The participant must have demonstrated clinical stability on twice daily dosing of eliglustat tartrate (Genz-112638). Female participants of childbearing potential must have a documented negative pregnancy test prior to administration of the first dose of eliglustat tartrate (Genz-112638) in this study. In addition, all female participants of childbearing potential must use a medically accepted form of contraception throughout the study, i.e., either a barrier method or hormonal contraceptive with norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol or similar active components. The patient must meet certain criteria at the time of screening, including hemoglobin level ≥9 g/dL, platelet count ≥70,000/mm^3, spleen volume ≤25 multiples of normal (MN), and liver volume ≤2.0 MN. The patient must consent to provide a blood sample for genotyping for Gaucher disease and for CYP2D6 to categorize the participant's predicted rate of metabolism, if these genotyping results were not already available for the participant. The patient must be willing to abstain from consumption of grapefruit, grapefruit juice, or grapefruit products for 72 hours prior to administration of the first dose of Genz-112638 and throughout the duration of the study. The patient must not have any evidence of neurologic disorder or pulmonary involvement related to Gaucher disease and must not be transfusion-dependent. The patient must not have any clinically significant disease, other than Gaucher disease, or serious intercurrent illnesses that preclude participation in the study. The patient must not be known to have any of the following: clinically significant coronary artery disease, clinically significant arrhythmias or conduction defect, or positive for the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody, Hepatitis C antibody, or Hepatitis B surface antigen. The patient must not have received an investigational product (other than eliglustat tartrate (Genz-112638)) within 30 days prior to administration of the first dose of eliglustat tartrate (Genz-112638) in this study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who served in the military for 5 years and was honorably discharged. He has a history of anxiety and depression, which he believes were triggered by his time in the service. He has been struggling with suicidal thoughts and has made one suicide attempt in the past year. He recently visited the VA emergency department due to suicidal ideation and was referred to the SAFE VET intervention. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide two contacts with telephone numbers for tracking purposes. He is currently living in a residential facility and has a cell phone number where he can be reached. He is able to read and understand English and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male or female volunteers over the age of 18 who are registered in the French social security scheme. The volunteers must not have any contraindications to Magnetoencephalography (MEG) and/or Electroencephalography (EEG) or Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Additionally, all categories of protected persons are excluded from this trial. If you meet these criteria and are interested in participating, you will be required to sign an informed consent form. The trial aims to optimize the parameters, sequences or paradigms in order to improve the quality and relevance of data obtained from several non-invasive devices, including per-operative MRI, MEG, EEG, SPECT-CT, and motor platform. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of new technologies and their applications in the field of medical research.

A 22-year old college student was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma. She noticed enlarged lymph nodes in her neck and experienced fatigue for several weeks. She is currently receiving chemotherapy at the University of Southern California (USC) Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center and Hospital. She lives with her parents and has a younger brother. She is an active student who enjoys playing soccer and volunteering at a local charity. She is concerned about her health and the impact of cancer treatment on her life. She has been experiencing anxiety and difficulty coping with the diagnosis and treatment. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn about the impact of the AYA services on her care and to provide feedback on ways to improve the care for other AYA cancer patients.

The patient is a 48-year-old female who underwent a coronary angiogram three months ago and was diagnosed with CAD. She was started on aspirin and a statin medication four weeks ago. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She denies any bleeding disorders or recent hospitalizations for MI or unstable angina. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is using adequate contraception. Her vital signs are stable and within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 10 years ago. He has been receiving treatment with carbidopa-levodopa enteral suspension (CLES) at a dose of 1000 mg LD per day for the last 6 months. He has no history of allergies or significant medical conditions, and he is not taking any other medications. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has two adult children who live nearby. He is able to communicate and willing to participate in the study. His BMI is 27. He has normal skin without any burns, scars, or large tattoos in the area of administration. He has negative serum serology for Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) or Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) at the screening visit. He has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism in the past 12 months. His electrocardiogram (ECG) rhythm is normal. His renal and liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no psychiatric, neurological or behavioral disorders that may interfere with the conduct or interpretation of the study. He has not experienced blood loss of greater than 500 mL in the last 3 months.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with focal dystonia in her right hand 2 years ago. She works as a graphic designer and has noticed that her symptoms have worsened over time, making it difficult for her to complete her daily tasks. She has tried various treatments, including physical therapy and medications, but has not seen significant improvement. Her symptoms include involuntary muscle contractions and abnormal postures in her right hand, which cause difficulty in gripping and holding objects. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is not taking any medications for her dystonia. Her family history is negative for any movement disorders. She is willing to participate in the study to help advance the understanding of dystonia and potentially find new treatments.

A 65-year-old man with a history of end-stage renal disease and a functioning right upper arm arteriovenous fistula for hemodialysis presents to the vascular clinic with complaints of difficulty with hemodialysis due to recurrent access dysfunction. His past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He has a history of coronary artery disease and has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement in the past. His medications include aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, metformin, and insulin glargine. On examination, the patient has a palpable thrill and bruit over the right upper arm arteriovenous fistula. Duplex ultrasonography reveals a 70% stenosis at the venous anastomosis. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is a suitable candidate for enrollment.

52 year old male diagnosed with type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 5 years. He has a history of poor glycemic control with HbA1c levels consistently above 53 mmol/mol (7.0%). The patient is currently on metformin and a low-carbohydrate diet. He is able to use the telemonitoring devices provided and is cognitively able to participate in the trial. The patient is fluent in Italian and is willing to fill in questionnaires related to the study. He has no severe comorbidities that would limit his life expectancy to less than 12 months. The patient is not pregnant. Overall, he is interested in participating in the trial to help improve his diabetes management and to potentially reduce healthcare costs associated with his condition.

A 67-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is scheduled for cataract surgery at the Wills Eye Hospital. She was referred to the resident CPEC clinic by her primary ophthalmologist. She has a history of poor compliance with medical appointments but has managed to make it to her pre-operative visit at the CPEC clinic. During the visit, she was informed that she needed to complete pre-admission testing (PAT) to ensure that she was medically cleared for surgery. She was given a list of tests to complete at a local laboratory, but did not follow through with obtaining the tests. Her surgery was subsequently cancelled. She was rescheduled for surgery but missed her appointment again due to transportation issues. She was then enrolled in the randomized, prospective, intervention study and was randomized to the intervention group where on-site pre-admission testing was mandated. She was informed that she needed to complete her testing at the CPEC clinic on the same day of her pre-operative visit. She completed the testing and her surgery was successfully performed without any complications.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis. He is currently in the pubertal stage according to the Tanner scale. He is an active individual who enjoys playing sports and has been experiencing some difficulty with glucose tolerance. He is currently taking medication to manage his cystic fibrosis and his condition is stable. He has no other known medical conditions and does not smoke or use any drugs. He is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to adhere to the study protocol. His parents are supportive of his participation and will be involved in ensuring he adheres to the study protocol. His BMI is 20.5, and his lung function tests are normal. He has no exacerbation of his clinical picture and is not currently on any antibiotics.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for the past 6 months. She has lost 10 pounds in the past month and is feeling fatigued. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has a family history of inflammatory bowel disease, with her father having Crohn's disease. Her physical examination is notable for tenderness in the lower abdomen and rectal bleeding on digital rectal examination. Her laboratory values show an elevated C-reactive protein level and anemia. She has not previously taken thiopurines for her IBD. She is willing to participate in the study and is randomized to the genotyping group. She undergoes genetic testing and is found to have a heterozygous variant in one of the three genes tested. She is started on a lower dose of azathioprine and will be monitored closely for response to treatment.

This is a 65-year-old female who has been admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory failure. She has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently experiencing an exacerbation of her symptoms. She is requiring non-invasive ventilation to support her breathing and improve her oxygen saturation levels. She has an arterial line in place for continuous monitoring of her blood pressure and is able to cooperate with the NIV treatment. She does not have any contraindications to NIV therapy and has a fair short term prognosis. She will be considered for enrollment in the SmartCare Driven Pressure Support-Non Invasive Ventilation Feasibility Study to test the feasibility of using the Smartcare NIV computer-driven system to automatically adapt ventilator settings during non-invasive ventilation.

32-year-old female, 9 weeks pregnant with her first child, and has a history of slightly elevated fasting blood glucose levels (between 5.1 mmol/L and 7.0 mmol/L) in the first trimester. She is attending regular antenatal examinations and has accurate left mentoposterior (LMP) verified by ultrasonography (USG). She does not have a history of diabetes before pregnancy, multiple pregnancy, or complications that affect glucose metabolism such as hyperthyroidism. She is not taking any medications that could affect glucose metabolism, such as glucocorticoids or diuretics. She is willing to give birth in the research center and is not infected with hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or HIV. She is not undergoing any non-natural pregnancy procedures such as intrauterine insemination (IUI) or in-vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET). She is eligible for the study and could potentially benefit from interventions that aim to manage her blood glucose levels during pregnancy to improve maternal and fetal outcomes and prevent metabolic disorders in both mother and child.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer. She has been diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma and is scheduled for surgery to remove her breast and axillary nodes. She is generally healthy, with no history of allergies, medication use, or chronic pain conditions. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her BMI is within the normal range. She speaks fluent English and is able to communicate effectively. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

45-year-old male of Japanese ethnicity presents with upper GI symptoms including heartburn and regurgitation. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past six months and has tried over-the-counter antacids with minimal relief. He is referred for an upper GI endoscopy as part of this international cohort study comparing upper GI symptoms and endoscopy findings in Canada with Japan and Iran, and correlating this with the upper GI microbiome. Written consent will be obtained from him. He will complete three symptom questionnaires and a demographic one before endoscopy. Saliva collection device will be applied for collecting saliva and microbiota from the oral cavity. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) will be performed thereafter and brushing of the esophagus, stomach, and the duodenum will be done using a sterile sheathed brush to sample collect gut microbiota and gastric biopsies will be done for assessing H.pylori status. He will also undergo measurement of nitrate reductase activity (NRA) in his oral cavity. This will be done on twenty erosive gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD) patients, twenty non-erosive GERD patients, and twenty patients without any endoscopic or clinical GERD.

A 45-year-old male visited a dental clinic with a complaint of painful sores in his mouth that have been bothering him for the past few weeks. The patient reports difficulty in eating and speaking due to the pain. He has no history of taking any medication or topical steroids for the past two months. The patient has no history of systemic corticosteroid use for the past six months. He denies any history of diabetes, hypertension, or hepatitis infection. The intraoral examination showed multiple erythematous erosions on the buccal mucosa, tongue, and palate. The diagnosis of atrophic and erosive oral lichen planus was made. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is willing to use the medication as directed and follow up for the assessment of the appearance score and severity of pain.

The patient is a 12-year-old African American girl who is currently in the 7th grade. Her parents have provided written consent for her to participate in a study aimed at reducing the risk of HIV and other sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) among adolescents. The patient has no history of sexual activity and is interested in learning more about how to prevent HIV and other STDs. She is currently attending a participating school, and her parents are supportive of her participation in this study. The patient is fluent in English and able to read at a 7th-grade level. She has no known medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. The patient is willing to attend the required sessions, which will consist of group discussions, videos, games, brainstorming, experiential exercises, and skill-building activities. She will also complete self-reports concerning sexual behaviors, condom use, and knowledge about STDs at various points during the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing hair loss for the past 5 years. He has tried various treatments, including over-the-counter products and prescription medications, but none of them have provided significant improvement. He has a family history of male pattern baldness. He does not have any scars or wounds on the alopecia area and does not suffer from any skin disease or serious cardiovascular disease. His preoperative examinations remain healthy. He does not take any anticoagulant drugs and is not currently suffering from any active infections or autoimmune diseases. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of nanofat grafting for the treatment of his androgenic alopecia.

A 35-year-old woman, fluent in English, visits the Lowry Family Health Center for a routine primary care visit. She has a history of high blood pressure and is currently taking medication for it. She also reports a family history of diabetes and wants to take proactive steps to prevent it. She is interested in participating in the study and is able to understand the self-management goal concept. She shows no signs of cognitive impairment or hearing impairment.

Patient A is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding for the past year. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has completed her family planning and has decided to undergo a laparoscopic hysterectomy to alleviate her symptoms. She has been diagnosed with benign uterine fibroids, which are causing her heavy bleeding. She has been informed about the two different approaches for closing the uterine artery during surgery and has given her consent to participate in the study. She understands the risks and benefits of both methods and is willing to be randomized to either the closure of the uterine artery at its origin or at the cervix. She has been excluded from the study if she had a malignant disease or if she required an emergency laparoscopic hysterectomy.

This is a 54 year-old female who has recently undergone surgery for ovarian cancer. She is still in the early stages of her recovery and has been having difficulty with her oral intake, experiencing nausea and vomiting. She has been advised to take small, frequent meals to help with her recovery, but has found it difficult to keep food down. Her doctor has recommended her for a clinical trial that involves taking an oral supplement called serum bovine immunoglobulin protein isolate. The supplement may help to provide her with the necessary nutrition to aid her recovery, and may also improve her quality of life. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and is able to provide informed written consent. She has no history of allergies to beef.

A 27-year-old primipara pregnant woman visited the hospital for her regular prenatal check-up. She is currently in her 24th week of pregnancy and is able to read and write in Turkish. She has no chronic systemic disease, communication problems, or psychiatric problems. Her fetus has no abnormalities, and there have been no pregnancy-related complications thus far. She has expressed some fear of childbirth during her previous visits. She is interested in participating in a study to reduce her fear of childbirth and improve her childbirth self-efficacy. She has no plans for a planned cesarean section and is willing to attend the training program provided through the motivational interview method.

The patient is a 19-year-old college student who is currently in the class of 2021.5 at a northeastern university. They have reported hazardous alcohol use, and have expressed interest in participating in a study aimed at reducing harmful alcohol use among college students. The patient is willing to provide self-reported behavioral information and information about their social ties to others in their college class. They are also willing to participate in a Brief Motivational Interview to discuss their alcohol use. The patient is not currently undergoing treatment for alcoholism or any other substance abuse disorder. They do not have any medical conditions that would preclude them from participating in the study.

Patient is an 80-year-old male from the United States with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are managed with medication. He has no history of respiratory or neurological disorders. His MMSE score is 20, indicating mild cognitive impairment. He reports difficulty sleeping at night and his partner reports loud snoring and episodes of gasping during sleep. He has not been diagnosed with sleep apnea previously. He is currently under the care of a neurologist and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He has no contraindications to MRI and is willing to undergo nocturnal respiratory polygraphy.

The patient is a 50 year old male with a missing mandibular molar tooth. He is a non-smoker and has no history of therapeutic radiation to the head or jaw. He has no known systemic diseases and is not currently taking any medications. He has good oral hygiene and has not experienced any active infections or inflammation in the area intended for implant placement. He is physically able to tolerate conventional surgical and restorative procedures. He has a signed informed consent and is willing to be evaluated for each study visit. He has a healthy opposing dentition and his minimum primary stability during implant placement is above 35Ncm. He is reliable and able to attend all study visits.

Patient is a 52-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing palpitations and occasional irregular heartbeats for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. His past medical and drug history are unremarkable. His BMI is 28, BP: 135/85, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for normal electrolyte levels and liver and kidney function. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 3 months. He is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50 year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 5 years. She has been taking methotrexate for the past 2 years, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She has also tried other non-biologic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in the past, but has not had satisfactory results. She reports moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness, particularly in her hands and feet, which affects her ability to carry out daily activities. She has a DAS28-ESR score of 4.5 points. She is currently on a stable dose of prednisolone (7.5 mg/day) and takes NSAIDs as needed for pain relief. She has no history of major surgery within the past 8 weeks and has not been exposed to tocilizumab or any other biologic DMARDs. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use reliable means of contraception during the study. Her hematologic, renal, and liver function are within normal limits.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with esophageal cancer after experiencing difficulty swallowing food for the past few months. Endoscopy and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. CT scan revealed lymph node involvement, and the patient was scheduled for surgery following neoadjuvant chemoradiation. The patient has a history of smoking and moderate alcohol consumption. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. The patient has a WHO-performance score of 1 and has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. He has no history of claustrophobia or any metallic implants that are non-MR compatible. His liver function tests are normal, and he has a normal serum transferrin saturation level.

33 yo F who is currently pregnant with her first child, at 17 weeks gestation, residing in a coastal region of China. She has a history of mild asthma, which is well controlled with an albuterol inhaler. She reports a healthy diet and is not currently taking any supplements. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the correlation between DHA intake and DHA concentrations in blood and breast milk. She is able to read and write in Mandarin and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days and has not taken any DHA supplements.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer with no hormone or HER2 receptor expression. The cancer has spread to her lungs and liver. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and has received prior chemotherapy, but has not had any progression or intolerance on the single agent chemotherapy. The patient has measurable metastatic tumors by CT scan and has adequate biological parameters, including an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) > 1500 mm3, platelet count ≥ 100×109 L, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL, serum creatinine ≤2.0, total bilirubin ≤ 2 mg/dL, AST/ALT ≤ 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) range, and a thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) within institutional normal limits. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an acceptable contraceptive method for the duration of the study and for 4 months following the last dose of pembrolizumab and 30 days following the last dose of chemotherapy on this trial. The patient has not undergone major surgery within 4 weeks prior to Day 1 of treatment in this study and has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or any of their excipients, or any of the events outlined in the Contraindication or Special Warnings and Precautions sections of the product or comparator SmPC or Prescribing Information. The patient is willing to complete the informed consent process and adhere to the protocol treatment plan and follow-up requirements. The patient is eligible to be enrolled in the pembro plus gemcitabine arm for the treatment of her metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

A 32 year old man with a history of Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) infection comes to the clinic for follow-up. He was diagnosed with HBV eight months ago and started treatment with adefovir for 12 weeks. However, he did not respond well to the treatment and his HBV viral load remained high. His healthcare provider has now recommended switching to entecavir for further treatment. The patient has not received any other nucleoside treatment for more than two weeks and does not have any co-infections with HIV, HCV, or HDV. He has a positive HBsAg and has tested positive for both HBeAg positive and negative. His pretreatment HBV DNA level was 15,000 copies/mL. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given his consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been experiencing recurrent diarrhea and abdominal pain for the past 6 months. He has been diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) according to the Rome III criteria. His symptoms have not improved with dietary changes, and he has recently undergone a breath test which revealed the presence of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). He has no history of celiac disease or inflammatory bowel disease, nor is he currently undergoing immunosuppressive treatment. He is not pregnant and has no active cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy and safety of Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 in treating SIBO in individuals with IBS.

A 55-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with a productive cough, fever, and body aches. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He works in a hospital as a nurse and has direct contact with patients. He has never received the influenza vaccine before. He reports that he is usually too busy to go to his primary care doctor for routine check-ups and vaccinations. He lives with his wife, who has a history of asthma, and they have two young grandchildren who visit them regularly. He denies any recent international travel or exposure to sick individuals. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 101°F, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. Lung auscultation reveals bibasilar crackles. The patient is offered the option of receiving the influenza vaccine or being referred to a community provider for vaccination.

We are looking for healthy male or female volunteers between the ages of 18 and 55 years old for a pilot study examining the within subject variability of Clexane. Female subjects of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test at the Screening Visit and be willing to use two methods of contraception from Day 1 until 3 months afterwards. Subjects must not have any clinically significant abnormal serum biochemistry, haematology, coagulation factors and urine examination values within 14 days of the first dose. Exclusion criteria include a history or presence of significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, or psychiatric disease, as well as recent use of NSAID and/or aspirin (within 4 weeks of first dose) or the use of any pharmacological agents known to significantly induce or inhibit drug-metabolizing enzymes within 30 days of the first dose. Subjects with any medical condition requiring regular treatment with prescription drugs will also be excluded. The study will involve two Treatment Periods, each of 2 days duration, and during each Treatment Period, subjects will reside at the Clinical Unit. Study drug will be administered on the morning of Day 1 following an overnight fast. Pharmacokinetic (PK) samples will be collected pre-dose and up to 36 h post-dose (x14 samples) for the measurement of enoxaparin. Safety will also be evaluated at specified times throughout the study. There will be at least 7 days between each dose administration. The Post-Study Follow-Up will be conducted on Day 2 of Treatment Period 2 after completion of the 36 h PK blood sampling and vital sign check.

A 43-year old male with a history of hyperlipidemia and a family history of heart disease is seeking medical attention for his high cholesterol levels. He has been trying to manage his cholesterol through lifestyle changes such as diet and exercise, but his latest lab results showed that his LDL-C level is 6.5 mmol/l. His current medications include metformin for type 2 diabetes and lisinopril for hypertension. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his cholesterol levels and reduce his risk of heart disease.

Patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of idiopathic scoliosis. The patient has a double major curve measuring 50 degrees at the thoracic level and 40 degrees at the lumbar level. The patient has been experiencing back pain, and the curve has been progressing rapidly over the past six months. The patient has failed conservative treatment, including physical therapy and bracing, and is scheduled for spinal fusion surgery. The patient has no known allergies and is in good health. The patient's parents have consented to the use of local tranexamic acid administration as part of the study. The patient's platelet count is within normal limits, and the patient has no bleeding disorders. The patient is classified as ASA class I.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been referred to the clinic for a full colonoscopy. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no family history of colon cancer or polyps. She has no symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits. She has signed the informed consent form for the clinical trial on cold snare polypectomy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria. The endoscopist will document all polyps

A 45-year-old female patient presented with recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and bloating, associated with nausea and vomiting. She had a history of cholelithiasis and was scheduled to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She had no significant past medical history and denied any allergies to medications. Her vital signs were stable, and she had a body mass index of 27 kg/m². She was not using any opioids or corticosteroids in the preoperative period. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the free and informed consent form. She was randomized to the magnesium sulfate group and received 40 mg/kg of magnesium sulfate in saline solution 15 minutes before anesthetic induction. The anesthetic induction was started with lidocaine 1.5 mg/kg, fentanyl 3 µg/kg, propofol until clinical hypnosis, cisatracurium 0.1 mg/kg, and intubation after adequate neuromuscular relaxation. Maintenance was with sevoflurane in concentration under clinical demand, repeating boluses of fentanyl 1 µg/kg, and cisatracurium 0.03 mg/kg, as needed. The patient will be monitored for the primary outcomes of time between the end of anesthetic administration and bispectral index (BIS) > 60 and a battery of neuropsychological tests to assess postoperative cognitive dysfunction tested in the Brazilian population 3 h after the end of anesthetic administration. Secondary outcomes such as response to the brief pain inventory questionnaire and opioid consumption in the first 2 postoperative days will also be assessed.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with schizophrenia 3 years ago. She has been on antipsychotic treatment for the past 2 years, including a 12-month treatment with asenapine under protocol 25517. She has shown improvement in positive symptoms such as delusions and hallucinations, but still experiences negative symptoms such as lack of motivation and social withdrawal. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently on any other medication. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in this long-term extension trial to further test the efficacy and safety of asenapine and a comparator agent (olanzapine) in the treatment of schizophrenia.

A 25-year-old healthy woman who works as a marketing executive and has no underlying medical conditions came to the clinic for a routine check-up. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she does not smoke or consume alcohol or drugs. She has never participated in a clinical trial before and is not currently taking any dietary supplements or medications, except for oral contraceptives. Her BMI is 22 kg/m2, and her blood chemistry values are within normal ranges. She exercises for 3 hours a week and maintains a healthy diet. She has no history of malignant, metabolic, or endocrine diseases, or previous cardiac infarction.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes since the age of 11. She has experienced multiple episodes of hypoglycemia in the past and has lost warning of these episodes. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has not had any seizures or other neurological issues. She does not take any antiepileptic medication, neuroleptics or benzodiazepines. She does not have a history of stroke or other brain disease, cardiovascular disease or allergies to heparin. She has not abused alcohol, drugs or medications. She has been on insulin therapy for more than 5 years and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the activity in the brain, the cognitive function, and the skin temperature when patients are exposed to repeated hypoglycaemia. The purpose of the study is to improve the understanding of hypoglycaemic EEG changes and skin temperature changes in patients with type 1 diabetes.

A 4-year-old boy was referred to the clinic by his pediatrician due to concerns about his social and communication skills. The boy was born at term with no complications during delivery. His developmental milestones were delayed, and he did not start speaking until the age of 3. He has difficulty making eye contact, and his play is repetitive and restricted. His parents report that he has become increasingly withdrawn and irritable. The boy has never had any major medical issues or injuries. The physical exam was unremarkable, except for mild hypotonia. The boy was diagnosed with autistic disorder based on DSM-IV criteria, as confirmed by the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS). The boy will be enrolled in the study as part of the autism group, and he may be considered for the regressive subtype group depending on his clinical course. Over the course of several years, the boy will undergo various tests and procedures, including comprehensive medical history, behavioral assessment, physical and neurological examination, polysomnography (PSG) and electroencephalogram (EEG), and blood work for laboratory assays. The study aims to identify subgroups of children with autism with profiles that comprise distinct biological/behavioral phenotypes. The boy's progress will be monitored to explore known and new subtypes of autism.

The patient is a 2-day-old full-term male neonate born via spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 27-year-old G1P1 mother. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy and prenatal care. The neonate weighed 3.5 kg at birth and had an Apgar score of 5 at 10 minutes. The neonate was resuscitated with positive pressure ventilation for 2 minutes and then transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit. The cord blood pH was 6.9 and the base deficit was 18 mmol/L. The neonate was diagnosed with perinatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy based on moderate encephalopathy according to the Sarnat and Sarnat staging system. The neonate was started on whole-body cooling within 6 hours of birth, and the treatment was continued for 72 hours. The neonate is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets all the inclusion criteria and has none of the exclusion criteria. The parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have given their consent for the neonate to participate.

A 50-year-old female patient presented with a breast lump on her right breast. She had no significant past medical history and was not taking any medications. A biopsy revealed invasive ductal carcinoma that was estrogen receptor positive. The tumor size was 2 cm and there was no evidence of lymph node involvement on imaging. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status was 1, indicating that she was able to carry out normal daily activities with mild symptoms. She was within the age range (40-60 years) for the trial and met all the inclusion criteria. However, she had no interest in participating in the study and opted for standard treatment with tamoxifen alone.

A 48-year-old Caucasian man with a history of primary cutaneous melanoma presents with concern for recurrence. He had undergone surgery for the removal of the melanoma, and the sentinel node biopsy did not detect any melanoma deposits. He is anxious about the possibility of relapse and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for adjuvant treatment. He is in good health with no history of any significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His family history is negative for any cancer-related conditions. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. His performance status is 0. His laboratory values meet the eligibility criteria. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory testing, and other requirements of the study. He has no history of previous cancer therapy, and he has not received immunosuppressive or immunodeficient medication. He has no serious cardiac, gastrointestinal, hepatic, or pulmonary disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to provide tumor tissue for biomarker analyses. He has signed written informed consent and is willing to comply with the contraceptive requirements of the study.

42 year-old man with a history of HIV infection for 8 years, currently on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with no history of opportunistic infections, malignancy or CNS disorders. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with concentration for the past year. He is employed and works as a graphic designer. He has no history of substance abuse, depression, or psychiatric illness. He is in a stable relationship and reports no sexual dysfunction. He is fluent in English and able to provide written informed consent.

A 50 year old male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis was referred for liver transplant evaluation. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 6 months and is currently on the transplant waiting list. In the physical exam, he has an enlarged liver with ascites and jaundice. His laboratory tests show elevated levels of bilirubin, liver enzymes and INR. He has a history of hypertension and his current medications include furosemide, spironolactone, and propranolol. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient has an ASA III status and is able to give a written informed consent. The study aims to compare the use of sugammadex versus neostigmine after rocuronium infusion during liver transplantation to prevent post-operative residual curarization.

A 50 yo F with a histologically proven diagnosis of high grade serous ovarian cancer, who has undergone 3 prior lines of chemotherapy and does not carry a deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutation, is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient should have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST 1.1 guidelines, and recurrent platinum-resistant disease. The patient should have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-2, a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, and adequate organ and bone marrow function. Adequate blood pressure and thyroid function should be confirmed, and the patient should be able to swallow and retain oral medications without gastrointestinal illnesses that would preclude absorption of cediranib or olaparib. The patient should be postmenopausal or have evidence of non-childbearing status. The patient should not have been exposed to any IP during the last 4 weeks prior to enrollment, or have received previous treatment with PARP inhibitor or anti-angiogenic treatment within 6 weeks prior to starting treatment. The patient should not have cancer antigen-125 (CA-125) only disease without RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, major surgical procedure within 2 weeks prior to starting treatment, or clinically significant signs and/or symptoms of bowel obstruction within 3 months prior to starting treatment. The patient should not have persisting ≥Grade 2 CTCAE toxicity from previous anti-cancer treatment(s), central nervous system metastases, or history of myocardial infarction within 6 months prior to starting treatment. The patient should not have left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < lower limit of normal (LLN) per institutional guidelines, or <55%, if threshold for normal not otherwise specified by institutional guidelines, for patients with the following risk factors: prior treatment with anthracyclines, prior treatment with trastuzumab, prior central thoracic RT, including exposure of heart to therapeutic doses of ionizing RT, history of myocardial infarction within 6-12 months prior to start of IPs, prior history of other significant impaired cardiac function.

A 60-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer and previous treatment with docetaxel presents with increased fatigue, weight loss, and bone pain. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. Imaging studies reveal the presence of metastatic disease in the bones, and a biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The patient's PSA levels have been rising despite previous treatment. The patient has not received any other anti-cancer therapy for the last 28 days. His medical history is notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of autoimmune disease, liver disease, or other malignancies. The patient is willing to undergo biomarker studies, including fresh tumor biopsies if needed. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and will be assessed for DNA repair defects (BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, PTEN, CHEK2, RAD51C, RAD51D, PALB2, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) by T-NGS of metastatic sites or liquid biopsy. His organ function is adequate, and he has a life expectancy of more than 24 weeks.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain that radiated to his left arm. ECG revealed ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V5. He was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and was taken for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with successful epicardial reperfusion. However, he developed significant left ventricular (LV) dysfunction after the procedure. He was started on standard medical therapy for myocardial infarction and was referred for consideration of bone marrow-derived stem cell (BMSC) transfer to augment LV function recovery of the heart. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria of the study. He has no prior history of coronary artery bypass grafting, pulmonary edema, cardiogenic shock, or significant co-morbidities that would exclude him from the trial. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

65 yo M with a history of mild-to-moderate open angle glaucoma and cataracts bilaterally. Patient has been using topical glaucoma medications for the past year with good compliance but has noticed increased difficulty with daily activities due to worsening vision. Patient is currently on timolol 0.5% twice daily and latanoprost 0.005% once daily. Patient is interested in exploring surgical options to improve both his glaucoma and cataracts. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Mild osteoarthritis - No history of intraocular surgery within the last 3 months - No other ocular pathology affecting vision.

The patient is a 68-year-old female who has been experiencing difficulty with mobility and muscle weakness for the past year. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with medication, and osteoporosis, managed with calcium and vitamin D supplements. She is not currently participating in any dietary or exercise interventions, and is willing to consent and follow the study procedures. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m and can speak and understand English. She has no history of falls or major psychological/mental illness, and has not participated in any clinical trial or exercise intervention program in the past 3 months. She does not have lactose intolerance or uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension. She is not currently on any medication that would exclude her from the study, and does not have any major systemic diseases such as liver or kidney disease, advanced gastrointestinal disorders, advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, advanced rheumatoid arthritis, or cancer. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her muscle strength and quality of life.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing flu-like symptoms for the past 24 hours. She has a fever that has not responded to over-the-counter medication and a sore throat. She tested positive for influenza through a rapid virus antigen test. She has no known allergies to baicalin or Paracetamol tablets. She does not live in a long-term care facility and does not have any chronic respiratory, cardiovascular, hematological, neurological, or metabolic diseases. She is not immunosuppressed and is not obese. She has not taken any antiviral medication for influenza in the past 24 hours and has not received the influenza vaccine or research monoclonal antibody in the past year. Her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or lactating and is not planning to have a family in the next 6 months. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months. She is willing to sign an informed consent form to participate in the clinical trial.

A 8-year-old Caucasian boy with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) was referred to the study by his school psychologist. The boy has difficulty with social interaction and communication, as well as restricted interests and repetitive behaviors. He has an IQ of 85, as measured by Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children. He lives with his parents and younger sister. His mother reports that he has difficulties participating in community activities such as sports, playdates, and community events. She feels that his lack of social interaction and community participation is impacting his overall quality of life. The boy is currently receiving occupational therapy and speech therapy. His medications include risperidone and clonidine for behavioral management. His parents are interested in participating in the study and have provided written consent. The boy is able to read and write and will provide written consent as well.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with a recurrent primary CNS tumor. Despite standard therapy, the tumor has progressed, and the patient is now experiencing symptoms such as headaches, nausea, and impaired vision. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 80%, indicating some limitations in physical activity. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. The patient is fertile but will use effective contraception during the study. The patient has an absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/μL, a platelet count of 120,000/μL, and hemoglobin levels of 9 g/dL. The patient's creatinine clearance and glomerular filtration rate are both 80 mL/min, and their serum creatinine level is 0.9 mg/dL. The patient's bilirubin level is within the normal range, and their ALT level is 50 U/L. The patient's albumin level is 2.8 g/dL, and their levels of sodium, potassium, magnesium, and calcium are all normal. Despite the patient's neurological deficits, which have been stable for the past 2 weeks, they are eligible for the study. The patient has no clinically significant systemic illness that would compromise their ability to tolerate study therapy or interfere with the study procedures or results. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to MK0752 and has not received prior treatment with this drug. The patient has not received any investigational or biologic agents in the past 7 days or any chemotherapy in the past 3 weeks. The patient is not currently taking any enzyme-inducing anticonvulsant drugs or any other anticancer or investigational drug therapy. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and follow-up evaluations.

This is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and severe chronic heart failure (NYHA class III b). He presents with significant dyspnea on exertion and fatigue, with a peak oxygen uptake of <20 mL/min/kg body weight. His left ventricular ejection fraction is <25%, and his left ventricular end-diastolic diameter is >60 mm. He has no history of exercise-induced myocardial ischemia or cardiac decompensation within the last 8 weeks, but he does have ventricular arrhythmias (>Lown 4b) and is protected by an ICD. He is not insulin-dependent,

A 50-year-old woman with Type 2 diabetes has been experiencing blurred vision in her right eye for the past few months. She was referred to an ophthalmologist who diagnosed her with early proliferative diabetic retinopathy and recommended scatter photocoagulation surgery. The patient has never had any prior laser treatment and is currently on oral antihyperglycemic agents for the management of her diabetes. She is willing to participate in the observational study of DME following scatter laser photocoagulation and can provide informed consent. The patient is cooperative and has good media clarity and pupil dilation for the procedure. Her baseline optical coherence tomography (OCT) shows a central subfield thickness of 280 microns and her visual acuity is 20/25 in the study eye. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient does not have a history of ocular inflammation, glaucoma, or major ocular surgery in the past 6 months. She is not planning to have any ocular surgery in the next 8 months. She is not currently receiving treatment for DME and has not received any treatment for DME in the past 6 months. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study eye.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with lower limb lymphedema. She has been experiencing swelling, discomfort, and reduced mobility in her legs for the past year. The patient has no history of cancer treatment, active wounds, or pulmonary edema. She is mentally able to understand and follow instructions provided by the study personnel. The patient can read and comprehend English and is willing to provide written and informed consent. She does not have any inbuilt electrical stimulators such as a cardiac pacemaker. The patient is interested in trying the Monterey Investigational System and willing to use it daily for one week at home to assess its usability.

A 30-year-old female presents with a sore throat that started two days ago. She reports pain on swallowing and a scratchy sensation in her throat. She has not taken any medication for the pain. She has no history of chronic illness or allergies. She denies any fever, cough, or other respiratory symptoms. Physical examination reveals erythema and swelling of the oropharynx, but no exudate or ulcerations. Vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory results show a white blood cell count of 6.5 x 10^9/L. She is diagnosed with acute viral pharyngitis and is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the efficacy and tolerance of Ambroxol lozenges 20 mg for sore throat. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 42-year old woman who works as an office manager is morbidly obese with a BMI of 41. She has been struggling with her weight for years, and despite multiple attempts to lose weight through various diets and exercise programs, she has not been successful. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She was referred to the Bariatric Clinic at the Toronto Western Hospital for weight loss surgery but has decided to decline it. She was diagnosed with insulin resistance (HOMA-IR value of 3.5) by her primary care physician. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes medication. She does not have any known gastrointestinal diseases or previous gastrointestinal surgery. She is a non-smoker, and she is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She does not take any antibiotics, prebiotics, probiotics, iron supplements, or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She is excited to participate in the clinical trial to see if stool transplantation can help her with her insulin resistance and weight loss.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is undergoing an allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) using a conditioning regimen containing alemtuzumab and radiotherapy. She has a matched sibling donor available and both the patient and the donor are CMV seropositive. The stem cell harvests are expected to be at least 4.0 x 10^6 CD34 cells/kg. She has not undergone any prior bone marrow transplantation and is not concurrently participating in another therapeutic transplantation study.

This is a 28-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester, with no medical history of chronic diseases or complications. She speaks Spanish and is interested in participating in a study that focuses on promoting healthy eating habits for her child. She is willing to stay in the Basque Country until her child reaches 18 months of age. She plans on breastfeeding her child and has no intention of restricting her diet. She has never participated in any clinical trial before and is excited to contribute to the development of new methods to promote healthy eating habits for children.

The patient is a 45 year old male with a history of chronic kidney disease. He has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath for the past few months. Laboratory tests have revealed a hemoglobin level of 9 g/dL, indicating anemia. He is not on dialysis and has not received epoetin or any other erythropoietic substance. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for his anemia. He is not currently taking any investigational drugs and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

74-year-old male diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease according to national guidelines presented to the clinic with his wife, who is also his primary caregiver, for routine follow-up. The patient has been struggling with memory loss, confusion, and disorientation, and his condition has been gradually worsening over the past year. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 19 and Functional Assessment Staging Test score of 5. He lives with his wife who provides him with daily care and support. They have one adult child who lives out of state and visits occasionally. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all of which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His wife has been experiencing a high level of caregiver burden, which has led to depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbances. The patient and his wife are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to develop and implement an intervention to reduce caregiver burden and improve their quality of life. They are willing to commit to the 24-month study and follow-up assessments.

A 35-year-old man came to the clinic, seeking treatment for his addiction to cocaine and alcohol. He has been a heavy drinker for the past 10 years and has been using cocaine for the last 5 years. He has tried to quit on his own several times but has relapsed each time. He has no medical history of severe psychiatric symptoms, heart disease, or significant illnesses. He is not taking any psychotropic medication or opioid analgesics. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent. He lives within a commutable distance of the Treatment Research Center (TRC) at the Penn/VA Center for Studies of Addiction, University of Pennsylvania. He is currently not pregnant or lactating, and he is using acceptable methods of birth control. He has a BMI of 29, and his waist to hip ratio is less than 0.9. Based on his drinking history, he meets the drinking criteria as measured by the Timeline Followback (TLFB) (Sobell, 1995), and in the past 30 days prior to consent, he has used no less than $100 of cocaine. He has not taken any investigational medication within the past 30 days. He is committed to following the protocol requirements and attending weekly sessions of Cognitive Behavioral Coping Skills Therapy (CBT) and medical management (MM). He is eligible for participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy and is scheduled for an elective cesarean section in two weeks' time. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no known allergies. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. She has no history of abdominal surgeries or previous cesarean sections. She is currently at 38 weeks gestation and the estimated fetal weight is normal. She has been counseled on the two different closure techniques for the rectus sheath and has consented to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old Caucasian woman presents with a 3.5 cm lump in her left breast that was discovered on routine mammography. Biopsy reveals invasive ductal carcinoma. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy for 4 months and imaging shows a significant reduction in tumor size. She is now considering breast-conserving surgery and has been referred for this clinical trial. She has no prior history of breast cancer, and her family history is negative for any cancers. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. She is married with two children and works as a schoolteacher. She is willing to undergo any necessary procedures for the trial and understands the risks and benefits associated with participating. Her ASA class is II.

A 55-year-old Asian man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 5 years. He has been taking metformin for the last 6 months, but his blood sugar levels are still not well controlled. He has a BMI of 35 kg/m² and a C-peptide level of 1.5 ng/mL. He has no history of cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, hematological, oncological, endocrine, psychiatric, or rheumatic diseases. However, he has been experiencing symptoms of uncontrolled diabetes such as frequent urination, thirst, and fatigue. He does not smoke or consume alcohol.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of diabetic retinopathy. She has been receiving intravitreal injections of VEGF inhibitors in both eyes for the past 6 months. She has experienced discomfort during these injections in the form of pain and pressure around the eye. She is willing to participate in a research study to evaluate a novel intraocular injection guide that may increase comfort levels during these injections. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no other medical conditions or medications that would interfere with her ability to participate in the study. The patient is fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) six months ago. He underwent chemotherapy as the first-line treatment, but his cancer has relapsed. The patient is married with two children and works as an accountant. He is physically fit, exercises regularly, and maintains a healthy diet. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His performance status is good, and he has a life expectancy of at least 16 weeks. His medical records confirm the diagnosis of intermediate grade B-cell NHL. He is willing to use adequate contraception for six months following participation in the study. He has been approved for an autologous stem cell transplantation and meets all standard clinical parameters for candidates of autologous transplant. He has undergone a chemotherapy-based conditioning regimen and has a cryopreserved unselected hematopoietic progenitor cell (HPC) product of at least 3 x 10^6/kg CD34+ cells. He does not have evidence of disease progression after salvage therapy. He has a released cryopreserved T cell product and is not requiring supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation, oxygen saturation of 90% or higher on room air. He does not require pressor support, does not have symptomatic cardiac arrhythmias, and has normal kidney function. He has no signs or symptoms of active infection or positive blood cultures. He does not have any history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to cetuximab. He does not have brain metastases or CNS involvement. He has no presence of other malignancies or history of prior malignancy within 5 years of study entry. He understands the basic elements of the protocol and the risks/benefits of participating in this phase I/II study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is currently undergoing fertility treatment. She has no known eye diseases and has never received treatment for dry eye. She is in good health and has no significant medical history. She will be participating in a study to determine the relationship between estrogen and progesterone levels and eye dryness in women during their fertile years. The study will involve three meetings with a doctor from the ophthalmology department, which will take place during her regular appointments at the fertility clinic. During each meeting, blood tests for estrogen, progesterone, and luteinizing hormone (LH) will be conducted, along with an eye examination that includes a Schein questionnaire, examination of the external eye with a microscope, Schirmer test, tear break up time test, and checking the intraocular pressure with a tonometer. The purpose of the study is to collect data to determine if there is a relationship between hormone levels and eye dryness in women undergoing fertility treatment.

A 43-year-old male presents with complaints of poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has a history of obesity and was recently diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with an AHI of 22 on a diagnostic polysomnogram. He has been using positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy for the past month with good adherence but reports persistent difficulty falling and staying asleep. He reports an Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score of 15, indicating at least "moderate" insomnia, and a sleep onset latency of more than 30 minutes, three or more nights per week during two weeks of sleep diary monitoring.
