He does not have any untreated psychiatric disorders, drug or alcohol abuse, or neurological degenerative diseases. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating different treatments for insomnia in patients with OSA.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has previously participated in a SU011248 protocol for metastatic renal cell carcinoma. She has responded well to the treatment and is now eligible to continue the therapy. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of central nervous system metastasis and is otherwise healthy. She has provided informed consent to continue the SU011248 treatment as part of this rollover protocol.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman, G1P0, with a singleton pregnancy at term, presented to the obstetric clinic for a routine checkup. She has no known systemic diseases and has not been taking any vitamin D or calcium supplements. She denies smoking cigarettes. Her medical and obstetrical history is unremarkable, and she has had a normal pregnancy course so far. The investigators are interested in studying the relationship between maternal and cord blood 25-hydroxyvitamin-D3 [25(OH)D] and calcium concentrations and placental calcification in low-risk obstetric population at term. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and she is invited to participate in the clinical trial.

John is a 38-year-old veteran who served in Iraq for two years. He was honorably discharged from the military five years ago and currently lives with his wife and two children. John has been diagnosed with PTSD and has been seeking treatment at the Veterans Affairs (VA) healthcare system for the past year. He has been smoking for 15 years and currently smokes 10 cigarettes per day. John is interested in quitting smoking but has been unsuccessful in his previous attempts. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to improve his chances of quitting smoking and to receive additional support for his PTSD. John is able to connect the Health Buddy in his home and has no severe psychiatric symptoms or cognitive impairment.

The patient is a 61-year-old man with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma. He was diagnosed with stage IV disease six months ago and has received two lines of systemic therapy, but the disease has progressed. A recent computed tomography (CT) scan showed multiple liver metastases, one of which is measurable according to RECIST 1.1. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His PD-L1 status is CPS ≥1. He has no history of brain metastases or thromboembolic disease. His medical history is notable for hypertension, which is well controlled on amlodipine. He has no history of cardiac disease or major surgery in the past six months. His laboratory results are within normal limits, including adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. He has no known allergies to any component of telatinib or Keytruda. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and agrees to use it for four months after the last study drug dosing. He is able to swallow tablets.

A 35 year old woman presents with redness, pain, and sensitivity to light in her left eye. She was diagnosed with non-infectious uveitis a year ago and has been experiencing repeated exacerbations and remissions. She is interested in participating in a study that may lead to improved treatments for her condition. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is able to provide a blood sample.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been diagnosed with high-grade microtia. She has been recommended for ear reconstruction using autologous rib cartilage. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies to silicone. She does not have diabetes mellitus or any vascular disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the random treatment allocation of the silicone gel on one half of the scar. She will be followed up for three months after the surgery to evaluate the scar formation using clinical, physiological, and histological parameters.

A 52-year-old male patient presents with a history of metastatic or locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. The patient has undergone standard therapy but the cancer has not responded. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive vaccine therapy, cyclophosphamide, and cetuximab to treat the pancreatic cancer. The patient has a performance status of 1, with WBC, hemoglobin, and platelet count within the normal range. The patient's creatinine, bilirubin, ALT, and AST levels are also within the normal range. The patient has no active infections or uncontrolled medical conditions that would increase the risk of toxicities or complications of the study therapy. The patient has no gastrointestinal tract disease resulting in an inability to take oral medication or a requirement for IV alimentation. The patient has no active peptic ulcer disease and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has not had any other malignancy within the past 5 years except for nonmelanomatous skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer, or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. The patient is HIV negative and has no active autoimmune disease or prior autoimmune disease requiring medical treatment with systemic immunosuppressants. The patient has no known or suspected hypersensitivity to sargramostim (GM-CSF), cyclophosphamide, pentastarch, corn, or DMSO. The patient has not had a prior severe infusion reaction (> grade 3) to a monoclonal antibody. The patient has not received any other concurrent anticancer vaccine therapy and is not receiving any other concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, gene therapy, biologic therapy, or investigational therapy.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of endometriosis confirmed by laparoscopy 6 months ago. She has been experiencing moderate to severe pelvic pain with a numeric rating scale (NRS) score of 7 out of 10. She has been using ibuprofen as a rescue pain medication as directed by her physician. She is sexually active and currently using spermicide-coated condoms as a method of contraception. She has no history of pregnancy, lactation or abnormal genital bleeding. She is willing to use ibuprofen as a rescue pain medication if needed as per the investigator's instruction. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to test a new treatment option for endometriosis-associated pelvic pain.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. She was diagnosed with a benign unilateral ovarian cyst confirmed by ultrasonography. She has regular menstrual cycles that occur every 28 days. She has no history of endocrine disease, thyroid abnormalities, or hormone replacement therapy. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is in proper health for laparoscopic surgery and has signed and approved informed consent. The patient has no history of malignancy in the female genital area and has only one ovarian cyst. The patient's serum AMH level is greater than 0.05 ng/ml. The patient is considered to be able to participate in the clinical trial by researchers.

A 52-year-old man with a history of chronic back pain came to the clinic seeking alternative pain management options. He has tried various conservative treatments in the past, including physical therapy and medications, but has not found significant relief. He has been diagnosed with failed back surgery syndrome and has been deemed a candidate for spinal cord stimulation. His pain is described as burning and shooting, with a mean intensity of 7 on a 0 to 10 visual analogue scale. He has had an MRI of the lumbar and thoracic spine within the past year, which showed no compressive spinal pathology or intradural implants. He has been cleared by a psychologist as a suitable candidate for the procedure. He is not currently enrolled in another trial and has no history of coagulation disorders or chronic anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has provided written informed consent.

A 35 year old male visited the dermatology clinic with severe itching and scaling on his skin. He had been experiencing these symptoms for about 2 years and had been diagnosed with plaque psoriasis. He had tried various topical creams and ointments prescribed by his primary care physician, but none of them had provided significant relief. In the physical exam, he had thick red patches of skin with silver-white scales covering about 20% of his body surface area. His psoriasis area severity index (PASI) score was 17 and his physician global assessment (PGA) score was 4. He had never taken any biologic agents or immunosuppressive medications. He was otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or current medication use. He was interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his condition.

55-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with NASH and fibrosis stage F2 on a liver biopsy within the past 24 months. He has a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and is currently on metformin and insulin. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obstructive sleep apnea managed with CPAP therapy. He reports fatigue, mild abdominal pain, and occasional nausea. He denies any history of alcohol abuse, drug abuse or smoking. His current BMI is 33.5 kg/m2 and he reports no significant changes in his weight in the past 6 months. His liver function tests show an elevated ALT of 80 U/L and AST of 45 U/L. His Fibroscan VCTE score is 7.5 Kpa. He has no history of any liver disorder other than NASH and no clinical suspicion of any other liver disorder. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating a new drug for the treatment of NASH and NAFLD.

A 50-year-old woman who has been on dialysis for the past 5 years is presented as a candidate for renal transplantation. Her past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. She is currently on medication for all of these conditions. She has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. She has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is being evaluated for a first renal transplantation and has a heart-beating cadaveric donor available. She has been informed about the study and has provided a signed and dated informed consent form. She is currently not pregnant and has been advised to use a safe contraceptive method throughout the study. She is able to comply with all study related requirements and can receive oral medication.

A 25-year-old non-smoker woman, with a BMI of 22.5, is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no history of drug or alcohol addiction/abuse and has not undergone any surgeries or suffered from any illnesses in the last 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no known allergies to naproxen, NSAIDs, or heparin. She has never experienced an allergic reaction such as asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria, and hypotension associated with the use of aspirin or other NSAIDs. She has no history of gastrointestinal ulceration, bleeding, or perforation. She does not use tobacco products and has not received any drugs as part of a research study within the last 30 days. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

John is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing pain in his knee for over six months. He is finding it difficult to climb stairs and walk long distances. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has a radiological evidence of Kellgren Lawrence Grade II to IV. He is currently taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief which have not changed in the last four weeks. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and instructions of the site study staff. He is a non-smoker and has no known clinically significant liver abnormality. He has not had any major injury to the knee within the last 12 months and has no history of allergic reactions to human albumin or excipients in 5% human albumin. He is not currently taking any IA injected pain medications in the study knee and no analgesics containing opioids. He is not using any topical treatment on the osteoarthritis index knee. He is not on any significant anticoagulant therapy and has not used any human albumin treatment in the last three months.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who lost his right arm in a car accident five years ago. He has been using a myoelectric prosthesis for the past year. His past medical history is non-significant. He is currently not taking any medications. His medical records show that he has adapted well to using the prosthesis and has not reported any significant issues with it. He is

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He is currently on his third cycle of chemotherapy with R-CHOP. He developed fever and neutropenia after the second cycle of chemotherapy. He was hospitalized and received broad-spectrum antibiotics without any improvement. He has no history of invasive fungal infections. His baseline ANC is 1000/mm3, and his current ANC is 200/mm3. His liver and renal function tests are normal. He has no history of severe allergic reactions to antifungal agents. He is not on any other investigational drugs or devices. He does not have any contraindications for the study drug. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled for a foot surgery due to a bunion. She has no known allergies to any medication or solution. The patient is generally healthy, with no underlying medical conditions. She has never undergone a surgical procedure before and is understandably nervous about the operation. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has been informed about the two study arms, and the potential benefits and risks of each method of skin antisepsis. She has been instructed to follow the preoperative instructions and to report any adverse events or discomfort promptly to the surgical staff. The patient is aware that she may be randomized to either Study Arm #1 or Study Arm #2, and that the study will help determine which method of skin antisepsis is more effective and safe.

Sophie is an 8-year-old girl who was diagnosed with severe pneumonia. She was admitted to the hospital with a fever of 39°C, cough, and shortness of breath. Chest X-ray showed multilobe involvement and increased respiratory rate. Her oxygen saturation was 90% on room air. Blood tests revealed elevated inflammatory markers and a serum M. pneumoniae antibody level of 1:640. She has no history of chronic illness or immunodeficiency, and she is not taking any medications. After receiving antibiotics therapy, her symptoms improved but she still had some pulmonary lesions, including consolidation and atelectasis. Sophie's parents were informed about the clinical trial and consented for her participation. She was randomized into the high dose group and received methylprednisolone 10 mg/kg/d for 3 days followed by tapering in 9 days, combined with sequential treatment with azithromycin. After her discharge, she will be followed up at 1, 3, and 6 months to assess the number of pulmonary lesions and monitor any adverse events.

35-year-old male patient who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained multiple injuries, including blunt trauma to the chest and abdomen. Upon arrival at the scene, the patient was hypotensive with a systolic blood pressure of 65 mm Hg, and tachycardia with a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. The patient was quickly transported to the emergency department where he was found to be in hypovolemic shock. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this study as he has a prehospital systolic blood pressure of 70 mm Hg or less. The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study. The patient is randomized to receive a single 250cc IV dose of either 7.5% hypertonic saline with 6% dextran-70 (HSD), 7.5% hypertonic saline alone (HS), or normal saline as the initial fluid for prehospital resuscitation. The patient's data will be collected throughout their hospital stay, up to 28 days.

An 68-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 presents for a clinical trial evaluating the bioavailability of amino acids in high-protein nutritional supplements. The patient reports no significant medical history and is a non-smoker. He does not have any gastrointestinal conditions or allergies to milk products. He is currently not taking any medications or supplements that contain protein or amino acids. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He has not yet started HCV treatment but plans to initiate treatment in the near future. The patient has been living a healthy lifestyle, avoiding alcohol and other liver-damaging substances. He has not been diagnosed with any additional liver diseases, such as autoimmune hepatitis, hepatitis B, alcoholic liver disease, or HIV. The patient is able to travel to Mount Sinai for the study and understands and speaks English. He is willing to sign informed consent and participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant and is not currently incarcerated.

62 year old man diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon. He has undergone previous chemotherapy with FOLFOX and has developed progressive disease with liver metastases. He is currently considering treatment with cetuximab and has available tumor tissue for molecular analysis. He has no significant comorbidities and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV metastatic cervical cancer with bone involvement, after being previously treated with chemotherapy. Her cancer is positive for HPV type 16. Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. She is not pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy during the study period. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) is 1, meaning she is fully active but has some physical limitations. Her bone marrow, liver and renal function are adequate. She has measurable disease according to modified RECIST 1.1 and irRECIST. She has no skin disorders that would interfere with subcutaneous injection. She is willing to use acceptable means of birth control during the study.

The patient is a 52 year-old male who underwent a liver transplant 5 years ago due to end-stage liver disease secondary to alcoholic cirrhosis. He is currently taking immunosuppressive therapy consisting of tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. He presents with symptoms of COVID-19, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. A nasopharyngeal swab confirms the presence of SARS-CoV-2 virus. He has no other significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with respiratory diseases such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He lives alone and works as a carpenter. He has no recent travel history and has not been in close contact with anyone known to have COVID-19. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old Hispanic woman presented to Methodist Dallas Medical Center (MDMC) with complaints of chronic abdominal pain and yellow discoloration of eyes and skin for the past month. She reported a history of hepatitis B infection 10 years ago, but has not received any specific treatment. She denied fever, vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits. Physical examination revealed scleral icterus, hepatomegaly, and tenderness on palpation of the right upper quadrant. Laboratory testing showed elevated liver enzymes, total bilirubin, and abnormal coagulation profile. Abdominal ultrasound revealed findings consistent with liver cirrhosis and dilated bile ducts. An endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) was performed to obtain a liver biopsy for histological analysis. The patient met the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial as she was 18 years or older and underwent EUS-guided liver biopsy at MDMC. She did not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 55-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption presents with a mass in his neck and difficulty swallowing. He was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil after a biopsy. He received chemotherapy and radiation therapy six months ago, but the mass reappeared, and the biopsy confirmed the recurrence of cancer. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that he is ambulatory but has some restrictions in his physical activity. His blood work and imaging tests show no signs of metastasis. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the study's procedures and requirements. He has not received any other cancer treatments in the past 2 weeks and has not taken any corticosteroids in the past 2 weeks. He has no history of other autoimmune diseases and has normal thyroid function indicators. He is negative for HIV, Treponema pallidum, and hepatitis C antibodies. He has no known allergies to recombinant humanized monoclonal antibodies or any of their excipients. He is willing to comply with the study schedule and requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from anal fissure for the past 10 weeks. She experiences severe pain during bowel movements and has noticed occasional bleeding. She has tried topical creams, but they have not provided significant relief. She has no known allergies and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have any immune deficiency or immunosuppression. She does not take anticoagulant medications and has never had pelvic radiotherapy. Her physical exam does not show any signs of acute anal inflammation or internal hemorrhoids of grade 2 or higher. She has not undergone a previous treatment with botulinum toxin or lateral sphincterotomy. She has no known cardiac or pulmonary diseases that may affect the function of the Cardiopulmonary system. She has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to receive treatment with the new medical device for the injection of botulinum toxin.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU with shortness of breath, cough and fever. He has a history of smoking and hypertension. He was intubated and started on mechanical ventilation. The chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with pneumonia. The patient was diagnosed with early-onset pneumonia caused by Gram-negative bacteria. His creatinine clearance was measured to be 140 mL/min/1.73m², indicating augmented renal clearance. He has not received any antibiotics in the past three months and does not have any immunosuppressive conditions or risk factors for multidrug-resistant bacteria. He does not have a history of anemia, and he is not on any diuretic treatment. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial to study the pharmacokinetics of Ceftaroline in critical care patients with early-onset pneumonia and augmented renal clearance. The trial aims to identify optimal ceftaroline administration schemes in critical care patients with various degrees of renal impairment. The study will help to determine the best dosing regimen of ceftaroline for critically ill patients with early-onset pneumonia to optimize patient outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia (ICD-10 F20.0) who has been experiencing symptoms for the past 10 years. Despite being treated with several antipsychotic medications, including olanzapine, risperidone, and aripiprazole, the patient has not shown significant improvement in his symptoms. The patient's PANSS total score is 85, and he scores at least 4 on the PANSS items for Delusions, Conceptual disorganization, and Suspiciousness. The patient has refused treatment with clozapine. The patient is not currently using any benzodiazepines but has a history of substance abuse with cocaine and amphetamines. The patient has signed informed consent and power of attorney.

A 9-year-old girl with a history of asthma diagnosis comes to the clinic with her parents seeking alternative treatments to improve her condition. She has been using inhaled corticosteroids regularly for the past 6 months, but still experiences frequent asthma symptoms such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. The parents report that their daughter misses several days of school each month due to asthma exacerbations and has been hospitalized twice in the past year. During physical examination, the child is found to have mild wheezing and decreased breath sounds on auscultation. Spirometry shows a mild obstructive pattern, with a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 75% predicted. The child is enrolled in the clinical trial and randomized to the intervention group, where she will receive 6 sessions of the Buteyko method twice a week. The goal is to assess the effectiveness of this method as an adjunct therapy in the treatment of children with asthma. The investigators will assess quality of life, pulmonary function, and the six-minute walk test before and after the intervention. The child's parents will also receive educational interventions in relation to asthma.

50 year old man with biopsy-proven nasopharyngeal carcinoma, WHO type 3, with accessible tumor for biopsy. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any prior treatment for the cancer. The patient has no significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He is currently studying in college and has a normal BMI of 22 kg/m2. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any drugs. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. He has no family history of cardiac or any other major disease. He is willing to practice highly effective birth control methods as he is sexually active but not planning to have children in the near future. He has no history of syncope, cardiac arrest or any cardiac arrhythmia. His ECG results are normal. He has no febrile illness or any symptomatic viral, bacterial or fungal infection within the past week. His blood pressure is within the normal range with a mean systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg and mean diastolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg. He has not been diagnosed with HIV, hepatitis C or B antigen.

Patient is a 12-year-old boy who is overweight with a BMI at the 80th percentile for his age and gender. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes and is considered at high risk for developing the disease. He has not been diagnosed with any metabolic or gastrointestinal diseases, and his parents report that he has no history of soy allergy. The patient is not currently taking any vitamin supplements or medications that would interfere with the study parameters. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the study and have signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for over a year. He has been taking metformin at a stable dose for the past 6 months. His BMI is 29.6 kg/m² and his HbA1C level is 8.2%. He has not taken insulin before and is willing to comply with regular injections of insulin. He has no history of severe hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperglycemic hyperosmolar status. His eGFR is 70 mL/min. He does not take any immunosuppressants, corticosteroids or cytostatics. He has not taken any hypoglycemic or hyperglycemic drugs within the past 4 weeks. He has never undergone pancreatectomy or pancreas/islet cell transplant. He has no history of mental disorder or malignancies.

An 75-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is scheduled for induction chemotherapy in a week. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all of which are well controlled with medications. He lives alone but has a supportive family who visits him regularly. He is retired but used to work as an engineer. He is independent in activities of daily living (ADLs) and walks with a cane due to mild osteoarthritis in his right hip. He has no history of falls in the past year. He is a non-smoker, has no history of alcohol abuse, and exercises moderately for 30 minutes a day, four times a week. He has no known allergies and has not had any recent surgeries. His cognitive function is intact per his primary care physician. He speaks English fluently, understands the study requirements, and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for two years without success. After consulting with her doctor, it has been determined that her infertility is due to premature ovarian failure. She has been advised to undergo oocyte donation and is currently considering her options. This will be her first oocyte donation cycle. The patient is fluent in Spanish and is able to read and fill out questionnaires in the language. She has no medical indications for single embryo transfer and has not undergone any previous oocyte or embryo donation cycles.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She is scheduled for breast-conserving surgery (BCS) and sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) in the coming weeks. She has no history of surgery or radiotherapy in the operated breast in the past 2 years, and has not received neoadjuvant systemic therapy. She is not pregnant or lactating. Her blood glucose level on the day of surgery is below 12 mmol/l. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the LightPathTM Imaging System for ex-vivo assessment of margin and lymph node status in breast cancer surgical specimens. She agrees to have an intravenous injection of 5 MBq/kg, up to a maximum 300 MBq of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) prior to surgery. She will undergo BCS and SLNB per standard of care, and her resected breast tissue and lymph nodes will be imaged using the LightPathTM Imaging System. She understands that the CLI results will not be used to influence any surgical or clinical decision-making. She agrees to wear a badge dosimeter during the surgery and recovery period, and understand that staff handling the surgical specimens will also wear ring dosimeters.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with bipolar disorder (BD) for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension (HTN) and has been on antihypertensive medication for the past 6 months. Despite the medication, the patient reports poor adherence to the antihypertensive medication, missing doses on at least 20% of days in the past month, as identified by the Tablets Routine Questionnaire (TRQ). The patient is willing to participate in psychiatric interviews and has given written, informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is fluent in English and has the ability to read and respond to text messages. The patient has a systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg and is currently on mood stabilizing medication. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. The patient will be followed for a 3-month period and will receive the iTAB-CV intervention, delivered via mobile phone, to increase adherence to antihypertensive medication and BD medication. The intervention will include daily texts with psychoeducational and motivational content, medication reminders, contextual cues, and immediate reinforcement for medication taking behavior. Assessments that include evaluation of treatment adherence, psychiatric symptoms, self-efficacy for medication taking behavior, illness beliefs, medication attitudes, and habit strength for both antihypertensive and BD medications will be conducted at four time points over the 3-month time period. Blood pressure will be measured at each of the four contacts.

The patient is a 60-year-old African American male who has been diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He is currently taking L-DOPA/DDCI in combination with other anti-PD drugs and has been experiencing the "wearing-off" phenomenon for the past few months, with an average total daily OFF time of 2 hours while awake. Despite optimal anti-PD therapy, he is still experiencing the end-of-dose deterioration. He was referred to the clinical trial by his neurologist and has not participated in any previous clinical trials. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He lives with his wife and adult children and is retired after working as a mechanic for 40 years. He is able to perform most activities of daily living independently, but has difficulty with fine motor skills and balance. He is excited to participate in the clinical trial and hopes it will improve his quality of life.

A 7 year old boy was referred to the clinic because of rapid weight gain and hypoventilation. His parents report that he gained 20 kg in the last year and complains of excessive sweating and breathing difficulties during sleep. In physical examination, he is obese with BMI of 30 kg/m2, has a round face, and no signs of puberty. Laboratory tests reveal low levels of thyroid hormones, and elevated levels of insulin, leptin, and adiponectin. A sleep study showed central hypoventilation during sleep, and an abdominal ultrasound was normal. The patient was diagnosed with ROHHAD syndrome after ruling out other genetic causes of obesity. He is currently being treated with nocturnal ventilation and a strict diet, but his weight continues to increase.

This is a 63 year-old male who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 2 years ago. He has been taking Levodopa daily with a dosage of 300mg. He has not experienced dyskinesia as of yet. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He reports some mild tremors and stiffness in his limbs but is otherwise functional in his daily activities. He is willing to participate in the study to help understand the predicting factors of dyskinesia in Parkinson's patients. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been experiencing vision problems for the past year. He has been wearing glasses for nearsightedness, but it has been affecting his daily activities and he is interested in exploring other options. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no history of strabismus,

56-year-old female with a history of stage IIIc ovarian cancer who underwent debulking surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She has had multiple recurrences and has been treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy, including bevacizumab, trabectedin, and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, with no response. Her most recent scan showed progression of disease with multiple peritoneal metastases and a rising CA-125 level. Biopsy confirmed that the tumor is positive for folate receptor alpha (FRalpha) by immunohistochemistry (IHC) with >= 50% of tumor staining >= 2+ intensity. She has no history of brain metastases or significant intercurrent illness, and has adequate organ function with no peripheral neuropathy above grade 1. She is willing to undergo a biopsy 48-72 hours after the first dose of IMGN853 and gemcitabine on day 1 of cycle 1 of treatment. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to use adequate contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose of study treatment.

A 58-year-old male presents with a history of unexplained weight loss, fatigue, and abdominal pain. He reports that his symptoms started about 6 months ago, and have been gradually worsening. He has not noticed any skin rashes or hives, but he frequently experiences flushing, itching, and abdominal cramps. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Physical examination is significant for hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse lymphadenopathy. Laboratory analysis is remarkable for an elevated serum tryptase level, as well as elevated levels of histamine and leukotrienes. A biopsy of a lymph node is consistent with systemic mastocytosis. The patient is diagnosed with advanced systemic mastocytosis, specifically aggressive systemic mastocytosis (ASM), and is eligible for the clinical trial of ibrutinib. He is able to provide informed consent for protocol participation, has an ECOG performance status of 1, and is estimated to have a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. He meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

A 62 year old woman, who has been dealing with diabetes for the past 10 years, visits the clinic with a non-healing wound on her left foot. She has been receiving standard wound treatment for the past 2 weeks, but there has been no significant improvement. Upon examination, a diagnosis of advanced peripheral artery disease (PAD) with tissue loss is confirmed, with a foot ulcer size of 1 cm². A recent endovascular procedure was attempted on her left leg, but there was no significant improvement in toe brachial index (TBI) post intervention. Her TBI is at 0.49 and her toe pressure is 45 mmHg with flat wave forms. She is willing to forgo treatment with hyperbaric oxygen, nerve stimulation or sympathectomy for the treatment of advanced PAD from time of consent to 6 months following the initial injection of study drug. She is generally in good health, aside from her diabetes, and is eager to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of SDF1 Plasmid Treatment.
As this is an online experiment, there is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial. Any adult over the age of 18 with access to social media sites can participate in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman from a rural area in India who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and tired most of the time, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She also reports difficulty sleeping and concentrating. She scores a 13 on the PHQ-9 questionnaire, indicating moderate to severe depression. Her hemoglobin A1c level is 9.5%, indicating poor diabetes control. Her blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg and her LDL cholesterol level is 140 mg/dL. She is currently taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily and is not on any antidepressant medication. She has never seen a mental health professional for her depression, but reports that she has talked to her family members about her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the trial and provide consent for randomization. She has a fixed address and contact details, and is able to attend the diabetes clinic visits and participate in the intervention.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy female who is not pregnant and has a BMI within the range of 18.5 and 29.9 kg/m2. She has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. She does not smoke, drink excessively or use drugs. She is not currently taking any medication that might affect the results of the trial, nor has she participated in any other investigational drug trial in the past two months. She is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and maintain adequate contraception during the whole trial period. She does not have a history of asthma or pulmonary hyperreactivity, allergic rhinitis requiring treatment, clinically relevant cardiac arrhythmia, or bacterial and viral infections of the lung including tuberculosis. The patient is willing to sign and date the written informed consent prior to admission to the study in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and the local legislation.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently underwent surgery for an orthopaedic infection. He is experiencing localized pain and erythema around the site of the surgery. The patient has not received systemic antimicrobial therapy for more than 7 days since surgery and has been administered local antibiotics at the site of the infection. The patient would normally be managed with a prolonged course of systemic antibiotics to treat the infection. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient has no other infections that would require additional systemic antibiotic treatment beyond 7 days after surgery. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial involving an Investigational Medicinal Product related to infection. The patient's specimens for microbiological analysis have been taken at the time of index surgery.

A 25-year-old Chilean man, who works as a computer programmer, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a live attenuated hRSV vaccine. He is in good health and has a history of having received the Bacillus Calmette Guerin (BCG) vaccine once in his life. He has never been diagnosed with any systemic disease, nor does he have any history of psychiatric or autoimmune disorders. His body mass index is 23 kg/m2, and he weighs 75 kg. He is willing and able to attend all study visits and follow the specified instructions, including fasting and not doing intense physical exercise during the previous 24 hours to visits and 72 hours post-vaccine. He has no signs of latent or active infectious diseases by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB), and he is negative for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B superficial antigen (HBsAG) and anti-Hepatitis C Virus (HCV). He has no evidence of primary or secondary immunodeficiency, and he has not used immunosuppressors during the last 6 months. He has not used inhaled corticosteroids during the last year or has any antecedents of bronchial hyper-reactivity. He does not have any antecedents of intradomiciliary contact with subjects with Tuberculosis or other mycobacteria. He has no history of substance abuse (drugs or alcohol) and has never had a severe allergic reaction or anaphylaxis to vaccines. He has not had any serious adverse events associated with the previous BCG vaccination. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to use contraceptives during the whole study duration.

A 25-year-old female with a history of hip pain and instability since adolescence. She has been diagnosed with hip dysplasia and has undergone an MRI which showed central compartment pathology. She is scheduled to undergo a periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) for her hip dysplasia. She has not had any prior surgeries on her hip or pelvis and does not have any known connective tissue disorder, neuromuscular disorder, or skeletal dysplasia. She is willing and capable of giving informed consent and completing all required follow-up visits for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure with a normal ejection fraction (HFNEF) and a body mass index (BMI) of 32. He has reported experiencing exercise intolerance and a reduced quality of life due to his condition. The patient has a heart failure clinical score of 4 and has not experienced any significant changes in cardiac medication within the last 4 weeks. He has no valvular heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, recent or debilitating stroke, cancer, or any other noncardiovascular conditions with a life expectancy of less than 2 years. The patient's creatinine level is within normal range (<2.5mg/dL) and he has no significant anemia. He has no history of psychiatric disease and plans to remain in the area for the next 6 months. The patient has passed the screening tests for pulmonary function, echocardiogram, and exercise.

For the healthy group, the patient is a 35-year-old female with no history of joint pain or swelling. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She is willing to undergo joint sonography to establish normal synovial measures in her joints.  For the RA group, the patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of joint pain and swelling for the past 5 years. She has been previously diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and has been on treatment with disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) for the past 3 years. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. She is willing to undergo joint sonography to establish a predictive sonographic value of synovium in her affected joints.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her hands, making it difficult to perform daily activities. She has been prescribed medication to manage her symptoms but has not seen significant improvement. She has been recommended to undergo physiotherapy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of magnetotherapy in treating rheumatoid arthritis. She has II ° and III ° of advancement of radiological changes and functional changes. She is in remission with low or moderate RA activity: DAS28. She has no history of taking steroid anti-inflammatory drugs or undergoing additional physiotherapy treatments for her hands. She is willing to undergo kinesiotherapy with or without magnetic field and is committed to completing the research program. She is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and congestive heart failure. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate CHF and has a left ventricular ejection fraction between 20 to 40 percent on echocardiography. The patient has not been diagnosed with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and does not have hypertension higher than 140/90 mmHg at rest. He has not been using sympatholytic agents such as clonidine, methyldopa, or reserpine. The patient does not have any significant non-cardiac disease that could affect cardiovascular regulation or autonomic neuropathy of any cause. He has no leg injuries with nerve damage and has good bladder control. The patient has no recent history of alcoholism or drug abuse and has no significant psychiatric disorders. The patient has not experienced adverse events to AT1-receptor blockers. He is likely to tolerate being off digoxin and off blockers of the RAS for a short period. The patient has not experienced an ischemic event within the past 3 months, and his serum creatinine is not higher than 200 mmol/L. The patient is not taking digoxin for atrial fibrillation and does not require treatment with aldactone. He does not have more than mild stable angina while on beta-blockers and/or calcium antagonists, and he is not on coumadin.

A 62-year-old retired construction worker was diagnosed with COPD five years ago. He has a history of smoking for 40 years and quit smoking two years ago. He reports shortness of breath with exertion, especially when climbing stairs or carrying heavy objects. He has a chronic cough with phlegm production. He is currently taking albuterol and tiotropium inhalers. He has a sedentary lifestyle due to his difficulty with breathing, which he finds frustrating as he used to enjoy working out and weightlifting. He lives alone and has two adult children who live out of state. He reports no other medical issues and is not taking any other medications. He is motivated to improve his lung function and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him increase his exercise tolerance.

The patient is a 24-year-old smoker who has been smoking for the past 5 years. She is a Hong Kong resident and is able to communicate in Cantonese. She smokes about 10 cigarettes a day and has been trying to quit smoking for the past few months but has not been successful. She is interested in participating in the Quit to Win Contest 2019 to receive incentives and social support to help her quit smoking. She is willing to participate in the study and use instant messaging tools like WhatsApp or WeChat for communication. She has not participated in any other smoking cessation programs or services. She is a full-time student and is currently in good health. Her exhaled carbon monoxide level is 7 ppm, as assessed by a CO Smokerlyzer. She is highly motivated to quit smoking and is willing to try different cessation supports provided by the study.

A 16-year-old female presented with moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris on her face. She has a history of occasional menstrual irregularities and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no significant medical history or allergies to medication. She currently uses a combination of over-the-counter topical agents and oral supplements for acne treatment. She has no current or previous use of prescription acne medications. She is willing to comply with study instructions and return to the clinic for required visits. Her vital signs and physical exam are within normal limits. She does not have any other dermatological conditions or use any potentially irritating over-the-counter products.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has never been on antiretroviral therapy before and has a CD4 count of 350/ul and an HIV-1 RNA PCR value of 20,000 cop/ml. He works as a software engineer and is in a monogamous relationship. He denies any alcohol or illicit drug use. His medical history is unremarkable and he has no current symptoms related to HIV infection. His labs show normal hemoglobin, neutrophil, platelet, AST/ALT, pancreatic amylase, creatinine clearance, and total bilirubin levels. He does not have any other serious medical conditions or a history of radiation therapy, cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents, or immunomodulating agents. He has negative serum pregnancy test and does not plan to have children in the near future. He is able to understand and provide written informed consent for the study.

45-year-old female with newly diagnosed high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome presenting with neutropenic fever and gastrointestinal symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, well-controlled with medications. She is currently not on any antibiotics. Her stool sample is collected and screened for suitability for autologous fecal microbiota transplantation (AFMT) as part of the clinical trial PreventiOn of DYSbioSis Complications With Autologous FMT in AML Patients. She is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed and written consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency, currently on glucocorticoid therapy. She experiences irregular menstrual cycles and hirsutism despite being on treatment, and is interested in exploring other options for managing her condition. She has no other significant medical or psychiatric conditions and her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use medically acceptable methods of contraception if sexually active. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of a new, extended-release form of hydrocortisone called Chronocort to the conventional, immediate-release form of hydrocortisone. She has provided written informed consent and is in good general health.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of stage IIIc ovarian cancer. She underwent initial debulking surgery followed by six cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy, which resulted in complete remission. However, 6 months later, she developed recurrent disease with multiple peritoneal nodules and was started on second-line chemotherapy. Despite treatment, her disease progressed, and she now has metastatic disease to the liver, lung, and bones. She experiences fatigue, abdominal distention, and difficulty breathing. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril and amlodipine. She has no known allergies. Her physical exam is remarkable for a palpable abdominal mass and mild ascites. Her laboratory studies show a white blood cell count of 4.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dl, and platelet count of 150 x 10^9/L. Her creatinine, liver function tests, and electrolytes are within normal limits. She has no evidence of hepatitis B or C infection. She has not received any immunosuppressive therapy or organ transplantation in the past. She understands the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl diagnosed with relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with bone marrow involvement. She has previously undergone one standard frontline chemotherapy and one salvage regimen, but her disease has relapsed. The patient experiences fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional fever. She has undergone leukapheresis to harvest T cells, which will be used to produce an autologous CAR T product directed against CD19-expressing tumor cells (CD19-CART01). After lymphodepletion with conventional chemotherapeutic agents, the patient will receive CD19-CART01 intravenously. The patient has given voluntary informed consent to participate in the study. She is in good general health and has no other medical conditions. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to practice birth control from the time of enrollment on this study and for four months after receiving the preparative regimen. Her clinical performance status is Karnofsky greater than or equal to 60%, and her BM involvement is measurable or evaluable. Her legal guardian has given informed consent, and the patient has provided verbal assent as she is greater than or equal to 12 years of age. The patient does not have severe, uncontrolled active intercurrent infections, HIV, or active HCV and/or HBV infection. She is not expected to have a life-expectancy of less than 6 weeks, and her hepatic and renal function are adequate. She does not have blood oxygen saturation < 90% or cardiac function lower than 45% by ECHO. The patient has not recently received any concurrent or recent prior therapies that would disqualify her from enrollment in the study.

A 9 year old boy was referred to the clinic by his teacher due to difficulty in reading and comprehending texts. He is currently in the 3rd grade and is struggling to keep up with his peers. The boy has no known history of ocular problems and has never undergone visual therapy or orthoptic treatment. He underwent a complete ophthalmic examination by a pediatric ophthalmologist and orthoptist, and all ocular structures were found to be within normal limits. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. The boy was diagnosed with a reading disability by an educational psychologist and is confirmed to have no ophthalmic anomaly. He is eligible for the clinical trial and will undergo further testing to evaluate his saccadic inaccuracies and diagnose dyslexia.

50-year-old female with a history of smoking (20 pack-years) was found to have a 10mm pulmonary nodule on chest CT. She has no history of lung cancer or other malignancies. She reports occasional cough without sputum production or hemoptysis. She has no dyspnea, chest pain or weight loss. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She denies any allergies. She has no history of recent IV contrast administration. She is scheduled for a biopsy to determine the nature of the nodule. She understands the study procedures and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old man who suffered a myocardial infarction a month ago is currently taking aspirin (81mg/d) and clopidogrel (75mg/d) to prevent re-occurrence. He has a history of high blood pressure and is currently taking medication to manage it. He is a former smoker and has not smoked for the past 10 years. He drinks alcohol occasionally and has no history of liver or kidney disease. His platelet count and hemoglobin levels are within the normal range. He has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or bleeding disorders. He is willing to participate in the study and provides written informed consent.

A 62-year-old man, who works as an accountant, was diagnosed with HPV-negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) of the oropharynx. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and quit the habit 5 years ago. The patient has undergone a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of HNSCC, and CT scans showed no evidence of distant metastases. He is currently experiencing pain and difficulty swallowing, and his voice has changed. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. His laboratory analysis showed adequate hematologic, renal, and liver function. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this cancer. The patient has no other major medical conditions, and he is willing to comply with the study procedures. He has signed an informed consent form indicating that he understands the purpose and procedures required for the study and is willing to participate. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial, and his participation will be assessed by the investigators for the highest safe dose of oral rigosertib that can be used with cisplatin and CRT.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has a family history of cardiovascular disease. She is overweight with a BMI of 30 and has been diagnosed with high blood pressure. She has a low Prime Diet Quality Score and has been advised to improve her diet to reduce her risk of developing heart disease. She is willing to participate in a dietary intervention study to improve her diet quality and reduce her risk of cardiovascular disease. She does not have diabetes, established cardiovascular disease, or any medical condition that would limit her ability to complete the study requirements. She does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol and is willing to make changes to her dietary habits. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in learning more about personalized dietary advice incorporating biomarker profiles.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He has undergone two prior lines of therapy but has experienced a relapse. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG Performance Scale. He has measurable disease with a paraprotein level of 7g/L. His haematological and renal parameters are within the eligibility criteria. He has not received prior therapy with pembrolizumab or any anti-PD-1, L1 or L2 inhibitor. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and has not received any investigational agent within the last 28 days. He has not had a prior allogenic stem cell transplant. He has not received plasmapheresis within the last 4 weeks. He has a negative urine pregnancy test and agrees to use adequate contraception during the trial. He has no known hypersensitivity or intolerance to cyclophosphamide or lenalidomide or any of its excipients. He has recovered from any toxicity and complications from prior interventions. He is able to tolerate thromboembolic prophylaxis. He has no known active CNS myeloma and/or carcinomatous meningitis. He has no significant cardiac disease or active infections. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial and follow the trial protocol.

A 32-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with HIV but has not started on antiretroviral therapy (ART) within the past 3 months is eligible for this clinical trial. He lives within 60 km of the testing center and speaks English fluently. He has no history of substance abuse or mental incapacity that would prevent him from providing informed consent. He is not pregnant. The patient has expressed some concerns about starting ART and has been hesitant to initiate treatment. He reports feeling overwhelmed by the diagnosis and is unsure about the potential side effects of ART. He also feels unsure about disclosing his status to friends and family and is worried about the potential stigma associated with being HIV-positive. Despite these concerns, he is open to receiving support from peers who have experience living with HIV and is interested in exploring the Treatment Ambassador program.

Patient is a 12-year-old boy from the United States who was diagnosed with primary myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) in 2001. He has been receiving supportive care, including transfusions and prophylactic antibiotics. His past medical and drug history are unremarkable. His BMI is 18, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for low hemoglobin levels (8.5 g/dL), low platelet count (60,000/µL), and low WBC count (2,800/µL). The bone marrow biopsy shows dysplasia of all three hematopoietic lineages with less than 5% myeloblasts. No chromosomal abnormality was detected.

A 53-year-old female patient with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has been scheduled for a hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. She has a high comorbidity score and is concerned about the potential side effects of the transplantation, including graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) and infectious complications. The patient is willing to participate in the PACT study, which involves the prophylactic administration of donor-derived TCM. She meets the inclusion criteria, having a Hematopoietic Cell Transplant-Co-morbidity Index (HCT-CI) score of 3 and being over 50 years old. The patient is also in complete remission, with less than 5% blasts in the bone marrow. She is planned to receive a Cluster of Differentiation 34+ (CD34+)-purified stem cell graft after conditioning with fludarabine-melphalan-thio-thepa-ATG (ATG=Antithymocyte globulin). The patient has a HLA-matched stem cell donor, who has passed the EU Tissue and Cells Directive and fulfilled the requirements for allogeneic donor blood testing. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male presented with a 3-month history of a slowly growing, non-tender lesion on his left temple. Biopsy confirmed the lesion to be a basal cell carcinoma (BCC) with infiltrative growth margins, measuring 3.5 cm in diameter. The patient was referred to a dermatologist for further management. Dermatological evaluation revealed a high-risk BCC not amenable to radical surgery due to its size and location on the temple. The patient had no history of Gorlin Syndrome, nor any other contraindications to radiotherapy. He was otherwise in good health, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Laboratory tests revealed adequate hematopoietic and hepatic function, with a calculated serum creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 80 mL/min. The patient reported no history of recent or current participation in another experimental drug study, nor any other uncontrolled medical illness. He provided written, signed informed consent and was enrolled in the study.

36yo male with a history of Crohn's disease diagnosed 10 years ago, presents to the clinic with symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea with urgency, and fatigue. He has been on mesalamine and prednisone for the past 6 months with minimal improvement in his symptoms, and his CDAI is > 220. A CT scan showed active disease in the small bowel. He has no history of abdominal surgery in the past 8 weeks and has not had a change in the dose of steroids or immunomodulators in the past 2 weeks. He is not pregnant and has no active bacterial infection or undrained abscess. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the use of PET-CT scans in the management of Crohn's disease and is willing to initiate biologic therapy if required.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years with no success. She has a history of fibroids and has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, and bloating. She has undergone multiple rounds of in vitro fertilization (IVF) with no success. She has no history of allergies and takes only prenatal vitamins daily. Her family history is negative for infertility. She lives with her husband and has no children. Her abdominal ultrasound reveals multiple fibroids, with the largest measuring 7cm in diameter. She is prescribed Ulipristal acetate (Esmya) to reduce the size of her fibroids before undergoing another round of IVF. She takes the medication for 3 months and then undergoes another round of IVF. The study will collect data on the impact of Esmya on her fertility and the modalities of its prescription. She will be followed up until she achieves pregnancy or embryo transfer failure, up to four attempts, or if she discontinues the ART treatment or is lost to follow-up.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is a university student majoring in computer science. He is generally healthy with no history of chronic illnesses or surgeries. He is physically active and enjoys playing soccer with his friends. His BMI is within the normal range for his height and weight. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He has no history of neurological disorders or muscular pathologies. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about how Vojta Therapy can improve the stabilizing muscles of the trunk.

A 25-year-old male patient with epilepsy has been experiencing seizures for the past 5 years. He is currently undergoing scalp EEG monitoring for clinical care at Seer Medical. He has previously tried various anti-epileptic drugs and has experienced moderate success with his current medication. He is able to manage his condition with medication, but is interested in participating in this study to help further the understanding of the physiological signals before and during seizures. He does not have any cognitive or psychiatric conditions that would hinder his ability to use the seizure detection devices or complete the surveys.

The patient is a 14-year-old adolescent who is scheduled for a digestive endoscopy. The patient has no known psychiatric or neurological disorders and has never undergone an endoscopy before. The patient is fluent in both English and French and has a body weight of 60 kg. The patient has no known allergies to benzodiazepines or any other medications. The patient is not currently taking any anxiolytic medication and has not received oral, intravenous or inhaled corticosteroids in the last two days. The patient is not pregnant. The patient and their parent or legal guardian are willing to participate in the study and have provided informed consent.

55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus presents to the outpatient clinic of Assiut University Heart Hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. Patient reports a family history of cardiovascular disease. The patient has been taking medications for hypertension and diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. Physical examination reveals a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, and a body mass index (BMI) of 32. Laboratory workup shows elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. The patient is diagnosed with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial investigating the association between dietary habits and risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases in Assiut governorate.

A 62-year-old man was recently diagnosed with advanced gastric adenocarcinoma. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer. He has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. His tumor is HER2/neu-negative and PD-L1-positive. He has measurable disease. He is willing to use adequate contraception as he is sexually active. He has no known history of autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency, and is not currently receiving any systemic steroid therapy or other forms of immunosuppressive therapy. He has no active infections and has not received any live vaccines within the past 30 days.

45 yo F with history of thyroid cancer, status post total thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine ablation. She is currently on levothyroxine and has stable thyroid function. She presents for follow-up with her endocrinologist and reports no changes in her weight or appetite. She is interested in participating in a study related to adipose tissue and is willing to undergo surgery to obtain adipose tissue samples. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and exercises regularly. She has no significant medical history besides thyroid cancer and takes no other medications. She is willing to undergo fasting blood sample collection and physical examination as part of the study. She has no contraindications for the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

As this is a single patient expanded access program, there is no specific patient description provided for this trial. However, it is important to note that this trial is for patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who have exhausted all other treatment options, and their physician believes that tucatinib may provide a potential benefit. Physicians interested in requesting a single patient IND should contact Seattle Genetics' Medical Information (medinfo@seagen.com) for more information.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with Nijmegen breakage syndrome. He has a history of recurrent infections and suffers from growth retardation. He has a younger sister who is also diagnosed with the same condition. His parents are healthy and non-consanguineous. His past medical history is significant for multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent infections. He is currently on prophylactic antibiotics and immunoglobulin replacement therapy. He is compliant with his medications and follows up regularly with his pediatrician. He is enrolled in school and is in the sixth grade. He enjoys playing video games and watching movies. His parents are very supportive of his health and have agreed to participate in the clinical trial. They understand that the study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of low dose treosulfan in HSCT for NBS.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman diagnosed with progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), a rare neurodegenerative condition that causes severe motor and non-motor symptoms. The patient experiences freezing of gait, cognitive decline, and difficulty with language. Medical treatment and rehabilitation have been limited in improving her symptoms. The patient has no history of seizures or pacemakers, and is an outpatient. She is interested in participating in a pilot, randomized, cross-over, double-blind trial to evaluate the efficacy of Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (DTMS) in improving her motor functions, freezing of gait, and cognitive decline. The patient is willing to undergo 14 sessions of high frequency DTMS over a 4-week period, targeting the left Broca and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been experiencing neuropathic pain for the past 6 months. He was involved in a car accident which resulted in a spinal cord injury, and now he has specific dermatomes that are affected by brush allodynia. He rates his average pain level as an 8 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale. He has been taking pain medications but has not experienced any significant relief. He is right-handed and willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of pregabalin and tramadol SR in treating his neuropathic pain. He does not have any other co-existing pain that cannot be differentiated from neuropathic pain of peripheral origin. However, he has a history of diabetes mellitus, but his HbA1C levels are within the acceptable range. He is excited to potentially benefit from the study and help further research in the field of neuropathic pain.

A 15-year-old male adolescent has been diagnosed with depression, exhibiting symptoms such as lack of energy, loss of interest in activities, and feelings of worthlessness. The patient has no physical limitations and is interested in sports and physical activity. The patient's parents are willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the Revival Active Program. The patient has no co-morbid mental health diagnosis, is not at high risk of self-harm/suicide, and has no history of self-harm or harming others. The patient is currently receiving psychotherapy and medication management for depression.

A 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 3 years. She has been treated with various disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) but has not yet been treated with tocilizumab. She is experiencing moderate to severe pain in her joints, especially in the hands and feet, which is affecting her ability to perform daily activities. She has been referred to a rheumatologist who has recommended subcutaneously administered tocilizumab as a treatment option. She received her first injection of tocilizumab a week ago and is now being considered for inclusion in the ARATA clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effectiveness and tolerability of the drug in everyday clinical practice.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He has been diagnosed with mild renal impairment with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. The patient is currently on oral hypoglycemic and antihypertensive medications. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and has not been exposed to any investigational drugs in the past 12 months. The patient does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse and has not experienced any acute illness within the past 14 days. The patient has a BMI of 25.0 kg/m2 and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient has no known history of allergy or hypersensitivity to glepaglutide. The patient is willing to comply with the contraception and study restrictions.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who identifies as gay and is sexually active. He is HIV-negative and has no history of sexually transmitted infections (STIs). He is currently using condoms for protection during anal intercourse with his partners. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the safety and acceptability of a rectal gel that may prevent HIV transmission. He is willing to abstain from anal intercourse and insertion of anything rectally, including sex toys, for the duration of the study participation. He is able to communicate in English and is willing to provide adequate locator information, as defined in the site SOP. He has no history of excessive daily alcohol use or illicit drug use that includes any injection drugs, methamphetamines (crystal meth), heroin, or cocaine including crack cocaine, within the past 12 months. He is in good health and does not have any allergies to methylparaben, propylparaben, sorbic acid, and components of N-9. He is willing to abstain from participating in other research studies involving drugs, medical devices, or genital products for the duration of study participation (until all follow-up visits are completed). He meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 32-year-old male patient was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B a few months ago. He has never received any anti-viral treatment for hepatitis B. The patient is HBeAg negative and anti-HBe positive. His serum HBV-DNA level is over 2000 IU/mL and his ALT level is over 1.25 ULN but below 10 ULN. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of clevudine monotherapy versus tenofovir monotherapy versus combination therapy of clevudine and tenofovir for 96 weeks in HBeAg negative patients with chronic hepatitis B who are naïve to anti-VHB therapy. The patient is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and not taking any systemic anti-viral, anti-neoplastic, or immuno-modulatory treatment. He has no history of cirrhosis or bridging fibrosis on liver biopsy. The patient doesn't have any other medical condition associated with chronic liver disease other than hepatitis B. His neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and abide by the requirements of the study.

45-year-old male with a history of complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) type 1 presented with severe pain in his right arm and hand for the past six months. The patient has been on multiple pain medications, including opioids, but has not found relief. He reports an average daily pain of 8 out of 10 on the pain scale and has allodynia in his right arm and hand. The pain is predominantly affecting his right extremity, and he has no history of other pain diagnoses or bilateral pain. The patient is willing to complete behavioral, clinical, and neurophysiological measurement procedures and is able to provide informed consent. He has no history of claustrophobia and is able to undergo MRI and MEG. The patient is not currently on any medications that would interfere with the study, and he has no history of substance use disorder.

A 35-year old female who underwent sleeve gastrectomy 18 months ago is attending her discharge follow-up appointment. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. Her past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obstructive sleep apnea. Her BMI was 42.2 kg/m2 before the surgery and she lost 30 kg after the procedure. However, she has been struggling with keeping the weight off and reports difficulty with adhering to a healthy diet and regular exercise routine. She has a smartphone and is comfortable with receiving and sending text messages in English. She is highly motivated to maintain her weight loss and is interested in participating in the study to receive additional support after discharge from the bariatric service.

A 32-year-old Caucasian man has recently been diagnosed with stage I seminoma testicular cancer. His tumor is over 4cm and there is stromal invasion of the rete testis by tumor cells. His alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level is normal. He has no prior history of testicular cancer or any other cancer. He does not have any chronic pulmonary disorders or serious concomitant systemic disorders. He is married and has no children. He works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known hypersensitivity or contraindications for the study drugs. He has adequate organ function, including normal levels of serum aspartate transaminase (ALT), total serum bilirubin, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), platelets, and creatinine clearance.
