He is willing to use safe contraception during the study. He is fully informed about the study and has signed the written informed consent document.

47 year old male diagnosed with chronic phase chronic myeloid leukaemia, treated with imatinib for 24 months. The patient has achieved a CCyR, but still has a detectable disease with no molecular response MR 4.5 or better. The patient's past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia and a remote history of tobacco use. The patient is currently not on any other medications and has normal organ function. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore additional treatment options for his condition. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to provide written informed consent.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been enrolled in the Clinical Pharmacy Cardiac Risk Service (CPCRS) at Kaiser Permanente Colorado due to a history of cardiovascular disease. She currently uses tobacco in the form of cigarettes and is interested in quitting. She is a fluent English speaker and has been a continuous member of KPCO in the Denver/Boulder area. She will be eligible for the study and is excited about the opportunity to receive brief, structured, telephone tobacco cessation counseling from a clinical pharmacy specialist.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as there are no eligibility criteria mentioned in the description. This study is a longitudinal cohort study of 514 pairs of white male veteran twins, examining the genetic effects on the variation of cardiovascular and pulmonary risk factors. The study has been ongoing since 1966 and includes three examinations of the cohort over an eighteen year period, with a fourth exam conducted in 1995. The objective of the fourth exam was to evaluate the relationship between cardiovascular risk factors, cognitive performance, and brain morphology.

A 35 yo female diagnosed with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) with contamination obsessions and handwashing compulsions may be eligible to participate in a clinical trial titled "Measuring Automated Behavioral Observations & Vocal Expressions (ABOVE)." The study aims to synchronize automated measurements of behavior, gaze, vocal prosody and brain activity, with simultaneous recordings of clinical contexts. The study will require screening followed by one testing session lasting approximately two hours. The participant will be asked to complete interviews, rating scales, video, audio, behavioral assessments, and heart rate measurement. The study will use the Provocation OC task and the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) to evoke OCD-related distress and anxiety unrelated to OCD. A neutral baseline and a positive affect induction, the Broad-Minded Affective Coping procedure (BMAC) will also be presented. The order of Provoc and TSST will be counterbalanced across the subjects. The study will also include up to 4 subjects that have consented to receive a DBS implant on a separate protocol. Inclusion criteria for OCD subjects include a minimum score of ≥16 on the Y-BOCS and on a stable pharmacologic regimen. Exclusion criteria include a documented lifetime diagnosis of psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, alcohol or substance abuse/dependence reported within 6 months, excluding nicotine, and the subject is deemed at high risk of suicidal behavior or impulsivity.

A 42 year old male with a history of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 5 years. Has previously tried topical treatments and phototherapy with no significant improvement. The patient has not received any biologic therapy and is currently not taking any systemic therapy for psoriasis. The patient has a PASI score of 20, a PGA score of 4, and approximately 20% of body surface area affected. The patient does not have erythrodermic, pustular, guttate, or medication-induced forms of psoriasis or other active skin diseases/infections. The patient has no history of active tuberculosis or hypersensitivity to any component of the IMP formulation, comparable drugs, or latex.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who presented to the hospital with a firm painless mass in the right testis. The patient reports that the mass has been present for several weeks and has slowly been increasing in size. The patient denies any other symptoms. Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender mass in the right testis. Scrotal ultrasound is performed, which shows a solid mass with increased vascularity. Tumor markers are elevated with an AFP level of 350 ng/mL, HCG level of 2500 mIU/mL, and LDH level of 560 U/L. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis is performed, which shows no evidence of metastasis. The patient undergoes orchiectomy, and the pathology report confirms a diagnosis of mixed germ cell tumor with elements of embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, and teratoma. The patient is referred to an oncologist for further management and treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with end-stage lung disease and is currently awaiting lung transplantation. She has a history of smoking for 30 years and has quit smoking for the past 5 years. She reports experiencing shortness of breath during moderate physical activity, such as walking up stairs or carrying groceries. She has been referred to a rehabilitation program to improve her exercise capacity before undergoing lung transplantation. The patient has no other significant medical history and does not have any addictions that may interfere with exercise. She has provided her consent to participate in the study and will undergo a 3-month hospital-based preoperative exercise training program. The 6-minute walk test, 10-meter walking speed test, and 5-times sit to stand test will be performed at the beginning and end of the rehabilitation program by the same physiotherapist, with 20-minute rest periods between each test session. The results of the tests will be analyzed to determine the patient's exercise capacity and how the delta values calculated for each test reflect the rehabilitation outcomes after the exercise program.

A 54-year-old male with a history of melanoma presents to the clinic with an unresectable stage IV melanoma. The patient's tumor has been confirmed to be BRAF V600E mutation positive from a certified lab. The patient has not received any treatment for the past 4 weeks. The patient has no active infections and is confirmed to be HIV negative, HBsAg negative, and anti-HCV Ab nonreactive. The patient has no underlying medical condition that would make the administration of study drug hazardous or obscure the interpretation of adverse events. The patient has not received any prior treatment with temsirolimus or AZD6244 or any prior mTOR or MEK inhibitor. The patient has no evidence or history of significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, psychiatric, or gastrointestinal disease that would make the administration of temsirolimus or AZD6244 hydrogen sulfate unsafe. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 3 months with an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1. The patient is willing to utilize reliable contraception during the study and for at least 4 months after the final study drug infusion or ingestion.

A 45-year-old male patient, who works as a nurse, was admitted to the COVID-19 unit at Amiens CHU with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 based on the nasopharyngeal sample. He has been in isolation for the last 5 days and has shown some improvement in his symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that uses saliva collection as an alternative to the nasopharyngeal sample for COVID-19 detection. He has no history of chronic respiratory diseases and is not under any medication. The patient is mentally and physically stable and has provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who presents with a persistent cough, fever, and weight loss over the past few weeks. He is a construction worker and has been working in dusty areas for the past year. He denies any past medical history or significant family history. On physical examination, he appears thin and has a fever of 101.5°F. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral crackles. A chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates. Sputum samples are collected and tested positive for mycobacterium tuberculosis. He is diagnosed with drug-sensitive, smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria. He weighs 80 kg and is taking no medications. He has no history of seizures, alcohol or drug abuse and has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 8 weeks. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to conceive during the study or within a month of completing the treatment. He is willing to use effective birth control methods throughout the study and for a month after stopping the treatment.

The patient is a 57-year-old man admitted to the ICU with severe sepsis. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was feeling unwell for a few days with fever, chills, and fatigue before presenting to the emergency room. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, he is febrile with a temperature of 38.9°C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and hypotensive with a blood pressure of 85/50 mmHg. He is alert and oriented but complains of generalized weakness and shortness of breath. His lungs are clear, and his abdomen is soft and non-tender. His laboratory tests reveal leukocytosis (18.5), elevated lactate (4.5), and elevated C-reactive protein (220). Blood cultures are drawn, and he is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. He is started on fluid resuscitation and vasopressor support to maintain a mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg. An echocardiogram is performed, which reveals an ejection fraction of 50%, and mildly reduced left ventricular diastolic function. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is enrolled in the study.

This is a 52-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C virus-induced liver cirrhosis. He has been asymptomatic but was recently diagnosed with portal hypertension based on imaging findings. He has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding, ascites, or encephalopathy. He is currently on medical management for his cirrhosis and is willing to participate in the study. He has no contraindications for portal pressure gradient measurement via radiological evaluation. He has no history of esophageal, gastric, liver, pancreas, or spleen tumors. He has no severe uncontrolled coagulopathy or hemodynamic instability. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who is in good health and lives an active lifestyle. She enjoys gardening, walking, and spending time with her grandchildren. She has completed high school and has been retired for several years. She takes a standard multi-vitamin but does not take any other supplements regularly. She is a non-smoker and has never taken hormone replacement therapy. She has no history of significant chronic disease and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how tart cherry juice may benefit her health.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. He has been deemed surgically unresectable or appropriate for non-surgical definitive therapy. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse. He presents with dysphagia, hoarseness, and difficulty breathing. His ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory tests show normal organ and marrow function, with an ANC of 2,500/mm3, platelets of 150,000/mm3, and Hgb of 11g/dL. His total bilirubin is 1.3mg/dL, albumin is 3.2 g/dL, and AST/ALT are within normal limits. His glomerular filtration rate is 50 mL/min. He has no history of allergic reaction to Apatinib and Tegafur Gimeracil Oteracil. He has no other concurrent disease that would make him inappropriate for participation in the study. The patient understands the study requirements and is willing to sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulties achieving and maintaining an erection for the past year. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer and underwent radical prostatectomy and radiation therapy, which he believes may have contributed to his erectile dysfunction. Despite taking oral medications prescribed by his urologist, he has not been able to achieve satisfactory erections for sexual intercourse with his partner. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new non-invasive 3D-printed external penile device that may help him achieve successful and satisfying sexual intercourse. He has a supportive female partner who is willing to participate in the study. He does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent him from wearing or operating the external penile device.

A 45-year-old male with a history of obesity and high blood pressure was diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) after an ultrasound showed increased hepatic echogenicity and blurring of liver vasculature. He has been struggling to lose weight and has tried various diets without success. He drinks alcohol occasionally but does not exceed the maximum limit of 140g/week for men. He has no history of cirrhosis, viral hepatitis, cancer, or cardiovascular disease. He is not taking any medications that affect liver function or lipid and glucose metabolism. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of intermittent fasting on NAFLD and hopes to improve his overall health and reduce his risk of developing chronic diseases. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol and attend all study visits.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU due to severe pneumonia. He has no history of any chronic diseases, cancer, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or irritable bowel syndrome. He has never taken any immunosuppressive agents. On admission, his initial systolic blood pressure was 120 mmHg and his initial pulse rate was 90 bpm. He did not require any emergent operation at the brain or torso. He did not need any vasopressor medication or transfusion.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presented to the Emergency Department with a fever of 38.5°C, cough and shortness of breath for the past 3 days. She reports body aches and fatigue, but denies any nasal congestion or sore throat. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has been working in close contact with the public in a retail store for the past week. A rapid influenza antigen test was negative, and a PCR test was ordered to confirm the diagnosis. The patient's chest X-ray showed mild bilateral interstitial infiltrates. She was admitted to the hospital for supportive care and started on oseltamivir. Further laboratory workup revealed leukopenia with a white blood cell count of 3,000/mm3 and elevated liver enzymes (ALT 80 U/L, AST 70 U/L). The patient's respiratory symptoms gradually improved over the next 3 days, and she was discharged home on oral oseltamivir for a total of 5 days. The PCR test results later came back positive for H1N1 influenza, confirming the diagnosis.

65-year-old male with a long-standing history of hypertension and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) including nocturia, weak urinary stream, and hesitancy. He has been taking amlodipine for his hypertension for the past year, but his LUTS have persisted. He denies any history of prostate cancer or surgery. His blood pressure has been consistently in the range of 140-160/90-100 mmHg despite being on amlodipine. He has not used any agents to influence his LUTS symptoms in the last 4 weeks. He is willing to participate in the trial and meet the inclusion criteria.

This is a 25-year-old male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He has a body weight of 70kg, which is within ±20% of his calculated ideal body weight. He has no pathological symptoms or findings and has undergone laboratory testing, including hematology, blood chemistry, urinalysis, and 12-lead electrocardiogram, which all yielded suitable results. He has received a detailed explanation of the clinical trial and has fully understood it, and agrees in writing to comply with the study requirements. He has not taken any prescription drugs, natural drugs, herbal medicine, non-prescription drugs, or vitamin supplements within 14 days before the first administration of the clinical trial drug. He is a non-smoker and has not consumed alcohol regularly exceeding 210g/week within 6 months of screening. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing and able to use reliable contraception from screening to 14 days after the last drug administration.

The patient is an 80-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital due to confusion, disorientation, and difficulty with memory. She was diagnosed with dementia and has a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) score of 2. She is currently receiving treatment for her condition but her family members have expressed concerns about the quality of care she is receiving. They have noticed that different healthcare professionals seem to have different approaches to her care, and they feel that there is a lack of communication and collaboration between the healthcare team members. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve the interprofessional education and practice model for dementia care in acute settings.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with terminal cancer. She is currently receiving hospice care at home. She reports experiencing moderate to severe pain that is not adequately controlled by her current medications. The patient is able to self-administer her medication through an infusion pump. She speaks English fluently and has the ability to provide informed consent. Her estimated life expectancy is less than 3 months. She has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to Hylenex. She has not received infusion therapy for pain management in the past 14 days. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She has no chest congestion or difficulty breathing. She is able to eat and drink, and her urine output is normal. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

42 yo female with BMI of 32 kg/m2, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 6 years, on metformin 1000mg BID and glipizide 10mg daily. HbA1c of 8.7%, fasting blood glucose of 178mg/dL. She has also been struggling with weight loss and has a history of unsuccessful attempts at diet and exercise. No known history of heart or liver disease, thyroid disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or cancer. No previous treatment with GLP-1 agonists or gastric bypass operation. She does not consume alcohol or smoke. She is interested in participating in the study to explore other potential treatment options for her type 2 diabetes and weight loss goals.

A 32-year old construction worker sustained second-degree burns over 15% of his body while working on a job site. He underwent a split-thickness skin graft procedure to help with the healing process. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He is a dedicated worker and is looking forward to a swift recovery so that he can return to work. The patient is able to understand and follow instructions given to him by the medical staff. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

As per the study description, the clinical trial is seeking non-opiate dependent cocaine users to evaluate the effects of pergolide on cocaine taking and its physiological and subjective effects. Therefore, the patient should be a non-opiate dependent individual with a history of cocaine abuse. They should have used cocaine within the last six months and must not have received any substance use treatment in the past month. They should be in good physical and mental health and be able to provide informed consent. Additionally, they should not have any significant medical or psychiatric conditions that could interfere with the study's objectives. The patient should be willing to stay at the study site for the entire duration of the study and adhere to the study's protocol, including drug abstinence and attendance at study visits. The study site will provide further information on eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of stable angina who will undergo a coronary drug eluting stent implantation. He has been taking aspirin (100mg/day) and standard-dose clopidogrel (600mg loading dose followed by 75mg daily maintenance dose) for at least 7 days prior to the procedure. However, he has high on-treatment platelet reactivity according to a point-of-care platelet function test, with P2Y12 reaction units (PRU) >= 230. He has not been on chronic therapy with statins. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus and has been taking medications for these conditions. He has no known allergies and no history of liver or kidney disease, myopathy or malignancy. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 57-year-old man comes to the clinic with a history of prostate cancer for the last 3 years. The patient initially presented with a high PSA score and was diagnosed with prostate cancer through biopsy. The patient underwent androgen deprivation therapy but experienced progression of disease as defined by a 20% increase in the sum of the longest diameter of target lesions. The patient is now diagnosed with metastatic androgen-independent prostate cancer with a PSA level of 25 ng/mL. The patient has no history of CNS metastases and is in good general health with ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has not received any prior immunotherapy, chemotherapy, or radiation therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the inclusion criteria, including having an absolute neutrophil count greater than 1,500/mm^3, platelet count at least 100,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is using effective contraception. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or other medical or psychiatric illness that would preclude study participation.

54-year-old female with a history of chronic hepatitis C infection for at least 6 months and is treatment-naïve. She has no evidence of cirrhosis or other significant liver disease. She has no history of significant or unstable cardiac disease, hepatic decompensation, or hepatocellular carcinoma. She has not undergone any organ transplant, excluding corneal transplants and skin grafts.

A 54-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents with cough, shortness of breath and chest pain. A chest x-ray shows a right lung mass. CT scan of the chest and abdomen show a 4 cm right upper lobe lung mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy and a left adrenal gland metastasis. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the lung. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy for any malignancy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate organ function. He is willing to undergo a biopsy of the tumor and is willing to take an investigational drug.

3-month-old healthy male infant born after a full-term pregnancy with a birth weight of 3 kg, who has received all the standard EPI vaccines. The infant's parents have been properly informed about the study and have signed the informed consent form. The parents are also available for the entire period of the study and reachable by study staff for post-vaccination follow-up. The infant has no history of congenital abdominal disorders, intussusception, or abdominal surgery. The infant has no known or suspected impairment of immunological function and has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the rotavirus vaccine. The infant has not received any rotavirus vaccine before and has no fever or history of known rotavirus disease, chronic diarrhea, or failure to thrive. The infant's baseline level of ALT or AST is within normal limits. There is no clinical evidence of active gastrointestinal illness, and the infant has not received any IM, oral, or IV corticosteroid treatment. The infant does not reside in a household with an immuno-compromised person, and has not tested positive for HBV, HCV, or HIV infection. The infant has not received a blood transfusion or blood products, including immunoglobulins.

The patient is a 22-year-old woman who was diagnosed with congenital fourth cranial nerve palsy a few years ago. She has never undergone any surgery or treatment for this condition. She reports that she has always had a slight head tilt to the right side since childhood. She has noticed that her teeth and jaw are misaligned and she is self-conscious about her smile. She has a natural teeth occlusion and is interested in exploring treatment options for her jaw and teeth misalignment. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications currently. She is willing to participate in the study and provide consent for the necessary measurements and assessments.

A 35-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer after noticing a lump in her left breast during a self-examination. Her medical history is significant for mild asthma and migraines, but otherwise, she has been healthy. She is premenopausal and her tumor is estrogen receptor positive. The patient has not received any prior treatments for breast cancer such as chemotherapy or endocrine therapy. She is willing to stop taking any medication that could affect her sex hormone status, including hormone replacement therapy (HRT). The patient is concerned about her diagnosis but is committed to finding the best treatment options. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She has a supportive family and friends who will help her through this difficult time.

A 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of advanced adenocarcinoma of the lung with metastasis to the liver, who has received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, presents with progressive disease. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 1 and Karnofsky 80%. He has no brain metastases or other significant CNS illnesses. His WBC is 5,000/mm^3, absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mm^3, platelet count is 90,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin is 10 g/dL. His bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are normal, and his creatinine clearance is 80 mL/min. He has no symptomatic congestive heart failure or unstable angina pectoris. He has no ongoing or active infections or psychiatric illnesses. He is not pregnant or nursing and has negative pregnancy test. He is willing to use effective contraception. He has received prior chemotherapy and radiation therapy and has recovered from its effects. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and has no other concurrent anticancer investigational or commercial agents.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. She has a history of depression and anxiety for which she has been receiving treatment for the past 3 years. She has been prescribed Deplin® by her physician as an adjunct therapy to her current antidepressant medication. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. She is currently employed full time and has a supportive partner at home. She is willing to participate in the study and complete the required surveys.

A 45-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) at a local hospital. He is currently experiencing symptoms such as difficulty in swallowing, recurrent nosebleeds, and hearing loss. The biopsy report confirmed type III NPC. The patient is generally healthy with no significant medical history, and his current Karnofsky performance status (KPS) is 90. The patient's laboratory results show a white blood cell count (WBC) of 6.2×109/L, neutrophil granulocyte (NE) count of 2.8×109/L, Hemoglobin (HGB) of 13g/L, and platelet (PLT) count of 260×109/L. Liver and kidney function tests were normal, with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) within the normal range. His estimated creatinine clearance rate (CCR) is 80ml/min, indicating good kidney function. The patient has not yet received any anti-tumor treatment, including radiotherapy or chemotherapy. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The potential participant is a female athlete between the ages of 13-16 who participates in a sport that has an increased anterior cruciate ligament injury rate. She will be asked to participate in a research study to determine if an eighteen-session strengthening program can decrease her risk for anterior cruciate ligament injuries. The program will consist of neuromuscular and proprioceptive exercises to improve her landing techniques. The participant will be given two questionnaires and undergo functional and movement tests pre and post-program. All tests will be video recorded and used only for the purpose of conducting the research study. Follow-up will occur one year later to assess any lasting effects and validate any results. Males and females outside of the age range of 13-16 will be excluded from participation.

The patient is a 10-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of severe hemophilia A. He has received more than 50 exposure days with a previous Factor VIII (FVIII) product. The patient's parent or legally acceptable representative agrees to adhere to all protocol requirements. The patient has no history of or current FVIII inhibitors, and has not received any investigational medical product within 30 days prior to the first rVIII-SingleChain administration. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to any FVIII product or hamster protein. The patient is not currently receiving IV immunomodulating agents or chronic systemic corticosteroid treatment. The patient's serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) values are within normal limits at Screening. The patient's serum creatinine values are also within normal limits at Screening. The patient has no evidence of thrombosis within 3 months before Day 1 of the study. The patient has not experienced a life-threatening bleeding episode or had major surgery or an orthopedic surgical procedure during the 3 months before rVIII-SingleChain administration.

A 4-year-old boy with delayed speech and language development, as well as difficulty with social interaction and play skills. He has been previously diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and has been receiving therapy at a local community center. The child's mother is the primary caregiver and is interested in participating in the WHO Caregivers Skills Training Program to learn new techniques to better interact and communicate with her son. The family lives in a rural community in Rawalpindi, Pakistan and has limited access to specialized healthcare services. The child is otherwise healthy and does not have any other physical or mental health conditions.

A 62-year-old retired librarian was recently diagnosed with muscle invasive bladder cancer. She had been experiencing symptoms of hematuria, frequent urination, and pain during urination for the past few months. She had no significant past medical history and was not on any medications. She lives alone but has a supportive network of family and friends. She is concerned about the impact of the surgery on her quality of life, particularly in terms of continence and sexual function. She has been informed about the modified technique for uretero-ileal anastomosis and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has good renal function with serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL. She is willing to adhere to the follow-up regimen and is currently in good overall health with a good performance status. She has undergone the necessary preoperative assessments, including contrast-enhanced pelvi-abdominal CT scan and laboratory investigations. She has undergone bowel preparation and is ready for the surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic lower back pain for the past 10 years. The pain is described as sharp and shooting, and radiates down both legs. She has tried multiple pain medications and physical therapy but has not found relief. She was recently implanted with a Boston Scientific Spectra neurostimulation system with a CoverEdge surgical lead. She is interested in participating in the CoverEdge Algorithm Programming Study to explore programming features of the device in hopes of achieving better pain relief. She has no cognitive impairment and is able to assess pain relief and complete study assessments. She has signed a valid, Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved informed consent form and is 18 years of age or older.

56-year-old postmenopausal woman with a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis for 8 years presents with persistent pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances despite medication use. The patient reports a pain score of 6 out of 10 and difficulty sleeping at night. She has been on methotrexate and sulfasalazine for the past 3 years, with no significant improvement in symptoms. The patient is interested in alternative therapies and has heard about the potential benefits of pulsed magnetic field (PMF) therapy. She has no history of lupus, sleep apnea, or restless leg syndrome, and is not on high-dose prednisone or equivalent. She has not had any recent surgeries or implanted devices. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the PMF pad treatment.

The patient is a 20-year-old male with a history of Ewing's tumor of the pelvic bone. He was diagnosed 2 years ago and underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, he experienced a relapse 6 months ago with metastases to the lungs. He completed salvage chemotherapy with a partial response. He has been referred for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from a matched unrelated donor. His donor has been identified, and HLA typing has been confirmed. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 90% and no significant comorbidities. He has normal cardiac, renal, and hepatic function. His lung function tests are also normal. He is willing to undergo myeloablative conditioning with busulfan, melphalan, and thiotepa followed by T-cell depleted peripheral blood stem cell transplantation. He has been counseled about the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and has given informed consent for participation in this clinical trial.

A 65-year-old male patient presents with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. He is scheduled for an elective coronary artery bypass surgery due to severe stenosis in his left anterior descending coronary artery. He reports occasional chest pain with exertion, relieved by rest. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the epigastric area. His laboratory tests including platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and serum creatinine are all within normal limits. He denies any history of bleeding diathesis. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has been taking aspirin for the last three months as part of his cardiac treatment.

10-year-old male diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who has experienced more than one relapse or failed at least two remission induction regimens. Bone marrow aspirate indicates more than 25% blasts (M3 marrow) and CD52 expression on at least 25% of malignant cells at relapse. The patient has not received prior alemtuzumab or its components and has recovered from prior immunotherapy and chemotherapy. The patient has a Karnofsky/Lansky performance status of 50-100% and normal liver and kidney function. No evidence of dyspnea or exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry is greater than 94%. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or has nursing plans for 3 months after the study participation, and has a negative pregnancy test. The patient is not experiencing serious uncontrolled medical conditions, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, autoimmune thrombocytopenia, or serious uncontrolled infection. The patient has not received any other concurrent anticancer immunomodulating agents and has recovered from prior chemotherapy, and more than two weeks have passed since the last radiotherapy session. The patient has experienced seizures in the past but is well-controlled with anticonvulsants, and CNS toxicity is less than or equal to grade 2. The patient has received one dose of prior intrathecal (IT) methotrexate, cytarabine, and hydrocortisone; IT cytarabine alone; or IT methotrexate alone allowed as part of initial diagnostic spinal tap, and prior hydroxyurea therapy is allowed.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past few months. Echocardiography revealed severe aortic stenosis with an ejection fraction of 50%. He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He is currently on amlodipine 5 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. He has no known allergies. The physical examination reveals a systolic murmur in the right upper sternal border and bilateral basal crackles in the lungs. His blood pressure is 145/90 mm Hg, and heart rate is 85 beats per minute. His lab results are within normal limits. Cross-sectional imaging shows severe aortic stenosis and no other significant findings. He is a candidate for aortic valve replacement surgery and will be considered for enrollment in the clinical trial evaluating different strategies of pericardial drainage after aortic valvular surgery.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been struggling with hair pulling for over a year. She often pulls out her hair when she is feeling anxious or stressed, especially during school. She has tried to stop on her own but has been unsuccessful. She is currently in 7th grade and has been experiencing teasing from her peers due to her hair loss. Her parents are concerned about the impact this is having on her self-esteem and social life. She has no other medical or psychiatric conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is in good physical health and has no known allergies. Her parents are willing to participate in the study and provide consent for her involvement.

11-year-old female with Turner's syndrome diagnosed at birth. She has been receiving growth hormone therapy since the age of 4 years. She has no significant medical history, and her current medications include growth hormone and vitamin D supplements. She is currently attending school and has no significant learning or behavioral difficulties, although she sometimes feels left out and struggles to make friends. She and her parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the potential benefits of estrogen therapy on her mental and social functioning. She is willing to undergo regular assessments and testing over the course of the study. She is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection for 10 years. He was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection based on anti-HCV serology and detectable HCV-RNA plasma level. He has compensated liver disease with Child-Pugh Grade A. He has not received any prior therapy with interferon or ribavirin and any investigational medication within the past 6 weeks. He has no history of any other significant illness. He is willing to use two effective forms of contraception during the treatment and during the 6 months after the end of treatment as he has a female partner of childbearing age. He has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes is seeking to improve her glycemic control. She has been treated with oral hypoglycemic agents and has an HbA1c level of 8.5, indicating poor control of her diabetes. She has no other significant medical history and is physically active. The patient is fluent in English and has a telephone at home. She has a blood glucose machine and is willing to participate in a one-year study. The patient has been approved by her physician to participate in the study and is able to understand and provide informed consent. She has not experienced an acute coronary event in the past 6 months or been diagnosed with a medical condition that precludes adherence to study dietary recommendations. She is not following a low-carbohydrate high-fat dietary regimen such as the Atkins diet or currently following the South Beach Diet. The patient is not legally blind or significantly visually impaired.

32F with a history of depression since adolescence, treated with various antidepressants and psychotherapy with limited success, was referred to the study by her psychiatrist. She reports feeling constantly unhappy, uninterested in activities she used to enjoy, and lacking motivation to engage in anything. She also reports feeling hopeless about her future and having difficulty concentrating. She has no significant medical history or substance abuse history. She is currently taking sertraline 100mg daily and has been on this dose for the past 3 months with no significant improvement in her mood. She has had no prior treatment with rTMS, transcranial direct current stimulation, or electroconvulsive therapy. She is right-handed with normal vision and intelligence. She completed high school and has a college degree. She has no history of significant head trauma, neurological disorders, or alcohol or drug abuse. She is not pregnant and is able to provide informed consent. She is interested in participating in the study and hopes that this treatment will help her feel better.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with varicose veins in her left leg. She has no significant medical history and is in good overall health. The patient reports that she has been experiencing pain and discomfort in her left leg, especially when standing for long periods of time. She has tried wearing compression stockings, but has not found them to be effective in relieving her symptoms. Her physician has recommended endovenous laser treatment (EVLT) as a treatment option. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of variable lidocaine concentrations in tumescent anesthesia for pain control during and after the procedure. She understands the informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the trial.

A 30-year-old healthy male, with no history of significant illnesses, is eligible to participate in a bioequivalence study of Metformin 500 mg tablets. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has a weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 22. He has no significant findings in his medical history, physical examination, and laboratory evaluations. He is negative for the disease markers of HIV 1 and 2, Hepatitis B and C, and Syphilis. His AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels are within the normal range. His ECG shows normal morphology and measurements, with QTcB or QTcF less than 450

The patient is a 25-year-old Thai woman who has no history of any ocular disease. She wears glasses with a refractive error of -2.50 diopters in both eyes. She has no history of ocular surgery or laser treatments. She is generally healthy and does not have any systemic diseases such as diabetes. She is interested in participating in a study to determine the subfoveal choroidal thickness in normal Thai eyes. She has no family history of any ocular disease. She has read and understood the information provided on the study and has given her written informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic knee pain and difficulty with mobility due to primary knee arthrosis. He has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, pain medication, and weight loss, but has not obtained sufficient relief. His bone quality is estimated to be sufficient for implantation of knee prosthesis. The patient is mentally competent and has provided informed and written consent to participate in the study. He does not have any neuromuscular or vascular diseases in the affected leg and is not using any non-steroid anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID). The patient does not have a history of osteoporosis or knee arthrosis following fracture sequelae. He is not pregnant nor at risk of getting pregnant throughout the 2-year follow-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and takes no regular medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2, which falls within the range of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2 as required for this study. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has never participated in an investigational drug trial before. His vital signs, including BP and PR, are within normal limits, and his 12-lead ECG and clinical laboratory tests show no clinically relevant abnormalities. He gives his informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of Diamond-Blackfan Anemia (DBA). She has been transfusion-dependent for the past 6 months, requiring at least one unit of red blood cells per month. She has been on a stable dose of prednisone (40 mg/day) for the past 3 months, with no improvement in her transfusion requirements. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her laboratory test results are as follows: ANC 2000/uL, Platelet count 120,000/uL, Serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, Direct bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN), and Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 1.5 x ULN. She has been disease-free of prior malignancies for more than 5 years. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use two acceptable methods of birth control if she becomes sexually active during the study. She is able to take aspirin daily as prophylactic anticoagulation. She is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

A 62-years-old man diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) 8 years ago. He has been managed with watchful waiting, and his disease has remained stable until recently when he presented with fatigue, night sweats, and abdominal fullness. CT scan revealed new lymphadenopathy measuring 5cm in the retroperitoneum, with bilateral submandibular lymph nodes. PET-CT scan confirmed FDG avid lymph nodes and splenomegaly. Biopsy of the lymph node showed transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). He has received one cycle of R-CHOP therapy, but a repeat PET-CT scan showed persistent disease in the lymph nodes. The patient is an otherwise healthy male with ECOG performance status of 1. He has no significant medical history, and he has not had any previous exposure to PNT2258. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and available for at least 2 cycles (6 weeks).

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity was diagnosed with peripheral T-cell lymphoma. He presents with a 2-month history of fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. On physical examination, he has bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. Workup showed elevated LDH and leukocytosis. CT scan revealed multiple enlarged lymph nodes and splenomegaly. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of peripheral T-cell lymphoma. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He has no active infections, no other active malignancies, and no history of active seizures. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1, and his estimated life expectancy is at least 12 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and he is willing to use effective contraception during the study. The patient has no history of uncontrolled or severe cardiovascular disease, bleeding, diarrhea, or intestinal obstruction, and no hypersensitivity to albumen. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to investigate the efficacy and safety of endostar combined with CHOP regimen as first-line treatment for peripheral T cell lymphoma.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation and recurrent episodes of palpitations despite taking antiarrhythmic medications. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion. He has been referred for catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation. He has consented to participate in the study and has no contraindications to transoesophageal echocardiography. He lives independently and has no history of psychological or cognitive impairments. He is willing to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 52-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis is being treated at Northwestern Memorial Hospital for liver disease. He is currently a candidate for liver transplant and has a MELD score of 12. He has been experiencing fatigue, sleep disturbances, and depression, which have been affecting his daily life. He is able to read and speak English and has the cognitive ability to complete the measures required for the study. He has not received a liver transplant before and does not have hepatic encephalopathy or acute liver failure. He is willing to participate in the study to help improve the understanding of HRQoL in pre-liver transplant candidates with low MELD scores.

A 45-year-old Chinese woman with a history of primary hypercholesterolemia and no lipid modifying drug treatment for at least 6 weeks. She has high LDL-C levels ranging from 3.36-4.88mmol/L (130-189 mg/dL) and fasting triglyceride levels < 350 mg/dL. She has been on a cholesterol lowering diet for the past 6 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a highly effective birth control method. She has no history of liver transaminase levels higher than 1.5 x upper limit of normal or a positive test for human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. The patient has not been diagnosed with diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, advanced cancer, or endocrine disease. She has not had any surgeries or severe injuries in the past 6 months. Additionally, the patient has not participated in any other studies in the past 3 months and has not been treated with a fibric acid derivative, probucol, warfarin, systemic corticosteroid, cyclosporine or other immunosuppressant agent within the prior 12 weeks.

27 year-old female with a history of mild to moderate perennial allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and mild asthma due to sensitization against house dust mites. She reports experiencing symptoms such as nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy, watery eyes. These symptoms occur year-round and are exacerbated by exposure to dust and other allergens. She is currently managed with antihistamines, nasal corticosteroids, and rescue inhalers for her asthma symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the safety and effectiveness of a combination treatment for her allergies and asthma. The patient is not pregnant and agrees to practice an effective method of contraception during the study period. She has no relevant cardiovascular, renal, pulmonary or endocrine diseases, no history of autoimmune disease, no history of active infectious disease, no current diagnosis or history of malignancy, no relevant neurological or psychiatric disorder, and has not used an investigational drug within three months before enrollment.

This is a 25 year old male with no significant past medical history. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. The patient has provided a signed informed consent indicating that he is willing to participate in the study. The patient does not have any evidence or history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease. He has not undergone gastrectomy and does not have gout/hyperuricemia, with sUA level within the normal range at screening. The patient has not experienced an episode of nephrolithiasis or ureterolithiasis.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of Type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome. He has a BMI of 33 and elevated blood pressure. He also has dyslipidemia and has been on statin therapy for the past year. Despite this, his most recent lipid panel showed persistent hyperlipidemia. He works as a truck driver and has a sedentary lifestyle due to the nature of his job. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He has no prior history of heart disease, but his father had a heart attack at the age of 65. He is compliant with his medications and has no known drug allergies. His most recent A1C was 7.5%, and he has been managed by his primary care physician for the past 5 years. He is willing to attend frequent clinic visits and follow recommendations for aggressive risk factor modification. He has no known contraindications to MRI.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She has a BMI of 24 and has had a healthy pregnancy thus far. She will be undergoing a scheduled cesarean section with a Pfannenstiel incision. She does not have any chronic medical conditions that would affect wound healing, such as diabetes, liver disease, or chronic anemia. She is not on any anti-coagulant therapy and does not have a pacemaker. She has been advised about the study and has given her consent to participate.

A 68-year-old man presents with a history of hematuria and dysuria. He has been smoking for over 30 years and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He underwent a transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) procedure and was diagnosed with muscle invasive urothelial cancer of the bladder. He is not a candidate for radical cystectomy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. The patient has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Scale. His screening labs show an absolute neutrophil count of 2,100 /mcL, platelets of 130,000 /mcL, hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, serum creatinine of 1.1 x upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate aminotransferase of 1.2 x ULN, alanine aminotransferase of 0.9 x ULN, serum total bilirubin of 0.9 x ULN, albumin of 3.2 mg/dL, international normalized ratio of 1.2 x ULN, prothrombin time of 1.1 x ULN, and activated Partial Thromboplastin Time of 1.0 x ULN. The patient is willing to use 2 methods of birth control during the study and for 120 days after the last dose of study medication. He has not received prior targeted small molecule therapy, radiation therapy or systemic chemotherapy for urothelial bladder cancer including neoadjuvant chemotherapy. His performance status and lab values make him eligible for the trial.

29-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation with a history of chronic hypertension and mild proteinuria presents with worsening edema and elevated blood pressure. She reports occasional headaches and blurry vision. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and anxiety. The patient is currently not taking any medications except for her prenatal vitamins. Her obstetric history includes one previous term delivery via C-section due to fetal distress. Her ultrasound shows a fetus measuring at the 34th percentile for gestational age with increased resistance in the uterine arteries. Her labs show a platelet count of 125,000 and mildly elevated liver enzymes. She is able to read and understand informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with a relapsed Ewing's sarcoma. She has undergone previous treatment including surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy, but the cancer has not responded. The patient and her family have decided to participate in a phase I clinical trial that evaluates the tolerance and effects of tariquidar, given in combination with one of three anticancer drugs, for treating solid tumors. The patient will receive tariquidar with either doxorubicin, vinorelbine, or docetaxel. The study requires routine blood tests twice weekly and examinations by a doctor at least once weekly during treatment. The patient must have adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function, as well as normal cardiac ejection fraction by echocardiogram if receiving doxorubicin. The patient or her legal guardians must sign a document of informed consent indicating their understanding of the investigational nature and risks of the study.

As this is an educational intervention study, there are no patients involved. However, the study is looking for schools and teachers who are willing to participate in the intervention. The inclusion criteria for schools are that they must be interested in implementing the social and financial education curriculum with their students in primary and secondary schools during the academic year 2014. The study is also looking for teachers who teach entrepreneurship, social studies, or mathematics and are interested in participating in the study by receiving training on the use of active-learning methods to implement the curriculum with their students. The study does not have any exclusion criteria, except for non-consenting individuals.

The patient is a 42-year-old mother of a 7-year-old boy who was initially diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma two years ago. The boy underwent aggressive treatments, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. However, the cancer relapsed a few months ago, and the mother is now faced with difficult decisions regarding the next course of action. The mother is currently in a state of emotional distress and is struggling to balance her desire to provide her son with any possible chance of survival with her concerns about the potential negative impact of aggressive treatments on his quality of life. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study to gain a better understanding of parental decision-making for children with relapsed neuroblastoma.

A 50-year-old male with a history of tremors and stiffness in his left hand for the past 18 months has been diagnosed with early Parkinson's disease. He has been taking L-dopa for the past 3 months, and the dose has been stable at 400 mg/day. He has not taken any other medications for Parkinson's disease. He is currently working as a software engineer and has noticed difficulty in typing and performing fine motor tasks. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a body mass index of 25. His family history is negative for any neurodegenerative diseases. He is able to self-inject the investigational product and is willing to comply with all study procedures. He has signed the informed consent form voluntarily. His Modified Hoehn and Yahr stage is 1.5.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is HIV-1 and -2 uninfected and resides in a metropolitan area in the United States. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an experimental HIV vaccine. She has no significant medical history and is in good general health. She has never participated in a HIV vaccine trial before. She has a pre-existing adenovirus 5 neutralizing antibody titer of 1:1500 ratio. She is willing to use acceptable forms of contraception from at least 21 days prior to enrollment through the duration of the study. The patient is able to understand and willing to comply with the study requirements and willing to be followed for the duration of the study. She has no history of immunosuppressive medications, blood products, immunoglobulin, live attenuated vaccines, or investigational research agents within 30 days prior to first study vaccine administration. She does not have active syphilis infection, autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency, serious angioedema within the past 3 years, body mass index (BMI) of 40 or less OR BMI of 35 or less with certain other criteria. She has never been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus type 1 or 2, and she does not have uncontrolled hypertension, bleeding disorder, cancer, seizure disorder, absence of spleen, or certain abnormal laboratory values. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 28-year-old woman diagnosed with bipolar disorder with a history of hospitalizations due to manic episodes is currently receiving outpatient mental health services at a community clinic in Norway. She reports experiencing mood swings, irritability, and difficulty sleeping. She has a history of substance abuse and is currently in recovery. She lives alone and is unemployed due to the difficulties she has faced managing her condition. She has a supportive family who live nearby and help her with daily tasks. She is fluent in Norwegian and is willing to participate in the study. She is motivated to learn new skills to manage her illness and improve her quality of life.

A 30-year-old Hispanic woman who is 32 weeks pregnant tested positive for HIV during her routine prenatal screening. She has no history of any medical issues and has been attending all her prenatal appointments regularly. She is currently on a standard of care antiretroviral prophylaxis, which includes ZDV 300 mg, 3TC 150mg and LPV/r 400/100 twice a day starting as soon possible after 14 weeks of pregnancy + ZDV 300 mg every 3 hours during labor. She has been adherent to her medication regimen and has not experienced any side effects. She has no history of drug abuse or smoking. She is married and has a 2-year-old son who is HIV negative. She intends to deliver at a study site and bring her infant for postnatal care for at least 6 months. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study. Her CD4 cell count is not known. She has agreed not to breastfeed. She has no concurrent participation in any other clinical trial.

The patient is a 2 month old male infant who was diagnosed with idiopathic clubfoot deformity. The baby was born full term without any complications during delivery. The parents noted the deformity shortly after birth and brought it to the attention of their pediatrician who referred them to an orthopedic surgeon. The baby has been undergoing the Ponseti technique of manipulation and casting for the past month. The baby has no other medical conditions, and is exclusively breastfed. The baby's mother is a stay-at-home mom and the father works as an accountant. Both parents are involved in the care of the baby and are interested in participating in the study to help improve the experience of their child during casting. The baby has not been given any analgesics within three hours prior to data collection.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing limited range of motion in her left shoulder for the past six months. She has no history of trauma, but has been under a lot of stress due to work and family issues. She describes the pain as dull and achy, with occasional sharp pains when she moves her arm in certain positions. She has tried physical therapy and pain medications, but has found little relief. The patient is in otherwise good health, with no other medical conditions. She is motivated to try new treatments and is interested in exploring mind-body therapies to help alleviate her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements and potential risks. She is not currently under psychiatric care or using prescription psychotropic medication.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia with no siblings or suitable related/unrelated donor for allogenic transplantation. The patient was previously treated with chemotherapy but did not achieve complete remission. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, but otherwise, he is relatively healthy. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and swelling in the area of his dental implant. He has a history of good oral hygiene and has been under regular dental check-ups every 6 months for the last 5 years. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He works as a software engineer and lives with his wife and two children. He is in good general health and takes no medications regularly. His medical history is unremarkable. He has one dental implant in the lower right molar area which was placed 3 years ago. He noticed the swelling and discomfort around the implant for the past 2 weeks. The implant was evaluated by his dentist and was diagnosed with initial peri-implantitis. The patient was advised to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of non-surgical treatment with and without photodynamic therapy on initial peri-implantitis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 52-year-old male presents with a complaint of thick, yellow, and brittle toenails. He has been experiencing this problem for the last 2 years, and it has been gradually worsening. He has a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension, both of which are currently well controlled. He denies any pain or discomfort in the affected toenails but is bothered by their appearance. On examination, he has thickened, discolored toenails with hyperkeratosis at the distal edge. The great toenails are affected bilaterally, with 50% involvement of the area of the nail unit. There is no lunular involvement, and there is at least 2 mm of uninvolved nail growth as measured from the proximal nail fold. A KOH preparation and culture confirm the diagnosis of distal subungual onychomycosis. The patient is otherwise healthy and is not taking any medications that could interfere with the study. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of TMI-358 for the treatment of his toenail fungus.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from his sibling donor two years ago. He had a molecular relapse three months ago and has received several rounds of standard donor lymphocyte infusion (stdDLI) with a dose of at least 107 CD3+ cells/kg, but failed to achieve a sustained remission. He is currently not receiving any immunosuppressive treatment for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). His performance status is 1 according to ECOG and his liver and renal function are normal. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma 2 years ago. She received definitive radiation therapy and chemotherapy, and her tumor was in remission for 18 months. However, she recently started experiencing headaches, facial numbness, and tinnitus. She underwent imaging studies that revealed a recurrence of the tumor in the nasopharynx and retropharyngeal lymph nodes. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is an active non-smoker. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she has no significant comorbidities. She is willing to undergo contrast MRI scan and PET/CT scan and has an anticipated survival time of greater than 12 months. She wants to explore new treatments and is willing to participate in clinical trials to improve her chances of survival. She understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to sign informed consent.

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of schizophrenia and no history of diabetes presents to the clinic. He has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for 10 years and has been on antipsychotic medications for the past 5 years. Currently, he is prescribed olanzapine (Zyprexa) to manage his symptoms. His BMI is 26.5 kg/m2 and he has gained 10 kg over the past year. He reports feeling more hungry and tired since starting the medication. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of antipsychotic medications on energy intake and expenditure. He is willing to provide urine samples for the doubly-labeled water method and is able to comply with the study requirements. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

Patient A is a 30-year-old female who has been diagnosed with hypophosphatasia (HPP) based on genetic testing. She has been experiencing low-traumatic fractures, hip pain, and arthropathy. She has no history of any other musculoskeletal diseases, inflammatory disorders, or genetic disorders affecting bone. She doesn't have diabetes mellitus type 1 and 2, COPD, chronic kidney or liver dysfunction, or any malignancy. She is not using any systemic glucocorticoids or experiencing any eating disorders. She has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. She will undergo complete serological and radiological examinations to assess her bone status. The study will analyze her bone microstructure using High resolution peripheral quantitative computer tomography (HR-pQCT) and measure microRNAs (miRNAs) in her serum using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Additionally, her body composition, vitamin D levels, and established bone turnover markers including PINP, CTX, and sclerostin will be analyzed.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who was born at full term with a normal birth weight. He is in good health and has no known medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medication that affects his appetite or food intake. He has no significant learning, behavioral or emotional difficulties. He is willing to consume 50g of HFCS-55, sucrose or glucose, or a control treatment, and have his food intake measured 60 minutes after consumption. He is also willing to have his subjective appetite measured at 15, 30, 45, 60 and 90 minutes.

The patient is a 43-year-old female with a history of type II diabetes and a BMI of 42. She has been struggling to control her blood sugar levels despite medication and lifestyle changes. She is interested in bariatric surgery to help with weight loss and diabetes management. Her recent lab work showed a hemoglobin A1c level of 8.3%, indicating poor glycemic control. She has no history of significant heart disease, pulmonary embolism, proliferative retinopathy, or renal failure. Her liver function and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She is mentally and legally capable of providing consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has never had a colonoscopy before. He has no history of colon cancer or polyps in his family, but he is interested in getting screened for colorectal cancer. He has never had any symptoms of colon cancer, such as rectal bleeding, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel habits. He does not take any medications regularly and has no significant medical history. His physical exam is unremarkable. He agrees to participate in the PREDICT study and is able to provide written, informed consent. He understands the responsibilities of trial participation and is willing to comply with study procedures. He is not positive to Fecal Immunochemical Test or Fecal Occult Blood Test, and he is not undergoing CRC surveillance colonoscopy. He is not at high risk for CRC, and he does not have a personal history of CRC, IBD or hereditary polyposic or non-polyposic syndromes. He has not had previous resection of the sigmoid rectum, and he is not on anticoagulant therapy, which precludes resection / removal operations due to histopathological findings. He is not undergoing an emergency colonoscopy.

32F with a history of occasional low back pain for the past 6 months, which has been getting progressively worse. No history of trauma or injury to the back. The pain is localized to the low back region without any radiation or referred pain. The pain is worse with prolonged sitting and standing, and relieved by lying down. No weakness or numbness in the lower extremities. No history of fever, weight loss, or night sweats. No history of inflammatory rheumatologic disease, cancer or fibromyalgia. No suspicion of fibromyalgia. The patient is able to read the handout and fill out the questionnaires. The patient has not been habitually in a prostrate position.

Patient is a 24-year-old male from the United States who works as a software engineer. He has no past medical history and no known drug allergies. He weighs 165 lbs and has a BMI of 23. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He is able to provide written informed consent and has access to a telephone. He has not received any vaccines within the past 14 days and has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products within the past 90 days. He has not received any systemic glucocorticoids or other immune-modifying drugs within the past year. He is in good health and has no significant neurological or psychiatric diagnoses.

The patient is a 24 year-old Caucasian male. He is HIV-1 negative, B Hepatitis negative, and C Hepatitis negative. He is a non-smoker with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He has no current or past history of psychiatric disorder, and is not taking any prescription or over-the-counter products. He does not use any form of recreational drugs, and has not consumed grapefruit or xanthine-containing beverages in the past 15 and 48 days, respectively. He has no history of hepatic disease, renal disease, GI diseases, chronic infectious disease, heart disease, lung disease, neurologic disease, endocrine disease, etc. On screening and check-in, his lab results and EKG are within the limits stipulated in the protocol. His Alanine S. Transaminase(AST)/Alanine L. Transaminase(ALT) levels are within normal range, as well as his Bilirubin and Amylase levels. He has an Absolute Neutrophil Count of 2000/mL and a Hgb of 12.0 g/dl. His Platelets are within normal range, and his Serum Creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dl. He is able to give consent and is in good health as determined by medical examination.

A 28-year-old Haitian woman presented to the GHESKIO Centers in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, with a recent diagnosis of HIV. She reported feeling sad, hopeless, and having difficulty sleeping for the past month. She denied any suicidal thoughts or attempts. She has never been diagnosed with depression before and did not seek treatment for her symptoms. She reported a history of physical and emotional abuse from her previous partner, who is also HIV positive, and currently incarcerated. She lives with her sister and two young children, and works as a street vendor selling clothing. She has a high school education and is fluent in Haitian Creole. Her vital signs were within normal limits, and the physical exam was unremarkable. She scored 14 on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) indicating likely major depression. She was confirmed for major depression on the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) and met all inclusion criteria for the study. She was found to have no exclusion criteria and agreed to participate in the study.

A 67 year old man was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 3 years ago and underwent treatment with lenalidomide and dexamethasone. Initially, he responded well to the therapy and achieved partial remission but eventually became refractory to lenalidomide after 18 months of treatment. He then underwent treatment with bortezomib and dexamethasone but experienced disease progression after 6 months. He presented to the clinic complaining of fatigue, bone pain, and difficulty walking. His laboratory tests showed creatinine clearance of 45 ml/min, absolute neutrophil count of 1200/uL, platelet count of 80,000/uL, and hemoglobin of 9 g/dL. He had a serum monoclonal protein level of 2.5 g/dL, and a bone marrow biopsy revealed 50% plasma cells. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

63 year old male with advanced stage lung cancer who has been experiencing sleep disturbances for the past week. He is currently being treated at the Supportive Care outpatient clinic at M.D. Anderson Cancer Center. His Karnofsky performance status score is 70. He is an English speaker and agrees to return to M.D. Anderson Cancer Center for follow-up visits. He has no history of retinal disease, is not currently on amiodarone, thiazide diuretics or epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors, and is not receiving ultraviolet A light/ultraviolet B light therapy or tanning sessions at salons. He has not received light therapy in the past as part of treatment for other disorders or as a study subject. He does not have a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea or narcolepsy and has less than 2 hours of direct exposure to outdoor natural light per day. He is willing to use the Litebook device for 30 minutes every day for 28 days and complete the necessary diaries and questionnaires.

A 65-year-old male presents with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 10 years, well-controlled with metformin. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has a history of smoking (quit 5 years ago). He reports occasional episodes of chest pain on exertion for the past 6 months. He has no history of hypertension or dyslipidemia. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 80 beats/min, and his BMI is 28 kg/m2. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory results show HbA1c of 6.8%, fasting blood glucose of 130 mg/dL, total cholesterol of 200 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol of 130 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 50 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 150 mg/dL. ECG shows sinus rhythm with mild left ventricular hypertrophy. He is scheduled for coronary angiography for clinical purposes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and occasional palpitations. He reports feeling dizzy and lightheaded during these palpitations. He has not had any previous cardiac monitoring and is interested in finding out if his symptoms are related to an arrhythmia. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the long term continuous monitoring ECG device. He has no known skin allergies or conditions that would prevent him from wearing the Zio® Patch.
