He is not receiving pacing therapy or anticipated to receive external cardiac defibrillation during the monitoring period. He is not anticipated to be exposed to high frequency surgical equipment during the monitoring period.

This study is seeking to enroll married or cohabitating couples who have been together for the past three months in which one partner is an OEF/OIF/OND veteran with PTSD. The veteran must have experienced a specific combat-related event or high magnitude operational experience during a military deployment in support of OIF/OEF/OND that resulted in PTSD. The study will compare two cognitive-behavioral therapies - Prolonged Exposure (PE) and Cognitive-Behavioral Couples Therapy (CBCT) for PTSD. The study aims to identify whether any significant differences exist between PE and CBCT in treating PTSD and improving relationship functioning. Both partners in each couple will complete several assessments measuring psychological distress and relationship functioning at five time-points throughout the study, but only the partners assigned to the CBCT group will be involved in the actual therapy sessions. The study is looking to enroll 76 couples who are willing to make a commitment to treatment as prescribed by their randomization in this study, speak and read English and are stable for at least 6 weeks on any psychotropic medications either partner may be taking. Exclusion criteria include severe intimate aggression, current suicidal ideation, alcohol dependence, severe cognitive impairment or an ongoing psychotic or bipolar disorder.

As this clinical trial is only investigating the promoter hypermethylation status and expression of certain genes in Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)-related gastric cancer, there are no specific eligibility criteria for patients. Any patient diagnosed with EBV-associated gastric cancer or non EBV-associated gastric cancer may be eligible to participate in this study.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who presented to the emergency room with sudden onset of severe pain in the right lower abdomen. The pain started about 6 hours ago and has been constant. She reports loss of appetite, nausea, and occasional vomiting. She denies any fever or chills. She has a history of irregular menstrual periods and is sexually active. She is not currently taking any medications, and she has no known allergies. On physical examination, the patient appears uncomfortable and has a slight fever. There is tenderness in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen, and there is rebound tenderness as well. Blood tests show an elevated white blood cell count. An ultrasound was performed, but it was equivocal and not diagnostic. The referring physician in the ER decides to continue diagnostic workup for suspected appendicitis by performing a CT scan. The patient will receive oral contrast material for approximately 180 minutes, and prior to the CT, the investigators intend to repeat the ultrasound. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 10-year-old boy was brought to the hospital by his parents because he was experiencing severe difficulty breathing for the past few hours. He was diagnosed with asthma when he was 5 years old and has since been taking inhalers and oral medications to control his symptoms. Despite these treatments, he still experiences occasional asthma attacks. At the hospital, his PRAM score was 9 and he did not respond to conventional treatments such as oxygen therapy, continuous nebulization of beta2 agonist, and oral corticosteroids. His blood gas analysis revealed hypercapnic acidosis with pCO2 > 45 mmHg and pH < 7.35. He was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with status asthmaticus. He is not known to have any other chronic conditions and has national health coverage. His parents have signed the informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial testing the use of High Flow Nasal Cannula as a potential treatment for status asthmaticus in children.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with no personal history of colorectal polyps or cancer or inflammatory bowel disease. He has no family history of familial adenomatous polyposis, hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (CRC), or CRC in more than 1 first-degree relative. He has not been adherent to standard CRC screening recommendations at the time of his index office visit. He is able to communicate with ease in English. He has not taken any antibiotics or antifolate medications (e.g., sulfasalazine, methotrexate) in the past 6 weeks. He has no other significant medical history or ongoing medical issues. He is motivated to participate in the study and willing to undergo fecal occult blood test 3 weeks after the screening office visit.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with tyrosinemia type I. He was born with jaundice and hepatosplenomegaly, and was found to have elevated levels of tyrosine and methionine in the blood. He was started on nitisinone and a low-tyrosine diet, which has helped to control his symptoms. He has been followed by one of the participating sites and his parents have given permission for him to participate in the study. The patient has been compliant with his treatment and has had regular check-ups with his healthcare provider.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) diagnosed 3 months ago. She underwent induction chemotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy and now requires a stem cell transplant. She is scheduled to undergo high-dose chemotherapy as a conditioning regimen for the transplant. She reports a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 5 years ago. She has no significant past medical history and no known allergies. Her performance status is good with a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80%. Her laboratory results show serum creatinine within normal limits and total bilirubin levels of 1.5mg/dl. She has no dental infections and no signs of systemic infections. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her informed consent.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with acute liver failure due to hepatitis B. He was unconscious and intubated, and his condition was critical. His family was informed about the severity of the situation and the possible need for liver transplantation. However, they were hesitant to give consent for transplantation due to religious beliefs. The medical team was faced with ethical and legal dilemmas as they were unsure how to proceed with the treatment plan without informed consent from the patient or his family. This patient will be considered for inclusion in the NORIDES study to explore the barriers in the process of achieving informed consent from critically ill patients.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with colon cancer and requires radical resection of the colon. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. Her physical exam is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no evidence of dehydration. Her laboratory values are all within normal limits. She has consented to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

Patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath for the past 2 months. She has a history of smoking for 30 years and has been trying to quit for the past year. A chest X-ray showed a suspicious lesion in her left lung and a CT scan confirmed a mass in the upper lobe of her lung, measuring 3 cm. She was referred to a thoracic surgeon for biopsy and further management. Pathology confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the lung. Her cancer is staged as T2aN0M0. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical comorbidities.

67-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and a left bundle branch block who underwent successful cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT-D) implantation. The patient is currently on optimal medical therapy with a stable functional class of heart failure (NYHA II). The patient is able to undergo a cardiac magnetic resonance examination, and the device is equipped with the SyncAV® programming software. The PQ interval before implantation was ≤ 250 ms. The patient does not have high-grade AV block, any contraindication concerning a safe CMR performance, terminal heart failure (NYHA IV) or cardiac decompensation. The patient is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 1 year and is not a woman with child-bearing potential or pregnant. The patient does not have a history of drug abuse.

The patient is a 57-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer with symptomatic ascites. He has been receiving chemotherapy for 6 months with minimal improvement in the ascites. He reports feeling bloated and short of breath. On examination, he has a distended abdomen with fluid wave and dullness to percussion. His blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. He is admitted to the medical oncology service for symptomatic relief of his ascites through abdominal paracentesis. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial comparing the rates of hypotension in patients with malignancy-related ascites undergoing abdominal paracentesis with and without prophylactic intravenous albumin infusion. He agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes for the past 2 years. She is overweight with a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are also managed by medications. She is currently on a strict diet and exercises regularly to control her blood glucose levels. She has not taken any medications to control her blood glucose levels in the past 2 months. Her most recent HbA1c level was 8.5% and her fasting blood glucose level was 9.0 mmol/l. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the nature, significance, potential benefits, inconvenience, and risks associated with the study. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has not had any major surgeries in the past year. She is not pregnant or in lactation. The patient is currently taking antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications, but not oral hypoglycemic agents or insulin. Her liver and kidney function tests are within the normal range. Her cardiovascular and cerebrovascular functions are good, and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medications.

The patient is a 25-year-old right-handed woman who works as a data analyst. She has no history of wrist or hand injuries and no current medical conditions. She exercises regularly and is in good physical shape. She has never participated in a clinical trial before. While she speaks German fluently, she does not have any language barriers to understand instructions. She is not currently taking any medications or participating in any other medical device or medicinal product study. She is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the advancement of medical research and to learn more about her own wrist joint movements. She is able and willing to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a US resident who is 18 years or older and able to provide electronic informed consent. They have a personal smartphone and are fluent in English. The patient is interested in contributing to critical research for COVID-19 and is willing to share their health data via a mobile application. They are looking for ways to help reduce the spread of the disease and are open to participating in current and future studies for diagnostics, treatments, and vaccines related to COVID-19. The patient is not currently experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19, but is interested in proactively contributing to research efforts to help mitigate the impact of the pandemic.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male with a BMI of 28. He has no history of chronic disease, medications or allergies. He has normal hemoglobin, MCV and reticulocyte values, and his transferrin saturation (TSAT) is greater than or equal to 20% with a total iron binding capacity (TIBC) of at least 250 ug/dL. His serum ferritin level is within the normal range for males (23-336 ng/mL). He has not taken any iron supplements for the past 14 days and has not received IV iron within the past 6 months. He has no concurrent or recurrent disease that could affect the action or disposition of the investigational products utilized in this study. He has no acute illness within the past 14 days and is not currently taking any medication except for occasional acetaminophen or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. He has no known intolerance or hypersensitivity to iron-containing products and has not participated in an investigational drug study within the past 30 days. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and restrictions and has no medical conditions that would preclude participation in the study.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer two years ago. He has undergone standard therapy including chemotherapy and hormone therapy, but his cancer has progressed. His most recent scan showed metastases to his liver, lungs, and bones. He experiences significant pain and fatigue and has lost weight. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new treatment. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not a regular or recreational user of any illicit drugs. He is otherwise in good health with no significant medical history. He has not participated in any clinical trials within the past four weeks and has not had chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the past four weeks. He is negative for HIV and has no history of Hepatitis B or C. He is interested in participating in the trial to try a new treatment that may help him manage his symptoms and potentially improve his cancer prognosis.

A 52-year-old male smoker is interested in participating in a clinical trial for early detection of COPD. He has a history of smoking for 30 years, with an average of one pack per day. He works as a construction worker and has frequent exposure to dust and other pollutants. He has noticed occasional shortness of breath and coughing but has not sought medical attention. He has no known respiratory diseases other than COPD. He takes no regular medications and has no allergies. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

A 60 year old male smoker was diagnosed with locally advanced squamous cell lung cancer, confirmed by CT scan. He has never received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy before. He is generally in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. His hemoglobin level is 11.5 mg/dL, platelet count is 140,000/μL, and absolute neutrophil count is 3000/μL. His serum creatinine level is 1.1 times the upper normal limit, bilirubin level is within normal limits, and liver function tests are normal. His FEV1 is 1.6 L and CB6 is within normal limits. He has signed the informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer after experiencing breast pain and noticing a lump in her breast during a self-examination. A mammogram and biopsy confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is eligible for breast-conserving surgery followed by radiation therapy. She has no contraindications for contrast-enhanced MRI examination. She has dense breasts, and the extent of the breast cancer is not yet determined. She will be assigned to one of the three treatment groups and undergo diagnostic imaging to determine the size and location of the cancer before surgery.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2 and is not taking any regular medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical research. She does not have diabetes or any other chronic conditions. Her blood pressure is within normal limits at 120/80 mmHg. She reports no history of respiratory, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic, hematological, lymphatic, neurological, cardiovascular, psychiatric, musculoskeletal, genitourinary, immunological, metabolic and dermatological or connective tissue disease. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of heart failure and left bundle branch block. He has been on cardiac resynchronization therapy for the past 2 years with a biventricular pacing at 92%. He has been experiencing frequent episodes of ventricular ectopy, and his recent Holter monitor revealed a high burden of ventricular arrhythmias. He has been referred for a catheter ablation procedure to treat his ventricular arrhythmias. He is currently on optimal medical therapy for heart failure including beta blockers and ACE inhibitors. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the impact of catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias on his biventricular pacing.

Maria is a 40 year old woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain for several months. She has a history of fibroids and has been advised by her gynecologist to undergo laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy for the removal of her uterus. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal otherwise. She weighs 60 kg and is 5'6" tall. She has agreed to participate in this study and has been randomized to receive the QL block before her surgery. She understands the requirements of the study and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of cardiomyopathy. He was diagnosed with cardiomyopathy 5 years ago and has been on treatment since then. Despite treatment, he continues to experience symptoms such as shortness of breath and fatigue. There is no clear etiology for his cardiomyopathy, but his father was also diagnosed with cardiomyopathy at a similar age. The patient is interested in participating in a genetic study to better understand the genetic basis for his condition and potentially help identify any genetic mutations that may be contributing to his cardiomyopathy. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent. The patient is not currently pregnant and is not participating in any other active treatment study.

A 9-year-old girl was referred to the clinic for evaluation of her congenital upper limb deficiency. She was born without her left arm below the elbow. She has been using a passive prosthesis since the age of 3, which has limited functionality. She is an active child who enjoys playing sports and outdoor activities. Her parents have concerns about her ability to participate in certain activities due to her prosthesis limitations. The 3D printed myoelectric prosthetic device has been recommended to her as a potential option to improve her daily activities and quality of life. The family speaks English fluently and is interested in participating

This is a 62-year-old male with a medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral vascular disease. He is scheduled for an elective vascular surgery which requires a groin incision due to significant peripheral artery disease. He has a BMI of 35 and is a former smoker. He is currently not on any immunosuppressive medications and does not require insulin for diabetes mellitus. However, he has a history of previous abdominal surgery and is hospitalized for 2 days before surgery due to preoperative evaluation. He is capable of providing informed consent and is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule.

A 46 year old woman with no known history of coronary artery disease but with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity. The patient presents with chest pain and is diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome. The patient undergoes coronary angiography within 24 hours of onset of symptoms which shows no obstructive coronary atherosclerosis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with follow-up requirements. The patient has not undergone previous revascularization and does not have serious concurrent disease with a life expectancy of less than one year. The patient provides written informed consent and is not pregnant or breastfeeding, nor intends to become pregnant during the study. The patient does not have a known allergy to contrast agent that cannot be adequately pre-medicated.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with aggressive B-cell lymphoma after presenting with fever, night sweats, and weight loss. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. His performance status is 1 on the ECOG scale and he has an age-adjusted IPI score of 2. He has no history of other malignancies, except for a basal cell carcinoma on his nose that was successfully treated with surgery three years ago. He has not undergone any prior treatment for his lymphoma, but he did receive one cycle of steroids to improve his symptoms before initiating the trial. He has signed informed consent to participate in the study.

45 yo female with a BMI of 38 kg/m2 presents with complaints of shortness of breath, wheezing and coughing for the past 6 months. She reports using her albuterol inhaler more frequently than before. She has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, obstructive sleep apnea treated with CPAP, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. She has tried multiple diets and exercise programs without significant weight loss. She is a non-smoker and has never undergone bariatric surgery or vagotomy. She is compliant with her medical visits and able to provide informed consent. She has no history of significant cardiac disease or valvulopathy.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes five years ago. She is currently managing her diabetes with oral medications and diet modifications. She is looking for ways to further improve her blood sugar control and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She works as a librarian and enjoys reading and gardening in her free time. She does not have any significant medical history, does not smoke or drink alcohol, and has no known allergies. She is interested in learning more about diabetes-specific nutritional formulas and is willing to try new products to help manage her diabetes.

A 45-year-old right-handed man presents with Dupuytren's disease causing a fixed flexion contracture of his left ring finger. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication. The patient has signed the agreement form and is affiliated with the national health system. The patient is eligible for the open palm technique of surgical treatment. The patient does not have any allergies to the components of the dressings used in the study. He is not diabetic and does not require insulin. He is not undergoing any anti-cancer treatment and is not pregnant. The patient is willing to attend follow-up visits for the study.

A set of twin preterm infants, one weighing 1600 grams and the other weighing 1200 grams, born at 30 weeks gestational age and admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit. Both infants received enteral feeding within the first 21 days of life. The larger twin was diagnosed with a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) which was managed with medical therapy. The smaller twin was diagnosed as asymmetrical small-for-gestational age (SGA). Both infants meet the eligibility criteria for the Nutritional Study in Preterm Infants, which evaluates the use of a preterm infant formula containing ingredients similar to those found in breastmilk. The twins' mother has consented to their participation in the study. Past Medical History: - Mother's pregnancy was complicated by preterm labor and premature rupture of membranes.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-CSH) for hematological pathology. He has been diagnosed with inaugural chronic graft versus host disease (cGVHD) that requires systemic treatment. The patient weighs 70 kg and has received conditioning treatments for the transplantation. The patient has not received any previous treatments for cGVHD and is not suffering from exclusive pulmonary cGVHD. The onset of cGVHD occurred after the 100th day post-transplantation and is not occurring after a donor lymphocyte injection (DLI). The patient does not have overlaps syndrome aGVHD-cGVHD or late aGVHD. The patient has no relapse or progressive disease and has controlled infections. The patient has not undergone a second allograft and has leukopenia levels ≥0.5G / l at screening. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder who is currently experiencing a Major Depressive Episode. She has been treated with lamotrigine (Lamictal) for at least 4 weeks at a dose of 100 mg per day, but has not responded adequately to the treatment as her 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) rating is still above 15. She is not currently taking any other antidepressants or mood stabilizers. She has a history of substance use disorder but has been clean for 8 months prior to the start of the study. She has no known allergies or intolerances to lamotrigine or memantine. She is not pregnant and is using adequate contraception. She has no significant medical illnesses or comorbid psychotic disorders. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has given informed consent as approved by the local IRB.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of spinal cord injury resulting in a neurogenic bladder. He is currently practicing clean intermittent catheterization on a daily basis as part of his regular care. He has been experiencing occasional urinary tract infections and is concerned about the long-term effects of his bladder condition on his renal health. The patient is seeking a more convenient and efficient way to monitor his bladder pressure and capacity, and is interested in participating in this study to test the novel pressure monitoring device in a home setting.

Pt is a 52yo M with a history of smoking for 30 years presenting with cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath for 2 weeks. CT scan of the chest shows a 5 cm left lung mass with hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy of the mass confirms non-small cell lung cancer, stage IIIA (T1-3, N2). The patient has no prior history of lung cancer or chemotherapy. His performance status is 90%, and he has no significant comorbidities. His white blood cell count is 5,000/mm^3, platelet count is normal, hemoglobin is 12.5 g/dL, and creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min. His bilirubin, serum glutamate oxaloacetate transaminase (SGOT), and serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (SGPT) levels are all within the normal range. The patient has no hearing loss, no symptomatic peripheral neuropathy, and no peptic ulcer disease under active treatment. He has no other medical illnesses that are not controllable by appropriate medical therapy. The patient has no other malignancy within the past 5 years except for a basal cell skin cancer that was adequately treated. He is not pregnant or nursing, and the pregnancy test is negative. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during the trial.

This is a 53 year old female who underwent gastric bypass surgery to address her morbid obesity 5 years ago. Since the surgery, she has been experiencing episodes of hypoglycemia, with a blood sugar level of less than 70 mg/dL, which can be asymptomatic and lead to complications. These episodes have been occurring more frequently, despite dietary modifications and changes in medication. She has been experiencing symptoms of neuroglycopenia such as dizziness, confusion, sweating, and fatigue. Her past medical history is significant for obesity, hypertension, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. She has no history of diabetes, myocardial infarction, or bleeding disorders. She is currently taking medication for hypertension and acid reflux, and has not had any major surgical operations within the last 30 days. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use any illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the use of a continuous glucose monitor can help reduce the number and severity of her low blood sugar episodes.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer that was previously treated with Bacillus-Calmette-Guerin (BCG) therapy. Despite receiving an adequate course of BCG therapy, the patient's cancer has persisted and is now considered unresponsive to BCG. The patient has been diagnosed with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without high-grade Ta or T1 papillary disease. The patient is not a candidate for radical cystectomy and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has adequate organ function and has not received systemic anti-cancer therapy in the past 4 weeks. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive intravesical (IVE) administration of CG0070, an investigational agent for the treatment of NMIBC that has failed BCG therapy.

25 yo F diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes at age 15. Currently on a continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) via an insulin pump with a stable insulin regimen of 0.8u/kg per day for the past year. Her most recent HbA1c is 8.2%. She has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She has no history of pancreatitis, medullary thyroid carcinoma, or liver disease. She has a normal complete blood count with no anemia. She has not donated blood in the past 8 weeks. She is not currently taking any diabetes medications other than insulin. She is not pregnant or lactating/breastfeeding. She is willing to use two methods of contraception during the entire study and for an additional 3 months after the end of dosing with the investigational product. She is able to provide written informed consent approved by an Institutional Review Board (IRB). She is interested in participating in this pilot study for individuals with Type 1 Diabetes who are willing to add a GRA (Glucagon Receptor Antagonist) to their current Diabetes treatment regimen. She understands that there will be 10 study visits over the course of approximately 8 weeks, with 4 weeks of once weekly, subcutaneous GRA (REMD-477) injection. She is willing to undergo testing which includes 2 MRI scans, 2 glucose challenges, and 2 insulin withdrawal challenges along with physical assessments and vitals.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese woman who has recently been diagnosed with epilepsy and requires antiepileptic drug treatment. She has no history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, diabetes mellitus, or any other significant systemic diseases. She is not currently taking any hormone replacement or glucocorticoids, and has not taken oral contraceptive pills in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant and has not undergone oophorectomy. She is willing and able to take her medication reliably.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy Japanese male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23. He has no history of any medical condition affecting drug absorption and is not taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs. He has 4 biological grandparents who were born in Japan, making him eligible for the Japanese cohort. He does not have a prolonged QTc-interval or QRS interval. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential. He is willing and able to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 90 days after the last dose of palbociclib in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been on hemodialysis for three years due to end-stage renal disease. He has a history of gout attacks for the past five years and has been taking allopurinol for the last year. Despite taking allopurinol regularly, he has still been experiencing gout attacks. He has no other significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has a family history of gout, with his father experiencing similar symptoms. He does not smoke cigarettes or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally, but not excessively. His physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable except for elevated serum uric acid levels. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to determine if changing the timing of his allopurinol administration will help to prevent further gout attacks.

59F with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and obesity presents to the emergency department with complaints of headache and blurry vision. Her blood pressure is noted to be 160/95 mmHg during the visit. She reports a history of non-adherence to her blood pressure medications due to side effects, such as dizziness and fatigue. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or abdominal pain. She has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is notable for hypertension in her mother and sister. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better manage her blood pressure and improve her self-care management.

55-year-old current smoker with a history of COPD and hyperinflation, with a post-bronchodilator FEV1 of 60% predicted and a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.65. The patient has a smoking history of 20 pack-years and has experienced one COPD exacerbation in the past year, which required treatment with antibiotics and systemic steroids. The patient has no significant cardiovascular abnormalities and no history of atrial fibrillation or pacemaker, bypass or stent. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the study.

A 56-year-old Chinese man with advanced melanoma complains of a new mole on his left arm that has been growing rapidly for the past 2 months. The mole is now about 2 cm in diameter and is unevenly colored. He also has a 3 cm swollen lymph node in his right armpit. He has no history of melanoma or other skin cancers. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has never smoked, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no allergies to any medications. He is married and has 2 children. He works as a salesperson and travels frequently. He is generally active and walks for at least 30 minutes every day. His ECOG performance status is 1. His blood tests show the following results: Hemoglobin 120 g/L, Neutrophils 3.5×10^9/L, Platelets 150×10^9/L, Total bilirubin 1.1×ULN, ALT 1.2×ULN, AST 1.3×ULN, Creatinine 0.9 ULN, LVEF 55%, QTcF male 430 ms.

This study does not require a specific patient description as it is recruiting patients who are undergoing routine liver MRI at the study site. The inclusion criteria specify that patients undergoing routine liver MRI with one of the four clinical scanners at the site are eligible for the study. The exclusion criteria are limited to patients who are not undergoing routine liver MRI. Therefore, any patient meeting the inclusion criteria can be considered for participation in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been referred to undergo a cardiac MRI scan to evaluate the extent of his ischemic heart disease. He has provided informed consent to participate in this study which aims to evaluate the efficacy of a high-fidelity, MRI-conditional 12-lead ECG monitoring system developed by MiRTLE Medical. The patient is eligible for the Ontario Health Insurance Plan. He does not have any contraindications for CMR imaging and is not hemodynamically unstable. He does not have a permanent pacemaker/ICD or aneurysm clip/carotid artery vascular clamp. The patient does not suffer from claustrophobia.

Pt is a 50yo F with a confirmed diagnosis of endometrial cancer through biopsy. The patient has no contraindications to surgery and is scheduled for a hysterectomy by laparoscopy, laparotomy, or robotic surgery. The patient has a preoperative MRI within 30 days of surgery at MD Anderson Cancer Center, which shows <50% myometrial invasion and disease confined to either anterior or posterior wall of the uterus. The patient has no prior history of endometrial ablation and no exposure to metformin within 6 months of endometrial cancer diagnosis or at the time of diagnosis. The patient has no known allergies to proflavine or acriflavine and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient understands and is willing to sign a written Informed Consent Document (ICD).

This is a 65-year-old female with a history of essential tremor. She has been experiencing tremors in both her hands for the past 5 years, which have significantly impacted her ability to perform daily activities. She has tried various medications and therapies, but has not seen much improvement. She has been referred for MRgFUS tremor therapy, and has agreed to participate in this clinical trial. She is able to understand and give informed consent for the study. She has no contraindications for MRI, and has no intracranial clips, metal implants, or external metallic devices/objects/clips within 10 mm of her head. She is not pregnant or potentially pregnant, and a pregnancy test (urine test) will be done for her at the time of check-in at Tisch. She is not considered a vulnerable population and meets all eligibility criteria for this study.

A 62-year-old male presents with a history of right shoulder pain for the past 6 months. The pain has been gradually worsening and is now affecting his daily activities. He reports no history of trauma or injury to the shoulder. The patient has tried conservative treatments including rest, physical therapy, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs with no relief. Physical examination reveals limited range of motion in the right shoulder with pain on passive and active range of motion. There is no evidence of rotator cuff tear or instability. The patient is not taking any prescription pain medication for conditions unrelated to the shoulder. The patient has no known allergy to hyaluronate preparations. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his osteoarthritis of the shoulder.

32 yo F with a history of chronic upper abdominal pain and bloating for the last 6 months. Patient has tried various over-the-counter antacids and dietary changes with no significant improvement. She reports no history of peptic ulcer or gastroesophageal reflux disease. She has no gastrointestinal surgery or history of gastrointestinal bleeding, mechanical obstruction, or perforation. She has no history of gastrointestinal cancer, pancreatic or biliary disease, inflammatory bowel disease, acute gastritis, or Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. She does not have irritable bowel syndrome or any other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant or lactating. Her liver function tests and renal function tests are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of combination therapy of Motireb 5/100 mg in functional dyspepsia patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She is 5'6" and weighs 250 pounds with a BMI of 40. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol. She does not drink alcohol or smoke. She reports feeling tired and sluggish often and has noticed some abdominal discomfort. She has been diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and has been recommended for a liver biopsy by her healthcare provider. She has no history of chronic hepatitis B or C or any other chronic liver disease. She is currently taking medication for her blood pressure and cholesterol. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo imaging procedures. She is not claustrophobic and has no known allergies to FDG dye. However, she is concerned about lying still for one hour during the FDG-PET scan due to discomfort from her abdominal pain.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fever for the past 4 days. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but otherwise has been generally healthy. Upon admission, she tested positive for COVID-19 and a chest CT scan was ordered. The CT scan revealed abnormalities in her lungs consistent with pneumonia. She has agreed to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the usefulness of chest ultrasound in the management of COVID-19 patients with respiratory signs. She is conscious and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 35-year-old female patient with Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia was referred for participation in a clinical trial. The patient has a family history of high cholesterol and has been on lipid-lowering medication for the past 6 months. She is currently taking a combination of statins and ezetimibe, which has helped to reduce her LDL-C levels. The patient is non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her weight is 65 kg and she has been maintaining a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and has no history of heart problems, renal disease, liver disease or malignancy. Her lipid values meet the pre-specified criteria for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge and improve her own health outcomes.

A 9-year-old girl with a history of peanut allergy presents with symptoms of hives, itching, and facial swelling after accidentally ingesting peanut butter. She has had previous episodes of anaphylaxis, including difficulty breathing and wheezing. Her serum SPT value was found to be 5 mm greater than control, and psIgE was 1.2 kUa/L. She is currently avoiding all peanut-containing products and carries an epinephrine autoinjector with her at all times. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially desensitize her to peanuts and reduce her risk of anaphylaxis in the future. She has no other medical conditions and is currently taking no medications. Her parents provide written informed consent for her participation in the study.

A 58 year old male with a history of hypertension and Type 2 diabetes visited the clinic with complaints of fatigue, weakness and shortness of breath. Further investigations led to a diagnosis of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Stage 4, with a serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL. The patient was also found to have anemia with a hemoglobin (Hgb) level of 9.8 g/dL and a transferrin saturation (TSAT) level of 22%. The patient has never received a red blood cell transfusion, and has not received any androgen therapy or erythropoiesis stimulating agent (ESA) treatment in the past. The patient's BMI is 32, and liver function tests and cardiac function tests were normal. The patient's blood pressure is controlled on medication, and there is no history of heart failure, myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndrome, or stroke. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of AKB-6548 in pre-dialysis subjects with anemia.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with depression and anxiety disorder. She has been receiving treatment from a mental health service for the past year. Recently, she has been feeling lethargic and unmotivated to engage in physical activities, spending most of her time sitting or lying down. She has expressed an interest in participating in a study aimed at reducing sedentary behavior. She is fluent in English and able to give informed consent. She is motivated to decrease her sedentary behavior and willing to engage in the study. She is currently not taking any medication that may interfere with her physical activity levels. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

38F with history of endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain, scheduled for a laparoscopic procedure for diagnostic and possible therapeutic intervention. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She does not have any history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, and has no contraindications to general anesthesia. She has been fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent to participate. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

A 67-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) has been undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) for the past six months. She has experienced a decline in muscle mass, strength, and function, leading to frailty and a reduced quality of life. The patient has no other active or uncontrolled diseases and is not currently engaging in moderate-intensity exercise. She has a BMI of 27 and a Kt/V of 1.2. The patient is willing and able to perform exercise safely and is within the peak VO2 range of 10 to 20 ml/kg/min, equivalent to moderate functional impairment in patients with heart failure. She does not have temporary vascular access, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, active vasculitis, active autoimmune disease, malignancy, severe obesity (BMI > 35), alcoholism or other recreational drug use, unstable cardiac disease, peripheral vascular disease, or lung, liver, or intestinal disease. The patient has not received anabolic, catabolic, or cytotoxic medications in the past 3 months and has not been excessively exposed to radiation.

A 60-year-old male patient presents with newly diagnosed non-metastatic prostate cancer. He has a Gleason score of 7 and a PSA level of 10 ng/mL. He has not received any previous cancer treatment or ADT. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He is physically active and reports no cognitive problems. He has no history of dementia or other neuropsychiatric diseases. The patient is willing to undergo a 7 Tesla MRI scan and complete brief cognitive testing on an iPad. He has no contraindications for MRI, including no history of metal in his eyes or removed from his body, no cardiac pacemaker, no intrauterine device, and no uncontrollable motion disorder. The calculated creatinine clearance is above 45 ml/min. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers learn more about the effects of ADT on cognitive function in prostate cancer patients.

A 49-year-old female patient presents with symptoms of COVID-19, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection via a respiratory tract sample RT-PCR assay. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril for management. She has no known allergies or contraindications to the medications being used in the trial. She has not received any other medications for COVID-19 treatment. Her liver function tests are normal, and she has no history of liver disease. She has a BMI of 29 and is generally in good health. She is not pregnant or nursing, and has no history of seizure disorder or long QT syndrome. She weighs 68kg and has a GFR of 70 ml/min. She is a candidate to receive Hydroxy Chloroquine according to the MOHP protocol.

A 45-year-old male patient presents with a history of HIV infection for the past 10 years. He has been treated with various antiretroviral regimens but has experienced virologic failure on at least two of them. His most recent HIV RNA test showed a count of 25,000 copies/mL. He has a good past medical history with no other medical conditions. His laboratory parameters are within normal limits, with a platelet count of 250,000/uL, hemoglobin level of 12 gm/dL, and absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/uL. His SGOT/SGPT levels are within 2xULN. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressants or cytotoxic agents. He has no history of seizure disorder or any other psychiatric illness requiring ongoing intervention. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of PEG-Intron in heavily treatment-experienced HIV-infected patients.

A 25-year-old woman presents with severe menstrual cramps and abdominal pain during her last 3 menstrual cycles. She reports experiencing nausea, fatigue, and headaches around the time of her period. She rates her pain as greater than 35mm on a 100 mm visual analogue scale. The patient has not been diagnosed with any organic causes of dysmenorrhea such as endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease. She has not had any recent surgery or trauma to her abdomen or pelvis. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past month and is willing to comply with the protocol required for the study. She is not taking any other NSAIDs or analgesics for pain relief.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who has been diagnosed with ischemic cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 35%. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. He smokes a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He complains of palpitations and shortness of breath on exertion. He has been on beta-blockers for a year but has not experienced significant symptom relief. His Holter monitor shows PVCs with a burden of over 10,000 per day. His liver function tests and thyroid function tests are normal. His EKG shows sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs. He has never had an ablation procedure or taken amiodarone for PVCs. He is willing and capable of giving informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a BMI of 40 kg/m² who has been struggling with obesity for many years. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, which have been difficult to manage with medication alone. After consulting with her healthcare provider, she has decided to undergo bariatric surgery. She has been classified as ASA 3 due to her medical history and current health status. She has provided written consent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo the necessary monitoring procedures during her surgery. She has no history of atrial fibrillation, cardiac arrhythmias, aortic aneurysm > 4.5 cm, or peripheral arterial occlusive disease. She is able to provide informed consent and does not have any cognitive or linguistic barriers.

Patient is a 70-year-old man with a history of osteoarthritis and scheduled for an orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia. He has a Mini-mental Status Exam (MMSE) score of 22, indicating no cognitive impairment. He speaks and understands English fluently. He has no history of delirium and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He is not taking any of the excluded medications and has no history of intolerance to ramelteon or riboflavin. He does not consume alcohol heavily and has no known liver or inflammatory conditions that would compromise his safety or data quality in the study.

A 28 year old healthy male presents himself for a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of ketoconazole or rifampicin on the pharmacokinetic characteristics and safety of LC15-0444. He is within the age range of 20 to 50 years and has a BMI of 23. He has a total body weight of 65 kg. His medical history is unremarkable and he has no history of any gastrointestinal disease or surgery. He has not donated blood or blood components within the past 60 days. He does not consume excessive alcohol or caffeine and he does not smoke excessively. He agrees to use an adequate means of contraception during the clinical trial. He is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 27-year-old Chinese woman with healthy skin who has been experiencing mild to moderate acne for the past few years. She has been prescribed Differin® gel 0,1% by her dermatologist to treat her acne. However, she has noticed some skin irritation, redness, and dryness on the treated area. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce skin irritation by using a moisturizing lotion in conjunction with the Differin® gel. She has not used any topical corticosteroids or retinoids for at least 2 weeks prior to the trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She gives her informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 21-year-old male diagnosed with severe hemophilia A. He has been previously treated with plasma-derived FVIII concentrates and has received prophylaxis or on-demand therapy with FVIII. He has had at least 150 documented exposure days (EDs). He has no detectable FVIII inhibitory antibodies and has never had a history of FVIII inhibitory antibodies. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol. He is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study, and he has not been diagnosed with any other inherited or acquired hemostatic defect. He is mentally competent to provide informed consent, and he has voluntarily provided signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old Kyrgyz woman of high altitude ethnicity, born, raised, and currently living at an altitude of 3,000 meters above sea level. She has a history of dyspnea on exertion and occasional chest pain. She has not been diagnosed with any pulmonary or cardiovascular condition and is not currently taking any medication. She has no history of smoking or excessive erythrocytosis. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical examination is unremarkable. She will undergo echocardiography to confirm high altitude pulmonary hypertension with a mean pulmonary artery pressure >30 mmHg. If confirmed, she will be invited to participate in the longitudinal cohort study for further evaluation of the course of her condition. If not confirmed, she will be considered as a healthy high altitude control subject.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of a venous leg ulcer on his left lower leg for the past 3 months. The ulcer is approximately 3 cm x 3 cm in size and is located just above his ankle. He has been receiving standard wound care treatment for the past month but has not seen any significant improvement. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control his blood pressure. He is a smoker and smokes approximately half a pack of cigarettes per day. He works as a construction worker and spends most of his day on his feet. He has noticed that the ulcer becomes more painful towards the end of the day. He has not noticed any signs of infection, such as fever or redness around the ulcer. His BMI is 28 and his blood pressure is currently well-controlled at 128/82.

45-year-old male admitted to the neurointensive care unit with refractory status epilepticus with continuous seizures despite treatment with first- and second-line antiepileptic medications. The patient has a history of temporal lobe epilepsy and has failed multiple antiepileptic medications. He has been placed on anesthetics/sedating agents (barbiturates or benzodiazepines) to control his seizures and has been on this treatment for over 24 hours. The patient has no significant past medical history and has a stable metabolic condition. The patient has no history of liver failure, coagulopathy, or fatty acid oxidation disorder. The patient is willing and able to tolerate enteral feeds. The patient has a total cholesterol of 250 mg/dL. The patient has provided consent to the study and does not have family refusal.

A 45-year-old female office worker who is overweight and has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 has expressed interest in participating in the clinical trial. She has never participated in regular exercise but is willing to start. She has no history of diabetes, hypothyroidism or any other medical conditions that could affect energy metabolism. She is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant within the next 18 months. She has normal resting systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and is not taking any medication that would affect her blood pressure or heart rate. She has no history of myocardial infarction or valvular disease. She has not experienced any significant weight loss over the past 12 months and does not have any orthopedic complications that would prevent her from participating in the exercise program. She is willing to provide informed consent and has obtained consent from her personal physician to participate in the study. She is excited to improve her health and start an exercise program with the guidance of the study's behavioral strategies.

The patient is a 27 year old woman who is currently 12 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a history of healthy pregnancies in her family and has not had any complications in the past. She is of Thai ethnicity and currently resides in Bangkok. She works as a nurse in a local hospital and is married to a businessman. She has completed her Bachelor's degree in nursing from a reputable university and has been working for the past 3 years. She does not smoke or drink and has a healthy lifestyle. She exercises regularly and follows a balanced diet. She has no significant medical history and has not been diagnosed with any genetic disorders or inherited conditions. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for prenatal carrier screening for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in order to ensure the health of her unborn child. She is willing to undergo the necessary tests and procedures for the trial and is committed to following the protocol. She is fluent in Thai and English and is willing to provide informed consent for the trial.

45-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis by a rheumatologist, currently experiencing moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness in her fingers, wrists, and knees. She has been prescribed methotrexate and prednisone by her rheumatologist to manage her symptoms, but she is still experiencing significant joint pain and stiffness on a daily basis. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of autoimmune inflammatory arthritis other than RA. She is willing to provide written consent for participation in the registry and to provide Personally Identifiable Information (PII). She is currently receiving an Eligible Medication (methotrexate) and has been for the past 6 months. She has not participated in any double-blind randomized clinical trial of an RA drug before and is not planning to do so during the course of the registry.

This is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset right-sided weakness, difficulty speaking and confusion. He was diagnosed with a right hemispheric stroke after undergoing MRI. He is a native French speaker, right-handed and has no history of neurological disease. He has no sensory disturbances such as blindness or deafness. The patient is able to read and comprehend the newsletter provided by the study. He has not experienced a stroke before, nor has he been diagnosed with dementia. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with end-stage renal disease due to polycystic kidney disease. He has been on hemodialysis for the past year and requires aminoglycoside antibiotics to treat a recurrent urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout. His medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and allopurinol. He reports no known allergies to any medications. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is affiliated with the French social security system.

45 year-old man with a history of HIV-1 infection, currently on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen consisting of two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) plus an integrase inhibitor (INI) for the past 2 years, with a plasma HIV-1 RNA level of less than 50 c/mL. He is in good health, with no history of opportunistic infections or significant comorbidities. He has recently been informed of a clinical trial investigating the efficacy, safety, and

25-year-old premenopausal female with a regular menstrual cycle and in good general health, without any clinically significant systemic disease. She has an intact gastrointestinal tract, uterus, and cervix, and vaginal and cervical anatomy that is conducive to easy genital tract sample collection. The patient is protected from pregnancy by using combined contraceptives (oral or patch) and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements, including swallowing tablets. She has not had a hysterectomy, is not currently pregnant or planning to get pregnant during the study period, not breastfeeding, and has not used Depo-Provera or other progestin-based contraceptives in the last 10 months. The patient has not been diagnosed with or treated for any STI in the last three months and has negative test results for Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhea, Chlamydia trachomatis, HIV, and Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). She does not have chronic or acute vulvar or vaginal symptoms, and does not have a known bleeding disorder that could lead to prolonged or continuous bleeding with biopsy. The patient has not used corticosteroids, antibiotics, anticoagulants, antifungals, or antivirals in the last two weeks or anticipated use during the study. She has a Grade 1 or lower laboratory abnormality, per the 2014 update of the Division of AIDS, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Disease (DAIDS) Table for Grading the Severity of Adverse Events, or clinically insignificant laboratory abnormality as determined by the clinician. The patient has no abnormal findings on laboratory or physical examination or a social or medical condition that would make participation in the study unsafe or would complicate interpretation of data. She has no history of gynecological procedures (including genital piercing) on the external genitalia, vagina, or cervix within the last 14 days.

A 56-year-old man has been experiencing severe back pain and fatigue for the past few months. He consulted his primary care physician who referred him to an oncologist. A bone marrow biopsy was performed and revealed the presence of multiple myeloma. The patient was informed about the REMNANT study and agreed to participate. He is in good overall health and meets all the inclusion criteria for part one of the study, including being eligible for high dose therapy with autologous stem cell support. He will receive standard of care first line treatment according to Norwegian national guidelines; bortezomib- lenalidomide - dexamethasone for 4 pre-transplant induction and 4 post-transplant consolidation cycles (all 21-d cycles). After induction, he will undergo tandem or single ASCT, depending on toxicity and response to first ASCT.   If he achieves MRD negative complete response 30-45 days post consolidation, he will move on to the randomized part of the study. He will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive second line treatment at MRD reappearance (arm A) or at progressive disease as defined by the IMWG criteria (arm B). He will receive the same 2.L treatment; carfilzomib - dexamethasone - daratumumab. (all 28-d cycles) Second line treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable AEs or patient withdrawal. In arm A, MRD Euroflow will be assessed every 4 months and he will start second line treatment at loss of MRD negative CR. In arm B, he will be followed up by standard criteria and start second line treatment at progressive disease.

A 58-year-old woman comes to your clinic after being diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has no significant past medical history, and her only medication is an occasional ibuprofen for headaches. She reports a recent 10-pound weight loss and fatigue, but denies any fever, night sweats, or other systemic symptoms. Physical examination reveals a palpable abdominal mass, but there is no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy elsewhere. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and the patient is scheduled to receive immunochemotherapy (R-CHOP). The patient is informed about the high risk of pneumococcal infections due to her upcoming treatment, and the importance of vaccination against this infection. She is offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of a prime-boost anti-pneumococcal vaccination strategy with Prevenar® and Pneumovax®. She is interested in participating and agrees to undergo the necessary evaluations and procedures.

A 62-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has been experiencing palpitations and irregular heartbeats for the past year. ECG and Holter telemetry confirm long-term persistent AF. The patient has been treated with antiarrhythmic drugs, but without success. The patient is scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and has consented to participate in a clinical trial involving surgical ablation of AF during CABG. The patient has no history of heart valve disease, prior cardiac surgery, or an active pacemaker. Transthoracic echocardiography shows an ejection fraction greater than 30%.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer 3 years ago. She underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. The treatment was successful and she remained in remission for 2 years. However, she recently started experiencing abdominal pain and bloating. A CT scan revealed the recurrence of her cancer. Her oncologist recommended that she undergo another round of chemotherapy with carboplatin. However, she had an allergic reaction to carboplatin during her previous treatment, which resulted in the discontinuation of the drug. She has no known allergies to any other medications. She is otherwise healthy, with a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80%. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her BMI is 25 with a BP of 120/80. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading and gardening in her free time. She has two adult children who live nearby and are supportive of her treatment. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help prevent another allergic reaction to carboplatin.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. She has undergone three lines of treatment, including bortezomib and lenalidomide-based regimens, but the disease has progressed. She is currently experiencing bone pain, fatigue, and anemia. Her medical history is notable for hypertension and osteoporosis. She takes lisinopril and calcium supplements. She has never had any allergic reactions to cellular products. Her ECOG score is 1, and her echocardiography shows normal diastolic function, LVEF of 60%, and no severe arrhythmia. She has no active pulmonary infections, normal pulmonary function, and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. Her absolute neutrophil count is 1.5 × 109 / L, and her platelet count is 80 × 109 / L. Her total serum bilirubin is 0.9mg / dl, serum ALT is 25 U/L, and serum creatinine is 1.2mg / dl. She has no contraindications for peripheral blood apheresis. She is expected to survive more than 12 weeks. She is postmenopausal, and her pregnancy test is negative.

The patient is a 28-year-old G2 P1 pregnant woman who is 14 weeks pregnant. She is employed as a marketing manager and lives in a suburban area with her husband. She reports a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise prior to pregnancy. She has no medical or obstetric history and no contraindications for physical activity during pregnancy. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is interested in participating in a study to promote physical activity during pregnancy and is willing to use social media and motivational interviewing to improve her physical activity levels during pregnancy.

An 80-year-old male patient has recently been diagnosed with non-small-cell lung cancer (stage IIIB) and is scheduled to undergo surgical resection. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. He takes amlodipine, atorvastatin, and acetaminophen for pain relief. He has never undergone surgery before and has no known allergies to medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild osteoarthritis in his knees. He is fully oriented and has no cognitive impairment. His laboratory workup shows no abnormalities. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 75 kg. He has no history of clinically significant disease and does not take any prescription or non-prescription medications, dietary or herbal supplements. He has not received any investigational drugs within the last 30 days. His blood pressure and electrocardiogram are within normal limits. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to provide informed consent. The participant is Japanese and has 4 biological Japanese grandparents who were born in Japan.

This clinical trial is looking for individuals who have participated in dietary trials in the past. The trial is specifically looking to include individuals who were randomly assigned to a treatment group for at least 3 weeks and were provided with suitable control, which means that they exchanged animal protein for plant protein. The trial is not restricted by age, sex or specific medical conditions, but individuals with non-human studies, nonrandomized treatment allocation, trials of less than 3 weeks, or lack of suitable control will be excluded. The purpose of this study is to determine whether replacing animal protein with plant protein has any effect on cardiometabolic risk factors, including blood lipids, glycemic control, blood pressure, body weight, uric acid, markers of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and kidney function and injury. The findings from this study will be used to inform dietary guidelines and health claims development to promote better health outcomes for individuals with or at risk of heart disease and diabetes.

The patient is a 62 year old man who has been a smoker for over 30 years, smoking up to 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He has been diagnosed with COPD and has experienced shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past 2 years. He has been using a SPIRIVA® HANDIHALER® inhaler 18mcg (TIOTROPIUM) for the past 6 months to manage his symptoms, but he still experiences occasional exacerbations. His post-albuterol FEV1 is 55% of predicted normal and his FEV1/FVC ratio is 0.63. He has never been diagnosed with asthma or any other respiratory disorder. He has no history of lung resection surgery, and his body mass index is 26/kg/m2. He is not currently using Long Term Oxygen Therapy and has not been diagnosed with cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further manage his COPD symptoms.

A 29-year-old male athlete presented to the clinic with complaints of persistent right shoulder pain for the past 6 months. He is an avid basketball player and had a history of multiple injuries, including a dislocated shoulder that required surgery. He is otherwise healthy and has no chronic medical illnesses. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is sexually active and uses condoms for contraception. He is physically fit and exercises regularly. He has no history of any surgery other than the shoulder surgery. He is interested in participating in the study to help other patients who may benefit from the findings of the study.

35-year-old HIV-positive male with a history of treatment with 3TC and FTC, currently receiving stable antiretroviral treatment for at least 3 months with an undetectable viral load (<50 cop/mL) for at least 1 year prior to inclusion. CD4 count is >350 cells/μL and the patient is naïve to integrase inhibitors. The patient is interested in simplification of their antiretroviral treatment regimen and is willing to change due to intolerance or interest in simplification. The patient has not had virological failure with ART regimen that included 3TC or FTC or previous virological failure did not have a population genotype with M184V/I or K65R/E/N mutations. The patient is able to understand and give written informed consent.

A 56-year-old female patient presented with a complaint of abdominal pain and bloating, accompanied by a change in bowel habits. She reported no history of colon cancer in her family. She had a medical history of high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes, which were all well-controlled with medications. She denied any allergies. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory tests showed elevated CEA and CA125 levels. Colonoscopy revealed a mass in the sigmoid colon, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of distant metastases. She received three cycles of first-line systemic therapy without any significant adverse events. Follow-up scans showed stable disease by RECIST 1.1. Her performance status was Karnofsky 80. She was willing to use an acceptable contraceptive method for the duration of the study and for 30 days following the last dose of study drug. She met all the inclusion criteria and had none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a 35-year-old female who presents with two sensitized teeth, which are not adjacent to each other and preferably in different quadrants, which demonstrate cervical erosion, abrasion and gingival recession. She experiences qualifying response to tactile stimuli as defined by a score of </= 20 grams, and qualifying response to air blast stimuli as defined by a score of >/= 1 on the Schiff Cold Air Sensitivity Scale. The patient has a good general health with no known allergies to products being tested, and has been using a non-desensitizing dentifrice for 2 weeks prior to entry into the study. She has a minimum of 10 natural teeth, excluding 3rd molars. The patient has not exhibited gross oral pathology, is not pregnant or lactating or intending to become pregnant, and does not require anesthetic during scaling. She does not have dental pathology that may cause pain similar to tooth sensitivity, nor large amounts of calculus. The patient has not had desensitizing treatment or tooth bleaching within 90 days of screening appointment, and does not have advanced periodontal disease or treatment for periodontal disease within the past twelve months. She does not have mobility greater than one in her sensitive teeth, nor extensive/defective restorations (including prosthetic crowns), suspected pulpitis, caries, cracked enamel, or used as abutments for removable partial dentures. The patient is not regularly using sedatives, anti-inflammatory drugs, or analgesic, and is not participating in any other clinical study or receipt of an investigational drug within 30 days of the screening visit at the start of the study.

A 42-year-old man with a known history of Von Hippel-Lindau disease and a family history of kidney tumors presents with a recent diagnosis of a 5 cm renal tumor. The patient has no history of chronic medical conditions and is currently asymptomatic. A computed tomography (CT) scan was performed to evaluate the tumor, which confirmed the diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma. The patient underwent screening tests including brain magnetic resonance imaging, blood and urine tests, 24-hour urine collection, ultrasound of the testicles, hearing test, and eye exam. The tests were all within normal range. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial examining the efficacy of 17AAG in treating kidney tumors caused by Von Hippel-Lindau disease. The patient will receive 17AAG infusions into a vein once a week for 3 weeks out of every 4, for 3 months. Repeat testing will be conducted after 3 months, including MRI scans to measure changes in tumor activity, blood flow, and number of blood vessels in the tumor since the pretreatment scans. Additional tests will be performed to evaluate the effect of 17AAG on the tumors. The patient is willing to undergo re

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who was diagnosed with acromegaly two years ago. She has been receiving treatment with a somatostatin analogue for the past 6 months, but her IGF-1 level remains elevated at 1.5 times the upper limit of the age-adjusted normal range. She has not received any other treatment for acromegaly in the past 12 weeks. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She takes only one medication for hypertension and has no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and has been on optimal medication therapy for the last 3 months. He was diagnosed with DCM six months ago and has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue with limited activity. He has been classified as NYHA Class III. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 35% and left ventricular end diastolic dimensions (LVEDd) is 57 millimeters. He has agreed to switch from ACE inhibitors to ARB for the treatment duration. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating, and he is taking adequate birth control as assessed by the investigator. He has no history of HBV, HCV or HIV infection, and his hemoglobin level is 11.5 g/dL. His renal function and hepatic function are normal. He has no history of acute myocarditis or coronary artery disease. The patient is not on immunosuppressive or immunomodulation therapy. He has no history of valvular heart disease, hypertrophic/restrictive cardiomyopathy, or constrictive pericarditis. The patient has not participated in any investigational study of a new drug, biologic, or device in the past six months. He does not have left ventricular noncompaction, an LVAD, or a history of heart transplant. The patient's DCM is not due to amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, connective tissue disease, peripartum cardiomyopathy, alcoholism, endocrine dysfunction, or illicit drug use.
