He has no prior history of cardiac resynchronization therapy or stroke. The patient is not currently experiencing severe systemic infection, hemodynamic instability, or active malignancy or tumor. He weighs 72 kg (158 lbs).

A 58-year-old African American man residing in Utah is invited to participate in a clinical trial aimed at increasing colorectal cancer (CRC) screening uptake among African American men. The patient must self-identify as non-Hispanic Black/African American, was born in the US, between the ages of 45-75, have a working telephone, speak and understand English, and have a phone with internet capabilities. The trial will take place in barbershops, which are culturally appropriate and trusted venues in African-American communities, and will target masculinity barriers to care and psychosocial factors related to CRC screening uptake. The patient will participate in focus groups, cognitive interviews, and an online survey to validate and test a culture-specific scale of masculinity barriers to care (Masculinity Barriers to Care Scale, MBCS). They will also be invited to participate in a pilot mixed methods intervention aimed at increasing CRC screening uptake among African American men. The primary outcomes for the pilot are recruitment, sample size estimation, preliminary efficacy, and acceptability. The patient must be willing to participate in the study and have a vested interest in increasing their CRC screening uptake.

A 45-year-old Asian woman is seeking treatment for a pterygium growth on her left eye. She has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has not had any previous ocular surgeries and does not have any ocular surface disease. Her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with correction. The pterygium measures approximately 3mm by 4mm and is causing her discomfort and irritation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) in assessing graft vascularization after primary pterygium excision with either LCAT or AMT. She does not have pterygia in both eyes and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Unfortunately, as this is an observational study, we cannot generate a patient description for this clinical trial as patients are not actively recruited. Instead, the study will collect data from patients who have already been admitted to participating hospitals with a diagnosis of first ever acute stroke (ICD-10: I61, I63 and I64).

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was diagnosed with COVID-19 by PCR testing. She has been experiencing symptoms for the past two weeks including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. The patient's chest HRCT showed a pneumonia pattern with a damage to 35% of the lung parenchyma. She has been taking over-the-counter medications for her fever and cough, but they have not been effective in relieving her symptoms. Her CRP blood level is 70 mg/ml and ferritin blood level is 700 μg/ml. The patient has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to blood transfusions. She has not required mechanical ventilation but is experiencing difficulty breathing and requires supplemental oxygen at home. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who recently had an abnormal prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test result during his annual physical exam. The patient has no known history of prostate cancer or any other significant medical conditions. The digital rectal exam was normal. The patient has agreed to undergo a diagnostic prostate biopsy to determine if he has prostate cancer. The patient has not taken any antibiotics in the past month and has no known allergies to fluoroquinolones. The patient has normal renal function.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He has not experienced any symptoms of cardiovascular disease, such as chest pain or shortness of breath. He recently attended a cardiovascular screening program provided by Life Line Screening and was found to have no significant carotid artery disease or atrial fibrillation. He completed a detailed questionnaire and provided information on his prior medical history, current medications, exercise habits, and family medical history. He was tested for abdominal aortic aneurysm and peripheral vascular disease, and the results were negative. He was provided with a written report and advised to consult his GP to discuss abnormal results. He has agreed to participate in a long-term follow-up study to determine the contemporary risk of stroke in a large population.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is planning to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy before surgical excision. She had a fine needle aspiration biopsy that confirmed metastasis to an axillary lymph node. Her imaging studies will be monitored to evaluate the response to the chemotherapy. She does not have any allergies to lidocaine or gadolinium, and she has not had any prior axillary radiation. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have any contraindications to MRI. She is scheduled for target axillary lymph node dissection, which will include the localized lymph node and sentinel lymph node. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and will have a Magseed placed into the biopsy proven lymph node either before or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. She will also undergo standard mammographic and sonographic imaging before and after chemotherapy, as well as a non-contrast enhanced breast MRI to evaluate and reduce the artifact in the axilla created by the Magseed. The efficacy of localization with the Magseed will be evaluated within a week of placement, and the lymph node containing the Magseed will be identified and excised during surgery.

A 56-year-old Caucasian woman was recently diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She noticed abdominal bloating and pelvic pain for the past month. She went to see her gynecologist, who performed a pelvic exam and ordered an ultrasound. The ultrasound revealed masses in her ovaries, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of ovarian cancer. She underwent a surgery to remove the tumors and started chemotherapy two weeks ago. Her CA125 tumor marker level was above normal threshold level at diagnosis. She is experiencing nausea and fatigue due to chemotherapy. She is married and has two children. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her past medical history is unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options. Her CA125 tumor marker level is still elevated.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a recently diagnosed invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother being diagnosed at age 50. The patient underwent biopsy and imaging studies that confirmed the presence of a 2.5 cm tumor in her left breast, with no evidence of metastases. She was offered surgery as the first line of treatment but refused. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or medication use. She has no known allergies. Her physical exam is unremarkable, with no palpable lymphadenopathy or signs of distant metastases. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her BMI is 24. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is randomized to receive standard Unit's protocol with aspirin.

A 56-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. She has no history of receiving chemotherapy before and has no option for surgery. She has a performance status of 2 and is able to care for herself but unable to perform any physically demanding work. The patient has confirmed colorectal adenocarcinoma with metastatic disease. She has at least one measurable lesion according to the RECIST criteria with a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient has not received any systemic treatment for advanced or metastatic disease, and she has not been previously treated with bevacizumab. She has finished adjuvant treatment at least 6 months before the study inclusion. There are no indications of CNS disease, peripheral vascular disease, or psychiatric disability that would impair her ability to grant informed consent or interfere with compliance of taking oral medication. The patient has no other neoplastic disease during the last five years, except cured basal cell carcinoma of the skin and cervical carcinoma in situ. She has a history of myocardial infarction over a year ago but is currently stable. The patient has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease or physical integrity of the upper gastrointestinal tract, and she is able to take oral medication. The patient has normal organ function, with no severe, uncontrolled intercurrent infections or other severe, uncontrolled concomitant diseases. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, and she has no history of unexpected serious adverse events to fluoropyrimidine treatments or known dihidropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency. The patient has not received any investigational drug or agent/procedure within 30 days of randomization.

This is a 32-year-old female who was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) four years ago after experiencing visual disturbances and weakness in her legs. She has previously been treated with disease-modifying therapies and has been stable without any relapses for the past six months. However, she has been experiencing frequent episodes of heat intolerance, which cause her to feel weak and dizzy, and affect her ability to perform daily activities such as reading, walking, and driving. She has also been diagnosed with INO (internuclear ophthalmoplegia), an ocular motor syndrome that affects her eye movements. Her condition has been evaluated using objective methods such as infrared oculography and VEPs (visual evoked potentials), which have confirmed the presence of axonal conduction changes in demyelinated pathways. The patient has a peak saccadic acceleration ratio (abducting eye/adducting eye) of greater than 2S.D. above the mean derived from a normal control group. The patient is otherwise in good health and has voluntarily signed the informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no known allergies to the study drug, ACTHAR, and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to use appropriate birth control methods during the study period. The patient has no history of drug or ethanol abuse within the past year and is able to understand the demands of the protocol.

A 58-year-old man presents with a history of heart failure and an ejection fraction of 35%. He has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for it for the past 10 years. He complains of shortness of breath on exertion and orthopnea. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or chronic kidney failure. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has never been diagnosed with permanent atrial fibrillation or infiltrative cardiomyopathy. He reports no history of lung disease. He is married and has two children. His current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol, and furosemide. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effects of CPAP on ventricular function modifications.

A 62-year-old woman diagnosed with heart failure classified as NYHA II is being considered for a clinical trial evaluating a sensor-controlled digital game (SCDG) to motivate self-management behaviors of weight monitoring and physical activity. She is able to walk independently without a cane or walker, and owns a smartphone. She understands English and has passed a mini-cognitive screen. She has no history of renal failure or end-stage illness. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her management of heart failure and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

A 35-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and a body weight of 60 kg is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is not currently taking any prescription medications but has used over-the-counter fexofenadine for seasonal allergies in the past. She is not pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after the last dose of study drug. She has no history of significant medical conditions or allergies to medications. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 28 days. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who underwent a lung transplant for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis two years ago. He was diagnosed with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) three months ago after experiencing a significant decline in his pulmonary function test (FEV1). He is currently receiving immunosuppressive treatment according to institutional standards. The patient has no active invasive bacterial, viral or fungal infection, is not on mechanical ventilation, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to cyclosporine A and has a serum creatinine value of 90 μmol/L. He has not received an investigational drug as part of a clinical trial in the past six months. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the use of aerosolized liposomal cyclosporine A in the treatment of chronic rejection in lung transplant recipients with BOS.

A 42-year-old woman with a history of intravenous drug use and no previous treatment for Hepatitis C presents with symptoms of fatigue and jaundice. She has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past 6 months. She is diagnosed with genotype 1 HCV infection and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new treatment. She agrees to use two forms of contraception during treatment and following the last dose of ribavirin. She has no history of HIV or Hepatitis B infection and has not received any previous interferon or ribavirin-based therapy or investigational anti-HCV agent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 42-year-old female who presented to the emergency department with a severe headache, nausea, and vomiting. A CT scan revealed an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and she underwent treatment with external ventricular drainage. She has no significant past medical history and is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to measure the neuroinflammatory response in patients with SAH and the effectiveness of medications in managing acute headache pain and preventing the development of persistent headaches.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has had knee pain for the past 4 months. He was diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the knee with KL radiological grade 3 according to ACR criteria. He has been taking paracetamol to relieve pain. His pain intensity in the target knee is ≥40 mm and <80 mm measured by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), and ≤ 20 mm in the contralateral knee. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. He has not undergone any previous surgery on his knee, including arthroscopy. He has no musculoskeletal conditions affecting the target knee that would impair proper evaluation. He has no joint inflammatory disease or microcrystalline arthropathies. He is willing to comply with study procedures and is able to provide informed consent. He has not received any previous treatments including hyaluronic acid, steroids, glucosamine sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, diacerein, NSAIDs, or any investigational drugs. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to SH or paracetamol.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and has undergone one round of adjuvant chemotherapy. She has no history of heart, liver, or kidney disease and her general health is good. Her BMI is 25 and her ECOG performance status is 1. Her bone marrow function, liver and kidney function are all normal. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the last four weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction. She has given her consent to participate in the study.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD by a pediatrician. The patient's mother reports that he has difficulty with focus and attention in school, and frequently forgets to turn in assignments. The patient has been prescribed oral methylphenidate (Ritalin) by his pediatrician for the last 6 months, but his mother reports that he frequently forgets to take his medication before school. The patient is currently attending school and is involved in extracurricular activities. His mother reports that she is interested in exploring alternative treatment options that may be easier to manage with his busy schedule. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions, and has not experienced any adverse effects from previous medication use. The patient's mother is willing to bring him to all study visits and comply with study protocol.

A 35-year-old Hispanic woman was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis three months ago. She presents with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. She has no significant past medical history and has never been on any medications for ulcerative colitis. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use recreational drugs. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not received any live virus vaccines in the past three months. She is willing and able to comply with the study visits and requirements. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore more treatment options for her ulcerative colitis.

A 45 year old farmer from a rural village in Guangdong, China came to the clinic for a routine checkup. He has never had a comprehensive eye examination before and has no known eye problems. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. He reports that his vision has been gradually worsening over the past few years, but he has not sought medical attention for it. He works long hours in the fields and spends a lot of time outdoors. He is concerned about his vision and is willing to participate in the educational intervention promoting acceptance of comprehensive eye examination in rural Guangdong.

A 49-year-old woman underwent bilateral lung transplantation at the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) six months ago due to severe pulmonary fibrosis. She has been on immunosuppressive medication ever since. Recently, she has noticed shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue, and dry cough. Her pulmonary function test (PFT) showed a decline in Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) to 70% and Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) to 65% of her best post-transplant baseline. A CT scan revealed pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis consistent with a diagnosis of restrictive chronic lung allograft dysfunction (RCLAD). She is not currently smoking and has no known allergies to medications. She has no current or expected use of any contraindicated therapies. She has normal renal and liver function. She is willing and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant who is brought in by his mother for routine vaccination. The infant is in good health and has no significant medical history. He is the first child of his parents and was born full-term by normal vaginal delivery. The infant is exclusively breastfed and is meeting all age-appropriate developmental milestones. The mother reports that there is no family history of immunodeficiency disorders or vaccine adverse reactions. The infant is not on any medications and has not received any other vaccines in the past 30 days. The mother has provided written informed consent for her child's participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 4-year-old male child who has been diagnosed with high caries risk at his last dental check-up. During the examination, a visible white spot lesion was detected on the buccal surface of his primary maxillary right central incisor with an ICDAS II score of 2. The child has no known systemic diseases and is generally healthy. The parental consent to participate in the study has been obtained. The child has no allergies to milk products. The selected tooth does not have a cavitated lesion or any enamel defects. The child will be randomly allocated to either the study group or the control group and will receive the assigned varnish treatment every two weeks for six weeks. The child will be followed up at 6 weeks, 18 weeks, and 30 weeks for Visio-tactile assessment and DIAGNOdent measurements to evaluate the effectiveness of the varnish in remineralizing the white spot lesion.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with chronic kidney disease undergoing regular hemodialysis treatment for the past 2 years. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes and has been on medication for both conditions for the past 5 years. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has not engaged in any regular exercise program for the past 6 months and his mobility is normal. He experiences occasional muscle cramps during hemodialysis sessions. He has not been diagnosed with any autoimmune diseases, cancer, infectious diseases or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. He has not had any cardiovascular or neurological events in the past. He is not pregnant, and he is not a lower limb amputee. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the exercise program.

The patient is a healthy male volunteer aged between 18 and 55 years old. He does not have any history of bleeding abnormalities or cardiovascular events. He is not allergic or hypersensitive to the active compounds or any of the excipients used in the study. The patient is willing and able to stay at the clinical site for approximately 8 nights over 9 days and to return to the clinic approximately 7 days after discharge. He is not taking any medications currently and has not taken any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in the past 14 days. He has no significant medical history and is a non-smoker.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of non-valvular atrial fibrillation. He was recently prescribed rivaroxaban to manage his condition. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is compliant with his medications and has not experienced any major bleeding or emergency surgeries in the past. He has not been diagnosed with any bleeding disorders or liver disease. He is a non-smoker and has a moderate alcohol intake of 2-3 drinks per week. He has no known drug allergies. The patient has been enrolled in his healthcare plan for more than 6 months and has a confirmed initiation date for rivaroxaban. He has not been prescribed any other oral anticoagulants during this time period.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who recently visited his primary care physician for a routine check-up. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. He is currently overweight with a BMI of 30 and consumes a diet low in fiber. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol regularly. His blood work revealed a fasting venous glycemia of 1.15 g/L, which is in the prediabetic range. He has never been diagnosed with diabetes and is not on any antidiabetic medication. He has no history of metabolic disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, or food allergies. He has not undergone any recent surgeries, is not under any dietary supplements that could affect the trial, and is not taking any medications that could significantly affect the parameters being followed in the study. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and has signed an informed consent form. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and agrees to be registered on the volunteers in biomedical research file.

25 yo F with T4 complete spinal cord injury due to motor vehicle accident, admitted to inpatient rehabilitation for comprehensive rehabilitation program. Patient has no documented history of osteoporosis or fractures. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent osteoporosis and willing to take oral fosamax. She has no contraindications to the study drug and is able to sit/stand upright for 30 minutes. She is willing to complete 3 visits over the course of 12 months and undergo DEXA scans every 6 months.

The patient is a 56 year old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of overactive bladder for several months. She feels a sudden and strong urge to urinate frequently, and sometimes experiences urinary incontinence. These symptoms have been interfering with her daily activities and causing her to feel embarrassed in public. She has tried several medications prescribed by her urologist, but they have not been effective in relieving her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of neurological disorders or urinary tract infections. She is interested in participating in this non-invasive clinical trial using electrical stimulation of the foot to treat her OAB symptoms. She is able to communicate in English and is willing to follow the protocol for home therapy. She has no implanted electrical stimulators and is not allergic to Cipro or Bactrim.

A 45-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with both HIV and Hepatitis C virus infections is being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial. The patient has not been treated for either infection before and currently meets the criteria for receiving highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). The patient has no known primary resistance mutations to NRTIs, Integrase inhibitors, or PIs. The patient has no history of advanced liver cirrhosis or any other chronic liver disease, including alcohol abuse or hemosiderosis. The patient is not currently on or planning to undergo any anti-HCV therapy during the study period. The patient has not had any acute or chronic hepatitis B or other hepatotropic virus infections within the last 6 months. The patient is able to sign written informed consent and is willing to undergo regular monitoring throughout the study period.

A 45 year old woman has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and social distancing guidelines, she is unable to attend in-person appointments and is feeling isolated and anxious. She has no history of regular physical exercise and is concerned about maintaining her physical health and nutritional state during this time. She is also experiencing emotional distress due to her recent diagnosis and the uncertainty of her treatment plan. She is interested in participating in a trial that would provide her with remote support and guidance on exercise, nutrition, and psychological wellbeing through virtual clinics. She is willing to give informed consent to participate in the trial.

Patient is a 55-year-old man who presents to the emergency department with a complaint of hematemesis within the past 12 hours. He has a history of alcohol abuse and hypertension, but otherwise is in good health. He denies any history of allergies or prior gastrectomy. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility for a clinical trial comparing erythromycin infusion versus gastric lavage prior to emergency endoscopy to improve the quality of examination in patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The study aims to determine whether erythromycin infusion is better than gastric lavage in this population. The endoscopic procedures will be recorded on Digital Video Disc (DVD), and the quality of examination of the upper gastrointestinal tract will be assessed by two endoscopists blinded to the cleansing strategy using scales designed by Frossard and Avgerinos. The secondary endpoints will be the need for a second-look endoscopy, the mean number of blood units transfused, the need for surgery or arteriography, and the mean duration of hospitalization. The patient will be randomly assigned to receive either erythromycin infusion or gastric lavage by nasogastric tube prior to emergency endoscopy.

The patient is a 30-year-old male military veteran who has been diagnosed with PTSD for the past 2 years. He has tried various treatments, including psychotherapy and medication, but continues to experience moderate to severe symptoms, including nightmares, flashbacks, insomnia, and anxiety. He has heard about the potential benefits of cannabis for PTSD and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore this treatment option. He is willing to abstain from marijuana use during the 2-week baseline assessment period and commit to smoking up to 1.8 grams of cannabis daily during the study. He is proficient in reading and writing in English and able to effectively communicate with site staff. He agrees to use only marijuana provided by the site staff, keep it securely stored, and not share or distribute it to anyone else. He is not currently abusing any illegal drugs and is willing to attend all study visits and complete evaluation instruments. He is not pregnant or nursing, and is practicing an effective means of birth control.

A 28-week pregnant woman delivered a baby boy weighing 980 grams at Sheba Medical Center. The baby was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to maternal hypertension. The mother received antenatal steroids before delivery. The baby was intubated and taken to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for respiratory support. The baby has no known cardiac or chromosomal anomalies. The mother had no significant medical or surgical history. She is HIV negative and has no allergies to any medication. She is currently in good health and is eager to participate in this clinical trial.

24-year-old female with a BMI of 21.5, no history of chronic medical conditions, and no prior supplementation with citrulline, glutamine, ornithine a-ketoglutarate or stimol® presents for the clinical trial. Currently, she is not taking any medication, including anabolic agents, and has not received artificial feeding in the past. She has no history of renal, cardiac, respiratory, or hepatic insufficiency, and no chronic inflammatory disease. Her fasting blood glucose is 5.2 mmol/L (93.6 mg/dL). She is not pregnant and is using oral contraceptive measures. She is affiliated with French health insurance and has provided informed consent to participate in this study. She has no history of participating in any other clinical trials within the past year.

A 45-year-old European male with a history of moderate to severe hypertension is seeking treatment options to lower his blood pressure. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications for hypertension. The patient has no known allergies and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is not planning on becoming pregnant or lactating during the trial period. The patient has not experienced any recent myocardial infarctions, unstable angina pectoris, percutaneous coronary intervention, severe heart failure, hypertensive encephalopathy, cerebrovascular accident (stroke) or transient ischemic attack. The patient has no clinically significant abnormal laboratory values at screening and has been ruled out as having secondary hypertension.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman with a long history of smoking, 40 pack years, and a diagnosis of COPD with chronic bronchitis. She reports a chronic productive cough with sputum production several days a week for the past 4 weeks. She has been using inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting bronchodilators for the past 6 months with minimal improvement in her symptoms. Spirometry revealed a forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) of 55% of the predicted and a FEV1/FVC ratio of 65%. She has not been treated with oral prednisone or oxygen therapy in the past 6 weeks. She is willing to participate in the study to assess the effectiveness and safety of the new drug, BIO-11006 Inhalation Solution, in inhibiting mucus secretion and reducing inflammation in her lungs.

A 10-year-old girl with a history of asthma since the age of 4 is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She experiences occasional wheezing and coughing, particularly during the allergy season. She takes an inhaled corticosteroid twice a day and a rescue inhaler as needed. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and have provided written consent. She has never smoked and is in good health with no other systemic or debilitating conditions.

A 26-year-old female who recently completed her graduate studies in business administration. She is in a steady relationship and uses oral contraceptives as her primary method of birth control. She is a non-smoker and doesn't use any drugs or supplements. She has a balanced diet and exercises regularly. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. She is interested in participating in this study as she believes it may help her understand the effects of oral contraceptives on her folate levels.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 5 years ago presents with medically refractory, disabling tremors in her left upper extremity. She has tried multiple medications for tremor suppression, including propranolol and primidone, but has not found any relief. She has no history of seizures or intracranial hemorrhage. She is not currently taking any medications that increase the risk of hemorrhage or coagulopathy. She has no implanted metallic devices or claustrophobia. She is willing and able to tolerate the required prolonged stationary supine position during treatment. She has not participated in another clinical trial in the last 30 days. She is able to provide informed consent and attend all study visits. Her Tremor Rating Scale score is 3 and her Clinical Global Impression-Severity score is 6, indicating significant impairment of normal daily functions. MRI imaging confirms the presence of a unilateral thermal lesion in the ventralis intermedius nucleus of the thalamus as the target tissue for MRgFUS treatment.

A 63-year-old woman was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) three months ago. She presented with a cough, weight loss, and shortness of breath. A CT scan showed a 5 cm mass in her right lung and multiple metastases in her brain. She underwent a biopsy, and the molecular profile of the primary tumor was obtained from a block of paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed tissue. The results showed an EGFR mutation. She started treatment with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) and has been responding well to treatment so far. Her Zubrod performance status is 1. Her most recent physical examination and lab results were performed yesterday and showed the following: A pleasant, cooperative woman with a BMI of 23.6 kg/m2, non-icteric, and alert. BP: 130/80 HR: 80/min RR: 20/min Hgb: 11.5 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 4200/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 30 U/L ALT: 25 U/L Alk P: 120 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl ESR: 40 mm/hr. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo collection of blood samples at baseline and every 12 weeks for up to 6 times.

The patient is a 24 year old pregnant female in her third trimester. She is of Ugandan descent and lives in a rural community. She has had a healthy pregnancy and has received adequate prenatal care. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has no known allergies. She is married and lives with her husband and two young children. She plans to deliver at a local health facility with the assistance of a traditional birth attendant. She has been informed of the study and has given her consent to participate. She is willing to follow the protocol for umbilical cord cleansing with a single application of 4% chlorhexidine if randomized to the intervention group.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma based on the SWOG criteria. He has symptomatic MM stage III according to Durie-Salmon staging system with multiple osteolytic lesions. He has already undergone one prior therapy but has progressive disease. His paraprotein levels in the serum are over 1g/dl. He is currently not experiencing any active systemic infection, and his vitals are stable. He weighs 80 kg and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. He has no history of clinically relevant cardiac disease, and his ECG shows no evidence of arrhythmia, 2nd degree or greater AV block or prolonged QTc interval. He has normal serum biochemical values, and his haematology values are within normal limits. He is not taking any experimental drugs, and he does not have any known hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol. He has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old male with a diagnosis of Fragile X Syndrome (FXS) presents for participation in a clinical trial investigating GABA physiology in FXS. He has a confirmed diagnosis of FXS with full mutation and aberrant FMR1 methylation. His medical history is significant for intellectual disability with an IQ score between 40 and 80 points. He has no history of active medical problems, sensory impairments, or severe psychiatric disorders. He does not use benzodiazepines and has no contraindications for PET or MRI. He is physically healthy and able to remain seated for more than 10 minutes. He is willing to travel to Stanford for the study. The patient understands the study's purpose and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a family history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). She has noticed a gradual decline in her vision over the past year and has been diagnosed with early stage AMD. She has been advised to take supplements containing lutein and zeaxanthin, but is interested in exploring other options for improving her vision. She is in good overall health, does not have glaucoma, and has not been taking any dietary supplements. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of an oil-based kale extract or fresh kale in improving her vision and increasing her macular pigment optical density (MPOD).

32-year-old female with a history of excessive daytime sleepiness for the past 5 years. She reports sleeping 10-12 hours per night and still feeling exhausted during the day. She has tried multiple medications including modafinil and methylphenidate without any improvement in her symptoms. She has no history of sleep apnea, restless leg syndrome, or narcolepsy. She has also never been diagnosed with any metabolic disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of primary hypersomnia. She has consented to undergo testing for GABA-related abnormalities and has been found to be eligible based on the in vitro assay. She has no contraindications for the use of flumazenil and has not taken any benzodiazepines in the past 6 months. She is willing to participate in the study and follow all the procedures.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Crohn's disease. He has been in sustained remission for over a year with a PCDAI score of 0. He has been following the Crohn's Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED) and has eliminated gluten and milk fat from his diet. His CRP and calprotectin levels are within normal range. He has not had any complications related to his disease and is not currently taking any immunomodulators or biologics. He is interested in participating in the Challenge study to determine if he can safely consume some of the products that were eliminated from his diet. He has a supportive family who is willing to comply with the study's requirements.

A 28-year-old female contact lens wearer presented with a history of dryness, burning sensation, and irritation while wearing lenses for more than 8 hours a day. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of any ocular diseases. She has been using the same brand of contact lenses and solution for the past year. She does not have any allergies to medications or any other substances. She works as a computer analyst and spends most of her day working on a computer. She does not smoke and exercises regularly. She is currently not pregnant or lactating.

A 50-year-old Chinese woman was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She has a family history of diabetes and leads a sedentary lifestyle due to her desk job. She reports difficulty managing her blood sugar levels despite taking medications as prescribed. She often feels overwhelmed and alone in her struggle with diabetes. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves peer support to help her better manage her diabetes. She resides in a stable place and provides her voluntary participation and consent to participate in the trial. She does not have any major psychiatric conditions or reduced life expectancy. She is not currently enrolling in any other research program. She hopes that peer support will help her gain better control of her diabetes and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman from Uruguay who has been a smoker for 20 years and quit smoking 3 years ago. She was diagnosed with COPD 2 years ago and has had one spirometry test confirming the diagnosis in the last 12 months. She regularly attends outpatient specialist consults for her COPD symptoms, which have been stable according to her medical records in the past 2 months. The patient reports experiencing early morning, daytime and nighttime symptoms related to her COPD. She has no other chronic respiratory diseases or sleep apnea syndrome. The patient is able to read and comprehend written instructions and is willing to complete the required questionnaires for the study. She has signed an informed consent document indicating her willingness to participate in the study.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with heart failure. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 10 years. He also has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 5 years ago. He has no known allergies and no family history of heart disease. He experiences shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion, but otherwise feels well. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 40%. He has not had any recent cardiac events or surgeries. His current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol, and furosemide. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg and his BMI is 29. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and walking for exercise.

A 28-year-old man fell off his bicycle while riding on a downhill trail. He landed on his outstretched hand and experienced immediate pain and swelling in his wrist. He presented to the emergency department within a few hours of the injury, where he received a physical exam and imaging studies. The computed tomography scans showed a proximal pole fracture of the scaphoid. The fracture was diagnosed within 5 days of the injury. He is fluent in English and is literate. He has no other fractures or injuries. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to analyze the clinical and radiological outcomes of patients with a proximal pole fracture of the scaphoid.

A 55-year-old man was referred to the hospital for heart valve replacement surgery due to severe aortic valve stenosis. He had palpitations, shortness of breath, and chest pain on exertion for the past 6 months. He is a retired engineer and has a history of hypertension for the past 10 years, which is well-controlled by medication. He is a non-smoker and doesn't have diabetes or any other significant medical history. His echocardiogram revealed aortic valve area of 0.8 cm², peak gradient of 75 mmHg, and mean gradient of 50 mmHg. His left ventricular ejection fraction was within normal limits. He was scheduled for heart valve replacement surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass. He was randomized to the experimental group and underwent remote ischemic preconditioning using a tourniquet prior to the surgery. He did not have any pre-existing renal dysfunction and did not have any peripheral vascular disease affecting the lower limbs.

60 year old man with a history of primary knee osteoarthritis and severe knee pain, which limits his daily activities. He has tried conservative treatment measures including physical therapy, oral medication for pain relief, and knee injections, but has found no significant improvement in his symptoms. He has a BMI of 26.5, and no other significant medical comorbidities. He is scheduled to undergo a cemented total knee arthroplasty with the Evolution medial-pivot knee system at the Orthopedic and Traumatology Clinic 2nd of the Rizzoli Orthopedic Institute. He has agreed to participate in the pilot study evaluating the functional outcome during the execution of high functional demand motor tasks, such as walking on an unstable surface, stair ascent and descent, and maximal knee flexion under load (lunge). He will undergo gait analysis and evaluation scales at the Movement Analysis Laboratory of the Rizzoli Orthopedic Institute before the surgery and at a 6-month follow-up visit. He is willing to comply with the post-operative rehabilitation program according to the normal clinical practice.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) that has not responded to initial treatments. The patient has undergone two induction regimens, but the bone marrow aspirate taken within 2 weeks of the diagnosis showed greater than 5.0% bone marrow blasts, indicating that the patient is not in remission. The patient has no other life-threatening conditions requiring treatment other than AML. The patient's estimated creatinine clearance is greater than or equal to 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and the serum bilirubin, AST/ALT, and alkaline phosphatase levels are within normal limits. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of greater than or equal to 70%, and the estimated left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 40%. The patient is willing to comply with medication and has appropriate caregivers. The patient has signed informed consent, and there is no evidence of uncontrolled infections or active central nervous system leukemia. The patient has not received chemotherapy within 21 days of registration, and the peripheral blasts are less than or equal to 10,000/μL at the time of registration. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the Multi-center Study of Myeloablative Allo Stem Cell Transplant for Non-remission AML Using CloBu4 Regimen.

A 50-year-old woman, Mrs. Smith, was recently diagnosed with stage 2 breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy of her right breast and axillary node dissection. The biopsy revealed estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-negative, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer. Her medical history includes hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. She is on a daily dose of atorvastatin (20mg) and lisinopril (10mg). She does not smoke and has a BMI of 27. She exercises three times a week, doing low-impact aerobics and yoga. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her family history is significant for breast cancer in her maternal grandmother. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the role of antioxidants during chemotherapy and their potential impact on toxicities and disease-free survival.

A 62-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of knee pain that has been persistent for the past 6 months. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled by medication. He recently retired from his job as a construction worker due to the severity of his knee pain. The pain is described as aching and throbbing, with occasional sharp pains, mostly localized to the medial aspect of the right knee. The patient reports difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, and performing routine daily activities. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they provide only temporary relief. On physical examination, the patient is noted to have moderate tenderness to palpation over the medial joint line of the right knee, with mild swelling and crepitus on active and passive movement. He has a limited range of motion and difficulty bearing weight on the affected leg. The patient meets the American College of Rheumatology criteria for primary osteoarthritis of the knee. He rates his knee pain as 7 out of 10 on an 11 point numeric pain rating scale. The patient is willing to participate in the study and abide by the protocol and treatment schedule. He does not have any implants that are incompatible with electrical stimulation, and he does not have any uncontrolled concomitant disease affecting the knee.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of metastatic prostate cancer that has not responded to hormone therapy. The cancer has spread to his bones and he is experiencing bone pain. He has undergone previous treatments including hormone therapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no history of primary cancer except for basal cell skin cancer. He has no contraindications to anthracycline treatment. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and he has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. His blood work shows a neutrophil count greater than 1500/mm3, a platelet count greater than 100,000/mm3, and a hemoglobin level greater than 9 g/dL. His liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. He has not received chemotherapy before and has not received any radiation therapy in the past 3 months. He has not received any estramustine treatment for at least 1 month. He is willing to participate in a randomized clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of methylprednisolone with or without doxorubicin in treating his metastatic prostate cancer.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who underwent a hysterectomy (total or supra-cervical) in the past and is now experiencing pelvic organ prolapse. She has been experiencing symptoms such as a sensation of vaginal bulging, discomfort during intercourse, and difficulty with bowel movements. The patient has been advised to undergo robotic-assisted sacrocolpopexy, which is a minimally invasive surgical procedure used to treat pelvic organ prolapse. The patient is willing to participate in this study to help evaluate the efficiency of the Colpassist vaginal positioning device during robotic-assisted sacrocolpopexy. She is fluent in English and has no plans for future pregnancy. She is not currently pregnant and has no other medical conditions that would make her ineligible for the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman who is currently undergoing treatment for breast cancer at the Radiation Oncology Department at the University of Pennsylvania. She has been experiencing moderate levels of stress and anxiety related to her diagnosis and treatment, and is interested in exploring non-pharmacological interventions to manage her symptoms. She has no prior experience with visual art making, but is open to trying it as a potential tool for stress reduction. She is able and willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 45-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic sigmoidectomy for sigmoid colon cancer. The surgery was uncomplicated, and the patient was discharged on the fourth postoperative day. On the seventh day after discharge, she presented to the emergency department with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. CT scan of the abdomen revealed an anastomotic leak with associated abscess formation. She was taken to the operating room for an exploratory laparotomy and the leak was identified at the anastomotic site. The surgeon deemed the anastomosis not suitable for reanastomosis and opted for an end colostomy. An endoluminal vacuum (E-Vac) therapy was placed at the site of the anastomotic leak. The patient is currently being monitored for any complications related to the E-Vac therapy. She is willing to participate in the registry and has provided her consent to be included in the study. She is 45 years old, with no significant past medical history, and no known allergies.

28-year-old male, newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has no prior history of antiretroviral drug treatment and his plasma viral load is 1200 copies/ml. He is clinically stable and has no active opportunistic infections. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and no known hypersensitivity to any of the products under study. He has not used any drugs that may affect lipid and/or glucose metabolism for at least 30 days prior to inclusion in the study. He is willing to use barrier contraceptive methods during the study as he is sexually active. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or any other conditions that would contraindicate the use of any of the drugs under study. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and undergo tests and examinations.

A 35 year old male was admitted to the hospital with thermal burns on his right arm and chest caused by an accident at work. He has no history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure or asthma. His vital signs are stable and he is able to communicate well in English. His EKG revealed first degree heart block. He is not taking any interacting medication and did not receive propranolol within the last 6 months. He is not diabetic or pregnant. He has no history of hyperthyroidism, and is not using any medication for peripheral vascular disease or vasospastic disorder. He does not exceed daily acceptable chronic opioid use prior to burn.

A 22-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of food and gender on the pharmacokinetic profile of SUVN-G3031. She has no history of GI, hepatic, or renal disease, and has not had any recent illnesses, medical/surgical procedures, or trauma. She has tested negative for serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody. The subject is interested in the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures and requirements.

25 year old healthy male who does not smoke and is not currently taking any medications. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other chronic illnesses. He enjoys drinking red wine occasionally and is interested in participating in a study to determine the effects of red wine and cognac on coronary circulation.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who underwent renal transplant surgery from a living donor 8 weeks ago. She has a history of end-stage renal disease due to polycystic kidney disease. She is currently on a triple immunosuppressive regime consisting of cyclosporine, Enteric coated mycophenolate, and corticosteroids. Her serum creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL and she has not experienced any rejection episodes so far. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She has no history of malignancy or severe liver disease. She is willing to participate in the study and adhere to the study protocol.

A 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension is being evaluated for a potential heart condition. He has normal liver function and no history of significant bleeding. He does not have a history of kidney disease, but his last laboratory results showed a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 50 mL/min. He is otherwise healthy and has not had any significant medical problems in the past. He is currently not taking any prohibited medications or OTC vitamins and herbal supplements. He has no known allergies. He has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 15 years. He has a history of hypertension, peripheral arterial disease, and a previous foot ulcer that has healed. He presents with a chronic pressure ulcer on his left heel that has been present for 2 months. The wound is classified as a Stage III pressure ulcer with moderate exudate. He has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to the dressing or its components. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol instructions and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is not currently participating in another investigative drug or device trial and is suitable for NPWT according to the investigator's judgement and Instructions for Use.

Maria is a 50 year old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She has been taking medications to control her blood glucose levels for the past 5 years. She regularly checks her blood glucose levels and maintains a balanced diet. She has a family history of hypertension and cardiovascular diseases. Her blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg without BP lowering medications. She has experienced occasional headaches but has not been diagnosed with hypertension yet. She has no history of heart attack or stroke. Her vitamin D levels are below 20 ng/ml. She has no history of recent weight loss, pregnancy or heavy alcohol consumption. She has not followed any extreme diets in the past 3 months. Her labs and physical exam are normal otherwise. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the role of vitamin D in hypertension and immune mechanisms of type 2 diabetes.

This is a 53-year-old male who was diagnosed with glioblastoma (GBM) six months ago. He underwent standard radiation therapy and temozolomide, but his disease progressed and he was found to have recurrent GBM by diagnostic biopsy. He is currently bevacizumab-naïve and is eligible to participate in Cohort B of the ongoing Phase 2 study of Durvalumab (MEDI4736) in patients with GBM. His performance status is ECOG 1 and he has adequate hematologic, renal and hepatic function. He has measurable disease confirmed by histopathology and his last baseline MRI scan was performed within 14 days prior to Study Day 1. He has no prior exposure to durvalumab or other programmed cell death-1 (PD-1), programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1), cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) antibodies, and no history of autoimmune disease or primary immunodeficiency. He is not currently pregnant or breast-feeding, and agrees to use a medically acceptable form of contraception for the duration of the study. He has given written informed consent and is willing and able to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 78-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 5 years. She has a medical history of hypertension that is being treated with medication, and she has also had a previous ischemic stroke. Her current medication includes atenolol, lisinopril, and aspirin. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She presents with complaints of dizziness and shortness of breath. Her vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mm Hg and a heart rate of 80 bpm. Her physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Laboratory studies reveal an INR of 2.5. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of idrabiotaparinux sodium in preventing clots in the brain and other organs. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and has no contraindications to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 45 year old female who reports feeling excessively tired during the day, loud snoring at night, and occasional pauses in breathing while sleeping. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage her blood pressure. She has a BMI of 31 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea with an AHI of 35. She does not have any other suspected sleep disorders or muscle diseases that may interfere with the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to read and sign the informed consent form. She is interested in trying the iNAP® Sleep Therapy System to improve her sleep quality and overall health.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has experienced a major cardiac arrest. He was found unconscious at home by his wife and was immediately taken to the nearest hospital. The patient had no prior history of cardiac issues and was in overall good health. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient was unresponsive, and CPR was initiated. The patient was successfully resuscitated after 20 minutes of CPR and was transferred to the ICU for further management. The patient underwent targeted temperature management to prevent neurological damage, and he is now eligible for this study. The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score after cardiac arrest was 6, and there was no neurological cause of the cardiac arrest. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated for respiratory support. The patient's current vital signs are stable, and he is receiving appropriate medical care. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old unmarried man who experienced a manic episode 2 months ago, characterized by an elevated mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and distractibility. He was diagnosed with bipolar disorder type I by a psychiatrist and has no comorbid medical or psychiatric conditions. The patient is currently receiving treatment with lithium and olanzapine, which effectively controlled his manic symptoms. The patient has completed high school and has a job as a data analyst, reporting no significant cognitive difficulties at work. He is a non-smoker and occasionally consumes caffeine. The patient has no history of substance abuse, and his urine drug screen is negative. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 67-year-old man with a history of pancreatic cancer that has metastasized to the liver. He presents with jaundice, pruritus, and weight loss. He has a performance status of 2 and is not a candidate for surgical resection. Imaging studies reveal a malignant stricture of the extra-hepatic biliary tree. He has no history of allergies and takes only pain medication for his cancer-related pain. His vital signs are stable, and his laboratory studies show elevated liver function tests with total bilirubin of 10 mg/dL. He has no prior history of biliary tract surgery and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He is able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old male veteran who suffered a spinal cord injury resulting in paraplegia 5 years ago came to the clinic with a history of recurrent pressure ulcers in the sacrum area. He has had multiple hospital admissions due to pressure ulcer complications, which have been a significant burden on his health and finances. Despite receiving treatment for his pressure ulcers, they have recurred within a few months. He is proficient in English and has access to a telephone for follow-up. He has no cognitive impairment and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore effective interventions for reducing recurrent pressure ulcers.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with small cell lung cancer (SCLC). She has a history of smoking for 20 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy for SCLC 6 months ago and is currently in remission. Her oncologist recommended her to participate in the clinical trial to determine the prevalence and significance of paraneoplastic autoantibodies in various types of cancer patients. The patient signed the informed consent form and agreed to participate. She is willing to provide blood samples for autoantibody determinations and HLA typing. She is living with her husband and two children and works as a teacher in a local high school. She denies any neurological symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or memory loss.

A 50 year old female patient visited her gastroenterologist for a routine check-up. She has a family history of colon cancer, with her mother being diagnosed with it at the age of 60. She has no personal history of adenomas or colon cancer. She is in good health, with no significant medical history or comorbidities. She has an average BMI, and her bowel preparation is good. The patient is able to understand and follow study procedures and has signed the informed consent. She is eligible for the clinical trial as she meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with oromandibular dystonia (OMD) by a movement disorders specialist. She has been experiencing involuntary muscle contractions in her jaw and tongue, which is affecting her ability to speak and eat properly. She has not received levetiracetam before and is not on any other medication for her dystonia. She has not received botulinum toxin injections for the past 12 weeks and is willing to abstain from receiving any during the study. She is able to take medication orally and has an estimated creatinine clearance (eCrCL) of more than 50 mL/min. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant within 6 months and is willing to use an effective method of contraception from the time of enrollment until 3 months after the last dose of the study medication. She does not have any psychiatric co-morbidities such as depression, psychosis or phobic disorders, has not had a history of brain tumor, stroke, documented history of peripheral trauma to the mouth, jaw or face within a year from the onset of dystonia, epilepsy or seizures. She does not have postural instability, frequent falling, severe vertigo or dizziness and severe ataxia. She is willing to provide consent for the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a past medical history of a heart attack that occurred 3 years ago. He underwent coronary artery bypass surgery and has been on anti-arrhythmic medications since then. Despite the medications, he has been experiencing recurrent episodes of ventricular tachycardia, which have been managed by his implanted cardioverter-defibrillator. His most recent episode was 2 weeks ago. He is currently on amiodarone and beta-blockers, but his symptoms have not improved. He has been referred to the Cleveland Clinic for a catheter ablation procedure using a new mapping algorithm called parallel mapping. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has signed an informed consent form. He does not have any reversible causes of ventricular tachycardia, contraindications to anticoagulation therapy, or history of drug or alcohol dependency. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with all post-procedural follow-up requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia. She had a history of palpitations and chest pain that occurred intermittently for the past 6 months. She had an episode of sudden loss of consciousness and was resuscitated by the emergency medical team. She underwent further evaluation that confirmed the diagnosis of ventricular tachycardia. She was started on anti-arrhythmic drugs, but her symptoms persisted. She was referred for a clinical trial that aims to determine whether electrophysiologic study (EPS) or Holter monitoring (HM) was the better method for selecting effective long-term antiarrhythmic drug therapy in patients with sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or an episode of aborted sudden death. She was eligible for the trial and underwent Holter monitoring to determine the average number of premature ventricular contractions per hour. She was found to have an average of 40 premature ventricular contractions per hour and was referred for electrophysiologic testing. She was randomized into an EPS arm of drug testing and received, in random sequences, up to six antiarrhythmic drugs. When an effective drug was found, she underwent a predischarge HM and exercise test. Follow-up continued for one year after the last subject had been randomized. The primary endpoint in the trial was time to arrhythmia recurrence during therapy with a drug predicted to be effective by either EPS or HM.

The patient is a 56 year-old Chinese man who has been experiencing persistent knee pain in his left knee after exercise, weight loss and physical therapy. He has a diagnosis of osteoarthritis in his left knee with Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) classification Grade 2, as confirmed by X-ray examination conducted in the last 3 months. He rates his pain as moderate to severe on the 100mm Visual analogue scale(VAS) with a WOMAC A1 score of 55mm. He has not undergone any surgery on his left knee in the last 6 months and has not received any hyaluronic acid-based injection or steroids into his left knee in the last 6 months. He has not been diagnosed with bilateral knee osteoarthritis or any inflammatory conditions affecting his knee joint. He has no clinically significant valgus or varus deformity of his knee joint, no ligamentous laxity or unstable meniscus, and no history of septicemia or clinically considered sub-acute infection of his knee joint. He is not pregnant or lactating and has no known allergy to guanylin and/or any active ingredient or excipient of hyaluronic acid-based injection/diclofenac sodium. He is willing and able to understand and sign the Informed Consent Form (ICF) that has already been approved by the Independent Ethics Committee (IEC).

A 35-year-old female patient presented to the clinic with complaints of lower back pain that has been ongoing for several months. She describes the pain as dull, aching, and constant, which is worsened with prolonged sitting and standing. She also reports morning stiffness and difficulty in bending forward. The patient has a history of psoriasis but no prior diagnosis of spondyloarthritis. After a thorough physical exam and diagnostic tests, the patient is diagnosed with axial spondyloarthritis. The physician prescribes certolizumab pegol as part of the treatment plan. The patient is newly prescribed CZP and considered reliable and capable of adhering to the observational plan. She signs the Patient Data Consent Form and agrees to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old Japanese man who has been experiencing chronic cough, breathlessness, and wheezing for over a year. He was a heavy smoker and quit smoking 2 years ago. He has not been diagnosed with any other lung disease. He has a history of hypertension and controlled with medication. He reports difficulty walking long distances and performing daily activities due to his respiratory symptoms. Upon examination, the patient has decreased breath sounds and expiratory wheezing. Spirometry shows a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.65 and FEV1 of 55% predicted. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has not been on any LAMA, LABA or ICS maintenance therapy in the past 6 months. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 42-year-old male with a history of GERD presents for an esophageal-gastro-duodenoscopy (EGD) due to persistent heartburn and difficulty swallowing. He weighs 75 kg and is otherwise healthy. He does not have any allergies to medications. He is not taking any medications currently. He reports occasional alcohol consumption but no smoking. He has never undergone sedation for a medical procedure before. He has normal vision and hearing.

57-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced pancreatic cancer confirmed by biopsy. The cancer is considered inoperable by radiological and surgical evaluation. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a 30 pack-year smoking history. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He has normal organ and marrow function, with leukocytes greater than 3,000/uL, absolute neutrophil count greater than 1,500/uL, platelets greater than 100,000/uL, total bilirubin less than 1.5 X ULN, AST (SGOT)/ALT (SGPT) less than 2.5 X ULN, and creatinine less than 1.5 X ULN. He has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to gemcitabine and oxaliplatin or other agents used in the study. The patient has no active brain or leptomeningeal disease and no uncontrolled intercurrent illness. He is willing to use adequate contraception and has agreed to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 65-year-old Hispanic man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 8 months ago. He has been on hormone therapy for the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve his bone health and body composition. He is not an active soccer player or participant in any other exercise or lifestyle intervention program for the past 12 months. He has a BMI of 28 and is currently taking Lisinopril for hypertension. He speaks both English and Spanish fluently and has a smartphone to receive text messages. He has been cleared by his treating oncologist to participate in the trial. He has no history of heart disease or other active cancer. He is interested in making positive lifestyle changes and is willing to commit to participating in the study for its duration.

A 57-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing shortness of breath and a persistent cough. She underwent biopsy and CT scan as part of the diagnostic workup. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NSCLC. She has not received any systemic therapy for lung cancer before. CT scan showed a primary tumor measuring 5 cm in size and mediastinal lymph node involvement. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal organ function. She has no history of radiotherapy to the region of the chest that would impede the treatment of the study malignancy. Her pregnancy test is negative, and she agrees to use adequate contraception during the study treatment. She is willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to receive Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT) followed by concurrent mediastinal chemoradiation with or without consolidation chemotherapy.

A 35-year-old male from Bangladesh, who has been exposed to arsenic via contaminated drinking water and has a well water arsenic concentration of more than 10 ug/L. He has no known renal disease and is not currently taking any nutritional supplements. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of folic acid and creatine as therapeutic approaches for lowering blood arsenic. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and does not plan to participate in any other clinical trials during the study period.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with stage II colon cancer. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m², which classifies her as obese. She has never had any surgery before, and she does not have any history of heart or lung disease. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. She has been a non-smoker for the past 10 years. Her pulmonary function test shows normal lung volumes and mild restriction with a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio of 80%. She has been scheduled for laparoscopic resection of her colon cancer, and she has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of different doses of dexmedetomidine infusion on lung mechanics and oxygenation during the surgery.

A 48-year-old woman has a history of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) for over 5 years, which has not been well controlled despite previous ethmoidal surgery. She has been taking oral corticosteroids intermittently over the past two years and has also had three courses of antibiotics during that time. Her sinus Computed tomography Lund-Mackay score is 16 and her Sinonasal Outcome Test -22 (SNOT-22) score is 35. During her last visit to the clinic, she underwent an ASA-challenge test which was positive, indicating that she has Acetyl salicylic acid (ASA)-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD). She has given her consent to participate in the AirGOs-medical clinical trial, which involves randomized double-blinded prospective controlled treatment. She will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment arms: ASA-desensitization po tablet daily for 11 months (n=36) or placebo po tablet daily for 11 months (n=18). She will receive the ASA challenge and desensitization/placebo according to a modified international protocol. During the ASA challenge, she will be monitored to see if she is ASA-challenge positive, and if so, she will be randomized and begin the trial by using a blinded ½ tablet of 250 mg ASA or ½ tablet of placebo daily at home for the next month. The dosing will be increased at a hospital setting after one month, and she will continue using blindly 250 mg ASA 1 tablet or placebo 1 tablet daily at home for the next 10 months. If she does not tolerate the up-dosing of ASA/placebo, she will continue using blindly ½ tablet of 250 mg ASA/placebo daily at home for the next 10 months. She will also undergo nasal, blood, and urine sample tests during the trial. Her symptoms and side-effects will be monitored during each visit. She will visit the doctor and/or nurse at 1, 5, 11, and 12 months post-starting with the treatment, and her lung function (eNO, nNO, PEF, spirometry) will be monitored. The primary end point of the study is to see if there is a change in nasal endoscopic nasal polyp score at -4 days vs. +11 months post-randomization, and the secondary end point is to measure change in SNOT-22 score at -4 days vs. +11 months post-randomization, and change in relative Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1 %) without bronchodilator at -1 month vs. +11 months post-randomization. She is eligible for the clinical trial as she meets all the inclusion criteria and has none of the exclusion criteria.

A 68-year-old man who recently retired from his job as an accountant is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new influenza vaccine. He has no history of major illness, but he does have high blood pressure, which is well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and exercises regularly by taking brisk walks around his neighborhood. He has never participated in a clinical trial before. He has no known allergies and takes no medications other than the blood pressure medication. He is married and lives with his wife, who is also retired. They have two adult children who live nearby.
