He is looking forward to contributing to the development of a new vaccine that may help protect older adults like himself from influenza.

59-year-old male with a history of headaches, nausea, and vomiting for the last 3 months. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the left temporal lobe of the brain, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of glioblastoma multiforme. The patient underwent surgical resection followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. After completion of the standard treatment, a follow-up MRI showed no evidence of residual disease. The patient is now being considered for this clinical trial to receive cellular adoptive immunotherapy comprising aldesleukin-stimulated lymphokine-activated killer cells intracranially at the time of therapeutic craniotomy with the aim of improving progression-free and overall survival. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no other significant medical issues that would preclude surgery or aldesleukin therapy.

45-year-old female with a history of locally advanced breast cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. She underwent neoadjuvant therapy with TCHP (docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, pertuzumab) followed by lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. Pathology revealed a 2 cm invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR negative, HER2-positive (3+ by IHC). She completed adjuvant radiation and one year of trastuzumab. Last month, she presented with progressive shortness of breath and cough. Imaging revealed multiple pulmonary nodules and pleural effusion. A biopsy confirmed metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Performance status is 1. She has no history of brain metastases, no uncontrolled pain, and adequate organ function. She received no other anti-tumor treatment or investigational drug within the last 28 days. She has not had any major surgeries within the last 28 days and no curative radiation within the last 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and would like to learn more about her options.

A 32-year-old Afghan woman presents with a fever that has lasted for the past 3 days. She lives in a remote village in Afghanistan and has limited access to healthcare facilities. She reports feeling weak and tired and experiencing chills and sweats. She has no history of malaria but reports that several members of her family have had malaria in the past. She has not traveled recently. She has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. On examination, her temperature is 38.5°C, and she appears pale and fatigued. Her spleen is not enlarged. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old male office worker is seeking to participate in a clinical trial studying sleep patches. He reports that he is generally in good health and is not taking any medications. He has a BMI of 25 and has not traveled more than three time zones in the past month. He works a typical day job and usually goes to bed between 9-12 PM, getting on average 6 hours of sleep per night. He reports experiencing unrefreshing sleep for the past month and is willing to limit his alcohol and caffeine intake during the testing period. He reports no history of sleep disorders or contact dermatitis to adhesives. He scores ≤ 2 on the depression scale and ≤ 3 on the anxiety scale. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe headache and loss of consciousness. Diagnostic head CT scan revealed acute intracranial hemorrhage measuring 8 mL. He has no history of seizure or other medical conditions that would make him unsuitable for the SENSE device monitoring or study participation. He is willing and able to comply with the study procedures. The patient has signed a written informed consent form.

50-year-old male with a history of sporadic duodenal adenoma diagnosed and resected at Westmead hospital in 2010, now presents with intermittent episodes of obscure gastrointestinal bleeding and iron deficiency anemia. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all well controlled on medication. He has no significant family history of gastrointestinal malignancies, FAP, or PJS. The patient has undergone a colonoscopy within the last three years, which did not reveal any polyps or malignancies. The patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the prevalence of small bowel polyps in patients with sporadic duodenal adenomas.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising for the past few months. He went to his primary care physician for evaluation and was referred to a hematologist. The hematologist ordered blood tests, which revealed abnormal levels of white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The patient has not received any prior treatment for his AML. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale, meaning he is able to carry out normal daily activities with some difficulty. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. His serum creatinine, AST, ALT, and total bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He has no known infections or other active malignancies. He has signed informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman complaining of intense vaginal itching, burning sensation, and discharge that started three days ago. She reports no history of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis and has not taken any antifungal medication in the last seven days. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no known immunosuppression. She has not been diagnosed with any other vulvovaginal or systemic diseases and has no known hypersensitivity to azole derivatives. A vaginal swab revealed a positive KOH fresh examination for yeasts (hyphae, pseudohyphae) and later confirmed with a positive Candida spp. culture. The vaginal score sum is ≥ 2. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of different doses of albaconazole for the treatment of acute non-complicated vulvovaginitis due to Candida spp.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a body mass index of 43. She has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years, despite various attempts to lose weight through diet and exercise. She has no past medical history of any significant medical conditions. Her family history is positive for obesity, with her mother and sister also being overweight. She is currently on no medications and does not have any allergies. She has been referred for laparoscopic obesity surgery by her primary care physician to aid in her weight loss journey. She presents at the clinic with no skin diseases in the operation area. Her lab study is as follows: FBS: 95 mg/dl Cholesterol: 220 mg/dl TG: 180 mg/dl LDL: 145 mg/dl HDL: 35 mg/dl.

The patient is a premature baby boy who was born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1.2 kg. He had a history of respiratory distress syndrome and was intubated for the first week of life. On routine retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) screening at 32 weeks postmenstrual age, he was found to have Stage 3 Zone 2 ROP in both eyes. He received treatment with laser photocoagulation as part of the VGFTe-ROP-1920 study. He is now 9 months old and has been discharged from the neonatal intensive care unit for 5 months. He has been followed up by his ophthalmologist regularly and has not had any significant ocular or systemic adverse events related to the treatment. His parents have provided informed consent to participate in the extension study to evaluate the long-term outcomes of pediatric patients who received treatment for ROP in the VGFTe-ROP-1920 study.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is at 39 weeks gestational age and has been advised to undergo induction of labor due to prolonged pregnancy. She has a Bishop score of 4, indicating an unripe cervix. She has no history of uterine scar or multiple pregnancy and her fetus is in cephalic presentation. She is fluent in French and has French Medical Public Insurance. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial that compares two rhythms of administration of prostaglandin vaginal gels for cervical priming before induction of labor in term patients. She has shown interest in participating in the study and has given written informed consent for inclusion.

A 24 yo male who is a nonsmoker and has a normal body mass index is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating autoregulation of the choroid during isometric exercise. The study is looking for men aged between 19 and 35 years who have normal findings in the medical history and physical examination unless the investigator considers an abnormality to be clinically irrelevant. Participants should have normal laboratory values, normal ophthalmic findings, and ametropy less than 3 Dpt. The participant should not have a history of hypersensitivity to the trial drug or to drugs with a similar chemical structure, or any gastrointestinal, liver, or kidney disease, or other conditions known to interfere with, distribution, metabolism or excretion of study drugs. The participant should not have donated blood during the previous 3 weeks and should not have participated in a clinical trial in the 3 weeks preceding the study.

A 45-year-old female patient is admitted to the hospital with a high fever and chills. She complains of feeling weak and has been experiencing fatigue for the past few days. She was previously healthy and had no history of recent hospitalization. Her blood cultures are positive for Enterobacteriaceae and she is diagnosed with bacteremia. The microorganism is found to be non-susceptible to third generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone and ceftazidime), but susceptible to both PTZ and meropenem. She meets the inclusion criteria for the PETERPEN clinical trial and is willing to participate. She has no known allergies to any of the study drugs and has not previously participated in this trial. She is not currently participating in any other interventional clinical trial and is not expected to die within the next 48 hours.

The patient is a 28-year-old physically active woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She follows a healthy diet and exercises regularly, but has noticed that her blood lipid levels are slightly elevated. She has no known allergies to fish, milk, egg, or gluten. She does not smoke and is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of heart disease, intestinal dysfunction, kidney dysfunction, or insulin secretion problems. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if dietary intake of cod residual material meal can help regulate her blood lipid and glucose levels, and potentially improve her body composition.

67-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and cough. He was diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia and started on antibiotics. However, his respiratory status rapidly deteriorated, and he was intubated and transferred to the medical ICU. He was diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and received mechanical ventilation, prone positioning, and other supportive care. Despite aggressive treatment, he remained critically ill for several weeks before gradually improving and eventually being discharged from the ICU. This patient would be an eligible candidate for the study on ARDS in Taiwan, and his long-term outcomes could be recorded to help improve the management and treatment of ARDS in the future.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain for the past 2 years. She has undergone a pelvic MRI at CHUGA, which showed an isolated endometriotic lesion in the utero-sacral ligament. She has been advised to undergo laparoscopic surgical treatment and has agreed to participate in this research study. The patient is fluent in French and able to complete the questionnaire based on EHP 30. She does not have any functional urinary or digestive signs related to endometriotic lesions and has not undergone extensive pelvic surgery related to endometriosis in the past. She is not pregnant and is not involved in any other clinical research study. The patient is affiliated with a social security system and is available for a follow-up of 6 months.

The patient is a 25-year-old female from the United States with a confirmed peanut allergy. She has a history of experiencing mild to moderate allergic reactions after eating peanuts, including hives, itching, and swelling. She has never experienced a severe or life-threatening reaction. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find a new treatment for her peanut allergy. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 55 kg. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a reliable form of contraception. She has not participated in any interventional studies for the treatment of peanut or food allergies in the past 12 months and has not received any investigational products in the past 3 months. She has not received systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressant drugs within the past 2 weeks and is not taking beta blockers, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin-receptor blockers, or calcium channel blockers. She has no history of ischemic cardiovascular diseases or drug, alcohol, or substance abuse. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol requirements and can communicate effectively with the investigator and staff.

The patient is a 58 year-old man who has noticed changes in his urinary habits in the last few months, including increased frequency and urgency. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level was found to be elevated at 5 ng/ml during routine screening. Digital rectal examination revealed no palpable abnormalities. He has no history of prostate cancer in his family. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. He does not smoke, but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not undergone a prostate biopsy before and has not taken any analgesics in the past 24 hours. MRI showed a PIRADS score of 4 in his prostate gland.

A 29-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia presents with symptoms of auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech. He has been on risperidone but has not had significant improvement in his symptoms. He has no history of Parkinson's disease, seizure disorder, cerebrovascular accident, diabetes mellitus, clinically significant gastrointestinal disorders, or severe impairment of the liver or kidneys. He has no known drug allergies or hypersensitivity to antipsychotics. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and effectiveness of paliperidone in the treatment of schizophrenia.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who is experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past 5 hours. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. Upon examination, he is found to have ST-segment elevation greater than 1 mm in two or more contiguous leads between V1 and V4 or new left bundle branch block. The patient is admitted to the emergency room immediately. After further evaluation, the diagnosis of anterior acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is confirmed. The patient undergoes successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stenting within 6 hours of experiencing AMI symptoms. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the IC-HOT clinical trial, including being between 18 and 80 years of age, having anterior AMI, experiencing clinical symptoms consistent with AMI for ≤6 hours, and having successful angioplasty with a TIMI flow grade of 0, 1, 2, or 3 flow in the LAD. The patient has none of the exclusion criteria, such as prior CABG surgery, impaired renal function, or a history of intracerebral mass, aneurysm, arteriovenous malformation, or hemorrhagic stroke. The patient agrees to all required follow-up procedures and visits.

A 32-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective surgery to remove a benign ovarian cyst. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no known allergies. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has never had any problems with anesthesia or intubation in the past. She has a normal airway with a Mallampati score of Class I. Her physical exam is unremarkable. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is an expectant mother who is currently 36 weeks pregnant. She is planning to deliver at the Royal Alexandra Hospital. She has a history of a healthy pregnancy and has been attending regular prenatal check-ups. The patient has no known allergies and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided consent. The aim of the study is to compare the accuracy and speed of heart rate assessment using a tap-based smartphone application versus the standard auscultation method during neonatal resuscitation. The study will collect data over a period of 12 months and all newborn infants delivered at the hospital between 22+0-41+6 weeks gestation will be eligible for inclusion. The patient will have routine heart rate measurement using electrocardiogram (ECG) as a comparison for accuracy. The study is expected to improve the accuracy and speed of neonatal resuscitation, potentially reducing morbidity and mortality outcomes for newborn babies.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU for sepsis secondary to pneumonia. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated, and his sedation level is RASS -3. His urine output has been decreasing over the past 24 hours, and his bladder pressure is measured to be 15mmHg. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no history of renal disease. His current medications include vancomycin, piperacillin/tazobactam, and norepinephrine at 0.2µg/kg/min for blood pressure support. His laboratory values show a white blood cell count of 16,000/mm3, creatinine of 1.2mg/dL, and a lactate level of 4.2mmol/L. He has mild peripheral edema but no abdominal distention. He has no history of allergy or adverse reaction to furosemide. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is not excluded for any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been diagnosed with tongue cancer. She has no significant medical history and is currently in overall good health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. The patient has been advised to undergo curatively intended radiotherapy with a total dose of 50-70 Gy. She is eligible for the trial as she meets all of the inclusion criteria. The patient has been informed about the study and its potential benefits and risks, and has provided informed consent to participate. She will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group. The patient will be monitored throughout the treatment period for any acute mucositis and any side effects associated with the use of the intraoral stent. The aim of the study is to confirm that the use of an intraoral stent will result in a lower dose to the palate throughout the treatment period, thereby reducing any potential side effects associated with radiotherapy of tongue cancer.

A 28-year-old male athlete who regularly participates in running and soccer has been experiencing mild discomfort in his Achilles tendon for the past few weeks. He is otherwise healthy with no underlying medical conditions or history of lower leg injury. He has not been taking any medications or drugs. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of circulatory disorders or cardiovascular diseases. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of deep friction massage on the Achilles tendon blood flow to potentially alleviate his discomfort.

54 yo M with end-stage cardiomyopathy received a heart transplant 6 months ago. The patient is currently enrolled in the Outcomes AlloMap Registry (OAR) Study and is undergoing regular AlloMap testing. An AlloMap sample will be drawn for research use along with the dd-cfDNA specimen at the time of the next for-cause biopsy where the center's infrastructure permits. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in this observational sub-study named D-OAR, which aims to investigate the utility of donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) as a surveillance tool in the management of heart transplant recipients. The patient has not had more than 1 prior AlloMap and is not pregnant. The patient will also undergo two follow-up dd-cfDNA specimens within 8 weeks after the for-cause biopsy, if being treated for rejection and/or graft dysfunction, as per their standard of care schedule.

Patient is a 63-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and underwent drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. She is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy and has no digestive symptoms. She has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or gastrectomy, cardiac insufficiency, thyroid dysfunction, or ongoing infections. She has not used antibiotics, bismuth, or sucralfate within the last month and has not been excluded from the trial. She does not have any gastrointestinal symptoms, such as acid reflux, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, stomach ache, or diarrhea, and has not been confirmed to have a peptic ulcer with Hp infection. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore the relationship between Helicobacter pylori (Hp) infection and the prognosis of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and to determine the significance of Hp eradication therapy in preventing major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) in patients on dual antiplatelet treatment.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been experiencing progressive neurological symptoms such as difficulty walking, muscle weakness, and cognitive impairment for the past 5 years. She has also noticed the appearance of yellowish-orange nodules on her tendons. A neurological exam shows mild to moderate spasticity, brisk reflexes, and mild gait ataxia. Further evaluation reveals elevated levels of cholestanol and bile acid precursors in her serum. Genetic testing confirms a diagnosis of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis. The patient has no history of significant medical problems or allergies, and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the use of chenodeoxycholic acid as a treatment for her condition.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who just gave birth to her first child vaginally at 38 weeks gestation. She had a second-degree perineal tear during delivery and did not require any antibiotics during labor. She is otherwise healthy with no history of chronic illnesses or medication use. She is breastfeeding her newborn and has no allergies. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate whether prophylactic antibiotics can prevent infection after perineal tear.

A 68-year-old male patient, retired, presents with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and type 2 diabetes. The patient was admitted to the hospital for worsening shortness of breath and ankle swelling. The patient was diagnosed with heart failure and started on a diuretic regimen, which effectively managed his symptoms. The patient is able to communicate effectively and does not have any cognitive impairment. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at improving self-care behaviour in heart failure patients. The patient's medical history includes a myocardial infarction 5 years ago, and a coronary artery bypass graft 3 years ago. The patient's medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, and furosemide. The patient has a supportive family and is motivated to learn ways to manage his heart failure symptoms.

A 24-year old female was diagnosed with schizophrenia last year. She reports feeling paranoid and hearing voices that tell her to harm herself. She has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past 6 months, which has helped with her symptoms. She is a high school graduate and works as a part-time cashier. She lives with her parents and younger sister. The patient reports having difficulty remembering things like where she placed her keys or what she had for breakfast. She also reports feeling unorganized and easily distracted. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her memory. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is fluent in English and able to sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 65 year old man who has been experiencing knee pain and stiffness for several years. The pain has worsened over the past year and has been limiting his ability to perform daily activities such as climbing stairs and walking for extended periods. He has tried various non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but they have not provided long-term relief. The patient has been diagnosed with severe osteoarthritis of the knee and has been recommended for a total knee replacement (TKR) surgery. He is fluent in English and has the capacity to understand the study protocol. He is not currently on warfarin therapy or any other medication that would render tourniquet use undesirable. He does not have any evidence of chronic or recent DVT in the index limb, and his thigh circumference is not greater than 100 cm. The patient is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of recurrent episodes of major depressive disorder with moderate to severe symptoms, despite treatment with multiple antidepressant medications. She has no history of psychotic or bipolar disorder and has not had any alcohol or drug abuse within the last 6 months. She is not currently taking any medications that would contraindicate SSRI therapy. She has no history of seizures or neurological illness. She has normal plasma glucose levels and no diagnosis of diabetes. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to understand the effects of sleep deprivation on antidepressant response.

A 26-year-old healthy male presents as a recreational cyclist who is interested to participate in a clinical study. He is a non-smoker and does not use any vaping products. He confirms that he is not a regular user of anti-inflammatory medications such as ibuprofen. He has no history of kidney disease or diabetes. He is physically active and enjoys cycling as a recreational activity. He is currently working in a tech company and spends most of his day sitting at his desk. He is concerned about his hydration levels during his cycling activities and is interested to learn more about the impact of hydration on kidney function during exercise. He is excited to participate in the study and contribute to the understanding of AKI biomarkers during cycling in the heat.

The patient is a 30 year old woman of Mediterranean descent, who has been diagnosed with Behçet's disease 2 years ago. She experiences oral and genital ulcers, uveitis and skin lesions. She also suffers from musculoskeletal involvement such as arthritis and arthralgia. She reports having a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in regular physical activity. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no other chronic diseases or psychiatric disorders. She is willing to participate in the study and has a cooperative level that can adapt to the evaluation and exercise program.

A 64-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer with bone metastases is experiencing significant bone pain. The pain is localized to the pelvic region and has been increasing gradually for the past month. The patient is currently receiving radiation therapy to alleviate the pain. However, the patient is concerned about the possibility of experiencing a pain flare after the radiation therapy. The patient has a history of hypertension and is taking medication for it. He has no other significant medical history. The patient is able to communicate his pain score at the planned radiated bony metastatic site. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written consent. The patient's KPS score is 70, and the baseline worst pain at the planned radiated bony metastatic site is 4.

The patient is a 35-year-old English speaking woman who has experienced physical and sexual assault leading to the development of PTSD symptoms. She is currently medically healthy and has no major medical disorders. She does not have claustrophobia and is able to lie still in a confined space. She does not have any magnetic metallic or electronic implants, pacemakers, or vascular stents. She does not have any permanent makeup or tattoos with metallic dyes. She is not currently pregnant and has not experienced a loss of consciousness greater than 10 minutes. She does not have any physical disabilities that prohibit task performance, blindness or deafness. She does not have any psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia. She is willing to participate in the study and is enthusiastic about the potential benefits of the research.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago. He has been under antiretroviral therapy for the past 18 months and his viral load is currently undetectable. He is sexually active with multiple partners and is concerned about his risk of contracting sexually transmitted infections. He has heard about the benefits of voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) in reducing the risk of HIV transmission and is interested in undergoing the procedure. He is currently in WHO HIV clinical stage 1, has no known bleeding or coagulation abnormalities, and has good control of his diabetes. He is willing to take an HIV test and agrees to be circumcised by PrePex as part of the study. He is able to understand the study procedures and requirements and agrees to return to the health care facility for follow-up visits until complete healing is achieved. He is able to comprehend and freely give informed consent for study participation.

A 30-year-old single mother of two children, aged 8 and 10, presents to Kisumu County Hospital in Western Kenya for routine HIV care. She has been receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 5 years, and her viral load has been undetectable for the past 3 years. During her visit, the healthcare provider informs her about the Financial Incentives to Increase Pediatric HIV Testing Pilot Study (FIT-Pilot) and explains the study's purpose and procedures. The mother reports that she is unsure of her children's HIV status and would like them to be tested. She is interested in participating in the study and agrees to be randomized into one of the three arms. The mother is highly motivated to ensure that her children are healthy and would like to learn more about the financial incentives and how they will work to increase HIV testing. She is willing to complete the post-test questionnaire and provide feedback on the effectiveness of the intervention. The mother is a suitable candidate for the study and meets all the inclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female with a history of cervical adenocarcinoma, stage IIIA, who underwent a radical hysterectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy in 2018. In 2019, she presented with recurrent disease involving the pelvic lymph nodes and underwent radiation therapy. She had a partial response to radiation therapy but developed anorexia and fatigue. She was evaluated by her oncologist for recurrent disease and was found to have progressive disease involving the pelvic sidewalls and para-aortic lymph nodes. A biopsy confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma of the cervix. The patient was referred for enrollment in the clinical trial for first-line chemotherapy for recurrent cervical cancer. She met all eligibility criteria and provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

25-year-old male with a history of convulsive seizures presents to the hospital with complaints of disturbed sleep and involuntary limb movements during sleep for the past 3 months. The patient has no history of psychiatric illnesses or seizures due to toxic or metabolic causes, infections, or structural causes. The seizures were eyewitnessed by a physician and were confirmed to be true epileptic seizures. The patient has not received any antiepileptic drugs before. A standard polysomnographic study was conducted and periodic limb movement index and frequency were found to be high. The patient was diagnosed with genetic generalized epilepsy according to the ILAE 2010 criteria and was enrolled in the study. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire, and sodium valproate was initiated in therapeutic doses. The patient will be followed up for six months, and EEG will be done after the follow-up period to assess seizure recurrence.

A 65 year-old man with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) diagnosed 4 years ago. He has received 4 lines of prior therapy and is now experiencing relapse of the disease. He presents with fatigue, unintentional weight loss, and enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axilla, and groin. He has no history of asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. His ECOG performance status is 1. His absolute neutrophil count is 1100/mm^3 and his platelet count is 75,000/mm^3. His serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL, total bilirubin is 0.9 mg/dL, and SGOT and SGPT are both within normal limits. He has not received prior treatment with daratumumab, but has been on ibrutinib for the past 6 months with suboptimal response (< PR). He has measurable disease and is willing to return to the enrolling institution for follow-up. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to practice a highly effective method of birth control during and after the study. He does not have any other serious medical conditions, laboratory abnormalities, or psychiatric illness that would prevent him from signing the informed consent form.

A 50-year-old female with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and heart failure presented to the cardiology clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion. She has been diagnosed with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy 6 months ago when she was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of heart failure. Her ejection fraction was found to be 35% on echocardiography. She has been on a stable regimen of heart failure medications including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. She has no history of coronary or ischemic heart disease. She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is well controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol abuse. She is physically active and walks for 30 minutes daily. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of Doxycycline in patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy and heart failure to improve her symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion.

32F presenting with symptoms of sneezing, itching, runny nose, and respiratory distress. The patient has a history of allergic asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis. She has been receiving treatment with leukotriene receptor antagonists and histamine receptor antagonists, which were prescribed by an Immunology and Allergy specialist. The patient is married, has a stable income, and has never been pregnant. She does not smoke and does not use any contraceptive methods. The patient has never been diagnosed with cancer, and has not undergone a hysterectomy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare HPV screening results between women diagnosed with atopic disease and healthy women without a history of atopy.

A 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus has been experiencing proteinuria for the past six months. She was diagnosed with diabetes 10 years ago and has been on metformin and sitagliptin. Her blood pressure is well controlled with amlodipine and lisinopril. She has no significant past medical history, family history or allergies. She is married with two children and works as a nurse. She monitors her blood glucose levels regularly and follows a diabetic diet. She also exercises regularly. Her most recent labs showed an eGFR of 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 and a UACR of 0.9 g/g. She was started on canagliflozin and her UACR was rechecked, showing a value of 0.8 g/g. However, her nephrologist recommends she participate in the AFFINITY study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of atrasentan in patients with proteinuric glomerular disease. The patient is willing to participate and understands the study requirements.

A 62-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C and alcohol use disorder was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) six months ago. He underwent transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) three months ago. His past medical history also includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is married and has two adult children. The patient reports no symptoms. His most recent laboratory results showed slightly elevated liver enzymes. He is currently being evaluated for Yttrium-90 radioembolization as part of his standard of care. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is able to provide informed consent and understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial. He does not have a history of hypersensitivity to contrast agents or any other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. She underwent a wide excision surgery, and four clips were placed in the tumor bed to avoid geographic misses. The tumor size was less than 20 mm, and the surgical margins were clear. She has no history of cardiac dysfunction or psychiatric problems. Her forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is 1.8 L/m, which is within the inclusion criteria. She has no history of smoking or respiratory problems. She has no history of cancer or radiation therapy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided full informed consent.

Pt is a 35yo M with a confirmed diagnosis of Crohn's disease, currently in a moderate flare with abdominal pain, diarrhea and weight loss. He has a history of recurrent flares and has been on various medications including a 5-ASA, corticosteroids, and immunomodulators with varying success. He has no other significant medical history or co-existing conditions.

75-year-old female with a diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 25 presents with her daughter as her care partner. She has a stable pharmaceutical regimen for the past 6 months and can travel to the centre. The patient has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis but is well-controlled with medications. She currently walks for 10 minutes three times a week and has no history of cardiovascular disease. The patient has adequate English to understand exercise training, hearing and vision for cognitive tests, and is able to comply with assessment and training schedule. She has been screened safe for exercise by a physician and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28 year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 28th week of pregnancy. She is experiencing frequent and severe leg cramps at least twice a week, which is causing discomfort and difficulty sleeping at night. She has no history of any other medical conditions and has a healthy pregnancy so far. She speaks Norwegian as her first language and is able to provide written consent to participate in the trial. She is not carrying twins and does not have any signs of edema or pre-eclampsia. She has not been taking any magnesium supplements prior to the trial.

A 55 yo F with a history of essential hypertension, presenting with systolic blood pressure of 150 mmHg at screening and 165 mmHg after two weeks wash-out. She has no history of hypertensive retinopathy, myocardial infarction, coronary or peripheral revascularization, stroke or TIA. She has well-controlled Type II diabetes with an HbA1c of 6.5%. She has no history of chronic heart failure, kidney transplant, or liver disease. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using highly effective contraception. She is not taking any medication that interacts with CYP3A4 enzymes. She has no psychiatric conditions that might impair medication intake, and her life expectancy is over 6 months. She works during the day and has no other mandatory indication for treatment with antihypertensive medications.

A 24-year-old female was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 8 months ago and has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms despite treatment with mesalamine and prednisone. She reports having 6-8 bowel movements per day with bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and urgency. She has lost 10 pounds in the last month due to poor appetite and nausea. Her Mayo score is currently 8. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 30 days, nor has she received any monoclonal antibody therapy within the last 12 weeks. She is willing to participate in The PROSPECT Study to receive investigational medication for her condition.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been practicing endurance training for more than a year. He is in good health, with no history of medication use or smoking. He exercises at least three times a week, and his VO2 max is greater than or equal to 50 ml/kg/min. He has a BMI of less than 25 kg/m2. He reports that he is interested in improving his cycling performance and is eager to participate in the study. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to supplements or medications. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the prescribed supplementation regimen. He is physically fit and has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

A 35 year old female with a BMI of 32.5kg/m2 who has struggled with weight management for several years. She has no history of bariatric surgery, but has attempted various weight-loss programs in the past with limited success. She is motivated to participate in this study and is willing to adhere to the proposed dietary interventions. She does not have a history of excessive alcohol consumption, bipolar disorder or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and is not currently using anti-depressant or anti-psychotic medications. She has not been diagnosed with an eating disorder or any other active disorder that may lead to significant weight changes. She is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant in the next year. She has well-controlled diabetes mellitus and is only taking one oral medication.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who suffered a traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage due to a motor vehicle accident. He was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 6 and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. A brain computed tomography (CT) scan showed diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage and a small intraventricular hemorrhage. His blood pressure was well controlled, and he did not require any surgical intervention. He has no history of malignancy or cerebrovascular stroke. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, indicating a normal weight. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. The patient's family has been informed about the study, and he has provided informed consent to participate.

32F with no significant past medical history scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient is currently on oral contraceptive pills and has no known allergies. She has a normal BMI and is a non-smoker. She has been classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification I. The patient has been informed about the study and has consented to participate. She is able to understand the study concept and has no premedication that would interfere with her cognitive abilities.

This clinical trial is not applicable to patients as it is a survey study aimed at investigating and tracking housestaff attitudes on patient care, patient safety, communication, and overall quality within the institution. It does not involve any medical intervention or patient participation. Therefore, there is no patient description needed.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with metastatic malignant lesions in the lumbar vertebral body. He has been experiencing chronic pain in the lower back (worst pain score of 7/10) which has limited his daily activities. He has already been treated with standard therapies but has not experienced any significant pain relief. The patient is a suitable candidate for the OsteoCool™ RF Ablation System and is willing to participate in the study. He has a Karnofsky score of 80 and is able to provide a signed and dated informed consent. However, the patient has a heart pacemaker implanted (in Europe and Canada only) and therefore may not be eligible for the study. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the study duration. He is not currently participating in any other clinical study that may add additional safety risks and/or confound study results.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of heart failure such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs for the past year. She has a family history of heart disease and was recently diagnosed with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (TTR). Her diagnosis was confirmed through a biopsy of the heart that showed positive staining for TTR amyloid deposits. The patient's echocardiogram revealed a left ventricular wall thickness of 14 mm and a reduced ejection fraction of 35%. Her glomerular filtration rate is 60 ml/min/1.73m2, and she has no proteinuria or hematuria. She has no history of liver disease or transplant and her liver function tests are within normal limits. Her thyroid function tests are also normal. The patient has not undergone any major surgery or acute coronary syndrome in the past 3 months. She has never been diagnosed with HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. She has not undergone any investigational drug therapy for amyloidosis within the past 4 weeks. She is willing to self-administer subcutaneous injections of the study drug, inotersen, on a weekly basis for a period of 24 months. She is willing to comply with all study requirements, including returning to the treating center for follow-up visits and taking daily oral Vitamin A supplementation throughout the study and for 3 months thereafter. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 42-year-old Hispanic woman presented with a body mass index (BMI) of 29.5 kg/m2 and a weight change of 2 kg in the last 12 months. She has no known allergies and is a non-smoker with no history of high alcohol use. She is not currently taking any medications, including vitamin supplements. She has no history of kidney, cardiovascular, hematological, respiratory, gastrointestinal, endocrine, or central nervous system disease, and no psychiatric disorders or active cancer within the last five years. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve her cardiometabolic risk factors and reduce her risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

A 42-year old male office worker was experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past two weeks. He also noticed blood in his stool. He went to a gastroenterologist for a check-up and was diagnosed with a gastric ulcer confirmed by endoscopy. He reported taking NSAIDs regularly for his lower back pain. He denied any other medical conditions or allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat his gastric ulcer and improve his overall symptoms.

A 60-year-old male patient presents with a history of ankle pain and swelling after falling from a low height. The physical examination revealed tenderness, swelling, and bruising around the ankle joint. X-ray imaging confirmed the diagnosis of a low energy ankle fracture. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to undergo surgical intervention for the fracture. The patient does not have a history of previous ankle surgery and does not have any disorders of bone metabolism other than osteoporosis. The patient has no significant cognitive impairment or neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease or dementia.

A 7 year old boy presents with difficulty in walking and loss of balance for the past few weeks. His parents noticed that he had trouble coordinating his movements and was falling more often than usual. He has been complaining of headaches and had an episode of vomiting last week. Upon physical examination, there is a weakness in the left arm and leg with impaired coordination. An MRI of the brain was performed which showed a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma. The family was informed of the poor prognosis and limited treatment options. They were offered to enroll the child in a clinical trial studying the effectiveness of nimotuzumab in children with intrinsic pontine glioma. The parents are willing to participate in the study and understand the potential benefits and risks involved. The boy meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is scheduled to start treatment within 14 days of the MRI.

An 80-year-old man presents with a history of progressive memory loss, difficulty with language, and problems with visual perception. He lives with his wife and needs assistance with daily activities. He has a history of hypertension, for which he is taking medication, and has had two episodes of transient ischemic attack (TIA) in the past. His ophthalmologist has recently diagnosed him with bilateral cataracts, which have been causing blurred vision and difficulty with daily activities such as reading and watching television. He is reluctant to undergo cataract surgery due to concerns about worsening cognition and quality of life. He has agreed to participate in this clinical trial to determine whether cataract removal can improve his vision, perception, independent function, and quality of life while managing Alzheimer's disease. His wife will be his research partner and will assist with protocol adherence and provide information about his daily activities and behavioral symptoms.

Patient is a healthy, non-smoking 30-year-old male with a body weight greater than 55 kg. He has no known allergies to fimasartan, ketoconazole, or rifampicin. He has no existing cardiac, hematological, hepatic, renal, or gastrointestinal diseases, and has no history of serious psychological disorders. He has not participated in a clinical trial within the last 2 months prior to the start of the study and has tested negative for drug and alcohol screening.

A 48-year-old female presents with pelvic pain and bloating that have persisted for the past 2 months. She has also noticed a decreased appetite and a 5-pound weight loss over the same period. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She denies any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. No family history of cancer is reported. On physical examination, a palpable mass is felt in the lower abdomen. Pelvic ultrasound reveals a complex, solid-cystic mass measuring 8 cm in diameter. CA-125 level is elevated at 563 U/mL. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis shows no evidence of distant metastases. Biopsy of the mass reveals a high-grade serous carcinoma. She is diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer and is offered enrollment in a clinical trial comparing tri-weekly paclitaxel and carboplatin versus weekly paclitaxel and carboplatin. She meets all eligibility criteria and consents to participate in the trial.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on evaluating the accuracy and reliability of a scoring system for laryngeal views during intubation, rather than involving patient participation. The study will involve an expert panel scoring images of laryngeal views obtained from patients receiving general anesthesia.

The patient is a 60-year-old man complaining of chronic knee pain and stiffness. The pain started gradually and has been worsening over the past year. The patient reports difficulty walking and climbing stairs. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. The patient does not have any significant medical history and is generally in good health. The patient is willing to attend all follow-up visits and comply with all study-related procedures and rehabilitation protocols. The patient is a Spanish citizen, speaks and reads Spanish fluently. The patient does not have any neuromuscular or vascular disease in the affected leg and has sufficient bone quality for total knee arthroplasty. The patient has primary knee osteoarthritis and is eligible for the study.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. She has been experiencing fatigue and occasional abdominal pain for the past few months, prompting her to seek medical attention. Her liver biopsy shows significant inflammation and fibrosis, indicating a clinical indication for treatment. She is genotype 1 and has been anti-HCV positive for over 6 months. She has no history of bleeding esophageal varices or other signs of decompensation. Her neutrophils count is 1.5 x 109/L and platelets count is 70 x 109/L. Her S-creatinine level is within normal limits. She has no history of severe psychiatric disorder, autoimmune disease, severe heart disease, previous organ or stem cell transplantation, malignancy, thyroid disease or severe retinopathy. She does not have drug abuse history. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not received any antiviral or immune modulating treatment in the last 6 months. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate if the duration of treatment of hepatitis C can be individualized based on how fast the hepatitis C virus concentration in the blood decreases.

28-year-old pregnant female who is either in her first or second pregnancy with no prior history of significant medical conditions presents for evaluation of uteroplacental health. She has a pre-pregnancy BMI within the range of 18.5 to 39.9 kg/m2. She is non-smoker and non-alcoholic. Her pregnancy is confirmed by ultrasound and is less than 14 weeks gestational age at the time of the screening. She has no known fetal chromosome abnormality, structural malformation or syndromes in the current pregnancy. She has no pre-existing autoimmune conditions or any vasculopathy. She has no history of sickle cell anemia or sickle cell trait. She is not at high risk for gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, fetal growth restriction (FGR), abruptio placentae secondary to hypertension or pre-eclampsia, stillbirth, or intrauterine fetal death. She has no contraindications to MRI. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 52-year-old woman diagnosed with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer that has recurred or progressed after receiving paclitaxel by 3 or 24 hour infusion in the past 6 months. She has completed prior platinum-based chemotherapy and has recovered from its myelosuppressive effects for at least 3 weeks. Her Karnofsky performance status is at least 60%, and she has a life expectancy of not specified. She has no active or uncontrolled infections and has not previously developed severe hypersensitivity reactions to paclitaxel. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using an effective method of contraception. She has no history of grade 3-4 peripheral neuropathy of any etiology. She is willing to participate in a single center, open-label study and receive paclitaxel intravenously every week as a 1-hour infusion. She is aware that she will receive prophylactic anti-allergy premedication prior to paclitaxel treatment.

4-year-old boy with a history of inguinal hernia who is scheduled for surgery. He has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics or dexmedetomidine. The patient's parents are anxious about their child's pain after surgery and are interested in exploring options for pain management. The child has no known bleeding disorders or neurological conditions.

Patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing numbness and tingling in her feet and hands for the past year. She also reports difficulty with balance and falls. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She has undergone a series of tests, including blood work and imaging, but no clear cause for her symptoms has been identified. She has been referred to this clinical trial to assess the prevalence of familial amyloid neuropathy due to transthyretin gene mutations (TTR-FAP) among patients with neuropathy of unknown etiology. The patient has provided written informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria, including having undergone minimal assessment for neuropathy as defined by the French National Health Authority. The patient has not been previously investigated for a TTR mutation and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma and has a history of smoking. She has smoked an average of 10 cigarettes per day for the past 20 years, resulting in a total of 14 pack-years. She has never been pregnant or lactating. The patient has experienced a drop in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) greater than 20% after provocation with small particle adenosine of less than 20 mg at the first visit. She has not had an asthma exacerbation in the last six weeks, nor has she suffered from an upper respiratory tract infection in the last four weeks. The patient's FEV1 is greater than 50% of predicted and greater than 1.2 liters. She has been diagnosed with asthma and does not have any other pulmonary disease that could influence the study results. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester, currently at 20 weeks of gestation. She is a non-smoker and does not have any known systemic disease. She has not received any periodontal treatment within the last six months and has more than 10 teeth. Her BMI is within the normal range (24 kg/m2). She has a history of good oral hygiene practices and visits the dentist regularly for routine check-ups. She has no known allergies and takes a prenatal vitamin supplement daily as prescribed by her obstetrician. She is excited about being a first-time mother and wants to ensure that her oral health is well-maintained during pregnancy and postpartum. She has provided her consent to participate in the study to help further the understanding of oral health biomarkers during pregnancy and postpartum.

A 42-year-old man has recently been diagnosed with HIV and is looking to participate in a clinical trial to better understand the effects of anti-HIV therapy on nerve and brain function. He has not yet started any treatment for his HIV. He has a history of depression for which he takes daily medication. He does not have any substance abuse problems. He has no history of neurological disorders or peripheral neuropathy. He currently works as a graphic designer and enjoys hiking and playing basketball in his free time. He is interested in contributing to research that could improve the lives of others living with HIV.

Pt is a 54yo M with a medical history significant for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) diagnosed 5 years ago. He has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath and coughing over the past 6 months. His lung function tests have shown a decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusion capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO). He is currently on oxygen therapy and has been taking pirfenidone for the past 2 years. Despite treatment, he continues to experience symptoms and has been referred to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness, safety, and tolerability of BMS-986278 in participants with lung fibrosis. He is a non-smoker and is otherwise healthy.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) for the past year. He reports loud snoring, frequent waking during the night, and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 36 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed as obese. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication for it. He works as an accountant and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He reports that he does not engage in regular physical activity and finds it difficult to make time for exercise. He has tried various diets in the past but has not been successful in losing weight. He is a non-smoker and occasionally drinks alcohol. He is interested in participating in the study to try to improve his sleep apnea symptoms and overall health.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained a deep 2nd thickness burn on his left forearm while at work. The burn covers an area of approximately 6 cm x 6 cm and was caused by contact with a hot metal surface. The patient has no known allergies and has not received any topical medication for the burn prior to enrollment in the clinical trial. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old Korean woman who has been experiencing jaundice for the past two weeks. She has been feeling weak and has lost her appetite. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is negative for cancer. The physical examination revealed mild jaundice, and the vital signs are stable. The laboratory results showed elevated liver enzymes, bilirubin, and CA19-9. The imaging studies revealed a hilar mass with a maximum diameter of 2.5 cm, and the biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma. The patient has Child-Pugh A liver function, and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the inclusion criteria. She has no history of biliary stent placement, distant metastases, or other malignancy type other than cholangiocarcinoma. She has no moderate to severe ascites, biliary perforation, or other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been suffering from osteoarthritis in her right knee for several years. She has tried various non-operative treatments but has found little relief. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical or surgical history. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a BMI of 30. Her knee deformity is mild, and there is no evidence of any other orthopedic or medical condition that would affect postoperative pain control. Her A1C is 6.2, and she has no history of seizures or allergic reactions to any medication. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent.

A 25-year-old female with Fitzpatrick skin type III comes to the clinic with mild to moderate acne on her face, chest, and back. She has been struggling with acne for a few years and has tried various over-the-counter treatments but has not seen significant improvement. She is otherwise healthy, does not smoke, and has no history of allergies or photosensitivity. She is not taking any medications and has not had any recent cosmetic procedures. She is willing to refrain from using any cosmeceutical agents or topical agents during the study and is able to comply with all follow-up requirements. She is interested in participating in the study to try out the photopneumatic system and improve her acne.

The patient is a 45-year-old female scheduled for an elective major abdominal surgery. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She does not have any history of lung disease or airway deformity. She has never used CPAP or oxygen therapy before. She is mentally competent and able to give informed consent.

35 yo male with a BMI of 27.5 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new form of once-weekly semaglutide. The patient has no significant medical history and is considered to be generally healthy based on the results of physical examination and clinical laboratory tests performed during the screening visit. The patient is not currently taking any prescription medications or herbal products and has not used any non-prescription drugs within 14 days prior to the day of screening. The patient does not abuse or intake alcohol or drugs and is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. The patient is willing to receive 7 once-weekly injections in total and attend 19 study visits with the study doctor. The patient understands that they may have to stop the study if the study doctor thinks that there are risks for their health.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the ICU due to severe metabolic acidemia with moderate acute kidney injury. He has a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2, and chronic kidney disease stage III. He has been experiencing worsening fatigue, nausea, and shortness of breath for the past week. Upon admission, his arterial blood gas showed a pH of 7.15, bicarbonate concentration of 18 mmol/l, and a PaCO2 of 42 mmHg. His creatinine level was elevated to 2.5 mg/dL. The patient was started on renal replacement therapy and mechanical ventilation. Despite these interventions, his acidemia persisted. The primary investigator of the study approached the patient's family and explained the possibility of including him in a clinical trial that investigates the use of sodium bicarbonate for the treatment of severe metabolic acidosis with moderate or severe acute kidney injury in the ICU. The family agreed to participate, and the patient was enrolled in the study. He is closely monitored by the medical team, and the investigators will administer sodium bicarbonate infusion titrated to maintain the pH equal or more than 7.30 according to the protocol. The goal is to determine whether sodium bicarbonate infusion can improve long-term survival of critically ill patients with severe metabolic acidemia and acute kidney injury. The patient is covered by public health insurance and provided informed consent for the study.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman who presents with a high fever, severe headache, joint pain, and rash. The symptoms have been ongoing for the past three days and have progressively worsened. The patient has no history of diabetes or tumors. The patient reports no recent travel outside of Guangzhou, China. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 39.5°C, a diffuse maculopapular rash on the trunk and extremities, and tenderness of the joints. Initial laboratory testing shows thrombocytopenia and leukopenia. Dengue virus NS1 antigen test is positive. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and will be evaluated for further treatment.

A 53-year-old female with a history of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) presented to the oncology clinic with complaints of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. She was diagnosed with low-grade NHL two years ago, and has undergone chemotherapy with rituximab and bendamustine with a partial response. However, her symptoms have returned and a biopsy confirmed a relapse of her disease. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80% and her bloodwork shows an absolute granulocyte count of 2,000/mm3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. She has adequate renal and hepatic function. She has not received any treatment for the past four weeks and has no other active medical problems. She is willing to participate in the expanded access study of Iodine I 131 Tositumomab (BEXXAR) therapeutic regimen for patients with relapsed or refractory low-grade or transformed low-grade non-Hodgkin's B-cell lymphoma.

A 42-year-old male patient with a history of primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) for the past 5 years is looking to participate in a clinical trial for a new treatment option. His platelet count has been consistently <30x10^9/L and he's been on various ITP therapies over the years. He has no other underlying medical conditions, no allergies to medication, and is not currently taking any immunosuppressants, biologics, or other therapies. He has not had any live vaccinations in the past 8 weeks and does not plan to have any during the study period. He has not had any gastrointestinal bleeding in the past 6 months and does not have a history of thrombosis. He is willing to comply with the washout period for any previous treatments before starting the study.

The patient is a 57-year-old Chinese man who experienced severe chest pain and shortness of breath while at rest. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but is otherwise healthy. He was rushed to the hospital and diagnosed with anterior STEMI. He has consented to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of intravenous metoprolol combined with remote ischemic post-conditioning (RIPC) in improving myocardial protection in Chinese patients with anterior STEMI. He is randomized to receive either metoprolol, RIPC, metoprolol & RIPC, or placebo treatment before reperfusion. His blood pressure is stable, and he is not in cardiogenic shock or experiencing heart failure symptoms. He has no known allergies to metoprolol and does not have a history of asthma or need for bronchodilators. His PR interval is normal, and his heart rate is within normal limits. He understands the study and has given informed consent to participate. The patient will be followed up for 1 year with office visits or telephone calls to assess his health status and any adverse events.

25 yo M university student who is a regular waterpipe smoker for the past 3 years, smoking approximately 3 times per week with friends. He reports no major health problems and has never smoked cigarettes. He is interested in participating in a study to investigate the effects of waterpipe smoking on pulmonary functions and oxidative stress parameters. He has signed the consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol. Past Medical History: - No significant medical history.

41-year-old female with a history of psoriasis and nail changes, including pitting, ridging, and discoloration, presented to the Rheumatological Clinic in Olsztyn with pain and stiffness in her fingers. A US examination revealed distal interphalangeal joint extensor tendon enthesopathy. She has not been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis or osteoarthritis of hands. The patient has been previously treated with topical corticosteroids and phototherapy for her nail psoriasis, but has not received systemic treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effect of methotrexate on the development of enthesopathy.

A 52-year-old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with complaints of fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance, and mild shortness of breath on exertion. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed and fried foods. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He has a BMI of 31 and a waist circumference of 104 cm. On examination, his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and his heart rate is 75 bpm. He has mild tenderness on palpation of his liver, and his laboratory workup shows elevated fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, triglycerides, and LDL cholesterol levels. He meets the criteria for the diagnosis of metabolic syndrome. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effects of glycine on atherosclerosis and metabolic syndrome-related parameters.

The patient is a 30-year-old Singaporean Indian male who presents with a BMI of 28. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not have any significant medical history and is not on any medications. His family history is positive for type 2 diabetes in his father and hypertension in his mother. He has no known allergies. He was born at term with a birth weight of 2.8 kg. The patient is interested in participating in the study to understand more about the influence of ethnicity on metabolic disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a cerebral aneurysm. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. She has no other significant medical history. She underwent a cerebral angiogram, which revealed a small aneurysm in the left middle cerebral artery. The patient was referred for potential pre-operative embolization. She has not had any previous surgeries or interventions related to her cerebral aneurysm. She has no known allergies or contraindications to iodinated contrast media. She is not pregnant and is not trying to get pregnant. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

32 yo F diagnosed with Crohn's disease 2 years ago after presenting to the ER with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She was initially treated with mesalamine and prednisone, but her symptoms persisted and she was started on anti-TNF therapy, which provided some relief but not complete remission. She has tried other immunomodulators, but has not responded to them. She has had multiple hospitalizations for disease flares, the most recent one being 2 months ago. She is currently on a stable dose of prednisone but has been unable to taper off due to persistent symptoms. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options and hopes to achieve complete remission. She is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and uses adequate contraception.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer six months ago. She has previously undergone one chemotherapy regimen and has shown progression of the disease. She has measurable disease and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance status of 1. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and she has no history of diabetes mellitus, chronic hepatitis, or HIV. She has not received prior treatment with epothilone, capecitabine, or docetaxel. She has not received radiation therapy that included 30% or more of major bone marrow-containing areas, and there is no evidence of brain or leptomeningeal metastases. The patient's current treatment with trastuzumab has been discontinued 28 days prior to study medication, and she is not on any other systemic treatment for cancer. She is not pregnant and uses an adequate method of contraception to avoid pregnancy throughout the study and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose of investigational products.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been experiencing episodes of sleep-related eating disorder (SRED) for the past 6 months. He reports waking up during the night and eating large amounts of food, often high in calories and fat, without any recollection of the events the next day. He has gained approximately 10 pounds during this time and feels embarrassed and ashamed about his behavior. He has no other known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to swallow capsules and follow instructions. He is not a night shift worker and has no history of kidney or liver disease. He has never taken Topiramate or Topamax for any condition.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years. He has a BMI of 42 and has been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea. Despite multiple attempts to lose weight through diet and exercise, he has not been successful in achieving sustained weight loss. He has been advised to undergo bariatric surgery and has been evaluated by a multidisciplinary team for eligibility. He has been deemed eligible and has agreed to participate in the study. He is

Patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has been admitted to the hospital for treatment of a severe respiratory infection. Due to the severity of his condition, the medical team recommends placement of a Power PICC line for intravenous access. The patient has no known allergies or past reactions to contrast material. He is able to provide informed consent for the procedure. His ECG shows normal sinus rhythm. His plasma creatinine level is within normal limits.

A 23-year-old woman who is 8 weeks pregnant seeks a surgical abortion due to her current living situation and financial instability. She has never had any surgical procedures before and is feeling anxious about the upcoming procedure. She reports having mild cramping and spotting, but no other significant health issues. She has never been diagnosed with a coagulopathy and is not taking any medications. She is fluent in Norwegian and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help other women seeking abortion. She is aware of the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to provide written consent. She is interested in receiving the best possible care during the procedure and is open to receiving medication that may help alleviate any pain or discomfort during the procedure.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and has been sober for the past six months. He is currently experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. He has been previously treated with medications, but they have not shown significant improvement. The patient is married and works as a construction worker. He has a BMI of 28 and is a smoker. His liver function tests show elevated levels of bilirubin and AST/ALT.
