The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and is willing to undergo the infusion of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells. The patient is willing to provide written consent and is in good overall health with no significant problems in other vital organs.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath for the past year. He was diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and has been treated with two different antiarrhythmic drugs without success. He has a history of sporadic episodes of persistent atrial fibrillation that were successfully cardioverted in the past. He has no history of congestive heart failure and his ejection fraction is normal. His left atrial diameter is within the normal range. He has not undergone any previous ablation procedure.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing persistent moderate to severe symptoms, including swelling and tenderness in at least 6 of her joints. She has been taking Methotrexate (MTX) at a stable dose (around 20 mg/week) for the last 6 months, but her symptoms have not improved significantly. Her hsCRP level is 8.0 mg/L at screening. She has not received any biologic DMARDs or other investigational drugs for RA. She has been taking NSAIDs for pain relief, but she stopped taking them 2 weeks ago as required by the study. She does not use high potency opioid analgesics. She does not have any other significant medical conditions, and her physical exam and lab studies are within normal limits. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements, including undergoing MRI assessments.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is planning to have a caesarean delivery due to breech presentation of the fetus. She is currently in her third trimester of pregnancy and has not experienced any severe psychiatric disorders or neurological diseases in the past. She does not have any current or previous somatic disease or malformations. Her pre-gestational BMI is 23, which is within the healthy weight range. She is fluent in Danish and has no visual or hearing impairments. She has not been exposed to radiation > 10 millisievert (mSv) within the last year and does not have any alcohol or drug abuse history. She is willing to participate in a longitudinal study that will investigate the relationship between sex hormones, stress-regulation, and serotonergic signaling in pregnant women and their risk for developing perinatal depression. The study will involve collecting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) at the latest point in pregnancy during the planned caesarean delivery, and follow-up visits across late pregnancy, delivery, and up to 6 months postpartum to evaluate changes in serotonergic tone, brain structure

Pt is a 82yo M, retired professor, with a history of hypertension well controlled on 1 medication, osteoporosis, and cataracts. He is seeking to participate in a research study focused on understanding the mechanisms that promote health and disease in the elderly population. He is able to understand and grant informed consent and is willing to comply with all protocol-specified procedures. He has not been previously enrolled in The Scripps Genebank Healthy Elderly Cohort. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any significant chronic conditions, including cancer, coronary artery disease, stroke, deep vein thrombosis, chronic renal disease, autoimmune or inflammatory conditions, Alzheimer's or Parkinson's disease, or diabetes. He is not currently taking any medications that would disqualify him from participation. He is excited to contribute to research that may benefit society and reduce medical costs.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has relapsed. He has undergone one chemotherapy regimen in the past, but it was not successful in eradicating the cancer. He is not eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation due to his age. The patient has a performance status of 2 on the ECOG Performance Scale. He is experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. The patient has measurable disease and adequate organ and bone marrow function. He is willing to use an adequate method of contraception for the duration of the study. The patient is available for periodic blood sampling and study-related assessments. He has not received any chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or biological therapy within the last 30 days. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trial within the last 30 days. He has not received any HDAC inhibitor in the past. The patient does not have active CNS lymphoma and/or lymphomatous meningitis. He does not have a primary central nervous system lymphoma. The patient does not have known hypersensitivity to the components of study drug or its analogs. He does not have known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the trial. The patient is not a regular user of any illicit drugs or substances. He does not have uncontrolled intercurrent illness or circumstances that could limit compliance with the study. The patient does not have a history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or lab abnormality that might confound the results of the study. He has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery or other procedures that might interfere with the absorption or swallowing of the study drugs. The patient does not have an active second malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer and carcinoma in situ of the cervix. He is HIV negative and does not have active hepatitis B or C.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has spread to her bones and liver. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past. She is currently experiencing mild bone pain and fatigue. Her biopsy results showed hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, and FGFR-altered advanced breast cancer. She is not currently taking any other medications except for occasional over-the-counter pain relievers. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score is 1. Her lab tests show an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,500/mm3, platelet count of 120,000/mm3, hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, total bilirubin level of 0.9 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels of 60 U/L, estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 60 mL/min, and normal calcium and phosphate levels. She has no history of corneal or retinal disorders, and her ophthalmologic examination was normal. She is willing to take sevelamer and follow a low-phosphate diet if needed. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old woman living in a rural village in Mayuge District, Uganda, came to the clinic for her annual check-up. She has never been screened for cervical cancer and is interested in learning more about it. She has two children and is currently not pregnant. She is not experiencing any symptoms related to cervical cancer. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help improve cervical cancer screening in her community. She has not had a hysterectomy and has not been treated for cervical cancer in the past. She is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 52 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with oligometastatic lung cancer. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and she is currently on medication for it. She has undergone a biopsy and histologically proven to have Stage I Non Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) with three or fewer lung metastases. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She is physically able to undergo all aspects of the treatment and is intellectually capable of completing questionnaires. The patient's ECOG performance status is between 0-2 and her body habitus enables Calypso tracking. She has undergone an MRI/4D-CT and has had Varian Calypso beacons placed in the lung. The tumour diameter is 5cm or less. The patient has not undergone high-dose thoracic radiotherapy and has at least two Calypso beacons implanted in the lung. She has not received cytotoxic chemotherapy within 3 weeks of commencement of treatment or concurrently with treatment. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating and is willing and able to complete quality of life questionnaires.

The patient is a 28-year-old female professional singer who has been performing for the past 5 years. She has noticed a decrease in her vocal performance recently and has been experiencing fatigue and hoarseness. She has no known laryngeal pathology and has not received vitamin B12 treatment for at least 4 weeks. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has completed and signed an informed consent form. She has never been diagnosed with vitamin B12 deficiency and does not have any bleeding disorders. She is not planning to start any new treatments or medications during the study period.

The patient is a 68-year-old man with a history of COPD. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chronic coughing for the last 10 years. He has been using a portable oxygen tank (E-cylinder) for the past year, which has been cumbersome, heavy, and difficult to carry around. He has difficulty with his daily activities and exercises due to the weight of the tank. He has been advised by his doctor to enroll in a clinical trial that compares a lightweight ambulatory oxygen device versus the standard portable E-cylinder device. He meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including having had no disease exacerbation within the 4 weeks prior to study entry, receiving long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT), and having a partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (PaO2) less than 60 torr. He is a former smoker, with no other significant medical history or comorbidities.

There are no eligibility criteria for this clinical trial, so a patient description is not necessary. However, it is important to note that the study is a population-based screening study, which means that it aims to recruit a diverse and representative sample of men and women aged 25 and older who are undergoing routine screening or testing involving a blood draw. The study will screen for transferrin saturation levels and will recruit potential 'case' participants with confirmed elevated transferrin saturation levels and matched random 'control' participants with confirmed non-elevated transferrin saturation levels. A random subgroup of approximately 20-40 percent of the participants will be genotyped for known variants related to iron metabolism and overload.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a chronic dry cough that has been ongoing for more than 6 months. She reports that the cough is worse at night and is not relieved by any over-the-counter cough suppressants. She denies any history of allergies, asthma, or smoking. She has been evaluated for gastroesophageal reflux disease, postnasal drip, and asthma, and all have been ruled out by a minimum of an 8-week trial of antacid therapy with a PPI given twice daily, an antihistamine and decongestant combination, and an inhaled steroid and a short-acting beta-agonist combination, respectively, with no improvement in cough. She has no other significant past medical history and takes no medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment for chronic cough of unknown cause.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with monochorionic twins. She was diagnosed with twin anemia-polycythemia sequence (TAPS) during her last ultrasound scan. Her obstetric history is unremarkable, and she has never had a multiple pregnancy before. She does not smoke or consume alcohol, and her prenatal screening tests were normal. She is currently at 25 weeks of gestation, and her twins are at TAPS stage 2. Her physician has recommended her to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of fetoscopic laser surgery in improving the outcome of TAPS twins. She is willing to participate in the trial and has given written informed consent. She does not have any known congenital abnormalities, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has recently undergone a prostate biopsy due to elevated PSA levels. The biopsy revealed non-metastatic cancer of the prostate gland with a Gleason score of 7. He has no history of other forms of cancer and has not undergone any previous systemic therapy for his prostate cancer. He is otherwise in good health and is able to comply with the study requirements.

As this is a clinical trial for a smartphone app aimed at DWI offenders and their concerned family members, there is no specific patient description required. The inclusion and exclusion criteria are based on meeting the specific requirements for participation in the trial, rather than any particular medical condition or health status.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic abdominal pain for over 6 months. She has previously been diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis on CT scan and ERCP. She has tried various pain medications including morphine, but the pain still persists and significantly affects her quality of life. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new treatment option that may provide better pain control and improve her overall well-being. She has no known allergies to local anesthetics and is willing to undergo an endoscopic ultrasound procedure. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable and she does not have any other medical conditions.

The patient is a premature infant born at 30 weeks gestational age and admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit at the University of Minnesota Masonic Children's Hospital. The infant is currently stable on room air and has not required respiratory support for at least 5 minutes. The parents of the infant have provided written consent within 1 week of admission to the NICU for participation in the study. The infant has no known congenital abnormalities or medical conditions that would prevent air displacement plethysmography (ADP) measurements.

A 30-year-old female patient presents to the Qasr Einy faculty of dentistry outpatient clinic complaining of hypersensitivity in her incisors, cuspids, bi-cuspids, and first molars on facial surfaces of her teeth. The patient reports experiencing pain (VAS score: 3 or greater) during application of stimulus such as airblast and tactile sensitivity test. She has a tooth with exposed root surface that is also hypersensitive. The patient has no chronic medical condition that requires the regular use of anti-inflammatory pain medications. She has not used or applied a desensitizing varnish within the last four weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and can provide informed consent.

A 63-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the nephrology clinic with a complaint of fatigue and weakness. Her medical history is significant for end-stage renal disease (ESRD), for which she has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 4 months. She is currently taking IV vitamin D sterols for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Her laboratory results show a mean bio-intact parathyroid hormone (biPTH) level of 130 pg/mL, a mean corrected serum calcium level of 8.9 mg/dL, and a mean serum phosphorus level of 5.5 mg/dL. The mean calcium phosphorus product is 48.5 mg²/dL. She has no history of parathyroidectomy in the last 12 weeks, no recent myocardial infarction, and is not currently enrolled in any other investigational device or drug trials. She is able to swallow tablets and agrees to use highly effective contraceptive measures throughout the study.

Patient is a 55-year-old male who presents with a 4-month history of progressive pain in the right side of his neck, difficulty swallowing, and hoarseness. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and drinks alcohol socially. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass on the right side of his neck, and he is diagnosed with metastatic or recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. His ECOG performance status is 1. Laboratory studies show no significant abnormalities. He has not received any palliative chemotherapy previously, and he has no history of peripheral neuropathy or hearing loss. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma in both eyes. Despite being on maximum tolerated medical therapy, his intraocular pressure (IOP) remains poorly controlled, with an average IOP of 24 mmHg in the right eye and 26 mmHg in the left eye. He has also undergone a previous laser trabeculoplasty that did not provide significant improvement in his IOP. His visual acuity is 20/25 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left eye. Slit lamp examination reveals open angles in both eyes and a well-formed anterior chamber. Gonioscopy shows grade 3 angles in both eyes. His optic nerve head appears healthy in both eyes with no evidence of glaucomatous damage. He has no history of other ocular or systemic diseases, and he is not taking any systemic steroids. He has been counseled on the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent to participate.

A 54-year-old male patient diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) presented to the nephrology clinic for hemodialysis treatment. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years, which is managed with medication. He has a BMI of 28 and a neck circumference of 42 cm. He has no history of snoring or sleep apnea. He is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. He has no history of craniofacial abnormalities. His lab results show a serum creatinine level of 3.5 mg/dL and a blood urea nitrogen level of 60 mg/dL. He has been referred for a kidney transplant and was advised to undergo hemodialysis. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial study and has given consent to participate.

A 35-year old software engineer is interested in maintaining a healthy lifestyle. He has a sedentary job and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He tries to go to the gym twice a week but finds it hard to maintain a regular routine. He lives with his wife and two children. He enjoys cooking and often prepares meals at home. He is not allergic to any food and doesn't follow any specific diet. He likes to track his physical activity and dietary intake using his smartphone. He is familiar with different health and fitness applications and is willing to try new ones. He is generally healthy, with no chronic medical conditions, and takes no medications. He is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve his health and wellbeing.

A 5-week-old male infant presents to the clinic with symptoms of colic. He was born at 39 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. He has been exclusively breastfed since birth and has been gaining weight appropriately. The mother reports that he cries for more than 3 hours a day, for more than 3 days a week, and that his crying is inconsolable. She has tried various soothing techniques, but nothing seems to work. The infant has no history of antibiotic treatment or probiotic supplementation, and there is no history of allergies in the family. The pediatrician has ruled out any chronic illness or gastrointestinal disorder in the infant. The infant is healthy and meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of Lactobacillus Reuteri DSM 17938 versus placebo in the treatment of infantile colic. The parent has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 2-hour-old neonate born at a low-income hospital in South India, weighing 2.1 kg with a gestational age of 38 weeks. The infant required resuscitation at birth and had a 5-minute Apgar score of 4. Clinical examination revealed signs of encephalopathy, including poor feeding, lethargy, and hypotonia. The infant's mother is a 29-year-old housewife who had an uneventful pregnancy and received routine antenatal care. She had no significant medical or surgical history and delivered vaginally without any complications. The infant's father is a 32-year-old construction worker who also has no significant medical history. The family lives in a rural area and has limited access to medical facilities. The parents have given informed consent for their infant to participate in the clinical trial, which will provide 72 hours of whole-body cooling using the Tecotherm-HELIX cooling equipment to improve the infant's neurological outcome. Temperature will be continuously monitored using a rectal probe connected to a digital data logger. The aim of the trial is to examine the efficacy of low-technology cooling equipment in administering effective and stable whole-body cooling in encephalopathic infants in low-income countries.

The patient is a 50-year-old individual who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes for over a year. Their most recent hemoglobin A1c level falls between 6.0% and 10%. The patient is not currently engaging in any physical activity or undertaking any regiment or lifestyle modification intervention. They are not taking exogenous insulin and do not have any cardiovascular or pulmonary diseases. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve their glucose tolerance and control, as well as their overall physical fitness.

6-year-old female with a history of atopic dermatitis (AD) and peanut allergy, as diagnosed using the Atopic Dermatitis Registry Network (ADRN) Standard Diagnostic Criteria. The patient has a self-reported history of a positive oral food challenge to peanut and a peanut skin prick test wheal ≥ 8 mm. The patient is currently experiencing active AD without a history or current manifestations of eczema herpeticum (EH). The patient's parent/guardian is able to understand and provide informed consent and the patient can provide assent as applicable per Institutional Review Board (IRB) guidelines and regulations. The patient has no history or current manifestations of any other skin disease other than AD that might compromise the stratum corneum barrier or any other concomitant illnesses. The patient has not received any biologics or investigational drugs within 5 half-lives (if known) or 16 weeks of the Screening Visit, and has not received immunotherapy within 12 months of the Screening Visit.

The patient is a 21-year-old female college student who is interested in improving her balance and postural control. She has never suffered from any musculoskeletal injuries and has no known balance disorders. She leads an active lifestyle, regularly engaging in fitness activities such as running, weightlifting, and yoga. She is excited to participate in this study to improve her balance and see how training on unstable surfaces can benefit her overall fitness.

A 42 year old woman came to the clinic for a routine mammogram that revealed an abnormality in her left breast. Upon further testing, she was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has no significant medical history and does not have any chronic illnesses or allergies. She is currently not on any medications. She is married and has two children. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She is nervous about the possibility of cancer spreading to her lymph nodes and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative staging methods. She is willing to undergo the proposed preoperative high-resolution axillary ultrasound, fine needle aspiration biopsy, and molecular analysis using real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently studying at a university. She has a body mass index of 22. She has no significant medical history and is in good health, as confirmed by medical history. She is not pregnant, nor is she lactating. She is of childbearing potential and agrees to use an adequate contraception method. She has reliable access to a consistent means of telephone contact and agrees to stay in contact with the study site for the duration of the study. She has never received an investigational product for the past 60 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer. She has not received any live attenuated vaccines in the last 4 weeks or inactive vaccines in the last 2 weeks before enrollment. She has no history of confirmed or suspected CHIKV infection, and has not lived in a CHIKV-endemic area for a cumulative stay of greater than 30 days in 5 years. She has no history of autoimmune disease or immunosuppressive condition, acquired or congenital, as determined by medical history and/or physical examination. She has no history of inflammatory arthritis, neurologic disorder, or chronic administration of an immunosuppressant or other immune modifying drug. She does not use antipyretic or analgesic medication on a daily or every other day basis. She has no acute illness at the time of enrollment. She has no significant disorder of coagulation requiring ongoing or intermittent treatment. She has no history of alcohol abuse or drug addiction. She has not donated blood or blood products > 450 mL within 30 days of dosing. She is not an employee or first degree relative of the Sponsor, CRO, or study site personnel.

56 yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and no prior history of stroke presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness, slurred speech, and facial droop. CT scan reveals a large vessel occlusion in the left MCA territory. The patient is ineligible for intravenous thrombolytic treatment due to recent surgery, but is a candidate for endovascular treatment. Baseline NIHSS score is 12, and the patient has no remarkable pre-stroke functional disability. The patient is able to provide informed consent. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Right hip replacement surgery 2 weeks prior - No history of prior stroke

45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and stage 4 chronic kidney disease. The patient is currently not taking any beta-blockers and has not participated in any drug trials in the past. The patient is able to provide informed consent and comply with the study protocol and procedures. The patient has no history of mental disability, asthma exacerbation with beta-blocker therapy, allograft organ transplantation, or electrocardiographic bundle branch block. The patient is not currently taking any medications that may interfere with the study. The patient is willing and able to undergo stress testing.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital when she was 9 years old. She completed treatment 18 years ago and has been enrolled in the St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study. She is currently experiencing difficulties with executive functioning, including difficulty with multitasking and organizing tasks. She reports that her symptoms interfere with her work and daily life activities. She has no history of head injury or other neurodevelopmental disorder. She is fluent in English and able to understand study instructions. She is not currently taking medication for her symptoms and has not participated in a past trial of neurostimulation. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any implanted medical devices or metal in her head. She is willing to commit to the study protocol, including completing home-based cognitive training and receiving transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) twice a week for 6 months.

72-year-old female with a history of primary gonarthrosis who underwent total knee replacement (TKA) one year ago. The patient reports stiffness in the operated knee and difficulty with daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. The patient denies any current or past history of Dupuytren's nodules or contractures in the hands or any other risk factors associated with fibrosis diathesis. The patient has not undergone any additional procedures to increase range of motion postoperatively. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the cause of knee stiffness and potential treatment options.

65 yo F with a history of osteoarthritis of the knee for the past 5 years with a pain intensity score of 7 on a 11-point numeric rating scale. The patient has been on stable analgesic medications for the past 3 months. She reports occasional breakthrough pain and has used acetaminophen for relief. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential new medication for her pain. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - GERD - Osteoarthritis of the knee - Depression treated with escitalopram 10mg daily - History of tobacco use, quit 10 years ago.

The patient is a 13-year-old boy who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia six months ago. He has completed his chemotherapy regimen and is now scheduled for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. He has no significant past medical history except for his cancer diagnosis. He is able to tolerate upper arm blood pressure inflation and is participating in the BMT Biorepository study (2012-1156). His systolic blood pressure is within normal range and there is no evidence of cardiomyopathy or congenital heart disease. His kidney function is normal and he does not have a central line in both upper extremities. His platelet count is within normal range and there is no known clotting disorder or hypercoagulability. He speaks fluent English.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness in her hands and knees for the past 6 months. She has noticed that her symptoms are worse in the morning and after prolonged periods of sitting. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers but has not found much relief. She has a history of hypothyroidism, for which she takes levothyroxine, and seasonal allergies, for which she takes loratadine. She has no history of hypertension, cardiovascular disorders or kidney disorders. She is interested in exploring alternative treatments for her arthritis and is willing to participate in a clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old Hispanic man with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension. He has been on hemodialysis three times a week for the past two years. The patient has reported feeling hopeless and sad for the past six months, with a noticeable change in his usual demeanor. He also experiences difficulty sleeping, loss of appetite, and decreased motivation to engage in activities he once enjoyed. The patient has a Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score of 35 and a Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) score of 42. The patient does not have a history of hospitalization in the last six months and is able to communicate fluently in Spanish. The patient has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

As this is a clinical trial for a mental health intervention, a patient description is not applicable. Instead, the study is recruiting participants who are either first-year undergraduate students or graduate students at the 5 Claremont Colleges or in the community and are 18 years or older. No specific medical history or health conditions are required for eligibility.

A 30-year-old male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He is generally healthy, with a BMI of 25. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. He is not taking any prescription or non-prescription medications, vitamins, or supplements. He has no history of drug or other allergies. His ECG showed a QTcB of 440 msec. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research.

A 60-year-old male with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, according to international criteria, is being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial on cognitive phenotypes in Parkinson's disease. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has not had any neurological co-morbidity and is currently taking Levodopa for Parkinson's disease. The patient reports mild cognitive difficulties, including slight mental slowing and mild executive dysfunction. The patient is fluent in English and is able to read and understand the information form for the trial. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trial or study in the past 30 days and is not currently being treated with deep brain stimulation. The patient does not have any metallic devices that could be incompatible with the study assessments.

A 56-year-old Caucasian man presented with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He had no history of structural heart disease, valvular heart disease, or heart failure. He had attempted anti-arrhythmic medication but had multiple recurrences of AF despite therapy. He was referred for catheter ablation of AF. He underwent the procedure, which was successful, and he was discharged home. He was scheduled for follow-up visits at 3, 6, and 12 months post-procedure. He agreed to participate in the DECAAF study and underwent a DE-MRI within 30 days prior to the ablation procedure to quantify the degree of atrial structural remodeling or fibrosis pre-ablation. Following ablation, DE-MRI was obtained at 3, 6, and 12 months follow-up to detect and quantify ablation-related scar formation. The institution where the ablation was performed continued post-procedural care following standard of care procedures. Atrial arrhythmia recurrences were catalogued up to one year post-ablation and predictors of recurrences of AF were determined by statistical analysis. The specific mechanism and electrophysiological characteristics of atrial arrhythmia recurrence were also analyzed. The patient did not have any contraindication for DE-MRI with a full dose of Gadolinium-based contrast agent and had no previous left atrial ablation or surgical procedure. He had a CrCl of 76 ml/min and had no contraindication for the study.

A 45-year-old man has been diagnosed with gallstones during a routine check-up. He has no symptoms or signs of acute or chronic cholecystitis, but his doctor has recommended an elective cholecystectomy. The patient has never had any abdominal surgeries before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to analyze the learning curve for a new dissection technique called "fundus first with ultrasonic tissue coagulation". He is willing to have video recordings of his surgery analyzed by independent surgeons and to have his intra and postoperative complication rate recorded in the Swedish registry of gallstone surgery and ERCP (GallRiks).

A 45-year-old female presents with joint pain, swelling, and stiffness in her hands and wrists, along with fatigue and low-grade fever. She has a family history of autoimmune diseases, including SLE. She has a positive ANA and RF test, indicating possible rheumatoid arthritis or SLE. She has never been diagnosed with either disease before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the possible correlation between DcR3 genetic polymorphisms, DcR3 expressions, and autoimmune phenotypes. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial as she has SLE symptoms.

52 year old woman with a medical history of hypertension requiring medication management for the past five years. Despite medication, her blood pressure readings have been consistently above 140/90 mmHg. She has some difficulty adhering to her medication regimen due to a busy work schedule and forgetfulness. She has access to a smartphone and is interested in learning about ways to improve her medication adherence and overall quality of life. She is able to swallow tablets without difficulty and has no history of cognitive impairment or insulin dependent diabetes.

45 y/o male with a history of type 2 diabetes diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient's HbA1C levels have been consistently high, currently at 9.5%. He has been taking oral antidiabetic drugs for the past 6 months, but his blood glucose levels are still not well controlled. The patient has never been treated with insulin before. He has no history of proliferate retinopathy or maculopathy. The patient has no known hypoglycemia unawareness or recurrent major hypoglycemia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of insulin detemir in controlling his blood glucose levels.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who received a kidney transplant 6 months ago due to end-stage renal disease. She is currently on immunosuppressive medication, including tacrolimus and mycophenolate mofetil. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She reports feeling well since her transplant but is concerned about her risk for infection and rejection. She has no history of opportunistic infections or rejection episodes. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the required protocol.

This is a 42-year-old female with a history of stage III melanoma of the right lower extremity. She initially underwent wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy with a negative sentinel node. She then received adjuvant high-dose interferon for one year. She was without evidence of disease for approximately two years when she developed recurrent melanoma in the same area of her right lower extremity. She then underwent a complete lymph node dissection with the removal of one positive lymph node in the groin. She was then treated with high-dose interleukin-2, but was unable to tolerate the therapy due to developing significant hypotension. She then received palliative radiation therapy to the right lower extremity. She has had stable disease for approximately one year, but has developed a new lesion on the right lower leg that has been biopsy-proven to be melanoma. She has no evidence of disease in the rest of her body.

A 6-year-old boy was brought to the clinic by his parents, who noticed that their son has been experiencing unusual fatigue, fever, and night sweats. After performing a series of tests, the doctor diagnosed the boy with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The boy has no prior history of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or steroid use. The doctor explained to the parents that their son is eligible for the Total Therapy XVII clinical trial, which aims to improve the cure rate and quality of life of children with ALL. The trial will use precision medicine strategies based on inherited and acquired leukemia-specific genomic features and targeted treatment approaches, including immunotherapeutic approaches such as CAR T-cell therapy or blinatumomab for refractory B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). The doctor explained that the treatment plan will be tailored to their son's risk group and cell type (T or B cell) and will consist of three main phases: Remission Induction, Consolidation, and Continuation. The parents gave their written informed consent for their son to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 56 year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) at stage 2 and has a creatinine clearance (CLCR) of 60 ml/min. He is currently taking metformin for diabetes, lisinopril for hypertension, and simvastatin for dyslipidemia. He has no other significant medical history, and his physical examination is unremarkable. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study, including medication administration and blood/urine sample collection.

A 40-year-old man who works as a manager in a high-pressure finance job is experiencing feelings of exhaustion, burnout, and anxiety. He has been struggling with these symptoms for several months, and they have started to impact his work performance and personal life. He has noticed that he is easily irritable, has difficulty sleeping, and feels overwhelmed by his work responsibilities. He has no history of psychiatric or medical conditions but has been experiencing high levels of stress at work due to increased workload and pressure from his superiors. He is interested in participating in an online therapy program and has access to a computer and the internet. He speaks Swedish fluently and is willing to commit to the program. He has not received any psychological treatment for stress-related difficulties in the past year.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has a chronic non-healing foot ulcer on the plantar surface of his right foot that has been present for more than 4 weeks. The ulcer has not responded to conventional therapy, including wound dressings, antibiotics, and offloading. The patient reports occasional pain and discomfort in the affected foot, but denies any signs of infection such as fever, chills, or malaise. His medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and peripheral neuropathy. He has no history of hematologic disorders or acute inflammatory disorders. He is not currently undergoing chemotherapy, nor is he pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is currently not pregnant and is not planning on becoming pregnant in the near future. She is sexually active and using a double barrier method for contraception. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, including herbal products. She has not donated blood or plasma within the past 56 days and has not used tobacco or nicotine products within the past 3 months. She has no history of celiac disease, food allergies, or vegetarian diets. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of VI-0521 on the pharmacokinetics of an oral contraceptive.

The patient is a 20-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester living in the Kisenso district of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She presents to the Maternité Esengo Health Center for antenatal care and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to prevent malaria during pregnancy. She understands the study requirements and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is not known to have any allergies to Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) or Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) and is not on any ongoing antibioprophylaxis with cotrimoxazole. She is not currently experiencing any issues requiring hospital admission and is not considered to be at high risk for pregnancy complications.

A 16-year-old high school student presents with complaints of difficulty falling asleep and waking up in the morning. She reports that she has been struggling with this problem for the past year and it is affecting her school performance and daily activities. She has a regular school attendance with a fixed start time, but she frequently stays up late at night and finds it hard to fall asleep before midnight. She usually wakes up around 9 am on weekends, which is an hour later than her usual school day wake time. She does not have any significant medical history or medication use. She denies any alcohol or nicotine use. She has normal color vision. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve her sleep using evening amber glasses and a stable wake time.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer) that cannot be treated with surgery. He has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy for liver cancer. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 due to mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort. His platelet count is 110,000/mm^3, and his absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 1,700/mm^3. His alkaline phosphate (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are both within the normal range. His bilirubin level is 1.5 mg/dl. He does not exhibit Child Pugh scale grade C cirrhosis. His serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dl. He underwent radiofrequency ablation for a liver tumor 3 months ago, but the tumor has continued to grow, and a biopsy is needed to confirm the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. He is not pregnant, and he is willing to use an accepted and effective method of contraception during the study. He has no history of untreated malignancy other than liver cancer. He is not allergic to boron, mannitol, or bortezomib. He does not have a history of untreated bleeding diathesis, international normalized ratio (INR) > 1.5 or Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) > 1.5 x institutional ULN. He does not have baseline peripheral neuropathy > grade 1. He is not on verapamil or any medication that interacts with doxorubicin.

A 42-year-old male with a history of Crohn's disease who presents with abdominal pain and tenderness, fever, and leukocytosis. CT scan reveals a complicated intra-abdominal infection with abscess formation. He has been on immunosuppressive therapy with azathioprine and prednisone for his Crohn's disease for the past year. He has no known allergies to any antibiotics. He has not received any systemic antibacterial therapy for cIAI within the 48 hours prior to the first dose of IV study drug therapy. The patient has not participated in any investigational drug or device study within 30 days of study entry. He is willing to use an approved method of contraception for the duration of the study treatment period.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee who has been experiencing chronic insomnia for more than 6 months. She reports having difficulty falling asleep at night, frequent awakenings, and difficulty returning to sleep. She rates her typical arthritic pain as 6 out of 10, which is impacting her ability to sleep and function during the day. She currently takes non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief. She is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine products. She drinks 1-2 cups of coffee a day. She has no significant medical history other than her osteoarthritis of the knee and her insomnia. She has never been diagnosed with any psychiatric disorders or substance abuse problems. She is willing to discontinue all use of centrally acting agents and analgesics within 24 hours of pain testing sessions and discontinue all use of the medications listed in #10 for two weeks prior to starting the study. She is willing to provide consent to contact her physician to establish the diagnosis and obtain medical record information. She is willing to undergo blood tests prior to receiving drug and understands that she will be excluded from further participation if she exhibits any abnormalities in the liver enzyme panel or tests positive for pregnancy or toxicology.

The patient is a 35-year-old Chinese Han male diagnosed with schizophrenia as confirmed by a physician. He has been experiencing symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and negative symptoms. The patient has a PANSS total score of at least 70 at baseline, making him eligible for the study. He is currently not using any antipsychotic medication and has not used seroquel or risperidone within the past 28 days. The patient has no history of substance or alcohol dependence and is not currently using any cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors or inducers. He has no medical conditions that would affect the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of the study treatment. The patient is able to understand and comply with the requirements of the study and has provided written informed consent. He does not have diabetes mellitus and his absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is above 1.5 x 109/L with normal ALT and AST values in the liver function test. The patient will be treated with either seroquel or risperidone for a duration of 6 weeks and will be evaluated using standard psychiatric rating scales such as PANSS, CGI, CDSS, AIMS, and SAS.

A 58-year-old female diagnosed with small cell lung cancer with extensive stage. She had already undergone first-line therapy with EP and second-line therapy with topotecan but experienced relapse within three months. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to take oral medication. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her hematologic and hepatic function levels are within normal range. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, epilepsy, bleeding tendency, thrombosis or embolism, severe uncured wounds or fractures, or dehydration. She has no other tumor within the past five years, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has the ability to understand and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no history of pelvic operations, pelvic inflammatory disease, endometriosis, or uterine fibroids. She is generally healthy and has a body mass index of 25. She does not smoke and is not taking any medications that could potentially affect pelvic blood flow. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of clomiphene citrate on uterine blood flow in women with unexplained delayed conception.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no history of adverse reactions to lipid-lowering agents or HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors. He weighs 70 kg and is currently not taking any medications. He has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse, and has no significant medical conditions. The patient is not lactating or of childbearing potential.

John is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has a history of hypertension that is managed with medications. He has not been diagnosed with diabetes, but his fasting glucose levels have been borderline high in the past. He is a retired accountant and enjoys playing golf and spending time with his family. He is scheduled to receive external beam radiation treatment with androgen deprivation therapy for curative treatment of his prostate cancer. John has a primary care provider who manages his hypertension and he is able to read and write English. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve his overall health and quality of life.

The patient is a 34-year-old female with a history of Crohn's disease diagnosed 8 years ago. She has been on maintenance therapy with mesalazine and infliximab for the past 2 years and is currently in remission with no symptoms. She has a high-stress job and tends to neglect her health due to work demands. She owns a smartphone and is familiar with its use. She has no history of mental illness or physical limitations that would prevent her from collecting a fecal sample and using the smartphone application. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of smoking for 30 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past two weeks. His chest X-ray reveals pleural effusion on the right side of the lung. He has no significant past medical history and no known allergies. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders or hypertension. He has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has undergone resection of the stomach due to gastric cancer. He is currently experiencing nutritional deficiencies and is at risk for malnutrition. His weight falls within the range of 60-75 kg. He has no history of diabetes mellitus, and his lipid metabolism is within normal range. His liver and kidney function tests are also normal. He has no known allergies to the ingredients in the trial product nutrient, and he is not currently undergoing chemotherapy. He has signed the confirmed consent letter to participate in the trial. He has no contraindications to fluid infusion and is not currently experiencing acute pulmonary edema, brain edema, or functional insufficiency of the heart. He has not received regular parenteral nutrition within 7 days prior to the trial.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with early invasive breast cancer. She has a BMI of 30 and no prior history of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery within the past 6 months. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes, but her family history reveals that her mother and grandmother both had type 2 diabetes. The patient has no other significant medical history or ongoing medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) two years ago. She has undergone two lines of chemotherapy, including rituximab and anthracycline, but unfortunately, she relapsed after both treatments. She also received autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) but presented with relapse within 12 months after the procedure. Her disease has progressed despite receiving targeted CD19 therapy, including CD19 CAR T cells. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, fever, and weight loss. Her ECOG performance status score is 1, and she has adequate organ function. She is eligible for leukapheresis assessment and preculture of T cells. She has measurable disease according to the "IWG Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma" and has provided written informed consent/assent. She is not pregnant or lactating, has no uncontrolled active infection, and does not require corticosteroid therapy.

A 56-year-old man with a history of metastatic renal cell carcinoma presents with fatigue, weight loss, and decreased appetite. He has undergone nephrectomy and has received prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease. Imaging shows multiple liver and lung metastases, as well as lymphadenopathy. His ECOG performance status is 1, and his laboratory workup is notable for elevated creatinine (1.8 mg/dL) and normal liver function tests. He has no history of brain metastases, bleeding diathesis, or coagulopathy. He has not undergone any major surgery, open biopsy, or radiation therapy within the past 4 weeks. The patient has not received any investigational agents within the past 4 weeks and is willing to comply with study procedures. He has no known hypersensitivity reactions to bevacizumab or sunitinib and is not on therapeutic doses of coumadin.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 5 years. She has been treated with methotrexate at a dose of 20mg/week for the past year, but has not responded adequately to treatment. She has also received treatment with one anti-TNF alpha agent, which did not provide significant relief of her symptoms. She reports experiencing moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness, particularly in her hands, wrists, and knees, which has significantly impacted her ability to perform daily activities and work. She has no history of serious infections or other medical conditions. She is currently a non-smoker and does not have a history of alcohol or substance abuse. She is eager to participate in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her condition.

62-year-old male with a history of smoking and COPD, who has been diagnosed with lung cancer in the left lung. The patient is scheduled to undergo thoracic surgery under left lower decubitus position, using a left-sided double lumen tube. The left main bronchus size is adequate for a 35Fr, 37 Fr, or 39 Fr double lumen tube. The patient has no dislocation or great movement of double lumen tube depth.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy woman who is currently using non-hormonal contraception methods. She has a regular menstrual cycle that lasts for 28 days with a variation of +/- 2 days. She is fluent in German and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no health-related issues that may affect her menstrual cycle and is not taking any medication or substances that may affect the menstrual cycle or any of the physiological parameters being investigated. She is not suffering from sleeping disorders and does not travel frequently across time zones. She is interested in participating in this study as she believes it will help her better understand her menstrual cycle and improve her overall health.

Patient is a 28-year-old female from the United States who was diagnosed with Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP) two years ago. She has undergone a colectomy with ileo-rectal anastomosis and currently has a few rectal polyps. She has a history of allergies but is not allergic to fish. Her past medical and drug history are unremarkable. She is not pregnant and does not have any plans to become pregnant during the study. Her BMI is 25, BP: 118/72, HR: 76/min. She is currently not taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but is taking a daily 75mg aspirin for cardioprotection.

Pt is a 50yo M with a recent diagnosis of stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx, who is scheduled to undergo surgical resection. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. Laboratory values within the past 14 days reveal WBC of 5.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count of 250 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 12.0 gm/dL, serum creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, and SGOT of 30 IU/L. Pt has not received any prior investigational therapy and has only received one prior chemotherapy regimen for systemic disease. He is able to provide written informed consent and has a negative pregnancy test (male patient). The patient is eligible for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with low risk Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS) six months ago. He has been under treatment with Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agent (ESA) but his disease has relapsed during the treatment, and he has become transfusion-dependent. He requires at least 4 units of Red Blood Cells (RBCs) over any 8 consecutive weeks, and his pretransfusion Hemoglobin (Hb) level is less than or equal to (<=) 9.0 grams per deciliter (g/dL). He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 due to fatigue and weakness from his MDS. He has no known allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to talacotuzumab and daratumumab or their excipients. He has not received any chemotherapy, immunomodulatory or immunosuppressive therapy, corticosteroids (greater than [>]30 milligram per day [mg/day] prednisone or equivalent) within 28 days prior to randomization. He also has not received other treatments for MDS within 28 days prior to first dose (example [eg], azacitidine, decitabine, lenalidomide, Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agent (ESA) (8 weeks for long-acting ESAs). He has no history of hematopoietic stem cell transplant. The patient has a Del(5q) karyotype, but he has failed with the treatment of lenalidomide. The source documentation for lenalidomide treatment failure has been verified by the sponsor. The patient has adequate iron stores, defined as transferrin saturation greater than 20 percent (%) and serum ferritin greater than 400 nanogram per Milliliter (ng/mL), measured within the screening period, or adequate iron stores as demonstrated by recent (within 12 weeks prior to first dose) bone marrow examination with iron stain.

28 year old female who has been unhappy with the appearance of her nose for several years. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history. She has not had any previous nasal surgeries or procedures. She has never been diagnosed with any cutaneous disorders or conditions that affect scarring. She is interested in undergoing primary open rhinoplasty surgery to improve the appearance of her nose. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old Russian man who had a recent acute myocardial infarction and was discharged from the hospital within the last 6 months. He resides permanently in Moscow and is seeking follow-up care at outpatient clinic №9. He has a confirmed discharge summary of his AMI. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily and amlodipine 5mg daily for his hypertension. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He has agreed to sign the informed consent form for the processing of his personal data.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who has had sexual intercourse with men and has had multiple sexual partners in the past 5 years. He has never been tested for HIV and is interested in participating in a study that can help improve our understanding of HIV infection in homosexual and bisexual men. The patient is willing to undergo regular study visits every 6 months, including interviews, specimen collection, and physical examinations. He has no history of injection drug use and is not perinatally infected with HIV.

A 15-year old high school student is being referred by her school counselor to a community health clinic in Flint, MI, for a routine check-up. She is active in various clubs, including the debate team and the student council, and enjoys playing basketball in her free time. She has never tried marijuana before and is committed to avoiding it. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings. The patient has a history of seasonal allergies and has had her appendix removed when she was eight. She is fluent in English and can provide informed assent. She has a good relationship with her parents and is comfortable discussing sensitive topics with them. She is willing to participate in the study and understands that her participation is voluntary.

The patient is a 66-year-old man who has a history of uncontrolled type 2 diabetes, obesity with a BMI of 38, chronic kidney failure and chronic heart failure. He was recently admitted to the Emergency Department with a large area of necrosis involving the perineal and perianal regions. He is currently experiencing severe pain and discomfort in the affected area, along with fever and chills. The patient is insulin-dependent for his diabetes and has been struggling to manage his blood sugar levels. Despite his chronic conditions, he is motivated to participate in clinical trials and follow the treatment plan recommended by his healthcare providers.

This is a 32-year-old male with a history of beta-thalassemia intermedia. He has been diagnosed with iron overload with a liver iron concentration of 7 mg Fe/g dw and a serum ferritin level of 450 ng/mL. He does not receive regular blood transfusions and has not received a transfusion in the past 6 months. He has no significant proteinuria and his creatinine clearance is above 40 ml/min, with a serum creatinine level within normal range. His ALT level is within the normal range. He does not have active hepatitis B or C or cirrhosis. He weighs 80 kg, which satisfies the weight requirement for dosing of 5 mg/kg with one tablet of 125 mg. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of deferasirox for non-transfusion dependent thalassemia.

The patient is a 52 year old male diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer with bone metastases. He has been undergoing radiation therapy for the past 4 weeks to manage the pain associated with bone metastases. The pain has reduced significantly since the start of radiation therapy. He is currently taking pain medications and a hormone therapy. He has no history of claustrophobia or any other psychological disorders. He has no surgical spine hardware at the region of interest. His medical history is significant for hypertension for which he is taking medication. He has no history of allergies or any other significant medical conditions. He is a retired engineer and spends most of his time reading and watching TV. He lives with his wife and has two grown-up children who live in a different state. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to undergo the MRI with the custom-built MRI coil for the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a known history of chronic heart failure. He has been experiencing worsening symptoms of dyspnea at rest and has been admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) within the last 48 hours. Despite receiving treatment with intravenous diuretics, vasodilators, and/or positive inotropic drugs, the patient's symptoms have not improved, and he remains in NYHA Class III or IV. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than or equal to 35% as assessed by echocardiography, radionuclide ventriculography, or contrast angiography within the last 12 months. The patient is able to provide written, signed, and dated informed consent or has a legally authorized representative who can do so. The patient has not undergone a cardiac resynchronization procedure within the last 30 days and is not expected to undergo such a procedure within the next 3 months. The patient has not received amrinone or milrinone within 24 hours before the start of the study drug infusion. The patient has not experienced a stroke or TIA within the last 3 months prior to randomization, and their systolic blood pressure is greater than 90 mmHg and heart rate is less than 120 bpm. The patient is not intubated or otherwise unable to comply with the pre-study assessments. The patient has no history of Torsades de Pointes, severe renal insufficiency, significant hepatic impairment, or a history of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or unstable bronchial asthma. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has not taken any Investigational Product or participated in any other clinical study within the last 4 weeks.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman from the United States who has been recently diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. She is scheduled for a partial mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection in two weeks. She has a past medical history of hypertension which is well controlled with amlodipine. She takes occasional ibuprofen for mild joint pain. Her BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. She has no known allergies or history of opioid use.

54-year-old male patient admitted to the medical/surgical ICU due to septic shock secondary to a urinary tract infection. The patient is currently mechanically ventilated and has been receiving enteral nutrition for the past five days. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. The patient's current weight is 85 kg with a BMI of 29.2. The patient's medical team is considering enrolling the patient in a retrospective study examining protein and energy intake in enterally fed critically ill patients before and after the introduction of a very high protein enteral nutrition formula. The study aims to assess whether the introduction of the new formula results in meeting protein targets in critically ill patients. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, making the patient a good candidate for enrollment.

45-year-old male with a BMI of 26 presented to the ER with signs of sepsis including high fever, elevated heart rate, and low blood pressure. He was diagnosed with a severe urinary tract infection and admitted to the ICU for treatment. He has a history of hypertension, well controlled on medication, and no other significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He has no known drug allergies. Laboratory tests revealed a low albumin level of 2.8 g/dL, indicating possible fluid overload. He has no history of seizures or liver disease, and his ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. He is not on dialysis, and his CrCl is above 60 mL/min. He is able to provide informed consent and is expected to survive for at least 7 days. He has no other conditions that may affect his adherence to the protocol.

63-year-old female admitted to the ICU with sepsis, hypotension, and acute kidney injury. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. She was admitted to the hospital with complaints of fever, chills, and shortness of breath. During her hospitalization, she developed septic shock and AKI, requiring initiation of CRRT with CVVH. The patient has a central venous catheter in place, and her hemodynamics are currently being supported with vasopressors. The patient is alert and oriented but appears fatigued. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds in the right lower lobe, and chest X-ray confirms the presence of a consolidation in the right lung. The patient has been started on broad-spectrum antibiotics for her sepsis. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and has no known exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 43-year-old female with a BMI of 38 kg/m2, who was diagnosed with DMII 4 years ago. She lives in a rural area and has limited access to healthcare services. She is currently on metformin and has struggled to control her blood sugar levels despite adhering to a strict diet and exercise regime. She has no history of myocardial infarction, thyroid disease, or renal dysfunction. Her current diet consists of high-calorie, high-carbohydrate meals, and she consumes alcohol occasionally. She is eager to participate in the study to improve her health, and is willing to follow the OPTIFAST dietary replacement intervention to achieve partial remission of her DMII. She understands the potential benefits and risks of the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a history of coronary artery disease and a family history of cardiovascular disease. He has been undergoing lipid therapy for the past 6 months and is medically stable. His apolipoprotein B level is greater than or equal to 120 mg/dL, and his LDL level is between 100 and 190 mg/dL without medication. The patient has no metallic implants or pacemaker and is medically able to undergo the MRI procedure. He does not have immediate plans for carotid endarterectomy and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His liver function test is normal, and the serum creatinine level is within the normal range. The patient has controlled high blood pressure, and the fasting glucose level is within the normal range. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of cholesterol-lowering medications in decreasing the fat content of atherosclerotic deposits in people with coronary artery disease or carotid artery disease.

56-year-old male with a history of ischemic heart disease, presenting with symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has been diagnosed with multi-lesion coronary artery disease and is being considered for coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The patient is willing to comply with the specified follow-up evaluations and has provided written informed consent approved by the appropriate Medical Ethics Committee. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and there are no contraindications to anti-platelet and/or anticoagulant therapy. The patient does not have any medical illness that may cause non-compliance with the protocol, confound the data interpretation, or is associated with a limited life expectancy. The patient is not currently participating in another investigational drug or device study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity. The patient is scheduled to receive induction chemotherapy with the cisplatin/fluorouracil (PF) regimen for at least two cycles of the same length, which will be a minimum of 14 days. The patient has been experiencing mouth pain during the first cycle of chemotherapy and has an OMDQ question 2 score of ≥ 2 during CT Cycle 1. The patient has a Karnofsky performance score of ≥ 60%, and laboratory assessments show that he meets all eligibility criteria. The patient has no history of radiation therapy to the head and neck, no active infectious disease excluding oral candidiasis, and no current use of antibiotic rinses or troches. The patient has no history of alcohol abuse syndrome or chronic immunosuppression. The patient is not seropositive for HIV or hepatitis B or C, and has not used any investigational agent within 30 days of signing informed consent. The patient is willing and able to understand and sign the study-specific Informed Consent Form (ICF) approved by the site's Institutional Review Board.

Patient is a 70-year-old woman diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease with a Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of 15. She has been experiencing clinically significant apathy for at least four weeks, with a frequency assessed by the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) as 'Very frequently'. The patient has a primary caregiver who spends more than ten hours a week with her and supervises her care, and is available to accompany her to study visits and participate in the study. The patient and caregiver are fluent in written and spoken English to participate in study visits, physical exams, and outcome assessments. The patient has not had any changes to AD medications within the month preceding randomization, and is not currently being treated with any antipsychotics. The patient does not meet criteria for Major Depressive Episode, and does not have clinically significant agitation, aggression, delusions, or hallucinations. She has not been treated with psychotropic medications in the 2 weeks prior to randomization, and is not currently being treated with medication contraindicated for concurrent use of methylphenidate. She does not have uncontrolled hypertension, symptomatic coronary artery disease, serious structural cardiac abnormalities, cardiomyopathy, serious heart rhythm abnormalities, or a family history of sudden death or death related to heart problems. The patient does not have glaucoma, pheochromocytoma, or known or suspected hypersensitivity to methylphenidate or its excipients. The patient does not have any CNS abnormalities or other vascular abnormalities such as vasculitis or pre-existing stroke, motor tics or a family history or diagnosis of Tourette's syndrome, seizures (convulsions, epilepsy), or abnormal EEGs. The patient does not have any condition that makes it medically inappropriate or risky for her to enroll in the trial.

A 35-year-old woman is concerned about the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles on her face. She is generally healthy, a non-smoker and not currently taking any medications. She has not had any recent cosmetic treatments or surgeries. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new laser treatment for wrinkles. She is willing to comply with all the requirements of the study, including biopsies, being photographed, following post-treatment care, and attending all treatment and follow-up visits. She is not pregnant, planning to get pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of keloids or compromised wound healing. She is not allergic to lidocaine or epinephrine.

The patient is a 55-year-old Latino woman diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer that has spread to other organs. She has undergone chemotherapy but it has not been effective in controlling the cancer. She experiences a lot of stress and difficulty communicating with her family about her illness. She speaks both English and Spanish fluently. She lives in New York and has a primary caregiver who is her daughter. She is willing to participate in the study and audio-recorded sessions. She has a score of 8 on the Blessed Orientation-Memory-Concentration Test (BOMC). Her oncologist has discussed her prognosis with her and her family. She does not have any history of substance use, dependence, schizophrenia, or bi-polar disorder.

The patient is a 10-month-old male infant who has been experiencing mild to moderate diaper rash for the past week. His mother reports that the rash appears red and irritated, but there are no open sores or blisters present. The infant's skin is otherwise healthy and he has no other medical conditions. He has not been on any topical or oral antibiotics or antifungals within the past 4 weeks, and his mother has not used any zinc-containing diaper rash creams within 48 hours of the first sample. The infant is not immunocompromised. The study aims to investigate the microbiome composition of his skin experiencing diaper rash in order to determine if the type of bacteria present influences the onset and severity of erythema associated with diaper rash.

The patient is a 23-year-old Caucasian woman who is planning to get pregnant. She has received at least one dose of CERVARIX in the past and is currently residing in the United States. She has no history of any chronic illness or any known allergies. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and is available for phone interviews. She has not received any investigational or non-registered product (drug or vaccine) during the study period. The patient's last menstrual period was 60 days after receiving the last dose of CERVARIX. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old woman presents with a history of HIV infection for the past 3 years. She has been taking antiretroviral therapy with lopinavir/ritonavir and Truvada for the past 2 years and has been stable with undetectable viral load since then. She is currently not using any form of hormonal contraception and has regular menstrual cycles. She is interested in using the DMPA injection as her preferred method of contraception but is concerned about the potential interaction between DMPA and her current antiretroviral therapy. She has no history of venous thromboembolism or any other medical or psychiatric illness that can interfere with her participation in the study. Her CD4 count is above 200 and she has been advised by her primary HIV care provider that she is eligible to receive LPV/r and Truvada.
