She is willing to use a barrier method of contraception during the study and for at least 56 days after completion of the study. She is not currently on HAART and is willing to delay HAART until week 12 of the study. She has no history of allergy to any of the study pharmaceuticals and has not been exposed to any investigational drug or placebo within 4 weeks of baseline.

The patient is a 35-year-old man with profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. He has difficulty communicating with others and has been using hearing aids for the past five years. Unfortunately, his hearing loss has progressed, and he is no longer benefiting from the hearing aids. He has been evaluated by an audiologist and found to have hearing thresholds of 90 dB in 250 Hz, 100 dB in 500 Hz, 1000 Hz, 2000 Hz, 3000 Hz, and 4000 Hz. He has been recommended to undergo cochlear implantation. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He does not have any developmental disabilities, and his ear anatomy is normal. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to preserve residual hearing after cochlear implantation using dexamethasone and hyaluronic acid.

A 56-year-old man presented to the clinic with a chronic cough and shortness of breath. He has a 30-year history of smoking cigarettes and has tried to quit several times but was unsuccessful. He was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and was staged as IIIA based on the TNM classification 7th edition. He is currently undergoing concomitant radio-chemotherapy, which includes dual therapy with platinum salts. He has signed the consent form and is affiliated with the social security scheme. He does not have any metallic implants or electronic medical devices that are incompatible with MRI. He does not have claustrophobia or severe renal insufficiency. His blood glucose levels are within normal limits.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a COVID-19 vaccine. He is currently working from home due to the pandemic and has been practicing social distancing and wearing a mask in public. He has no chronic health conditions and is not taking any medications. He is physically active and has a BMI of 25. He has not received any other vaccines in the past 28 days and has not been diagnosed with COVID-19. He is not planning to receive any other vaccines during the trial period. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. He is willing to use highly effective methods of birth control if he is a female of childbearing potential. He is available for clinical follow-up through the last planned visit and is expected to be compliant with protocol procedures.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who has been experiencing tremors in his left hand and foot for the past 6 months. He has also noticed a slight decrease in his sense of smell. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for Parkinson's disease or any other neurological disorders. On examination, there is a 2-3 Hz tremor in his left hand and foot, and his motor function is otherwise normal. The diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson's disease is made based on the MDS clinical diagnostic criteria for PD. The patient is drug-naïve and has not received any dopaminergic treatment for his condition. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of NR supplementation on Parkinson's disease symptoms.

Pt is a 62yo F admitted to the hospital for treatment of pneumonia. Upon admission, she was screened for nutritional risk using the NRS-2002 system and was found to have a total score of 4, indicating she is at nutritional risk. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and has lost 10 pounds in the past month due to poor appetite and difficulty eating. She reports feeling weak and fatigued, and has noticed a decline in her overall health. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or renal failure, and is able to understand and speak German fluently. Her expected hospital stay is 5 days, and she is otherwise stable.

A 55-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse presents with complaints of abdominal distension, fatigue, and occasional vomiting. He was diagnosed with cirrhosis and endoscopic examination revealed esophageal gastric varices. The patient's liver function tests were abnormal with elevated levels of AST, ALT, and bilirubin. The patient is currently not taking any vasoactive drugs or beta-blockers. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed written consent. The patient reports no history of previous surgical or endoscopic treatment for esophageal gastric varices, no hepatic encephalopathy or comatose status, and no gastro-renal vein shunt. The patient has no history of severe coagulation disorders or severe active bacterial infections. The patient has no history of severe cardiovascular disease or renal function insufficiency. The patient does not have any allergies to the trial medication and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

This clinical trial is seeking normal healthy subjects who are new to acupuncture and able to read Chinese with no communication barriers. Participants should not have any medical disorders, including neurological and psychological disorders, and should not have used medications that may affect the cardiovascular system within the past week. Additionally, individuals who experience painful or uncomfortable sensations in their upper and lower limbs should not participate in the study. If you meet these criteria and are interested in learning more about the physiological responses associated with deqi during acupuncture, you may be a suitable candidate for this study.

28-year-old Chinese female diagnosed with Bipolar II Disorder with a current depressive episode. She has a history of recurrent depressive episodes and was previously treated with a combination of lithium and quetiapine. She has been off medications for 2 weeks and has a HAMD score of 20. She has never received light therapy before and is willing to participate in this study. She has no significant medical illness and is not pregnant. She is able to provide informed consent and has no eye conditions that could be negatively affected by bright light. She reports no history of suicidal behavior or attempts.

52-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis and hypertension, currently taking lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She has been experiencing joint pain for the past year and was prescribed celecoxib by her rheumatologist. However, after starting celecoxib, she experienced severe gastrointestinal discomfort, including nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Her rheumatologist suspected that her adverse reactions could be due to a pharmacogenetic variation and referred her to participate in the clinical trial for pharmacogenetic testing. The patient provided informed consent and was enrolled in the study pharmacy. Pharmacogenetic testing was conducted to determine the hereditary component of her adverse reactions to celecoxib. The results of the testing will be used to develop a reliable standard of procedure for pharmacogenetic testing in the community pharmacy.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who presents to the clinic with a history of prostate cancer. He was initially diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago and underwent a radical prostatectomy followed by radiation therapy. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels were monitored closely post-surgery and were initially low but have been steadily rising over the past year. He was started on androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) with bilateral surgical castration but his PSA levels continued to rise. He was then started on enzalutamide, but his PSA levels have continued to rise, indicating the development of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). The patient has not received prior chemotherapy. His past medical and drug history are unremarkable. His BMI is 26, BP: 130/85, HR: 80/min. The patient is willing to participate in clinical trials and has been referred to this study.

A 35 year old woman who has lived in Washington state her entire life and has never worked as an agricultural worker is interested in participating in a clinical trial for delayed-type hypersensitivity to Coccidioides immitis. She has no history of coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis or blastomycosis and has not traveled for more than 30 days in designated areas of California, Arizona, Nevada, Utah, New Mexico, Texas and Mexico, Central and South America or for more than 7 days in restricted areas of California, Arizona and Texas. She has no active medical disease, does not abuse alcohol or drugs, has not had an influenza-like illness or immunizations in the past 4 weeks, and is not currently being treated with corticosteroids, cytotoxic or immunosuppressive drugs. She has no atopic or contact dermatitis, psoriasis, erythema nodosum, or urticaria and has not had a previous skin test with coccidioidin or SD Coccidioidin. She has no known adverse reaction to thimerosal, Candida, or Trichophyton skin test antigens. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have an immunodeficiency disease or HIV infection.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who recently noticed discoloration and thickening of her toenail. She has been experiencing mild discomfort and pain when wearing shoes. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is concerned about the appearance of her toenail and would like to participate in a clinical trial to find a potential solution. She is willing to abstain from the application of other topical medications or cosmetic products to the toenail during the trial and is willing to forego professional pedicures for the duration of the study. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate for the full duration of the study.

A 57-year-old male presented with a lump on the right side of his neck, which he noticed while shaving. The lump has been growing gradually over the past few months and has become painful. He also experiences difficulty in swallowing, especially solid foods. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and drinks alcohol regularly. A biopsy was performed which showed squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil. CT scan revealed a large mass in the right tonsil with metastasis to the right cervical lymph nodes. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is willing to undergo tumor biopsies. He is not on anticoagulation therapy and has never received prior cancer therapy or investigational agents for his head and neck cancer.

A 60-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the hospital with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia. The patient has been intubated and on mechanical ventilation for 72 hours. A suspicion of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) has been raised with a Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score modified ≥ 5. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria for duration of mechanical ventilation, suspicion of VAP with a high clinical pulmonary infection score, and informed consent. The patient has no history of statin use and is not receiving any medications that are contraindicated with simvastatin. The patient or his surrogate is committed to full support and is able to receive enteral study drug. The patient has no severe chronic liver disease and has not received cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, lopinavir, ritonavir, itraconazole, kétoconazole, érythromycine, clarithromycine, télithromycine, néfazodone, verapamil, or diltiazem. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of simvastatin in treating VAP.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who exercises at least twice a week and has a body mass index of 25 kg/m². She has no history of knee injuries or neuromuscular conditions affecting gait. She is interested in participating in a pilot study investigating the dose-response relationship between physiological load and blood biomarkers for articular cartilage. The study involves a 30-minute walking stress test under three loading conditions: A: 80%, B: 100% and C: 120% of her body weight. Blood samples will be taken before and after the walking test to measure changes in the biomarker concentration. She will need to attend three separate test days, each lasting 2.5 hours. She understands that this is a controlled randomized block design study and that all participants will perform the same three walking stress tests in random order. She is willing to undergo venipuncture for blood sample collection and understands that the serum will be separated and frozen for later analysis. She is excited to participate in the study and contribute to the understanding of the in vivo mechanobiology of human articular cartilage.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the hip joint. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her hip, making it difficult for her to walk or perform daily activities. She has no history of neurological disorders affecting motor function of the lower extremity, foot and ankle disorders limiting ambulation, bone metabolic disorders other than osteoporosis, or multi-systemic inflammatory arthritis. She has been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and physical therapy, but her condition has not improved. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if the new short, metaphyseal-fitting cementless anatomical femoral stem will provide her with major functional improvements and radiographically secure implant fixation.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) based upon the Revised NCI-sponsored Working Group guidelines for CLL. He had previously undergone chemotherapy treatment but has relapsed and is now refractory to the treatment. The patient has adequate renal and liver function with no significant abnormalities in his laboratory results. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work activities, such as office work or light housework. The patient has not received any systemic treatment regimens for CLL/SLL within the last four weeks, and it has been at least four weeks since the completion of any previous treatment regimen, including radiation and biologic therapies. The patient has a predicted life expectancy of at least 6 months. He is willing to give informed consent and to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with HIV infection. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history or allergies. He has been sexually active with multiple partners in the past, but always used condoms. He is currently not in a relationship and has not engaged in sexual activity for the past 3 months. He works as a software engineer and does not use any recreational drugs. His physical examination is normal, and his laboratory results show a CD4 count of 450 cells/mm3 and a viral load of 20,000 copies/mL. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance HIV research and potentially benefit from the novel 4-drug anti-HIV combination. He is willing to use a barrier method of birth control during the study and for 30 days after the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who participated in the New England Smoking Cessation and Reduction in Pregnancy Trial (SCRIPT). She is currently pregnant and in her second trimester. She reported smoking five cigarettes per day before becoming pregnant but quit smoking as soon as she found out she was pregnant. She is interested in participating in this study because she wants to ensure that her unborn child was not affected by her previous smoking habits. She is of Hispanic ethnicity, has completed high school education, and is married. She lives in a low-income household with her husband and two children. She has no history of medical or psychiatric problems. She is willing to provide urine samples for analysis of the 3-HC:C biomarker.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He has noticed a gradual worsening in his tremors, stiffness, and slowness of movement. He has been on levodopa/carbidopa for the past 3 years, but has noticed a decline in his cognitive function, including short-term memory and difficulty with executive functioning. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of liver, cardiovascular or renal disease. He is able to walk without assistance for at least 1 minute. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. He understands that he may withdraw his consent at any time. He has no known allergies to insulin and has no inflammation of the nasal cavity that may prevent absorption of insulin.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the emergency department with abdominal pain and fever. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. He reports having a dull, aching pain in his abdomen that started two days ago, and has been experiencing fever and chills. The patient's abdomen is tender and distended, and his bowel sounds are diminished. Blood tests show elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein levels. The patient is diagnosed with acute peritonitis and is scheduled for surgery. He has given oral consent to participate in the study. The patient is currently receiving vasopressor treatment.

A 14-year-old girl was diagnosed with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (SJIA) six months ago. She has a history of fever, rash, and joint pain for two weeks, which led to her diagnosis. She has been treated with anakinra, but she has not achieved complete remission. Her symptoms include daily fever spikes, rash, joint pain, and stiffness. Her parents are concerned about her growth since she has not grown much in height in the last year. She is not allergic to any medication, and her medical history is unremarkable. She is up to date with her immunizations, but she has not received any inactivated vaccines in the last three months. Her laboratory tests show elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) levels of 45 mg/L (normal range < 10 mg/L) and normal liver and kidney function tests. She is willing to discontinue anakinra and participate in this clinical trial to try canakinumab.

A 45 year old woman who has been experiencing lower back pain for the past 3 months decides to visit Jaseng Hospital of Korean medicine for treatment. She has no known medical conditions and is not on any medication. She lives with her family and has not travelled outside of the country recently. She wears a mask and practices social distancing as much as possible. She has not had any symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath. She is interested in the hospital's response strategy to prevent COVID-19 spread and is willing to participate in the satisfaction survey regarding its preventive measures during her visit.

A 50-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled to undergo radiation therapy as part of his treatment plan. He has no history of skin diseases such as psoriasis or eczema, and has not received topical or systemic chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks. He is in good overall health and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo blister induction and collection of blister fluid before and after radiation treatment. He has signed the informed consent form and is committed to complying with the study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been struggling with obesity for several years with a BMI of 38. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has not engaged in regular physical activity for a long time. She has a family history of breast cancer, and she is concerned about her risk of developing the disease. She has no active chronic illnesses or cognitive impairment, and she is a non-smoker. She is not currently taking any medications or hormone replacement therapy. She is interested in participating in a study to improve her health and reduce her risk of breast cancer. She is aware that the study involves aerobic exercise training and diet recommendations, which she is willing to follow. She hopes that the study will help her improve her insulin resistance, sex hormones, and depression.

53-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and recent myocardial infarction underwent cardiac surgery with pulmonary arterial catheter monitoring due to low cardiac output syndrome. The patient had a history of hypertension and was on antihypertensive medication but with occasional episodes of uncontrolled hypertension. The patient has no history of aortic regurgitation, circulatory or cardiac assistance, or active pacemaker. The patient is currently stable but needs to undergo monitoring for cardiac output and other parameters of cardiovascular function using the Niccomo device.

A 32-year-old healthy male presents for a Phase I clinical trial study. He has a BMI of 23.5 and a total body weight of 75 kg. He has no significant medical history and all laboratory values are within normal range. He is willing to use adequate contraception and not donate sperm from admission to clinical research center until 6 months post dosing. He has stopped all intermittent medications including over the counter, herbal, and nutriceuticals at least 14 days prior to admission to the clinical research center. He is willing to abstain from alcohol 48 hours prior to admission to the clinical research center and throughout the dosing and evaluation period. He has no significant physical incapacity and is negative

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a solid tumor. The tumor is located in her pancreas and is about 2 cm in size. She has not received any systemic or loco-regional treatment for the tumor in the last month. Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of [18F] fluoroazomycin arabinoside. Her body weight is 155 pounds, and her body mass index (BMI) is 27. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She will undergo PET-CT scans using [18F] fluoroazomycin arabinoside to help doctors plan better treatment for her solid tumor.

65-year-old Chinese male, retired factory worker, with a 30 pack-year history of smoking, presents to the respiratory department of a tier 2 hospital in China with a chronic cough and shortness of breath on exertion. He has no history of asthma, tuberculosis, or other respiratory illness. He reports occasional wheezing and chest tightness when exposed to dust and smoke. He is currently not on any medication and has no significant medical history, although he does have a family history of COPD. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. Pulmonary function tests confirm a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of less than 0.7 and a moderate reduction in FEV1. He is enrolled in the COPD group of the cohort study for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in China.

62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who suffered a left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke 4 months ago. He presented with severe right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The patient received tPA therapy and was admitted to the hospital for further management. Imaging revealed an infarct involving the left MCA territory. The patient underwent inpatient rehabilitation and was discharged to home with residual right-sided weakness and difficulty with fine motor tasks. He is currently receiving outpatient physical and occupational therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of navigation repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in stroke rehabilitation to potentially improve his motor function. He is able to walk independently and does not require assistance with activities of daily living.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer during a routine check-up. His oncologist has informed him that the cancer is incurable and that his life expectancy is estimated to be 6 months or more. The patient is feeling overwhelmed and anxious about the diagnosis and is experiencing intrusive thoughts and avoidance of trauma memories. He is worried about how this will affect his quality of life and his ability to cope. The patient's spouse is also experiencing significant distress and is finding it difficult to provide emotional support to her husband. The patient and his spouse are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to prevent post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in advanced cancer patients and their partners by using a neuroscience-based technique called the Memory Structuring Intervention (MSI) combined with vagal breathing. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria, including having an albumin level above 30g/liter, a WHO performance score of less than 3, and being covered by social insurance. The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including not having cerebral metastases and not suffering from a psychological vulnerability that might alter his judgment capacities.

60 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with typical intermittent claudication lasting for at least 3 months with no improvement. Treadmill test findings are consistent with this diagnosis. He has objective evidence of Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease with an Ankle brachial index measure (ABI) of 0.7 and systolic ankle pressure (AP) of 40 mmHg. He has patent femoral inflow above the level of injections recently documented with Doppler ultrasonography. He does not have any illnesses limiting his exercise capacity and does not have pain at rest. He has not previously been treated with any angiogenic growth factor. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to practice a medically accepted method of birth control. He does not have any serious concomitant medical conditions that are not adequately controlled and does not have any current alcohol or drug abuse.

The ideal patient for this clinical trial is a healthy male volunteer between the ages of 20 and 45 years old. He must weigh at least 50 kg and have a calculated body mass index (BMI) of between 18 and 29.9 kg/m². He must agree to use effective contraceptive methods and not provide sperm for up to 28 days after the administration of the clinical trial drug. He should be informed of the investigational nature of the study and voluntarily agree to participate.   The patient should not have a history or presence of a clinically significant and active cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatobiliary, renal, hematological, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immune, dermatologic, neurologic or psychiatric disorder. He should not have experienced symptoms indicating acute illness within 28 days prior to the first administration of the investigational product.   The patient should not have any medical history that may affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. He should not have genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactose dehydrogenase deficiency or glucose-galactose uptake disorder. Additionally, he should not have any clinically significant active chronic disease.

7-year-old male child with a history of recurrent tonsillitis and sleep-disordered breathing presents to the clinic for a scheduled tonsillectomy. The child has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. There is no history of asthma or atopic dermatitis. The child has not had any upper respiratory infections in the past 2 weeks. The child has no known cardiac disease, hypertension or diabetes mellitus. The patient's parents have given their informed consent for the child's participation in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is visiting the clinic for a routine medical check-up. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, malignancy, or severe renal or hepatic disease. The patient's resting blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and he is not taking any medications that might affect inflammation. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare the usefulness of 18 FDG-PET and MDCT in assessing the vascular inflammatory status and vulnerability.

63-year-old male diagnosed with inoperable locally advanced urothelial carcinoma with disease recurrence or progression during or after a platinum-based chemotherapy regimen. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) score of 1 with calculated creatinine clearance of 65 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula). No prior treatment with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 agent or with CTLA-4 receptor. No known hypersensitivity to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent. No known pia meningeal metastasis or active central nervous system (CNS) metastasis revealed by CT or MRI. Asymptomatic brain metastases for at least 1 month.

A 32-year-old male patient presents with a history of chronic nasal obstruction and recurrent episodes of nasal discharge for the past 2 years. He complains of a whistling sound while breathing from the nose. The patient reports a history of previous nasal surgery, which has not provided any relief for his symptoms. On examination, the patient has a nasal septum perforation with an area less than 1 cm². The patient has no history of genetic diseases, tuberculosis, nasal cancer, drug abuse, or mental illness. He is not currently taking any medication, and he has no history of autoimmune diseases or corticosteroid use. The patient is willing and able to attend regular visits to the hospital and follow the protocol procedures. The patient is a suitable candidate for the study and may benefit from the collagen membrane combined with human clinical grade umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells transplantation.

A 25-year-old student complains of a headache, pressure sensation in the forehead and cheeks, stuffy nose and an overall feeling of fatigue. She reports the symptoms started two days ago and have been worsening. She has no history of allergies or chronic sinusitis. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is not currently taking any medications. She has never used Ectoin® Rhinitis Nasal Spray or Sinupret forte before. She is able to understand and comply with the study's requirements and willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been referred for a CT scan due to persistent abdominal pain. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to medications and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has a history of hypothyroidism, but it is under control with medication. She has normal renal function and no current local infections or bacteremia.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a BMI of 34. He has been obese for the past 10 years and has tried several weight loss programs without success. He is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. He has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a diet high in fat and sugar. He reports feeling depressed and anxious, and has a family history of depression. He has no history of substance abuse or smoking. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the neurohormonal and behavioral correlates of obesity and weight loss. He is able and willing to provide written informed consent for the trial.

A 35-year-old male patient was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a pelvic fracture. The patient underwent surgical stabilization with SI screws at Shock Trauma. Six months post-surgery, the patient is still experiencing pain associated with the pelvic fracture and is taking narcotics for pain management. The patient is English-speaking and is able to understand the study requirements. The patient has skeletal maturity and his surgeon agrees to randomization. The patient is able to attend orthopaedic follow-up appointments for the next 12 months. The patient has no history of spinal cord injury and is ambulatory. The patient is not currently pregnant and is not enrolled in any other studies that prohibit co-enrollment.

Part 2: The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from atopic dermatitis for the past 10 years. She experiences severe itching and redness on her forearms and antecubital fossa. She has a history of asthma and hay fever and has had generally dry skin in the past year. She has never been diagnosed with any other skin conditions. She is currently not on any topical prescription treatment for eczema and has not received any systemic treatment or phototherapy in the last 6 months. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using highly effective contraception. She is excited to try the new treatment and hopeful that it will provide relief from her symptoms.

A 28-year-old Hispanic woman came to the clinic seeking treatment for her alcohol use disorder. She reports drinking every day for the past six months, with an average of six drinks per day. She has tried to quit drinking on her own but has been unsuccessful. She speaks Spanish as her primary language and prefers to communicate in Spanish. She is willing to commit to 8 weeks of treatment and follow-up. She has no untreated bipolar or schizophrenic disorder and no current legal case pending. She does not meet DSM-5 criteria for another current substance use disorder.

A 48-year-old Arab male with type 2 diabetes mellitus, who presents to the ophthalmology clinic with visual impairment in his right eye. He reports a gradual loss of vision over the past few months, which has been affecting his work as a salesman. The patient has a history of poor glycemic control, with a HbA1c of 9% on his last follow-up. On examination, the patient has a BCVA of 20/50 in his right eye and central macular edema is confirmed by OCT imaging. The patient has no history of glaucoma or previous treatment with AVEGF injection. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of aflibercept versus ranibizumab in the management of DME.

A 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of high grade (G3) advanced Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor. The tumor is unresectable locally advanced or distant metastatic, with a Ki-67 proliferative index of over 20%, according to WHO 2010 classification. The patient has undergone first-line systematic chemotherapy but has shown progression. The patient has at least one measurable nidus as per RECIST1.1 criteria. The patient has normal organ function, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-1, and a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient is willing to sign informed consent and is using an adequate method of contraception. The patient does not have any severe or uncontrolled diseases or any record of arterial or venous thromboembolic events in the last six months. The patient has not participated in any other anticancer drug clinical trials within the last four weeks, and does not have any history of immunodeficiency or drug abuse.

A 25-year-old Swazi woman visited the clinic to get tested for HIV as part of a routine check-up. She is currently single and uses condoms inconsistently. She is sexually active with multiple partners and reports that she has never been tested for HIV before. She has a BMI of 23 and has no history of any chronic illness. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is not on any medication. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 4 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is unremarkable.

40-year-old male who has been experiencing pain at the medial attachment of fascia plantaris for the past 6 months. He reports experiencing first step pain in the morning and finds it difficult to stand or walk for prolonged periods of time due to the pain. He has not received any treatment for this condition previously. The patient is generally healthy and does not have any known arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, or psoriasis. Upon ultrasound scanning, the thickness of the fascia is above 4 mm. The patient is able to read and understand Danish. He is willing to try physical training, glucocorticoid injections, or a combination thereof to help alleviate his symptoms. He is not currently taking any pain medication and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

A 55-year-old woman was referred to the gastroenterology clinic for a screening colonoscopy. She has a family history of colon cancer, and she has never had a colonoscopy before. She is anxious about the procedure and is concerned about pain and discomfort during the examination. She works as a teacher and has a busy schedule, which adds to her stress levels. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is fluent in English and has no hearing impairment. She has agreed to participate in the study and is interested in using music to help her relax during the procedure. She will choose her own music to listen to during the colonoscopy.

56 year old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C and alcohol abuse. The patient presents with symptoms of jaundice, abdominal pain, and pruritus. After imaging studies, a tissular biliary lesion is detected with suspicion of malignancy. The patient is referred to the gastroenterology division of the Ecuadorian Institute of Digestive Diseases (IECED) at OmniHospital Academic Tertiary Center for further evaluation. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs an informed consent. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial as they have a tissular biliary lesion detected by POCS. The patient does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. The patient will undergo cholangioscopy using the SpyGlass® System in order to diagnose and classify the biliary lesion. Biopsies will be taken to confirm the diagnosis and to correlate with the classification system. The patient will be followed up for 6 months with POCS to confirm the diagnosis and to monitor for any changes in the lesion.

A 51-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes was recently diagnosed with stage 4 chronic kidney disease. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is between 15 and 30 ml/min, and his plasma bicarbonate concentration is 18 meq/L. He takes metformin and insulin to manage his diabetes and lisinopril to control his blood pressure, which is within normal range. He doesn't smoke and doesn't consume alcohol. He is currently not taking any sodium bicarbonate supplementation and has not used it in the last month. He has no history of heart failure, liver cirrhosis, or kidney transplant. He is willing to participate in the study and has no history of non-adherence to medication.

The patient is a 19-year-old male who is currently a part of the Lille Rowing Hope Pole. He has been training at the Centre de Ressources, d'Expertise et de Performance Sportive (CREPS) de Wattignies for the past few months. He has a healthy dental status with at least 28 natural teeth in occlusion. He does not have any current or past neurological, ear nose and throat, ophthalmological, or orthopedic issues that may affect his balance. He does not have any temporomandibular joint disorders, orofacial symptoms, or chronic pain. He is not currently undergoing any dental or periodontal care. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not consumed alcohol in the past 24 hours and is willing to give informed written consent to participate in the study. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and is not currently participating in any other study.

60 year-old male scheduled for robotic-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy. No significant past medical or surgical history. He has a body mass index of 24 kg/m2 and is classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists class II. No previous history of neurological deficit, psychiatric diseases, alcoholism or drug dependence, serious hearing or visual impairment, or any other serious medical conditions. He is able to comprehend and sign an informed consent form, and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy 35-year-old woman who has no history of major illnesses or surgeries. She has a BMI of 22.4 kg/m^2 and is a non-smoker. She has not previously participated in any clinical trials involving investigational drugs, devices, or off-label use of approved drugs. She is not currently taking any medication for a medical condition that is not compatible with the inclusion criteria, and is willing to abstain from salt-substitutes containing potassium for the duration of the study. She has normal clinical laboratory test results and serum potassium levels within the normal range. She is willing to use two medically accepted methods of contraception with all sexual partners during the study and for 90 days following the final dosing, as she is a sexually active female. She has given written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures and is reliable and willing to make herself available for the duration of the study, and to follow site-specific study procedures. She is willing to comply with the use of an electronic data capture system. She has not donated blood of more than 50 mL within the last 60 days, and does not consume natural licorice and/or natural licorice-containing products and/or grapefruit and/or grapefruit juice within 7 days of first dosing and/or anticipated consumption during the study.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 4 months ago. The patient has a history of joint pain and stiffness in the hands and feet for the past 2 years, which intensified over the last few months. The patient has not been treated with any biologic therapy. The patient has 8 swollen and painful joints out of 66 and 12 tender joints out of 68 assessed. She has not been treated with methotrexate. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no other significant medical history. The patient is a married housewife with 2 children. She is not pregnant and is using an IUD for contraception. She is willing and able to self-administer subcutaneous injections. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has no known allergies to medications.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer. She has received prior endocrine therapy for metastatic disease and has progressed on at least one line of endocrine therapy. The patient is considered an appropriate candidate for chemotherapy. She has undergone a biopsy for her cancer and has PD-L1-positive breast cancer, defined as 10 or greater expression of PD-L1 on the combined positive score (CPS) including both tumor and immune cells determined by central testing of a fresh or archival tumor biopsy with the PD-L1 immunohistochemistry 22C3 assay. She has evaluable or measurable disease per RECIST 1.1. She will need to undergo at least two research biopsies, paired research stool collections, and study treatment including evaluations and follow-up visits. The patient will be randomized into one of two groups: Group A will receive Sacituzumab Govitecan and Pembrolizumab, while Group B will receive Pembrolizumab alone. Prior chemotherapy must have been discontinued ≥14 days prior to initiation of study therapy. Prior biologic therapy must have been discontinued at least 28 days prior to study treatment initiation, and all toxicities related

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was diagnosed with breast cancer and confirmed metastasis between July 1st, 2010 and June 30th, 2011. She has been managed for her disease at the same setting where the final diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer was performed. She has no history of concurrent or other primary malignancies, except for curatively resected non-melanoma skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer. The patient's medical records will be reviewed retrospectively as part of a multicenter, national chart-review study on the epidemiology and therapeutic management of metastatic breast cancer in Romania. The purpose of the study is to provide an accurate, evidence-based description of the incidence of progression of metastatic breast cancer and its clinical management.

The patient is a 45 year old woman complaining of chronic pelvic pain and pain in the buttocks and thighs for the past 2 years. The pain is described as burning, stabbing and aching in nature and is aggravated by sitting, walking and sexual activity. She has tried various medications and physical therapy without significant improvement. She has no history of trauma or surgery in the pelvic or gluteal region. On physical examination, there is tenderness in the perineal and gluteal region. The patient meets the criteria for pudendalgie and clunealgie according to the 5 Nantes criteria and is a candidate for transgluteal surgical treatment. She has no history of medical conditions that would exclude her from the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy female with no prior history of pulmonary or cardiac diseases. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. She is an American Society Anesthesia physical status I. The patient is interested in participating in a research study on the effect of positive pressure ventilation and body positioning on volumetric capnography. She is willing to undergo the protocol, which includes spontaneous, pressure support, and control pressure ventilation using a tight nasal mask. The patient understands that the study will involve continuous recording of volumetric capnography and electrical impedance tomography (EIT) during the protocol. She is comfortable with the different body positions that will be randomly tested. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and has no abnormal spirometry results.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who wears contact lenses on a regular basis. She has a spherical prescription of -3.00D in both eyes and a spectacle cylindrical correction of -0.50D in each eye. Her visual acuity with her current contact lenses is adequate for her daily activities. She does not have any ocular or systemic disorders that would contraindicate contact lens wear, and she is not currently using any topical medication for her eyes. She has not had any eye surgeries in the past and does not have any corneal distortions from previous hard or rigid lens wear. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not participated in any other contact lens or care solution clinical trial or research within the past two weeks. She is willing and able to follow the study protocol and understands her rights as a research subject.

A 57-year-old female patient was diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She has already undergone first line chemotherapy but her disease has progressed. She experiences severe pain, fatigue, and loss of appetite. She has been referred to a clinical trial that investigates the effect of early palliative care on the quality of life of patients with advanced cancer. She is eligible for the trial as she has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and is able to read and respond to questions in Dutch. She has no history of cognitive impairment and has not met the palliative support team more than once or had a consultation within 6 months of inclusion. She is willing to participate in the trial and has signed an informed consent form.

A 40 yo female with a history of chronic pancreatitis and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, confirmed by a fecal elastase test with a level of 90 mcg/g of stool. She experiences frequent abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea. She has been taking pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy but still experiences symptoms. She has no history of alcohol abuse, drug abuse, or excessive alcohol consumption. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has no known allergies to pork protein and is willing to ingest pork products. She has no history of pancreatic cancer or any other malignancies, no history of viral hepatitis or HIV infection, and no other acute or chronic diseases that could influence the study results or pose a risk to her safety.

32-year-old female diagnosed with OCD (based on DSM-IV criteria) with a primary symptom of checking. She has been unmedicated for the past 3 months and her Y-BOCS score is currently 20. She has no history of major head trauma or psychosurgery and does not have any active substance abuse. She does not have a seizure disorder or any other significant neurological disorder. She is not currently experiencing active suicidality and is not pregnant. She does not have severe claustrophobia, ferromagnetic metal in her body, a pacemaker or defibrillator, or any other condition that would make MRI scanning unsafe or inappropriate. She is not currently undergoing cognitive/behavioral therapy and has not initiated any such therapy within the last 3 months.

48-year-old male with a history of hypertension and occasional chest discomfort presents to the cardiologist's office for evaluation. The patient reports occasional shortness of breath with exertion but denies any episodes of syncope or palpitations. A stress test is ordered, which reveals evidence of inducible ischemia. A coronary angiogram is performed which confirms the diagnosis of stable coronary artery disease. The patient is deemed eligible for medication therapy or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The cardiologist discusses the risks and benefits of both treatment options with the patient but is uncertain if the patient fully understands the information given to him. The patient is approached by the clinical trial specialist to participate in a pilot randomized trial of a decision aid for patients with stable coronary artery disease. The patient agrees to participate in the trial and is scheduled for follow-up survey 3 months after treatment decision.

Patient is a 48-year-old female with a biopsy-confirmed diagnosis of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the left breast. Mammography and CE-MRI imaging have shown DCIS measuring greater than or equal to 4cm. The patient desires breast-conserving therapy and is interested in participating in the clinical trial for Targeted Intra-Operative Radiotherapy for the Management of Ductal Carcinoma In-Situ of the Breast. The patient has no evidence of microinvasion or invasive carcinoma on imaging or core biopsy of the breast or axillary nodes. The patient has no history of collagen vascular diseases, serious psychiatric or addictive disorders, and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty with balance and has fallen several times in the past year. He has a history of cataract surgery in both eyes and wears glasses for corrected vision. His visual acuity is 20/50 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. He has no visual field loss and normal color vision. He has no history of sleep disorders or dementia, and his overall health is stable. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illegal drugs. He does not take any prescription medications on an acute or as-needed basis that could alter his sleep-wake cycle. He reports no history of nocturia. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the possibility of improving his balance while not impacting his sleep patterns.

A 3-year old girl named Sofia is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial about the spread and susceptibility of Streptococcus pneumoniae in healthy children aged less than 5 years in the area of Milan and surroundings, Lombardy, Italy. Sofia is in good health and lives with her parents and older brother. She attends daycare three times a week and has had no recent history of antibiotic use. Sofia is up to date with her vaccinations, including the pneumococcal vaccine. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has not been hospitalized in the past year. Sofia's parents are willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent for their daughter's involvement.

A 45-year-old Hispanic woman with a history of recurrent abdominal pain and bloating was referred to the Endoscopy Unit of Hospital Clinic of Barcelona for an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. She reported occasional heartburn and regurgitation but denied any dysphagia or weight loss. She has never been diagnosed with Helicobacter pylori (Hp) infection before and has not taken any antibiotics or proton-pump inhibitors in the past 4 weeks. Physical examination was unremarkable. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy will be performed with high definition endoscopes (Olympus, Germany) without magnification by three endoscopists. After the routine examination of the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum, the presence of a regular or irregular arrangement of collecting venules will be evaluated in real-time during gastric exploration in the lower part of the lesser curvature of the gastric body with good insufflation, close to the incisura angularis. If minute red points were visible regularly and homogenously, the finding will be scored as RAC positive (RAC+). If this finding was absent or there was a patchy distribution at the site of close observation, it will be defined as RAC negative (RAC-). Hp infection status will be determined by mucosal biopsies. The patient is not taking any antithrombotic or anticoagulant medications and has no history of Hp eradication. She has not been diagnosed with any significant endoscopic findings in the past. She has agreed to participate in the study and has met all inclusion criteria.

A 65-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of recurrent infections, fatigue, and weight loss. Further work-up showed an M-spike in his serum protein electrophoresis, and bone marrow biopsy revealed 10% plasma cells, consistent with the diagnosis of MGUS. He is a retired engineer with a BMI of 33 and has a history of snoring and daytime sleepiness. His sleep study showed moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. He is not currently receiving any treatment for his MGUS and has never been treated for sleep apnea. He is interested in participating in a study that investigates the relationship between sleep apnea and plasma cell dyscrasia.

A 30-year-old female with no significant medical history, BMI of 22 kg/m2, and a total body weight of 60 kg. She has not had any recent upper or lower respiratory tract infections, and has tested negative for Human Immunodeficiency Virus, Hepatitis A, B and C. The patient has no abnormalities in lung function, nose or nasopharynx. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of RV521 against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV).

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of leukemia who was admitted to the hospital due to a fever of unknown origin. He has been receiving chemotherapy for the past 3 months and is currently neutropenic. Blood cultures were drawn and grew Candida albicans, indicating a possible candidemia. The patient is currently receiving antifungal therapy and will be enrolled in the clinical trial to test the newly developed biosensor for fungal detection. The patient will be one of 15 participants and will have blood samples drawn to be tested with the (FUNGDETECT) sensor to determine its efficacy in detecting and quantifying fungal cells in human blood samples. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks involved.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who suffered a left hemisphere stroke 9 months ago. He has since experienced difficulty with language processing, particularly word retrieval. He is a native English speaker with adequate hearing and vision to complete the tasks. The patient has no history of neurological disease or major mental illness. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has not undergone any previous tDCS or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) procedures.

This is a 45 year-old female who has been experiencing moderate to severe dry eye symptoms for the past year. She has been using artificial tears to alleviate the discomfort, but finds that they only provide temporary relief. She has a history of contact lens use, but has stopped wearing them due to the discomfort they cause. She reports feeling a constant burning sensation in her eyes, as well as occasional blurred vision. She has tried other treatments in the past, including cyclosporine, but did not find them to be effective. Her corrected visual acuity is 20/20, but she has a Schirmer's test result of 8mm/5min in her right eye and 6mm/5min in her left eye, with a TBUT of 8 seconds. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and is excited to potentially find a long-term solution to her dry eye symptoms.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman in her third trimester of pregnancy with an uncomplicated singleton pregnancy. She has been experiencing snoring and occasional pauses in her breathing while sleeping, and has reported feeling more tired during the day. She has no history of chronic medical conditions or complications during her pregnancy. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the potential risks of sleep disordered breathing during pregnancy on the developing fetus and newborn infant. She is willing to complete a sleep questionnaire and undergo an overnight polysomnography if necessary. She understands that her placenta and umbilical cord blood will be collected and analyzed after delivery, and that her newborn will undergo a neuro-behavioral evaluation within the first 48 hours of life. She meets the inclusion criteria for group 1 of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer three years ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy, and is currently on hormonal therapy. She reports feeling fatigued on a regular basis, which has been impacting her daily life and activities. She has tried various methods to alleviate the fatigue, including changing her diet and increasing her physical activity, but has not experienced significant improvement. She does not have a history of brain tumors or any psychological or psychiatric treatment. She is physically healthy aside from some occasional joint pain. She speaks fluent Dutch and is able to complete the questionnaires. She is willing to participate in an explorative study to identify the physiological and neurophysiological determinants of postcancer fatigue and to potentially find a treatment option that can improve her quality of life.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma and had a complete tumor resection surgery. He has never received any systemic anti-HCC therapy before. His CT scans indicate no tumor lesions at baseline, and his Child-Pugh score is class A. He has no history of central nervous system disease, mental illness, unstable angina, congestive heart failure, severe arrhythmia, or other severe uncontrolled diseases. His body surface area is 1.8 m2. He has no history of investigational drug or similar drug allergy. He is willing to participate in a randomized double-blinded, placebo-controlled, multi-center clinical trial to evaluate the effect of Injectable Tyroserleutide on the recurrence-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, and safety and tolerability of subjects after the resection of hepatocellular carcinoma.

12-year-old male athlete who is a competitive swimmer presented with complaints of neck pain. The pain has been ongoing for the past 3 months and is localized to the right side of his neck. He reports that the pain is worse during swimming practice and has been affecting his performance. He denies any recent trauma, fever, or other systemic symptoms. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the midpoint of the upper border of the trapezius muscle on the right side. The tenderness is graded as II according to the tenderness grading scheme. The patient has no history of neurological or dermatological disorders. He also does not have any history of chronic pain in both sides of the body, fibromyalgia or systemic disease. He has not received any myofascial trigger points injection in the past. The patient and his parents were informed about the study and agreed to participate. He was then enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to one of the three groups.

This clinical trial is not recruiting patients. It is a study that will analyze stored blood samples previously collected from participants in eight different studies of carriers of the human T-lymphotropic virus type I (HTLV-I). The study aims to identify chemical and protein markers in the blood of people who carry HTLV-I, which is associated with various pathologies, including an increased risk of a rare and aggressive cancer called adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL). The study will also examine differences in these markers before and after the onset of ATL.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help researchers determine which formulation of sulindac may be more effective in preventing cancer. He is in good health, has no significant medical history, and is not currently taking any medications. He has not used any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 inhibitors, including ibuprofen, ketoprofen or naproxen, for at least 6 months. He has no allergies or hypersensitivity to sulindac or other NSAIDs. He is willing to provide the required biologic specimens and abstain from consuming alcoholic or caffeinated beverages for 24 hours prior to the study drug administration and until all blood samples have been drawn. He is not currently using any herbal products, and he has not had cancer within the past 3 years except nonmelanomatous skin cancer, localized prostate cancer, carcinoma in situ of the cervix, or superficial bladder cancer that was previously treated more than 6 months ago.

A 55-year-old man was found unresponsive in his home by his family members. They called the emergency services, and the paramedics arrived within 5 minutes. The patient was in ventricular fibrillation, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was initiated. Advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) protocol was followed, and the patient received an initial dose of epinephrine (1mg) and amiodarone (300mg). After 2 minutes of CPR, the patient remained in ventricular fibrillation, and a second dose of epinephrine (1mg) was given. After another 2 minutes of CPR, the patient was still in ventricular fibrillation. The study protocol was initiated, and the patient received a third dose of epinephrine (1mg) associated with arginine-vasopressin (40 UI). After 5 more minutes of CPR, the patient converted to sinus rhythm, and spontaneous circulation was restored. The patient was transferred to the hospital, where he was admitted to the ICU.

The patient is a 23-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with high-grade osteosarcoma. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing persistent pain in his left leg for the past few months, which led to a medical consultation. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in his left femur with no evidence of metastasis. He underwent neoadjuvant induction chemotherapy and is currently considered a candidate for surgical resection. His performance status is WHO 1 and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is willing to undergo the study procedures, including the use of chemotherapy and experimental drugs. He is not allergic to any medications. He has no known complications such as diabetes mellitus or coagulation disorders. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently undergone a kidney transplant. He received a cadaveric kidney transplant and is currently taking a CNI-based regimen for immunosuppression. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage it. He has no known allergies, and his physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable. He is currently employed as an accountant and has a wife and two children. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with study requirements. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS). He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. He has been receiving transfusions of packed red blood cells for the past two months due to anemia. He has also been diagnosed with thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of less than 100,000/µl. The patient has failed to respond to other treatments for MDS and has opted not to participate in bone marrow transplantation. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is not currently on any other treatments for MDS or AML. He has not undergone major surgery within the past 3 weeks and has fully recovered from any previous surgeries. The patient is willing to adhere to the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the study and has signed an informed consent document indicating his understanding of the purpose and procedures required for the study.

As there are no eligibility criteria mentioned for this clinical trial, it is not possible to generate a patient description. The study is designed to investigate drug-gene interactions on the incidence of non-fatal myocardial infarction and stroke for hypertensive patients. Therefore, patients who meet the inclusion criteria for this study will be recruited based on the research objectives.

A 50 yo F with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic pain in the right hip is scheduled to undergo a total hip arthroplasty under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril 10 mg daily. The patient is 5'6'' and weighs 160 pounds, with a BMI of 25.8 kg/m2. She is capable of reporting her perceived pain using numeric pain scales and operating a patient controlled anesthesia (PCA) device. The patient does not have a known allergy, hypersensitivity, or contraindication to acetaminophen, and has normal liver and renal function. She is able to read and speak English fluently. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 50-year-old male patient presents with chronic lower back pain and is scheduled to undergo a thoracoabdominal surgery. He has a history of hypertension, which is under control with medication. He has no previous diagnosis of neurological or psychiatric diseases. The patient has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is ASA II. The patient is being monitored invasively for additional medical reasons, which makes them eligible for the study.

A 30 yo F recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis as per McDonald's criteria with an EDSS score of 3. She has been experiencing symptoms such as weakness in the limbs, difficulty walking, and occasional numbness in her left hand. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a subcutaneous injections as a disease-modifying therapy. She has had no exacerbations in the past 6 months and is stable on her current medication. She is willing to participate in the study and has no other significant medical conditions. She is able to give informed consent for the study.

A 45-year-old female patient who recently visited her primary care physician for a routine check-up was informed that her BMI falls under the category of overweight. She has a family history of type II diabetes, and her physician recommended a screening for abnormal glucose metabolism. She is not on any medication for any medical condition and has no significant past medical history. She reports no symptoms such as excessive thirst or urination, blurred vision, or weight loss. Her vital signs are within normal limits. The physical examination is unremarkable, except for elevated BMI. Fasting blood glucose, insulin levels, hemoglobin A1c, and 2-hour post-prandial glucose levels were measured. The results indicate the possibility of pre-diabetes. The patient is recommended to participate in a clinical trial that uses saliva samples to identify early pre-diabetes and type II diabetes. She is informed about the study design and consents to participate. The patient is included in the trial and asked to provide a saliva sample for analysis of transcriptome markers. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has a sibling diagnosed with colorectal cancer. She is a Singaporean citizen and has no personal history of inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, or colorectal polyps. She has never undergone screening colonoscopy before and is unsure about the procedure and its benefits. She is concerned about the cost of the screening and whether her insurance will cover it. She has some knowledge about colorectal cancer but is not aware of the screening guidelines set by the Ministry of Health in Singapore. She is willing to participate in the study to learn more about screening colonoscopy and to potentially encourage her siblings to undergo the procedure.

A 35 year old Asian American male, who has been living in New York City for 5 years, is a current smoker, smoking 15 cigarettes per day. He has attempted to quit smoking multiple times in the past without success. He has never used Chantix for smoking cessation. He is interested in participating in the study and willing to complete three-month follow-up assessments in person and provide a telephone number. He does not use any other tobacco products or e-cigarettes, nor does he use marijuana. He is not pregnant and is able to provide written consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is scheduled for an elective cardiac surgical procedure with extracorporeal circulation. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. He is currently taking medications for these conditions, including metoprolol, lisinopril, and metformin. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He has undergone a previous cardiac catheterization and was found to have significant stenosis in his left anterior descending artery. His echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 45%. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of smoking for 40 years. He presents to the clinic with complaints of pain in his legs when walking short distances. He states that the pain goes away with rest. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are controlled with medication. He also takes medication for acid reflux. He is currently retired and does not engage in regular physical activity. His past medical history is significant for a minor heart attack 5 years ago, which was treated with angioplasty. He has no family history of peripheral artery disease. His most recent lab results show an ABI of 0.7 and LDL cholesterol of 130 mg/dl. He is fluent in Dutch and able to read and understand questionnaires. He is able to undertake an exercise test.

A 10-year-old Chinese boy was diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency at the age of 6. He was referred to an endocrinologist due to short stature and delayed growth milestones. His parents reported no significant medical history and denied any consanguinity. He was born at term with a birth weight of 3.1 kg and had no neonatal complications. He was currently on PEG-Somatropin therapy for the past 1 year and has shown significant improvement in his growth velocity. His height was recorded as 125 cm at the start of his treatment and has increased to 137 cm after 1 year of therapy. He had no significant adverse effects and has been compliant with his therapy. His bone age was consistent with his chronological age. His parents have given their consent for him to participate in the extension study to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of PEG-Somatropin in the treatment of his growth hormone deficiency. They understand that he will need to complete scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other procedures. They are willing to cooperate and sign the informed consent.

A 43-year-old female was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma three months ago. She presented with a history of fever, fatigue, and weight loss. She also complained of headaches and blurry vision. After further evaluation, she was found to have CNS involvement with lymphoma. She was started on R-CHOP chemotherapy and underwent whole-brain radiation therapy. Her symptoms improved, but she was found to have persistent CNS involvement on surveillance imaging. She is a married mother of two children and works as a teacher. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her written consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old female who has been experiencing knee pain for the last 8 months. She describes her pain as a dull ache in her knees that is present most of the day, especially when she tries to walk or climb stairs. She has been taking over-the-counter pain medications and using heating pads to alleviate her pain, but the relief is only temporary. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has been diagnosed with it by a physician. Her recent X-rays and MRI confirm the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis. She is generally healthy and has no history of other medical conditions that would interfere with her participation in the study. She is willing to undergo MRI of the knee and is not taking any intra-articular injections of hyaluronan or glucocorticoids. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to provide informed consent.

A 35 year old male with a history of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) diagnosed according to the international classification of sleep disorders-3 (ICSD-3) criteria and is currently using continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) as the primary therapy, complains of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS)

The patient is a 38 year-old male who works as a computer programmer and spends most of his day typing on a keyboard. He has been experiencing numbness and tingling in his left hand, specifically in the ring and little fingers, for the past 6 months. He has also noticed weakness in his left hand when gripping objects. The symptoms have been affecting his work and daily activities, prompting him to seek medical attention. Physical examination revealed tenderness over the cubital tunnel and positive Tinel's sign with reproduction of symptoms. No other neurological deficits were noted. He has no history of trauma or injury to the elbow or wrist. He is otherwise healthy and does not take any medication regularly. He does not smoke or drink alcohol.

A 50-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment at a local hospital. She has experienced nausea and vomiting as a side effect of the chemotherapy. She has tried anti-nausea medications but they have not been fully effective in relieving her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known allergies to medications or foods. She is interested in complementary therapies and is willing to try reflexology to see if it can help alleviate her symptoms.

A 27-year-old healthy woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial for research studies related to immune system and inflammatory diseases. She works as a freelance graphic designer and has no underlying diseases or medical conditions. She has regular menstrual cycles and uses oral contraceptives. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. Her past medical history is significant for a broken arm when she was a child. She has no known drug allergies or history of drug abuse. She is interested in donating blood, urine, and buccal mucosa samples for research purposes. She understands the investigational nature of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

64F with a 4-year history of bilateral knee pain attributed to osteoarthritis, which has been refractory to conservative medical management, including NSAIDs, physiotherapy, and weight loss. She reports pain while walking, standing, and climbing stairs. She rates her pain as 7 out of 10 on the Visual Analog Scale. She has Grade 2 Osteoarthritis as diagnosed on standing weight-bearing knee radiographs per the Kellen-Lawrence Grading scale. She has no active malignancy or infection in the affected knee. She has had no corticosteroid injection in the affected knee in the past 3 months. She has no history of rheumatoid arthritis or other seronegative arthropathy. She has not had any previous surgery (excluding arthroscopy) of the affected knee. She meets the inclusion criteria for the Genicular Artery Embolization to Reduce Pain Associated with Unilateral Mild to Moderate Osteoarthritis study.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with open angle glaucoma (OAG) and is currently being treated with ocular hypotensive medication. She has been taking the medication for the past 3 months but is still experiencing elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) with a reading of 24 mm Hg in both eyes during her last check-up. Her corrected visual acuity in each eye is +0.5 logMAR by ETDRS (equivalent to 20/63). She has not had any previous glaucoma intraocular surgery or glaucoma laser procedures in either eye. She has not had refractive surgery in either eye. She has not experienced any ocular trauma, surgery or laser treatment in the past 6 months. She has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the formulation or to topical anesthetics. She has not had any contact lens wear within 30 minutes of instillation of study medication. She has not taken any other ocular medication in the past 30 days except for ocular hypotensive medication.
