She does not have any clinically significant abnormalities in laboratory tests or systemic disease that may interfere with the study. She is willing and able to give signed informed consent and follow study instructions. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using medically acceptable birth control.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in the left knee, which has been causing him significant pain and difficulty walking. He has been scheduled for total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and has given informed consent for inclusion in the study. He has no history of substance or alcohol abuse and has not used any opioids in the past. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no known allergies to any of the drugs to be used in the study. The patient is ASA class 2 and is able to use PCA. He has no contraindications for spinal anesthesia.

56-year-old male with a history of smoking, alcohol use, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) for which he takes daily proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). He presents with dysphagia and a 20-pound weight loss over the past 6 months. Endoscopy shows a 5 cm mass in the mid-esophagus that biopsies as adenocarcinoma. CT scans show no evidence of distant metastases. He is referred to a thoracic surgeon who determines he is a candidate for an esophagectomy with gastric pull-up reconstruction. He is informed of the study and agrees to participate. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has no prior upper abdominal surgeries. He is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and complete the entire study as specified in the protocol, including follow-up visits.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has struggled with her weight for most of her adult life. She currently has a BMI of 35.5 kg/m2, which puts her in the Class II obesity category. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past, but has not been able to lose weight and keep it off long-term. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative weight loss treatments. The patient has no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications or supplements that would interfere with the study. She is willing to undergo the intragastric balloon implantation procedure and follow the study protocol for the 12-month duration of the trial. She understands the risks and benefits of the procedure, and is committed to making lifestyle changes to support her weight loss goals.

A 50-year-old male patient is scheduled for left-sided thoracic surgery for lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit smoking 5 years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for several months. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed with hypertension but it is well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies to any medications. He exercises regularly and has no history of heart or lung disease. He has never undergone any thoracic surgery before. He is able to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. She underwent one course of induction chemotherapy but failed to achieve complete remission. The patient has less than 20% bone marrow or peripheral blood blasts. The patient also has a high-risk feature defined by adverse cytogenetics (deletion 5q) and a high-risk molecular abnormality (FLT3 mutation). The patient has an HLA-matched unrelated donor who is 18 years old and weighs 120 pounds. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and a Karnofsky score of 70. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 50% and no uncontrolled arrhythmias or symptomatic cardiac disease. The patient's FEV1 and FVC are both 60% of expected, corrected for hemoglobin, and the patient's DLCO is 55% of expected, corrected for hemoglobin. The patient's bilirubin and SGPT are both within normal limits. The patient is negative for hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody. The patient has a serum creatinine level of 1.4 mg%. The patient is willing to use an effective contraceptive measure while on the study. The patient does not have any known allergies to mouse proteins.

A 42-year-old female with a history of hypertension and metabolic syndrome is being considered for enrollment in the clinical trial. She has a BMI of 32, waist circumference of 98 cm, and fasting plasma glucose level of 6.2 mmol/L. She is currently taking a diuretic and an ACE inhibitor for her hypertension, but her blood pressure is not well-controlled with readings averaging around 150/95 mm Hg. She reports occasional headaches, but denies any other symptoms. She has no known history of diabetes or heart disease. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if a new medication regimen could better control her hypertension and improve her metabolic parameters.

A 48-year-old female presents with a history of locally recurrent breast cancer. She was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 5 years ago, treated with surgery, chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She completed her treatment and was on regular follow-up. She has a history of smoking for 10 years, but quit smoking 3 years ago. She now reports a new lesion in her breast, with metastasis to her liver and lungs. She has previously received taxane as neo-adjuvant and adjuvant therapy. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or targeted therapy for metastatic breast cancer. She is currently not on any hormonal therapy. Her blood pressure is within normal limits and she has no history of high blood pressure crisis. She has no history of brain metastasis or open biopsy in the past 28 days. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for advanced breast cancer and is willing to comply with all necessary requirements for the study.

The patient is a 78-year-old male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease. He presents with chest pain that started 2 hours ago and radiates to his left arm. He also complains of shortness of breath and diaphoresis. He has no history of allergies and takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin daily. He lives alone and has no family history of heart disease. The physical examination shows a blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg, a heart rate of 95 bpm, and normal lung sounds. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. The patient is taken to the cardiac catheterization lab, where he undergoes successful PCI with stenting to his right coronary artery. His platelet reactivity is measured 24 hours after PCI and found to be PRU≥235, indicating clopidogrel resistance. The patient is informed of the clinical trial and agrees to participate. He meets all eligibility criteria and is randomized to receive either prasugrel 5mg or clopidogrel 150mg daily. His platelet reactivity will be assessed on day 15, and then treatment crossover will be performed. On day 30, platelet reactivity will be determined as well.

A 38-year-old male patient is scheduled for elective surgery to repair a sports injury. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of chronic medical conditions or allergies. His height is 180cm, and his weight is 85kg. The patient does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He takes no regular medications, and his preoperative lab tests are within normal limits, except for a slightly low hemoglobin level of 11.8 g/dL. The patient is informed about the noninvasive measurement of hemoglobin and consents to participate in the study. The patient's hemoglobin level will be measured both invasively and noninvasively using the Pronto® device to assess the reliability of the noninvasive measurement. The patient is expected to comply with the study protocol and attend preoperative appointments as scheduled.

This is a 62-year-old male with peripheral vascular disease, Rutherford Classification 2, who has been recommended for revascularization of the native vessel through percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) or bypass. The patient has a visible stump of at least 1.0 cm beyond the origin of the profunda artery and at least one infrapopliteal artery in continuity with the native femoropopliteal artery that is patent (<50% DS). The patient's reference vessel diameter is between 4.0 mm and 7.0 mm, and the stenosis in the superficial femoral artery (SFA) and/or popliteal artery above the knee is between 70% and 100% DS (occlusion) with a total lesion length between 1.0 cm and 15.0 cm. The patient is willing and able to comply with the specified evaluations during hospitalization and all required follow-up examinations. The patient is between the ages of 18 and 85 years and has provided written informed consent before execution of study procedures. The patient does not have a contraindication to intravenous contrast material, heparin, aspirin or other medications required for a percutaneous interventional procedure. The patient does not have a known bleeding or hyper-coagulation disorder, serum creatinine > 2.0 mg/dL, or uncompensated congestive heart failure. The patient is not currently enrolled or has been previously enrolled in this study, suspected or confirmed pregnancy, or have had a myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accident/transient ischemic attack within the last 60 days. The patient does not have subintimal guidewire placement following pilot channel creation through a stenosis or occlusion with any excimer laser catheter, calcification likely to prevent the passage of the excimer laser catheter or CLiRpath® Photoablation Atherectomy system, iliac stenosis >/= 50% DS that is not treated prior to enrollment in this study, or ipsilateral and/or contralateral iliac treatment of a stenosis prior to enrollment with final residual stenosis >/= 30%. The patient does not have lesions proximal and distal to the treatment site that are >/= 50% DS at the time of enrollment, contralateral leg disease that requires treatment within the next 30 days and prior to completion of the 30-day follow-up, or planned or predicted cardiovascular surgical or interventional procedures outside of the ipsilateral leg within 30 days after entry into this study, and prior to completion of the 30-day follow-up. Lastly, the patient does not have perforation or dissection of grade "C" or greater seen during or after the creation of the pilot channel.

A 54-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with abdominal pain and bloating. She has a history of ovarian cancer, which was treated with platinum-based chemotherapy. However, the cancer has recurred and progressed within 6 months of the last chemotherapy. Imaging studies show measurable metastatic disease on CT scans of the abdomen and pelvis. Her CA-125 tumor marker has also doubled from its nadir value. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, platelet count of 120,000/mm³, hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, and neutrophil count of 2.0 x 10³/mm³. Her serum creatinine is within normal limits, and her bilirubin, AST/ALT levels are less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal. She has no childbearing capacity and her LVEF is greater than or equal to 50% by ECHO or MUGA scan. She has no known hypersensitivity to study drugs and no active secondary malignant tumor within the past 5 years. She has not received prior chemotherapy with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin hydrochloride, other anthracyclines, or gemcitabine hydrochloride. She is not receiving any other concurrent tumor-specific therapy for ovarian cancer.

Pt is a 75yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease, presenting with worsening dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. Echocardiogram revealed severe aortic stenosis with aortic valve area of 0.8 cm2, peak gradient of 70 mmHg, and mean gradient of 45 mmHg. The patient also reported occasional angina. CT scan showed an aortic valve annular size of 25 mm. The patient was evaluated by the Heart Team and deemed to be at intermediate risk for surgical aortic valve replacement. He met all other inclusion and exclusion criteria and was offered enrollment in the HLT Meridian Valve CE Mark Trial. The patient provided written informed consent and underwent the investigational procedure with successful implantation of the HLT System. The patient will be followed up for safety and performance evaluation.

A healthy, non-smoking male or female between the ages of 18 and 55, with a BMI between 18.0 and 32.0 kg/m2 is needed for a Phase 1, open-label, single-dose, randomized, 2-period crossover study to assess the bioequivalence of pacritinib following administration of 400-mg doses of P3CT (Reference) and FMI (Test) formulations. The study aims to determine the bioequivalence of pacritinib and to characterize the PK of pacritinib. The participant must not have ingested pacritinib before and must not have any clinically significant findings from medical history, physical examination, and vital signs. The participant must also have normal laboratory evaluations, a negative test for selected drugs of abuse, and negative hepatitis and HIV antibody screens. Female participants must not be pregnant or lactating and must agree to use one of the approved forms of contraception during the study period. Male participants must agree to use one of the approved methods of contraception. The participant must also be able to comprehend and willing to sign an Informed Consent Form. The study excludes individuals with a history or clinical manifestation of clinically significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, metabolic, allergic, dermatological, neurological, or psychiatric disorder, among others. Participants must not have any acute or chronic condition that would limit their ability to complete and/or participate in this clinical study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who resides in a malaria-endemic area. He recently participated in a study comparing the efficacy of chloroquine and amodiaquine for the treatment of malaria. The child presented with malaria symptoms, including fever and chills, and tested positive for malaria with more than 20 parasites per 200 leukocytes. Despite receiving treatment with chloroquine or amodiaquine, his malaria did not resolve. The child is willing to participate in the study evaluating the efficacy of re-treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) for malaria. He does not have an allergy to sulfadoxine and/or pyrimethamine. The child will be followed up for 35 days and will be visited once a week for a finger prick blood sample to be taken. If the child gets malaria during the follow-up, he will be treated according to the guidelines of the Bandim Health Centre. All treatments during the follow-up will be free.

A 25-year-old man who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is generally healthy, has no significant medical history, and takes no medications. He doesn't smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is willing to comply with the study protocol, including the use of effective contraception during the trial. His body weight is 70 kg, and his BMI is 23.2 kg/m2. He signed the informed consent form and understands the study's contents, process, and possible adverse reactions. He has no known history of allergies to the study drugs or allergies constitution. He has never had alcohol abuse and has not donated or lost blood over 450 mL within 3 months prior to screening. The 12-lead ECG shows no clinically significant abnormalities. He is negative for viral hepatitis, HIV, and syphilis.

A 16-year-old Caucasian male presents with red and swollen toes, which have been painful for the past two weeks. He reports that these symptoms started during the confinement period due to the COVID-19 pandemic. He denies any fever, cough, shortness of breath, or other respiratory symptoms. He also denies any recent travel or known exposure to someone with COVID-19. He has no significant past medical history, and he is not taking any medications. He lives with his parents and his younger brother, who also did not experience any symptoms. The patient's physical exam reveals erythematous and swollen toes with no evidence of ulcers or blisters. The rest of his physical examination is unremarkable. The patient and his family provide written informed consent to participate in the ECCES study.

This is a 32 year-old female with a long-standing history of asthma who has been using inhaled corticosteroids as maintenance therapy for the past 12 months. She has had several exacerbations in the past year, including a hospitalization for asthma. Her medication regimen has been adjusted several times in an attempt to control her symptoms, but her asthma remains poorly controlled. She has not been prescribed Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol xinafoate before and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of this medication in controlling her asthma symptoms. She does not have any history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or respiratory tract cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been intubated for the past 3 days due to respiratory failure. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been on home oxygen therapy for the past year. He developed a fever of 101°F yesterday and has been coughing up yellowish-green sputum. A chest X-ray was performed, revealing infiltrates in both lungs. The patient was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, but his condition has not improved. The respiratory therapist has recommended colistin inhalation as a possible treatment option for ventilator-associated pneumonia suspected to have multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria. The patient has no known allergies to polymyxin and his creatinine clearance is above 30ml/min. He has been assessed as eligible for the clinical trial and has consented to participate.

Sophie is a 16-year-old high school student who was admitted to the psychiatric hospital after attempting suicide by overdose. She has a history of depression and anxiety, and has struggled with family conflict and feeling isolated from her peers. At the hospital, she received stabilization treatment and was deemed no longer a threat to herself. Sophie has a supportive mother and stepfather who are willing to participate in aftercare. They speak English fluently and are able to travel to the study site at CHOP. Sophie does not have a history of psychosis or intellectual disability, and is not being discharged to a residential placement. She is interested in participating in outpatient aftercare to reduce her risk of future suicide attempts and improve her mental health.

A 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia for the past 5 years. She reports experiencing widespread pain, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping. She has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she takes medication. She is currently not on any pain medications. She has noticed that she avoids certain activities due to fear of worsening her pain. She reports feeling anxious and frustrated with her condition, and is interested in participating in research to better understand her symptoms. She is literate and willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of headaches, nausea, and vomiting for the past 2 months. She also reported experiencing seizures for the past 3 weeks. An MRI revealed a solitary brain tumor with ring-like contrast enhancement and edema. The patient has no previous history of primary tumor elsewhere. Her medical history is significant for depression, which has been managed with medication for the past year. She has no known allergies to diary products, marine products, egg protein, soya, or peanut protein. She is an alert female with no acute distress. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her BMI is 24. Her neurological exam showed no deficits. A preliminary histopathological assessment suggested glioblastoma, and she is a potential candidate for surgery.

The patient is a healthy male between the ages of 18 and 55 with a BMI between 18.0 and 30.0 kg/m^2. The patient has no history of significant medical conditions, drug abuse, smoking, or alcoholism. They have not participated in any clinical trials within the past three months and are willing to follow the procedures outlined in the protocol. The patient has normal laboratory test results and a normal 12-lead ECG. They are able to communicate with the investigative site staff and have signed an IRB/REC-approved informed consent form. The patient and their partner agree to use an acceptable double barrier method for birth control from the Screening visit through 3 months after the last dose of test material. The patient must not be mentally or legally incapacitated.

56 year old male with a history of peptic ulcer disease and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) for the past 10 years. The patient has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) regularly but still experiences occasional reflux symptoms. He has no known allergies to any medications and no history of Helicobacter pylori infection. He has not undergone any upper gastrointestinal surgery or resection. He is willing to undergo both the C13-CAC Breath Test and 24-hour Gastric pH Monitoring. He has no other significant medical history except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication.

50 year-old male Veteran who has been smoking cigarettes for 30 years with a 20 pack-year smoking history. He reports that he has tried to quit smoking multiple times, but has been unsuccessful. He also reports daily marijuana use and drinking 3 cups of coffee a day. He is interested in quitting smoking and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help him quit. The patient is generally healthy and has no history of other substance abuse or dependence. He lives within commuting distance of the VA San Diego Healthcare System. He has an exhaled CO level of 12 ppm. He is able to read, write, and give voluntary informed consent. He has no history of severe head trauma, epilepsy, or other neurological diseases, and his cardiovascular, liver, and renal function are stable. He is not currently taking any medications that might affect the central nervous system. He is not pregnant.

An 80-year-old female resident of a long-term care facility with a history of hypertension, osteoarthritis, and a previous stroke was admitted to the hospital with a Stage III pressure ulcer on her sacrum. The ulcer measures 15 cm2 and has evidence of infection with P. aeruginosa. The patient complains of pain and discomfort in the affected area. She has no history of diabetes or other chronic medical conditions. The patient has provided signed informed consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures. She has no known allergies to any components of SilvaSorb hydrogel. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is not currently on any investigational drug or other intervention within the past 30 days. There is no evidence of chronic stool incontinence or planned surgical wound closure within the study period. The patient does not have organ failure, acute respiratory failure, chronic renal failure or diagnosed osteomyelitis. The patient is on daily aspirin for prevention of stroke.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is 30 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has been diagnosed with severe preeclampsia during her routine prenatal check-up, with a blood pressure reading of 170/110 mmHg and proteinuria of 3+. She complains of headache, visual disturbances, and upper abdominal pain. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking antihypertensive medication for it. The fetal ultrasound shows normal growth and well-being. The treating physician has recommended expectant management and has referred her to the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the study procedures.

The patient is a 45 year old Hispanic male who has never been diagnosed with any cardiac disease and has no known risk factors for such conditions. He is a non-smoker, has a normal physical examination and normal ECG results. His blood pressure is within normal limits with a systolic blood pressure of 110mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 70mmHg. His fasting blood glucose level is 85mg/dL and his total cholesterol level is 180mg/dL. He has not been taking any medications and has no history of significant medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in a research study that aims to collect cardiovascular magnetic resonance data from Latin American countries in order to establish normal reference standards for this population. He is willing to undergo CMR imaging as part of the study procedures.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has struggled with obesity for several years. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 44 and has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in the past. She currently uses a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine to manage her OSA. The patient has been referred for bariatric surgery and is considering participating in a clinical trial that aims to develop a novel pathway to decrease the cost and waiting time to manage bariatric surgical patients with OSA. The study will involve a screening process using the STOP-Bang questionnaire, and the patient will be randomized into either the Sleep Study group or the Oximetry group. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to potentially reduce the costs and time associated with managing her OSA during the bariatric surgery process.

65 yo M admitted to the medical intensive care unit with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to pneumonia. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 48 hours. The patient is able to provide consent in English. The patient has no history of metastatic lung cancer. The patient is not pregnant and is not a prisoner or ward of the state. The patient is eligible to participate in the ASTERS Study to assess the role of sphingolipids in ARDS.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a distal radius fracture following a fall. She has a past medical history of hypertension and is currently on antihypertensive medication. She is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies to local anesthetics. The patient has consented to participate in a clinical trial studying the effects of neostigmine as an adjuvant to bupivacaine in ultrasound guided supraclavicular brachial plexus block. She is scheduled to undergo a supraclavicular brachial plexus block with 25 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine and 1 mL of either normal saline or neostigmine (0.5 mg). The procedure is expected to last 60-90 minutes and the patient will be monitored for 24 hours post-operatively for pain levels and any adverse effects related to the technique or drugs used in the procedure.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of leukemia, who has been hospitalized for fever and cough for the past 3 days. He had a recent central line insertion for chemotherapy. Blood cultures obtained on admission were positive for Candida albicans. The patient has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medications. He has normal liver function tests and no other significant medical history. He weighs 30 kg. The patient is able to tolerate oral medication, and has sufficient venous access for study medication administration and laboratory monitoring. The patient's legal guardian has provided informed consent for study participation.

A 10-month-old Caucasian male infant is brought to the pediatrician's office with a fever of 102°F, ear pain, and fussiness. The baby's mother reports that the baby has been pulling at his ears and crying inconsolably. The baby has had no prior history of ear infections. On examination, the pediatrician noted redness and bulging of the eardrum on the right side. The baby's temperature is 101.4°F, and his weight is 8 kg. The baby is otherwise healthy, and his vaccines are up to date. The baby is not allergic to any medications, and he has not been treated for ear infections in the past two weeks. The baby's mother consents to enroll him in the clinical trial to test the safety profile of amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium containing a reduced concentration of clavulanate potassium for the treatment of acute otitis media.

A 45-year-old, right-handed office worker with a 6-month history of pain in the right elbow presents to the clinic. The patient reports that the pain started gradually and has worsened over time. The pain is located on the lateral side of the elbow and is aggravated by activities that involve gripping or lifting objects, as well as by wrist extension. The patient reports no history of trauma to the elbow or any other medical conditions. On physical examination, the patient has tenderness over the lateral epicondyle and pain with resisted wrist and long finger extension. The patient's elbow range of motion is within normal limits. The patient has no history of elbow surgery or fracture, elbow instability, or elbow arthritis on radiographs. The patient's pain score is 6/10 using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). The patient speaks English and is able to comply with study protocols and follow-up visits.

Patient is a 40-year-old man who has been experiencing painful urination, difficulty in urination, and pelvic pain for the last 6 months. He has been diagnosed with chronic bacterial prostatitis based on clinical symptoms and laboratory evidence of prostatitis. He has a history of two previous episodes of prostatitis in the past year. He has not taken antibiotics for the last 14 days and has not received any medication for treating prostatitis in the last 7 days. He is able to take oral medications and has not undergone any surgery in the last 6 months that may affect bladder or prostate. He is not taking any medications that may affect bladder or prostate. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

Maria is a 60-year-old woman who underwent a unicondylar knee implant surgery (iUni®) in 2015 due to osteoarthritis. After the surgery, she has been able to perform daily activities with ease and without any pain. She has not experienced any complications related to the surgery or implant. She has also regularly followed up with her physician and has been compliant with all post-operative care instructions. She is willing to participate in the follow-up study to provide information on the long-term outcomes of her surgery and implant. She signs the informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

Patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of primary open-angle glaucoma, currently using topical glaucoma medications to manage her condition. She has been diagnosed with glaucoma for the past 10 years and has been using eye drops to manage it. However, she has noticed some difficulty with instilling the eye drops and feels that she may not be doing it correctly. The patient is interested in participating in this study to learn more about the proper technique for using eye drops and to potentially help others who may be experiencing similar issues.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has just given birth to her premature baby girl at Foothills Medical Centre, Calgary, Alberta. The baby was born at 30 weeks gestation and is currently in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). The mother is in good health and has agreed to participate in the Alberta BLOOM Preterm Neonate Study. She speaks and understands English and is willing to comply with all study procedures. She lives in the Calgary Metropolitan Region and has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or congenital gastrointestinal anomalies. She is the legal guardian of her baby girl and is looking forward to contributing to the study that aims to gain a better understanding of the microbiome establishment in very preterm infants.

The patient is a 30-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with intermediate-risk cytogenetics. He has undergone induction chemotherapy and is currently in complete remission. However, further treatment is needed, and a bone marrow transplant is recommended. Unfortunately, no matched related donor is available, and the patient does not have the luxury of waiting for a matched unrelated donor. The patient is eligible for the Cord Blood Stem Cell Transplantation Study (COBLT) and will be evaluated for transplantation with HLA-mismatched, unrelated-donor umbilical cord blood stem and progenitor cell units (UCBU). The patient has no significant medical history, and his physical exam is unremarkable. The patient has been informed of the risks and benefits of cord blood transplantation and has consented to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 months. She has been on methotrexate for the past 6 months and has not shown any significant improvement. She complains of severe joint pain and stiffness, particularly in the knees and wrists, and has difficulty carrying out her daily activities. Her ESR is 30mm/h and CRP levels are 1.5mg/dL. She has 4 swollen joints out of 66 joints assessed and 8 tender joints out of 68 joints assessed. She has not been pregnant in the past 6 months and is not currently nursing. She has not been previously treated with tacrolimus and does not have any history of renal dysfunction or hepatic dysfunction. She has no history of heart disease or respiratory disease. She has not been treated with any investigational product in the past 3 months. She is interested in enrolling in the clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of tacrolimus in active rheumatoid arthritis patients who showed unsuccessful response to existing DMARDs.

An 67-year old retired school teacher, Mrs. Johnson has been living in Birmingham, Alabama for over 30 years. She is a widow and lives with her son and his family. She enjoys spending time with her grandchildren, reading books and watching TV. She has been noticing difficulty in reading small print and has been experiencing occasional blurry vision. She believes it is just a part of aging and hasn't seen an eye doctor in a few years. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has never had any eye surgeries or eye conditions. She is an African American and is interested in learning more about eye care and how to maintain her vision. She is fluent in English and is a member of a senior center in her community.

50-year-old woman with a 5-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus is currently on a diet and exercise regimen. She has reported difficulty in maintaining her blood glucose levels within the target range and her most recent HbA1c was 8.2%. She has no known history of unstable concomitant disease and has not been treated with any oral hypoglycemic agent within the last 3 months prior to enrollment, except for metformin hydrochloride which she has been taking for the past 2 years at a stable dose. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of PF-00915275 to see if it can help her better control her glucose levels.

56M US military Veteran with a history of transfemoral limb loss due to trauma 10 years ago. The patient currently uses a socket suspension technology prosthesis and has normal cognitive function with no physical limitations or underlying medical conditions that may prevent him from being a suitable candidate for the study. The patient is committed to participating in baseline and follow-up evaluations for the entire duration of the study and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient is a non-smoker and is not currently on active or reserve military duty. The patient has not experienced systemic bacterial infection or localized infection at the stump site within the previous 6 months and has not had more than one limb amputated. The patient's body mass index (BMI) is 28 and there is no evidence of vascular compromise proximal to the surgical site. The patient is not currently pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant within the first year of follow-up. The patient has no renal insufficiency and is not currently on oral anticoagulation.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who recently underwent a colonoscopy to remove an adenomatous polyp in her colon. She is postmenopausal and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is willing to abstain from chronic use of NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors during the study. She is in good health and does not have any significant renal or hepatic disorder or bleeding disorder. She has never been diagnosed with Familial Adenomatous Polyposis or Hereditary Non-Polyposis Colorectal Cancer. She is willing to limit aspirin use to less than or equal to 325mg po QOD or 162.5mg po QD during the study. She is willing to return for follow-up tests and evaluations. She is currently not taking any investigational medications and has not received any in the past 30 days.

A 5-year-old boy was recently diagnosed with ADHD after exhibiting symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity both at home and at preschool. He has no previous history of medication for ADHD, and his parents are interested in exploring medication options to help manage his symptoms. The child has no known allergies or intolerances to medications, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. His height and weight are within the normal range for his age, and his Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test 4 (PPVT-4) score is above 70. The child's ADHD RS-IV Preschool-Home Version score is above the 90th percentile for both the hyperactive-impulsive subscale and inattentive subscale, as well as the total score. The child's Global Assessment Scale (CGAS) score is below 55, indicating significant impairment in several areas of functioning. The child has not received any investigational products or devices within the past 30 days and has not been treated with atomoxetine in the past 30 days.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and has been in recovery for the past year. She has been on medication and has been attending therapy sessions regularly. She has a supportive family who has been helping her through her recovery process. She is fluent in French and has a good understanding of the language. She is interested in participating in the study to help identify the specific processes of recovery for bipolar disorder and hopes that her experiences can contribute to the development of new therapeutic devices based on the recovery model.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of bulimia nervosa for the past 5 years is seeking treatment. She reports episodes of binge eating and purging at least twice a week. She has tried several forms of therapy in the past, but they have not been successful in controlling her bulimic behavior. She is currently not taking any medication for bulimia nervosa. She is in good health otherwise and is eager to participate in this clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of N-acetylcysteine.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a history of stress urinary incontinence for the past 2 years. She reports that she has been experiencing leakage of urine during coughing, sneezing, or laughing, which has been affecting her daily activities and social life. She denies any frequency, urgency or burning sensation during urination. She has tried pelvic floor exercises without significant improvement. She has no history of pelvic surgery or radiation therapy. She has no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. She is married and has two children delivered vaginally. She is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol occasionally and exercises regularly. Her physical examination revealed no pelvic organ prolapse and normal vaginal mucosa. Her urine dipstick was negative for infection. Urodynamic testing confirmed the diagnosis of stress urinary incontinence. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of the incontinence ring.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who suffered from an ischemic stroke 8 months ago, resulting in hemiparesis and difficulty with motor function. He has been receiving physical therapy and rehabilitation, but the progress has been slow. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. He is currently not participating in any other clinical trials or taking any investigational drugs. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve his condition and has read and understood the informed consent form. He is willing to undergo the UCBMC transplantation if he meets the eligibility criteria. The patient is HLA-matched with an umbilical cord blood unit and has been cleared by the investigator to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old man visited his urologist with complaints of difficulty urinating and lower back pain. After a physical examination, a PSA test and biopsy were performed, and the patient was diagnosed with locally advanced prostate cancer. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently not on any medication. His family history is negative for prostate cancer. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a subcutaneous four months sustained-release formulation of triptorelin. The patient has an estimated survival time of over 12 months according to the investigator's assessment. The patient's testosterone level is 200 ng/dL at screening. He has no history of prior surgical castration or prostate cancer therapy within the past 2 months. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study-related procedures.

55 year old male, former construction worker, with a history of asbestos exposure, presents with worsening shortness of breath and cough for the past 2 months. He underwent a biopsy that revealed malignant pleural mesothelioma with overexpression of mesothelin. Patient received 1st line treatment with platinum in combination with pemetrexed, but had locally confirmed progression. He has measurable disease and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) of 1. His bone marrow, liver, and renal function are adequate. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 55%. The patient has no history of bleeding diathesis, brain metastases, or meningeal tumors. He has no ongoing or active infections and no pre-existing cardiac conditions. The patient is interested in participating in the study and meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with mild aortic stenosis. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels for which she takes lisinopril 10 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. She has a BMI of 28 and a family history of heart disease. She reports occasional shortness of breath with exertion but denies chest pain or syncope. She is a retired teacher and leads an active lifestyle, walking daily for exercise. She has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. Her recent echocardiogram showed a peak Doppler aortic valve velocity of 3.0 m/sec. Her LDL-C level is within the targeted level according to the Canadian guidelines. She reports excellent medication adherence and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old female teaching staff member at Sulaiman Al Rajhi Colleges has been experiencing occasional headaches and fatigue for the past few months. She visited the university clinic and her blood pressure was measured as 135/85 mm Hg. She was informed that she has elevated blood pressure and was advised to monitor her blood pressure regularly. The physician informed her about a clinical trial that is assessing the effectiveness of hibiscus sabdariffa on lowering blood pressure in individuals with elevated blood pressure. She is interested to participate in the study and meets the eligibility criteria. She has no history of hypertension or other comorbid conditions, and is not taking any regular medication. She is not allergic to hibiscus sabdariffa and has not been a regular user of hibiscus. She was informed that she will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group, and will be required to drink a 240 ml serving of hibiscus sabdariffa 1 time a day for 3 months if she is assigned to the intervention group. She will be required to visit the clinic at the official start of the trial, at 1 month after the official start, at 2 months after the official start, and at 3 months after the official start (at the end of the trial) to measure her blood pressure and to fill out questionnaires regarding sleep quality and stress levels. She will also have a blood sample withdrawn twice during the trial to measure her LDL levels. She was informed that her participation is voluntary and that she can withdraw at any time without any consequences. She was also informed that her data will be kept strictly confidential and that the study investigators will ensure anonymity before proceeding with the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe headache, nausea, and vomiting. He reports losing consciousness for a brief period of time before regaining consciousness. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. On examination, he is alert but disoriented to time and place. His blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Neurological examination reveals left-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria. CT scan of the brain shows acute ischemic stroke in the posterior cerebral circulation. The patient is scheduled for emergency endovascular treatment and has a modified Rankin score of 1 prior to onset. He has no known allergies to anesthetics or analgesics.

Pt is a 45yo M recently diagnosed with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. He has no significant past medical history and is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment. The patient reports experiencing feelings of anxiety and depression since his diagnosis and is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the psychological aspects of patients with pancreatic cancer. He has completed at least 8 years of school education and is able to sign the informed consent form. The patient is currently not taking any psychotropic drugs or undergoing psychotherapeutic or psychological treatment. He has adequate family and social support and is interested in improving his quality of life during treatment.

30-year-old male diagnosed with HIV and receiving care at an HIV clinic in Uganda. The patient reported feeling low mood, loss of interest in activities, trouble sleeping, and decreased appetite during a routine screening using the Patient Health Questionnaire-2. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has consented to participate. He is medically stable and has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for 6 months. He has not received any antidepressant treatment before. The patient is able to communicate in English and has no history of active opportunistic infections.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who recently underwent aortic surgery and had BioGlue applied to the site. He is now experiencing symptoms that require aortic re-operation. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is a retired construction worker and is married with two adult children. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for participation in the study. He does not have a history of vasculitis, active infection (endocarditis), chronic inflammatory condition, or autoimmune disease.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male with a body weight within +-20% of his normal weight (Broca index). He has no significant medical history, nor does he suffer from any gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. He has no history of central nervous system or psychiatric disorders, orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, blackouts, chronic or relevant acute infections, or allergy/hypersensitivity. He has not taken any medication with a long half-life within at least one month or less than ten half-lives of the respective drug before enrolment in the study. He has not used any drugs that might influence the results of the trial within seven days prior to administration or during the trial. He has not participated in another trial with an investigational drug within two months prior to the start of the study. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use drugs. He has not donated blood (>100 ml) within four weeks prior to administration. He has not engaged in excessive physical activities within two weeks prior to administration or during the trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, which has spread to his liver and bones. He has already undergone chemotherapy and radiation, but his tumors have continued to progress. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score is 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 3 months. He has no known brain metastases or primary brain tumors. He has no active infections or gastrointestinal diseases that would interfere with the administration of oral medication. He has no history of thromboembolic events or bleeding diathesis within the past 6 months. His blood work shows adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. He has not tested positive for hepatitis C antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen, or Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) -1, -2 antibody. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of daily doses of BMS-986115 as a potential treatment option for his advanced solid tumors.

Patient is a 32-year-old African-American man who is currently using heroin and cocaine and is seeking treatment for opioid dependence. He has a past history of substance abuse and has been in and out of rehab multiple times. He is currently employed but has been experiencing financial difficulties due to his addiction. He has a supportive family who is encouraging him to seek treatment. His medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension which is currently controlled with medication. He is not currently taking any medications other than his blood pressure medication. He is willing to use medically effective forms of contraception while in the study.

A 26-year-old woman, currently pregnant with her first child, is seeking prenatal care. She has a history of hypertension and is currently being treated with medication to manage her blood pressure. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is fluent in English and has access to high-speed internet on her laptop. She is interested in participating in the Birthly study as she is experiencing pregnancy-related anxiety and is hoping that the online childbirth education platform will provide her with the necessary tools and resources to manage her anxiety and prepare for childbirth. She is receiving prenatal care at the University of Pennsylvania Health System and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic knee pain for several years due to osteoarthritis. The pain has worsened over time, and she has difficulty walking and performing daily activities. She has been scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty with a participating surgeon to help alleviate the chronic pain. She is able to follow the study protocol and speaks English fluently. She has no history of hepatic or renal insufficiency, is between the ages of 18 and 80, and has a planned use of regional anesthesia. She does not have any allergies or intolerances to the study medications, but her BMI is above 40. She has no history of diabetes or chronic gabapentin/pregabalin use, but she has been taking opioids for her chronic knee pain for the past 6 months.

A 28-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 volunteered for this clinical trial. She has no history of any significant medical condition, gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease. Her family history is negative for long QT syndrome. She has no ongoing allergies or hypersensitivity. She has normal veins and is comfortable with repeated venipuncture. She has no history of claustrophobia and has undergone an MRI scan in the past with normal results. She is of non-childbearing potential and has provided signed, written and dated informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia 3 months ago. She received frontline therapy and achieved hematologic complete remission. However, her disease has now relapsed with a value of at least 1 x 10^-4 (0.01%) by multicolor flow cytometry and/or by next generation sequencing (NGS). She has no active or co-existing malignancy with a life expectancy of at least 12 months. Her performance status is 1. Her creatinine clearance is 60 ml/minute, and her bilirubin level is within normal limits. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has no active or uncontrolled disease/infection as judged by the treating physician. She is willing to sign the consent form. She has not received monoclonal antibodies therapy within the last 2 weeks before the study entry. She is not known to be human immunodeficiency virus positive (HIV+). She does not have active central nervous system (CNS) or extramedullary disease. She is not receiving any investigational drug within the last 2 weeks before study entry.

The patient is a sedentary 35-year-old woman diagnosed with obesity with a BMI of 35 kg/m2. She does not have a history of diabetes, liver or renal diseases, major cardiovascular events, bariatric surgery, or sleep apnea. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has not undergone any weight changes greater than 3 kg in the last 3 months and is not taking any medication or steroids. She works regular hours and has a normal sleep pattern. She has not been diagnosed with any allergies or viral infections. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help researchers investigate the regulation of de novo lipogenesis in adipose tissue and its relationship to insulin sensitivity in obese individuals.

A 60-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 3+4. The patient has no prior treatment for prostate cancer and has declined conventional treatment options such as active surveillance, radical prostatectomy, radiation therapy, cryosurgery, and hormone therapy. The patient has undergone a bone scan and CT abdomen/pelvis within the last 6 months, with negative results for metastases. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 10 years and is in good health, with an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) criteria of II. The patient has undergone a multi-parametric MRI at UCLA within the last 6 months, demonstrating a region of interest (ROI) of MRI suspicion level 3 or higher with a calculated prostate volume of 60cc. The patient has undergone a transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy with more than 10 systematic biopsy cores and more than 2 MRI-ultrasound fusion targeted biopsy cores from above the MRI-derived ROI, which confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. The patient desires focal therapy and is willing to sign informed consent for the FLA treatment through the 12-month follow-up visit. The patient does not have any significant cancer outside of the MRI target (ROI) area, and does not have any active urinary tract infection or prostate abscess, chronic or acute prostatitis, or neurogenic bladder. The patient is not currently taking any 5-alpha reductase inhibitors and does not have any significant rectal surgery, rectal fissure, fibrosis, stenosis, or other anatomic abnormality precluding insertion of transrectal device.

A 56-year-old female patient has been admitted to the intensive care unit with a diagnosis of sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome. The patient has been receiving continuous enteral feeding through a nasogastric tube, however, she has been experiencing intolerance to the feeding with gastric residual volume more than 250 ml checked by aspiration technique. The patient has no known allergies to interventional drugs or acetaminophen. She has not received any study drugs or metoclopramide within 24 hours of inclusion. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or surgery on GI system within 24 hours of inclusion. She does not have Crohn's disease, GI perforation or obstruction, short bowel syndrome, or liver failure. The patient's transaminase enzymes, prothrombin time, and total bilirubin levels are within normal limits. The patient is not on hemodialysis or CRRT, and she is not hemodynamically unstable. She has a mean arterial pressure of 85 mmHg and is not receiving any inotropes or vasopressors. The patient's hemoglobin concentration is 9.5 mg%, which is above the exclusion criteria. The patient is not pregnant, and her actual body weight is within 1.5 times the ideal body weight. The patient does not have Myasthenia Gravis or a history of opioid drug abuse.

The patient is a 62-year-old female who has recently suffered a new onset stroke. She is currently admitted to the inpatient rehabilitation unit at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. She has the ability to follow one-step commands and has achieved a total score of at least 5/6 item pairs on the Complex Ideational Material-Short Form from the Boston Diagnostic Aphasia Examination and a total score of 16 or greater on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment with a score of 6/6 on the orientation subtest. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities and is willing and able to participate in the study. The patient is motivated to participate in cognitive motor therapy using a videogame platform to enhance her cognitive and sensorimotor abilities.

A 35-year-old male with a history of occasional low back pain presents to the orthopedic clinic with a three-day history of worsening pain. The pain is localized to the lower back and is described as a dull ache with occasional sharp, stabbing pain. The patient reports no history of trauma or recent strenuous activity. He denies any other associated symptoms such as numbness, tingling or weakness in the legs. The patient is generally healthy, does not smoke or consume alcohol, and has no significant past medical history. On examination, the patient has positive Gower's sign, painful arc of motion and poor reversal of lumbopelvic rhythm. The straight leg raise test is greater than ninety-one degrees. The patient meets 3 of the 4 clinical prediction rules for lumbar stabilization. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has access to the video-based exercise instructions.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive breast cancer four months ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. She is now scheduled to receive adjuvant chemotherapy for six cycles. She is concerned about the potential cognitive side effects of chemotherapy, as she has noticed some mild memory problems in the past few months. She lives with her husband, who assists her with daily activities. She is fluent in English, has completed high school, and is retired. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve or maintain cognitive function during chemotherapy.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) and has had multiple relapses of diarrhea despite multiple courses of antibiotics. He was previously treated with Fecal Transplant (FMT) with successful resolution of his symptoms. However, he has had a recent relapse of CDI and is now being considered for another FMT. He is currently an inpatient and has no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo a colonoscopy to obtain biopsies and stool specimens for analysis. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he is able to provide informed consent.

54-year-old male diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy 4 months ago, and deemed free of disease at last assessment. The patient is scheduled for a follow-up clinic visit with a provider who has agreed to participate in the trial to evaluate the effectiveness of HN-STAR in the management of head and neck cancer survivors. The patient is able to read and speak English, and is cognitively and physically able to complete study surveys. The patient is willing to complete study assessments via smartphone, tablet or computer 3, 6, and 9 months after the designated clinic visit. The patient has no prior history of cancer other than non-melanoma skin disease and has received both chemotherapy and radiation therapy as treatment for head and neck cancer. The patient has no concurrent enrollment in other interventional symptom management study protocols, and is willing to participate in the trial. The patient's primary care provider is willing to complete a brief, confidential telephone interview conducted by the research team.

The patient description for this clinical trial is not applicable as it is a cohort study aiming to recruit all newborns from patients treated with ART in the center, without any specific patient characteristics or criteria for enrollment. Therefore, the study is not looking for specific patients to participate, but rather all newborns born from patients treated with assisted reproductive technology at the Reproductive Medical Center, First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University in China.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with liver cancer. The patient has a history of hepatitis B and has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and fatigue for the past few months. The patient has been referred for liver resection and has agreed to participate in the study. The patient has no known contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging and is willing to undergo the necessary tests and procedures. The patient has no other significant underlying diseases or disorders that may limit their ability to participate in the study. The patient is fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent.

A 45-year-old non-smoking woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 3 years ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial to analyze respiratory mechanics in patients with RA. She has not experienced any respiratory symptoms or complications related to her RA. She takes methotrexate and corticosteroids for her RA as prescribed by her rheumatologist. She has no history of lung disease, heart disease, or other chronic illnesses. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She is enthusiastic about contributing to medical research and willing to undergo respiratory function tests as part of the study.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with a neuroendocrine tumor based on previous imaging studies. He has a history of chronic abdominal pain, weight loss, and diarrhea. He has tried various medications for symptom relief, but with limited success. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman, who is a single mother of two children, has been struggling with alcohol use disorder (AUD) for the past 3 years. She has been in and out of treatment programs, but has not been able to maintain sobriety. She is enrolled in Vermont Medicaid and has an Android smartphone. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to address her AUD. She has no current suicidal intent and has been assessed as needing Level 3.1 care. She is motivated to participate in the trial to help herself and to contribute to the advancement of treatment options for others with AUD.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is sexually active and has never been diagnosed with HIV. He is a graduate student and lives alone in a rented apartment near the university campus. He enjoys playing soccer and basketball with friends on weekends. He has never been involved in any intravenous drug use or other high-risk behaviors that could put him at risk for HIV infection. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His BMI is within the normal range and his blood pressure is 120/80. He has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to vaccines. He is willing to undergo the required HIV testing and understands that this study is designed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of an experimental HIV vaccine. He has completed the questionnaire to assess his understanding of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He is not currently using any form of contraception but agrees to use an acceptable method during the study period if he becomes sexually active. He has never received any smallpox immunization or HIV vaccine in previous studies.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with no known medical conditions. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and does not smoke or consume alcohol. He does not use any prescription or over-the-counter medications. He has a sedentary lifestyle but is willing to follow the study protocol which includes refraining from physical activity for a certain period of time. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is willing to comply with the study restrictions. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to medical research and to learn more about his own health.

42-year-old female diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus for over 5 years. Patient has been using a Medtronic pump (Minimed 530G) for continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) in a basal-bolus regimen with a rapid-acting insulin analogue for the past 2 years. Patient's current HbA1c level is 8.5% (69 mmol/mol). Patient has a BMI of 31 kg/m^2. Patient is willing to take at least 3 daily meal-time insulin bolus infusions every day throughout the trial. Patient has not had any myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina or transient ischaemic attack within the past 180 days prior to the day of screening. Patient does not have any planned coronary, carotid or peripheral artery revascularisation. Patient has not been hospitalized for ketoacidosis in the past 180 days prior to the day of screening. Patient has not been treated with any medication for the indication of diabetes or obesity other than stated in the inclusion criteria in a period of 90 days before screening.

28 year-old male who identifies as gay and has had multiple sexual partners over the past six months. He has not consistently used condoms during anal sex and has tested negative for HIV within the past month. He reports occasional use of recreational drugs during sexual encounters. He has been assessed by a healthcare provider and deemed eligible for PrEP due to his high risk of HIV acquisition. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the impact of PrEP on his sexual and psychological health, as well as his adherence to the medication.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer after undergoing a colonoscopy for rectal bleeding. The biopsy results confirmed an adenocarcinoma, and a CT scan revealed multiple liver metastases. The patient has no history of previous treatment for metastatic disease and has an ECOG performance status of 1. Her blood counts (WBC, platelets, hemoglobin) are within normal limits. Her bilirubin level is 1.2 times the upper limit of normal, and her alkaline phosphatase level is 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. Her proteinuria is negative by dipstick, and her 24-hour urine collection shows 0.5 g of protein. The patient has no evidence of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and has no serious, non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture. She has no significant ophthalmologic abnormality. The patient has undergone no major surgical procedure or open biopsy in the last 28 days. The patient is not pregnant, and she is willing to use effective contraception during the study. The patient has measurable lesions on CT scan that are at least 20 mm in one dimension. She has no evidence of CNS disease, and she has no exclusive bone metastasis. The patient is eligible for the induction therapy with bevacizumab combined with either modified FOLFOX7, XELOX2, or FOLFIRI. If she has stable or responding disease after induction therapy, she will be randomized to receive maintenance therapy with either bevacizumab alone or bevacizumab+erlotinib.

John is a 56-year-old man who visited his primary care physician after experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and nocturia. He underwent a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) test which revealed an elevated PSA level of 6.4 ng/mL. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed which revealed a low-risk prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 3+3 involving 2 cores, each with less than 50% involvement. He was referred to The Center for Cancer Prevention and Treatment at St. Joseph Hospital to participate in the active surveillance program. John is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is able to comply with the scheduled follow-up appointments. He is married and has two grown children. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing golf and hiking in his free time. He is concerned about the possibility of needing treatment for his prostate cancer but is open to the option of active surveillance to avoid unnecessary side effects of definitive therapy.

Sophie is a 10-month-old female infant who was recently diagnosed with galactosialidosis after experiencing developmental delays and recurrent infections. She was born to non-consanguineous parents and her birth and neonatal history were unremarkable. Sophie's physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly, coarse facial features, and mild hypotonia. Further testing including urine analysis, blood work, and genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of galactosialidosis. Her family has no history of lysosomal storage disorders or other genetic conditions. The family was referred to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital for further evaluation and management. Sophie's parents are interested in participating in clinical trials that may help improve their daughter's condition and are willing to provide medical records and participate in telephonic interviews.

A 45 year old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer in 2015 after experiencing persistent pain in her left breast. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of HER2 negative breast cancer. She was treated with several rounds of chemotherapy and endocrine therapy, but her cancer progressed despite treatment. She has provided written consent allowing for data and samples to be used in the future and is willing to participate in this study. The patient has historical HER2 fixed tissue IHC stained slides and is eligible for the study as she meets all the inclusion criteria. She has no history of other malignancies and her historical HER2 status is IHC 0.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer. She underwent optimal debulking surgery less than 6 months ago and has not received any prior chemotherapy. She has a performance status of 1 and her blood counts are within normal limits. She does not have any CNS or brain metastases. She has no major medical conditions except for her ovarian cancer. She is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She has no psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that would prevent medical follow-up or compliance with the study protocol. She has not had a myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, transient ischemic attack, or unstable angina within the past 6 months. She has no uncontrollable nausea, clinically significant peripheral vascular disease, abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess. She is not hypersensitive to any component of pemetrexed disodium. She is able to take folic acid, vitamin B12, and dexamethasone according to protocol. She has not received more than 4 courses of carboplatin and paclitaxel IV as neoadjuvant chemotherapy for advanced, unresectable disease. She is not receiving concurrent antineoplastic or antitumor agents not part of the study therapy. She meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

A 25-year-old female visited the emergency department of the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics with the complaint of chest pain and shortness of breath. She was evaluated by the ED team and diagnosed with pneumonia. The patient was prescribed medication and advised to follow-up with Family Medicine as an outpatient. She is fluent in English and comfortable with text messaging. She has a smartphone with text messaging capabilities. The patient has no history of following up with the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics Family Medicine before. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 62-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) a few months ago. He has a history of cirrhosis due to alcohol use. The patient has undergone radiofrequency ablation (RFA) treatment for his HCC and is now experiencing recurrence with a discrete hypervascular tumor present on two consecutive imaging studies. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently well-controlled with medication. He is married with two adult children and lives with his wife. He is retired and enjoys gardening and reading. He has no history of smoking or drug use. He is currently not experiencing any symptoms from the tumor. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options and potentially help others in the future.

14-year-old female with a history of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is scheduled for posterior spinal fusion correction surgery. The patient has no known coagulopathy or platelet dysfunction. The patient has been experiencing increased back pain and decreased range of motion in recent months. The patient and her parents have been educated on the risks and benefits of the surgery and have provided informed consent. The patient will be closely monitored during and after surgery for any adverse events. The patient will be eligible for discharge once they meet the predetermined discharge criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cervical lymph node metastasis from an unknown primary tumor. The patient has undergone radical modified dissection of the neck within the past 8 weeks and has R0 or R1 disease after the procedure. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1 and she has a Karnofsky score of 80%. The patient has no other prior or concurrent malignancy except for adequately treated basal cell skin cancer. The patient is willing and able to complete quality of life questionnaires and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient's fertility status is unknown. The patient has not received any prior therapy for carcinoma of unknown primary except neck dissection. The patient is eligible to participate in a randomized phase III trial to compare different radiation therapy regimens for the treatment of metastases to the lymph nodes in the neck from an unknown primary tumor.

55 y/o female presenting with symptoms of pelvic statics disorders including genital dryness, irritation, burning, and itching of vulvas and vagina. The patient also reports decreased lubrication, discomfort, and pain during sexual activity, as well as decreased arousal, orgasm, and desire. The patient has not undergone any previous surgeries for pelvic organ prolapse or urinary incontinence, and does not have any chronic medical illnesses or liver disease. The patient's BMI is below 35 kg/m2, and there is no history of thromboembolic disease or hormone-dependent malignancies. The patient has not used medication or phytoestrogens within the last month before the start of the study, and there are no conflicts with their partner regarding sexual disorders.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) for the past 2 years. He has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), recurrent prostatic bleeding, and recurrent acute urinary retention. He has tried medical treatments for his BPH, but they have not provided significant relief. The patient has no history of coagulation disorders or previous prostatic surgery. He has not taken finasteride before. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of liver or renal impairment. The patient is fit for surgery and has consented to participate in the clinical trial. His prostate size is between 60-100 grams, and there is no evidence of bladder pathology or suspected/proved cancer prostate.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been suffering from osteoarthritis of the knee joint for the past few years. He has been experiencing severe pain and limitation of movement, which has significantly affected his quality of life. The patient has been advised by his orthopedic surgeon to undergo a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) to relieve his symptoms. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history, but he has a family history of hypertension. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has agreed to be randomized to one of the three nerve blocks being studied. He does not have any psychiatric illnesses or allergies to medications, and he has not been taking opioids on a regular basis.

The patient is a 67-year-old retired teacher who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 2 years. She is in Hoehn and Yahr stage 1 and has no motor fluctuations or dyskinesias. She is currently taking levodopa-carbidopa, pramipexole, and amantadine for her PD symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are currently well-controlled with medication. She lives alone and has no history of falls or cognitive impairment. She is concerned about her memory and cognitive abilities and is interested in participating in a cognitive training program to improve her brain function. She has no history of dementia and has good visual acuity. She is willing to commit to the study requirements and is available for the scheduled assessments and training sessions.

A 35-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 15 years has been using the Omnipod® insulin patch pump and Abbott FreeStyleLibre sensor® for the past 5 years.
