Her A1C has been fluctuating between 7.5% to 8.5% despite her best efforts to manage her diabetes with lifestyle modifications and insulin therapy. She has no known allergies to nickel or adhesive. She is currently using rapid insulin except FIASP with a maximum of 60 IU per day. She is affiliated with the French social security system and is able to understand the study information and provide written informed consent. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and has no psychiatric disorders or rapidly progressing ischemic or proliferative retinopathy before laser treatment. She is interested in participating in the trial to explore the potential benefits of the MEDTRUM A7+ TouchCare insulin patch pump over the Omnipod® patch pump for better management of her diabetes.

A 10-year-old male patient was referred to the Clinic by his school counselor. His parents reported that their son had difficulty making friends and often preferred to be alone. He also had a hard time in social situations and would become visibly anxious and upset. The patient's academic performance was also declining, and he was struggling to keep up with his peers. Upon evaluation, the patient was diagnosed with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder and anxiety, specifically social phobia. He scored above 70 on the IQ test and spoke English fluently as his primary language. The patient's parents consented to enroll him in the cognitive-behavioral therapy clinical trial for children with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder and anxiety.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with systemic sclerosis. She has been experiencing skin tightening, particularly on her hands and face. She has also noticed difficulty swallowing and has experienced occasional heartburn. She has no history of smoking or illicit drug use. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is currently taking over-the-counter antacids for her heartburn symptoms. Her physical exam is notable for tight and shiny skin on her hands and face, and her skin score is 20. She has no significant medical history and her lab studies are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential treatment options for her condition.

A 54-year-old female presents with multiple skin lesions on her face, scalp, and arms. She reports that the lesions have been present for several months and have increased in number over time. She has not received any treatment for them in the past 3 months. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of actinic keratosis (Olsen grade I/II). Her laboratory values are within normal limits. She is in good general health and is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and uses oral contraceptives. She has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 3 months.

A 25-year-old female who works as a nurse is interested in participating in the Glycaemic Response to a Liquid Meal Tolerance Test clinical trial. She has a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2 and has no history of diabetes or gastric bypass surgery. She is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies to dairy or soy. She undergoes a finger-stick glucose test, and her fasting plasma glucose level is 82 mg/dl (4.6 mmol/L). She is willing to provide written informed consent and is looking forward to contributing to the study.

This is a 50 year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) for the past 5 years. He is currently on a stable dose of metformin therapy for the past 3 months. His HbA1c level at screening was 7.5%. He has a BMI of 30 kg/m^2, a resting supine blood pressure of 140/80 mmHg, and a normal 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) with QTcB interval of 430 msec. He has no major illnesses in the past 3 months and has no significant chronic medical illnesses not related to diabetes. He has no history of gastrointestinal diseases influencing drug absorption, no history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse, and has not participated in any clinical trial within the past 3 months. He has not donated or lost blood in the past 3 months and is not currently taking any anti-diabetic therapy other than metformin. He has no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications or components thereof and has no active neoplastic disease or history of neoplastic disease within 5 years of study entry. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study, able to comply with the protocol requirements, and able to communicate in person and by telephone in a manner that allows all protocol procedures to be carried out safely and reliably in the opinion of the investigative site staff.

79-year-old female with chronic neurologic disease, residing in a nursing home for long-term care, who has experienced falls and difficulty swallowing in the past. She is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the feasibility of using sign displays to communicate fall, dehydration, and pulmonary aspiration risks in nursing homes. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with monthly interviews. The patient has some mild cognitive impairment but is able to understand the study requirements and procedures. She will undergo a brief screening assessment to determine her risk of falling, dysphagia, and dehydration and will be given a corresponding risk display by the investigator. The patient will be monitored for a minimum of 3 months, with daily recording of events and monthly assessments. The study aims to improve communication among health professionals to prevent adverse events and improve the patient's overall quality-of-life.

The patient is a 65-year-old male veteran who has been taking Ativan for anxiety for the past 6 months. He has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has noticed that his thinking and concentration have been affected. He has a history of falls and is concerned that the medication may be contributing to his balance problems. He has a primary care provider at the VA and has access to a smartphone and computer. He is interested in participating in a trial to help him reduce or stop taking Ativan.

A 24-year old female student is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is healthy, with no significant past medical history. Her family has no history of major illnesses. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 58 kg. She is a non-smoker, doesn't consume alcohol or use any illicit drugs. Her diet is balanced and includes fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins. She is on no medications or supplements. She is willing to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She is an active individual who enjoys yoga and jogging.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent a mastectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She is currently taking tamoxifen and vitamin D supplements. She reports having frequent hot flashes (more than 14 per week) which make her uncomfortable and affect her daily life activities. She prefers not to take hormones due to her history of breast cancer. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with losartan. She has no history of asthma, COPD, or congestive heart failure. She is post-menopausal and has a CD player at home. Her family history is negative for breast cancer. Her lab study is as follows: BP: 120/80 mm Hg, FBS: 95mg/dl, HbA1c: 5.7%, cholesterol: 190 mg/dl, TG: 120 mg/dl, LDL: 110 mg/dl, HDL: 45 mg/dl.

This is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with hypertension. She has been taking a low dose of amlodipine for the past 4 weeks but her blood pressure remains elevated at 160/100 mmHg. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of a new hypertension medication. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and understands that she may have to stop taking her current medication for the duration of the trial. She has no history of cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events and has not been diagnosed with any hematopoietic disorders. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to contribute to the development of new treatments for hypertension.

The patient is a 58-year-old female with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. She has had a previous myocardial infarction and has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement. She is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. During her pre-operative evaluation for cardiovascular surgery, she is found to have a malnutrition universal screening tool (MUST) score of 2. She has lost 5% of her body weight over the past month due to poor appetite and nausea. She denies any significant dysphagia or difficulty chewing. Her lab results show a serum albumin level of 3.2 g/dL and a total lymphocyte count of 1100/mm3. She has been referred to participate in a randomized controlled pilot study evaluating the use of oral nutritional supplementation in nutritionally at-risk cardiovascular surgery patients. She will receive the oral nutritional supplement for 30 days prior to surgery, continuing throughout her surgical hospitalization and until hospital discharge.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a body mass index of 23 kg/m2 and a blood pressure of 128/82 mmHg. He is a social drinker, consuming an average of one drink per day and has not had an episode of binge drinking over the previous 30 days. He is willing to maintain his current diet and physical activity pattern throughout the trial and consume the standard meal provided by GI Labs the evening before each test day. The patient is willing to abstain from strenuous exercise, alcoholic drinks, and cannabis use 24 hours before study visits and to refrain from driving or operating any vehicle when leaving GI Labs after the test visit. He is willing to sign a statement acknowledging that he has consumed alcohol that morning and to maintain current dietary supplement use throughout the trial. The patient has no major illness or surgery requiring hospitalization within 3 months of the first study visit after screening and no history of cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal or hepatic disease. He is eligible to receive income in Canada and is covered by a health insurance such as OHIP. The patient understands the study procedures and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study and authorization to release relevant protected health information to the study investigator. He is willing to

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with heart failure for the past year. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and reduced exercise tolerance for the past 6 months. His current medications include enalapril, furosemide, and spironolactone. He has a history of hypertension, but it is currently well-controlled. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is less than 40%. He reports feeling weak and tired most of the time and has difficulty completing daily activities. His hemoglobin concentration is between 9.0 and 12.5 g/dL. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his functional status and increase his exercise tolerance.

A 7-year-old male child presents with short stature and a height less than the 5th percentile for his age and sex. He has decelerated growth velocity of less than 5 centimeters per year and radiographic evidence of delayed bone age (greater than 1 SD below the mean for his chronological age). Provocative testing with two growth hormone secretagogues (insulin and arginine) failed to raise his serum GH concentrations to 10 microgram/Liter. The child is prepubertal as determined by Tanner staging. He has no history of smoking or illicit drug use, nor does he have any known hepatic, renal, cardiac, or thyroid disorders. The child is not currently taking any medications known to induce or inhibit hepatic CYP1A2, NAT-2, XO, CYP2D6, or CYP3A4 activity. He has no history of hypersensitivity reactions to dextromethorphan or caffeine. The child has not received prior treatment with rhGH or corticosteroids or thyroid hormone. He is willing to be enrolled in the clinical trial to understand the effect of rhGH therapy on hepatic drug metabolism.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of heart failure and an ejection fraction of 30%. He has been on optimal medical therapy, including beta-blockers, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, and diuretics for the past year. He has been experiencing symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and fatigue, despite medical therapy. His echocardiogram shows a left bundle branch block, and he is deemed eligible for cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator (CRT-D) device implantation according to the latest ESC guidelines. He has no previous LV lead implant attempts and is due for de-novo implantation of a Platinium 4LV CRT-D device (or any newer 4LV CRT-D model manufactured by MicroPort CRM). He is able to read and understand the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. His renal function is normal, and he has no history of myocardial infarction or cardiac revascularization within the past 40 days. The patient has no known tricuspid valvular disease or any type of tricuspid replacement heart valve (mechanical or tissue). He is not currently enrolled in another clinical study and has no history of drug addiction.

A 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with severe COPD and has been receiving long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) for the past 2 years. Despite LTOT, he has experienced several exacerbations in the past year, leading to hospitalizations and courses of antibiotics and prednisolone. He has difficulty walking and performing basic daily tasks due to his respiratory insufficiency. He does not smoke and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to potentially improve his quality of life and reduce the number of exacerbations he experiences. He speaks Danish fluently and is capable of handling the Airvo warm humidifier after instruction.

The patient is a 27 year old woman who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and has decided to terminate the pregnancy. She is seeking a safe and effective method to do so and has been informed about the option of using a Foley catheter. She has an unfavourable cervix and is willing to participate in this study to determine the efficacy of the two most commonly used insufflation volumes of Foley catheter (30mL and 50mL). She has a singleton pregnancy and has no history of multiple pregnancies. She is in good general health and has no known medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She has provided informed consent and is willing to follow all study procedures and attend all required follow-up appointments.

A 60-year-old male who suffered a stroke 9 months ago and has been experiencing chronic hemiplegia on his right side. He is currently undergoing rehabilitation therapy to improve his mobility, including physiotherapy sessions 3 times a week. The patient is able to walk with the assistance of a cane, but he tires quickly and has difficulty walking for long periods of time. He has no other medical conditions and is currently taking medications for hypertension. He is motivated to improve his mobility and willing to participate in a physiotherapy intervention to achieve this goal.

The patient is a 50-year-old non-smoking man who had undergone coronary bypass surgery three months ago. He was diagnosed with progressive atherosclerosis confirmed by angiography. His fasting blood cholesterol levels at the time of entry were in the range of 185. The patient has been advised to participate in the Cholesterol-Lowering Atherosclerosis Study (CLAS) to determine whether combined therapy with the lipid lowering agents colestipol hydrochloride plus niacin would produce significant change in coronary, carotid, and femoral artery atherosclerosis and coronary bypass graft lesions as determined by angiography. The patient is willing to undergo the study procedures and follow the prescribed diet and medication regimen. He understands that the study is randomized and selectively-blinded and that he may receive either 30 grams (g) of colestipol hydrochloride plus 3 to 12 g of niacin daily or to placebo, in addition to diet intervention. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would preclude his participation in this trial.

This is a 56-year-old male with a past medical history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who is currently undergoing induction chemotherapy at Princess Margaret Hospital (PMH). The patient has been prescribed voriconazole as prophylaxis against invasive fungal infections (IFI) due to the high risk associated with his condition. The patient has also undergone fine needle aspirate and bronchoalveolar lavage, which have shown probable or proven fungal infections. Imaging studies have revealed crescent signs suggestive of invasive fungal infections. The patient is able to tolerate oral intake of medications. The patient has no history of severe mucositis, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea or neutropenic enterocolitis.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with ovarian cancer three years ago after presenting with abdominal pain and bloating. She underwent maximum cytoreductive surgery followed by intraperitoneal and intravenous chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She achieved complete remission after the initial treatment but unfortunately, the cancer recurred after 14 months. She underwent salvage chemotherapy with cisplatin and gemcitabine and achieved a second complete remission. She completed 6 cycles of chemotherapy and was closely monitored with imaging and CA-125 levels. During her regular follow-up, a recurrence was detected in the peritoneal cavity, and she underwent cytoreductive surgery again followed by a third-line chemotherapy with carboplatin and liposomal doxorubicin. She achieved a third complete remission and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the possibility of consolidation treatment with catumaxomab. She is generally in good health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no significant medical history and her laboratory parameters are within normal limits. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and has given her informed consent to participate in this trial.

As this clinical trial is focused on school-age adolescents, the patient description will be based on that age group. The patient is a 14-year-old female student in grade 9 at a local high school. She has a history of getting sick easily and missing school due to colds and flu. Her parents are concerned about her health and want her to receive all recommended vaccines. However, they have not been able to keep track of her vaccination schedule and often forget to sign consent forms for vaccinations at school. The student is interested in receiving the vaccines but has not been able to independently schedule appointments or get vaccinated due to transportation and other logistical barriers. She is generally healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. She is motivated to participate in the study and hopes that the intervention will make it easier for her and her parents to keep track of her vaccinations and get them done on time.

The patient is a newborn baby girl who was born prematurely at 28 weeks with a birth weight of 1200 grams. She is currently being cared for in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to her premature birth. She has been stable for the past 72 hours with no active infections or episodes of apnea. She has not been diagnosed with any genetic anomalies, chromosomal aberrations, or congenital heart malformations. Her ultrasound showed no signs of intraventricular hemorrhage or periventricular leukomalacia. She passed her bilateral hearing screening test with Automated Auditory Brainstem Response testing. Her parents have given informed consent for her to participate in the study investigating the effects of different music genres on heart rate variability in extremely and very low birth weight newborns.

A 60 year old male with a diagnosis of bladder cancer has been scheduled for an elective robot-assisted laparoscopic radical cystectomy. He has no significant past medical history aside from hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. He is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the effects of lung-protective ventilation during the surgery. He has not had any previous lung surgeries and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who gave birth to a healthy baby girl three days ago. She is currently staying at a perinatal care center in Germany. Her room receives many visitors, including her relatives and friends, who come to see her and the newborn baby. The patient is concerned about the risk of infections from the visitors or personnel, especially since her baby is still very young and vulnerable to infections. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce the risk of infection associated with visitors and personnel on perinatal care stations. She is willing to follow the study protocol, which may include special measures such as voice prompts for hand disinfection. She is able to provide informed consent and has sufficient language skills to understand the study requirements.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman in her 35th week of pregnancy. She has had a healthy pregnancy so far with no complications. During the most recent ultrasound, it was discovered that her baby is in breech presentation. The patient is concerned about the potential risks of a breech birth and is willing to consider external cephalic version to attempt to turn the baby into the head-down position. She has no history of placenta previa or fetal abnormalities. The patient is able to give written consent and has no limitations in her ability to do so.

The patient is a 56-year-old man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 10 years ago. He has been able to maintain good glycemic control with a combination of metformin and glipizide. However, his most recent blood tests showed elevated serum creatinine (1.7 mg/dL) and proteinuria of 500 mg/24 hours. Despite being on an ACE inhibitor, his blood pressure remains slightly elevated at 140/90 mmHg. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has no known history of heart disease or stroke. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the effects of rosiglitazone on his renal function and proteinuria.

A 35-year-old woman is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. She has no significant medical history or allergies to medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. The anesthesiologist will be using neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) during the procedure to facilitate surgery. The patient has consented to participate in a study evaluating a novel train of four (TOF) stimulator that assesses the neuromuscular junction of a patient under anesthesia. The goal of the study is to evaluate the efficacy and accuracy of the device in comparison to the standard of care with a hand-held stimulator. The device will be applied to a suitable anatomic location for TOF stimulation/monitoring, and an electrical pulse will be applied to stimulate the patient's motor point. The location for this stimulation will be on the patient's forearm over the ulnar nerve area or on the patient's face in the distribution of the facial nerve. The responses measured by the device will be recorded electronically and compared to the anesthesiologist's interpretation of the number of muscle twitches induced by peripheral motor point stimulation. The device application and monitoring will be carried out at different time points in the procedure, under the same conditions as the currently utilized peripheral nerve stimulators to judge neuromuscular transmission and anesthesia effectiveness. The patient will be monitored pre- and post-surgery following the current standard of care. The study includes normal, healthy subjects (adults) admitted for surgical procedures, and the patient meets the inclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female patient who had contracted polio during childhood came to the clinic with complaints of pain, weakness, and fatigue. She has been experiencing these symptoms for many decades. She has a history of polio with partial or complete neurological and functional recovery. Her function has been stable for more than 15 years. She has new onset of muscle weakness in one or more limb muscles, as determined by history and clinical examination. She has no other neurological diseases or conditions that may account for the symptoms or interfere with the experimental interventions. She has no implanted devices, such as pumps, pacemakers, or metal fragments in the skull or eye. She is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old male veteran who served in Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Iraqi Freedom presented to the clinic with symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). He reported experiencing nightmares, flashbacks, and hypervigilance. He also has difficulty sleeping and constantly feels on edge. He has been on medication for PTSD for the past year, but has not noticed any significant improvement. He is still able to work but it has been difficult for him to maintain relationships. He has internet and smart phone access and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman with a personal history of treated melanoma. She has undergone surgical excision of a melanoma lesion on her left arm two years ago and has not had any evidence of disease since then. She has a family history of melanoma, with her father having been diagnosed with the disease at age 55. The patient has a high-risk mole phenotype, with more than 50 normal moles on her body. She has access to a computer connected to the internet and is not currently adhering to recommendations for skin self-examination. The patient is proficient in speaking and reading English and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic rhinosinusitis for the past 5 years. She reports nasal congestion, postnasal drip, facial pressure, and diminished sense of smell. She has tried multiple medical treatments, including nasal sprays and antibiotics, but her symptoms persist. She is scheduled to undergo endoscopic sinus surgery with the placement of a steroid-eluting nasal spacer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine whether she will need to take oral steroid pills after the surgery. She has no other significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. She is fluent in English and is able to complete all study evaluations and questionnaires. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 57-year-old female with a medical history of osteoarthritis and bone pain. She has been experiencing dyspepsia and gastric discomfort while taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for her arthritis symptoms. She has not had any history of gastrointestinal hemorrhage or peptic ulcer complications. She has tested negative for H. pylori during screening tests. The patient is expected to require regular anti-inflammatory therapy for arthritis symptom management. She is not taking any anti-ulcer medications, COX-2 inhibitors, or double anti-platelet therapy. She has not had gastric or duodenal surgery and does not have any other conditions that may increase risk or decrease the chance of obtaining satisfactory data for the study objectives.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with resistant hypertension. He has been on multiple antihypertensive medications but his blood pressure remains elevated (daytime systolic ambulatory BP >135mmHg). He has no history of myocardial infarction or any cardiovascular event within the past 3 months. He has not been diagnosed with heart failure and has a normal LVEF. He is not taking psychotropic agents, antidepressants, or NSAIDs. He drinks alcohol occasionally but not more than 2 standard drinks in a day. He has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to minocycline or other tetracyclines. He has signed the informed consent to participate in the study.

John is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of atrial fibrillation such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He has never had an ablation procedure before and is interested in exploring this option. He is willing to sign the consent form and has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He has no contraindications for the ablation procedure, and recent imaging shows no thrombus in his left atrium.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the liver and bones. The patient has failed or is not a candidate for standard therapies and is seeking alternative treatments. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 and is medically able to tolerate a high fat meal and to fast as per protocol. The patient is expected to have a survival time of at least 3 months in the opinion of the Investigator. The patient has no prior history of treatment with an Hsp90 inhibitor, and has not used antacids within 7 days of Study Day 1. The patient has not undergone major surgery or radiation within 28 days of the first dose of BIIB021, and has no uncontrolled, severe medical illness that could compromise protocol objectives. The patient has not had a history of gastrectomy or major surgery to small intestine, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, chronic diarrhea, or any thrombotic event occurred <3 months prior to Day 1. The patient is not currently experiencing any active bacterial or viral infection requiring concurrent treatment, and has no history of hepatitis B or C or human immunodeficiency virus. The patient has not experienced central nervous system metastasis or any conditions that may predispose them to seizures, such as a history of seizure or previous significant head trauma, drug or alcohol abuse.

A 62-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease has been taking statins for the past 6 months to manage his high cholesterol levels. Despite his medication, his recent blood tests showed that his triglyceride levels are still high (2.1 mmol/L). He is otherwise healthy, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol socially. He has a family history of heart disease, and his father had a heart attack at the age of 55. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Gefarnate Tablets in lowering his triglyceride levels and reducing his risk of future cardiovascular events.

43 yo F with a history of locally recurrent breast cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. She initially underwent lumpectomy and radiation therapy, followed by 6 cycles of chemotherapy with Avastin. She had a partial response to treatment, but during follow-up imaging, it was discovered that there was disease recurrence in the breast and axillary lymph nodes. She underwent mastectomy and lymph node dissection, followed by another 6 cycles of chemotherapy with Avastin. Her most recent imaging showed progression of disease in the lung and liver. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive Avastin in combination with chemotherapy as second- and third-line therapy. She has no other active malignancies, adequate renal function, and no clinically relevant cardiovascular disease. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with a history of vulvar itching, burning, and pain for the past 2 months. She describes the symptoms as severe and interfering with her daily activities, including sexual intercourse. She has no known allergies and has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications. The physical examination reveals white plaques and papules on the vulva with areas of excoriation and echymosis. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of lichen sclerosus. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of LS and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and signs the informed consent. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and agrees to use two forms of birth control during the study.

34 F with a h/o Crohn's disease for the past 3 years, confirmed by radiography and endoscopy. She has been on conventional and biologic therapy for CD, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She presents with moderate to severe CD as assessed by CDAI components of stool frequency (SF), and abdominal pain (AP) scores, and endoscopic evidence. The patient has demonstrated intolerance to conventional and biologic therapy for CD. She has a negative urine pregnancy test result at screening and baseline. The patient does not have any complications of CD such as symptomatic strictures or stenoses, short gut syndrome, or any other manifestation. Additionally, she does not have any medical contraindications preventing her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old female with a history of psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing red, scaly patches on her scalp, elbows, and knees, which have been gradually increasing in size and number. She has not received any systemic or topical treatment for the past 6 weeks. She has no history of erythrodermic psoriasis, pustular psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis. She is willing to undergo NB-UVB therapy as a treatment option for her psoriasis condition. She has no history of any photosensitive disorder or any contraindication to phototherapy exposure.

A 52-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of breast cancer is experiencing a recurrence of the disease with metastasis to the liver and bones. She has undergone surgery and chemotherapy for her breast cancer, but the disease has come back. She is experiencing pain in her bones and fatigue. The patient has a family history of breast cancer, but no other significant medical history. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She is willing to undergo a biopsy procedure for research purposes and understands and agrees to sign the informed consent document for participation in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been recently diagnosed with a primary malignant central nervous system tumor. He underwent an MRI which showed a measurable lesion consistent with the diagnosis. The tumor is located in the right hemisphere of his brain and is causing symptoms such as headaches, dizziness and blurred vision. He is scheduled for surgical resection of the tumor and has been approached to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate a new imaging system for detecting residual tumor tissue during the surgery. He has normal renal and liver function and has not received any prior therapy for the tumor. He is not pregnant or planning to conceive a child within the next 30 days. He has no ongoing serious medical conditions that could put him at increased risk of worsening his condition. He understands the purpose and procedures of the study and is willing to participate.

Patient A is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with Stage II breast cancer 6 months ago. She underwent surgery and is currently receiving endocrine therapy. She has been experiencing menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, and mood swings. She has tried various remedies but has not found any significant relief. She works as a teacher and enjoys spending time with her family. She does not have any other significant medical history, and her current medications include endocrine therapy for breast cancer. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of mind-body medicine in managing her menopausal symptoms. She has read and understands the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Pt is a 42yo F with past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She is a non-smoker with no history of bleeding disorders or favism. The patient is scheduled to undergo an abdominal hysterectomy for symptomatic uterine fibroids. She has no personal history of uterine, ovarian, or cervical cancer. The surgeon has agreed to participate in the trial and the patient is willing to receive 1000mg of intravenous vitamin C a day before and during the surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and has been using clean intermittent self-catheterisation (CISC) for the past year. She suffers from recurrent urinary tract infections (UTI), which are causing her discomfort and affecting her quality of life. She has been prescribed antibiotics for each episode of UTI but is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the potential benefits of antibiotic prophylaxis. She is willing to take a daily low-dose of antibiotics to prevent UTI and is able to adhere to a 12-month follow-up period. The patient is able to take at least one of the recommended prophylactic antibiotics and is not currently taking any medication that would interfere with the study. She understands the study requirements and is able to give informed consent.

This is a 60 year old male with a history of heavy smoking who was recently diagnosed with unresectable Stage III non-small cell lung cancer. He completed primary thoracic chemo-radiotherapy consisting of two cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy and a minimum radiation dose of greater than or equal to 50 Gray, and has stable disease according to the Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST) Version 1.0. His platelet count is greater than or equal to 140 * 10^9 per liter, white blood cell (WBC) greater than or equal to 2.5 * 10^9 per liter, and hemoglobin greater than or equal to 90 gram per liter. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 1. He has no history of previous lung cancer specific therapy other than primary chemo-radiotherapy, and has not received immunotherapy or investigational systemic drugs within 4 weeks prior to enrollment. He does not have metastatic disease or malignant pleural effusion at initial diagnosis or at trial entry. He does not have autoimmune disease, a recognized immunodeficiency disease, or any preexisting medical condition requiring systemic chronic steroid or immunosuppressive therapy. He does not have clinically significant hepatic or renal dysfunction, clinically significant cardiac disease, or infectious process that could compromise his ability to mount an immune response.

72-year-old woman with a history of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and hypertension presents for evaluation. She has a history of multiple hospitalizations for heart failure exacerbations despite optimal medical management. Recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 55% and mechanical dyssynchrony with a regional mechanical delay of 75ms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a new pacing method for HFpEF. She is able to complete cardiopulmonary exercise testing and has an expected lifespan greater than 12 months beyond study enrollment. She has not undergone cardiac surgery or had a myocardial infarction in the past 90 days. She has no significant valvular disease, myocarditis, or amyloidosis. She does not have a permanent pacemaker and her creatinine level is within normal limits. She does not have permanent or chronic sustained atrial fibrillation, a PR interval greater than 250 milliseconds, or severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has high-risk coronary artery disease but does not have an indication for percutaneous coronary intervention at enrollment. She is willing and able to give informed consent and available for appropriate follow-up times for the length of the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman with a singleton pregnancy. She is in her third trimester and has been booked for an elective cesarean section due to a history of previous cesarean delivery. She has no known medical disorders involving the heart, liver, kidney, or brain. She does not have diabetes mellitus or hypertension. She has no known blood disorders or history of requiring blood transfusions. She has no risk factors for uterine atony such as macrosomia, polyhydramnios, or multiple pregnancies. She does not have placenta previa or placental abruption. She has no known fibroid or adenomyosis. She does not have severe preeclampsia or uterine anomalies. She is not receiving anticoagulant therapy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial comparing buccal misoprostol versus IV oxytocin in prevention of postpartum hemorrhage.

50-year-old female with a BMI of 27.5, presented to the clinic with a complaint of fatigue, increased thirst, and frequent urination. Lab tests revealed a finger stick fasting blood glucose of 115 mg/dL and a serum fasting glucose of 105 mg/dL. The patient has no prior history of diabetes, but her mother was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at age 55. The patient reports no significant medical history, but takes a daily multivitamin and supplements with omega-3 fatty acids. The patient is interested in participating in a research study to help manage her blood sugar levels and reduce her risk of developing diabetes.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of memory loss and difficulty with daily activities such as dressing and grooming. He has been previously diagnosed with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease and has been on a stable dose of donepezil for the past 6 months. He has a reliable caregiver who is able to accompany him to study visits. He has no history of significant neurological or psychiatric disorders other than AD. He has no significant medical conditions and is able to tolerate the study medication. He understands the nature of the study and has provided informed consent.

25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2, no history of chronic or congenital diseases and normal vital signs. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. He has not taken any prescription or non-prescription drugs within the last 10 days prior to the first dose of investigational product(s). He is willing to abstain from drinking grapefruit juice or caffeine during the study period, and he can eat the standard meals provided by the institution. The participant has signed an informed consent form and agreed to proper contraception during the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer six months ago. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation treatments, but he still experiences severe pain that impacts his daily life. The patient has tried multiple pain medications, but none have provided relief. He has a history of smoking cigarettes, but he quit two years ago. The patient is currently taking opioids for pain management, but he still experiences breakthrough pain. He has no history of psychiatric illness or neurological disorders. The patient is interested in trying cannabis to alleviate his pain and improve his quality of life. He has experience inhaling substances and is willing to comply with the study procedures. The patient is informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

60-year-old male with a history of left main coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. The patient has a recent history of chest pain and was found to have significant coronary artery disease on angiography. The patient was deemed a candidate for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). The patient is not in an emergent or salvage situation, and there is no evidence of significant comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of the heart/lung machine versus off-pump CABG techniques.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has no history of allergies and is currently not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy with cisplatin-based regimen. She has experienced nausea and vomiting in the past with other treatments and is concerned about the side effects of chemotherapy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that could help prevent or reduce these symptoms. Her physical examination is normal, and she has no history of peptic ulcer disease. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is available for follow-up visits as required by the study protocol.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with recurrent meningioma. She had undergone two surgeries previously, but the tumor has come back. She complains of headache, nausea, and vomiting. She is otherwise healthy with no history of allergies or using any medications. Her family history is not significant. She works as a teacher and has two children. She is currently on a low dose of steroids to control her symptoms. The abdomen is soft and non-tender. Her bowel sounds are normal. Her heart rate is 80/min and blood pressure 120/80 mmHg. The lab results are normal. The MRI shows a recurrent meningioma with evidence of tumor progression. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy treatments. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive sunitinib (SU011248) to treat her recurrent meningioma.

A 5-year-old girl is scheduled for tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis and sleep apnea. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She had no previous surgeries and no known allergies. The child is afebrile and has no active respiratory symptoms. Her parents have given consent for her to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old female presents to the emergency department with severe shortness of breath and difficulty speaking. She reports no prior history of respiratory problems but does have a history of asthma. Upon examination, the patient's respiratory rate is 30 breaths per minute, and her oxygen saturation is 87%. She is alert and oriented but visibly distressed. The medical team determines that the patient requires emergency rapid sequence intubation to secure her airway. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical study and is willing to participate. She has no history of maxillofacial trauma or immobilized cervical spine. The patient does not require fiberoptic guided intubation, and there is no ongoing CPR. The medical team obtains written confirmation from a physician not involved in the study and obtains written informed consent from the patient. The patient is randomized to one of the two groups, with the computer-generated code maintained in an opaque envelope that will be opened immediately before randomization.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) two months ago. He has not received any systemic therapy for metastatic disease. The patient has a performance status of 1 and reports occasional fatigue and difficulty in concentration. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient had a colectomy for his colon cancer and also had a biopsy of a liver lesion that confirmed the diagnosis of mCRC. The patient has no history of previous chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has a formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor specimen with an associated pathology report documenting pMMR/MSS mCRC. The patient does not have any CNS metastases or leptomeningeal disease requiring immediate treatment with radiation therapy or steroids. The patient's QTcF interval is within the normal range.

A 24-year-old healthy female is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the effect of buprenorphine on QT interval corrected for heart rate (QTc) in healthy volunteers. She is a full-time student and works part-time in a coffee shop. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no personal or family history of prolonged QT interval or disorders of cardiac rhythm. She is not allergic to buprenorphine, any excipient of BTDS, opioids, psychotropic or hypnotic drugs, and/or moxifloxacin or any member of the quinolone class of drugs. She has normal physical examination, vital signs, ECG, and clinical laboratory values. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any illicit drugs. She is willing to refrain from strenuous exercise or contact sports during the study. She uses an intrauterine device as a contraceptive method.

A 57 yo F recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after presenting with abdominal pain and jaundice. CT scan revealed a 4 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver with no distant metastasis. She has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. She has no uncontrolled coagulopathy and is classified as Child-Pugh class A. She has not received any prior treatment for HCC. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for RFA using separable clustered electrodes as a curative treatment for her HCC.

This is a 35 year-old premenopausal female with a known BRCA1 mutation and a family history of breast cancer. She has regular menstrual cycles and no history of breast, uterine, cervical or ovarian cancer. She is not currently breastfeeding nor planning for pregnancy in the next 6 months. She has no known hypersensitivity to radiological contrast media or ulipristal acetate. She is not currently taking anti-estrogens, GnRH analogues or hormonal contraceptives, corticosteroids or antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy or moderate or potent inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4. She has no contraindications to MRI and has not had any prior breast enhancement/augmentation surgery. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for breast cancer prevention and is willing to undergo a biopsy and take ulipristal acetate for 3 months.

42 year-old man with a BMI of 38.5 kg/m² who has been struggling with obesity for several years. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea. Despite multiple attempts to lose weight through diet and exercise, he has been unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. He has been scheduled for an elective bariatric surgery to help him achieve his weight loss goals and improve his overall health. He is not taking any medication for his hypertension or diabetes at this time, but has been advised to continue taking his CPAP machine for his sleep apnea. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in this clinical trial.

Patient is a 40-year-old male who presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of sharp, severe pain in his right flank. The pain radiates to his back and groin and is accompanied by nausea and vomiting. He also reports passing a small amount of blood in his urine. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Upon examination, the patient appears uncomfortable and is tender to palpation in his right flank. A urinalysis reveals the presence of red blood cells. The treating physician suspects renal colic and plans to order a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to limit CT scanning in suspected renal colic.

The patient is a 49-year-old male who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has had a relapse. The patient has received chemotherapy in the past, but the leukemia has not gone into remission. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, fever, and chills. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has never smoked or used any recreational drugs. His blood pressure is 135/80, his heart rate is 85 bpm, and his temperature is 38.5°C. His lab results indicate that his bilirubin is within normal range, SGOT is slightly elevated, alkaline phosphatase is within normal range, and creatinine is within normal range. He is willing to undergo bone marrow aspiration and biopsy to determine the extent of the leukemia. He has central venous access and his ECOG performance status is 2. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore treatment options for his refractory leukemia.

45 yo F with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease (stage 3) presents to the clinic with symptoms of fatigue, muscle cramps, and weakness. Her recent blood work showed low serum magnesium levels (0.78 mmol/L) and eGFR of 45 mL/min. She has been taking lisinopril for hypertension control. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of oral magnesium supplementation on intracellular magnesium in subjects with chronic kidney disease. She has no history of hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, or kidney transplant. She has no comorbidity that makes study participation and completion impossible. She has no history of parathyroid hormone > 600 pg/L and is not currently pregnant. She has provided written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman aged 55 diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has not responded to previous hormone therapy. The patient has a history of breast cancer and has undergone adjuvant chemotherapy in the past. She has no history of bleeding diathesis or hepatitis B or C. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 1 and is able to perform some activities of daily living. She has at least one measurable lesion that is at least 20 mm by CT scan or MRI. The patient is estrogen-receptor and/or progesterone-receptor positive, with at least 10 fmol/mg cytosol protein or positive by immunohistochemistry. The patient has not received estrogen replacement therapy for at least 4 weeks and has not received any other prior additive hormonal therapy except third-generation aromatase inhibitors or tamoxifen. The patient is not currently receiving any other investigational drug for breast cancer. The patient is not on long-term warfarin but is currently taking a stable dose of bisphosphonates. The patient is willing to receive fulvestrant intramuscularly on day 1 of each course and is willing to be followed every 3 months for 5 years or until disease progression.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a diagnosis of moderate open-angle glaucoma in the left eye. He has been on multiple IOP-lowering medications for the past 6 months, but his intraocular pressure (IOP) remains elevated above the target range despite maximal tolerated medical therapy. The patient has no other ocular comorbidities and is otherwise healthy. He is able and willing to comply with the protocol requirements and understands and signs the Informed Consent form. The patient has not had any ocular surgery in the left eye within the last 6 months and does not have any active inflammation or infection in the left eye. The patient does not wear contact lenses and does not have any corneal conditions that may inhibit normal incisional healing or impair visualization of the implant inside the anterior chamber.

25 year old female with no history of ocular disease, ocular surgery or trauma, and no current use of topical ocular medications. She has been wearing daily disposable contact lenses for the past 5 years with no reported issues. She has no personal or family history of allergic conjunctivitis. She has no systemic diseases or medications that may affect tear production or composition. She is willing to participate in the study and able to attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 42 year old man who was diagnosed with melanoma a year ago. He has received treatment for the primary tumor but recently discovered that the cancer has spread to other parts of his body. He is experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional pain. He is otherwise healthy with no history of other major illnesses or surgeries. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He enjoys playing basketball and watching movies in his free time. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and hopes to contribute to finding a cure for melanoma.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and receiving Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy (HAART) for three years. He has been experiencing weight gain and elevated lipid levels, including high cholesterol and triglycerides. He has been diagnosed with dyslipidemia according to the Mexican Official Standard Norms of 2002. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has no known allergies to fish. He is currently active in the SMART database from HIV/AIDS department of the Civil Hospital in Guadalajara "Fray Antonio Alcalde". He has agreed to sign the informed consent form and attend all scheduled appointments for the study. The patient's BMI is 28.5 and he is willing to make dietary changes and take the assigned supplements to improve his lipid levels and overall health.

A 62-year-old male patient was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma in the right hemi colon. The patient has no significant past medical history and is generally in good health. The tumor is localized between the cecum and the right 1/3 of transverse colon, as confirmed by enhanced CT scan of chest, abdominal, and pelvic cavity. The tumor is categorized as T stage 2 and N stage 1. There is no sign of distant metastasis. The patient is suitable for curative surgery and has given informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies or intolerances to medications or anesthesia.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage III oropharyngeal cancer. She has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications. She presents with difficulty swallowing and a sore throat. Upon further evaluation, she was found to have a mass in her throat. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor and is now scheduled to receive radiation therapy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help improve the assessment and treatment of lymphedema and fibrosis in oral cancer patients. She is able to speak and read English and understands informed consent. Her cognitive function is intact, and she is willing to undergo routine follow-up.

A 14-year-old Caucasian female adolescent complains of being overweight and feeling tired most of the time. She is 5 feet 5 inches tall and weighs 180 pounds, which puts her BMI above the 95th percentile for her age group. She reports irregular periods and is currently in Tanner stage 4. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She denies any history of diabetes or other endocrine disorders. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings and is the middle child. She is an only child who is currently in high school and is not involved in any extracurricular activities. She eats a typical American diet and doesn't have any dietary restrictions. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is negative for any significant medical problems.

As this clinical trial uses previously collected data, no specific patient description is needed. Participants in this study will be selected from those who have already been enrolled in pre-specified epidemiologic studies. The study will analyze data from these participants to identify the lifetime risk for cardiovascular disease among various ethnicities. Participants who have pre-existing cardiovascular disease prior to study entry will be excluded.

A 40-year-old man came to the clinic with complaints of right shoulder pain and difficulty lifting his arm overhead. He reported that the pain started a few months ago and has been gradually worsening. He denied any history of trauma or injury to his shoulder. On physical examination, he had pain with passive shoulder flexion and internal rotation, and a positive Neer and Hawkins-Kennedy test. He had no red flags for serious pathology. His baseline pain level was 5 out of 10 on the numeric scale. He was diagnosed with unilateral shoulder impingement syndrome and was deemed eligible for the clinical trial. He does not have a history of shoulder surgery, elbow, hand or wrist disorders. He is not currently experiencing any shoulder instability and has not been diagnosed with any misdiagnosed cervical spine disorders.

The patient is a 35-year-old male veteran who served in the Army for 8 years. He has been experiencing sleep problems for the past 6 months, including difficulty falling asleep, frequent awakenings, and early morning awakenings. He reports feeling tired and fatigued during the day and has difficulty concentrating. The patient does not have a history of traumatic brain injury but was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after his deployment to Iraq. He is currently taking sertraline for his PTSD but reports no improvement in his sleep problems. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol and has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and can be contacted via phone. His baseline cognitive function test results are within the normal range, and his pressure pain testing results are unremarkable. His wrist actigraphy data indicates that he has an average sleep duration of 5 hours per night with multiple awakenings. His self-report questionnaire scores indicate moderate sleep disturbance and mild depression.

A 45-year-old female with no significant medical history presented to the emergency department with sudden onset shortness of breath and chest pain. A computed tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) was performed which revealed a segmental pulmonary embolism. She was diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and started on oral anticoagulants (OAC) as per routine clinical practice in Denmark. She is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the treatment of VTE in real-life patients. The trial is open to all patients aged 18 or above who have been diagnosed with incident VTE at Danish public hospitals between 2006 and 2015 and received their first-time prescription for anticoagulant drugs within 30 days after the index date. Patients with cancer will be excluded from the study due to their use of low molecular heparin directly from the hospital, which cannot be captured by redeemed prescriptions at pharmacies.

This is a 60 year old female with a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She presented with postmenopausal vaginal bleeding and was diagnosed with endometrial cancer after undergoing a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Pathological analysis revealed grade 3 endometrial cancer with myometrial invasion greater than 50%. CT scans showed no evidence of distant metastases, but pelvic lymph node metastases were identified. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1 and normal liver and renal function. Her white blood cell count, granulocytes, and platelets are within normal limits. She has no history of pelvic radiation therapy or other malignancies within the past 5 years. She has provided study-specific informed consent and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines chemotherapy with adjuvant radiation therapy for high-risk endometrial cancer.

Patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and stable angina who is scheduled to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) due to significant coronary artery disease. The patient has been randomized to receive a novel cardioplegic formula with MPS® (Myocardial protection system) and use the MiECC (Minimal extracorporeal circulation system) during the procedure. The patient has provided informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria for the study. The patient has not had a myocardial infarction within the past seven days and does not have any other interventions planned besides CABG. The patient has not denied the use of their data for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain radiating to his left arm. He was diagnosed with Non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). The patient has a history of smoking for 30 years, but he quit smoking 6 months ago. He has been diagnosed with localized periodontitis of stage II and grade B. He has never received any periodontal therapy or antibiotics for the last 3 months. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. He has no history of diabetes or any other metabolic disorders. The patient has completed high school and works as a construction worker. He is married and has two adult children. He currently takes aspirin (1 × 100 mg per day) for one month as directed by the physician. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his overall health and to contribute to medical research.

As this is a clinical trial for semen donors, a patient description is not applicable. Instead, potential semen donors who meet the inclusion criteria for the IAD, IVF, or ICSI groups may be eligible to participate in the trial. They would need to be evaluated by the clinic and meet the specific criteria outlined in the inclusion criteria section.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of liver cirrhosis. He was diagnosed with alcohol-related cirrhosis 4 years ago and has been sober since then. He has never participated in a clinical trial before. He currently takes lactulose and spironolactone for his cirrhosis. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He denies any history of drug abuse or recent infections. He does not consume excessive amounts of caffeine or alcohol. He is fluent in German and able to understand and comply with the study protocol. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to scientific research and potentially learn more about his liver disease.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His biopsy showed a Gleason score of 7 (3+4). His PSA at diagnosis was 12 ng/mL. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or hypertension. He is currently not taking any medications for these conditions. His blood pressure at the initial visit was 120/80 mmHg. He has no known allergies to any medications or dietary supplements. He exercises regularly but has not received any formal exercise advice. His BMI is 27 kg/m², and he has a waist circumference of 102 cm. He is interested in participating in a study that could potentially help him reduce the risk of metabolic syndrome while undergoing androgen deprivation therapy for his prostate cancer.

65-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis presented to the clinic for evaluation of bone density. She has a T-score of -2.8 on lumbar spine DEXA scan and has a history of vertebral fractures. She has not taken any teriparatide medications in the past. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She denies any history of liver or kidney disease, hypercalcemia, or anemia. She has normal levels of vitamin D and does not take any supplements. She has never had cancer or radiotherapy in the past. She does not have any history of psychiatric disease or alcohol/substance abuse. She has not taken any bisphosphonates in the past 12 months and is not currently taking any estrogen, selective estrogen receptor modulators, or calcitonin. She is not currently taking any systemic corticosteroids or any other medications that may affect bone metabolism. She has never taken teriparatide, other PTH analogues as patches or injectables, strontium, fluorine or any intravenous bisphosphonate therapeutic dose. She has not had any episodes of nephrolithiasis or urolithiasis in the past 5 years. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or malabsorption syndromes. She is not currently taking any investigational drugs and her medical condition does not contraindicate treatment with an investigational drug.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male presents with a small, painless bump on his cheek that has been growing slowly over the past year. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He has no known allergies. He reports a history of sunburns and occasional tanning bed use in his youth. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol on rare occasions. Physical examination reveals a 8mm, well-defined, nodular lesion with no palpable lymphadenopathy. The lesion is located on his left cheek. His skin exam is otherwise unremarkable. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) with nodular histology subtype and no evidence of perineural involvement. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the narrowest excision margin for BCCs on the head and neck.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of self-injurious behaviours and suicidal ideation. She has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD). She reports experiencing intense emotions that are difficult to manage and often result in impulsive behaviours. She has been hospitalized twice in the past five years for suicidal ideation and self-harm. She is currently receiving treatment as usual, which includes medication and individual therapy, but has not found it helpful in managing her symptoms. She is able to read and write in English and is willing to participate in the study. She is not currently participating in DBT treatment.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of pain in her right elbow. She works at a computer for long hours and has been experiencing pain on the outer side of her elbow for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain started after she began playing tennis regularly. She has tried rest, ice, and compression, but they have not provided significant relief. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. Her physical examination shows localized tenderness on the outer side of her right elbow. There is no evidence of swelling or deformity. She has a BMI of 27. She is not taking any NSAIDs or prescription pain medications for her tendinitis. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the therapeutic ultrasound can help alleviate her pain.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss. His CD4 count has been consistently low, with a nadir of 250 / mm3, and his viral load has been above 20,000 copies / ml. The patient has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years but has shown limited response to treatment. He has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions, and he does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and has provided informed consent for the study. The investigating physician has explained the study's purpose, procedures, and potential risks and benefits to the patient, and the patient has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 52-year-old Asian woman who has been diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. She has a history of smoking for the past 20 years and was diagnosed with EGFRm (del19) NSCLC. She has been treated with an EGFR TKI but has progressed on therapy. She has also received other lines of therapy for her cancer. Her performance status is 1, and she has no significant comorbidities. Her vital signs are stable, and she is able to perform activities of daily living independently. She has no prior history of brain metastases, and all her blood tests and liver function tests are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in additional PK studies as required and has a tissue sample available for testing.

The patient is a 20-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with Friedreich's Ataxia. He has experienced symptoms of the disease for at least 2 years, including progressive difficulty with coordination and balance. He is currently able to walk unassisted but has noticeable gait disturbance. He is currently taking medication for other comorbid conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and is in good health otherwise. He has no contraindications to gadolinium contrast or non-contrast MRI evaluation. He weighs 75 kilograms and does not have any known allergies. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with all study procedures, including the use of contraception for the duration of the study drug dosing and one month after completion of the study. He is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study timeframe.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of low back pain for the past six months. The pain is described as a dull ache in the lower back, with occasional sharp pain radiating down the left leg. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medications, physical therapy, and chiropractic treatments with limited relief. He reports difficulty with standing and walking for long periods of time, and has had to modify his daily activities due to the pain. He has no history of balance or neuromuscular disorders, spine surgery, or diabetes. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if the balance reeducation protocol can help improve his pain, function, and postural control.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who works as a teacher and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She has a history of mild hypertension with a systolic blood pressure ranging from 140-150 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure ranging from 80-90 mmHg. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol beyond the recommended guidelines, and has not been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus or any other chronic illness. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She is not currently taking any medication for hypertension, diuretics, or medications that interfere with the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). She has not used nasal decongestants or any over-the-counter or herbal preparations within the past 2 weeks and does not consume more than 4 cups of coffee per day. She is willing and able to give written informed consent and is able to comply with the trial requirements.

A 40-year-old woman was referred to the study by her psychiatrist due to her longstanding history of schizophrenia. She was diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 22 and has been experiencing symptoms for over 18 years. She reports experiencing auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. She has been hospitalized several times due to her symptoms, and has been taking antipsychotic medication consistently for the past 10 years. She reports some improvement in her symptoms but still experiences difficulty in social situations. She has a high school education and has been unemployed for several years due to her symptoms. She lives with her parents and has limited social interactions outside of her family. She speaks English fluently and is able to give informed consent for the study. She is not currently pregnant.

A 20-year-old male with a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 presents to the clinic with multiple skin lumps and bumps, as well as occasional pain in his legs. He has noticed these growths since he was a child, but they have recently become more prominent and uncomfortable. Physical exam reveals multiple neurofibromas on the skin, and imaging shows the presence of plexiform neurofibromas. The patient has no known history of high-risk neurofibroma or malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor. He has no other significant medical history and no allergies. MRI with diffusion weighted imaging is recommended to evaluate the extent of the neurofibromas and to diagnose any high-risk tumors. The patient consents to participate in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of neurofibromatosis.

A 57-year-old woman presents with complaints of persistent upper abdominal pain, loss of appetite and weight loss. She was diagnosed with advanced gastric adenocarcinoma after a biopsy of her stomach. She had previously undergone two rounds of chemotherapy with no significant improvement in her condition. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work or normal daily activities. Lab work is within the required intervals for the study. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent. She has not received more than two prior systemic therapies for advanced disease and has not received another anticancer therapy within 3 weeks prior to randomization. She has not undergone major surgery within 2 weeks prior to randomization and has no CNS metastases. The patient does not have any other severe or uncontrolled medical conditions.

60-year-old male with NYHA Stage D heart failure and a history of hospitalizations for heart failure exacerbation. The patient has been on 2 weeks of consecutive IV dobutamine and is followed at the UMMC outpatient heart failure clinic. The patient is not on ivabradine and is willing to follow-up with the UMMC outpatient heart failure team. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has a resting heart rate of 90 beats per minute and is unable to tolerate beta blockers due to side effects. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 20% and high levels of NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity troponin. The patient has a history of smoking and has quit 5 years ago. The patient is compliant with medications and has no known drug allergies.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of immobilization due to a recent leg injury. She presented with sudden onset of leg pain, swelling and redness. The ultrasound confirmed the presence of deep venous thrombosis in her left leg. She has no previous history of thromboembolism or bleeding disorder. Her past medical history is remarkable for asthma which is well-controlled with inhaled corticosteroids. She is not taking any antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants.
