Her family history is negative for thromboembolism. She has no history of recent surgery or hospitalization. The vital signs are stable with BP: 120/80 mmHg, HR: 80 bpm, RR: 16/min, and O2sat: 97%. She is not pregnant and not lactating. She has no history of thrombophilia or thrombocytopathy.

The patient is a 30-year-old female from the United States, who has been diagnosed with plaque psoriasis for over a year. She has participated in the ISA04-03 study and has completed the study up to and including Visit 9. She is sexually active and is practicing a highly effective method of birth control. She has no plans of becoming pregnant during the course of the study. Her past medical history is unremarkable except for psoriasis. She is not currently taking any medications for psoriasis but has used topical treatments in the past. She weighs 65 kg and is able to keep study appointments and cooperate with all study requirements. She has given her written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures. She has no history of alcoholism or drug addiction and has no known allergies to cyclosporine or any of the constituents of the voclosporin formulation. Her family history is negative for psoriasis. She is willing to continue practicing contraception during treatment and for ≥ 3 months after the last dose of voclosporin.

The patient is a 53-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 6 years. He has been treated with metformin for the past 4 months and has been compliant with his medication regimen. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.3%. He has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and has been trying to make lifestyle modifications to improve his health. He has never participated in an exenatide clinical study before and is willing to receive weekly subcutaneous injections of Exenatide LAR as part of this trial.

40 yo female office worker who has been experiencing mild to moderate stress and fatigue for the past few months. She reports feeling overwhelmed with her workload and responsibilities at home. She has tried some relaxation techniques such as yoga and meditation, but has not found them to be very effective. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if Panax Ginseng, vitamins, and minerals can help improve her symptoms. She does not have any medical conditions that would exclude her from the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

54 year old female diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. The patient completed chemotherapy treatment consisting of carboplatin and docetaxel 2 years ago. The patient has since been in remission. The patient reports experiencing hearing loss and tinnitus within the last year. The patient has no history of pre-existing hearing issues and did not receive radiotherapy to the head and neck area. Past Medical History: Breast cancer as above. The patient has no known history of hypertension, diabetes, or other chronic illnesses. The patient reports a history of depression and anxiety.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder for the past six months. She has been on antidepressant therapy for the past three months but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms, including persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in daily activities. She has a history of depression in her family, with both her mother and paternal grandmother experiencing the same symptoms. She is currently employed as a teacher but has been struggling to manage her workload due to her depression. She has no other significant medical or psychiatric history and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to take a pregnancy test if necessary.

A 7-year-old boy with a history of chronic kidney disease has been experiencing growth retardation. His height is currently at -3.5 standard deviations (SD) from the mean for his age and the annual growth velocity (HV SDS) is < 0 SD according to Reinken (1992). His parents are average height and his target height is -1 SD according to Tanner (1986). He has not yet entered puberty, with testis volume ≤ 3 ml. His medical history also includes a congenital heart defect which was surgically corrected in infancy. He is not currently participating in any other clinical studies and has never been treated with growth hormone before. His pediatric endocrinologist has recommended growth hormone therapy to improve his growth rate.

25-year-old healthy male with no known medical conditions and no history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or drug use. He is not currently taking any medications prescribed by the University Hospital RWTH Aachen, Germany. He has no known hypersensitivity to xenon and is willing and able to understand and follow the instructions provided by the study personnel. He is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. The cancer is estrogen-receptor positive and has progressed despite previous systemic therapy. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 2 and has a BMI of 31 kg/m2. She has no history of hypo- or hyperglycemia, and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has never been treated with exemestane or mTOR inhibitors. She is willing to sign the informed consent form for the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, weight loss, and jaundice for the past 2 months. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or consume alcohol. He underwent a CT scan which revealed a mass in the head of the pancreas. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Upon further evaluation, the patient is categorized as "Category 2" borderline unresectable LAPC by central radiological review. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 12 weeks. His blood work shows adequate hematological, renal, and hepatic function. He has not received any prior therapy for his disease, and his disease is measurable by RECIST 1.1 criteria. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He agrees to use effective contraception methods throughout the study and for 6 months after the final dose of trial drug. He has no history of metastatic PDAC or other invasive malignancies diagnosed within the last 5 years. He is not allergic or hypersensitive to ABX or GEM and has not been taking routine oral anti-oxidant supplements. He has no significant acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition, disease, or laboratory abnormality that would place him at undue risk or interfere with the study. He is not taking warfarin and has no significant history of stroke, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, or ventricular arrhythmia requiring medication or mechanical control within the last 6 months. He does not have cirrhotic liver disease, ongoing alcohol abuse, or known chronic active or acute hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. He is not known to be infected with HIV.

Patient is a 28-year-old male from Jakarta, Indonesia who has a history of injecting heroin within the past 30 days. He is currently enrolled in methadone maintenance treatment and agrees to keep bi-weekly appointments if selected for the study. He meets DSM-IV criteria for opiates dependence with physiologic features. His past medical history is unremarkable and he has no significant cognitive impairment or other medical disorders that may impair his ability to participate. He is willing and able to give informed consent and is not concurrently participating in another treatment study. His current address is in Jakarta and he is not planning to move. He provides adequate locator information.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with fever, cough, and difficulty breathing. He was diagnosed with pneumonia and later developed sepsis. He has an abnormal leukocyte count of 15×109 /cmm and has secondary organ dysfunction with elevated liver enzymes and decreased urine output. He has no history of chronic illness or previous hospitalizations. He has been started on antibiotics and is receiving supportive care in the pediatric intensive care unit.

A 50-year-old male patient has been scheduled for a total knee prosthesis surgery due to osteoarthritis. He has a medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His blood pressure readings have been within normal range for the past 6 months. He has not experienced any cardiovascular events in the past. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the presence of a Systolic Pressure Index as a marker of risk of cardiovascular events after peri-operative high-risk surgery outside the cardiac and vascular surgery. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is over 40 years of age and is scheduled for a total knee prosthesis surgery, which is listed in the orthopedic surgery category. He does not meet the exclusion criteria as he does not have any pathology that would make it impossible to measure Systolic Pressure Index and his life expectancy is greater than 6 months.

78 year old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent (DES) placement to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) 2 years ago. He has been stable on aspirin, atorvastatin, and a beta-blocker. Recently, he has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue. Echocardiography reveals severe aortic stenosis with a mean gradient of 45 mmHg and aortic valve area of 0.7 cm2. He is NYHA class III. He is evaluated by a heart team, including a cardiac surgeon, who agrees he is a candidate for both TAVI and SAVR. He is able to provide written informed consent and agrees to comply with all required post-procedure follow-up visits. He is randomized to the study and agrees to undergo surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) if randomized to control treatment. He is excluded from the study if he had an acute myocardial infarction ≤ 1 month before the intended treatment, has concomitant severe valvular disease (mitral, tricuspid or pulmonic) requiring surgical intervention, has complex coronary artery disease, has hypertension with a pregnancy, or refuses surgery for aortic valve replacement.

68 year old man with a confirmed diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, who has undergone surgical implantation of a deep brain stimulation (DBS) system and is awaiting initial programming session. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise in good general health. There is no history of psychiatric illness or dementia. The patient is able to understand and provide informed consent for the study. They have no significant cognitive impairment and are able to follow directions regarding the motion sensor based assessments.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) 3 years ago. He has undergone treatment with multiple chemotherapy regimens, but the disease has relapsed. He is not eligible for allogeneic stem cell transplantation and is currently undergoing palliative care. He has a clinical performance status of 2 and is expected to survive for more than 12 weeks. His creatinine level is within normal range, cardiac ejection fraction is >50%, and baseline oxygen saturation is >92%. His total bilirubin, ALT and AST levels are within the normal range. He has no other malignant tumors or severe cardiovascular or respiratory diseases. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 20-year-old male diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF) at the age of 2. He has a homozygous p.Phe508del mutation, which is the most common mutation in CF patients. He has been treated with symptomatic treatments for years, but recently he started taking Lumacaftor-Ivacaftor combination therapy as part of a clinical trial. He has been taking the medication for one year and is being closely monitored by the French Society Cystic Fibrosis. He is able to expectorate and has not expressed any opposition to the secondary use of his sputum and stool samples for Lum-Iva-Biota project. The aim of this project is to monitor the evolution of his respiratory mycobiota and microbiota profiles under Lumacaftor-Ivacaftor therapy. The project aims to demonstrate that changes in the hydration of secretions at the pulmonary and intestinal levels related to this therapy promote a change in the lung and gut mycobiota and microbiota profiles which may achieve the characteristics of the "healthy type" in terms of composition, richness and diversity.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for over 6 months. The pain is located in the lumbar region and is described as a dull, aching sensation that is exacerbated by sitting or standing for long periods of time. The patient reports that the pain is also sometimes accompanied by some stiffness and occasional numbness in the lower extremities. He has tried various forms of treatment, including physical therapy and medication, but has not experienced any significant relief. He is currently not engaging in any sports or fitness training specifically for the lower back muscles. He works as an office manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He is married and has two children. He is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study to find effective treatment for his chronic low back pain.

A 54-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with a recurrence of HER2 positive cancer. The patient has previously undergone surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy but has now progressed and is not eligible for any standard or curative treatment. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1 and has no active infectious diseases. Brain metastases are not present or have been treated. The patient has not received any immunotherapy within the last 8 weeks or chemotherapy, radiotherapy, molecular-targeted therapy, or biological therapies (including HER2 directed therapies) within the last 4 weeks. The patient has not received any investigational drug within the last 4 weeks or concomitantly with this study, except for investigational immune-stimulatory therapy (e.g. checkpoint-regulator targeted treatment). The patient is willing to participate in this Phase 1 trial and meet all the inclusion criteria.

54-year-old male with a diagnosis of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with metastasis to the liver, bone and brain. He has received multiple lines of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy. His oncologist is considering clinical trial options for him and has recommended enrollment in the SYNERGY-AI registry. The patient has given informed consent for his medical records to be accessed for the purpose of AI-based precision oncology clinical trial matching. He has also consented to participate in the registry to evaluate the feasibility and clinical utility of using an AI-based tool to match him with clinical trials that may benefit him. His performance status is ECOG 1, and his organ function is normal. The patient is motivated to participate in the registry and explore all possible treatment options to fight his cancer. His cancer-related biomarkers, gene variants, fusion, and rearrangements have been tested and are available for analysis. The patient is eager to learn more about the clinical trial options that may be available to him through the registry, and he looks forward to working with his primary provider and the VTB program to make informed decisions about his treatment.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic with chronic low back pain with occasional radiation to the right leg for the past 6 months. Her pain is rated at 7/10 on the numerical rating scale. She has a history of lumbar spondylosis and mild spinal stenosis on MRI. She works as a nurse and spends most of her day on her feet. She has tried various treatments including physical therapy, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and acetaminophen, but none of them provided significant relief. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. She owns an iPhone 12 and is comfortable using mobile phone applications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the feasibility and value of using smartphone applications to collect objective, quantitative functional data from patients under active treatment for chronic pain.

A 50-year-old woman presents with complaints of fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice for the past six months. She reports having a history of autoimmune disorders, including primary Sjogren's syndrome. Laboratory test results showed elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels at 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) levels, and elevated levels of anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA). Her liver biopsy results were consistent with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). She has been on ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) treatment for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have not improved. She has not taken any immunosuppressive or investigational agents in the past 30 days. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of etrasimod (APD334).

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus for more than 5 years with a confirmed Negative C-peptide. He is currently using an external insulin pump and rapid insulin analog for more than 3 months, specifically a Medtronic Paradigm Real-Time or Veo™ model. He is educated in and practicing functional insulin treatment and carbohydrate counting for more than 3 months. His basal infusion rate is ≥ 0.5 Unit/h, and he self-monitors his blood glucose frequency more than four times a day. He is aware of hypoglycemia and has not experienced any severe hypoglycemic events in the past. He does not have any known impaired renal function with a creatinine clearance greater than 60ml/min. He does not have gastroparesis or any serious or unstable disease likely to induce a glycaemic control deterioration. He is not currently receiving treatment with corticosteroids.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with primary glioma. The glioma is at an early stage and was detected within the last 4 months. The patient has no prior history of brain tumors or any other significant medical conditions. He does not smoke, use drugs or consume alcohol regularly. He has a healthy lifestyle, exercises regularly, and follows a balanced diet. He has a family history of cancer, with his mother being diagnosed with breast cancer in her 50s. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide blood samples for genetic analysis.

A 42 year old patient was referred to the clinic by her rheumatologist due to her recent diagnosis of systemic sclerosis. She had been experiencing skin tightening and thickening on her arms, legs, and face for the past 6 months, and had also been experiencing difficulty breathing. Imaging studies showed interstitial lung damage consistent with systemic sclerosis. She had no significant past medical history, and was not currently taking any immunosuppressive treatments except for corticosteroids. Upon examination, she had a modified Rodnan score of 20 and a DLCO of 60%. She was educated on the study and was interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her condition.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD) for the past 6 months, including tremors and difficulty with coordination. She has not yet been prescribed any medication for PD, but has been experiencing apathy, which has become increasingly concerning for her and her family. She has no history of psychiatric or somatic diseases and has not been taking any antipsychotics, antidepressants, anxiolytics or psychostimulants. Her Mini Mental State Examination score is 28 and her Mattis dementia rating scale score is 135, indicating no signs of dementia. She has no history of depression and her MADRS score is less than 15. She meets the criteria for apathy as defined by Robert et al (2009) and her Lille Apathy Rating Scale score is -18, indicating mild apathy. She is willing to participate in the study and agrees to use effective contraception during the duration of the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has had a history of depression for the past 10 years. She has been on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) medication for the past 5 years but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is currently not taking any other medications and has no other significant medical history. She does not smoke or use drugs recreationally but admits to occasionally drinking alcohol socially. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using reliable contraception. She has no known allergies and is willing to discontinue her SSRI medication for the duration of the trial if necessary. She has never used any serotonergic psychedelic drugs in any form. She is willing to be contacted by email and video call and has online access. She is able to give fully informed written consent. She is interested in participating in the study to possibly find a more effective treatment for her depression.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of short bowel syndrome (SBS) due to surgical resection of a significant portion of his small intestine. He has been dependent on parenteral nutrition (PN) for the majority of his nutritional needs. The patient previously participated in the TED-C14-006 or SHP633-301 studies and has completed all study-related procedures. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in this long-term safety and efficacy study of teduglutide in pediatric participants with SBS. The patient is willing and able to adhere to study requirements and is expected to continue PN therapy throughout the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has had ongoing issues with wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. He has a history of asthma and is allergic to house dust mites. His asthma is currently moderate and well-controlled with inhaled glucocorticosteroids and occasional use of reliever drugs. The patient and his parents have given informed consent for participation in the clinical trial and the patient has been assigned to the active treatment group. The patient has not taken anti-parasite or oral corticosteroid medications within the past 6 months. The goal of the clinical trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of specific immunotherapy to house dust mites in improving the patient's asthma symptoms, reducing the need for reliever drugs, improving lung function, and enhancing overall quality of life.

A 25-year-old Caucasian male, non-smoker, with no significant medical history presents for the study. He is currently not taking any medication and does not have any known allergies. He is physically active, but not an elite-level athlete. He consumes a balanced diet, including seafood once or twice per week. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential benefits of omega-3 fatty acids in reducing the risk of Alzheimer's disease. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to take the EPA+DHA supplement for one month. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 65-year-old man, who lives alone in his apartment, has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia, presented to the clinic with a history of falling twice in the past year. He had no injury and had a complete recovery after the falls. He reported feeling dizzy and unsteady when getting up from bed or a chair. He also reported having occasional urinary incontinence and constipation. His medications are metformin, aspirin, and atorvastatin. His BP was 130/80 mmHg, and his pulse was regular at 80 bpm. His neurological examination was normal. He was referred to the Falls Prevention Clinic for further assessment and management. In the clinic, he was assessed by a multi-disciplinary team, including a nurse, physiotherapist, and occupational therapist. His balance and mobility were assessed, and he was prescribed a home-based exercise program to improve his lower limb strength and balance. He was also prescribed vitamin D supplements and advised on home safety modifications. His medications were reviewed, and his antihypertensive medication was adjusted. He was followed up in the clinic for six months and reported no further falls.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with advanced gastric adenocarcinoma. The cancer has progressed despite receiving first-line chemotherapy treatment with S-1 and cisplatinum. The patient is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating, and nausea. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to take medication orally. The patient has not received S-1 + CPT-11 as a first-line treatment, and the total dosage of S-1 in the first-line treatment was over 1,680mg/m2. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks and meets the required blood count criteria. The patient has not received any other cytotoxic agents therapy, immune-therapy, or radiation therapy for this cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the study and can provide written informed consent.

A 54-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. She has received at least one line of standard systemic treatment for locally advanced or metastatic disease setting of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She has measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version (v)1.1. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has a life expectancy of at least 4 months. Her leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, and hemoglobin are within normal limits. The total bilirubin and creatinine levels are within 1.5 x the institutional upper limit of normal (ULN), and the aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase [SGOT])/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase [SGPT]) are within 2.5 x institutional ULN. The patient has adequately controlled thyroid function and blood pressure. She has no history of myocardial infarction within the last 12 months, stroke or transient ischemic attack within the last 6 months, or NYHA classification of III or IV. The participant has no clinically significant peripheral vascular disease or abdominal aortic aneurysm (> 5 cm) or aortic dissection. The patient has not had any major surgical procedure, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to starting cediranib. She has no history of bowel obstruction within 1 month prior to starting study drugs, hemoptysis or any significant bleeding within the last 1 month prior to enrollment, presence of cavitation of central pulmonary lesion, or history of abdominal fistula, intra-abdominal abscess, or gastrointestinal perforation within the 3 months prior to enrollment. The patient does not have current dependency on intravenous (IV) hydration or total parenteral nutrition (TPN). The participant has no evidence of coagulopathy or bleeding diathesis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 60-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis of the knee for the past 8 years. She reports experiencing pain that significantly interferes with her daily activities, such as walking, climbing stairs, and standing for prolonged periods. She has tried several medications, including NSAIDs and acetaminophen, but they provide only minimal relief. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is postmenopausal. She has no other significant medical history or current health problems. She is willing to discontinue taking NSAIDs and other analgesics for the duration of the study and avoid unaccustomed physical activity. The patient is not receiving any other treatments for her knee pain, such as physiotherapy or acupuncture. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and restrictions, including using medically acceptable methods of birth control if applicable. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and does not have any factors that would jeopardize the evaluation or safety or be associated with poor adherence to the protocol. The patient has access to a telephone and technology.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with Lyme disease 6 months ago and despite being treated with antibiotics, she continues to experience moderate fatigue and joint pain. She is interested in alternative therapies to help manage her symptoms and is willing to dedicate 30 minutes each day to either Kundalini Yoga or meditation. She has access to a smartphone and is comfortable completing questionnaires online. She does not have a current daily practice of mindfulness-based stress reduction, meditation, or yoga. She lives in the United States and is fluent in English. She has not started any new medical or psychiatric treatments in the last 8 weeks and is willing to delay starting any new mind-body practices until after the study is completed. She is willing to not start any new treatments during the 8 weeks of the study and is willing to continue in the study for 8 weeks, even if assigned to the wait-list group. She is willing to provide records of her prior diagnosis and treatment for Lyme disease and is willing to receive push notifications to her smartphone or computer.

Maria is a 58-year-old woman who presented with rectal bleeding and occasional constipation over the past few months. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled on medications. She has no family history of colon or rectal cancer. Physical exam revealed a palpable mass in the rectum, approximately 4 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy revealed a T2N0M0 adenocarcinoma in the lower rectum. Preoperative MRI confirmed that the tumor only invaded the muscular layer and there was no evidence of lymphatic or distant metastasis. She has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade II, and has provided informed consent. She has no history of familial adenomatous polyposis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease. She is not currently receiving any cancer treatment or medications. Based on her eligibility criteria, she could potentially be enrolled in the clinical trial to compare the short and long term outcomes of simple transanal local excision，transanal local excision following radiotherapy or total mesorectal excision for the treatment of Rectal Cancer.

A 45-year-old female patient with metastatic ErbB2 positive breast cancer was referred for participation in a clinical trial examining the effects of esomeprazole on the pharmacokinetics of orally administered lapatinib. The patient has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy and is currently being treated with lapatinib. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has provided written informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including adequate bone marrow function and a calculated creatinine clearance greater than or equal to 50 ml/min based on Cockcroft and Gault. The patient has a total bilirubin level within normal institutional values and an alanine transaminase level that is less than or equal to 3 times the upper limit of institutional values. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction within the normal institutional range based on ECHO or MUGA. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use contraception as specified in the protocol. The patient does not have malabsorption syndrome or a disease affecting gastrointestinal function and has not had resection of the stomach or small bowel. The patient has not received treatment with any investigational drug in the previous four weeks, with the exception of lapatinib. The patient is not receiving any prohibited medication within the timeframe indicated on the prohibited medication list in the protocol. The patient does not have physiological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that would prevent compliance with the protocol and has adequate venous access for protocol-related blood draws.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing memory loss, confusion, and seizures for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and occasional alcohol use. He presents to the hospital with his wife, who reports that his symptoms have been progressively worsening and that he has become increasingly agitated and aggressive. On examination, the patient is disoriented and has difficulty with recall and attention. Neurological examination reveals mild left-sided weakness and hyperreflexia. A brain MRI is performed, which shows evidence of temporal lobe inflammation. A lumbar puncture is performed, and the patient is found to have LGI1 antibodies in his cerebrospinal fluid. The patient is diagnosed with LGI1-associated encephalitis and is enrolled in the clinical trial to investigate cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in LGI1-E patients.

A 46-year-old male with a long history of severe, recalcitrant, plaque-type psoriasis is seeking a new treatment option after failing at least one systemic therapy. The patient has psoriatic involvement of at least 20% of BSA and a PSGA score of 6. He has not received any systemic psoriasis treatments for the past 4 weeks or UV-based therapy for the past 2 weeks. He is not currently taking warfarin or any medication for gastrointestinal ulceration. His serum chemistry values are within the normal range. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and restrictions and is willing to return to the clinic for the follow-up evaluation as specified in the protocol. He is aware that he may be required to use an approved method of birth control for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents to the Emergency Department with a complaint of dizziness and spinning sensation associated with a change in head position. She reports having experienced similar episodes for the past two weeks. She denies any hearing loss or ear pain, but reports mild nausea and vomiting. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She denies any history of substance abuse and has no known allergies. She is able to provide informed consent and is not pregnant. She has not taken any antiemetic medications in the past 24 hours. Further evaluation reveals peripheral origin of vertigo.

A 34-year-old woman was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) six months ago. She experiences joint pain, fatigue, mouth sores, and a rash on her face that worsens with sun exposure. Her ANA titer is 1:640, and she had positive anti-dsDNA antibodies. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and mycophenolate mofetil to manage her symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and is in good health overall. She has no allergies to medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of SLE.

The patient is a 35-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. The patient has been in clinical remission for the past four weeks and has had a symptomatic relapse within the past two years. The patient has been taking mesalazine for the past four weeks and is capable of giving written informed consent. The patient is not currently experiencing symptoms of active colitis and has a modified Baron sigmoidoscopy score of 0 or 1. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for this study and is willing to participate. The patient has no history of Crohn's disease, corticosteroid use, or other serious medical or psychiatric illness that would compromise the study. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is not currently taking azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow the medication regimen as prescribed.

A 72-year-old retired man was admitted to the hospital with complaints of persistent chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking medications for these conditions, including metformin and lisinopril. He also takes aspirin and simvastatin daily. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago. He lives with his wife and is able to perform his activities of daily living independently. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

45 year old male diagnosed with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) for 3 years. He has been experiencing gastrointestinal (GI) tract symptoms such as difficulty swallowing and bloating. He has been treated with various medications but has not experienced significant relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve his symptoms and potentially advance the understanding of SSc. Past Medical History: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) Hypertension Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) Osteoporosis Depression Anxiety Medications: Prednisone, Methotrexate, Pantoprazole, Calcium and Vitamin D.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who received a kidney transplant two years ago due to end-stage renal disease. He has been following up with his healthcare provider at Toulouse Hospital since the transplant. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. His physical exam and lab studies were normal, except for his creatinine levels, which have been stable at 1.3 mg/dL. He has not received any treatments that could interfere with lymphocyte populations, such as IL6 blockers, PD1 blockers or CTL4 blockers. He has not had a splenectomy in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of heart failure, diagnosed 3 years ago. She is currently taking furosemide 40mg, lisinopril 10mg, and spironolactone 25mg daily. She reports occasional episodes of joint pain and discomfort, for which she takes ibuprofen 200mg as needed. She denies any recent changes in her medication regimen or medical history. Her vital signs are stable and within normal limits. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

35 F, G3P3, with a history of contraceptive pill use for 5 years and currently seeking an alternative method of contraception due to side effects. She has regular menstrual cycles and has never used an IUD before. She has been counseled on the use of IUD and has chosen it as her preferred method of contraception. She has no history of PID, STIs, or cervical cancer. She is not pregnant nor is she less than 4 weeks postpartum. She has no known allergies to copper or progesterone.

As this is a case report proposal and not a clinical trial with patient enrollment, it is not appropriate to generate a patient description for this study. However, the study aims to describe the clinical course and outcome of a neonate with congenital long QT syndrome and congenital complete heart block who experienced frequent episodes of torades des pointe and ventricular tachycardia. The study will analyze the infant's medical records to include his age, date of birth, medical record number, inpatient labs, inpatient echo reports, outpatient echo reports, inpatient and outpatient EKG's, inpatient pharmacy records, the results of his genetic analysis, his history and physical, transfer notes, daily progress notes, consultation reports and operative reports from his admission beginning 9/30/04. The study aims to shed light on the clinical characteristics, management, and outcome of infants with congenital long QT syndrome and congenital complete heart block.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a history of normal fasting plasma glucose and normal glucose tolerance. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between oxyntomodulin, GLP-1, and glucagon in relation to appetite, food intake, gastric emptying, and energy expenditure. The patient reports no history of diabetes, pre-diabetes, or impaired glucose tolerance. She has no family members with diabetes and has never been diagnosed with obesity, inflammatory bowel disease, or undergone any bowel surgery. The patient reports no history of nephropathy or liver disease. She is not taking any medications that cannot be held for 24 hours. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old child diagnosed with congenital heart disease and in need of a Fontan procedure. The child has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and decreased appetite. The child's parents are concerned about the upcoming surgery and want to ensure the best possible outcome. The child has no known allergies or medical conditions other than the congenital heart disease. The parents are willing to provide informed consent for the child to participate in the clinical trial evaluating fluid balance and edema formation in children undergoing the Fontan procedure.

56 yo M with metastatic HER2+ adenocarcinoma of the GE junction, showing disease progression after trastuzumab and multiple lines of chemotherapy including FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, and paclitaxel. Patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. Imaging reveals multiple metastatic lesions in the liver and lymph nodes. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - History of smoking, now quit - Appendectomy and cholecystectomy in the remote past.

A 4-year-old boy was brought to the clinic by his mother due to symptoms of ear pain and fever. He has been experiencing a mild fever of 100.5°F for the past three days and has been crying more often than usual due to ear pain. The mother also noticed that her son has been pulling at his ear. Upon examination, the doctor found that the boy has acute otitis media. He has not had any previous episodes of ear infections and does not have any allergies to medications. The boy's mother is willing to participate in the clinical trial and adhere to the daily tympanometry monitoring.

The patient is a 31-year-old woman who has been struggling with emotional eating and binge eating for the past few years. She has a history of depression and anxiety, and has been engaging in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) for the past month. She has noticed a significant weight gain over the years and has been trying to lose weight through various fad diets and exercise programs, but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to promote a healthy lifestyle and reduce the risk factors associated with eating pathology and NSSI. She is currently not pregnant and resides in the United States.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who presents to the clinic with symptoms of fever, chills, headache, and fatigue. He reports having traveled to a malaria-endemic region in Africa two weeks ago for a business trip. He had taken prophylactic medication as prescribed during his trip, but he stopped taking it three days ago because he thought he was no longer at risk of contracting malaria. He reports experiencing recurrent fevers and chills over the past few days, and he has been taking over-the-counter antipyretics to manage his symptoms. Upon examination, the patient has an axillary temperature of 38.5°C, and he has a positive blood smear for P. falciparum with an asexual parasitemia count of 20,000/µL. The patient has no history of any chronic medical conditions, and he has not taken any antimalarial drugs in the past two months. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including his liver and renal function tests. The patient weighs 75 kg and has a body mass index of 24 kg/m2. He has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive treatment for his malaria.

24-year-old female living in a rural area of Uganda. She presents to a government-run health center with a fever and chills. She reports feeling tired and weak and has been experiencing intermittent headaches for the past few days. She denies any recent travel outside of her village, any exposure to sick individuals, or any known allergies. She reports having had malaria in the past and was treated with antimalarial medication at that time. On examination, her temperature is 38.5°C, and she appears mildly dehydrated. No other significant findings were noted. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo rapid diagnostic testing for malaria. She has no known medical history and is not currently taking any medications.

54 year-old man with a history of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema who has recently been diagnosed with end-stage lung disease. The patient has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, and wheezing, despite maximal medical therapy. Pulmonary function tests have shown a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 25% of predicted, and a diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 20% of predicted. The patient has been referred for lung transplant evaluation and is considered a new candidate for the procedure. The patient has no history of heart or lung transplant, and does not have any uncontrolled severe comorbidities.

A 54-year-old male patient with a confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer and no evidence of distant spread of the disease. The patient has undergone previous treatments including hormonal therapy and radiation therapy which provided temporary relief but the cancer has progressed. The patient is in good physical health with no severe or uncontrolled medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the feasibility of combined administration of LBH589 with radiotherapy in hopes of finding a more effective treatment option for their prostate cancer.

A 16-year-old high school student has been experiencing low mood, lack of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping for the past 6 months. She has lost interest in hobbies that she once enjoyed and has been struggling with concentration and motivation in school. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia or organic mental disorder. She is not currently receiving psychotherapy or taking any psychotropic medications. She is interested in participating in this study to help manage her depressive symptoms.

56 year old male smoker with a recent diagnosis of extensive stage small cell lung cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia but is otherwise healthy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently. Imaging studies show multiple metastases in the liver and bones. The patient is willing to undergo chemotherapy and immunotherapy as first-line treatment and agrees to participate in the clinical trial. He has no history of autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency or recent infections. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with study procedures.

Patient is a 30-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) who is scheduled to undergo a first treatment by loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). She has no history of any medical conditions that would preclude her from undergoing local cervical block anesthesia or general/spinal anesthesia. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

Maria is a 34-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder for the past 6 months. She has been experiencing symptoms such as feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities that used to bring her joy. She has a total score of 25 on the IDS-SR and a total score of 20 on the IVRS HAM-D (17 items). Her CGI-SI score is 4, indicating moderately ill or much worse. Maria is currently an outpatient and her depressive episode has lasted for 10 weeks. She has no history of seizure or seizure disorder, anorexia nervosa or bulimia, panic disorder, OCD, PTSD, or acute stress disorder within the past 12 months. She is not diagnosed with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or any other psychotic disorder. She has no history of manic episodes, and no other DSM-IV axis II diagnosis that would suggest non-responsiveness to pharmacotherapy or non-compliance with the protocol. Maria has not undergone treatment with a depot neuroleptic in the past, and her systolic blood pressure is normal. She is not pregnant, lactating, or trying to become pregnant. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse or dependence within the past 12 months and has no suicidal thoughts or attempts within the past 6 months. Maria has not taken another investigational product for the NDA filing or for the post-manufacturing/marketing approval study within the past 12 weeks. She is not currently participating in another clinical study in which she is or will be exposed to an investigational or non-investigational drug or medical device. Maria has no history of withdrawal from the investigational clinical trial of 323U66 SR due to any adverse events, no hypersensitivity to 323U66 (bupropion), no risk of homicide, no serious cerebral or physical symptom(s), and no major depressive disorder due to direct physiological effects of a general medical condition(s).

30-year-old Chinese woman who is sexually active and has had two lifetime sexual partners. She has no prior history of genital warts or cervical disease. She is currently using effective contraception and has not had a fever in the past 24 hours. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the prevention of HPV and is within the age range of 20 to 45 years old.

A 28-year-old English-speaking woman gave birth to a preterm infant at 29 weeks gestational age. The infant is currently in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and requires complex healthcare management due to prematurity-related complications. The mother has been experiencing anxiety and depression since the birth of her child and is struggling to understand and manage the care required for her preterm infant. She is interested in participating in the PREEMIE PROGRESS program to learn evidence-based family management skills to better equip her to meet the chronic, complex healthcare needs of her preterm infant. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 56-year-old woman with a 10-year history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the outpatient clinic at Slagelse Hospital for a routine check-up. She reports occasional shortness of breath and mild fatigue. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or autonomic neuropathy. Her current medications include metformin and sitagliptin for diabetes management. She has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. Her fasting glucose and HbA1c levels are 145 mg/dL and 7.5%, respectively. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and her BMI is 26.5 kg/m2. Upon examination, no significant findings are noted. The patient is informed of a clinical trial studying the association between Type 2 diabetes mellitus and cardiac function and is interested in participating.

A 60-year-old male with a confirmed clinical diagnosis of fragile X-associated tremor ataxia syndrome (FXTAS) is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient's serum creatine kinase, complete metabolic panel, complete blood count, liver function tests, renal function tests, platelets, and EKG are within normal limits. The patient is mentally competent and able to provide written informed consent. There is no history of severe renal or hepatic disease, and the patient has not had abnormal creatine kinase or platelet count in the past 6 months. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use adequate protection during the study. The patient has no known allergies or sensitivities to the drug or its formulations. The patient is not concurrently participating in another clinical study, has no active substance use or dependence, and is not suffering from any serious illness requiring systematic treatment or hospitalization.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus 5 years ago. He has been taking metformin and glipizide for the past 3 years to control his blood sugar levels. Despite medication, his latest HbA1c reading is 8.5%. The patient has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and has not experienced any heart attack or stroke in the past 6 months. He does not have significant kidney disease and his blood pressure is under control. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who has been diagnosed with osteoporosis. She has experienced a gradual loss of height over the past few years and has noticed an increase in the curvature of her upper back. She has had a bone density scan which confirmed a diagnosis of osteoporosis. She is otherwise healthy and active, with no history of neurological or spinal problems. She is retired and spends her free time gardening and walking her dog. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research in the field and is willing to commit to the time required for the assessments. She is able to travel to the clinic for the assessments and is willing to provide written consent to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old Hispanic woman has been experiencing severe headaches for the past year. She has been diagnosed with migraine by her physician based on her symptoms, which include throbbing pain on one side of the head, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound. She experiences these attacks 2-3 times per month, and they last for 24-48 hours. She has no prior history of cerebral or cardiac vascular events. She has never been pregnant or breastfed. She is not taking steroids for any other medical conditions. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate inflammatory markers in patients with migraine, tension type headache or cluster headache. The aim of the study is to identify an inflammatory marker for migraine and to compare the levels of inflammatory markers between the different types of headaches.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been hospitalized for a month with a serious fungal infection. She has been treated with standard antifungal therapies, but has not improved. She has a history of asthma and allergies, and takes daily medications for both. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no known drug allergies. Her abdomen is tender to palpation, and she has a fever of 101.2°F. Blood tests reveal leukocytosis with left shift and elevated liver enzymes. Imaging studies show evidence of a fungal infection in her lungs, liver, and spleen. She has agreed to participate in this clinical trial to receive extended treatment with Voriconazole, a new drug developed to treat fungal infections. Before beginning treatment, she will undergo a physical examination, blood and urine tests, and an eye examination. She will receive Voriconazole twice a day by infusion into a vein or by tablets taken by mouth for up to 12 weeks. She will be examined at weeks 4, 8, and 12 of the study, and one week after treatment stops. Blood and urine samples will be collected at each visit, and an eye examination will be done at the end of the treatment period and at other visits if vision problems develop. The aim of the study is to determine the efficacy, safety, and toleration of Voriconazole in treating serious fungal infections that have not responded to standard therapies.

A 35-year-old female patient presents to the primary care clinic with a history of multiple unexplained somatic symptoms for the past 6 months. She has been experiencing fatigue, headaches, muscle pain, and gastrointestinal issues. The patient reports that she has visited the clinic more than 10 times in the past year with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She denies any history of psychiatric disorders, suicidal thoughts, or addiction to toxic substances. She has never received psychotherapy in the past year, and she is willing to participate in the trial. The patient speaks fluent Spanish and has no plans to move from the area. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or current health issues.

A 28-year-old woman, who is a graphic designer, visited the clinic because she has been feeling frustrated with her inability to focus on tasks for extended periods. She has a history of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and was diagnosed at the age of 10. She has been on and off medications for ADHD, but has not been on any medication for the past 3 months. She does not smoke or drink alcohol, and has no history of illicit drug use. She has no known allergies and her medical history is unremarkable. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day and her BMI is 25. She has no history of asthma, peptic ulcer disease, or pheochromocytoma. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past month.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder. He has been experiencing episodes of mania for the past several months, with symptoms including racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, and increased energy levels. He has never been treated for his bipolar disorder and has not taken any medications for it. He has a history of substance abuse, having used cocaine and marijuana in the past year. He has no other medical or neurological disorders that would interfere with the MRI scan. He is currently unemployed and lives with his parents. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the procedures involved. He is not currently using any medications for his bipolar disorder or any other medical conditions. He is not currently in a manic episode and has a YMRS score of 8.

60 year-old man with a history of cirrhosis of the liver and a Child-Pugh score of A will be participating in this clinical trial. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and swelling in his legs. He has not been able to work due to his symptoms and has been relying on family members for support. He has been on a stable dose of lactulose for the past 30 days. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with all the requirements of the study. He weighs 70 kg and has not been on any medication that the Sponsor and the Investigator felt was not appropriate for use during the study. He has no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, neurological, immunological, or psychiatric disorder(s), as determined by the Investigator. His serum sodium, creatinine, and potassium levels are within the normal range. He has not had any significant illness or hospitalization within the last 14 days and has no suspected site of active infection. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or malabsorption defined with steatorrhea. He has no history of active gastrointestinal bleeding, defined as melena, hematochezia, or hematemesis requiring hospitalization within the last 30 days. He has no history of seizures within the last 72 hours and has tested negative for drugs of abuse and alcohol. He has not donated or lost blood or plasma within the last 30 days and has no known hypersensitivity to sodium phenylbutyrate or similar drugs. He has not taken any investigational drugs within the last 30 days.

A 28-year-old male who is sexually active and has tested positive for syphilis is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He has previously been treated with penicillin for a different infection and did not experience any adverse reactions. He reports having a rash and a painless sore on his genitals for the past few weeks. He denies any other symptoms such as fever, headache, or muscle aches. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. He is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. He is willing to return for follow-up visits and blood sampling. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. His past medical history is unremarkable, and his family history is negative for any sexually transmitted infections.

This is a 38 year old female with a history of chronic musculoskeletal pain, specifically neck pain, who has experienced childhood adversity. She has reported a score of 4 or higher on the Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACE) Scale, indicating significant childhood trauma. She has not been diagnosed with a current psychotic disorder and is able to communicate effectively in English. She is not scheduled for surgery within the next 2 months. She is currently taking medication for her pain, but is interested in participating in a study that may help her manage her pain better. She will be randomized to either a therapeutic interview condition or a waitlist control condition, and will complete follow-up measures at five weeks after the interview. She hopes that the therapeutic interview will help her better understand the role of stress and emotions in her pain, and improve her ability to communicate with others in her interpersonal relationships.

The patient is a 5-year-old child who was born prematurely at 30 weeks of gestation. The child was included in the EPIPAGE 2 and EPIRMEX study, and has undergone a magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) at term-equivalent age to evaluate the structural abnormalities in the brain. The MRS analysis will be performed by the CEMEREM laboratory, UMR 6612 CNRS/Université de la Méditerranée/Division of Medical Imaging. The child's periventricular area, basal ganglia, and brain stem were analyzed. The child has also undergone a full cognitive assessment in EPIRMEX at the age of 5 years. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the relation between the MRS analysis at term-equivalent age and the executive functions at the age of 5 years corrected in very preterm infants. The child has no severe chromosomal anomaly or central nervous system malformation diagnosed prenatally or on examinations in the neonatal period.

Patient A is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic shoulder pain for several months. He works in construction and has noticed a decrease in his ability to perform his job due to the pain and limited range of motion in his shoulder. He was diagnosed with a massive rotator cuff tear and has been experiencing pseudoparalysis with active flexion less than 45°. Despite undergoing physical therapy, he has not seen significant improvement in his condition. He speaks both German and English fluently and is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the feasibility of a robotic mediated therapy in a clinical setting. He has no history of neurological disease or other conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is hoping to improve his range of motion and reduce his pain so he can return to his job and normal daily activities.

The patient is a 3-year-old child living in Guatemala with their caregiver. The child was recently diagnosed with diarrhea and was prescribed oral rehydration salts (ORS) and a 10-day treatment of zinc. The caregiver accompanies the child to a public health care center for treatment and will be participating in a clinical trial testing the effectiveness of health center co-packaging and counseling messages to improve adherence to the prescribed zinc treatment. The caregiver is willing to sign a consent form and participate in the study. The child has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma a year ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy as part of her cancer treatment, and her cancer is currently in remission. However, her treatment has put her at moderate-to-high risk of premature ovarian failure, which could affect her fertility in the future. As a result, she was offered ovarian tissue cryopreservation (OTC) by the ovarian cryopreservation service, which she accepted. She is now being approached to participate in a study that aims to understand the experiences of teenagers and young adults who have been offered OTC prior to cancer treatment. The study will involve an interview about her experiences with OTC, and she will be asked to reflect on her thoughts and feelings about the procedure. She is eligible to participate in the study as she is between the ages of 11 and 25, has received a cancer diagnosis with a moderate-to-high risk of premature ovarian failure, has been offered ovarian cryopreservation, and is aware that the procedure has taken place. She is excited to participate in the study as she believes it is important to raise awareness about fertility preservation options for young cancer patients.

63-year-old male with a history of localized prostate cancer, who underwent definitive non-prostatectomy therapy (radiation therapy) in [**2009**]. He has been followed closely by his urologist and oncologist with routine PSA testing, which has been stable until recently. The patient reports a recent rise in PSA levels and is currently undergoing further evaluation for possible recurrent prostate cancer. His current PSA level is 4.8 ng/mL. He has no significant family history of prostate cancer. He has no significant comorbidities and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient has not undergone any prostate biopsy within the past month, and has not undergone any cryotherapy, external beam radiation, or high intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) within the past year. Thus, he meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

56-year-old male with a clinical and radiological diagnosis of stroke that occurred approximately 2 months ago. The patient has been clinically stable for at least one month and has provided signed and dated informed consent for the study. The patient has no other conditions that would interfere with adherence to treatment and is not currently enrolled in any other research studies. The patient has no history of joint or muscle pain or any other conditions that could interfere with the proposed therapy. However, the patient has some comorbidities that are clinically stable. The patient will undergo evaluation of clinical and neurophysiological data performed before and after treatment to identify predictors of different responses from rehabilitation therapy. The patient will participate in a single Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) session and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) will be performed in the baseline and after the tDCS session. The study aims to identify predictors of stroke recovery and optimize and individualize existing treatments.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy with chronic tonsillitis and obstructive sleep apnea. He has a history of snoring, witnessed apneas, and daytime sleepiness. The patient underwent a polysomnography that confirmed the diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea. The patient has no significant medical history, but he is allergic to penicillin. The patient is scheduled for an adenotonsillectomy under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation. He has no limitation for movement of the neck or concerns of the stability of the cervical spine.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman who has been donating platelets for the past two years. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet. She has passed all the necessary health clearances for blood donation. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She will have a small amount of blood taken during her next platelet donation for the purpose of this study. She understands that the sample will be anonymized and will be used for research only. She understands that there may be a risk of bacterial contamination in platelet concentrates and that this study aims to improve the detection of such contamination using molecular biology techniques. She is willing to cooperate with the researchers and provide any additional information or samples as needed.

A 28-year-old man was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 2 years ago. He has been treated with interferon beta-1a for the past 2 years but continues to experience relapses every 6 months. His last relapse was 2 months ago, which left him with numbness and tingling in his left hand and leg. His EDSS score is 2.5. The patient is now considering switching his medication to Hikma Generic DMF (Sclera® or Marovarex ®) and has been referred to participate in this study. The patient has no history of severe adverse reactions to medications and has been compliant with his current medication. He is a non-smoker, has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and has no significant medical history other than RRMS. The patient has read and understood the study information and has agreed to participate in the study by providing written informed consent.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has been experiencing restless legs syndrome and periodic leg movements during sleep for the past 6 months. He reports difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep due to the sensations in his legs. The patient has no history of neurological or psychiatric diseases and is not currently taking any medications that may affect his sleep or wake state. He has not been diagnosed with narcolepsy-cataplexy or upper airway resistance syndrome. The patient has undergone hospital routine for periodic leg movements diagnosis and has a PLMS index of 12. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help develop a better understanding of the relationship between periodic leg movements and cardiovascular risk.

35-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years with no success. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) by her gynecologist. She underwent one cycle of IVF previously, but only 2 oocytes were retrieved, and none of them fertilized. Her AMH level was found to be 1.7 ng/mL, and her FSH level was 10.5 mIU/mL on day 2 of her menstrual cycle. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially increase her chances of conceiving.

A 58-year-old man presented with fatigue, weight loss, and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are being treated with medications. On physical examination, he has an enlarged liver and spleen. Laboratory tests showed elevated protein levels in his urine, elevated creatinine and BUN levels, and anemia. The patient underwent a biopsy, which showed deposition of amyloid proteins in his organs, confirming the diagnosis of systemic AL amyloidosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers a risk-adapted therapy for AL amyloidosis, and he meets the eligibility criteria for the trial. The patient is willing to undergo high-dose melphalan (MEL) with autologous stem cell transplant (SCT) followed by adjuvant dexamethasone (dex) and thalidomide (thal) as per the study protocol.

8-year-old male diagnosed with MPS IVa with a history of reduced leucocyte GALNS enzyme activity confirmed by laboratory assay. He is able to walk independently but experiences difficulty due to skeletal problems such as knock-knees and lax ligaments. He has not undergone recent orthopaedic surgery and is not currently using any investigational product or medical device. The patient and his legal guardian are willing to provide written informed consent and assent, and willing to comply with all study procedures as far as physically possible. The patient has no concurrent disease or condition that would interfere with study participation or safety.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22. She does not smoke or consume alcohol or caffeine-containing products. She has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medications (except for hormonal contraceptives) in the past 14 days and has not consumed any vitamins or herbal products in the past 7 days. She has no history of significant cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, pulmonary, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, or neurologic disease. She has no history of asthma, bronchiospasmic disease, chronic bronchitis, sinus bradycardia, and greater than 1st-degree conduction block. She has no allergies or hypersensitivity to nadolol, propranolol, or other β-adrenergic receptor blockers, bendroflumethiazide, sulfonamide-derived drugs, thiazides, or other related products. She is not pregnant or lactating and has a negative serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) pregnancy test. She has normal laboratory evaluation, including a negative HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C test result.

11 yo M with a history of behavioral issues and aggression, diagnosed with ADHD and oppositional defiant disorder (ODD) by a child psychiatrist. He is currently taking methylphenidate for ADHD but has not shown significant improvement in his behavior. He has a history of physical aggression towards family members and peers at school, leading to several suspensions. His parents are concerned about his behavior and are willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the psychophysiological correlations of aggression and response to aversive stimuli in children diagnosed with ADHD and conduct disorder. The child has an IQ of 90 and is willing to participate in a randomized, double-blind controlled trial. Past Medical History: - ADHD - ODD - Allergic rhinitis - No history of serious head injury or epilepsy.

Sarah is a 14-year-old female who has been recommended for orthodontic treatment to correct her crowded teeth. She has a permanent dentition and has a minimum of 3 mm of extraction space that needs to be closed by moving her anterior teeth or canine distally. She maintains good oral hygiene and has no other medical or dental conditions. She lives in San Antonio, TX, and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of a device that provides a light vibration and speeds up tooth movement during orthodontic treatment. She has no use of bisphosphonates and is not pregnant. She is excited to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the instructions given to her.

A 45-year-old male presents with fatigue, reduced libido, and reduced sexual functioning. He has a history of hypogonadism and his morning serum testosterone is ≤ 297 ng/dL. He is in good health based on medical history, physical examination and clinical laboratory tests. His body mass index (BMI) is between 18 and 31. He has no history of prostate cancer, palpable prostatic mass(es), generalized skin irritation or significant skin disease. He is not on any medications that could be considered anabolic or could interfere with androgen metabolism. He has no clinically significant anemia or renal dysfunction, hyperparathyroidism, uncontrolled diabetes or history of cardiovascular disease. He has not used estrogens, Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists/antagonist, human growth hormone (hGH), or testosterone products within the specified time frame.

The patient is a 25-year-old female diagnosed with Crohn's disease three years ago. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and weight loss despite being on various medications. A colonoscopy with biopsies revealed stricturing and fistulizing Crohn's disease in the ileocecal area. She has been advised to undergo ileocecal resection surgery and has provided written consent for the procedure. She is not pregnant and is not currently on antibiotics or probiotics. Her life expectancy is greater than one year.

A 32-year-old male presents to the emergency department with severe right lower abdominal pain. He reports that the pain began suddenly and has been gradually worsening over the past 6 hours. He denies any recent fever, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and denies any drug or alcohol use. On physical examination, there is tenderness and guarding noted in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen. The patient is alert and oriented, with normal vital signs. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of C-reactive protein and white blood cells, which are indicative of inflammation. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of Complement cascade activation biomarkers in the diagnosis of acute appendicitis.

Pt is a 30yo male with a body mass index of 28.5 kg/m2 and a body weight of 80 kg. He has been struggling with abdominal subcutaneous fat, with a thickness of 5.5 cm by pinch method surrounding the center of the treatment area. He has maintained a stable lifestyle for the past 6 months with regular exercise and eating habits. He is willing to commit to an acceptable contraceptive regimen with his partner from the time of screening and throughout study participation until 12 weeks after the last study drug dose. He has no known allergies or sensitivities to the study drug and/or excipients. His liver function, renal function, and coagulation disorders are within normal limits. He has not undergone any esthetic procedures in the past 6 months and is not on any prescription or over-the-counter weight reduction medication or weight reduction programs within the past 3 months. He has not used the therapeutic agents S-mephenytoin, terfenadine, buspirone, fexofenadine in the past 2 days prior to dosing until 1 day post-dose, whichever is later. He is willing to receive topical anesthesia and has not been diagnosed with diabetes or cardiovascular disease.

A 50 year old woman was diagnosed with hypertension during a routine check-up at her family practice office located in Chieti. She has been prescribed antihypertensive medication and advised to monitor her blood pressure (BP) at home.
