However, she admits to having difficulty in accurately measuring her BP at home and often forgets to measure it. She speaks and reads Italian and has a phone number and email address. She has no mental illness, cognitive impairments, or pregnancy. She lives with her husband and has a sedentary lifestyle with no regular physical activity. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of a family nurse-led home blood pressure management (HBPM) training program in improving BP control.

The patient is a 20-year-old college student who reports binge drinking on weekends with friends. She reports drinking 4-5 drinks per occasion and experiences hangovers, missed classes, and regrets about her behavior. She is concerned about her drinking and wants to reduce it, but she finds it difficult to resist peer pressure. She is a full-time student majoring in psychology and has a part-time job at a coffee shop. She lives with roommates in off-campus housing and enjoys socializing with friends. She has no significant medical or psychiatric history and takes no medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs but occasionally uses e-cigarettes. Her physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any abnormalities. BP: 110/75 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7500 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) for the past 5 years. She is currently taking disease-modifying drugs to manage her condition. She has a history of obesity with a BMI of 32 and a waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) of 0.6. She has been struggling to lose weight despite several attempts at dieting and exercise. She is fluent in English and has access to a telephone. She is able to walk 25 feet without assistance and does not have any severe sensory or motor impairment that would limit her participation in the study. She has no history of food allergies or need for a special diet preventing her from consuming the recommended diet. She has no concurrent ongoing behavioral or pharmacological weight loss interventions. She has no history of insulin-dependent diabetes or serious pulmonary/cardiac conditions. She has been stable in her weight with no history of more than 10 pounds weight loss or gain in the past 3 months. She has no planned or recent joint replacement surgeries. She has no serious psychiatric disorder, current suicidal ideation, or current binge eating disorder. She has no current medical conditions where weight loss is contraindicated, as indicated by her primary care physician. She has answered "no" to all 7 questions on the Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire (PAR-Q), indicating no contraindications to exercise. She is interested in participating in the telehealth obesity intervention for patients with MS.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who is generally healthy and enjoys participating in recreational physical activities such as running and cycling. She is a non-regular caffeine user, does not smoke and is not currently taking any medication. She has no history of respiratory, cardiovascular, or neuromuscular disease. She is not pregnant and has no known injuries that would limit her ability to exercise. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of ketone supplements on athletic performance. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 45-year-old female patient presented with a history of recurrent episodes of nausea, vomiting, and generalized weakness for the past 6 months. She reported a recent episode of falls and difficulty in walking. On examination, she appeared dehydrated, and her vital signs were within normal limits. Laboratory investigations showed hyponatremia with a serum sodium level of 125 mmol/L. Other electrolyte levels were within normal limits. The patient denied any history of diuretic use or excessive fluid intake. An initial diagnosis of Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) was made. The patient was enrolled in a clinical trial aimed at evaluating the different types of osmotic dysregulation in SIADH. She met the eligibility criteria for the study, and informed consent was obtained. The patient underwent an osmotic stimulation with infusion of hypertonic saline, and AVP and copeptin levels were measured. The results of the study will help to classify the type of SIADH the patient is suffering from and further analyze the pathophysiology of SIADH.

The patient is an 80-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with colon cancer and is scheduled for colorectal surgery in the next few weeks. She lives alone in her own apartment and is able to perform most of her daily activities independently. However, she is concerned about her ability to recover from the surgery and maintain her independence afterwards. She is generally in good health but experiences occasional shortness of breath and fatigue when exerting herself. She takes medication for high blood pressure and a daily multivitamin. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her prepare for the surgery and improve her overall health and wellbeing.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days and does not suffer from any endocrine disorders such as PCOS or thyroid dysfunction. Her BMI is 25 and she has normal TSH and prolactin levels. She has no history of ovarian surgery, radio/chemotherapy or endometriosis. She has undergone basic infertility investigations and the results revealed an AMH level of 1.8 ng/mL and an AFC of 6. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to develop a personalized approach to ovarian stimulation, taking into account genetic, functional and hormonal biomarkers. She hopes that this approach will increase her chances of success and reduce the time it takes to achieve pregnancy.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who was diagnosed with malignant melanoma that has metastasized to his lymph nodes and lungs. He has previously undergone surgery to remove some of the tumors and radiation therapy to the remaining ones. He has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and coughing up blood. He does not have any other significant medical history or current illnesses. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He occasionally drinks alcohol but has cut back since his diagnosis. His physical exam shows some enlarged lymph nodes and decreased breath sounds in his lungs. His lab studies show a normal CBC, but his LDH level is elevated. A CT scan confirms the presence of metastatic disease in his lymph nodes and lungs. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits. He is married with two children and works as an accountant.

A 56-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder that has metastasized to his lungs. He has already undergone neoadjuvant chemotherapy containing a platinum compound, but the disease progression has not stopped. The patient is now seeking an alternative treatment and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities with some difficulty. He has completed all major surgeries and biopsies more than 28 days ago. He has no known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or other recombinant human antibodies. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has agreed to use effective contraception during and for at least six months after completion of the study treatment. He is willing to undergo blood collection periodically for pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic correlative studies. The patient does not have a history of serious cardiovascular disease, bleeding diathesis, or coagulopathy. He has not received prior antiangiogenic therapy primarily targeting the vascular endothelial growth factor pathway. The patient is willing to receive VEGF Trap IV over 1 hour on day 1 and repeat the treatment every 14 days in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of pain and stiffness in the jaw joint for the past 6 months. The pain is localized to the left temporomandibular joint and is aggravated by chewing and talking. She has difficulty opening her mouth, and her maximum mouth opening is less than 30mm. Her lateral and protrusive movements are also impeded. The patient has no history of trauma or any significant medical illness. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. She has all her teeth intact and has not undergone any invasive or surgical treatments of TMJ. The physical examination reveals tenderness over the left TMJ, and there is a clicking sound during jaw movement. The patient is diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the left temporomandibular joint. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of TMJ-OA and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 35 year old female complains of occasional numbness and tingling sensation in her right hand. She works as a graphic designer and spends most of her day typing and using the mouse. She has no history of carpal tunnel syndrome, arm or hand surgery, or any existing upper extremity deformities. She has no open wounds or lesions in her hand or forearm. She is not diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis or any other autoimmune disorder. She has agreed to participate in the study to determine the relationship between age and carpal tunnel size.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for several months. He has been taking over-the-counter sleep aids and has noticed that they are becoming less effective. He reports feeling fatigued during the day and has noticed a decline in his overall health. He has not exercised regularly in the past 6 months but is otherwise healthy. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He does not smoke or consume alcohol, and he is willing to adhere to the conditions of the study. He is interested in exploring non-pharmacological options to improve his sleep quality.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and is currently undergoing hemodialysis. He has a history of hypertension and hyperuricemia, with serum uric acid levels consistently above 7.0 mg/dL. He has not been on any urate-lowering therapy such as allopurinol or probenecid. He has not been hospitalized in the past 3 months and is in stable clinical condition. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated for this study. The patient will be reassessed after two months for changes in ADMA serum level, serum hsCRP, and serum uric acid levels.

A 62 year old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer four years ago. He has undergone radical prostatectomy and radiation therapy, but the PSA levels increased after a year. Since then, he has been on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with a GnRH analogue. He has now developed bone pain and a bone scan showed multiple bone metastases. He is experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and decreased appetite. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. His serum testosterone level is below 50 ng/dL. His serum albumin is 3.2 g/dL and serum potassium is 4.0 mmol/L. He has no significant comorbidities and has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. A biopsy of the bone metastasis shows adenocarcinoma of the prostate without neuroendocrine differentiation or small cell features. The tumor specimen obtained prior to treatment initiation by interventional radiology guided biopsy shows overexpression of androgen receptor (AR)-C terminal and AR-N terminal and PTEN with lack of ARV7 expression along with and ki67 =<10%. There is no combined RB loss and p53 mutation and no expression of neuroendocrine markers CD56 and chromogranin. He is willing to use birth control methods during the study treatment.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. He works as a construction worker and has been experiencing fatigue and occasional abdominal pain for the past few months. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He underwent biopsy and was found to have RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer. He has completed eight cycles of 5-fluorouracil-based chemotherapy plus cetuximab and has stable disease. His ECOG Performance Status is 1, and he has measurable lesions that meet the RECIST 1.1 criteria. His expected survival is greater than 16 weeks. He has no history of CNS metastatic disease or prior cerebral metastasis. His labs and clinical assessments are within normal limits for the study. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 60-year-old man came to the dental clinic with complete edentulism in his mandibular arch. He has had dentures for the past 10 years, but they have been loose and uncomfortable. He has also noticed that he has difficulty chewing and speaking properly. He has a history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy. His mandibular ridge height is 8 mm and has a width of 10 mm, without the need for bone grafting. He has a class I ridge relation and a zone of keratinized mucosa. He has a U-shaped arch and does not smoke. He is compliant and willing to participate in the clinical trial to improve his oral health and quality of life.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with sickle cell disease (hemoglobin SS) who has experienced multiple episodes of severe vaso-occlusive pain crises in the past two years despite treatment with hydroxyurea. He has also experienced osteonecrosis in two of his joints despite supportive care measures. He has no HLA matched sibling or 10/10 matched unrelated donor. He has failed prior hydroxyurea therapy and meets the protocol specified organ function criteria. He is willing to participate in this pilot study to receive a haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplant (HaploHCT) using a new combination of drugs (chemotherapy) that does not completely wipe out the bone marrow cells and most of the donor CD4+ T cells (a type of immune cells) will be removed (depleted) before giving the blood stem cell transplant to the patient to improve transplant outcomes. The patient understands that the COH-MC-17 regimen is a non-myeloablative regimen (cyclophosphamide, pentostatin and rabbit-anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG)) followed by a CD4+ T-cell-depleted haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplant (HaploHCT). He is willing to comply with the study requirements including follow-up visits and other study procedures. He understands that the study aims to determine the safety and feasibility of the regimen and its ability to induce a mixed chimeric status in severe sickle cell disease patients. He agrees to use adequate contraception prior to study entry and 6 months post-transplant.

A 44-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer two years ago. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, and her current scans show that her disease is stable. She is in generally good health, with no significant medical history other than her breast cancer. She has a performance status of ECOG 0, and her estimated life expectancy is at least 6 months. Her lab results show normal liver, kidney, and blood cell function. She has not been on any anti-cancer therapy for at least 4 weeks. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She has no history of autoimmune or immunodeficiency disorders, and she does not have pleural effusions or ascites requiring frequent paracentesis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options and contribute to research efforts.

This clinical trial is a retrospective study and does not require a patient description. However, it is important to note that the study is evaluating the effectiveness of intra-disc infiltrations in patients with active disc disease who were hospitalized between 2007 and 2014 in the Rheumatology Department for intradiscal infiltration. The study aims to assess the duration of pain relief, the impact of the infiltrations on NSAIDs and/or analgesics, and the effectiveness of the infiltrations in different subgroups such as those with a history of spine surgery, spondylolisthesis, or scoliosis. Patients aged over 18 years old are eligible for inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 5 years. She is experiencing difficulty in sleeping and reports a Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) score of 7. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine for SLE and has no other significant medical history. She works as a graphic designer and spends most of her time sitting in front of the computer. She reports no regular exercise routine and has a sedentary lifestyle. She lives with her husband and two children and is responsible for household chores. She has a healthy diet and is a non-smoker. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her sleep quality and overall health. She is willing to commit to the exercise program and follow-up appointments. She is able to read and understand the informed consent form and is willing to sign it.

A 32-year-old male who has been smoking at least 20 cigarettes a day for the past 5 years. He has tried to quit smoking multiple times but has failed due to strong cravings and withdrawal symptoms. He is generally in good health and does not have any medical conditions that would interfere with the study medication or participation. He does not use any psychoactive drugs or medications. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He lives in Little Rock, Arkansas or the surrounding area.

A 26-year-old healthy male with no history of chronic diseases or psychotic symptoms is being recruited for a clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of DW1029M. The patient has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 and weighs 68 kg. He has no known drug allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past two months. The clinical trial will involve a single oral dose of the medication, which will be taken with 240 mL of water. The patient will be monitored for adverse events, and will undergo vital sign checks, EKG, laboratory tests, and physical examinations at scheduled intervals. The study is intended to investigate the efficacy and safety of DW1029M in the treatment of diabetic kidney disease. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

Patient A is a 16-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent asthma symptoms for the past three months. She has been using an inhaled corticosteroid as part of her asthma treatment for the same period. She has a history of seasonal allergies but no other major medical issues. Her current medication regimen includes albuterol as a rescue inhaler, which she has been using as needed. She is willing to switch to using the study medication, vilanterol inhalation powder, as her rescue medication for the duration of the study. She has not participated in a vilanterol study before and is willing to use a birth control method if she is of childbearing potential. Her pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is between 40%-90% predicted and she has demonstrated reversibility of FEV1 of at least 12% and 200mls. She has not had a respiratory infection in the past four weeks and has not experienced an asthma exacerbation in the past three months. She is currently not taking any other investigational medication or medication prohibited for use during the study.

A premature newborn infant weighing 1.5 kg with gestational age of 30 weeks, admitted to the Neonatal Care Unit (NICU) at Maternidade Dr. Alfredo da Costa, Lisbon. The infant is currently being exclusively fed with human milk and is expected to continue to be fed with human milk during their stay in the NICU. The infant is expected to be discharged alive from the hospital. There are no diagnosed innate metabolism disorders and the infant is not a multiple of grade >2. The parents have provided consent for their infant to participate in the study, which aims to assess the effect of target fortified human milk on the growth quality of very preterm infants.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of heart failure and an ejection fraction of 30%. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and reduced exercise tolerance. His cardiologist has recommended cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) to improve his symptoms. He is currently taking medications for heart failure, including a beta-blocker and an ACE inhibitor. His ECG shows a QRS duration of 150 ms. He has provided informed consent to participate in this study and is willing to undergo CRT device implantation. He does not have any recent history of myocardial infarction or NYHA Class IV symptoms.

It is not possible to generate a patient description for this clinical trial as it does not involve patient recruitment. This study will only use previously collected data from participants in the San Diego Population Study. Therefore, there are no eligibility criteria for individual patients.

Pt is a 55yo F with a 10-year history of knee pain and stiffness, particularly in the medial compartment of the right knee. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by her orthopedic surgeon and has tried a variety of conservative treatments including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections without significant improvement. She reports difficulty with activities of daily living, particularly going up and down stairs and getting in and out of chairs. She has a BMI of 26 and does not have any other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of knee bracing on reducing her pain and disability.

A 50-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She is currently obese with a body mass index (BMI) of 38 and has been experiencing inflammation in her adipose tissue. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes or cardiovascular disease but has a family history of breast cancer. Her current medications include a daily multivitamin and calcium supplement. She is fluent in English and interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce inflammation in fat tissues and lower the production of substances such as estrogens that may increase the risk of developing breast cancer. She is not currently taking any medication known to induce amenorrhea and her serum estradiol level is less than 20 pg/mL. She is willing to stay in the hospital for about 2 weeks and take Celebrex for approximately 10 days while eating a diet similar to what she consumed before coming into the hospital for the study. Her medical history does not include any of the exclusion criteria listed for this study.

A 41-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been in remission for 18 months but recently presented with a lump in her left breast. A biopsy confirmed the recurrence of her cancer. She is now feeling anxious and concerned about her health. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is currently unemployed and lives with her husband and two children. She reports no significant family history of cancer. Her pathology report confirmed that she has triple-negative breast cancer, and her tumor tested positive for the androgen receptor. She is currently not on any medication for her cancer. She is willing to participate in clinical trials to receive the best possible treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who recently tested positive for COVID-19 and is experiencing severe respiratory symptoms. He has been hospitalized due to pneumonia and requires oxygen support. The patient has a confirmed volume of lung damage by CT scan and an oxygen saturation of less than 93%. He is able to proceed with inhalation by self. The patient must be able to understand the study objectives and risks and provide signed and dated informed consent. He does not have severe respiratory failure at the time of screening due to COVID-19 pneumonia, and there is no history of medical resuscitation for 14 days before randomization. The patient does not have any serious medical conditions or deviations of clinical laboratory parameters that would prevent safe participation in the study. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have liver function failure, ANC <500 cells/µL, platelet count <50000 cells/µL, creatinine level ≥ 1.5 from the upper limit, uncontrolled or untreated arrhythmia with clinical manifestations, myocardial infarction within the last 6 weeks, congestive heart failure (NYHA Degrees 3 or 4), respiratory failure in the last 6 months, or home use of oxygen in severe chronic respiratory disease (COPD). The patient does not have quadriplegia or primary immunodeficiency, tuberculosis, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, aspergillosis, or other invasive mold/fungal infection in anamnesis, or internal or bone marrow transplantation for 6 months before randomization. There is no known infection with hepatitis B or C viruses requiring therapy.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. He has been experiencing frequent auditory hallucinations, hearing voices that he believes are real and external. These hallucinations occur multiple times a day, making it difficult for him to concentrate and function normally. Despite trying various antipsychotic medications, his symptoms have not improved significantly. He has no contraindications to TMS and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

55-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) and a current class I-IIa indication for ablation. He presents with palpitations, shortness of breath, and occasional chest discomfort. Past medical history includes hypertension, mild dyslipidemia, and a remote history of tobacco use. He is currently on a beta-blocker and an anticoagulant. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and complete all required study procedures through 12 months. His life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 12 months. However, he has not undergone any previous ablation procedure using a high-density and high-power short duration approach, nor has he undergone tricuspid or mitral valve repair surgery. The patient does not have persistent or long-standing persistent AF and does not have a left atrial diameter greater than 5.0 cm. The patient is not currently experiencing thrombus in the left atrium or left atrial appendage and has not undergone MI, CABG, or PCI within the preceding 3 months. Left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than 35% and the patient is currently NYHA class I or II.

A 52-year old female was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia six months ago. She has completed her chemotherapy and is currently in complete remission. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes Losartan. She lives with her husband and two children. She works as a teacher and is looking forward to returning to work. The patient complains of fatigue and occasional bruising. Her platelet count is currently 25/nl. She has not experienced any bleeding episodes so far. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the therapeutic platelet transfusion regimen as described.

67-year-old male with a history of myopia and hypertension presented to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of decreased vision in his right eye. Examination revealed macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with identifiable retinal breaks. The patient was deemed eligible for pneumatic retinopexy and is phakic. The patient has no history of intraocular inflammation, uncontrollable elevated IOP, open-angle glaucoma, or previous vitrectomy or scleral buckle procedure. There is no evidence of proliferative vitreoretinopathy of type C or D. The patient has no current blood in the vitreous, corneal opacity or other conditions which limit the view of peripheral retina. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the tolerability of INS37217 Intravitreal Injection for the treatment of macula-on or macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.

The patient is a 42-year-old female with a history of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and infrequent bowel movements for the past year, which have significantly impacted her daily life. She has tried various dietary changes and over-the-counter laxatives with limited success. She has not used any prebiotic, probiotic, or laxative products in the last 10 days. She has no known allergies to any of the ingredients in the dietary supplement being studied. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is motivated to participate in the study and willing to follow the assigned diet restriction scheme with or without inuline, choline, and silymarin supplementation for the duration of the study.

A 35-year-old healthcare worker presents with a history of frequent hand washing due to her job requirements. She has noticed that her hands are becoming increasingly dry and irritated, which is affecting her ability to perform her duties. She has a past medical history of atopic dermatitis and seasonal allergies. She is currently taking over-the-counter antihistamines for her allergies. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effects of hand washing and hand sanitizer on skin proteins and lipids. She is willing to temporarily withhold the use of topical corticosteroids and antibiotics on her hands for 7 days prior to the study. She will also withhold the use of moisturizers on the area 24 hours prior to the visit. She has not taken a bleach bath within 7 days of the visit and will not take a bath or shower on the day of the visit. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not taken any systemic immunosuppressive drugs or biologic medications within the specified time frames.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who has been diagnosed with relapsed T-cell leukemia. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past, but the disease has returned. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and bone pain. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the presence of leukemia cells. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and he has no history of liver or kidney disease. He is able to swallow tablets and capsules and is willing to comply with the safety monitoring requirements of the study. The patient has not received prior treatment with gamma-secretase inhibitor RO4929097 or dexamethasone.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus for 3 years. She has been receiving multiple daily insulin injections for the past year. Her body mass index is 25 kg/m2 and her total body weight is 60 kg. Her HbA1c level is 7.5%, fasting C-peptide levels are 0.4 ng/mL, and her CBC and platelet counts are within normal limits. She is willing to sign the study informed consent document and is in good general health with no infections, active tuberculosis (TB), late severe complications, or concomitant medical conditions that would influence the outcome of the trial. She has not been treated with angiotensin-converting enzymes/angiotensin II receptor blockers (ACE/ARB) in the past month. She is not pregnant and agrees to use oral contraceptives for 21 days prior to the first dose and until 28 days after the last dose. She has not had a total daily insulin dosage exceeding 1.0 U/kg/day or a change in total daily insulin dose level of more than 50% (increase or decrease) within the past 3 months, and has not been treated with any diabetes medication other than insulin. She does not have a score of 4 or more restricted responses on the Clarke Hypoglycemia Awareness Survey, and her systolic and diastolic blood pressure are within normal limits. She does not have clinical worsening of retinopathy or neuropathy in the previous 3 months, or clinical worsening of nephropathy in the previous 3 months, with serum creatinine within normal limits. She does not have a history or presence of acute or chronic pancreatitis, or active infections at screening and during the study, and does not have a history of asthma or TB. She has not received any investigational product within 30 days of admission into this study or had any prior or existing exposure to INGAP-P, glucagon-like peptides (GLP-1, GLP-2, or analogs), ustekinumab, or TNF blocking agents. She is not known to have hypersensitivity to INGAP-P or any excipient used in the formulation, or to ustekinumab or any components of the product. She is not concurrently or planned to participate in any other clinical study during the conduct of this study, and has tested negative for cocaine, opiates, amphetamines, or cannabinoids. She is able to fill out and maintain a daily diary during the screening period prior to dosing. She is negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), or hepatitis C seropositivity in blood sample taken during screening.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes who is scheduled for elective cardiac surgery due to severe aortic stenosis. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 mL/min/1.73m². The patient has been on medication for hypertension and diabetes for the last 5 years, and has no previous history of renal replacement therapy. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the influence of elevated baseline serum creatinine and body composition on acute kidney injury in cardiac surgery. The patient's participation in the trial will involve providing informed consent, undergoing preoperative testing and monitoring during and after the surgery, and providing blood and urine samples for evaluation of novel biomarkers for AKI. The patient's eligibility for the trial will be based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

56 year old male with a recent diagnosis of metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma with lymph node and bone metastases. The patient's past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled on medications. He has no history of prior cancer or autoimmune diseases. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, and his estimated glomerular filtration rate is 64 mL/min. He has

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with atypical endometrial hyperplasia. She desires to preserve fertility and is reluctant to undergo hysterectomy due to personal reasons. The patient has no other medical comorbidities and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of oral Megestrol acetate and the levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUD) in treating atypical endometrial hyperplasia. She has been advised that she will be randomized to receive either oral Megestrol acetate or the LNG-IUD and will be followed up for a period of time to determine the ability and duration of the treatment to produce complete regression. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent definitive radiation therapy and has been on intermittent hormonal therapy for the past year. His PSA levels have been rising steadily over the past 6 months, and he has developed bone pain in his hips and lower back. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of other cancers or significant medical conditions. He is married and lives with his wife. The physical exam is remarkable for mild tenderness in the lower back and hips. The lab results show a PSA level of 22 ng/mL and a WBC count of 6,500/mm^3. The patient has been on a low calcium diet for the past month.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 2 years ago. She is 5'5" tall and weighs 84 kg (BMI: 30 kg/m2). She has been prescribed oral hypoglycemic agents and insulin to control her blood glucose levels. However, her blood glucose levels remain high despite medication. She is a homemaker and has a family history of T2DM. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and she has no history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. She has not had any abdominal surgery in the past. She is willing to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the follow-up protocol. She has no history of drug or alcohol dependence, and she is not currently participating in any other conflicting research protocol.

A 32-year-old male triathlete who has been training for endurance sports for the past 8 years is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He typically trains 6 days a week, with a combination of running, cycling, and swimming, for a total of 15-20 hours per week. He has no history of gastrointestinal disease and is a non-smoker. He has no current medical conditions and is not taking any drug therapies. He has a history of normal blood pressure and is not a vegetarian. He is interested in the study as he is curious to see if his training status will affect the absorption of flavonoids into his body. He is willing to follow the special polyphenol-free diet and record his dietary intake for 2 days preceding each trial and during the day of the experimental trial.

A 49-year old administrative assistant was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia. She is currently taking Metformin, Glipizide, and Pioglitazone. Despite being on these medications, her blood sugar levels remain high, with her latest HbA1c being 8.9%. She reports fatigue and frequent urination. She is aware of the importance of diet and exercise and has tried to make lifestyle modifications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is motivated to improve her diabetes management and willing to try new medication options.

The patient is a 76-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation after experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both well-controlled with medications. He has never had a stroke or transient ischemic attack, but he does have an enlarged left atrium and a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. He is currently taking medications for his hypertension and diabetes, as well as a blood thinner to prevent clotting. He has not had any major surgeries or medical procedures in the past six months. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits. He has given informed consent to participate and is willing to adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) at stage III. She completed the standard first-line chemotherapy treatment and her response was stable disease (SD). Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 2. Her lab results are within normal limits, with the exception of elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels. She has no history of CNS metastases, but has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with one medication. She has no other active malignancies or autoimmune diseases requiring systemic treatment. She is not currently on chronic systemic steroids or experiencing any active infections. She has no known allergies to any component of Anlotinib. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and has signed the informed consent form.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer that has spread to other parts of the body is seeking treatment options after progression following his first-line therapy. His medical history includes hypertension and he is a non-smoker. The patient underwent a biopsy and confirmed a protein status of ATM by IHC archival tumor sample. He has one measurable and/or non-measurable lesion that can be accurately assessed by imaging (CT/MRI) at baseline and follow up visits. He has not received any previous treatment with a PARP inhibitor, including olaparib. The patient has only received one prior chemotherapy regimen for the treatment of gastric cancer in the metastatic or recurrent setting. He has not been diagnosed with any second primary cancer, except for adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) for the past two years. She reports frequent abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea, which significantly affects her quality of life and work productivity. She has tried various medications and dietary changes without much improvement. She has no comorbid medical problems affecting her gastrointestinal system, and she has not previously undergone any surgery related to her GI tract. She has never participated in a low FODMAP diet or any other dietary therapy. She is willing to maintain a stable dosage of her IBS medications during the baseline period and is open to "rescue" medications as needed. Her colonoscopy and flexible sigmoidoscopy findings were normal, and she has not been diagnosed with celiac disease. She is not currently pregnant, and she is not taking any probiotics, antibiotics, laxatives, or narcotics.

A 45-year-old woman received a kidney transplant 2 years ago due to end-stage renal disease caused by lupus nephritis. She has a history of hypertension that was diagnosed at the age of 32. She is currently on a stable anti-hypertensive regimen of Losartan, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide. She also takes Tacrolimus, Mycophenolate Mofetil, and Prednisone as part of her immunosuppressive regimen. She has no known allergies to medications. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She reports that her last blood pressure check was 142/88 mm Hg at a local pharmacy. She has not been hospitalized in the past 6 months. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to better understand and manage her nocturnal hypertension. She has no history of falls, atrial fibrillation, Parkinson's Disease, severe orthostatic hypotension, or autonomic dysfunction.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension. He was diagnosed with hypertension four years ago and was prescribed medication for it. However, he has been non-adherent to his medication and his blood pressure has been consistently high (BP>140/90 mmHg) at his recent visits to the clinic. He works as a construction worker and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not exercise regularly and his diet mainly consists of processed and fast foods. He is married and has two children. He has a family history of hypertension. He is fluent in English and has no significant psychiatric comorbidity. He is interested in learning more about how to manage his hypertension and is willing to participate in the study.

A 46-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent episodes of biliary colic. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril (10 mg/day). She denies any history of liver disease, drug or alcohol abuse. She has no known food allergies or intolerances. Her BMI is 28. She has been advised to fast for at least 8 hours prior to surgery. She is currently taking no medications other than lisinopril. She is a non-smoker and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

60-year-old male with bilateral knee arthritis and chronic pain who has been advised by his orthopedic surgeon to undergo bilateral knee arthroplasty at AKUH Karachi. He has tried conservative treatments for his knee pain, including physical therapy and medications, but has not achieved significant relief. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of Prolene sutures and staple sutures for skin closure after the surgery. He is physically fit with an ASA level of II and has a functional class of II. He is able to comprehend the details of the trial and is willing to provide informed consent for participation. He has no history of cognitive impairment and has no documented allergies to Prolene or stainless steel. He is undergoing elective bilateral TKR under the care of the selected surgeon for the study.

The patient is a 6-month-old infant who was brought to the emergency department by his parents with a history of cough, nasal congestion, and fever for the past 2 days. The patient is diagnosed with bronchiolitis after a thorough clinical examination by the pediatrician. The patient has a respiratory rate of 50 breaths per minute and a heart rate of 130 beats per minute. Oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. The patient is admitted to the pediatric hospitalist medicine group for further management. The patient is randomized to the NoseFrida group and the parents are given the device and instructions on how to use it. The parents are encouraged to use the device as often as possible, especially before feedings and sleep. The patient receives frequent nasal suctioning throughout the hospital stay and is deep suctioned as clinically needed. The patient is discharged after 3 days with an improved respiratory score and no need for supplemental oxygen. The parents report high satisfaction with the NoseFrida device and its ease of use.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread body pain and tenderness for the past year. She has also been struggling with fatigue, poor sleep, and mood disturbances. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by her primary care physician and has tried various medications and therapies without significant improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential new treatment for fibromyalgia. She has not taken duloxetine before and does not have a history of psychoses, bipolar disorder, or schizoaffective disorder. She does not have any other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with study requirements.

A 35-year-old male was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has been deemed a high-risk patient due to relapsed disease. He has undergone chemotherapy and is now planning to undergo HLA-matched related sibling nonmyeloablative hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. After the transplantation, he will be enrolled in a clinical trial to receive autologous tumor cell vaccine with or without donor lymphocyte infusion. The cancer cell vaccine will be produced using his own tumor cells. The donor lymphocytes will be obtained from the same relative who donated stem cells for the transplantation. The primary objective of the clinical trial is to determine the time to relapse and overall survival of high-risk AML patients treated with this regimen. The study will also evaluate the safety and tolerability of the regimen and determine the maximum tolerated dose of donor lymphocyte infusions. The patient is eager to participate in the clinical trial and hopes that it will improve his prognosis.

A 24-year-old female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2, who does not have any gastrointestinal complaints, and has not undergone any major abdominal surgery will be eligible for this clinical trial. She should not have any severe cardiovascular, respiratory, urogenital, hematological/immunologic, HEENT, dermatological/-connective tissue, musculoskeletal, metabolic/nutritional, endocrine, neurological/-psychiatric diseases, allergy or have undergone any laboratory assessments that might limit participation in or completion of the study protocol. The patient should not have gastrointestinal or hepatic disorders that influence gastrointestinal absorption or transit. Additionally, the patient should not be using any medication that can alter gastric emptying or intestinal transit or influence satiety/energy intake, except oral contraceptives. The patient should not be pregnant, lactating, wish to become pregnant during the study or have a positive pregnancy test at inclusion. Finally, patients with a history of excessive alcohol consumption, smoking or HIV-positive state should not be included.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She has been on metformin 1000mg twice daily and has maintained an HbA1c level of 7.2%. She has no complications related to diabetes so far. The patient is interested in participating in the "Heidelberg Study on Diabetes and Complications" to further understand the metabolic dysbalance and its potential impact on her health. She is able to understand and follow the study procedures and is willing to undergo yearly examinations and tests. She has no history of acute infections or fever, immune suppressant therapy, psychiatric diseases requiring treatment, alcohol or drug dependency, and has not participated in any interventional studies. The patient has no metallic or magnetic implants, allergies against MRI contrast, and her waist circumference is 95cm. She is willing to undergo clamp study and bioimpedance measurement.

A 45-year-old male with no significant medical history presented to the emergency department with a deep second-degree burn on his lower leg sustained from a work-related accident. The patient was treated with appropriate wound care and referred to a wound care specialist for follow-up. Upon examination, the wound measured approximately 12 cm2 and had a skin defect. The patient was approached to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of VistaCare® in accelerating the formation of quality granulation tissue and reducing preparation time to cover the wound compared to traditional dressings. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has given written consent. The patient does not have any associated pathologies, does not smoke, and is fluent in French. The wound is located below the knee, and the patient does not require surgical debridement. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and is able to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of smoking and a recent diagnosis of metastatic pancreatic cancer. The patient received one prior systemic regimen for metastatic disease. The patient has no history of radiation therapy, but he had a surgery for a hernia repair 3 weeks ago. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his blood work is within normal limits. The patient is currently not receiving any other anticancer treatment. He has no known neurotoxicity and has no significant history of cardiac disease. The patient is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. He enjoys gardening and watching sports. He has no known allergies and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to explore innovative treatments for his cancer.

The patient is a 52 year-old male with a history of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, which has progressed despite several lines of systemic therapy including chemotherapy and immunotherapy. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. His recent blood work shows absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2.5 x 10^9/L, Hemoglobin (Hb) level of 12 g/dL, and Platelet count of 150 x 10^9/L. His total bilirubin level is 0.8 X Upper Limit Normal (ULN), AST and ALT level are within normal range, and his serum creatinine level is 0.9 ULN. He has no history of autoimmune disease, interstitial lung disease or active pneumonitis. He is negative for HIV and HCV. He has no symptomatic/active central nervous system (CNS) metastases or other tumor location necessitating an urgent therapeutic intervention. He has not received any systemic treatment with any immunosuppressive medication within one-week prior treatment start. He has no significant ECG abnormalities or chronic liver disease. He is affiliated to a social security system or an equivalent system. The patient agrees to pre- and on-treatment tumor biopsies and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the study and for 5 months after the last dose of study drug.

The patient is a 57-year-old female diagnosed with rectal cancer. The biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma of the rectum. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, pelvic radiation, or prior colorectal cancer. Pelvic MRI shows node-negative (N0), T2 rectal cancer located 6 cm from the anal verge. The closest distance between the tumor edge and mesorectal fascia is 7mm. She has no metastasis or obstructing rectal cancer. She is eligible for conventional laparoscopic low anterior resection or transanal hybrid-laparoscopic low anterior resection with or without a temporary diverting stoma. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has a BMI of 30 and no history of fecal incontinence. She is not pregnant or breast-feeding and is not receiving any other study agents. She has no large uterine fibroids or uncontrolled intercurrent illness.

The patient is a 63-year-old man with a history of Parkinson's disease diagnosed 8 years ago. He has been taking levodopa-carbidopa for the past year with partial improvement of motor symptoms. However, he experiences frequent falls or near falls (>2/week) and has poor balance. His falls are not due to apparent non-CNS etiologies such as heart problems, orthopedic issues, or peripheral neuropathy. He is ambulatory and uses a cane for support. He does not have dementia with a score of MMSE 30. He is not taking any cholinergic or anticholinergic medications and has not used Warfarin in the past 10 days. He is eligible for the study and can participate in the clinical trial.

A 50 year old woman was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus after presenting with increased thirst, frequent urination and fatigue. She has no other known medical problems and is not on any medications. Her HbA1c level at the time of diagnosis was 7.5%. She is willing to comply with a treatment and follow-up regimen and is able to perform intensive diabetes management. Her creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL, liver function tests are within normal limits, and she does not have severe anemia, proliferative retinopathy, or heart failure. She has a history of stable angina and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 8 months ago. She is not pregnant, willing to get pregnant or practice any contraceptive method, and she speaks fluent English. She does not have a history of heavy alcohol or illicit drug use.

Patient is a 42yo male who received a living donor kidney transplant 5 years ago. He has been on Tacrolimus BID (Prograf) for immunosuppression since the transplant. His serum creatinine has been stable at 1.6 mg/dL with no episodes of acute rejection. His recent Tacrolimus trough levels have been in the target range but he sometimes forgets to take his BID doses on time. He has agreed to participate in the study and has been converted to Tacrolimus OD (Advagraf) as part of the study protocol. The patient will undergo regular monitoring of his renal function and Tacrolimus levels for a period of 6 months post-conversion to determine if there are any changes in his renal function, and if any dose adjustments are necessary based on his ethnic background and pharmacogenetics. The patient will also undergo genotyping to determine his CYP3A5 genotype, which may help to inform his optimal Tacrolimus dosing in the future.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B 5 years ago. He has been regularly monitored by his physician and has been taking antiviral medication as prescribed. His medical history also includes high blood pressure, which is being treated with medication. Recently, he was diagnosed with a single lesion of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in his liver, which was within the MiLan criteria for ablation. He underwent thermal ablation surgery to treat the lesion and is now being considered for participation in a clinical trial to assess tumor recurrence using combi-elastography imaging technology. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any other serious illnesses that would prevent him from participating in the study.

A 48-year-old male patient with a history of smoking and occasional alcohol intake is diagnosed with local advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He presents with symptoms of nasal obstruction, headache, and epistaxis for the past 2 months. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known drug allergies. The patient underwent neo-adjuvant chemotherapy and concurrent chemo-radiotherapy. He is currently experiencing mucosal ulceration and salivary gland damage, which has affected his appetite and caused him to lose weight. The patient can still feed through the mouth, and his ECOG status is 1. His hemodynamic indices are normal, with a white blood cell count of 5.5×109/L, neutrophil count of 2.2×109/L, platelet count of 180×109/L, and hemoglobin level of 110g/l. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the impact of nutrition on his condition.

35-year-old male office worker with chronic low back pain for the past 6 months presents to the doctor with concerns about his ability to continue working due to the pain. He has been offered a rehabilitation program through the NHS, but he is unsure if it will be enough to help him stay at work. He reports that the pain is worse when he sits for long periods of time and has been affecting his productivity at work. He has tried over-the-counter pain medication, but it only provides temporary relief. He is fluent in English and is referred by his GP in South Nottinghamshire for this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression for the past six months. She has been feeling worried and nervous most of the time, has trouble sleeping, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has also been experiencing physical symptoms like headaches, stomach problems, and muscle tension. She has never received any formal mental health treatment before but is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any history of substance abuse or severe mental illness. She is currently taking a low dose of an antidepressant medication prescribed by her primary care physician. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and she does not have any medical conditions that would interfere with her participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes. She has been managing her condition with metformin for the past year, but her blood sugar levels are still not well-controlled, with a fasting plasma glucose (FPG) of 220 mg/dL and an HbA1c of 8.5%. She has never taken NSAIDs before and has no history of allergy to aspirin. She is generally in good health, but she does have a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She is interested in participating in the TINSAL-T2D clinical trial to see if salsalate can help improve her blood sugar control and potentially lower her risk of complications associated with diabetes. She is willing to use an appropriate contraceptive method if necessary during the study.

The patient is a Filipino individual who has received or will receive at least one dose of Prevenar, a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. They have not previously discontinued Prevenar therapy due to safety concerns. No information regarding their age, gender, medical history, or current health status is necessary for inclusion in this study.

This is a 55 year-old female with a history of obesity, BMI of 35, and non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). She has been on warfarin therapy for the past year to prevent blood clots and strokes associated with NVAF. She has had no major bleeding events or thrombotic events while on warfarin. However, she is interested in switching to a DOAC (direct oral anti-coagulant) medication due to the inconvenience of frequent INR monitoring required with warfarin. She has been clinically stable and has not had any recent hip or knee replacement surgeries. She is enrolled in the VA health care system and has Medicare coverage. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and safety of DOACs vs warfarin among obese patients with NVAF.

Patient is a 45-year-old female from the United States who works as an office manager. She wears multifocal contact lenses for at least one month and wears lenses for minimum wear 4 days/week and 10 hours/day. She spends at least 5 hours a day using digital devices such as computer, tablet, or smartphone. She spends more than 10 hours indoors at least 5 days a week. She has not been diagnosed with any active ocular disease or infection, and has not undergone refractive error surgery. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy at the time of enrollment. She is willing and able to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule and to wear test lenses for minimum 5 days/week and 10 hours/day. Her current refraction indicates a reading addition of +1.75 and she is able to achieve 0.18 logMar (20/30) binocular distance acuity with the test lenses.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a history of diabetes and hypertension. He presents to the wound care clinic with a chronic wound on his left foot that has been present for several months. The wound is a grade 3 ulcer and is located on the plantar aspect of his foot. The patient reports pain and difficulty with walking due to the wound. His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. The patient has no known allergies to medications or dressings. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

28-year-old female with a confirmed genetic diagnosis of Prader-Willi Syndrome. She has a history of early onset obesity and abnormal pubertal development. Her BMI is currently 32.5 and she has struggled with weight loss attempts in the past. She also experiences significant behavioral problems related to food, including hyperphagia and food-seeking behaviors. She has no history of pulmonary disease or abnormal endocrine findings. She is not currently taking any medications for her PWS or weight loss. She has no significant psychiatric history or current symptoms of anxiety or depression. She is motivated to participate in the study and willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He is experiencing difficulty with walking and balance, and his symptoms have been gradually worsening over time despite taking antiparkinsonian medications. He is currently at Hoehn & Yahr stage 3 in the ON state and stage 4 in the OFF state. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He lives alone and is able to manage his activities of daily living with some difficulty. He has no history of cognitive impairment or psychiatric disorders. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his condition.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with colon cancer, underwent surgery to remove the tumor and received chemotherapy. During a follow-up visit, imaging tests showed the presence of liver metastases. The patient is generally in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no significant medical history or allergies. The patient has not received any radiation therapy to the liver and has not undergone any chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks. His platelet count, hemoglobin, and ANC are within normal limits. The patient is willing to undergo percutaneous placement of localization seeds for stereotactic targeting and planning. He is able to complete questionnaires alone or with assistance and is willing to be followed up for at least 8 weeks after the completion of the study treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer, which has metastasized to her liver and lungs. She has previously undergone chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and hormone therapy, but the cancer has progressed despite these treatments. She is now seeking alternative treatment options and has been referred for a clinical trial testing a new drug called PM00104. She has no other significant medical history and her performance status is good (ECOG 0). Her lab results are within normal limits, including normal liver and kidney function. She has a negative pregnancy test and is willing to use contraception during the study period. She has not received any radiotherapy or chemotherapy in the past 6 weeks and has no brain or meningeal metastases. She is able to comply with the treatment and follow-up requirements of the trial. She has no known hypersensitivity to any of the components of the drug product. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially benefit from testing a new treatment option.

A 28-year-old Caucasian woman who is interested in becoming an egg donor has come to the clinic. She is in good health with no underlying conditions and has a normal menstrual cycle of 28 days. She has a BMI of 21 kg/m2 and has never been exposed to radiation or hazardous chemicals. She has no history of drug use and has no family history of hereditary chromosomal diseases or sexually transmitted diseases. She has had an ultrasound that confirms that she has a normal uterus and ovaries with an antral follicle count of 15. She is interested in participating in the study to investigate the correlation between vitamin D levels and ovarian response to controlled stimulation.

45 y/o female with chronic lower back pain on the right side for the past 6 months. Pain is described as dull, achy and constant, with occasional sharp exacerbations with movement. The pain is exacerbated with prolonged sitting, standing and walking. The patient reports no history of trauma, fever, chills, or urinary symptoms. She has tried multiple over-the-counter pain medications with minimal relief. The patient has never tried acupuncture before and is interested in participating in a study to evaluate a new tool for measuring needle manipulation during acupuncture treatment. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study.

A 58-year-old woman has been suffering from knee pain for several years, which has worsened over time. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and her orthopedic surgeon has recommended a total knee replacement surgery. She has no history of blood clots or bleeding disorders, nor does she have any allergies to medications. She is currently taking daily low-dose aspirin to manage her hypertension. She exercises regularly, eats a healthy diet, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of aspirin versus rivaroxaban in preventing blood clots after the surgery.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL) and had received at least one line of systemic therapy for MCL, but her disease has relapsed, become refractory or progressed. She is in good general health with an ECOG Performance Status of 2 or less. She completed anticancer treatment with chemotherapy, small molecule inhibitors, immune modulator drugs, biologics, and/or treatment with other anticancer agents at least 3 weeks prior to treatment, or 2 weeks if progressing, and has recovered from clinically significant toxicity associated with treatment. She has not undergone prior therapy with Venetoclax or alternate BCL-2 inhibitor. Her blood counts and organ function are adequate with no history of significant liver disease, active bacterial or viral infections, or bleeding diathesis. She has no active concurrent malignancy requiring active therapy and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to remain abstinent or use a contraceptive method with a failure rate of < 1% per year during the treatment period and for at least 30 days after the last dose of venetoclax or 18 months after the last dose of rituximab, whichever is longer. She is also willing to refrain from donating sperm if male.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. During his follow-up imaging, he was found to have multiple brain metastases. He underwent a biopsy of one of the lesions, which confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic lung cancer. The patient has no significant past medical history and no history of neurological disease or symptoms. He has a Karnofsky score of 80 and is currently on a medication regimen for the treatment of his lung cancer. Imaging studies revealed the presence of more than four brain metastases, and the patient is a candidate for stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). He is willing to participate in the registry study and is able to undergo MR imaging studies.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who is an avid basketball player. He experienced a sudden twisting injury to his right knee during a game two weeks ago. He immediately felt a pop and experienced severe pain and swelling. He was unable to bear weight on his right leg and was taken to the emergency room. An MRI confirmed a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) of his right knee. He has been referred to an orthopedic surgeon who will evaluate his knee and determine whether he needs surgical treatment or rehabilitation only. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the natural course and recovery after ACL injury. He speaks fluent Swedish and is able to understand written and spoken Swedish language. He has no history of cognitive impairments or other illnesses that impair his function.

45-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and scheduled to receive induction, consolidation and salvage chemotherapy, and autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplantation according to the GIMEMA AML1310 protocol. The patient has no history of significant infections or recent hospitalizations. Past medical history includes hypertension and dyslipidemia, both well controlled with medications. The patient has no known drug allergies. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the prospective study on severe infections on AML patients.

A 62-year-old male presents to the emergency department with flu-like symptoms, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of heart disease and is currently on medication for hypertension. The patient reports having been in contact with someone who tested positive for COVID-19. Upon examination, the patient's respiratory rate is 28 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air. Chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates consistent with COVID-19. The patient is admitted to the hospital for further management and treatment. The patient is not currently on any vitamin D supplementation and has no history of renal failure requiring dialysis. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial and signs the consent form.

The patient is a sexually active 30-year-old woman who has a history of abnormal pap smears in the past. She has not undergone any cervical surgeries and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse for at least 24 hours before the study visit. She does not have any current gynecological infections or discharges and has not undergone any medical or cosmetic surgery involving the reproductive organs or genitals within the past 6 months. She is not currently enrolled in any research studies involving the application of vaginal formulations. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no other condition that would contraindicate her participation in the study.

A 60-year-old male diagnosed with Waldenstrom's Macroglobulinemia and confirmed CD20 positive according to the recommendations of the 2nd Workshop on WM. He has recurrent fever, night sweats, weight loss, and fatigue. He also experiences hyperviscosity, lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly. He has undergone prior treatment for WM comprising at least one regimen containing a therapeutic anti CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab administered for more or equal than 2 doses of antibody treatment and/or a therapeutic chemotherapy, alkylating agent, purine analogue, bendamustine administered for more or equal than 2 cycles of treatment. He is currently relapsing after 6 months of the last administration of first line or subsequent treatment. He has a life expectancy of more than 3 months and an ECOG less or equal than 2. He meets the following pretreatment laboratory criteria at the screening visit conducted within 28 days of study enrollment: ASAT 2.5 times the upper limit of institutional laboratory normal value, ALAT 2.5 times the upper limit of institutional laboratory normal value, total bilirubin 1.5 times the upper limit of institutional laboratory normal value unless clearly related to the disease or Gilbert syndrome, calculated or measured creatinine clearance by MDRD 40 mL minute. He is willing to use a highly effective method of birth control for the duration of the therapy up to 6 months after end of therapy. He has no history of anaphylactic reaction following exposure to humanized monoclonal antibodies, allogeneic transplantation, or treatment with phosphatidylinositol 3 kinase PI3K inhibitors including idelalisib or GA101. He has not undergone treatment with any other investigational agent or participating in another trial within 30 days prior to entering this study.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male with a history of osteoarthritis presents with hip pain that has been worsening over the past year. He has difficulty with daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. The pain is persistent even with rest and over-the-counter pain medication. The patient has been a member of KPNW for the past 2 years. He is scheduled to undergo total hip replacement surgery in 2 weeks. The patient has no history of substance abuse or chronic pain and is not currently being managed by a pain clinic. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to reduce opioid exposure following surgery.

56 year old man with a long history of biliary colic and recurrent cholangitis. The patient has been diagnosed with complicated hepatolithiasis, with multiple intrahepatic bile duct stones and stenosis of the left and right hepatic ducts. The patient has undergone previous open cholecystectomy, but has no other history of abdominal surgery. The patient's liver function is Child-Pugh level A, with no evidence of biliary cirrhosis, ICG level of 11%, and a residual liver volume to standard liver volume ratio of 50%. The patient is in otherwise good general health and is willing to undergo either robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgery or open surgery for the treatment of his complicated hepatolithiasis.

A 35-year-old female patient presented to the High Myopia Clinic with a history of progressive myopia since childhood. Her refraction error was -12.5 diopters in both eyes, and her axial length was 30.5 mm. She complained of decreased vision in both eyes with occasional floaters and photopsia. The patient was otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and she was not taking any medications. Ophthalmic examination revealed bilateral posterior staphylomas, diffuse chorioretinal atrophy, and multiple yellowish-white lesions at the posterior pole, consistent with punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC). The patient's best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in both eyes. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) showed focal elevation of the retinal pigment epithelium/Bruch's membrane (RPE/BrM) complex with outer retinal layer disruption in the area of the PIC lesions. Fluorescein angiography (FA) and indocyanine green angiography (ICG) showed early hypofluorescence with late staining of the inflammatory lesions, and midphase hypocyanescence at the posterior pole that extended beyond the lesions visible on FA and fundus. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial to determine the role of PIC in the progression of pathological myopia. She underwent a detailed ophthalmologic examination at baseline and every 6 months during the follow-up period of 2 years. The examinations included measurements of best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), refraction, slit lamp biomicroscopy, biometry for determination of axial length, fundus examination, FA, ICG, and assessment of fundus autofluorescence (FAF) and SD-OCT. The study will help to identify the diagnostic criteria of PIC lesions in highly myopic patients, determine the risk factors for the development of PIC, and calculate the progression rate of PIC-related lesions, by the size change during follow-up.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with early stage breast cancer. The biopsy results confirm that she has invasive ductal carcinoma. The tumor is small, measuring only 1.5 cm, and is located in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. The patient has undergone a lumpectomy and sentinel node biopsy. The margins are clear of cancer cells, and only one lymph node was found to be positive for cancer. The patient has no history of any other cancer and is not currently receiving any other treatments. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no co-existing medical conditions that would limit her life expectancy. She is post-menopausal and not currently pregnant or nursing. She has no known collagen vascular disease or psychiatric or addictive disorders. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.
