The patient is a 43-year-old female with a history of breast cancer. The patient has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past and is now scheduled for a surgery to remove a suspected lesion in her breast. The patient has no known allergies, and her laboratory and physical examination parameters are within acceptable limits. The patient is willing to participate in a research study that will collect biologic samples from the tumor and the surrounding normal tissue during the surgery. The study aims to identify novel molecular and biologic therapeutic targets for future cancer therapies. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is a fitness enthusiast and enjoys playing basketball and soccer. He sustained a non-contact injury to his right knee during a basketball game a month ago, and was diagnosed with an ACL tear. He is experiencing pain, swelling, and instability in his right knee, which is affecting his ability to play sports and perform daily activities. He has not had any previous knee injuries or surgeries. He does not smoke, use corticosteroids or chemotherapy medications, and has no known allergies to bovine products or gelatin. He has a BMI of 25 and has no history of knee infection or severe osteoarthritis. He is interested in participating in the BEAR III trial to explore a new treatment option for his ACL injury and potentially avoid undergoing traditional ACL reconstruction surgery.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with Waldenstrom's Macroglobulinemia two years ago. He underwent chemotherapy with rituximab which resulted in a partial response lasting for eight months. He is currently experiencing a relapse of his disease and his hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL. He also has symptomatic splenomegaly and mild peripheral neuropathy related to his Waldenstrom's disease. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living with some limitations. His medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently taking medication for it. He does not have any history of cardiac disease or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He is a retired teacher and spends his free time reading books and watching TV. He is married and lives with his wife who helps him with his daily activities. He has two adult children who live in a different city. He does not wish to have any more children and is willing to use adequate contraceptive measures during and six months after the end of the trial.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after presenting with fatigue, weakness, and frequent infections. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He is married with two children and works in construction. He is physically active, exercises regularly, and maintains a healthy diet. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is in good health. He has not received any prior chemotherapy for AML or myelodysplastic syndromes. He is negative for HIV and has no known allergies to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to tipifarnib. The patient is currently not taking any medications and has no other uncontrolled illnesses.

A 10 year old girl who participated in the V70P5 study in Finland comes to the clinic for a follow up. She is a healthy child with no medical history. She had received the V70P5 vaccine 2 years ago and didn't experience any adverse reactions. Now, she is being invited to participate in a new study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccines when given as a booster dose. Her parents are interested in the study and want to know more about the benefits and risks of revaccination. The study aims to assess whether revaccination with adjuvanted or unadjuvanted seasonal influenza vaccine is safe and effective in boosting immunity against influenza viruses in children. The girl is excited to participate in a new study and help advance medical research.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe headaches that are unresponsive to over-the-counter pain relievers. She has also noticed visual disturbances, including double vision and blurring of vision. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. She has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. She has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. She is now being evaluated for possible giant cell arteritis and is a potential candidate for the clinical trial.

This is a 45-year-old female with a history of HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer. She has received at least 2 prior lines of anti-HER2-targeted therapies, including Trastuzumab-containing regimens. The patient has documented radiological disease progression during the most recent treatment regimen for metastatic disease. She has a measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1. HER2 overexpression and gene amplification in the invasive component of the primary tumor or metastatic disease site have been confirmed, according to the criteria for HER2 positivity. The patient's hormone receptor status and breast molecular subtype have been determined by Prediction Analysis of Microarray 50 (PAM50) on the pre-treatment biopsy of metastatic lesion obtained during screening. She has progressed on at least 2 lines of anti-HER2-targeted therapies for metastatic breast cancer. The most recent treatment regimen for metastatic disease included Trastuzumab and chemotherapy. The patient has not received Trastuzumab in combination with pertuzumab as the last treatment for MBC. She has agreed to provide 2 tumor biopsies and has not received any investigational drug within 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, preceding the first dose of study treatment. The patient has a baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of >=50%, based on Echocardiogram (ECHO) or Multigated acquisition (MUGA) and above the testing institution's lower limit of normal. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0 or 1. She is able to swallow and retain orally administered medication and does not have any clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may alter absorption. She has adequate baseline organ function, including hematologic, hepatic, and renal function.

The patient is a 64-year-old male with a history of stage III non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has undergone multiple treatments including chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but due to the unresponsiveness of these treatments, he is now eligible for a new clinical trial. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has not undergone surgery for his lung cancer. The patient has no history of other malignancies apart from non-small cell lung cancer in the last three years. The patient has no known hypersensitivity reaction to nivolumab and has not undergone any organ transplantation or stem-cell transplantation. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty with urination for the past few months. He often feels the need to urinate frequently, especially at night. His urine stream is weak, and he has noticed that his bladder does not empty completely. He has also experienced some pain or discomfort during urination. He visited his primary care physician, who referred him to a urologist. The urologist performed an ultrasound and confirmed that the patient has benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to help further the understanding of BPH diagnosis. He is in stable condition and has provided informed consent.

A 32-year-old French-speaking male with a history of schizophrenia, currently stabilized according to his treating psychiatrist, presents with symptoms of social withdrawal, difficulty in understanding facial expressions, and reduced emotional expression. He has no history of head injury, substance abuse, or neurological disorders. He is right-handed and has a good command of the French language. He is currently taking an antipsychotic medication as prescribed. His family history is negative for any psychiatric disorders. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand the cognitive and affective processes behind his empathic disorder and to contribute to the development of objective markers for improved management.

56-year-old female with a history of breast cysts who recently had a mammogram showing a suspicious area that requires further evaluation. She has no prior history of breast cancer or breast biopsy. She has no family history of breast cancer. The patient is generally in good health and has no significant medical history or allergies. She is willing to undergo further diagnostic testing to ensure the accuracy of her breast cancer screening. The patient is able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to participate in a 6-month follow-up mammogram after the biopsy.

A 28-year-old healthy male participant is needed for a clinical trial investigating the bioequivalence of Mylan quinapril hydrochloride 40 mg tablets compared to Parke-Davis Accupril® 40 mg tablets. He has a normal BMI, and no history of chronic diseases, drug or alcohol abuse, or allergies to quinapril or related products. He must not have used any medication, vitamins, or herbal products within the last 14 days prior to the initial dose of study medication, and should not have ingested any alcoholic, caffeine- or xanthine-containing food or beverage within the 48 hours prior to the initial dose of study medication. He should not have any recent, significant change in dietary or exercise habits. A pre-study medical evaluation (physical examination, laboratory evaluation, 12-lead ECG, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests, HIV test, and urine drug screen including amphetamine, barbiturates, benzodiazepine, cannabinoid, cocaine, opiate screen, phencyclidine, and methadone) will be performed within 14 days of the initial dose of study medication to ensure that he is healthy and normal. He should weigh at least 60 kg (132 lbs) and be within 15% of Ideal Body Weight (IBW), as referenced by the Table of "Desirable Weights of Adults" Metropolitan Life Insurance Company, 1999. He should not have any difficulty swallowing or any gastrointestinal disease that could affect drug absorption. He will be required to practice abstinence or use an acceptable form of contraception throughout the duration of the study if he is a woman of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 70-year-old Chinese woman who has been experiencing occasional forgetfulness and difficulty in remembering names and faces. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or medication use. She is able to understand verbal and written Chinese instructions and is willing to provide informed consent for the study. She has no history of substance abuse and has never been diagnosed with a major NCD.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage II colorectal cancer during a routine colonoscopy. He has a history of smoking, but quit several years ago. He is overweight and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies and takes medication for high blood pressure. He is fluent in English and lives with his wife. His preoperative evaluation has revealed that he is a suitable candidate for elective resection of the lesion. He has no other significant medical, physical or mental conditions besides his cancer. He has a BMI of 32 and his labs show no evidence of anemia, sepsis or organ failure.

45 year-old man recently diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer with a history of smoking (20 pack-years). He presents with shortness of breath and cough, and a CT scan showed a 2.5 cm mass in the right lower lobe. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. PET scan showed metastases to the liver, adrenal gland, and bone. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an anticipated life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He has received no more than one prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, which was chemotherapy. He has measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 that has not been treated with local therapy within 6 months of study treatment. At least one site of disease is accessible to provide repeat biopsies for tumor tissue for sequence and immunological analysis. He has screening laboratory values that meet the inclusion criteria and does not have an untreated central nervous system metastasis. He has not received radiation therapy within 4 weeks prior to Week 0, Day 1 of study treatment. He does not have an active or history of autoimmune disease, HIV infection, or active chronic hepatitis B or C. He is not pregnant or nursing.

A 12-year-old Hispanic girl was referred to the clinic by her school counselor due to her extreme fear of flying. She has never been on an airplane but experiences significant anxiety and panic attacks at the mere thought of flying. She also avoids any situations that may lead to flying such as family vacations or trips. Her parents report that she has always been anxious and shy since she was a toddler, but her fear of flying has worsened in the past year. She has difficulty sleeping and concentrating due to her anxiety. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She speaks fluent English and is in the 7th grade.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who is concerned about her gum health. She has a history of periodontitis and has not undergone any periodontal therapy in the last 12 months. She has at least 6 teeth per quadrant with a pocket depth ranging from 4-6 mm. She does not have any involvement of the furcation and does not have any systemic conditions that may affect the study treatment. She is not pregnant and does not use any antibiotics, anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive drugs. She does not use any mouthwash with antimicrobials and is not on any hormonal contraceptives. She does not have a history of hard-drinking or smoking. Her tooth mobility is within normal limits (class I). She is generally in good health and is willing to participate in the study after being informed of the possible risks involved.

35F survivor of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) during childhood, with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and occasional headaches, is being recruited for a clinical trial. The patient is currently not taking any medications and is not pregnant. She has a sedentary lifestyle and is not currently exercising at moderate or vigorous intensity for more than 30 minutes three times or more per week. The patient has been identified from the University Hospital of the West Indies (UHWI) records and traced using last known addresses by experienced field workers. The patient resides in the same community as the community control participant who will be matched for sex and age within 5 years. The patient will be assessed for anthropometry, cardio metabolic profiles, cognitive and emotional domains at baseline, and post a six-month intervention of supervised aerobic exercise and omega-3 supplementation. The patient will undergo a full oral glucose tolerance test with samples for glucose and insulin at 30 minutes, 60 minutes, 90 minutes, and 120 minutes after 75 grams glucose orally. The patient will also undergo cognitive testing using the NIH Toolbox Cognitive battery to assess executive function, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, attention, episodic memory, working memory, and processing speed. Blood samples will be taken to assess plasma levels of insulin and glucose, lipids, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, insulin-like growth factor, and omega-3 fatty acid profile in erythrocytes. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl who presents with a history of toothache in the lower left jaw. The child is in good general health with no known systemic diseases or physical or mental disabilities. The parents have provided written informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. The dentist performs a clinical examination and diagnoses the tooth as having reversible pulpitis. The tooth is cariously exposed and vital. The tooth is restorable, and hemostasis is achieved after complete pulpotomy. The child has no history of spontaneous or prolonged pain, swelling, tenderness to percussion or palpation, or pathological mobility. Pre-operative radiographic pathology such as resorption (internal or external), per-radicular or furcation radiolucency is not present. The child is able to attend follow-up visits, and there is no history of a previously accessed tooth.

A 35-year-old woman is seeking an elective complete abdominoplasty (C-ABD) procedure for aesthetic reasons. She has no significant past medical history and is in good health, with no history of significant medical or neuropsychiatric conditions. Her body mass index is within the acceptable range for the study. She is a non-smoker and is not currently taking any capsaicin-containing products or CNS active agents as an analgesic adjunct medication. She has no known history of allergy to chili peppers, capsaicin, acetaminophen, bupivacaine, fentanyl hydromorphone, or oxycodone. She is willing to sign the informed consent form and commit to an acceptable method of birth control during the study. She is not currently taking any opioids greater than 15 mg of oral morphine equivalents per day.

A 55-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of difficulty moving his left arm and hand after experiencing a stroke six months ago. His Fugl Meyer score for upper limb function was 48 out of 66. He has been receiving physical therapy but has not seen significant improvement in his motor skills. His medical history is remarkable for hypertension and dyslipidemia, but his blood pressure and lipid levels are currently well-controlled with medication. He does not have a history of epilepsy or seizures. He is able to carry out motor imagery exercises based on a timed test. He has signed informed consent and is affiliated with the social security system. He does not have any surgical clips or metal implants that would be a contraindication for magnetic stimulation or MRI. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the lung. He presented with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. Imaging studies showed multiple lung nodules and lymph node involvement. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of lung cancer. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of other medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and has no family history of cancer. He works as a software engineer and enjoys spending time with his family. He is interested in exploring all available treatment options, including clinical trials. He is willing to provide his tumor tissue for molecular profiling and has a good understanding of the study requirements. His ECOG performance status is 1.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who was recently diagnosed with gastric cancer liver metastasis. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the primary gastric carcinoma. The patient has no significant past medical history or family history of cancer. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is currently receiving treatment at a hospital in China and is willing to participate in the study. He has provided informed consent and is committed to following the study protocol. The patient is compliant with treatment and is not lost to follow-up. All of his clinical data is available and he meets the eligibility criteria for the trial.

This clinical trial is seeking a renal transplant recipient who has been immunized against Cytomegalovirus. The patient must not have clinical evidence of active viral infection and should not be on treatment that includes induction antilymphocyte antibodies. The ideal candidate will be willing to participate in the trial and have health insurance. This trial aims to assess the risk of CMV infection post-transplantation and analyze the cellular immunity of the patient with the QuantiFERON®-CMV Test. If you meet these criteria and are interested in participating in this study, please contact the trial coordinator for further information.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy who has been experiencing difficulty with attention and focus in school. He is easily distracted and has trouble completing tasks. His parents report that he is constantly in motion and has difficulty sitting still. He has had these symptoms for at least 6 months, and they are causing significant impairment in his academic performance and social interactions. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has not had any prior treatment for ADHD. The patient and his parents are interested in exploring medication options to help manage his symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with branch retinal vein occlusion in his left eye. He has not experienced any macular edema, but has noticed some blurriness and distortion in his vision. He has no other known ocular or systemic diseases. He has never undergone any treatment for his retinal vein occlusion. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential benefits of ultra-wide-field fluorescein angiography in managing his condition. He is willing to provide written consent and comply with all study requirements.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is a pilot study to test the precision and validity of autofluorescent flavoprotein imaging (AFI) for diagnosing small fiber neuropathy (SFN). The study is recruiting healthy volunteers who meet the inclusion criteria and do not have any pre-existing neuropathy or previous allergic reaction to local anaesthetics. The study design involves the delivery of nociceptive electrical stimuli to the third finger of each subject, and application of lidocaine/prilocaine cream and an 8% capsaicin patch to test the reliability and validity of AFI for capsaicin-induced small nerve fiber degeneration. The outcomes of the study will provide a significant step in developing an objective, rapid, and non-invasive diagnostic tool to diagnose patients with SFN, which may also be utilized as a biomarker in studies that assess the efficacy of novel treatments for SFN.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and was found unresponsive at the scene. On arrival of the ground EMS, the patient had a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 3. The patient was intubated with an orotracheal tube by the ground EMS and transported to the nearest hospital. Upon arrival, the patient was transferred to the helicopter EMS for transport to a regional trauma center. During transport, the patient was sedated and mechanically ventilated. The patient was admitted to the ICU upon arrival at the trauma center. The patient's neurological exam revealed a GCS score of 5 with fixed, dilated pupils. The patient was placed on a mechanical ventilator and underwent a CT scan of the head, which revealed a large subdural hematoma with midline shift. The patient was taken to the operating room for an emergent craniotomy and evacuation of the hematoma. The patient remained intubated and mechanically ventilated postoperatively and was transferred back to the ICU. The patient is currently stable on the ventilator, but the medical team has concerns regarding the potential for airway complications and are considering pre-hospital advanced airway management by the helicopter EMS.

A 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer that has spread to his bones. He has been admitted to USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center and Hospital for a bone marrow biopsy to determine the extent of the cancer. He reports experiencing anxiety and fear related to the biopsy and has a history of mild claustrophobia. He is currently taking pain medication for bone pain and reports moderate pain during the procedure. He has no history of epilepsy, dementia, Parkinson’s disease, or other neurological disorders. He is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the trial. He has a BMI of 28 and no other medical conditions that would contraindicate participation.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with Type-2 diabetes mellitus 7 years ago. She has been taking metformin 1000mg twice daily along with a sulfonylurea agent for the last 2 years. Her HbA1c levels have been consistently above 7% despite this treatment regimen. She has now been prescribed dapagliflozin by her treating physician 3 months ago. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She is a homemaker and has no history of any major medical or surgical illnesses. Her current medical history and physical examination were unremarkable. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and her blood pressure is well-controlled at 130/80 mmHg with medication. Her most recent lab results showed the following: Fasting glucose: 150 mg/dL, HbA1c: 7.5%, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR: 85 ml/min/1.73m2, Total cholesterol: 190 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol: 45 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol: 120 mg/dL, Triglycerides: 150 mg/dL. She has no history of pregnancy or lactation.

A 28-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5 and a body weight of 65 kg is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She is in good health with no chronic or acute illnesses and has no known allergies to medications. She is not currently taking any medications and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She is sexually active but using reliable contraception. She does not smoke and consumes alcohol moderately. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate is greater than 80 mL/min/1.73 m2. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is willing and able to give fully informed written consent. She has not had any significant surgeries or abnormal medical history. She has tested negative for hepatitis B & C and HIV. She has no objections from her General Practitioner to participate in the trial.

This is a 55 year-old male with a history of chronic liver disease who has been admitted to the ICU due to complications. The patient is currently receiving enteral nutrition but has developed new onset feed intolerance. The patient has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past and is not receiving enteral nutrition through gastrostomy or jejunostomy. However, the patient has a history of hypothyroidism and is currently receiving treatment for it. The patient is not on any prokinetic medication and is not allergic to them. The patient has no known contraindications for prokinetics. The patient has not been diagnosed with uncontrolled sepsis with DIC, has no requirement for two or more vasopressors, and has no organ failure requiring high inotropic support. The patient does not have a history of traumatic brain injury, raised intracranial pressure, myasthenia gravis, or connective tissue diseases. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to give consent for study enrollment. The patient is within the age range of 18-70 years.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who was diagnosed with low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma 2 years ago. She underwent debulking surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy consisting of carboplatin and paclitaxel. She had no evidence of disease recurrence during the first year of follow-up but subsequently developed invasive recurrence. She has a paraffin-embedded tumor specimen available for central analysis and evaluation for mutations. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other cancers or major surgeries.

A 6-year-old boy is brought in by his parents for an eye examination. He has a history of strabismus and his parents have noticed that he frequently closes one eye while watching TV or playing video games. The boy has no other medical conditions and is up to date on all vaccinations. During the examination, the boy's visual acuity is found to be 20/40 in his right eye and 20/20 in his left eye. The boy is diagnosed with amblyopia in his right eye and is eligible for this clinical trial. He is randomly assigned to the case group and will receive Interactive Binocular Treatment (IBiTTM) without patching for one month. He is excited to play I-BiT™ games and is looking forward to improving his vision.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been incarcerated for two years. She has a history of trauma and is experiencing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), including flashbacks, nightmares, and hyperarousal. She has a history of substance abuse and has been in and out of the criminal justice system for several years. She is currently taking medication for depression and anxiety. Despite receiving some mental health services while in prison, she continues to struggle with her symptoms and is interested in participating in a new treatment program for PTSD. She is able to read at a 6th-grade level and has an IQ of 85. She has no scheduled transfer or release in the next 12 weeks, which is the duration of the intervention. She is interested in learning more about cognitive processing therapy (CPT) and is willing to commit to attending the 12-week group sessions. She is aware that she will be randomized to either the CPT group or the waitlist control group, but is eager to participate in the study and hopeful that it will help her manage her PTSD symptoms.

A 53 year old woman with a history of iron deficiency anemia, with hemoglobin less than 12 g/dL and ferritin less than 45 g/dL, and a positive fecal occult blood test within the past 6 months. She has no history of colon cancer or adenoma herself but has two first-degree relatives diagnosed with colon cancer at ages 55 and 58. She has no active gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and her weight is less than 300 pounds. She is willing and able to undergo endoscopic or radiologic procedures, and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials involving drugs, medical devices, and/or biologics. She is not pregnant and uses effective contraception.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has a history of heavy smoking for over 20 years. He has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer after presenting with cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His ECOG/Zubrod status is 1. A CT scan of the chest and upper abdomen, including the adrenal glands, has revealed a mass in his right lung and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum. A bronchoscopy and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NSCLC. The biopsy also showed that the tumor is adenocarcinoma. The patient is considered to have Stage IIIa disease according to the 1998 staging system of the American Joint Commission on Cancer for lung cancer. The patient is expected to undergo a thoracotomy with the intention of a curative resection for primary NSCLC. He is a candidate for complete resection of the carcinoma via lobectomy with or without sleeve resection. The patient has never received chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this cancer. The patient is medically fit for surgery and is available for follow-up. He has not had a thoracotomy or thoracoscopy in the past 5 years, and he does not have evidence of pleural effusion. His treating physician deems him to be at low risk for recurrence from prior malignancies.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM2) diagnosed 6 years ago. She has been regularly attending the primary care unit for the past 6 months and her A1c level is greater than 7%. She is not currently taking any medications for her DM2. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not use alcohol or illicit drugs. She has no history of active infection, chronic corticosteroid use, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, advanced renal disease, heart failure, cirrhosis, dementia, current pregnancy or lactation, current cancer, or any disease that might affect survival in the next 5 years. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about structured diabetes self-management education and how it can help her better manage her disease.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating and alternating diarrhea and constipation for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) based on Rome III criteria. She has no history of major abdominal surgery or other organic gastrointestinal diseases. She has not taken any antibiotics, probiotics or laxatives within the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no severe systemic disease or endometriosis. She has agreed to undergo colonoscopy examination as part of the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy scheduled to undergo outpatient surgery for the removal of tonsils and adenoids due to obstructive sleep apnea. He has a history of recurrent tonsillitis and snoring at night. He is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. He is not taking any medications, and there are no known allergies. His parents are concerned about his surgery and want to ensure that they understand the pain management plan. They have access to a computer and the internet and are willing to use the website provided by the paediatric anaesthesia unit of the Rouen University Hospital to improve their understanding of the pain medication prescribed for their child.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with mitral valve disease. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it. He also reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue. His BMI is 28, BP: 140/90, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for normal electrolyte levels and liver and kidney function. Echocardiography shows tricuspid annular dilatation of more than 40mm. Tricuspid regurgitation is less than 2+. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study and is available for all required follow-up visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit after presenting with severe symptoms of COVID-19 pneumonia, including respiratory distress and a respiratory rate of 35 rpm. He tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 through molecular testing. His oxygen saturation at rest was 88%. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient's family has a history of heart disease, but he has never had any heart-related issues. The patient is alert and oriented, and he has given his consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme six months ago. He underwent surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy, but his cancer has recurred. He has experienced three progressions since his initial treatment. His Karnofsky performance score is 70%. He has no history of hypertension, thromboembolic events, or hemorrhages. He has normal kidney and liver function. He is not taking any medication that may interfere with the study results. He has not received any c-Met, HGF, VEGF, VEGFR, thalidomide, tamoxifen, immunotherapeutic agents, vaccines, or monoclonal antibody therapy. He has not been treated with alkylating agents or chemotherapy within the past four weeks. He has not received any corticosteroids within the past week. He has undergone a stable dose of corticosteroids for one week. He has no active CNS hemorrhage. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to take contraceptive measures during the study. He has signed the informed consent approved by the Institutional Review Board.

A 58-year-old African American woman was diagnosed with Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma six months ago. She has received standard therapy, but unfortunately, the disease has relapsed. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new drug called CCS1477. She has adequate organ function, and there is no evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases. She has not received any chemotherapy, investigational agents or other anti-cancer drugs within the last 14 days or 5 half-lives of the first dose. There is no history of major surgical procedures or significant traumatic injury within the last four weeks. She is not taking any strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 substrates with a narrow therapeutic range. However, she is taking a statin, which she will discontinue prior to starting study treatment. Her unresolved reversible toxicities from prior therapy are CTCAE grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, and there is no evidence of QTcF prolongation (> 480 msec).

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male subjects between the ages of 18 and 45 years with a BMI between 18 and 30 kg/m2 and weighing at least 50 kg. The subjects should also have suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture and be able to inhale from dry powder inhaler devices and pressurized metered-dose inhaler devices according to given instructions. Exclusion criteria include a history of any clinically significant disease, GI, hepatic or renal disease or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. Subjects with any clinically significant abnormalities in clinical chemistry, hematology, or urinalysis results or vital signs after a 5-minute rest are also excluded. Additionally, subjects with any clinically significant abnormalities on 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) or prolonged QTcF (>450 msec) are excluded. Subjects with a history of drug or alcohol abuse, or smokers or those who have used nicotine products within the previous 3 months are also excluded. Finally, subjects who have participated in a clinical study investigating clinical evaluation methods 1 month prior to the administration of investigational product and those with positive results on screening for serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody are also excluded.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who underwent uncomplicated cataract surgery with phacoemulsification and in-the-bag IOL implantation three years ago. He presented with blurred vision, floaters and decreased visual acuity in the right eye. Nd:YAG laser was performed to treat posterior capsular opacification. Six months later, he developed an epiretinal membrane (ERM) in the right eye, which caused distortion and decreased vision. The patient underwent pars plana vitrectomy without gas tamponade. The preoperative refraction of the right eye was -1.00 D spherical and -1.50 D cylindrical. The patient's ocular examination showed a BCVA of 20/50 in the right eye. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as he is a pseudophakic patient who underwent pars plana vitrectomy for ERM without gas tamponade.

A 52-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) with high-risk features. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He has been receiving chemotherapy for the past 6 months and has received more than 10 red blood cell transfusions. His ferritin level is greater than 500 ng/ml. He is planned to undergo allogeneic stem cell transplantation after reduced intensity conditioning from an unrelated donor. The patient is willing to participate in the ALLIVE observational trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has no known contraindications for MRI imaging.

A 45-year-old female with a history of asthma presented with persistent cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath despite taking her current medication regimen of inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting beta-agonists. She reports her symptoms interfere with her daily activities, including work and exercise. She has no allergies to medications and has not experienced any recent asthma exacerbations requiring hospitalization or oral/parenteral corticosteroids. She has a positive response to the reversibility test. She is a non-smoker and does not have any other significant medical conditions. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination reveals diffuse wheezing throughout the chest. Her FEV1 is 60% of predicted normal post-bronchodilator. She is currently taking beclometasone dipropionate 1000 µg and formoterol 24 µg daily. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of beclometasone/formoterol single inhaler for her moderate to severe persistent asthma.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who works as a laborer in a factory. He has a high school education but did not pursue further studies. He is a current smoker and has been smoking for the past 10 years. He smokes approximately 10-15 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to reduce his nicotine dependence. He speaks fluent English and is able to read and write in English. He is not currently taking any medications or using any other nicotine products. He has no significant medical history and is not currently pregnant or nursing.

58F with ESRD undergoing hemodialysis via left upper arm arteriovenous fistula, presents with decreased blood flow during dialysis. She reports occasional mild discomfort at the site of the fistula, but denies any other symptoms such as fever, chills, or redness. Physical examination reveals a bruit over the fistula and a thrill on palpation. Doppler ultrasound reveals a significant stenotic lesion in the mid-segment of the fistula. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been compliant with her medications and has never missed a dialysis session. She has no known allergies to contrast media, ASA, clopidogrel, or paclitaxel. She has not undergone any prior surgical or vascular interventions within the past 2 weeks and has no plans for any such interventions in the next 30 days. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has noticed a lump in her right breast during a self-examination. She has no personal or family history of breast cancer, but she has breast implants and is currently taking hormone replacement therapy for menopausal symptoms. The lump was also detected during a mammogram and ultrasound, and a biopsy is recommended to determine whether it is cancerous. The patient is concerned about the accuracy of the biopsy and is open to alternative imaging methods. She is willing to participate in the photoacoustic imaging clinical trial after understanding the procedure and signing the informed consent document. She is in good health, with no other medical conditions that would affect her participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with high grade serous ovarian cancer (HGS-EOC) two years ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy and is currently in remission. She has a history of irregular Pap smear results, but has never been diagnosed with cervical cancer. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve early detection methods for ovarian cancer. She is married and has two children. She works as a nurse and leads an active lifestyle. She has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her medical history includes hypothyroidism, for which she takes levothyroxine. She is fluent in Italian and has access to the internet for communication with the study team. She is willing to provide her medical records and undergo any necessary tests for the study.

45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with breast cancer for the first time. She has no history of metastasis and has given written informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no clinical diagnosis of neurological or cognitive impairment. She does not have type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is willing to participate in the study and adhere to the dietary guidelines provided.

Unfortunately, as this study is focused on existing cohorts (ARIC and CHS), it is not possible to generate a patient description for this particular clinical trial. Participants must already be enrolled in these cohorts in order to be eligible for inclusion in the study.

60-year-old male with end-stage liver disease due to hepatitis C virus infection is scheduled to undergo liver transplantation. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease stage 3. The patient is currently not receiving any antibiotics and has not had any recent infections. The patient has been informed of the study and is willing to participate.

A 55-year-old male with a history of Parkinson's disease presents to the Movement Clinic of Shohada-e-Tajrish Hospital with complaints of tremors and difficulty walking. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease three years ago and has been on levodopa/carbidopa therapy since then. He reports experiencing "off" periods, during which his symptoms worsen, despite taking his medications on time. He denies any history of other neurological diseases or diabetes. He has never used insulin before. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his physical exam is significant for resting tremors and bradykinesia. His gait is slow and shuffling, and he has difficulty with balance. He is able to walk independently but experiences difficulty with turning and stopping. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his symptoms.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male with a history of GERD for the past 10 years presents with difficulty swallowing and heartburn. He has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) for the past 6 months with some relief of symptoms, but he still has difficulty swallowing. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has a family history of colon cancer, but no other significant medical or surgical history. He has had an upper endoscopy before, which showed Barrett's esophagus. Biopsies taken at that time showed low-grade dysplasia. He has been advised to undergo another endoscopy with biopsy to evaluate for any progression of the dysplasia. His BMI is 29. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of ESD versus EMR for treatment of early Barrett's adenocarcinoma.

40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with premature ovarian failure and is planning to undergo IVF with donor eggs. She has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. She has not participated in any other clinical trials with medication and is willing to adjust to the study protocol. She has signed the informed consent form and is eager to participate in this study to increase her chances of a successful pregnancy.

A 16-year-old female presents to the University of Michigan Psychiatric Emergency Services with suicidal ideation. She reports feeling overwhelmed and helpless due to ongoing bullying at school. The patient has no prior history of mental health problems and denies any substance use. The patient's parents are present during the visit and report feeling concerned and unsure of how to best support their daughter. The patient speaks English fluently and is accompanied by her parents/legal guardians. They have provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 58-year-old male with a history of atrial flutter and on Class III antiarrhythmic drug therapy presents with recurrent episodes of palpitations and dizziness. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia. The patient is in good physical health and agrees to comply with follow-up visits and evaluation. The patient has not undergone any prior atrial flutter ablation treatment and has not had a recent myocardial infarction within the past 3 months. The patient does not have any significant coronary heart disease or heart failure and has no evidence of intracardiac thrombus or a history of clotting disorders. The patient is not allergic to heparin and has not participated in another investigational study.

25 year-old African American male who is a regular co-user of alcohol and smoked marijuana. He is physically active and enjoys strength training but has not participated in a biceps-specific conditioning program in the past 6 months. He does not report any wrist/hand, elbow, or shoulder pain in the past 3 months. He denies any chronic medical conditions or major psychiatric disorders. He does not have a medical marijuana prescription and only consumes marijuana using inhalational methods. He reports no symptoms of moderate depression and is not a woman who is pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. He owns a smartphone with a cellular/data plan and is able to give informed consent.

A 45-year-old female patient presents with symptoms of deep venous obstructive disease, including swelling, pain, and discomfort in the lower extremities. She has a history of May-Thurner syndrome and has previously undergone treatment for deep vein thrombosis. Imaging (duplex ultrasonography, magnetic resonance venography, CT-venography) has confirmed venous obstruction in the common femoral vein. The patient is willing to undergo percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) and stenting with or without endophlebectomy (surgical desobstruction) of the common femoral vein and/or arteriovenous fistula creation. The patient has no known intolerance to anticoagulant medication and has a life expectancy of more than 1 year. The patient's data will be entered into a prospective digital database for ongoing registration of deep venous reconstructions.

Patient is a 75-year-old retired teacher who lives alone in a single-story house. She fell once last year while reaching for something on a high shelf, and since then, she has become more cautious with her movements. She has a smartphone and regularly uses it to stay in touch with her family and friends. She is comfortable with technology and uses her tablet to read books and watch TV shows. She reports feeling a little unsteady on her feet, especially when walking on uneven surfaces or climbing stairs. However, she can rise from a standard height chair without assistance and move around her house without a walking aid. She does not participate in any strenuous physical exercise but tries to take daily walks around her neighborhood. She is excited to learn more about the Safe Step application and how it can help her improve her balance and strength, so she can continue to live independently without fear of falling.

32-year-old Icelandic woman with a history of sexual assault, who has been experiencing intrusive memories of the event at least three times per week for the past four weeks. She is able to attend 3-8 remote sessions with a researcher and has access to a smartphone. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to monitor her intrusive memories in her daily life. She is fluent in Icelandic and able to read the study materials in Icelandic. She does not have a current psychotic disorder, manic episode, or acute suicidality.

The patient is a 55-year-old Hispanic man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 10 years. He has a history of poor glycemic control with an A1C level of 9.5%, despite taking metformin and glipizide. He is also struggling with hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient primarily speaks Spanish and has limited access to diabetes education in his community. He has been receiving primary care at the Grady North DeKalb Health center and has a valid Grady card. The patient is interested in participating in a group visit setting to learn more about managing his diabetes and to receive support from other patients with the same condition.

The patient is a 68 year old male Veteran who has been physically active throughout his life. He enjoys cycling and walking as part of his daily routine. He has never been diagnosed with any cardiac, pulmonary or metabolic diseases. He takes medications for hypertension and high cholesterol, which have been well-controlled with medication. He is retired and lives with his spouse. He has no history of fractures or bone diseases. He is interested in participating in research that will help improve his health and wellbeing.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has undergone surgical castration for prostate cancer and has been experiencing hot flashes for more than 30 days. The patient is on stable prostate cancer therapy for at least 45 days prior to entering the study. He complains of moderate to severe hot flashes which affect his daily activities and quality of life. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medication. The patient is willing to maintain a daily paper diary to record the frequency and severity of hot flashes during the treatment period. The patient is alert and cooperative and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study drug. The patient is interested in participating in the study to alleviate his hot flashes and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been recently diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer that has spread to her lymph nodes. Her biopsy results show that her tumor is estrogen and/or progesterone receptor positive. She has not received any prior systemic treatment for recurrent or metastatic breast cancer. She has undergone a bilateral oophorectomy and has been amenorrheic for over 3 months. Her ECOG performance status is 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light physical activities, such as light housework or office work. She has no serious hypersensitivity to letrozole or other components of the study drug. She has no other prior or concurrent malignancy except for a basal cell carcinoma that was treated a year ago. She is willing to undergo chemotherapy and hormone therapy as first-line treatment for her breast cancer.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 25. He has no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatologic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, immunologic, dermal, neurologic, or psychological disease. He does not take any prescription medication and has not used any over-the-counter medication or oriental medication in the past 7 days. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. His blood pressure is within normal range (SBP 120 mmHg, DBP 80 mmHg) and his laboratory test results are within normal limits. He has no known hypersensitivity reaction to S-amlodipine, amlodipine, valsartan, or dihydropyridine derivatives. He has not donated blood or received blood transfusion in the past 60 days. He has not participated in any clinical investigation in the past 60 days. He has not consumed grapefruit juice or taken any inducer or inhibitor of drug metabolism enzyme such as barbital in the past 28 days. His serum potassium concentration is within normal range (4.0 mEq/L). Based on these criteria, he is eligible to participate in the clinical trial to assess the pharmacokinetic characteristics of Lodivixx Tab. 5/160mg in healthy male subjects.

A 52-year-old woman has been diagnosed with primary endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium. The cancer has been determined to be at stage I, and the patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has been presented with the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial comparing Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy (TLH) and Total Abdominal Hysterectomy (TAH) for the treatment of her cancer. The patient is physically fit and has no serious concomitant systemic disorders, and is willing to undergo surgery as part of the study. She has a good understanding of the study's objectives and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, diagnosed 5 years ago. He was prescribed with amlodipine and atorvastatin, and his blood pressure and lipid levels have been well controlled. He presents to the clinic with chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. He is diagnosed with coronary artery disease and needs coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). He has been taking acetylsalicylic acid for the past 2 years as a preventive measure for his cardiovascular disease. His past medical history is not significant for any other medical issues. His family history is negative for any cardiovascular disease. His lab study is as below: FBS: 95 mg/dl HbA1c: 5.7% Cholesterol: 160 mg/dl TG: 90 mg/dl LDL: 90 mg/dl HDL: 50 mg/dl.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The diagnosis was confirmed by biopsy, and the cancer has progressed to stage IIIB. The patient has no history of cancer or chemotherapy. The patient has a history of smoking and currently smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. The patient is in good general health with no significant comorbidities. The patient is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has consented to receive mapatumumab in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel as first line therapy.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Unfortunately, her cancer has progressed and she has been treated with anthracyclines, taxanes, and capecitabine, as well as trastuzumab due to her Her-2 positive disease. Her oncologist has documented experience in a prior eribulin clinical trial. She has an ECOG performance status of 2 and adequate kidney, bone marrow, and liver function. She is willing and able to comply with all aspects of the treatment protocol and has provided written informed consent. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a highly effective method of contraception. She has no history of congestive heart failure or serious cardiac arrhythmia, but has experienced grade 2 neuropathy from previous treatments. She has not received any investigational drugs within the past 4 weeks or any chemotherapy, radiation, biological or targeted therapy within the past 2 weeks. She is interested in participating in this expanded access program with eribulin for the treatment of her advanced breast cancer.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital after experiencing chest pain for the past 3 hours. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication for both conditions. The patient has never smoked and does not have a family history of heart disease. He was diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction, and the medical team recommended intervention with Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold. The patient agreed to participate in the IRIS-BVS AMI Registry and signed the written informed consent form. His medical history and current condition meet the inclusion criteria for the study, and he does not have any of the exclusion criteria. The patient is willing to take dual antiplatelet therapy for one year and has a life expectancy of more than one year.

This is a 7-year-old male with a medical history of sickle cell anemia. He was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at birth and has been followed up at the Pediatric Hematology Unit since then. He has been hospitalized several times for vaso-occlusive crises and has received blood transfusions in the past. He has a history of enlarged spleen and has been monitored for acute splenic sequestration. He has not undergone splenectomy yet. He is currently on hydroxyurea therapy and penicillin prophylaxis. His most recent laboratory results showed a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, reticulocyte count of 8%, and platelet count of 300,000/mm3. He has no history of thrombotic events.

A 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer after experiencing several weeks of shortness of breath, coughing, and fatigue. He underwent first-line platinum/etoposide treatment which resulted in disease control. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has measurable disease according to RECIST Version 1.1 criteria. His bone marrow, liver, and renal function are adequate. A Formalin Fixed Paraffin Embedded (FFPE) or frozen tumor tissue material is available for testing. He has not had previous therapies with Tivantinib or other known c-MET inhibitor. He has not had radiotherapy for target lesions or major surgical procedure within 4 weeks prior to the inclusion in the study. He has no history of malignancy within the past five years, excluding basal cell of the cervix or prostate cancer with a value of prostate-specific antigen <0.2 ng/mL. He has no history of cardiac disease or known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use adequate contraception if of childbearing/reproductive potential. He has no gastrointestinal disorders that may interfere with the absorption of Tivantinib and is able to swallow the complete doses of Tivantinib. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the treatment and follow-up.

A 27-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer in a local IT firm is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of PF-06751979 on the pharmacokinetics of midazolam in healthy adults. He has no significant medical history and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or illicit drugs. His weight is 75 kg and his body mass index is 24.5 kg/m2. He is willing to comply with the study requirements, including taking multiple doses of PF-06751979 and undergoing blood draws and other assessments throughout the study period. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

65 F with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with complaints of shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. She had no prior history of heart disease or heart failure. Upon evaluation, she was found to have clinical features consistent with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Her LVEF was measured to be 55%, and she had no evidence of significant valvular disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or pericardial constriction. Her peak VO2 was less than 80% predicted, with metabolic exercise testing indicating a cardiac cause for limitation. Formal lung function testing showed no evidence of lung disease. Contrast-enhanced myocardial stress testing did not reveal reversible myocardial ischemia. Echocardiography did not show exercise-induced mitral regurgitation. She had a BMI of 28 and no locomotor cause for exercise limitation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with uveitis affecting the posterior segment of her left eye. She has a history of sarcoidosis, for which she has been receiving treatment for the past 2 years. Despite treatment, her visual acuity has declined in the affected eye and she experiences persistent inflammation. Conventional diagnostic methods have been unable to determine the cause of her uveitis. She is being considered for a diagnostic pars plana vitrectomy to obtain a vitreous sample for further testing and to potentially establish a diagnosis. She has no significant medical history other than sarcoidosis and takes no other medications. On examination, the affected left eye has a visual acuity of 20/200 and exhibits diffuse vitreous opacities, retinal vasculitis, and posterior synechiae. The right eye is unaffected. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other complaints or symptoms.

A 6-year-old female child is scheduled to undergo elective ambulatory urologic surgery under general anesthesia combined with regional block. She has no significant medical history and has been classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I. The child's weight is 22 kg and her height is 120 cm. She has never undergone any surgery before and has no known history of adverse reactions to anesthetic agents. She has not received any premedication and will undergo a mask induction with either incremental sevoflurane 2-8% or single breath sevoflurane 8% in a 70 % nitrous oxide and 30% oxygen mixture with a 10 L/min fresh gas flow. The child will receive either sevoflurane or desflurane by adjusting end-tidal concentration to deliver a minimum alveolar anesthetic concentration (MAC) of 1. The nitrous oxide in oxygen concentration will be reduced to 66% and total gas flow rate will be reduced to 5 LMP. During the surgery, intraoperative analgesics or other sedative drugs will not be given unless the child's heart rate increases > 20% of the baseline after incision or during the operation. If required, fentanyl 0.5-1 mcg/kg intravenously will be given to supplement analgesia throughout the operation. After the surgery, the child will be transported to the post-anesthetic care unit (PACU) where emergence agitation score and pain score will be assessed by experienced PACU nurses blinded to the inhaled anesthetic agents. The child will be reunited with her parents in the PACU after an initial admission and stabilization phase. The duration of stay in the PACU will also be recorded.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has metastasized to her liver, bones, and lungs. She has been receiving chemotherapy and radiation for the past six months, and her symptoms have improved slightly, but she still experiences fatigue, pain, and shortness of breath. She has been unable to work since her diagnosis, and her husband's income is not enough to cover all their expenses. She has been struggling to pay for her medical bills, medications, and other basic needs. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers understand and address the financial distress that many cancer patients face. She is able to read, write, and speak English fluently, and has no evidence of severe cognitive impairment. She is willing to complete the questionnaires and sign the informed consent.

This is a 5-year old Dutch-speaking male with a history of cleft palate, without involvement of the lip or nose, who has undergone surgical repair with modified Furlow palatoplasty or modified Furlow according to Sommerlad at the AZ Sint-Jan Brugge-Oostende av. The patient is currently receiving postoperative care and speech therapy by the cleft team of the general hospital Sint-Jan Bruges. The patient has not received any corrective surgical procedure for velopharyngeal dysfunction after the modified Furlow technique alone or in combination with intravelar veloplasty by Sommerlad. The patient does not have any clinically diagnosed hearing difficulties, stutter, cognitive or motoric disabilities. The patient has not received intensive speech therapy prior to their fifth life year. The patient is being followed up routinely by the cleft team at the hospital and will be asked for consent to participate in the study to register their demographic, surgical and speech-related data. The parents of the patient will also be asked to complete a quality of life questionnaire concerning their child, at the time of speech evaluation through self-report or through an interview with the clinical research coordinator.

55 year old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years on metformin therapy. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity with a BMI of 33.5. She reports a stable body weight over the past 3 months. She has no history of congestive heart failure or clinically significant cardiac, liver or kidney disease, and her creatinine level is within normal range. She is not on insulin or sulfonylureas and has not received thiazolidinedione treatment for at least 3 months prior to randomization. She reports no use of systemic glucocorticoids or any other medication known to affect glucose tolerance. She is willing to comply with study requirements and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain for the past year. He has a history of gallstones and has been scheduled for an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) procedure at Dartmouth-Hitchcock. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not currently taking any medications. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing upper-gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea and acid reflux for the past month. He has tried over-the-counter antacids but has not experienced any relief. He has no significant past medical history, is not taking any medications, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for any gastrointestinal diseases. He is interested in participating in the MCE Direct Visualization of Drug Behavior in Upper-gastrointestinal Tract clinical trial to help better understand his condition and potentially find a more effective treatment. Upon further evaluation, he meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to sign the informed consent.

A 48-year-old male patient was diagnosed with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection 5 years ago during routine screening. He has been HBeAg negative since then. He has a history of heavy alcohol use but has been abstinent for the past year. His liver biopsy, performed 6 months ago, showed chronic hepatitis B with moderate activity and mild fibrosis. He was recently diagnosed with hepatitis delta virus (HDV) co-infection based on positive anti-HDV antibodies and HDV-RNA. His liver function tests showed an alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level of 70 U/L, with normal levels of total bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase. He has no history of liver cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, or other liver diseases. He has no history of drug abuse or psychiatric disorders. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and restrictions. He is using a highly effective method of birth control and has agreed not to donate sperm during the study and for 3 months after the last dosing of the investigational medicinal product. He is able to provide the written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 35-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy to remove the tumor and is scheduled to undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy. She has regular menstrual cycles and is premenopausal. She has no prior history of cancer except for a basal cell skin cancer that was removed several years ago. She is otherwise healthy and fit to undergo chemotherapy. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or endocrine therapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help prevent early menopause caused by chemotherapy. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study period if required.

10-year-old child diagnosed with HIV-1 infection since birth, currently receiving stavudine and lamivudine combination therapy for the past year. The child's viral load has been below 400 copies/mL for the past 6 months. The child has a history of mild renal dysfunction and osteoporosis, but is otherwise healthy. The child's parent/guardian is willing to participate in the study and follow the study requirements.

A 55-year-old man was referred to the hematology clinic with complaints of fatigue, night sweats, and mild intermittent fever for the past 6 months. He also reports unintentional weight loss of 5 kg during this period. Physical examination revealed palpable lymph nodes in the cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, and inguinal regions, the largest being 3 cm in diameter. The spleen was palpable 4 cm below the left costal margin. No hepatomegaly or ascites were detected. Laboratory tests revealed a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, leukocyte count of 12,000/μL, neutrophils 60%, lymphocytes 30%, and platelet count of 220,000/μL. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was elevated at 450 U/L (normal range, 135-225 U/L). Flow cytometry analysis of the cervical lymph node biopsy showed follicular lymphoma (grade 2). PET-CT scan revealed enlarged lymph nodes in multiple regions, with the largest in the left inguinal region measuring 4.1 cm. The patient was diagnosed with stage III follicular lymphoma based on the Ann Arbor staging system. He is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. He is married and has 2 children. He works as a teacher, and he is a non-smoker and non-drinker. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0. He has not received any previous cancer treatment. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years and occasional alcohol use. He presents with abdominal pain that radiates to his back, and he has lost 10 pounds over the last month. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medications. He has no known allergies. The physical examination shows jaundice and tenderness in the epigastric region. The laboratory studies reveal elevated bilirubin levels and elevated liver enzymes. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The patient is deemed a candidate for curative-intent pancreatectomy by the surgeon. The patient has not received any prior radiation therapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, investigational therapy, or surgery for pancreatic cancer. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0-1, and the patient has a Total Neuropathy Score less than 2. The patient's absolute neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits, and the total bilirubin and creatinine levels are within the acceptable range. The patient has no known Gilbert's Syndrome or homozygosity for UGAT1A1*28 polymorphism. The patient has no comorbid conditions that would prohibit curative-intent pancreatectomy.

Patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) according to DSM-5™ classification code (296.3x). The patient has a history of recurrent Major Depressive Episodes confirmed by the Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI). The patient has been experiencing depressive symptoms for the past 6 months and has a Montgomery Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score of 35 at both Screening and Baseline Visits. The patient has no other current psychiatric disorders or Axis I disorders as assessed by the MINI. The patient has no history of manic or hypomanic episode, schizophrenia, or any other psychotic disorder, including major depression with psychotic features (DSM-5™ criteria). The patient has no personality disorders, intellectual disability, pervasive development disorder, attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, organic mental disorders, or mental disorders due to a general medical condition (DSM-5™ criteria). The patient has not had a lack of response to previous treatment with vortioxetine.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who went to his doctor for a regular check-up. He has a family history of colon cancer, with his father having been diagnosed at age 60. He has no symptoms of colorectal cancer, such as rectal bleeding, abdominal pain or unexplained weight loss. However, his fecal immunoassay test came back positive, indicating the possibility of the presence of blood in his stool. He has no known chronic inflammatory disease, and has not made any intense physical effort in the past three days. He is willing to undergo a colonoscopy to further investigate the possible cause of his positive test result. The patient is affiliated to a social security scheme and has given his informed, written and express consent to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old man with HIV-1 infection presents with concerns about recent weight gain and a family history of heart disease. The patient's viral load has been undetectable for over a year while on a non-integrase strand transfer inhibitor-based regimen. He has no known history of hypertension, diabetes, or high cholesterol levels. His current medications include tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and efavirenz. The patient is willing and able to understand and sign an informed consent written in the English language. He has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to any of the components of the study but has not received long-term systemic immunosuppressive therapy or prohibited therapies within 60 days prior to screening/day 1 visit. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to donate eggs or sperm or conceive or father a child at any time during the study and 6 weeks following the end of the study. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand the effects of dolutegravir-based regimen on weight gain, metabolic profiles, and cardiovascular disease risk factors in people living with HIV.

A 35-year-old male presents as a healthy volunteer with no significant past medical history. He reports no current or previous use of any substance that may affect the autonomic nervous system, including coffee or medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial focused on hypovolemic shock diagnosis in prehospital settings. He meets the eligibility criteria and has no contraindications for the study. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 47-year-old woman, diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer, presents with a new metastatic lesion in the liver after receiving first-line therapy of anthracyclines and taxanes. She reports experiencing fatigue, anorexia, and occasional nausea. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She has two children, both grown and living independently. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable liver mass in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory analysis is within normal limits except for elevated liver function tests, CA 15-3 and CEA. The CT scan revealed a 4 cm hypodense mass in the right hepatic lobe.
