The biopsy confirmed it to be a metastatic lesion from the breast cancer. She is eager to participate in clinical research and has expressed interest in immunotherapy.

52 year old woman diagnosed with hereditary hemochromatosis presenting with fatigue, nausea, and abdominal pain. She has a history of iron overload due to hereditary hemochromatosis and has been receiving regular phlebotomy to reduce iron levels. Her most recent iron level is 3200 mcg/L and she has a liver biopsy scheduled in the coming weeks to assess the degree of hepatic iron overload. The patient is interested in participating in a non-invasive study to assess her liver iron levels using MRI. She has no contraindications to MRI and is willing to comply with the study requirements. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hereditary hemochromatosis.

A 35-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent episodes of biliary colic. She reports feeling anxious about the upcoming surgery and has a history of anxiety and panic attacks. She has no significant medical history except for mild asthma controlled with an inhaler. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is proficient in French and has no hearing or visual impairments. She has no head or face wounds and no known neurological diseases. She does not suffer from chronic pain or take analgesics regularly. She is not currently taking any medication that affects the autonomic nervous system or causes dizziness. She is interested in exploring non-pharmacological approaches to pain and anxiety management and has consented to participate in the study.

73 year old woman with a diagnosis of dementia according to DSM-IV TR criteria. She has a score of 14 on the MMSE. She lives at home with her husband who is available to assist her at least 2 days per week. She speaks German as her dominant language. She has not received home based occupational therapy for dementia within the last 6 months. She has no relevant behavioral problems as assessed by the neuropsychiatric inventory (NPI) and has no depressive episodes as assessed by the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). She does not have any mental or physical disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the study. She has no history of addictive disorder and is not currently taking any medication that would likely cause an impairment of cognitive performance during the trial. She has never participated in another clinical trial.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been suffering from faecal incontinence for the past 5 years. She describes episodes of uncontrolled bowel movements, which occur several times a day, and has caused her significant embarrassment and distress. She has tried several conservative treatments such as dietary changes, pelvic floor exercises, and medications, but none of them have been effective in controlling her symptoms. She has no known history of neurological or gastrointestinal disorders, and her bowel movements are regular. She is willing to participate in a trial that may help improve her continence and quality of life. She has no known allergies, is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is mentally stable. Her colonoscopy results were normal.

The patient is a 30 year-old Caucasian woman who has been experiencing menstrual migraines for the past year. She experiences migraine attacks 2-3 times per month, starting 2-3 days before the onset of menstruation and lasting for 2-3 days. She describes the pain as severe, throbbing and located on one side of her head. She also experiences nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light and sound during the attacks. She does not have any family history of migraine in her first-degree relatives. She does not smoke or chew gum and has not consumed any food or drink in the last 30 minutes. She has not taken any hormonal medications or supplements in the past 3 months. She has regular menstrual cycles and is able to keep headache diary data for at least three months in advance of the visit to confirm the diagnosis. She understands the procedures required for the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) after presenting with a persistent cough, night sweats, and weight loss. She has no previous history of cancer, chemotherapy, or radiation therapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. Her blood work shows adequate hematological function. She has two or more signs of unfavorable prognosis according to the International Prognostic Index (IPI) score of 2-4. She has agreed to offer informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. She has no history of transformation of mature cell lymphomas to DLBCL, HIV-associated DLBCL, concomitant other cancer, congestive heart failure, unstable angina, severe cardiac arrhythmias and conduction disturbances, myocardial infarction, renal insufficiency, liver failure, acute hepatitis, active phase of chronic hepatitis B or C, severe pneumonia, life-threatening bleeding, severe mental disorders, or decompensated diabetes. She is not pregnant.

12-year-old J has a history of nut allergies and has experienced anaphylactic reactions to walnuts and other tree nuts. J has a positive skin prick test to walnuts and other tree nuts, as well as a specific IgE level of >0.35 kU/L. J has confirmed walnut allergy and a second tree nut allergy with a positive oral food challenge. J's family is interested in exploring oral immunotherapy as a potential treatment option to reduce the risk of anaphylaxis to tree nuts. J is otherwise healthy and does not have any chronic medical conditions requiring therapy. The family has provided written informed consent, and J has provided written assent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35 year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for the past few weeks. She has no history of liver disease, but has a family history of colon cancer. She has a BMI of 28 and is currently taking medication for hypertension. She does not have any known allergies to iodine or contrast media. Her renal function is normal, with a GFR of 75 mL/min/1.73m2. She is able to hold her breath for at least 15 seconds. She has no contraindications for undergoing a CT scan. She is willing to sign an informed consent form for the study.

Patient is a 16-year-old female with a history of moderate acne vulgaris on her face. She has had acne for the past 2 years, and has tried over-the-counter treatments with little success. She presents with at least 20 inflammatory lesions (papules and pustules) and 25 non-inflammatory lesions (open and closed comedones) on her face, and an IGA score of 3. She has no nodulocystic lesions and no excessive facial hair. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of generic Clindamycin 1% gel (Akorn) compared to the marketed product Clindamycin 1% gel (Greenstone LLC) for the treatment of her acne vulgaris.

45-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis undergoing elective aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting at our hospital. The patient has no history of blood transfusion or any known bleeding disorders. Preoperative hemoglobin level is 132 g/L and EuroSCORE-II is calculated to be 14%. The patient has been cleared for surgery and will be enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who complains of sensitivity in her upper right teeth whenever exposed to air. She is concerned about the aesthetics of her smile due to a recession of her gums in her upper right canine area. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she does not smoke or use any medications. She has good oral hygiene habits, and her full-mouth visible plaque index and sulcus bleeding index are both less than 20%. She is not pregnant and has no systemic disorders. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of the Semilunar Coronally Positioned Flap (SCPF) procedure for treating gingival recessions, with or without Enamel Matrix Derivative (EMD). She meets the inclusion criteria of having a buccal Miller class I gingival recession with a height greater than or equal to 2.0 mm and less than 4.0 mm in her upper right canine or premolar area, and a height of keratinized tissue greater than or equal to 2 mm.

A 47-year-old male patient with a history of prostate cancer that has metastasized to the bones and liver. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with no significant improvement. The patient is currently experiencing severe pain in the bones and liver region, along with fatigue and weight loss. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of 12 weeks or more. The patient has not received any other anticancer therapy or participated in any other clinical trial within the last 30 days. The patient does not have a history of hypersensitivity reactions to any of the components of the investigational product or other drugs of the same class. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. Her most recent blood count showed a slightly low red blood cell count and a slightly high white blood cell count. She has no known allergies and is able to provide informed consent. She is willing to participate in the study and has been informed of the procedures involved. She is able to comply with the study requirements and attend all necessary appointments. She has no visible signs of hemolysis or clotting, and her blood sample is successfully scanned on OLO within the first attempt.

A 35 year old male with a longstanding history of excessive daytime sleepiness, sudden loss of muscle tone, and cataplexy episodes was referred to the clinic for evaluation and management. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale score was 18, and his symptoms had been present for over 10 years. After a polysomnography and multiple sleep latency test, he was diagnosed with narcolepsy with cataplexy. He was not taking any medication at the time of evaluation. He has no significant medical or psychiatric history, and no history of head trauma or seizures. He does not have sleep apnea or work in shifts. He is not on a sodium-restricted diet, and he has no metal implants in his body. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of Xyrem® on the brain dopamine system in narcolepsy patients.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who underwent lumpectomy for stage T1 invasive ductal carcinoma in her right breast. The margins of the resected specimen were histologically free of tumor. She has no history of prior breast or thoracic radiation therapy, or any collagen-vascular disease. Her tumor is estrogen receptor positive. She has undergone sentinel node biopsy which was negative for malignancy. She has no evidence of distant metastasis. She is willing and able to sign an informed consent form and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Conture® Multi-Lumen Balloon to deliver accelerated partial breast brachytherapy.

A 57-year-old male visited the clinic for follow-up visit after undergoing a radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer 8 months ago. He has completed adjuvant androgen deprivation therapy and is currently on no medication. His latest PSA level was undetectable. He reported feeling anxious and depressed since the diagnosis of prostate cancer and subsequent treatment. He has no history of neurological or musculoskeletal disorders that may inhibit exercise. He is a non-smoker with a family history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is currently well controlled with medication. He exercises occasionally, but not regularly. His BMI is 28.5 kg/m2 and his waist circumference is 100 cm. He is right-hand dominant and has no history of seizures or epilepsy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to examine the effect of an acute bout of exercise on his well-being.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has had myopia for several years. She has been wearing glasses and contact lenses but is interested in exploring other options for vision correction. She is in good health and has no known allergies or medical conditions. The patient is not pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant in the near future. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ReLEx smile for the correction of myopia. She has read and understood the informed consent document and is willing to undergo the procedure and follow-up visits. The patient has a stable refractive error and has not had any significant changes in her prescription in the past year. She has no history of eye diseases, surgeries, or injuries. She has a good understanding of the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has noticed a decrease in her vision over the past few months and was referred to an ophthalmologist. Upon examination, she was found to have severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with macular edema. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left eye. She has no media opacities and no previous history of laser treatment or ocular surgery. She is able to read and follow instructions and has given consent to participate in the trial. She is not being treated for glaucoma or any other diseases of the retina or optic nerve. The quality of her retinography, angiography, and OCT images is sufficient for inclusion in the trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced renal cell carcinoma two years ago. She has undergone a right nephrectomy and has received several rounds of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, but her cancer has progressed and is currently metastatic. She experiences fatigue, weight loss, and occasional shortness of breath. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and is able to perform most of her daily activities independently. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her laboratory values are within normal range except for mildly elevated liver enzymes. Imaging studies show multiple lung and bone metastases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to have a central venous line placed.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who is morbidly obese with a BMI of 42 kg/m2. She has a history of restrictive lung disease with a Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) of 80% of predicted values. She has been scheduled for laparoscopic bariatric surgery, which is expected to last for not more than 3 hours. She has not had any previous abdominal surgery. She is an otherwise healthy individual with no history of heart or kidney disease. She is not taking any antiarrhythmic drugs, beta or calcium channel blockers. She does not have any known allergies to study drugs. She has agreed to participate in the study and her American society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status is II.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of primary biliary cholangitis and metastatic breast cancer. She is scheduled to begin chemotherapy for palliative purposes. The patient's platelet count at the time of screening is 70,000/mcL. Her liver function tests show mild elevations in AST and ALT, and she has a diagnosis of cirrhosis. She has not received any cytotoxic therapy in the past 12 months. Her ECOG performance status is 1. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception during the study period. She has no history of immune causes of thrombocytopenia and does not have leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome. She does not have bone metastases or a known bleeding disorder or platelet dysfunction. The patient is not on anticoagulation or NSAIDs within 7 days of enrollment, except for celecoxib. She has no concurrent lymphoma and no pre-existing portal vein thrombus, mesenteric thrombus, or splenic thrombus that is not in the context of tumor invasion. The patient is not receiving any of the drugs that may interact with Avatrombopag.

This is a 65 year-old female with a history of hypertension and diabetes who presents to the emergency department with fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Upon examination, she is found to have tachycardia, tachypnea, and bibasilar crackles. Her initial laboratory results show elevated white blood cell count and lactate levels, and she meets the criteria for severe sepsis. The treating physician plans to give at least 1-liter of crystalloid after initial ultrasound is performed. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

56-year-old first-generation Korean American female living in the Washington-Baltimore area. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has an HbA1c level of 9% within the last 6 months. She speaks limited English and is struggling to manage her diabetes due to language and cultural barriers. She reports feeling isolated and lacking confidence in her ability to manage her diabetes. She currently takes metformin and has hypertension. She is willing to participate in all aspects of the study and agrees to use home glucose monitoring with a telephone transmission system and to receive diabetes self-help education. She has no physical or mental health conditions that would limit her participation in the study. She provides written consent to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to permit contact with her own medical care provider.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who has been diagnosed with liver disease and is currently on the waitlist for liver transplant. He has a history of hypertension and has been on antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years. Recently, he has noticed increased fatigue, swelling in his legs and ankles, and decreased urine output. His serum creatinine level has been found to be elevated on routine blood work, indicating possible kidney injury. He is being considered for dual kidney-liver transplantation and will undergo a non-invasive urinary test to detect any kidney damage. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no contraindications to kidney biopsy if needed.

A 45-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with aortic aneurysm and planned to undergo aortic surgery requiring deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) with antegrade selective cerebral perfusion. She has a medical history of hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine 10 mg daily. She has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or previous surgeries. The patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The preoperative assessment shows that her ejection fraction is 55%, and her cognitive function is normal with a MMSE score of 29. She has no known history of stroke or neurological disorders. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to assess the impact of cerebral oximetry monitoring on neurological outcomes in aortic arch surgery patients.

A 20-month-old male child was brought to the clinic by his mother, who is HIV-positive. The child was exposed to nevirapine during delivery as part of the prevention of mother-to-child transmission program. The child has not yet received any antiretroviral treatment and is eligible for treatment. The child has not experienced any severe opportunistic infections or tumors, nor does he have a history of toxicity to perinatal nevirapine. The child is expected to remain in the area for the next 6 months. The mother has consented to enroll the child in the Pediatric Nevirapine Resistance Study to determine if a sequential protease-inhibitor/nevirapine-based regimen is effective for the treatment of HIV-infected children who have been previously exposed to nevirapine. The child will be randomized to one of two groups: to continue on the protease-inhibitor containing regimen or to switch to the nevirapine-containing regimen. The study will monitor the child's virologic suppression for 6 months after randomization to determine the success of the treatment regimen.

A 35 year old woman visited the clinic complaining of fatigue, blurry vision, and difficulty walking. She reported a history of episodes of tingling sensations in her legs and arms that lasted for several days or weeks and then disappeared. Her MRI showed multiple white matter lesions in the brain and spinal cord, consistent with the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a and experiencing some improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a research study to help advance understanding of the disease and improve treatment options. She is willing to answer a questionnaire and provide blood samples for genetic and biomarker analysis.

45 year old man with a family history of heart disease. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue during exercise for the past few months. His echocardiogram showed left ventricular hypertrophy with a thickness of 14mm. He has not been diagnosed with any type of cardiomyopathy before. His past medical history includes hypertension and high cholesterol. He is willing to undergo a blood test for genetic sequencing to look for abnormal TTR gene. He does not have significant aortic stenosis.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is a non-smoker and is generally healthy. He has a BMI of 25.0 kg/m^2 and weighs 70 kg. He is sexually inactive and has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse. He has no known allergies to any medications or excipients. He is not lactose intolerant and does not have any significant medical or psychiatric history. His seated blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and his heart rate is 70 bpm. He has not donated blood or experienced any significant blood loss in the past 56 days. He has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 28 days. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the procedures outlined in the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for 2 years. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. The patient has tried steroid treatment and topical budesonide with immunosuppressants, but they have not been effective. The Harvey-Bradshaw Index score is 7. The patient has not received any biologic treatment for her Crohn's disease. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided signed informed consent. The patient has no contraindications to Hyrimoz™ or Zessly™ according to the prescribing recommendations in her country. She has not participated in any interventional clinical trial for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases nor received any investigational agent or procedure within 30 days prior to enrollment.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness for the past year. He has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea and uses a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine at night to manage his symptoms. He has not had any recent changes in his CPAP settings. He denies any history of substance abuse or significant psychiatric disorders. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol, but is otherwise healthy. He does not have any suicidal ideation. His physical exam and lab studies are normal, except for mild hypertension. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve his daytime sleepiness.

32-year-old female with a history of abnormal cervical Pap smear results, confirmed to have cervical high grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) at a recent screening. She has been diagnosed with HPV types 16 and 18 and is currently seeking treatment options. She meets the eligibility criteria for the REVEAL 1 clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study. She has no history of adenocarcinoma-in-situ (AIS), high grade vulvar, vaginal, or anal intraepithelial neoplasia or invasive cancer, and her cervical lesion(s) are fully visualized on colposcopy. She is post-menopausal and not actively trying to conceive, and is willing to use a contraceptive method with a failure rate of less than 1% per year from screening until Week 36. She has a normal electrocardiogram (ECG) and does not have any medical conditions that would jeopardize her safety or interfere with study assessments or endpoint evaluation. She has no bleeding or clotting disorders that would contraindicate IM injections and is not currently taking blood thinners. She has at least two acceptable sites available for IM injection.

A 28 year old woman was diagnosed with osteosarcoma at the age of 16 and completed her treatment four years ago. She has been followed up regularly by the Pediatric Hematology/Oncology staff and physicians at St. Louis Children's Hospital and is currently receiving care from the Siteman Cancer Center's Lifelong Outcomes Clinic at Siteman South County. She has a BMI of 27 kg/m^2 and is considered at risk for poor cardiovascular health. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the trial.

As this is a chart review study, there is no need for patient recruitment. However, a patient description within the scope of this study could be: A pediatric patient who underwent vascular ring division at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta at Egleston Hospital between 2001 and 2004, and had a diverticulopexy performed during the procedure. The patient's medical records will be reviewed as part of the study to collect data regarding the ease of the procedure and the overall outcome.

Mrs. Lim, a 57-year-old retired teacher, was admitted to the hospital due to an acute ischemic stroke two weeks ago. She is now medically stable and will be discharged from the hospital soon. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or heart disease. She has a history of smoking but stopped 5 years ago. She lives with her husband and has two adult children who visit her regularly. She has a caregiver who is her husband. She is able to sit unsupported for 30 seconds, stand on her non-paretic leg for more than 4 seconds, and walk at least 2 meters with maximum of 1 person assist. She can follow a 3-step command. She is expected to be discharged home and has access to a computer with internet connection. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves tele-rehabilitation intervention, as she wants to improve her functional recovery after the stroke.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is a regular smoker, with a history of smoking for the past 5 years. She has tried to quit smoking before but without any success. She is currently not on any smoking cessation treatment. The patient has no known allergies to any medications or ingredients. She has no history of any psychiatric illness, but she does have occasional anxiety which is not currently being treated. The patient is in good general health, with normal blood pressure, heart rate, and body temperature. She has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2. The patient has no history of using non-cigarette tobacco products or e-cigarettes. She does not plan to become pregnant in the near future. The patient has no history of using any medication that is administered intranasally. She also does not have any braided hair that would cause noise in EEG recording.

A 55-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of metastatic melanoma. She has undergone multiple treatments including surgery and chemotherapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than three months. She has no history of HIV, hepatitis B or C, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her blood tests show a normal absolute neutrophil count and platelet count, and her hemoglobin level is greater than 8.0 g/dl. Her liver function tests are normal, and her total bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5 mg/dl. She has not received any systemic therapy for at least four weeks prior to enrolling in the trial. She is willing to practice birth control during the study and for up to four months after the cells are no longer detected in her blood. She has no history of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to any of the agents used in the study, and her left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than 45%. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is interested in participating in the study to explore cell therapy using IL-12 modified tumor white blood cells as a potential treatment for her metastatic melanoma.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of corneal neovascularization in his left eye. The patient reports that his vision has been blurred for the past six months, and he has been experiencing discomfort and irritation in the affected eye. The patient is in generally good health, with no significant medical conditions. He has no history of ocular or periocular malignancy, and he has not used contact lenses in the past two weeks. The patient has not received any treatment with anti-VEGF agents or intravitreal or periocular steroids in the past 30 days. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he is willing to comply with study assessments for the full duration of the trial. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility based on the extent of corneal neovascularization and other inclusion criteria. If eligible, the patient will be randomized to receive either Interleukin-1-Receptor Antagonist eye drops or placebo. The patient will be monitored for safety and efficacy throughout the trial.

The patient is a 70-year-old female with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. She lives with her daughter who serves as her primary caregiver. The patient has been experiencing chronic musculoskeletal pain for over six months, with pain intensity rated at 7 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale. She has not started any new pain treatments or medications in the past month. The patient's Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 22, indicating mild cognitive impairment. She is able to communicate and follow instructions with some assistance. The patient and her daughter have a wireless internet connection at home and are willing to participate in teleyoga classes together. The patient's daughter is also willing to receive yoga treatment at the same time as her mother. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, osteoporosis, and mild depression. She takes medications for these conditions as prescribed by her primary care provider. The patient has not practiced yoga in the past 12 months.

Sophie is a 32-year-old woman who has a history of EBV-positive lymphoma. She was previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation therapy but her cancer has returned and is now considered refractory. She has no other significant medical history and her physical exam is normal. Her laboratory studies show adequate hematologic, hepatic and renal function. She has not received any other treatment for her cancer in the past 4 weeks. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and return to the study center for all clinical evaluations and required follow-up. She is affiliated with the French social security regime. Sophie does not have any known primary CNS lymphoma or CNS metastases. She does not have any active bacterial, viral, or fungal infections requiring systemic therapy. She does not have known active hepatitis B virus infection or circulating hepatitis C virus on qPCR. She has not been diagnosed with refractory graft versus host disease or known history of HHV-6 chromosomal integration or HIV infection.

The patient is an enlisted United States Air Force Airman-in-Training (AiT), aged between 18-25 years old, currently enrolled in a technical training class at the 365 or 363 Training Squadrons of the 82 Training Wing (82 TRW). The AiT must be in their first year of enlistment and their training class must be between 37-91 class days in length. The AiT may have experienced relationship disruptions or social isolation, which could increase their risk for suicidal thoughts and behaviors. The AiT is willing to participate in an active training program called Wingman-Connect, designed to build protective factors in kinship (healthy bonds), guidance (support from mentors and mental health), purpose (goals, sense of being valued and valuable), and balance (self-care and support). The AiT is willing to be randomized to either receive the Wingman-Connect training or to be in the control group. The AiT is willing to comply with all requirements of the study, including attending all training sessions and completing all assessments.

The patient is an 18-year-old African American male who is sexually active and has engaged in penetrative sex (penile-vaginal or penile-anal) at least once in the past 2 months. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to reduce the incidence of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among African American teen males. He is attending the clinic for the expressed purpose of being tested for STIs and is willing to return for the two planned follow-up assessments. He does not have HIV.

A 45-year-old female presents with persistent low back pain for the last 6 months. She has tried non-surgical therapies including physical therapy and pain medications without significant relief. She reports the pain is worse when sitting or standing for long periods of time and is relieved when lying down. She has no history of neurological or radiographic evidence of active radicular pain due to anatomical compression. MRI imaging shows early lumbar disc degeneration at the L4/L5 level. Her Oswestry Disability Index score for low back pain is 40 and her low back pain score as measured by Visual Analog Scale (VAS) is 6 cm. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a single administration of Intradiscal rhGDF-5 for the treatment of early stage lumbar disc degeneration.

50 year old male, recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 infection. He has no prior treatment with interferon or ribavirin. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and he has no history of liver disease or other medical conditions. He weighs 85 kg, and his current height is 5'9". He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Pegasys and Copegus combination therapy in relation to IL28-b gene expression. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to father a child during the trial.

A 46-year-old woman presents with a history of Stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) for the past 2 years. She has been on treatment for hypertension for the past 5 years. Her serum creatinine level has been stable at 2.0 mg/dL for the past 6 months. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, lung disease, liver disease, cancer, or immunosuppressant or antiretroviral therapy. She is a non-smoker and takes no hormone replacement therapy. She is married, with two teenage children, and works as a school teacher. Her physical examination is within normal limits, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, pulse rate of 75 beats per minute, and a body mass index of 28. She reports that she does not engage in any regular exercise, but is willing to participate in the study. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in improving her overall health.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. The cancer has spread to the liver and lungs, causing her to experience fatigue, abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. She has never received chemotherapy treatment for this cancer before. CT scans confirm the presence of measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no history of other malignancies and her HIV and hepatitis status is negative. She is not on immunosuppressive therapy. Her cardiac and pulmonary functions are satisfactory. She has not had central nervous system metastases or untreated spinal cord compression. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and able to complete the quality of life questionnaire in either English or French. She is sterile and does not plan to have children during the study period.

A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer 10 months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy to treat her cancer. She has been cancer-free for the past 6 months. She reports feeling fatigued and has gained weight since her treatment ended. She has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of her time at home. She is interested in increasing her physical activity but feels overwhelmed by the idea of going to a gym. She has a smartphone with internet access and a compatible Fitbit device. She is married and has two children. She works from home part-time and is available to participate in the intervention program. She is fluent in English and is willing to commit to the 12-week program. She has no medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

A 55 year old female has been diagnosed with an advanced solid tumor for which no curative therapy exists. She has no prior or concurrent primary brain tumor or brain metastasis. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and she is expected to live at least 12 weeks. Her granulocyte count is at least 1,500/mm3 and platelet count is at least 100,000/mm3. She does not have an inherited predisposition to hypercoagulation, and her bilirubin and SGOT are normal. Her creatinine is no greater than 1.5 mg/dL. She does not have uncompensated coronary artery disease on electrocardiogram or physical examination, and has not had a myocardial infarction or severe unstable angina within the past 6 months. She does not have severe peripheral vascular disease related to diabetes mellitus and has not had deep venous or arterial thrombosis within the past 3 months. She does not have a history of pulmonary embolism within the past 3 months, and no other significant medical illness. She is not pregnant or nursing, and has tested negative for pregnancy. She will use effective contraception as she is fertile. She has not had any other malignancies within the past 5 years except basal or squamous cell skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She has not had any other concurrent investigational drugs, and will not receive any concurrent biologic, chemotherapy, hormonal, radiotherapy or surgical therapy during the trial.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman with osteoarthritis of both knees. She has been experiencing severe pain and restricted mobility for the past two years, despite undergoing nonoperative therapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of standard posterior cruciate-retaining and high-flexion posterior cruciate-retaining total knee prostheses. The patient has no history of inflammatory arthritis, but has been diagnosed with osteoporosis. She is otherwise in good health and able to walk independently. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 9 year-old boy who has been diagnosed with a left frontal lobe tumor. He is scheduled for elective craniotomy surgery under general anesthesia. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status of II. He is not on any medication at present and has no allergies to any of the study drugs. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or chronic headaches. He has no peri-incisional infection. His body mass index is within the normal range for his age. He is able to understand the instruction of pain scales before surgery. His parents have given informed consent for his participation in the study.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as there are no eligibility criteria listed. This trial appears to be focused on laboratory and animal studies rather than human participants.

A 54-year-old man with a history of metastatic soft tissue sarcoma is being considered for a Phase II clinical trial to assess the efficacy of ipilimumab plus nivolumab in combination with cryotherapy. He has previously undergone one systemic therapy for sarcoma, including adjuvant systemic therapy which was discontinued due to progressive disease. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 3 months. His lab values meet the eligibility requirements, including ANC ≥ 1,000/mm^3, platelet count ≥ 75,000/mm^3, and creatinine clearance > 45 mL/min. The patient has resolved any toxic effects of prior therapy to NCI CTCAE, version 5.0, Grade 1 or less. He is willing to adhere to contraception for a period of 7 months after the last dose of nivolumab. He has not received any live/attenuated vaccine within 30 days before initiation of treatment on this protocol. He does not have any known autoimmune disease, HIV, hepatitis B or C, or active pulmonary disease with hypoxia. He has not received any systemic treatment with either corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications within 7 days of registration. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently admitted to the Maastricht University Hospital due to cardiovascular problems. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. He is currently on blood pressure medications and statins. The patient has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is able to walk without assistance and has no difficulty communicating. The patient has provided written consent for participation in the study. He is expected to stay in the hospital for at least three days. The patient has normal vision and is not diagnosed with dementia. He is willing to participate in the regular measurements and complete the questionnaires provided by the research nurse, which is expected to take no more than 30 minutes per day.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing discomfort in his left eye for the past few months. He was diagnosed with a pterygium, which has been causing him visual disruption. The patient has not had any previous ocular surface surgeries, and he does not have any other ocular surface diseases apart from the pterygium. He is able to understand the nature of the procedure and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not allergic to local anesthetics, and he is not pregnant. He has no history of glaucoma or any conditions that may require glaucoma surgery in the future.

Patient is a 70yo retired male with a history of knee osteoarthritis for the past 5 years. He complains of significant pain, stiffness and decreased mobility in his knees. The patient has tried various treatment options with little success, including pain medication and physical therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of aquatic physical therapy for knee osteoarthritis. The patient is able to walk without the need for aid equipment and has no contraindications for exercise. The patient has not participated in any nutrition or physical activity programs within the past 2 months and has no metal implants in the lower limbs. The patient is willing to commit to the eight-week program and follow-up assessments.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer that has metastasized to her liver and bones. She has been experiencing increasing pain over the past few weeks which has been difficult to control with non-narcotic painkillers like ibuprofen and acetaminophen. She reports an average pain level of 7 out of 10 on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and is having difficulty sleeping at night. She has no known allergies and has been prescribed several medications for her cancer treatment, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She lives with her husband and two adult children who help take care of her. She has no history of drug abuse and is able to communicate effectively with the investigators. She is committed to avoiding pregnancy during the study period.

A 32-year-old woman presents with chronic low back pain that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. She rates her pain as a 6 out of 10 on a numeric pain scale. She has no history of inflammatory, rheumatological diseases, tumor or vertebral fracture. She does not experience leg pain but has difficulty performing daily activities such as bending, lifting and carrying objects due to her back pain. She is physically active but has not undergone physical therapy or changed her physical activity in the previous 3 months. The patient understands Portuguese well enough to fill in the questionnaires. She is not pregnant and has no contraindications to exercise. She has no planned travel in the next 12 weeks and is not geographically inaccessible.

The patient is an 70-year-old retired teacher who lives with her husband in a single-story house. She is active and enjoys gardening and taking walks around her neighborhood. She has never fallen but is concerned about the risk of falling as she ages. She has normal reflexes and muscle tone. She does not have any lower extremity fractures or surgeries in the past 5 years, nor does she have any noticeable gait impairment, low back pain, decreased disease-related vision, dizziness, history of heart problems, bone mineral density <.65, or mini-mental score <24. She is interested in participating in the study to learn ways to prevent falls and improve her overall balance and coordination.

A 58-year-old female presents with a history of mucosal melanoma of the head and neck (MMHN) with no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient has undergone prior local resection to the primary tumor and has no regional lymph nodes present. The patient has a white blood cell count of 5.2 × 109/L, absolute neutrophil count of 2.8 × 109/L, hemoglobin concentration of 100 g/L, and a platelet cell count of 120 × 109/L. The patient's liver function tests show an Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) and Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) of 1.5×ULN. The patient's creatinine clearance rate is 80 mL/min. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has no history of previous RT or chemotherapy. The patient has no severe previous or intercurrent disease that may affect the compliance of the study. The patient consents to the follow-up till death, the study termination or the end of the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old non-smoking woman with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or cancer. Her blood pressure is regularly measured at less than 130/80 mmHg. She does not take any medications known to affect lipid metabolism or insulin resistance, hormones, or blood thinning agents. She does not engage in strength training with resistance weights for more than four hours per week. Her LDL-cholesterol and total cholesterol levels are within normal range for her age and sex. Her fasting triglycerides are below 300 mg/dL and fasting glucose concentration is below 110 mg/dL. The patient is willing to abstain from alcohol and dietary supplements during the study. She has been in a weight-stable state (± 3% of body weight) for at least three months prior to the study.

A 25-year-old woman who works in a veterinary clinic has been suffering from rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms such as nasal congestion, runny nose, itchy eyes, and sneezing when she is exposed to cats. She has a history of allergy to cats, confirmed by a positive skin prick test result with a wheal diameter greater than 3 mm compared to the negative control. She also has a positive specific IgE test result against Fel d1, with a class 2 rating. Her rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms are severe enough that they interfere with her daily activities. She does not have a history of uncontrolled asthma or any other significant health issues. She is interested in participating in this trial to see if cat hair immunotherapy can help alleviate her allergy symptoms.

A 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 35 has been recently diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. She lives in the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area and is looking for ways to manage her symptoms. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. She is currently taking a multivitamin and calcium supplement but no other medications or dietary supplements. She is interested in participating in a 12-week weight loss program that includes education and counseling on healthy lifestyle changes. She is willing to take a supplement three times a day and is committed to attending weekly sessions. She has no history of heart disease, stroke, or diabetes. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs, and she exercises for 30 minutes, three times per week. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic lower limb ischemia (Fontaine-Pokrovsky Stages IIa-III). He has been experiencing pain and cramping in his legs during physical activity, which is relieved by rest. He has tried conservative therapy without success and is not a candidate for surgical or endovascular vessel reconstruction. He does not have any other diseases that may affect the outcome of the study, nor does he have a history of addictive disorders or substance abuse. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer. She has undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor and is currently receiving chemotherapy. The patient reports experiencing significant physical symptoms, including fatigue, pain, and shortness of breath, as well as psychological distress related to her diagnosis and treatment. She has difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in activities that she previously enjoyed. Despite these symptoms, the patient is motivated to maintain a high quality of life throughout her treatment. The patient speaks fluent English and is able to complete electronic questionnaires. She has not received specialized palliative care within the last 6 months and is willing to participate in symptom screening at every outpatient visit. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light physical activity such as office work or light housework. She has a good support system in place, including her husband and two adult children, who are involved in her care. The patient's estimated prognosis is greater than 6 months, according to her primary oncologist.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old female with no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 25 and weighs 60 kg. She is not currently pregnant and has a negative serum hCG pregnancy test. She does not have a history of alcohol abuse or excessive alcohol intake. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the bioavailability of acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) between Esomeprazole and Aspirin after multiple dose administration.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer three years ago. She underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Six months ago, she was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the liver and bones. The patient received trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and T-DM1, and she progressed on these therapies. The patient now reports experiencing mild headaches for the past two weeks. An MRI revealed a small brain lesion. The patient has no neurological symptoms and is otherwise in good health. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Blood work within 14 days of the first dose of the study intervention was normal: WBC: 7.5 x 10^3/uL, Platelets: 250 x 10^3/uL, Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL, Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL, AST: 35 U/L, ALT: 40 U/L, Total bilirubin: 0.5 mg/dL, Albumin: 4.0 g/dL. The patient is willing to undergo treatment with Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and signs the informed consent form.

An 70-year-old retired man from Norway was referred to a specialist health care center for treatment of depression. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months, including loss of interest in hobbies, decreased appetite, difficulty sleeping, and feelings of hopelessness. He has no significant medical history except for mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He lives alone and has two adult children who visit him occasionally. He has no history of dementia or severe aphasia. He speaks Norwegian fluently and is able to understand and follow instructions. He has no known allergies to any medications. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing a persistent cough for the past three months. He has also been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. A chest X-ray revealed the presence of a small nodule in his left lung. Further imaging tests confirmed that the nodule was growing and had increased in size over the past few weeks. His pulmonologist recommended a bronchoscopy procedure to obtain a sample of the nodule for further testing. After discussion of the risks and benefits of the procedure, the patient provided written informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any high-risk conditions for the performance of bronchoscopy and is not pregnant.

55 year-old man presenting to the Mile Square Health Center for his routine check-up. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently on lisinopril and atorvastatin. He reports no urinary or prostate symptoms, but has a family history of prostate cancer, his father was diagnosed at age 65. He is interested in discussing prostate cancer screening with his primary care provider. His last PSA level was 2.5 ng/mL and was performed 2 years ago at his last check-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) in her second complete remission (CR2). She was diagnosed with AML three years ago and has undergone chemotherapy and bone marrow transplantation with an autologous stem cell transplant, but the cancer relapsed. She has been undergoing treatment with chemotherapy and has been deemed a suitable candidate for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, there is no currently available HLA-A, B, C, DRB1 and DQB1 matched related or unrelated donor. She has no significant medical history and her physical examination is unremarkable. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and her heart rate is 70 beats per minute. She has a Karnofsky score of 90% and does not have any inadequate organ function. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has been deemed suitable for it by a panel of hematologists.

A 9-month-old infant boy was admitted to the hospital with a cough, fever, and wheezing for the past 3 days. The baby was born full-term without any complications and has been developing normally. He has no significant past medical history, and all his immunizations are up to date. The baby was not exposed to any known respiratory illnesses or sick contacts. On physical examination, he was noted to be tachycardic, tachypneic, with bilateral wheezing, and mild intercostal retractions. His oxygen saturation was 91% on room air. The chest X-ray showed evidence of hyperinflation and peribronchial cuffing. The nasopharyngeal swab tested positive for Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). The baby was started on oxygen therapy, nebulization, and intravenous fluids. Despite the treatment, the baby's symptoms persisted, and he was admitted to the hospital for further management. The parents were approached for consent for the clinical trial to evaluate a single intravenous dose of Motavizumab for the treatment of RSV illness in hospitalized children.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has chronic moderate pain due to musculoskeletal issues. He has been taking prescription opioid and non-opioid analgesics for the pain on at least 15 of the 30 days prior to the initial baseline/screening visit. He has no history of dependence on opiates, stimulants, alcohol, or benzodiazepines, and has not used any illicit or recreational drugs in the past 30 days. He does not have a current neurological disorder or a current major psychiatric disorder. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and provide written consent. He is not receiving long-acting opioids, such as methadone, LAAM, or sustained release morphine, for treatment of pain. He has not had recent surgery or a major medical procedure that could interfere with study participation. He will need to discontinue all non-study-related opiates during study participation and use an acceptable method of birth control if female.

56F with a history of hypertension, presented to the emergency department with fever, altered mental status, and tachycardia. Upon admission, the patient was diagnosed with septic shock and acute renal failure. She was randomized to receive either continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH) or intermittent hemodialysis (IHD) for renal replacement therapy. The patient's systemic hemodynamics and interstitial tissue concentrations of lactate, pyruvate, glucose, and glycerol were obtained at baseline, 6, 12, 18, and 24 hours after initiation of renal replacement therapy using muscle microdialysis. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, but no other significant medical conditions. She is cooperative and able to provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) five years ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, spasticity, and cognitive impairment, affecting her mobility and quality of life. She is currently able to walk at least 100 meters without resting and stand for at least half an hour. She is willing to participate in the study and is excited to try video game-based physical activity training as a non-pharmacological therapy to manage her MS symptoms. She has no other neurological disease and has not undergone any orthopedic surgery that may affect her balance. She is mentally stable and does not have any serious cognitive or psychiatric disorder.

Middle-aged woman, postmenopausal, with a BMI of 30 kg/m2, non-smoker, who engages in light recreational activities and consumes no more than one alcoholic drink per day. She has no history of hepatic, renal, hematological, peripheral vascular disease or stroke/neurovascular disease, diabetes, hypertension, or sleep apnea. She is not currently taking any medications for any of these conditions nor has any clinically diagnosed anxiety or depression. She has no significant surgical history or other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in a study on meal timing and blood pressure.

A 58 year old man with a history of cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C is scheduled to undergo orthotopic liver transplantation due to end-stage liver disease. The patient has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past 2 years. His Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score is 23, and he has a prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) due to his liver disease. The patient has no history of hemostatic pathology or any other significant medical history. He is affiliated with a social security system and has received clear information regarding the study. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and is within the age limit of 18 years or older. He is not currently participating in any other study protocol and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with obesity for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has not been successful in losing weight. Her body mass index (BMI) is 40, and she is eligible for bariatric surgery. She is scheduled to undergo the surgery in a few weeks. Her past medical history is significant only for occasional headaches, and she is not taking any medication. She works in an office and spends most of her time indoors. Her diet is not well balanced, and she admits to not eating many foods rich in vitamin D. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of a monthly high dose of vitamin D3 on bariatric surgery patients. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. She is willing to provide information about her supplement use, sun exposure, and diet as part of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. He has difficulty sleeping, feels fatigued and has a loss of interest in activities he used to enjoy. He has not sought any help for his symptoms until now. He is currently employed as a software engineer and works from home due to the pandemic. He is married and lives with his wife and two children in a suburban area. He has a supportive family and has no significant medical history. He has not taken any medication for his symptoms or received any psychiatric treatment in the past. He was referred to a psychiatric consultation by his family physician and is willing to participate in the study. He has access to a computer with a web camera and internet connection at home. He is comfortable with technology and has used videoconferencing software for work meetings in the past.

A 68-year-old man presents with a history of prostate cancer that was initially treated with external beam radiation therapy 5 years ago. His PSA levels have been steadily increasing over the past year, and a biopsy confirmed the recurrence of prostate cancer. Salvage cryotherapy has been recommended as a treatment option, and he has consented to participate in this clinical trial. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension for which he takes medication. His current PSA level is 9.2 ng/mL. He has no known distant metastases and no history of major rectal surgery. His urinary function is normal, and he has no known urinary or rectal anomalies. He is currently an active retiree and enjoys playing golf and spending time with his grandchildren.

The patient is a 3-month-old female infant referred to the study by her pediatrician due to elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin on two separate laboratory tests. She was born at full term via uncomplicated vaginal delivery with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. Her neonatal period was unremarkable, and she was discharged home with her parents after 48 hours. However, at the 2-month well-child check, her laboratory tests revealed elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin. A repeat test at 3 months showed persistent elevations. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of fever, vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, or poor feeding. She is currently exclusively breastfed, and there is no family history of liver disease. Physical examination is unremarkable, with no hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, or other signs of illness. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Parental/LAR permission has been obtained for participation in the study.

As this is a follow-up study, a patient description cannot be generated as the study only includes patients who have already been stabilized on OP Depot. This means that the patients have already been enrolled in a previous study where they received OP Depot and showed significant improvement in their symptoms. The purpose of this follow-up study is to assess the long-term efficacy of OP Depot in these patients. Therefore, the patient description would be similar to the previous study, where patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder were enrolled and stabilized on OP Depot.

8 year old girl with no history of emotional, behavioral or learning problems. She was born at full-term and of normal birth weight. She does not have any significant medical history and is not currently on any medication or special diet. She is in the 75th percentile for weight and height for her age and sex. Her parents report that she enjoys watching TV during meals and is often exposed to food advertisements. They are interested in participating in a study that examines the effects of food advertisements on satiety and food intake in children.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer five years ago. She received multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, and was also treated with trastuzumab emtansine as part of a Genentech / Roche-sponsored parent study. Her cancer went into remission for a few years, but has recently returned. She is still receiving trastuzumab emtansine treatment and her physician believes she may continue to benefit from it. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the safety extension study. She is willing to use contraception during the study period as she is of childbearing potential. She is highly motivated to participate in the study to potentially continue to receive benefit from the treatment.

Patient is a 35-year-old man from the United States who has been recently diagnosed with mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis after experiencing symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He has been on a stable dose of 5-aminosalicylates for the past 2 weeks. He has no significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and consumes less than 6 oz of wine or equivalent per day. His BMI is 24, BP: 120/80, HR: 80/min. Laboratory results show some mild abnormalities in renal function and liver enzymes, but no other clinically significant abnormalities. He is willing to comply with the study requirements, can swallow capsules, and provides written informed consent.

A 64-year-old Caucasian man presents with symptoms of fatigue, reduced muscle mass, and decreased sexual desire. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. He denies any history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has not undergone any surgeries. His family history is negative for any prostate or hormonal problems. He is not taking any supplements or medications apart from his hypertension medication. His recent lab reports show low levels of testosterone (240 ng/dl), and his PSA levels are normal (6 ng/ml). He has no urinary symptoms, as his IPSS score is 5. He is married and has two grown-up children. He is interested in participating in the study to determine the effects of testosterone replacement therapy on prostate tissues in aging men with androgen deficiency.

This is a 45 year-old female diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia. She is currently in remission after initial chemotherapy but is in need of a bone marrow transplant. She has a fully HLA-matched (10 of 10) related donor who is willing to undergo GCSF mobilization and apheresis. The patient has good renal and liver function, and her pulmonary function is within normal limits. She has not undergone a prior allogeneic transplant. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce the risk of graft-versus-host disease after her transplantation.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who has been diagnosed with epilepsy. She has experienced recurrent seizures for the past year and is currently on anti-epileptic medication. She has a history of head trauma from a car accident when she was 18 years old. She is fluent in English and able to understand the nature of the study. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She wears glasses for corrected vision. She does not have any other neurologic or psychiatric conditions and has no sensory deficits. She has not used any substances in the past 3 months and does not have any clinically significant substance dependency. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past few weeks. She underwent an imaging test that revealed an abnormal pelvic mass. She has no previous history of cancer and is in overall good health. Her performance status is not specified, and her life expectancy is not known. She has not undergone any prior treatments for this condition. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help doctors diagnose ovarian cancer more accurately. She has been informed that the trial involves collecting blood samples for proteomic profiling before and after surgery. The patient is willing to undergo surgical evaluation within the next three weeks and is committed to participating in the study for up to 10 years.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 three months ago. She experienced mild symptoms, including cough, fever, and body aches, but did not require hospitalization. She has since recovered from the acute phase of the infection but has been experiencing persistent shortness of breath and fatigue. She is interested in participating in a study that will investigate the long-term effects of COVID-19 on respiratory, cardiac, sleep, and mental health. She is affiliated with a French social and health insurance system and is willing to provide informed consent for biological collection.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who suffered a left hemisphere stroke 3 months ago. She presents with hemiparesis and difficulty walking, relying on a walker for mobility. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. She has completed a course of inpatient stroke rehabilitation and is currently receiving outpatient physical therapy twice a week. She reports difficulty with fine motor tasks, such as buttoning clothes, as well as with gross motor tasks, such as walking and standing up from a chair. She has a history of falls and is concerned about her ability to safely navigate her home environment. Her medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and metoprolol. Physical examination shows decreased strength and sensation on the left side, with a mildly spastic left upper extremity and flaccid left lower extremity. Her gait is slow and unsteady, with a shortened left step length and decreased push-off on the left foot. Her Berg Balance Scale score is 30/56, indicating moderate fall risk. Her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28/30, indicating intact cognition. MRI of the brain shows a left middle cerebral artery infarct with no evidence of hemorrhage or mass effect. Her current medications do not include any drugs known to affect motor coordination.

There is no patient involvement in this clinical trial as it is focused on comparing the effectiveness of different intubation devices during pediatric resuscitation on a child manikin. The eligibility criteria are focused on experienced emergency medical personnel with at least one year of work experience in emergency medicine who can give voluntary consent to participate in the study. The exclusion criteria are limited to those who do not meet the above criteria or have wrist or low back diseases.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after experiencing headaches and seizures. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is single and lives with her parents. She works as a graphic designer. She has no significant family history of cancer. Her Karnofsky performance score is 80, and her Lansky performance score is 90. She is currently taking levetiracetam to control her seizures. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has signed the necessary consent forms. She is able to swallow capsules and undergo serial MRI scans. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is committed to following the study protocol.

A 22-year-old woman presents with symptoms of paranoia and delusions for the past month. She reports hearing voices and having difficulty concentrating. She has no previous history of psychiatric illness or treatment with antipsychotic medications. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medication. Her physical examination is normal, and there is no evidence of any organic disorder. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 7-year-old male child with a history of wheat allergy. The patient's parents reported that the child has had previous allergic reactions after consuming wheat products, such as hives, itching, and swelling. The patient was diagnosed with IgE-mediated wheat allergy by a physician. The patient has no other known allergies or medical conditions. The patient is not currently on any oral immunotherapy or skin care products containing wheat. The patient has occasional mild eczema on the arms and legs, but it does not affect daily activities. The parents have agreed to participate in the study and have signed the consent form. The patient will undergo a medical examination, skin status evaluation, and blood sample collection to determine baseline immunoglobulin E levels to wheat and omega-5 gliadin. The primary outcome will be the change in specific immunoglobulin E levels after the patient stops using wheat-containing skin care products. The patient will be monitored throughout the study for any adverse reactions.

55F with end-stage lung disease secondary to cystic fibrosis, on the lung transplant waitlist for over 2 years, was referred to the living donor lung transplant program. The patient has a history of recurrent respiratory infections, chronic cough, and dyspnea on exertion. She has a significant decline in her lung function with a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) less than 30% predicted. Despite optimal medical therapy, the patient's condition continued to deteriorate, and she was experiencing frequent hospitalizations. The patient was evaluated by the transplant team, and it was determined that she was a suitable candidate for living donor lung transplantation. The patient underwent thorough evaluation, including pulmonary function tests, imaging studies, and psychological evaluation, and was deemed eligible for the procedure. The patient provided voluntary, written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to return for all the required post-operative follow-ups.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who presents with hematuria and flank pain. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 5 years ago. He has no other significant medical history. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Urinalysis shows microscopic hematuria. CT urogram reveals a filling defect in the left ureter suggestive of UUT-UC. He is scheduled for diagnostic ureterorenoscopy and is a candidate for minimal invasive endoscopic treatment. He has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with Asperger's Syndrome. He is a Pennsylvania resident and is interested in participating in a social skills training program for adults with Asperger's Syndrome or high-functioning autism. He is able to fluently speak in full sentences and has a verbal IQ of 100 on the Kaufman Brief Intelligence Test, Second Edition. He is looking to improve his ability to initiate and maintain conversations, establish friendships, and develop social skills for job interviews and dating. He does not have a significant language delay and does not exhibit aggression towards peers. He is not currently enrolled in high school and has no secondary disorders of anxiety or depression that would prevent his participation in the treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking male with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 who has a history of osteoarthritis and takes over-the-counter NSAIDs occasionally for pain relief. He has no history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) or peptic ulcer disease. He has not participated in any investigational treatment studies in the past 4 weeks. He has no known allergies or intolerances to aspirin or omeprazole. He does not have any uncontrolled acute or chronic medical illnesses or gastrointestinal disorders that would endanger him if he were to participate in the study. He does not have any history of schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and provide written informed consent. He does not have excessive alcohol use or recent history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has not ingested grapefruit or grapefruit juice within the past 10 days and does not plan to ingest it during the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with chronic hepatitis B infection. He was diagnosed with hepatitis B 5 years ago and has been on antiviral treatment with entecavir for the past year. His HBV DNA level is currently less than 1000 copies/ml and HBsAg level is less than 3000 IU/ml. He has not experienced any significant side effects from his current treatment. His liver function tests show normal levels of ALT and AST. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or current illnesses. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

John is a 62 year old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. After discussing treatment options with his healthcare provider, he has decided to undergo laparoscopic prostatectomy. John has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He has no known allergies to medications and has never had any issues with anesthesia in the past. John is able to understand and participate in pain scoring systems. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will compare the effectiveness of Quadratus Lumborum Block and Transversus Abdominis Plane Block for post-prostatectomy analgesia.

A 30-year-old male patient with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV came to the primary care clinic for his routine check-up. He reported drinking heavily at least once per month (5 drinks or more) and sometimes drinks more than 14 drinks per week. He identifies as gay and has had sex (oral or anal) with a male partner in the past 12 months. He has been stabilized on his current ART regimen for at least 3 months prior to study enrollment. He does not use intravenous drugs and is not currently receiving treatment for alcohol or drug problems. He is interested in participating in the study to reduce his heavy drinking and improve his overall health.
