A 42-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician due to a history of hypertension and elevated homocysteine levels. She has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 2 years and has been taking medication to control her blood pressure. Despite medication, her systolic blood pressure has been consistently in the range of 130-149 mmHg. She has a history of smoking, but quit 3 months ago. Her alcohol intake is limited to occasional social drinking. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or other chronic illnesses. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2. Laboratory evaluation revealed that her homocysteine level was above 10µmol/l. She is not currently taking any dietary supplements or medications other than her antihypertensive medication. She has agreed to participate in this clinical trial to assess the effect of the combination product (Verum) on her blood pressure and endothelial function. She has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 40-year-old female diagnosed with systemic sclerosis, displaying diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis with involvement proximal to the elbow or knee and a modified Rodnan Skin Score of ≥ 14. She also has pulmonary fibrosis or alveolitis on CT scan, abnormal EKG, and gastrointestinal tract involvement confirmed on radiological study. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of an autologous stem cell transplant using a regimen of immune suppressant drugs and chemotherapy that is less toxic to the heart. She meets the inclusion criteria for the age group, diagnosis, and pulmonary involvement. She does not have any exclusion criteria, and has a good comprehension of the irreversible sterility as a side effect of therapy.

This is a 10-year-old male with a past medical history of epilepsy diagnosed at age 5. He has been on multiple anti-epileptic medications including carbamazepine, lamotrigine, and valproic acid with limited success in controlling his seizures. He has an average of 4 seizures per week with no identifiable triggers. He has no other significant medical history and is up to date on all vaccinations. He has a normal BMI and no feeding difficulties. He is currently in school and performing at grade level. His family is willing to try the ketogenic diet as a treatment option for his epilepsy and is able to commit to at least 12 weeks of treatment.

55-year-old male with a past medical history of COPD, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and fever for the past 3 days. On examination, he was tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 26 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. Chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with pneumonia. The patient was admitted to the ICU for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and started on nasal high flow oxygen therapy with a FiO2 of 60% and a flow rate of 50 L/min. He was intubated and mechanically ventilated for 24 hours and then successfully extubated. The patient continued to receive nasal high flow oxygen therapy for an additional 48 hours with a gradual decrease in FiO2 and flow rate until he was able to maintain an oxygen saturation of >92% on room air. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 66-year-old woman who served in the US Army during the Vietnam War received a letter inviting her to participate in a study on the long-term health outcomes of women veterans. She served as a nurse in a military hospital in Japan from 1968 to 1970, where she treated injured soldiers who were transported from Vietnam. She recalls the long hours she spent working in the hospital and the emotional toll it took on her. She has had trouble sleeping and has experienced anxiety and nightmares related to her time in the service. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the long-term effects of her service. She is retired now and enjoys spending time with her grandchildren. She reports occasional joint pain and stiffness, but is otherwise in good health. She is willing to complete a mailed survey, participate in a telephone interview, and allow the study investigators to review her medical records. She is excited to contribute to research that could help improve the health and well-being of women veterans who served during the Vietnam War.

This is a 42-year-old female who presented with a headache and blurry vision. Brain MRI showed a mass lesion in the left temporal lobe with surrounding edema. Subsequent biopsy revealed a high-grade glioma. The patient is being considered for surgical resection, but there is concern for pseudoprogression due to recent radiation therapy. The patient is otherwise healthy with no major medical comorbidities and has a performance status score of 80 on the KPS scale. She has no history of allergies to imaging agents and is able to comply with the sedation requirements for PET-CT examination. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent/assent.

For this clinical trial, the patient must be an adult male or female between the ages of 18 and 75. They must have a body mass index within the range of 18.0 to 40.0 kg/m2 and a minimum weight of 50 kg at screening. Females must be of non-childbearing potential, and males must agree to abstinence or use a highly effective method of contraception.   For hepatic impairment subjects, they must have a diagnosis of chronic (> 6 months) stable hepatic insufficiency, a stable medication regimen, and be in good general health with concurrent illnesses associated with hepatic impairment. They must have evidence of cirrhosis due to HCV, HBV, cryptogenic, alcohol abuse, or NASH. They cannot have evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma and must have hepatic impairment as assessed by a Child Pugh classification score at screening.  For healthy subjects, they must be demographically matched to a hepatically impaired subject and be medically healthy with a clinically significant medical history.   Exclusion criteria include a history of drug or alcohol abuse within 6 months prior to dosing, a history of clinically significant hypersensitivity reactions to the study drug or related compounds, a history of febrile illness or evidence of infection within 14 days prior to dosing, and a history of major surgery within 4 weeks of dosing. Other exclusion criteria include a positive pregnancy test or lactating for females, a diagnosis or history of Gilbert's syndrome, and a positive result for HIV at screening.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He has been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 mL/min/1.73 m². He is currently taking lisinopril and metformin to manage his hypertension and diabetes, respectively. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has no known allergies to any medication. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his written informed consent. His BMI is 27 kg/m². The physical examination and laboratory tests conducted at the screening visit show no significant abnormalities, except for the decrease in eGFR. The subject is judged to be in a stable condition and acceptable for study participation.

12 yo F with cystic fibrosis (CF) and F/MF genotype, who completed the study drug treatment in the parent study (VX19-445-116, NCT04353817) for the triple combination therapy of elexacaftor (ELX), tezacaftor (TEZ) and ivacaftor (IVA). The patient experienced a significant improvement in lung function and decrease in pulmonary exacerbations during the parent study. The patient had no history of study drug intolerance in the parent study. The patient and their family are interested in continuing the triple combination therapy to maintain the improved lung function and overall health. The patient is compliant with medication regimen and able to attend study visits as required.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms related to hypogonadism, such as decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, fatigue, and decreased muscle mass. He has not been treated for hypogonadism in the past 3 months and has not used any testosterone injectable product, transdermal or gel products in the past 2 weeks. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of clinically significant hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurological, or allergic disease. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 80 kg. He has no history of drug allergies or regular alcohol consumption exceeding 14 drinks/week. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days and uses no prescription or nonprescription drugs and dietary supplements within 7 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of investigational product. He is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 25-year-old female with a history of recurrent otitis media and otorrhea. She had tympanostomy tube insertion 6 months ago and has been experiencing persistent otorrhea since then. She has tried various ear drops and antibiotics without any significant improvement. On otoscopy, there is evidence of otorrhea and tympanic membrane perforation. She has no known drug allergies and is not currently pregnant. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is currently 18 weeks pregnant. She is seeking an abortion and has decided to undergo dilation and evacuation. She is experiencing anxiety about the procedure and is concerned about the pain associated with the osmotic dilator insertion. She has no prior experience with TENS therapy. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies or contraindications to TENS therapy. She is able to read and speak English and is willing to sign the informed consent form. The patient is not incarcerated and does not have preterm premature rupture of membranes or evidence of intra-amniotic infection. She does not have a cardiac device implanted and has normal sensation in the area of electrode placement. She has not used TENS therapy before and is not opioid dependent. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old female who was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast six months ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Recently, she has developed bone pain and a PET scan revealed metastatic disease to her bones and liver. She is experiencing fatigue and difficulty with physical activity but is still able to perform light work. Her blood tests show adequate organ function. She has no history of heart problems or high blood pressure. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore further treatment options.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who had undergone gingival depigmentation procedure a year ago. The brown pigmentation of his gums has returned, and he wants to undergo the procedure again. He maintains good oral hygiene and has a plaque index of less than 1. He has a thick gingival biotype, and his keratinized gingiva is more than 2mm. He has never smoked, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is not taking any medications that could affect healing. He has not undergone any periodontal surgery in the last six months. He has not undergone any dental treatment in the last month. He is not pregnant or lactating. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and wants to know more about the non-eugenol periodontal pack with and without PRF.

The patient is a 52 year old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but the cancer has continued to progress. Further evaluation showed that her cancer is positive for androgen receptor and PTEN. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1. She is able to swallow and retain oral medication and does not have any clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may alter drug absorption. She has not had any prior use of PI3K inhibitors or anti-androgen therapies. She is willing to use highly effective contraception to prevent pregnancy or agree to abstain from heterosexual activity throughout the study. She has signed the informed consent form prior to the performance of any screening procedures and is able to comply with protocol requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently suffered a sub-acute stroke. He was diagnosed with an ischemic brain injury by an MRI scan done 6 weeks after the onset of the stroke. He has volitional control of his non-paretic arm and has at least minimal antigravity movement in the shoulder of his paretic arm. He has some wrist extension of the paretic arm in the antigravity position. He is able to score > 6 of 10 of abbreviated Mental Test and can follow instructions and provide informed consent for the study. He does not have any additional medical, cardiovascular, or orthopedic conditions that would hinder the proper assessment and treatment. He does not use cardiac pacemakers and does not have any receptive dysphasia. He does not have a significant upper limb peripheral neuropathy or severe shoulder, elbow, wrist, or finger contractures that would preclude a passive range of motion of the arm. He does not have skin allergy that would prevent electrical stimulation. He is not involved in any drug studies or other clinical trials.

A 10 year old boy with B Thalassemia Major is being considered for a clinical trial assessing endocrine and nutritional status. He has been receiving regular blood transfusions since the age of 2 and has been experiencing slow growth and low weight. His BMI is below the 10th percentile for his age and gender. The patient has no known endocrine abnormalities and has not received any nutritional intervention before. His parents are willing to have him participate in the study and are committed to following the nutritionist's advice for calorie intake and balanced diet. The patient's siblings will serve as the control group for the study.

A 45-year-old female has recently been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and is scheduled to receive adjuvant anthracycline chemotherapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities. She has no history of cardiac disease, but has been taking a beta-blocker for high blood pressure. Her bloodwork shows a hemoglobin level of 120 mg/L, platelet count of 150 x 10^9/L, and white blood cell count of 6 x 10^9/L. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially prevent heart damage from the anthracycline chemotherapy. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period as she is premenopausal.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is a professional cellist in an orchestra. She has been experiencing chronic neck and shoulder pain for the past six months, which is affecting her ability to play her instrument. She has tried physical therapy and massage therapy, but has not noticed any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is motivated to try new treatments to improve her pain and is not afraid of needles. She does not have any coagulation disorders and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and hopes to improve her pain so she can continue to perform in her orchestra.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who presents with a history of persistent toothache in his lower left jaw. He reports that the pain has been gradually increasing over the past few months and has become unbearable in the last few days. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. On clinical examination, there is tenderness to percussion and palpation of the mandibular left first molar. Radiographs reveal periapical radiolucency with a minimum size of 2.0 × 2.0 mm. The tooth is diagnosed with pulpal necrosis and requires primary root canal treatment. Patient is informed about the clinical trial evaluating the effect of smear layer on endodontic outcome and is willing to participate. He meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. The patient is randomly allocated to the smear layer positive group (SP) and is scheduled for treatment.

A 28-year-old healthy woman who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no known history of cardiac or systemic diseases and has not experienced any complications during her current pregnancy. She is expecting her first child and is excited to participate in a study that may help provide valuable information about the changes in cardiac function during and after pregnancy. She is physically active and maintains a healthy diet. She has no history of smoking or drug use and drinks alcohol in moderation. She has undergone a baseline echocardiogram, which was found to be normal. She is motivated to attend all scheduled appointments and follow the study protocol diligently.

The patient is a healthy 6-year-old boy who was born in the same quarter as the reference FluMist vaccinee. He has no known medical conditions that put him at high risk for complications of influenza, such as chronic cardiovascular and pulmonary disease. The boy has received previous vaccinations, but not the trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (TIV). He is willing to participate in the study in order to help evaluate the safety of FluMist vaccination in children.

27 F who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is willing to participate in a dietary intervention study aimed at assessing the effects of Fibre Grains on blood glucose levels. The patient has no regular medication use, and her nutritional supplements are documented and acceptable. She has a family history of diabetes, with one grandparent having the condition. The patient has no psychiatric disorders, does not regularly use drugs of abuse, and is not pregnant or lactating. She has no significant alcohol intake and her blood pressure is within normal limits. The patient has no active infections, allergies to insulin, or bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. Her laboratory values are within normal ranges, including fasting glucose and 2-hour postprandial glucose levels. The patient is reliable and willing to follow study procedures, making herself available for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 6 year old boy diagnosed with autistic disorder. He has a history of chronic gastrointestinal problems including constipation, abdominal pain, and bloating. He has not experienced any gastrointestinal infections or abnormalities. He is currently not taking any medication, undergoing any behavioral therapy, or following any specific diet. His parents are interested in enrolling him in a clinical trial to treat his gastrointestinal symptoms. His recent laboratory tests are within normal limits, and he does not have IgA deficiency. He has not participated in any other investigational studies.

This is a 25 year old male who is in good general health with no known medical conditions. He has a BMI of 28 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research. He does not take any prescription or non-prescription medications, herbals or foods that are known to alter P-glycoprotein or CYP3A activity. He is not HIV positive and has no family history of type 2 diabetes. He provides informed consent and is willing to undergo MRI and PET scanning as part of the study.

A 45-year-old man presents with chronic back pain and widespread pain throughout the body. He has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by the Back & Pain Center at the University of Michigan. He reports difficulty sleeping due to the pain and has tried various pain medications with limited relief. He has no history of autoimmune disorders or recent surgeries, but he does have a history of alcohol dependence which he has been in recovery from for the past year. He is currently not taking any medications for his pain. He is able to read and converse fluently in English and is interested in participating in the study to try and improve his pain management strategies.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from widespread pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances for more than a year. She has visited several medical specialists and undergone numerous diagnostic tests, but no specific diagnosis has been established. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by a rheumatologist and is currently receiving medication for pain and sleep. She is married with two children and works as a part-time accountant. She reports that her symptoms have a significant impact on her daily life and limit her ability to perform her work and household tasks. She has tried different types of physical exercise programs and relaxation techniques, but none have provided significant relief. She is interested in participating in the PNE and PE program to learn more about her condition and to improve her physical and emotional well-being. She is willing to commit to attending the weekly sessions for six weeks and to follow the exercise program at home. Her BMI is 27.9, and her blood pressure and other vital signs are within normal limits. She does not smoke or consume alcohol.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese woman who was diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer that has metastasized to her lungs. She has undergone standard treatments including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy, but the tumor has continued to grow despite these treatments. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, and her life expectancy is greater than 3 months. She is using effective contraception and is not pregnant. She has no history of recent stroke or autoimmune disease that is not controlled by NSAIDs. She has no history of cardiovascular conditions or other diseases that would contraindicate the use of an investigational drug. Her organ function is adequate for participation in the study. She has not received any investigational agents or participated in any other clinical studies within the past 4 weeks.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. She has been treated with infliximab for the past 7 months, but despite the treatment, she has not achieved remission. She reports experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. The patient has previously tried other treatments including mesalamine and prednisone, with no success. She is now interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential beneficial effects of probiotics as adjuvant therapy in ulcerative colitis patients with insufficient response to anti-TNF treatment. She is willing to take the probiotic formula IDOFORM Travel® for 8 weeks, and undergo colonoscopies, gut biopsies, and provide fecal samples and serological markers as part of the study. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study, and has signed informed consent. She meets all the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

35 year-old male with a history of mild asthma and intermittent atopic dermatitis presented with occasional wheezing and skin rashes. He has been using a short-acting beta-agonist inhaler as needed for asthma symptoms and a topical corticosteroid cream for skin rashes. He reports occasional seasonal allergies but denies any other medical conditions or use of vitamin D or systemic antihistamines. He is interested in participating in a study to explore the role of vitamin D and its receptor gene polymorphisms in patients with asthma and atopic dermatitis.

30 year old female with a history of infertility for 2 years. The patient has been attempting to conceive for 2 years without success. She has no history of prior pregnancies or miscarriages. Her menstrual periods occur every 28-30 days and last for 5 days. She has no known history of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) or other reproductive disorders. The patient is not currently taking any vitamin D supplements or medications for systemic disease. She has no history of ovarian surgery or gonadotoxic therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and ovarian reserve in infertile women.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who has been struggling with facial lipoatrophy for the past 2 years. She has noticed a significant loss of volume in her cheeks and temples, which has caused her to feel self-conscious about her appearance. She has tried various skincare products and makeup techniques to hide her facial asymmetry, but has not found any satisfactory results. She is in good overall health and has no history of autoimmune or connective tissue diseases. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception if needed. She has not had any cosmetic or surgical procedures in the treatment area for at least 6 months. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive treatment with Princess® FILLER and hopes to see an improvement in her facial appearance.

A 67-year-old male presents with a diagnosis of hormone-refractory prostate cancer that has progressed despite androgen deprivation therapy. The patient has measurable or evaluable disease and has experienced a PSA increase defined as 2 consecutive rises, with the first increase in PSA occurring at least a week after the reference value. The patient's PSA increase is at least 25% above the reference value, and the absolute PSA value is greater than 5 ng/mL. The patient has not received more than 1 prior chemotherapy regimen and may have received prior immunomodulatory therapy. The patient is currently taking a single agent LHRH agonist or antagonist. The patient

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of left thigh mass that has been growing over the past several months. He reports intermittent pain and discomfort in the area of the mass. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals a firm, non-tender mass measuring approximately 10 cm in diameter in the left thigh. There is no overlying skin changes or erythema. Imaging studies, including CT scan and MRI, confirm the presence of a soft tissue sarcoma. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. He has previously received anthracycline-containing chemotherapy for advanced disease but progressed after the first-line treatment. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. He has no significant cardiac, renal, or liver disease, and his estimated life expectancy is at least 16 weeks. He is willing to undergo central revision and BRCA1 and BRCA2 evaluation. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and his serum pregnancy test is negative. He is willing to use adequate barrier birth control measures during the course of the trial and for 5 months after the last dose of study drug. He is able to swallow oral medications and has no history of bleeding diathesis or seizure disorders requiring medication. He does not have any severe or uncontrolled medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the trial. He has no history of noncompliance with medical regimens and is willing and able to return for scheduled visits.

The patient is a 54-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 8 months ago. He underwent chemotherapy with cytarabine and daunorubicin, followed by consolidation chemotherapy with high-dose cytarabine. Unfortunately, he relapsed 4 months later and received additional chemotherapy with no response. He has no siblings and his children do not match his HLA type. He is currently seeking alternative treatment options and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a reduced intensity haploidentical transplant. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. His cardiac function is normal with an ejection fraction of 55%. He has good pulmonary function with a DLCO of 70%. His liver and kidney function are also normal. He has a performance status of 80%. He is willing to use contraception as he is married and his wife is post-menopausal. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

This is a 32 year-old female who has been experiencing frequent panic attacks over the past few months. She also reports feeling anxious in social situations and has difficulty sleeping due to worry. She has consulted her primary care physician who referred her to a specialist for further evaluation. After completing an assessment, she was diagnosed with panic disorder with agoraphobia and was recommended to undergo cognitive behavioral therapy. However, due to long wait times for face-to-face psychotherapy, she was offered participation in the Velibra study. She has internet access and is proficient in German, which is the language used in the program. She has provided written informed consent and has not recently started or changed anxiolytic medication.

The patient is a 40-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who is scheduled to undergo allogenic bone marrow transplant (BMT) from his brother who is a HLA match. He has completed chemotherapy and is currently in remission. He has no prior history of bone marrow or stem cell transplant. His vital signs are stable and he has no active infections. He has no known allergies to medication. All laboratory workup are within normal limits, and his white blood cell count is expected to recover in the next few days. He has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old male smoker with a 20 pack-year history comes to the clinic for a scheduled thoracic surgery. He has been trying to quit smoking for the past month and has not used any systemic corticosteroids during this time. He reports experiencing shortness of breath and coughing, especially during physical activity, which he attributes to his smoking habit. He has not experienced any significant weight loss recently and has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He has not been diagnosed with any other major medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the impact of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) on muscle regeneration.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of chronic pain related to endometriosis. She is scheduled to undergo a major urologic procedure in three days. She has a history of opioid sensitivity and reports experiencing side effects such as nausea and dizziness while taking these medications. She is currently taking gabapentin and acetaminophen for her chronic pain. Her past medical history is significant for depression and anxiety, which are currently well-controlled with medication. She has never had a history of drug or alcohol abuse. Her family history is non-significant. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures and provide a written informed consent.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl attending a public school in Duque de Caxias, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. She enjoys playing outside with friends but also spends a lot of time watching TV and playing video games. She often eats fast food or processed snacks for lunch and dinner and drinks sugary beverages throughout the day. Her parents are concerned about her unhealthy habits and have signed a consent form for her to participate in a school-based trial aimed at promoting healthy diet and physical activity. The trial involves adding nudging actions to the intervention group, and the family is excited to see if these small changes can make a big difference in their daughter's health.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (PD) 5 years ago. He has been on levodopa therapy for the past 3 years and has noticed a significant improvement in his motor symptoms. However, he has developed motor fluctuations and dyskinesia, which have been difficult to manage. The patient was recommended for subthalamic nucleus (STN) deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery and underwent bilateral STN DBS with the Medtronic Percept PC implantable neural stimulator 6 months ago. The patient has been optimized for clinical stimulation and medication for at least 3 months post-surgery. The patient has provided formal consent to participate in the study. The patient has a robust beta peak (detectable using the Percept BrainSense Survey feature; ≥ 0.7 µV/rtHz), intra-operatively (assessed via Lead Confirm technology from Alpha Omega). The patient has exhibited a good response to stimulation (30% improvement on UPDRS III compared to baseline OFF), at least 3 months post-surgery. The patient is not currently experiencing any significant stimulation-induced side effects and does not require unusual programming parameters such as very high (> 200 Hz) or low (< 100) frequencies. The patient does not have an implanted cardiac device and the Medtronic Percept TM PC indicates no need for elective-replacement-indicated (ERI) at the start of the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was diagnosed with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) based on clinical presentation, radiological, biochemical and genetic investigations. He has been experiencing bone pain, weakness, and growth retardation. He has not participated in any interventional clinical trials and is not currently on any treatment regimen. His parents have provided informed consent and he will be enrolled in the XLH registry. Follow-up data will be collected through routine visits to his treating physician.

A 28 year old female with a history of periodontitis marginalis adulta progressiva lenta presenting with gum recession and tooth sensitivity. The patient reports discomfort during previous scaling and root planning procedures and is interested in participating in a study comparing local anesthesia methods. The patient does not have any known allergies to local anesthetics and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is fluent in Danish and able to provide oral and written consent.

A 26-year-old female living in a rural area in Zambia with her husband and their 3-month-old daughter is eligible for this clinical trial. She is the primary caregiver of her daughter and has been attending regular health check-ups at the local health facility. She is concerned about her daughter's development and wants to learn more about how to improve her child's cognitive and language development. She is willing to participate in the parenting group sessions and attend fortnightly group meetings. She is willing to provide informed consent and is available to participate in the household surveys and in-depth interviews. She is not planning to move from her health center catchment zone during the study period. She is excited to learn from other caregivers and contribute to the study's findings.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who recently suffered a spinal cord injury following a car accident. He is currently undergoing inpatient rehabilitation to regain his mobility and independence. He uses a manual wheelchair for at least 50% of his mobility. He experiences occasional shoulder pain and stiffness, which is hindering his ability to perform activities of daily living, such as dressing and grooming. He is motivated to participate in this study to help develop a biopsychosocial prospective surveillance model to prevent shoulder pain and dysfunction in individuals with SCI. The patient has no preexisting neurological conditions or other health complications that could influence upper extremity function. He is willing to attend follow-up sessions at 6 months and 1 year following SCI.

Maria is a 47 year old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 3 years ago. She is currently under intensive insulin therapy and takes fast insulin before breakfast. Her HbA1c level is 8.2% (66mmol/mol). She has a BMI of 28.5 Kg/m2 and is in menopause, currently taking hormone replacement therapy. She has no history of neurological, endocrine or liver diseases, cancer, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She is HIV negative and has never suffered a stroke or acute myocardial infarction, nor undergone any gastrointestinal resection. Maria is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the acute effects of a low and high glycemic index breakfast on her glycemic response and satiety.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a BMI of 35. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right hip joint, which has significantly affected his mobility and quality of life. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has been advised by his orthopedic surgeon to undergo hip arthroplasty for better quality of life. He has given informed consent to participate in the trial and is willing to follow the study protocol.

A 56-year-old man who works as a construction worker presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He reports no recent travel history or exposure to sick contacts. He has a history of smoking and occasionally drinks alcohol. On examination, he appears to be in moderate distress, with mild tachypnea and tachycardia. Lung auscultation reveals diminished breath sounds and crackles in the right lower lobe. His oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. A chest X-ray confirms the presence of infiltrates in the right lower lobe. The Binax NOW® assay is positive for S. pneumoniae. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with chest pain that started 2 hours ago. The pain is described as a crushing sensation in the center of the chest, radiating to the left arm and jaw. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking for 30 years. He has never had a heart attack before. On physical examination, the patient is diaphoretic and in distress. His vital signs are as follows: heart rate 110 beats per minute, blood pressure 160/95 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, temperature 98.6°F. His electrocardiogram shows ST-elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. The patient is started on aspirin, heparin, and ticagrelor and taken to the cardiac catheterization lab for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI). During PPCI, the culprit artery is identified, and thrombus aspiration and pre-dilatation are performed. The patient is then randomized into the study between a drug-coated balloon (DCB) only strategy or drug-eluting stent (DES) in a 1:1 ratio. The patient will be followed up for 9 months and undergo a control coronary angiography, including measurement of the fractional flow reserve (FFR) of the treated lesion(s). The patient is eligible for this clinical trial.

64-year-old Caucasian male with a history of metastatic castrate refractory prostate cancer presented to the oncology clinic with complaints of increasing fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. He has a history of prostate cancer and underwent a radical prostatectomy 10 years ago. He was diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer 5 years ago and has received multiple lines of therapy, including androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, and abiraterone. His most recent scans showed progression in liver, bone, and lymph nodes. Laboratory studies revealed an elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level of 45 ng/mL. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications. Given his progressive metastatic castrate refractory prostate cancer, he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. The biopsy revealed an invasive ductal carcinoma with a size of 2.1 cm, HER2-negative, and ER/PR-positive. An axillary ultrasound showed no lymph node involvement. The patient is currently receiving paclitaxel chemotherapy following surgery, which is expected to continue for 12 weeks. She reports experiencing mild tingling and numbness in her hands and feet, which is suspected to be related to the chemotherapy. The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, or any other significant medical conditions. She is currently taking no medications and has a negative pregnancy test. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to complete questionnaires on her own.

The patient is a 45-year-old man living with HIV for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing increased stress and anxiety associated with his medical condition and is looking for ways to cope with these negative emotions. The patient has a good understanding of the English language and lives within an hour of the participating hospital. He does not have severe depression, current suicidal ideation, substance abuse, or impaired cognitive function. The patient is interested in participating in a mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) program to manage his stress and anxiety symptoms.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been diagnosed with keratoconus with progressive worsening of his symptoms. He experiences frequent changes in his eyeglasses and contact lenses prescriptions. He has no previous history of refractive surgery or collagen cross-linking treatment. He has no complaints of eye pain, redness, or discharge. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in both eyes. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals thinning of the cornea, Vogt's striae, and Fleischer's ring. Pentacam imaging shows an asymmetric bowtie pattern with high keratometry value (K-max=55D) and high pachymetry value (500 microns). He is interested in participating in clinical research to help improve understanding and treatment of keratoconus.

72 F with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presents to her primary care physician with complaints of fatigue, loss of appetite, and difficulty sleeping. She reports feeling "down" for several weeks and has experienced a decrease in energy level, interest in activities, and motivation. She has no suicidal ideation or psychotic symptoms. Her primary care physician diagnoses her with major depression and prescribes escitalopram. Despite some improvement, her symptoms persist over the next several months. She is referred to a specialist who diagnoses her with vascular depression, given her history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and recommends adding nimodipine to her treatment regimen. She is eligible for this clinical trial, as she meets the inclusion criteria, including having a DSM-IV diagnosis of major depression and cerebrovascular disease risk factors, such as hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is willing and able to swallow oral medication and has a family member who is willing to participate as a source of corroborating information. She speaks English and has adequate hearing capacity. She does not meet the exclusion criteria, such as having a history of epilepsy or allergy to study medication. She agrees to participate in the study and is randomized to receive nimodipine in addition to her antidepressant medication. Over the course of the study, she attends weekly and monthly study visits, undergoes cognitive and physical tests, and has an EKG performed at specified intervals. After 8 months, her use of medication is lowered and then ended, and she attends three weekly study visits.

A 65-year-old man with a history of heavy alcohol consumption presents with jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal discomfort. The patient reports weight loss of 10 pounds in the past month, loss of appetite, and occasional nausea. Laboratory testing reveals elevated bilirubin (total bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL), elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase levels. CT scan shows a mass in the hilar region of the liver, and biopsy confirms cholangiocarcinoma. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is possible, and the patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is otherwise in good general condition (ECOG 0-1) with no significant history of bleeding or clotting disorders, and no evidence of cardiopulmonary deterioration.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and loss of appetite for the past few months. Imaging studies have shown a mass in his liver, which was later confirmed to be hepatocellular carcinoma by biopsy. The patient is considered a candidate for surgery to remove the tumor, and he has agreed to participate in this clinical trial to help advance liver cancer research. He has no known history of other cancers, and his hemoglobin level is within the normal range. He is not currently pregnant or attempting to become pregnant. The patient has not had a recent biopsy or intervention to remove the tumor. He is willing to have blood samples collected at several time points before and after his surgery to help researchers develop a new blood test for detecting liver cancer recurrence or progression.

Pt is a 32yo F with a BMI of 32. She has a history of recurrent miscarriage (3 consecutive pregnancy losses) in the first trimester. She has not undergone any fertility treatments and has been trying to conceive naturally for the past 2 years. She reports no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. The patient has agreed to participate in the study after being informed of the potential risks and having signed the informed consent form.

A 42-year-old male patient with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) has been receiving dialysis treatment for the last 6 months. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of inflammatory, hepatic, or respiratory diseases. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He will be randomized into either the control group or the tested group, and will receive either standard therapy or alpha-lipoic acid (thiotacid R) in addition to his standard therapy. The patient will be followed up during the study for treatment tolerability and will undergo laboratory examinations at baseline and after 3 months of treatment.

The patient is a newborn baby boy who was diagnosed with congenital heart disease during prenatal ultrasound. His parents are both in their early thirties and have no family history of heart disease. The baby was delivered via C-section at 38 weeks and weighed 3.2 kg. He was immediately transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit for further evaluation and management. Cardiac evaluation revealed a complex congenital heart defect requiring surgical repair. The baby will undergo surgery at Children's Medical Center Dallas and will be eligible to participate in the study. The parents have been fully informed about the study and have consented to their child's participation. The baby will undergo pre-operative head ultrasound to determine resistive indices and Doppler flow of the middle cerebral artery. A multi-source-detector near infrared spectroscopy device will be placed on the baby's scalp to collect data about regional tissue oxygenation and blood flow during surgery. Post-operative head ultrasound will be performed within 4 hours to determine resistive indices and Doppler flow. A third head ultrasound will be performed within 48 hours of discharge to screen for periventricular leukomalacia. In addition, the baby will be evaluated by a trained pediatric neuropsychologist at 12 months of age, and will have the option to provide a DNA sample for genetic testing. The baby will be followed up for a total of 6 years, from enrollment to the final neurocognitive assessment.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with COPD for the past 7 years. He is a retired construction worker and has a 50 pack-year history of smoking. He quit smoking 2 years ago after being diagnosed with COPD. He is currently using inhaled bronchodilator and corticosteroid. He has a history of hypertension, well-controlled with medication. He reports that he experiences shortness of breath during daily activities such as walking or climbing stairs. He has not had any exacerbations for the past 4 weeks. He is able to walk for approximately 5 minutes before experiencing significant shortness of breath. His oxygen saturation during rest is 92% on room air. He has no history of neuromuscular or cardiovascular conditions that limit test performance. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a history of obesity-related comorbidities including hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 42 kg/m2 and has been experiencing symptoms of micronutrient deficiency such as anemia, hair loss, and brittle nails. She is not on any medication for her obesity or comorbidities. The patient has agreed to participate in a prospective study evaluating micronutrients in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. The study will investigate the value of zinc to copper ratio as a possible biomarker of trace elements imbalance and correlate it with lipocalin 2 (Lcn2) with respect to anthropometric measurements and other metabolic biomarkers. The patient will undergo preoperative and 9-month postoperative evaluations including measurement of BMI, waist circumference, complete blood count, and biochemical biomarkers such as fasting blood glucose, lipid profile, serum iron and ferritin, serum Ceruloplasmin, Zn and Cu levels, CRP, serum insulin, serum leptin, and lipocalin-2 (Lcn2). The patient does not have any gastroesophageal reflux and is not experiencing any hormonal disturbances such as hypothyroidism or Cushing's syndrome.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and chest pain. He has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but he is not taking any medications for these conditions. He has no history of lung disease or immunodeficiency. Upon physical examination, the patient is found to be tachypneic and hypoxic, with an oxygen saturation of 85% on room air. He is subsequently intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. The patient is evaluated within 24 hours of intubation and is expected to remain mechanically ventilated for at least 48 hours after the first study procedure. The patient consents (or a surrogate consents if the patient is unconscious or has an altered mental status) to participate in the study.

A 42-year-old man who works as a construction worker fell from a ladder and fractured his right hand 6 weeks ago. He underwent surgery to repair the fracture and has since been experiencing sensitivity and pain in the affected hand. He is right-handed and the injury has made it difficult for him to perform his work duties. He has been taking oral pain medication, but it only provides temporary relief. He has been referred to participate in this clinical trial by his physician, and he is interested in exploring new treatment options for his condition. He is in good overall health and has no history of cardiac or vascular disease. He is willing to participate in the trial and follow the instructions for exclusive focus on somatosensory rehabilitation for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for more than 30 years and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He has no history of any other chronic diseases, and his lung function test showed that he is a suitable candidate for surgery. The tumor is staged as IIB, and there is no involvement of mediastinal lymph nodes. The patient is currently considering his treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the best course of treatment. He is aware of the potential risks and benefits of neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is willing to be randomized between receiving 3 courses of Carboplatin plus Paclitaxel or no chemotherapy before surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past year. She describes her pain as a constant dull ache that intensifies when she stands or walks for extended periods. She has tried various pain medications and physical therapy, but her symptoms persist. She is currently employed as an administrative assistant and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She reports feeling frustrated and limited by her pain, which is affecting her ability to perform her job and engage in leisure activities. She has regular access to the internet and is interested in trying new self-help interventions to manage her pain. She has no history of cancer or other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the trial.

The patient is a pregnant woman in her third trimester who resides in a rural area in Limpopo, South Africa. She is 24 years old, has completed secondary education, and lives with her husband and their two children, ages 1 and 3. The family obtains their drinking water from a nearby river, which is often contaminated with dirt and debris. The woman is concerned about the quality of the water and wants to ensure that her children have access to clean drinking water to prevent illnesses and stunting. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will test the effectiveness of two point-of-use water treatment technologies to improve clean drinking water access and reduce enteropathogen burden among children in her community. She is willing to be randomized to receive either a silver-impregnated ceramic disk, a water filter, the safe-storage water container alone, or no intervention to help researchers determine which technology is most effective. She understands that her children will be followed every three months for 2 years to assess height, weight, and pathogen burden in stool samples, and cognitive assessments will be completed at 2, 5, and 7 years of follow-up. She hopes that participating in this trial will not only benefit her family but also contribute to improving child health in low-resource settings.

55 yo F with a history of hypertension, obesity (BMI 33 kg/m²), and dyslipidemia. She presents with exertional dyspnea and fatigue, and was recently diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (PH-HFpEF) based on right heart catheterization (RHC) with a mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) of 28 mmHg, pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) of 15 mmHg, and transpulmonary gradient (TPG) of 13 mmHg. The patient also has a fasting triglyceride level of 178 mg/dL and low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) level of 38 mg/dL. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study with confirmed diagnosis of PH-HFpEF, three or more features of metabolic syndrome, and no contraindication to metformin use. She is not currently taking metformin or any other medication for PH-HFpEF. She is a non-smoker and has no history of major cardiovascular events or procedures within the past 6 weeks. She has no severe valvular disease or other medical condition that would prevent her from participating in the study. Her eGFR is 63 mL/min/1.73 m². She has not received an investigational product or participated in a drug research study within the past 15 days. She has been on a stable dose of PDE5i for the past 6 months.

The patient is a 3-month-old male infant who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of respiratory infection. He was born full-term via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and his birth weight was 3.5 kg. He received all routine vaccinations and has no significant medical history. His parents report that he has been coughing, sneezing, and having difficulty breathing for the past 3 days. He has also been experiencing fever of 101°F. On physical examination, the infant is alert and responsive, but appears to be in mild respiratory distress with tachypnea and nasal flaring. Lung auscultation reveals bilateral coarse crackles. Nasopharyngeal aspiration (NPA) was performed for microbiological diagnosis. The infant was diagnosed with symptomatic respiratory infection and was enrolled in the clinical trial. The parents of the infant have given their consent to participate in the study.

The study is seeking adult volunteers aged 21-50 who work full-time (5 consecutive days M-F) and have a self-reported regular sleep schedule with sleep duration of more than 5 hours and up to 6.5 hours. The study is also looking for individuals who regularly use an alarm clock during the workweek and have a regular time in bed of no more than 7 hours. Candidates must have a self-reported sleep latency of no more than 30 minutes and wake after sleep onset of no more than 30 minutes. Eligible participants must be able to read, write, and speak English and provide written informed consent prior to admission. Exclusion criteria include participation in another interventional study in the past 30 days, major controlled or uncontrolled medical conditions, current use or use of within the past month of a prescription or over-the-counter sleep medication or stimulant, and pregnancy. Individuals with a diagnosis of sleep disorders, excessive alcohol intake, planned air travel, or travel across more than one time zone one month prior to and or during the anticipated period of the study with PowerSleep device use are also excluded.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 35, making her obese. She leads a sedentary lifestyle and seldom engages in any physical activity. She has high cholesterol levels but does not have any other systemic diseases or conditions, such as hypertension, diabetes, or cardiovascular disease. She is interested in finding ways to improve her health and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of interval training on muscle mass and strength in obese adults. She is available to commit to a 12-week training program that involves three sessions per week.

The patient is a 62-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer. He had been treated with several androgen targeted therapies with no significant response. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive a new treatment for his condition. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial including documented castration resistant prostate cancer, documented PSCA+ tumor expression, and progression of disease as evidenced by rising PSA or radiographic evidence of new metastatic foci. The patient has not had prior chemotherapy with cabazitaxel or docetaxel, but if he had, at least 2 weeks must have elapsed prior to leukapheresis. The patient has no known contraindications to leukapheresis, steroids or tocilizumab. The patient's total serum bilirubin, AST, ALT, and creatinine clearance are all within normal limits. The patient has a cardiac function and left ventricular ejection fraction within normal limits. The patient agrees to use acceptable birth control methods throughout the study therapy and for 3 months after the final dose of study treatment. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria for the trial including clinically significant arrhythmia, optic neuritis or other immunologic or inflammatory disease affecting the central nervous system, bleeding disorders, history of stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 6 months, active infection, active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection, HIV infection, or any other condition that would contraindicate the subject's participation in the clinical study due to safety concerns with clinical study procedures.

A 45-year-old male with a below-the-knee amputation due to a traumatic injury sustained from an accident. He has been using a prosthetic for the last three months and has been experiencing skin irritation and breakdown at the stump site. He has no history of keloid formation or autoimmune conditions affecting the skin. He is a non-smoker and is not currently on any chronic immunosuppressive therapies. He has no history of bleeding disorders, infections, or necrotic tissue on any stump ulcers. He is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, biopsy/injection procedures, wound care instructions, treatment plan, and other study procedures for the duration of the study. He is able to comprehend the informed consent document and has provided consent for participation.

A 15-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with stage IV high-risk rhabdomyosarcoma (alveolar subtype) involving the right maxilla, nasal cavity, and orbit. He received 9 cycles of chemotherapy including vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide, followed by ifosfamide and etoposide, and radiation therapy to the primary site and metastatic sites. However, his disease progressed after the therapy. His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with amlodipine 5 mg/day. He has no known drug allergies. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. His family history is negative for cancer. He has a performance status of 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. His cardiac ejection fraction is 55% and creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min/1.73 m². His bilirubin level is 2.5 mg/dL. His diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 72% predicted. He has not undergone previous stem cell transplantation. He has an unrelated umbilical cord blood donor who is a 4/6 HLA match and KIR-mismatched for one HLA-C group. His cord blood specimen has 2.5 x 10^7 nucleated cells/kg patient ideal body weight.

This is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking and a diagnosis of localized lung bulla. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain, and a chest CT scan confirmed the presence of the bulla. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1 and an ASA score of 2. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has the ability to sign informed consent. He has a heart ejection fraction (EF) of 60 and a BMI of 23 kg/m^2. The patient has no history of tuberculosis or other diseases that could cause pleural adhesion or more pleural effusion.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction for the past 8 months. He has been in a stable heterosexual relationship for the past 2 years. He has been diagnosed with dyslipidemia and has been taking a stable dose of a statin medication for the past 6 months. He has not initiated any additional therapy to treat his dyslipidemia. The patient has an International Index of Erectile Function - Erectile Function domain score of 20, indicating moderate erectile dysfunction. He does not have a history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or life-threatening arrhythmia in the past 6 months, and is not on nitrate therapy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of flexible dosing with vardenafil for the treatment of his erectile dysfunction.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who suddenly experienced a severe headache, weakness on the right side of his body, and difficulty speaking. His wife immediately called for emergency medical assistance, and he was transported to the hospital where a CT scan was performed, revealing no evidence of hemorrhage. The patient was diagnosed with an acute ischemic stroke and his National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was measured at 14. His medical history includes high blood pressure and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He has never had a stroke before, and he is not currently taking any anticoagulant medication. The patient arrived at the hospital within 5 hours of symptom onset. He is willing to participate in the FRALYSE clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with malignant melanoma three years ago. He has undergone several surgeries and radiation therapy in the past, with limited success. Recently, he received treatment with an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody but did not respond well. He has measurable disease, and at least one injectable tumor lesion that has not been irradiated or has been irradiated but with disease progression documented at the site subsequent to radiation therapy. He is currently in good health and has a life expectancy of at least three months as per the investigator. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. His performance status according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) is 0. His lab results show normal serum albumin, ANC, platelet count, and prothrombin. His bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are within the normal range. He has signed informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has not received prior treatment with an adenovirus-based gene therapy and is not currently receiving any concurrent treatment that would interfere with the effect mechanisms of atezolizumab and LOAd703. He is not currently taking any medications that are prohibited during the study period, and he agrees to use acceptable highly effective contraceptive methods during the study period. He has no history of severe allergic anaphylactic reactions to chimeric human or humanized antibodies, or fusion proteins, and no known hypersensitivity to CHO cell products or any component of the atezolizumab formulation.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease who has been scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. He has an ejection fraction greater than 40% and only mild mitral regurgitation. He has no other valvular involvement. He is not hemodynamically unstable and is not intubated or sedated. He is not an emergency patient from the cath lab. He does not have any other significant medical history or comorbidities.

A 56-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer (stage IV) 2 years ago. She has been treated with two lines of chemotherapy and is now starting nab-paclitaxel as her third line of treatment. She is HER2-negative according to the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) and Anatomical Pathology (CAP) criteria. She has no underlying medical or psychological disorders that would compromise her ability to give informed consent for the study. She is married and has three grown children. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She exercises regularly and enjoys hiking and yoga. She has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to any medication. She is not currently taking any other medications.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety for the past 6 months, including difficulty concentrating, feeling on edge, and muscle tension. She is currently not physically active and does not regularly practice yoga or mind-body activities. The patient has a smartphone and is willing to wear a Fitbit to track her physical activity for one week prior to the study intervention. She is capable of performing moderate intensity movements such as sitting, standing, kicking, pulling, pushing, bending her elbows, bending her body forward, bending her knees, lying down and getting up. She is not pregnant and has no serious chronic medical conditions or psychiatric and/or neurological disorders that would preclude her from participating. The patient is willing to be randomized into one of the three conditions and undergo cognitive and psychosocial assessments at baseline and post-intervention.

The patient is a 52-year-old post-menopausal woman who recently experienced vaginal dryness and discomfort during intercourse. She has been previously treated with Ainara® vaginal gel in a clinical trial and is interested in participating in a follow-up study to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of the medical device. She is not pregnant and has not had a menstrual period in over a year. Her body mass index is within the range of 18.5 to 36 kg/m2. She is willing to use only lubricated condoms or a spiral as contraceptive methods during the study period. She has no history of malignancy or genital bleeding, and has not used estrogen vaginal treatment or systemic estrogen therapy for at least 6 months before the study. She has no major medical conditions that would compromise participation in the study or lead to hospitalization during the study. She has no acute or chronic infectious diseases and no history of psychiatric illness or drug or alcohol abuse. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and provide written informed consent prior to participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with haemophilia A with an inhibitor titre of >5 BU/ml. He has been experiencing frequent bleedings and has been treated with both recombinant activated Factor VIIa concentrate (rFVIIa) and activated prothrombin complex concentrate (APCC) in the past. The patient does not have any other significant medical conditions and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of localized prostate cancer, diagnosed through biopsy with a Gleason score of 6. The cancer is in its early stages, and the patient has chosen to manage it through active surveillance. He is otherwise healthy and free of significant co-morbidities. His PSA level has been consistently low, and he has not undergone any previous treatment for prostate cancer. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 0 and has signed a written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He is able to swallow the soft gelatin capsule form of the drug, which is approximately 6mm long. His prostate cancer is clinically localized (T1-2, NX or N0, MX or M0), and he meets the voiding requirements with an IPSS score of 15 and Qmax < 15 cc/s. He has adequate hematopoietic and hepatobiliary function and is willing to use an effective double barrier method of birth control during the study and for 30 days after the last administration of OMN54. The patient has not undergone any previous surgical intervention for BPH and has no history of other malignancies, except for adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer. He is not currently experiencing active uncontrolled infection or concurrent uncontrolled hypertension. He has no history of congestive heart failure, hepatic disease, or renal disease. He is not refractory to nausea and vomiting, nor does he have any chronic gastrointestinal diseases or significant bowel resection that would preclude adequate absorption. The patient is not known to be hypersensitive to any of the three botanical constituents of Aneustat or any of the plants belonging to the Ganodermataceae family, Labiatae or Lamiaceae families, or Aneustat excipients. He is not currently undergoing concurrent administration or exposure within 30 days of investigational drugs and devices, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or immunotherapy.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who underwent laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery two years ago. She has regained more than 15% of her minimum weight following the surgery and is experiencing discomfort and pain due to the dilatation of the anastomosis. She is seeking treatment to control her weight and improve her quality of life. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is currently controlled with medication. She has no history of liver disease, psychiatric disorders, or neoplasia. She is not pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant within the next 12 months. She does not have any allergies to anesthetic compounds. The patient understands the study procedures and has signed the informed written consent form. She is willing and able to complete all stages of the study.

A 30 year old woman with a history of anxiety and depression came to the clinic seeking help to improve her mood and emotional well-being. She has been experiencing mild to moderate symptoms of anxiety and depression for the past year and has been on antidepressants for six months. She owns a smartphone and is able to read and understand English. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve her gratitude and decrease her symptoms of anxiety and depression. Her PHQ-9 score is 7 and GAD-7 score is 3. She is not planning to initiate any new program that could increase her positive affect during the study period. Her medication dose has been stable for the past three months.

A 42-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection for the past 2 years. He is HBeAg negative and has been on nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) treatment for the past 24 months. His HBsAg levels are greater than 100 IU/mL. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and is in good health. He has no history of hepatitis A, C, D or E virus infection, HIV-1 or HIV-2 infection, or liver disease of non-HBV etiology. He has not shown any signs of hepatic decompensation, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He does not have any significant laboratory abnormalities or cardiac disease. He has not taken any therapies disallowed per protocol. He is willing to use highly effective contraceptive measures during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, diagnosed 1 year ago. He has a history of hepatic encephalopathy which has been stabilized with lactulose and rifaximin. His MELD score is 18. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 6 months. He has no evidence of varices on recent upper endoscopy, and he is on primary prophylaxis with propranolol. He reports decreased exercise tolerance in the past few months and is no longer able to maintain his previous level of physical activity. He denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or lower extremity edema. His medications include lactulose, rifaximin, propranolol, and furosemide. He has no known allergies. He is a former smoker and quit 10 years ago. He denies any alcohol or drug use. He lives alone and is retired. He is willing to participate in the study and able to comply with study requirements.

A 14-month-old female child was brought to a nutritional program in Burkina Faso by her mother, who reported that the child had been experiencing poor appetite, lethargy, and frequent diarrhea for the past two weeks. The child's weight was measured at 6.8 kg, and her height was 69 cm. The child's mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) was 110 mm, indicating severe acute malnutrition (SAM). The child did not have any nutritional edema. The mother reported that the child had not received any antibiotics in the past 7 days and did not have any known allergies to macrolides/azalides. The child was able to eat ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) during a feeding test. The child's medical history was unremarkable, and there were no signs of congenital abnormalities or chronic debilitating illness that could interfere with the treatment of SAM. The mother provided consent for the child to participate in the 8-week study. The child was randomized to receive a single dose of oral azithromycin along with RUTF as part of the outpatient treatment for SAM. The child will be followed up at weekly clinic visits over the 8-week study period to monitor nutritional recovery and any adverse events.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who sustained a spinal cord injury in a car accident two years ago resulting in partial upper limb impairment in both arms. He reports difficulty in performing everyday tasks such as dressing, grooming, and feeding himself. He has been undergoing traditional motor, sensory, and cognitive rehabilitation therapy with some improvement, but still experiences significant limitations in his daily activities. He is interested in participating in the RePlay clinical trial to further improve his upper limb function. He speaks English fluently and is able to follow instructions. He has no emotional disability that would interfere with participation.

The patient is a 55 year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is preparing for a renal transplant. He has a history of hypertension and has been on antihypertensive medication for the past 10 years. He also has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes. He has been on dialysis for the past year and his last echocardiogram and stress test were done 6 months ago, which showed no abnormalities. He has no other significant medical history, and is currently not taking any medications other than his antihypertensive medication. He is willing to participate in the study and follow all study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) based on the revised El Escorial score criteria. He has been experiencing muscle weakness and fasciculations in his arms and legs for the past year, which have progressively worsened. He has difficulty with daily activities such as dressing and grooming, and he now requires assistance with these tasks. The patient is currently being followed in the competence center of Brest Universitary Hospital. He has no history of venous thromboembolism or other neurodegenerative diseases. The patient has provided consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the association between venous disease thromboembolic and ALS.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl who has been undergoing orthodontic treatment to correct her malocclusion for the past two years. She wears fixed appliances and has been experiencing some difficulty with maintaining good oral hygiene. She has noticed the appearance of white spot lesions on her teeth and is concerned about the potential impact on her dental health and appearance.
