She has no history of significant dental problems and is generally in good health. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her physical examination and laboratory studies are unremarkable. She has been advised to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a Casein Phosphopeptide-amorphous Calcium Phosphate (CPP-ACP) paste on plaque, gingivitis, and white spot lesions. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her oral health and prevent further damage to her teeth.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with lung cancer, confirmed by biopsy. He is a former smoker and has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He has undergone radiation therapy and chemotherapy, but the tumor did not respond adequately. His PET scan demonstrated a hypermetabolic lung mass, measuring 3.5 cm. He has no significant medical or surgical history other than his lung cancer. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. His lab results showed hemoglobin of 13.5 g/dL, platelets of 250,000/mm³, and a white blood cell count of 7,500/mm³. His liver function tests are within normal limits. His kidney function tests showed creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL and creatinine clearance of 75 mL/min/1.73 m². His ionized calcium, magnesium, and phosphorus levels are normal. He is willing to undergo two tumor biopsies and is willing to practice birth control during and for two months after treatment.

A 10-year-old boy was referred to the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia for a clinically indicated Voiding Cystourethrography (VCUG) examination due to a history of recurrent urinary tract infections. He has no known allergies to any medications or food. He is in good health, and is not currently taking any medications. His parents have agreed to allow him to participate in the contrast enhanced Voiding Urosonography (ceVUS) examination as part of this clinical trial. The boy's parents have consented to his participation and he has given his assent. The boy will not require sedation for either the VCUG or ceVUS examinations.

The patient is a 28 year-old woman who has been using the ENG-implant for contraception for the past 3 months. She has been experiencing prolonged and frequent bleeding episodes for the past month, lasting for more than 7 days at a time. She is sexually active and has one partner. She has no known allergies and takes no medications. She has regular menstrual cycles prior to implant use and no history of abnormal uterine bleeding. She has not been pregnant or given birth in the past 6 months, and is not currently breastfeeding. She is fluent in English and has a cellphone that is capable of receiving and responding to daily text or email messages. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to continue using the implant for at least 6 months.

A 9 year old girl with intellectual disability and multiple congenital anomalies including cardiac defects, cleft palate, and limb abnormalities was born to non-consanguineous parents. She has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has difficulty with feeding due to her cleft palate. She has been seen by multiple specialists, but her molecular diagnosis remains unclear. Her parents are healthy and have no history of genetic disorders. They have consented to participate in the GENOME FIRST APPROACH project for trio analysis.

57 yo woman with a medical history significant for oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy, confirmed by genetic testing with a PABPN1 gene mutation, and ptosis of the right upper eyelid. The patient has undergone previous surgical interventions for ptosis with unsatisfactory results. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of ptosis to muscular dystrophy oculopharyngeal by myoblast autologous graft. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to undergo a muscle biopsy of a healthy muscle for cell amplification to be used in the transplantation procedure. The patient is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the experimental treatment and is willing to follow-up with the study for up to 3 years. The patient is not pregnant nor lactating and is committed to using suitable contraception during the study.

56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is scheduled for coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath upon exertion for the past few months. His cardiac catheterization revealed significant blockages in his coronary arteries, requiring CABG surgery. The patient has no known bleeding disorders and is not taking any anticoagulant medications. He has no history of liver or kidney disease, and his pre-operative laboratory values are within normal limits. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial examining the effect on blood loss of topical and intravenous tranexamic acid in cardiac surgery patients. He will receive either pericardial lavage with 2 gr tranexamic acid in 200 ml normothermic saline solution, pericardial lavage with 200 ml normothermic saline solution without TA, or no pericardial lavage as part of the control group. The study aims to determine whether the addition of topical tranexamic acid reduces post-operative blood loss by 25% in patients scheduled for cardiac surgery on cardiopulmonary bypass, receiving intravenous tranexamic acid.

A 55-year-old female patient with a history of hypertension and no prior history of cardiac disease presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe headache and vomiting. A CT scan reveals a subarachnoid hemorrhage. The patient is admitted to the neurosurgical ICU for management of the hemorrhage. During her hospitalization, she develops cardiac complications including atrial fibrillation and myocardial infarction. She is treated with anticoagulation and cardiac medications. After her condition stabilizes, she is approached for enrollment in the clinical trial studying the impact of cardiac complications on outcomes of patients after subarachnoid hemorrhage. She meets the inclusion criteria and agrees to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy young adult with no significant medical history or chronic illnesses. The patient is not currently taking any medications, except for occasional over-the-counter allergy medication. The patient is not pregnant and agrees to avoid pregnancy during the study duration. The patient does not use caffeine or nicotine. The study aims to investigate the differences in how dietary fats are converted to energy and how this affects fat oxidation and energy intake. The patient will be randomly assigned to either a control formula diet or a high oleic acid formula diet, and will be monitored for body composition changes before and after each diet. The patient will undergo indirect calorimetry in the fed and fasting state to measure the rate of fat oxidation and energy expenditure. The study is seeking healthy young adults between the ages of 18-35 years who are not on continuous medication.

52F with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. The patient has been experiencing numbness and tingling sensations in both feet for the past 2 months. Upon examination, the patient was diagnosed with diabetic foot with a grade 2 ulcer on the right foot. The patient is currently being treated with antibiotics and wound dressings. The patient has no history of amputation, retinopathy, nephropathy or neuropathy. The patient's current medications include metformin, glipizide, and lisinopril. The patient has a history of smoking for 10 years and quit 5 years ago. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has completed high school and currently works as a cashier. The patient has no known psychological conditions and is able to provide informed consent. The patient has no visual or hearing impairments and is able to answer questionnaires. The patient is willing to participate in the study and attend the Multidisciplinary Diabetic Foot Consultation.

45 year-old male with a history of dyspnea on exertion and fatigue presents with worsening symptoms over the past few months. He reports difficulty climbing stairs, and has had to cut back on his exercise routine. Physical examination reveals an elevated jugular venous pressure, a loud P2 on cardiac auscultation, and lower extremity edema. Echocardiography confirms the presence of right ventricular enlargement and elevated pulmonary artery pressures. Cardiac catheterization shows a mean pulmonary artery pressure greater than 25 mm Hg and a pulmonary vascular resistance greater than 3 Wood units. The patient is diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and started on PAH-specific therapy. He is approached to participate in a clinical trial testing a new imaging modality for detecting pulmonary vascular remodeling in PAH using positron emission tomography (PET)-CT scanning with [89Zr]-bevacizumab. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and agrees to participate.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman diagnosed with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) by the Curacao criteria. She has a history of pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs) that were treated with embolotherapy. She has undergone chest CT scans for surveillance of PAVMs after embolotherapy. The patient is now being considered for participation in a clinical trial that will evaluate whether graded transthoracic contrast echocardiography (TTCE) can accurately predict PAVM size and amenability to treatment in patients who have undergone PAVM embolization. The study requires the patient to be within the age range of 18-89 years old and have a prior diagnosis of one or more PAVMs treated by embolotherapy. The patient should have had a chest CT performed within the Penn system for surveillance of PAVMs after embolotherapy. The patient should not have a known PAVM recurrence on the most recent chest CT with feeding artery size amenable to repeat embolotherapy or a known history of intracardiac shunt or discovery of intracardiac shunt during transthoracic contrast echocardiography.

A 2-week-old male newborn is referred to the centre for repair of a complete unilateral cleft lip and palate malformation. The baby was born at term via spontaneous vaginal delivery, with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. The baby has no significant medical history and is currently being breastfed. Physical examination reveals a complete cleft on the left side of the lip extending into the nostril and a cleft in the soft and hard palate. The baby is otherwise healthy and developmentally appropriate for age. There is no history of consanguinity, genetic disorders or congenital anomalies in the family history. The baby has not undergone any presurgical orthopaedics other than passive palatal plate. There is no history of previous lip/ palate repair. The parents have provided informed consent for the baby to undergo the current surgical method for repair of the cleft lip and palate malformation.

A 32-year-old right-handed man with a history of alcohol addiction is seeking help to overcome his addiction. He has been sober for three months and is motivated to participate in clinical research. He has no other psychiatric disorders except for alcohol dependence. He has no severe illnesses or metal implants. He is not currently taking any medications, including psychotropic substances. He is fluent in English and has no issues with claustrophobia. He is not pregnant.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing frequent painful urination with cloudy urine and an unpleasant odor for the past three days. She has no history of urinary tract infections but has been sexually active with a new partner. She has no known anatomical or functional abnormalities of the urinary tract, and no history of immunosuppression, diabetes or serious comorbidities. She has not been on any antibiotic treatment in the past four weeks. She is interested in participating in the Noroxin Efficacy and Safety Trial.

This is a 46-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of breast cancer. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment and is experiencing chemotherapy-related anemia. She has a baseline hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL which is below the normal range. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities without difficulty. She has no history of active second cancer except for adequately treated skin cancer and in situ (pre-invasive) cervical cancer. The patient has no history of deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), cardiovascular accident (CVA), transient ischemic attack (TIA), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), or other arterial thrombosis. She is not taking any specifically excluded concomitant medications or therapies, including prophylactic anticoagulation therapy for recurrence of prior thrombovascular event (TVE). The patient is expected to receive at least 12 weeks of chemotherapy after enrollment into the study. She will participate in the study for up to 32 weeks, which includes a 2-week screening period to determine eligibility, a 26-week treatment period, and a 4-week follow-up period to have end-of-study assessments performed.

The patient is a 78 year-old man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who is not currently on dialysis. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, for which he has been taking medications for the last 10 years. He has never smoked and only drinks alcohol socially. He lives alone and is able to take care of himself with some difficulty due to arthritis. He has not yet made a decision about starting dialysis and is interested in participating in a study that may help him better understand his options and make an informed decision. He speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent.

A 62 year old male patient is scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery due to severe coronary artery disease. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy. His preoperative hematocrit and platelet count are within normal ranges. He has not taken any GPIIb/IIIa antagonists within 48 hours of surgery. He is a non-smoker and has

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing numbness, tingling, and pain in her right hand for the past few months. The symptoms have been gradually worsening, and she has difficulty with fine motor tasks, such as typing and buttoning her clothes. She was diagnosed with moderate carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) based on abnormal median sensory latency with prolongation of the distal motor latency. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. She has no history of diabetes, thyroid disease, wrist fracture, or any connective tissue disease. She is willing to practice effective contraception during the study period. She is willing to follow the protocol requirements and attend routine follow-up visits. She has not participated in any other investigational drug or device study within the last 30 days prior to the baseline visit. She is a candidate for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 28-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a traumatic brain injury. He was hospitalized for several days in the intensive care unit and subsequently transferred to a rehabilitation hospital for further care. He has been experiencing confusion, disorientation, and restlessness since the injury. His cognitive function has been impaired, and he has difficulty staying alert during the day and sleeping at night. He has also shown psychotic-like symptoms, including hallucinations and delusions. The patient is responsive and not in a minimally conscious state. He has no history of seizure disorder or psychiatric hospitalization. The patient is expected to require at least two more weeks of hospitalization for neurorehabilitation.

A 35-year-old woman has been experiencing severe menstrual cramps and heavy bleeding for the past year. She has been trying to conceive for the past six months, but has been unsuccessful. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her menstrual cycle is regular and lasts five days. She has not had any previous surgeries. She has no known allergies. She is fluent in English and understands the purpose of the study. She has given written consent to participate in the study.

47-year-old woman with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and abnormal uterine bleeding. She was diagnosed with a benign polyp during a diagnostic hysteroscopy. She is interested in an outpatient hysteroscopic polypectomy but is unsure about which method to choose. She has no history of malignancy and is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial. Past Medical History: Hypertension, Hypercholesterolemia.

The patient is a 28 year old African-American female who is currently 26 weeks pregnant. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a college graduate and works as a teacher. She is married and has two children. She has never smoked or used drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her pregnancy has been uneventful so far, but she has a family history of high blood pressure. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help contribute to the understanding of preeclampsia and its potential impact on race.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital for a coronary artery bypass graft surgery due to chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medications. He is a retired accountant and is married with two children. He is a non-smoker and doesn't use any drugs or alcohol. His labs show a serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL, which is above the normal range. His baseline creatinine was 1.2 mg/dL. He developed oliguria and was started on renal replacement therapy due to acute kidney injury after the surgery. He has no history of end-stage renal disease, dialysis, or kidney transplantation. He has not signed any DNR or "do not escalate care" orders. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of pre-diabetes. He has a family history of diabetes and has struggled with weight management for the past few years. His BMI is 31. He has not been diagnosed with any other significant medical conditions and is able to perform daily activities without difficulty. He has not undergone any major surgeries and does not have any metal implants. He is willing to comply with the study schedule and procedures. He does not have any food allergies or intolerances. He does not have any chronic gastrointestinal disorders or history of colectomy or malabsorptive bariatric surgery. He is not taking any insulin or hypoglycemic medications. He does not have any major genetic immune dysfunction or acquired immune deficiencies due to infections. He has not undergone chemotherapy or any immunosuppressive medications. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not participated in any other clinical studies. He is able to understand the study's purpose, significance, and consequences and make decisions accordingly. He is not claustrophobic and is able to undergo MRI testing.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who were employed at the Mayak nuclear production plant in Ozyorsk, Russia between 1948-1972 in the nuclear reactor, radiochemical production plant, or plutonium production plant, and have remained local residents. The study is investigating the relationship between genetic differences and the development of chromosomal abnormalities in individuals who were exposed to higher radiation doses than those received by their counterparts in other countries. Participants must have estimates of their external and internal radiation exposures available and have remained cancer-free at the time of enrollment. The study involves providing a blood sample for genetic studies and answering a questionnaire about demographic information, family health history, history of benign tumors, and history of smoking and alcohol consumption. The study is seeking to recruit approximately 350 individuals for the exposed population. A comparison group will also be included, consisting of current and former workers in the auxiliary plants at the Mayak facility who were employed from 1948-1972, have remained local residents, and have estimates of their external gamma dose. Individuals selected for the comparison group will be frequency-matched according to age and gender to the exposed worker population.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has no known allergies and takes no medications. She has never received the influenza vaccine before. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses oral contraceptives. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, substance abuse, cancer, excessive daytime sleepiness, or narcolepsy. She has no temperature or acute symptoms on the day of vaccination. She has no history of anaphylactic-type reactions to egg consumption or previous influenza vaccines. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has access to a consistent means of telephone contact. She has not received any other vaccines within the past 14 days and does not plan to receive any other vaccines during the study period.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of sinusitis for the past 10 days. She reports having a headache that is located mainly at the front of her head, as well as nasal congestion and a persistent cough. She denies having any fever or chills, but reports feeling fatigued and having difficulty sleeping due to the discomfort of her symptoms. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Her physical exam reveals tenderness over the maxillary sinuses and clear rhinorrhea. Her vital signs are within normal limits. An X-ray shows opacification in the maxillary sinuses. A culture material is obtained by sinus puncture and sent for Gram stain, quantitative culture and susceptibility testing prior to initiation of antimicrobial therapy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

The patient is a 60-year-old French-speaking woman with no significant medical history. She does not have any chronic severe disease and is not currently pregnant. She is interested in participating in the PPS3 study and has given written consent for genetic analysis. She is willing to undergo an extensive clinical examination, including a 2-hour holter ECG, a carotid doppler echo tracking, and a step test. She is aware that the study will follow up her cardiovascular morbidity and mortality for at least 10 years. She has no objections to genetic analysis and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 53-year-old male who was diagnosed with HBV-related liver cirrhosis five years ago. He received antiviral therapy and has been compliant with it ever since. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it regularly. He has never had any respiratory diseases or heart problems. He smokes five cigarettes a day but does not drink alcohol. He recently had an endoscopy that showed the presence of esophageal and gastric varices and red signs. He is currently Child-Pugh <10 and meld <29. The patient has not taken any antibiotics, prebiotics, probiotics, or proton pump inhibitors in the past two weeks. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with a BMI of 31 kg/m2. He has a history of elevated blood glucose levels with impaired glucose tolerance, confirmed by a 2-hour plasma glucose level of 150 mg/dL. He has no history of diabetes or any other significant medical condition. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his time sitting in front of a computer. He does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly. He exercises occasionally but not regularly. He has not participated in a weight-reduction program or had significant weight changes in the past 6 months. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 beats per minute. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities, except for a slightly elevated liver enzyme level, which was not more than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal range. He is willing to provide informed consent and comply with the study protocol.

68-year-old male with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years, currently being treated with lisinopril 10mg once daily. He also suffers from osteoarthritis of the knee and takes ibuprofen 400mg twice daily for pain relief. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high despite the medication, and his physician suspects that the ibuprofen may be contributing to this. The patient is willing to participate in a study to determine the effects of different NSAIDs on blood pressure control in hypertensive patients with osteoarthritis.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with advanced-stage ovarian cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and bloating. She has no history of cancer in her family and no known genetic mutations. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and now has viable residual tumors. She is willing to participate in the study and provide tissue samples for genomic profiling. She has no contraindications for immunohistochemistry or targeted capture sequencing. Her medical history includes hypertension, controlled with medication, and she is not currently taking part in any other clinical trials. She is fully aware of the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 43-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of advanced non-small cell lung cancer. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past and has also received radiation therapy. He has no history of liver or kidney disease and has normal blood counts. He is currently not taking any other medications or supplements. He has mild dyspnea on exertion but is otherwise able to perform activities of daily living without difficulty. He is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has not received any anti-cancer therapy for 21 days before the study drug administration. He has no untreated brain or meningeal metastases, but he has a stable treated brain metastasis without any cavitation or hemorrhage. He has not received any CYP3A inhibitors, CYP1A2 inhibitors, CYP2C19 inhibitors, or CYP2C8 substrates within 21 days prior to initial study drug administration. He is not currently enrolled in another clinical trial.

A 55-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. She underwent a lumpectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, which showed no evidence of lymph node metastasis. Her tumor was ER/PR-positive and HER2-negative. The patient has no significant medical history, she is a non-smoker and non-drinker, and does not use illicit drugs. She has two children and is post-menopausal. The patient was referred for adjuvant radiotherapy with helical tomotherapy at Institut Claudius Regaud (Toulouse, France). She is willing to participate in the REBECCA study and has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the study. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The patient has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with severe aplastic anemia. She has undergone one treatment course of immunosuppression with a regimen containing antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine but has not responded to it. Her platelet count is less than 30,000/micro L and she requires at least 4 platelet transfusions in the 8 weeks prior to study entry. Her neutrophil count is less than 500/micro L and her hemoglobin level is less than 9.0 g/dL, requiring at least 4 units of PRBCs in the eight weeks prior to study entry. She weighs 60 kg and has no history of allergies or medication use. Her family history is negative for severe aplastic anemia, but her mother has a history of autoimmune disease. She lives with her husband and two children. Her lab results are remarkable for creatinine level of 1.8 mg/dL, direct bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, SGOT of 80 U/L and SGPT of 75 U/L. Her cytogenetics performed within 12 weeks of study entry did not show evidence of a clonal disorder. Her overall health is stable and she is willing to take oral contraceptives or refrain from pregnancy if of childbearing potential.

13-year-old male diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes 2 years ago. He struggles with keeping up with his daily blood glucose checks and adjusting insulin dosages accordingly. His parents have been supportive but sometimes forgetful of reminding him to complete these tasks. The family currently uses Verizon as their mobile carrier and have access to a working cell phone. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in the study and have expressed interest in receiving weekly text message reminders to help with self-management of Type 1 Diabetes.

56 yo M with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presents to the emergency department with sudden cardiac arrest. Bystander CPR was initiated and the patient was defibrillated twice prior to return of spontaneous circulation. On arrival to the hospital, the patient remains comatose and is started on therapeutic hypothermia with a target temperature of 33°C. The patient is admitted to the intensive care unit for further management. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - No prior history of cardiac disease

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was diagnosed with moderate Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) at the age of 3. He has difficulty communicating and socializing with others, and struggles with repetitive behaviors. The patient has been on a stable psychiatric medication regimen for the past 6 months. Fragile X testing was performed and the results were negative. The patient has no known genetic syndrome and does not have any coexisting psychiatric conditions such as depression, bipolar disorder, or Tourette syndrome. He has no history of metabolic disorders or abnormal thyroid function. He has not received prior cell therapy, IVIG, or immunosuppressive therapy. The patient and his parent/guardian are English-speaking and able to travel to Duke University for the study appointments. They are willing to participate in all study-related assessments, including protocol follow-up. The patient's parent/guardian has provided consent for him to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old Hispanic male with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 4 for 2 years. He is currently taking a stable dose of vitamin D for the last 2 months. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. He had a kidney transplant 10 years ago, which was functioning well until 2 years ago when his kidney function started to decline. He is not on dialysis but is being monitored by his nephrologist every 3 months. He has no history of fractures or bone diseases other than osteoporosis or renal osteodystrophy. He has never been treated with bisphosphonates or any other anti-osteoporosis therapies. He has no history of leukemia, multiple myeloma, lymphoma, amyloid or paraproteinemias. He does not have any congenital or acquired collagen of bone diseases. He is able to walk and has no lower extremity amputations. He weighs 200 lbs. He is interested in participating in this study to help find a non-invasive method to detect abnormal bone protein content and to contribute to the research on bone disorders in chronic kidney disease.

52-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory failure secondary to pneumonia. The patient had a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a prior myocardial infarction. Upon admission, the patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated. Arterial blood lactates levels were measured at admission and every 6 hours during the first day, and at H48. The patient's lactate levels were found to be elevated, with a peak level of 4.5 mmol/L. The patient's SOFA score was 12, IGS II was 47, and APACHE II was 22. The patient was treated with antibiotics, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor support. Despite aggressive treatment, the patient's condition continued to deteriorate, and he eventually passed away on day 3 of his ICU stay. The patient's lactate levels were found to be a strong predictor of mortality, with a sensitivity of 85% and a specificity of 75%. This study aims to evaluate the accuracy of blood lactates levels in predicting mortality in ICU patients and compare it to classic prognostic scores such as SOFA score, IGS II, and APACHE II.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who underwent orthotopic heart transplantation six months ago due to ischemic cardiomyopathy. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, furosemide, aspirin, and atorvastatin. He has a history of smoking but quit ten years ago. He is retired and lives with his wife. He reports occasional chest discomfort and shortness of breath with exertion. He has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 45 ml/min. He is fluent in French and able to read and understand written information in French. He has no history of allergic reactions or side effects after gadolinium infusion. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. He has undergone endomyocardial biopsies within the past 72 hours, which did not show any signs of acute cellular rejection grade 1R or antibodies mediated rejection pAMR1.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids. She is scheduled for a robotic-assisted laparoscopic myomectomy, a minimally invasive surgical procedure using a robot to remove uterine fibroids. The patient has no history of chronic pain or medication use for pain. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no neuromuscular disease or legal protection. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, which is within the normal range. She has been informed about the study during her anesthesia consultation and has consented to participate. The study aims to evaluate the performance of the NoL index in discriminating nociceptive from non-nociceptive stimuli during her robotic surgery. The anesthesia procedure will be the same for all patients, as part of the usual care in the department. The NoL monitor will be added for the purpose of this study, but the results will be hidden from all physicians. All settings will be left to the physician in charge. The patient's data will be extracted on a dedicated USB key at the end of the surgical procedure before transfer to the recovery room. The data will be safely stored before analysis.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of hypertension controlled with medication. He was recently diagnosed with a meningioma after experiencing headaches and vision disturbances. He is scheduled for an elective craniotomy to remove the tumor. He has no history of diabetes or other medical conditions. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He lives with his wife and three children.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has had type 2 diabetes for 10 years. She presents to her primary care physician's office for a routine follow-up appointment. She reports that she has been taking her diabetes medications inconsistently over the past several months due to forgetfulness and stress at work. Her current medications include metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg once daily. Her last A1c value was 8.5% and her LDL cholesterol was 120 mg/dL. She reports that she tries to eat a healthy diet and exercises regularly but has been struggling to maintain her routine due to work demands. Her current BMI is 31.2. She has medical and pharmacy coverage through her employer-sponsored health plan, and there have been no lapses in her coverage over the past year. She has not participated in any disease management programs in the past.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who suffered a traumatic spinal cord injury following a motor vehicle accident. The injury occurred at the level of T6 and resulted in a motor incomplete SCI with a total lower extremity motor score of 3. He underwent posterior laminectomy with stabilization/fusion surgery within 48 hours of injury. The patient is currently admitted to Vancouver General Hospital and is able to communicate in English. He has no associated traumatic conditions and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the Optical Monitoring with Near-Infrared Spectroscopy for Spinal Cord Injury Trial as he hopes that this novel NIRS sensor technology can aid in his recovery and improve his future quality of life.

Pt is a 35yo F presenting with an adnexal mass and experiencing pelvic pain for the past 6 months. Pelvic examination revealed a palpable mass, and transvaginal ultrasound showed a 5cm cystic lesion in the right ovary. The patient has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She has no allergies and has never had surgery before. After discussing the options of laparoscopic surgery for removal of the cyst, the patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial comparing transumbilical versus transvaginal specimen retrieval at minilaparoscopy. She meets the inclusion criteria and does not have the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 52-year-old female patient who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. She has not received any previous treatment for her cancer. She is currently being considered for immunotherapy as a first-line treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on determining the therapeutic landscape and the reason for immunotherapy cessation. She is willing to undergo detailed follow-up as per the protocol and has signed the informed consent form. She has no history of prior malignant tumors except for non-melanoma skin cancer that was cured more than 5 years ago.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after presenting with abdominal pain and jaundice. He has no prior history of liver disease or cancer. Imaging studies revealed a single tumor in the right lobe of his liver that measures 6 cm in diameter with no evidence of portal invasion or extrahepatic spread. He is currently being evaluated for liver transplantation but does not meet the Milancriteria. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and Child-Pugh Class B liver function. He has no previous history of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or transarterial embolization. He has a discrete hepatic artery feeding the tumor with vessel diameter greater than 1.5 mm. He is eligible for the Bridge to Orthotopic Liver Transplantation (OLT) - Surefire Precision vs Endhole Embolization With DEBTACE clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria.

57-year-old female with a history of hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) presented to the nephrology clinic for follow-up. She reports occasional lower back pain and mild generalized weakness, but denies any other symptoms. Her blood pressure is currently well-controlled on medication. Labs reveal a creatinine level of 2.2 mg/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 40 mL/min/1.73m². The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the relationship between oxalate and urate metabolism and CKD progression. She has not taken antibiotics or lipid- or urate-lowering therapy in the past 3 months, and has not been hospitalized in the preceding 3 months. She has not been diagnosed with anemia, systemic or malignant diseases, acute inflammation processes, or active hepatitis. She has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past 6 months and has a well-functioning peritoneal access. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to provide informed consent to participate.

I apologize, but based on the information provided, it seems that this clinical trial does not require a patient description as it is a study on attitudes towards patients with chronic low back pain and does not involve patients directly. Instead, it involves medical and physiotherapy students at two Scottish universities.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of vaginal itching and discharge for the past week. She has not had any prior vaginal infections or sexually transmitted infections. She is sexually active with one partner and uses condoms as a form of contraception. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has not been pregnant nor is she currently breastfeeding. She gives her informed consent to participate in the study. Her KOH preparation test is positive for budding yeast and/or pseudohyphae and her wet mount test is negative for T. vaginalis and clue cells. She has no other medical conditions that could interfere with the study.

A 36-year-old female presents with a history of non-constipated irritable bowel syndrome symptoms for the past 6 months. She experiences frequent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea. She has tried various over-the-counter medications without much relief. She has no known allergies and has never been treated with antibiotics or probiotics in the last 4 weeks. She is willing to maintain a symptom diary during the treatment period. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and there is no clinical suspicion of organic disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of Bacillus clausii administration on irritable bowel syndrome symptoms.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has recently undergone a lumpectomy for stage T1, ER-positive, invasive ductal carcinoma in her left breast. The surgical margins were clear, and axillary lymph nodes were negative. She has no prior history of breast cancer or breast or thoracic radiotherapy. She has completed chemotherapy and is currently on adjuvant endocrine therapy. Her performance status is good with no active collagen-vascular disease or Paget's disease of the breast. She has no history of synchronous bilateral breast cancer, and her tumor size is less than 3 cm in maximum diameter.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl with genetically confirmed Noonan syndrome. She presents to the clinic with short stature and decreased growth velocity. She has a history of heart defects and developmental delay. Her past medical history is significant for recurrent ear infections and tonsillitis. She is currently not on any growth-promoting therapies such as recombinant human Growth Hormone (GH) or IGF-1 treatment. She is not taking any medications for her condition. Her family history is negative for Noonan syndrome or any other genetic disorders. She has no known allergies. The patient and her parents have provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of colorectal cancer. She was initially diagnosed 2 years ago and underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. Surveillance imaging revealed the development of multiple liver metastases with involvement of both lobes of the liver. A total of 6 liver lesions have been identified, with the largest measuring 4 cm in diameter. Imaging also shows that one of the metastases is in close proximity to the first order portal branch. The patient has been evaluated by a surgical oncologist who recommends a two-stage hepatectomy with portal vein embolization. However, the patient is hesitant to undergo two separate surgeries and is interested in alternative options. She meets the inclusion criteria for the one-stage surgical procedure being studied in this clinical trial and is interested in participating. The patient has good performance status with no significant comorbidities and is willing to undergo surgery as part of the study protocol.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 35. She has been struggling with obesity for several years and has tried various diets and exercise programs with little success. She is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco or nicotine products. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. She has normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels, and no abnormality in serum albumin, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, calcium, and phosphorus. She is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception throughout the study period. She has no history of bipolar disorder, psychosis, suicidal attempt or postpartum depression, and her score for depression and anxiety is less than 11 on the Hospital Anxiety and Depression (HAD) Scale. She has no history of diabetes mellitus, seizure disorder or predisposition to seizures, bulimia or anorexia nervosa, and has not undergone surgical intervention for obesity. She has not used any anorectic agents, weight loss agents, dietary supplements to promote muscle building, enhance mood, or reduce appetite, adrenergic blockers, beta blockers, anti-psychotic agents, clonidine, theophylline, cimetidine, oral corticosteroids, anti-depressant, topiramate, Depo-Provera®, smoking cessation agents, and frequent, known use of opioid or opioid-like analgesics. She has not participated in any previous clinical trial conducted by Orexigen Therapeutics. She is willing and able to comply with all required study procedures and schedule and to give written informed consent.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy participants who are in good general health and have a body weight of at least 50 kg and a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18 to 32 kg/m2. Participants should have a negative SARS-CoV-2 serology test and should not have a history or presence of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, hematological, or neurological disorders capable of significantly altering the absorption, metabolism, or elimination of drugs or interfering with the interpretation of data. Participants with any malignancy within the past 5 years, except for basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 3 years, are excluded from the study. Additionally, participants with a history of a severe allergic reaction before enrollment that has a reasonable risk of recurrence during the study or any chronic or clinically significant medical condition that would jeopardize their safety or rights, including type 1 diabetes mellitus, chronic hepatitis, drug or alcohol abuse, asthma (except for childhood asthma), autoimmune disease, psychiatric disorders, or heart disease, are also excluded. Participants who have received a licensed or investigational biologic agent, such as monoclonal antibodies, within 3 months or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) before the randomization are not eligible to participate.

Maria is a healthy 28-year-old woman who works as a graphic designer. She has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. Maria is a non-smoker and has never used any tobacco products. She has no dietary restrictions and is willing to consume a high calorie, high-fat breakfast and other standard meals provided during the domiciled periods of the study. Maria is willing to abstain from alcohol beginning 48 hours prior to each admission until discharge from the study center at the end of each domiciled period. She is able to take and retain oral medications. If sexually active and of childbearing potential, Maria agrees to use two effective methods of contraception beginning at the Screening Visit until 60 days following the last dose of study drug. Maria has a negative serum pregnancy test and provides written informed consent after the nature of the study has been explained and prior to the commencement of any study procedures. Her baseline B lymphocyte count is >150 cells/µL (0.15 x109 cells/L). Maria has no prior or ongoing medical conditions, medical history, physical findings, or laboratory abnormality that, in the Investigator's opinion, could adversely affect the safety of the participant or make it unlikely that the participant will comply with the protocol or complete the study per protocol. She is not taking any medications or supplements and has no known allergies. Maria is willing to attend the necessary visits to the study center and to be domiciled overnight where required.

A 50-year-old female presents with a history of knee pain and stiffness, especially in the morning, for the past 6 months. She has been previously diagnosed with Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) and has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief with limited effect. She has not taken any Chinese medicine for the treatment of KOA in the last 7 days. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. Her joint function and X-ray stage are in the I-III range. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a newborn, between 37 weeks gestation and 72 hours of age, born to an HIV-infected woman. The infant is not breastfed and is not born to a woman who received either passive or active immunotherapy during pregnancy. The patient is not born to a woman who is hepatitis B surface antigen positive. The infant is currently receiving AZT at study entry, except for those enrolled in ACTG 076. The parent or guardian has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements. The infant does not have any documented or suspected serious bacterial infection, metabolic illness, or other immediate life-threatening conditions.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with primary hypercholesterolemia who has been receiving atorvastatin at a stable dose of 20mg for the past 6 weeks. He has been compliant with his medication and has been following a cholesterol-lowering diet. His LDL-C level was found to be 120 mg/dL (3.10 mmol/L) during his last check-up. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of alirocumab in lowering his LDL-C levels. He has no history of type 1 or type 2 diabetes and his triglyceride levels are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraceptive methods during the study period.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing unexplained physical symptoms, such as chronic pain, fatigue, and gastrointestinal issues. She has been referred to the Clinic for Functional Disorders at Helsinki University hospital (HUS) by her primary care physician. She is married with two children and works part-time as a teacher. She has a history of anxiety and depression and has been taking antidepressants for the past two years. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but she drinks alcohol occasionally. Her physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any abnormalities. She speaks Finnish fluently and is able to fill out the required forms for the study. She has given her informed consent to be enrolled in the study and is willing to complete the PROMs questionnaires at the designated time points.

Unfortunately, as this is an observational post-market registry and not a clinical trial, there are no patients to recruit or describe. This registry is designed to gather data from patients who have already undergone a procedure using a Medtronic Coronary and Structural Heart product. The aim is to collect data on real-world device safety and performance, as well as to identify any new device-related complications or emerging risks. Patients who meet the inclusion criteria and are treated at participating hospitals will be enrolled in the registry and followed according to routine care practices.

Patient is a 27-year-old female who underwent bunionectomy surgery 2 days ago. She has a history of occasional headaches but has no other medical conditions. She reports having moderate to severe pain at the surgical site, rated 7 out of 10 on a pain scale. She has not participated in any other studies involving investigational drugs or devices in the past 30 days.

A 9-year-old male child, diagnosed with ADHD, is referred to the clinic by his school counselor. He has never been treated for ADHD before. He has no other known medical conditions and is up to date with his vaccinations. He is not taking any other medication or supplements. His parents report that he has difficulty paying attention in class and completing tasks. He is also impulsive and frequently interrupts others while they are speaking. The child is willing to participate in the study, and his parents provide informed consent.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman of Mediterranean origin is seeking prenatal care. She is in her first trimester of pregnancy and has no significant medical history. She has no history of anemia or any genetic disorders in her family. She reports that her husband's family has a history of thalassemia. Her obstetrician orders a blood count and Hgb electrophoresis analysis to screen for thalassemia. The results are obtained from the H2 automatic counter and indicate hypochromic microcytic anemia. However, the RBC number and the RDW are normal, which raises suspicion for β thalassemia carrier status. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial and will be further evaluated for β thalassemia carrier status using the algorithm SVM (support vector machine) to determine a reliable formula for diagnosis.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastases to the liver and bones. He has an ECOG performance score of 1 and has completed first-line chemotherapy with carboplatin and pemetrexed. The patient has been on palliative care and has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. CT scan of the chest shows a 3 cm mass in the left lower lobe of the lung, which is accessible by EBUS. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer a potential therapeutic option. He has no known allergies to cisplatin or its derivatives and has adequate organ and marrow function. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo the EBUS-TBNI procedure.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago. She has been taking levodopa and carbidopa combination therapy for the past 2 years, but she has recently experienced worsening of her motor symptoms including tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia. Her neurologist has recommended adding a non-ergot dopamine agonist, piribedil (CLARIUM), to her treatment regimen. The patient has never taken piribedil before and is willing to participate in the post marketing surveillance study to monitor the safety and efficacy of the drug. She is in good general health, with no significant medical history, and is able to give informed consent.

A 65-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and was diagnosed with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He has been using home oxygen therapy for the past year. The patient reports a persistent cough and shortness of breath with exertion. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has a 20-pack-year smoking history and quit smoking 5 years ago. His last pulmonary function tests showed an FEV1 of 1.2 L (40% predicted), an FVC of 2.8 L (70% predicted), and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.43. His arterial blood gas analysis shows a PaCO2 of 57 mmHg and a PaO2 of 58 mmHg. He is clinically stable and has not used NPPV for at least 1 hour. His BMI is 28 kg/m².

A 48-year-old man with a long-standing history of hypertension presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up. He has been on antihypertensive medications for over 5 years, including a diuretic, but his blood pressure is still not well controlled. He reports occasional headaches and shortness of breath on exertion. The patient does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He has no history of diabetes, dyslipidemia, or cardiovascular disease. His family history is unremarkable. On examination, his blood pressure is 160/95 mmHg. His heart rate is regular, and his lungs are clear. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, and there is no peripheral edema. Laboratory tests including renal function, electrolytes, and lipid profile are within normal limits. He is diagnosed with resistant hypertension and is referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating renal denervation as a treatment option. After further evaluation, he meets the inclusion criteria of the trial and is randomized to receive CRD or a sham procedure. He will be followed up for 6 months to evaluate the effect of the intervention on his blood pressure and other renal, hemodynamic, and hormonal variables.

A 28-year-old female respiratory therapist, who has been working in a hospital for the past 3 years, presents to the clinic after being in contact with COVID-19 patients. She reports that she has been experiencing mild symptoms such as cough and fever for the past few days. She has no known allergies or medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for hydroxychloroquine chemoprophylaxis as she is concerned about her exposure to COVID-19. She provides informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 52-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is currently undergoing her first round of chemotherapy. Her past medical history is only significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume any alcohol. The patient is currently experiencing mild nausea and fatigue as side effects of the chemotherapy. Her physician has ordered a MiCK assay to determine the effectiveness of the chemotherapy drugs being used. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help further research on the effectiveness of the MiCK assay. She understands that her medical records will be reviewed and her physician will be asked to complete a questionnaire about the usefulness of the assay. She is willing to provide her consent for her data to be used in this study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing moderate-to-severe postherpetic neuralgia pain for at least 3 months since the resolution of the skin rash (shingles). He has a BMI between 17 and 36 and has been recording postherpetic neuralgia pain severity on a Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS - 12) "over the past 12 hours" on a 0 - 10 scale with "0" being no pain and "10" being the most severe pain the subject could imagine, each morning and night for three consecutive days prior to the Treatment Visit. He must report a baseline score of 4 or greater on the following Numerical Pain Rating Scale (NPRS-NOW) "How would you rate your pain RIGHT NOW using a zero to ten scale, where zero equals no pain and ten is the worst pain you can imagine" to be eligible for dosing. He is not actively abusing alcohol or drugs and is able to refrain from alcohol for a period beginning 24 hours prior to the treatment visit until the end of the study. He has no scheduled surgical procedures during the period of study duration and has no history of any active serious medical conditions including cancer, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, hematologic, neurologic, or psychiatric disease that would contraindicate study participation. He has not taken a fixed scheduled opioid regimen within 3 days prior to the Treatment Visit and has not used a short-acting "as needed" opioid less than 12 hours prior to dosing or an "as needed" NSAID dose less than 24 hours prior to dosing. He has not applied lidocaine patches or dermal analgesics within 7 days prior to the Treatment Visit and has not received an anesthetic block within two weeks of the Screening Visit or any prior neurolytic nerve block in the area of the PHN pain. He is not taking tricyclic, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) antidepressants for PHN (or for indications other than pain) and the dosage has been changed within 14 days of the Treatment Visit. He is not taking gabapentin (Neurontin), pregabalin (Lyrica), or duloxetine (Cymbalta) and the dosage has been changed within 14 days of the Treatment Visit. He has not taken any medication that is a substrate of the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP2C9 within 4 days of dosing with the study drug or is unwilling to refrain from such medications through the course of study drug treatment. He has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medication within three days prior to the Treatment Visit, or herbal agents or other nutraceutical products within 14 days prior to the Treatment Visit, that in the

A 7-year-old male child was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 2. He has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been hospitalized several times for exacerbations. He is currently on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and takes vitamins A, D, E, and K supplements. His most recent pulmonary function test showed an FEV1 of 70% predicted. His weight-for-age percentile is between the 10th and 50th percentile, and his height-for-age percentile is between the 25th and 50th percentile. He has no known allergies and is compliant with his treatment regimen. He lives with his parents and siblings and attends school regularly. He has no other significant medical history or chronic illnesses. His parents have provided written informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 67-year-old man with a history of wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in the left eye, which was diagnosed 2 years ago. He previously received multiple intravitreal injections of Lucentis® (Ranibizumab) for the left eye, with a positive response. He also has visual impairment due to diabetic macular edema (DME) in the right eye, which was diagnosed 1 year ago. He has not received any intravitreal injections for the right eye. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from receiving Lucentis®. He is willing to participate in an observational study to monitor treatment patterns and receive repeated intravitreal injections of Lucentis® over a 24-month period, including optional OCT monitoring, under real-life conditions. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 72-year-old male who has been diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and has been experiencing a gradual loss of central vision in his left eye. He has no prior history of photodynamic therapy (PDT) or intravitreal triamcinolone treatment. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient reports no other ocular or systemic diseases. Best-corrected visual acuity in the study eye is 20/80. Fundus examination of the study eye shows a subfoveal choroidal neovascular membrane (CNV) with predominantly classic features secondary to AMD. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including frequent follow-up visits, and is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

44-year-old female, complains of chronic constipation for the past 4 years. She reports abdominal pain, bloating, and feeling of incomplete evacuation after bowel movements. She has tried various medications and lifestyle modifications but they were not effective in relieving her symptoms. She has no history of major surgeries or underlying medical conditions. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is unremarkable. She has undergone a dynamic defecography test which has revealed an internal rectal prolapse and rectocele. Her external sphincter is adequate on rectal digital examination. She has been offered the option of participating in the Transtar registry to undergo the Transtar procedure for her ODS. She is willing to participate in the registry and has provided informed consent.

The patient is an adult who has been diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma and has undergone placement of the XEN 45 Gel Stent as a standalone procedure or in combination with phacoemulsification between 1 January 2014 and 1 October 2015. The patient's medical records will be reviewed retrospectively to assess the long-term safety and performance of the XEN 45 Gel Stent. There are no other specific eligibility criteria or exclusion criteria for this study.

A 75-year-old male patient with a history of Alzheimer's disease is admitted to the cognitive and behavioral unit (CBU) of a hospital due to severe behavioral symptoms. The patient has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease for 3 years and has been experiencing episodes of aggression towards his family members and caregivers. He has been prescribed medications for the management of his symptoms, but they have not been effective. The patient's wife is his primary caregiver and is in frequent contact with him. The patient has a Clinical Dementia Rating of 2 and requires assistance with most activities of daily living. He has no history of major medical problems and is currently not taking any medications other than those prescribed for his Alzheimer's disease. The patient is informed about the study and agrees to participate.

There is no patient involvement in this clinical trial as it is evaluating the effectiveness of a medical device, the kneeling stool, for use during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in hospital. The trial is seeking doctors and nurses who work in the emergency department and have American Heart Association Basic Life Support (AHA BLS) provider certification. Participants with heart, wrist, or low back disease, or who are pregnant, are excluded from the trial.

67 year old male with a diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) for 2 years. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, history of myocardial infarction 5 years ago, type 2 diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Current medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin, metformin, and albuterol inhaler as needed. He has experienced increasing shortness of breath with walking and is interested in participating in a study to help improve treatment options for IPF.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy diagnosed with Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) with the R206H ACVR1 mutation. He has previously participated in Clementia's natural history study (NCT02322255). The patient has not experienced any flare-up symptoms within the past 4 weeks, including at the time of enrollment. He is not taking any medications that are strong inhibitors or inducers of cytochrome P450 (CYP450) 3A4 activity or kinase inhibitors such as imatinib. He does not have elevated amylase or lipase levels above the upper limit of normal (ULN) or a history of chronic pancreatitis. The patient's aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase levels are within normal limits. His fasting triglycerides are below 400 mg/dL. The patient's family has agreed to use two highly effective forms of birth control as he is a minor. The patient is able to undergo all study procedures, including low-dose WBCT (excluding head), without sedation. The patient has no significant medical history that would exclude him from participation in the study.

A 55-year-old man who has been experiencing shoulder pain for the past year and has tried non-operative management without significant improvement. He has been referred to the Orthopedic Department for further evaluation. Radiographs show glenohumeral joint osteoarthritis with reduction of joint space and osteophyte formation. The patient has pain at night and during overhead activity, and consumes pain medication regularly. He is able to read trial information in Danish and has given informed consent. He has not had any previous shoulder surgery involving the humeral head or glenoid cavity. He does not have any alcohol or drug abuse problems that can compromise rehabilitation and follow-up appointments. He is able to understand instructions in Danish and can follow the rehabilitation protocol and answer the questionnaires. He does not have brachial plexus palsy and has not had any previous fractures around the shoulder. MRI scan confirms that he does not have a full thickness total tear of one or more of the rotator cuff tendons. CT scan also confirms that he does not have glenoid retroversion ≥ 20° that does not allow glenoid component fixation without bone graft or need an augmented glenoid component.

A 42-year-old male with a history of alcohol and substance abuse and a recent loss of employment. He has been struggling with gambling for the past year, spending more money than he can afford and feeling guilty about it afterward. He also reports having anger issues, often losing his temper with family members and friends. He has no history of major thought disorders, manic episodes, or legal charges/sentencing. He is able to attend 12 one-hour weekly outpatient individual sessions for the treatment.

This is a 9 year-old male with type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 2 years ago. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of diabetic ketoacidosis during the past month. He is compliant with his insulin regimen and checks his blood sugar levels regularly. He has no other chronic diseases that may affect calcium-phosphorus metabolism. He is in Tanner stage 1 for all variables. His parents have provided informed consent for him to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effect of vitamin D supplementation on bone mineral density, serum 25 hydroxyvitamin D levels and hand grip strength in preadolescents with diabetes mellitus type 1. He will be randomized to receive either 500 IU or 1000 IU vitamin D supplementation for 12 months in a double-blind controlled trial. His serum levels of calcium, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and HbA1c will be measured every 3 months in spring, summer, autumn and winter. Bone mineral density will be assessed at the beginning and end of the study, and hand grip strength will be measured every six months.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 120 days ago and received an allogeneic bone marrow transplant from her brother. She has been experiencing fatigue since her transplant and has been struggling to perform her daily activities. She is currently on medication for her high blood pressure and has been advised to maintain a healthy diet and exercise routine. Recently, she has been feeling particularly down and has been experiencing sleep disturbances. Her last physical exam and lab tests showed the following results: A healthy-looking woman, non-icteric, cooperative and alert Weight: 68 kg Height: 165 BP: 130/80 HR: 84/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 5000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 2800/mm3) Plt: 200000 /ml AST: 31 U/L ALT: 41 U/L Alk P: 120 U/L Bill total: 0.9 mg/dl ESR: 80 mm/hr. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to alleviate her fatigue and improve her quality of life.

13F, prepubertal, Tanner stage 1, with a BMI-SDS>-2 and Height-SDS ≥ -2.5, has been referred to the study for evaluation of her growth. The patient reports no chronic or acute illnesses, no history of malignancy, and no known gastrointestinal or neurological disorders. She is not on any medications that may affect her appetite, weight, or growth. Her parents report that she has always been short and lean for her age, and they are concerned about her growth. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent forms. Further evaluations will be done to determine if she meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

Sophie is a 56 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with bladder cancer. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and leads an active lifestyle, regularly participating in yoga and Pilates classes. Her family history is negative for cancer. After discussing treatment options with her urologist, she has decided to undergo a robotic assisted cystectomy with intracorporeal ileal conduit. She has been informed of the possibility of participating in a clinical trial comparing two methods of bowel anastomosis during the surgery. She understands the trial requirements and is willing to participate in the study if deemed eligible.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who recently had a scare with a lump in her breast that turned out to be benign. However, the experience has left her feeling anxious about her breast health and she is interested in participating in breast cancer screening research. She has no personal or family history of breast cancer, but her mother had colon cancer in her 50s. She is a non-smoker, exercises regularly, and follows a healthy diet. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has private health insurance and is willing to comply with study requirements. She is interested in contributing to breast cancer research and hopes to gain peace of mind from participating in this study.

This is a 28 year old African American mother of a 2 year old child living in central Alabama. She is currently enrolled in the First Teacher Home Visiting Program through the Family Guidance Center of Alabama. She is interested in participating in a study focused on healthy habit development to reduce the risk of obesity in herself and her child. She has no significant past medical history and is generally healthy. She is not currently enrolled in a diet and weight loss program and her child has no history of a feeding or eating disorder. She is willing to participate in the study for 12 months and attend monthly home visits with a trained home visitor who will provide a program focused on habit formation and home environment modification conducive to key behaviors relating to obesity prevention. She understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive the standard home visitation program or the standard home visitation program with the HABITS program embedded within it.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing chronic plaque type psoriasis vulgaris for the past 5 years. He has never received any treatment for his psoriasis, but is interested in exploring alternative treatment options. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for Vit D: 18ng/ml (insufficiency) and otherwise healthy. (Ca: 9.8mg/dl, Phosphorus: 3.5mg/dl, PTH: 35pg/ml)

A 30 yo F with a long-standing history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) diagnosed by Rome 4 criteria, experiencing frequent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits. She has tried various medications and dietary modifications but has not found significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the small bowel and its microbiome. She has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgeries and is not currently taking any medications that could alter gastrointestinal function or acidity. She has a BMI of 25 and has not had any recent abdominal or pelvic surgeries or radiotherapy. She has not been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease or diverticular disease and has not experienced any swallowing difficulties. She has two to three bowel movements per week and is willing to follow the required schedule and interventions for the study.

A 55-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of discomfort in her pelvic area. She reports a sensation of pressure and heaviness around her vagina and rectum, as well as difficulty urinating. She has noticed that these symptoms have worsened over the past few months, especially when she has been standing or walking for long periods of time. She has no history of surgery or childbirth, but she is postmenopausal. On pelvic examination, there is a visible bulge in the vaginal wall, and the cervix is low. The patient is diagnosed with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse and is informed about the treatment options. She expresses a preference for conservative management and is willing to try vaginal pessaries. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating. She signs the informed consent and agrees to attend follow-up appointments. She has a negative cervical cytology and no vaginal bleeding of undetermined cause. She is able to return to controls.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate allergic asthma for the past 2 years. He experiences occasional coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. He has never been hospitalized or intubated due to asthma. He has tried multiple inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators but still experiences symptoms. His BMI is 28, BP: 128/80, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is unremarkable. He has no history of anaphylaxis or other lung diseases such as COPD. He is currently not on any other medications for asthma.

This is a 35 year old female who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She was diagnosed with Diminished Ovarian Reserve (DOR) after undergoing several fertility evaluations. She has no history of illicit drug or tobacco use and has not had ovarian surgery within the past 90 days. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of Inofolic Plus® in improving her egg parameters. She has no known allergies to any of the components in the supplement and is willing to take it as directed.

The patient is a 60 year old man who had knee arthrodesis using Wichita Fusion Nail 2 years ago due to severe osteoarthritis. He has been experiencing discomfort and pain in the knee joint and has been advised to undergo removal of the nail. He has no other medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. MRI and X-ray imaging have confirmed the need for removal of Wichita Fusion Nail. He has not had any other kinds of intramedullary nails used for the knee arthrodesis.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with severe obstructive sleep apnea. He is overweight with a BMI of 32 and has a history of high blood pressure. He reports snoring loudly during sleep and experiencing frequent episodes of waking up gasping for air.
