He is compliant with his continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy and reports improvement in his symptoms with its use. He is currently not taking any medication for his sleep apnea. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac conditions. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a computer technician and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the understanding of the relationship between sleep apnea and atrial fibrillation.

The patient is a 25 year old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of uncomplicated acute rhinosinusitis for the past 10 days. She has nasal congestion, facial pain and pressure, postnasal drip, and a cough. She has not received treatment with antibiotics or intranasal corticosteroids for this episode. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any significant medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with study procedures and restrictions and is able to give informed consent. She has not had any history of acute rhinosinusitis within the past 12 weeks or other sinonasal conditions within the past 3 years. She has not used any antibiotics or antiviral medications within the past 30 days or any analgesics or antipyretics within the past 1 day. She has not used corticosteroids or any medications that may affect nasal symptoms within the past 30 days. She does not have any known hypersensitivity or allergy to corticosteroids or any excipients in the product.

A 65-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer came to the clinic complaining of recurrent pain in his lower back and hips. He has a PSA level of 25 ng/mL, which has been rising steadily over the past few months. His previous imaging studies showed new osseous lesions and an increase in measurable soft tissue disease. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has no known allergies to FDHT or FDG. He understands the study and has provided informed consent.

56F with a history of tinnitus in both ears for over a year. The patient reports mild to moderate severity of tinnitus and has been unresponsive to standard tinnitus medication. Pure-tone audiometry testing showed normal results with a threshold of ≤ 25 dB hearing level in all frequencies from 250 to 8000 Hz. Tympanometry, stapedius reflex tests, and otoscopy showed normal middle ear status. The patient has no history of a DSM-IV Axis-I psychiatric disorder, intolerance to TMS, severe personality disorder, or current suicidal ideation. The patient is not on medication that may be a risk factor for seizures, except for occasional use of benzodiazepines at low doses. The patient has no history of epilepsy, seizure, or heat convulsion, and no metallic particles in the head or any implanted devices. The patient is able to communicate adequately with the examiner and has given oral and written consent to participate in the trial. The patient is not pregnant and uses adequate birth control. The patient does not have severe hearing impairment.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who fell while playing on the playground and has a laceration on his forehead that requires stitching. He is accompanied by his mother, who reports that he is very anxious and fearful of needles and medical procedures. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical or surgical history. He has no known allergies or sensitivities to medications. His vital signs are within normal limits for his age. The patient is able to communicate and follow instructions. He has no other injuries requiring medical attention at this time. The treating physician has deemed the laceration repair necessary and predicts that the patient will resist positioning for the procedure. The patient has not had any previous exposure to dexmedetomidine or other sedative medications.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with follicular B-cell lymphoma (grade 2) 3 years ago. He was treated with chemotherapy and achieved a complete remission, but unfortunately, his disease relapsed 6 months ago, and he is now experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. He is married, has 2 children, and works as an accountant. His Karnofsky Performance Status is 80% (ECOG 1). The physical examination is remarkable for the presence of multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and axillary regions. Laboratory tests show an absolute neutrophil count of 1800 cells/dL, platelet count of 80,000 cells/dL, AST of 52 IU/L, ALT of 48 IU/L, total bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dL, and creatinine level of 90 µmol/L. The patient has no active central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and his serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin pregnancy test is negative. He is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study. The patient has a minimum life expectancy of 6 months.

The patient is a 28-year-old German woman who has been experiencing mild depression symptoms and anhedonia. She is interested in participating in a study that monitors her mood over a one-month period. She has access to a suitable device and internet, and is willing and able to complete all study procedures. She works as a freelance writer and spends most of her time working from home. She has no history of mental health disorders other than mild depression. She does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. She is currently not taking any medication for her depression symptoms.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who works as a software engineer. She is generally healthy, with no chronic medical conditions and no history of significant allergies. She has not received any influenza vaccine in the past 6 months and is not planning to receive any other vaccines during the course of the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to become pregnant in the next 30 days. She is interested in participating in this study to help contribute to the development of a new quadrivalent influenza vaccine. She is able to understand and comply with the study procedures and is willing to provide written informed consent. She has no underlying diseases or therapeutic interventions that might adversely affect her immune response.

The patient is a 78-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and severe aortic stenosis. The patient has been experiencing dyspnea on exertion, chest pain, and fatigue for the past few weeks. Echocardiography revealed a mean aortic valve gradient of 43 mmHg, aortic valve area of 0.7 cm2, and left ventricular ejection fraction of 50%. CT angiography revealed a bicuspid aortic valve (Sievers 1) with a severely calcified aortic valve (Agatston score of 3500). The mean aortic annulus diameter was measured to be 19mm. The patient is considered for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) with either Acurate TM or Lotus Edge TM valve. The patient's CT-scan is uploaded to FEops HEARTguide for pre-procedural planning. The Heart Team first decides on the valve type and size, pre-dilatation, post-dilatation, preferred implantation depth, and comfort scale level. The Heart Team then makes a final decision after the simulation of FEops HEARTguide for the final pre-procedural planning. The patient will be enrolled in Cohort A of the study, and the implanted device, size, and depth will be recorded. The follow-up period will be 30 days.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is 36 weeks gestational age. She reports a history of depression and anxiety, which has worsened during her pregnancy. She has feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of interest in daily activities. She scores 14 on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. She has no history of severe pregnancy complications or other medical conditions. She has a BMI of 25 and is classified as ASA II. She has no contraindications to the use of ketamine or s-ketamine. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman has been diagnosed with localized recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma. She had undergone radiotherapy a year ago and was disease-free for 6 months, but now has recurrent T1N0M0 according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th staging. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 80 and no other malignant tumors. She is mentally stable and has no history of heart disease or pulmonary dysfunction. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who underwent surgery for a tibial non-union fracture using AUGMENT® Injectable Bone Graft as part of the BMTI-2009-01 protocol. He has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption but is otherwise healthy. He underwent regular follow-up evaluations and radiologic tests during the first 2 years after surgery and showed good healing progress. He has not experienced any adverse events related to the AUGMENT® Injectable Bone Graft. He is now being asked to return for long-term follow-up evaluations and radiologic tests at or after the 5-year mark since his original surgery. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and make himself available for the planned follow-up evaluations and radiologic tests.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 4 years. He has been on metformin alone for the past year but has not achieved his target HbA1c level of 8%. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, hepatic dysfunction, or renal insufficiency. He has a BMI of 29 and is currently on a 2000 calorie per day diet with regular exercise. He is not currently taking any other medications for his diabetes.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who is in her third trimester. She has been experiencing high blood pressure (160/95 mmHg) and her urine tests show proteinuria with a dipstick value of 3+. She was diagnosed with pre-eclampsia by her obstetrician. She has no history of underlying renal disease and her serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to assess the benefit of L-arginine, the precursor to nitric oxide (NO), to blood pressure and recovery of the glomerular lesion in pre-eclampsia. She will be randomized to receive either L-arginine or placebo until day 10 post-partum. Her blood pressure, glomerular filtration rate and proteinuria will be assessed on the third and tenth days postpartum by inulin clearance and albumin-to-creatinine (A/C) ratio. NO, cyclic guanosine 3'5' monophosphate (cGMP), endothelin-1 (ET) and asymmetric-dimethyl-arginine (ADMA) and arginine levels will be assayed prior to delivery, on the third and tenth day postpartum. She will be closely monitored to ensure her safety and health throughout the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who has been scheduled for an elective lower segment cesarean section. She has no known medical conditions and is generally healthy. She is at 38 weeks' gestation and has been experiencing some anxiety about the upcoming surgery. She speaks English fluently and has given consent for the operation. She has no history of cognitive impairment or previous cerebrovascular events.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on assessing perceptions, confidence, uptake, and trust in potential COVID-19 vaccines among healthcare providers and at-risk population subgroups. The study aims to develop and test COVID-19 vaccine messaging that boosts vaccine confidence and trust among these key at-risk subgroups.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently received a diagnosis of invasive breast cancer following a biopsy. She is currently planning to undergo surgery at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will use Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scans to monitor how well her tumor responds to treatment. She understands that she will need to undergo at least one PET/CT scan and possibly two, and that the scans will require her to lie on a table for about an hour. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, as her tumor is operable (T1-T4) and she does not have a history of severe renal disease or a prior breast cancer in the study breast within the last five years.

A 45-year-old male presented with a history of snoring and witnessed apnea episodes during sleep. He has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and has been treated with a mandibular advancement device (MAD). However, he still experiences apnea episodes when sleeping in a supine position. His medical history is significant for hypertension and obesity, with a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m². He is not a smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is currently not using any medication for his OSA. He has been referred to the Antwerp University Hospital to participate in a clinical trial comparing MAD therapy with sleep positional trainer (SPT) and the combination of MAD and SPT in patients with positional sleep apnea using MAD. He will undergo two consecutive polysomnographies (PSGs) in randomized order: one PSG with SPT, one PSG with SPT and MAD. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, with a supine dependent OSA after MAD Therapy and an AHI supine of 30/h and AHI non-supine of 5/h on PSG with MAD in situ. His BMI has remained unchanged since the baseline PSG. He is excited to participate in the study and hopes to find a solution for his positional sleep apnea.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at a young age. She has been treated with inhaled aztreonam three times daily in a 4 weeks on/off cycle treatment regimen for the past 6 months. She has had chronic colonization with Burkholderia spp. and has had at least two positive microbiological cultures in expectorated sputum within the last 12 months. She is currently seeking to participate in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy of inhaled Alginate oligosaccharide (OligoG) in reducing the microbial burden of Burkholderia spp. in her expectorated sputum samples. She has not had any changes in her underlying therapy or physiotherapy technique or schedule within the last 14 days prior to screening visit. She does not have any history of organ transplantation, lactose intolerance/milk allergy, current malignant disease, or documented/suspected clinically significant alcohol or drug abuse. She is willing to provide sputum samples for microbiological evaluation throughout the study and is able to perform pulmonary function tests according to the ATS/ERS criteria. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She understands and is willing to follow the study instructions and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the clinic by her parents due to a persistent rash on her arms and legs. She has a history of atopic dermatitis and has been treated with corticosteroids in the past for flares. The rash is itchy and red, and the parents report that she scratches it frequently, especially at night. The objective SCORAD score at the time of presentation is 30. She has no fever or other symptoms. Upon examination, the rash is found to be dry and scaly. There are no signs of infection or ulceration. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the benefits of emollients in the management of their daughter's atopic dermatitis.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman diagnosed with preeclampsia at 37 weeks of gestation. She presents with high blood pressure, proteinuria, and mild edema. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies or chronic illnesses. She has not received any analgesic medication during her pregnancy. She is scheduled for an elective caesarian section due to concerns for maternal and fetal health. Her height is 165 cm, weight is 70 kg, and her BMI is 25.8 kg/m2. She has no history of magnesium therapy or chronic pain syndrome. She has no contraindications for central neuraxial block and is willing to undergo regional anesthesia. She is able to communicate effectively and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 26-year-old female who presents with complaints of breast pain and tenderness. She has noticed these symptoms for the past 2 months and they seem to be increasing in intensity. She has no history of breast cancer or any other breast-related disease. Her menstrual cycles are regular and she denies any family history of breast cancer or other breast disorders. Her BMI is 24, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. She has no significant past medical or surgical history. Her laboratory studies are within normal limits. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the consent form.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension who presented to the emergency department with a cough, fever, and shortness of breath for the past 3 days. Chest X-ray shows infiltrate in the left lower lobe, and he is diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia. He has no history of hospitalization or recent antibiotic use. He is able to give written informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. He has no aspiration pneumonia, nosocomial pneumonia, purulent pleurisy, exacerbation of COPD, neutropenia, chronic infection with current antibiotherapy, immunosuppression, active neoplastic disease, organ transplant, pregnancy or HIV diagnosis with a CD4 count <200 cells/μL.

A 56-year-old woman who lives in Southeast Minnesota has been diagnosed with uncontrolled diabetes with a most recent hemoglobin A1c level of 10.5%. She was admitted to the hospital 3 months ago due to a diabetic foot ulcer and has had multiple emergency department visits in the past 6 months due to uncontrolled blood sugar levels. She is currently on metformin and insulin but has difficulty managing her medication regimen and adhering to a healthy diet and exercise routine. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. She lives alone and is community-dwelling. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her diabetes management and prevent future hospitalizations.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). She has a history of smoking and was experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for several months before seeking medical attention. She lives with her husband and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading and gardening in her free time. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is fluent in English and able to provide written informed consent. She plans to receive her cancer treatment at MD Anderson Cancer Center. She has identified her husband as her primary caregiver, who has agreed to participate in the study. She is experiencing significant physical and emotional distress due to her diagnosis and is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how early palliative care consultation can improve her quality of life and manage her symptoms.

A 30-year-old lactating woman of South Asian descent came to the clinic with a history of P. vivax malaria. She has been breastfeeding her infant for the past 2 months without any complications. The patient has no history of G6PD deficiency, and she is not pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to study the pharmacokinetics of primaquine in lactating women and their infants. The patient provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol for the duration of the trial. She has no known hypersensitivity to primaquine and has not taken any medications other than antipyretics in the past 7 days or Chloroquine in the past 2 months. Her hematocrit level is within the normal range, and she has not taken primaquine since her most recent malaria episode. The patient is eager to contribute to malaria research and hopes that this study will help provide more information about the safety of primaquine use during lactation.

A 62-year old retired teacher with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath presents to the hospital for evaluation. The patient states that they have been experiencing chest pain for the past week and that their breathing has become more difficult. They deny any history of heart disease, but do have a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient has never had a coronary angiography before. They have never had any previous surgeries or procedures. The patient is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. They have a family history of heart disease, with their father having a heart attack at the age of 65. On physical examination, the patient is alert and cooperative. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. The patient's ECG does not show any signs of acute ischemia, but the physician is considering further evaluation of the coronary arteries via coronary multislice computed tomography (MSCT) angiography to rule out any potential blockages.

The patient is a 45 year old Hispanic male with a history of type 2 diabetes. He was recently hospitalized due to COVID-19, and his A1c levels have been consistently above 7% in the last 90 days. He speaks both English and Spanish and has access to a cell phone that can receive/send text messages. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his glucose control and reduce his risk of hospital readmission. He lives in the US/Mexico border area and has experienced difficulties accessing diabetes care due to his location and the COVID-19 pandemic. He is motivated to learn more about COVID-19 mitigation strategies and believes that a low-cost digital texting platform could be helpful in managing his diabetes and staying informed about the pandemic.

The patient is a 69-year-old man who fell at home and sustained a displaced femoral neck fracture. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is independent in his daily activities and lives with his wife. He is currently taking blood pressure medication and a daily multivitamin. He has never had surgery before and is hesitant about undergoing a procedure. His BMI is 27.9 and he is a non-smoker. He has good range of motion in his hip joint and no other musculoskeletal issues. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to contribute to research and help improve outcomes for future patients.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. She has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and dizziness due to anemia with hemoglobin levels consistently below 10.0 g/dL. She has not received any erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) within the past 12 weeks and has a transferrin saturation (TSAT) level of 20%. She has not experienced any upper or lower gastrointestinal bleeding within the past 6 months and does not have any systemic hematologic disorders. She has not had any acute myocardial ischemia, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, hospitalization for congestive heart failure, stroke or transient ischemic attack,

A 28-year-old male was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder. He lives alone and works as a freelance graphic designer from home. He has a high school diploma and has no prior experience with mental health treatment. He takes medication as prescribed by his psychiatrist and has no history of substance abuse. He is interested in learning more about self-management interventions for his condition and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He is comfortable using smartphones and has access to a reliable internet connection. He is fluent in English and has no hearing, vision, or motor impairments.

The patient is a 60-year-old female with Type II diabetes, diagnosed 10 years ago. She is scheduled to undergo a 5-hour cardiac bypass surgery under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, both under control with medications. She has no history of diabetes-related complications such as nephropathy, retinopathy or neuropathy. Her Hba1c level is 7.2, and her BMI is 30. She is currently taking oral hypoglycemic agents, metformin and glimepiride, and her most recent fasting glucose level was 120 mg/dL. She has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is alert and oriented, cooperative and able to provide informed consent to participate in the trial. She has been informed of the study objectives and procedures and has agreed to participate.

This is a 35 year-old female with a history of drug addiction who has been stabilized on a daily dose of racemic methadone for the past 6 months. She is not using any other drugs of abuse and has been compliant with her methadone regimen. Her electrocardiogram (ECG) was recently performed and showed a QTc interval of 460 ms, which puts her at risk for fatal arrhythmias. She has no history of serious psychiatric or somatic disease and is not pregnant. She has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to switch from racemic methadone to R-methadone to determine if it will reduce her QTc interval and lower her risk for arrhythmias. She is able to cooperate with observed daily drug intake and understands the informed consent process.

A 16-year-old male with a history of HIV infection for 2 years presents to the clinic with his legal guardian. The patient is aware of his HIV-positive status and has been receiving HAART medication. His viral load is undetectable with a CD4 count of 650 cells/mm³. The patient is able to communicate effectively in English and shows no signs of active homicidality, suicidality or psychosis. He has no history of HIV dementia and has an IQ score above 69. The legal guardian is a 35-year-old female who is fluent in English and has been involved in the patient's medical care since diagnosis. The legal guardian is not experiencing any severe depression and is willing to discuss end-of-life care with the patient. Both the patient and the legal guardian consent to participate in the study. The patient is not in foster care and knows his HIV status.

Patient is a 10-year-old girl with a history of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets (XLH). She has been receiving treatment with large oral doses of phosphate and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, but has been experiencing secondary hyperparathyroidism (HPT) with hypertension and hypercalcemia as side effects of the treatment. The patient has normal serum calcium and creatinine concentrations. She is not hypersensitive to any component of cinacalcet.

50 year-old male with a history of dry eye syndrome for the past 2 years presents with bilateral eye redness, burning sensation, and gritty feeling. He has been using artificial tears regularly for relief but has not seen significant improvement. On examination, the patient has a Lissamine green conjunctival staining sum score of 6 out of 12, and a global symptom score (SANDE) of 45 mm. The patient has a corrected Snellen visual acuity of 20/20 in each eye. He has not used cyclosporine ophthalmic emulsion 0.05% (Restasis) within the past 3 months and has no history of seasonal or perennial allergic conjunctivitis. The patient is not currently using any topical ophthalmic medications and has no active eye disease other than dry eye syndrome. The patient has not undergone corneal transplant or cataract surgery within the past 3 months.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman scheduled for gynecologic surgery in two weeks. She has a history of endometriosis and has been experiencing pelvic pain and discomfort for the past few months. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the lower abdomen and pelvis. Laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient is expected to tolerate oral medication within 12 post-operative hours and will require an indwelling catheter for a minimum of 12 post-operative hours after starting oral medication. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits. She is not pregnant and does not have any contraindications to phenazopyridine HCl.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with severe asthma and is currently taking maintenance medication, including inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists. She has been experiencing asthma symptoms for over a year, including coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, despite using her rescue inhaler regularly. She has a pre-bronchodilator FEV1 of 65% of predicted after medication stabilization during the baseline period, and her PC20 is less than 8mg/ml per methacholine inhalation test using standardized methods. She has had at least one day of asthma symptoms during the 2 weeks of the baseline diary period. She is a non-smoker and is willing to undergo bronchoscopy as required by the study. She has no history of immunosuppressant therapy, insulin-dependent diabetes, or lung cancer. However, she has experienced four or more infections of the lower respiratory tract requiring antibiotics in the past 12 months, and has had four or more asthma exacerbations requiring oral steroid pulses in the past 12 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been suffering from erectile dysfunction for more than 6 months. He has a history of radical prostatectomy and is currently being treated for diabetes. The patient has an IIEF-EF score between 11-22, indicating a moderate to severe erectile dysfunction. The patient is in a monogamous relationship and has a willing and motivated partner who is also willing to participate in the study. The patient is mentally competent, understands all study requirements, and is willing to undergo two minor surgical procedures, including liposuction and injection of autologous SVF into the corpora cavernosa. The patient's medical history does not indicate any contraindications for the study, such as bleeding or clotting disorders, autoimmune disorders, or significant active systemic or localized infections. The patient is willing to limit alcohol intake and eliminate the use of recreational drugs for sexual encounters. The patient is willing to be available for all baseline, treatment, and follow-up examinations required by the protocol.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who works as a dental hygienist. She complains of chronic neck pain that she has been experiencing for the past year. She rates her pain as 8 out of 10 on a pain scale and notes that it interferes with her job and daily activities. She has not had any previous neck or shoulder surgeries, and she does not have any accompanying shoulder problems. She has been prescribed pain medication and physical therapy in the past, but her symptoms persist. She has a score of 12 points on the Neck Disability Index. She is willing to comply with the rehabilitation program and complete the study. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications.

The patient is a 45-year-old Hebrew-speaking woman scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia for cholecystectomy. She has a history of gallstones and has been experiencing intermittent right upper quadrant pain for the past few months. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable and her physical examination is within normal limits. She is currently taking no medications and denies any allergies. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her family history is positive for hypertension in her father. She is working as a teacher and is under moderate stress. She is fluent in Hebrew and able to answer the questionnaire by herself. She has been evaluated by an anesthesiologist one day before the surgery and is scheduled to have the same anesthesiologist perform her anesthesia during the surgery. The duration of the surgery is estimated to be approximately 2 hours.

47-year-old male who sustained a traumatic brain injury 2 years ago in a motor vehicle accident. The patient has been experiencing chronic headaches, dizziness, and balance difficulties since the accident. The patient has not consistently engaged in any physical activity since the accident and has not practiced yoga in the last year. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is able to attend the yoga sessions without any transportation restrictions.

A 55-year-old male presents with a history of recurrent diverticulitis. He reports abdominal pain localized in the left lower quadrant, associated with fever and diarrhea. The patient is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. His medical history includes hypertension, for which he takes losartan 50 mg daily. Physical examination reveals mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant, but no palpable masses or peritoneal signs. Laboratory results show a white blood cell count of 12,000/μL and a C-reactive protein level of 25 mg/L. A computed tomography (CT) scan confirms the presence of sigmoid diverticulitis with a localized abscess. The patient is admitted to the hospital and undergoes intravenous antibiotic therapy and percutaneous drainage of the abscess. After resolution of the acute episode, the patient is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic sigmoid resection with anastomosis. The surgeon plans to use ICG-fluorescence guidance complemented with enhanced reality to evaluate the perfusion of the intestinal tissue before performing the anastomosis. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is eligible to participate. He is informed about the study and consents to participate.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain and discomfort for several months. She underwent an ultrasound and CT scan, which revealed the presence of a solid mass in her pancreas. Her doctor has recommended an endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) to obtain tissue samples for diagnosis. The patient has agreed to participate in the SharkBITE study, which aims to compare the diagnostic performance of two different types of needles, the standard needle and the SharkCore needle, in obtaining tissue samples from solid pancreatic masses. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and meet the eligibility criteria for the study, as she has a solid pancreatic mass and has no contraindications to pancreatic biopsy. She will be observed after the procedure and followed up with a phone call at 7 days to check if she has developed any new symptoms since the procedure. The patient hopes that participating in this study will help improve the diagnostic accuracy of EUS-guided tissue sampling and potentially reduce the need for repeat procedures.

53yo man presents to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He is diagnosed with a ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. He is not taking any medications at the moment. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no contraindications to FD-OCT guidance.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic lower back pain due to lumbar disc herniation. He is overweight with a body mass index of 28 kg/m2 and has no history of diabetes or any other chronic illnesses. He is scheduled to undergo a spinal surgery for discectomy. He is not taking any medications affecting glucose homeostasis. He has no history of cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, auto-immune, or hematological diseases. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has provided informed consent for the study and a dedicated peripheral IV line has been placed for blood sample collection.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy. She has a history of type 2 diabetes for 10 years and has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty reading for the past year. Her ophthalmologist has recommended that she undergo retinal oximetry to measure the oxygen saturation in her retinal vessels using the newly developed Oxymap device. The patient has no other significant medical history and is currently taking metformin to manage her diabetes. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of her condition and potentially benefit from new developments in retinal oximetry technology.

55 year old woman with a history of metastatic colorectal cancer to the liver. She was initially diagnosed with colon cancer 2 years ago and underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX. She was found to have liver metastases shortly after completing adjuvant chemotherapy, and was started on systemic chemotherapy with FOLFIRI and bevacizumab. Despite treatment, her liver metastases have continued to progress, and she is now experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. Imaging studies show that more than 80% of her metastatic disease is confined to the liver, and she has no involvement of the portal vein. She has a performance status of 1, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She has not undergone previous liver embolization, and is not allergic to contrast media. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials, and is affiliated to social security. She has provided written informed consent and is interested in exploring alternative treatment options.

A 62-year old woman was recently diagnosed with marginal zone lymphoma after presenting with fatigue, night sweats, and a lump in her neck. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis. Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is not currently taking any medications. The patient is a retired teacher and lives with her husband. They have two adult children. She enjoys gardening and reading. She has no history of smoking or drug use. The patient's performance status is 1. Her recent laboratory studies showed a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, a platelet count of 120,000/mm3, and a white blood cell count of 6,000/mm3. She has normal liver and kidney function. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help others and potentially improve her own health.

The patient is a 48-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has previously undergone endocrine therapy and cyclin dependent kinase (CDK)4/6 inhibitor treatment, but her condition has progressed. She is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional bone pain. The patient has no history of other serious medical conditions and is willing to undergo mandatory tumor biopsy. She has normal organ function and is able to swallow capsules. She has not received chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer previously. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and is not currently enrolled in any other study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with chronic lower back pain, who has been on opioid therapy for 6 months. He has been taking oxycodone 60mg twice a day. Despite taking stool softeners and increasing fibre intake, he has been experiencing constipation for the past 4 weeks. The patient has no history of allergies, and his family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. He has no significant medical history and does not take any other medications. The patient has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. The patient is married, has two children, and works as a construction worker. He reports feeling bloated and has had difficulty passing bowel movements. He denies any vomiting, nausea or abdominal pain. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His physical examination is unremarkable except for the presence of mild abdominal distension. His lab work is within normal limits, except for a mild elevation in his liver enzymes, which are likely related to his opioid use.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled for a day case arthroscopic shoulder surgery. She has a history of mild asthma but it is currently well controlled with inhalers. She has no other significant medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. Her body mass index is 26 and her weight is 65kg. She has never had a nerve block before and is not allergic to local anaesthetic. She has no opiod tolerance and does not take any medication regularly. She is fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

28-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy with no significant medical history has been referred to the study by her obstetrician. The patient is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She has had three uncomplicated pregnancies in the past, all resulting in healthy full-term infants. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance scientific knowledge in the field of pregnancy complications. She has been informed of the study's requirements and is willing to comply with all necessary procedures and follow-up appointments. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and frequent urination for several months. He has a family history of chronic renal failure and gout, with both his father and uncle being affected by these conditions. His blood tests reveal a low eGFR of 45 ml/min/1.73m2, indicating chronic renal failure. He has not experienced any hematuria or proteinuria, and his blood pressure has been normal. He has not been diagnosed with any other autoimmune or infectious diseases, and he has not been exposed to any medications or toxins that may have caused his renal symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to identify the genetic mutations responsible for hereditary tubulointerstitial nephritis.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic renal anemia and has been receiving maintenance treatment with subcutaneous darbepoetin alfa for the past 8 weeks. Despite this treatment, her hemoglobin levels have been fluctuating and she has been experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath. She has not had any blood transfusions in the past 8 weeks and does not have poorly controlled hypertension or any history of acute or chronic bleeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous C.E.R.A. for the maintenance of hemoglobin levels.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma. She reports experiencing mild abdominal discomfort and bloating for several months, but did not seek medical attention until she noticed blood in her stool. Upon undergoing an upper endoscopy, a biopsy was taken and she was diagnosed with primary gastric MALT lymphoma with no peripheral or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. She has not undergone any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for her gastric lymphoma. She has tested positive for H. pylori infection via histology and rapid urease test, and will undergo further tests to confirm the diagnosis. She has stage IE disease and has no involvement of other organs. The patient has agreed to provide achieved pathologic material for immunohistochemical study and for RT-PCR t(11;18)(q21;q21) determination. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no history of extranodal lymphoma and has not undergone any prior anti-H. pylori therapy. The patient's cardiopulmonary status is stable and allows for repeat endoscopy. The patient is eligible for the study.

A 62-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the clinic complaining of fatigue, swelling in his legs, and shortness of breath. His medical history also includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. Laboratory results show an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 47 mL/min/1.73m2 and a spot urine albumin:creatinine ratio of 56 mg/g. The patient is diagnosed with progressive diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and is being considered for the Patient-Derived Stem Cell Therapy for Diabetic Kidney Disease clinical trial. He meets the inclusion criteria, including being between the ages of 45-75 years old, having an eGFR between 25-55 mL/min/1.73m2 with a decline of 5 mL/min over 18 months or 10 mL/min over 3 years, and a primary cause of kidney disease being diabetes without suspicion of concomitant kidney disease beyond hypertension. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including not having a recent cardiovascular event, not being on anticoagulation therapy requiring heparin bridging for procedures, and not having an active malignancy. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with complaints of occasional headaches and blurred vision. His current medications include metformin and glimepiride. His HbA1c is 8.5% and his fasting plasma glucose level is 190 mg/dl. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg and his BMI is 28 kg/m². The patient has no history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, unstable angina pectoris, or myocardial infarction within the last 6 months prior to study inclusion. His urinary albumin excretion (UACR) is 60 mg/g (early morning spot urine) and his eGFR is 65 ml/min/1.73m² (MDRD Formula). The patient does not have any severe disorders of the gastrointestinal tract or other diseases which interfere with the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of study drugs. He is willing to comply with the protocol and provide written consent for the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian female who has been experiencing fatigue and muscle weakness for the past few months. She has a history of staying indoors due to her work and study schedule and has not been exposed to sunlight for an extended period. She is not currently on any medication or supplements containing vitamin D. Her blood test showed that she has borderline deficiency in vitamin D levels. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in increasing her vitamin D levels.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing hearing loss in her left ear for the past year. She has been diagnosed with a tympanic membrane perforation and is scheduled for myringoplasty surgery at the ENT-department, University hospital of Tromsø. She has no history of chronic secretion or cholesteatoma. Her hearing loss has been affecting her daily life, making it difficult to communicate with others and enjoy social activities. She is fluent in Norwegian and is willing to participate in the study. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who has been diagnosed with aortic valve stenosis. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well-controlled with medications. He presents with symptoms of chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue. Imaging studies reveal severe aortic valve stenosis with a mean gradient of 50 mmHg and an aortic valve area of 0.7 cm². The patient is deemed a suitable candidate for isolated aortic valve replacement and is scheduled for surgery. During the procedure, the ATS 3f® Aortic Bioprosthesis, Model 1000 (size 19mm) is implanted as a replacement for the patient's native aortic valve. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is geographically stable, able to return to the implant center for follow-up visits. He has been adequately informed about the study and has consented to his participation.

The patient is a 23-year-old female diagnosed with sickle cell disease at the age of 5. She has been experiencing an average of 4 sickle cell related crises or complications per year for the past 3 years. She has been on hydroxyurea therapy for the past year and her dose has been stable for the last 6 months. Her medical record shows that she has had no transfusions in the past 4 months and her HbA level at screening was less than 20%. Her initial two HbF levels were 2.5% and 2.8%, obtained 3 days apart. Her other medical history is non-significant. She is currently not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. She is able to swallow tablets and is willing to comply with the necessary study procedures. Her BP: 120/80, HR: 80/min and BMI: 24. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The lower extremities are normal with no edema. She has no history of chronic opiate use, alcohol or drug abuse. She is not infected with HIV-1 or hepatitis B or C.

Maria is a 58-year-old woman who works as a school teacher. She was diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer after experiencing abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and unintentional weight loss. She underwent gastroscopy, which revealed a large tumor located in the stomach, confirmed by biopsy. A CT scan showed that the cancer had spread to nearby lymph nodes but not to other organs. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and is otherwise healthy. She has no history of prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Her lab studies are within normal limits. She is eager to participate in the clinical trial to receive the best treatment for her condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and limited mobility in her right thumb for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the carpometacarpal (CMC-1) joint, which has been confirmed by imaging studies. She has a minimum DASH score of 40 at baseline and an average VAS pain score greater than or equal to 40 at baseline on a 100mm VAS. She has radiographic evidence of Stage II OA with no free-floating bodies in the CMC-1 joint and subluxation of less than one-third of the target CMC joint. She does not have any significant comorbid medical conditions that could exacerbate pain symptoms or adversely affect physical functioning or healing of the thumb CMC joint. She is willing to return to the clinic for follow-up visits at the required times per protocol and follow the requirements of this protocol. She has not had previous surgery on the target CMC joint or on the wrist of the target hand and does not have any other life circumstances that would interfere with study participation. She is able and willing to provide voluntary consent to participate in the study.

57-year-old male patient with a history of hepatitis B and alcohol abuse was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) at an advanced stage. He underwent a partial hepatectomy but developed disease progression within 6 months. The patient has no history of deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, or cerebrovascular accident. He has not received any surgical procedure, radiofrequency ablation, or intra-arterial chemotherapy within the last 30 days. The patient has Child-Pugh classification A and an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no ascites, pleural effusions or pericardial fluid refractory. The patient has adequate organ function and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 5-year-old male with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is experiencing feeding problems, including mealtime behavior problems, repetitive behaviors, and sensory sensitivities. The child has a receptive language level of 18 months and resides with his mother >50% of the time. The child's medications have been stable for the past 6 weeks and there are no planned changes during the study period. The child does not have any known serious medical conditions that would impact diet or appetite and is able to safely chew and swallow age-appropriate textures. The child has not been hospitalized in the past year and is not being fed via nasogastric or gastrostomy tube. The mother has sufficient proficiency of the English language to comprehend the PT-F program.

Patient is a 16-year-old female high school student from the United States who complains of chronic, widespread pain throughout her body, which has been present for the past six months. She also experiences fatigue, sleep disturbances, cognitive changes and mood disorders. She has previously tried standard of care (SOC) treatment for her condition, but has not experienced significant relief. She is not currently taking any medications, and her past medical history is unremarkable. Her physical examination shows tenderness on pressure of soft tissues, but is otherwise within normal limits. She reports having moderate to severe physical impairment, as her pain interferes with her daily activities. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions that could explain her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to use contraceptive methods for the duration of the study and for 30 days after receiving the last dose of the study drug. She is able to provide electronic records and has no cognitive impairment interfering with the clinical evaluations.

Patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of hypertension and no known cardiovascular disease. He has undergone a 2D Echo with or without contrast obtained within 6 months prior to enrollment (Day 0). The patient is currently in sinus rhythm and is able to communicate effectively with the trial personnel. He has provided signed informed consent after receiving a verbal and written explanation of this clinical trial. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use an adequate and medically approved method of contraception to avoid pregnancy for the duration of the study. The patient has not undergone any major surgery within 4 weeks prior to screening and is not currently participating in any investigational drug, device, or placebo study. The patient is not known to have any hypersensitivity to perflutren or any of the excipients in DEFINITY®.

58-year-old male with a long history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and significant associated co-morbidities, including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, was referred to our center for evaluation for potential AF ablation. The patient has been on multiple anti-arrhythmic drugs (AADs) for many years, but his symptoms have not been well-controlled, and he has experienced multiple hospitalizations due to AF-related complications

A 45-year-old male patient presented to the hospital for elective surgery to remove a suspicious mass in his abdomen. He has a medical history of hypertension, but takes medication to manage it. He has no known allergies and has not taken any medication prior to surgery. Upon evaluation, the anesthesiologist determined that the patient had a Mallampati classification of 4 and therefore has a suspicious difficult airway. The anesthesiologist decided to try a rapid induction strategy using high flow nasal cannula oxygenation support, short-term effect anesthesia with Propofol and Remifentanil for sedation and analgesia, and Sugammadex to reverse the muscle relaxant. The patient has signed the informed consent and is classified as ASA classification II. The surgery is expected to last over two hours. The patient does not have any dysfunctions of liver, kidney or heart and has no infection of the mouth or nose. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any neuromuscular diseases.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past few months. She has been diagnosed with cholelithiasis and has been advised to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing different surgical approaches for cholecystectomy. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, with an ASA score of 2 and no history of cholecystitis or suspected bile duct problems. She is willing to sign the specific informed consent form for the trial and is eager to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge for this condition.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered from a recent anterior mandibular fracture due to a fall from a ladder while working on a construction site. He has no history of chronic illnesses or medical complications. The patient presents with pain and swelling in the mandible, difficulty in eating and speaking, and an inability to close his mouth properly. The fracture is determined to require open reduction and internal fixation. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and agrees to attend follow-up visits for a minimum period of 3 months. The patient has a full set of natural teeth and is not medically compromised.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital for acute heart failure. He has a history of hypertension, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. His symptoms started with shortness of breath and fatigue, and he was found to have elevated BNP levels on admission. He received standard medical therapy for his heart failure, including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers, and his symptoms improved. He is expected to be discharged from the hospital, but his healthcare provider is concerned about his risk of readmission, which is high given his medical history and the high rate of readmissions for heart failure patients. The healthcare provider is interested in enrolling him in a clinical trial utilizing Spire Health Tags to monitor his physiologic variables for a 30-day period following discharge to identify any potential risk markers for readmission. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has agreed to use the Spire Health Tags continuously for 30 days.

A 58-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with a non-small cell lung cancer. The biopsy confirmed that it was Stage II and treatment options were discussed with him. The patient has decided to undergo chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy before surgery to improve the efficacy of the surgery. He is scheduled to undergo a CT Perfusion Scan before and after the treatment to determine the efficacy of the treatment. The patient does not have a history of adverse reaction to contrast agent administration and has no known renal disease.

This is a 45-year-old female patient residing in Italy who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe Rheumatoid Arthritis according to the 1987 American College of Rheumatology criteria or 2010 ACR/European League Against Rheumatism RA Classification Criteria. She has not received any previous treatment with abatacept and has been initiated with abatacept SC either as 1st or 2nd line biologic treatment after inadequate response to previous therapy with one or more DMARDs according to Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) locally approved. The patient is able to read and write and has given informed consent to participate in the study. She is expected to follow-up and comply with the data collection procedures over the entire study observation period, which is 24 months.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a large uveal melanoma in her left eye. The tumor thickness is greater than 10mm and the basal diameter is greater than 16mm, as measured by ultrasound examination. She has no history of metastatic cancer and is willing to undergo enucleation. She has normal vision in her right eye and has never had any previous adverse reactions to intravitreal injections. She has a clear view of the fundus and no history of cataracts or vitreous hemorrhage. She is not currently pregnant.

A 30-year-old male software engineer who works at a tech company is interested in participating in the study. He reports that he has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a wide variety of foods from all food groups. He is in good health and does not have any medical conditions or chronic illnesses. He has no dietary requirements or severe allergies that prevent him from consuming major food groups. He is an iPhone user and is willing to download the mobile application. He is willing to commit to the study period and can comply with the study requirements. He does not have any experience with dietary data collection or analysis, nor has he participated in any research studies before. He does not plan to partake in vigorous physical training or exercise during the study period.

John is a 58-year-old man who has been suffering from urinary symptoms for the past year. He has noticed a decrease in his urinary stream, difficulty initiating urination, and a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been recommended by his urologist to undergo surgery. John is interested in a minimally invasive alternative to transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) and has been informed about prostatic urethral lift (Urolift). He is affiliated to a French health insurance system and his International Prostatic Symptom Score is 18. His prostate volume is 60cc as per ultrasound and his peak urine flow rate is 8ml/sec on a voided volume of 200ml. He has no history of prostate or bladder cancer and has not undergone any previous surgeries. He has normal PSA levels and no active urinary tract infections. John is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess if Urolift could be a cost-effective therapeutic strategy compared to TURP/LASER surgery.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a history of seasonal allergies. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. He does not have any clinically relevant abnormalities identified by a detailed medical history, full physical examination, including blood pressure and pulse rate measurement, 12 lead ECG and clinical laboratory tests. He is a CYP2D6 extensive metabolizer, as predicted by CYP2D6 genotyping. He has not consumed alcohol regularly and denies any regular medication use or illicit drug use. He has not donated blood in the last 56 days. He is willing and able to comply with the Lifestyle guidelines described in the protocol. The patient is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge.

A 35-year-old woman, who works as a teacher, presented with difficulty falling asleep and maintaining sleep for the past 2 weeks. She reports an average of 5 hours of sleep per night, which has led to daytime fatigue, irritability, and decreased work performance. She denies any significant medical or psychiatric history and is currently not taking any medications. She consumes caffeine in the form of coffee, with a maximum of 2 cups per day. She has tried various sleep hygiene practices, such as avoiding screen time before bed, but has not found any relief. She has heard of the potential benefits of honey for sleep and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess its feasibility and effectiveness. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

16 y/o who is currently pregnant and has expressed interest in enrolling in a program to assist with parenting. The patient speaks both English and Spanish and has not been served at the enrollment site in the prior six months. She is not currently enrolled in the Nurse Family Partnership program. The patient is willing to participate in the study data collection and understands that she may be assigned to receive either the PYD or AFLP program.

The patient is a 65 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19. The patient has developed respiratory distress with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute and a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 280. The patient has also shown an increase in ferritin and LDH levels, as well as a decrease in lymphocyte count. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders but has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to antithrombin or its components. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent or has a delegated representative who can provide consent on their behalf. The patient is not immunocompromised due to cancer or transplant and is not pregnant.

56-year-old female with a history of non-small cell lung cancer with metastases to the liver, bone, and brain. She has received first line chemotherapy with carboplatin and pemetrexed with good response and has continued on maintenance pemetrexed. However, she has developed progressive disease with new bone lesions and increasing liver metastases. Recent MRI of the brain showed stable disease. She is currently experiencing pain due to her bone metastases and is considering participating in clinical trials for novel treatment options. The patient has a good performance status with an ECOG score of 1 and adequate organ function. She has no history of interstitial pneumonia, arterial thromboembolism, bleeding tendency, or coagulopathy. She has not received any major surgery or other cancer treatments within the last 4 weeks. The patient has one measurable lesion and is willing to participate in clinical trials.

The patient is a 52-year-old man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. His HbA1c level is between 7.5% and 10%, and he has been taking metformin for over 8 weeks but has not seen improvement in his blood glucose levels. He has a body mass index greater than 18 kg/m2. He has no history of weight loss pill use, systemic corticosteroid treatment, or insulin use in the past 3 months. He has not undergone percutaneous coronary intervention or had a serious cerebrovascular accident or stroke in the past 6 months. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past 3 months, and no medical history of cancer in which remission could not be achieved within 5 years. He has no history of bladder cancer or active bladder cancer, uninvestigated macroscopic hematuria, or major surgery. His fasting blood glucose level is not over 239.6 mg/dL, and his systolic or diastolic blood pressure is not over 160 mmHg or 100 mmHg, respectively. His serum creatinine level is not over 1.5 mg/dL for men or 1.4 mg/dL for women. His albumin/creatinine ratio is not over 2000 mg/g, and his fasting triglyceride level is not over 5.1 mmol/l (452 mg/dL). The patient has agreed to participate in the trial and will be randomized to one of the three treatment groups being tested: glimepiride monotherapy, alogliptin monotherapy, or alogliptin-pioglitazone combination therapy. He will be closely monitored for 6 months with 6 surveys conducted during that time period. The investigators will measure his HbA1c levels, CGMS, and general characteristics such as body weight and vital signs. The patient understands that he may be withdrawn from the trial at any time if he does not comply with the treatment regimen or if he experiences adverse events.

This clinical trial does not require a patient description as it is a study involving healthy volunteers only. Participants must be 18 years or older and previously healthy. The study aims to determine the hemodynamic effects of a fluid bolus with two different temperatures in healthy individuals. The study does not include patients who are critically ill or have medical conditions that would affect the hemodynamic response.

Patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease by a neurologist. The patient is currently at Hoehn & Yahr stage 3 and has trouble with balance and walking endurance. The patient is able to walk 30 meters, but experiences non-motor symptoms such as depression, anxiety, sleep disturbance, and fatigue which negatively impact their quality of life. The patient has not received deep brain stimulation surgery and does not have any significant neurological conditions other than Parkinson's disease. The patient does not have any musculoskeletal conditions affecting their gait, balance, or functions and does not present with on-off motor fluctuations. The patient has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score of 26, indicating no cognitive impairment. The patient is interested in participating in a 6-month balance and brisk walking program to alleviate their non-motor and motor symptoms and enhance their walking capacity, balance performance, and quality of life.

A 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Thomsen disease, a non-dystrophic myotonia, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The patient reports experiencing muscle stiffness and difficulty relaxing his muscles after exertion or sudden movement. He has no history of muscle weakness or other related health conditions. He is not claustrophobic, pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no metallic objects in his body. The patient is willing to undergo MRI scans and strength tests to help researchers better understand the contractile properties of hypertrophic muscles in individuals with non-dystrophic myotonia.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy Japanese male who works as an office worker. He has no history of any disease or drug or alcohol abuse. He takes no medication and has no known allergies to drugs or food. He leads an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical research. He has read the information provided and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study. He is available to attend all scheduled visits and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 35-year-old woman has been experiencing constipation for the past 6 months. She reports having fewer than three bowel movements per week and has to strain to pass stool. She describes the stool as hard and lumpy, and she often feels that her bowel movements are incomplete. She has tried various over-the-counter laxatives, but they have not provided any relief. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has a healthy diet and exercises regularly. She does not smoke and consumes alcohol only occasionally. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the potential risk factors for constipation and hopes to contribute to the development of more effective treatments for this condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. He has no history of persistent visual impairment, macular edema, severe non-proliferative retinopathy, proliferative retinopathy, or retinal vascular occlusion. He has not undergone ocular injections, laser treatment of the retina, or intraocular surgery other than cataract surgery without complications. He does not have any contraindications for fundus photography or mydriatic medications. He is not currently enrolled in an interventional study of an investigational device or drug. He provides written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-month-old male who was brought to the emergency department due to a laceration on his forehead caused by a fall. The child is otherwise healthy and has no known medical conditions. He is up to date on his vaccinations and has not undergone any surgical procedures in the past. The child is accompanied by his mother, who speaks fluent English and consents to participate in the study. The child has not received any central nervous system drugs or known neurotoxic drugs in the past 30 days and has not suffered from any CNS illnesses or pathologies in the past 30 days. The child is cooperative and responsive to his mother's soothing and touch, but is agitated and crying due to the pain from the injury. The attending ED physician determines that the child requires procedural sedation with ketamine to facilitate wound closure.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman, residing in Baltimore City, with a history of depression and anxiety, is seeking prenatal care. She is currently enrolled in a home visiting program and is interested in participating in a study that will provide her with perinatal mental health services. She is experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she previously enjoyed. She also reports experiencing anxiety related to her pregnancy and is concerned about her ability to cope with the demands of motherhood. She has not sought treatment for her mental health concerns previously but is willing to participate in this study to receive support and treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing pain and discomfort in the anal area for the past few months. He has noticed some discharge and occasional bleeding while passing stools. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. He works as an office clerk and does not engage in any heavy physical activity. He denies any history of inflammatory bowel disease or malignancy. Upon examination, there is a small opening in the anal region with some surrounding inflammation. The patient is diagnosed with a simple anal fistula and is advised to undergo surgery. He agrees to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare two surgical techniques for treating anal fistulas. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and signs an informed written consent.

8-year-old girl diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) 2 months ago. Currently, the patient is undergoing chemotherapy and is scheduled for routine blood draws and lumbar punctures to monitor her treatment progress. The patient has tolerated treatment well thus far with minimal side effects. The patient's parents are interested in participating in research studies that may help improve the management of their child's illness. The patient has no known genetic conditions that predispose her to the development of cancer.

A 10-year-old boy was referred to the clinic by his pediatrician for growth hormone treatment. He is short for his age and his height is below the 3rd percentile. He has no significant past medical history, no allergies, and has never had surgery. He lives with his parents and younger sister and attends school regularly. His parents are supportive of his treatment and are willing to participate in the observational study. The patient is not on any other medications and does not have any chronic illnesses. He is active and plays soccer twice a week. He has no history of non-adherence to medications or medical treatments. He is fluent in Czech and communicates well with his parents and healthcare providers.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who presented with dysphagia and weight loss over the past 6 months. He also complains of occasional chest pain and regurgitation of food. He has a past medical history of hypertension, controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or consume alcohol. His family history is negative for cancer. On physical examination, he appeared malnourished and had bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. He underwent an endoscopy, and a biopsy was taken from the lesion. The biopsy report confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. The CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of distant metastasis. The multi-disciplinary esophageal oncology team recommended neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by esophagectomy. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial after signing the informed consent form.

A 45-year-old male was recently diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). He underwent chemotherapy followed by his first allogeneic HSCT (matched unrelated donor) a month ago. He is currently in remission, and the post-transplant biopsy confirmed no minimal residual disease. He lives with his wife and two children. He works as a software developer and enjoys spending time with his family. He is physically active and enjoys playing basketball on weekends. He is currently on prophylactic antibiotics and antifungals. He has recovered well from his transplant and has no signs of GVHD. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the treatment for AML patients who undergo HSCT. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with colon cancer. He has a history of hepatitis C and his alpha-fetoprotein levels are elevated. A CT scan of the abdomen has been performed, but the results were inconclusive. The patient has been referred to the gastroenterology clinic for further evaluation. He has no advanced heart or lung disease that would preclude conscious sedation. The patient will undergo EUS and EUS-FNA examination to determine the presence of a primary or metastatic carcinoma of the liver. Depending on the results, he may be referred to an oncologist, pulmonologist, or cardio-thoracic surgeon for further management.

This is a 25-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of a recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (rRSV A/Maryland/001/11) challenge virus. She is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 23. She does not have any significant medical history or laboratory abnormalities. She has not previously participated in an RSV study or received any investigational products within the last 30 days. She is willing to follow the admission and isolation requirements for the indicated duration per protocol. She is using effective birth control methods and is not planning to become pregnant in the timeframe that begins 30 days prior to the inoculation and ends 30 days after inoculation. She is available for the duration of the trial and is willing to refrain from blood donation during her participation in the study. She understands and demonstrates comprehension of the protocol procedures and knowledge of RSV illness by passing a written comprehension examination with a score greater than or equal to 70%. She is willing to have nasopharyngeal (NP) or blood samples saved for future respiratory virus research.

The patient is a 54-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis due to hepatitis C virus infection. He has been diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through biopsy and imaging studies. He has been found to be a suitable candidate for the oral multikinase inhibitor, sorafenib, due to his disease progression and inability to undergo curative or locoregional therapies. He has provided informed consent to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of sorafenib treatment using positron emission tomography (PET) with [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG-PET) to monitor the tumor response.
