The aim of the study is to detect early effects of sorafenib treatment in advanced HCC and correlate them with other radiologic findings measured by computed tomography (CT) and diffusion-weighted nuclear resonance imaging. The patient's life expectancy is greater than three months, and he has no other active cancer than primary liver cancer.

A 30 year old healthy female with regular menstrual cycles comes to the clinic to participate in a pharmacokinetic study. She has no significant medical history or chronic conditions. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is using a reliable form of birth control. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research. The patient is informed about the study procedures, risks and benefits, and consents to participate. Her vital signs are within normal limits and her physical exam is unremarkable. She is eligible for this study and is enrolled.

Patient A is a 70-year-old female who was diagnosed with primary hyperparathyroidism during a routine check-up. She complains of occasional fatigue and mild muscle weakness, but otherwise has no symptoms. Her serum calcium level is mildly elevated at 2.60 mmol/L (normal range: 2.20-2.55 mmol/L) and her serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) level is elevated at 85 pg/mL (normal range: 15-65 pg/mL). Her bone density scan shows a T-score of -1.5 at the lumbar spine and -1.2 at the hip. She has no history of fragility fractures. She has not undergone any previous parathyroid surgery and her disease is sporadic. She understands the information given and is willing to comply with scheduled follow-up.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, diabetes, cardiopulmonary diseases, malignancies or liver or renal disease. He is not taking any medication that may affect gastric function, and he does not have any contraindications to MRI. He is not allergic to motilitone. He is sexually active, but has been using adequate contraception during the study period. He has not undergone abdominal surgery or upper GI endoscopy within the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve treatment options for patients with functional dyspepsia.

14-year-old adolescent male with a BMI in the 70th percentile for his age. He has a family history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is an occasional smoker, having started smoking at the age of 12. He has a sedentary lifestyle, spending most of his free time playing video games or watching TV. He often eats fast food and drinks sugary beverages. His parents have agreed to participate in the study. Past Medical History: No significant medical history.

A 54-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 12 years. He has been experiencing pain and burning sensation in both feet for the past 8 months. He has been previously diagnosed with diabetic peripheral neuropathy and has been taking over-the-counter pain medication for relief, but the pain persists. He has no history of major depression and his diabetes is well-controlled with medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new medication for the treatment of diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman from the United Kingdom who has recently been diagnosed with obesity. She has tried various diets and exercise regimens in the past, but has struggled to lose weight and keep it off. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She is interested in exploring weight management options and has recently been prescribed liraglutide by her primary care physician. This will be her first time using this medication. She is registered with a primary care practice that is part of the CPRD database and has been under their care for over a year. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery in two weeks. He reports experiencing high levels of anxiety and fear related to the surgery and has difficulty sleeping. He has no history of psychiatric illness, cognitive impairment, or chronic pain. He is currently not taking any medication for anxiety or depression. He has completed high school education and has no significant visual impairment. His preoperative DASS-21 depression score is less than 10. He speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old woman presents to the OB/GYN clinic with a history of missed period for 7 weeks. She had a positive home pregnancy test and was referred for an endovaginal ultrasound. The ultrasound revealed an empty gestational sac with no fetal pole. The patient reports no abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding. She has a history of two previous uncomplicated pregnancies and deliveries. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable with no allergies or chronic illnesses. She is currently not taking any medications. She is married and works as a nurse. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease and reports no significant vaginal bleeding. She is over 18 years of age and has a hematocrit level of 35. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to manage her non-viable pregnancy and is willing to abstain from intercourse for 72 hours.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 2 years ago. She has received treatment with at least one biological DMARD, but did not achieve satisfactory improvement. She is currently experiencing joint pain, stiffness, and swelling, which have significantly affected her daily activities. She has no history of serious infections or tuberculosis. Her liver function is normal, and her blood test results show an ANC of 1,200 cells/mm3, a lymphocyte count of 1,500 cells/mm3, and a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has no history of galactose intolerance or glucose-galactose malabsorption. The patient has been prescribed Xeljanz as a treatment option for her RA, and has received at least one dose of the medication. She is willing to participate in the post-marketing surveillance study for Xeljanz.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty hearing conversations with his family and friends. He has not used hearing aids before and is interested in trying them to improve his quality of life. He has bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and his pure-tone audiometry test results show a PTA (0.5-2 KHz) of 55 dB in his better ear. He does not have any deformity of his pinna or ear canal. He speaks Thai fluently and has no known retrocochlear lesions. He is willing to participate in the study and help assess the effectiveness of the P02 digital hearing aids.

A 30-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22 kg/m^2 and a weight of 70 kg presents to the study site for screening. He has no significant medical history, no current or chronic liver disease, no known hepatic or biliary abnormalities, and no regular alcohol consumption within the last 6 months. He has no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications, or components thereof or a history of drug or other allergy that contraindicates their participation. He is not currently or likely to take antacids (H2 receptor antagonists, proton pump inhibitors [PPI] blockers, etc.) at any point during the study. He has not taken part in any clinical trial and has not received any investigational product within 30 days, 5 half-lives or twice the duration of the biological effect of the investigational product (whichever is longer). He is not a smoker, does not use tobacco- or nicotine-containing products, and has negative urinary cotinine levels. He has a normal urinalysis and serum creatinine at the screening visit, and his peripheral blood neutrophil count is above 2 x 10^9/L. The patient is capable of giving written informed consent and agrees to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

A 65-year-old male with a history of multiple myeloma is experiencing mild back pain related to vertebral compression fractures in his T12 and L3 vertebrae. His pain level is at a 3 on the Visual Analog Scale and he is currently on a stable analgesic regimen. He has no evidence of epidural disease or cord compromise on magnetic resonance imaging. He has a life expectancy greater than 6 months and his myeloma is currently under control with chemotherapy. His hematologic parameters are adequate with a platelet count of 60,000/μL and an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent document. He has no significant comorbidities or contraindications to general or local anesthesia. He has no other primary tumors and his VCF morphology is suitable for balloon kyphoplasty.

A 40-year-old African American woman who underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) 3 years ago was referred for this clinical trial. She was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and underwent HCT after chemotherapy treatment. She is currently in complete remission and has no symptoms of coronary artery disease (CAD). However, she has been diagnosed with hypertension and is on medication to control it. She has no previous history of ischemic heart disease, stroke, or cardiomyopathy/congestive heart failure. She has normal renal function and is not pregnant. She has no known allergy to intravenous (IV) contrast, no sustained or symptomatic ventricular dysrhythmias uncontrolled with drug therapy or implantable device, and no significant conduction defects. She has no current clinical evidence of moderate-to-severe obstructive pulmonary disease or reactive airway diseases requiring therapy. She has no history of drug sensitivity or allergic reaction to beta-blockers, and is not currently taking calcium channel blockers such as verapramil and diltiazem.

A 32-year-old female presents to her primary care physician complaining of difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep at night. She reports feeling tired throughout the day and has trouble concentrating at work. She has never been diagnosed with any significant medical or psychiatric conditions and is currently not taking any medications. She has no history of sleep apnea or any other sleep disorders. She is fluent in English and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication to help her sleep. She is not pregnant nor trying to become pregnant.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. She noticed symptoms upon waking up in the morning. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and occasional snoring. Her medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin. Her family history is negative for stroke but positive for hypertension and diabetes. The patient is able to move her left arm slightly and can barely move her left leg. She has difficulty with speech and is unable to complete sentences. She has a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. Ultrasound showed a 60% stenosis of the right internal carotid artery. The Berlin sleep apnea questionnaire suggests a high risk of having sleep apnea. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for treatment of pain. He is 180 cm tall and weighs 75 kg (BMI: 23.1). He exercises regularly and is in good physical shape. He does not smoke or use any drugs, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of any major illness or medical conditions, and he is not taking any medication or supplements. He has a normal resting heart rate and blood pressure. He is willing to comply with all the study requirements, including contraception, and he understands and agrees to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent pain in her left foot due to a longstanding bunion deformity. The patient is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is scheduled to undergo elective orthopedic foot surgery under general anesthesia. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of II. She has no history of chronic pain therapy or blood coagulation disorders and is not using anticoagulants. She has no known allergies to the study drugs.

54 year-old man with a history of elevated PSA levels and a previous biopsy that confirmed localized prostate cancer. He is scheduled to undergo radical prostatectomy for treatment as standard of care. He has never received any prior therapy for prostate cancer or used 5-alpha reductase inhibitors. He has normal renal function and no known allergies to contrast agents. He is able to comply with the pre-operative imaging panel and has no contraindications to MRI. He does not have a hip prosthesis or any other metal implants in the pelvis. He has not had any previous surgeries that would interfere with the imaging studies.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years. He has been diagnosed with both asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been experiencing mucus hypersecretion. He has been taking bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids, but they have not provided significant relief. He has not had any recent exacerbations in the past month and is generally stable. He is currently not taking any illicit drugs or alcohol and has no history of psychiatric disorders. He is not a pregnant or nursing mother, and he has been using effective contraception. He is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. However, he has a history of coagulation disorders and is currently on anticoagulation therapy, which may make him ineligible for bronchial biopsies.

A 35-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 3 years ago, and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 2 years, presents to the clinic. He has a history of treatment with NNRTIs but has experienced subsequent failure. He has a CD4 cell count of 350 cells/mm3 and an HIV-1 RNA level of 10,000 copies/mL. He has not experienced any recent opportunistic infections or AIDS-defining illnesses. He has no history of seizures or CNS lesions, and his 12-lead electrocardiogram is normal. He reports occasional diarrhea but no other gastrointestinal symptoms. He has no active infections requiring therapy and has not received any systemic therapy for cutaneous Kaposi's Sarcoma. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and he is negative for HCV antibody and HepBsAG.

A 32-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo a caesarean section under general anesthesia due to fetal distress. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to local anesthesia. She has a history of gestational diabetes mellitus, but her blood sugar levels have been well-controlled with diet and exercise. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits, and she has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, or neurological disease. She has adequate verbal communication and is willing to participate in the study. She has been informed of the potential benefits and risks of the study and has provided written informed consent.

35-year-old male with a history of nasal congestion and difficulty breathing through the nose for more than 3 months, despite medical management with topical nasal steroids, topical or oral decongestants, and oral antihistamine/decongestant combination. He reports snoring and waking up feeling tired and unrested. He also reports having daytime fatigue and difficulty concentrating at work. He denies any history of nasal trauma, rhinoplasty or other nasal surgeries, nasal or sinus tumors, pituitary surgery, or sleep apnea. His BMI is 25 kg/m2, and he has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders. He is currently not taking any medications that may affect sleep quality, daytime or dream anxiety. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

48-year-old male with a history of peripheral arterial disease presents to the hospital with acute onset of pain in his right leg. Upon evaluation, he is found to have decreased blood flow in his right lower extremity. The patient is admitted to the vascular yard for further management and is scheduled to undergo an ultrasound doppler to evaluate the blood flow. The patient has expressed concerns about the discomfort associated with being transferred to the ultrasound department for the procedure and the long wait times associated with it. He is willing to participate in a study that aims to evaluate the impact of performing the ultrasound doppler directly at the bedside on patient satisfaction.

The patient is a 43 year old woman who has been the primary caregiver for her husband since he sustained a traumatic brain injury in a car accident six months ago. She reports feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with the demands of caring for her husband while also managing their household and two young children. She has noticed a decline in her own mental and physical health since taking on the role of caregiver, including symptoms of depression and increased stress. She has a high school education and is willing to discuss any potential abuse issues related to her caregiving role. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve her problem-solving abilities and alleviate some of the burden associated with caring for her husband.

56 year old woman with a history of hepatitis C and cirrhosis presenting for evaluation for liver transplantation. She reports occasional abdominal pain and bloating, and occasional episodes of rectal bleeding. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. She has no family history of liver disease or gastrointestinal malignancies. On physical examination, she is noted to have mild hepatomegaly and no other abnormalities. Laboratory testing reveals elevated liver function tests consistent with her history of cirrhosis, but no other significant abnormalities. She is scheduled to undergo esophagogastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy as part of the evaluation process for liver transplantation. She provides informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 6 months. He is generally healthy and within the normal weight range for his height. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly. He works a steady 9-5 job and does not have any history of shift work. He has not traveled across time zones in the past month. He has not donated blood in the past 8 weeks. He has not participated in any other research study. He is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 45 year old woman with a history of heart failure presents to the clinic with persistent symptoms despite optimal pharmacological therapy for the past 4 weeks. She reports shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. She denies any recent myocardial infarction, unstable angina, syncope, cerebral vascular accident, or SCD. She has not received defibrillation therapy within the past 3 months. The patient does not have any known or suspected baroreflex failure or autonomic neuropathy. She has not been diagnosed with significant carotid plaque or stenosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the CVRx Barostim Neo System in the treatment of heart failure.

The patient is a 32 year old female who is overweight with a BMI of 30. She is a software engineer and spends most of her time sitting in front of a computer screen. She has a sedentary lifestyle and exercises less than once a week. She is a low dairy consumer, consuming less than 500 mg/d Ca2+ per day. She has regular menstrual cycles and is not pregnant. She does not have any allergies to dairy protein but is lactose intolerant. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 2 drinks of alcohol per day. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve her diet, exercise, and lifestyle. She is willing to comply with the dietary and exercise interventions and attend regular counseling sessions with the study dietitian/nutritionist. She has no history of heart, kidney, liver, or pancreatic disease and is not taking any vitamin or mineral supplements. She has no gastrointestinal disease or condition and has not had any recent orthopedic injury.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman with a history of symptomatic heart failure, who has been unable to tolerate beta-blocker therapy or has been treated with sub-optimal dosages of beta-blocking agents (<25% of optimal dosage) due to intolerance. She has been diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and has experienced shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. Her echocardiogram shows severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 30%. The patient is hemodynamically stable, but her condition has not improved with standard heart failure therapy. The patient does not have chronic atrial fibrillation, permanent antibradycardia pacing, mechanical tricuspid valve, or severe aortic stenosis or other primary valve disease causing cardiomyopathy. The patient is eligible for the REBEAT trial to evaluate the effect of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) combined with beta-blocker therapy.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of acute leukemia presents to the clinic for evaluation. Her past medical history is significant for chemotherapy treatment for acute leukemia that was diagnosed 8 months ago. She received standard anti-leukemic therapy and achieved complete remission confirmed by bone marrow evaluation. However, her cytogenetic analysis revealed abnormalities involving chromosome 7q, which places her at high risk for relapse. Her WBC count was greater than 100,000/mm3 at diagnosis. Her physical examination shows no acute distress. Her vital signs, including blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate, are within normal limits. She has no visible lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Her laboratory studies reveal bilirubin and liver enzymes within normal limits. Her creatinine level is also within normal limits. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet the eligibility criteria.

A 57-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with Stage IV non-squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC). He has no significant comorbidities and has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. He has not undergone any prior systemic treatment for his lung cancer, and has not received radiotherapy in the last 6 months. He has controlled blood pressure with systolic BP of 140 mmHg and diastolic BP of 80 mmHg. He has no history of sensory neuropathy, hearing impairment, or cardiac disease. He has no brain metastases and has not experienced any thrombotic or embolic events in the last 6 months. He does not have any significant pleural effusion or ascites. He is willing to use adequate barrier birth control measures during the course of the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) that has relapsed after his first-line treatment regimen. He has been previously treated with chlorambucil-based therapy but his disease has progressed and is now refractory to this treatment. His symptoms include fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies to any medications. His physical examination is remarkable for bilateral cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests show a white blood cell count of 65,000/μL, hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 120,000/μL. Imaging studies reveal splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy. He has no history of tuberculosis or hepatitis B or C.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who has undergone chemotherapy as part of the MRC-LEUK-AML12 protocol. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 90% and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 6 weeks. He has been experiencing fevers and shortness of breath for the past week and chest X-ray has shown a nodular infiltrate in the right upper lobe. A CT scan shows multiple nodules in both lungs and a liver lesion, which is concerning for a deep-seated fungal infection. He has no known intolerance to liposomal amphotericin B or sargramostim. His blood work shows: Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL WBC: 3.5 x10^9/L Platelets: 110 x10^9/L Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 35 U/L Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 40 U/L Alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 60 U/L Bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL. He has not received sargramostim in the past 3 months and has not received liposomal amphotericin B in the past 2 weeks.

The patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis. She has been diagnosed with osteoporosis for 3 years and has a screening bone mineral density of 2.7 S.D.s below the mean for young adults at the lumbar spine. She has not had any osteoporotic fractures in the past year and is not currently taking any medications for osteoporosis. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with medication, and she has no history of metabolic bone disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of an investigational drug for the prevention of new spinal fractures.

An 68-year-old retired man named Mr. Lee has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for over 5 years. He lives in the community with his wife and is able to read and communicate fluently in Chinese. Mr. Lee has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medications regularly. He reports that he often forgets to take his medication on time and has difficulty managing his diet due to his love for sweets. He also experiences occasional blurry vision and numbness in his feet. Mr. Lee has never participated in any self-care interventions before and is willing to learn more about managing his diabetes. He is motivated to improve his health and quality of life. Mr. Lee has a score of 21 on the Chinese version of the Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities measure, indicating a degree of self-care deficit.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male who is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no history of significant illnesses or surgeries in the past 5 years. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally, but not excessively. He is willing to comply with the study and lifestyle restrictions and is able to provide informed consent. He has no history of constipation, diarrhea, or frequent bowel movements and has no significant rectal pathology. He is willing to be confined to the clinical research unit (CRU) and adhere to the study requirements. He has no clinically significant abnormalities or infections and tests negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV. He has no history of regular tobacco use or use of nicotine-containing products in the past 6 months and tests negative for urine drug test. He has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to hydrocortisone or any of the inert components of the formulations being tested. He has not participated in another clinical study within the past 60 days.

A 45-year-old Greek-speaking woman with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer has been receiving chemotherapy treatment for the past month. She has been experiencing fatigue and low mood since starting treatment and is interested in exploring complementary therapies to help manage these side effects. She has no history of psychosis or PTSD symptomatology and is not currently receiving any other psychological support. Her doctor has cleared her for participation in the study.

A 45 year old woman was recently diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has spread to the pleura. She is scheduled to start an induction therapy for the cancer treatment. She has provided her consent to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the Oncogramme, a test used to predict the response of cells to different chemotherapy regimens. She has been identified as an eligible candidate as her disease is measurable according to RECIST 1.1 criteria by Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). She has not undergone any targeted therapy, hormone therapy, or radiation therapy yet. She has expressed her willingness to participate and comply with the monitoring requirements of the trial. She is not currently enrolled in any other therapeutic trial with an experimental molecule in the indication concerned. She has been informed about the trial and understands the protocol. She is insured and has access to social support.

This is a 28 year old female who is pregnant with her second child. Her first child was delivered by emergency cesarean section due to fetal distress. She has no significant medical history and her pregnancy has been uneventful. She has opted for an elective cesarean section for her second delivery and has agreed to receive spinal anesthesia with intrathecal morphine for pain control. She understands the numerical rating scale for pain score and is willing to participate in the study. She has an ASA classification of II.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The cancer was found during a routine check-up, and he has no symptoms. The biopsy shows a Gleason score of 7. He has no evidence of lymphatic or haematogenous metastases, and his chest x-ray, CT scan of abdomen and pelvis, and bone scan are negative. His PSA value obtained within one month of randomization. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no concurrent medical conditions likely to significantly reduce prospects of five-year survival. The patient is willing to complete self-administered QOL questionnaire and accessible for follow-up at intervals specified in the protocol. The patient does not have a history of prostatectomy, prior pelvic radiotherapy, or previous hormone treatment for prostate cancer. The patient is not currently on bisphosphonate therapy and has no serum creatinine > 2 x ULN, osteoporosis resulting in >30% loss in vertebral height in one or more thoraco-lumbar vertebrae, liver disease resulting in ALT or AST levels >3 x ULN, or prolonged continuous glucocorticoid therapy > 10 mg/day of prednisone equivalent (>6 months). The patient is eligible for the RADAR trial and will be randomized to one of four trial arms.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl with a history of ulcerative colitis that has been difficult to manage with traditional first-line maintenance therapy. She has previously failed or been intolerant to several medications, including biologics, steroids, and immunomodulators. She has had visual or histologic evidence of inflammation confirmed through colonoscopy within the last 105 days. Her PUCAI score is greater than 9, indicating active ulcerative colitis. She has negative test results for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and Human Immunodeficiency Virus. She is willing and able to participate in the study requirements, including serial stool collection, survey completion, and clinic visits. She is willing to undergo telephone follow-up to assess for safety and adverse events. She is able to swallow antibiotic, FMT or placebo capsules and willing to have an enema for purposes of induction therapy. She is free of any known food allergy and has no history of aspiration, gastroparesis, or surgery involving the upper gastrointestinal tract. She is willing and able to give informed consent/assent as appropriate for her age. She is not currently in clinical remission and has mild to moderate disease. She is not currently taking antibiotics and has no known prior experience with donor FMT. She meets all of the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with idiopathic scoliosis and is scheduled for elective posterior spinal fusion surgery. She has no history of drug abuse and does not suffer from any preoperative neurological deficits. The patient is classified as ASA I-II and has no known allergies to the drugs that will be used in the study protocol. She is able to use a visual analogue scale and does not have any pulmonary, cardiac, or neuropsychiatric disorders. The patient has been informed of the study and has given written consent to participate. She will be randomly assigned to either the patient-controlled intermittent bolus epidural analgesia (PCIEA) group or the patient-controlled continuous epidural analgesia (PCCEA) group with morphine for postoperative pain control. Pain score, morphine usage, postoperative nausea and vomiting, pruritus, rate of satisfaction, sedation scores, and motor block will be assessed at postoperatively 2., 4., 6., 8., 12., 18., ve 24.hour, in all patients. The data will be analyzed using IBM SPSS statistics software 22.0.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who arrived at the emergency department with a sudden, severe headache. He describes it as the worst headache of his life. He has no significant past medical history but reports that his father had a stroke in his 60s. The patient is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. After a CT scan, it was found that he had a ruptured cerebral aneurysm. He was immediately admitted to the hospital and underwent surgical clipping of the aneurysm. The patient is now stable and has been approached to participate in a clinical trial examining the safety and pharmacokinetics of sodium nitrite in preventing cerebral vasospasm. The patient is willing to participate and has no known pregnancy, sickle cell disease, or G6PD deficiency. He is not currently on any anticoagulant therapy.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been experiencing pain and discomfort in his right leg for the past few months. He visited his orthopedic surgeon and underwent several tests which revealed the presence of a benign bone lesion in his right femur. The surgeon has suggested surgical curettage (removal of tumor and scraping) to treat the lesion. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has been offered inclusion in the study comparing PRO-DENSE injectable regenerative graft to ultraporous beta-TCP (VITOSS® morsels, OrthoVita, Inc.), the latter combined with bone marrow aspirate (BMA). He is able to read and understand the informed consent and is willing to return to the office for follow-up appointments and X-rays for at least two years. The patient has no active or chronic infections and does not have any bone marrow disorders. He has no contraindications to the use of Vitoss or Prodense as listed on package inserts. He prefers to use synthetic filler in combination with autologous bone marrow aspirate rather than autologous or allogeneic graft material alone. He works as a manager in a retail store and is married with two children. He enjoys playing golf and spending time with his family.

The patient is a 47-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. He has been diagnosed with primary knee osteoarthritis with malalignment and requires treatment by osteotomy. His condition is classified as grade II on the Kellgren-Lawrence scale, and he experiences pain on walking (15 m) of at least 40 mm. His range of motion is greater than 90 degrees. He has not had any previous surgery on his affected knee, nor has he had any intraarticular intervention within the last 3 months. He has not taken any oral SYSADOA treatment (chondroitin, glucosamine, diacerein) within the last 2 months. He is in good general health and is able to attend regular hospital appointments. He has no known hypersensitivity to any component used in the study. He is willing to use an adequate contraceptive method as he is a sexually active man.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently in her 31st week of pregnancy. She has a history of preterm labor in her previous pregnancy and is therefore at risk for preterm labor in this pregnancy. She has been treated with Magnesium Sulphate for neuroprotection in the past 24 hours. The patient has no known genetic diseases or fetal abnormalities. She has been receiving regular prenatal care and has had no complications during this pregnancy. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medications other than the prenatal vitamins prescribed by her obstetrician. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. The patient has given her consent to participate in this clinical trial, and she understands that her participation is voluntary.

A 27-year-old female was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago and has completed curative treatment involving multimodal therapy. She has been experiencing severe fatigue, pain, and distress since then, which has disrupted her daily life and impacted her ability to achieve her goals. She is currently under the care of a medical provider at Duke Cancer Institute and can speak and read English fluently. She is willing to participate in a novel behavioral symptom management intervention that will provide peer support and teach skills to improve her symptoms and symptom interference. She is also willing to use a mobile application to assist with symptom monitoring and connect with group members. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial and is able to give informed consent.

A 29-year-old woman visited her primary care physician with a history of sinus congestion and facial pain for the past 10 days. She has a history of seasonal allergies and has had a few episodes of sinusitis in the past few years. She reports no fever, no vision problems, no nasal discharge, and no toothache. She is not currently taking any medications except for ibuprofen as needed for pain. She is otherwise healthy, non-smoker, and drinks alcohol occasionally. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the maxillary sinuses, but otherwise unremarkable. She is diagnosed with acute bacterial sinusitis and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known allergies to penicillin or beta-lactams. She has no history of chronic kidney disease, hepatic impairment, or antibiotic-associated colitis.

25 y/o, healthy male with no significant medical history, non-smoker, with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m^2. The participant is in a committed relationship and uses medically effective contraception. He has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 4 weeks and has not used any prescription or over-the-counter drugs within the last 2 weeks. The participant has not donated blood or plasma within the specified timeframes and has not had a history of drug or alcohol misuse within the last 6 months. The participant has no history of heart, liver, gastrointestinal, kidney, lung, hormonal, blood, nerve or psychiatric disease, and has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery or gall bladder removal.

A 15-year-old female high school student presents to the clinic with her mother seeking treatment for panic attacks. She reports experiencing unexpected feelings of intense fear, rapid heartbeat, and shortness of breath that started two months ago. She has been avoiding social events, school, and other activities because of her fear of having a panic attack in public. She has never had any psychiatric diagnosis before, and her medical history is unremarkable. She denies any symptoms of depression, suicidal ideation, or self-harm. She has no history of substance abuse or any medication use. She lives with her parents and a younger sibling, and their family has no history of psychiatric illness. She has no known allergies and has never been hospitalized. Her physical exam is normal, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She is cooperative and oriented to time, place, and person. She is assessed to meet the DSM-IV criteria for panic disorder with agoraphobia. Her mother is supportive and willing to participate in the treatment. She has not been on any medication for her symptoms.

Patient is a 25-year-old Japanese male with no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and has a body mass index within the range of 18.0 to 30.0 kg/m2. He has normal blood pressure, ECG, and laboratory values for hematology, biochemistry or urinalysis. He is not taking any prescription or non-prescription medication, vitamins, or herbal supplements within 14 days before the study treatment. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse in the past 5 years and no known drug allergies or hypersensitivities. He has not donated blood recently and has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B or C, and syphilis. He does not have any dermatological disease at the application site and has not been exposed to excessive or chronic ultraviolet radiation in the past 4 weeks or planned during the study period. He has agreed to use an adequate contraception method during the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who is undergoing his first colonoscopy for screening purposes. He has no personal or family history of polyposis or nonpolyposis syndrome. He is generally healthy and has no known inflammatory bowel disease. He has no current symptoms of gastrointestinal issues and has not experienced any abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or changes in bowel habits. He has not undergone any previous colonoscopies or other gastrointestinal procedures. He is willing to provide informed consent for the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with participation. He is not currently experiencing any coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia, and is not undergoing colonoscopy for emergency reasons or active colitis.

A 35-year-old Hispanic male presented to the clinic with complaints of lower back pain and stiffness for the past 1 year. The pain was insidious in onset, worse in the morning, and improved with activity. He also reported a family history of ankylosing spondylitis (AS), with his father being diagnosed with the condition in his 40s. The patient underwent a complete physical examination, which revealed limited lumbar spine mobility and tenderness at the sacroiliac joints. Radiographs of the sacroiliac joints showed evidence of bilateral sacroiliitis, and the diagnosis of AS was confirmed by the modified New York criteria. The patient expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial investigating the genetic determinants of AS severity. He is fluent in both English and Spanish and is willing to attend regular study visits for the next 5 years.

A 45-year-old woman who has previously received treatment for frown lines between her eyebrows is interested in participating in a long-term safety study of repeat treatment with Mentor Purified Toxin. She has noticed the presence of glabellar rhytides for over a year and is unhappy with their appearance. She is in good physical and mental health, has no history of autoimmune disease, and is not currently taking any medication that would interfere with the study. She has not received any dermal filler treatment to the glabellar area in the past 6 months and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She understands the protocol and has signed the informed consent document. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is looking forward to seeing the long-term effects of the treatment.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of multiple sclerosis presents with complaints of memory loss and difficulty with concentration. She reports difficulty remembering names, dates, and appointments. She also reports difficulty with tasks that require multiple steps, such as preparing a meal or following a recipe. Her neurological examination reveals mild upper and lower limb weakness with no sensory deficits. The patient has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia and is not currently taking any medications. MRI shows multiple T2 and gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the periventricular and subcortical regions of the brain. She has a history of optic neuritis and has been diagnosed with MS for over 10 years. She has an EDSS score of 4.5. She is not pregnant and has no contraindications for lumbar puncture or NMR.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 2 years ago. He was treated with induction chemotherapy consisting of anthracycline and cytarabine, which resulted in complete remission. However, the disease relapsed 6 months later and he received a second cycle of chemotherapy with similar drugs, resulting in a partial response. Recently, he has been experiencing increasing fatigue, shortness of breath, and fever. His blood counts revealed a relapse of AML, and he was referred to the trial. He has no other significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with amlodipine. He is a non-smoker and works as an accountant. He lives with his wife and two children. His performance status is 1 according to Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) criteria. His laboratory values meet the eligibility criteria, except for the serum creatinine level, which is 55 mL/min. He has given written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 70-year-old female who has been diagnosed with pneumonia and has been hospitalized for treatment. She has no history of neurological, orthopedic or heart disease. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. She reports feeling weak and fatigued, with shortness of breath and coughing. She is able to speak in full sentences but needs to take breaks to catch her breath. Her vital signs are stable and within normal limits. She is not currently using any prosthetic devices in her lower limbs. The patient is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in a physical therapy intervention to help improve her physical and functional status.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent redness on her face for several months. She has noticed that her face becomes more red when she is stressed or after consuming certain foods and drinks. She has tried using various over-the-counter creams and ointments to reduce the redness, but has not seen any significant improvement. She has been diagnosed with facial rosacea by a dermatologist and has a Clinician Erythema Assessment (CEA) score of 4 and a Patient Self Assessment (PSA) score of 5. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new topical gel that may help reduce her facial redness. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any medications that would exclude her from the study.

Patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic knee pain for the last 8 months. The patient has been diagnosed with primary knee osteoarthritis of the medial femoro-tibial compartment, according to the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria, and has a Kellgren & Lawrence grade III. The patient's pain score on Huskisson's VAS is 60 mm, and the score on Lequesne's index for the knee osteoarthritis is 9. The patient has not undergone any knee joint surgery in the last 3 months and has not received any basic treatment of arthritis with SYSADOA, symptomatic slow-acting drugs for osteoarthritis (chondroitin sulfates, glucosamine sulfates, diacerhein, hyaluronic acid, and food supplements for joint care) in the last 3 months. The patient has not taken any medication having an influence on pain, including NSAIDs, in the 5 days preceding the inclusion. The patient is currently not taking any medication for his knee pain but is experiencing regular pain and functional disorders. The patient has signed the written informed consent for their participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 36 year old male who was admitted to the intensive care unit due to sepsis. He was initially diagnosed with pneumonia, but his condition quickly deteriorated with high fever and difficulty breathing. He is currently being treated with antibiotics and is on mechanical ventilation to support his breathing. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and takes no medication regularly. He has no known allergies and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He is fluent in English and is able to read and understand written information. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical knowledge and improve patient outcomes.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been struggling with weight management for the past few years. She has a BMI of 28 and weighs 175 pounds. She has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse and is able to read and write in English. She does not have any history of major depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or any type of obsessive-compulsive disorder. She is currently taking medication for migraine headaches, which are well-controlled. She has not used any prescription or non-prescription weight loss products in the past. She has never been diagnosed with an eating disorder or experienced any sensitivity or allergy to the ingredients in the product. She has no history of heart disease, stroke, or arrhythmia but has been diagnosed with hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. She has not had a seizure in the past 5 years and has not been diagnosed with cancer or inflammatory bowel disease. She is not currently taking any TNF-alpha inhibitor, COX-2 inhibitor, or JAK inhibitor medications. She has not undergone any weight loss procedures including bariatric surgery. She is interested in participating in the study to see if daily intake of the ISOThrive supplement can help her achieve her weight loss goals and improve her overall health.

This study is seeking patients who have a history of allergic contact dermatitis to para-phenylenediamine (PPD), a common ingredient found in hair dyes and other cosmetic products. The ideal participant is between the ages of 18 and 65, of any gender, and able to understand and comply with the protocol of the study. Female participants must use a contraceptive method. Participants must not have any evolutive skin disease in the testing zone (lower back) and must not have received systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressive treatment during the previous month, or local corticosteroid treatment the week before the patch testing. Patients who have a clinically significant disease or are pregnant or lactating are excluded from the study. The research team is seeking patients who have a positive PPD patch test and a history of PPD contact dermatitis, as well as healthy volunteers with a negative PPD patch test and no history of PPD allergic contact dermatitis. Patients who have earned more than 4500€ in indemn

The patient is a 22 year old male who was recently diagnosed with Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) after experiencing symptoms such as fever, fatigue, and abdominal pain. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He has not received any treatment for HLH in the past two weeks, nor has he undergone any surgeries in the past four weeks. His laboratory indicators are adequate for enrollment in the study. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has provided a negative pregnancy test. The patient has a history of asthma but is otherwise healthy. The patient has been informed about the study and has signed an informed consent form.

65 year old female with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic knee pain. She has been experiencing difficulty with mobility and daily activities due to the pain in her left knee. The patient has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, corticosteroid injections and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but these have not provided adequate relief. She is now considering knee replacement surgery and has been offered the option to participate in the ROSA Total Knee Post Market Study. The patient is willing to undergo either robotic-assisted or conventional knee replacement surgery and is able to provide informed consent. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities.

The patient is a 22-year-old male college student who has been drinking heavily for the past year. He reports feeling depressed and hopeless, as well as experiencing a lack of motivation to attend classes and study. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been diagnosed with alcohol dependence. He reports drinking at least six drinks per day, seven days a week. He also reports experiencing a lack of appetite and difficulty sleeping. He has no prior history of psychiatric illness, but he has a family history of depression. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. He is willing to use contraceptive methods during the study period.

This is a 32 year-old female who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 4 years ago. She has experienced perianal lesions that have worsened over the past year. She reports experiencing pain, discomfort and bleeding during bowel movements. She has tried topical treatments and antibiotics, but has not experienced significant improvement. The patient is willing to participate in this study to help researchers better understand perianal lesions in Crohn's disease patients and to potentially improve treatment options for herself and others with this condition.

56-year-old Caucasian male with a 30-pack-year smoking history presents with a cough and shortness of breath. A CT scan revealed a right upper lobe lung mass with mediastinal lymph node involvement. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the lung with an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation. He was started on osimertinib as the second-line treatment after failure of first-line chemotherapy. However, he developed gradual progression on osimertinib treatment with a minor increment of tumor burden (> 10% but < 20% in the sum of target lesions). He has no significant past medical or surgical history and his ECOG performance status is 1. He is currently on no other medications and has no allergies to any medication. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including LFTs, CBC, and renal function tests. He is married and works as a sales representative. He has a negative smoking history in the past 5 years and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with all study assessments.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who underwent heart transplantation 2 years ago due to end-stage heart failure. He was diagnosed with cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) following a coronary angiography, and his resting heart rate has been measured to be greater than 80 bpm. He reports experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activity, which has been affecting his daily life. He does not smoke or consume alcohol and is currently not taking any medications. He has no history of renal failure or any other conditions that could affect exercise performance. He is willing to undergo a VO2 max test and sign informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is experiencing pain in her lower abdomen and missed her last menstrual period. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and is not currently using any form of contraception. Upon visiting her gynecologist, she was diagnosed with ectopic pregnancy through ultrasound imaging. She has no known history of endometriosis, ovarian surgery, systemic chemotherapy or assisted reproductive technology treatment. She has never been pregnant before and is currently not taking any medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the effects of salpingectomy and Methotrexate administration on ovarian reserve in ectopic pregnancy. She is willing to undergo laparoscopic surgery or take systemic Methotrexate as per the study protocol.

62-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on chronic hemodialysis for the past 6 months, presenting with secondary hyperparathyroidism (intact PTH levels > 300 pg/mL). The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking calcium supplements and phosphate binders but has not received any vitamin D analogs. His corrected serum calcium is 9.8 mg/dL, and serum phosphate is 5.2 mg/dL after adjusting dialysate calcium and phosphate binders. The patient has no history of liver cirrhosis, active kidney transplantation, previous parathyroidectomy, malignancy, or chronic infection/inflammation. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

48-year-old female diagnosed with relapsed multiple myeloma, who has been prescribed Pomalyst® capsules at a dose of 3mg by her oncologist. The patient has a history of receiving multiple lines of chemotherapy and has previously been treated with Revlimid® and Velcade®. She has a history of hypertension and is on medications for the same. The patient has no history of any other major medical conditions and is currently not on any other medications. She has been advised by her oncologist to continue taking Pomalyst® for a period of 2 years and 6 months as part of her treatment plan. She has given her consent to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Pomalyst® under actual use in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.

A 28 year old pregnant woman with a pre-pregnancy BMI of 28 kg/m2 presents to a northeastern US clinic for her initial prenatal visit at 10 weeks of gestation. She is a first-time mom and is excited about her pregnancy. She reports that she has always struggled with her weight and has tried various diets in the past without success. She is interested in gaining a healthy amount of weight during her pregnancy and is open to making lifestyle changes to achieve this goal. She speaks English fluently and plans to continue receiving prenatal care at this clinic for the duration of her pregnancy.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who suffered a traumatic brain injury (TBI) 10 months ago while playing a contact sport. He was in a coma for 3 weeks and has since recovered consciousness but has been struggling with cognitive and motor function. He has difficulty with attention, memory, and executive function. He also experiences weakness and dyscoordination of his upper limbs, which makes it difficult for him to complete daily tasks such as dressing and grooming himself. He requires assistance to walk and has difficulty maintaining balance. He has been attending physical therapy and occupational therapy for the past few months but has not seen significant improvement in his function. He is motivated to participate in the study to improve his ability to participate in his daily life roles. He is currently medically stable and able to follow two-stage commands.

Sophie is a 12 year old girl who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with a B-cell precursor (BCP) phenotype. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Her parents reported that Sophie has been experiencing fatigue, fevers, night sweats, and weight loss over the past few weeks. She underwent a bone marrow biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of ALL. Sophie's physician discussed the French Protocol for the Treatment of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) in Children and Adolescents with her parents, and they consented to participate in the trial. She met all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria. She will be randomized to receive either one infusion of ONCASPAR® 2500 IU/m2 at D12 or two infusions of ONCASPAR® at 1250 IU/m2 each at D12 and D26 during induction therapy. Her treatment will be closely monitored throughout the study.

Pt is a 12yo M with a history of sickle cell anemia, scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent cholecystitis. The patient has a history of multiple hospital admissions for pain crises requiring red cell transfusions, and has received 4 transfusions in the past year. Preoperative hemoglobin level was 8.5 g/dL. The patient will be admitted to the hospital for the surgery and will be monitored throughout the perioperative period. The patient will be transfused with red cell concentrates as needed based on the hemoglobin level and clinical status during and after the surgery. All transfusions will be recorded and analyzed for the study.

A 6-year-old girl was diagnosed with atopic dermatitis (AD) by her pediatrician two years ago. She has a history of frequent flare-ups with severe itching, redness, and scaling of her skin. Her AD involves her face, neck, trunk, and extremities, covering approximately 15% of her body surface area. She has previously used over-the-counter creams and ointments, but they only provided temporary relief. She has not used any topical treatments for AD in the past two weeks. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of immunodeficiency or other skin disorders. Her parents have agreed to apply the study drug as instructed and follow the study protocol.

A 28-year-old Malaysian woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the bioavailability of different forms of folate supplements. She is healthy, has no chronic diseases, and has never been pregnant. She is not currently taking any vitamin supplements. She is interested in participating in the trial because she wants to ensure that she is getting enough folate to support her overall health. She has heard that there are concerns about the long-term effects of folic acid consumption and is curious about the potential benefits of L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate (L-MTHF) supplements. She is excited to potentially contribute to this important research and is willing to commit to the 12-week trial period. She is aware of the risks and benefits of participating in clinical trials and is eager to learn more about the study and how she can help.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing low back pain for the past month. She describes the pain as constant and dull, with occasional sharp, shooting pains down her legs. The pain has been interfering with her ability to work and participate in daily activities. She rates the pain as an 8 out of 10 on the pain visual analog scale (VAS). She has not undergone any recent back surgeries and has not taken any opioid or psychotropic drugs within the past 4 weeks. She has not been diagnosed with any severe gastrointestinal, liver, renal, or heart diseases, and her blood pressure is within normal range. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written consent.

A 4-year-old English-speaking boy who is toilet trained and scheduled for a voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) is eligible for this clinical trial. He has no known allergies to midazolam and has no history of urethral stricture or reconstruction. He has no abnormal sensations in the pelvic area and no history of sexual abuse. He does not have severe developmental delay and has not been diagnosed with any anxiety disorders. He has been experiencing some anxiety about the upcoming procedure and his parents are interested in having him participate in this study to see if midazolam can help make the experience less traumatic.

The patient is a 19-year-old female who has been experiencing episodes resembling epileptic seizures, but with no medical explanation. She has been diagnosed with psychogenic non-epileptic seizures (PNES) by a medical doctor using video/EEG. She is seeking treatment for her PNES and is willing to participate in an 8-week therapy program. She has a supportive family member (her mother) who is also willing to participate. She does not have any history of substance use or psychosis, and does not have severe intellectual disability. She has been diagnosed with epilepsy in the past, but her neurologist confirms that her epileptic seizures are currently under control. She is looking forward to participating in the study and hopes to gain strategies to better manage her PNES symptoms.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled to undergo abdominal surgery at Castle Hill Hospital. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 85 kg. He has a history of hypertension but it is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use any drugs. He is employed as a construction worker and enjoys spending time with his family. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his recovery from surgery. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who has been experiencing persistent shoulder pain for the past 6 months. He is right-handed and works as a construction worker. He reports that the pain has been interfering with his ability to work and perform daily activities. He has no significant past medical history or drug allergies. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the shoulder joint with limited range of motion in abduction and external rotation. Imaging studies reveal a small to medium rotator cuff tear, less than 3cm in diameter. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is able to complete the required clinical follow-up.

A 13-year-old Hispanic male was referred to the study by his pediatrician after being diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance during a routine check-up. He is overweight with a BMI of 29.2 kg/m2 and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods and sugary drinks. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any medications. His vital signs and physical exam are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle program and his mother is willing to participate with him. They currently reside in the Greater New Haven area and do not have any plans to move in the next six months.

57-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic or recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, specifically in the oropharynx. The patient has not received any prior systemic cancer therapy for recurrent or metastatic disease except for chemotherapy which was part of multimodal treatment completed 6 months prior to enrollment. The patient has detectable measurable disease through imaging exams such as CT or MRI. The patient has tumor tissue available for PD L1 expression testing and HPV p16 status testing. The patient does not have any prior treatment with anti PD1, anti PD L1, anti CTLA 4 antibody, or any other antibody or drugs targeting T cell costimulation or checkpoint pathways, or cetuximab or EGFR inhibitors in any treatment setting. The patient does not have any active autoimmune disease, type I diabetes, hypothyroidism that needs hormone replacement, active infection, or psychiatric disorder. The patient has adequate hematologic, renal and hepatic function. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for first-line treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck.

A 32 year old woman, diagnosed with Primary Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (pITP) for the past 2 years, has been experiencing symptoms such as sudden bruising and bleeding from the gums and nose. She has been experiencing fatigue, which has been affecting her daily activities. Her menstrual cycles have also been irregular and heavy, leading to anemia. She has been on multiple medications to manage her condition, but still struggles with her symptoms. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve the understanding of HRQOL in pITP patients and to potentially improve her own quality of life. She has no history of psychiatric conditions or major cognitive impairments. She is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old African American woman who has just given birth to her first child. She is excited and eager to learn how to take care of her newborn. She is visiting the pediatrician for the first time and is interested in learning about safe infant sleep practices. She is a primary caregiver for her child and is willing to participate in a research study to learn more about infant safety and safe infant sleep practices. She has a reliable phone number and has access to a DVD player.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy from a low-income household who attends a participating school. He has a BMI at the 80th percentile and has been struggling with unhealthy eating habits and low levels of physical activity. The patient's parents have given informed consent for him to participate in the study. The patient does not have any intellectual disabilities or physical disabilities that would prevent him from participating in the study. He has never attended a summer camp before and does not plan to attend one during the year that he participates in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who recently suffered from a myocardial infarction (MI) two weeks ago. He is a non-smoker and does not have a history of drug abuse. He presents with mild chest discomfort and shortness of breath upon exertion. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he was taking medication before the MI. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for a lesion in the left anterior descending artery. His ejection fraction on echocardiography was found to be 50%. He is currently hospitalized at St. Olavs Hospital and is able to participate in exercise groups. He has no history of unstable angina or heart failure. He is interested in participating in the study and contributing to the development of knowledge regarding the effect of early onset exercise training after MI.

A 35-year-old male warzone veteran presents with symptoms of depression and PTSD. He reports experiencing a morally injurious event during his deployment that continues to interfere with his functioning. He has a history of substance abuse and suicidal ideation, and has difficulty resuming meaningful activities and relationships. The patient is eligible for VHA care and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled pilot study to evaluate the acceptability and feasibility of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for moral injury (ACT-MI). The patient does not have any acute intoxication/withdrawal symptoms, mania, psychosis, aggression, catatonia, or cognitive impairment. The patient is not pregnant, has not demonstrated significant violence towards VA staff, and is not currently participating in another psychotherapy research study or an evidence-based psychotherapy for a condition related to moral injury.

45-year-old male patient who recently underwent a renal transplant due to end-stage renal disease. The patient received induction therapy with Campath-1H and has been receiving calcineurin inhibitor therapy, CellCept, and prednisone for the past 2 months. The patient has a PRA value of 10% and a GFR of 60 ml/min. The patient has not undergone any other organ transplant and is willing to participate in the study to determine if discontinuation of calcineurin inhibitors is possible without compromising long-term graft function.

This is a 30 year-old female with a BMI of 24.8 who works in an office and is mostly sedentary. She typically has one bowel movement per day but has occasional constipation. She is a non-vegetarian and consumes fast food for most of her meals. She drinks alcohol occasionally, but never more than 2 drinks per week. She has not taken antibiotics in the last 3 months, and does not take any dietary supplements. She has no history of diabetes, GI illnesses, or surgeries, and has no known food allergies or intolerances. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her gut health and learn about the impact of diet on the microbiome.

32F with a BMI of 35, G1P0 at 39 weeks gestational age was referred to the hospital for induction of labor due to gestational hypertension. The patient has a history of obesity and gestational diabetes, which was well controlled with diet and exercise. Fetal growth parameters were normal, and the patient had no history of previous cesarean section or uterine surgery. On examination, the cervix was closed, thick, and posterior, with a Bishop score of 4. The patient was informed about the risks and benefits of both modes of induction of labor - vaginal dinoprostone and single balloon Foley catheter - and consented to participate in the MODOBAT study. The patient met all inclusion criteria and had no exclusion criteria. The patient's medical history was reviewed, and she was assigned to the single balloon Foley catheter arm of the study. The patient underwent successful induction of labor and delivered vaginally without any complications.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has been scheduled to undergo an elective lobectomy as a part of his treatment plan. He has a history of smoking for 35 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and has not undergone any previous thoracic surgeries. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with an opioid use disorder (OUD) and is currently receiving prenatal care at a reproductive health clinic. She is at less than 34 weeks gestation and has a delivery date no later than December 15, 2022. She is fluent in English and willing to adhere to the study schedule. She does not have any plans to move out of the obstetrical provider treatment area within the study timeframe of approximately 44 weeks. She has provided her informed consent to participate in the study. She is not currently hospitalized, incarcerated, or institutionalized, and does not have any pending court cases that would make incarceration likely during the study treatment period.

A 55-year-old man with a history of non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer presents with complaints of headache and visual disturbances. Upon further evaluation, he is found to have brain metastases without any neurosurgical indication. He is asymptomatic at the time of evaluation and has not received any chemotherapy for his cancer. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and at least one measurable lesion according to the RECIST criteria. He has adequate biological functions and an estimated survival of at least 12 weeks. He is willing to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures. He is using effective contraception as his wife is of childbearing age. He is not presenting with any systemic disorder that would compromise his participation in the study. He is not incapable of discontinuing his aspirin treatment and does not have any neuropathy of grade > 2. He is not participating in any other clinical trial and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

As this study is focused on school mental health providers, a patient description is not necessary. Instead, the participants will be recruited from middle and high schools in two economically and ethnically diverse districts in the Seattle area who meet the inclusion criteria of being a school mental health provider, such as a school psychologist or school social worker.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus for 3 years. She has been using an insulin delivery system with rapid-acting insulin analog for the past 6 months. She reports difficulty in managing her blood sugar levels and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would help her better manage her diabetes. Her current body mass index is 24 kilogram per meter squared and her hemoglobin A1c level is 8.5%. She has no known allergies or history of hypersensitivity to insulin lispro. She has not experienced severe hypoglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis in the past 6 months. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the requirements of up to 6 days of inpatient time.

A 28 year old female who is surgically sterile comes in for a clinical trial for Clarithromycin 500 mg Extended Release Tablets under non-fasting conditions. She has no significant medical history and is in good physical condition as determined by medical history, complete physical examination, and laboratory tests. She has no history of significant past illness expected to affect the investigation. Laboratory tests including Hemoglobin, hematocrit, RBC, WBC, differential count, serum electrolytes (Nz, K, Cl), fasting blood glucose, BUN, bilirubin, creatinine, AST, ALT, LD, alkaline phosphatase and urinalysis are all normal. HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and drugs of abuse testing were done for screening purposes and all were negative. She has also undergone an Electrocardiogram and is deemed eligible for the study. She has read and signed the Consent Form. She does not smoke or use tobacco products nor is she currently using nicotine products.

Patient is a 9-year-old boy attending the Manville School for children with behavioral health challenges. He has a history of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and has been struggling with impulse control and self-regulation in the classroom. The patient's parents have provided consent for their child to participate in the study. The patient has no medical condition that would exempt him from participating in physical education classes. The patient is able to participate in the study without parental opt-out.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with end-stage kidney disease who has been undergoing hemodialysis for the past 4 years at the Assiut health insurance hospital. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension for the past 10 years. He presents with a complaint of dizziness, nausea, and vomiting during his hemodialysis sessions. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse and no previous history of psychotic disorders. He has not been hospitalized recently and is clinically stable. He has not been diagnosed with advanced heart failure. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore the association between IDH and dialytic age in diabetic hemodialysis patients.

75-year-old female with a history of hypertension and osteoporosis presented to the emergency department with severe pain in her left hip after a fall.
