Imaging revealed a pertrochanteric hip fracture and she was scheduled for surgery with a short intramedullary nail. She has an ASA score of 2 and weighs 80 kg. She does not have any allergies to medications and is not on any medication for thrombotic disease or DIC. Her renal function is normal with a serum creatinine level of 80 micromol/L. She has not been previously operated on the same hip and does not have any malignancy or pathological fracture. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the use of tranexamic acid to reduce blood loss during the surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old HIV-positive woman who has been diagnosed with asthma. She is currently being treated with inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators. She has a history of smoking but has quit smoking for the past 5 years. She is currently employed as a nurse and works 12-hour shifts, 3 days a week. She reports occasional shortness of breath and wheezing episodes, particularly during her shifts at work. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand the relationship between obesity, inflammation, and asthma in people with HIV. Her BMI is 32. She has no history of lung resection, active cancer, or recent hospitalization. She has no contraindications to pulmonary function testing and no active infections. She is willing to undergo the bronchoscopy procedure if selected for the optional sub-study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of pain and swelling in the sacrococcygeal region for the past year. He has been diagnosed with pilonidal sinus and has been treated with antibiotics and painkillers in the past. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use any recreational drugs. He is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria.

A 27-year-old female patient with a history of attention deficit disorder with hyperactivity came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial. She was diagnosed with ADHD in childhood and has been taking psychostimulant medication for the past year. She has a regular sleep schedule and does not experience any sleep disturbances. She has no history of alcohol or drug addiction. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has a history of migraines but is currently not experiencing any symptoms. She has completed high school and has a regular job with daytime hours. She is willing to abstain from her psychostimulant medication for 72 hours to participate in the study. She has no psychiatric comorbidities and is not under supervision or guardianship. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

54-year-old male with a history of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) diagnosed 3 years ago presented to the oncology clinic with relapsed disease. He received prior treatment including rituximab and two combination chemotherapy regimens. He has no history of autologous stem cell transplant. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has measurable disease on CT scans. Laboratory studies showed adequate organ function. He has no CNS involvement or epidural involvement. He has no history of myelodysplastic syndrome, allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplantation, and he is not eligible for autologous stem cell transplant. He has no history of other prior lymphoid malignancy other than B-cell NHL. He has no known hypersensitivity or intolerance to any of the active substances or excipients in the formulations for ENTO. He has no evidence of uncontrolled systemic bacterial, fungal, or viral infection. He is not currently taking proton pump inhibitors. He is willing to use a protocol-recommended method of contraception throughout the study and for 30 days after the last dose of ENTO or VCR, whichever is later. He understands and signs a written informed consent form.

A 30-year-old female diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis 2 years ago is eligible for this clinical trial. She has been under treatment with interferon beta-1a for the past year, with no other significant health issues. She is affiliated with a social security scheme and can provide written, free, and informed consent. She has no contraindication to the use of oxygen, is not pregnant or lactating, and has no known respiratory, cardiovascular, or vascular pathology. She has no ophthalmoparesis or incapacitating nystagmus, and her vision is normal with no retinopathy or glaucoma. She has not used vasoactive substances, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, steroids, statins, or antidiabetics in the last 48 hours. She has not consumed alcohol within the last 8 hours. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo an examination of her retinal arterioles using the adaptive optics technique.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a study that aims to understand how visual patterns lead to eye movements. She has no history of significant medical or psychiatric illness and is not taking any medications. She has normal vision and has never worn contact lenses. She has no history of eye surgery or trauma. She understands that the study involves facing a screen on which spots or patterns of light are projected and responding to these patterns by voice, eye movements, or hand movements. She is comfortable with the study procedures, including the recording of eye movements using either electro-oculogram, infrared detector, or contact lens ring. She is available to attend study sessions that last less than four hours and is excited to participate in research that could lead to a better understanding of the physiology of the visuo-motor system in normal humans.

67-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) six years ago. He has received several rounds of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, but his disease has relapsed. He is currently experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His physical examination is unremarkable. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He denies any tobacco or alcohol use. He has no known allergies. His laboratory tests show an absolute neutrophil count of 1.2 x 10^9/L, a platelet count of 70 x 10^9/L, and a total bilirubin of 1.1 mg/dL. His creatinine clearance is estimated to be 60 ml/min. He has no history of embolic events or deep venous thrombosis. He is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He is able to provide informed consent and does not have any serious medical condition, laboratory abnormality or psychiatric illness that would prevent him from participating in the study.

Pt is a 25yo right-handed healthy male with no significant medical history. He has no history of neurodegenerative or cardiac disease. He has never received reflexology therapy and is naive to the practice. He has no skin lesions or history of recent fractures in his feet. He reports no history of phlebitis or deep vein thrombosis. The patient is willing to participate in an MRI examination to evaluate the specific effect of foot reflexology on diaphragm function.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who had a stroke 6 months ago and has been experiencing difficulty reading since then. He is a native English speaker and has no history of mental illness or degenerative disease. He has no visual or auditory acuity impairment and does not abuse drugs. He is willing to participate in the 90-120 free treatment sessions and can go in the MRI scanner for 3 to 6 scans. He understands that the study requires a time commitment of approximately 11-30 weeks and is willing to return for the 3-month post-treatment follow-up assessment and MRI. His current medications include aspirin and atorvastatin. The patient has no history of claustrophobia or pregnancy.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian male who was diagnosed with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and has progressed during treatment with at least one prior therapeutic regimen. He has no history of brain metastasis or leptomeningeal disease or spinal cord compression. He has adequate organ function, and his life expectancy is over 3 months. He has not received more than three prior systemic treatment regimens in the advanced or metastatic setting and has received at least one but not more than two prior anti-angiogenic therapy regimens. He has no history of autoimmune disease and no GI disorders. He is not taking warfarin anticoagulant therapy. He has a surgical history of appendectomy but has not had major surgery within 4 weeks before the first study drug administration. He has no known history of HIV. He is not participating in another therapeutic clinical trial. He is willing and able to swallow oral medications.

A 42-year-old woman has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She works as an office administrator and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has tried several treatments, including medications, physical therapy, and massage therapy, but none have provided significant relief. She rates her pain as an 8 out of 10 on the numerical pain scale and reports that certain postures and movements exacerbate her pain. She also experiences disability, scoring 18% on the Oswestry Disability Index. She has not had any previous spine surgeries or physiotherapy treatments in the past six months. She is fluent in Portuguese and is seeking primary clinical care for her low back pain.

52F with a history of type II diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a prior myocardial infarction (MI) presented to her primary care physician with complaints of pain, numbness, and cold sensation in her left foot. She also reported that she is unable to walk more than a few steps without having to rest due to the pain. She describes the pain as a sharp, stabbing sensation that is constant and worsens with activity. On physical examination, her left foot is cool to the touch, and there is decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick. Her left dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are weak and thready. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.6 on the left and 0.9 on the right. She was referred to a vascular specialist who performed an angiography, which confirmed a total occlusion of the left superficial femoral artery (SFA). The patient meets the inclusion criteria as she has symptomatic non-acute limb ischemia requiring treatment of an infrainguinal artery, has Rutherford Clinical Category 3, and has evidence of a clinically significant CTO located in a peripheral vessel below the infrainguinal ligament confirmed by angiography at the time of the procedure. She also meets the angiographic inclusion criteria as the target CTO has moderate to severe calcification and is long (≥5 cm). She has no history of psychiatric disorder, and there is no evidence of distal embolization in the index extremity unresolved prior to crossing. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, and she is able and willing to provide written informed consent prior to the study procedure.

This is a 56-year-old male who was diagnosed with locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma. The cancer was classified on pelvic MRI and rectal ultrasonography. The patient has T3N1 disease, with the tumor located in the middle rectum. The patient has no contraindication to treatment with capecitabine and is able to receive radiotherapy of 50 Grays in 5 weeks. The patient will undergo chemoradiotherapy and then surgery after 8 to 10 weeks. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or under guardianship. The patient is able to undergo the trial's medical follow-up and is covered by health insurance. The patient has been provided with information and has signed informed consent. This patient is eligible for the Fibroblast Before and After Neoadjuvant Chemo-radiotherapy in Patient With Locally Advanced Rectal Adenocarcinoma clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with acute shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a past medical history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the last 5 years. He is a smoker and has a history of occasional alcohol use. The patient's echocardiogram showed left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% indicating cardiogenic pulmonary congestion and edema. His oxygen saturation was 88% at room air (21% FiO2). He was started on diuretic therapy and other cardiac medications. The patient's pulse oximetry improved to 94% after the therapy. His chest X-ray showed pulmonary infiltrates consistent with pulmonary edema. He is now being considered for participation in a clinical trial investigating the feasibility of collecting respiratory parameters

A 65-year-old man was referred to the cardiology clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion for the past 6 months. He also reports occasional chest pain on exertion. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and drinks alcohol socially. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and simvastatin. On examination, the patient is noted to have elevated jugular venous pressure, and a grade 3/6 systolic murmur is audible on auscultation. An echocardiogram reveals moderate to severe mitral regurgitation with left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%. The patient is deemed high risk for surgical intervention due to his comorbidities and age. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an investigational device for percutaneous trans-catheter repair of his mitral valve. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and no exclusion criteria are present.

A 32-year-old woman came to the dental clinic to replace a missing tooth in the upper left jaw. The missing tooth was a premolar, and it was located in the front of her mouth, just behind the canine tooth. She had lost the tooth a year ago due to a car accident. The gap in her teeth made her self-conscious and she was looking for a solution to improve her smile. She had good oral hygiene and no active periodontal disease. The surrounding teeth were healthy, and the dentist recommended a single implant crown to replace the missing tooth. The patient agreed to the treatment and the implant crown has been installed for a year now. The patient is satisfied with the outcome and is interested in participating in a study that explores the esthetic outcomes and patient-reported outcomes of single implant crowns.

The patient is a 45 year old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection 2 years ago. He has not been on any direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy. His liver fibrosis is Metavir stage F1 based on a liver biopsy performed 8 months ago. He has no history of decompensated liver disease, hematologic disease, renal disease or dermatologic disease. His screening laboratory values are within the institutional normal range, with liver enzymes and bilirubin levels also within normal limits. He has no history of receiving any HCV experimental vaccine or any serious diseases other than HCV infection. He is not currently on any immunomodulators, systemic cancer chemotherapy, or antiretroviral agents. He is not allergic to any vaccine components. He is willing to use adequate contraception as required and has tested negative for pregnancy. He has no history of lactation.

Patient is a 38-year-old man who has been living with HIV/AIDS for the last 5 years. He has been a smoker for the last 15 years and smokes at least 15 cigarettes per day. He is highly motivated to quit smoking and has tried to quit many times but has not been successful. He lives in New York City and is willing to try e-cigarettes or NRT for 12 weeks to quit smoking. He has no history of severe or untreated cardiopulmonary disease such as asthma or emphysema. He has not used NRTs or e-cigarettes in the last 30 days. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any medical condition that precludes the use of nicotine patch or gum. He has agreed to be randomized and followed up with for the study.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (SPMS) for the past 5 years. She experiences difficulty in walking, with an average time of 10 seconds to walk 25 feet. She also experiences hand dexterity challenges, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties. She has tried various medications to manage her symptoms, including Baclofen and Tizanidine, but has not seen significant improvement. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies. Her current Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score is 5.5. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of Domperidone in reducing the progression of her disability. She understands the benefits and risks of the trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of primary tetrahydrobiopterin deficiency (PBD) presents with hyperphenylalaninemia. The patient has a medical history of biallelic pathogenic mutations in PTPS gene and abnormal enzymatic activity of the PTPS enzyme. The patient has been on therapy for management of their signs and symptoms of PBD and is clinically stable. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol and has not used tobacco for the past 2 weeks. The patient has no significant chronic medical illness other than PBD as determined by the investigator. The patient has not undergone any gastric surgery and is able to tolerate oral medication. The patient has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to BH4 or related compounds or any excipients in the study drug formulation. The patient is not currently participating in any other investigational drug study and has not participated in any other study within the past 30 days. The patient has no history of alcohol or

A 25-year-old healthy Caucasian male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of different gas mixtures on pain. He has no history of any significant medical conditions, allergies, or skin diseases. He is willing and able to complete the requirements of the study and has signed the written informed consent form. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and has not donated blood in the past three months. He is able to feel a distinct pin-pick sensation on normal skin.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is a policy-related survey and does not involve patient participation. The study is a cross-sectional retrospective telephone survey based on questionnaires to collect information on issues related to tobacco control in Hong Kong. The participants will be randomly selected and required to answer a questionnaire via telephone. All data will be collected anonymously and analyzed by statisticians. The eligibility criteria for participants are being 15 years old or above and being a Cantonese or Mandarin speaker. The exclusion criteria are being unable to provide a consent form and speaking a language other than Cantonese or Mandarin.

70-year-old female with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's dementia who has been experiencing increased agitation and aggression towards her caregiver for the past month. She has not received treatment with antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, or antidepressants within 1 month prior to study entry. She has a caregiver who can provide accurate information and assist with assessments during the study. The patient (or her legally acceptable representative) has signed the informed consent form. The patient has no history of severe allergies or multiple adverse drug reactions, no symptoms of tardive dyskinesia or neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and has not participated in a clinical trial of any investigational drug within 1 month prior to study entry. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study as she has a diagnosis of dementia according to DSM-IV criteria and has active symptoms of Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD) on Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI). She is eligible to participate in the study to obtain information about her symptoms and treatment received for BPSD.

Mrs. Gupta, a 30-year-old housewife, gave birth to a baby boy weighing 2.1 kg at a government hospital in Delhi. The baby was born at 38 weeks of gestation and had no complications during delivery. Mrs. Gupta has a history of gestational diabetes which was well-controlled with diet and exercise. She received regular antenatal care and had no other complications during pregnancy. The baby was breastfed exclusively for the first two weeks and then started to receive some formula milk due to poor weight gain. Mrs. Gupta lives within 6 km of the hospital and plans to continue living in the area for the next 6 months. She has given her consent to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of vitamin D supplementation on low birth weight infants. She understands that her baby will receive either vitamin D supplements or a placebo on a weekly basis until 6 months of age. She is willing to provide information on her baby's diet and sun exposure during the study period and to bring her baby to the hospital for any illness.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it involves collecting epidemiological data from individuals residing in the Caen-Normandie Metropole area who have experienced any type of stroke, regardless of their demographics or medical history.

A 65-year-old male patient came to the clinic with complaints of blurry vision and difficulty in reading. He was diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes and has been advised to undergo surgery. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies and has not undergone any eye surgeries in the past. His previous eye exams have not shown any abnormalities. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all follow-up visits and procedures.

The patient is a 9-year-old male child who was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) due to severe pneumonia. He has been in the PICU for 10 days and is expected to stay for at least another week. He was intubated and received mechanical ventilation for 5 days before being extubated. His vital signs are stable, and he is currently receiving oxygen therapy via nasal cannula. He has had no other significant medical history and has not undergone any surgical procedures. He is alert and responsive, but weak and fatigued. He is able to move his limbs but has difficulty standing up and walking on his own. His muscle mass appears to have decreased, and he has lost weight since admission. His family is supportive and present at the hospital, but they are experiencing significant emotional and economic stress due to his illness.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is scheduled for a cesarean section delivery in two weeks. She has a history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy. She is 5'5" tall and her BMI is 32 kg/m2, as recorded at her last clinic appointment. She has no relevant drug allergies and has not received any medical therapies that would result in a tolerance to opioids. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) in limited stage. He has completed platinum-based chemotherapy and received definitive thoracic radiotherapy. He has no history of brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease and an MRI of the brain within 28 days prior to registration documenting no evidence of brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease. He has responded to first-line therapy and has no evidence of progression in the opinion of the treating investigator. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1. He has no contraindication to MR imaging or gadolinium contrast administration during MR imaging. He has no other metastatic malignancies requiring current active treatment and no severe active comorbidities. He is not pregnant and agrees to use an effective contraceptive method during PCI and for six months after completing PCI. He speaks and understands English and has agreed to participate in cognitive function testing. He has been informed of the investigational nature of this study and has signed and given written informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and hypertension. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion for the past 6 months, and has been scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery at the institution. He has no history of lung disease, and his pulmonary function tests are within normal limits. He has never had a thoracotomy or pleural effusion, and has no known pleural diseases or fibrosis. He is not currently participating in any other studies, and his surgery is not urgent or emergent in nature. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to be randomized into either the standard or experimental group for chest tube placement after the procedure.

16-year-old female student who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of binge eating and purging behaviors at least once a week for the past six months. She reports feeling out of control during these episodes and has noticed a significant impact on her self-esteem and social life. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is currently not taking any medication and has no history of psychiatric disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers individual therapy to help her manage her bulimia symptoms. She is willing to attend regular therapy sessions and complete assessments throughout the study period.

The patient is a 30 year old female who is interested in improving her body contour through liposuction. She has no history of organ failure or cancer. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She has a BMI of 25 and weighs 140 pounds. She works as a marketing executive and enjoys running and yoga in her free time. She is excited to participate in this study as it aligns with her interest in scientific research and sustainability. She is willing to donate

58F with a history of posterior vitreous detachment and symptoms of floaters for the past 6 months, which have been affecting her daily activities such as reading, driving and watching TV. The floaters are constant and have not shown any improvement over the past few months. She has no other significant ocular history and has never undergone any ocular surgery. Her corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes and the intraocular pressure is normal. She is willing to undergo the intervention and has provided informed consent. She does not have any concurrent ocular or systemic illnesses and is not on any medications that may interfere with the study. The patient has no history of retinal detachment or psychiatric problems.

A 32-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department (ED) with symptoms of opioid overdose. He reports a history of heroin use and has been using opioids for the past 6 months. The patient has a past medical history of depression and anxiety but is not currently taking any medications. On physical examination, he is drowsy, has pinpoint pupils, shallow breathing, and decreased respiratory rate. The ED physician diagnoses the patient with an opioid overdose and administers naloxone. The patient is stabilized and is referred to a local non-profit community-based addiction recovery program, Faces and Voices of Recovery (FAVOR), for further evaluation and treatment. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the FAVOR Opioid Recovery Coaching Evaluation clinical trial and is considered eligible.

A 12-year-old girl with a confirmed diagnosis of Wolfram syndrome presents to the clinic with a history of juvenile-onset diabetes mellitus, diabetes insipidus, optic nerve atrophy, hearing loss, and neurodegeneration. She has been experiencing progressive visual impairment and has difficulty seeing objects from a distance. Her current medications include insulin for diabetes mellitus and desmopressin for diabetes insipidus. She has no significant past medical history, including no history of liver disease, cardiovascular disease, or respiratory disease. She is able to provide written informed consent and is accompanied by her parents who also provide their consent for her participation in the clinical trial. She has no known history of central apnea or ventilation requirements. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical examination is unremarkable except for her visual impairment.

A 19-year-old female who has been experiencing jaw pain for the past year is interested in participating in a clinical trial for TMD. She has no dental-facial anomalies and has not undergone any orthodontic or orthopedic treatments. She has not taken any muscle relaxants or anti-inflammatory medications for her pain. She is currently in college and her pain is affecting her ability to concentrate on her studies. She is looking for an effective and cost-efficient treatment option.

A 35-year-old male non-smoker presents as a volunteer for a clinical trial. He is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He works as a software engineer and has no known exposure to infectious diseases. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He does not have any known allergies to medications, food, or environmental factors. He is not currently in contact with any at-risk groups and has not received any vaccines in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to use a reliable method of contraception if he is of childbearing potential. He is not currently experiencing any significant symptoms such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 47yo woman who presented with a palpable mass in her right breast. A biopsy was performed, which confirmed a diagnosis of ER-positive breast cancer. The patient has no significant medical history and has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer. She underwent both 18F-FES PET/CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT scans at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center within 1 week after diagnosis. The patient's medical history and imaging results are available for review.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. Her hormone receptor status was positive for estrogen and progesterone. She is scheduled to start adjuvant hormonal therapy with Arimidex. She has no history of other cancers or significant medical conditions. She understands the benefits and risks of the ductal lavage procedure and has given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of high intraocular pressure (IOP) in both eyes. He was diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma in his right eye 6 months ago and has been on topical B-adrenergic antagonist treatment. His left eye was also found to have elevated IOP during a routine eye exam. He has no history of acute angle closure, severe trauma, intraocular surgery, or argon laser trabeculoplasty. He does not wear contact lenses and has no history of severe dry eye syndrome or ocular inflammation/infection. He has no other significant ocular history or findings that would prevent reliable applanation tonometry. He has no history of cardiac failure, sinus bradycardia, second or third degree of atrio-ventricular block, bronchial asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He has not participated in any other clinical study within the last month.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 7 years ago. She is currently on a basal-bolus insulin regimen with Glargine as her basal insulin and two prandial insulin shots per day. Her HbA1c level was 8.6% during her last visit to the endocrinologist. She has been experiencing occasional episodes of hypoglycemia in the last three months, which have been managed with the help of her husband. She is currently taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily. She is a retired teacher and enjoys walking and gardening as her physical activities. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m² and her serum creatinine level is within normal range. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her informed consent.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who was diagnosed with phenylketonuria (PKU) shortly after birth through newborn screening. She has been following a strict low-phenylalanine (Phe) diet her entire life and uses a Phe-free protein substitute on a daily basis. She has not been taking any omega-3, antioxidant, (multi)vitamin and/or (multi)mineral supplements for the past six weeks. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study. She does not have any current psychiatric or substance use disorders and is not currently taking any psychotropic or inotropic medications. She has no acute illnesses and does not have any family members taking part in the study. She meets the inclusion criteria for PKU patients in the study and the exclusion criteria for both PKU and non-PKU comparison subjects.

The patient is a healthy young adult between the ages of 28 to 73 years old who has previously received the Tdap vaccine either from Boostrix or Sanofi Pasteurs' Adacel. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no history of neurological disorders or seizures. They are not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the 31-day follow-up period post-vaccination. The patient has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products within the last three months or any tetanus or diphtheria-containing vaccine within the last five years. They do not have any acute or chronic, clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic or renal functional abnormalities, as determined by physical examination or laboratory screening tests. The patient is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and provide written informed consent for vaccination at Year 9 time point.

A 50-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction, who has received an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) due to left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 35% would be eligible for this clinical trial. Patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy, pre-identified hereditary arrhythmia syndrome (e.g. long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, etc), or left ventricular ejection fraction >35% and no implantable cardioverter-defibrillator would not be eligible for this study. The study aims to determine if hereditary factors influence the risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias (ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation) in patients who have received an ICD after myocardial infarction. As part of the study, the patient would be surveyed regarding their personal ICD history and that of their siblings. The prevalence of ICD therapies will be ascertained in the patient, their siblings, and the overall cohort to determine the sibling recurrence risk ratio for appropriate ICD therapies remotely after MI.

This is a 32 year-old female who is currently 33 weeks pregnant with a single and otherwise uncomplicated pregnancy. She presents to the hospital with recent history of leaking and positive Fern test. She has not yet gone into labor and it has been less than 24 hours since her primary medical assessment. An ultrasound examination earlier in her pregnancy estimated her gestational age to be 18 weeks. She has not received antenatal steroids yet. The fetal heart rate trace is normal using an external ultrasound transducer. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study. She does not have any excluded conditions such as multiple pregnancy, HIV positive status, active HSV cervical lesions, major fetal anomaly, intrauterine growth restriction, preeclampsia, placenta abruption, clinical chorioamnionitis or non-reassuring fetal testing.

A 43-year-old female with a history of diabetes complains of stiffness and pain in her left shoulder. She reports the gradual onset, and the pain is worse at night. She is a homemaker and has been unable to perform daily activities such as cooking and cleaning due to the pain and stiffness. She has not had any shoulder surgery in the past. She denies any history of trauma or other known causes of Adhesive Capsulitis. She has not received any treatment for her condition yet. Her past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. She is taking medication for her diabetes and hypertension. She has no known allergies. She is married and has two children. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her HbA1c is 7.2%. She has no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with chronic heart failure for the past 3 years. The patient is in New York Heart Association functional class II-III, and his left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is less than 45%. The patient is currently taking an ACE-inhibitor, an angiotensin receptor blocker, and a beta-blocker, all of which are stable doses. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of dyspnea and fatigue when performing daily activities, but there have been no hospitalizations or adjustments to medication within the past month. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or invasive treatments such as PCI or CABG within the past month. The patient has no history of cognitive decline or psychiatric disorders apart from depression and anxiety disorders. The patient is willing to use electronic Medication Adherence Support System (MASS) to improve and monitor medication adherence.

A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman with advanced metastatic breast cancer who has progressed on anastrozole treatment will be eligible for this clinical trial. The patient has a confirmed diagnosis of estrogen-receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer and has received prior treatments, such as tamoxifen or fulvestrant. The patient must have recovered from any adverse events related to previous therapy prior to enrollment. Adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function is required, as well as fasting serum cholesterol and triglycerides within normal levels. The patient must not have received previous treatment with mTOR inhibitors or radiotherapy within four weeks prior to enrollment, except for localized radiotherapy for analgesic purposes or for lytic lesions at risk of fracture. The patient must not be currently receiving hormone replacement therapy or concomitant immunosuppressive agents or chronic corticosteroids use. The patient must provide written informed consent before any screening procedure and according to local guidelines.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing hoarseness and throat clearing for more than 4 weeks. She has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses, and she is not taking any medications. She works as a teacher and has two children. She denies any history of smoking or drinking alcohol. On examination, her voice is hoarse, and her throat is slightly red. The lab results are normal. She has not taken any alginate preparations, H2-blockers, prokinetic agents or antacids within 7 days, or proton pump inhibitors within 14 days before screening. She has no history of endotracheal tube intubation or radiation therapy. She has not participated in any investigational drug trials within 4 weeks before entering the study. She is willing to participate in the study, and she has signed the informed consent form.

A 10-year-old boy was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of COVID-19 including cough, fever, and shortness of breath. He tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection through PCR testing. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. His parents have consented to his participation in the clinical trial and are willing to comply with study instructions. Convalescent plasma is available and ABO compatible. The patient is expected to remain hospitalized for the duration of the trial.

A 32-year-old female patient presents with a history of atopic dermatitis since childhood. She reports recurrent pruritus, dryness, and skin lesions on her arms, legs, and neck. She has tried several topical treatments before, including emollients, topical corticosteroids, and calcineurin inhibitors, but they only provided temporary relief. The patient is generally healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medication or undergoing any other treatments for her atopic dermatitis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy of a topical Sertaconazole cream 2% in improving her symptoms. The patient signs the informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria with a SCORAD score of 35.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male patient presents to the clinic with a history of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that was diagnosed and surgically resected 2 years ago. The patient has been regularly followed up for the past 6 weeks after the surgery. The histopathology report showed that the tumor was an adenocarcinoma with no anaplastic component, and the mediastinal node station was sampled. The patient is willing to participate in a screening trial to detect second primary lung cancer early. The patient has no history of severe hypertension, and his blood pressure is currently well-controlled. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction within the past 6 weeks. The patient is clinically able to undergo pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and bronchoscopy. The patient has no acute respiratory infection. The patient has no prior uncontrolled malignancy except for nonmelanomatous skin cancer. The patient had no adjuvant chemotherapy or radiotherapy or thoracoabdominal surgery within the past 6 weeks.

A 32 year old female nurse has been working on night shifts for the past 6 months. She is generally healthy but has noticed that her sleep cycle is disturbed and she often feels tired and unenergetic. She has gained weight and her blood pressure has been slightly elevated in her last check-up. She is interested in participating in the EuRhythDia study to improve her cardiometabolic health and sleep quality. She does not take any prescription medications, supplements or drugs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known ophthalmological, skin or physical disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is willing to sign the informed consent and comply with the study requirements.

This is a 35 year old female who has been suffering from major depressive disorder for the past 3 years. She has been treated with various antidepressant medications including sertraline, citalopram and bupropion, but has not experienced any significant improvement in her symptoms. Her Hamilton-17-item scale score is currently 27. She has refused to participate in the PHRC national rTMS 2007 study and has also failed treatment with venlafaxine. She does not have a history of bipolar disorder or depression with psychotic characteristics. She has not been diagnosed with schizophrenia or any other neurological or neurosurgical pathologies. She does not have any contraindications to the practice of rTMS and has not undergone any metallic prosthetic implants or foreign bodies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. However, she has shown resistance to Escitalopram.

A 45-year-old male with a history of primary hip osteoarthritis presents with chronic hip pain and stiffness that has worsened over the last year. The pain is affecting his ability to perform routine activities and his quality of life. He is otherwise healthy and physically active, participating in regular exercise and outdoor activities. He has not undergone any previous surgical interventions for his hip condition.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been experiencing perennial allergies for the past 2 years. She frequently suffers from symptoms such as nasal congestion, runny nose, itchy and watery eyes, and sneezing. The symptoms are particularly severe during the spring and fall seasons. The patient has a positive skin test to dust mites and mold. She is in good health and has no history of significant medical conditions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is practicing a medically acceptable method of contraception. The patient has not received any investigational drug within the past 30 days and does not have any respiratory tract infections requiring oral antibiotic treatment within the past 2 weeks. The patient has not had any nasal surgery or sinus surgery within the previous year. The patient does not have any significant pulmonary disease or arrhythmia. She is not known to have a history of alcohol or drug abuse.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He underwent a radical prostatectomy, and his pathology report revealed a Gleason score of 7 (4+3) with negative surgical margins. His PSA was undetectable postoperatively, but it has been rising, and his most recent PSA was 0.5 ng/ml. The patient is interested in pursuing further treatment options to prevent cancer recurrence. After discussing the risks and benefits of radiation therapy, he has decided to participate in this clinical trial investigating the use of Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) post-prostatectomy. The patient has completed written informed consent and is willing to complete EPIC, PORPUS, and EQ-5D questionnaires as part of the study. His PSA level is within the eligibility criteria for the study, and he has no history of pelvic radiotherapy or contraindications to radical pelvic radiotherapy.

A 7-year-old boy with a clinical diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is being referred to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the validity of an eye gaze paradigm in predicting ASD. The boy was diagnosed with ASD by the Cleveland Clinic Center for Autism Diagnostic Clinic, and is currently receiving treatment for his condition. He has a history of delayed speech and social communication skills, and has difficulties with social interaction and repetitive behaviors. He is currently in a mainstream school program with special education support. He wears corrective lenses and has no other known medical conditions. The boy's parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman of African American ethnicity, who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 2 years. She has been overweight for most of her life and has a BMI of 32. She is currently taking metformin 1000mg twice a day for her diabetes control. Her HbA1c levels have been fluctuating between 7.5-8.2% in the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension and is on lisinopril 20mg once a day. Her lipid profile shows a total cholesterol level of 220mg/dl and LDL-cholesterol of 140mg/dl. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no known history of liver or kidney disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her diabetes control and learn about lifestyle modifications that may benefit her overall health.

A 28-year-old fair-skinned female working as a nurse at a local hospital has volunteered to participate in the study. She has been working night shifts for the past 6 months, which involves working 12-hour shifts from 7 pm to 7 am. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She does not have a history of skin infections or skin cancers. She does not have any known allergies to lidocaine local anesthetic. She is able to comprehend the procedures and risks involved in the study. She is willing to fill out a 3-month calendar of her work schedule. The participant does not have any history of sleep disorders such as sleep apnea or insomnia. She is not pregnant or nursing. Overall, she is in good health and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 2-month-old infant who presents with cough, wheezing, shortness of breath and fever. The infant was born full-term without complications and has been healthy until now. The parents report the symptoms started 2 days ago and have been getting worse since then. The infant is admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit due to the severity of the symptoms. A diagnosis of moderate to severe bronchiolitis is made according to HAS 2019 criteria. Further evaluation shows hypophosphatemia. The infant does not have a history of renal failure, tubulopathy, previous disorder of phospho-calcium balance, malignant pathology, cardiac, aortic or hepatic surgery. The infant is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the association between hypophosphatemia and bronchiolitis.

This is a 32 year old female with a history of Behcet's disease, presenting with active peripheral arthritis involving multiple small and large joints. She has been on multiple DMARDS in the past, but due to inadequate efficacy and side effects, she is currently not taking any DMARDS. She has not responded well to NSAIDs either. She has not been pregnant and is willing to use reliable means of contraception during the study if needed. She has no other significant medical history and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 52-year-old African American female who has been experiencing mild to moderate knee pain for the past six months. She is obese with a BMI of 32 and has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She has been managing her blood pressure and glucose levels with medication and diet. She reports that her knee pain is affecting her daily activities, such as walking, climbing stairs, and standing for extended periods of time. She has been prescribed pain medication and referred to a specialist for further evaluation. She is interested in exploring treatment options that may reduce her pain and improve her quality of life. She is open to discussing treatment options and making informed decisions with her physician. She is willing to participate in the Shared Decision Making (SDM) tool study to evaluate its effectiveness in improving her understanding of treatment options for her knee osteoarthritis.

A 35 year old woman came to the clinic complaining of sudden and unexpected panic attacks for the past 6 months. The attacks occur at least once a week and last for about 10-15 minutes. She also experiences intense fear, palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, nausea, and dizziness during the attacks. She has no history of major psychosis, social phobia, obsessive-compulsive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, or alcohol abuse and dependence. She is not currently taking benzodiazepines. In the latest Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAM-D), she scored 20, indicating moderate to severe depression. She is interested in participating in the study to find a better treatment for her panic disorder.

A 35-year-old man presented to the clinic seeking help for his alcohol addiction. He has been drinking heavily for the past 5 years and has tried quitting on his own multiple times, but relapsed every time. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He exercises regularly, but admits to having a poor diet. He has no history of allergies or any chronic illness. He is currently not on any medication, but has been on antidepressants in the past for a short period of time. He speaks and understands English fluently. He is interested in stopping or reducing his alcohol use and is willing to adhere to all study requirements. He has a supportive wife who is willing to accompany him to the study visits and drive him home after dosing.

A 45-year old female marketing executive is interested in improving the volume of her midface. She has noticed a decrease in plumpness of her cheeks and feels that her face looks tired and aged. She has never had any facial injections before. She is in good health, with no significant medical history or allergies. She is not currently on any medications. She has two children and is using contraception. She is a non-smoker and leads an active lifestyle. She is concerned about the safety and efficacy of the treatment and would like to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the performance and safety of YVOIRE Volume Plus. She is eager to improve the appearance of her face and regain her confidence.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it is a retrospective analysis of data already available on patients who have undergone cardiac surgery. The study will analyze data from patients who underwent cardiac surgery at Emory University Hospital, Crawford Long Hospital, or the Atlanta Veterans Affairs Medical Center. However, eligibility criteria for the study have been provided, which includes patients who underwent cardiac surgery at these hospitals and excludes those who had emergent operations, presence of AF or Aflut at the time of surgery, NYHA class IV heart failure at the time of surgery, hyperthyroidism, implanted

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to severe sepsis caused by a suspected Gram-negative bacterial infection. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. He has no known allergies to antibiotics. The patient has been receiving antimicrobial therapy for the infection and is expected to remain in the hospital for at least 48 hours following enrollment. The patient has intravenous access and is willing and able to provide informed consent. He has not received any tetracycline antibiotics within the past 7 days and has not used isotretinoin within the past 2 weeks. The patient has not undergone major surgery within the past 48 hours and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is being monitored for intracranial hypertension but is not currently being treated for it. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo required blood sampling.

47yo male with stage IV squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx who has undergone initial treatment with chemotherapy and is scheduled to receive combined chemo-radiotherapy treatment for his standard cancer care. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 80% and normal organ and marrow function. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent document and is not currently receiving any other investigational agents. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use adequate contraception prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation.

A 50-year-old man with a history of end-stage lung disease secondary to alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency underwent double-lung transplantation. The patient is currently in the ICU and is intubated and mechanically ventilated. He has a history of smoking and has been abstinent for the past 5 years. His past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 90 bpm, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 95% on mechanical ventilation. The patient is receiving intravenous fluids and vasopressors to maintain hemodynamic stability. The patient's chest X-ray shows good lung expansion with no evidence of consolidation or effusion. The patient is a suitable candidate for the measurement of lung water by transpulmonary thermodilution following lung transplantation.

A 47-year-old male diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme presents with evidence of tumor progression or recurrence. He has previously undergone surgery and radiation therapy for his cancer. His Karnofsky performance status is 70%, and he has an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3, platelet count of 120,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin of 10g/dL. His serum BUN and creatinine levels are within normal limits, as are his total bilirubin and direct bilirubin levels. His SGOT and SGPT levels are slightly elevated but still within the acceptable range, and his alkaline phosphatase level is normal. His life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He has agreed to give palliative radiation prior to initiating chemotherapy with the study drug. The patient has previously received chemotherapy but not within the past 4 weeks. He has not received nitrosourea or mitomycin C in the past 6 weeks or vincristine in the past 2 weeks. He has not completed radiation therapy, interstitial brachytherapy, or radiosurgery within the past 4 weeks. The patient has no acute infections requiring intravenous antibiotics and no frequent vomiting or medical conditions that could interfere with oral medication intake. He has no previous or concurrent malignancies at other sites and is not known to be HIV positive or have an AIDS-related illness. He is not pregnant or nursing.

32-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection during a routine check-up at a community health clinic. The patient has no previous history of ART treatment and has not experienced any symptoms associated with HIV-1 infection. The patient is in good general health, with no significant medical history, and has not been diagnosed with any other chronic medical conditions. The patient is able to comply with protocol requirements and instructions and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not currently breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the study period. The patient has a life expectancy that is deemed sufficient by the investigator for study participation. The patient is not anticipated to need to change ART before the study ends.

32-year-old F with a history of bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder diagnosed at the age of 22. She has been a daily smoker for the past 10 years, smoking approximately 1 pack per day. She has tried to quit smoking several times but has been unsuccessful. She is currently on a regimen of lithium and venlafaxine for mood stabilization and depression. She is interested in reducing her cigarette smoking and ultimately quitting, but has found it challenging to do so on her own. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a smoking cessation study that uses nicotine replacement therapy and counseling to help her quit smoking.

A 46-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent surgery to remove the tumor. The pathology report revealed that the tumor was malignant, and the patient was advised to undergo radiotherapy to the axillary region. She has no history of orthopedic injuries or trauma involving the upper extremities. She is an active individual, regularly participating in physical activities such as jogging, yoga, and swimming. Her medical history reveals that she has no chronic illnesses or significant medical conditions, and her current medications include a daily multi-vitamin supplement. She has a BMI of 23 and is a non-smoker. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the importance of exercise therapy during radiotherapy to help manage upper extremity function-related side effects.

A 54-year-old female patient who underwent a breast cancer surgery three weeks ago and has been experiencing severe post-operative pain that is not relieved by her current opioid analgesic treatment. Her treating physician has decided to introduce an additional non-opioid treatment such as an antiepileptic or an antidepressant to help manage her pain. The patient is able to understand and sign the informed consent form and has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders that could interfere with the study. She does not have any substance use disorders or consume recreational drugs, including cannabis. She is fluent in French and is willing to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhea for the past two years was recently diagnosed with endometriosis after undergoing laparoscopy. She has been seeking treatment for her condition and has been advised to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the use of levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) versus etonogestrel implant (ENG) in controlling her symptoms. She is interested in participating in the trial and has signed the consent form. She meets the inclusion criteria of the trial, and her pain scores on the visual analogue scale (VAS) are ≥ 4. She has no current wish to get pregnant and is willing to use either the LNG-IUS or the ENG implant. She does not have any contraindications to the use of either contraceptive option. She does not have a history of liver disease, progestogen dependent tumors or abnormal bleeding. She is not an alcohol or drug abuser. She is excited to be part of the trial and hopes to improve her quality of life by finding a more effective treatment for her endometriosis.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who underwent surgery for breast cancer 6 months ago. She has had persistent swelling in her arm, which has been diagnosed as lymphedema. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no history of adverse reactions to contrast agents used in imaging studies. She has normal renal function and no contraindications for undergoing magnetic resonance lymphangiography and lymphoscintigraphy. She is willing to participate in this study to evaluate the usefulness of magnetic resonance lymphangiography in the postoperative follow-up of lymphedema.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal bloating and discomfort for the past few months. She has a history of endometriosis and has undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (removal of uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes) a year ago. The biopsy of the removed tissues showed stage III epithelial ovarian cancer. She received 6 cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel and has been in remission for the past 6 months. She is otherwise healthy with no history of allergies or using any medications. Her family history is negative for cancer. She has two children and works as a teacher. Her physical examination is unremarkable. Her laboratory results are normal with no evidence of disease recurrence. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive a new combination of chemotherapy drugs that may improve her chances of long-term remission.

The patient is a 25-year-old non-smoking female with a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2. She is in good health and has no known allergies to cefadroxil or related drugs in the family of cephalosporins or penicillins. She has not taken any prescription medication within the past 14 days or over-the-counter medication within the past 14 days, except for spermicidal/barrier contraceptive products. She has no history of drug abuse, psychiatric or psychological disease, or recent significant illness. She is not pregnant, lactating, or using any hormonal contraceptives. She has not donated blood or participated in a plasmapheresis program within the past 56 days. She has no significant medical or organ abnormalities and has normal findings in the physical examination, 12-lead ECG and vital signs. She is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and will be available for the entire study period. The patient will be evaluated for her relative bioavailability of cefadroxil 500 mg capsules when dosed under fed conditions.

42F with a history of mild to moderate carpal tunnel syndrome in her right dominant hand for 4 months, which presents with numbness and tingling in the right hand's thumb, index, middle, and half of the ring finger, as well as weakness in gripping and manipulating objects. No prior treatments have been performed. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions or significant medical history. She is able to understand and communicate her symptoms and is willing to complete the questionnaires required for the study. She is not currently pregnant or taking any oral drugs, physiotherapy treatment, or splinting for carpal tunnel syndrome.

The patient is a 60-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the last 5 years. He has a long history of smoking and has a pack-year history of 40. He currently experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion and has a productive cough with yellow sputum. He is compliant with his inhaler medications, including a short-acting bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid. He has been prescribed oxygen therapy for the last year and uses it regularly. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or lower extremity swelling. He has no history of pulmonary embolism or lung cancer. He has no other significant medical history and does not take any other medications. He is married, retired, and lives with his spouse. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 35-year-old male with a history of cluster headache diagnosed by an IHS criteria is experiencing frequent attacks. He has previously used sumatriptan 6 mg StatDose for the treatment of cluster headache with successful response. He is currently taking verapamil for cluster headache prevention, which he has been on for over a month. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, epilepsy or renal/hepatic dysfunction. He has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of sumatriptan or any of its components. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate contraception if sexually active. He is able and willing to self-administer subcutaneously administered Imitrex and agrees to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 60-year-old female who was recently admitted to the hospital after experiencing a sudden onset of hemiparesis on her left side. She was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke and is currently 3 days post-admission to the hospital. She has been experiencing difficulty with balance, walking, and ankle impairments. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She is able to follow instructions and has no signs of cognitive impairment or aphasia. She has no open wounds or skin diseases below her knee on her affected limb, and she does not experience severe pain in her legs. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to commit to the intensive rehabilitation program.

55 year-old man diagnosed with Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) on routine screening. CT scan showed a 4 cm tumor in the right lobe of the liver with no evidence of vascular invasion, extrahepatic disease or portal hypertension. Patient has no significant past medical history and liver function tests are within normal limits. The patient has agreed to undergo surgical intervention for the tumor and has been randomized to the SHVE group in the clinical trial. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent. The surgery is scheduled for next week.

The patient is a 32-year-old male veteran who has been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and substance use disorder (SUD). He has a history of alcohol and drug abuse, and has been struggling with PTSD symptoms such as flashbacks, nightmares, and hypervigilance. The patient has been receiving mental health and substance abuse treatment at a VA facility, however, he still experiences significant symptoms of PTSD. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for PTSD in patients with SUDs. The patient speaks English fluently and is willing to be videotaped during therapy sessions. He does not have acute psychotic symptoms or severe suicidality, and has stable medical and legal situations that will allow him to complete the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF). He has been experiencing episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue despite being on anti-arrhythmic medication. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all well-controlled with medication. He has no history of stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or other thromboembolic events. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is married and works as an accountant. He has never undergone any surgical procedures. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his ECG shows AF with a ventricular rate of 80 beats per minute. His echocardiogram reveals an ejection fraction of 55%, mild left atrial enlargement, and no evidence of valvular disease. His lab studies are normal, with a creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1C of 6.5%, and LDL cholesterol of 80 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) in the assessment of left and right atrial appendages (LAA and RAA) for the detection of thrombi before his AF ablation procedure.

This is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with locally advanced rectal cancer. She underwent a colonoscopy after experiencing symptoms of rectal bleeding and abdominal pain. Biopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of rectal cancer, and a CT scan revealed involvement of the surrounding lymph nodes. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no significant comorbidities. She will be receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy in combination with adaptive-intensity modulated imaging-guided radiotherapy. The total dose to clinical target volume (CTV) will be 45 Gy, with a concomitant boost of 5 Gy to gross tumor volume (GTV), delivered with IMRT-SIB technique in 25 fractions. After 2 weeks of treatment, she will be evaluated with 18 FDG-PET and sequential boost of 5 Gy (in 2 fractions) will be planned. She meets all eligibility criteria for the AIDA-RE-1 clinical trial.

A 52-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer, which was treated with radical prostatectomy 2 years ago, presents with a recent onset of abdominal pain and weight loss of 10 pounds over the past 2 months. He reports no other significant medical history or allergies. He is married and has two adult children. He is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially, and denies any illicit drug use. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory results show normal liver and renal function. CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis reveal the presence of an abdominal mass measuring 7 cm in size, consistent with a solid tumor. A biopsy of the mass confirms the presence of adenocarcinoma with no available curative or effective therapy options. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to use effective contraception during the study.

A 35 year old man came to the clinic with a fever, cough, and a sore throat for the past 3 days. He is a smoker and has a history of seasonal allergies. He has not taken any antibiotics in the last 2 weeks. Upon examination, his temperature was 101.2°F and his throat was red with no exudate. His lungs were clear on auscultation. Blood tests showed a slightly elevated white blood cell count and Procalcitonin level of 0.5 ng/mL. The patient provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman is scheduled for an elective cesarean delivery at 38 weeks gestation. She has no significant medical history and is in good health. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently not taking any medications. She has had no complications during her pregnancy. She has a BMI of 25. She is allergic to codeine and reports mild nausea with the use of morphine in the past. She has been experiencing mild to moderate back pain during her pregnancy. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of hydromorphone for post-cesarean delivery analgesia.

A 14-year-old girl was diagnosed with kyphoscoliosis at age 10. She has a 70-degree curvature of her spine and has been experiencing back pain that is affecting her daily activities. She has been evaluated by a spine surgeon and deemed a candidate for spinal correction surgery. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or allergies. Her physical exam and lab results from her last visit were within normal limits. Her weight is 55 kg, height is 162 cm, BP is 110/70, HR is 80/min, and RR is 18/min. She has no history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathies. She and her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial to optimize blood conservation and analgesia during her spinal correction surgery. They understand the potential risks and benefits of the study and have provided written informed consent.

A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman with type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic. She has had diabetes for the past 10 years and has been taking metformin (1500mg/day) for the past 3 months. Her most recent HbA1c level was 7.2%. She has no history of macular edema, congestive heart failure, chronic renal failure, or liver disease. Her AST and ALT levels are within normal limits. She has no history of endocrine disorders, osteoporosis, or bone fractures. She has not been taking any medications that would exclude her from the study. She is able to provide written informed consent and has no physical limitations. Her BMI is 28. She reports no current fractures or history of cancer. She is interested in participating in the study to help understand the relationship between diabetes and osteoporosis.

The patient is a 28-year-old American woman who has been diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). She has been experiencing impulsiveness, emotional disturbance, and difficulty in maintaining interpersonal relationships. She has been on psychotherapy for the past 3 months but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is currently taking medication for her BPD and has not made any changes to her medication in the past month. She has no history of traumatic brain injury, metal objects in her skull, or uncontrolled chronic diseases. She does not have any comorbidities with other mental illnesses except for anxiety and depressive symptoms. She has not engaged in self-injury or suicidal attempts in the past 2 weeks. She is willing to provide her oral and written informed consent to participate in the study.

28-year-old woman with type I diabetes mellitus, diagnosed at age 10, managed with insulin therapy. The patient has been on basal/prandial insulin regimen for the last 3 months, and her latest HbA1C was 8.5%. The patient has not used an insulin pump for at least 3 months. She has no history of severe hypoglycemia or ketoacidosis. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of the SmartGuard® function on external insulin pump to prevent hypoglycemia. The patient is willing to come for regular follow-up visits and comply with the study protocol. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is not pregnant.

8-year-old male patient diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma in the right thigh, with a history of previous chemotherapy and surgery. The patient has been experiencing pain and swelling in the right thigh, which has been worsening over the past few weeks. Imaging studies have revealed a recurrence of the tumor with multiple metastases to the lungs. The patient is currently undergoing evaluation for possible enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of radiotherapy combined with apatinib mesylate in the treatment of rhabdomyosarcoma in children. The patient and their legal guardians have expressed interest in participating in the trial and are willing to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits. The patient's vital signs and laboratory indicators are within normal limits except for anemia, which is being managed with transfusions. The patient is expected to have a predicted survival period of more than 3 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with bone cancer and needs to undergo surgery. He has been experiencing excruciating pain in his affected bone for the past few months which has affected his daily activities and overall quality of life. The patient is in overall good health with no known allergies to opioids, bupivacaine, midazolam, PGL or NSAIDs, and has not been diagnosed with chronic pain or psychiatric disorders. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient will undergo bone surgery with or without soft tissue cancer surgery type II or III under general or epidural anesthesia at Tel-aviv Sourasky Medical Center. During the pre-anesthesia interview, the patient will be given a full explanation of the drug, PCA and the numerical rating scale (NRS).

A 32-year-old woman and her 35-year-old husband have been trying to conceive for the past three years without success. They have undergone several rounds of in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) but have not been successful. They have been experiencing emotional distress and are feeling overwhelmed with the process. They have agreed to participate in the study and have provided their mobile phone numbers. They are proficient in the German language and have smartphones. They are interested in receiving additional psychosocial support during their infertility treatment and are willing to try a low-dose online intervention.

45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, no previous hospitalizations, and no recent travel history was diagnosed with COVID-19. Despite receiving standard medical treatment and oxygen therapy, the patient's oxygen saturation (%Sat02) remained below 93%. Blood gas analysis revealed a Pa02/Fi02 ratio of less than 300 mmHg, and inflammatory markers such as IL-6, D-dimer, ferritin, LDH, CRP, and fibrinogen were above the normal range. A CT scan showed a worsening of total severity score (TSS). The patient's ECOG status was 2. The patient has no previous thoracic radiation therapy or chemotherapy and has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness. The patient has been informed about the ultra-low dose radiation therapy and has provided verbal agreement to participate in the clinical trial.

A 65-year-old woman was admitted to the emergency department because of a fall from a ladder, which caused a severe shoulder pain. Radiography showed a displaced fracture of the proximal humerus involving the metaphysis. The patient was scheduled for surgery, and A.L.P.S® Proximal Humerus Plating System was used for the fixation of the fracture. After surgery, the patient underwent physical therapy and rehabilitation to regain shoulder strength and range of motion.
