Her medical history includes hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and osteoarthritis of the knees. Her last physical exam and lab study were performed two weeks ago and showed the results below: A well-nourished female, non-icteric, cooperative, and alert. Weight: 70 kg, Height: 165 cm, BP: 130/80 HR: 78/min, RR: 18/min, Hgb: 12.5 g/dL, WBC: 8000/mm3 (Neutrophil: 5800/mm3), Plt: 320000 /mL, AST: 25 U/L, ALT: 28 U/L, Alk P: 80 U/L, Bill total: 0.9 mg/dL. The patient reports moderate pain in the shoulder and difficulty with daily activities such as dressing and bathing. She is willing to participate in the study and speaks English fluently.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with a history of HIV infection. He has been on triple drug cART regimen including 2NRTI for the past 2 years and has achieved plasma HIV RNA suppression to undetectable levels (<50c/mL). The patient is currently in care at a HIV treatment center in the Netherlands and has consented to participate in the ATHENA study. The patient has no documented mutations associated with 3TC or DTG resistance of at least low level, and there is no evidence of Hepatitis B coinfection. The patient is otherwise in good health and is compliant with his current medication regimen. The patient is a suitable candidate for the DTG/3TC treatment arm of the DUALING study.

A 55-year-old female diagnosed with early type 2 diabetes is currently taking metformin for glycemic control. She is overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m² and has been following a strict diabetic diet recommended by her physician. She is experiencing postprandial hyperglycemia despite following the recommended diet and metformin therapy. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of an amino acid and chromium-picolinate containing drink on glucose metabolism.

A 55-year-old male patient from the local community presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He reported no recent travel, but his wife had tested positive for COVID-19 a week ago. The patient's oxygen saturation was 86% on room air, and he required immediate oxygen therapy at a rate of 6 liters per minute. Chest X-ray revealed extensive bilateral infiltrates and ground-glass opacities consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient was diagnosed with COVID-19 severe pneumonia and admitted to the ICU for mechanical ventilation. His medical history was significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. He was currently taking metformin and lisinopril. The patient had no known drug allergies. He was aware of the clinical trial and expressed interest in participating to potentially improve his outcome. His laboratory results showed elevated inflammatory markers and a positive COVID-19 PCR test. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and did not meet any exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 3 years ago. She has completed surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. She is currently on endocrine therapy and has been experiencing chronic pain for the past year. Her pain is described as aching and throbbing in her joints and muscles, which is affecting her quality of life. Her worst pain score is 8 out of 10. She has not taken duloxetine or milnacipran before and is willing to discontinue any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or opioid pain medications prior to the study. She is postmenopausal and is willing to comply with the study requirements. Her medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. (BP: 130/80, HR: 70/min)

A 68-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease according to UK Brain Bank Criteria is being considered for participation in a feasibility study evaluating the effectiveness of occupational therapy in Parkinson's disease. The patient lives at home and is experiencing difficulty with daily functioning due to his condition. He is currently not receiving occupational therapy and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. His wife is available to provide informal support at least two times a week as a caregiver. He does not have any comorbidities that would prevent him from actively participating in the intervention.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma. Following surgery, she was found to have a mutation in the epidermal growth factor receptor gene. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score is 1. She has no prior history of anti-cancer therapy and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy to Icotinib as an adjunctive treatment. She is physically able to comply with the study protocol and understands the nature and potential risks of the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that has metastasized to the liver. He has been recommended by his oncologist to consider first or second-line chemotherapy for palliative treatment. The patient is experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and fatigue. He is currently taking pain medication to manage his symptoms. The patient is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He has a college education and is fluent in English. The patient is interested in learning more about his treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve his understanding of the risks and benefits of chemotherapy. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to involve his wife in the informed consent process.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently experienced chest pain while performing physical activity. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medications for both conditions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a sedentary lifestyle, but he is willing to make lifestyle changes if necessary. He has undergone diagnostic tests and was diagnosed with a de novo coronary artery lesion. The treating physician has recommended percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to treat the lesion, and the patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the safety and performance of two stents coated with the same drug. He understands the study requirements and the treatment procedures and is willing to comply with all specified follow-up evaluations. The patient meets the clinical inclusion criteria for the study and has a target lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 50% and a reference vessel diameter of between 2.75mm and 4.0mm. He is not currently participating in another investigational drug or device study and does not have any co-morbid condition(s) that could limit his ability to comply with study follow-up requirements or impact the scientific integrity of the study.

Linda is a 54-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The tumor was found to be wild-type KRAS and she had received irinotecan-containing regimens as first-line chemotherapy but has experienced disease progression within the last 3 months. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate bone marrow and liver function. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that her tumor is negative for EGFR expression by PharmDx Kit. She has not been exposed to cetuximab or any other EGFR-targeted treatment before. She has no history of CNS metastases or radiation for CNS metastases, no intestinal obstruction or impending obstruction due to peritoneal carcinomatosis, and no evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding. She has not undergone surgery within the last 4 weeks and has no other serious illness or medical conditions. She has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 24-year-old female who has been experiencing knee pain during daily activities for the past 6 months. The pain is primarily located in the front of her knee and is aggravated during activities such as prolonged sitting, stair ascent or descent, and squatting. She has not experienced any trauma to her knee and the pain has persisted despite taking pain medications. The patient rates her pain at a 6 out of 10 on a visual analogue scale. She has no history of knee surgery or head injury, and does not have any tenderness or laxity in her collateral or cruciate ligaments. She has not been diagnosed with any other knee conditions such as Osgood-Schlatter or Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different exercise programs for patellofemoral pain.

The patient is a 35-year-old African American male who works as a software engineer in a tech company. He has been struggling with weight gain for the past few years and has a BMI of 30. He has a sedentary lifestyle due to the nature of his job, and he admits to having a high-fat, high-calorie diet. He has tried various weight loss programs in the past with limited success. He is married with two children and is motivated to lose weight to improve his health and overall quality of life. He has no known history of inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, or any other inflammatory conditions. He has not taken antibiotics in the past four weeks, and he has not undergone bowel preparation for colonoscopy in the past week. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how his gut microbiota may be affecting his weight and to receive support in making lifestyle changes to improve his health.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing fatigue, bruising, and petechiae for the past 3 weeks. She has no significant medical history or family history of bleeding disorders. Upon examination, her platelet count is found to be less than 30×10^9/L and she has several areas of bruising and petechiae. She is diagnosed with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). She is admitted to the hospital and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive treatment for her condition. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1, and has not received any medication that affects her platelet count in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant or nursing, and does not have any other autoimmune diseases.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo a hysterectomy surgery due to uterine fibroids. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She exercises occasionally but not on a regular basis. She has no allergies to any medications. She is able to communicate well in both Taiwanese and Mandarin. Her BMI is 25 and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She has no hearing problems or any other medical issues that would prevent her from participating in this study. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the preoperative exercise regimen.

55 y/o white female, postmenopausal for 3 years, non-smoker, with a BMI of 25 kg/m2, and no relevant medical history. No history of coronary artery disease, postural hypotension, bronchial asthma, hypersensitivity to the study or any relevant diseases within 4 weeks before study drug administration. No history of venous or arterial thrombotic/thromboembolic events or cerebrovascular accident. No use of systemic or topical medicines or substances which oppose the study objectives, or smoking, or use of sex hormones in any forms. No clinically relevant findings in the ECG, systolic blood pressure is within normal limits, and heart rate is regular and within normal limits. No clinically relevant findings in the gynecological examination. Not currently participating in another clinical study.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it does not involve enrolling patients. Instead, it involves the measurement of exhaled breath condensate (EBC) pH in mechanically ventilated patients in the ICU. The study aims to determine if EBC pH measurements in the water condensed in the trap of the expiratory arm of the ventilator can replace EBC collected by coolant chamber with gas standardization using Argon as an inert gas, and if EBC pH could predict ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) and mortality. Inclusion criteria for the study are patients who require endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation for at least 48 hours due to non-pulmonary cause, and exclusion criteria are patients who require mechanical ventilation due to specific pulmonary conditions or are expected to be ventilated for less than 2 days.

A 55 year old female patient is diagnosed with AL cardiac amyloidosis after presenting with shortness of breath, fatigue, and peripheral edema. She has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. Her echocardiogram shows evidence of restrictive cardiomyopathy with thickened ventricular walls and decreased ejection fraction. NT-ProBNP levels are elevated at 500 pg/mL. She consents to participate in the clinical trial and is planned to undergo plasma cell-directed chemotherapy. She is able to undergo PET-CT imaging and complete a 6-minute walk test. She has no known allergies to F-18 florbetapir.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester with a singleton pregnancy. She has no significant medical history and has not had any previous surgeries or complications during pregnancy. She is scheduled to undergo a cesarean delivery for medical reasons. She does not have any allergies to medications and has not used opioids in the past 12 hours. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the postoperative respiratory monitoring trial.

65F with a past medical history of primary osteoarthritis of the femorotibial medial joint of the right knee, diagnosed 3 years ago.She complains of a dull, aching pain in the right knee that has been progressively worsening over the past year. She reports difficulty walking for long periods of time and going up and down stairs. She rates her pain as 7/10 on the VAS scale. She has tried acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain relief, but it only provides temporary relief. She has not received any intra-articular injections in the past year. Her BMI is 28. She is not pregnant, lactating, or of child-bearing age. She has no known allergies to hyaluronic acid, acetaminophen, or ibuprofen. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 3-month-old boy who has been diagnosed with viral bronchiolitis and has been experiencing apnea episodes. He was brought to the pediatric emergency center Al-Sadd in Qatar. The baby has no known allergies and has not been previously treated with caffeine. He does not have any cardiovascular congenital abnormalities, gastroesophageal reflux disease, or any significant medical history. His electrolytes and glucose levels are normal, and there is no suspicion of sepsis, seizure disorders, inborn errors of metabolism or renal/hepatic impairment. The baby is not diagnosed with major congenital anomalies of the respiratory tract. The parents have been approached and have given verbal and written consent for their child to participate in a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of caffeine citrate for the treatment of apnea associated with bronchiolitis in young infants.

A 56-year-old female with a diagnosis of advanced ovarian cancer that has spread to other parts of her body is being considered for a clinical trial. She has already undergone several rounds of chemotherapy but her condition has not improved significantly. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, which means she is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities but is unable to perform any strenuous activity. She has no known gastrointestinal abnormalities or procedures that could affect the absorption of alisertib. She has not been treated with any moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers in the past 14 days. The patient has no known hypersensitivity or intolerance to itraconazole or similar class agents. The purpose of the trial is to evaluate the effect of multi-dose administration of itraconazole on the single-dose pharmacokinetics of alisertib. The patient will be given alisertib tablets in Part A and Part B, with itraconazole oral solution administered only in Part A. The participation in Part A is approximately 25 days, and Part B participation involves repeating 21-day cycles. The maximum duration of treatment with alisertib will be 12 months unless the investigator determines that the patient would derive clinical benefit from continued treatment beyond 12 months. The patient will be monitored closely throughout the trial to evaluate the effect of itraconazole on the pharmacokinetics of alisertib.

62-year-old female with a history of COPD with frequent episodes of dyspnea on exertion and decreased quality of life, despite current medications. She has no history of sleep apnea or use of non-invasive positive pressure ventilation. She has no severe bilateral nasal obstruction and her cardiovascular disease is stable with no recent myocardial infarction or revascularization procedure. She has no implanted cardiac pacemaker or ICD, no unstable arrhythmia, and no congestive heart failure with ejection fraction < 40%. Her hypertension is well-controlled, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. She has no history of end-stage renal disease, end-stage liver disease or known pregnancy. She is not taking any medications for pain control, sleep, benzodiazepines, or methadone. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of high-flow therapy in COPD at home.

A 25-year-old male athlete who experienced a total primary ACL rupture during a soccer match eight months ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of single-bundle ACL reconstruction (SBACLR) and double-bundle ACL reconstruction (DBACLR) in terms of cartilage damage. He has been under conservative treatment and physical therapy since the injury occurred. He has no other ligament injuries in the knee, rheumatoid arthritis, or other contraindications for the study. His BMI is 22, and he has no history of fractures around the knee joint or osteochondral avulsion. He is willing to attend the study and has signed the informed consent form. The subject has not undergone any previous surgery on the knee joint.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male who presented with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He smokes a pack of cigarettes a day for the past 30 years. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He doesn't have any significant family history of cancer. A chest X-ray showed a mass in the right lung, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. He underwent a complete resection of the tumor and paired lymph nodes, and the histopathological analysis showed positive lymph nodes. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help researchers understand more about the molecular alterations in resected lung cancer. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study for the next two years, with three years of follow-up. He has not received chemotherapy before surgical treatment.

The patient is a male or female between the ages of 18 and 70 years who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus infection or hepatitis D virus coinfection. They must have a body mass index (BMI) within 18.0 kg/m2 to 35.0 kg/m2, inclusively and be a light, non-, or ex-smoker. The patient must be willing to comply with all study procedures and be available for the duration of the study. If female, they must meet one of the following criteria: be of childbearing potential and agree to use an acceptable contraceptive method or be of non-childbearing potential. If male, they must be able to procreate and agree to use an acceptable contraceptive regimen and not donate sperm from the first study drug administration to at least 90 days after the last drug administration. They must have serum HBsAg positive at screening and at least 6 months prior to screening, serum HBeAg positive and HBV DNA ≥ 20,000 IU/mL or serum HBeAg negative and HBV DNA ≥ 2,000 IU/mL at screening, and ALT and AST < 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) at screening and on the day prior to the first study drug administration (Day -1). For subjects coinfected with chronic HBV and HDV only, they must also have HDV RNA in serum ≥ 500 IU/mL at screening and evidence of HDV infection (HDVAb or HDV RNA) at least 6 months prior to screening. The patient must not have a history of significant hypersensitivity to clevudine, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or any related products, and must not have any significant history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, neurological, psychiatric, endocrine, immunologic or dermatologic disease. The patient must also not have any clinically significant muscle disorders, myopathies, or other forms of liver disease, and must not have a history of tuberculosis or active illicit drug use. The patient must be able to provide signed and dated informed consent form (ICF).

A 45-year-old man with a BMI of 38 is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. He has a history of hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea, which is being managed with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). His pre-operative oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. He has never had any adverse reactions to anesthesia or opioids in the past. The attending anesthesiologist decides to use opioid-free anesthesia for this patient based on his expertise. The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated during the procedure, with a lung protective ventilation strategy in place. During the surgery, the patient's lung compliance drops below 40 ML/cmH20, and a lung recruitment followed by high PEEP is given. The patient is extubated and transferred to PACU where the lowest oxygen saturation without adding oxygen therapy is noted. After the patient is given an opioid as an analgesic, his oxygen saturation is noted again. Finally, at the time of discharge from PACU, the patient's oxygen saturation is recorded. If his postoperative saturation drops below 94%, oxygen therapy is given and noted.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with HIV infection 6 years ago. He has been on standard combination antiretroviral therapy with 2 NRTIs and 1 PI for the past 5 years. His last viral load was undetectable (<50 copies/mL) and his CD4 count is stable at 600 cells/mm3. He has no history of substance abuse or non-adherence to his medication regimen. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. He is sexually active with his partner, who is also HIV positive and on antiretroviral therapy. He agrees to use two methods of birth control during the study period. He has no malignancy, AIDS-defining illnesses, or other significant underlying diseases. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 30-year-old male who presented with symptoms of COVID-19 infection, including fever, cough, and headache, to his primary care physician. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medication. The patient has no known allergies to hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, azithromycin, or any macrolide antibiotics. His potassium, magnesium, and calcium levels are within normal limits. His ECG shows a QTc of 430ms. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has National Health Insurance coverage and is not currently enrolled in another therapeutic clinical trial for COVID-19. The patient is randomized into the experimental group and is started on hydroxychloroquine and azithromycin therapy on day 2 of his illness. He maintains a daily diary to record his symptoms and drug intake. The GP follows up with the patient on days 5, 8, 14, and 28 to assess his clinical progress. A nasopharyngeal swab, ECG, and blood sample are taken at baseline, and the patient is included in the ancillary virological study to assess the evolution of viral load at days 8 and 14.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with congenital heart disease associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (CHD-PAH). He has a history of congenital heart disease and has undergone multiple surgeries in the past, including aortic valve replacement and repair of a ventricular septal defect. He experiences shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain with exertion. He used to work as a construction worker but had to quit his job due to his disease. He is married and has two children. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He takes multiple medications including diuretics, vasodilators and anticoagulants. His most recent echocardiogram showed an enlarged right ventricle and pulmonary artery pressure of 45 mmHg. His lung function tests showed reduced gas volumes and impaired gas exchange. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with the study.

A 55-year-old male former smoker was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the lung. The cancer is locally advanced and has spread to the lymph nodes. The patient has no comorbidities, but he has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has never received chemotherapy, radiation or surgery for his cancer. The patient underwent FISH-testing, and the results showed that he is positive for ROS1 translocation. He is currently able to swallow pills and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to participate in the EUCROSS clinical trial and has signed the written informed consent. His baseline laboratory results showed normal bone marrow, liver and renal function, and he meets the eligibility criteria for the trial. He will be treated with crizotinib at a dose of 250mg twice-daily and will undergo regular CT or MRI scans to assess the tumor response to treatment. If disease progression occurs, he will be treated beyond if clinically indicated. The study team will also perform an optional re-biopsy if resistance to crizotinib treatment occurs to identify mechanisms of resistance. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse effects of the treatment, and he will be advised to use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after completion of treatment.

5 year old girl scheduled for an elective adenotonsillectomy. She has no significant past medical history and is considered to be in good health with an ASA score of 1. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitive reactions to dexmedetomidine. She does not have any known cardiac arrhythmias or congenital heart disease. The patient does not have autism or pervasive personality disorder.

Sarah is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to her spine. She has been experiencing increasing back pain and weakness in her legs. Imaging studies revealed a spinal tumor that requires surgical intervention and adjuvant radiation therapy. Sarah has no known allergies and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is currently taking tamoxifen and has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She has a good support system at home and is motivated to undergo treatment. As part of her treatment plan, Sarah has been enrolled in a clinical trial comparing the use of carbon/PEEK pedicle screws versus titanium pedicle screws in spinal tumor surgery. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has given her informed consent to participate.

A 45-year-old female with a history of Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm (BPDCN) has failed one prior therapy and is experiencing relapsed or refractory BPDCN. The patient has no history of corticosteroid dependence on doses greater than physiological replacement and has no contraindications or hypersensitivity to fludarabine or cyclophosphamide. The patient has not undergone previous treatment with anti-CD123 CAR-T treatment, but may have been treated with non-CAR-T anti-CD123 agents, such as tagraxof

55 year-old male with a history of outdoor work and sun exposure who presents with dry and cracked lips, especially on the lower lip. He also reports occasional bleeding and discomfort when eating or speaking. Physical examination reveals erythema and scaling of the lips, consistent with actinic cheilitis. The patient has not received any treatment for actinic cheilitis in the last 3 months. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of actinic cheilitis. The patient is willing to respect the timeframe of clinical consultations and is interested in participating in photodynamic therapy with metil 5-aminolevulinate for the treatment of actinic cheilitis. The patient does not have a history of squamous cell carcinoma or any type of immunosuppression.

72-year-old male with a history of recurrent MDD, currently experiencing a major depressive episode for more than 2 years, presented to the psychiatric clinic complaining of persistent sadness, hopelessness, anhedonia, fatigue, insomnia, and poor appetite. He reports that he has tried multiple antidepressant medications with no significant improvement in his symptoms. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. He had a cardiac stress test 6 months ago, which was normal. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen as needed for his joint pain. His family history is significant for depression, but no history of suicide or suicide attempts. He denies any history of substance use or abuse. He has a Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 28. His depression symptoms are assessed based on the Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Clinician rated (IDS-C30) with a total score of 36. The participant has had nonresponse (less than or equal to 25% improvement) to at least one antidepressant treatment (based on Massachusetts General Hospital - Antidepressant Treatment Response Questionnaire [MGH-ATRQ] criteria) in the current episode of depression. The participant is currently taking one of the oral antidepressant treatments with nonresponse that is documented on the MGH-ATRQ. The participant is eligible for the study based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She has been treated with adalimumab for the past 2 years with some improvement in her symptoms. However, she still experiences abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue. She has a history of intolerance to azathioprine due to side effects such as nausea, vomiting, and headaches. The patient is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has no known drug allergies. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the combination therapy of adalimumab with methotrexate as she has heard about the potential benefits of this treatment option. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and follow the study procedures.

The patient is a 63-year-old Caucasian man who has been diagnosed with resectable colorectal cancer. The tumor is located at the sigmoid colon and measures 5.5 cm in diameter. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or chemotherapy, radiation, and his blood routine test and hepatic or renal function test are normal. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. He has no severe comorbidities such as heart attack or stroke and has not been diagnosed with malignancy in the last 5 years. He is in good health overall and does not have any conditions that would prevent him from tolerating general anesthesia, pneumoperitoneum, or surgery. He is not pregnant or in the breastfeeding period. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials involving therapy and is willing to attend all required appointments for the clinical trial.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman from the United States who has been experiencing anal incontinence for the past year. She reports that she has difficulty controlling gas and stool, especially when she is physically active or after eating. She has tried Kegel exercises and biofeedback therapy in the past, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has never been pregnant and has no history of hemorrhoids or inflammatory bowel disease. Her BMI is 25, BP: 120/80, HR: 80/min. She is willing to participate in a study to investigate a novel physical therapy intervention to improve her symptoms. She is able to voluntarily contract her pelvic floor muscles based on manometry measures.

25-year-old male with a 10-year history of type 1 diabetes mellitus, currently using continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) for the past 6 months. He has a total daily insulin dose of 0.8 units/kg and his HbA1c is 7.5%. He has no known allergies to insulin or related products. He has never had any major hypoglycemic episodes. He has a history of hypertension which is currently well-controlled on medication. He has no history of heart, liver, or kidney disease. He is not currently pregnant nor intending to become pregnant. His BMI is 24 kg/m2. He has provided informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who was diagnosed with moderate to severe Hidradenitis Suppurativa (HS) three years ago. She has tried various treatments, including antibiotics and topical creams, but they only provide temporary relief. She has been recommended to start on adalimumab treatment by her dermatologist. She works as a nurse and has a busy schedule. She lives with her husband and two children, aged 5 and 7. She is in good health otherwise, with no significant medical history. She is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand how her experience with adalimumab treatment can be improved, and to help other HS patients in the future.

62 year old woman with a history of cholecystectomy presenting with right upper quadrant pain, jaundice, and pruritus. MRI revealed a common bile duct stricture with upstream dilatation consistent with a bile duct injury. The patient has no known history of liver disease or alcohol abuse. She has no known allergies and is not taking any current medications. She is willing and able to undergo surgical intervention.

The patient is a newborn baby boy born at 27 weeks gestation at Oslo University Hospital. He weighs 950 grams and is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The baby was born via emergency C-section due to the mother's preeclampsia. The mother received steroid injections prior to delivery to help with fetal lung maturation. The baby has been stable since birth, but is currently on mechanical ventilation due to immature lungs. The parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have given their consent for the baby to participate. The baby has no known congenital malformations or genetic diseases. The medical team will evaluate the baby's eligibility for the study based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Pt is a 23yo M with a history of mandibular prognathism resulting in malocclusion and difficulty with oral hygiene. He has been experiencing jaw pain and difficulty chewing for several years. After consultation with an oral surgeon, he has been recommended for single osteotomy bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) surgery to correct his jaw alignment. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He understands and consents to the use of the new osteosynthesis system for his surgery and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. Concomitant surgeries are not planned.

The patient is a 49-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV colon cancer. The cancer has spread to her liver, and she has up to five liver metastases. She is experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has never had radiation therapy or any other treatment to her liver or abdomen. She is able to perform activities of daily living without assistance. She has a Zubrod Performance Status of 1. Her biopsy confirmed the primary malignancy, and she is expected to survive for more than 6 months. She has undergone contrast-enhanced CT, MRI, and PET/CT scans, which have identified the liver metastases. The tumors are located outside the Central Liver Zone, and she has the ability to spare a critical liver volume as defined by the protocol constraints. She is not currently receiving any other antineoplastic therapy, including surgery, cryotherapy, radiofrequency ablation, chemo-embolization, conventionally fractionated radiotherapy, brachytherapy, or hepatic artery chemotherapy. She has no history of Crohn's Disease or Ulcerative Colitis or active peptic ulcer disease. She has Child-Pugh class A hepatic cirrhosis. She is mentally sound and able to understand the proposed protocol treatment and consent process. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use effective contraceptive methods.

The patient is a 32-year-old African American female who was born and raised in the United States. She has a bachelor's degree in psychology and works as a customer service representative. She is married and has two children. She has no history of major health problems and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in this study because she wants to better understand her risk of developing certain diseases. She has access to the internet at home and is comfortable using technology. She has never experienced motion sickness or any other vestibular disorders. She wears glasses for nearsightedness, but her vision is otherwise normal. She is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about the virtual reality technology.

42-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis s/p total colectomy and end ileostomy. The patient has been using a Dansac Nova one-piece flat skin barrier for the past 6 months and reports occasional peristomal skin irritation with a score of 2 or less. He lives independently and is able to care for his stoma. He currently uses a drainable pouch and is willing to wear a 1-piece flat cut-to-fit 10-55 mm. The patient is at least 6 weeks postoperative and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study. He has not been involved in any other stoma care study in the past 30 days and does not have any medical conditions that would compromise his participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of partial edentulism who has been rehabilitated with functional dental implants and prostheses for over a year. He has been recently diagnosed with peri-implant mucositis, which has resulted in bleeding on probing and a probing depth of up to 5mm, but there is no evidence of bone loss beyond the first two threads of the implant. Additionally, he has been diagnosed with gingivitis in homologous teeth to the implants. He is a non-smoker and is not currently on any maintenance therapy. He has not received any periodontal treatment in the last six months and has not used any antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive drugs during the same period.

A 35 year old female presents with a 2-year history of breast pain. She has been diagnosed with fibrocystic breast disease and has been experiencing severe pain with a VAS pain score of 7 out of 10. The pain is bilateral and constant, and she reports difficulty sleeping and performing daily activities due to the pain. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, massage therapy, and hot/cold compresses, but none of these interventions have provided adequate relief. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any medications. She has no history of coagulopathy or infection at the site of the procedure. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her chronic mastalgia.

The patient is a 8-year-old boy diagnosed with Pervasive Developmental Disorder not otherwise specified (PDD-NOS). The boy experiences significant difficulties in social interaction, communication, and restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior or interests. He is currently taking risperidone to control his symptoms, but he still experiences difficulties in his daily life. The boy's weight is above 30 lbs, and his IQ is greater than or equal to 35. The patient's parents are willing to participate in the parent management training program to help their child manage his PDD-NOS symptoms.

A 52-year-old woman came to the clinic for a follow-up visit after being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 6 months ago. During the visit, her liver enzyme tests were above the upper limit of normal, and an MRI scan showed evidence of hepatic steatosis. She was diagnosed with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and was referred to participate in a clinical trial. She is currently taking metformin to manage her diabetes, and her HbA1c is 6.8. She reports no alcohol consumption and no history of liver disease. She is interested in participating in the trial and has given written informed consent. She is not pregnant and practices adequate contraception. She has no contraindications to sitagliptin use or MRI scans. She has no history of drug-induced liver disease or gastrointestinal bypass surgery. She will be randomized to receive either sitagliptin or placebo for 24 weeks and will be monitored for symptoms of liver disease, side effects of sitagliptin, and serum biochemical and metabolic indices.

A 16-year-old girl was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis by genetic testing when she was 6 years old. She has chronic cough, sputum production, and a history of recurrent respiratory infections. Her most recent pulmonary function test showed an FEV1 of 40% predicted. She is compliant with her current CF treatment regimen, which includes dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, and azithromycin. She has never had a lung transplant, and she has never been hospitalized for CF exacerbation in the past year. She has no known history of allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) or hypersensitivity to plasma products. She is a non-tobacco user and has no history of recreational drug use. She is not pregnant and does not have any significant medical or psychiatric illnesses. She is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis. She has experienced skin irritation, itching, and redness with raised, scaly patches on her skin. She has tried various topical treatments, but none have provided significant relief. She is currently not pregnant and is willing to participate in the clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DSXS. She is in good overall health and has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the treatment plan as directed by the study clinicians.

55-year-old male with a history of poorly controlled diabetes presents with a non-healing wound on his left foot after a partial amputation of the forefoot. The wound is greater than 10 cm2 in size and has not responded to moist wound therapy. The patient has evidence of therapy-controlled diabetes with an HbA1C less than or equal to 10%. Adequate nutrition to enable wound healing is evidenced by a prealbumin level of greater than or equal to 16 mg/dl or an albumin level of greater than or equal to 3 g/dl within 7 days of screening. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent, comply with follow-up visit schedule, and maintain a treatment diary. The patient also has adequate perfusion in the affected extremity as evidenced by Grade 1 or 2 PVR waveform as confirmed at screening. The patient is eligible for clinical trial enrollment to compare V.A.C. negative pressure wound therapy to moist wound therapy in the treatment of diabetic foot amputation wounds.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has sustained a complete rupture of her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) while playing basketball. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, allergies, or current use of medications. Her BMI is 23. She is scheduled to undergo bone-tendon-bone (BTB) ACL reconstruction surgery with a participating surgeon and is willing to follow the study protocol. She speaks fluent English and is able to provide informed consent. She has no history of diabetes or chronic use of gabapentin/pregabalin or opioids. Her American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) score is II. She is open to the use of regional anesthesia and does not have a BMI over 40.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes two years ago. She is currently on intensive insulin therapy and her HbA1c is below 10%. She is of Greek origin and follows a typical Mediterranean diet. She has no food allergies or any other medical conditions. Her family history is negative for diabetes. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She weighs 68 kg and is 165 cm tall. She has no history of neuropathy, kidney disease, hematological disturbances, liver disease, thyroid problems, arrhythmia, heart disease or cancer. She is mentally stable and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for 5 years. She is currently pregnant and is in her 8th week of gestation. She has been taking CZP for the past 12 weeks to manage her rheumatoid arthritis symptoms. She has not experienced any major side effects from the CZP therapy. The patient has no history of tuberculosis or other significant medical conditions that would affect her ability to participate in the study. She has not received any live vaccines within the past month and does not plan to receive any during the study. The patient has not had a positive or indeterminate IGRA or TST test result at screening. She is willing to continue CZP therapy throughout her pregnancy and for at least 12 weeks postpartum. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopes that her participation will contribute to better understanding of the safety and effectiveness of CZP in pregnant women with chronic inflammatory diseases.

75yo active male with a history of hypertension and mild osteoarthritis of the hip, who presented with a fall and inability to bear weight on his right lower extremity. X-rays revealed a displaced femoral neck fracture. He underwent surgery for a hemiarthroplasty of the hip joint via an anteriorolateral approach with partial repairing of soft tissue. Postoperatively, he has been compliant with physical therapy and has shown improvement in his gait and ability to bear weight. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the outcomes of full versus partial repairing of soft tissue surrounding the hip joint in femoral neck fracture patients.

Patient is a 25-year-old female who presents with moderate to severe pelvic pain and has a history of endometriosis confirmed by laparoscopy. She has been experiencing painful periods and pelvic pain during intercourse for several years. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medication with little relief. She has not been pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. The patient is in good general health and is willing to comply with electronic diary entry for the duration of study participation. She is not currently using hormonal contraception but is willing to use an acceptable non-hormonal method of contraception during the study. The patient has not participated in another clinical trial with investigational medicinal products and is not currently using endometriosis-specific treatments for symptom relief except rescue pain medication according to protocol.

This is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with preeclampsia and chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia. She is currently hospitalized in the high-risk pregnancy clinic at the Hospital of Ribeirão Preto. She is in her 32nd week of gestation and has no other maternal diseases or fetal complications as per diagnostic ultrasound examinations and fetal monitoring. However, she has been experiencing musculoskeletal pain and anxiety, which has been affecting her quality of life. She has consented to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of a physical therapy protocol aimed at reducing musculoskeletal pain and anxiety and improving quality of life in women with preeclampsia. She will be required to answer questionnaires regarding her quality of life and discomfort levels before and after undergoing the physiotherapy protocol. The progress of her pregnancy and the wellbeing of the fetus will also be monitored through imaging and laboratory tests. She is hopeful that this trial will help her manage her pain and anxiety and improve her overall quality of life during her pregnancy.

N/A - No patient description is required for this clinical trial as it is a study on physiological responses to exercise and not a treatment or intervention for a specific medical condition. Participants in this trial would be healthy individuals.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was diagnosed with Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) three years ago. He received chemotherapy and achieved complete remission (CR) with imatinib therapy. However, he suffered a relapse and underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) six months ago. The transplantation was successful and he is currently in remission. The patient has no significant medical history or comorbidities. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the efficacy of TKI therapy based on molecular monitoring of BCR/ABL levels after allo-HSCT.

A 55 year old woman came to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and distension. She was previously diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer and underwent multiple rounds of chemotherapy with recurrence of the disease. A CT scan showed peritoneal surface dissemination of the tumor that cannot be completely resected at time of abdominal exploration. She is currently not receiving any systemic therapy due to her platinum-resistant status. Her latest lab results showed normal renal and hepatic function, with ANC of 2,300/µL, platelets of 115,000/µL and Hgb of 10 g/dL. She has an ECOG Performance Score of 1. She has a peritoneal catheter placed 3 weeks ago and is willing to undergo intraperitoneal talimogene laherparepvec (TVEC) therapy for the treatment of her peritoneal surface malignancy. She has no known history of active autoimmune disease or immunosuppression, nor received previous treatment with talimogene laherparepvec or any other oncolytic virus. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use acceptable methods of effective contraception during study treatment and through 90 days after the last dose of talimogene laherparepvec.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and has been recommended for kidney transplant by his healthcare provider. He has been on dialysis for the past year and is currently on the waiting list for a deceased donor kidney. He has no history of any other organ transplant and has not received any immunosuppressive medications in the past. He has no known allergies or intolerances to any medication. He is currently married with two children and works as a construction worker. He is physically active and enjoys playing basketball with his friends. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He has no other medical conditions that could interfere with the study protocol. He has been fully informed about the study and has given his written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been sedentary for the past year. She has a BMI of 28 and has never smoked. She is a retired teacher who enjoys reading and gardening. She has no significant medical history and takes no prescription medications. She has experienced mild allergies in the past but has not required prescription medication for them. She lives independently and is post-menopausal. She has not been vaccinated for the flu in the past year and has not had any infections in the last six months. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her overall health and immune function. She has no history of severe arthritis, mental illness, or clinical depression. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in a 10-month moderate aerobic exercise training program.

A 16-year-old Caucasian male complains of persisting fatigue for the past 6 months. He states that he is constantly tired, and his energy levels are low throughout the day. He also experiences difficulty in concentrating and has missed several days of school due to the fatigue. He denies any recent infections or illnesses. He has no history of any chronic disease or drug abuse. He does not have any allergies or hypersensitivity. His family history is negative for any chronic diseases. He has no history of any abnormal ECG or blood pressure. He is not currently taking any pharmaceuticals. His BMI is in the normal range. He has a supine heart rate of 68 beats/min and a supine systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg.

Patient is a 22-year-old female college student who presents with a history of a slowly progressing, discolored, and hardened patch on her left upper arm. She reports that it has been present for the past 6 months, and it has not resolved despite her attempts to use various moisturizers and over-the-counter creams. She denies any history of trauma, systemic symptoms, or other skin lesions. She has no significant past medical history, and she is not taking any medications. She is not pregnant and does not have any known renal disease. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to try a new topical treatment for morphea.

A 35-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of ulcerative colitis has been in remission for the past month. She is currently taking mesalamine 3 grams per day. She has no prior bowel surgery except for an appendectomy when she was 18 years old. She is not pregnant and not at risk of pregnancy. She is not allergic to aspirin, mesalamine, or other salicylates. She does not have HIV or hepatitis B or C. She is interested in participating in a study to compare the maintenance of mild to moderate ulcerative colitis remission with six months of treatment with 1.5 grams of mesalamine pellets each day versus placebo.

A 55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed for 5 years, is seeking to participate in a clinical trial evaluating microvascular response in diabetic patients. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of foot ulcers or neuropathy. He does not smoke and drinks occasionally. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to research on diabetes and its complications. He has no allergies to any food or drugs.

The patient is a 14-year-old male with a clinical consensus diagnosis of ASD as defined by DSM-5 and confirmed by the Autism Diagnostic Observation schedule-2. He has an IQ score of 85 as measured by the Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence - Second Edition (WASI-II). He has no comorbid externalizing behaviours as assessed by the Childhood Behaviour Checklist (CBCL) and no clinically assessed self-injurious behaviour. The patient is fluent in English and is interested in socializing with peers but finds it challenging to navigate social situations. He is currently attending school and is receiving support from a school counsellor to develop his social skills. He has no other significant medical issues and his physical health is good. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in a social skills group training program and are excited to learn more about the KONTAKT program.

62 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that has metastasized to other parts of the body. The patient has previously been treated with at least one systemic therapy for metastatic disease. The patient must have measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 criteria with at least two lesions. The patient must express mesothelin (MSLN) and have HLA-A*02:01. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. The patient is capable of understanding and providing a written informed consent. The patient is at least 3 weeks from last systemic treatment for metastatic disease, and has a serum creatinine of ≤ 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) or estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) > 60 mL/min. The patient must have total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 X ULN, and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) < 5 x ULN. The patient must have dyspnea of grade 1 or less and oxygen saturation (SaO2) of ≥ 92% on ambient air. The patient must have an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) > 1500 cells/ mm^3. The patient must not have a history of solid organ transplant or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant. The patient must not be receiving corticosteroid therapy at a dose equivalent of > 0.5 mg/kg of prednisone per day. The patient must not have an active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppressive therapy. The patient must not have uncontrolled concurrent illness including, but not limited to, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient must not have untreated brain metastases. The patient must not be receiving active treatment for prior immune related adverse event to any immunotherapy. The patient must not have significant underlying neurologic disease.

A 55 yo F with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, who recently underwent a Coronary Computed Tomographic Angiography (CCTA) that revealed a significant amount of calcification in the coronary arteries. She has no history of myocardial infarction or stroke, but is concerned about her risk for cardiovascular events. She is not on any medications that could interfere with the study and has a life expectancy of over 2 years. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of Vitamin K2 supplementation on the progression of coronary artery calcification.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a primary diagnosis of Non-Inflammatory Degenerative Joint Disease (NIDJD) in the left hip joint. He has been experiencing chronic hip pain and stiffness for several years, which has progressively worsened and now significantly limits his daily activities. He has been evaluated by a physician who has recommended a primary cementless total hip replacement using the Tritanium® Acetabular Shell. The patient has signed an IRB approved Informed Patient Consent Form and is willing and able to comply with postoperative scheduled clinical and radiographic evaluations and rehabilitation. The patient has a BMI of 28 and does not have any active or suspected latent infection in or about the affected hip joint. He does not have any neuromuscular or neurosensory deficiencies that would limit the ability to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the device. The patient does not have any systemic diseases or metabolic disorders leading to progressive bone deterioration, and is not immunologically suppressed or receiving steroids in excess of normal physiological requirements. The patient has not undergone any previous total hip replacement or hip fusion surgery, and does not have any known sensitivity to device materials. The patient is not a prisoner.

A 45-year-old male with a known history of gout presents to the rheumatology clinic with a complaint of acute gout flare in the left big toe. The patient has been diagnosed with gout for the past 5 years and has experienced at least two gout flares in the past 12 months. He is currently on allopurinol 300mg daily to lower the serum uric acid levels. He reports no history of other rheumatologic or autoimmune diseases. He has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2. The patient is not taking any pain medications for his gout flare. The physical examination reveals a swollen and tender left big toe with erythema and warmth. The range of motion of the joint is limited due to the pain. The diagnostic workup confirms the diagnosis of acute gout flare. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a topical treatment for acute gout flare.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain in his right knee due to osteoarthritis for the past few years. The pain has been interfering with his daily activities, and he has been advised to undergo a total knee arthroplasty to alleviate the pain. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has not had any previous surgery on his knee. He speaks and understands Danish fluently. However, he is slightly overweight but not obese, with a BMI of 28. He does not have any known allergies to local anesthetics. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of a compression bandage in prolonging analgesia after total knee arthroplasty.

A 27-week gestational age male infant weighing 800g at birth is eligible for this clinical trial. The infant is currently 3 days old, and the mother's prenatal and obstetrical history is unremarkable. The infant is receiving mechanical ventilation support for respiratory distress syndrome and has been started on parenteral nutrition. Blood cultures were obtained at birth, which were negative. The infant has not received any prior antifungal therapy. The parents have provided consent for their infant to participate in this study.

The patient is a 55 year old Hispanic male with a history of end stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis for the past 5 years. He has a central venous catheter (CVC) placed in his right internal jugular vein for hemodialysis access. He has been experiencing difficulty in withdrawing blood from the CVC during his dialysis sessions for the past 2 weeks. He has no history of allergies and is currently taking medications for hypertension and diabetes. He has no history of bleeding disorders or recent surgeries. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial.

A 52-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital for a total knee replacement surgery due to severe osteoarthritis. He has a history of chronic back pain for which he has been using opioid medications for the past year. He is currently taking oxycodone 10 mg every 6 hours for pain management. His pre-surgery morphine equivalent is 30. He has an ASA score of 2 and is otherwise healthy. The patient is interested in exploring non-pharmacologic pain management strategies to avoid the potential side effects of opioids. He has no history of skin disease or allergies and is cognitively intact.

A 30-year-old Chinese male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5 kg/m^2, which falls within the inclusion criteria of the trial. He has not donated blood or plasma in the past month or more than 400 mL within the past 3 months. He reports smoking occasionally but not more than 5 cigarettes per day, which is within the exclusion criteria of the trial. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge and help others in the future.

Sarah is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer. She has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with no success in controlling her disease. She is experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. Her performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive MK-4166 monotherapy or MK-4166 plus pembrolizumab combination therapy for her advanced solid tumor. She has measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. She has adequate organ function, and her pregnancy test was negative. She is willing to use two methods of birth control, and she is not on any chronic systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive medication. She has not participated in any study of an investigational agent or used an investigational device within the last 28 days. She is not expected to require any other form of antineoplastic therapy while on the study.

A 50-year-old male who works as a construction worker has been experiencing mild venous disease on his bilateral lower extremities for the past 6 months. He has skin type III and is in good health. He has no history of skin conditions, deep vein thrombosis, thrombophlebitis, thromboembolic disease, and/or underlying hypercoagulable medical condition. The patient has no history of neurological conditions, and he is ambulatory. He is not taking disulfiram, tamoxifen, or oral hormone therapy. He has not undergone any other cosmetic or surgical treatments to the treatment area in the past three months. He is willing to follow study instructions and complete all required visits, as well as has agreed to and signed the written informed consent form. He is not pregnant, lactating or in childbearing age. He is sexually active and is using an approved contraceptive measure.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis, and the patient is currently scheduled for surgery. The tumor size is 3 cm in diameter, and imaging studies have failed to detect any regional or distant metastases. The patient has no significant past medical history, and his performance status is ECOG 1. The patient has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function, and his blood pressure is well-controlled with antihypertensive medication. The patient has undergone FDG-PET/CT, DCE MRI, and DWI MRI, and tumor and normal mucosa biopsies have been obtained during staging endoscopy. Blood samples have also been collected for translational research. The patient is not currently participating in any other interventional clinical trials, and he has given written informed consent to participate in this study. The patient is not diabetic, does not have interstitial lung disease, and has not experienced significant weight loss in the last 6 months. The patient is willing to use an adequate method of contraception to avoid pregnancy in case of female partner during the study and for 6 months beyond stop of treatment.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her vital signs were stable upon arrival. A neurological exam revealed a right-sided facial droop, dysarthria, and right hemiparesis. National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was calculated as 9. CT scan of the brain showed a left middle cerebral artery (MCA) ischemic stroke. She was treated with intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) within the recommended time frame. After being admitted to the hospital, she received a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program including physical and occupational therapy. She is now enrolled in the study for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) use in acute stroke. She is able to stand and transfer with moderate assistance. Her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28. Her paretic index finger shows impaired flexion/extension motion at the metacarpophalangeal (MP) joint. She does not have a history of seizure, metal in the head, or psychiatric disorders. She is not receiving tricyclic antidepressants or neuroleptics. She is able to follow three-step commands and does not have hemineglect. She does not depend on a ventilator, nasogastric tube, or implanted medical device. She has no other co-morbidities impairing upper extremity function. She is expected to stay at Courage Kenny Rehabilitation Institute for at least 7 treatment days.

As this is a clinical trial focused on assessing the impact of SBAR on safety attitudes in the perinatal department, there are no specific patient descriptions required for this study. The trial is open to all physicians and nurses working in the perinatal department, regardless of their gender, age, or medical history.

The patient is a 17-year-old high school student who has been struggling with moderate acne vulgaris for the past year. She experiences papules and pustules on her forehead, cheeks, and chin. She has tried over-the-counter acne treatments with little success. She is otherwise healthy and does not take any medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial as she is eager to find an effective treatment for her acne.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 8 months ago. She has been on several disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) but has had inadequate response. She has been experiencing moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness in her fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders, hips, knees and ankles, and has difficulty performing daily activities. Her swollen joint count (SJC) is 6 and tender joint count (TJC) is 8. She is currently taking prednisone 5 mg/day and ibuprofen 800 mg three times a day for pain control. She has no history of major surgery or recurrent infections. She is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous versus intravenous administration of tocilizumab for the treatment of her rheumatoid arthritis.

A 28-year-old healthy female presents for a bioequivalence study for SHR-1314. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She weighs 58 kg and has a BMI of 22. She is able to understand and communicate with the investigator and has given written informed consent to participate in the study. She has normal physical examination results and laboratory test results, including blood, chemistry, urine, drug screening, coagulation function test, ECG and X-ray chest test. She has no history of hypersensitivity to any of the study drug constituent, chronic or recurrent infectious disease, ongoing alcohol or drug abuse or any known malignancy or history of malignancy of any organ system within the past 5 years. She has not participated in any clinical study for any drug or medical device within 3 months before screening and has not been vaccinated with live attenuated vaccine within 12 weeks prior to screening. She is not pregnant or nursing. The investigator has deemed her suitable for participating in this study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stage II hypertension with a systolic pressure of 165 mmHg. He has been taking amlodipine monotherapy for the past 6 months with little improvement in his blood pressure. He has no history of allergies to ARBs, CCBs, or thiazide diuretics. He is not taking any other antihypertensive medications. He has no history of stroke, heart attack or unstable angina, autoimmune diseases, or liver disease. He has not had any surgical or medical condition that might alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of any drug. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has not had any drug or alcohol abuse within the last 2 years. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the trial.

Patient is a 60-year-old Hispanic male who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer after experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He has a smoking history of 20 pack-years and has worked in construction for over 30 years, which may have exposed him to wood smoke. He has previously undergone a biopsy and has tissue samples available for research purposes. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand the frequency of EGFR mutations in Hispanic/Latino individuals with lung cancer. The study will involve examining his lung tissue collected from the previous biopsy to determine if he has any EGFR mutations. The patient hopes that the study will lead to better personalized approaches for the treatment of lung cancer in the Hispanic/Latino community.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male had a stroke 6 months ago, which resulted in paralysis in his right arm and leg. He has been undergoing physical therapy for the past 4 months, but he still has difficulty with movement in his affected upper limb. He has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or any musculoskeletal disorder. He is able to follow instructions and communicate effectively. He has no family history of epilepsy. He is married and lives with his wife. He used to work as an accountant before his stroke. His past medical history is unremarkable. He has no sensory impairment, and he can sit on a chair independently for more than 30 minutes. His Brunnstrom's recovery stage is stage 4. His Modified Ashworth Scale score is 2. His Barthel Index score is 50. His Upper Extremity Subscale of the Fugl-Meyer Motor Function Assessment score is 20. His Thermal Quantitative Sensory Testing is normal.

A 50-year-old man with recurrent episodes of heartburn and acid regurgitation for the past 1 year came to the clinic seeking treatment for his symptoms. He has been taking over-the-counter antacids regularly for relief. He has no history of esophageal or gastric surgery, Barrett's mucosa or severe co-morbidities. He is not taking any anticoagulant or immunosuppressive drugs. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally, not exceeding 5 units per week. He has no history of any allergies. He is willing to stop taking PPIs for at least 10 days before the tests. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find out more about his condition and to help others with similar symptoms.

A 25-year old healthy female who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She takes no medications and has no significant past medical history. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She does not have any allergies or history of severe allergic reactions. She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. She is willing to use contraception during the study and for at least 3 months after study completion. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 42-year-old female who works as an accountant is morbidly obese with a BMI of 45. She has a history of hypertension for 5 years and has been on antihypertensive medication. She does not have a history of liver disease, but her recent blood tests showed elevated liver enzymes. She has no history of alcohol abuse and her viral hepatitis markers are negative. She is on a low-fat diet and exercises regularly but has not been able to lose weight. She is interested in bariatric surgery as a treatment option for her obesity and liver health. She has not taken any antibiotics or probiotics in the last month and is not on any immunomodulatory drugs. She understands the study requirements and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She lives with her husband and two children and has a supportive family.

A 45-year-old African-American woman has been undergoing hemodialysis treatment for the past 5 years due to chronic kidney disease. She has a medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. She is compliant with her medications which include lisinopril, metformin, and atorvastatin. She has no known drug allergies. She has been receiving darbepoetin alfa on a weekly basis to maintain her hemoglobin levels within the target range. She has had no recent hospitalizations or surgical procedures. She denies any active infections or symptoms such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath. She has no history of blood clots or bleeding disorders. Her vital signs are stable and within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate reticulocyte and hemoglobin kinetics under different ESAs and administration intervals. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of shortness of breath and coughing up pink, frothy sputum. She has been diagnosed with pulmonary edema, but the underlying cause is not known. She has no history of steroid use and is otherwise healthy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the analysis of sphingolipid metabolism in patients with pulmonary edema. She will provide samples of bronchoalveolar lavage and EDTA-blood for the analysis of sphingolipids, ceramide, sphingomyelin-phosphodiesterase, and cytokines as part of the study.

This is a 56 year old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B who was found to have a 4.5 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver on routine ultrasound imaging. Further evaluation with CT and MRI confirmed the presence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) without evidence of extrahepatic spread. The patient underwent surgical resection of the tumor and the postoperative pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. The patient has no history of other malignancies and has not received any treatment for the HCC prior to surgery. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history except for a remote history of smoking, which he quit 10 years ago. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of the use of ultrasound imaging in predicting histological differentiation grade of HCC.

A 45 year old woman came to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath and bone pain. She was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago and underwent lumpectomy, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, her cancer has metastasized to her lungs and bones. Her HER-2 status was found to be 3+ using IHC. She underwent brain MRI which revealed no metastasis. She has no history of allergic reaction to docetaxel. Her performance status is 1, and her liver, kidney and cardiac functions were normal. She is not pregnant or nursing, and has no other concurrent illness. She is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent.
