A 25 year old female presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and wheezing. She has a history of asthma and has been using her rescue inhaler more frequently in the past few days. She reports no fever or chest pain. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. Upon examination, she is found to have wheezing in both lungs and decreased air movement. Her oxygen saturation level is 92% on room air. The patient is diagnosed with an asthma exacerbation and treated with nebulized albuterol and ipratropium, and intravenous corticosteroids. After improvement, the patient is discharged from the emergency department and is given a prescription for an inhaled corticosteroid and a rescue inhaler. The patient is approached for participation in a clinical trial comparing three different inhalers for the prevention of asthma relapse after discharge from the emergency department. She meets the inclusion criteria and is not excluded based on the exclusion criteria.

As this is a pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity study for patients already diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and enrolled in the ALL2GETHER pilot protocol, the patient description would be limited to those who meet the inclusion criteria. The patient should have been diagnosed with ALL and currently receiving treatment on the ALL2GETHER pilot protocol. There are no specific age or gender requirements mentioned in the eligibility criteria, so the patient can be of any age or gender. The patient should not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has been diagnosed with antisocial behavior problems and is a forensic inpatient in a psychiatric hospital. He has a history of depression, anxiety, and poor sleep quality. The patient is currently not taking any vitamin D supplements or any other medication. He has a history of drug and alcohol abuse, but is currently sober for six months. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has an intelligence quotient greater than 70. He understands the study requirements and agrees to attend all appointments and follow the study protocol.

A 50-year-old premenopausal female with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer after recurrence following an initial diagnosis of localized disease. She has been enrolled in the protocol for high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue using the "STAMP V" regimen. She has not been enrolled in any other research transplant protocol whose primary endpoint is response duration or recovery time from toxic effects. She has no brain or CNS metastases and her hormone receptor status is not specified. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80-100% and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. Her WBC count is at least 3,000/mm3 and platelet count is at least 100,000/mm3. Her bilirubin and SGOT levels are no greater than 1.5 and 2.5 times normal, respectively. Her creatinine is no greater than 1.8 mg/dL and creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min. She has a systolic ejection fraction of at least 50% and no significant cardiovascular disease or cardiac arrhythmia requiring drug or device intervention. Her DLCO and FEV1 are greater than 50% and she has no significant peripheral neuropathy or CNS disease. She is not pregnant or lactating, is not HIV positive, and has no concurrent active infections requiring IV antibiotic therapy. She has no significant gastrointestinal bleeding or uncontrolled peptic ulcer disease, no history of inflammatory bowel disease, and no clinically significant autoimmune disease. She has no other serious illness or medical condition and has not received any investigational drugs within the last 4 weeks. She is not currently receiving concurrent chemotherapy or corticosteroids, radiotherapy, or investigational drugs. She may be a suitable candidate for this clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of interleukin-12 in treating women with metastatic breast cancer who have received high-dose chemotherapy and peripheral stem cell transplantation.

A 45-year-old female presents with a recent diagnosis of ovarian cancer. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy greater than 6 months. Imaging has revealed the presence of 3 synchronous lesions in her abdomen and pelvis. She underwent surgery and received chemotherapy, but her disease has recurred and she is not a candidate for further systemic therapy due to comorbidities and previous severe toxicity. Salvage surgery or other local therapies are not feasible. She has undergone BRCA1/2 gene testing, and the results show a somatic mutation in BRCA1. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of SBRT in oligo-metastatic/persistent/recurrent ovarian cancer. The lesions are all smaller than 5 centimeters in diameter.

42 year old male with a history of HIV infection for 5 years, confirmed by ELISA and p24 antigen testing. Patient reports symptoms of shortness of breath, cough, and fever for 4 days. Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates consistent with Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP). The patient has not received any prior treatment for PCP prophylaxis or therapy. The patient has an (A-a) DO2 of 38 mmHg on room air. The patient has no known allergies to clindamycin, lincomycin, primaquine or related drugs, and has no history of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, NAD methemoglobin reductase deficiency, or hemoglobin M abnormality. The patient has not received any systemic steroids or investigational agents within 14 days of study entry and has not received any antiprotozoal therapy for the current episode of PCP or prophylaxis within 6 weeks of study entry. The patient does not have severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or any other medical condition that precludes oral therapy. The patient is willing to sign an informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a BMI of 23. She reports no history of significant medical conditions and is not on any medications that may affect salivation or taste. She has no allergies or dietary restrictions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She does not smoke and is not currently dieting, nor does she have a history of binge eating. She enjoys the taste of lemon and lime and scores at least 50 on a 100 mm visual analogue scale. Her score on the Three Factor Eating Questionnaire-Cognitive Restraint scale is less than or equal to 12, indicating low dietary restraint. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially aid in decreasing her food intake and promoting weight management.

This is a 22 year-old male with a history of epilepsy, diagnosed with partial onset seizures at the age of 18. He has been treated with two standard anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) for the past 3 years, with the doses meeting the daily dose specified for the treatment of epilepsy in the package insert. The frequency of his seizures has been 15 times in the past 12 weeks and at least twice in every 4 weeks. He has not been diagnosed with status epilepticus in the past 3 months and has not undergone surgery for epilepsy within the past 2 years. The patient has no history of oral treatment with Levetiracetam (LEV). He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of levetiracetam as an adjunctive treatment for partial onset seizures.

A 55-year-old man presents with chronic shoulder pain and limited range of motion. He reports a history of a fall onto his outstretched arm several months ago. Imaging studies reveal a full-thickness rotator cuff tear. The patient has no history of prior shoulder surgery or recurrent tears. He is fully cognitively intact and able to understand and follow instructions for the post-operative rehabilitation protocol. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially decrease the likelihood of retear after arthroscopic repair.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who suffered an ischemic stroke six months ago. He has a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and type 2 diabetes. He takes medications to manage these conditions. He experienced numbness on his left side, difficulty speaking, and weakness in his left arm and leg. He was hospitalized for a week and received treatment for his stroke. He has since recovered but is concerned about the risk of another stroke. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on the secondary prevention of stroke. He is willing to follow the study requirements and attend regular follow-up appointments.

22-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia spectrum disorder, presenting with positive symptoms such as auditory hallucinations and delusions. He has been on multiple antipsychotic medications, but the side effects have been difficult to manage. He has a history of drug abuse, but is currently abstinent. He is able to understand and speak English fluently, and is willing to participate in the study. He has no history of sleep apnea, heart condition or seizure, and has no known drug allergies. He is able to swallow a pill. The treating physician has determined him to be healthy and eligible for the study.

Marie is a 38 year old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression for the past year. She has been seeing a therapist and taking medication, but has not seen much improvement in her symptoms. She has no history of chronic illnesses or physical disabilities, and has not participated in a healing ceremony before. Marie is interested in exploring alternative forms of therapy and is excited about the possibility of participating in a traditional African healing ceremony.

A 16-year-old female who is currently on intensive community probation has been identified as a potential candidate for the CHOICES-TEEN intervention. She has a history of vaginal intercourse with a male in the last 90 days and has reported inconsistent and ineffective use of contraception and condoms. She also reports drinking at risk levels and smoking. She speaks English and is available for the follow-up period. She is not pregnant or infertile.

The patient is a 45-year-old right-handed male who suffered a stroke 2 months ago. He was diagnosed with ideomotor apraxia, which has affected his ability to perform skilled hand movements. He reports difficulty in performing tasks such as using utensils or tools, and has trouble with gestures like waving goodbye. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders prior to the stroke. His physical exam is unremarkable except for mild weakness in his left hand. He has given informed consent to participate in this study. He will undergo two outpatient sessions, each lasting up to 3 hours, in which he will have an MRI scan. During the scans, he will be asked to perform a series of skilled hand movements with his right hand in response to directions on a screen. The movements will be recorded on videotape for analysis. He will also complete a medical history questionnaire and a physical exam. He will not be eligible for the study if he has any metallic implants or if he is pregnant.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the last 2 years. He has tried several medications for benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH) without significant improvement. His international prostate symptom score (IPSS) is 18 and his peak urinary flow rate (Qmax) is 10 ml/sec. His prostate size, as measured by transrectal ultrasound (TRUS), is 70cc. He has not been diagnosed with bladder cancer or any neurological disorder affecting bladder function. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing two laser techniques for treating BPH: Holmium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (HOLEP) versus (greenlight) XPS Laser Photoselective Vapo-Enucleation of Prostate (PVEP). The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no active urinary tract infection. He is not in retention secondary to BPH and does not have a history of bladder cancer within the last 2 years.

A 35-year-old Caucasian woman is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to having gallstones. She has a history of anxiety and is currently taking medication for it. She exercises regularly and has no respiratory issues. She is married and has two children. She is concerned about the postoperative pain and would like to participate in a study that could help alleviate the pain without taking more medication. She is willing to perform breathing exercises using the biofeedback device (ResCalm) if it can help manage postoperative pain. She has no history of any major surgeries or chronic illnesses. She is an ASA class 2 patient. Her preoperative STAI score is 45.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who is a non-vegetarian and consumes a regular diet. She has no history of ingestion of Carbamazepine or any other medication. She lives in a suburban area in Israel and consumes vegetables regularly. She has no history of chronic illnesses or ongoing medical treatment. Her urine and hair samples have been tested to determine the presence of any pharmaceuticals at baseline, which came out negative. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the required diet and drinking water guidelines throughout the study period.

A 56-year-old male presents with a history of recurrent episodes of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory workup is significant for an elevated bilirubin level of 2.5 mg/dL and an elevation in liver enzymes. An ultrasound of the abdomen reveals a dilated common bile duct with the presence of multiple small stones. He is referred for evaluation and treatment of suspected bile duct stones via endoscopic ultrasound. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome and underwent an angioplasty to open a blocked artery. His blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg at admission. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it regularly. He has no history of asthma, COPD, glaucoma, or prostatic disorders. His ECG showed no evidence of arrhythmias or atrio-ventricular block. He is currently stable and able to tolerate oral medications. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the treatment of acute coronary syndrome.

62-year-old man from rural Punjab, Pakistan, who suffered a stroke 6 months ago and has been experiencing difficulty in performing daily activities like dressing, eating, and walking. He speaks Punjabi and has limited education. He is currently undergoing physiotherapy and speech therapy at a local hospital. He lives with his wife and two adult children who help him with his daily activities. He has no other major medical conditions and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic cancer. He has completed 5-FU based chemoradiation therapy more than 4 weeks ago but no more than 12 weeks ago. He has a completely resected disease or unresectable locally advanced disease. He expresses HLA-A2 and has histologically or cytologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the pancreas that expresses CEA either by IHC or serology. He has not received any previous CEA vaccine and does not have any known autoimmune disorders or conditions of immunosuppression. He has normal organ and marrow function and an ECOG performance status of 0-1. He has a life expectancy greater than 3 months and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He does not have any active second malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of type 1 diabetes. He has been on insulin therapy for the past 5 years and struggles to maintain his blood sugar levels within the target range despite following a strict diet and exercise regimen. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no other chronic illnesses. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the potential benefits of metformin as an add-on therapy to insulin for glycemic control in type 1 diabetes. He has not been pregnant, lactating, or taking any other anti-diabetic drugs.

58-year-old male with a history of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of CP-461. The patient has intermediate-risk CLL according to the Rai Staging System, and has failed at least one prior chemotherapy regimen which included fludarabine. The patient has not received any therapy within the last 4 weeks and has fully recovered from the acute effects of prior therapy. The patient's platelet count is 85,000/mm3 and hemoglobin is 9 gm/dL. The patient has an expected remaining life span of more than three months and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is not currently pregnant, lactating or planning to become pregnant during the trial. The patient is willing and able to sign an informed consent document.

A 13-month-old boy from a low-income family in Bangladesh was brought to the clinic by his mother. He was born full-term and had no significant illnesses in the past. His mother reported that he had a poor appetite and was not gaining weight as expected. He weighed 7.8 kg and his height was 72 cm, which was below the average for his age. He had no signs of acute illness, and his physical exam was unremarkable. His family has no history of chronic illness, and he is not on any medications. He has not been vaccinated yet. His mother is breastfeeding him and also feeds him with homemade rice, lentils, and vegetables. The family has no access to clean drinking water and uses water from a nearby stream for drinking and cooking.

A 30-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of multiple sinonasal surgeries due to recurrent sinus infections is scheduled for a reconstructive procedure to correct a deviated septum. She is a non-smoker, with no known allergies, and she reports a moderate caffeine intake. She is currently taking no medications. Upon examination, the patient reports a decreased sense of smell and taste, which she attributes to her previous surgeries. She has no current symptoms of sinusitis. The tongue examination reveals a normal anatomy of the fungiform papillae, and the patient reports being able to taste various compounds, including bitter compounds such as caffeine and PROP. Her genotyping results reveal that she is heterozygous for the TAS2R38 receptor gene (AVI/PAV). She agrees to participate in the study and completes a beverage frequency questionnaire and taste test before the scheduled procedure. She will provide nasal epithelium and taste tissue samples during the procedure, which will be analyzed for TAS2R38 mRNA expression and AHL-induced respiratory defenses. If necessary, she will provide additional samples during any subsequent sinonasal procedures.

A 20 year old college student who is a varsity soccer player has recently suffered a concussion during a game. He has a history of previous concussions from playing soccer and has been cleared to play after each one. He is complaining of headaches, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. He has been advised by his coach to take some time off from practice and games until he is cleared by a doctor. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help determine when it is safe for him to return to play. He speaks English fluently and does not have any other medical conditions that would interfere with the tests.

The patient is a healthy male or female between the ages of 21 to 55 years old. They have no history of clinically significant diseases and are not currently experiencing any health issues. They are willing to participate in a Single-Dose Pharmacokinetics and Relative Bioavailability Study of Tolterodine from Two Microspheres in Powder Blend Extended Release Formulations compared to the commercial extended release capsules. The patient should be able to understand and comply with the study requirements and provide informed consent to participate. They will be required to attend study visits and follow study procedures as outlined by the researchers.

A 27-year-old sexually active male with no history of HIV infection is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a gel called OB-002H for vaginal and rectal administration. He is in good health, with no significant underlying medical conditions, and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past three months. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and agrees to local sexually transmitted infection (STI) reporting requirements. He is willing to be sexually abstinent (anal and vaginal sex) for 72 hours before and after each visit except Visit 1. He is also willing to abstain from inserting any non-trial products for rectal or vaginal application for 72 hours prior to each trial visit. He is willing to use highly effective contraceptive methods during trial participation. His BMI is within the range of 18-30 kg/m2. He has not had any recent surgeries or pregnancies and does not have chronic or recurrent symptomatic vaginal candidiasis.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing hearing loss for the past 5 years. She is a native English speaker and has been using hearing aids for the past year, but they no longer provide sufficient benefit for her. She has been recommended for cochlear implantation and has agreed to participate in this clinical trial. Her unaided detection threshold is currently at 70 decibels hearing level at 125 Hz. She has no cognitive delay or impairment. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her hearing outcomes and potentially benefit other patients in the future.

A 10-year-old child diagnosed with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy presents with difficulty walking due to tightness and stiffness in the muscles of their legs. The child is able to walk without assistive devices but has trouble maintaining balance and falls frequently. They have no history of respiratory difficulties, kidney disease, or allergies to any medications. The child has not taken oral baclofen or other anti-spasticity medications in the past three months and has not received botulinum toxin injections or undergone any ankle, foot, lower leg, or Achilles tendon surgery in the past year. The child is able to follow instructions and comply with the strengthening program and strength testing required for the clinical trial.

A 25-year-old male college student who exercises regularly is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of tart cherry on exercise-induced muscle damage. He has a BMI of 23 and has not experienced any lower limb musculoskeletal injuries that prevented him from exercising in the last three months. He is in good health and does not have any known health conditions that could interfere with the data collection protocol. He is willing to participate in both the molecular mechanism of action part of the study (Part A) and the muscle recovery part of the study (Part B). He is willing to follow the supplementation guidelines and other instructions provided by the experimenter, including abstaining from caffeine, alcohol, and strenuous exercise for two five-day periods during the follow-up period (days 6-10 of the trial). He is willing to wear a triaxial accelerometer throughout each arm of the trial and keep food diaries for the duration of each arm of the trial. He is willing to abstain from consumption of anti-inflammatory or analgesic medications, including NSAIDs and aspirin, for 48 hours prior to and throughout each arm of the trial. He is not currently using any prescription medication or nutritional/dietary supplements. He does not have any allergies or sensitivities to cherries or any of the additional ingredients found within the tart cherry test products. He is able to provide voluntary written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis and previous total knee replacement surgery 5 years ago presented to the orthopedic clinic with pain and swelling in her right knee. She reported difficulty walking and performing daily activities. Imaging studies revealed loosening of the components of the previous knee replacement and the need for revision surgery. The patient was informed about the study and agreed to participate. She has not received intravenous vancomycin in the past week and has no known hypersensitivity to vancomycin. She has no significant cardiac or respiratory abnormalities and has no contraindications to using the intraosseous vascular access system. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has given her informed consent.

Patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She has undergone primary surgical cytoreduction followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. However, her cancer has relapsed and she is now experiencing symptoms such as pelvic pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. She has been referred for gene therapy as a potential treatment option. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including having tissue available for biopsy, no significant peritoneal fibrosis, and a site of disease less than 5 cm in diameter. She has normal hematopoietic, hepatic, renal, and cardiovascular function, and is HIV-negative. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no acute infections. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has no allergies to the study reagent. The patient is hopeful that this treatment will be effective in treating her cancer and is excited to participate in the trial.

A 42-year-old female with a history of multinodular goiter and compressive symptoms, such as dysphagia and difficulty breathing, is scheduled for thyroidectomy. She has no known allergies and has never experienced any bronchitis or asthma. She is currently on no medication and has no significant past medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no family history of thyroid disease or respiratory issues. She is generally healthy and has no known risk factors for postoperative complications. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and difficulty breathing for the past few months. The patient's medical history includes frequent respiratory infections and an inability to perform daily activities without assistance. The patient has been referred for Pimax evaluation and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to establish a non-invasive and indirect measure of Pimax. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any other contra-indications for nuclear magnetic resonance.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is currently working as a software engineer. She has a BMI of 25 kg/meters squared and is generally healthy. She usually eats three meals a day and has no known food allergies. She does not smoke or take any prescription or non-prescription drugs that may affect appetite or food intake. She is willing to avoid alcohol the day before and during test days and to refrain from eating after 10 pm the evening before test sessions. She is interested in participating in this study to learn more about how energy density and cognitive framing of satiation using food information can influence her consumption at a meal. She has not participated in a similar study in the past year and is not a student, faculty, or staff member in nutritional sciences or psychology.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis. She has been experiencing symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for the past 6 months. She has previously been treated with corticosteroids and 6-mercaptopurine, but has not responded adequately to these therapies. She is now being considered for treatment with Golimumab. The patient has no history of cancer, type one diabetes, or autoimmune diseases. She has no current infections or inflammation other than related to her ulcerative colitis. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent. The patient has undergone a tuberculosis screening and has tested negative.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her third trimester. She has a history of depression and is concerned about the potential for postpartum depression after giving birth. She is sedentary, defined as exercising 60 minutes or less per week, and has received healthcare provider consent to participate in this clinical trial. She is fluent in English and able to walk for 30 minutes continuously. She has no musculoskeletal problems or conditions that would make exercise unsafe or unwise. She is not currently enrolled in another exercise or weight management study and is not taking medication that interferes with heart rate response to exercise. She is willing to be randomly assigned to either the exercise intervention or the health and wellness contact control condition. She has read and signed the consent form and is committed to participating in the study to prevent postpartum depression.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is concerned about his cholesterol levels. He is 170 cm tall and weighs 80 kg. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. He has a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease. He has never been diagnosed with any medical conditions but wants to take steps to improve his health. His current LDL cholesterol level is 130 mg/dL and his triglycerides are within normal limits. He does not take any lipid-lowering medication or supplements. His blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg and his BMI is 27.68. He does not smoke or use any drugs. He has no history of significant medical or surgical conditions that could limit his participation in the study.

This clinical trial may be suitable for a 49-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer that has spread to her spine. She had undergone radiation therapy for the spine metastasis 8 months ago, but now her symptoms have returned. She is experiencing back pain that radiates down her legs, weakness in her legs, and difficulty walking. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. She has not yet undergone surgery or laser interstitial thermotherapy but is willing to consider spine radiosurgery. She is able to lie supine for up to 2 hours and has no more than 3 contiguous vertebral body levels treated at a single site, and no more than 3 discontiguous vertebral body levels treated. She has radiographic evidence of progression at a spinal site previously irradiated greater than 6 months prior to randomization. She has received prior conventional external-beam radiation therapy to the site of interest to no more than a critical neural tissue dose equivalent dose (EQD)2/2 of 42 Gy in a single session or 50 Gy cumulative over multiple sessions and cauda equina dose EQD2/2 of 50 Gy in a single session or 60 Gy cumulative over multiple sessions. She has a vertebral body site to be treated located from T1 to L5. She is willing to undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spine and sign informed consent verifying that she is aware of the investigational nature of this study. She is not pregnant and has no history of lymphoma or myeloma.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a diagnosis of stage III colon cancer. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment and has completed 3 cycles so far. He has a history of hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any recreational drugs. He is married and has two children. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. He is interested in participating in the study and has given his consent to receive an mRNA anti-SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. He understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with them. He has no known immune deficiency other than his cancer diagnosis.

Patient is a 47-year-old female who has been experiencing lower back pain for the past year. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and pain management with no improvement in her symptoms. MRI revealed degenerative disc disease and spinal stenosis at L4-L5 and L5-S1 levels. The patient has a BMI of 28 and is a non-smoker. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications that could inhibit fusion or bone metabolism. The patient has agreed to participate in the Accell Evo3™ Demineralized Bone Matrix in Instrumented Lumbar Spine Fusion clinical trial to undergo spinal fusion using Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion (TLIF), with Accell Evo3 as an adjunct. She is willing and able to attend all follow-up appointments and undergo required radiographic exams up to 24 months post-surgery. The patient has signed the informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria, with no exclusion criteria applicable to her.

A 6-year-old male patient was scheduled for a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in the IGT department. The patient had no known medical conditions and no history of anesthesia. Physical examination revealed no cranio-facial anomalies, cervical spine/upper thoracic anomalies or laryngomalacia/tracheomalacia. The patient did not have chronic hypoxemia or any other cardiac conditions with right to left shunts. The patient will be positioned in a supine position during the procedure. The patient and their legal guardian have provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 30 presents with concerns about her weight and overall health. She has no known chronic diseases and is considered generally healthy. She is willing to maintain a consistent diet and exercise pattern throughout the duration of the study and is willing to consume a dairy and egg-based fat challenge meal twice, at the start and end of the study. She has no history of allergic reactions to fruit, dairy or egg products, but is a former smoker who quit over a year ago. She is not currently taking any dietary supplements and is willing to refrain from their use throughout the trial. She does not consume fatty fish on a regular basis and has no history of cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes mellitus, inflammatory bowel disease, lactose intolerance, or any other chronic health condition. She has not undergone any gastric bypass or other surgery that physically alters her gastrointestinal tract. Her blood pressure is within normal limits and her fasting serum triglycerides are less than 200 mg/dl. She is not currently taking any lipid lowering or blood pressure lowering medications or dietary supplements. She is not taking Coumadin, aspirin, or other medications that influence hemostasis, and has not taken antibiotics within the past week. She is not currently using any medications with vasoconstricting properties. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use a medically approved form of birth control. She does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not consume more than 14 alcoholic beverages per week. She has not participated in another clinical trial within 28 days of enrollment into the study.

Patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of gout for the past 8 years. Despite dietary modification and allopurinol treatment, his serum uric acid (sUA) level remains elevated at 8.5 mg/dL. He experiences recurrent flares in his big toe, ankle, and knee joints, which have a significant impact on his daily activities. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has no significant medical history of cardiovascular, renal, pulmonary, hepatic, gallbladder or biliary tract, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, or psychiatric diseases. He is not currently taking any UA-lowering medications. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and agrees to participate in the study. He has a BMI of 27 kg/m^2 at screening. He is a married heterosexual male and does not plan to have children. He has negative urine and serum pregnancy tests. He does not have any history of stomach or intestinal surgery, HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, or hepatitis C antibody. He has normal liver function aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and total bilirubin levels. He has not experienced any gout flares that have resolved within 14 days prior to the first treatment with study drug. He is not known to have a hypersensitivity to URAT1 inhibitors, XOIs, or related compounds. He has not received any other investigational product within 30 days prior to the dose of study drug on Day 1 or planning to take an investigational agent during the study. He has not used any drugs or nutrients known to modulate cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A activity or any strong or moderate inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4, starting from 14 days prior to dose administration on Day 1 until the final end of study assessments. He has not participated in strenuous exercise from 48 hours prior to Check-in (Day -1) or during the study through the final end of study assessment. He has not donated or lost a significant volume (>500 mL) of blood or plasma within 30 days prior to Check-in (Day -1). He has no malignancy within 5 years of the screening visit.

10-year-old boy with a history of chronic immune-thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) and autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is being considered for a second-line immunomodulatory treatment. The patient has failed first-line treatments including immunoglobulins and corticosteroids. The patient is not currently under immunosuppressants for any other immunological pathology. The patient and his legal representatives have been informed about the clinical trial and have agreed to participate. The patient is registered in the OBS'CEREVANCE database and meets the inclusion criteria for this study.

A 22-year-old female undergraduate student from a private university in João Pessoa, northeastern Brazil presents with a history of being in a stable heterosexual relationship for over a year and having an active sex life. She has never been pregnant or given birth. She is clinically healthy and has agreed to participate in a study evaluating the consistency of three questionnaires for sexual function evaluation in young healthy women. She is willing to participate in an 8-week training program consisting of bipedal exercises performed at home. She has signed the informed consent to take part in the study.

A 25 year old woman with no history of neurological disorders or conditions comes to the clinic interested in participating in a cognitive control study. She is fluent in English and has no difficulty understanding or speaking the language. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. She reports no current or past use of drugs or alcohol and has never undergone brain surgery or had any brain devices or implants. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no personal or family history of mental or psychiatric disorder. The patient is seeking to participate in this study because she is interested in learning more about cognitive control and is excited to contribute to research in this area.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) at stage IIb due to Fontaine for the past 6 months. He has a history of smoking for 40 years and quit smoking 3 months ago. He takes medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His ABI is less than 0.9, and he has radiologic occlusion in the arteria femoralis superficialis and arteria poplitea. He is expected to be available during the study participation for over 12 weeks through his healthcare center. He has no history of malignant tumors, hemophilia, psoriasis vulgaris, recent stroke, or infections of the auricle and external auditory canal. He has not had a pacemaker or defibrillator implanted, and his transcutaneous partial pressure of oxygen (tcpO2) is less than or equal to 50 mmHg. He has no concomitant disease that could limit the significance of the investigation of the walk distance or improve/worsen the walking or perfusion of the extremities in a relevant way. He has not been on a structured walking training program or had any changes in PAVK-relevant medication or concomitant medication with the potential to improve or worsen the walking or perfusion of the extremities in the last 3 months. He has not participated in any other clinical trial with insurance-protection and has not used a therapy with stimulation of the afferent parts of vagus on the ear in the past.

The patient is a healthy adult between 18 to 65 years of age with no history of lung disease or smoking. They have a forced vital capacity (FVC) or forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1) greater or equal to 80% of predicted values (Pereira et al., 1992). The patient is able to follow and retain verbal commands and is willing to provide signed consent to participate in the study. They have no history of pregnancy or intolerance to nebulization. The patient will be randomized to receive either a mesh nebulizer or jet nebulizer to inhale 99mTc-DTPA with an activity of 1 mCi with the normal saline to a total dose of 4 mL with JN (Misty Max, Air Life, Yorba Linda, USA) oxygen flow of 8 L / min and 1.5 mL with MN (Aeroneb Solo with Ultra adapter; Aerogen Galway, Ireland). Scintigraphy will be used to determine distribution of deposition and mass balance between compartments.

The patient is a 42-year-old African American male with no history of hypertension, diabetes, or any other cardiovascular disease. He has a BMI of 25 and does not exercise regularly. He has not taken antibiotics or medications that impact intestinal function in the past 3 months and has no plans of travel out of town during the study periods. He does not smoke or use tobacco products. He will be participating as a normotensive control subject in a proof of concept pilot study to investigate the relationship between gut microbial dysbiosis and hypertension in African Americans. As part of the study, he will provide stool and blood samples and complete a 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to compare the abundance of fecal butyrate-producing microbes, circulating butyrate concentrations, and average blood pressure responses during the day and overnight. He will not be taking any anti-hypertension medication during the study.

Sophie is a 9-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with visual impairment since birth. She wears glasses and her visual acuity after correction is 6/24. She attends a school for visually impaired children and has been experiencing forward head posture, which is characterized by hyperextension of upper cervical and flexion of lower cervical spine. Her craniovertebral angle is less than 50°, indicating the presence of the postural deviation. She has no history of injury or deformities in the cervical region and is free from any rheumatic or congenital heart disease. She is not currently participating in any sports activities and does not have any intellectual or mental disabilities. Sophie has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of muscle energy technique on forward head posture and cervical mobility in visually impaired children.

A 60-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, dry cough, and fatigue for the past 3 weeks. She has a history of polymyositis and dermatomyositis diagnosed 5 years ago. She has been on oral prednisone at 20 mg/day, and methotrexate at 10 mg/week, which has been controlling her symptoms. However, she stopped taking her medications a month ago due to financial constraints. The patient has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is married and has two adult children. On examination, her oxygen saturation is 92% on room air, and her lung auscultation reveals bibasilar crackles. Laboratory tests show an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). A chest x-ray shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates. She was diagnosed with interstitial pneumonia associated with polymyositis/dermatomyositis and started on intravenous methylprednisolone at 500 mg/day. After 3 days, her symptoms improved, and she was started on oral prednisone and methotrexate again. The patient was then approached to participate in a survey for long-term use of Prograf capsules to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the medication in patients with interstitial pneumonia associated with polymyositis/dermatomyositis in acute clinical settings.

The patient is a 54 year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery and received carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy as first-line treatment. Unfortunately, her cancer recurred within 3 months of completing chemotherapy. She then received topotecan as second-line treatment but her cancer continued to progress. She is currently experiencing abdominal pain and bloating, as well as fatigue and loss of appetite. Her CA-125 level has risen to 300 U/mL, indicating disease progression. She has

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum located 7 cm from the anal margin. He has no history of pelvic radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The tumor was staged as T3 and a multidisciplinary consultation meeting has recommended chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy prior to total mesorectal surgery. He is operable and likely to receive radiation therapy and chemotherapy. He has no history of other cancers, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is willing to use two medically validated methods of contraception during treatment and up to 6 months after the last treatment as he has a partner. He is affiliated with a social security scheme of a member country of the European Community and is able to submit to the medical follow-up of the test. He has been informed of the study and has given his informed and written consent.

A 19-year-old female student visited the dermatology clinic with a history of moderate to severe acne vulgaris. She has tried multiple over-the-counter topical products and oral antibiotics with limited success. She has not used any acne treatment products for the last two weeks. She has no other significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is willing to stop her current acne treatment to participate in the study. She has no facial hair.

62-year-old male with a history of elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels and a biopsy-proven diagnosis of locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The patient has not received any prior treatment for prostate cancer. He has good performance status and a life expectancy of at least 3 years. The patient has no history of ventricular arrhythmia or dysfunction, no congestive heart failure, no symptomatic coronary artery disease, no prior myocardial infarction, and no history of thromboembolic disease within the past 12 months. He has no other significant cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. His hematology and liver function tests are within normal limits. The patient is willing to use effective barrier method contraception as he is fertile. He has not participated in another investigational study within the past 3 months and is not currently on any over-the-counter or herbal drugs that have estrogenic activity.

A 12-year-old female patient who received one or two doses of MenACWY conjugate vaccine at 2 to 10 years of age is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She must be in good health as determined by the outcome of medical history, physical examination, and clinical judgment of the investigator. A negative urine pregnancy test is required before enrollment. The patient must not have any history of documented or suspected invasive meningococcal disease, and should not have received any other meningococcal vaccine since participation in the previous study. She should not have any serious, chronic, or acute illnesses or diseases, or any confirmed or suspected condition with impaired/altered function of the immune system. The patient should not have received any vaccine within 28 days prior to the study enrollment or planned administration during the study period. She must not have participated in any clinical trial with another investigational product 28 days prior to the first study visit or intent to participate in another clinical study at any time during the study period.

A 56-year-old man was diagnosed with choroidal melanoma in his left eye during a routine eye exam. He underwent I-125 plaque brachytherapy as a local treatment plan for his ocular melanoma. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication. He is a retired engineer and enjoys hiking and gardening. He has never smoked and only drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known family history of ocular or skin cancer. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of choroidal melanoma.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 7 years ago. She has been on medication for the last 5 years and has experienced a mild improvement in her symptoms. However, she still experiences significant fatigue, which affects her daily activities. She has difficulty walking long distances due to fatigue and leg weakness. She is a stay-at-home mom with two children and spends most of her time taking care of them. She enjoys watching TV and reading books. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her resting systolic blood pressure is around 120 mmHg. She can walk for 6 minutes without rest, but feels significant fatigue afterwards. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in research studies. She has not participated in any clinical trials related to MS or exercise before.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of periodontitis. He has been experiencing bleeding gums, bad breath, and loose teeth for the past few months. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and takes no medications. Upon examination, it is found that he has localized chronic periodontitis with probing depths of at least 4 mm in all quadrants. He consents to non-surgical periodontal treatment with scaling and root planing and photodynamic therapy (PDT) for approximately 6 months. The patient has no allergies to photosensitizers or dyes and is not pregnant or nursing. He is willing to follow the treatment plan and attend all follow-up appointments. His diabetes is well-controlled with an HbA1c level of 6.5 mmol/L. The patient has not taken antibiotics or steroids for the past three months.

A 58-year-old man was referred to the clinic after attending a UK national AAA screening programme. A routine ultrasound test revealed an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) of 4.8 cm. He was subsequently enrolled in the AAA surveillance programme and his aorta has been monitored every year. His latest ultrasound scan, performed 3 months ago, showed an increase in the diameter of his aorta to 5.1 cm. As part of the standard clinical practice in Torbay and South Devon, he underwent a cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) in the Pre-assessment Clinic in Torbay Hospital, where he was identified as a potential participant for the clinical trial. He is a non-smoker, has no significant past medical history, and is currently taking medication for mild hypertension. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He is able to safely perform a cardiopulmonary exercise test and understands verbal and written instructions in English. He has no contra-indications to exercise or cardiovascular problems. He has not participated in any other treatment trials.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He has a BMI of 26 and is currently using condoms as his preferred method of contraception with his partner. He lives within a reasonable distance from the clinic and is willing to comply with the protocol of the trial. He has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational drugs in the last 30 days. His physical exam and laboratory tests were unremarkable at the time of screening. His PSA level is within normal limits according to local laboratory values. He has no history of hypertension or primary testicular disease, and his EKG is normal. He has no known hypersensitivity to progestins or androgens and has no family or personal history of venous thromboembolism. He has no known history of reproductive dysfunction, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, or prostatic disease. He has no known dermatitis or severe skin disorder, and his PHQ-9 score is less than 15. He is not allergic to any ingredient in testosterone/nestorone gel, including alcohol, and has no known history of untreated sleep apnea. His IPSS score is less than 15. His sperm concentration is ≥ 15 million sperm per milliliter ejaculate.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of recurrent HER2-negative gastric cancer. He has a performance score of 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology and is able to swallow and retain orally administered treatment. He has no history of another malignancy, brain metastases, or spinal cord compression. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has a history of first-line platinum/fluoropyrimidine doublet regimen for advanced gastric cancer and is showing progressive disease. He is refractory or disease progression within 6 months of adjuvant treatment. He has recovered from any treatment-related toxicity. He has a history of gastrectomy. He has at least one measurable disease by RECIST version1.1. His organ system functions are adequate, and he has no serious and/or unstable pre-existing medical, psychiatric disorder or other conditions that could interfere with subject's safety, obtaining informed consent or compliance to the study procedures. He does not have any known immediate or delayed hypersensitivity reaction or idiosyncratic reaction to drugs similar or related to afuresertib and taxanes. He is not currently using warfarin for therapeutic anticoagulation but is using low molecular weight heparin. He has no contraindications to the doses of paclitaxel defined in the protocol. He does not have a history of reduction in standard of care paclitaxel dose for peripheral neuropathy. His QTcF interval is less than 470 milliseconds. He is not known to have HIV infection or active hepatitis B or C.

72-year-old female with a history of memory impairment for the past 2 years, difficulty with daily activities and mild cognitive impairment, diagnosed by previous neuropsychological assessment. She is currently taking donepezil 10 mg daily for the past year with mild improvement in cognitive function, but continued difficulty with daily activities. Her Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE) score is 27 and her Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) score is 0.5. She has a stable caregiver to attend the patient study visits. Her MRI brain scan is concordant with the diagnosis of clinical a-MCI. She has no known allergy to components of the vaccine or history of anaphylaxis or severe allergic reaction. She does not have an active infectious disease or history of autoimmune disease. She has normal kidney and liver function, and no history of asthma or reactive airway disease. She does not have any major uncontrolled systemic conditions or history of cancer. Her hematological, biochemical, and urine analytical parameters are within normal limits. She does not have any history of central nervous system disorder or psychiatric condition that could interfere with cognitive function. She has a Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) score of 3 and does not have any history of suicidal behavior. She does not have any history or signs of cerebrovascular disease or diagnosis of probable or clear vascular dementia. She does not have any relevant pattern of microvascular disease or lacunar or territorial infarcts on her MRI. She does not have any bleeding disorder or abnormal coagulation profile. She is not currently being treated with anticoagulants or antiaggregant therapy. Her Modified Hachinski Ischemic Scale score is 2. She has not had surgery with general anesthesia within the past three months and is not scheduled for surgery during the study period. She has not received systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants within 30 days prior to visit 0. She has not received any vaccination within 2 months prior to the first IMP dose. She has not previously been randomized in this trial or participated in another clinical trial within the previous 1 month to screening visit. She does not have alcohol or drug abuse or dependence. She has no absolute or relative contraindications to MRI examination. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol and return for follow-up visits. She is not pregnant or nursing. Her EKG is within normal limits.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. She had a healthy pregnancy and delivery with her first child. She is currently 28 weeks pregnant and has been diagnosed with preeclampsia after experiencing high blood pressure and proteinuria. Her BMI is 24 kg/m2 and she has no major medical history. She has not used any illegal drugs or alcohol during her pregnancy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has not received any prenatal steroid therapy.

A 30-year-old female with no significant medical history presented for a volunteer study. She denied any previous surgeries, hospitalizations or chronic illnesses. She reported taking occasional over-the-counter medications for headaches or menstrual cramps. She had no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and she does not smoke. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. Her vital signs were stable within normal limits. She reported no history of heart disease, stroke, or any heart rhythm abnormalities. She signed the informed consent and agreed to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form. Her weight was 60 kg and her BMI was 22. She had a normal physical exam and normal laboratory tests, including normal liver function tests. She had a normal ECG with a heart rate of 70 bpm and no evidence of conduction abnormalities. She met all eligibility criteria and was enrolled in the study.

A 60-year-old man with a history of COPD presents with worsening shortness of breath, increased cough, and sputum production for the past week. He has been compliant with his medications, which include a long-acting bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid. He has no fever, chest pain, or recent travel history. His oxygen saturation on room air is 88% and improves to 92% with supplemental oxygen. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.29, PaCO2 of 62 mmHg, and PaO2 of 59 mmHg. Chest x-ray shows hyperinflation and patchy infiltrates. The patient is admitted to the ICU for hypercapnic acute respiratory failure and started on non-invasive ventilation (NIV) with a pressure support of 15 cm H2O and a positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 5 cm H2O. Despite improvement in his respiratory distress, the patient exhibits significant discomfort during breaks of NIV when switched to standard oxygen. He complains of dry mouth, nasal congestion, and irritation of the throat. The investigators propose to enroll him in a clinical trial comparing the use of high-flow heated and humidified nasal oxygen therapy (HFHO) to standard oxygen during breaks of NIV. The aim is to determine if the use of HFHO increases the number of ventilator-free days (VFDs) and alive at day 28 in patients with hypercapnic ARF admitted in an ICU, an intermediate care, or a respiratory care unit, and requiring NIV. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is randomized to the HFHO group. He is closely monitored throughout the trial for his tolerance of NIV and HFHO.

32F presents with pain and discharge from the perianal region. She reports having had recurrent abscesses in the past, but this time she noticed a persistent discharge. Examination revealed a high anal fistula with no evidence of fecal incontinence or significant scarring. Endoluminal ultrasound and MRI were performed to confirm the diagnosis and identify the internal opening. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of perianal surgery or irritable bowel disease. She has no history of diabetes and has been managing her health with regular exercise and a healthy diet.

A 32-year-old male presents with concerns regarding fertility. He and his wife have been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. He has a history of working in a factory where he was exposed to chemicals and has been smoking for the past 5 years. Semen analysis reveals a low sperm count of 8 million per milliliter and poor motility of 30%. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effects of an antioxidant dietary supplement on sperm parameters.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia has been receiving treatment for the past 4 years. He lives with his parents and works part-time at a local shop. He experiences negative symptoms such as social withdrawal, lack of motivation, and anhedonia. He also reports difficulties with cognitive functioning, including memory and attention. He is compliant with his medication regimen of risperidone 2mg daily, but he still experiences symptoms. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has no history of seizures, epilepsy, or head trauma. He does not have any metal in his head or implanted devices. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to adhere to the treatment schedule.

A 65-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with worsening heart failure symptoms, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He had an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) device with cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT-D) implanted for the past 2 years. His device has the OptiVol capability and has been monitoring his heart rate variability, daily heart rate, and intrathoracic impedance continuously. His most recent device check showed an increase in heart rate and a decrease in intrathoracic impedance, indicating worsening heart failure status. The patient's hemoglobin level was 11 g/dL and he was not residing in a convalescence center prior to admission. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and may be a good candidate to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate device diagnostic data for hospital discharge readiness in heart failure patients.

A 47 year old woman with a history of breast cancer is referred to the clinical trial. She was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer 2 years ago and has been receiving systemic therapy. Despite treatment, the cancer has progressed and metastasized to her lungs and liver. A recent blood test showed the presence of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) clusters. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is not currently taking digoxin or digitoxin and does not have any history of atrial fibrillation, ventricular fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia, atrioventricular heart block 2nd or 3rd degree, sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, or Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome. Her organ and marrow function are adequate. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the course of the study. She uses safe contraception method. She does not have any known hypersensitivity to Digoxin, other cardiac glycosides or included compounds. She is willing to comply with the procedures and required visits of the study.

A 62-year-old male non-smoker was diagnosed with a myocardial infarction 45 days ago. He lives with his wife in a non-smoking household. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently under control with medication. He works as a salesman and drives to different cities for work. He is concerned about the effects of air pollution on his health and is interested in participating in a study that investigates the use of facemasks to decrease exposure to ambient air pollution. He is not currently pregnant, and does not plan to have children during the study period.

A 60-year-old male presents with a history of stable angina and positive stress test. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and diabetes mellitus, all well controlled with medications. He is currently on aspirin, atorvastatin, metformin, and lisinopril. He has no known allergy to contrast media, heparin, bivalirudin or antiplatelet medications. He has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or peptic ulcer disease. He has normal renal function with a serum creatinine level of 1.0 mg/dL. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. Angiographic evaluation revealed a single vessel disease with a target lesion located in the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) artery with a diameter stenosis of 80% by visual estimation. The reference vessel diameter (RVD) of the target lesion is 3.5 mm by visual estimation. There are no other significant lesions in the coronary arteries. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria of the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease for 3 years. He has been taking a stable dose of a single dopamine agonist for the past 6 months, which has helped in controlling his motor symptoms. His Hoehn and Yahr Stage is II, and he experiences tremors, stiffness, and difficulty in initiating movements. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. He does not have any history of substance abuse, psychosis or depression. He has no cognitive dysfunction, and his Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28. He lives with his wife and has no children. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the requirements.

This is a 52 year old female with a history of primary Sjögren's Syndrome who has been experiencing persistent musculoskeletal pain despite current treatment with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She does not have controlled arterial hypertension and has not received any intraarticular or systemic use of Glucocorticoids in the last 4 weeks. She has been diagnosed with liver values above 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). The patient has not been pre-treated with Cyclosporine A and does not have any active infection or neoplasia. She does not have any relevant cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic or psychiatric disease. The patient has not received any life-vaccination within 4 weeks prior to the start of study medication. Her weight is within the range of 45kg to 110kg.

A 45 year old woman has been diagnosed with a rare, solid tumor that is refractory to standard treatment. She is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has provided written informed consent and her bone marrow function is adequate. Her serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL and her calculated creatinine clearance is 70 ml/min based on Cockcroft and Gault. Her total bilirubin is 1.5 times the upper limit of normal of institutional values and her aspartate and alanine transaminase are less than 3 times the upper limit of institutional values. She has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 50% based on electrocardiogram (ECHO). Her resting oxygen saturations are 97%. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have malabsorption syndrome or a disease affecting gastrointestinal function. She has no evidence of symptomatic or uncontrolled brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease. She is not considered medically unfit for the study by the investigator. She has not had a known immediate or delayed hypersensitivity reaction or idiosyncrasy to drugs chemically related to the investigational product. She is not currently taking anilinoquinazolines, such as gefitinib or erlotinib. She has no history of immediate or delayed hypersensitivity reaction to midazolam or any component of the formulation, including benzyl alcohol (cross-sensitivity with other benzodiazepines may exist). She does not have narrow-angle glaucoma which is a contraindication to midazolam use. She has not received treatment with any investigational drug in the previous 4 weeks and has not received chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic therapy or hormonal therapy within the past 14 days, with the exception of mitomycin C within the past 6 weeks. She is not currently receiving amiodarone or has received amiodarone in the 6 months prior to screening. She is not taking regular doses of opiates that in the opinion of the investigator would put the patient at risk of clinically significant respiratory compromise when midazolam is administered.

35-year-old Caucasian male with a history of recurrent Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is seeking treatment for his condition. He has experienced multiple episodes of depression in the past and is currently experiencing a relapse. He is proficient in Danish and has no history of substance abuse or organic mental disorders. He has not undergone previous Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) or Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) and is not currently receiving psychotherapy or taking anti-psychotic medication or benzodiazepines. He has no contraindications for undergoing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) procedures for research purposes. The patient is interested in participating in the study to investigate mechanisms of MBCT and predictors of treatment outcome.

A 45-year-old Hispanic male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia was referred to the hospital for a pacemaker placement due to symptomatic bradycardia. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. The patient has no history of keloid formation, bleeding disorder, or allergies to non-latex skin adhesives. The patient has been informed about the study and given the option to participate. The patient is willing and able to complete the study protocol and has signed the informed consent. The patient is expected to be available for follow-up visits for a total of 3 months after the procedure. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 1 year.

Patient A is a 35-year-old woman who underwent hysteroscopic sterilization procedure in February 2011. She has continuous medical and pharmacy benefits since August 2010 and has completed 12 months of follow-up period after the procedure. She has no history of postpartum tubal ligation procedure and has not undergone any sterilization procedure during the baseline period. She has not been pregnant or delivered a baby within 6 weeks prior to the index date. The patient has only undergone hysteroscopic sterilization procedure and has not had any concurrent procedures on the same day for any other reasons beyond the purpose of sterilization. She has been experiencing pelvic pain since the procedure and is concerned about the potential risks associated with the procedure.

25-year-old female with no significant medical history, currently studying in college, interested in participating in a clinical trial. No known allergies to medications or any family history of adverse reactions to drugs. BMI within the range of 18.0 to 30.0 kg/m2. No history of fainting, collapse, syncope, orthostatic hypotension, or vasovagal reactions. Not currently pregnant or lactating. No surgical or medical conditions that may interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of the study treatment. Willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the study protocol.

A 45-year-old male patient who is a smoker and has been diagnosed with lung cancer is scheduled for Video-Assisted Thoracotomy (VATS) surgery in two weeks. He is currently taking opioid medications for pain control. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension, for which he takes daily medications. He has no known allergies. The patient speaks and understands English. He has had prior surgeries and has no implanted pacemaker or defibrillator. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 73-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure. She presents with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue, despite optimal medical therapy. Echocardiography revealed severe tricuspid regurgitation with a regurgitant volume of 50 mL and a pulmonary artery pressure of 45 mmHg. The patient has no prior history of tricuspid valve repair or replacement. The local site Heart Team has determined that the patient is appropriate for transcatheter tricuspid valve repair using the Edwards PASCAL Transcatheter Valve Repair System. She is willing and able to provide written, informed consent and is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who presented to the hospital with a history of persistent pain in his right leg. Imaging studies revealed a large osteolytic lesion in the distal femur. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of high-grade osteosarcoma. Further workup showed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has no significant medical history and has never undergone any surgeries or chemotherapy treatments. He is otherwise healthy and has been active in sports. The patient and his family have been informed about the study and have given their consent to participate.

There is no patient description required for this particular clinical trial as the study focuses on the implementation of lung ultrasound by hospitalists in the management of patients hospitalized with COVID-19. The eligibility criteria only applies to physicians and advanced care provider faculty at the University of Colorado Hospital.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing gaz incontinence for the past 6 months. She has been managing her symptoms with over-the-counter medications but has not found any relief. She is affiliated with national health security and has read and signed the information letter and consent form. She is not pregnant, has not used antibiotics, probiotics, or IPP for the past 3 months, and has no history of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. She has no history of ischemic, inflammatory colitis, or colorectal cancer. She does not have diabetes and is not allergic to metronidazole. She has no known psychiatric diseases and is fluent in French.

A 45 year old woman has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has been on insulin therapy for two months. She uses a pen device for self-injection of all diabetes-related medications. Her BMI is 35 kg/m² and her Hemoglobin A1c concentration is 8.5%. She self-monitors her blood glucose at least twice per day with a memory blood glucose meter. She is currently on a stable diabetes treatment regimen and is able to read, write and follow instructions in English. She has no history of intravenous drug abuse and is not pregnant. She has no medical condition that would contraindicate treatment with the study product or have the potential to confound interpretation of the study results. She has not participated in any of the clinical studies mentioned in the exclusion criteria. She is anxious about the needle size and is looking for a shorter, thinner pen needle that is less intimidating and more comfortable.

62-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease (CAD) with previous stent placement was referred for cardiac surgery. He reports occasional chest pain on exertion and shortness of breath. Physical examination revealed no significant abnormalities. Echocardiography showed moderate aortic stenosis and moderate mitral regurgitation. Coronary angiography revealed significant stenosis in the left anterior descending (LAD) artery and right coronary artery (RCA). Elective cardiac surgery was planned for coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). The patient has never used steroids or anti-inflammatory drugs routinely and has no history of asthma, COPD, or autoimmune diseases. He has not participated in any other clinical studies and has no history of decompensated heart failures, liver or kidney disease. The patient has a BMI of 26kg/m2 which falls within eligibility criteria. The patient has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

A 7-year-old boy with ataxic cerebral palsy is being considered for participation in a clinical trial studying the effects of core stability training in ataxic cerebral palsied children. He has level IV according to the gross motor function classification system and his ataxia severity score is less than 25 according to the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA). He has no visual impairment or spasticity, and does not experience uncontrolled convulsions. He has been diagnosed with ataxic cerebral palsy and has not been diagnosed with ataxia-telangiectasia, spinocerebellar ataxia, or Joubert syndrome. He is able to understand and follow directions, and his parents have consented to his participation in the study.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of COPD, diagnosed 2 years ago. He has been prescribed a LABA/ICS inhaler for maintenance therapy, which he has been using for the past 9 months. He reports experiencing exacerbations of his COPD symptoms, including coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, approximately once every 3-4 months. He has a history of smoking, having smoked a pack a day for 20 years before quitting 5 years ago. He reports occasional use of albuterol inhaler for rescue therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and safety of Tiotropium and Olodaterol combined inhaler versus his current maintenance therapy. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.
