The patient is a 35-year-old female who was rescued from a house fire and admitted to the intensive care unit with smoke inhalation injury. She was unconscious upon arrival and had to be intubated. She had been exposed to smoke for an extended period and had inhaled a large amount of carbon monoxide and cyanide. Her oxygen saturation level was 84% on room air. She was immediately placed on mechanical ventilation and received hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Her condition gradually improved, and she was extubated after 5 days. She had a history of asthma and was a smoker. She was discharged after 10 days with instructions to stop smoking and follow up with her primary care physician. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of smoke-inhalation injury and to identify prognostic factors among patients who receive hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with a myocardial infarction and underwent a coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for stable coronary artery disease. He has no history of kidney disease or use of contrast. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is greater than 60ml/min. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He works as a sales representative and is married with two children. His physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any other abnormalities. Blood pressure: 130/85mmHg, Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL, White blood cell count: 8000/mm3, Platelet count: 250,000/mL, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL, Blood urea nitrogen (BUN): 15 mg/dL. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

57-year-old African American male diagnosed with prostate cancer six months ago. The patient had elevated PSA levels (10 ng/mL) and a biopsy showed a Gleason score of 8 (4+4). The patient underwent radical prostatectomy and had an undetectable PSA post-surgery. The patient was previously enrolled in MCC#18523 and had a high-risk Decipher test score (>0.45). The patient is currently in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient completed genomic classifier (GC) testing on biopsy and had a high-risk Decipher score. The patient received radiation therapy with short-term androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and has been followed up for over 2 years. The patient has no history of claustrophobia or pre-existing comorbidities that would prevent them from undergoing a PET imaging test. The patient has not received any radioisotope within 5 physical half-lives, IV X-ray contrast medium within 24 hours, or high-density oral contrast medium within 5 days prior to study drug injection.

A 35-year-old female who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the glycemic index of different varieties of dates. She has no known allergies to dates or any other food items. She is generally healthy, with no history of diabetes, metabolic syndrome, or any other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the course of the trial. She maintains a balanced diet and exercises regularly. She is excited to participate in this trial, as she believes it will help her make informed choices about her food consumption in the future.

A 50-year-old man with a diagnosis of Hodgkin's lymphoma has been scheduled for an autologous stem cell transplant. He has no history of psychiatric illness or any other significant medical condition. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He is currently not taking any medication other than the prescribed ones for his cancer treatment. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is scheduled to have his first autologous stem cell transplant and is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

55-year-old male with a history of chronic ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath with minimal exertion for the past 6 months. He underwent a contrast coronary ventriculography which showed multivessel coronary disease and poor left ventricular function with an ejection fraction of 35%. Further evaluation with cardiac ce-MR and PET imaging verified his eligibility for the study with an end-systolic volume of 150 ml and residual viability of 40% of the left ventricle. The patient has been deemed a poor candidate for surgical revascularization alone due to the severity of left ventricular dilation. Therefore, he has been enrolled in the clinical trial and randomly allocated to undergo surgical revascularization with autologous bone marrow-derived stem cells injection in viable territories. Follow-up evaluation will be performed at 1 year to assess the improvement of left ventricular volumes and contractility through ce-MR and PET imaging, as well as metabolic stress tests and quality of life questionnaires.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who is generally healthy and active. She is 170 cm tall and her weight is 70 kg. She has never been diagnosed with osteoporosis, but she is concerned about her risk due to a family history of the disease. She exercises regularly, but does not engage in vigorous activity more than 2 times a week. She speaks and reads English fluently, and is able to use a cell phone app. Her current diet does not meet the recommended amount of dietary calcium, as she consumes less than 200 mg daily. She is not currently receiving medical care for any chronic condition, and is not taking any medications that would affect bone health. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not had any cancer treatments in the past 5 years. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her improve her bone health and prevent osteoporosis.

The patient is a 16-year-old adolescent presenting with a history of soft tissue sarcoma stage IV. The diagnosis was confirmed through biopsy, and imaging studies show measurable tumor lesions in the lungs and liver. The patient underwent initial treatment with surgery and radiation therapy with limited success. The patient and their family have expressed interest in participating in the clinical trial for the treatment of children and adolescents with soft tissue sarcoma stage 4. The patient has demonstrated cooperation and willingness to participate in follow-up examinations. There is no history of participation in another clinical trial, and the patient has not experienced death due to the sickness within the past four weeks. The patient meets all eligibility criteria and is a suitable candidate for the study.

52 yo F diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the lungs and liver. Patient has recently started chemotherapy and targeted therapy. Patient lives with her husband and two children, and her husband is her primary caregiver. The patient identifies as African-American/Black and speaks English fluently. The patient has experienced fatigue, sleep disturbance, and anxiety since starting treatment, and her husband has noted an increase in his own caregiver burden. The patient and her husband are interested in participating in this study to better understand the impact of the patient's symptoms on the caregiver and to potentially help others in similar situations.

35F with a history of dental calculus formation and regular dental prophylaxis every 6 months. She reports occasional bleeding from her gums while brushing her teeth. She has no known systemic or chronic illnesses and takes no medications. On examination, there is mild gingival inflammation and moderate calculus formation on the lingual surfaces of her mandibular anterior teeth. She has at least 20 sound natural teeth and is compliant with oral hygiene instructions. She has no sensitivity to tartar-control toothpaste and is not currently receiving any dental treatment that would result in the removal of plaque or calculus. She is willing to adhere to the study protocol and attend study recalls.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of ulcerative colitis for 10 years was referred for colonoscopy for surveillance purposes. She had a colonoscopy 3 years ago, which showed active disease in the left colon. Her symptoms have been well controlled with mesalamine and azathioprine. She denies any recent changes in bowel habits, abdominal pain, or rectal bleeding. She has no significant past medical history and takes no other medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is significant for her mother having colon cancer at age 60. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo additional biopsies during her colonoscopy for research purposes.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of hereditary angioedema (HAE). She experiences an average of one HAE attack per month and has been treated with C1INH therapy in the past. She has not received any C1INH therapy or any blood products for treatment or prevention of an HAE attack within 14 days prior to the first dose. She has not received any ecallantide (Kalbitor), icatibant (Firazyr), or antifibrinolytics (e.g., tranexamic acid) within 14 days prior to the first dose. She has not made any changes to her androgen therapy (e.g., danazol, oxandrolone, stanozolol, testosterone) within 14 days prior to the first dose. If she is a female, she has not started taking or changed the dose of any hormonal contraceptive regimen or hormone replacement therapy (i.e., estrogen/progestin containing products) within 3 months prior to the first dose. She has no history of abnormal blood clotting or other coagulopathy and has not had an allergic reaction to CINRYZE or other blood products in the past. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not received an immunization within 30 days prior to the first dose. She is willing to strictly adhere to the protocol-defined schedule of assessments and procedures.

A 10-year-old boy has been diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder and has an IQ score between 55 and 85. His parents report that he frequently displays disruptive behavior, including outbursts of anger and irritability. He is currently not on any medication to manage these behaviors. He is able to communicate verbally, but struggles with social interactions and has difficulty understanding sarcasm and non-literal language. He is in a mainstream school setting and receives accommodations for his ASD diagnosis. He has no known medical or psychiatric conditions that would require alternative treatment. His parents are interested in exploring cognitive-behavioral therapy as a potential treatment option for their son's irritability and disruptive behaviors.

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic with abdominal pain that was diagnosed as a gallbladder stone by her gastroenterologist. She was scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy surgery. She has a past history of hypertension and is currently under medication for the same. She has no history of any other major illnesses or surgeries. The patient is not a smoker and consumes alcohol socially. She is physically active and follows a balanced diet. She has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 11-year-old girl in the 6th grade, who is currently enrolled in a school in central Texas. She is physically active and enjoys participating in sports, but does not consume a calcium-rich diet. She has not had any fractures or bone-related injuries in the past. The patient's parents have provided their consent for her to participate in the study. The patient is also enrolled in at least 2 semesters of physical education at school.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis and alcohol abuse. He presents with abdominal pain and weight loss over the past 6 months. Imaging studies reveal a 2.5 cm solid pancreatic mass in the head of the pancreas. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications regularly. His family history is negative for pancreatic cancer. He has no known allergies and has not had any surgeries in the past. His lab results show elevated levels of pancreatic enzymes including amylase and lipase. He is a heavy smoker with a 30-pack year history. He is otherwise healthy and active with no major comorbidities. He has been referred for EUS-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic mass for further evaluation and diagnosis.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who sustained a spinal cord injury at the thoracic level 2 years ago in a motorcycle accident. He is paraplegic and uses a wheelchair for mobility. He reports chronic neuropathic pain in both legs with a pain intensity of 6 out of 10 on the numerical pain rating scale (NPRS) test. He has been taking gabapentin and amitriptyline for his pain for the last 6 months. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, or head injuries. He does not have any visual or cognitive impairments. He is interested in participating in the study as he wants to find an alternative treatment for his chronic neuropathic pain that can help him improve his quality of life. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and is able to take time off from work for the study.

50 year old male with a newly diagnosed retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma (RPS). The patient has no prior history of cancer or systemic therapy. The RPS is unifocal and has not spread to other parts of the body. The tumor is considered operable and suitable for radiotherapy based on imaging studies and multidisciplinary consultation with a surgeon, radiation oncologist, and radiologist. The patient has a WHO performance status of 1 and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. The patient is willing to undergo either surgery alone or radiation therapy followed by surgery and is prepared to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule. The patient has no significant comorbidities and has normal laboratory values for WBC, platelet count, total bilirubin, and creatinine clearance. The patient has no history of bowel obstruction, mesenteric ischemia, or severe chronic inflammatory bowel disease. The patient is not currently pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception during the study treatment period and for at least 1 month after surgery.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of lower respiratory tract infection including cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past 3 days. She visited the hospital and was diagnosed with influenza A by virologic tests. Her symptoms are severe enough to require hospital care and antiviral (oseltamivir) treatment. The patient has no known history of hepatic failure, end-stage renal failure, or cardiac arrhythmia, and does not take any immunosuppressants. She is not pregnant or lactating, and does not have any known contraindications to azithromycin. The patient is able to provide written, informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 19-year-old female university student who was diagnosed with HIV six months ago presents to the clinic for follow-up. She is currently on antiretroviral therapy and has been adherent to her medication regimen. She reports no significant side effects. Her CD4 count is 420 cells/mm3, and her viral load is undetectable. She is sexually active and has had two sexual partners in the past year. She has no history of abnormal cervical cytology or cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. She has never received the HPV vaccine before. A pelvic exam reveals no abnormalities, and her Pap smear is negative. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the HPV vaccine in HIV-positive females. She agrees to undergo HIV voluntary counseling and testing and use adequate contraception during the study period.

A 25-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician due to excessive urination and thirst. She has a family history of diabetes insipidus (DI). She reports drinking up to 5 liters of water per day and urinating frequently, up to 20 times per day, and wakes up several times at night to urinate. She denies any recent changes in her diet or exercise routine. She has not experienced any recent weight loss or gain. On physical examination, she is afebrile with normal vital signs. Her skin is dry, and her mucous membranes are moist. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender. Neurological examination is normal. Laboratory tests show low urine osmolality and high serum osmolality, consistent with DI. She is referred to the clinical trial for further evaluation of her condition.

A 42-year-old male diagnosed with Schizophrenia 8 years ago is experiencing moderate to severe Tardive Dyskinesia symptoms, including involuntary facial and limb movements, which have been present for the last 6 months. Despite being on a stable dose of antipsychotic medication, the patient has not experienced any relief from TD symptoms. The patient has a history of alcohol and substance abuse but has been sober for the last year. He is currently unemployed and living with his parents. He has no history of cardiac or respiratory problems. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is seeking treatment for his TD symptoms and is interested in participating in the clinical trial for MT-5199.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing anterior knee pain for several months. The pain has failed to respond to conservative treatment, which included lifestyle changes and over-the-counter NSAIDs. She was diagnosed with lateral patellar compression syndrome and underwent arthroscopic lateral patellar release. MRI before the operation showed early stages of patellofemoral degenerative changes with no loss of articular surface. She has never had knee surgery before and does not have a history of patellar instability, smoking, or diabetes mellitus. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves the use of Hyaluronic acid injection to potentially alleviate knee pain and improve recovery time.

A 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes for over a year, with a HbA1c level between 7.0% and 10.0%. He has no known complications of diabetes and is taking medication regularly. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the SmartCare-diabetes management system and has agreed to participate voluntarily. He has no severe chronic diseases, renal disease, or liver disease. He is not an insulin pump user and is not currently registered for any other clinical research. He is literate and has been assessed as relevant by the investigator.

25 yo F, G1P0, at 20 weeks gestation, presents to an ANC clinic in Honiara for the first time in this pregnancy. She reports occasional headaches and fatigue but denies any fever, chills, or body aches. She reports no previous use of chloroquine prophylaxis in this pregnancy. She is willing to adhere to all requirements of the study and provides informed written consent. She plans to stay in Honiara for antenatal care and delivery. Her haemoglobin level is 10 g/dL, and she is not using folic acid in a dose of 5 mg daily. She has never had an allergic reaction to sulfa drugs. She is excited to participate in the trial to help improve malaria prevention for pregnant women in the Solomon Islands.

This is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for stage IIIc ovarian cancer diagnosed 18 months ago. She has received two platinum-based regimens plus paclitaxel and has documented progressive disease on treatment, making her a refractory patient. Her ECOG performance status is 1 and her life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 12 weeks. She has normal cardiac function and blood pressure, and adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. She has not received any investigational agents while on study and has not had more than two previous chemotherapy lines or previous treatment with anthracycline. She has not had a myocardial infarction within the last six months, unstable angina, congestive heart failure, or serious cardiac arrhythmia requiring medication. She has no history or evidence of CNS disease and is not experiencing any active or uncontrolled systemic disease/infections or serious illness or medical conditions. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 47-year-old female with a diagnosis of advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck has failed previous standard therapy and is no longer likely to respond to such therapy. The patient has measurable disease per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST). She has not received prior systemic therapy with pazopanib or ixabepilone alone or in combination. However, she has received prior systemic chemotherapy, immunotherapy or biological therapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her organ function is adequate with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 11 g/dL, platelets of 150 x 10^9/L, prothrombin time and international normalized ratio and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) < 1.2 x upper limit of normal (ULN), total bilirubin < ULN, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) < 2.5 x ULN, serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, urine protein to creatinine ratio < 1, and total serum calcium of 10.0 mg/dL. The patient has no history of pregnancy or nursing. She has not had prior radiation to > =or = 30% of major bone marrow containing areas. She has no history or clinical evidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastases or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. The patient does not have clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may increase the risk of GI bleeding or may affect absorption of investigational product. She has no history of another malignancy and must be at least 3 years disease-free. The patient has no presence of uncontrolled infection, prolongation of corrected QT interval (QTc) > 480 msecs, history of any one or more of the following cardiovascular conditions within the past 6 months: cardiac angioplasty or stenting, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, coronary artery bypass graft surgery, symptomatic peripheral vascular disease, Class III or IV congestive heart failure, as defined by the New York Heart Association (NYHA), or poorly controlled hypertension. There is no history of cerebrovascular accident, pulmonary embolism or untreated deep venous thrombosis (DVT) within the past 6 months. The patient has not had prior major surgery or trauma within 28 days prior to the 1st dose of study drug. She has no evidence of active bleeding or bleeding diathesis. The patient does not have known endobronchial lesions or involvement of large pulmonary vessels by tumor or hemoptysis within 6 weeks of the 1st dose of study drug. The patient does not have neuropathy Grade 1.

A 54-year-old male Caucasian patient was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after experiencing severe headaches and vision changes for several weeks. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor, and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. He has no history of prior cancer or chemotherapy. His Karnofsky performance status is 70%, and he is in good general health, with no significant medical or psychiatric illnesses. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy or heart disease. His laboratory tests indicate a WBC count of 4,000/mm3, ANC of 2,000/mm3, platelet count of 120,000/mm3, hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, bilirubin of 1.5 times ULN, SGOT of 2 times ULN, creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, and serum sodium of 135 mmol/L. He has negative pregnancy test results, and he is willing to use effective contraception during the study. He is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study, and he has not undergone radiotherapy to the brain. He is eligible for the study and willing to participate.

A 60-year-old Chinese woman was diagnosed with endometrial cancer and recommended for surgical treatment. She has a history of hypertension and controlled with medication. She denies any other significant medical history or family history of thrombosis. Her preoperative laboratory tests reveal WBC 5.2×10(9)/L, NEU 3.0×10(9)/L, PLT 170×10(9)/L, serum bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, transaminase 18 U/L, BUN 16 mg/dL, and Cr 0.7 mg/dL. She is not taking any medications that can affect blood clotting. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She is scheduled to undergo surgical treatment for her cancer and is approached for participation in a clinical trial investigating thromboprophylaxis after surgery for gynecologic malignancy in China.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who lost her upper left central incisor due to trauma. She had a dental implant placed in the esthetic zone and has been wearing a temporary crown for the past 3 months. She is a non-smoker and has no history of periodontitis or any systematic diseases. Her dental implant has a conical connection and she is willing to have an all-ceramic permanent restoration. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance the field of implant dentistry and improve the long-term success of dental implants.

This clinical trial does not involve direct patient recruitment or intervention as it is an observational study involving the general adult Norwegian population during the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old female diagnosed with inoperable advanced ovarian cancer with metastasis to the liver and lungs. The patient is currently receiving standard palliative care at a hospice setting and has no further curative options available. The patient has been experiencing significant fatigue with a BFI score of 7. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 4 months as determined by the investigator. The patient is willing and able to complete quality of life questionnaires. The patient has not taken any central nervous system stimulators within 30 days before screening and has not enrolled in or completed any other investigational drug trials within 30 days before screening. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Score is 60%. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any uncontrolled systemic disease. The patient is interested in participating in the PG2 treatment trial to improve her fatigue.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of ALS diagnosed 3 years ago. He has gradually lost the ability to speak and move his limbs, and now requires assistance with all activities of daily living. He communicates mainly through eye movements and gestures. He has no cognitive impairments and is able to understand and follow instructions. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and lives in the Philadelphia region.

A 42-year-old man who works as a carpenter suffered a fresh peripheral nerve injury in his right arm while operating heavy machinery at work. He has no history of cardiovascular disease and has not had a heart attack in the past 6 months. His injury is not due to any pre-existing pathological conditions. He has no current infections or any chronic health conditions that might affect his ability to receive surgery. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study's requirements and has provided written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma. He has a history of working in construction for over 30 years and was exposed to asbestos during his job. He presented with shortness of breath, chest pain, and cough for a few months. Imaging studies revealed pleural effusion and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of mesothelioma. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to perform most activities of daily living but experiences some restriction in physical activity. He has no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, primary immunodeficiency, or allogeneic organ transplant. His laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1800/mm³, hemoglobin of 11.0 g/dL, platelets of 120,000/mm³, serum creatinine clearance (CL) of 70 mL/min, albumin of 3.2 g/dL, total bilirubin of 1.0x upper limit of normal (ULN), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST)/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) of 2.0x ULN. He is willing to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study and agrees to undergo treatment and scheduled visits and examinations including follow-up. He is also willing to provide archived tumor tissue and blood samples for research. He has no current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication and no active infections, including tuberculosis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He has no history of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and has not received live attenuated vaccination within 30 days prior to study entry or within 30 days of receiving durvalumab.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian female with a history of atopic dermatitis (AD) since childhood. She has moderate to severe disease with a SCORAD-index of 45. She frequently experiences pruritic inflammatory skin lesions on her arms, legs, and neck. The patient has tried multiple topical steroids, topical/systemic antibiotics, and antihistamines in the past, but none of them have provided long-lasting relief. She has not received phototherapy within the last 12 weeks before inclusion. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of skin cancer, dysplastic naevi, photosensitive skin diseases, autoimmune diseases, or relevant cardiovascular diseases. She has skin type III according to Fitzpatrick. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) three years ago. She has been experiencing fatigue for the past six months, with a global score on the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS) of 60. Her neurologist has recommended treatment for her fatigue. She has not started any new disease-modifying therapy or antidepressant therapy in the past three months. Her Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) is 4.0. She is not currently using energy drinks or any other substances that may interfere with the study. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She is affiliated with health insurance coverage.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing upper abdominal pain and jaundice for the past few weeks. He has been diagnosed with a gallstone in the common bile duct and requires an elective ERCP procedure. He has no known allergies to propofol or opioids and is able to cooperate during the procedure. He has an ASA class of 2 and has no significant medical history, including no history of drug addiction or mental retardation. He has normal liver and kidney function and no significant heart or lung disease. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and will be randomized to either patient-controlled sedation or target-controlled infusion of propofol during the procedure. He will be closely monitored by the anaesthesiologist and anaesthesia nurse throughout the procedure to ensure his safety and comfort.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of smoking for the last 20 years. He smokes at least a pack of cigarettes per day and has a history of 15 pack-years. He has no significant past medical history, is not currently taking any medications, and has no known allergies. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate whether daily aspirin use can reduce the risk of developing lung cancer. He has not taken aspirin or other NSAIDs in the past 14 days and has not used any inhaled or systemic glucocorticoids in the past 7 days. He has no history of peptic ulcer disease, clinically significant bleeding, or thrombocytopenia. His INR is normal, and he has no current diagnosis of malignancy or COPD. He is not taking any systemic anticoagulants and does not take more than 250 mg of fish oil supplementation daily. He is willing to comply with the study design and freeze urine samples at his residence if needed.

A 28-year old female software engineer has a BMI of 22. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. She is physically active and maintains a healthy lifestyle. She is not currently using any medications or supplements. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or blood disorders. She has never donated blood and is not planning on doing so during the study. She has no known allergies or sensitivities. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the course of the study. She agrees to use a medically approved method of birth control during the study. She is willing to wear sunblock and avoid excessive sun exposure. She is interested in participating in the study to help evaluate the bioequivalence between a single oral dose of vitamin D3 gummy vitamin versus vitamin D3 tablet in healthy adults.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on histologic diagnosis and alpha fetoprotein (AFP) levels. He has previously received first-line treatment with sorafenib but experienced treatment failure. His current Child-Pugh score is 6, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance score (ECOG PS) is 1. He has adequate organ function with hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, neutrophil count of 2,200/mm3, and platelet count of 80,000/ul. His total bilirubin level is 1.5 mg/dL, and his alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels are within normal limits. His serum creatinine level is 0.9×ULN. He has no history of HIV infection or allogeneic organ transplantation. He has not experienced any gastrointestinal bleeding within the past 30 days and has no history of esophagus varicosity burst hemorrhage. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study and will take reliable contraceptive measures during and two weeks after the trial.

A 50-year-old woman was diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and received radiation therapy 2 years ago. She has no history of bleeding related to tumor or radiotherapy during or after radiation. She is a non-smoker, non-alcoholic, and has no significant medical history. She is not currently taking any medication for lipid-lowering or other medical conditions. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. She has no history of stroke, myocardial infarction, liver diseases, thyroid dysfunction, inadequately controlled hypertension, or epilepsy. Her family history is negative for hypercholesterolemia. Her LDL-C level is between 100mg/dL（2.5mmol/L）and 190mg/dL（4.9mmol/L）. A recent ultrasound showed that her carotid stenosis is less than 50%. She is willing to take contraception during the trial if necessary. She has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document. The patient meets the eligibility criteria and is a good candidate for the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who works a sedentary job and reports low levels of physical activity. He has no known history of cardiovascular disease or heart disease. He is interested in improving his physical activity habits and is willing to participate in a two-year follow-up study. He is married and has two children. He has a high school education and works full-time as a sales representative. He currently does not engage in any regular exercise activities but is interested in starting a walking routine. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He reports no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. He is willing to participate in follow-up surveys and provide information about his physical activity habits.

The patient is a 17-year-old male who has been diagnosed with relapsed Ewing's sarcoma. He has previously received chemotherapy and radiation therapy for his initial diagnosis, but the disease has returned. He has measurable disease and is experiencing symptoms such as pain and limited mobility due to the tumor. His Lansky score is greater than 30, indicating that he is able to carry out his activities of daily living with some assistance. His blood counts and kidney function are satisfactory, and he has no evidence of liver dysfunction. He has not experienced hematuric cystitis in the past. The patient and his parents have provided written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who underwent heart transplant surgery six months ago. He has a history of coronary artery disease and had a heart attack two years ago. Since the surgery, he has been doing well and has no symptoms of heart disease. His medications include immunosuppressants to prevent rejection of the transplanted heart. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the impact of early microvascular disease on future occurrence of cardiac allograft vasculopathy in heart transplant recipients. He meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

Patient Description:  Group 1 and 2: The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of serious acute or chronic illness, including gastrointestinal issues, and is a non-smoker. The patient is not on any regular medication that interferes with gastrointestinal function and has not taken part in any other clinical study in the last 3 months. He is willing to adhere to the study procedures and understand the requirements of the study.  Group 3: The patient is a 32-year-old female with a BMI of 27 kg/m2. She has been diagnosed with constipation predominant irritable bowel syndrome and has failed to respond to at least one laxative treatment. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of serious acute or chronic illness, including gastrointestinal issues, or substance abuse. The patient is not on any regular medication that interferes with gastrointestinal function and has not taken part in any other clinical study in the last 3 months. She is willing to adhere to the study procedures and understand the requirements of the study.

53-year-old male with a history of bronchiectasis confirmed by HRCT. He presents with a persistent cough and sputum production, despite previous treatment with inhaled and systemic antibiotics. He is a non-smoker with no significant history of lung disease, and no evidence of emphysema, COPD or asthma. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient will undergo a bronchoscopy under sedation to allow for a sample of bronchial epithelial cells to be taken. The main objective of the study is to gain a deeper understanding of the underlying disease mechanisms of bronchiectasis, which will help in the development of future drug discovery. This study will help to identify novel targets for future treatments and ultimately, find a cure for bronchiectasis.

A 48-year-old female patient, who was previously diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, had relapsed after two lines of therapy. She had undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but showed no significant improvement. The physical exam revealed palpable lymph nodes in the neck and axilla. Her laboratory studies were significant for low hemoglobin (7.8 g/dL) and platelet count (65 x 10^9/L). She had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2. She had no history of chronic systemic immunosuppressive therapy or corticosteroids. She had no symptoms of CNS involvement or cardiac disease. She expressed willingness to follow the CC-99282 Pregnancy Prevention Plan (PPP).

This study is looking for participants who are interested in attending a massive musical show and are willing to undergo a COVID-19 screening test prior to entering the event. The aim of the study is to detect asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infected people and carry out the event in a safe environment. The study will randomly select participants with a negative antigen test to attend the event and a control group who will not enter the event. Both groups will undergo a new PCR test 8 days after the event and a questionnaire 10 days after the event to control for symptoms. The inclusion criteria will allow only adults aged 18-59 years without comorbidities and who do not live with old adults in their homes to further reduce the risk of potential complications and transmission to at-risk individuals. The indoor activity will include an array of measures designed to reduce the risk of transmission, including mandatory wearing a mask, restricted outdoor areas of bar and smoking, enhanced ventilation, and avoiding queues. All participants will have downloaded an app in their smartphones for contact tracing during the event. If you are interested in participating in this study, you must have a negative antigen test performed up to 24 hours before the event and not have any of the exclusion criteria listed, such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, chronic lung diseases, a positive test for detection of SARS-CoV-2, or recent contact with someone with a confirmed diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with confirmed cystic fibrosis diagnosed at the age of 6. The patient has a history of frequent hospitalizations and has been on multiple treatments including inhaled antibiotics, hypertonic saline, and azithromycin. Despite these treatments, the patient still experiences frequent pulmonary exacerbations and has declined in lung function over the years. The patient's current FEV1 is 29% predicted. The patient's BMI is 18.5, and she has experienced recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating, diarrhea, and constipation. The patient's physician has recommended triple combination therapy through the EAP program, and the patient has agreed to participate in this observational study to track her pulmonary health, intestinal health, and overall health over the next year. The patient is able to perform spirometry according to ATS criteria and understands and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who enjoys moderate alcohol consumption on weekends with friends. He is generally healthy, does not smoke, and exercises regularly. He works as a graphic designer and has a BMI of 24. He has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He has not taken any prescription medications in the past 14 days or over-the-counter medications in the past 7 days. He has no significant medical history, including cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, or psychiatric disease. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant. He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow the study diet. He weighs at least 65 kg and has a BMI between 19 and 35 kg/m2. He is excited to participate in the study to learn more about the potential effects of alcohol on HC-ER.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman who is physically active and exercises regularly. She follows a balanced diet and is interested in exploring plant-based protein sources to complement her nutrition. She has no history of chronic diseases, recent weight changes or use of medications that might interfere with the study. She has not been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal or infectious disease. She is not a vegetarian or vegan. She is willing to commit to a 2-week unilateral resistance exercise program and follow the supplementation protocol as directed. She is interested in contributing to research that might benefit women's health and overall well-being.

A 42-year-old male with a 5-year history of Crohn's disease was referred to a gastroenterologist due to persistent abdominal pain, diarrhea and rectal bleeding despite treatment with adalimumab for 16 weeks. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. The patient is married with two children and works as a software developer. He reports a stressful work environment but is otherwise physically active and has no known allergies. His current medication regimen includes adalimumab, mesalamine, and a proton pump inhibitor. His BMI is 27. Laboratory studies show a CRP level of 25 mg/L and fecal calprotectin level of 400 µg/g. Physical examination reveals mild abdominal tenderness but no palpable masses or organomegaly. No perianal or abdominal abscesses are observed. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of drug concentration to predict the recapture of response in Crohn's disease patients with loss of response.

The patient is a 14-year-old African American female who is overweight with a BMI greater than or equal to the 95th percentile for her age and sex. She is currently in Tanner stage 3 of puberty. Her vitamin D levels are less than 20 ng/mL, which makes her eligible for the treatment phase of the study. She has no chronic medical conditions, takes no medications that can affect growth, nutrition, bone health, vitamin D metabolism, glucose, or insulin sensitivity. She is committed to adhering to the supplementation and study completion. She is fluent in English and has no known history of hypercalcemia or hypercalciuria.

The patient is a 65-year-old Chinese woman who has been diagnosed with advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. She has already received two lines of chemotherapy but her cancer has progressed. She has no history of smoking and her EGFR status is wild-type. She complains of shortness of breath, fatigue, and weight loss. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work such as office work or light housework. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other malignancies. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

Patient is a 58-year-old man from the United States who comes to clinic with a history of depression for over 2 years. He has been previously treated with multiple antidepressants, but his symptoms have not improved. He is currently on sertraline 200 mg/day, bupropion 300 mg/day, and quetiapine 50 mg/day with no improvement in his symptoms. He has no history of psychotic disorders or bipolar disorder. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. His physical examination, laboratory studies, and ECG are unremarkable. He has a score of 28 on the MADRS and 16 on the QIDS-SR. He is willing to participate in all tests and examinations required by the protocol and has signed an informed consent document.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of dry eye disease for several months. She complains of burning, itching, and redness in her eyes, as well as a gritty sensation like there is something in her eyes. She has tried over-the-counter lubricating eye drops but has not found any relief. She has not had any recent eye surgeries or other medical conditions that may be contributing to her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies.

52-year-old female with a history of glioblastoma multiforme, diagnosed in 2016, underwent debulking surgery and radiotherapy with temozolomide. The patient developed recurrent GBM with an increasing contrast-enhanced lesion in the left parietal lobe. She underwent re-resection and pathology confirmed recurrent GBM. MRI showed a 4 cm lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding edema. She is currently on dexamethasone 4mg three times a day. No known allergies. The patient has no prior history of EGFR- or VEGFR-based therapy. She is otherwise healthy and has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. All other laboratory values and vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is postmenopausal and not currently sexually active.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has had a pacemaker implanted for sinus node dysfunction. He reports feeling fatigued and tired easily, especially during activities and exercise. He smokes occasionally and consumes alcohol occasionally. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medications. He has no history of orthopedic or vascular disability that prevents normal walking, and has no difficulty with exercise. He is willing and capable of providing informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain for the past 6 months. She has a history of fibroids and was diagnosed with several uterine fibroids during a transvaginal ultrasound. The largest fibroid measures 5 cm in diameter. She has no plans to become pregnant in the next 3 months and is not currently breastfeeding. She has no known history of cancer and is not using any investigational drugs or therapies. She has no known hypersensitivity to the active substance of ESMYA or to its excipients. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of ESMYA as a pre-operative treatment for uterine fibroids.

A 27-year-old male, non-smoker, with a body weight of 75 kg, working as a software engineer, presented for the clinical trial. He has no medical history of any cardiac, hematological, hepatic, renal, or gastrointestinal diseases. He does not have any known allergies to medications. He exercises regularly and leads a healthy lifestyle. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 2 months. He provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

35-year-old male with a history of seasonal allergies presents with a cough that has been bothering him for the past 12 hours. He reports nasal congestion, runny nose, and mild headaches but denies fever or shortness of breath. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies. He reports using over-the-counter cough syrups in the past for similar symptoms but without significant relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new cough treatment. Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild nasal congestion.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is in need of a kidney transplant. He has no significant past medical history and is willing to undergo a kidney transplant surgery. He has been approved for the surgery and meets the inclusion criteria for the control group of the study. Before the surgery, 1ml of peripheral EDTA anticoagulant from the recipient and 1ml of peripheral EDTA anticoagulant from the donor will be collected. After the surgery, he will undergo blood and urine collection at 1 week, 2 weeks, and 3 weeks to evaluate the abundance variations of nuclear genome and mitochondria-derived dd-cfDNA in the kidney transplant recipients' blood and urine. The patient understands the study protocols and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been previously diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) and has undergone initial therapy with surgical resection and external beam radiation. However, the patient experienced a recurrence of the tumor after first-line therapy and has been deemed a treatment failure. The patient is now being offered participation in a clinical trial that will test the safety of a new treatment approach called super-selective intraarterial cerebral infusion (SIACI) of Cetuximab (Erbitux). This technique will allow for the delivery of a higher concentration of the drug directly to the brain while sparing the rest of the body from systemic side effects. The trial aims to enhance the survival of patients with relapsed/refractory GBM/AA. The patient will receive a single dose of Mannitol and Cetuximab via intraarterial infusion, followed by a period of observation to assess for toxicity. If no toxicity is observed, the patient will receive their chosen chemotherapy regimen as determined by their treating oncologist. The patient must have a confirmed and evaluable tumor site and a Karnofsky performance status greater than or equal to 60%. The patient must also have adequate hematologic reserve and meet other pre-enrollment chemistry and coagulation parameters. The patient must agree to use a medically effective method of contraception during and for a period of three months after the treatment period. Women who are pregnant or lactating, and patients with significant inter-current medical or psychiatric conditions that would place them at increased risk or affect their ability to receive or comply with treatment, are excluded from the trial. Informed consent must be obtained at the time of patient screening either by the patient or a legalized authorized representative (LAR) of the patient.

55 year old female with type 2 diabetes, diagnosed 5 years ago and controlled with oral medications, presents with a history of hypertension and a previous myocardial infarction. The patient is on a stable dose of statin and fibrate therapy for the past 9 months. She has undergone a colour duplex examination which revealed the presence of at least one atheromatous plaque causing 30% narrowing of the internal carotid artery. The patient is post-menopausal and is not on any hormonal therapy. She has no history of insulin use for glycaemic control, ketoacidosis, gangrene or transient ischaemic attack. The patient is not lactating, pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. She has not had alcohol or drug abuse in the last 6 months. The patient is willing to give her signed informed consent to participate in the study.

35-year-old pregnant woman G3P2 at 39+3 weeks of gestational age presented to the obstetric clinic for scheduled first elective cesarean section. She has a history of two previous uncomplicated vaginal deliveries. Her pregnancy has been uneventful, with regular prenatal care and no complications. She has no significant medical history, no chronic illnesses, and no allergies to medications. She denies any history of recurrent urinary tract infections during the pregnancy. She has no contraindications to spinal anesthesia. Her BMI is 28, and she has gained appropriate weight during pregnancy. She is a nonsmoker and does not consume alcohol. She is married and has a supportive husband. She understands the risks and benefits of the urinary catheterization and has consented to participate in the study.

30 year old woman with no significant medical history, not currently taking any medications, and a non-smoker is eligible for this clinical trial. She has no significant occupational exposure to air pollution and has not been diagnosed with any intercurrent illness. The patient is interested in contributing to research on the effects of air pollution on cardiovascular health and is willing to participate in this study as a healthy volunteer. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who presents to the clinic with bleeding gums during brushing and flossing. He reports a history of smoking and has not seen a dentist in over a year. His past medical and drug history is unremarkable. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/85, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is within normal limits. (HbA1c: 5.6%, Glucose: 110 mg/dL, Cholesterol: 180 mg/dL)

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has been in remission for 6 months after chemotherapy. He has no significant medical history other than the AML diagnosis. He received an HLA-identical sibling donor transplant for his AML. He has completed all standard therapies and now needs a stem cell transplant. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that tests a new method to prevent graft versus host disease (GVHD). He has normal liver and kidney function, and his pulmonary

Patient is a 40yo man who has recently been diagnosed with high normal blood pressure during a routine check-up. His clinic BP readings have been consistently in the range of 135/85 to 138/89 mmHg over the past 3 visits. He has no known history of hypertension or any other medical conditions. He is otherwise healthy, physically active, and maintains a healthy diet. He has a family history of hypertension, with both his parents having been diagnosed with high blood pressure in their 50s. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent the onset of hypertension and maintain his overall health.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are under control with medication. He has also previously undergone a right ventricular (RV) pacemaker implantation due to atrioventricular (AV) block. The patient is currently experiencing symptoms of heart failure including shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise capacity. His echocardiogram shows reduced left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction of 30%, and a wide QRS complex of 130ms. He is being considered for an upgrade to cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) and is eligible for this clinical trial.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 5 years ago. She is currently on antiretroviral therapy, which has helped her achieve viral suppression. However, she has been experiencing symptoms of metabolic syndrome, including abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, and elevated cholesterol levels. She is worried about the long-term effects of metabolic syndrome on her health and has been looking for alternative treatments. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is a vegetarian and follows a healthy diet. She exercises regularly by doing yoga and walking. She does not have any known kidney or liver disease. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of berberine on metabolic syndrome in people living with HIV under viral suppression. She hopes that this study will help her improve her metabolic profile and reduce her risk of developing cardiovascular disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with gastric cancer, who is scheduled to undergo a gastrectomy. He has no known allergies or medical conditions, and is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I. The patient reports experiencing moderate to severe pain in the abdominal area, which is affecting his ability to perform routine activities. He has no history of spine anomaly or abdominal surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits associated with the different pain management options.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been experiencing severe lower back pain that radiates to his right leg for the past 8 months. The pain is described as sharp and burning and interferes with his daily activities. The patient has tried conservative treatment options such as physical therapy, pain medication, and acupuncture, but has not experienced significant relief. Imaging studies reveal that the patient has degenerative foraminal stenosis. The patient is scheduled for a lumbar foraminotomy procedure and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has no history of trauma, tumor or infection and does not have any other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is not pregnant and does not have any major surgery within the past 3 months. He has not had any prior nerve block procedures and is willing to undergo the SNRB without IV sedation. He is available for the entire study duration of 12 months.

This study does not involve direct patient recruitment or enrollment as it is using data from participants already enrolled in the Black Women's Health Study residing in New York, Los Angeles, or Chicago. Therefore, patient descriptions are not applicable for this trial.

The patient is a 22-year-old male college student enrolled at the University of Wyoming. He is a native English speaker and is currently enrolled full-time as an undergraduate student. He has self-reported symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and has previously been diagnosed with ADHD by a medical professional. He reports experiencing five or more inattention symptoms on the DSM-5 Symptom Checklist during the pre-screener. He has no history of prior stimulant use and meets low risk for stimulant medication use contraindications. He is not pregnant or attempting to become pregnant and has no history of major depressive disorder, panic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, or substance use disorder

The patient is a 45 year old male who presented with a history of fatigue and abdominal discomfort. He is overweight with a BMI of 30 and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His liver function tests showed elevated liver enzymes and an ultrasound revealed fatty liver. He was diagnosed with metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and has been advised to make lifestyle modifications including weight loss and regular exercise. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He is interested in participating in research to find a better understanding of the causes of MAFLD and potential new treatments.

35F with a BMI of 43.5 kg/m2, diagnosed with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for 4 years. She has been struggling to control her blood sugar and blood pressure despite being on multiple medications. She has tried various weight loss methods including diet and exercise but has not been successful in achieving long-term weight loss. She is motivated to undergo bariatric surgery to improve her health and quality of life. She has no history of previous bariatric surgery. She understands the risks and benefits of laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of Clostridium botulinum neurotoxin A (BTX-A) injection into the pyloric sphincter during the operation to decrease the risk of postoperative gastric leakage.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who underwent surgical extraction of three molars, including one partial bony mandibular third molar impaction. He reports moderate to severe postoperative dental pain and is not currently taking any medication for anxiety, depression, or schizophrenia. He weighs 175 pounds and has a BMI of 22. He has no significant medical conditions and has not taken any pain relievers or anti-inflammatory drugs within the last 24 hours. He has no history of adverse reactions to acetaminophen, ibuprofen or any anesthetic agent used in the extraction. He is able to swallow medication whole. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding.

This is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic gastritis, who presented with epigastric pain and weight loss. Endoscopy revealed a large, ulcerated lesion in the antrum of the stomach, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies showed no evidence of distant metastasis or involvement of the esophagus, but lymph node involvement was suspected. The patient underwent laparoscopy and PLS was negative for peritoneal metastasis. The final diagnosis was Borrmann type 4 gastric cancer with N1 lymph node involvement. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy for any malignancy, and his ECOG performance status is 1. He has adequate organ function and is able to maintain sufficient oral intake. The patient has no other malignancies or severe complications and is willing to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male with a history of COPD presents to the hospital with shortness of breath, cough and wheezing. Upon evaluation, he is found to have worsening respiratory distress, and a chest X-ray confirms the presence of a COPD exacerbation. The patient is started on nebulizers, steroids, and antibiotics; however, his condition continues to deteriorate, and he requires mechanical ventilation. The patient is sedated and intubated. After stabilization, the patient is approached for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating spirometric data in mechanically ventilated COPD patients. The patient consents to participate, and spirometry will be performed daily once he is awake and cooperative. The patient will be evaluated for eventual rate of successful extubation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her right knee for the past year. She reports that the pain is worse when she is walking or standing for long periods of time. She has been diagnosed with medial knee osteoarthritis by x-ray and arthroscopy. Her knee pain has been managed with conservative treatment such as physiotherapy, weight loss, and pain medications, but has not improved significantly. Her correction angle is 8 degrees. She does not have a history of infection in the knee, rheumatoid arthritis, cancer, neurological disease, kidney disease or metabolic disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare two techniques for high tibial osteotomy (HTO) for the treatment of medial knee osteoarthritis. She understands that she will be randomly assigned to either the opening wedge or closing wedge group and will be followed for 2 years with repetitive evaluations to assess her knee function and range of motion.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and in her first trimester. She has not experienced any complications during the pregnancy so far. She has a history of two previous pregnancies, both of which resulted in spontaneous abortions in the first trimester. The patient is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She does not smoke, consume alcohol, or use drugs. She has no known allergies. The patient is willing to provide vaginal specimens for the study and agrees to follow-up visits at week 19 of gestation. The patient has no history of bacterial vaginosis or any other vaginal infections.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with salivary gland cancer of the head and neck three years ago. He underwent surgery followed by radiation therapy, but unfortunately, the cancer recurred and metastasized to his lungs. He received one line of systemic chemotherapy, but it was not effective. He is now experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and persistent cough. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing golf on weekends. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and hopes to find a treatment that can improve his condition. His performance status is 1 and he has adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal functions. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial.

32-year-old male diagnosed with hemophilia A at birth. He has a history of multiple joint bleeds and has been receiving prophylactic treatment with factor VIII concentrate since childhood. He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 3 years ago and started on antiretroviral therapy, which included two NRTIs and one NNRTI. However, his HIV viral load has remained detectable despite adherence to the treatment regimen. He has also experienced side effects such as nausea and fatigue. His CD4+ T lymphocyte count is currently 350 cells/mm3. He has no history of opportunistic infections or malignancies. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new integrase inhibitor called MK-0518 in combination with his current antiretroviral therapy. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

28-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a meningococcal vaccine. She is willing to comply with all protocol procedures and time commitments of the study. She is willing to practice an effective birth control method as necessary for 6 months after the first vaccination. She has no history of allergy to any vaccine or aluminum hydroxide. She has not received any live vaccine, Investigational New Drug (IND) products, or significant immunosuppressive therapy in the 28 days prior to, or any inactivated vaccine within 14 days before initial vaccination or throughout the study. She has not received parenteral immunoglobulin or blood products within 3 months of study initiation. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse/dependence. She does not plan to leave the area during the study such that she would miss 1 or more study days. She has not received any group B meningococcal outer membrane protein (OMP) vaccine or a vaccine containing meningococcal OMP.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was admitted to the emergency ward with a fever, chills, and severe abdominal pain. She was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection and prescribed antibiotics by the attending physician. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. The patient has not been hospitalized in the past year and has not received any antibiotics in the past three months. She is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

This is a 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to monitor the functional variation in her breasts during her menstrual cycle. She has a normal breast tissue and regular menstrual cycles that do not vary by more than 5 days. She is not taking any oral contraceptives or birth control medications in the past six months. She has no history of breast cancer or breast surgery, and she is not taking any light-sensitive drugs for photodynamic therapy. She is interested in learning more about how endogenous hormones affect breast tissue physiology and the potential benefits of Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy imaging in detecting changes in hemoglobin concentration and tissue scattering. She is motivated to participate in this study and is willing to undergo two months of self-monitoring.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with Stage 4 Chronic Kidney Disease. She was diagnosed with CKD a year ago due to hypertension and has been undergoing treatment with angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and diuretics. She has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been experiencing fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and shortness of breath lately. Her blood pressure is well controlled, and she has been adhering to a low protein diet. She is not on hormone replacement therapy, tobacco products, or antioxidants. She has not been diagnosed with any autoimmune disease and her liver enzymes are within the normal range. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her vascular health and possibly reduce her risk of cardiovascular disease.

A 54-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of weakness and lack of movement in his right arm after suffering from a stroke 2 weeks ago. He is right-hand dominant and is having difficulty with daily activities like holding a cup or using utensils. He is medically stable and has an AMT score of 8/10. His Motricity Index Arm Score is 35/100. He is able to stand with minimal assistance but has pre-existing moderate oedema in his hand. He does not have any pre-existing shoulder or upper limb pain. He is not a resident of any institution and does not have any psychiatric problems. He is interested in participating in the Neuro Hand Orthosis Program to help regain movement in his paralytic arm.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male with a history of colon cancer presents to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss. He had undergone a surgical resection of the colon tumor previously and had completed adjuvant chemotherapy six months ago. Imaging studies reveal multiple metastases in the liver and lungs. Histological examination confirmed the presence of colorectal cancer. The patient's performance status is 1 according to the WHO criteria. Laboratory results are within normal limits, including kidney and liver function tests. The patient is planned to receive systemic treatment with fluoropyrimidine monotherapy with or without bevacizumab. The patient has not received prior treatment for metastatic disease or radiotherapy to the affected area. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

This is a 45 year-old female who has been diagnosed with non-infectious ocular inflammatory disease, specifically retinal vasculitis involving the arteries or veins. Her fundus is viewable with wide-field FA in both eyes, but only one eye will be included in the study. She is currently not on any non-steroidal immunosuppressive therapy, but is willing to start the trial medication, Acthar. She is not pregnant and has no history of malignancy or known hypersensitivity to Acthar. She has not received systemic corticosteroids or periocular/intraocular injections of medications to control inflammation within the past 6 weeks. She does not have any severe disease that would warrant critical attention or deemed unsafe for the study by the investigator. She is willing and able to sign the informed consent form.

52-year-old female with a BMI of 39.5 kg/m2 and history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She was diagnosed with stage III chronic kidney disease (CKD) six months ago, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 40 ml/min and microalbuminuria. She has been struggling with weight loss despite multiple attempts with dietary modifications and exercise. Her current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and amlodipine. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effects of intentional weight loss interventions in CKD patients. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. She is willing to undergo lifestyle modification or bariatric surgery to achieve weight loss and improve her kidney function. She understands that she will be part of a non-randomized prospective study and will undergo blood tests, renal function studies, and body composition measurements at baseline, 3-, and 6-month intervals. She is excited to participate in this study and hopes to improve her overall health and well-being.

The patient is a 50 year old female who has been diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma. She has completed the OTX-16-002 trial with bilateral treatment and completion through a minimum of week 12. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and visit schedule for one year. She has provided written informed consent, approved by the appropriate Institutional Review Board. She has not had more than 1 replacement, per eye, during participation in the OTX-16-002 trial and has not had punctal or canaliculi related adverse events during the OTX-16-002 trial which required discontinuation. She has not used any prohibited medications during the OTX-16-002 study or the period between OTX-16-002 and this trial (with the exception of short term medication used to treat an adverse event or rescue therapy). She has not missed more than 2 visits during participation in the OTX-16-002 trial.

A 32 yo F presenting with a history of depression for the past 2 years with no prior history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. Currently taking fluoxetine for depression. She reports difficulty concentrating and forgetfulness. She has no known medical conditions and no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is interested in participating in the neuropsychological evaluation trial to better understand her cognitive function.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who suffered a severe neurological injury resulting in quadriplegia after a motor vehicle accident. He has been hospitalized in the neuroICU of Montpellier University Hospital, France for more than 48 hours and requires mechanical ventilation. The patient's neurological injury was assessed and found to be stable. The patient is alert and responsive but has limited mobility due to the neurological injury. The patient has no history of allergy to any medication. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is currently receiving sedation and is scheduled to undergo sedation weaning soon. The patient is eligible for this study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being an adult with severe neurological injury and requiring mechanical ventilation for >48 hours. The patient will be divided into either the beneficiaries or non-beneficiaries group based on the criteria for using suspension walking used in standard practice in the unit. The study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and benefits of using a specific suspension walking device (LiteGait®) for patients with severe neurological injuries in the neuroICU.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered a traumatic injury to his left arm in a motor vehicle accident. He underwent surgery for an arm arterial repair using a synthetic graft 9 months ago. He complains of persistent cold intolerance, pain, and weakness in his left hand. He reports difficulty with daily activities such as buttoning his shirt and holding a cup of coffee. He is currently taking acetaminophen for pain relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the occurrence of blood vessel occlusion in the arm after at least 6 months of surgery and the impact of this event on the sensory and motor function of the hand. He understands that the study will involve physical exams, non-invasive tests, duplex doppler ultrasound and questionnaires. He is willing and able to comply with follow-up tests/procedures and questionnaires.

A 8-year-old boy with Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH) presented to the clinic with complaints of pain in his lower molars. The pain started a week ago and has progressively increased in intensity. The patient has a history of asthma and eczema, but his conditions are well-controlled with medications. He has no allergies to any medications. He is under the supervision of his parents and has a telephone at home.
