The patient has been diagnosed with MIH and has multiple enamel and dentin fractures in his lower molars that require restorative treatment. He rates his pain as 7 out of 10 on a visual analog scale. He has never undergone any dental procedure before and is anxious about the upcoming treatment.

The patient is a 24-year-old female who has been struggling with anorexia nervosa for the past 5 years. She has been in and out of treatment centers and psychiatric hospitals, but has not yet found a successful treatment. She is currently underweight, with a BMI of 16.5, and is experiencing cognitive and emotional symptoms such as anxiety, depression, and difficulty concentrating. She reports feeling constantly fatigued and has reported changes in her sleep patterns, often staying up late at night and sleeping during the day. Her family is supportive, but she currently lives alone and has limited social connections. She has no history of substance abuse, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her eating disorder.

A 45-year-old male patient has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past year. He has tried physical therapy and pain medication but has not found relief. MRI scans show that he has a herniated disc in his lumbar spine. His doctor has recommended lumbar spinal surgery to alleviate his symptoms. He has no history of previous spinal surgery and is not pregnant. He meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is interested in participating to help advance spinal surgery techniques.

A 35-year-old female with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 came to the Clinic for participation in a clinical trial. She has no history of coronary heart disease, diabetes, atherosclerosis, or peripheral arterial disease. Her laboratory test results were normal except for a slightly elevated blood pressure. She does not smoke and has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. She is not pregnant or planning to be pregnant during the study period. She understands the study procedures and has provided informed consent to participate. She is willing to consume the study products as directed and to avoid alcohol consumption for 24 hours prior to each clinic visit. She has no plans to change her smoking habits and is willing to maintain a stable body weight, activity level, and dietary pattern except for the use of the study products. She is not taking any lipid-altering drugs, weight-loss medications, or supplements known to alter lipid metabolism. She has not used EPA/DHA from a drug or supplement within four months of visit 1 and has not consumed fatty fish more than twice per month. She is not allergic to study products or any of their ingredients.

A 42-year-old Hispanic man with a history of mild-to-moderate hypertension presented with occasional headaches and shortness of breath on exertion. He had been taking Amlodipine 5mg daily for the past 6 months. His blood pressure readings were averaging 145/95 mmHg during his office visits. He denied any chest pain, palpitations, syncope, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or lower extremity swelling. He had no significant past medical history and was not taking any other medications. He had a BMI of 29. His physical examination was unremarkable except for elevated blood pressure. Laboratory tests including complete blood count, renal function, and electrolyte levels were within normal limits. ECG was normal. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) was performed over 24 hours and showed an average systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 90 mmHg. He was then enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the trough and peak effect of once daily Micardis plus.

A 32-year-old woman with a clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes for the past 5 years presents with well-controlled HbA1c levels (7.2%). She has been on a stable insulin regimen for the past 3 months and uses an insulin pump. She has no history of severe hypoglycemia or autonomic nerve dysfunction. Her BMI is 26 kg/m2. She has no history of hepatic or renal disease, cardiovascular or pulmonary disease, gastrointestinal disease or CNS disease. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is currently not taking any medications that interfere with gastric emptying. She understands and signs the informed consent document and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. She practices appropriate contraception and agrees to take every precaution to ensure that pregnancy will not occur during the study.

56 year old male with a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia presented to the cardiology clinic with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few weeks and has been using nitroglycerin to alleviate the chest pain. The patient is a former smoker and quit 3 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and takes only lisinopril and atorvastatin for his hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, respectively. His vital signs are within normal limits and he has no signs of heart failure. His EKG shows ST-segment depression in the inferolateral leads. A cardiac catheterization is planned to evaluate the patient's coronary arteries. The patient is interested in participating in a study that will compare the safety and effects of fasting or not fasting overnight before a cardiac catheterization.

A 28-year-old Hispanic female presented to the psychiatric clinic with symptoms of schizophrenia. She reported experiencing auditory hallucinations and delusions of persecution for the past 2 months. She has no previous history of psychiatric illness and was diagnosed with schizophrenia based on DSM-5 criteria during her first visit. She has been experiencing significant functional impairment and is currently unable to work. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse but is a regular smoker. She provided informed consent and agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will study the efficacy and safety of an investigational drug in acutely psychotic people with schizophrenia. Her CGI-S score was 5 and her PANSS total score was 85 with PANSS item scores of 4 or higher for delusions, conceptual disorganization, hallucinations, and unusual thought content. She is in good general health, with no significant medical history or laboratory abnormalities. She is not pregnant or lactating.

A 42-year-old male with a history of malignant melanoma presents to the oncology clinic with elevated LDH levels. He was diagnosed with stage IV melanoma two years ago when he presented with multiple subcutaneous nodules and enlarged lymph nodes. He underwent surgical resection of the nodules and received adjuvant therapy with interferon alpha. He responded well initially, but the disease progressed after six months, and he was started on vemurafenib and cobimetinib. He continued therapy for six months and had a partial response, but he eventually developed resistance to the treatment. His LDH levels have been increasing for the past six months, and he now has multiple new subcutaneous nodules, lymphadenopathy, and lung metastases. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has adequate hepatic, renal, and bone marrow function. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. He is not on any prohibited foods or supplements, and he does not have a history of retinal pathology.

The patient is a 27-year-old pregnant female in her first trimester of pregnancy. She has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and has been medically cleared for participation in the study by her primary care obstetrician. She has no history of preterm birth, spontaneous abortion, gestational hypertension, or pre-eclampsia in her current pregnancy. She has no history of intrauterine growth-restriction, second- or third-trimester bleeding, placenta previa, incompetent cervix, or cerclage. She does not have severe anemia, heart or lung disease, HIV or AIDS, or any magnetic metallic objects in her body. She is willing to have placental biospecimens collected at delivery. The patient will be asked to wear an activity monitor to track her physical activity levels throughout her pregnancy.

9-year-old female, born in Spain to immigrant parents from a country with a high incidence of TB. The patient and her family plan to visit relatives in their home country for a period of 1 month. The patient has no history of TB or LTBI and does not have any known immunodeficiency or congenital diseases.

A 58-year-old man who has had his first episode of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (MI) two months ago is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. He has no known history of cardiovascular disease (CVD), hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia but has a family history of CVD. He is a retired school teacher and is currently living with his wife. He reports a history of smoking, but he quit six years ago. He has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism. He reports moderate physical activity, including walking for 30 minutes a day, five days a week. He has no known history of depression or psychological distress. He reports good sleep quality and no sexual dysfunction. He is currently taking medication for hypertension, but no medication for diabetes or hyperlipidemia. His BMI is 26. He is willing to participate in every phase of the study and provide written informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of obesity for the past 15 years came to the clinic seeking treatment options. Her current weight is 135 kg with a BMI of 46. She has attempted various weight loss methods including dieting, exercise, medication, and bariatric surgery, but none have been successful in achieving long-term weight loss. She has a sedentary lifestyle and her daily calorie intake is high. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are poorly controlled. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her family history is negative for obesity, but her mother and sister have a history of diabetes. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the possibility of deep brain stimulation as a treatment option for her obesity.

This is a 24 year-old healthy male who does not smoke and has no history of metabolic disease. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of blackcurrant juice on cognitive performance, blood flow, and blood glucose levels. He is willing to consume a single serve of 'Blackadder' blackcurrant juice and undergo blood tests to assess the pharmacodynamics of the juice. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no known medical conditions or history of psychiatric disorders.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of Crohn's disease comes to the clinic for her routine check-up. She has undergone bowel surgery in the past and is currently in remission without the need for immunosuppressive drugs. She reports experiencing occasional abdominal pain and bloating, but no diarrhea or blood in her stool. Due to her high inherent TNF-α production, the doctor informs her about a clinical trial that is investigating the effects of parenteral fish oil on immune modulation in Crohn's disease patients. The patient is interested in participating and meets all the inclusion criteria. She is a non-smoker and does not consume fatty fish more than twice a week. She has no history of metabolic disorders, active fistulas, or other inflammatory/immune-mediated conditions. She is not currently on any medications other than 5-aminosalicylic acid preparations. Her blood work shows a C-reactive protein level of 8 mg/L, which is within the study's criteria. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not allergic to fish, chicken, eggs, or soybeans. The doctor discusses the trial's potential benefits and risks with the patient, and she agrees to participate.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who presented with a complaint of pain in the lower right jaw. She has been experiencing this pain for the past 3 weeks and it has been gradually getting worse. She reports sensitivity to hot and cold beverages and difficulty with chewing on that side. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. On dental examination, she was found to have a non-vital mandibular molar with apical periodontitis. She is considered eligible for the study since she is medically free, between 18-40 years and has a non-vital mandibular molar with closed apex. The patient is informed about the study and agrees to participate. She will be randomly assigned to either the control group or the intervention group and will be required to record post-operative pain at specific time points. She will also have a CBCT scan at 6 and 12 months after the treatment to assess peri-apical healing.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with osteoarthritis in both knees and hips. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in the joints for the past 5 years, which has been progressively worsening. She has tried various non-pharmacological methods such as physical therapy and weight loss, but they have not provided significant relief. The patient has a stable medical history with no significant past surgeries or hospitalizations. Her current medications include over-the-counter pain relievers and occasional use of prescription pain medications. The patient has a BMI of 29 and is classified as ASA 2. She has good communication skills and is willing to follow instructions during the study. The patient has no known contraindications against the use of local anaesthetics and is not pregnant. She is scheduled for elective total hip and knee arthroplasty and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old Caucasian male who consumes alcohol occasionally. He has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, abdominal surgery or alcohol abuse. He does not take any medications that may interact with ethanol metabolism or intestinal permeability. He does not smoke and has a normal BMI of 23 kg/m2. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is interested in participating in the study to gain more insight into the effects of moderate alcohol drinking on the small intestinal permeability.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo DIEP-flap breast reconstruction surgery at the participating department. The patient has a history of hypertension, but is well-controlled on medication. She is a non-smoker and is not currently using cortisone or any other immunosuppressants. The patient does not have diabetes mellitus type 1 or 2, nor does she have any connective tissue disease. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve her wound healing and scar formation after the surgery.

This is a 35-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the bioavailability of different formulations of AZD9977 and dapagliflozin and the influence of food in selected formulations in healthy volunteers. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m² and weighs 55 kg. She has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal disease, or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. She has not received any new chemical entity within the last 3 months and has not donated plasma or blood within the last month or lost more than 500 mL of blood within the last 3 months. She is a non-smoker and has not used nicotine products within the last 3 months. She has no history of severe allergy/hypersensitivity to drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to AZD9977 or dapagliflozin. She is able to communicate reliably with the investigators and understands the German language. She has no clinical signs and symptoms consistent with COVID-19, and has not been hospitalized or required mechanical ventilation due to COVID-19.

A 67-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer a year ago and underwent surgical removal of his prostate. However, his cancer recurred and he was started on androgen blockade therapy. His PSA levels have been rising steadily despite the treatment. He has no significant medical history, except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC).

45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient is undergoing evaluation for coronary artery disease and is scheduled for transradial coronary angiography. Prior to the procedure, the patient will undergo evaluation of the palmar arterial arch circulation as a quality control measure. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the follow-up Doppler ultrasound examination. The patient has not undergone any prior coronary artery bypass surgery.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-metastatic breast cancer. She has been recommended for adjuvant hormone therapy and is concerned about the impact it may have on her sexual function. She is sexually active and has a supportive partner. She has no history of heavy psychiatric pathology and is able to understand and consent to participate in the study. She is not currently pregnant or receiving adjuvant chemotherapy.

A 76-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with elevated PSA levels and a biopsy consistent with prostate cancer. The patient is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic radical prostatectomy. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, but has no history of central nervous system disease or psychiatric illness. He is able to perform activities of daily living independently and has a standardized Mini Mental Test score of 27. He has no history of arrhythmia or previous open heart surgery, and his renal and liver function are within normal limits. The patient is classified as ASA II. The patient has provided informed consent and wishes to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the effect of preoperative intravenous amantadine sulfate on the prevention of early cognitive dysfunction.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy for this condition. The patient's cancer has metastasized and he has measurable disease, with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded) as >= 20 mm with conventional techniques or as >= 10 mm with spiral CT scan. He has no acute intercurrent illness or infection and his ECOG performance status is =<2 (Karnofsky =>60%). The patient has normal organ and marrow function including leukocytes=>3,000/uL, absolute neutrophil count=>1,500/uL, platelets =>100,000/uL, hemoglobin >= 8g/dl, total bilirubin within normal institutional limits, and creatinine =<2.0 xULN OR creatinine clearance >60 mL/min/1.73 m**2 for patients with creatinine levels above institutional normal. The patient has a history of non-melanoma skin cancer and is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient will be treated with OSI-774 by mouth once a day and every 3 weeks with docetaxel and cisplatin, given by a continuous infusion into a vein over 1 hour and followed by an infusion into a vein of cisplatin over 2 hours. Treatment with docetaxel and cisplatin is given every 3 weeks for 18 weeks. The patient will continue to take OSI-774 until his disease worsens, until side effects become too severe, or until his doctor thinks it is no longer benefiting him. The patient will be asked to have blood drawn once a week for routine lab tests and every 6 weeks during treatment, he will have blood tests, and imaging tests including a chest x-ray and a CT scan of the head and neck area. The patient may continue receiving OSI-774 for as long as his cancer responds to study treatment. There will be no cost for OSI-774 or for any tests and procedures performed solely for this research study.

A 30-year-old male with a history of epilepsy since childhood, currently taking a combination of two antiepileptic drugs, presents with an increase in seizure frequency and intensity over the past 6 months. Despite increasing the doses of both medications, he continues to have seizures at least twice a week, which significantly affects his daily life and work. He reports experiencing adverse effects, such as dizziness, headache, and fatigue, which further impair his quality of life. He has no significant medical or surgical history, no known allergies, and is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the predictive and modulating factors of pharmacoresistance to antiepileptic drugs, and to potentially receive a more personalized treatment plan. He is able to give reliable information and has a caregiver who can assist with monitoring his seizure frequency and adverse effects. He is not pregnant and has no severe comorbidities that would impede interpretation.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of congenital hearing loss in the right ear. The patient has been recommended for an ear level bone anchored sound processor and has been referred by an audiologist for the Minimally Invasive Ponto Surgical Technique (MIPS) study. The patient has healthy bone quality and has not undergone any previous procedure for placing Oticon Medical Ponto implants and abutments. The patient is willing and able to participate in follow-up appointments and has no history of psychiatric disease or mental disability. The patient is not currently undergoing any treatments that may compromise bone quality at the implant site. The patient's natural skin height is within the range required for the study.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with hypertension (high blood pressure) during a routine check-up. She is currently taking an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACE-I) to manage her blood pressure. She has a history of seasonal allergies and has had no surgeries in the past. She is married with two children, and uses an intrauterine device (IUD) for contraception. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 25. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She has no history of heart disease, respiratory or neurological problems, and has no known drug allergies.

A 45 year old woman has been scheduled for an ambulatory surgery at the Surgical Center Emile Galle. She has a social security affiliation and has agreed to participate in the study. She has access to technology equipment such as a smartphone, touchpad, and computer with a web browser (Chrome or Internet Explorer), webcam, and microphone. She is willing to use the platform for video-conferencing and has a printer available. She has no history of any medical conditions that would fall under the exclusion criteria for the study. She has no objections to being randomly assigned to either the teleconsultation or traditional consultation group.

A 55-year-old Chinese woman, who is overweight and has a family history of diabetes, went to the clinic for a routine check-up. Her fasting plasma glucose level was found to be elevated, and she was diagnosed with pre-diabetes. She has no history of acute cardiovascular disease or gastrointestinal disease. She is not taking any anti-diabetic agents or dietary supplements that affect glucose or galactose metabolism. She has no lactose or galactose intolerance, and she is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of eating disorder. She is willing to use adequate and effective contraception during the study period. She is able to consistently record her food intake to facilitate the CGMS evaluation. She is interested in taking part in the clinical trial to test whether a medicine named BTI320, also known as SUGARDOWN®, can help to lower her blood sugar levels.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was involved in a car accident and has multiple injuries, including a fractured femur and rib fractures. He is currently in the intensive care unit and is being ventilated. He has a stable hemodynamic status with a mean blood pressure of 75 mmHg. He has no history of central venous thrombosis or cervical spine surgery. He is not currently receiving noradrenaline treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and has a registered social security number. His family members have also given their consent for his participation.

A 45-year-old man was recently diagnosed with Erdheim Chester disease after experiencing persistent fatigue, bone pain, and unexplained weight loss. He underwent a biopsy of a bone lesion and the pathology confirmed the presence of BRAF V600 mutation. He has no significant medical history and has not received any prior treatment for ECD. He is currently asymptomatic with no evidence of visceral involvement. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0. He is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has no clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities. His laboratory values show an ANC of 2.2 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 12.8 g/dL, and platelets of 220 x 10^9/L. His serum bilirubin, AST, ALT, and creatinine levels are within normal limits. He has no history of cardiovascular risks or retinal vein occlusion. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate contraception for the duration of study participation. He is able to travel to the treating center for the duration of the trial.

A 27-year-old male with a history of choroideremia, a genetic disorder that causes progressive vision loss, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been experiencing visual difficulties, including difficulty seeing in low light and loss of peripheral vision. The patient has undergone multimodal imaging that revealed anomalies consistent with CHM. He has been identified as carrying the CHM mutation and is interested in participating in the study to help further research on inherited retinal dystrophies. He has appropriate health insurance and has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 62 year-old female with a diagnosis of osteoarthritis in her right knee. She has been experiencing severe pain and stiffness in the knee for several years, which has significantly impacted her quality of life. She has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy, pain medication, and corticosteroid injections, but they have not provided long-term relief. Her orthopedic surgeon has recommended a primary total knee replacement to alleviate her symptoms and improve her mobility. She has no history of prior knee replacements or motor impairments.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been struggling with obesity for most of her adult life. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has been unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. She has a past medical history of hypertension and sleep apnea. Her current medications include Lisinopril 20mg daily for hypertension and a CPAP machine for her sleep apnea. She has no history of liver disease or diabetes. She is scheduled to undergo bariatric surgery in the coming weeks. Prior to the surgery, a liver biopsy will be performed to confirm the presence of NASH. If NASH is confirmed, she will be randomized to receive either metformin or placebo for a period of 1 year. She is willing to participate in this study to potentially improve her liver health and overall health outcomes.

Patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with osteopenia based on Tscore (-2.5 SD ≤ Tscore ≤ -1 SD). She has a history of mild hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She has no history of bone diseases, cancer, diabetes, kidney failure, liver disease, or any systemic inflammatory diseases. She has not been on any drugs that affect bone metabolism for the past two years, and does not smoke. Her BMI is 25. She exercises regularly and has no physical disabilities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the effects of oligopin supplementation on bone turnover markers and antioxidant changes in postmenopausal women with osteopenia.

The patient is a 56-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer in her left breast. She underwent a lumpectomy and the surgical margins were negative. Her pathology report confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma, ER positive, PR negative, and Her2/neu negative. She has no history of collagen-vascular disease and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her breast MRI prior to surgery revealed no evidence of disease outside of the planned lumpectomy volume. Her mammogram did not show any malignant calcifications. The patient is willing to undergo additional screening and meet the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial. The fiducial markers required for IGRT can be successfully placed for her. The ratio of the planned target volume (PTV) to the ipsilateral breast ratio (IBR) is less than or equal to 25%. Radiotherapy is anticipated to begin within 10 weeks of her lumpectomy.

A 75-year-old retired teacher came to the clinic complaining of difficulty hearing. She reported that she has been experiencing hearing loss for the past few years and it has been affecting her daily interactions with family and friends. She has been feeling isolated and frustrated due to her hearing impairment. She has no history of dementia or any other neurological disorders. She is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. She is living in her own house and is able to perform her daily activities independently. Her hearing was tested and showed a moderate hearing loss in both ears. She was advised to use hearing aids and was referred to the clinical trial investigating the relationship between hearing impairment and dementia in older adults.

The patient is a 60 year old male of Hispanic origin with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who recently underwent angioplasty for a single vessel stenosis. The patient is working as an accountant and is married with two adult children. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is moderately physically active and enjoys playing golf and gardening. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to provide informed consent within one week after the procedure. The patient does not have any mobility issues and is able to walk several blocks without difficulty.

The patient is a 23 year-old female who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 14. She has been using an insulin pump for the past 2 years and has been monitoring her glucose levels regularly. Her HbA1c levels are currently at 8.5%. She has a history of hypoglycemic episodes and has been hospitalized for severe hypoglycemia twice in the past year. She is currently not taking any other antihyperglycemic agents or medications that alter gastrointestinal motility. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use a highly effective method of birth control during the trial. She has no history of severe complications related to diabetes such as nephropathy, neuropathy or retinopathy. She is compliant with her current treatment and is willing to follow the study recommendations.

A 34 year old nurse who works at Lake Forrest Memorial Hospital is eligible for this clinical trial. She has been working at the hospital for the past 5 years and has not been diagnosed with COVID19. She has no known medical history of cardiovascular disease or other medical conditions that may affect her ECG readings. She has been regularly screened for COVID19 as part of the hospital's protocol and has tested negative so far. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the purpose and potential risks involved.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. She has been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment and is being followed up by her neurologist. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and osteoporosis. She takes lisinopril and alendronate. She lives independently and is still able to perform her activities of daily living. She has a BMI of 28 and is physically active. She underwent a tau-PET imaging study, which showed positivity. She has a LAR who will be accompanying her to all study visits and will provide study partner-reported outcomes. She does not plan on traveling during the study period. She has no hearing, vision, or motor deficits that would limit her ability to complete study physical assessments. She has not had a myocardial infarction, angina, stroke, or transient ischemic attack in the past 6 months, nor does she have chronic heart failure. She is not currently taking cholinesterase inhibitors or memantine. She does not have substance or alcohol abuse. She has no uncontrolled psychiatric or systemic lupus erythematosus disorder. She has no malabsorption, and her AST/ALT levels are normal. She is not known to have HIV or active hepatitis B or C infection. She has no invasive fungal or viral infections. She is not hypersensitive or allergic to Dasatinib or Quercetin. She does not have uncontrolled pleural/pericardial effusions or ascites. She has no active invasive cancer except for non-melanoma skin cancers. She is able to tolerate oral medications. She has no uncontrolled diabetes, gastric bypass/reduction, Crohn's disease, myopathies, or significant liver disease. She is not taking therapeutic doses of anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents.

A 50-year-old woman with type II diabetes for 10 years presents to the clinic for a routine nerve conduction study. She complains of occasional numbness and tingling in her toes and feet, as well as occasional shooting pains. She has no history of non-diabetic neuropathy caused by genetic, metabolic, inflammatory diseases, toxic agents, or drug-induced factors. She has no known allergies to anesthesia or any other medications. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and sign an approved informed consent form. The study aims to determine if ultrasound can detect diabetic peripheral neuropathy by measuring the cross-sectional area of the Posterior Tibial Nerve (PTN) in diabetic patients with distal symmetric polyneuropathy (DSPN) as compared to diabetic patients without DSPN. The study is seeking type I and type II diabetic patients who have been diagnosed for more than five years and are scheduled for routine NCS.

A 40-year-old male with HIV and Hepatitis C virus (HCV) who has been on tenofovir-based antiretroviral therapy with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) protease inhibitors (HIV PI/r) for the past 6 months. He has a history of injection drug use and alcohol abuse. His most recent HCV RNA test showed a viral load of 25,000 IU/mL. He has no previous history of renal disease and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 80 ml/min. He is not pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy. He is willing to participate in the study and has no medical, social, or mental-health issues that could interfere with study participation or the study outcomes.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been regularly attending the Outpatient Clinic of the Diabetes Centre at the University Hospital in Thessaloniki, Greece. He has been diagnosed with type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for 8 years and has been taking Premixed Human Insulin 30/70 twice daily along with metformin for the last 3 years. His baseline HbA1c level is below 7%. He has no history of major cardiovascular events in the last 6 months and has not been hospitalized for any acute illness in the last 2 weeks. He is not pregnant and is able to understand the study procedures and sign the consent form. He has been self-monitoring his blood glucose levels and his measurements are within the desired range (>80mg/dl and <130mg/dl) for the past week.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage III Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma two years ago. She has undergone chemotherapy and is currently in remission. The patient's oncologist recommends allogeneic stem cell transplantation as the next course of treatment. The patient presents with no known allergies and has no significant medical history other than her cancer diagnosis. She is currently taking medications for hypertension and has a blood pressure reading of 130/80 mmHg. Her laboratory test results show normal liver and kidney function. The patient is well-informed about the clinical trial and has signed the written informed consent. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is not participating in any other experimental drug trials. The patient has no uncontrolled infections and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

Patient is a 26-year-old pregnant woman from Kenya who has been diagnosed with HIV. She has access to a mobile phone and plans to remain in the study area for at least two years. She has no history of drug resistance and has not started antiretroviral therapy (ART) yet. She is currently receiving prenatal care and is interested in participating in the study to improve her adherence and retention in care for the benefit of her and her unborn child.

35-year-old male with a history of hypertension and mild renal dysfunction (creatinine clearance between 60 and 89 mL/min calculated by Cockcroft-Gault equation) presents for screening. He currently takes lisinopril and amlodipine for his hypertension. He reports no other significant medical history and denies any current symptoms. He has a body weight of 70 kg and is 5'10" tall. He has no history of gastrointestinal disease or surgery that may affect absorption of the investigational product. He is negative for serum and urine hCG and does not plan on providing sperm or egg during the clinical trial. He is willing to use effective contraceptive methods during the trial. He is a non-smoker and does not drink heavily. He has not taken any over-the-counter drugs or dietary supplements within the past 14 days. He is willing to provide blood and urine samples during the post-study visit.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and diabetes. She has been admitted to the hospital with a fever and chills, and blood cultures have identified the presence of gram-negative bacillus bacteremia. The patient is currently receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics, but the treating physician is unsure of the optimal therapy due to the lack of rapid identification and susceptibility testing. The patient is cooperative and able to provide informed consent. She has no known allergies to antibiotics. The patient is currently hospitalized and receiving care at a facility with a laboratory staffed to perform both rapid testing and routine testing during business hours. She meets the inclusion criteria for the RAPIDS-GN clinical trial and is therefore eligible for enrollment.

56yo male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and recurrent exacerbations. He was recently admitted to the ICU with respiratory distress and diagnosed with pneumonia. He is currently intubated and mechanically ventilated with a PEEP of 8cm and Fi02 of 50%. The patient has a history of smoking and has been unable to quit. He is currently on a variety of medications including bronchodilators, inhaled steroids, and antibiotics. The patient is being considered for enrollment in an exploratory clinical study of Neutrophil Activation Probe (NAP) for Optical Molecular Imaging in Human Lungs. This study aims to test the safety and efficacy of NAP, an imaging agent that detects activated neutrophils and damaging enzymes, in patients with inflammatory lung disease. If the study demonstrates safety and the ability to image activated neutrophils, it may lead to future studies in patients with acute lung injury (ALI).

A 55 year old woman presents to the ophthalmology clinic with decreased vision and distortion in her left eye for the past 6 months. She has a past medical history of hypertension and is on medication for it. The initial ophthalmic examination reveals that the patient has idiopathic polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (IPCV) in her left eye. She has had prior treatment with anti-VEGF monotherapy of ≥8 injections in the previous twelve months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive 3 monthly (Q4W) intravitreal injections of Zimura™ (1 mg/eye) in combination with anti-VEGF therapy (Avastin® 1.25 mg/eye or Lucentis® 0.5 mg/eye or Eylea® 2 mg/eye). The patient understands that the purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of Zimura™ intravitreous injection in combination with anti-VEGF therapy in subjects with IPCV. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no exclusion criteria.

A 57-year-old male presents with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He complains of cramping pain in his left leg with walking that resolves with rest. Physical examination reveals absent left dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses, and a non-healing ulcer on the left ankle. Doppler ultrasound confirms a diagnosis of peripheral artery disease. The patient is Rutherford category 4 and is scheduled for endovascular balloon angioplasty and stenting on the femoro-popliteal segment. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has no history of Buerger's disease, aortoarteritis or any other chronic lower limb ischemia of other etiology. He is not currently undergoing treatment for cancer or diabetes mellitus, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 40-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of obesity with a BMI of 36kg/m2. He reports having occasional fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. He was recently diagnosed with obesity-related glomerulopathy (ORG) after a renal biopsy, with proteinuria levels ranging from 0.5-3.5g/d. His LDL levels are higher than 3.37mmol/L. His eGFR, calculated using the CKD-EPI formula, is 45ml/min. He does not have a history of endocrine disorders or drug-induced obesity, type 2 diabetes, or other renal diseases. He reports no current use of medications or supplements that may interfere with the Sevelamer Carbonate treatment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and able to comply with the study protocol.

As this is an extension study, a patient description is not needed as the trial is only open to patients who have completed the CSTI571B1201 study. Therefore, only those who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria of the previous study are eligible for this extension study.

A 50-year-old male veteran who served in the Army and was deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan is experiencing symptoms of PTSD and alcohol abuse. He has not sought mental health care in the past 3 months and is not currently engaged in any treatment. He is married with two children and has a supportive family who has frequent contact with him. His spouse is enrolled in the Readiness and Resilience in National Guard Soldiers study (RINGS) and has regular access to the internet. The veteran has also participated in the RINGS study and has screened positive for PTSD and/or AUD through their responses to a RINGS survey. The family is eligible to participate in the study and will be randomly assigned to either the VA-CRAFT or control (no treatment) condition. The study aims to provide pilot data on the effectiveness of VA-CRAFT on Veterans' mental health service utilization and family members' well-being, personal quality of life, perceived relationship quality with the Veteran, and communication about treatment seeking.

63F with a history of GERD and occasional dysphagia was referred for gastroscopy by her primary care physician. She reports no significant weight loss, nausea or vomiting, or abdominal pain. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She denies any prior history of upper gastrointestinal tumors. She is currently on lisinopril, atorvastatin, and calcium with vitamin D supplementation. She has no known drug allergies. She consents to intravenous anesthesia for the procedure. She has not had a gastroscopy in the past year and expresses willingness to participate in the study. Her previous gastroscopy did not show any significant findings. She has no history of esophageal or stomach surgery or endoscopic surgery. She is not pregnant and does not take antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs. She is able to cooperate with data collection and signs the informed consent.

A 32-year-old Hispanic woman presents with irregular menstrual cycles, hirsutism, and excess hair growth on her face, chest, and back. She reports difficulty losing weight despite regular exercise and a balanced diet. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. Her BMI is 35.3 kg/m2, and she has a waist circumference of 98 cm

28-year-old non-smoking female with a history of mild dental staining and discoloration. The patient has no known allergies to any dental products or ingredients, and maintains good oral hygiene. She has no fixed orthodontics appliances or untreated caries or periodontitis. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no known systemic illnesses. The patient has not had any previous dental bleaching treatments and has at least one tooth with a VITA shade of A3.5 or darker in the maxillary anterior region. The patient is willing to sign an informed consent form and refrain from tobacco use during the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of acute or chronic medical illness, gastrointestinal disease, or major surgery within the past 4 weeks. He is a non-smoker and has not used nicotine products or Varenicline within the past 3 months. He has not had a blood transfusion or donated blood or plasma within the past 4 weeks. He is sexually active and will use effective birth control throughout the study and for 90 days after the last dose. He does not have a history of cardiac arrhythmias or unexplained syncope. He has normal neurological exam results, which makes him eligible to participate in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of BMS-933043 in healthy subjects. He has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been suffering from degenerative arthritis for the past 5 years. He has been on a variety of medications, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and corticosteroids, but has not experienced significant relief from his symptoms. He has difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to the pain and stiffness in his knees. He is an active person who enjoys playing golf and traveling, but his arthritis has limited his ability to do these things. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he is looking for new treatment options that could help him regain his mobility and quality of life. He is in good overall health and has not had any major medical problems in the past. He does not smoke or drink alcohol and maintains a healthy weight. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He is married and has two adult children. He is retired and spends his time volunteering and pursuing his hobbies. He is excited about the potential benefits of stem cell therapy and is willing to undergo the necessary procedures to participate in this study.

The patient is a 70 year old man who has been diagnosed with a cataract and is scheduled for cataract surgery. He does not have any known allergies or hypersensitivities to bromfenac or salicylates. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Bromfenac ophthalmic solution in cataract surgery.

A 35-year-old female with a history of occasional lower back pain seeks to participate in the clinical trial for Cyclobenzaprine HCl tablets. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her physical exam and laboratory results are unremarkable. She has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. She denies any drug or alcohol dependence and has negative test results for HIV and hepatitis B or C. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

A 45-year-old man was found unconscious in his home by his wife and was immediately taken to the hospital by the Emergency Medical Service (EMS). The patient has a history of hypertension and smoking. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient was found to have a pulseless electrical activity (PEA) cardiac arrest. The EMS initiated advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) protocol, including chest compressions, endotracheal intubation, and epinephrine administration. Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) was achieved after 15 minutes of resuscitation. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) for further management. The post-resuscitation electrocardiogram (ECG) showed no ST segment elevation. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the head and chest revealed no signs of trauma or other non-cardiac causes of the arrest. The patient is now stable and conscious, and there is no apparent neurological deficit. The patient is affiliated with the French Social Security Health Care plan.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with operable pancreatic cancer. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is scheduled to undergo a pancreatectomy and has been identified as a potential candidate for this pilot study investigating the link between meat-borne carcinogens and pancreatic cancer. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the study, including being at least 18 years old, having adequate hepatic function, and providing voluntary written consent for participation. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including having a tumor size less than 3 cm, a CA-19-9 level less than 400, and no ascites. She will receive a single oral dose of radiolabeled MelQx and undergo serial blood draws and urine collections over a 24-hour period. Additionally, normal pancreatic tissue and normal small bowel tissue will be collected from the resected (waste) tissue at the time of her pancreatectomy.

The patient is a 70-year-old male veteran who has been diagnosed with diabetes and hypertension. He has been experiencing difficulty controlling his blood sugar levels, with his most recent HgA1C value greater than or equal to 7.5. His blood pressure is also elevated, with a systolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 140. He has a history of smoking and currently smokes 10 cigarettes per day. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies any illicit drug use. He lives independently and has a supportive family who help him with his medical care. He is able to perform all activities of daily living without assistance. He has no history of dementia or any other cognitive impairment. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his diabetes-related outcomes and is committed to attending the collaborative group clinics and working with his healthcare provider to set and achieve goals for his care.

An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes has been diagnosed with AML. He has already received one induction course of chemotherapy but did not achieve complete remission. He is currently stable with a peripheral blast count of 20,000/microlitre. His performance status is 2 (able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature, e.g., light housework or office work). He has no history of congestive heart failure or any other significant cardiovascular disease. He has not received any other anti-cancer therapy in the last two weeks. He has no history of significant interstitial lung disease or gastrointestinal disorders. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with complaints of severe abdominal pain and nausea. She was diagnosed with acute appendicitis and underwent an emergency appendectomy. She was discharged from the hospital with discharge instructions and medications. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide daily. She is fluent in English and has access to a computer with internet access at home. She is willing to participate in the study and provide feedback on the effectiveness of online videos as a supplement to ED discharge instructions.

The patient is a 28 year old male who sustained a spinal cord injury (SCI) at the T4 level in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago. He is currently using a wheelchair as his primary means of mobility. Since his injury, he has noticed a decline in his psychosocial wellbeing, including decreased social interactions, increased sedentary behavior, and limited participation in activities outside of the home. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he is motivated to improve his overall quality of life. He is in good health and has been cleared by his physician to participate in the study. He owns an iPhone and is able to download and use the research platform. He is able to understand, communicate with, and be understood by research personnel. His injury level is at T4, which allows sufficient arm function for rowing during the exercise intervention. He does not have any acute or chronic medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study. He is excited to try the hybrid functional electrical stimulation row training (FESRT) as he has not previously completed this type of exercise.

54-year-old female diagnosed with uterine papillary serous cancer (UPSC) at surgical stage 3c disease. The patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic and aortic node sampling, omentectomy, and peritoneal cytology. The serous-papillary component of the specimen was found to be 40 percent. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy regimens for UPSC. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has adequate bone marrow, renal, hepatic and neurologic function. She has been informed of the investigational nature of the study and has signed an informed consent form. The patient has no pre-existing neurotoxicity greater than grade 2. She has no uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia or diabetes mellitus. The patient has no history of other malignancy within the last 5 years that could affect the diagnosis or assessment of UPSC. She has no history of serious cardiac disease that is not adequately controlled. The patient has no active serious infection or other serious underlying medical condition that would otherwise impair her ability to receive protocol treatment. She has no serious medical or psychiatric illnesses that would prevent informed consent. The patient has no prior significant allergic reactions to drugs containing cremophor, such as cyclosporine or vitamin K. She has no known hypersensitivity to paclitaxel, carboplatin or Cremophor EL. The patient has not received prior whole pelvis radiotherapy and does not have uncontrolled pelvic inflammatory disease that would contraindicate pelvic radiotherapy. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not receiving other investigational therapy.

A 45-year-old man with a history of acute myeloid leukemia with poor prognosis is being considered for participation in a clinical trial. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past, but the disease has not gone into remission. His treating physician has recommended a haploidentical unmanipulated transplant with post-transplant cyclophosphamide administration. The patient is willing to undergo the transplant and has a donor without exclusion criteria. He is assessed to have a comorbidity Sorror index less than 6 and has an assessable disease by analytic, molecular, or image techniques. The patient is informed about the clinical trial and is willing to give informed consent according to the legal requirements. He does not have any underlying serious medical statement or any important psychiatric disorder that would prevent his participation in the study. He is not currently participating in any other interventional clinical trials and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

50-year-old male with metastatic poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma with an unknown primary site. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy and is able to perform activities of daily living with minimal assistance. The patient has adequate bone marrow, liver functions, and kidney function. The patient has no recent history of cardiovascular disease or meningeal metastases. The patient understands the nature of the study and has given written informed consent.

A 35-year-old man presented to the clinic with complaints of significant mood swings. He reported experiencing episodes of depression, as well as periods of extreme elation, racing thoughts, and decreased need for sleep. He had a history of bipolar disorder and had been previously diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II. He was currently experiencing a depressive episode and had not undergone any treatment for the past month. He had no other mental illness or a history of physical disease. He was able to understand the content of the assessment and was willing to cooperate with the study. His latest lab results were within normal limits, and he had not received modified ECT for at least four weeks before entering the group.

A 42-year old woman, who has been trying to conceive for 2 years, was diagnosed with poor ovarian response. She and her husband have no previous children. She has a history of endometriosis and has undergone two laparoscopic surgeries to remove endometrial tissue. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is otherwise healthy. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has tried several natural remedies to improve her fertility. She is anxious to explore all treatment options to increase her chances of conception. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine which treatment protocol would be most effective for her.

A 35-year-old female presents with a history of asthma for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing occasional wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, especially during exercise. Her past medical history is significant for seasonal allergies and she is currently taking an inhaled corticosteroid (fluticasone propionate) and a long-acting beta-agonist (salmeterol) combination inhaler twice daily. She has not had any exacerbation of her asthma in the past 6 months and her last spirometry test showed a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 80% predicted. She is otherwise healthy with no significant co-morbidities and her BMI is 24. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She will be asked to wear a plain white t-shirt and perform a period of 5 minutes of tidal breathing while sitting in front of the SLP device (Thora-3Di, Pneumacare Ltd) at the Lung Function Department. She will then undergo a bronchodilator challenge test as part of the clinical care, and the SLP measurement will be repeated on completion of the test.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the hospital 10 days ago with a history of sudden onset of right-sided weakness and slurred speech. A CT scan and MRI confirmed the diagnosis of an ischemic stroke affecting the left middle cerebral artery territory. The patient received thrombolytic therapy and was started on antiplatelet medication. He has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and diabetes mellitus. His past surgical history includes a cholecystectomy and a hernia repair. The patient is alert and oriented to time, place, and person. He can follow commands and communicate effectively. On examination, he has right-sided hemiparesis, with a power of 3/5 in the upper limb and 4/5 in the lower limb. He is able to walk with assistance. The National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score is 6, with 2 points in item 5a and 4 points in item 5b. The patient has been referred for rehabilitation, and the treating physician believes that he may benefit from the addition of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to conventional physical therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provides written informed consent.

A 55-year-old male patient came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has a family history of colorectal cancer as his father was diagnosed with the disease at the age of 65. He has no personal history of advanced adenomas or colorectal cancer. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and sits in front of a computer for long hours. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. He has no known allergies and is not on any medications. He has health insurance coverage.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who suffered a left ischemic stroke 10 weeks ago. He is currently undergoing outpatient physical therapy twice a week. He has no history of neurological or psychological disorders other than the stroke. He has been diagnosed with high blood pressure but it is currently under control with medication. He has no history of epilepsy, migraine headache, or pacemaker. He is not pregnant and has no metal implants in his head or body. He has not received any Botulinum toxin injections in the past 3 months. He is able to follow instructions and has a Mini Mental State Examination score of 28. He has moderate impairment in his left upper limb function with an UE-FMA score of 35. He is interested in participating in this study to further improve his rehabilitation progress.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital due to a gunshot wound that occurred during a gang-related dispute in his community. He has a history of involvement in local gang activity and has been previously arrested for drug possession. He is currently unemployed and lives with his girlfriend. He speaks fluent English and has completed high school. He has no history of mental retardation or active psychosis. He is willing to participate in the study to help reduce his risk of future violent injury.

55 yo male with a history of IgM monoclonal gammopathy and worsening polyneuropathy with an INCAT score of 5, referred for evaluation of potential treatment options. The patient reports significant numbness and tingling in both feet and hands, making it difficult to walk and perform daily tasks. Physical examination reveals decreased sensation in both lower extremities and distal upper extremities. Laboratory tests show anti-MAG antibody titers > 1.1000 BTU (ELISA). The patient has no other concurrent causes of polyneuropathy, and has not received any previous treatment with rituximab or concurrent immunosuppressive therapies. The patient is interested in participating in the RIMAG study and willing to provide informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old male diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and homozygous for the F508del-CFTR mutation. He has a weight of 65 kg and a FEV1 of 60% of predicted normal for his age, gender, and height. He has a history of chronic therapies for CF lung disease, including hypertonic saline and azithromycin, which have been stable for the past 6 months. He has no history of ventricular tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, or prolonged QT and/or QTcF interval. He has not undergone solid organ or hematological transplantation. He has no history of alcohol abuse or drug addiction in the past year. He does not use continuous or nocturnal supplemental oxygen. He is willing to participate in a Phase 1 clinical trial to assess the pharmacokinetics and absorption dynamics of N91115 and to identify an initial starting dose for Phase 2 trials.

A 42-year-old female patient presented with chronic non-specific low back pain that started 6 months ago. She describes her pain as a dull ache that is present most of the day, and it increases with prolonged sitting and standing. She rates her pain as a 5 on a visual analogue scale (VAS) from 0 to 10. She works as an accountant and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She has never had back surgery or a serious injury to her back. She has tried different medications and physical therapy, but none have provided significant relief. She has a normal body mass index (BMI) and is generally healthy. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no history of cancer, infections, or other serious medical conditions. She is interested in participating in this study to see if pilates exercises can help alleviate her chronic low back pain.

Patient is a 46-year-old woman from the United States who recently noticed a small lump in her breast during a self-examination. She has no previous history of breast cancer in her family and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 24. She underwent a mammogram and ultrasound exam, which revealed a small 1.5 cm tumor in her left breast. Biopsy confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma, positive for estrogen and progesterone receptors, and negative for HER2 expression. MRI showed no other suspicious lesions in the breast or axilla. The patient's bra cup size is C. She is interested in participating in a minimally invasive treatment option and is willing to undergo HIFU treatment followed by a partial mastectomy if necessary.

52F with a history of breast cancer s/p chemotherapy and radiation therapy presented with recurrent, metastatic disease to the liver, lung, and bone. The patient has undergone multiple lines of treatment, including hormonal therapy and chemotherapy, with limited response. On recent imaging, there is evidence of disease progression with new lesions noted in the liver and lung. The patient is experiencing significant fatigue, decreased appetite, and weight loss. She underwent further evaluation with a tissue biopsy, which confirmed metastatic breast cancer. She meets the eligibility criteria for the BDB001-102 clinical trial, and the study team has recommended this trial as a potential treatment option. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the treatment, laboratory monitoring, and required clinic visits. She has an ECOG score of 1, with a minimum life expectancy of 3 months. The patient's laboratory values are within the acceptable range for the study, and she has no significant history of heart, liver, or kidney disease. She has no active infections and is negative for HIV and hepatitis A, B, and C. The patient has no history of psychiatric or substance abuse disorder that would interfere with her ability to cooperate with the requirements of the study. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she has agreed to use contraception during the treatment period and for at least 120 days after the last dose of study treatment. She has no known active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past two years, and she has no history of interstitial lung disease.

A 29 year old woman who works as a teacher came to the clinic with complaints of persistent worrying and rumination regarding her work and personal life. She reported experiencing anxiety attacks and difficulty sleeping due to excessive worrying. She scored above the 75th and 66.7th percentile on the Ruminative Response Scale and the Penn State Worry Questionnaire respectively. She has no history of depression or generalized anxiety disorder but has a family history of anxiety. She is interested in participating in the study to learn coping strategies and prevent the onset of depression and anxiety.

A 55-year-old male with a history of advanced, relapsed prostate cancer that is considered unresponsive to traditional treatments. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1 and has normal neurologic examination findings. He has fully recovered from any prior surgical procedures and reversible side effects of prior therapy for cancer including radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. The patient's medical and psychiatric history, as well as serum chemistry and hematology tests, indicate that he is in appropriate health for the study. He is willing and able to comply with study restrictions and to return to the clinic for evaluations. He is also using medically accepted methods of contraception as he is a man capable of producing offspring. However, the patient has a serum creatinine value of 1.7 mg/dL, which exceeds the maximum value allowed for participation in the study. Therefore, he is not eligible to participate.

55-year-old postmenopausal woman with a BMI of 25 kg/m², a non-smoker for the past 6 months, and no history of severe disease or malignant tumor. The patient has not used any systemic or topically active medication, herbal remedies, prescription or non-prescription drugs from screening to the first drug administration, except for occasional use of paracetamol or ibuprofen. She has no history of orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. The patient has no known allergies, hypersensitivity or non-allergic drug reactions. She does not consume alcohol regularly and her urine screen is negative for any drug or cotinine. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of BAY1161116.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who regularly donates blood to help others. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He has no history of any major medical or psychiatric illnesses. He does not take any medications other than occasional over-the-counter painkillers for headaches. He reports feeling tired and weak lately and sometimes has difficulty concentrating at work. He has not had any recent illness or fever, and his physical examination is unremarkable. His blood pressure is within normal limits, and his hemoglobin level is 13.5 g/dL. However, his serum ferritin level is found to be below 50 microg/l, indicating low iron stores. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the effects of intravenous iron replacement on general well-being and fatigue in iron-depleted blood donors.

A 62-year-old retired male, who has a history of smoking 10 pack-years, presented with a persistent cough and progressive dyspnea on exertion for the last 6 months. He has also lost approximately 7 kg of weight during this time. He has no history of significant occupational exposure to dust, fumes or chemicals. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. He is a widower and lives alone in a small apartment in a moderately polluted area near an industrial zone. He has completed high school and worked as a manual laborer before retiring. On examination, he has a BMI of 28, moderate respiratory distress and fine inspiratory crackles on auscultation. Pulmonary function tests showed a restrictive pattern with a decrease in diffusing capacity. A high-resolution CT of the chest showed bilateral, sub-pleural, basal predominant reticular opacities with traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing. The patient was diagnosed with probable Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis based on "ATS / ERS / JRS / ALAT" 2018 criteria by a multi-disciplinary discussion. He has been referred to the clinical trial to understand the influence of socio-economic and environmental factors on the natural history of IPF.

A 62 year old woman has been experiencing severe pain in her left hip for the past few years. She reports difficulty in walking and performing daily activities. She has a medical history of hypertension and osteoporosis. Her medications include lisinopril for blood pressure regulation and calcium supplements for osteoporosis. She is a non-smoker and denies any history of alcohol abuse. The patient has been referred to University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust for an elective primary unilateral total hip replacement (THR). She has been informed about the clinical trial evaluating the use of an acetabular alignment guide combined with three-dimensional CT-based planning in THR and has agreed to participate in the study. The patient is able and willing to comply with all study requirements and has provided written informed consent. She does not have any significant orthopaedic deformities and is deemed suitable for an uncemented primary acetabular implant. She is able to undergo planning imaging and has not participated in any other clinical trial of an investigational medicinal product in the last 90 days.

Maria is a 16-year-old girl who just gave birth to her first child, a healthy baby boy weighing 3.2 kg, in a hospital in Porto Alegre, Brazil. Maria lives with her parents and her boyfriend, who is the father of the baby. Her mother, Ana, is supportive of her decision to breastfeed the baby but has limited knowledge about the benefits of exclusive breastfeeding. Ana is willing to participate in counseling sessions with Maria to learn more about breastfeeding and how to support her daughter in this process. Maria's boyfriend is also supportive of her decision to breastfeed and wants to learn how he can help during breastfeeding and complementary feeding. Maria has no history of breast or nipple complications, and she does not have any medical conditions that could impact her ability to breastfeed. She is willing to participate in the study's counseling sessions both in the maternity ward and at home. Maria and her family have access to transportation to attend all the scheduled appointments.

We are looking for healthy male subjects between the ages of 18 and 45 years old, with a body weight of at least 50 kg and a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 28 kg/m2. They should not have a history of alcohol abuse or allergies to the study drugs or multiple drugs and food allergies. They should not have donated or lost blood over 450 mL within 3 months prior to screening and must have a 12-lead ECG without clinically significant abnormalities. Any subjects with known history of allergy to study drugs, positive for viral hepatitis (including hepatitis B and C), HIV and syphilis, or deemed unsuitable by the investigator for any other reason are excluded. The subjects must sign the informed consent form and fully understand the contents of the trial, the process, and possible adverse reactions. They must be able to complete the study according to the trial protocol and have no pregnancy plan within 3 months after the last dose of study drug and voluntarily take effective contraceptive measures.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking for 8 years and was diagnosed with asthma 2 years ago. She experiences shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness, especially after physical exertion or exposure to smoke. She uses a rescue inhaler up to 2 times a day. She has tried using inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in the past, but they did not seem to help her symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her spirometry test shows an FEV1 of 80%. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old man who was recently diagnosed with prediabetes (A1c of 6.2%). He is overweight with a BMI of 28 and has been struggling to lose weight despite regular exercise and a balanced diet. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. His fasting glucose is 6.1 mmol/L and lipid profile is within normal range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his insulin sensitivity and prevent the development of type 2 diabetes. He is willing to follow the study protocol and consume either green banana flour or placebo for four weeks.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy diagnosed with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (hoFH). He has been taking the optimal dose of statin and other lipid modifying therapies (LMTs) for the past four weeks. He is a high school student and lives with his parents. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his time playing video games. He has a BMI of 28 and a blood pressure of 116/76 mmHg. His medical history is unremarkable, and he does not have any chronic diseases such as diabetes or thyroid disorders. He is interested in sports, but due to his high cholesterol levels, he has not been able to participate in physical activities. His parents are concerned about his health and are looking for alternative treatment options. They are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have signed the informed consent form.

A 37-year-old Hispanic woman presented at the Clinic with decreased vision in her left eye. She reported a history of ocular histoplasmosis in her left eye, which was diagnosed one year ago. The patient had received no previous treatment for the disease. The physical examination showed a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/60 in the left eye. The fundus examination revealed the presence of a subfoveal choroidal neovascular lesion. The lesion was less than 5400 microns in diameter. The patient had no other ocular conditions that could require medical or surgical intervention. The patient provided written informed consent and agreed to comply with study assessments for the full duration of the study. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraception.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic diarrhea and abdominal pain for the past 6 months. She has lost 15 pounds unintentionally and has noticed that her stools have become watery and more frequent. She has tried over-the-counter anti-diarrheal medication with no relief. She has a family history of inflammatory bowel disease. Her physical examination is significant for abdominal tenderness and normal bowel sounds. Laboratory tests reveal normal electrolytes, liver enzymes, and thyroid function. Stool studies are negative for infectious causes of diarrhea. A colonoscopy with biopsies shows the presence of microscopic colitis. She has not received any treatment for this condition before. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 30-year-old man presents with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and easy bruising for the past month. He also reports experiencing night sweats and weight loss of approximately 10 pounds over the same period. Physical examination reveals pallor, mild hepatomegaly, and palpable lymph nodes in the neck and groin.
