Blood tests show a leukocyte count of 50,000/μL with 80% blasts, and a bone marrow biopsy reveals BCR-ABL-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He is married and has two children. He works as a software developer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a good social support system and is highly motivated to participate in the clinical trial.

A 42-year-old female patient was diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection, which confirmed the diagnosis of invasive breast cancer. The tumor was estrogen receptor-negative, progesterone receptor-negative, and HER2-negative. The pathology report showed no lymphovascular invasion and clear surgical margins. The patient has no significant medical history, including no history of cardiovascular disease. The patient is postmenopausal and has no family history of breast cancer. The patient has completed adjuvant chemotherapy and is now eligible to participate in the BEATRICE study to compare the efficacy of adjuvant chemotherapy alone versus adjuvant chemotherapy with 1 year of bevacizumab in preventing invasive disease-free survival.

A 29-year-old woman from Ghana presented to the obstetrics clinic for her first prenatal visit. She reported that she had been feeling well during her pregnancy and had not experienced any complications. She had a history of schistosomiasis infection during her childhood, which was treated with praziquantel. She immigrated to the United States from Ghana two years ago and was unaware of any current schistosomiasis infection. Her medical history was significant for hypothyroidism, which was controlled with levothyroxine. She denied any allergies or other medical conditions. She reported that she had been taking prenatal vitamins since she found out she was pregnant. Her vital signs were within normal limits, and her physical exam was unremarkable. Laboratory tests revealed a positive serology for schistosomiasis. The patient was informed about the study and agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She signed the informed consent form and was scheduled for follow-up visits for the duration of her pregnancy.

The patient is a 52-year-old Hispanic male who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite for the past few months. He is married and has three children. He works as a construction worker and has been with the same company for over 10 years. He enjoys playing soccer with his children and spending time with his family. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He is scheduled for a surgical procedure to remove the tumor in the liver in the next few weeks. He is interested in participating in the Personal Resilience Empowerment Program Study to learn how to manage his health and well-being during this challenging time.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 2 years ago. He has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms, including frequent diarrhea with blood and mucus, abdominal pain, and cramping. He has had an inadequate response to basic treatments and has failed to tolerate biological agents. He has no history of allergies or other medical conditions, and he is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His laboratory tests show a C-reactive protein level of 25 mg/L and fecal calprotectin level of 800 mg/kg. His clinical severity of ulcerative colitis is classified as severe based on the Mayo score. He has not previously received Xeljanz. He has not had any significant infections or other serious medical conditions. He is not pregnant and does not have any hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose galactose malabsorption. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

This is a 6-year-old girl named Lily who attends a local elementary school. Her parents have expressed concern about her hand hygiene habits, especially in light of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. They are interested in enrolling her in a clinical trial that aims to improve handwashing practices in young children. Lily is generally healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to learn new techniques for keeping her hands clean and germ-free.

38-year-old male with hereditary angioedema (HAE) with recurrent episodes of swelling in the face, hands, and feet. He has previously been treated with C1 esterase inhibitor (C1-INH) concentrate, but he still experiences frequent attacks. He has been prescribed lanadelumab as a prophylactic treatment to prevent future HAE episodes. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of lanadelumab in patients with HAE, and will have their biological samples analyzed at the Laboratory of Immunology of CHUGA. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a recent diagnosis of high blood pressure, with systolic blood pressure readings consistently above 130 mmHg. He owns an iPhone and expresses a desire to increase his physical activity. He is able to walk for 10 minutes without pain and is fluent in English. He is not currently taking any hypertension medication and has no known diagnosis where physical activity would be contraindicated. He has not had any recent acute cardiovascular events and does not have any major psychiatric illnesses.

51F who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. She has completed curative therapy (surgery and radiation) within the past 120 days and is currently NED based on clinical and radiographic evaluations. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her vital signs are within normal limits. Her blood work at the Screening Visit shows a white count of 4.8x109/L and hemoglobin of 12.5 g/dL. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol. She has no known allergies to Candin® or yeast, and no history of severe asthma requiring emergency room visits or hospitalization within the past 5 years. She has not received the PepCan vaccine before and has no history of recurrence of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The patient is not pregnant or attempting to become pregnant and is not breastfeeding.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of obesity and high blood pressure. She has been experiencing fatigue and mild abdominal discomfort for the past few months. She does not consume alcohol nor does she smoke. Her past medical history is only significant for hypothyroidism, which is well controlled with medication. She has not had any surgery or hospitalization in the past year. She does not take any medication for her liver condition. Her blood tests show elevated levels of ALT, AST, and ferritin. Imaging exams confirm the diagnosis of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of silymarin in improving her liver function. She does not have any other chronic illnesses and is willing to participate in all stages of the research.

A 65-year-old retired male who has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He has never had herpes zoster or received any vaccine for varicella or zoster. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is not taking any immunosuppressive therapy and has never been diagnosed with immune dysfunction. He has not received any other vaccination recently. He does not have any fever or other acute illness on the day of vaccination. He is interested in participating in this study and is willing to use acceptable methods of birth control if applicable.

This is a 54 year old male who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) after experiencing symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, and swollen lymph nodes. The patient has an Eastern Collaborative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1 and an International prognostic index (IPI) score of 2. The patient has been receiving the standard R-CHOP Protocol (Rituximab + Vindesine + Cyclophosphamide + Epirubicin + Prednisone) treatment for DLBCL. The patient has more than 1 measurable nidus (common CT or MRI scanning diameter ≥ 20 mm, and spiral CT scanning diameter ≥ 10 mm) and has normal blood routine, hepatorenal function, and cardiac function. White blood cell count (WBC) is 5.0×109/L, neutrophil count is 2.0×109/L; platelet (PLT) count is 125×109/L; hemoglobin (HGB) is 100g/L; serum bilirubin (Bil) is 1.2 folds of the upper limit of normal value, alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are ≤2 folds of the upper limit of normal value, and serum creatinine (Scr) is 1.0mg/dl. The patient has an expected survival time of more than 3 months and is well informed of the study and has signed the informed consent forms. The patient has not received administration of Rituximab. The patient does not have DLBCL affected by primary breast gland, lung, testis, bone, peri-orbit, peri-spine, central nerve system, and bone marrow. The patient is not complicated with other non-DLBCL primary malignant tumors, and does not have poor compliance with their families. The patient does not have uncontrolled metastatic nidi of central nerve system, dysfunction of important organs and severe cardiac diseases like congestive heart failure, uncontrollable arrhythmia, angina pectoris that needed long-term drug administration, valvular heart diseases, myocardial infarction, and refractory hypertension, pregnancy or lactation, chronic infectious wounds, and history of uncontrollable psychological diseases. The patient has not had previous treatment with Cinobufacini Tablets.

The patient is a 35-year-old African American woman who has no chronic medical condition and does not use tobacco or any anti-platelet drugs. She is interested in participating in the study to help contribute to scientific research. She has no history of bleeding disorders or any other medical complications. She leads an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. The patient has no known family history of any blood disorders or coagulation issues. She is willing to undergo the platelet aggregation test and follow the study protocol. The patient is well-informed about the study and has consented to participate.

A 68-year-old retired Caucasian male with sensorineural hearing loss is seeking a new hearing aid device that can help him communicate better with his family and friends. He reports difficulty hearing in noisy environments and struggles to follow conversations on the phone. He has been using a hearing aid device for the past 5 years, but he is not satisfied with its performance. He is currently not taking any medications and has no significant medical history. He has mild arthritis in his hands, but it does not affect his daily activities. He is a retired engineer and enjoys reading, watching TV, and spending time with his grandchildren. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate a new open-source speech processing platform, as he believes it could improve his quality of life. His hearing loss has been confirmed by an audiogram, and he is not cognitively challenged or legally blind.

A 32-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her second trimester came to the clinic for a routine prenatal check-up. She has a history of one previous preterm birth at 34 weeks gestation. During her first pregnancy, she was diagnosed with cervical insufficiency and was given a cervical cerclage to prevent preterm birth. She is concerned about the possibility of preterm birth in her current pregnancy and is looking for any additional monitoring that can be done to help prevent it. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her current pregnancy is uncomplicated, and she has been receiving regular prenatal care.

A 25 year old woman who is self-conscious about her cellulite on both thighs is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce its appearance. She has tried various cellulite creams and home remedies in the past, but has not noticed any significant improvement. She is currently not taking any medication and has no known allergies to any of the ingredients in the study product. She is willing to apply the cream as directed for 16 weeks and maintain her habitual diet and lifestyle throughout the trial period. She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or lactating. She is committed to using a medically approved form of contraception throughout the study period. She understands the study procedures and has provided informed consent to participate.

54 y/o male with a history of stable angina, presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a family history of heart disease. The patient is currently on aspirin, atenolol, and simvastatin. Physical exam reveals a blood pressure of 140/80 mmHg, heart rate of 85 bpm, and normal lung sounds. An ECG shows changes consistent with myocardial ischemia. The patient is scheduled for an invasive coronary angiogram as part of their clinical management. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient does not have a history of PCI or CABG, complicated complex congenital heart disease, artificial pacemaker or internal defibrillator leads implanted, implanted artificial heart valve, severe arrhythmia, impaired chronic renal function, or allergy to iodine. The patient's body mass index is 28 kg/m2 and left ventricle thickness is within normal limits. The patient is not experiencing any unstable hemodynamics or life-threatening diseases.

45 year-old man with a history of glioblastoma multiforme diagnosed 2 years ago, treated with surgery, radiation therapy, and temozolomide chemotherapy. He experienced a recurrence of his tumor six months ago and has been treated with bevacizumab. His most recent MRI showed disease progression. The patient is currently on a stable dose of dexamethasone 4 mg per day. He has a KPS of 80% and no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has not received prior treatment with rindopepimut or bevacizumab.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy woman with a BMI of 23. She has no history of any medical disorders and is not taking any prescription medications or non-prescription drugs. She occasionally takes routine vitamins but has not taken paracetamol in the last 24 hours. She does not smoke or abuse alcohol or drugs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using highly effective contraceptive methods. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the blood concentration levels of Semaglutide using two different injection tools. She is willing to attend all scheduled site visits and stay at the research unit for 4 days and 3 nights if required.

A 45-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a history of chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. The pain was described as a dull, aching sensation in the lower back that radiated to the legs, making it difficult to walk for long periods of time. The patient rated her pain intensity as 7 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale. She had no history of nerve root compromise, serious spinal pathology, or back surgeries. The patient is fluent in Portuguese and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for alternative treatments. She has no serious cardiovascular or metabolic diseases and is not pregnant. The patient is seeking relief from her chronic low back pain and is willing to participate in a randomized, triple-blinded, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of photobiomodulation therapy.

50 y/o male diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) with hemoglobin concentration and platelet count below the institution's lower limit of normal. The patient has not received any cancer chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past. No apparent infections, serious complications (heart, liver, or kidney disease), serious bleeding tendency or serious CNS symptoms are present. The patient is not suffering from fever (excluding tumor fever), interstitial pneumonia or pulmonary fibrosis. No active multiple cancers are present and the patient is not receiving any other investigational products within 6 months before registration in this study. The patient has no prior allergies to medications that are similar to the investigational product (purine nucleoside derivatives). The patient is not pregnant, of childbearing potential or lactating.

A 40-year-old woman has been diagnosed with metastatic melanoma and has failed standard therapy, including high-dose aldesleukin therapy. She is HLA-A*0201-positive and has measurable disease. Her performance status is ECOG 0-1, and she has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. Her hematopoietic profile is in normal ranges, with an absolute neutrophil count >1,000/mm^3, platelet count >100,000/mm^3, hemoglobin >8.0 g/dL, lymphocyte count >500/mm^3, and WBC >3,000/mm^3. She has no coagulation disorder, ALT and AST levels are <3 times the upper limit of normal, and bilirubin levels are ≤2.0 mg/dL. She is negative for hepatitis B antigen and hepatitis C antibody (unless antigen-negative). Her creatinine levels are ≤1.6 mg/dL. She has no major cardiovascular or respiratory illness and has an LVEF ≥45% by stress cardiac test. She is HIV-negative, has no major immune system illness, and no active systemic infection or opportunistic infection. She has no primary or secondary immunodeficiency and has no history of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to study drugs. She is not pregnant or nursing, and a negative pregnancy test has been confirmed. She is fertile and agrees to use effective contraception during and for 4 months after completion of study treatment. She has signed a durable power of attorney.

A 6-year old girl presented to the dental clinic with her mother for a routine check-up. She is in good general health and has no known medical conditions. Her mother reports that she brushes her teeth twice a day and flosses regularly. The child has a deep cavity in her left lower molar tooth, but she is asymptomatic and doesn't complain of any pain or sensitivity. Clinical examination revealed a vital pulp with carious exposure. There is no evidence of pulp degeneration, excessive bleeding from the root canal, internal root resorption, inter-radicular and/or periapical bone destruction, swelling, or sinus tract. The child is cooperative and able to follow instructions. The dentist recommends a pulpotomy procedure and stainless steel crown restoration. The mother agrees to have her daughter participate in the clinical trial comparing MedCem MTA and Formocresol as pulp medicaments.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 6 years ago. She presents to the clinic with a history of poor glucose control despite oral hypoglycemic agents and is currently on a stable dose of metformin. Her HbA1c is 8.5%. She also has a history of hypertension and is taking amlodipine for blood pressure control. She does not have any other significant medical history or allergies to contrast agents. She has a BMI of 30 and is a non-smoker. She has not had any previous renal artery intervention or myocardial infarction. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and maintain a stable dose of medication for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing excessive worry and anxiety for the past 6 months. She reports feeling restless, fatigued, and having difficulty concentrating. She has a history of anxiety and depression for which she previously received treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) but did not respond well. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She reports that her symptoms have been interfering with her daily life and causing her distress. She scores a Hamilton Anxiety Scale total score of 23 at screening and baseline, with a score of 3 on both Item 1 (anxious mood) and Item 2 (tension). She scores a Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale total score of 12 indicating a mild level of depression. She meets the criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 4th Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR®). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new treatment for her anxiety symptoms.

The patient is a 68 year-old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has undergone treatment by surgery and/or ablative radiation therapy at least 2 months prior to entry. His clinical stage D0 disease has been confirmed with serum PSA values > 2 ng/ml by two measurements at least two weeks apart. He has no prior history of a second malignancy and has a Karnofsky performance score of > 70. He has not received any immunosuppressive therapy, chemotherapy, chronic treatment dose corticosteroids (greater than the equivalent of 10 mg prednisone per day), or radiation therapy to >30% of the bone marrow within 6 months of the first vaccination. He is not on concurrent androgen ablative (hormonal) therapy, or has completed this therapy at least one month prior to study entry. He has not demonstrated PSA progression during any prior hormonal therapy or chemotherapy. He has no known evidence of bone metastases or non-regional lymph node involvement (stage D2 disease) as determined by bone scan or CT scan. He has not been treated previously with another investigational anti-tumor vaccine.

A 45-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) was referred to the clinic for evaluation. He reports experiencing episodes of chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue during physical activity. The physical examination revealed a maximum left ventricular wall thickness of 18 mm, with no evidence of resting left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. He was on optimal standard medical therapy according to international guidelines, including beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers. The patient is willing to participate in the study and can comply with the required visits and medication regimen. He has no history of chronic obstructive airways disease, asthma, or diabetes. His body mass index is within the acceptable range for the study. The patient has not taken potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, and his QTc interval is within normal limits. He has no significant renal or hepatic impairment. A urine pregnancy test was negative, and he is using highly effective contraceptive precautions. The patient has not participated in any clinical studies within the last two months. The patient is currently taking simvastatin 20 mg daily, which is allowed in the study.

32yo female nurse with a Bachelor's degree in Nursing. She has a family history of obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. She is currently not diagnosed with any cardiovascular, metabolic, or neoplastic diseases. She has a sedentary lifestyle due to the nature of her job, but she tries to exercise at least 30 minutes a day after work. She has been trying to follow a Mediterranean diet for the past year, but she admits to occasional lapses due to work stress. Her current anthropometric measurements are within normal limits, and her lipid profile and blood pressure are also within normal ranges. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about her adherence to the Mediterranean diet and its impact on her health.

A 35-year-old man who works in the healthcare industry is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is in good health and has no history of chronic medical conditions. He has not experienced any diarrheal episodes or abdominal pain in the past 6 months. He has not taken any antibiotics or anti-diarrheal medicines in the past week. He is not currently pregnant. He is available in the study area for the duration of the trial. He is interested in participating in the study to help contribute to the development of a vaccine that can help prevent cholera and improve public health.

An 83 year old man who resides in a long-term care facility "de Wingerd". He has been diagnosed with major neurocognitive disorder by a specialist doctor. He is able to stand straight for at least 10 minutes without aid and has corrected visual acuity sufficient to work on a TV screen. He does not have mobility impairments that would inhibit exergame training. He does not have any severe acute or uncontrolled health problems, orthopedic or neurological diseases that would prohibit exergame training. He is interested in participating in this study to help improve his cognitive and physical abilities.

A 32-year-old Hispanic woman with a pre-pregnancy BMI of 31.2 presented for her first prenatal visit at 12 weeks gestation. She has a family history of diabetes, with her father and two siblings diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She has no personal history of diabetes or gestational diabetes. She works as a nurse and spends most of her day on her feet. She reports no complications or comorbidities associated with her pregnancy. She is interested in participating in the Monitored Home Exercise in Pregnancy study to reduce her risk of developing gestational diabetes. She is comfortable with utilizing technology-based interventions and is willing to commit to the prescribed exercise program. She speaks fluent English and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 30.5 presents with a recent diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking metformin and has been on a stable dose for the past three months. He reports experiencing frequent thirst and urination, fatigue, and blurred vision over the past few weeks. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or stroke. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly, but his diet is not strictly controlled. He has no known allergies to medications. His HbA1c level is 8.7%. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a novel compound proposed for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss of 12 pounds within the last 6 months presented to the hematology/oncology clinic. Physical examination revealed bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and a spleen palpable 4 cm below the costal margin. The patient had no significant past medical history, except for hypertension which was well controlled with medications. Blood tests showed a white cell count of 45,000/mL, hemoglobin level of 10 g/dL, and platelet count of 120,000/mL. Flow cytometry of peripheral blood showed mature B-cell lymphocytosis with the expression of CD19, CD5, CD23, CD20, and surface immunoglobulin kappa light chain restriction. The patient was diagnosed with Binet stage B CLL and met the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial, which includes treatment with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide alone or in combination with rituximab. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, a CIRS score of 8, and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He has no history of autoimmune cytopenia, Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia, or other active malignancy. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 35-year-old male patient with HIV was referred to the clinic by his primary care physician for evaluation of metabolic syndrome. He has been diagnosed with HIV for the past 5 years and is currently on antiretroviral therapy. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. His BMI is 31 kg/m², and he has a waist circumference of 105 cm. He has a family history of heart disease and hypertension. His blood pressure is 138/92 mmHg, and he has dyslipidemia with a total cholesterol of 240 mg/dL, LDL of 160 mg/dL, HDL of 35 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 180 mg/dL. His fasting glucose is 115 mg/dL. He has no history of liver or renal disease. He is motivated to modify his lifestyle and make changes to improve his health. He is married and has one child. He is fluent in English and has no known allergies.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has not undergone any treatment for her cancer yet and is eager to participate in a clinical trial that could help identify the underlying molecular causes of her disease. She is willing to undergo a biopsy procedure to provide tissue and blood samples for research purposes. She has no history of pregnancy and is not currently pregnant. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures and requirements.

A 35-year-old female office worker with a BMI of 32 kg/m² is interested in participating in a weight loss program. She has tried various diets and exercise routines in the past but has been unable to achieve significant weight loss. She has no significant medical history, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally. She reports no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no history of bariatric surgery or other significant surgeries. She has no history of clinically significant disease or condition. She reports no history of eating disorders, night eating syndrome or sleep eating. She reports no history of consuming more than 32 ounces of sugar-sweetened beverages per day. She reports eating in 3 meals and 2 snacks per day. She reports no history of extremely slow eating or grazing eating pattern. She reports brushing her teeth twice a day and has had a dental check-up within the last 6 months. She reports no functional problems when swallowing solids or liquids. She does not wear braces or any fixed orthodontic appliances. She lives within 20 miles of the clinic and has reliable transportation. She is willing to sign a behavioral contract to use the SMART device during all meals and eating episodes, attend all study visits, and properly care for the device. She is willing to use adequate contraception throughout participation in the study.

A 56 yo F with comorbidities including chronic lung disease, diabetes, and severe obesity (BMI ≥40), who has tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection through a PCR test. She has a peripheral capillary oxygen saturation (SpO2) of ≤94% on room air at screening and is at high risk for ARDS. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and agrees to use acceptable methods of contraception. She has no known hypersensitivity or allergy to colchicine and has not participated in any other clinical trial of an experimental treatment for COVID-19. She is not currently requiring mechanical ventilation and has no evidence of liver disease, renal impairment, or hepatic impairment. She is willing to refrain from prolonged exposure to the sun or agree to use at least SPF 50 on all exposed skin and protective clothing during prolonged sun exposure throughout participation in this study and/or treatment with VERU-111.

A 45 year old male patient with a history of hypertension is scheduled for elective total aortic arch repair under moderate hypothermic circulatory arrest with selective antegrade cerebral perfusion. The patient has no history of diabetes or stroke and is not on any medications that may interfere with the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient is expected to have a left jugular venous bulb cannula successfully placed.

A 54-year-old male patient came to the cancer center with a diagnosis of resectable colon cancer without distant metastases. He had no significant medical history and was generally in good health. The patient was eager to participate in the clinical trial for TVB 2640 for resectable colon cancer and other resectable cancers. The patient was able to provide written informed consent and met the eligibility criteria for the study. He had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, adequate bone marrow function, and no significant ischemic heart disease or myocardial infarction within 6 months before the first dose of the study drug. The patient had a negative urine pregnancy test, and he agreed to use two methods of birth control during the course of the study. The patient was willing to comply with all study requirements and was randomized to receive either TVB-2640 or placebo in a 2:1 fashion. The patient will receive the study drug for 10-21 days, and the last dose of the study drug will be on the day before the surgical resection. The patient will be evaluated and graded for adverse events according to the NCI Common Terminology for Adverse Events (CTCAE), version 4.03. The patient will be followed for 4 weeks after the last dose of the study drug to monitor for any drug-related adverse events.

A 26-year-old healthy female with a body mass index of 22 kg/m2 came to the clinic as a volunteer for a clinical trial. She has no history of diabetes mellitus, gastric diseases, gastro-intestinal surgery, smoking or use of gastric mobility medicines. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is interested in contributing to research studies and has a flexible schedule to participate in the study. She is willing to follow the protocol and procedures of the study and is looking forward to learning more about the effect of chewing lollipop on gastric volume and gastric emptying.

The patient is a 15-year-old Latino male who has been admitted to the psychiatric unit due to suicidal ideation and a previous suicide attempt. He lives with his mother and two younger siblings in a low-income neighborhood in Rhode Island. He reports feeling overwhelmed by schoolwork, family problems, and social pressures from peers. He has a history of depression and anxiety and has been seeing a therapist for the past year. The patient is fluent in English and Spanish and identifies strongly with his Latino heritage. His mother is supportive of his treatment and is willing to participate in therapy sessions. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is open to trying the new treatment option (SCBT) to help prevent future suicidal crises.

A 45 year old male has been experiencing muscle weakness and stiffness, as well as difficulty with fine motor movements for the past 6 months. He has no prior history of neurological disorders and is otherwise healthy. He has not experienced any respiratory or swallowing difficulties, and is able to walk with assistance. His forced vital capacity is within normal range (70% predicted). He has not received any treatment for his symptoms. His cognitive function is intact with a score of 27 on the Mini-Mental State Exam. He has no history of orthostatic hypotension or abnormal lab values. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential treatment options for his condition.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with a sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The patient's past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was evaluated with a CT scan of the head, which ruled out hemorrhagic stroke. He met the diagnostic criteria for acute ischemic stroke and was treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. The patient's baseline laboratory tests showed a normal complete blood count and coagulation profile. He has no history of bleeding disorders or anticoagulant therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the research.

6-month-old infant with a history of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection presents to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit with severe bronchiolitis. The patient is on non-invasive positive pressure ventilation support and has been receiving conventional treatment for 2 days with minimal improvement. The patient's parents have given consent for the child to participate in a prospective randomized study on the use of Intrapulmonary Percussive Ventilation for children with bronchiolitis on non-invasive ventilation support. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of adding physiotherapy using Intrapulmonary Percussive Ventilation to conventional treatment. The infant meets all inclusion criteria for the study and is enrolled in the trial.

This is a 32-year-old HIV-positive male who has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the past 2 years. He has been able to maintain viral suppression below 30,000 copies/mL of blood and his CD4 T cell count is greater than 400 cells/cmm. He has not received any immunomodulatory agents such as IL-2 or interferon in the past 5 years, and has no history of liver disease, drug or alcohol abuse, or malignancy. He is willing and able to comply with the study guidelines and travel to the NIH every 2-4 weeks for follow-up visits. He is willing to undergo genetic testing for HLA and designate a person for durable power of attorney for medical research and medical care purposes at the NIH Clinical Center. He understands the risks associated with immunosuppression and fluctuation on HIV viral levels, but is interested in participating in the study to help advance HIV research. He is also willing to use an effective means of birth control while receiving treatment through this study and 3 months following treatment.

This is a 10-year-old child who is above the 85th percentile for weight and is considered overweight. The child's parents also have a BMI of 25 or higher and have agreed to attend all parent/child treatment meetings as the participating parent. The child is able to speak and comprehend English. The child does not have any thought disorders, suicidality, bipolar disorder, or drug or alcohol dependence, and does not have any physical disability or illness that prevents performance of physical activity at level equivalent to a brisk walk or that places severe restriction on diet. The child is not on a medication regimen that affects weight and is not involved in active psychiatric treatment for an ongoing problem that causes either social or occupational impairment. The child also does not have an eating disorder or subclinical levels of eating disturbance.

This is a 28-year-old male who is generally healthy with no history of gastrointestinal, liver or kidney diseases. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of drug dependency or alcohol abuse. The patient has a BMI of 23 kg/m2, falls within the age range of 18 to 45 years and has clinical laboratory values within the laboratory's stated normal range. The patient is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and is available for the entire study period. The informed consent form has been signed by the volunteer. There is no history of tuberculosis or prophylaxis for tuberculosis, and the result of the urine screening of drugs of abuse is negative.

The patient is a 40-year-old Hispanic man who is overweight with a BMI of 35. He has been experiencing chronic pain in his left knee for the past year and has been advised to undergo arthroscopic surgery. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medications regularly. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He works as a truck driver and is physically active during work hours. He has no known allergies and has never had surgery before. He speaks English fluently and consents to participate in the study. His pulmonary and cardiac functions are within normal limits. He has no history of difficult airway or aspiration risk. His surgery is expected to last for 2 hours, and he will not require postoperative ICU admission. He has no plans for regional anesthesia or MAC during the surgery.

The patient is a 50-year-old Canadian man who was recently hospitalized at the University of Ottawa Heart Institute (UOHI) for an acute myocardial infarction. He has been a smoker for the past 20 years, smoking an average of 15 cigarettes per day. He has a past medical history of hypertension, obesity, and dyslipidemia. He takes medications for these conditions which include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. He is married with two children and works as an office manager. He is motivated to quit smoking but has been unsuccessful in previous attempts. He is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help him quit smoking.

A 50-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with masked hypertension during a routine check-up. She has no history of hypertension and has not been taking any anti-hypertensive medication. Her clinic blood pressure was measured to be less than 140/90 mmHg, but her 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring showed readings between 135/85 and 150/95mmHg during the daytime. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the short-term efficacy of Gastrodia and Uncaria Drink in treating hypertension. She has no history of secondary hypertension, stroke, CKD, myocardial infarction, liver or kidney dysfunction, arrhythmia or psychiatric disorders. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 25-year-old male who has been leading a sedentary lifestyle for the past year. He has no prior experience with cycling training and is currently not enrolled in any other exercise program. His body mass index (BMI) is within the range of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2. The patient does not have any history of cardiovascular or metabolic disease, nor is he taking any regular oral medication. Additionally, the patient is a non-smoker and reports engaging in less than 3 hours of physical activity per week.

A 45 yo woman who has been experiencing bloating and pelvic discomfort for the past few months. She has also noticed that her abdomen has become distended and she has lost her appetite. Her primary care physician performed a pelvic exam and discovered a mass in her left ovary. Further testing, including a CT scan and elevated CA-125 levels, have raised suspicion for possible ovarian cancer. She has been referred to a gynecologic oncologist who has recommended a biopsy or surgery to confirm the diagnosis. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of a blood test for Cancer Associated Antibodies (CAAA) as an aid in the initial diagnosis of ovarian cancer. The study will involve collecting blood samples from women with suspected ovarian pathology and comparing the results of the CAAA test to pathology/cytology results or clinical history for healthy women. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no history of hematological malignancies, autoimmune disorders, or previous or current tumors. She is not currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment.

The patient is a 45 year old man who recently tested positive for Covid-19 and has been experiencing symptoms for the past 5 days. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He reports having a dry cough, shortness of breath, and fever. He has not required hospitalization and is currently isolating at home. His oxygen saturation levels have been stable and he has not required supplemental oxygen. He has been advised by his healthcare provider to monitor his symptoms and seek medical attention if they worsen. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Covid-19 treatment and is willing to be hospitalized if necessary.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman scheduled to undergo laparoscopic gynecologic surgery for the removal of an ovarian cyst. She has a medical history of mild hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine for blood pressure control. She has no known allergies to any medications, including general anesthetics. She has no history of neuromuscular diseases, electrolyte abnormalities, liver or kidney dysfunction, or ocular lesions. Her physical status is classified as ASA I. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits involved.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has progressed despite prior treatment with chemotherapy, including anthracycline and taxane. She has measurable disease according to the RECIST criteria, with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured, and a cytological or histological confirmation of breast carcinoma. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. She has adequate renal and liver function, with serum creatinine levels less than 1.5 mg/dL and bilirubin levels less than or equal to 1.5 mg/dL. The patient has adequate bone marrow function, with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin levels of at least 10.0 g/dL, and platelet counts of at least 100 x 10^9/L. She is willing and able to complete the FACT-B questionnaire, Analgesic Diary, Pain VAS, and the tumor-related symptomatic assessment. The patient has a sample from the diagnostic biopsy (paraffin block) available, and she has given written informed consent prior to any study-specific screening procedures with the understanding that she may withdraw consent at any time without prejudice. She has not received chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal therapy, or Herceptin within 2 weeks of E7389 treatment start, and she does not have radiation therapy encompassing more than 10% of marrow. The patient does not have prior treatment with Mitomycin C or nitrosoureas, and she has not undergone high dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell rescue in the past two years. The patient does not have pulmonary lymphangitic involvement that results in pulmonary dysfunction requiring active treatment, including the use of oxygen, and she does not have active symptomatic brain metastasis or meningeal carcinomatosis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is not a woman of childbearing potential with either a positive pregnancy test at Screening or no pregnancy test. She does not have severe/uncontrolled intercurrent illness/infection, significant cardiovascular impairment, organ allografts, known positive HIV status, prior malignancy, other than carcinoma in situ of the cervix or non-melanoma skin cancer, unless the prior malignancy was diagnosed and definitively treated ≥ 5 years previously with no subsequent evidence of recurrence, pre-existing neuropathy > Grade 1, hypersensitivity to halichondrin B and/or halichondrin B chemical derivative, or participated in a prior E7389 clinical trial.

A 30-year-old male with a history of chronic dysphagia and food impaction for the past 6 months. He has been evaluated by his gastroenterologist and has undergone upper endoscopy with biopsy, which revealed eosinophilic esophagitis. He has been treated with proton pump inhibitors without improvement. He has no history of heart or lung disease, is not pregnant or lactating, and does not have diabetes or chronic renal failure. The patient is able to read and understand English.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) in the neuropsychiatric department of Assiut University Hospitals. He has a mild form of GBS and is able to walk, but experiences weakness and tingling in his legs and arms. The patient has no history of renal impairment or hepatic cell failure. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of mini-pool intravenous immunoglobulin (MP-IVIG) in hastening recovery and reducing the complications of GBS. The patient will be monitored for any adverse events and will be assessed for improvement in general health and integration into social life.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with dysphagia and requires a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) for nutritional support. The patient has consented to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the use of capnography during sedation with midazolam and propofol. The patient has no history of hypotension, bradycardia or hypoxemia, and is classified as ASA I. The patient is 5'10" tall, weighs 80 kg and has a BMI of 25. The patient has no known allergies and is on no medications. The patient is scheduled for the PEG procedure in two weeks.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has a history of heart failure. He has been experiencing difficulty in breathing at night and snoring loudly, which has prompted him to seek medical attention. He has been diagnosed with severe sleep apnea and has been recommended for implantation of a LivaNova CRT-P device. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to attend routine follow-up visits beyond one year. He does not have chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure and is not already included in another clinical study that could confound the results of this study. He does not have drug/alcohol addiction or abuse, nor is he under guardianship. He is eager to participate in the study to help understand the correlation between sleep apnea, arrhythmias, and cardiac remodeling in heart failure patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with AIDS two years ago. He has been receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) and his viral load is currently undetectable. He has no ocular manifestations and his best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. He wears glasses for mild myopia (-1.50 D) and has no significant astigmatism. His intraocular pressure is within the normal range (15 mmHg). He has no history of eye surgery or trauma. He is currently not taking any medication for any ocular condition. He has no family history of glaucoma. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his day in front of a computer screen. He has no complaints of visual disturbance or any other ocular symptoms. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol requirements.

A 52-year old male who works as a truck driver was referred to the clinic for evaluation of a non-healing ulcer on his left leg. He has a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been trying to manage his diabetes through diet and exercise. He smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He reports that the ulcer has been present for about 3 months and has not responded well to previous treatments. He complains of pain and discomfort around the ulcer site, and it is hindering him from performing his job effectively. The ulcer is about 3 cm in diameter and is located below the knee on the medial aspect of his left leg. He has been receiving compression therapy for the past 2 months.

Patient is a 60yo male who was recently diagnosed with stage II lung adenocarcinoma. The patient underwent lobectomy of the affected lung and the resected tissue was collected for this study. The patient has no history of uremia, other malignant disease, or liver cirrhosis. The patient also has no history of pneumonia or pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient has not been on long period of medications. The patient's age falls within the inclusion criteria of the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who has been experiencing anxiety and obsessive thoughts that have been affecting her daily life. She has difficulty sleeping, concentrating in school, and participating in social activities. Her parents have noticed that she is often worried and irritable, and she has expressed fear of being separated from them. The patient has no comorbid diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder, conduct disorder, untreated or severe ADHD, or low IQ. She is eligible for the Cool Kids programme and her parents have given written, informed consent for her to participate in the study. The patient is willing to participate in the programme and attend all scheduled sessions.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who has not used any tobacco or nicotine-containing products for the past 6 months. Her BMI is 24, and she weighs 65 kilograms. She has no significant medical history, and her laboratory profiles, medical histories, ECGs, and physical examination results are clinically insignificant. She is sexually abstinent and is willing to use two approved methods of contraception during the study. She has not participated in any other investigational clinical trial in the last 30 days and has no abnormalities in her laboratory values at screening or check-in.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy woman who is interested in participating in an acupuncture study to explore the effects of antihistamines on pain relief. She has never undergone acupuncture treatment before but is open to alternative therapies for pain management. She reports occasional mild headaches and menstrual cramps but has not taken any medication for these conditions in the past three weeks. She is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant in the near future. She has no history of chronic medical conditions that require active medical intervention or monitoring. She does not have any skin diseases or allergies that might interfere with the EA procedure or assessments. She does not have any implants, such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, or electronic medical equipment in her body. Overall, she is excited to learn more about how acupuncture and antihistamines can work together for pain relief and is willing to commit to the study protocol.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the anus. The diagnosis was confirmed by biopsy after presenting with symptoms of anal pain, bleeding, and discharge. A CT scan revealed a 2 cm mass in the anal canal with involvement of the adjacent lymph nodes. The tumor is staged as T2N1M0. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of Grade 1. He has no history of previous radiation therapy, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy. He has no known allergies to dextran, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has provided written informed consent and HIPAA authorization to participate in the study.

30-year-old male who is a non-smoker and non-vegetarian. The patient has no known metabolic diseases and is not on any chronic medications. The patient is in good health and has no history of recent illnesses or hospitalizations. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials to contribute to medical research and has no known allergies.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who received a kidney transplant 6 months ago due to end-stage renal disease caused by hypertension. He was discharged from the hospital with a functioning graft and was prescribed azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone for immunosuppression. Despite receiving education about the importance of medication adherence, he has been struggling with taking his medications consistently. He has missed several doses and sometimes takes them at different times than prescribed. He is currently experiencing some mild side effects from the immunosuppressive medications, including nausea and diarrhea. He speaks English fluently and lives in the United States. He is not currently receiving treatment for any other medical conditions and is not taking any medications other than those prescribed for his transplant. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve medication compliance and reduce the risk of acute graft rejection and graft loss.

The patient is a 65 year old male who noticed a sudden decrease in his vision in his right eye 2 weeks ago. He reports that he felt like a curtain was coming down over his eye and he could not see anything below it. He also reports seeing floaters and having difficulty reading small print. He has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. Examination reveals a dilated retinal venous system and retinal hemorrhages in all 4 quadrants of the right eye. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) testing shows central macular edema with a central point thickness of 300 microns. His visual acuity score is 20/200 in the affected eye by the ETDRS visual acuity protocol. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The patient underwent surgical resection of the tumor and received chemotherapy, but the disease recurred. The patient is now radiation-naïve and is eligible for this clinical trial to receive P276-00 in combination with radiation. The patient has completed any prior chemotherapy and has recovered from the toxic effects of the therapy. The patient has measurable disease as per RECIST criteria and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient's organ and marrow function are normal, and the patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for this study.

Unfortunately, as this is a laboratory research study involving the use of biologic specimens only, there are no patients that can be described for this trial. The study is utilizing endometrial biopsy samples collected from subjects who meet the inclusion criteria for other trials.

68-year-old independent woman with a BMI of 26, currently not engaging in regular exercise but is able to perform daily activities without assistance. She has noticed a decline in muscle strength and power over the past few years, which has led to difficulty with tasks such as climbing stairs and carrying groceries. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve physical function and potentially reduce the age-related loss of muscle mass and function. She has no history of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cardiac arrhythmias, or active cancer. She has no surgical diseases that would compromise participation in exercise regimens. She does not have any implanted magnetic devices incompatible with MRI scanning. She is willing to be randomized into one of three groups, which may include a supervised, high-intensity progressive resistance training program conducted three times weekly in a local fitness center or a "guided" moderate-intensity home-based resistance training program conducted with elastic bands and body weight three times weekly. She is aware that she may also be randomized into a control group that does not engage in any physical activity intervention.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of proteinuria and decreased kidney function. She was previously diagnosed with dense deposit disease (DDD) and has undergone multiple rounds of immunomodulatory therapy with no significant improvement. Her 24-hour urine protein is >1 gram/day, and her urine protein:creatinine ratio is >1.0. Her creatinine level has decreased slightly with treatment, but her estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) remains below 30 ml/min/1.73m2. She is willing and able to sign informed consent and agrees to use birth control during the trial. She has no history of meningococcal disease and is willing to be vaccinated against it. She is not currently taking any other immunomodulatory therapies and has no comorbid conditions that would interfere with the trial. She is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve her kidney function and histologic parameters.

The patient is a 62 year old woman who has been experiencing intermittent abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits over the past few months. Her primary care physician has recommended a colonoscopy, but the patient is hesitant due to the invasiveness of the procedure. She is interested in participating in the German Colon Capsule Registry study as an alternative to traditional colonoscopy. The patient has no history of intestinal obstruction, dysphagia or pregnancy. She is willing to provide consent for the study and is eager to contribute to the evaluation of safety, quality assurance and quality control of colon capsule endoscopy.

55 yo F with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, currently on lisinopril and atorvastatin. Patient is interested in self-management of her health conditions and has expressed willingness to participate in a clinical trial. She is able to read and understand English without assistance. She has no known drug allergies and is not pregnant or nursing. No significant family history of heart disease. The patient is compliant with her current medications and has had no recent hospitalizations or emergency department visits related to her hypertension or high cholesterol.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis and recurrent bouts of acute pancreatitis. He has been referred to the University of Minnesota for a total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation (TPIAT) due to intractable pain and poor quality of life. He has no prior history of diabetes mellitus, but his fasting blood glucose level is mildly elevated at 105 mg/dL. He is not taking any medications for diabetes or any other conditions. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to improve the function of the transplanted islets and reduce the risk of diabetes mellitus after the TPIAT. He has no history of immunoglobulin (IgA) deficiency or liver disease, and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He has not been diagnosed with any infectious diseases such as HIV, hepatitis B or C, and tuberculosis. The patient has no history of demyelinating disease or lupus erythematosus. He has no hematological abnormalities and is not taking any corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents. The patient is not allergic to etanercept or alpha-1 antitrypsin, and he has no coagulopathy or need for anticoagulant therapy. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has no untreated psychiatric illness or neurocognitive disorder that would interfere with his ability to give informed consent.

Maria is a 32-year-old woman who has a history of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results. She is currently not pregnant and has not undergone a hysterectomy. Maria has no previous experience with self-sampling devices. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications. Maria is interested in participating in the clinical trial to validate human papillomavirus assays and collection devices for self-samples and urine samples. She is willing to provide two urine samples using the Colli-Pee device and two vaginal self-samples, one with a cotton swab and the other with a plastic brush, at the colposcopy centre. She understands the purpose of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent. Maria is excited to contribute to improving the accuracy of cervical cancer screening tests and hopes that this study will help increase access to screening for women who may face barriers to traditional screening methods.

A 16-year-old high school student came to the clinic with apparent feelings of sadness and hopelessness. She has been feeling this way for several weeks and has lost interest in things she used to enjoy. She has also had trouble sleeping and concentrating on schoolwork. She is afraid to talk to her parents about how she feels because she worries they will think she is weak or crazy. She has heard that people with depression are often stigmatized and that makes her feel even more isolated. She has been hesitant to seek help because of this stigma, but she knows she needs to do something to feel better. Her family has no history of mental illness. She is an only child and has a close relationship with her parents. She is currently taking no medications.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depression. She has been taking antidepressant medication for the past 6 months and reports feeling stable. She lives in a rural area and has difficulty accessing mental health services due to the distance and transportation issues. She works as a freelance writer and spends most of her time at home. She has a history of alcohol abuse but reports that she has been sober for the past year. She has no history of hospitalization for psychiatric reasons. Her Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) score is 60. She has access to a telephone and is comfortable using it. She is interested in participating in the study to have access to more frequent psychiatric care without having to travel long distances.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who has been experiencing hair loss for the past year. He has noticed a receding hairline and thinning hair on the crown of his head. He has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He has tried using various hair treatments and shampoos but has not seen any improvement. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the treatment schedule and post-treatment follow-up. He has no known allergies to any of the ingredients in the test products. The patient's hair loss is classified as mild to moderate androgenic alopecia (AGA) graded IIv, IIIv, IV or V according to the Hamilton-Norwood classification. He is willing to use the same shampoo, refrain from changing his hair style or hair dyeing during the study, and to refrain from any therapy affecting hair during the study. He is also willing to have photographs of the treated area taken. The patient has no other hair loss disorders, such as alopecia areata, scarring alopecia, and has not undergone hair transplant surgery, scalp reduction surgery or hair weave or tattooing of the alopecic area. He is not suffering from any active dermatological condition in the treated area such as scalp atrophy. Upon enrollment in the study, the patient will be randomly assigned to receive treatment with either the study medication or placebo.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She is feeling overwhelmed and anxious about her diagnosis but is determined to fight the disease. She has a history of smoking but quit a year ago. She is currently taking vitamin supplements and has no known drug allergies. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is physically active. She has no history of cardiac disease or neurological symptoms suggestive of brain metastases. Her medical history is unremarkable except for an appendectomy in her teenage years. She has not received prior chemotherapy for the treatment of recurrent or metastatic breast cancer. She is willing to undergo a biopsy to provide tissue for correlative studies. Her performance status is 1 by ECOG criteria. Her life expectancy is greater than 12 weeks. She has normal organ and bone marrow function documented within 14 days prior to enrollment as defined by the protocol. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study.

A 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. Cardiac catheterization revealed significant three-vessel coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis. The patient is scheduled for elective cardiac surgery with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and cardioplegic arrest. Due to the high perioperative risk profile, the patient is eligible to participate in the SUSTAIN CSX®-Trial. The patient will be randomized to receive either a daily perioperative high-dose selenium or placebo until postoperative day 10 or upon earlier discharge from ICU. The study aims to investigate the effects of perioperative high dose selenium supplementation in high-risk cardiac surgical patients undergoing complicated open heart surgery, and the investigators hypothesize that the therapeutic strategy tested in this randomized trial may contribute to fewer complications, less organ injury, and fewer deaths. If the hypothesis is proven true, the simple, inexpensive nutrient may change clinical practice and improve health outcomes.

A 19-year-old woman with spastic cerebral palsy was referred to the Stockholm Habilitation Center to participate in a study aiming to improve physical function and muscle health in teenagers and young adults with cerebral palsy (CP) through flywheel resistance exercise. She has been diagnosed with CP since birth and has been receiving physical therapy and occupational therapy to improve her mobility and independence. Her Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level is II, which means she is able to walk with hand-held mobility devices and is able to walk short distances without assistance. She has not had any surgical treatments of the knee extensor apparatus within the last 12 months and has not received botulinum toxin treatment within the last six months. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve her muscle strength, balance and gait performance.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who was diagnosed with disseminated coccidioidomycosis infection. She presents to the clinic with a persistent cough, fever, and night sweats. Her past medical history is significant for asthma and she is currently on a low dose of inhaled corticosteroids. Her family history is not significant for any medical issues. Her lab study shows a positive Coccidioides polymerase chain reaction, and a complement fixation titer of 1:64. She has been taking high dose fluconazole for the past 3 months, but her symptoms have not improved. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not take any medications that would increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and her electrocardiogram shows no signs of prolonged corrected QT interval or Left Bundle Branch Block. She is able to attend regular clinic visits and is willing to use contraception if necessary.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained multiple injuries, including a traumatic brain injury, fractured ribs, and a lacerated spleen. He was admitted to the ICU and has been receiving intensive medical care for the past 5 days. He has been intubated and mechanically ventilated since admission, and has undergone surgery to repair his spleen. He is currently receiving antibiotics to prevent infection, as well as medications to manage his pain and blood pressure. He has a history of hypertension and is a former smoker, but quit 2 years ago. He is married and has two young children. He has no known allergies, and his family history is unremarkable. The patient is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme. She has completed initial treatment involving radiation therapy and is 3 months post-treatment. She is currently maintained on a stable corticosteroid regimen for the past 7 days. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 80%, indicating that she is able to care for herself with little help from others. Her hematologic, renal, and liver function are all adequate. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to practice contraception during the study. She has no serious concurrent infections or clinically significant cardiac disease. The patient is not allergic or sensitive to sulfa-containing medications. She understands the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He is currently not taking any prescribed or non-prescribed medications. He is 178 cm tall and weighs 75 kg, with a body mass index (BMI) of 23.7 kg/m2. He is interested in participating in this study to help advance medical research. He has no known allergies to medications or other substances. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly.

50 y/o male with open-angle glaucoma diagnosed 2 years ago, currently on Travoprost Intraocular Implant (G2TR). The patient's best spectacle corrected visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes. The patient has previously qualified for GC-009 clinical trial with the Travoprost Intraocular Implant. The patient's angle anatomy is open with no peripheral anterior synechia (PAS), rubeosis, or other angle abnormalities and is able to provide an adequate and interpretable visual field examination result. The patient is willing to attend scheduled follow-up exams for the duration of the study, able to provide written informed consent on the IRB/IEC-approved Informed Consent form, and has not undergone any incisional glaucoma surgery or history of laser iridotomy or laser trabeculoplasty within the last 90 days. The patient does not have any active inflammation or edema, clinically significant dystrophy or guttata, significant scarring or irregularities, or any corneal disorders that would inhibit visualization of the nasal angle. The patient does not have any ocular or systemic disorders that may interfere with IOP measurement reliability or compromise their participation in the study. The patient has not undergone any changes in existing chronic systemic therapy that could substantially affect IOP or the study outcomes within 30 days prior to Visit 1 (screening), or anticipated change in such therapy during the study duration. The patient does not have any known allergy, hypersensitivity, or contraindication to the study medications or their components, namely prostaglandin analogues. The patient is able to visualize the implantation site via surgical gonioscopy.

A 28-year-old mother of two children, aged 2 and 5, residing in the city of Edmonton, presents with limited income and difficulties accessing necessary health and social services for her family. The family receives low-income assistance in the form of Alberta Works Income Support and Alberta Child Health Benefits. The mother is interested in participating in the Families First Edmonton study to explore innovative service-delivery models that may help overcome the barriers she has faced in accessing health and social services. She is able to provide signed consent and is committed to participating for the entire follow-up period. She is fluent in English and does not require a translator.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis during the spring allergy season. She reports nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes. She has never used beclomethasone dipropionate or flunisolide for her symptoms. She does not have any significant concomitant medical conditions and has not used corticosteroids or any other allergy medications during the study. She does not use tobacco or any tobacco products. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help validate the Preference Module of the EARNS-Q questionnaire.

A 27-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick skin type II is interested in participating in the NatrOVA Photoallergy Study. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to adhesives or medical tape. She is not currently pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy during the test period. She has no history of severe reactions from exposure to sunlight and has not used any photosensitizing medications. She does not have any clinical significant skin diseases, asthma, or severe respiratory disease requiring chronic medication. She currently takes occasional over-the-counter pain relievers but no systemic antihistamine medication. She has not participated in any clinical trial or patch test for irritation or sensitization within the past 4 weeks. She is interested in contributing to the study and has signed a written informed consent form and HIPAA authorization.

A 55-year-old male who has been experiencing pain and a rash on his left side for the past week. He has never had similar symptoms before and is seeking medical attention for the first time to address this issue. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not currently participating in any other research studies.

A 10-year-old boy with a history of CNS malignancy presents with recurrent disease. The patient underwent surgical resection and radiation therapy two years ago for a malignant brain tumor. He has had multiple relapses and has received multiple chemotherapy regimens, but his disease continues to progress. His most recent MRI shows a large enhancing lesion with surrounding edema. He has no other significant past medical history, but he has been on dexamethasone for the past two weeks. His performance status is 70 on the Karnofsky Performance Scale. His laboratory results are within normal limits. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have signed the informed consent document.

54 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and occasional smoking presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. CT scan revealed a cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage with a hematoma volume of 60ml. Onset to diagnosis time was 3 hours and 45 minutes. Glasgow Coma Scale was 14 points. The patient is able to provide consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of Shengdi Dahuang Decoction in the treatment of acute hemorrhagic stroke.

A 57-year-old man presented with abdominal pain, weight loss, and jaundice. He was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in the head of the pancreas, which is deemed resectable. He has no significant medical history and his ECOG performance status is 0. He has no known allergies to Fluorouracil (5FU), oxaliplatin or gemcitabine. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for pancreatic cancer. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a novel neoadjuvant treatment strategy incorporating 5-fluorouracil/leucovorin with oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy in combination with chemo-radiation with gemcitabine.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of tricuspid atresia underwent a lateral tunnel Fontan procedure at age 6 years. She has been followed by a pediatric cardiologist at a regional children's hospital since her surgery. She has had excellent functional status since her Fontan procedure and has not had any major complications or hospitalizations related to her Fontan circulation. She completed high school and has a full-time job as a graphic designer. She is married and has no children. Her most recent electrocardiogram (ECG) showed normal sinus rhythm and her echocardiogram showed preserved ventricular function with no significant valvular stenosis or regurgitation.
