She is not currently being evaluated for or listed for cardiac transplant and has not undergone any Fontan revisions or conversions. She is not currently pregnant.

This study is seeking participants who are habitual soft contact lens wearers and are willing to participate in a bilateral, randomized, double-masked study comparing the surface refractive index shift and lens absorption/adsorption of tear components of Kalifilcon A lenses versus Dailies Total1 and Precision1. The ideal participant for this study would be 18 years or older and have full legal capacity to volunteer. They should have physiologically normal anterior segments without any clinically significant biomicroscopy findings, no active ocular disease or allergic conjunctivitis, and not be using any topical ocular medications. Participants should be willing and able to follow instructions and have signed a statement of informed consent. They should not be participating in any conflicting studies, and should be considered a suitable candidate for participation by the Investigator. Approximately 10 participants will be enrolled in this study.

29 F diagnosed with schizophrenia at age 23 years. She is currently on olanzapine for the past year with a dose of 20mg/day. She has gained 10kg since starting the medication and has expressed concerns about her weight gain and its impact on her self-esteem. She is interested in participating in a weight management program to help her manage her weight and improve her overall well-being. Additionally, she has no history of renal or endocrine diseases and has not had a weight change greater than 3kg in the past three months. She is willing to cooperate with all tests and examinations required by the protocol and has a sufficient understanding to participate adequately in the weight management program. She has provided informed consent and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 13-year-old male student who is currently studying in a boarding school in Bogor, West Java, Indonesia. He was diagnosed with pediculosis capitis, a parasitic infestation that causes scalp pruritus and quality of life disturbances. He has medium length hair and he is willing to participate as a research subject after being explained the details of the study. He has not received any chemical treatment for pediculosis capitis within the last 10 days and he does not have a history of permethrin hypersensitivity. He does not have any mild-to-severe secondary infection and his hair is not too long or too short. He will be asked to complete both visual analog scale (VAS) and 5-D itch scale to assess the severity of scalp pruritus and the impact on his quality of life. The data recorded from his responses will be used for statistical analysis to determine the relationship between the two pruritus scales.

The patient is a 29-year-old primigravida woman at 39 weeks gestation presenting to the labor and delivery unit with contractions every 5 minutes lasting 60 seconds. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on labetalol 200 mg twice daily. She denies smoking, drinking, or using illicit drugs. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. Her prenatal care has been unremarkable, with no complications. On physical exam, her cervix is 4 cm dilated and 80% effaced. Fetal heart rate monitoring is reassuring. She requests epidural analgesia for labor pain relief. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and sign the informed consent form. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

This is a 30 year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22. She has no known congenital or chronic diseases and is not currently taking any medications. She regularly exercises and maintains a healthy lifestyle. She has no history of regular alcohol intake and does not smoke. She has no history of gastric resection or blood transfusions. She has no known allergies to any of the study drugs. She has read and understood the contents of the consent form and has agreed to use contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of melanoma. He has been experiencing severe headaches, seizures, and difficulty with speech, which led to a diagnosis of brain metastases. The patient has no history of autoimmune diseases or prior treatment with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2 antibodies. He has been treatment-naive to nivolumab. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. His BRAF status has been determined, and it is negative. The patient's white blood cell count, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, hemoglobin, serum creatinine, AST, ALT, bilirubin, and LDH are all within normal limits. The patient has no active infections, and no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders. He has no known allergies to the study drug components. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to use appropriate contraception methods.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has opted for breast reconstruction with tissue expanders following her mastectomy. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or diabetes, and has a BMI of 26. She has no history of radiation therapy and is not immunocompromised. She is willing to undergo the use of AlloMax as part of her reconstructive surgery. She has a supportive family and is motivated to participate in the study to help advance the field of breast reconstruction.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who habitually consumes caffeine on a daily basis. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and fasted blood glucose levels of 90 mg/dL. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and abstain from any nutritional supplement and herbal preparation 48 hours prior to the study visit. He does not have a history of diabetes mellitus or uncontrolled hypertension. He does not suffer from primary or secondary insomnia and is not currently receiving treatment for insomnia. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of EnXtra.

The patient is a 25 year old Hispanic male who recently immigrated to the United States for better opportunities. He works as a construction worker and has limited English proficiency. He has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety, such as constant worry, difficulty sleeping, and feeling on edge. He also reports feeling sad and hopeless at times. He has never received any mental health treatment before and is hesitant to seek help due to language barriers. He has a history of hypertension and has been prescribed medication by his primary care physician. He lives with his wife and two children in a small apartment. He is interested in learning English and improving his job prospects. He has been referred to the study by his primary care physician who believes that he would benefit from mental health evaluation and treatment.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with sarcoma. She has undergone next-generation sequencing profiling which revealed the presence of an alteration in fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) 2. She has progressed following at least one standard prior chemotherapy regimen. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, with mild fatigue and is otherwise healthy. She has a history of treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin. She has no evidence of cardiac disease and has an echocardiogram that shows normal cardiac function. Her blood counts and liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of allergic reactions to any medications. She is willing to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study and is able to swallow and maintain pills. She has agreed to use an adequate form of contraception during the study and for 4 months after completing rogaratinib (BAY 1163877) administration. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

29-year-old woman who is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and experiencing symptoms of fatigue and poor sleep quality. She has not been diagnosed with any pregnancy complications such as preeclampsia, preterm labor, preterm rupture of membranes, gestational diabetes, or cervical incompetence. She can read Chinese and is willing to complete questionnaires and give blood samples for a study investigating the effects of modified TaiChi exercise on maternal stress, fatigue, sleep quality, biomarkers, and infant gestational age and birthweight. She will be randomly assigned to either the TaiChi group or comparison group and will be asked to practice the exercise at home or keep on her usual daily activities, respectively. Additionally, she will be asked to complete questionnaires and give blood samples at specific intervals during her pregnancy and after delivery. The study aims to refine a TaiChi exercise program suitable for pregnant women, investigate the relationships between prenatal stress, fatigue, sleep quality, biomarkers, and infant outcomes, and test the effects of the exercise on reducing stress and fatigue, promoting sleep quality, modulating biomarkers, and preventing adverse infant outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B (HBV) infection. He had previously received lamivudine (LVD) treatment but developed resistance with evidence of at least one LVD resistance substitution (valine, isoleucine or serine) at reverse transcriptase codon 204 (M204V/I/S). He presents with a high HBV DNA level of more than 1.72 x 10*4* IU/mL (approximately 10*5* copies/mL) and an alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level within the normal range. He is documented to be hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) positive and hepatitis B e antibody (HBeAb) negative at screening. The patient has compensated liver function with an international normalization ratio (INR) of ≤ 1.5, serum albumin level of ≥ 3 g

42 yo F with relapsed AML refractory to multiple rounds of chemotherapy. Patient has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Patient has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and bruising easily. Upon evaluation, patient was found to have pancytopenia and a bone marrow biopsy confirmed relapsed AML. Patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has been deemed eligible for the Thalidomide Anti-Angiogenesis Therapy of Relapsed or Refractory Leukemia study. Patient has signed informed consent and agrees to use safe contraceptive methods during the treatment and for at least 4 months after the treatment is completed. Serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. Performance status is 2. Patient will be monitored closely for any side effects and will take Thalidomide tablets at bedtime daily until remission. The dose will be increased gradually and modified according to side-effects. The drug will be given daily up to the time of complete remission then as long as it is beneficial.

A 50-year-old woman visited the clinic and was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She has no symptoms such as pain, lumps or discharge from her breasts. Her biopsy showed invasive ductal carcinoma that measured 1.5 cm in diameter. Her cancer was estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor negative, and HER2/neu negative. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. The pathology report showed that 1 of 16 lymph nodes was positive for cancer. She received adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for 4 cycles every 3 weeks, followed by paclitaxel for 12 cycles every week. She completed her chemotherapy one month ago and is now planning to participate in a clinical trial investigating the combination of DJ-927 and capecitabine for metastatic breast cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with pancreatic cancer six months ago. He previously underwent standard-of-care chemotherapy, but the disease has progressed. He presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Imaging studies reveal measurable lesions in the pancreas, liver, and peritoneum. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or organ transplant requiring immunosuppression. Laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count of 1,500 cells/mm3, platelet count of 125,000 cells/mm3, total bilirubin within normal limits, AST and ALT levels slightly elevated but within normal limits, alkaline phosphatase levels within normal limits, serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, and normal anion gap and arterial blood pH. The patient has no history of hypertension or cardiovascular disease. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular ejection fraction. The patient is not receiving systemic corticosteroids and has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the study medication. The patient is willing to undergo biopsy during the screening period if considered safe by the Investigator. He is willing to provide blood samples and a tumor biopsy specimen 8 weeks after the start of treatment if considered safe by the Investigator. He agrees to practice effective contraception for up to 1 year after completion of therapy.

The patient is a third-generation Japanese-American man in his late 40s who is concerned about his risk for cardiovascular disease. He has a family history of hypertension, high cholesterol, and heart disease. He works a sedentary job and admits to a diet high in processed foods and fast food. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses but is slightly overweight and struggles with central obesity around his waistline. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand his risk factors and potentially make lifestyle changes to improve his overall health.

A 35-year-old male with a history of mild to moderate asthma for the past 10 years presented at the clinic for this clinical trial. He has been able to manage his asthma symptoms with the use of a short-acting beta2-agonist metered dose inhaler. He is a non-smoker and has not used any nicotine-containing products for at least 2 years. His body mass index (BMI) is within the range of 18-25 kg/m^2. He is generally in good health, with no other significant medical history. During the screening visit, he demonstrated no significant decrease in absolute forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1). He has not experienced a decrease in AM or PM peak expiratory flow (PEF) below the Stability Limit on any 2 consecutive days prior to the Baseline Visit. He has not required the use of more than 8 inhalations per day of the short-acting beta2-agonist metered dose inhaler (MDI) or more than 2 nebulized treatments per day of 2.5 mg albuterol, on any 2 consecutive days from the Screening Visit up to the Baseline Visit. He has not experienced an exacerbation defined as a clinical deterioration of asthma that resulted in emergency treatment, hospitalization due to asthma, or treatment with additional, excluded medication (other than short-acting beta agonists [SABA]) at any time from the Screening Visit up to the Baseline Visit. He has not been hospitalized for treatment of asthma or required oral corticosteroids for treatment of asthma within the past 6 months, or has ever required ventilator support for respiratory failure secondary to asthma.

42-year-old female with a history of stress urinary incontinence. She has noticed leakage of urine with activities such as coughing, laughing, and exercising. She has undergone multichannel cystometry, which confirmed the presence of genuine stress incontinence. She has not undergone any previous treatment with pelvic floor physiotherapy with biofeedback, functional electric stimulation, or weighted vaginal cones. She does not have any history of pelvic organ prolapse, abnormal vaginal anatomy, or significant medical conditions that could interfere with participation in the study. She is fluent in both French and English and can provide informed consent. She is not pregnant and is willing to comply with the study requirements for a minimum of six months.

A 45-year-old female office worker was found to have subclinical hypothyroidism during a routine health check-up. She has no significant past medical history, and she takes no regular medications. She complains of feeling tired and sluggish, especially in the mornings, and has gained some weight over the past year despite no significant changes in her diet or exercise regimen. She has no history of heart disease, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married with two children and is generally in good health. She has no known allergies and has never had surgery. She is interested in participating in the study to help with research on subclinical thyroid dysfunction.

60-year-old male with a history of heart failure (NYHA Class III) for 2 years, presents with complaints of increasing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs. The patient has been managed with standard medical therapy for heart failure, including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers. He has been hospitalized twice in the past 6 months for heart failure exacerbation and required intravenous treatment. He has no history of COPD or restrictive airway disease. The patient is not on continuous positive inotropic therapy, has no known atrial or ventricular septal defects or mechanical right heart valves, and is not enrolled in any concurrent studies. The patient has no severe non-cardiac conditions limiting 6-month survival. The patient's serum creatinine is within the normal range. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has no plans for heart transplantation within 6 months. The patient is not pregnant and is not of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus who is currently 39 weeks pregnant. She has been attending the high-risk obstetrical diabetic clinic and has good compliance with clinic visits and home glucose monitoring. She has a singleton gestation, intact membranes, and a cephalic presentation. Her estimated gestational age is at least 38 weeks by ACOG dates. Her amniotic fluid index (AFI) is greater than 5 cm and her Non-Stress Test is reactive. She has a Bishop score of less than or equal to 4 and uterine contractions less than or equal to 12/hour. She is interested in participating in a study on outpatient cervical ripening with orally administered misoprostol. The study will enroll 128 patients, 64 of whom will receive misoprostol 50mcg PO q day for two days (days 1 and 4) and 64 of whom will receive placebo (vitamin C) q day for two days (days 1 and 4) for cervical ripening and labor induction. The study will assess the efficacy and safety of oral misoprostol in an outpatient setting, as well as the cost differential in inpatient and outpatient utilization of misoprostol for cervical ripening and labor induction. She will be observed in the antepartum

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who was born prematurely with a birth weight of 1200 grams. He is attending kindergarten and is doing well academically, but his parents have noticed that he has difficulties understanding other people's emotions and intentions. He also struggles with social interactions and often misinterprets social cues. He has no history of neurological or developmental disorders and has no current medical issues. His parents are interested in participating in a study that explores the development of theory of mind in children born prematurely, and they are willing to provide informed consent for their child's participation in the study.

A 65-year-old man came to the clinic with complaints of memory loss and difficulty with daily tasks. His family has noticed that he is becoming more forgetful and is having trouble following conversations. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, but no prior psychiatric conditions. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and cholesterol. His cognitive screening test showed mild cognitive impairment, and his [11C]PiB PET imaging demonstrated amyloid binding. He is otherwise healthy and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study, including having a study partner who can provide information about his cognitive and functional abilities. He is willing and able to undergo the study procedures and follow the study schedule.

A 57-year-old male patient presented to the hospital with worsening shortness of breath, coughing, and increased mucus production for the last 3 days. He has a known history of COPD with FEV1/FVC ratio of 45%. He is not a smoker but has a history of working in a dusty environment. He reports that he has not been able to complete his daily activities due to his respiratory symptoms. He has no history of cardiac events or tracheal intubation. He has no other chronic respiratory diseases, neurological or psychiatric comorbidities. Physical examination reveals diminished breath sounds and wheezing in the lung fields. His oxygen saturation level is 89% on room air. He is admitted to the hospital for exacerbation of COPD. During hospitalization, he will be asked to wear a pedometer to measure his daily steps. On the second day of his hospitalization, a blood test will be performed to explore different markers of inflammation and oxidative stress. He will also undergo ultrasound measurement of the sectional area of the Rectus Femoris and maximal voluntary contraction of quadriceps (MVCQ) on the second, fifth, eighth day of hospitalization, on discharge and on the sixtieth day after hospitalization to assess muscle mass and strength. This study will help identify the determinants associated with the onset of amyotrophy induced during exacerbation of COPD and may provide a better understanding of the mechanisms of muscle dysfunction in COPD exacerbation.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who occasionally uses e-cigarettes (less than four days a week and more than once a month). She has no history of chronic medical or major psychiatric problems, including asthma, and does not suffer from heavy snoring or sleep apnea. Her pre-bronchodilator FEV1 or FVC is above 80% predicted, and she has no metal in her body, no known allergy to gadolinium, and no history of kidney problems. She has not used any conventional cigarettes, marijuana, illicit drugs, or medication or inhalers (excluding hormonal contraceptives) in the past 30 days. She also has not reported binge drinking in the last two weeks. She has not had any adverse symptomatic response to e-cigarette exposure in the past.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain that radiates to his back. He describes the pain as sharp and stabbing and rates it an 8 out of 10. He has no significant past medical history and denies any recent trauma or illnesses. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally. He reports feeling generally unwell and experiencing shortness of breath. Upon examination, he is tachycardic with a heart rate of 110 bpm and his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. An electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and a diagnosis of acute pericarditis is made. The patient is admitted to the hospital and started on ibuprofen 600mg tid. During his hospital stay, he undergoes additional tests including echocardiography and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I and CRP blood tests. He is then approached about participating in a clinical trial investigating prognostic biomarkers in patients with acute pericarditis and agrees to provide written informed consent. He is followed up regularly for 18 months and undergoes blood sampling to measure plasma biomarkers and imaging tests to quantify imaging biomarkers. The study aims to establish the value of biomarkers in predicting clinical outcomes such as pericarditis recurrences, constrictive pericarditis, and the need to switch to second-line treatment.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who tested positive for COVID-19 by a locally obtained viral diagnostic test. He has a history of coronary artery disease and diabetes requiring medication. His symptoms include fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has not been hospitalized for COVID-19 and is not currently receiving dual antiplatelet therapy or anticoagulation. His D-dimer level was found to be greater than the upper limit of normal for the local laboratory within 2 weeks of the COVID-19 test and prior to randomization. He has no known allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to rivaroxaban or its excipients.

A 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic with a non-healing ulcer on the plantar aspect of his right foot. He reports that the ulcer has been present for more than 8 weeks and has not responded to previous conventional treatments. The ulcer is approximately 2 cm in diameter, 0.5 cm deep, and shows no signs of infection. The patient reports no pain or discomfort but is concerned about the lack of healing. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent. The patient has no history of autoimmune diseases and is not currently taking any immunosuppressors. He is able to attend weekly evaluations and perform daily ulcer cleansing. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. His ankle/brachial index is within normal limits.

A 35-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past five years presents with a history of poor response to conventional antipsychotic medication. He experiences persistent symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and social withdrawal, which have resulted in his inability to function and engage in daily activities. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not on any medication for other illnesses. He has no history of renal or liver disease, diabetes, or hypertension. The patient is not taking thiazides or ACE inhibitors. The treating physician has recommended participation in an open-label trial of allopurinol for four weeks to assess its effectiveness in improving his symptoms. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial.

A 57-year-old Caucasian male has been diagnosed with stage IV NSCLC. He has a history of smoking and was diagnosed with COPD 5 years ago. His initial treatment was with chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He developed a pleural effusion and had to undergo a pleurodesis. He then received pembrolizumab for 6 months, which initially showed a partial response but then progressed. He discontinued pembrolizumab and is currently on no therapy. He has a performance status of 1 and has no other significant medical history. He reports occasional fatigue and shortness of breath but is otherwise doing well. His CT scan shows progression of disease in the lung and liver. His HbA1C is 6.2%, and his creatinine clearance is 78 mL/min. He has no evidence of brain metastasis. He is willing to undergo a tissue biopsy for biomarker analysis. He understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with colorectal cancer. The patient underwent a colonoscopy due to rectal bleeding and was found to have a cancerous mass in the descending colon. The patient has no significant past medical history, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a financial analyst and enjoys playing golf in his free time. The patient is scheduled to undergo minimally invasive surgery with curative intent. He has no planned ostomy creation at the time of enrollment. The patient's serum creatinine level is 1.2, measured within 30 days of surgery. He is fluent in English and has no history of postoperative nausea and vomiting. The patient does not have a history of congestive heart failure, systolic heart failure, or diastolic heart failure.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who suffered a severe traumatic brain injury in a motor vehicle accident. He has been admitted to the neuro-resuscitation unit of the hospital and is currently undergoing peak monitoring with cerebral temperature measurement by an intra-parenchymal sensor. His current temperature is 39°C, and he is experiencing brain pain. He has no significant medical history other than the brain injury. The patient is not under any legal protection measure, and he is not a pregnant or breastfeeding woman. The patient has not participated in this study before.

35 yo F with a history of grass pollen induced rhinoconjunctivitis with no asthma, referred by her primary care physician for evaluation and possible enrollment in a clinical trial. She reports symptoms of sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and itchy eyes that occur mainly during the spring and summer months, and have interfered with her daily activities. She reports using over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal sprays with limited relief. She has a positive skin prick test response to Phleum pratense at her initial visit, and specific IgE against Phleum pratense, IgE Class 3. Her FEV1 is 90% of predicted value at the initial visit. She is currently using a combination oral contraceptive for birth control. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to adhere to dose and visit schedules, and use a medically acceptable and adequate form of birth control. She has no history of recent immunosuppressive treatment, severe asthma, anaphylaxis with cardiorespiratory symptoms, chronic urticaria and angioedema, or chronic sinusitis, and has no other clinically significant condition or situation that would interfere with the study evaluations or optimal participation in the study. She is not currently participating in any other clinical study and is not a family member of the investigational study staff conducting this study.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy from France who has been diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) caused by a nonsense mutation. He has been receiving usual care treatment with commercial supply of Translarna (Ataluren) for the past year. He is able to walk independently but frequently suffers from muscle weakness, particularly in his legs. His past medical history is significant for a genetic mutation causing DMD, but he has no other significant medical conditions. His family history is unremarkable. He is currently taking Translarna as his primary treatment for DMD. He and his parents have agreed to participate in the study and provide written informed consent. The patient will be followed for at least 5 years from the date of enrollment.

66-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. On arrival, he developed VF cardiac arrest and received CPR for 12 minutes before return of spontaneous circulation was achieved. He remained comatose with a Glasgow Coma Score of 6 and was transferred to the ICU for further management. The patient was intubated, and hypothermia treatment was initiated. He was maintained at 33°C for 24 hours, followed by rewarming for 12 hours. Neurological assessments were performed at 24, 48, and 72 hours after the return of spontaneous circulation. The patient's condition improved over time and he was successfully extubated on day 5. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the TIMECARD study and was enrolled in the registry for further analysis of the factors influencing the application of hypothermia treatment and prognostic evaluation under hypothermia treatment.

The patient is a 53-year-old man who has been experiencing upper abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty swallowing for the past few months. He has lost some weight recently, but he attributes it to his new diet plan. He has a family history of gastric cancer, as his father passed away from the disease. The patient has never smoked or drank alcohol. He underwent an endoscopy, which revealed a tumor in his stomach. Biopsy confirmed it to be gastric adenocarcinoma. CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of metastasis. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He has a normal blood count and organ function. He is willing to use contraception during the study and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

32 F with a history of infertility for 2 years, presenting with unexplained infertility. Her previous workup showed normal ovarian reserve with FSH level of 9 mIU/mL, E2 level of 60 pg/mL and AMH level of 2.5 ng/mL. Antral follicular count was 7 follicles in one ovary. Her partner's semen analysis showed mild male factor with a concentration of 15 million sperm/mL. She has a BMI of 25. She has never undergone any fertility treatments before and is interested in undergoing her first cycle of IVF.

A 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5, who exercises regularly, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for improving her core strength. She has no history of hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, abdominal operations or spinal surgeries. She has no known neuromuscular or joint diseases, and she is not pregnant. She is willing to commit to performing abdominal draw-in maneuvers twice a week for six weeks, with or without blood flow restriction.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity and at rest for the past year. Despite being on maximal medication, he still experiences these symptoms. A coronary angiogram shows that he has significant stenosis in his coronary arteries, but he is not eligible for angioplasty or bypass surgery due to diffuse stenosis and small vessels. A pharmacological adenosine-assisted perfusion MRI reveals that he has reversible myocardial perfusion defects. He is diagnosed with severe coronary heart disease and is offered participation in a clinical trial for catheter-mediated endocardial adenovirus VEGF-D gene therapy. The trial aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of this gene therapy in patients with severe coronary heart disease who are not eligible for other treatments. The primary objective of the trial is to assess the safety of the gene therapy, while the secondary objective is to evaluate its efficacy in improving myocardial perfusion, left ventricular function, and functional status. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is interested in participating.

Pt is a 55yo F with a history of breast cancer who has been on an aromatase inhibitor (AI) for the past 2 years. She reports experiencing vaginal dryness and pain with intercourse since starting AI therapy, which has had a negative impact on her sexual health quality of life. She has not used any other treatments for breast cancer such as chemotherapy or radiation within the past 12 months. She has no known sensitivity to medications containing testosterone and has not used exogenous hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in the past three months, including systemic and local estrogen or testosterone therapy. The patient is postmenopausal, or two years since her last menstrual cycle. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of using a daily compounded vaginal testosterone cream for 4 weeks (28 days) on her reported experience of vulvovaginal symptoms accompanying the use of AIs and their associated quality of life and sexual functioning.

A 32-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of itchy, dry patches on her skin, particularly on her arms and legs. She has had these symptoms for the past few months, and they have not improved with over-the-counter creams. She does not have any other known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has not been exposed to any new soaps or detergents. On physical examination, her skin is dry and scaly, and there are patches of erythema and excoriation. A dermatologist confirmed that she has mild atopic dermatitis affecting approximately 3% of her body surface area. She is willing to stop using any topical treatments for at least 14 days before starting the clinical trial. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use a highly effective method of birth control during the study period. She does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus. He has been dependent on insulin therapy for glycemic control for the past 10 years. Despite strict adherence to insulin therapy, he experiences frequent episodes of severe hypoglycemia, which has impacted his quality of life. He underwent pancreatic islet transplantation 6 months ago, and since then, his hypoglycemia has significantly reduced. He is currently insulin-requiring and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the mechanisms of glucose counterregulation in pancreatic islet transplantation. He has no history of type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 30-year-old Japanese male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus for the past 3 years. He is currently being treated with insulin aspart (NovoRapid®) injections and has been on this medication for the past year. The patient has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and is a non-smoker. He has no history of donating blood or plasma in the past 6 months. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any other medications. He has good overall health and is willing to participate in the trial to help advance research in the treatment of type 1 diabetes.

10-year-old female with a history of cleft palate and velopharyngeal dysfunction presents with difficulty with articulation and nasal regurgitation. The patient has undergone speech language therapy without significant improvement. The patient is now scheduled for surgical correction of the VPD with a pharyngeal flap. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial comparing the standard pharyngeal flap to the experimental mucosal/submucosal flap. The patient does not have any syndromic conditions and this will be the patient's first pharyngeal flap surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with a badly decayed right mandibular first molar. The tooth has been causing her pain for several weeks, and she has been unable to eat on that side of her mouth. On examination, the tooth is tender to percussion, and there is evidence of a large cavity on the occlusal surface. The distance from the height of the inter-radicular furcation of the mandibular molars to the mandibular canal is measured to be 12 mm. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of allergies or any significant medical conditions. She has not had any previous dental implants or extractions.

The patient is a 24-year-old man who has been using injection drugs for the past 2 years. He lives in an unstable housing situation and has a history of incarceration. He has not been tested for COVID-19 and is concerned about his potential exposure. He is aware of the risks associated with his drug use and is interested in accessing testing services through the Syringe Services Program. He speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with invasive Aspergillosis or invasive Mucormycosis in Korea. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been receiving treatment for his respiratory issues for the past 5 years. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain for the past 2 weeks. Upon examination, he was found to have pulmonary infiltrates and positive cultures for Aspergillus or Mucor species. He has been informed about the PMS study of Cresemba and is interested in participating. He has provided consent to participate in the study and is willing to follow the routine clinical practice for the treatment of his condition.

78-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and osteoporosis presented to the emergency room after a fall at home. Imaging studies revealed a displaced intertrochanteric hip fracture. The patient is generally independent with ambulation and does not require a wheelchair for mobility. She has no cognitive or language barriers and is able to provide informed consent. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery within 72 hours of admission and is willing to participate in a randomized clinical trial comparing the use of a sliding hip screw or InterTAN intermedullary nail for fixation of her hip fracture.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of hepatitis B infection and cirrhosis. He was diagnosed with a single hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lesion measuring 5.5cm in diameter on an ultrasound scan. He underwent radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for the lesion 4 months ago and the recent follow-up imaging showed no evidence of residual or new HCC lesions. He has no history of extrahepatic metastasis, encephalopathy, or gastrointestinal bleeding. His liver function tests are within normal range, and he has a platelet count of 70,000/mm3. He is currently not on any medications except for a daily multivitamin supplement. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of low-dose thalidomide as an adjuvant therapy after RFA for HCC.

57-year-old male with metastatic cancer, diagnosed with NY-ESO-1 expressing tumor. He previously underwent systemic standard care for metastatic disease, but showed no response or recurrence. He has 2 brain metastases that were treated and are now stable. He has a clinical performance status of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) 0 and

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III melanoma and is currently receiving immunotherapy treatment with a monoclonal antibody that blocks CTLA-4. She has developed a rash on her skin that is suspected to be immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced dermatitis. She is being recommended to undergo skin biopsy as part of routine and standard clinical care. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has measurable disease as per RECIST 1.1. She is not taking any antibiotics currently and has not used any topical or systemic steroids within the past 14 days. The patient is not pregnant and has no medical condition that would increase the risk associated with study participation. She is able to personally sign and date informed consent indicating that she has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study.

A 32-year-old man was involved in a motor vehicle accident and suffered a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) six months ago. He has been experiencing persistent symptoms such as difficulty concentrating, forgetfulness, and mood swings. He has also been having trouble with his balance and dizziness. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any medications. He is fluent in English and has no pending litigation.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with salivary gland cancer that cannot be removed during surgery. He has not received any chemotherapy before. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no other chronic illnesses and has never smoked or used recreational drugs. He is an active individual who exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. The patient presents with no physical symptoms other than a small, painless lump in his neck that was discovered during a routine physical exam. Imaging studies confirmed the presence of a malignant tumor in his salivary gland, which has spread to nearby lymph nodes. His ECOG performance status is 1. His blood counts, liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with advanced adenocarcinoma of the breast with locoregionally recurrent disease. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperthyroidism, both of which are adequately controlled with medications. She is currently on letrozole therapy and has shown partial response to the treatment. She has undergone bilateral mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection in the past. Her local laboratory results indicate ER+ and PgR+ tumor and HER2- breast cancer. She is not pregnant and has no known hypersensitivity to letrozole or its excipients or to any CDK4/6 inhibitor excipients. She has consented to participate in the Post Marketing Surveillance Study to observe the safety and efficacy of IBRANCE®. She understands the study's objectives and has signed the informed consent document.

The patient is a 44-year-old man who has been HIV-positive for the last five years. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the last three years, which has been effective in keeping his viral load undetectable. He has been experiencing pain, tingling, and numbness in his feet for the last six months, which has been affecting his quality of life. He has tried various over-the-counter pain medications and herbal remedies, but they have not been effective in relieving his pain. He has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. He has no history of cardiac disease or seizure disorder. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of acupuncture and amitriptyline in reducing his pain caused by peripheral neuropathy.

John is a 56-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital with a fever of 101.5°F, chills, and fatigue. He has a history of alcohol abuse and was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis 2 years ago. He has been receiving treatment for his liver condition and has not had any episodes of hepatic encephalopathy in the past year. He also has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He denies any recent travel or exposure to sick individuals. Blood cultures were obtained and one was positive for Staphylococcus aureus. He meets two out of four systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria with a heart rate of 98 beats per minute and a respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute. His WBC is 11,800 cells/mm³ with 5% immature neutrophils. He is started on antibiotics and shows improvement over the next several days. He is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial studying immune resolution after S. aureus bacteremia.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital after a motor vehicle accident. He sustained multiple fractures and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. After five days of hospitalization, he developed a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. His chest X-ray showed infiltrates in both lungs, and he was diagnosed with hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP). He has no history of chronic lung disease, smoking, or recent antibiotic use. He is currently receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics for HAP, but his clinical condition has not improved. The medical team has decided to enroll him in a clinical trial to compare different sampling methods for determining the etiological agent responsible for HAP. He is able to provide informed consent and does not have any other exclusion criteria for the study.

32 yo F with a history of asthma diagnosed by a provider with one emergency department visit in the preceding 24 months with a diagnosis of asthma. The patient has health insurance coverage through an Anthem, Inc. affiliate and owns an iPhone 6s or later. The patient is a resident of the United States and comfortable reading and writing in English. The patient has not participated in a prior pilot study investigating the same digital tools, is not currently enrolled in any other asthma or pulmonary studies, and is not currently on any immunologic for asthma. The patient does not have any of the following diagnoses: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Emphysema, Cystic Fibrosis, any malignancy other than a non-melanoma skin cancer, any dementia diagnosis, neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Parkinson's), schizophrenia, or heart failure. The patient is not on dialysis and is not postpartum with delivery in the past 8 weeks.

A 15-year-old male with Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) currently residing at Latham Centers School in Brewster, MA is being considered for participation in a clinical trial titled "Optimizing the Social Engagement System in Prader-Willi Syndrome: Insights From the Polyvagal Theory". The patient has been diagnosed with PWS since infancy and has exhibited behaviors consistent with compromised social engagement system (SES), including difficulties with emotional regulation, socialization, and coordination of suck/swallow/breathe. The patient has normal hearing and vision (corrected) and is fluent in English. He has no history of heart disease, hearing impairment, or seizure disorder. The patient's legal guardian has provided consent for the patient's participation in the study.

A 28-year-old woman came to the clinic for a routine checkup. She is sexually active with her male partner and uses condoms as contraceptive method. She has noticed that she experiences discomfort and dryness during intercourse. She is interested in trying a sexual lubricant to improve her sexual experience. She has no history of pregnancy or breastfeeding. She reports no known allergies or sensitivities to any of the study products. She has a cell phone and internet access and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 35-year-old African American male with sickle cell anemia presents with shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a history of multiple hospitalizations for pain crisis and has been on hydroxyurea for the past 2 years. He was diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension 6 months ago based on an echocardiogram that showed an elevated tricuspid jet velocity of 3.3 m/s. He has been started on sildenafil and bosentan. He has had two follow-up echocardiograms since his diagnosis, and the most recent one showed a tricuspid jet velocity of 2.6 m/s. He has no history of smoking or drug use. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is significant for cholecystectomy due to gallstones. His family history is negative for any pulmonary or cardiac problems. He is currently on folic acid and a daily multivitamin. His Hb level is 8.5 g/dL. He has not had a right heart catheterization yet.

35-year-old male patient involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a two-line mandibular fracture with a parasymphyseal fracture on the left side. The patient has no significant medical history and is fit for the procedure under general anesthesia. The patient has favorable contralateral non-comminuted simple mandibular fracture in the parasymphyseal and angle regions amenable to treatment using intra-oral approach. The patient has sufficient dentition to reproduce occlusion. The patient has no history of occlusion disturbances or skeletal malocclusion. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of single locking miniplate versus two conventional non-locking miniplates in the management of parasymphyseal fractures.

A 10-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with osteosarcoma and underwent surgical resection of the tumor. She is currently receiving chemotherapy and her oncologist has recommended that she undergo additional imaging tests to monitor her response to treatment. She has a history of asthma controlled by albuterol inhaler and no known allergies. She is able to lie comfortably on a bed inside the scanner and has no electrical or ferromagnetic implants.

A 34-year-old female patient was diagnosed with Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder based on the 2015 international consensus diagnostic criteria and a positive test for astrocyte water channel aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody. She has an EDSS score of 5.5 and has experienced at least 2 relapses within the first two years of diagnosis. She has not been treated with rituximab or any other monoclonal antibodies within the past 6 months. Her medical history is unremarkable except for a mild allergy to penicillin. She is currently not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. She has voluntarily signed informed consent to participate in the study.

A 42-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no prior history of cancer. She has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising for the past few weeks. Her physical exam reveals hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. Laboratory tests reveal an elevated white blood cell count, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. A bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of AML with 25% blasts. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she has de novo AML with high-risk features. She has been randomized to receive induction chemotherapy with cytarabine, daunorubicin, and etoposide. She will undergo a second course of therapy with cytarabine IV every 12 hours on days 1-8 and daunorubicin and etoposide as in course 1. She has also been randomized to receive filgrastim (G-CSF) subcutaneously or IV daily beginning on day 1 of each course of induction chemotherapy and continuing until blood counts recover, for up to a maximum of 28 days. She will not receive tretinoin therapy during and following induction chemotherapy. Her quality of life will be assessed at 3 months.

A 22 year old college student comes to the clinic complaining of feeling sad, hopeless and exhausted for the past few weeks. She has difficulty concentrating and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy like hanging out with friends or playing sports. She reports having trouble sleeping and has lost her appetite. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or organic mental disorder. She is not currently undergoing any psychotherapy or taking any psychotropic medications. She meets the criteria for mild-to-severe symptoms of depression and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of emotional working memory training on reducing depressive symptoms.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) according to Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV) criteria. He has been treated with Immediate-release methylphenidate (IR-MPH) for 4 weeks before enrollment, but previous treatment is considered unsatisfactory due to lack of effectiveness. The patient is still attending school and has been taking 10 milligram (mg) IR-MPH daily before enrollment. The patient is able to comply with the study visit schedule and his parents/caregiver and community school teacher are willing and able to complete the protocol-specified assessments. The patient has no serious or unstable medical illness, no clinically significant gastrointestinal problems, no glaucoma, no ongoing seizure disorders, no psychotic disorder, and no hypersensitivity to methylphenidate.

As this is a school-based hand washing program, there are no specific patient descriptions required for this trial. The study will involve children in elementary one and six who attend private primary schools in Mzuzu City, Malawi, with a piped tap water source. The study will require written parental consent for their child to participate in the program. Children whose parents do not give consent, and those who attend government primary schools or schools without piped tap water source will be excluded from the study.

52-year-old male with severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease presents for cardiac surgery with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on metformin, losartan, and atorvastatin for the past 3 years. His preoperative echocardiogram showed a mean aortic valve gradient of 52 mmHg, an aortic valve area of 0.6 cm2, and an ejection fraction of 45%. His preoperative laboratory tests showed a hemoglobin level of 13.8 g/dL and normal liver and renal function tests. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no history of hematologic diseases or blood transfusions in the past 3 months. He is willing to participate in the study and provide blood samples for the measurements of oxidative stress markers and cytokines at different time points during and after the surgery.

The patient is a male or female adult aged 18 years or older who has been experiencing moderate to severe chronic low back pain for at least 3 months, related to nonmalignant and nonneuropathic conditions without radiation or with only proximal radiation (above the knee). They must have been on a stable opioid regimen, equivalent to 20 to 160 mg of morphine for the last 2 weeks prior to the screening visit. The patient must require continuation of opioid analgesic treatment in the range of 40 to 160 mg (inclusive) of morphine or its equivalent daily and be likely to benefit from chronic around-the-clock opioid therapy for the duration of the study. The patient should have an average pain score over the last 14 days and the last 24 hours of ≥ 5 on an 11-point numerical rating scale (NRS) and must be willing and able to be compliant with the protocol, capable of subjective evaluation, able to read and understand questionnaires, willing and able to use a diary per protocol, and read, understand, and sign the written informed consent in English. Exclusion criteria include subjects with acute spinal cord compression, acute compression fracture, seronegative spondyloarthropathy, acute nerve root compression, cauda equina compression, fibromyalgia, reflex sympathetic dystrophy or causalgia (complex regional pain syndrome), diabetic amyotrophy, meningitis, discitis or back pain due to secondary infection, tumor, or postherpetic neuralgia. They also exclude subjects with a history of opioid, alcohol, medication, or illicit drug abuse or addiction, and those who had surgical procedures directed towards the source of chronic low back pain within 6 months of the screening visit or planned during the study. Other protocol specific inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.

The patient is a 32 year-old woman who has been experiencing debilitating migraines for the past 3 years. The headaches are often accompanied by nausea, vomiting and sensitivity to light and sound. The headaches usually last for 24-48 hours and occur 2-3 times per month. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not been effective in relieving her symptoms. She has not used triptan medications in the past. Her current headache care is inadequate and she is seeking better treatment options. She has no known allergies to medications and does not use analgesic medication on a daily or near-daily basis.

Patient is a 65-year-old man from the United States who presents with headaches, jaw pain, and scalp tenderness for the past 2 months. Physical examination reveals temporal artery tenderness and decreased pulsation, and laboratory studies show an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 70 mm/hr. The patient is diagnosed with giant cell arteritis (GCA) and is currently taking 40 mg of prednisone daily. The patient has not been treated with any Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitors or interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibitors in the past. The patient has no history of infections or use of immunosuppressant treatments in the past 6 months. The patient is postmenopausal and not considering pregnancy.

Patient is a 53-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with HER2 positive breast cancer after a routine mammogram. The tumor is clinically T2 and has spread to the axillary lymph nodes. She has no history of other primary malignant tumors or major surgeries unrelated to breast cancer. Blood work shows that her organ and bone marrow function are within normal limits. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a KPS score of 90. Her left ventricular ejection fraction is 60% on echocardiography. She has not received any prior chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, targeted therapy or reflexotherapy for her disease. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old non-smoking female with a body mass index of 25 is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases and her renal function is normal. She has not taken any dietary or herbal supplements within the last six months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the bioavailability of xanthones from mangosteen juice in adult human subjects. She is aware that she will be required to fast overnight for at least 10 hours, and then ingest 2 ounces of 100% mangosteen juice as part of a western-style breakfast. Blood samples will be collected at various intervals over the course of 24 hours, and urine will be collected for the same period. She is willing to refrain from consuming mangosteen-containing products until the final blood collection at 24 hours. She is excited to participate in this study to contribute to the understanding of the health-promoting effects of mangosteen juice.

The patient is a 35 year old mother of a 5 year old boy who had a tracheotomy at 6 months of age due to a congenital airway abnormality. The child has been followed by one of the three participating centers since the tracheotomy was established and has had multiple hospitalizations for respiratory infections. The mother reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious about caring for her child's tracheotomy at home and worries about his health and safety. She has had difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. The father, who is also participating in the study, reports similar feelings of anxiety and depression related to his child's medical condition. The family is hoping to gain insights and support from participating in this study.

62-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, scheduled for an elective colonoscopy due to a family history of colon cancer. The patient reports no prior history of gastrointestinal issues and has not had any prior colonoscopies. She is able to communicate effectively with study personnel and is willing to comply with study requirements. The patient is aware of the nature and risks of the study and has given written informed consent. She does not have any known or suspected liver disease, cardiovascular disease, renal insufficiency, or electrolyte abnormalities. The patient has not had any bowel surgery within the past 2 years or active inflammatory bowel disease. She does not have diabetes or a history of diabetes, nor is she clinically dehydrated. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to abstain from alcohol consumption from one day before colonoscopy until discharged from the study. She is not currently taking any prohibited medications or investigational agents and does not have any known contraindications or allergies to the study medication.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on evaluating the efficacy of a system used to detect medically significant bacteria and yeasts in isolated colonies from various sample types processed by the clinical laboratory. The inclusion criteria for the study states that patients with infections from certain yeasts, Gram positive or Gram negative bacteria can be included. Therefore, the trial does not require any specific patient participation or involvement.

Pt is a 35yo F scheduled for elective rhinoplasty. She has no history of diabetes, motion sickness, or postoperative nausea and vomiting. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no contraindications or hypersensitivity to the study medications. She is an ASA physical status I. She has not taken any antiemetic drugs or steroids within 24 hours before anesthesia. She has been informed on how to use the patient controlled analgesia device during the postoperative period. She has consented to participate in the study and is willing to be randomized to receive either dexamethasone with ondansetron or dexamethasone with dimenhydrinate for prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting.

68-year-old retired female with a history of congestive heart failure (CHF) and recurrent hospitalizations for heart failure exacerbations. She was diagnosed with CHF 5 years ago and has been on multiple medications including beta-blockers and diuretics. Despite optimal medical therapy, she has a limited exercise capacity and experiences dyspnea with minimal exertion. She has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%. She has been hospitalized for CHF exacerbation and is willing to participate in the 6-week EMS training program. She has no significant pulmonary or neuromuscular diseases, has not received inotropic intravenous agents in the past 10 days, and does not have a pacemaker or ICD implant. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to tolerate the electrical stimulation.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who had a liver transplant 2 years ago due to cryptogenic cirrhosis. He is currently under immunosuppressive therapy with tacrolimus and mycophenolate mofetil. He has reported general fatigue and malaise in the past month, but no other symptoms. He has no history of Bartonella infection or any other significant medical conditions. His blood work shows mild elevation of liver enzymes (AST 60 U/L, ALT 70 U/L) and normal bilirubin levels. He has agreed to participate in the study and provide blood, skin and urine samples for analysis. He has signed the consent form and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 15-year-old adolescent diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis. He was diagnosed with CF at the age of 6 based on a positive sweat test and genetic testing. He has been receiving treatment for his condition since then. He has never experienced any signs or symptoms of pulmonary exacerbation, and his pulmonary function test (PFT) has been within normal limits. He is compliant with his treatment regimen and able to perform acceptable and reproducible spirometry. He lives with his parents and attends school regularly. He is an active participant in sports and enjoys playing soccer. He does not have any other significant medical history, and he has not participated in any clinical trials for CFTR correctors or potentiators or gene therapy trials. He is not pregnant.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman, who is currently at 10 weeks gestation, is seeking antenatal care at a primary healthcare clinic in Harare, Zimbabwe. She has had no antenatal care thus far in this pregnancy. She reports no significant medical history and no history of urinary tract infections. She is not on any medications and denies any drug allergies. She is married and lives in a rural area with her husband and two children. She plans to deliver her baby at the primary care clinic where she is receiving antenatal care. She is able to identify the date of her last menstrual period and is willing to participate in the study. She has not received any antibiotics in the past 2 weeks and is not currently on any long-term antibiotic treatment. She has no symptoms of urinary tract infection. She willingly signs the consent form and is enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. She is scheduled to undergo elective surgery in the coming weeks. She has a history of hypertension, high cholesterol, and arthritis. Her current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and naproxen. She is able to perform activities of daily living independently, but reports feeling fatigued and has difficulty walking long distances. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and has no known food allergies. Her BMI is 29.5. Her primary language is English, and she has a basic understanding of French. She is willing to participate in a personalized 4-week prehabilitation program consisting of exercise and nutrition counseling with post-workout whey protein supplementation to improve her functional capacity before surgery.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD and currently takes methylphenidate for his symptoms. He experiences a decrease in appetite and weight loss due to the medication. His parents are concerned about the negative effects of the medication on his growth and development. The boy's past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. His parents are fluent in English and are reliable in keeping appointments for clinic visits and tests.

A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with type I diabetes 4 years ago. She is currently on insulin therapy, requiring 0.8 units/kg/day. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.2%. She has had no episodes of ketoacidosis in the past 6 months and has not experienced any episodes of hypoglycemia requiring the help of others. She has no history of severe gastrointestinal disease, pancreatitis, thyroid nodules or malignancy. She has not participated in any investigational treatment trial within the last 6 weeks prior to enrollment. She has no history of severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease or renal transplantation. She has no known hypersensitivity to Exenatide, Liraglutide or any product component. She is willing to avoid pregnancy during the study period and has provided a signed informed consent. She is eligible for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 10-year-old child residing in the Greater Banjul area. The child is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. The chest X-ray is normal and the Mantoux test result is ≥ 10mm in the widest diameter. The T-SPOT-TB test is positive and the HIV antibody test is negative. The child has no history of previous TB or treatment for TB. There is no clinical case of TB, and the child is not currently participating in any other clinical trial except SCC 1041 and 1034. There is no clinically significant history or evidence of skin disorders, allergy, immunodeficiency, or organ-specific disorders causing immunodeficiency. The child is not likely to travel away from the study area during or for the duration of the study. There is no chronic use (≥14 days) of any oral or systemic steroid or use of other immunosuppressive/ immunomodulating agents. The child is eligible to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the qualitative and quantitative modulation of T-cell responses and clinical disease progression with the supplementation of Vitamin A or placebo.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stable ischemic heart disease six months ago. She has been taking aspirin, statins, and blood pressure medication as per the national guidelines. She has no past history of psychiatric illness and has not been diagnosed with any other chronic disease that significantly reduces her life expectancy or quality of life. Her current medications are well-tolerated, and she has no known drug allergies. She reports experiencing persistent stress, which is reflected by her increased pressure pain sensitivity score of 70 on the chest bone. She has no planned heart operation, and her heart medication has not changed in the last month. She is willing to participate in the study voluntarily and has signed the consent form.

A 55-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with lung cancer at stage IIIA in the pneumology ward of Mulhouse Hospital (France) between April and November 2016. He has no history of any chronic disease and is currently not enrolled in any other clinical trial. He experiences shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. He has been advised to undergo surgery and radiation therapy for his condition, which he is willing to undergo. However, he is concerned about the side effects of the treatment and the management of his symptoms. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the impact of a coordinating nurse in a personalized care program for lung cancer patients. He has no uncontrolled psychological problems and has agreed to participate in the study.

This is a 45-year-old Persian gentleman who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking metformin to help manage his blood sugar levels but has had difficulty adjusting to his new lifestyle and managing his diabetes on his own. He is interested in participating in the Farsi Diabetes Self-Management Education (FDSME) program to learn more about how to properly manage his diabetes and improve his overall quality of life. He is fluent in Farsi and is able to participate in a group program. He is excited to learn more about the program and hopes to gain valuable knowledge and skills to better manage his diabetes.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 24. He has no significant medical history, and his vital signs and physical examination are within normal limits. He has never participated in any other investigational drug trial within the last 90 days. He does not have any history of malignancy, stomach or intestinal surgery or resection. He does not have any significant hypersensitivity, intolerance, or allergy to any drug compound, food, or other substance. He agrees to remain abstinent or use contraceptive measures and refrain from donating sperm during the study. He is not pregnant, lactating or breastfeeding.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of chronic hepatitis C, genotype 2, presents with fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. He was diagnosed with hepatitis C 2 years ago after presenting with flu-like symptoms and was found to have elevated liver enzymes. He has never received interferon or ribavirin treatment before. His liver function tests show elevated AST and ALT, and his HCV RNA level is positive on serum testing. His abdominal sonography is normal, and he has no evidence of liver cirrhosis or other medical conditions associated with chronic liver disease. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for his chronic hepatitis C.

A 55 year old female patient with a history of atrial fibrillation and valvular heart disease is scheduled for elective valvular heart surgery. She has no other significant medical history and is not on any medications. She reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion. Physical examination reveals an irregularly irregular heart rhythm with a heart rate of 85 beats per minute and a blood pressure of 132/78 mmHg. Her respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and her oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. Her chest exam reveals clear breath sounds with no wheezing or crackles. Her abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. She has no peripheral edema. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman receiving long-term warfarin therapy for a history of deep vein thrombosis. She presents to the Anticoagulation Management Service at the University of Alberta Hospital for routine monitoring of her INR. During her visit, she mentions that she is scheduled to undergo a minor surgical procedure in 2 weeks and will need to temporarily discontinue her warfarin therapy. The AMS recommends a "bridging" therapy with low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) during the perioperative period. She agrees to the plan and is advised to stop taking warfarin 5 days prior to the procedure. On the day of the procedure, her INR is 1.2, indicating that the warfarin has been adequately cleared from her system. Following the procedure, she is advised to resume warfarin therapy and is asked to participate in a randomized trial comparing a "loading" dose of warfarin (1.5 times her typical maintenance dose for 3 days) to her usual maintenance dose for restarting warfarin therapy. She agrees to participate in the trial and provides written informed consent.

Patient A is a 15-year-old female who has been experiencing trouble sleeping for the past several months. She has difficulty falling asleep at night and wakes up frequently throughout the night. She reports feeling tired and irritable during the day as a result. She has tried over-the-counter sleep aids without success. She is from a low-income family and has limited access to healthcare services. She has a mobile phone and has access to the internet. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in an online and mobile device delivered sleep intervention. She does not have any current substance use disorder or major medical conditions. She is not currently receiving psychotherapy for her sleep health deficits.

A 45-year-old female diagnosed with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer that has progressed after at least two HER2-targeting treatment regimens or progression after (ado-)trastuzumab emtansine treatment. The patient has measurable or non-measurable disease that is evaluable per RECIST 1.1, ECOG performance status ≤ 2, and an estimated life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient should not have a history of infusion-related reactions and/or hypersensitivity to trastuzumab, (ado-)trastuzumab emtansine, or keratitis. The patient should have adequate organ function and blood cell counts. The patient should not have a history of clinically significant cardiovascular disease or untreated/symptomatic brain metastases. The patient should not have a history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or evidence of active pneumonitis on screening chest CT scan.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male with a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels has been attending the stroke prevention clinic at University Hospital, London, ON, Canada. He is currently taking medications to manage these conditions. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods and saturated fats. He has not experienced any major cardiovascular events but is concerned about his risk of developing atherosclerosis. He is willing to participate in the study and provide stool samples and blood for analysis. He is able to complete the Harvard Food Frequency Questionnaire and has no missing data on variables used in the regression model.

A 55-year-old male with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma, which has metastasized to his liver and lungs, is seeking alternative treatment options. He has undergone chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery, but his cancer has continued to progress. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of less than 6 months. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. His kidney, liver, and cardiac functions are all within normal limits. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent document.
