A 60 year old male patient presented to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and scheduled for coronary artery bypass (CABG) surgery. He was randomized in the RECESS study (NCT00991341) and is eligible for the ancillary study, RECAP. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has provided written informed consent for both studies. The patient has no history of sickle cell disease and has not participated in any clinical trial within the previous 30 days. He is able to be randomized in the RECESS study and is scheduled for CABG surgery.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with early glaucoma in one eye. She has no other ocular co-morbidities and her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She wears glasses for reading and distance vision. Her refractive error is -2.50 DS in both eyes. She has no history of ocular surgery or trauma. Her intraocular pressure (IOP) is well-controlled with medication. She has undergone reliable SAP visual field testing with fixation loss < 33%, false positive < 15% and false negative < 20%. Her optic disc shows glaucomatous changes and SAP MD is not worse than -6dB. She is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of Smart Supra Perimetry (SSP) in identifying early glaucomatous visual field loss.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with moderate severe asthma, who has been using high dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) with long-acting beta-2-agonists (LABA) for at least 4 months. The patient has experienced at least one asthma exacerbation within the past year that required treatment with systemic corticosteroids and/or hospitalization. The patient is not a smoker or former smoker with a smoking history of 10 pack years or more. The patient has a pre-bronchodilator FEV1 of at least 50 percent predicted of normal value and an ACQ-5 score of more than or equal to 1.0 and less than 4.0 at screening. The patient is capable of giving signed informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form and protocol. The patient is also willing to replace their current short-acting beta2-agonists (SABA) treatment with albuterol/salbutamol aerosol inhaler at the start of the study for use as needed. The patient does not have any known pre-existing respiratory conditions other than asthma, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), positive hepatitis C antibody test result, or any known allergy or intolerance to a monoclonal antibody or biologic or to any components of the formulation used in the study. The patient is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or a woman of childbearing potential who is not willing to follow highly effective contraceptive methods. The patient is not a regular user of systemic corticosteroids for conditions including asthma within 3 months prior to screening and does not have any other clinically significant uncontrolled condition or disease state that would put the safety of the patient at risk through study participation or would confound the interpretation of the efficacy results if the condition/disease exacerbated during the study.

This is a 55-year-old male with a past medical history of diabetes mellitus type 2 for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing numbness, tingling, and burning sensations in both feet for the past 6 months. Upon further evaluation, he was diagnosed with diabetic peripheral neuropathy and failed the 5.07 (10g) monofilament test in multiple sites. He is able to ambulate independently without the use of any assistive devices and has no evidence of neurological or orthopedic conditions. He does not have any joint pain, swelling, or limited range of motion in the lower extremities. He has no visual problems that are not correctable with glasses or contact lenses. His passive range of motion is within normal limits. He does not have any severe systemic diseases other than diabetes or its complications, and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His BMI is 27 kg/m2. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves gait training to prevent foot ulceration.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with PTSD. She has been experiencing symptoms for the past six months following a traumatic event. She currently takes birth control pills containing 30mcg of ethinyl estradiol. She has never been pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. She is currently taking medication for anxiety, which has not been effective in treating her PTSD symptoms. She lives with her partner and has a stable job. She is willing to participate in a research study to explore alternative treatment options for her PTSD symptoms. She has no history of breast cancer or hormone-responsive cancer. She does not have any metallic implants or devices that would interfere with magnetic resonance imaging. She does not have a history of self-injurious behavior.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with stage 4 non-small cell lung cancer that has progressed following standard systemic therapy. He has received chemotherapy and targeted therapy in the past, but the disease has continued to progress. The patient has measurable disease with at least one pulmonary lesion measuring more than 1 cm in greatest dimension that would be amenable to SBRT and at least one measurable lesion that would be outside of the SBRT treatment fields. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and no history of brain metastases. The patient has no ongoing or recent use of high dose oral corticosteroids, and has no unresolved CTCAE grade >2 toxicity from previous anti-cancer therapy. The patient has no history of allogeneic organ transplant or autoimmune disease, and has no active malignancy other than NSCLC. The patient has an adequate renal function and blood counts. The patient has signed a written informed consent and is willing to receive a daily subcutaneous injection of CDX-301 (75 µg/kg) for 5 days, beginning on the first day of SBRT. The patient is willing to receive SBRT to a single pulmonary or extrapulmonary lesion, according to the regimen that will be determined by the treating physicians.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with aortic stenosis and is scheduled for elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is not currently experiencing any symptoms related to his cardiac condition. He has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a harsh systolic murmur heard best at the right upper sternal border. His echocardiogram shows severe aortic stenosis with a peak gradient of 80 mmHg and an aortic valve area of 0.7 cm². He has a modified SOFA score of 0. His laboratory tests, including complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, and liver function tests are within normal limits. He is not on any medications that would interfere with the study. He meets all the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria for the study.

A 52-year-old male presents with a history of cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has never smoked and has no significant medical history. A CT scan reveals a mass in his left lung, and a biopsy confirms a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Further genetic testing reveals that he has an EGFR mutation. He is started on treatment with gefitinib and has been continuously receiving the medication for 4 years without evidence of disease progression. He has an overall survival of 6 years from the time of his NSCLC diagnosis. He has provided informed consent to participate in the Gefitinib Long-term Survivor Study to help further understand the genomic profile of long-term survivors and to potentially identify predictive factors for gefitinib long-term efficacy. He is willing to provide archival tumor tissue and blood samples for analysis. He is currently asymptomatic and able to carry out his daily activities without any limitations. He is married with two children and works as an accountant.

The patient is a 55-year-old male resident of rural Wisconsin who has limited knowledge about cancer prevention and screening. He has not undergone any cancer screening tests in the past and is not aware of any cancer prevention strategies. He is interested in learning more about cancer prevention and screening and is willing to participate in educational sessions. He does not have any history of cancer or any other serious medical conditions. He is willing to be surveyed about his intent to change his behavior and his actual behavior changes related to cancer prevention and screening. He is open to participating in a community-based program aimed at reducing rural cancer disparities.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in severe trauma. Upon arrival at the emergency department, the patient presented with a massive haemorrhage and was in haemorrhagic shock. The patient received 3 or more packed red blood cells within one hour and was in need of a massive transfusion. The patient is now scheduled for surgery at the Hospital Universitario de Canarias and therefore meets the inclusion criteria for this study. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of Parkinson's disease for the past 7 years. He is currently taking carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet) but has noticed that the medication is no longer providing adequate control of his symptoms. He experiences tremors in his right hand and arm, difficulty with initiating movements, and occasional freezing of gait. He has been recommended for DBS surgery by his neurologist and has consented to undergo the procedure. He has no history of allergies and does not smoke. His family history is negative for movement disorders. He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He is currently employed as a college professor. His MRI scan shows normal brain anatomy with no significant abnormalities. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the DBS surgery and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to test the effects of Dexmedetomidine on microelectrode recording during the procedure.

A 28-year-old female diagnosed with relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis (MS) 3 years ago is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating the immunologic effects of Prebiotics versus Probiotics in MS. She has been experiencing symptoms such as weakness, numbness, and tingling in her legs, arms, and face. She has been receiving treatment with Ocrelizumab for the past year. She does not have a history of autoimmune disorders, major bowel resection, or any of the active uncontrolled gastrointestinal illnesses listed in the exclusion criteria. She reports having no active relapse or steroid use within the past 3 months and has not taken antibiotics, pre or probiotic supplements in the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in this study to explore alternative treatment options and improve her overall health. She is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) with >10% blasts on bone marrow examination. He had received standard induction chemotherapy, but he failed to achieve complete response (CR) or relapsed after prior therapy. He is not a candidate for potentially curative treatment, and he has not received systemic antineoplastic therapy or radiotherapy within 14 days before the first dose of study drug, except for hydroxyurea. He has no evidence of uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions or clinically uncontrolled central nervous system (CNS) involvement. He is HIV-negative, hepatitis B surface antigen-negative, and has no known or suspected active hepatitis C infection. He has no ongoing anticoagulant therapy that cannot be held to permit bone marrow sampling. He does not use acetaminophen, acetaminophen-containing products, or statins on the day before dosing, day of dosing, and day after dosing with MLN4924. He has no major surgery within 14 days before the first dose of study drug. He is willing to refrain from donating blood for at least 90 days after his final dose of MLN4924 and (for male patients) willing to refrain from donating semen for at least 4 months after his final dose of MLN4924. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He is willing to practice two effective methods of contraception or abstain from heterosexual intercourse. He does not have any serious medical or psychiatric illness. He provides voluntary written consent and has suitable venous access.

58 year old woman presenting with shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue, and occasional chest pain. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and aortic valve stenosis. Echocardiography revealed moderate to severe aortic stenosis with an aortic valve area of 0.8 cm² and mean gradient of 45 mmHg. Patient was evaluated by a cardiothoracic surgeon and deemed to be a candidate for aortic valve replacement. She has provided informed consent to participate in the Aortic Replacement Using Individualised Regenerative Allografts - ARISE (the "Surveillance") study. The patient has no known connective tissue disorders, rheumatic disorders or coronary artery abnormalities. She has no known hypersensitivity to SDS, SDC, human collagen or Benzonase®. She is willing to comply with study requirements and agrees to be followed for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old mother of a 6-year-old boy who has been exhibiting externalizing behaviors such as aggression, defiance, and impulsivity. The mother reports that her son's behavior has been causing significant stress and disruption in their household and has led to strained relationships with family members and friends. She has sought help from her primary care clinic and has been referred to participate in a clinical trial examining the effectiveness of the Comet-program, a Swedish parent training program. The mother is fluent in written Swedish and has access to a computer and/or phone, making her eligible for both the internet-based and group format interventions. She is willing to participate in the study and provide consent for her and her son's involvement. The mother reports no social problems that would require intervention from social services. She is motivated to participate and hopeful that the Comet-program will help improve her son's behavior and their family dynamics.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been experiencing unexplained symptoms for several years. She has been to multiple doctors and specialists, but no one has been able to provide a definitive diagnosis. Her symptoms include muscle weakness, fatigue, difficulty breathing, and episodes of rapid heart rate. She has also experienced unexplained weight loss and has trouble sleeping. She is frustrated by her lack of answers and is interested in participating in the DiRiP study to try to finally get a diagnosis and find appropriate treatment. Her family history is negative for any similar symptoms or conditions. She is willing to undergo genetic testing and additional omics analysis to help identify the cause of her symptoms.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing abdominal pain and weight loss. A CT scan revealed a solid mass in the pancreas. The patient was referred for EUS-guided tissue acquisition for diagnostic purposes. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders and has given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has not been previously diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and has not previously participated in the present study. The patient does not have a cystic lesion and the pancreatic lesion is visible on EUS. The patient is not in an emergency situation and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Multiple Myeloma three years ago. She received an autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) and is currently in partial remission. She experiences persistent exhaustion that affects her daily activities. She is not currently employed and does not work night shift. She has not used light therapy to alleviate fatigue or depressive symptoms in the past. She has no history of bipolar disorder or manic episodes. She has not been diagnosed with any secondary cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and is not planning to travel across meridians during the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and gout. She has been taking allopurinol for the past 6 months, but her gout attacks have not been well controlled. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, and amlodipine. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. She does not have any allergies to medications. She has normal liver function tests and serum albumin levels. Her protein/creatinine ratio is 4.5, indicating significant proteinuria. Her MDRD GFR is 40 ml/min. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or surgeries. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to sign the consent form and participate in the study.

A 28-year-old woman who is 25 weeks pregnant comes to the clinic seeking advice and support during her pregnancy. She is a first-time mother and has been experiencing some physical discomfort and emotional stress. She reports having trouble sleeping due to the changes in her body, and she often feels anxious about the upcoming birth. She has been searching online for information on pregnancy, but she finds it difficult to determine which sources are trustworthy. She is interested in participating in a virtual community of other pregnant women to share experiences and ask questions. She is in good health, has no underlying medical conditions, and has completed a college degree. She is willing to participate in the study and is excited about the possibility of receiving additional support during her pregnancy.

The patient is a 6-year-old child scheduled for an ambulatory surgery under general anesthesia for the first time. The child has expressed anxiety and fear about the upcoming procedure and has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and eating. The child's parent/guardian agrees to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a virtual reality psychological preparation app called Little Journey in reducing peri-operative anxiety. The child and parent/guardian are fluent in English and have access to a smartphone or tablet to use the app. The child has no history of significant visual or hearing impairments that would prevent app use. The child is otherwise healthy and meets the inclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bulimia nervosa according to DSM 5 criteria. She reports experiencing recurrent episodes of binge eating, during which she consumes large amounts of food within a short period of time and experiences a sense of loss of control. Following these episodes, the patient engages in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise in order to prevent weight gain. The patient reports that she experiences significant distress and impairment in her daily functioning due to her symptoms. She has a history of depression and anxiety and is currently taking medication for both conditions. The patient reports that she has tried various treatments for her bulimia, including therapy and medication, but has not experienced significant improvement. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying decision-making in bulimia nervosa and to potentially contribute to the development of new treatments for the disorder. The patient is right-handed and has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders other than bulimia, depression, and anxiety. She is affiliated with the French public health insurance and is willing to sign an informed consent form.

57-year-old male diagnosed with follicular lymphoma, who has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with little success. The patient has experienced multiple relapses and is currently refractory to treatment. He presents with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, groin, and axilla. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial using 131I-rituximab as a potential treatment option.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage III melanoma after noticing a mole on his back that had changed in appearance. He underwent surgery to remove the mole and surrounding tissue, but the biopsy showed that the cancer had spread to nearby lymph nodes. He is currently undergoing treatment with pembrolizumab, a new drug that has shown promise in treating advanced melanoma. However, his doctors have recommended that he participate in a clinical trial to assess the effectiveness and safety of the combination of pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and understands that there may not necessarily be therapeutic benefit from taking part. He is in generally good health, with no history of immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease, and has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG performance scale. He has at least one lesion that is appropriate for high-dose radiotherapy and another lesion that will not be irradiated but must be measurable to assess the abscopal effect of the treatment. He is aware that he will need to attend hospital every 3 weeks for the duration of the trial to check for any side effects of the drug, have routine blood and clinical biochemistry tests, and administer the next dose of pembrolizumab. Additionally, he may consent to have additional tumour biopsies and blood tests for research purposes. He understands the potential risks and burdens associated with the study, including the possibility of experiencing side effects from the study drug and radiotherapy, as well as the need for frequent hospital visits and tests. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial and agrees to use adequate methods of contraception if he is of childbearing potential. He does not have any exclusion criteria for the trial.

A 55-year-old female was admitted to the hospital with sudden difficulty in speaking and weakness on the right side of her body. Her medical history revealed hypertension and high cholesterol. MRI of the brain showed white matter hyperintensities (WMH) on FLAIR imaging, consistent with a diagnosis of a stroke. The patient had no history of multiple sclerosis or other neurological disorders. She has a MoCA score greater than 13 and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no non-organic implants or devices that are not MRI-compatible. She has no history of allergic reactions to gadolinium and does not have any contraindications to MRI. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and appoint a Durable Power of Attorney for NIH research. She is physically able to lie comfortably on her back for up to 1 hour and has no psychological contraindications for MRI. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and does not have renal insufficiency.

A 45-year-old woman presents with frequent nocturnal leg cramps that have been occurring for the past 6 months. She experiences these cramps in her calves and they wake her up at night, causing significant sleep disturbance. She has tried stretching and massage techniques, but they provide only temporary relief. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. On physical examination, palpation of her gastrocnemius muscle reveals the presence of trigger points. Her electrolyte levels are within normal limits and there is no evidence of any musculoskeletal or infectious disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effectiveness of myofascial trigger point injections for the management of her nocturnal leg cramps.

The patient is a 70-year-old female resident of an assisted living facility in London, Ontario. She has been living there for the past 6 months due to difficulty with activities of daily living, such as dressing and bathing. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She takes medications for both conditions, as well as a daily multivitamin. She has reported difficulty with her memory and has answered "yes" to the question of if she has difficulty with her memory. She is able to read, write, and understand English. She scored a 20 on the Mini Mental State Examination. She reports spending most of her day sitting or lying down due to her limited mobility caused by her osteoarthritis. She is willing to participate in a study to reduce sedentary behaviour and improve her cognitive function. She is aware that the study involves taking a 10-minute light intensity PA break three times throughout the day and recording this activity in a diary. She is willing to wear an activity tracker to monitor her adherence to the intervention.

A 25-year-old healthy male presents for a clinical trial assessing the effect of food on the pharmacokinetics of YHD1119. He has a BMI of 22.5 and has not suffered from any significant disease in the past. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has no known allergies to medications. He has not taken any investigational products in the past 3 months. The physical examination shows normal vital signs, including blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate. The laboratory tests and ECGs are within normal limits. He is able to provide a signed written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 56-year-old Caucasian man with newly diagnosed metastatic colon cancer is seeking a clinical trial that will help him with personalised treatment. He has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is married with two children and works as a financial analyst. He has undergone surgical resection of his primary tumour and has completed six cycles of FOLFOX chemotherapy with minimal side effects. His CEA level is currently above the upper limit of normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help him achieve the highest efficacy while minimizing the risk of toxicity. He is willing to provide blood samples on a weekly basis and is open to personalised dosing based on his data. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is an active duty member of the military and has been scheduled for a vasectomy at Nellis Air Force Base. He is generally in good health and has no history of chronic pain medication, benzodiazepine use, or pain management. The patient has a history of anxiety and is interested in exploring alternative methods for pain relief and anxiety reduction during the vasectomy procedure. He has no history of needle shock or blood/injury phobia. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares auricular and body acupuncture to clinic standardized pre-vasectomy medications for pain control and anxiety reduction during the procedure. He understands that he will be required to keep a medication usage diary for the recovery period and complete a patient satisfaction survey 2-4 days after the procedure.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with obesity with a Body Mass Index (BMI) above the 97th percentile of Hernandez references from 1988. He lives in the Tarragona health-care region with his family and has been referred to the clinical trial by his primary care physician. He is in good health and does not have any other endocrine disorders. His family is willing to participate in the study and attend all scheduled visits. The family is interested in learning new approaches to healthy eating and physical activity to help reduce the child's BMI and improve overall health. The child is fluent in the local language and the family is literate.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that overexpresses HER2/neu. She has received initial chemotherapy for metastatic disease and shows at least a partial response with no disease progression. She has no CNS metastases and bone lesions as the only site of metastatic disease, but with evidence of clinical improvement and no new lesions on x-ray. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 90%, and her life expectancy is at least 6 months. Her WBC is at least 2,500/mm3, absolute neutrophil count is at least 1,000/mm3, and platelet count is at least 100,000/mm3. Her bilirubin and SGOT levels are within normal limits, and her creatinine level is less than 2.0 mg/dL. Her LVEF is at least 45% by radionucleotide ventriculogram, and she has no uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina, or congestive heart failure. She has not had coronary angioplasty or myocardial infarction within the past 6 months and has no uncontrolled atrial or ventricular cardiac arrhythmias. Her FEV1 and DLCO are at least 50%. She is not pregnant or nursing and has tested negative for HIV. She has no insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled active systemic infection, other significant nonmalignant disease, or other malignancy in the past 5 years except surgically cured nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She has received prior chemotherapy not exceeding a total cumulative dose of 360 mg/m2 of doxorubicin and no more than 6 standard courses of pretransplant salvage chemotherapy. She has not had more than 3 months of prior weekly taxane therapy and has received no bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplantation. She is eligible for concurrent tamoxifen therapy for estrogen receptor-positive patients who have not received prior hormonal therapy and concurrent pamidronate for bone lesions.

Patient is a 42-year-old man who works as a construction worker. He comes to clinic with complaints of knee pain and difficulty walking for the past 6 months. Upon examination, the patient has a varus malalignment of the leg and intact lateral joint compartment. His ROM in hip, knee and ankle of the affected leg is physiologically age-appropriate. His BMI is 28, and he has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has no known equine protein allergy or immunological abnormalities, and he is not undergoing immunosuppressive treatment. He has no history of active malignancy or systemic disease. He has no metal or metal implants near vulnerable structures, and he does not have a pacemaker or other implanted devices. He is able to provide informed consent.

32-year-old female with a bachelor's degree in psychology and currently employed as a mental health counselor. She has been experiencing decreased psycho-physic state and feels that her relationship with her partner has been strained lately. She is motivated to enhance her own well-being and is willing to make lifestyle changes, including doing exercises related to mental well-being and relationship building. She is familiar with technology and is willing to use technological wellness coaching tools. She does not work night shifts and does not have any acute health conditions or serious diseases. She is not experiencing chronic pain affecting functionality and has not planned any long periods of absence from work during the coaching period. She is not currently participating in any other study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) 2 years ago during a routine check-up. He has not received any treatment for his CLL and is currently classified as Stage I. The patient reports feeling generally well with no symptoms related to his CLL. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has no other significant medical history and reports no allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he hopes that it will provide him with more information about his CLL and whether he will require treatment in the near future. He is willing to undergo the required testing and follow-up visits. The patient understands the study requirements and has the capacity to give informed consent.

The patient is a 38-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain radiating to his back. He has a history of heavy alcohol use and reports experiencing similar episodes of pain in the past. Upon admission, his lipase levels were found to be elevated, confirming a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. He has been receiving opioid pain management but is still experiencing significant discomfort. He is hemodynamically stable with a MAP of 75 mmHg and has received 4 L of IV crystalloid fluid within the first 24 hours of admission. He has no history of heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, upper GI bleed, or inflammatory bowel disease. He has no known allergies to NSAIDs, ketorolac, or aspirin. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time and is able to provide consent to participate in the clinical trial. He meets all other eligibility criteria and is a candidate for the study.

54-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of low-grade non-Hodgkin's B-cell lymphoma confirmed by biopsy. He has not received any previous treatment for the lymphoma including chemotherapy or radiation. His tumor tissue expresses the CD20 antigen as evidenced by immunoperoxidase stains of paraffin-embedded tissue showing positive reactivity with L26 antibody. He has Ann Arbor stage III extent of disease after complete staging. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and an anticipated survival of at least 6 months. His absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is >1500 cells/mm3 and platelet count is >100,000 cells/mm3 within 14 days of study entry. Renal function and hepatic function are adequate with serum creatinine <1.5 x upper limit of normal [ULN], total bilirubin <1.5 x ULN and aspartate transaminase [AST] <5 x ULN within 14 days of study entry. He has bi-dimensionally measurable disease with at least one lesion ≥2 x 2 cm (by computed tomography [CT] scan). He is not pregnant or nursing and agrees to use effective contraception for 6 months following the radioimmunotherapy. He is not concurrently receiving either approved or nonapproved anti-cancer drugs or biologics.

The patient is a Caucasian woman, aged 25-35 years old, who is a resident of New Mexico and works indoors without significant history of prolonged, excessive sun exposure. She has a light skin complexion, and she does not have a diet high in oily fish nor is she taking any oral vitamin D supplementation. She does not use tanning beds and is not pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will complete a daily sun diary and undergo a monthly blood draw for serum measurements. She is interested in learning more about her vitamin D status and the potential risks and benefits of sun exposure in relation to melanoma prevention.

65-year-old female patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with decreased vision in her right eye. She was diagnosed with age-related cataract and recommended to undergo cataract surgery by her ophthalmologist. The patient has no known allergies to medications and is not pregnant. This will be her first cataract surgery. She has consented to participate in the study to evaluate the efficacy of prophylactic administration of the topical NSAID ketorolac tromethamine 0.5% (Acular®) on cystoid macular edema (CME) after cataract surgery.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a complaint of waking up multiple times during the night to urinate. She reports that she has been experiencing this symptom for the last 6 months and it is affecting her quality of life by causing daytime fatigue and irritability. The patient has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or any other medical conditions. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. Physical examination did not reveal any abnormalities. Urinalysis and urine culture were negative for infection. The patient's serum sodium levels were within normal limits. Based on the symptoms and investigation, the patient was diagnosed with nocturia. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial for Minirin Melt in patients with nocturia and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

40-year-old female with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past 24 hours. The pain is located in the right lower quadrant, and she reports a fever of 100.4°F. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, but has a family history of appendicitis. Upon physical examination, tenderness is noted in the right lower quadrant with rebound tenderness. The patient is otherwise healthy with no chronic medical conditions. She consents to participate in the study and is enrolled after meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

A 24-year-old healthy male non-smoker with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and a weight of 60 kg is interested in participating in a clinical trial. The patient has no history of chronic illnesses, drug or alcohol abuse, and has not taken any prescribed medication in the last 14 days or OTC medication in the last 7 days. The patient has no history of heart failure or bleeding disorder and has not suffered significant blood loss in the past 3 months. The patient is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and provide written informed consent. The patient has not taken any study drug in the period 0 to 3 months before entry to the study and has no history of psychiatric illness requiring medications. The patient has a normal ECG and chest X-ray and has normal blood pressure, pulse rate, oral temperature, and respiratory rate.

This is a 48-year-old female who was recently hospitalized at the HFHS Main Campus hospital for an acute coronary syndrome. She has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, but otherwise, she is relatively healthy. She underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and has been referred to the outpatient cardiovascular rehabilitation program at the HFHS Detroit location. She is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the impact of the JHI CR Platform on patient referral, recruitment and retention rates and overall patient satisfaction in cardiovascular rehabilitation programs at the HFHS. She is willing to participate in the study and follow study requirements, including responding to several surveys at the baseline and periodically during the study. She does not have any active substance abuse or unstable psychiatric condition and is able to exercise safely. Her referring physician has not identified any medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

34-year-old female diagnosed with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis with a positive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and has been successfully treated with NSAIDs for the past six months. She experiences moderate to severe pain in the lower back, hips, and sacroiliac joints, along with stiffness and limited mobility. She has no known allergies to NSAIDs and is currently not taking any other prescription medication. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the role of information/expectancies in the response to Ibumetin and placebo. She has a mobile phone and is willing to report her pain and stress levels via SMS as instructed in the study protocol. She understands that she will need to abstain from any other substances that can influence the treatment, such as alcohol, both prescription and nonprescription drugs, and herbal medicine, on the days of the study. She is aware that she will receive placebo during the study period and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She signs the Informed Consent Form and The Data Release Form before inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain, weight loss, and change in bowel habits for several weeks. She has noticed a lump in her lower abdomen and feels discomfort when lying down. She has never had any surgical procedures before and is concerned about the possibility of surgery. She is generally healthy, does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and has no significant medical history. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and answer questionnaires. She is willing to participate in the study and complete the questionnaires.

The patient is a 45-year-old non-smoking female who presented with a history of cough, shortness of breath, and chest discomfort for the past 6 months. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of malignancy. A chest CT scan showed multiple mediastinal lesions with the largest measuring 2.5 cm in diameter. The patient underwent a bronchoscopy procedure to obtain a biopsy for diagnosis. She was randomly assigned to the experimental group and underwent endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) followed by endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial mediastinal cryobiopsy (EBUS-TBMCB). The procedure was successful with no immediate complications. The samples obtained were sent for pathological examination. The patient was followed up for confirming the diagnosis and any potential complications.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male who does not smoke and has no history of chronic medical conditions. He has no allergies or past surgeries. His BMI is within normal range. He is willing to participate in the study as a volunteer. He has been informed about the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She is scheduled to start her first lifetime treatment with paclitaxel. She is fluent in both French and English. She has no history of taking chronic H1 antagonists or systemic corticosteroids. She is capable of giving free and informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has no known allergies or intolerances related to the administration of cetirizine, diphenhydramine, placebo or any ingredient in their formulation. She has not received paclitaxel, docetaxel or paclitaxel nanoparticles linked to albumin in the past. She has mild renal impairment with a Cockcroft-Gault of 60 milliliters/minute. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not receiving paclitaxel under desensitization protocol. She has no documented or reported dysphagia or other pathophysiological condition preventing a tablet from being swallowed whole. She is not taking any medication that may interact with oral cetirizine. She is not participating in another clinical trial simultaneously.

Pt is a 40yo M with a history of end-stage renal disease due to IgA nephropathy. He is scheduled to receive his first renal allograft from a living donor, with a single HLA-mismatch. The donor is his brother. The patient has been on dialysis for the past 2 years and has no history of previous transplants. He is compliant with his medications, including phosphate binders and erythropoietin-stimulating agents. His most recent labs show a serum creatinine of 10.4 mg/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 6 mL/min/1.73m2. The patient has no history of malignancy or chronic active infection. He is not taking any medications that would exclude him from the study. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old woman from Nigeria who was recently diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain for several months. She was referred to one of the participating centers in Nigeria where she underwent clinical and echocardiographic evaluation that confirmed the diagnosis. She is able and willing to return for a 6-month follow-up and has provided written consent to participate in the PAPUCO registry. She has no significant past medical history, is not on any medication, and has no known allergies.

This is a 56-year-old woman who has been experiencing vision problems in her left eye for the past few months. She has been diagnosed with wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in her left eye, which has not been previously treated. She has a best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/100 in her left eye. She has not participated in any other AMD studies or used any other investigational medicines. She has not received anti-VEGF treatment in her non-study eye during the last 4 weeks, and does not have any other retinal diseases that may lead to loss of visual acuity. She has not had any intraocular surgery or laser treatment during the last 3 months. She does not have any serious diseases that may affect her ability to comply with the study's procedures. She has been deemed eligible for the LUCAS (Lucentis Compared to Avastin Study) and will be randomized to receive either bevacizumab (Avastin) or ranibizumab (Lucentis) for the next 2 years. Her treatment interval will be determined using an "inject and extend" protocol, with regular follow-up and injection until the macula is dry. She will be closely monitored for any complications and offered continued treatment after the study is completed.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He has a history of ankle sprains in the past, but this time he fell from a height of about 5 feet while working and landed awkwardly on his left foot. He presents to the emergency department with severe pain, swelling, and difficulty bearing weight on his left ankle. X-rays show a Weber C fracture with associated syndesmotic injury. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not take any medications regularly. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of both treatment options. He is able to provide informed consent and has no neuropathic conditions affecting his left leg.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of high myopia who underwent phakic intraocular lens (pIOL) implantation surgery in his right eye 5 years ago. He has noticed a gradual decrease in vision in his right eye over the past year and has been experiencing frequent eye redness and irritation. His ophthalmologist has recommended pIOL explantation surgery to address the endothelial cell loss in his eye. The patient is willing to participate in a tear and aqueous humour analysis study to explore the molecular background of endothelial cell loss in patients with phakic intraocular lenses. He has no history of ocular comorbidities or immune-compromising conditions and is able to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been a smoker for the past 10 years, smoking at least 10 cigarettes per day. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history or ongoing medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effect of switching from cigarette smoking to using IQOS on exercise capacity. He is physically active but does not engage in vigorous physical activity for more than 45 minutes per week. The patient is not taking any medication that may affect blood volume such as erythropoietin, diuretics, and beta-blockers. His BMI is within normal range (20-25 kg/m2). The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with them. The patient is not a current or former employee of the tobacco industry, nor is any of his family members. He is mentally and physically capable of giving consent and participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and discomfort. Imaging studies revealed the presence of gallstones, and the patient has been scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. The patient has no known allergies or sensitivities to paracetamol and has not taken any oral paracetamol within the past 8 hours. The patient is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent and cooperate with the study procedures. The patient has no serious cardio-respiratory co-morbidities and is suitable for the protocol anaesthetic technique. The patient has not experienced nausea or vomiting with morphine in the past.

A 3-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with symptoms of fever, cough, and difficulty breathing. His parents report that he has been unwell for the past two days and has not responded to over-the-counter medications. On examination, the child appears ill and is febrile with a temperature of 39°C. His lung sounds are diminished and there is mild retractions noted. Blood tests reveal raised levels of white blood cells and C-reactive protein. A chest X-ray shows consolidation in the left lower lobe of the lung. A lumbar puncture is performed, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis is negative for bacterial meningitis but positive for pneumococcal meningitis. The child is admitted to the hospital for further management and treatment. The child is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating Prevnar in the prevention of invasive pneumococcal disease in the Spanish paediatric population.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has just undergone a cesarean section. She has no history of drug abuse and is not hypersensitive to either naproxen or tramadol. She is currently experiencing pain and discomfort and is looking for the best option for pain management. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medication except for prenatal vitamins. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman who has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has not used any nicotine-containing products for at least 3 months prior to the first dosing and throughout the study. She has a body mass index (BMI) between 18.0 and 32.0 kg/m2. She has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse within the past 18 months prior to the first dosing. She has no history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reaction to the study drug, systemic retinoids, fluorescein, or parabens, or to the inactive ingredients in the study formulation. She has not had any ocular surgery or laser within the past 6 months prior to screening, and has no history of herpes simplex keratitis. She has no current ocular conditions that require the use of topical eye drops. She has no macular integrity issues or optic nerve head abnormalities on retinal exam. She has no active seasonal allergies, including ocular allergies. She does not wear contact lenses. She has not taken any drugs known to be significant inhibitors and inducers of CYP3A4 enzymes, including St. John's Wort, for 30 days prior to the first dosing and throughout the study. She has not taken any ocular medication of any kind, including artificial tears, antihistamines, anticholinergics, and/or oral/nasal steroids for 30 days prior to the first dosing and throughout the study. She is willing to refrain from or anticipates the use of any drug, including prescription and non-prescription medications, herbal remedies, or vitamin supplements beginning 14 days prior to the first dosing and throughout the study, unless permitted by the Investigator or delegate.

The patient is a 27-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with schizophrenia according to the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10). He is currently experiencing his first episode and has not received treatment for the condition. He has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism, and has not received a blood transfusion in the past month. He has not been treated with Modified Electric Convulsive Therapy (MECT) in the last 3 months. The patient has no other physical or neurological diseases, and has not experienced any traumatic brain injuries. He is within the age range of 17-40.

This is a 65-year-old male with a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). He was diagnosed with HFrEF 5 years ago and has been treated with a combination of medications including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta blockers. Despite optimal medical therapy, he continues to experience symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. He was referred for echocardiographic evaluation and subsequently underwent echo-guided biventricular pacemaker optimization to improve his cardiac performance. This study aims to compare the baseline and final cardiac performance measures using novel measurements including Doppler and 3D echo diastolic and systolic markers. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for Cohort 1 of the study and has provided consent to have his echocardiogram data analyzed.

Patient is a 16-year-old male who is attending the ECU Pediatric Comprehensive Healthy Weight Clinic for obesity. He has a BMI of 35 and a waist circumference of 40 inches. He enjoys playing video games and spending time online, but he has expressed interest in becoming more physically active. The patient has no major medical conditions, and he is not taking any medications. He is able to read and write in English and is interested in participating in the physical activity intervention. The patient has a supportive family who is willing to help him achieve his weight loss goals.

A 25-year-old female with type 1 diabetes living in Quebec receives an email inviting her to participate in a short online survey regarding her experience living with diabetes during the COVID-19 pandemic. She has been registered in the BETTER registry for the past year. She has been experiencing anxiety and stress due to the pandemic and the restrictions it has imposed on her daily life. She has had difficulty accessing diabetes supplies and has felt insecure about food availability. She is interested in participating in the study to share her experience and potentially help inform policies and resources for people living

The patient is a 55-year-old Hispanic woman who presents to her primary care clinic for a routine check-up. She reports no significant medical history and takes no regular medications. She has never been screened for colorectal cancer and is interested in learning more about the screening options available to her. She prefers non-invasive tests and would like to receive tailored information about the different screening options. She speaks both English and Spanish fluently and is comfortable using touch-screen technology. She has no family history of colorectal cancer. Her vital signs are normal and she appears to be in good health. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study as she is over 50 years of age and has not had a colonoscopy in the last 10 years or completed a fecal occult blood test in the past year.

A 16 year old male who has been admitted to the Child and Adolescent Drug and Alcohol Dependence Treatment Center (CEMATEM) in Istanbul due to substance use disorder. He has been using various substances for over a year and has not participated in any regular exercise training program for the past six months. He does not have a history of psychotic disorder or current psychotic symptoms, physical disabilities or medical problems. He is able to adapt to the evaluation and treatment program. He does not have any respiratory system problems such as bronchiectasis, asthma, and tuberculosis, or infectious health problems such as HIV or hepatitis B. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with the exercise program.

A 32-year-old male with a history of chronic suppurative otitis media presents to the clinic with complaints of hearing loss and persistent ear discharge. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He denies any recent travel or exposure to loud noises. On physical examination, the tympanic membrane is perforated with a limited anterior remnant. The patient reports that the discharge has been dry for the past 3 months. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his hearing and reduce the risk of recurrence of the perforation. His HbA1c is normal, and he has no history of liver or kidney disease. He does not have any immune-compromised conditions. The patient understands the study design and is willing to participate in either the endoscopic double flap or endoscopic single flap group.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with plaque psoriasis by a dermatologist. He has a Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) score greater than 0 and his serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels are confirmed to be less than 60 nmol/L at visit 1. He is not allergic to nuts, does not have primary hyperparathyroidism, granulomatous diseases, or reduced kidney function. His blood pressure is within normal range, and he does not have poorly controlled diabetes or renal stones. He has not been diagnosed with or treated for organ cancer within the past 12 months and is not currently pregnant. He is not using vitamin D supplementation above 800 IU (20 microgram) or active vitamin D drugs, nor has he used phototherapy/light therapy or heliotherapy as prescribed by a dermatologist within the last month before inclusion. He is not currently taking any oral or injection drugs for psoriasis or psoriasis arthritis that could influence psoriasis severity. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of vitamin D supplementation on psoriasis severity and positively influence the cardiometabolic profile and skin microbiota of persons with psoriasis through a winter season.

This is a 10-year-old female diagnosed with Pearson Syndrome, a rare mitochondrial disease characterized by multisystem involvement, including hematological abnormalities, pancreatic insufficiency, and progressive liver disease. The patient has been experiencing episodes of metabolic crisis in the past year and has high baseline lactate levels. She has also been diagnosed with proximal tubulopathy and is experiencing growth retardation. The patient's mother has tested negative for mitochondrial DNA mutations or deletions. The patient has not undergone any previous cell or gene therapy and is not suffering from any chronic severe infections or malignant diseases. The patient is currently transfusion independent and is able to undergo leukapheresis. The patient and her family are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have given their written informed consent.

A 35-year-old male who received his first kidney transplant from a heart-beating deceased donor 6 months ago is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is currently on lymphocyte-depleting induction therapy and was treated with rabbit antithymocyte globulin with a total dose of 5 mg/kg. His cold ischemia time was 25 hours. He has no history of TB or splenectomy. He is not currently pregnant or nursing, and he is not planning to become pregnant during the study period. He is willing to attend all 16 visits required during the 48-week study period. His weight is 70 kg.

A 58-year-old male patient diagnosed with chronic heart failure. The patient has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and diabetes. The patient has not been on statins previously. The patient reports occasional chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. The patient's current medication regimen includes diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is available for follow-up appointments.

A 55-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis presents with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Endoscopy reveals bleeding esophageal varices and he is diagnosed with acute esophageal variceal bleeding (EVB) attributed to his cirrhosis. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of acute hemorrhage from esophageal varices and portal hypertension attributed by cirrhosis. He has not undergone any endoscopic injection sclerotherapy (EIS) or endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) within the past 6 months and has not received any shunt or transjugular intrahepatic porto-systemic stent shunt (TIPS) procedure. His current bleeding episode is not associated with gastric varices and he does not have any severe illness such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), septic shock, cerebral vascular event, acute coronary syndrome, or uremia. He is not allergic to vasoactive drugs and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing tooth sensitivity and difficulty chewing over the past few years. She has been diagnosed with moderate to severe tooth surface loss and has been informed that she requires an elevation of vertical dimension of occlusion by 2-5mm. She has at least one occluding pair of posterior teeth on each side and is class 1 skeletal relation. She has compensated tooth surface loss and is seeking a restorative treatment that is conservative, retrievable, and cost-effective. She is eligible to participate in the clinical trial comparing the use of partial overlay dentures and fixed temporary crowns for the elevation of vertical dimension of occlusion. She will be monitored for symptoms associated with the elevation of vertical dimension of occlusion, such as headaches, muscle tenderness, clenching, grinding, and difficulty in chewing and swallowing. She will also be asked to fill out an OHIP questionnaire to report her satisfaction with the treatment.

45-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 7 years. The patient has been taking metformin 2000mg/day and dapagliflozin 10mg/day for the past 3 months, but has not achieved adequate glycemic control with HbA1c levels of 8.5%. The patient has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is compliant with a diet and exercise program. The patient has no history of secondary diabetes, gestational diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis, diabetic coma, pre-coma, lactic acidosis, or acute or chronic metabolic acidosis. The patient has no history of hypopituitarism or adrenal insufficiency, pulmonary infarction, severe pulmonary dysfunction, or other hypoxemia. The patient has no history of severe infectious disease or severe traumatic systemic disorders. The patient has no history of end-stage renal disease or dialysis. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to galactose, lactase, or glucose-galactose. The patient has no history of liver cirrhosis, chronic active hepatitis B or C, cholecystitis, acromegaly, asthma, or major skin allergies. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of evogliptin when added to ongoing metformin and dapagliflozin combination therapy.

A 15-year-old female high school student has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past few months. Her grades have been declining and she has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has also been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has lost her appetite. She has no history of drug or alcohol use. She is living with her parents, who are willing to accompany her to all assessment sessions and attend parent sessions as prescribed. She has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder by a licensed mental health professional and has not received any prior cognitive-behavioral treatment. She is able to speak, read, and understand English sufficiently well to complete study procedures. She has never been diagnosed with any co-occurring conditions such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. She is not currently taking any psychopharmacologic medications and is willing to maintain her medication regimen throughout the study if prescribed. Her parents have provided consent for her to participate in this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old Asian woman with a BMI of 22. She has no known history of chronic medical illness and is not currently taking any medications that can affect gastrointestinal function. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to milk, egg, or bread. She is able to give informed consent and is interested in participating in the study.

A 45-year-old woman has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 9 months, according to the revised 1987 American College of Rheumatology criteria for the classification of rheumatoid arthritis. She has been experiencing moderate to severe active RA with swollen joint count (SJC) of 8 (66 joint count) and tender joint count (TJC) of 10 (68 joint count) at the time of screening and baseline. Her C-reactive protein (CRP) level at screening was 1.1 mg/dL and her erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 35 mm/hour. She has been taking methotrexate (MTX) 15mg/week (oral) for the past 16 weeks, at a stable dose over the past 4 weeks. She has never been pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning a pregnancy during the Treatment Period of and 12 months after the last infusion of study drug. She has no history of other autoimmune diseases. She has no active infection or history of serious or chronic infection. She has no significant cardiac disease or moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has no allergy or sensitivity to components of the drug vial or any of the materials used for infusion.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the hospitalist service at the University of Michigan Hospital with a fever, chills, and difficulty breathing. He was diagnosed with severe sepsis and was started on antibiotics and other supportive treatments. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is otherwise in good health. He is currently experiencing difficulty standing and walking due to weakness and fatigue. He has been referred to the physical therapy program as part of a clinical trial to determine whether an additional physical therapy program can improve his mobility and functional outcomes. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study and will receive individualized physical therapy treatment in addition to his usual care. The treating therapists have been trained to ensure patient safety and will monitor his progress closely. He will be contacted 30 days after discharge to assess his ability to perform routine tasks at home.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with unstable angina. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking. He underwent coronary angiography, which revealed significant stenosis in multiple vessels. He requires stent implantation to treat the lesions. The target lesion stenosis is greater than or equal to 70%. The lesion is suitable for stenting and OCT imaging. The patient is willing and able to comply with the specified follow-up schedule. He has signed the Ethics Committee approved informed consent prior to undergoing any study-specific procedure. The patient has not participated in any other investigational study that has not completed the primary endpoint or that clinically interferes with the study endpoints. He has negative pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment.

70-year-old male presented to the emergency department after a fall at home. He reported pain in his right hip and was unable to bear weight on that leg. Physical examination revealed deformity and tenderness over the right hip. Radiographic imaging confirmed an intertrochanteric femur fracture (AO classification 31-A1). The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He has no known allergies and is a non-smoker. He lives with his wife and is independent with all activities of daily living. The patient is scheduled to undergo hip fracture fixation with a Gamma Nail by one of four orthopaedic trauma surgeons at William Beaumont Hospital Royal Oak. The patient's mechanism of injury is low energy and he does not have any other injuries to the ipsilateral lower extremity.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with COVID-19. He has been experiencing severe respiratory failure and requires admission to the ICU. His lymphocyte count is lower than 0.6 x 109/L. The patient has a history of hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia but does not have any liver or renal disease. He is not pregnant or lactating and does not have a history of depressive disorder or autoimmune diseases. His body mass index is within the range of 18-25 points. The patient has not undergone any organ or bone marrow transplantation and is not receiving anti-HCV treatment. He has not experienced permanent blindness in one eye or any retinal detachment. The patient's PSA level is less than 3 ug/L, and he does not have nycturia more than three times. The competent physician has considered participation in the study appropriate for the patient.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who was diagnosed with COVID-19 around 6 weeks ago after experiencing fatigue, fever, and shortness of breath. He was hospitalized for a week and received oxygen therapy but did not require mechanical ventilation. He was discharged from the hospital but has continued to experience respiratory symptoms including cough and breathlessness. A CT scan of his chest shows residual changes of post-COVID parenchymal involvement in more than 20% of the lung parenchyma. He is not currently receiving any respiratory support and his oxygen saturation is around 90-92% on room air. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is not pregnant or lactating. He does not have a known history of lung parenchymal disease before his COVID-19 diagnosis. He has no contraindications for prednisolone and is willing to provide informed consent.

This is a 12-year-old female who was diagnosed with T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) approximately three months ago. She underwent induction therapy as part of the COG-AALL0434 study protocol, but unfortunately, her bone marrow biopsy at day 29 showed greater than 25% blasts, indicating induction failure. She has since received additional chemotherapy and is being closely monitored for response. As part of this clinical trial, a bone marrow sample from her initial diagnosis will be analyzed for gene expression and compared with a 116-member genomic classifier to confirm an association between IF status predicted by the classifier and actual induction outcome. Additionally, her sample will be used to explore whether there is an association between early relapse, as defined by bone marrow or extramedullary relapse within 18 months of diagnosis, and previously identified 5-member and 57-member genomic classifiers.

The patient is a 28-year-old transgender woman who has been living as a woman for the past 6 years. She has been on hormone therapy for the past 3 years, taking spironolactone and oral 17-β estradiol, prescribed by a medical provider. She is generally healthy and does not have any history of cardiovascular diseases, diabetes or heart failure. Her BMI is 24.2 kg/m2 and her blood pressure is 118/72 mmHg. She is not currently taking any anti-platelet therapy or anti-coagulant therapy, or any statin therapy. She has not had any gender-affirming hormone therapy within the last 12 months. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential cardiometabolic effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy and hopes to contribute to the knowledge base for the benefit of other transgender women.

A 32-year-old male with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in complete remission after induction chemotherapy. He has a fully matched related donor who is willing to donate peripheral blood stem cells for the transplant. The patient has no significant comorbidities and is physically fit. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or prior malignancies. The patient's cardiac function, renal function, liver function, and pulmonary function are all within normal limits. There is no evidence of active bacterial, viral, or fungal infections. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent and is committed to complying with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease 4 years ago. He has been experiencing worsening symptoms including tremors, slow movement, and difficulty with balance. He is currently taking carbidopa-levodopa and has been on a stable dose for the past 6 months. The patient is willing to remain on this medication for the duration of the study. Despite medication, the patient still experiences fluctuations in his motor function throughout the day. He has not undergone any previous surgeries or treatments for Parkinson's Disease. The patient has no history of suicide attempts or symptoms of impulse control disorder.

52-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C presents with refractory ascites, requiring frequent large volume paracentesis. He has no history of hepatic encephalopathy or spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. His current medications include lactulose, spironolactone, and furosemide. He denies alcohol use but has a significant history of tobacco use. His most recent laboratory values are as follows: total bilirubin 3.5 mg/dL, INR 1.8, serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, and serum sodium 131 mEq/L. The patient has been stable on his current medications for the past 3 months, and his recent ultrasound showed no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma. He has no known allergies or hypersensitivities to terlipressin. He is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to have a continuous infusion of terlipressin administered via an ambulatory pump for a total of 28 days.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing diarrhea predominant IBS symptoms for the past 3 years. She describes her pain intensity as a 5 on a visual analog scale (VAS). She has not taken any antibiotics in the past month and does not have any known digestive or severe non-digestive organic diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the efficacy of Lactobacillus FARCIMINIS in improving her IBS symptoms.

The patient is a 78-year-old woman who has been living in a nursing home for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and has moderate to severe impairment in her daily decision-making abilities. She often exhibits agitated and aggressive behaviors, which can be difficult for the nursing home staff to manage. The patient's family has been consulted to identify music that the patient may have preferred when she was younger. The patient is able to hear and has shown some interest in music in the past. She has not previously participated in the Music and Memory program. The patient is generally in good health, with no major medical conditions or disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the trial.

45-year-old female with chronic low back pain for the past 8 months, with a numerical pain scale between 4-7 cm. The pain is worse with prolonged sitting and standing and is relieved with rest. She has no history of inflammatory or rheumatological diseases, tumors, infections or vertebral fractures. She is not currently involved in any litigation and does not have fibromyalgia or any symptomatic musculoskeletal diseases in lower limbs. She has no symptomatic diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system, or diabetes mellitus. She has no rigid deformities in her foot and has not used insoles in the last three months. She has not undergone medical or physiotherapeutic treatment for low back pain or any problem in lower limbs in the last three months. She has not changed physical activity or undergone physical therapy in the previous 3 months. She is not pregnant and has no difference in lower limb length greater than 2 cm. She has not had lumbar spine, lower limb or abdomen surgery in the previous 6 months and has not undergone previous spinal surgery or spinal infiltration for pain relief in the last 3 months. She does not have serious scoliosis and is not allergic to the material of the insole. She does not have any planned travel in the next 12 weeks and has geographic accessibility.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia, characterized by sweating, tremors, confusion, and blurred vision. The symptoms improve with the intake of glucose. She has gained about 10 kgs in the last six months due to increased appetite. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and she is on medication for the same. She is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. Her family history is negative for diabetes. The blood glucose levels during the hypoglycemic episodes were found to be less than 2.8 mmol/L. Endocrine workup revealed an elevated serum insulin level during the symptomatic period. Imaging studies showed a solitary pancreatic lesion, raising suspicion of insulinoma. She has no gastrointestinal dysfunction and has no known allergies.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been experiencing blistering and itching on her skin for the past year. She has noticed the appearance of fluid-filled blisters that rupture easily, leaving painful and raw areas on her skin. The blisters tend to appear in clusters on her arms, legs, and abdomen. She has sought treatment from her primary care physician, who referred her to a dermatologist. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. She has no known allergies. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is under the care of the dermatology referral center in Reims.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no known psychiatric or neurological disorders. He is a graduate student studying psychology and is interested in participating in research studies. He has completed a self-reported State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and is found to have high trait anxiety. He is willing to participate in a study examining the effects of oxytocin on behavior and neural activity in males with high trait anxiety. He reports no history of head trauma, substance abuse, or medication use. He is comfortable with undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scanning and completing various questionnaires related to his emotions, empathy, and anxiety. He understands the study's potential risks and benefits and is willing to comply with the study's protocol.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She completed trastuzumab treatment for 1 year and then participated in a phase I study of lapatinib and trastuzumab combination therapy.
