She had a partial response to treatment and continued on lapatinib monotherapy after completing the study. She has been on lapatinib for 6 months with no significant side effects. She is interested in participating in the rollover study to continue lapatinib treatment until it is approved by the FDA. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol-specific birth control measures. She has no history of heart disease or other significant medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol.

45-year-old male admitted to the hospital with sepsis and septic shock. The patient has a history of hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He presented with fever, chills, and shortness of breath, and was found to have pneumonia on chest X-ray. Despite initial fluid resuscitation, the patient remained hypotensive and required vasopressors to maintain a mean arterial pressure > 65 mm Hg. His lactate level was > 2 mmol/L. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has not taken any vitamin C or thiamine supplements prior to enrollment. He is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing numbness and tingling in her right hand. She works as a typist and spends long hours typing on her computer. She has a past medical history of asthma, but it is well-controlled with medication. She is not currently taking any medications for pain or anxiety. She is married with two children and is an active member of her community. She enjoys gardening and attending her children's sports events. She has never undergone surgery before and is a bit anxious about the procedure. She is scheduled to undergo surgery to repair a broken bone in her right hand.

The patient is a 45-year-old overweight man who has struggled with his weight for many years. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. He has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about how his gut microbiota may be affecting his metabolism and weight. He is willing to undergo rectal administration of SCFA and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who lives in the Portland Metropolitan Area and has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) for 3 years. Her type of MS is relapsing-remitting. She is currently taking disease-modifying medication and balance medications. She is able to walk 50 feet without assistance but experiences difficulty with balance and gait. She reports feeling fatigued and has been experiencing decreased quality of life due to her MS symptoms. She has not participated in qigong, tai chi, or yoga in the last 6 months. She is not pregnant or nursing and has not had an MS relapse in the last 30 days. She is interested in participating in community qigong classes to explore alternative therapies for her MS symptoms.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of high blood pressure that was first detected during a routine check-up. She has a family history of hypertension, but no other cardiovascular risk factors such as smoking, high blood pressure, and diabetes mellitus and is physically active. The patient's blood pressure readings have been consistently high, with the latest reading at 148/92 mmHg. Her fasting glucose and triglyceride levels (85 and 102 mg/dL, resp.) were within normal limits. The patient reported no use of antihypertensive medications. She is proficient in reading, comprehension, and expression skills and owns a smartphone. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve her knowledge and behavior regarding hypertension, treatment compliance, and self-health management using an outpatient chronic disease health management platform.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who presented with abnormal vaginal bleeding and was subsequently diagnosed with cervical cancer. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has a BMI of 25 and is a non-smoker. She has two children and is not planning to have any more pregnancies in the near future. She has no history of any autoimmune diseases, digestive system diseases, or any other medical conditions that could interfere with the study results. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old Samoan woman who is concerned about her health and weight. She has four Samoan grandparents, and her BMI is 34.6 kg/m2. She is physically inactive according to the WHO Global Physical Activity Questionnaire, and she is motivated to make behavior changes to improve her health. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the 5-week study period. Her weight is less than 180 kg, and she does not have any medical conditions that would prevent physical activity or make participation inadvisable. She does not have a history of significant weight loss (>10 kg) in the last 6 months. She is interested in using step counting devices (FitBit Zips) and scales (BodyTrace) to self-monitor physical activity and weight. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

Pt is a 45yo M with a history of smoking for 20 years, hypertension, and a family history of premature heart disease. He presents with chest pain, shortness of breath, and sweating. He reports a history of occasional angina-like chest pain, but this episode is the longest and most severe he has experienced. On exam, he has a blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg, a regular heart rate of 90 bpm, and bilateral basal crackles on lung auscultation. An electrocardiogram reveals ST depression in leads II, III, and aVF. Labs reveal elevated troponin levels. The patient is diagnosed with unstable angina and admitted for further management. The patient consents to participate in the study and is enrolled after meeting inclusion criteria.

Patient A is a newborn baby boy, born at a participating center in the Rhone Alpes Auvergne region. He was born full term, weighing 3.2 kg, to parents who also reside in the same region. The parents have consented to participate in the study. The study will follow the baby for up to 1 year, during which time he will be monitored for any respiratory symptoms that could be associated with RSV infection. The study will also collect a blood sample from the baby's umbilical cord at birth for analysis of RSV-specific antibodies. The objective of the study is to determine the main predictors of RSV hospitalization in infants, including socio-demographic factors, clinical risk factors, level of cord-specific antibody at birth, and virus characteristics. The study hopes to provide valuable information to guide future vaccine policies aimed at preventing RSV infection.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of obesity and elevated blood pressure. She has also been experiencing high levels of blood sugar and cholesterol. The patient has a waist circumference of 105 cm and a fasting blood glucose of 120 mg/dl. Her blood pressure measures 140/90 mmHg, and her triglyceride levels are 180 mg/dl while her HDL cholesterol is 35 mg/dl. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes, hepatic failure, or heart failure. Her creatininemia is within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her metabolic syndrome and reduce her risk of cardiovascular events.

The patient is a 16-year-old high school student who is visiting their primary care physician for their annual check-up. They are generally healthy, with no chronic medical conditions or significant past medical history. They report feeling stressed due to school work and extracurricular activities but have no other significant emotional or behavioral concerns. The patient is fluent in English and is able to comfortably communicate with their physician. They are comfortable using technology, including iPads and audio recording devices. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve communication between adolescents and their healthcare providers regarding behavior change. They are willing to complete surveys and questionnaires as part of the study and are comfortable with audio recording their conversations with their physician.

A 26 year old woman has been struggling with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 3 years. She has been taking antidepressant medication for the past 2 years but has not seen much improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study inflammation in the brain of people with MDD. She has no current serious medical condition and is able to give written informed consent. She has not been diagnosed with drug or alcohol dependence. She has no history of seizures or brain damage from head trauma, and her MRI scan does not show any brain abnormalities. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and uses birth control. She is willing to undergo a PET scan and an MRI scan after providing blood samples for the study. She is aware of the potential risks associated with the scans and is not claustrophobic. She is a non-smoker and has not been exposed to radiation in the past. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating to help further the understanding of the role of inflammation in MDD.

A 55-year-old male patient diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus approximately 10 years ago. He has been on stable glycemic control during the last 3 months with metformin and gliclazide. He has been suffering from painful distal symmetric sensorimotor polyneuropathy due to diabetes for the last 2 years, which is also confirmed by a DN4 score of 6. The patient has been experiencing pain with an average NRS score of 7 and a worst NRS score of 9 for the past 2 weeks. He has been compliant with diary data and has satisfactory diary data during the 14-day Pain Observation period. The patient has no other neuropathy or pain conditions that could confound the study results. He has no history of suicidal ideation/behavior or opioid use disorder. The patient has not used marijuana or cannabidiol (CBD) during the 30 days prior to starting study drug. The corrected QT interval at Screening was within normal limits, and the patient has no hematological abnormalities or chronic infections. He has not been exposed to COVID-19 or shows any symptoms of COVID-19 infection.

A 52-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer has been scheduled for chemotherapy treatment with cisplatin-containing regimen or doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. She has no prior history of chemotherapy for any malignancy and is physically fit with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has not experienced any nausea or vomiting in the last 24 hours and has negative pregnancy test results. She does not have any known diagnosis of dementia or central nervous system disease. The patient has not received any antipsychotic agents such as olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, clozapine, phenothiazine or butyrophenone within 30 days prior to registration. She has no history of uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, or acute myocardial infarction in the previous six months. The patient's serum creatinine is within normal limits, and her AST or ALT levels are below three times the upper limit of normal. She speaks and understands English fluently and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on the evaluation of web-based training for physicians to interpret florbetapir-PET scans. The trial will use scans from previous studies with subjects who had Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, or were cognitively normal volunteers, as well as an autopsy cohort.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis for the past 8 years. She has been experiencing foot drop which affects her walking and increases her risk of falls. She is currently using a walking stick to aid her mobility. She has a history of relapse in the past year but has been stable for the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES) for foot drop. She is able to walk for at least 2 minutes with or without walking aids. She has no known allergies to adhesive tape. She is willing to attend two appointments at Slateford Medical Centre to fit the FES unit and to participate in data collection. She is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo adjuvant chemotherapy as part of her treatment plan. She has no history of cranial radiation, brain surgery, or intrathecal therapy. She is fluent in English and can provide informed consent. She reports no prior history of cancer or neurological disorders. She has been experiencing some difficulties with memory and concentration since her diagnosis and chemotherapy is expected to exacerbate these symptoms. She is not currently taking any psycho-stimulant or CNS depressant medication. She is taking venlafaxine for her depression, which is well-controlled. She has not had a Mini-Mental Status Examination but reports no significant issues with cognitive functioning at present. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how to manage her cognitive symptoms during cancer treatment.

This is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and chest pain. Upon evaluation, the patient was diagnosed with acute heart failure and was admitted to the hospital. During the hospitalization, the patient received diuretic therapy and was closely monitored for signs of fluid overload. At the time of discharge, the patient's symptoms had improved, and he was deemed ready for discharge. However, to prevent readmission for exacerbation of HF within 30 days, the patient was enrolled in the HOPE-HF study, which will use a lung impedance device to monitor lung fluid accumulation and assess the patient's readiness for discharge. The patient has not had a cardiac resynchronization device implanted during the current hospitalization, and his estimated glomerular filtrating rate is above 30 ml/min, making him eligible for the study.

A 68-year-old male patient presents with a long-standing history of osteoarthritis and chronic hip pain. He was recently diagnosed with primary total hip arthroplasty by his orthopedic surgeon and has been scheduled for surgery next month. He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is an ex-smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and does not drink alcohol. He is independent in his activities of daily living and has no history of dementia. He reports occasional low back pain but denies any other significant medical or surgical history. He has been informed about the study and is interested in participating to help improve postoperative pain management for future patients.

32-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of Gaucher disease, currently enrolled in the ICGG Gaucher Registry. She is 16 weeks pregnant and seeking to participate in the Gaucher Pregnancy Sub-registry. The patient has previously received enzyme replacement therapy and is currently being managed by her treating physician. She has a history of mild anemia and bone pain, and her most recent bone density scan showed osteopenia. The patient understands the nature of the study and has provided signed informed consent to participate in the sub-registry. She is willing to provide information about her medical and obstetric history, pregnancy, and birth, as well as consenting to data collection for her infant's growth through month 36 postpartum.

The patient is a 54-year-old female with a history of degenerative disc disease and chronic low back pain. She has tried multiple conservative treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and epidural steroid injections without significant improvement. She has no significant medical history and takes only occasional over-the-counter pain medication. On physical examination, she has tenderness to palpation over the lumbar spine and limited range of motion. Imaging studies reveal multilevel degenerative disc disease with loss of disc height and facet arthropathy. She is scheduled for thoracolumbar spinal fusion surgery and has available preoperative standing lateral radiographs. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the conditions of enrollment.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent knee pain for over a year, which has limited his daily activities and mobility. He has been diagnosed with AMOA of the knee and his doctor has recommended either Open Wedge HTO or primary unilateral partial knee arthroplasty with Oxford Partial Knee with Microplasty® instrumentation. Patient B has undergone either of these procedures within the last year and is willing to participate in the Oxford UKA and HTO Post-market Clinical Study to compare the performance and safety of these two procedures. He is able to provide written informed consent and is not diagnosed with any systemic disease that could affect his safety or the study outcome.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiotherapy with a radiation dose of 68-72 Gray. He has developed grade II oral mucositis as a result of the treatment, which is causing him discomfort and difficulty in eating and speaking. He has a Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) of 80, indicating that he is able to carry out most activities of daily living with some difficulty. He has no known allergies to medications, and he is not currently experiencing diarrhea or any other severe infections. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written consent for the specific procedures involved in the protocol. He is interested in finding a way to manage his oral mucositis and hopes that this trial will offer a solution.

A 35-year-old woman residing in the schistosomiasis affected area of Napu is seeking participation in the clinical trial. She has been living in the area for the past 10 years and has not been diagnosed with schistosomiasis before. She has not experienced any symptoms related to schistosomiasis such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, or blood in the urine. The patient has two children, ages 5 and 8, who have also not been diagnosed with schistosomiasis. She is willing to provide informed consent for herself and assent for her children to participate in the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study procedures and agrees to the collection and storage of specimens. She has no known history of any medical conditions and is not taking any medications at this time.

58 year-old Hispanic woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. She has been treated with insulin injections for the past year in combination with metformin. She has a BMI of 35 kg/m^2 and has not used GLP-1 receptor agonists, thiazolidinediones or dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors in the past 3 months. She has no history of multiple or severe allergies to drugs or foods and has not donated blood or plasma in the past month or more than 500 mL within the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of NN1250 in subjects with type 2 diabetes of different race and/or ethnic origin.

The patient is a 60 year-old man who suffered a stroke six months ago which resulted in hemiparesis on the left side of his body. Although he is able to walk without physical assistance, his walking speed is less than 1.0 m/s. He has no other cardiopulmonary, metabolic, neurological or orthopedic injuries that may affect his ability to walk. He takes medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He is retired and lives with his spouse. He enjoys gardening and taking walks in his neighborhood. He is interested in participating in a study to improve his walking ability and overall health.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. She has never been diagnosed with coronary artery disease, but is concerned about her risk for heart problems. She was referred to the diabetes department at Pitié-Salpêtrière hospital in Paris for a one-day hospitalization to assess cardiovascular comorbidities. During her hospitalization, she underwent a toe-brachial index measurement, which was found to be within the normal range. Her coronary artery calcium score was also measured and found to be elevated. She has no history of Raynaud's syndrome and has not opposed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is generally healthy and physically active. He participates in regular exercise and is not experiencing any muscle-related complaints such as numbness, spasm, or atrophy. He does not have any history of musculoskeletal, nervous system, or peripheral blood diseases, severe trauma to the lower limbs, or acute inflammation or bone fractures. He has normal joint mobility and muscle tension and does not have severe osteoporosis. He is between 18-55 years of age and is willing to participate in a study that aims to develop a new method of muscle strength testing using quantitative ultrasonic technology and a convolutional neural network. He understands that there will be an isokinetic muscle strength test and that ultrasound imaging will be used to measure muscle thickness, average echo intensity, and the level of muscle hyperemia.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with recurrent ovarian epithelial cancer. She has previously undergone primary therapy and one second-line therapy but has experienced a relapse. Her histologic cell type is serous adenocarcinoma. She has detectable disease in the form of baseline values of cancer antigen (CA)-125 at least twice the upper limit of normal. Her Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) performance status is 1. She has recovered from the effects of recent chemotherapy and surgery. She currently takes Flomax for her BPH. Her absolute neutrophil count is greater than or equal to 1,500/mcl, platelets are greater than or equal to 100,000/mcl, creatinine is less than or equal to institutional upper limit of normal (ULN), bilirubin is less than or equal to 1.5x ULN, serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) is less than or equal to 3x ULN, alkaline phosphatase is less than or equal to 2.5x ULN, and neuropathy (sensory and motor) is less than or equal to the NCI CTCAE version 4 grade 1. She has not had prior therapy with bortezomib, and she has not received prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy for any abdominal or pelvic tumor other than for the treatment of ovarian cancer. She is not pregnant and is practicing an effective form of contraception.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian male complaining of progressive knee pain and stiffness for the past two years. He states that his symptoms have significantly affected his daily activities, especially walking and climbing stairs. He has a history of osteoarthritis in his right knee and has unsuccessfully tried conservative treatments such as physiotherapy and pain medications. He is willing to undergo total knee replacement surgery and has agreed to participate in the study. He does not have any significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not have any allergies. He is married and has two adult children. He is retired and used to work as a construction worker. He is physically active and used to enjoy playing sports before his knee pain started. He has a BMI of 32. His knee alignment is within the inclusion criteria. His preoperative classification according to ASA is 2.

A 25-year-old female with a known peanut allergy, confirmed by skin-reactivity testing and sera testing for specific IgE, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She is not currently taking any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, aspirin, beta-blockers, or angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. She has not taken any antihistamines within the last 5 days, and has not received oral corticosteroids within the last 14 days. She is scheduled for a diagnostic food challenge and is willing to participate in the study. She has signed an informed consent form and has no significant co-morbidities. She is not pregnant and has no uncontrolled asthma or risk of severe food-induced anaphylaxis.

42 yo F with confirmed BRCA2 mutation via genetic testing, seeking a better understanding of risk reduction strategies and support in making informed decisions about cancer prevention. She is currently receiving regular follow-up care with her primary care physician and has no history of ovarian cancer. She has never undergone bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and is not currently pregnant nor has she given birth in the last 6 months. She is fluent in English and interested in participating in a follow-up telephone-based genetic counselling intervention to receive ongoing guidance and support from a professional about the latest risk reduction strategies. Past Medical History: - Family history of breast and ovarian cancer - No personal history of cancer

28yo pregnant woman in her third trimester, living with HIV, with a history of good compliance with antiretroviral therapy. She presents for routine prenatal care and is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing a vaccine against Group B Streptococcus (GBS). She is a non-smoker, has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and has not received any vaccine in the last 28 days. She has no known allergies to any vaccine components and has not experienced any significant illness within the past 4 weeks. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated thus far, with no history of hypertension, diabetes, or proteinuria. She is willing to be contacted by telephone during the study and is open to having her infant participate in the study as well. She is seeking to contribute to medical research and help protect her newborn from GBS.

The patient is a 19-year-old student attending a pre-graduate education center in Mexico City. They regularly use their smartphone for various activities, including social media, messaging, and browsing the internet. The patient reports experiencing occasional feelings of sadness and anxiety, particularly related to academic stress and pressure to succeed. They deny any thoughts of self-harm or suicide but acknowledge that they have struggled with depression in the past. The patient is interested in participating in the study and agrees to download the MeMind app to complete the self-administered questionnaire. They understand the purpose of the study and have given their informed consent to participate. The patient has no history of legal issues or guardianship.

A 48-year-old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital is seeking help for her chronic pain that has been affecting her daily life for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia and has undergone multimodal pain rehabilitation in the past but still experiences residual emotional problems such as depression and anxiety. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is married and has two teenage children. She exercises regularly but has been limited by her chronic pain. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is fluent in reading and writing Swedish and has access to the internet. She has not received any psychological treatment from a psychologist or psychotherapist in the past year.

52-year-old woman presented with progressive fatigue, weight loss, and edema in her legs. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly and peripheral edema. Lab findings showed an elevated serum creatinine level and proteinuria. Renal biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of AL amyloidosis. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has an ECOG score of 1. She has adequate residual organ function and no history of multiple myeloma, peripheral neuropathy, or hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron or mannitol. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

A 45-year-old woman with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis is experiencing moderate to severe pain, swelling, and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and ankles. She has been on methotrexate for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have not improved. She is currently taking NSAIDs for pain relief. She has a history of hypertension and is taking medication for it. She has no allergies to any food or drugs. She has never been pregnant and is currently practicing birth control. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has not received any live vaccines in the past 3 months. She has not used any experimental/investigational biologic DMARD in the past 3 months. She is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all study visits.

A 65-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease complains of progressive cognitive decline, including problems with memory, language, and executive functioning. He reports difficulty with day-to-day activities, such as managing finances, shopping, and cooking. He has a reliable informant, his wife, who accompanies him to all appointments and provides information about his daily activities. He has undergone extensive psychometric testing and has a Mini Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of 13 and a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) of 2. He has no other medical conditions that could account for cognitive deficits. He takes medication for hypertension, but no medication that could affect CNS functions, such as benzodiazepines or neuroleptics. He has no history of head trauma or substance abuse.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. She has previously received treatment with a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor, but has experienced disease progression. She has measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 and has known HPV status. Her performance status is either 0 or 1 and she has reasonable organ function as defined in the eligibility criteria. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial. She is not currently participating in another study and has not received investigational therapy within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of treatment. She does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. She does not have a known history of active TB (Bacillus Tuberculosis). She is not hypersensitive to pembrolizumab, epacadostat, or any of its excipients. She has not received prior therapy with an IDO inhibiting agent. She does not have a known history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) (HIV 1/2 antibodies) or active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C. She has not received a live vaccine within 30 days of planned start of study therapy. She does not have a history or presence of an abnormal electrocardiogram (ECG) that, in the investigator's opinion, is clinically meaningful.

45 yo male with a history of hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism. Has not received any prior treatment for this condition. The patient does not have any history of chronic metabolic disorders. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial to study the effects of testosterone replacement therapy on endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and insulin resistance. The study aims to compare the effects of daily transdermal testosterone implementation and intramuscular injection over three weeks. The patient is interested in participating in the study to contribute to scientific research and explore potential benefits of testosterone replacement therapy.

Pt is a 40yo M diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia in chronic phase. He has been on Imatinib for the past 6 months but has not achieved complete cytogenetic response. He presents with fatigue, malaise, and low-grade fever. CBC shows leukocytosis with white blood cell count of 40,000/μL, and differential reveals 20% blasts. Bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of chronic myelogenous leukemia in chronic phase. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is currently off any antileukemic therapy and has been off hydroxyurea for more than 2 weeks. The patient is not pregnant, and effective contraception will be used throughout the trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian man who recently underwent a prostate biopsy that showed a newly diagnosed prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 7. His PSA level is 42 ng/mL. He has no history of non-cutaneous malignancy in the past 5 years. He is scheduled to have his prostate cancer consultation as his first consultation after diagnosis. He is currently not enrolled in any clinical trial for the treatment of cancer, but he is willing to participate in biospecimen studies. He has no history of impaired decision-making capacity, and he is able to read and comprehend English. He is married with two children and is retired. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. He is otherwise healthy and active, regularly engaging in physical activities such as walking and gardening. He is concerned about his prostate cancer diagnosis and is looking for more information and guidance to make informed decisions about his treatment options.

A 25-year-old pregnant woman with a history of opiate dependence presented to the Faculty Medical Center for prenatal care. She has been sober for 6 months and is receiving treatment for her addiction. She was recently diagnosed with Hepatitis C and is concerned about the impact it may have on her pregnancy and her future health. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study to learn more about the disease and how to manage it. She hopes to gain knowledge that will help her protect her baby and improve her own health.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy who has been consistently shorter than his peers. He has no significant medical history or family history of growth disorders. He has not been treated with growth hormone therapy in the past. His height measurements taken in the past 6 months show that he is below the 3rd percentile for his age and sex. He has normal thyroid function and normal karyotype. He has not yet entered puberty and his bone age is less than 10 years old. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the study.

59-year-old male with a history of pancreatic cancer and previous radiation therapy presents with a new liver metastasis. A biopsy confirmed the metastasis, and the patient is scheduled to receive radiation therapy. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80, indicating that they are able to care for themselves but may need occasional assistance with more strenuous activities. The patient is able to commit to the MRI scans required prior to treatment. The patient has a history of mild obstructive sleep apnea and has used CPAP therapy in the past without complications. The patient does not have any implanted metal devices or foreign bodies that would prevent MR imaging. The patient's creatinine levels are within normal limits. The patient does not have severe claustrophobia and is not pregnant. The patient is a suitable candidate for the study and will be enrolled in Arm 2 for the protocol with CPAP.

A 56-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of hepatic metastatic uveal melanoma (HMUM). Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Imaging studies reveal a solitary hepatic lesion measuring 4 cm in diameter, with no evidence of other distant metastasis. She is deemed eligible for curative surgery (R0). She is willing to participate in the ct DNA R0 study and is able to stand a blood collection. The patient has been fully informed about the study and has signed the consent form. She has no history of psychiatric illness and is able to submit to medical monitoring for the duration of the trial. Her BMI is 25, and she is a non-smoker. She is currently not taking any medication that would interfere with the study.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with Charcot Marie Tooth disease (CMT) type 1A. She was diagnosed at the age of 5 when she started experiencing difficulty in walking and running. She has a family history of CMT, with her mother and older brother also being diagnosed with the same condition. She has been receiving physical therapy and orthotics to help with her mobility. Her current medications include gabapentin for neuropathic pain and vitamin D supplements. She is able to walk short distances without assistance, but tires easily and requires a wheelchair for long distances. She also experiences weakness in her hands and has difficulty with fine motor skills, such as buttoning her clothes or tying her shoes. Her latest nerve conduction studies show slowed nerve conduction velocities. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help with the development of a new CMT Pediatric Scale that could help with the evaluation of the disease severity in children.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of high-risk prostate cancer. He was diagnosed with the disease 6 months ago and has been undergoing hormonal therapy since then. He experienced urinary symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and nocturia for the past year, which prompted him to visit his doctor. He has a family history of prostate cancer, with his father and grandfather both having been diagnosed with the disease. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a financial analyst and enjoys reading books on finance in his free time. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. His BMI is 24 with a BP of 130/80. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is scheduled to undergo radical prostatectomy with extended pelvic lymph node dissection as part of his standard of care therapy. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and will use an acceptable form of birth control for a period of 7 days after the 99mTc MIP-1404 injection.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV melanoma after noticing a new mole on her back that started to grow rapidly. She underwent surgery to remove the mole and surrounding tissue, but the cancer had already spread to her lymph nodes and liver. She has been receiving chemotherapy and immunotherapy for the past few months but has not seen any significant improvement. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but otherwise, she is in good health. She is HLA-A2 positive and HLA-B44 positive. She is interested in exploring other treatment options and is willing to participate in clinical trials.

62 yo M diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer with bone metastasis on imaging. Scheduled for biopsy as part of standard of care. INR and platelets within eligible range for study. No history of HIV, Hepatitis B or C infections. Not taking any medications that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been struggling with heart failure for the past year. She experiences shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema in her legs. She has been diagnosed with New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III HF and is currently taking medications to manage her symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and has been on medications for it for the past 5 years. She has no known allergies to medications and has never had any heart surgeries. She has a normal renal function and is not pregnant or lactating. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial. She has a life expectancy of approximately 2 years.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy with adenotonsillar hypertrophy, who is scheduled to undergo adenotonsillectomy at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. He has no known allergies or medical conditions, and is not currently taking any medications. The patient's parents have consented to his participation in the study, and he has been randomized to receive either montelukast or placebo in Same Day surgery. The patient is expected to stay overnight for observation following the procedure. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of preoperative Montelukast as an analgesic for adenotonsillectomy, with the primary objective being to determine whether montelukast reduces the amount of opioid pain medication required postoperatively compared to those receiving placebo. The secondary objectives include evaluating post-surgical outcomes such as pain scores and number of Emergency department visits and/or phone calls for postoperative pain-related complaints.

A 10-year-old boy was diagnosed with biliary atresia shortly after birth. He underwent Kasai procedure at 2 months of age, but unfortunately, the procedure was unsuccessful. His liver function deteriorated progressively and he was listed for liver transplantation. He underwent liver transplantation at Memorial Hospitals in 2018. He has been followed up regularly by his transplant team and has been doing well. He is currently 12 years old and is on immunosuppression medications. His parents have been very supportive and have ensured he adheres to his medication regimen. He participates in school activities and enjoys playing soccer with his friends.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman scheduled for elective surgery for a benign ovarian cyst. She has a history of occasional acid reflux but is not on any medications for it. She has a BMI of 25 and does not have asthma. She has been classified as ASA Class II. She has a Mallampati score of II. She has never had any issues with anesthesia in the past. She has no known allergies to isoflurane or propofol.

The patient is a healthy 35-year-old male with a body weight within ±20% of his ideal body weight. He has no significant medical history, and he has not donated whole blood or blood components within the past two months. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past three months. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in a Phase I clinical trial to compare the pharmacokinetics of DP-R213 to its individual components.

This is a 10 year-old female with a diagnosis of sickle cell disease (SCD) who has been receiving medical care at a pediatric hospital in France for the past 2 years. She has experienced frequent episodes of intense pain, which have caused her to miss school and other activities. Her parents report feeling overwhelmed and stressed about managing her condition, and have expressed a desire for more support and resources. The patient is currently taking hydroxyurea, but her symptoms have not significantly improved. She is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. The family speaks French as their primary language, but they are proficient in English as well.

A 58-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and has been taking warfarin for the past year. He had a recent INR test which showed that his INR level was below the therapeutic range. He is concerned about the accuracy of his current INR measurement device and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new in vitro diagnostic device for measuring the INR. He has no acute conditions in the past month and is willing to provide capillary blood drops taken from the fingertip for the study. He meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with papillary thyroid cancer. The primary tumor size is 1.5 cm on ultrasound, and there is evidence of lymph node enlargement in the paratracheal lymph node group. The patient has no history of coagulation disorders or vocal cord palsy. The patient requires total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection but does not need lateral compartment neck dissection or mediastinal dissection. There is no evidence of massive extracapsular extension to surrounding soft tissues. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of the no-tie technique using the harmonic scalpel in total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been taking one oral hypoglycemic agent and managing his diabetes with diet and exercise. His glycosylated haemoglobin A1 (HbA1c) is between 6.5% and 8.5% at screening. He has a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 35 kg/m2. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders besides type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and medically treated hypertension. He has no history of epilepsy, psychiatric disorders or relevant neurological disorders besides polyneuropathy. He has never participated in another trial with an investigational drug within two months prior to administration or during the trial. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is not currently taking any medication that might reasonably influence the results of the trial or that prolong the QT/QTc interval. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the whole study period from the time of the first intake of the study drug until one month after the last intake.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and occasional alcohol use presents to the emergency department with a laceration to his arm. He has no history of lower extremity injuries or vascular disorders. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has a BMI of 27. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and has no other medical conditions. The patient has light skin pigmentation and does not smoke. He is interested in the study and willing to have his skin pigmentation and muscle oxygenation measured using the reflectance colorimeter and INVOS cerebral oximeter, respectively.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and occasional rectal bleeding for the past few months. She has a family history of colon cancer and has never had a colonoscopy before. She has been following a low-residue diet and has completed her bowel preparation as instructed. She has no known allergies to meperidine or propofol and has not undergone any partial colectomy in the past. Her American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) risk class is 2. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45 yo F who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension for the past 5 years. She is currently living in a therapeutic coordination apartment due to her precarious situation. She has been struggling with managing her chronic conditions and has been experiencing a perceived burden of treatment. She is willing to participate in the study and hopes that the Health Education program will help her develop coping skills and strategies to better manage her illness, improve her quality of life and empower her to take control of her health. She speaks French fluently and has no cognitive or speech impairments, making her eligible for the study.

45-year-old female diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes for the past 3 years presents with a sedentary lifestyle and a body mass index (BMI) of 30, indicating obesity. She works as an office administrator and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She reports feeling tired and unmotivated to exercise, often citing work and family responsibilities as reasons for her lack of physical activity. She currently takes metformin to manage her diabetes and has no other significant medical history. She is a fluent English speaker and resides in Alberta. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her physical activity levels and overall health.

A 30-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 has volunteered to participate in a clinical trial to assess the bioavailability of budesonide and formoterol delivered via Symbicort pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) with and without a spacer device. He has no history of COPD or asthma and has never smoked. He is not taking any prescribed or non-prescribed medication, and he has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to Symbicort. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease, or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. He has suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture. He has a normal FEV1 of 90% of predicted value and FEV1/FVC ratio of 75%. He is not currently involved in another clinical study, and he has not donated plasma or blood in the past month. He has provided signed and dated, written informed consent prior to any study specific procedures.

The patient is a male, 30 years old, who participated and completed the HIGH: low study and is willing to participate in the follow-up study. He has not stopped his treatment at Hvidovre Hospital and does not have any known medical conditions that could interfere with the study outcomes. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is available for the required follow-up appointment. The patient has no history of substance abuse or current use of drugs that could interfere with the study outcomes. The patient's medical history includes no chronic illnesses or previous surgeries. He is currently employed and is compliant with his medication regimen.

The patient is a 49-year-old male who suffered a tibial plateau fracture from a skiing accident. He is an active individual who enjoys skiing and hiking. The patient is currently experiencing moderate to severe pain in the injured knee and requires operative fixation. The patient has no prior history of tibial plateau fracture on the ipsilateral knee, but he does have a history of mild depression that is currently being managed with a low dose SSRI. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. He is ambulatory and otherwise healthy. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve pain management for others who may undergo tibial plateau surgery in the future.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of a thyroid nodule and underwent a total thyroidectomy due to papillary thyroid carcinoma. The patient has no history of any other medical conditions, and she is not taking any medications. The patient has no known drug allergies. The patient has never been intubated before and has no history of difficult intubation. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient will be randomized to undergo one of the four vocal cord imaging techniques - direct laryngoscopy, videolaryngoscopy, fiberoptic laryngoscopy or ultrasonography - to visualize the vocal cords after extubation. The efficacy of the method, the duration of the procedure and the hemodynamic responses will be monitored and compared between the groups.

A 28-year-old woman presents with recurrent epigastric pain and bloating. She reports that these symptoms have been present for the past few months and are worse after meals. She has not been previously treated for H. pylori infection. The patient does not have any alarm symptoms such as anemia, persistent vomiting, hematemesis, dysphagia, significant weight loss, or a palpable mass in the abdomen. She is not taking any immunosuppressive therapy or acetylsalicylic acid. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she reports no allergies to any medications. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She underwent a urea breath test, which came back positive for H. pylori infection. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He complains of severe chest pain that limits his daily activities, including walking and climbing stairs. Despite optimal medical therapy for thirty days, including long-acting nitrates, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers, his angina remains class III-IV of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) grading system. He is not a candidate for surgical or percutaneous coronary intervention, as determined by two independent professors of internal medicine. The patient has shown reversible ischemia of the left ventricular wall demonstrated by Dobutamine Stress Echocardiography (Dobutamine ECHO). The patient has no history of recent acute coronary syndrome, PCI, CABG, or unstable angina within thirty days prior to screening. The patient has no history of de-compensated congestive heart failure or hospitalization due to CHF during the three months prior to screening. The patient has no life-threatening rhythm disorders, and his forced expiratory volume in one second is within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet all of the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old Arabic-speaking woman who has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression for the past few months. She reports feeling overwhelmed, hopeless, and having trouble sleeping. She has never received any formal psychiatric treatment in the past, but has tried various self-help strategies such as meditation and exercise to manage her symptoms. She reports having access to a computer and smartphone, and is able to read and write in Arabic. The patient denies any current or past suicidal ideation, alcohol addiction, or history of major psychiatric disorders. She is not currently undergoing any psychological treatment, and has not made any recent changes to her psychiatric medication. She is interested in participating in the study to receive treatment for her symptoms in a culturally adapted format.

A 35-year-old female who works as a marketing executive is interested in participating in a clinical trial focused on improving sleep duration and quality. She reports typically only getting 5-6 hours of sleep per night during the workweek due to her demanding job and often finds herself feeling fatigued during the day. She has a BMI of 24 and is in good overall health. She does not have any diagnosed medical conditions and is not taking any medications except for occasional over-the-counter pain relievers. She does not smoke, but she does drink alcohol socially on weekends. She has never been diagnosed with insomnia or sleep apnea but sometimes struggles to fall asleep at night. She is interested in learning how improving her sleep habits and duration could impact her overall health and well-being.

Daniel is a 14-year-old male diagnosed with autism by a child and adolescent psychiatrist. He experiences difficulty with social interactions, communication, and repetitive behaviors. He has been struggling with aggressive behavior towards his siblings, teachers, and peers at school. He has no history of seizures or gross neurological deficits. He is currently not taking any psychotropic medications. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has no major medical problems such as cardiac, liver, endocrine, or renal diseases. He has a baseline QTC of 410 msec. His height and weight are within normal limits for his age. He and his parents have been informed about the study and have given their consent and assent, respectively. He will be participating in the 6-week pilot study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ziprasidone in treating his autism symptoms. He will be assessed weekly by the research team and will be treated openly with ziprasidone at a dosage range of 5 mg/day to 40 mg/day. Any untoward effects will be measured and recorded at each visit. Lab studies will also be obtained at baseline and repeated at the end of the treatment phase.

A 19-year-old male diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) had undergone chemotherapy for a period of 6 months with no significant improvement. The latest bone marrow biopsy showed 60% blasts. The doctor recommended him to participate in a clinical trial of CD19-CART treatment for ALL. His laboratory results showed that he had normal liver and kidney function, with a creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dl, ALT/AST levels of 35/40 U/L, and a bilirubin level of 0.9 mg/dl. He has not received any systemic steroids or gene therapy products before. He is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 5 years. She has been on oral hypoglycemic agents for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing decreased vision in her left eye for the past 6 months. Examination shows diabetic macular edema in her left eye. The patient has not received any prior treatment for macular edema with laser therapy. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) score in the left eye is 60 letters (20/63 ETDRS). The retinal thickness in the left eye is 325um by OCT. She does not have any ocular conditions that would prevent a 2-line improvement in visual acuity. The patient does not have a history of elevated intraocular pressure in response to steroid treatment or glaucoma. The patient does not have any other ocular conditions that could contribute to macular edema. The patient has been diagnosed with diabetic macular edema and is eligible for the clinical trial.

A 44-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She is married with two children and works as a marketing executive. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been taking antidepressants for the past year. She is worried about the impact of her diagnosis on her family and her career, as she has a demanding job that requires frequent travel. She is interested in seeking support from others who have been through similar experiences, but is hesitant to attend in-person support groups due to her busy schedule and fear of being recognized by colleagues or acquaintances. She has limited experience using online support groups, but is open to exploring this option. She is tech-savvy and frequently uses social media platforms for personal and professional purposes. She hopes to find a supportive community where she can share her experiences and emotions without feeling judged or isolated.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with opioid use disorder for the past 2 years. He has tried to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He has been receiving medication-assisted treatment (MAT) as part of his standard clinical care for the past 6 months. He has moderate severity of opioid use disorder and meets 4 or 5 DSM-V criteria. He has no acute medical problems requiring immediate inpatient treatment and has no history of psychotic disorders. However, he has a history of anxiety and depression. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized clinical trial and is able to read and write in English. He is not pregnant and is willing to share health-related data with his primary care clinicians. At the study intake, he has been abstinent from opioids for the past 2 weeks and is taking prescribed medication to treat the disorder. He is willing to provide the name, verified telephone number, and address of at least 2 contacts willing to help locate him if necessary during follow-up. The patient is interested in using an evidence-based mobile health system (A-CHESS) to help him manage his opioid use disorder.

A 60-year-old man presents with a history of venous leg ulcers that have been present for over a year. He reports a history of venous insufficiency and has tried various treatments, including compression stockings and standard wound care, without success. He has a single ulcer on his lower leg that measures approximately 5 cm x 5 cm and has not healed despite previous treatments. He reports pain and discomfort in the area and is looking for a new treatment option. He is Medicare eligible, and his laboratory values indicate adequate platelet count, hemoglobin levels, and serum albumin. He has no known allergies to any components of Aurix. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has adequate venous access for repeated blood draws required for Aurix administration.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis. She has failed to taper steroid treatment within one year and has been experiencing active inflammation during her current disease flare. The patient has a negative stool test for pathogen bacteria, and her TPMT genotype is homozygous wild-type. She has a normal kidney function with a GFR greater than 50 ml/min and a normal ALT level. The patient is currently taking oral 5-Asa and is willing to comply with all trial procedures and be available for the duration of the trial. She has not previously received thiopurin treatment or participated in other interventional clinical trials. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not received other biologics besides anti-TNFα.

A 46-year-old man came to the clinic for a follow-up visit for his type 2 diabetes. Despite his current insulin therapy, his HbA1c levels have been consistently high at 10.5% for the past 6 months. He is concerned about the negative impact of uncontrolled diabetes on his health and quality of life. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has access to a smartphone and is willing to use the GlucoMe App at home. He has never used any other diabetes management app before. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or any other severe chronic illness.

The clinical trial is looking for girls aged between 9 and 14 years, who are enrolled in a government primary or secondary day school in Mwanza city (or neighbouring district if included) and living in the same area without plans to move away in the next 36 months. They should be born female, in good health, and willing to participate in the study. Girls who are diagnosed with chronic conditions, such as autoimmune conditions, degenerative diseases, neurologic or genetic diseases, HIV-positive, or immunocompromised, pregnant, less than three months post-partum, currently breastfeeding, allergic to one of the vaccine components or to latex, or have been previously vaccinated against HPV are excluded from the trial.

A 55 year old male patient was admitted to the ICU with a history of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus and hypertension. He had been experiencing fever, shortness of breath, and cough with yellow sputum production for the past 5 days. His initial chest X-ray showed consolidation in the lower lobe of the right lung. Sputum culture was performed and Klebsiella pneumoniae was detected with drug sensitivity testing revealing resistance to multiple antibiotics. The patient was started on intravenous antibiotics and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. Despite aggressive treatment, the patient's condition deteriorated rapidly and he passed away within 48 hours of admission to the ICU. Data collected during his stay will be included in the clinical trial to study the clinical characteristics of critically ill patients with Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.

The patient is a 65-year-old female who has been caring for her 75-year-old husband with dementia for the past 8 months. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to her caregiving duties, which include managing her husband's medications, helping him with daily activities, and monitoring his behavior. She also reports feeling isolated and lonely, as she has had to cut back on her social activities to provide care for her husband. She speaks English as her primary language and has access to a telephone. She resides in Southeastern New England with her husband, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has no cognitive impairment, as evidenced by an MMSE score of 28.

Patient is a 32-year-old female from the United States who is interested in participating in a clinical trial related to neuropsychiatric disorders. She has completed her education with a Bachelor's degree and has no history of claustrophobia or metal exclusions. She is willing and able to provide voluntary written informed consent. The patient has a family history of schizophrenia and is interested in contributing to research on this disorder. She has no history of cannabis use disorder.

The patient is a 35-year-old non-smoking female who is fluent in English. She reports being healthy and has no history of taste or smell loss, oral disorders, or food allergies. She is not taking any prescription pain or insulin medication, and does not have any current oral lesions, canker sores, or piercings. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the role of salivary contents in taste perception and food liking.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in her left leg. She has been prescribed warfarin to prevent further blood clots from forming. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She is generally healthy, with no history of significant medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She has not received warfarin treatment previously for any clinical indication. She has undergone genotyping screening for CYP2C9 and VKORC1, and the results indicate that she is not predicted to be most sensitive to warfarin. Her neutrophil count is within normal range.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been experiencing musculoskeletal pain for several months. She reports pain in her knees, back, and shoulders, which has been interfering with her everyday life, making it difficult to participate in physical activities and attend school regularly. She has no history of musculoskeletal pain prior to this and has not had any injuries or accidents that could explain the pain. She has been to her general practitioner (GP) for evaluation, and her GP has referred her to participate in a study investigating prognostic factors for adolescents with musculoskeletal pain in general practice. She is interested in participating in the study and has given written consent. Her parents are also willing to participate in the study and have completed the parent questionnaire. She will be followed up at 3, 6, and 12 months and continuously every 1-5 years to assess the progression and prognosis of her musculoskeletal pain.

The patient is a 70-year-old Korean male residing in the south-west area of Seoul. He is retired and living with his spouse in their own home. He has a history of hypertension for which he takes daily medication. He has no history of diabetes or cardiovascular disease. He is physically active and enjoys taking daily walks around his neighborhood. He has a BMI of 25 and his waist circumference is within normal limits. He has been a non-smoker for the past 20 years and doesn't consume alcohol. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the relationship between diabetes and mortality in the elderly Korean population. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in follow-up examinations.

Mrs. Lee is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has been experiencing depressive symptoms, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She also has trouble sleeping and experiences fatigue throughout the day. She has been taking donepezil for the past four months and has not had any significant changes in her condition. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help alleviate her depressive symptoms. She has not taken any antidepressant medications in the past four weeks and does not have a history of bipolar disorder or schizophrenia. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She has no history of seizures, brain surgery, or organic brain disease. Her MMSE score is 18 and her GDS-15 score is 7. She has recently had a brain MRI which showed mild atrophy. She is willing to attend six visits over the course of 24 weeks and has a caregiver who can accompany her to every visit. She is willing to take the study medication as prescribed and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

A 35-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a complaint of hair loss. She has been experiencing hair loss for the past 6 months, which has been causing her significant distress. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She has not started any pharmacological treatment for hair loss yet. She uses a mild shampoo with a conditioner and never uses any hair dye or hair straightener. She has no history of allergies or atopy. She has regular menstrual cycles and uses a combination oral contraceptive pill. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day, five days a week. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new hair loss prevention lotion.

Pt is a 38yo M with a 12-year history of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis, which has been resistant to topical treatments. The patient has a body surface area involvement of 30% and plaques with significant elevation above the surrounding normal skin. The patient has previously received phototherapy and systemic agents, but has not responded satisfactorily. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of kidney disease, coronary or cerebral vascular disease, or active malignancy. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraceptive methods throughout the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He underwent treatment with concomitant chemoradiotherapy six months ago and is currently in complete remission. He complains of difficulty sleeping due to snoring and episodes of breathing cessation during the night. He reports feeling tired during the day and having difficulty concentrating at work. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He lives with his wife and two children and works as a sales executive. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance the knowledge about the consequences of oropharyngeal cancer treatment on sleep quality.

A 26-year-old woman diagnosed with borderline personality disorder who has been experiencing major depressive episodes that have not responded to medication. She reports feeling hopeless, sad, and isolated, with difficulty sleeping and a lack of energy. She has tried multiple antidepressants without success and has been referred for rTMS treatment. She is willing and able to adhere to the treatment schedule and has a normal CBC and thyroid functioning. She is not pregnant and has no history of psychotic disorders or significant neurological conditions. She is currently receiving psychotherapy and has been in stable treatment for at least three months. She has not had a severe suicide attempt requiring medical intervention in the past three months.

Jean is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer last year. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and has had surgery to remove the tumor. Although the treatment has helped, her oncologist has informed her that there is a possibility of recurrence. Her oncologist has recommended that she consider participating in a Phase I clinical trial to explore new treatment options. Jean is feeling overwhelmed and confused about the idea of participating in a clinical trial, and she is unsure about the risks and benefits. She is hoping to have a thorough discussion with her oncologist about the trial and wants to ensure that she has a good understanding of the potential outcomes before making a decision.

A 27-year-old healthy man who works in finance is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no underlying medical conditions and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He exercises regularly by jogging and lifting weights at the gym. He doesn't smoke and drinks alcohol only occasionally. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is in a committed relationship but does not plan to have children in the near future. He is willing to comply with contraception requirements during the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients but rather a community-level seroprevalence survey. The study aims to establish the seroprevalence of SARS-COV-2 in an Argentinian slum three months after the first case was reported. The participants are individuals over 14 years old, selected from a probabilistic sample of households in the slum. The study uses a finger prick puncture ELISA test to detect COVID-19 antibodies. There are no specific patient characteristics required for this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence (SUI) symptoms for the past 2 years. She has previously attempted conservative treatments such as behavior modifications, bladder exercises, and biofeedback, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is a nurse and is very active in her job, often working long hours and lifting heavy patients. She has no other medical problems and is not taking any medications that affect lower urinary tract function. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is available for the follow-up evaluations required by the study protocol. Her BMI is 24.5, and she has no history of pure urge incontinence or mixed urinary incontinence where urge incontinence is the predominant factor. She has experienced SUI symptoms for over 6 months prior to signing the informed consent. She has had no more than 2 episodes of awakening to void during normal sleeping hours.

A 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hypertension for 2 years and has been regularly monitored at the hypertension outpatient clinic of Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre (HCPA) for more than six months. She has been taking antihypertensive medication, but her blood pressure has not been well controlled. She has a family history of hypertension and cardiovascular disease. She has a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in sodium and saturated fats. She works as an office manager and experiences stress at work. She has no history of cognitive impairment or dementia.

A 30-year-old Caucasian female presented with a history of frequent episodes of dizziness, lightheadedness, palpitations, and fatigue for the past 2 years. Her symptoms were exacerbated during standing and relieved when she sat or lay down. She also complained of headaches, brain fog, and difficulty concentrating. The patient had been to multiple healthcare providers with no clear diagnosis. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she was not taking any medications. She denied any significant family history of cardiovascular or neurological diseases. She was a non-smoker and had a BMI of 23 kg/m2. Her vital signs were stable in the supine position, but upon standing, her heart rate increased from 70 bpm to 120 bpm, and her blood pressure remained stable. She had no orthostatic hypotension (a drop in blood pressure ≥ 20/10 mmHg), and her symptoms persisted for at least 6 months. A tilt table test was positive for POTS. The patient was referred to the autonomic clinic for further evaluation, where she underwent muscle sympathetic nerve activity testing (MSNA), which showed a resting MSNA of 30 bursts/min, confirming the diagnosis of primary central sympathetic activation type of POTS (psPOTS). The patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a blood pressure medication (Moxonidine) on her symptoms during standing.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption but has been sober for the past year. The patient is overweight with a BMI of 32, and after further evaluation, the doctor has diagnosed him with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through liver biopsy. He has not been diagnosed with hepatitis C and has no history of liver disease besides NAFLD.

A 26-year-old female patient who has been experiencing recurrent regurgitation of recently ingested food into the mouth. She has been diagnosed with rumination syndrome and has not responded well to previous treatment options. She is in good overall health with no relevant organic diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and able to attend the 3 sessions over a 10-day period. She will be required to complete daily questionnaires to track the number of rumination events. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to find a more effective treatment option for her rumination syndrome.

63-year-old male with a history of chronic intractable pain in the lower back and left leg for the past 2 years. The patient has tried various pain management treatments, including medications and physical therapy, but has not experienced significant relief. The patient reports a pain intensity level of 8 on a 0-10 numerical rating scale (OPI-NRS-11) over the last 180 days. The pain has significantly impacted his daily activities, including walking and sitting for prolonged periods. He has undergone routine psychological/psychiatric evaluation as per study site's requirement and passed the evaluation. The patient is willing and able to comply with all protocol-required follow-up evaluations. He is not currently on any anticoagulant medications that cannot be discontinued during the perioperative period. He is not a high surgical risk and can operate the Precision Spectra™ System either by self or with a caregiver. The patient has not participated in any other investigational drug or device clinical trial that may influence the data that will be collected for this study. He has not been implanted with any active implantable device(s) to treat his pain (IPGs, implantable drug pumps, etc.) or pacemaker or Implantable Cardiac Defibrillator. The patient is not a woman who is pregnant or nursing or intends to become pregnant during the course of the trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with an ischemic stroke of unknown origin.
