She presented with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking, which resolved after a few hours. CT and MRI scans confirmed the presence of a stroke, but no obvious cause. Further investigation revealed the presence of a patent foramen ovale (PFO), a small opening between the upper heart chambers that did not close after birth. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of cardiac disease, vascular disease, or neurological disorders. She is able to perform her daily activities independently and is willing to participate in the PC-Trial to compare the effectiveness of medical treatment versus catheter closure of the PFO to prevent further strokes. The patient is not pregnant, does not have any contraindications for antithrombotic or anticoagulant therapy, and is able to provide informed consent.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with uterine fibroids and scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control her blood pressure. She has no known allergies to medications, food or any medical products. She has never experienced any difficulties with anesthesia or intubation in the past. Her physical examination, including airway assessment, is normal. Her lab results show no abnormalities. She has provided written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

45-year-old female diagnosed with Stage II breast cancer is eligible for this clinical trial. She is scheduled to undergo breast-conserving therapy and sentinel lymph node biopsy. Clinical examination of her nodal basin is negative. She is not receiving any investigational agents and has no history of allergic reactions attributed to ICG or other agents used in the study. She does not have any underlying lung disease and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to sign a written informed consent document and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 57-year-old non-smoking female who was recently found to have a 2 cm pulmonary nodule during a routine CT screening. She has no history of lung cancer or other significant medical conditions but reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion. She works as a librarian and enjoys reading and gardening in her spare time. She has a supportive family and lives with her husband and two adult children. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand her pulmonary nodule and potentially avoid invasive procedures. She has read and understands the informed consent and is willing to sign it.

This is a 48-year-old female with a history of established cardiovascular disease. She was diagnosed with angina pectoris and underwent diagnostic angiography which revealed a >50% stenosis of one of her coronary arteries. She has been on statin and anti-hypertensive medication for the past two years and has been compliant with her medication regimen. She has a history of smoking but quit six months ago. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to identify gene networks linked to cardiovascular disease in endothelial cells.

52-year-old male diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis 2 years prior. The patient has been prescribed various non-biologic DMARDs such as methotrexate and sulfasalazine, but has not responded well to these treatments. The patient has not been prescribed a biologic before and is currently evaluating treatment options. The patient has no known contraindications for Inflectra and is not known to have any hypersensitivity to infliximab, its excipients or other murine proteins. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess the real-life drug persistence of CT-P13 and to contribute to the scientific understanding of RA, AS, and PsA treatments. The patient is located in Canada and is willing to complete questionnaires on electronic tablets.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms for several years, specifically during the fall season when ragweed is prevalent. She reports nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes. She has tried various over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal sprays, but has not found significant relief. She has undergone skin testing for allergies and has tested positive for ragweed. She is generally in good health and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any medical conditions or take any medications that would interfere with the study results. She is available for the duration of the study.

60-year-old male with a history of tobacco use presented with a lump in his neck and difficulty swallowing. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck (SCCHN). Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the hypopharynx and bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, with no evidence of distant metastases. He has no significant medical history and no history of autoimmune disease. He is currently afebrile with no recent weight loss. His ECOG (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group) performance status is 1. He has no known allergies, and his laboratory parameters are within normal limits. He is not taking any medications or supplements. He has no history of immunodeficiency or active autoimmune conditions. He has not received any prior PD-1 or PD-L1 treatment. He has not received systemic chemotherapy within the past 2 weeks or a live vaccine within the past 30 days. He is willing and able to sign the consent form and has a standard of care biopsy planned.

A 65-year-old man presents with ongoing knee pain for the past year. He describes the pain as a dull ache that is sometimes accompanied by sharp, shooting pains. The pain is located in both knees, but is more severe in the right knee. He reports stiffness in the mornings and after sitting for long periods of time. The pain limits his ability to walk for long distances or engage in physical activities. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and topical creams, but they only provide temporary relief. He has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by his physician and meets the ACR clinical criteria. He is willing to participate in a study that aims to better understand the different pain phenotypes in knee osteoarthritis. He has no history of major knee trauma or lower extremity trauma or surgery. He has no other pain condition and is otherwise healthy.

A 57-year-old African American woman was diagnosed with colon cancer located between the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid junction. The tumor was found during a routine colonoscopy. The biopsy results showed adenocarcinoma. CT scan revealed cT3 stage and no metastasis to other organs. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation treatment. Her general condition is good with ASA 2 classification. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and expressed her willingness to comply with the demands of the study.

A 57-year-old male patient came to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain, bloody stools, and weight loss. He had a history of colon cancer and had undergone surgery to remove the tumor. However, his latest imaging studies showed that the cancer had metastasized and spread to other parts of his body. The patient was diagnosed with RAS-mutated, microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer that was unresectable. He had received two prior regimens of therapy for unresectable or metastatic CRC including fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based regimens. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status was 1. He had measurable disease, and his hemoglobin level was 8.6 g/dL. The patient was willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, laboratory tests, pharmacokinetic collections, and other requirements of the study. He provided a signed and dated Institutional Review Board (IRB) approved written informed consent form (ICF) in accordance with regulatory and institutional guidelines for both the study and exploratory biomarker analyses. After undergoing screening, he was histologically confirmed to have adenocarcinoma of the colon or the rectum that is metastatic or unresectable. He was determined to have RAS-mutated (KRAS or NRAS) and microsatellite stable/proficient in mismatch repair, as assessed by immunohistochemistry

Pt is a 45yo M with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease, presenting with angina and shortness of breath. The patient has never been on a statin before and has a history of combined dyslipidemia with LDL-cholesterol of 90 mg/dL and non-HDL-cholesterol of 150 mg/dL. The patient is not diabetic and does not have cardiogenic shock or heart failure with symptoms of New York Heart Association class III/IV, nor does he have renal or hepatic dysfunction. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not diagnosed with familial hypercholesterolemia. The patient has intermediate coronary artery stenosis (diameter stenosis ≥30% to ≤60% by visual estimation, diameter ≥2.0 mm to ≤4.0 mm, de novo lesion in native coronary artery) in which virtual histology-intravascular ultrasound (VH-IVUS) could be feasible. The patient is a candidate for this clinical trial as he meets the eligibility criteria.

25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, non-smoker, and BMI of 22 kg/m². No current medications or supplements. No history of drug or alcohol abuse. No family history of significant illnesses. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and is available for the required study visits.

35 year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection diagnosed 2 years ago. He has been receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) with saquinavir-sgc (Fortovase®) 1600 mg b.i.d. for the last 6 months and has been maintaining a viral load less than 400 copies/mL. He is currently in good health with no significant past medical history. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use any recreational drugs. He is sexually active with multiple partners and understands the importance of using a reliable form of contraception. He has been adhering to his ART regimen and is willing to comply with study requirements. He is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Pt is a 32yo M diagnosed with bipolar disorder according to the DSM 5. The patient has an elevated PANSS score of 5 and above, indicating severe symptoms of mania and depression. The patient is currently taking medication to manage their mental condition. The patient has a personal smartphone and is able to provide informed consent. There is no history of violence or suicidal tendencies. The patient is not undergoing dialysis treatment nor has a legal guardian. The patient is willing to wear a wristwatch to collect physiological, physical and behavioral data as part of the observational study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) three years ago. He has been experiencing progressive muscle weakness in his legs and feet, leading to difficulty with balance and walking. He is able to stand for short periods of time but requires assistance to maintain his balance. He is not currently using any mobility aids. He is interested in participating in a study to evaluate his postural control using new force platforms. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications that could affect his balance. He understands and has signed the informed consent form.

A 6-year-old female child has been experiencing persistent and distressing thoughts and compulsive behaviors that interfere with her daily life. She frequently washes her hands, cleans her toys, and checks and rechecks if the doors and windows are locked. Her symptoms have been present for at least 3 months and cause significant impairment in her daily functioning. She has no other physical or mental health issues and is not taking any medication. The child's parents are willing to participate in a treatment program for her OCD and committed to attending all sessions.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with sickle cell disease diagnosed at birth. She has a history of recurrent hospitalizations for acute chest syndrome and vaso-occlusive pain crises, requiring multiple blood transfusions. She has also developed osteonecrosis of the hips, which causes chronic pain and difficulty walking. Her current treatment includes hydroxyurea and pain management with opioids. She has a performance status of 1 and is willing to participate in the trial. Her sister is a suitable HLA-matched donor and has agreed to donate stem cells for the transplant. She is not pregnant and does not have acute hepatitis, severe renal impairment, or HIV.

The patient is a 35 year old man living in a rural area of India. He works as a farmer and has a history of lymphedema in his right leg for the past 5 years. The swelling has gradually progressed and he now experiences pain and stiffness in his leg, which limits his mobility and ability to work. He has not undergone any treatment for his lymphedema, and his hygiene practices are limited due to lack of knowledge and access to resources. He is married with 2 children and lives with his family in a small house. He has not traveled outside his village in the past year. He does not have any other significant medical history or comorbidities. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent. He is able to comprehend the study requirements and instructions for hygiene practices. His BMI is 24 with the BP of 120/80. There is no evidence of hepatic or renal dysfunction or CNS disease.

42-year-old woman with a BMI of 30.5 and a waist circumference of 96cm. She has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a high-fat diet. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia but is not currently taking any medication for them. She does not have a history of diabetes or cardiovascular disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her health and is willing to follow a calorie-reduced diet and increase her daily activity level. She has access to the internet and is willing to use web-based questionnaires. She is covered by health insurance and is compliant with the recommendations of National Law in force relating to biomedical research. She does not use any medications or supplements to manage body weight or body fat and has not used any probiotic supplements in the last 6 weeks. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs or alcohol. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study. She has never participated in a clinical trial with an investigational product or drug within 60 days prior to screening. She is willing to comply with the protocol and study restrictions and is available for all study visits.

This is a 28 year old female who has been trying to conceive with her partner for the past 2 years without success. She has a known history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been diagnosed with primary infertility. She has no prior history of thyroid disorders or treatment for infertility. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has never been pregnant before and has no known history of sexually transmitted infections. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the relationship between thyroid function and anti-mullerian hormone levels in infertile patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of diabetes mellitus and gastroparesis, which was confirmed by a gastric emptying study. She experiences frequent nausea, vomiting, bloating, and early satiety. She has tried various medications and dietary modifications without significant relief. She is interested in participating in the study to help diagnose and possibly improve her condition. She has no claustrophobia or other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. She has received at least two treatment methods in the past but has not shown significant improvement. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She has no known hypersensitivity to TQB3602 or its excipient and has no peripheral nerve diseases greater than grade 2. She experiences mild diarrhea occasionally but has not had any grade >1 during the screening period. She has not received any chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or other systemic antitumor therapies within 14 days before the first dose. She has not received ixazomib and less than 5 half-life before the first dose. She has not received allogeneic stem cell transplant. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not participated in other clinical trials within 4 weeks before participating in this trial. She is willing to use an adequate method of contraception starting with the first dose of study therapy through 6 months after the last dose of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in her left breast. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and showed that it is the primary site of the lymphoma. She underwent a staging workup which revealed stage I disease with no evidence of involvement in other organs or lymph nodes except the left axillary lymph nodes. The patient was started on the R-CHOP regimen which consists of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone. She has completed one cycle of treatment and is scheduled to receive six more cycles over the next few months. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or comorbidities. Her vital signs are stable, and she is able to perform activities of daily living without any significant limitations. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the impact of rituximab in patients with primary breast DLBCL.

54 yo M with past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presents to the emergency department with chest pain and subsequently goes into cardiac arrest. He is successfully resuscitated and transferred to the ICU for therapeutic hypothermia per protocol. During the cooling process, the patient develops shivering and is given cisatracurium IV infusion as per protocol. The patient is then randomized into the study and assigned to either the cisatracurium infusion group or the cisatracurium prn bolus group. The patient's temperature is closely monitored and recorded. The study aims to determine if there is a difference in the time it takes to reach the target temperature between the two groups. The patient's overall outcome will also be assessed. Past Medical History: Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia.

A 32-year-old male patient with a history of muscular dystrophy, specifically Becker muscular dystrophy, presents to the clinic. He reports difficulty with daily activities due to muscle weakness in his upper extremities, particularly the shoulder girdle and proximal upper limb portions. He is wheelchair-bound and requires assistance with many activities of daily living. He has no history of epilepsy, and he is not dependent on non-invasive or invasive ventilation. He reports no behavioral or psychiatric disorders. His cognitive skills are intact, and he is able to understand and manage the device. His arm length measured from the shoulder to the elbow is 27.5 cm, and his forearm length measured between elbow and wrist is 20.4 cm. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that assesses the fit, safety, and usability of a motorized exoskeleton device (BRIDGE / EMPATIA exoskeleton) to support the execution of daily activities.

48-year-old male with a history of gastric cancer diagnosed as locally advanced (UICC stage, T4, N2, N3) after D2 resection. The tumor was located in the distal stomach and histologically confirmed as adenocarcinoma. The patient has completed surgery and has at least 15 lymph nodes removed. The patient is currently in good health with an ECOG score of 1. The patient has not received any previous radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient's organ function is within normal limits with ANC ≥ 2*109/L, Platelets ≥ 100*109/L, AST and ALT ≤ 2.5×ULN, TBIL ≤ 1.5×ULN. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is not a woman of childbearing potential.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo adjuvant chemotherapy. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, and is currently taking amlodipine (5 mg/day) and atorvastatin (40 mg/day). She has no history of cardiac disease or significant arrhythmias. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her ECOG performance status is 0. A baseline echocardiogram shows a normal LVEF. She is scheduled to receive 4 cycles of adriamycin and cyclophosphamide every 2-3 weeks. Her ER and PR status are positive, and her HER2 status is negative. She has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study and has signed the informed consent document. She is able to swallow tablets and does not have any gastrointestinal disease or malabsorption issues. She is not taking any medications that interact with simvastatin or increase the risk of myopathy. She meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has a history of hypertension and diabetes. He presents to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of decreased vision in his right eye. He reports that he has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty seeing fine details for the past few weeks. He denies any pain or redness in the eye. On examination, his visual acuity is 20/30 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. Intraocular pressure is within normal limits. Anterior segment examination is remarkable for mild nuclear sclerosis in both eyes. Dilated fundus examination of the right eye reveals a subtle area of retinal thickening and possible neovascularization in the temporal macula. The left eye is unremarkable. The patient is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial as he has visually significant posterior retinal pathology requiring imaging of the retina with a mydriatic fundus plenoptic camera.

Patient A is a 28-year-old female who has been wearing FRESHLOOK® COLORBLENDS contact lenses in hazel for at least two days a week for the past year. She has light brown eyes and has not had any eye injuries or surgeries in the past 12 weeks. She has no pre-existing ocular irritation and is not currently enrolled in any clinical trials. She does not have any systematic or ocular abnormalities, infections or diseases that would affect the successful wear of contact lenses. She does not use any medications that would contraindicate contact lens wear. She has spectacles that provide acceptable near vision to wear over study lenses as needed to evaluate cosmetics of the lenses. She is willing to sign the informed consent document or have her legally authorized representative sign it if she is under the age of consent.

60-year-old male diagnosed with advanced prostate cancer and currently receiving monthly injections of Lupron for the past 6 months. He has a stable PSA level and a baseline testosterone level below the castration level. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1, with occasional fatigue and mild difficulty with activities of daily living. He has a history of hypertension, well controlled with Lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia, managed with Atorvastatin. He has no known drug allergies or adverse reactions to Lupron. He has no prior history of chemotherapy, radiotherapy or prostatectomy. He is compliant with his current treatment and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of Trelstar versus Lupron or Zoladex in treating his prostate cancer. He is able to provide signed, informed consent and has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months.

The patient is a 72-year-old retired woman living with her husband in a suburban area. She is fluent in Mandarin and has completed high school education. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She reports occasional joint pain in her knees and hips, but otherwise, she is generally in good health. She has been living independently and has no difficulty performing activities of daily living. The patient exercises regularly by taking daily walks and practicing tai chi. She has a good support system with her husband, children, and grandchildren living nearby. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve the health of older adults in her community.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia for the past 10 years. The patient has been taking atorvastatin for the past 2 years to control his cholesterol levels. The patient's latest lipid panel showed an LDL-cholesterol level of 120 mg/dl and fasting serum triglycerides level of 220 mg/dl. The patient is generally in good health with no significant medical history. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or drugs of similar chemical classes. The patient is not a woman of child-bearing potential. The patient has no concomitant medications that are known to impact the safe use or efficacy of atorvastatin based on drug labels. The patient has no conditions that might impact the safety or biologic activity of the study drug.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather healthcare professionals and lay persons who routinely use safety lancets to collect blood samples. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable.

A 38-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department with severe pain in his abdomen. He described the pain as sharp and constant, with a pain score of 7 out of 10 on a numeric rating scale from zero to ten. He has no past medical history of chronic pain syndrome, and he has not taken any analgesics in the past six hours. He has no reported allergies to either paracetamol or morphine. He has a history of mild hypertension and is currently on medication. He is a non-smoker and occasional social drinker. The patient's vital signs were stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, a respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. His oxygen saturation level was 98% on room air. He is alert and oriented to time, place, and person, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15. The patient signed the informed consent to participate in the study, and he was randomized into the group receiving paracetamol and morphine.

A 63-year-old female patient presented with a history of blurred vision and difficulty in reading for the past few months. She had a medical history of hypertension and was on medication for the same. She was a non-smoker and did not consume alcohol. Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/60 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Slit-lamp examination revealed corneal guttae and stromal edema in the right eye, and the left eye showed mild corneal guttae with normal endothelial cell density. The patient was diagnosed with Fuchs endothelial dystrophy in the right eye and was advised for Descemet's stripping with endothelial keratoplasty (DSEK) surgery with pre-cut donor grafts from the eye bank. She was counseled about the study and provided with an informed consent document to read and sign. The patient was found to be eligible for the clinical trial and was enrolled for the study. She underwent successful DSEK surgery with pre-cut donor grafts and was scheduled for follow-up visits to assess the outcomes of the procedure.

A 58-year-old male non-smoker was diagnosed with stage 1B non-small cell lung cancer in his right lung lobe. He had no prior history of cancer and was in good health. He underwent surgical removal of the tumor and had no adjuvant therapy. The tumor specimen was stored as part of his previous clinical trial participation. The patient has signed a written informed consent document for this study and is willing to provide additional tumor tissue for biomarker analysis. He has no known allergies and is currently taking medication for hypertension.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is HIV-negative and sexually active. She is currently using a combination of condoms and oral contraceptives to prevent pregnancy. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications or supplements. She is a nonsmoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has a regular menstrual cycle and her last menstrual period was 10 days ago. She is willing to abstain from sexual activity for the duration of the study period. Her BMI is 22 kg/m2 and her total body weight is 60 kg. She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and lifestyle guidelines. She has no history of abnormal bleeding or bruising, kidney disease, alcoholism or drug abuse, significant gastrointestinal bleeding, or severe or recent cardiac or pulmonary events. She has not used any hormonal contraceptives within the last 30 days and has not received Depo-Provera within the last 120 days. She has not tested positive for Neisseria gonorrhoea, Chlamydia trachomatis, Trichomonas vaginalis, or syphilis at screening. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She meets all other inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria for this study.

50-year-old female presents with chronic constipation, incomplete evacuation, and a feeling of a blockage in the rectum. She has tried various laxatives, enemas and dietary modifications without much relief. On physical examination, she has a rectocele and a redundant sigmoid colon. Colonoscopy shows no significant findings. MRI defecography reveals a rectocele, enterocele and a significant descent of the pelvic floor. She is scheduled for a STARR procedure to relieve her outlet obstruction. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or any other bowel or rectal disorders.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman with a diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) per ACR criteria. She has a past medical history of SLE for the last 5 years and has been treated with hydroxychloroquine and prednisone. She has no other significant past medical history and has not been diagnosed with any chronic infections or cancer. She is not pregnant and is between the ages of 18 and 65. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on lupus and its treatment options.

A 58-year-old woman was diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma 2 years ago after experiencing vision loss in her right eye. She has been using brimonidine 0.2% eye drops for the past 6 months to manage her intraocular pressure but has noticed persistent eye redness as a side effect. She is a retired teacher who enjoys reading and gardening. She has no known allergies to medications and has not had any surgeries or procedures in the past 6 months. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she takes no other medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the potential benefit of Lumify™ in reducing eye redness while maintaining her glaucoma medication regimen.

A 35-year-old male patient presents with a 4-month history of non-bloody, watery diarrhea that has not responded to conventional antidiarrheal medication, including Lomotil and Imodium. The patient has a documented HIV infection, and the diarrhea has become so severe that it is affecting his quality of life. He reports having 5-7 bowel movements per day, with each episode lasting for approximately 30 minutes. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications or supplements. He is willing and able to self-administer injections of study medication and has a responsible family member who can assist if needed. The patient provides written consent prior to study entry. The patient has not received experimental antidiarrheal drugs within one month of study entry and does not have evidence of co-existing conditions such as idiopathic ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, or acute stool culture positive bacterial colitis. The patient's stool weight averages over 500 g/day during the 2 baseline periods.

A 55-year-old Chinese man was diagnosed with hypertension 3 years ago. He has been taking enalapril for the past 2 years and has been experiencing dry cough as a side effect. He has no history of stroke or any other cardiovascular diseases. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 29. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of drug allergies or any other significant medical conditions. His current medication includes enalapril and a daily multivitamin supplement. He is willing to participate in the study and provide blood samples for genetic testing.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been suffering from recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS) for the past 5 years. She experiences bouts of shallow, painful oral ulcers every 2-3 months, which last for about a week and affect her ability to eat and speak. She has tried various over-the-counter medications and topical treatments, but with limited success. She has no autoimmune diseases or immunosuppressive conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is Caucasian, non-pregnant, and does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of probiotics on the microbiome in saliva and feces, as well as the severity and frequency of RAS outbreaks.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has undergone neoadjuvant chemoradiation consisting of 6 cycles of gemcitabine and nb-paclitaxel. The patient is eligible for surgery and is scheduled to undergo a Whipple procedure. However, the surgical team has identified close margins, and therefore the patient is a candidate for brachytherapy treatment with the CivaSheet. The patient has not received prior radiation therapy for any other cancer and does not have metastatic disease. The patient is medically fit to undergo anesthesia and has signed an informed consent to participate in this initial feasibility study. The patient has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of colon cancer. He was diagnosed with stage III colon cancer three years ago and underwent surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX regimen. He had no evidence of recurrence until a year ago when he developed abdominal pain and was found to have multiple liver and lung metastases. He received multiple lines of chemotherapy including FOLFIRI and FOLFOXIRI, but his disease continued to progress. His last MRI scan showed further progression of his disease and he was referred to the clinical trial. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has adequate function of liver, kidneys and bone marrow. Genetic testing revealed KRAS mutation in his primary tumour. He has measurable disease according to RECIST and is willing to provide blood samples and paraffin embedded tissue for translational research. He is not currently on any other experimental treatment and has no other significant medical conditions. He has a history of smoking and has quit recently. He is married with two adult children and works as a sales manager. He is willing to use efficient birth control during the study.

54 yo F with personal history of gastric cancer diagnosed at age 48, with no family history of the disease. Patient underwent total gastrectomy and has been followed up regularly without recurrence. Genetic testing revealed a pathogenic germline mutation in the CDH1 gene. Patient has no other personal history of cancer and no history of other gastric cancer syndromes. Patient's first-degree relatives have not undergone genetic testing for CDH1 mutation. Past Medical History: - Gastric cancer diagnosed at age 48 - Total gastrectomy - CDH1 gene mutation

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is concerned about his health and has a family history of obesity and diabetes. He has been trying to make changes to his diet and has been considering switching from sugar-sweetened beverages to artificially sweetened beverages as a way to lower his calorie intake. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help determine if this switch is beneficial for his overall health and reduce his risk for developing obesity and diabetes. He is willing to follow a specific diet plan and drink either water or artificially sweetened beverages as instructed by the study protocol. The patient is in good health and has no known medical conditions, is not taking any medications, and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past.

Patient A is a 40-year-old female who has struggled with weight loss for the past few years. She has a BMI of 33 and is considered obese. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She works as a teacher and is a mother of two children. She has tried various diets and weight loss programs in the past, but has not been able to maintain long-term weight loss. She is motivated to participate in this clinical trial to learn more about how an almond enriched hypocaloric diet can help her lose weight and improve her overall health. She enjoys nuts and has no known allergies or sensitivities. She is willing to comply with all study-related procedures and is excited to join a group of like-minded individuals who are also focused on improving their health through weight loss.

A 55-year-old male smoker presents with a persistent cough and increasing shortness of breath. He reports a weight loss of 5 kg over the past 2 months, loss of appetite, and fatigue. He has a history of heavy alcohol use and hypertension. His physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. A chest X-ray reveals a large mass in the right lung. A subsequent CT scan confirms a 6 cm mass in the right upper lobe with mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy. The biopsy confirms non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has no prior history of cancer or exposure to chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, or biological therapy. His ECOG performance status score is 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for mild anemia and elevated liver function tests. The patient is willing to comply with the trial and follow-up procedures and is able to understand the nature of the trial and give written informed consent.

This is a 28-year-old healthy male with a normal BMI, who has not been diagnosed with any chronic disease or any abnormal medical examination results. He is a non-smoker and does not consume excessive amounts of caffeine or alcohol. He has not participated in any clinical investigations within the past 60 days and has not donated whole blood within the past 60 days, or component blood within the past 30 days. He has no history of drug abuse, and does not have any known hypersensitivity to acebrophylline, xanthine or food. He has not been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal disease or undergone gastrointestinal surgery that could affect drug absorption. The subject has no serious active cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatologic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, immunologic, dermal, neurologic, or psychological disease or history of such disease. He has signed and dated an informed consent form indicating that he has decided to participate in the study after being informed of all pertinent aspects of the study.

A 30 yo F with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy. She is premenopausal, has regular menstrual cycles, and has a uterus and ovaries. She is interested in preserving her fertility and would like to participate in a study to assess changes in her ovarian reserve before, during, and after chemotherapy. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and has provided written informed consent. She does not have any medical conditions known to be associated with premature ovarian failure or ovulatory dysfunction, and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

A 29-year-old woman is currently 10 weeks pregnant and seeking routine antenatal care. She has a personal history of mild asthma, which is usually triggered by seasonal allergies. Her symptoms include occasional wheezing and shortness of breath, which are relieved by using her inhaler. Her partner also has a history of asthma. She has not been taking any vitamin E supplements but is interested in optimizing her vitamin E intake during pregnancy to reduce the risk of her child developing asthma. She is willing to give informed consent to participate in the study procedures and is able to comply with the requirements of the study. She does not have any other significant medical conditions or taking any medications that may interfere with the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old veteran who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for the past 3 months. The pain is described as dull and achy, and is worse with prolonged sitting or standing. The pain score is 6 out of 10 on the pain scale. The patient has not undergone any lumbar spine surgery in the past and is not on any prescription medications affecting musculoskeletal pain. The patient reports no progressive neurologic deficits due to nerve root or spinal cord compression. He is not involved in any litigation pertaining to back pain or workers compensation claims. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of tailored education/exercise (E/E) intervention alone vs. E/E plus chiropractic care for chronic low back pain. The patient is enrolled in VA medical care and meets the eligibility criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) for over a year. He presents with symptoms such as difficulty initiating urination, weak urine stream, frequent urination, and nocturia. He reports an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) of 15 and an IPSS Quality of Life (QoL) score of 4. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 8 ng/mL. He has not undergone any previous treatment for BPH. He has no history of prostate cancer, acute urinary retention (AUR), or lower urinary tract instrumentation within the past 30 days. He has no other significant medical history or current medication use. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive with her husband for the past year presents with a history of two previous miscarriages at 8 weeks and 10 weeks of gestation. She has regular menstrual cycles and no history of endocrine disorders or abnormal uterine cavity. She and her husband have a regular marital life with no consanguinity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the role of mucosal-associated invariant T cells in cases of miscarriage.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of diverticulitis and a recent diagnosis of colon cancer. He is scheduled to undergo an elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery with the creation of an anastomosis, located 10 cm proximal from the anal verge. He is in good general health and is willing to comply with the protocol-specified follow-up evaluations. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days and does not have any contraindications to general anesthesia. His internal diameter lumen of the colon falls within the range of 25-34 mm. He has not experienced any recent major surgical or interventional procedures, and has not been taking regular steroid medication in the last 6 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing abnormal uterine bleeding for the past six months. She has a family history of endometrial cancer. She is currently not on any hormone replacement therapy. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control her blood pressure. She is a retired teacher and lives with her husband. She has no history of smoking or drug use. She is concerned about her abnormal bleeding and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help diagnose her condition. Her BMI is within the normal range, and she exercises regularly. She has no history of cervical cancer or coagulation disorders. She is not pregnant or suspecting pregnancy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension presents with pain in his right lower leg after walking for a few minutes. The pain is relieved after resting for a few minutes. He also reports a tingling sensation and numbness in his toes. On physical examination, the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are weak, and there is decreased sensation in the right foot. An ankle-brachial index (ABI) is performed, and the result is 0.7. The patient is diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) with Rutherford classification 5. An angiogram shows a 90% stenosis in the below-knee popliteal artery. The patient is currently taking medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who gave birth to her first child two weeks ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath since delivery. Her prenatal labs showed that she had iron deficiency anemia, and her hemoglobin level was 9.5 g/dL at the time of delivery. Her postpartum course has been uncomplicated, and she is currently breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of her anemia. She has no known allergies or medical conditions other than anemia. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is willing to practice birth control during the study period.

As this is a retrospective data analysis study, there is no need for a patient description. The study will use patient data from the Hungarian National Health Insurance Fund's Database, and patients who have received at least one dose of regorafenib treatment cycle will be included in the analysis.

A 63-year-old male patient with end-stage lung disease has been on the waiting list for a bilateral lung transplant for 6 months. He is currently on supplemental oxygen and experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion. He has a history of smoking and quit 10 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has been informed about the option of participating in this clinical trial and has provided informed consent for participation.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who sustained partial thickness burns to his lower limbs after being involved in a house fire. The burns cover approximately 20% of his body surface area and are located primarily on the anterior and lateral aspects of both legs. He was admitted to the hospital for wound care and pain management. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently receiving IV fluids and opioid pain medication for pain management. He is not intubated or sedated and does not have any facial burns. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible for enrollment.

Patient A is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing gum recession and sensitivity around her teeth. She has noticed that her teeth look longer than before and there is less gum tissue covering them. She has a history of gum disease and has lost several teeth due to it. She is a non-smoker and has no known systemic diseases. She is interested in undergoing a soft tissue graft to improve the appearance of her gums and reduce sensitivity. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and return for follow-up visits. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to sign it. She has no known allergies to cyanoacrylate.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with schizophrenia and alcohol dependence. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been unable to abstain from alcohol for more than a few days at a time. He has been treated with multiple oral medications to help with alcohol dependence, but has not been able to maintain sobriety. He currently takes an antipsychotic medication and a mood stabilizer for his schizophrenia. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will compare the effectiveness of a new long-acting injectable form of naltrexone to the traditional oral form of the medication. He has reported drinking alcohol on at least four days during the 30 days prior to enrollment in the study. He is currently receiving outpatient psychiatric treatment at a study site and has been involved in the community for the past six months. He has no history of opioid use and has a negative urine screen for opiates. The study physician has determined that he meets all eligibility criteria and is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial.

62 yo M with a history of BPH and LUTS that has been unresponsive to medical therapy. He has an IPSS score of 22 and a QOL score of 4. His peak urinary flow rate (Qmax) is 12 ml/sec with a voided volume of 150 ml. He has a TRUS prostate size of 95 ml. He is not currently on anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy but takes low-dose aspirin (100 mg) daily. He has an ASA score of 2 and has no neurological disorders affecting bladder function. He does not have active urinary tract infections or bladder cancer and has not had an acute myocardial infarction or open-heart surgery in the past 180 days. He is interested in participating in the trial to explore alternative treatment options for his condition.

This clinical trial is not applicable for an individual patient as it is a population-based intervention targeting 7th grade students and their caregivers in 12 enrolled schools in medically underserved Appalachian counties in southwest Virginia. Students who are in the 7th grade and enrolled in the 12 selected schools during the years their school is randomized to one of the cohorts are eligible to participate. Parents/caregivers of the enrolled middle school students are also eligible to participate. However, data from students with major cognitive disabilities that could compromise self-report behavioral data quality will be excluded. Overall, the aim of this trial is to determine the effectiveness of Kids SIPsmartER in improving sugar-sweetened beverages behaviors among 7th grade students and their caregivers, with the secondary aim of assessing changes in secondary student outcomes, caregiver SSB behaviors and home environment, and maintenance of outcomes at 19-months post-baseline.

28-year-old pregnant female in her third trimester of pregnancy with no prior history of cesarean section, pelvic tuberculosis, genital tract cancer or ectopic pregnancy. She is attending prenatal care and desires to use the Copper T380 intrauterine contraceptive device (CuT380A-IUCD) for contraception postpartum. She plans to stay in the area for at least 5 months postpartum. She is not known to have ruptured membranes for greater than 24 hours prior to delivery, has no infection diagnosed by a clinician, and no fever of greater than 38° during labor or delivery. She is willing to be randomized to receive the IUD immediately postpartum or at the 6-week postpartum visit. She will be followed at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after IUD insertion, and be assessed at those time points for satisfaction with the method and IUD expulsion.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who lives in Indiana with her husband and two children. She is eligible for SNAP and is interested in participating in SNAP-Ed lessons to improve her dietary habits. The patient speaks and reads English fluently and is willing to complete three 45 minute surveys and up to 2 dietary recalls and a food frequency questionnaire at the designated time intervals. She is willing to stay in touch with research staff during the study period. The patient has not participated in NEP lessons within the last year and is not pregnant. She is willing to wait 1 year to start FNP lessons. The patient has access to a computer with high-speed internet connection at her home and is comfortable with using it. She is willing to complete the assessments via telephone with assistance from researchers if needed. The patient is interested in improving her food security and dietary quality and maintaining her BMI.

This is a 49 year old female with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who was diagnosed with stage III HER2-positive breast cancer in the left breast. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and trastuzumab, followed by a left modified radical mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. Pathological examination revealed a complete pathological response in the breast and axillary lymph nodes. She received adjuvant radiation therapy and is currently on trastuzumab as maintenance therapy. She has been in complete remission for 40 months. She has provided consent for use of her archived tissue samples for this study.

A 45-year-old woman visited the dental clinic with a complaint of toothache. She had undergone root canal treatment for her left lower first molar 2 months ago. She has no history of systemic diseases, and her oral hygiene is good. The periapical x-ray showed no evident damage and no root fracture. The dentist noticed that there were three walls of intact tooth tissue after root canal treatment. The patient was informed about the clinical trial comparing the comfort and durability of Ceramic vs Resin Block Endocrown and she agreed to participate. She signed the informed consent form and was assessed according to FDI criteria for marginal adaptation after restoration, receiving a class A assessment. She has no history of mental illness or systemic diseases and is capable of self-care.

A 20-year old college student was diagnosed with glucose transporter type 1 deficiency (G1D) when he was 7 years old. He has been on a ketogenic diet for the last 10 years, which consists of high fat, low carbohydrate, and adequate protein. He has a history of seizures that are well-controlled on his current medication regimen, which includes Levetiracetam and Topiramate. He experiences occasional headaches but denies any other neurological symptoms. He has no known allergies and is not taking any new medications. He lives on campus and has a healthy social life. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to explore the compatibility of C7 oil with his ketogenic diet, and he understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study.

A 55-year-old male presents to the clinic with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. He has a blood pressure range of 130/85 mmHg and is currently on medication for his hypertension. The patient has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. He also has a family history of heart disease. The patient underwent an angiogram that revealed the presence of coronary artery disease. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help reduce the progression of atherosclerosis in his coronary arteries.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who is generally in good health. She has no history of physical or psychiatric disorders and does not consume drugs or alcohol. She speaks German fluently and is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the effects of emotional stimulation on mood. She is willing to complete questionnaires and participate in the required activities as part of the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been experiencing urinary symptoms, such as difficulty urinating and frequent urination, for the past 6 months. His PSA level is slightly elevated at 5.5 ng/mL, and his digital rectal exam (DRE) shows a hard nodule on the left lobe of the prostate gland. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient has no known allergies and is not claustrophobic. However, he has a history of metal implants in his right knee due to an injury sustained during his military service. The patient is willing to undergo further diagnostic testing to determine the cause of his symptoms and has been referred for a multi-parametric prostate MRI to assess the prostate gland. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the accuracy of prostate cancer detection and has agreed to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. He reports that the pain has been progressively getting worse and has started to affect his daily activities, such as climbing stairs and walking for extended periods of time. He rates his pain as a 7 out of 10 on the VAS pain scale. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee by his primary care physician. He has not had any corticosteroid injections in the past month or systemic corticosteroid use in the past two weeks. He does not have any autoimmune diseases or recent serious illnesses. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. His platelet count is within normal range and his hemoglobin levels are above 10 g/dL. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressants and is not enrolled in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who had a stroke 6 months ago. He has been experiencing difficulty with walking and has been using a cane for support since then. He has a caregiver, his wife, who provides assistance with his daily activities. He has some cognitive impairment due to the stroke but is able to understand instructions. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication to control his blood pressure. He is a retired office worker and spends most of his time at home. He has a small apartment with limited space for walking. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his walking ability and reduce his dependency on the cane. He is willing to learn how to use the Moterum iStride Solution™ and the Moterum Digital Platform for telemedicine communication. He is motivated to participate in the study and hopes to see improvement in his gait function. His weight is within the limit of 275lbs.

Pt is a 35yo M with a history of schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder, currently a member of Kaiser Permanente Northwest (KPNW). Pt has been stable on medications for the past year and is interested in participating in a low-cost, joint consumer/counselor-led health education and support intervention that will foster self-care and recovery. The patient is able to attend group sessions and complete questionnaires, and has no psychotic symptoms that interfere with group interactions. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve his recovery and functioning.

This is a 42 year-old male who presents with a history of right-sided inguinal hernia. He reports intermittent pain and discomfort in the area for the past year, which has worsened in the past month. He reports no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Physical exam reveals a reducible right inguinal hernia. The patient has elected to undergo surgical repair of the hernia and has been scheduled for the procedure. He has an ASA physical status classification of II. He has no history of systemic hypertension, cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular insufficiency, coagulation abnormalities, renal or hepatic insufficiency, infection at the injection site, strangulated hernia, or hypersensitivity to local anesthetics.

6 year old girl with history of recurrent UTIs and known congenital abnormalities of the urinary tract, currently being followed by a pediatric urologist. She has had multiple DMSA scans in the past to evaluate for renal scarring. She is otherwise healthy and has no known contraindications to MRI. She is scheduled for another DMSA scan as part of her routine clinical care and is approached about participating in the study. Her parents are interested in a potential alternative to the DMSA scan and consent to her participation.

A 48-year-old male, native English speaker, is seeking treatment for chronic low back pain. The patient has a history of lumbar spine surgery for lumbar spondylosis and disc protrusion, which was performed 8 months ago. The patient has been experiencing moderate to severe low back pain, with occasional leg pain, since the surgery. The patient is not currently receiving compensation or disability benefits and is not using illicit drugs or opioids. The patient has no severe physical impairments or co-morbid medical conditions that would significantly impair physical functional status. The patient is willing to participate in the longitudinal follow-up study for up to 6 months after the surgery. The patient is able to read and speak fluent English and is willing to provide written informed consent. The patient has not been diagnosed with any major diseases or diagnoses that may influence pain or function. The patient has not been previously diagnosed with fibromyalgia and scores less than 3 on the 2011 FM Survey Criteria.

54 year old female with a new diagnosis of primary glioma, presenting with a 6-month history of increasing headaches, nausea, and vomiting. She also reports difficulty sleeping and feeling fatigued during the day. MRI shows a left parietal lobe glioma, with significant mass effect and midline shift. She has no history of seizures or other neurological disorders. The patient has been started on corticosteroids and referred for radiation therapy. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. Medications: lisinopril, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen as needed.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) within the last year at Northwestern University Sleep Clinic. He has documented mild to moderate OSA and qualifies as "very sleepy" on the Epworth Sleepiness Scale. His neck circumference is 18.5 cm. He has never undergone neck liposuction before and does not have any significant medical history. He has no allergies to lidocaine or epinephrine. He does not take any blood thinners and has no bleeding diathesis. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has a Body Mass Index of 28kg/m2. The patient is otherwise healthy and is able to undergo the liposuction procedure. He has been offered continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment but has declined it due to discomfort. The patient is interested in exploring other options to help alleviate his OSA symptoms and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 38-year-old male employee working in the Pragati Textile Industry Private Limited, Nepal, who has been diagnosed with pre-diabetes, with a HbA1c level of 6.2%. He has a family history of diabetes, and his BMI is 28. He is interested in participating in the work-site intervention study to prevent diabetes. He is not taking any medication for hypertension or diabetes, and he is not pregnant. He is willing to attend the education sessions and follow the dietary recommendations. He is excited to participate in the study and is hopeful that the interventions will help him prevent diabetes and improve his overall health.

45 yo M with a history of secondary liver cancer and scheduled for hepatic embolization procedure to treat the tumor. The patient has no known history of cirrhosis or anemia, and has normal liver function markers (ALT, AST, and bilirubin), INR, and platelet count. The patient has no known allergies to acetaminophen and is willing to take extra strength acetaminophen (4g/day) for the 3 days prior to the procedure as part of the study. The patient is willing to have blood drawn at least 12 times for research purposes and to stay for ~18-21 hours after being discharged from the Department of Radiology. The patient is willing to complete a study diary for 3 days prior to and the day of the procedure and will refrain from using acetaminophen, other than the study drug, during the dosing phase through a minimum of 5 days post-procedure. The patient is willing to consume less than 3 alcoholic drinks per day while taking study drug (acetaminophen group only) and will be in the Denver metro area for the duration of the study. The patient is not currently enrolled in a clinical trial, has not participated in a clinical trial within the 30 days prior to the procedure, and does not plan to participate in a clinical trial during the 5 day post-procedure follow-up period.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and jaundice for the past 6 months. She has a history of gallstones and has had a cholecystectomy 2 years ago. Her medical history includes hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is scheduled to undergo therapeutic biliary ERCP due to suspected choledocholithiasis. However, her biliary cannulation proves to be difficult, with unsuccessful attempts after 5 minutes. She is otherwise healthy and meets the inclusion criteria for this study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with atrial fibrillation six months ago. He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well controlled with medication. He is scheduled to undergo electrical cardioversion in two weeks. He has no history of limb trauma or upper limb artery stenosis. He is not currently taking any vasoconstrictive agents. He is able to give written informed consent to participate in the study. During the study, he will be awake, fasting, and in a supine position. He will be admitted to the hospital for the procedure and all measurements will be taken in the intensive care unit at an ambient temperature of 21°C. He will undergo ankle brachial index measurements using both oscillometric and Doppler methods before and after electrical cardioversion. The measurements will be repeated three times with each method and the mean will be used for the calculations. The study nurse, trained at the vascular department, will perform all ABI measurements.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is in good health and has no history of chronic illnesses. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and leads an active lifestyle. She does not smoke and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient reports that she has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions and is not currently taking any prescription medications or supplements. She has not experienced any viral or bacterial infections within the past 21 days. The patient is interested in participating in clinical research and is willing to undergo medical tests and procedures as part of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently admitted to the hospital due to a severe flare-up of Crohn's disease. She has been experiencing severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, and vomiting, and has lost a significant amount of weight over the past few weeks. Upon admission, her lab tests showed that she was severely malnourished and in need of intravenous nutrition. The patient has a history of Crohn's disease for 10 years and has had multiple hospitalizations for disease exacerbations in the past. She has tried various medications for Crohn's disease management, including steroids, immunomodulators, and biologic therapies, but has not achieved adequate control of her symptoms. She has also had a history of iron-deficiency anemia and has received iron infusions in the past. The patient is currently on no medications other than those for Crohn's disease management. She has no known allergies and has never smoked or used recreational drugs. The patient speaks fluent English and is able to provide a 1 liter breath sample daily for the study. She is expected to stay in the hospital for at least 7 days from enrollment and is willing to participate in the study to help further research on nutritional status in patients receiving intravenous nutrition.

A 35 year old woman came to the clinic for a gynecological surgery. She has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding and lower abdominal pain for the past few months. She is physically active, with a BMI of 24. She has no known allergies to any medication and is currently taking no medications. She has a history of sinus bradycardia but it is well managed with medication. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The doctors believe that she is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial due to her age and medical history.

A 9-year-old boy is admitted to the gastroenterology unit of Assuit University Children Hospital with a history of chronic diarrhea for the past 3 weeks. The patient's parents report that he has had more than 3 loose stools per day, which are watery and foul-smelling. The patient has also experienced abdominal cramping and occasional vomiting. He has no history of fever or weight loss. The patient has been given oral rehydration solutions (ORS) at home, but the symptoms persist. The patient has no significant past medical history or family history of gastrointestinal disorders. The physical examination reveals mild dehydration, with dry mucous membranes, sunken eyes, and decreased skin turgor. The abdomen is soft, with no hepatosplenomegaly, and no palpable masses. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of being between 1 month to 17 years of age and having diarrhea for 14 days or more.

An 80-year-old male presents with a history of recurrent episodes of depression over the past 5 years. He describes feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated. He reports difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in his hobbies. He has no history of manic or psychotic symptoms. His medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoarthritis. He takes lisinopril and acetaminophen as needed for pain. He denies any history of substance abuse. He has a Mini Mental State Examination score of 28. He has not taken any antipsychotics in the past 3 months, fluoxetine in the past month, monoamine oxidase inhibitors in the past 4 weeks, or any other antidepressants or mood stabilizers in the past week. He meets the DSM-IV-TR criteria for major depressive disorder and has a total score of 25 on the MADRS and a total score of 18 on the HAM-D. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of saredutant in elderly patients with major depressive disorder.

This is a 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus who has been experiencing symptoms of autonomic neuropathy for the past year. She has difficulty breathing and feels short of breath, particularly when performing physical activities such as climbing stairs or walking uphill. She also experiences fatigue and weakness in her respiratory muscles. She has no history of congestive heart failure or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and her body mass index is within normal range. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of inspiratory muscle training on her respiratory muscle strength and to potentially alleviate her autonomic dysfunction. She has read and signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who has been living with HIV for 5 years. He has been receiving highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) and has a viral load of less than 50 copies/ml and a CD4+ T cell count of 200 cells/mm3. He is currently taking a regimen that includes one NNRTI and two NRTIs. He has experienced some side effects from the medication, including nausea and fatigue, but has been able to manage them with over-the-counter remedies. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that is testing the effectiveness of intermittent short cycles of HAART in maintaining viral suppression and CD4+ T cell counts while minimizing toxicity and improving patient lifestyle. He is willing to comply with the medication regimen and attend regular clinic visits for blood tests and leukapheresis every 3 to 4 months while on the study. He has no significant medical history, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and practices safe sex.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with moderate Alzheimer's disease with a score of Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) of 15. He has been taking memantine for the past 2 months but has not seen any significant improvement in his cognitive function. His serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25OHD] concentration is found to be < 30 ng/mL indicating hypovitaminosis D. The patient has no history of hypercalcemia or any other severe medical conditions. He has given his informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient does not have any contraindications to memantine or vitamin D, and he is not enrolled in any other clinical trial.

A 45-year-old female presented with shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue, and occasional chest pain for the past 3 months. She has a history of Sjogren's syndrome, diagnosed 5 years ago, and has been on hydroxychloroquine and prednisone therapy with good control of symptoms. She denies any recent infections, surgeries, or hospitalizations. She has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. Her vital signs were stable on initial evaluation. Physical examination revealed decreased breath sounds at the lung bases and mild jugular venous distension. Echocardiography showed right ventricular dilation and hypertrophy with an estimated pulmonary arterial systolic pressure of 60 mmHg. Further evaluation with right heart catheterization confirmed the diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension with a mean pulmonary arterial pressure of 40 mmHg, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 12 mmHg, and pulmonary vascular resistance of 750 dyn•s•cm5. She has been on combination therapy of bosentan and sildenafil for the past 4 months with good symptom control. Her modified New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class was II. She was approached and provided with information about a clinical trial involving a single infusion of tezosentan and has agreed to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer. He has been experiencing persistent abdominal discomfort, bloating, and nausea for the past few months. A CT scan has revealed the presence of a large tumor in the stomach and several small nodules in the liver. The patient has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and he has an estimated life expectancy of more than 3 months. His blood work shows adequate kidney and liver function, and his bone marrow function is also normal. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy, and his last radiation therapy was more than 4 weeks ago. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for advanced gastric cancer and meets the eligibility criteria for this phase II trial evaluating the response rate of combination chemotherapy with S-1 and Irinotecan as a first-line therapy.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes after presenting with symptoms of increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. Her fasting plasma glucose was found to be between 200-300 mg/dl (A1C level between 7% and 10%). She has not been previously treated with any anti-diabetic medication. She is able to self-administer insulin injections and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any history of liver or renal impairment or recent cardiovascular events. Her 2-hour C-peptide level is above 1.8 ng/mL. She has no other significant medical history but is slightly overweight with a BMI of 27 kg/m². She is currently not taking any medication and is excited to participate in the study to help manage her diabetes.

Patient is a 50-year-old man who lives in Miami-Dade county, Florida. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He has a high school diploma and has some college education. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history. He has never had to deal with end-of-life issues personally but has some knowledge about hospice care through friends and family members. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about end-of-life issues and to contribute to research that may help improve care for patients and families facing these difficult situations.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. He has no prior history of heart disease, but his doctor recommended OAC due to his increased risk of stroke. The patient is hesitant to start taking medication and has concerns about the potential risks and side effects. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of the benefits and risks of OAC and to make an informed decision about his treatment options. He is able to provide informed consent and has no history of valve surgery or existing OAC therapy.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He has undergone cardiac catheterization which showed significant three-vessel disease. He was scheduled for a coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and modified ultrafiltration. He has a documented allergy to penicillin and is prescribed vancomycin as a prophylactic antibiotic. The patient has normal renal and liver function and has no clinical or laboratory signs of infection. Preoperatively his laboratory values were within normal limits, including a creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, an AST of 25 U/L, and an ALT of 20 U/L. He was not obese or pregnant, nor did he have a vancomycin allergy or any active infections. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance the knowledge of the effects of modified ultrafiltration on vancomycin levels during cardiac surgery.

A 38-year-old Caucasian male with a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis presents with complaints of foot pain and difficulty walking. He reports a gradual onset of pain in his left foot over the past year, which has worsened in the last 3 months. He describes the pain as a dull ache that is worse with prolonged walking or standing. He also reports difficulty walking and a feeling of instability in his left foot. He denies any recent injuries or trauma to his foot.
