He has been on medication for his ankylosing spondylitis for the past 5 years and reports good control of his symptoms. He has no history of ankle surgery, muscle disease, or neuropsychiatric illnesses. He reports good balance and vision. He is married and works as a computer programmer. He is physically active, regularly participating in swimming and cycling. He is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester with a normal pregnancy history and a singleton cephalic presentation at term is eligible for this clinical trial. She has an ASA physical status of I or II and is in the early active phase of labor. She has no diagnosed fetal abnormalities and is not morbidly obese. She has no contra-indications to regional anesthesia.

46-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 6 years. She has been on methotrexate for the past year and has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. Her disease activity is high, with more than 10 tender and swollen joints, and her hsCRP level is >10mg/L. She has not been exposed to secukinumab or any other biologic medication for the treatment of her RA. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is not currently using any investigational drugs or devices.

A 55-year-old man with a history of heavy alcohol use is scheduled for elective surgery in the next four months. He has been referred to participate in this research study to assess the efficacy of pre-operative alcohol use reduction interventions. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He reports drinking 4-5 drinks per day on average for the past 10 years. The patient is motivated to reduce his alcohol use and is willing to participate in the study. He is physically able to attend two intervention sessions and complete study questionnaires. The patient is not currently experiencing any psychotic symptoms and his surgery requires general anesthesia.

A 29-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 is interested in participating in the clinical trial for IBD98-M. Upon medical screening, she reports no clinically significant illnesses or surgeries within the past 4 weeks. She has no history of neurological, endocrinal, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematological, immunologic, psychiatric, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic, or metabolic disease. She has never been diagnosed with pyloric stenosis, gastric or duodenal ulcers, or urinary tract obstruction. She is sexually active with a male partner and agrees to use an intra-uterine contraceptive device for at least 4 weeks prior to study drug administration and throughout the study. She is capable of giving informed consent. She has never had an allergic reaction to mesalamine, salicylates, aminosalicylates, hyaluronic acid, or related drugs. She tests negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV. She does not use drugs or consume more than 14 units of alcohol per week. She has not participated in a clinical trial involving the administration of an investigational or marketed drug within the past 30 days. She has not used prescription medication within 14 days prior to the first dosing and over-the-counter products within 7 days prior to the first dosing, with the exception of the occasional use of acetaminophen (up to 2 g daily). She has not donated plasma within 7 days prior to dosing and has not lost more than 499 mL of blood within 56 days prior to the first dosing. Her hemoglobin level is 135 g/L and hematocrit level is 0.41 L/L at screening. She is not breastfeeding.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent a renal transplant two years ago due to end-stage renal disease. He was diagnosed with Hepatitis C virus (HCV) Genotype 4 after the transplant and has been stable on immunosuppressive therapy. His current creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min, indicating stable graft function. He has not received any treatment for HCV so far. The patient has no history of significant psychiatric disorder, has not participated in any investigational compound trials in the last 30 days, and is willing to comply with the study procedures. His recent blood chemistry (3 days ago) was normal: Hgb: 13.5 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 150000 /ml PT: 11 second PTT: 35 second INR: 0.9 Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl U/A: Color: yellow Appearance: clear PH: 5.5 Specific gravity: 1.015 Glc: negative Nitrite: negative Ketone: none Leukocyte esterase: negative RBC: negative WBC: 0 WBCs/hpf U/C: negative. The patient understands the study procedures, alternative treatments available, risks involved with the study and voluntarily agrees to participate by giving written informed consent.

55-year-old female with a clinical and radiographic diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee, previously treated with NSAIDs but withdrew due to side effects. The patient is currently experiencing a flare of signs and symptoms of OA and is classified as functional class II. She has no other clinically significant diseases and is post-menopausal. The patient has no history of neoplastic or malabsorption diseases and is not taking any of the excluded medications.

A 22-year-old woman recently discovered she is pregnant and has decided to terminate the pregnancy. She is currently at 18 weeks gestation and has scheduled a dilation and evacuation (D&E) procedure. She has no known history of bleeding disorders or thromboembolic events. She is able and willing to give informed consent and is able to understand and sign written consents in English. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and is otherwise healthy.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He is a non-smoker and exercises regularly by doing cardio exercises for an hour thrice a week. He has no history of chronic or acute infections, renal, hepatic, pulmonary, neurological or psychiatric diseases, and has not been diagnosed with diabetes. He does not have any known alcohol, substance or drug abuse, or concomitant medication. He typically consumes one 12 oz can of soda per day and has no other significant dietary restrictions. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the impact of sugar sweetened beverages on his metabolism. He understands the study protocol and is willing to comply with it.

As this is a registry study for safety surveillance of Dazhuhongjingtian injection in China, a patient description is not needed. The study will be conducted on patients who are already receiving Dazhuhongjingtian injection in the selected hospitals from 2017 to 2019. Therefore, patients will not be recruited for this study.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing occasional constipation for the past few months. She has been having less than 3 bowel movements per week and has been experiencing hard stools and the feeling of incomplete evacuation. She has not been under a doctor's care for her constipation, and she has not used any other products or therapies to treat it. She is in good health as determined by laboratory results, medical history, and physical exam. She has a BMI of 25.2 kg/m2, and she agrees not to change her current dietary habits, smoking habits, and activity levels during the study. She has given voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the trial. She has not suffered from chronic constipation due to any underlying cause or any of the other exclusion criteria listed above.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male who has experienced sudden vision loss in his left eye. He visited an ophthalmologist and was diagnosed with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) which has been present for less than 6 months. His visual acuity in the affected eye is between 20/800 to 20/50. He has not received any previous treatment with anti-angiogenic drugs. He has no history of any other ocular disorders or surgeries. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate if intravitreal bevacizumab can improve his visual acuity compared to the control group.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman of Indian origin who has been trying to conceive for the past 3 years with her husband. They have been unsuccessful in their attempts and have sought medical help. She has a history of menstrual irregularities and has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). She has never undergone any fertility treatment before. She is a vegetarian and follows a healthy diet. She doesn't smoke or consume alcohol. She works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. She has a BMI of 28. Her labs show elevated LH and FSH levels and an ultrasound confirms the presence of multiple cysts in her ovaries. She has no other significant medical history. She and her husband have agreed to participate in the study and undergo IVF/ICSI treatment.

52-year-old male with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for 8 years. He has been managing his diabetes with Metformin, but his recent lipid profile shows LDL-C levels of 3.1 mmol/l, which is above the new European guidelines. He has not been on any cholesterol-lowering medication for the past 3 months. He has a BMI of 28, blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, and HbA1c of 7.2%. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or any other significant medical conditions. The patient has agreed to start taking Crestor 10mg and has given permission to use his data for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman living in India who has been diagnosed with HIV infection. She has not had any previous treatment for cervical precancer or cancer. She is currently not pregnant and has no history of cervical, vaginal, or vulvar cancer. She has not undergone any cervical procedure in the past 6 months. She is physically and mentally fit to provide written informed consent. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to improve cervical cancer screening methods in HIV-infected women in India. She is currently attending an HIV care and treatment clinic in Pune, India. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher in a private school and has a master's degree in education. She is interested in reading books and enjoys spending time with her family. She rarely does exercise, and her BMI is 23. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and there are no significant findings in her physical exam.

Patient is a 26-year-old woman who has undergone a first trimester induced abortion. She is interested in exploring options for contraception and is willing to participate in a study on the effects of immediate provision of intrauterine contraception. She has no history of uterine anomaly, infection, copper allergy or any other contraindication for spiral insertion. The patient is fully informed about the study and has signed the consent form. She is willing to comply with follow-up visits and complete questionnaires on quality of life.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who exercises regularly and has no history of muscle diseases or myopathies. He is physically active and participates in regular cardio and weight training exercises. He has no tattoos in the scanning region and is not pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits. The patient's hemoglobin and collagen levels will be measured using Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography (MSOT) before and after exercise, and over time, at different muscle positions. The patient understands that the study is a pilot study designed to investigate the effect of exercise on hemoglobin levels and consistency of measurements in healthy adults, and that the information obtained from this study will be used to design future studies in patients with muscular diseases.

A 45-year-old transgender woman was referred to the clinic for HIV treatment. She had been diagnosed with HIV six months ago and was started on a regimen containing tenofovir and emtricitabine. She has been on hormone therapy for the past two years to feminize her body. She reports taking estradiol and spironolactone daily. She has no significant medical history and is adherent to her antiretroviral regimen. She is compliant with her hormone therapy and has no history of sexually transmitted infections. She is willing to abstain from sexual activity and intravaginal products for at least 72 hours prior to the sampling day. She is fluent in English and has signed the informed consent document indicating that she is willing to participate in the study. She is available for scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests and other trial procedures. She is compliant with the diet and lifestyle guidelines necessary for the study period. She has an estimated calculated creatinine clearance of 95mL/min by the Cockcroft-Gault formula, a hemoglobin grade of 1 and coagulation testing grade of 1. She has no clinical or surgical abnormalities that would preclude sample collection.

54-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 5 years ago, currently managed with oral hypoglycemic agents. She has a BMI of 28.5 and has been experiencing difficulty in managing her blood pressure, which has been consistently above 140/90 mmHg for the past 6 months. She is a regular user of an android smartphone and is interested in participating in a study that involves using a smartphone application for managing her diabetes. Her HbA1c levels are between 6.5% and 10%. She has no prior history of severe chronic diabetic complications, heart failure, liver or renal dysfunction, or other major illnesses. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and willing to download and use the smartphone application for the duration of the study.

This is a 46-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer after noticing a lump in her breast. She underwent a lumpectomy, and the pathology report showed that she has stage II breast cancer with 2 affected lymph nodes. She has an ECOG performance status of 0 and is in overall good health. She has not received any prior radiation, chemotherapy, hormone therapy, or immunotherapy. Her hematology profile shows platelets of 120xGpt/l and neutrophils of 2.5xGpt/l. Her liver function tests and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She is not pregnant and uses effective contraception. She has no clinically relevant peripheral neuropathy, heart infections, or heart failure, and her cardiac rhythm is normal. She has no active infections or hypercalcemia. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

A couple living in Sweden has recently given birth to a healthy baby girl. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of different pertussis vaccines. The baby is currently 2 months old and has no history of pertussis confirmed by culture. There is no renal failure or any other serious chronic illness associated with failure to thrive in the baby's medical history. The baby has not received any gammaglobulin or immunosuppressive drugs, and there is no manifest immunosuppression. The parents are fluent in the language used in the study and have no communication barriers. They are willing to participate in the study and are open to any of the four vaccine groups (acellular 2-component, acellular multicomponent, whole-cell pertussis vaccine, or diphtheria-tetanus vaccine as control).

Patient is a 35-year-old Hispanic man who has been smoking cigarettes for the past 10 years. He smokes an average of 10 cigarettes per day and is interested in quitting smoking in the next 30 days. He is currently not participating in any other smoking cessation program or taking any medication to quit smoking. He has an active cellphone with unlimited text messaging capability and is willing to attend two study visits, one at the beginning and one after 6 months, and receive at least one phone call between visits. He knows how to send/read text messages and is fluent in both English and Spanish. He does not plan to move from New Jersey in the next 6 months and no other household member is enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old female college student who has been experiencing seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms for the past two years during the ragweed season. She reports symptoms of nasal congestion, itchy and runny nose, and sneezing. She has tried over-the-counter medications such as antihistamines and nasal sprays, but they only provide temporary relief. She does not smoke and has no history of allergies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the study to help further understand the mechanisms of her allergic rhinitis symptoms and potentially find better diagnostic tools for future treatment. She has a positive response to a skin prick test for short ragweed allergen and is willing to comply with the washout periods for prohibited medications.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury at T12 level due to a motor vehicle accident 2 years ago. He has been experiencing severe neuropathic pain in both legs described as burning and shooting sensations with a score of 8 on a numerical rating scale (range of 0 to 10). He has tried anticonvulsants, antidepressants, and NSAIDs without satisfactory pain relief. He also experiences autonomic dysreflexia, defined as a rise of systolic pressure by more than 30 mmHg during noxious skin stimulation or when the bladder or bowel is full. He is in ASIA-A category, meaning he has a complete spinal cord injury, with no motor or sensory function below the level of the injury. The patient is currently taking medication for pain management, but it is not providing him with significant relief. He is willing to comply with the protocol and scheduled visits and has a letter of clearance from his primary care physician. He is literate at an 8th-grade level or above. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not pregnant.

A 68-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, cough and difficulty breathing for 3 days. He was diagnosed with COPD with chronic bronchitis and emphysema 6 years ago. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is a former smoker with a 30 pack-year smoking history. He stopped smoking 2 years ago. He has been using inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists for COPD management. Arterial blood gas analysis showed a pH of 7.25 and PCO2 of 60 mmHg. He was treated with non-invasive ventilation for 5 days and then weaned off the ventilator. He was discharged with supplemental oxygen with a prescription for inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. He has had two hospitalizations for acute exacerbations of COPD in the past year.

Sophie is a 10-day-old infant born at Crouse Hospital weighing 1.8 kg. She was delivered by C-section due to fetal distress at 34 weeks gestation. She was admitted to the NICU due to respiratory distress syndrome and was started on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP). Her respiratory distress improved and she was weaned from nCPAP on day 5 of life. On day 7 of life, she was found to be colonized with MRSA on routine weekly screening of her nares, umbilicus, and groin. She is otherwise clinically stable and does not have any signs of infection. Her parents have provided consent for her to participate in the study. She has no history of previous S. aureus infection at the time of initial positive S. aureus colonization screen. She does not have any fatal or irreversible conditions, congenital conditions that would prevent specimen collection or treatment application, and is expected to have a sufficient length of NICU admission to be included in data analysis.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty reading for the past few months. She has no history of inherited retinal diseases or other acquired retinal/macular diseases. She has been diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) by an ophthalmologist. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. She has agreed to participate in the study and has filled out the informed consent form.

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with Diffuse Large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) six months ago. He has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy but the cancer has not responded well to the treatment. His oncologist has suggested that he participate in a clinical trial to receive a combination of buparlisib and ibrutinib. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and is in good overall health with no significant medical history. He is married with two children and works full-time as a software engineer. He exercises regularly, eats a balanced diet, and has never smoked. He has no known allergies to any medications. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman diagnosed with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS). She has been on treatment with Dimethyl fumarate (DMF) for the past 6 months. During her last routine blood test, her absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) was found to be low. The ALC was monitored for the next 2 months, and it continued to decrease. As a result, the decision was made to discontinue DMF treatment due to lymphopenia. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to describe the reconstitution of ALC after DMF discontinuation. She had a total of 2 ALC assessments: one at DMF initiation and another before the database extraction. She did not have any other reasons for DMF discontinuation. The patient is willing to provide consent for the collection of her data for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman referred to the Florida Hospital Center for Interventional Endoscopy for an EUS FNA procedure to obtain core biopsy of a pancreatic mass. During the procedure, the 19 gauge needle experienced dysfunction and was unable to obtain core tissue. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as she requires a second attempt at core tissue procurement using a 22 gauge needle. She is not pregnant and is aware of the study requirements and possible risks and benefits. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

43-year-old female with a history of chronic abdominal pain for the past 6 months. The pain is described as sharp, stabbing, and localized to the right lower quadrant of the abdomen. The patient reports that the pain is constant, worsened with movement, and has a negative impact on her daily activities. The patient has had prior imaging studies including an abdominal ultrasound and CT scan to exclude other causes of abdominal pain. The imaging studies were unremarkable. In addition, the patient has tried multiple pain management therapies including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, acetaminophen, and physical therapy with minimal relief. The patient has a baseline Brief Pain Inventory score of 7. The patient has no history of abdominal wall hernia or other chronic pain syndromes including fibromyalgia. The patient is not pregnant and has no allergies or contraindications to study medications. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital due to chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He takes daily medications for these conditions. He has never had a blood clot before. He is currently on bed rest and is expected to stay in the hospital for at least 48 hours. The patient is being admitted to a ward with computerized physician order entry (CPOE).

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV. He has a history of injection drug use within the past 6 months and is willing to participate in the study. He reports feeling overwhelmed and uncertain about how to navigate the healthcare system to receive adequate HIV and substance use care. He is not currently on antiretroviral therapy and is willing to provide informed consent for the study. The patient lives within the catchment area of local antiretroviral therapy and medication-assisted treatment clinics and does not plan on moving out of the catchment area within the next 24 months. The patient is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions that would interfere with his participation in the study.

This is a 25 year old male who is generally healthy, with no significant medical history. He does not have any current medications or allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no history of diabetes or thyroid disease. He is able to swallow tablets without difficulty. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the absorption rate and pharmacodynamic of different formulations of paracetamol. He is willing to have a catheter inserted in an antecubital vein for blood samples and to have his blood pressure and pulse rate measured every 10 minutes during the first hour of the experiment, and then every 30 minutes for the remainder of the trial day. He is aware that adverse events may be monitored and registered during the experiment. He is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and to provide informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 61-year-old male with a history of smoking and a recent diagnosis of advanced lung cancer. The patient has not undergone any prior systemic chemotherapy or biologic therapy. The patient has non-squamous histology NSCLC and is at Stage IV. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. Measurable or non-measurable disease has been detected as defined by solid tumor response criteria (RECIST). The patient has a neutrophil count greater than or equal to 1500/μL, a platelet count greater than or equal to 100,000/μL and a hemoglobin level greater than or equal to 9.0g/dL. The total bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5mg/dL, and the transaminase level is less than or equal to 2.5 x ULN. The serum creatinine level is less than or equal to 1.5 x ULN. The patient's INR is less than or equal to 1.5, and the PTT is no greater than the ULN. The patient does not have serious non-healing wound ulcer or bone fracture, and has not undergone major surgical procedure, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to Day 1 or anticipation of need for major surgical procedure during the course of the study. The patient has not undergone radiation therapy within 3 weeks prior to initiation of treatment. Female subjects must be postmenopausal, surgically sterile, or using effective contraception. All females of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days prior to the initiation of treatment. Informed consent must be obtained in writing prior to the initiation of treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer two years ago. She has undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy followed by six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. After six months, her CA125 level started to rise, and a CT scan showed a recurrence of the disease in the pelvis. She then underwent debulking surgery followed by six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy again. Her CA125 level has been stable for eight months, but she now presents with abdominal pain and distension. A CT scan reveals a recurrence of the disease in the pelvis and peritoneum. She has a platinum-free interval of more than 12 months and is therefore eligible for the trial. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and has no serious concurrent medical or psychiatric illness. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception while on treatment and for three months following the completion of treatment. She has signed the informed consent form and is interested in participating in the trial to compare the progression-free survival of two treatment regimens for relapsed ovarian cancer.

8-year-old male with a history of respiratory distress and hypoxia since birth. Diagnosed with chILD caused by genetic mutation in ABCA3 gene at the age of 2. Patient has been on intermittent courses of systemic steroids with only limited efficacy. Patient has been hospitalized multiple times with worsening respiratory symptoms and recurrent infections. CT imaging shows diffuse infiltrates consistent with chILD. Patient has no history of HCQ treatment in the past 3 months. Patient and parents are willing to comply with all aspects of the study treatment and study requirements. Signed and dated informed consent of the patient's parents is available. No known hypersensitivity to HCQ or other ingredients of the tablets. No known retinopathy or maculopathy. No known glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase deficiency resulting in favism or hemolytic anemia. No known hematopoetic disorders. No known participation in other clinical trials during the present clinical trial or not beyond the time of 4 half-lives of the medication used, at least one week. No known hereditary galactose intolerance, lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose-malabsorption. No simultaneous prescription of other potentially nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic medication at the discretion of the treating physician.

A 30-year-old married couple expecting their first child received a prenatal diagnosis of complex congenital heart defect in the second trimester. The baby is due in 4 weeks, and the couple has been struggling with anxiety and stress related to their child's health condition. The couple is English speaking and able to read. They have no history of mental illness or substance abuse. The baby will require palliative or reparative surgery in the first year of life. The couple has agreed to participate in the study and will be randomized to either the guided participation (GP) or usual care (UC) group. They will receive an electronic tablet that will be their own to keep, and they will participate in sessions to develop communication competencies in the context of infant care. Data will be collected prior to the infant's discharge, and at 2 and 6 months after the infant's birth. The couple will participate in self-report surveys, assessment of heart-rate variability (HRV), infant feeding, interviews concerning the parents' communication and co-parenting pattern, and couple problem-solving sessions. The feeding and problem-solving sessions will be video recorded for in-laboratory coding.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hospital-acquired pneumonia. He is currently admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with a diagnosis of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to Acinetobacter Baumannii. The patient has been treated with carbapenems in the past, but is now resistant to them. His Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) is greater than 6, indicating severe pneumonia. The patient does not have any known allergies to colistin and is not currently experiencing an asthma attack. However, he is in a shock state and therefore may not be eligible for the trial. The patient's medical history and current condition make him a potential candidate for this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of intravenous colistin plus nebulized colistin in treating VAP due to carbapenems resistant Acinetobacter Baumannii.

8 year-old male with a history of repaired ASD and VSD who presents with increasing shortness of breath and fatigue. Echocardiography showed mildly elevated pulmonary artery pressure and moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Cardiac catheterization demonstrated mild pulmonary hypertension with normal pulmonary vascular resistance. The patient was started on sildenafil and referred for a cardiac MRI to assess for any additional cardiac abnormalities. Past Medical History: 1. Repaired atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD) at 6 months of age. 2. Mild asthma. 3. Allergies to peanuts and penicillin. 4. No prior history of surgery, hospitalization or significant illnesses. 5. No family history of heart disease or sudden cardiac death. 6. Up-to-date with all vaccinations. 7. No current medication use.

A 58-year-old male was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. His medications include lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. He has been compliant with his medications and has not missed any doses. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. On examination, he was tachypneic with bilateral rales on lung auscultation, and had elevated jugular venous pressure. His blood pressure was 150/90 mmHg, pulse rate was 100 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation was 90% on room air. ECG showed sinus tachycardia with left ventricular hypertrophy. His laboratory tests showed elevated BNP levels. He was diagnosed with acute decompensated heart failure and was stabilized with diuretics and nitrates. He met the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial, including LVEF < 40%, elevated BNP levels, and requiring hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure. He did not receive any IV vasodilators or inotropic drugs during his hospital stay. He was interested in participating in the study and provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with advanced Hodgkin's disease. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is currently employed as a teacher and lives alone. She enjoys reading and hiking, but has not been able to engage in these activities due to her illness. Her disease is classified as stage III with involvement of multiple lymph nodes. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy for Hodgkin's disease. She has no other active malignancies and is HIV negative. She is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She is eager to participate in this clinical trial and hopes to receive the most effective treatment for her condition.

50-year-old male with history of persistent atrial fibrillation (>7 days) and longstanding persistent atrial fibrillation (>12 months, but ≤3 years). The patient has failed at least one class I or class III antiarrhythmic drug and required at least one electrical or pharmacologic cardioversion. The patient has a left atrial diameter <60 mm confirmed by echocardiography and no contraindications to systemic anticoagulation with heparin or oral anticoagulants. The patient does not have severe renal dysfunction or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with detected pulmonary hypertension. The patient is willing to give informed consent and plan to undergo pulmonary vein isolation as the first procedure for symptomatic persistent atrial fibrillation. The patient will be randomized for either radiofrequency or cryoballoon ablation treatment. The patient will be monitored for 12 months to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the procedure.

A 50-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes visited his general practitioner for a routine check-up. His HbA1c was measured at 8.5%, indicating poor glycemic control. He reported that he eats a lot of fruits and vegetables to maintain a healthy diet. He is currently on metformin but has struggled to control his blood sugar levels. He does not have any history of severe cardiovascular, renal, or endocrine diseases. He does not require a translator and is not pregnant. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of fruit consumption on his blood sugar levels.

A 45-year-old female patient who has been experiencing heavy and painful menstrual cycles for the past few months was referred to a gynecologist. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is generally active, but has had to miss work due to her symptoms. After a thorough evaluation, her gynecologist recommends a hysterectomy. The patient is anxious about the procedure, as she has never had surgery before. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to optimize outcomes for patients undergoing gynecological surgery. The patient speaks English fluently and has no plans of traveling during the study period. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocols provided.

A 62-year-old female who recently underwent hip fracture surgery is seeking assistance for her recovery. She lives alone and does not have any immediate family members who can provide care for her. She is looking for an online education and skill development program to guide her through her recovery process. She is tech-savvy and has access to a computer and internet connection. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to not only help herself but also contribute to the development of a program that can help others in similar situations.

A 56-year-old male stroke survivor who suffers from right-sided weakness and difficulty with daily activities. He is currently receiving neuro-rehabilitation treatment at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital at Linkou. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves aerobic training in addition to his usual rehabilitation. He is able to ride a semi-recumbent stepper and has no comorbidities such as cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure or diabetes. He has a resting heart rate of 80 beats per minute and no history of atrial fibrillation or flutter. He is mentally stable and does not suffer from confusion or cognitive dysfunction.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old female who regularly donates blood. She has a history of low iron levels and has been deferred from donating in the past. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications other than a daily multivitamin. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study with a fingerstick Hb value of 12.2. She will be asked to participate in the study and will be provided with a study information sheet and asked screening questions. She will be required to sign an informed consent before any study participation. During her donation, an EDTA and red top tube will be taken from the diversion pouch to determine baseline CBC and ferritin levels, respectively. If her ferritin levels are below 20, she will be eligible for enrollment into the low ferritin group and will be offered oral iron replacement therapy. She will be given 200 tablets of Ferrous gluconate 325 mg (36 mg elemental iron) and instructed to take one at lunch and one at bedtime. Between 25 and 35 days, a study nurse will contact her to assess her compliance and tolerance with the iron replacement therapy. She will be asked to return to donate after her deferral period and will be notified of her results. If she experiences any adverse events, she will be instructed to contact the study physician or nurse immediately.

A 58-year-old Caucasian man presents with persistent lower back pain that radiates to his legs. He reports numbness and weakness in his legs, making it difficult to walk or stand for long periods. He has tried physical therapy, pain medication, and steroid injections, but the symptoms persist. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. On examination, he has reduced range of motion and tenderness over his lower back. He has no neurological deficits. His MRI reveals lumbar canal stenosis and disc herniation at L4-L5. He is interested in surgical treatment and has consented to participate in the clinical trial.

25 year old male diagnosed with schizophrenia 2 years ago presents with a history of violent behavior including physical altercations with family members and law enforcement. He reports auditory hallucinations and delusions, and has been non-compliant with his medication regimen. He has a history of substance abuse with occasional use of marijuana and methamphetamine. He has no known allergies and has not been diagnosed with any other serious medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the effects of Omega-3 fatty acids on the violent behavior associated with his schizophrenia.

A 25-year-old female was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes 7 years ago. She uses an insulin pump and regularly monitors her blood sugar levels. Her BMI is within the normal range (21.5) and she has no family history of diabetes. She is currently not taking any medications other than her insulin pump. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is unremarkable. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses a reliable form of birth control. She has no history of movement disorder or psychiatric illness. She is able to tolerate PET imaging and has normal liver and renal function tests.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer. She has previously undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy but the cancer has progressed. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to investigate the effect of rifampicin on the PK parameters of olaparib. The patient has normal organ and bone marrow function as measured within 28 days prior to administration of investigational product. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient is postmenopausal and has negative urine pregnancy test. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations. She is not receiving any systemic chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 2 weeks prior to study treatment. The patient is not receiving inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4. The patient has no brain metastases and has not undergone major surgery within 2 weeks of starting study treatment. The patient is not considered a poor medical risk due to serious uncontrolled medical disorder, non-malignant systemic disease, uncontrolled seizures, or active uncontrolled infection. The patient does not have diabetes mellitus, gastric, gastro-oesophageal, or oesophageal cancer, and is able to swallow orally administered medication. The patient is not breastfeeding and is not immunocompromised. The patient has no known active hepatic disease, hypersensitivity to rifampicin or olaparib, or concomitant medication contraindicated for use with rifampicin. The patient has a resting ECG at screening with measurable QTc interval less than 470 msec at 2 or more time points within a 24-hour period and has no family history of long QT syndrome. The patient weighs more than 50 kg. The patient meets all other eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has undergone allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute lymphocytic leukemia. He presents with symptoms of graft-versus-host disease, including skin rash, diarrhea, and liver dysfunction, which have not improved with corticosteroid treatment. The patient is resistant or dependent on corticosteroids and has a moderate or severe form of chronic Graft-versus-host disease in the skin or mucosa. The patient is being treated at one of the participant centers (Hospital Clinico, Valencia, Spain; Hospital Clinico, Salamanca, Spain; Hospital Ramon y Cajal, Madrid, Spain; Hospital Murcia, Spain; Hospital de Navarra, Pamplona, Spain) and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no uncontrolled infections and has a performance score of 3 or higher. The patient has adequate vascular access for extracorporeal photopheresis.

A 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and heart failure was referred to the study by his cardiologist. He reports a NYHA functional class III symptoms, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and peripheral edema. He is currently taking furosemide, metoprolol, lisinopril, and insulin. His blood pressure is within normal limits, and his BMI is 29. He has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. He has completed high school and is currently employed as a manager. He reports difficulty sleeping due to shortness of breath and orthopnea. He also reports occasional chest pain and dizziness. He has never received massage therapy or relaxation exercises before. He is willing to participate in the study and has no plans to receive any other complementary or integrative therapy during the study period.

A 30-year-old Thai male with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV infection and a viral load of less than 50 copies for at least 12 weeks is being considered for a clinical trial. He has been on a standard PI-containing HAART regimen with 2 NRTIs and has not experienced any AIDS defining illness. He has no history of taking CYP450 inhibitors or inducers, nor any gastric acid-reducing drugs within 14 days of enrollment in the study. His ALT/AST and creatinine levels are normal, and he has no relevant history or current condition that might interfere with drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion. He is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and has signed the informed consent form. He is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no active opportunistic infections or history of drug abuse. The patient will be started on the generic 200/50 mg lopinavir/ritonavir tablets 400/100 mg bid with a low-fat diet and will undergo therapeutic drug monitoring of lopinavir after 4 weeks to ensure steady-state. Safety data will be obtained at baseline and week 4, and efficacy data will be obtained after 48 weeks of follow-up.

A 68-year-old male veteran with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and peripheral artery disease presents with a dysvascular lower limb amputation that occurred 2 years ago. He is currently ambulatory using a lower limb prosthesis, but he reports difficulty staying active due to his amputation. He is otherwise in good health, with controlled blood pressure and no history of heart conditions. He is an English speaker and is interested in participating in the Physical Activity Behavior Change (PABC) intervention trial to improve his physical activity level and overall health. He is retired and lives alone, but has family nearby who can provide support if needed. He is excited to try the wrist-worn wearable activity sensors and home-based tablet computer to track his physical activity and receive real-time feedback, and hopes that participating in the trial will help him achieve his physical activity goals.

A 28 year old woman with a history of perennial allergic rhinitis presents with nasal congestion, runny nose, and sneezing that have persisted despite treatment with an intranasal steroid spray (fluticasone) for the past 2 weeks. She reports being allergic to dust mites and mold based on previous skin prick testing. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the potential benefit of adding montelukast to her treatment regimen. She has no physical signs or symptoms suggestive of renal, hepatic, or cardiovascular disease, and is not pregnant or nursing. She has not used any systemic or topical steroids, antihistamines, or decongestants in the past 30 days, and has not undergone immunotherapy dose escalation. She does not have nasal polyps or a significantly displaced septum, and has not had an upper respiratory tract infection within the past 14 days. She is able to understand the purpose of the study and agrees to comply with all study requirements.

A 55-year-old male presents with difficulty reading small print up close. He has a history of myopia and wears glasses for distance vision. He has no history of ocular surgery and does not have dry eye symptoms. His corrected distance visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes and he has a near add of +1.75 D in the non-dominant eye. His photopic pupil size is greater than 3.0 mm in the non-dominant eye and his corneal thickness is greater than or equal to 500 microns in the non-dominant eye. He has no macular pathology based on dilated fundus exam or optical coherence tomography (OCT) image. He is willing and able to sign and understand a written Informed Consent Form and return for scheduled follow-up examinations for 24 months after the corneal inlay surgery. He does not have any exclusion criteria, such as ocular pathology or disease, taking medications that might confound the study outcome or increase the risk of adverse event, or participating in other ophthalmic or non-ophthalmic drug/device clinical trials during the time of this clinical investigation.

The patient is a 12-year-old Japanese girl who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with active juvenile arthritis of unknown origin by a rheumatologist. She has been treated with NSAIDs and methotrexate, but her symptoms have not improved significantly. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is currently attending school and participating in extracurricular activities, but her joint pain and stiffness are affecting her daily activities. She and her parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

A 28-week gestation male infant born via vaginal delivery presents to the Neonatology Centre. The infant was delivered prematurely due to maternal preeclampsia and had a birth weight of 1.1 kg. The infant has been receiving neonatal intensive care including mechanical ventilation, intravenous antibiotics, and total parenteral nutrition. The infant's parents have given consent for the infant to participate in a clinical trial aimed at assessing the incidence and risk factors of nephrocalcinosis in very preterm infants. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has had a renal ultrasound to confirm the absence of congenital defects.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy woman who is interested in undergoing tumescent liposuction to remove excess fat from her abdomen and thighs. She has no known allergies and does not take any medications regularly. She is a non-smoker and has no history of significant medical problems or surgeries. She is physically active and exercises regularly, including running and strength training. She works as a graphic designer and enjoys spending time with her family and friends. Her BMI is within the normal range. She has never had any bleeding disorders or psychiatric problems. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve the safety of tumescent liposuction and reduce the risk of post-operative complications.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with prediabetes. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father and two uncles having had heart attacks in their 50s. He is concerned about his risk and wants to take steps to prevent heart disease. He is currently taking Metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. He is overweight with a BMI of 29 and is looking to lose weight. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in regular physical activity. He is able to speak and understand English and is willing to participate in the study. He has not been diagnosed with CHD and is not currently participating in any other risk communication study for chronic disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of alcohol use disorder (AUD) for the past 12 years. He has recently completed a successful withdrawal program and has been abstinent from alcohol for one month. He has no current delusional psychiatric disorders but has a history of depression and anxiety, for which he takes anxiolytics. He has no known neurological or cardiological disorders and is not taking any medication that may affect heart rate or cognitive function. He is a smoker but reports no other substance abuse. He has been recruited for a clinical trial to study mechanisms of emotion regulation in alcohol-abstinent patients. The trial aims to evaluate his emotional regulation processes through physiological indicators such as heart rate variability, electrodermal response, and pupil diameter. He will also be evaluated clinically through a structured interview and cognitive assessment. During the trial, he will be presented with high emotional inducing stimuli, such as pictures and video sequences, representing human interactions and will be asked to evaluate the intensity and valence of the stimuli using the Self-Assessment Manikin. He is willing to participate in the study to understand the emotional regulation deficits and improve his recovery from AUD.

A 55 year old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic respiratory insufficiency (CRI) comes to the clinic for rehabilitation. He has been using a non-invasive mechanical ventilation (NIV) during night time for the past 8 months. He complains of severe dyspnea and fatigue during exercise at low load. He reports that his quality of life has been severely affected due to his respiratory condition. He has not had any disease re-exacerbations in the past 4 weeks and is currently clinically stable. He has no history of cardiac diseases, orthopedic or neuromuscular illnesses. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of daily NIV during physical training for improving exercise tolerance and quality of life.

The patient is a 42-year-old Caucasian female who has struggled with binge-eating disorder for the past 5 years. She reports having 4-5 episodes of binge eating per week, during which she consumes large amounts of high-calorie foods in a short period of time and feels a loss of control over her eating. She has tried various diets and exercise programs to manage her weight, but has been unsuccessful in maintaining weight loss. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 35 and is otherwise in good health with well-controlled Type II diabetes. She is currently taking metformin for her diabetes and lisinopril for hypertension. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help manage her binge-eating disorder and potentially lose weight. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an acceptable method of birth control. She has no history of schizophrenia, other psychotic disorders, or bipolar disorder, and is not currently abusing drugs or alcohol. She has not initiated formal psychiatric therapy for her binge-eating disorder in the past 6 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 6 months ago. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she is taking lisinopril. She denies any history of cardiovascular disease or diabetic complications. Her hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is 8.5%, and she is not receiving treatment with any anti-hyperglycemic agents (AHAs) for at least 12 weeks. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She reports maintaining a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a well-balanced diet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help improve the methods of determining the renal threshold for glucose excretion in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck region that has metastasized. He has completed radiation therapy and surgery 28 days prior to registration, and all adverse events have been resolved. He has not received any prior chemotherapy for the metastatic disease. His Zubrod performance status is 1, and he has measurable disease that has been assessed within 28 days prior to registration. He is willing to submit archived tissue specimens for immunohistochemistry correlative studies. He has no active infection requiring systemic therapy and no evidence of bleeding diathesis. He is not on therapeutic anticoagulation. He has no significant history of cardiac disease, and he is able to take oral medication without crushing, dissolving or chewing tablets. He has not had any other malignancy in the past five years. He is informed of the investigational nature of this study and has signed and given written informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

A 45-year-old man presents with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. His BMI is 30, and he has a history of prediabetes, diagnosed 6 months ago. His FPG is 110mg/dl, and his HbA1c is 6.0%. He is currently taking Lisinopril and Lovastatin for his comorbidities. He is married with two children and works as an IT specialist. He reports that he has difficulty making healthy food choices and engaging in physical activity due to work-related stress. He is willing to participate in a research study that aims to prevent the transition from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. He is willing to eat study food (a PowerBar) and is able to use a computer for a prolonged period of time.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of RRMS according to the McDonald 2010 criteria. She has been receiving natalizumab treatment for the past 2 years, with no missed doses. She is now being switched to daclizumab due to safety concerns. Her EDSS score is confirmed to be between 0 to 5.5 at screening. She has not been treated with daclizumab or any other forms of daclizumab such as Zenapax® prior to enrollment. She is currently practicing effective contraception and is willing to continue it for the duration of the trial. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past year, no known severe hypersensitivity or opportunistic infections, no known cardiac, endocrinologic, hematologic, hepatic, immunologic, metabolic, urologic, pulmonary, neurologic (other than MS), dermatologic, psychiatric, or renal diseases. She has not discontinued natalizumab due to suspicion of PML, and has not been diagnosed with primary progressive, secondary progressive, or progressive relapsing MS. She is not currently participating in any other investigational study and has not been treated with immunosuppressive or immunomodulating treatments including mitoxantrone, azathioprine, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide, or mycophenolate mofetil. She has tested negative for Hepatitis C virus (HCV Ab) and Hepatitis B virus (HBsAg and/or HBcAb) and has no known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

A 22 year old university student has decided to participate in the clinical trial for a COVID-19 vaccine. He is in good general health and has not been previously infected with COVID-19, as confirmed by a negative serum antibody screening. He is able to understand the informed consent and willing to complete all the study procedures for the entire 6-month follow-up period. He has no history of seizures, epilepsy, or other brain or mental diseases, or allergies to any components of the investigational vaccine. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not received any immunodepressant or corticosteroid treatments or other research medicines in the last 6 months. He has not received any attenuated vaccines in the last month or inactivated vaccines in the last 14 days. He is excited to contribute to the scientific efforts to combat COVID-19 and hopes to receive the experimental vaccine.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male with a history of colon cancer that was diagnosed 2 months ago. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and has now been diagnosed with metastatic microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). He has no other significant past medical history and is currently not on any medication. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and exercises regularly. He reports no difficulty with daily activities and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. His histologic documentation of advanced or metastatic CRC has been confirmed, and he has no defective DNA mismatch repair (MSI). He has not received any prior systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic disease. He has at least one lesion that is measurable by RECIST v1.1. His organ function is adequate, and he has no medical conditions requiring systemic anticoagulation. He weighs 75 kg and uses adequate contraception method as per protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He has been on oral medication for glycemic control but has not been able to achieve the desired blood glucose levels. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.7%. He has been recommended by his endocrinologist to switch to insulin therapy and has been prescribed either NovoMix® 30 or Levemir®. He has agreed to participate in this observational study to evaluate the effectiveness of the insulin therapy under normal clinical practice conditions. He does not have any other significant medical conditions and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 65-year-old male smoker with a long history of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) presents with chronic critical limb ischemia. The patient reports severe pain in his right foot, especially at night, which is interfering with his sleep. He also reports numbness and tingling in the affected limb. The patient has tried various medical treatments, including blood thinners and vasodilators, but has not experienced significant relief. His vascular surgeon has recommended surgical intervention, either bypass or angioplasty, to improve blood flow to the affected limb. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if measuring tissue oxygen saturation can improve clinical decision making for patients with chronic critical limb ischemia.

A 52 year old woman has been experiencing gum bleeding and bad breath for the past year. She has noticed that her teeth have become more sensitive to hot and cold temperatures. She has not been to the dentist in over 5 years due to financial constraints. Upon examination, the dentist finds that she has advanced periodontitis with deep pockets and significant bone loss. The dentist recommends a treatment plan that includes root planing and scaling to remove the plaque and calculus buildup in her teeth. The patient agrees to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effect of different root planing techniques on tooth surface topography. She will be randomly assigned to one of four groups and will have a single tooth extracted post-treatment for analysis.

A 62 year old male patient was recently admitted to LLUMC Rehabilitation Institute for inpatient care after suffering an ischemic stroke. He is fluent in English and has completed high school education. He has no history of allergies to pomegranates, traumatic brain injury, neurodegenerative disease or any other neurologic condition that may have an impact on cognitive functioning. He has no active renal or liver disease and has not had an intracerebral hemorrhage in the past 6 months. He is not taking warfarin (Coumadin). The patient is willing to participate in the study to determine whether pomegranate supplements can improve cognitive functioning following stroke.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension. He was diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) measuring 6.5 cm in diameter and underwent endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) procedure a year ago. He presents to the clinic for a follow-up imaging study as part of the EVAR follow-up protocol. The patient has a history of coronary artery disease and is currently taking medication for hypertension and dyslipidemia. He has no known allergies to contrast agents or iodine. His lab studies are as follows: FBS: 110 mg/dl, HbA1c: 6.8%, Cholesterol: 180 mg/dl, TG: 150 mg/dl, LDL: 105 mg/dl, HDL: 45 mg/dl. The patient has no other significant medical history.

Pt is a 45yo M with a 10-year history of hyperlipidemia, with his last LDL-c measured at 120 mg/dL and TG at 280 mg/dL, despite being on statin monotherapy. The patient has no known history of cardiovascular disease but has a strong family history of early onset coronary artery disease. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history or medication use. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the efficacy of combination therapy with statin and choline fenofibrate in patients with inadequately controlled TG despite receiving statin monotherapy. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to fenofibrate and no abnormal ECG findings.

As this is a retrospective observational study, a patient description is not necessary. However, it can be noted that any patient who presented with a clinical diagnosis of tetanus in Fujian Province during the study period would be eligible for inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 4-month-old healthy infant who is not breastfed. The infant has no history of chronic or severe diseases that could interfere with the evaluation criteria. The infant has not taken antibiotics in the last 2 months. The family has a history of allergies, but the infant has not shown any signs of allergies or gastrointestinal disorders. The infant is currently being fed with a regular formula and has no known allergies. The parents are willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol as required.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD combined subtype and has exhibited depressive and manic-like symptoms, including irritability, affective instability, and reactive aggression. He has been taking stimulant medication for the past 2 months, but his mood symptoms persist. His parents have noticed that he struggles to maintain friendships and has difficulty controlling his emotions. He has also been

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been a smoker for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing cough and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. She has never been diagnosed with any lung disease before. The patient is a nonsmoker and has no history of tuberculosis or lung cancer. She has no other medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient is a well-nourished and alert female with no acute distress. Lung examination reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes. Pulmonary function tests reveal a moderate obstructive pattern with a FEV1/FVC ratio of 60%. Chest X-ray shows bilateral nodular infiltrates. The patient is diagnosed with pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis based on lung HRCT and lung function testing. She is enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate the outcome of adult pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis based on lung HRCT and lung function.

The patient is a 17-year-old male who has been diagnosed with osteonecrosis of the hip due to a hematologic malignancy. He has been undergoing treatment at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and has been recommended for Hip Core Decompression (HCD) surgery by his primary physician and orthopedic surgeon. The patient and his parents have been informed about the study and have provided written consent to participate. The patient does not have any premorbid condition that prevents him from ambulating and does not have any serious non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture. The patient will undergo functional outcome measures, including pain, functional mobility, endurance, quality of life, and gait patterns, pre-operatively and post-operatively over time. The study will observe and collect information on functional outcomes following HCD surgery in children, adolescents, and young adults with osteonecrosis of the femoral head. The results of this study will provide valuable information for the future development of treatment programs designed to target identified limitations specific to this population.

An African American mother and her 11-year-old child are invited to participate in a study aimed at testing the effect of a parenting intervention on metabolic syndrome. The child is currently in 5th grade and is generally healthy. The mother is concerned about her child's health and well-being, and is open to participating in the study to learn more about how to promote better family relationships. The family resides in an urban area and the child attends a public school. They have no history of metabolic syndrome or other chronic diseases. The mother is interested in learning more about how to improve her parenting skills and create a more supportive family environment. They are excited to participate in the study and look forward to the potential benefits it may bring for both themselves and their community.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with fair skin and light wrinkles around her nasolabial folds. She works as a marketing manager and is very conscious about her appearance. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has never had any cosmetic procedures before and is curious about trying a minimally invasive procedure to reduce the appearance of wrinkles around her mouth. She does not have any significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use appropriate contraception during the study. She has never experienced any allergic reactions to cosmetic products and is willing to discontinue all dermatological treatments during the trial. She understands the study's requirements and is willing to comply with all the follow-up visits.

A 48-year-old man presents with a recent diagnosis of colorectal cancer liver metastases. He has no history of liver surgery for CRLM and there is no evidence of unresectable extrahepatic disease. His clinical risk score (CRS) is 4 and he is scheduled to undergo liver resection for CRLM. He is able to read and write in English and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any concurrent malignancy, and is not an international patient.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past 6 months. The pain is constant and has been affecting his daily life, making it difficult for him to perform routine tasks such as bending and lifting. He has tried various pain medications and therapies, but none have provided significant relief. He scored 40% on the Oswestry questionnaire. He has no history of neurological deficiencies or spine surgery. He has not been diagnosed with cancer or any vertebral fractures. He has not received any steroid injections in the past month and is not on regular steroid or narcotic drug treatment. He is not pregnant. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the therapeutic effect of MDcure device on his chronic lower back pain.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain and discomfort for the past 6 months. She reports that her symptoms are worsened by stress and certain foods, and that she has noticed changes in the frequency and form of her bowel movements. She has not undergone any previous abdominal surgery and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has tried over-the-counter medications to relieve her symptoms, but has not found any significant relief. She is currently taking a daily multivitamin and a probiotic supplement. The patient has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. She is willing to participate in the study and able to give informed consent. The patient will undergo a small battery of diagnostic tests that include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) to evaluate areas of inflammation in the gastrointestinal tract associated with IBS and measure improvements in that inflammation in response to effective integrative interventions.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil. He underwent a left tonsillectomy and neck dissection, which revealed metastasis to the left level II and III lymph nodes. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient has been informed about the option of reconstructive surgery using either an anteromedial thigh (AMT) or anterolateral thigh (ALT) flap and has consented to participate in this clinical trial. The patient's medical records show no evidence of missing data.

A 43-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis diagnosed 5 years ago is seeking treatment at the clinic. He has been experiencing moderate to severe flare-ups of UC for the past 6 months. He has tried several treatments including oral corticosteroids, 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP), and anti-tumor necrosis factor therapy, but none of them have been effective at managing his symptoms. He has not undergone colectomy and does not have a history of a fistula or a stoma. He is currently not taking any medication for UC. He has no known allergies to any medication and has not been diagnosed with tuberculosis, hepatitis B or C, or HIV. He is willing to discontinue 6-MP for at least one week before the first dose of study medication.

A 45-year-old female stroke survivor who had a right-sided hemiplegia 6 months ago is being recruited for a survey research study on the design and utility of Rehab in a Crate, a therapy gym designed for post-stroke rehabilitation. The patient has been undergoing physical therapy to improve her mobility and motor function, but finds it difficult to regularly attend appointments due to transportation issues and the high cost of therapy. The patient is interested in learning about innovative and affordable ways to continue her rehabilitation at home, and hopes to provide feedback on the design of this new product. She has no other significant medical history and is able to communicate effectively.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant female in her 3rd trimester. She is healthy and has no previous medical history. She has no current complaints and has been receiving routine prenatal care. She is scheduled for a routine obstetric scan to evaluate fetal growth and development. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. Her BMI is 25.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently healthy and has a regular menstrual cycle. She is not pregnant and is willing to use a non-hormonal method of contraception during the study. Her BMI is between 18.0 and 35.0 kg/m². She has no history of irregular uterine bleeding or known hypersensitivity to any of the investigational or reference product ingredients. She has no intention of becoming pregnant during the course of the study and has not had any complications related to contraceptive use in the past. She has not been diagnosed with any conditions associated with an increased risk of venous or arterial thromboembolism, nor does she have any history of pregnancy-related cardiomyopathy or impaired cardiac function. She has no history of systemic lupus erythematosus or migraine with aura. She has no history of hepatocellular adenoma or malignant liver tumors, and no history of hormone-related malignancy. She has not received any investigational drugs within the last two cycles prior to the start of the Pre-Treatment Cycle. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with a non-healing ulcer on his left foot that has been present for over four weeks. The ulcer is located on the sole of the foot and measures approximately 2 cm in diameter. The patient has been receiving standard-of-care treatment for the ulcer, but it has shown no signs of improvement. The patient's HbA1c is 8.7%, and he has no history of coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, or other major health issues. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ENERGI-F703 for diabetic foot ulcers.

45 y/o female with papillary thyroid carcinoma, previously treated with surgery and radioactive iodine, now with unresectable disease and evidence of disease progression within the last 6 months. The patient has radiographically measurable disease with multiple lung nodules and elevated thyroglobulin levels. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is currently on thyroxine suppression therapy. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy, radiotherapy or receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The patient has no history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to sunitinib. The patient's corrected QT interval (QTc) is within normal limits. The patient has no history of serious ventricular arrhythmia or other significant electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormalities. The patient's blood pressure is well-controlled on medication. The patient has no history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within 28 days of treatment. The patient has no history of cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or transient ischemic attack within 12 months prior to study entry. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, stable/unstable angina, symptomatic congestive heart failure, or coronary/peripheral artery bypass graft or stenting within 12 months prior to study entry. The patient has no history of pulmonary embolism within the past 12 months. The patient has a normal liver function test and kidney function test. The patient is not taking any medications that are potent inducers or inhibitors of the CYP3A4 liver enzyme. The patient has no history of brain metastases. The patient is not pregnant, and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient is able to swallow and retain sunitinib tablets. The patient has a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. The patient understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 45-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with complaints of dizziness, weakness and shortness of breath. He reported a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he was taking medications irregularly. His vital signs showed a heart rate of 140 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute and blood pressure of 80/50 mm/Hg. Laboratory results revealed a lactate level of 6.0 mmol/L. The patient was diagnosed with shock and admitted to the hospital.
