14-year-old Caucasian male presented to the emergency department after a skateboarding accident. He reports that he landed awkwardly on his left ankle and felt immediate pain. On physical examination, there was tenderness and swelling over the lateral aspect of his left ankle. X-ray imaging revealed a displaced Juvenile Tillaux fracture of the distal tibia. After discussion with the patient and his family, they consented to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and denies any drug or alcohol use. He is an avid skateboarder and plays soccer recreationally.

John is a 45-year-old employee at Ohio University who has been diagnosed with hypertension and dyslipidemia. He has been struggling with weight gain over the past few years and has a BMI of 32. John is married and has two teenage children. He is interested in improving his health and reducing his risk of chronic disease. John does not smoke, but admits to drinking alcohol occasionally. He has a sedentary job and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. John is looking for a lifestyle intervention program that can help him manage his hypertension and dyslipidemia, lose weight, and improve his overall health. He is excited about participating in the Complete Health Improvement Program (CHIP) and hopes to learn strategies for making long-term lifestyle changes.

60-year-old male veteran who recently received a fecal occult blood test (FOBT) kit from the Veteran Affairs Medical Center in San Diego. He has no history of colon cancer or any other gastrointestinal issues. He is generally in good health and has no significant medical history. He is interested in completing the FOBT but has concerns about the process and is unsure about the importance of colon cancer screening. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to determine whether mailed educational reminders can improve patient compliance with CRC screening. He meets all eligibility criteria for the trial.

A 62-year-old woman presented with complaints of pain and stiffness in the right knee for the past 6 months. She reported difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, and getting up from a chair. She denied any history of trauma or injury to the knee. She had a medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2, and hypothyroidism. She was taking metoprolol, lisinopril, metformin, sitagliptin, and levothyroxine. Her blood sugar levels were well-controlled with medication. She had a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She was a non-smoker and had no known drug allergies. On physical examination, she had tenderness and swelling in the right knee joint with a limited range of motion. The left knee joint was normal. X-rays of the right knee showed osteophytes and joint space narrowing, consistent with the diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis. The patient was scheduled to undergo knee arthroplasty surgery at the Schulthess Clinic and was enrolled in the clinical trial as part of the waitlist. The patient resides in the Canton of Zurich and provided signed written informed consent to participate in the study. She does not use any walking aids and has no disorders that affect gait or balance function.

A 35-year-old sedentary woman, who has been weight-stable for the past year, wishes to lose weight and improve her lipid profile. She does not smoke or have any history of regular exercise in the past 3 months. She has no history of CVD, diabetes, depression, eating disorders, chronic medications, kidney disease, cancer, food allergies or intolerances to items used in meals. She has no abnormality in thyroid or Electrocardiograph, and has not taken any anti-obesity medication or weight loss drugs or dietary supplementations for weight control. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the prescribed diet plan.

The patient is a 30-year-old male, who had a traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) due to a motor vehicle accident about 2 years ago. He is classified as ASIA grade C and has intact spinal reflexes below the level of injury. He has been using a wheelchair since the injury and has been undergoing physical therapy for rehabilitation. He is currently not taking any medications related to SCI or spasticity. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or seizure disorders. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he is in overall good health. He is willing to comply with the medically-acceptable method of contraception during the trial. His BMI is 24, and he does not have any joint contractures or skeletal fractures. He is not currently undergoing any other interventional clinical trials, and he does not have any implanted medical devices that are not MRI-compatible. He meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of severe congenital hemophilia B. He has no history of FIX inhibitors or coagulation disorders other than hemophilia B. He is currently not participating in any other clinical trial and has not received any treatment within the last 30 days. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. He has agreed to use highly effective birth control throughout the study. The patient has affirmed informed consent with signature confirmation before any trial-related activities. The patient's factor IX gene mutation is not 128G>A and he does not have any significant contraindications to participation in the trial.

The patient is a 57-year-old Caucasian woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. She has completed one regimen of chemotherapy and is looking for additional treatment options. She has a history of smoking and quit 5 years ago. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently well controlled on medications. She reports occasional shortness of breath and cough, but denies any chest pain or hemoptysis. On physical examination, she appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Vital signs are within normal limits. She has no palpable lymph nodes, no evidence of clubbing or cyanosis, and breath sounds are clear bilaterally. Laboratory studies reveal normal CBC, liver function tests, and renal function. Imaging studies show extensive lung involvement with multiple bilateral lung nodules and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. She is interested in participating in the expanded access protocol to receive Lucanix® and improve her overall survival.

The patient is a 27-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has a history of noncompliance with medication and has been hospitalized twice for exacerbation of symptoms within the last year. He lives with his parents and is currently unemployed. He has a history of substance use, specifically marijuana and alcohol, but has been sober for the past 6 months. He is currently taking aripiprazole but has experienced significant weight gain and is interested in alternative treatment options. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 60 days. He is willing to use a medically acceptable method of birth control if necessary. He is able to understand the nature of the study and has given his informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of severe heel pain that has been ongoing for over a year. She has tried conservative treatments including physical therapy, orthotics, pain medication, and rest, but her symptoms have not improved. She reports pain with walking and standing that is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. She works as a nurse and is on her feet for most of the day. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial heel and plantar fascia. She has a limited ankle dorsiflexion range of motion due to gastrocnemius contracture. She has no history of previous heel spur surgery, plantar fasciotomy, or extracorporeal shockwave therapy. She is willing to undergo surgical intervention and meet the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial comparing instep plantar fasciotomy with and without gastrocnemius recession.

Maria is a 32 year old woman who works as a teacher. She presented to the clinic with a cough and fever that started 5 days ago. She also has pain in her chest while coughing. She is a non-smoker and has no past medical history of any chronic illness. Physical examination revealed audible rales in her left lung and her white blood cell count was elevated at 13,500/mm3. Chest X-ray confirmed the presence of pneumonia in the left lung. She has never been diagnosed with any immune function disorder. She has no known allergies to any medications including macrolides. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is in good health with no known medical conditions. She does not smoke and has a BMI of 22. She has not traveled to any malaria-endemic areas in the past 12 months and has no history of malaria. She is surgically sterile and using a combination oral contraceptive approved by the US FDA. She understands the procedures involved and has given fully informed, written consent to participate in the study. She is willing to defer blood donations to the Australian Red Cross Blood Service for 6 months. She has good peripheral venous access. She has not had a severe allergic reaction, anaphylaxis or convulsions following any vaccination or infusion. She has no evidence of increased cardiovascular disease risk and no history of splenectomy. She is not currently receiving treatment for any psychiatric diagnosis. She has not had any acute illness within the past four weeks and has no significant intercurrent disease of any type.

A 55-year-old male patient diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presents with a history of cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of locally advanced NSCLC with an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation. The patient was started on first-line EGFR-TKI therapy and showed a good response initially. However, the patient progressed after six months of treatment. The patient provides written informed consent to participate in a real-world study to assess molecular testing, treatment patterns, and associated clinical outcomes among patients with EGFR mutation-positive locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who have progressed from first-line EGFR-TKI therapy. The patient is currently not involved in any other intervention study and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

This is a 58-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has progressed despite receiving first-line standard treatment. She has been confirmed to have locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with at least one measurable lesion. She has no known EGFR sensitive mutations and ALK gene rearrangements. Her tumor tissue samples have been tested for biomarkers and she has been found to be anti-PD-L1 positive and CD8 expression is ≥20%. She has an ECOG PS of 1 and sufficient organ and bone marrow function as defined in the inclusion criteria. She has not received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody or other immunotherapy in the past, nor has she received anti-tumor vaccines or other immunostimulatory anti-tumor drugs within the past month. She has not been diagnosed with central nervous system metastasis with symptoms and does not have a history of pulmonary fibrosis, interstitial pneumonia, pneumoconiosis, drug-related pneumonia, severely impaired lung function or other lung diseases. She does not have active tuberculosis, HIV or syphilis infection. She has not been diagnosed with any active autoimmune disease that requires systemic treatment or used immunosuppressive drugs within 4 weeks before the first administration. She has not undergone major surgery or non-thoracic radiation therapy >30 Gy within 4 weeks before the first medication, chest radiation >30 Gy within 24 weeks before the first medication, or palliative radiation <30 Gy within a week before the first medication. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not participated in other drug clinical trials within the past four weeks. She has provided written informed consent and is eligible to participate in the phase II study of anti-PD-1 antibody, sintilimab, as second-line therapy for biomarker-selected advanced or metastatic NSCLC.

As this is an observational study, a patient description is not required. However, if a patient were to be enrolled in the study, they would have experienced a retained surgical foreign body (RSFB) during a previous surgical procedure. Any patient who meets this criterion would be eligible for inclusion in the study. There are no specific patient characteristics or demographics required for this trial.

A 60-year-old Caucasian man who has been on antihypertensive treatment for the past 6 months presents with poorly controlled blood pressure. His systolic blood pressure was measured at 152 mmHg during two visits spaced 10 days apart. His medical history is significant for a previous coronary artery disease and a family history of cardiovascular disease in his father who had a heart attack at the age of 53. He is a current cigarette smoker and his total cholesterol level is 225 mg/dl with a low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol level of 145 mg/dl. He denies any history of diabetes or renal failure. He has no significant hepatic or hematological disorders, alcoholism, or drug addiction. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has no history of atrial fibrillation or flutter, and no valvular heart disease that could preclude ECG interpretation for left ventricular hypertrophy.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking male who has recently undergone complete resection of a T2a non-small cell lung cancer with no evidence of nodal involvement. The tumor measures 5.5 cm in diameter and has been confirmed as non-squamous histology. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal blood counts, liver and renal function. The patient has no history of other malignancies and has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized trial comparing chemotherapy with observation as adjuvant treatment for early stage non-small cell lung cancer.

The patient is a healthy 2-month-old female infant, born at full term, with no significant medical history. She has received routine vaccinations including Hepatitis B vaccine at birth and DTP, Hib, IPV, and Rotavirus at 6 weeks of age. She is being cared for by her parents who are both in good health. The family has no known allergies to any medications or vaccines. The infant has no known bleeding disorders or conditions associated with prolonged bleeding time. The family is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman was recently diagnosed with osteoporosis and has a family history of cardiovascular disease. She takes calcium and vitamin D supplements daily but does not consume foods rich in vitamin K2. She has no history of major medical conditions, surgeries, or hospitalizations in the past year. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her bone density and reduce the risk of blood-vessel calcification and sclerosis.

The patient is a 16-year-old high school student who has been struggling with social anxiety disorder. She experiences intense fear and anxiety in social situations, which has significantly impacted her academic performance, social life, and overall well-being. Her symptoms include excessive self-consciousness, sweating, trembling, nausea, and difficulty speaking, especially in front of peers or authority figures. She has not received any formal treatment for her social anxiety disorder, but has been seeking help from her school counselor. She is fluent in English and is currently in 10th grade. She does not have any current diagnosis of substance use or conduct disorder, psychotic symptoms, or suicidal ideation. She is willing to participate in a 12-week cognitive-behavioral, school-based group intervention delivered by trained school counselors to help manage her social anxiety disorder.

A 16-year-old Hispanic male presented with a history of obesity since childhood. His BMI was 42 kg/m2 with severe comorbidities, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and moderate-to-severe sleep apnea. He had tried multiple diets and exercise regimes but had been unable to achieve significant weight loss. He reported feeling self-conscious about his weight and had experienced bullying from his peers. He denied substance abuse or other medical conditions that could have contributed to his obesity. His family history was significant for obesity and type 2 diabetes in his mother and maternal grandmother. He was interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating sleeve gastrectomy as a potential treatment option for his obesity and associated comorbidities, including NAFLD. He understood the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and was willing to adhere to the postoperative treatment plan.

A 56-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) and no previous history of radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The patient's tumor is inoperable, and only a biopsy has been performed. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 80 and has adequate hematological, renal, and hepatic function. The absolute neutrophil count is 2,200/mm3, and the platelet count is 130,000 per mm3. The serum creatinine level is within normal limits, and the total bilirubin and liver enzymes are also within normal limits. The patient is not currently receiving corticosteroids but has been advised that they may be necessary in the future. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the consent form.

Pt is a 35yo F with a BMI of 43 who underwent sleeve gastrectomy 2 years ago. She has been experiencing symptoms of gastro-oesophageal reflux (GERD) such as heartburn, regurgitation, and chest pain despite treatment with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) for the last 6 months. She reports that her symptoms are worse when she lies down and after meals. She has tried dietary modifications such as avoiding spicy and fatty foods but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medication for both conditions. She denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. She is interested in participating in a study to identify the risk factors for GERD after bariatric surgery and to determine if there are any preventative measures that can be taken preoperatively to reduce the risk of developing GERD.

54 year old female with a confirmed diagnosis of advanced breast cancer, which has metastasized to the liver and lungs. The patient has failed standard treatments and is not eligible for further standard treatments. The estimated survival time is more than 3 months. The patient has at least one assessable tumor lesion according to RECIST 1.1. The patient has an ECOG physical strength score of 1. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for organ function: Blood routine (ANC≥1.5×109 / L, PLT≥75×109 / L, Hb≥80g/L), liver function (TBIL≤1.5×ULN, ALT≤2.5×ULN, AST≤2.5×ULN), renal function (Cr ≤ 1.5 × ULN, and creatinine clearance > 50 ml), and coagulation function (APTT ≤ 1.5 times ULN, PT ≤ 1.5 times ULN, INR ≤ 1.5 times ULN). The patient agrees to use reliable methods of contraception during the trial period and at least 6 months after the last dose. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the trial. The patient has not received radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, endocrine therapy or immunotherapy within 4 weeks before the first administration, or other unlisted clinical trial drug therapy. The patient has not undergone major organ surgery (excluding puncture biopsy) or significant trauma within 4 weeks before the first administration. The patient has no adverse reactions of antineoplastic therapy in the past that have not been restored to CTCAE grade 5.0≤1 (except for hair loss and other adverse reactions that the investigator judges have no safety risk). The patient does not have brain metastasis, spinal cord compression, or cancerous meningitis with clinical symptoms, or other evidence that the metastasis of brain and spinal cord has not yet been controlled. The patient has not previously received treatment with PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors. The patient has not experienced immune-related adverse events (> grade 3) in immunotherapy (irAE). The patient does not have active or recurrent autoimmune diseases, interstitial lung disease, uncontrolled active infections, positive HIV antibody test, active hepatitis B or C virus infection, serious cardiovascular disease, history of alcohol or drug dependence, mental disorder or poor compliance, or plans to receive a live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks before the first administration or during the study period.

The patient is a 78-year-old man residing in a nursing home. He has been feeling sad and hopeless for the past few weeks, and he has lost interest in activities he used to enjoy. He also complains of difficulty sleeping and concentrating. The nursing home staff has noticed that he has become withdrawn and is not participating in activities as much as he used to. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is on a regimen of lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has no history of psychiatric illness, but his family members report that he has been increasingly isolated and disinterested in activities since moving to the nursing home. He scores a 14 on the Mini Mental State Exam and an 18 on the Geriatric Depression Scale. He meets the DSM-IV criteria for major depressive disorder and is eligible to participate in this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old Indian male presents with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus 7 years ago and has been taking oral hypoglycemic agents with diet and exercise modifications. His HbA1c levels have been fluctuating between 7-9% despite the treatment. The patient has been experiencing weight gain and needs a change in his treatment regimen. The physical examination reveals a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m², and his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg. Laboratory tests reveal an HbA1c level of 8.3%, and his fasting plasma glucose level is 180 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in the observational study of Levemir® to help manage his diabetes and achieve better glycemic control while reducing weight gain. He does not have a history of hypersensitivity to insulin detemir or any of its excipients. He is not pregnant, lactating, nor planning to become pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis for the past two years. She has tried various topical treatments, but none have provided significant relief. Her psoriasis covers approximately 15% of her body surface area and she has a PASI score of 16 and a Physician's Global Assessment score of 4. She has not received any systemic therapy or phototherapy for her psoriasis in the past six months. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate birth control measures during the study and for six months after the last dose of study treatment. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and has not received any biologic therapy, DMARDs, or systemic psoriasis therapy in the past four weeks. She has not been enrolled in any other clinical trials in the past three months.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who is in good health and has no known medical conditions. She has a BMI of 22.5 kg/m² and is a non-smoker. She is of non-Japanese origin and is willing to adhere to contraception restrictions throughout the study period. The patient has no history of cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, hematological or neurological disorders, and has no evidence of liver disease or neuropsychiatric disease. The patient has not received any glucocorticoid therapy within the past month and has no history of pancreatitis or elevation in serum lipase and/or amylase greater than 1.5 × ULN. The patient is not allergic to LY3540378 or related compounds and has not donated blood or participated in a clinical study that required similar blood volume drawn within the past 30 calendar days. The patient is willing to refrain from alcohol consumption and has no known allergy to iodine (shellfish allergy) or sensitivity to lithium carbonate.

A 25-year-old woman came to the clinic with symptoms of scabies. She reported intense itching that was worse at night and had been present for about 2 weeks. Upon examination, scabies tunnels were identified on her fingers and wrists. She had no past history of scabies and had not received any treatment for scabies in the past 4 weeks. She had no known allergies to the study medications and did not have any damage to her central nervous system. She stated that she was not pregnant or breastfeeding and did not have HIV or any other serious immunodeficiency. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial and provided her consent. Blood samples were taken on day 0, and she was administered either ivermectin or permethrin. Clinical examinations and pictures were taken on day 0, day 14, and day 28. She completed VAS for pruritus, DLQI and SF-36 on day 0, day 14 and day 28 as part of the study.

A 45-year-old non-smoking female with a missing tooth requiring a single tooth extraction for dental implant placement. The patient has adequate restorative space for an implant-retained restoration and at least 10mm of alveolar bone height. The patient has a dehiscence of the buccal or lingual bony plate of the tooth socket extending no more than 50% of the total depth of the socket. The patient has no active infections or medical conditions that would decrease the probability of soft tissue and bony healing. The patient is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule and has no history of bisphosphonate use or long-term steroid therapy.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic cancer, which has spread to the liver. He has already received one line of chemotherapy, but it has not been effective in controlling the cancer. He experiences fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite. He has no other significant medical history, and his ECOG performance status is 1. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options. He is generally in good health and has no major issues with his organ function. The patient is looking for a treatment that can improve his quality of life and prolong his survival. He is willing to undergo further testing and receive investigational treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of opioid dependence who is currently on buprenorphine maintenance therapy. He reports occasional episodes of pain, which he believes are related to his previous drug use. He has been stable on his current dose of buprenorphine (12 mg) for the past 6 months and has not used any illicit substances during this time. He is able to communicate fluently in English and is willing to participate in experimental pain testing procedures. He reports no current use of prescribed or over the counter analgesic agents and has no known allergies to hydromorphone or buprenorphine. He is not currently pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the trial.

35 year old Finnish-speaking male with no significant medical history, currently in good general health, weighing 70 kg and with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2. The patient is sexually active and uses a hormonal contraceptive method. The patient has regular intestinal transit and has no history of major gastrointestinal surgery. The patient does not take any regular medication or vitamins, and does not use any herbal products. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the active substances or excipients of the drugs being studied. The patient consumes less than 600 mg of caffeine per day and does not smoke or use nicotine-containing products. The patient has not donated blood or lost a significant amount of blood within the past 90 days. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and communicate effectively with study personnel.

A 35-year-old female with Type 1 Diabetes was diagnosed at the age of 14. She is currently managing her diabetes with an insulin pump and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system. Her HbA1c is 7.5%. She lives an active lifestyle and enjoys hiking and swimming. She is currently studying to become a nurse. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any allergies. She does not have any known microvascular complications. She has never participated in a study involving the GBP-based sensor. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements.

The patient is a 28-year-old non-smoking female who works as a marketing executive. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription medication. She occasionally drinks alcohol socially but does not have a history of alcoholism or drug addiction. She is 5'5" tall and weighs 130 lbs, with a BMI of 21.6. She has no history of allergies to medications in the fluoroquinolone class. She is currently not pregnant and is using effective birth control. She has no history of significant illnesses or surgeries in the past 4 weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the bioavailability of ciprofloxacin 1000 mg ER tablets of Dr. Reddy's with that of CIPRO® XR 1000 mg of Bayer Pharmaceuticals Corporation under fasting conditions.

This is a 62-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach after undergoing gastroscopy and CT scans of the abdomen and chest. The tumor was found to be surgically resectable, and a multidisciplinary team meeting has determined that a curative gastrectomy is the best course of action. The patient has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is willing and able to undergo surgery, but has some concerns about the possibility of a futile gastrectomy. The patient has been informed about the study and has given informed consent to participate.

A 30-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 23.5 is interested in participating in the clinical trial for BI 695501. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. She has no allergies or hypersensitivity to medications, excipients, or device materials. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not received any live vaccine within the last 12 weeks prior to enrolling in the trial. The patient is willing to provide signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to admission to the trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with right-sided colon adenocarcinoma. She has no history of any other malignancy within the past 5 years and has a performance status (ECOG) of 1. She has adequate hematological, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have any pre-existing peripheral neuropathy. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

Sophia was born at 26 weeks gestation and weighed 800 grams. She was admitted to the NICU at a participating NRN center and received care for 4 months before being discharged. She has been followed up by her pediatrician since then, and has been receiving regular developmental assessments. She is now 22 months corrected age and is eligible for the NICHD NRN Follow-Up study. Sophia's mother had a history of hypertension during her pregnancy, but her neonatal outcome was otherwise unremarkable. Sophia has been growing well and has not required any medical equipment or medication. She has been reaching developmental milestones within a normal range, but her pediatrician has recommended her to undergo detailed neurodevelopmental, neurosensory and functional assessments to ensure that she is developing normally. Sophia's family lives in a middle-class neighborhood and has a stable income.

The patient is a 58 year-old man who was diagnosed 2 years ago with squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue, which was treated with surgery and radiation therapy. Unfortunately, he experienced a recurrence of the cancer in the same area and has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and immunotherapy with no significant improvement. A recent biopsy confirmed the presence of residual disease. He has no known allergies or medical problems other than the cancer. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently taking pain medication for his cancer-related symptoms. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 70%. The tumor is visible on the oral cavity and is easily accessible for treatment with photodynamic therapy.

The patient is a 35 year old female who has a family history of Gitelman syndrome. She has not been diagnosed with the condition but has been identified as a heterozygous carrier of the mutation in the SLC12A3 gene coding for the thiazide sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine whether there are any metabolic risks or benefits associated with being a heterozygous carrier of the mutation. She does not currently have any symptoms of Gitelman syndrome or other related conditions, but is willing to participate in the study to help advance medical research and potentially benefit others with similar genetic profiles.

A 50-year-old woman with a family history of breast and ovarian cancer visited the clinic for an ovarian cancer screening study. Her mother was diagnosed with ovarian cancer at the age of 60 and her sister was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 45. The patient has never been diagnosed with cancer, but she is concerned about her risk of developing ovarian cancer. She has not experienced any symptoms related to ovarian cancer such as abdominal pain, bloating, or difficulty eating. The patient has both ovaries and has never used fertility drugs. She has a BMI of 25 and maintains a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet.

A 7-year-old boy was brought to the pediatric dental clinic by his mother due to a complaint of tooth sensitivity and pain while eating. Upon examination, it was discovered that the first permanent molars on both sides of his mouth were affected by Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH). The boy had no history of any other dental problems and did not have any syndromes. He was born and raised in Araraquara, São Paulo, Brazil, and was eligible for the clinical trial as he met the inclusion criteria. The dentist recommended that the boy receive sealant treatment on his MIH-affected molars, and his mother agreed to enroll him in the study. The boy underwent the four clinical exams as part of the study and his sealants were evaluated for anatomic form, marginal adaptation, retention, and presence of caries.

A 56-year-old male patient with chronic hepatitis C and biopsy-proven cirrhosis presented for enrollment in the SIM-SOF trial. He was diagnosed with hepatitis C 10 years ago and has not undergone treatment before. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of HIV or HBV coinfection. He has not suffered a decompensation event and his liver function, as measured by Child-Pugh score, is less than 7. His baseline laboratory values revealed a total bilirubin of 2.1 gm/dL, INR of 1.8, serum albumin of 3.2 gm/dL, and platelet count of 70,000 per cubic milliliter. His renal function, as measured by GFR, is 70 ml/min. He was found to have genotype 1a hepatitis C. He is willing to practice contraception during the trial and is not planning to become pregnant.

This is a 52-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who was recently diagnosed with stage IV kidney cancer that has spread to his lungs and liver. Biopsy of the metastatic lesions confirms renal cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for his cancer. He has no prior history of allergic reactions to medications and has no known immune deficiency. He has a normal bilirubin level, and AST/ALT levels are within normal range. His creatinine clearance is greater than 60 mL/min and his platelet count is greater than 100,000/mm^3. He is negative for pregnancy and is not currently nursing. He has no significant history of cardiac disease, pulmonary dysfunction, or psychiatric illness. He is willing to use effective contraception during and for 6 months after study participation. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of UCN-01 in treating his advanced kidney cancer.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 3 years. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. She is a nonsmoker and works as a nurse. She is currently taking fluticasone dipropionate/salmeterol (FP/SAL; Seretide® 125) as a maintenance therapy for asthma. She has had at least two prescriptions for ICS/LABA therapy as FP/SAL in the past year. She does not have any other chronic respiratory diseases but has a history of seasonal allergies. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is willing to switch to beclomethasone dipropionate/formoterol (BDP/FOR; Fostair® 100/6) for the purpose of the study.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain for the past year. She has been to several doctors, and after multiple tests, she was diagnosed with fibromyalgia. She has tried various treatments, including medication and physical therapy, but has not experienced significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if a new therapy can help alleviate her symptoms. She has no history of ischemic heart disease or uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes, and her depression is mild and being managed with therapy.

63-year-old female with a history of chronic renal failure requiring intermittent hemodialysis for the past 5 years was referred to the nephrology department for evaluation. She has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, and a BMI of 27 kg/m2. The patient complains of fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss of 8 pounds over the past month. She has also noticed a decrease in her hand strength while carrying objects. On physical examination, the patient appeared malnourished with a BMI of 22. She has a weak hand grip and muscle wasting in the upper extremities. Laboratory investigation showed hypoalbuminemia with a serum albumin level of 3.2 g/dL (normal range 3.5-5.0 g/dL) and elevated serum creatinine level of 5.6 mg/dL (normal range 0.5-1.5 mg/dL). She meets the inclusion criteria for the EASY clinical trial and has no exclusion criteria. She has given a signed agreement after a detailed explanation of the protocol on the basis of the information sheet and is likely to comply with it.

The patient is a 65 year old man who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. He has been experiencing shortness of breath during physical activity such as walking, climbing stairs or carrying groceries. His daily activities are limited due to his breathing difficulties. He is currently on maintenance inhalers and bronchodilators prescribed by his physician. He has not had any exacerbations or hospitalizations related to his COPD in the past 3 months. He lives with his spouse who helps him with his daily activities. He is retired and enjoys reading, watching television and spending time with his grandchildren. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has not been able to participate in any physical activity due to his COPD symptoms. His BMI is 27 and his blood pressure is 130/80. He has no other significant medical history.

A 45-year-old man presents with a history of chronic jaw pain and difficulty opening his mouth. He has a history of multiple dental procedures and has been diagnosed with temporomandibular joint disorder (TMJ). He has tried multiple treatments including physical therapy, medications, and splint therapy, but has found no significant relief. He also reports episodes of fatigue and muscle weakness, but has not been diagnosed with any specific condition. He is interested in participating in clinical studies that may offer new treatment options for his condition. The physical examination reveals tenderness over the TMJ, limited range of motion of the jaw, and mild muscle weakness on manual testing. Laboratory tests are within normal limits. Diagnostic imaging studies may be required to determine eligibility for specific clinical studies. He is eager to participate and contribute to the advancement of research in the field of dentistry and craniofacial disorders.

This is a 45-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with Child Pugh Class B liver cirrhosis. He has been experiencing sleep disturbances and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of increased blood ammonia levels on sleep quality and pupillary light response. He does not have a history of alcohol misuse in the past 6 months and has not had any episodes of hepatic decompensation leading to in-patient admissions in the past month. He has not received any anti-HE treatment and does not have a history of significant head injury or neurological/psychiatric comorbidity. He is not taking any neuroactive medication or medication known to affect sleep. He has not traveled across more than two time zones in the past 3 months and has not worked in shift work in the past 5 years. He does not have any contraindications for arterial puncture. He is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the study.

A 28-year-old healthy male came to the clinic to participate in the Phase IV clinical trial of the seasonal split influenza vaccine Anflu. He has not received any seasonal split influenza vaccine in the past 3 years and has no history of allergy to eggs or ovalbumin. He is able to provide a legal identity card for recruitment and has given his informed consent to participate in the trial. He has not participated in any other clinical trials during the study and has not received any immunosuppressive agents during the past month. He is in good physical and mental health and has no history of autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency. He does not have any acute episodes of chronic diseases or conditions, including chronic hepatitis, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular diseases. He is not suffering from Guillain-Barre Syndrome and does not have a history of severe adverse reactions to vaccines such as anaphylaxis, hives, respiratory difficulty, angioedema, or abdominal pain. He is not planning to become pregnant or breastfeed during the study. He has not taken any immunosuppressive medications or cytotoxic medications or inhaled corticosteroids within the past six months (with the exception of corticosteroid nasal spray for allergic rhinitis or topical corticosteroids for an acute uncomplicated dermatitis). He has no psychiatric condition that precludes compliance with the protocol, past or present psychoses, past or present bipolar disorder requiring therapy that has not been well controlled on medication for the past two years, disorder requiring lithium or suicidal ideation occurring within five years prior to enrollment. He has no medical, psychiatric, social condition, occupational reason or other responsibility that, in the judgment of the investigator, is a contraindication to protocol participation or impairs his ability to give informed consent.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the ICU at the Puerto Rico Trauma Hospital after a severe car accident. He suffered multiple fractures and was intubated due to respiratory failure. On the 4th day of his hospital stay, he developed a fever and was diagnosed with a hospital-acquired pneumonia caused by a multi-drug resistant strain of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol socially. He works as a construction worker and exercises regularly. His renal function is normal. He has not received any antibiotics for the pneumonia yet. He is married and has two children.

34 F with a history of atopic dermatitis for the past 5 years. She reports itching, redness, and scaling of the skin on her face, neck, and arms. She has tried multiple topical treatments including corticosteroids and calcineurin inhibitors but has not achieved significant improvement. Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at screening visit was 20 and Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score was 4. She has not had any systemic treatment for atopic dermatitis in the past 6 months. The patient has no known history of immunosuppression or active infections. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of dupilumab monotherapy compared to placebo treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman in her 38th week of gestation, presenting to the labor and delivery unit with regular contractions. She has a history of uncomplicated pregnancy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. She is requesting epidural analgesia for labor and is capable of understanding and signing the written informed consent. The patient has no language barriers and is able to communicate effectively in English. She does not have any conditions that could compromise her sensitivity to cold. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

35 yo F with primary infertility and regular menstrual cycles presents for evaluation of options for fertility treatment. She has a BMI of 23kg/m2, and her early follicular-phase FSH level is within normal limits (8 IU/l). She has no history of diabetes, heart disease, liver disease or inflammatory/autoimmune disease. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and has no history of being a "poor responder" to previous stimulation cycles. She has not experienced recurrent miscarriage or severe OHSS in previous cycles. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the Long Antagonist protocol versus the Long Agonist protocol for Controlled Ovarian Stimulation (COS) in an In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) try, and is willing to undergo the necessary medical evaluations to determine her eligibility for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with advanced melanoma that has spread to his lymph nodes and lungs. He underwent surgery to remove the primary tumor but it has since returned. The patient has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not seen any significant improvement. He is HLA-A*0201 positive and has gp100 reactive cells obtained and evaluated while participating in the Surgery Branch protocol. The patient is in good overall health with a performance status of ECOG 1. He has no major medical illnesses, but he is a former smoker and has a history of respiratory dysfunction. He is willing to practice birth control during treatment and for four months after receiving the preparative regimen. The patient is willing to sign a durable power of attorney and is able to understand and sign the Informed Consent document. He has not undergone any major surgical procedures in the past three weeks and all his toxicities have recovered to a grade 1 or less. The patient is eager to participate in the clinical trial and hopes to see an improvement in his condition.

A 35-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and wheezing. She was diagnosed with asthma two years ago and has been on controller therapy for the past year. However, her asthma symptoms have not been well-controlled, and she experiences frequent exacerbations requiring the use of rescue inhaler more than twice a week. She is also struggling with weight management and has a BMI of 33 kg/m2. She has tried various diets and exercise regimens in the past but has not been successful in achieving sustainable weight loss. She is motivated to participate in a weight loss intervention trial and has access to the internet to participate in the program. She has not had bariatric surgery and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to provide informed consent and complete diary cards for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep for at least a month. She has tried various sleep aids but has not found relief. She does not have any other underlying medical conditions that could be contributing to her insomnia. The patient is willing to try traditional Chinese medicine as a potential treatment option and is able to understand and comply with the study requirements. She is able to read and fill out questionnaires on her own.

A 75-year-old male patient with a history of smoking (45 pack-years) presented with persistent cough and chest pain. His chest X-ray and CT scan showed a 2.5 cm mass in the upper lobe of his right lung. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PET scan revealed no evidence of metastasis. He has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. He has a performance status of 2 due to mild dyspnea with walking. His laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count, liver function tests, and renal function tests. He has not received any previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his cancer. He is not a candidate for platinum-based therapy due to his age (>70 years) and performance status. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the written informed consent. He is using an adequate method of contraception as his wife is postmenopausal.

62-year-old male with a history of smoking, presented with cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. Chest X-ray showed a mass in the left lung. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and molecular testing revealed an EGFR mutation. He underwent treatment with first-generation EGFR inhibitors but unfortunately had a relapse after 6 months. He then received second-generation EGFR inhibitors but again had a relapse after 7 months. His T790M mutation status was negative and met amplification was not detected. He is currently experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and decreased appetite. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago after smoking for 25 years. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His performance status is 1 according to the ECOG criteria. He is willing to participate in clinical trials and has signed the informed consent form.

33 year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection for 3 years, currently on a stable antiretroviral regimen of ATRIPLA ® for the past 2 years. His last standard plasma viral load was undetectable and his CD4 count is above 400/mm3. He has been compliant with his medication and has not experienced virologic failure. He is not currently using any other chronic medication and has no contraindications to the study drug. He has no evidence of previous mutations to efavirenz, tenofovir, and emtricitabine. He is willing to provide written informed consent and commit to acceptable contraceptive use for the duration of the study. He is able to follow the protocol visits and has no current signs of alcoholism or drug use.

This is a 29-year-old female who has been struggling with symptoms of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) for several years. She has difficulty concentrating, completing tasks, and staying organized. She has tried various medications for ADHD in the past, but has not found relief from her symptoms. She does not have any other clinically unstable psychiatric conditions, and is not currently using drugs or alcohol. She has no history of renal or hepatic impairment, nor any condition that will require treatment with opioid analgesics. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is currently not on any medication for ADHD. Her primary language is English. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess whether naltrexone as a monotherapy can be effective in treating her ADHD symptoms.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian male who was diagnosed with stage II prostate cancer based on a prostate biopsy. His Gleason score is 6, and his prostate-specific antigen level is 15.0 ng/mL. He has not received any prior treatment for prostate cancer, and he is scheduled to undergo prostatectomy in the next 4-5 weeks. He has no other prior malignancy, and his life expectancy is estimated to be more than 5 years. He is willing and able to take finasteride, selenomethionine, and/or placebo for 3-5 weeks prior to his surgery. He has not taken any 5-α reductase inhibitors, hormonal therapy, or radiotherapy in the past year. He also has not participated in any other clinical trials involving a medical, surgical, nutritional, or lifestyle intervention in the past 30 days. He does not take any selenium dietary supplements at doses greater than 200 mg/day, including multivitamin supplements. He is retired and spends his time fishing and gardening. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He does not smoke, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known drug allergies.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been struggling with abdominal obesity for several years. She has a waist circumference of 95cm and an ultrasound viscerofatty index of 4.2. She has tried various diets and exercise programs, but has not been able to achieve sustainable weight loss. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of endocrine or nervous system disorders. She does not take any medications for diabetes, hypertension or hyperlipidemia. She has not undergone any surgery or medication for weight loss. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent voluntarily. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any hepatic-renal dysfunction or mental illness. She has normal sight and hearing.

Mrs. Johnson, a 78-year-old female with a history of hypertension, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis, presents with complaints of dizziness and lightheadedness when standing up, which has been progressively worsening over the past few weeks. She has had no falls or syncope episodes. She is currently taking lisinopril for her hypertension. On examination, her blood pressure is normal when lying down but drops significantly upon standing up. She meets the criteria for orthostatic hypotension. She is able to stand and walk independently. She consents to participate in the study and is randomized into Group 1. On the first day of the study, she drinks three large glasses of clear liquid (33cl) for hydration. On the second day, venous contention is applied in the morning. The orthostatic hypotension test is performed on both days. She will be monitored for any adverse effects during the study.

A 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia was scheduled for elective cardiac surgery due to his worsening angina symptoms. He is married, retired, and lives with his wife. He has completed high school education and is able to read and write. He has no history of psychological or neurological diseases. He is not on any medications except for his blood pressure and cholesterol-lowering medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies. He has never had surgery before and is slightly anxious about the upcoming procedure. He is willing to participate in the study to help improve the understanding of postoperative cognitive dysfunction.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 about a week ago. She is currently experiencing shortness of breath and has been admitted to the hospital for worsening respiratory symptoms. She requires non-invasive ventilation support and her BCRSS score is ≥3. Her IL-6 levels are found to be >40 pg/ml along with elevated levels of d-dimer, PCR, ferritin, and fibrinogen. She has no other comorbidities that could lead to an unfavorable outcome. She has not been on any immunosuppressive anti-rejection therapy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the use of anti-IL6R antibody therapy for the control of virus-induced Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS) in patients with elevated levels of IL-6.

14-year-old female with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) who has been wearing a Boston brace for 18 months is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. She has Risser stage 4 with no growth between 2 visits and is 2 years post-menarche. She has been compliant with her bracing regimen and has been attending regular follow-up appointments at the Duchess of Kent Children's Hospital (DKCH) in Hong Kong. The patient's Cobb angle measurement at the last clinic visit was 28 degrees, and she has reported good health-related quality of life (HRQOL) using the Scoliosis Research Society 22-item questionnaire (SRS-22). The patient and her family have been informed about the study and are willing to participate. They understand the potential benefits and risks of the two different brace weaning protocols and are willing to have their daughter randomly assigned to either the immediate or gradual brace weaning protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for 8 years. He is currently on levodopa-carbidopa intestinal gel (LCIG) treatment for the last 6 months, with a stable regimen of 1000 mg levodopa per day, administered via a jejunal tube connected to a portable infusion pump. Despite this treatment, the patient experiences rapid shifts between impaired locomotion and drug-induced dyskinesias, commonly known as the on-off syndrome. The patient has a Hoehn and Yahr score of 3 on Duodopa treatment and is in general good health, as judged by the investigator, with a body mass index of 25. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, no seizure disorders, and is not currently on any medications that could affect the metabolism of levodopa. The patient is willing to refrain from fathering a child during the study and is willing to use a highly effective contraceptive measure during relevant systemic exposure to the investigational drug and the first menstrual cycle after treatment cessation (if applicable).

This clinical trial does not involve direct patient participation, as it is focused on developing an algorithm for automated detection of macular diseases using OCT images. Therefore, there is no need to generate a patient description for this trial.

A 45-year-old female with a history of stage III breast cancer, HER-2 negative, treated with surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy, presented with persistent cough and shortness of breath. CT scan of the chest showed multiple lung nodules with the largest measuring up to 2.5 cm in diameter. Biopsy of the lung nodule confirmed metastatic breast cancer. The patient had no significant past medical history, with normal organ function and good performance status (ECOG PS 1). The patient has not received any chemotherapy for at least 2 weeks before enrollment in the study. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been living with HIV for over ten years. He has been regularly taking antiretroviral therapy for the past six years and has had undetectable HIV-RNA levels for the past five years. He has not experienced any AIDS-defining illnesses and is currently in good health. He is willing to participate in the study and provide signed and dated informed consent. He is between the ages of 18-65 and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. He has no history of injection drug usage or mental disorders. He is willing to engage in study activities for the duration of the two-year study.

A 32-year-old woman with a BMI of 29 kg/m² and light activity level presented to the nutrition clinic for a clinical trial. She has no known chronic diseases, does not take any medications or supplements, and does not have any allergies to nuts or other foods. She typically eats a regular snack at least three times per week. She is a non-smoker and exercises lightly 1-2 times per week. The trial aims to investigate the effects of high fat and high protein snacks on appetite hormones and satiety. The study will involve a seven-day menu with a second snack provided daily, with the type of snack depending on the study group. She will be asked to rate her feelings of hunger using a validated visual analog scale (VAS) questionnaire, and blood samples will be obtained to measure appetite hormones at the beginning and end of the study. She meets all the eligibility criteria to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been suffering from Crohn's Disease for the past 8 years. She has been experiencing moderate symptoms for the past 6 months with CDAI scores ranging from 220-450. She has been taking 5-ASA for the past 2 weeks with a stable dose and corticosteroids at a dosage of 40 mg per day with a stable dose for the past 2 weeks. She has not received Infliximab treatment in the past 4 weeks and has been taking 6-Mercaptopurine for the past 8 weeks with a stable dose. She has also been on antibiotics with a stable dose for the past 2 weeks. The patient has not taken methotrexate, cyclosporine or any experimental drugs in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, has never had a total proctocolectomy with a stoma, and has not had bowel obstruction or surgical bowel resection within the past 90 days. She is not currently on Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN), CYA, or tacrolimus.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been wearing daily disposable contact lenses for the past year. She experiences discomfort and dryness in her eyes after wearing her contact lenses for more than 6 hours a day. Her Eye Dryness Score (EDS) at the end of the wear day is 45 and she meets the classification for symptomatic contact lens wearers according to Young et al. She has used artificial tears at least once in the last 30 days. She is willing to use the study drops twice a day for 12 weeks and to stop using her habitual rewetting drops and artificial tears during the study. She has no known sensitivity to the investigational product or diagnostic substances to be used in the study. She does not have any history of ocular disease or infection within the past 30 days, and has not undergone any refractive error surgery such as LASIK within the last 12 months. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy at the time of enrollment. She is willing and able to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule.

Pt is a 45yo F with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, currently admitted to the hospital with DKA. She is being treated with an insulin drip due to persistent hyperglycemia and acidosis. The patient has been NPO for the past 24 hours and is receiving parenteral nutrition. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled on medications. She is currently alert and oriented, with no signs of cognitive impairment. The patient has no known allergies to Levemir or sulfonamides. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 65-year-old woman was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. She has been experiencing gradual worsening of her symptoms despite being on levodopa therapy. She is currently experiencing levodopa-induced dyskinesias which have been impacting her daily activities. She has no history of Parkinson's disease-related surgeries or any heart conditions. Her medical history is otherwise stable with no ongoing unstable medical conditions. She is willing and able to participate in this clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of itchy and irritated eyes. She has been diagnosed with Demodex folliculorum and is seeking treatment for her condition. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent letter. She does not wear contact lenses and has corneal sensitivity within physiological limits. She agrees to refrain from using ocular lubricants and eye-related cosmetics during the study period. She is willing to use the study products and able to follow instructions regarding study procedures and maintain the appointment schedule. She does not have any known active ocular disease or infection, and has not undergone refractive error surgery. She is a non-smoker and is not pregnant, lactating or planning a pregnancy at the time of enrollment.

A 60-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital after a fall in her home, which resulted in a fracture of her left wrist. Further investigation revealed that she has been diagnosed with osteopenia, a precursor to osteoporosis. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, and she is on medication for this. She had a hysterectomy at the age of 45 and has not had any children. She is retired and lives alone. She has a good support system with her daughter living nearby. She is independent with her activities of daily living and enjoys taking walks. She is concerned about her bone health and would like to learn more about osteoporosis prevention and management. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in a group setting. She resides in South Australia and has not sustained any fractures due to high trauma.

A 24-year-old woman with sickle cell disease presented to the clinic with a history of frequent painful episodes and hospitalizations due to vaso-occlusive crises. She has been on hydroxyurea for the past 6 months, which has helped to reduce the frequency of her episodes. She is currently taking folic acid in the equivalent of 1 mg per day orally. Her past medical history is significant for sickle cell anemia and she has had more than 6 vaso-occlusive crises in the past 12 months that required hospital visits. She does not have a history of pyruvate kinase deficiency or red blood cell-specific form of pyruvate kinase mutation. Her laboratory results are within normal limits, and she is otherwise in good general health. She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has provided negative pregnancy test results during screening and is willing to use contraception from the time of providing informed consent to 28 days after the last dose of AG-946.

This clinical trial is not recruiting patients, as it is a retrospective study evaluating the influence of a massive transfusion protocol on coagulation, use of blood products, coagulation factors, and ROTEM evolution over three years. Therefore, there are no specific patient descriptions for this study.

Maria is a 56 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She was admitted to the intensive care unit after developing acute respiratory failure and requiring non-invasive ventilation. She has a functional classification state of 2 according to Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group. Her family is aware of her admission and is supportive of her treatment. She has no history of cancer recurrence and is not currently experiencing any other complications related to her cancer treatment. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy female who has not had any major illnesses or surgeries. She has no history of chronic illnesses or immunosuppression, and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to any medications or vaccines. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and does not use any recreational drugs. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She is not a healthcare worker and does not have close contact with children under the age of 1 or persons with known immunocompromising conditions. She is able to understand and comply with the planned study procedures and is available for all study visits. She is willing to refrain from smoking tobacco for 28 days post-vaccination. She is willing to use an acceptable contraception method from 30 days before study vaccination until 60 days after vaccination. Her vital signs and laboratory values are within the acceptable range for enrollment in the study. She has not received any live vaccine within 30 days of study vaccination or an inactivated vaccine within 14 days of study vaccination. She has not received a vaccine against pertussis in the past 2 years.

The patient is a 28 year old female who is 37 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is of Asian descent and has a BMI of 24 kg/m2. She has a history of mild asthma, but it is well-controlled with albuterol inhaler. She is married and works as a teacher. She has no history of coagulopathy or increased intracranial pressure. She has no known allergies to bupivacaine or fentanyl. She has requested an epidural for pain control during labor and has agreed to participate in the study. She is able to give informed consent and is in overall good health, classified as an ASA class Ⅰ.

A 65-year-old Caucasian male presented to the pulmonology clinic with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for 10 years. He has a history of smoking for 40 years and has been abstinent for the past two years. He reported dyspnea with exertion, cough with sputum production, and occasional wheezing. He denied any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he was taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. His vital signs were stable, and his physical examination was significant for decreased breath sounds and expiratory wheezing on lung auscultation. His pulmonary function test showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 60%. He was diagnosed with stable COPD and was offered respiratory muscle training as part of his pulmonary rehabilitation program. He consented to participate in the study and was randomized to the concurrent inspiratory and expiratory muscle training group.

The patient is a 8-year-old Caucasian boy with a diagnosis of relapsed high-risk neuroblastoma based on revised INRC criteria. He has completed at least one cycle of induction and consolidation therapy with an INRC criterion of partial response. However, he showed new progressive disease (revised INRC criteria progressive disease) as described in Park, et al. (2017). He has no previous therapeutic 131I-MIBG treatment. All soft tissue lesions identified on CT/MRI scans are iobenguane-avid lesions on an iobenguane (123I) scan or any non iobenguane avid lesions biopsy proven to be non-tumor lesions. He has adequate cryopreserved autologous peripheral blood stem cells. He is not sexually active. He is in good general health with no significant medical history. His Karnofsky Performance Status is 80%. His liver function parameters are within normal range. His cardiac function is also normal. He has no history of total body irradiation. He has no significant active infections.

Patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of hemorrhoids and anal fissures. He has experienced recurrent episodes of pain, bleeding, and difficulty passing stool. The patient has been scheduled for proctology outpatient surgery to treat his condition. He is worried about the surgery and has many questions about the procedure, recovery, and pain management. He is interested in participating in a study that offers additional support and consultation with a nurse both before and after the surgery to help him feel more prepared and confident in his recovery. The patient is able to communicate well and is willing to participate in the study. He is covered by a social security scheme and is not bedridden.

Patient B is a 10-year-old child who has no history of strabismus or any visual impairment. The child has normal visual acuity for their age, scoring 10/10 on the Test of Cadet Rossano 2. The oculomotor examination was normal, with no evidence of strabismus. The child's binocular vision was less than or equal to 60 sec/arc on the stereoscopic vision test. Refraction without cycloplegia was within normal limits: less than 2 diopters of myopia, less than 1.5 diopters of hyperopia, less than 1 diopter of astigmatism, and less than 1 diopter of anisometropia. Examination of the fundus without pupillary dilation was normal. Axial length was also normal for the child's age, measured by non-contact biometer to eliminate refractive offset anomaly axial length by abnormal. The child does not have any history of anterior eye problems, and their behavior suggests good cooperation when taking a photo. The child does not have any limb abnormalities, and there is no scheduled surgery without the use of curare. The child is eligible to participate in the study.

This is a 52 year-old male who was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) 3 years ago. He underwent surgical resection followed by radiotherapy and chemotherapy with temozolomide. The patient was then followed up with regular MRI scans, which showed no evidence of disease progression until recently, when he started experiencing headaches and seizures. A repeat MRI scan revealed a new enhancing lesion at the site of the previous tumor, which could represent either pseudoprogression or radiation necrosis. The patient is now being offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial that will use the PET radiotracer [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) to distinguish between these possibilities. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and is able to provide informed consent.

Pt is a 50yo M with a history of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and hypertension, currently using continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment. Despite the use of CPAP, the patient reports poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness. The patient is interested in alternative treatments for OSA and is willing to try a sedative medication to improve OSA severity. The patient has no known history of cardiac, pulmonary, renal, neurologic, neuromuscular, or hepatic disease. The patient does not have any known psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any medications that may affect sleep or breathing. The patient does not smoke, drink more than 3 oz of alcohol per day, or use illicit drugs. The patient drinks 2 cups of coffee per day. The patient has not experienced any desaturations to below 70% lasting greater than 10 seconds in duration per event on polysomnography.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of moderate-severe psoriasis. He has been undergoing dermatological treatment for the past 6 months, but still experiences significant symptoms such as pruritus, scaling, and pain. He reports feeling distressed and frustrated with the impact of psoriasis on his daily life, including social interactions and work performance. He is interested in participating in a study that may improve his quality of life, and is able to communicate effectively with the investigator. He has no history of mental illness or psychiatric treatment, nor does he have alcohol or drug abuse issues.

72-year-old Caucasian male with a history of osteoporosis presents with severe back pain that has persisted for the past 3 months. He has no history of cancer or any other significant medical conditions. He has tried non-surgical management options including pain medications and physical therapy, but has not experienced any significant relief. Imaging studies reveal a vertebral body compression

The patient is a 65-year-old man who underwent total hip replacement surgery due to severe osteoarthritis of the right hip joint. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is controlled by medication. He denies any allergies or previous surgeries other than the hip replacement. He has not had any recent infections, and he does not smoke or use illicit drugs. The patient is currently experiencing pain and swelling in the right hip joint, accompanied by fever and redness. His physical examination shows signs of inflammation, including warmth and tenderness around the joint. Radiological imaging confirms the presence of a prosthetic joint, and there is evidence of bone resorption and periosteal reaction. The patient's lab results show elevated levels of C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Synovial fluid analysis reveals an elevated white blood cell count and leukocyte esterase test strip, indicating the possibility of a prosthetic joint infection. The patient has not received any antibiotic treatment, and he is willing to participate in the clinical trial to aid in the diagnosis of his condition.

The patient is a 25-year-old Caucasian male with no significant past medical history. He is 5'11" and weighs 160 lbs, with a BMI of 22.3 kg/㎡. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has not participated in any investigational product study within the past 3 months. The patient signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

63-year-old male with a history of colorectal cancer diagnosed 3 years ago. A routine follow-up CT scan revealed liver metastasis. The patient underwent a liver biopsy, which confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma consistent with metastatic colorectal cancer. The patient received chemotherapy, and repeat scans showed stable disease. However, on a subsequent scan, the patient was found to have progression of liver metastasis with multiple new lesions.
