The patient is now being considered for radioembolization with either SIR-spheres or TheraSphere due to metastatic malignancy of the liver. The patient is in good general health with an ECOG performance status of 1, and has undergone diagnostic imaging of the abdomen utilizing CT with contrast within the past 4 weeks. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with appropriate contraception during the study.

62 y/o male with known history of CAD and previous stent placement in the RCA presented with recurrent angina and positive stress test. Coronary angiography showed a calcified lesion in the mid LAD with 80% stenosis and a reference vessel diameter of 2.8 mm. The lesion was deemed complex and suitable for the PREPARE-CALC trial. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled on medications. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He is currently asymptomatic aside from the recurrent angina and has no history of myocardial infarction or heart failure. He has given informed consent to participate in the trial.

67 year old male with a past medical history of metastatic urothelial carcinoma who has progressed after prior therapy with platinum-based regimen and anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy. The patient is currently experiencing worsening symptoms including fatigue, decreased appetite, and pain. The patient has an ECOG performance status score of 1 and has received prior treatment with cisplatin-containing chemotherapy given in the neo-adjuvant/adjuvant setting followed by anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in the metastatic setting. The patient has no evidence of brain metastases, and their hematologic counts and hepatic function are adequate. The patient has a history of hypertension, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and hyperlipidemia, all well-controlled on medications. The patient is willing to use two methods of birth control or be surgically sterile or abstain from heterosexual activity for the course of the study through 6 months after the last dose of study drug.

A 22-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe menstrual pain for the last 3 months is seeking alternative treatment to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). She has been using NSAID to alleviate her pain but is concerned about the side effects of the medication. She has been diagnosed with primary dysmenorrhea (PD) and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for ESWT. She has a relatively regular menstrual cycle, with a duration of 28 days, and experiences maximum pain intensity over 60 mm according to the 10 cm visual analog scale (VAS). She has not taken oral contraceptives or regularly taken mineral or vitamin supplements in the past 3 months. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed an informed consent form. She has no history of epilepsy, gastrointestinal, cardio-vascular or renal diseases. She is not pregnant and has no plans of getting pregnant during the trial. She has never tried acupuncture before.

60 year-old man with stage 4 pancreatic cancer who is currently admitted to a hospice for end-of-life care due to his poor prognosis. He has been experiencing breakthrough pain despite being on regular oral morphine and has had at least one episode of breakthrough pain in the last 24 hours. His family members are willing to participate in the study and administer the study medication if needed. The patient has the capacity to consent to participation and is interested in exploring alternative methods for managing his symptoms. He is fluent in English and able to understand verbal explanations and written information provided. There is no history of substance abuse in the patient or his family members.

28yo male with a long history of panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, and specific phobia. He has tried various medications in the past with limited success and is interested in trying a non-pharmacological approach to managing his symptoms. He currently has a HAMA score of 22 and a CGI score of 4. He is able to attend therapy regularly and has no planned hospitalizations or moves during the study time frame. He does not have a current suicidal tendency or comorbid psychiatric disorder. He does not have a current alcohol or substance use disorder, and has no severe medical illness or condition that would affect participation in the study. He is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

54 yo Japanese male with a history of CAD and elevated LDL-C levels despite being on a maximally tolerated dose of statin therapy. Patient has a documented intolerance to at least one statin. Patient has been categorized as 'high risk' by the Japan Atherosclerosis Society (JAS) 2017 guidelines. The patient has no history of heart failure or cardiac arrhythmias that are not controlled by medication or via ablation. The patient's blood pressure is well controlled with antihypertensive therapy. The patient has no active liver disease or severe concomitant non-cardiovascular disease that carries the risk of reducing life expectancy to less than 2 years. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial assessing the efficacy and safety of inclisiran in Japanese participants with high cardiovascular risk and elevated LDL-C levels.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast by core needle biopsy. The tumor is measurable and is greater than or equal to 2cm. The patient is clinically staged as M0 (non-inflammatory) and has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. She has no evidence of distant metastatic disease and has not had an excisional or incisional biopsy for this primary breast tumor. She has no inflammatory breast cancer and no synchronous contra-lateral breast cancer. The patient has not participated in the NSABP B-40 study, and she has not had therapy for invasive breast cancer, including irradiation, chemo-, immuno-, and/or hormonal therapy. She is not currently on any hormonal therapy such as raloxifene, tamoxifen, or other selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), either for osteoporosis or breast cancer prevention, or sex hormonal therapy such as birth control pills, ovarian hormonal replacement therapy, etc. The patient has no nonmalignant systemic disease that would preclude her from being treated with the standard of care chemotherapy regimens consisting of either doxorubicin (A), cyclophosphamide (C), and a taxane (T) such as docetaxel, paclitaxel, or Abraxane (nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel [nab-paclitaxel]) administered in any sequence and combination the treating physician determines or docetaxel (T) plus cyclophosphamide (C). The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed an approved consent form conforming to institutional guidelines prior to study entry.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with neuroblastoma after experiencing abdominal pain and a palpable mass in her abdomen. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of stage IIB neuroblastoma without N-myc amplification. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Her performance status is good, and she has no significant comorbidities. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Surgery is recommended as the primary treatment for her localized resectable tumor, and she is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of surgery alone for her stage of neuroblastoma.

Patients who are currently enrolled in the Systolic Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT) who are aged 50 years or older and have high cardiovascular risk are eligible to participate in this observational study. Patients who have contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) such as intracranial metal prostheses, weight over 300 pounds, claustrophobia, and certain types of hardware used in pacemakers or prostheses will be excluded. The study aims to examine the factors affecting the progression of atherosclerosis in patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), and the investigators will take advantage of the unique opportunities provided by the parent study to study this issue. If you are a SPRINT participant and meet the eligibility criteria for this study, you may be invited to participate in the SPRINT - Factors Affecting Atherosclerosis Study (FAST) to help advance our understanding of CKD and its impact on cardiovascular health.

A 29-week gestational age male neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 23-year-old G1P0 mother with an uncomplicated pregnancy. The infant weighed 1050 grams at birth and required intubation and surfactant administration at delivery due to respiratory distress syndrome. The infant was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for further management. Initial laboratory studies revealed elevated bilirubin levels, and the infant was started on phototherapy. The infant will be eligible for the study and will have TcB measurements obtained at approximately 30 minutes after the TSB is drawn, and then again 24 hours after initiation and completion of phototherapy. Basic demographic data such as gestational age, ethnicity, and gender will be collected, as well as relevant laboratory data such as blood type of mom and infant, Coomb's test results, and enteral and intravenous nutrition data. The results, date, time, and location of the TSB and TcB will be collected for analysis. The study will be conducted during the first week of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder. He has undergone platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease, but his cancer has either relapsed or is refractory to prior therapy. He has a missense HRAS mutation found through molecular profiling, which makes him eligible for the study. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and acceptable liver and renal function. He has not received any FTase inhibitor treatment in the past. The patient understands the study's requirements and has provided written and voluntary informed consent. He has no history of clinically relevant coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, or cerebrovascular attacks. However, he does have a history of mild neuropathy.

This is a 65-year-old female with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, who underwent a central venous catheter placement for chemotherapy treatment of breast cancer. She developed fever, chills, and redness at the site of the catheter insertion after 3 days of the procedure. Blood cultures were obtained, which grew coagulase-negative staphylococci. She was started on vancomycin, but her fever persisted, and the catheter was removed. She was then screened for eligibility for this clinical trial of tigecycline for catheter infections caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis and other coagulase-negative staphylococci. She met the inclusion criteria, having a positive blood culture for coagulase-negative staphylococci, and failing previous antibiotic therapy. She was not neutropenic and did not have endocarditis or osteomyelitis. She did not have any known allergies to tigecycline or tetracyclines. She agreed to use contraception during the study period and was enrolled in the first phase of the trial.

A 42-year-old male patient was diagnosed with a grade IV glioma, and he is currently admitted to the Neurology service at MSKCC. He has been experiencing symptoms such as headaches, seizures, and difficulty with speech and motor function for the past few months. He has been receiving treatment from a neuro-oncologist and has had several outpatient visits. He has a good understanding of English and is willing to participate in the study. His wife, who has been providing him with emotional and physical support, has also agreed to participate in the study as a caregiver. They both understand the risks, benefits, and alternatives to participating in this study. The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale score is 15, and he is oriented to self, age, place, year, and month.

The patient is a 10-year-old child who has been experiencing frequent episodes of tonsillitis. The child has a history of asthma and is currently using an inhaler. The child is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. The parents have provided informed consent for the child to undergo tonsillectomy surgery. The child is able to provide assent to participate in the study. The child is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASAPS) Classification 2. There are no concurrent surgeries or any other conditions that would make the child unsuitable for the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of abdominal pain that started around his belly button and has now migrated to the right lower quadrant. He has also experienced nausea and vomiting, and has not been able to pass gas or have a bowel movement for the last 12 hours. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical exam reveals right lower quadrant tenderness with rebound and guarding, and a low-grade fever of 100.9°F. Laboratory studies show a white blood cell count of 12,000/mm3 and a C-reactive protein level of 25 mg/L. An abdominal CT scan is ordered to confirm the diagnosis of acute appendicitis. The CT scan reveals an inflamed appendix with surrounding fat stranding and no evidence of perforation. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is offered the opportunity to participate in the clinical trial.

A 34-year-old Caucasian woman, who has been married for 5 years, is experiencing difficulties with sexual arousal. She reports difficulty achieving and maintaining sexual arousal during sexual activity with her partner. She has a history of early-stage gynecologic cancer that was successfully treated. She is currently receiving treatment at the BC Centre for Sexual Medicine for her sexual arousal difficulties. She has no other significant medical history. She is proficient in English and is willing to take part in group sessions. She is currently not taking any medication that could affect sexual function. She is looking for a brief, evidence-based approach to treat her acquired FSAD. She is in a stable relationship with her partner and has no history of psychiatric illness. Her sexual dysfunction has caused some distress in her relationship, and she is looking for help to improve her sexual function and overall quality of life.

A 37-year-old pregnant woman at 38 weeks gestation with no significant medical history, presenting for an elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. The patient has not taken any medications including heparin and aspirin within 7 days of surgery. She has no known allergies to hydroxyethylstarch, corn, starch, or any drugs. The patient is fluent in English and understands the nature of the study. No history of high blood pressure, heart abnormality, kidney or liver disease or insulin-dependent diabetes.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who was diagnosed with a brain tumor based on imaging. He has not received any oncologic treatment yet. His calculated glomerular filtration rate is 80 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The patient and his legal guardians have agreed to sign a written informed consent and HIPAA authorization in accordance with institutional guidelines. The patient does not have any clinically significant signs of uncal herniation. He has no known allergic or hypersensitivity reactions to parenteral iron, parenteral dextran, parenteral iron-dextran, or parenteral iron-polysaccharide preparations. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and there is no suspicion of pregnancy. The patient does not have any contraindication for 3Tesla (3T) MRI. The patient does not have any known iron overload, and hemochromatosis has been ruled out prior to study entry with normal values of the transferrin saturation (TS) test and serum ferritin (SF) test. The patient has not received ferumoxytol within 4 weeks of study entry.

A 60 yo F with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer is scheduled to undergo curative-intent adjuvant treatment with neurotoxic chemotherapy, specifically taxanes. She has no prior history of peripheral neuropathy due to any cause, is not taking regular opioid-containing medications, and is not currently on anticonvulsants or other neuropathic pain medications. She has no history of coronary artery disease or congestive heart failure, and her ECOG Performance Status is 1. She is able to sign informed consent and complete questionnaires by herself or with assistance. She has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. She is not currently taking any vitamin E supplements and is willing to employ adequate contraception during the study. She is not currently taking anticoagulant medication and does not have diagnosed diabetes requiring insulin or oral hypoglycemic medications. She does not have head or neck cancers and is not scheduled to undergo radiation therapy while on the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a history of alcohol dependence. He has been abstinent for 7 days and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for alcohol use disorder treatment. He lives alone and is currently unemployed. He reports no allergies and takes no medications. He has no history of neurological disorders or seizures. He is right-handed and reports no hearing impairment. He has no history of psychiatric disorders other than alcohol dependence. He has no ferromagnetic objects in his body and is not afraid of enclosed spaces. He is willing to practice effective birth control methods during the study period. He is willing to provide urine samples for analysis of alcohol use.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy admitted to the pediatric medical service at Boston Medical Center due to a severe asthma exacerbation. He was brought in by his mother who reports a history of asthma attacks and the inability to control his symptoms at home. The patient is currently receiving oxygen therapy and bronchodilators, and his condition is improving. The family is English-speaking and has agreed to participate in family-centered walk rounds. The patient's mother is actively involved in his care and is present at the bedside each morning of hospitalization. The patient has no history of child maltreatment or neglect, and his admission does not involve a social assessment or concern by the patient care team. Additionally, the patient has not been transferred to or from the PICU as part of his inpatient care and has not been transferred from an outside institution for further care.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 5 on hemodialysis for the past 2 years. Her serum phosphate level has been consistently above 5.5 mg/dL despite taking sevelamer carbonate (Renvela®) as her current phosphate binder therapy. She has no history of dysphagia, bowel obstruction, ileus, or severe gastrointestinal motility disorders. Her medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. She is on insulin therapy, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 28.8 kg/m2 and her laboratory values are as follows: serum creatinine 8.5 mg/dL, serum calcium 9.2 mg/dL, serum phosphorus 6.8 mg/dL, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) 450 pg/mL. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

54-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer and lymphedema of the upper limb. She underwent a left modified radical mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection in [**2009**]. The patient noticed swelling and heaviness in her left arm in the following months, and was diagnosed with lymphedema. She has been receiving standard treatment for lymphedema, including manual lymphatic drainage and compression bandaging, but still experiences limitations in her daily activities due to the swelling and weight of her arm. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the use of muscle strengthening exercises in addition to complex physical therapy as a potential treatment for lymphedema. She has no history of renal dysfunction, deep vein thrombosis, heart disease, or active skin infections, and has not undergone any lymphedema reduction treatment in the past three months.

A 43-year-old woman with neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) has been diagnosed with bilateral vestibular schwannomas (VS) causing hearing loss, tinnitus, and vertigo. Her treating physician has recommended surgery for clinical indications, and the patient is scheduled for surgery within 4 weeks. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 70%, and she is able to care for herself with occasional help from others. Her hematologic, renal, and liver function tests are all within normal limits. She has stable neurologic deficits for more than a week and can swallow tablets. She has no serious concurrent infection or medical illness, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not received concurrent therapy for her tumor within the last 4 weeks. She has not received cytochrome P450-inducing anticonvulsants or similar agents within 10 days prior to starting lapatinib, and she does not have any significant gastrointestinal disorders or known cardiac disease requiring treatment. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent, has a normal cardiac left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by multiple-gated acquisition (MUGA) scan or transthoracic echocardiogram, and is willing to follow acceptable birth control methods to avoid conception.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who is scheduled for a routine screening colonoscopy. He has no previous history of colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, or colon resection. He is not currently pregnant or lactating, and he has never been incarcerated. He has no known allergies to peppermint oil or any other medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. His renal function is normal, and he does not have any non-correctable coagulopathies.

55-year-old male diagnosed with high cholesterol level during routine screening. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and coronary artery disease. He is currently on fluvastatin (40 mg/day) for the past 6 months with no significant improvement in his lipid profile. His last LDL-C level was 4.1 mmol/L. He reports occasional muscle aches but denies any significant muscle weakness. He is compliant with his medications and follows a healthy diet and regular exercise routine. He has no history of liver disease or myopathy. His BMI is 28 kg/m2. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy of rosuvastatin compared to his current medication.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with sickle cell disease at the age of 8. He has a history of recurrent vaso-occlusive crises (VOC) requiring multiple hospitalizations and blood transfusions. His genotype is HbSS. He has been taking hydroxyurea for the past 4 years to reduce the frequency and severity of VOCs. He is currently not experiencing any acute pain crisis, but reports occasional mild to moderate pain in his joints and bones. He is a non-smoker and does not have any history of lung infections or asthma. His most recent laboratory results show a total hemoglobin level of 8.1 g/dL, a reticulocyte count of 11.5%, and a lactate dehydrogenase level of 400 U/L. He is interested in participating in the study to help better understand the potential of exhaled carbon monoxide as a non-invasive marker of hemolysis in sickle cell disease.

This is a 52-year-old male who was recently admitted to the hospital after experiencing an acute brainstem stroke. He is currently experiencing dysphagia and has difficulty swallowing. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) applied over the pharyngeal motor area in improving his dysphagia symptoms. The trial will involve 60 patients with acute isolated brainstem stroke and dysphagia, with 30 patients receiving real stimulation and 30 patients receiving sham stimulation over a period of 4 consecutive days. The primary outcome being measured is the Penetration/Aspiration Scale after 4 consecutive days of stimulation, with secondary outcomes including changes in electromyographic parameters and pharyngeal cortical motor evoked potentials, changes in the Dysphagia Severity Rating Scale (DSRS), in the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), and in the "Dysphagia Limit Test". The patient will undergo swallowing evaluation through fiberoptic endoscopy, and his feeding status will be evaluated using the clinical "Dysphagia Severity Rating Scale", the "Functional Oral Intake Scale", and the "Dysphagia Limit Test". The patient will be randomly assigned to either the active treatment or sham group, and all patients will be evaluated at baseline and after 4 consecutive days of stimulation. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with severe COPD diagnosed 5 years ago. He presents to the clinic with shortness of breath, persistent cough, and wheezing. He reports having chronic hypoxemia and is currently on supplemental oxygen therapy. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He is currently taking amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin, and inhalers (albuterol and fluticasone). He reports no recent acute exacerbation or respiratory infection. His pulmonary function test shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 50% and a DLCO of 40% predicted. His oxygen saturation on room air is 87%. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and provides informed consent.

58 yo M admitted to the emergency department with symptoms of acute ischemic stroke, including right-sided weakness and slurred speech. The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was greater than 4 points, and the patient was deemed eligible for tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) treatment. The patient has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease but has a previous history of hypertension that is well-controlled on medication. The patient does not have a right-to-left cardiac shunt, and temporal windows are present. A CT scan confirms a clot in the middle cerebral artery. The patient has provided consent to participate in the study examining the safety, tolerability, and activity of microbubble-enhanced clotbust treatment as an adjunctive therapy to tPA treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He has not received any treatment for his condition and is currently treatment-naive. He has a history of heavy alcohol use but has been sober for the past year. He is a smoker and consumes 1-2 packs of cigarettes per day. He reports fatigue, abdominal pain, and occasional nausea, but denies any recent weight loss or jaundice. His BMI is 26 kg/m². His HCV RNA viral load is 2.5 x 10^6 IU/mL. He does not have co-infection with HIV or Hepatitis B Virus. He has no significant acute or chronic medical illness and is not taking any medications that could interfere with the study drug. He has not undergone any major surgery in the past 4 weeks and has not had any gastrointestinal surgery that could impact the absorption of the study drug. He is willing to be enrolled as an inpatient for 16 days.

A 45-year-old male veteran with a history of heartburn and regurgitation for the past 6 months presented to the gastroenterology clinic for evaluation. He has been taking over-the-counter antacids with no relief of symptoms. He denies any chest pain, dysphagia, or weight loss. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. Physical examination is unremarkable. An upper endoscopy was performed, and there were no erosive changes noted. The patient was diagnosed with non-erosive reflux disease (NERD) based on the presence of reflux symptoms and an abnormal esophageal pH result. He was offered participation in a clinical trial evaluating the use of narrow band imaging (NBI) in the diagnosis of NERD. The patient provided informed consent and was enrolled in the study. He will undergo NBI endoscopy with biopsies of the distal esophagus to assess for specific features that may be predictive of NERD. He will also be randomized to receive proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy or placebo and will undergo repeat NBI endoscopy to assess for resolution of NERD features. The patient will be followed up for 12 weeks with validated GERD questionnaires to assess symptom response to therapy.

A 32-year-old woman who had a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia 2 years ago is invited to participate in a research study. She had a full-term singleton pregnancy that lasted 38 weeks. She has a history of hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine 5mg daily. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She does not take NSAIDs, steroidal medications, statins, or other anti-inflammatory supplements. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in learning more about the study and willing to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis. He has been admitted to the hospital for the treatment of ascites and is experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating. He has no recent history of abdominal surgery and has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions that could lead to ascites. The patient has a social insurance and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and will undergo testing for IL-8, IL-6, and leptin levels in the ascitic fluid to determine the diagnostic performance of these markers for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). His Child-Pugh score will also be assessed to determine if there is a correlation between clinical features and the diagnostic performance of the markers.

A 40-year-old man was diagnosed with major depressive disorder approximately 6 months ago. He has been receiving treatment with two types of antidepressants for the past 8 weeks, with no significant improvement. He complains of difficulty falling asleep and maintaining sleep, with frequent awakenings during the night. These symptoms have been present for the past 3 months and have significantly impacted his daily life. He reports feeling tired and low energy during the day. He has no history of substance abuse or dependence, and he denies any current use of alcohol or drugs. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has no significant medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications other than his antidepressants. He works a day shift job and has no history of sleep apnea or periodic limb movement disorder. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol, which includes not changing his medication for the first 4 weeks of the study and participating in audiotaped treatment sessions.

A 64-year-old man has been experiencing difficulty in reading and blurry vision. He has been diagnosed with bilateral age-related cataracts and is scheduled for surgery. He has no history of ocular surgeries or laser treatments, tumors, or color abnormalities. He does not have diabetes, arterial hypertonia, or pseudoexfoliation-syndrome. He is not taking any medication. He is highly motivated to have the best possible visual outcome after surgery.

A 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage III melanoma on his back. He underwent surgery to remove the cancerous lesion and surrounding tissue. He has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health with a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80. He is HLA-A *0201 positive. His white blood count is within normal limits, and he has no history of autoimmune diseases or immunodeficiency. He is negative for HIV antibodies. He has no history of immunization with gp100 or MAGE-3. He is not currently taking any immunomodulating agents, systemic or inhaled steroid therapy, or hormone replacement therapy. He has no active systemic infections and is not lactating. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve the ability of his immune system to fight melanoma cells.

A 45-year-old female patient visits the general surgery outpatients clinic for a regular check-up. She has a family history of colon cancer, with her father being diagnosed with the disease at the age of 55. The patient is a housewife and has no significant medical history apart from occasional headaches. She has never undergone a colorectal cancer screening before and is interested in learning more about the disease and screening methods. The patient has no known allergies to any medication.

35F with history of regular menstrual cycles, experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding (PBLAC score of 200) for the past 2 months. She reports clots and needing to change her tampon or pad every hour or less. She has no previous history of fibroids or other gynecological conditions. She is not pregnant and has no desire for future fertility. She has a normal hemoglobin level and is not on any anti-coagulation therapy. She is willing and able to complete the follow-up requirements outlined in the study design section of the protocol and is willing to sign a consent form. She has no contraindication to MRI and no history of renal disease or uncontrolled hypertension.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with keratoconjunctivitis sicca (dry eye syndrome) by her ophthalmologist. She has been experiencing symptoms of dry, itchy, and red eyes for the past 6 months, which have been interfering with her daily activities. She has tried over-the-counter artificial tears and ointments, but they provide only temporary relief. She has no history of allergies or autoimmune diseases. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or current medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially provide a long-term solution to her dry eye symptoms.

56 yo M who underwent a CABG and aortic valve replacement procedure with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and COPD with a 30 pack year smoking history. Postoperative day 2 patient developed atrial fibrillation which was treated with anti-arrhythmic medications. Patient reports moderate levels of anxiety and pain in the hospital setting. Patient is interested in the feasibility of acupuncture treatment for arrhythmias and is able to provide informed consent. English-speaking patient with no additional cardiac or non-cardiac procedures. Platelet count is within normal limits. No sternal wound infections or wound-vac system application are present. The patient is not pregnant and is capable of completing all aspects of the trial. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - COPD (30 pack year smoking history) - CABG and aortic valve replacement procedure.

56yo male with a history of small cell carcinoma of the bladder, who has progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy. His current disease presents with lung metastases, liver metastases, and nodal disease. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate normal organ and marrow function. The patient has not received any prior treatment with PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors, including durvalumab or an anti-CTLA-4, including tremelimumab. The patient has not received any immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab or tremelimumab. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks based on assessment by the treating investigator. The patient has measurable disease by RECIST 1.1.

A 6-year-old girl was diagnosed with bile acid synthesis defects since infancy. She has been experiencing chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, and growth retardation. Her previous treatments with fat-soluble vitamins and medium-chain triglycerides showed inadequate results. Her medical history includes no other significant illnesses or surgeries. She is currently being treated with Cholbam for the past 2 months, and her symptoms have significantly improved. She has gained weight, and her diarrhea is less frequent. Her parents are willing to participate in the REPLACE Registry for Cholbam for the next 10 years to continue monitoring her progress and contribute to the research on the safety and effectiveness of this medication.

A 52-year-old man who has been on hemodialysis therapy for chronic kidney disease for the past year has been experiencing gum bleeding and bad breath for the past few months. He has noticed that his gums appear swollen and reddened. He has lost four teeth in the past year due to decay and his dentist has advised him to undergo periodontal treatment. He has no history of diabetes or liver disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of non-surgical periodontal therapy on serum albumin levels in patients on maintenance hemodialysis therapy.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl named Anna who is scheduled to undergo a peripheral venepuncture during her visit to a hospital clinic. She speaks Czech fluently and is able to distinguish three different sizes using toys. Anna's parents have given their informed consent for her participation in the study. She is generally healthy and has not received any analgesia prior to the procedure. During the assessment, Anna will be asked to evaluate her pain intensity using the Simplified Faces Pain Scale (S-FPS) and the Simplified Concrete Ordinal Scale (S-COS) on three different occasions: before the venepuncture, immediately after the venepuncture, and 5-10 minutes after the venepuncture. The attending nurse and the researcher will also evaluate Anna's pain using the Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) scale. Anna's ability to distinguish three sizes will be assessed using three identical toys of different sizes. Anna's parents will be present during the whole process but will not evaluate Anna's pain. They will be instructed not to provide verbal or behavioral cues to Anna during the data collection process.

A 32-year-old female presents with a history of obsessive-compulsive disorder for the past 10 years. She reports persistent unwanted thoughts and repetitive behaviors that interfere with daily functioning. She has tried various medications and therapies in the past but has not experienced significant improvement. Her current symptoms include checking and washing compulsions, as well as hoarding tendencies. She has no history of stroke, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or bipolar affective disorder. She is able to swallow tablets without difficulty. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study factors that may help predict medication response in OCD. She is willing to be randomly assigned to receive either clomipramine or escitalopram or duloxetine if she has previously tried the other medications. She is curious to learn how genetic markers and cortical inhibition may play a role in her medication response.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment or intervention, as it is an observational study to collect data from medical records of participants with Hepatitis C in Brazilian reference centers. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable.

This clinical trial is not applicable for individual patients because it is an observational study comparing infants of Ethiopian-origin mothers to non-Ethiopian origin mothers. It is not seeking individual participants but rather analyzing existing data from infants born at Hillel Yaffe medical center in 2009.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with general developmental delay in both cognitive and motor skills. He was born full term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. The mother reports that he was slow to reach developmental milestones such as sitting up, crawling, and walking. He currently attends a special education program for children with developmental delays. The medical history is unremarkable, and there is no family history of developmental delay or intellectual disability. The patient has undergone the Bayley Scales of Infant Development (BSID) test at the age of 18 months and 2.5 years. The results of the BSID test showed mild to moderate delay in all developmental areas. The current diagnosis of the child is GDD, and he is being followed by a pediatrician and a developmental therapist. The family has expressed interest in participating in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of the child's future developmental trajectory and potential interventions that may be beneficial for his development.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 18 and 50 who has not been diagnosed with malaria in the past 10 years. The patient is willing to participate in a study that involves receiving an injection of live infectious malaria parasites along with antimalarial medications to see if it can protect against malaria infection. The patient must have reliable access to the clinical trial center and be available to participate for the duration of the study. They must also be willing to undergo frequent outpatient clinic visits and keep track of their temperature and symptoms during certain sections of the study. The patient must not be pregnant or breastfeeding, and must have a negative HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C test. The patient must be willing to use reliable contraception during the study period if they are a female of childbearing potential. The patient must not have any medical conditions that would interfere with the study, including chronic or subclinical conditions that could be exacerbated by the administration of the PfSPZ-CVac components or malaria infection. They must also not have a recent travel history to a malaria endemic area or be planning to travel to a malaria endemic area during the study period. Finally, the patient must not have any contraindications to repeated phlebotomy or any other finding that would interfere with protocol adherence, assessment of safety or reactogenicity, or the patient's ability to give informed consent.

A 45-year-old male patient presented with a history of melanoma with one or more macroscopic lymph node metastases. He has no history of in-transit metastases within the last 6 months, and no other malignancies, except for a history of adequately treated skin cancer. He has a World Health Organization (WHO) Performance Status 1 and is willing to undergo triple tumor biopsies and extra blood withdrawal during screening and in case of relapse. He has not received prior immunotherapy targeting CTLA-4, PD-1 or PD-L1, and has not been on immunosuppressive medications within 6 months prior study inclusion. The patient has normal laboratory values and does not have any underlying medical conditions that would make the administration of study drug hazardous or obscure the interpretation of toxicity determination or adverse events. He is willing to use appropriate methods of contraception for 23 weeks after the last dose of investigational drug. The patient is capable of understanding and complying with the protocol requirements and has signed the Informed Consent document.

A 45-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has relapsed following chemotherapy. The patient has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy (cytarabine and an anthracycline) with no response. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and frequent infections. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 70% and a DLCO of 60%. The patient has a related donor who is an allele level haplotype-match at HLA-A, B, C, DP Beta 1 (DRB1), and DPB1 loci. The patient has no active CNS leukemia and no active infections. The patient is willing to undergo decitabine and total-body irradiation followed by donor bone marrow transplant and cyclophosphamide. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to use adequate birth control during the study treatment.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of psoriasis for over 10 years. He has been treated with topical steroids, phototherapy, and biologic therapy in the past, but has not responded well. He has a total body surface area (BSA) involvement of 8% and a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) Score of 16. He has a documented history of metabolic syndrome with elevated blood pressure, triglycerides, and a waist circumference greater than 40 inches. He is also a diabetic and has a history of high hs-CRP levels. He is not currently on any statin therapy or oral prednisone. He has no other history of systemic inflammatory diseases, chronic infections, or malignancies. He has normal renal function with a CrCl of 60 ml/min. He has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 or had any cardiac complications from it. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the impact of Tildrakizumab therapy on his coronary vasoreactivity and myocardial mechanics. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures. He is available for the duration of the study and is able to attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently in her sixth month of pregnancy. She has had a healthy pregnancy so far, with no complications or risk factors present. She is currently seeking to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effect of maternal DHA supplementation on the development of newborns. The trial involves consuming a balanced Mediterranean diet, along with two glasses of dairy products per day, for the remainder of her pregnancy and throughout lactation. She will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, with one group receiving a supplement of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and the other receiving a placebo. The study will involve taking blood samples from the mother at various points during and after pregnancy, as well as samples of mother's milk. The development of the newborn will be evaluated through cognitive and motor tests during the first year of life. The patient does not have any lactose intolerance or systemic illness, and is eager to participate in the study to potentially improve the development of her child.

A 2.5-year-old male child with the history of neonatal encephalopathy that required therapeutic hypothermia. The child was born at 37 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 3.2 kg via normal vaginal delivery. The child was initially admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit and was diagnosed with neonatal encephalopathy due to perinatal global hypoxic ischemic injury. The child was treated with therapeutic hypothermia for 72 hours and subsequently discharged home. The child's medical history was significant for episodes of seizures that were well-controlled with medication. The child's developmental milestones were delayed, and the child had difficulty with gross and fine motor skills. The child had a history of frequent respiratory infections and had been hospitalized for pneumonia once. The child had no significant cardiac or renal problems. The child was brought to the follow-up clinic for detailed cardiac, renal, neurological, haematological and neurodevelopmental assessments as part of this clinical trial. The parents provided written informed consent for the child's participation in the study.

The patient is an 80 year old woman who has been experiencing lower back pain for several months. She reports that the pain is worse with activity and has been limiting her ability to perform daily tasks. She has a history of osteoporosis and recently had a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan that revealed a T-score value less than -2.5. Further evaluation with imaging shows a thoracolumbar burst fracture with associated neurological compromise. She has not undergone any previous spinal surgery or vertebroplasty and does not have any malignancies or chronic steroid administration. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial on short segment fixation in thoracolumbar osteoporotic fracture and is interested in participating.

A 48-year old woman was diagnosed with uterine leiomyosarcoma six months ago. She underwent a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The pathology report indicated a stage III uterine leiomyosarcoma with high-grade histology. She has no other significant past medical history. She is married and has two children. She is currently not working. She reports some abdominal discomfort, but no other symptoms. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help treat her cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 5 years ago. She has been experiencing joint pain, stiffness, and swelling in her hands, wrists, and feet. She has been taking methotrexate for the past year, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that examines the relationship between inflammatory disease activity and endothelial function in RA patients treated with methotrexate and TNFalpha inhibitors in combination. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol and is able to give written informed consent. She has no history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, tuberculosis, histoplasmosis or listeriosis, and has not experienced persistent or recurrent infections. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses a reliable method of contraception. She has not used prednisolone more than 10 mg daily for 2 weeks at inclusion and has not used TNFalpha-inhibitor in the last 4 weeks. She has no history of cancer, uncontrolled diabetes, congestive heart failure, or recent stroke.

A 35-year-old male presents to the hospital with a 3-month history of nasal congestion, intermittent fever, and fatigue. He has lost 8 pounds in the past month. The patient has no significant past medical history, and he is not taking any medications. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Physical examination reveals an enlarged left cervical lymph node, and nasal endoscopy shows a nasal mass obstructing the left nasal passage. Biopsy of the nasal mass confirms the diagnosis of stage II NK/T-cell lymphoma. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and his bone marrow and organ functions are adequate. The patient has no prior history of pancreatitis and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient's blood glucose level is normal, and he has no contraindications for steroid use. The patient has no known history of other malignancies.

This is a 16 year-old female who has a history of self-injury. She has been cutting herself for the past 2 years as a way to cope with stress and emotional pain. She has been struggling with depression and anxiety and has seen a therapist in the past, but has not found it helpful in stopping her self-injurious behavior. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to understand the experiences and perceptions of adolescents who engage in nonsuicidal self-injury and to explore the impact of a brief mindfulness intervention on self-injury attentional bias. She is able to communicate in English and is not experiencing a suicidal crisis at the time of the study procedures.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to the intensive care unit due to severe sepsis secondary to pneumonia. He has a history of heavy smoking for the last 20 years, smoking one pack per day. He has been mechanically ventilated for the last 48 hours and is expected to remain ventilated for at least another week. His vital signs are stable, and he is receiving antibiotics and supportive care. He is experiencing nicotine withdrawal symptoms, such as anxiety, restlessness, and irritability. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has not used any form of nicotine replacement therapy in the last two weeks. He understands Dutch and has no known allergies to nicotine or patches.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who lives in Pondicherry, India. He works as a fisherman and spends most of his day on the sea. He has been experiencing swelling and pain in his legs for the past year. He visited a local clinic, where he was diagnosed with lymphatic filariasis caused by W. bancrofti infection. He has not received any treatment for filarial infection in the last two years. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive new treatment for his condition. He does not have any known medical problems or allergies. He weighs 65 kg and is 170 cm tall. He is married and has three children. His wife is not pregnant, and he is not aware of any other family member with a similar condition. He is able to read and write in Tamil and has no difficulty in understanding and following instructions. He is willing to provide written informed consent and is willing to receive home visits by the staff of the center.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been completely edentulous in the lower jaw for the past 2 years. She has been using conventional complete dentures but is experiencing difficulty with chewing and speaking. She has good general health and has not undergone any surgical procedures in the past year. She is a non-smoker and does not have any history of drug or alcohol abuse. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has adequate bone height and width in the mandible to receive 3 implants. She is willing to participate in the study for at least 3-4 years and is able to understand and respond to surveys used in the study. She does not have any severe TMDs related to joint pathology and is not suffering from any psychological or handicapped conditions that may hinder her involvement in the study.

A premature infant boy was born at 32 weeks of gestation and weighed 1500 grams at birth. He was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and has been under observation for the past 48 hours. His parents have been informed about the study and have given their written consent for his participation. The infant is hemodynamically stable and has not shown any signs of congenital intestinal obstruction or perforation, nor has he been diagnosed with gastroschisis, large omphalocele, or congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Additionally, he does not have any major congenital heart defects. The infant has not been transferred to another NICU and is eligible for the study. The researchers will randomly assign the infant to receive either the probiotics or placebo and will monitor him until 6 months post-discharge for the development of any infections or complications.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of metastatic melanoma. The patient underwent surgical resection of the primary lesion but developed metastatic disease in the lungs and liver. He has been treated with a combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA4) for the past 6 months. The patient has experienced some mild immune-related adverse events, including diarrhea and fatigue. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient has no significant medical history, and his laboratory values are within normal limits. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study and has a peripheral blood sample available for analysis. He is able to understand the nature of the study and is willing to comply with the study-related procedures.

A 25-year-old woman with a history of seasonal allergies and no known drug allergies presents to the clinic. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for hypersensitivity reactions to Vitrase (ovine hyaluronidase). She is in good health and has not taken any topical or systemic corticosteroids or antihistamines in the past 30 days. She has never been diagnosed with an active or chronic disease that may affect her immune function. She denies any history of alcohol or drug abuse within the past 6 months. She is willing to avoid any disallowed medications throughout the study.

A 26-year-old nulliparous woman at 39 weeks of gestation presents to the labor floor for induction of labor due to gestational diabetes mellitus. She has a history of no chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications. The fetal ultrasound showed a non-anomalous, singleton cephalic presenting fetus. The patient has no history of asthma or cardiac or hypertensive disease. She has received appropriate antenatal care throughout the pregnancy, with no complications noted. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in a randomized trial to compare propranolol versus placebo for induction of labor.

63 year old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presents with rectal bleeding and discomfort. Physical examination revealed grade 3 internal hemorrhoids, and a colonoscopy confirmed no evidence of malignancy. The patient was scheduled for an open hemorrhoidectomy surgery in the outpatient surgery unit. The patient speaks fluent French and has no objection to the use of his medical data in the context of this study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled for an elective breast surgery. She is otherwise healthy with no known medical conditions, and her BMI is within the normal range. She has no history of allergies to local anesthetics, and her ECG shows no abnormalities. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the nature of the study. She has given her consent to undergo either left thoracic paravertebral block or right interscalene block, as determined by randomization.

Maggie is a 68-year-old woman who has been concerned about her memory lately. She has difficulty remembering names and faces, and sometimes forgets where she parked her car. She has a family history of Alzheimer's disease, as her mother was diagnosed with the disease in her late 70s. She is currently taking medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which have been stable for the last 30 days. She is considered sedentary according to the Telephone Assessment of Physical Activity. She has no significant history of psychiatric disorders or drug/alcohol abuse. She has no history of stroke or cancer in the last 5 years. She has no significant pain or musculoskeletal disorder that would prohibit her from participating in an exercise program. She is willing to undergo a brain MRI scan and is cleared for exercise by her primary care physician. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce her risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who attends a high school in Baltimore-Washington, DC. She lives with her mother in a neighborhood that has been identified for this study. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) in the overweight range and is concerned about her weight and physical activity level. She reports that she is not involved in any sports or after-school activities and spends most of her free time watching TV or using social media on her phone. She has a history of unhealthy eating habits, including frequent consumption of fast food and sugary drinks. The patient reports that her mother works long hours and often brings home fast food for dinner. The patient and her mother live in an apartment complex that has a small playground but limited options for physical activity or healthy food choices nearby. The patient has no known medical or psychological conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is motivated to improve her health and is interested in learning more about how her neighborhood environment may be affecting her physical activity and eating habits.

A 53-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, and mood swings, for the past 6 months. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and is generally in good health. She has never been diagnosed with any significant comorbidities or diseases, and she is not currently taking any medication or supplements for her menopause symptoms. She has never had breast cancer or other malignancies, and she has not experienced any significant thromboembolism. She does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Nordic Kudzu in reducing her menopause symptoms.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with metastases to the liver, bones, and brain. He was recently hospitalized for shortness of breath and a CT scan revealed a non-high risk deep vein thrombosis in his left calf. He has a history of smoking and is currently receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of bleeding disorders or allergies to heparin. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He lives with his spouse and is able to receive outpatient LMWH treatment.

62 yo M with a history of open-angle glaucoma on latanoprost eye drops for the past 6 months presents for a routine follow-up with his ophthalmologist. Patient reports compliance with eye drop regimen but notes that he often blinks excessively and experiences eye irritation after administration of the drops. He has no other ocular or systemic complaints. The ophthalmologist informs the patient of a clinical trial being conducted to investigate the potential benefits of eyelid closure after eye drop administration. The patient is interested in participating and meets the study's inclusion criteria. The ophthalmologist reviews the study procedures and obtains the patient's consent to participate. The patient will be scheduled for 3 study visits, none of which will be part of routine clinical care. The patient will be instructed NOT to use his latanoprost eye drop on the day preceding study visit 1. During the first visit, the patient will be instructed in eyelid closure and randomized to perform eyelid closure for either 1 or 5 minutes after receiving a single drop of latanoprost in one eye, while the other eye serves as the control. IOP measurements will be obtained at baseline, 1 hour, 24 hours, and 1 week after the eye drop administration. The patient will be instructed to continue EC at home in the selected eye for the designated amount of time until the third study visit. The total duration of the study is 1-2 weeks, and the patient will continue his routine care throughout the study.

Patient is a 45yo male with a history of chronic sinusitis who is scheduled to undergo functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) under general anesthesia. He is in good overall health and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists classification of II. The patient weighs 70 kg and is 175 cm tall. He has no known history of neurological or psychiatric diseases, and has normal vision and hearing. The patient is able to communicate in Chinese Mandarin. He does not have any heart rate or gastrointestinal issues, urinary incontinence, asthma, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The patient does not have any known allergies to medications, including Butorphanol. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to comply with the protocol and procedures of the clinical trial.

A 35-year-old office worker seeks to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of physical training on physiological and psychological stress reactions and cognitive function. The participant reports that he has good health and is sedentary, with no history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or psychiatric illness. He works full-time in an office setting and is interested in improving his physical fitness and stress management skills. He is not taking any medication that could affect the outcome measures of the study. He is willing to commit to the 6-month intervention and adhere to the prescribed exercise regime.

A 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia and substance use disorder (cocaine) based on the Structured Clinical Interview for the DSM-5 (SCID). He has been stable on his current antipsychotic medication for the past month, and has demonstrated good compliance with his outpatient medications. He reports using cocaine on at least 4 of the past 30 days prior to randomization with at least one use in the week prior to randomization. He does not have any significant medical conditions or history of seizure disorder. He is willing to use appropriate birth control methods during the study, but is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is not currently on medications to treat substance use (disulfiram, naltrexone, acamprosate,methadone, buprenorphine, varenicline or buproprion). He is interested in participating in the study and is able to attend visits at one of the three sites in the US (UMass Medical School, Worcester MA, Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) or the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC)).

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) five years ago based on the McDonald criteria. She has been experiencing increasing levels of disablement including impairment, activity and participation, and socio-behavioral parameters. Her EDSS score is between 5.0-8.0. She is currently being treated with interferon-beta-1a and has been having regular visits with her neurologist. She experiences fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty with balance and coordination. She is eager to improve her quality of life and maintain muscle strength through exercise but finds it challenging to attend physical therapy sessions at a clinical setting due to mobility limitations. She lives with her husband who is supportive and willing to assist her with her daily exercise regimen. She does not have a history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, epilepsy, pacemaker, implanted defibrillator, unstable fractures, or other musculoskeletal diagnoses. Her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is > 22.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who is generally in good health. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and is willing to practice methods of birth control. She has not recently received any vaccinations or investigational agents. She has a negative history of drug abuse and a negative test result for drug(s) of abuse. She is willing and able to give written informed consent for study participation and provide consent for access to medical data. The patient does not have abnormal blood pressure or pulse rate, and does not have an abnormal screening electrocardiogram (ECG). She is not currently planning a pregnancy or lactating. The patient is available to be confined at the clinical research for a portion of each period.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl diagnosed with spastic cerebral palsy. She is able to walk independently for 20 meters with a slightly abnormal gait. She has difficulty with balance and coordination, and her gross motor function level is II. She is able to sit independently but has difficulty maintaining her balance for a prolonged period of time. She has no history of hip dislocation or severe contracture. Her Modified Ashworth Scale score is 1 for both lower extremities. She has no visual or auditory problems and is able to understand and follow simple verbal instructions. She has not had any botulinum toxin injections or surgical operations in the last 6 months. She is interested in participating in the study and has voluntary acceptance to participate.

A 58-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of chest pain that radiates to his left arm. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and he is a smoker. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 days, and they are not relieved by rest or nitroglycerin. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease based on his symptoms and a positive stress test. He is not currently experiencing an acute myocardial infarction. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates a new therapeutic strategy for ischemia-reperfusion injury.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of depression for the past 3 years. He has been on various antidepressant medications, but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most days. He has difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in his hobbies and social activities. He has no history of substance abuse or dependence. He is currently not receiving any formal psychotherapy. He is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. He has never taken vilazodone (SB-659746-A or EMD 68 843) in the past. He has no history of cardiac, renal, neurologic, cerebrovascular, hepatic, hematologic, metabolic or pulmonary disorders. He is not currently taking any psychotropic drugs or migraine medications with a serotonergic mechanism of action. He is not taking CYP3A4 inhibitors such as grapefruit juice, ketoconazole, diltiazem, and macrolide antibiotics or montelukast. He is willing to comply with the visit schedule and study procedures.

A 28-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 volunteers for a clinical trial to evaluate the relative bioavailability of TT-00420 tablet and capsule formulations and to evaluate food effect on the pharmacokinetics of TT-00420 tablet. She has no history of clinically serious disease and is not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medication (other than occasional paracetamol for headaches). She has no known history of alcohol or drug abuse and does not smoke or use nicotine-containing products. She has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease, or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. She is of non-childbearing potential and is willing to use highly effective contraception methods throughout the study. She is able to sign the informed consent and comply with the protocol.

A 65-year-old woman was diagnosed with non-metastatic, estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer and underwent surgery followed by adjuvant therapy with an approved non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole). She has been receiving the therapy for 18 months and has not experienced any fractures or other significant side effects. She has a family history of osteoporosis and has experienced some mild bone pain in the past. Her bone mineral density (BMD) scan shows that she is at risk of developing osteoporosis. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent bone loss and fractures while receiving her breast cancer treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) six months ago. She is currently on methotrexate and prednisone to manage her symptoms. She lives alone in a small apartment and has been under quarantine for the past three weeks due to the COVID-19 outbreak. She has been experiencing increased anxiety and sleep disturbances since the quarantine began. She has no history of psychiatric disorders but has a family history of depression. She is willing to participate in the study to help understand the psychological impact of quarantine on RA patients.

A 28 year old male who regularly participates in physical activities such as weightlifting and running. He has no history of chronic low back pain or any surgery to change the structure of his joints within the lower extremities. He has no known blood clotting disorder, peripheral vascular disease or systemic or widespread pain disorder. He is not currently under any activity limitations and has not experienced any significant injuries in the past six months.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She and her partner have been diagnosed with infertility and are interested in pursuing IVF or ICSI. She has a normal menstrual cycle length of 28 days and her BMI is within the range of 18-29 kg/m^2. She has no history of endocrine abnormalities or ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. She has both ovaries and no ovarian or abdominal abnormalities that would interfere with ultrasound examination. She has not had more than three unsuccessful COH cycles since the last established ongoing pregnancy. She has not used hormonal preparations within 1 month prior to randomization and has no contraindications for the use of gonadotropins. She is willing and able to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure. He has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs. His medical history reveals that he has been prescribed medication for hypertension for the past 5 years. He underwent an echocardiogram which showed left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF≤35%). He is currently in New York Heart Association functional class III-IV and his QRS is ≥120 ms. He has been optimized with medical treatment. He has been implanted with a Medtronic CRT-ICD device equipped with fluid accumulation diagnostics, AT/AF monitoring capability, wireless telemetry for automatic remote data transmission, and alerting system for physicians. He has not received CareLink® Network Monitor and was not managed by the Cardiac Compass report reviewing. The Carelink Network is available at his home and he is willing and able to use the Medtronic CareLink® Network Monitor and to perform the required duties at home. He is willing and able to sign an informed consent form. He does not have permanent AT/AF and his life expectancy is greater than one year.

54-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking presents to the emergency department with sudden, severe chest pain radiating to his back. CT scan reveals an acute aortic dissection involving the ascending aorta. The patient is hemodynamically stable without pharmacological support at the time of admission to the hospital. The patient is willing and able to comply with the standard follow-up visits planned after the implantation procedure and is willing and able to give informed consent. The patient is fit for open surgical repair involving circulatory arrest. The patient has no known sensitivities or allergies to nitinol, polyester, platinum-iridium, or polyethylene, no systemic infection or endocarditis, no free ruptured aorta, no acute or suspected acute stroke, and is not on inotropes at the time of arrival to the hospital. The patient has no need for mitral valve repair or replacement and is not currently enrolled or planning to be enrolled in another active study. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. The patient does not have an uncorrectable bleeding anomaly or a known sensitivity to radiopaque contrast agents that cannot be adequately pre-treated. The patient's eGFR is greater than 45 ml/min/1.73m2 before the intervention. The patient has no active malignancy causing expected survival to be less than 3 years and no other medical, social, or psychological problems that would preclude the patient from participating in this study.

A 58-year-old man, who works as an accountant, came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has a history of hypertension for the past 5 years, which is being managed by his primary care physician. He does not have diabetes, but his father had type 2 diabetes. He has no history of kidney disease or transplant. He has no known allergies to medications. His blood pressure measurements over the past year have been consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He has not seen his physician in the past 12 months. He is physically active, walking for at least 30 minutes every day. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of heart failure or cognitive impairment. He has no visual impairment and can read and understand information provided to him.

Patient A is a 7-year-old female who lives in a rural area of India. She attends school and enjoys playing outside with her friends. She has experienced abdominal pain and occasional diarrhea for the past few months. Her parents brought her to the local health clinic where she was diagnosed with soil-transmitted helminths (STH). She has no known allergies or medical conditions, and her parents have consented for her to participate in the clinical trial. She will receive albendazole treatment and will be monitored for the effectiveness of the treatment.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the drug-drug interaction of pyrotinib with a moderate CYP3A inducer. She is in good health and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and has not used any drugs or substances known to be inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4/5 within 90 days prior to the study. She has a body weight of 55 kg and a BMI within the range of 19-26 kg/m2. She has not donated blood or other blood products in the past 90 days and is willing to refrain from doing so during the trial. She has normal liver function test results and has not experienced any important primary organ diseases. Prior to participating in the trial, she will sign the informed consent and fully understand the trial content, process, and possible adverse reactions.

A 45-year-old woman is employed as an office manager and also takes care of her mother who is a Veteran diagnosed with depression and anxiety. She helps her mother with grocery shopping, managing finances, arranging medical appointments, and providing medication. She feels overwhelmed and stressed out while juggling her work and caregiving responsibilities. She has been feeling anxious and fatigued lately, which is affecting her work productivity. She is looking for a solution to manage her stress and maintain her work and caregiving roles effectively.

A 10-year-old male diagnosed with left-sided infantile hemiplegia due to a brain injury during birth, resulting in hemiplegia of the right side of his body, including the face, arm, and leg. The child has moderate intelligence and attends school, but suffers from poor attention, particularly visual attention, which affects his learning and acquisition of new skills. The child has no history of epilepsy, second stroke, or medication for psychiatric illness, and is not color blind. The lesion is on the non-dominant hemisphere. The child and their parents have been informed about the study and have given their consent for the child to participate in the study.
