The child will be randomly assigned to the group that will receive transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) with visual attention activities or the sham tDCS group with similar activities. Before and after the study, the child will undergo the Stroop-color testing and academic reading test to evaluate the effect of tDCS on visual attention span.

A 72-year-old female presents with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient has not received the pneumococcal vaccine before and is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the advancement of medical research. She reports no allergies to vaccines or any other medications. The patient denies any recent illnesses or hospitalizations. She is physically active and maintains a healthy diet. The patient's medical history is unremarkable except for controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin as prescribed by her primary care physician. The patient is willing to provide blood samples before and after receiving the pneumococcal vaccine for the evaluation of antibody production.

A 6-month-old baby boy was born with a heart defect and has undergone surgery to repair it. However, he has been consistently sick since birth and his doctors suspect that he may have Complete DiGeorge Anomaly (cDGA). After conducting several tests, his doctors confirm the diagnosis of cDGA. Without proper treatment, his immune system will remain compromised and he may not survive beyond 2 years of age. The only possible treatment for cDGA is thymus transplantation, which is still under investigation. The baby boy's parents are desperate to find a way to save their child's life and are willing to participate in this clinical trial. They understand the potential risks involved and are committed to following the protocol. They hope that their son will receive a successful thymus transplant and that his immune system will start to function normally.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD by his pediatrician. He exhibits symptoms of hyperactivity, inattention, and impulsivity, which have been causing problems at school and at home. His parents are concerned about his academic progress and social interactions with other children. The boy has no other medical conditions and is currently not on any medication for his ADHD. The parents have access to a computer with internet and are willing to participate in a clinical trial. They are interested in exploring non-medication treatment options for their son's ADHD symptoms. They hope that the Nurtured Heart Approach will help improve their son's behavior and quality of life.

The patient is a child between the ages of 3-18 years old who has been diagnosed with medically refractory epilepsy and is undergoing pre-surgical evaluation at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children. The child will be considered for inclusion in this study if they are undergoing SEEG recording as part of their clinical investigation. The suitability for the SEEG recording will be determined by a specialist epilepsy multidisciplinary team (MDT) and if the child qualifies, they will be invited to participate in this study during routine outpatient clinic visits. The study will involve the use of specially designed SEEG electrodes that can measure signals from single brain cells in order to assess whether studying the changes in the firing of individual cells improves our ability to localize seizures and therefore improves outcomes following surgery. Participation in the study is voluntary and requires informed consent from the child and their parents. The study will not alter the current patient pathway for children with medically refractory epilepsy undergoing pre-surgical evaluation and will not affect surgical planning and execution. Following the period of monitoring, the care of these children would not be altered in any way. The investigators aim to recruit 30 patients over a period of 3 years, of which 50% will have a normal MRI and 50% will have an identifiable lesion.

The patient is a 10-year-old Hispanic female who is concerned about her weight. She is currently in the 97th percentile for her age group and has a BMI of 28.5 kg/m2. She does not have any chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications, antibiotics, or probiotics. She has not experienced any enteritis symptoms such as diarrhea in the past month. She does not have a family history of obesity or metabolic disorders. She is otherwise healthy and active, participating in dance classes twice a week. Her parents have expressed concern about her weight and are willing to participate in the study to help her reach a healthy weight. They are willing to provide information about her nutritional intake and allow for analysis of her gut microbiome. They have given written and oral consent for their daughter's participation in the study.

The patient must be a healthy male or female between the ages of 18-50 years old with a body mass index (BMI) of 18 to <30 kg/m2 inclusive. They must have no clinically significant 12-lead ECG abnormalities, a QTc interval <450 ms for males and <470 ms for females, and a resting heart rate between 45-90 beats/minute at screening and check-in. They must be willing to use an acceptable method of contraception (double barrier) while participating in the study from screening onwards and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug. They must be willing and able to comply with all study procedures and have no concurrent disease or condition that would interfere with study participation or safety. They should not have a history of clinically significant cardiac condition, including myocardial ischemia or infarction, congestive heart failure, left ventricular hypertrophy, or cardiomyopathy. They should not have a history of palpitations, seizures, unexplained syncopal episodes, or symptomatic arrhythmias, or any condition that could lead to electrolyte disturbances. Additionally, they should not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse or any psychiatric, behavioral, or neuromuscular condition that may compromise the Investigator's evaluation of drug effect.

A 23-year-old woman who is a college student with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m^2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has a history of seasonal allergies but is not allergic to milk. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She typically eats breakfast every day and enjoys a variety of foods. She consumes a moderate amount of dairy products and sometimes drinks fruit juice or soda with meals. She is curious about how different beverages might affect her appetite and blood sugar levels. She is available to attend all study visits and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with early-stage cervical cancer. She has not undergone any treatment yet and is eligible for surgical excision. Her circulating CD4+ lymphocyte count is at least 400, and she has no history of hepatitis B or C. She has not been exposed to smallpox vaccination and has reacted to 2 or more antigens on the Pasteur Merieux CMI test. Her WBC count is greater than 3,000, and her platelet count is greater than 120,000. She has no bleeding disorder, and her bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are all within normal range. Her creatinine level is less than 1.3 mg/dL. She has no ongoing infection, no HIV antibody, and no serious medical or psychiatric illness. She has not had a second malignancy within the last 5 years, except for curatively treated basal cell skin cancer. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using adequate contraception. She does not have any household contact with chronic steroid therapy, renal or other allograft, known immunodeficiency, eczema or children under 5 years old.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) stage IIIA, who has undergone high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation at Vanderbilt University 1 month ago. He has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. The patient's physical examination is unremarkable, except for a palpable lymph node on the left side of his neck. The patient has undergone a fluorine 18-fludeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (PET) scan within 70 days prior to the high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation, and will have another PET scan at approximately 30 days and 100 days after the transplantation. The patient's blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 75 beats per minute, and BMI is 25. The patient is alert, oriented, and in no acute distress. He has no significant family history of cancer or other medical conditions.

The patient is a 24-year-old Norwegian woman who has experienced two or more episodes of patella dislocations in her right knee. She has been experiencing pain, stiffness, and instability in her knee and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to address her recurrent patella dislocation. The patient has no history of bilateral dislocations, and is committed to rehabilitation and following the study protocol. She has no established patellofemoral arthrosis and has a tibial tuberosity trochlear groove distance (TT-TG) less than 20 mm. The patient is a Norwegian citizen, and falls within the age range of the study at 24 years old. The patient has undergone imaging studies, including CT and MRI, and meets all inclusion criteria for the study. The patient will undergo clinical examinations, functional tests, arthroscopy, and various scoring systems, including the Kujala score, Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), Lysholm score, Tegner activity score, visual analogue scale (VAS) and Activity Scale. She will be followed up for 3 months, 6 months, 12 months, and 36 months.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) for the past 2 years. She reports abdominal pain, bloating, and alternating episodes of diarrhea and constipation. The symptoms have greatly affected her quality of life, causing her to miss work and social events. She has tried various over-the-counter remedies with little relief. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or current medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for IBS.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain and was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation acute myocardial infarction (STEMI). He underwent successful primary percutaneous coronary revascularization within the first 12 hours after the onset of symptoms. He has a medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of coronary artery disease or any other cardiovascular conditions. He has a history of allergic reaction to contrast media. He has no history of renal dysfunction or malignancy. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old non-smoking woman who has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for over a month. She has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Her tumor has been confirmed to have the ALK rearrangement. She has not received any prior treatment with ALK inhibitors. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no CNS metastases, and her tumor tissue is available for central analysis. She has at least one measurable lesion as per RECIST v1.1. Her labs show normal organ function, and her QT interval is within normal range. She is post-menopausal and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing to use a highly effective form of contraception during the study. She understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has provided signed and dated informed consent. She is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits and study procedures.

The patient is a 30 year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. She has regular menstrual cycles with no history of polycystic ovary syndrome or endometriosis. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and does not smoke or use drugs. Her partner has no known fertility issues. She has not undergone any fertility treatments previously. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to increase her chances of pregnancy through IVF.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who has no history of musculoskeletal or neurological disease, cancer, coagulation disorder, mental illness, or drug addiction. He is not currently experiencing any pain or taking any analgesics, neuroleptics, antidepressants, corticoids, or alpha2-blockers. He does not have any allergies to the ultrasound gel and has no history of cardiac illness, vascular disease, regional scars, skin transplants, or hypoesthesia. He has not received extracorporeal shockwave therapy within the last two weeks. The patient has voluntarily agreed to participate in the study and has signed a written informed consent. The patient will be asked to undergo the induction of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness in the non-dominant biceps brachialis muscle and will be randomized to receive either (1) focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (Verum), (2) sham shock wave (Sham) or (3) no treatment (Control). The patient will be followed up 72 hours after the induction of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness.

Sophie is a 7-month-old baby girl who was born full-term and has been formula-fed since birth. She weighs 7.5 kg and her height is at the 50th percentile for her age according to the EURO Growth Guidelines. She has been introduced to fruits and vegetables as complementary foods for the last two months. She is currently in good health and has never had any gastrointestinal issues or allergies. Her mother speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in this study. Sophie is not taking any medication, and her mother confirms that she has not taken any antibiotics or laxatives in the last 14 days. Sophie has no history of drug or alcohol abuse by her mother, and there are no reasons for her to be excluded from the study according to the PI/study personnel. Her parents have voluntarily agreed to participate in this clinical trial and have successfully completed the informed consent form.

This study does not involve enrolling patients for a clinical trial. It is a national health interview survey in Taiwan aimed at gathering health-related data from a representative sample of the population. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is currently hospitalized with gross hematuria and passing blood clots. Her urine cytology and PCR tests have confirmed the presence of Polyoma BK virus. She has a Foley catheter in place and has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study. Her serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dl and her calculated creatinine clearance is 65 ml/min using the Cockcroft-Gault Creatinine Clearance formula. Her urine protein is less than 100 mg/dl and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not received prior therapy with formalin or carboprost 1 mg % administered intravesically and has no hypersensitivity to cidofovir, probenecid, or sulfa-containing medications. She has not received prior cidofovir therapy within 2 weeks and has not been enrolled in the study before. She is willing to use 2 acceptable methods of birth control during the study period and for 2 months afterward. She does not have evidence of end-organ adenoviral infection.

A 13-year-old Egyptian boy from a rural area in Sohag governorate comes for a dental examination. He has no apparent medical issues and complains of no dental pain. He has a full set of permanent teeth that have fully erupted, and there are no apparent orthodontic problems. He has not had any previous dental treatment or restorations, and his teeth do not show any notable wear or decay. He has no sensitivity or adverse reactions to dental materials. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no craniofacial developmental abnormalities. He has no teeth with malalignment or rotation, and there are no teeth with any inaccuracy caused by the impression taking, pouring impressions with dental stone, or any damage or breakage while the dental casts had been stored. There are no teeth with developmental anomalies such as microdont teeth, teeth with extra cusps or big talon cusps, or peg or conical shaped teeth. Additionally, he does not have any supernumerary or supplemental teeth.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a liver lesion through a previous imaging test. She is scheduled for a liver biopsy as part of her standard care. She has no contraindications to getting a contrast-enhanced MRI examination, and her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 based on her recent serum creatinine levels. She has no known history of claustrophobia or allergic reactions to magnetic resonance contrast material. She has not been diagnosed with late-stage renal failure or implanted with any non-MRI compatible medical devices. She is not a prisoner or a member of any other vulnerable populations. She speaks fluent English.

This is a 68-year-old right-handed woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of vestibular stimulation on sleep. She has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep for the past few months and is interested in exploring non-pharmacological options to improve her sleep quality. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and does not take any medication that is known to influence sleep. She does not have any history of neurological or psychiatric diseases and has a MoCA score of 28. She does not smoke or use any drugs, and drinks alcohol moderately, with no more than 2 glasses of wine per week. She consumes less than 2 drinks or foods containing caffeine per day. She does not have a history of sleep disorder, shift work, or recent travel across time zones. She typically sleeps for 7 hours per night, but has been experiencing frequent awakenings and difficulty falling back asleep. She does not have any skin allergies or sensitivity, and does not have any diseases of the vestibular system. She is excited about the possibility of participating in this study to potentially improve her sleep quality and overall well-being.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus 2 years ago. He has been taking metformin at a dose of 1000 mg daily for the past 6 months. His HbA1c level has been ranging between 7.5% to 8.5% in the past 3 months. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and he reports no history of diabetic complications or cardiac problems. He is currently unemployed and lives alone. His family history is positive for T2DM in his father and grandfather. He has no known drug allergies or medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who was involved in a serious car accident 2 years ago. Since then, she has been experiencing recurrent intrusive thoughts and nightmares related to the accident. She avoids driving and has trouble sleeping. She has been diagnosed with PTSD by a psychiatrist. She is currently not taking any medications for her symptoms. She has a history of mild depression and anxiety, but has not been on any medication for these conditions in the past year. She is not currently pregnant or nursing. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for her PTSD.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman living in a rural area of Nanhe County, Hebei province, China. She had an ischemic stroke two months ago and has been diagnosed at the county hospital. Currently, she is in a clinically stable condition and not receiving acute stroke treatment. She is able to communicate in Mandarin and has basic communication ability. The patient is willing to participate in the study and give participant informed consent. She lives in her own house with her husband and will continue to live in the village for at least nine months during the next 12 months. She has no serious life-threatening disease or expected life span of less than 6 months. The patient is eager to receive secondary stroke prevention care and is interested in learning new technologies to improve her health.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with cirrhosis of liver. He is currently asymptomatic and has no history of chronic kidney disease. His kidney function tests are within normal limits with a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL and creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. He has not undergone any contrast imaging procedure in the last 4 weeks and has no history of anaphylaxis to contrast media. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of N-Acetyl Cysteine in preventing Contrast Induced Nephropathy in patients with cirrhosis of liver.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and feelings of anxiety. She is currently in her junior year of high school and has been struggling with academic stress. She has no past medical history of psychiatric illness, but she has been feeling low and irritable lately. She has been finding it hard to focus and has been experiencing frequent headaches. She has tried over-the-counter sleep aids with little success. The patient is not currently taking any prescription medications or herbs that affect sleep. She has never been hospitalized for substance use or suicide attempts. She reports no known history of sleep apnea or major medical conditions. The patient has not received psychotherapy for depression, anxiety, or sleep health deficits in the past. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been on chronic hemodialysis for the past six months due to end-stage renal disease. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, both of which are currently well-controlled. She has no history of active malignant disease or liver cirrhosis. Her current hemodialysis treatment is stable and adequate with a Kt/V of 1.5 and she undergoes hemodialysis for 4 hours 3 times weekly. Her current hydration status is edema-free and she doesn't have any neuroid-muscular diseases. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She will undergo various assessments to evaluate her nutritional status including blood tests, anthropometry, MIS, GNRI, bioelectric impedance analysis, and several measures of clinical outcome including prospective mortality and hospitalization.

This is a 60 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and knee osteoarthritis. He has been experiencing pain in his knee with a VAS score of 4 out of 10. He has not taken any analgesics in the last 24 hours and is not currently using anti-inflammatory steroids, tranquillizers or antidepressants. He is not sensitive to touch and has no systemic inflammatory disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the immediate effects of manual therapy versus TENS on pain management in patients with knee osteoarthritis. He understands that there is a possibility of receiving either manual therapy or TENS and that the study will be evaluating the efficacy of the interventions. He is willing to undergo the assessments prior to the intervention, immediately after it and 72 hours after it. He has no cardiac pacemaker and is otherwise in good health.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has been struggling with heroin addiction for the past five years. He has attempted to quit using heroin several times but has been unsuccessful. He has a history of depression and anxiety and has been on medication for these conditions in the past. He is currently unemployed and lives with his girlfriend who is also a heroin user. He has no children and no significant medical history other than his addiction. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help him overcome his addiction. He has agreed to have his significant other participate in the program with him. He is not currently taking any medications other than those prescribed for his depression and anxiety. He has no allergies to any of the medications being used in the trial. He is not currently in any other substance abuse treatment program. He is willing to undergo detoxification and participate in outpatient treatment for six months.

62-year-old male, former smoker with a 35 pack-year history of smoking, diagnosed with moderate to very severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with a pre and post-albuterol/salbutamol FEV1 of <=70% predicted normal value at Visit 1. The patient is experiencing shortness of breath (dyspnoea) with a score of >= 2 on the Modified Medical Research Council Dyspnoea Scale (mMRC) at Visit 1. The patient is not diagnosed with asthma, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, active lung infections (such as tuberculosis), and lung cancer. The patient has no significant respiratory conditions other than COPD. The patient has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to any anticholinergic/muscarinic receptor antagonist, beta2-agonist, lactose/milk protein or magnesium stearate or a medical condition such as narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy or bladder neck obstruction that contraindicates study participation or use of an inhaled anticholinergic or beta2 agonist. The patient has not been hospitalised for COPD or pneumonia within 12 weeks prior to Visit 1 and has not had lung volume reduction surgery within the 12 months prior to Screening (Visit 1). The patient's 12-lead ECG conducted at Visit 1 shows no abnormal and significant ECG finding. The patient is not using any medications that would exclude him from the study. The patient has signed and dated written informed consent prior to study participation.

A 50 year old female is scheduled for coronary artery bypass graft surgery due to significant blockages in her coronary arteries. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but is otherwise healthy. She is concerned about her recovery after surgery and is interested in participating in a study that explores the benefits of exercise on cardiac rehabilitation. She is able to walk short distances without difficulty and has no advanced vision defects. She has not been diagnosed with any pulmonary, neurological or musculoskeletal diseases that would limit her participation in exercise training. She has an ejection fraction of 60%. She is willing to cooperate in verbal and auditory terms to complete the exercise program.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer after presenting with abdominal pain, bloody stool, and unintentional weight loss. She underwent a colonoscopy which revealed a large mass in her descending colon. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Further imaging studies revealed multiple liver lesions consistent with metastatic disease. She was started on first-line chemotherapy with 5-fluorouracil and irinotecan. After several months of treatment, her disease progressed and she was deemed ineligible for surgery. She is now being considered for a clinical trial that includes intermittent oral Xeloda, or iv fluorouracil/leucovorin, in combination with intravenous Eloxatin (oxaliplatin). She is a non-smoker with a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work or sedentary activities such as light housework or office work. She has no history of previous treatment with oxaliplatin or any previous chemotherapeutic agent or systemic anticancer regimen for metastatic disease. She understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is interested in participating to potentially benefit from a new treatment option.

The patient is a 31-year-old female with a BMI of 23. She has been trying to conceive for more than a year with no success. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and her last period started 4 days ago. She has no known medical conditions or history of infertility in her family. She presents with normal uterine and adnexal ultrasound findings consistent with assisted reproductive technology (ART). Her hormone levels of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and estradiol (E2) are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the efficacy and safety of highly purified menotropin (Menopur®) with follitropin beta (FOLLISTIM®) in patients undergoing gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles. She agrees to comply with the requirements of the protocol, including scheduled clinic visits and laboratory tests. She has not participated in any experimental drug study within the past 30 days and is not a gestational or surrogate carrier.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. The patient was diagnosed at stage IV and has undergone tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy but failed to respond to it. The patient has a confirmed ALK-positive status. The patient has at least one evaluable or measurable lesion as per RECIST version 1.1. The patient has not received systematic chemotherapy for advanced lung cancer but has undergone neoadjuvant therapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient is expected to survive for at least 3 months. The patient has undergone a serum pregnancy study within 2 weeks prior to the first dose and the results are negative. The patient is using birth control during the study period and within 180 days after the last administration of the study drug. The patient meets the laboratory test value criteria for the study. The patient voluntarily joined the study, signed informed consent, has good compliance, and will follow up. The patient has not previously received any T cell costimulation or immunological checkpoint treatment, including but not limited to CTLA-4 inhibitors, PD-1 inhibitors, PD-L1/2 inhibitors, or other T cell-targeting drugs. The patient does not have an active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment. The patient does not have interstitial lung disease, drug-induced pneumonia, radiation pneumonitis requiring steroid therapy, or active pneumonia with clinical symptoms or severe pulmonary dysfunction. The patient does not have a previous or current history of cancer other than NSCLC, except for non-melanoma skin cancer, in-situ cervical cancer, or other cancers that have received curable treatment and have shown no signs of recurrence for at least 5 years. The patient has fully recovered from toxicity and/or complications from any intervention prior to initiation of treatment (i.e., ≤ grade 1 or level required at baseline, excluding fatigue or hair loss). The patient does not have a tendency to hereditary bleeding or coagulopathy. The patient does not have clear or suspected brain metastases. The patient does not have clinical symptoms or diseases of the heart that are not well controlled. The patient does not have uncontrolled hypertension or hyperglycemia after treatment. The patient does not have a clinically uncontrollable third interstitial fluid. The imaging (CT or MRI) does not show that the tumor invades the large blood vessels or is highly likely to invade the important blood vessels during the follow-up study and cause fatal bleeding. The patient does not have a history of immunodeficiency, including HIV positive, or other acquired, congenital immunodeficiency disease, or history of organ transplantation and bone marrow transplantation. The patient does not have active hepatitis B or hepatitis C. The patient has not received or will receive a live vaccine within 30 days of the first treatment. The patient has not applied NMPA standard modern Traditional Chinese medicine preparation against lung cancer and immunomodulator simultaneously. The patient does not have allergic reactions to test drugs for this application. The investigator has not determined that the subject had other factors that might lead to the termination of the study.

Patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm (PanNEN) confirmed by biopsy. The patient underwent surgical intervention for the PanNEN, and a pre-operatory CT scan with IV contrast was performed in the institution between 2009 and 2017. The patient has no known allergies to contrast agents and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not pregnant.

A 42-year-old Asian woman was diagnosed with PTCL-NOS after experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and fever for several weeks. She underwent chemotherapy with CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) and achieved partial remission but relapsed after 4 months. She received two cycles of brentuximab vedotin (BV) but the disease progressed. She was referred to the clinical trial for Copanlisib and Gemcitabine in Relapsed/Refractory PTCL. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, with a bi-dimensional measurable lesion in the liver. Her laboratory results showed a serum Cr of 1.3 mg/dL, AST 25 U/L, ALT 22 U/L, bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, PT 12.5 seconds, aPTT 31 seconds, lipase 25 U/L, ANC 2000/µL, platelet count 90,000/µL, and hemoglobin 10 g/dL. Her LVEF was 60%, which is within the normal range. She has no history of CNS involvement, diabetes, hepatitis B or C, HIV, interstitial lung disease, or other malignancies within the past 3 years. She has no serious illness or medical conditions, and she is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A premature baby boy weighing 750 grams was born at 25 weeks gestation to a 30-year-old woman. The baby boy has respiratory distress and requires respiratory support. He has no known chromosomal abnormalities or central nervous system abnormalities. The parents have agreed to participate in the study.

A 12-year old girl living in Botswana was diagnosed with HIV/AIDS two years ago. She is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and has been experiencing good control of her viral load. Her past medical history is significant for mild asthma and she is currently being treated with a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid. She lives with her parents and two siblings. The patient complains of occasional body aches and fatigue. She is able to attend school regularly but has missed some days due to feeling unwell. She enjoys playing with her siblings and friends but feels tired easily. She doesn't have any other chronic health conditions unrelated to HIV/AIDS. She doesn't take any vitamin D supplementation above 400 IU/d. She and her family are committed to participating in the 12-week study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in HIV-infected children and adults living in Botswana.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who experienced a traumatic event 6 months ago. She has been experiencing symptoms of PTSD, including flashbacks, avoidance behaviors, and hyperarousal. Her parents have noticed a significant change in her behavior since the event, including difficulty sleeping and increased anxiety. She has no pre-existing mental health conditions and is not currently taking any medication for her symptoms. She has no history of seizures, head injuries, or other neurological conditions. She is currently attending school and has not missed any significant amount of time due to her symptoms. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and are willing to bring her to all necessary appointments.

A 45-year-old woman presented to the clinic with severe pain in her right flank that radiated to her groin. She has a history of recurrent kidney stones for the past 5 years. Her symptoms started 2 days ago with nausea and vomiting. She reports passing small stones in the past, but this time the pain is more severe and the stones are not passing. She underwent a CT scan that showed a 6 mm stone in her right kidney. She is currently taking ibuprofen for pain relief, but it only provides temporary relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her pass the stone without the need for anesthesia. She is a non-smoker and doesn't have any known allergies. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and occasional headaches. She takes lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension management. She is otherwise healthy and physically active.

The patient is a 45 year old woman with a history of uterine prolapse and pelvic organ dysfunction, which has been causing her significant discomfort and embarrassment. She has undergone vaginal gynaecological surgery for prolapse repair and is currently in the post-operative phase. She is experiencing difficulty controlling her bladder and bowel movements, and is also experiencing pain and discomfort in her pelvic area. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of physiotherapy treatment on pelvic function in post-surgical patients. She has no history of malignancy, and has not undergone anti-incontinence surgery or laparotomy. She is willing to undergo pre- and post-operative physiotherapy treatment as part of the trial, and is willing to be evaluated at 3, 6 and 12 months post-operatively. She hopes that the trial will help her regain control over her bladder and bowel movements, and improve her overall quality of life.

Patient is a 27-year-old sexually active woman who presented with lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge. She reports having unprotected sex with a new partner two weeks ago. She also reports having a history of PID and has been treated before. The patient is experiencing pain with a VAS score of 6. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has no history of gynecological tumors or other diseases that may affect the clinical trial. She is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and not preparing for pregnancy within the next 6 months. The patient has not taken similar drugs in the past two weeks and is not participating in or has participated in any other clinical trials in the past three months.

A 45 year old male presents to the urology clinic with severe colicky pain in the right flank region for the past 2 days. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and has passed kidney stones in the past. On examination, there is tenderness in the right flank region and the patient has a guarded gait. The ultrasound reveals a 1.5 cm radio-opaque stone in the right upper ureter with a high attenuation value of 1100 HU. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of ultraslow rate of SWL versus slow rate, power ramping SWL for ureteric stones with high attenuation value.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past two years. She has tried multiple antidepressant medications and psychotherapy treatments but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She presents with feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and anhedonia. She has a MADRS score of 30 and a CGI-S score of 5. She is currently not pregnant or lactating and is using an acceptable form of birth control. She is willing to comply with all the requirements of the study and is considered by the investigator to be likely to adhere to the protocol. She has not been treated with botulinum toxin A in the past 12 months and does not have another Axis I disorder as a principal diagnosis in the past 6 months. She does not have a history of substance abuse or dependency in the past 2 months and has tested negative for illicit drugs on urine drug screen. She has not endorsed MADRS item 10 (suicidal ideas) at a level of 5 or more or attempted suicide in the past six months. She is not considered to be at a significant risk of committing homicide and does not have an unstable medical condition. She has not had a change in her medication or psychotherapy treatment regimen in the past month and has not proved to be refractory to three or more adequate antidepressant treatments with methods that have different mechanisms of action.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty with urination. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has tried several medications without success. He is experiencing urgency, frequency, and incomplete emptying of the bladder, which is causing him discomfort and interfering with his daily activities. He also reports occasional bladder pain. He has no history of pelvic surgery or bladder malignancy, and he is willing to participate in the study. He is not currently pregnant nor has a history of STDs or bacteriuria. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He is looking for a solution to his urinary problems and hopes to contribute to the development of customised therapies for lower urinary tract dysfunction.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who has tested positive for HIV. She is currently receiving care at a study site and is interested in participating in the study to help future HIV-positive pregnant women and their babies. The patient is in her second trimester and has been receiving antiretroviral therapy since she tested positive. She has a history of injection drug use and has been on methadone maintenance treatment for the past year. The patient reports good adherence to her medication regimen and has been attending all of her scheduled prenatal appointments. She is primarily concerned about the potential transmission of HIV to her unborn child and wants to ensure that she is receiving the best care possible.

A 30-year-old woman, who had her first baby 6 weeks ago, came to the clinic feeling down and overwhelmed. She has been crying a lot and feeling hopeless. She has no energy to do anything and has lost interest in things she used to enjoy. She also has trouble sleeping and eating. She has no previous history of depression or anxiety. She has been married for 5 years and has a supportive husband. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently breastfeeding and has no medical conditions. She has a stable job as an accountant and has been on maternity leave for the past 6 weeks.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a family history of breast cancer. She recently discovered a lump in her left breast and underwent a biopsy. She is anxious about the results of the biopsy and is keen to receive timely notification of the results. She is comfortable with modern technology and frequently uses her smartphone and computer to communicate with her healthcare providers. She prefers to receive notifications through the online patient portal as it is convenient and accessible at any time. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study to share her preference for biopsy notifications.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired man who leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a BMI of 28 and has never smoked. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, renal, liver disease or HIV. His family history is positive for hypertension (his mother) and diabetes (his father). He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He is interested in improving his health and willing to participate in a research study that investigates the impact of short-term exercise on cardiovascular health.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester visits a study site for a routine check-up. She is fluent in both English and Spanish and has a cell phone with text messaging capabilities. She has never received the inactivated influenza vaccine before and is willing to receive it at the visit. She has no contraindications to the vaccine and has not taken any antipyretics in the past 6 hours. She is willing to report any adverse events, specifically fever, via text message through the end of her pregnancy. She is in good health and has no history of complications in prior pregnancies.

A 65-year-old woman with bilateral visually significant senile cataract visits the clinic complaining of difficulty in reading, driving and recognizing faces. The patient has no history of any ocular diseases or surgeries. The patient's corneal astigmatism is less than 2.0 diopters and potential acuity meter (PAM) is better than 0.2 LogMar. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. The patient is interested in undergoing cataract surgery and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the visual performance, total and high order wavefront aberrations and contrast sensitivity in eyes implanted with one monofocal aspheric intraocular lens (IOL) and two spherical IOLs (SofPort AO, Soflex,AcrySof®IQ (40 eyes), AcrySof®Natural and AMO®Sensar).

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal AF that has been symptomatic and refractory to at least one antiarrhythmic medication. He has had at least one episode of AF documented by ECG or Holter within 12 months of randomization in the trial. The patient is not currently on continuous anticoagulation therapy with warfarin for > 4 weeks prior to ablation but is willing to undergo a transesophageal echocardiogram to exclude the presence of thrombi or other abnormalities that discourage performing the procedure. He is able and willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has no contraindications to systemic anticoagulation with heparin or coumadin and has not previously undergone atrial fibrillation ablation, either by surgery or by percutaneous catheter. He has a left atrial size of < 55 mm and does not have hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism. The patient is not currently enrolled in another investigational drug or device study and does not have a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator.

17-year-old male football player with no history of injury or medical conditions. He has been playing football for the last 5 years and currently trains 5 days a week with his team. He is committed to improving his game and is willing to participate in the study. He reports no difficulties with balance or coordination and is excited about the opportunity to incorporate cognitive-based neuromuscular exercises into his training program.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU with sepsis and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include metoprolol, lisinopril, and metformin. Upon admission, his SOFA score was 7, with a lactatemia of 3.5mmol/l, pH of 7.14, PaCO2 of 40mmHg, and bicarbonatemia of 16mmol/l. He is intubated and on mechanical ventilation. His blood pressure is stabilized with norepinephrine. He is not on renal replacement therapy, and his urine output is maintained at 40 ml/h. He has no history of gastrointestinal disorders or chronic diarrhea. He is not pregnant and has no protected medical status. His estimated life expectancy is greater than 48 hours. He has not received Sodium Bicarbonate in the past 24 hours. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

A 32-year-old female patient was admitted to the hospital with acute respiratory distress syndrome and was placed on mechanical ventilation. The patient's medical history was significant for a recent motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple fractures of the pelvis and femur requiring surgical intervention. During the course of her hospitalization, the patient developed hypotension with a mean arterial blood pressure of 60 mmHg. The patient did not have a history of intracranial disease, and there was no evidence of local causes in the eye. The patient did not need high PEEP and had no known history of cardiac disease or organ failure at admission. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and was enrolled in the clinical trial to examine the Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter measurement for the prediction of fluid responsiveness in hemodynamically unstable patients.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who was born prematurely at 29 weeks of gestation. He did not have cerebral palsy but his parents noticed some difficulties in his language development. He had some speech therapy sessions in the past and currently attends a special education program. He is currently in first grade of elementary school and having difficulties in reading and writing. His parents reported that he has trouble pronouncing some sounds and often confuses letters. He also has some difficulties in following instructions and understanding complex sentences. He has no other medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the LAMOPRESCO-2 study, which aims to assess the effect of a specific language stimulation program on the learning of written language. The patient will be randomized to either the intervention or control group, and his progress will be monitored for the next 2 years.

A 10-year-old Caucasian male with cystic fibrosis is being followed at the pediatric center for his condition. He has a history of chronic respiratory infections, requiring frequent hospitalizations and pulmonary treatments. He is currently on a regimen of inhaled bronchodilators, mucolytic agents, and antibiotics. The patient and his parents are fluent in French. The patient presents with complaints of difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep at night, as well as excessive daytime sleepiness. He is also experiencing frequent nightmares. The patient's parents report that his symptoms have been ongoing for several months, and they have tried various methods to improve his sleep hygiene without success. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial investigating sleep disorders in children with cystic fibrosis.

A 70-year-old man visited the clinic for his routine check-up. He had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He was concerned about his physical and mental health as he had noticed a decline in his balance and memory. He had never participated in any structured exercise program and was considered sedentary. He denied any hearing or visual impairment and was not under any psychotropic treatment or beta-blockers. His MMSE score was 29, indicating cognitive health. The cardiologist conducted a maximal VO2 cycle-ergometer test and confirmed that the patient was suitable for moderate physical activity. The patient was interested in participating in a training program that could improve his cognitive and physical functions and was willing to comply with the study schedule and procedures.

Patient is a 28-year-old female from the United States who presents with a missing upper front tooth due to trauma. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. Her BMI is 22, BP: 110/70, HR: 80/min. Her oral hygiene is good with a full mouth plaque score of 20%. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has not undergone any previous dental procedures or radiation therapy in the head-neck area. Her periodontal condition is healthy. She is interested in immediate restoration procedure for her missing tooth and has voluntarily agreed to participate in the clinical trial.

A 3 weeks old female infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with respiratory distress. The infant was born at term via spontaneous vaginal delivery to a mother with no prenatal complications. The birth weight was 2.8 kg and the Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes respectively. The infant had meconium-stained amniotic fluid and was intubated immediately after birth due to poor respiratory effort. The chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates consistent with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and echocardiography confirmed the diagnosis of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN). The infant was started on mechanical ventilation and inhaled nitric oxide therapy but did not respond to these treatments. The ECMO team was consulted and the infant was cannulated for veno-arterial ECMO. The infant is now stable on ECMO support but with high ventilator settings. The parents have been approached for emergency consent for their infant to participate in a clinical trial investigating markers of inflammation and lung recovery in ECMO patients for PPHN.

This is a 4-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by a licensed healthcare professional. He has a history of primarily speaking in one-word utterances and struggles to follow complex instructions. The child's primary language is English and he is available for transportation to attend 3, 1-hour sessions per week for 12 weeks. He does not exhibit significant problem behaviors that interfere with structured intervention. The child's parents are interested in helping improve their child's communication skills and are willing to participate in the study to investigate the effects of applied behavior teaching procedures on the emergence of generative language.

This is a 64-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma. She has experienced intense pruritus as a result of obstructive jaundice, and has been suffering from recurrent biliary sepsis and progressive hepatic failure. She has been unable to undergo surgery owing to her advanced age and comorbid illnesses. Her quality of life has been poor, and her prognosis is grave. She has undergone stent insertion both at ERCP and via percutaneous transhepatic routes, but has returned with recurrent cholangitis necessitating frequent stent changes. She has no evidence of metastatic disease, and her serum bilirubin level is currently below 100µmol/L. She has a Karnofsky index of 50%, and is willing to provide written consent for the study. She has not had any previous inserted metallic biliary stents and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was diagnosed with idiopathic nephrotic syndrome 2 years ago. He has been treated with prednisone and has responded well to the treatment. However, he has experienced multiple relapses and has undergone repeated prednisone therapy. He is currently experiencing another relapse and is in need of steroid treatment. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

John is a 28-year-old male who was involved in a motorcycle accident resulting in severe traumatic brain injury. He arrived at the emergency department with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 7 and was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. A CT scan of the head revealed a subdural hematoma and diffuse axonal injury. He underwent surgical evacuation of the hematoma and was transferred to the ICU for further management. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His family members consented for his participation in the clinical trial. His hemodynamic status is stable, with a heart rate of 80 bpm and a mean arterial pressure of 80 mmHg. His initial ICP reading was 18 mmHg.

58 year old male with a history of advanced lung cancer with metastasis to the liver, lymph nodes and brain. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and has been experiencing progression of his disease. Performance status is ECOG 1. Hematopoietic parameters are within normal limits, and liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. Patient did not have any prior allogeneic or autologous bone marrow transplant, and has not received any other investigational therapy in the last 4 weeks. No history of active uncontrolled infection or AIDS-related illness. The patient is willing to use effective contraception as he is fertile and has a partner who is of child-bearing age.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no prior history of cancer or autoimmune disease. The patient is currently experiencing symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and change in bowel habits. Imaging studies have confirmed that he has locally-advanced colorectal cancer. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has not received any prior treatment with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CTLA-4 antibody, or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or immune checkpoint pathways. His MSI-H status has been confirmed by central lab testing. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy and safety of IBI310 in combination with sintilimab for his type of cancer.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis, specifically the homozygous CFTR mutation p.Phe508del. She has been experiencing symptoms related to her gastrointestinal tract, including chronic constipation and abdominal discomfort. She has previously undergone appendicectomy and cholecystectomy surgeries, but has not had any other gastrointestinal tract resections. She has not been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease or coeliac disease, nor does she have any history of gastrointestinal malignancy. She has a Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 60% predicted using Global Lung Initiative criteria, according to clinical records. She is able to understand the requirements of the study and has the capacity to consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from overactive bladder symptoms for the past 5 years. She has tried multiple antimuscarinic agents such as tolterodine, oxybutynin, and solifenacin, but none of them have been effective in managing her symptoms. She has been diagnosed with idiopathic detrusor overactivity (DO) and is considered refractory to conventional anticholinergics. She has no history of bladder outlet obstruction or recurrent urinary tract infections. She is not currently taking any psychoactive agents that may affect bladder function. She has no cognitive impairment and is not currently pregnant. She is not on anticoagulant therapy or aminoglycosides. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril. She has no history of neurological disorders or other medical issues that may interfere with bladder function.

33-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22.5 presents for a food-effect study on lofexidine. She has no significant past medical history and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco products. She reports no current use of prescription or over-the-counter medications or supplements. She is not currently sexually active and agrees to use double barrier contraception if she becomes sexually active during the study. She is willing and able to consume the high-calorie, high-fat breakfast meal provided during the study period. She has normal vital signs, including sitting heart rate of 68 bpm, systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg, and diastolic blood pressure of 70 mmHg. She has no known allergies to lofexidine or related drugs. She is willing and able to remain in the study unit for the entire duration of each confinement period. She has no clinically significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, oncologic, or psychiatric disease or any other condition that would jeopardize her safety or the validity of the study results. She has not experienced any syncopal episodes or seizures in the past. She has not had any acute disease states within the past 7 days. She has not donated blood or plasma within 30 days prior to the first dose of study medication. She has not participated in another clinical trial within the past 30 days. She has not used any prescription medications within the past 14 days or OTC medications, including nutritional supplements, within the past 7 days. She has not used tobacco products within the past 60 days. She has no prior history of substance abuse or treatment. She has a negative pregnancy test result and negative urine screen for drugs of abuse. She has no history of Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, or HIV infection and tests negative for all three at screening. She has no orthostatic hypotension or QTcF prolongation at screening.

A 38-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis who underwent ileal pouch-anal anastomosis. She now presents with relapsing pouchitis that is chronic antibiotic refractory, despite multiple courses of antibiotic therapy. Her symptoms include abdominal pain, diarrhea, and urgency of bowel movements. She has an mPDAI score ≥5 assessed as the average from 3 days immediately prior to the baseline endoscopy visit and a minimum endoscopic subscore of 2. She has had at least three recurrent episodes within the last year, each treated with ≥2 weeks of antibiotic therapy. She has not been treated previously with an anti-IL12/23 or an anti-IL23 antibody, and has not received any investigational or approved biologic agent within 30 days of baseline. She has no active or untreated latent tuberculosis, chronic hepatitis B or C virus infection, or history of human immunodeficiency virus infection. She has no active severe infection or history of malignancy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and receive concomitant antibiotic treatment with ciprofloxacin or metronidazole from baseline through Week 4, and intravenously (IV) ustekinumab ~6mg/kg at baseline and subcutaneously (SC) ustekinumab 90mg every 8 weeks thereafter until Week 48. She is willing to have pouchoscopy with biopsy sampling performed to assess efficacy at Week 16 and Week 48 using mPDAI and PDAI scores.

32 y/o female presents to the clinic with coughing and wheezing for the past 5 days. She reports that she has been feeling fatigued and has had trouble sleeping due to the coughing. She denies any fever, chest pain, shortness of breath, or sputum production. Her medical history is significant for seasonal allergies and occasional asthma attacks, for which she uses an albuterol inhaler. She does not smoke and has no known drug allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria. She has a DCS score of 4 at the screening visit. The HCG test at the screening visit is negative. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not participated in any other clinical trial within the past two months.

A 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and heart failure presents to the emergency department with worsening shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He reports feeling increasingly weak and unable to perform his daily activities. On examination, he is found to have a rapid heart rate, elevated blood pressure, and crackles in his lungs. Laboratory tests reveal hyponatremia and elevated serum creatinine levels, indicating renal dysfunction. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of hypertonic saline solution in heart failure, and is interested in participating in the study to improve his symptoms and prevent further renal damage.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing intermittent pain in the lower abdomen on the right side for the past month. She also reports having difficulty urinating and has noticed blood in her urine. She has no significant medical history, does not take any medications, and has no known drug allergies. She has a family history of kidney stones with her father having experienced them in the past. Upon examination, she is found to have a 2.5 cm stone in her right kidney. Her serum creatinine level is within normal range. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer that is positive for estrogen and progesterone receptors. She has completed all treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation) within the past 6 months. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 and a waist circumference of 38 inches, indicating that she is centrally obese. She has not experienced a weight reduction of 10% or more in the past 6 months and currently participates in less than 60 minutes of structured exercise per week. She speaks English and is in breast cancer remission with no detectable disease present. She is free from chronic diseases including uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid disease. She does not smoke and is willing to travel to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for the study. She is able to initiate a supervised exercise program and understands and is willing to sign the informed consent document.

A 50-year-old female with a BMI of 30.5 and a waist circumference of 38 inches who is generally healthy except for slightly elevated LDL cholesterol levels for the past year. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, or diabetes. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She does not use illicit drugs or medications that may affect cholesterol levels. She has not taken any nutritional supplements that may contain any of the components of the study product for at least 14 days before the screening. She is menopausal and currently not taking any hormone replacement therapy. She has no history of known or suspected substance abuse or psychiatric disorder. She is willing and able to give written informed consent and comply with all study procedures, including maintaining her usual diet and regular activity. She is able to communicate in English and has no difficulty with digestion or absorption of food.

58-year-old male who underwent a liver transplant 5 years ago due to hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient is currently on long-term immunosuppressive therapy, including cyclosporine A and glucocorticoids. The patient has a history of skin cancer, having undergone excision of a squamous cell carcinoma lesion on his left arm 2 years ago. The patient is currently receiving regular follow-up care with a dermatologist for skin checks and management of his skin cancer risk. The patient has provided informed consent for his data to be used in the Swiss Transplant Cohort Study.

A 32-year-old man presents with a left testicular mass that was discovered on self-examination. He has no significant medical history and denies any symptoms. Ultrasound shows a 4.5 cm mass in the lower pole of the left testis with no evidence of metastasis. He undergoes a left radical orchiectomy, which reveals a seminomatous germ cell tumor. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis shows a single retroperitoneal lymph node measuring 3 cm. His serum tumor markers are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would evaluate the efficacy of primary retroperitoneal lymph-node dissection (pRPLND) for his stage II seminomatous germ cell tumor. He is a non-smoker, has no significant past medical history and he is fluent in German.

A 35-year-old African male, who recently tested positive for HIV, is seeking treatment. He resides in an area with a high incidence of tuberculosis (TB) infection. His CD4+ T cell count is 40 cells/mm^3, and he has no symptoms of TB. He has normal liver and kidney function and is negative for hepatitis B surface antigen. He is willing to start antiretroviral therapy (ART) with efavirenz as soon as possible. He has a Karnofsky performance score of 80, is able to swallow medications and is willing to provide informed consent. He is not currently using any prohibited medications and has not received any ARV or combination of ARVs for more than seven days. He has no known allergy or hypersensitivity to the components of study-required ART or TB treatment. He does not have a history of MDR TB or exposure to a household member or co-worker with known MDR TB within the last 12 weeks. He is not actively using drugs or alcohol. He meets the inclusion criteria for the REMEMBER trial and is eligible to participate.

63 year old male patient who was diagnosed with ischemic CVA two months ago and has been receiving medical care since then. The patient is currently experiencing persistent hypertension with a blood pressure reading of 150/92 during the follow-up visit. The patient has agreed to participate in the HIPPOCRATE study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is fluent in French and is affiliated with a social system. The patient has no major cognitive or motor troubles, and no severe concomitant pathology. The patient does not have a cardiac arrhythmia or obesity with a circumference of the arm greater than 33 cm. The patient has a generalist and is willing to attend the follow-up consultation. The patient's estimated creatinine clearance is greater than 30 ml/mn. The patient is eligible for the study and will be invited to participate in the optimised follow-up strategy, which includes the tensional auto-measure, education about hypertension, and multidisciplinary visit for resistant patients.

32F of Middle Eastern descent with a history of Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and Behçet's disease (BD) diagnosed more than a year ago. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, chest pain, joint pain and fever attacks due to inflammation of the serous membranes, as well as oral and genital ulcers, uveitis and skin lesions. The patient has also reported musculoskeletal involvement such as arthralgia, enthesis and sacroiliitis. The patient's condition has caused higher levels of pain, fatigue, depression and anxiety, leading to sleep disturbance and reduced quality of life. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the patient has been experiencing increased stress, anxiety and decreased motivation due to social isolation, home quarantine and restricted movement. The patient is willing to participate in a study to compare pain, sleep, fatigue, physical activity level and quality of life, and question exercise habits before and after the Covid-19 outbreak in patients with FMF and BD. The patient is between the ages of 18-65, has signed the informed consent form, and is cooperative and able to respond to evaluation scales. The patient does not have any other chronic diseases, psychiatric disorders or cognitive impairment.

A 25-year-old male who is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He is not taking any medication and has not donated blood in the last three months. He reports consuming fish less than twice a week and has no plans to travel during the winter of 2006-2007. He has no known chronic diseases or malabsorption syndromes. He is willing to abstain from taking any kind of vitamin, mineral or dietary supplement during the study. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and agrees to have blood samples collected at various intervals throughout the study period. He is a Caucasian and has low habitual fish intake. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial.

57 yo M with advanced metastatic melanoma previously treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy presenting with new areas of progression. Patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and meets inclusion criteria for this phase I trial. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1, with an expected life of at least 3 months. The patient has no severe hematology or cardiopulmonary, liver or kidney diseases, and has a hemoglobin level of 10.3 g/dL, neutrophile granulocyte level of 1.9 x 10^9/L, and blood platelet level of 120 x 10^12/L. The patient has completed chemotherapy of the whole body at least 4 weeks before inclusion, and radiotherapy of the whole body and partial palliative radiotherapy are completed at least 4 weeks before inclusion. The patient is not currently on corticosteroids and has no history of autoimmune disease.

58-year-old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia presented for elective cardiac surgery. He has been on lisinopril, atenolol, and atorvastatin for several years with good control of his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. His family history is notable for coronary artery disease in his father and brother. Physical examination revealed no abnormal findings except mild peripheral edema. Preoperative laboratory studies were within normal limits. His echocardiogram revealed moderate mitral stenosis with mild to moderate regurgitation and mild aortic stenosis. The patient provided informed written consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 60-year-old male with a history of diabetic retinopathy and hypertension presents for a follow-up evaluation at the Kresge Eye Institute. The patient has previously undergone several fluorescein angiography procedures and has experienced mild nausea with the standard dose of fluorescein. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the image quality obtained with a full dose versus a half dose of intravenous fluorescein. The patient has no known major perfusion defects on previous angiograms and does not have significant photophobia or visually significant cataracts. The patient provides informed consent and is randomized to receive either a 250mg or 500mg dose of intravenous fluorescein for their next fluorescein angiography procedure. The patient is looking forward to contributing to research that may improve the safety and efficacy of this commonly used procedure.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently had a maxillary central incisor extracted due to a hopeless prognosis. The patient has a history of smoking but has quit smoking for over a year. The patient has good oral hygiene and has no history of periodontal disease. The patient has no systemic conditions that may influence the outcome of the study and is not currently taking any medications that may affect the gingiva. The patient has no history of radiation therapy in the head and neck area within the last three years or any history of bisphosphonate use. The patient has enough clearance for an implant crown and has sufficient bone apical to the root apex of the hopeless tooth. The patient has no observable gingival changes due to the use of medications such as calcium antagonists, anticonvulsives, immunosuppressives, anti-inflammatory medications, etc. The patient has no untreated deep carious lesions or defective restorations that can potentially exacerbate during the course of the experiment. The patient is interested in participating in the study to achieve the best esthetic outcome after implant placement.

The patient is a 15-month-old toddler who completed their primary immunization series with PCV7 during infancy. They are clinically healthy and have no history of vaccine-related contraindicating events or allergies to vaccine components. The toddler has not previously been immunized against MenC infection. Their parents/legal guardians understand the nature of the study and agree to participate, as well as keeping a Subject Diary. The toddler has not received any blood products or immunoglobulins within 90 days of study entry or planned during the study period. They do not have any serious diseases or dependent relationships with the study investigator or team member. The toddler is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to investigate the safety and immunogenicity of the MenC-TT vaccine when administered concomitantly with a PCV7 booster.

This is a 16-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with primary ovarian insufficiency (POI) after presenting with missed periods and amenorrhea. She has no other chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications that affect bone metabolism. She speaks English fluently and is willing to give informed consent/assent to participate in the study. She will receive transdermal estrogen replacement therapy starting at 25 µg/patch applied weekly, with the dose increased at subsequent study visits that will occur at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. She will undergo bone density and body composition measurement by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry at each visit, along with blood tests to monitor hormone levels and safety assays. She will also undergo cognitive functioning assessment, quality of life assessments, and nutrition and physical activity surveys. She has been matched with a healthy adolescent control participant based on age and race, and will be regularly monitored for 24 months.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer that has spread to his liver. He has no other metastatic sites except for a few small nodules in his lungs. He has never received any chemotherapy before, except for perioperative or adjuvant chemotherapy, which was discontinued more than a year ago. He is in good overall health with a performance status of 1. He has no significant medical history or allergies to medications. He is not taking any prescription medications, but occasionally takes over-the-counter painkillers for mild joint pain. He has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. He drinks alcohol socially, but not excessively. He has a partner and two adult children. He is willing to undergo the required medical monitoring during the trial and is able to provide informed consent.

Maria is a 58-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She underwent chemotherapy and surgery and is currently in remission. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to swallow and retain oral medication. Maria has an HLA type that is eligible for the trial. She is positive for tumor expression of NY-ESO-1 or LAGE-1 by immunohistochemistry (IHC) and/or reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RTPCR). She has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. Maria's lab results show that her ANC is greater than or equal to 1,000/uL, her Platelets (PLT) are greater than or equal to 100,000/uL, and her Hemoglobin (Hgb) is greater than or equal to 8 g/dL.
