Her total bilirubin is less than or equal to 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN), serum aspartate aminotransferase (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase [SGOT]/AST) or serum alanine aminotransferase (serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase [SGPT]/ALT) is less than or equal to 3 x ULN, and her serum creatinine is less than or equal to 2 x ULN. She has been informed of other treatment options and is willing to participate in the trial. Maria has no history of severe autoimmune disorders requiring use of steroids or other immunosuppressives. She is not currently undergoing chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or immunotherapy and has not undergone any of these treatments in the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or nursing, and agrees to use acceptable contraceptive methods during treatment. She is mentally sound and able to give informed consent and comply with the requirements of the study.

As this study is looking for male participants only, we will describe a male patient for this trial. Patient A is a 25-year-old male who works in a manufacturing company that requires prolonged standing work. He has been experiencing occasional low back pain, especially after long hours of standing at work. He is otherwise healthy, has no history of any significant medical conditions or surgeries, and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol occasionally, and exercises regularly. He has a height of 5'9" and weighs 160 pounds. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of the 'Chairless Chair' exoskeleton, which he hopes will help alleviate his low back pain and discomfort caused by prolonged standing work. He is willing to provide informed voluntary consent and comply with all the study procedures.

A 42 year old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of persistent headaches and pain in the neck for the last 2 months. She also reports having difficulty swallowing food and has lost some weight in the last few weeks. She has a history of nasopharyngeal carcinoma and had undergone radiation therapy a year ago. She was recently diagnosed with recurrent and metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and is not suitable for local treatment. The patient has no known allergies and has not undergone chemotherapy or radiotherapy for the last 6 months. Her performance status is 1 (ECOG) and her blood test results show WBC > 4.0X109/L, PLT > 100X109/L, with normal hepatic and renal function. She has no central nervous system metastasis and has no serious concurrent illness. The patient has signed and dated the informed consent form and is willing to comply with trial requirements.

The patient is a 63-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has been scheduled to receive 3 or 4 courses of first-line palliative chemotherapy comprising carboplatin and vinorelbine at Nottingham University Hospital National Health Service Trust. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work, but is unable to perform any strenuous activity. He has no history of cardiac pacemaker implantation, epilepsy or spinal cord pathology. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is able to use neuromuscular electrical stimulation device as required by the study. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese male who has been diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma with positive EBV infection. He has undergone two rounds of platinum-containing chemotherapy with no improvement of his condition. The patient has measurable target lesions according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version (RECIST 1.1). The patient's MHC-I is HLA-A11 subtype, and he is expected to have a survival time of more than 12 weeks. His ECOG score is 1, and he has good bone marrow, kidney, liver, heart, and lung function. He is able to establish the venous access required for the collection and has no contraindications for white blood cell collection. The patient is aware of the trial and has signed an informed consent form. The patient has no symptomatic brain metastasis, other malignant tumors within the past 5 years, or any other uncontrolled active disease that impedes participation in the trial. He is not infected with hepatitis B or C, HIV, or suffering from severe heart and cerebrovascular diseases such as coronary heart disease, angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, arrhythmia, cerebral thrombosis, and cerebral hemorrhage. The patient is not on long-term immunosuppressive agents after organ transplantation and has no medical or mental history that may increase the risk associated with participating in the study or interfere with the interpretation of the results. The target cell transfection rate is above 30%, and T cell expansion is sufficient under CD3/CD28 stimulation conditions. The patient is willing to comply with the research requirements.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with stage IV renal cell cancer. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or biological therapy. He is scheduled to undergo debulking nephrectomy to remove the tumor in his kidney. The tumor is approximately 3cm in size. The patient meets the prognostic criteria for intermediate risk disease as defined by Motzer criteria. He has multiple metastatic lesions in his lungs and liver, with the largest lesion measuring 1.5cm. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has a life expectancy of greater than six weeks. He is not HIV positive and has no history of venous thromboembolism. He has no significant cardiac disease or arrhythmia. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 50 year old male patient with a history of coronary artery disease and hypertension was scheduled for a planned cardiothoracic surgery. During the surgery, mild to moderate bleeding was observed at the target site despite standard conventional surgical hemostatic methods. The patient's coagulation profile was found to be normal. The surgical team has decided to enroll the patient in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of CELSTAT for hemostasis. The patient has no history of renal, neurological, ophthalmological, urological or gynecological surgery, and does not have any congenital coagulation disorder. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. She has been managing her diabetes with oral hypoglycemic medications for the past two years and has a current HbA1c level of 7.2%. Her blood pressure is currently 145/90 mmHg and has been managed with antihypertensive medications for the past year. She has no history of angina, myocardial infarction, or stroke. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient has not used ginseng within the past month and has no known sensitivity or allergy to any test product or placebo ingredients. She is post-menopausal and has normal thyroid, kidney, and liver functions. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and hopes to find a more effective and safe long-term management option for her high blood pressure while managing her type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who recently underwent Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection (ESD) for Early Gastric Cancer. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She does not have any known allergies. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of Ilaprazole 20mg or Rabeprazole 20mg in ulcer healing rate and prevention of gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to attend all required follow-up appointments. She has no history of major surgery that can affect gastric acid secretion, and is not currently taking any medication that would interfere with the study. The patient is able to give informed consent and is willing to sign the Informed Consent Form.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who requires an MRI scan to investigate his recent headaches. He has no significant medical history, and his physical exam is unremarkable. He is not on any medications and has no known allergies. He is anxious about the upcoming MRI and scores 25 on the modified Yale preoperative anxiety scale. He has fasted appropriately and is not taking any antiepileptic medications. He is classified as ASA class I. The boy's parents are willing to accompany him during the MRI scan and post-anesthesia recovery. They have provided consent for their child's participation in the study.

A 52-year-old woman with biopsy-confirmed breast cancer and skin metastases is being considered for this clinical trial. She has measurable skin metastases and distant metastases outside of the skin that can be measured by RECIST. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and is not currently receiving any local therapy. Her organ and bone marrow function are adequate, and she has no history of allergic reactions to imiquimod or its excipients. She is currently on chemotherapy for her metastatic breast cancer, but her distant metastases are non-responsive to the current regimen. She is willing to undergo fine-needle aspiration for tumor assessment and is using a medically acceptable means of contraception.

A 45-year-old male with a family history of sudden cardiac death presents with episodes of palpitation and lightheadedness. He reports no significant medical history, no hypertension, no diabetes, no dyslipidemia, and no substance abuse. Physical examination is unremarkable. The electrocardiogram shows sinus rhythm with occasional ventricular ectopics. The echocardiogram shows normal cardiac function and no structural abnormalities. The patient has been referred to a cardiologist for further evaluation. He meets the inclusion criteria for the VIGILANCE study, as he has unexplained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and a family history of sudden cardiac death. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to travel to the hospital for research purposes. The patient is informed that he will undergo a noninvasive electrocardiographic imaging procedure using 256 electrodes placed on his thorax and a CT scan to obtain the anatomy of his heart and torso. He will also be asked to participate in a National Dutch registry for patients with unexplained polymorphic VT and/or VF and their family members. He does not have any exclusion criteria and is able to provide informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IIIB breast cancer and underwent mastectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy. She completed her primary treatment with curative intent 18 months ago. However, she is experiencing difficulties in managing her health and quality of life due to her cancer history. She has a low level of physical activity, and her diet lacks fruits and vegetables. She is also struggling with posttraumatic growth. She is currently experiencing anxiety and depression and has a feeling of isolation. She is interested in participating in the Health Partnership Program that aims to support cancer patients to cope with exercise, diet, and posttraumatic growth through a tailored program. She is a Korean speaker and reader, able to communicate with Korean. She is willing to participate in the trial and has the ability to understand the study purpose and provide written informed consent. She does not have any secondary cancer or recurrence, and she is not planning to undergo any surgery, radiation therapy, or chemotherapy in the near future. She does not have any major health problems that contraindicate exercise or nutrition intervention. She is not pregnant, has no signs of infection, and does not have thrombocytopenia or anemia. Her SGOT and SGPT levels are within normal range, and her creatinine level is not above 1.2 mg/dL. She does not have any severe psychiatric disorder or suicidal tendencies, and she does not experience dyspnea.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who works in an office and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She is 5'5" tall and weighs 180 pounds, which puts her in the overweight category. She has no major health issues, but her doctor has told her that she needs to lose weight and exercise more to improve her health. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to promote physical activity among overweight persons. She is not currently physically active and has no major contraindications for unsupervised physical activity. She speaks English fluently and is able to read and write. She lives within one hour of the study location and has reliable transportation. She is willing to participate in the study for the duration of the study period.

A 54-year-old man suffered from chest pain and shortness of breath while doing his daily activities. He was taken to the emergency room and was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He was referred for primary PCI within 12 hours of symptom onset. He is compliant with his medications, which include aspirin and statins. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no other significant medical history. He does not smoke and he does not drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the best antiplatelet therapy for patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI.

A 54-year-old man who had a kidney transplant 4 years ago is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. He was previously enrolled in the CTOT-05 study and is willing to participate in this retrospective study. His past medical history is significant for end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension and diabetes. He received a deceased donor kidney transplant 4 years ago and has been taking immunosuppressive medications since then. He has had no episodes of acute rejection and his graft function has been stable throughout this period. His current medications include tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. He has no history of malignancy or chronic infections. He is compliant with his medications and has been following up with his transplant team regularly. He is willing to provide consent for this study and is available for follow-up visits.

A 54-year-old male with newly diagnosed glioblastoma multiforme underwent tumor resection. He has not received any systemic therapies, radiation, tumor-treating fields, or intratumoral therapeutic agents. His tumor tissue tested positive for EGFRvIII expression and negative for MGMT promoter methylation. He is in otherwise good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no history of autoimmune diseases, interstitial lung disease, or pneumonitis. He has not undergone allogenic bone marrow or solid organ transplant. He does not have active Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection, or any other active, uncontrolled infection. He has adequate organ function and provides written informed consent. He is willing to use acceptable birth control methods. He does not have tumors primarily localized to the brain stem or spinal cord.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, ophthalmological, or hormonal disorders. He has never been diagnosed with any diseases of the central nervous system or psychiatric disorders. He has a resting heart rate of 65 bpm and has not experienced any relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. He does not have any chronic or acute infections and has no history of allergies or drug hypersensitivity. He has not taken any long half-life drugs in the last month or less than 10 half-lives of the respective drug prior to administration. He is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 60 g of alcohol per day. He does not abuse drugs, has not donated blood within the last four weeks, and has not engaged in excessive physical activities within the last week. All laboratory values are within the reference range and of no clinical relevance. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. After completion of the treatment, she was started on an aromatase inhibitor but experienced disease progression. She is currently experiencing bone pain and fatigue, and a bone scan revealed multiple bone metastases. Her hormone receptor status is estrogen receptor-positive and progesterone receptor-negative. She has no neurological symptoms and is not receiving corticosteroid treatment for any reason. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her blood counts, liver enzymes, and kidney function are within normal limits. She has no significant medical history except for hypertension controlled with medication. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She is able to swallow and retain oral medication.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with end-stage renal disease who has been on haemodialysis for the past year. He has a history of chronic uremic pruritus that has been present for more than 8 weeks and has a severity score of 8 on the visual analogue scale. Despite using oral antihistamines and skin moisturizers, he has not experienced any relief from the pruritus. He has not taken any medication with presumed antipruritic effects in the past week. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and comply with the study requirements. He has no known allergies to Pregabalin and does not have liver cirrhosis or any active dermatological disorder other than UP. He does not have decompensated heart failure or any acute illness.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with lymphoma 7 years ago and has been in remission for the past 5 years. She is currently not on any active anti-cancer therapies and has access to a smartphone or computer with internet access. She has been recently diagnosed with hypertension and is taking medication for it. She is not physically active and has a sedentary lifestyle. She is a non-smoker and is willing to provide informed consent. She is interested in participating in the SmART Heart clinical trial to learn how to manage her heart health and reduce her risk of future heart disease.

65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and atherosclerotic peripheral artery disease. Patient presents with symptoms of moderate to severe intermittent claudication with the ability to walk at least 2, but not more than 11 minutes on a graded treadmill test using the Gardner protocol. The patient is currently on a stable dose of atorvastatin 20 mg for the past 6 weeks. The patient has a femoral popliteal artery with 50% stenosis by ultrasound. The patient has no history of critical limb ischemia or any other comorbid conditions that limit walking ability. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent. The patient does not have any active systemic inflammatory disease or infectious disease within the past month, no systemic disorders such as hepatic, renal, hematologic, and malignant disease. The patient is not allergic to contrast media with iodine or DVDMS, and does not have a diagnosis of porphyria. The patient is not pregnant nor nursing, and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials.

A 60-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the left upper lobe. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He underwent pulmonary function testing (PFT) and was deemed suitable for 3-dimensional conformal radiation therapy (3DCRT) or intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) or image-guided radiation therapy (IGRT). He has been scheduled for simulation, and he will be enrolled in a prospective study to record his breath holding times at various phases of respiration during the course of radiotherapy, including the effect of respiratory training. During the study, he will be asked to perform deep breathing exercises/spirometer ball exercises to improve his breath holding times. The patient will be counseled about respiratory training and provided with a spiroball device to use at home. He will have regular visits to the physiotherapy department to reinforce respiratory training, and objective recordings of his spirometer ball (whenever used) will be recorded. The patient will be asked to perform three different types of breath holds, including deep inspiratory breath hold, deep expiratory breath hold, and normal mid-ventilation breath hold. The study will help determine the optimal time to perform radiation therapy during breath holding and the effect of respiratory training on breath holding times. The patient will be monitored closely throughout the study to ensure that he tolerates radical RT.

This is a 32 year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for 8 years, who has been suffering from persistent auditory hallucinations despite being treated with different antipsychotic medications for the past 2 years. The hallucinations are distressing and persecutory in nature, and have led to social withdrawal, anxiety and depression. The patient has not responded to previous CBT treatments for his hallucinations. He has no history of substance abuse or neurological disorders. The patient is currently taking a stable dose of medication and has been compliant with his treatment for the last 2 months prior to enrollment in the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman with a history of mandibular prognathism and maxillary hypoplasia. She has been experiencing difficulty with chewing, biting, and speaking which has affected her confidence and social life. She is currently working as a marketing executive and has a sedentary lifestyle. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not on any medications. She has never undergone any surgery before. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her chances of a successful orthognathic surgery and to reduce the risk of long-term neurosensory disturbance. She understands that the trial involves taking oral Melatonin supplements before and after surgery to potentially improve her neurosensory recovery. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up appointments. She is excited about the possibility of better facial sensation and restoring her confidence after the surgery.

A 58-year-old male presents with abdominal discomfort, weight loss, and fatigue for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but otherwise has been healthy. He has not undergone any previous surgeries or radiation therapy. His family history is negative for cancer. A colonoscopy was performed, revealing a mass in the sigmoid colon. Biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed metastases to the liver and peritoneum. He underwent a partial colectomy with pathology confirming stage IV colorectal cancer. He was started on FOLFIRI (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, and irinotecan) chemotherapy but had progressive disease after 3 months of treatment. A repeat CT scan showed progression of liver and peritoneal metastases. He was offered participation in a clinical trial investigating the combination of regorafenib and pembrolizumab for the treatment of advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer. The patient provided written informed consent and met all eligibility criteria for the trial.

45 year-old woman with a history of fibromyalgia for the past 5 years. She reports constant pain and stiffness in her neck, shoulders, and back, as well as frequent headaches and fatigue. She has tried multiple medications in the past, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and muscle relaxants, but has not found significant relief. She is currently not taking any medications for fibromyalgia. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new controlled release formulation of pregabalin, as she hopes it will provide better pain relief with fewer side effects. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and understands that she may receive a placebo at some point during the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old transgender woman who identifies as bisexual. She has been smoking cigarettes daily for the past 5 years and has attempted to quit multiple times without success. She reports feeling depressed and anxious at times, and occasionally turns to cigarettes as a way to cope with stress. She is interested in participating in a study that could provide her with support and resources to quit smoking. She has access to a computer and a valid email address. She is motivated to make a change and is willing to commit to the study's requirements.

42-year-old male with a history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy diagnosed 6 years ago after experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath during exercise. The patient has been managed with beta-blockers and regular cardiac monitoring, but has recently reported increased fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance. On echocardiography, the patient has asymmetric septal hypertrophy with a maximal wall thickness of 20mm and no evidence of severe valvular disease or prior myocardial infarction. The patient has no history of atrial fibrillation. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the potential correlations between myocardial deformation parameters and the severity of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, as well as the risk for arrhythmias.

A 45-year-old female with a history of severe allergic reactions to blood transfusions due to incompatible red blood cells was referred to the clinic. She has a rare blood type and has experienced severe anemia due to heavy menstrual bleeding. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and no other significant medical history. She is fully informed about the trial and willing to participate. Her hemoglobin level is currently 5.8 g/dL, and she is experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue. She has signed the informed consent form and is ready to receive treatment with HBOC-201.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with early stage breast cancer during a routine mammogram. The cancer is invasive and has not spread to the lymph nodes or other parts of the body. The tumor is small, measuring less than 3.5 cm, and the woman is considered a good candidate for breast conserving surgery. She has not had any previous radiation to the affected breast and has not received neoadjuvant treatment. She does not have a BRCA1/2 gene mutation. The woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy and toxicity of intra-operative radiation therapy (IORT) as a single fraction after breast conserving surgery. She understands that this is a registry trial and is willing to have her outcomes followed for local and regional control, toxicity, and morbidity.

A 56-year-old male presented to the emergency department with sudden onset left-sided weakness and slurred speech. He arrived at the hospital within 3 hours of symptom onset. His past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of smoking. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no known drug allergies. Upon arrival, he was assessed by the emergency department physician and underwent a non-contrast CT scan of the head which showed a right middle cerebral artery infarct. He is conscious and able to follow commands but has significant left-sided weakness and a facial droop. No other significant neurological deficits were observed. His vital signs were stable, and his laboratory tests were within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his informed consent to participate.

A 28-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital is interested in participating in the study. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or current medications. Her BMI is 22 kg/m2, and she has no history of smoking or alcohol/drug abuse. She is currently using hormonal contraception and has a normal Tuberculosis test and Electrocardiogram (ECG). She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months and has never received certolizumab pegol. She is willing to comply with all the study requirements and has given informed consent.

45 yo F with a history of carpal tunnel syndrome on the right hand, scheduled for elective surgery. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies to local anesthetics. Her BMI is 26, and she is not taking any antiarrhythmic or adrenergic medications. She has no known history of hepatic and renal insufficiency, chronic pain, or neuromuscular disorders. The patient does not have a language barrier or cognitive or psychiatric disorder. She has not experienced postural hypotension or autonomic dysfunction in the past. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy male or female aged between 18 and 65 with a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 31.0 kilogram/square meter (kg/m^2) and body weight between >=36kilogram (kg) and <=100kg. The patient has no history of liver disease, regular alcohol consumption, sensitivity to heparin, or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. They have not participated in any clinical trials and have not been exposed to more than four new chemical entities within the past 12 months. The patient has normal blood pressure, heart rate, and no history of blood donation in excess of 500 mL within a 56-day period. They have not consumed Seville oranges, grapefruit or grapefruit juice and/or pummelos, exotic citrus fruits, or grapefruit hybrids from 7 days prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient has no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications, or components thereof or a history of drug or other allergy that contraindicates their participation. They have not used prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements within 7 days (or 14 days if the drug is a potential enzyme inducer) or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient has normal haemoglobin values and no phenotypic Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, determined by a quantitative assay of enzyme activity. They have normal potassium and magnesium levels, and cotinine levels indicative of non-smoking or non-regular use of tobacco- or nicotine-containing products within 30 days prior to screening. The patient has a negative pre-study Hepatitis B surface antigen and negative Hepatitis C antibody result within 3 months of screening, and a negative pre-study drug/alcohol screen.

The patient is a 3-week-old full-term male neonate who was diagnosed with a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. He is scheduled to undergo thoracoscopic surgery to repair the hernia. The patient has no other medical history, and his parents report no significant family history of medical conditions. He was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery with no complications and has been exclusively breastfed since birth. He has had no issues with feeding, and his weight gain has been appropriate for his age. The patient's physical examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no apparent abnormalities. The parents have consented to participate in the study and have been advised of the necessary fasting hours before the surgery. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, with a body weight of 3000 gm.

55F with a history of osteoarthritis of the right hip presents for elective total hip replacement surgery. Patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking Lisinopril. Physical exam reveals no significant abnormalities. Patient has no known allergies. Patient has been cleared for surgery by her primary care physician and is able to provide informed consent. Surgery is scheduled to begin at 11:00 AM. The patient has been advised that she will receive either general anesthesia or regional anesthesia for this procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with advanced stage ovarian cancer. She has been receiving palliative care for the past 6 months due to the progression of her disease. She experiences constant pain and discomfort, which has greatly affected her quality of life. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been struggling to find ways to cope with her illness. She has always had an interest in art and has dabbled in painting and drawing in the past. She is interested in participating in an art therapy program to help her cope with her illness and improve her overall well-being. She is fully aware of her condition and has given informed consent to participate in the study. She has normal cognitive function and is physically able to participate in the art therapy process.

A 25 year old male with a history of seasonal allergies to grass pollen and year-round allergies to house dust mites. He experiences symptoms of allergic rhino-conjunctivitis and asthma, which often require the use of medication. He has not received any immunotherapy treatment before. He is interested in participating in this study to assess the effect of subcutaneous allergen-specific immunotherapy on his allergic symptoms and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 12-year-old female who was brought to the hospital emergency department with a sore throat, fever, and difficulty swallowing. Her past medical history is not significant for any chronic illness or recent hospitalizations. Upon examination, the patient's tonsils are enlarged and inflamed, and there is tenderness in her neck. A throat swab was collected in Liquid Amies based transport medium for Group A Strep testing. The patient and her legal guardian provided informed consent and assent for extra research samples. The patient has not undergone antibiotic treatment yet. The specimen volume collected is more than 850 µL and is received in good condition. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35 year old male who works as a construction worker. He has a past medical history of a concussion from falling off a ladder at work about 10 months ago. Since then, he has been experiencing headaches, dizziness, difficulty concentrating, and trouble sleeping. He has tried various medications and therapies, but none have provided significant relief. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married with two children and is the main provider for his family. He is interested in participating in the study to see if Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy can help improve his symptoms and allow him to return to work and provide for his family without the constant burden of his post concussive syndrome symptoms.

A 30-year-old woman noticed redness, swelling, and discharge in her left eye for the past 2 days. She has no history of eye problems and wears contact lenses occasionally. She denies any recent eye trauma or exposure to irritants. She does not have any known allergies or medical conditions. She has not used any eye drops or antibiotics for this condition. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat her bacterial conjunctivitis.

Pt is a 28yo MSM with a history of HIV infection, currently receiving regular HIV care for the past 6 months. The patient has had no history of active infection or malignancy within the past 12 months and is not receiving chemotherapy, immunosuppressant, or IVIG within the past 12 months. The patient has not received HBV vaccination within the past 1 month and is not allergic to HBV vaccine. The patient has not received any other vaccination within the past 1 month, such as influenza, pneumococcus, HPV, HAV, varicella vaccine. The patient has a birth date after 1986/7/1, is aged 20 years or older, and is seronegative for HBsAg, anti-HBs (<10 mIU/ml), and anti-HBc at screening (within 1 month of the first dose). The patient is seeking VCT for at least once for HIV-negative patients over the past 12 months. The patient does not have stage 4 and 5 of chronic kidney disease (GFR<30 mL/min/1.73m) or receive dialysis.

A 45-year-old man, who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, presents to the emergency room with complaints of increased thirst and frequent urination for the last 3 weeks. He has no significant past medical history and denies any family history of diabetes. His vitals are stable, and his physical exam is unremarkable except for dry mucous membranes. His lab work shows an HbA1c of 8.5%, with a fasting blood glucose level of 200 mg/dL. He is informed of his diagnosis and given the option to participate in a clinical trial testing a bicycle exercise followed by an intensive lifestyle intervention for 3 months. He agrees to participate and signs the informed consent document. He is randomized to the intervention group and is instructed to perform 30 minutes of bicycle exercise at 60% of his calculated maximum heart rate, followed by an intensive lifestyle intervention, on top of non-pharmacological standard care. He is discharged the same day after rehydration, and follow-up visits are scheduled at the Clinic of Endocrinology for further instructions and consultation. He is motivated to make lifestyle changes and is willing to engage in weekly motivational coaching via telephone by the study psychologist.

26 year old pregnant woman in her first trimester, residing in Shenyang, China with no history of neuropsychiatric disorders. She is planning to receive prenatal care and give birth at Shengjing Hospital. This is her first pregnancy and she is excited to participate in the CMUBCS to contribute to research on the interplay between genes and environmental factors on disease etiology in children. She is willing to provide lifestyle data and clinical data at different stages of her pregnancy and her child's development, as well as biological samples including blood and tissue samples.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic constipation for over a year. He has tried various laxatives and dietary changes, but none have provided long-term relief. He typically has two or fewer bowel movements per week and often feels a sensation of incomplete evacuation. He has not undergone any surgeries related to his constipation and does not have any known anorectal malformations, colorectal or anal organic lesions, or pelvic floor disorders. He is not currently taking any laxatives but may need to take up to 15 mg of bisacodyl as a rescue medication during the trial. He understands and speaks French fluently and is willing to participate in the study. He has signed the informed consent form and is affiliated with a social security system. He does not have any implanted electronic devices or skin lesions that would prevent the installation of electrodes. He is not participating in any other biomedical research protocols.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of perianal fistula. He has undergone one surgery in the past for this condition but has experienced recurrence of the fistula. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or rectovaginal fistula. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has no active or latent infection by HIV, HBV or HCV. He is not currently receiving immunomodulatory treatment for any other reason. The patient has no history of malignant tumors, except for basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, and has not had a tumor in remission within the past 5 years. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics or Gadolinium (MRI contrast agent). The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his signed, written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has no history of allergies and takes daily vitamins. She lives with her husband and two teenage children. She works as an accountant in a private firm. She has started oral capecitabine chemotherapy as an adjuvant treatment after completing her surgery and radiation therapy. She has been experiencing mild to moderate nausea and diarrhea since starting the medication. She has no difficulty with swallowing or any other adverse effects. Her performance status is ECOG 1. She speaks and understands Malay and English languages fluently. She has given written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital due to shortness of breath and fever. He has a history of hypertension, but otherwise, his medical history is unremarkable. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker and has been in good health until now. Upon admission, a chest X-ray showed a new infiltrate, and he was diagnosed with nosocomial pneumonia. He has been hospitalized for three days and has been on oxygen therapy. His vital signs are stable, and he has no other signs of systemic infection. His serum pregnancy test is negative. He is not on dialysis, and his estimated creatinine clearance is above 16ml/min by Cockcroft Gault formula. He has no known pulmonary disease that would preclude evaluation of therapeutic response. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a newborn infant, born at 32 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1.8 kg. The infant was delivered by C-section due to maternal preeclampsia. The baby boy was admitted to the NICU for respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and was treated with surfactant therapy and mechanical ventilation. He has been on continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) for the past 3 days and is gradually weaning off. The infant has no known genetic or chromosomal abnormalities and is not suspected to have any muscular dystrophy or neurological disorders. He has not had any respiratory infections during his NICU stay. His urine and blood samples have been collected for routine laboratory tests and are within normal limits. He is currently on total parenteral nutrition (TPN) and is tolerating feeds well. His oxygen saturation levels have been stable on room air for the past 12 hours. He has been monitored closely by the NICU team and is making steady progress. The parents have given their consent for the infant to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, which revealed micrometastases in one lymph node. She did not receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she is not pregnant or nursing. She has no active infections and no history of invasive cancer within the past 5 years. She is planning to undergo adjuvant whole breast irradiation including the low axilla. She is willing and able to complete questionnaires alone or with assistance.

The patient is a 26 year old woman who is currently pregnant and in her second trimester (between 24 and 28 weeks gestational age). She has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions prior to her pregnancy and does not have a family history of diabetes, hypertension, or other chronic illnesses. She has been receiving regular prenatal care and has had no complications thus far. She has no history of multiple gestations or any known congenital malformations. She is willing to have her blood drawn between 24w0d and 28w6d weeks gestational age for the purpose of this study.

The patient is a full-term newborn who was born via vaginal delivery. The mother experienced meconium-stained amniotic fluid during the delivery, and the baby was immediately suctioned after birth. However, the baby developed respiratory distress, and a chest X-ray showed evidence of meconium aspiration syndrome. The baby is currently receiving synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV) and is eligible for the clinical trial. The baby does not have any history of congenital or hereditary diseases.

A 38 year old woman struggling to conceive for the past 2 years comes to the clinic seeking help. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has undergone fertility treatment in the past with poor response. Her BMI is 27 kg/m2 and she has no chronic medical conditions. Upon evaluation, she is diagnosed with poor ovarian reserve (POR) according to the ESHRE Bologna criteria, with an antral follicle count of 4 follicles and AMH level of 0.8 ng/mL. She has previously undergone two episodes of POR with maximal stimulation of 300 IU. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has given written informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old active male who has been diagnosed with a rotator cuff tear. The tear is degenerative and partial, greater than 50% thickness and less than 3 cm in length. MRI tear classification is Patté's I or II in coronal view, Goutalier's less than 2, Fukuda's less than 2, and Seebauer's 1A maximum. The patient has not undergone any surgical procedures on the affected shoulder before and has not received two or more glucocorticoid injections in the last year. The patient is in good health and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of early versus delayed postoperative mobilization after arthroscopic rotator cuff tear repair. The patient is hoping to return to their previous level of activity as soon as possible and is willing to follow the prescribed rehabilitation program to achieve the best possible outcome.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently experienced occasional episodes of palpitations and shortness of breath. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the accuracy of a watch for detecting atrial fibrillation. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she has no issues with expressing consent. She is affiliated with a social security system and is physically capable of wearing a watch on her wrist. She has not undergone any electrical stimulation by pacemaker. She is willing to sign the informed consent form and participate in the study.

A 3-year-old Gabonese boy named Jean has been selected for this clinical trial. He lives in a rural area with his parents and two siblings. His family has a history of malaria, and Jean has had the disease twice in the past year. He is otherwise healthy, and his immunizations are up to date. His parents have given written consent for him to participate in the study and are committed to bringing him to all follow-up appointments. Jean is not currently experiencing any acute illness, and his laboratory screening tests are within normal ranges. He has never participated in a malaria vaccine trial before and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder ICD-10 F31.2 six months ago. She has a past medical history of depression and anxiety, for which she has been taking escitalopram and clonazepam respectively for the past 2 years. She has a family history of bipolar disorder, with her father and aunt both diagnosed with the same condition. The patient has been experiencing manic episodes with grandiosity, hyperactivity, and decreased need for sleep. She has also experienced depressive episodes with feelings of hopelessness, sadness, and suicidal ideation. The patient has been compliant with her medication regimen and has not experienced any adverse effects. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and there are no abnormalities noted on physical examination. Her medical records show no evidence of other medical conditions or substance abuse. She has a history of smoking, but she has quit for the past 6 months. The patient has been under the care of a psychiatrist and has been receiving regular therapy sessions.

A 57-year-old woman presented with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She also reported unintentional weight loss and fatigue. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no history of cancer. She did not smoke or consume alcohol. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the pancreas, and a biopsy confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). She underwent surgical resection of the tumor and surrounding tissue. Pathology reports confirmed the diagnosis of PDAC. The patient was approached for participation in a clinical trial investigating the genetic mutations associated with pancreatic cancer. She agreed to participate and provided informed consent. Her tissue samples were genotyped for the three most common founder mutations in Ashkenazi Jews, and it was found that she carried a BRCA1 mutation. Heterozygote normal and abnormal tissue were microdissected to look for loss of heterozygosity at the BRCA1 allele. She was included in the study as she met the inclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, fever, and cough. She has a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been a smoker for 20 years, smoking a pack of cigarettes per day. She has not been vaccinated for COVID-19. Her oxygen saturation was 88% on admission, and a chest X-ray revealed bilateral infiltrates. She was diagnosed with moderate to severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and was started on mechanical ventilation with low tidal volume and high PEEP. A repeat arterial blood gas showed a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of 95 mmHg. She is receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics and intravenous steroids. She has no known allergies. Her vital signs are stable, and she is alert and oriented. She has consented to participate in the study and meets all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a medical history of type 2 diabetes and coronary artery disease. He has previously undergone a percutaneous coronary intervention and is currently taking statins for cholesterol control. His most recent LDL cholesterol level was 110 mg/dL despite the use of statins. His HbA1c is 7.5%, and he is being treated with metformin and a sulfonylurea. He has no history of triglyceride levels greater than 400 mg/dL, renal dysfunction, or current use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. He has not been diagnosed with any other conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and understands the potential benefits and risks.

A 26-year-old Chinese male who is in good health and has a BMI within the range of 18.5 to 28.0 kg/m2. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He does not have any gastrointestinal diseases that may affect the absorption of the study drug, and he does not have a history of drug abuse. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effect of food on the pharmacokinetic profile of BPI-7711.

The patient is an 82-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with aortic stenosis and requires surgical intervention. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She lives independently but has some difficulty with mobility due to arthritis. She takes medications for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia, including amlodipine and atorvastatin. She has undergone previous surgeries including a hip replacement and a hysterectomy. She has been informed about the study and has given written informed consent to participate. She will be undergoing elective surgery and will be monitored for post-interventional mortality until day 30.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a candidate CHIKV vaccine. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He lives in Oxford, England and has not traveled to any CHIKV endemic regions. He does not have any bleeding disorders or history of significant bleeding or bruising following injections or venepuncture. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and is able to provide written informed consent. Additionally, he is willing to allow the investigators to discuss his medical history with his General Practitioner. He agrees to refrain from blood donation during the course of the study and is willing to practice continuous effective contraception if he is female.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic genotype 1 HCV infection for the past 8 months. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past year. He is currently working as a carpenter and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and fishing. He is married and has two children. His liver biopsy shows mild to moderate fibrosis. His HCV viral load is 2.5 million IU/mL. He has never received any prior HCV treatment. He does not have any significant medical history or chronic medical conditions. His neurological exam is normal, and he has no history of epilepsy or cerebral vascular accidents. He is willing to use a protocol-specified method of contraception during the study period as his wife is of childbearing potential. He is interested in participating in the trial to potentially improve his HCV infection and overall health.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who attends a mainstream primary school and has been diagnosed with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders V (DSM-5). He scored below the 5th percentile on the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2 (MABC-2) and scored a total score below 55 on the DCD questionnaire 2007 (Chinese version). He does not have any known significant congenital, cognitive, psychiatric, neurological, sensory, musculoskeletal, or cardiopulmonary disorder that may affect motor performance. He is not receiving active treatment such as physiotherapy. The patient may have comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but this is not a disqualifying factor. The patient is able to follow instructions properly and does not demonstrate excessive disruptive behavior during the assessments.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who has been diagnosed with positive cytomegalovirus and is scheduled to undergo a donor stem cell transplant. The patient has no history of allergies or underlying medical conditions that may affect the study. The patient is willing to comply with study and follow-up procedures and has a guardian who is willing to sign a written informed consent. The patient has a 10/10 high/intermediate resolution HLA donor allele match and is seronegative for HIV and HCV. The patient has not received any investigational CMV vaccine or anti-CMV therapy in the last 6 months. The patient has not received any live attenuated vaccines, allergy treatment with antigen injections, or immunosuppressive therapy with alemtuzumab, cyclophosphamide, or ATG. The patient is not currently taking any antiviral medications with known therapeutic effects on CMV such as GCV/VAL, FOS, Cidofovir, CMX-001, or maribavir. The patient is not receiving prophylactic therapy with CMV immunoglobulin or prophylactic antiviral CMV treatment. The patient is not enrolled in any other clinical trials using investigational new drug (IND) drugs with unknown effects on CMV or with unknown toxicity profiles. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and the patient's guardian agrees to use effective contraception prior to and for up to 90 days post-HCT.

35-year-old male with a history of recreational gambling presents with concerns about his gambling behavior. He reports spending several hours each week gambling online, often resulting in significant financial losses. He has attempted to cut down on his gambling, but finds it difficult to resist the urge to gamble when stressed. He scores 8 on the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) and expresses a desire to reduce his gambling behavior or quit altogether. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of an online gambling intervention and agrees to complete a 6-week and 6-month follow-up survey.

A 32-year-old female patient presents to the psychiatry clinic with a history of bipolar disorder. She has been experiencing a major depressive episode for the past 8 weeks, characterized by feelings of sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest, and energy. The patient has a past history of manic episodes, but none in the last 6 months. She is currently taking lithium carbonate and has been stable on this medication for the past 6 months. The patient is an outpatient and is willing to provide written informed consent. She has no other Axis I disorder within the past 6 months and her current episode of depression does not exceed 12 months or is less than 4 weeks.

52 year old M with a history of hypertension and anxiety, scheduled for an elective hip replacement surgery. Patient has had previous surgeries under anaesthesia without any complications. Patient expresses concerns about the process of obtaining informed consent for anaesthesia and how it may impact their overall experience. Patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. No legal guardians appointed.

10-year-old male with a history of recurrent respiratory infections, chronic cough, and nasal congestion since infancy. He was diagnosed with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) at the age of 5 years old. He is currently on standard medications for PCD including inhaled hypertonic saline, inhaled bronchodilators, and prophylactic antibiotics. He reports experiencing exercise intolerance and shortness of breath with physical activity. His parents note that he is less active than his peers and often tires easily during play. He has no cognitive or neurological disorders, and no orthopedic issues that would prevent him from participating in physical activities. He has not had any acute infections or pneumonia in the past 3 months and is otherwise stable. The patient has no visual problems that would interfere with the evaluations.

A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman presents to the clinic complaining of vaginal dryness and pain during intercourse. She has not had a period in over 2 years and was not using any hormonal therapy or vaginal lubricants. She reports experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and they have been progressively worsening. She has no history of abnormal genital bleeding, hypertension or endometrial hyperplasia. She has never been diagnosed with any vaginal infections, sexually transmitted diseases or gynecological malignancies. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no family history of breast or ovarian cancer. Her physical exam is significant for vaginal dryness, pallor and thinning of the vaginal walls. Her vaginal pH is above 5 and vaginal smear shows low maturation index. She is willing to participate in the study and sign an informed consent. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

47 year old female diagnosed with stage II breast cancer initiating first line adjuvant therapy with paclitaxel. No history of neuropathy or lower extremity amputation. No preexisting musculoskeletal conditions affecting gait or balance. No prior exposure to taxane or other chemotherapy or targeted therapy associated with neuropathy. No current use of neuropathic pain medications. Able to walk and stand without assistance. Willing to provide informed consent for study participation.

The patient is a 25-year-old, healthy female who weighs 60 kg and has a BMI of 21. She is a non-smoker and has not used any recreational drugs in the past 3 months. She is fluent in English and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of any cardiovascular, hematological, renal, hepatic, pulmonary, endocrine, gastrointestinal, immunological, dermatological, neurological, or psychiatric disease. She has not undergone any significant surgery within the past 4 weeks and has not had any upper respiratory tract infection within the past 2 weeks. She has not had any history of GERD, heartburn, or nausea requiring the regular use of antacids or any use of H2 histamine blockers or proton pump inhibitors within the past 12 months. She has no history of Helicobacter pylori infection and her QTcB is within the normal range. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has a negative pregnancy test. She has not donated blood or plasma recently and has not used any systemic medications within 30 days before the first dose of the study medication. She has not ingested grapefruit or grapefruit juice within 48 hours before dose administration. She has not received any investigational product or device, or participated in a drug research study within 30 days before the first dose of study medication. She meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old woman who works as an office assistant has been diagnosed as sedentary by her family physician due to her lifestyle. She spends most of her day sitting at a desk and has been struggling to find the motivation to exercise regularly. She has a BMI of 31 and is concerned about her health, especially since her father has a history of heart disease. She is currently not on any medications and has no significant past medical history. She is married and has two children. She is interested in participating in the functional training program and learning more about nutrition counseling. She does not have any physical or mental disabilities and is not pregnant. She is looking forward to incorporating exercise into her daily routine to improve her health and overall quality of life.

Maria is a 24-year-old woman who is in good health and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and is not currently taking any medications. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses oral contraceptives. Her vital signs, electrocardiogram and laboratory tests at screening are all normal. Maria has no known allergy to propofol or any components of either formulation. She has no family history of malignant hyperthermia. She has a BMI of 22.3 and has no difficulty with venous access. Maria is interested in participating in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m2. She has no significant underlying illnesses, but has a family history of diabetes. She has never smoked and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. Her fasting blood glucose levels are within normal limits and her blood pressure is below 130/90. She is interested in participating in a study examining the effects of hesperidin on insulin sensitivity. She is willing to take either hesperidin or a placebo for the 4-week treatment phase and is able to comply with the study procedures, including dietary and physical activity questionnaires, blood and urine tests, at-home and clinic blood pressure monitoring, and the glucose clamp test. She is able to give informed consent for all procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with a fever of 39°C, cough, and shortness of breath. She reports feeling unwell for the past 3 days and her symptoms have progressively worsened. She has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies. She denies any recent travel, exposure to sick contacts, or recent hospitalizations. Upon examination, her respiratory rate is elevated, and she has wheezing and crackles in her lungs. The treating physician suspects a lower respiratory tract infection and orders a nasopharyngeal swab for the FilmArray respiratory panel assay plus a blood sample for the PCT assay. The patient consents to participate in the study. The results of the FilmArray® RP2plus are reported in real-time to the treating physician, indicating the presence of a viral respiratory pathogen. The PCT result is also reported in real-time, showing a value of <0.10 µg/L. Based on this collective data, the physician decides to withhold antibiotics and provide supportive care to the patient.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman came to the clinic for her routine prenatal check-up. She is currently 18 weeks pregnant with her first child. She reports feeling extremely tired and fatigued lately, and has noticed that she has been short of breath more often than usual. She has a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and reports irregular periods. She has never been diagnosed with anemia before. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Her family history is significant for anemia in her mother. Her baseline hemoglobin (Hb) level is 10.5 g/dL, and her ferritin level is 15 ng/mL, indicating iron deficiency anemia. She is eligible for the clinical trial and is willing to participate.

A 62-year-old man with a history of osteoarthritis in his knee joint has been experiencing chronic knee pain and limited mobility for the past two years. He has previously tried non-surgical treatment options such as physiotherapy and pain medications, but with no significant relief. He is married, retired, and lives with his wife. He does not have any history of smoking or alcohol use. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications currently. He exercises regularly to maintain his overall health and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the TruMatch® System for knee prosthetic surgery. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent.

A 62-year-old male retiree who resides in the United States has been experiencing insomnia symptoms for over 3 months. He reports difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep, with a sleep onset latency (SOL) and/or wake after sleep onset (WASO) greater than 30 minutes for at least 3 nights per week. He typically sleeps for no more than 6.5 hours per night and feels fatigued throughout the day. These symptoms have been causing significant distress and affecting his social and occupational functioning. He has a regular access to a computer and the internet and is willing to use them for the study purposes. He can read and speak English fluently. He has no history of psychological or psychiatric treatment for insomnia and has not initiated such treatment within the past 3 months. He does not have a history of psychotic or bipolar disorder or current severe depression, high risk of suicide, or substance use disorder within the past year. He does not have any symptoms suggestive of untreated sleep disorders other than insomnia (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, periodic limb movement disorder). He is not suffering from severe cognitive impairment or any uncontrolled medical condition that is deemed to interfere with the study procedures or put him at undue risk.

A 52-year-old male patient was diagnosed with primary hypercholesterolemia and had previously participated in the 12-week double-blind, efficacy and safety parent study (P00692) which he successfully completed. He is willing to follow the prescribed NCEP Step 1 diet for the duration of the study. He is married and has two children. He is physically active and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week. He has no known allergies and is not taking any other medication. He is willing to practice an effective barrier method of birth control for the duration of the study as per the eligibility criteria. He has no history of HIV infection or any other medical condition that may interfere with the study.

A 55-year-old male patient is experiencing abdominal pain and fatigue. He has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis and is being monitored for the possibility of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and has been sober for the past 6 months. He has never received any treatment for HCC. He is married and has two children. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He has no known allergies to any medication or contrast agents. He has no history of HIV or any other serious medical condition. He has not participated in any other investigational trials in the past 30 days. He is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception if needed.

A 60-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is scheduled for a coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. He has been taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for the past 3 years. He has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. He exercises 3 times a week for 30 minutes. His last echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 45%. He has no history of lung disease or significant respiratory symptoms. His renal function and liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no known allergies to any drugs or food. He is married and lives with his wife. He works as a manager in a software company and has a sedentary lifestyle.

A 53-year-old male patient presents with a history of left-sided neck dissection surgery for papillary thyroid carcinoma 6 months ago. He reports experiencing persistent pain in the left upper trapezius muscle for the last 3 months, which has limited his range of motion in lateral flexion and rotation. The patient also reports tenderness and muscle spasms in the affected area. Physical examination reveals a palpable intramuscular taut band and provocation of the clinical symptoms by compression of the active trigger point. The patient has not received any medication or other therapies for MPS within the previous 2 months. He has no pacemaker and is not pregnant. There is no open wound at the treatment area. The patient has no history of cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy, cervical spine fracture or spondylolisthesis, rheumatoid arthritis, coagulopathy, epilepsy or any psychological disorder. The patient is interested in enrolling in the clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of extracorporeal shock wave therapy on his cervical myofascial pain following neck dissection surgery.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and has previously received tuberculosis treatment for more than a month but has not achieved sputum conversion. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial for a new immunomodulator drug called Mycobacterium w, which has been found to be effective in treating patients with leprosy and has also shown promise in the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient is not co-infected with HIV, hepatitis B or C, and has normal renal, liver and hematological functions. He is not pregnant or lactating, and is not severely malnourished with a body mass index (BMI) of 22. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old male athlete with a lower limb amputation. He has been competing professionally in paralympic sports for the past 5 years. He has experienced no injuries or respiratory infections in the past 3 months. His past medical history is remarkable for his amputation and he has no other systemic problems. He is not taking any medications. He has been training regularly for at least 3 hours per day, 5 days per week for the past 3 years. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no visual or hearing impairments. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the relationship between respiratory function and core muscle strength in athletes with disabilities.

28 year old male with a history of cystic fibrosis, presenting with increased cough, sputum production, and fatigue. The patient has had multiple hospitalizations for pulmonary exacerbations and has previously tested positive for P. aeruginosa and B. cepacia in sputum cultures. He is currently receiving treatment with meropenem and meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. The patient has no known hypersensitivity or intolerance to meropenem and has not experienced seizures. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for participation in the study.

A 32-year-old Hispanic male was referred to the clinic for evaluation of opioid and cocaine use. He has been using opioids for the past five years and cocaine for the past three years. He reports daily use of opioids, which he injects intravenously, and cocaine use two to three times a week, which he snorts. The patient reports a history of depression and anxiety but has not been on any medication for these conditions. He denies any current suicidal or homicidal ideation. The patient has no history of seizures or loss of consciousness from traumatic injury. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is able to read and understand forms and interviews in English.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been struggling with a non-healing wound on her leg for the past 2 months. She has tried various treatments but none of them seem to work. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, but is otherwise unremarkable. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She is mentally stable and able to care for herself. Her wound is approximately 5cm x 5cm in size. There is no evidence of mental illness or drug abuse. She has not participated in any similar experiments in the past 3 months. She has no serious infectious diseases and has not undergone any recent surgeries or suffered from any severe traumas or stressful situations. She is willing to comply with the long-term follow-up requirements of the study.

A 27 year old man came to the clinic interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is currently working as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a BMI of 27 kg/cm² and no known chronic disease. He does not take any medication and is a non-smoker. His latest lab reports show fasting plasma glucose levels within the normal range and HbA1c within 4-6%. He has no history of mental illness and has good peripheral veins. He is willing to participate in the establishment of a serum bank and is affiliated with a social security scheme.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic lumbar spine pain for the past 5 years. He is scheduled for elective lumbar spine surgery and has been taking a daily morphine equivalent dose of 80 mg for the past year. He has no history of cancer-related pain or adverse effects attributed to opioid tapering or lofexidine use. He does not have any medical or surgical conditions that could be adversely impacted by opioid tapering or use of lofexidine. The patient is generally healthy, with no comorbid psychiatric or neurological conditions. He does not have an active substance abuse disorder and is able to function in an ambulatory care setting without the use of supportive gait aids. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

54 year old man with type 2 diabetes for 10 years, currently receiving care at a primary care clinic in Durham County, NC. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse and is interested in receiving support for quitting both. He has a BMI of 32 and reports occasional non-medical use of prescription pain medications. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and depression. He takes metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and sertraline daily. He has a designated medical home and is capable of making decisions regarding his healthcare. He is interested in participating in the study to receive support for substance use cessation and improve his overall health outcomes.

The patient is a 30-year-old man with a BMI of 25. He has no known history of hypertension or cardiovascular, respiratory, neuropsychiatric, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, or immunologic diseases. He is a non-smoker and has not used any illicit drugs or consumed more than 2 cups of coffee per day in the past 6 months. He has no known drug allergies. He works as a software engineer and has a regular exercise routine. He has a normal ECG and laboratory results from recent blood biochemistry, hematology, and urinalysis tests. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse and has tested negative for a urine drug screen at the study screening. He is willing to practice an effective method of birth control throughout the study. He is willing to be confined to the testing facility for at least 10 hours before dosing and for 72 hours after dosing in each treatment period. He is willing to return for additional assessments as required. He is willing to provide a DNA sample for genotyping to determine his CYP2D6 metabolizer status. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who lives in a rural area in Ethiopia. He complains of abdominal pain and diarrhea. He has no other medical condition. His parents are farmers and he helps them on the farm after school. He attends school regularly and is in the seventh grade. The patient is well-nourished and cooperative. The physical examination showed tenderness in the abdomen and the stool sample was positive for soil-transmitted helminthes (STH). The patient has no known history of allergic reaction to albendazole. The patient and his parents agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent sheet.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with high-grade carotid artery stenosis, with a Doppler flow velocity of 1.5 m/sec at a Doppler angle of 50-60°. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on medication for hypertension and diabetes for the past 5 years, and he is currently taking a statin for his hyperlipidemia. He has not had any previous carotid surgery or stroke within the past 30 days. He has not been diagnosed with any inflammatory diseases or malignancies, and he is not receiving any anti-inflammatory treatment. He is able to provide informed consent and participate in the study investigations. His kidney function is normal, with a GFR of 70 ml/h. He does not have any contraindications for MRI.

34-year-old healthy male with a regular sleep schedule and no prior history of sleep disorders. He works a typical 9-5 job and is able to consistently get 7-8 hours of sleep per night. He does not have any chronic medical conditions, is not taking any medications, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He does not have a history of color blindness and has a BMI of 25. He is interested in participating in research to better understand the effects of sleep length and circadian regulation on the body clock's response to bright light.

65M with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed 2 years ago, treated with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for a total of 18 months.
