The patient has no reported history of metastasis or other significant comorbidities. He is currently under routine surveillance with PSA checks, and his PSA levels have remained low and stable. He has a BMI of 30 and has been struggling with weight gain since starting ADT. He reports feeling fatigued with occasional hot flashes, and a reduced libido. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. His current medications include a daily multivitamin, and a statin for hyperlipidemia. The patient is interested in participating in a lifestyle modification program and is willing to modify his diet and participate in blood and urine collection. He is able to walk more than two city blocks and is able to comprehend informed consent and procedural requirements. The patient speaks fluent English and is over 40 years old.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with persistent fatigue during and after her cancer treatment. She completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy six months ago and is currently undergoing hormone therapy. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than those related to her cancer treatment. She is able to provide written informed consent and is fluent in English. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in her right breast. She reports difficulty with daily activities due to her fatigue and is interested in participating in a study to better understand the causes of fatigue in cancer patients. She is willing to have blood drawn and complete questionnaires about her physical activity, fatigue, depression, and quality of life. She is also willing to participate in optional tests, including computer games testing her memory, attention, and ability to follow directions, and hand grip strength test to evaluate physical strength.

A 55-year-old African American woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 10 years and hypertension for 5 years, presented to the clinic with the complaint of fatigue and decreased urine output. Her laboratory tests showed an elevated serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL, and a 24-hour urine protein excretion of 1.5 g. An ultrasound of her kidneys revealed bilateral small kidneys with increased echogenicity, and a diagnosis of diabetic nephropathy was confirmed. She was otherwise in good health, with no significant medical history, and no history of allergies or intolerance to any medication. She was not currently taking any medication for her diabetic nephropathy, but was on a stable dose of antihypertensive medication. She met all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and did not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

45 yo F recently diagnosed with breast cancer scheduled for elective breast cancer surgery. She is a daily smoker and has a history of smoking for the past 15 years. She has tried to quit smoking several times in the past but has been unsuccessful. Her current smoking habit is approximately 10 cigarettes per day. She reports experiencing mild nicotine withdrawal symptoms when trying to quit smoking such as irritability, restlessness, and difficulty concentrating. She is able to read and write Danish and is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing the effect of a brief preoperative smoking intervention on postoperative complications in women undergoing breast cancer surgery. She does not consume more than 35 units of alcohol per week and does not have any diagnosed psychiatric diseases or preoperative neo-adjuvant chemotherapy.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a transient ischemic attack (TIA) two months ago. She presents with recurrent episodes of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She has been on anticoagulation therapy with warfarin for the past month but the symptoms persist. Further evaluation with carotid Doppler ultrasound reveals a >70% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. She is indicated for carotid artery stenting (CAS) and agrees to participate in the study. She has been on dual antiplatelet therapy (acetylsalicylic acid [ASA] 100 mg + clopidogrel 75 mg per day) for the past 10 days. She undergoes neurological examination and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and 24 hours after CAS. Venous blood samples are collected within 24 hours before CAS for laboratory evaluation including hematology, coagulation markers, vWF antigen, PAI-1 activity, PAI-1 polymorphism 4G/g, Multiplate (ASA and clopidogrel resistance test), and anti Xa activity. She has no contraindication for MRI.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has a venous leg ulcer on her right lower leg that has been present for 3 months. She reports that the ulcer started as a small blister that eventually broke open and has not healed since. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control her blood pressure. She denies any allergies to medications or dressings. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with study procedures. Her wound measures approximately 5 cm in diameter and has peri-wound skin that is dry and flaky. She reports occasional pain at the wound site, especially during dressing changes. She will be randomized to either the silicon adhesive dressing or acrylic adhesive dressing arm of the study. The investigator will assess her wound and peri-wound skin at baseline and follow her for up to three weeks to evaluate changes in the wound and peri-wound skin and to assess pain before, during, and after dressing removal.

The patient is a premature newborn with a birth weight below 1000 grams. They were born in the hospital between January 2005- December 2006 (before) or July 2007- June 2009 (after). They do not present with any signs of cholestasis at birth and have not been diagnosed with any diseases associated with cholestasis. The patient has not been transferred or deceased before 28 days of life.

This clinical trial is open to all staff physicians at the university hospital. The trial aims to test the effectiveness of a portable stress management device (PSMD) in reducing physician stress and enhancing their well-being. To be eligible, physicians must not have a history of major depression or currently screen positive for it. Those who participate in the trial will be randomly allocated to either the intervention or control group, and will be monitored for 28 days. The intervention group will be trained in a relaxation breathing technique and provided with a PSMD to use daily, while the control group will receive standard care. At the end of the 28-day trial, stress and physiological parameters will be measured again. Following this trial, there will be an additional 28-day trial extension for both groups to assess the effectiveness of the PSMD in real-life situations without ongoing support from the research team. This trial presents an opportunity for staff physicians to learn stress management techniques and discover tools that can help them cope with the stress of their work.

36-year-old female who presents with symptoms of insomnia and depression for over 3 months. She reports difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, and waking up feeling unrefreshed. She also reports feeling sad, hopeless, and lacking interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has a history of anxiety and has tried multiple medications with limited success. She consumes 1-2 cups of coffee per day in the morning. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, does not have a history of bipolar disorder or psychosis, and has not received cognitive behavioral therapy within the past year. She is not currently exposed to trauma and is not working a rotating shift that overlaps with 2400h. She is willing to undergo fMRI scanning for the study.

50-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer is eligible for this clinical trial. She has a history of breast cancer and has undergone a mastectomy on the affected side. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past. She is currently asymptomatic with non-life-threatening metastases. She has measurable disease by radiograph, CT scan, MRI, nuclear medicine bone scan, or physical examination. She has not undergone any hormonal therapy in the past 3 months and has not undergone any chemotherapy in the past month. She has no active brain metastases. She has a granulocyte count of at least 1,500/mm^3, a platelet count of at least 50,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin of at least 8 g/dL. Her bilirubin and SGOT levels are less than 1.5 times normal. She has a creatinine level no greater than 1.8 mg/dL and creatinine clearance of at least 60 mL/min. She has a BUN no greater than 1.5 times normal. Her LVEF is at least 50% at rest by MUGA. She has no uncontrolled hypertension. She is HIV negative and has no other serious medical or psychiatric illness that would preclude study participation. She has no other prior or concurrent malignancy within the past 5 years except curatively treated squamous cell carcinoma in situ of the cervix, basal cell skin cancer, or any other curatively treated disease in complete remission. She has not undergone any prior trastuzumab therapy. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis caused by hepatitis C virus infection. He has been experiencing taste disorders including metallic taste in the mouth, loss of taste sensation and food aversion for the past 6 months. He has lost 10 pounds in the past 3 months due to the decreased food intake. His liver function tests show a Child-Pugh class A disease with total bilirubin of 1.2 mg/dL, albumin of 3.5 g/dL, INR of 1.1, and platelet count of 110,000/μL. His MELD score is 8. He denies any history of hepatic encephalopathy, neurological or respiratory disease. He has stopped alcohol consumption for the past 2 years. He is currently taking furosemide, spironolactone, and lactulose. He has no known drug allergies.

25 year-old male who is a competitive runner and has been experiencing anterior knee pain for the past 6 months. The pain is located around the patella, and he describes it as a dull ache that is aggravated by running, jumping, and stairs. He rates the pain at 60 mm on a visual analogue scale (VAS) from 0 mm (no pain) to 100 mm (worst imaginable pain). He has tried rest, ice, and stretching, but the pain persists. He has no history of knee or ankle surgery, and has not had physical therapy in the past month. He is not pregnant and is not taking anticoagulants. He has a palpable taut band in the vastus lateralis muscle, and reports tenderness in this area. The pain is reproduced with compression, and he recognizes the referred pain as familiar. The patient has no history of neurologic conditions and no local infections.

A 37-year-old male who sustained a closed head injury in a motor vehicle accident six months ago presents with symptoms of depression including sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities he used to enjoy. He has no history of pre-existing neurological or psychiatric conditions, and is currently not taking any psychotropic medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has a stable medical history. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of escitalopram in the treatment of post-TBI depression.

45 yo F with a BMI of 30 and a recent diagnosis of mild dyslipidemia (LDL cholesterol 160 mg/dl, HDL cholesterol 38 mg/dl). She reports exercising less than two times per week and is otherwise healthy. She is interested in improving her cardiovascular health and has no known history of diabetes or hypertension. She is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study and is willing to be randomized to any group.

A 45-year-old male Indonesian patient with a history of tuberculosis, who was previously treated with anti-TB drugs for 6 months, presents with persistent cough and sputum production for the past 3 weeks. The patient denies any history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He has no significant medical history, but he does have a family history of tuberculosis. He works as a driver and is married with two children. He lives in a crowded household with his extended family. His chest X-ray shows lung lesions and bacterial smear examination is positive for acid-fast bacilli. The rapid molecular test for rifampicin resistance has been performed, but the result is inconclusive due to improper specimen handling. The patient is referred to a study center for further evaluation and management.

A 28-year-old female who works as a nurse is interested in participating in clinical trials as a healthy volunteer. She has no significant medical history, and her last physical examination was normal. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. She has a BMI of 22, and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is currently not pregnant, and she uses oral contraceptives as her preferred method of contraception. She has never participated in any clinical trial before.

23 year-old woman who is 36 weeks pregnant with a singleton gestation, presenting for an elective cesarean section due to a previous cesarean delivery. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She has received spinal anesthesia for the procedure. She has no history of headaches or migraines. She has no contraindications to the use of aminophylline. She has given informed consent to participate in the study.

A 28-year-old woman who is 5'5" tall and weighs 210 pounds is pregnant with her first child. She has a pre-gravid BMI of 35 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated and she plans to exclusively breastfeed her infant for at least 3 months with the support of her partner. She has a history of obesity and has struggled with weight loss in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the relationship between maternal obesity, breast milk composition, and infant growth.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer two years ago. He underwent prostatectomy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has spread to other parts of his body. He has been receiving hormonal therapy with LHRH agonist, but his PSA levels have been increasing despite the treatment. His current PSA level is 14 ng/mL. He has no history of major surgeries or other cancers. He has no psychiatric disorders and is in good overall health. His ECOG performance status is 1. He is not on any other medications for cancer or other conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer a new treatment option for his metastatic prostate cancer.

67-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented with complaints of numbness and tingling sensations in both feet for the past 6 months. He also reported experiencing occasional shooting pain in his feet, which has been affecting his daily activities. Physical examination revealed decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick in both feet, and diminished ankle reflexes. Electromyogram confirmed the suspicion of polyneuropathy. The patient was informed about the study and provided with a detailed explanation of the procedure. After obtaining free informed consent, the patient was enrolled in the experimental group for the measurement of small size type C nerve fibre conduction velocity. The patient was not under any medication that could interfere with the results of the test. The patient was instructed to avoid any food or drinks that contain caffeine or alcohol for 24 hours before the test. The control group will be recruited from the neurology department, and the patient meets none of the exclusion criteria for this study.

Patient is a 52-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with atrial septal defect. He is currently on medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has a BMI of 28 and his vital signs are stable. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medication known to interact with the study drugs. His laboratory studies including coagulation profile, liver, and renal function tests are within normal limits. He has no history of GI surgery or dysphagia. He has given informed consent for the study and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

55-year-old male with persistent atrial fibrillation diagnosed by 24-hour Holter monitoring. The patient has no prior history of AF ablation or cardiac surgery. He is currently on anticoagulation therapy without any contraindications. The patient has no history of stroke in the last 3 months and is in good functional class (New York Heart Association functional class I-II). He has no history of blood clotting abnormalities, oesophageal surgery, or advanced chronic kidney disease. The patient is willing and able to sign an informed consent form and undergo all procedures described in the study protocol and consent form.

A 9-year-old male presents with multiple skin bumps on his face, neck, and trunk that have been present for several weeks. The bumps are small, flesh-colored, and some have a central dimple. The patient denies any pain or itching. The family history is negative for similar skin conditions. The patient is in good general health and has no significant medical history. The patient and his parent or legal guardian have provided written informed consent/assent. The patient has between 3 and 70 treatable MC at baseline. The patient is willing and able to follow study instructions and likely to complete all study requirements. The patient has not received treatment with topical calcineurin inhibitors or steroids on MC or within 2 cm of MC lesions within 14 days prior to Baseline, nor has he received treatment for MC during the 14 days prior to Baseline with podophyllotoxin, imiquimod, cantharidin, sinecatechins, topical retinoids, oral or topical zinc, or other homeopathic or over the counter (OTC) products including, but not limited to, ZymaDerm and tea tree oil, cimetidine and other histamine H2 receptor antagonists (including Zantac).

The patient is a 55-year-old male who works in construction and spends most of his day standing. He has noticed that his legs feel heavy and swollen at the end of the day. He has a history of varicose veins and has tried compression stockings, but they are uncomfortable to wear for long periods. He has not received any treatment with venoactive drugs in the past four weeks. He is generally healthy, with no history of alcohol or drug abuse, peripheral artery disease, or lymphatic edema of the lower extremities. He has not had any surgery related to his chronic venous disease, and none is planned. He is willing to sign the informed consent form and participate in the study.

Pt is a 45-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). He has been experiencing weakness and muscle atrophy for the past 6 months, which has been progressively getting worse. He has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. His forced vital capacity is 70% predicted and his ALSFRS-R score is 35, with respiratory items score of 12. He has declined 4 points on ALSFRS-R in the last 3 months. He has been started on riluzole 50mg twice daily for the past month with no serious side effects. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to give informed consent. He has no family history of ALS and has not undergone a tracheotomy or continuous ventilator-dependent. He has normal liver and kidney function tests and has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease or any other significant medical history.

61-year-old man who suffered an ischemic stroke three months ago and has been struggling with reduced arm and hand function since then. He has been receiving outpatient rehabilitation therapy but has not seen significant improvement in his upper extremity hemiparesis. He is motivated to participate in a research study that could help him regain his independence and improve his quality of life. His past medical history includes well-controlled hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has no history of cognitive disorders and has a MoCA score of 26.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese woman who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She works as a marketing executive and is physically active. She has a BMI of 22.2 kg/m2 and weighs 50 kg. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not used any hormonal contraceptives in the past 3 months. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol frequently. She has not used any prescription or over-the-counter medications in the past 7 days. She has not donated blood or lost more than 200 mL of blood in the past month. She has not been diagnosed with any hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, neuropsychiatric diseases, or any condition that may affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. She is willing to refrain from caffeine, alcohol, fruit juices, and smoking/tobacco products for at least 48 hours prior to Check-In and until the end of Safety Follow Up. She is also willing to refrain from eating and drinking poppy seed-containing products and grapefruit-related citrus fruits within 7 days prior to dosing until after the collection of the final PK blood sample (Day 4). She gives her informed consent and is willing to comply with all scheduled visits and study procedures.

A 25 year old female patient has a history of bipolar depression and has been experiencing symptoms of residual depression such as persistent sadness, hopelessness, and low energy levels for the past two months. The patient has been taking two psychotropic medications which have been started two weeks prior to the baseline day and have remained unchanged in dosage. She is a non-smoker and has no history of substance or alcohol dependence. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures and restrictions. She has a MADRS score between 10 and 34 and a YMRS score less than 7. The patient has no history of florid manic episodes, major depressive episodes, or current psychosis. She is not at significant risk of committing suicide or harming others. The patient has no history of stroke, brain degenerative disorders, or brain trauma. She is deemed suitable by the investigator to attend cognitive tasks despite the severity of her symptoms.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer. He has undergone chemotherapy but did not respond well to it. He is experiencing significant pain and has lost weight over the past few months. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating he is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities with some difficulty. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to cancer therapy. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 28 days and is not currently receiving any other investigational agents. He has not received a live vaccine within the past 28 days. He is willing to provide recent tumor tissue for testing, if feasible. He does not have any active infections or evidence of active autoimmune disease. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he agrees to use effective contraception during the study and for 4 months after receiving the last dose of study drug.

A 29-year old woman from a rural area presents to the clinic with vaginal bleeding and abdominal cramps. She was pregnant and had not received any prenatal care. She reports no previous history of medical problems, surgeries or hospitalizations. She is married and has two young children. She is a homemaker and helps her husband in the farm. On examination, her vital signs are stable. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender. Her cervix is dilated, and the ultrasound shows an incomplete abortion with debris in the uterus. She is otherwise in good health with no signs of severe infection or hemodynamic disturbances. She has no known contraindications to the study drug. She is willing to provide contact information for follow-up. She speaks the local language and has limited education.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with acute leukemia who has received a cord blood transplant (UCBT) from an unrelated donor. He is currently at risk for cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) and adenovirus (AdV) reactivation or infection. He has completed his conditioning regimen and has started engrafting. His current ANC is 800/ul. He does not have any evidence of GVHD > Grade II and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He has no history of severe renal or hepatic disease. He is currently on low dose steroids (0.3 mg/kg prednisone) for GVHD prophylaxis. He is at least 30 days post-transplant and is not on FiO2 of >60%. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction (ED) for the past 6 months. He has tried sildenafil in the past but found it to be ineffective. He is currently in a stable sexual relationship that has lasted for more than 6 months. He has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or life-threatening arrhythmia in the past 6 months. He is not currently on nitrate therapy. The patient is generally in good health and is not taking any other medications. He works as a sales representative and leads an active lifestyle with regular exercise. He is willing to participate in the study and is looking forward to evaluating the efficacy and safety of vardenafil for the treatment of his ED.

This is a 38 year old male with a history of multiple sclerosis for the past 6 years. He has previously participated in a PET imaging study at Turku PET centre. He has had multiple relapses in the past and has been on disease modifying therapy for the past 3 years. He presents with recent onset of left-sided numbness and weakness, which has been confirmed on neurologic examination. MRI of the brain and spine reveals multiple T2 hyperintense lesions consistent with MS. He has no known contraindications to MR scan investigations and has no history of claustrophobia or anxiety disorder. He is willing to participate in the study and provide blood samples and complete patient-reported outcome measures.

58 year old male with controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of painful peripheral diabetic neuropathy for over 6 months. The patient reports experiencing burning, tingling, and numbness in both feet, which has significantly impacted his daily life and overall quality of life. The patient has no known allergies to Citrullus colocynthis fruit oil and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has no other known pain conditions or ulcers on his lower extremities. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 50-year-old woman recently diagnosed with stage IV colorectal cancer with no prior exposure to anti-VEGF treatments is being considered for this clinical trial. She has a wild type tumor RAS status and a wild BRAF status. She is in good general condition with a WHO grade of 2 and a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. She has read and understood the information letter and has signed the consent form. The patient is affiliated to a social security scheme and is using effective contraception. She has no history of arterial thromboembolism, lymphedema of the bilateral upper limbs, or poor understanding of spoken or written French. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and does not plan to breastfeed within 6 months after the last administration of the treatment. She is not currently participating in another drug trial and has no history of psychological or sensory abnormalities likely to prevent her from fully understanding the conditions required for her participation.

49-year-old female with a history of multiple vaginal deliveries, presenting with a complaint of fecal incontinence for the past 2 years. The patient reports severe incontinence, with 6 or more episodes per day, and a Wexner score of 15. She has tried various dietary modifications, pelvic floor exercises, and biofeedback therapy, but none have provided significant improvement. She has no history of prior surgical intervention for fecal incontinence. Physical examination reveals an internal sphincter defect and an external sphincter defect of 80°. No anal fissures or anorectal tumors are noted. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of autologous mesenchymal stem cells from the adipose tissue (CMMAd) in the treatment of fecal incontinence. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to provide voluntary written informed consent.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue and swelling in his legs for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels but has been taking medications to manage both conditions. He has never had any heart-related issues before. Upon further medical examination, it was discovered that he has an enlarged heart and reduced ejection fraction. He has undergone ECG, echocardiography and laboratory tests, but no known etiology of his cardiomyopathy has been confirmed. He has no history of cardiac pacemakers, nerve stimulators or metal foreign bodies in his body. His glomerular filtration rate is 60 ml/min. He has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who works as a teacher in a rural area of Thailand. She has been diagnosed with uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, with positive peripheral blood asexual forms. She does not have any complications from the infection and is currently receiving treatment. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant in the near future. She weighs 60 kg and is in good health with no history of chronic disorders. She does not have any mental health issues and is not imprisoned or institutionalized. She is interested in participating in a study that will help understand how iron supplements and fortification affect individuals with malaria. She is willing to undergo blood tests and take an iron supplement or other iron intervention, as determined by the study protocol. She hopes that her participation will contribute to improving the health of individuals in malarious areas, especially children.

As this clinical trial is focused on the pre-hospital management of non-severe traumatized patients, a suitable patient description would be as follows:  The patient is a 25-year-old male who suffered a fall from a height of about 2 meters while working on a construction site. He has a visible wound on his forehead and complains of pain in his left arm and right leg. He is conscious and alert, with no signs of confusion or disorientation. He reports no loss of consciousness, vomiting, or nausea. He has no history of medical conditions or allergies. He is not taking any medications. He is currently being attended to by a private ambulance equipped with a teletransmission device.

Patient is a 7-year-old girl from the United States who has been referred to the pediatric dental clinic at Children's Medical Center Dental Clinic (CMC Dental Clinic) for treatment of two primary teeth with deep caries. The patient has no significant medical history and is in good general health. The patient's parents have consented to participation in the study and understand the possible risks and benefits of both treatment options. The patient is cooperative and able to tolerate dental treatment with local anesthesia. The selected teeth are vital, asymptomatic, and match in terms of the size and location of the carious lesion. The teeth are expected to be retained in the mouth for at least eighteen months. The patient has no history of spontaneous pain and no radiographic evidence of internal or external resorption, intraradicular or periapical bone loss, loss of lamina dura, or widening of the periodontal ligament space.

55-year-old male diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy with neovascularization, who underwent retinal surgery with intravitreal injections of anti-VEGF agents with limited success in reducing the neovascularization. The patient currently presents with recurrent neovascularization and worsening visual acuity despite continued anti-VEGF treatment. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the association between CD160 expression on endothelial cells and retinal vascular disease. The patient has no history of other ocular diseases or systemic diseases that affect the eyes. Past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is not under law protection and is able to give informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is an 18-year-old Taiwanese female who is a new entrant to a university. She received a complete 4-dose hepatitis B vaccination in her infancy. She has no history of liver disease or hepatitis B infection. She is not currently taking any medication that could interfere with the study. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She will undergo a blood test to determine her serum anti-HBs titers during entrance health examination. If her anti-HBs titers are below 10 mIU/ml, she will receive additional HBV vaccination boosters according to the routine governmental suggested schedules. The anamnestic effect will then be observed in both groups. She will be followed up for the duration of the study and will provide blood samples for analysis at various time points.

As this is a retrospective analysis of adult COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU, no patient description can be generated. The recruitment of patients for this trial has already taken place, and the study is now focused on analyzing the data collected from the medical records of the patients who met the inclusion criteria. The study aims to identify the prognostic factors that are associated with poor outcomes in COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU.

A 67-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has been hospitalized for 7 days and has required supplemental oxygen via a high-flow nasal cannula. His current oxygen saturation level is 88% on 35 liters of oxygen per minute. The chest x-ray showed bilateral infiltrates. He has consented to participate in the clinical trial for LB1148. His laboratory test results are as follows: Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL, WBC: 10,000/mm3, Platelets: 300,000/mm3. His renal function and liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no known contraindications to tranexamic acid. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and procedures.

A 4-year-old boy was referred to the pediatric surgeon for an elective hernia repair surgery. He has a history of recurrent inguinal hernias and has undergone surgery before. His general health is good, with an American Society of Anesthesia score of I. He weighs 18 kg and is within the age range of 2-6 years required for the study. He is not allergic to any medications, and his family has no history of bleeding disorders. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known cardiac, pulmonary, or neurological diseases. The parents have given informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old Asian woman who experiences symptoms of lactose intolerance after consuming dairy products, including bloating, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. She reports avoiding dairy products, but feels that this limits her dietary options and would like to find a solution to improve her lactose digestion. The patient has not participated in any clinical studies with drugs or medical products within the last 30 days and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She does not have an allergy to milk protein and has not had any issues with lactase preparations in the past. The patient does not have any known metabolic or gastrointestinal diseases that affect the absorption, metabolism, or excretion of food components except for lactose intolerance. She is not currently taking any drugs that influence the resorption of food components or gastrointestinal motility. The patient has not had any recent surgeries that affect her current health. She does not have any psychiatric diseases, epilepsy, risk for suicide, or eating disorders such as anorexia or bulimia. The patient does not abuse alcohol or drugs and is legally capable of participating in the study.

A 32-year-old male with a history of occasional abdominal pain presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain in the right lower quadrant. The pain started two days prior and had gradually intensified. He also reported nausea and vomiting. On physical examination, there was tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower quadrant. The patient was diagnosed with gangrenous appendicitis and underwent an emergency appendectomy. During the surgery, the surgeon found that the appendix had ruptured, and there was frank pus in the abdominal cavity. The patient was hospitalized for five days for postoperative care and was discharged with instructions for wound care. He has no history of immunocompromising conditions, and he is not obese. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with follicular lymphoma two years ago. She has undergone one line of rituximab-based chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. However, her disease has relapsed with progressive adenopathy in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions. She has no B symptoms, and her blood count is within normal limits. CT scans show multiple lymph nodes with the largest measuring 3.5 cm. She is being considered for enrollment in a phase I clinical trial that will test the safety and efficacy of a combination of venetoclax, lenalidomide, and rituximab hyaluronidase. She has no significant medical history and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to any of the study drugs. She has not received prior treatment with lenalidomide or venetoclax but has received rituximab with no significant side effects. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old male, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus a year ago, is seeking care management for his condition. He has been struggling to manage his blood sugar levels despite following a strict diet and exercise regimen. He has a BMI of 33 and a HbA1c value of 8.9%. He is currently taking metformin and insulin injections as prescribed by his primary care physician. He has no known history of coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, liver disease, or cancer. He is not currently pregnant nor using any form of birth control. He has access to broadband internet in his home and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that uses telemonitoring technology to monitor his diabetes.

The patient is a 45-year-old Asian man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection 8 years ago. He has been on long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy, specifically entecavir, for the past 4 years. His last HBV DNA test showed an undetectable level. He has a history of heavy alcohol use, but he has been sober for the past 2 years. He has no history of liver cirrhosis or liver transplantation. He reports occasional fatigue, but denies any other symptoms related to his CHB infection. He is currently employed in a physically demanding job and has no significant comorbidities. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates stopping long-term NA therapy for CHB patients.

A 14-month-old infant diagnosed with cerebral palsy with total body involvement was referred for this clinical trial. The infant's parents have been seeking alternative treatment options and expressed interest in stem cell therapy. The infant's head circumference was within normal limits according to Nellhaus standard. The infant has no history of meningitis or encephalitis, congenital infections, metabolic disorders, or chromosomal abnormalities. The infant's MRI showed no severe anatomical abnormalities. The parents have given informed consent for the infant to participate in the study, including examination, therapy, blood sampling, and observation. The infant will be randomized to receive either umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UCMSCs) and conditioned medium (CM) therapy, UCMSCs only, or standard therapy as a control. The study will evaluate and compare the effectiveness of each treatment option in improving the infant's cognitive and gross motor function, as well as chemical factors.

A 55-year-old woman who has been postmenopausal for the past two years, visited the clinic complaining of vaginal dryness and discomfort during sex. She is in good health and has no history of any chronic diseases. She has never used a vaginal ring or any other form of vaginal contraception. She is sexually active with her partner and uses male latex condoms for contraception. She is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively. She is willing to comply with all study requirements, including abstaining from vaginal intercourse and the use of study-approved vaginal products during the study period. She has no history of adverse reactions to latex or the study products. She is willing to provide adequate locator information and agrees not to participate in any other research studies involving drugs, medical devices, vaginal products, or vaccines for the duration of the study. She is HIV-negative and willing to use male condoms for the duration of the study. She is willing to refrain from inserting any non-study vaginal products or objects into the vagina for the duration of the study. She does not have any exclusionary laboratory abnormalities or other conditions that would preclude informed consent or make study participation unsafe.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). She presented to the clinic with shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain on exertion. She has a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) which was treated with anticoagulants for the past 6 months. She has never smoked and has no history of lung disease. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to contribute to the understanding of CTEPH and improve patient care in the long-term. Her pulmonary artery pressure is 32 mmHg at rest and she has an abnormal pulmonary angiogram confirming chronic thromboembolic disease. She is classified as NYHA functional class III.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV infection 5 years ago. He has been receiving HAART for the past 2 years, and his viral load has been undetectable (<50 copies/mL) for the last 2 years. However, despite achieving viral suppression, his CD4+ count has not shown significant improvement. He has been experiencing fatigue, occasional night sweats, and recurrent respiratory tract infections. He is a single man who lives alone and works as a freelance graphic designer. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His past medical history is significant for a bout of pneumonia 2 years ago. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has not been on any chemotherapy or interferon/ribavirin treatment for at least a year. He has not been diagnosed with any other chronic infections. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been receiving chronic hemodialysis treatment for the past 2 years due to end-stage renal disease. She has a functioning arteriovenous fistula. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medications. Her BMI is 23 kg/m2, and she has not experienced any significant weight loss in the past 3 months. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have any chronic inflammation, ongoing infections, or cancer. She has not experienced any recent cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events. She is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medications. Her serum albumin concentration is greater than 32 g/l. She is able to follow the study diet and test procedures. She has not experienced any rapid reduction in residual renal function in the period prior to entry into the study. The patient has not shown intolerance to on-line hemodiafiltration.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who is scheduled for a lumbar epidural catheter insertion for postoperative pain management after a major abdominal surgery. He has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in the area for a few weeks and is looking forward to getting some relief. He has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is over 18 years old. He has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to any of the dressings being compared in the study. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He will be monitored throughout his hospital stay to ensure that the epidural catheter is functioning properly and that there are no complications related to the dressing used to secure it.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m². She has no history of chronic medical or surgical illness and is not taking any medication. She has normal blood pressure, with a systolic BP of 120 mmHg and a diastolic BP of 80 mmHg. Laboratory tests, including complete blood count, liver function tests, and renal function tests, are within normal range. She has never used cannabis, opiates, cocaine, or amphetamines, and has no history of drug abuse or hypersensitivity to drugs. She has not taken any platelet inhibiting drugs or anticoagulants in the last month. She has no metallic intra-corporeal devices and does not suffer from claustrophobia. She has not participated in any interventional clinical research in the last 3 months and is not in custody due to administrative or legal decision or under tutelage or being admitted in a sanitary or social institution. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the written informed consent.

The patient is a 58 year old Chinese male who was recently diagnosed with ischemic stroke after presenting with sudden weakness on the right side of his body. He was hospitalized and underwent a CT scan which confirmed the diagnosis. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, and has been a smoker for the past 20 years. His current medications include antiplatelet therapy, blood pressure and glucose-lowering medications. He works as a construction worker and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and has two grown children. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to provide informed consent.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTI) over the past year. She experiences burning sensation while urinating, frequent urination, and lower abdominal pain. Her urine tests showed the presence of bacteria and she was prescribed antibiotics each time. She drinks less than 1.5 L of fluids per day and has been told by her doctor to increase her water intake. However, she finds it difficult to remember to drink enough water throughout the day. She is interested in participating in the S-HYDRACYST clinical trial to see if increasing her daily water intake will reduce the frequency of her UTI recurrences. She is pre-menopausal, married, and works as a teacher. She is generally in good health, with no history of severe or uncontrolled organic disease that could interfere with the study. She is willing to consume 1.5 L of drinking water per day on top of her usual consumption and is excited to receive regular hydration coaching support.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained multiple injuries, including fractures of the pelvis and right femur, as well as a closed head injury. He was admitted to the hospital for care of his injuries and is expected to remain hospitalized for at least 24 hours. Based on his injuries, he has a moderate to high risk for the development of venous thromboembolism (VTE). He has no previous history of VTE or bleeding disorders, and is not currently taking any medications that could affect his coagulation status. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol for surveillance and prophylactic measures for VTE.

A 35-year-old non-smoker female patient has been experiencing severe toothache and has been diagnosed with a root fracture. The dentist has recommended extraction of the affected tooth. The patient is in good health and has no history of any medical conditions. She is not pregnant and has not undergone any radiotherapy or chemotherapy in the past 5 years. She is interested in preserving the alveolar ridge post-extraction to maintain the aesthetic and functional outcome of the extraction site.

45-year-old male who works in construction presents with pain on the lateral aspect of his right elbow that has been present for the past 6 months. The pain is worse with gripping and lifting objects. The patient denies any previous elbow injuries or surgeries. He has tried rest, physiotherapy, and anti-inflammatory medication with no significant improvement. On examination, there is tenderness over the lateral epicondyle and pain with resisted wrist extension. Cozen's test is positive. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a novel treatment for lateral epicondylitis.

56 F with a h/o rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 8 years, presenting with joint pain, swelling, and stiffness particularly in her hands, wrists, and knees. She has been on consistent treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and methotrexate (MTX) for the past 3 years, but her symptoms have been worsening. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. She is currently not taking any vitamin E or omega-3 supplements. Her recent ACR score is 6. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of simultaneous supplementation with omega-3 fatty acids and vitamin E in the treatment of RA. She is compliant with medication and willing to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese woman who is in good health, has no history of allergic reactions to vaccines and has not participated in any drug or vaccine trials in the past 4 weeks. She has no acute illness, chronic diseases or presence of fever at the time of vaccination. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period and agrees to use adequate contraception if applicable. She has not smoked more than 20 cigarettes a day and has not been diagnosed with malaria in the past or resided in a malaria-endemic region or had malaria exposure within the last two years. Her hematology and clinical chemistry tests as well as urine routine tests are normal and she does not have positive markers for HBV or HCV infection. She is willing to participate in the study for the duration of the trial and has provided signed written informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus infection with HBeAg positivity and HBV DNA load of 1,500 copies/ml. He has been receiving peginterferon alpha 2a treatment for six months, but his HBV DNA load has remained persistently high. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and he is negative for human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis C virus, and hepatitis D virus. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and there is no evidence of neoplastic diseases of the liver. He has no history of autoimmune hepatitis or psychiatric disease. He has been regularly attending medical appointments and adhering to the treatment regimen. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). She has undergone (re)induction/consolidation chemotherapy and achieved Complete Remission (CR) in morphologic, but not in cytogenetic or molecular aspects. She is not eligible for Stem Cell Transplantation (SCT). Her performance status is 80% according to the Karnofsky score and 2 according to WHO. Her renal, pulmonary and hepatic functions are adequate, with a serum creatinine level of 1.5 mg/dl, a Sat O2 of 98% and normal liver function tests, respectively. She has a LVEF of 55% as determined by echocardiogram. She has no history of HIV or Hepatitis C Virus infection, nor is she pregnant or nursing. She has no signs or symptoms of fluid retention. She has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer. She has bidimensionally measurable disease and is not suffering from uncontrolled CNS metastases. She has previously undergone two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease as adjuvant therapy or for advanced disease, but they were not effective. She has not received radiotherapy for the past two weeks and has not taken any drugs known to interfere with platelet function, such as aspirin or NSAIDs (including ibuprofen), for the past two weeks. She has a platelet count of at least 50,000/mm^3 and a neutrophil count of at least 2,000/mm^3. Her PT and PTT are within normal limits and her bilirubin and transaminases are not greater than 1.2 mg/dL and three times normal, respectively. Her creatinine is no greater than 1.6 mg/dL or her creatinine clearance is at least 70 mL/min. She is seronegative for hepatitis B or C and is not pregnant or nursing. If she is fertile, she agrees to use effective contraception during and for 2 months following study participation. She has not received any immunotherapy for metastatic disease and is not currently receiving any hormonal therapy. She has not taken any hormonal therapy for the past two weeks. She has not taken any steroids except for management of severe or life-threatening toxic effects arising from bryostatin 1. She has not taken any anticoagulants for the past two weeks, or any aspirin for the past two weeks or any NSAIDs for the past two days. If acetaminophen is inadequate for pain control, she agrees to take oral narcotics such as codeine or oxycodone. She has a SWOG performance status of 1 and her Karnofsky performance status is 80%. Her life expectancy is at least 18 weeks. She has no active infections requiring antibiotics and is seronegative for viral hepatitis.

A 9-year-old boy with a formal diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and assessed overall and verbal IQ of 73 was referred for the study. He has difficulty engaging in social interactions with peers and adults, and he struggles with turn-taking during conversations. He is currently attending a mainstream elementary school with classroom support but has limited socialization opportunities due to his preference for solitary activities. He enjoys listening to music and often hums or sings along to his favorite songs. He has no history of seizures or other neurological conditions but reports hypersensitivity to loud sounds. He is not currently taking any psychiatric medication.

A 35-year-old female patient is scheduled for elective surgery due to chronic pelvic pain. The patient reports feeling tired and weak for several months and has noticed increased hair loss. On physical examination, the patient appears pale, and her conjunctiva is slightly icteric. Vital signs are stable, and the abdomen is soft and non-tender. Laboratory evaluation shows hemoglobin of 9.5 g/dL, MCV of 68 fL, MCH of 22 pg, and ferritin of 10 ng/mL. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding or menorrhagia. The patient denies any alcohol or drug use and is not on any medication. She has no known allergies. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the non-invasive measurement of Zinc protoporphyrin for detecting iron deficiency.

The patient is a healthy male between the ages of 20 and 50 who is either having difficulty conceiving with his partner, has been diagnosed with male factor infertility, has undergone a vasectomy, or has undergone a vasectomy reversal. He is able to speak, understand, and write English and does not have any medical or personal issues that would impair his ability to adhere to the protocol. He is willing to participate in the study and provide signed informed consent. The patient does not currently take any investigational drugs or participate in any treatment trials for any condition. He is mentally stable and able to follow the study protocol, including reviewing the TRAK™ Instructional Booklet, collecting semen specimens, and testing semen specimens.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been experiencing progressive difficulty in walking and numbness in his feet for the past three years. He has a history of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) and has been receiving treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) for the past two years. Despite treatment, his symptoms have worsened over time with increasing weakness in his lower extremities and difficulty with balance. His most recent EMG shows a significant decline in nerve conduction velocity (NCV) parameters. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. He is not surgically sterile or post-menopausal and agrees to use two highly effective methods of birth control during the study and for two months after treatment termination. He does not have any other chronic handicapping disease and is able to perform the 10 meters walking test. His laboratory tests are within normal limits according to the reference laboratory values. He is compliant with the study procedures and is easily contactable by the investigator in case of emergency.

This is a 63-year-old female patient who has been experiencing severe knee pain due to osteoarthritis for the past year. She has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and pain medication, but has not experienced significant relief. She has now been scheduled for total knee replacement surgery and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of regional anesthesia for knee prosthesis surgery. She has no coagulation disorder or infection at the puncture site, and is not currently experiencing any neuropathy or allergic reactions to local anesthetics. She has normal renal and hepatic function, and is not currently suffering from chronic pain or drug abuse. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU for alcohol withdrawal syndrome. He has a history of alcoholism and has been on a benzodiazepine regimen for the past 3 days to manage his symptoms. The patient has been noted to be hypoactive and difficult to arouse, with a RASS score of -2. The CAM-ICU is positive for delirium. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but has no other significant medical history. The patient is not currently taking any other medications. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. The patient has no known drug allergies. The laboratory studies show a normal complete blood count (CBC) and basic metabolic panel (BMP). The liver function tests are elevated, with an AST of 120 U/L and ALT of 90 U/L. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially reduce his duration of delirium and ICU stay.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer and is scheduled to start intravenous chemotherapy soon. He has no history of other cancers and his family history is negative for colorectal cancer. He has a past medical history of hypertension that is managed with medication. He does not smoke, but drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing golf on the weekends. He is fluent in French and has no difficulty communicating. He has read and understood the information letter and has signed the consent form. He is willing to participate in the study and is committed to attending all scheduled follow-up appointments.

A 35 yo F with a known history of type 1 diabetes diagnosed 10 years ago, presents for a clinical trial comparing hypoglycemic counter regulatory responses. Her HbA1c levels are between 42-86 mmol/L and she has no known hypoglycemia-associated autonomic failure. Her BMI is within the range of 22-28. She is not on any medication that could interfere with the trial and has no history of smoking or drug abuse. She has given written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 36-year-old pregnant woman with a BMI of 38 kg/m2. She is in her 39th week of gestation and is currently admitted to the Duke Birthing Center for spontaneous vaginal delivery. She has had no previous vaginal deliveries and her cervix is dilated at 5 cm. The patient is experiencing severe pain, rated as 8/10 on the numeric pain rating scale. She is not using chronic opioids and has no major cardiac disease. The anesthesia team has consulted with her and obtained consent for anesthesia services. She speaks fluent English and is interested in receiving epidural analgesia for labor pain relief. She has been approached by a member of the study team and meets the inclusion criteria for the DPE technique in Labor Epidural for Morbidly Obese Women clinical trial. She has agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 38 year-old woman who underwent gastric bypass surgery for obesity six months ago. She has lost a significant amount of weight but has noticed that she has lost a lot of muscle mass as well. She has been feeling fatigued and has noticed a decrease in her physical abilities. She is currently taking a multivitamin and a calcium supplement, but has not been following a specific protein intake plan. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her regain some of her lost muscle mass and improve her overall quality of life. She has no history of allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is willing to increase her physical activity and follow a leucine-enriched essential amino acid supplementation plan for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 57 year old female diagnosed with COPD (GOLD stage III) and has been prescribed inhalers for the past 3 years. She experiences shortness of breath during physical activity and has had difficulty with daily activities such as climbing stairs or walking long distances. She is a former smoker and has not participated in any pulmonary rehabilitation programs. Her lung function test results show a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 35% predicted and a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 45% predicted. Her baseline maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) is 56 cmH2O and she reports a modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale score of 3. She has no history of other respiratory or cardiovascular diseases, and her current medications include albuterol and tiotropium inhalers. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on improving respiratory muscle function and reducing her dyspnea symptoms.

A 32-year-old woman is experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain. She has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. An ultrasound revealed multiple uterine myomas, with the largest measuring 8 cm. She wishes to preserve her fertility and is interested in undergoing laparoscopic myomectomy. She is in good health and has no history of previous surgeries or medical conditions. She has a plasma AMH level of 4 pmol/l.

A 45-year-old female with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis is seeking a new treatment option as her current combination of non-biologic DMARDs and NSAIDs is no longer effective in managing her symptoms. She has not yet received any biologic DMARDs and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that offers a subcutaneous tocilizumab option. She is currently on a stable dose of oral corticosteroids (10mg/day prednisolone). She has no history of major surgeries or other autoimmune diseases. She is willing to use reliable contraception methods during the study period as she is of childbearing potential. She has not received any investigational agents in the last 4 weeks and has not been exposed to tocilizumab before.

A 55-year-old woman suffered a stroke 4 weeks ago and has been receiving rehabilitation therapy as part of an early supported discharge program. She has residual upper limb movement deficits and is unable to lift her hemiparetic arm from her lap onto a table. She is physically and cognitively able to comply with the study protocol and has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment score of 26. She is able to walk and transfer to a chair with assistance and has a carer who is willing to assist her with donning and doffing the garment. She does not have a skin disease or allergy to garment material. She does not have severe pain in her affected arm or hand. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her arm recovery following the stroke.

Patient is a 27-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, no current prescription or over-the-counter medication use, and no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient does not have any clinically significant laboratory abnormalities and has normal blood pressure readings. The patient has no history of retinitis pigmentosa or nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, and has no known allergy to or previous adverse events with PDE5 inhibitors or their constituents. The patient will be able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to fast for at least 10 hours prior to and for at least 4 hours following dosing in treatment groups A, C and D. The patient is willing to eat a standardized high-fat breakfast 30 minutes prior to dosing in treatment group B. The patient has no history of smoking within 6 months and has a negative cotinine test. The patient is willing to come to the study site on the evening before each treatment and remain at the site until the 24-hour PK sample has been drawn. The patient has negative serology for HIV, HCV antibody, and HBsAg. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

Maria is a 50 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and her oncologist has recommended that she undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or other gastrointestinal disorders. She is not pregnant and uses reliable contraception. Her current medications include amlodipine for hypertension and prophylactic fluoroquinolone for her HSCT. Maria is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her prevent Clostridium difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD) during her HSCT.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 5 years. He has been having difficulty with his vision, and upon examination by a retina specialist, he was diagnosed with Diabetic Macular Edema (DME). His visual acuity is measured to be between 25 and 75 letters at baseline. He has never received any anti-VEGF or intravitreal treatment for his DME. He is currently taking metformin and insulin to manage his diabetes. He has no history of ocular surgery or ocular inflammatory or autoimmune disease. He has no known allergies to medications. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form. He is an active individual who enjoys hiking and spending time with his family.

Patient A is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing troubling climacteric symptoms for the past few months. She has been having hot flashes, night sweats, difficulty sleeping, and mood swings which have been negatively affecting her quality of life. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of hormone replacement therapy or any other menopause-related treatments. She has not been taking any complementary treatments for her symptoms. Her Menopause Rating Scale II score is 4, indicating moderate symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of the homeopathic remedy Ovaria comp. to relieve her symptoms. She has no known allergies to bee poison or any other components of the remedy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection six months ago. She is HBeAg negative and has been on lamivudine therapy for the past 24 weeks. Her serum HBV DNA has been suppressed, but she has experienced some side effects from the medication including headache, fatigue, and nausea. Her liver function tests have remained stable, with no signs of liver damage. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of switching from lamivudine to adefovir dipivoxil as a potential alternative treatment option. She has no history of alcohol or drug use and has not participated in any investigational trials involving administration of any investigational compound within the last two months. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and attend all necessary follow-up visits.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of diabetes and critical limb ischemia (CLI) who has been recommended for a major lower extremity amputation. He has a BMI of 25 and has been maintaining good nutrition. He does not have any history of liver disease, severe asthma, or heavy alcohol consumption. He is not actively receiving chemotherapy or taking carbamazepine. He has no known allergies to N-acetyl-cysteine (NAC) or Indocyanine Green (ICG). He has not had any prior amputations on the ipsilateral limb. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of NAC on amputation stump healing and perfusion.

A 36-year-old male diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago with a CD4 cell count of 150/mm3 is currently receiving prophylactic treatment for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. He has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. His medical history is significant for a positive titer for Toxoplasma gondii. He has not been diagnosed with any other immunosuppressive disease or co-existing conditions. The patient has not been treated with clindamycin, fansidar, methotrexate, trimetrexate, spiramycin, azithromycin, clarithromycin, 566C80, and/or sulfa agents other than anti-PCP agents. He has no history of ocular, pulmonary, or central nervous system (CNS) toxicity or CNS lesions. The patient has no neurologic deficits except peripheral neuropathy. He has not experienced grade 3 or higher nausea and/or vomiting. The patient is willing to participate in the study and be randomized to receive pyrimethamine or placebo three times a week. He understands that he will be evaluated bi-weekly for the first month and every other month thereafter for at least 24 months.

John is a 33 year old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for 5 years. He lives with his parents and is currently taking antipsychotic medication for his condition. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no significant abnormalities on his electrocardiogram (ECG) or vital signs. He has not had a change in his medication dose for 3 months prior to screening and is considered clinically stable. He has a total Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) score of 40 with a BPRS score of 3 for #10 (hostility) and #14 (uncooperativeness) at the screening visit. He has a history of receiving and tolerating antipsychotic medication within the usual dose range employed for schizophrenia. He does not have any medical condition that would make him inappropriate for entry into the study. He is able to discontinue the use of all antipsychotic medication at least 5 days prior to the start of the treatment period and during the study period. He is a non-smoker and consumes only 1 cup of coffee per day. He is not a woman of childbearing potential. John is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has a history of elevated liver enzymes and ultrasound findings suggestive of fatty liver disease. He reports occasional alcohol consumption (less than 10 drinks per week) and has no history of drug or soft drink abuse. He is not known to have chronic hepatitis, biliary or autoimmune liver disease, or HIV. The patient has no known genetic or metabolic liver disease. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 and complains of occasional abdominal discomfort. The patient has given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of stable angina presents to the German Heart Centre Munich for a scheduled coronary angiogram. The patient is generally in good health and has no history of acute myocardial infarction, cardiac enzymes elevation, or regular intake of drugs containing nitroglycerin. The patient provides written informed consent to participate in a randomized controlled double-blind single-center study investigating the effects of verbal suggestions and intracoronary injections on the diameter of coronary arteries. The patient is assigned to one of the four arms of the two experiments: Experiment A: Intracoronary (i.c.) placebo-infusion together with a standardized verbal suggestion of coronary vasodilation vs. i.c. placebo-infusion without verbal suggestion. Experiment B: i.c. infusion of a very low dosed nitroglycerin together with a standardized verbal suggestion of coronary vasodilation vs. i.c. nitroglycerine infusion without verbal suggestion. The patient does not have hypotension, renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, or prinzmetal's angina, nor is he pregnant or experiencing acute psychiatric disease or cognitive impairment.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of episodic migraines for over 5 years. She experiences an average of 7-8 migraine attacks per month, which last for 24-48 hours and are characterized by a pulsating headache on the right side of her head, nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried various medications, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and triptans, but has not experienced significant relief. She is currently taking propranolol as a prophylactic treatment, which has reduced the frequency of her migraines to some extent. She reports feeling anxious and depressed due to the impact of migraines on her everyday life. She has a Master's degree in literature and works as a teacher. She is married and has two children. She is comfortable with using a smartphone and has access to a stable internet connection. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to listen to music for 1-2 sessions per day using the Music Care application. She understands the study requirements and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester who is receiving prenatal care at one of the selected clinics and planning to deliver at the study hospital is eligible for this clinical trial. The woman must be able to answer questions in English and willing to participate in the study. She should have provided maternal dietary data during pregnancy and a cord blood sample at delivery on which lymphocyte proliferation had been measured. The aim of the study is to examine associations of maternal gestational n-3 and n-6 fatty acid intake, fatty acid levels in umbilical cord blood, fetal growth, and early childhood overweight with markers of allergy and inflammation at the age of 3 years. The study will provide detailed dietary data on the mother and infant, maternal and cord blood samples, and data on anthropometric, social, environmental, demographic, economic, psychological, and lifestyle variables. The study will also measure immune outcomes at age 3 years in a subset of 370 cohort participants.

This is a 42-year-old mother of two, living in a rural village in Kenya. She is seeking help for her 14-year-old daughter who has been exhibiting symptoms of depression and anxiety. The daughter has been experiencing difficulty in school and has been withdrawing from family and friends. The mother reports that there has been a lot of conflict in the household, and she feels overwhelmed and unsure of how to help her daughter. The family is interested in participating in a study that could help improve their relationships and the mental health of both the daughter and the mother. They are open to receiving counseling from lay counselors and through existing community social structures. They are willing to commit to attending sessions and engaging in interventions that are tailored to their specific needs.

45-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has previously undergone percutaneous coronary intervention and is eligible for further intervention using the Nobori® DES system. The patient provides written informed consent to participate in the e-NOBORI registry and is willing to comply with the mandatory antiplatelet treatment post-procedure.

45-year-old male presented to the emergency department with acute onset of severe epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting. He has a history of peptic ulcer disease and has been taking proton pump inhibitors intermittently. On physical examination, he has tenderness in the epigastric region with guarding and rebound tenderness. CT scan shows signs of free air and fluid in the peritoneal cavity, indicating a perforated peptic ulcer. The patient is informed about the two surgical options for correction - laparoscopic and open techniques - and agrees to participate in the trial. He is able to sign the consent form and meet all inclusion criteria.
