A 7-year-old boy was brought in for a consultation regarding his height. His parents expressed concerns that he was significantly shorter than his peers and had not experienced a growth spurt. His medical history was unremarkable, and he had no previous diagnosis of any chronic diseases. The patient reported no bone pain, fractures or any other symptoms. His physical examination revealed a height of 111 cm (less than the 3rd percentile for his age and sex), a weight of 19 kg (less than the 5th percentile for his age and sex), and a BMI of 15.3 kg/m² (less than the 5th percentile for his age and sex). His pubertal stage was Tanner stage 1. No facial asymmetry, limb length discrepancy or other skeletal deformities were noted. His vital signs were within normal limits. Laboratory tests including thyroid function, growth hormone, insulin-like growth factor-1, and cortisol levels were ordered. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial to determine the cause of his short stature.

The patient is a 63-year-old man with a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing dysphagia and weight loss for the past several months. He was referred to a gastroenterologist for further evaluation and underwent an upper endoscopy, which revealed a mass in the mid-esophagus. Biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. Further staging workup, including a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, showed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient was deemed a candidate for surgical resection and was referred to a thoracic surgeon. After careful consideration and discussion of the risks and benefits of the two surgical approaches, the patient has agreed to participate in this randomized controlled trial comparing robot-assisted thoraco-laparoscopic esophagectomy with open transthoracic esophagectomy. The patient is in good overall health, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no significant medical comorbidities and has never undergone thoracic surgery. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was diagnosed with colon cancer two years ago. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and received chemotherapy as an adjuvant treatment. However, a few months ago, he started experiencing abdominal pain and was found to have metastases to the liver and lungs. He received multiple lines of chemotherapy, but his disease has continued to progress. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is currently experiencing fatigue and loss of appetite. He has no history of brain metastases or uncontrolled pleural effusions, and has no known chronic inflammatory or autoimmune disease.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a history of recurrent episodes of swelling in various parts of her body, including her face, hands, and feet. These episodes of swelling are often accompanied by pain and discomfort, and can last for several days. The patient has been diagnosed with hereditary angioedema (HAE) and has experienced at least one attack per month in the past. She has tried various treatments, including antihistamines and corticosteroids, but has not found relief. The patient is sexually active and uses contraception. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past. She has not taken any ACE inhibitors or estrogen-containing medications in the past month. She has no liver function abnormalities and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing and able to read, understand, and sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He is generally healthy and has no history of chronic medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not use any drugs or alcohol. His BMI is 24 kg/m^2 and his fasting plasma glucose level is within the normal range (80 mg/dl). He has no allergies to medications or any food items. He has not donated blood or undergone any surgeries in the past 6 months. He is not taking any prescription medications or dietary supplements. He does not consume grapefruit or grapefruit juice. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for follow-up visits.

A 42-year-old female patient with a history of locally advanced breast cancer presents for neoadjuvant chemotherapy at the Oxford Cancer Centre. She has no significant past medical history and is in good general health. The patient has consented to participate in the study and is willing to undergo the diagnostic core biopsy and the ultrasound elastography scan. She has a localisation coil as part of routine medical care. The patient has no movement disorder that could interfere with the scan. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and help advance breast cancer treatment options.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with periodontal disease during a routine dental check-up. She has not received any treatment for the disease yet. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is not taking any medications and has not recently used antibiotics. The patient will be asked to participate in a clinical trial investigating the relationship between periodontal disease and sepsis. The trial will involve non-surgical periodontal treatment and blood draws for culturing and biomarker analysis. The patient will be informed about the potential risks and benefits of participation in the trial and will have the opportunity to ask questions before deciding whether to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing severe pain in her left hip for the past 6 months that is affecting her daily activities. She was diagnosed with Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and is scheduled to undergo hip arthroscopy with Dr. Wolff. The patient has no known allergies to ropivacaine or morphine, and she is not pregnant. She speaks and reads English fluently. She has not used any narcotics for her hip pain before her surgery. The patient has no pre-existing chronic pain disorder such as fibromyalgia. She is willing to participate in the study to compare the effectiveness of two different pain control methods during and after hip arthroscopy surgery.

A full-term male baby with gestational age of 40 weeks and postnatal age of 24 hours is admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit due to suspected encephalopathy. The baby had an APGAR score of 3 at 5 minutes and required resuscitation for 10 minutes after birth. The baby has received one dose of phenobarbitone for clinical seizures. EEG monitoring has commenced within the first 48 hours of birth and has shown cumulative seizures of more than 3 minutes in duration. The baby's parents have given written informed consent to participate in the NEMO1 clinical trial. The baby has not received any diuretics such as furosemide or bumetanide in routine clinical management within the last 24 hours. Total serum bilirubin is within normal limits. The baby is not on any other anticonvulsive medication other than phenobarbitone. Renal function tests are normal and there is no evidence of severe electrolyte depletion.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, fever, and cough. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He is a non-smoker and rarely drinks alcohol. The patient has been feeling unwell for the past week and decided to come to the hospital when he started experiencing difficulty breathing. Upon admission, his oxygen saturation was 90% on room air, and he required oxygen therapy of 6L per minute nasal cannula to maintain the saturation above 90%. Laboratory analysis showed a low absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) of 800 cells/mm3. A nasopharyngeal swab was positive for COVID-19. He was started on standard-of-care treatment for COVID-19, including dexamethasone at 6mg once daily. The patient was informed about the clinical trial with CYT107 to improve immune reconstitution in COVID-19 patients with lymphopenia. He expressed his interest in participating in the trial and signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 58 year old male with a history of GERD symptoms for the past 10 years. He was diagnosed with Barrett's esophagus with low grade dysplasia 3 years ago and has been undergoing endoscopic surveillance with biopsies every 6 months. His latest biopsy results showed no progression to high grade dysplasia. He works as a construction worker and enjoys outdoor activities like hiking and fishing. He is married with two children and does not have any significant medical history other than GERD. He currently takes omeprazole 20mg daily for his GERD symptoms.

Pt is a 35yo F recently diagnosed with FSGS after presenting with proteinuria and edema. She has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has undergone a kidney biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. She has been informed and has signed an IRB-approval informed consent form to participate in the study. The patient is not seropositive for HIV, Hepatitis C or B viruses. She also does not have any current malignancy or a history of malignancy within the past 5 years. The patient has no uncontrolled concomitant infections and is not pregnant or lactating. She does not have any form of substance abuse or psychiatric disorder.

A 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for over 5 years, presents with frequent episodes of coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. Despite using her current inhaler, which contains an inhaled corticosteroid and a long-acting beta-agonist, her symptoms are not well controlled, and she has experienced at least one asthma exacerbation requiring a visit to the emergency room in the past year. She is a non-smoker and has no known history of COPD. She is currently using a medium to high dose of inhaled corticosteroids as part of her daily asthma regimen, which has been stable for at least 4 weeks. Her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) post-albuterol at screening was 65% predicted. Her ACQ-7 score is 2.5. She is compliant with electronic diary entries and demonstrates acceptable inhaler technique. She has not used any systemic corticosteroids or had any respiratory infections or asthma exacerbations treated with additional ICS within the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant and is using acceptable contraception measures.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma 2 months ago. She has not undergone any previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this condition. Her performance status is at 70%, and she is able to complete daily tasks with some assistance. Her medical history includes hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, which are being managed with medication. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her blood tests show a WBC count of 4,200/mm2, absolute neutrophil count of 2,100/mm2, hemoglobin level of 11 g/dl, and platelet count of 120,000/mm2. Her liver function tests reveal a bilirubin level within the normal range, SGOT and SGPT levels within 2 times the upper limit of normal, and alkaline phosphatase levels within 3 times the upper limit of normal. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who underwent previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with coronary stenting. He is currently on a maintenance dose of 75 mg clopidogrel and 100 mg aspirin daily. He presents with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and is currently taking pantoprazole for symptom management. He has no history of liver disorders, bleeding disorders or current infections. His platelet count is within normal limits (150,000-450,000/mL). He has not been on bivalirudin or glycoprotein IIb/III antagonists within the last 7 days. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the influence of pantoprazole on the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel.

35 y/o male with a history of psoriasis and had previously participated in Genentech study ACD2601g. The patient had been on efalizumab therapy for the past 6 months, but developed a rapid onset of inflammatory psoriasis disease recurrence within 2 months of discontinuing efalizumab therapy. The patient is seeking immediate therapeutic control for the recurrence of psoriasis symptoms. The patient has provided written informed consent and is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential. The patient is currently an outpatient and is eligible to participate in this pilot investigational study.

A 35-year-old woman who has given birth to two children and reports experiencing chronic headaches and back pain for the past year. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers and massages, but the pain persists. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to identify whether there is an association between childbirth and chronic headache and back pain. She is willing to complete a survey and answer questions related to her headache and back pain symptoms.

A 53 year old man was admitted to the hospital with severe chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and was scheduled for open heart surgery with Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) machine due to the long bypass time of more than 60 minutes. His left ventricular ejection fraction was 50%, which was considered normal. He had no history of acute infection, hepatic or renal failure, cancer, or any autoimmune disease. He had not used any steroids in the two weeks prior to the operation and had no coagulation abnormalities. He was prescribed low-dose intra-operative corticosteroids (dexamethasone and methylprednisolone) as anti-inflammatory modulators to reduce the risk of postoperative complications. The study will monitor the levels of T regulatory cells (Tregs) and IL-17 and correlate the relationship between Treg, IL-17, and micro RNA-155.

54 yo female with a long-standing history of systemic sclerosis, presents with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue over the past few months. She has a history of pulmonary hypertension and is currently on a combination of sildenafil and bosentan therapy. Patient reports some improvement in symptoms but still experiences significant dyspnea with minimal exertion. She has a history of Raynaud's phenomenon and diffuse scleroderma with skin thickening and tightening, and joint contractures. She is also being treated with methotrexate and prednisone for her scleroderma. On physical examination, there is evidence of digital ulcers and some mild peripheral edema. An echocardiogram showed an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) of 65mmHg. Right heart catheterization confirmed the diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension with a mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) of 45mmHg. The patient is scheduled for an MRI as part of the non-invasive assessment of pulmonary artery pressure clinical trial.

A 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He underwent a coronary computed tomography angiography (cCTA) that showed evidence of coronary artery disease (CAD). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will assess the effectiveness of FFRCT-guided evaluation in the diagnosis and management of his condition. He is able to provide written informed consent and is clinically stable, with no active or serious life-threatening disease that could affect his life expectancy.

56-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, who is scheduled for an elective coronary angiography with planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, but his current medical management is adequate. He is able to provide informed consent and is not experiencing any acute coronary syndrome symptoms or signs. He has not undergone prior coronary artery bypass grafting surgery and does not have any severe valvular or pulmonary conditions. He has not been diagnosed with heart failure and has normal renal function. He is willing to wear a SmartCardia patch for 30 minutes before and after the procedure as part of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with intrahepatic biliary tract cancer. The cancer has spread to his liver and cannot be removed surgically. The patient has undergone other treatments such as chemotherapy but with no significant improvement. He is now a candidate for a Phase II clinical trial that will test the combination of immunotherapy agents Durvalumab and Tremelimumab with Specific Internal Radiotherapy (SIRT). The patient has been fully informed about the study and has provided written consent. He is over the age of 18 and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He has a histologically documented diagnosis of locally advanced or limited metastasized intrahepatic biliary tract cancer that is not amenable to curative treatment. The patient has adequate bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function, and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies with investigational products within 21 days prior to the first dose of the study treatment. The patient has not received prior immunotherapy or other investigational agents, and has no presence of peritoneal carcinomatosis or brain metastases. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study, including hospital visits for treatment and scheduled follow-up visits and examinations.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with cervical carcinoma presents with complaints of lower abdominal pain and heavy vaginal bleeding. She reports that the pain and bleeding have been worsening over the past few weeks. She has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption, but she quit smoking a year ago. She has no significant past medical history and has never undergone any surgical procedures. During physical examination, a large mass is palpable in the lower abdomen. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80. Her routine blood test, liver function, and kidney function are normal. She has no history of coagulation disorders or anemia. The CT scan reveals cervical carcinoma of stage III. The patient is willing to undergo interventional therapy and has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. She is fully informed about the study protocol and has given her informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate depression. He has been experiencing feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities he once enjoyed, and has been having trouble sleeping. The patient is fluent in German language and is not currently taking any psychotropic medications. He does not have a history of bipolar disorder, psychotic disorder, substance dependence, cardiovascular disease, severe kidney or liver disease, or epilepsy. The patient is not allergic to capsaicin or sesame oil. The patient is not a third-year or above student in medicine, pharmacy, or psychology nor has he completed studies in medicine, pharmacy, or psychology. The patient is interested in participating in the study to better understand how positive expectations can impact the way he experiences emotions related to his depression.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male who has no history of malaria or any other significant illness. He has not participated in any research study involving an investigational product in the 30 days preceding enrolment, nor does he have any planned use during the study period. He has not received any recombinant adenoviral vaccine in the past. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and to allow the investigators to discuss his medical history with his General Practitioner. As a male, he is willing to use barrier contraception until three months after the last vaccination. He has no history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine. Additionally, he has no history of anaphylaxis in reaction to vaccination. He meets all the eligibility criteria and provides written informed consent to participate in this study.

A 54-year-old Hispanic man with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) has an A1C level of 8.2%. He has been on stable oral hypoglycemic agents for the past 5 months. He has no history of smoking and his BMI is 32. He has a history of hypertension and is taking medication for the same for the past 2 years. He has no history of congestive heart failure, ischemic heart disease, severe pulmonary disease, liver or kidney disease. He has no vascular disease such as myocardial infarction, stroke, or peripheral vascular disease. He has no history of cancer or psychiatric disease. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no known hypersensitivity to perflutren. His screening O2 saturation is 96%. His eGFR is 60 mL/min/1.73. He has no history of bladder/kidney infections but had UTI once in the past year.

64F with recent diagnosis of pneumonia and lives in a rural area with limited access to medical facilities was referred to the Rural Home Hospital (RHH) proof of concept study by her primary care physician. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Her medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. She presents with shortness of breath, cough and fever. She has been prescribed antibiotics, but her symptoms have not improved. She reports no history of hospitalization or surgeries in the last 5 years. She lives with her husband who is able to assist with her care. She has never been involved in any clinical studies before, but is interested in participating in this study as it offers the possibility of receiving care in the comfort of her own home. Upon evaluation, it was determined that she meets the clinical inclusion criteria for the study. She has capacity to consent and her husband has agreed to stay with her for the first 24 hours of admission. She is able to independently ambulate to bedside commode. She has been screened for all exclusionary criteria and has been cleared by the on-call MD to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis of the right knee presents to the clinic with complaints of persistent pain and stiffness in the knee joint. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 years and has been taking tylenol on an as-needed basis to manage the pain. The pain has become more frequent and intense in the past few weeks, and she is finding it difficult to perform routine activities such as walking and climbing stairs. She has not been taking any NSAIDs for her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. On physical examination, there is tenderness and mild swelling in the right knee joint with limited range of motion. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) 10 years ago. She has been experiencing gradual vision loss and has been unable to perform activities of daily living without assistance. She is legally blind and has been unable to work since her diagnosis. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. She is married and has two children, ages 7 and 9. She has never smoked or used any illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially restore some of her vision. She has not participated in any other interventional clinical trial in the past 30 days.

54-year-old male with a history of snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness presents to the sleep clinic for evaluation of sleep apnea. He has a past medical history of hypertension, obesity, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. The physical exam reveals a blood pressure of 142/92 mm Hg, a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m2, and a neck circumference of 17 inches. Laboratory studies reveal an HbA1c of 8.5% and a serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL. The patient is referred for respiratory polygraphy to assess for sleep disordered breathing. This patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. The study aims to identify patients with unrecognised heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and the patient's history of hypertension, obesity, and diabetes mellitus puts them at risk for this condition.

A 16-year-old Hispanic girl came to the clinic with a history of being overweight since childhood. She has been experiencing fatigue and abdominal pain for the last six months. The physical exam revealed hepatomegaly and elevated liver enzymes. The ultrasound showed fatty liver. Liver biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with a NASH Activity Score of 4. Her body mass index (BMI) was 37 kg/m2. She was informed about the study comparing weight loss surgery (WLS) with comprehensive lifestyle intervention (CLI) for adolescents with NASH. The study aims to determine the most effective treatment and identify diagnostic biomarkers for NASH. The WLS group will receive vertical sleeve gastrectomy (VSG), and the CLI group will receive dietary, activity, and behavioral interventions provided by trained study staff. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study as she is between 12-19 years of age with a BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 and has a liver biopsy confirming definite or borderline NASH with a minimum histological NASH Activity Score of ≥ 3. She gave written informed consent, and her parents provided informed consent. She was excluded from the study as she has a history of WLS.

The patient is a 45-year-old non-smoking woman with no significant medical history. She takes no prescription medications and uses over-the-counter pain relievers as needed. She has a BMI of 28.6 kg/m2 and is in good general health. The patient has no history of asthma, COPD, or bleeding disorders. She has not had any surgeries or blood transfusions within the past year. The patient has no history of peptic ulcer disease. She has not donated blood or platelets within the past 60 days. The patient does not have any tongue piercings or braces, partials, or dentures. She is willing to use acceptable methods of birth control or abstain from sex during the study period and agrees to have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test. The patient has no history of sensitivity or allergy to aspirin. She has had no recent infections, including HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. She has no cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, endocrinological, hematological, immunologic, metabolic, neurological, or gastrointestinal disease. The patient has no clinically significant physical examination findings. She is willing to provide written informed consent.

An 80-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia was admitted to the hospital for chest pain and shortness of breath. He has been living in a nursing home for the past two years and is under the care of a primary care physician. He takes a daily regimen of metformin, simvastatin, lisinopril, and aspirin. Upon admission, the patient's blood pressure was 160/90 mmHg, and he had a heart rate of 90 beats per minute. The patient was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome and started on dual antiplatelet therapy and a beta-blocker. The patient was hospitalized for 5 days and was discharged on the same medications with additional medications for gastroprotection. He has a follow-up appointment in two weeks with his primary care physician. The patient's son, who is his legal representative, provided written informed consent for the patient to participate in the study. This study will evaluate the impact of additional pharmaceutical care on preventing drug-related readmissions among elderly patients like the patient in this case.

A 55-year old male was recently diagnosed with multiple myeloma, a type of blood cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He is married and has two adult children. The patient had some lower back pain and fatigue, which led him to seek medical attention. He underwent a series of tests and was diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He received induction chemotherapy and stem cell mobilization with cyclophosphamide and filgrastim. The patient tolerated the treatment well and is scheduled to undergo autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplantation. The patient is a non-smoker and denies any use of illicit drugs. He is not allergic to Vitamin C and is not pregnant. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of melphalan with or without holmium Ho 166 DOTMP followed by peripheral stem cell transplantation in treating multiple myeloma.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been hospitalized for 10 days due to severe hospital-acquired pneumonia. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and has been recently diagnosed with hypertension. He has no known allergies and is currently taking blood pressure medication. He had a fever for the first few days of hospitalization, and his white blood cell count was high at 12,000/μL. The patient has not received any systemic antibacterial activity against gram-negative bacteria for the last 48 hours. His respiratory secretions test positive for aerobic gram-negative bacilli. The patient is conscious and alert. He has no history of primary pulmonary fibrosis, cystic fibrosis, lung cancer, or any other lung-related diseases. He has not been on glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants, nor does he have any known immunodeficiency. His liver and renal function are normal. The patient agrees to take effective contraceptive measures as he is of childbearing age.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who tested positive for COVID-19 four days ago. She is experiencing fever (101.5°F), cough, and fatigue. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medication. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has taken fluoxetine in the past. She is aware of the potential benefits and risks of participating in this study and is willing to provide informed consent. She is not currently hospitalized and has no active bleeding or other medical conditions that would exclude her from participation. She has not taken any medications that would interfere with fluoxetine treatment. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has a normal QTc interval. She speaks English fluently.

Pt is a 42yo M who has recently been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He has already received two prior therapies but has experienced progression of his disease. He is otherwise healthy and has a WHO Performance Status grade of 1. Pt has at least one site of measurable disease and has discontinued any previous monoclonal antibody or radioimmunotherapy. He is willing and able to sign the informed consent form and comply with the study protocol. The study will evaluate the highest tolerated dose, safety and activity of HCD122 in patients with non-Hodgkin's or Hodgkin's lymphoma who have progressed after at least two prior therapies.

The patient is a 55-year-old male Filipino diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus three years ago. He has been experiencing frequent urination, thirst, and weight loss. He was recently diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) after his 24-hour urine protein test showed a level of 350 mg/d. His serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dl. He has no history of non-DM renal disease, cardiovascular diseases, or stroke. He has been taking metformin and insulin to manage his diabetes. He does not have any urinary tract infection. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Sulodexide in Filipino diabetic patients with CKD.

75-year-old female with a recent history of memory loss and difficulty with word-finding. Patient reports feeling more forgetful over the last several months and has noticed a decline in her ability to perform daily activities, such as cooking and cleaning. She has also become more withdrawn from social activities and has lost interest in hobbies she once enjoyed. Patient has a family history of dementia, with her mother being diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in her 70s. Patient has undergone neurological evaluations and has been diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia. She is being followed by a specialized clinical team for further evaluations and treatment. A blood sample will be proposed for this clinical trial to further study the genetic basis of her condition. Patient has consented to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He has been experiencing pain in his left Achilles tendon for the past 6 months, which has been affecting his daily activities and causing him to miss work. He has tried various conservative treatments such as rest, ice, compression, and elevation, but the pain persists. He has not received any physical therapy treatment in the past 4 months nor has he undergone surgery for his Achilles tendinopathy. He has not been receiving corticoid treatment or has any history of thrombophlebitis or systemic or cognitive disease. He is not pregnant and does not have a pacemaker, prosthesis or osteosynthesis, or any dermatopathies. He has been diagnosed with Achilles Chronic Tendinopathy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will investigate the effectiveness of Percutaneous Therapeutic Electrolysis (EPTE®) in improving his pain and function.

A 30-year-old female recent graduate who has not travelled to any malaria endemic country is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a malaria vaccine. She is in good health, has no known medical conditions and is not currently on any medication. She works as a teacher in a primary school and enjoys travelling to different parts of the world during holidays. She is willing to practice contraception during the study period and is reachable by phone throughout the study. She has received all routine vaccinations and has not participated in any previous malaria vaccine trials. She is excited to contribute to the development of a vaccine that may help prevent malaria infections in the future.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) a year ago. After receiving induction chemotherapy, he underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from an HLA-matched unrelated donor. Following the HSCT, he developed severe liver dysfunction with jaundice, ascites, and weight gain of more than 5%. His liver function tests showed a total bilirubin level of 3.2 mg/dL, and liver ultrasound revealed hepatomegaly. He was diagnosed with severe hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) with multi-organ dysfunction involving his lungs and kidneys. He was placed on mechanical ventilation and required renal replacement therapy. Despite supportive care, his condition continued to deteriorate, and his estimated mortality at Day+100 was more than 80%. He was approached about participating in a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of Defibrotide for the treatment of severe VOD in HSCT patients. He provided written informed consent and was enrolled in the study. He was randomized to receive 25 mg/kg/day of Defibrotide and was closely monitored for safety and efficacy outcomes.

This clinical trial is looking for healthy male and/or female subjects between the ages of 18 and 55 years who do not have any clinically relevant abnormalities. The subjects should not have any history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease, although untreated, asymptomatic, seasonal allergies are allowed. They should not have any condition that could affect drug absorption or show evidence of regular alcohol consumption or use of tobacco or nicotine-containing products within 3 months of screening. Additionally, they should not have been treated with an investigational drug within 30 days or 5 half-lives preceding the first dose of study medication. Females who are pregnant or nursing or females of childbearing potential are not eligible to participate. The study aims to recruit up to 15 healthy subjects for the study.

John is a 56-year-old male who has been diagnosed with colon cancer. He is scheduled for major abdominal surgery, including a laparotomy, at the Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center. John has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, psychiatric disturbances, senile dementia, Alzheimer's disease, seizures, or suicide risk. He is not pregnant, nursing, or using psychotropic drugs. John is not allergic to morphine or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). He has no history of chronic or acute pain of any origin, respiratory failure or insufficiency, uncompensated or congestive heart or hepatic failure, and is not scheduled for an emergency or palliative procedure. John is not using antidepressants, anticonvulsants, or muscle relaxants, and has not used any monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 2 weeks of surgery. John is willing to participate in the study to determine if combining continuous background infusion plus PCA MO (combined dosage) is more effective than PCA MO only for the treatment of postoperative pain following major abdominal surgery.

Sophia is a 34-year-old woman who recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy. She had a normal vaginal delivery at 39 weeks of gestation. Her baby was exclusively breastfed for the first 21 days of life. Sophia has no history of any chronic or metabolic disease. She did not take any medication or antibiotics during her pregnancy and did not have any complications during delivery. Her baby's birth weight was 7 pounds and 8 ounces, which falls between the 10th and 90th percentile for his gestational age. Sophia is of Caucasian descent and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of infant feeding on newborn metabolomic profile. She has read and understood the consent form and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer that has metastasized to his spine. He has been experiencing severe pain in his back and has received radiation therapy for symptomatic relief, but the pain has persisted. He has also undergone surgery for the prostate cancer but the metastases to his spine have continued to progress. The patient is experiencing difficulty with mobility and has been unable to work or participate in his regular daily activities. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently taking pain medication but is no longer receiving any other treatment for his metastatic disease. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial in the hopes of finding a more effective treatment option that will improve his quality of life and provide effective pain relief. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study as he has an established metastatic vertebral bony disease in the spine and is eligible for single level vertebral osteoplasty.

A healthy 28-year-old woman is expecting her first child and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent tuberculosis infection in her newborn. The woman has no history of substance abuse during pregnancy and does not reside with anyone who has active tuberculosis. She is willing to comply with the trial protocol and allow her child to complete all trial assessments. The newborn infant is expected to have a birth weight of at least 2,300 g and test negative for HIV by PCR if born to an HIV-infected mother. The infant will be administered a single dose of either VPM1002 or BCG SII within 14 days of birth, strictly intradermally. The mother will remain in the trial area with the child and be reachable by phone during the trial period. The woman has no history of participation in an interventional clinical trial prior to enrolment and will not take part in another clinical trial for the duration of the current trial period. She has no history of any malignant condition.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who has experienced his second episode of spontaneous pneumothorax in the past year. He is tall and lean with a height of 6 feet and a weight of 150 pounds. He has never smoked and has no significant past medical history. His family history is non-significant for lung diseases. He presented with sudden onset of chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with a pneumothorax and underwent a bullectomy of the lung. He is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand the molecular pathogenesis of this condition.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been experiencing persistent nasal congestion and post-nasal drip. He also complains of occasional throat irritation and difficulty swallowing. He has been using nasal sprays and over-the-counter medications for the past month but has not seen any improvement in his symptoms. He does not have any significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and works as an accountant. He is interested in participating in this study as he wants to avoid the inconvenience and cost of going to the hospital for the standard flexible nasopharyngoscopy procedure. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide consent. He rates his pain tolerance as moderate and is willing to complete the VAS surveys.

Patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis (CF) at the age of 2. He has been on a regimen of bronchodilators, antibiotics, and inhaled mucolytics for the past 10 years. Despite this, he has been experiencing increasing difficulty with cough, throat irritation, and saltiness with the administration of 5.8% hypertonic saline solution. His FEV1 is currently at 60% of the predicted value, and he has not experienced an infective exacerbation requiring antibiotic treatment in the last 30 days. The patient has never undergone a lung transplant and is compliant with his standard therapy. The patient has no known Burkholderia cepacia infection, and his plasmatic creatinine and transaminases are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the tolerability and acceptability of a formulation containing HS and Hyaluronic acid 0.1% with HS solution alone.

65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, presented for an elective inguinal hernia repair. The patient underwent preoperative evaluation which included a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) which revealed a pulmonary systolic pressure of 47 mmHg. The patient was enrolled in the Preoperative Pulmonary Systolic Pressure and Outcome After Non-cardiac Surgery:Threshold Analysis study, which aims to explore the relationship between pulmonary systolic pressure and major cardiovascular events after non-cardiac surgery. The patient's peri-operative information and surgical and anesthesia data were collected, and postoperative major cardiovascular, cerebral and kidney events were monitored and recorded. Logistic regression models were built and selected to identify independent risk factors relative to postoperative major cardiovascular and cerebral events. The study will calculate odds ratio, relative risk and relative risk ratio of various dichotomous cut points, identify trend breakpoints, and conduct propensity score analysis for causal inference.

A 72-year-old retired teacher, Ms. Smith, has been experiencing mild cognitive decline over the past year, which has affected her ability to drive and perform daily activities. She has no history of neurological, mental or psychiatric pathologies, and her scores on the dementia scale of Mattis are greater than 130, and the IADL score is 4. She is right-handed and currently holds a driving license. She is fluent in French and is willing to comply with all the procedures of the study. She is an affiliate of the social security scheme and has agreed to be registered on the National File of Healthy Volunteers. Ms. Smith has no planned changes in her lifestyle and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. She has no significant visual or motor pathology, nor any dependencies on medicines, drugs, or alcohol. She has no contraindications to MRI and has no history of motor tics or Gilles de la Tourette syndrome. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, and she is not consuming any psychotropic drugs or related products. She has no dysthyroidism, thyrotoxicosis, or pre-existing cardiovascular disorders. She has no history of cerebrovascular disorders, cerebral aneurysm, vascular abnormalities, including vasculitis or stroke. She has no significant abnormalities on MRI and EEG according to the investigator's judgment. She has no untreated hypertension, pheochromocytoma, hepatic, or renal insufficiency. She is not obese according to the WHO classification. She is not on any of the concomitant treatments that are contraindicated at baseline and throughout the study period.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rectal cancer after undergoing a routine colonoscopy. Her CT scan showed T3/4 and node-positive disease. She has no history of prior radiotherapy to the pelvis and is suitable for pre-operative chemo-irradiation and surgical resection. She is in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no contraindications to MRI or PET/CT and is willing to undergo these scans. She has no history of psychological illness or condition that would interfere with her understanding of the study requirements. She is willing and able to give informed consent.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of smoking presents with complaints of neck pain and difficulty swallowing for the past 3 months. Imaging studies revealed the presence of a mass in the nasopharynx, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The patient has no previous history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. Laboratory results show normal hematology and chemistry profiles, with a calculated creatinine clearance of 80 ml/min. The patient provides informed consent according to institutional and/or university human experimentation committee requirements. The patient is accessible for treatment and follow-up, and has normal serum calcium levels. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

There is no patient description required for this study as it is a cross-sectional survey aimed at obtaining information on chronic pain prevalence and patterns in the Hong Kong population. The study will be conducted through telephone interviews with randomly selected households, and verbal consent will be obtained from eligible participants.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) and has been advised to undergo an allogeneic stem cell transplantation due to unresponsiveness to standard treatments. Unfortunately, he does not have a matched related or unrelated donor available. His oncologist has recommended him for a clinical trial investigating the safety and feasibility of ultra-low dose Interleukin 2 (ULD IL-2) as GVHD prophylaxis in haploidentical allogeneic stem cell transplantation for patients with hematologic malignancies. The patient has a haploidentical donor available, and he meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial. He has no major anticipated illness or organ failure, and his psychiatric health is stable. He is able to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent. The patient has no prior history of allogeneic stem cell transplantation and has not received IL-2 therapy before.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with a right-sided lung tumor. He is currently under evaluation for surgical resection. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are controlled with medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His lung function tests are within normal limits. He has no history of lung disease or respiratory infections. His body mass index is 26.5 kg/m2. He is scheduled for a lateral decubitus lung surgery. He has been informed about the study and is willing to participate. He is able to read and write and has signed the consent form for participation.

A 42-year-old female was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two months ago. She had been experiencing fatigue, fever, and frequent infections for several weeks before the diagnosis. She underwent chemotherapy treatment but her disease did not go into remission. Her physician has recommended a reduced intensity allogeneic stem cell transplant, and the patient has agreed to participate in this clinical trial. She has a matched unrelated donor available, and her ECOG performance status is 1. Her bone marrow biopsy showed 30% blasts in bone marrow. She has no uncontrolled infections or active CNS involvement, and her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She has never had an allogeneic stem cell transplant before. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has been on oral hypoglycemic agents and has been trying to maintain her blood sugar levels with dietary modifications. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking anti-hypertensive medications for the past 5 years. Recently, she has noticed an increase in urinary protein excretion and her latest lab results show a urinary protein creatinine ratio of 1.2 g/g creatinine. She has also been diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy. Her serum creatinine is within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is already following dietary management. She has no history of any other renal disease or severe hepatic disease. She has not had any episodes of anaphylaxis from angiotensin II receptor blockers in the past.

A 55-year-old Chinese man with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with dyslipidemia and a history of acute coronary artery disease. He has a BMI of 26 and is a current smoker. He is compliant with his medications and regularly attends his follow-up appointments. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the impact of treatment on his cardiovascular risk factors and to potentially improve his long-term outcomes.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing worsening symptoms of depression over the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated for most of the day, nearly every day. She has also noticed an increase in hot flashes and night sweats, which have been interfering with her sleep. She has not been using any medications to manage these symptoms. She has a history of depression, but has not been on any medication for the past 2 years. She has never used hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and has no other mental health diagnoses. She is in a stable relationship and has two grown children. She works full-time as an administrative assistant and reports no significant stressors at work or at home. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

A 42-year-old South Asian male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes presents with moderate to severe vitamin D deficiency. He is currently taking metformin and has a stable dose for the past 4 weeks. His HbA1c is 8.5%, and he is able to communicate effectively in Norwegian. He has no significant renal or liver disease, and his blood pressure is well-controlled on antihypertensive medication. He has no history of kidney stone disease or malignancy in the past 5 years. He has never undergone bariatric surgery and has a BMI of 32 kg/m2. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to adhere to the study protocol for the next 6 months.

The patient is a 51-year-old woman who presents with a recurrent brain tumor. She has a history of stage IV breast cancer, which was diagnosed 4 years ago and is currently in remission. She underwent a craniotomy for resection of the brain tumor 2 years ago, but unfortunately, the tumor has recurred. She is currently experiencing headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty with balance. Imaging studies reveal a 3 cm mass in the left frontal lobe. The patient has a Zubrod Performance Score of 1 and is otherwise in good health. She has no history of psychiatric illness that would interfere with her ability to complete treatment or follow-up. The radiation oncologist and neurosurgeon have determined that the GammaTile loader device would be appropriate for her adjuvant brachytherapy of the central nervous system. The patient is able to undergo post-operative CT for implant assessment and follow-up imaging. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for over a year, despite undergoing six months of conservative back pain care which includes medications, massage, and acupuncture. She has a BMI of 26, and is not pregnant or nursing. She has been diagnosed with moderate radiographic degeneration of an intervertebral disc from L1 to S1, with a disc suspected of causing CLBP. Her MRI showed a modified Pfirrmann score of 4 on the index disc, with Modic Grade II changes, and contained disc protrusion. Her low back pain is rated at 70 mm on a 100 mm VAS scale, while leg pain is less than 20 mm on the same scale. Her ODI score is 65 on a 100 point scale. She is not taking any systemic immunosuppressants, nor has she undergone any surgical procedure on the disc at the index or adjacent level. She has not been a recipient of prior allogeneic stem cell/progenitor cell therapy for any indication or autologous stem cell/progenitor cell therapy or other biological intervention to repair the index intervertebral disc. She is willing to undergo treatment and be available for each examination scheduled over the study duration, and has signed the informed consent and country-appropriate privacy forms.

A 62-year-old Caucasian man has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and is scheduled for resection of the pancreatic tumor. He has been experiencing mild abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and weight loss for the past few months. He denies any history of alcohol or tobacco use. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen. He has no known drug allergies. He has been able to maintain oral intake but has been experiencing some nausea and vomiting. He is married with two adult children and works as a retired accountant. His family history is negative for pancreatic cancer or any other malignancies. His ECOG performance status is 1. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his outcome.

A 22-year-old female university student is admitted to a hospital for treatment of anorexia nervosa. Her BMI is 16.2, and she has been struggling with the disorder for three years. She has a history of rigid thinking, a tendency to focus on details rather than the big picture, and difficulty shifting her attention and perspective. She has also shown resistance to traditional treatments and has not been able to make significant progress in recovery. She speaks fluent French and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of cognitive remediation therapy (CRT) in treating anorexia nervosa. She is aware that the study involves 10 sessions of either CRT or sham therapy (ST) over a period of 5 weeks, and that she will be assessed before and after the treatment, as well as at 6 months and 1 year of follow-up. She understands that the study is designed to determine whether CRT can improve cognitive functioning and clinical status in AN patients, and whether the impact of CRT is similar in both anorexic restrictive and binge-purging subtypes. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 15 year old female student in Santiago, Chile currently attending the 10th grade at a local high school. She is experiencing feelings of sadness, hopelessness and a lack of interest in activities that she previously enjoyed. She is struggling to concentrate in class and experiencing difficulty sleeping at night. She has not received any prior treatment for depression, but her parents and school counselor are concerned about her mental health. She scores between 5 and 14 on the depression questionnaire PHQ-9 adolescent version. She has access to a computer and the internet, and is willing to participate in the program. The student has no history of suicidal thoughts, is not currently taking antidepressant drugs, and is not undergoing psychotherapy. The student and her parents have provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman in her first pregnancy. She is currently in her 18th week of gestation and resides in a rural area in Burkina Faso. She presents at the antenatal clinic for her first booking and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for malaria prevention during pregnancy. She has no history of sensitivity to sulphonamides and is not clinically diagnosed with AIDS or HIV. Her family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. She intends to stay in the study area for the duration of her pregnancy and is willing to provide informed consent to join the trial. The patient is currently sleeping under a long-lasting insecticide-treated bed net. She is eligible for the trial and will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment or intervention. It is a study of the regional implementation of a collaborative lung function testing program in Catalonia, Spain. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions needed.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo radiation therapy as part of her treatment plan. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) of 2 due to fatigue and weakness related to her cancer diagnosis. She has no distant metastases and her blood work shows a granulocyte count greater than 2000 and a platelet count greater than 100,000. Her creatinine levels are normal, less than 2.0. She has no known allergies to amifostine and has not participated in any investigational drug trials in the past four weeks.

A 34-year-old woman diagnosed with systemic sclerosis 2 years ago presented with complaints of joint pain and stiffness, difficulty swallowing, and breathing difficulties. She was referred to the rheumatology consultation at the University Hospitals Leuven for management. Her medical history includes hypothyroidism and mild depression for which she is currently on medication. She is a non-smoker, social drinker, and works as a teacher. She is married and has two children. She is interested in participating in the study and has given informed consent. She is able to complete the questionnaires in Dutch and does not have any severe psychiatric comorbidity.

A 45-year-old male with a history of migraines and a recent episode of transient ischemic attack (TIA) presenting for elective craniotomy for resection of a right frontal lobe meningioma. The patient's past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both controlled with medications. Physical exam reveals no focal neurological deficits and the patient has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15. The patient's BMI is within normal limits. Preoperative laboratory values are within normal limits. The patient has no history of drug abuse and has not taken any medication that would contraindicate the use of a b-blocker. The patient's preoperative heart rate is 68 bpm. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate.

72-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic pain in the right knee. The patient has tried conservative management with physical therapy, analgesics, and intra-articular injections without significant relief. The patient has elected to undergo primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as recommended by her orthopedic surgeon. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or medication use. The patient is able to give informed consent and has adequate cognitive ability to participate in the study. The patient is enrolled in the fast track circuit and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who visits the pediatric dentistry clinic with his mother for a routine dental check-up. He has a history of cavities in his primary molars and has been receiving regular dental treatment. He has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. His mother reports that he brushes his teeth twice a day and she helps him floss. His mother has completed high school education and has average oral hygiene. The dental examination will be performed while the child is seated on the dental chair, with the use of sterile diagnostic instruments under daylight. The examiner will carefully inspect all surfaces of the teeth, and a custom-made examination chart will be filled for each child including date, name, age, address, gender, medical history, and previous dental treatment. The primary teeth will be evaluated using deft index, and permanent teeth will be evaluated using DMF index according to the WHO criteria. After the diagnosis, the child and his mother will be given printed sheets translated into Arabic, which will include his caries status, the right oral hygiene method to be followed in order to maintain good oral health, and any caries lesions that need treatment by restorative material or preventive measures.

The patient is a 35 year old Hispanic female who went for a routine Pap smear, which revealed an abnormality. She underwent a colposcopy which confirmed the diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade II. She is currently married and has two children. She works as a nurse practitioner and has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She previously had a tubal ligation and is not currently using any contraception. She is compliant with medical treatment and is willing to participate in the study. She has no history of breast cancer or other malignancies. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who is physically active and spends at least 60 minutes daily performing easy to moderate physical activities. She has a BMI of 27, which is within the overweight range. She does not have any history of falls, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, or orthopedic or neurological conditions (i.e., stroke). Her blood pressure is consistently below 140/90 mmHg and she does not have a history of heart conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not take medications that cause dizziness or slow movement. The patient is able to communicate fluently in English and understands written instructions. She is interested in participating in a community-based multimodal intervention program that can improve her physical and mental health. She is willing to commit to a simple, 15-minute exercise program at least 2-3 times a week. She is also willing to participate in a small group with friends or family members to improve social engagement and peer-to-peer support.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) and a recent CT scan that showed calcifications in his prostate gland. The patient denies any history of prostate cancer or any other significant medical history. He is not on any medications, supplements or herbal remedies. He has no history of implanted devices or metallic objects in his body. He has no history of claustrophobia or severe vertigo. He is able to give consent and is willing to adhere to the experimental protocols. He does not have any history of being incarcerated. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the diagnostic and treatment approaches for prostate calcifications.

23-year-old Chinese female who is a non-smoker and non-drinker with no significant past medical history is interested in participating in a Phase 1 study for evaluating the PK, safety, and tolerability of BG00012. She is currently not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 30 days after the last dose of the study medication. She is fluent in Chinese and English and has given written informed consent for the study. She has no history of severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis, HIV infection, or any other major disease that could potentially affect study participation. She is willing to comply with all study-related procedures and follow the guidelines provided by the study coordinator.

The patient is a 35-year-old Asian male who presented with chronic hepatitis B infection. He was diagnosed with HBsAg-positivity six months ago and has a history of exposure to other nucleoside analogues before starting TDF. He reports feeling fatigued and has noticed a decrease in appetite. He has no history of alcohol abuse or other liver diseases. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is currently not taking any medication for hepatitis B. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of TDF in Asian chronic hepatitis B patients.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been admitted to the ICU due to pneumonia. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her current medications include lisinopril and simvastatin. She is at a high risk of developing blood clots due to her prolonged bed rest and history of hypertension. The treatment team has initiated enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis at a standard dose of 30 mg twice daily. She has a BMI of 32 and an APACHE II score of 15. She meets the eligibility criteria for this study and has provided informed consent to participate. A baseline TEG® will be performed, and she will be randomized to receive either standard dosing of enoxaparin or TEG® guided dosing of enoxaparin. She will undergo weekly ultrasound duplex examination of the lower extremities to check for the presence of deep venous thrombosis. The study personnel will assess her daily for any bleeding complications. The study will be terminated if significant bleeding complications occur.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who had a heart attack 5 years ago and was treated with drug-eluting stents (DES) in his left anterior descending artery (LAD). He was compliant with his medications and lifestyle modifications but presents with recurrent chest pain and shortness of breath over the past 2 months. His cardiac catheterization shows recurrent restenosis within the DES in his LAD, despite being treated with both sirolimus and paclitaxel-eluting stents. He is now being considered for intracoronary brachytherapy using the Novoste beta-emitting catheter. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies to aspirin, clopidogrel, or heparin. He has no significant medical conditions that would interfere with his participation in the study. The patient is willing to comply with all protocol-specified procedures and follow-up and is able to understand and sign informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with joint pain and stiffness in multiple joints including her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles. She reports difficulty with mobility due to the pain and stiffness. She has no previous history of rheumatoid arthritis treatment and has not taken methotrexate (MTX) or any other disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. She is a nonsmoker and drinks alcohol socially. Examination reveals swelling and tenderness in the affected joints and limited range of motion. Her laboratory tests show elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Based on the 2010 American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) criteria, she meets the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). She is ACR functional class I-III and has ≥ 6 swollen joints (from a swollen joint count based on 66 joints (SJC66)) and ≥ 6 tender joints (from a tender joint count based on 68 joints (TJC68)) at both screening and Day 1.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain and difficulty walking due to osteoarthritis in his right knee. He has tried various conservative treatments, including physical therapy, medication, and injections, but none of them seem to provide significant relief. As a result, his orthopedic surgeon has recommended a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) to improve his quality of life. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies or bleeding disorders. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. He does not have any other significant medical conditions. The patient has been informed about the risks and benefits of the study and has provided written consent to participate.

The patient is a 10-year-old male with a newly diagnosed solid tumor. He has no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. His Karnofsky/Lansky performance score is ≥50 and he is able to tolerate enteral medication administration. He is planned to receive a myelosuppressive chemotherapeutic regimen that includes at least two of the following agents: actinomycin, carboplatin, cisplatin, cyclophosphamide, daunorubicin, doxorubicin, etoposide, ifosfamide, and topotecan. The cycle length is either 14 or 21 days and the regimen will alternate myelosuppressive chemotherapeutic agents in an X-Y-X-Y format, such that the same chemotherapy is given every other cycle. He has no known allergies to soy or any soy-based food or supplement, and is able and willing to comply with all study-related procedures. His parents have given informed consent and he has agreed to assent to the study. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or incarcerated. He has no pre-existing neutropenia, cytopenia, bone marrow failure syndrome, or history of gastric or duodenal ulcers or hyperacidity syndromes. He is not enrolled on a therapeutic or supportive care clinical trial within the last 30 days, and he has no current acute or chronic leukemia diagnosis. He does not require medication dosing via an enteral feeding tube that terminates in the duodenum or jejunum.

The patient is a 75-year-old man diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment. He has reported memory and cognitive complaints and has a clinical dementia rating of 1. He is currently able to perform activities of daily living with a Barthel Index score of 80. The patient does not have any recent history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, or heart surgery, and does not suffer from severe asthma. He has not been diagnosed with any other neurological disorders and does not have any joint deformities that would prevent him from performing exercise or cognitive training. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and is able to follow instructions.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a histologically confirmed advanced malignancy that has progressed following standard therapy. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his cancer has continued to progress. He is willing to undergo a new tumor biopsy at screening and during treatment. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is likely to complete at least 56 days of treatment. He does not have symptomatic or uncontrolled brain metastases and has never received anti-CD73 treatment and/or adenosine receptor A2a (A2aR) inhibitors. He has no history of autoimmune disease within the past 2 years, and his cardiovascular function is normal. He has no active infections and is not currently receiving systemic anti-cancer therapy or chronic steroid therapy. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and understand the risks and benefits of participating in this clinical trial.

As this clinical trial involves collection of tissues from patients undergoing elective neck dissection, it is not appropriate to generate a patient description. The patients will be selected based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria mentioned in the description, and their tissues will be used for analysis.

A 14-year-old male with Nephropathic Cystinosis was diagnosed at the age of 5. He has been compliant with his treatment, which includes cysteamine drops every 6 hours and a low sodium, low protein diet. He has been experiencing deteriorating kidney function with elevated serum creatinine levels and a decline in creatinine clearance estimated by Schwartz Formula. His current creatinine clearance is 50 ml/min/1.73m2. He has no other significant medical history, and his medications include cysteamine drops, sodium bicarbonate, and calcium supplements. He has no known allergies. He has a good understanding of the trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is an adult who has previously participated in the SPD405-309 study and has been exposed to lanthanum carbonate (Fosrenol) for the treatment of hyperphosphatemia. The patient has been compliant with the treatment and has not experienced any adverse events related to the medication during the previous study. The patient has agreed to continue the treatment for an additional 5 years and is willing to undergo regular follow-up visits to monitor for any bone adverse events or other serious adverse events. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

As an observational study, this clinical trial does not require a specific patient description as participants will be selected based on whether they receive a Botox® injection for urinary incontinence in France. However, it is important to note that patients with urinary incontinence associated with overactive bladder, whether due to neurogenic detrusor overactivity or idiopathic overactive bladder, may be eligible to receive Botox® injections as per standard of care in clinical practice in France.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who recently presented with severe back pain. She has a history of smoking and has been diagnosed with osteoporosis. She reports that the pain started suddenly, and it is a constant ache that is exacerbated by movement. She rates the pain as 8 out of 10 on the VAS scale. She underwent diagnostic MRI and disc puncture, which confirmed the diagnosis of acute pyogenic spondylitis of the thoracolumbar spine. Blood cultures and microbiological analysis were also performed. Her vertebral body involvement, as documented on CT, is less than 50% of VB height. She is otherwise healthy and does not report any other significant medical history. She is currently receiving antibiotic treatment for her condition. Her mobility is limited due to the pain, and she is unable to perform daily activities such as cooking and cleaning. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore other treatment options that may improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been diagnosed with psoriasis vulgaris for the past 2 years. She has lesions located on her arms and legs that have been bothering her and impacting her daily life. She has tried different topical treatments in the past, including corticosteroids and vitamin D analogues, but has not seen significant improvement. She has not received any systemic or experimental biological therapies for psoriasis within the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She has no known hypersensitivity to the investigational products and does not have any skin manifestations on the plaque test areas in relation to other dermatological disorders.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who was diagnosed with a recurrence of a CNS tumor. The pathology report confirms the diagnosis. The child has undergone multiple treatments in the past, but the tumor progression continues. The child is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 2 months. The child has not received any myelosuppressive chemotherapy in the past 3 weeks and has demonstrated recovery from the last course of chemotherapy, with an ANC of ≥ 1000/uL. The child has not undergone craniospinal radiation in the past 3 months, and focal radiation in the past 4 weeks. The child is not taking Itraconazole or Phenytoin, and is not on any medication interacting with the CYP3A4 substrate. The child has adequate bone marrow, renal, liver, and pulmonary function. The child is on a stable dose of steroids for more than a week prior to enrollment. The child has a Karnofsky/Lansky score of 50 or greater. The child is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and if of childbearing potential, will practice an effective method of birth control while participating in the study.

The patient is a 62 year old male with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation and coronary artery disease. He has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent implantation. His CHA2DS2VASc score is 3, indicating a high risk for stroke. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of liver or kidney disease, and his GFR is above 60 ml/min/1.73m2. He does not have any bleeding disorders or a history of intracranial or GI bleeding. He is not currently taking any medications that would interact with the study drugs. His platelet count and hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as a retired engineer and is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research.

A 40-year-old male patient with a history of chronic pancreatitis presents with severe and persistent pain in the upper abdomen. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of pain for the past 6 months, despite treatment with pain medications. The patient's medical history includes alcoholism and prior episodes of acute pancreatitis. The patient has undergone previous endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with placement of a plastic pancreatic stent, which provided temporary relief of symptoms.
