The patient has a VAS pain score of 25 and reports pain occurring at least twice a week. Imaging studies reveal a distal dominant stricture with upstream ductal dilation of the pancreatic duct, consistent with Cremer Type IV. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the WallFlex Pancreatic Metal Stent clinical trial and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 38-year-old female runner presents with pain and stiffness in her right Achilles tendon. She has been experiencing symptoms for the past six months and has tried rest, ice, and stretching, but has not seen any improvement. She reports no previous surgeries or corticosteroid injections below the knee. The patient has a normal lipid profile and no history of diabetes or arthritis. Ultrasonography revealed abnormalities in the right Achilles tendon. The patient is willing to comply with both intervention arms of the study.

The patient is a 37-year-old female who has been experiencing vertigo, imbalance, and hearing loss for the past year. She has tried vestibular rehabilitation therapy, which has not improved her symptoms. Further evaluation revealed a dehiscent superior semicircular canal on the left side. The patient has no other significant medical history, is not pregnant, and is in good general health. She is ambulatory and independent in her daily activities. She has agreed to undergo the transmastoid and tegmen mini-craniotomy cartilage cap occlusion surgery to manage her condition.

50 yo female with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis per ACR criteria. The patient has been on methotrexate (MTX) and hydroxychloroquine combination therapy for over 3 months and is willing to take concomitant multivitamin or the equivalent of 400 I.U. vitamin D and the equivalent of 1000 mg of elemental calcium daily. The patient has at least 4 swollen joints and at least 6 tender joints at screening and baseline (28 joint count). The patient also has a CRP > Upper Limit of Normal at screening. The patient has not had a history of clinically significant disease, surgery within the previous 3 months (except for minor dental and cosmetic), history of drug or alcohol abuse, bleeding disorder, gastrointestinal bleeding within 5 years of screening, severe migraines or headaches, glaucoma, active diabetic retinopathy, visually compromising cataract, opportunistic infection within the previous 12 months, active tuberculosis (TB), serious local infection (e.g., cellulitis, abscess) or systemic infection (e.g., septicemia) within 3 months prior to screening, fever or symptomatic viral or bacterial infection within 2 weeks prior to screening, positive for Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody, positive for HBsAg, known positive HIV antibody, or a history of hypersensitivity to glucocorticoids and/or dipyridamole. The patient has not been treated with oral, intra-articular, intramuscular, or intravenous glucocorticoids within 6 weeks prior to screening; inhaled glucocorticoid is permitted. The patient has not been treated with any tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα) biologic, anakinra or abatacept within 2 months prior to screening, rituximab, or another investigational drug 3 months prior to screening. The patient is not being treated with anticoagulants including: dipyridamole, warfarin, clopidogrel, ticlopidine; Acetylsalicylic acid > 150 mg per day. The patient's ALT or AST laboratory values do not exceed 1.5 x ULN, and the patient's HbA1C value is not > 7.0%. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other study with investigational drug or device, is not female and pregnant or lactating, and is willing and able to comply with the requirements of this protocol.

64-year-old male with a history of stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment. Patient reports experiencing chronic pain for the past 3 months, which has been controlled with 60 mg/day morphine equivalent. However, patient reports experiencing 2-3 episodes of breakthrough pain per day, lasting around 30-60 minutes each time. Breakthrough pain is described as sharp, stabbing pain in the chest and back. The pain is severe enough to interfere with daily activities and disrupt sleep. The patient has no known allergies to pain medications and has not received any other pain treatments in the past week. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old male presents with a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and has been experiencing pain and swelling in his right leg for the past few months. On examination, a large mass is palpable in the thigh region. MRI confirms the presence of a high-grade malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST). Biopsy results confirm the diagnosis. The patient has already undergone one cycle of cytotoxic chemotherapy, but the tumor has not responded to the treatment. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently on any medication. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

This is a 34 year old female who presented to the emergency room at Karolinska University hospital Solna within the past 72 hours following a traumatic event. The patient has been diagnosed with PTSD and is eligible for participation in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of modified prolonged exposure therapy in preventing the onset of PTSD. The patient has no ongoing intoxication or serious psychiatric comorbidity that demands attention. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to recall the traumatic event. The patient will undergo evaluation and, if eligible, will be randomly assigned to receive modified prolonged exposure therapy or attention control. The patient will receive three weekly treatment sessions and undergo assessments at 2, 6 (primary endpoint) and 12 months after the intervention. The patient understands that data will be quality monitored by an independent party and that the study will adhere to the Helsinki Declaration.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer that has spread to his liver and bones. He has undergone previous treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has progressed. The patient's physician has recommended participation in a clinical trial that is testing a new treatment called Rhenium 188-P2045. This treatment is designed to attach to type 2 somatostatin receptors that are frequently expressed in small cell lung cancer and other neuroendocrine cancers. This will then deliver radioactivity to kill the cancer cells. The patient will undergo a Tc99 P2045 scan to determine if they have cancers that can be treated with Re188 P2045. If the scan demonstrates that the tumor is positive for SSTR2, the patient will receive Re188 P2045. The goal of this study is to determine the highest dose of Re188 P2045 that can be safely administered after topotecan as well as to determine if topotecan will increase the chance that the tumor will express SSTR2. The patient will be monitored for any side effects of the treatment and follow-up scans will be done to assess the effectiveness of the treatment. The patient will need to use adequate contraception prior to study entry and throughout the duration of the study participation. They will also need to have normal organ and marrow function, be able to understand and sign a written informed consent document, and meet other eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced breast cancer that has relapsed after adjuvant chemotherapy. She is currently undergoing second-line chemotherapy that includes doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1 and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has adequate organ function and her laboratory values are within the acceptable range. She has no active or inactive hepatitis, HIV, or other uncontrolled infectious disease. She has not received radiation therapy in the past 4 weeks. She has not been diagnosed with any other type of cancer in the past 5 years except for superficial non-melanoma skin cancer or cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. She has not shown intolerance to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor treatment. She has not taken any other study drug used in a clinical trial within the past 30 days. She does not have any clinically significant unstable medical abnormality, psychiatric disorder, chronic disease, alcohol or drug use disorder, or other significant biological, psychological, or social factor that could interfere with satisfactory study completion or confound its outcome. She has no unstable heart disease or significant neurological or psychiatric disorders. She does not have poorly controlled hypertriglyceridemia or diabetes. She has not received systemic chemotherapy with doxorubicin anticancer agent to treat metastatic or recurrent breast cancer. She does not have Grade 2 or higher peripheral sensory neuropathy prior to the screening visit or first dosing of the study drug. She has not undergone significant gastrectomy with intractable nausea and vomiting, chronic gastrointestinal disease, or clinically significant sequelae that would interfere with proper absorption of the study drug. She has not been administered with systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to administration of the study drug. She has not received trastuzumab.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a diagnosis of metastatic lung cancer. He has been referred to the palliative care clinic due to his declining health status and increasing symptom burden. Despite being aware of the seriousness of his condition, he has not engaged in any discussions regarding advance care planning. He is able to communicate clearly and has a PPS score of 70. He has a supportive family who are involved in his care and decision-making. He has no history of cognitive impairment or psychiatric treatment. He has not yet signed an advance directive.

This is a 12-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT). He has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to his CKD. He has been experiencing high levels of plasma intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) and has a mean of two consecutive central laboratory iPTH values ≥ 300 pg/mL. His corrected calcium value is ≥ 8.8 mg/dL. He has been receiving standard of care treatment which includes therapy with Vitamin D sterols, calcium supplementation, and phosphate binders. The patient and their parent/legal guardian have provided written informed consent and the patient has provided written assent as required by institutional guidelines. There is no history of congenital long QT syndrome, second or third degree heart block, ventricular tachyarrhythmias or other conditions associated with prolonged QT interval. The corrected QT interval (QTc) is within normal limits. The patient is not on any concomitant medication that may prolong the QTc interval or potent cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) inhibitors.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with gout, with a history of recurrent gout flares in the past year. He has been on allopurinol for the past 6 months, but is still experiencing flares. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His other medical conditions are stable and he is not taking any other medications. He has no known allergies. He has abstained from alcohol and drug use for the past year. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his BMI is 28. He is willing to take colchicine or naproxen to prevent gout flares during the study. He is sexually abstinent and not planning to have children in the next 4 months. The patient understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with them.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who is scheduled to undergo an elective abdominal surgery that is expected to last more than two hours. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, and his current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no known allergies. He has been advised by his surgeon that he may be eligible for a clinical trial that involves an Assisted Fluid Management (AFM) Feature to guide his fluid management during and after surgery. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 38 year old male who has a family history of Huntington's disease (HD). He has recently noticed involuntary movements in his limbs and face that have been getting progressively worse over the last few months. His father was diagnosed with HD at the age of 45 and passed away at the age of 55 due to complications of the disease. He has two siblings, one of whom has tested positive for the HD gene mutation and is showing early signs of the disease. The patient has never been tested for the gene mutation but is concerned about his own risk. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. He enjoys playing tennis and spending time with his family. His BMI is 26 and he has no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance research on HD and potentially contribute to finding a cure for the disease.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with muscle-invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. He has a history of smoking and hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He works as a construction worker and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and fishing. He has a supportive family and is married with two adult children. His physical exam and laboratory studies are unremarkable except for anemia (Hgb 9.5 g/dL) and leukopenia (WBC 2,500/mm³). He is currently receiving his third course of neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and cisplatin. He is willing and fit to receive a fourth course of chemotherapy according to the study protocol. He has no prior history of malignancy except for superficial TCC. He does not have untreated hydronephrosis or contraindications to radical radiotherapy. He has not received prior pelvic radiotherapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with low to intermediate risk prostate cancer. He has opted to manage his condition with active surveillance and has been on this management program for the past 8 months. He had a recent mpMRI scan which showed a detectable lesion with an M score of 4 using Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PIRADS) version 2 reporting criteria. The patient has no contraindications to apalutamide and has a normal full blood count, renal and liver function tests. He has not had any prior systemic therapy or androgen deprivation therapy. The patient is alert and oriented, with no neurological deficits, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status is 1. He is willing to participate in the trial and has given informed consent. The patient has no pelvic or hip metalwork and is able to undergo a prostate 3T mpMRI scan.

A 54-year-old man with a history of Type 2 diabetes and stable CAD, who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity for the past few months. He was evaluated by his cardiologist and underwent a coronary arteriogram which showed significant stenosis in one of his arteries. The cardiologist recommended either initial elective revascularization with aggressive medical therapy or aggressive medical therapy alone, with equal probability. The patient agreed to participate in the BARI 2D trial and was randomized to the revascularization and insulin providing (IP) strategy of glycemic control, with a target HbA1c level of less than 7.0%. He has been compliant with the treatment regimen and has reported improvement in his symptoms. He is able to perform all tasks related to glycemic control and risk factor management. He has no history of bypass surgery or prior catheter-based intervention within the 12 months before study entry. He does not have class III or IV CHF, creatinine greater than 2.0 mg/dL, or HbA1c greater than 13%. He does not require major vascular surgery concomitant with revascularization and does not have left main stenosis greater than or equal to 50%. He does not have non-cardiac illness expected to limit survival, hepatic disease, or fasting triglycerides greater than 1000 mg/dL in the presence of moderate glycemic control. He has no current alcohol abuse or chronic steroid use. He is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant within the next five years. He is able to understand and cooperate with protocol requirements and is geographically accessible for follow-up.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She is experiencing breathing difficulties and is currently receiving oxygen therapy. She has a past medical history of asthma and hypertension. She is married and lives with her husband and two children. She works as a nurse in a hospital and was exposed to the virus during her work. She has not received any experimental treatment for COVID-19 before. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. Her laboratory tests show a white blood cell count within normal range and her serum ferritin level is below 2000 mcg/ml. She is not currently taking any medications, including steroids or lithium carbonate. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old African American male who has been smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He works as a construction worker and is physically active at work, but does not engage in regular exercise outside of work. He is married with two children and is the primary breadwinner for his family. He is interested in quitting smoking for his health and for financial reasons. He is willing to take medication to quit smoking and is able to attend all study visits.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the hospital for orthopedic surgery on his left hip due to osteoarthritis. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He is a retired construction worker and is married with two grown children. He has never participated in a clinical trial before. He understands and speaks English fluently and is able to understand pain assessments. He is able to wear a motion tracking device on his wrist and is under the care of the acute pain service.

A 52-year-old female with metastatic breast cancer, who has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy and hormone therapy without success, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has no other known malignancies and meets all other inclusion criteria. She has measurable disease according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and has adequate organ and marrow function. She is sexually active and agrees to use medically acceptable methods of contraception during the course of the study and for at least 11 days after the last dose of study treatment. She tests negative for pregnancy at screening. She has not received any other investigational agents within 28 days of the first dose of the study drug and has recovered from any adverse events due to previous investigational or other agents administered more than 28 days prior to study enrollment. She has no uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses such as ongoing or active infection, diabetes, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, or cardiac arrhythmia. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not known to be positive for the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). She has no allergies or hypersensitivity to components of the cobimetinib formulation.

The patient is a 45 year-old male who underwent a liver transplant 12 weeks ago due to liver failure caused by chronic hepatitis B. He has been taking tacrolimus twice daily since the transplant surgery, and his average trough level has been between 3-10 ng/mL. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 28 days and is not taking any forbidden concomitant medications. He has normal renal function and hepatic function. He has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders. He is capable of understanding the purpose and risks of the study and has given written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma on her scalp. The affected area is approximately 3 cm in diameter and located on the top of her head. The patient has no other medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. She is concerned about the potential scarring and prolonged wound healing associated with conventional wound closure methods. The patient has intact skin surrounding the wound for at least 2.5 cm. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for wound closure using the SUTUREGARD device for a specified time period. The patient is informed that there may be some discomfort during the procedure and that she will be monitored for any adverse effects. She understands that her participation is voluntary and that she may withdraw at any time without affecting her medical care.

A 9-year-old boy with spastic cerebral palsy is experiencing limited range of motion in his ankles, which affects his ability to walk and participate in physical activities. He has difficulty dorsiflexing his ankles, and his parents have noticed that he tends to walk on his toes. He has never undergone surgery on his lower limbs, and has not received botulinum toxin injections or elongation casts in the past three months. He does not currently take any analgesic medications. His past medical history is significant for cerebral palsy diagnosis at age 2, and he has been undergoing physical therapy for several years. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. He enjoys playing soccer and basketball with his friends, but is limited by his ankle stiffness. His parents are interested in exploring new treatment options to improve his mobility and quality of life.

45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage I HER2/neu positive breast cancer after a mammogram found an abnormality. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary node dissection with clear margins and negative lymph nodes. She has no significant past medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 0. Her labs are normal, including a normal echocardiogram. She is not pregnant or nursing and agrees to use effective birth control during the study. She has no history of peripheral neuropathy, chemotherapy, or other active serious infections.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has had recurrent warts on her hands and fingers for the past 2 years. She has tried various over-the-counter treatments, including salicylic acid and cryotherapy, but the warts keep coming back. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her occupation is a preschool teacher. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to try a new treatment option. She does not have any known allergies to Candida antigen or any other medications. She has not had a fever or any immunosuppressive disorders. She has not received any wart therapy in the past month.

78-year-old male diagnosed with heart failure presents to the heart failure clinic for the first time. He is a retired accountant and lives alone in a small apartment. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He reports difficulty adhering to his sodium restricted diet due to lack of knowledge about low sodium food choices. He has tried to reduce his sodium intake by avoiding salty snacks, but he still experiences shortness of breath and swelling in his legs. He is willing to participate in the study and learn about color-coded cue cards for selecting low sodium foods. He speaks fluent English and is physically able to go grocery shopping.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He had a history of multiple abdominal surgeries due to a perforated appendix, and he had undergone a laparotomy for recurrent adhesions. During his current admission, it was discovered that he had developed an enterocutaneous fistula with an output of approximately 200cc/day. His vital signs were stable, and he was otherwise healthy. He agreed to participate in the clinical trial to determine the efficacy of VAC therapy devices in promoting closure of enterocutaneous fistulae. He has no prior history of abdominal radiation or any distal obstruction, entero-atmospheric fistula, or any intra-abdominal or metastatic cancer.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of a non-progressive spinal cord injury at the level of C4 due to a motor vehicle accident. He has been classified as ASIA C and has been living with the injury for over a year now. The patient has mild spasticity in his lower extremities but it does not interfere with his daily activities. He is not currently taking any spasticity management medications but has been taking over-the-counter pain medications occasionally for lower back pain. The patient is medically stable and able to comply with the protocol requirements. He is interested in the clinical trial to evaluate the effects of acute intermittent hypoxia therapy on his spinal cord injury. The patient has no history of sleep apnea or any other medical conditions that may affect his participation in the study. He is not currently involved in any other movement research study or therapy program and is not planning on becoming pregnant.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who was involved in a car accident two days ago. She was the driver of the car and was hit on the driver's side by another car traveling at a high speed. She was wearing her seatbelt at the time of the accident. She was taken to the emergency department and was found to have a pelvic ring fracture. She was admitted to the hospital and underwent a CT scan to further evaluate the extent of the fracture. She is currently experiencing moderate to severe pain in her pelvic region and has limited mobility. She has no significant past medical or surgical history and is not taking any prescription medications. She is fluent in French and has provided consent to participate in the study.

A 12-year-old boy was recently diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (DM) after experiencing symptoms of polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss. He has no family history of DM or Celiac Disease (CD). He has not taken antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors, aspirin, or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs recently and has not had any alcohol intake within the past 48 hours. He has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery before, nor is he currently on antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. His parents are also willing to provide consent for him to participate.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with end-stage heart failure who is undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation as a bridge to heart transplant. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus that are well controlled with medications. He has no history of cerebrovascular disease or neurological deficits. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, aspirin, and clopidogrel. He has been experiencing worsening shortness of breath and fatigue, which prompted evaluation by a cardiologist. His echocardiogram revealed severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 10%. The patient has been deemed a suitable candidate for LVAD implantation, and he will be monitored closely after the surgery for any complications. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study, and he understands that his medical treatment will not deviate from the standard of clinical care.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with the KRAS G12C mutation. She has received platinum-containing chemotherapy and an anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD1/PDL1) antibody, but her disease has progressed. She is now ineligible for standard treatment options and is seeking alternative treatments. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise in good health. She has the ability to take an orally administered drug and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. She has not had prior treatment with an inhibitor specific to KRAS G12C and has not had any solid organ transplantation. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 28 year old woman who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing solid food for the past few months. She has visited several doctors who have not been able to provide any relief. Further evaluation shows that she has been diagnosed with eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) with an esophageal peak eosinophil count (PEC) of 20 eosinophils per high powered field (eos/hpf). She experiences dysphagia, defined as solid food going down slowly or getting stuck in the throat with an average frequency of 3 episodes per week over 2 weeks during the Screening period. She has not undergone dilation of an esophageal stricture within 12 weeks prior to Screening EGD, nor has she used corticosteroids for the treatment of EoE within 8 weeks prior to Screening EGD. She is not on any protocol-specified immunomodulatory therapies within the protocol-specified timeframe prior to Baseline (eg, dupilumab, benralizumab, omalizumab, or infliximab within 12 weeks; a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator at any time). She is not pregnant and is willing to comply with all study visits and procedures for the Extension Treatment Period.

A 65-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy and permanent atrial fibrillation presents with worsening dyspnea on exertion, fatigue, and decreased exercise tolerance. He has been on optimal medical therapy for his heart failure for the last 6 months with no significant improvement in his symptoms. His echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30% and a left ventricular end-diastolic diameter of 60 mm. His ECG reveals a wide QRS complex of 140 msec. The patient is classified as NYHA class III and has been experiencing symptoms for over 6 months. The patient is an appropriate candidate for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) and is being considered for the Spanish Atrial Fibrillation and Resynchronization Study.

A 50-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician due to the persistent pain associated with fibromyalgia. She has had the symptoms for 3 years and has been diagnosed by a rheumatologist. She complains of chronic pain, fatigue, and tenderness throughout her body. She has a history of cervical and lumbar pain. She is currently not on any opioids. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day and has tried various treatments, including massage therapy and acupuncture, but with limited success. She works as an accountant and her symptoms make it difficult to focus on her work. She is married and has two children. She does not smoke and is not on any medications. Her past surgical history is significant for a hysterectomy.

Patient is a 27yo male with a history of non-affective psychotic disorder, currently prescribed antipsychotic medication. The patient has experienced 2 episodes of psychosis in the past 2 years, including an index episode, and has had contact with mental health services. The patient reports experiencing basic symptoms such as increased vividness of color vision and mild subjective cognitive problems. The patient is fluent in English and has a fixed abode. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to use a mobile phone app to monitor basic symptoms, conventional early signs, and relapse over an extended period.

The patient is a 28 year-old pregnant woman living in a rural community in Kenya. This is her second pregnancy and she has had a healthy pregnancy so far. She has received some prenatal care at a local clinic, but is interested in joining a community-led peer-support group called Chama cha MamaToto. She is excited to learn more about health, social, and financial literacy and hopes to meet other pregnant women in her community. She has a supportive partner and family, and is interested in participating in a savings/loans program to help with expenses related to her pregnancy and newborn. She is open to being part of a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of chamas.

A 45-year-old male with bilateral post-lingual hearing loss is seeking treatment options to improve his hearing. He is currently using hearing aids but is experiencing difficulty understanding speech and hearing in noisy environments. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the behavior of the long latency Auditory Evoked Potential (P300) in individuals with unilateral Cochlear Implant (CI). He has no history of prelingual hearing loss or any other significant medical conditions. He is willing to undergo CI surgery and participate in the P300 testing before and after the surgery. He is hoping that this study can contribute to the understanding of the mechanisms of brain plasticity involved in the recovery of hearing function after CI surgery.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male presents with complaints of fatigue, bloating, and discomfort in the upper right quadrant of his abdomen. He has a history of being overweight and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. He reports drinking alcohol 2-3 times a week, but denies any significant alcohol intake within the past 2 years. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with losartan. He denies any history of liver disease, hepatitis, or drug use. On physical examination, he has a tender, slightly enlarged liver. Laboratory tests reveal elevated liver enzymes (ALT 65 U/L, AST 55 U/L) and a platelet count of 150,000/μL. Abdominal ultrasound shows evidence of fatty liver disease. He has no history of autoimmune disease, diabetes, or HIV, and his medications are limited to losartan for hypertension. He is willing to maintain the same lifestyle during the clinical trial period and has given his voluntary consent to participate in the trial. He meets all of the inclusion criteria, and none of the exclusion criteria.

55-year-old female with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnosed two years ago. The patient has been treated with one prior regimen of chemotherapy without significant improvement. The patient was previously tested negative for ALK mutation (Group A). The patient presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. CT scan reveals a new metastatic lesion in the liver. The patient has ECOG performance status of 1, adequate bone marrow, renal, liver, and pancreatic function. The patient has not received any prior systemic treatment for advanced or metastatic disease, and there is mandatory tumor tissue available for analysis. The patient has no significant medical conditions, gastrointestinal abnormalities, or cardiac history. The patient is not currently experiencing any active infection requiring systemic therapy and has not undergone any organ transplantations or allogenic stem cell transplantation.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with light chain (AL) amyloidosis nine months ago and has been participating in the NEOD001-001 study. He has completed the treatment and is willing to continue with the open-label extension study. His bone marrow reserve, hepatic and renal function are adequate as demonstrated by ANC of 1.2 ×109/L, platelet count of 85 × 109/L, hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, total bilirubin of 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (× ULN), and AST/ALT levels within normal limits. His seated systolic blood pressure is between 90 to 180 mmHg and his ECOG Performance Status is 1. He has agreed to use highly effective physician-approved contraception from 30 days prior to the first study drug administration to 90 days following the last study drug administration. He has not received any anticancer therapy within the last 14 days and has fully recovered from the toxic effects of any prior treatment. He has not undergone any major surgery, radiotherapy, or transplant within the specified time frame. He has no history of infusion-associated adverse events or hypersensitivities to NEOD001 or any of its excipients. He does not have any secondary malignancy, uncontrolled infection, or uncontrolled symptomatic orthostatic hypotension. He has no history of myocardial infarction, uncontrolled angina, severe uncontrolled ventricular arrhythmias, or electrocardiographic evidence of acute ischemia within the last 6 months. He is not lactating or HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C positive. Overall, he meets the eligibility criteria for the open-label extension study of NEOD001 in subjects with light chain (AL) amyloidosis.

A 25-year-old man was brought to the hospital after a car accident that left him with a traumatic spinal cord injury. He is currently experiencing complete motor loss below T6 level and is diagnosed with ASIA A. His blood pressure upon admission was 110/70 mmHg. His medical history is unremarkable, and he does not have any known allergies. He is not currently taking any medications. He has no history of substance abuse or dependency. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial.

A 5-year-old boy was diagnosed with moderate to severe motor impairment due to an acquired brain injury 2 years ago. His injury was a result of a car accident that left him with significant physical limitations, including difficulty with gross motor function. He has been receiving physiotherapy treatment for the past year, but his progress has been slow. His parents are eager to explore alternative treatments that may help improve his motor function. He has no history of visual or hearing loss, and has not been diagnosed with any other neurological or developmental disorders. He meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and his parents are interested in enrolling him in the experimental group to receive tRNS Brain Noninvasive Stimulation in addition to his physiotherapy treatment.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was previously diagnosed with clear cell ovarian cancer. Her cancer has returned and spread, and she is experiencing progression of the disease. She has already undergone one platinum-based chemotherapy regimen for her primary disease, but it was not successful in stopping the cancer from coming back. She has measurable disease as defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her lab results show that she has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,900/mcl, platelets greater than or equal to 100,000/mcl, leukocytes of 4,000/mcL, hemoglobin of 11 g/dL, serum albumin of 3.2 g/dL, prothrombin time (PT) such that international normalized ratio (INR) is less than or equal to 1.3 x upper limit of normal (ULN), partial thromboplastin time (PTT) less than or equal to 1.3 x ULN, creatinine of 1.1 times the ULN, bilirubin less than or equal to 1.5 ULN, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) less than or equal to 2.5 times the ULN. She has had no major surgical procedures or significant traumatic injuries within the past 28 days. She is able to swallow pills.

A 55-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years is seeking to improve his blood sugar control. He has health insurance coverage within Ontario and lives in the Hamilton region. He is currently registered in Diabetes Hamilton and has access to mail and the internet at home. His baseline A1c is 8%, higher than the recommended target of less than 7%. He is able to read and understand English and willing to provide informed consent to participate in the trial. He is not currently pregnant and does not reside in an institution that provides diabetes care. He is not cohabiting with any study participant and does not reside outside the city of Hamilton. He is willing to comply with the protocol and follow the personalized diabetes self-management recommendations and feedback provided by the trial.

The patient is a 64 year old man who has been experiencing severe hip pain for the past year, which has significantly affected his mobility and quality of life. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the hip joint and is scheduled for a total hip replacement surgery via lateral approach. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is on medication for both conditions. He has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 25 and his platelet count is within normal limits. He has never had any neurological/neuromuscular or psychiatric diseases and is able to comprehend the study requirements. He has never had any opioid dependence and is not allergic to any medications. He has agreed to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

A 68-year-old man presents with concerns about his overall physical health and mobility. He has noticed a decline in his strength and endurance in recent years, and wants to maintain his independence for as long as possible. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of heart disease or stroke, and has never smoked. He is retired and lives alone, but has a good support system of friends and family. He is interested in participating in a study that could help him improve his muscle health and function. He is able to sign informed consent and is free-living prior to admission. He is not on a weight-loss diet and has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He has no history of cancer, respiratory disease, or liver disease. He is not currently taking corticosteroids, and has not taken androgens or growth hormone within the past 6 months. He is not currently on anticoagulant therapy or any medication that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive breast cancer in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast. She underwent a lumpectomy with negative margins and has not received any adjuvant therapy. The tumor size measured 3.5 cm before surgery, and she has no evidence of lymph node involvement. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoporosis. She is currently taking lisinopril and calcium supplements. Her height is 5'4'' and weight is 135 lbs. Her vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, she has no evidence of skin involvement or connective tissue disorders. She is comfortable in the prone position, and her breast size is adequate for the breast immobilization device. She has no history of psychiatric or addictive disorders that would preclude obtaining informed consent. She is willing to use an effective contraceptive method during the study. She has not received radiation therapy to the involved breast and does not have any physical disability that would prevent her from being set up in the prone position.

Patient is a 47-year-old man diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in 2017. He underwent radiation and temozolomide (TMZ) therapy after his initial surgery. He also received bevacizumab therapy for a minimum of 8 weeks, but his GBM progressed following this treatment. His baseline MRI shows progression of the disease. The patient had a recent resection of recurrent tumor and has recovered from surgery. He has a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) of 80 and a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. Laboratory tests show adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient has not received prior treatment with TPI 287, and has not been enrolled in Protocol No. TPI-287-17. The patient is willing to abstain from sex or use adequate contraception for the duration of the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study drug. The patient has signed and dated informed consent form prior to screening evaluations.

A 32-year-old male was involved in a motorcycle accident resulting in severe traumatic brain injury. He was admitted to the ICU with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) of 6, intubated, and mechanically ventilated with invasive arterial pressure monitoring. He has a history of duodenal ulcer and is currently taking acetylsalicylic acid for chronic headaches. His platelet count is within normal limits, and his liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. He is not currently in a barbiturate coma. He is not pregnant.

A 12-year-old girl presents with a history of mother's multiple sclerosis (MS), diagnosed 13 years ago, and treated with methylprednisolone (MP) for relapses during pregnancy. The girl was born full-term without any perinatal complications. The girl's mother received high doses of MP (1000mg over 3-5 days) for relapse treatment during pregnancy. The girl's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is an alert female with no acute distress. Her BP: 120/80, HR: 80/min, and BMI: 22. Her physical examination is normal. The girl and her legal guardians have given written consent to participate in the study. The girl is eligible for the "Effects of a Multiple Sclerosis Relapse Therapy on Offspring Neurocognitive Development and Behaviour" clinical trial, which aims to examine the effects of prenatal MP exposure on offspring structural and functional brain development, stress sensitivity, and cognitive and behavioural performance.

A 9-year-old boy visits the clinic with his parents stating that he is having difficulty hearing in one ear since birth. His parents also report that his speech development is slower than his peers. The boy underwent a hearing test, which confirmed sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear. He was then referred to a specialist who performed an MRI that revealed an enlarged vestibular aqueduct. The specialist informed the family about a clinical trial that aims to identify the genetic factors responsible for the inner ear malformation associated with hearing loss. The family is interested in participating in the trial as they want to understand the cause of their son's hearing loss and how it may affect his overall health. The boy's parents and siblings are willing to undergo the necessary tests and procedures to assist in the study.

Maria is a 28-year-old woman who is 6 weeks pregnant. She presented to the clinic with vaginal bleeding and pelvic cramping. She has a positive history of a previous ectopic pregnancy that was treated with methotrexate. She is married and has two children. She has no history of chronic illness or hospitalization. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. Her family history is negative for any significant medical or genetic conditions. She has not participated in any research studies in the past 6 months. Her serum human chorionic gonadotropin level confirms her pregnancy, and an ultrasound is performed to diagnose her pregnancy location. The ultrasound shows a gestational sac in her right fallopian tube, confirming her diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy.

A 42-year-old male patient is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic nephrectomy due to a large renal tumor. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke, consume alcohol or use any illicit drugs. He works as a sales representative and exercises regularly. He has no family history of renal disease and has never had any prior surgeries. He weighs 80 kg and is 6 feet tall. On physical examination, his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 70 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no palpable masses or organomegaly. Laboratory tests show that his serum creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR is 90 ml/min/1.73m2, and his electrolytes, liver function tests, and complete blood count are all within normal limits. He has no proteinuria or hematuria. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department complaining of shortness of breath. She reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been experiencing shortness of breath for the past two days and has noticed an increase in swelling in her ankles. She denies chest pain or pressure. On examination, she is found to have a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation of 90% on room air, and bilateral crackles on lung auscultation. She is hemodynamically stable. She is a potential candidate for the clinical trial assessing the economic impact of BNP assay in elderly dyspneic patients presenting to the emergency department.

An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and diabetes. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to exacerbations of his COPD, which have resulted in shortness of breath and difficulty with daily activities. His daughter, who lives in another state, is concerned about his ability to live independently and is interested in exploring home automation and telemonitoring options to help him stay in his own home. The patient is able to perform most activities of daily living, but reports having some difficulty with mobility and falls frequently. He has already installed some home automation devices, such as a smart thermostat and a security system, but is interested in expanding this technology to help manage his chronic conditions. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of automation tools and telemonitoring in improving his quality of life and reducing the risk of hospitalization.

Patient is a 25-year-old healthy male from the United States who works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His BMI is 22.0 kg/m^2. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical examination and laboratory tests are within normal limits, including a normal 12-lead ECG. He is willing to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures and is willing to use adequate contraception during and for up to 3 months after participation in the study. He provides signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain in her legs for the past 6 months. She has been previously diagnosed with lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) based on an MRI scan that shows narrowing of the central canal and foramen. She has been experiencing persistent neurogenic claudication and has difficulty walking for more than a few minutes without experiencing pain in her legs. She has been on stable pharmacological treatment for pain and sleep disorders for the past 2 months. She reports an average pain intensity score of 7 out of 10 on the Visual Analog Scale during walking. She has no other neurological or psychiatric disorders but has a history of migraines. She has not had any head trauma resulting in a loss of consciousness, epilepsy, neurosurgical intervention, or intracranial hypertension. She is not pregnant and does not have any other medical conditions that would be considered absolute or relative contraindications for tDCS.

45-year-old male with a history of colon cancer and permanent central venous catheter placement for chemotherapy. The patient was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and redness at the site of the catheter. Blood cultures were positive for Staphylococcus aureus, and the patient was started on antibiotics. Despite antibiotic therapy, the patient continued to have symptoms and imaging studies were inconclusive for catheter infection. The patient is being considered for catheter removal, but the potential risks and costs associated with the procedure are a concern. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the diagnostic value of PET/CT and microcalorimetry in detecting catheter infection, and potentially avoiding unnecessary catheter removal. Past Medical History: - Colon cancer - Permanent central venous catheter placement for chemotherapy - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - No known drug allergies - Non-smoker

The patient is a 30-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with Adult Onset Still's Disease (AOSD). He has been experiencing recurring fever, joint pain, and a typical rash for the past few weeks. He has undergone treatment with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and glucocorticoids, but his symptoms have not improved. He has not received any conventional or biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in the past. He has no history of any other serious chronic-inflammatory diseases or active infections. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 9000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl

65 year-old male diagnosed with metastatic GastroIntestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST) in [**4-12**]. He underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor and was started on imatinib 400mg orally once daily. He has been on imatinib for the past 12 years with no recurrence of the tumor. He has been followed up regularly with imaging studies to monitor for any disease progression. He is currently in good health and able to read and answer questionnaires. He has agreed to participate in this study and has provided written informed consent. Past Medical History: Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite dietary and exercise therapy for the past 6 weeks, the patient has been unable to control his blood glucose levels effectively, with FPG levels ranging up to 270mg/dL at screening. The patient has not received any oral anti-hyperglycemic drugs for the past 6 weeks and is not currently on insulin therapy. The patient's BMI is within the range of 20.0kg/m2 to 40.0kg/m2. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 62 year old woman has been suffering from chronic knee pain for the past 5 years which has progressed to the point that she is now having difficulty walking and performing daily activities. She has been taking strong opioids daily for the past 6 months to manage her pain. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. Her BMI is 30 and she does not have any history of alcohol or substance abuse. She has not been diagnosed with any cognitive dysfunction or malignancy. She has been recommended total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as a treatment option for her condition. She has agreed to participate in this study to evaluate the efficacy of preopioid versus nonopioid pain management in TKA.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a vaccine for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS). She has no history of chronic or acute illnesses, and her medical exams and laboratory tests have no significant findings. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. She has not received any immunosuppressive or cytotoxic medications, blood products, or immunoglobulin in the past six months. She has not received any live attenuated vaccines in the past 30 days or medically indicated subunit or killed vaccines in the past 14 days. She has no history of serious adverse reactions to vaccines, autoimmune disease, asthma, diabetes mellitus, thyroidectomy, serious angioedema episodes, hypertension, bleeding disorder, malignancy, seizure disorder, asplenia, or psychiatric conditions. She is willing to receive HIV test results and donate blood for sample storage to be used for future research. She agrees to consistently practice contraception using a barrier method for at least 21 days prior to enrollment and through Week 32 of the study. She is willing to comply with the study schedule, which includes nine clinic visits and three telephone follow-up contacts, and to report any symptoms to a study physician.

8-year-old male with good general health and cooperative behavior, presenting with at least one molar affected by Molar-Incisor Hypomineralisation (MIH). The patient's parents or legal guardians have given informed consent for the child to participate in the trial. The child has not undergone orthodontic treatment and does not have any health conditions that would impair dental treatment. The MIH molar does not have any post-eruptive breakdown, occlusal surface is not covered by a gingival operculum, and does not have any caries dentine lesion (ICCMS score C), restorations or sealants. The child is willing to assent to participate in the research.

The patient is a 40-year-old man with end-stage renal disease who has been on hemodialysis for the past year. He has been on the waiting list for a cadaveric kidney transplant for the past 6 months. He has a history of high blood pressure and diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medications for these conditions. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for a slightly elevated creatinine level. He meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and has agreed to participate.

A 25-year-old male presents as a healthy individual with no known medical conditions. He does not smoke or drink and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction or abuse. He has not taken any systemic prescription medication in the past 14 days and has not donated blood or plasma recently. He is willing to abstain from donating blood or plasma for four weeks after completing the study. He is sexually active, but not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to practice an acceptable barrier method of birth control for the duration of the study if female and of childbearing potential. He will undergo screening procedures, including general observations, physical examination, and clinical laboratory procedures to ensure he meets the inclusion criteria. If selected for the study, he will receive a single oral dose of either 10 mg Citalopram Hydrobromide tablets by Purepac Pharmaceutical Co or 10 mg CELEXATM tablets distributed and marketed by Forest Pharmaceuticals, Inc. under fasting conditions. He will be closely monitored for any adverse reactions and will be advised not to donate blood or plasma for four weeks after completing the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with rectal cancer based on the results of a biopsy. She has no prior history of abdominal or pelvic surgery and is classified as ASA score 2. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. She has no other significant medical conditions and takes no other medications. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the possibility of using the Micro Hand S robot for her rectal cancer surgery. She is willing to undergo a retrospective study for this purpose and has no other plans for surgery or treatment at this time.

The patient is a 56-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with multiple myeloma. She is fluent in English and has no difficulty reading or writing in the language. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that she is fully active but may experience symptoms with strenuous activity. The patient has not previously practiced Tai Chi, Qi Gong, or Yoga, and is not currently experiencing any syncopal events or Grade 3 or higher neuropathy. She has no history of major depressive disorder or anxiety disorder, nor does she have chronic dizziness or vestibular disorders. The patient has been referred to the clinical trial by the BMT transplant coordinator staff at Mayo Clinic Arizona and is currently undergoing evaluation for autologous stem cell transplant. She has expressed an interest in participating in the study and is willing to attend the training session per study protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing difficulty with walking and feels that his gait has become shuffling and slow. He reports that he has been mostly sedentary for the past 3 months and has not engaged in any regular physical activity. The patient uses no walking aids and has not experienced any falls in the last 12 months. He has been on anti-Parkinsonian medication for the past 3 weeks and has adapted to the medication. He has no other neurological or musculoskeletal conditions affecting walking. The patient has no history of chest pain at rest or during exercise in the last 3 months, and has not had any heart attack, angioplasty, or heart surgery in the last 6 months. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 28. He is interested in participating in a home-based treadmill walking program to improve his walking capacity and quality of life.

25F diagnosed with asthma at the age of 10, currently on inhaled corticosteroids and a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) for rescue. The patient reports frequent episodes of shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing despite being on medication. She has a history of poor inhaler technique and has difficulty coordinating her breathing while inhaling medication. She has missed work and school due to asthma exacerbations. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. She has not taken any investigational drugs in the past 30 days and is not taking any medications that would exclude her from the study. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to improve her asthma management and is able to comply with the study requirements.

There are no specific patient descriptions for this clinical trial as the study uses archived plasma samples for evaluation purposes. The samples were collected from individuals from different geographic regions, including Nigeria, Georgia, Cambodia, and Belgium, and have already been characterized for HCV, HIV, and HBV serology status using approved diagnostic assays. The study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance and operational characteristics of 13 different HCV RDTs on these archived samples, including those from patients with or without HIV co-infection. Therefore, the study does not involve any direct patient recruitment or enrollment.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male, a heavy smoker for the past 10 years, presents with a persistent cough and difficulty breathing. The patient reports smoking at least 20 cigarettes a day and has tried to quit smoking several times but has failed. He reports no significant medical history and takes no medications. The patient is fluent in English and provides written informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. He has a baseline CO reading of 17ppm at the intake session, which is greater than 10ppm, making him eligible for the study. The patient's blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate are within the normal range, and he has no history of substance abuse, including alcohol, opioids, cocaine, marijuana, or stimulants. He does not have any contraindications to transdermal nicotine use based on his medical history, and he has no history of abnormal heart rhythms, tachycardia, and cardiovascular disease. He also does not have any history of major depression or suicidal attempts. The patient is not currently taking any smoking cessation medication or receiving treatment for smoking cessation or research program. However, he has used nicotine replacement therapy in the past, which makes him ineligible for the study. The patient is willing to provide a blood sample to assess the nicotine metabolite ratio and is committed to living in the area for the next 12 months.

A 35-year-old male presents with a history of ADHD, diagnosed at the age of 8. He reports difficulty staying focused and completing tasks at work, which has led to poor job performance and frequent reprimands from his supervisor. The patient is currently not on any medication for his ADHD and is unsatisfied with his current treatment plan. He has a total ADHD-5-RS score of 26, indicating moderate to severe impairment. The patient is physically and mentally competent, with an IQ score of 90 based on the KBIT-2. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and has signed the informed consent document. The patient has no known allergies to methylphenidate or amphetamines and has not experienced serious adverse reactions to methylphenidate in the past. He has no history of hypertension or clinically significant ECG abnormalities. However, he is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is not homeless and is able to attend all required visits.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl complaining of muffled hearing and pressure in her right ear. She reports that she has had a cold for the past week and her symptoms have not improved with over-the-counter medications. She has no history of ear infections or surgeries. Upon examination, there is a mild erythema of the right tympanic membrane and the mobility of the tympanic membrane is restricted. Tympanometry shows negative pressure in the right ear. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. She is willing to discontinue breastfeeding if applicable. The patient's parents have provided consent for their child to participate in this clinical trial.

A 52-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of chronic back pain. He has been experiencing this pain for several years and it has been affecting his work and daily activities. He has tried taking pain medications, but the relief is only temporary. He has also tried chiropractic treatment, but he did not notice any significant changes. He is currently not taking any medications for pain. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known history of neurological disorders. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he is hopeful that OMT will improve his cognitive function in addition to relieving his pain.

The patient is a 37-year-old woman who has been experiencing heartburn and acid regurgitation for the past 6 months. She has tried over-the-counter antacids and lifestyle modifications, but her symptoms have not improved. She visited a gastroenterologist and underwent an endoscopic examination which confirmed a diagnosis of erosive esophagitis (EE). She was prescribed a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) for 8 weeks and underwent a follow-up endoscopy which showed healing of the esophageal mucosa. She continued on maintenance therapy and had another follow-up endoscopy which showed no further erosions. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable and she is not pregnant or lactating. She does not have a history of gastrointestinal cancers, esophageal foreign bodies, neoplasms, gastric or esophageal surgery, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, primary esophageal motility disorders, esophageal strictures, or eosinophilic esophagitis. She has not been hospitalized for GERD as a primary or secondary diagnosis.

A 46-year old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 5 years ago. She has been on methotrexate therapy for the last 2 years with no major complaints. She experiences occasional mild pain in her hands and feet. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently controlled with medications. She lives with her husband and two children. She works as a teacher and is able to perform her job well. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is currently not taking any biologic therapy for her RA. Her DAS28 score is 2.7, indicating low disease activity. She has not experienced any cardiovascular events in the past. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the potential benefit of adalimumab therapy in reducing her cardiovascular risk. She is able to administer subcutaneous injections herself or has a caregiver who can assist her. She is willing to use a reliable method of birth control during the study period. She has normal renal function and fulfills all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer after presenting with urinary frequency and urgency, nocturia and hesitancy. He has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He is engaged to be married and has expressed concerns about his fertility. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level was 8 ng/mL and biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 7 (3+4). His clinical stage was T1c. After discussing treatment options with his urologist, he has opted for brachytherapy. He is able to ejaculate and has provided written informed consent for the study. He has never had any history of infertility or vasectomy. He has not undergone previous chemotherapy or pelvic radiotherapy, nor has he used androgen deprivation therapy or alpha blockers. He has not used 5 alpha-reductase inhibitors within the last 4 months. He will undergo both high dose rate and low dose rate brachytherapy and will have his sperm count and quality evaluated before and after the treatment.

The adult patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian female with a history of ligneous conjunctivitis since birth. She experiences recurrent episodes of conjunctival inflammation and thickening of the eyelids which impairs her vision. She also has a history of recurrent sinus infections, difficulty breathing and swallowing due to involvement of the nasopharynx and tracheobronchial tree. In addition to these symptoms, she has experienced difficulty with wound healing and has had multiple surgeries to address obstructions in her gastrointestinal and urinary tracts. She has provided informed consent to participate in this study and is diagnosed with compound homozygous Type 1 plasminogen deficiency.

A 50-year old female was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She lives with her husband and their two teenage children. The patient is scheduled for breast surgery with axillary lymphnode dissection. She is experiencing lymphorrhea, which is causing her discomfort and inconvenience. Her surgeon has informed her about the clinical trial for the extended-release of Octreotide (LF-PB) and recommended she consider participating. The patient is interested in exploring all possible treatment options to manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is capable of understanding the details of the trial. The patient is not pregnant and has negative serum pregnancy test. She has not undergone previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy within five years and does not have any significant medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

John is a 35 year old man who was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been struggling with hallucinations and delusions for the past year, which has made it difficult for him to work and maintain social relationships. He has been hospitalized for the past month due to a recent psychotic episode. John has a history of substance abuse, but has been clean for the past 6 months. He has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. John is willing to participate in the study and has previously been treated with oral risperidone, which he tolerated well. He is able to provide written informed consent and is currently an inpatient at the hospital. John's lab results are within normal limits.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman presenting with irregular menstrual cycles and excessive hair growth on her face, chest, and back. She has a family history of diabetes and obesity. She has not been on any medication for the past six months and her thyroid function and prolactin levels are normal. She has not been diagnosed with any metabolic, cardiovascular, respiratory, or hepatic disease. She has a BMI of 27 kg/m2. The patient is interested in participating in the study to understand the relationship between insulin resistance and PCOS. She is willing to undergo blood tests and follow the study protocol.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and underwent emergency coronary angiography which revealed a 100% occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. Percutaneous coronary intervention was performed successfully and the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit. However, 48 hours later, he remained unconscious with a FOUR-score of <M4, and head computed tomography (CT) was ordered as per routine protocol in the participating center. The CT scan showed no signs of intracranial bleeding, but the radiologist noted generalized oedema in the brain. The patient was enrolled in the TTM-2 CT-substudy and pseudonymized original CT images were uploaded to the digital platform for analysis. Two study radiologists blinded from clinical data performed analyses according to protocol, including manual and automated measurements of the differentiation between the grey and white matter. The primary outcome of the study is the neurological outcome at 6 months after cardiac arrest using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). The patient's next of kin has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has a history of coronary artery disease and has been diagnosed with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue lately. She is currently on a beta-blocker to control her heart rate but is still experiencing symptoms. She has no history of congestive heart failure. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in the study to help advance medical research and potentially improve her own health.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has been struggling with a diabetic foot ulcer for the past month, which has been graded as Wagner grade 2. He has been using traditional treatment methods, but the ulcer has not shown any significant improvement. He has no history of autoimmune diabetes or gestational diabetes. He has no other known medical conditions but has experienced mild kidney function impairment in the past. His blood glucose levels are controlled with oral medication and his HbA1c is 7.5%. His lipid levels and blood pressure are within normal limits. His ulcer has not been infected and he has not experienced any cerebrovascular disease. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive either traditional treatment or transplantation of autologous PRG combined with autologous BMMSCs for treatment of his diabetic foot ulcer.

A 24-year-old healthy male, who works as a computer programmer, is interested in participating in the phase Ia study of ChAd63/MVA PvDBP. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has not received any vaccines in the 30 days preceding enrollment and has not participated in any other clinical trials involving investigational products. He has not visited any malaria endemic regions in the past six months. He is willing to practice continuous effective contraception during the study and is not planning to donate blood during the course of the study. He is willing to allow the investigators to discuss his medical history with his General Practitioner. He provides written informed consent and understands the study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past year. She has been treated with escitalopram (20mg/day) for the last 8 weeks but has not experienced any significant improvement in her symptoms. She continues to have persistent feelings of sadness, worthlessness, and hopelessness. She is experiencing a lack of motivation, difficulty sleeping, and has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has also noticed that she has difficulty recognizing and expressing her emotions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to switch to a different antidepressant and improve her emotional functioning. She has no history of suicidal thoughts or attempts. She is not currently taking any other medications and has no significant medical history.

70-year-old Caucasian male presented with complaints of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss of 10 pounds in the last 2 months. Physical examination revealed palpable lymph nodes in the neck, left supraclavicular, and left axillary regions. Laboratory investigations showed anemia with hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, elevated LDH, and normal liver and renal function tests. A biopsy of the left cervical lymph node revealed CD30+EBV+DLBCL. The patient had received standard R-CHOP chemotherapy but showed no response after two cycles. The patient was then evaluated for the clinical trial of Brentuximab Vedotin in CD30 Positive Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) Positive DLBCL of Elderly. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a healthy, non-smoking female between the ages of 18 and 55 with a BMI ranging from 17.5 to 30.5 kg/m2 and a total body weight of at least 50 kg. She has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurological, or allergic disease. She has not had any regular alcohol consumption exceeding 7 drinks per week in the past 6 months and has not used any investigational drug within 30 days prior to the first dose of investigational product. She has not used any prescription or nonprescription drugs and dietary supplements within 7 days prior to the first dose of investigational product. She is willing to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She is willing to use an acceptable method of nonhormonal contraception for the duration of the study and for the specified time after follow-up. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not discontinued use of oral contraceptives for medical reasons. She does not have a history of sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. She has not donated blood of approximately 1 pint (500 mL) or more within 60 days prior to dosing.
