She is not a subject who is investigator site staff members directly involved in the conduct of the study and their family members, site staff members otherwise supervised by the investigator, or subjects who are Pfizer employees, including their family members, directly involved in the conduct of the study.

The patient is a primary caregiver of a child who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia and has completed treatment and is now in remission. The caregiver is able to communicate in either English or Taiwanese language. The caregiver is experiencing stress related to caring for the child and managing their medical needs. They are living with the child and other family members and are interested in exploring ways to improve family functioning and resilience.

A 42-year-old male was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has no history of any other significant medical conditions. He will be starting his first course of chemotherapy soon. He has not had any previous organ transplants. He has no known allergies to any medication. He is willing to participate in this observational study to help advance the understanding and treatment of invasive fungal infections.

The patient is a 6-year-old Hispanic male who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at 2 years old. He was born prematurely at 26 weeks and weighed 2.5 pounds at birth. He had a difficult course in the neonatal intensive care unit with respiratory distress syndrome and required mechanical ventilation for 3 weeks. He also had a grade III intraventricular hemorrhage and was treated with shunt placement. He has significant spasticity in his legs and arms, making it difficult for him to walk and use his hands. He has been receiving rehabilitation treatment for the past 2 years, including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy. He has shown some improvement, but his progress has been slow. He lives with his mother and grandmother, who both work full-time. His mother is hopeful that the stem cell transplantation may provide a more significant improvement in his condition. He was screened and met the eligibility criteria for the study.

Patient is a 56-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation who is a candidate for cryoablation procedure. He has a BMI of 27 and has been on anticoagulation therapy for the past 2 years. His medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no significant past surgical history, and his baseline laboratory values are within normal limits. He is able to read, write and understand English, and has no cognitive or communication impairments. He is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

This is a 56 year old male with a history of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma who has relapsed after initial treatment. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 2 and is expected to have a survival of greater than 3 months. The patient has measurable disease and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of decitabin plus R-GDP. The patient has no history of epilepsy or other CNS disease, and does not have active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection or any other uncontrolled active infection. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no other uncontrolled medical disorders that would prevent participation. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has consented to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) after experiencing severe headaches, blurred vision, and confusion which led to a seizure. The patient underwent cytoreductive surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy with temozolomide, but unfortunately, the tumor recurred after a few months. The patient has not received any other systemic or ITV adjuvant chemotherapy regimen in addition to temozolomide, nor has he received any other therapies designed specifically to treat the recurrent GBM. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) of 70% and has recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy. The patient has normal hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing and able to sign the informed consent document and undergo tumor biopsy and Ommaya reservoir placement. The patient does not have any contraindications to having placement of a ventricular access device such as Ommaya reservoir and does not have clinical and/or neuroradiographic evidence of hydrocephalus or increased intracranial pressure. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and women of childbearing years must have a negative serum pregnancy test.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing blurry vision in her right eye for the past few months. She was recently diagnosed with a cataract and has scheduled for phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation in the capsular bag. She has no history of ocular inflammation or pain but has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. She wears glasses for reading and distance vision. She is currently not taking any medications that could interfere with the study drug. She has no history of noninfectious inflammatory ocular disease, diabetic retinopathy, or age-related macular degeneration. The intraocular pressure in both eyes is within the normal range. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve her vision and contribute to medical research.

This is a 29-year-old female who is generally in good health. She has a body mass index of 24.5 kg/m^2. She does not smoke and has not donated blood or plasma in the past three months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effect of insulin degludec after different routes of injection in healthy subjects. She is willing to refrain from smoking and the use of nicotine gum or transdermal nicotine patches during the inpatient period.

A 25-day-old male infant, born at 26 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 800 grams, was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit due to respiratory distress syndrome requiring mechanical ventilation. He received surfactant therapy and was started on a weaning protocol. On day 20, he developed worsening respiratory distress requiring re-intubation. The neonatologist decided that endotracheal intubation is necessary and propofol will be used for sedation. The patient does not have any known major congenital anomalies or neurological disorders, no abnormal upper airway, and his mother did not receive any sedatives or opioids before or during delivery. The patient's medical history includes a patent ductus arteriosus and a positive blood culture for coagulase-negative staphylococcus, which was treated with antibiotics. His current medications include caffeine, vancomycin, ampicillin, and furosemide. The patient's vital signs are stable at the time of inclusion in the study.

A 25-year-old healthy male comes to the clinic for a clinical trial. He is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 22 kg/m², and weighing 70 kg. He has never been diagnosed with any cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, metabolic, hematologic, neurologic, psychiatric, systemic, infectious, or ocular disease. He has no history of drug hypersensitivity or allergic disease diagnosed and treated by a physician. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and he does not consume excessive amounts of beverages with xanthine bases. He has no history of major surgeries or drug metabolizing enzyme inducing agents and inhibitors such as barbiturates. He has not taken any drugs or herbal medicines (except paracetamol) during the last 14 days prior to the first administration, any over-the-counter medicines or vitamins during the last 7 days prior to the first administration, and any investigational product from other clinical trials within 60 days from the start of the study. He has normal blood pressure, heart rate, and ECG recording on a 12-lead ECG, and laboratory parameters within the normal range. He is willing to abstain from smoking 24 hours prior to admission until discharge and to avoid intensive muscular effort during the study. He has normal dietary habits and is covered by the Health Insurance System and/or in compliance with the recommendations of National Law in force relating to biomedical research. He is able to sign a written informed consent prior to selection and is not under administrative or legal supervision.

The patient is a 14-year-old female who has been diagnosed with bilateral knee osteoarthritis. She has been experiencing pain in both of her knees and has difficulty walking and climbing stairs. She is otherwise healthy and active, playing basketball and volleyball before her diagnosis. She lives with her parents and has no significant medical history. She does not take any medications and does not have any known allergies. She is scheduled for bilateral varus rotational osteotomy (VRO) with or without associated soft tissue and osseous procedures. She has not received any anticoagulants or hormonal therapies in the days prior to surgery. She has agreed to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks.

The patient is a 20-year-old student from Sulaiman Al-Rajhi Colleges in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. She is in good health and has no history of any major illnesses. Her BMI is 22, and her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. She has no known allergies or dietary restrictions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of omega-3 fatty acid supplements on cognitive brain domains and reaction time. She has never taken any supplements before and is willing to follow the instructions and take the supplements regularly as directed. She is aware of the potential side effects of supplements and understands the importance of following up with the study team and reporting any adverse effects.

58-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and a recent diagnosis of AL amyloidosis. She has undergone chemotherapy and stem cell transplantation and has achieved a complete response to therapy. A baseline bone marrow biopsy was obtained at the time of diagnosis, which will be used to create the primer-probe sets required for MRD testing by Q-PCR. The patient will be enrolled in the study and annual bone marrow aspirates will be taken for research purposes to test for MRD. The patient is willing to allow her bone marrow samples to be used in this study and will sign a consent form specifically for this purpose. She has no known allergies and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 56-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU after suffering a severe stroke. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He is currently on anticoagulant therapy with warfarin due to a previous deep vein thrombosis. The patient's INR levels need to be closely monitored to prevent bleeding or clotting complications. He is eligible to participate in a clinical trial that compares the accuracy of two POC-tests, INRario2 and CoaguChek, with laboratory results. The study aims to determine whether these tools can be used effectively in the clinical daily routine for ICU patients between the ages of 18-99. The patient does not have lupus erythematodes or anti-phospholipid-antibodies, which are the exclusion criteria for this trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been experiencing severe itching without any visible rash or skin lesions for the past 6 months. The itching is generalized and occurs throughout the day, but is worse at night, affecting his sleep quality. He has no history of allergies, and his skin appears normal on examination. He has a history of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), which was diagnosed during routine blood tests 2 years ago. His most recent serum protein electrophoresis showed an increase in the monoclonal protein level. He has been under the care of a hematologist at Brest CHR and is currently being monitored with periodic blood tests. He has not been taking any new medications, and there have been no recent changes in his medical history. He has given his non-opposition to participate in this study to investigate the frequency and characteristics of pruritus in patients with monoclonal gammopathy.

The patient is a 25-year-old female of Hispanic origin with non-segmental vitiligo. She has been receiving standard of care treatment for 6 months, consisting of topical corticosteroids and NB-UVB phototherapy, but has not seen significant improvement in her depigmented lesions. She has two comparable depigmented regions on her arms that are at least 10 cm2 in size. The patient has no history of cardiac insufficiency, skin cancer, or allergy to clarithromycin. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to give written informed consent. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to UVB or UVA light or local anesthesia. She is competent to understand the procedures involved in the study.

The patient is a 12 year-old boy with end-stage renal disease requiring peritoneal dialysis for the past 6 months. He has a history of recurrent peritonitis but has been stable for the past 3 months. He is currently using a cycler machine for his dialysis treatment and has a catheter in place with no dysfunction. He has no significant medical history other than renal disease and is not on any medication other than those prescribed for his renal condition. He has a normal body mass index and is physically active. He lives with his parents and siblings and attends school full-time. He has no known allergies and has not been hospitalized in the past year. He and his parents are willing to participate in the study and understand the potential benefits and risks associated with the study procedures.

Pt is a 28yo M with a recent diagnosis of early-stage Hodgkin's Lymphoma with a bulky lesion in his mediastinum. He is currently being treated with ABVD x 4 and is scheduled for consolidation radiotherapy on his bulky lesion. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no other medical history. He has provided written consent to participate in a non-interventional study to assess the specificity and overall accuracy of interim dual-point acquisition PET in predicting treatment outcome. The study aims to reduce false positive results in the interim-PET scan interpretation by performing a dynamic study with 2 different time points of image acquisition. The patient will also undergo a DW-MRI sub-study to assess the pattern of FDG uptake at baseline in untreated patients affected by Hodgkin's lymphoma. The patient does not have diabetes mellitus or any implanted biomedical devices and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 22-year-old university student who has donated blood once before without any major issues. She is generally healthy and does not have any chronic medical conditions. However, she reports feeling anxious and nervous before and during blood donation, which has led to dizziness and fainting in the past. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to learn techniques to reduce vasovagal symptoms during future blood donations. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. She is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of stable coronary artery disease. He underwent a treadmill test, which was positive for ischemia. He has been on medical management with aspirin, statin, and beta-blocker for the last six months. He does not smoke and has a BMI of 28. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 72 bpm. His physical exam is unremarkable, with no signs of heart failure. His recent laboratory tests are within normal limits, including liver function tests. He is scheduled for elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the next week. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 42 year old woman with a history of glioblastoma multiforme presents with recurrent headaches and visual disturbances. MRI confirms tumor progression and she is no longer responding to her current treatment regimen. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her Karnofsky Performance Status is 70% and her life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 8 weeks. The patient has not received any treatment with enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants. She agrees to practice adequate contraception during the trial period and has signed an informed consent indicating her awareness of the investigational nature of the study. She meets all other eligibility criteria and is considered for enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with a swollen main artery in the abdomen. He is scheduled to undergo open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair surgery. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication to control these conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given full informed consent. He has an estimated pre-operative glomerular filtration rate greater than 30mls/min/1.73m2 and does not have significant upper limb peripheral arterial disease or a history of upper limb deep vein thrombosis. He is not taking glibenclamide or nicorandil and does not have a known history of myocarditis, pericarditis or amyloidosis. The patient does not have severe hepatic or respiratory disease and has not undergone previous axillary surgery.

The patient is a healthy adult male or female between the ages of 18 and 55, with a Body Mass Index (BMI) between 18.5 and 29.9 kg/m2. The patient has no significant medical history, including no gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders, and has not undergone surgery of the gastrointestinal tract (except appendectomy). The patient has no history of central nervous system diseases or psychiatric disorders, neurological disorders, or relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells or blackouts. The patient has no chronic or acute infections or relevant allergies/hypersensitivity (including allergy to drug or its excipients). The patient is not a smoker, alcohol abuser, drug abuser, and has not donated blood within four weeks prior to the start of study. Female patients are not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study or within 1 month after study completion, and have adequate contraception during the study and until 1 month after study completion.

The patient is a 24-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the Meninigococcal Conjugate Vaccine containing Serogroups A, C, Y, W and X (MCV5). She has never received any vaccination against Neisseria meningitidis and has no known exposure to the bacteria. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is currently using an effective licensed method of birth control. She has no history of meningitis, seizures, or any neurological or psychiatric disorder. She has not received any other vaccine within the past 30 days and is not planning to receive any vaccines during the study period. She has no known allergies to any component of the three study vaccines, no history of serious adverse reactions following administration of Tetanus Toxoid, Diphtheria Toxoid, or CRM containing vaccines, and no history of Guillan-Barré syndrome. She does not have any confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immune-deficient condition or any family history of congenital or hereditary immunodeficiency. She has not received chronic administration of immune-suppressants or other immune-modifying agents within six months prior to administration of the study vaccine. She has no laboratory confirmed infection of hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or human immunodeficiency virus. She has no major congenital defects or serious chronic illness, no acute or chronic clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic, or renal functional abnormality, and no known bleeding disorders. She has not received immunoglobulins and/or any blood products within the three months preceding the administration of the study vaccines, and has no history or signs of alcohol or substance abuse within the past year. Her BMI is below 30, and she is willing to comply with all planned study procedures and be available for all study visits.

75 yo F with a history of knee pain for the last year that has been getting progressively worse. She reports difficulty performing activities of daily living, such as climbing stairs and getting up from a seated position. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis and has a Kellgren-Lawrence Scale score of 2. She has tried physical therapy and medication, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She is independent in ambulating, but reports some difficulty with balance. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or neurological disorders. She is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve her physical function and quality of life.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past three years due to end-stage kidney disease. He was diagnosed with hypertension and diabetes ten years ago, and despite a good control of his blood sugar and blood pressure, his kidney function deteriorated significantly. He has been experiencing difficulty with ultrafiltration in the past few months, leading to a decrease in his overall dialysis efficiency. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs and drinks alcohol only occasionally. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. He is motivated to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

25-year-old female, recently graduated from college and started her first job as an administrative assistant. She has been in a relationship for two years and is not ready to start a family yet. She has been using oral contraceptives for the past year but has experienced side effects and is interested in exploring other options for birth control. She lives in Salt Lake County and has limited income, making it difficult for her to afford highly effective reversible contraception (HER-C). She is fluent in English and is seeking contraceptive counseling and services at a participating Planned Parenthood clinic in the area. She is interested in learning more about HER-C and is willing to participate in the study to help increase access and understanding of these methods.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. His cancer is inoperable and is at stage IIIA. He has received one prior chemotherapy treatment for advanced disease. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1, and he is able to swallow pills without any difficulty. He has no known allergies to any of the study drugs. He has negative serum beta-HCG test and is under active contraception (for females of childbearing potential). His ANC is 2000/mm3, platelet count is 120,000/mm3, estimated creatinine clearance is 60 cc/min (as measured by the Cockcroft-Gault equation), bilirubin is 1 mg/dl, and SGPT is 1.5x nl. He has no peripheral neuropathy of Grade 2 or higher. He has not received previous radiation therapy to the chest and does not have a history of CHF/MI or other significant cardiac history within the last six months. He is willing to sign an informed consent form to participate in the clinical trial.

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of redness and visible blood vessels on her face. She has had this problem for several years, and it worsens when she is under stress or exposed to sunlight. She has tried several creams and lotions, but they did not help much. She has no history of allergies or skin diseases. She is not pregnant, and she is not planning to get pregnant in the near future. She is not using any contraception. She works in an office and is not exposed to chemicals or irritants.

42yo female with a history of advanced ovarian cancer diagnosed five years ago. She underwent a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, and lymph node dissection. The patient received six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel as adjuvant chemotherapy. She experienced a recurrence of cancer three years later and was treated with liposomal doxorubicin, followed by weekly paclitaxel. Subsequently, she received bevacizumab followed by olaparib. Most recently, she was treated with gemcitabine and carboplatin. The patient is experiencing progression of the disease with increased abdominal pain and distention. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed a 4 cm left adnexal mass, multiple peritoneal implants, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1.

43 yo female with a history of recurrent ovarian cysts and pelvic pain is scheduled for a laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy. She has no significant medical history and is an ASA class I patient. Patient weighs 70 kg, and her height is 5'6". She has no allergies to any medications. The patient has provided verbal consent to participate in the study. She has no history of neuromuscular disease, renal or hepatic disease, and is not taking any medications that are excluded by the study criteria. The patient has no open skin sores in the locations needed for electrode application. The patient has a BMI of 25.

John is a 45-year-old man with a history of recurrent calcium oxalate stones. He has been diagnosed with a heterozygous mutation of the AGXT gene through genetic testing. John is interested in participating in a study that examines the effects of this mutation on endogenous oxalate production. He is willing to comply with a controlled low-oxalate diet for five days and is able to provide blood and urine samples throughout the study. John is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 52-year-old man, who works as a truck driver, came to the clinic complaining of excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring. He has a history of smoking and his BMI is 32. He also reports occasional leg swelling and discomfort. He has no known allergies or underlying medical conditions. He takes no medications regularly, but sometimes takes over-the-counter pain relievers for headaches. He is married and has two children. He reports feeling tired and fatigued during the day, and often feels like he hasn't slept at all. He is interested in participating in a study that could help him understand his symptoms better.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS). He has been experiencing progressive fatigue, weight loss, and shortness of breath over the past few months. An echocardiogram showed left ventricular hypertrophy with an average thickness of 12 mm. The patient's 12-lead ECG revealed unexplained low voltage. The patient has been referred to a specialist for further evaluation and is suspected to have systemic amyloidosis. The patient has no known allergies to amyloid PET imaging agents, but has a history of claustrophobia. The patient is willing to undergo the PET/MR imaging and biopsy if necessary.

A 5-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with caries in his primary molars. He has no signs of pulp disease and does not experience spontaneous pain. He has a history of good oral hygiene and has been brushing his teeth twice a day. He is generally cooperative during dental appointments and has no known allergies to dental materials. His parents are supportive of participating in the study and are willing to comply with all follow-up appointments.

An 80-year-old female patient with a history of depression and anxiety was admitted to the geriatric psychiatry ward due to worsening of her symptoms. She had been taking fluoxetine and lorazepam for the past 3 months with no significant improvement. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and osteoporosis for which she takes multiple medications. She has a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 22/30 indicating mild cognitive impairment. Physical examination reveals no significant findings except for mild hypotension. The patient is capable of providing informed consent and has agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and is in good physical health as determined by a recent physical examination, vital signs, clinical laboratory tests, and 12-lead ECG. He does not have any allergies or drug hypersensitivity. He does not have a history of alcohol or substance dependence in the last 12 months, and his urine drug screen is negative. He does not have any MR exclusion criteria, elevated intracranial pressure or glaucoma. He has not had hypertonia, cardiac insufficiency, or myocardial infarction within the last 6 months. He has normal liver and renal function. He has not taken any prescription psychotropic medication within 28 days prior to screening, nor has he taken any non-prescription medication, including analgesics and supplements such as vitamins and herbal supplements, within 48 hours prior to the baseline visit. He is willing to participate in a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group design with 3 treatment conditions (lamotrigine + ketamine, placebo + ketamine, placebo + placebo). He is willing to undergo two scanning sessions (acute + post 24 hrs.) and to have blood samples taken at specific timepoints to determine the plasma pharmacokinetics of lamotrigine and ketamine.

A 25-year-old Chinese male with a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a clinical study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of a single oral dose of ozanimod. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. He does not smoke or use any tobacco or nicotine-containing products and has not used any recreational drugs in the past 2 years. He drinks less than 2 cups of tea or coffee per day and does not consume any other caffeinated drinks. He is willing to practice a highly effective method of contraception and is not planning to have surgery or donate blood during the study period. He has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

The patient is a 45 year old male who is scheduled to undergo a hernia repair surgery that is expected to take approximately 3 hours under general anesthesia with an endotracheal tube. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies or sensitivities to any anesthetic agents or analgesic drugs. He does not have a cardiac pacemaker and does not have atrial fibrillation or more than 5 ventricular extra systoles/minute. He is not currently taking any opioids or neuromuscular blocking agents. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

I apologize, but there is no patient involved in this clinical trial. This clinical trial is directed towards healthcare professionals who have experience working in health institutions for at least 3 years.

A 50-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years presents for participation in a clinical trial. She is currently on metformin and a sulfonylurea to manage her diabetes. Her fasting plasma glucose level is 160 mg/dL and her HbA1c level is 8.2%. She has no history of renal or liver disease, and her hemoglobinopathy test is negative. She is not pregnant nor planning to conceive. She is willing to provide written and audio-visual informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She has no known allergies to the investigational product.

The patient is a 12-year-old female who has been diagnosed with acute liver failure (ALF). She was transferred from a referring hospital to the study site within 24 hours of hospitalization. She has no history of acute acetaminophen toxicity, mushroom poisoning, or a known malignancy. She is not pregnant and meets the inclusion criteria for enrollment in the Pediatric Acute Liver Failure prospective database. She exhibits no signs of cerebral herniation, has no intractable arterial hypotension, no inotropic drugs, and no signs of sepsis. Her parents have given informed consent for her to participate in the double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of intravenous N-acetylcysteine (NAC) vs. placebo for the treatment of non-acetaminophen ALF. The purpose of the trial is to examine the safety and efficacy of intravenous NAC in children with ALF for whom no antidote or other specific treatment is available. She will be evaluated and initiated the treatment within the first 24 hours of hospitalization.

The patient is a 17-year-old sexually active female who is seeking a reliable contraceptive method. She has been sexually active for the past year and uses condoms inconsistently. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections and has had an annual gynecologic exam with a normal Pap smear. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has regular menstrual cycles with moderate cramping, lasting around 5 days. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not currently pregnant and has not used emergency contraception in the past month. She is English-speaking and able to read and understand the consent form.

A 35-year-old male with a history of chronic back pain presents to the rheumatology clinic with complaints of stiffness and pain in his lower back, which has been present for over 6 months. He reports that the pain is worse in the morning and tends to improve with activity. He has been on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for the past 3 months with no significant improvement. He has a family history of ankylosing spondylitis. Physical examination reveals limited lumbar spine mobility, with tenderness and swelling at the sacroiliac joints. Blood tests show elevated C-reactive protein levels. MRI shows evidence of bone marrow edema in the sacroiliac joints, consistent with active ankylosing spondylitis. The patient is initiated on TNF inhibitor treatment with CZP. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of novel quantitative MRI measures for AS. He has not received any biologic treatment in the past 6 months and is not on more than 10mg of prednisone per day. He is not pregnant and does not have fibromyalgia or any other reasons for back pain.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) following a history of unstable relationships, impulsive behavior, and emotional instability. She is a single mother with a 14-month-old daughter. She reports experiencing low mood, anxiety, and feelings of emptiness. She has a history of self-harm and suicidal ideation. She is currently taking medication for depression and anxiety. The baby's father is not involved in the child's life, and the patient has limited social support. She lives in a small apartment with her daughter and struggles with managing her daughter's behavior, especially when she is upset or crying. The patient's daughter is healthy and meeting developmental milestones. The patient is interested in participating in a program that may help her better understand her daughter's needs and improve their relationship.

A 62-year-old male presents with a history of a fall 2 weeks ago, resulting in a headache and dizziness. He has been experiencing difficulty with balance and coordination. A cranial computed tomography reveals a chronic subdural hematoma. The patient has no allergies, and his medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker and lives independently. He is willing to undergo surgery for the hematoma and participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus. He has normal liver function and no history of organ allograft. His creatinine clearance is 90 mL/min based on the Cockcroft-Gault formula. He has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma and is currently receiving chemotherapy. He is interested in participating in the study to further understand the pharmacokinetics of Genasense in patients with normal renal function. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has no coexisting conditions that would require him to continue therapy during the treatment phase with a drug known to alter renal function.

A 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with a fever of 101.5°F, dry cough, and shortness of breath for 3 days. On admission, his oxygen saturation was 88% on room air, respiratory rate was 24 breaths per minute, and blood pressure was 150/90 mmHg. Chest X-ray revealed bilateral infiltrates. COVID-19 testing was positive. The patient was started on supplemental oxygen and treated with azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine. Despite treatment, the patient continued to deteriorate and required intubation on day 5 of hospitalization. Laboratory studies revealed a peak ferritin level of 11,200 ng/mL and lactate dehydrogenase of 740 U/L. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the use of etoposide in patients with COVID-19 infection with evidence of cytokine storm. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria and is willing to participate in the study.

As this clinical trial is focused on the prevalence of ESBL-Enterobacteriaceae colonization among ICU staff, there is no patient description required. The study is looking for voluntary non-medical staff members (i.e. nurses and nursing assistants) and medical staff in two French ICUs who are willing to participate in the assessment of self-reported risk factors for MDR-bacteria colonization by performing a rectal swab with isolation of ESBL-producting Enterobacteriaceae.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit due to severe shortness of breath and difficulty breathing. He has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and coronary artery disease. The patient is currently on a ventilator and has been diagnosed with pulmonary edema. The medical team is trying to determine whether the pulmonary edema is cardiogenic or non-cardiogenic. The patient does not have a history of asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The medical team is considering enrolling the patient in a clinical trial to evaluate a digital diagnostic method for pulmonary edema. The trial requires patients in the intensive care unit who are currently using a ventilator and excludes patients with asthma, COPD, or those not on a ventilator. The medical team believes that this trial may provide valuable insights into the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary edema in critically ill patients.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who lives alone in Taiwan. She has been struggling with daily activities due to her frailty and has a Cardiovascular Health Study Phenotypical Classification frailty index of 1. She can communicate in Chinese and Taiwanese and has no hearing or visual impairments that affect her daily activities. The patient's Canadian Study of Health and Aging Clinical Frailty Scale (CSHA- CFS) Chinese In-Person Interview Version score is between 3-6. She is able to stand and walk with a walker for 5 meters, but her gait is unsteady and she is at risk of falling. She has no history of alcoholism, epilepsy, brain tumor, brain surgery, schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. She is willing to participate in a 12-week intervention study that will help improve her lower extremity strength and overall health.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been taking tamsulosin hydrochloride for the past 2 months to treat lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS). He reports experiencing overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms such as urinary frequency and urgency with or without incontinence for the past 3 months. He is willing and able to complete a 3-day diary and Quality of Life questionnaires. He has an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) score of 10. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 3.5 ng/mL, and he has undergone a prostate biopsy that was negative for cancer within the past 2 years. He is currently using a highly effective birth control method with his partner. He has not participated in any interventional trials within the past 30 days. He is not currently on any prohibited medications and has not started, stopped, or changed the dose of any restricted medications within the past 30 days. He is not experiencing any hematuria or urinary tract infections. He has not undergone any pelvic or prostate surgery, and he does not have any neurological disorders or diabetic neuropathy. He is not currently experiencing postural hypotension or syncope or postural orthostatic tachycardia. He does not have moderate or severe hepatic impairment or severe renal impairment. He does not have any clinical significant ECG abnormalities or hypersensitivity to any components of mirabegron or tamsulosin hydrochloride. He has not previously received mirabegron in the past 6 months.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is scheduled for an elective colonoscopy. He reports no history of adverse reactions to sedatives or anesthetics. He weighs 190 pounds and is 5 feet 10 inches tall. He does not smoke, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. The patient has given informed consent for the study and meets the criteria for conscious sedation. He is able to understand the use of patient-controlled sedation.

The patient is a primiparous woman who has just delivered a singleton baby vaginally. She is between the ages of 20-35 and has no history of operative deliveries, multifetal pregnancy, or cesarean delivery. She is able to cooperate for an effective Valsalva maneuver and is not handicapped in the lithotomy position. The patient has consented to participate in the study and is willing to undergo two 3D transperineal ultrasound evaluations - one within 36 hours of delivery and another at 3 months post-delivery. The patient's medical history does not include any conditions that would exclude her from participation in the study.

A 65 year old man with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, fatigue, and leg swelling. He reports feeling more tired than usual over the past few weeks and has noticed a decrease in his urine output. Physical examination reveals bibasilar crackles and peripheral edema. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 100 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. His serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dL and his estimated creatinine clearance is 40 cc/min. He is diagnosed with decompensated heart failure and renal dysfunction and is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the addition of nesiritide to standard therapy.

A 58-year-old man presented to the emergency room with chest pain that has been ongoing for the past hour. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He takes medication for hypertension and a daily aspirin. He has never had a heart attack before. He gives consent to participate in the trial and agrees to follow the study protocol. He has no known allergies to any medication.

A 14-year-old girl presents with symptoms of anxiety, including excessive worry about school performance and social interactions. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year, which have been affecting her daily life and causing her to avoid social situations. The patient has no family history of anxiety disorders, but she does have a history of depression in her family. She has not received any treatment for her anxiety symptoms. She will be assessed for anxiety disorders and compared to a control group of adolescents without anxiety disorders. If she meets the inclusion criteria, she will be enrolled in a CBT treatment program for 8-12 weeks to investigate the relationship between emotional regulation strategies and treatment effectiveness in childhood anxiety disorders.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who was diagnosed with biliary atresia at 3 months of age. He underwent Kasai operation at 4 months of age. He has been suffering from prolonged jaundice and occasional episodes of fever and diarrhea. He has been hospitalized twice due to cholangitis. Currently, he is on ursodeoxycholic acid and vitamin supplementation. He has gained appropriate weight for his age and height, and his physical examination is unremarkable except for jaundice. His laboratory tests show elevated bilirubin levels and mildly elevated liver enzymes. He has not received any immunosuppressant therapy or systemic immunoglobulin in the past 6 months. His parents are both healthy and non-consanguineous. He attends preschool and enjoys playing with his classmates.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy woman who works as a graphic designer. She is right-handed and has no history of neurological or psychiatric diseases. She has never received acupuncture treatment before and has no medical knowledge about acupuncture. She is interested in participating in the study and has free time to take part in the measurements. She does not have any cognitive handicap, severe speech disorder, or history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has not undergone any neurosurgical intervention or suffered from brain injury. She does not have any chronic disease that requires regular medication. She is not pregnant and is not planning to get pregnant in the near future. She has no contraindication for acupuncture or MRI, such as anti-coagulation therapy, pacemaker, claustrophobia, cochlear implant, or metallic implants. She signs an informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 72 year-old female who was brought to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. Upon evaluation, she was diagnosed with a perforated gastric ulcer and deemed to require immediate surgical intervention. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She lives alone and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. She has no history of falls or fractures. She has never had surgery before and is anxious about the procedure. She has a supportive family who is involved in her care.

The patient is a 35 year old Hispanic male who has been diagnosed with bipolar affective disorder and is currently experiencing depressive symptoms. He has been smoking tobacco for 15 years and is finding it difficult to quit smoking. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for 2 years. He works as a construction worker and reports frequent stress at work. He has a wife and two children and is actively involved in their lives. He is currently taking medication for bipolar disorder and attends therapy sessions regularly. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 6 months ago after experiencing tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia. He has not been started on any symptomatic treatment for his Parkinson's disease symptoms yet. His Hoehn & Yahr stage is 2. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He denies any history of gastrointestinal surgery but has a history of occasional hemorrhoids. He is not taking any diuretics or anticoagulant medications. His last physical exam and lab study was performed last week and showed the results below: A well-nourished man, non-icteric, cooperative, and alert Weight: 75 kg Height: 175 BP: 130/80 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 4500/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 32 U/L ALT: 42 U/L Alk P: 120 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl ESR: 20 mm/hr.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman with a history of Rhesus disease and alloimmunization is seeking care from a specialist. She has had two previous pregnancies with blood transfusions given in utero due to fetal anemia. She is currently at 23 weeks of gestation and her latest blood test shows high levels of anti-D antibodies. She is concerned about the risks involved in amniocentesis and is interested in a non-invasive alternative to predict fetal anemia. She has no other medical problems and has been taking prenatal vitamins throughout the pregnancy.

A 60-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with complaints of dizziness and palpitations. He had a history of myocardial infarction and underwent a coronary artery bypass grafting procedure 2 years ago. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His electrocardiogram showed complete heart block, and he was diagnosed with sick sinus syndrome. The patient is interested in receiving a pacemaker implantation to address his condition. He is willing to participate in the Austria Study to evaluate the difference between screw-in leads actively fixed in the septum and tined leads passively fixed in the apex concerning electrical parameters and implantation time, as well as the influence of stimulation location by type of lead on QRS width, ejection fraction, and NYHA class.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who resides in Toronto, Canada. She speaks English as her primary language and is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve the nutritional quality of food products. She is a working professional and does most of the grocery shopping for her household. She owns an iPhone 7 and is comfortable using smartphone applications. She has no history of chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in an online survey on a minimum screen size of 9.7 inches.

42 yo F with a history of Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome (APL) and receiving warfarin therapy for several years. Patient has a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) secondary to APL. Patient has been using a point of care device (CoaguChek XS) to monitor their International Normalized Ratio (INR) at home. However, there have been concerns regarding the accuracy of the device due to the presence of antibodies in APL patients. Patient was approached to participate in a clinical trial to compare the accuracy of the CoaguChek XS in measuring INR in patients with APL. Patient will be measured by both the CoaguChek XS and a standard lab as a reference point to determine the accuracy of the device. Patient is willing to participate in the study to help improve the accuracy of INR monitoring in APL patients. Past Medical History: - Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome (APL) - Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) - Pulmonary embolism (PE) - Hypertension - Obesity

A 35-year-old woman with a history of two vaginal deliveries came to the clinic with complaints of moderate fecal incontinence symptoms. She has tried conservative therapies such as dietary changes, exercise, and biofeedback but has not been satisfied with the results. She is married and has two children. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. She exercises regularly by jogging for 30 minutes a day, 3 times a week. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. She is not currently pregnant nor considering future childbearing. She has not had a hysterectomy within the last six months. She has not had a previous implantation of mesh or trauma to the pelvic area. She has no history of pelvic radiation, evacuation disorder, or rectal prolapse. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to sign an informed consent form.

This is a 56-year-old male who was brought to the emergency department via ambulance after experiencing sudden onset right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. FAST scores were 3 (Facial droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty) and the patient was last seen well 45 minutes prior to arrival. CT scan showed a left middle cerebral artery infarct. The patient's systolic blood pressure was measured at 170 mmHg. He has a history of hypertension and regularly takes medication for it. The patient is able to provide brief informed consent for the trial.

A 7-year-old male child with a history of easy bruising and excessive bleeding after minor injuries. He was recently diagnosed with severe hemophilia B with documented factor IX levels of 1%. He has never been treated with any factor IX concentrate or blood components. The child has no history of inhibitors or hypersensitivity reactions associated with any factor IX concentrate administration. He has no other coagulation disorders or concurrent clinically significant major disease that would make him unsuitable for enrollment. The child's parents are willing to comply with study requirements and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been experiencing unexplained weight loss, fever, and night sweats for the last few weeks. He also complains of a persistent cough and shortness of breath. Physical examination reveals enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, armpits, and groin. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes confirms a diagnosis of large cell lymphoma. The patient is eligible for a clinical trial that aims to compare the effectiveness of various chemotherapy drug combinations in treating advanced-stage large cell lymphoma in pediatric patients. The study involves randomization into two treatment arms, and patients will receive a combination of chemotherapeutic drugs with or without intermediate-dose methotrexate/high dose cytarabine as maintenance therapy following induction therapy. The researchers aim to characterize further the immunophenotypic and morphologic correlates of pediatric large cell lymphoma. The patient must not have received prior therapy and must be under the age of 22. Adequate contraception is required for fertile patients.

The patient is a 50-year-old man diagnosed with stage IV melanoma. He has multiple metastases to the lymph nodes, lungs, and liver. The patient has been treated with chemotherapy in the past but has progressed on the treatment. He has at least one cutaneous or lymph node mass that is 1 cm or larger and amenable to biopsy and percutaneous injection and can be accurately measured with standard calipers. The patient has been tested for expression of HLA-A2 prior to the study. The patient has detectable intratumoral T cells measured in the index lesion that is to be injected with rF-TRICOMTM by immunohistochemistry (IHC) for CD4, CD8 or another T cell marker, or by real-time RT-PCR for CD8a, CD4, or other T cell transcripts. The patient does not have untreated or edematous brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease, and treated CNS disease is allowed provided the patient remains stable off corticosteroid therapy. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and has been diagnosed with no other concurrent uncontrolled illness that would preclude study participation. The patient has no prior fowlpox virus-based therapy, and more than 4 weeks have passed since the patient's prior chemotherapy.

A 35-year-old male with a family history of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is presenting to the clinic with symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He has undergone a restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) due to the presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in his colon. His genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of FAP. He is currently taking mesalamine to control his symptoms. He has not used any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or probiotics in the past three months. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of sulindac and VSL#3 - inulin in treating or preventing adenoma development in the ileal anal pouch.

55 y/o male with a history of type 2 diabetes diagnosed 5 years ago, controlled on metformin 1000mg twice daily. His most recent HbA1c level was 7.2%. He has a BMI of 28 and a C-peptide level of 2.0 ng/ml. He has no history of hematological abnormalities, liver or kidney disease, congestive heart failure, or malignancies. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how different diets can affect his blood glucose levels.

Patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent a successful kidney transplant surgery three years ago. He is currently receiving Prograf® based immunosuppressive therapy as part of his post-transplant treatment. The patient has stable whole blood trough level concentrations of Prograf® and is clinically stable. He has not received any other organ transplant and is not currently receiving sirolimus immunosuppression therapy. The patient is willing to participate in a Phase II open-label, multi-center conversion study to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety and effectiveness of tacrolimus in stable kidney transplant patients converted from a Prograf® based immunosuppression regimen to a modified release tacrolimus based immunosuppression regimen.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. Despite his best efforts, his glycaemic control has been suboptimal with a recent HbA1c value of 8.5%. He reports feeling overwhelmed by the daily management of his diabetes and has been experiencing depressive symptoms for the past 6 months, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in his usual hobbies. He also reports feeling guilty about his poor glycaemic control and struggles with adhering to his diabetes self-care plan. He speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in a 12-month trial to improve his glycaemic control and manage his depressive symptoms. He is not currently receiving psychiatric or psychotherapeutic treatment and is not taking antidepressant medication. He does not have any history of suicidal ideation or severe mental illness. He does not have any severe somatic illnesses or terminal illness. He is able to provide written informed consent and is not under guardianship.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent upper abdominal pain, fullness, bloating and early satiety for the past three months. She has visited several physicians and underwent several diagnostic tests without obtaining a clear diagnosis. She feels anxious and frustrated about her condition, and her symptoms have started to affect her social life, as she is avoiding eating out or attending social events. She is currently taking over-the-counter antacids and probiotics but has not experienced any significant relief. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that could provide her with a better understanding of her condition and a more comprehensive treatment approach. She has completed high school education and is literate. She does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 35-year-old male patient, originally from Southeast Asia, recently immigrated to the Vallés Occidental region. He complains of fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and nausea. He has no significant medical history but admits to having unprotected sex with multiple partners. Blood tests reveal positive HBsAg, indicating acute hepatitis B infection. He has not received any medical treatment for his condition yet. He is eligible for this clinical trial and can provide valuable data for the study's aim.

A 28-year-old Caucasian woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles, but her partner has been diagnosed with male factor infertility. She has no significant past medical history or known allergies. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She takes a daily multivitamin and follows a healthy diet and exercise regimen. She has previously consented to perform oocyte donation and is willing to donate for research purposes. She has a BMI of 24. She has both ovaries present and an antral follicle count (AFC) of 22. She has not participated in any other clinical studies that could affect the objectives of this study, and is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study. She has signed an informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old female patient who was diagnosed with acute biliary pancreatitis following endoscopic retrograde cholangiography for cholelithiasis. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She has no known allergies or other medical conditions. She has not undergone any prior abdominal surgeries. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 60-year-old woman was brought to the Emergency Department (ED) by her family members after she briefly passed out while getting out of bed this morning. She recovered quickly after lying down and rested for a few minutes before she was brought to the ED. She has no history of any heart disease, stroke, or other serious illnesses. She is on no medications except for a daily multivitamin. She has no allergies, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with lifestyle changes. She has never experienced syncope before. She is concerned about her episode of syncope and wants to know what caused it. She underwent a thorough evaluation in the ED, including an ECG, blood tests, and a physical exam. Her ECG was normal, and her blood tests were within normal limits. Her hematocrit was 36%, and her systolic blood pressure was 120 mm Hg. She did not complain of shortness of breath or chest pain. She was not admitted to the hospital and was advised to follow up with her primary care physician. She was invited to participate in a clinical trial to validate the "San Francisco Syncope Rule".

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years. He is currently taking a combination of medications for his hypertension, including an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high, with a systolic blood pressure of 160 mmHg and a diastolic blood pressure of 95 mmHg. He has no significant medical history, and all his laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is available for hospitalization from the day before the trial medication administration until the morning of the day after administration. He has no known hypersensitivity to angiotensin II receptor antagonists and has not been treated with the trial medication of the present study before. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, possibly pregnant or planning to become pregnant during this study. The investigator has determined that the patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder for the past 5 years. She has been taking lithium as a mood stabilizer for the last 2 years and has been stable on her medication regimen. She is planning to become pregnant and wishes to continue her lithium therapy during her pregnancy. She has sought advice from her psychiatrist who has referred her to this clinical trial. She has no history of substance abuse, suicidal ideation or any other psychiatric illness. She is fluent in English and has the ability to provide informed consent. She is receiving regular obstetrical care and has no other medical conditions. She is excited to participate in this study to help understand the effects of lithium on her and her baby during pregnancy and postpartum.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of angioedema for the past year. She has no known allergies and has not been able to identify any triggers for her angioedema episodes. The episodes typically last for several hours and occur at random intervals. She has not been diagnosed with hereditary angioedema or any other related conditions. She is not currently taking any anticoagulant therapy and has no history of hemostasis disorders. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of the potential role of coagulation pathways in her condition.

A 52-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage III oropharyngeal cancer and is scheduled to undergo radiation treatment. She is physically active and has no history of cancer or radiation treatment. She has completed high school and is proficient in English. The patient has a good orientation to time, person, and place and has a Zubrod performance status of 1. The patient has no history of oropharyngeal dysphagia unrelated to cancer diagnosis. She is interested in participating in a research study to help her complete the swallowing and dental care exercises she is supposed to perform during radiation treatment.

A 55-year-old male came to the clinic for a routine colonoscopy exam. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet consisting of fruits, vegetables, and lean meats. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for colon cancer. He has never had a colon polyp or any symptoms of colon cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with locally advanced primary breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer in her family. She has noticed a lump in her breast and has experienced pain and discomfort. She underwent a mammogram and biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis. She is scheduled for primary surgery (wide local excision or simple mastectomy) and axillary dissection (clearance). She has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. She is a non-smoker, has a healthy lifestyle and exercises regularly. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is concerned about the extent of the disease and the possibility of metastasis. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the ability to determine the extent of breast cancer using enhanced ultrasound.

A 54-year-old woman with a history of primary myelofibrosis presents with worsening fatigue, night sweats, and abdominal discomfort. She has been treated with Ruxolitinib in the past, but has required dose reductions due to myelosuppression. Her most recent bone marrow biopsy showed a fibrotic marrow with a cellularity of 30%, and JAK2 V617F mutation was detected. Her Eastern Co-operative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study. Laboratory tests show an ANC of 125/mL and platelets of 40,000/mL. Her AST and ALT levels are within normal limits, but alkaline phosphatase is 5 times the ULN. Her bilirubin, amylase, and lipase levels are normal. She has attempted 12 weeks of Ruxolitinib therapy, but has required dose reductions and has had an inadequate response. She has never received any investigational product. The patient is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and provide written informed consent.

A 35-year-old female who is a primary snus user is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has been using snus for the past five years, and her usual brand is a non-mint flavor. She reports using one container of her usual brand per week. She does not smoke cigarettes or use any other tobacco or nicotine-containing products. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medication. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. She is willing to use a form of contraception acceptable to the Principal Investigator. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and able to perform the required study procedures. She agrees to exclusively use the investigational product and not use any other tobacco- or nicotine-containing product during the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the last 5 years. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is currently not working and spends most of his time resting at home. He has never had any heart problems in the past. He has not been hospitalized in the last 6 months. His last echocardiogram showed moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation (grade 3/4). His current medications include amlodipine, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand his condition and improve his prognosis. He is able to walk for short distances without any discomfort, but climbing stairs or walking uphill is challenging. His blood pressure is currently 140/90 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 beats per minute. His BMI is 28.5, and he weighs 85 kg. His lab results show a normal lipid profile, FBS: 110 mg/dl, and creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, genotype 1. He has never received treatment for HCV before. He reports mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort but denies any other significant symptoms. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril 20 mg daily. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally on weekends. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild abdominal tenderness. His liver function tests are within normal limits except for slightly elevated AST (60 U/L) and ALT (80 U/L). His HCV RNA level is 1,500,000 IU/mL. He had a liver biopsy 2 years ago, which showed mild fibrosis (F1) and minimal inflammation (A1). He is not co-infected with HIV or hepatitis B virus. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol requirements.

A 48 year old male with a new diagnosis of stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the lower esophagus. He has no prior history of cancer or treatment for cancer. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He has no tracheo-oesophageal fistulas or direct invasion of the tracheal mucosa or major bronchi. He has not received prior thoracic radiotherapy, systemic chemotherapy, or esophageal surgery. He has no history of atrioventricular arrhythmia, cardiac failure, or second or third degree heart block. He has no history of significant coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction in the last 12 months. He has no active infection, uncontrolled hypertension, active uncontrolled gastric or duodenal peptic ulcer, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring hospitalization in the 6 months prior to inclusion in the study. He has no history of drug abuse or known allergic reactions to any of the components in the study treatment. He is willing to use an effective contraceptive method if there is a risk of conception and/or pregnancy. His tumour tissue is available for immunohistochemical analysis of EGFR expression and other biological markers.

54 y/o female with a recent diagnosis of breast cancer, currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She reports experiencing moderate to severe pain in her breast and chest area, which has been ongoing for the past month. She has been taking pain medication prescribed by her oncologist, but has not experienced significant relief. She reports that the pain is affecting her ability to perform daily activities and is causing her distress. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the consent form. She has not had any recent operations or interventional therapy related to her cancer pain. She is fluent in English and is able to cooperate with the study requirements. She does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with end-stage renal disease due to polycystic kidney disease. He has been on the kidney transplant waiting list for over 4 years and has developed anti-HLA antibodies against potential donors. His current anti-HLA antibody MFI is 4,500. He is willing to undergo desensitization therapy in order to increase his chances of receiving a kidney transplant. He has a normal recent cardiac workup and has been vaccinated against pneumococcus and meningococcus B and C. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and is affiliated with a social security scheme. He has no active underlying infections or neoplasia. He does not have any contra-indications for rituximab, tocilizumab, or apheresis.

A 65-year-old female with a body mass index of 35 kg/m2 visits the clinic with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and reduced physical activity. She reports difficulty falling and staying asleep at night, and feels unrested in the morning. She has no history of diabetes, liver dysfunction, or active neoplasms. However, she does report a history of hypertension and mild cognitive impairment. She is on medication for hypertension and has regular follow up with her physician. Her physical examination reveals reduced muscle mass, and she experiences difficulty in performing daily activities. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to identify biomarkers of sleep quality, sarcopenia, insulin resistance, oxidative stress, and inflammation associated with prefrailty in middle-aged and elderly obese subjects. She is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the study protocol.

A 35 year old woman came to the clinic with a complaint of chronic diarrhea and abdominal cramps for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and has tried several conventional therapies without success. She is experiencing at least three bowel movements per day with urgency and loose stools. She also reports bloating, gas and abdominal discomfort. She is willing to make daily calls on a touch-tone telephone. In the physical exam, she has no significant findings. Her TSH is within normal limits. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no history of malignancy.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory failure caused by severe pneumonia. He has a history of COPD and was already on home oxygen therapy prior to admission. On admission, he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. His arterial and central venous lines were placed for hemodynamic monitoring. A urinary catheter was also inserted for routine monitoring. The patient is responsive to verbal stimuli but appeared to be in significant respiratory distress. His vital signs are stable but his arterial blood gas analysis indicated a mild respiratory acidosis with a pH of 7.31 and partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) of 52 mmHg. The patient is eligible for the study because he meets the inclusion criteria of having mechanical ventilation, arterial and central venous lines, and a urinary catheter. He is also eligible because he does not have acute or chronic renal failure with anuria, continuous renal replacement therapy, hemodynamic instability, or is less than 16 years of age.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who received a heart transplant 6 years ago due to end-stage heart failure. He was enrolled in the SCHEDULE (NCT01266148) study, where he received early initiation of everolimus and early elimination of cyclosporine as part of his immunosuppressive regimen. He completed the 12-month main study and the 3-year follow-up visit. He is currently due for his routine annual clinic visit, which will also serve as a 5-year follow-up examination since his transplantation and inclusion in the original SCHEDULE study. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has not experienced any major adverse events related to his immunosuppressive therapy. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use illicit drugs. He is interested in participating in the follow-up examination and has provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 72-year-old man with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently under the care of the Family Health Unit in Recife, Northeast Brazil. He has been struggling to manage his diabetes and maintain a healthy lifestyle. He has a history of smoking, but quit 10 years ago. He lives alone and does not have any mobility issues. He is able to perform his activities of daily living independently. He has not been hospitalized recently, and he does not have any chronic complications of diabetes in advanced stages. He can communicate effectively, and his cognition is intact. However, he has limited knowledge of diabetes and its management. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that can help him improve his diabetes management and promote healthy habits.

4-year-old male with a history of hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention. Parents report difficulty with following instructions, staying on task, and regulating emotions. The child is easily distracted and has a hard time completing age-appropriate activities independently. The child has not been on medication for ADHD before. The child's IQ is estimated to be above 80. The parents are willing to participate in a non-pharmacological intervention study for their child's ADHD. There is no history of other severe mental disorders or physical diseases that may interfere with the assessment and intervention.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has decided to undergo robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) surgery. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications. He lives with his wife and has two adult children who live nearby. He is fluent in Dutch and can read and fill out questionnaires without any difficulty. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2. He does not have any liver or renal disease, neuromuscular disease, hyperthyroidism, or coagulopathy. He has never had an allergic reaction to any of the medications or substances listed in the exclusion criteria. He is aware of the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with uterine leiomyosarcoma that has progressed despite previous treatment.
