She has a history of surgery and radiation therapy for the primary tumor. She presents with abdominal pain and bloating, along with other non-specific symptoms. Imaging studies reveal the presence of measurable lesions in the abdomen and pelvis. The patient has a GOG performance status of 1 and no other invasive malignancy within the past 5 years. Her platelet count is 120,000/mm³, absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mm³, and hemoglobin level is 11 g/dL. Her creatinine level is within normal limits, and her bilirubin, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and CPK levels are also normal. She has no active infection requiring antibiotics and no neuropathy greater than grade 1. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or biologic therapy for uterine sarcoma, and has not received chemotherapy for any abdominal or pelvic tumor within the past 5 years. She has not received trabectedin or radiotherapy within the past 5 years to any portion of the abdominal cavity or pelvis other than for treatment of uterine sarcoma. She has not received concurrent amifostine or other protective agents. The patient is willing and able to have a central venous catheter.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who regularly engages in physical activity and maintains a healthy lifestyle. She has no known medical conditions or history of respiratory issues. She enjoys singing and has some experience with it, but is not a professional singer. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the physiological demands of singing for lung health. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies or other health conditions that would prevent her from participating in the singing or walking components of the study. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study's exercise instructions.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. Despite previous treatment with Docetaxel, the disease has progressed and the patient has received at least one of the four FDA-approved therapies, such as Abiraterone Acetate, Enzalutamide, Cabazitaxel, or Radium-223. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-1 and at least one measurable site of disease. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has a castrate level of testosterone maintained by continued gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues. The patient has not had major surgery within the past 4 weeks and is not experiencing concurrent uncontrolled medical conditions that may interfere with participation in the study or affect the interpretation of the study data. The patient has no neuromuscular disorders, active uncontrolled or symptomatic central nervous system metastases or a history of hypersensitivity to LDE225 or drugs of similar chemical classes. The patient is not planning to embark on a new strenuous exercise regimen after initiation of study treatment and has not taken part in an experimental drug study within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, of initiating treatment with LDE225. The patient is not receiving other anti-neoplastic therapy besides Docetaxel and is not receiving treatment with medications known to be moderate and strong inhibitors or inducers of Cytochrome P450 3A4/5 (CYP3A4/5) or drugs metabolized by Cytochrome P450 2B6 (CYP2B6) or Cytochrome P450 2C9 (CYP2C9) that have narrow therapeutic index. The patient does not require the use of warfarin (substrate of CYP2C9) and does not have impaired cardiac function or clinically significant heart disease.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital for exacerbation of his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He takes multiple medications for his chronic conditions, including a beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor, a statin, and insulin. He lives alone and has difficulty remembering to take his medications on schedule, which has led to missed doses and occasional hospitalizations for exacerbations of his chronic conditions. He is interested in participating in a study that may help him better manage his medications and reduce his risk of hospitalization. He is able to use technology, including smartphones and computers, and has a basic understanding of how to use electronic devices. His physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable except for his chronic conditions.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old male who has tested negative for HIV on ELISA. He has no history of immunodeficiency, chronic illness, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. His HLA haplotype includes one or more of the following alleles: A33, B8, B27, B35, or Bw62. He has not received any live attenuated vaccines in the past 60 days and has not used any experimental agents in the past 30 days. He has not received any blood products or immunoglobulin in the past 6 months. He has not engaged in injection drug use within the last 12 months prior to enrollment and has lower risk sexual behavior as defined by AVEG. He is available for follow-up for the planned duration of the study, which is 12 months.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. He has a history of diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease. He has been hospitalized several times over the past year for complications related to his chronic conditions. He is currently on multiple medications to manage his conditions. He is alert and oriented, but complains of feeling weak and tired. His vital signs are stable, but his blood glucose levels are elevated. He is admitted to the General Hospitals Wards of Barnes-Jewish Hospital for further management of his conditions.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her joints for the past year. She is married and works as a nurse. She has two children, ages 12 and 14. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She takes methotrexate and prednisone for her RA. She has no other chronic medical conditions and her lab results are within normal limits. She speaks French fluently and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled for a surgical procedure that requires general anesthesia. He has a medical history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is otherwise healthy. The patient has never had a reaction to the BIS patch or any other anesthesia in the past. He is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the study. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He is classified as ASA I-II. The patient has no allergies to any medication or medical devices.

The patient is a 50-year-old male smoker with a 30-year history of cigarette use. He smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and has a cough with occasional sputum production. He reports no shortness of breath or wheezing. His lung function test shows mild to moderate airflow obstruction. He has no history of asthma or allergies. He is not currently taking any medications and has no significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo repeated bronchoscopies for long-term follow-up.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of his body. He has undergone hormonal therapy, but his disease has progressed despite the treatment. He complains of fatigue, weight loss, and difficulty urinating. His physical exam shows an enlarged prostate and no other abnormalities. His lab results show a serum PSA level of 10 ng/mL. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has no history of brain metastasis. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two adult children. He has not received any cytotoxic chemotherapy or radioisotope therapy in the past. He has not received any cytochrome P450 enzyme-inducing antiepileptic drugs or rifampin or St. John's wort. He is not taking any inhibitors of CYP3A or combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV. He is willing to use effective contraception during and for at least 3 months after completion of study therapy, as he is fertile.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV renal cancer. He has undergone surgery and radiation therapy, but the cancer has metastasized to his lungs and liver. He has been on chemotherapy for the last 3 months, but his cancer has progressed despite treatment. He is now eligible for the cyclophosphamide plus vaccine therapy clinical trial. He has no significant medical history and is HIV negative. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is physically active and has no significant cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. His performance status is ECOG 1. He is willing to participate in the trial and understands the risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with hormone receptor (HR)+, HER2- node-negative breast cancer. She has no history of any other cancer. She has a history of hypertension and is currently being treated for it. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading books in her free time. She was initially seen with a lump in her breast, and a biopsy confirmed breast cancer. The tumor is clinically stage I. She has no evidence of any lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. Her pathology is ER/PR-positive and HER2-negative. She is advised to undergo neoadjuvant endocrine therapy for four weeks as part of this clinical trial. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has undergone all the required baseline evaluations and her lab values are within normal limits. She is using adequate methods of contraception and has tested negative for pregnancy.

The patient is a 28-year-old primigravida who is currently 31 weeks pregnant. She presents to the obstetric clinic with complaints of sudden onset of swelling in her hands and feet, along with a headache and visual disturbances for the past 2 days. Her blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg, and she has proteinuria +2 on urine dipstick. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not on any medications. She denies any significant family history of hypertension or preeclampsia. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her prenatal care has been regular, with no significant issues noted during previous visits. She has no known chronic diseases, and she has not been diagnosed with any autoimmune disorders. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with colorectal cancer. He is scheduled for a planned resection surgery. He has a BMI of 28 and has no known allergies. He has not had any prior laparotomy or abdominal surgery. He is not currently on antibiotics and has not had any active infections. The incision length for his surgery meets the labeling requirements for the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent using the governing IRB approved form.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain and distension. Imaging studies reveal a perforated viscus, and the patient is scheduled for emergency abdominal surgery. Following the surgery, the patient experiences complications such as anastomotic leaks and post-operative bleeding that require repeat surgery. The patient is between the ages of 18-99 and meets the inclusion criteria for the Emergency General Surgery for Non-trauma clinical trial. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and will be followed up for 1 year after discharge. The patient understands that the study involves no additional treatment or interventions and that the potential benefits of the study may help future patients with similar conditions. The patient is aware of the potential risks of breach of confidentiality, but is confident in the research team's ability to maintain confidentiality and protect his PHI.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with cervical cancer during a routine gynecological examination. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma in situ. She has no history of any other malignancy, and her performance status is good. The tumor size is less than 2cm, and there is no evidence of lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. She has no relevant medical history and her Karnofsky index score is 90. She has been informed of the study and has provided written consent to participate. She is willing to undergo either sentinel lymph node dissection or entire pelvic lymph node dissection and has no contraindications for the anesthesia. She understands the study requirements and is able to comply with the follow-up visits.

A 65 year old male presented to the clinic complaining of episodes of transient vision loss in his left eye, weakness and numbness in his left arm and leg, and difficulty speaking. He has a history of smoking for 30 years, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Upon examination, carotid bruits were present bilaterally. An initial carotid ultrasound showed a greater than 50% stenosis in the left carotid artery. Further imaging is required to determine the best course of treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has attempted suicide and recently left the emergency department. She has been struggling with depression and anxiety for the past year and has been receiving treatment from a mental health professional. She is able to provide written informed consent and owns a mobile phone that can be used for SMS monitoring. She is not under guardianship and is capable of making her own medical decisions. She is willing to participate in the study and hopes that it will help her manage her suicidal thoughts and behaviors.

This is a 62 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has a Gleason score of 8 and his PSA level is 22. He has no history of cancer in his family, but is of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry. He has access to a computer and the internet, and is interested in learning more about genetic testing for prostate cancer. He has not undergone genetic testing for inherited cancer risk before. He is able to provide informed consent and communicates effectively in English.

Patient is a 34-year-old female who has presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain. She rates her pain as 8/10 on the visual analog scale (VAS). She has a history of endometriosis and has been experiencing worsening pain for the past few days. There is no nausea or vomiting, but she has been experiencing constipation. She has not taken any pain medications prior to arrival at the emergency department. The patient consents to participate in the study and has no contraindications to the products used in the course of the study. She is not experiencing any vital distress and is able to adequately assess the intensity of her pain according to the VAS.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who lives in a rural area of the state. She has a history of high blood pressure, but her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with word-finding, which has been concerning to her and her family. She has no history of neurologic or psychiatric disorders, and her physical exam is unremarkable. She takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and aspirin 81 mg daily. She has completed high school and some college coursework. She has no difficulty with hearing or vision. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on cognitive testing methods and their potential benefits for patients like herself who live in rural areas.

A 45-year old male accountant has been diagnosed with Barrett's esophagus with intestinal metaplasia without dysplasia during a routine upper endoscopy. He has a history of heartburn and acid reflux for the past 10 years. He used to take over-the-counter antacids and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) as needed. He denies any weight loss, difficulty swallowing, or chest pain. He is married with two children and he is a non-smoker. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes Amlodipine. He does not have any significant past medical history. His physical exam is unremarkable. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to undergo extra biopsies and brushings. He is able to tolerate the blood draw and has signed the informed consent form. He is willing to complete questionnaires and attend future endoscopic procedures for extra biopsies.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease and has been receiving continuous hemodialysis (CVVHD) for the past 2 months. She has an indwelling arterial line for monitoring purposes. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of cardiac arrhythmias or any other significant medical conditions. Her vital signs show a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98%. She has no fever or signs of infection. Her lab results show a serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL and serum electrolyte levels within normal limits. She is not pregnant and her temperature is normal. She has no history of open thoracic cavity or non-pulsatile cardiac flow.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with coronary artery disease through coronary angiography. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He has not undergone any previous heart surgeries or procedures such as CABG or PCI. He has no history of malignant tumors or chronic kidney disease. He has not experienced any external ear trauma or diseases. He is willing to participate in the study and have images of his ears taken to calculate his Frank Score for correlation analysis with his Syntax Score.

A 10-year-old male with a history of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) for 8 months, having had an insufficient response to previous treatment, is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. The child's platelet count averages 25×10^9/L, with no single count greater than 35×10^9/L during the screening period. The child has no known history of secondary ITP or thrombosis, inherited thrombocytopenia, myelodysplastic syndrome or congenital heart abnormalities or arrhythmias.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is experiencing pain and limited range of motion in her right shoulder, which has been ongoing for the past 4 months. She has tried physical therapy, rest, and over-the-counter pain medications, but her symptoms have not improved. An MRI revealed a full thickness supraspinatus tendon tear, and her orthopedic surgeon has recommended surgical intervention in the form of a rotator cuff repair. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of autoimmune connective tissue disorders, and is willing and able to provide informed consent and participate in all procedures and follow-up evaluations necessary to complete the study. She has not had any previous surgery on her right arm within the past 6 months, and does not have any significant medical conditions that would interfere with protocol evaluation and participation. She is not pregnant and has no known allergy or sensitivity to aminoglycoside antibiotics. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial involving the use of human dehydrated umbilical cord allograft in her supraspinatus tendon repair, and understands that she may be randomized to either receive the allograft or not.

This is a 45 year-old male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and a left bundle branch block. Despite optimal medical therapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and beta-blockers, he remains in NYHA functional class III with symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. His echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30% and a QRS duration of 160 milliseconds. The patient has not had any recent episodes of acute heart failure or interventions for coronary artery disease. He is in sinus rhythm and has no known allergies to sulphur hexafluoride. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing and able to provide written informed consent.

As this is an observational study, there are no specific patient descriptions required for enrollment. However, eligible participants for this study include residents of Bocozel or Grande Saline who were at least 12 months of age at the time of completion of the cholera vaccine campaign and were not pregnant at the time of vaccination. Cholera cases must seek treatment for acute non-bloody diarrhea and be diagnosed with cholera through rapid testing and culture. Non-cholera diarrhea cases must seek treatment for acute non-bloody diarrhea and test negative for cholera through rapid testing and culture. Controls must be residents of Bocozel or Grande Saline who did not seek treatment for diarrhea during the study period and were eligible for the vaccination campaign.

A 30-year-old male veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan came to the VA hospital with chronic pain and symptoms of PTSD. He has been experiencing recurring flashbacks and nightmares of his time in combat, causing him to have difficulty sleeping and concentrating. He also reports having physical pain in his lower back, neck, and shoulders, which he attributes to his military service. The patient is currently enrolled in the PTSD treatment program at VACHS, West Haven, and is willing to participate in a 12-week Mindful Yoga Therapy program that requires him to attend two 75-minute sessions per week. The patient has no prior regular yoga or meditation practice in the past month and is not diagnosed with comorbid psychotic disorders or bipolar disorder. The patient speaks and reads English fluently and is willing to undergo diagnostic, neurocognitive, and psychophysiological assessments as part of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has been diagnosed with the disease for several months and has received no previous chemotherapy for the metastasis. The cancer has spread into his liver and lungs, causing him to experience severe fatigue, abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. He has no history of other medical conditions except for hypertension, which is well-controlled by medication. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently able to perform his daily activities but finds them difficult due to the pain and fatigue. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to try and improve his condition. On physical examination, he appears well-nourished, alert, and cooperative. His blood pressure is within normal limits, and he has no evidence of any neurological or cardiovascular abnormalities. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 40-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and a BMI of 29 has been struggling with weight loss despite dietary modifications and medication. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works in an office. He has no history of heart disease but has a family history of type 2 diabetes. He takes metformin to control his blood sugar levels. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. He exercises occasionally but finds it difficult to maintain a consistent routine. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him lose weight and control his hunger.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis for the past 2 years. He has been experiencing mild gait ataxia and a restricted ambulation, with a walking duration of less than an hour. He is able to walk at least 50 meters with the aid of a walking aid. He understands the purpose and risks of the study and has provided signed and dated informed consent. He has not been treated with fampridine or 3,4-diaminopyridine in any formulation prior to this study. He does not have a history of seizure, epilepsy, or other convulsive disorder, except for febrile seizures during childhood. He has not undergone any treatment with anti-epileptic medications specifically prescribed for the treatment of epilepsy. He has not experienced an MS exacerbation within the 60 days prior to the screening visit. He has not used mitoxantrone, cyclophosphamide, rituximab, alemtuzumab, daclizumab, cladribine, or any other immune suppressant (except FTY720) or antibody (except natalizumab) within 3 months prior to the screening visit, or scheduled use during study participation. He has not undergone pulsed steroid treatment within the 60 days prior to the screening visit, or at any time during the screening period. He does not have any significant concomitant disease states such as renal failure, hepatic dysfunction, cardiovascular or pulmonary disease, malignant disease, or acute urinary tract infection. He is willing and able to practice effective contraception during the study and for 30 days after his last dose of study treatment. He is able to understand the patient information sheet and comply with the requirements of the protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who is scheduled for an elective surgery. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He has no other significant medical history, including no malignancies or recent heart issues. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has not had any epileptic seizures in the past 3 months. He is married and has two adult children. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce the number of procedures required to obtain preoperative autologous erythrocytes. The patient is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all necessary appointments.

The patient is a 42-year-old right-handed woman who is concerned about her weight. Her BMI is in the range of 28-35 kg/m2. She works as an accountant and has been married for 10 years. She has two children aged 8 and 10 years old. She does not smoke or use drugs, and she drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no history of major psychiatric disorders or medical or neurological disorders. She has not taken any drugs that could affect cerebral blood flow or neurological function within the past 3 weeks. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her control over food cravings and eating behavior.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on evaluating a new strategy for healthcare professionals to improve compliance with infection prevention practices, and does not involve direct patient care.

A 53-year-old man has been diagnosed with early-stage Parkinson's disease. He has completed the pivotal, double-blind S308.3.003 trial and is willing and eligible to continue with the open-label safety extension study. He has no other major medical conditions and is not taking any other medications for Parkinson's disease. He has a history of high blood pressure and is currently taking medication to control it. He underwent a physical examination and ECG at the end of the maintenance phase of the previous study and had no abnormal findings. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is interested in contributing to Parkinson's disease research.

This clinical trial does not have any specific eligibility criteria or patient population. It aims to examine the relationships of obesity and fat patterning with morbidity and mortality in Black Americans using data from the Charleston Heart Study, which began in 1960 with the examination of a random sample of 2181 residents of Charleston County, including approximately one-third of the sample being Black. The study includes cross-sectional relationships between anthropometric measures of body dimensions and dependent variables of diabetes, blood pressure, plasma lipids and glucose, and left ventricular wall thickness, as well as the identification of anthropometric predictors of survival over a 25 year period with reference to mortality for coronary heart disease, cardiovascular disease, and all-cause mortality. The study also examines changes in the shapes of individuals over a 24 year interval and the importance of changes in anthropometric measurements with aging for predicting various health outcomes. Therefore, this clinical trial does not require any specific patient description.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD5D) for 3 years. She has been on dialysis for the past year and her vascular access has a blood flow of more than 300ml/min. She has no history of neoplasia or hepatitis B. She has a family history of heart disease, with her father having had a heart attack at the age of 60. She is currently taking medications for hypertension and has a BMI of 28. She has no other significant medical history and is a non-smoker. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56 year-old man who has been diagnosed with a pancreatic tumor that requires surgical resection. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has not undergone any major surgeries in the past. He has good understanding of the study requirements and has provided written informed consent. He has health insurance cover. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is scheduled to undergo a pancreatic resection with or without anastomosis (cephalic duodenopancreatectomy, median pancreatectomy, left pancreatectomy, enucleation) and is able to comply with the instructions and information provided for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chordoma, a rare type of bone cancer that occurs in the skull base and spine. He has undergone surgery and radiation therapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. He is in overall good health with a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80%. His blood work shows adequate organ function, with normal levels of ANC, platelets, hemoglobin, bilirubin, ALT, AST, and serum creatinine. He does not have any active bacterial, fungal, or viral infections. He has no history of cardiovascular conditions or syncope of cardiovascular etiology. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. He is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a newborn baby who requires intensive care in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge. The baby is being monitored continuously for heart rate, oxygen levels, and temperature using specially designed monitors. The baby is currently tethered to the monitors with wires. The clinical team is considering using a new wireless monitoring system that would free the baby from the wires. The study has two parts. In the first part, the accuracy of the new wireless system will be compared to the existing wired system. In the second part, the parent(s) will be asked to hold the baby for Kangaroo Care while being monitored with the new wireless system, and their experience will be assessed through an interview. The study population will include up to 24 participants recruited from the NICU at Addenbrooke's Hospital. The eligibility criteria include written, informed parental consent, being cared for on the NICU, and no intolerance to silicone or silicone gel adhesives, or pacemaker or other implanted electronic device.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been experiencing migraine with aura for the past two years. She experiences severe headache, vision disturbances, and nausea during her attacks. She has tried various medications for the treatment of her migraine, but has not found any significant relief. She has a history of transient ischemic attack (TIA) and has been diagnosed with a patent foramen ovale (PFO) with a moderate-to-large right-to-left shunt. She has been advised to undergo a PFO closure procedure to prevent future TIAs and strokes. She has normal blood pressure and heart rate and her BMI is within the normal range. She is not currently taking any medications, but has a history of allergies to aspirin and nickel. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of PFO closure on her migraine symptoms.

Pt is a 60yo F with a history of osteoarthritis of the right knee, which has led to significant pain and limited mobility. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, corticosteroid injections, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs but has not experienced significant relief. She is considering total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as a treatment option. She does not have any significant medical history that would prevent her from undergoing surgery. She is willing and able to give informed consent and is within the age range of 21 and 80 years old. She has no prior arthroplasty, patellectomy or osteotomy with the affected knee. She does not have significant co-morbidity that affects her ability to ambulate. Her flexion contracture is less than 15 degrees and extension lag less than 10 degrees. On standing AP radiograph, her tibial subluxation is less than 10 mm. She does not have lateral or medial collateral ligament instability (less than 10° varus/valgus), and her leg length discrepancy is less than 10 mm. Her bone quality does not preclude uncemented fixation. She is not pregnant and has no active or prior infection. She does not have morbid obesity (BMI < 40) or medical conditions that preclude major surgery. She does not have severe osteoporosis or osteopenia, nor does she have any neuromuscular impairment. She is thus eligible to participate in this study to determine if the reprocessed saw blades used during TKA work as well as a new saw blade.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing hearing loss for the past 5 years. He has difficulty hearing conversations, especially in noisy environments. He has also noticed that he needs to turn up the volume on the TV and radio to hear them clearly. He has not received any audiological intervention before. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He is married and has two adult children who live nearby. He enjoys reading books and watching movies, but his hearing loss has made it difficult to enjoy these activities. He does not have any significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. His family history is negative for hearing problems. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his hearing and overall quality of life.

A 67-year-old retired engineer was diagnosed with prostate cancer five years ago. He underwent radical prostatectomy followed by radiation therapy. He was started on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with leuprolide and bicalutamide. He tolerated ADT well and had a good quality of life. Three years ago, he developed progressive bone pain, and his imaging showed metastatic prostate cancer. He was started on abiraterone and prednisone. He achieved a good response with abiraterone, but his PSA started to rise after about a year. He then underwent docetaxel chemotherapy and achieved a partial response. He has been off chemotherapy for six months, and his PSA is now rising again. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new drug for his cancer. He is married and has two adult children. He is fairly active, enjoys spending time with his family, and enjoys reading. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. He has no other significant medical history. He is willing to provide blood samples and tumor tissue for research.

A 6-year-old girl was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit with severe acute respiratory infection symptoms, including cough, runny nose, and fever. The patient's parents reported that she had been experiencing these symptoms for three days and they had progressively worsened. Upon admission, the patient was found to have difficulty breathing and was immediately intubated. A nasopharyngeal swab was taken for laboratory analysis. The patient was diagnosed with laboratory-confirmed influenza and was treated with antiviral medication. The patient's clinical course was complicated by acute respiratory distress syndrome and sepsis, requiring mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Despite aggressive treatment, the patient's condition deteriorated, and on day 5 of admission, the patient died due to influenza-associated complications. The patient's parents provided informed consent for participation in the study. The patient's medical history was significant for chronic lung disease and a history of hospitalization for pneumonia.

A 40-year-old male with a history of trauma to the right shoulder and upper extremity requiring surgical intervention is being considered for a clinical trial to prevent chronic post-surgical pain (CPSP). The patient had previously been healthy and physically active, working as a construction worker. However, following the trauma, he has been experiencing severe pain in the right shoulder and arm, limiting his ability to work and perform daily activities. The patient understands English and has given written consent to participate in the study. He has not been diagnosed with any chronic pain conditions or major depression, and is not currently using opioids. The patient will be assigned to either a group that receives a single shot brachial plexus block or a control group that receives general anesthesia only, based on the preference of the patient or the surgeon. The patient will be followed up for 6 months to assess pain scores and pain interference through a questionnaire and Brief Pain Inventory.

A 65-year-old male patient who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is being evaluated for the comparison of femoral prosthesis-rotation in conventional x-ray, axial CT slices and 3D-reconstructed CT. The patient has no significant medical history and has been experiencing pain and discomfort in his knee. He has been experiencing difficulty in walking and performing daily activities. The patient has undergone physical therapy and medication, but the pain persists. The patient is not lactating or pregnant. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old African American woman came to the clinic with a history of hypertension. She was diagnosed with hypertension five years ago and has been taking amlodipine 5mg daily, but her blood pressure remained uncontrolled. She measures her blood pressure at home using a digital monitor, and the readings are usually higher compared to her office visits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of a new antihypertensive drug called Rasilez. She is not currently taking any other medication for hypertension or any other medical condition. She has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary artery bypass graft, percutaneous transluminal coronary intervention, congestive heart failure, or renal failure. She has no malignancy or medical condition that would prevent her from completing the study. She is willing to sign an informed consent form and is committed to complying with the study requirements.

A 38-year-old woman was diagnosed with a single endometrial polyp through a diagnostic hysteroscopy. The size of the polyp is approximately 1.5 centimeters. She has no history of gynecological malignancy and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and has given her informed consent. She has social security coverage and no contraindications to general or spinal anesthesia. She does not have any associated submucosal myomas or other pathologies.

The patient is a 72-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was admitted to the hospital for an elective coronary angiography due to recent chest pain. The patient has a serum creatinine level of 1.8 mg/dL, indicating chronic renal failure. He is not on dialysis and has not been previously included in the trial. The patient agrees to participate in the study and provides informed consent.

The patient is an 80 year old male living alone in a small apartment in Manhattan. He has been housebound for the past year due to his difficulty in walking and performing daily activities. He requires assistance for bathing, dressing, and preparing meals. He has a history of multiple hospitalizations in the past year due to recurrent infections and falls. He has Medicare coverage and is able to provide informed consent. He speaks English fluently. He has no active drug use or firearms in his home. He is willing to accept a home-based primary care physician as his primary care physician. He has no cognitive impairment and is able to communicate effectively. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive better care and improve his quality of life.

54 yo M with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and heart failure (EF 35%) with persistent symptoms despite maximal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) including an ACE inhibitor, beta-blocker, and loop diuretic. The patient has fatigue with minimal activity, shortness of breath with only minimal exertion, and recurrent hospitalizations for heart failure exacerbations. The patient has a history of low serum total T3 levels (measured at 80 ng/dL) with normal TSH levels. The patient is stable with no changes in functional class or hospitalizations for 2 weeks prior to screening. The patient is currently on a stable dose of GDMT for at least 3 months prior to randomization. The patient has an LVEF of 35% documented within 6 months prior to randomization. The patient is able to give informed consent and meets all other inclusion criteria. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and is using reliable contraception. The patient has not had a myocardial infarction, unstable ischemic heart disease, stroke, or a coronary revascularization procedure within 4 weeks prior to randomization, nor does the patient expect a coronary revascularization procedure, cardiac transplant, or left ventricular assist device placement in the next 24 weeks. The patient has not received any other investigational agent or device within 4 weeks prior to randomization. The patient has no non-cardiac underlying medical conditions expected to impact mortality within 24 weeks after randomization. The patient has not been diagnosed with other thyroid disorders or used thyroid supplements or any preparation containing thyromimetic agents within 24 weeks prior to randomization. The patient has no supraventricular arrhythmia refractory to conventional treatment. The patient is willing to comply with study requirements and has provided informed consent.

A 50-year-old man was referred to the study with a history of cirrhosis diagnosed 2 years ago due to alcohol abuse. He has been sober for 18 months, and he is currently under the care of a hepatologist. He is taking furosemide and spironolactone to control his ascites. He reports mild fatigue but denies other symptoms such as jaundice or itching. He has no history of hepatitis B or C, and his liver function tests are mildly elevated. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and his weight is 80 kg. He has no history of allergies to amide-type local anesthetics or any other medications. He is willing and capable of providing written informed consent for the study.

There is no need for a patient description in this clinical trial as it is focused on anesthesia care providers rather than patients. The study aims to survey the attitudes of anesthesia care providers towards pay for performance (P4P) and how they may differ between faculty, CRNAs, and residents. The goal is to understand their concerns and modify the P4P program accordingly to maintain job satisfaction.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who is a non-smoker and has a body mass index of 26 kg/m2. He has no history of HIV, hepatitis C, or hepatitis B virus, and has never received an H5N1 influenza vaccine. He has not participated in any other clinical trial within the last 30 days and has no metal implants at the site of injection. He does not have any autoimmune disease, serious medical conditions, or any process that would affect his immune response. He is not currently taking immunosuppressive drugs or systemic or topical steroids (excluding inhaled and eye drop-containing corticosteroids). He has not received any blood products within the last 3 months and has not used any drugs of addiction or daily alcohol use greater than the study limit in the week prior to starting the study. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and has provided written informed consent in accordance with institutional guidelines. He has a deltoid or quadriceps available for injection and does not have primary thrombocytopenia.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking for 15 years, averaging 15 cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit several times before using nicotine replacement therapy and other medications, but has not been successful. She is motivated to quit smoking and is not currently taking any medication for depression, psychosis, or cognitive disorders. She has no history of substance abuse other than smoking and has not been abstinent from cigarettes for more than 3 months in the past year. She is not currently using any nicotine replacement therapy, bupropion, varenicline, clonidine, or nortriptyline, nor has she undergone cognitive-behavioral therapy for smoking cessation in the past 3 months. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception during the study if she is premenopausal. She is affiliated with a health insurance system and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Sophie is a 28-year-old woman who works as a flight attendant. She has been experiencing severe anxiety and fear of heights for as long as she can remember. She avoids going up tall buildings, crossing bridges, and flying, which is making it difficult for her to perform her job properly. She has tried different types of therapy, including cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and exposure therapy, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She has never received any brain stimulation treatment or been diagnosed with any neurological or severe physical illnesses. Sophie is a German native speaker and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of blurred vision and floaters in his left eye. He was diagnosed with a macular hole, and his ophthalmologist recommended vitreoretinal surgery. The patient has no significant medical history and does not smoke nor drink alcohol. He is currently taking over-the-counter ibuprofen for pain management, but he does not have any other medications or allergies. The patient has no known history of complications with surgeries or anesthesia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the management of pain and inflammation following retinal surgery using a dexamethasone implant compared with topical steroids.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain for several months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. He is a heavy smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and his cardiologist recommended an elective on-pump cardiac surgery. His preoperative laboratory results show a red cell distribution width of 14.5%, a mean platelet volume of 8.2 fL, a platelet/lymphocyte ratio of 22, and a neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio of 3.5. He has no known allergies and has never had any previous surgeries. He is married and works as a sales executive. He is able to perform regular daily activities without difficulty, but he experiences shortness of breath and chest pain during physical activity. He weighs 90 kg and is 175 cm tall, with a BMI of 29.4. He is not currently taking any medications for pain or discomfort. He is interested in participating in the study to help researchers determine factors that may help predict outcomes in cardiac surgery.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior systemic anticancer therapy for the treatment of his renal cell carcinoma. He has undergone a total nephrectomy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1 and is in the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) good or intermediate category. His bone marrow, liver, and renal function are adequate, as assessed by the laboratory requirements conducted within 7 days prior to treatment. The patient's life expectancy is at least 12 weeks. The patient has no history of cardiac disease or bleeding diathesis. He has not had deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolus within 12 months of the start of treatment. The patient does not have a history of delayed healing of wounds, ulcers, or bone fractures. He is not undergoing renal dialysis. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has a negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days prior to the start of treatment. He is willing to use adequate barrier birth control measures during the course of the trial and three months after the completion of the trial. The patient has not undergone major surgery or radiotherapy within 4 weeks of the start of the study, nor has he received any investigational drug therapy outside of this trial during or within 4 weeks of study entry.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been experiencing pain in his lower right jaw for several weeks. He has been advised by his dentist that he needs to have his impacted lower right third molar extracted. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is physically fit and exercises regularly. He works as a software developer and is fluent in English. He provides written informed consent prior to enrollment. He is not pregnant or lactating. He does not plan on becoming pregnant during the duration of the study. He is willing and capable of understanding and cooperating with the requirements of the study. He has not participated in any previous placebo response and pain scale education training program. He does not have any medical condition that could adversely impact his participation, safety, or conduct of the study. He does not have a known history of intolerance, severe allergy, or hypersensitivity to Ibuprofen, opioid analgesics, Lidocaine, or acetaminophen. He has not abused any prescription medication or alcohol within two years before the start of the study. He has no surgical complications that could compromise his safety or confound the results of the study. He is not taking any corticosteroid chronically or has taken systemic corticosteroids within 4 weeks of the proposed date of surgery. He is not taking any central nervous system (CNS) active drugs such as benzodiazepines, tricyclic antidepressants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) or serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) for pain. He has not used acetylsalicylic acid, acetaminophen or nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug (NSAIDs) within 5 half-lives prior to the planned day of the surgery. He is not taking an antihypertensive agent(s) or a diabetic regimen at a dose that has not been stable for at least 28 days. He does not have a history of seizures, or currently taking anticonvulsants. He does not have dysphagia and/or cannot swallow study medication whole. He is able to adequately communicate with study staff, properly give informed consent, or otherwise comply with study procedures. He has not participated in another clinical trial of an investigational drug or device within 30 days of screening visit or is schedule to receive an investigational product while participating in the study.

25F with a history of seasonal allergies and allergic conjunctivitis presents with symptoms of redness, itching and tearing of both eyes for the past 2 days. She reports that these symptoms have been recurrent every year around the same time and have responded poorly to over-the-counter medications. She denies any history of ocular surgery, ocular trauma or other ocular diseases. On examination, visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and there is bilateral conjunctival injection with chemosis and mild discharge. She has a positive skin test to common allergens and a positive conjunctival provocation test to histamine. She is not currently pregnant and is using adequate birth control. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and has signed the informed consent form and HIPAA document. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medications.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He recently had an angiogram which showed that he has significant blockages in his coronary arteries and his cardiologist recommended him for the CABG procedure. He is currently taking medications for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is retired and spends most of his time with his family. He has no history of any major surgeries and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

Patient A is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer in her right breast. She underwent a core biopsy which confirmed the presence of axillary metastasis. The patient is scheduled to undergo an axillary lymph node dissection of Berg's levels I and II. She is otherwise healthy with no known drug allergies or renal dysfunction. The patient has not undergone a modified radical mastectomy. She has been informed about the clinical trial investigating the use of normal saline, gentamicin solution, and clindamycin solution lavage in axillary lymph node dissection. She is interested in participating in the trial and has provided informed consent.

A 35-year-old woman has been diagnosed with depression by her primary care physician. She has been prescribed an antidepressant medication but has not yet started taking it due to concerns about the potential side effects. She is employed and has commercial health insurance. She has no history of dementia, schizophrenia, or any other mental health disorders. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the impact of patient cost-sharing on antidepressant therapy and utilization of adjunctive therapies.

A 42-year-old woman with a medical history of relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis for the past 6 years, currently being treated with Avonex. She has had 3 relapses in the past year despite treatment with Avonex. She has no known contraindications to MRI and is not pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the potential of adding Topamax to her current treatment regimen to evaluate its neuroprotective effect. She is able to attend regular appointments and follow study requirements.

A 32-year old software engineer was brought to the emergency department by ambulance after experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath and dizziness at work. He has no prior medical history or ongoing medical conditions. He is not taking any medications and denies any drug use or smoking. He lives alone in an apartment and has no significant family history of medical conditions. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time, but is visibly anxious. He reports his chest pain is subsiding but he still feels some discomfort. The patient is cooperative and willing to participate in the study.

8-year-old female with a recent onset of redness and discharge in the left eye. The patient has been experiencing discomfort and itching in the affected eye, and the symptoms have been worsening over the past 2 days. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently using contact lenses. Upon examination, the patient was diagnosed with acute bacterial conjunctivitis. The patient has no uncontrolled systemic or debilitating diseases and is willing to discontinue contact lens wear for the duration of the study. The patient has not previously been treated with besifloxacin, fluoroquinolones, or any other study drugs. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for their child's participation in the clinical trial.

A 25-year-old male who is sexually active with multiple partners and practices unprotected sex. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, takes no chronic medications, and has no known allergies. He is a non-smoker and non-drinker. He has never participated in a HIV vaccine trial before and is willing to comply with the study protocol. He has tested negative for HIV-1, HIV-2, and HIV p24 antigen within the last 8 weeks. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, and his BMI is within the normal range. He has not received any live attenuated vaccines, subunit or killed vaccines, or allergy treatments with antigen injections within the last 30 days. He is willing to use adequate contraception for the duration of the study if he is of childbearing potential. He has no history of immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease, malignancy, or other serious medical conditions.

A 50-year-old female with type 2 diabetes taking metformin 2000 mg daily for the last 6 months. She has poor glycemic control with HbA1c of 9.2% and fasting plasma glucose of 200 mg/dL. She has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and has not experienced a weight loss of more than 10 pounds in the last three months. She has never used any thiazolidinedione (TZD) medication before and has not used insulin in the last year. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use two medically accepted forms of contraception if of childbearing potential.

30 yo F with a history of infertility for 2 years who has had at least 1 previous cycle of treatment with injectable gonadotropins within the past 6 months. She is premenopausal and aged 18-40 years with a usual cycle length greater than 35 days with less than 6 menses per year. She has a positive response to a progesterone challenge within the past 6 months or during the screening period. She has normal Papanicolaou (PAP) smear within 6 months prior to initial visit. Her male partner has an acceptable semen analysis within 6 months prior to study entry. She has a BMI less than 35.0 kilogram per square meter (kg/m^2) and patency and apparent normality of at least 1 fallopian tube with an ipsilateral functional ovary, as documented by an hysterosonogram or hysterosalpingography (HSG) within 3 years prior to study entry. She has local laboratory screening results demonstrating the following, within the past year: (a) prolactin within normal limits (b) Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) within the normal limit for the early follicular phase at the local laboratory (c) thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) within normal limits. She has been willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study and has voluntarily provided written informed consent and a subject authorization under Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), prior to any study-related procedure not part of normal medical care, with the understanding that consent could be withdrawn by the subject at any time without prejudice to their future medical care. The male partner has also provided a written subject authorization under HIPAA. She has not been treated with any gonadotropin multi-dose formulation in vials or administered by Pen device in the past 6 months and does not have any significant allergic disease, which could interfere with study treatment. She does not have any known infection with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B or C virus and has not had prior severe Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS). She has not had any significant allergic response to gonadotropin preparations and does not have any contraindication to pregnancy or carrying pregnancy to term. She has not had any poor response in a prior gonadotropin stimulation cycle and has not had prior excessive response to gonadotropin stimulation. She has not been treated with gonadotropins, clomiphene citrate, insulin-sensitizing agents (e.g., metformin, Avandia®) or Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH) analogs within 1 month prior to study entry. She does not have hypothyroidism (untreated) or hyperprolactinemia (untreated) and does not have abnormal, undiagnosed, gynecological bleeding. She does not have known current American Society Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Stage 3 or 4 endometriosis or a residual ovarian cyst with a mean diameter >25 mm or an estradiol (E2) >100 pg/mL at the baseline examination. She has not had three or more consecutive pregnancy losses, due to any cause and does not have known current substance abuse (including smokers consuming more than 5 cigarettes/day). She has not participated in another investigational drug or drug delivery system trial within 3 months prior to study entry.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer six months ago. She has a history of hypertension for which she takes amlodipine 5 mg daily. She is not currently receiving chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Her blood pressure is consistently above 140/90 mmHg despite her current medication. Her creatinine and potassium levels are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her hypertension while undergoing cancer treatment.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). He has been experiencing urinary frequency and urgency for the past year and has been taking medication to manage his symptoms. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is looking forward to his upcoming transurethral prostatectomy to alleviate his urinary symptoms. He has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and is in good physical health with an ASA status of I. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics and has not been on corticosteroid therapy or alpha2 blockers. His baseline body temperature is within normal limits.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon during a routine colonoscopy. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a family history of colon cancer with both his father and grandfather being diagnosed in their 50s. He is scheduled for a laparoscopic colectomy with planned primary anastomosis. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He has never had an adverse reaction to local anesthetics or opioids. He does not drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. He understands the study procedures and is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule.

A 55-year-old male with a diagnosis of Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) and a b3a2 breakpoint mutation. The patient has been receiving treatment with imatinib mesylate for 2 years, with documented complete cytogenetic response on multiple examinations. However, the patient still has detectable residual disease at the molecular level. The patient has a WHO performance status of 1 and normal bilirubin, AST, ALT, and creatinine levels. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has tested negative for pregnancy. The patient is willing to use effective contraception if they are fertile. The patient does not have any severe active infections or serious medical illnesses that would preclude study completion. The patient does not have known immunodeficiency or autoimmune disorders. The patient is not currently receiving any concurrent immunosuppression or systemic immunosuppressive medication, nor is the patient receiving any concurrent dose escalation of imatinib mesylate or other investigational products.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing severe headaches and occasional seizures. An MRI revealed a suspicious mass in the brain, and a subsequent biopsy confirmed the presence of glioblastoma. The patient has not undergone any definitive surgical therapy yet. The lesion is approximately 12 mm in size and is located in the right frontal lobe. The patient has no history of brain cancer, whole brain radiation, cerebrovascular disease, or dementia. He does not have any known allergies to FDG or gadolinium based contrast agents. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is not pregnant.

A 40-year-old Japanese man has been scheduled for an elective surgery under sevoflurane anesthesia. He is in good health, without any history of neuromuscular disorders or significant renal or hepatic dysfunction. The anticipated duration of the surgery is between 1.5-3 hours, during which the administration of neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) will be required. The patient has agreed to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not using any medication that is expected to interfere with the rocuronium or vecuronium given in this trial. The patient has not previously participated in P05956 or any other trial with sugammadex. The patient is ASA class 1-3 and is within the age range of 20-65 years old, and is of Japanese ethnicity.

A 30-year-old man and his partner have been trying to conceive for over a year without success. The patient has no significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with any sexually transmitted disease. He denies smoking, alcohol consumption, and illicit drug use. He works as a software engineer and has no exposure to any environmental toxins. His partner is 28 years old, healthy, and has regular menstrual cycles. She has no history of infertility or sexually transmitted diseases. The couple is motivated to participate in the study and have signed the informed consent form. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to take the Test dietary supplement (TDS) containing carnitine, vitamins, and trace elements for 6 months. The patient will undergo spermogram before intake and 2 and 4 months after starting the TDS. The couple will be screened for conception, pregnancy, and newborn during the 12th month of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a histologic diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity. The cancer is classified as T3N1M0. The patient has no history of cardiovascular comorbidities, major metabolic disorders, or recent massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage. The patient is not currently using any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or corticosteroids. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Score is above 80, and the patient is willing and able to fully participate in the study. The patient has not had previous head and neck cancers. Hemoglobin levels are above 10gm/dl, and the white blood cell count and platelet count are within normal limits. The patient's total bilirubin, AST, and ALT are all within 2 times the upper limit of normal, and the serum creatinine level is below 2 times the upper limit of normal. The patient has signed an informed consent before enrolling in the study.

A 28-year-old HIV-positive male who is an active military beneficiary comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has been diagnosed with HIV for the past 5 years and has been on antiretroviral therapy for 3 years. He has no history of MRSA colonization or infection. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen and reports no recent hospitalizations, surgeries, or use of antibiotics. He denies any history of skin infections, abscesses or boils, but reports occasional skin irritation and itching. The patient is interested in participating in a study to investigate the prevalence and incidence of MRSA colonization and infection among HIV-infected individuals. The patient is willing to attend study visits which are every 6 months for a two year period and consent to decolonization procedures for clearance of MRSA carriage and prevention of MRSA infections if necessary.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who had a work-related accident resulting in a laceration of the left wrist, causing damage to the median nerve and flexor tendons in zones I to IV. The patient underwent surgical reconstruction of the median nerve and flexor tendons with primary grafting at the Hospital of the Medical School of Ribeirão Preto, University São Paulo. The patient is currently in her first week of postoperative recovery and is experiencing sensory deficits in the left hand, including numbness and tingling. The patient has no history of chronic metabolic or degenerative diseases and has not suffered any central nervous system injury. The patient's hand and wrist range of motion is limited and she is experiencing discomfort and pain. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve her sensory recovery and functional outcomes.

A 32-year-old male with a history of a motor vehicle accident presents with chronic pain in his back, legs, and feet. He was diagnosed with a spinal cord injury and underwent surgical interventions to stabilize his spine. Despite the surgical interventions, he has been experiencing pain for the last six months, with a numerical rating scale (NRS) score of 7/10. The patient has tried traditional pain management techniques, including pain medication and physical therapy, without significant improvement. The patient has a regular computer and internet access, and fluency in English. He is willing to participate in a pilot study to assess the effectiveness of internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy pain management programme (CBT-PMP) on people with spinal cord injury pain. He has not undergone any other psychological treatments, and his mental health is stable without requiring psychiatric management. He meets the inclusion criteria for this study and will be assessed for eligibility to join the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer three months ago. She underwent surgical cytoreduction followed by taxane-platinum combination chemotherapy. The patient responded to initial treatment but had a recurrence of the disease. The patient's current CT scan shows a large mass in the pelvis with multiple nodules in the liver, indicating the cancer had progressed to stage IV. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternate treatment options. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has no history of any autoimmune or inflammatory disorders. She has never received anti-PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 treatments in the past. She has no history of allogenic organ transplantation and her recent lab tests show that her organ functions are normal. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations including follow up.

Patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced lung cancer. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and difficulty breathing, and has decided that she does not want a breathing tube placed in her windpipe to assist her breathing. She has been admitted to the hospital and will be treated with oxygen, medications like morphine, and noninvasive ventilation (NIV) or bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP) to help with her breathing. As a do-not-intubate (DNI) patient, she is eligible to participate in a study that aims to monitor the use of NIV in DNI patients and assess the experiences of patients, family members, and caregivers with NIV compared to other approaches to palliating symptoms. The study will also collect data on dyspnea score, comfort, and pain on a daily basis, and healthcare providers will be asked to fill in a questionnaire at discharge. The patient has consented to participate in the study and hopes that her experience will help improve the use of NIV and provide more comfort to patients with advanced lung cancer and other severe chronic diseases.

A 55-year-old Caucasian man complains of persistent knee pain for the past 8 months. He describes his pain as a dull ache, which is present most of the day. The pain increases with movement and walking. He has difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from a sitting position. He has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not provided much relief. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting at his desk. He has not had any knee surgeries in the past. He underwent an MRI scan a week ago, which showed grade 3 osteoarthritis according to the Kellgren and Lawrence radiographic criteria. His BMI is 28.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was diagnosed with major depressive disorder six months ago. She has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and worthlessness. She has difficulty concentrating and making decisions. She also complains of fatigue and lack of energy. She has been receiving treatment from a mental health professional and is currently taking antidepressant medication. She has access to the internet through her smartphone and laptop. She is interested in participating in the study because she is looking for additional ways to manage her symptoms. She does not have any other mental health disorders and is not currently engaging in any other psychiatric treatment.

The patient is a 34-year-old male who sustained multiple injuries in a car accident, including open fractures of the left tibia and fibula, a laceration of the liver, and a concussion. He was transferred to the ICU for critical care management. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is a nonsmoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient is currently receiving mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support, and continuous renal replacement therapy. His vital signs are stable, but he remains in a comatose state. The patient's family has given informed consent for participation in the study.

Patient is a 4-year-old healthy girl with no history of chronic respiratory disorders or acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization for the past 4 weeks. She has no signs or symptoms of nasal congestion, adenotonsillar hypertrophy, or sleep apnea. Her laboratory analyses are within the reference range, and her lung function test results are normal with a negative bronchodilator test result. The patient's parent or legal guardian has signed the informed consent form for the study. The patient has not undergone preterm birth and has no chronic respiratory disorder of prematurity, primary immunodeficiency, or chronic rhinosinusitis, and has not had recurrent bronchitis or pneumonia. The patient does not have any implanted or external active medical devices such as pacemakers. The patient has no personal or family history or clinical evidence of asthma, atopy, or other chronic respiratory disorders that put her at high risk for asthma and allergy. She is within the age range of 18 months to 6 years and is of any sex.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing back pain for the past 5 years, which has progressively worsened over time. She has also noticed a hunched posture and difficulty standing upright for long periods of time. Upon seeking medical attention, she was diagnosed with adult degenerative scoliosis with a curvature of the spine measuring 35 degrees. She has a sagittal vertical axis of 6cm, pelvic tilt of 28 degrees, and thoracic kyphosis of 65 degrees. She is currently considering surgical intervention to correct her spinal deformity and improve her quality of life. She meets the inclusion criteria for the Prospective, Multi-Center Adult Spinal Deformity Outcomes Database Registry.

52-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was referred for cardiac surgery. The patient's cardiac surgery was scheduled as non-emergency and is expected to last more than 2 hours and requires the use of extracorporeal circulation, including coronary bypass(es), valve replacement(s), and associated procedures and on-pump minimal invasive surgery. The patient is scheduled to receive mechanical ventilation via tracheal intubation. He weighs 80 kg and has a body mass index of 28 kg/m2. He has given informed consent and has expressed willingness and ability to comply with all study requirements. His medical history is significant for coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. He has no history of drug abuse or dependence, and he has not received any investigational drugs within the past 30 days. The patient does not have a history of resuscitation or known resistance to benzodiazepines or history of paradoxical effects after administration of benzodiazepines. He has no known history of hypersensitivity to benzodiazepines, propofol, remifentanil hydrochloride, neuromuscular blockers, flumazenil, or other anesthetic agents. The patient has no history of epilepsy, myasthenia gravis or myasthenic syndrome, or acute narrow-angle glaucoma. He has no significant allergies or any clinically significant findings that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old child diagnosed with bilateral congenital cataracts. The child has undergone a complete ophthalmologic exam and is scheduled for cataract surgery. There is no history of ocular trauma or other eye conditions. The child is otherwise healthy with no history of chronic illnesses, allergies or medication use. Consent has been obtained from the parent or legal guardian to participate in the study.

This is a 35 year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of Relapsing Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) for the past 3 years. She has been on Rebif for the past year with documented injection site tolerability issues. The patient has been clinically stable with no relapses or disability progression for the past 6 months. The neurological history has been documented for the past year. The patient is qualified for Avonex® (Avonex Pen) according to the approved indication for RRMS. The patient has accepted magnetic resonance imaging. The patient has not been on Avonex during the 12 months prior to the study.
