The patient has not had any relapses or confirmed disability progression during the 6 months prior to the study. The patient is not on Betaferon with Neutralizing Antibodies (NAbs) more than 400 TRU (tenfold reduction units) and is not on Rebif with NAbs with more than 100 TRU. The patient does not have secondary progressive multiple sclerosis or primary progressive multiple sclerosis. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have a history of severe depression or attempted suicide or current suicidal ideation. The patient does not have any medical or psychiatric conditions that compromise the ability to give informed consent, to comply with the protocol, or to complete the study. The patient does not have uncontrolled seizure disorder, myopathy or clinically significant liver disease. The patient is able to comply with protocol requirements for the duration of the study. The patient does not have known hypersensitivity to interferon-beta or other human proteins including albumin. The patient does not have a history of drug abuse in the 6 months prior to screening. The patient has not been treated with any of the following in the 30 days before day 1: systemic corticosteroids, ACTH, or other investigational drugs. The patient is not participating in any other study involving investigational or marketed products, concomitantly or within 30 days prior to entry in the study. There is no likelihood of requiring treatment during the study period with drugs not permitted by the study protocol.

A 58-year-old man presents to the clinic with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and currently takes medications for both. He underwent a nuclear myocardial perfusion scan a few months ago, which showed mild to moderate ischemia. The visual scan interpretation of the myocardial perfusion scan was definitely abnormal. He has not undergone any revascularization procedure since then. He reports occasional palpitations but denies any syncope or near-syncope. He has no known drug allergies or history of kidney or liver disease. His current blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg. His creatinine clearance is 72 ml/min. He has an upcoming appointment for coronary angiography.

The patient is a 38 year old male who recently experienced severe pain in his back and flank. He visited his primary care physician, who referred him to a urologist. A CT scan revealed a 2.5 cm stone in his right kidney. The patient was advised to undergo percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) to remove the stone. He has no significant past medical history and is not allergic to any medications. He is not taking any medications currently. He is able to provide informed consent and fill out study documents. The patient is able to understand and speak English fluently. He is willing to participate in a randomized, double-blinded trial to assess the effects of paravertebral block on intra-operative and post-operative pain control.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) six months ago. He has undergone treatment with PD-1 inhibitor immunotherapy (pembrolizumab) but his cancer has progressed and spread to other places in his body. He has a history of hepatitis B virus infection, which is being managed with antiviral therapy. His Child Pugh score is A and his ECOG performance status is 1. He has no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders or any other major medical conditions. He is not currently on any other anticancer therapies and has not had any major surgeries within the last four weeks. He has no known allergies to any of the study drugs or drug excipients. He has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study period and is willing to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits. He has provided signed informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman who lives in one of the 25 counties of Wisconsin and is a member of a participating HMO recently enrolled in Wisconsin Medicaid (BadgerCare Plus) and has been smoking at least 5 cigarettes a day for the past week. She works as a cashier at a local grocery store and has been smoking for 20 years. She has tried to quit smoking in the past, but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in participating in a smoking cessation program and is willing to attend visits at her primary care clinic every 6 months, provide urine samples, and complete follow-up phone calls. She is fluent in English and is willing to inform the WTQL of any changes in her address, phone number, clinic attended, or health plan.

The patient is a 55 year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma at stage III, with relapsed or primary refractory multiple myeloma after 2 courses of standard therapy, and progressive disease. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and measurable disease as defined by serum M protein of 2.5 gm/dl. He has no history of bone marrow transplantation. He is at least 18 years of age and has normal marrow function with an ANC of 2.5x10 9/L and platelets of 80X10 9/L. He has normal organ function with bilirubin of 1.2XULN, AST and ALT of 1.5XULN, and serum creatinine of 1.8 mg/dL. He is using a contraceptive measure during participation as appropriate. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and restrictions and has signed written informed consent. He has not received any investigational drugs within 4 weeks of the first day of study treatment, and has no history of second cancer or active gastrointestinal ulceration. He has no hypersensitivity to CEP701 or any component of CEP701 and no intolerance of dexamethasone. He is not currently receiving warfarin or HIV protease inhibitor treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking female who has been experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past 3 months. The cough is productive with occasional blood-streaked sputum. She also complains of chest pain and fatigue. A chest X-ray reveals a mass in the right lung and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. Further imaging shows multiple metastases to the liver and bones. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any previous chemotherapy or systemic anti-cancer treatment. She does not have any CNS metastases or other malignancies in the past 5 years. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

A 60-year-old female diagnosed with a pancreatic tumor in the head of the pancreas is scheduled for a pancreatoduodenectomy by open approach. The patient's ASA score is less than 4 and she is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has no known allergies to bovine or collagen derivatives. The patient has provided informed consent for the use of Hemopatch as a sealant at the pancreaticojejunostomy after the surgery. The patient has no history of diabetes or other pancreatic disorders. She is medically stable with no other significant comorbidities.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian woman who was diagnosed with AML six months ago. She underwent induction chemotherapy, but unfortunately, her disease relapsed three months after completing chemotherapy. She has no significant past medical history and does not use any medications regularly. She presents with fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising. Her physical exam is significant for pallor and scattered bruises on her upper and lower extremities. Her vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. Laboratory evaluation reveals a white blood cell count of 10,000 cells/mm3, hemoglobin of 8 g/dL, and platelet count of 25,000 cells/mm3. The bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of relapsed AML with FLT3-ITD mutation. The patient has exhausted standard treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male veteran who suffered a motor incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI) at the T3 level about 1 year ago. The patient has been medically stable and has received clearance from a physician to participate in the trial. The patient has residual balance deficits and is unable to participate in walking activities. The patient has a neurologic level of the SCI between T1-T10 with an American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale (AIS) C. The patient has not had any orthopedic problems in the lower extremities and has a passive range of motion of the legs within functional limits. The patient has a modified Ashworth Scale score of less than 3 and can tolerate 30 minutes of standing. The patient is able to ambulate 10m with no physical assistance, but uses a single cane for support. The patient is willing and able to provide transportation to and from the testing location and is interested in participating in the trial to improve his dynamic balance and increase his participation in walking activities.

The patient is a 50-year-old male of Hispanic ethnicity who has been diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection of genotype 1. He was previously treated with Pegylated Interferon plus Ribavirin (PR) treatment but was considered a PR Partial Responder. He has not received any treatment for HCV for the past 3 years. He has a history of heavy alcohol use but stopped drinking 2 years ago. He is a smoker and smokes 1 pack per day. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control it. He has no history of cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has no evidence of decompensated liver disease or coinfection with hepatitis B virus or human immunodeficiency virus. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of HCV and is willing to use at least two effective methods of contraception during the study period.

45-year-old male with a history of ankle fracture and is planned for open reduction and internal fixation surgery. The patient has a history of occasional alcohol use but denies any history of substance abuse or dependence. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He is interested in exploring non-opioid options for

The patient is a 70-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He has been experiencing the typical motor symptoms of the disease such as tremors, rigidity, and slow movements. He is not able to perform his daily activities without assistance due to the severity of his motor symptoms. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and arthritis. The patient is a retired engineer and has been married for 42 years. He has three children and five grandchildren. His cognitive function is adequate and his Montreal Cognitive Assessment score is 25. He has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders. He is fluent in the native language of the experimental site. The patient has no implanted metallic devices or foreign objects in his body. He is not claustrophobic and is willing to participate in the MRI part of the experiment.

60 year-old male who has been experiencing severe shoulder pain for several years, with increasing difficulty in performing daily activities such as dressing and grooming. The patient has no prior history of shoulder surgery or prosthetic implantation. Patient has been diagnosed with end-stage osteoarthritis of the shoulder and has been recommended to undergo primary total shoulder arthroplasty. The patient is willing to participate in the observational study and has given his consent to participate. The patient resides in France and is able to answer the questionnaire independently. The patient is affiliated to a social security scheme and is not participating in any other clinical study. The patient does not have any infection or degenerative neurological disease and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock caused by an abdominal infection. He has a history of hypertension, but no other significant medical conditions. Upon admission, he required norepinephrine and phenylephrine to maintain blood pressure, and his modified Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score indicated acute renal failure. He has not received any surgery, chemotherapy, or radiation for malignancy in the previous 12 months, and is not pregnant or lactating. He has not received any chronic immune suppression, and is not enrolled in another interventional study. The treating physician is committed to aggressive care, and the patient's family is supportive of his participation in the trial. The patient will be randomized to receive either 300 million cryopreserved, allogeneic, bone marrow derived MSCs or placebo.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating serum sex steroid hormones. She has no history of chronic medical conditions, including endocrine or reproductive disorders. She is not taking any medications, supplements or hormone replacement therapy. She has never been diagnosed with cancer, and she has no known family history of cancer. Her last menstrual period was 5 years ago, and she has experienced no vaginal bleeding or spotting since then. She is willing to fast overnight before having blood drawn as part of the study. She is employed and interested in contributing to medical research. She understands the nature of the study and the potential risks and benefits involved, and she is willing to provide informed consent. She is available for follow-up appointments as needed.

We are looking for individuals who are currently homeless, at least 18 years of age, and have smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime to participate in our clinical trial. We are testing the effectiveness of an integrated intensive smoking and alcohol intervention using cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) compared to usual care (brief smoking cessation and brief alcohol counseling). Participants must have an AUDIT score between 5 and 26, and be willing to attend study sessions and follow the study protocol. Exclusion criteria include the use of smoking cessation medications or interventions in the last 30 days, unstable medical illness that requires immediate medical care, an AUDIT score less than 5 or greater than 26, pregnancy or other Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) contraindications, current history or in the past 6 months of psychotic disorder or major depressive disorders that are not stable on treatment for the past 3 months, and cognitive impairment. All participants will receive 12 weeks of treatment with nicotine patch plus nicotine gum/lozenge, and counseling will include weekly individual sessions for 3 months followed by study data collection visits for 3 months. The goal of this research study is to enhance smoking cessation rates for homeless smokers and recruitment and retention will be enhanced by use of gift cards, bus passes, other non-monetary incentives, attractive intervention materials, collaboration with homeless shelters, and advice from a Community Advisory Board.

The patient is a 28-year-old female residing in Bangkok, Thailand. She is a healthy individual with no known allergies, chronic respiratory, heart or kidney disease or any metabolic disease such as diabetes. She has not received any flu vaccination in the previous 6 months or any other vaccine in the past 30 days. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use reliable contraception during the study period until the final day of follow-up. She has not donated blood or received any blood products or immunoglobulins in the preceding 3 months. She is not receiving any therapy such as aspirin, warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin, aminopyrine or immunosuppressive drugs, and has not received any antiviral agents within 48 hours of vaccine administration. She has a US passport and is willing to give informed consent and attend follow-up appointments for the study procedures.

The patient is a 55 year old woman with end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis. She has a newly created arteriovenous fistula (AVF) in her left upper arm that was surgically created 2 months ago. The flow rate of the AVF was measured to be greater than 800 ml/min using the ultrasound dilution technique. She has been undergoing maintenance hemodialysis for the past 3 years, with a history of rope-ladder cannulation technique. She has developed venous aneurysms and vascular stenosis at the sites of the arterial needle insertion, leading to AVF dysfunction. The patient has been enrolled in the present prospective study that aims to compare the outcomes of AVF between the puncture direction at arterial needle sites same as blood flow and opposite to blood flow. The investigators hypothesize that aneurysms and stenoses will be decreased if the direction of inserted arterial needle were same as the direction of blood flow, when compared to the opposite direction puncture. The study requires regular follow-up visits, which the patient is able to attend without any hindrance.

A 45 year old man with a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia has been scheduled for a coronary artery bypass graft surgery at NYU Winthrop Hospital. The patient is experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath upon exertion. He is a non-smoker, doesn't consume alcohol or use recreational drugs. He is currently on medication for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient has been informed about the study which involves a new pain control technique for cardiac surgery patients. He has given his consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo the procedure. He is in stable condition and is expected to recover well from the surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with endometrial cancer. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She does not smoke, use illicit drugs, or drink alcohol. Her physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. She has been scheduled for a laparotomy procedure via a vertical midline incision to remove the cancer. The incision will be closed with staples or sutures, and the surgeon will use Spectrum Near-Infrared (NIR) imaging with Indocyanine Green (ICG) dye to measure blood flow around the incision before and after closure. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study, and her incision will be monitored for blood flow to help promote a less complicated recovery.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis of the knee joint. He has been experiencing significant pain and limitations in mobility in the affected knee, which has led to a recommendation for elective, unilateral, primary total knee arthroplasty. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities, and is not taking any medications that would affect gastrointestinal motility. He has a fasting glucose level of 120 mg/dL and HbA1c level of 6.5%. He is able to provide valid consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of high grade cervical dysplasia diagnosed 3 years ago. She underwent a loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) and has been following up with her gynecologist regularly since then. She has no history of anal dysplasia or anal cancer. She is sexually active with her partner and uses condoms for contraception. She does not smoke cigarettes or drink alcohol. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension that is well controlled with Lisinopril. Her family history is negative for any cancers. She is currently taking a daily multivitamin and calcium supplement. She presents to the clinic for follow-up and is interested in participating in a study about anal Pap smear and HPV DNA testing for women with high-grade cervical dysplasia. Her lab results are as follows: FBS: 95 mg/dL HbA1c: 5.6% Total Cholesterol: 170 mg/dL TG: 80 mg/dL LDL: 100 mg/dL HDL: 50 mg/dL.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman presenting with symptoms of vaginal bulge and pelvic pressure. Pelvic exam reveals anterior and apical prolapse Stage 3 (according to POP-Q) and stress urinary incontinence (SUI). She has had previous surgery for prolapse and is currently using a pessary. She has no history of chronic vaginal infections or colorectal diseases, and her coagulation profile and immune function are normal. She has not received prior pelvic irradiation and is not experiencing chronic pelvic pain. She is interested in pursuing surgical treatment for her prolapse and is a candidate for either Calistar A or Calistar S mesh implantation. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is available for at least 6 months of follow-up.

A 50-year-old male diagnosed with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has progressed despite previous treatment with EGFR-TKI. The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1 and a confirmed tumor EGFR sensitive mutation positive in previous tumor samples, including G719X, exon 19 deletion, L858R, L861Q. The patient also has a confirmed tumor harboring the T790M mutation by central lab with a biopsy sample taken after failure of first generation EGFR TKIs. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and adequate organ function with acceptable levels for bone marrow reserve, liver function, and kidney function. The patient has not received anti-cancer treatment prior to EGFR TKIs, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and other anti-cancer drugs for advanced stage. The patient has also resolved toxicities from prior therapy less than CTCAE grade 1 (except alopecia) and minimum 7 days of washout period from previous erlotinib, gefitinib or icotinib. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 3 months and without CNS metastases or asymptomatic patients with brain metastases. The patient also provides signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 21-year-old college student comes to the clinic with concerns about excessive drinking. He reports drinking at least 5 drinks in one sitting at least once in the past month. He admits to drinking alcohol on most weekends and feels like he is not in control of his drinking habits. He often drinks to the point of blacking out and has been in dangerous situations due to his drinking behavior. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him reduce his alcohol consumption. He denies any history of alcohol dependence or major depressive disorder. He is willing to participate in a randomized trial and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study.

5yo boy with congenital heart disease (CHD), diagnosed with tetralogy of Fallot, scheduled for surgical correction. The patient has no known drug allergies, and has not been previously diagnosed with renal dysfunction or diabetes. The patient has normal liver function with no abnormality in liver profile. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 35-year-old mother who was born in a Latin American country and speaks Spanish. She has a 12-year-old child who is currently enrolled in middle school and speaks both English and Spanish. The mother is concerned about her child's susceptibility to tobacco use and is willing to participate in a family-based tobacco use prevention intervention program. She has not previously participated in the Padres Informados parenting program. The mother is actively involved in her community and is open to collaborating with community organizations to improve the health and well-being of her family. She is willing to provide consent for herself and her child to participate in the study.

A 27-year-old male presents for screening for the L. Brevis CD2 Strain Persistence in Oral Cavity study. He reports being in good health and having no history of oral cavity pathologies. He has not taken any antibiotics or probiotics in the last three months. He does not have any systemic diseases or allergies to soy proteins. He has read and understood the informed consent document and is willing to participate in the study. The subject's oral cavity will be evaluated by the clinical team to confirm his eligibility for the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes and obesity. He recently underwent a liver ultrasound as part of his routine medical exam, which revealed abnormal liver fat accumulation. His liver enzymes were also found to be elevated on routine blood work. He has been advised to lose weight and improve his diet but has struggled to do so. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his liver health. He is currently taking metformin for his diabetes and a low dose of a blood pressure medication. He has no history of liver disease, hepatitis, or excessive alcohol consumption. He has no contraindications for MRI scanning. He is willing to follow a study diet for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing asthma symptoms for the past 6 months. She was previously diagnosed with mild persistent asthma and her FEV1 is 70% of predicted normal. She has been using inhaled corticosteroids for the past 4 weeks and her asthma symptoms have been partially controlled. She has a history of smoking, but has quit smoking six months ago. She has not used any investigational drugs in the past 30 days and has not experienced an asthma exacerbation or a clinically relevant change in asthma medication in the past 4 weeks. Her medical history is unremarkable with no clinically significant disorders. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the importance of adhering to visit schedules and entering information in a daily diary. She agrees to use an acceptable method of birth control as she is of childbearing potential.

A 26-week-old premature male infant weighing 950 grams was born via emergency C-section due to maternal pre-eclampsia. The infant required intubation and mechanical ventilation shortly after birth and has been receiving respiratory support for the past 12 weeks. The infant has had multiple episodes of apnea and bradycardia requiring frequent interventions with positive pressure ventilation and medications to stimulate breathing. The infant has had a bedside echocardiogram showing mild tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricular hypertrophy. The infant has a history of patent ductus arteriosus that was treated with indomethacin. The infant is currently receiving nasal cannula oxygen support and is tolerating feeds via a nasogastric tube. The infant is stable but requires close monitoring and frequent interventions to maintain respiratory stability. The parents have consented to participate in the study and the infant is eligible for enrollment.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with lumbar spondylosis without myelopathy by a previous doctor. Her pain is rated at 7 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale (NRS), and she has been experiencing difficulty with daily activities due to her pain. She has not received any treatment for her condition yet. She takes no other medications and has no significant past medical history. She speaks English fluently and has no hearing impairments. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of adverse reactions to midazolam, lidocaine or bupivacaine. She has no active infection, clotting disorder, or on anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy. She has not had any previous lumbar medial branch block or lumbar radiofrequency ablation. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with a fever. He has a history of hypertension and occasional headaches, but denies any recent illnesses or infections. On examination, his axillary temperature was measured to be 38.2°C using a mercury thermometer. He does not have any history of otitis externa/media or soft-tissue infection over the axillary fossa or forehead. There was no occlusion by earwax or any signs of severe illness or trauma. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study as his axillary temperature exceeded 37.5°C.

31-year-old female with naturally curly hair (type III) who is interested in trying a keratin hair treatment to straighten her hair. She has no history of hair loss or previous keratin treatments. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no chronic medical conditions. Her scalp is healthy and free of any infection, injury, or surgery. She has a hemoglobin level of 12mg/dl and is not currently under treatment for anemia. She is excited to participate in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the non-formaldehyde keratin hair treatment.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) for the past 2 years. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles, with fewer than 8 periods in the preceding year. She has also experienced hirsutism and acne, consistent with an excess in androgen production. The patient has a BMI of 32 and has not been pregnant before. She has been taking oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) for the past year to regulate her menstrual cycles. The patient is willing to discontinue OCPs for the duration of the study, which may last up to 36 weeks. She is willing to participate in the study, including the collection of blood specimens. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to doxycycline or tetracycline and has no history of Cushing's syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, or congenital adrenal hyperplasia. The patient's liver function tests and renal function tests are within normal limits. She is not currently taking metformin, statins, glucocorticoids, spironolactone, or anti-estrogens.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He experiences occasional chest pain and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. His most recent stress test showed signs of myocardial ischemia, which led to the recommendation for coronary angiography. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the Motion and IntraCoronary Ecg Ischemia Development Study (MICE) to better understand the sequence of events that occur during an ischemic event. He meets the eligibility criteria as his target main branch lesion is located in a native coronary artery with a diameter of ≥ 2.5 mm and ≤ 4.5 mm, and his target side branch lesion is located in a native coronary artery with a diameter of ≥ 2.0 mm. He does not have significant ST-T changes and has an LVEF of > 30%. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend follow-up appointments as necessary.

The patient is a 45-year-old female from Mexico with a history of heart failure diagnosed 2 years ago. She presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs. She is currently on optimal medical therapy but has been experiencing worsening symptoms. Her NYHA class is III and her LVEF is 30%. She has not received any previous CRT therapy and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule and able to return for follow-up visits. She gives her written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old male presents with bilateral cataracts and complaints of blurred vision and difficulty reading. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but these conditions are well-controlled with medication. He is not allergic to any medications. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/50 in the left eye. Pupil diameter measures 6.5 mm in both eyes. He has no history of previous eye surgery or trauma. He is not on any medication that affects pupil size. He has no known neurological disorders and no history of glaucoma, uveitis, corneal, retinal or optic nerve disease. He is scheduled for bilateral phacoemulsification under topical anesthesia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares a new injectable mydriatic combination to standard mydriatic eye drops for pupil dilation during the surgery.

This is a 54 year-old male with a recent diagnosis of dyslipidemia. He has a family history of heart disease with his father and brother both having heart attacks at a young age. He has a sedentary lifestyle and poor eating habits which he acknowledges and is willing to change. He has no known history of myopathy, diabetes, or coronary artery disease. He is currently not taking any medications for his dyslipidemia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the most effective treatment for his condition. He has signed informed consent and is willing to make necessary lifestyle modifications.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has been married for 5 years and is trying to have a child with his wife. He has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and has been advised to undergo IVF+/-ICSI. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a history of poor nutrition and consumes a lot of processed food. He doesn't smoke or drink. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. His BMI is 28.1, and his blood pressure is normal. His semen analysis shows decreased sperm motility and morphology, but normal sperm count. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if taking folic acid supplements can improve his chances of success with IVF+/-ICSI. He has social insurance, and his wife is also willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who comes to the clinic with a complaint of severe tooth pain in her upper right back teeth. The patient has a history of dental caries and has undergone previous dental fillings. The pain started three days ago and has been progressively getting worse, with a pain score of 3 out of 5 on the five-face scale. The patient has no known drug allergies and is not taking any medications. Upon examination, the dentist confirms symptomatic irreversible pulpitis of maxillary primary molars using periapical radiographs, percussion, and cold test. The patient exhibits positive behavior on the Frankl's behavior rating scale (rating 4 on the Frankl's scale). The patient is an American Society of Anesthesiologists class 1 patient aged 5-9 years. The teeth have two-thirds of each root remaining, and there is no periapical lesion or interradicular radiolucency. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as she has moderate to very severe (2-4) five-face scale pain scores in the 24-hour period before the procedure, and there are no teeth with pathologic root resorption or excessive mobility.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who has been experiencing diarrhea for the past 2 days. The diarrhea is watery and he has passed at least 5 stools per day. He has also been vomiting and has a low-grade fever. His mother has been giving him ORS solution, but the diarrhea and vomiting have persisted. She brings him to the hospital and he is admitted to the pediatric unit. The doctor examines him and notes that he is mildly dehydrated. The doctor explains to the mother that her child is eligible to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of different zinc formulations for the treatment of diarrhea. The mother agrees to participate in the study and her child is randomized to receive either zinc tablets or zinc suspension along with the recommended treatment for diarrhea as per WHO protocol. The child's stool sample is collected and sent for culture and sensitivity. The child is followed up every 8 hours by a trained RMO who records the child's progress in a follow-up form. The RMO also documents the child's compliance with the medication and any adverse effects associated with it. The patient is discharged after two weeks of illness and will be followed up at home.

Patient is a 56-year-old Chinese male who presents with a history of smoking for over 25 years. He was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history or prior cancer history. His BMI is 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 72/min. He is willing to provide informed consent and detailed clinical information including his tumor stage, grade, size and smoking history. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer and is willing to provide a surgical specimen and blood sample. He is interested in participating in this study to help advance research on NSCLC and to potentially benefit future patients with the disease.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male with a history of NSCLC, previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation, presents with worsening dyspnea on exertion and a persistent cough. The patient has a history of heavy smoking, but quit smoking 6 months ago. PET-CT shows progression of the lung cancer with multiple new lesions in the lung and lymph nodes. The patient has no brain metastasis or active infections. The patient is ECOG 1 and has a good performance status. The patient has no autoimmune disease or active medical disorder that would impair the ability to receive study treatment. The patient has no prior malignancies in the past 2 years. The patient has not received any other anticancer approved or investigational agents. The patient has measurable disease as defined by RECIST v1.1. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and any locally-required authorization to participate in the study. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations including follow-up. The patient is of non-reproductive potential. The patient is not receiving systemic steroids at a dose ≥ 10mg/day of prednisone or the equivalent.

This is a 54-year-old male with a history of renal cell carcinoma that has metastasized to other parts of his body. He has previously undergone systemic therapy, including sunitinib and temsirolimus, but has not achieved successful outcomes. His current performance status is 1, indicating he is ambulatory and able to carry out light work. He has evaluable disease according to Response Criteria for Solid Tumors. The patient is not currently on therapeutic anti-coagulation but may be permitted if clinically stable and has been on it for at least 3 months. The patient has not had any major surgeries requiring general anesthesia within the last 4 weeks. The patient has not had any documented central nervous system tumors or metastasis to the CNS. The patient has not taken any investigational drugs within the last 4 weeks or 5 half-lives of the prior investigational drug. The patient has no history of thromboembolic events or bleeding disorders within the last 3 months.

A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension and heart failure presents with worsening symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath and decreased exercise tolerance despite maximal medical therapy. He has been diagnosed with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and has been recommended for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). However, during the attempted placement of a lead via the standard coronary sinus route, the lead could not be positioned due to adverse vein anatomy. The patient is now being considered for a new technique, interventricular septal puncture, to allow for LV endocardial pacing. The patient is currently taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation, but no contraindications to oral anticoagulation have been identified. The patient has been deemed fit for the procedure by his cardiologist and has agreed to participate in this pilot study to evaluate the feasibility and safety of this new technique. The patient will undergo multiple techniques to optimize lead placement, including speckle-tracking echocardiography, electrical mapping of the LV activation pattern, and cardiac output monitoring during the procedure to try and find the optimal site for each patient. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse events and will be followed up to assess echocardiographic, biochemical, and functional response to the procedure.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for 2 years. She has been struggling to maintain good glycemic control despite her efforts to adhere to a standard method of counting carbohydrate and fat/protein exchanges. She reports that it is difficult to estimate serving sizes and calculate the amount of insulin needed for each meal. The patient has a computer at home and access to a kitchen with sufficient space to accommodate the ELKa system. Her current glycated hemoglobin level is 9.5%. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if using the ELKa toolset will improve her glycemic control and make it easier to manage her diabetes. She has no other medical conditions that would interfere with the evaluation of the study results. The patient and her parents provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 60-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with stage IB non-small cell lung cancer. He underwent a CT scan, which showed a 2.5 cm tumor in his upper left lobe. He has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication, and he had a myocardial infarction six months ago. He underwent successful angioplasty and has been stable since then. His performance status is 1. He had no prior surgery, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy for NSCLC. His laboratory results are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study. He is aware that he has a 50/50 chance of receiving chemotherapy either before or after surgery. He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits. He is not taking any other experimental treatments or hormonal cancer therapy.

32-year-old female diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 5 years ago. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and migraines. She has been on Gilenya for the past 8 months with good tolerability. She reports occasional numbness and tingling in her right leg, but otherwise denies any significant neurological symptoms. She has completed at least 12 years of education and is physically capable of completing neurometric testing and MRI studies. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential cognitive benefits of Gilenya and contribute to research efforts to improve treatment options for MS.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B. She has been experiencing fatigue, mild abdominal discomfort and yellowing of the skin and eyes. She has a history of occasional alcohol use but has stopped drinking since the diagnosis. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Her family history is negative for liver disease. On examination, she has hepatomegaly with mild tenderness, but no signs of cirrhosis or ascites. Her laboratory results show elevated ALT levels (3 times the upper limit of normal), elevated bilirubin levels (2 times the upper limit of normal), and a positive HBeAg test. Her HBV DNA level is between 1.00E＋05 IU/ml and 9.99E＋09 IU/ml. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the combination treatment of PEG-Tα1 and adefovir to manage her chronic hepatitis B.

A 36-year-old man who sustained a traumatic brain injury in a motor vehicle accident two years ago is currently experiencing difficulties in reading and writing. He is a former college student and had no prior history of reading or writing difficulties. Since his injury, he has had difficulties with decoding words, understanding written information, and expressing himself in writing. He has been receiving therapy at Quality Living Inc. in Omaha, Nebraska, for the past year. He is a native English speaker and has no known vision or auditory impairments. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve his reading and writing capabilities and hopes to return to college and complete his degree.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with kidney stones and requires lithotripsy. He has a history of hypertension and occasional migraine headaches, for which he takes medications. He has never undergone anesthesia or sedation before and is concerned about the risks associated with the procedure. The patient reports no allergies or adverse reactions to medications in the past. During the pre-operative evaluation, he is classified as an ASA II (moderate systemic disease) due to his hypertension. The patient is informed about the study and consents to participate. He is randomized to the research group and will undergo sedation during the lithotripsy procedure. The patient is assured that he will receive standard of care during the procedure and that the study will simply involve monitoring his brain activity through EEG electrodes placed on his forehead and scalp. The patient is instructed to report any awareness during the procedure to the anesthesia team. After the procedure, the patient will be monitored in the post-anesthesia care unit until he meets discharge criteria. The patient is informed that he will be compensated for his time and participation in the study.

35-year-old Italian woman who has been suffering from chronic migraine for the past three years. She experiences unilateral and pulsating pain of moderate to severe intensity, which is aggravated by routine physical activities and is combined with nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia. Her headache occurs on an average of 18 days per month, greatly impairing her daily activities and affecting her quality of life. She has tried multiple pharmacological therapies with limited success and is currently not taking any medication for her migraine. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore non-pharmacological interventions for the management of chronic migraine and is willing to adhere to the study procedures. She has no co-occurring psychiatric or chronic medical conditions and is not pregnant or lactating.

52-year-old male with a history of liver cancer diagnosed three years ago. The patient underwent surgical removal of the tumor but unfortunately, the cancer has recurred, and the patient has undergone Sorafenib treatment for a period of six months. The patient's cancer has shown progression despite Sorafenib treatment, and the patient is currently seeking additional treatment options. The patient has Child-Pugh Class A cirrhosis and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not received any previous systemic investigational agents for HCC except for Sorafenib. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has recently received a diagnosis of CIN 2/3 or CIN 3 after a biopsy of the cervix. She has had regular pap smears and has never had an abnormal result before. She has no history of cervical cancer, sexually transmitted infections or other reproductive health issues. She is in a monogamous relationship and uses condoms for contraception. She has a GOG Performance Status of 0 and is willing to return for follow-up visits. She has no known immunocompromised conditions and has a negative HIV test. She has a history of asthma and takes an inhaler as needed. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to practice an acceptable form of contraception during the trial period. She has signed an informed consent and authorization for release of personal health information. Her CBC/Platelets, renal function, hepatic function, and glycemic control are all within normal limits. She is not taking any medication that is metabolized by the CYP3A4 isoenzyme or any of the concurrent medications listed as exclusion criteria. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and has a negative urine pregnancy test within 14 days of starting the trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection six months ago. He started antiretroviral therapy immediately after his diagnosis and has been virologically suppressed, with his HIV viral load <50 copies/mL. He has been on a stable ART regimen that includes three antiretroviral drugs for the past year. His CD4 counts have been stable, with a count of 500 cells/mm3 at the screening visit. He is currently not experiencing any HIV-related symptoms. He has a history of occasional marijuana use but has not used any other drugs or alcohol in the past six months. He is currently unemployed but is actively seeking employment. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or any physical or psychiatric disorders that could impair his ability to complete the study. He is willing to comply with all study procedures, including the analytical treatment interruption (ATI), collection of blood samples, and adherence to the ART regimen, and is available for the planned duration of the study. He is currently not sexually active and is not planning on becoming sexually active during the study period. He is not currently taking any medications that are not compatible with vesatolimod.

The patient is a 16-year-old adolescent who has been experiencing persistent sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities for the past 6 months. He has also been diagnosed with emerging personality disorder by his psychiatrist. He has a history of self-harm and suicidal ideation. He has been admitted to Brookside adolescent unit due to an increase in self-harm behavior. The patient is currently not attending school and has difficulty forming and maintaining relationships with peers and family members. He has no history of autistic spectrum disorders or severe learning disabilities. The patient is willing to participate in a treatment program that specifically focuses on his co-morbid diagnosis of depression and emerging personality disorder. He is motivated to receive treatment and improve his quality of life.

56-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) that has spread to his lungs and bones. The patient has been treated with sunitinib in first line and axitinib in second line. He has been experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and bone pain. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the study to understand the clinical outcomes of patients treated with sunitinib in first line and axitinib in second line in a real world setting for mRCC.

A 46-year-old male was recently diagnosed with esophageal carcinoma. He has not received any preoperative chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to establish large tissue sections for esophageal carcinoma to observe the tumor landscape on a microscope. He is interested in contributing to medical research and believes in its potential benefits to future patients.

A 32-year-old healthy male participant who previously received a TBE vaccine for adults as part of a clinical trial presents for the evaluation of the long-term immunogenicity of the vaccine. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He reports no adverse reactions to the previous TBE vaccine and is willing to participate in this study to determine the persistence of antibodies after a booster immunisation. The participant has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions that would interfere with the evaluation of the study objectives.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has been on chemotherapy for the past 9 months and has had progression of her disease on her current regimen. Her performance status is ECOG 1, and she has an estimated survival of at least 6 months. The patient has a tumor sample available for NGS testing and is within 10 weeks of starting her current line of therapy. She has no serious uncontrolled intercurrent medical or psychiatric illness and is able to comply with the requirements of the study. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to provide written informed consent prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been in good health for the past few years. She works in a busy office environment and takes public transportation to and from work daily. She has experienced occasional respiratory infections in the past and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent future infections. She has no history of chronic illnesses and is not taking any medications. She has not received a flu vaccine in the past year and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the immunogenicity of the inactivated influenza vaccine formulation for the 2007-2008 season.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with ulcerative colitis-associated pouchitis is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating the safety and effectiveness of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT). The patient has a history of inflammatory bowel disease and has undergone an ileal pouch anastomosis to treat his condition. The patient experiences frequent inflammation of the ileal pouch and has previously been treated with antibiotics, probiotics, and prebiotics without much improvement. The patient is not currently taking immunosuppressive therapy, has not been diagnosed with Crohn's disease or C. difficile infection, and is not on anti-coagulant therapy. The patient is willing to undergo FMT and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is currently being treated at Emory Clinic and/or Emory University Hospital and is between the ages of 18 and 65.

The patient is a 30 year old man who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has never received any antiretroviral therapy (ART) before and his plasma HIV-1 RNA level is greater than or equal to 1000 copies/mL. He has signed and dated written informed consent to participate in the study. He has no history of allergy or intolerance to the study drugs or their components or drugs of their class. He has no evidence of an active Centers for Disease and Prevention Control (CDC) Category C disease, except cutaneous Kaposi's sarcoma not requiring systemic therapy. He has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years or ongoing malignancy other than cutaneous Kaposi's sarcoma, basal cell carcinoma, or resected, non-invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. He has not been treated with an HIV-1 immunotherapeutic vaccine within 90 days of Screening. He has not been treated with any of the following agents within 28 days of Screening: radiation therapy; cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents; any immunomodulators. He has not been exposed to an experimental drug or experimental vaccine within either 28 days, 5 half-lives of the test agent, or twice the duration of the biological effect of the test agent, whichever is longer, prior to the first dose of investigational product. He has no evidence of primary viral resistance based on the presence of any major resistance-associated mutation in the Screening result or, if known, any historical resistance test result. He has no acute laboratory abnormality at Screening that would preclude his participation in the study of an investigational compound.

The patient is a 45-year-old male experiencing chronic anal pain due to anorectal diseases, such as hemorrhoids and anal fissures. He has tried various conservative treatments, including topical creams and ointments, sitz baths, and dietary changes, but none have provided long-term relief. He has no significant medical history, does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and is not currently taking any medications. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. He has been scheduled for an anorectal procedure and has consented to participate in a clinical trial comparing multi-drug analgesia with standard solution for post-operative pain control.

As this clinical trial is specifically targeting Tibetan residents of India, a suitable patient description would be:  The patient is a Tibetan individual residing in one of the Tibetan colonies in India. They are over 18 years old and willing to participate in a survey related to metabolic syndromes and HIV infection. They may or may not have a prior diagnosis of metabolic syndromes or HIV infection. They are willing to undergo an HIV quick test and complete questionnaires related to risk factors for both conditions. They are able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP). He experiences stiffness and weakness in his legs, making it difficult to walk and maintain balance. He also complains of urinary urgency and occasional constipation. The patient is married with two children and works in an office job. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication for his HSP. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the understanding of non-motor symptoms in HSP and potentially benefit from any new treatments that may arise from the research.

The patient is a 68-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 26 kg/m squared. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and has normal vital signs for her age (BP 130/70 mmHg, HR 70 bpm). Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is well controlled on amlodipine 5 mg daily. She has no history of renal, hepatic, or gastrointestinal disease. She is post-menopausal and has no intention of becoming pregnant. Her medication includes amlodipine 5 mg daily and vitamin D3 1000 units per day. She has no history of metabolic disturbances or cardiovascular, pulmonary, chronic respiratory, immunologic, endocrine, neurologic, psychiatric, or thromboembolic disease. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

50-year-old Caucasian male with no significant medical history except for seasonal allergic rhinitis. The patient has a body mass index of 23 kg/m2 and blood pressure and pulse rate within the acceptable range for the study. The patient is a non-smoker and has not been exposed to artificial ionizing radiation within the last 12 months. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials during the previous month. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who work in assisted living facilities, family members of residents with dementia, and public health dental hygienists. The trial aims to modify a program that reduces pneumonia among nursing home residents with dementia to make it appropriate for assisted living residents with dementia. Participants must be 18 years of age or older, able to read and speak English fluently, and willing to provide direct care to residents in participating assisted living communities or receive mouth care from AL staff. Exclusion criteria include not providing direct care to residents in participating assisted living community, not having a family member who received mouth care from AL staff, and not being employed by the NC DHHS Oral Health Section. Residents with teeth or dentures, a diagnosis of dementia, and not requiring antibiotic prophylaxis prior to oral hygiene examination, currently on hospice or tube-feeding, or expected to die or be discharged in the next six months are eligible to participate.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has no history of stroke or heart disease. He is currently not taking any anticoagulant medication. He is concerned about the potential side effects of the standard care treatment with Vitamin K Antagonist (VKA). The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the use of Pradaxa as an alternative to VKA for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has no other medical history that would exclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been taking prescription opioids for chronic back pain for the past 2 years. He is currently being treated at one of the investigator's partner sites and speaks English fluently. He has a history of opioid use and has experienced some adverse effects such as constipation and drowsiness. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He has a high school education and no prior history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is interested in reducing his dependence on opioids and learning more about naloxone. He has no significant medical conditions and is able to give informed, voluntary, written consent to participate in the study.

A 31-year-old female who has been referred for cervical screening at U.T.M.D. Anderson Hospital, Houston, TX, USA. She has a history of regular Pap smear tests with no abnormal results. She is not pregnant and has not received any treatment to her cervix. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. The patient will undergo a physical examination and a pap smear as part of the screening process. If eligible, she will then undergo a multi-spectral digital colposcopy with and without acetic acid application. If any abnormal cells are identified during the colposcopy, a biopsy of the cervical canal will be performed. The patient will be fully informed of the investigational nature of the study and will be required to provide written consent before participation.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who lives in a rural community in Vietnam. He was diagnosed with hypertension six months ago during a routine check-up at the local health clinic. Since then, he has been taking medication prescribed by his doctor, but he still experiences occasional high blood pressure readings. He is married with three children and works as a farmer. He has limited access to healthcare and relies on traditional remedies for minor ailments. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about his condition and how to manage it effectively. He speaks Vietnamese and has basic literacy skills.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of pulmonary hypertension and tricuspid regurgitation, leading to right-sided heart failure. He has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema in the lower extremities. He has previously undergone a right heart catheterization within the past year to rule out left-sided failure. The patient is currently taking furosemide for diuresis. He has no history of renal dysfunction, and his serum creatinine level is within normal limits. The patient is not currently taking an angiotensin I converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo water immersion for 3 hours on one day.

54-year-old male with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma with unresectable metastatic disease confirmed on imaging within the last 28 days. The patient has not received previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy. ECOG Performance Status is 1. Adequate major organ functions are confirmed within 14 days before registration. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months after registration. The patient is not positive for HER2 status and has not received previous treatment with platinum agents or fluoropyrimidines therapy within 6 months prior to registration. The patient has no previous history of serious hypersensitivity to fluoropyrimidines or platinum agents, adverse reactions suggestive of dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency, active hepatitis, heart disease that is serious or requires hospitalization, or being treated or in need of treatment with flucytosine, phenytoin or warfarin potassium. The patient has no chronic diarrhea, active gastrointestinal bleeding, or clinical suspicion or previous history of metastasis to brain or meninges. The patient is willing to practice contraception and has no poor oral intake or psychiatric disorders which are being or may need to be treated with psychotropics.

Patient is a pregnant woman aged 18-40 years who is currently in labor. The patient does not have a history of pre-term delivery, metabolic diseases such as insulin resistance, diabetes, gestational diabetes, hypertension or thyroid disease, or cancer. The patient is willing to provide consent to participate in the study. The study aims to evaluate the presence and quantity of non-caloric sweeteners in the patient's breast milk at delivery, at 2 months, 4 months, and 6 months of age of the newborn. The study also aims to evaluate the composition of the intestinal and milk microbiota in order to identify changes attributable to the consumption of ENC in the newborn's umbilical cord blood and mother's breast milk. This study will help determine the potential effects of ENC consumption on the development of metabolic disorders and changes in microbiota in newborns, providing valuable insights for the development of future dietary guidelines.

Looking for 20 healthy female participants aged between 18 to 40 years, who do not regularly consume soy products, chickpeas or other supplements with a high content of isoflavones, and are not taking any drugs that may affect uptake. Participants should not be pregnant or breastfeeding, and should not have participated in any other clinical trials within the last 3 months. Those with severe cardiovascular, psychiatric, neurological and/or kidney disease, alcohol or substance abuse, and acute illness are not eligible for this trial. The aim of the study is to determine the effects of food matrices and processing on the bioavailability of active compounds derived from red clover. Participants will receive red clover derived isoflavones in five different formulations over a period of 5-6 weeks, with a minimum of 5 days washout period between each phase. Blood plasma samples will be collected pre- and post-ingestion of a formulation, and blood tests will be conducted at intervals to monitor bioavailability. The primary endpoint is to determine whether fermented extract is more bioavailable than unfermented extract.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU with confirmed COVID-19 disease. She has radiological evidence of COVID-related pneumonia with ground-glass opacities on CT scan. She is currently on mechanical ventilation and has elevated levels of inflammatory markers such as CRP, IL-6, IL-1 and TNF-a, which are correlated with increasing disease severity. She has no history of peripheral vascular disease, arm surgery, or radiation/lymph node dissection. The patient's clinical team deems it safe to proceed with the RIC procedure.

68F retired, living alone with no caregiver. She reports to her primary care physician during a regular check-up, that she has been experiencing difficulty hearing during conversations with her family and friends, which has resulted in social isolation. Upon screening, she is found to have possible hearing loss. She is interested in participating in a study to assess how effective screening is when combined with additional educational material. She is able to give informed consent and speaks and understands English. She does not currently wear a hearing aid and does not have any concurrent health condition that would limit participation. She is eligible for the study.

The patient is an 80-year-old man who has been living in a nursing home for the past year. He has been diagnosed with advanced Alzheimer's disease and is currently in the moderate stage of the disease. He has difficulty with daily activities such as dressing and bathing, and his communication skills have been declining rapidly. He does not have any hearing impairment that may affect his participation in the activities. He is not currently taking any medications for his Alzheimer's disease. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and mild osteoarthritis. He enjoys listening to music and is able to follow along with simple melodies. He is not currently participating in any music therapy interventions. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has a supportive family who is involved in his care at the nursing home.

7-year-old female with a history of dental caries requiring fillings in multiple deciduous teeth. She presents with positive cooperation level according to the Frankl Behavior Scale and has sufficient mouth opening for dental treatment. There is no history of systemic or developmental disorders or allergies. The patient will be included in the study to compare the effectiveness of the Comfort-in system and infiltrative anesthesia with a traditional injector for local anesthesia application during dental procedures. The patient will be randomized into either the needle-free injection system (Comfort-In) group or the dental injection group. Pain intensity and anxiety levels will be assessed during and after the procedure using the Wong-Baker facial expressions and pain grading scale and the Modified Children's Dental Anxiety Scale face version, respectively. The patient will not be excluded unless supplemental anesthetics are required during the procedure.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) due to hypertension. He has been taking medications for blood pressure control for the past 3 years. He has a history of high uric acid levels and reports having occasional pain in his big toe joint. He denies having any gout attacks in the past. His recent lab tests show that his serum uric acid level is 8.5 mg/dL. He is following a low salt, low protein, and low purine diet. He has no other significant medical history except for occasional lower back pain and mild osteoarthritis in his knees. He is married, has two adult children, and works as a clerk in a government office. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a BMI of 28 and his blood pressure is well controlled at 130/80 mmHg. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the potential benefits of febuxostat in lowering his serum uric acid level and delaying the progression of his CKD.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently discharged from the hospital after an acute coronary syndrome event. He had an elevated ST segment on his EKG and his troponin levels were also elevated. He underwent coronary angiography and had stents placed to treat severe lesions. His GRACE score is over 118, indicating a high risk for 6-month mortality. His CHA2DS2-VACS score is over 2, indicating a high risk for stroke. He does not have a history of atrial fibrillation, and did not experience any episodes of atrial fibrillation during his hospital stay. He does not have a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, nor does he have an indication for one in the near future. He is able to understand the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not participating in any other clinical investigations and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. His life expectancy is greater than 24 months.

Patient is a 19-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 10. He has been receiving care at a pediatric diabetes clinic and is now preparing to transition to adult care. He has been experiencing some anxiety and concerns about the transition process and how it might impact his diabetes management. He lives with his parents and is currently enrolled in college. He has been managing his diabetes independently for several years now with support from his parents and healthcare team. He is interested in participating in this study to share his experiences and expectations around the transition process and to help develop recommendations that could improve the transition process for other emerging adults with type 1 diabetes.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer two months ago after presenting with abdominal pain and weight loss. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for this condition. She has an ECOG performance status of 2, but she is still able to perform most of her daily activities. Her laboratory results show that she has adequate hematopoietic, hepatic, and renal function. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy for her condition. She has no history of allergic reactions to any medications. She understands the requirements of the study and has provided signed informed consent. She is willing to use adequate contraception since the signing of informed consent until at least 3 months after stopping the study medication.

Maria is a 52-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset shortness of breath and chest pain. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Physical examination revealed tachypnea and mild hypoxemia. Her electrocardiogram was normal, and her chest X-ray showed no significant abnormalities. Pulmonary embolism was suspected, and she underwent ventilation-perfusion pulmonary tomoscintigraphy. The results were inconclusive, and further diagnostic tests are required. Maria is willing to participate in this exploratory metabolomics study to identify specific metabolic profiles that can predict the results of the ventilation-perfusion pulmonary tomoscintigraphy in subjects undergoing this examination for suspected acute pulmonary embolism. She understands the procedures involved and provides informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with stage C liver cancer. He has a history of hepatitis B and has been taking antiviral medication for the past year. The patient is currently undergoing palliative therapy with hepatic arterial chemoembolization, chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Statin in prolonging disease-free survival. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not on any other medications. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to provide informed consent for additional treatment with Statin.

The patient is a 26-year-old healthy male who works as an IT professional. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. He does not smoke, consume alcohol or use any recreational drugs. His family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. His BMI is 23 kg/m2. He is fluent in the local language and able to communicate well with the study investigator. He has no known allergies to medications or excipients. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to medical research and further his understanding of the potential health benefits of curcumin.

The patient is a 62 year old man who has been experiencing chronic leg ulcers for the past 6 months. He has been receiving home care services for his ulcers and finds them emotionally distressing and painful, impacting his quality of life. His recent ankle brachial pressure index (ABPI) test showed a result of 0.85. He is able to provide written consent and communicates in English. He has no history of diabetes or cognitive impairment. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the most effective compression bandaging technology for his ulcers.

The patient is a 28 year-old female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 2 years. She experiences moderate active UC symptoms with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloody stools. She has not had any systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss. She has not had a bowel resection, and does not have an ostomy or pouch. She has not had colon cancer or dysplasia in the colon. She is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not been on cyclosporine, azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate or TNF-α inhibitors in the last 12 weeks. She is not suffering from coeliac disease or lactose intolerance. She is able to understand the information material and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian male with a medical history of hypertension, congestive heart failure, and advanced chronic kidney disease. The patient has been on maintenance hemodialysis for the past 2 years and has a biocompatible membrane with a Kt/V > 1.2. The patient has been experiencing a decline in cardiorespiratory fitness and has a left ventricular ejection fraction less than 50%. The patient's C-reactive protein level is greater than or equal to 2 mg/L. The patient has no known allergies to rubber, latex, Escherichia coli or anakinra. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is 18 years of age or older. The patient has not used immunosuppressant or anti-inflammatory therapies in the past month, and has no active rheumatologic disease. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate is less than 30 mL/min/1.73m2.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with a single hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) of 4 cm in diameter. He has no history of hepatitis B or C, but he has been a heavy drinker for the past 20 years. He is currently abstaining from alcohol. He has no other significant medical history, and his blood tests show normal liver and kidney function. He is interested in exploring treatment options for his HCC and is open to participating in clinical trials. He has no known psychiatric or addiction problems, and he is able to provide informed consent. He has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past 6 months. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to undergo percutaneous microwave ablation (MWA) and cellular immunotherapy with cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to undergo treatment at the study site.

40-year-old female with a BMI of 33 kg/m² and a sedentary lifestyle presents with complaints of fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion, and difficulty performing daily activities.
