She has no known chronic diseases but has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. She reports a history of occasional snoring but denies any other sleep-related symptoms. She is interested in participating in an exercise study to improve her overall health and is willing to commit to 3 sessions per week for 8 weeks. She has not undergone bariatric surgery in the past 18 months and does not have any autoimmune or inflammatory diseases requiring long-term therapy.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury as a result of a motor vehicle accident 6 months ago. He has been experiencing persistent pain since then, which has been affecting his quality of life and daily functioning. The pain is localized to his lower back and legs, and is described as aching, burning, and shooting. He has been taking non-opioid pain medications but has not found them to be effective in managing his pain. The patient has no history of substance abuse or major psychiatric disorders. He is willing to participate in a 6-week program of physical therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, and methadone treatment to manage his pain. He has no allergies to latex, methadone, or diphenhydramine, and does not have any planned surgeries. The patient is motivated to find a way to manage his pain and improve his functioning.

A 54-year-old woman has been recently diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy treatment with docetaxel. She has no history of diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, or prior radiotherapy. She is not currently taking any medications that may confound the study data assessment. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance research into chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy. She will undergo a full medical history and physical examination, as well as blood and urine tests and imaging studies to determine her eligibility for the study. If she meets the eligibility criteria, she will be required to participate in seven visits, one before the start of chemotherapy and six after the scheduled treatment visits. At each visit, she will complete questionnaires to rate and describe any pain, numbness, or tingling during the course of chemotherapy. She will provide blood samples at every visit and have nerve conduction tests during the second, fourth, and sixth visits. She will also have a skin biopsy, either from a site that appears to be experiencing nerve damage or (for those who are not developing nerve damage symptoms) from a site near the first biopsy location. The data collected from this clinical trial will be used to identify the molecular-genetic mechanisms involved in chemotherapy-induced neuropathy in cancer patients and to develop novel pharmacological targets to be evaluated in future studies.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who just gave birth to a healthy baby boy. The baby was born at full term with a gestational age of 39 weeks and a birth weight of 7 pounds 8 ounces. The mother is in good health, with no significant medical or drug history. She plans to exclusively feed her infant the study product (formula-fed infants) as the sole source of nutrition for the duration of the study. The mother intends not to administer vitamin or mineral supplements, solid foods or juices to her infant during the study. The baby is currently 4 days old at the time of enrollment.

The patient is a 4-year-old Swedish child who participated in a cord clamping trial at birth. The child was born full-term to a healthy mother after a normal pregnancy. The mother was a non-smoker and had no haemolytic disease, and the pregnancy had no complications such as preeclampsia, diabetes, or prolonged rupture of membranes. The child was born via vaginal delivery with cephalic presentation, and there were no complications during delivery. The child's mother had understood the meaning of the study and had provided written informed consent. The child had either received early cord clamping (ECC) or delayed cord clamping (DCC) at the time of birth. The child is now between 48 and 51 months old and is eligible for the neurodevelopmental testing. The child's parents have been informed about the testing and have received a letter containing information about the study, including time and location for the testing, and the two questionnaires, SDQ and ASQ. The parents have answered these questionnaires before the visit to the psychologist. After the neurodevelopmental testing, the parents will receive a written report, and if abnormal results are discovered, due action will be taken.

56-year-old male with a history of ischemic stroke and hypertension. He was previously treated with amlodipine and lisinopril, but his blood pressure has been difficult to control. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has no history of dementia or other severe systemic diseases. He was previously able to perform activities of daily living independently but currently has a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 3 due to residual weakness in his left arm and leg. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce his risk of recurrent stroke.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has tested positive for COVID-19 and is experiencing symptoms such as fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. He has not taken aspirin in the past month. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He has not had any active gastrointestinal bleeding in the past 3 months and his platelet count is normal. He is able to understand the potential risks and benefits of the study and can follow up with the required evaluations. He does not have any history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has not had any cardiac stent placement in the past year and does not have any medical conditions that may interfere with the research behavior or lead to increased risk. He is expected to benefit from the use of aspirin in reducing the incidence of severe and critical symptoms and shortening the hospitalization duration.

A 58 year old female with a primary diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the knee. She has been experiencing progressive knee pain and stiffness for the past year, which has significantly limited her daily activities. She has tried conservative management including physical therapy, weight loss, and medications, but her symptoms have continued to worsen. She has a BMI of 35 and is otherwise healthy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the High Flex and Standard Rotating Platform Total Knee Arthroplasty to determine which option would provide better flexion and improve her quality of life.

A 25-year-old non-smoking female with good oral hygiene presents to the clinic with concerns about gum recession on the upper front teeth. She reports no previous periodontal surgery and has no known contraindications for surgery. Clinical examination reveals Miller Class II gingival recession defects with at least 3 mm depth on the buccal aspect of the upper right and left central and lateral incisors. The patient has a healthy periodontium with full-mouth plaque score (FMPS) and full-mouth bleeding score (FMBS) less than 15%. The CEJ is identifiable with a step of ≤1 mm at the CEJ level and no associated caries, deep abrasion, restoration or pulpal pathology. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the root coverage and aesthetic results of connective tissue graft positioned apical to the CEJ (CAF+CTG-ACEJ) with CAF+CTG positioned on the CEJ (CAF+CTG-CEJ) for treating isolated gingival recession defects.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of impulsivity, mood swings, and unstable relationships since early adolescence. She has a history of self-harm and attempted suicide. She has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder by a mental health professional. She has tried several psychotherapies but did not experience any significant improvement in her symptoms. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. She is not pregnant and is using adequate contraception. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has the ability to understand and sign the consent form.

A 25 yo F who was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and is currently an inpatient at a psychiatric facility. She has reported experiencing negative impacts of stigma related to her condition, which has caused her to feel isolated and embarrassed. She has expressed interest in participating in a study to help her cope with these feelings. She has a good understanding of the study and is able to give informed consent. She is fluent in English and is able to complete the interview in English. She has no history of substance misuse or acquired brain injury. She is currently receiving care from a clinical in-patient team and is able to participate in the study.

A 14-year-old Hispanic male was recently diagnosed with recurrent osteosarcoma in the left femur, following initial treatment with chemotherapy and surgery. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with no response. The patient is experiencing pain and mobility issues due to the tumor. The patient is eligible for the Phase 1 study of eribulin mesylate in pediatric participants with recurrent or refractory solid tumors (excluding CNS), including lymphomas. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of being between 12 months and 18 years of age, having measurable or evaluable disease, and having a Karnofsky score of at least 50%. The patient has fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior anticancer chemotherapy, as required by the study. The patient has adequate bone marrow, renal, and liver function, as well as adequate cardiac function. The patient has not received prior therapy with eribulin mesylate or other investigational drugs, and is not currently receiving other anticancer agents or drugs that prolong the QTc. The patient is willing to comply with all aspects of the protocol and has provided written informed consent.

A 65-year-old woman with a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in her right eye and diabetic retinopathy (DR) in her left eye presents to the clinic for a clinical trial. She has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty reading small print for the past few months in both eyes. The patient has undergone OCT scans in the past and is able and willing to undergo additional scans for this clinical trial. She agrees to give informed consent and has no evidence of macular disease other than AMD and DR in either eye.

Samantha is a 55-year-old woman who has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. She had a recent episode of chest pain and was diagnosed with stable angina. Her cardiac catheterization revealed coronary artery disease (CAD) with 70% stenosis of her left anterior descending artery (LAD). She was started on a low dose (81 mg) aspirin daily and scheduled for percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) procedure. She has been compliant with her medication and has not taken any NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors for at least 10 days prior to the procedure. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication and her Hgb A1c and FBS are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the biosynthesis of PGD2 during PTCA procedure.

This is a 32-year-old active duty military member who has been experiencing chronic shoulder pain rated at a minimum of 4 out of 10 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale. The pain is not related to any traumatic injury and is not referred from the cervical spine. The patient is right-handed and does not have any bleeding disorders. They are not currently taking any anticoagulant medications and do not have a full-thickness rotator cuff tear. The patient is able to lie prone and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve the understanding of how dry needling works to relieve musculoskeletal pain.

Patient B is a 12-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 3 years. She experiences wheezing, coughing, and chest tightness when exposed to dust mites and pollen. She is currently taking albuterol as a rescue inhaler, but her symptoms are not well-controlled. She has never been hospitalized for asthma and does not have any other underlying medical conditions. She has a resting forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 80% predicted and her skin-prick test is positive for Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus. Her parents are willing to participate in the study and she is able to perform reproducible spirometry, whole body plethysmography and interrupter technique. She is not currently taking β-blockers, astemizole or oral corticosteroids, nor is she receiving immunotherapy.

A 54-year-old woman who had breast cancer in 2015 and underwent surgery, chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She is currently in remission and is being followed-up regularly by her oncologist. She reports experiencing discomfort and pain during sexual intercourse, as well as occasional urinary incontinence. She has had two vaginal deliveries and currently works as a teacher. She does not smoke and reports moderate alcohol consumption. She lives in the city of Campo Belo, Minas Gerais and has agreed to participate in a study investigating pelvic floor dysfunction in cancer survivors. She will be interviewed by telephone and asked about her socioeconomic indicators, gynecological-obstetric history, life habits, as well as specific questionnaires for the evaluation of pelvic floor dysfunction, functional performance and quality of life. The study aims to verify the prevalence of pelvic floor dysfunction among cancer survivors and evaluate the impact on their quality of life and functional performance.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer and bone metastases. She experiences moderate to severe pain, with a pain score of 7 on the Worst Pain scale of the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI). She currently takes opioids for pain management. She has not received bisphosphonate treatment in the past three weeks and has not undergone radiotherapy to bone in the past four weeks. She does not have hypersensitivity to ibandronate and does not have CNS or meningeal metastases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially alleviate her bone pain.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of high-grade retroperitoneal sarcoma presenting with increased abdominal girth and pain. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the retroperitoneum involving the left kidney and adrenal gland. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of intermediate-grade sarcoma. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and had a partial response to treatment. She met the eligibility criteria for the Preoperative Proton Radiotherapy for Retroperitoneal Sarcoma study and was consented for participation. Her medical history also included hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She had no history of smoking or alcohol use. Physical examination revealed a well-nourished patient with a palpable mass in the left abdomen. She had no significant neurological deficits, and her laboratory studies were within normal limits. The patient was able to understand the study requirements and provided signed informed consent. She was started on proton radiotherapy as per the study protocol. Follow-up will be conducted as per the study schedule.

Sarah is a 58-year-old woman who works as a teacher. She has a family history of hypertension and has been experiencing high blood pressure readings during her routine visits to the doctor's office. She has not been taking any antihypertensive medications but is generally healthy without any other significant medical problems. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has also been monitoring her blood pressure at home and has noticed significant variability in her readings. Her systolic blood pressure ranges from 135 to 155 mmHg while her diastolic blood pressure ranges from 85 to 95 mmHg. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce blood pressure variability in essential hypertension. She has no contraindications to study treatments and is willing to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who smokes about half a pack of cigarettes per day. She has been smoking for the past 10 years and has tried to quit several times without success. She visits the emergency department at the "Maggiore della Carità" University Hospital in Novara, Italy due to a mild chest pain. During the triage interview, she self-reports as a smoker and expresses a willingness to quit. She is informed about the clinical trial and agrees to participate. She provides informed consent and is allocated to the intervention group. She completes a baseline questionnaire about her smoking habits, health status, socio-demographic characteristics, and degree of addiction. She also undergoes the 5As-based counseling performed by the ED nurse. The counseling includes a strong, clear, and personalized advice to quit, assessment of her readiness to quit, and assistance in her quit attempts. She is also provided with information about the Treatment Center for Tobacco use (CTT) of the Addiction Department of the Local Health Unit of Novara (ASL NO) and is asked if she wants to be contacted by the CTT to start an intensive treatment. She agrees to be contacted by the CTT. Follow-up questionnaires are administered to her by telephone at 6 and 12 months to assess the outcomes of the intervention.

A 65-year-old male with a 4-year history of Parkinson's disease presented to the neurology clinic with complaints of severe freezing of gait (FOG). He had undergone bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation (STN-DBS) surgery 6 months ago but still experienced FOG in his "off" state. His current medications included levodopa-carbidopa 25/100 mg four times a day, pramipexole 1.5 mg daily, and amantadine 100 mg twice a day. The patient had no history of other significant medical or surgical illnesses. His baseline UPDRS part I, II, IV, FOG-Q, and PDQ-39 scores were 7, 15, 8, 29, and 31, respectively. He had a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 25. He was able to walk independently and had no other significant neurological deficits. The patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the frequency effect of STN-DBS through the dual system on his FOG.

An 70 years old male patient with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, presented to the cardiology clinic with complaints of palpitations and occasional dizziness. The patient denies any history of stroke or heart failure. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and diabetes. The patient has a regular follow-up with his cardiologist and has undergone ECGs in the past. The patient does not have any permanent pacemaker or implantable defibrillator. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for home monitoring for atrial fibrillation using a Microlife Blood Pressure Monitor.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus two years ago seeks to participate in this study. He reports a history of uncontrolled diabetes with HbA1c levels ranging from 8.5% to 10% despite taking metformin 1000 mg twice a day. He has a sedentary lifestyle and admits to poor dietary habits. He recently participated in a diabetes improvement program and was able to achieve an HbA1c level of 7.2%. He is now motivated to maintain tight glycemic control and is willing to participate in the study to determine the optimal frequency of maintenance intervention needed to prevent glycemic relapse. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation during a routine medical check-up. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He takes medications for each condition daily. He has no history of stroke, transient ischemic attack, or other thromboembolic events. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is physically active and enjoys playing golf regularly. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a family history of high cholesterol. He has been diagnosed with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) and has been receiving lipid apheresis treatment. He has no prior history of cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes. He does not smoke and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is not currently experiencing any endocrine or gastrointestinal disorders. The patient is within the age range of 18-60 years and is eligible for participation in the study.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who fell from a ladder and sustained a fracture of the proximal humerus. X-ray showed a three-part fracture of the humerus. He has no history of shoulder or upper extremity fractures. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is right hand dominant and works as a mechanic. He is able to perform activities of daily living independently. He has no history of rheumatoid arthritis or any other bone disease. He has not undergone any previous surgery on his shoulder. He understands the study requirements and is willing to participate.

Mrs. Johnson is a 62-year-old woman who has been admitted to the hospital with sepsis and acute renal failure. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She was initially treated with fluid resuscitation and antibiotics but her renal function continued to deteriorate, and she was started on noradrenaline infusion for hemodynamic support. The treating clinicians are uncertain about the balance of benefits and risks likely to be conferred by treatment with different membranes. They anticipate treating her with haemofiltration for at least 72 hours. Mrs. Johnson meets the inclusion criteria for initiating haemofiltration due to oliguria that has been unresponsive to fluid resuscitation measures. She has given informed consent to participate in the study comparing high cut-off haemofiltration with standard haemofiltration in acute renal failure.

A 46-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic HCV genotype 1 infection for the past 5 years. She has previously been treated with ribavirin/PEG-INF combination therapy for 24 weeks, but her viral load remained positive. She has not received any HCV treatment in the past 12 weeks. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she is on lisinopril 20 mg daily. She had a liver biopsy 16 months ago, which showed Metavir fibrosis score F3. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her written informed consent. She has no history of allergy or intolerance to telaprevir, and her medical record shows no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma, coagulation disorders, or HIV/HBV co-infection. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2. She is currently using two contraceptive methods and is insured under the French social security system.

Patient is a newborn baby boy born at 39 weeks of gestation weighing 3.5 kg. He was delivered via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. The baby has no known genetic or metabolic diseases. The mother had a healthy pregnancy, with no significant medical history. The baby is currently admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for a clinically indicated operation. The parents have given their consent for the baby to participate in this observational study.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has been suffering from severe pain in her right leg for the past six months. She reports the pain as burning, tingling and sharp, and it has been interfering with her daily activities. She has tried several pain medications but they have not provided sufficient relief. Examination shows no obvious neurological deficits but there is tenderness on palpation of the lumbar spine. Imaging studies reveal a herniated disc at the L5 level. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. It is important to note that the patient is not taking any medication that affects coagulation or platelet function, and has no known hypersensitivity to local anesthetics.

Unfortunately, as this clinical trial is focused on assessing the attitudes and effectiveness of a virtual intervention for primary care professionals, there is no need for patient participation. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently in her third trimester of pregnancy. She has a history of anxiety and depression, and her obstetrician has identified her as being at risk of postpartum depression. She is currently receiving regular prenatal check-ups at the MGH Obstetrics Program. She is married and works part-time as a graphic designer. She enjoys painting and reading books in her free time. She has a supportive family and a close group of friends. She has a history of substance use disorder, but she has been sober for the last two years and has been attending regular support group meetings. She has not experienced any obstetric complications during her pregnancy, and her baby is healthy. She is not currently taking any medications that may interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help prevent postpartum depression and improve her bonding with her baby.

The patient is a 13-year-old boy complaining of pain in his hip and difficulty walking. He has a history of being overweight and has been experiencing the pain for the past few weeks. The pain is in his left hip and is aggravated by physical activity. The patient has difficulty walking and is using crutches for support. On examination, there is tenderness in the left hip and a limited range of motion. X-ray imaging reveals a moderate to severe slipped capital femoral epiphysis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. The patient is a good candidate for surgical treatment for slipped capital femoral epiphysis.

A 25 year old female patient diagnosed with beta-thalassemia major presents to the clinic. She has been receiving regular blood transfusions for the past 10 years and has been on iron chelation therapy for the last 2 years. Her serum ferritin levels have been decreasing over the last 6 months, with two consecutive readings showing levels below 500 ng/ml. The patient is willing to cooperate with the study procedures and has a good understanding of the requirements of the study. She has no history of serious immunologic hypersensitivity to any medication and has not participated in any investigational drug study in the last 30 days. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use medically acceptable forms of birth control during the study and a month afterward. The patient is in good general health and has no known contraindications to the designated procedures and restrictions of the protocol.

A 54 year old man came to the clinic complaining of gradually worsening headaches over the past few months. He has a history of glioblastoma and received surgery and radiation therapy a year ago. His MRI confirmed glioblastoma recurrence with a size of 3 cm. He also experienced mild cognitive impairment and difficulty in moving his right arm. His KPS score was 80. He has no history of immunotherapy and has not received any live vaccines in the past 30 days. His hematologic, renal, and hepatic functions are adequate with no underlying autoimmune disease. He has not been treated with any other investigational agent in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has provided written informed consent.

A 45-year-old female with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer presented with a history of worsening fatigue and shortness of breath. The patient had previously undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiotherapy with limited success. A recent PET scan showed progression of the disease to the liver, lungs, and bones. The patient's ECOG performance status was 1, and her life expectancy was estimated to be greater than 3 months. The patient had adequate organ functions, and at least 4 weeks had passed since her last chemotherapy treatment. She had no history of CNS metastasis, was not receiving any other investigational agents, and was willing to follow the protocol required evaluations. The patient agreed to practice effective contraception and signed the informed consent form. She was deemed eligible for the study and is a suitable candidate for the upcoming clinical trial.

A 40-year-old man presented to the clinic with persistent abdominal pain for the past 6 months. He had a history of chronic pancreatitis based on imaging studies. The pain was localized to the upper abdomen and was described as constant, dull, and achy. The patient had been on multiple medications including analgesics, proton pump inhibitors, and pancreatic enzyme supplements with no significant improvement in pain. The patient was diagnosed with alcohol-induced chronic pancreatitis 2 years ago, with no history of pancreatic cancer or duct obstruction. He had no significant past medical history and was a non-smoker. In the physical examination, he had tenderness in the upper abdomen and no signs of neurologic or cardiac disease. The patient was willing to participate in the study and gave written informed consent. The patient understood the requirements of the study and was willing to comply with the study visit schedule and requirements.

Patient B is a 2-year-old female with a history of epilepsy, diagnosed at 6 months of age. She has a history of focal impaired awareness seizures, with a frequency of 2-3 seizures per week, despite being on a stable dose of 2 antiepileptic drugs (AEDs). She weighs 8 kilograms and has had brain imaging (MRI) ruling out a progressive cause of epilepsy. Her interictal EEG is consistent with epilepsy. She has not had any episodes of status epilepticus requiring hospitalization in the past 3 months. She has not had epilepsy surgery in the past year nor is she scheduled for surgery in the next 6 months. She has not used intermittent rescue benzodiazepines more than once in the past 2 weeks. She is not on a ketogenic diet and is not taking felbamate or vigabatrin. She has no significant active hepatic or hematological diseases. She has no clinically significant laboratory abnormalities or any clinically acute or chronic disease. She is eligible for this study as she is between 1 month and less than 4 years of age and meets all other inclusion criteria. Her parents have provided informed consent for her participation in this study.

A 45 year old man with a clinical diagnosis of painful diabetic neuropathy complains of persistent, burning pain in his feet and ankles for the past year despite trying various pain medications. He is not on any other medications and has no other underlying medical conditions. He has been informed about the study and is willing to participate, and understands the trial's procedures and requirements. He provides informed consent prior to participating in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old college student who has been experiencing anxiety and stress related to academic pressure. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and is a native English speaker. She is right-handed and has no metal implants or piercings that cannot be removed from the body. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the relationship between brain activity and emotions. She is willing to undergo MRI scanning and is not claustrophobic. She is not pregnant or possibly pregnant. She is in good health and is not taking any medications that may affect her brain function. She is willing to participate in a study that involves learning to increase blood flow in certain brain regions using advanced feedback techniques.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and has a family history of heart disease. His physical examination revealed a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, heart rate of 90 bpm, and respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute. Laboratory results showed elevated levels of LDL cholesterol and HbA1c. An electrocardiogram showed ST-segment depression in leads V1-V4. Coronary angiography revealed a de novo, single-vessel lesion in the left anterior descending artery, with a reference vessel diameter of 3.2 mm and a lesion length of 18 mm. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the REPARA study, and the use of a bioresorbable device for coronary intervention is indicated. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no contraindications for dual antiplatelet therapy.

A 55-year-old man came to the clinic with a complaint of knee pain that has been bothering him for the past 2 years. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking oral anti-inflammatory medication for the past year. He works as a carpenter and has a BMI of 30. He is married with two children and uses barrier methods of contraception. He has not taken aspirin or naproxen-containing medications for the past 7 days and has not taken any anti-inflammatory medication or acetaminophen for the past 5 days. He has noticed a significant increase in his knee pain over the past month, as measured by a 15-point increase in WOMAC Visual Analog Score between his screening visit and baseline study entry visit. He has never participated in a clinical trial before but is willing to try new treatments. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with CIDP 3 years ago. He has been receiving IVIg infusions every 4 weeks for the past 2 years, which have been effective in managing his symptoms. He has been able to continue his treatment at home for the past year. He lives with his wife and two adult children who are supportive of his condition. He is retired and spends most of his time at home, but enjoys gardening and cooking. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He has no history of allergies or other medical conditions. He is comfortable using technology and has access to a reliable internet connection at home. He is interested in participating in the trial to evaluate the effectiveness of the telemonitoring system to manage his CIDP.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian male who was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia. The patient is an independent individual who lives alone and has no history of any chronic medical condition. The patient's baseline functional status before the illness was assessed by a Barthel Index score of 90, indicating good functional ability. The patient was transferred to the medical ICU and required intubation and mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. The patient has been intubated for less than 72 hours, and the patient's estimated six-month mortality is less than 50%. The patient has no history of rapid evolving neurological or neuromuscular disease. The patient has not been enrolled in any other clinical trial. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 68-year-old Japanese man diagnosed with moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (3+ MR). He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiac surgery or structural heart disease. His symptoms include fatigue, shortness of breath, and occasional chest pain upon exertion. He has been referred to the study for possible treatment with a MitraClip implant. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and has provided informed consent to participate in the post-marketing clinical use surveillance study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who had a stroke 8 months ago. He is currently experiencing difficulty using his right hand and has residual upper extremity hemiparesis. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. His upper extremity Fugl-Meyer score is 50, which is below the cutoff score of 66 for inclusion in the study. His Mini Mental State Exam score is 27, which is above the cutoff score of 24 for inclusion in the study. He is able to elicit a discernible and reliable MEP following single-pulse TMS to the lesioned hemisphere, which meets the inclusion criteria for the study. He has no history of neurological disease other than stroke and has no contraindications to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) or peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS). He is not currently taking medications that act on the central nervous system other than selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).

This is a 62-year-old woman with a history of advanced ovarian cancer. She underwent surgery and received standard chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. However, she experienced disease progression and was found to have lung metastases. She underwent additional chemotherapy with topotecan and liposomal doxorubicin, but her disease continued to progress. She now has advanced solid tumors with kidney dysfunction, as evidenced by a creatinine clearance of 40 mL/min. She has no active brain metastases and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and meets all other eligibility criteria for this study. She has not received prior treatment with exatecan mesylate or any other investigational drugs within the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She has given informed consent to participate in this phase I clinical trial to evaluate the maximum tolerated dose of exatecan mesylate in patients with advanced solid tumors and varying degrees of renal dysfunction.

A 28-year-old healthy woman who is not pregnant, not breastfeeding, and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception consistently during the treatment period and for at least 30 days after the dose of study treatment. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2, is a non-smoker, and is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications or dietary/nutritional supplements (except for multivitamins at the recommended dose and paracetamol, up to 2g in any one day). She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the last 2 years and has a negative screen for drugs of abuse, cotinine, or alcohol. She has no history of any surgical or medical condition that might significantly alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of CB-0406. She has no active or recurring clinically significant disorder of any system and her hematology, clinical chemistry, coagulation, and urinalysis test results within normal ranges. She is able and willing to comply with the protocol and study procedures.

A family consisting of a 38-year-old mother, a 40-year-old father, and two children aged 8 and 10 are sought for a clinical trial focused on promoting regular physical activity. The family lives in the Greater Victoria Area in British Columbia and currently reports low physical activity levels. The target children are not meeting Canada's physical activity guidelines. The family will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The comparison group will receive Canada's family guide to physical activity guidelines, while the intervention group will receive the same guidelines along with family physical activity planning material. The family will be required to participate for six months, with follow-up assessments at designated intervals. The study is looking to evaluate the effectiveness of the planning condition in improving adherence to regular physical activity compared to the control condition. The study will also evaluate the effect of the planning condition on motivational, health-related quality of life, and health-related fitness outcomes. The family will need to complete a Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire (PAR-Q) to ensure that they are safe to participate in physical activity.

A 44-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. She has never received any treatment for this condition. Her medical history reveals that she had a blood transfusion during her cesarean section 20 years ago. She is currently asymptomatic and is in good health, as confirmed by a physical exam and laboratory tests. She has no known allergies or drug sensitivities. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements and restrictions of the study protocol. Her body weight is 60 kg, and her BMI is 25.2 kg/m2. She has no history of cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, biliary, gastrointestinal, or renal disorders, or cancer within the past 5 years. Her AST, ALT, and alkaline phosphatase levels are <3.0xULN, and her bilirubin level is <1.5xULN. Her ECG shows an average QTcB of 420 msec. She is positive for HCV RNA and anti-HCV antibody at the time of screening, with an HCV viral load of 150,000 IU/mL and HCV genotype 1a. She has not undergone liver biopsy in the past, but her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has not consumed any red wine, seville oranges, grapefruit or grapefruit juice and/or pummelos, exotic citrus fruits, grapefruit hybrids or fruit juices for the past 14 days. She has not taken any prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements (including St John's Wort) for the past 7 days. She is mentally and legally competent to give written informed consent.

The patient is a 23-year-old female with a Class I bimaxillary dentoalveolar proclination. She has a full permanent dentition and good oral hygiene. She complains of crowded teeth and is interested in orthodontic treatment. She has no systemic diseases, signs or symptoms of temporomandibular disorders (TMD), and has not had any previous orthodontic treatment. She has all of her permanent teeth, with healthy bone around her first molars. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing lingual lever arm mechanics vs conventional lingual orthodontic mechanics for the correction of her bimaxillary proclination.

The patient is a 12-year-old adolescent who is up-to-date on all recommended vaccinations but has not yet completed the HPV vaccination series. The patient is a student in New York State and is registered with a participating practice that was randomly selected for this study. The patient's immunization record is in the New York State Immunization Information System (NYSIIS) database. The patient is in good health with no history of allergies or chronic medical conditions. The patient's parent or guardian has provided consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old child who has been diagnosed with a peanut and tree nut allergy. The child and their family express anxiety about casual exposure to peanuts and tree nuts through skin contact or being near the offending food. The child has not had any severe allergic reactions but has experienced discomfort and anxiety in social situations where food is present. The child is currently taking antihistamines for seasonal allergies but has no other known medical conditions. The family is interested in participating in a study that aims to reduce the child's anxiety and improve their quality of life by having the child hold and touch a cup containing the offending allergen in addition to education. The family is able to understand and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 2 years ago. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisone to control her symptoms. She has experienced two flares in the past year, one of which required hospitalization. She has a history of depression and anxiety but is currently managing well with therapy and medication. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. Her current symptoms include joint pain and stiffness, fatigue, and mild skin rash. She has not had a SLE flare in the past 3 months and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially help with her monitoring and treatment plan. She has given her consent and is affiliated with the French social security system. She has not had any recent viral infections and does not have any other chronic inflammatory diseases.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing fatigue and muscle weakness for the past few months. He has been feeling generally unwell and has noticed a decrease in his overall physical activity level. A blood test reveals that his serum 25OHD levels are in the range of 20-40 nmol/L. He has not made any changes to his medication in the past four weeks. The patient has no history of serious diseases such as cardiovascular disease or diabetes. He has not been taking any vitamin D supplements. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on genetic, proteomic, and metabolomic profile in adipose tissue.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with Friedreich's ataxia. She was diagnosed with the condition at the age of 18. She has a homozygous GAA repeat expansion. She is able to walk with assistance from a walker for short distances but has difficulty with balance and coordination. She has a score of 24 on the mFARS_neuro scale. She is able to perform basic daily activities with minimal assistance. She takes daily multivitamins but does not exceed 30 mcg/day of biotin supplementation. She has no history of aspiration, aspiration pneumonia or recurrent episodes of pneumonia. She has no history of arrhythmia or unstable coronary artery disease. She is not on any investigational drug or device. She weighs 50 kg.

A 46-year-old data entry specialist has been experiencing numbness, tingling, and weakness in her left hand for the past few months. She has difficulty gripping objects and performing her work duties. She went to see her primary care physician who referred her to an orthopaedic surgeon. The surgeon diagnosed her with carpal tunnel syndrome based on the EMG results. She has no other musculoskeletal injuries. She is an otherwise healthy non-smoker with no significant medical history. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial for post-operative pain management in carpal tunnel release surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing symptoms such as tremors, stiffness, and slow movement for the past 2 years. He is currently taking dopamine agonists and levodopa to manage his symptoms. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to attend study visits every 6 months for up to 5 years without undue hardship. He has no history of atypical parkinsonian syndromes or definite dementia. He has not received any drugs that might interfere with dopamine transporter SPECT imaging within 6 months of screening. He has no medical or psychiatric conditions or lab abnormalities that might preclude participation.

The patient is a 64-year-old man with a history of stage IV prostate cancer that has become resistant to hormone therapy. He has received two prior hormonal interventions, including antiandrogen therapy, without a sustained response. The patient has no brain metastases or other CNS disease. His PSA has increased by more than 50% over baseline on at least two measurements at least two weeks apart. He has no prior chemotherapy or experimental therapy for metastatic disease. His performance status is CALGB 1 and his life expectancy is at least three months. The patient has no primary muscle disease and no active, uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infection. His bilirubin, AST/ALT, and prothrombin time are normal. His creatinine clearance is at least 70 mL/min. The patient has no other serious medical illness that limits survival to less than three months, no psychiatric condition that would preclude informed consent, and no other malignancy within the past five years except inactive nonmelanomatous skin cancer or adequately treated stage I or II cancer in remission. The patient is not taking megestrol or other hormonal agents, systemic or inhaled corticosteroids (intranasal and topical steroids are allowed), heparin, warfarin, or aspirin.

This is a 55-year-old active male who recently fell while playing basketball and experienced severe pain in his right shoulder. He visited a local orthopedic clinic and was diagnosed with a massive rotator cuff tear based on the MRI images. The tear was identified to be more than 5 cm in diameter. The patient has been experiencing significant pain and difficulty with activities of daily living, including dressing, combing hair, and reaching overhead. He has not undergone any previous shoulder surgery or therapy. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide scores for the study. The patient does not have any systemic infections or infections at the surgical site. The patient is currently not taking any medication for pain or other conditions. The patient is in otherwise good health and is physically active.

70 year old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the clinic with a complaint of difficulty in remembering things and daily activities for past 6 months. He is accompanied by his spouse who reports that he forgets appointments, misplaces things, and has difficulty following conversations. The patient denies any history of head injury, alcohol or drug abuse. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only socially. His medications include lisinopril, simvastatin, and metformin. His physical exam reveals no focal neurological deficits but he scored 22 out of 30 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). The patient is proficient in English and does not require a translator. He has no visual impairment. Based on his cognitive symptoms and the physical exam, he is diagnosed with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and is referred to a specialist for further evaluation and treatment.

A 9-year-old girl with a confirmed diagnosis of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets (XLH) presents to the clinic with skeletal malformations including bowed legs, bone pain, and dental abnormalities. Her serum calcium level is within normal range, but her fasting PTH level is higher than normal. She has been taking a stable dose of standard therapy for XLH rickets for at least 2 months prior to study entry. Her parents are willing to provide informed consent for her participation in the study. She does not have concomitant kidney failure or receive treatment with agents that may affect skeletal metabolism.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but has been taking medications to manage them. He has no history of diabetes or smoking. His recent exercise stress test showed an abnormal result, and his primary physician referred him to a cardiologist for further evaluation. His cardiologist suspects coronary artery disease and recommends a non-invasive coronary angiography and myocardial perfusion imaging using 320 detector computed tomography (CORE-320). The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets the eligibility criteria, except his BMI is 42. He is currently taking lisinopril, amlodipine, and atorvastatin for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

This is a 46-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic hypercalcemia for several years. She has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, frequent urination, and muscle weakness. She has no history of hyperparathyroidism or any other genetic disorders associated with hypercalcemia, and has not been diagnosed with neoplasia or granulomatosis. She is interested in participating in a genetic analysis for medical purposes to identify potential underlying genetic causes of her hypercalcemia.

The patient is a 30-year-old French woman who has been experiencing symptoms of flu for the past 24 hours, including cough, sore throat, headache, and fatigue. She has a documented fever of 38.5°C and has tested positive for influenza A on a rapid diagnostic test. She has no history of asthma or chronic bronchitis, and her creatinine clearance is above 30 ml/min. She is not pregnant and has no history of depression or psychiatric disorders. She has not received any influenza vaccination within the last 12 months and is not currently taking any medications for her symptoms. She is a member of the social security or CMU. She is willing to give written informed consent and complete a questionnaire for the clinical trial. She is able to use the diskhaler to administer zanamivir if assigned to that treatment group.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been on antipsychotic medication for the past 2 years but has experienced intolerable side effects such as weight gain and sedation. He is currently stable and has not had an acute exacerbation in the past 8 weeks. He has no history of hospitalization for psychiatric illness in the past 8 weeks. He has no significant medical condition or chronic disease. He has not attempted suicide in the past 6 months and has no active suicidal ideation with or without specific plans. He is not at significant risk of harming himself or others. He has not been treated with quetiapine or quetiapine XR in the past 6 weeks and has no history of inadequate response or intolerability to quetiapine or quetiapine XR. He is willing to participate in a 52-week clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of an investigational drug for people with schizophrenia.

The patient is a 28-year-old mother of a 6-month-old baby boy diagnosed with single ventricle congenital heart disease (SVCHD). She is a stay-at-home mom and lives with her husband and son in a suburban area. She has a history of anxiety and depression, which was managed with medication before pregnancy. During the pregnancy, she received prenatal care and was referred to a specialized hospital for the management of her son's heart condition. Her son had his first heart surgery at 3 days old and now needs a second palliative surgery. She is worried about her son's health and future, and she feels overwhelmed with the responsibilities that come with caring for a medically complex infant. She has noticed that she has been having trouble sleeping and has flashbacks of her son's first surgery. She is interested in participating in the study to help other families going through similar experiences and to learn more about her own mental health.

A 30-year-old female with a BMI of 25.5 and no significant medical history presents for enrollment in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker with no history of drug abuse. She reports no allergies to any of the investigational drug or ingredients. She is not currently taking any medication that may affect the trial results. She has not participated in any clinical trials or donated blood within the past 3 months. She is not currently pregnant or planning on becoming pregnant within the next 6 months. She is willing to comply with the study procedure and complete the study. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a premature very low birth weight (VLBW) infant born at 31 weeks gestation and weighing 1500 grams. The infant is appropriate for gestational age and the parents have given their consent for participation in the clinical trial. The infant has no respiratory disease, has a good Apgar score of 8 at 5 minutes, and does not have any syndromes affecting growth. The infant is not small for gestational age and does not require any medication beyond vitamins, iron and caffeine.

72-year-old Caucasian female presented to the oncology clinic with a newly diagnosed adenocarcinoma of the breast, confirmed with histology. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. She does not have a history of neurological disorders, stroke, or head injury. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, substance abuse, or HIV/AIDS. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have any visual or hearing impairments that would preclude her from completing interviews or neuropsychological testing. She is not taking psychoactive medications, and her dose of any medications has been stable for at least two months prior to enrollment. She has not received any chemotherapy or hormonal therapy for breast cancer. She is willing to participate in the optional neuroimaging portion of the study and does not have any contraindications to MRI. She is eligible for the study and is a suitable candidate for the evaluation of the impact of systemic therapy on cognition in older breast cancer patients.

A 3-month-old male infant was brought to the emergency department with a fever of 39.5OC. He was born full-term via a normal vaginal delivery, and his mother received adequate prenatal care. The infant has been exclusively breastfed and has no known allergies. He has been healthy until this episode. On physical examination, the infant was alert, irritable, and had a heart rate of 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute, and a temperature of 39.5OC. His fontanelle was normal, and his skin was warm and dry. His lungs were clear, and his heart sounds were regular without murmurs. The abdomen was soft and non-tender, and there was no hepatosplenomegaly. The neurological examination was normal. The sepsis workup was initiated, and the infant received an intravenous dose of acetaminophen. The decision was made to perform a lumbar puncture to rule out meningitis. The infant's legal guardian provided informed consent for the procedure and the subsequent participation in the clinical trial.

68 year old male with a 30-pack year smoking history presenting with chronic cough and dyspnoea on exertion. The patient reports worsening symptoms over the past year and has previously been diagnosed with COPD. Spirometry shows an FEV1/FVC ratio of 62% and an FEV1 of 55% predicted. The patient is currently using an albuterol inhaler as needed for symptom relief. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. The patient denies any history of asthma or recent myocardial infarction. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options for his COPD.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with a descending thoracic aortic aneurysm measuring 6 cm in diameter. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has a family history of aortic aneurysms but no personal history of connective tissue disorders. He has no history of drug abuse and has not participated in any other investigational device or drug study within the last year. He is a candidate for surgical repair and is classified as ASA Class III. He has no history of myocardial infarction or cerebral vascular accident within the last 6 weeks. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 40-year-old female with a history of atherosclerotic vascular disease. She is currently taking clopidogrel to prevent thrombotic events. Her past medical history is significant for depression and she has been on fluoxetine for the past 6 months. She is not a smoker and has no history of hemorrhagic disease or peptic ulcer. Her liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. Her platelet count is 210 G/L and % platelet aggregation is 75%. She weighs 70 Kg and has a BMI of 25. Her current medications include fluoxetine, clopidogrel, and a multivitamin supplement. She has no known allergies to any medications. Her MADRS score is 17, indicating mild to moderate depression. She has not participated in any clinical or device trial in the past 3 months.

A 52-year-old male with a history of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer presents with progressive shortness of breath and cough. He has failed two lines of standard chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Biopsy of the lung lesion revealed high expression of PD-L1, and he was found to have no CNS involvement. He is currently receiving palliative care but is interested in participating in clinical trials. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, adequate organ function, and no history of autoimmune disease, interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis, or active infections. The patient has previously not participated in any pembrolizumab (MK-3475) trial or received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, and anti-PD-L2. He is willing to use an adequate method of contraception for the course of the study through 120 days after the last dose of study medication if needed.

The patient is a 25-year-old non-smoking female with a history of gum recession. She has noticed that her gums have receded significantly over the past year, and it has become a cosmetic concern for her. She has good oral hygiene habits and brushes twice a day and flosses once a day. Upon examination, the patient has bilateral Miller class I-II gingival recession defects on her upper incisors, canines, and premolars. The patient has an identifiable cemento-enamel junction (CEJ) and no restorations or superficial caries in the affected areas. She has no history of periodontal surgical treatment on the involved sites. The patient has sufficient palatal donor tissue, with a thickness of at least 2.5 mm, for the indicated subepithelial connective tissue graft. She is not currently pregnant or lactating, and has not taken antibiotic medication within the past 6 months. The patient's molars are not affected, and she has no mobile or fully restored teeth.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of chronic kidney disease is scheduled for an arteriovenous fistula revision under regional anesthesia. The patient has a medical history of hypertension and is on antihypertensive medication. He is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is currently not experiencing any pain or discomfort in the area where the surgery will take place. The patient has consented to participate in the study and has no known allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia.

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with advanced liver cancer two months ago. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but unfortunately, his cancer has continued to progress. His oncologist has informed him that no other standard therapeutic options are available, and he has been given a life expectancy of less than 12 weeks. He is now interested in participating in a clinical trial for FP-1305. He has provided a recent tumour sample for biomarker analysis, and it has been confirmed that he is eligible for the trial. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his bone marrow, liver, and kidney function are all within the required limits. He has no history of brain metastases, severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, or active infections. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to practise highly effective contraception during the trial and for three months after the completion of treatment. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in this study and is willing to sign a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a 30 pack-year history of cigarette smoking. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been hospitalized several times in the past for acute exacerbations. The patient has been compliant with his medication regimen, which includes salmeterol/fluticasone inhaler, tiotropium, and albuterol as needed. He reports increasing shortness of breath and cough with production of yellow sputum for the past 4 days. He presents to the emergency department and is diagnosed with an acute exacerbation of COPD. The patient is admitted to the hospital and started on systemic steroids for the exacerbation. He has no history of diabetes or peptic ulcer disease. The patient's medical history also includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease for which he is taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He is a retired construction worker and reports no environmental exposures to irritants or pollutants. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the optimal dosage of systemic steroids for the treatment of acute exacerbations of COPD.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male presents with a diagnosis of resectable colonic cancer. He has no significant past medical history, no allergies, and takes no medications regularly. He has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for 20 years but quit 5 years ago. He consumes 1-2 alcoholic beverages per week. His BMI is 27. He reports experiencing mild abdominal discomfort for the past month, but no significant changes in bowel habits. Physical examination is unremarkable. CT scan reveals a 4 cm mass in the ascending colon. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial and consents to participate.

A 54-year-old male with recently diagnosed esophageal adenocarcinoma, planning to receive neoadjuvant treatment including radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. The patient has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use but quit smoking upon diagnosis. He has no known blood disorders and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is interested in participating in research studies to further understand his cancer and potential treatment options. He has no history of being deprived of freedom or protected by law.

A 45-year-old female presents to the hospital with mild respiratory symptoms and has been recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She has a past medical history of hypertension but is currently not taking any medications. Her laboratory workup shows normal liver function tests and a creatinine clearance of 70 ml/min. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known immunocompromised condition and is not taking any medication that can affect her immune system. She does not have any comorbid medical conditions, such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, asthma, COPD, or malignancy. She does not have any allergies to Hydroxychloroquine and/or Nitazoxanide. She has no contraindications towards the study medication including retinopathy, G6PD deficiency, and QT prolongation.

63-year-old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department complaining of shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He has a history of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and was diagnosed with NYHA Class IV heart failure. He has been hospitalized three times in the past year due to HFpEF exacerbation. He is currently on optimal medical therapy for his heart failure, including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. He has no history of prior heart surgery or heart attacks. His physical exam revealed bilateral crackles in his lungs and significant lower extremity edema. His echocardiogram showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%, consistent with his diagnosis of HFpEF. He has no evidence of intra-cardiac thrombus. His minimal endocardial height from Apex to Mitral Annulus is >60mm at end systole. His pulmonary wedge pressure is >15 mmHg documented by right heart catheterization. He is willing and able to adhere to the required follow-up visits and testing, and has a good understanding of the study requirements and treatment procedures. He is not currently participating in another treatment investigational study and has no psychosocial condition that would preclude successful participation.

A 27-year-old woman is in her third trimester of pregnancy with a singleton pregnancy. She plans to breastfeed her baby and has no history of breastfeeding difficulties with her previous child. She has no underlying health conditions and takes prenatal vitamins daily. She has never had a C-section and is hoping for a vaginal delivery. She has no history of neonatal morbidity and has never required admission to a neonatal intensive care unit.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He is ineligible for high-dose therapy with stem-cell transplant due to his overall health and age. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 2 due to myeloma. He has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy for multiple myeloma. He has adequate hepatic and renal function, as well as hematopoietic function. His platelet count is 110,000/mm3 and his absolute neutrophil count is 1200/mm3. He has no history of pathologic fractures, infection, or symptomatic hyperviscosity. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no active gastrointestinal dysfunction that could interfere with absorption of study treatment. He is willing to take prophylactic anticoagulation as recommended by the study. He is able to provide written informed consent in accordance with national, local, and institutional guidelines. He has not received selinexor or another XPO1 inhibitor previously. He has no known intolerance, hypersensitivity, or contraindication to glucocorticoids, bortezomib, lenalidomide, and selinexor. He has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He is not actively experiencing symptomatic ischemia or congestive heart failure of New York Heart Association Class ≥3. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a benign nodule on her thyroid. She has experienced hoarseness and difficulty swallowing. She has no history of thyroid or parathyroid surgery. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medication regularly. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no contraindications to anesthesia and surgery. She is able to receive and understand information related to the study. She is affiliated with the French social security system.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has never smoked or used nicotine-containing products and is willing to comply with the study restrictions, including contraception requirements. She has no history of clinically significant disease or abnormalities, including allergies or infections. She has no history of cardiac arrhythmia or conduction abnormalities, and her ECG is within normal limits. She has not received any investigational drugs or CYP2D inhibitors within the past 5 half-lives of such drugs. She has no history of suicidal thinking or behavior or other significant psychiatric disorders. She has no history of acute narrow-angle glaucoma or any other condition that would make her unsuitable for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research.

The patient is a 26-year-old male who sprained his ankle during a basketball game seven days ago. He reports experiencing pain and swelling in the ankle, and difficulty bearing weight on the affected foot. The patient has no history of ankle injuries or surgeries, and is generally healthy with no known allergies or sensitivities. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements, including regular intake of the nutritional supplements. He is not currently taking any medications that may interact with the experimental or placebo supplements. The clinician has confirmed the diagnosis of an acute ankle sprain through clinical examination.

A 35-year-old female presented with a history of chronic abdominal pain, bloating, and alternating bowel habits. She was previously diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) by her primary care physician based on her Rome IV criteria. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 years and has tried various diets and medications without much relief. She works as a software engineer and her work requires her to sit for prolonged hours. She denies any history of recent infections, travel, or any significant changes in her lifestyle. She has no significant medical history other than mild asthma and seasonal allergies. She denies any family history of gastrointestinal disorders. A physical examination was unremarkable. A comprehensive stool analysis and colonoscopy were performed and both were normal. She was then referred to the Clinical Nutrition Clinic of "Petrucciani" Nursing Home of Lecce (LE), Italy, for further evaluation. She will be enrolled in a clinical trial to identify if her IBS symptoms are due to non-celiac gluten sensitivity (NCGS) or fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAPs) intolerance. She will follow a balanced normal-caloric low-FODMAP and gluten-free diet for a period of 4 weeks. If she experiences a significant improvement in her symptoms, she will be enrolled in the phase 2 of the study, which includes a challenge with gluten or with placebo based on the Salerno criteria.

A 52-year-old Caucasian male with a history of smoking is diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He reports a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis. He has no other significant medical history, and his family history is unremarkable. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and is in good general health. He has an ECOG performance status of 0. He is willing to undergo radical image-guided radiotherapy with curative intent. He has given informed consent to participate in the Hamlet.rt study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of lung cancer that has spread to his pleura. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past but has not experienced significant improvement in his cancer. His recent scans showed that the tumor has continued to grow and his oncologist has recommended participating in a clinical trial. The patient has undergone a physical examination, blood tests, electrocardiogram, and pulmonary function tests to determine his eligibility for the trial. The results showed that he is in good overall health with an ECOG performance status of 1. His platelet count is greater than 100,000, and his ANC is equal to 1500 without transfusion or cytokine support. He has adequate hepatic function, and his serum creatinine is less than or equal to 1.6 mg/ml. He is willing to sign an informed consent and understands the experimental nature of the therapy. The patient will be admitted to the hospital for treatment for approximately 10 days during each 28-day treatment cycle. During this time, he will receive a 4-hour infusion of Depsipeptide followed by a 72-hour infusion of Flavopiridol. Blood tests will be done before and after each Depsipeptide infusion and 3 more times for the next 24 hours, and at various times over 4 days during the Flavopiridol infusion to evaluate the effects of the medicines. Heart function will be monitored with several EKGs before and during the Depsipeptide doses. Tumor biopsies will be done before treatment begins and on the fifth day of the first treatment cycle. Additional treatment cycles may be offered to patients whose tumors have shrunk or remained stable with therapy. Patients whose tumors have not responded to therapy or who have developed severe drug side effects are taken off the study. The study is expected to last for 2-4 years, and 48 patients will be enrolled.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with lower-risk MDS, diagnosed according to WHO/FAB classification that meets IPSS-R classification of very low, low, or intermediate risk disease. The patient was previously treated with an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (ESA) without success, due to non-response or response that is no longer maintained. The patient has an endogenous serum erythropoietin level > 200 U/L. The patient requires red blood cell transfusions, with an average transfusion requirement of ≥ 2 units/8 weeks of pRBCs confirmed for a minimum of 16 weeks immediately preceding randomization. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1, indicating some limitations in physical activity, but able to carry out light work. The patient is a female of childbearing potential (FCBP), who has undergone a hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy, making her unable to become pregnant. The patient has not been naturally postmenopausal for at least 24 consecutive months. The patient is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. The patient has not been previously treated with Lenalidomide, Luspatercept (ACE-536) or sotatercept (ACE011). The patient has MDS not associated with del 5q cytogenetic abnormality, and has no known clinically significant anemia due to iron, vitamin B12, or folate deficiencies, or autoimmune or hereditary hemolytic anemia, or gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient has no prior allogeneic stem cell transplant, known history of diagnosis of AML, or use of any anticancer cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agent or treatment, other RBC hematopoietic growth factors, or investigational drug or device within 4 weeks prior to randomization. The patient has controlled hypertension and has not had a major surgery within 4 weeks prior to randomization. The patient has had no history of stroke, deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary or arterial embolism within 6 months prior to randomization. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no significant medical condition, laboratory abnormality, or psychiatric illness that would prevent her from participating in the study.

This is a 63 year-old male who was diagnosed with myelofibrosis (MF) 2 years ago. He has been treated with hydroxyurea and anagrelide to control his high platelet and white blood cell counts. However, he has developed progressive fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats over the past few months. His latest bone marrow biopsy showed worsening MF with intermediate risk according to Lille scoring system. He is currently classified as ECOG performance status 1. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has signed informed consent. He has not had any chemotherapy within the past 2 weeks and has recovered from any toxic effects. His serum bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT and creatinine levels are all within acceptable limits. He has been advised to use effective methods of contraception as he is still sexually active.
