He is willing to travel to M. D. Anderson for the first cycle of azacitidine and is able to receive later cycles of treatment courses from a cancer doctor in his community.

The patient is a 55-year-old retired Army veteran who served in Afghanistan. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of interest in activities he once enjoyed. He is currently receiving care at a VA Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) associated with the Houston VAMC for other health issues, such as hypertension and diabetes. He has not received psychotherapy in the past year and has not been diagnosed with bipolar, psychotic, or substance abuse disorders. He is able to understand and follow instructions and is willing to participate in the study. He lives alone and has limited access to transportation due to his health conditions, which makes it difficult for him to attend regular therapy sessions. He is interested in receiving treatment for his depression and improving his quality of life.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma. She presented to her primary care physician with symptoms of headaches, nausea, and dizziness. Further evaluation with MRI revealed a single lesion located in the left hemisphere of her brain, with a diameter of 4 centimeters. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of glioblastoma. She has no prior history of cancer and has not received any previous treatment for glioblastoma. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is married and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and is passionate about gardening. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient recruitment as it is focused on investigating cognitive processes using functional MRI with healthy adult volunteers. The trial requires participants who are native English speakers, right-handed, and free of psychiatric, neurological, or other medical disorders that would constrain interpretation of their performance during functional neuroimaging studies. Additionally, participants must not have medical contraindications to MRI procedures, CNS active medications, or claustrophobia. Pregnant women are also excluded from participation due to the unknown effects of the high magnetic field on a developing fetus. The trial is not seeking patients with a specific medical condition or disorder.

A 42-year-old man with a history of injection drug use presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue and abdominal discomfort. He reports a previous history of hepatitis C infection, but has never received treatment for it. His laboratory results show a positive HCV RNA viral load of 15,000 IU/mL and a liver biopsy conducted two years ago showed no evidence of cirrhosis. The patient denies any history of hepatocellular carcinoma or HIV infection. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive treatment for his hepatitis C infection.

A 70-year-old woman presents with concerns about her balance and falls. She reports having fallen twice in the past year, resulting in minor injuries. She has no significant medical history but reports some mild joint pain in her knees and hips. She is active and enjoys walking, but is cautious due to her fear of falling. She is interested in participating in a study to improve her balance and reduce her risk of falls. She has not received physical therapy in the past month and has no recent history of orthopedic surgery. She rates her self-perceived balance as "poor". She has no significant vision problems and is able to understand instructions.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been struggling with keratosis pilaris on both of her upper arms. She has tried various over-the-counter treatments, but none have provided significant relief. Her skin type is Fitzpatrick Skin Type II. She has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the 810 nm diode laser can provide a more effective treatment for her keratosis pilaris. She has not received any laser therapy to her arms in the past year and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

4-week-old formula-fed male infant with a birth weight of 3.5 kg, born at term with an uneventful delivery. The infant is generally healthy and has been gaining weight appropriately since birth. The parents have been supplementing with formula since the first week of life, and the infant consumes about 2-3 formula feedings per day, each feeding 60-90 ml. The parents have noticed that the infant's stools are somewhat hard and infrequent, occurring every 2-3 days. The parents are concerned about the infant's stool pattern and are interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effects of high sn-2 palmitate infant formula on stool composition, stool characteristics, and gastrointestinal tolerance. The parents have provided written informed consent and are willing to comply with study procedures. The infant has no known allergies or medical issues.

28 F with a h/o GAgP presenting with generalized bleeding on probing and pocket probing depth greater than 5 mm. She has good general health, is not pregnant or lactating, and is not suffering from any other systemic diseases. She has not received antimicrobials in the previous 3 months, is not taking long-term anti-inflammatory drugs, and has not received a course of periodontal treatment within the last 6 months. She does not smoke. There are 20 teeth present and at least 2 teeth with pocket probing depth greater than 7 mm (including incisors and first molars, in addition to two other non-contiguous teeth between them). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of scaling and root planning or full-mouth ultrasonic debridement with amoxicillin and metronidazole for the treatment of GAgP.

57-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) with measurable disease. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and  adequate renal function with a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dl and a calculated creatinine clearance of 60ml/min. The patient also has adequate hepatic function with a serum bilirubin level of 1.5 mg/dl, and an alkaline phosphatase, ALT and AST of less than three times the upper limit of normal. The patient has evidence of adequate bone marrow function with an absolute neutrophil count of 1800 cells per deciliter and a platelet count of 110,000 per deciliter. The patient has no history of hypercalcemia, hemoptysis, haematemesis, coagulopathy or thrombosis, and is not requiring anticoagulation for any reason. The patient has not received any palliative radiation therapy within 2 weeks, has a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, and no history of unstable angina, congestive heart failure or stroke within the past 6 months. The patient has not undergone a major surgical procedure, open biopsy or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to the day of initiation of treatment, and has no minor surgical procedures such as fine needle aspirations or core biopsies within 7 days prior to the day of initiation of treatment. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and has a urine calculated creatinine clearance of 55ml/minute. The patient has no history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within 6 months prior to Day 0, and no serious, non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture. The patient is able to comply with study and follow-up procedures and has signed informed consent that will detail the investigational nature of the study in accordance with the institutional and federal guidelines. The patient has clinically significant pleural effusions or ascites that have been drained prior to enrollment on the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old Hispanic woman who is pregnant with her first child and has a pre-pregnancy BMI of 29. She is fluent in English and is currently 35 weeks and 3 days pregnant. She plans to deliver at a hospital that is part of the select hospital/birth facility systems included in the trial. She has no contraindications to breastfeeding as specified by the American Academy of Pediatrics and has never had breast reduction surgery or radiation. She is interested in breastfeeding after birth and has no indication for delivery before 37 weeks gestation. She has no history of gestational or pre-existing diabetes.

A 53-year-old woman has recently been diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of cancer. The patient underwent surgery to remove the tumor, followed by six cycles of chemotherapy. She is currently in remission and is being followed up regularly by her oncologist. She has given informed consent to have her blood collected for the plasma bank as part of the 'Pharmacogenetics and proteomics studies in patients receiving novel anticancer agents' study. The patient has not withdrawn her consent to have her blood samples used for research.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who was diagnosed with soft tissue sarcoma of the upper arm. She underwent core needle biopsy and confirmed to have stage II sarcoma. She has no evidence of metastatic disease and is medically operable. She has not received any prior radiotherapy to the primary site or adjacent site that results in overlapping radiation fields. She has undergone MRI and CT chest scan to assess distant disease. Her Karnofsky Performance Status is 80. She is currently not pregnant and is practicing adequate contraception. She has no history of metastatic disease from a primary other than sarcoma. The tumor size is 15 cm maximal dimension. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 68-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with low-flow, low-gradient (LF-LG) aortic stenosis (AS) with a preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%. Her indexed aortic valve area (AVA) is ≤ 0.6 cm²/m² and mean transvalvular gradient is < 40 mmHg. She has been experiencing shortness of breath on exertion, chest pain, and fatigue. She does not have any history of renal failure, tumor with metastasis, or pregnancy/lactation. She is interested in participating in the Multicenter Prospective Study of Low-Flow Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis (TOPAS Study) to help improve the diagnosis and clinical management of LF-LG AS.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) caused by severe pneumonia. Despite receiving maximal medical therapy, her condition continued to worsen, and she was placed on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiopulmonary support. She has no history of illicit drug use or arrhythmia, and she has never received a heart transplant. She is currently being monitored in the ICU, and her heart rate variability will be recorded and analyzed as part of this clinical trial to determine its association with outcomes in patients on ECMO.

Pt is a 12yo male with a diagnosis of NAFLD, presenting with elevated liver enzymes and a BMI z-score > 85th percentile. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or other secondary causes of fatty liver disease such as Wilson disease or viral hepatitis, and is not currently taking any weight loss medications. The patient has been struggling with weight management and has had difficulty adhering to lifestyle changes consisting of caloric restriction and exercise. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effects of a Mediterranean diet compared to a low-fat diet on changes in liver health and overall weight management.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing burning pain in her feet and hands for the past year. She also reports numbness and tingling sensations in those areas. The pain is more severe at night and affects her ability to sleep. She has no history of diabetes or thyroid problems. Her medical history is significant for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has never used recreational drugs or consumed alcohol in excess. She underwent a skin biopsy that showed a decrease in the density of cutaneous nerve fibers, suggesting small fiber neuropathy. She is currently being managed at Brest University Hospital and is eligible for the study.

A 38 year old woman has recently tested positive for COVID-19 after experiencing mild symptoms of fatigue, body ache, and dry cough. Her husband and two children have also tested positive for COVID-19. The family is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the immune response to COVID-19 in a household study design. The woman is generally healthy, has no known allergies, and is not pregnant. She understands the study procedures and is willing to provide blood samples and oropharyngeal swabs every 10 days for a period of 12 weeks, and then every 4-8 weeks for a year. She is interested in knowing if she and her family develop anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies and whether they are immune to the virus. She hopes that this study will help in identifying the asymptomatic carriers and help in controlling the spread of COVID-19.

Pt is a 35yo M with a BMI of 28. He exercises only 2 hours per week and is interested in participating in a study that will evaluate his body composition, training, performance, and recovery. He has no history of metabolic disorders, heart disease, arrhythmias, thyroid disease, renal, hepatic, autoimmune or neurological diseases. He is willing to maintain his current diet and exercise routine during the study and agrees to refrain from taking any anti-inflammatory supplement or medications to prevent any further nutritional or drug related protection against exercise induced muscle damage. He is willing to wear an accelerometer to track his activity during the entire study. He has a resting blood pressure of systolic pressure between 135-85 mmHg and a diastolic pressure between 85-50 mmHg. He is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials or weight loss programs involving diet, exercise, physical activity or the potential ingestion of an active drug or dietary supplement. He has not consistently consumed whey protein/plant protein and/or 1,000 mg of fish oil within the previous 4 weeks prior to enrollment. He is a non-smoker and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He has no musculoskeletal condition prohibiting him from participation.

A 12-year-old girl with acyanotic congenital heart disease presents for cardiac bypass surgery due to progressive symptoms of dyspnea and fatigue. She has no other significant medical history, and her vital signs are within normal limits. Echocardiography reveals moderate left ventricular hypertrophy and mild aortic stenosis. Blood work shows normal levels of hemoglobin, electrolytes, and kidney function. The patient's parents have provided consent for her to participate in the study, and pre and post bypass blood samples will be taken to investigate how soluble MER levels change after myocardial ischemia and reperfusion injury induced by cardiac bypass.

A 45-year-old Hispanic woman came to the clinic for a routine check-up. She has a family history of diabetes and high blood pressure. Her latest lab test results showed an HbA1c level of 6.1%, which is in the prediabetic range. She has been struggling with her weight for the past few years and has difficulty managing her diet due to her busy lifestyle. She speaks Spanish and is willing to participate in a peer health coaching program to prevent diabetes. She is not currently taking any medication for diabetes and is under the care of a patient-centered medical home model team. She is eager to learn more about how she can make lifestyle changes to reduce her risk of developing diabetes.

A 32-year-old female patient with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 came to the Clinic seeking IVF treatment. She has been married for two years and had been trying to conceive naturally for the past year but was unsuccessful. Her medical history was unremarkable except for a history of laparoscopy for endometriosis. The patient had regular menstrual cycles every 28 days, with a menstruation duration of 5-6 days. Her FSH levels were less than 10 IU/l. An ultrasound scan revealed the presence of both ovaries. The patient was excluded from the study due to the presence of endometriomas. However, the patient was interested in participating in a different study and was provided with information about ongoing clinical trials.

47-year-old male with a diagnosis of unresectable cutaneous melanoma with metastases to the lymph nodes and lungs. The patient has previously undergone treatment with ipilimumab and has had a three-week washout period. The patient has measurable disease after the resection of target lesions for TIL growth. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has adequate renal, hepatic, and hematologic function. The patient has tested positive for Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) antibody titer on a screening test. The patient has no untreated central nervous system (CNS) metastases greater than 1 cm in greatest dimension and no evidence of peri-tumoral edema present on brain imaging. The patient is not taking prednisone greater than 10mg or equivalent per day. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has no significant psychiatric disease that would prevent adequate informed consent or render immunotherapy unsafe. The patient has not received prior immunotherapy whose side effects have resulted in a requirement of immunosuppressive medications or has other autoimmune conditions that require immunosuppressive medications at the time of screening. The patient tests negative for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis B core antibody, Hepatitis C antibody, Human T-lymphotropic Virus (HTLV) I or II antibody, and is both Rapid plasma reagin (RPR) and Fluorescent treponemal antibody (FTA) negative. The patient has no invasive malignancy other than melanoma at the time of enrollment and within 2 years of screening. The patient is willing to use two FDA-accepted forms of contraception during sexual intercourse with female partners of childbearing potential from the start of PD-1 antibody therapy and up to at least 31 weeks from the last dose of nivolumab. The patient has no history of coronary artery disease or significant pulmonary disease.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial as it is not a study that involves patients directly. Instead, it is a study that evaluates the impact of a Bedside Paediatric Early Warning System (Bedside-PEWS) on early identification of children at risk for near and actual cardiopulmonary arrest, hospital mortality, processes of care, and PICU resource utilization in 22 paediatric hospitals. The study aims to improve the quality of care of all eligible patients admitted to the participating hospitals.

Patient is a 58-year-old male from the United States who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past two years. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis in his lower back and has tried various over-the-counter pain relievers, but have provided only temporary relief. He has no known allergies to lidocaine, menthol or methylparaben. He has reliable access to the internet and is willing to comply with the study protocol. His baseline pain intensity is 7 out of 10 on the pain scale. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to find a better pain relief option.

A 56-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath. Her blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, and her total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol levels are elevated at 220 mg/dL and 140 mg/dL, respectively. She is currently taking a statin and an anti-hypertensive medication. Coronary angiography reveals a significant de novo lesion in her right coronary artery, and she is being considered for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The reference vessel diameter of the lesion is 3.2 mm, and the stent size will be 3.0 mm with a stent length of 18 mm. She has not undergone any previous PCI or coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The patient has no contraindications to anti-platelet agents and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl living in a rural community in Eastern Uganda. She has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past several months, and her grades in school have been declining. Her parents have taken her to a traditional healer, but her symptoms have not improved. The family decides to visit a nearby health center to seek further medical attention. The health center is participating in a randomized controlled trial that aims to integrate child and adolescent mental health (CAMH) into primary health care (PHC) and traditional healers' services. The trial is being conducted to improve access to mental health services for children and adolescents in Uganda. The patient is eligible to participate in the trial as she is seeking medical attention from a public health system that does not have a psychiatric nurse allocated.

The patient is a 54-year-old male diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) confirmed by pathology or radiological images with typical features. A CT scan revealed at least one tumor nodule with a dimension of ≥ 2 cm. The patient has chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection with HBV DNA level >10^4. The patient's liver function is Child-Pugh Class A or B with total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x upper limit of normal, and ALT and AST ≤ 2.0 x the upper limit of normal. The patient has a peripheral white blood cell count of ≥ 3×10(9)/L and peripheral platelet of ≥ 50×10(9)/L. The patient has an expected survival time of not less than 3 months and an ECOG score of 0-2. The patient has not received prior systemic chemotherapy or chemoembolization. The patient does not have tumor thrombi in the main branch of the portal vein or tumor involvement more than 70% of the whole liver. The patient also does not have extrahepatic metastasis, congestive heart failure > NYHA class 2, history of HIV infection, or active clinically serious infections. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have substance abuse, medical, psychological or social conditions that may interfere with the patient's participation in this study. The patient is also not known or suspected to have an allergy to any agent given in association with this trial. The patient is able to swallow oral medication and is not inclined to thrombosis or hemorrhage, or active hemorrhage within the past month.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it aims to include all pediatric patients admitted to the ICU at Assiut University children hospital over one year aged from 1 month to 18 years, with the exception of those less than one month old or who die on arrival. The study aims to determine the profile and outcome of all eligible patients in order to improve the quality of care.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus that is controlled with oral medications. He is scheduled to undergo elbow surgery due to a recent injury. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status of II and has no regional anesthesia contraindications. He has no significant neurological disorders or history of substance abuse. The patient understands the block and follow-up instructions and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not currently using opioids for pain management. He has no known local anesthetic hypersensitivity or allergy.

Patient is a 54-year-old male from the United States who was recently diagnosed with hormone refractory, metastatic prostate carcinoma. He has completed all available standard therapies for this disease but has not responded to treatment. He has no significant medical history and has not undergone any previous cancer treatment. His overall health status is good with a BMI of 25 and no significant comorbidities. His laboratory findings are within normal limits except for prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels, which are elevated.

The patient is a 42 year old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent a mastectomy on her left breast followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. After the surgical procedure, she began to experience swelling in her left arm, which was diagnosed as lymphedema. She has been undergoing treatment for lymphedema for the past 6 months, but has not seen any significant improvement. She experiences discomfort and heaviness in her arm, which affects her daily activities. She is a stay-at-home mother with two children and has a supportive family. She is interested in alternative therapies and has tried acupuncture for other conditions in the past. She has a history of migraines and takes over-the-counter medication for relief. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and exercises regularly. She has a BMI of 25 with a blood pressure of 120/80. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for the swelling in her left arm. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the consent form.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes for the past 3 years. He is currently under stable glycemic control using oral antidiabetic medication. He has also been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 5 years and is on a stable regimen of medication including an ACE inhibitor to control his blood pressure. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or stroke. He is an office worker and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 27 and he has a BP of 140/90 mmHg. He reports experiencing occasional headaches but no other significant medical history. He has undergone a physical examination and has no clinically significant findings. He is willing to use double-barrier contraception if applicable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his endothelial function and BP control.

56 F with a h/o partial edentulism and missing four teeth in succession. She is currently wearing a removable partial denture. She has no significant medical history and is systemically healthy. She has good maxillomandibular relation and maximal mouth opening of 7 mm. She maintains good oral hygiene but has a mild parafunctional habit of bruxing at night. Her periodontal status is healthy with probing pocket depths of <3 mm and no bleeding on probing. She has no maxillary sinus involvement and no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no systemic diseases that would contraindicate oral surgical treatment and is not currently taking any medications like bisphosphonates or steroids. She is willing to return for follow-up examinations and is a non-smoker. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and getting dental implants placed using two different CBCT-derived templates.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with upper extremity deep-vein thrombosis. She has a history of breast cancer and underwent a mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection one year ago, after which she received adjuvant chemotherapy. She currently has a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) line in place for receiving her ongoing cancer treatment. She has been experiencing pain, swelling, and redness in her affected arm for the past few days and was diagnosed with upper extremity DVT by ultrasound imaging. She has no history of bleeding disorders or renal failure, and her weight is within normal range. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive Fragmin treatment for three months and to be monitored for long-term outcomes. She is able to return for repeat diagnostic testing and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who underwent a total hip replacement surgery on his right hip 10 months ago due to osteoarthritis. He has been experiencing difficulty with daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and getting in and out of a car. He has a BMI of 28 and is otherwise healthy. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve his mobility and learn more about his joint mechanics. He has not had any previous lower limb ailments or surgeries apart from the hip replacement. He is able to walk unassisted and does not have any medical conditions that could affect physical movement such as a stroke.

The patient is a 50 year old man who is experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. After undergoing diagnostic tests, it was determined that the patient requires a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the implantation of at least one drug-eluting stent. The patient is currently taking aspirin and is willing to participate in the Plavix, Prasugrel and Drug Eluting Stents Pilot Trial. He weighs 80 kg and his hematocrit and platelet count are within the validated ranges for the Verify Now P2Y12 test. The patient has no known platelet disorders or active pathological bleeding. He has never experienced a stroke or TIA and has no history of hepatic impairment or NYHA Class III or greater for heart failure. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to clopidogrel, prasugrel or ASA.

A 55-year-old male smoker was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with an activating EGFR mutation. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy for his cancer. Recently, he has developed brain metastases and has been experiencing symptoms such as headaches, nausea, and confusion. His performance status is ECOG 2. He has no other major health issues and is not on any other medication. He understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 34 year old woman who has been experiencing a high level of stress due to her demanding job as a project manager. She has been feeling exhausted, irritable, and has difficulty sleeping for the past 3 months. She has no history of substance abuse or mental illness, and has never received any psychological treatment before. She is fluent in Swedish, has regular access to a computer and internet, and is interested in participating in an online treatment program for her stress-related symptoms. Her current medication includes birth control pills and over-the-counter pain relievers for menstrual cramps. She has no history of suicidal ideation or attempts. She is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions.

A 40-year-old woman with a history of celiac disease presents with ongoing symptoms despite being on a gluten-free diet for the past 2 years. She reports frequent episodes of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and bloating, which have a significant impact on her quality of life. She has been compliant with her gluten-free diet and has not consumed any known sources of gluten. The patient has detectable serum celiac-related antibodies and HLA-DQ typing consistent with celiac disease (DQ2 and/or DQ8). She has experienced at least one of the following symptoms at least once per week during the month before screening: diarrhea, loose stools, abdominal pain, abdominal cramping, bloating, or gas. The patient weighs 65 kg and does not have any other chronic, active GI disease or severe complications of celiac disease. The patient is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period and is not currently breastfeeding.

42 yo M with chronic bilateral leg edema and varicose veins presenting to vascular clinic for evaluation and management. Patient reports difficulty with ambulation due to the heaviness and discomfort of his legs. No history of deep venous thrombosis or recent surgery. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Sleep Apnea - Chronic Kidney Disease - Obesity - History of smoking (quit 2 years ago) - No history of liver or heart disease, or immuno-deficiencies.

Patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman who is scheduled for an elective caesarean section in spinal anesthesia. She has no previous history of opioid or psychotropic medication use. She is in overall good health and has an American Society of Anaesthesiologists physical status of II. She has no local skin infections at the sites of acupuncture. She is able to give written informed consent and understands the study questionnaire.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed five years ago. He has been on metformin 2000mg/day for the past six months, but his blood sugar levels remain uncontrolled, with HbA1c levels of 8.5%. He has a BMI of 35 kg/m2 and fasting serum triglycerides of 200 g/dL. The patient has no significant medical history of cardiovascular disease, liver disease, or gastrointestinal disease. He is currently not on insulin therapy and has not experienced diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar nonketotic coma, or any other major diabetic complications. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of combining metformin with either muraglitazar or pioglitazone.

Male, 45 years old, diagnosed with chronic cluster headache according to ICHD-IIIb criteria. The patient experiences recurring episodes of unilateral, periorbital pain accompanied by autonomic symptoms such as tearing, nasal congestion, and ptosis. The patient has tried various treatment options including oxygen therapy and triptans, but with limited success. The patient has not been diagnosed with cardiac arrhythmia or other known autonomic dysfunction. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will be required to undergo pupillometry, actigraphy, and heart-rate variability monitoring for two weeks, once during a cluster bout and once during a remission phase. The patient will be required to mark the occurrence of headache attacks by pressing a button on the actigraph during the registration. The patient will also be asked to fill out the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index before and after registration to report subjective sleep quality. The patient will be excluded from the study if any cardiac arrhythmias or known autonomic dysfunction are detected.

45 y/o male who has tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and experiencing symptoms such as cough, fever and shortness of breath. He has access to a smartphone and is able to respond to questionnaires in Danish. Currently, he is not hospitalized and does not live in a nursing home. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Mild asthma.

A 27-year-old healthy man came to the clinic for a routine eye check-up. He has no history of ocular disease and his vision is 20/20 with glasses. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day in front of a computer screen. He has no history of dizziness or motion sickness from playing video or computer games. He has no family history of ocular disease. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly, at least 3 times a week for 30 minutes a day. He is interested in participating in clinical trials that can improve vision for people who are visually impaired.

A 58-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia was diagnosed with coronary artery disease after experiencing chest pain during exercise. He will undergo coronary artery bypass grafting surgery as part of his standard medical care. He has no history of heart failure, kidney failure, liver failure, infective disease, or cancer. He is not currently taking glucocorticoids or estrogens and is a non-smoker. He has no history of mental disorders. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week and maintains a healthy diet. He has never undergone any cardiac surgery before.

Pt is a 67yo M with a history of osteoarthritis presenting for a total knee replacement. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He reports no history of lung disease or smoking history. He is currently on amlodipine 10mg, atorvastatin 40mg, and low-dose aspirin. Preoperative pulmonary function tests were within normal limits. The patient will be monitored in the postoperative period for the development of atelectasis using the Air-Test. The study aims to determine the accuracy of the Air-Test in detecting atelectasis in elderly patients undergoing orthopedic surgery. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50 year old male who was recently diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma after experiencing chest pain, shortness of breath, and coughing for several weeks. He underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis and immunohistochemistry testing showed that his tumor expresses PDGFR-beta and C-kit. He received pemetrexed-based chemotherapy but experienced disease progression. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. His baseline hematological values are within normal limits and he has no co-existing tumors of different histologic origin. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and has no history of psychiatric disabilities that would interfere with his ability to give adequate informed consent. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to practice a medically approved method of contraception during the study period. He has no uncontrolled active infections and is otherwise in good health.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22. She has no history of any significant medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has signed the informed consent document and is willing to participate in the study. She will undergo a medical exam, including blood pressure and pulse rate measurement, a 12-lead Electrocardiogram (ECG), and clinical laboratory tests, to ensure she is healthy and meets the eligibility criteria. She will be required to fast overnight and will be given a high-fat, high-calorie meal to compare the effect of food on AG-013736 blood levels.

A 45-year old woman was diagnosed with type II diabetes 5 years ago. She is married and has two children. She works as a sales representative for a pharmaceutical company. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obesity. She complains of occasional blurred vision and difficulty seeing at night. She has never had any ocular surgeries or intravitreal injections. Her medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin and aspirin. She has no known allergies. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is an alert and cooperative woman who is able to comply with follow-up. She has been diagnosed with moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) based on her last eye exam. Her HbA1c is 9.3. She has no other ocular or systemic diseases.

56-year-old male with end-stage renal disease due to hypertension and diabetes. Currently receiving hemodialysis three times a week for the past year. Has been evaluated for kidney transplant and found to be a suitable candidate for living donor kidney transplant. No history of previous kidney transplant or multiple organ transplant. Negative for HIV, HBsAg, and HCV. No severe lung disorders or allergies that would prevent administration of rATG or Basiliximab. Leukocyte and platelet counts are within normal limits. No history of malignant disease within the last 5 years. Willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of severe headaches, blurred vision, and swelling in her hands and feet since last week. She is currently 35 weeks pregnant with her first child and has never experienced this kind of discomfort before. Her blood pressure is measured to be 160/100 mm Hg, which is significantly higher than her normal range. She also has high levels of protein in her urine, indicating a possible case of pre-eclampsia. The doctor recommends immediate hospitalization for further evaluation and treatment. Upon admission, the doctor collects a venous cord blood sample from the newborn to measure adiponectin levels as part of a cross-sectional, hospital-based study. The mother and newborn are informed about the study and give written consent to participate. The newborn is enrolled as a case due to the mother's pre-eclampsia diagnosis.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. She reports experiencing blurred vision at night and difficulty reading. She has had no previous ocular surgeries and has no history of ocular diseases. She currently takes no medications for ocular or systemic conditions. The patient is able to self-administer eye drops and is willing to record the times the drops were instilled. She is also willing to sign the written informed consent form and complete the entire course of the study. The patient has no known sensitivity to any of the ingredients in the study medications. She is postmenopausal and has no plans to become pregnant. The patient has not used a topical NSAID within 1 week of study entry and is not currently involved in another investigational study or has participated in one within the 30 days prior to entering this study. The patient is otherwise healthy and is expected to be compliant with the study protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has completed the 12-week treatment period and 16-week durability period in the G201002 clinical trial for stress urinary incontinence. She has been diagnosed with stress urinary incontinence for the last 4 years and has reported symptoms such as urine leakage during coughing, sneezing, laughing, or other physical activities that put pressure on her bladder. The patient is currently not taking any medication that affects lower urinary tract function. She has been compliant with the study protocol and has communicated all adverse events and other clinically important information to study personnel. The patient is able to read, understand, and provide written, dated informed consent to participate in the Durability Extension Study to further assess the long-term durability of response to GTx-024 on SUI symptoms. The patient has no history of any physical condition that might put her at risk or interfere with the interpretation of study results.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease who has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue. He has been diagnosed with severe ischemic mitral valve regurgitation, and his cardiologist has recommended surgery to repair or replace the valve. He has been taking medications for his heart condition, including beta-blockers and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. He does not have any other significant medical history, and he has not had any previous surgeries. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of stage IVB mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sezary syndrome (SS) that has not responded to at least one type of treatment recently came to the clinic. The patient has a performance status of 0 or 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance scale and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. The patient has measurable disease based on modified severity-weighted assessment tool (mSWAT). The leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, hemoglobin, serum total bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), serum creatinine, international normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin

Patient is a 35-year-old male who sustained an ankle fracture after a fall while playing basketball. The injury was diagnosed in the emergency department and the patient was referred to the orthopedic department for further evaluation. X-ray imaging confirmed the fracture and the patient was admitted to the hospital for immobilization with a plaster cast. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient has no known kidney disorder, heart failure, malignancy or bleeding disorder. The patient is not pregnant and has no planned follow-up at another hospital.

A 10-year-old boy with autism was referred to the clinic by his pediatrician. He has difficulty with social interactions and language development. He often repeats phrases and has difficulty understanding sarcasm or figurative language. His parents also reported that he has compulsive behaviors like lining up toys and arranging them in a specific order. He has never been treated with fluoxetine or any other serotonin reuptake inhibitors. He has not had any electroconvulsive therapy or taken any investigational drugs for at least a month. He is not currently taking any psychotropic drugs and has not taken any long-acting phenothiazines for at least six weeks. He has no history of seizures or cerebrovascular disease, and he is not currently pregnant or nursing. He has no significant medical illness or systemic disease. His IQ is above 50, and he does not have a family history of bipolar disorder or any other mental disorders. He does not have any significant autoaggressive behaviors or suicidal risk. He has no history of hypersensitivity to fluoxetine or other serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

11-year-old male with a BMI of 32.5 kg/m², sedentary lifestyle and irregular physical activity. No evidence of metabolic, hormonal, orthopedic, and cardiovascular disease at the time of the study's commencement. The patient has not participated in any regular exercise training program (except physical education classes, two days a week) at least 6 months before the commencement of the study and throughout the protocol. The patient's pubertal stage is 4, according to the Tanner system of pubertal staging. The patient is not under any pharmacological treatment.

54-year-old male with a history of esophageal cancer status post-esophagectomy and radiation therapy. The patient has been experiencing difficulty in maintaining weight due to poor oral intake and is at risk of malnutrition as determined by clinical evaluation. The patient consumes approximately 1,800 kcal/day and requires an additional 300 kcal/day from an oral nutritional supplement. The patient is able to communicate clearly and has provided informed consent for participation in the study. The patient does not have cow's milk protein allergy, inherited metabolic conditions, significant renal or hepatic impairment, dysphagia requiring thickened fluids, or uncontrolled inflammatory bowel disease. The patient is not currently participating in any other studies involving investigational or marketed products. The investigator has no concerns regarding the patient's ability or willingness to comply with protocol requirements. The patient will be evaluated for tolerance and acceptability of 'MONACO' for at least 2 further weeks.

39-year-old female with a history of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) diagnosed 10 years ago during her first pregnancy. She has had several episodes of bruising, bleeding gums, and petechiae over the years. Her platelet counts have been fluctuating between 30-40 x 10exp9/L, despite treatment with prednisone, IVIG, and rituximab. She is currently on a stable dose of prednisone and has not had any major bleeding episodes. However, she recently developed a dental abscess and requires tooth extraction. Her platelet count is 30 x 10exp9/L and needs to be increased before the procedure to prevent excessive bleeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of eltrombopag as a bridging therapy before surgery. She is aware of the potential side effects and risks associated with the medication and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or on any other medication that could interfere with the study outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in first relapse. He has not undergone prior myeloablative therapy or transplant. The patient is in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no history of invasive aspergillosis or active hepatitis. He is HIV-negative and has no active infections. The patient has a haploidentical female donor who is his mother. The donor is genotypically-matched and haploidentical for HLA-A, B, C, DRB1, and DQ loci. The donor differs for 2 or 3 HLA alleles on the unshared haplotype in the GvHD direction. The patient agrees to undergo haploid allogeneic transplant using the CliniMACS system and has provided written informed consent.

A 63-year-old Caucasian male presented with a history of difficulty urinating, occasional blood in his urine and lower back pain. He denied any weight loss, anorexia, or bone pain. He had a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). He was taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for his hypertension and dyslipidemia. On physical examination, his prostate gland was enlarged and hard with a nodule palpable at the right lobe. His digital rectal examination (DRE) showed no fecal impaction, masses, or rectal wall thickening. His initial serum Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) level was 12.5 ng/mL, and his biopsy revealed a T2a prostate adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 7 (3+4). The patient was referred to the urology department, where he was presented with the three primary treatments for localized prostate cancer, radical retropubic prostatectomy, external-beam radiotherapy, and interstitial brachytherapy, and their possible side effects. After a shared decision-making process with his physician, the patient chose to undergo radical retropubic prostatectomy. He met the inclusion criteria and was enrolled in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old Lebanese woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) by her gynecologist. She is a non-smoker and does not consume caffeine. Her BMI is 27.2, and she has no significant medical history, except for a history of depression, which is under control with medication. She is willing to participate in the study and attend all clinical follow-ups for the next three years. She is medically suitable to undergo ovarian stimulation and has normal serum chemistry and hematology screening tests. She has tested negative for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C serology. She has no history of malignancy and has undergone a complete history and physical examination.

A 56-year-old Hispanic woman who lives in a low-income area of New York City. She is a single mother with two teenage children and works as a part-time cashier. She has a history of irregular Pap tests and has never had a mammogram or colorectal cancer screening. She has been receiving care at a community health center for the past year, but she has not been able to keep up with her cancer screenings due to her busy work schedule and lack of transportation. She is concerned about her health and wants to participate in a study that could help her stay on top of her cancer screenings. She is able to speak and understand English and is willing to receive follow-up services by telephone with a Prevention Care Manager (PCM). She does not have any acute illness or distress and is eligible for the study as she meets all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old male with no significant medical history. He weighs 70 kilograms and has a body mass index of 24 kg/meter squared. He has received the pneumococcus (Pneumovax 23) vaccine within the last 4 years and the seasonal influenza vaccine for the current season. He is willing to follow the contraception guidance specified in the protocol during the study and for 3 months after the last dose of the study drug. He has not been exposed to investigational or marketed therapeutic proteins, such as monoclonal antibodies, fusion proteins, bispecific molecules, or antibody drug conjugates, within the last 60 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to dosing. He has not been previously exposed to ALXN1830. He has no history of hepatitis B or C or human immunodeficiency virus infection and does not have anatomic or functional asplenia or primary antibody deficiencies.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of premenstrual syndrome (PMS) for the past year. She reports moderate to severe symptoms during the luteal phase of her menstrual cycle, including mood swings, bloating, breast tenderness, and fatigue. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not taking any medications. The patient does not smoke and has no history of chronic diseases or psychiatric or gynecological problems. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of whole-body vibration versus aerobic exercise on inflammatory status in females with PMS. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and is open to receiving supplementation as part of the study.

The patient is a 78-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with bladder cancer. She has a history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, and diabetes mellitus. She has difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to her frailty. She has been assessed using the Fried Frailty Score and scored 2. She is scheduled to undergo cystectomy with urinary diversion as her treatment. She has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate. The patient has no known allergies to the class of drugs under study and has no history of non-compliance, drug or alcohol abuse. She is able to follow the procedures of the study and has no language problems or psychological disorders. She has been evaluated for dementia and is found to have no significant cognitive impairment. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Due to her age and medical history, she is at high risk for postoperative morbidity and mortality. She is a suitable candidate for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria for the trial.

This is a 47 year-old postmenopausal Japanese woman with a history of ER+ HER2- breast cancer that has progressed despite previous lines of chemotherapy and endocrine therapy. She has not received any prior treatment with CDK4/6 inhibitors. She has a performance status of 1 and one measurable lesion that can be assessed by CT. She has no unresolved toxicities from prior therapy that are greater than CTCAE Grade 1. She has no evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases or life-threatening metastatic visceral disease. She has no history of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of AZD9833. She has adequate bone marrow reserve and organ function. She is willing to participate in an open-label study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and anti-tumor activity of AZD9833.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of asthma for the past 2 years. She has a history of allergies, including seasonal allergies to pollen and dust mites, and sometimes experiences shortness of breath and wheezing during allergy season. She currently takes a combination of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists as prescribed by her physician. Her morning pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is 80% of predicted normal. She is of Caucasian origin and has no history of severe asthma exacerbations requiring hospitalization in the past year. She has never taken an investigational CXCR2 antagonist or any tool-substances used for the purpose of this study. Her sputum samples show an increased number of neutrophils, with a relative neutrophil count of 60% of total sputum cell count. She is willing to participate in the study and sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer three months ago. He underwent surgery to remove the primary tumor and started chemotherapy with fluorouracil and irinotecan. However, he experienced disease progression after two cycles of chemotherapy. He is now looking for other treatment options and is considering enrolling in a clinical trial. He reports no significant medical history and no allergies. His current medications include acetaminophen and oxycodone for pain control. He is a smoker with a 30-pack-year history and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a construction worker and has a physically demanding job. His performance status is Karnofsky 80%, and his hemoglobin level is 11.5 g/dL. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and his creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL. He has no history of heart disease or bowel obstruction. He has never had radiotherapy or biologic therapy for his cancer. He is interested in learning more about the trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who recently underwent scheduled cardiac surgery by sternotomy with cardiopulmonary bypass. After extubation, he was diagnosed with a pulmonary atelectasis based on the chest X-ray. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. The patient's vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 125/70 mmHg, respiratory rate of 18/min, and heart rate of 80/min. He has no cardiac arrhythmia or hemodynamic instability. The patient is alert and oriented with no complaints of pain. His lung sounds are diminished on the right side. The patient consents to participate in the trial and is willing to receive the proposed treatment.

A 62-year-old man presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medications for both. The patient underwent a cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe calcification of his coronary arteries. The treating physician recommends percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the use of rotational atherectomy (RA) to debulk the calcified lesions. The patient is provided with information about the ROVUS Asia Registry and agrees to participate in the study. He signs the informed consent form and provides the necessary information about his medical history and current medications. The patient's target lesions have at least moderate calcification and meet the angiographic criteria for the study. The patient is willing to comply with all research and follow-up requirements, making him eligible to participate in the study.

This is a 45-year-old man with a history of chronic hepatitis C (HCV) and HIV co-infection. He has a history of substance abuse and is currently experiencing neurocognitive impairment (NCI) with a GDS greater than or equal to 0.35. He is planning to receive HCV treatment from his primary care physician within the next month. He has not received treatment with pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) in the past and does not have cirrhosis or bridging fibrosis. He does not have any other active inflammatory processes or psychiatric disorders that would preclude adherence to study requirements. He is willing to participate in a study that observes the effects of newly developed direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatments on the central nervous system (CNS) of individuals with chronic HCV, specifically focusing on how HIV alters the relationship between HCV cure and CNS outcomes.

52 yo F with a long-standing history of osteoarthritis of the right knee with varus deformity, presenting with complaints of severe pain, stiffness, and difficulty walking. Patient failed conservative management and elected to proceed with a unilateral total knee replacement. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Obesity (BMI 34) - Depression - GERD - Hypothyroidism - Sleep apnea - Chronic low back pain. Current Medications: - Lisinopril 20mg daily - Atorvastatin 40mg daily - Metformin 1000mg twice daily - Sertraline 50mg daily - Pantoprazole 40mg daily - Levothyroxine 88mcg daily. Physical Exam: - Severe varus deformity of the right knee, limited range of motion, diffuse tenderness, and crepitus on palpation. - No significant leg length discrepancy noted on visual inspection. - No evidence of valgus deformity, extra-articular lower limb deformities or previous knee surgery.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who is scheduled for a dental appointment. He has a history of anxiety during medical procedures and often experiences fear and discomfort during these appointments. He is enrolled in the participating institution for the study and has obtained the necessary authorization from his parents to participate. The child is generally healthy and does not have any psychomotor disorders that would prevent him from using the fear faces scale. The child is covered by social security and is able to understand and follow instructions. The aim of including the child in the study is to validate the self-assessment fear scale and to determine its effectiveness in helping children like him to better describe their fear levels during consultations or medical procedures.

A 22-year-old female college student has been dealing with asthma since childhood. She is currently on a daily inhaled corticosteroid and a short-acting bronchodilator for rescue. She reports experiencing symptoms of chest tightness and shortness of breath at least twice a week, interfering with her daily activities and sleep. She has no history of smoking or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She has not participated in any other clinical trials involving drugs or medical devices in the past 30 days. She is willing to participate in this observational pilot study to evaluate the impact of FeNO assessments on asthma treatment decisions. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. She is available for follow-up visits and willing to comply with study requirements.

A 60-year-old male suffered a left hemisphere ischemic stroke two months ago, which resulted in expressive aphasia. He is right-handed and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no other neurological or psychiatric conditions. He is currently undergoing speech-language therapy but has had limited improvement. His initial language testing showed impaired verbal fluency, repetition, and naming, consistent with moderate-severe Broca's aphasia. He is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve his language difficulties. He has no history of metal implants or claustrophobia, and he is not pregnant. MRI evaluation is acceptable to him. He is willing to undergo either real or sham tDCS, and he understands the study design is double-blind and randomized.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy of African American ethnicity. He has a BMI of 38 and has been diagnosed with severe obesity. The patient's parents have noticed that he has become increasingly sedentary in recent months and are concerned about his overall health. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. He is able to understand instructions and complete all study procedures. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any significant physical or mental disabilities that would impede his ability to participate in the study. The patient is interested in participating in the study to better understand how his obesity may be affecting his physical activity and overall health.

A 55-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in the right knee presents with severe knee pain and difficulty walking. The patient has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief, but the medication is no longer effective. He is scheduled to undergo primary total knee arthroplasty and is interested in participating in the study. The patient's BMI is 35 kg/m2, and he has no known allergies to trial medications. He has not used opioids chronically, and his renal function is normal. The patient is eligible to receive spinal anesthesia and is not scheduled for surgery over the weekend. He is willing to receive two injections, one periarticular injection and a single shot adductor canal block, but understands that he may receive a placebo in one of the injections. The patient is eager to participate in the study to potentially improve his recovery and reduce his need for post-operative pain medication.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with PCOS according to the Rotterdam criteria. She complains of irregular periods, difficulty in achieving pregnancy, and weight gain. She has never received any induction of ovulation in the preceding 3 months before enrollment. She has no history of any contraindications to metformin and has not undergone any surgical management of PCOS. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the vaginal administration of metformin for the treatment of PCOS. She is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all scheduled visits. She understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with moderate-to-severe chronic periodontitis. She has a history of poor oral hygiene with a plaque index (PI) of 2.0. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies or history of systemic diseases. She has not taken any antibiotics within the past 6 months and does not require prophylaxis of antibiotics. Upon examination, the patient has pocket depths of 6-7mm and horizontal bone loss in two quadrants of her jaw. Her teeth do not have gingival recession, endodontic lesions, or furcation involvement. She has been selected as a participant in a randomized, double-blinded, controlled clinical trial at the Ataturk University Department of Periodontology in Erzurum, Turkey. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of T-PRF treatment combined with open flap debridement on biological markers in GCF and periodontal outcomes in chronic periodontitis patients. The patient has provided written informed consent for her inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis for the past 8 years. She has been experiencing pain, stiffness, and limited mobility in her knee joint, which has made it difficult for her to perform her daily activities. She has tried various treatments such as physical therapy, pain medications, and steroid injections, but none of them have provided long-term relief. She has been referred to a rheumatologist who has recommended a knee lavage procedure to help alleviate her symptoms. The patient is apprehensive about the procedure due to her fear of pain and anxiety. She has no prior history of knee lavage, and her medical history is significant for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of psychiatric diseases or current use of psychotropic drugs. Her lab results are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the hypnosis intervention clinical trial to help manage her pain perception during the lavage procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia at Mayo Clinic Rochester's Fibromyalgia Clinic. She has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain, chronic fatigue, depression, sleep disturbances, and poor concentration for over a year. She has not been taking any medications for these symptoms. She has had a hysterectomy and is willing to travel to Mayo Clinic Rochester for the initial instruction visit. She is able to apply the transdermal magnesium chloride as directed and complete the questionnaires and daily diary. She speaks, writes, and understands English fluently. She is not on dialysis or magnesium supplements. She is willing to give informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection. He has been HBsAg and HBeAg positive for over 6 months. The patient has a history of alcohol abuse and has been sober for the last 6 months. He is currently not experiencing any symptoms of decompensated liver function such as ascites, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy, or spontaneous peritonitis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with the study requirements.

A 32-year-old male OEF/OIF veteran came to the clinic seeking help to quit smoking. He has been smoking for 10 years, and currently smokes approximately 10 cigarettes per day. He has tried to quit smoking in the past using nicotine gum, but was not successful. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or severe memory loss. He has a phone with reliable access to the internet. He is willing to make a quit attempt in the next 30 days and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is currently receiving ongoing care at the DVAMC.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with thyroid carcinoma and underwent a thyroidectomy. She has a history of dry eye syndrome and uses artificial tears frequently. She does not wear contact lenses and is not taking any medications that affect tear production. She has not had any ocular trauma or previous radiation therapy for other diseases. She does not have any other autoimmune diseases or conditions that may alter tear production. She has no history of pterygium, Graves' disease, blepharitis or other conditions that may reduce tear production or lead to rapid evaporation. She has been offered radioactive iodine therapy for the ablation of remaining thyroid tissue and metastases and is considering participating in a clinical trial evaluating lacrimal drainage system obstruction associated with this treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old Danish resident who has been diagnosed with myasthenia gravis (ICD-10 code 70.0) and is subscribed to E-boks, the Danish system for receiving secure digital emails. The patient has no other major comorbidities and is interested in participating in the study. They are able to understand and read Danish and have access to a computer with internet connection. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent and answer the six validated and translated questionnaires online through REDcap, as well as wear an accelerometer for 7 days to measure their activity level.

45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes for 5 years, actively using Twitter with over 1,000 followers. She is currently managing her diabetes through diet and exercise, but has experienced difficulty maintaining her blood glucose levels within target range. She has expressed interest in finding additional resources and support to help her manage her condition more effectively. She frequently engages with health-related content on Twitter, and has shown interest in learning more about diabetes management strategies. She reports having access to a smartphone and internet connection, and feels comfortable using Twitter as a communication channel. She has no history of pregnancy, and is not under 21 years of age.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with clinically definite MS two years ago. She has an EDSS score of 3, indicating moderate disability. She has been receiving immunomodulatory therapy for the past year and has been stable in terms of her MS symptoms. However, since the COVID-19 outbreak, she has been feeling anxious and worried about her health. She has been practicing social distancing and has been unable to attend her physical and cognitive rehabilitation therapies due to the pandemic. She has been experiencing fatigue, sleep disturbances, and a decrease in her physical activity levels. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak on her MS symptoms and to receive support during this difficult time.

An overweight 44-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and sitagliptin presents with an interest in adjustable gastric banding (AGB). She has a BMI of 38.3 kg/m² and a fasting glucose concentration of 140 mg/dL on two occasions. She has tried multiple diets and exercise regimens but has been unable to achieve significant weight loss. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of AGB on postprandial glucose metabolism independent of weight loss. She is willing to attend the Mayo Clinic Clinical Research Unit (CRU) for a screening visit and is excited about the possibility of contributing to the development of novel interventions for the prevention and treatment of Type 2 diabetes and obesity.

The patient is a 30 year-old female who has been practicing trail running for the past 5 years. She has completed at least 2 races per year, with distances ranging from 40 to 80 km. She has no known chronic cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic or neuromuscular disease. She is physically active and exercises regularly, with a focus on strength training and endurance. She has no history of sleep disorders or psychiatric pathologies. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and does not have any legal protection measures or restrictions. She is currently living in Grenoble and is available before and within 15 days after the race. She has a social security scheme and is able to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old female presenting with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. She has a history of smoking for over 30 years and has been diagnosed with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) which has metastasized to her liver. She has undergone 4 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy but has experienced disease progression. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is otherwise healthy and has no other malignancies in the last 5 years. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. Her vital signs are within normal limits and she meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

Patient is a 6-year-old boy diagnosed with Tetralogy of Fallot. He has had two previous cardiac surgeries, including a Blalock–Taussig shunt procedure at 2 months of age and a complete repair at 2 years of age. He has a history of hypoxic episodes and has been on oxygen therapy since birth. He is currently on medications for heart failure including digoxin, furosemide, and enalapril. His preoperative hematocrit is 34%, blood urea nitrogen is 12 mg/dL, creatinine is 0.7 mg/dL, and electrolytes are within normal limits. His RACHS1 score is 3. During the intraoperative period, his hematocrit values before CPB, during CPB, after CPB and after reversal of the heparin with protamine will be recorded. His aortic cross clamp time, body temperature, urine volume, and diuretic use during CPB will also be recorded. Postoperatively, his blood gas and lactate values, hematocrit, chest tube drainage, iv fluids (crystalloid and colloid), and blood products will be recorded at postoperative 6th and 24th hours. The vasoactive agents, the inotrope score, the amount of urine, and the use of diuretics will be recorded. The length of stay in the intensive care unit and the duration of mechanical ventilation will also be recorded.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) following a course of intravenous antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. She was treated with oral metronidazole and her symptoms resolved, but she is concerned about the possibility of recurrence as she requires another course of antibiotics for a dental infection. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. She denies any history of inflammatory bowel disease or other chronic diarrheal illness. The patient has not previously taken oral vancomycin or had any adverse reactions to it. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the intervention. The patient's renal function is normal with a serum creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 80 mL/min/1.73m2. She is not pregnant and is expected to survive longer than 72 hours.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who works indoors and spends little time outside. She has a history of vitamin D deficiency and has been prescribed vitamin D supplements by her primary care physician. She is interested in exploring alternative ways to increase her vitamin D levels and is considering sunbed tanning. She has no history of skin cancer, granulomatous disease, liver disease, or kidney disease. She is not taking any photosensitive medications and is not currently pregnant. She has not used a sunbed in the past 60 days and does not have any travel plans to sunny destinations during the study period. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating to determine if sunbed tanning can help improve her vitamin D levels.

A 30 yo otherwise healthy female who is interested in participating in clinical research studies. She has no chronic medical conditions, is not currently taking any medications, and has not had any recent illnesses or hospitalizations. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the required follow-up visits. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She has not traveled to countries where Shigella or other enteric infections are endemic within the past two years, and does not have a history of microbiologically confirmed Shigella infection. She has not received a previous experimental Shigella vaccine or live Shigella challenge. She has normal nasal and pulmonary function and has not had any recent sinusitis or rhinitis. She does not smoke and does not have a history of inflammatory arthritis. She has no significant abnormalities in pre-admission screening lab results and is not allergic to ciprofloxacin or ampicillin. She is willing to comply with inpatient rules and regulations.

A 25-year-old male patient was diagnosed with leukemia and underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant. He has been struggling with chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) for 6 months after the transplant, despite the use of steroid therapy. The patient has been experiencing skin rash, joint pain, difficulty swallowing, and diarrhea, which are considered as cGVHD symptoms. The patient is otherwise in good health, with no history of significant medical conditions other than leukemia. The patient's original marrow donor will undergo leukapheresis to collect lymphocytes.
