The lymphocytes will be processed to preferentially select anti-inflammatory Treg cells, and then infused into the patient through an intravenous catheter. The patient will also self-administer low-dose interleukin-2 (IL-2) daily through an injection under the skin for 8 weeks, starting from the day of donor Treg cell infusion. Steroid therapy will continue during the first 6 weeks of IL-2 therapy, and the dose of steroids may be reduced after week 6 if the cGVHD improves. The patient will be observed for about an hour after the Treg cell infusion and will have regular assessments to evaluate the cGVHD symptoms. The patient will also be asked to keep a drug diary to document when and where they took the study drugs. The patient will be required to use adequate contraception during the study. The effects of IL-2 on the developing human fetus are unknown. Women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation. The patient must also have adequate organ function and meet other eligibility criteria to participate in this phase I clinical trial.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) six months ago. He underwent chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. However, a routine follow-up scan showed a relapse and he was found to have high-risk aggressive lymphoma. He underwent an autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT) and is currently recovering well. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has no other serious health conditions. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of maintenance therapy post-ASCT.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has recently been discharged from the hospital after being admitted for dehydration and urinary tract infection. She lives alone in her own home and has no contact with the Municipality. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She is currently taking medication for these conditions. She is able to communicate and collaborate well. She complains of some pain in her lower back and legs, but she can walk independently. She has a BMI of 27, and her nutritional status is satisfactory. She has no signs of dementia and is alert and oriented. Her grip strength and chair-to-stand test results are normal. She rates her pain as 3 out of 10 on the Verbal Ranking Scale. Her quality of life is moderate, and she has a strong sense of coherence. She is willing to participate in the study and hopes to improve her overall health and prevent any further loss of function.

A 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years came to the clinic. She has a history of endometriosis that was diagnosed by laparoscopy 1 year ago. She has undergone two in-vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles with the transfer of 5 high-quality embryos, but both cycles failed to result in clinical pregnancy. She has regular menstrual cycles and her partner has a normal semen analysis. She has no congenital or acquired uterine or tubal abnormalities, and her hormonal profile is normal. She has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 20-29. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may increase her chances of conceiving.

Patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of severe pneumonia requiring intubation for 4 days in the ICU. He was recently extubated and has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and coughing during meals. He has not had any prior history of dysphagia. The patient's medical team has ordered a swallow consult within 48 hours of extubation and he is being considered for participation in a clinical trial evaluating the sensitivity and specificity of the Yale Swallow Protocol in identifying aspiration in recently extubated patients. The patient is able to speak English and has no known contraindications for a FEES. He has no history of facial fractures, is not NPO for any other procedures, and does not have an elevated bleeding risk. He is alert and oriented with no significant agitation. The patient has no known allergies to dairy.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who is married and has two children. She has no significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with breast cancer or any other cancer. She is interested in learning more about the benefits and risks of mammography screening for breast cancer. She has no family history of breast cancer but is concerned about her risk as she ages. She is active, exercises regularly, and follows a healthy diet. She has a college education and works as a marketing executive. She is interested in participating in research studies and hopes that her participation can contribute to improving women's health.

A 60-year-old male was admitted to the ICU of a hospital in Spain due to COVID-19 infection. He tested positive for COVID-19 through real-time PCR. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes. He was intubated and required mechanical ventilation for 2 weeks. He also received ECMO for 5 days. He was discharged from the hospital after a month of ICU admission. He experiences shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue for the past 2 weeks. He is willing to participate in a study that aims to determine the long-term respiratory and cardiovascular consequences, quality of life, and mortality rate of patients who were admitted to the ICU due to COVID-19 infection in Spanish hospitals. He is also willing to provide a blood sample for the epigenetic study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who recently had an abnormal Pap smear result. She had a colposcopy, which revealed a lesion on her cervix. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. She has never had pelvic radiation or a hysterectomy. She is not pregnant and has two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading and cooking in her free time. She is willing to participate in research studies and is able to give informed consent.

A 40-year-old healthy female, previously diagnosed as a persistent nasal carrier of Staphylococcus aureus (SA), presented to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial that aims to assess the eradication of SA from the nasal cavity. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m2 and has not smoked in the past 3 months, as confirmed by a urinary cotinine test. She has no acute or chronic illness or infection and has not taken any prescribed or over-the-counter medication within the last 14 days, except for hormonal contraceptives. She has not used any topical or systemic antibiotics within the past month. She has not participated in any clinical trial within the last 3 months. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse in the previous 12 months. She is a fertile female but agrees to comply with acceptable contraception. She has no open wound, lesion, inflammation, erythema or infection affecting the nostrils, nose, upper lip, and area of skin close to the nose. She has no history of nasal surgery, including cauterization in the last 12 months, nasal polyps, significant anatomical nasal abnormality, or in-situ nasal jewelry or open nasal piercings. She has no history of abnormal bleeding, bruising, frequent nosebleeds, or diagnosis of von Willebrand disease. She has no autoimmune disease or hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients of Bactroban® Nasal Ointment, i.e., mupirocin, white soft paraffin, Softisan 649 (mixed diglycerinester of fatty acids). She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and agrees not to take part in another clinical trial at any time during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents to the clinic with a complaint of chest pain that started two weeks ago. The pain is a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that radiates to his left arm and jaw. He reports that the pain is brought on by exertion and relieved by rest. He has not had any previous episodes of chest pain or heart attack. He currently takes medications for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is a smoker and has been smoking for the past 30 years. He drinks alcohol occasionally but denies any illicit drug use. He works as a construction worker and is physically active on his job. He has no family history of heart disease. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help diagnose the cause of his chest pain.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma. She has a history of smoking for 25 years, and has been experiencing shortness of breath, persistent cough, chest pain and unintentional weight loss. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The diagnosis was confirmed by a biopsy of the lung tissue. The patient is scheduled to undergo lung surgery to remove the tumor. She has provided consent to participate in a molecular analysis study of her tumor tissue. She is willing to provide additional samples for this study and has no history of cancer other than lung adenocarcinoma. The patient is in overall good health and is eager to contribute to the advancement of cancer research.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with non-infectious uveitis. She has been experiencing significant visual disturbances related to lens opacification. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. She does not have glaucoma or ocular hypertension. She has no active inflammation and is not currently experiencing any symptoms related to her uveitis. She is interested in participating in the study as she hopes it will improve her vision and quality of life. She has no known allergies or adverse reactions to previous surgeries or medical treatments. She is an active retiree who enjoys spending time with her grandchildren and participating in community events.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of chest pain and non-obstructive coronary artery disease (20-70% luminal diameter narrowing) documented by coronary angiograms. He has not experienced a myocardial infarction, been treated with coronary artery bypass grafting or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty. He does not have unstable angina or any lesion > 20% luminal narrowing in the left main coronary artery. He has no history of congestive heart failure, NYHA class II - IV, severe renal dysfunction, symptomatic peripheral artery disease, drug or alcohol abuse, active liver disease or hepatic dysfunction, prior cerebrovascular accident or transient ischemic attack, or malignancy. He is not currently enrolled in another investigational device or drug study. He has no deformities of the digits of the upper extremities and is not suffering from a medical condition prohibiting blood flow occlusion in both arms. He is willing and able to comply with the study and its scheduled visits and procedures.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was involved in a car accident while driving under the influence of alcohol. He was taken to the hospital immediately after the accident where he was tested positive for alcohol in his blood. The accident caused him severe injuries including fractures in his leg and arm. He is currently undergoing treatment for his injuries and is expected to be in the hospital for a few weeks. He has a history of occasional drinking but has never been involved in an accident before. He is a college student and

A 35-year-old female patient who has a family history of colorectal cancer comes to the clinic for screening. She has been diagnosed with Lynch Syndrome and has a genetic mutation in the MSH2 gene. She has undergone a colonoscopy and the doctors have confirmed that she is tumor-free. She has no history of colorectal cancer, but she is at high risk of developing it due to her genetic condition. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to take mesalamine for the next two years. She is not pregnant and is using highly effective contraception. She has no history of renal insufficiency or severe liver disease. She is mentally stable and is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the study. She has signed the informed consent form and is ready to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic knee pain and discomfort for the past year. He has a history of a meniscal tear in his left knee and has undergone partial meniscectomy surgery in the past. He has been experiencing difficulty with daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs due to the pain and stiffness in his knee. He has no other significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and does not consume alcohol excessively. His BMI is 28. He has a healthy right knee with no pain or functional limitations.

This is an 80 year-old female with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. She was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, which is locally advanced and inoperable. The patient is currently undergoing treatment by radiotherapy. The oncologist has recommended that the patient take part in a study that involves the use of validated geriatric assessment tools, including the G8 screening test, to evaluate the patient's overall health and fitness for treatment. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and has expressed willingness to participate in the study.

A 24-year-old woman, who is a full-time student, is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a probiotic on gastrointestinal function, wellness, fecal bacteria and blood biomarkers. She is in good health and has no known medical conditions or allergies. She does not take any medications, antibiotics or probiotic supplements. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is willing to complete multiple online questionnaires, take a daily capsule (either probiotic or placebo) for 8 weeks, and provide blood and stool samples at various times throughout the study. She has daily access to a computer with internet access and is comfortable using it for the study. She has no history of gastrointestinal disease, chronic disease or immune-compromising diseases. She understands that she will not receive any direct medical benefit from participating in the study but is interested in contributing to scientific research.

57 year old man with a history of hypertension and occasional headaches, who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. Imaging showed a spontaneous lobar and basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with a volume of 40 ml. His GCS score was 8 on admission. He is currently being managed in the neurology ward with conservative measures, but hematoma removal surgery combined with decompressive craniectomy has been suggested. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of this approach and reduce his chances of long-term disability. Past Medical History: Hypertension, occasional headaches, no history of previous stroke, diabetes, or heart disease.

A 47 year old female with chronic low back pain for over 6 months, with a pain score of 6/10 on the visual analog scale. She has had previous physical therapy sessions and has been prescribed analgesics, but with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She reports difficulty with daily activities such as walking and sitting for prolonged periods of time. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in alternative therapies and willing to participate in a four-week physiotherapy program enriched with yoga exercises and regimen measures, as indicated by a doctor. She is able to commit to attending therapy sessions twice a week for 60 minutes and is willing to perform yoga exercises daily at home.

62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity presented to the hospital on [DATE] with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Upon admission, he was found to have a positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 and was diagnosed with moderate Covid-19. His oxygen saturation was 92% on room air and improved to 95% with 4L of nasal oxygen. He was started on standard oxygen therapy and received treatments for his symptoms. Despite these treatments, his oxygen saturation remained at 94-95%. He was approached to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of hydrogen therapy delivered by a nasal cannula in addition to conventional oxygen therapy in patients with moderate Covid-19. The patient was informed of the potential risks and benefits of the study and provided written consent. He met all inclusion criteria and did not have any exclusion criteria. He was randomized to receive either hydrogen therapy or standard oxygen therapy alone and will be monitored closely for any adverse effects.

A 55-year-old man with a history of chronic kidney disease (stage 4) presents with elevated serum phosphorus levels. He has been on a low-phosphorus diet for the past 6 months but his phosphorus levels remain elevated. His medication regimen includes calcium carbonate and vitamin D supplements. His most recent serum phosphorus level was 5.2 mg/dL. He is not yet on dialysis and his kidney function is stable. He reports no allergies to shellfish or sensitivity to chitin. He has no history of active malignancy, infection, or liver disease. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is willing to chew gum for 60 minutes and understands the requirements of the study. He is currently not enrolled in any other clinical trials and has not received any investigational products in the past 28 days. He is able to comply with the prescribed therapy and is willing to maintain a stable diet appropriate for his stage of kidney disease. His salivary flow rate by Saxon test is greater than or equal to 1 g/2 min.

A 32-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of HIV for the past 3 years. She has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past two years and her viral load is currently undetectable. However, she has been a smoker for the past 10 years and smokes about 10 cigarettes a day. She has tried to quit smoking before but has not been successful. She owns an Android smartphone and is interested in using a mobile health app to help with smoking cessation. She understands and reads English and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has a permanent address and contact information. She blows a CO level of 8 into a breath analyzer at baseline. She is excited to participate in this study to improve her health and well-being.

Patient A is a 45-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with hypercholesterolemia. Despite being on a stable dose of atorvastatin, his low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels are not well-controlled. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently on any other medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. His BMI is within the normal range. Laboratory tests show that his LDL-C level is above the recommended range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Bococizumab (PF-04950615;RN316) in lowering his LDL-C levels. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including regular subcutaneous injections of the study drug every two weeks.

The patient is a 42-year-old Caucasian male who was recently admitted to Hershey Medical Center for a severe asthma attack. He has been a smoker for the past 15 years, smoking at least 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He has tried to quit smoking several times before, but has not been successful. He is motivated to quit smoking and is interested in participating in the Penn State TXT2STAYQUIT Study to receive additional support to help him stay quit after he is discharged from the hospital. He has a cell phone and is comfortable receiving text messages. He speaks and reads English fluently and has no cognitive impairment. He is not currently enrolled in any other smoking cessation programs. His hospital stay is expected to be at least 2 days.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end-stage renal disease. He has been experiencing poor appetite and has lost weight over the past few months. He reports feeling weak and tired throughout the day and has difficulty completing activities of daily living. His body mass index is currently 20 kg/m2 and his serum creatinine level is 7 mg/dL. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medications. The patient is willing to participate in a study examining the effects of protein supplementation during dialysis to improve muscle mass, functional status, and quality of life. His high sensitivity CRP level is 4.5 mg/dL, making him eligible for the study. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures, including monitoring of his dietary intake and regular blood draws.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who was diagnosed with a ventricular septal defect (VSD) during a routine check-up. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient's VSD has a diameter of 5mm and a margin to aortic valve distance of 3mm. The patient's echocardiogram shows a left to right shunt of the ventricular shunt. The patient weighs 40kg and is in good general health. The patient and their family have been informed about the study, and they have given their informed written consent to participate in the study.

A 54-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with stage III endometrial carcinoma with a clear cell histology. She had a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) and omentectomy. The final pathology report showed a 2 cm residual tumor with no lymph node involvement. She has no history of prior cancer or chemotherapy. She has a good performance status (GOG 1) and has no significant comorbidities. Her blood counts, liver and kidney functions are all within normal limits. She has not undergone any prior pelvic or abdominal radiotherapy.

A 65-year-old male was diagnosed with locally relapsed prostate cancer following radical radiotherapy. His PSA levels have been rising and he has been on androgen suppression therapy with antiandrogens. He is in good health with a World Health Organisation (WHO) performance status of 1. He has a PSA value of 80 ng/mL at study entry and his hepatic, renal, and haematological functions are all adequate. He has not received chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy within the last 28 days, and he does not have any concurrent severe medical illnesses or psychiatric pathology likely to affect protocol compliance. He has not been previously treated with prostate brachytherapy or AdNRGM and CB1954. He is willing to use at least two methods of contraception and agrees not to father a child within 12 months following AdNRGM administration. He is able to travel for regular hospital assessments.

The patient is a full-term newborn male baby delivered by normal vaginal delivery with a birth weight of 3 kg. The baby was diagnosed with metatarsus adducts at birth, and the deformity was observed in both feet. The baby has no other medical problems or congenital anomalies. The baby's parents are willing to participate in the study and are cooperative with the healthcare team. They have no history of physical or mental illness. The mother is currently breastfeeding, and the baby is growing and developing normally. The family lives within a reasonable distance from the hospital and is available for follow-up visits. The baby has not undergone any interventions for the metatarsus adducts at this time.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently had a diagnosis of nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. He is a smoker and has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. He has no prior history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. A transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) revealed a thrombus in his left atrial appendage (LAA) within the past 72 hours. He has not been treated with any anticoagulant therapy in the past month. He is willing to use adequate contraception if sexually active. He has no history of intracardiac thrombus, free-floating ball thrombus, intracardiac tumor, or known left ventricular or aortic thrombus. His bleeding risk is low. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Edoxaban in resolving the LAA thrombi.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently underwent hip replacement surgery. He was diagnosed with pulmonary embolism (PE) a week after the surgery and has been receiving anticoagulant therapy since then. He complains of excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and frequent episodes of awakening during the night. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He has never been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) before. He has a BMI of 32 and his neck circumference is 42 cm. His oxygen saturation level is 92% on room air. He denies smoking or using any illicit drugs. He works as an office manager and does not engage in any strenuous physical activity. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He has no history of any lung disease.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who has never received the Hepatitis B vaccine before. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study and has given written informed consent. She has no history of Hepatitis B vaccination, and her medical history, clinical examination, and laboratory tests establish that she is healthy and eligible for the study. She is of childbearing potential but practices adequate contraception and has a negative pregnancy test. She has not received any investigational or non-registered product, immunosuppressants, or immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to the first vaccine dose. She has not received any vaccine other than the influenza vaccine within 30 days preceding the first dose of vaccine. She has no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition, history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine, or current serious neurologic or mental disease. She does not have any past or current malignancies and lymphoproliferative disorders, acute or chronic, clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic, renal functional abnormality, autoimmune disease or anemia, or acute disease at the time of enrollment. She is not pregnant or lactating, has no history of chronic alcohol consumption and/or drug abuse, and has no other conditions that the principal investigator judges may interfere with study findings.

This is a 50-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with extensive stage small cell lung cancer. She has no history of prior cancer except for nonmelanomatous skin cancer. The patient is in overall good health and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no significant medical history or psychiatric illness that would affect her ability to comply with the study requirements. The patient has measurable disease and is eligible for chemotherapy but has not received prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. She has brain metastases but is neurologically stable at study entry. The patient is not currently pregnant or nursing, but is of childbearing potential and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study. She is able to swallow capsules and has no contraindications to receiving the study drugs.

The patient is a 40-year-old Caucasian male who has been experiencing symptoms of heartburn and acid reflux for the past 3 months. He reports a burning sensation in the chest and throat, especially after eating spicy or fatty foods. He has tried over-the-counter antacids, but they only provide temporary relief. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. His last endoscopy showed no evidence of mucosal break or other gastrointestinal issues. He experiences at least mild symptoms on at least 2 days/week or at least moderate symptoms on at least 1 day/week. He is able to understand and follow instructions and is committed to complying with the study requirements. His HAM-D score is 2.

45-year-old female with a history of chronic low back pain and radicular pain in the left leg for the past 6 months. Pain is described as constant, dull, and achy, radiating down to the foot. She has tried various conservative treatments including physical therapy and NSAIDs but has not experienced significant relief. She has been referred to interventional pain management for further evaluation and management. MRI shows a disc herniation at L4-L5 level, which is thought to be the cause of her symptoms. She is scheduled for a lumbosacral transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI) and has been randomized into the group receiving either a 22-gauge or 25-gauge needle. She has consented for the study and is aware that she may experience some pain during the procedure. She has no contraindications to the procedure, is not pregnant, and has a BMI of 28.

45 year-old Asian female with a BMI of 29.5 and a waist circumference of 102 cm. She has been struggling with elevated LDL-cholesterol levels and has been looking for natural ways to improve her cholesterol and glucose levels. She has a family history of diabetes, but does not have any personal history of diabetes. She has been taking a stable regime of hypertension medications for the last 6 months with good control of her blood pressure. She does not take any vitamin, mineral, dietary or herbal supplements. She has not experienced any significant weight changes in the last 3 months. She enjoys a healthy and balanced diet but has been struggling to incorporate more plant-based protein sources. She does not have any liver or renal disease and has not been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease or any other gastrointestinal disorders. She is excited to be a part of this clinical trial to improve her health and to help others in the future.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 3 years. He has been managing his diabetes with a daily injection regimen that includes NPH insulin and insulin lispro. His Hemoglobin A1c is 8.5% and his prescription medication regimen has been stable for the past 2 months. He lives within a 60-minute drive-time radius of the central monitoring location and is willing to remain within a 120-minute drive-time radius throughout the study. He has someone over 18 years of age who lives with him and is willing to check on him if needed. He is willing to wear one infusion set and one Dexcom CGM sensor and change sets every other day throughout the study. He has a mobile phone that he is willing to keep with him and answer calls from study staff. He is willing to avoid the use of drugs that may dull the sensorium, reduce sensitivity to symptoms of hypoglycemia, or hinder decision making during the period of participation in the study. He has no history of liver disease, pancreatic disease, or coronary artery disease. He has no history of seizures or untreated mental illness. He is not on any electrically powered implants that might be susceptible to RF interference. He is not allergic to adhesive or tape that must be used in the study. He is willing to avoid using acetaminophen for the duration of the study. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 65-year-old man with a history of smoking for over 25 years was diagnosed with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) two years ago. He is currently taking medications for COPD and has not had any exacerbations, hospital admissions, or changes in treatment in the last three months. He is retired and spends most of his day indoors. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and no history of alcoholism or malnutrition. He has no other significant respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, musculoskeletal or metabolic pathologies. He is interested in increasing his level of physical activity to improve his exercise capacity and quality of life.

The patient is a 43-year-old African American male suffering from moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). He has been diagnosed with OSA for the past 2 years and has been using a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) device with a fixed pressure setting. He complains of difficulty sleeping and daytime sleepiness despite the use of his CPAP device. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is employed as a construction worker and has no known psychiatric or medical conditions that could interfere with the study. He speaks and writes fluent English. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his sleep quality and adherence to therapy.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who has been diagnosed with pre-diabetes based on her medical history and screening results. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 29 kg/m2 and has been experiencing mild symptoms of elevated blood glucose levels such as fatigue and increased thirst. Her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication and she has no significant abnormalities in liver or kidney function. She is not currently taking any thiazolidinediones, steroids, anti-depressants, or weight loss drugs. She is postmenopausal and practices appropriate birth control. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

28yo male with cystic fibrosis, FEV1 49%, currently on Kalydeco and Orkambi, presents with shortness of breath and difficulty breathing with exertion during daily activities. He reports frequent episodes of coughing with purulent sputum production, which have been ongoing for the past year. He reports having to stop frequently during exercise due to shortness of breath and reports a decrease in exercise tolerance over the past year. He is currently a non-smoker and has a past smoking history of 5 pack-years. He is able to read and understand English.

This is a 55 year old male with a history of presbyopia who has been wearing reading glasses for several years. He is currently working as a software engineer and spends a significant amount of time in front of a computer screen. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His best corrected distance visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. He has no significant ocular history and has never undergone any ocular surgery. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the AcuFocus Corneal Inlay ACI7000PDT for the correction of his presbyopia. His preoperative cycloplegic refraction is plano in both eyes with no more than 0.75D of refractive cylinder. His central corneal thickness is greater than or equal to 500 microns in both eyes and his corneal power is between 41.00D and 47.00D in all meridians in both eyes. He is willing and able to return for scheduled follow-up examinations for 12 months after surgery. He has demonstrated tolerance to monovision blur as determined by monovision contact lens trial. He does not have dry eye syndrome or any other ocular pathology that would prevent an acceptable visual outcome. He is not taking any medications that may affect wound healing or have significant ocular side effects. He is not pregnant, lactating, or of child-bearing potential.

Patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who has never participated in a clinical trial before. He has no history of organic or psychological pathology and is not currently taking any prescription medication. The patient has a BMI within the range of 18 to 30 and has normal vital signs and electrocardiographic recording. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to drugs and is not suspected of drug abuse. The patient does not consume alcohol daily, smoke or have acute alcohol poisoning in the last week. He has not donated blood in the last three months and has not participated in any other investigational drug study in the previous 3 months. The patient understands the purpose of the study and is willing to follow instructions and collaborate during the course of the study. He is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception from the moment of signing the informed consent until 6 months after the end of his participation in the study.

As this clinical trial involves facial allotransplantation, the patient should have severe facial deformities caused by burn, trauma, or tumor resection. The patient should have extensive defects in the right buccal division combined with severe cicatricial contracture deformity, upper lip, total nose, the front wall of the right maxillary sinus, the lateral right orbital wall and infraorbital wall, the right zygomatic bone, and a large portion of the right parotid gland. The patient should have already undergone traditional reconstructive procedures, including free skin graft, application of local flaps, tissue prefabrication, tissue expansion, and free tissue transfer, but these procedures can only cover the wound without bony framework. The patient should be in good health, with normal function of heart, liver, and kidney. The blood type of the donor should be the same as the patient's, and at least 3 sites should be matched within 6 HLA sites. Patients with abnormal function of heart, liver, or kidney, and donors with a different blood type and only 1 or 2 sites matched within 6 HLA sites should be excluded.

This study is a retrospective analysis of patients who have tested positive for COVID-19. You may be eligible if you have been diagnosed with COVID-19 through a positive RT-PCR test. The study aims to evaluate if patients who have developed pulmonary embolism during the course of COVID-19 show different clinical and laboratory findings compared to those who did not develop pulmonary embolism. No additional treatment or intervention will be provided as a part of this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) for the past 10 years. He has been struggling with weight management and has a BMI of 38 kg/m². He has been on multiple oral hypoglycemic agents but still has poor glycemic control with HbA1C levels of 8.5%. He is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco products. He does not have any history of seizures or use of tricyclic antidepressants. He underwent routine preoperative upper endoscopy which revealed gastritis and esophagitis, requiring follow-up endoscopy in the post-operative period. He is interested in participating in the study to investigate the small intestinal remodeling and reprogramming of glucose metabolism following laparoscopic Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB).

A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The symptoms started about 2 hours ago. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. On examination, the patient is alert and oriented but has right-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria. His blood pressure is 180/100 mmHg, heart rate is 90 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. A non-contrast CT scan of the brain is performed, which shows a left middle cerebral artery territory infarct with an ASPECTS score of 7. The patient is deemed a candidate for mechanical thrombectomy and is transferred to the interventional radiology suite. After successful recanalization of the occluded vessel with a mTICI score of 2b/3, the patient is randomized to receive either rt-PA or placebo. The patient or his surrogate has provided informed consent. The patient has no history of significant pre-stroke functional disability with a pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale of 0. The estimated delay to onset of rescue intraarterial rt-PA administration is within 24 hours from symptom onset. The patient meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for the study.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer and is currently receiving chemotherapy treatment at Massachusetts General Hospital. He is married with two children and holds a bachelor's degree in economics. He is currently employed as a financial analyst and has a stable income. He lives with his wife in a suburban home and has a supportive social network of family and friends. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty reading or understanding medical information. He has no previous history of chemotherapy treatment for his current disease.

55 yo female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 years, currently experiencing symptoms of joint pain and stiffness despite being on Enbrel for the past 6 months. The patient is in clinical remission, defined as DAS28 less than or equal to 2.6 and has been for the preceding 6 months. The patient is willing to stop taking Enbrel for 56 days and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore a novel therapeutic paradigm for RA, remission maintenance. The patient is not taking oral prednisolone at doses > 10mg/day or undergoing changes in NSAID or glucocorticoid dosing regimen during the 4 weeks prior to randomization. The patient is not receiving DMARDs other than Enbrel and methotrexate and has not had any significant changes in their current methotrexate regimen within the 3 months prior to dosing. The patient has no allergies to the study medication or components thereof and has no history of drug or other allergy that contraindicates their participation. The patient has no active infections and no significant cardiac, pulmonary, metabolic, renal, hepatic or gastrointestinal conditions that would place them at an unacceptable risk as a participant in this trial. The patient is willing and capable of giving written informed consent, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with Fabry disease. He has been experiencing severe pain in his hands and feet, which has been increasing in intensity over the past few months. He also reports having gastrointestinal symptoms, including diarrhea and abdominal pain. He has not been receiving enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for the past 6 months. His urine GL-3 levels are four times higher than the upper limit of normal. He has never been treated with migalastat or other iminosugars. He is currently taking angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors for his blood pressure, which have been stable for the past 4 weeks. He is sexually active and agrees to use medically accepted methods of birth control during the study and for 30 days after study completion. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with her weight for years. She has a BMI of 28 and regularly consumes sugary foods and drinks. She has two children, ages 8 and 10, who are also overweight. She is interested in participating in a research study that aims to improve her overall health and help her lose weight. She is willing to commit to a low energy diet for two months and participate in the program for a total of 12 months. She does not have any medical conditions that would exclude her from the study and is able to attend all required appointments during normal working hours.

This study is seeking medical residents who are in their first year of specialty training in Portugal between the ages of 23 and 45. The specialties being studied include General Surgery, Neurosurgery, Orthopedics, Internal Medicine, Gastroenterology, Cardiology, Rheumatology, Endocrinology, Oncology, Intensive Medicine, Pediatrics, Radiology, Clinical Pathology, Neurology, and Psychiatry. The participant must have no history of major psychiatric disorders, such as drug abuse with dependence, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or schizoaffective disorder. The resident must be committed to participating in the study and willing to sign the informed consent form. However, those who have attended an international formative stage with a duration over 12 months or attended a medical specialty for more than one year previously are not eligible for the study.

A 45-year-old female patient was admitted to the medical intensive care unit with a history of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 24 hours prior to enrollment in the trial. She has no history of tracheostomy, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), or transfer from an outside hospital with more than 24 hours of mechanical ventilation. The patient is orally intubated with an endotracheal tube and is therefore eligible for the trial. She will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group with the CleanSweep™ Closed Suction System or the control group with the standard in-line suction device. She will also receive the ventilator bundle that consists of head of bed elevation, ETT cuff pressure management, deep vein thrombosis prevention, daily sedation interruption and SBT, and oral care every 4 hours with chlorhexidine at 12pm (noon) and 12am midnight. The patient's progress will be monitored closely to evaluate the effect of the CleanSweep™ Closed Suction System on time to first successful spontaneous breathing trial, length of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU stay, length of total hospital stay, and occurrence of ventilator-associated events.

A 10-year-old female patient with beta thalassemia major presented to the pediatric hematology clinic with a history of receiving regular blood transfusions since the age of 6 months. Her latest ferritin level was 1200 ng/mL, indicating transfusion-associated iron overload. The patient was started on deferasirox as an iron chelating agent to manage the iron overload. However, after a few weeks of treatment, she experienced drug-related toxicities including nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. The patient's parents consented to participate in the pharmacogenetic study to investigate the genetic polymorphisms of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A (UGT1A) subfamily, multi-drug resistance-associated protein 2 (MRP2), and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). The aim of the study is to identify the genetic factors that may contribute to drug-related toxicities in patients receiving deferasirox and to find the optimal target population for this therapy.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B. The patient has completed protocol NV-02B-003 without any serious adverse events attributed to study drug and remains seropositive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have signs of decompensated chronic hepatitis B. The patient is willing to participate in an extension study to compare the safety and effectiveness of treatment beyond 1 year of telbivudine and telbivudine combined with lamivudine.

56-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with hematuria and urinary frequency. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) with predominant urothelial histology. CT scan shows non-metastatic disease, with no evidence of lymph node involvement. He is deemed eligible for Radical Cystectomy (RC) + Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection (PLND) and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. His organ function is adequate. He has not received any prior systemic treatment for cancer, including anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1/L2 or anti-CTLA-4 therapy. He has no known additional malignancy that is progressing or requiring active anti-cancer treatment. He has never received a live or live attenuated vaccine within 30 days before the first dose of study intervention. He does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or a known history of HIV infection, Hepatitis B infection or known active Hepatitis C infection. He does not have a known psychiatric or substance abuse disorder.

A 42-year-old male patient who works as a construction worker and enjoys playing basketball in his free time has been experiencing knee pain for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with a meniscal tear and scheduled for an outpatient arthroscopic meniscectomy surgery. He lives with his wife and two children and has arranged for his wife, who works part-time as a nurse, to be his primary caregiver during the preoperative period. He speaks English fluently and is comfortable using electronic devices. He has no history of chronic pain or mental health issues.

The patient is a 24-year-old female who is generally healthy and physically active. She has no history of chronic pain, mental health disorders or cardiovascular disease. She does not smoke and has never had any surgery. She is proficient in English and does not have any difficulty with physical exercise. She has not been diagnosed with any chronic illness, pulmonary disease, diabetes, Raynaud disease or claustrophobia. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the influence of baseline pain sensitivity and expectation on the pain response following exercise.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has metastasized to her lungs and liver. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has progressed despite treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help monitor her cancer progression and treatment response. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and has signed the consent form. She has no known vascular diseases or mental health conditions that could interfere with the study. The patient is currently not taking any targeted therapy but is open to the possibility of receiving it if it is deemed beneficial for her treatment.

A 35 year old woman came to the clinic with complaints of persistent low mood, lack of energy and interest in daily activities for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate major depression by psychiatrists according to the diagnostic criteria for depressive episodes in DSM-5 (American Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (Fifth Edition)) and her Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAMD-17) score is 12. She has never taken any antidepressant medications or other treatment for depression before. Her body mass index is 23.5, and she has no history of allergic reactions to milk protein or lactose intolerance. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no other serious diseases. She agreed to intake study product during the study period and has signed written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with colon cancer. After discussing treatment options with her physicians, she has opted for surgical intervention. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to manage her blood pressure. Her BMI is 27. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any other significant medical history. She is scheduled to undergo a colorectal surgery at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, and her data will be stored in the perioperative data warehouse. She has provided written consent to participate in the study and follow the ERAS protocol as part of her perioperative care.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial, as it is focused on assessing the impact of a forgiveness education program on psychological well-being in children and teachers in conflict zones. However, potential participants would need to be in 5th grade (US equivalency, aged 10-12) and teachers of 5th grade classes. The study will take place in Northern Ireland, Israel/Palestine, and Taiwan. Participation in the study will require consent from teachers, students, and their parents. The study will involve a 12-week forgiveness education program, which will be administered by trained teachers. The study will use various measures to assess the impact of the forgiveness education program on psychological well-being, including the Enright Forgiveness Inventory, the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System, the Ethnic Prejudice Scale, the Herth Hope Index, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and academic achievement scores. The study aims to determine if such education can increase psychological well-being in children and teachers in conflict zones.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). His aortic diameter is between 35 and 49mm, making him eligible for the LIMIT clinical trial. He has no known history of diabetes mellitus and his HgbA1c is below 6.5%. He is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. He has an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 45 ml/min/1.73 m2 and is able to take oral medication. He is willing to undergo two computed tomographic aortograms (CTA) and q6 monthly blood draws, as well as complete SF-36 quality of life forms. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to metformin hydrochloride or iodinated radiographic contrast medium. He has an expected survival of at least two years and has not undergone prior surgical AAA repair or anticipated repair within two years. He does not have any known syndromic aortic conditions or severe liver disease, jaundice, or active hepatitis. He is not currently participating in any other investigational drug trials and is not pregnant, lactating, or intending to become pregnant.

The patient is an 8-year-old Ojibwe girl who lives on the reservation with her parents and siblings. She is in the 3rd grade and enjoys playing with her friends and spending time with her family. Her parents are both enrolled tribal members and are actively involved in the community. They are concerned about the high rates of substance abuse among youth on the reservation and are interested in participating in a prevention program. The family is excited to participate in the family-centered alcohol and drug prevention program, which includes cultural lessons to strengthen family interactions, decrease substance use, and teach parenting and social skills. They understand that sessions will last around 3-hours, including a meal, youth and parent breakout sessions, and group-based discussions, and are willing to commit to the 14-week program. They are also willing to participate in pre- and post-tests to help evaluate the program's effectiveness for delaying and/or preventing adolescent onset of alcohol and drug use.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia. She has a history of hepatic encephalopathy and mild ascites. Her Child-Pugh score is 10 and MELD score is 18. She is scheduled to undergo an elective invasive procedure and requires a platelet transfusion to manage the risk of bleeding associated with the procedure. Her baseline platelet count is 40,000/µL, and her serum sodium level is 137mEq/L. She has no history of arterial or venous thrombosis, and she is not currently on any investigational drugs. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she agrees to use contraception during the study. She has no physical limitations to ingest and retain oral medication and is able to understand and comply with protocol requirements. She provides signed and dated written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She is currently in the hospital with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Her chest X-ray and computed tomography (CT) scan showed atypical pneumonia. She has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her vital signs are stable, and she is receiving oxygen through a nasal cannula to maintain adequate oxygen saturation levels. She has consented to participate in this clinical trial and is eligible for treatment with AN69ST hemofilter based extracorporeal blood purification. She is not pregnant and does not have any conditions that would exclude her from the study. She will be closely monitored for selected biochemical, immunological, and coagulation parameters in combination with radiological imaging to guide clinical practice and tailor therapy consisting of early initiation of blood purification using the oXiris® (AN69ST) filter, systemic heparinisation, and respiratory support.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who suffered a stroke three months ago, resulting in left hemiparesis and difficulty with fine motor tasks of her left hand. She has been undergoing physical therapy for the past two months but has not seen significant improvement in her hand function. She is a retired teacher and currently lives with her husband. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to medications. She is able to follow instructions and is willing to comply with the therapy protocol. She has the ability to grasp and lift the test object. She has no history of myasthenia gravis, Eaton-Lambert syndrome, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or any other disorder that might interfere with neuromuscular function. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse or any relevant neuropsychiatric conditions. She has no infection or skin disorder at an anticipated injection site. She has no condition or situation that, in the investigator's opinion, may put her at significant risk, confound the study results, or interfere significantly with her participation in the study. She has no history of surgery or other significant injury to either upper extremity causing mechanical limitations that preclude task performance. She has no previous neurological illness such as head trauma, prior stroke, epilepsy, or demyelinating disease. She has no complicating medical problems such as uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes with signs of polyneuropathy, severe renal, cardiac or pulmonary disease, or evidence of other concurrent neurologic or orthopedic conditions precluding her from complying with the study protocol. She is not currently being treated with intrathecal baclofen.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from Indonesia who is scheduled for urology surgery. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history and his BMI is 26. The patient has been informed about the study and has given consent to participate. He has no relative or absolute contraindications to spinal anesthesia and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the crossed leg sitting position or traditional sitting position group.

The patient is a 20-year-old woman who gave birth to a premature infant weighing less than 1000 grams. The infant was enrolled in a previous study conducted between 1998-2000 on fluconazole prophylaxis for prevention of fungal colonization and infection in preterm infants. The infant survived and is now at least 18 years of age. The woman, who is the infant's biological mother or legal guardian, is willing to participate in this study and provide information on the infant's neurodevelopmental outcome and quality of life. The woman has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and has no known allergies to fluconazole. She is able to comprehend and communicate in English and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with end-stage renal disease who is currently receiving dialysis treatment. He has been on dialysis for the past 3 years and has been actively seeking a living donor for a kidney transplant. He has a history of high blood pressure and is currently taking medication for it. He has no known allergies and has never had an organ transplant before. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He has a BMI of 29 and is generally in good health, except for his kidney disease. He has been cleared by his healthcare team for a kidney transplant and has an identified live donor who is an HLA-A2 mismatch. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive the study treatment TX200-TR101, which involves using his own immune cells to help prevent rejection of the donated kidney. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to adhere to the study requirements.

This clinical trial is seeking African-American umbilical cord blood donors who are participating in the National Marrow Donor Program cord blood collection protocol C-2844. The study aims to collect information about the donors' demographics, maternal history, gestational history, and delivery through questionnaires. Cord blood units (CBU) will be collected in utero and transported to the Stem Cell Processing Laboratory for evaluation. The study seeks to correlate the total nucleated cell yield of cord blood units with the aforementioned factors. There are no specified medical or prior concurrent therapy requirements for participation.

A 52-year old man, who works as a construction supervisor, was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue. He underwent a biopsy and imaging studies which showed no evidence of metastasis. He reports occasional pain in the tongue and difficulty speaking and swallowing. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He has never smoked or used any illicit drugs. He occasionally drinks alcohol, mostly on weekends. He is married with three children. He is an active man who enjoys playing basketball and running. He is currently scheduled for a surgical resection of the tumor with curative intent. The patient is willing to participate in the study, understands the risks and benefits, and is willing to comply with the study procedures. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. His recent laboratory results showed a creatinine clearance of 68 mL/min, ANC of 1.5 x 10^9/L, leukocytes of 5.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 12.5 g/dL, and platelets of 180 x 10^9/L. He has no history of autoimmune disease or organ transplant. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 35-year-old Chinese woman presents with a history of psoriatic arthritis symptoms for at least 6 months. She has been diagnosed with active plaque psoriasis and nail changes consistent with psoriasis. She experiences moderate to severe PsA with BSL ≥3 tender joints out of 78 and ≥3 swollen joints out of 76. Her rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-CCP antibodies are negative. She has never been exposed to secukinumab or other biologic drugs that directly target interleukin-17 (IL-17) or IL-17 receptor. She is not taking high potency opioid analgesics. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraception during the entire study. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study and has given a written, signed, and dated informed consent. This patient is an ideal candidate for this clinical trial, as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 32 year-old male who was diagnosed with thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) related to aHUS (atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome) last year. The patient was previously enrolled in the clinical trial OMS721-TMA-001 and had shown improvement in his disease markers while on treatment. However, after the trial ended, the patient experienced a relapse of his symptoms. The patient's treating physician believes that continued treatment with OMS721 may be beneficial for the patient's condition. The patient is 18 years or older, has no known hypersensitivity to OMS721 or any excipients, and does not have any serious medical conditions that may increase the risk of OMS721 treatment. The patient and his family have been informed about the compassionate use program and have provided informed consent for the patient to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who suffered a closed humeral shaft fracture in a fall while playing basketball. He is an English speaker and his age is within the range of 18-65 years old. He is seeking treatment within two weeks of his injury and is available for follow-up for at least 12 months. He is able to sign informed consent. He does not have any additional long bone injuries of the upper or lower extremities that would compromise outcome assessment. He is not immunocompromised and is able to comply with post-operative rehabilitation protocols or instructions. He has no previous retained hardware in the humeral shaft.

A 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presents to the hospital with symptoms of renal failure. Initial laboratory results indicate elevated creatinine and BUN levels, and a nephrology consult recommends initiation of intermittent hemodialysis. The patient has no known history of cardiac disease or arrhythmias and is not taking any medications that would contraindicate the use of mannitol. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce the frequency of low blood pressure events during dialysis.

The patient is a 3-month-old infant who underwent a surgical procedure to create an ileostomy due to a congenital bowel problem. The baby's parents have been struggling to cope with the demands of managing the ileostomy, including the need for parenteral nutrition. The medical team has informed the parents about a clinical trial that investigates the benefits of mucous fistula refeeding between enterostomy creation and enterostomy closure. The parents have shown interest in enrolling their baby in the study and are willing to comply with the treatment and follow-up procedures. The baby has not undergone a resection of the ileocecal valve, does not have colostomy, small bowel atresia, chromosomal abnormalities, or Hirschsprung's disease. The baby also does not have an intestinal perforation due to a hemodynamic heart defect.

This is a 45-year-old male with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 3 infection. He has had this condition for over six months and has a viral load greater than or equal to 10,000 IU/mL. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and has agreed to use protocol-specified methods of contraception if engaging in heterosexual intercourse. He does not have a history of clinically significant illness that may interfere with treatment or assessment, nor does he have chronic liver disease of a non-HCV etiology. He is not infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has had type 2 diabetes for 10 years. She reports that her blood sugar levels have been poorly controlled despite taking metformin and insulin. She has also noticed that her vision has been getting blurry and she has difficulty reading small print. She was referred for a dilated eye exam where she was diagnosed with moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of glaucoma, cataracts, or other eye diseases. She has never undergone any interventional therapy for her diabetic retinopathy. Her most recent A1c was 8.5%, and her creatinine level was within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of alpha lipoic acid for the treatment and prevention of diabetic retinopathy. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 55-year-old man, retired from a desk job, with a history of colon polyps, had a colonoscopy scheduled for 2 weeks from the day of his visit to the clinic. He has no other underlying medical conditions, but he has a family history of colon cancer. He is generally healthy, but he sometimes forgets appointments or important tasks. He is independent, lives alone, and has a cell phone. He has adequate health literacy and trusts his physician. He is willing to participate in the study and believes that he would benefit from the IVR messaging system to remind him of his upcoming colonoscopy appointment.

This is a 56 year-old female diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer with measurable disease. She has a history of hypertension and is on a stable regimen of anti-hypertensive therapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her absolute neutrophil count is ≥ 1,500/mm^3 and her platelet count is ≥ 100,000/mm^3. Her prothrombin time (PT)/international normalized ratio (INR) is ≤ 1.5 and her partial thromboplastin time (PTT) is < 1.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN). Her alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are < 3 times ULN and her bilirubin is ≤ 1.5 times ULN. Her creatinine is ≤ 1.8 mg/dL and she has protein negative on urine dipstick. She has no history of arterial thromboembolic events within the past 6 months, serious nonhealing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture within the past 28 days, significant traumatic injury within the past 28 days, ongoing or active infection, or concurrent prophylactic filgrastim (G-CSF) or sargramostim (GM-CSF). She has not received prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, but adjuvant therapy completed at least 12 months before first evidence of metastasis is allowed.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has a history of smoking for 30 years. He was recently diagnosed with stage I non-small cell lung cancer located in the upper lobe of his right lung. He is scheduled to undergo a video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) lobectomy. He has no history of significant medical conditions and takes no regular medications. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He is fluent in English and can answer self- and interviewer-administered questions in English. He is willing to participate in this randomized treatment and understands the potential benefits and risks of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She presented with symptoms of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She was admitted to the hospital and received treatment with oxygen therapy and antiviral drugs. Her respiratory symptoms improved gradually, and two consecutive nucleic acid tests of respiratory specimens such as sputum or nasopharyngeal swabs were negative after 10 days of treatment. However, during a routine screening visit, her blood sample tested positive for COVID-19. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial and sign the informed consent. She has no known allergies to favipiravir. She is not pregnant or lactating. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, but she has stable liver, kidney, and heart functions. She has no history of mental disorders, substance abuse or dependence. She is not participating in any other clinical research.

A 62-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during a routine check-up. The tumor is 4.5 cm in diameter and located in the right lobe of the liver. The patient has been referred for liver transplantation and has been listed for a transplant. He is currently waiting for a donor liver to become available. The patient has Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) score of 7 and has good liver function. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history.

A 42-year-old woman presents to the clinic after undergoing a biopsy that confirmed the presence of unilateral invasive breast cancer. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy, with a performance status of 0. The breast cancer was fully removed through surgery, including the breast tumor and axillary nodes. The histology of the breast cancer shows ER-positive cancer cells, with no HER2 overexpression. The patient is uncertain about the potential benefit and toxicity of adjuvant chemotherapy and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient has not received any previous systemic or locoregional treatment for the present breast cancer. She is willing to comply with the scheduled visits and follow the study's protocol, and has signed informed consent for participating in the clinical trial.

A 68-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with symptoms of acute decompensated heart failure. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has a history of myocardial infarction and is currently on aspirin, atorvastatin, and metformin. She reports shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs for the past few days. On examination, she is found to have jugular venous distension, bibasilar crackles, and lower extremity edema. Her blood pressure is 148/90 mmHg, heart rate is 95 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air. Her chest X-ray shows pulmonary edema. Echocardiogram from her previous hospitalization shows ejection fraction less than 50%. She fulfills the modified Framingham criteria for heart failure. She has baseline data available within 1 hour of initial ED therapy and is willing to give informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with adenoid cystic carcinoma with overexpression of KIT, which has recurred after previous treatment. She has a measurable target lesion with a diameter of 2 cm which has been confirmed by computed tomography (CT) scan. She is able to swallow oral medication and has a WHO performance status of 1. Her hematological, hepatic, and renal functions are normal. She has no history of cardiac disease or recent ischemic events, and her 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is normal. She has no other active malignancies, infections, or systemic diseases. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using effective contraception. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

54-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis and a loop ileostomy for the past 2 years. The patient has been using the Hollister 2-piece New Image pouching system for the past 6 months and has been experiencing frequent leaks, causing skin irritation and discomfort. The patient is compliant with changing the pouching system at least twice a week but is interested in finding a solution that will improve the lifespan of the equipment and reduce the frequency of changes. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has a stoma with a diameter of 50mm. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 2 months and is not currently receiving systemic or local steroid treatment in the peristomal area. The patient has no known allergies to surgical grade stainless steel and has not participated in a clinical study in the past 30 days. The patient's ostomy skin tool score is below 3.

21-year-old female varsity-level tennis player with a history of shoulder pain and limited range of motion in her dominant arm. She has been playing tennis for 10 years and has been experiencing pain in her shoulder for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse when serving and overhead shots. She has tried rest, ice, and heat therapy in the past, but the pain and limited range of motion persist. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the eight-week posterior shoulder stretching program will help alleviate her pain and improve her range of motion. She has not had any previous surgical procedures or fractures of either shoulder and is not currently receiving treatment for any condition affecting either shoulder.

54 yo M with a history of osteoarthritis in the left hip and a prior acetabular fracture repair with hardware placement, now presenting with worsening hip pain and decreased mobility. He has been recommended for total hip arthroplasty and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new device that may reduce the risk of infection after surgery. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - T2DM - Former smoker (quit 10 years ago) - No history of prior prosthesis infection or active infection - BMI of 28 - Medications: lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin.

A 35-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption presents with a persistent cough and weight loss. He has no significant past medical history. The chest X-ray shows findings consistent with pulmonary tuberculosis. GeneXpert and HAIN MTBDR plus confirmed susceptibility to RIF and INH. He agrees to participate in the trial and provides written informed consent. He weighs 75 kg and is within the age range of 18 to 65 years. He is willing to avoid foods high in tyramine during the trial period. He is sexually active but willing to use effective contraception methods during the trial. He is negative for HIV and has a CD4 count >220 cells/mm3. He has no history of any intolerance to study drugs or contraindicated conditions. There is no evidence of clinically relevant cardiovascular, metabolic, gastrointestinal, neurological, psychiatric, or endocrine diseases. He has no significant lung conditions other than TB, and respiratory function is normal. His laboratory findings are within the normal range. His ECG shows no clinically relevant changes. He has not taken any restricted medication in the past month or enrolled in other clinical trials.

A pregnant woman presents with preterm labor at 30 weeks gestation. She has no significant medical history and no family history of preterm birth. The baby is delivered via emergency C-section due to fetal distress. The newborn weighs 1200 grams and is admitted to the neonatal unit. The baby stays in the unit for 50 days and is finally discharged at 36 weeks postconceptional age. The mother consents to participate in a clinical trial investigating body composition at discharge and neurological development at 2 years in very preterm infants.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RR-MS) two years ago. She has experienced several relapses in the past year and her neurologist has recommended that she begin treatment with oral dimethyl fumarate (DMF). She is currently not taking any medications for MS. Her Expanded Disability Status Score (EDSS) is 4.5. She is able to understand the purpose and risks of the study and has given oral informed consent for the TEC-ADHERE study. She has no memory or psychiatric disorders that would prevent her from completing questionnaires in the study.
