This is a 7-year-old girl who has been experiencing recurrent respiratory infections for the past few months. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of coughing, sneezing, and a runny nose. She has been visiting the pediatric department at a specialist children's hospital for treatment. She has been diagnosed with trachitis/bronchitis, acute upper respiratory tract infection, and pneumonia in the past. She has been prescribed different medications for each diagnosis, but her parents have noticed that the medication compliance has been an issue. Her parents are concerned about her condition and have agreed to participate in this clinical trial to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of respiratory diseases in pediatric patients.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of Crohn's disease affecting only the small bowel or ileocecal region. He has been experiencing moderate to severe disease activity and has been initiated on vedolizumab with or without thiopurines or methotrexate. He is currently undergoing treatment for his condition, but his response to vedolizumab is unknown. He is not pregnant and is over 18 years of age. He has no contraindications for MR enterography and is able to provide informed consent.

Pt is a 28yo healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the bioavailability of tolvaptan administered via nasogastric tube to tolvaptan tablets swallowed intact. She meets the inclusion criteria as she is healthy, between the ages of 18-40, and has a BMI within 20% of ideal body weight. She is willing to give written informed consent prior to entering the study. She has not participated in another study within 30 days of the study period and has not consumed alcohol within 24 hours prior to study days 1 and 8 of the study schedule. She is not currently taking any medications, juices, or herbal supplements that may affect drug absorption. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not had any intestinal surgery or gastrointestinal disorder that may affect drug absorption, and has no significant cardiac, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, biliary, renal, hematological, neurological, or psychiatric disease as determined by medical history and physical examination. The patient is interested in contributing to the advancement of medical knowledge and is willing to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who suffered a stroke six months ago and has been experiencing hemiparesis since then. He has been diagnosed with Ischemic Stroke and has undergone clinical examination and imaging to confirm the diagnosis. His hemiparesis is considered to be spastic and falls between 1 and 2 degrees on the Ashworth scale modified for muscle group of ankle plantar flexor. He is able to walk without the use of assistive devices but has limited range of motion in passive dorsiflexion (less than 5 degrees). The patient has no cognitive impairment and scored above 22 on the Mini-Mental State Examination. He has no clinical comorbidities that may interfere with the intervention such as high blood pressure or cardiac arrhythmias. The patient has no pathological deformities of the lower limbs or presence of scabs on malleolus. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the influence of Kinesio Taping® in paretic tibialis anterior muscle during patient gait and balance after stroke.

Pt is a 30yo M with a 5 yr history of type 1 diabetes, currently on insulin pump therapy. He has a history of frequent hypoglycemic events and has difficulty controlling his glucose levels due to acetaminophen's interference effect on the current continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system he is using. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of the Dexcom G6 CGM system with a non-interferent sensor. The patient is compliant with his diabetes treatment and is willing to adhere to the study protocol for the duration of the study. He has no known gastroparesis or abnormal liver function.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease due to diabetic nephropathy has been undergoing hemodialysis for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and peripheral artery disease. He reports a sedentary lifestyle due to his physical limitations and feels fatigued most of the time. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to participate. He is able to perform physical activity for 30 minutes per dialysis session and has no medical contraindications to perform physical exercise. The patient is affiliated with the French Social Security system and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. He is clinically stable and is interested in finding ways to improve his overall health and quality of life.

A 28-year-old male came to the clinic with a history of bipolar I disorder. He has been experiencing manic episodes for the last 3 weeks and was voluntarily hospitalized at the start of the study. He has a history of at least one documented manic episode prior to the study initiation. His initial Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) score was 25 and Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score was 18. He has no history of substance dependence or seizure disorder. He is not pregnant or nursing. He is willing to participate in a double-blind study to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of risperidone compared with placebo after 3 weeks of treatment in patients with bipolar disorder who are experiencing manic episodes.

A 32-year-old female patient is scheduled for outpatient laparoscopic surgery for the diagnosis and treatment of endometriosis. She has a history of dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility. The patient has no history of chronic pain or opioid use. She has no known allergies to pain medication. She takes no medications regularly and her medical history is unremarkable. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. The patient is physically active and regularly participates in yoga classes. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help find the optimal opioid prescription for post-operative pain control.

25 yo female with a history of mild asthma, diagnosed according to GINA guidelines, presents with a positive skin prick test for grass mix and has had a positive response to an incremental inhaled allergen challenge with house dust mite allergen or grass pollen allergen. She is a non-smoker with a history of less than 1 pack a year and has been a non-smoker for at least the last five years. Her FEV1 is 85% of predicted. She meets the criteria of being a healthy subject with no clinical evidence of allergic rhinitis and respiratory disease (e.g. asthma) and has a negative skin prick test for grass mix or D. pteronyssinus at or within 12 months prior to the screening visit. She has a negative response to an incremental metacholine challenge (PC20 ≥ 8mg/ml) and has a total IgE (Immunglobulin E) of <100 IU/ml. She is not pregnant, not nursing, and is using a highly effective method of contraception during the entire study. She has no history of upper or lower respiratory tract infection four weeks prior to the informed consent visit, no past or present disease that may affect the outcome of the study, and no clinically significant pathological findings in safety laboratory tests. She does not take any medication other than short acting inhaled beta agonists, paracetamol for pain relief, birth control medication, hormonal replacement therapy, dietary and vitamin supplements. She has no history of life-threatening asthma and no suspected hypersensitivity to any ingredients of the medication in line with bronchoscopy (bronchodilators, sedatives and local anesthetics). She has no conditions or factors that would make her unlikely to be able to undergo bronchoscopy or incremental allergen challenge and no conditions or factors that would make her unable to undergo MRI such as metal containing implants, remainders of shell splinters or bullets, or claustrophobia. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is able to understand the protocol requirements, instructions and study-related restrictions, the nature, scope, and possible consequences of the study. She has not participated in a clinical trial 30 days prior to enrollment and has not had a segmental allergen challenge three months prior to treatment.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare histiocytic disorder. He presented with fatigue, weight loss, and chest pain. Imaging showed bilateral symmetrical osteosclerosis and retroperitoneal and mediastinal fibrosis. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of Erdheim-Chester disease. The patient is willing to participate in the International Rare Histiocytic Disorders Registry (IRHDR) and has signed the informed consent. There is a suitable pathology sample available for central review.

Patient is a 28-year-old male from the United States who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is within the normal range and he is not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. He is willing to fast for the required duration of the study and has no known allergies to ondansetron or related medications. He is available for follow-up visits and is able to provide informed consent.

A 62-year-old woman suffered a mild stroke that affected the right side of her body, including her right leg. She is currently receiving inpatient physical therapy care and is medically stable. The patient is able to understand and communicate in English. She requires minimal assistance for bed mobility and coming to sitting from the supine position. She has not undergone any lower extremity amputation and is able to reach overhead, grasp an object, and feed herself with her left upper extremity. The patient is motivated to participate in the study to help improve her lower extremity function and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with colon cancer and is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic partial large bowel resection with primary anastomosis. She has an American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Score of P2 and is scheduled to receive postoperative pain management primarily with opioid analgesia via intravenous (IV) patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). She is able to read, write, and fully understand the language of the study diary and has voluntarily provided informed consent. She has no history of total colectomy, gastric bypass, previous bowel resection, or short bowel syndrome. She has not taken therapeutic doses of opioids for the consecutive 7 days immediately before surgery and has not participated in a clinical trial with alvimopan or taken alvimopan in the past 30 days. She has no diagnosed history of alcoholism or drug addiction, constipation, pelvic floor disorder, or GI disorders known to affect bowel function. She has no history of laxative dependence or daily use and is willing and able to complete the study diary.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) four years ago. She has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy and is currently experiencing a relapse of the disease. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no significant medical history. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, except for a mildly elevated serum creatinine level of 1.5 mg/dL. She has not received ibrutinib or participated in an ibrutinib clinical trial before. She is willing to practice a highly effective method of birth control during and after participation in the study if she is of childbearing potential and sexually active. She has signed the informed consent document and agreed to give complete access to her medical records. She meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for the named patient program.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who presents with a history of back pain and difficulty walking. She reports that the pain has been present for several months and has progressively worsened. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but her symptoms have not improved. MRI imaging reveals a tumor involving the spine with extraosseous extension or arising in paraspinal soft tissues with tumor involving or abutting the dura. Biopsy results confirm the presence of a malignant tumor. The patient has no history of genetic disease or medical condition associated with an abnormal radiation sensitivity. She is otherwise in good health and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to undergo surgery to remove the tumor and participate in the intra-operative dural brachytherapy with Yttrium-90 plaque applicators. Her Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) is 80, indicating that she is able to carry out normal activities with little to no difficulty. She has no evidence of cord/cauda malfunction for causes other than the effect of local tumor growth or due to metabolic effects of the tumor.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of metastatic prostate cancer. He has been experiencing severe pain in his lower back and hips for several weeks, which has been affecting his quality of life. Imaging studies have shown the presence of bone metastases in these areas. He has been recommended for palliative radiation therapy, with the standard treatment being 5-10 fractions of radiation. The patient is willing to consider alternative treatment options and is able to provide informed consent. However, he is not a candidate for single fraction palliative radiation, as determined by his healthcare provider. The patient is otherwise in stable condition and has no other significant medical history.

Patient is a 52-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 6 years. He has been taking metformin (1500 mg/day) for the past 2 years to control his blood sugar levels. The patient is also being treated for hypertension with an ACEI for the past 6 months. His HbA1c level at screening is 8.2% and his plasma volume has not been measured before. He has no history of diabetic ketoacidosis, type 1 diabetes mellitus, pancreas or beta cell transplantation, or diabetes secondary to pancreatitis or pancreatectomy. He has not experienced any severe hypoglycemic episodes in the past 6 months. He has no known allergies to any medications.

The patient is a 62 year old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and advised to undergo coronary artery bypass surgery. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not have any significant past surgical history. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He does not smoke tobacco but is an occasional user of marijuana for recreational purposes. He is able to read and write in English and has a good understanding of the study. He has no preoperative opioid use and does not have any known hepatic or renal dysfunction. His left ventricular ejection fraction is above 50%. He is willing to give his consent for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is scheduled for a lumpectomy procedure to remove the cancerous tissue. She has no history of autoimmune disease and has never received neoadjuvant chemotherapy prior to lumpectomy. The patient is fluent in English and able to read and understand the consent form. She understands that the Zenith FLIM Diagnostics imaging device is an investigational technology that is being tested to visualize the operative margins in real time during the lumpectomy procedure to improve the accuracy of margin assessment. She is willing to participate in the study and have her lumpectomy specimen and shaved margins evaluated with the Zenith FLIM imaging device. She is aware that the results of the FLIM analysis will not be used for diagnosis or treatment decisions, and that the study is designed to evaluate the accuracy of the Zenith FLIM margin results compared to pathology results. She is also aware that the specimens will no longer be sterile once they are placed in the Zenith FLIM device and that the device will not come into contact with her during the procedure.

55-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 7 years presented to the clinic with complaints of increased stiffness and pain in the joints over the past few months. She was previously treated with methotrexate and prednisone, but she continued to have active disease with a DAS28 score of 5.5 and HAQ score of 1.8. She was deemed eligible for treatment with etanercept and was enrolled in the clinical trial. The patient has been experiencing difficulty in performing activities of daily living due to her RA symptoms, including difficulty in walking, standing, and performing household chores. She has a sedentary lifestyle due to the joint pain and stiffness. She is otherwise healthy with no significant comorbidities and is compliant with her medications. She has no contraindications for etanercept therapy and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman scheduled for a laparoscopic colectomy due to a history of colon polyps. She has no known allergies to local anesthetics and has not developed a tolerance to opioids. She is able to use IV-PCA for pain management. The patient has no history of previous abdominal surgeries or intestinal obstructions, and this procedure is not an emergency. She falls within the age range of 20 to 80 years old.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has a history of peripheral artery disease (PAD) with stenosis of the femoral and/or popliteal arteries. The patient has been experiencing symptoms such as leg pain and weakness, especially during physical activity. The patient has previously undergone plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) but has not received any treatment in the past 90 days. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with study follow-up requirements. The target lesion is located at least 10 mm below the common femoral bifurcation and terminates distally at or above the end of the P1 segment of the popliteal artery, with a target vessel diameter between 4mm and 7mm. The target lesion has angiographic evidence of ≥70% stenosis by operator visual estimate. The patient has no significant stenosis in the inflow and outflow arteries, and the target lesion is free from any prior stent or other interventions. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 2 years and has no known allergies to contrast medium or antiplatelet treatments. The patient has no impaired renal function, is not dialysis dependent, and is not receiving immunosuppressant therapy. The patient does not have a known or suspected active infection at the time of the index procedure and has a platelet count within the range of 100,000/mm3 to 700,000/mm3. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal hemorrhage requiring a transfusion within 3 months prior to the study procedure and does not have a coagulopathy that precludes treatment with systemic anticoagulation and/or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). The patient has no history of stroke within the past 90 days or myocardial infarction within the past 30 days. The patient is not incarcerated, mentally incompetent, or abusing drugs or alcohol. The patient is not participating in another investigational drug or medical device study that has not completed primary endpoint(s) evaluation or that clinically interferes with the endpoints from this study, or is planning to participate in such studies prior to the completion of this study. The target lesion does not have severe calcification and does not involve an aneurysm or is adjacent to an aneurysm (within 5 mm). The target lesion does not require treatment with alternative therapy such as stenting, laser, atherectomy, cryoplasty, brachytherapy, re-entry devices, or subintimal dissection techniques. The patient does not have significant target vessel tortuosity or other parameters prohibiting access to the target lesion, and there is no presence of thrombus in the target vessel.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo elective abdominal surgery at the University Hospital Olomouc. She has a history of mild hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. She is currently not taking any other medications. The surgery is expected to last approximately 4 hours. The patient will be transferred to the ICU postoperatively, where she will be randomized into either the Plasmalyte (PL) or Ringerfundin (RF) Groups for perioperative fluid therapy. The patient is eligible for the study as she meets the age requirement and has no exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with moderate to severe facial erythema associated with rosacea. She has been experiencing frequent flare-ups and is looking for a treatment that can help reduce her symptoms. She is in good general health and does not have any underlying medical conditions. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use a reliable form of contraception during the study period. She has fair skin and is willing to minimize external factors that might trigger rosacea flare-ups. She has not undergone any facial laser surgery or had any blood dyscrasia. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 30 days. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to comply with all study requirements and procedures.

The patient is a 56 year old male diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease 2 years ago. He has been experiencing motor complications despite taking Levodopa and dopa agonist as prescribed by his neurologist. He is responsive to the medication with an improvement between Off and On UPDRS by at least 33% of the Motor UPDRS. His current HOEHN & YAHR staging is 3. He is otherwise in good health with no significant cognitive impairment and a score above 21 on the MMSE. He has not had any intracranial surgeries or implantation of a device for Parkinson's Disease in the past 2 years. His MRI does not show any gross atrophy or any other pathology of the brain. He has not been exposed to any investigational drug or procedure within 1 month prior to study entry and is not enrolled in a concurrent study that may confound results of this study. He has no active infectious diseases and is not on chronic immunosuppressive transplant therapy. He has a systolic blood pressure (supine) above 90 mmHg and a resting heart rate below 100 bpm. He is willing to give written informed consent.

A 38-year-old woman presents with a BMI of 42 kg/m² and is scheduled for bariatric surgery due to severe obesity. She reports having occasional bleeding gums and bad breath but is not currently receiving any dental treatment. The patient has no history of steroid or anti-inflammatory drug use, nor has she taken antibiotics for the past three months. The patient is affiliated with the Social Security system and has no previous participation in other research protocols. She will be examined for the presence and severity of periodontitis and separated into group 1 if moderate or severe periodontitis is detected, or group 2 if there is no or mild periodontitis. The day before the surgery, a blood sample will be collected for the analysis of inflammatory markers, and stimulated saliva, periodontal, and feces samples will be taken for bacterial determination. During the surgical procedure, a sample of visceral adipose tissue will be collected and used for periodontal bacteria detection and inflammatory marker analyses. The patient will be informed of the study's purpose and provided with all the necessary information before consenting to participate.

48 yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with chest pain and was found to have significant coronary artery disease on angiography. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement for a culprit lesion in the left anterior descending artery. He is currently stable and asymptomatic on optimal medical therapy, including statin therapy. His blood pressure is well-controlled on lisinopril and amlodipine, and his blood sugar is well-controlled on metformin. He has a family history of coronary artery disease, with his father having a myocardial infarction at age 60. He is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago. He has no history of recent surgeries, cancer, or inflammatory diseases. The patient will be enrolled in the study to assess plasma myeloperoxidase levels in patients with coronary artery disease.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with sepsis, hypotension, and altered mental status. The patient was intubated and transferred to the surgical intensive care unit where he received central venous access and invasive hemodynamic monitoring. The treating physician has determined that the patient requires continued invasive monitoring. The patient has no history of neck or body radiotherapy or previous or active upper-extremity deep venous thrombosis. Informed consent has been obtained from the patient.

28-year-old woman who delivered a premature baby at 30 weeks gestation, currently hospitalized at Besancon University Hospital. The baby was born due to the mother's poorly followed pregnancy, in a poor socio-economic environment and unstable family and occupational status. The patient is experiencing financial loss, transportation problems to get to the hospital, and isolation. She is concerned about the future and how to balance her work and taking care of her premature baby, who will need long-term support. The patient is interested in receiving social and psychological support, as well as information on how to care for her child after leaving the hospital.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU due to a severe car accident. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. He does not have any known respiratory diseases. He is conscious and responsive, but has multiple fractures and is in severe pain. The doctors have placed him on a ventilator to assist with his breathing. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has never been pregnant.

A 16-year-old male with a history of delusions and hallucinations since the age of 14. He was initially treated with risperidone, but due to lack of efficacy and side effects, the treatment was switched to quetiapine. He is currently under the care of a child and adolescent psychiatrist and has been on quetiapine for the past 6 months. He lives with his parents and younger sibling and attends high school. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 6-year-old boy was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). He lives in Maryland with his parents and younger sister. His family speaks English fluently. He was born at term and had no significant medical history or hospitalizations prior to his diagnosis. He is currently receiving chemotherapy and is being followed by a pediatric hematologist. His parents are concerned about his exposure to pesticides as they live in an urban area where they often see pest control trucks. They are interested in participating in a study that investigates the link between pesticide exposure and childhood cancer. They are willing to provide blood and urine samples for analysis and are willing to answer a questionnaire about their lifestyle and environmental exposures.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) 2 years ago. He has been receiving optimal PAH therapy but still experiences functional class III symptoms of right ventricle failure. He is on sildenafil, endothelin receptor antagonists, and prostacyclin analogs. He has never had a right heart catheterization, but his echocardiogram showed an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 60 mmHg. He has a history of hypertension, but it is under control with medications. He is a nonsmoker and does not drink alcohol. He is a computer programmer and works from home. He exercises regularly, but he has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue lately. He has not taken any anti-inflammatory drugs in the past 3 months, and he has no history of chronic inflammatory disorder or malignancy. He is not taking any medication that could interfere with the study. He has normal kidney function, platelet count, and white blood cell count. He is willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control throughout the study.

Pt is a 9yo M with a history of refractory epilepsy, with daily seizures despite treatment with multiple antiepileptic drugs. The patient has been on corticosteroids and ACTH in the past, which were tapered off two weeks ago. The patient's seizures have been affecting his daily functioning and quality of life, and his family is seeking alternative treatments. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no chronic systemic disease. The family is willing to participate in regular follow-up visits and maintain a daily seizure log. The patient has not previously received ketogenic diet or modified Atkins diet and is not suspected of having a mitochondrial disorder. The family is motivated and capable of complying with the low glycemic index diet therapy.

The patient is a 48 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (stage IC) after experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and a feeling of fullness for several weeks. She underwent surgery to remove the tumour, followed by chemotherapy. She has completed six cycles of chemotherapy and is currently in remission. She is interested in participating in a study that could potentially help identify better treatments for ovarian cancer patients like herself. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of major health problems or surgeries. She is willing to provide a tissue sample for molecular studies as part of the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with diffuse large cell lymphoma. She has undergone standard treatments, but her disease has progressed within the last 6 months. There are no other curative treatment options available to her, and her life expectancy is expected to be at least 2 months. She has no active systemic infection and meets all inclusion criteria. Her DLCO is above 40%, and her LVEF is above 40%. Her creatinine level is below 2.0 mg/dl, and her total bilirubin and AST levels are below 1.5x ULN and 3x ULN, respectively. She is not pregnant and is willing to use appropriate birth control during the study period. She has not had a previous allogeneic stem cell transplant, and she does not have HLA antibodies to donor HLA type.

62-year-old female with a history of herpes zoster infection on the left side of the body that healed about 6 months ago. She has been experiencing postherpetic neuralgia pain in the left side of her body, including the left arm, chest, and back. The pain is described as constant, burning, and shooting in nature with a severity of 7 out of 10 on a visual analog scale. She has tried various medications including gabapentin, amitriptyline, and topical lidocaine with no significant pain relief. She has no history of botulinum toxin use or immunization. She is otherwise in good health and has no other medical conditions.

A 45 year old woman has been experiencing pain in her lower back and abdomen for the past few days. She has noticed blood in her urine and has difficulty urinating. She visits a urologist who performs an ultrasound and discovers a kidney stone that is 2.5cm in size. The doctor recommends a percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PNL) to remove the stone. The patient agrees to the procedure and is informed about the clinical trial comparing the 18F Peel-way Sheath versus the 18F Access Sheath with a Suction-evacuation Function MPCNL for the Management of 2-5cm Size Kidney Stones. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial as she is between the ages of 18 to 70, has normal renal function, and has an ASA score of Ⅰ and Ⅱ. She does not have any congenital abnormalities or undergone any transplant or urinary diversion. She consents to participate in the trial and will be closely monitored throughout the procedure.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and in her second trimester. She has no history of diabetes or gestational diabetes and has not received any pharmacological treatment known to affect glucose metabolism. She is receiving prenatal care at a hospital and is being screened for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during the 24-32 weeks of gestation. She has not been diagnosed with any clinically significant neurological, endocrinological or other systemic diseases, and is not carrying multiple pregnancies. The patient has given written informed consent to be included in the study and has agreed to have her plasma TMAO concentration levels determined by stable isotope dilution liquid chromatography with online electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry. The patient will be included in the study if she meets the inclusion and exclusion criteria and has fasting blood samples collected before 20 weeks of gestation (if she is a nested case-control subject). The aim of the study is to investigate the association between plasma TMAO concentration and GDM.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has recently lost her maxillary incisor due to trauma. She is in good physical health and has a stable medical history. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products, and she does not use any medications that may affect bone metabolism. Her oral hygiene is adequate, with an estimated plaque score of less than 20%. She has no history of periodontal disease, and the teeth adjacent to the study site are stable, with minimal restorations and no signs of periodontal bone loss. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing and able to comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has no history of diabetes or postprandial hypoglycaemia and dumping syndrome. She has no established cardiovascular disease or cerebrovascular disease. Her blood pressure is within normal limits at 120/70 mmHg. She does not have Raynaud's disease or severe impairment of renal, hepatic, thyroid or adrenocortical function. She is not currently being treated with any anti-hypertensive treatment, lipid-lowering therapy or systemic steroids. She is not lactating or pregnant. She does not have any established vascular disease and has not undergone bariatric surgery. She has not experienced any significant weight changes within the last 3 months. She is eligible to participate in the clinical trial examining the involvement of KATP channels on the microvascular actions of the incretin GLP-1 and its analogues in healthy individuals.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with moderate periodontitis (stage II) based on a recent dental examination. She reports having occasional bleeding while brushing her teeth, and her dentist has noted pockets measuring between 3-4 mm. She has no history of periodontal therapy or antibiotic therapy in the past six months. She is a non-smoker, and her medical history is unremarkable. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the use of local delivery drugs as an adjunctive treatment to scaling and root planing for periodontitis, and the evaluation of gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) biological molecular markers (MMP-8). She understands the study requirements and has provided informed consent to participate.

A 65-year-old male patient was referred to the Department of Otorhinolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery, Helsinki University Central Hospital (HUCH), for PEG tube placement due to severe dysphagia caused by a recent stroke. The patient had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but was otherwise in good health. Laboratory tests showed normal electrolyte and coagulation parameters. The patient's BMI was 27 kg/m2, and there was no evidence of large volume ascites. The patient had not undergone a previous gastrectomy and was not suffering from sepsis. The patient was included in the study and underwent PEG tube placement. The follow-up period was aimed to run from PEG tube placement to the last clinical evaluation (minimum 12 months) or the time of death. The patient was monitored for complications related to the procedure and clinical status at each follow-up visit.

Patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He has been treated with metformin and sulfonylureas for the past 6 months, but his hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) level has remained high at 8.5%. The patient has never used insulin before and is willing to add basal insulin glargine U300 to his existing oral antidiabetic drug regimen to achieve better glycemic control. He has not experienced any adverse reactions to his current medications. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen and is able to monitor his blood glucose levels regularly. He has medical insurance but is concerned about the cost of the insulin and hopes that it will be affordable.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) visited the fertility clinic for assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment. She has been trying to conceive for more than a year without success. Her ultrasound showed at least 25 small follicles in one of her ovaries and her ovarian volume was greater than 10ml. She has no major uterine or ovarian abnormalities. She was diagnosed with PCOS and has undergone ovarian stimulation with gonadotropins for ART treatment. On the day of ovum pick up (OPU), at least 15 follicles were observed. The patient has consented to participate in the clinical trial to test the feasibility of applying a single COC CAPA-IVM strategy versus the group COC culture CAPA-IVM. She meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with COPD and has been experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing for the past 3 years. He is a former smoker, having quit 2 years ago after smoking for 30 years. He has a history of exposure to environmental pollution and indoor pollutants due to his occupation as a factory worker. His current medications include bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids, and oxygen therapy. His BMI is 28, BP: 135/80, HR: 85/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for elevated WBC count and C-reactive protein level. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the impact of particulate matter on his respiratory health and to potentially prevent future exacerbations of his condition.

This clinical trial is for participants who have already completed a previous study involving a single dose of 100,000 IU Vitamin D3 at the beginning of winter. The patient must be willing to participate in an additional blood draw. There are no specific age, gender, or health-related eligibility criteria provided. However, individuals who were not part of the previous study are not eligible to participate.

72 yo F with a recent diagnosis of mild dementia and living with her husband of 50 years. She has a history of good oral hygiene but has been experiencing difficulty in remembering to brush her teeth daily. Her husband has noticed that she has been having increased difficulty with oral hygiene and is willing to participate in the study. She has four natural teeth and is physically able to brush her own teeth. She is community-dwelling and has not been hospitalized for any psychiatric disorder in the prior year. She is interested in participating in a study to improve her oral health and maintain her independence. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Osteoporosis - Arthritis

55F with a history of obesity (BMI 35), hypertension, and compensated cirrhosis due to NASH was referred for evaluation of weight loss options. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. She denies alcohol consumption or smoking. Her most recent labs revealed elevated liver enzymes and imaging showed evidence of liver fibrosis. She reports a history of dieting without success and a sedentary lifestyle due to fatigue. On exam, she appears overweight with mild abdominal distention, no jaundice, no stigmata of chronic liver disease, and no asterixis. She has no peripheral edema, no spider angiomas, and no palmar erythema. Cardiovascular exam is significant for hypertension with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, regular rhythm, and no murmurs. Respiratory, abdominal, and neurologic exams are unremarkable. The patient is interested in participating in a weight loss program and is willing to comply with study requirements. She is not currently taking any weight loss medications or participating in a supervised weight loss program. She has no contraindications to an MRI.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU with respiratory failure due to confirmed COVID-19 infection. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is well-controlled with medication. Upon admission, he required invasive ventilation and had a lung ultrasound examination performed within the first week of start of ventilation. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has not undergone ECMO support and is above 18 years of age.

A 42-year-old woman with a known history of Rendu-Osler-Weber syndrome presents with recurrent episodes of gastrointestinal bleeding. She reports a history of multiple blood and iron infusions in the past 6 months due to her condition. She also underwent multiple endoscopic interventions with argon plasma coagulation but the bleeding persisted. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and migraine headaches. She is currently on amlodipine for hypertension and takes sumatriptan as needed for migraines. She denies any allergies or previous surgeries. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals telangiectasias over the lips and tongue. Laboratory investigations reveal iron-deficiency anemia. Gastrointestinal endoscopy shows multiple telangiectasias in the stomach and duodenum. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of her condition and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old Chinese woman who is concerned about her excess body fat. She has a body fat percentage of 35% and has struggled with weight loss in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of daily supplementation of 3.2 g CLA on body fat reduction and lipid profile. She is overweight with a BMI of 29.2 and has a sedentary lifestyle due to her office job. She has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension controlled with medication. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has no gastrointestinal problems that may affect her compliance with the procedure. She is willing to participate in regular lifestyle counselling sessions and follow the study protocol.

A 68-year-old man diagnosed with multiple myeloma that is not eligible for transplant. He has not received any prior treatment for his disease. The patient reports fatigue, bone pain, and weight loss in the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medications for his comorbidities. On physical examination, he has tenderness in his lower back and hips, and laboratory tests show elevated immunoglobulin levels in his serum. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for participation in the clinical trial testing the combination of ibrutinib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent. The patient agrees to comply with the study's requirements, including providing bone marrow aspirate and core, and blood samples for correlative research purposes.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past three years. He currently manages his diabetes with metformin and a diet and exercise regimen. His HbA1c is 8.2%. He has a BMI of 29 kg/m² and has no significant medical history or allergies to drugs or foods. He does not have any history of hypoglycemia or blood transfusions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new study drug for type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been struggling with alcohol and cocaine addiction for the past 5 years. He has a history of multiple relapses and has been in and out of rehab facilities. He is currently sober from alcohol for the past month but reports continued use of cocaine. The patient is motivated to quit using cocaine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that could potentially help him stay sober. He is in good physical health and is currently not taking any medications for his addiction. The patient is looking for additional support to aid in his recovery and hopes that this clinical trial will provide him with the necessary tools to achieve his goal of sobriety.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for sitagliptin therapy. She has no history of cardiovascular, hepatic, endocrine (such as diabetes), renal, pancreatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, immunologic, hematologic, or neurologic disease. She is currently not taking any medications and has not taken any in the last 30 days. Her metabolic, renal, hepatic, and hematological laboratory tests are all within normal limits. She is between 21 to 60 years of age and is willing to comply with the study protocols and procedures.

This is a 43 year-old female who recently started experiencing joint pain and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and knees. She has not received any prior treatment for rheumatoid arthritis. She has no history of joint function impairment due to any other condition. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who lives in Cruzeiro do Sul, Brazil. She has been experiencing fever (axillary temperature ≥37.5o C) for the past 48 hours and has no other obvious causes of fever. She visited the clinic and was diagnosed with P. falciparum malaria. She has a documented weight of 60kg and has no history of chronic or severe underlying diseases. Her hemoglobin level is 10 g/dl. She is willing to return to the clinic and/or accept home visits for regular check-ups during the 28-day follow-up period. She has never been pregnant and is not currently pregnant. She has not used any antimalarial drug in the previous 30 days. She is eligible for the study and will be treated with artemether-lumefantrine for three days, with doses according to the Brazilian guidelines for malaria control. Her clinical and parasitological parameters will be monitored for a 28-day follow-up period to evaluate the efficacy of the combination therapy. She will be asked to come back on Days 2, 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 for clinical evaluation and blood tests using microscopy. A blood sample will be collected on filter paper on the first day and on the day of suspected failure to try to differentiate the parasite genotypes using techniques based on polymerase chain reactions. The results of this efficacy evaluation on the drug combination will help the Brazilian Ministry of Health to evaluate the national policy for treatment of malaria caused by P. falciparum.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease six months ago. He has been undergoing dialysis for the past three months due to his condition. He has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue, which has led to a decrease in his quality of life. He is married and has two children. He works as a computer programmer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His blood pressure is well controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiac or cerebrovascular diseases. His laboratory results show an elevated blood urea nitrogen level of 45 mg/dL and a creatinine level of 6.2 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in the resistance training clinical trial to improve his physical capacity and quality of life.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who experienced a recent STEMI and is scheduled to undergo ICA to assess non-culprit lesions. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. The patient has no known allergies to medications or contrast agents. His recent renal function tests show a P-creatinine level of 100 micromol/L. He has no history of atrial fibrillation. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old African-American woman with a history of diabetes presents to a health center on the South Side of Chicago for her routine check-up. She was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago and has been struggling to manage her blood sugar levels. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. Her most recent HbA1c was 8.5%, and her blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg. She has been on metformin for the past year and is currently taking it twice a day. She reports difficulty adhering to her medication regimen due to financial constraints and forgetfulness. She also reports difficulty following a healthy diet due to limited access to fresh fruits and vegetables in her neighborhood. She is interested in learning more about diabetes management and improving her health outcomes. She is eligible to participate in the Improving Diabetes Care and Outcomes project as she meets the inclusion criteria of having a diabetes diagnosis and attending one of the participating health centers.

This is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer. She underwent a diagnostic biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis. Her tumour is ER-negative, HER2-negative and PR-negative. She has a tumour size of 2.5 cm and there is no evidence of metastatic disease. She is fit to receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy and has an ECOG performance status of 0. She underwent BRCA mutation testing and was found to be germline BRCA positive. She has a Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocytes (TILs) score available and her CK5/6 and EGFR +/- Androgen Receptor IHC score is also available. She is willing to comply with the Protocol for the duration of the trial including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is aware that she should not conceive during the treatment period and therefore should routinely use effective forms of contraception, throughout her participation in the trial and for at least 6 months after the last dose of trial treatment. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial and none of the exclusion criteria.

35 yo right-handed male OEF/OIF veteran who deployed to Iraq with a history of PTSD. The patient is currently on a stable psychotropic medication regimen for at least four weeks prior to enrollment. He has no history of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or bipolar disorder, substance abuse, or dependence. The patient has not had a seizure disorder or severe traumatic brain injury in the past. He has not attempted suicide within the previous two years nor has any active suicidal ideation within the past month. The patient is not currently taking benzodiazepines except for bedtime dosing only, nor is he currently taking stimulant medication. He has no known allergic reaction to modafinil or currently taking medication that may have altered metabolism if taken with modafinil. The patient is willing to participate in the required schedule of evaluations, including an in-person baseline evaluation, a phone evaluation at one week, and in-person evaluations at two and four weeks.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who recently experienced persistent upper abdominal pain along with frequent vomiting and weight loss. He visited his general practitioner and underwent a series of diagnostic tests, including CT scans and biopsy, which revealed that he has locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has no significant past medical history except for a history of mild hypertension which is managed with medications. He is married and lives with his wife and two adult children. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 26 with BP of 140/90. He is able to perform his activities of daily living without assistance. He has no history of HIV or hepatitis B or C. He is willing to travel to a foreign country if required for the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presents with a history of hoarseness and chronic cough for the past six months. She reports that her symptoms worsen at night and after eating. She also complains of a sore throat and a feeling of something stuck in her throat. She has tried over-the-counter remedies, but they have not provided any relief. She does not have any history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or drug abuse. She has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. Her physical examination is unremarkable, except for mild erythema and edema of the posterior pharynx. A laryngoscopy reveals moderate to severe reflux laryngitis with grade 3 arytenoid erythema. She is diagnosed with laryngitis associated with gastroesophageal reflux and is eligible for the clinical trial. She signs informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria, including having a confirmed diagnosis of gastroesophageal reflux by 24-hour pH impedance monitoring. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to protein pump inhibitors. She agrees to discontinue the use of any proton pump inhibitors or H2 receptor antagonists for seven days prior to the start of the study drug. She is enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Lansoprazole 30mg twice daily in the treatment of laryngitis associated with gastroesophageal reflux.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a BMI of 22.8 who is willing to participate in a clinical trial for the evaluation of endogenous markers for the assessment of CYP3A activity using metabolomics. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medication. He has no history of drug abuse and has never participated in any clinical trials within the last 60 days. The patient is willing to follow the study protocol and has provided written informed consent. He will be admitted to the Clinical Trials Center, Seoul National University Hospital on the day before dosing and will be overnight-fasted from 10 p.m. of Day -1. He will undergo scheduled procedures including clinical laboratory tests, electrocardiograms, and pharmacokinetic samplings. He will be discharged on Day 2 and will visit the Clinical Trials Center on Day 5-7 for ketoconazole administration. He will be admitted again on Day 7 for period 2 and will undergo scheduled procedures for period 2 (ketoconazole co-administration phase) and period 3 (rifampicin co-administration phase). The study participation will be terminated on the post-study visit (Day 30-32).

A 60-year-old male with a history of open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension presents to the ophthalmology clinic. Despite being on beta-blocker monotherapy for over 30 days, his intraocular pressure (IOP) has been difficult to control, with a mean baseline IOP of 20 mmHg in his right eye and 22 mmHg in his left eye. He has no known allergies to prostaglandin analogues or any component of the study medications. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes, and he is able to understand and sign the informed consent form. He has not had any ocular surgeries or procedures in the past year, and he is not currently taking any excluded medications. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if travoprost/timolol can provide better IOP control than his current beta-blocker medication.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy female who works as a nurse. She has no history of major medical conditions and is a nonsmoker. Her weight is 65 kg, with a BMI of 22.1 kg/m2. She has normal blood pressure, and her ECG is within normal limits. She is currently using hormonal contraception and is willing to continue using it throughout the study period. She has no history of allergies or hypersensitivity to medications. She has not received any live vaccines in the past four weeks and has not donated blood in the past eight weeks. She has not participated in any drug study in the past 60 days. She has no history of alcohol abuse or drug addiction. Her urine drug screen and alcohol breath test are negative. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to abstain from alcohol during the study period. She also agrees to use adequate contraception from screening until 90 days after the follow-up visit. She meets all the inclusion criteria and has none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 3-year-old girl who has been experiencing ear pain and difficulty hearing for the past few weeks. Her parents report that she had a cold a few weeks ago and since then, she has been pulling at her ears and complaining of discomfort. They have also noticed that she seems to be having difficulty understanding them when they speak to her. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of chronic pulmonary or cardiac diseases, immune deficiency, or allergic rhinitis. The patient's parents have agreed to participate in the study and have signed the written informed consent form. The patient will undergo a definite diagnosis of OME with symptoms and examination to confirm eligibility for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with myxoid liposarcoma in her left thigh 3 months ago. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis and was offered radiotherapy followed by surgery to remove the tumor. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Her family history is negative for cancer. Her physical examination reveals a palpable mass in her left thigh that measures 8 cm in diameter. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work, but is restricted in physically strenuous activity. Her lab studies show no significant abnormalities. She is interested in participating in clinical research studies and has provided a signed informed consent.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 3 years without success. She has a history of two previous IVF cycles with poor ovarian response. Her BMI is 24. She has no known allergies and is not diabetic. She has regular menstrual cycles and no history of pelvic infections or surgeries. She is willing to participate in the trial and has given written informed consent. She will be randomly assigned to either the study group or the control group. During the study, she will receive DHEA 25 mg t.d.s daily for 12 weeks before starting the IVF/ICSI cycle if she is in the study group. She will be monitored for ovarian response and will undergo oocyte retrieval and embryo transfer according to the study protocol. The primary outcome measure is the pregnancy rate, which will be assessed 2 weeks after embryo transfer.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing irregular bleeding for the last six months. She has a history of obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. She has been on hormone replacement therapy with estrogen for the last five years. She has not undergone any previous treatment for endometrial hypertrophy or cancer. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of endometrial cancer.

A 54-year-old male was diagnosed with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) last month. He is currently seeking treatment options and has been recommended to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the cost and effectiveness of sunitinib compared to interferon-alfa. He is willing to take part in the trial and has given his informed consent. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication for it. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a construction worker and exercises regularly to maintain his physical fitness. He has no known allergies or any other medical conditions.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has a family history of diabetes, with his father and grandfather both having the disease. He works as an office manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has been trying to manage his diabetes through diet and exercise, but his HbA1c levels have been consistently above 8.0%. He has never required insulin therapy. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is generally healthy and has a BMI of 24 kg/m^2. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. She does not smoke or use any illegal drugs. She has normal bowel movements and her last menstrual period was two weeks ago. She has a negative serum pregnancy test and is not currently breastfeeding. She has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of JNJ-72537634 compared with placebo.

35 y/o female with a BMI of 32 kg/m^2 and no significant past medical history. She is functionally ambulatory and available for an 8-hour visit to the Emory University Hospital Clinical Research Center. The patient reports no history of chronic diseases, hospitalizations, or current pregnancy. She has not taken any diabetic or lipid-lowering prescription medications in the past 12 months and does not have any active malignant neoplasms or autoimmune diseases. The patient has no history of tuberculosis, HIV, or other chronic infections and has not been diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes or any advanced renal disease. She also reports no recreational or prescription drug or alcohol abuse or any history of gastrointestinal diseases or intolerance to dietary fat. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to help improve the assessment of cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with a BMI in the obese range.

The patient is a 23-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent skin and lung infections for the past 5 years. She also has a history of eczema since childhood. She has been treated with antibiotics several times for her infections, but they keep coming back. She has a family history of similar symptoms in her mother and brother. Her most recent blood work showed elevated levels of immunoglobulin E (IgE) which is suggestive of Hyper IgE syndrome. Her doctor referred her to NIH for further evaluation and management. She is willing to participate in the study as she hopes to better understand her condition and find an effective treatment. She has no contraindications for IV contrast media or coronary CTA. She is mentally and socially stable and able to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with gastric cancer and is scheduled to undergo distal gastrectomy with Billroth II + Braun anastomosis. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The preoperative evaluation concluded that the patient is at clinical staging cT2N1M0. The patient has given consent to participate in this clinical trial, which aims to investigate the potential effect and superiority of antiperistaltic versus isoperistaltic Billroth II + Braun reconstruction in distal gastrectomy. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and there are no exclusion criteria present. The patient is informed of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and has consented to proceed.

A 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago and has completed her chemotherapy treatment. She has been experiencing incomplete hair regrowth and has been struggling with hair thinning and hair loss since the end of her chemotherapy. She is currently using a wig to cover her head, which makes her feel self-conscious and embarrassed. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her with her hair problems. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to the components of the topical lotion, CG428, and is physically and psychologically able to participate in the trial. She has not undergone any hair transplants or used any anti-hair-loss treatments or hair growth treatments.

A 55-year-old man presented at the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath during exercise, even with minimal exertion. He has no history of cardiac or lung disease, but he does have a family history of heart disease. His resting heart rate and blood pressure are within normal limits. His BMI is 30 kg/m². His echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 55%, which is within normal limits. His NTproBNP levels were 180 pg/ml. His pulmonary function tests showed no significant respiratory disease. His thyroid function tests were also normal. He is able to pedal during the cardiometabolic stress test.

32-year-old male diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 2 years ago with a history of recurrent flares requiring hospitalization. Currently presenting with moderate to severe disease activity with a Mayo score of 9 points, including bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. The patient has been on mesalamine and prednisone with no significant improvement in symptoms. The patient does not have any history of immunosuppression or foreign travel. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 56-year-old woman was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of severe community-acquired pneumonia. She has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, but her medications were discontinued upon admission. The patient was started on broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy as per the hospital protocol. Blood cultures were obtained, and the patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated due to respiratory failure. On day 3 of hospitalization, blood cultures came back positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae. The patient's condition improved, and she was extubated on day 7. However, the patient remained febrile, and her CRP levels remained elevated. The patient was randomized to the "PCR group" for the duration of antibiotic therapy. Serum CRP levels were monitored daily, and antibiotic therapy was discontinued when levels were below 35mg/L with clinical improvement. The patient was discharged on day 14 of hospitalization, with no evidence of recurrence of infection or isolation of multidrug-resistant bacteria.

52 yo F with history of ESRD secondary to IgA nephropathy who underwent deceased donor renal transplant in 2014. She initially had good graft function but developed biopsy-proven chronic active antibody-mediated rejection in 2017. Despite treatment with plasmapheresis, IVIG, and increased immunosuppression, she continues to have slowly declining renal function with a current estimated GFR of 28 mL/min. Recent DSA testing has shown persistent positivity to multiple HLA antigens. The patient is otherwise healthy and without significant comorbidities. She is interested in participating in clinical trials to try and improve her renal function and prevent the need for dialysis or re-transplantation.

A 58-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension is scheduled for an elective thoracic surgery that requires one lung ventilation with a left-sided double lumen tube. The patient has been diagnosed with lung cancer and is undergoing treatment for the past 6 months. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy with moderate success. He has not experienced any significant side effects from the treatment. He reports a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He also has a history of chronic bronchitis and recurrent pneumonia. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and has no known allergies. His physical status classification is ASA II. He has no history of pneumothorax, pleural effusion, emphysema or past history of pleurodesis. His pulmonary function test results are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who sustained a burn injury to her right arm and leg. The burn covers approximately 20% of her total body surface area. She is admitted to Children's Hospital Colorado for skin grafting procedure. She is accompanied by her parents who provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. She is otherwise healthy with no known allergies. She reports pain at the sites of the burns and is currently being managed with pain medication. The patient is cooperative and able to follow instructions. She is able to communicate her pain level using a pain scale. The patient and her parents are interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce her pain and improve wound healing.

A 52-year-old woman with a previous diagnosis of HER2-positive breast cancer presents with metastasis. She has previously received a taxane and trastuzumab for advanced/metastatic disease, and has undergone two lines of systemic cytotoxic therapy. Her biopsy-confirmed solid malignancy has progressed after receiving at least one line of standard/approved therapy in the advanced setting. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. Her absolute neutrophil count is greater than or equal to 1,500/mm3, platelet count is greater than or equal to 100,000/mm3, and hemoglobin is greater than or equal to 9.0 g/dL with no blood transfusion in the past 28 days. Her total bilirubin is less than or equal to 1.5 x the upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are less than or equal to 3.0 x ULN (or less than or equal to 5.0 x ULN in the presence of liver metastases), and serum creatinine is within normal institutional limits or creatinine clearance is greater than or equal to 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 for patients with serum creatinine levels above institutional ULN. She has undergone resolution of all acute toxic effects of prior therapy and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 70 year old male who has been experiencing a gradual loss of vision in his left eye over the past 3 months. His best corrected visual acuity on the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) chart is between 20/40 and 20/200 (0.5 - 0.1). He has not received any treatment with IGIV within the last 3 months prior to the run-in. He has not previously received photodynamic therapy (PDT), vitrectomy, transpupillary thermotherapy (TTT), or any specific pre-treatment of choroidal neovascularization (CNV). There is no subfoveal blood in the study eye if ≥ 1/2 disc diameter as measured by slit lamp during the run-in period. The patient has no history of anaphylaxis or severe systemic response to immunoglobulin or with a blood product. He does not have cardiac insufficiency (NYHA III/IV), cardiomyopathy, significant cardiac dysrhythmia requiring treatment, unstable or advanced ischemic heart disease, or severe or uncontrolled hypertension (diastolic > 95 mmHg or systolic >170 mmHg). The patient is male, therefore, there are no concerns about pregnancy or contraception. His serum creatinine levels are normal and he does not have known selective immunoglobulin A (IgA) deficiency. He is not currently on any other investigational drugs and does not have conditions whose symptoms and effects could alter protein catabolism and/or immunoglobulin (IgG) utilization. He does not have a known hypercoagulable state or history of thromboembolic events, and he is not on continuous systemic steroid treatment. The patient is mentally competent and able to give informed consent. He has no history of diabetes mellitus requiring drug treatment. He does not have any acute or known ocular diseases such as glaucoma, arterial or venous occlusions, or acute ischemic optic-neuropathy, and his visual acuity is not impaired due to opacities in the lens or vitreous.

72-year-old female with a history of hypertension, osteoarthritis, and depression presents with severe fear of falling. The patient has experienced multiple falls in the past, resulting in a decreased sense of confidence and avoidance of activities she used to enjoy. Despite efforts to increase her physical activity, the patient finds herself limiting her movements and engaging in sedentary behavior due to her fear. She reports feeling socially isolated and depressed as a result. The patient has no recent history of substance abuse and has not been diagnosed with any psychotic disorder or bipolar disorder. She lives alone in a single-story home and has a phone. The patient's primary care provider has approved her participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of chronic stable angina and a recent episode of non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. He has undergone coronary angiography which revealed a significant stenosis in the left anterior descending artery. The patient is a suitable candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug eluting stent, in accordance with the applicable guidelines. He does not have unprotected left main disease or planned PCI of three vessel disease. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in this post-approval study.

53 yo M with a history of hypertension for 15 years, despite being on multiple antihypertensive medications, including lisinopril, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide. His average office blood pressure readings have been consistently above 160/90 mmHg despite being on this medication regimen. His blood pressure readings at home, taken twice daily, are also high, with an average reading of 170/100 mmHg. He has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or stroke. He is a non-smoker and his BMI is 31. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new device that may help control his blood pressure.

A 16-year-old male diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) based on clinical symptoms, laboratory, and colonoscopic findings, including histopathologic results of the intestinal mucosa. The patient has been on immunomodulator therapy (azathioprine) for the past 6 months, but his symptoms have not improved. He has frequent diarrhea (5-6 times/day) with visible blood and mucus. He also complains of abdominal pain, cramping, and fatigue. The patient's Pediatric Ulcerative Colitis Activity Index (PUCAI) score is 30, indicating mild activity. The patient has been enema trained and is willing to undergo FMT therapy. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of allergies, immunodeficiency, HIV/AIDS, or bone marrow transplantation. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male healthcare worker with no history of COVID-19 infection presents for the clinical trial. He has been vaccinated with the Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2 vaccine and is interested in knowing more about his mucosal immunity against SARS-CoV-2. He has no known allergies and is in good health. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no history of neck breathing or any nasopharyngeal or oropharyngeal anomalies that would prevent saliva collection using Salivette.

A 64-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with locally recurrent urinary tract cancer. He has undergone surgical resection and adjuvant radiation therapy. Three years later, he was diagnosed with metastatic urothelial carcinoma. He has been experiencing lower back pain and hematuria. He is currently on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain management. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. He is married with three grown children. He is an active member of his community and enjoys playing golf with his friends. He reports feeling fatigued and has lost some weight in the last few months. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance research on urinary tract cancer.

The patient is a 16-year-old adolescent who presented to the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario after experiencing passive suicidal ideations for the past two weeks. The patient reports feeling hopeless and helpless and has been struggling with maintaining familial relationships. The patient's caregivers are a mother and father who are both committed to attending the majority of the six sessions of the brief group intervention. The patient has no history of suicidal attempts or gestures and is not currently receiving mental health services. The patient has no major substance abuse issues or behavioral problems and is able to commit to attending the majority of the sessions.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Barrett's mucosa with high grade dysplasia. He presented with dysphagia and discomfort during swallowing. Gastroscopy revealed the presence of a short segment of approximately 2cm circumferential disease in the oesophagus. Biopsies confirmed high grade dysplasia. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently on a proton pump inhibitor for reflux symptoms. He is able to provide informed consent and is eligible for the study as he meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 14-year-old girl named Lily was diagnosed with stage 4 neuroblastoma with MYCN amplification. She underwent a biopsy procedure, and a cryopreserved tumour sample was collected at the time of diagnosis.
