Lily's parents provided written informed consent for her participation in the study, and she is affiliated with a social security scheme. She is within the eligibility criteria of the MICCHADO study and has been enrolled in cohort 1. Currently, she is undergoing treatment for her cancer and is being monitored closely.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who has been experiencing snoring and restless sleep for the past few months. She often wakes up feeling tired and irritable, and her parents have noticed that she has difficulty concentrating during the day. She has no known medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. The patient is accompanied by her parents who are concerned about her sleep and overall wellbeing. The ENT specialist has recommended conducting a ventilatory polygraph to investigate the possibility of obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS). The family has agreed to participate in the study to help evaluate the feasibility of pediatric RP in an ENT department routine practice and to contribute to the evaluation of the automatic signal analysis in children.

A 43-year-old male who is admitted to the ICU due to respiratory failure and is being supported with mechanical ventilation. The patient has been diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) according to the 2012 Berlin Criteria. The patient is currently receiving parenteral nutrition (PN) and/or enteral nutrition (EN) to meet their daily caloric needs. The patient is expected to have an ICU stay longer than 72 hours. The patient's basic demographic data will be collected, as well as daily caloric intake, days of ICU stay, days of hospital stay, hospital mortality, and days of ventilator use. The patient will be enrolled in the study to determine the effect of caloric supplement on clinical outcomes in acute lung injury patients.

A 60-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastases. He has been surgically castrated and has a serum testosterone level of ≤ 50 ng/dL. He has metastatic disease in bone documented on bone scan or in soft tissue documented on CT/MRI scan. He has progressive disease at study entry in the setting of medical or surgical castration as defined by PSA progression, soft tissue disease progression, or bone disease progression. He has not been treated with second-generation androgen receptor inhibitors, a PARP inhibitor, cyclophosphamide, or mitoxantrone for prostate cancer. He has not received platinum-based chemotherapy within 6 months prior to Day 1, nor has he experienced disease progression on platinum-based therapy within 6 months. He has not been treated with opioids for pain related to either primary prostate cancer or metastasis within 28 days prior to Day 1. He has not used potent P-gp inhibitors within 7 days prior to Day 1, nor has he undergone major surgery within 2 weeks before Day 1 or palliative localized radiation therapy within 3 weeks before randomization. He has an ECOG performance status of ≤ 1 and a life expectancy of ≥ 12 months. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He has no known history of myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, or prior malignancy, except carcinoma in situ or non-melanoma skin cancer, Stage 0 or Stage 1 cancer <3 years before randomization that has a remote probability of recurrence or progression in the opinion of the investigator.  He is able to provide a personally signed and dated informed consent document.

A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago is seeking treatment for progression of her disease. She has previously received anti-estrogen treatment and adjuvant therapy. She has completed chemotherapy and radiotherapy with no adverse effects. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her current medications include lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, both taken once daily. She has no known allergies. She has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living without difficulty. She has no history of adrenal insufficiency or Cushing's syndrome. She has measurable lesions on imaging scans and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of letrozole 2.5 mg/day monotherapy as second-line endocrine therapy for advanced breast cancer.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient recruitment as it does not involve any intervention or treatment. It is a prospective study aiming to determine the incidence and clinical and molecular epidemiology of Staphylococcus lugdunensis infections in hospitalized patients. Therefore, patient descriptions are not required for this trial.

A 45-year-old woman with biopsy-proven idiopathic membranous nephropathy presenting with nephrotic syndrome, with a proteinuria of 4.5 g/day and serum albumin of 25 g/l. She has a normal eGFR of 77 ml/min, but beta-2-microglobulin excretion is above 500 ng/min, indicating a high risk for renal failure. The patient has a strong desire for future family expansion and is therefore considered a relative contra-indication for cyclophosphamide treatment. She has not received cyclophosphamide treatment before and does not display intolerance to it. The patient has no clinical, biochemical, or histological signs of any underlying systemic diseases and has no current infectious diseases or active gastric or duodenal ulcers. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraceptives. The patient has no clinical signs of renal vein thrombosis and does not have asthma or any allergic conditions or hypersensitivity reactions. She has not had an allergic reaction to synthetic ACTH in the past.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer through mammography and ultrasound. She underwent a wide local excision surgery to remove the tumor and sentinel lymph node biopsy. The biopsy results showed that the tumor was invasive adenocarcinoma, and there were no lymph node metastases. She has not received any neoadjuvant chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, or radiotherapy before the surgery. She has no history of any other malignant tumors. She is in good physical condition, with an ECOG performance scale of 0. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the effectiveness of an additional boost dose to the tumor bed in reducing local recurrence rate and improving cosmetic outcomes. She has also agreed to provide frozen tumor material and blood samples for genetic and protein profiling.

62 year-old male with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease presents to the hospital with shortness of breath and fatigue. He reports experiencing mild chest pain over the past few days. On admission, he is found to have systolic heart failure with an ejection fraction of 25%. He is started on appropriate medical management including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta blockers. The patient is informed about the PREMEDIC observational study and is willing to participate. During his hospital stay, health data will be collected to evaluate the concordance between his actual patient management and the therapeutic proposals from a medical algorithmic decision support software. The patient is 18 years or older and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained a mild to moderate sprain in his left ankle while playing basketball two days ago. He reports experiencing moderate pain and swelling in the affected area, and has been advised by his primary care physician to rest, ice, compress and elevate his ankle. He is not currently taking any pain medication or undergoing any other treatments for his injury. The patient has no known allergies or sensitivities to soy lecithin or soy lecithin-containing products, and is not currently undergoing treatment for chronic pain or severe systemic disease. He is willing to discontinue any pain medication or treatments not provided as part of the study, and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive a topical cream formulation consisting of 10% ketoprofen for the local treatment of pain associated with his acute soft tissue injury.

A 28-year-old woman presented to the clinic with complaints of persistent sadness, anxiety, and low mood for the past 6 months. She is a teacher and has been experiencing stress and burnout due to work. She has been prescribed antidepressants and cognitive-behavioral therapy, but she is still struggling with her symptoms. She has a history of depression and anxiety disorder, and she scores 18 on the DASS-21 depression subscale and 10 on the DASS-21 anxiety subscale. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence and reports occasional cannabis use, less than once a month. She has normal vision, and she is right-handed. She has no history of neurological disease, head trauma, or brain surgery. She practices yoga for 30 minutes a day but has no experience with mindfulness meditation. Her BMI is 23.5, and she weighs 137 lbs. She is interested in participating in the MindfulPCfMRI study to explore the effect of mindfulness training on her brain function and self-regulation ability.

This clinical trial does not involve enrolling patients or administering any interventions. It is a retrospective study that will examine the records of patients who underwent anesthesia and surgery at a tertiary hospital between 2010 and 2014 and subsequently died in the hospital. Therefore, no patient description is required.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of systemic scleroderma (SSc) for the past 8 years. She has recently been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. Her medical history includes hypertension and hypothyroidism, both well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker, and has no history of exposure to environmental toxins or occupational exposures. She reports no recent travel history. She is currently being followed up at AP-HM for SSc. Physical examination reveals bilateral basal fine crackles and a mildly elevated jugular venous pressure. Her oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Pulmonary function tests reveal a restrictive pattern with a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 60% predicted and a diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of 52% predicted. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest shows findings consistent with interstitial lung disease (ILD). Given her history and symptoms, she is a candidate for participating in the clinical trial evaluating the serum soluble fractalkine as a biomarker of pulmonary fibrosis in systemic sclerosis.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with CD20+ follicular lymphoma. She has not yet received any treatment for the condition. Imaging tests have revealed Stage III disease with multiple lymph nodes affected in the abdomen and pelvis. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes confirmed the diagnosis of CD20+ follicular lymphoma. The patient has no history of allergies and has not received any monoclonal antibody therapy in the past. She has not undergone an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant and does not have chronic hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has an ECOG performance status of 1.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of type-2 diabetes for the past 5 years. She has been taking aspirin for the past 12 months to prevent any complications of diabetes. She reports snoring and restless sleep at night. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. She does not smoke and drinks one glass of wine per week. Her BMI is 32, and she has no history of cardiovascular events or inflammatory disease. She is not currently participating in any other studies and has medical care insurance. She has not had any changes in her medications in the past 10 days. She is able to participate as an ambulatory patient.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has never undergone colorectal cancer screening. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis for which she takes medication. She has no history of cancer or colorectal cancer in her family. She is an English-speaking individual who uses the internet frequently. She understands the importance of colorectal cancer screening but has not undergone the test due to a lack of awareness and understanding of the screening process. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about her risk for colorectal cancer and the benefits of colorectal cancer screening. She has no cognitive or physical impairments that would prevent her from participating in online surveys and following the study protocol. She is willing to provide informed consent and follow-up with the study requirements.

A 25-year-old African American man diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at the age of 3 is seeking to participate in a clinical trial to further understand priapism, a medical issue that he has experienced in the past. The patient reports experiencing priapism episodes several times over the past year, lasting up to 6 hours and causing him severe pain, discomfort and embarrassment. He currently takes hydroxyurea to manage his sickle cell disease and has undergone chronic transfusion in the past. The patient is able to communicate effectively with the interviewer and is eager to participate in the study to help advance the understanding and treatment of priapism in men with sickle cell disease.

A 25 yo male who is in good health and physically active. He has no history of anemia, inflammation, or diabetes. He has not had any muscle injuries in the lower limbs or spine in the previous six months, and has not experienced any musculoskeletal injury during the study. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of phototherapy using different light sources (laser and LED) during combined training on clinical, functional, and psychological outcomes and vascular endothelial growth factor. He is willing to undergo six weeks of combined training (sprints and squats) and a new six-week training period with adjusted loads. He agrees to receive the recovery strategy related to the group to which he belongs and is willing to have active or placebo phototherapy applied by a trained therapist between sprints and squats, bilaterally to six sites of the quadriceps in direct contact with the skin. He understands that the dosage applied will be 30J per site and that he will need to participate in clinical, functional, and psychological outcome measurements.

Patient is a 45yo male who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 6 months ago based on the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 1988 revised criteria. The patient presents with a history of joint pain, swelling, and stiffness in both hands and wrists. The patient has been taking NSAIDs and DMARDs for the past 3 months and has not required any dose adjustments during this time period. The patient has no history of malignancy or stem cell transplantation. The patient's Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) is less than or equal to 30 at the baseline visit. The patient is not on >7.5 mg prednisone a day nor has received any intra-articular corticosteroid injections during the previous 30 days. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical research study involving the evaluation of another investigational drug within 90 days of entry into this study. The patient is not pregnant as confirmed by a negative urine pregnancy test at the randomization visit. The patient is willing to use effective means of contraception for the treatment phase of the trial and for 90 days thereafter. The patient has not used "fish oil" within the previous 4 weeks of the baseline visit. The patient's serum creatinine level is within normal range. The patient has an 1(II) IFN value of at least 100% of the PBS IFN value within 1 month or less prior to the baseline and has shown at least a 25% reduction in APL A12 + 1(II) IFN from 1(II) IFN concentration. The patient has consented to participate in the study and is willing to discontinue all "herbal remedies" as described in the protocol.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman living in a rural area of Masindi, Uganda. She is in her first pregnancy and has just reached 24 weeks of gestation. She has not had any complications so far and has been attending antenatal care at the local health center. She is excited but also anxious about the upcoming birth of her child. She has heard about a new program that combines scheduled home visits by Community Health Workers (Village Health Teams) with mobile phone consultations to improve newborn care. She is interested in participating in the program and hopes to learn more about caring for her baby. She lives with her husband and two other family members in a small house with no running water or electricity. They have a small farm and rely on subsistence farming for their livelihood. She is looking forward to the VHT visits and hopes to receive useful information and support for a healthy pregnancy and safe delivery.

A 55-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with brain metastases. She has undergone chemotherapy as the first line treatment for brain metastasis. Her estimated survival period is greater than 12 weeks, and her ECOG score is less than 2. She is willing to participate in a research study that aims to test the cerebrospinal fluid, blood and tissue by the latest second-generation sequencing technology at different time points, to dynamically monitor the gene mutation status of cerebrospinal fluid, blood and tissue, to explore the role of cerebrospinal fluid biopsy in the diagnosis and treatment of non-small cell lung cancer with brain metastases. She has enough tissue specimens for lung cancer related gene detection, and there is at least one evaluable lesion based on the criteria of RECIST 1.1. She is tolerable for lumbar puncture with no contraindication and is able to comply with the research requirements and follow-up procedures. She has signed the informed consent prior to the beginning of any substantive test procedure.

A 45-year-old male civil servant, who works in the research institution located in São Paulo, is interested in participating in a study investigating the relationship between coffee consumption and subclinical atherosclerosis. He has no prior history of cardiovascular disease and has not been diagnosed with any chronic condition. He is a coffee enthusiast and consumes at least 3 cups of coffee per day. He is willing to undergo a computed tomographic (CT) examination to quantify coronary artery calcium (CAC) and provide dietary data through a validated food frequency questionnaire. He understands the study's potential risks and benefits and has signed a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 24-year-old female who has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) according to the Rotterdam Criteria 2003. She has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles, acne, and weight gain. She has not been taking any medication for PCOS or any other condition. She is a non-smoker and is physically able to perform exercise. Her BMI is 27 kg/m², and she has a waist circumference of 90 cm. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her cardiometabolic profile and reduce her risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. She currently engages in light physical activity, such as walking, for about 30 minutes per day, 3-4 times per week. She is fluent in English and meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study. Her family history is negative for cardiovascular disease or other metabolic disorders.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled for a cesarean delivery due to hypertension and gestational diabetes. Her pre-pregnancy BMI was 32. She has a history of previous cesarean deliveries and is considered high-risk for post-operative wound complications. The patient is aware of the study and consents to participate. She will be randomly assigned to either the negative pressure wound therapy group or the standard dressing group. The wound suction device will be placed over her cesarean incision after surgery and kept in place for 72 hours. The patient will be closely monitored for any signs of wound infection or complications.

The patient is a 32-year-old healthy male who works in a melamine manufacturing facility. He has been working in the facility for the past 3 years and has not experienced any health problems so far. He has no history of chronic diseases or any hormonal treatment. He has a normal BMI and exercises regularly. He is willing to participate in the study to help reduce the ambient melamine exposure in the workplace and prevent any potential health problems. He is able to collect his urine samples during mornings and afternoons for one week before and one week after the intervention. He is also willing to provide blood samples on Fridays morning and allow workplace air samples to be taken for 5 consecutive days. He understands that the study will continue to monitor his melamine exposure and collect blood samples on 12th and 24th month intervals after the intervention. He meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 42-year-old man was diagnosed with retroperitoneal soft-tissue sarcoma. He had no previous history of cancer or radiation therapy. He has a Karnofsky index of 80% and is in good overall health. He works as a construction worker and exercises regularly. He has no metal implants in the area of the sarcoma and is not participating in any other clinical trial. He has no active medical implants and is not pregnant. He is willing to participate in the study and has completed the patient information and written consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old HIV-positive man who has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 12 years. He has had undetectable viral load for the past 10 years, with a CD4+ count of 700 cells/µL. He has no history of AIDS-defining events and no evidence of residual viremia for the past 5 years. He has expressed interest in pausing his ART and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the frequency of spontaneous control of viral replication after ART pausing for up to 12 months. He is a non-smoker with no significant medical history, including no diagnosis of cancer or major adverse cardiac events. He has normal kidney function and no history of HIV-related thrombocytopenia. He is not currently using any experimental therapy and has not used any HIV vaccine in the past. He is willing to adhere to the study requirements and is not currently using drugs or alcohol.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who has no known medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol on a regular basis. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, and his weight is within the acceptable limit of 132 kg. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, cancer, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, hematological, or neurological disorders. He has normal clinical laboratory test results and has a systolic blood pressure of 125 mm Hg and a diastolic blood pressure of 80 mm Hg. He has no history of drug abuse and has tested negative for drugs and alcohol. He is willing to follow all study procedures and is able to make himself available for the duration of the study. He has given written informed consent prior to any study procedures being performed.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer that has metastasized to the lungs. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has continued to progress. She has a solid tumor in her right lung that is greater than 2 cm in diameter. She has also had a biopsy of the tumor to confirm the presence of CXCR4 expression. She is not pregnant or lactating and has normal blood cell counts. She has not received any imaging agents with a radioisotope or labeled molecule in the past 10 half-lives. She does not have a history of severe claustrophobia and weighs less than 325 pounds. She has not participated in any other trials involving the infusion of radioactive isotopes/molecules for research purposes or plerixafor. She is willing to use 2 forms of contraception 3 weeks prior to the study start and 1 month after the administration of 64Cu-plerixafor. She has a Karnofsky Performance Scale Index (KPSI) of at least 70.

The patient is a 10-year-old child diagnosed with neonatal diabetes shortly after birth. Genetic testing confirmed that the child has a mutation in one of the subunits of potassium channels. The child is currently being treated with glibenclamide pills, but the dosage is too high for the child's age and weight. The child has difficulty swallowing pills and the pills need to be crushed and diluted in water before administration, which is not the recommended method of administration. The child has no known allergies to sulfonylureas or other antidiabetic or antibiotic sulfamides. The child's parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the safety and effectiveness of a new oral solution of glibenclamide (Glinbentek) developed specifically for pediatric patients. The child is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian man who has been diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He is currently using insulin to manage his diabetes. He reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia and difficulty adhering to his medication regimen. He owns a cell phone and has access to the internet. He has a blood sugar monitor and supplies. His recent HbA1c reading was 8.5%. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological conditions that might impair his ability to participate in the study. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no active cancer other than basal cell carcinoma or cervical or breast cancer in situ. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident within the last 6 months. He has no active infection or serious underlying medical conditions that would impair his ability to participate in the trial. He is able to read and understand the informed consent form and provide written consent. He has no plans to move over the 6-month period of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is 34 weeks pregnant and scheduled for a planned cesarean delivery due to a history of a previous cesarean delivery. She has a history of opioid addiction and is currently in recovery. She has been clean for 18 months and attends regular counseling sessions. She experiences occasional back pain due to the added pressure of pregnancy on her spine. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the use of Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) therapy for pain management after cesarean delivery. She is willing to learn how to use the TENS device and follow the study protocol.

A 35 yo F with a history of schizophrenia presents with acute symptoms of auditory hallucinations and delusions. She has been on multiple antipsychotic medications in the past, but none have been effective in managing her symptoms. She has a total PANSS score of 95 at the screening test. She does not have any history of substance-related disorder or diabetes mellitus. She is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of ER OROS Paliperidone compared to placebo and olanzapine. She understands the nature of the study and has given her written consent to participate. She is currently an outpatient, but may require hospitalization in the future if her symptoms worsen.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction presented with chest discomfort and was diagnosed with multi-vessel coronary artery disease. He was scheduled for elective first-time coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. He denied any allergies to medications and had no history of opioid abuse. His medications included aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He had a creatinine level of 1.1 mg/dL and liver function tests within the normal range. His ejection fraction was 50% on echocardiogram. His electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm with no signs of arrhythmia or prolonged QT interval. He did not require oxygen therapy and had not used inotropic agents or intra-aortic balloon pump to maintain hemodynamic stability. He had no history of pulmonary disease. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of preoperative oral methadone in reducing postoperative pain for patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

The patient is a 26-year-old female with a history of mild to moderate asthma for the past 2 years. She experiences occasional shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing, especially during exercise or exposure to allergens. She does not smoke and has no history of other respiratory diseases. She is not currently taking any systemic corticosteroids or leukotriene modifiers. Her FEV1 is 80% predicted and her AMP challenge PC20FEV1 is 45 mg/mL. She is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. She has not used any investigational drug in the past 30 days. She is willing to substitute her pre-study prescribed asthma medication for study medication and able to attend all study visits. She has satisfactory technique in using the pMDI and is willing to keep a daily diary of her symptoms and medication use. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35 year old woman was diagnosed with a bone tumor in her right femur. She underwent a biopsy and was placed on a chemotherapy treatment protocol at the Rizzoli Orthopedic Institute. She is currently in her third round of chemotherapy and has been experiencing fatigue, which has been affecting her quality of life. She reports feeling tired all the time, having difficulty with daily activities, and feeling unmotivated. She also reports experiencing some pain in the affected area. She speaks fluent Italian and is willing to participate in the study. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage III melanoma on his right arm two years ago. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and was then treated with ipilimumab (3mg/kg) as an induction therapy. The patient had a partial response to the treatment and remained stable for 6 months. However, the disease progressed despite the initial treatment and he is now experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss. The patient has not undergone any other cancer treatments since completing the ipilimumab induction therapy. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are both well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only socially. The patient has no known allergies to medications. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass on his right arm measuring approximately 4 cm in diameter. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore additional treatment options for his advanced melanoma.

A 6-year-old girl was diagnosed with CDKL5 Deficiency Disorder (CDD) when she was 3 years old. She has been on anti-seizure medication since her diagnosis, but still experiences up to 8 convulsive seizures per month. She lives with her parents and two older siblings in a rural area. She attends school and has an Individualized Education Plan (IEP) due to her developmental delay. She is nonverbal but communicates with her family and teachers through gestures and a communication device. Her medical history is significant for mild asthma that is well controlled with medication. She has never had any heart or neurological problems. Her parents are willing to participate in the trial and have given their consent.

A 28-year-old healthy male came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for DBPR108. He works as a software developer and has no underlying disease. He is married for 2 years and uses condoms as a contraceptive method. He has a body weight of 75 kg and a body mass index (BMI) of 23.4 kg/m2. He is able to provide written informed consent and willing to comply with the study protocol procedures and restrictions. He has no history of alcohol abuse or smoking. He has not donated blood or participated in another clinical study within the past 8 weeks. He has not used any prescription or non-prescription medication, herbal remedies, vitamins or minerals within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives of the drug, whichever is longer, prior to dosing until end of study. He has no history or presence of any disease or condition known to interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. He is not a smoker and has not used nicotine-containing products within the last 6 months prior to the screening for the current study.

67F with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral arterial disease (PAD) with prior endovascular intervention to the left superficial femoral artery (SFA) and right below-the-knee (BTK) artery. The patient presents with complaints of rest pain in the right foot and has been found to have significant stenosis in the right SFA and BTK artery on imaging. The patient is currently on aspirin 81 mg daily. The patient has no known allergies to aspirin or clopidogrel. The patient is estimated to have a survival of at least 1 year, has a platelet count of 200,000 mm3, and a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. The patient has no planned surgeries or procedures in the next 12 months.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. He has been taking donepezil for the past 6 months and has been on a stable dose for the past 4 months. He lives at home with his wife who serves as his primary caregiver. He is fluent in the language in which the standardized tests will be administered. He has no other significant medical conditions and is expected to live for at least 2 more years. He has not received any previous anti-amyloid or vaccine treatment for Alzheimer's disease and has not been exposed to 3APS before. He is able to swallow pills without difficulty. He has provided signed informed consent along with his wife who will also be involved in his care throughout the study.

57-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C and cirrhosis was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient is asymptomatic and has no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. Imaging studies revealed a solitary, 5 cm lesion in the right lobe of the liver with no evidence of extrahepatic spread. Laboratory studies showed Child-Pugh A liver function with normal bilirubin and albumin levels. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has not received any prior systemic therapy for HCC or any immunotherapy treatment. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate. The patient is suitable for TACE therapy as assessed by the investigators. The patient has signed the informed consent document and is ready to begin treatment with tislelizumab combined with conventional TACE.

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of hypertension for the past 2 years. The hypertension was difficult to control with multiple medications, and she was referred to an endocrinologist for further evaluation. She reports feeling tired and weak with frequent headaches. Physical examination reveals no significant findings except for elevated blood pressure. Laboratory evaluation reveals hypokalemia and elevated aldosterone to renin ratio. She undergoes imaging studies, which reveal a unilateral adrenal mass. She is diagnosed with primary aldosteronism and is referred for surgery. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the subtype of her aldosteronism and to compare the long-term outcomes of different procedures. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no history of malignant tumors, severe heart disease, or other conditions that would exclude her from participating. She is willing to undergo AVS or unilateral adrenalectomy and has no allergy to ACTH.

The patient is a 25-year-old female to male transgender individual who has been experiencing gender dysphoria since adolescence. They are in good health with no history of serious illness or mental disorder. They do not take any medications or supplements regularly, and they do not smoke or drink alcohol. They have no known allergies or infectious diseases. They are proficient in Swedish and have no language difficulties. They are interested in participating in the study and want to receive hormone replacement therapy to help align their physical body with their gender identity. They have been cleared by their healthcare provider to participate in the study and have no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes type 1. They understand the risks and benefits of the study and have given their informed consent to participate.

A 62-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with colon cancer during a routine colonoscopy. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on medication for these conditions and his blood pressure and blood sugar levels are controlled. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and constipation for the past few months. His CT scan showed a mass in the sigmoid colon with no evidence of lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. He is scheduled for an elective colorectal surgery as part of his cancer treatment. He has no pre-existing chronic pain, is not taking any medication that may interfere with pain, and has no significant psychiatric disorders. He does not have any hepatic or renal impairment, convulsive conditions, autoimmune disorders, or taking any antiarrhythmic drugs.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been struggling with obesity and metabolic syndrome for the past few years. Despite trying different diets and exercise regimens, she has been unable to lose weight and improve her metabolic parameters. She has a BMI of 33 and has noticed an increase in her blood glucose and triglyceride levels. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes or hypertension, but her blood pressure is borderline high. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for her condition. After undergoing screening tests to confirm eligibility, she will receive a fecal microbial transplant using a pill form from a lean donor. She will also be given a variety of fiber supplements, including resistant starch type 4, acacia gum, and soluble corn fiber, for a period of 6 weeks. The effects on her metabolic parameters, weight, and dietary intake will be followed, and her microbial composition will be measured in stool samples. The primary objective of the study is to determine if FMT combined with fiber supplementation has a clinically significant effect on metabolic outcomes in obese individuals with metabolic syndrome. This is a Phase II clinical trial with a single center at the University of Alberta, and the study duration is 12 weeks. The patient must be between the ages of 18-64, have a BMI of greater than 30, and have a fluctuation of total body weight over the last 6 months of less than 10%. She must also have a fasting plasma glucose level of greater than 5.6 mmol/L or Hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%, with at least one of the following criteria: fasting triglyceride ≥1.7 mmol/L, HDL cholesterol <1.03 mmol/L in males or <1.29 mmol/L in females, or an established diagnosis of hypertension or systolic blood pressure ≥130 or diastolic blood pressure ≥85 mmHg. The patient must not have a systolic blood pressure ≥180 or diastolic blood pressure ≥110 mmHg at screening, triglyceride ≥6 mmol/L, active substance abuse or excessive alcohol consumption, or a history of oropharyngeal or significant esophageal dysphagia, inflammatory bowel disease, colon cancer, or colonic polyps with high-grade dysplasia.

45 yo woman with a history of metastatic colorectal cancer who has relapsed after standard of care treatment is being evaluated for a first-in-human study of SYN004, a monoclonal antibody that binds to the EGF receptor on cancer cells. The patient has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but her disease has progressed despite treatment. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient has measurable non-irradiated sites of disease according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. She has adequate bone marrow, liver, renal, and cardiac function. The patient has no active autoimmune disease or immune deficiency. She has not received treatment with a monoclonal antibody or chemotherapy within 4 weeks of enrollment. The patient has no active infections or history of cerebrovascular accident, transient ischemic attack, or subarachnoid hemorrhage within 6 months prior to screening. She has no history of interstitial lung disease or active, non-infectious pneumonitis. The patient has provided written informed consent and has agreed to stay in contact with the study site for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently using medication to manage his symptoms. He has had COPD for the past 5 years and has noticed a decline in his ability to perform daily activities due to shortness of breath and fatigue. The patient has a history of smoking and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He is generally able to manage his symptoms with medication, but is interested in participating in a study that aims to prevent COPD-related disability. The patient is a member of a large regional health maintenance organization and is willing to undergo a detailed physical assessment to measure his respiratory impairment and functional limitation. He is also willing to participate in structured telephone interviews to assess his disability outcomes at baseline and 18-month prospective follow-up. The patient is interested in learning about the modulating effects of specific risk and protective factors on the progression from functional limitation to COPD-related disability.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with CD19-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has gone through first-line and second-line treatments but failed to achieve complete remission. She has had a stem cell transplantation more than a year ago, but the disease has recurred. The patient is experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in her neck, underarms, and groin. She has a good appetite and is able to perform daily activities with moderate difficulty. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history except hypertension treated with medication. She is currently taking amlodipine and lisinopril, and they are well-controlled. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive CD19 CAR-T therapy.

The patient is a 34-year-old man who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He is undergoing treatment at the hospital of Nancy and has been scheduled for allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HLA matched donor). He will receive a graft of peripheral blood stem cells and GVHD prophylaxis by ciclosporin and antilymphocyte serum +/- mycophenolate mofetil or methotrexate. The patient has no history of HIV, HBV or HCV. The study aims to investigate the effects of intestinal microbiota changes and early post-transplant immune reconstitution on patients like him. The study hypothesizes that variation of some bacterial taxa may influence post-transplant immune reconstitution, particularly invariant Natural Killer T cells. The patient will be asked to participate in the study to simultaneously explore intestinal microbiota changes and early post-transplant immune reconstitution, and to correlate biological data with clinical data such as antibiotics use, stress level, and GVHD. This will be a preliminary (proof of concept), monocentric, interventional, prospective, non-randomized, and analytic trial.

A 50 year old woman diagnosed with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ genotype) with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and frequent respiratory infections. She is currently not receiving augmentation therapy. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is a former smoker and has a 20 pack-year smoking history. She has undergone a hysterectomy and cholecystectomy in the past. She is currently on inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids for her COPD. She is interested in participating in the study to gain a better understanding of her condition and potentially contribute to the development of new treatments.

A 56-year-old female presents with a history of memory loss and difficulty with daily activities. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease after undergoing a series of cognitive and neurological tests. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with amlodipine. She has no history of autoimmune disorders, allergic or anaphylactic reactions. She is an alert female with no acute distress. Her BP: 140/85, HR: 72/min and BMI: 29. Her neurological exam is consistent with Alzheimer's disease, including decreased attention span, impaired memory, and difficulty with language and spatial orientation. The Mini-mental status exam score is 22 and the Rosen-Modified Hachinski Ischemia Score is 3. MRI shows no cortical infarct, micro hemorrhage, multiple white matter lacunes, or extensive white matter abnormalities.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who works in an office as an administrative assistant. She spends most of her workday sitting and has noticed that she has gained weight and her blood sugar levels have been higher than usual. She has a BMI of 30 and her HbA1c level is 6.5%. She does not smoke and has no history of foot or lower limb injuries or serious medical issues. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help her improve her metabolic health. She has not taken any medication to control her high blood pressure or blood glucose, nor is she on any hormone replacement therapy or corticosteroids. She has not used any prebiotics, probiotics or antibiotics in the last three months, nor does she have any serious food allergies or restrictions. She is willing to commit to regular intervals of standing and light-intensity physical activity as part of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man scheduled for elective unilateral hand surgery due to carpal tunnel syndrome. The patient has a history of mild hypertension and has been on amlodipine for the past six months. He denies any history of allergies, psychiatric illness or chronic opioid use. His body mass index is within normal limits. He has never had surgery before and is eager to learn about the different pain management options available to him.

67 year old man living in a remote area, with a history of hypertension and smoking, presents with symptoms suggestive of acute stroke. He reports sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking, which started approximately 3 hours ago. The patient is unable to walk and has slurred speech. The patient's wife calls the EMS and reports the symptoms. The EMS arrives within 30 minutes and assesses the patient, administering glucose testing to rule out hypoglycemia. The patient confirms the onset of symptoms to be within the last 8 hours. There are no known allergies or contraindications to contrast agents. The patient consents to participate voluntarily and is willing to sign a written informed consent.

45 year-old male with a history of hypertension and no significant past surgical history. During a routine physical exam, a mass was discovered on his left kidney via ultrasound. CT scan showed a 3 cm mass in the upper pole of the left kidney, concerning for renal cell carcinoma. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80 and is willing to sign consent for the study. He is planning to undergo a robotic assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) and has no contraindications to discontinue Plavix, Coumadin or other anti-platelet or anti-coagulant medications. The mass has been determined by the surgeon to be suitable for RAPN without clamp. The patient is 18 years or older and meets all eligibility criteria for the study.

A 55-year-old female presented with a 6-month history of right knee pain and stiffness, which has been progressively worsening. The patient reports a dull, achy pain in the knee that is exacerbated by weight-bearing activities and relieved with rest. She denies any history of trauma to the knee or any other joints. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. She denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation over the medial and lateral joint lines of the right knee, as well as crepitus with range of motion. The patient underwent radiographic imaging, which revealed moderate degenerative changes in the right knee joint, consistent with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 osteoarthritis. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of Fresh Platelet Rich Plasma With Concentrated Leukocytes or Fresh Platelet Rich Plasma Without Concentrated Leukocytes in the Treatment of Knee Cartilage Degeneration. She is willing to participate and signs the informed consent.

The patient is a 64-year-old male who has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) by his urologist. He has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), including urgency, frequency, and difficulty urinating, with an International Prostate Symptoms Score (IPSS) of 15. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications. He is able to comply with the study protocol procedures and has provided written informed consent. He does not have a history of prostate or bladder neck surgery, active urinary tract infection, or neurological disease that may affect bladder function. He does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. His renal and hepatic function are normal. He has not participated in any study involving the administration of an investigational compound within the past 30 days.

A 6-year-old girl with a diagnosis of Achondroplasia is seeking to participate in a clinical trial. She has genetic confirmation of the condition and is currently prepubertal with Stage 1 breasts. The patient is able to stand without assistance, and her caregiver is willing and able to administer subcutaneous injections of the study drug. The patient has not received any treatment of human growth hormone or any other medication known to affect stature or body proportionality within the previous 6 months of the screening visit. Additionally, there is no history or presence of injury or disease of the growth plate(s) other than Achondroplasia that affects growth potential of long bones. The patient is hoping to participate in the trial to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of TransCon CNP administered once weekly to treat her condition.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing tooth pain and sensitivity when eating or drinking hot or cold foods and beverages. She has a history of dental caries and has undergone previous dental fillings. Upon dental examination, it is found that she requires a single crown to restore the damaged tooth. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare different core build-up materials for dental use. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, as she is over 18 years of age and able to provide informed consent. She is not pregnant and maintains good oral hygiene practices.

A 55-year-old male patient presents with persistent cough and shortness of breath. He has a 30 pack-year smoking history and has been a smoker for 40 years. A chest X-ray and CT scan reveal a mass in the left lung consistent with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient undergoes surgical resection of the tumor at Tianjin Cancer Hospital in 2010. The histological examination confirms the diagnosis of NSCLC. The patient did not receive any systemic or local treatment before surgery. He has intact follow-up information and no other malignant tumors. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial that aims to identify gene mutation profile for Chinese lung squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma patients. The study will analyze the relationship between gene mutations and clinical characteristics and follow-up treatment. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is an appropriate candidate for the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old English-speaking woman who drinks 1-7 alcoholic drinks per week. She has no history of drug or alcohol dependence and has previously consumed at least 2 drinks in one hour. She has no major medical problems, including diabetes or high blood pressure, and no prior neurological or psychiatric history. She has not been diagnosed with liver or kidney disease, chronic gastrointestinal disease, or obesity (BMI < 30 kg/m2). She is not taking any psychoactive medications, and has not had any prior head trauma resulting in a loss of consciousness > 15 minutes. She has no MR exclusions including claustrophobia, intracranial, orbital, or spinal metal implants, pacemakers, cochlear implants, cardiac stents or other non-MR-compatible implants or devices. She is interested in participating in a study to learn more about how alcohol and its metabolite, acetate, affect brain function.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is currently 12 weeks pregnant. She has a history of gestational hypertension in her previous pregnancy and her BMI is 32 kg/m2. She is a stay-at-home mom with one child and no history of smoking or drug use. She has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. She has no known history of sleep apnea and is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the sleep study. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her pregnancy outcomes and is willing to be randomized to either the Sleep Study + CPAP group or the Standard Prenatal Care group. She is able to read and understand the consent form and is willing to deliver and complete her postpartum visit at Naval Medical Center San Diego.

55-year-old Caucasian male with a history of stage III melanoma diagnosed 6 months ago, which was surgically resected. The patient has fully recovered from the surgery and has no evidence of disease. The patient is HLA-A*0201 positive and has a Karnofsky performance status of >80%. The patient has no history of chemotherapy, chronic infections with HIV, hepatitis B or C, or autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus or rheumatoid arthritis. The patient is not pregnant and has no known allergies to gentamicin, tobramycin, streptomycin, or amikacin. The patient does not have any known retinal or choroidal eye disease. The patient has not been previously treated with any of the peptides used in the trial, melanoma protein vaccine, melanoma whole cell vaccines, or with Montanide. The patient does not have any allergy to shellfish.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has not received any prior treatment for his condition. He is in generally good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is able to perform most activities, but tires easily during more strenuous activities. The patient has no history of acute promyelocytic leukemia or prior chemotherapy for AML. The patient has also not undergone prior intensive chemotherapy or stem cell transplantation for the treatment of myelodysplastic syndrome. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive the standard induction/consolidation therapy with the addition of CX-01 at one of the two different dose levels.

A 45-year-old male patient presented to the hospital with severe abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. He has a history of chronic pancreatitis and had undergone multiple endoscopic interventions in the past. Abdominal CT scan showed a large pancreatic fluid collection with solid debris on the anterior aspect of the pancreatic body measuring 10 cm x 8 cm. The patient was referred for endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided drainage of PFCs with LAMS placement at Vanderbilt Medical Center. The patient was willing and able to give informed consent. He had no other significant medical history, was not taking any medications, and had no known allergies. Physical examination revealed mild epigastric tenderness with no rebound or guarding. Laboratory tests showed elevated amylase and lipase levels. EUS confirmed the presence of a large PFC with solid debris. The solid component of the PFC was assessed to be more than 30%. The patient was deemed eligible for the clinical trial and was randomized to receive either Lumen Apposing Metal Stents alone or Lumen Apposing Metal Stent plus Double Pigtail Stent for endoscopic drainage of pancreatic fluid collections.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who sustained an open tibia fracture after a motorcycle accident. He underwent antibiotic treatment within 2 hours of presentation at the hospital and underwent his first operative debridement within 24 hours of presentation. He is scheduled to have definitive wound closure within 14 days of initial injury. The patient has an open Gustilo-Anderson Type IIIA fracture of the tibia shaft, without a fibula fracture. His tibia fracture requires open fracture reduction and internal fixation with intramedullary (IM) nailing. The patient's IM nail has been cross-locked for stability with a 4-5mm interlock, with a minimum of 1 static screw above the fracture site and 1 static screw below the fracture site, and all IM nails have a diameter between 8.5-12mm with 1.0-1.5mm over-reaming of the canal. The temporary use of external fixation prior to IM rodding and DWC is allowed. Upon stabilization of the tibia fracture, the patient has a cortical deficit of less than or equal to 1.0cm involving no more than 50% of the tibia circumference. Gap assessments were made with calibrated radiographs or visual inspection. In addition, patients are not likely to require a secondary procedure(s) to promote bone healing. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study procedures including all pre-operative, post-operative, and rehabilitation requirements. The patient is able to give voluntary informed consent to participate and has signed an informed consent form specific to this study prior to study treatment and DWC. The patient is not a prisoner, is not currently participating in another investigational trial or having participated in a clinical investigation within the last 90 days or intend to during the course of the study. The patient is not skeletally immature (<18 years of age or radiographic evidence of open tibial physes). The patient does not have Type I, II, or IIIC open tibia fractures according to the Gustilo-Anderson classification. The patient does not have an active malignancy or a history of any invasive malignancy (except non-melanoma skin cancer), unless the patient has been treated with curative intent and there have been no clinical signs or symptoms of malignancy for at least 5 years. The patient does not have any medical condition or life circumstances that in the surgeon's opinion could impact their ability to return for follow-up visits and/or complete the required assessments and postoperative rehabilitation.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through a routine blood test. She has a sedentary lifestyle and is overweight, with a BMI of 31. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She does not smoke, rarely drinks alcohol, and has no history of liver disease or other chronic inflammatory diseases. She has not taken any supplements or foods containing probiotics in the last 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her liver condition and is willing to consume probiotics as part of the treatment.

A 28-week gestational age female infant with a birth weight of 1200 g was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit due to prematurity. The infant was born to a mother with a history of hypertension and gestational diabetes. The infant has been receiving routine medical care and has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions. The infant is currently being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of enteral administration of bovine lactoferrin in the prevention of sepsis in preterm infants with birth weight ≤ 1500 g and/or gestational age ≤ 32 weeks. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, and the parents have given their informed consent for participation.

This is a 35 year old female with a history of chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and stiffness for more than 3 months. She reports difficulty sleeping, morning stiffness, and headaches. Past medical history is significant for depression and anxiety. She has tried multiple treatments including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), acetaminophen, and muscle relaxants without significant improvement. She has not received any specific treatment for fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) in the past. She is able to travel to Seattle-based clinic 9 times and is willing to participate in the study. There are no exercise contraindications or significant psychopathologies. She meets the American College of Rheumatology criteria for FMS.

A 65-year-old Asian male, who was a retired teacher, was recently diagnosed with advanced non-squamous Non Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) stage IV. The patient initially presented with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He has never smoked in his life, but he has a history of exposure to second-hand smoke at home and at work. He has no significant past medical history, except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medications. He has no history of allergies or significant surgical procedures. His performance status according to Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) is 1, meaning that he is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities with some restrictions. The patient has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, or biological therapy. He is able to take folic acid and vitamin B12 supplementation. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is expected to have an estimated life expectancy of at least 12 weeks.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of chronic kidney disease with a baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 50 mL/min per 1.73 m2. He presents to the clinic with symptoms of unstable angina and is scheduled for coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on amlodipine and atorvastatin. He has no history of AKI, dialysis or sensitivity to contrast medium. He does not have any bleeding or coagulopathy diseases and is not currently taking any nephrotoxic drugs, vitamin E, vitamin C, or N-acetylcysteine (NAC). He is not currently on angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers. He has no known allergies to any medications.

A 38-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and has two children, ages 6 and 8. She and her husband are both employed, but their work schedules have been disrupted due to her treatment schedule and their children's school schedules. The family has been struggling to balance work, childcare, and medical appointments. The patient's husband has been taking on more responsibilities at home, but he is also dealing with the stress of his wife's illness. The patient and her husband are both fluent in German and are interested in receiving additional support during this difficult time. They have agreed to participate in the Familien-SCOUT study and have provided informed consent.

A 57-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with chest pain that occurred 2 hours after she had finished lunch. She works as a secretary and spends most of her time sitting at a desk. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and has been taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for the past 5 years. She is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. An electrocardiogram (ECG) revealed ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4, and she was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). She underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the placement of a drug-eluting stent in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). She was started on dual anti-platelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel. Her platelet function was monitored, and she was found to have high on-treatment platelet reactivity, indicating inadequate platelet inhibition in response to clopidogrel administration. She has been identified as a carrier of the CYP2C19*2 allele, which has been associated with a 1.5- to 6-fold increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events in patients treated with clopidogrel following PCI. She has been offered the opportunity to participate in the RAPID STEMI study, which will evaluate the feasibility, efficacy, and safety of a pharmacogenetic approach to anti-platelet therapy for the treatment of STEMI patients following PCI using point-of-care genetic testing for the CYP2C19*2, *17, and ABCB1 3435 C>T alleles. She has agreed to participate in the study and will undergo point-of-care genetic testing for the CYP2C19*2, *17, and ABCB1 3435 C>T alleles. Based on the results of the genetic testing, she may be randomized to receive either prasugrel or clopidogrel as part of the personalized approach to dual anti-platelet therapy following PCI. She will be closely monitored for efficacy and safety during the 1-month follow-up period.

Patient is a 43-year-old male who meets the DSM IV criteria for current alcohol dependence, including "loss of control over drinking." The patient is not currently engaged in, and does not want treatment for, alcohol related problems. The patient is able to read and understand questionnaires and informed consent, and lives within 50 miles of the study site. The patient is able to maintain abstinence for up to three days (without the aid of detox medications) as determined by self-report and breathalyzer measurements. The patient does not have a history of opiate abuse or a positive urine drug screen for opiates. The patient does not currently smoke and does not have metal objects in the head/neck or a history of claustrophobia leading to significant clinical anxiety symptoms. The patient does not currently meet DSM IV criteria for any other psychoactive substance dependence disorder, any other psychotic disorder or organic mental disorder, or have current suicidal ideation or homicidal ideation. The patient does not have a need for maintenance or acute treatment with any psychoactive medication including anti-seizure medications and does not have clinically significant medical problems such as cardiovascular, renal, GI, or endocrine problem that would impair participation or limit medication ingestion.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a history of moderate to severe asthma. She has had the condition since childhood and has been on regular inhaled corticosteroids for the past 5 years. Despite this treatment, she still experiences frequent exacerbations and has persistent sputum neutrophilia. She is currently taking FP 250mg BID or equivalent. The patient has not had any recent asthma exacerbations or acute respiratory illnesses in the past 4 weeks. She has a body mass index within the range of 18.5-37.0 kg/m2 and has documented reversibility (>12%) to short-acting bronchodilator. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of cardiovascular disease, malignancy, gastrointestinal disease, hepatic disease, renal disease, haematological disease, neurological disease, endocrine disease, or pulmonary disease other than asthma. She has no history of life-threatening asthma or intubation. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol requirements and instructions. She has signed and dated written informed consent and is able to understand the study requirements. She is not pregnant or nursing and agrees to use one of the contraception methods listed in Section 8.1 for an appropriate period of time prior to the start of dosing and until 3 months after last dose. The patient has no history of taking prescription or non-prescription drugs (including vitamins and dietary or herbal supplements) that may interfere with the study.

A 5-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Dravet syndrome presents with a history of recurrent seizures that have been uncontrolled with two different anticonvulsants. His seizures are characterized as convulsive and occur multiple times a week. He has tried valproic acid and levetiracetam, but neither medication has been effective in managing his seizures. The patient has a documented SCN1A mutation and has been diagnosed with Dravet syndrome by two pediatric neurologists. The patient's parents are seeking compassionate use of Stiripentol as a treatment option. The patient has no other significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications for his seizures.

A 62-year-old man with a diagnosis of metastatic prostate cancer is currently receiving regular oral opioid treatment. He has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and often wakes up feeling tired. He reports having pain at night which wakes him up frequently. He speaks the language used at the study center fluently and is able to comply with all study procedures. He has no severe cognitive impairment and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) by her primary care physician during a routine check-up. She has a medical history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. She is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic. Her current laboratory values show a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 45 mL/min. She experiences occasional fatigue and muscle weakness, but no other symptoms related to her kidney function. She has no known history of vasculitis, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or severe osteodystrophy. She is willing to participate in a research study that aims to examine the effect of regular aerobic exercise on preserving renal function, improving aerobic capacity, physical and psychosocial function, strength, cardiovascular function, general well-being, and quality of life in patients with CKD. She is able to walk 20 meters without assistance and has no current infections or antibiotic use within the last month. She has given written informed consent for the study.

A 25-year-old woman with a history of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) came to the clinic with a painful and swollen right arm. She had experienced similar episodes before and was currently taking oral prednisone to manage the flare-up. She had difficulty moving her right arm, which had been immobilized due to the pain. She was diagnosed with FOP when she was a child and has had multiple flare-ups that have led to abnormal bone formation in her muscles and tendons, causing restricted movement and disability. She has tried various treatments, including surgery, to prevent the progression of the disease, but with limited success. She is not currently using any medication that could interfere with the study. She is willing to participate in the study and is looking for a treatment that could prevent flare-ups and maintain her mobility.

The patient is a 17-year-old male diagnosed with advanced cancer with an estimated overall survival of less than 50%. He has been receiving cancer care at Seattle Children's Hospital for the past two months. He reports feeling sad, anxious, and overwhelmed about his diagnosis and the impact it has on his life. He finds it challenging to communicate his needs and preferences to his healthcare providers and his family members. He is interested in participating in a research study that could help him develop skills to better manage stress and improve his quality of life. His parents are supportive of his participation in the study and are willing to attend a family meeting as part of the intervention. The patient is fluent in English and able to read and understand both English and Spanish. He is cognitively able to participate in interviews and express his thoughts and feelings.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of chronic hepatitis B infection for the past 15 years. He has been on antiviral therapy with entecavir for the past 5 years and has achieved viral suppression. The patient has never had any symptoms of liver disease and has never been diagnosed with cirrhosis. He has a family history of liver cancer with his father having died from the disease. The patient is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol in moderation. He presents for his routine follow-up visit and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for surveillance of hepatocellular carcinoma. His laboratory tests show normal liver function tests and alpha-fetoprotein levels. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. The patient has no contraindications for participation in the trial and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of advanced soft tissue sarcoma. He has previously undergone surgical resection and radiation therapy but has experienced disease progression. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1, with occasional difficulty in walking long distances. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. The patient is retired and lives with his wife in a rural area. He enjoys gardening and spending time with his grandchildren. The treating physician has assessed him as unsuited for standard chemotherapy due to his age and overall health status. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is indicated for

8-year-old female with a history of atopic dermatitis for the past 5 years presents to the clinic with exacerbation of her symptoms. She has a history of frequent flare-ups and has tried various topical steroids and emollients with little improvement. She reports itching, redness, and dryness of her skin, particularly in the area of her elbows, knees, and face. She also reports occasional weeping, crusting, and pustules. On examination, she has erythematous, scaly, and excoriated patches on her extremities and face. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She has not been prescribed bleach baths in the past but has tried various home remedies including vinegar baths. The patient and her parents are willing to participate in the study and understand the follow-up requirements. The patient resides in the US and is available for in-clinic follow-up assessments at 1, 3, and 6 months after initiation of treatment.

A 30-year-old Caucasian female presents with a history of depression that started ten years ago. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and having difficulty sleeping and concentrating. She has tried various antidepressant medications in the past and has undergone cognitive-behavioral therapy, but she still experiences persistent symptoms of depression. She is currently not taking any medications for depression. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or other major psychiatric disorders. She does not have Addison's disease, Cushing's disease, or other known dysfunction of the HPA-cortisol axis. She does not have rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other conditions associated with increased inflammation. She does not regularly use non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications, steroids, or other medications known to interact with the inflammatory process of the HPA axis. She is not pregnant and does not have a history of substance abuse or dependence in the last month. She does not smoke cigarettes regularly. She has no history of fainting or other significant adverse events during blood drawing in the past. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on depression and potentially find a more objective diagnostic tool.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has no history of any other medical conditions or surgeries. Her tumor is estrogen and progesterone receptor negative. She is planning to receive anthracycline-based chemotherapy. She is concerned about the potential impact of chemotherapy on her ovarian function and wishes to preserve her fertility. She has regular menstrual periods and her FSH level is 8 mlU/ml in the follicular phase. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to prevent chemotherapy-induced ovarian failure. She has not received any prior cytotoxic treatment and has no known hypersensitivity reactions to investigational compounds or incorporated substances. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use adequate non-hormonal contraceptive measures during the study treatment. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 65-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her daughter due to progressive memory loss and difficulty with daily activities. The symptoms started approximately 2 years ago and have been gradually getting worse. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her family history is significant for her mother having Alzheimer's disease. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for mild forgetfulness. She scored 19 out of 30 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). A positron emission tomography (PET) scan showed amyloid deposition consistent with Alzheimer's disease. She has a reliable caregiver who accompanies her to all clinic visits. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m2.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III Hodgkin's disease two years ago. She received standard chemotherapy and radiation therapy and achieved complete remission.
