However, six months ago, she started experiencing fever, weight loss, and night sweats. Her PET/CT scan showed relapse of Hodgkin's disease involving multiple sites, including lymph nodes and spleen. She has no history of heart disease, no significant pulmonary disease, and her renal function is normal. She is HIV-negative and has no clinical evidence of AIDS. She is not pregnant and has a negative pregnancy test. She is willing to undergo high dose chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and peripheral stem cell transplantation.

This is a 32 year-old Asian female who has been trying to conceive for the past year but has been unsuccessful. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days and has been diagnosed with endometriosis stage II. She is eligible for in vitro fertilization (IVF) and/or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) using fresh or frozen ejaculated sperm from her partner. Her BMI is 25 kg/m2 and she has no known history of thrombophilia or systemic disease. She has not used any fertility modifiers or hormonal preparations in the last menstrual cycle before randomization. She is willing to accept transfer of 1-2 embryos.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient's tumor is inoperable and has spread to the local lymph nodes. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy for metastatic NSCLC. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. The patient currently does not smoke and has no other significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient's performance status is 1 according to ECOG/Zubrod/SWOG criteria. The patient's baseline laboratory values are within normal limits, including adequate bone marrow function, renal function, and hepatic function. The patient's life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 8 weeks. The patient is a male over the age of 18. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating, and is using an effective means of contraception. The patient has a histological diagnosis of NSCLC that is advanced and cannot be treated adequately by radiotherapy or surgery, or metastatic disease. The patient has not received prior therapy with an epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor, including erlotinib, gefitinib, and cetuximab, as well as any investigational HER-1 inhibiting agent. The patient has not had a myocardial infarction or ischemia within the 6 months before Cycle 0' Day 0, and does not have uncontrolled clinically significant dysrhythmia. The patient has not had a history of prior malignancy within the prior five years, with the exception of non-melanoma carcinomas of the skin, and carcinoma in situ of the cervix. The patient has not had prior radiotherapy to an indicator lesion unless there is objective evidence of tumor growth in that lesion. The patient does not have uncontrolled metastatic disease of the central nervous system, and has not had radiotherapy or surgery within the 2 weeks before Cycle 1' Day 1. The patient does not have any co-morbid conditions that, in the view of the attending physician, renders the patient at high risk from treatment complications.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who presents with a large mass in his throat that has been growing rapidly over the past few months. He reports difficulty swallowing, weight loss, and occasional hoarseness. He has a history of heavy smoking and alcohol use. On physical examination, there is a large mass in the oropharynx that is obstructing the airway. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. CT imaging reveals a large mass in the oropharynx with involvement of the cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for Arm 1 or Arm 3 of the trial, with a T3 primary tumor and regional nodal disease. He does not have a history of prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for HNSCC, and he has no other significant medical history. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 47-year-old male with a history of cryptogenic cerebrovascular accident (CVA) presents with recurrent episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and mild weakness in the right upper and lower extremities. He has no history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or diabetes mellitus. A brain MRI reveals acute infarction in the left middle cerebral artery territory. A transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) shows a permeable foramen ovale (PFO). The patient is referred to a cardiology clinic for further evaluation and management. The interventional cardiologist recommends occlusion of the PFO to prevent future cryptogenic CVAs. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of this intervention and meets the eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of hepatitis B virus infection. He was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with pulmonary metastasis after undergoing a CT scan. The intrahepatic tumors have been controlled with repeated locoregional therapies such as transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and radiofrequency ablation therapy (RFA). He is now eligible to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the efficacy of sorafenib to 5-fluorouracil/mitomycin for HCC patients with pulmonary metastasis. The trial requires that the patient has at least one, bi-dimensionally measurable, pulmonary metastasis without intrahepatic viable tumor. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a Child-Pugh class score of B (Child-Pugh score 7). Laboratory tests conducted within 7 days prior to screening indicate that the patient has adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient has not received prior systemic chemotherapy and has no history of organ allograft or active clinically serious infections. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will be closely monitored for any adverse events.

A 35-year-old male, with a history of chronic low back pain (CLBP) for more than 3 months, is being sought for a clinical trial investigating the relationship of pressure pain threshold (PPT) with pain intensity, pain affect, and disability in patients with CLBP. The patient must not have any specific underlying pathology as the cause of their CLBP. They should not have any neurological or metabolic diseases, coagulopathies, or skin diseases in the low back region. They must not have undergone spinal surgery nor evince bruising to PPT testing. The patient should also have a DASS-21 score of less than 28 for depression, less than 20 for anxiety, and less than 34 for stress. The study participant shall be thoroughly briefed about the research project, its objectives, procedures, and potential benefits and discomforts before undergoing assessments. If the patient agrees to participate, they will undergo PPT measurement using a manual Algometer, followed by a session of physiotherapy treatment. The patient will be asked to document their pain intensity, pain affect and disability.

This is a 30 year old female with a past medical history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) diagnosed two years ago. She reports experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and alternating constipation and diarrhea. She has tried various medications and dietary modifications in the past but has not found significant relief. She has no other major medical illnesses and is not currently taking any medications for her IBS. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer relief for her symptoms. She understands that the trial involves taking either a placebo pill or no treatment for a period of 3 weeks and will involve three visits to the study center. She is willing to participate and will be evaluated for eligibility during her screening visit.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been trying to conceive for the past two years. She has undergone several cycles of In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) without success. During previous cycles, she produced a maximum of four oocytes with conventional stimulation. Ovarian tests revealed abnormalities, indicating poor ovarian reserve. She has no known contraindications for heparin. She presents with regular menstrual cycles, and her medical history is unremarkable. She has no history of thromboembolic events or bleeding disorders. She and her partner are motivated to undergo IVF treatment and are willing to participate in a clinical trial assessing the role of heparin in improving pregnancy outcomes in poor responders.

A 35-year-old male volunteer from the Danish Blood Donor Study with no previous history of headaches is interested in participating in the Multiomics After Headache Provocation study. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no history of substance abuse. He has not taken any medications in the past six months and has no chronic illnesses or mental health conditions. He has a healthy BMI of 24 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He is willing to undergo headache provocation with isosorbide mononitrate and provide three blood samples for RNA and metabolomic analysis. He is interested in contributing to the understanding of headache pathophysiology and hopes that his participation in the study will lead to the development of more efficient headache treatments.

A 52-year-old man was admitted to the Neurosciences Critical Care Unit (NCCU) due to a severe head injury sustained in a car accident. He was intubated and mechanically ventilated. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he is a smoker. He was not on insulin infusion at the time of admission, but his glucose levels were high on admission, and a single confirmed reference blood glucose level was measured at 11.5 mmol/L. His injury is severe, and he is expected to stay in the ICU for more than 48 hours. The patient is alert and cooperative, and he understands the nature of the study. The patient's family has also been informed of the study, and they have given their consent for the patient to participate. The patient does not have any known allergies to insulin. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for a slightly elevated white blood cell count. The patient is not pregnant. The patient's head injury is being managed conservatively, and he is not receiving therapeutic hypothermia. The patient has not been diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic non-ketotic coma (HONK).

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents with symptoms of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She has a history of recent travel to a high-risk area for COVID-19 and has been in contact with a confirmed COVID-19 positive individual. She has tested positive for COVID-19 on a nasal swab PCR test. She has been advised to undergo a routine laparoscopy for a gynecological issue. She does not have any significant medical history or comorbidities. She is willing to participate in the study and has social security care.

45yo male with a history of long-term exposure to arsenic in his occupation as a metal welder, who presents with severe chronic itching that has been refractory to standard treatments. He has been experiencing the symptoms for the past 6 months and rates his itch severity as 7 out of 10 on the numeric rating scale. He has been using topical anti-pruritic agents, but the relief is only temporary. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the study protocol. His hair arsenic concentration is 2 μg/g. He is a non-smoker and has not used illicit drugs. He has not been diagnosed with any basic itchy dermatological diseases such as eczema.

A 45-year-old male patient underwent major cardiac surgery and has been admitted to the Cardiac Surgical Intensive Care Unit (CICU) at Hamilton General Hospital. The patient has an arterial line in place and is currently being monitored for vital signs such as blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate. The patient has a history of hypertension and is on medication to control blood pressure. The patient does not have any known allergies to device contact adhesive. The patient is conscious and able to communicate. The patient's blood pressure is within the test range for the phase of the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

45 yo M with HIV diagnosed 10 years ago, currently on stable combination anti-retroviral therapy with a plasma HIV viral load of <200copies/ml for ≥6 months. The patient has a history of hypertension and a family history of heart disease. Recent blood work showed a total cholesterol level of 210 mg/dL and LDL cholesterol level of 130 mg/dL. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if starting statin therapy earlier than current Australian guidelines recommend can delay progression of atherosclerosis. A carotid ultrasound showed mild thickening of the carotid intima media. The patient has not used statin, fibrate, or ezetimibe within the last six months and has no contraindications to statin use. The patient's cardiovascular disease risk is moderate, with a 10-15% 10-year risk of CVD.

A 35-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV-1 antibody by an ELISA test and Western blot. Her CD4+ cell count is 250 cells/mm3. She is currently on antiretroviral therapy with tenofovir, emtricitabine, and dolutegravir. She has a history of candidiasis and has been on fluconazole for the past 6 months. She has no history of drug allergy or known drug hypersensitivity. The patient is willing to use a reliable form of contraception. She is able to provide written informed consent and willing to comply with the study requirements. She has no history of intravenous drug abuse, alcohol or substance abuse in the last year. The patient has no clinically important disease, including hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, or gastrointestinal disease. She has no malabsorption, severe chronic diarrhea and is able to maintain adequate oral intake.

A 34-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for over a year. She has been experiencing chronic active disease with symptoms such as abdominal pain, frequent diarrhea, and bloody stools. She has been on maintenance treatment with immunosuppressive drugs and anti-TNF therapy for the past 8 weeks but with little improvement. Her disease is limited to the left side of the colon, and endoscopic pictures show E1-E2 disease or extended to the transverse colon but not beyond the hepatic flexure. She has an activity score greater than 5 and an endoscopic score greater than 2. Bacterial infection (Clostridium difficile) has been ruled out. The patient is not currently hospitalized and does not require intravenous treatment or immediate surgery. She is not on Prednisone> 20 mg / d and does not have any contraindications to the use of neuromodulator. The patient is not pregnant and is affiliated with a social protection scheme. She has signed an informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with low HDL (high-density lipoprotein) levels at her last check-up. She has a family history of heart disease, with her father having a heart attack in his 50s. Her current HDL level is 0.8 mmol/L (32 mg/dL) and her triglyceride level is 3.5 mmol/L (310 mg/dL). She has been taking simvastatin 40 mg for the past 6 months to manage her cholesterol levels. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is currently using an effective form of contraception. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her HDL levels and reduce her risk of heart disease.

A 10-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with a high-grade B-cell lymphoma. She presented with enlarged lymph nodes in her neck, armpits and groin-area, which have been growing for several weeks. She also complained of fatigue and night sweats. A biopsy of the affected lymph node confirmed the diagnosis of lymphoma. The patient has no significant past medical history except for occasional ear infections. She is not taking any medications and has no known allergies. The patient is hepatitis B negative, not currently pregnant, and not currently nursing. She is known to be fertile but is not sexually active. She has not undergone any previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study, and her parents have provided informed consent.

32 year old female with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 who is generally healthy and has no history of diabetes, gastrointestinal disorders, or metabolic disorders. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of artificial sweeteners on gut microbiota and glucose metabolism. She reports consuming artificial sweeteners occasionally but is willing to consume them daily during the trial. She is willing to complete weekly food diaries and complete a food frequency questionnaire. She has not used probiotics or antibiotics within the past 6 months.

A 65-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with severe bilateral osteoarthritis of the knees. She has been suffering from knee pain and difficulty walking for over five years. She was referred to an orthopedic surgeon for a total knee replacement arthroplasty (TKRA). The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking Metformin and Lisinopril for her medical conditions. She has been taking these medications for several years and her blood pressure and blood sugar levels are well controlled. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her height is 5'4'' and weight is 160lbs. She has no history of any hematologic, thromboembolic, hepatic, renal, or coagulation disorders. Her preoperative hemoglobin level is 120 g/L. Her serum ferritin level is 80 ng/ml and transferrin saturation (TSAT) is 15%. She is willing to participate in the study and is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the study.

A 54-year-old male patient who was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of severe pneumonia that has progressed to sepsis. The patient is currently receiving intravenous therapy of fluconazole for a suspected fungal infection. The patient has no history of significant allergies or adverse reactions to antifungal medications. The patient has a central venous catheter in place that will be used for blood sample collection during the study. The patient and/or their next of kin have provided written informed consent for participation in the study. The patient has no history of HIV, hepatitis B or C, or tuberculosis.

A 55 year old man presented to the emergency department with chest pain that started 2 hours ago. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, and he is a smoker. He does not have a history of diabetes. In the physical exam, his blood pressure was 150/90 mmHg, heart rate was 80 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 bpm, and oxygen saturation was 97% on room air. He had no significant findings in lung and heart auscultation. His ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. His troponin level was elevated. He was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome and was randomized into the GIK2 group in the clinical trial.

Patient 1: The patient is a 45-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU with respiratory distress due to underlying chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She has no evidence of current or chronic infectious diseases and has not received any antifungal therapy within the past 8 weeks. She is not on any immunosuppressive therapy but is receiving inhaled corticosteroids for her COPD. She is eligible for inclusion in group 1 of the NOBICS study.  Patient 2: The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of leukemia who was admitted to the ICU with fever, chills, and hypotension. Blood cultures have grown Candida albicans and he meets the EORTC/MSG definitions for invasive candidiasis. He has not received antifungal therapy within the past 8 weeks but is receiving immunosuppressive therapy with methotrexate for his leukemia. He is not eligible for inclusion in the NOBICS study.  Patient 3: The patient is a 55-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU with sepsis and blood cultures positive for Staphylococcus aureus. She has not received antifungal therapy within the past 8 weeks but is receiving glucocorticoids with a prednisone equivalent of 10mg/d for her asthma. She is not eligible for inclusion in the NOBICS study.  Patient 4: The patient is a 70-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU after suffering a stroke and is intubated and mechanically ventilated. He has no evidence of current or chronic infectious diseases and has not received any antifungal therapy within the past 8 weeks. He is not on any immunosuppressive therapy. Despite his intubation, he currently has no clinical or laboratory markers of infection. He is eligible for inclusion in group 4 of the NOBICS study.

55-year-old male presents with a history of colon polyps and a family history of colorectal cancer. During a routine colonoscopy, a sessile serrated polyp (SSP) measuring 10mm in size was identified and removed by snare polypectomy. The pathology report indicated hyperplastic polyp with focal serration. The patient was referred to a tertiary endoscopic resection practice for further evaluation. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or medications.

A 32-year-old man who works in the construction industry was recently diagnosed with high-grade glioma. He underwent surgery to remove as much of the tumor as possible and is now eligible for this clinical trial. He has no history of cancer, but his father passed away from lung cancer. He is married and has two children. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly but has been experiencing weakness and difficulty with coordination since his diagnosis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He takes no other medications and has no known allergies. He is interested in participating in this trial to improve his chances of a successful outcome and to help advance research in the field.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a BMI of 42. She has been struggling with obesity for several years and has tried various diets and exercise programs with little success. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, which she attributes to her weight. She is currently taking medication for both conditions. She has consulted with a bariatric surgeon and has been recommended for bariatric surgery, but her surgeon would like her to lose some weight before the surgery to decrease the surgical risk. The patient is interested in participating in a weight loss study that may help her achieve her goal. She does not have any pathologies of the GI tract and is not taking any anti-coagulant or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications. She is willing to be randomized to either the device or sham procedure group and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman who lives in a rural area of Guatemala with her husband and two children. She is currently less than 20 weeks pregnant and regularly visits the local Ministry of Health clinic for prenatal care. She uses an open fire for cooking and purchases wood for fuel. The patient does not smoke cigarettes and does not have any medical conditions that require prescription medication. She has a mobile phone and is the primary person responsible for cooking in her household. The patient intends to stay in the study area for at least one year and is able to give informed consent. She does not have a multiple pregnancy and is not identified as a high-risk pregnancy by her physician. Additionally, she does not routinely carry a child less than 2 years old on her back.

59-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 pneumonia based on a positive PCR test. The patient was started on oxygen via nasal cannula and was later intubated due to worsening respiratory status. The patient had a PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 150 mmHg and was diagnosed with moderate ARDS. His laboratory values revealed a CRP level of 135 mg/dL, D-dimer level of 750 ng/mL, and IL-6 level of 20 pg/mL. The patient is being considered for inclusion in the clinical trial to receive targeted corticosteroids. He has no known allergies, and his medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. The patient is willing to comply with study-related procedures and assessments and has signed an informed consent form. He is not pregnant and does not have any active bacterial, fungal, or mycobacterial infections.

7-year-old girl diagnosed with perinatal brachial plexus injury. She has limited use of her affected arm and hand, with difficulty in activities such as dressing, writing, and playing. She has been receiving occupational therapy for the past year, with improvement in her arm strength and range of motion. She is able to cooperate with interventions and assessments. She has no other co-morbid diagnoses and is not allergic to any constraint intervention materials. Her parents have consented to her participation in the study and are willing to continue her current occupational therapy regime throughout the study period.

A 28-year-old male presents with a history of intravenous drug use and testing positive for HIV. He is currently struggling with opioid addiction and has been using heroin for the past year. He has attempted to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in seeking treatment and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He has a history of depression and anxiety but has not sought treatment for these issues. He reports occasional benzodiazepine use for anxiety. He has no history of opiate use for pain management. He is currently homeless and engages in commercial sex work to support his addiction. He is motivated to change his lifestyle and improve his overall health.

A 55-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure presents with shortness of breath, fatigue, and peripheral edema. The patient has a preserved systolic function with an ejection fraction of 50%. Past medical history includes hypertension, but no active hepatitis, cirrhosis, or diabetes. The patient is not on any aldosterone antagonist therapy or any other medication for heart failure. Blood pressure is well-controlled at 130/80 mmHg. The patient's renal function is normal, and potassium levels are within the normal range. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of canrenone on cardiovascular mortality in patients with congestive heart failure and preserved systolic function.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with primary central nervous system lymphoma. He is a retired accountant and has a history of hypertension, which is currently being controlled with medication. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. His initial symptoms were headaches and confusion, and he underwent a brain biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He has no evidence of systemic disease on chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scan. His ECOG performance status is 1, and his laboratory results are within normal limits. He has no history of prior chemotherapy or immunosuppression, and his HIV test is negative. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive chemotherapy with MT-R followed by autologous stem cell transplantation to treat his primary central nervous system lymphoma. He is able to swallow medication without difficulty and is willing to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) for the past 6 years. She is currently being treated with Ocrevus and her disease is stable with an EDSS score of 3. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and no other significant medical history. She has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 infection or received convalescent plasma or polyclonal antibody treatments for COVID-19 in the past 3 months. She is willing to provide informed consent and complete the patient questionnaires associated with this study. She has not received high dose steroids, IVIG, or PLEX in the past 3 months. She is able to complete the blood sample collection process for this study. She is not on any concurrent immunosuppressive therapy, active systemic cancer, primary or acquired immunodeficiency diseases, or systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury 2 years ago in a car accident. He has an incomplete spinal cord injury classified as AIS C with a lesion at the T11 level. He has limited mobility and requires a wheelchair for long distances. His body mass index is 25.5. He does not have any history of seizure, head injury with loss of consciousness, severe alcohol or drug abuse, or psychiatric illness. He has normal cognitive function and is able to provide informed consent. He is not pregnant and uses appropriate contraception. He does not have any ferromagnetic material in the brain or spine, nor does he have any cardiac or neural pacemakers. He does not have any fixed contractures in the lower extremities, severe osteoporosis, severe spasticity, or decubitus ulcers that interfere with harness support or walking. He does not have uncontrolled diabetes or severe orthostatic hypotension.

A 58 year old woman has been experiencing pain and stiffness in both of her knees for the past year. She has difficulty walking and climbing stairs, and the pain worsens with prolonged activity. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis and has been taking over-the-counter pain medication to manage her symptoms. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of mobilization with movement (MWM) on pain and function in patients with knee OA. She has not had any lower limb surgery or received any intra-articular corticosteroid or hyaluronic acid injections in the past 6 months. She is able to walk at least 6 meters with or without an aid. She has no altered sensation around her knee and no cognitive difficulties. She is not currently using oral corticosteroids and has no contraindications to manual therapy.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been struggling with weight gain, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol levels over the past year. Despite making changes to her diet and exercise routine, she has not seen any significant improvements in her health. She has a family history of diabetes and heart disease, which has increased her concerns about her overall health. She is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and cholesterol. She is interested in participating in a study that could potentially help her manage her metabolic syndrome and improve her overall health. She is willing to take oral cinnamon supplements as part of the study and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a waist circumference of 90 cm. He has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a diet high in processed foods. He has no known history of diabetes, hypertension, or chronic diseases. He does not take any medications or supplements. He has no family history of diabetes, hypertension, or any other chronic illnesses. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 12 mg/dl. He has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 28 year old pregnant woman, G1P0, came to the clinic for her routine check up. She is in her 38th week of gestation and her pregnancy has been unremarkable so far. She had gestational diabetes, which was well-controlled with diet and exercise. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no significant medical history, and she has no allergies. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical exam is unremarkable. Her obstetrician recommended a cesarean delivery due to fetal macrosomia. She consented to participate in the study if she develops shoulder pain during or after the procedure.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester living in a rural community in Pakistan. She is married and has two children, both of whom were born at home without any complications. She is currently experiencing symptoms of psychological distress, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She also reports experiencing anxiety and stress related to her pregnancy and caring for her young children. She has not received any previous treatment for her emotional symptoms. Her husband works as a farmer and their household income is very low. She is not currently taking any medications and has not had any serious medical problems during her pregnancy. She is interested in participating in a study that could help improve her emotional well-being and strengthen her relationship with her new baby.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis. He underwent a biological aortic valve replacement surgery with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. His medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has a history of a myocardial infarction 5 years ago and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement. He is currently on aspirin 81mg daily and a statin medication. His physical examination is within normal limits, and his ECG shows normal sinus rhythm. His baseline INR is normal, and there is no evidence of hypercoagulable or bleeding disorders. He has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate.

A 12-year-old boy with a diagnosis of spastic diplegia, GMFCS level 1, and currently in year 7 of a mainstream school is being asked to participate in this clinical trial. He has been prescribed bilateral moulded AFOs to aid his walking. The patient has been using AFOs for the past 2 years and has been able to maintain his mobility and independence with their use. However, his parents have reported that he sometimes refuses to wear them, especially when he is around his peers. The patient does not have any behavioral or communication problems and is able to understand and cooperate with the gait analysis process and interviews. He has not undergone any invasive procedures in the past 6 months and is not planning to undergo any in the next 6 months. The patient and his family have agreed to participate in the trial and are willing to provide their feedback on the experience of using AFOs.

A 67-year-old female complains of blurred vision and distortion in her left eye for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension, but no other underlying disease and is not on any medications. Ophthalmic examination reveals exudative age-related macular degeneration with significant subretinal fluid and/or cystoid macular edema as assessed by optical coherence tomography in the left eye, with a minimum of 300 µm within the central subfield. Best corrected visual acuity of 70 ETDRS letters (20/40) in the left eye. She has had prior treatment in the left eye with at least 3 anti-VEGF treatments within the prior 2-6 months, throughout which clinical examination and SD-OCT imaging has shown recurrent or persistent exudative activity, as shown by the presence of intraretinal or subretinal fluid, and/or subretinal exudation or hemorrhage. Her total lesion size is ≤9 disc areas, containing ≤50% hemorrhage and ≤50% subretinal fibrosis and ≤50% retinal pigment epithelial atrophy in the left eye. She has reasonably clear media and reasonable fixation ability in the left eye to allow for good quality tomography and fundus photography. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the RBM-007 clinical trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was rushed to the emergency department after experiencing sudden onset of numbness in her left arm and left leg. She was diagnosed with acute ischemic stroke and is currently within the 3-hour window for treatment. She has a total NIH Stroke Scale score of 7, with deficits in motor power and attention. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is not currently taking any medications for these conditions. She has never had a stroke before and has no history of bleeding disorders or major surgery in the past 14 days. She is not pregnant and has no history of gastrointestinal or urinary tract hemorrhage in the previous 21 days. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent for the study.

This is a 28-year-old male who sustained a complete transection injury to the digital nerve of his left index finger while using a power tool at his job. The injury occurred 5 days prior to presentation to the clinic. The patient has no known allergies to the constituent polymer of the investigational device, has no history of peripheral neuropathy or neuropathic pain, and is not taking any neuromodulator medication. There is sufficient healthy soft tissue for primary closure without adjunctive soft tissue procedures, and gap closure between the nerve ends can be achieved by flexion of the extremity without excessive tension. The patient is willing and able to provide a signed Patient Informed Consent Form and follow the study instructions and likely to complete all required study procedures and visits. The patient is not currently participating in any other investigational drug or device trials, does not have any chronic ischemic conditions of the extremity, and does not have a diagnosis of type 1 Diabetes Mellitus or uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

28 yo pregnant female in her third trimester with no known complications. She has a BMI of 28 and reports occasional snoring and waking up feeling tired despite getting a full night's sleep. She denies any history of hypertension, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, or any chronic medical conditions. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help better understand how maternal sleep disordered breathing can affect fetal growth and development. She is willing to undergo sleep studies and other tests as required by the study protocol.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. The patient is currently scheduled to receive chemotherapy in either the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting. She has an ECOG status of 0 or 1 and is performing less than 150 minutes of structured moderate-intensity or strenuous intensity exercise per week. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study. The patient has no history of any other malignancy treated within the past 3 years (other than non-melanoma skin cancer) or presence of metastatic disease. She has no contraindications to cardiopulmonary exercise testing and is willing to be randomized to one of the study arms. The patient has no mental impairment leading to inability to cooperate and no other condition or intercurrent illness that, in the opinion of the investigator, makes her a poor candidate for the trial.

42yo male with a history of recurrent appendicitis, presenting for elective appendectomy. The patient has no significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and his BMI is within normal limits. He has not been on any chronic pain medications and has no known allergies to study medications. The patient has not had any recent respiratory tract infections and has no history of cardiac disease, psychological disorders, respiratory diseases, or renal or hepatic failure. There is no history of coagulation disorders. The patient has not had any prior abdominal surgeries or trauma.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 who regularly consumes three meals a day and participates in moderate exercise activities such as running and aerobics classes for a total of 5 hours per week. She is an unrestrained eater with a score of less than 15 on the Three Factor Eating Questionnaire. She has no history of significant disease or allergies and is not taking any medication that can affect carbohydrate or lipid metabolism. She does not have any swallowing difficulties and does not exercise more than 7 hours per week. She consumes alcohol occasionally but not more than 2 drinks per day. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to determine the effects of soy protein/soy fiber on measures of satiety.

A 22 year old college student who regularly uses e-cigarettes for the past 6 months is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She usually vapes sweet flavored e-liquids with medium nicotine strength (9-12mg/mL). She does not have any mouth or throat problems that would prevent her from vaping comfortably or any health problems that would affect her sense of taste or smell. She does not have any allergies to food ingredients or propylene glycol or vegetable glycerin. She has never been diagnosed with pulmonary disease or asthma and has not experienced any respiratory allergies. She is not currently trying to quit vaping and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

The patient is a 35 year old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 18. He has been managing his diabetes for the past 17 years with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) for the past 4 years. His HbA1c levels have been consistently below 7.2%. He leads an active lifestyle, being able to engage in moderate physical activity for at least 20 minutes. He reports no symptoms of diabetic late complications except for simplex retinopathy. He is currently not pregnant or nursing. His occupation is in the field of IT and he is excited to participate in research that could potentially improve the management of diabetes.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of painful menstrual periods and heavy menstrual bleeding. She has been diagnosed with adenomyosis based on imaging studies and has been experiencing symptoms for the past 2 years. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medications. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of progestin treatment for the management of adenomyosis. Her last menstrual period was 7 days ago, and she is currently in the early secretory phase of her menstrual cycle. She has no history of malignancy and is premenopausal. She is eager to contribute to research that may help find a more effective treatment for adenomyosis.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing peripheral neuropathy symptoms for the past year, including numbness and tingling in both feet, which has affected his mobility and quality of life. He has tried other medications and therapies for neuropathy, but has not experienced significant improvement. He has been prescribed Metanx® for the past 6 months and has been taking it as directed. The patient has no other significant medical history, and his current medications include Metformin and Lisinopril for his diabetes and hypertension respectively. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. His height is 5'9" and his weight is 190 lbs. He has a BMI of 27.5. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 35-year-old mother with a 6-year-old son who has been experiencing behavioral issues, including hyperactivity and impulsivity, is seeking psychiatric care at the Université Hospital of Besançon, France. This is their first consultation request, and they are both eligible to participate in the pilot study. The mother works part-time as a teacher and has a supportive spouse. The child is currently in primary school and has no known medical conditions or allergies. They have not received any psychiatric care in the past, and the mother is looking forward to receiving individualized clinical management to help her son.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing a persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. The patient has undergone first-line treatment but has experienced a relapse and is now seeking alternative treatment options. The patient has a performance status (PS) of 2 and is otherwise healthy. The patient is willing and able to comply with the schedule of visits, treatment protocols, laboratory tests, and other requirements of the study. The patient has not received systemic treatment with either corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days of the first dose of study drug. The patient has not had any previous malignancies within the last 2 years. The patient has been diagnosed with NSCLC, and the stage of the tumor is stage IIIB/IV. The patient is eligible to participate in this study and is willing to undergo second-generation sequencing technology and liquid phase factor platform for detection of efficacy and side effects of immunotherapy.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who reports occasional dizziness and imbalance. She has a history of falls in the past year, but has not sustained any major injuries. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. The patient has no known history of diabetes mellitus or cervical spine instability. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has normal neck range of motion and no visual impairments. She is generally active and independent, but is concerned about her balance and wants to take steps to reduce her fall risk. The patient is well-dressed and well-nourished, and appears to be in good overall health.

A 52-year-old female patient with a history of metastatic breast cancer presents with a new mass in her left breast. She has previously received two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease, but the cancer has continued to progress. The patient has no history of radiation therapy to her left breast, and there is no diffuse bone marrow involvement on OctreoScan scintigraphy. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 2, and her Karnofsky score is 60. The patient's laboratory values are within normal limits, with a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm3, and a platelet count of 150,000/mm3. The patient has a history of hypertension and depression, both of which are well controlled with medication. She has no history of congestive heart failure, and her ejection fraction is normal. The patient is not pregnant and uses effective contraception. Her OctreoScan scintigraphy shows positive somatostatin receptors (grade 3) in the breast mass. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for this study.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 3 years ago. She has been treated with Tysabri (BG00002) for the past 14 months and has been stable for the last 12 months with no relapses, no new lesions, and no disability progression. However, her neurologist recommended transitioning her to Tecfidera (BG00012) due to the potential risk of developing progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) associated with Tysabri treatment. The patient has agreed to the transition and started Tecfidera treatment a month ago. She is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the effectiveness of Tecfidera treatment post-Tysabri. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no significant comorbidities. She has no history of other autoimmune diseases or malignancies. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is currently employed as a teacher and has two children. She has no significant limitations in her daily activities and reports no adverse effects from either Tysabri or Tecfidera.

58-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2 presented to the Emergency Department with fever, chills, and confusion. Blood cultures were drawn and grew Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). He was diagnosed with septic shock and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Despite initial improvement, he developed worsening hypotension and was transferred to the ICU for further management. His blood pressure stabilized with the initiation of vasopressor support. He was started on daptomycin at the standard dose of 6 mg/kg/day, but after 72 hours, there was no improvement in his clinical condition. Therefore, he was deemed eligible for the study and randomized to receive a daily dose of 12mg/kg of daptomycin to better characterize the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of high-dose daptomycin in septic shock patients. He will be closely monitored for adverse events and clinical response to treatment.

A 62-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years complains of burning and shooting pain in both feet for the past 6 months. The pain is moderate to severe and interferes with his daily activities. He takes metformin and glipizide to control his blood sugar levels. His HbA1c is 8.5% at screening. He does not have any history of allergies or chronic illnesses. He does not smoke or drink. He has a BMI of 30. He has no history of amputations or open ulcers. He has no history of peripheral vascular disease or Charcot joint. He has no history of other types of neuropathy. He is married and has two children. He is retired and used to work in construction. He has not been regularly exercising due to his pain. His VAS score for pain is 70mm at the end of the washout phase.

The patient is a 16-year-old African-American male with sickle cell disease. He presents with severe pain in his right leg and chest pain for the last 12 hours. He reports no fever or chills. He has a history of recurrent hospitalizations for pain crises and has been treated with multiple blood transfusions in the past. His current medications include hydroxyurea, folic acid, and ibuprofen as needed for pain. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg, a heart rate of 90 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. His oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. He reports no recent steroid use and has no known allergies. His laboratory results show a serum CRP level of 7.0 mg/L. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 55 year old woman who underwent surgery for early stage epithelial ovarian cancer at the National Cancer Center in Korea between January 2001 and December 2010. She is currently not receiving any active cancer treatment and is available for telephone communication. The patient has no history of deep vein thrombosis. The clinical research coordinator will contact her to participate in a cross-sectional and questionnaire study to identify the incidence, feature, and clinical significance of leg lymphedema after gynecologic cancer treatment. The telephone interview questionnaire for Lower Extremity Edema (LEE) and gynecologic cancer lymphedema questionnaire (GCLQ) will be conducted to collect information on onset, severity, location, duration, and management of LEE. The patient will also be questioned to exclude other causes of LEE. The patient's participation in the study will help to identify effective management strategies for leg lymphedema after gynecologic cancer treatment.

This is a 67-year-old male veteran who is receiving healthcare at one of the five Veterans Health Administration medical centers in the southwest United States - Greater Los Angeles, Loma Linda, Long Beach, San Diego, or Las Vegas. He has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and has had at least two ICD-9 diagnostic codes for PD (332.0) in the administrative data from October 1, 2010, to present date or until recruitment target is met. He is at least 18 years of age and has the capacity to provide consent for study participation. He is not a study subject in the Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) VA cooperative study as these subjects are not to enroll in any other study per DBS study protocol. He is interested in participating in a randomized controlled trial to test the "Coordinated Care for Health Promotion and Activities in Parkinson's Disease" intervention in the VA. The objective of this trial is to implement and analyze whether a nurse-led, coordinated care management intervention, Care Coordination for Health Promotion and Activities in Parkinson's Disease (CHAPS), compared to usual care will improve adherence to evidence-based practice guidelines and improve health outcomes in Veterans with Parkinson's disease. He is willing to undergo a structured telephone survey at baseline, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months of the trial and is aware that he will be provided $25 per survey as compensation.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been taking Microgynon 30 for the past month as a contraceptive method. She has BMI of 23. She is a non-smoker and drinks less than 2 units of alcohol per week. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no chronic medical conditions or abnormal laboratory results. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not donated more than 1500 mL of blood in the past 12 months. She has not participated in any other clinical trial within the past 84 days. She has no history of seizure disorder or brain injury. She is willing to use an additional method of contraception during the study. She is willing to comply with study procedures, instructions, and restrictions.

Patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is currently between 24 and 33 weeks and 6 days gestational age. She presents with contractions of at least 6 per hour, uterine irritability, or symptoms such as cramping, pressure, and backache, with or without documented contractions. The patient has a cervical dilatation of less than 3cm and less than 100% effacement, and intact membranes. She does not have ruptured membranes, a known congenital anomaly, vaginal bleeding, cervical dilatation of 3cm or more, complete effacement, or a cerclage. The patient is not carrying triplets or greater and has not been transferred onto tocolytics. The patient has agreed to participate in the study, which will evaluate the use of both sonographic cervical length and fetal fibronectin in women being evaluated for suspected preterm labor. She will be randomized to either a standard arm or a protocol arm and will be managed accordingly. The primary outcome of the study is the length of stay in the triage area before discharge.

A 32-year-old female with a history of major depressive disorder presented with persistent symptoms of low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, and decreased appetite. She had previously tried multiple antidepressant medications and psychotherapy with little to no improvement in her symptoms. Her current medications include escitalopram and bupropion, but she continues to experience significant depressive symptoms. She has no history of psychotic features, bipolar disorder, or substance abuse. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no contraindications for anesthesia or ECT. She has given informed consent to participate in this study and is willing to undergo functional connectivity magnetic resonance imaging (fcMRI) before and after a full course of ECT.

The patient is an active duty military service member, a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing subacute low back pain for the past 6 weeks. He reports that the pain began after a strenuous physical training session and has been persistent since then. The patient's pain is described as a dull ache in his lower back, with occasional sharp pains that radiate down his left leg. He rates his pain as a 6 out of 10 on the pain scale. The patient reports difficulty with daily activities, including bending, twisting, and lifting objects. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to participate in an exercise or strengthening program.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of esophageal cancer. He was initially diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma and underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, he experienced a recurrence of the disease after completion of his first-line treatment. His performance status is ECOG of 1, and he has a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. He has no history of brain metastases or severe allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to Cetuximab or Bevacizumab. He has no history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy, myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 6 months prior to study enrollment. He has no known CNS disease, significant vascular disease, or symptomatic peripheral vascular disease. He has no evidence of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and has not undergone any major surgical procedures or experienced significant traumatic injury within the past 28 days. He is not pregnant or lactating and is using effective means of contraception. He is willing to comply with study and follow-up procedures and has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and currently taking methotrexate. She has been experiencing knee pain and swelling for the past several months. The patient has a history of allergies to corticosteroids and has not received any other immunosuppressive therapy for RA. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effectiveness of anti-TNF therapy on RA using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and ultrasound imaging. The patient will undergo evaluations of disease activity criteria for RA, including a DAS28 score. She will also undergo MRI and Doppler US to assess the volume and CE of the draining PLN and synovial inflammation in her knee joints before and after anti-TNF therapy or B cell depletion therapy. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse effects and must provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 46-year-old Caucasian woman presented with complaints of chronic nasal congestion, postnasal drip, facial pain and pressure for the past 2 years. She reports that her symptoms have not improved despite trying multiple over-the-counter medications and antibiotics. She denies any history of asthma, allergies, or previous sinus surgeries. She has never smoked and does not consume alcohol. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism, which are well-controlled on medication. Physical examination reveals bilateral nasal polyps and tenderness over the maxillary and frontal sinuses. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the sinuses shows evidence of chronic rhinosinusitis with a Lund-Mackay score of 6 out of 24. She has failed conservative medical therapy and has stopped treatment with topical or systemic corticosteroids for at least two months prior to endoscopic sinus surgery. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to pneumonia and septic shock. She required invasive mechanical ventilation and invasive blood pressure monitoring. A central venous catheter has been placed for hemodynamic monitoring. The patient is in need of fluid challenge to improve her blood pressure and organ perfusion. The patient has no history of head injury and is not a DNR patient. The patient is eligible for the trial as she meets all the inclusion criteria, and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 35-year-old woman presented with sudden onset vision loss in her right eye. She was diagnosed with a macula off primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachment. She has no significant past medical history, doesn't smoke or consume alcohol. She is an office worker who spends most of her day working on a computer. She underwent a physical examination and was found to be otherwise healthy. Her best corrected visual acuity in the right eye is 20/400. She was offered two treatment options: Pneumatic Retinopexy or Pars Plana Vitrectomy. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial to help the medical community evaluate the best treatment option for primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachment repair. She is willing to comply with all study-related procedures and sign the informed consent form.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with epilepsy in her early twenties. She experiences partial seizures that sometimes generalize. She lives with her husband and two children. She works as a nurse in a local hospital. Her past medical history is significant for high blood pressure and a previous right-sided breast cancer for which she underwent a lumpectomy and radiation therapy five years ago. She is currently on levetiracetam 3000mg/day and lacosamide 200mg/day, which have been effective in controlling her seizures. However, she has gained significant weight over the years and her BMI is 35. She mentions that her weight gain has caused her to be self-conscious and has affected her daily activities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her lose weight. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is compliant with her medications and follows up with her healthcare providers regularly.

30-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and impaired glucose tolerance as confirmed by a 2-hour post-prandial glucose level of 8.5mmol/l and fasting plasma glucose level of 6.0mmol/l. The patient denies any history of cardiovascular diseases or stomach and intestinal diseases. He is not lactose intolerant and does not take any medication that affects energy and glucose homeostasis or absorption of foods. The patient has not been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus and has not taken anticoagulants. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands that he may need to lose 500 ml of blood during the course of the trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with colon cancer. She works as a librarian and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has a BMI of 31.2 and a waist circumference of 102 cm. She is married with two grown-up children. She has never smoked or used any drugs. She reported feeling anxious about the upcoming surgery and is worried about her recovery process. Her cardiac assessment is normal. She has no history of orthopedic or neuromuscular disease. She completed the six-minute walk test with a distance of 360 meters. Her labs are within normal limits. She is eligible for the trial and will be randomized into either the prehabilitation or the standard care group.

A 65-year-old male patient presents with a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension. He has a non-healing wound on his right foot that has been present for several months. Despite several treatments, including antibiotics and topical agents, the wound has not healed. The patient is experiencing pain and difficulty walking due to the wound. He has no history of infectious diseases or mental disorders. He is not pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and receive local LED phototherapy with local transplantation of autologous dermal fibroblasts for the treatment of his non-healing wound.

A 58-year-old woman had an ischemic stroke 3 months ago and is experiencing difficulty in using her paretic arm. She has a Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) score of 32 out of 66. She is right-handed and the stroke affected her left side. She has no history of epilepsy or hemispatial neglect. She is able to communicate and participate in therapy sessions. She has no cognitive impairment and her Mini Mental State Exam (MMSE) score is 27 out of 30. She is not currently experiencing upper limb pain and has no contraindications to electroacupuncture or MRI. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate effectiveness of scalp electroacupuncture on motor function of the upper limb in convalescence phase of ischemic stroke. She has read and signed the informed consent form indicating her willingness to comply with the demands and restrictions inherent to the study.

Sophie is a 7-year-old girl who has been attending the same school for the past year. She has no history of ocular surgery or genetic disease. Her parents report that she spends most of her time indoors, either studying or watching TV. She has no complaints of eye pain or discomfort but they have noted that she often squints when reading or watching TV. Sophie's visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes during her last routine eye exam. Her family has no history of myopia or any other ocular disorders. Sophie's parents are willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has spread to her bones and liver. She has been receiving hormone therapy but has not experienced any improvement in her condition. The patient has measurable disease and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 1. She is post-menopausal and has undergone surgical sterilization. She has a negative pregnancy test and agrees to use two barrier methods of contraception or abstain from intercourse for the duration of the study. Her absolute neutrophil count, platelets, and hemoglobin levels are within normal range. Her prothrombin time and international normalized ratio (INR) are within 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) unless receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. Her potassium and magnesium levels are within normal limits, and her calculated creatinine clearance is above 30 mL/min. Her serum total bilirubin is within 1.5 times the ULN, and her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are within 2.5 times the ULN. Her alkaline phosphatase is within 2.5 times the ULN. The patient has voluntarily agreed to participate by giving written informed consent and has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks in the opinion of the treating investigator. She is willing to continue on the same AI therapy and agrees to participate in imaging protocol 7184 and is separately consented. The patient has not derived clinical benefit from prior endocrine therapy and has not received an ER blocking therapy within the past 6 weeks. She has not had prior treatment with an histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor and is not currently on any systemic steroids that have not been stabilized to the equivalent of =< 10 mg/day prednisone during the 30 days prior to the start of the study drugs. The patient does not have uncontrolled brain metastases or NYHA class III or IV congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 6 months, QTc > 0.47 seconds, or uncontrolled arrhythmia. She does not have Type I diabetes mellitus, known active viral hepatitis, a "currently active" second malignancy, or any condition, therapy, or laboratory (lab) abnormality that might confound the results of the study or interfere with the patient's participation.

Newborn male, born at 38 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 3.5 kg, delivered via spontaneous vaginal delivery. Mother was diagnosed with schizophrenia and was prescribed antipsychotic medication throughout her pregnancy. The infant was exposed to the antipsychotic medication throughout gestation. The mother's prenatal care was adequate with no reported complications during pregnancy. The infant has no congenital malformations or any history of liver dysfunction, renal dysfunction, or cardiovascular diseases. The infant is currently 4 weeks old and is being breastfed. The infant's neurobehavioral development will be evaluated by the Bayley-III assessment tool in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been suffering from allergic rhinitis symptoms during the birch pollen season for the past 5 years. She experiences symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes. She has a positive allergy test for birch pollen and Bet v 1. She has not received any immunotherapy in the past 3 years and is not symptomatic to perennial allergens or active seasonal allergy during the trial. She has no history of severe medical conditions or immunodeficiency conditions, including HIV. She is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, nor does she intend to be during the study. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol as instructed.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2). He has been experiencing symptoms of tinnitus, dizziness, and hearing loss. MRI scans have shown the presence of a vestibular schwannoma (VS) with a longest diameter of 2.5 cm. Surgery is not an option for him due to the high risk of complications. He has been informed of all available treatment options and has expressed a preference for participating in this clinical trial. He meets the eligibility criteria of having a confirmed diagnosis of NF2, measurable disease with at least one VS measuring 1.5 cm or larger, and a word recognition score of less than 90% in the affected ear. He has normal organ and marrow function, as well as a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He has not had chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past 4 weeks and has not experienced any major surgical procedures or traumatic injuries within the past 28 days. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for at least 6 months after the completion of bevacizumab therapy. He has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of participating in this study and has signed a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 50-year-old Chinese man who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction for the past 6 months. He is currently in a committed relationship with his female partner and is sexually active. He has not been taking any medication for his erectile dysfunction. He has no history of kidney, liver, heart, blood sugar level, eye, or central nervous system problems. He has no penile deformity or penile implant. He has not been diagnosed with HIV infection. He is not taking any medication that is not allowed in this clinical trial. He has no known allergies to tadalafil. He is not planning to father a baby, nor is his partner pregnant. He has not participated or discontinued from any other clinical trial in the past 30 days. He has not participated or discontinued from any other tadalafil clinical trial. He has no history of drug, alcohol, or substance abuse within the past 6 months.

A 56-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with lymphoma and is scheduled for high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplant. She has a history of hypertension and has been on medications for the past 5 years. She is a non-smoker and denies any history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has no known allergies to medications. Her baseline laboratory tests are within normal limits. She reports good oral hygiene and no history of dental problems. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to prevent oral mucositis, a common side effect of chemotherapy.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a body mass index (BMI) of 39. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both well-controlled with medication. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past without any significant weight loss. Her medical record shows no evidence of gastrointestinal infections, inflammatory bowel disease, thyroid diseases, or cancer. She has not taken any antibiotics in the last 6 months. She is interested in bariatric surgery and has been informed about the potential risks and benefits. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study to analyze changes in oral and intestinal microbiota before and after the surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who is generally healthy and has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.0 to 35.0 kg/m2 and a body weight of at least 50 kg. She is not pregnant or nursing and is not currently taking any medications that may affect the study results. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the nature of the trial and the potential risks and benefits involved.

A 35-year-old male with a history of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 8 years visited the clinic seeking treatment. The psoriasis affects more than 15% of his body surface area and causes him significant physical discomfort and emotional distress. He has tried topical treatments with little success and is now considering systemic therapy. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. He has no known allergies and is willing to use a highly effective form of contraception if needed.

The patient is a 35 year old refugee from Syria, currently living in Denmark. She has experienced multiple traumatic events, including being a witness to bombings and losing loved ones in the conflict. She has been diagnosed with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and is referred to an outpatient psychiatric clinic by her general practitioner. She speaks Arabic and is fluent in English. She is married and has two young children. She is currently unemployed and spends most of her time at home taking care of her children. She has difficulty sleeping, experiences nightmares, and avoids situations that remind her of her traumatic experiences. She also experiences feelings of guilt and shame related to her experiences. She has been receiving treatment from a psychologist for the past few months, but has not seen significant improvement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares music therapy with verbal psychotherapy to see if there is a more effective treatment for her PTSD. She is generally in good health and is not currently using any substances.

A 45 year old woman with a diagnosis of uterine fibroids has been recommended for a total laparoscopic hysterectomy. She is in good general health with no history of malignancy. She does not smoke and does not have any chronic medical conditions. She has not undergone any previous pelvic surgeries. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different electrosurgery devices for colpotomy. She understands the trial will randomize her to receive either a monopolar HOOC or plasma kinetic bipolar spatula during the procedure. She is willing to undergo vaginal exams and provide follow-up data on vaginal dehiscence, colpotomy duration, amount of mist during colpotomy, and amount of bleeding.

A 32-year-old African American woman has tested positive for HIV using ELISA test and Western blot confirms her diagnosis. She has no symptoms of HIV disease except for persistent generalized lymphadenopathy (PGL). She has no history of malignancy other than cutaneous basal cell or cervical carcinomas. She has no significant underlying medical illness that could interfere with the study completion. She has not taken any antiretroviral drugs for more than 3 months or any experimental therapy within 4 weeks of study entry. She has not taken any systemic corticosteroids within 4 months of study entry. She is willing to be followed by the study center for the entire 3-year duration of the study. She is mentally and physically healthy and able to provide informed consent. She is not abusing drugs or alcohol.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who smokes at least 20 cigarettes daily for the past year. She is in good health with a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 60 kg. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding, and is using a medically acceptable means of birth control. She is able and willing to comply with all scheduled visits and procedures of the study. She has never participated in any clinical trials nor has she donated or lost blood within the past 3 months. She understands and has signed the informed consent document indicating that she is aware of all pertinent aspects of the study.

A 50 year old male patient who suffered a heart attack about 2 weeks ago complains of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but is not on any medications. Physical examination is remarkable for tachycardia and bibasilar rales. ECG shows ST-elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin level is elevated. Coronary angiography shows an occluded infarct-related artery (IRA). The patient is otherwise in good health and willing to participate in clinical trials.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a known history of type 2 diabetes for the past 7 years. He has been using an insulin pump for the last 2 years to manage his diabetes. His last HbA1c was 8.5% three months ago. He has given his informed consent to participate in this study. He has been compliant with his medication and has a daily insulin requirement of 1.2U/kg/day. He has been taking pictures of his meals and snacks for the last 3 days as part of the study protocol. He does not have any comorbidities that could interfere with the study completion. He also has no difficulty in understanding the study procedures and is deemed fit by the investigator to comply with the operating instructions of the CGM equipment.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with primary CNS lymphoma (PCNSL) after experiencing headaches and vision changes for several weeks. The patient underwent treatment with high-dose methotrexate-based induction chemotherapy but unfortunately did not achieve optimal response (CR or PR). The patient has no prior history of immune checkpoint inhibitors or Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors. The patient is currently not on any other cancer treatments or medications. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2. The patient has no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders and is negative for HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), HCV-RNA, and anti-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-1/2 antibodies. The patient has a measurable brain parenchymal lesion that can be measured by brain MR or CT images. The patient has adequate organ functions, with serum aspartate transaminase (AST) and serum alanine transaminase (ALT) and total serum bilirubin all being within normal limits.
