The patient has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,200/mL, platelets of 75,000/mL, and hemoglobin of 9.0 g/dL. The patient's serum creatinine is within normal limits, and the prothrombin time/International normalized ratio (PT/INR) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) are both within normal limits. The patient has not had any major surgeries within the past 4 weeks and has not undergone any prior radiation with curative intent or minor surgeries/procedures within the past 2 weeks. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, has signed and dated the informed consent document, and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the study and for 12 months after the last dose of RAD or at least 2 days after the last dose of aclabrutinib monotherapy, if the patient receives acalabrutinib monotherapy for greater than 12 months after the last dose of RAD administration.

Patient is a 25-year-old male from the United States who is in good health and has no significant past medical history. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 22 kg/m^2. He is a non-smoker and does not use any nicotine-containing products. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He does not work in shift jobs and has not crossed more than 2 time zones within the last 48 hours. He has no current or history of sleep disorder. He has good peripheral venous access. He has no hearing impairment. He will be able to perform the CogState battery. He is willing to abstain from alcohol and drugs throughout the study.

55 year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of hypercholesterolemia, currently on a cholesterol-lowering medication, presents with a desire to reduce the dosage of medication and explore alternative options for cholesterol reduction. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has maintained a stable body weight over the last 6 months. She has no history of major cardiovascular events, familial hypercholesterolemia, hypothyroidism, liver or renal disease, or cancer. Her serum triglycerides are within normal limits and her blood pressure is well controlled. She does not consume more than 2 drinks of alcohol per day. She is interested in participating in a long-term dietary portfolio study that includes viscous fibers, soy products, almonds, and plant sterols, with the option for continuation up to 5 years. She is willing to have routine blood tests and measurements of blood pressure and body weight taken over the course of the study.

A 32-year-old woman living in Goncha Siso Enese district of East Gojam Zone, Ethiopia is interested in participating in the Trachoma Amelioration in Northern Amhara (TANA) clinical trial. She is a healthy individual with no known allergies to macrolides or azalides. She has no history of pregnancy or current pregnancy, and her child is over 6 months of age. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the protocol requirements. She understands the study's purpose and is aware that she may not receive the study antibiotic azithromycin if she falls under the exclusion criteria. She is willing to undergo the monitoring, treatment of trachoma, and examinations required for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old Japanese woman who has been experiencing severe knee pain due to osteoarthritis for the past few years. She has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief but has not found much relief. She has a BMI of 28 and is otherwise in good health. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has not had any previous knee surgeries and does not have any neuromuscular or neurosensory deficiencies. She is willing to undergo primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and has signed the Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved, study specific Informed Patient Consent Form. She is willing and able to comply with postoperative scheduled evaluations.

75-year-old male with bilateral cataracts and no previous ocular surgeries or history of retinal/vascular disorders, who is seeking surgical intervention for his cataracts. He has been experiencing difficulty with night driving and has noticed a decrease in his visual clarity overall. His corrected distance visual acuity is currently 20/50 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. He has no known neuro-ophthalmological conditions, inherited retinal disorders, or any other comorbidities that would prohibit him from participating in the study. The patient is able to understand the objectives of the trial and willing to comply with the post-operative follow-up schedule.

A 25-year-old female college student with a spinal cord injury came to the clinic seeking a more compact and lightweight wheelchair that can be easily transported and provide better mobility in tight spaces. She has been using a manual wheelchair for the past 3 years and is an experienced wheelchair user. She is able to transfer independently and has no active pressure sores. She drives her own vehicle from the vehicle seat. Her current wheelchair is too bulky and difficult to navigate in crowded places such as her university campus and public transportation. She has a 16" seat width and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the Endeavor manual wheelchair. She is excited to have the opportunity to try out a new design that could potentially improve her mobility and make her daily activities easier.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with mixed dentition phase (permanent incisors and molars erupted). He presents with complaints of jaw pain and headaches upon waking up in the morning. His parents report that he has a habit of grinding his teeth at night. He has no history of dental caries or chronic diseases that affect muscles or motor coordination. He is not currently taking any medications, such as anti-inflammatory agents, muscle relaxants, corticoids, anticonvulsants, or antidepressants. He is willing to cooperate during the evaluation. The patient will be evaluated for eligibility in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of infrared LED photobiomodulation therapy in children with sleep bruxism.

The patient is a 43-year-old Chinese woman who lives with her husband and their two children. She has been taking care of her sister who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 2 years. She works as a part-time clerk in a local company and also takes care of her children's daily needs. She has been feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the demands of caregiving and work. She has noticed a decline in her own mental health and has been experiencing anxiety and depression. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications for her mental health. She is fluent in Cantonese and has a moderate to high burden of care, as assessed by the Family Burden Interview Schedule.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and between 24 to 41 weeks of amenorrhea. She is a French speaker and understands the language well. She has a single pregnancy and requires intermittent monitoring. She does not have any known allergies to silver, polyamide, synthetic materials, or STIMEX gel. She does not have any wounds on her stomach. She is not participating in any other clinical trial and has not participated in one in the past one month. She does not have any defibrillator, vagus nerve stimulator, or high-frequency surgical device. She is not equipped with any device for electric stimulation. She is not under protection or incapable of following the procedure of use. She is affiliated with a social security system. She is interested in participating in this trial and has provided consent after receiving information from the investigator or midwife.

A 36-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder type II presents with severe depressive episodes lasting more than 6 weeks. She has been treated with various antidepressant medications in the past, but has not responded to any of them. She is currently taking lithium for mood stabilization. She reports having difficulty with concentration, memory, and decision-making. She has no other significant medical history, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication that may help treat her bipolar depression.

The patient is a right-handed 30-year-old male with no history of neurological or movement disorders. He has no contraindications to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). He reports being in good health and has not suffered any head trauma or undergone any neurodegenerative disorder. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the role of the premotor cortex in motor skill learning. He has no history of TMS and is willing to undergo an MRI scan prior to TMS testing at Emory Rehabilitation Hospital. The patient has read and understood the consent form and is willing to participate in the study. He will be compensated for his time.

This is a 55-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She was diagnosed with a permanent ischemic stroke based on encephalic MRI. She is eligible for intravenous thrombolytic treatment according to National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke criteria. She has no history of pacemaker, surgical ferromagnetic clips, cochlear implants, intraocular metallic foreign body, or iron implants. She does not have claustrophobia and has not expressed any known intolerance to contrast media (DOTAREM). She has normal kidney function with a Glomerular Filtration rate of 60 ml/min. She is able to accept protocol information and has been informed about the study. She has not expressed any opposition to participating in the study.

A 25-year-old female patient with a confirmed diagnosis of asthma according to GINA guidelines will be eligible for this study. She has been receiving daily treatment with inhaled corticosteroids up to the maximum dose per day indicated in the package leaflet for the past month. The patient has a Forced Expiratory Volume in one second (FEV1) of ≥50% of the predicted normal value for the patient, demonstrated after a washout period of at least 6 hours during which no short-acting β2-agonist has been inhaled. She has demonstrated an increase of ≥12% and ≥200 mL in FEV1 over her pre-bronchodilator value within 30 minutes after inhaling a total of 200 µg/180 µg of salbutamol/albuterol Metered Dose Inhaler (MDI) (or equivalent dose of Dry Powder Inhaler [DPI]) (the reversibility test). The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or of childbearing potential, and is using a reliable form of contraception. She does not have Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), is not a current smoker, and has not used tobacco products within the 6-month period prior to Visit 1, or who have a smoking history of greater than 10 pack years. She has not been hospitalized for an acute asthma attack/asthma exacerbation within 6 months prior to Visit 1, nor has she had an emergency room visit for an asthma attack/asthma exacerbation within 6 weeks prior to Visit 1. Additionally, she has not had a respiratory tract infection or emergency room treatment for an asthma attack/asthma exacerbation within 4 weeks prior to Visit 1. The patient does not require the use of ≥8 inhalations per day of short-acting B2-agonist (100 µg/ 90 µg salbutamol/albuterol MDI or equivalent dose of DPI) on any 2 consecutive days from Screening to Randomization.

A 42-year-old morbidly obese woman with a BMI of 48.4 kg/m² who has struggled with weight loss for several years. She has been evaluated by the Surgical Weight Loss Program of the Bariatrics Center of University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC) and has been approved to have a sleeve gastrectomy (SG) surgery at UNMC. She has not had any previous bariatric surgeries, but had a lap band placement and removal over two years prior to the surgery. She has no history of small bowel resection, right colectomy, or cirrhosis. She is not currently taking or planning to take any bile acid sequestrants. The patient is willing to participate in a study that will evaluate the effect of SG on post-prandial serum bile acids and how it impacts weight loss and co-morbidity resolution after surgery. She is able to read and write, and is willing to complete a meal challenge pre-operatively, and at 1, 3, and 12 months post-operatively, with measurement of post-prandial serum and urine bile acids. She is also willing to score satiety before and after the meal challenge using a Visual Analog Scale, and provide pertinent data from her medical charts at the time of the surgery.

The patient is a 16-year-old Latina female who identifies as bisexual. She has a history of self-harm behavior in the past 6 months and has shown signs of depression and emotion dysregulation. She lives with her mother and is willing to participate in assessments and treatment. She does not have any history of DSM V developmental disorders, organic mental disorders, or psychotic disorders. She is currently not in crisis and does not report any ideation with a specific plan and means to complete the plan. She is willing to accept assignment to either condition and provide sufficient locator information for follow-up.

The patient is a 32-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer. He has no known medical conditions and has never been hospitalized. He has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has not had any symptoms related to the virus. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. He consumes alcohol occasionally on social occasions. He has no known allergies to any medications or vaccines. He has not received any vaccines in the past 14 days and is not planning to receive any vaccines in the next 28 days. He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits. He is not pregnant or lactating, nor is he planning to have a child in the immediate future. He has been informed about the nature of the study and has voluntarily given written informed consent according to local regulatory requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with keratoconus 2 years ago. She has a stable refraction based on six subjective refractions within ±0.50 diopters of spherical equivalent during the past six months after corneal collagen cross-linking (CXL). Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is +0.3 LogMAR (20/40) with spectacles. Her central cornea is clear with a normal anterior chamber depth greater than 3 mm to endothelium, and intraocular pressure (IOP) of <20 mm Hg. Her preoperative endothelial cell count is within the FDA recommendations for her age and anterior chamber depth. She has a width of Angle greater than 30° and a pupil diameter of less than 6.25 mm. She has no history of corneal opacification, scars, cataract, retinal detachment, glaucoma, retinopathy, macular degeneration, neuro ophthalmic diseases, or ocular inflammation. She also has no history of keratitis or peripheral marginal degeneration. She has not undergone any previous corneal or intraocular surgeries and has not been diagnosed with autoimmune or connective tissue disease. Her central corneal thickness is greater than 450 μm, which is considered as the safety thickness for the residual stroma after removal of the epithelium during CXL.

11 year old female with a history of first unprovoked seizure, presenting with loss of consciousness and shaking of the right arm and leg. Her medical history is unremarkable, with no history of head trauma or family history of epilepsy. EEG showed epileptiform discharges. She has not yet started any anti-epileptic drugs. She enjoys listening to classical music, particularly Mozart's compositions. She has no hearing or cognitive impairments. Her parents are interested in exploring alternative therapies for her epilepsy, and are willing to have her participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of Mozart's music therapy.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for over a year. He has been on a stable dose of metformin for the past 6 weeks and has a HbA1c level of 65 mmol/mol (8.1%). He has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and is currently not on any antihypertensive medication. The patient has no signs or symptoms of coronary artery disease, and a cardiac MRI performed within the past year showed normal ejection fraction. The patient has not had any cardiac surgery or angioplasty within the past 3 months and does not have a history of stroke or any clinically significant cerebrovascular disease. He has no known cardiovascular disease and is not currently undergoing treatment for any malignancy. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is willing to comply with the study procedures and requirements. The patient has no contraindications to MRI and CT-PET scanning. The patient is willing to provide signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45 year old woman has been experiencing heart palpitations and shortness of breath for several months. She went to see her doctor and was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. Her body mass index (BMI) is 32, indicating that she is overweight. She has tried various diets and exercise regimens in the past, but has struggled to maintain a healthy weight. She is currently taking medication to manage her symptoms, but her doctor has recommended that she undergo atrial fibrillation ablation. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of an intensive weight loss program for patients undergoing atrial fibrillation ablation. She has signed the informed consent and is willing to travel to Hamburg for the duration of the study.

A 54-year-old male with a history of diabetes and coronary artery disease, who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath. He has undergone multiple diagnostic tests and has been recommended to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. His left ventricle ejection fraction (LVEF) is above 50%, and he has multivessel coronary disease detected by coronarography. The patient is stable and has no history of acute myocardial infarction or heart failure. He has no neoplastic disease, chronic diseases that may affect the inflammatory profile both systemic and epicardial or acute coronary syndrome. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits associated with the treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has recently immigrated from a country with a high incidence of tuberculosis. He has undergone a routine medical examination as part of his immigration process and was found to have a positive tuberculosis skin test (TST). He has no symptoms of active tuberculosis, but his chest x-ray was unremarkable. He works as a construction worker and has a wife and two children. He has no previous history of tuberculosis or any other significant medical conditions. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is concerned about the potential side effects of the medication and would like to participate in a clinical trial that compares the standard 6-month course of isoniazid with a shorter 3-month course of isoniazid and rifampin. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits. He has no history of hepatopathy or allergy to drugs.

A 30-year-old female patient who has undergone previous in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment and has at least one cryopreserved embryo is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient should be over 18 years old and not have any exclusion criteria. The study aims to investigate the effect of endometrial scratching on the transfer of cryopreserved embryos. The patient will be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will undergo endometrial scratching in the cycle preceding the transfer of the cryopreserved embryo, while the control group will not. The study will monitor the implantation and pregnancy rates of both groups to determine if endometrial scratching has a positive effect on the transfer of cryopreserved embryos.

A 42-year-old woman has been experiencing chronic neck pain for the past 6 months. The pain is usually moderate to severe and affects her daily activities, including work at a desk job. She describes the pain as a dull ache that radiates to her shoulders and upper back. She has tried pain medication and physical therapy, but the relief is only temporary. She has no history of spine surgery or osteoporosis. She is medically cleared to participate in exercise and can ambulate in the community without an assistive device. She has not attended Pilates or Yoga classes before. She is willing to attend 12 one-hour exercise classes instructed by experienced Physical Therapists with additional yoga or Pilates training. She is able to get up and down off the floor and make medical decisions independently. She is looking for a new approach to manage her chronic neck pain and is excited to participate in this study.

A 56-year-old postmenopausal Caucasian female with invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer 2 years ago. She has received two lines of anti-HER2 based regimens with at least one regimen with Trastuzumab. Despite these treatments, her cancer has progressed and is now metastatic. Biopsy results showed the tumour harbours a PIK3CA mutation. She is experiencing mild fatigue and occasional shortness of breath, but is otherwise stable. She has no significant medical history and no other known health issues. She exercises regularly and follows a balanced diet. She is currently not taking any medication. Her last HbA1c was 6.5% and fasting plasma glucose was 110 mg/dL. She has no history of bowel disease or cardiovascular disease. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial. Her ECOG performance status is 1.

30 year old healthy male with no history of significant medical conditions. BMI is within the range of 18 and 27 kg/m2. The patient is a non-smoker and has not consumed any tobacco products in the past year. They have no history of alcohol or drug abuse within the past year. They have no difficulty swallowing tablets or capsules. The patient has no history of asthma, urticaria, or other allergic type reactions after taking medications. They have not participated in any other clinical trial involving drug administration and collection of blood samples or donated blood in the preceding 12 weeks prior to the start of the study. Blood pressure and pulse rate are within normal limits. The patient has given informed consent in written form.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with colon cancer. He has no significant past medical history and has never received chemotherapy before. He is scheduled to start capecitabine chemotherapy at John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County. His performance status is good, with no significant limitations in his activities of daily living. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. His liver function tests, including AST/ALT, are within the normal limits. He has agreed to stop all vitamin supplements except for vitamin D. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on the validation of a computerized movement analysis system for colonoscopies and involves physicians/nurses with experience in colonoscopy and patients undergoing screening colonoscopies.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was found unresponsive in his home by his family members. They called emergency services immediately, and the patient was transported to the nearest hospital. Upon arrival, the patient was found to have had an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and was resuscitated after 10 minutes of CPR by paramedics. The patient was intubated and transferred to the ED of the participating hospital for further post-cardiac arrest care. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. He has no known drug allergies. Upon arrival at the ED, the patient was hemodynamically stable with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg and a heart rate of 90 beats per minute. The patient is conscious and alert but confused. The patient's family is supportive of aggressive organ supportive management.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He does not smoke or use any tobacco or nicotine-containing products. He does not consume any alcohol on a regular basis and has not consumed more than 4 units in the past 6 months. He weighs 70 kilograms and has a body mass index (BMI) of 23. He has no known liver or biliary abnormalities and has normal liver function tests. He has not participated in any clinical trials or taken any new medications in the past 3 months. He has no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications or drug allergies. He has not consumed any red wine, seville oranges, grapefruit or grapefruit juice and/or pummelos, exotic citrus fruits, grapefruit hybrids or fruit juices in the past 7 days. He is willing to use an approved method of contraception if he has a female partner of child-bearing potential during the study. He is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer after noticing a lump in her right breast during a self-exam. A biopsy confirmed that the cancer is HER2+ and she was advised to undergo chemotherapy with trastuzumab and taxane. Unfortunately, during the course of her adjuvant chemotherapy, recurrence was detected. The patient experienced a significant amount of anxiety and fear when she learned about the recurrence, but is determined to fight the cancer and is open to participating in clinical trials to find a treatment that works best for her. She has adequate organ function and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG)-Performance Status is 0. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not tested positive for HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. She is willing to submit written informed consent for study entry and understands the risks associated with the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol abuse presents with severe epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting for the past 2 weeks. His weight has decreased by 5 kg in the past 3 months. CT scan of the abdomen shows a mass in the head of the pancreas. Biopsy confirms pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension for which he takes medication. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He is scheduled to undergo pancreatic surgery in the next 2 weeks. He reports moderate anxiety about the surgery and postoperative complications. He is willing to participate in a prehabilitation program and early mobilization after surgery to improve his outcomes.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who recently experienced an acute coronary syndrome event and was hospitalized. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. His recent lipid panel showed an LDL cholesterol level of 120 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare the effectiveness of high-dose rosuvastatin versus low-dose rosuvastatin plus ezetimibe on carotid plaque inflammation. The patient understands that he will undergo 18FDG PET/CT imaging and that the study will last several months. He is willing to provide written consent to participate and has no history of carotid endarterectomy or stenting.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of smoking for 25 years and diagnosed with lung cancer. The patient is scheduled for lung resection surgery and has been classified as ASA II. The patient does not have a history of severe cardiovascular disease but has been diagnosed with mild hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. The patient has normal lung function with FEV1 of 85% predicted and FEV1/FVC ratio of 75% predicted. The patient has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate. The patient does not have any known allergies to medications or any other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. The patient has been advised to stop smoking prior to the surgery and has been compliant with the advice. The patient is currently taking medication for hypertension and has been advised to continue taking the medication as prescribed. The patient is otherwise healthy and fit for surgery.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia who has been experiencing symptoms for the past 5 years. He has a history of auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. He has been treated with antipsychotic medication but still experiences difficulty with memory and executive functioning, which has affected his ability to maintain employment and engage in daily activities. He has no history of neurological conditions or substance abuse within the past month. He is fluent in English and willing to participate in cognitive training.

45-year-old female with recently diagnosed stage 1 invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. She underwent breast-conserving surgery and is scheduled to receive radiation therapy as part of her treatment plan. The patient has no history of prior breast cancer, has good performance status, and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of different radiation therapy regimens on cosmetic outcome and patient-reported outcomes. She has no history of ipsilateral breast irradiation and her resection margins were negative.

50 year old female with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic hip pain that has been worsening over the past year. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and pain management without significant relief. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has no known psychological disorders. She is eager to explore surgical options and has been recommended for a total hip replacement using the Summit™ hip system. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the need for regular follow-up appointments. She has no history of participation in a clinical study with an investigational product in the last 12 months and is not currently involved in any injury litigation claims. She is motivated to improve her quality of life and willing to give voluntary, written informed consent to participate in the investigation.

14-year-old male patient with a previous diagnosis of Crohn's disease for 6 months, presenting moderate to severe symptoms despite conventional therapy. The patient has a history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and fatigue. The patient has not been treated with infliximab or any biological products. The patient has no severe intestinal strictures or previous stoma surgery. The patient and their parents are willing to participate in the clinical study and comply with the study requirements. The patient is currently enrolled in school and is able to understand and follow study instructions.

The patient is a 68-year-old female who has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue for the past year. Upon further evaluation, she was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis with an estimated aortic valve area of less than 1 cm2. She is scheduled to undergo aortic valve replacement surgery within the next 8 weeks. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and able to tolerate the required pre- and post-operative cardiac MRI, blood draws, 6-minute walk test, and arterial tonometry. She has no history of coronary artery disease and is able to undergo cardiac MRI with gadolinium contrast. She has no implanted medical devices or metallic objects in her body that would hinder the MRI examination. Her LV ejection fraction is greater than 50% and her estimated glomerular filtration rate is greater than 60 mL/min/1.73m2. She understands the study requirements and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 26 year old healthy female, non-smoker, with a BMI of 22 kg/m2, presents to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no history of respiratory disease, malignancy, or drug abuse. She is not allergic to lactose and has not used any prescription medication in the past 14 days, nor any over-the-counter preparations, including dietary and herbal supplements in the past 5 days. She is willing to abstain from alcohol, caffeine, and xanthine-containing beverages for 24 hours prior to and 24 hours after dosing. She has a good general health as determined by medical history, physical examination, spirometry, ECG and clinical laboratory tests. She is willing to give written informed consent and practice barrier contraception until she is discharged from the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a BMI of 24 kg/m2. She is a non-smoker and has no chronic diseases or hypertension. She is fluent in English and has good writing skills. Her dietary habits include consuming 5-6 portions of red and/or processed meat per week, with an average consumption of 80g per day. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently taking any medications except for oral contraceptives. She has not participated in any other research study in the last three months. She works a 9-5 job and enjoys cooking and trying new recipes. She also enjoys outdoor activities like hiking and running. She is interested in participating in this study to learn more about dietary patterns and their impact on her health.

A 15-year-old adolescent girl diagnosed with cancer and currently undergoing anti-cancer treatment at the MD Anderson Children's Cancer Center, Houston, Texas. The patient speaks and understands English and resides in the Greater Houston area. She has been diagnosed with cancer within the past 3-12 months and is eligible for this study. She is able to provide IRB-approved pediatric assent for participation in the study. The patient's parent, a 42-year-old mother, is also eligible for the study as a self-identified parent of the patient. The mother speaks and understands English and resides in the Houston metropolitan area. She is able to provide IRB-approved informed consent for participation in the study. The patient does not have any cognitive impairment or emotional distress that would limit her participation in the group discussion.

Patient A is a 35-year-old female who survived the Sichuan earthquake that happened 5 years ago. Since the earthquake, she has been experiencing symptoms of depression and Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). She has difficulty sleeping, nightmares, flashbacks, and feelings of hopelessness. Her relationships with family and friends have also been affected, as she has become more withdrawn and irritable. She is currently unemployed and has been struggling to maintain a stable income. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Interpersonal Therapy to help her manage her symptoms and improve her interpersonal functioning. She is able to attend weekly therapy sessions and is willing to give verbal informed consent. She does not have any history of drug or alcohol dependence.

45 yo F with a history of a right wrist fracture with subsequent development of CRPS type 1 characterized by severe pain (VAS score 8/10) and allodynia in the affected limb. She has tried various pain medications with minimal relief and has been receiving physical therapy with limited success. No other major medical or psychiatric history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition.

This is a 56 year old male with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia who presented to the hospital with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was confirmed to have COVID-19 infection by a respiratory tract PCR test. He has been hospitalized for 4 days and requires supplemental oxygen therapy. He has not received any investigational drugs or newly approved COVID-19 treatments within the past 30 days. He has no history of hypersensitivity to study treatments or similar drugs. He has not participated in any other clinical trial of an experimental treatment for COVID-19. He is not expected to receive any other agents or potential direct acting antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 during study drug dosing. He does not currently require admission to the ICU or mechanical ventilatory support. He has no evidence of cytokine storm syndrome or multi-organ system failure. He does not have a confirmed co-infection with influenza. His creatinine clearance is within normal limits. He has no history or current diagnosis of ECG abnormalities indicating significant risk of safety for participants participating in the study. He is willing to use basic methods of contraception during dosing of study treatment as he is a man of child-bearing potential. He has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old male patient with a history of coronary artery disease and ischaemic mitral regurgitation presents to the hospital for elective surgery for coronary revascularisation with repair of the mitral valve. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 30%. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain for several months. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no known allergies to any medications or food. He takes medications for hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, and diabetes mellitus. He has no history of liver or kidney disease. He is married and has two adult children. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to sign an informed consent.

A 35-year-old woman visited the family practice clinic with symptoms of a urinary tract infection. She was prescribed a course of oral antibiotics for 7 days. She has no history of gastrointestinal or vaginal symptoms. She is generally healthy and active, with no history of chronic bowel or digestive disorders. The patient has never taken a probiotic supplement but is willing to try one if it may decrease the chance of antibiotic-associated side effects. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and her medical history does not include any conditions that may contribute to diarrhea. She is not currently taking any laxatives or stool softeners. She is able to be contacted via telephone for follow-up.

A 27-year-old female with a history of using cosmetic products in the same category presents for a safety study of Dermacyd PH_DETINBACK (Lactic Acid) Sweet Flower. She has no history of lactation, pregnancy, or gestational risk. Her medical history is significant for seasonal allergies but she denies any atopic antecedent or allergy to cosmetic products. There is no evidence of active cutaneous disease in the evaluation area. She is willing to follow the study procedures and attend the clinic at the scheduled time. She is not currently taking any anti-inflammatory, immunosuppression or anti-histaminic drugs. She reports no diseases that cause immunology decrease, such as diabetes or HIV, and has no endocrinal pathologies. She also reports no intense solar exposure in the 15 days prior to the evaluation and has not received any treatment until four months before the selection. Her skin test in the region is integral.

A 52-year-old man with a history of multiple myeloma came to the clinic for a follow-up appointment. He has been previously treated with a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug, and an anti-CD38 antibody. His latest labs showed a serum M protein level of 0.7 g/dL and a kappa to lambda FLC ratio of 75. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status score of 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. He has no history of other malignancies and has not undergone any BCMA-directed therapy. He has good hematologic, renal, and hepatic function. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is interested in learning more about SEA-BCMA as a potential treatment option.

The patient is a 25-year-old lactating mother who gave birth to a healthy infant 10 days ago. She is exclusively breastfeeding her baby and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her and her child's nutrition. She has not consumed moringa leaf in the past and is willing to consume it in the form of porridge. She has no significant medical history and her child is healthy and within the age range of 6-59 months. The patient is able to feed her child orally and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 50 year old Japanese woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 3 years. She has been taking metformin as her sole oral antidiabetic medication, but has been experiencing inadequate glycemic control, with an HbA1c level between 7.0% and 10.0%. Her BMI is within the range of 17 to 40 kg/m2 and her creatinine clearance is greater than 30 mL/min. She has no history of type 1 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, biliary disease, or chronic or acute pancreatitis. She has not used a GLP-1R agonist or DPP-IV inhibitor in the past 6 months. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to examine the long term safety and efficacy of weekly subcutaneously injected albiglutide in combination with her current oral antidiabetic medication for a period of 52 weeks.

34-year-old male presenting with symptoms of depression including persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities he once enjoyed. He also reports difficulty sleeping, decreased appetite, and low energy levels. He denies any history of substance abuse or dependence, psychotic symptoms, or bipolar disorder. The patient has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a study to better understand the hormonal levels associated with major depressive disorder.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She was diagnosed with diastolic heart failure and has been previously hospitalized due to heart failure. The patient is currently on stable doses of heart failure medications including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-adrenergic antagonists, and aldosterone antagonists. The patient reports difficulty with exercise and is classified as NYHA functional class II-IV. The patient has not experienced any acute myocardial infarction or stroke within the past 6 months. The patient has not been diagnosed with COPD or any systemic inflammatory or collagen vascular disease. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study as she is premenopausal. The patient has not used any investigational drugs within the past 30 days and has not been exposed to alagebrium before. The patient has not been diagnosed with HIV or hepatitis C, and does not have hepatitis B surface antigen.

A 62-year-old male patient underwent radical prostatectomy for a prostate carcinoma with a Gleason score of 7 (4+3). Pathological examination revealed a pT3a tumor with a negative surgical margin. His PSA level was undetectable for 6 months postoperatively, but then increased to 0.5 ng/ml. Imaging studies did not show any evidence of metastatic disease or lymph node involvement outside the pelvis. He has a Karnofsky performance score of 80%. He has no other significant medical history, but has a family history of prostate cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the safety and efficacy of a hypofractionated radiotherapy for the prostate bed with or without the pelvic lymph nodes.

Pt is a 35yo F with a history of extensive burns on her right leg, requiring a skin graft surgery to be performed. She has been dealing with this wound for over a year, and despite multiple surgical interventions, it has failed to heal. She is otherwise healthy with no other comorbidities. The wound is located on the anterior aspect of the right leg and measures approximately 8cm x 6cm. The patient has been informed about the trial and has provided written and informed consent to participate.

A 56-year-old male presents with a history of chronic hepatitis B and C, and has been diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient has no previous history of systemic chemotherapy or any other treatment for his cancer. He has undergone transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) and is currently stable with no major side effects. The patient's liver function tests show a Child-Pugh score of 7, indicating mild to moderate liver dysfunction. The patient has no other significant medical problems and is able to carry out his daily activities with minimal assistance. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials and would like to explore the option of receiving BAY43-9006 treatment for his cancer.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been in a monogamous relationship with his partner for the last two years. He has been experiencing erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation during sexual intercourse for the last six months. He scores 18 on the International Index of Erectile Dysfunction (IIEF) and 13 on the Premature Ejaculation Diagnostic Tool (PEDT). He has no history of genital abnormalities, epilepsy, or severe renal insufficiency. Additionally, the patient has not experienced any medical events such as surgical interventions or neurologic conditions. He is not currently taking any medication that may affect the study drug's pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic properties. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who recently underwent hysteroscopic treatment for retained products of conception. She has a history of two previous pregnancies, both of which resulted in uncomplicated vaginal deliveries. She presents with complaints of persistent pelvic pain and heavy vaginal bleeding. A vaginal ultrasound reveals retained products of conception and she is scheduled for hysteroscopic treatment. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of Intercoat (Oxiplex/AP gel) in decreasing intrauterine adhesions and is willing to participate in the study. She has no signs of infection upon admission and is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 22. She is currently studying at a university and lives a healthy lifestyle with a balanced diet and moderate exercise routine. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. She has normal blood pressure and heart rate. Her lab results are within normal range, including hemoglobin, hematocrit, RBC, WBC, differential count, serum electrolytes (Na, K, Cl), fasting blood glucose, BUN, bilirubin, creatinine, AST, ALT, LD, alkaline phosphatase, and urinalysis. She has negative results for HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and drugs of abuse testing. She has no history of treatment for alcoholism, substance abuse, or drug abuse within the past 24 months, and no history of malignancy, stroke, diabetes, cardiac, renal or liver disease, or other serious illness. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, or any macrolide antibacterial agent. She has normal sitting systolic blood pressure and diastolic pressure, as well as heart rate above 50 beats per minute. She is able to read and sign the consent form. She has not donated blood within the past four weeks and does not smoke or use tobacco products or nicotine products.

An 82-year-old woman resides in a nursing home and has been experiencing incontinence for the past year. She has tried various disposable pads, but none of them seem to be effective in preventing leakage. She reports feeling embarrassed and uncomfortable due to the constant need for changing her pad. She has a MMSE-score of 25 and is able to communicate verbally. She takes medications for hypertension, osteoporosis, and arthritis. She has a history of falls and requires assistance with activities of daily living. The nursing home staff notes that she often experiences skin irritation and discomfort due to the incontinence. The patient and her family express interest in trying new technology that could improve her quality of life and reduce her discomfort.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who experienced sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath while at rest. He was immediately brought to the emergency department and diagnosed with ST Elevated Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) based on electrocardiogram (ECG) findings. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which have been well controlled with medication. He is currently on aspirin and clopidogrel. The patient has never undergone any cardiac interventions before and has no known allergy to contrast media. He has adequate pulses at both radial and ulnar arteries. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

A 30-year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection confirmed by two independent assays is eligible for group 1A of the clinical trial. He has been off ART for at least 8 weeks and has a plasma HIV-1 RNA level below 100,000 copies/ml. His CD4 count is above 300 cells/μl. He has no history of AIDS-defining illness within the past year and has no chronic medical condition other than HIV infection. He has never received any experimental HIV vaccine in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and use two effective methods of contraception if he engages in sexual activity that could lead to pregnancy. He has not received any vaccination within 14 days before the 10-1074 infusion. He has no history of severe allergic reactions or severe reaction to a vaccine or drug infusion. He has not participated in another clinical study of an investigational product currently or within the past 12 weeks, nor is he expected to participate in another study during this trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with multiple anterior teeth restorations. She reports experiencing occasional sensitivity and discomfort when eating hot or cold foods. She has a history of moderate caries risk and has had previous dental treatments including fillings and root canal therapy. The patient has a missing tooth due to trauma and currently wears a removable partial denture. She reports no history of orthodontic treatment. The patient is in good general health and has no contraindications for dental treatment. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent form and is willing to return for follow-up appointments.

42-year-old male diagnosed with HIV infection 2 years ago. He is currently taking emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and darunavir/cobicistat for the last 1 year. His latest viral load was 5,000 copies/mL and CD4 count was 300 cells/mm3. He has no history of nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor therapy. The patient reports good adherence to his current regimen and has not missed any doses in the past month. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options and contribute to HIV research. The patient has no history of malabsorption or chronic diarrhea and does not have any chronic nausea or vomiting. He has no history of seizures or any other significant medical events in the past 30 days. The patient does not have any active substance abuse and is compliant with his current treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who suddenly experienced difficulty speaking and weakness on the right side of her body. She was taken to the hospital within 3 hours of symptom onset. Upon evaluation, she was found to have a large vessel occlusion in her left middle cerebral artery. She has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is an alert and cooperative individual with no signs of dementia. She is being offered endovascular clot retrieval as a treatment option.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who is brought in by his mother for a routine eye exam. He has no history of eye or vision problems, and his family has no history of ocular diseases. He was born full-term and has been meeting all developmental milestones. He is currently not taking any medications. His mother reports that he enjoys playing on her smartphone, and he is comfortable looking at screens for short periods of time. The patient appears cooperative and is able to follow simple instructions. His visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and there are no apparent abnormalities on external examination. The patient is eligible for the study, and the mother consents to participate.

65 year old woman with stage IV lung cancer and metastasis to the bones, presenting with dyspnea at rest and requiring oxygen at 4 liters per minute to maintain an SpO2 > 90%. She reports that she experiences shortness of breath more frequently during the day and at night, which makes sleeping difficult. She has a history of COPD and asthma. Her current medications include albuterol, tiotropium, and oral morphine for pain management. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. She is currently under palliative care with the goal of symptom management. She has an oral consent to participate in the study. She is able to communicate effectively and understands the risks and benefits of the study. She has no history of non-invasive ventilation and does not require curative care.

31-week gestational age preterm infant, currently in NICU, born to a 26-year-old primigravida mother, who had an uncomplicated pregnancy until preterm labor. The infant has a birth weight of 1300 grams and is currently receiving oxygen therapy via nasal cannula. The family has no history of chronic or mental illness, and both parents are able to be present at the hospital for at least 10 hours a day. The infant has not been diagnosed with any congenital disease, brain injury, or musculoskeletal deformities. The family has consented to participate in the study, and the infant will be randomized to receive either early physical therapy intervention or standard care.

A 62-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with B-Cell Lymphocytic Leukemia (B-CLL) after experiencing persistent fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has not received any previous chemotherapy for B-CLL. She is currently at Rai Stage II with evidence of progression, including progressive lymphadenopathy with multiple sites of involvement and an increase in lymphocytes over the past two months. Her hemoglobin is currently 10 g/dL, platelet count is 90x10 to the ninth/L, and her absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 1.2x10 to the ninth/L. She has a WHO performance status of 1 and her serum creatinine, total bilirubin, AST, and ALT are within normal limits. She has no history of bone marrow transplant, autoimmune thrombocytopenia, or serious cardiac or pulmonary disease. She has not used any investigational agents in the past 30 days and does not have a known history of HIV, active tuberculosis, or central nervous system involvement with CLL. She is not pregnant or lactating and has agreed to use effective contraception while on study treatment.

45 year-old male with a history of unsuccessful dietary attempts to lose weight. He has a BMI of 31 kg/m^2 and has dyslipidemia that is being treated with statin therapy. He is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a study to help him lose weight and improve his overall health.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with myelofibrosis. He has previously participated in the MF-TG101348-001 study and completed the trial. He is currently stable and interested in participating in a long-term study to evaluate the effects of SAR302503 (TG101348) over a longer period. The patient is in good general health with no known medical abnormalities that would increase the risk associated with study participation. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 62-year-old man with knee osteoarthritis has been recommended for a total knee arthroplasty. He has no history of cardiac, hepatic or renal dysfunction. He is not currently taking any pain medication. He is otherwise healthy with an ASA score of 2. He is interested in participating in a randomized control study investigating the effectiveness of Dexmedetomidine for procedural sedation during the surgery to reduce postoperative pain. He has been informed of the potential risks and benefits and is willing to participate in the study.

We are looking for infants diagnosed with an isolated cleft palate under the care of a collaborating center for a clinical trial comparing the side-lying sleep positioning to back-lying. The aim is to determine the clinical effectiveness in infants with cleft palate of side-lying as compared to back-lying sleep positioning in reducing oxygen desaturation resulting from obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). Infants who are 3 to 5 weeks of age when monitored and parents willing to give consent and able to complete study procedures are eligible. Infants with associated cleft lip, born prematurely, with cardiorespiratory disease, requiring an intervention to assist with breathing or feeding are excluded. This study aims to provide parents with clear guidance on sleep positioning that could potentially limit the negative impact of OSA on their child's development.

A 72-year-old Chinese woman presents with decreased vision in her left eye for the past 3 months. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoporosis, for which she takes lisinopril and calcium supplements, respectively. She denies any history of ocular trauma or surgery. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in the left eye is 20/200. Slit-lamp examination of the left eye shows mild cataract, but no signs of inflammation or infection. Dilated fundus examination reveals active choroidal neovascularization (CNV) lesions secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in the left eye, affecting the central subfield. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirms the presence of subretinal fluid and intraretinal fluid. The total area of CNV in the left eye is estimated to be greater than 50% of the total lesion area. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of brolucizumab to aflibercept for the treatment of her neovascular AMD.

65-year-old Caucasian female with a history of Fuchs' endothelial corneal dystrophy presented with decreased visual acuity and glare. The patient has a history of cataract surgery in her left eye with an intraocular lens implant. She has not undergone any previous corneal surgeries or transplants. Her medical history is notable for hypothyroidism currently managed with levothyroxine. She denies smoking or drinking alcohol. She is retired and does not engage in any high-risk activities. On examination, her right eye shows corneal edema with a central guttae, and her visual acuity is 20/80. Intraocular pressure is within normal limits, and the rest of the anterior segment exam is unremarkable. The posterior segment exam reveals no abnormalities. Corneal topography demonstrates high astigmatism and irregularity. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating small incision DLEK surgery to treat her corneal endothelial dysfunction.

34 yo F, healthy with no significant medical history, non-smoker and non-drinker, with regular menstrual cycles, and no plans for pregnancy in the next 3 months. BMI is within the range of 19.0-25.0 kg/m2. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She has no allergies to the active substance or to isosorbide dinitrate and has no history of dysphagia or any disorder that may interfere with drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion, e.g. gastrointestinal, liver, kidney conditions. She has not had any significant changes in her diet or exercise habits within the last 3 months prior to screening. She has no food restrictions or intolerances and has not had any hospitalization or surgery within the last 3 months prior to screening. She has not made a blood donation or had a comparable blood loss within the last 3 months prior to screening. She has not participated in another study of an investigational medication within the last 3 months and has not taken any drugs known to have a well established toxic potential to major organs within 3 months prior to study administration. She has no clinically significant blood, kidneys, endocrine, gastrointestinal, respiratory, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, immunological and neurological disease. She is not lactating or pregnant and has had no unprotected sexual intercourse within 14 days prior to first drug administration. She has no history of drug abuse within the past 5 years, using any recreational drugs within 3 months prior to screening, or positive test results for urine drug scan. She has no positive test results for HIV, Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody or treponema pallidum. She has not used any drugs known to induce or inhibit hepatic drug metabolism within 28 days prior to study administration and has not taken any prescription medication or over the counter within the 14 days prior to study administration. She does not consume caffeine or any other beverages or foods that might affect drug absorption, metabolism or excretion, include coffee, tea, coke, chocolate, Animal viscera, dragon fruit, mango, grapefruit, grapefruit beverages or foods, etc. beginning 48 hours before each study medication administration through each study confinement period. She has not taken any vitamins or herbal medicines (includes herbs in the diet) beginning 48 hours before each study medication administration through each study confinement period. She has no illness during the screening stage and has no history of blood phobia or belonephobia. She is considered reliable and capable of adhering to the protocol visit schedule or medication intake according to the judgment of the investigator.

45-year-old female with a history of drug-resistant epilepsy since childhood. She has undergone multiple anti-epileptic drug regimens with no improvement in seizure frequency. She has been referred for surgical resection planning and is scheduled for intracranial EEG monitoring over a period of a week. The patient is able to give informed consent and has no major systemic illnesses or severe cognitive or psychiatric impairments. She does not report any excessive use of alcohol or other substances. The patient will be asked to participate in computer-based cognitive and emotional processing tasks during the monitoring period as a part of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 4 years ago. He received androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), which initially halted the progression of the disease. However, he has since developed hormone-refractory disease, as evidenced by the appearance of new lesions on bone scan and a rising PSA value. He has been experiencing lower back pain and difficulty walking due to bone metastases. He has not undergone any chemotherapy, biologic therapy, or alternative anti-cancer directed therapy. His performance status is 1, and he has no history of brain metastasis or untreated spinal cord compression. Prior radiation therapy was completed more than 4 weeks prior to registration. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his hormone-refractory prostate cancer.

This clinical trial is designed for children between the ages of 18 to 42 months who attend a community daycare. The study aims to determine the fluoride availability in saliva and dental biofilm after the use of increasing amounts of fluoride toothpaste. The trial requires 15 children who are willing to participate in the study and have their teeth brushed twice a day with different amounts of fluoride toothpaste. The study has a crossover and blind design. Children who have at least one active caries lesion will be excluded from the trial. Parents or guardians will need to sign an informed consent form for their child to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has a history of auditory hallucinations and delusions. He has been on antipsychotic medication for the past two years and has been following up with a mental health facility. He is living with his parents and has no job. He spends most of his time at home and rarely goes out or interacts with others. He has a high school education but has never attended college. He has a BMI of 26 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He has a history of smoking but has recently quit. He has been compliant with his medication regimen for the past six months. He has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to share his medical records with the researchers. He has not been hospitalized in the past 12 months for acute psychotic symptoms.

A 56-year-old man with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for the past 2 years presents for elective heart surgery with extracorporeal circulation. He has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild left ventricular hypertrophy. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His ejection fraction is above 45%. The patient has not undergone any previous cardiac surgeries, and he is not experiencing any symptoms of heart failure. He has a normal creatinine level of 100, and no history of endocarditis or peripheral vascular disease. The patient is able to understand the objectives and scope of the study and is willing to participate. His left atrium size is within the acceptable range for the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with gastric cancer in 2012. She presented with a 6-month history of abdominal discomfort, nausea, and vomiting. She had no significant past medical history and was a non-smoker. Biopsy of the gastric tumor showed it to be an adenocarcinoma. HER2 expression status was evaluated and found to be overexpressed. Staging workup revealed metastatic disease to the liver and lungs. She was started on a regimen of chemotherapy and Herceptin, and her response was monitored regularly. She completed 6 cycles of treatment and responded well, with a significant reduction in tumor size and improvement in symptoms. Her treatment was continued with Herceptin maintenance therapy. Her most recent CT scan showed stable disease with no new lesions. She has been on Herceptin maintenance therapy for 3 years and has experienced minimal side effects. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further investigate the role of Herceptin in the treatment of HER2-positive gastric cancer.

32-year-old male recently diagnosed with HIV with CD4 counts of ≥ 350/µL. The patient has no history of cotrimoxazole prophylaxis and no known drug allergies. He is currently asymptomatic and has not had any previous opportunistic infections. The patient has agreed to participate in a randomized controlled trial that will assess the impact of prolonged cotrimoxazole preventive therapy (CPT) on

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a BMI of 23. She has no medical history of metabolic diseases, allergies, or smoking. She has expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a food product rich in polyphenols on cognitive function and mood. She reports no issues with her cognitive function or mood but is interested in potentially improving her overall health and well-being through dietary changes. She leads an active lifestyle and has a balanced diet but is willing to incorporate the test product into her daily routine for the duration of the study.

This is a 53-year-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes and periodontitis. She has been struggling to control her blood sugar levels for the past year and has noticed that her gums bleed easily when brushing her teeth. She has also experienced bad breath and occasional tooth sensitivity. She is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant. She has been enrolled in a clinical trial to assess the prognostic effect of non-surgical periodontal therapy on serum levels of high sensitivity c reactive protein in patients with periodontitis and type 2 diabetes. She hopes that this study will provide valuable information on the correlation between these two chronic disorders and help improve her overall health.

A 9-year-old girl is being seen for follow-up outpatient care at a burn center. She sustained a severe burn injury when she was 4 years old, covering more than 50% of her body. The injury required multiple surgeries and skin grafts. The patient's medical history is significant for asthma, which is managed with daily inhaled corticosteroids. She does not have any known liver disease or preburn malnutrition. She has not used any multivitamins or steroids in the past. She is currently not taking any medications. She is accompanied by her mother and both have agreed to participate in the study. They have provided written informed consent and HIPAA authorization.

A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) three years ago. She has been experiencing episodes of muscle weakness, numbness, and tingling sensations. She has been treated with interferon-beta for the past two years, but her disease has progressed to an EDSS score of 4. She has no history of cardiac, endocrinological, hematological, hepatic, immunological, metabolic, urological, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, dermatological, psychiatric, renal, and/or other major diseases that would preclude the administration of natalizumab for the duration of the study. She is not pregnant and is willing to practice effective contraception during the study. She has signed informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial. She is starting on Tysabri monotherapy and will be monitored over the next 2 years to evaluate the effect of Tysabri on her MS lesions and normal appearing brain tissue (NABT).

This clinical trial is not applicable for patients as it is a quality improvement and research program for high-risk newborn infants and their families in Switzerland. The study focuses on collecting and analyzing data from neonatal units in Switzerland to ensure the quality and safety of medical care for high-risk newborn infants. There are no specific patient eligibility criteria for this study.

A 55-year-old man with a diagnosis of stage III colon cancer has been scheduled to receive chemotherapy for a maximum of 4 courses. He is in good health and has no underlying disease. He is currently taking daily medication to manage his blood pressure. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is not pregnant or nursing. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has no history of cardiac abnormalities or psychological problems. He has not received radiotherapy for the past 7 days and will not receive any during the study. He has not received any chemotherapy for the past 7 days and will not receive any concurrent prohibited medications (e.g., CYP3A4 inhibitors or other antiemetic medications). He has not received any antinausea medications for the past 7 days. He is not currently enrolled in any other investigational trials.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the past 6 months. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) of 14. His maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax) is between 5-15 ml/sec and he has a voided volume of at least 150 ml. The patient has no history of urinary tract infections or primary neurological conditions affecting bladder function. He is willing to participate in a 12 week study to evaluate the effects of UK-369,003 on his urinary symptoms and erectile function. The patient is willing to complete several questionnaires and provide blood samples during the study.

The patient is a 40 year old woman who recently visited her dentist for a routine check-up complaining of sensitivity to cold and hot temperatures in her upper right molar. Upon examination, the dentist discovered that the tooth had a necrotic pulp and asymptomatic apical periodontitis. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has no allergies to dental materials and has not received antibiotics in the past three months. The tooth can be properly isolated with rubber dam, and the patient has no periodontal pockets greater than 4mm. There is no evidence of previous endodontic treatment, open apex, crown/root fracture, root resorption, or calcifications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide microbiological samples during the different stages of the treatment protocol.

25-year-old male, sustained deep partial thickness burns on his right lower leg in a motor vehicle accident. The patient underwent debridement and was found to be a good candidate for split-thickness skin grafting. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has signed an informed consent and is willing to comply with the treatment for 3 weeks. He is willing to be randomized to either the MEBO dressing or standard care group. The patient's thigh area is suitable for the donor skin graft and is at least 5 x 5-cm in size. The patient is not pregnant or breast-feeding and has no known immune deficiency disorder. The patient understands that the study will take place at Zagazig University and is willing to travel there for treatment.

The patient is a 12-year-old Hispanic girl in 7th grade at a participating school. She speaks English fluently and is interested in playing new computer games designed for middle school children. She is willing to participate in the JUEGA study and provide her opinion on the games. Additionally, she is open to learning about health behavior and making wise choices to reduce the risk of having sex, drinking, and using drugs. She understands the importance of reducing these risks, especially since Miami has one of the highest HIV and AIDS rates in the United States. She does not have any developmental delays.

A 32-year-old woman has been wearing daily disposable soft contact lenses for the past 3 years. She works as a software developer and spends most of her day in front of the computer. She has no known eye conditions and has never had any eye surgeries. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She wears her contact lenses for approximately 10 hours per day, 5 days per week. She is interested in trying out new contact lenses to see if there are any improvements in comfort or vision. She does not currently wear Oasys 1-Day, MyDay, or Moist contact lenses.

Pt is a 10-year-old male with spastic cerebral palsy who is experiencing difficulty with range of motion and movement patterns compared to typically developing children. The patient has been diagnosed with GMFCS level II and has the ability to perform at least one bi-lateral heel raise. The child has not undergone any orthopaedic or neural surgery to the lower limb in the past 2 years, nor has he received Botulinum Toxin A injections in the last 6 months or planned during the intervention. The patient does not have any learning or behavior impairments that prevent full participation in the intervention. The patient and their family are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve stretching interventions for children with cerebral palsy. The trial will involve a combined strengthening-stretching intervention of the calf muscle, and the outcome measures will include muscle-tendon structure and gait analysis to assess functional improvements. The patient is aged between 7 and 14 and meets all eligibility criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes two years ago. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past six months, such as loss of interest in activities, feelings of worthlessness, and lack of energy. He is currently taking metformin to manage his diabetes, but his blood glucose levels are still not well-controlled. He smokes, drinks alcohol regularly, and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has access to the internet and is willing to participate in a web-based collaborative care system. The patient is fluent in Mandarin and has a score of 12 on the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). He is interested in improving his diabetes management and addressing his depressive symptoms.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of keratoconus. She has experienced a gradual worsening of her vision over the last year, making it difficult to perform daily activities such as driving and reading. She has tried different types of contact lenses, but none have been able to provide her with adequate vision correction. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to enhance the thickness, stability, and optical conformation of the cornea through the placement of preserved corneal tissue. She is willing and able to follow all instructions and comply with the schedule for follow-up visits. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to the test article or its components.

55 year-old male diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma for the past 5 years, currently treated with timolol eye drops once daily. He presents with a recent increase in IOP and visual field defects. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. He has never been treated with prostaglandin analogs or carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Best corrected visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes. Slit lamp examination reveals mild cataracts in both eyes. Ophthalmoscopy shows optic disc cupping and thinning of the neuroretinal rim, with no signs of glaucoma progression. His IOP measures at 24mmHg in the right eye and 26mmHg in the left eye after washout of timolol eye drops for 3 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with study medication use.
