The patient is a 30-year-old male who was diagnosed with Perthes disease when he was 8 years old in Norway. He experienced persistent hip pain and difficulty walking, which prompted his parents to seek medical attention. Upon further evaluation, Perthes disease was diagnosed, and he underwent several treatments, including bracing and physical therapy. He was followed up for several years, during which time he underwent periodic X-rays and physical examinations. The patient is willing to participate in the current study to assess the long-term outcomes of Perthes disease and its impact on his quality of life. He is able to give informed consent and has no other skeletal dysplasia.

Maria is a 56-year-old postmenopausal woman who is a breast cancer survivor. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy and currently is on oral anti-estrogens. She complains of vaginal dryness, burning sensations, and pain during intercourse. She has not used any estrogen replacement therapy in the past year. She has no history of pelvic or genital radiation therapy. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. Her recent CBC, glucose, and liver function tests are normal. She is not taking any omega-3 fatty acid supplements and has no known sensitivity or allergy to fish oil or omega-3 fish products. She is willing to undergo venipuncture at 0, 3, and 6 months and is able to follow the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and suffered from blunt chest trauma. He was initially managed conservatively with analgesics and chest wall strapping, but he continued to experience persistent pain in the chest. Imaging studies revealed a sternal fracture, and he was referred to the Assiut University Heart Hospital for further evaluation and management. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He has no allergies to medications. On examination, he is in mild distress due to pain. His vital signs are stable, and his oxygen saturation is normal. There is tenderness over the sternum, but no visible deformity or crepitus is noted. His chest X-ray shows a displaced sternal fracture. He has no associated injuries with an AIS score of less than 2. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo surgery using the LCP plates and screws fixation technique.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for several months. She has been diagnosed with bile duct stones and is scheduled for an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) procedure. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and does not have any other medical conditions that would contraindicate endoscopic techniques. The patient is not currently enrolled in another investigational study that would directly interfere with the current study. The investigator has determined that the patient is suitable for inclusion in the study.

A 35-year-old male veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan was referred to the VA hospital with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PCS) after sustaining a blast-related mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) during his deployment. He reports headaches, memory problems, and difficulty concentrating. He also experiences symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), such as nightmares and flashbacks. The patient has been married for 10 years and has two children. His wife, who is also his primary caregiver, reports that their relationship has been strained due to his symptoms. They have difficulty communicating and problem-solving effectively. The patient does not have a history of major psychiatric disorders or substance abuse. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that provides psychoeducation, communication, and problem-solving skills in a multifamily group (MFG) setting. The aim of this study is to improve community integration, interpersonal and emotion regulation skills, and marital satisfaction in married combat veterans post-deployed from Iraq or Afghanistan with mTBI and/or significant posttraumatic stress (PTS) or combat-related stress (CS). The patient will be randomized to receive either the Multifamily Group for TBI for Couples (MFG-mTBI-C) or a health education group which offers a supportive environment and basic education without skills training. The patient's participation will be preceded by 2-3 individual couples sessions. The patient and his spouse will be assessed pre- and post-treatment and 6 months post-treatment.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who reports occasional cannabis use through vaporization. He has no significant medical or psychiatric history and is in good general health based on physical examination, medical history, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, and screening urine and blood tests. He tests negative for recent cannabis use in urine at the screening visit and at clinic admission, as well as negative for other drugs of abuse, including alcohol. He is able to expectorate 3-5 mL of "native" oral fluid over a 5-minute period. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit and a negative urine pregnancy test at clinic admission. He has a body mass index (BMI) in the range of 19 to 36 kg/m2 and a blood pressure at screening visit that does not exceed a systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 150 mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of 90 mmHg. The patient reports no allergies to any of the ingredients used to prepare cannabis brownies (chocolate, eggs, wheat, etc.). He also reports no use of Over-the-Counter (OTC), systemic or topical drug(s), herbal supplement(s), or vitamin(s) within 14 days of experimental sessions, and no use of a prescription medication (with the exception of birth control prescriptions) within 14 days of experimental sessions. He has not used hemp seeds or hemp oil in any form in the past 3 months or dronabinol (Marinol) within the past 6 months. The patient has no history of xerostomia (dry mouth), mucositis, gum infection or bleeding, or other significant oral cavity disease or disorder that may affect the collection of oral fluid samples. He does not have a history of clinically significant cardiac arrhythmias or vasospastic disease (e.g., Prinzmetal's angina), and his EKG results are normal. The patient reports no history of epilepsy or seizures. The patient is not enrolled in another clinical trial or have received any drug as part of a research study within 30 days prior to dosing.

74-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and venous reflux disease presents with a non-healing venous stasis ulcer on her right lower leg. She reports that she has had the ulcer for several months and has tried various conventional wound therapies, including dressings and pressure off-loading, but has not seen any improvement. The ulcer has a surface area of approximately 20 cm2 and is located on the medial aspect of her lower leg. The patient has undergone venous hemodynamic correction via compression and sclerotherapy, but the ulcer has not improved. She is able to ambulate but reports some difficulty due to pain and discomfort associated with the ulcer. The patient is interested in participating in the DL-VSU-201 clinical trial to receive Dermacyte® Amniotic Wound Care Liquid, as she hopes it will help heal her non-healing venous stasis ulcer.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD by a child psychiatrist. He has difficulty paying attention in class and completing his homework. He is described as fidgety and restless, and he also interrupts others when they are speaking. He has been taking medication for his ADHD for the past 6 months and it has improved his behavior at school, but his parents still notice some difficulties with his attention and impulsivity at home. His FSIQ is above 90, and he is performing at grade level in his classes. He enjoys playing video games and sports. His parents are supportive of him participating in the study and are willing to attend the parent training sessions. He does not have any major neurological disorders or other brain disorders that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was previously diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma. He has been treated with sunitinib therapy, but unfortunately, he has progressed after the treatment. The patient is currently enrolled in a phase III study sponsored by Wyeth Pharmaceuticals, which aims to evaluate the efficacy of second-line therapy with either temsirolimus or sorafenib. The patient has provided written consent to be included in this correlative studies protocol, which will evaluate levels of serum factors of circulating VEGF and soluble VEGFR, circulating tumor cells, and circulating endothelial cells assayed at baseline and over the course of initial treatment. The aim of this study is to explore the relationships between these biomarkers and baseline patient factors, measurable disease response, and clinical progression. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of significant comorbidities, and has a good performance status. He has a supportive family and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a body mass index of 22. He has no history of chronic or congenital diseases and has no abnormal symptoms or findings on a medical examination. He has not taken any investigational products or bioequivalence test drugs in the past 6 months and has not taken any drugs that may affect the clinical trial in the past 10 days. He has not donated blood or blood components in the past 2 months. He is willing to comply with all instructions and has voluntarily given written informed consent to participate in the study. He understands the nature of the study after receiving detailed explanations from the researchers. He agrees to use double contraception method from the first administration of the investigational product until 7 days after the last administration of investigational product. He is able to consume a high-fat meal provided during the study.

25 year old Caucasian female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and no history of chronic diseases or smoking. The patient is not taking any medications and has not had any significant weight changes in the last 3 months. She has not undergone any overweight or intestinal surgery and her hemoglobin level is within normal range. The patient has no history of decreased renal function. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the mechanism of action of GLP-2.

56 yo F diagnosed with stage III follicular lymphoma after presenting with fatigue, night sweats, and a 5 cm left cervical lymph node. Biopsy revealed grade 2 follicular lymphoma with BCL2 gene-Jh rearrangement. PET/CT showed involvement of cervical and axillary lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow. Patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise in good health with an ECOG performance status of 0. Bone marrow biopsy showed less than 50% involvement with lymphoma. Laboratory studies show WBC 6.0K/uL, hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL, platelets 130K/uL, bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, AST 32 U/L, ALT 28 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 65 U/L, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as a previously untreated patient with histologically confirmed follicular lymphoma, Ann Arbor stage III, and measurable disease. She has normal organ and marrow function and is not receiving any other investigational agents. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is interested in participating in the study.

A 5-year-old girl was brought to the clinic with symptoms of fever, cough, and difficulty breathing. She was diagnosed with a respiratory infection and treated with antibiotics. Her symptoms improved, but she continued to have a persistent cough. Her physician suspected a secondary bacterial infection and prescribed clindamycin. She has a history of asthma and takes daily inhaled steroids. Her weight is 20 kg, and her height is 110 cm. Her last physical exam and lab study was performed 2 weeks ago and showed no significant abnormalities. She is able to take oral medications and has sufficient IV access for study drug administration and PK sample collection. Her parent has provided informed consent for her participation in the trial.

50 year-old male with a long-standing history of type 2 diabetes, currently on metformin and glipizide. No history of smoking. No significant past medical history otherwise. Patient presents with stable blood sugar levels and is seeking to participate in the study to assess the pharmacokinetics of two formulations of MK-1006. No history of major endocrine, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, blood, liver, immune, kidney, respiratory, or genitourinary abnormalities or diseases. No history of cancer or neurological disorders.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cancer of the cervix. She has been married for 10 years and has two children. She works as a nurse and has always been an active and independent person. She is worried about the impact of cancer on her sexuality and her relationship with her husband. She has noticed a decrease in her libido since her diagnosis and is finding it hard to communicate with her partner about her feelings. She is currently undergoing treatment and is scheduled to complete it in three months. She is interested in participating in a study that looks at the relationship between cancer, sexuality and communication in couples. Her cancer is in the early stage, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has no history of psychiatric illness or other cancer, and there are no signs of metastases.

The patient is a 50 year old male who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 3 years. His HbA1c level during the last clinical visit was 9.2% (77 mmol/mol). He is currently taking non-insulin antihyperglycemic drugs but it is not adequately controlling his blood sugar levels. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, both of which are being managed with medication. He is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is currently working as an office manager and is able to control his diabetes with his current medication regimen. He has no history of severe hypoglycemia resulting in coma/seizures or hospitalization for diabetic ketoacidosis in the last 6 months before screening visit. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he hopes to improve his diabetes management and potentially reduce his medication burden.

57-year-old female with a history of GERD presented with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss. Endoscopy and biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the gastro-esophageal junction. CT scan revealed metastatic disease to the liver and lungs. The patient underwent liver and lung biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic adenocarcinoma with HER2 positivity. The patient did not receive prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease. The patient is currently experiencing an ECOG performance status of 2. The patient has adequate renal function with creatinine clearance greater than or equal to 45 mL/min. The patient has no other significant medical history except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 50%. The patient is not pregnant and has no evidence of active infections with HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.

A 56-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer came to the clinic complaining of abdominal pain and weight loss. She was diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas with metastasis to the liver and peritoneum. She underwent gemcitabine-based chemotherapy with limited response, and now has no standard treatment options. Her ECOG Performance Status is 1, and she has adequate cardiovascular function with no history of serious cardiac diseases. Her neutrophil count is 2.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin is 120 g/L, and platelet count is 130 x 10^9/L. Her bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels are within normal limits, and her creatinine level is 0.9 x UNL. She has not received more than 240 mg/m2 of doxorubicin or 300 mg/m2 of epirubicin in the past. She is not receiving any drugs that are known to interact with pantoprazole. She has no untreated brain or meningeal metastases, and her treated brain metastases have been stable for over 3 months. She has well-controlled hypertension and is not on clopidogrel. She is willing to give written, informed consent prior to study participation.

A 65-year-old retired teacher visited the community services for older adults in Flanders, interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle program. She enjoys gardening and taking walks but has noticed a decrease in her physical abilities lately. She has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She is able to attend weekly meetings and is excited to be included in the co-creation process for the AHAA program.

A 25-year-old male who presents to the emergency department with pain and swelling in his right hand after punching a wall in a fit of anger. The patient reports that he has never experienced anything like this before and is concerned about his ability to work with his hand in the future. After being evaluated by the emergency department staff, the patient is referred to the division of plastic and reconstructive surgery at Sunnybrook hospital. During the initial consultation, the patient is informed about the clinical trial comparing short-term function and pain after no treatment or splinting for boxer's fracture. The patient is eligible for the study as he has a true boxer's fracture and is a candidate for either supportive splinting or tensor bandage. The patient speaks, reads, and writes English fluently and agrees to participate in the study. The patient is followed up with their hand surgeon at 4-, 8-, and 12-week intervals and asked to perform a grip strength test with a Jamal Hydraulic hand Dynanometer, fill out a Brief Michigan Hand Questionnaire, and complete a demographics survey. The patient is willing to participate in the study to help determine which treatment option will lead to shorter functional recovery and less pain during the first four weeks after initial treatment.

A 28-year-old healthy female presents for septorhinoplasty with planned bilateral osteotomies. She reports no nasal symptoms or complaints, such as rhinorrhea, sneezing, itchiness, or nasal obstruction. She denies any history of asthma or smoking. She has no known allergies, and her past medical history is unremarkable. She has no known systemic disorders or malignancies. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to adhere to visit schedules. She provides written informed consent and is willing to use adequate contraceptive precautions.

67-year-old male diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma located in the middle and lower rectum through colonoscopy and MRI imaging. The tumor is assessed as a depth of invasion that was confined to pT2, bN0 by ultrasound colonoscopy and/or pelvic MRI. The patient has a negative circumferential resection margin confirmed by MRI. He has no history of lower abdominal surgery, no signs of acute intestinal obstruction, bleeding or perforation needing emergency surgery. He has no unresectable distant metastasis or multiple metastases. He has not received neoadjuvant radiotherapy before surgery. The patient has a performance status (ECOG) of 1. The patient has given written informed consent for participation in the trial. He understands the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 58-year-old Greek man who has been smoking for the past 20 years. He was diagnosed with COPD 2 years ago and has been on treatment with a long-acting inhaled bronchodilator (LAMA) alone. He reports experiencing symptoms of breathlessness, cough and expectoration that have gradually worsened over time. He is able to perform his daily activities but with limitations due to his symptoms. He has not experienced any exacerbation within the last month before enrollment into the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is capable of completing the COPD questionnaire in Greek by himself. His past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is not currently participating in any other study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is in good overall health and has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions during her pregnancy. She is currently in her 24th week of pregnancy and is experiencing some fatigue and occasional nausea, but otherwise has had a normal pregnancy course. She has not previously consumed beetroot juice and is not allergic to it. She is not taking any medications that could alter endothelial function and has not taken any antibiotics in the past two weeks. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits.

A 35-year-old woman has been struggling with asthma for the past 10 years. Despite being on various asthma medications, she has been experiencing frequent asthma attacks and has had to make multiple visits to the emergency department over the past year. She was diagnosed with moderate-to-severe persistent allergic asthma and was started on omalizumab therapy per steps 5 & 6 of the NHLBI guidelines. She tested positive for specific IgE to perennial allergens and had a baseline total serum IgE level measured within the past year. She has been following up at AAIAST/AARC for the past 8 years and has been receiving omalizumab therapy for the past 6 years. Her asthma control test (ACT) score has improved since starting omalizumab therapy, and she has experienced fewer asthma exacerbations and ER visits. However, she still experiences occasional asthma symptoms and has been prescribed a rescue inhaler for use as needed. She is compliant with her omalizumab therapy and has not experienced any adverse reactions. She is interested in participating in the REALITY study to help better understand the long-term effectiveness of omalizumab therapy in real-life clinical practice and to identify predictors of response to the treatment.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of open angle glaucoma. Despite being compliant with medical treatment, his intraocular pressure (IOP) has remained uncontrolled. He has a history of trabeculectomy surgery on his right eye 2 years ago, with mitomycin C used as an adjuvant therapy, which resulted in a significant decrease in IOP, however, he experienced postoperative complications including low IOP and endophthalmitis. He is now scheduled for trabeculectomy surgery on his left eye and has been selected for this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bevacizumab as an alternative adjuvant therapy to mitomycin C. He has no history of systemic thrombo-embolic events and has not had any ocular surface infections within the past few weeks. He is willing to comply with the postoperative follow-up plan of at least 6 months.

A 52-year-old female was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy to remove the tumor from her left breast. She has no history of any other major illnesses or surgeries. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of anti-inflammatory phytomedicines on regulation of stromal immune cells and fibroblasts in breast cancers. She has read the consent form and is willing to provide a sample of her surgically removed breast tissue for the study. She is not pregnant and does not have any minor children or neonates.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) six months ago. He experiences pain and discomfort in his legs when walking, which limits his ability to exercise and complete daily activities. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no history of stroke or heart attack. He has never smoked but has a family history of cardiovascular disease. He is able to walk independently but is limited by his symptoms. His ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.85. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his walking ability and quality of life.

A 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and previous myocardial infarction presents to the emergency room with chest pain and shortness of breath. On arrival, the patient was found to be unresponsive, and CPR was initiated by the emergency team. The patient was intubated by the anesthesiology team, and a mechanical chest compression device was applied. The patient's initial rhythm was ventricular fibrillation, which required three shocks to achieve return of spontaneous circulation. The patient remains in cardiac arrest, and the team is continuing CPR. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this pilot study and will be randomized to one of the three ventilation modes for the next 15 minutes.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory distress and fever. He has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing shortness of breath for the past 2 days and his fever started yesterday. He is currently on insulin therapy and metformin for his diabetes. He has no known allergies to any medications. On examination, he is found to have tachypnea and tachycardia with a temperature of 38.5°C. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg with a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. His oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. His chest X-ray reveals bilateral infiltrates. His laboratory tests show elevated white blood cell count and elevated blood glucose levels. He meets the criteria for sepsis as defined by the 3rd consensus guidelines (sepsis 3) in 2016. He will be included in the clinical trial to compare causes and outcomes of sepsis between diabetics versus non-diabetics in Assiut University Hospital.

A 9-month-old infant living in Guatemala and consuming solid foods for at least the past 30 days. The infant is apparently healthy and not presently suffering from any acute illnesses like fever, diarrhea or respiratory tract infection. The infant is not severely malnourished and his/her mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) is over 115 mm. The mother/caregiver is willing to feed the infant with lipid-based nutrient supplements (LNS) over the three test days and over the 2-week home-use period, and report on his/her consumption and reactions and practices for daily use. The mother/caregiver is also willing to participate in discussion groups and planning to remain in the study area for at least the following three weeks. The infant does not have any known peanut, soy or milk allergies.

62 year old woman with a history of advanced breast cancer that has recurred and metastasized to her lungs, liver and bones. Recently, she has developed severe pain in her right hip and difficulty walking due to the cancer spreading to her bones. She has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiotherapy with no response. The patient is currently experiencing a decline in her performance status with an ECOG score of 2. She has normal renal and liver function and blood counts with no history of hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, mannitol or any of the cyclooxygenase (COX-2) inhibitors, sulfa drugs or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She has no active gastrointestinal (GI) ulcers or history of GI bleeding resulting from prior therapy with NSAIDs. The patient is willing to undergo a new treatment regimen and is not a candidate for standard treatment due to her comorbidities. She has no other concurrent invasive malignancy and is not currently on chemotherapy, radiotherapy or anticancer surgery. The patient is willing to use effective contraception if fertile.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. He is a retired construction worker who was exposed to asbestos for many years during his career. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past but did not respond well to the treatment. He has no history of brain metastases and his ECOG performance status is 1. His platelet count is normal and he has no cardiac or pulmonary diseases within the past 12 months. He is not pregnant or nursing, and has no bowel obstruction or any condition that would impair his ability to swallow medication. He has no serious illness or medical condition that would preclude study treatment. He will be able to take oral medication and reside within a 1.5 hour drive from the participating center. He has not undergone any major surgery or radiotherapy in the past 4 weeks and is recovered from any prior treatments. He has not undergone any prior surgical procedures affecting absorption and has not received any other antiangiogenic agents or multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors in the past. He is not currently undergoing any other concurrent anticancer therapy or treatment with other investigational anticancer agents.

This is a 65 year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, both of which are medically managed. His PSA level was elevated to 8.5 ng/mL, and biopsy of the prostate confirmed adenocarcinoma, Gleason score 7 (4+3). Bone scan and CT scan revealed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient is currently considering options for treatment and is willing to consider radiation therapy. He has not undergone any previous pelvic radiotherapy and is willing to participate in a study that will collect and measure biomarkers in prostate cancer radiotherapy patients.

A 30-year-old female presented to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. She was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma 2 years ago and underwent chemotherapy with high dose alkylating agents. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, which was controlled with losartan 50 mg daily. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and exercises for 30 minutes, 3 times a week. She has regular menstrual cycles every 28 days and has not used hormonal contraception or replacement in the past 3 months. Her BMI is 25 kg/m2. She has no history of infertility or any other medical condition known to be associated with premature ovarian failure or ovulatory dysfunction. She is interested in participating in a study to assess urinary hormones in female cancer survivors to better estimate the reproductive window and potential implications for fertility.

65-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer presents with a loss of appetite and unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds over the past month. He has no history of diabetes or hypertension and is a former smoker. He is currently on chemotherapy with carboplatin and pemetrexed. He reports feeling nauseous and has developed a metallic taste in his mouth. He denies any abdominal pain, diarrhea, or vomiting. He has a performance status of 2 (Karnofsky score 70) and reports that his quality of life has been significantly impacted by his loss of appetite. His BMI is 23.3 kg/m². He has no significant allergies or chronic medical conditions and takes only over-the-counter multivitamins. He has not used any appetite stimulants before.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy woman who has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has no history of any significant medical condition, including gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. She has not undergone any surgery of the gastrointestinal tract, and she has no history of any neurological or psychiatric disorders. She is a non-smoker and does not abuse alcohol or drugs. She has not participated in any clinical trial with an investigational drug within the past 2 months, and she has not donated blood within the last 4 weeks. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study or within 2 months after the study completion. She is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study and until 1 month after study completion. She signs and dates the written informed consent form prior to admission to the study in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and the local legislation.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU after suffering a heart attack. He has a history of hypertension and was prescribed a vasopressor medication to increase his blood pressure. Due to his critical condition, he is at a high risk for developing blood clots. The doctors have recommended enrolling him in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of a blood clot medication with concomitant blood pressure medication. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and meets the eligibility criteria. His weight is 65 kg and he does not have any renal or liver problems.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with inguinal hernia and has been scheduled for open mesh herniorrhaphy under general anesthesia. He has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and has been classified as ASA risk classification of II. He has no other physical or mental conditions that may affect the quantification of postoperative pain after herniorrhaphy. He is fluent in English and has provided meaningful written informed consent for the study. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and the use of the pain scales. He has no known allergies to amide local anesthetics, opioids, bovine products or inactive ingredients of the test article. He has not undergone a prior herniorrhaphy on the side that is currently scheduled for repair. He has not used long-acting analgesics within 24 hours of surgery and is not using aspirin or aspirin containing products within 7 days of surgery. He has not undergone major surgery within 3 months of the scheduled herniorrhaphy. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse or misuse within 3 years of Screening or evidence of tolerance or physical dependency on opioid analgesics or sedative-hypnotic medications. He has no impaired liver function and has no clinically significant unstable cardiac, neurological, immunological, renal or hematological disease or any other condition that could compromise the patient's welfare or ability to communicate with the study staff. He is not at risk for infection or slow wound healing and has no chronic painful condition that might interfere with the assessment of pain associated with the herniorrhaphy. He is not routinely using pain medication that could confound the pain assessments during the study, nor has he been treated with agents that could affect the analgesic response within 2 weeks of surgery. He has not participated in a clinical trial within 30 days of surgery.

54F with a history of severe periodontal disease, tooth loss, and multiple failed attempts at dental implants. Patient is in good general health, with no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and does not smoke. She has well-controlled diabetes and maintains good oral hygiene. On examination, the patient has a severely resorbed posterior mandible with only 6-7 mm of residual bone height. Despite attempts at bone grafting, there is insufficient bone width for traditional implants. The patient is interested in implant-supported restorations but has been told that she is not a candidate due to her bone loss. She is willing to undergo surgery and follow-up for the 5-year duration of the study. The patient has a stable occlusal relationship and is in need of at least 2 implants in the posterior region of the mandible. The patient has a favorable medical history and is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 62 year old male with a history of COPD and a current diagnosis of acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (AHRF) requiring non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in the hospital. He has a smoking history of 50 pack-years and is currently on a combination of inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. He has no significant co-morbidities and has been successfully weaned off NIV for at least 48 hours. Overnight polysomnography has ruled out significant obstructive sleep apnea. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to be randomized to receive either home NIV or sham ventilation. He has also completed a period of acclimatization and training in using the home pressure support ventilators before discharge from the hospital.

54-year-old male with a history of smoking but no known respiratory conditions. BMI is 27. He has not undergone any thoracic surgery and is willing to participate in the trial. The patient is able to cooperate with instructions and is not currently taking any medication that would influence respiration.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent heartburn and regurgitation of stomach contents into her throat. She has been taking over-the-counter antacids for relief, but her symptoms have persisted. She has no significant medical history, and her family history is negative for gastrointestinal disorders. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She underwent a screening endoscopy, which revealed no visible abnormality on conventional white light (WL) endoscopic examination. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial examining the efficacy of i-scan technology in improving the detection rate of reflux esophagitis and inter-observer agreement between endoscopists compared with conventional WL endoscopic examination.

The patient is a sexually active 25-year-old woman who is interested in using hormonal birth control but does not have a current prescription from a doctor. She has health insurance and lives in an area with access to a participating Fred Meyer Pharmacy. She is able to communicate in English and plans to continue using the same pharmacy for her contraceptive needs. She is not pregnant and is at risk for unintended pregnancy.

Patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is RhD negative. She is currently in her second trimester and has had no complications thus far. She has a history of one previous pregnancy in which she received RhD immunoglobulin after delivery due to her baby being RhD positive. The patient is interested in participating in the study to determine her fetal RhD genotype non-invasively. She understands the potential benefits of this test, such as avoiding the unnecessary administration of RhD immunoglobulin, and is willing to provide her medical history for the study. The patient has no underlying medical conditions and is receiving routine prenatal care.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 8 months ago. The tumor was ER/PR positive and HER-2 negative. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Her BMI is 31.2 kg/m2, and she has a history of hypertension and a family history of breast cancer. She is currently on tamoxifen for hormonal therapy. She is interested in maintaining a healthy lifestyle and is willing to participate in a weight loss program that may help prevent cancer recurrence. She is fluent in English and able to read and comprehend written materials. She is able to walk at least 2 blocks, and she does not have any other comorbid conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

68F with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis presents for cataract surgery. She has a history of mild dry eye syndrome and has been using artificial tears as needed. She is not on any blood thinners or antiplatelet medications. She is scheduled for phacoemulsification under local anesthesia. Her preoperative visual acuity is 20/60 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Intraocular pressure is within normal limits. Biometry measurements show axial length of 22.5mm in both eyes. Iris color is blue in both eyes. There is no evidence of capsular pseudoexfoliation. She consents to participate in the study and rates her pain level during the surgery as a 2 out of 10 on the visual analog scale. The surgery proceeds without any unexpected events or complications.

Patient is a 45-year-old Mexican-American woman from Texas who has a child participating in the "Predictors of Smoking in Mexican American Youth" (MATCh) study. She is married and works as a teacher. She is fluent in both English and Spanish. She has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. She exercises regularly and tries to maintain a healthy lifestyle. She is interested in learning about interventions that can benefit her and her family's health. She is excited to participate in this study to help researchers design future interventions that meet the needs of her community.

A 2-year-old boy fell while playing at the park and hurt his leg. His parents took him to the emergency department at a local hospital. X-rays revealed a toddler's fracture on his lower leg. He is otherwise healthy and has no underlying medical conditions. His parents are concerned about having to manage a full cast for a few weeks and the inconvenience that comes with it. They are looking for a more convenient and comfortable way to manage their child's injury. They are open to participating in a clinical trial that compares traditional cast placement to a removable walking boot with respect to pain control and how quickly children can return to their usual activities. They speak English fluently and have access to a phone and email.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with bipolar II disorder five years ago. She has been experiencing prolonged periods of low mood and fatigue, coupled with occasional episodes of hypomania. Her current medications include escitalopram (Lexapro) and bupropion (Wellbutrin), which have provided some relief from her depressive symptoms. However, she still experiences mood fluctuations and has difficulty with daily functioning. She has never taken lithium or lamotrigine (Lamictal®). She is not pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. She is fluent in English and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find better treatment options for her condition.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, chest pain, and coughing up blood. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He also smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. The patient underwent a simplified Well's score assessment, which indicated a high likelihood of pulmonary embolism. A D-dimer test was also performed, and the results were above the threshold for suspected pulmonary embolism. The patient was offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the accuracy of multi-organ ultrasound for the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. He provided consent to participate in the study and underwent ultrasound scans before undergoing a multidetector computed tomography angiography (MCTPA) scan, which is considered the gold standard for diagnosing pulmonary embolism.

Patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who is undergoing screening for potential unrelated donor hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). The patient has already received multiple rounds of chemotherapy and is now being evaluated for a potential transplant as a treatment option. The patient is willing to provide written consent for participation in this study, which aims to identify the best HLA matched, and as appropriate, preferred KIR donor to improve protection against relapse and improve leukemia-free survival (LFS) after URD HCT for AML. The patient will be evaluated by a transplant center, which will select the best donor based on HLA matching and KIR genotyping, as well as other variables that indicate the best URD for the patient. The patient will be excluded if the preferred KIR donor is not selected in favor of a less favorable KIR genotype donor, and the center will report the reason for the choice.

The patient is a 35-year-old HIV-1 positive male with no previous history of antiretroviral therapy. He has a viral load of 350,000 copies/ml and a CD4 count of 150 cells/ml. He is experiencing occasional mild headaches, but otherwise feels well. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has no other chronic medical conditions. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and is available for at least 48 weeks of follow-up. He is sexually active and willing to use effective barrier contraception during the study period. He is not currently receiving any experimental medication.

Patient B is a 24-year-old female who has been struggling with anorexia nervosa for the past 5 years. She has tried various treatment methods in the past, including medication and therapy, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She currently has a BMI of 14.5 and experiences intense anxiety around food and weight gain. She is also highly self-critical and experiences feelings of shame and guilt related to her disorder. She is currently unemployed and lives with her parents, who are supportive but struggling to understand her condition. She speaks fluent English and is able to make a commitment to attend weekly appointments. She has not received Schema Mode Therapy in the past and is willing to participate in this pilot case series to explore the potential benefits of this treatment method.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with gastric cancer. He has no significant medical history and has never undergone any surgeries in the past. He reports experiencing occasional stomach discomfort and bloating, but no other symptoms. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. The patient's labs show normal values for liver function tests, complete blood count, and electrolyte levels. Imaging studies, including CT scan and endoscopy, confirm the diagnosis of gastric cancer. The patient is a non-smoker, consumes alcohol occasionally, and has a BMI of 27. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has been informed of the potential benefits and risks associated with prophylactic cholecystectomy during standard gastric surgery.

The patient is a 22-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV. He is a Colombian national and has never received any antiretroviral treatment before. He is currently under the care of a healthcare provider in Bogotá and meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has not experienced any significant symptoms since his diagnosis. He is currently not taking any medications other than those prescribed for his HIV. His healthcare provider has referred him for genotyping sequencing to determine the prevalence of pre-treatment resistance-associated mutations (RAMs) affecting reverse transcriptase, protease, and integrase enzymes. The sample will be sent to the Molecular Medicine Laboratory at Hospital Clínico Universidad de Chile for processing and analysis.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a spinal cord injury that occurred when he was 18 years old. He has been paraplegic for the past 12 years and uses a manual wheelchair for mobility. He has been experiencing pain in his right shoulder for the past 6 months, which has been interfering with his ability to perform daily tasks such as transferring and propelling his wheelchair. He has not had any recent hospitalizations, cortisone injections, fractures, or shoulder surgeries. He does not have a diagnosis of complete rotator cuff tear, rheumatoid arthritis, adhesive capsulitis, or complex regional pain syndrome. He has no history of major depression or alcohol abuse. He is motivated to participate in the study and has the ability to complete the 12 weeks of treatment.

A 35-year-old Hispanic woman with a long-standing history of type 1 diabetes presented with difficulty in maintaining her blood glucose levels within the optimal range despite following a strict insulin regimen. She had previously tried various continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems, but found them to be uncomfortable and inconvenient. Her medical history was significant for depression, for which she was currently taking sertraline. She denied any allergies and had no known cardiac arrhythmias, pacemaker or ICD. Her vital signs were stable and her physical examination was unremarkable except for the presence of multiple insulin injection sites in her abdomen. She was interested in participating in the RADAR study as she was eager to try a new wearable-based dysglycemia detection and warning system that did not require invasive monitoring. She was able to read and understand the informed consent document and gave her consent to participate in the study.

Lee is a 46-year-old man with a history of recurrent episodes of abdominal pain that were often associated with nausea and vomiting. He visited the hospital with the same complaints, and his imaging studies revealed the presence of gallstones in his gallbladder. He was diagnosed with cholecystitis and advised to undergo cholecystectomy. Lee agreed to participate in the Korean Surgical Quality Improvement Program (KSQIP) to contribute to the development of a risk model for post-cholecystectomy complications. He provided his consent and met all the inclusion criteria for the study. Lee did not undergo any other abdominal surgery simultaneously and did not have any history of gallbladder cancer or cholangiocarcinoma. He was keenly interested in the feedback system that would be provided to reduce the risk of complications, thereby improving the quality of surgical care.

Patient is a 52-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with hypercholesterolemia with a LDL-C level of 120 mg/dL. He is at high risk of CHD due to a family history of heart disease and his own history of smoking for 10 years. He has been on a maximally tolerated dose of statin for 8 weeks and has been on a stable, low-fat diet for 12 weeks. His weight has been stable for the past 6 weeks. His past medical history is unremarkable except for mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. He has not experienced any significant health problems in the recent past, including heart attack, stroke, coronary syndrome, unstable angina, heart failure, significant arrhythmia, liver disease, cancer, or type I diabetes.

A 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago and underwent surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy is experiencing daily hot flashes. She has been postmenopausal for 18 months and has no history of migraines or hepatitis. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She reports no symptoms of depression and has a negative urine drug screen for illegal substances. She is fluent in English and is willing to provide informed consent. She is currently taking tamoxifen as part of her adjuvant therapy for breast cancer. She reports that her hot flashes are severe and bothersome, affecting her daily activities and quality of life. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve our understanding of the role of serotonin in hot flashes after breast cancer and potentially discover new treatments for this symptom.

A 45-year-old female office worker who complains of neck pain that has been ongoing for more than 4 weeks. She reports that the pain is located in the upper cervical region and is characterized by a spasm of the cervical muscles. She has no history of previous manual therapy treatment and no loss of sensory or motor function. The patient has no known rheumatologic diseases, no structural damage on cervical spina, and no history of trauma. However, palpable trigger points are detected on the upper thoracic region. The patient is seeking treatment to alleviate her neck pain and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of myofascial releasing on neck pain related to trigger points.

45-year-old female with a history of chronic lower back pain for over a year, rated at 6 out of 10 on the pain scale, despite conservative therapies such as physical therapy and NSAIDs. Patient has no prior history of lumbar medial branch blocks or radiofrequency ablation therapy. Patient has no hearing impairment and is willing to participate in the study. Patient enjoys listening to classical music and has a smartphone with headphones. The patient is not pregnant and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 50 year old male who has been experiencing difficulty achieving and maintaining an erection for the past year. He is married and has three children. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and occasional alcohol use. He has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions or undergone any recent surgeries. The patient has tried oral medication for erectile dysfunction, but it has not been effective. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

62 year-old male with recently diagnosed metastatic colon cancer which has spread to the liver. He has no prior history of chemotherapy treatment and has not undergone radiation therapy. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension which is well controlled on medication. He presents with a complaint of fatigue and abdominal pain. A CT scan shows liver metastasis with no signs of any other organ involvement. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the colon. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Serum creatinine is 1.2 and calculated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault equation) is 70 ml/min, bilirubin is 1.5, and serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT) is within normal limits. Alkaline phosphatase is 1.8 x upper normal limit. Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 2,000/mm³ and platelet count is 110,000/mm³. The patient has no evidence of significant active infection and has a negative serum pregnancy test. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 35-year-old woman presented with a fever, cough, and mild shortness of breath that developed 3 days ago. She reported no other significant symptoms such as chest pain, wheezing or gastrointestinal symptoms. She denied any recent travel history or contact with confirmed COVID-19 patients. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and migraine headaches. She was not currently taking any medications. Her vital signs were stable on presentation, with a temperature of 38.2°C, respiratory rate of 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation of 95% on room air. Physical examination revealed no significant findings. Nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2 virus. She was diagnosed with mild COVID-19 and was offered participation in a clinical trial evaluating a single dose of Peginterferon Lambda-1a. She was willing to participate in the study, provided written informed consent and had no history of interferon use.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He is currently taking metformin at a stable dose of 2 grams per day, but his blood glucose levels are still not well controlled. His HbA1c level at screening is 8.5%. He has a history of hypertension for which he takes medication. He is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He is employed as a software engineer and is able to attend all the scheduled study visits. He has no known history of gastrointestinal disorders and has no significant medical history other than diabetes and hypertension. He does not have any history of pancreatitis or pancreatic surgery. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. His BMI is 27 kg/m^2 and there has been no significant weight change in the last 3 months. His laboratory findings are within normal limits. He has not participated in any previous clinical trials with lixisenatide. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol and able to self-administer subcutaneous injections.

The patient is a pregnant woman expecting a singleton pregnancy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves measuring fetal hemodynamics changes in response to mild pressure induced by the abdominal ultrasound transducer. She has no history of multiple gestation and is currently in good health. She will be undergoing routine prenatal care and monitoring throughout her pregnancy. She will be asked to participate in one ultrasound session where measurements will be taken with and without the application of mild pressure on the abdomen by the transducer. The study will help to better understand how fetal blood flow responds to external pressure and its potential implications for fetal well-being.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a diagnosis of cataract and moderate elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). The patient is currently on medical therapy to control IOP, but it has not been effective. The patient is experiencing difficulty with their vision and would like to explore surgical options. The patient has no history of glaucoma surgery or any other eye surgeries. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares the efficacy of phaco alone vs. combined phaco plus excimer laser trabeculotomy vs. combined phaco plus trabectome. The patient understands the risks and benefits of each procedure and is willing to be randomly assigned to one of the three groups. The patient's IOP is less than or equal to 35 mmHg, making them eligible for the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 60 kg. She has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurological, dermatological, or allergic disease. She has not had any febrile illness in the past 5 days and has no history of lymphoproliferative disorders or malignancy. She is not currently taking any medications. She has no known hypersensitivity to caffeine. She is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, lifestyle considerations, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of primary open-angle glaucoma. He has been on maximum tolerated medical therapy including acetazolamide tablets but still has uncontrolled intraocular pressure. He has no history of previous ocular incisional surgery or active intraocular infection/inflammation. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares two different surgical techniques for trabeculectomy. He has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of the surgery and has provided written informed consent. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has never smoked and has no known drug allergies. His visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes and his intraocular pressure is currently 24 mmHg in the right eye and 22 mmHg in the left eye.

A 55-year-old male was recently diagnosed with esophageal cancer after presenting with dysphagia and weight loss. Endoscopic biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the intrathoracic esophagus. The patient underwent thoracicoabdominal computed tomography (CT), endoluminal ultrasonography, and positron emission tomography (PET) for staging, which showed a resectable tumor (T2N0M0). The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of thoracic surgery or trauma on the right hemithorax. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has provided written informed consent. The patient is randomized into the trans-substernal group of the Lifting of Gastric Tube Through Trans-substernal Versus Trans-esophageal Bed Path in MIE trial. The patient will undergo a minimally invasive esophagectomy which will consist of 4 steps: (1) thoracoscopic esophageal mobilization followed by mediastinal lymphadenectomy; (2) laparoscopic gastric mobilization followed by abdominal lymphadenectomy and gastric tube construction; (3) cervical esophageal mobilization and transection; (4) lifting of the gastric tube to the neck for gastro-esophageal anastomosis through trans-substernal path. The patient will be followed up regularly to evaluate intra- and post-operative status, morbidity and complications, nutrition status, as well as quality of life after surgery. The results of the study may help to individualize treatment for esophageal cancer.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer two years ago completed adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation six months ago. She has been experiencing fatigue and weight gain since the completion of her treatment. She has a medical history of hypertension, high cholesterol, and type 2 diabetes. Her medications include Metformin, Lisinopril, and Simvastatin. She is a former smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is currently working as a part-time accountant and spends most of her time sitting at her desk. She is interested in increasing her physical activity but does not have access to a gym or a personal trainer. She speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in a randomized study to increase her physical activity. Her BMI is 29, and she has not had any major surgeries in the last 6 months. She has received medical clearance from her oncologist to participate in an unsupervised, moderate-intensity physical activity program.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage III adenocarcinoma of the colon. She underwent resection of the primary tumor and 6 cycles of adjuvant FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) chemotherapy. She has no history of other cancers or serious illnesses, and her performance status is 1. Imaging studies showed progression of her liver metastases. The patient is interested in enrolling in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past two years. She has been diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) and has not been ovulating regularly. She has a BMI of 28 and her partner's semen analysis is normal. She has not been treated with any medication for induction of ovulation. She has a history of laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed 5 years ago. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol and does not use any recreational drugs. She works as a teacher and has a supportive partner who is also eager to start a family. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of laparoscopic ovarian diathermy (LOD) versus clomiphene citrate (CC) in treating her anovulatory PCOS infertility. She is willing to undergo a general anaesthetic if she is randomized to the LOD group.

A 42-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of chronic back pain for the past six months. She describes the pain as a dull ache in her lower back that is aggravated by standing or walking for long periods. She has tried over the counter pain medications and physical therapy with no significant relief. She has no history of spine surgery and is not pregnant. Upon examination, she has tenderness in the lumbar spine region. She also has difficulty standing on one leg with her eyes closed without losing balance. She is a good candidate for operational intervention and may be eligible to participate in the clinical trial evaluating postural balance and stability among patients with cervical and back pain.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with a BMI of 33. He presents with symptoms of low testosterone levels such as decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and fatigue. He has been diagnosed with obesity-related hypogonadism by his primary care physician. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and no known history of diabetes. He is not currently taking any medication that affects the pituitary-gonadal axis. The patient has no history of prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, thrombotic or embolic disease, or epilepsy. He does not drink excessively or abuse drugs. His PSA level is within normal range. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore treatment options for his hypogonadism.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with coronary artery disease. She is a non-smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. She works as an accountant and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has a family history of heart disease, and her father had a heart attack at the age of 60. Her current medications include aspirin and a statin. She has no history of prior cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Her left ventricular ejection fraction is normal, and she has no other significant comorbidities. Her coronary angiography shows a stenosis ≥ 70% in the left main coronary artery and the left anterior descending and circumflex coronary systems. She is eligible for the ROMA trial and is randomized to the multiple arterial graft group. The trial aims to compare the outcomes of patients who receive one ITA vs two or more AGs for CABG, and the patient hopes that the use of multiple arterial grafts will lead to better long-term survival and improved quality of life.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with pectus excavatum, a congenital chest wall deformity that causes the breastbone to sink into the chest. She is scheduled to undergo Nuss procedure, a minimally invasive surgical technique that involves the placement of a curved metal bar under the sternum to elevate it. She is otherwise healthy and able to ambulate independently. She has no contraindications for epidural catheter placement and is willing to participate in the early rehabilitation program. She is able to understand and follow instructions and is capable of performing the six-minute walk test and lung function test. She has given her consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 3-day-old infant diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) and scheduled for a Norwood procedure. The baby was born full-term with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. The pregnancy and delivery were uneventful. The baby has been stable since birth and has been receiving care in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The baby has no significant medical history, and there is no family history of congenital heart disease. The baby's vital signs are stable, with a heart rate of 130 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. The baby's abdomen is soft, and there are no signs of abdominal distension or tenderness. The baby is being fed through a nasogastric tube and is tolerating feeds well. The parents have provided written consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who collapsed at a local gym while exercising. He was found to be unresponsive with no pulse and was immediately given cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) by bystanders. Emergency medical services (EMS) arrived and continued CPR, and after several minutes of resuscitation, they were able to restore the man's heartbeat (return of spontaneous circulation or ROSC). The patient was then intubated and transported to a participating hospital. The patient is currently unconscious (Glasgow Coma Scale <9) and is being ventilated with a high flow of oxygen (FiO2 at 100%) through an endotracheal tube (ETT). The patient's oxygen saturation is currently measured at ≥95% with the oxygen flow set at >10L/min. The patient has no pre-existing oxygen therapy (i.e. for COPD) and has no advanced care directives in place. The patient is willing to participate in the EXACT trial to determine whether reducing oxygen administration to target an oxygen saturation of 90-94%, compared to 98-100%, as soon as possible following successful resuscitation from OHCA improves outcome at hospital discharge.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman from the United States who has been diagnosed with generalized vitiligo for the past 5 years. She has noticed that her vitiligo has not progressed in the past 6 months and is interested in exploring treatment options. She has tried topical treatments in the past but has not seen significant improvement. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of vitiligo and is willing to undergo all necessary study-related procedures.

35-year-old African American woman G3P2 at 31+6 weeks of gestational age presented to the labor and delivery unit with complaints of cramping and lower abdominal pain that started about 2 hours ago. She has a history of preterm labor with her previous pregnancy that was stopped with betamethasone and nifedipine. The pain is intermittent and not relieved by rest, and she noticed increased vaginal discharge. She denies any vaginal bleeding, rupture of membranes or fever. She has no history of chronic illnesses, surgeries, or allergies. Her obstetric history includes two previous vaginal deliveries at term with no complications. She is a non-smoker and denies drug or alcohol use. Her prenatal care has been uncomplicated, and she received a full course of antenatal steroids at 29 weeks. On examination, her vital signs are within normal limits. Her cervix is effaced, and the cervical dilation is 3 cm with a fetal station at -2. The fetal heart rate is normal, and there is no uterine tenderness or contractions noted at the time of admission. Her fetal fibronectin test is positive, and an ultrasound shows a cervical length of 1.5 cm with no signs of cervical funneling. She is deemed eligible for the clinical trial and consents to participate.

There is no specific patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on the impact of telemedicine and telephone consultations on the quality of care, appropriateness of care utilization, patient safety, and cost-effectiveness. The study will involve children aged 14 years and below who visit the ED for medical reasons. However, the study does not require any specific medical condition or demographic information about the patients.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with metastatic melanoma. He has undergone standard therapy including high-dose interleukin-2 therapy but has not responded to the treatment. He is HLA-A*0201 positive and has measurable disease. Patient A does not have brain metastases and has no coagulation disorders. His absolute neutrophil count, platelet count, and hemoglobin levels are within normal range. He has no major cardiovascular or respiratory illnesses, and his LVEF is ≥ 45% by cardiac stress test. Patient A is HIV negative, Epstein-Barr virus positive, and has no active systemic infections. He has not had any prior severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to any of the study agents, including eggs. He is not pregnant or nursing, and has tested negative for pregnancy. Patient A is willing to complete a durable power of attorney (DPA) and is able to provide signed and dated informed consent prior to participation in the study.

A 32-year-old female with a history of bilateral nasal polyps and asthma, experiencing recurrent sinus symptoms for more than 3 months, bilateral opacity on CT-scan imaging, and visible nasal polyps at endoscopy. The patient has undergone surgical resection but has had a recurrence of the polyps. The patient has been diagnosed with asthma for more than 2 years and has not had an acute asthmatic attack requiring hospital admission for the last 4 weeks. The patient is in good health and free of any clinically significant disease that would interfere with the study schedule or procedures or compromise her safety. The patient is willing to give informed consent, adhere to visit schedules, medication restrictions, and agree to perform daily diary entries. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding or premenarcheal, and has agreed to use adequate forms of birth control from first dosing to at least 3 months after last dosing. The patient is not on any prohibited medication at screening without a full wash-out period and has not had acute sinusitis, concurrent nasal infection, or a nasal or upper respiratory tract infection within two weeks of inclusion. The patient does not have cystic fibrosis, primary ciliary's dysfunction or Kartagener's syndrome by history, has never been diagnosed with a parasitic infection, cancer, or a medical history of HIV or hepatitis B or C. The patient has not received specific immunotherapy within the previous three months.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is a non-smoker and physically and mentally healthy. She has no history of cardiovascular abnormalities or conditions, syncope, or significant previous cardiac arrhythmia. Her potassium levels and blood pressure are within normal ranges. She has no history of disease or dysfunction of any body system that is clinically significant. She is willing to refrain from strenuous exercise during the study period. She has no family history of Torsade de Pointes or long-QT syndrome, or cardiac death or sudden death without a preceding diagnosis of a condition that could be causative of sudden death. She has no chronic medical condition requiring prescription medications and has not received any known hepatic or renal clearance altering agents within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She has not donated plasma or blood within 30 days prior to the first dose of study medication or has a history of blood donation of more than 450 mL within 3 months prior to dosing. She has not used any prescription medications/products, within 14 days prior to dose administration on Day 1 of Treatment Period 1, unless deemed acceptable by the Investigator, nor has she used any over-the-counter, nonprescription preparations (including minerals, and phytotherapeutic/herbal/plant-derived preparations), within 14 days prior to dose administration on Day 1 of Treatment Period 1, with the exception of acetaminophen used at recommended doses. She has not used any investigational drug 30 days prior to Day -1 of Treatment Period 1. She is a sexually inactive female and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage 3 lung cancer and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. He was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory distress and fever. Despite receiving antibiotic therapy, his fever persists, and he is experiencing dyspnea and chest discomfort. He has a history of prolonged use of corticosteroids for his lung cancer treatment. His lab results show a high white blood cell count, and chest X-ray reveals infiltrates in both lungs. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has not received any antifungal therapy in the past three days.

A 35-year-old man with a medical history of type 1 diabetes for the past 10 years came to the clinic for a check-up. He has been using insulin pump therapy for the past 2 years and is currently using insulin lispro U-100. His latest HbA1c was 7.8%, and he experiences frequent hypoglycemic episodes despite his current insulin regimen. He has no history of hypoglycemia unawareness, but he had one episode of severe hypoglycemia within the past 6 months, which required assistance from another person to treat. He has not been hospitalized due to poor glucose control recently. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve his glucose control and reduce his risk of hypoglycemic episodes.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has never had a colonoscopy before. He has a family history of colon cancer and wants to make sure he is screened for polyps. He is in good health and has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or other gastrointestinal issues. He has not had any positive or negative colon assessments in the past five years. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent. He does not have any conditions that would preclude compliance with study and/or device instructions.

This is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. The patient presented with abdominal pain and weight loss, which led to the discovery of a mass in the pancreas. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of neuroendocrine carcinoma of the pancreas, with a Ki67 staining of 25%. The patient has undergone surgical resection of the tumor and is currently undergoing adjuvant chemotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in this study to help identify prognostic factors for this disease and improve treatment outcomes for future patients.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl scheduled for an elective tonsillectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis. She has no significant medical history and is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) status I. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has not had any prior surgeries or procedures requiring general anesthesia. She has never had an internal jugular venous catheterization or cardiovascular system anomaly. The patient is cooperative and able to follow instructions, and she has no known phobias or anxieties related to medical procedures. The patient's guardian has provided informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and leg swelling for the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has seen her doctor several times and has undergone various tests, but her symptoms have not improved. Her most recent test revealed that she has pulmonary hypertension, which is an increase of blood pressure in the pulmonary vascular system. The doctor has recommended her to participate in a clinical trial that involves testing the effectiveness of Regadenoson in diagnosing pulmonary hypertension. The patient will need to undergo a clinical evaluation, blood tests, and an ECG to make sure that Regadenoson is safe for her. If eligible, she will undergo right heart catheterization as part of her clinical care and will receive Regadenoson infusion and inhaled iNO. She will be monitored by the doctor throughout the procedure, and vital sign measurements will be taken to ensure that her heart rate and volume are within normal range.
