The purpose of this study is to see if Regadenoson may offer improved ease of use, single dose administration, and better tolerance for testing for pulmonary hypertension than iNO. The patient will need to sign an informed consent form before participating in the trial.

A 58 year old woman was diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon. She underwent colectomy and had liver metastasis. The patient received 5-FU/leucovorin regimen as first-line chemotherapy for 6 months followed by irinotecan and cetuximab as second-line chemotherapy for another 6 months. Despite the treatment, the disease progressed, and the patient developed lung metastasis. She is now seeking further treatment options. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of having histologically confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, measurable disease, and progression after prior first-line chemotherapy with 5-FU/LV regimen and second-line chemotherapy with irinotecan and cetuximab. She does not have any active brain metastases and has not received any GARFT inhibitors in the past.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who has experienced knee pain for the past 6 months. The pain is usually present when she is squatting down or going up and down stairs. She also experiences discomfort when sitting for prolonged periods of time. The patient reports that she can feel the cartilage of her patella when it is palpated and that she experiences pain when performing the Clark sign test. She has not received any knee operations in the past 3 months and does not have any neurological diseases. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the mechanical properties of tendon structures in patients with patellofemoral pain syndrome and to potentially receive an exercise program to alleviate her symptoms.

A 55-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital due to sudden onset left-sided weakness and slurred speech 8 hours ago. She has no history of stroke, but she has hypertension and hyperlipidemia which are being controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Physical examination revealed left-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria. National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 9. A brain computed tomography (CT) scan was performed which showed no hemorrhage. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed a right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory ischemic stroke. She is currently receiving treatment with intravenous thrombolysis and is stable. She has no history of dysphagia and is able to swallow without difficulty. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her laboratory results are as follows: Hgb: 12 g/dL, WBC: 7500/mm3, Plt: 250,000/mL, AST: 30 U/L, ALT: 35 U/L, Alk P: 100 U/L, Bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, as it is focused on evaluating a behavior change intervention to promote improved sanitation practices in peri-urban communities of Tamil Nadu, India. Instead of patients, the trial will involve randomly selected residents above 18 years of age from eligible wards with 60% or less toilet coverage from selected town panchayats in Tamil Nadu. The study aims to assess the impact of a multi-level behavior change intervention designed to promote toilet construction, exclusive toilet use, and maintenance, and will include two rounds of surveys to assess toilet ownership, toilet usage practices of family members, and beliefs, norms, and other factors influencing toilet use. The study will also conduct a process evaluation to monitor changes from baseline to endline and identify successful pathways or bottlenecks to the adoption of improved sanitation behaviors. The trial will also include qualitative research using observations and semi-structured interviews with respondents and stakeholders to assess exposure and reactions to the intervention.

10-year-old Caucasian male with a past medical history of primary immunodeficiency disease (PIDD) involving a defect in antibody formation is being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial. He has been receiving immunoglobulin G (IgG) replacement therapy for the past three months with an average minimum pre-study dose of 400 mg/kg BW / 4 weeks and a maximum dose equivalent to 800 mg/kg body weight (BW) / 4 weeks. His serum trough level of IgG at screening is > 6 g/L. He has no history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection. Laboratory values at screening are within normal limits, and he has no history of hypersensitivity or persistent reactions to previous infusions. He has no severe IgA deficiency or known allergy to hyaluronidase. He is not currently receiving antibiotic therapy for an active infection, and he has a platelet count of 100,000/μL. He is not pregnant or lactating at the time of enrollment. His parents have provided informed consent, and he is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

A 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He is scheduled for an angiogram/PCI and has been recommended to undergo the transradial approach for the procedure. He is currently on a regimen of aspirin, clopidogrel, and a beta blocker. He has no known allergies and is able to understand and follow all study procedures. His radial artery flow is normal and he is eligible for the trial.

A 62-year-old male with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease at stage II is experiencing difficulty with breathing and decreased lung volumes. He has a history of smoking but quit five years ago. He has no respiratory comorbidities or history of thoracic or abdominal surgery. He is not currently experiencing any infections or hemodynamic instability. His Mini Mental Examination score is 32. He is currently taking levodopa/carbidopa for his Parkinson's symptoms. He experiences bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremors. He is married and lives with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve his lung function and overall health. His spirometry and respiratory muscle strength measurements will be taken before the start of the study.

A 28-year-old female, who has had regular periods, is planning to have a baby with her male partner in the near future. The couple is currently using contraceptive methods and has not tried to conceive before. The female has no prior pregnancy and has not undergone any fertility treatment. She has no diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or any other serious medical condition. The male partner has also not tried to conceive before, has no fertility-related conditions, and has no history of serious medical conditions. Both partners are willing to participate in the ISIS Study, which aims to evaluate the effect of lifestyle factors such as antioxidant status and diet on the couple's fertility. The study will measure the time-to-pregnancy and early pregnancy loss, as well as assess the diet and antioxidant status of both partners prior to conception. The study excludes individuals who have tried for 12 months or more to achieve a pregnancy without success, have received a diagnosis of PCOS, have a serious medical condition, or have fertility-related conditions.

A 45-year-old man presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting. A CT scan revealed free air and findings suggestive of acute perforated diverticulitis. The patient was admitted to the hospital and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. After two days of medical management, the patient's condition deteriorated, and the decision was made to proceed with surgery. The patient was approached for consent to participate in the Scandinavian Diverticulitis Trial and agreed to participate. He is not pregnant and has no history of bowel obstruction.

A 50-year-old female is scheduled for a mastectomy with axillary dissection for the treatment of breast cancer. The patient was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma in the left breast after a mammography and biopsy. She has no history of other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is post-menopausal and has two children. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. She is not allergic to iodine and has no history of hyperthyroidism or coronary artery disease. The patient's creatinine level is within normal range. She has not been on any medications that could interfere with the ICG during the two weeks prior to surgery. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The purpose of the study is to determine if NIF fluorescent imaging is an effective approach to detect the margin of the breast tumor tissue. The primary objective is to define the histological distribution of ICG at the level of tumoral and healthy tissues of breast cancer patients, while the secondary objective is to evaluate the ability of fluorescent imaging to determine the tumor volume and boundaries of the tumor tissues. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent feelings of anxiety and worry for several months. She often feels overwhelmed and has difficulty making decisions due to her fear of the unknown. She finds herself constantly seeking reassurance from others and often engages in behaviors such as checking and rechecking things to alleviate her anxiety. She has no prior history of psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any medication for her symptoms. She is interested in participating in an online psychoeducation program to learn more about her intolerance of uncertainty and how to manage her symptoms. She denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicide.

The patient is a newborn baby girl diagnosed prenatally with congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM), which is a rare congenital lung anomaly that affects less than 1/10000 births. The baby girl was born via cesarean section at 38 weeks and weighed 2.8 kg. She is currently being monitored by a multidisciplinary team consisting of obstetricians, neonatologists, pneumologists, pediatric surgeons, radiologists, and anatomopathologists. The team will register her clinical, biological, radiological, and histological data into a multicentric database using Secutrial® software. The main goal of this project is to increase knowledge of clinical and radiological evolution of CCAM and to analyze the pathological embryological mechanism underlying this malformation. The team hopes to contribute to the definition of a standardized procedure at the Swiss level for the treatment of patients suffering from these malformations and to improve the assessment of lesion evolution related to CLA.

3-month-old Caucasian male with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis through newborn screening is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial assessing biomarkers of lung injury in CF infants. The patient has not yet shown any signs or symptoms of lung disease. The trial will involve blood, urine, and bronchial alveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples, as well as an oropharyngeal swab, at approximately 6 months and 1 year of age, along with quarterly urine collections during outpatient clinic visits for the first 2 years of life. Lung function testing will also be performed at these time points. If the patient experiences a pulmonary exacerbation requiring hospitalization, additional samples will be obtained at 3 time points during the hospitalization. Additionally, the patient will be followed for 2 years with quarterly urine, blood, and sputum collections, along with pulmonary function tests, as part of the study's CF ≥ 8 Years of Age cohort. The goal of the study is to determine if the concentrations of biomarkers of lung injury in urine, sputum, and blood can be used as potential biomarkers of early lung disease in CF patients. The patient must meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria for enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who presents to her primary care physician for a routine check-up. She reports a family history of diabetes and has been told by her physician that she is at risk for developing prediabetes. Her fasting blood sugar is 109 mg/dL, and her HbA1c is 6.1%. Her total cholesterol is 180 mg/dL, and her LDL-C is 110 mg/dL. The patient has no history of liver or renal disease and reports no gastrointestinal issues. She has not experienced any major illnesses or surgeries in the last 6 months. She is not currently taking any medications for blood sugar, blood pressure, or blood lipid control. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of freshwater clam extract and its combination on the improvement of glucose and lipid metabolism in prediabetes patients. The patient agrees to cooperate in the trial and signs the written informed consent.

The patient is a 73-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with hypertension and osteoporosis. She has been driving for over 50 years and relies on her car to go to the grocery store, attend doctor's appointments, and visit family and friends. Recently, she has noticed that driving has become more difficult due to poor vision and slower reflexes. She has also experienced some minor accidents and close calls while driving. Her daughter, who lives in another state, is concerned about her mother's safety on the road and has suggested that she consider alternative transportation options. The patient is open to exploring other options but is hesitant to give up her independence and the convenience of driving. She is fluent in English and has a 5-minute MoCA score of 25. She has identified her daughter as her study partner and is interested in participating in the trial to learn more about driving decision aids and how they may help her make informed decisions about her mobility needs.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease according to the UK Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank Clinical Diagnostic Criteria. He has been on stable antiparkinsonian medication for the past 6 months. He reports experiencing motor symptoms such as tremors and stiffness, as well as non-motor symptoms such as anxiety and depression. He has no history of allergies or intolerances to any foods or medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and has never used recreational drugs. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, but his blood glucose levels are well-controlled with metformin. His HbA1C is 6.5%. He is currently at Hoehn and Yahr stage II. He is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study.

A 55-year-old male was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago. He has been taking L-dopa/DCI for the past 6 months and has noticed some improvement in his motor symptoms. However, he still experiences non-motor symptoms such as depression, anxiety, and fatigue. He has no other underlying medical conditions and is not on any other medications. He is interested in exploring traditional Chinese medicine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy and safety of using Lingzhi (Ganoderma) in combination with L-dopa/DCI in the treatment of Parkinson's disease. He is able to provide informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria, including having a Hoehn and Yahr stage < 4 on stable L-dopa/DCI treatment.

A 57-year-old female presented with a diagnosis of advanced ovarian cancer that has spread to her lungs and liver. The patient underwent chemotherapy and surgery but her condition did not improve. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation. She is currently receiving palliative care and her quality of life has been significantly affected. The patient is interested in participating in the AZD7762 and irinotecan study as she is seeking alternative treatment options. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled by medication, and no other significant medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications other than those prescribed for her hypertension.

A 55-year-old African-American man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) presented with fatigue, shortness of breath, and fluid overload. He has been on dialysis for the past year and his medical history is significant for hypertension and diabetes. He is married with three children and has been unable to work due to his health condition. His income is below 250% of the federal poverty level. He is not currently on the waitlist for a kidney transplant and has limited knowledge about the transplant process. He is interested in learning more about his options for a kidney transplant and improving his quality of life. He is fluent in English and able to read and write in English. He does not have any hearing or visual impairments. He has not had a previous kidney transplant and has not been previously told that he is not a candidate for transplant.

The patient is a full-term neonate born with moderate-to-severe neonatal encephalopathy and is being treated with therapeutic hypothermia (TH) at a temperature goal of 33.5°C for a duration of 72 hours. The infant requires sedation and/or treatment to prevent shivering during TH, as assessed by the Neonatal Pain, Agitation, and Sedation Scale (N-PASS) scores and a modified Bedside Shivering Assessment Scale. The infant does not have any known chromosomal anomalies or cyanotic congenital heart defects. The infant's parents have provided informed consent for participation in the trial.

35 F with a h/o infertility for 2 years who underwent an initial workup including a hysterosalpingogram which showed patent tubes, and a semen analysis for her partner which revealed decreased sperm motility and count. She was diagnosed with unexplained infertility and underwent 2 rounds of ovulation induction with timed intercourse without success. She was then referred for in vitro fertilization (IVF) and was randomized to receive intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) and laser assisted hatching (LAH). She had antral follicle count of 12, and a baseline estradiol level of 32 pg/mL. She underwent ovarian stimulation with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist protocol and had 8 oocytes retrieved, 6 of which were mature. 5 oocytes were fertilized with ICSI and 3 embryos were available for transfer on day 3, all of which underwent LAH. She had a positive pregnancy test 2 weeks later and a subsequent ultrasound confirmed a singleton pregnancy. She delivered a healthy baby girl at term.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of recurrent and metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma presents with worsening symptoms despite prior treatment with multiple lines of chemotherapy. She reports experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and bloody stools. A recent CT scan showed progression of the disease with multiple metastatic lesions in the liver and lungs. Physical exam revealed diffuse abdominal pain and a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. She has an ECOG performance status score of 1 and her lab results show a hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dL, WBC count of 3000/uL, and a creatinine clearance of 70 mL/minute. She has no history of hypersensitivity to EGFR, JAK, or STAT antagonists/inhibitors, and has not received any investigational therapy within the past 30 days. She is not currently pregnant or lactating, and has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study.

50-year-old male with a history of liver cirrhosis and currently on the waiting list for orthotopic liver transplantation at the Fondazione IRCCS Cà Granda - Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico, Milan, Italy. The patient reports no history of diabetes or cystic fibrosis. The patient will undergo routine clinical and laboratory assessments, including a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), to evaluate insulin secretion and sensitivity before and at various time points after OLT. The patient will be followed for at least 10 years after OLT with yearly visits to monitor for abnormalities in glucose metabolism, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular disease, and other illnesses.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a recent diagnosis of advanced gastric adenocarcinoma. She has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is currently managed with lisinopril. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for this diagnosis. Imaging studies have shown unresectable metastatic disease, with multiple liver and lymph node metastases. Her ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has provided written informed consent for participation in the study. She has a measurable lesion in a previously non-irradiated area, which meets the criteria for inclusion in the study. Her estimated life expectancy is greater than 12 weeks. Her laboratory values are within the required limits, including GFR >= 60 milliliter per minute (mL/min), ASAT =< 2.5 * upper limit of normal (ULN), ALAT =< 2.5 * ULN, bilirubin =< 3 * ULN, ANC >= 1.5 * 10^9 per liter, platelets >= 100 * 10^9 per liter, and hemoglobin >=10 gram per deciliter (g/dL) without transfusions. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is using medically accepted contraception. She has no history of prior malignancy other than gastric cancer within the past 5 years. She has no known contraindications to treatment with cetuximab, capecitabine and cisplatin.

60-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation and complete heart block, presented to the hospital for evaluation of syncope. He had no history of coronary artery disease or valvular heart disease. He underwent implantation of a Micra AV system for AV block. At the time of implantation, the patient was in sinus rhythm. He was discharged home with no complications. He has had no symptoms of syncope since implantation. His medications include metoprolol and aspirin. He has no other significant medical history. His family history is negative for any cardiac diseases. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol of the AccelAV study.

A 58-year-old individual has a history of rectal cancer and underwent surgery for the same, which resulted in a permanent ostomy or anastomosis. The patient has been experiencing bowel dysfunction symptoms such as diarrhea and constipation, which have been affecting their quality of life. The last date of treatment for rectal cancer was 12 months ago. The patient has not been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) such as ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease. The patient is able to read, write and speak English, and all study materials and telephone calls are only available in English. The patient is willing to receive diet modification coaching via telephone and 3 motivational messages per week via email and/or text message for 17 weeks, or general healthy living education via telephone and 3 motivational messages per week via email and/or text message for 17 weeks. The patient is willing to complete all baseline questionnaires and meet all eligibility criteria for the study. The patient has been informed of the investigational nature of the study and is willing to sign and give written informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

45-year-old female admitted to the hospital for severe abdominal pain and gastrointestinal issues. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been struggling with suicidal thoughts in the past few weeks. She has no prior history of suicide attempts. The patient has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease and is currently receiving treatment for it. She is able to provide consent to participate in the study and is fluent in English. She has not been previously enrolled in this study and is admitted to a medical unit that is participating in the data collection weeks. The patient does not have any medical conditions or cognitive impairment that would prevent her from participating in the screening or assessment.

The patient is a 57-year-old man diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) at a clinical stage of IIB or III. The patient has no small cell carcinoma or stage IV disease, and there is no evidence of brain metastases. The physician plans to proceed with definitive chemoradiation to treat the cancer. The patient is medically suitable for early concurrent chemoradiotherapy, with radiotherapy dose expected to be 60 Gy or higher, and is able to tolerate positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. The patient has no poorly controlled diabetes and no other malignancy within the past 3 years except basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer or carcinoma in situ. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and has tested negative for pregnancy. If fertile, the patient will use effective contraception during and for 3 months after participating in the study. The patient has not had prior thoracic radiotherapy or concurrent intensity-modulated radiotherapy.

10-year-old female with a BMI of 31.5 kg/m², which is above the 95th percentile for her age and sex. She was referred to the study by her pediatrician due to concerns about her weight and potential risk for metabolic syndrome. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. The patient has no known genetic diseases that could account for her obesity, and is not taking any medications that could contribute to weight gain. She has no significant past medical history, but her physical exam reveals acanthosis nigricans on her neck, suggesting insulin resistance. Her fasting blood glucose level is 110 mg/dL, and her lipid panel shows elevated triglycerides and low HDL cholesterol levels. She is otherwise healthy and has no symptoms of diabetes or other metabolic disorders.

This clinical trial is a school-based cohort study conducted in Southern Malawi. The patient is a randomly selected student in one of the four participating schools. The student must be between the ages of 5 and 16 and have a parent or guardian available for consent. The student must not have a known allergy or adverse reaction to lumefantrine-artemether. The trial will involve blood samples for microscopy and molecular detection of parasites, as well as interviews about bed net use and antimalarial treatment. The trial will take place during the rainy and dry seasons of 2015, and the student must be attending the school during the time of the survey.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of HNF1A-diabetes for 5 years. She has been on Sulphonylurea monotherapy for the past 2 years. Her blood sugar levels are not well-controlled despite multiple dose adjustments. She has no other significant medical history and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. Her HbA1c is 8.5% and her FPG is 10.2 mmol/l. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

55yo male with a history of colon cancer, status post hemicolectomy, who presents for surveillance colonoscopy. Colonoscopy reveals multiple polyps, with the largest measuring 1.2 cm in size. Pathology confirms the presence of adenomatous polyps with high-grade dysplasia. The patient is scheduled for surgical resection of the primary colon neoplasm along with the polyps. The patient has no significant comorbidities and is not an insulin-dependent diabetic.

35 year old male diagnosed with schizophrenia according to DSM-5 criteria. Has been clinically stable for the past 3 months and is currently under the protection of health insurance. Has signed up for the study and given consent to participate. No current severe or unstable somatic illness or neurological history (no brain injury or surgery). No current substance use disorder, major depressive disorder or mental retardation. Has not had general anesthesia in the past 3 months and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Not under legal control or in an emergency situation. Not currently taking antipsychotic drugs for the past 3 weeks.

Patient is a 72-year-old male nursing home resident with a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. He has moderate symptoms, including cough, fever, and shortness of breath, but his SpO2 level is above 85% on room air. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials involving treatment for COVID-19, and he is willing and able to provide written informed consent. However, he has a known hypersensitivity to Fisetin and is taking a medication listed in Protocol Appendix 1, which will need to be safely held during the IP administration. The patient's laboratory results show total bilirubin, serum AST, and ALT within normal limits. His hemoglobin, white blood cell count, platelet count, absolute neutrophil count, and lymphocyte count are also within normal limits. His eGFR and plasma and/or serum glucose levels are also within normal limits. The patient's attending physician believes that he is an appropriate candidate for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing dryness and discomfort in both eyes for the past 6 months. She has a history of meibomian gland dysfunction and has been using artificial tears to alleviate her symptoms. She has no known allergies or chronic illnesses and is not taking any medications. She wears contact lenses occasionally but has not been wearing them regularly due to discomfort. She reports that her symptoms have been affecting her daily activities and causing her to miss work. Upon examination, her eyes appear red and irritated, and her tear production is reduced. There is evidence of meibomian gland dysfunction, with visible gland blockages and thickened gland secretions. There is no evidence of infection or inflammation. The patient has not undergone any ocular surgery within the past 3 months and does not have Sjogren's syndrome.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with complaints of fever, chills, and shortness of breath. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. Upon admission, her vitals were taken, and she had a temperature of 101.2°F, a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute. Blood work showed elevated white blood cell count, and chest X-ray revealed infiltrates in the lungs. The patient is currently admitted to the ICU at Cabell Huntington Hospital for further evaluation and treatment.

A 12-year-old boy with univentricular congenital heart disease is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. He has a history of hypoplastic left heart syndrome and underwent a Fontan procedure at the age of 2. He is currently in stable condition with no evidence of heart failure or arrhythmia. His parents have provided informed consent for his participation in the study. The patient is able to perform the required tests as he is above the minimum required height of 120 cm. He has no medical contraindications for the exercise test and is not pregnant. The patient is able to understand and follow instructions for the tests.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who had a successful surgical repair of a ventricular septal defect (VSD) 2 years ago. She is currently attending elementary school and has been cleared for physical activity by her cardiologist. However, her parents report that she is not very active and prefers sedentary activities such as watching TV or playing video games. They are concerned about her overall health and want to encourage her to be more physically active. She has no other medical conditions or disabilities that would limit her physical activity. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to optimize the health of children with congenital heart defects by promoting physical activity and healthy lifestyles.

A 42 year old woman with a history of invasive breast cancer comes to the clinic after noticing a lump in her right breast. She has undergone a mastectomy and chemotherapy in the past, but the cancer has spread to her lymph nodes and liver. She is HER2-negative and has been on endocrine therapy for the last 6 months. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets the following eligibility criteria for the POL6326 (Balixafortide) plus nab-paclitaxel or eribulin in patients with HER2-negative advanced breast cancer trial: she is female, over 18 years of age, has a confirmed diagnosis of invasive breast cancer, and has a locally advanced stage IIIB/C or metastatic stage IV disease. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy greater than 12 weeks. She has at least one measurable lesion per RECIST v.1.1 criteria and has been documented to be HER2-negative. She has had prior chemotherapy-based lines of treatment for advanced or metastatic disease, which have included an anthracycline and a taxane, and has been treated with at least one line of endocrine therapy. She has resolved all acute toxic effects of prior anti-cancer therapy to grade 1 as determined by the National Cancer Institute-Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE) v. 5.0 criteria. The patient is willing to provide a tumor biopsy and blood samples for exploratory studies as per study protocol. She is not under concurrent local radiotherapy for pain control or life-threatening situations, and does not have known active uncontrolled or symptomatic CNS metastases. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use highly effective contraceptive methods during the treatment period and for at least 90 days after the last dose of study treatment. She does not have any other concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical condition that would, in the Investigator's judgment, contraindicate patient participation in the clinical study.

Pt is a 24yo F with no significant past medical history, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the evaluation of a bedside mixing formulation of adjuvanted influenza vaccines. She has not received an influenza vaccine in the past year and reports no allergies to vaccine components, including egg/chicken products. She is in good health and has provided informed consent prior to enrollment. The patient does not have any serious medical conditions or reduced immune function, and has not recently used immunosuppressive therapy or received the influenza vaccine in the past year.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who has been using methamphetamine for the past 6 months. He reports using meth at least 4 times per month and engaging in unprotected sex with female partners during this time. He has not been in drug treatment in the past 30 days and is willing to be tested for HIV at baseline and follow-up. He is not currently mandated by the criminal justice system to receive treatment. He is able to provide a reliable address and phone number for contact and is not transient. He is not pregnant or attempting to become pregnant. He is not currently participating in another Project Safe study. He is not intoxicated or impaired mentally to the point that he cannot voluntarily consent to participate in the project and/or respond to the interview.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23.5 kg/m2. He has no history of diabetes or other medical conditions that could affect the study outcomes. The patient is willing and able to comply with the pre-visit instructions on diet and physical activity. He has no known allergies or intolerances to any of the ingredients in the study products. The patient understands the study procedures and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 60-year-old male patient is admitted to the critical care unit with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus. He was brought in with shortness of breath and was intubated due to respiratory distress. He has been on mechanical ventilation for the past 72 hours. His BMI is 29, and his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. His past medical history is significant for diabetic retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy. He has had no previous surgical procedures involving the upper or middle gastrointestinal tract. He is currently being fed through a nasogastric tube with a standard enteral tube feed formula. Blood sugars checked via basic metabolic panel and point-of-care glucose tests have been obtained at least every 6 hours. He has given informed consent to participate in the study.

This is a 22 year old healthy male who has been recently enlisted in the military. He has no known lower limb injuries or deformities and has not been prescribed any foot insoles by a physician or physiotherapist. He is physically active and engaged in regular exercise routines. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for the use of custom made foot insoles and standard shoes for the prevention of lower limb overuse injuries. He understands the study requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma. He has undergone complete front-line treatment, including induction chemotherapy, radioisotope (mIBG) treatment, appropriate local therapy, and myeloablative chemotherapy with autologous stem cell reinfusion. He has achieved a response status of stable disease or better (CR, VGPR, PR, SD). He has no requirements for palliative chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or surgery. He has not received any standard or experimental treatment for at least two weeks prior to starting the trial medication. He is HIV sero-negative and has no active or chronic-replicative hepatitis B infection. He has adequate functions of the heart, lung, bone marrow, liver, and kidney. He has no CNS disease or seizures within the past 6 weeks. His parents or guardian have provided written informed consent for his participation in the trial. The patient is willing to participate and is eligible for the trial.

This is a 55 year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes that has been managed with oral hypoglycemic agents for the past 2 years. Despite dietary modifications and medication adherence, his HbA1c levels remain elevated at 8.5%. The physician has recommended initiating insulin detemir therapy to better control his blood glucose levels. The patient has no known allergies and is willing to participate in this observational study to evaluate the safety of insulin detemir. He understands the study requirements and is compliant with regular follow-up visits.

A 9 year old girl with a diagnosis of right-sided hemiplegia due to unilateral cerebral palsy presents with difficulty performing daily activities such as buttoning clothes, holding utensils, and writing with her right hand. She has a Manual Ability Classification System (MACS) level II and Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level II, indicating moderate limitations in her manual and gross motor abilities. She has not had any hand orthopedic surgery or neuropharmacological interventions in the last 6 months. She is able to understand and respond to verbal instructions and has no allergies to materials used in upper limb orthosis. She has no other significant neurological conditions such as seizures or visual impairment. She is currently not receiving any treatments that would be incompatible with the study.

Pt is a 55yo M with a family history of colorectal cancer, presenting to his primary care physician for an annual check-up. He has no history of gastrointestinal symptoms, but his father was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 60. Upon discussing his family history with his physician, he learns that he is at increased risk for developing colorectal cancer and is offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial evaluating an interactive, web-based decision aid for colorectal cancer screening. Pt is fluent in written and spoken English and has not undergone any prior colorectal cancer screening. He has no major comorbidities that would preclude screening by any method. He is interested in learning more about the screening options available to him and making an informed decision with the help of the decision aid.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of gout for the past 5 years. He reports experiencing recurrent episodes of acute pain, swelling, and redness in his left big toe, ankle, and knee. He has a history of hyperuricemia, with a serum urate level of 8.5 mg/dL at the time of screening. He has been diagnosed with gout based on the American Rheumatism Association (ARA) Criteria for the Classification of Acute Arthritis of Primary Gout. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able and willing to comply with the visit/protocol schedules and provide informed consent. He is not currently taking any urate-lowering medication or other prohibited medication as outlined in the exclusion criteria. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and he has no history of renal, hepatic, or cardiac disease.

The patient is a 25 year-old female who has been diagnosed with gingivitis during a routine dental check-up. She has a history of good oral hygiene practices, including brushing twice a day and flossing regularly. She has not had any recent dental procedures or surgeries. She has a total of 28 teeth, with at least 5 teeth in each quadrant. She is not a smoker and does not wear any removable partial dentures. She is not currently pregnant and is not undergoing orthodontic treatment. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effects of using an intra-oral camera during supportive periodontal therapy.

This is a 22 year old female who was diagnosed with Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome (MRKH) at the age of 16 when she failed to start menstruating. She has no uterus and only a small portion of the upper vagina. She has normal external genitalia and normal breast development. She has a family history of MRKH, as her mother was also diagnosed with the same condition. The patient is interested in participating in this study, as she hopes it will lead to a better understanding of the genetic basis of MRKH and potentially lead to better treatments or prevention strategies for future generations. She is willing to provide a blood sample and uterine tissue, if it becomes available during clinical follow-up. Her parents and siblings are also willing to participate in the study as healthy relatives.

The patient is a 58 year-old male who was diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) six months ago. He has been receiving treatment with a hypomethylating agent (decitabine) but has not shown any significant improvement. He has had no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His ECOG performance status is 1. His most recent blood tests show total bilirubin and creatinine levels within normal limits, but his ALT (SGPT) level is slightly elevated (2.8 times the institutional upper limit of normal). He has no active infections and his cardiac function is stable. He understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to sign the informed consent form. He has no plans for pregnancy, and agrees to use a reliable method of contraception during the study.

A 35-year-old female of Asian ethnicity is seeking treatment for her moderate melasma. She is a non-smoker and has no underlying medical conditions. She works in an office and is not exposed to excessive sunlight. She has no history of skin cancer or other skin conditions. She has not used any topical steroids or hydroquinone for the past 3 months. She has not undergone any laser or dermabrasion to the face in the past 6 months. She does not have any blood clotting disorders or history of thromboembolic disease. She has not had any spontaneous abortions or kidney dysfunction. She is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is willing to take a pill twice a day for 4 months and undergo up to 5 monthly laser treatments to half her face. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the follow-up visits.

This is a 55 year old male who was recently diagnosed with Stage III follicular lymphoma. The patient has no history of chemotherapy other than local radiation therapy. The lymph node affected is greater than 2cm, and no evidence of primary or secondary CNS lymphoma has been found. The patient's ECOG score is 1 and the serum creatinine, bilirubin, and SGOT/SGPT levels are all within normal limits. The patient has no history of HIV or HBV infection and has tested negative for pregnancy (male gender). There is no evidence of any other unrelated neoplasm in the past 10 years. The patient is interested in participating in the study of the BiovaxId Tumor Derived Idiotype Vaccine, and is willing to provide tumor material by tissue biopsy for production of a patient-specific Ig idiotype vaccine conjugated to the immunogenic protein KLH. The patient is willing to undergo the PACE or CHOP-R chemotherapy and achieve a complete remission before receiving the vaccination. The patient understands that they will be randomized to either the active treatment arm or the control arm and will be followed for a minimum of 4 years post-randomization or until relapse.

Pt is a 16yo M high school football player who sustained a concussion during a game. He reported dizziness, headache, and nausea after the hit. He was removed from the game and evaluated by the athletic trainer. The concussion was suspected, and he was referred to the Concussion Clinic in the Sports Medicine Clinic at Children's of Alabama for further evaluation. Upon arrival, he provided informed consent/assent, completed a health and lifestyle questionnaire, and a 24-hour dietary recall. Standard of care measurements were taken, including height, weight, BMI, and resting blood pressure. He underwent the SCAT5 evaluation, which revealed cognitive impairment and balance issues. Research-specific evaluations were also conducted, including BIA for body composition and C3Logix evaluation for cognitive assessment. MRI scans were taken to evaluate the extent of the injury. The patient was randomized to receive either ketone supplementation or a placebo. He was provided with information regarding Return-to-Play progression and documents to track Return-to-Learn, supplement compliance, and GI distress. He will be followed throughout completion of the concussion protocol, up to one year. Follow-up visits will include standard of care measurements, SCAT5 evaluation, BIA, and C3Logix evaluation, as well as data collection sheets for Return-to-Learn Progression, supplement compliance, and GI distress. The primary objective is to determine whether ketone supplementation after a concussion will reduce long-term consequences and improve short-term functional status and outcomes in adolescents who have suffered a concussion.

A 50-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of dry, itchy eyes. She has been using artificial tears twice daily for the last 2 weeks, but her symptoms have not improved. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are controlled with medications. She has no history of ocular infection or surgery, and she is not a contact lens wearer. On examination, she has conjunctival and corneal staining in her left eye, and a TFBUT of 6 seconds in her right eye. She completed the OSDI questionnaire, and her score was 25. She has no other ocular or systemic illnesses that would exclude her from participating in the study. She is willing to commit to same brand of artificial tears throughout the study, and she is able to swallow large, soft gelcaps. She agrees to use a reliable method of contraception during the study, and she demonstrates a negative urine pregnancy test.

This is a 12-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. She has already undergone chemotherapy and her treating physician has recommended that she undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the next step in her treatment plan. The patient and her parents have opted to participate in a clinical trial that aims to identify which bone marrow transplant recipients are likely to progress to respiratory failure. They are willing to provide blood samples for the cytokine assay test that will be performed as part of the trial. The patient and her family hope that this study will provide valuable information and insights that can help improve the outcomes of HSCT for pediatric patients like her.

A 40-year-old female with a history of chronic knee pain due to osteoarthritis presents to the orthopedic clinic for a scheduled arthroscopic knee surgery. She has undergone previous surgeries including a meniscectomy and has been on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain management. She reports a Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS) score of 12 indicating moderate levels of catastrophizing thoughts about pain. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets all inclusion criteria for the study. She consents to participate in the clinical trial and is randomized to receive continuous nerve blocks delivered through a remote-controlled electronic pump. Post-operative pain is well-controlled with minimal opioid use and the patient is discharged from the hospital on the same day of surgery. She is able to complete self-reported questionnaires and activity tracking using a wearable device. At the 45-day follow-up visit, the patient reports improved quality of life and mobility compared to her previous surgeries. She is able to return to work without any issues and reports high satisfaction with the remote-controlled analgesia.

This is a 45 year-old female with no perception of light due to a congenital condition. She has a history of difficulty sleeping at night, including trouble initiating and maintaining sleep, and daytime sleepiness. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and restrictions, including committing to a fixed 9-hour sleep opportunity during the study. She has no current clinically significant cardiovascular, respiratory, neurologic, hepatic, hematopoietic, renal, gastrointestinal or metabolic dysfunction that is not currently controlled and stable. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, intolerance or hypersensitivity to melatonin or melatonin agonists, and does not smoke more than 10 cigarettes per day. She has not participated in a previous tasimelteon trial and is not currently using any central nervous system prescription or over-the-counter medication that affects the sleep-wake cycle, other than melatonin.

The patient is a 47-year-old male with a history of alcoholic pancreatitis who has been hospitalized multiple times in the past three years due to recurrent acute episodes. The patient reports drinking heavily on a regular basis despite experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting during and after drinking. The patient is motivated to reduce their alcohol consumption, but has struggled to make sustainable changes in the past. The patient is currently not hospitalized and has not experienced an acute episode of pancreatitis in the past four weeks. The patient has a mobile device with internet connection and is willing to wear the BACtrack Skyn sensor for two weeks to monitor their alcohol consumption. The patient does not have any medical or psychiatric conditions that would prevent them from participating in the study. The patient is not currently pregnant.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 3 years, with episodes lasting 30 minutes to 2 hours, and currently on antiarrhythmic drug therapy. He complains of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue during AF episodes. He has no other significant medical history except for mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of heart failure. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently retired but used to work as a construction manager. He has an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. His family history is negative for cardiac arrhythmias. His ECG shows AF with a heart rate of 120 bpm. He has no other significant findings on examination. His HAM-A score is 8.

A 62-year-old man is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent episodes of biliary colic caused by multiple gallstones. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with amlodipine 5mg/day. He denies any other significant medical history, allergies or medication use. The patient has been informed about the use of hemostatic agents/techniques during the surgery, and he has given his consent to participate in this observational study. The patient is willing to provide additional information about his surgery and recovery, including any adverse events related to the use of hemostatic agents/techniques.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with liver cirrhosis due to alcohol abuse. He has no previous history of decompensation of liver cirrhosis associated with portal hypertension. His recent videogastric examination showed small varices without red signs, and his ultrasound reports showed no ascites. His current medications include a daily multivitamin and a low-dose aspirin. His lab results show bilirubin levels of 2.5 mg/dl, platelet count of 40 x10E9/L, and quick test of 34%. He has no history of renal insufficiency or any comorbidities involving therapeutic limitations or life prognosis of less than 12 months. He has never received any treatment with nitrated or beta-blockers in the past two weeks and is not receiving anticoagulant treatment.

The patient is a 15-year-old male who has been experiencing moderate to severe acne vulgaris for the past year. He has tried over-the-counter treatments with little improvement. He has no known allergies and takes no medications regularly. His family history is negative for acne. He is willing to comply with study requirements and is able to attend all scheduled visits. The patient presents with moderate to severe acne vulgaris on his face with papules, pustules, and nodules. The inflammatory lesion count is 45 and the non-inflammatory lesion count is 80. He has fewer than two nodules present. The patient has no other dermatological conditions on his face that could interfere with clinical evaluations. He does not have a beard or mustache that could interfere with the study assessments.

65-year-old male, presented to the emergency department with chest pain, diaphoresis, and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, with a 30 pack-year history, and quit smoking 10 years ago. He has no known drug allergies. The patient's initial ECG showed ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads, and he was diagnosed with a first ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with successful revascularization of the right coronary artery. The patient's peak troponin level was 25 ng/mL, and his left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was measured at 40% by echocardiography. He is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel, as well as high-intensity statin therapy. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and he has agreed to participate and provide written informed consent.

50-year-old male with a history of elevated PSA levels with no prior biopsy, presents for participation in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of Diffusion Basis Spectrum Imaging (DBSI) in early detection of prostate cancer. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and meet the inclusion criteria for the "early detection cohort." The patient has no clinical contraindication to MRI and has not undergone prior prostate surgery. The patient is excited to participate in the trial and potentially contribute to improving the early detection of clinically significant prostate cancer.

A 25-year-old male diagnosed with Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 was enrolled in a previous clinical trial involving lumasiran. Following the completion of the study, the patient reports tolerating the study drug well and is willing to continue treatment. The patient is currently taking Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) and is willing to remain on a stable regimen for the study duration. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with study requirements. The patient has no clinically significant health concerns, except for PH1, and has no clinically significant cardiovascular abnormality. The patient's AST/ALT levels are within normal limits, and no other clinical safety laboratory result is considered clinically significant. The patient is not on chronic dialysis.

The patient is a 35-year-old Cambodian woman who speaks limited English. She presents to her primary care physician with complaints of feeling sad and hopeless for the past few weeks. She reports difficulty sleeping and a loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She denies any suicidal thoughts or plans. She has a family history of depression and anxiety. She is married with two young children and works as a cashier at a local grocery store. She reports feeling stressed about finances and the demands of her job and caring for her family. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She is alert and cooperative during the visit. She expresses difficulty in understanding and expressing herself in English and is interested in receiving help in her primary language. She is offered participation in a study that assesses the potential of Health Information Technology (HIT) to improve the screening and treatment of depression and post-traumatic stress among LEP Southeast Asians. She is informed that the study involves web-based training for her primary care provider, multimedia electronic screening for depression and PTSD, and clinical decision support. She is informed that her participation is voluntary and that she can withdraw at any time. She is also informed that her participation will not affect her medical care in any way.

32-year-old male patient, diagnosed with HIV-1 infection, living in a rural area of Vietnam, presents to a local health clinic for routine HIV care. The patient is ART naïve and has not received any prior treatment for HIV. The patient has given consent to participate in the MOVIDA project and is willing to provide blood samples for monitoring of viral load using the DBS system. The patient does not have any other significant medical history or co-morbidities. The patient is an injecting drug user (IDU) and is aware of the risks associated with HIV infection. The patient is committed to adhering to treatment and attending follow-up visits. The patient is fluent in Vietnamese and has a basic understanding of English.

A 65-year-old female retiree in good health with no significant medical history. She weighs 150 pounds, which is within +-25% of her normal weight (Broca-Index). She enjoys walking and light exercise, but does not engage in competitive sports. She is a non-smoker, does not drink more than 60 g of alcohol per day, and is not dependent on drugs. She has never participated in another study with an investigational drug within the last two months preceding this study. She has not donated blood within the last 4 weeks. She provides written informed consent prior to admission to the study.

A 45-year-old veteran who served in Afghanistan has been experiencing persistent nightmares, flashbacks, and emotional numbness since returning home. Despite receiving treatment from a psychiatrist, the symptoms have not improved significantly. He has tried two different types of treatment, but both have produced less than a 50% reduction in his symptoms. He has hypertension but is receiving stable treatment for it. He is fluent in English and has reliable internet access. He has never been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, acute psychosis, or opioid use disorder. He is not pregnant nor postpartum, and is not breastfeeding. Although he has had suicidal thoughts, he is currently not experiencing them. He is willing to participate in a new treatment approach that combines Ketamine infusions with online Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT). He is interested in being part of this clinical trial to explore new therapeutic options and gain new insights into the treatment of PTSD.

The patient is a 55 year old man who recently had a stroke. He is right-handed and the stroke affected his left side resulting in hemiparesis. He is currently living with his wife and has two adult children who live out of town. He used to work as a mechanic, but is now unable to work due to his condition. He has been undergoing standard rehabilitation therapy, but is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the robotic exoskeleton can help improve his walking abilities. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no other significant medical history and is able to communicate in English. He is motivated to participate in the study and has given informed consent. He is 5'9" and weighs 180 lbs, which makes him a suitable candidate to physically fit within the RE. He has no metal implants that are not MRI-compatible. His cognitive function is adequate to follow instructions and give feedback.

The patient is a 32-year-old non-smoking woman presenting with persistent asthma, which she has been experiencing for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing, especially at night or early in the morning. She is currently using an inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-agonist combination inhaler, but her symptoms are not well controlled. She reports a history of asthma exacerbations in the past year that required oral corticosteroids. She is willing to discontinue her current asthma medication for a washout period of time to participate in the study. Her pre-screening FEV1 is 80% of predicted normal value with a reversibility of 15% after salbutamol inhalation. She has no significant past medical history, and she is not taking any other medications. She is able to properly use a dry powder inhaler device and perform acceptable spirometry. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is able to take time off to participate in the study. Her family history is negative for asthma or any respiratory diseases. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He is undergoing chemotherapy treatment and has developed neutropenia with a leukocyte count of 800/mm3. He is experiencing shortness of breath with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths/minute and a saturation of 92% on room air. He has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease and is not on oxygen therapy. He has a body mass index of 25. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and comply with follow-up visits and testing schedule.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver. The patient is generally in good health, with no other significant medical conditions. There are at least two liver metastases, both of which are less than 3 cm in size and are eligible for both surgical resection and thermal ablation. The patient has not received any previous treatment for the liver metastases or the primary colorectal cancer. The patient is willing to undergo either surgical resection or thermal ablation for the target lesions. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including follow-up visits and imaging. The patient has no extrahepatic nodal or non-nodal metastases and has an ASA score of 1-3. The patient has not received any immunotherapy or chemotherapy within 6 weeks prior to the procedure. The patient will be assessed by an expert panel to determine eligibility for the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been suffering from mild to moderate atopic dermatitis for several years. His symptoms include dry, itchy skin, with redness and inflammation in the affected areas. He has been using 1% hydrocortisone ointment, a standard treatment, with some relief, but would like to try a natural alternative. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He lives with his parents and attends school regularly. His parents are willing to apply the ointment and participate in the study. Both the patient and his parents are able to communicate effectively and comply with study conditions. The patient has no known allergies to oregano.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 4 years ago. She has been taking efavirenz-based antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years. During her last check-up, her viral load was found to be between 5,000-60,000 copies/mL, and she was experiencing virological failure. Her genotype resistance test showed that she had developed resistance to first-generation non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as K103N and Y181C. Her CD4 count was above 200 cells/uL, and her creatinine clearance was above 50 mL/min. She weighs more than 35 kg. She is not pregnant, and she is not currently taking any prohibited concomitant medications listed in the protocol. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating in the trial to explore the efficacy of Doravirine in combination with Lamivudine and Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate in managing her HIV-1 infection.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He has been taking metformin and sitagliptin for the past 3 years to manage his blood sugar levels. The patient has a BMI of 30 and an HbA1c of 8.5%. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril to manage his blood pressure. The patient has no history of kidney disease, liver disease, or cardiovascular disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve his management of type 2 diabetes.

A 35-year-old immigrant woman, originally from Mexico, is a smoker who smokes around 10 cigarettes per day. She currently lives in New York City with her husband and two children, and her household income is below 200% of the current federal poverty level. She is interested in receiving smoking cessation counseling and financial management counseling to improve her family's financial situation. She speaks Spanish and English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have a representative who manages her funds, and she is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is open to participating in a 9-week intervention program and is willing to attend follow-up appointments to assess her progress and satisfaction with the treatment.

Patient is a 68-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the factors that contribute to cognitive decline in older individuals. Her medical history includes hypertension, well-controlled with medication, and occasional migraines. She is fluent in English and has good visual and auditory acuity. Her cognition is intact, with a Clinical Dementia Rating of 0 and a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 30. She has no significant co-morbid neurologic or psychiatric disease and has not been diagnosed with dementia or mild cognitive impairment. She has no contraindications for MRI or PET scans. She is willing and able to participate in all study procedures, including MRI and PET scans, and is committed to participating in the study for its duration. She is interested in contributing to the research efforts to better understand the factors that contribute to cognitive decline in older individuals and potentially inform future interventions for Alzheimer's disease.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with hypertension that is not responding to standard treatment. He has been diagnosed with primary aldosteronism and is currently being treated with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. He has no history of adrenal surgery or other adrenal conditions. He has a BMI of 30 and is in good general health. The patient is willing to consider adrenal surgery if necessary for the study. He has no contraindications for AVS, MTO-PET, or CT. The patient is not pregnant and has no family history of primary aldosteronism. The adrenal CT scan did not reveal any other tumors than adenoma or hyperplasia.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent asthma symptoms for the past year, despite medication and lifestyle changes. She has also been diagnosed with chronic nasal disease featuring nasal polyps and has experienced sensitivity to aspirin in the past. She is a non-smoker and has no significant comorbid conditions that could interfere with study results. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) and potentially improve the understanding and treatment of her condition.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV infection 2 years ago. He has been asymptomatic so far, and his CD4+ T lymphocyte count is currently between 350 and 550 cells/ul. He has not received any antiretroviral therapy or immunomodulatory treatment in the past month. He does not have any liver or kidney dysfunction, autoimmune diseases, or active diseases in respiratory, digestive, circulatory, blood, neuroendocrine or genitourinary systems. He is not suffering from cancer or any other chronic illness. He is sexually active and takes necessary precautions to prevent transmission of the disease. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 67 year-old male who suffered his first stroke 3 months ago. He has been retaining a nasal tube for feeding due to difficulty with swallowing, which has affected his quality of life. He has been receiving swallowing treatment from a language therapist and his caregiver has been providing oral care to him. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. He has no history of oral cancer or head and neck cancer. He is able to communicate his needs and has no cognitive impairment. He is eager to improve his swallowing function and oral health.

A 35-year-old woman has been struggling with obesity for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has not been able to lose a significant amount of weight. Her body mass index (BMI) is 40, and she suffers from sleep apnea and high blood pressure. She has been referred to the Baylor Weight Loss Surgery Center for primary bariatric surgery. She meets all the requirements for surgery and is interested in participating in the study. Her past medical history includes depression, which is currently managed with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. She works as a teacher and is physically active but has difficulty maintaining a healthy weight. She is excited about the possibility of losing weight with surgery and hopes that participating in this study will help predict the success of her weight loss journey.

The patient is a 35 year old male who was diagnosed with a prolactinoma and has been taking a dopamine agonist for the past 6 months. Despite treatment, the patient still experiences symptoms of hypogonadism, including low energy, decreased libido, and difficulty achieving and maintaining an erection. The patient has discontinued testosterone replacement therapy for at least 2 months and has a serum total testosterone level less than 300ng/dL with normal or low levels of LH and FSH. The patient is willing and able to attend scheduled visits and comply with dopamine agonist treatment. The patient will be considered for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of clomiphene citrate in treating persistent hypogonadism in male patients with prolactinomas under dopamine agonist treatment.

55 year old female with a diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis confirmed by a physician. She reports experiencing pain, aching or discomfort in or around the knee for the last year. She has not been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, polymyalgia rheumatica, connective tissue diseases, fibromyalgia or gout. She has not undergone knee replacement surgery nor is she on the waiting list for it. She has not had any acute injury to the knee in the last 6 months nor surgery in the back, hip, knee, foot or ankle joints in the last 12 months. She has an email address and daily access to a computer with internet connection. She can attend a 1.5-hour education session at the Mary Pack Arthritis Centre and a 1-hour assessment session at Vancouver General Hospital prior to beginning the study, and again 2 and 4 months later. She does not have a body mass index of equal to or greater than 40, has not received a steroid injection or hyaluronate injection in a knee in the last 6 months, and does not take medication that may impair activity tolerance. She is interested in improving her physical activity and reducing sedentary time, and is willing to participate in a research study that involves the use of a physical activity tracking tool, group education session, and remote coaching by a physiotherapist.

Melissa is a 26-year-old woman who is planning to travel to Mexico for a week-long vacation with her friends. She has no history of chronic illnesses and is in good health. She has not experienced any acute diarrhea in the past 7 days and has not taken any antibiotics or antidiarrheal medication within the last 24 hours. Melissa is fluent in English and has no difficulty understanding the language. She is excited about her upcoming trip but is concerned about the risk of developing travellers' diarrhea, which she has heard can be a common problem for travellers to Mexico. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if taking rifaximin can prevent the onset of this condition.

A 42-year-old woman has been diagnosed with stage IV melanoma that has spread to her liver and lungs. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, including pembrolizumab, but her cancer has continued to progress. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not on any medications. She is willing to undergo fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) and is able to comprehend and execute informed consent. She understands the risks associated with FMT administration, including the transmission of infectious organisms and the theoretical risk of developing diseases related to donor gut microbiota. She has measurable disease as per RECIST version 1.1 and is willing to participate in the correlative studies and provide tumor tissue for tumor biopsies. She has a performance status of 0 on the ECOG Performance Scale and demonstrates adequate organ function. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an adequate method of contraception during the course of the study through 120 days after the last dose of study medication.

45 yo F whose husband sustained a TBI in a motor vehicle accident resulting in severe cognitive and physical impairments. The patient is the primary caregiver and has had to quit her job to provide full-time care. She has reported feeling overwhelmed and isolated since her husband's injury. The patient's husband was recently admitted to the Shepherd Center ABI inpatient rehabilitation unit and the patient has expressed interest in participating in a peer mentor program to receive emotional support and guidance from someone who has gone through a similar experience. She speaks English fluently and plans to have her husband discharged to their home upon completion of his rehabilitation. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands that she may be randomly selected to receive one-to-one mentorship or general peer support under usual care.

The patient is a 45-year-old man living in the United States who has tested positive for COVID-19. He has been experiencing symptoms such as cough, fever, and shortness of breath for the past week and is interested in participating in the "Behavior, Environment And Treatments for COVID-19" clinical trial. He is willing to provide informed consent and understands that participation is voluntary. The patient has access to a computer or smartphone with internet capabilities and is comfortable using technology to enter and submit data. He is interested in contributing to the study to help better understand the natural history of COVID-19 and identify potential interventions to improve outcomes.

35 y/o mother of a 6-year-old boy with sensory processing issues (SPIs) who has been on the waitlist for a neurodevelopmental diagnostic assessment at the "Communication, Learning, and Behaviour" clinic at Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital for 3 months. The child has been experiencing difficulties in daily activities such as feeding, sleeping, and dressing. The mother reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the challenging behaviours related to her child's SPIs, which have impacted her confidence in managing her child's behaviour. She has not attended any parent education workshops or interventions targeting SPIs in the past. She has basic English comprehension reading and writing skills and access to the internet. She is interested in participating in the study to learn strategies to improve her parenting skills and increase her sense of competence in managing her child's SPI-related behaviours.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He has been experiencing symptoms of COVID-19, including cough, fever, and shortness of breath for the past week. He was admitted to the hospital and was diagnosed with COVID-19 through a positive test result. He requires oxygen supplementation via nasal catheter at a rate of 2 liters per minute. He is currently taking metformin and lisinopril for his diabetes and hypertension, respectively. He has no known allergies to medications. He is married with three children and works as a construction worker. He has never smoked or used illicit drugs and drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help find a treatment for COVID-19.

A 35 year old Japanese male with a diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension comes to the clinic seeking treatment options.
