He reports experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and dizziness with minimal physical activity. He has no significant past medical history but reports a family history of hypertension. On examination, the patient appears pale and fatigued. His vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 24 bpm, and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air. Lung examination reveals decreased breath sounds and crackles in both lung fields. Echocardiography shows an enlarged right ventricle and elevated pulmonary artery pressure. Right heart catheterization confirms the diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension with a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 34 mmHg and a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 12 mmHg. The patient's 6-minute walk test distance is 250 meters. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is interested in participating to assess the safety and efficacy of sildenafil in treating his condition.

28-year-old Caucasian female with a history of neurogenic bladder instability presenting with symptoms of urinary frequency and urgency. She has tried various medications in the past, including oxybutynin and tolterodine, with limited success. She does not have any known allergies to medications or their adjuvants. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements that could potentially interfere with the absorption or metabolism of the investigational product. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 40g of alcohol per day. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has provided written informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating and has had a negative pregnancy test.

The patient is a 36-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) for the past 5 years. She has been treated with immunomodulatory therapy for the past 3 years but currently experiences a moderate to severe intensity relapse characterized by an increase in pyramidal system function with a score of 2.5 on the EDSS scale. The patient has experienced no fever and has had one month of clinical stability prior to the relapse onset, which occurred less than 15 days ago. The patient has no known allergies to medications related to the study medication, and her renal function is normal. She has no history of serious adverse reactions to medications and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study, including regular MRI scans.

A 56-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted to the hospital with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She had a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and was taking Lisinopril and Atorvastatin. Her vital signs showed a temperature of 38.5°C, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, heart rate of 98 beats per minute, and blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. Physical examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right lower lobe of the lung. Laboratory tests showed an elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein level. Chest X-ray revealed infiltrates in the right lower lung field. She was diagnosed with pneumonia and started on teicoplanin therapy. The patient provided written informed consent to participate in a retrospective study evaluating the efficacy and safety of teicoplanin in Gram-positive infections. She met the inclusion criteria of age ≥18 years and duration of teicoplanin therapy ≥5 days. She did not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including allergy to teicoplanin, pregnancy, hematopoietic function disorder, or inability to evaluate efficacy and safety. Her creatinine clearance rate was calculated to be 80 mL/min, and she was assigned to Group A for teicoplanin dosing. The target Cmin was set to 15-30 mg/L, and her maintenance dosing was adjusted accordingly based on her serum trough concentrations and CLcr values.

The patient is a 9-year-old female who presents to the pediatric emergency department with severe pain due to a fractured arm sustained during a fall from her bicycle. The patient rates her pain as an 8 on a scale of 1-10. The patient is accompanied by her mother, who is fluent in English and able to help the patient complete self-report measures of pain. The patient has no known allergies or contraindications to opioids. The patient has not received any opioid or benzodiazepine medication within the preceding 6 hours. The patient has no history of liver or kidney problems and is not currently critically ill. The patient does not have a chronic pain condition. The treating physician has determined that the patient requires parenteral opioid analgesic to treat her pain, and the patient and her mother have consented to participate in the study.

72-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease who regularly attends the Parkinson Association of Granada for management of his symptoms. He reports limitations in his daily activities due to motor symptoms affecting his upper extremities. The patient has no history of auditive or visual disturbances, cognitive problems, psychiatric pathology, or traumatic pathology of the hand. He is willing to complete the battery of tests required for the study and is able to attend the intervention sessions. The patient is not currently experiencing any acute exacerbation of his symptoms.

A 62-year-old man has been diagnosed with colon cancer and is scheduled for elective bowel surgery. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies and has never had any major surgeries before. He does not smoke, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He is able to give informed consent for the clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male with a 20-year history of smoking presented to the clinic with a 3-month history of progressive hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, and a lump in the neck. A biopsy revealed squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx with involvement of the adjacent lymph nodes. Imaging studies confirmed the diagnosis of stage IV, unresectable head and neck cancer. He has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He has a good performance status and is able to carry out daily activities without assistance. His laboratory results showed normal liver function, hemoglobin level of 12 g/dl, platelet count of 150,000/mm³, and neutrophil count of 3.5/mm³. He has no known allergies to any medication. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

56-year-old male with a history of elevated PSA levels and abnormal digital rectal exams, and a family history of prostate cancer. Patient has never undergone a prostate biopsy before. Currently has no urinary symptoms, but is concerned about the possibility of prostate cancer. Patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo a pelvic MRI prior to the standard biopsy of the prostate. No history of ferromagnetic or other non-MRI compatible implants, no implanted pacemaker or defibrillator, and no history of allergic reaction to MR contrast material or abnormal kidney function.

56 year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, previous myocardial infarction, and angioplasty 2 years ago. He has been experiencing stable angina and has non-calcified plaque on prior CT. He has an abnormal exercise tolerance test. He is currently on a stable dose of statin for the past 6 months. His renal function is normal with an estimated creatinine clearance calculated using Cockcroft-Gault equation of 70 ml/min. His ALT and AST are within normal range. He has normal thyroid function and has had an exercise tolerance test performed within the past 6 months. His BMI is 28. He is not currently on any medication for weight loss and has not had any surgery within the past 30 days. He does not have any history of acquired immune deficiency syndrome or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He is mentally capable and has no history of dementia or Alzheimer's Disease. He is not currently receiving any chemotherapy or radiation for malignancy. He has not consumed more than 21 units of alcohol per week.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). He has a history of ulcerative colitis and has been undergoing annual surveillance colonoscopy with routine biopsy regime. He has agreed to participate in a clinical study evaluating the efficacy of laser-based endomicroscopy as a complement to white-light colonoscopy and chromoendoscopy for early detection of colon dysplasia. The patient does not have a history of allergy to fluorescein and is not currently taking B-blockers. He will undergo laser-based endomicroscopy during his next surveillance colonoscopy.

This study does not involve patients, but rather community-based organizations and their staff who work in the HIV/AIDS sector. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who noticed a new mole on her left calf about 3 months ago. The mole is about 6 mm in diameter, has irregular borders, and is dark in color. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She works as a teacher and enjoys outdoor activities, including hiking and gardening. She has fair skin and burns easily in the sun but does not use sunblock regularly. Her physical exam is significant for the suspicious mole on her left calf, with no other abnormal skin findings. She has no lymphadenopathy or other concerning exam findings. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the use of ultrasound as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for skin lesions.

The patient is a 35 year old healthy individual who has not received the influenza vaccine this season. They have no history of chronic medical conditions and are not on any medications. They have not experienced any significant adverse reactions to previous vaccinations. They are mentally competent and willing to give informed consent prior to study entry. They are available for all visits scheduled in the study and able to comply with all study requirements. The patient is interested in contributing to medical research and helping to improve the safety and effectiveness of the influenza vaccine.

The patient is a 35-year-old Punjabi immigrant residing in Montreal, Canada. He is generally healthy with no known medical conditions or allergies. He has been living in Montreal for the past 5 years and has been struggling with maintaining good oral hygiene. He brushes his teeth twice a day but often forgets to floss or rinse his mouth after eating. He occasionally experiences bleeding gums while brushing his teeth. He is interested in learning more about oral hygiene and self-care practices to improve his oral health. He has no history of orthodontic appliances or systemic diseases such as diabetes. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl who has undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) for leukemia. She has been experiencing cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue for the past two weeks. She has been prescribed antibiotics but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has no other medical conditions and is not on any immunosuppressive therapy. She is currently in stable condition and is able to perform routine activities with some difficulty due to her respiratory symptoms. Physical examination reveals some wheezing and decreased breath sounds in the lower right lung field. She is able to speak in full sentences without difficulty. The respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. She is willing to participate in the study and provide leftover respiratory tract secretions, paired blood and NP swabs, and clinical circumstances for the purpose of identifying pathogens and markers of host response to infection. She understands that this study may potentially improve the diagnosis of lower respiratory tract infections in pediatric HCT patients.

63-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the pancreas after presenting with abdominal pain and weight loss. CT imaging confirmed locally advanced disease with evidence of tumor infiltration into the surrounding vasculature. He underwent a Whipple procedure followed by adjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Two months later, imaging revealed disease recurrence with metastatic involvement of the liver. The patient was referred for consideration of clinical trial enrollment and was found to meet eligibility criteria for the study investigating the efficacy of CCI-779 in locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal laboratory values with the exception of mildly elevated bilirubin levels (1.3 times ULN). The patient is willing to undergo weekly IV infusions of CCI-779 and agrees to regular follow-up appointments to monitor disease progression and treatment response.

Hina is a 24 year old woman who gave birth to a healthy baby girl weighing 3.2 kg. She lives in a peri-urban area of Karachi, Pakistan with her husband and their extended family. She has a mid-upper-arm-circumference of 22.8 cm. She intends to exclusively breastfeed her baby for at least six months. She has no known allergies to peanuts, lentils, chickpeas, or dairy products. She had a normal delivery and has no known medical conditions that would prevent her from breastfeeding. She is willing to stay in the catchment area for the entire duration of the trial after enrollment. She understands the study requirements and has voluntarily given written consent to participate in the trial.

25-year-old female with a history of primary amenorrhea and diagnosed with idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (IHH) is being recruited for a clinical trial. She has never had a menstrual cycle and has been evaluated by a physician for her infertility. The patient has no other known medical conditions and has not been on any gonadal steroid preparations for at least one month. Her complete blood count (CBC) and thyroid function tests are normal, and she has a negative pregnancy test. The study will involve the administration of synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) to stimulate the pituitary gland and ovaries to induce ovulation and menstruation. The patient will receive pulsatile GnRH, which has been approved by the FDA for use in women with primary amenorrhea due to complete GnRH deficiency. The overall goals of this protocol are to continue to use pulsatile GnRH in GnRH-deficient and other anovulatory women for ovulation induction and to examine specific physiologic hypotheses, which can only be addressed in this patient population. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the study for any adverse effects, and her response to the treatment will be evaluated through regular follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 62-year-old retired teacher who was recently diagnosed with Chronic Lymphoid Leukaemia (CLL). She lives in the Finistere area of France with her husband and has two adult children who live away from home. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She noticed swelling in her neck and fatigue for a few months before visiting her primary care physician who referred her to an oncologist. The oncologist diagnosed her with CLL and suggested she participate in the OFICE registry. She is willing to provide informed consent and a blood sample at the time of enrollment to help guide future clinical studies for CLL treatment.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia presents for evaluation of his cholesterol medication. He has been taking atorvastatin for the past year and is interested in participating in a study to assess how atorvastatin is absorbed when given with LY2189265. He has a BMI in the normal range and has no known allergies to atorvastatin or GLP-1-related compounds. He has no history of pancreatitis or gastrointestinal disorders that could impact drug absorption. He reports occasional alcohol use but agrees to limit his intake during the study. He is willing to use two reliable methods of contraception with his female partner during the study. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to follow all study restrictions.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing oral discomfort and burning sensation for the past 3 months. She has noticed white, lacy patches on the inside of her cheeks and gums. Her primary care physician referred her to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with oral lichen planus after a biopsy. She has not received any treatment for the condition yet. She is otherwise healthy with no history of any significant medical conditions. She is not taking any medication on a regular basis. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is interested in alternative medicine and practices yoga regularly. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She does not have any history of substance abuse or allergies to medications.

35 F with a history of depression and dysthymia who has been experiencing moderate depressive symptoms for the past 6 months. She has tried various medications and psychotherapy in the past, but has not found significant improvement. She has a Goldberg Depression Test Score of 30. She is employed full-time and has been struggling with maintaining productivity at work due to her symptoms. She has heard about the potential benefits of music therapy for depression and is interested in participating in the study. She does not abuse alcohol or have any diseases as a consequence of alcohol abuse. She is not currently under psychiatric treatment for psychoses and her Goldberg Depression Test Score falls within the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a healthy individual between the ages of 18 and 50 who is scheduled for an elective surgery under general anesthesia. They have an ASA class I or II status and do not have a history of acid reflux. They have a BMI of less than 40kg.m-2 and do not require endotracheal intubation. They do not have predictors of difficult intubation and have a mouth opening of at least 2.5 cm. They are able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old adolescent girl who has started experiencing mood swings and emotional outbursts. She has a family history of depression, anxiety, and bipolar disorder. She has no history of any significant medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is currently in 8th grade and is doing well in school. She has no history of drug abuse or alcohol consumption. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about emotional regulation and how her brain processes emotions. She has no known endocrine disorders and meets all the inclusion criteria for healthy subjects. She is willing to undergo an fMRI scan and give her consent/assent to participate in the study.

45 y/o Chinese male diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) 5 years ago. He is currently taking metformin and a sulphonylurea (SU) but has been experiencing inadequate glycemic control with HbA1c levels between 7.5% and 8.5%. He reports adhering to his medication regimen and following a diabetic diet, but has not been able to achieve satisfactory blood sugar control. The patient has no history of diabetic ketoacidosis or type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). He has never experienced a severe hypoglycemic episode and has not been hospitalized for diabetes-related complications. The patient does not have any other significant medical history and is not currently experiencing any other illnesses.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with inflammation/infection during her pregnancy. She is currently at 36 weeks of gestation and scheduled for a C-section delivery. The obstetrician has informed the patient that 1 milliliter of amniotic fluid will be aspirated during the C-section before incision of membranes. The patient has consented to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the possible effect of amniotic fluid pH on neonatal respiratory morbidities in inflammation/infection-associated pregnancies. The patient has a normal healthy pregnancy, and there are no known congenital or chromosomal abnormalities. The patient understands that her amniotic fluid will be analyzed for pH levels, and her demographic features and clinical outcomes, as well as the incidences of neonatal respiratory morbidities such as respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and transient tachypnea of the newborn (TTN), will be recorded. The patient is committed to participating in the clinical trial to help improve the understanding of the effect of amniotic fluid pH on neonatal morbidities.

A 23-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 who does not smoke or use any tobacco or nicotine products and has not used these products for the past 2 months. She is able to read, write, and comprehend English at a sufficient level to understand study-related materials, has provided written informed consent before any study-related procedure was performed, and is willing and able to comply with all testing and study requirements. She has not used any medication (prescription or non-prescription) or herbal supplement, other than prescription hormone replacement therapy or contraception methods, within 21 days before Day -1. She has a negative serum pregnancy test at Screening and on Day -1 (CRU admission). She usually has at least 1 bowel movement a day based on self-reporting. She is willing to minimize the risk of inducing pregnancy from the time of signing the informed consent form to at least either 90 days (males) or 30 days (females) after the study drug dose. She does not have a history or presence of clinically significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, oncologic, vascular, metabolic, collagen, or psychiatric disease or any other condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would jeopardize the safety of the subject or the validity of the study results. She has not donated more than 500 mL blood during the 3-month period before Day -1, and does not have known intolerance of study drug/ingredients. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or not using a medically accepted method of contraception. She is able to abstain from artificial sweeteners from CRU admission to the end of study participation. She is not currently enrolled in another clinical study or has received an investigational drug or device within 30 days or within a time period consistent with a washout period of 5 half-lives before signing the ICF, whichever is longer. She has not already participated in this study.

The patient is an 80-year-old woman who has been living in a nursing home for the past year due to physical disabilities. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She has all her natural teeth and has complained of difficulty brushing and flossing due to arthritis in her hands. She has been receiving assistance from nursing staff for her daily oral care routine. She has a good appetite and eats a balanced diet. She enjoys socializing with other residents and participating in group activities. She has a positive attitude towards healthcare and has expressed interest in learning more about oral health. She is able to communicate effectively with staff and has no cognitive impairments. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs.

A 45-year-old man recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus was prescribed oral hypoglycemic agents, but his blood glucose remained uncontrolled. The patient's past medical history includes hypertension and dyslipidemia. He is married with two children and works as an office clerk. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28 kg/m², and his blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg. His fasting plasma glucose (FPG) is 180 mg/dL, and his HbA1c is 9.2%. The patient's treating physician has recommended starting him on Ryzodeg™ therapy to better control his blood glucose levels. The patient has been informed of the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PNET) that cannot be removed by surgery. She has had one prior therapy and completed chemoembolization six weeks ago. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, meaning she is fully ambulatory and able to perform light work, such as office work or light housework. Her life expectancy is estimated to be greater than three months. The patient has radiographically measurable disease, which is confirmed by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1 criteria. She has adequately controlled blood pressure, with systolic and diastolic readings below 140 and 90 mmHg, respectively, and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 60%. Her blood counts are within normal limits, with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2000/µL, platelets of 130,000/µL, and hemoglobin of 10.0 g/dL. Her liver function tests are slightly elevated, with total bilirubin and AST/ALT levels at 2.2 mg/dL and 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), respectively. She has an INR of

45 year old male with a history of deep vein thrombosis in the right leg and a pulmonary embolism in the past year. Despite 3 months of anticoagulation therapy, he still experiences shortness of breath and fatigue. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently on any medication. He has a BMI of 27 and is a non-smoker.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary CNS lymphoma (PCNSL) confirmed through biopsy. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for this. She has been experiencing headaches, confusion, and difficulty with balance and coordination. Her renal function has been compromised, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 60 mL/min. She has received previous high dose-MTX treatment and experienced renal failure, defined as doubling of the serum creatinine compared to the baseline value. Her blood tests show normal liver function and normal levels of bilirubin, ALT, and AST. She is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or intolerances to MTX or LV. She has no history of diabetes, hepatitis, or HIV infection. She is willing to use a reliable form of contraception during the study. She has not participated in any other clinical trial in the last month or during this study. She is able to provide informed consent or has a legal representative who can provide consent on her behalf.

A 22-year old college student with no known ocular health problems is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a safety study of bepotastine besilate ophthalmic solution. She wears glasses for nearsightedness, but it doesn't affect her daily activities. She has no history of eye surgeries or serious eye injuries. The patient is generally healthy, exercises regularly, and maintains a balanced diet. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is currently taking a multivitamin and an oral contraceptive. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

A 23-year-old female patient was referred to the oral and maxillofacial surgery clinic with complaints of pain and swelling in the lower left jaw region for the past 3 weeks. The pain is dull and intermittent, radiating to the ear and neck. The patient also reports difficulty opening her mouth and chewing on the left side. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon examination, there is tenderness and swelling in the lower left jaw region, and the patient has limited mouth opening. A panoramic radiograph reveals an impacted mandibular third molar with a mesioangular impaction. The patient is scheduled for surgical removal of the impacted third molar. The surgeon discusses the possible postoperative complications with the patient, including pain, edema, and swelling, and the need for postoperative mouthwash use. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of different boric acid concentrations in mouthwash for postoperative care after impacted wisdom tooth removal.

A 28 year old woman comes to the clinic complaining of recurrent intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviors that have interfered with her daily life. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for several years now and they have recently worsened. She feels compelled to wash her hands multiple times a day and if she doesn't, she experiences intense anxiety and fear of contamination. She also has intrusive thoughts about harming herself or others, which cause her significant distress. She has been avoiding social situations and feels that her relationships are suffering because of her symptoms. She has a score of 22 on the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS) and meets the diagnostic criteria for OCD according to the DSM-5. She is fluent in Dutch and has a live-in partner who is also fluent in Dutch and willing to attend all treatment sessions with her. She does not have any current severe suicidality, substance abuse, psychotic symptoms or OCD treated with deep brain stimulation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of the involvement of family in cognitive-behavioral group therapy for OCD.

A 23-year-old female with a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa who has been receiving outpatient treatment for the past 6 months. She has a BMI of 16.5 and has been struggling with disordered eating patterns for several years. She reports experiencing significant psychosocial impairment as a result of her eating disorder, including difficulty socializing and maintaining relationships, poor academic performance, and decreased work productivity. She has been referred to participate in the study by her treating psychiatrist and has provided written informed consent to participate. The patient is fluent in Spanish and is able to complete the questionnaires without any language barriers.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He has been experiencing severe pain in the upper abdomen that radiates to his back for several weeks despite taking high doses of opioids. The pain has been affecting his daily activities and his quality of life. The patient has had recent abdominal imaging (CT scan) within the past 2 months. He has undergone chemotherapy and biological treatment in the past, which are stopped 1 week prior to the radiation therapy. He is willing to participate in the study and has no psychological, familial, sociological or geographical conditions that could hamper compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2. The patient is not pregnant, a prisoner, or has any major psychiatric illnesses. The patient has not received any previous radiation therapy to the upper abdomen and does not have any conditions associated with increased side effects to radiotherapy (such as inflammatory bowel disease).

Patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain for over 3 months. He was diagnosed with chronic stable angina and has a history of myocardial infarction that occurred 5 months ago. The patient has undergone coronary angiography and it was found that he has stenosis of more than 50% in one of the major epicardial coronary arteries. The patient underwent an exercise tolerance test and manifested positive results (ST-segment depression ≥ 1 mm compared with at rest, with or without limiting angina). The patient is in good general health, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of ≥50%. The patient has no history of valvular disease, congenital heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, cerebral apoplexy, dissecting aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, acute myocarditis/cp. The patient's rest heart rate is within normal limits. The patient has not been diagnosed with nonrespiratory sinus arrhythmia or arrhythmia(e.g.,AVB(auriculo-ventricular block)ⅡⅢ,atrial fibrillation,atrial flutter,SSS(sick sinus syndrome)) or implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD). The patient has no history of uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled blood glucose, anemia, or severe concurrent pathology. The patient is not suspected of being addicted to alcohol or drug abuse or having severe complications that could make the condition more complicated. The patient's liver and renal function are within normal limits. The patient has not been taking any unapproved drugs during the study. The patient has not been taking amiodarone(in recent 3 months)and/or benzetimide, βblockers(in recent 7 days). The patient has no history of allergy or suspected allergic to the drug(e.g.，Hydrochloric ivabradine,atenolol, βblockers)or lactose. The patient is willing to use contraception during the treatment period and is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has not been diagnosed with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) requiring bronchodilators. The patient has not participated in any other trials in recent 3 months and is able to participate in the study as judged by the investigator.

A 62 year old man presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and lower back pain that started after having a cardiac catheterization procedure 2 days ago. He reports feeling weak and dizzy and has noticed dark, tarry stools. On physical examination, he is found to be hypotensive with a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg and tachycardic with a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. There is tenderness to palpation in the lower abdomen and lower back. CT scan reveals a large retroperitoneal hematoma. The patient is diagnosed with retroperitoneal hemorrhage due to cardiac catheterization and is admitted to the hospital for further treatment. He meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is enrolled in the study.

A 25 year old woman has been struggling with assertiveness. She finds it hard to express herself and often feels like she is being taken advantage of. This has led to low self-esteem and difficulty in personal and professional relationships. She has never sought therapy for this issue before and is not currently on any medication. She speaks and reads Swedish fluently and is interested in participating in an online intervention program to improve her self-assertiveness. She does not have severe depression and is not currently undergoing psychotherapy.

A 50-year-old female with a history of malignant salivary gland tumor presents with a T3 stage tumor with microscopically positive surgical margins. The patient underwent surgical resection with curative intent 6 weeks ago but has no evidence of gross tumor residual. The patient has no evidence of distant metastases and no synchronous or concurrent head and neck primary tumors. The Karnofsky score is 80, and the patient has adequate organ function. The patient has not received prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy to the head and neck region. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed written informed consent.

60-year-old Caucasian male, retired, with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is referred for a screening colonoscopy at a local hospital. However, he cancels the appointment due to anxiety and discomfort about the procedure. He has no prior history of gastrointestinal symptoms, and no personal or family history of colorectal cancer or polyps. He has never undergone any CRC screening tests before. He has a good understanding of the English language, and can read and write. He is not diagnosed with any cognitive, hearing, speech or vision impairments, and has no contraindications for colonoscopy. He lives with his wife, who is supportive of him undergoing screening. He is interested in learning more about the different screening test options available and reducing the barriers to colorectal cancer screening to make an informed decision about screening.

A 60-year-old retired teacher whose family has no history of dementia or cognitive decline. The patient is in good health with no significant medical history. She has completed 16 years of education and has a MMSE score of 28. The patient's spouse will participate in the study and will confirm the patient's reliability during the interview. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, psychiatric illness or insulin-dependent diabetes. She is not taking any medications that affect cognition. The patient is experiencing some difficulty sleeping at night, but she does not feel excessively sleepy during the day. The patient has never been diagnosed with OSA or any other sleep disorder. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A married couple is expecting their first child, due in two months. The mother is 28 years old and has had a healthy pregnancy thus far. She has no history of medical or genetic conditions and her family has no history of allergic disease. She plans to have a natural childbirth and will exclusively formula feed her baby. The baby is expected to be full-term and of average weight for gestational age according to the World Health Organization growth charts. The couple is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerance of a low-protein formula for their baby's first four months of life.

This is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medications to control her blood pressure. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is 55 mL/min, which places her in the moderate renal impairment group. She has not had any recent history of bleeding disorders or thromboembolic events, and has not taken any thrombolytics or anticoagulants in the past 30 days. She does not have any history of malignant disease or wound healing problems. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m². She is interested in participating in this trial to help advance research on cilengitide and its effects on patients with renal impairment.

A 60-year-old male patient was brought to the emergency department with difficulty in breathing for the last 2 days. The patient has a history of hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the last 5 years. He is a smoker and has a 20 pack-year smoking history. Oxygen saturation was 85% on room air, and he required immediate oxygen therapy. The respiratory rate was 30 breaths per minute, and auscultation revealed wheezing and crackles in both lung fields. Arterial blood gas analysis showed a pH of 7.32, PaCO2 of 60 mmHg, and PaO2 of 50 mmHg. The chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates. The patient was started on bronchodilators, steroids, and antibiotics. Despite initial treatment, the patient's respiratory distress worsened, and he required non-invasive ventilation support. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial comparing non-invasive mask ventilation vs cuirass ventilation in patients with acute respiratory failure.

55 year-old male with a history of heavy tobacco and alcohol use who presents with a 2-month history of difficulty swallowing and pain in the throat. He reports progressive weight loss of approximately 20 pounds over the past month. A biopsy of the lesion shows squamous cell carcinoma. Imaging studies reveal a large lesion in the oropharynx extending into the base of the tongue with multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck. He is considered unresectable by the head and neck surgeon due to extensive involvement of the tongue base and surrounding structures. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. Laboratory tests show adequate organ function, including leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, total bilirubin, AST/ALT, and creatinine clearance. The patient is willing to adhere to the study protocol and agrees to use an acceptable method of birth control during treatment and for 12 months after completion of treatment. The patient has no prior history of radiation to the head and neck area and has not received any prior treatment for head and neck cancer. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. There is no evidence of uncontrolled intercurrent illness or HIV infection. The patient does not have any documented or symptoms of peripheral neuropathy and has no history of allergic reactions to compounds similar to the ones used in this study.

A 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years came to the clinic complaining of difficulty sleeping at night. He is currently taking Losartan 50mg daily for his hypertension. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly for 20-30 minutes a day, 3 times a week. He has no known allergies to any food or medication. His BMI is 32.5 kg/m2.

A 45 year old woman with a BMI of 32 and a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes comes to the clinic seeking treatment options. She has been struggling with weight gain and elevated blood sugar levels despite following a strict diet and exercise regimen. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, pancreatitis or other gastrointestinal conditions. She is not pregnant and does not require prescription anticoagulation therapy. She has not undergone any previous GI surgery. She is willing to discontinue the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during the implant period. She has no active symptoms of kidney stones or known presence of gallstones. She does not have a family or patient history of known diagnosis or pre-existing condition of systemic lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, or other autoimmune connective tissue disorder. She has completed treatment for H. pylori and is negative for H. pylori. She is interested in participating in the registry observing EndoBarrier Treatment Outcomes in Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes and/or Obesity.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, worry, and nervousness. She has been referred to the older people's mental health service within NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde for treatment of her common mental health conditions. She has no history of psychosis, addictions, or cognitive impairment and is not at risk of self-harm. She speaks fluent English and is able to provide informed consent. She will be offered participation in a 10-week group program of Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT) as part of her treatment. Outcome measures will be administered before and after the program to assess changes in her wellbeing and functioning, and she will also be asked to participate in a semi-structured interview to discuss her experience of the intervention. The CFT group will be led by an experienced NHS Clinical Psychologist and will incorporate elements of mindfulness and techniques to improve self-compassion.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic seeking treatment for his morbid obesity. He has a BMI of 55 kg/m2 and has been struggling with his weight for over a decade. Despite trying various diets and exercise programs, he has not been successful in losing weight. He has a history of hypertension and sleep apnea, which have worsened with his weight gain. The patient has been evaluated by the Obesity-related specific committee and has been deemed eligible for Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy, which is recommended by the Haute Autorité de Santé. The patient has social protection and is willing to participate in the clinical trial investigating the use of fibrin glue (Tissucol®) during the surgery to reduce the incidence of postoperative complications such as gastric fistula, intra-abdominal hemorrhage, and intra-abdominal locoregional collection. He has no history of previous bariatric or gastric surgery, and his BMI is within the inclusion criteria. The patient is not allergic to Tissucol® and has consented to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old boy was referred to the Abdominal Pain Clinic at Children's Mercy Hospital due to recurrent abdominal pain for the past 3 months. The pain is located in the periumbilical region and is described as dull and crampy. The pain is not associated with any particular food or activity and is not relieved by bowel movements. He has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or surgeries. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is not taking any medications and has not had any previous hospitalizations. He speaks fluent English.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past 6 months. He has been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis by a rheumatologist and has psoriatic skin lesions. He has been on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) for the past few months, but his symptoms have not improved significantly. His rheumatologist has recommended that he start treatment with anti-TNF blocking agents, specifically etanercept or adalimumab. He meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial, including being anti-TNF naïve, having active psoriatic arthritis with at least one joint suitable for synovial biopsy, and being on a stable dose of DMARDs for at least 1 month prior to study entry. He is interested in participating in the trial to potentially benefit from more specific therapies for inflammatory arthritis and contribute to the development of better treatment options.

A 22-year-old female with a history of congenital heart disease has been under the care of a pediatric cardiology clinic at Duke University Medical Center since birth. She is currently in her last year of college and has been experiencing difficulty managing her condition while juggling her academic responsibilities. She has been struggling with fatigue, shortness of breath, and difficulty concentrating during class. She has access to a smartphone and is interested in participating in a peer coaching intervention to assist with her self-management skills. She has no history of cognitive delay and has never been seen at an adult cardiology clinic.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of diverticulitis comes to the clinic for an elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for the past few months. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He reports no allergies to medications. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant. His laboratory tests, including a complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel and coagulation profile are within normal limits. He has an ASA class II classification.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) for the last 5 years. He has experienced shortness of breath, coughing and wheezing on a daily basis, which has significantly impacted his daily activities. He has tried various medications, but they have not provided much relief. The patient has a history of smoking and currently uses oxygen therapy at home. He is motivated to improve his quality of life and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will help him to achieve this goal. He is able to walk for short distances, but experiences significant breathlessness with exertion. The patient has not participated in pulmonary rehabilitation in the last 6 months and has not been involved in any other research study involving exercise training in the last 6 months. He is fluent in English and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She had her yearly mammogram and the imaging showed a mass in her right breast. Her biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma. She had an MRI of her breast and axilla which showed no suspicious lymph nodes. She underwent lumpectomy and her surgical margins were negative. She is scheduled to receive adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. She is married and has two young children. She works part-time as a teacher's aide. She has no known allergies. Her family history is significant for breast cancer in her maternal grandmother. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially avoid the discomfort and potential complications associated with sentinel node biopsy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing pelvic pain and bloating for the past few months. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been trying to conceive for the past year with no success. She was referred for gynecological ultrasound which showed a mass in the right ovary that was unable to be classified. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided oral informed consent. MRI will be performed to help determine the nature of the ovarian mass.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been smoking cigarettes for 40 years. He has recently been diagnosed with mild COPD with an FEV1 of 70% predicted and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.6. The patient reports activity-related dyspnea, with a Baseline Dyspnea Index focal score of 8 and a MRC dyspnea scale of 3. He has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. The patient has no contraindications to clinical exercise testing and has never used daytime oxygen. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is committed to attending all study visits and complying with the prescribed dosing regimen.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl with a history of cystic fibrosis (CF) diagnosed by genetic testing. She has been experiencing chronic respiratory symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath, and has received multiple courses of antibiotics over the past year. Her most recent sputum culture shows the presence of P. aeruginosa, indicating chronic airway infection. She has had several hospitalizations for exacerbations and her lung function, as measured by FEV1, is currently at 45% predicted. The patient and her parents are interested in exploring alternative treatment options to manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial to gain access to aztreonam lysine for inhalation (AZLI), which has shown promising results in treating chronic P. aeruginosa airway infection in patients with CF. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which was diagnosed two years ago. He had undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but unfortunately, the tumor had progressed and become unresectable. The patient presents with a history of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and distention, and constipation for the last one month. He reports that he is unable to eat solid food and has lost significant weight over the past few weeks. On physical examination, the patient is emaciated and has a distended abdomen. The patient's ECOG performance status is 2. The patient's gastric outlet obstruction score is 1. The patient has no history of prior metallic stent placement, gastric surgery, or coagulation disorders. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

An 80 year old man with a history of Alzheimer's disease came to the clinic with his daughter, complaining of increased agitation, aggression, and motor disturbances. He also reported experiencing moderate pain in his lower back and hips. He has been on acetaminophen for pain management for the past few months but it does not seem to be effective anymore. His daughter is his primary caregiver and is in contact with him on a daily basis. The patient's CDR score is 2, indicating moderate dementia. He has a history of depression but has not experienced any major episodes in the past six months. He does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. His liver function tests are normal. His current medications include donepezil and memantine for dementia, and lisinopril and metoprolol for hypertension.

The patient is a 58-year-old post-menopausal woman who has been diagnosed with stage III colon cancer after undergoing a curative surgery. The patient has no evidence of metastatic disease and has signed a written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and the pre-treatment CEA is within the upper normal limit. The patient has no history of other malignancies within the last 5 years, except for curatively treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has no clinically relevant cardiovascular disease, medical history or current evidence of CNS disease, or clinically relevant psychiatric disability precluding informed consent. The patient is willing to use an effective contraception method. The patient has no peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1 (CTCAE v. 3.0). The patient is eligible for randomization between 2-8 weeks after the curative surgery.

The patient is a child between the ages of 6 months to 5 years residing in one of the 16 tribal villages in the Melghat region of Amaravati district in Maharashtra, India. The child is suffering from severe malnutrition as per weight for height criteria (WHO), weight for age criteria (WHO), MUAC (WHO), IAP grade III & IV. The child's parents or guardians have provided consent for the child's participation in the SAMMAN project, which aims to provide community-based health care to severely malnourished children in the region. The child will be treated by trained semi-literate village health workers who will provide growth monitoring, treatment for associated diseases like diarrhea, pneumonia, malaria, etc. and intensive behavior change communication to improve the child's nutrition. The project is being implemented as a pilot project in the region with the potential for replication in all tribal and rural parts of India.

A 29-year-old woman is currently 40 weeks and 4 days pregnant with her first child. She has had a healthy pregnancy so far, with no complications or medical conditions. She plans to have a natural birth without epidural anesthesia. She is interested in alternative methods to induce labor and is considering acupuncture. She has no history of acupuncture treatment or any other alternative therapies. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for the induction of labor.

A 23-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history came to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a novel light-based treatment to reduce morbidity in shoulder surgical patients. The patient reported no allergies to benzoyl peroxide or chlorhexidine and had no previous history of shoulder infections. He had not taken antibiotics within one month of the research visit and was not immunocompromised, nor did he have an active cancer or diabetes. The patient reported no skin lesions or abrasions over the deltopectoral interval and had not received topical corticosteroid treatment to either shoulder, or systemic corticosteroid treatment within 2 weeks of the research visit. He also had not received topical benzoyl peroxide treatment or blue light therapy to either shoulder within 2 weeks of the research visit. The patient had no prior incision over the deltopectoral interval of either shoulder and had no contraindications to blue light treatment. The patient was eager to contribute to the study and was willing to follow the protocol procedures.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with leukemia and will require long-term stay in the intensive care unit. The medical team has decided that a central venous catheter (CVC) will be necessary for his treatment. The boy is in otherwise good health, but he does have a history of fainting during medical procedures. He has no known allergies or other medical issues. The medical team will decide whether to use real-time ultrasound navigation or anatomical-based CVC insertion based on their experience and training. The primary goal is to ensure the CVC insertion is successful with minimal complications.

This clinical trial is not applicable for individual patients as it is a worksite program for bus drivers. However, if we have to describe the ideal candidate for this program, it would be a bus driver working at one of the four participating garages who is concerned about their weight and interested in making lifestyle changes to prevent weight gain. They should be willing to participate in a two-year multi-component environmental intervention that targets food availability, physical activity opportunities, the social environment, and media/promotion related to health food choices, physical activity, and body weight. They should not have any medical conditions that prevent them from participating in physical activity or dietary changes.

A 42-year-old male with a history of asthma and sleep apnea is scheduled for elective surgery. He is currently using a CPAP machine at night to manage his sleep apnea. He has a BMI of 32 and is a non-smoker. He has no allergies to any medication. He has been informed about the risks and benefits of awake tracheal intubation and has given his consent to participate in the study. He is able to understand oral and written information and has no difficulty with mouth opening.

A 45-year-old man with a confirmed HIV infection and latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) infection. He is currently taking antiretroviral treatment and prophylaxis for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia. He has a history of aminoglycoside treatment for an intercurrent infection. He is able and willing to comply with the treatment and clinical management issues. The patient has no current active tuberculosis, acute hepatitis, or peripheral neuropathy of grade 3 or 4. He has signed informed consent and has a perceived life expectancy of at least six months. The patient is in reasonably good health at the time of study entry.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained second-degree burns on his left leg and right arm while working in a factory. The burns were treated with split thickness skin grafts (SSG) from his thigh. The donor site is expected to be between 8 and 200 cm2 on a non-articulated area. He has no history of allergies and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has no other significant medical history and has not undergone any skin grafts in the past. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements, including regular clinic visits during the treatment period and follow-up period, and application of Oleogel-S10 on the SSG at every change of wound dressing. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient's pregnancy test is negative, and he is not breastfeeding. The patient is not diabetic and has no skin disorders that may affect the healing of the acute wounds.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years is currently experiencing mild cognitive impairment. He was diagnosed using the UK Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank Research Center Clinical diagnostic criteria. He has been under treatment for Parkinson's disease with Levodopa and Carbidopa. He has no history of other neurological diseases or psychiatric disorders. He has a normal liver and renal function. He has never undergone any surgery or radiation therapy. He is not allergic to IV radiographic contrast. The patient is able to enter the bore of the PET/CT scanner and lie still for the entire imaging time. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 25-year-old female with a body mass index of 22 is being recruited for a clinical trial investigating the effect of delivery route on the pharmacokinetics of Sufentanil NanoTab. She is a non-smoker and does not have any pulmonary disease or sleep apnea. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She is interested in participating in the trial to contribute to the development of new medications and advance medical research.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation two years ago. She is currently taking Rivaroxaban as a direct oral anticoagulant to prevent blood clots. She has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. She is also taking a low dose of aspirin daily. She has no history of stroke or any other medical conditions. She is able to read and understand the questionnaire and is willing to participate in the study. She has no history of dementia or cognitive impairment.

The patient is a 22-year-old Spanish-speaking low-income mother who recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy. She was diagnosed with depression during her pregnancy and has been receiving counseling and medications at a community health center in the Seattle, Washington area. She has access to a telephone and is interested in participating in the study. She lives with her partner and their baby in a small apartment. She has completed high school and is currently unemployed. Her partner works as a part-time delivery driver. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious about being a new mother and worries that she is not doing a good job. She is eager to learn more about how to be a better parent and improve her relationship with her baby. She has no history of acute crisis, hospitalization, or imprisonment.

Patient is a 68yo man who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. Upon evaluation, he was found to have an anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to blockage of the intracranial internal carotid artery. His NIHSS score was 10. He arrived within 24 hours of symptom onset and was deemed eligible for the Capillary Index Score Trial. The patient has no known allergies or previous medical history of note. He has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 36-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with Fabry disease. She has been experiencing neuropathic pain in her hands and feet for the past year. The pain is a constant burning sensation that interferes with her daily activities. She has not experienced any Fabry crises yet. She is married with two children and works part-time as a teacher. She has a family history of Fabry disease, with her father and brother both being affected. She has not received any treatment for Fabry disease yet. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not on any medications. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the purpose of the research.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been struggling with obesity for several years. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 33 kg/m^2 and has been experiencing difficulty with weight loss despite multiple attempts at dieting and exercise. She is a non-smoker and lives with her husband and two children. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is currently taking medication for both conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of a prebiotic supplement on glucose metabolism and gut microbiota. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the procedures outlined in the study protocol. She does not have any history of diabetes, psychiatric disorders, or gastrointestinal or liver disorders. She does not consume alcohol in excess and is not currently taking any pre- or probiotic supplements. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to provide fecal samples and undergo an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) and bio-impedance measurements.

Newborn baby boy born at 29 weeks gestational age weighing 1.2 kg who requires mechanical ventilation due to acute respiratory distress syndrome. The mother had a history of premature labor and was treated with antenatal steroids. The baby has no known congenital malformations or chromosomal abnormalities. He is currently receiving surfactant therapy and undergoing mechanical ventilation. The treating neonatologist has recommended the baby for enrollment in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of azithromycin in preventing lung injury induced by mechanical ventilation. The parents have been approached and provided with informed consent.

16-year-old Hispanic female with a history of asthma diagnosed by a physician at age 10. She is currently taking inhaled controller medication for her asthma. She has been compliant with her medication regimen, but her parents are worried about her adherence as she has been busy with school and extracurricular activities. She has experienced a few exacerbations in the past year, resulting in hospitalizations. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if financial incentives will help her remember to take her medication consistently. She is fluent in English and Spanish. She does not have any other significant medical history or chronic lung diseases.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a large kidney stone. He has a past medical history of hypertension and no other significant medical conditions. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no allergies to any medications. The patient is scheduled for percutaneous nephrolithotomy surgery (PNL) with urinary bladder catheter. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status of I. He is not obese (BMI < 30) and does not have chronic opioid use, bladder outflow obstruction, benign prostatic hyperplasia, or overactive bladder (OAB). The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements involved.

78-year-old female patient who has been admitted to the geriatrics unit for evaluation and management of multiple chronic conditions including hypertension, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis. The patient is taking multiple medications including lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, calcium, and vitamin D supplements. The patient also reports chronic pain and is currently taking ibuprofen as needed. The patient has a history of medication non-adherence and has difficulty remembering all of her prescribed medications. The patient has agreed to participate in the MATRIX-DPRS study to assess the use of the medication record managed by pharmacists in improving medication management and adherence in elderly patients.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who is experiencing difficulty with her vision due to cataracts. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has no history of intraocular surgery or glaucoma. She is employed as a secretary and her job requires her to spend long hours in front of a computer screen. She has a family history of cataracts and her mother had cataract surgery in her 60s. She has never worn contact lenses and wears glasses for distance vision only. Her current best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 20/50 in both eyes. Her intraocular pressure (IOP) is within normal limits and her angles are open upon gonioscopy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of phacoemulsification and MSICS for cataract surgery. She is willing and able to attend follow-up appointments for up to 6 months.

A 34-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia presents with frequent auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) for the past year. She has been receiving stable psychopharmacological treatment for the past 6 months, which includes risperidone (4 mg/day) and sertraline (100 mg/day). She reports hearing voices that are often critical and derogatory, which significantly affects her daily life and quality of life. She has no history of epilepsy or ferromagnetic or electromagnetic implants that may pose a risk during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and/or cTBS. She is not pregnant, and her urine samples test negative for illicit drugs and Phosphatidylethanol (PEth). She does not use benzodiazepines daily. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study's requirements.

This is a 56 year-old male who was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis based on laboratory findings and ultrasound imaging. He has a history of heavy alcohol use for over 20 years and has been struggling with addiction. He has been followed at a gastroenterology department and has had several hospital admissions due to complications related to liver cirrhosis, including ascites and hepatic encephalopathy. The patient speaks fluent Swedish and is willing to participate in the study. He has no other significant medical history, except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication.

A 45-year-old healthy male patient visited the dental clinic for an immediate dental implant procedure. He has a history of missing tooth due to trauma. The patient has adequate bone volume for the procedure, and there are no signs of periapical pathosis. He is a non-smoker and has good oral hygiene practices. The patient is not currently suffering from any systemic diseases that would contraindicate implant placement or surgical procedures. He is mentally stable and has no psychological problems. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to sign the informed consent.

A 25-year-old healthy civilian male presents seeking to participate in a clinical trial related to heat stress. He has no known medical illness and is not on any medication. He has no history of hypertension or diabetes. His past medical history is unremarkable. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He reports a balanced diet and no known allergies. He is interested in participating in the study and agrees to undergo medical examination and an interview with a nutritionist to assess his dietary intake of Astaxanthin. He is informed about the risks and benefits of the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease. Despite optimal pharmacological therapy, he experiences symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. The echocardiogram shows that he has left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 25%. The cardiac surgeon and interventional cardiologist have determined that he is not a candidate for conventional revascularization procedures such as coronary artery bypass graft surgery or percutaneous angioplasty. He has no history of neoplasms. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating gene therapy with hVEGF165 to induce angiogenesis and potentially improve his symptoms and left ventricular function.

Samantha is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She lives in a rural area and has limited access to diabetes education classes due to transportation issues. She struggles with managing her blood sugar levels and has experienced several episodes of hypoglycemia in the past. Samantha also suffers from mild hearing loss but wears hearing aids. She has a strong support system from her family and is willing to participate in a diabetes education program. Samantha is currently taking metformin and insulin to manage her diabetes. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. Samantha is interested in participating in a telemedicine group diabetes education program to learn more about how to better manage her diabetes and improve her overall health.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) 2 years ago. She has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. She has been on a strict low-fat diet and exercise regimen, but her liver function tests have been progressively worsening. She has been evaluated for a liver transplant and has been listed for transplantation. She has no significant past medical history, and her physical examination shows no evidence of ascites or edema. Her BMI is 30, and her liver function tests show elevated levels of liver enzymes. She is currently on medications for her symptoms, including pain medication and anti-inflammatory drugs. She has no contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging. She is considered a low to moderate transplant risk candidate, suitable for a marginal graft, as assessed by the UHB liver transplant listing MDT meeting. She has been informed of the VITTAL trial, and her eligibility for participation will be determined after further evaluation and testing.

An 70-year-old male diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease presents with complaints of difficulty sleeping at night and feeling sleepy during the day. He reports waking up frequently during the night and having trouble falling back asleep. He has tried over-the-counter sleep aids, but they have not helped. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with lisinopril. He has no history of psychiatric illness, and his medications include donepezil and memantine for management of his Alzheimer's disease. The patient's Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 24, indicating mild cognitive impairment. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial assessing sleep disturbance in Alzheimer's disease in the hopes of improving his sleep and daytime alertness.

The patient is a 23 year-old male who was hiking in a wooded area and was bitten by a copperhead snake on his right leg. He immediately sought medical attention and presented with mild swelling and tenderness at the bite site. He has no history of allergies or previous snake bites. He is currently not taking any medications and has no significant medical history. He is able to read and comprehend the written assessment tools and is willing and able to complete the follow-up schedule of assessments. He has signed the informed consent document and has confirmed his eligibility for the study within 24 hours of the envenomation. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not under the influence of drugs or alcohol. He is able to make reliable self-reports of functionality status based solely on the condition of interest. He meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

42-year-old female, smoker for 10 years, with a family history of early onset atherosclerosis in her father who suffered from a heart attack at 52 years old. She has a history of hypertension, controlled with medication, and hyperlipidemia with high LDL levels, despite dietary modifications. She reports occasional chest discomfort and shortness of breath upon exertion but no history of heart disease or other significant medical issues. She presents for evaluation of possible heart disease and is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating new heart imaging techniques. She is willing to undergo multiple MRI scans and angiography to assess her heart and blood vessels. She is currently not pregnant or lactating, has no implanted devices, and is clinically stable. She is able to provide informed consent and is capable of coming to the Clinical Center for the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who experienced an episode of cerebral infarction 10 days ago. He was admitted to the hospital with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. Following a CT scan that confirmed the diagnosis of cerebral infarction, he was treated with standard care and subsequently discharged from the hospital. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, for which he takes medication. He does not have a history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy. He is a retired accountant and lives with his spouse. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. His current weight is 80 kg, and his height is 170 cm. His blood pressure is currently well-controlled at 130/80 mmHg. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the safety and efficacy of clopidogrel for cerebral infarction treatment.

A 32-year-old father of a 6-month-old baby who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. He is experiencing symptoms of depression such as feelings of sadness and hopelessness, loss of interest in activities he once enjoyed, difficulty sleeping and concentrating, and changes in appetite. He is not currently taking any antidepressants or receiving any psychotherapy. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The father is available to attend the group parenting intervention sessions delivered by non-specialists and community health workers. He is able to complete a baseline assessment and participate in focus groups and in-depth interviews before and after the intervention. He is not currently experiencing active suicidal ideation or any other severe physical or mental disorders.

52yo female with a history of invasive lobular breast cancer diagnosed 4 months ago with biopsy-proven ILC, and a suspicious mass identified on recent imaging study, which could be metastatic disease. She is currently asymptomatic, with no known metastases. The patient has completed a course of neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is awaiting surgery. She has no known history of primary breast cancer or other malignancies. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and her medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. The patient is willing to undergo biopsy if necessary as per standard of care.

This is a 9 year-old male with a history of persistent bronchial asthma for at least 6 months. The patient has been on inhaled steroids in the past and currently uses a rescue inhaler as needed. His FEV1 is between 50-90% of predicted. He has no concomitant severe diseases or diseases which are contraindications for the use of inhaled steroids. He has not had a respiratory tract infection or asthma exacerbation within the last 30 days prior to entry into the study. The patient does not have a history of life-threatening asthma. He was not born premature and has never smoked. The patient is not currently pregnant nor does she intend to become pregnant during the course of the study. He is not currently breastfeeding and is using safe contraception.
