A 57 year old male with a history of primary central nervous system lymphoma diagnosed 2 years ago, who underwent radiation therapy and chemotherapy but was found to have relapsed. The patient is currently experiencing headaches, confusion and vision changes. MRI shows a new contrast-enhancing lesion in the right frontal lobe. Past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of smoking. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 2, ANC of 1,200/uL and a platelet count of 140,000/uL. Total bilirubin, AST and creatinine are within normal limits. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the POMALYST REMS program and provide tissue samples for correlative research purposes.

45-year-old female with a history of basal cell nevus syndrome and multiple basal cell carcinomas (BCCs) diagnosed clinically by a study investigator. She has no history of BCCs on the face, chest, or back impinging on vital sites. She meets the diagnostic criteria for basal cell nevus syndrome with the presence of more than 2 BCCs and three or more palmar and/or plantar pits. She has no known PTCH1 gene mutation. She is currently using adequate contraception and has documented one negative serum pregnancy test within 14 days prior to study entry. The patient is willing to abstain from applying non-study topical medications to the skin of the face for the duration of the study. She is willing to participate in the study and return for follow-up tests for 18 months. She has no history of invasive cancer within the past five years excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, Stage I cervical cancer, or CLL Stage 0.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia. She has a BMI of 31 kg/m² and has been experiencing weight gain over the past year. She is on a stable dose of antipsychotic medication for the past month with no dosage change, and has been deemed symptomatically stable by the clinical staff in the last two months. She has no history of alcohol or substance dependence, opioid use, or positive urine drug screen for opiates. She is not currently pregnant, does not have a known sensitivity to naltrexone, and does not have any medical disorder known to cause obesity. She is not currently being treated with insulin or Depo-Provera. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help manage her weight and improve her overall health.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of chronic lower back pain for over 6 months. He reports the pain to be constant and has a score of 6 on a 0-10 point Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) for average daily pain. He has been taking analgesic medication for the past 3 months but has not experienced significant relief. He is willing to discontinue the use of all rescue pain medications for the duration of the trial except for OTC oral acetaminophen. He is not on any psychoactive medication and has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. He has no history of failed back surgeries or spinal stenosis. He reports no radicular symptoms or diagnosis of shingles or post-herpetic neuralgia. He is willing and able to comply with all follow-up procedures and return for scheduled follow-up visits. He is willing to provide written informed consent and HIPAA authorization prior to enrollment into the study.

52-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with MLL+ acute leukemia presented with symptoms of fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. He denies any drug or alcohol abuse. He is currently not on any medications except for insulin and metformin for diabetes control. His physical examination is remarkable for pallor, mild hepatosplenomegaly, and petechiae. His laboratory results show pancytopenia with a white blood cell count of 1.5 K/uL, hemoglobin of 7.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 40 K/uL. Bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of MLL+ acute leukemia. He is scheduled to undergo allo-HSCT and is eligible to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma. He is a former heavy smoker and has a history of alcohol abuse. The patient has been referred to the study by his oncologist, and he has provided informed consent to participate. He is currently being treated with Sorafenib, and he is scheduled to have regular blood samples taken every 3-6 months for up to two years. The patient has no other active malignancies, and he has not plans to emigrate from Denmark. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes atorvastatin. He has no significant allergies, and his physical exam is unremarkable. The patient has not undergone any surgical interventions or radiation therapy for his HCC at this time.

The patient is a 43-year-old woman who has been experiencing urinary urgency and frequency for the past 6 months. She has had to wake up multiple times during the night to urinate, and she often experiences leakage on the way to the bathroom. The patient has previously been diagnosed with idiopathic overactive bladder and has tried antimuscarinic medication, but it was not well-tolerated. She is eager to participate in a clinical trial that could offer her relief from her symptoms. The patient has no history of urogynecological surgery or any other medical conditions that could affect her bladder function. She is not currently pregnant and has no intention of becoming pregnant during the study. The patient is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including completing a voiding diary and quality of life questionnaire. The strength of her pelvic floor muscles is 4/5, and she has no metallic implants or electronic devices in the areas between her lumbar region and lower extremities. The patient is excited to be part of a study that could potentially improve her quality of life and alleviate her symptoms.

The patient is a 62-year-old female diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago. She has received two lines of therapy, including bortezomib and lenalidomide, but her disease has relapsed and is refractory to current treatment. Her oncologist has recommended changing her treatment to a combination therapy composed exclusively of drugs from the list provided in the inclusion criteria. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She takes no other medications. Upon physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented with no acute distress. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her BMI is 25. There is no evidence of edema in the lower extremities, and her abdomen is soft with no tenderness or ascites. Bone marrow biopsy samples are clinically indicated for the patient, and she has provided written informed consent for participation in this study.

A 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing dry eye symptoms and has been diagnosed with early-stage cataracts (grade 1-3 according to LOCS III classification) in both eyes. She has a history of mild hypertension and is currently on medication. Her current corrected visual acuity is 0.8 in both eyes. She has not undergone any previous eye surgeries and is not planning to undergo cataract surgery in the near future. She wears glasses for reading and driving. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Visglyc eye drops in improving her dry eye symptoms and quality of life. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has no known allergies to any ophthalmic treatments.

The patient is a 25-year-old non-smoking, healthy female with a BMI of 25. She does not have any respiratory or nasal/sinus issues, and has not been on any inhaled medications or exposed to radiation within the past year. She is not currently pregnant, nursing, or sexually active. She has normal lung function with a FEV1 of 85% predicted and a FEV1/FVC ratio of 75%. She is willing to provide written informed consent in English and is available to participate in the study visits. She does not have facial hair that would need to be shaved.

The patient is a 32 year old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. He has been on a stable treatment regimen of two atypical antipsychotics for the past year and has not experienced any significant side effects. He lives alone in a small apartment and works part-time in a local grocery store. He has a history of substance abuse, primarily with marijuana, but has been sober for the past 6 months. He has a supportive family who visit him occasionally. He has no significant medical history or allergies to medications. He is currently not on any other medications or supplements. He is able to communicate clearly and understands the nature of the study. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all study visits.

A 45-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of psoriatic arthritis with moderate to severe joint pain, stiffness, and swelling. Her symptoms have been unresponsive to previous treatments including methotrexate and etanercept. She has a history of psoriasis for over 10 years, which has been managed with topical treatments. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the study period. She completed the feeder study without meeting any withdrawal criteria and is expected to benefit from participation in this Open-Label Extension study. Her recent laboratory test results are within normal limits. She is looking for a long-term treatment option that can help manage her psoriatic arthritis symptoms.

This is a 30 year-old female with a history of asthma since childhood. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and has been diagnosed with non-atopic asthma. She has never smoked and has no significant medical history other than asthma. The patient has occasional asthma exacerbations, but has not required oral corticosteroids in the past year. She is interested in participating in clinical research to help advance the understanding and treatment of asthma.

A 52-year-old Caucasian male with a history of glioblastoma multiforme presents with recurrent symptoms of headaches, nausea, and seizures. He had undergone surgical resection, radiation therapy, and temozolomide chemotherapy in the past. However, his symptoms have reappeared, and the MRI scan shows tumor recurrence. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. He is currently on no medications except for antiepileptic drugs. He has no allergies to any medications. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has never smoked or consumed alcohol. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written consent. His ECOG performance status is 1, and his KPS score is 80.

A 45-year-old male with a BMI of 32 kg/m2 has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and is currently taking metformin for glucose control. Despite medication, his HbA1c is still above 8.0%. He has not received any investigational product as part of a clinical study or GLP-1 analogue-containing preparation in the last 30 days. He has not taken any herbal preparations or drugs licensed for control of body weight or appetite, opiates, domperidone, metoclopramide or other drugs known to alter gastric emptying, glucagon, or warfarin prior to the start of the study. He does not have any contraindication to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and has no claustrophobia or dislike of confined spaces. He has not experienced any symptoms of acutely decompensated blood glucose control, has no history of type 1 diabetes mellitus or diabetic ketoacidosis, and has not been treated with daily SC insulin within 90 days prior to screening. He has not had recurrent unexplained hypoglycaemic episodes and does not have significant inflammatory bowel disease, gastroparesis, or other severe disease or surgery affecting the upper GI tract. He does not have acute or chronic pancreatitis and does not have significant hepatic disease. His AST, ALT, and total bilirubin are all within normal limits. He has normal renal function with an eGFR of 85 mL/minute/1.73m2. He has well-controlled hypertension with a systolic blood pressure of 135 mm Hg and a diastolic blood pressure of 85 mm Hg. He has no history of unstable angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack or stroke within 3 months prior to screening, or percutaneous coronary intervention or a coronary artery bypass graft within the past 6 months. He does not have severe congestive heart failure, New York Heart Association Class III or IV. He has a basal calcitonin level of 10 ng/L at screening and no history/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia. He has not had neoplastic disease within 5 years prior to screening and has tested negative for serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody. He does not have substance dependence or a history of alcohol abuse and/or excess alcohol intake. He drinks 1-2 units of alcohol per week.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been living with HIV for 7 years. He was recently diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, which was confirmed through a biopsy. The patient has not received any treatment for his lymphoma as of yet. He reports feeling fatigued and has experienced night sweats and weight loss over the past few months. His CD4 count is 80/mm3, and his viral load is undetectable. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 3. He has no known history of hepatitis or renal disease. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to adhere to the treatment regimen.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl who was born at 33 weeks gestation and spent 3 weeks in the NICU at Mount Sinai Hospital. She was discharged home with no major health issues, and has been receiving regular follow-up care at a local pediatric clinic. Her parents report that she has been meeting her developmental milestones, but they have noticed that she is slightly delayed in her speech and social skills compared to her peers. The parents have agreed to participate in the study and will bring their daughter to Mount Sinai Hospital for evaluation using the Bayley-III. They have also completed the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) questionnaire prior to the appointment.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is in good physical health and has a BMI of 22. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use an approved method of contraception for the duration of the study. She does not have a history of substance abuse disorder or use of opioids within the last 30 days. She is not a heavy caffeine drinker and has no history of intolerance or hypersensitivity to opioids or opioid antagonists. She has not used any prescription or over-the-counter medication within 14 days prior to study start, with the exception of prescription contraceptives. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of water consumption on the pharmacokinetics of ALKS 5461.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET). The tumor is unresectable and locally advanced, with no distant metastasis. The patient has been treated with lanreotide 120mg every 28 days for the past 6 months with good tolerance. At the time of inclusion in the study, the patient is not showing any signs of disease progression according to investigator assessment. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not received any previous therapy for PanNET except short-acting octreotide subcutaneous (SC) for symptomatic relief of functioning tumors. The patient has given consent to participate in the study and will be followed up for the next 24 months to assess the progression-free survival rate after treatment initiation with lanreotide 120mg every 28 days.

This is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) three years ago based on McDonald criteria. She has been clinically stable for the past two months, with no MS exacerbation or change in disease modifying therapy. Her Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDS) is 4.5, indicating moderate disability. She has no history of seizure disorder or epileptiform activity on EEG. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is 80, indicating normal renal function. She does not have any contraindication to DER and is not taking 4-aminopyridine. Her 6-minute walking test distance is 300m, which falls within the screening range of 50-500m. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is not breastfeeding, pregnant, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She has no cognitive deficits that would interfere with her ability to give informed consent or perform study testing. She has not been hospitalized for psychiatric illness in the past six months and does not have any other serious or unstable medical conditions. She has not used mitoxantrone (Novantrone) within the past six months.

56-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse leading to cirrhosis, classified as Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) class B. He has not undergone liver transplantation or transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) or portocaval anastomosis (PCA). He is currently stable without any confounding end-stage co-morbidity. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to give written informed consent. He has not participated in a previous study involving an investigational product for at least 90 days before enrollment. He is not currently pregnant or nursing and is using an acceptable method of contraception.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue for the past year. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been taking various antiarrhythmic drugs without success. He has been diagnosed with symptomatic persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and is refractory to or intolerant to at least one class I or III antiarrhythmic drug. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate hybrid therapy and heart team for AF. He has not undergone a previous AF ablation procedure and is willing to provide informed consent. However, he does have a left atrial size of 75ml/m² on transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE), which may be a potential exclusion criterion.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT) 5 years ago. He completed chemotherapy treatment and has had negative CT scans in the past 3 years. The patient is willing to attend follow-up for the next 5 years and has no contraindication to CT imaging. The purpose of this clinical trial is to use CT scans to follow up on patients who have been treated for metastatic testicular cancer in order to assess the frequency of relapse or recurrent abnormalities and assess the utility of CT scan-assessment in these patients. The patient will undergo a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis to screen for detectable abnormalities or indications of late relapse. If the scan is negative, he will be followed yearly by clinical examination and tumor marker assessment, and every 5 years by CT imaging. If the scan is positive, confirmation of relapse will be done by surgical excision or biopsy, and treatment will be initiated according to best clinical practice.

A 40-year-old woman gave birth to a full-term baby boy who developed seizures within the first 72 hours of life. The baby has been admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit at St. Louis Children's Hospital. The baby's Apgar score was 7 at 5 minutes and he required respiratory support at 10 minutes of life. The baby is suspected to have neonatal encephalopathy based on altered neurological behavior. The baby will be screened for eligibility for a clinical trial comparing "EEG Seizure Treatment Group" or ESG with a "Clinical Seizure Treatment Group" or CSG. The study will evaluate the impact of electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure treatment in neonatal encephalopathy. The baby is expected to be eligible for the trial if he meets the moderate-severe neonatal encephalopathy criteria or has suspected or definite neonatal seizures. The trial will monitor the baby's seizures and neuromotor disability, and conduct neurodevelopmental evaluations at 18 to 24 months.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with low-grade non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He has undergone three chemotherapy regimens and two antibody treatments, but his disease has relapsed. He is experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has no known lymphomatous involvement of the CNS and no seizure disorders or prior brain injury that could cause seizures. He has measurable disease on physical examination and imaging studies, with several tumor masses that are reproducibly measurable in two perpendicular diameters and larger than 1x1 cm. He has a performance status of 1 and has no history of intravenous drug abuse or behavior associated with an increased risk of HIV infection. He does not have peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1 and has ANC ≥ 750/μL, βHCG negative, Creatinine ≤ 2 x normal, Bilirubin ≤ within institutional normal limits, and AST and ALT ≤ 2.5 x upper limit of normal. He is willing to use two methods of birth control for 28 days prior to treatment and while under treatment with thalidomide and for four weeks after completing therapy, as he is a married man of childbearing potential. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive thalidomide in the hope that it will be effective in treating his relapsed low-grade non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who noticed a painless lump on his forehead a few months ago. He initially thought it was a cyst, but it didn't go away. He recently consulted with his primary care physician who referred him to a dermatologist. The dermatologist performed a biopsy and diagnosed him with Merkel cell carcinoma. Imaging studies revealed no evidence of distant metastasis, but the tumor is unresectable due to its location. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating he is able to perform most activities of daily living but is limited in strenuous activity. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment. He has not undergone any prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease and has not received adjuvant cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, or fluorouracil.

This is a 58-year-old male with a history of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (SCLC) diagnosed six months ago. He received first-line therapy with carboplatin and etoposide (CE) and had a partial response. His performance status is 1 on the ECOG criteria, and his expected survival is estimated to be above three months. He has adequate hematologic and hepatic function, with neutrophil count of 2.5×10^9/L, hemoglobin of 120g/L, platelets of 150×10^9/L, AST and ALT levels within normal limits, and bilirubin level within 1.5 times the upper normal limit. He is able to understand and voluntarily sign the informed consent and is willing to be followed up adequately. He has no history of bleeding tendency or coagulation disorders, and his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication (systolic pressure of 130 mmHg and diastolic pressure of 80 mmHg). He does not have any severe uncured wounds, ulcers, or fractures. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The researcher believes that the patient is suitable to participate in the study.

7 year old boy named Max who attends preschool in Nice, France. Max has no known medical conditions or allergies and has not been previously diagnosed with COVID-19. His parents have given informed consent for him to participate in the study. Max is covered by French insurance. He is excited to return to school and participate in the study to help contribute to the understanding of the spread of COVID-19 among children.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was diagnosed with HIV infection 3 years ago. He is currently being treated with antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is undetectable. He has a history of intravenous drug use in the past but has been clean for the past year. He does not consume alcohol regularly and denies any history of blood transfusions or organ transplants. He has no significant medical history of liver disease or viral hepatitis. He is currently employed as a sales representative and lives with his partner who is also HIV positive. He has been receiving regular follow-up care at the "Centre Hospitalier de la Côte Basque" and is willing to participate in the study.

58 year-old male patient diagnosed with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. He is about to start his 2nd line chemotherapy via a central venous catheter. He reports significant weight loss over the past few months and has an energy gap of more than 40% between his target energy intake and actual energy intake at screening. He has a functional digestive tract and is able to take oral intake. He has signed informed consent, and his ECOG score is 2. His BMI is 24.5 kg/m2. He has no known hypersensitivity to fish, egg, soya or peanut protein. He has no significant liver or renal dysfunction. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study. He has not participated in any clinical trial with an investigational drug or device in the past month.

50-year-old male with end-stage renal failure (ESRF) requiring thrice weekly hemodialysis for the past year. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral vascular disease. Currently, the patient's blood pressure is difficult to control during hemodialysis sessions, with a systolic blood pressure consistently above 150mmHg despite the use of antihypertensive medications. The patient reports experiencing thirst and increased interdialytic weight gain between dialysis sessions. He has no history of diabetes mellitus, malignancy, or recent acute myocardial infarction, congestive cardiac failure, stroke, or angina. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and is willing to provide written informed consent. He is not currently participating in any other clinical studies and has no plans to relocate or undergo living donor kidney transplant, change to peritoneal dialysis, or home HD during the study period.

A 45-year-old female with a clinical diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the clinic for follow-up. She was started on metformin monotherapy, but her glycemic control remains poor with an HbA1c of 8.5%. She is compliant with her medication and dietary intervention. She has no history of receiving any antihypertensive medication or second-line antidiabetic drugs. She has no known hemoglobin disorders, chronic kidney disease, or thyroid dysfunction. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of adding renin-angiotensin system inhibitors to standard antidiabetic therapy on glycemic control.

Patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman experiencing symptoms of genitourinary syndrome of menopause, including vaginal dryness, itching, burning, and painful intercourse. She has tried over-the-counter vaginal moisturizers and lubricants without relief. She has no history of vaginal infections or chronic urinary tract infections. She is not currently using any form of vaginal estrogen or apricot kernel oil. She has a history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman living in a remote area of Mongolia noticed a rash on her arm that had been getting progressively worse over the past few weeks. She has never seen a dermatologist before and it would take her several hours to travel to the nearest clinic that offers dermatology services. She has limited financial resources and cannot afford the cost of travel, as well as the cost of consultation and treatment. She heard about the tele-dermatology trial through her local health clinic and was excited to participate. She has a basic smartphone and is comfortable using it for communication. She hopes that the trial will provide a convenient and affordable way to get the care she needs without having to travel long distances.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with early stages of Alzheimer's disease. She lives with her husband and has two adult children who visit her regularly. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She is a retired teacher and enjoys reading, puzzles, and spending time with her grandchildren. She has noticed difficulty in remembering recent events and sometimes forgets where she put things. She is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and does not smoke. She is able to perform activities of daily living with some difficulty and has occasional behavioral problems, such as wandering and agitation. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her memory and increase her independence.

60-year-old male with a history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presented with a 3-month history of shortness of breath and cough. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the right lung, suspicious for lung cancer. The patient underwent a right pneumonectomy for lung cancer. The patient did not have a history of cardiac arrhythmias but was at high risk for postoperative atrial fibrillation. The patient was not on any calcium channel blockers or beta-blockers preoperatively. The patient's renal function was normal with a creatinine clearance of 70 ml/min. The patient did not have a history of Wolf Parkinson White syndrome or myasthenia gravis. The patient's COPD was classified as GOLD III.

65-year-old male patient admitted to Ramathibodi Hospital due to an acute onset of urinary retention. He has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been treated with medication for the past year. He denies any fever, chills, dysuria, hematuria, or lower abdominal pain. He has no history of urinary tract infections, diabetes mellitus, or other chronic medical conditions. He has no known drug allergies and is not taking any medications other than those prescribed for his BPH. Upon physical examination, his bladder is distended and tender, and he has no palpable masses or enlarged lymph nodes. He has no neurological deficits or weakness in his lower extremities. Laboratory tests show a normal complete blood count, renal function, and electrolytes. A urinalysis reveals no significant abnormalities. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial and gives his written informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with epithelial ovarian carcinoma 18 months ago and underwent a primary cytoreductive operation, followed by a platinum-based chemotherapy with a complete remission. She has no history of radiotherapy or endometrial carcinoma. She is currently experiencing abdominal discomfort, bloating, and pelvic pressure. A CT scan reveals a suspected recurrence of ovarian cancer. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has a good performance status (ECOG 0). She has no history of hormonal or chemotherapy for recurrence, and her bone marrow function, renal function, liver function, coagulation parameters, and neurological function are adequate. Her peripheral neuropathy is less than or equal to grade 2 according to CTCAE v4.03 criteria. Her serum creatinine is less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, and her creatinine clearance is greater than or equal to 60 ml/min. She has not had any acute hepatitis or acute infectious disease requiring intravenous antibiotics. She does not have immunodeficiency. She has no evidence of active coronary arterial disease or poorly controlled cardiac arrhythmia. She has no peripheral vascular disease greater than or equal to grade 3 or renal insufficiency with serum creatinine values greater than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal or GFR less than 60 ml/min. She has no history of cerebrovascular disease. She has no known allergies to carboplatin or cisplatin. She has a life expectancy of greater than or equal to 12 weeks.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) based on a biopsy-proven tumor. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of at least three months. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or external beam radiation for the past two and eight weeks respectively. The patient has adequate hematologic reserve with WBC 4000/mm3, absolute neutrophils 2000/mm3, and platelets 120,000/mm3. Pre-enrollment chemistry parameters show bilirubin, AST, ALT and creatinine levels within the normal range. Coagulation parameters (PT and PTT) are also within the normal range. The patient's radiographic procedures (MRI or CT scans) are within two weeks of treatment on this research study. The patient has no significant intercurrent medical or psychiatric conditions that would place them at increased risk or affect their ability to receive or comply with treatment or post-treatment clinical monitoring. The patient does not have radiological evidence of leptomeningeal disease, a history of allergic reaction to CTX, or initiated or completed chemo/RT. The patient is willing to use a medically effective method of contraception during and for a period of three months after the treatment period. The patient understands and gives written informed consent.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis. He has been experiencing symptoms of mild to moderate disease activity, including diarrhea, abdominal pain, and occasional rectal bleeding. The Pediatric UC Activity Index (PUCAI) score revealed a score between 10-55 points. He has no history of Crohn's colitis or IBD type unclassified (IBD-U) according to Montreal classification. He has not been treated with oral 5-ASA oral preparation with at least 50mg/kg/day for more than 3 days within 7 days prior to the screening visit. He has been diagnosed with infectious colitis, which has been ruled out by stool cultures, ova and parasite examination and Clostridium difficile assay. He has no fever greater than 38.5 degrees and is in general good health, based on medical history, physical examination, and screening laboratory results. He weighs more than 15kg and is willing to participate in the study and follow study procedures, as evidenced by a parent/legal guardian signing a written informed consent and the child providing assent. He is not currently being treated with steroids or rectal therapies and does not have any current renal disease or hepatic disease. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use acceptable contraception if sexually active.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male with a BMI of 22. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has no significant medical history and has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 90 days. He has no history of addiction to any recreational drug or drug dependence. The patient is in good general health, with no signs of HIV 1&2, hepatitis B&C, or RPR. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient has a normal 12 lead ECG and chest X-ray (FA view). He has no history of hypersensitivity to rabeprazole substituted benzimidazoles or any component of the formulation. The patient has not consumed prescription drugs or over-the-counter drugs for two weeks prior to the study check-in. He has not consumed grapefruit juice or xanthin-containing food and beverages for 48 hours prior to study check-in. The patient has negative results for drugs of abuse and alcohol breath analysis during the study check-in of each period. He has no history of seizures or abnormal diet. Overall, the patient meets the eligibility criteria for the Bioequivalence Study of Torrent Pharmaceutical Ltd.'s Rabeprazole Sodium Delayed Release Tablets Under Fasted Conditions.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain in her left heel for the past 6 months. The pain is localized to the heel and is worse in the morning, making it difficult for her to take the first few steps out of bed. The patient reports that the pain decreases after a few minutes of walking and reappears after long periods of standing or sitting. She has tried various treatments, including physical therapy, steroid injections, and orthotics, but none of them have provided significant relief. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of fractures, tumors, or previous operations in the lower extremities. She has no sensory disorders or balance problems and does not experience dizziness. She is able to walk on a moving track and is interested in participating in a study to test the effect of barefoot walking on chronic heel pain.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it involves a population-based study rather than individual patient recruitment. The study is looking to enroll all school children and adults within the selected communities who consent to participate, and those who do not have any chronic disease not related to schistosomiasis.

A 62-year-old man has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and scheduled to undergo elective trans-urethral resection of the prostate (TURP) under spinal anesthesia. The patient has no significant medical history, and his BMI is 25. His preoperative lab work and physical exam were within normal limits, and his initial body temperature was measured at 37.0 ˚C. The patient has not received any blood transfusion during surgery, and he does not have Parkinson's disease or any psychological disorder.

The patient is a 55 year old male who recently suffered from a myocardial infarction and underwent a cardiac stenting procedure. He is married with two teenage children and works as an accountant. He has a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and is a former smoker (quit 5 years ago). He is currently taking medication for his blood pressure and cholesterol. He is concerned about his health and wants to make positive lifestyle changes to avoid future cardiovascular events. He is willing to participate in the trial and complete the required surveys. He does not have any history of illicit drug use, psychiatric conditions, or dementia. He is able to follow-up and is willing to participate in cardiac rehabilitation. He is physically able to exercise and has no contraindications to exercise training.

28 year old Japanese woman diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 3 years ago. She has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, joint pain and swelling, and skin rash. She was started on oral prednisone and hydroxychloroquine which has helped with her symptoms, but she still experiences moderate to severe disease activity. She has not had any severe neuropsychiatric or renal manifestations related to her SLE. She weighs 52 kg and has no history of primary immunodeficiency or hepatitis B or C. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her disease management.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing joint pain and skin problems for several years. She has a family history of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, as her mother and sister have been diagnosed with the condition. She has noticed that her joints are very flexible and often dislocate easily. She also has hyperextensible skin that bruises easily and scars poorly. She experiences frequent headaches and sometimes feels lightheaded or dizzy. She has never been diagnosed with any heart or eye problems. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help identify the underlying genetic cause of her condition and improve understanding of the full range of symptoms associated with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. She is willing to undergo genetic testing and periodic clinical assessments to contribute to this research.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman aged between 50 and 70 years, with one year or more of amenorrhea and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) greater than 30 milli-International unit/mL. She has sexual dysfunction and is seeking treatment for it. She is not regularly practicing sexual activity, but still experiences sexual desire. She has no history of cardiac, renal, or hepatic diseases, diabetes mellitus, cognitive disorders, hormone-dependent tumors, or psychiatric illness. She does not consume more than two doses of alcohol per day and has not consumed Maca supplements or any other nutritional supplement known to cause changes in sexual function. She is not currently taking any medication that could affect sexual function, such as anti-epileptics, cytochrome P450 isoform 3A4 (CYP3A4) inducers, dopamine agonists, and other parkinsonian drugs, metoclopramide, androgens and antiandrogens, anti-oestrogens, fluoxetine, analogues of gonadotropin-releasing hormone, and other hormones and inhibitors, benzodiazepines prescribed for insomnia, sedatives and hypnotics, antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, and narcotics. She is willing to participate in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient B is a 50-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of heartburn and acid reflux for the past few months. She was diagnosed with erosive esophagitis (LA Grade C) confirmed on EGD screening 8 weeks ago and was treated with a standard dose of PPI medication. She underwent a follow-up EGD screening 1 week ago and it was confirmed that she has healed erosive esophagitis (no mucosal break observed according to LA classification). She is now interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DWP14012 in maintaining the healing of her erosive esophagitis. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, primary esophageal motility or pancreatitis, and does not currently take any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or antithrombotic drugs. She has no history of clinically significant disease and is willing to stop her existing erosive esophagitis treatment for the duration of the study. The patient is excited to participate in the study to help further research in the treatment of erosive esophagitis.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has a family history of colorectal cancer. Her father had colon cancer at age 60 and her maternal grandmother had rectal cancer at age 65. She has never had any symptoms related to colorectal cancer, such as abdominal pain or bleeding. She is in good overall health and has no history of colorectal cancer or polyps. She does not have any medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is interested in participating in the study to determine the best screening strategy for detecting colorectal cancer in individuals with a familial risk.

A 42-year-old female was diagnosed with fibromyalgia by her doctor about 6 months ago. She has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances for more than 3 months, which have significantly affected her quality of life. Despite previous treatments, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and physical therapy, she still suffers from depressed mood and general symptoms of fibromyalgia. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of S-Adenosylmethionine in treating her symptoms. She is not pregnant and does not have any manic or hypomanic conditions. She is able to provide informed consent and is open to medical supervision during the 8-week study period.

A 45-year-old male heart transplant recipient presents for a routine follow-up appointment. He received his heart transplant 2 years ago due to end-stage heart failure. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports good compliance with his immunosuppressive medications and has had no episodes of rejection since his transplant. He is currently able to work part-time as a consultant and enjoys walking for exercise. His vital signs are stable, and physical examination is unremarkable. The patient expresses interest in participating in the TransplantLines study to contribute to improving long-term patient and graft survival after transplantation. He is willing to complete questionnaires about his quality of life and participate in physical and cognitive tests during his next routine appointment.

35-year-old female with a diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization. She presents with dyspnea on exertion, fatigue, and peripheral edema. She has a past medical history of hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled on levothyroxine. She denies any significant tobacco, alcohol, or drug use. She has no significant family history of pulmonary hypertension. Her current medications include diuretics, oxygen therapy, and bosentan. On physical examination, she has jugular venous distension, a loud P2, and a palpable parasternal lift. Her laboratory workup is significant for elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels. She has no history of significant left heart disease, and her acoustic windows are optimal. She has provided informed consent and is affiliated with the French national health insurance.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past few weeks. He has a history of smoking for 25 years, but quit 5 years ago. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. He takes medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He has never had a chest CT examination before. He is scheduled to undergo a chest CT examination for the evaluation of pulmonary arteries and lung nodules. He is concerned about the radiation exposure associated with the procedure, but understands the importance of the examination for his health.

48-year-old female presents to the hospital with a cough, production of purulent sputum, shortness of breath, and chest pain. She also reports a fever of 101°F for the past two days. Upon examination, pulmonary rales and evidence of pulmonary consolidation are found. The patient has no history of bronchial obstruction or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She has not been hospitalized or resided in a long-term care facility within the past 90 days or 30 days, respectively. There is no history of viral or fungal pneumonia, Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, aspiration pneumonia, or other non-infectious causes of pulmonary infiltrates. The patient has no history of primary or metastatic lung cancer, cystic fibrosis or tuberculosis. The patient does not have HIV or myasthenia gravis. The patient has not received any systemic antibiotics during the prior seven days. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of PORT Risk Class II, III, or IV, and has lobar, multilobar, or patchy parenchymal infiltrate(s) consistent with acute bacterial pneumonia on a pulmonary imaging study.

A 34 year old woman was recently diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia. She has already undergone conventional dose chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cytarabine, but she failed to achieve a complete response. Her performance status is Karnofsky 70%. She has no major concurrent diseases that would make her a poor medical risk. Her bilirubin levels are less than 3mg/dL and her creatinine clearance is greater than 40 mL/min. She has not received any chemotherapy in the past 3 weeks and has recovered from any prior chemotherapy. She has not undergone any radiotherapy to 30% or more of her bone marrow and at least 4 weeks have passed since any prior radiotherapy. She has no history of mental incapacity that would preclude informed consent and is not incarcerated. She is willing to use effective contraception throughout the study.

A 35-year-old woman has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 3 years. She has been experiencing fatigue, fever, and swollen joints for the past few weeks, indicating an active phase of the disease. Blood tests show an increase in white blood cell count, indicating active lymphocyte activation. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or suffering from any other chronic inflammatory diseases or viral/bacterial infections. She is not suffering from CNS lupus or generalized lymphadenopathy. She is willing to undergo PET scanning and has a body habitus allowing for PET scanning. She is able to give written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The study is seeking premature infants between the gestational ages of 23 weeks and 27 weeks + 6 days, who are at risk of developing retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). The study aims to compare the severity of ROP among treated infants with an untreated control population, matched for gestational age at birth while confirming the dose of rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 is safe and efficacious. The infant must not have detectable gross malformations, known or suspected chromosomal abnormalities, genetic disorders, or syndromes. Any maternal diabetes requiring insulin during pregnancy would be excluded. The study will not accept infants who are born small for gestational age, have a persistent blood glucose level <2.5 mmol/L or >10 mmol/L at Study Day 0, or have any other condition or therapy that, in the Investigator's opinion, may pose a risk to the subject or interfere with the subject's ability to be compliant with this protocol or interfere with interpretation of results. Monozygotic twins and infants participating or planning to participate in another investigational study drug are also excluded. The study requires signed informed consent from parents/guardians, and each subject will be followed to PMA 40 weeks ± 4 days.

A 12-year-old male with a history of myopia and a family history of retinal detachment presents to the ophthalmologist with complaints of flashing lights and floaters in his left eye. Examination reveals a retinal detachment with grade 2 PVR. The patient is scheduled for vitrectomy surgery with the addition of methotrexate treatment as a part of this clinical trial. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any immunomodulatory therapies or medications that could interact with methotrexate. The patient's mother has provided informed consent and understands the study requirements. The patient is willing to comply with all study visits and has agreed to practice acceptable methods of contraception throughout the study as he is of child-bearing potential. Past Medical History: - Myopia - No known allergies - No previous surgeries

A 54-year-old man with a history of Alpha-1-Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD) has been experiencing shortness of breath during daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and carrying groceries. He has been a smoker for the last 30 years, but has quit smoking 8 weeks ago. His CT scan reveals bilateral heterogeneous emphysema, and his post-bronchodilator FEV1 is less than or equal to 45% predicted. He is compliant with his medications and is currently taking inhalers as prescribed by his pulmonologist. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial, and is able to attend all required follow-up visits. He has read and understood the informed consent form, and is willing and able to undergo bilateral LVRC treatment if he meets the eligibility criteria. He has not participated in any other pulmonary drug or device studies within the last 30 days, and has received Pneumococcal and Influenza vaccinations consistent with local recommendations and/or policy. He has no other conditions that would interfere with completion of the study or adversely affect outcomes.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who suffered a left hemispheric ischemic stroke a year ago. She was hospitalized for a week and then underwent three months of intensive rehabilitation. She is now able to walk independently for at least 10 meters with the use of a cane. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She is currently taking medications to control these conditions. She lives in the greater Montreal area and has access to a stationary bike at home. She is interested in participating in a study to improve her physical fitness and quality of life post-stroke. She has no severe cognitive deficits and has passed the screening cardiology examination and exercise stress test.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of chronic heart failure and NYHA functional class III. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, dyspnea, and reduced exercise tolerance for the past year. The patient's medical history includes myocardial infarction, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. The patient's current medications include lisinopril, carvedilol, and spironolactone. The patient has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% and a QRS duration of 150 ms. The patient is in sinus rhythm and has been on optimal pharmacological therapy for heart failure. The patient has no history of atrial fibrillation but has a history of occasional premature ventricular complexes. The patient has no history of peripheral vascular disease but has been diagnosed with moderate aortic valve stenosis. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and able to give informed consent.

45-year-old female with newly diagnosed metastatic breast cancer, hormone receptor-positive. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any prior treatment for metastatic disease. The primary breast tumor measures 3.5 cm in diameter on ultrasound. The patient has no history of seizures or claustrophobic reactions and is able to lie comfortably on a bed inside a PET camera for 90 minutes. The patient has no electrical implants or ferromagnetic implants. The patient is not pregnant, and a negative serum pregnancy test is obtained on the day of the PET procedure. The patient has no pre-existing medical conditions that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is concerned about the appearance of her facial skin. She has visible lines, pores, pigmentation, and elastosis that correlate to a score of 2-6 on the Fitzpatrick Classification of Wrinkling and Degree of Elastosis. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a medically acceptable form of birth control. She has not had any facial procedures or surgeries within the past 6 months. She is willing to follow the treatment and follow-up schedule and the post-treatment care. She is not planning to improve her skin appearance in a different procedure during the complete experimental period. She is willing to have photographs of the treated area taken that may be used for marketing and educational presentation and/or publications. She desires to improve her facial skin appearance and is interested in the combined treatment of Refirme ST and Matrix RF.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been struggling with his weight for the past few years. He has a BMI percentile greater than or equal to 95th for his age and sex. He lives with his mother and younger sister in a low-income neighborhood. They are insured by Medicaid and rely on public transportation to get to their primary care clinic. The patient enjoys playing video games and watching TV, but rarely engages in physical activity. His mother is concerned about his weight and has tried to encourage healthier eating habits, but has not seen much success. The patient is comfortable speaking English and is willing to participate in the study. He has no chronic conditions or medications that would interfere with the study intervention.

Pt is a 55yo M with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic knee pain. He reports difficulty with daily activities, including walking and climbing stairs. He has tried physical therapy and medications but has not experienced significant improvement. He is interested in exploring surgical options and has been recommended for primary total knee replacement. He is able to understand the study and willing to sign the informed patient consent form. He meets the inclusion criteria, including having intact collateral ligaments, and is willing and able to comply with postoperative evaluations and rehabilitation. He has no history of TKA or THA on the contralateral or ipsilateral side within the last year with an unsatisfactory outcome, and has no plans for lower limb joint replacement for another joint within one year. He has no severe deformities, varus/valgus deformity >10° (mech. axis), bowed femur > 20 degree, flexion contracture >10°. The patient is capable of understanding the patient scores in the national language. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including having no history of high tibial osteotomy or femoral osteotomy, no neuromuscular or neurosensory deficiency that would limit the ability to assess the performance of the device, and no systemic or metabolic disorder leading to progressive bone deterioration.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who comes in for a routine check-up with his urologist. He has a history of smoking for over 40 years and has been diagnosed with bladder cancer. He underwent a transurethral resection of the bladder tumor and is now experiencing regional or metastatic cancer. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no history of severe cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled congestive heart failure, or cardiac dysrhythmias. He has no active infections requiring parenteral antibiotics. He is not currently pregnant or nursing, and he has no other significant medical conditions. He has not received prior systemic chemotherapy, and he is not currently receiving local radiotherapy for pain control or life-threatening situations. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 52 year old male with a history of primary hypercholesterolemia. He has been taking atorvastatin 10 mg for the past 6 months and has not seen significant improvement in his LDL-C levels, which remain above 100 mg/dL. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease, with his father having suffered a heart attack at the age of 60. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing golf in his free time. He has not previously been instructed on a cholesterol-lowering diet. He has no history of diabetes or other significant medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 22-year-old man who identifies as a gay male. He lives in Bangkok and plans to start taking Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) within the next two weeks. He owns an Android smartphone and is able to speak and read Thai. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to increase adherence to PrEP through a smartphone app. He is not currently participating in any other experimental PrEP adherence intervention and has no plans to move out of Bangkok in the next 6 months. He is in good physical and mental health and is able to provide informed consent.

Looking for healthy adult volunteers with a BMI between 18 and 30 who have not donated whole blood within the past 60 days or component blood within the past 14 days. Participants must not have a history of clinically significant disease or clinically significant allergic disease. They must not have taken any investigational product within the past 90 days and must not be currently participating in any other clinical trial. All participants must sign the informed consent form prior to study participation.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian man experiencing blurred vision and distortion in his left eye. He noticed this problem about 2 months ago and it has been getting progressively worse. He has no pain or redness in his eye. He has a history of hypertension, but this is controlled with medication. He has no history of diabetes or any other ocular problems. He is not taking any medications for his eyes. His best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. He is able and willing to avoid high altitude travel, including airline travel, until gas resolution (approximately 6 to 8 weeks). He is willing to wear a wristband that informs any medical personnel that the patient has a gas bubble in the eye. He is able and willing to provide informed consent. He is willing to avoid supine position until gas resolution (approximately 6 to 8 weeks). He meets the study eye criteria with vitreomacular adhesion on OCT that is no larger than 3000 microns with visible separation of the vitreous on either side as seen on horizontal and vertical scans, confirmed by central reading center. His visual function is decreased and has been attributed to VMT. He has experienced distortion and a reduction in visual acuity. He recognizes difficulty with reading and using a computer. His visual acuity letter score is 60 (approximate Snellen equivalent 20/60). He is willing to wait 6 months before surgical intervention, provided visual acuity remains stable. He has no other ocular condition that might affect visual acuity during the course of the study or require intraocular treatment. He has no history of prior gas injection, ocriplasmin injection, or intraocular injection for any reason, and no history of prior vitrectomy. His intraocular pressure is <30 mmHg, with no more than one topical glaucoma medication, and no documented glaucomatous field loss for the eye to be eligible. He has no history of major ocular surgery within the prior 4 months or major ocular surgery anticipated within the next 6 months following randomization. He has no history of YAG capsulotomy performed within 4 months prior to randomization. He is phakic.

This is a 65-year-old male who presents with bilateral lower extremity pain while walking. He reports that the pain goes away after resting for a few minutes. A physical exam reveals absent pedal pulses bilaterally and decreased sensation in the feet. An ankle-brachial index (ABI) is performed and shows a value of 0.6 in both legs, indicating significant peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Further imaging reveals a femoro-popliteal lesion. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial and is randomized to receive immediate revascularization with peripheral transluminal angioplasty (PTA). The study will assess the effect of the intervention on endothelial function by measuring brachial artery flow-mediated and nitrate-mediated dilation, as well as plasma levels of inflammatory markers and coagulation factors. The patient will undergo follow-up evaluation after four weeks to assess the efficacy of the intervention.

A 35-year-old female with a BMI of 31.5 kg/m2 has been struggling to lose weight for the past year. She has tried various diets and exercises, but none seem to have a lasting effect on her weight. She has a sedentary lifestyle due to her desk job, and she finds it hard to resist high-fat foods. She has no known food allergies or intolerances, and she is not taking any medication or supplements that affect appetite or weight. She is interested in participating in a weight loss program and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with chest pain radiating to his left arm. On further evaluation, he was diagnosed with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (ACS). He was scheduled for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) as per the cardiologist's recommendation. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He is not allergic to any medications and has never participated in any clinical research studies. He has not received any thrombolytic therapy in the past 24 hours and is not currently receiving any oral anticoagulant agents. His platelet count is within normal limits, and he is not pregnant. He is willing to use an effective method of contraception if he is a woman of childbearing potential. He has no known history of internal bleeding or hemorrhagic diathesis. He has not received low molecular weight heparin in the previous 6 hours before PCI.

28 year old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 who is not currently on any medications or hormonal contraceptives. She does not consume alcohol or smoke cigarettes. She has no past medical history of chronic diseases or conditions and has never been pregnant or lactating. She is willing and able to use appropriate methods of contraception for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with a pituitary tumour. He has noticed some changes in his vision and has been experiencing headaches. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any history of asthma or sinus disease. He is a non-smoker and does not use any medications that could affect his sense of smell. He is an accountant and enjoys spending time with his family. He is scheduled to undergo endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery with nasoseptal flap coverage. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve surgical techniques and preserve his olfactory function.

A 72-year-old woman presented with bilateral cataracts and difficulty with her vision. She reported a history of myopia and astigmatism and had previously undergone LASIK surgery on her right eye. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril daily. Her visual acuity was 20/70 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. Upon examination, she was found to have a corneal astigmatism of 2.7 diopters in both eyes. She was deemed a suitable candidate for phacoemulsification cataract surgery and was offered the option to participate in a study comparing two different intraocular lenses: the AcrySof® IQ Toric High Cylinder Power IOL or the AcrySof® IQ Aspheric NATURAL monofocal IOL. She met all the inclusion criteria and did not have any of the exclusion criteria. She opted to participate in the study and chose to be implanted with the AcrySof® IQ Toric High Cylinder Power IOL in her right eye and the AcrySof® IQ Aspheric NATURAL monofocal IOL in her left eye.

A 50-year-old male presents with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation for the past year. He has been symptomatic with palpitations, shortness of breath, and occasional chest discomfort during episodes. He has failed at least 1 antiarrhythmic medication trial. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medications. He is currently not taking any anticoagulation therapy. His echocardiogram shows a normal left ventricular ejection fraction with no left atrial enlargement. He is not on any investigational drug or device study. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent. He has no contraindications to systemic anticoagulation with heparin or coumadin. He does not have a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.

68F diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knees, and has been experiencing pain and difficulty in movement. She has been affiliated with the social security scheme and is currently enrolled in a Spa Therapy program. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written consent. She has no history of inflammatory, tumoral, traumatic or infectious rheumatism, nor does she have any known cardiac decompensation. She can read and speak French fluently and has no disorders of concentration or compression of the written or oral French language. She is between the ages of 50-75 years old.

The patient is a 53 year old male who has been experiencing progressively worsening headaches and occasional seizures for the past 3 months. He visited his PCP and underwent brain MRI which revealed a right frontal lobe mass with contrast enhancement. He was referred to a neurosurgeon for further evaluation and underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of glioblastoma. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril for management. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as an accountant and has not experienced any work-related issues due to his symptoms. He is married with two children and has a supportive family. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80. He is willing to undergo surgery and additional treatment as recommended by his healthcare provider.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's disease who has been on immunosuppressive medication for the past 6 months. He has a history of gastrointestinal bleeding and has been managed by a gastroenterologist at Children's Hospital Boston. He has not received the influenza vaccine during the current season and has no contraindications to the vaccine. The patient is not currently experiencing fever or any other symptoms that would prevent him from receiving the vaccine. The patient is willing to participate in the study and have blood samples drawn at baseline and at Month 1 to evaluate the level of antibody titers and follow markers. He will also be monitored for side effects and adverse events from the vaccination.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. The patient has been experiencing abdominal pain and rectal bleeding for about three months prior to the diagnosis. Imaging studies revealed the presence of synchronous liver metastases. The patient has no prior history of cancer and has been generally healthy. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medication. The patient has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. The initial blood test showed an elevated platelet count of 420,000/μL. The patient is scheduled for surgery to remove the primary tumor and the liver metastases. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the role of preoperative platelet count as a prognostic factor in patients with synchronous colorectal liver metastases.

This is a 35-year-old woman who was displaced from her home due to a natural disaster. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety, including feelings of hopelessness, sadness, and worry. She has also been having difficulty carrying out daily tasks necessary for survival and recovery. She scored YES on the heart-mind screener for heart-mind problems and scored >16 on the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Scale. She does not have a severe mental disorder or an alcohol use disorder. She is interested in participating in a low-intensity psychological intervention that can address her emotional and practical problems. She is open to receiving the intervention in a group setting, delivered by paraprofessionals.

60 year old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C infection and mild liver impairment. He has been treated in the past with interferon and ribavirin therapy, but achieved only a partial response. He is currently not taking any medications for his liver impairment but is taking medication for his hypertension. He reports no recent significant medical history and is generally in good health. The patient has a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research and potentially benefit other patients with liver impairment.

The patient is a healthy male or female between the ages of 18 and 65 years. They have no significant medical history, normal physical examination results, and no clinically significant abnormalities in baseline laboratory values or on the 12-lead electrocardiogram. Female subjects must be post-menopausal, surgically sterilized, or have a negative urine beta human chorionic gonadotropin pregnancy test at initial screening and pre-injection on dosing day. They are willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this study. They are not currently enrolled in another investigational study and have no known hypersensitivity to the investigational drug or any of its components. They are not pregnant or lactating and do not have any other conditions that could interfere with the study.

Patient is a 58-year-old man from the United States who has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to chronic kidney disease. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years. His last recorded intradialytic blood pressure was 150/95 mmHg. He has no other significant medical history and his current medications include lisinopril, amlodipine, and metoprolol. He is able to provide informed consent and is deemed medically stable by his primary physician.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of gastrointestinal issues, including chronic gastritis and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He is scheduled to undergo an endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) procedure for the removal of a benign polyp in his stomach. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status of II and has no history of hepatic or renal insufficiency. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 (Kg/m2) and has no known allergies to the drugs used in the study. The patient has not received any anxiolytics, narcotics, antipsychotics, or opioids in the past.

This is a 58 year old male with a history of stable angina, diagnosed with a de novo coronary artery lesion. The patient has previously undergone coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery and is considered an acceptable candidate for repeat intervention. The patient experiences positive functional studies and reversible changes in electrocardiogram (ECG) consistent with ischemia. The study will compare the safety and efficacy of ExcelTM Sirolimus Eluting Stent with a Biodegradable Polymer versus Sirolimus Eluting Stent with Non-Biodegradable Polymer in the treatment of patients with de novo coronary artery lesions. The patient will be randomized to receive either the ExcelTM DES or the CypherTM DES. The primary endpoint will be ischemia-driven Target Vessel Failure (TVF) which is a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization at 12 months. The secondary endpoints include rates of stent thrombosis, target lesion failure, major adverse cardiac events, device and procedure success rates. The patient must meet the angiographic inclusion criteria and must not have any of the angiographic exclusion criteria. The patient must not be allergic to aspirin, clopidogrel and ticlopidine, heparin and bivalirudin, stainless steel, PLA, contrast media or sirolimus. The patient must not have evidence of an Acute Myocardial Infarction within 72 hours of the index procedure. The patient must not be participating in another device or drug study that has not reached the primary endpoint of the study. The patient must not have a co-morbid condition(s) that could limit the patient's ability to participate in the study or comply with follow-up requirements. The patient must not have undergone previous stenting anywhere within the target vessel(s) within the previous 12 months or require stenting within the target vessel(s) within 12 months after the study procedure. The patient must not have heavily calcified target lesion(s) which cannot be successfully pre-dilated or target lesion(s) involving a side branch >2.5 mm in diameter, or < 2.5 mm in diameter requiring treatment. The patient must not have an unprotected Left Main Coronary Lesion with a diameter of >= 50%.

A 50-year-old male presents with a history of chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) and has been undergoing treatment with imatinib mesylate for the past year. However, he has developed resistance to the drug and now presents with symptoms of advanced CML. He has a history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is now under control with medication. His liver and kidney function tests are normal. The patient is experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, meaning he is ambulatory but restricted in physically strenuous activity. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive dasatinib treatment and help advance medical knowledge in the treatment of CML.

A 30-year-old Hispanic female presents for her 28-week prenatal visit. She has a history of one uncomplicated pregnancy resulting in a healthy 2-year-old child. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medications. She received routine prenatal care, including initial laboratory tests and ultrasound, with no significant findings. She reports having had sex with one partner for the past year and no history of sexually transmitted infections. She is interested in learning more about the HPV vaccine and its potential benefits for her and her family. She speaks English fluently and is comfortable communicating in that language. She has not received any doses of the HPV vaccine before. She is willing to participate in the study, and the research team explains that she will be asked to complete a survey about her willingness to receive the HPV vaccine postpartum at her child's two-month well-child visit. The team will follow up with her after the visit to reevaluate her opinion. She agrees to participate and signs the informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been a light smoker for the past 5 years, smoking an average of 10 cigarettes per day. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is motivated to quit smoking and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him quit. He has no other medical conditions and is mentally and physically stable. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future. He is willing to participate in a study that involves both counseling and the use of FDA approved smoking cessation medications.

The patient is a 25-year-old nulliparous woman who is at 40 weeks of gestation. She has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes and her BMI is 30 kg/m2. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not participated in any interventional medicinal treatment studies. She has no known allergies to standard heparin and/or LMWH heparin. She has not used ASA compounds within the week preceding inclusion. She has no history of coagulation disorders and is not currently using any drugs that interfere with hemostasis.
