She has no diagnosed HIV or acute hepatitis. She has a singleton pregnancy with a normal estimated fetal weight. Her cervix is unripe with a score of 4 points according to Bishop/Westin scale. She is planned for labor induction after 4-7 days of IMP treatment. She understands and has signed an informed consent form and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol. She is able to understand the written and verbal instructions in the local language.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic neuropathic pain for over two years. She has tried various pain medications, but none have provided adequate relief. She has been referred for presurgical assessment due to her pharmacoresistance. She has no history of drug addiction or epilepsy. She has no implanted stimulation devices, and her analgesic treatment has been stable for over a month. She has access to the internet and is capable of using the relocated stimulation system. She uses effective contraception and is not pregnant or nursing. She has given her written consent to participate in the trial.

A 25-year-old healthy male came to the clinic for a routine physical exam. He is a college student, studying engineering, and has no underlying disease. He is single and uses condoms as his primary method of contraception. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is not on any medications or supplements. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 4 days a week. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. His past surgical history is unremarkable. He is interested in participating in clinical trials to help advance medical research.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl who is generally healthy and up to date on her routine vaccinations. She lives with her parents and 2 siblings in a suburban area. She attends preschool and has not had any recent illnesses or hospitalizations. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not have any allergies or chronic medical conditions. She is not taking any medications and has not received any investigational drugs or vaccines in the past 30 days. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her to participate in this clinical trial. She will receive one dose of a MenACWY conjugate vaccine, and her blood will be collected before and one month after the vaccine dose. She does not have a history of meningococcal disease or exposure to meningococcal serogroup A, C, W-135, or Y disease within the past year. She has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products in the past 3 months, and she does not have any confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition.

A 42-year-old man presents to his GP with complaints of a bulge in the groin area that occasionally causes discomfort. On examination, the GP diagnoses him with an inguinal hernia that requires surgical treatment. The patient is otherwise healthy, a non-smoker, and has no significant medical history. The GP explains the two referral options available, traditional pathway or direct electronic referral and booking for outpatient surgery. The patient agrees to participate in the trial and is randomly assigned to the electronic referral and booking group.

John is a 55-year-old male who was admitted to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. He was diagnosed with a small bowel obstruction and requires placement of a nasogastric tube as part of his treatment plan. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. He denies any known allergies. He is alert and oriented, and able to provide informed consent. He will be staying in the ICU for the next several days as part of his treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 infection five years ago. He has previously undergone pegylated interferon-based therapy for his condition but did not respond well to treatment. He currently experiences symptoms of fatigue, abdominal pain, and nausea. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. He is currently not taking any medications for his hepatitis C. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and viral load. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of celgosivir plus peginterferon alfa-2b, with or without ribavirin, for 12 weeks.

56-year-old female diagnosed with multiple myeloma is scheduled to undergo an autologous peripheral blood hematopoietic stem cell transplantation after receiving conditioning chemotherapy. The patient reports experiencing significant symptoms related to the disease and its treatment, including fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and pain. She is interested in alternative therapies to help manage these symptoms and has had some experience with acupuncture in the past. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the trial and has not had acupuncture treatment within the past 4 weeks. She is willing to participate in the study and is open to receiving either true acupuncture or sham acupuncture as part of her treatment regimen.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who suffered a traumatic brain injury from a motor vehicle accident two days ago. He was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 9. He has no significant past medical history and does not use any medications. He is married with two young children and works as a construction worker. His family is very concerned about his condition and would like to explore any potential treatments that could help him recover. He has no history of allergies and has never participated in any clinical trials before. He is able to provide informed consent for the study. His CT scan showed a moderate diffuse axonal injury and no skull fractures or cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea. He has no other significant medical problems and is otherwise healthy.

60 year old male with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, previously treated with surgery and radiation therapy, presenting with recurrent disease amenable to surgical resection. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. The patient does not have any other active malignancies or uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the trial and able to comprehend and sign a written informed consent document. The patient's medical history reveals no anginal chest pain and the patient is not taking nitrates or PDE5 inhibitors. The patient does not have any secondary conditions that cause priapism. The patient has not had a severe hypersensitivity reaction to any monoclonal antibody and has no allergies to the study drug components. The patient does not have any active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment or a documented history of clinically severe autoimmune disease, nor does the patient have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or current immunosuppressive therapy. The patient is not receiving any other investigational agents and has not received a live vaccine within 30 days of the planned start of study therapy.

A 32-year-old sexually active male with no history of injecting drug use, gonorrhea or syphilis in the last six months, or high-risk partner is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an HIV vaccine. He has not engaged in unprotected anal or vaginal intercourse in the last six months outside of a relationship with a regular partner known/presumed to be HIV negative. He is willing to undergo HIV and genital infection screening, and is available for follow-up for the duration of the study. He is using an effective method of contraception with his partner and is willing to undergo urine pregnancy tests prior to each vaccination. He has no clinically relevant abnormalities on history or examination and is not currently taking any medication or experiencing any chronic diseases. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is interested in contributing to scientific inquiry and is willing to comply with the protocol.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with diffuse large B cell lymphoma visited the clinic for a routine check-up. He has completed two lines of standard therapy including an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody but did not respond to treatment. He has no other underlying diseases and is not taking any medications. He occasionally drinks alcohol and has never smoked. He works as a teacher and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. His past medical history is significant for hypertension which is well controlled with medications. He has no history of central nervous system malignancies or symptomatic CNS metastases. He has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational drugs in the past 30 days.

A 35-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a deep burn injury on his right forearm. After initial stabilization, the patient underwent a split-thickness skin graft procedure for wound closure, resulting in a 25 cm2 donor site wound on his left thigh. The wound was created 2 days ago, and the patient is experiencing pain and discomfort in the affected area. He has no history of bleeding disorders, capillary fragility, venous or arterial disorders, or any other significant medical conditions. He has never been diagnosed with any autoimmune, hematologic, or malignancy diseases. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is not currently taking any medications, and he has not received any investigational drug, device, or biological/bioactive treatment within the last 30 days. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 25-year-old Finnish male who presents with a history of delayed puberty and infertility. He reports having anosmia (inability to smell) since childhood, as well as a small phallus and a history of cryptorchidism. He denies any hearing loss or bone deformities. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is motivated to participate in research to help improve understanding and treatment of Kallmann syndrome. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

A 32-year-old woman has been experiencing pelvic pain and infertility for the past year. She was diagnosed with a 5 cm endometrioma on her left ovary through an ultrasound. She has never undergone any surgical procedures on her ovaries before and has no history of thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, diabetes mellitus, or adrenal disorders. She has not received hormonal treatment within the past 3 months and is willing to participate in the study.

Pt is a 63yo F who has been experiencing unusual headaches and jaw pain for the past month. She reports feeling fatigued and has noticed some tenderness in her scalp. She has no significant past medical history and denies any fever, chills, or recent infections. On physical examination, her scalp is tender to palpation and she has temporal artery tenderness. Laboratory studies reveal an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 70 mm/hr and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 50 mg/L. A temporal artery biopsy is performed and shows evidence of giant cells arteritis. The patient has not been on any corticosteroid therapy for this condition. She is approached about participating in a clinical trial to study new biomarkers for diagnosis and management of giant cells arteritis.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has a history of alcohol abuse and presents with a recent onset of abdominal pain that has been progressively worsening over the past few weeks. He reports some weight loss and occasional nausea. The primary care physician has referred the patient to the Florida Hospital Endoscopy Unit for further evaluation of the pancreas. The patient has no prior history of pancreatic disease or surgery, and no other significant medical history. Upon physical examination, the patient has abdominal tenderness in the epigastric region with no palpable masses. Blood work shows elevated amylase and lipase levels. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy with a history of right knee pain and instability while playing basketball. He has been diagnosed by an orthopedic surgeon with a meniscal tear and scheduled for arthroscopic knee surgery. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. He has a normal BMI and his American Society of Anesthesiologist (ASA) functional status is II. He has no history of chronic opioid therapy, central or peripheral neuropathy, and is not allergic to clonidine or ropivacaine. The patient has not undergone anterior cruciate ligament reconstructive surgery. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

32 yo M involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in severe traumatic brain injury(TBI) and subsequent vegetative state(VS). The patient has been in the VS for 6 months with no signs of improvement despite various therapies. The family has agreed to enroll the patient in the clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of spinal cord stimulation(SCS) therapy. The patient is stable with normal body temperature, stable vital signs, and spontaneous breathing without an extra oxygen supply. The patient does not have a tracheotomy using metal trachea cannula and is feasible for magnetic resonance inspectors. The family has provided written informed consent for the patient's participation in the study. Past medical history is unremarkable.

45 year-old male scheduled for elective arthroscopic shoulder surgery. He has no significant past medical history and is classified as an ASA physical status classification 2. He does not have any allergies or contraindications to the medications used in the study. He has not been taking opioids prior to the surgery. The patient is able to understand and speak Dutch and is able to understand the PCIA system and NRS pain score system. He has agreed to participate in the study.

32-year-old female diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 12. She has been insulin-dependent for the past 20 years and has a history of multiple hospital admissions due to diabetic ketoacidosis. She has a BMI of 25 and has no previous history of organ transplantation or malignancy. She has been receiving adequate medical treatment for her diabetes under the guidance of an experienced diabetologist. She was recently diagnosed with renal failure and is eligible for renal transplantation according to local criteria. She has no history of hypercoagulability disorder, coagulopathy, or abnormal liver function tests. She has stable cardiovascular status and no active infections. Her serology tests for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C are negative.

The patient is a 34-year-old pregnant woman who has had a previous cesarean section and is scheduled to have a repeat cesarean section. She has no known allergies to local anesthetics, morphine, or epinephrine. Neuraxial anesthesia is planned to be the primary anesthetic for her surgery. The patient is in good overall health and has provided informed consent to participate in the study investigating whether the addition of epinephrine to the standard single intrathecal injection of hyperbaric bupivacaine for repeat cesarean will prolong its duration. The patient will be monitored for the onset, quality and duration of both sensory and motor components of the spinal block, as well as the incidence of known side effects.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States with a history of Type II Diabetes Mellitus and Peripheral Artery Disease. He underwent a transfemoral lower limb amputation due to complications from these conditions 6 months ago. He is motivated to walk with a prosthesis and his goal is to be able to perform household activities with ease. He lives with his wife and has a sedentary lifestyle due to his amputation. He is currently not receiving active treatment for cancer and has not had a stroke in the past 2 years. His MMSE score is above 24 and he is mentally capable of providing informed consent.

As this clinical trial involves healthy adult male volunteers, a specific patient description is not applicable. However, eligible participants must be between 18-45 years of age, weigh at least 52kg, and have clinically normal laboratory profiles. They should not have a history or presence of significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic or psychiatric disease, hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reaction to topiramate, nephrolithiasis or gout, or alcoholism or drug abuse within the past year. Additionally, they should not have used any drugs or other substances known to be strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP enzymes within a specific time frame and should not have participated in another clinical trial within 28 days of study start.

A 72-year-old female presents with a history of moderate-severe mitral regurgitation for the past 2 years. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been on guideline-directed medical therapy for her mitral regurgitation and her current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. She has been experiencing shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue, and her symptoms have progressed to NYHA Functional Class III. She underwent a transthoracic echocardiogram which revealed moderate-severe mitral regurgitation with a regurgitant volume of 50 mL and regurgitant fraction of 48%. She was referred to a multidisciplinary Heart Team and was deemed high-risk for open-heart surgery due to her age, comorbidities, and frailty. She was offered participation in a clinical trial to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and performance of the HighLife 28mm Transcatheter Mitral Valve. She is willing to participate in the study and provides signed informed consent.

45-year-old male patient with a BMI of 27 is scheduled for a thyroidectomy under general anesthesia. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for the past 3 years. The patient reports no family history of thyroid or esophageal disorders. The patient has no known allergies and has not undergone any previous surgeries. The patient's neck extension is normal, and there are no facial or upper airway anomalies. The patient has no history of esophageal surgery or abnormalities. The patient has been informed of the purpose of the study and has given consent to participate.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty in reading for the past few months. He has a history of age-related cataract which has been confirmed by a comprehensive eye examination. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/50 in the left eye. He has no history of ocular trauma or ocular surgery. He has mild hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. Pre-operative corneal astigmatism from IOL Master is less than 1 diopters. He is interested in presbyopia correction at the same time as cataract surgery. He has no other eye diseases that can affect capsule stability such as pseudoexfoliation syndrome or glaucoma. He is able to read and understand the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. The patient has undergone a lumpectomy and is planning to receive adjuvant chemotherapy with pegfilgrastim prophylaxis for four cycles. The patient is able to read and understand English and has provided informed consent. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has reported experiencing bone pain during previous chemotherapy cycles and is interested in participating in a study investigating the effect of patient education on reported bone pain in breast cancer patients receiving chemotherapy and pegfilgrastim. The patient is not currently experiencing any other painful conditions or taking any chronic pain medications.

A 55 yo F with a history of hypertension diagnosed 5 years ago. She has been on antihypertensive medications for the past 3 years, currently on a single medication. Her blood pressure readings have been consistently above 140/90 mmHg despite medication, and her last reading was 150/95 mmHg. She has a family history of hypertension and heart disease. She has no history of decompensated heart failure, severe renal failure, liver disease, or taking non-insulin antidiabetic medication. She is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent. She is committed to following the low-sodium diet as part of the educational program and urine sodium monitoring in order to optimize her hypertension treatment.

A 25 year old, otherwise healthy male smoker, who has been smoking an average of 10 or more cigarettes per day for at least 1 year prior to the screening visit, and has urinary cotinine levels indicative of smoking at screening. The patient must have a body weight greater than 50 kg and BMI within the range of 19 - 29.9 kg/m2. The patient should not have any current or past diagnosis of psychiatric disorder, cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, autonomic dysfunction, respiratory disease, liver disease, or gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient must be capable of giving written informed consent and must agree to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form. The patient must not have a positive pre-study drug/alcohol screen, and must not have consumed red wine, seville oranges, grapefruit or grapefruit juice (and exotic citrus fruits, grapefruit hybrids or fruit juices) from 7 days prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient must be willing to use one of the contraception methods listed in Section 8.1.1. This criterion must be followed from the time of the first dose of study medication until 3 months post-last dose.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with Hepatitis B diagnosed 5 years ago. She presents to the clinic with abdominal pain, fatigue, and jaundice. She has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. She is diagnosed with Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with a maximal diameter of 4 cm. Her Child-Pugh score is B9. She is listed for orthotopic liver transplantation at the participating institution. She has an Eastern Clinical Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her lab study shows the following results: AFP: 300 ng/mL; Bilirubin: 2.5 mg/dL; Albumin: 3.5 g/dL; Alkaline phosphatase: 150 IU/L; AST: 45 IU/L; ALT: 55 IU/L; GGT: 250 IU/L. She has no other invasive malignancy or coagulopathy. She has no contraindication to both contrast-enhanced MRI and CT. She agrees to use adequate methods of contraception.

The patient is a 32 year old male who has been diagnosed with bipolar I disorder after experiencing a manic episode characterized by elevated mood, grandiosity, and decreased need for sleep. He has a history of multiple manic episodes and has been previously treated with a mood stabilizer and an antipsychotic. His current symptoms include irritability, impulsivity, and decreased concentration. He is currently stable but has a history of non-compliance with medication due to side effects. He works as a graphic designer and is married with two children. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has no known allergies to aripiprazole or lamotrigine.

The patient is a 4 year old boy who has been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. He has completed the induction and consolidation phases of the BFM treatment strategy and is currently in the reinduction phase. He has achieved complete remission and is eligible for the continuation-therapy phase of the treatment. His white blood cell count at diagnosis was 18,000. He has not shown any prednisone poor response and does not have the t(9,22) or t(4,11) clonal translocations. He will be randomly assigned to either the treatment or control group to receive either conventional mercaptopurine and methotrexate chemotherapy only or pulses of vincristine and dexamethasone every 10 weeks for six cycles in addition to the continuation-therapy phase.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who works as a teacher. She has no history of any chronic medical conditions or cognitive problems. She is proficient in reading and writing in Turkish. She has never been diagnosed with any sensory processing disorders. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help with the cultural adaptation and validation of the Adult Sensory Processing Scale (ASPS) Turkish version. She is willing to provide informed consent and complete the ASPS questionnaire as part of the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who is a recreational athlete and plays basketball twice a week with his friends. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He is right-handed and right-footed. He has no history of neurological or orthopedic pathologies affecting his limbs. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve his athletic performance. He is physically active and exercises for 3-5 hours a week. He has no known allergies and has never undergone the TSST (Trier Social Stress Test). He is willing to undergo the isokinetic evaluation of his lower limbs and receive either anodal tDCS or sham tDCS.

A 32-year-old English-speaking female patient with HIV/AIDS is receiving care at Thomas Street Health Center. She has an income level that qualifies her as low-income. She has a high school education and is currently not employed. She does not have any other medical conditions besides HIV/AIDS. She has never received a pap smear screening and is interested in participating in a study to better understand the factors that might be preventing her and others like her from receiving these screenings. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) after experiencing recurrent kidney stones. She has been on a low-oxalate diet and taking potassium citrate to manage her symptoms, but continues to have elevated urine oxalate levels. She is not currently taking Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) or any other medication. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and her alcohol intake is minimal. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. She is willing to comply with study requirements and provide written informed consent. She is willing to use contraception if of child bearing potential.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with pre-diabetes. He has been experiencing occasional episodes of fatigue and mild headaches. He has no history of ischemic heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial occlusive disease. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he is not currently taking any medication. He has a BMI of 28, and his blood pressure and cholesterol levels are within the normal range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of metformin on endothelial function in pre-diabetic patients. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and after reading the "Information for the patient," he provides his written consent. He will be randomized to either group A, which will continue the treatment of 3 x 500 mg/day of metformin, or group B, which will receive an increased dose of 3 x 1000 mg/day of metformin. The study will involve regular follow-up visits and blood tests to monitor the patient's response to treatment. The patient is committed to complying with the study protocol and is excited to contribute to advancing medical knowledge in the field of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a medical history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection for the past 7 years. He was diagnosed with stage 5 chronic kidney disease (CKD) with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 25 ml/min and has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months. He has been previously treated with interferon and ribavirin with no response. He is now a candidate for treatment with Elbasvir (EBR) 50 mg/Grazoprevir (GZR) 100 mg for 16 weeks under the French Temporary Authorization for Use (ATU) program. The aim of the treatment is to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR) at 12 weeks after the end of treatment and to assess the safety of the therapy in HCV-infected patients with CKD. The patient is willing to participate in the retrospective efficacy and safety study and will undergo regular follow-ups and laboratory tests for the next 24 weeks.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing menstrual migraines for the past three years. She has a regular menstrual cycle lasting 28 days and her migraines occur between Day -2 and Day 5 of her cycle. Her migraines are severe, causing nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried various medications, including over-the-counter pain relievers and prescription triptans, but has not found significant relief. She is currently using double barrier contraception and is not planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not used steroid hormonal treatment or antiepileptic drugs or benzodiazepines in the past three months. She is willing to self-administer subcutaneous injections during the luteal phase of three consecutive menstrual cycles and is committed to recording her symptoms daily in an electronic migraine diary. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore a potential new treatment option for her menstrual migraines.

An 8-year-old boy was playing soccer with his friends when he fell and landed on his outstretched hand. He immediately felt pain in his wrist and was unable to move it. His parents brought him to the emergency department where an x-ray was taken and showed no visible fracture. However, he continued to experience pain and swelling in his wrist. He was referred to the pediatric distal radius US study to evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of using a diagnostic musculoskeletal ultrasound in pediatric distal radius fractures. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. He is generally healthy and active, playing soccer and basketball regularly. He has no previous history of fractures or injuries. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU after a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple traumatic injuries, including rib fractures, lung contusions, and head trauma. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. The patient is expected to require mechanical ventilation for at least the next two days. The patient has a history of smoking and is currently using nicotine replacement therapy. He has no known allergies or other medical conditions. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with cervical cancer stage II and is scheduled to receive radiation therapy and concurrent chemotherapy. She has no history of other cancer or major medical illness. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is able to provide written informed consent. She has no known allergy to contrast agents used in imaging procedures. She is willing to undergo a non-invasive imaging modality, including transvaginal photoacoustic and ultrasound imaging, to monitor her cancer treatment response.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, who has undergone neoadjuvant chemotherapy with anthracyclines in the past 6 months. She is scheduled for mastectomy or lumpectomy and will require general anesthesia for the procedure. She has effective contraceptive measures in place and her NT-proBNP levels are less than 125 pg/ml. She has been classified as ASA 1 or 2 and is affiliated with a social security system. She has been fully briefed about the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. She has no renal impairment with a creatinine clearance of more than 60 ml/min. She has no psychological, social, family, or geographical issues that would prevent her from receiving treatment or being monitored regularly. She has no history of cardiopathy, and is not pregnant.

A 30-year-old healthy woman who resides in a tropical region that is endemic for dengue fever is interested in participating in the clinical trial for a new dengue virus vaccine. She has no history of neurologic, heart, lung, liver, rheumatologic, autoimmune, or kidney disease. She has not used any illegal drugs or alcohol within the last 12 months and does not have any behavioral, cognitive, or psychiatric issues that would interfere with the study. Her laboratory test results are within normal limits. She is not currently taking any corticosteroids or immunosuppressive medications and has not received any live or killed vaccines within the last 4 weeks. She has never received blood products or a dengue virus or other flavivirus infection before. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use acceptable forms of contraception during the study. She is available for the duration of the study, which is 23 weeks for Cohort 1, and 32 weeks for Cohort 2. She is excited to contribute to the development of a vaccine that could potentially prevent dengue fever in her community.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) from a matched unrelated donor. Unfortunately, he developed steroid-resistant acute graft versus host disease (GvHD) after the transplant. He has been receiving standard of care treatment for GvHD, including steroids and other immunosuppressive drugs, but has not responded well. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently using any illicit drugs or alcohol. He is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including study visits and long-term follow-up. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. Blood pressure: 120/80, Hgb: 12.5 g/dl, WBC: 6000 /mm3, Plt: 200000/ ml, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dl, BUN: 15 mg/dl, Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

A 14-month-old girl is brought in by her parents for a routine check-up. She is up to date with her vaccinations and has no significant medical history. She was born full term and there were no complications during her delivery. She is meeting all of her developmental milestones and has no complaints. Her weight is in the 50th percentile and her height is in the 75th percentile. She is alert and active during the exam. Her physical exam is unremarkable. Her parents are interested in her participating in a clinical trial for a meningococcal vaccine. They have no concerns about the study and are willing to comply with all the requirements.

45-year-old male with a history of heartburn, regurgitation, and hoarseness for the past 6 months. The patient reports a Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) score of 10 and a Reflux Finding Score (RFS) of 15. The patient has not taken any proton pump inhibitors or steroids within the past 3 months and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of prokinetics as an additional medication to proton pump inhibitor for the management of laryngopharyngeal reflux disease.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been living with HIV for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing pain in his feet for the past year, which has been getting progressively worse. The pain is described as a burning sensation and is present throughout the day, often interfering with his daily activities. He has tried multiple non-narcotic analgesics and adjunctive pain medications, but they have not provided adequate relief. He has never used marijuana before and has no history of psychosis or dependence on cannabis. He is currently on stable doses of opioid and non-opioid analgesic medications. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if medicinal cannabis can provide relief from his painful HIV-associated distal, sensory-predominant polyneuropathy (DSPN).

A 42-year-old married man was admitted to the hospital after a car accident that resulted in severe traumatic brain injury (TBI). His wife, a 40-year-old woman, has been his primary caregiver since his discharge from the hospital. She has been experiencing significant emotional distress and physical and psychological morbidity due to her new role as a caregiver. She has also been feeling socially isolated. They have been married for 10 years and have two children. The patient is currently at a Ranchos Los Amigos Scale class of 4, meaning he is confused and agitated. The patient and his wife are fluent in English and have access to a personal computer with internet access in their home. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to support TBI caregivers and improve the quality of life and health status of both the caregiver and the TBI patient.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently 36 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has noticed that her baby's movements have decreased in the past few days and she is feeling worried about it. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker and has no history of any chronic medical conditions. She is a teacher and is married for 3 years. She has had regular prenatal care and all her ultrasounds have been normal so far, except for her most recent ultrasound, which showed that her baby's estimated fetal weight is below the 10th percentile. She has been offered to participate in a clinical trial that will examine the use of angiogenic factors for fetal growth restriction at term. She is considering participating in the study to help her baby and other women like her.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. She has been on medication for hypertension, and her latest BP readings have been consistently higher than 130/85 mmHg. She has no history of coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, or stroke. Her BMI is 28, and she does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, and she takes levothyroxine daily. She has no known gastrointestinal disease or bleeding disorder. Her renal function is within normal limits with a serum creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL, and her triglycerides are 180 mg/dL. She has no history of cancer, and she is not pregnant. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and participate in the 12-week study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with stomach cancer six months ago. He has already undergone surgery to remove the tumor, but the cancer has metastasized to other parts of his body. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment with cisplatin and fluorouracil. The patient has never received targeted therapy before. He has a history of smoking and moderate alcohol consumption. He reports experiencing nausea, vomiting, and decreased appetite due to chemotherapy. He has no history of other significant medical conditions. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to help identify potential biomarkers for predicting response or resistance to targeted therapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of AIDS diagnosis. He has recently been diagnosed with Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP) and has lost more than 10% of his body weight. He complains of shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. He is currently taking all the standard medications for PCP treatment. The patient is well-nourished, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He has no significant medical history or allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of Liposyn II 20 percent and Liposyn III 2 percent in treating his condition. He understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with all the visits and procedures. The patient has not used any immunomodulators or antiviral medication in the last three months.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has had bleeding gums during brushing and flossing for the past few months. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. She is a non-smoker and has almost 5 teeth per quadrant. Her oral hygiene is adequate, but she is interested in improving her oral health. She will be undergoing a session of Full Mouth-Erythritol Powder Air Polishing Therapy (FM-EPAPT) and will be randomly assigned to use either a manual toothbrush or Philips Sonicare Flexcare Platinum Toothbrush® for the next year. She is willing to attend all recall appointments and follow the agreed protocol for the study.

A 7-year-old boy with esotropia was referred to the ophthalmology department for strabismus surgery. He has a history of allergic rhinitis and takes antihistamines occasionally. He is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he is not taking any medication regularly. The patient's parents have given their consent for the surgery and the clinical trial. The patient is eligible for the trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 35 year old man with HIV infection presents with chronic diarrhea, defined as three loose or watery bowel movements a day for 5 days per week over 3 weeks. His CD4 count is less than 150 cells/µl, and he has a stable antiretroviral regimen that includes at least two nucleotide analogues for at least 4 weeks. His viral load is less than 10,000 copies/ml. Stool testing is positive for Cryptosporidium and negative for other enteric pathogens. He has a Karnofsky score of 80 and is willing to use acceptable methods of contraception. He has no history of hypersensitivity or significant intolerance to aminoglycosides, macrolide antibiotics, or colony-stimulating factors. He does not currently require intravenous fluids and has no active opportunistic infections.

50-year-old female diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) presented with symptoms of shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue. She has been on a stable dose of Ventavis (5 μg per dose) using the I-neb AAD System equipped with Power Disc-6 for the past 4 weeks. She has been diagnosed with IPAH for the past 2 years and has been treated with Ventavis since the diagnosis. She does not have a history of atrial septostomy. She has no other significant past medical history and is not taking any other medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of left-sided heart disease, obstructive lung disease, chronic renal or liver disease, uncontrolled systemic hypertension or hypotension, or cerebrovascular events in the past 6 months. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing symptoms such as tremors, stiffness, and slow movement for the past 5 years. He is taking medication for his Parkinson's disease, but it does not completely control his symptoms. He has no history of other neurological disorders, and he is not currently taking any medications that may interfere with the study. He has no history of dementia and no severe or unstable medical conditions. He is able to undergo MRI imaging and is not pregnant.

82-year-old male NH resident with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and dementia. The patient has been using a VE-surface mattress and has not been diagnosed with any pressure ulcers. The patient has been clinically assessed as moderate risk for new pressure ulcer development. The patient is able to move with some assistance but spends most of the day in a sitting or lying position. The patient will be included in the study and will be repositioned according to the NH-wide protocol for moderate risk residents. The patient does not have any "do not turn" orders or allergies to adhesive.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with high-risk stage I multiple myeloma is being considered for a donor peripheral blood stem cell transplant. He has been previously treated with thalidomide and lenalidomide but experienced relapse. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy greater than grade II and has no major medical or psychiatric disorders that would compromise his tolerance of the treatment regimen. He has no evidence of HIV infection, active hepatitis B or C infections, or liver cirrhosis. He has completed full courses of antifungal therapy and has no radiographic changes indicating pulmonary disease. He has a matched unrelated donor for stem cell transplant. The patient is able to lie supine for approximately 60 minutes, the anticipated duration of each treatment session, and has an ECOG performance status score of 1. His cardiac ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 50%, and his FEV1 and DLCO are both greater than or equal to 50%. His creatinine clearance or GFR is greater than or equal to 60 ml/min, and his serum bilirubin, SGOT, and SGPT levels are all within normal ranges. He has not received previous radiation or has received a maximum of 2000 cGy to non-thoracic spine and rib bone lesions or less than 20% of bone marrow. He is eligible for the TMI conditioning regimen.

Patient is an 80-year-old male residing in an assisted living facility. The patient has been edentulous for several years and currently wears complete dentures. The patient has been experiencing discomfort and difficulty with the lower denture, which has negatively impacted the patient's ability to chew and speak comfortably. The patient is dependent on assistance for activities of daily living and has no history of severe clinical depression, dementia, poorly controlled diabetes, immunosuppression, or treatment with bisphosphonates. The patient is willing to undergo a surgical intervention for implant placement and participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of implant-overdentures in improving denture satisfaction and other outcome measures.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 22.5, interested in participating in a clinical trial studying the effects of protein, calcium, and gut hormone secretion. The patient has no known allergies or adverse reactions to calcium or milk proteins, and has no history of kidney stones. They are not currently diagnosed with any gastrointestinal or metabolic disease, nor do they use any substances that may pose a risk to the experiment or themselves. The patient does not work in a shift-work environment and maintains a regular sleep-wake cycle. They have not experienced any recent changes in body mass. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and comply with study procedures.

The patient is a 4 year old boy from Saudi Arabia who is attending a nursery school. He has a full set of primary dentition with no history of any systemic conditions. He tends to snack on sugary foods and drinks such as candies, biscuits, and fruit juices. His oral hygiene is average and he brushes his teeth once a day with a fluoride toothpaste. He has a family history of dental caries and his mother is concerned about his oral health. He is not taking any antibiotics currently or within the past month. He has never used xylitol chewing gum or any topical fluoride in the past 4 weeks. His salivary mutants streptococci count is ≥ 105 CFU and his dft score is ≥ 3.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer. He is scheduled to receive external beam radiation therapy. He has no history of inflammatory or infectious conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or cirrhosis, nor any infectious diseases such as HIV, tuberculosis, or hepatitis. He does not have any other types of cancer and has not had major psychiatric disorders or alcohol or drug abuse within the past 5 years. He is not currently receiving chemotherapy or on any prescribed anti-inflammatory regimen such as steroids, non-steroidal anti-inflammatories, or tranquilizers. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Irritable Bowel Syndrome - Constipation (IBS-C). She is currently experiencing chronic constipation and abdominal pain. She has a known genetic mutation in SCN5A and has never taken mexiletine before. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to see if mexiletine will restore normal colonic motility. She has no known allergies to medications and is able to stay in Rochester for the duration of the testing period (9 days). She is able to complete the daily diary and has no coexisting neuromuscular disease or other serious medical illness. She is not currently taking any medications known to interact with mexiletine. Her current symptoms are affecting her daily life and she is hoping to find relief through this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old Asian male visited the hospital due to elevated liver enzyme levels. Further testing revealed that he was positive for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and had a high viral load. He was referred to the gastroenterology department for further evaluation and management. The patient has no history of liver disease and is asymptomatic. He has not undergone any treatment for HBV yet. He is classified as ASA I and has no serious systemic diseases. He has agreed to participate in the study to determine the effect of general anesthesia immunosuppressive on HBV replication. He will undergo general anesthesia for a scheduled orthopedic surgery. The patient is fully informed about the study and has voluntarily signed up to participate.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman who recently underwent a cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. She is experiencing severe postdural puncture headache, which is affecting her ability to care for her newborn and perform daily activities. She has tried conservative treatments such as hydration and analgesic agents but has not found relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of sphenopalatine ganglion block in treating her headache. She speaks fluent Turkish and has no known allergies to lidocaine. She does not have a severe nasal septum deviation.

58yo male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and a past myocardial infarction who presents with severe leg pain at rest and non-healing ulcers in his left foot. He has a history of angioplasty and stenting in his left femoral artery with residual stenosis. He has been on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel for the past year. He has been evaluated by a vascular surgeon who has deemed him a poor surgical candidate due to the extent of his disease and anatomy. The patient is on a statin and has been compliant with medication therapy. His ankle brachial index is 0.45, and he has a non-compressible digital artery. He is motivated for non-surgical options and willing to participate in clinical trials.

65-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to her primary care physician with complaints of headaches and occasional dizziness. On examination, her blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg. She reports compliance with her current medication regimen consisting of lisinopril 20 mg and amlodipine 5 mg daily. Repeat blood pressure readings over the course of several visits continue to show poor control of hypertension, with a mean systolic blood pressure of 155 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 92 mmHg. She has no significant past medical history and her Charlson score is less than 4. She has not been treated for hypertension by any other provider and is linked to her current primary care physician who has consented to participate in the study. She is willing to participate in the trial and meets the inclusion criteria of the study.

A 34-year-old HIV-positive woman was diagnosed with acute hepatitis C infection during a routine checkup at a local clinic. She had no history of hepatitis C infection or treatment for the same. She is healthy and has been on antiretroviral therapy for 3 years. Her CD4 count is 450 cells/µl. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She does not smoke and does not drink alcohol. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 4 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. She has not been on any medication other than antiretroviral therapy for her HIV. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the research in the treatment of acute hepatitis C infection in HIV-coinfected individuals.

A 45-year-old male with a family history of heart disease and high cholesterol has recently been diagnosed with dyslipidemia. He has noticed fatigue and shortness of breath during physical activity, and has been experiencing difficulty losing weight despite diet and exercise changes. His fasting blood glucose level is 110 mg/dL, total cholesterol level is 220 mg/dL, and his blood pressure is 140/92 mmHg. He is not currently engaging in regular exercise, but does have a sedentary job as an office worker. He has no history of vascular disease, cancer, diabetes, osteoporosis, neurological, kidney, pulmonary, digestive, or thyroidal disease, and has not experienced any musculoskeletal injuries or neuromuscular disorders. He does not have a pacemaker. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on metabolic syndrome.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a family history of heart disease. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath during exercise for the past few months. His BMI is 28.5 kg/m². He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use drugs. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin to control his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is regular at 72 bpm. His ECG shows sinus rhythm with no significant ST-T changes. He has not undergone any non-invasive or invasive coronary evaluation in the past 90 days. He is willing to undergo cCTA and FFRCT-guided evaluation and has no contraindications for the procedure. He is able to provide written informed consent and willing to comply with study follow-up requirements.

58-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of rectal cancer confirmed by biopsy. He reports a history of constipation and rectal bleeding for the past 2-3 months. He underwent a colonoscopy that showed a 5 cm mass located at 5 cm from the anal verge. A CT scan revealed the mass to be T3 with no evidence of metastasis. The patient has no prior history of pelvic irradiation, and his KRAS status was confirmed to be wild-type. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal bone marrow, hepatic, renal, and cardiac functions. He has no history of drug and/or alcohol abuse, no other active uncontrolled disease, and has not undergone prior exposure to EGFR-targeting therapies. The patient has given his informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a history of chronic atopic dermatitis for the past 3 years. She experiences frequent flare-ups with symptoms including itching, redness, and scaling of the skin. She has tried various topical treatments and antihistamines, but her symptoms have not been well-controlled. She has positive allergen-specific IgE at the screening visit. Her Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score is 16 and Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score is 4 (5-point scale) at the screening and baseline visits. She has more than 10% body surface area (BSA) of AD involvement at the screening and baseline visits. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of heart arrhythmias or alcohol or drug abuse.

32-year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection diagnosed at the age of 24. The patient has a history of treatment with multiple antiretroviral regimens including nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTI), non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTI), protease inhibitors (PI), and integrase inhibitors (INSTI). However, the patient has documented resistance to all four classes of antiretroviral drugs as defined by resistance (at least intermediate) to at least one drug in each class according to the Stanford algorithm. The patient has been regularly followed up by an Italian Infectious Disease Centre and has experienced virological failure despite treatment. The patient has not been diagnosed with any opportunistic AIDS-related infections or chronic conditions (comorbidity) and is compliant with antiretroviral therapy (ART). The patient has agreed to participate in the PRESTIGIO Registry to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of different antiretroviral regimes, evolution of genotype and phenotypic susceptibility of antiretroviral drugs, mortality, incidence of opportunistic AIDS-related infections and chronic conditions, determinants of clinical outcomes, ART compliance, and drug-economy indications related to the clinical management of this complex sub-population.

The patient is a 14-year-old male with a history of recurrent abdominal pain and diarrhoea. He has been referred to the gastroenterology clinic for further evaluation. He is a student in the 9th grade and lives with his parents and younger sister. He has no significant past medical history except for a recent episode of tonsillitis that was treated with antibiotics. His family history is negative for gastrointestinal diseases. He is currently not taking any medications except for occasional over-the-counter analgesics for abdominal pain. He denies any allergies. He is physically active and enjoys playing basketball with his friends. He is excited to participate in this study and believes that it will help him get a better understanding of his condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with Down syndrome. He lives with his parents and has a history of mild intellectual disability. He is able to communicate with his family and caregivers, and is able to comprehend and follow instructions. He has a history of snoring and sleep apnea, and his family reports that he has been experiencing difficulties with his sleep for several months. He is currently not on any medication for his sleep problems. His family has noticed that he has become more forgetful and has been having difficulty with his daily activities. He has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, and his cognition has declined over the past year. He has no history of any psychiatric disorders or other medical conditions that could affect his brain function. He is not currently receiving treatment with CPAP or any new psychoactive drugs. He and his family have agreed to participate in a research study to evaluate the prevalence of sleep disturbances in adults with Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease.

Pt is a 55yo M with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) who recently underwent elective coronary intervention. He is willing to participate in a cardiac rehabilitation program to improve his physical condition. Pt prefers moderate endurance training such as walking, cycling or running. He is eligible for the local rehabilitation program and is contractually capable and mentally able to understand and follow the instructions of the study personnel. He has an Ejection Fraction at discharge from hospital of 50%. Pt is willing to handle the new cardiac rehabilitation device (GEx system) and is able to perform exercise. He does not have severe congestive heart failure (NYHA III/IV) or severe valve disease without replacement. He has no slow healing wounds and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who has been experiencing pain and swelling in his left leg for several months. He has a family history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). He underwent an ultrasound which revealed a large varicose vein in his left leg. He was diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) and was recommended for endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) of the greater saphenous vein (GSV). The patient has no history of bleeding disorders, and he is not taking any blood thinners. He has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to take rivaroxaban for 5 days after the procedure. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical conditions.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with retinal dystrophy. He has noticed a gradual loss of peripheral vision in both eyes over the past year. He has no history of eye surgery or eye trauma. He has been taking vitamin supplements for his eye health. He complains of difficulty navigating in dimly lit areas and bumping into objects. He has no other medical conditions and is currently not taking any medications. The patient is well-nourished and well-dressed. On examination, his visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with correction. Pupil reflex to light is normal. Fundus examination shows retinal degeneration with peripheral visual field loss. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to monitor his visual field defects in a more objective way.

A 40-year-old male who suffered an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and was successfully resuscitated with therapeutic hypothermia. He is currently comatose and admitted to the intensive care unit. He has no allergies to antibiotics and has not received any antibiotic therapy before the cardiac arrest. He is not suspected or confirmed to be pregnant and has no tracheobronchial aspiration. He is willing to participate in the study to determine the potential benefits of prophylactic antibiotics in comatose survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with no history of anesthesia complications or impairment of the auditory system. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effects of two different sedation regimes on auditory evoked potentials and electroencephalogram (EEG). He is willing to participate in two separate sessions, each involving the administration of a different sedative drug combination (dexmedetomidine/remifentanil and midazolam/remifentanil) at clinically relevant sedation levels. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma and is scheduled for an elective nephrectomy surgery. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has no known allergies to medications or local anesthetics. He has never had peripheral neuropathy, bleeding diathesis, or any psychiatric disorders. He is not on any opioid therapy and has no inflammation or infection over the injection site. He is not morbidly obese and his physical status is classified as ASA II. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to undergo either the anterior subcostal or posterior approach for the ultrasound-guided Quadratus Lumborum Block.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and rectal bleeding for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension and takes amlodipine as an anti-hypertensive medication. She has never had a colonoscopy before. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. She does not have any significant family history of gastrointestinal disease. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant. She is mentally competent and able to provide informed consent. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her laboratory tests are within normal limits.

26 y/o female with a history of one previous caesarean section presents for scheduled repeat caesarean section due to fetal macrosomia. The patient is currently at 38 weeks gestation and has no other significant medical history. The patient has been diagnosed with Placenta previa during this pregnancy which is being managed conservatively. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivities to medications. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 5 years ago. He underwent radical prostatectomy and was treated with radiation therapy to the prostate bed. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels remained undetectable for 2 years post-treatment, but then began to rise slowly. He was started on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with leuprolide and has been on this therapy for the past 3 years. His PSA levels have been stable on ADT until recently, when they started to rise again. Imaging studies revealed the presence of 3 metastatic lesions in his bones. The largest lesion is in the sacrum and measures 1.8 cm in diameter. The patient has mild bone pain but is otherwise asymptomatic. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0. His testosterone level prior to ADT was 300 ng/dL. His hemoglobin level is 12.0 g/dL, platelet count is 200,000 x 10^9/uL, serum albumin is 4.0 g/dL, and his serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 65 mL/min. He has no evidence of visceral metastases or spinal cord compression. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help control his disease and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and who was recently diagnosed with moderate to severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He presents with shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. He is currently on mechanical ventilation, but despite the reduction of the instrumental dead space and the increase of the respiratory rate, he has refractory hypercapnia with a PaCO2 of 51 mmHg. Echocardiography revealed pulmonary arterial hypertension and right ventricular dilatation, indicating pulmonary vascular dysfunction. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He does not have any contraindications to curative anticoagulation and has jugular venous access. He is affiliated with social security.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who has been living with HIV for over 6 years. He is currently on Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy (HAART) and has a CD4 count of 350/mm3. He has also been diagnosed with cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. He works as a teacher and has a healthy lifestyle, not smoking or using any illicit drugs. He has not experienced any opportunistic infections and is clinically stable. His viral load is less than 200 copies/ml. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his immune system function and is willing to take low dose thalidomide or placebo for 28 days. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 45-year-old woman, who works as a full-time nurse, is considering bariatric surgery due to her BMI of 42 kg/m2. She has attempted various weight loss methods, including diets and exercise, but has not been successful in achieving significant weight loss. She has been cleared by her primary care physician to participate in a moderate level exercise program and is willing to comply with expected attendance and participation at all intervention sessions and testing appointments. She has reliable transportation and is excited to participate in the study to improve her physical performance and overall health. However, she does not have any orthopedic limitations that would preclude exercise testing and training.

45-year-old female with a history of chronic diarrhea and anemia of unknown origin presents for video capsule endoscopy (VCE) due to inconclusive results from previous diagnostic tests. She has no known gastrointestinal stenoses, adhesions, or diverticula of the small bowel, and is not affected by severe or diabetes-induced intestinal hypomotility. The patient has been informed about the study and has consented to participate. She will be randomized to receive either the MiroCam® or the Olympus® Enteropro EndoCapsule® during her VCE procedure, which will take place at the Medical University of Vienna over the course of the next six months. She has been advised of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to undergo the examination to help improve diagnostic yield for future patients.

The patient is a 25-year-old premenopausal woman with a BMI of 22. She is currently using non-hormonal, double-barrier method contraception and has no plans of attempting to become pregnant during the study or 30 days thereafter. The patient has no known allergies to medication and is able to swallow gelatin capsules. She has not used tobacco (nicotine products) for the past two years. The patient has no significant medical history and is in generally good health. Her laboratory values at screening are normal. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for all treatment and follow-up visits. She has not participated in any clinical trial with investigational medication within 30 days prior to the study and has no plans to take an experimental drug prior to the end of 30 days after participation in this study. The patient has no symptomatic uterine fibroids or endometriosis and is not using any hormonal treatments within 30 days of the first dose of study medication. She has no history of alcohol and/or drug abuse and no known active infection of HIV, Hepatitis A, B or C.

An 80-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital after falling down while walking in the park. She complained of severe pain in her left hip and was unable to move her left leg. On examination, there was tenderness and swelling over the left hip, and the left leg was shortened and externally rotated. Radiographic evaluation revealed a displaced intertrochanteric fracture. The patient has a medical history significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medications. She has no known allergies or history of thrombophilia. She is an English-speaking native and is expected to be medically optimized for surgery. Surgery is planned within 48 hours of admission. She has not undergone any recent surgeries, and there is no indication of infection or retained hardware around the affected hip. She is not undergoing percutaneous pinning of the hip fracture.

A 30-year-old woman gave birth to a 32-week preterm infant via a spontaneous vaginal delivery. The infant weighed 1.6 kg at birth and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The mother had no history of chorioamnionitis or prolonged rupture of membranes. The infant did not require resuscitation at delivery and had 8/9 on the Apgar score at 5 minutes. The infant was randomized for antibiotic treatment within the first 48 hours of life. The infant's clinical condition remained stable, and there were no signs of clinical illness such as respiratory distress, seizures, or need for vasoactive drugs. The infant was not diagnosed with any congenital anomalies. The parents provided consent for their infant to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old female presents with complaints of discomfort, dryness and redness in both eyes while wearing her monthly disposable contact lenses. She has been wearing contact lenses for the past 5 years and has never had any issues before. She works in an office and spends a lot of time in front of the computer. She denies any history of ocular diseases, surgeries, or allergies. Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She is willing to stop wearing her monthly lenses and wear the study lenses for at least 3 days per week and at least 8 hours per day. She is able to understand and sign the IRB-approved informed consent form.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who is a social drinker and reports consuming at least two heavy drinking episodes in the past 30 days according to the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criterion of 4 drinks for females. She is in good physical health with no history of head trauma, neurological conditions, or intracranial surgery. She is not taking any medications or have any medical conditions for which alcohol is contraindicated. She has good command of the English language and is willing and capable to provide written informed consent. She does not have any history of alcohol dependence or receiving treatment for alcohol dependence. She has normal body mass index and does not have any metal implants or paramagnetic objects within her body. She has no history of claustrophobia or panic attacks. She does not have any abnormal clinical laboratory findings including serum creatinine, liver function tests, elevated serum bilirubin, or pre-trial EKG results demonstrating clinical significant abnormality.

A 58-year-old male patient with a history of COPD for 7 years came to the clinic for a check-up. He has a smoking history of 20 pack years and is currently on a combination of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta2-agonists. He has had no exacerbations in the past year and his FEV1 is 65% of predicted normal values. He has no other significant medical history or allergies to medications. He has not undergone any thoracic surgeries and is not currently in any pulmonary rehabilitation programs. He is willing to discontinue his current medication for the duration of the study and is willing to sign an informed consent form. He is not on any medication for prostatic hyperplasia or bladder neck obstruction.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis. He was recently diagnosed with inoperable advanced hepatoma and has undergone failed surgical interventions and resection operations. His liver function is categorized as Child-pugh B, and he has a tumor occupancy of less than 70%. Imaging results from MRI, CT, and ultrasound have confirmed the diagnosis of hepatoma. His predicted life expectancy is greater than 6 months, and he has an ECOG score of less than 3, indicating that he can tolerate TACE. The patient has voluntarily agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has signed an informed consent form. He does not have complete obstruction of the main portal vein or tumor occupancy of 70% or more. He has not received TACE or other antineoplastons and does not have renal inadequacy with a Cr of less than 133 umol/L. The patient does not have severe cardiovascular disease or any other disease that could influence the proposal.

32 year old male athlete who sustained a posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear while playing football. The patient reports feeling a pop in his knee followed by pain and difficulty bearing weight. He underwent an MRI which confirmed a PCL tear. The patient has no history of knee surgery or significant knee injury. He is otherwise healthy and physically active. He is motivated to return to his previous level of activity and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to undergo PCL reconstruction using knot/press-fit technique.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in his right knee, causing him significant pain and difficulty with daily activities. He has been scheduled for a total knee replacement surgery. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. His pre-operative hemoglobin levels are within normal range according to the investigator. He has not participated in any clinical studies in the past and is willing to provide informed consent for this study. The patient does not have a history of haemophilia, cytotoxic drug use, or untreated anemia. He has not undergone any pre-donation or other autologous blood transfusion procedures.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who had a ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) 3 years ago. He was successfully treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) within 10 hours of the onset of chest pain. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not have a history of diabetes or heart failure. His recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 45% and mild left ventricular hypertrophy. He does not have any significant mitral regurgitation or valve disease. His current medications include aspirin, a beta-blocker, and a statin. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the study procedures.

62 year old male with a history of hypertension and stable angina presenting with chest pain on exertion. He is currently on aspirin, metoprolol and amlodipine. He has no history of myocardial infarction or other cardiac interventions. The patient reports that he has been experiencing chest pain for the past three months, with increasing frequency and intensity. The patient underwent an exercise tolerance test which was positive for ischemia. Coronary angiography was performed and showed a significant stenosis in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). The patient has provided informed consent to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of statin on coronary microcirculation dysfunction after percutaneous coronary intervention. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and will be randomly assigned to either the pre-treatment group or control group. The patient will receive atorvastatin 80mg/d for 4 days if assigned to the pre-treatment group. Percutaneous coronary intervention will be performed based on the decision of the attending physician and fractional flow reserve (FFR) and index of microvascular resistance (IMR) will be measured before and after the procedure to evaluate coronary microcirculation dysfunction. The patient will be monitored for adverse cardiac events for 1 year.

The patient is a 20-year-old female who underwent valve replacement surgery at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta due to mitral valve insufficiency caused by an atrioventricular septal defect. She had her first surgery at the age of six months to repair the defect, and at the age of 10, she underwent surgery to repair the mitral valve.
