However, the valve did not function properly, and she underwent a second surgery at the age of 12 to replace the mitral valve with a bio-prosthetic valve. Since then, she has been on anticoagulant therapy to prevent thromboembolic events. She has had no major complications or valve-related incidents since the surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the study and share her medical records for the retrospective analysis of valve replacement surgeries in children and adolescents.

Newborn male infant, born at 39 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 3.6 kg. No previous illnesses compatible with pertussis. Mother is Italian-speaking and accessible by telephone. The planned residence is in the clinic district for at least 1 year. The infant meets the weight criteria for the trial, with a weight at the first vaccination at least third percentile for boys. The infant has not received any prior pertussis vaccination and has no major congenital abnormality, failure to thrive, or known or possible immune system deficit. The infant is over 6 weeks to under 12 weeks of age and has no renal failure, no prior prolonged immunosuppressive therapy, no prior systemic corticosteroids, unless duration is less than 14 days and at least 48 hours since last dose. The infant has no perinatal central nervous system disease or damage, and no history of convulsions.

57 year old man diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) stage IIIE. He has completed 6 cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy with 8 infusions of rituximab, and achieved complete remission. His ECOG performance status is 1, and his IPI score at diagnosis was 2. He has no history of secondary malignancy or CNS involvement, and has normal renal function with a creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dl. He is HIV and Hepatitis negative, and has agreed to use appropriate contraception during the study.

The patient is a 47 year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past six months. The pain started after lifting a heavy object at work. He describes the pain as a dull ache that is constant, and occasionally sharp when he moves certain ways. He has tried over-the-counter pain medication, but it has not provided much relief. He smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol on weekends. He exercises occasionally, but has not been able to maintain a consistent routine due to the pain. He has no history of fractures, luxations, surgery, or musculoskeletal disorders in his low back or lower limb. He reports no leg pain or neuropathic pain. He is not currently receiving any physiotherapy treatment, and has not received any needle-based treatments in the past 6 months. He does not have any specific lumbar pathology, fibromyalgia, unstable cardiovascular diseases, or any other degenerative diseases. He is not currently taking any medications for depression or opioids for pain management. He is willing to consider participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatments for his chronic low back pain.

A 25-year-old Hispanic woman, who is sexually active, is interested in using birth control methods. She is married and has two children. She has tried hormonal birth control pills in the past but discontinued them due to side effects. She is concerned about gaining weight with hormonal birth control methods. She has a BMI of 25.1 and is generally healthy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will compare different progestin-only birth control methods to the non-hormonal copper IUC (ParaGard). She is willing to come back to the on-campus enrollment site for consent and enrollment activities. She is interested in the implant (Implanon) or levonorgestral-releasing IUS (Mirena) as her preferred method of birth control.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who recently underwent arthroscopic meniscal repair surgery on his left knee due to a complete tear in the red-white zone. He did not receive intra-surgical PRP injection during the procedure. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any anticoagulant medications or NSAIDs. The patient is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effect of PRP injection on post-meniscal repair outcomes regarding pain, functional state of the operated knee, and healing process. He is able to follow the pre-injection guidelines and is willing to receive intra-articular knee injection with PRP.

As this clinical trial is studying the validity and reliability of the Motor Accuracy-Revised Test in Turkey, the patient description is not applicable. However, the eligible participants for this trial are children between the ages of 6 and 8 years 11 months who do not have any physical, psychological, or mental disabilities and have the consent of both the child and the parents. The exclusion criteria include individuals with physical, visual, or hearing disabilities, mental retardation, or learning disabilities.

62-year-old male with a medical history significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presented to the nephrology clinic with complaints of fatigue, decreased appetite, and generalized weakness. Laboratory investigations revealed elevated serum creatinine of 2.5 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate (CKD-epi) of 20 ml/min/m². Further workup revealed chronic kidney disease stage 4. He has no history of organic gastro-intestinal disease or colonic surgery. He is not a recipient of a renal or solid organ transplant, and has not used any pre-/pro-/syn- or antibiotics in the preceding 4 weeks. He has been counseled on the importance of dietary modifications and management of his chronic kidney disease. He has been interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the hypothesis that AXOS can decrease intestinal generation and serum concentrations of microbial metabolites in patients with CKD not yet on dialysis.

25 yo M who recently sustained a non-contact injury to his right knee while playing soccer. MRI showed complete tear of the ACL with no other significant findings. He has no significant past medical history. The patient has elected to undergo surgical reconstruction of the ACL and has provided informed written consent to participate in this clinical trial. The patient is an avid athlete and is interested in optimizing his recovery and return to sports. He is compliant with follow-up appointments and willing to complete questionnaires and undergo objective knee joint assessments during the study period.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of attention deficit disorder since childhood. He has difficulty focusing on tasks and completing them, often feeling overwhelmed and distracted. The patient has tried various medications in the past, but has experienced unwanted side effects or found them to be ineffective. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of psychiatric disorders, epilepsy or brain injury. He is motivated to try non-invasive treatments for his condition and is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman diagnosed with primary hypothyroidism six months ago. She has been on levothyroxine treatment since then, but she still experiences symptoms such as fatigue, weight gain, and depression. Her TSH level is in the normal range, but her free T4 level is slightly low. She has no known history of cardiac disease, chronic obstructive lung disease, malabsorption disorder, gastrointestinal surgeries, significant renal or liver dysfunction, seizure disorders, or thyroid and non-thyroid active cancers. She is not pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy in the next 12 months. She has no history of uncontrolled psychosis, psychotropic medication use, steroid use, amiodarone, chemotherapy for cancer, iron supplement more than 325mg per day, carafate/ proton pump inhibitor use, or cholestyramine use. She is not scheduled for deployment. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if desiccated thyroid extract can help improve her symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 65-year-old female with severe to profound hearing impairment in both ears. She has been experiencing difficulty understanding speech in quiet environments, even with hearing aids. She has no history of cognitive impairment or neurological disorders. She is interested in receiving a cochlear implant and is a candidate based on her speech understanding test results, which showed less than 60% understanding at 65 dB SPL in the best aided condition. She has no contraindications for cochlear implantation and is willing to participate in the study.

54 year old female presented with a diagnosis of early stage breast cancer. Histology showed invasive ductal carcinoma with a tumor size of 2.5 cm. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary node dissection with 8 nodes sampled. Pathology revealed clear margins with no evidence of lymphovascular invasion or involved nodes. The patient's Zubrod performance status is 1. She has no history of collagen vascular disease, psychiatric or addictive disorders, or prior radiation therapy. She is currently not pregnant or lactating. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She is interested in convenient and minimally invasive treatment options for her breast cancer.

A 55-year-old female smoker underwent a uniportal VATS for the resection of a small nodule in her left upper lobe. The procedure was successful and the patient was discharged after three days. During her follow-up CT scan, a postoperative lung herniation was identified. The patient reported no symptoms and was advised to continue routine follow-up visits. The investigators contacted the patient to schedule a physical examination and symptom evaluation. The patient consented to participate in the study and reported feeling fine with no symptoms related to the lung herniation.

The patient is a 30-year-old Cantonese-speaking Chinese male who was diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 25. He currently resides in an assisted living facility and is under the care of a psychiatrist for his condition. The patient has a history of auditory hallucinations and delusions, which have been managed with antipsychotic medications. He reports occasional episodes of disorganized thinking and speech, but is generally able to communicate clearly and coherently. The patient has no history of diabetes or any known allergies to sugar or artificial sweeteners. He is able to understand the nature of the study and has provided informed consent to participate. The patient is physically able to perform the tasks required in the study and has no known history of intellectual disability or organic brain disorder.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of frequent outdoor activities and sun exposure. During his yearly dermatology check-up, his dermatologist identified a 5mm actinic keratosis lesion on his left shoulder. He has no history of skin cancer and is otherwise healthy. His blood work and other laboratory tests are all within normal limits. He has not taken any immunosuppressive medication or undergone any recent cosmetic or therapeutic procedures. He is willing to follow study instructions and commit to all study requirements. He has provided written informed consent and agreed to allow photographs of the selected lesion to be taken and used as part of the study data package.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus 10 years ago. She is currently on multiple daily insulin injections and has been on this treatment for the past 5 years. Her HbA1c level is 7.2%, and her BMI is 22.5 kg/m^2. She has a non-smoker history and does not use any form of nicotine products. The patient has no significant medical history or any family history of diabetes. She is interested in participating in this trial to contribute to the development of new treatment options for type 1 diabetes mellitus.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian woman who was recently diagnosed with uveal melanoma with metastasis. She is experiencing symptoms such as blurred vision, eye pain, and loss of vision in one eye. She has a history of hypertension but it is well-controlled with medication. She has never received any chemotherapy or immunotherapy treatment in the past. Her last major surgery was a cholecystectomy done two years ago. Her performance status according to the Karnofsky scale is 80%. Her blood tests show that her white blood cell count is 5,000/mm3, platelets are 110,000/mm3, and hemoglobin is 11.2 g/dL. Her liver function tests (AST and ALT) are normal, and her total bilirubin is 1.2 mg/dL. Her serum creatinine level is 1.1 mg/dL. The patient is not pregnant and is using a reliable method of contraception. She is willing to comply with medical monitoring and treatment.

52-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with symptoms of fever, chills, and malaise. He reports a recent urinary tract infection that was treated with oral antibiotics, but his symptoms did not improve. Upon examination, he is found to have hypotension, tachycardia, and altered mental status. Blood cultures are drawn, and he is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and norepinephrine for septic shock. Transthoracic echocardiography reveals left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an LVEF of 35%. The patient is sedated, mechanically ventilated, and adapted to the ventilator. The attending physician decides to initiate a fluid challenge to optimize cardiac output in septic shock. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The patient receives IV fluid therapy with 500 ml of crystalloid solution, and hemodynamic monitoring is conducted using transthoracic echocardiography and thermodilution monitoring. The patient and his trusted person have received oral and written information about the study.

This is a 25-year-old female who was referred to an orthodontist by her general dentist for treatment of malocclusion. She has been wearing traditional metal braces for 6 months now and is scheduled to undergo orthodontic treatment for another 6 months. She reports experiencing moderate pain during the initial week of treatment which subsided over time but has experienced occasional discomfort during adjustments. She maintains good oral hygiene and attends regular orthodontic visits as scheduled. She has no cognitive impairment and speaks Spanish fluently. She has consented to participate in the study and provide feedback on her pain level experience during orthodontic treatment.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has a history of smoking for over 40 years. He has been experiencing cough and shortness of breath for the past few months. He has also lost weight unintentionally. On physical examination, he has decreased breath sounds on the right side of his chest. His pulmonary function test showed a moderate obstructive pattern. A CT scan of the chest revealed a suspicious lesion in his right main bronchus. The patient has been referred for a bronchoscopy to evaluate the lesion. He has no significant past medical history, and he's not currently taking any medications. He doesn't have any known allergies. He doesn't drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a carpenter and has been exposed to sawdust and other construction materials for the majority of his adult life.

The patient is a 39-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his lower back for the past 3 years, and the symptoms have progressively worsened over time. The patient has been on traditional disease modifying drugs, including methotrexate, leflunomide, and sulphasalazine, but has not found significant relief from his symptoms. He is eligible to begin conventional biologic therapy and has consented to participate in this clinical trial. The patient has no past medical history of note and is not currently taking any other medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient is employed as a software engineer and leads a mostly sedentary lifestyle. He is married with two children and reports a good support system at home. The patient is willing to attend all follow-up appointments and adhere to the treatment protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with bipolar II disorder five years ago. She has been struggling with depressive episodes despite being treated with multiple combinations of medications, including lithium, quetiapine, and lamotrigine. She has a MADRS score of 28 and her depression has not improved with her current medications. She has no history of brain injury or neurological impairment, and her renal and hepatic function tests are within normal limits. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She is fluent in English and capable of giving informed consent. She has never received MSCs transplant within the last six months. She does not have a history of alcohol or substance abuse or dependence. She is currently not suicidal and is stable in terms of her medical and psychiatric conditions.

A 7-year-old boy diagnosed with nephroblastoma after presenting with abdominal pain, vomiting, and hematuria. Imaging studies showed a left-sided abdominal mass measuring 8 cm in diameter. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of nephroblastoma, and the patient was staged as favorable histology, stage II. The patient has no significant past medical history or family history of cancer. He is a non-smoker and has never been exposed to second-hand smoke. The patient's weight and height are within the 50th percentile for his age. He has no significant medical comorbidities and is compliant with medications. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or cardiotoxic nephrotoxic drugs in the past four weeks and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past four weeks. The patient has no history of mediastinal disease or mediastinal radiation therapy for other tumors. The patient's cardiovascular, digestive, neurological, circulatory, renal, liver, and blood tests are all within normal limits.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was recently diagnosed with primary hypertension during a routine check-up with her pediatrician. She has no prior history of hypertension and is not currently taking any medication for it. She is otherwise healthy and has no known medical conditions or allergies. Her BMI is within the normal range for her age and height. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if there is a correlation between primary hypertension and sleep disordered breathing. Her parents have consented to her participation in the study and the informed consent/assent form has been provided to her for review.

This is a 62-year-old female with a past medical history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on peritoneal dialysis. She has been on peritoneal dialysis for 6 months and has a stable renal function. Her serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) level has been consistently high, with the latest measurement being 295 pg/mL. She has no known history of parathyroidectomy or parathyroid intervention. She has been compliant with her current medication regimen, which includes activated vitamin D and phosphate binders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication for the treatment of secondary hyperparathyroidism. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old post-menopausal woman diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. Her disease was initially responsive to treatment, but recently she developed symptoms of recurrence including right breast swelling, pain, and bone pain. Imaging studies confirmed the presence of metastatic disease in the liver, bone, and lung. Her current treatment regimen consists of an aromatase inhibitor, but her disease has progressed despite this therapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. She has no history of diabetes or cardiac disease. She has never been pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. Her tumor is hormone receptor-positive and HER2-negative. A formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor sample from her primary cancer is available for central testing. She is willing to receive an LHRH agonist and meet all other inclusion criteria. She has not received prior treatment with fulvestrant or any AKT, PI3K, or mTOR inhibitors.

The patient is a 30-year-old female healthcare worker who is currently working at the Greifswald University hospital. She is willing and able to complete a written consent form and is willing to have her blood samples stored for future research. She is in good health and does not have any known medical conditions. She has not been diagnosed with COVID-19, nor has she been in close contact with anyone who has been diagnosed with COVID-19. She is interested in participating in this study to help researchers gain a better understanding of the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 in asymptomatic healthcare workers and to monitor the future spread of the disease by assessing serological responses. She is willing to participate in all six study visits and is willing to fill out the questionnaire at each visit. She understands that her participation in this study is voluntary and that she can withdraw at any time without any consequence.

A 50-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and diabetic neuropathy complains of numbness and tingling sensations in his feet and hands for the past 6 months. He reports difficulty in walking and holding things. He is currently on oral hypoglycemic agents and has been under an endocrinologist's supervision for the past 3 years. He has tried conventional treatments for diabetic neuropathy, but the symptoms have not improved. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and he is not HIV positive. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His family history is negative for any neurologic problems. His BMI is 28. His HbA1c is 8.5%. He has no difficulty in swallowing and is able to commit to the weekly time requirements associated with the study. He has intravenous access, and his endocrinologist has assessed and approved him for participation in this study.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who was brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. CT scan revealed an early massive cerebral infarction without cerebral hemorrhage or old infarction. The patient is conscious but with mild disturbance of consciousness. Paralysis of upper and lower extremities on the right side with grade 2 muscle strength in the affected limbs was observed. Blood pressure is within the normal range. The patient has no other severe medical complications, and his medical history is unremarkable. The patient has not received any thrombolysis or anticoagulation therapy. The patient's heart rate is 68 BPM and no sinus bradycardia is observed. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of hypertension that has been difficult to control despite being on four or more blood pressure-lowering medications. His average daytime blood pressure readings from a 24-hour ABPM were consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is above 45 ml/min/1.75 m2 and he has no active infections or known coagulopathies. He has not had any recent acute coronary events, stroke, or transient ischemic attacks. He has no clinically significant arrhythmias or severe liver disease. He is mentally competent and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 67-year-old male patient presented to the hospital after suffering a left middle cerebral artery stroke. He has been in the hospital for two weeks and was diagnosed with dysphagia. He has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and has had several episodes of aspiration pneumonia. A swallow study revealed impaired cough response. He has a history of hypertension and has never smoked. He is currently on antihypertensive medication and is able to move all four limbs, but he is still having difficulty with balance and coordination. His vital signs are stable and he is able to communicate effectively.

A 55-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital for a planned colonic resection with anastomosis. She had been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation for several months, which did not improve with dietary changes and laxatives. She underwent several diagnostic tests, including colonoscopy and biopsy, which revealed a malignant tumor in the colon. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Her pre-operative CRP level was 150 mg/L, which was within the inclusion criteria for the study. She agreed to participate in the study and is expected to return home after surgery. She does not have any other inflammatory diseases or take any anti-inflammatory medications. She is able to understand the study and has no opposition to participating.

A 56-year-old female patient was referred to an orthopedic surgeon for left knee replacement surgery. The patient has a medical history significant for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. She is a former smoker, quit smoking 5 years ago, and denies any alcohol or drug use. The patient is taking metoprolol, lisinopril, amlodipine, simvastatin, and metformin for her medical conditions. Her vital signs were stable on examination, and she had no pain or swelling in the affected joint. The patient has undergone several diagnostic tests, including X-ray, MRI, and blood tests, which confirmed the diagnosis of severe osteoarthritis of the left knee. She was advised to undergo left knee replacement surgery for the management of the condition. The patient was counseled regarding the benefits and risks of the surgery, including the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and the use of anticoagulant therapy for thromboprophylaxis. She gave her informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and meet the eligibility criteria.

38 year-old female with a history of asthma, presenting with episodic dyspnoea and wheezing with occasional cough for the past 2 years. She is currently not taking inhaled or oral corticosteroids, long-acting β2-agonists, leukotriene antagonists, sodium cromoglycate,or nedocromil sodium, anticholinergic agents, but has been using salbutamol inhaler as needed. She reports having occasional asthma exacerbations, but has not had any in the past 4 weeks. The patient has normal spirometry with baseline FEV1 of 85% of predicted value and FEV1/FVC of 78%. She has no significant medical history other than asthma and is a non-smoker. She has no history of respiratory infection in the past month and has never been diagnosed with COPD, bronchiectasis, or pulmonary embolism. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 25-year-old woman who lives in a dengue-endemic area presents with a history of dengue fever infection in the past. She is concerned about the possibility of contracting dengue fever again, especially since she heard about the potential for a more severe form of the illness if infected with a different serotype. She is generally healthy and has no history of Flavivirus infection or vaccine. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception throughout the trial period. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to be followed throughout the trial period.

A 25-year-old female patient was diagnosed with Gaucher's disease at a young age due to an enlarged spleen and liver. She underwent a splenectomy at age 10 and has been managing her disease with regular check-ups and a strict diet. She has not received enzyme replacement therapy for at least 1 year and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance research for the disease. Her medical history includes no other illnesses, and she is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to comply with all study requirements, including regular infusions and vitamin D supplementation.

A 25-year-old healthy male volunteer is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication. He has no history of chronic or acute medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has a BMI of 22 and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow the recommended dietary restrictions during the study period.

A 7-year-old boy has been struggling with social interactions and communication skills. His parents have noticed that he has difficulty making eye contact, understanding social cues, and making friends. The boy has also developed repetitive behaviors and routines. After consulting with a pediatrician, the boy has been diagnosed with autism. His parents have agreed to participate in a clinical trial studying the relationship between cerebral blood flow and autism in children. The boy has no known medical conditions, and his MRI scans will be part of his ongoing treatment. His parents are committed to helping their son receive the best care possible and are excited to contribute to research that may lead to better treatment options for children with autism.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of liver cancer presents with a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He is a non-smoker and non-drinker. He has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has no significant medical or surgical history. He has no known allergies to medication. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for mildly elevated AST and ALT. His ECOG performance status is 1. Imaging studies show a single lesion measuring approximately 4 cm in size that is confined to the liver and is amenable to surgical resection. He is eligible for conservative hepatic resection or liver resection with curative intent. He has no history of metastatic brain or meningeal tumors. He is registered in a national health-care system. He has not received any prior systemic or loco-regional treatment for HCC. He is not a candidate for orthotopic liver transplantation. He is not receiving treatment with any other investigational medicinal product within the past 28 days. He is not receiving concurrent or chronic co-administration of CYP3A4 inducers.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of chest pain, shortness of breath and fatigue. On examination, he was found to have a blood pressure of 85/50mmHg, cold and clammy skin, and a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. The electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, indicating an acute inferior wall myocardial infarction. The patient was diagnosed with cardiogenic shock, and despite aggressive medical therapy, his blood pressure remained low, and his condition deteriorated. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit and was started on mechanical circulatory support with Impella. The patient was stabilized, and his condition improved over the next few days. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial to investigate the current status and clinical outcomes of patients with cardiogenic shock. The patient has provided voluntary consent for his medical records and data to be used for the study during the entire study period. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, with the cause of cardiogenic shock being an acute myocardial infarction. The patient has not been diagnosed with any other non-cardiac morbidity, and he has not refused active treatment.

A 42-year-old male with newly diagnosed acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) presents for evaluation for a bone marrow transplant (BMT). He has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has no allergies to medications. His physical examination is unremarkable. His laboratory tests show that he is HIV negative and his liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has no active infections. The patient has a matched related donor with 6/6 HLA Class I and II compatibility. He is scheduled to undergo myeloablative conditioning treatment with busulfan and cyclophosphamide (BU-CY) and will receive a targeted busulfan dosing strategy aimed at a serum concentration greater than 600 ng/mL at steady state. The CD34+ stem cells for transplantation are available, with a target cell dose between 2 x 10^6/kg and 10 x 10^6/kg (actual body weight). The patient is willing and able to participate in all study assessments and has signed informed consent before any study-specific procedures are performed.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with significant carotid artery plaque with >70% stenosis during routine imaging. She has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), but her lipid profile revealed an LDL-C level of 3.2 mmol/L (124 mg/dL) despite being on a stable dose of atorvastatin for the past year. She was referred to a multidisciplinary team for assessment of carotid endarterectomy, but due to her asymptomatic status and high surgical risk, she was deemed unsuitable for the procedure. She has never been treated with a PCSK9 inhibitor and has no contraindications to Evolocumab treatment. Her MRI scan revealed the presence of a lipid-rich necrotic core (LRNC) within her plaque. She is willing and able to self-administer Evolocumab by auto-injector and has suitable refrigerated storage. She is also willing to undergo serial MRI scans and use highly effective contraception if needed.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of congenital heart disease. He has undergone previous cardiac surgery and is now scheduled for a cardiac catheterization procedure through the femoral artery and vein at the Hospital for Sick Children. He is currently taking medications for his heart condition, including a beta-blocker and diuretic. He has no known allergies and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is able to speak and understand English and has no cognitive impairments. His parents are with him and have given informed consent for him to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old female who underwent total shoulder arthroplasty with the first generation TITAN Total Shoulder System less than 5 years ago. She has a history of osteoarthritis of the shoulder and has been experiencing severe pain and limited range of motion in her affected shoulder. She has not received any revision surgeries involving the TITAN Total Shoulder System and is willing and able to participate in required follow-up visits at the investigational site and to complete study procedures. The patient is in overall good health, and has no significant history of neurological or emotional conditions that would pre-empt her ability or willingness to participate in the study. She is motivated to improve her shoulder function and is committed to attending all scheduled visits.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive with her partner for over a year without success. She was diagnosed with unexplained infertility and is scheduled to undergo in vitro fertilization (IVF) with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). The patient has blastocyst-stage embryos available for transfer. She has a mix of good-quality and poor-quality embryos. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve pregnancy outcomes in women undergoing IVF/ICSI.

The patient is a healthy 35-year-old male with no history of liver, kidney, gastrointestinal or heart disease. He has a body mass index of 28 kg/m2 and is currently in good health. He has never smoked and is not currently taking any prescription medications. He is willing to abstain from alcohol and avoid grapefruit-containing products during the study. He is willing to take 2 capsules of Visbiome, a probiotics supplement, twice a day (morning and evening) from Study Day 2 to 29. He is willing to fast overnight before the pharmacokinetic study days and abstain from alcohol-containing beverages 24 hours before and during the study visits. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who attends a daycare center. His parents have expressed concerns about his hyperactivity, impulsiveness, and lack of focus which have been affecting his behavior at home and at school. They have noticed that he has difficulty following instructions, staying still during activities, and engaging in quiet activities. They have tried to implement behavior management strategies at home but have not seen significant improvements. They are interested in non-pharmacological interventions for their child's ADHD. The child is a native English speaker and is physically able to participate in group play sessions. The child has not been previously diagnosed with any neurological disorders or pervasive developmental disorders. The child is not currently being treated with psychotropic medication. The child's IQ is above 80. The child has not previously attended parent management classes.

A 35-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) after experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain. She underwent a right heart catheterization (RHC) which demonstrated a mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) of >25mm Hg, a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) of ≤ 15, and a pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) of >3. Her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) is greater than 50% predicted normal and V/Q and/or CT scan excluded the thromboembolic etiology. She is currently not on any specific treatment for PAH and desires to participate in the program. She has no history of mental illness, drug/substance abuse, or unstable psychiatric illness. She has never participated in this program before and meets all the eligibility criteria.

35 yo woman with a history of persistent asthma diagnosed according to GEMA4.0 criteria and grade II bilateral sinonasal polyposis of Lildholdlt diagnosed by an otolaryngologist. She has been treated with intranasal topical steroids at high doses, but has not responded to this treatment. She has not had an exacerbation of asthma that required treatment with parenteral steroids in the past month. The patient does not have any concomitant chronic respiratory diseases, nor any other severe comorbidities. She has not had any previous nasal surgery. The patient has not been previously treated with corticosteroids or other immunomodulatory treatments. She is willing to undergo functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 63-year-old Dutch-speaking woman who has been experiencing degenerative arthritis in her right knee for the past two years. She has undergone conservative treatment such as physiotherapy, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and corticosteroid injections, but her symptoms have progressively worsened. She is scheduled for a primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA) due to osteoarthritis. The patient reports no history of inflammatory arthritis, severe cardiac complaints, or severe pulmonary disorders. The patient's BMI is 31, and she has no history of coagulation disorders or hospitalization in the previous two months. The patient has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 72-year-old female who has been diagnosed with colon cancer. Upon evaluation, she was found to have sarcopenia with reduced skeletal muscle mass and strength. She is scheduled for an elective surgery that will last more than 2 hours. She reports feeling weak and fatigued, with difficulty performing activities of daily living due to her decreased muscle strength. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, respectively. She denies any significant weight loss, unintentional or intentional, in the past year. Her lab studies showed: Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL Albumin: 3.2 g/dL Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL Glomerular filtration rate (GFR): >60 mL/min/1.73 m2 AST: 25 U/L ALT: 20 U/L Alkaline phosphatase: 75 U/L Total bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL The patient is able to walk independently and perform activities of daily living, but she reports difficulty with stairs and lifting objects. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is not currently taking any medications and has no significant medical history or chronic diseases. She has never participated in a drug study before and has not donated blood within the past 60 days. She is willing to comply with study restrictions and able to give written informed consent. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is using a reliable form of contraception and has a negative pregnancy test. She is in good general health as determined by medical history and physical examination.

60 year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension presents with bilateral lower extremity claudication that has been worsening over the past few months. He reports pain in his calves that is relieved with rest. He also reports intermittent numbness and tingling in his feet. Physical exam reveals decreased pulses in both feet and bilateral calf tenderness. An ankle-brachial index (ABI) is performed and shows a value of 0.7 on the right and 0.6 on the left, indicating PAD. The patient is scheduled for a procedure to treat his peripheral arterial lesions with the MicroStent™ System per the current indications for use. He is willing to sign a patient informed consent form to participate in this observational study. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidemia 3. History of smoking 4. No prior history of cardiovascular disease

53-year-old male, six months post stroke with chronic hemiparesis affecting the right lower limb, independently ambulates with a cane for short distances but has reduced gait speed and experiences fatigue. Patient reports residual weakness at the affected lower limb and has an activity tolerance of at least two hours with a rest period. No history of injury or unstable medical condition. No receptive aphasia or incontinence. No anesthesia at the lower limbs. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve gait function and muscle strength.

As this is a mentoring program, there is no specific patient description required. However, the study is looking for youths in Sweden who report a need for additional adult contacts and do not have a history of regular use of illicit drugs, repeated delinquent behavior or single acts of violence against persons, or ongoing contacts with psychiatric care or social services.

A 18-year-old sexually active female who is interested in trying out different birth control methods. She has been on oral contraceptive pills for the past year but has experienced some side effects such as decreased libido and mood swings. She is open to trying the vaginal ring as an alternative method and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the two methods. She speaks English fluently and is comfortable communicating in Spanish as well. She does not plan on becoming pregnant during the study time frame and is able to commit to using the study methods for 6 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) for the past 10 years. She has a history of smoking for 15 years but has quit smoking for the past 5 years. She presents to the clinic with severe claudication and rest pain in her right leg, which has become progressively worse over the past few months. She has tried conservative management with exercise and medication but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. Her physical examination reveals Rutherford grade 4 with a localized gangrenous ulcer on her right foot. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. Her laboratory findings show an HbA1c of 7.5%, total cholesterol of 210 mg/dL, and LDL cholesterol of 130 mg/dL. She has undergone stent implantation in her right femoral-popliteal artery but now presents with tosaka III in-stent restenosis with an occluded lesion greater than or equal to 5cm in length. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is willing to sign the informed consent to participate.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2 presented with proteinuric chronic kidney disease. He has been on a stable dose of angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) for the past 4 weeks, but his albuminuria has been increasing despite this treatment. He is 5'9" tall and weighs 85 kg, with a body mass index of 27.5 kg/m^2. His eGFR is 45 mL/min/1.73m^2 based on Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation at Screening Visit 1. The participant has a urine albumin to creatinine ratio of 3000 mg albumin/g creatinine based on the geometric mean of the replicated measurements using 3 sequential first morning void urine at Visit 2. He is willing to participate in the study and capable of giving signed informed consent form. He has no history of substance dependence or a positive screen for drugs or alcohol abuse. He is not currently taking any biologic drugs and/or small molecule targeting the immune system. The participant is not on any serum creatinine-altering drugs within 1 month prior to Screening Visit 1. He is not currently taking any concomitant medications known to be associated with Torsades de Pointes or potent inducers/inhibitors of cytochrome P450 3A4 within 4 weeks of Visit 3 (Randomization). He is not taking zileuton, cilastatin (dipeptidase-1 [DPEP1] inhibitor), or leukotriene receptor antagonists (eg, montelukast) within 4 weeks of Screening Visit 1. He is taking simvastatin at a dose of 20 mg per day but has not taken lovastatin or atorvastatin at doses > 40 mg per day within 1 month prior to Screening Visit 1. He is not concurrently enrolled in another clinical study involving an investigational treatment or drug or participation in a device study within 3 months prior to Screening Visit 1.

The patient is a 63 year old woman with a history of vision loss in her left eye. She has been diagnosed with Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy (PCV) and has never received any treatment for it. Her symptoms include blurred vision, distortion and difficulty in reading. She has not received any corticosteroids or anti-vascular endothelial growth factors and has not undergone macular laser treatment or photodynamic therapy. Her best-corrected visual acuity in the affected eye is between 20/30 and 20/100. She has no known allergies to fluorescein, iodine, indocyanine green, aflibercept or verteporfin. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer. She underwent debulking surgery and now requires adjuvant therapy. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or cerebrovascular accident. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception during and for at least 6 months after completion of bevacizumab therapy. She has no active infection and no history of allergic reactions to study drugs. She has no history of prior cancer treatment and has not received any anti-VEGF drugs. She has adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who had a single ventricle congenital heart disease at birth, which was corrected through a series of surgeries, ultimately leading to a cavopulmonary anastomosis (Fontan). She has been experiencing worsening symptoms of protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), which is causing her to lose proteins, fats, and other key nutrients into her intestines. Her parents have reported that she is lethargic, has lost weight, and has become increasingly irritable. She has a past medical history of asthma, which is well-controlled with medication. She is alert and oriented, but appears fatigued. Her physical examination is significant for tachycardia, diminished femoral pulses, and edema in her lower extremities. She weighs 48 pounds. Her parents have consented to her participation in the clinical trial and she has assented to participate as well.

56-year-old male with a history of rectal bleeding and a positive fecal occult blood test (FOBT) is referred for colonoscopy. He denies any recent change in bowel habits, diarrhea, or constipation. The patient has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Physical examination is unremarkable. The patient is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. The patient has no history of cardiac pacemaker or other implanted electro medical devices. The patient is not currently pregnant or nursing and practices medically acceptable methods of contraception. The patient has not undergone any prior abdominal surgery of the gastrointestinal tract. The patient is willing and able to comply with study and device instructions.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with high blood pressure during a routine check-up with her primary care physician. Her blood pressure readings have consistently been above 150 mm Hg, despite being on medication. She has a history of hypertension in her family and is currently taking medication for high cholesterol. She owns a cell phone with unlimited texting and is comfortable using technology. She lives alone and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her blood pressure control and learn more about home monitoring. Her arm circumference is within the eligible range. She does not have dementia and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a healthy female between the ages of 18 and 50 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of intravaginal administration of P2G12 antibody. She must be in good health and have no known or suspected vaginal diseases or abnormalities. She must also be willing to abstain from vaginal sexual intercourse for 72 hours before and after dosing and agree not to undertake any vaginal practices during study participation other than receptive intercourse with a male or use of sanitary tampons during menses. The patient must not have received any form of immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy in the past six months and must not be receiving any medications via vaginal route. The patient must be willing to attend seven visits over 13 weeks and undergo physical exams, vital sign checks, blood and urine samples, cervical smear tests, and colposcopy. Adverse event data will be collected throughout the trial to assess the safety of the P2G12 antibody. This study is important in the development of a monoclonal antibody that can help prevent and protect against HIV infection.

26 yo healthy male with no significant medical history, currently not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, and with normal findings on physical examination. He has a body mass index of 22.5 kg/m2, systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure of 75 mmHg, and pulse rate of 65 beats per minute. He has no history of fainting, collapse, syncope, orthostatic hypotension, or vasovagal reactions. He does not use nicotine or consume excessive caffeine. He has never been exposed to macitentan or rosuvastatin. He is able to communicate effectively with the investigator and is willing and able to comply with the study requirements.

52-year-old woman with a history of epithelial ovarian cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, with initial treatment of debulking surgery followed by adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy. She had been in remission for 2 years before experiencing abdominal pain and bloating. Imaging revealed a single, isolated recurrence and biopsy of the mass confirmed a platinum-resistant cancer. She is otherwise in good health, with a performance-status ECOG score of 1, and has adequate renal, hepatic, and bone marrow function. She is interested in participating in the trial and is physically fit for surgery.

A 48-year-old post-menopausal woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 32kg/m^2 presents with complaints of fatigue and abdominal discomfort. She reports no significant alcohol consumption or drug use. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. Laboratory studies reveal an elevated liver fat percentage of 8 percent as measured with Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy. The patient has stable dietary habits and a physical activity pattern for the past three months. She agrees to comply with the study protocol, follow diet and lifestyle recommendations, and not consume or use illicit drugs during the study. She is willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient has no history of diabetes or chronic heart failure, and has not experienced any clinically significant acute cardiac events within the past six months. She is not currently taking fibrates, thiazolidinediones, or medications that could interfere with glucose homeostasis/metabolism. The patient is a non-smoker and has not donated blood or blood products within the past month. She has not participated in any other studies or received any other investigational drugs or devices within the past 30 days. The patient tests negative for anti-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C Virus (HCV) antibody. Her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are within normal limits. Her conjugated bilirubin, international normalized ratio, and platelet count are also within normal limits. Her serum creatinine levels are 0.9 mg/dL, and she has no significant renal disease. The patient's hemoglobin A1c (HbA1C) and fasting plasma glucose (FGP) levels are within normal limits. Overall, the patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study to evaluate the effect of Elafibranor on hepatic lipid composition in subjects with nonalcoholic fatty liver.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has struggled with her weight for most of her adult life. She is currently overweight with a BMI of 30, and she has tried various diets in the past with limited success. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively. She is employed as a teacher and has a relatively sedentary lifestyle. She is generally healthy, with no major medical or psychiatric illnesses, and is not taking any medications or dietary supplements that could affect the study outcomes. She has no history of binge drinking or irregular menstrual cycles. She is willing and able to eat and drink only the foods and beverages on the study menus and is willing to eat in the dining hall. She has no plans for a vacation during the study that would preclude adherence to the prescribed diet. She is willing to undergo additional procedures in this ancillary study, including two abdominal subcutaneous fat aspiration biopsies under local anesthesia. She has no allergy or prior reaction to Lidocaine, and she does not have any medical conditions or medications that would increase the risk of bleeding, infection, or skin reactions.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who recently immigrated to the United States from a country with a high prevalence of Hepatitis B virus. He has not been tested for Hepatitis B before, but he reports feeling fatigued and experiencing abdominal pain. He is concerned about his health and wants to get tested for Hepatitis B. He has not started any treatment for Hepatitis B. He is willing to participate in the study and has voluntarily signed the informed consent form. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical conditions. He is 180 cm tall and weighs 75 kg.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic pain in his lower back and hip for the past 6 months. The pain is constant and dull, with occasional sharp shooting sensations. He has tried various treatments, including physical therapy and medication, but has not found long-term relief. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is not taking any medications, and he does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is physically active, regularly participating in outdoor activities such as hiking and cycling. He is willing to receive an MRI and is able to provide written informed consent. He is a suitable candidate for CRFA treatment according to his treating physician. He is able to understand the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with the protocol.

A 33-year-old Turkish woman with a history of two unexplained recurrent miscarriages below 20 weeks of pregnancy is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the interaction between recurrent miscarriage and dental health. She has had two successful, full-term pregnancies without any complications. She has no history of thyroid disease, hyperprolactinemia, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, autoimmune diseases, thrombophilia, diabetes mellitus, uterine/cervical abnormalities, polycystic ovary syndrome, active liver disease, or cardiovascular disease. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, use any drugs or caffeine. She has not had any infections, chromosomal abnormalities, or abnormal embryo karyotype. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m2. Her partner is 35 years old. She is interested in knowing whether oral health care patterns that may promote or alleviate oral inflammation are associated with the history of miscarriage in Turkish women.

The patient is a 30 year old female who has been experiencing toenail fungus on her big toe for the past 6 months. The nail has become discolored, thickened and brittle. She has not received any treatment for the condition and has not applied any nail polish or cosmetic products to the toenail. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to refrain from having professional pedicures during the course of the study. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to treat her toenail fungus and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old Swedish woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most days, with a loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has trouble sleeping and feels tired throughout the day. She has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric hospitalizations. She is currently not receiving any psychological treatment but has been prescribed an antidepressant by her primary care physician, which she has been taking for the past 2 months. She has access to a computer with an internet connection and can read Swedish. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for her depression.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who was born prematurely at 29 weeks of gestation. She was previously enrolled in Study ROPP-2008-01, Section D, where she received treatment for retinopathy of prematurity with rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3. She currently presents with no significant medical issues and is otherwise healthy. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in this long-term safety and efficacy outcome study. The patient is able to comply with the protocol as determined by the investigator.

The patient is a 55-year-old Asian man who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 2 years. He has been taking medication to control his blood pressure, but it has not been consistently within the normal range. He is generally healthy, with no other medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only on special occasions. His average salt intake is around 10 g/day. He is interested in participating in a study to help control his blood pressure and improve his overall cardiovascular health. The patient works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle, but is willing to make changes to his diet and incorporate exercise into his routine. His blood pressure at the last check-up was 148/92 mmHg, and he has been advised to reduce his salt intake. He is able to provide written consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of hives on most days of the week for the past six months. The hives are accompanied by severe itching and a burning sensation on the skin. The patient has tried antihistamines, but the medication did not provide relief. She has no history of angioedema, and the appearance of the hives is not triggered by any consistent or identifiable factors. She has no significant past medical history, but her family history is notable for allergies and asthma. The patient is seeking medical attention at CHU Brugmann Hospital to receive a diagnosis for her chronic urticaria and to participate in a clinical trial investigating the role of endothelial cells in the pathogenesis of the disease. She is willing to undergo nail fold videocapillaroscopy and molecular level testing to help researchers gain more insight into the disease and potential new treatments.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with HIV infection after presenting with flu-like symptoms. His CD4 T cell count is 220 cells/mm3, and he has not yet started antiretroviral therapy (ART). He has no history of diabetes, renal disease, or lactose intolerance. His current medications include acetaminophen for pain relief. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of synbiotic nutritional supplements to improve his immune recovery.

The patient is a 7-year-old male with a known history of herpes simplex infection. He presents with a fever, painful blisters on his lips, and difficulty eating and drinking due to mouth sores. The patient is able to swallow oral medication and is not currently taking probenecid. The patient and their parent/guardian are willing to participate in the study and comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired teacher who is fluent in French. She is in good health and has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. She has a health insurance policy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to study the correlation between iron load in the brain and age. She has had no previous MRI exams or neuropsychological assessments within the last year. She is not currently taking any psychotropic drugs and her MOCA score is 28. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge and to learn more about her brain health.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with advanced lung cancer, with metastasis to the liver and bones. The patient has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has progressed despite the treatment. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient is not currently on any cancer therapy and has no known allergies to medications. The patient is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures and has provided signed informed consent. The patient has adequate laboratory parameters and has not received systemic antibiotics treatment for at least 7 days before the first dose. The patient has no known history of allogeneic organ transplantation or immunodeficiency.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl with a history of bronchiectasis. She has been experiencing recurrent respiratory infections, cough, and difficulty breathing for the past few years. A computed tomography (CT) scan revealed the presence of bronchiectasis in her lungs. She has been receiving treatment for her condition, including antibiotics and chest physical therapy. Despite the treatment, she has been experiencing reduced daily functional physical ability and struggles to perform routine activities due to dyspnea. She will be participating in a clinical trial to evaluate and compare exercise capacity in CF and non-CF bronchiectasis patients. The trial will involve a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) to assess her aerobic exercise capacity, which will help the clinicians objectively evaluate her physiological functions and predict her outcome and mortality in different clinical circumstances. The aim of the trial is to create an individualized exercise prescription that can improve her lung function and reduce the rate of lung function deterioration. She will undergo spirometry to help evaluate her respiratory function before and after the CPET. She is eligible for the trial as she has evidence of bronchiectasis on CT, is over 7 years old, and has completed a maximal CPET test according to accepted criteria. She is not experiencing an exacerbation of her condition within three days before the exercise evaluation, and there are no other relevant chronic diseases that affect her test results.

A 12-year-old boy presents with multiple common warts on his right hand and arm. He has had these warts for over a year and has tried over-the-counter remedies with no success. The warts are causing him discomfort and embarrassment. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies to medications or ingredients. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of A-101 topical solution in treating his warts. He and his parent/guardian understand the study requirements and are willing to comply with all study instructions and attend all study visits. They also understand that the study medication will be applied twice a week and that they will need to use an active method of birth control during the study.

This is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) two years ago. He was initially asymptomatic but now reports extreme fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss of 15 pounds in the past 6 months. His recent laboratory tests showed a lymphocyte count of 25,000/µL, hemoglobin of 10 g/dL, and platelet count of 90,000/µL. He has a low-grade fever and diffuse lymphadenopathy with the largest node measuring 6 cm in diameter. He has no history of hepatitis or other viral infections. He has refused chemotherapy due to concerns about side effects and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of more than 3 years. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study.

A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents to the hospital with shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He is diagnosed with ADHF according to the ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis of acute heart failure 2008. He has never had a history of cancer, chemotherapy, or chronic inflammatory conditions. He has not had a recent acute myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization within the past 6 months. He has undergone laboratory examinations and treatment plan, and will be followed up for 1 year to analyze his 1-year outcomes to explore the prognostic indicators for patients with ADHF.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the lower abdomen, occurs several times a week, and is often severe enough to interfere with her daily activities. She also reports occasional bloating, constipation and diarrhea. She has been evaluated by her pediatrician and gastroenterologist, and after a thorough examination, they diagnosed her with functional dyspepsia and irritable bowel syndrome. She has no other significant medical history, and she does not take any medications. Her parents consented to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the effect of oral administration of a mixture of Bifidobacteria on the improvement of frequency and intensity of abdominal pain in children with FD and IBS. She has not taken any other probiotics in the 2 months prior to enrollment, does not have any intestinal motility disorders, and is willing to give informed consent.

A 58-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation and heart failure is being considered for enrollment in a clinical study. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. His medications include a beta-blocker, a diuretic, and an ACE inhibitor. He is currently unemployed and lives alone, but his daughter checks on him regularly. He is willing to wear the µCor device for up to 90 days and attend monthly office visits during the study period. He is able to answer weekly phone calls regarding his health status. He has no other significant medical history and has not participated in any other clinical studies. He does not have any skin conditions that would prevent him from wearing the device, and he has adequate cellular transmission access. He is capable of giving informed consent.

A 55-year-old patient diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) visited the clinic, complaining of fatigue, weakness, and frequent infections. The patient has received supportive treatment with blood transfusions and erythropoietin (EPO) injections for the past 4 weeks but did not show any significant improvement. The patient has no history of dystonic reaction or anaphylactic reaction to metoclopramide. The physical examination revealed a pale appearance, and the latest lab test showed hemoglobin levels less than 11g/dL and an absolute reticulocyte count less than 60,000/microliter based on two baseline lab tests. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use medically acceptable contraception during the study. The patient is not currently taking any medications that have a high risk of extrapyramidal side effects.

A 15-year-old patient with a history of solid tumor of non-hematopoietic origin and has undergone prior standard therapy but failed to achieve positive results. The patient weighs 50 kilograms and has a Karnofsky performance level of 70%. The patient has not received bevacizumab and irinotecan previously. The patient is not pregnant nor breastfeeding, and is currently using an effective contraceptive method. The patient has no uncontrolled infection or clinically significant unrelated systemic illness. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 8 weeks.

32-year-old male who works in finance and has occasional difficulty falling asleep due to work-related stress. He reports feeling tired during the day and has tried over-the-counter sleep aids in the past with limited success. He has no history of chronic insomnia or any other sleep disorders. He is not currently taking any prescription medications and does not have any significant medical history.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with psoriasis by a dermatologist. He reports occasional mild joint pain but has not been diagnosed with any chronic disease likely to cause musculoskeletal symptoms. He is able to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form. His past medical and drug history are unremarkable. He is married and has two children. His BMI is 28, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has had a history of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion for the past 6 months. The patient has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has undergone several diagnostic tests, including a coronary angiogram, which revealed a total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery (LAD). The estimated duration of the occlusion is at least 4 weeks. The patient was referred for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and was successfully recanalized. The reference diameter of the occluded artery is > 2.5 mm. The patient is not allergic to Sirolimus or zotarolimus. The patient is willing to participate in the PRISON IV trial, and written informed consent has been obtained. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is not participating in any other trial, and long-term follow-up is possible. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 1 year. The patient is not taking coumadins and is not contraindicated for ASA or Clopidogrel or heparin.

56-year-old male diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and underwent open hepatic resection. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has no history of substance abuse or organ allograft. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no medical, psychological, or social conditions that may interfere with their participation in the study or evaluation of the study results.

The patient is a 10-month-old male infant who has been experiencing loose, watery stools for the past 3 days. The infant has been passing stool more frequently than usual, at least 3 times a day. The diarrhea has been non-bloody and not associated with fever, abdominal pain, or vomiting. The infant has been breastfeeding and has not started any solid foods yet. The mother reports that she has been giving the infant plenty of fluids and has not noticed any improvement in the diarrhea. The infant appears well-hydrated and active, with no signs of dehydration. The infant has no chronic illnesses or surgical history. The mother consents to participate in the clinical trial and understands the study's purpose and potential risks. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is eligible for enrollment.

A 42-year-old man was diagnosed with infective endocarditis after presenting with fever, chills, and fatigue. He has a history of intravenous drug use and recently had a dental procedure. Blood cultures were obtained and grew Streptococcus viridans. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, but his symptoms persisted. Further testing with metagenomic sequencing did not identify any additional infectious organisms. He has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has agreed to participate in this study to potentially uncover any underlying sub phenotypes and receive personalized treatment for his infective endocarditis.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) for several years, despite taking maximum medical therapy. He reports frequent heartburn, regurgitation, and difficulty swallowing. He has been diagnosed with GERD based on abnormal pH testing. The patient has been recommended for treatment with the LINX Reflux Management System and has provided written informed consent to participate in the post-approval study. He is willing to comply with study requirements and the follow-up schedule and assessments. The patient has no known allergies to titanium, stainless steel, nickel or ferrous materials. He is expected to complete the follow-up through 60 months.

42-year-old male with biopsy-proven relapsed diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The patient has previously received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation, but the disease has progressed despite treatment. The patient is not a candidate for or has declined standard salvage therapy for their disease. The patient has measurable disease with at least one lesion that has a single diameter of >= 2 cm, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) of 1. The patient has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) >= 1000/uL, hemoglobin (Hgb) >= 9 g/dl, and platelets (PLT) >= 100,000/uL. The patient has normal serum bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), serum creatinine, magnesium, potassium, serum amylase, serum lipase, fasting plasma glucose, and serum calcium levels. The patient is willing to provide blood samples for correlative research purposes and to take buparlisib orally once daily (QD) on days 1-28.

A 27-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with a history of recurrent nonseminoma germ cell cancer. The patient had previously undergone adequate cisplatin-based chemotherapy, but the disease had recurred and was refractory to further chemotherapy. The patient had no other malignancy except for the second testicular primary tumor. The patient has evaluable disease with documented progression within the last 2 months, and the tumor markers have increased since the end of the last treatment. The patient has no active infection, no severe malnutrition, and no pre-existing grade 2 or worse neurotoxicity. The patient has no pre-existing edema, senility, or psychosis, and there are no other expected difficulties for follow-up. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and the patient is willing to use effective contraception. The patient has not undergone high-dose chemotherapy with or without stem cell transplant, and the patient is not amenable to curative radiotherapy or surgery.

Patient is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has a BMI of 25. He has no history of steroid hormone use or any medication that might interfere with steroid metabolism. He is sexually active and agrees to use a recognized effective method of contraception with any female partner during the course of the study treatment and recovery phases until recovery is confirmed and study exit occurs. He has not participated in another clinical trial involving an investigational drug within the 30 days prior to the first screening visit. His physical and laboratory findings are normal, and he has no elevated PSA or abnormal semen analysis. His blood pressure and PHQ-9 score are within normal limits. He has no history of hypertension, primary testicular disease, or disorders of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.
