He has no known history of cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, or prostatic disease or significant psychiatric illness. He has negative serology for active Hepatitis or HIV at screening visit. He has no history of known, untreated sleep apnea. He is not desiring fertility within 12 months of signing consent for study participation. He is not participating in competitive sports where drug screening for prohibited substances is routine. He is not using sex steroids or medications which might interfere with steroid metabolism. He is not using medications that will interfere or interact with DMAU or LNG. He does not have known hypersensitivity to any of the active substances of DMAU, of the excipients of the study treatment, or LNG.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who was recently diagnosed with Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP) after presenting with petechiae and ecchymoses on her arms and legs. She has no significant past medical history and does not have any chronic illnesses that could affect the quality of her life. She is currently not taking any medications. Her parents are concerned about her condition and would like to participate in a clinical trial that could help them understand the disease and its treatment better. They are willing to complete questionnaires related to the quality of life of their child and follow the treatment protocol set up in the region Pays de la Loire. They understand that their child will be followed for 6 months and will have blood tests done at J0 and 6 months. They are willing to provide additional blood samples for the study's blood sample collection.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma, diagnosed with stage IIIb (T3N2), and underwent curative D2 lymphadenectomy resection for gastric cancer. The patient has no macroscopic or microscopic evidence for remaining tumor and can be randomized to either study arm within 6 weeks after surgery. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and is ambulatory. The patient has not received any previous cytotoxic chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy, except for corticosteroids, for the currently treated gastric cancer. The patient has no evidence of metastatic disease and has at least 15 examined lymph nodes. The patient has no significant cardiac disease and has no physical integrity of the upper gastrointestinal tract or malabsorption syndrome likely to influence absorption of capecitabine, and can take oral medication. The patient has no peripheral neuropathy ≥ CTCAEv3 grade 1 and has no organ allografts requiring immunosuppressive therapy. The patient has no serious uncontrolled intercurrent infections or other serious uncontrolled concomitant disease. The patient has a creatinine clearance above 50 ml/min and normal laboratory values for ANC, platelet count, total bilirubin, ALAT, ASAT, and alkaline phosphatase. The patient has no prior unanticipated severe reaction to fluoropyrimidine therapy or known DPD deficiency. The patient is willing to practice contraception during the study and has not received any investigational drug or agent/procedure within 4 weeks before randomization. The patient has not received blood transfusions or growth factors to aid hematologic recovery within 2 weeks prior to study treatment start. The patient is not requiring concurrent use of the antiviral agent sorivudine or chemically related analogues.

A 3-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with tetralogy of Fallot shortly after birth. He underwent corrective surgery at 4 months of age, which included pulmonary valve reconstruction and patching of the ventricular septal defect. During follow-up visits, it was discovered that he has developed pulmonary artery stenosis and pulmonary insufficiency. As a result, he requires re-intervention in the form of cardiac catheterization or re-operation. The patient's legal representatives provided written informed consent for him to participate in the study. The patient has no other clinically relevant medical conditions, and there are no contraindications for MRI.

A 7-year-old boy is admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit with a diagnosis of severe sepsis. He presents with a fever, hypotension, and poor organ perfusion. Blood cultures are positive for sepsis, and the patient is started on antibiotics. The patient has a nasogastric tube in place and requires enteral nutrition for his management. His weight is 20 kg, and he has central venous access. The patient has no metabolic diseases or primary liver or renal failure. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for their child's participation in the study. The child will be monitored for the metabolism of methionine and cysteine during his stay in the PICU. The study will provide important knowledge that may lead to changes in the management of critically ill pediatric patients in the future.

We are looking for women who have previously experienced preeclampsia during pregnancy and are interested in participating in a study that aims to improve cardiovascular health. Preeclampsia is a condition characterized by high blood pressure and protein in the urine during pregnancy, which can increase the risk of developing heart problems later in life. We are testing whether a short course of atorvastatin (a type of drug commonly used to lower lipids and prevent cardiovascular disease) can improve vascular function in women who have a history of preeclampsia. Participants must be willing to take either atorvastatin or placebo tablets daily for four weeks, followed by a four-week period without treatment, then "crossover" to receive the alternative tablet for another four weeks. Blood vessel function will be measured using specialized noninvasive scans and taking a blood test at the beginning and end of each treatment period. The study will be conducted by the Departments of Cardiovascular Medicine and Obstetrics & Gynaecology at the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford. If you are a woman with a history of preeclampsia and interested in participating, please contact us to learn more about the study eligibility criteria and requirements.

An 11-year-old African American boy presents with a history of occasional joint pain and muscle weakness. His past medical history is unremarkable and he is not taking any multivitamin supplements. His physical examination is within normal limits. His BP: 110/72 mmHg, HR: 80/min and BMI: 21. Laboratory test results show that his serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) level is 17 ng/mL, which is below the normal range (30-100 ng/mL). His serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) level is within the normal range. He is eligible for the clinical trial of vitamin D3 supplementation (1000 IU/day vs. placebo) for 6 months, which will be initiated during fall and winter. The study will help establish the threshold level of serum 25(OH)D for defining vitamin D insufficiency in preadolescent and adolescent children, and assess the safety and efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in this age group. The primary outcome measure will be serum 25(OH)D and PTH, while the secondary outcome measures will include markers of bone formation and resorption. The study will also examine differences in serum 25(OH)D, PTH, and markers of bone turnover in African American vs. Caucasian children.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing blurry vision, eye pain, and redness in her left eye for the past month. She has a history of uveitis and has been previously treated with topical corticosteroids. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, allergies, or current medications. Her best corrected ETDRS visual acuity is 20/50 in the left eye. She agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she agrees to use adequate contraceptives during the study period.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was referred to a vascular surgeon due to a blockage in his left femoral artery causing leg pain and difficulty walking. He has never had any surgeries before and he is not taking any medications. He is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He is retired and lives with his wife. He denies any allergies to medications. He has no history of MRSA colonization or infection, HIV or long-term stay in an acute care or long-term care center. He is not on dialysis. He is able to fast for the preoperative period. His kidney function is normal. He is not experiencing any active infection requiring antibiotics preoperatively. He is not suffering from chronic wounds. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45 year old male who works as a construction worker. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right shoulder for the past 3 months. The pain is constant and worsens at night, making it difficult for him to sleep. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy but has not found any relief. He has no history of shoulder injury or surgery. He has a medical history of hypertension and is taking medication for it. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing to participate in the trial and has given fully informed consent. The patient's self-rated pain score on the pain assessment scale (NRS) is 7 out of 10. The range of motion (ROM) of his shoulder is limited with abduction not more than 135 degrees and external rotation not more than 20 degrees. The diagnosis of periarthritis of shoulder is confirmed based on the clinical symptoms and ROM limitation. The patient has not received any treatment of hyaluronic acid injection or corticosteroids within the past 24 weeks.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who recently visited her primary care provider at Columbia University Medical Center. She has a family history of breast cancer and is concerned about her risk for developing the disease. The patient's mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 60, and her sister was diagnosed at age 52. The patient has never had breast cancer or any other type of cancer. She is interested in learning more about her risk for breast cancer and any preventative measures she can take. The patient is fluent in both English and Spanish and is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old woman presented to the clinic with swelling and pain in her left leg. She has a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in her left leg 2 years ago which was treated with anticoagulation therapy. Her current symptoms have been ongoing for 6 months and have not responded to conservative treatment such as compression stockings and elevation. She underwent a magnetic resonance venography (MRV) which revealed suspicion of iliac vein stenosis or compression. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. She has a patent common femoral vein and femoral vein of the study leg. She's scheduled for iliofemoral venography to confirm the diagnosis and potentially treat iliac vein compression syndrome. She has no history of metal allergy, iodine allergy, or severe renal insufficient function. She is not pregnant and has no acute DVT or history of thrombophilia. She has no concurrent disease that would make her unsuitable for surgery.

The patient is a 35 year old male who has been experiencing pain in his left upper back tooth for the past few months. The pain is constant and throbbing in nature, and he has been taking painkillers to manage it. He has previously undergone root canal treatment for the same tooth but the pain has persisted. Upon examination, it was found that he has a periapical defect with a periodontal pocket greater than 6mm, confined to the buccal aspect of the interproximal space. He has no other medical conditions and is in good general health. He does not smoke and is not currently pregnant or lactating. He is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for his condition. He is currently employed as a software engineer and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. His BMI is 26 with a blood pressure of 120/80. There is no remarkable finding in his physical examination.

The patient is an 18 year old female who has been struggling with symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) for several years. She experiences difficulty with staying focused, completing tasks, and is easily distracted. She has tried various stimulant medications in the past, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of vitamin D as a potential adjunct to stimulant medication for the treatment of ADHD. She is physically healthy and has no history of substance dependence or major psychiatric disorders. She has not taken any prescription medications, vitamins or herbal supplements that could interfere with the study protocol within the past 2 weeks. She is fluent in English and has a Point of Care Test result for Vitamin D equal to or higher than 20 ng/ml. She is willing to provide voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who complains of fever, headache, and muscle pain for the past 24 hours. She reports no history of chronic diseases or any other health problems, but she is currently 4 months pregnant. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins as prescribed by her obstetrician. Her temperature is 38.5°C, and she has no other significant physical findings. She speaks Spanish fluently and is able to understand the informed consent form provided to her. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial after discussing the study with the research team.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis six months ago. He has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms of UC, including bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and cramping. He has tried corticosteroids, immunomodulators, and TNF-alpha antagonists, but has not had a satisfactory response. He has a Mayo score of 8 with an endoscopic subscore of 3. His UC extends proximal to the rectum, involving more than 15 cm of the colon. He has not undergone any colonic resection or surgical intervention for UC. He has no history of adenomatous colonic polyps or colonic mucosal dysplasia. He has no other major medical conditions, chronic infections, or immunodeficiency. He has not been exposed to vedolizumab or any investigational or approved biologic or biosimilar agents within the past 60 days or 5 half-lives of screening. He is willing to participate in the study and able to attend multiple clinic visits over a period of up to 71 weeks.

This is a 9 year-old child with a confirmed diagnosis of cerebral palsy (CP) and classified as level II according to the Gross Motor Classification System. The child has difficulty with balance, falls frequently and has poor postural control. The child also experiences difficulty with breathing and gets tired easily during physical activity. The child has not undergone any orthopedic surgery or Botox application in the lower extremities in the last 6 months. The child does not have severe uncontrolled convulsions and does not have any congenital malformations accompanying CP. The child is able to follow instructions and participate in physical therapy exercises.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with intermediate relapse-risk stage II prostate cancer. He underwent radiotherapy and hormone therapy for the treatment of prostate cancer within the past 6 months to 5 years. He has been experiencing erectile dysfunction since undergoing treatment and has a history of erectile dysfunction prior to starting cancer therapy. He has no anatomical genital abnormalities or concurrent conditions that would prohibit sexual intercourse or preclude study participation. He is not currently taking sildenafil or any other medication for erectile dysfunction. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to study the effectiveness of sildenafil in treating his erectile dysfunction.

A 52-year-old man was recently diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis after experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain during physical activity. His medical history includes hypertension and high cholesterol. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His cardiologist recommended surgical aortic valve replacement with the INSPIRIS RESILIA Aortic Valve™. He is scheduled to undergo the procedure with or without concomitant root replacement and/or coronary bypass surgery. He is willing to attend yearly follow-up visits at the registry center for up to 5 years and has provided written informed consent for the surgery and participation in the registry.

46 year old female with a long-standing history of high blood pressure, currently taking metoprolol and lisinopril for her hypertension. Despite medication, her blood pressure remains elevated, with readings averaging around 150/90 mmHg. She is concerned about the potential side effects of long-term medication use and is interested in exploring alternative treatment options. She has heard about renal sympathetic denervation using catheter ablation and is willing to participate in a study to determine patient preference. She has no history of illiteracy and is able to complete the written survey.

The patient is a 35-year-old pregnant woman with a BMI of 42. She is scheduled for an elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. She has no history of thromboembolism or liver disease, and she is not on any anticoagulant or anti-platelet therapy. She has been informed about the study and has provided written informed consent to participate. Her preoperative laboratory tests, including a full blood count and clotting profile, are within normal limits. During the surgery, her blood will be sampled for ROTEM analysis at baseline, immediately after the surgery, and 8 hours later. The investigators aim to compare her coagulation status with that of 20 non-obese pregnant women undergoing the same procedure. The study will help determine if the impact of surgery in inducing a hypercoagulable state is more evident in morbidly obese pregnant women than in their non-obese counterparts. The results of this study will help calculate the sample size for a future prospective controlled clinical trial to compare the incidence of hypercoagulability in morbidly obese parturients as opposed to their non-obese counterparts.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of Alzheimer's disease. She has been experiencing memory loss, confusion, and difficulty in performing daily activities for the past year. Her daughter is her primary caregiver and helps with her daily needs. The patient has a valid driving license and drives twice a week to run errands and attend medical appointments. However, her daughter has noticed that her driving skills have declined, and she has been involved in minor accidents in the past few months. The patient is anxious about giving up driving, and her daughter is concerned about her safety on the road. They are both interested in participating in an educational program to learn self-regulation strategies for safe driving and to prepare for a future cessation of driving activity. The patient's Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 22, and she is able to communicate orally and in writing to participate in clinical evaluations and workshops.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently 14 weeks pregnant. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2, which classifies her as overweight. She has no significant past medical history or chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, chronic hypertension, or thyroid diseases, and is not taking any dietary supplements or herbal products that may affect her body weight. She has a singleton pregnancy and is not carrying twins. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial, which involves lifestyle changes such as proper nutrition and regular physical activity. She has been provided with a diet plan that consists of 1500 kcal/day, which includes three main meals and three snacks in a day. She has been advised to engage in moderate physical activity for at least 30 minutes per day, three times a week, which includes walking and other low-impact exercises. She will be monitored throughout the trial to assess changes in her body composition, specifically fat mass and fat-free mass, using a bioimpedance analyzer. Blood samples will also be collected at baseline and at 36-38 weeks to investigate plasma pro- and anti-inflammatory markers related to obesity and visceral adipose tissue. She will attend follow-up visits at 16th, 20th, 28th, and 36th weeks to monitor her progress and adherence to the program.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has been diagnosed with stable angina pectoris and is scheduled for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using a drug-eluting stent (DES). He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. He has no known allergies to aspirin, clopidogrel, prasugrel, heparin, or iodinated contrast agents. He has undergone a recent angiography which revealed a significant stenosis in the left anterior descending artery. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 65 mL/min/1.73 m2 and serum creatinine level is 1.1 mg/dL. He has never undergone hemodialysis and has no history of hemorrhagic complications such as intracranial hemorrhage or gastrointestinal bleeding. He has no plans for surgical treatment after PCI within the next year. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

45-year-old male with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, diagnosed 2 years ago. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. His viral load has been consistently high, and he has not responded to any previous treatments. He is treatment-naïve and has never undergone any liver transplant. He has no co-infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He has not been diagnosed with any autoimmune liver disease or neoplastic disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of double filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP) in conjunction with peginterferon (Peg-IFN) and ribavirin (RBV) combination therapy for HCV genotype 1 patients with high viral load. He meets the eligibility criteria with regards to age, HCV genotype 1, and liver biopsy confirming chronic hepatitis C. He has no anemia, neutropenia or thrombocytopenia, and his serum creatinine level is within normal limits. He has not been diagnosed with any poorly controlled autoimmune diseases, pulmonary diseases, cardiac diseases, psychiatric diseases, neurological diseases, or diabetes mellitus. He is willing to have contraception during the trial period.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who is scheduled for an elective surgery in the pediatric orthopedics department. He has no known sleep disorders, but his parents report that he has difficulty falling asleep at night and often wakes up during the night. He is otherwise healthy with no underlying medical conditions that may affect sleep. He is not taking any medications that may affect sleep, and his renal and liver functions are normal. He does not have any autoimmune diseases or known intolerance to galactose or lactose. He is willing to participate in the study and his parents have provided written informed consent.

A 58 year old male stroke patient is admitted to the inpatient rehabilitation program at Istanbul Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Training and Research Hospital. He has difficulty moving his left arm and experiences severe pain in his left hand. The patient has been diagnosed with complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) after his stroke. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy, pacemaker, skin lesions on his hands, anxiety, sensory or motor aphasia, peripheral nerve injury, hand surgery, or Reynauld disease. The patient's dominant arm is the right arm. His medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He had a right middle cerebral artery thrombosis and has been in the hospital for 10 days. The patient's Brunnstrom stage for the affected arm is stage 3. The spasticity of the upper extremity has been assessed by modified Ashworth scale as grade 2. In CRPS group, CRPS severity scale was performed to evaluate the CRPS severity. This scale includes sensorial, autonomic and motor function. Also, neuropathic pain was assessed by Douleur Neuropathique 4 (DN4) Questionnaire and visual analog scale(VAS). The patient's eligibility for the study will be evaluated based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is an 18-year-old unmarried female college student with a regular menstrual cycle. She has no history of dysmenorrhea or gynecological diseases. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at exploring the pulse manifestation of physiological menstruation. She has given informed consent to have her radial artery sound waves collected using the "Pulse Detection System of Sound Waves" during the second to fourth day of her menstrual cycle and during the 20th to 28th day of the same menstrual cycle. She is currently not pregnant or lactating and has no severe diseases or infectious diseases. She does not have any tremors of her limbs. She studies at Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine and is interested in contributing to the study of traditional Chinese medicine.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma, the most aggressive type of brain tumor. He has undergone surgery to remove as much of the tumor as possible and is currently receiving chemoradiation therapy with temozolomide. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of primary glioblastoma cell lines in identifying new drug targets for the treatment of brain cancer. The patient meets the inclusion criteria as he has been diagnosed with glioblastoma, and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria as he does not have any other types of cancer and is not experiencing a tumor recurrence. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the clinical trial and has provided his informed consent.

A 32-year-old female patient presented with complaints of fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. She has a history of Hepatitis B infection for the past 3 years, which was diagnosed during routine screening for work visa. She was found to be HBeAg positive and her HBV DNA levels were 6 x 10^6 copies/mL. She has been taking clevudine 30mg daily for the past year with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She denies any history of alcohol or drug abuse. Physical examination reveals hepatomegaly and icteric sclera. Her laboratory investigations show elevated ALT levels at 110 IU/L, total bilirubin levels at 3.5 mg/dl, serum albumin levels at 3.8 g/dl, and prothrombin time (INR) at 1.2. Her hemoglobin levels are 12.5 g/dl. The patient is willing to give written informed consent and comply with the study requirements. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use an effective method of contraception during the study and for up to 3 months after the use of study drug ceases.

60 y/o male with a recent diagnosis of prostate cancer. Biopsy revealed stage T2 prostate cancer with a PSA level of 15 and a Gleason score of 7. The patient has no history of pelvic radiotherapy or inflammatory bowel disease. The patient has no hip prosthesis, pins, or screws. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy of a short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy for localized prostate cancer. The patient is willing to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

A 42-year-old female patient is diagnosed with a pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) with a Knosp grade of 4, which is invading the cavernous sinus. She has been experiencing severe headaches, visual disturbances, and fatigue for the past few months. She has no history of hypertension or any other underlying medical conditions. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not received any monoclonal antibody therapies in the past. She is scheduled to undergo transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) for the removal of the tumor. The patient has a WHO performance status of 1. She has been informed about the clinical trial and has given her written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old experienced alpinist who has previously climbed mountain peaks up to 5000 meters in height. He is in good health and has no history of heart, respiratory or kidney failure. He is not pregnant. The patient has no prior acclimatization and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled protocol to investigate the effectiveness of osteopathic manual medicine (OMM) and/or a 10 cmH2O end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) in preventing acute mountain sickness (AMS). The patient is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol. The patient has not undergone any osteopathic treatment in the past.

The patient is a 28 year-old male with a diagnosis of cerebral palsy. The patient has mild spastic diplegia, which mainly affects the lower limbs. He is able to walk with the assistance of a walker but has difficulty with balance and coordination. He has no previous history of using dalfampridine or any other medication for his condition. The patient is able to perform all the required study procedures and is able to fully extend and flex both hands. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 25-year-old woman arrives at the pediatric clinic with her 8-month-old son for a well-child visit. She is a single mother and works part-time as a waitress to support herself and her baby. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been taking medication for the past year. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. She had an unplanned pregnancy and did not receive preconception care before becoming pregnant. She is interested in learning about birth control options for the future and improving her overall health.

The patient is a 67-year-old male who has been previously diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and has undergone treatment with a hypomethylating agent (HMA) four times, but has not responded to the treatment. He is classified as intermediate 1-risk or high risk according to the international prognostic scoring system (IPSS). The patient has also been diagnosed with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) and acute myeloblastic leukemia (AML), both of which were previously treated with HMA, but he is unfit for intensive chemotherapy. The patient has undergone a recent baseline bone marrow examination, including cytogenetics, and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status of 2. The patient has normal liver and kidney function, with a total bilirubin level less than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT and AST levels less than 3 times ULN, and creatinine levels less than 2.5 times ULN. The patient is willing and able to comply with the protocol requirements and has signed informed consent. The patient is practicing an acceptable method of contraception, and a negative serum test for pregnancy was obtained within 72 hours prior to the start of investigational product. The patient has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to HMAs, and is not actively receiving any other anticancer therapy. The patient has a corrected QT (QTc) (Fridericia Correction Formula) less than or equal to 480 on electrocardiogram (ECG), and has normal electrolyte levels or can have them normalized with standard intervention on the day of treatment with study drug. The patient is not infected with hepatitis B, C or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and is not currently taking systemic treatment with either corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications. The patient has controlled hypertension (HTN) with a blood pressure level less than or equal to 160/90.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic low back pain due to a herniated disc. She had undergone surgery in the past but the pain persisted. She had a Medtronic rechargeable neurostimulation system implanted for pain management, and it has been in place for 3 months. She takes acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain relief. She is fluent in English and is able to provide signed and dated informed consent. She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures, including diary completion and visits. She is able to differentiate between pain associated with her back condition and other types of pain. She is not currently enrolled or planning to enroll in any other clinical studies that could potentially confound the study results. She is not pregnant and uses a medically acceptable form of birth control. She has no untreated major psychiatric comorbidity.

A 65-year-old male patient with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the gastroenterology clinic with mild epigastric discomfort. He did not report any weight loss, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, or change in bowel habits. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, liver function tests, and amylase and lipase levels, were within normal limits. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed a 2 cm cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas. The patient was referred for EUS with fine-needle aspiration (FNA) for further evaluation. EUS revealed a cystic lesion in the pancreas with septations and solid components. FNA was performed, and cystic fluid was obtained for cytokines analysis. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the role of cytokines levels in characterizing pancreatic cysts.

62 y/o male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral artery disease (PAD) presents with intermittent claudication in the left lower extremity. His ankle-brachial index (ABI) is measured at 0.5, indicating moderate to severe PAD. He has no current major medical problems or vasoactive medications, and is interested in participating in the Contrast Ultrasound Perfusion Imaging in PAD with Sonazoid clinical trial. The patient has no known allergies to ultrasound contrast agents, has not undergone previous limb amputation, and is not pregnant. The patient is a Rutherford class 3, indicating moderate claudication with walking up to 2 blocks before experiencing pain. He is compliant with his current medications and is interested in participating in the study to help further research in PAD diagnosis and treatment.

A 35-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with concerns about her weight and related health risks. She reports a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and a family history of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Despite attempts at diet and exercise, she has been unable to lose weight. She is interested in exploring options for weight loss and reducing her cardiometabolic risk factors. The patient is generally healthy with no major medical conditions or medication use. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of liquid meal replacements (LMRs) as a tool for weight loss and improving cardiometabolic risk factors.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has never had a transvaginal ultrasound before. She was referred by her gynecologist for further evaluation of an ovarian cyst. She feels anxious and worried about the procedure, as she has heard that it can be uncomfortable and painful. She lives with her partner and has two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading and hiking in her free time. She has never had any major health issues and does not take any regular medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in the research and hopes that the humanized service program will make her feel more comfortable and less anxious during the transvaginal ultrasound procedure.

A 45-year-old male with metastatic colon cancer presents with recurrent disease after initial definitive treatment. His performance status (ECOG) is 1. He has completed systemic chemotherapy but has not responded well to it. He has no prior radiation therapy. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory results are as follows: Absolute neutrophil count: 4,000/mm3; Platelets: 200,000/mm3; Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL; Calcium: 9.2 mg/dL; Total Bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL; AST: 48 U/L; ALT: 42 U/L; PT: 12 seconds; aPTT: 32 seconds. CT imaging shows multiple liver metastases and peritoneal carcinomatosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who was diagnosed with partial epilepsy 3 years ago. She experiences seizures on average twice a week despite being on multiple anti-convulsant medications. The seizures are characterized by a sudden loss of consciousness, followed by jerking movements of the arms and legs. She has tried two different anti-convulsant regimens in the past, but neither has been successful in controlling her seizures. She has no history of allergies or any other medical conditions. She is not pregnant and does not have any metal implants in her head. She has not been taking any neuroleptic or antidepressant medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with TMS. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 4-month-old infant presented to the clinic with a history of a persistent cough, which started 10 days ago. The cough is episodic, occurring in spells of 5-10 coughs, followed by a high-pitched inspiratory whoop. The child has had no fever, and the cough is more prominent at night. The infant has had all recommended vaccinations up to date, including the pertussis vaccine. The family has no history of chronic lung disease or immunodeficiency disorders. The infant is gaining weight appropriately and has no other symptoms. The physician suspects whooping cough and has recommended the infant to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of the pertussis vaccine used in Ivory Coast. The parents have given written consent for the infant to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer with metastasis to the liver, lymph nodes, and bones has been experiencing fatigue with a severity level of 6 out of 10 on the ESAS scale for the past 2 weeks. He is currently receiving chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He has a history of smoking and quit 6 months ago. He reports no other significant medical history. He is married and has two adult children. He lives with his wife in their own house. He retired from his job as a construction worker last year. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and has not been regularly exercising for the past year. His HADS score is 17, indicating no significant anxiety or depression. He speaks and understands English fluently. He has a life expectancy of at least 6 months as per his oncologist. His hemoglobin level is normal at 12 g/L.

Patient is a child between the ages of 8-10 with parent-reported difficulties in emotion regulation, as indicated by a score of 10 or higher on the total difficulties score on the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). The child must be fluent in English and not currently participating in another mental health intervention. The trial will randomly assign the child to receive either the Purrble, an interactive plush toy, or an active control (non-interactive plush toy). The primary outcome will be a daily measure of the child's emotion regulation capability, as reported by the parent, over a period of 4 weeks. The trial will be conducted in an enriched non-clinical US population, and a proportion of families will be interviewed post-deployment as part of process analysis.

32-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks gestation, presenting to the labor and delivery unit with contractions every 5 minutes and cervical dilation of 3 cm. She has a history of uncomplicated vaginal delivery and desires epidural labor analgesia for pain management during labor. The patient has no significant medical history, no allergies to local anesthetics, and no contraindications to epidural anesthesia. She reports a pain level of 8 out of 10 on the Numerical Rating Scale and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has no significant medical history and is currently in overall good health. She does not have any known allergies to medications or materials such as rubber. She has not previously experienced any severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions. She is not currently taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, or herbal supplements. She has not experienced any seizures or blackouts in the past. She has no history of any clinically significant cardiac, endocrinologic, hematologic, hepatic, immunologic, metabolic, urologic, pulmonary, neurologic, dermatologic, psychiatric, renal, and/or other major diseases. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to give informed consent. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing coughing and difficulty swallowing for the past month. He reports a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and has been taking proton-pump inhibitors for the past year. He denies any fever, chills, or recent weight loss. A chest X-ray shows no abnormalities, but a subsequent bronchoscopy reveals a benign tracheoesophageal fistula. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is interested in participating. He has no history of malignancy, is not currently on mechanical ventilation, and does not have any other clinical risk factors. He is not immunosuppressed nor has any local inflammatory process at fistulas borders.

Patient is a 35yo male who presents with a cold, runny nose, and nasal congestion. He reports moderate to severe symptoms, with a Jackson score of 5. He has not used any nasal wash products in the past 3 days and is not currently taking any medication for his symptoms. He does not have a history of allergies to seafood or any of the components of the products being studied. The patient is able to follow the guidelines of the medical device and has given his written informed consent to participate in the study. He has not participated in any other clinical studies in the past 30 days.

The patient is a 10-year-old child with Angle's class II division I malocclusion due to mandibular retrusion. The child's parents have given written consent for participation in the clinical trial. The child does not have mandibular shifts, severe crowding, anterior open bite, posterior crossbite, or any peri-oral habits. The child has not received any previous orthodontic or orthopaedic treatments.

A 30-year-old pregnant woman who is expecting twins is experiencing a short cervix (less than or equal to 25mm) between 20-28 weeks of gestation. She has no history of preterm labor or cervical incompetence. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medication. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has a supportive partner and is eagerly looking forward to the birth of her twins. She is covered by health insurance in France and is willing to participate in the study. She has no symptoms of infection, and her urine culture, CRP, and blood white cell count are within normal limits. She has no contraindications for pessary placement and is willing to accept follow-up.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of hypertension presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit. She has been struggling with medication adherence and has had difficulty tracking her blood pressure readings at home. She also reports feeling overwhelmed with managing her condition and would like to be more involved in her care. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could provide her with a tool to better track her health and communicate with her healthcare team. Her blood pressure readings at the clinic today are 150/90 mmHg. She is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and reports occasional headaches and dry cough as side effects. She has a family history of hypertension and heart disease. The patient is motivated to take control of her health and is willing to learn new skills to help manage her condition.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who serves in the military and works as a mechanic. He reports experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months, which he attributes to the physical demands of his job. He rates his pain as a 5 out of 10 on average, but it can increase to an 8 out of 10 after prolonged periods of standing, bending, or lifting heavy objects. He denies any radiating pain, numbness, or weakness in his legs. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they only provide temporary relief. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the SBST can help him manage his low back pain and prevent chronic disability. He is able to attend regular treatment sessions and can speak and understand English.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from Denmark who works as a software engineer. He has a BMI of 24 and exercises 3-4 times a week. He has never smoked and has no history of chronic diseases or regular medication use. He consumes alcohol occasionally and does not exceed the maximum recommended intake. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of different trout feeding regimes on cardiovascular risk markers. He understands that he cannot donate blood during the study and is willing to adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and mild obesity. The patient is scheduled to undergo an elective craniotomy for aneurysm clipping. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiology physical status of 2. The patient's BMI is 24.5 kg/m2. The patient has no history of renal, cardiovascular, or hepatic insufficiency. The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) is 15. The patient has no known allergies to study drugs. The patient is not currently breastfeeding or pregnant. The patient does not have preoperative epilepsy.

The patient is an adult male or female between the ages of 18 and 90 who has been experiencing chronic back pain due to facet joint osteoarthritis. They have had a positive diagnostic facet pain block with lignocaine and have stable analgesic regimen during the 4 weeks prior to enrollment. The patient must have a worst pain of at least 40 at any time during the preceding week (based on scale of 0 to 100, with 100 representing "pain as bad as you can imagine") using Visual Analog Scale (VAS). They should be free of local or intra-articular infection, tumor or other causes of localized LBP, for example Including spondylolysis/pars defect, and adjacent vertebral body compression fracture based on MRI evaluation. The patient must also have suitable facet joint anatomy for intra-articular injection and be willing and able to return for follow-up visits. They should be able to reliably provide pain assessment and be able to read and understand study instructions, and willing and able to comply with all study procedures. The patient should not have hypersensitivity, allergy, or significant reaction to any ingredient of the study drug, including double-stranded DNA, mannose, and sucrose. They should not have any high peri-operative risks that would preclude a safe facet joint injection procedure. They should not have a history of immunosuppressive therapy or be currently receiving systemic chemotherapy or radiation therapy for malignancy. The patient should not have clinically significant hepatic disease or severe anemia. They should not have a significant neuropsychiatric condition that would interfere with study participation. The patient should not be currently treated with systemic antibiotics or antivirals, anticoagulants, other than low-dose aspirin, or any investigational drug or device within 1 month before enrollment or current participation in a trial that included intervention with a drug or device; or currently participating in an investigational drug or device study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with heart failure 2 years ago. She has been on medication and has been managing her condition well. However, her cardiologist recently recommended an Automatic Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (AICD) due to the risk of sudden cardiac arrest. She is feeling anxious and overwhelmed at the thought of the procedure and the implications of having an AICD. She wants to learn more about the device and how to manage her stress and anxiety related to it. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. She does not have any language or cognitive barriers that would prevent her from understanding the study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy, anti-VEGF therapy, and anti-EGFR therapy. However, he is now no longer a candidate for these therapies. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has adequate renal, bone marrow, liver, and pancreatic functions, with an estimated creatinine clearance of 45 mL/min and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. His total bilirubin level is within normal limits, and his ALAT and ASAT levels are 2.5 x ULN. He has no history of cardiac problems or thrombotic events. He has a target lesion on CT scan and has no contraindication to Iodine contrast media injection during CT. He has registered in a national health care system. He has signed and dated informed consent and has a negative pregnancy test result. He is not breastfeeding or pregnant. He is willing to use adequate contraception during and at least 8 weeks after the last study drug administration. He has no history of HIV infection, active hepatitis B or C, or chronic hepatitis B or C requiring treatment with antiviral therapy. He has no history of organ allograft, seizure disorder requiring medication, or interstitial lung disease with ongoing signs or symptoms at the time of inclusion. He is able to swallow oral medication and has no malabsorption condition. He is not on any chronic treatment potentially interacting with the study medication.

Maria is a 28 year old sexually active woman who came to the gynecologist with a complaint of vaginal itching and burning sensation. She has been experiencing these symptoms for a week, and this is the first time she has had such symptoms. She denies any history of sexually transmitted infections or vaginal infections. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has been using hormonal contraceptives for the past 2 years. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Physical examination revealed erythema and white discharge in the vulvovaginal area. KOH wet mount examination confirmed the diagnosis of acute vulvovaginal candidiasis. The gynecologist prescribed a standard treatment with clotrimazole 500 single dose, which she agreed to take. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent sheet.

A 35-year-old female from Pakistan who speaks Urdu as her primary language and has no current chronic health problems such as chronic allergy, back pain, visual impairments, chronic skin problems, chronic lung problems, deafness or hearing problems, functional impairment in leg or arm or other chronic health problems. The patient is willing to participate in a study aimed at developing a Urdu version of the Short Form 36 Health Questionnaire. The patient is not currently experiencing any physical or mental health issues and falls within the age range of 20 to 60 years.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss for the past few months. He recently visited his primary care physician and underwent several tests including imaging studies which revealed a mass in his liver. Further evaluation confirmed the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. He has no previous history of cancer and has not received any cancer treatment in the past. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and he has Child-Pugh Cirrhotic Status A with a score of 7. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication with a reading of 130/80 mmHg. He has no history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy. He has not undergone any major surgical procedures or sustained any significant traumatic injuries in the past 28 days. He has not received any anti-angiogenic therapy or E7050 anti-cmet in the past. He has no brain metastases or clinically significant gastrointestinal bleeding.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with a history of cutaneous T cell lymphoma. He has tried several treatments including topical, phototherapy, and interferon, but his disease has progressed and is now refractory to these treatments. He presents with multiple erythematous plaques and nodules on his skin, which have been increasing in size and number over the past few months. He also reports experiencing itching, pain, and fatigue. His vital signs are within normal limits. He has no history of deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or hypersensitivity to thalidomide. His laboratory tests show adequate organ function, including liver, renal, and hematologic parameters. He is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and the requirements of the RevAssist® program. He is not currently receiving any other experimental drug or therapy and has not received chemotherapy or vorinostat in the past 3 months. He has not previously used lenalidomide. He has no active viral infections with HIV, HBV or HCV. He is expected to have a survival of > 6 months and is able to take aspirin daily as prophylactic anticoagulation. He does not have neuropathy greater than grade 2.

55-year-old male with no history of allergic reactions to vaccines or egg products, previously received 2 doses of clade 1 A/H5N1 vaccine derived from A/H5N1/VN/1203/04 as part of DMID Protocol No. 04-076. The patient is in good health, with a blood pressure of 125/85 mmHg, a heart rate of 70 bpm, and an oral temperature of 98.6°F. The patient is not immunosuppressed, has no active neoplastic disease, and has not received immunoglobulin or another blood product within the last 3 months. The patient has not received any vaccines within the last 2 weeks or plans to receive another vaccine within the next 28 days. The patient does not have any acute or chronic medical condition that would render vaccination unsafe or interfere with the evaluation of responses. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period and is able to understand and comply with the planned study procedures. The patient has provided informed consent prior to any study procedures.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who presents to the emergency room with a chief complaint of cough and shortness of breath for the past week. He reports that he has been feeling fatigued and has had a low-grade fever. The patient has a past medical history of asthma and has been using inhalers for the past 10 years. He reports that his asthma has been well-controlled until recently. He denies any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. On physical examination, the patient appears to be in mild respiratory distress with a respiratory rate of 22 breaths/minute. He has diffuse wheezing on lung auscultation. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. The patient is able to speak in complete sentences. His laboratory studies show a normal complete blood count and metabolic panel. The patient speaks English fluently and has been living in Guyana for the past 5 years.

Patient A is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Tourette syndrome by a psychiatrist. She has been experiencing multiple motor and vocal tics for the past 5 years, which have been significantly affecting her daily life. Her current medication regimen includes clonidine, which has not provided significant relief from her symptoms. She has no other comorbid psychiatric or medical conditions, and her IQ is within the normal range. She is currently using a reliable method of birth control and is willing to participate in an HMPAO SPECT scan at baseline and after 4 weeks of treatment. She has not made any recent changes to her medication or behavioral treatment for Tourette syndrome. She is interested in participating in the trial to see if EPI-743 can help alleviate her tic symptoms.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cervical dysplasia. She has a history of irregular Pap smears and has undergone colposcopy in the past. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy in the near future. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her family history is negative for any cancers. She is fluent in English and has no language difficulties. She has been referred to Vancouver General Hospital for a loop electrocautery excision procedure (LEEP) and has given informed consent for her tissue samples to be used in this clinical trial.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has a history of ankle sprain that occurred 2 years ago while playing basketball with her friends. She experienced pain, swelling and difficulty walking for a few days after the injury. Although the symptoms improved with rest and ice, she has been experiencing recurrent feelings of instability in her ankle and occasional pain during physical activity. She has not had any surgeries or fractures to her lower extremities. She has not experienced any acute injuries to her lower extremities in the past month. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effects of different taping techniques on chronic ankle instability.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman with myopia who is interested in undergoing refractive surgery to correct her vision. She has a prescription of -4.00 diopters in both eyes and has up to 2.50 diopters of astigmatism. She has no history of eye diseases or autoimmune disorders, and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She has had a comprehensive eye examination that included computerized videokeratography and has been deemed a suitable candidate for the study. She understands that one eye will undergo SMILE surgery and the other eye will undergo LASIK surgery, and that she will be followed up for one year after the procedures. She will receive topical antibiotics and steroids, and is willing to comply with the study's requirements.

A 27-year-old woman presented to the hospital at 28 weeks of gestation with premature rupture of membranes and preterm labor. She had regular prenatal care with no significant medical history. Her pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes, which was managed with diet modification. She received corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity and magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection. The baby was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to fetal distress. The baby weighed 1,100 grams and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) within 7 days after birth. The baby had no major congenital anomalies and was eligible for the study. The baby received standard neonatal care and was enrolled in the collaborative quality improvement program to improve outcomes for very preterm infants. The baby was closely monitored for any major morbidities and was followed up regularly for the duration of the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent a partial medial meniscectomy 8 months ago and continues to experience knee pain with a KOOS pain score of 70. He has neutral alignment within ±5º of the mechanical axis and at least 2 mm of intact medial meniscal rim that can support the NUsurface® Meniscus Implant. He is able to participate in the study-required follow-up visits, questionnaires, X-rays, and MRI's and can read and understand the English language. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to provide informed consent. There is no evidence of Outerbridge Grade IV cartilage loss on the medial tibial plateau or femoral condyle, complete disruption of the posterior root attachment of the meniscus, lateral compartment pain and Grade III or Grade IV Outerbridge cartilage score in the lateral compartment, varus or valgus knee deformity > 5º requiring a tibial or femoral osteotomy, laxity level of more than Grade II (IKDC), significant trochlear dysplasia, patellar instability, symptomatic patellar misalignment, or patellar compartment pain and Grade III or Grade IV Outerbridge cartilage score in the patellar compartment. The patient has no obvious radiological evidence of medial femoral squaring, anatomical variance in the medial tibial plateau, or irregularly shaped cartilage surface compared to a normal knee. The patient has a BMI ≤ 32.5 at the start of study treatment, and has no history of ACL reconstruction performed < 9 months prior to study treatment, or any previous medial femoral condyle surgery (not including microfracture) or High Tibial Osteotomy (HTO). The patient has no insufficiency fractures or avascular necrosis of the medial compartment, active infection or tumor (local or systemic), any type of knee joint inflammatory disease including Sjogren's syndrome, neuropathic knee osteoarthropathy, also known as Charcot joint, or any medical condition that does not allow possible arthroscopy of the knee. The patient is not currently involved in another investigation of the lower extremity, does not anticipate having another lower extremity surgery during the study period, and is not contraindicated for hyaluronic acid injections or corticosteroid injections. The patient does not have chondrocalcinosis, is not on immunostimulating or immunosuppressing agents. The patient has no ipsilateral or contralateral lower limb joint conditions that may affect ambulation or KOOS, is not a female who is lactating, expecting, or is intending to become pregnant during the study period, is not an active smoker, is not mentally incapacitated or have mental disability, is not a prisoner and does not have economic incentive not to improve. Finally, the patient does not have any co-morbidity that reduces life expectancy to less than 36 months and is not contraindicated for MRI (i.e., pacemaker, defibrillator, cochlear implants, etc.).

A 28-year-old woman gave birth to her first child 3 months ago. She has been feeling sad and hopeless for the past few weeks and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She often feels fatigued and struggles to fall asleep at night. She has not sought any treatment for these symptoms. She is fluent in English and has no history of substance abuse or mental illness. She is interested in participating in the study to receive help for her postpartum depression symptoms.

Patient is a 55-year-old male who presents to the clinic complaining of chest pain that started 2 hours ago. He has no previous history of cardiovascular disease, chronic renal disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or malignancy. He is not on any regular medications, including statins, antiplatelets, or anticoagulants. His BMI is 35, and he is a smoker. His blood pressure is 145/95 mmHg, and his heart rate is 85 beats per minute. His electrocardiography and echocardiography show no findings related to previous myocardial infarction, and his coronary angiography shows a critical stenosis in the left anterior descending coronary artery. He is able to communicate orally with the healthcare provider. He will be eligible to participate in the study as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who presented to the clinic with a painful rash on his left torso. He was diagnosed with herpes zoster and started valacyclovir hydrochloride treatment within 48 hours of onset of the rash. However, the pain and rash continued to worsen despite the treatment. He has no history of other significant medical conditions but is currently taking medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no history of cancer or immunosuppressive therapy. He is able to take oral medications and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 26-year-old pregnant woman with a singleton pregnancy at 39 weeks gestation. The patient has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications and is currently in active labor. The patient has no history of preterm labor or fetal anomalies. The patient has consented to participate in the clinical trial comparing the AN24 fetal monitoring device marketed by Monica Healthcare to the newer device, Novii. The patient is willing to have both devices placed on her abdomen during labor and agrees to have data abstracted from the second device after delivery. The patient is not scheduled for an imminent cesarean section.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases, which were detected at the time of the primary tumor resection. The patient has undergone standard chemotherapy protocol (FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, Capecitabine) and is still experiencing liver metastases. The patient has 2-8 metastases, and one metastasis is accessible for electrochemotherapy, which will be performed during the primary tumor operation. The metastases will be resected 2-3 months after the primary tumor resection. The patient's liver metastases are not more than 3 cm in diameter. The patient has a life expectancy of more than three months and a performance status of Karnofsky ≥ 70 or (World Health Organization) WHO ≥ 2. The patient is mentally capable of understanding the information provided and has given informed consent. The patient's coagulation is normal, and the patient has not shown any allergic reactions to bleomycin or received a cumulative dose of 250 mg/m2. The patient does not have impaired kidney function (creatinin > 150 µmol/l), nor does the patient have heart failure or a pacemaker. The patient does not have epilepsy or secondary primary tumors, except surgically treated noninvasive cancer of the cervix or surgically or irradiated basal cell carcinoma. The patient is eligible for the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with MPS I. He has been experiencing learning difficulties at school and has declined noticeably in his cognitive function over the past year. He is currently being treated with Aldurazyme® therapy, but has only been on this treatment for four months. The patient and his parents are willing and able to comply with study procedures, including written and computer-based testing as well as lying still in an MRI scanner for at least 40 minutes without sedation. The patient has not undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and does not have any medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is not pregnant or lactating and is not considering pregnancy. The patient has no contraindication for MRI and has normal spinal CSF flow.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of metastatic colon cancer. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not responded well to treatment. The patient has an ECOG score of 2 and ROBO1 expression detected in malignant tissues by immuno-histochemistry (IHC). Laboratory examination showed white blood cell count of 4 x 10*9/L, blood platelet count of 80 x 10*9/L, hemoglobin of 100g/L, lymphocyte count of 20%, total bilirubin of 90 mol/L, ALT and AST within normal limits and serum creatinine within normal limits. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 6 months and is willing to provide informed consent. The patient is willing to practice birth control after 2 weeks following the cell transfusion if required.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled for an elective surgery. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications regularly. She has a history of mild anxiety and nervousness before medical procedures. The patient does not suffer from any psychiatric or neurological diseases and does not have hearing or speech disorders. She does not use any psychiatric drugs or have a history of chronic alcohol use. She is currently working as a teacher and has had a good support system from her family and friends. She is excited to participate in the clinical trial to help improve the understanding and management of preoperative anxiety.

55 yo F with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents with sudden onset of dyspnea and chest pain. Patient was found to have acute left heart failure with pulmonary congestion and was intubated for mechanical ventilation. After 24 hours, the patient passed spontaneous breathing trials and is now ready for extubation. The patient's next of kin agrees to participate in a clinical trial comparing high flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) and non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for patients with acute left heart failure after extubation. The patient has no history of COPD, disturbance of consciousness, bulbar paralysis, dysphagia, facial deformity, or terminal tumor. The patient is eligible for the study and will be randomly assigned to either the HFNO group or NIV group.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been living with HIV-1 for the past 5 years. He has been taking ART and his HIV-1 plasma RNA level has been below 50 copies/mL for the past 6 months. He does not have any active systemic infections, except for HIV-1, and has tested negative for hepatitis B and C. He has not experienced anaphylaxis to other monoclonal antibodies and has not received any vaccination, immunomodulators, HIV vaccine, or systemic chemotherapy within the past 8 weeks. He is not currently pregnant or lactating and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. He has a body weight of 70 kg.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary Sjögren's syndrome based on the American-European Consensus Group 2002 and/or the American College of rheumatology (ACR) and the European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) 2016 classification criteria. She complains of dry eyes, dry mouth, fatigue, and joint pain. She has been taking hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) for at least three months as part of her treatment. She denies having any other autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, demato/polymyositis, mixed connective tissue disease, spondyloarthritis, primary biliary cholangitis, or autoimmune hepatitis. She has not received radiotherapy of the head and neck and has negative serologies for HIV, hepatitis B and C, sarcoidosis, graft versus host disease, and IgG4-related disease. She is not taking any medication that can interact with HCQ or interfere in HCQ blood levels. She does not have alcoholism, current infections, liver or heart failure, dialysis, or severe chronic renal failure (serum creatinine ≥3 mg/dL). She is not pregnant. She is willing to participate in the study and will sign the Free and Informed Consent Term (ICF).

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and is receiving oral antiplatelet therapy as a key treatment. He has never taken Clopidogrel, Prasugrel, or Ticagrelor before. He has no history of allergies to paracetamol, Prasugrel or Ticagrelor. He is currently fasting for at least 6 hours and has not taken any drugs that could alter gastric emptying times, such as calcium antagonists, alimentary tract treatments, opioid analgesics, tricyclic antidepressants, or antibiotics. He does not have any conditions or pathologies that could alter gastric emptying times, such as thyroid dysfunction, chronic renal failure, Parkinson's disease, scleroderma, amyloidosis, gastrointestinal disease, malignancy, advanced psychiatric or neurological disease. He is not experiencing vomiting and does not have cardiogenic shock, ventricular arrhythmia or resuscitated cardiac arrest, hepatic insufficiency, or severe respiratory disease. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He weighs between 65 and 85 kg and is affiliated with a social security system. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who presents to the clinic with sudden onset of visual impairment in his right eye. He reports that his vision became blurry over a period of a few hours and the next morning he woke up with complete loss of vision in his right eye. He also reports having a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. Upon examination, his visual acuity is worse than 20/64 in the affected eye. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He has not received any treatment for his vision loss.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 8 and a PSA level of 25 ng/ml. He has undergone radical radiation therapy and has been treated with LHRH agonist as part of the PCS IV clinical trial. However, he has experienced biochemical failure (PSA nadir + 2) or has completed a minimum of 3 years of follow-up post hormonal therapy. He is considered a high-risk patient due to the advanced stage of his cancer (T3 or T4). The patient is willing to participate in the study to assess DNA changes in high-risk prostate cancer to determine prognosis. Tumor blocks will be collected and analyzed to determine the presence of TMPRSS2-ERG gene fusion and PTEN deletion to determine the risk of recurrence and treatment failure.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a diagnosis of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient's HCC was diagnosed on the basis of biopsy and radiologic findings. The patient has no prior history of cancer and is in good general health. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not received any local therapy for HCC. The patient has adequate organ function, including liver function, renal function, and hematologic function. The patient has no known history of cardiac disease, serious myocardial dysfunction, active, clinically serious infections, or CNS tumors. The patient has no history of clinically significant gastrointestinal bleeding within the past 30 days. The patient is willing to comply with study requirements and provide written informed consent.

50-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was admitted to the medical-surgical ICU after experiencing respiratory distress. The patient has been on mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours and is currently using an alternating-pressure air mattress (APAM). The patient's weight is within the accepted limits for the mattress. The patient or their legal representative has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have a pressure ulcer upon ICU admission and is not pregnant. The patient will be randomized to either a 2-hour or 4-hour turning regimen to assess the effectiveness of postural turnings on preventing pressure ulcers (PU) grade ≥ II in patients in ICU on mechanical ventilation ≥ 24h that use APAMs. The patient's efficacy and safety will be monitored throughout the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been diagnosed with ADHD. She has been on stimulant medication for the past 6 months but is willing to discontinue the medication 2 days prior to the experiment. She is a freelance writer and spends most of her time working on her laptop at home. She is physically active and enjoys going for a run every morning. She has no history of epilepsy or any metallic implants. She has never been pregnant nor is she currently nursing. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatments for her ADHD symptoms. She is fluent in English and has no difficulty in understanding and following the instructions. She has never undergone tDCS before and is excited to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 3 years ago. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a as a disease-modifying therapy. She experiences gait instability and fatigue, which limits her mobility and ability to perform daily activities. She can walk with the assistance of a single cane but finds it challenging to walk long distances. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her walking ability and overall quality of life. She has no significant medical history except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiac or respiratory failure. She is able to give informed consent and willing to follow the study procedures.

8 year-old male with a history of dental caries and anxiety during dental visits. He has been recommended for dental care under MEOPA (a combination of nitrous oxide and oxygen) to manage his anxiety during the procedure. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in the study and have no objections. The patient does not have any difficulties with tracking and is available for follow-up appointments. The patient's parents have full parental authority and are not divorced or divorcing. The patient's dental condition is such that dental care can be performed under MEOPA and does not require general anesthesia.

The patient is a 55-year-old post-menopausal woman who has been experiencing symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy (VVA) for the past year. She complains of vaginal dryness, itching, and discomfort during sexual intercourse. She has not had any procedures in the genital area for at least 6 months prior to the treatment. The patient has no history of reconstructive pelvic surgery or any serious chronic condition that could interfere with the study compliance. She is a non-smoker with a normal pelvic organ prolapse quantification (ICS-POP- Q) system of < II. She has not used vaginal creams, moisturizers, lubricants or homeopathic preparations for at least 3 months. The patient has no history of thrombophlebitis, acute infections, or heart failure. She is not taking any antiplatelets, anticoagulants, thrombolytics, vitamin E or anti-inflammatories within 2 weeks pre-treatment. The patient has no medical condition that, in the investigator's opinion, would interfere with her participation in the study. She is not taking any medications that are photosensitive and has no history of keloid formation. The patient is willing and able to attend all scheduled follow-up visits.

A 45 year old woman with a history of obesity and high blood pressure presents to the clinic.
