She has been struggling with her weight for several years and has tried various diets and exercise programs without much success. Her blood pressure has been poorly controlled despite taking multiple medications prescribed by her primary care physician. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help her manage her blood pressure and improve her overall health. She is otherwise in good health, with no significant medical history or other chronic conditions.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). She has been on stable doses of metformin and pioglitazone for at least 8 weeks and has adequate glycemic control with HbA1c levels below 9.5%. She is considered overweight, with a BMI of 28 kg/m2. The patient is currently not taking any weight loss medication and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the previous 3 months. She has no underlying chronic liver disease, allergies, or hypersensitivity to target medication or its components. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is aware of the study procedure, alternatives, and risks and voluntarily agrees to participate by giving written informed consent.

42 year old male with a history of spinal cord injury resulting in neurogenic para-osteo-arthropathy, with limited range of motion and significant pain in his hips and knees. He has been experiencing difficulty with mobility and activities of daily living, despite physical therapy and pain management. The patient is being evaluated for surgical excision of the heterotopic ossification and has been recommended to undergo pre-operative CT scan and MRI with contrast. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no contraindications to contrast injection or imaging exams. The patient has no history of cardiac stimulator or metallic intraocular foreign bodies, and is not currently participating in any other interventional study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who recently tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection. He was admitted to the hospital due to difficulty breathing and low oxygen saturation levels. The patient requires supplemental oxygen to maintain oxygen saturation levels above 94%. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril for blood pressure control. The patient has not received any antiviral medications, antibiotics, or other treatments for COVID-19. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman has been concerned about the wrinkles around her eyes for the past year. She has tried various skin care products but did not find any improvement. She has no history of neurological conditions or muscle weakness. She has not participated in any clinical trial involving RT001 before. She is in good general health and is willing to follow study instructions. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy during the study but is a woman of child-bearing potential and is willing to use an effective method of birth control. She has moderate to severe lateral canthal lines (crow's feet wrinkles) which she hopes to improve through this clinical trial.

A 57-year-old Caucasian man presents with blurred vision in his left eye. He reports that his vision has been gradually deteriorating over the past few months. He denies any eye pain, redness, or discharge. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which he controls with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in the left eye is currently 20/80. Ophthalmologic examination reveals the presence of polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV) in the left eye. He has not received any intravitreal treatment in the past. He meets the age criteria for the study and is a suitable candidate for the intravitreal injection of aflibercept. He does not have a history of diabetic retinopathy or eye surgery within the past 3 months. He is interested in participating in the study to receive treatment for his PCV and improve his visual acuity.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and has decided to undergo in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment. This will be her first IVF cycle. She has no history of multiple pregnancies or any underlying medical conditions that may affect her fertility. She is a resident of Belgium and has a Belgian insurance number. She is aware of the legally enforced embryo transfer policy in Belgium and is willing to comply with the restrictions on the number of embryos transferred. She meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for this study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery due to ischemic heart disease. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. He does not have any history of neurological or psychiatric diseases. He has no family history of dementia or Alzheimer's disease. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a 45yo male with a history of chronic Hepatitis E virus infection confirmed by positive HEV RNA at least 3 months before Screening and positive for HEV RNA at the time of Screening. The patient has a documented previous ribavirin therapy or a documented contraindication for full dose (≥ 600mg qd) ribavirin monotherapy for at least 3 months. The patient has a BMI of 22 kg/m2, normal ECG, and laboratory parameters at screening: platelets ≥ 60,000/μL, INR ≤2.0 x ULN, HbA1c ≤ 10%, and creatinine clearance (CLcr) ≥ 30 mL/min. The patient has not been treated with any investigational drug or device within 42 days of the Screening visit and has a negative serum pregnancy test. The patient has not had clinically-relevant drug or alcohol abuse within 12 months of screening and is not on any prohibited concomitant medications within 21 days of the Baseline/Day 1 visit. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to SOF or formulation excipients. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent, able to comply with the dosing instructions for study drug administration, and able to complete the study schedule of assessments.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx. Despite undergoing standard platinum-based chemotherapy, his cancer has progressed, and he is now considered incurable with standard therapy. He has not received treatment with EGFr antibodies or EGFr small molecule inhibitors in the past. He has a past history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications except for occasional over-the-counter pain relief. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 35-year-old female marketing executive recently noticed that her alcohol consumption had increased significantly over the past few months. She typically drinks 3-4 glasses of wine each night after work and often goes out with friends on the weekends, consuming up to 10 drinks. She has tried to cut down on her drinking but has been unsuccessful. She is concerned about the impact of her drinking on her health and work performance. She does not have a history of alcohol abuse or dependence and does not have any other medical or psychiatric conditions. She is interested in participating in an online intervention to help her reduce her drinking. She regularly uses a computer and is comfortable with online tools. She is willing to be randomly assigned to either the intervention with assistance from a health educator or the intervention without assistance. She resides in Canada and is able to understand English.

A 47-year-old male with a complete spinal cord injury resulting in total loss of motor function below the level of lesion presents for evaluation of potential participation in a clinical trial studying the effect of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and weight-bearing on bone mass in individuals with spinal cord injury. The patient reports no history of endocrinopathies, normal thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, normal 25-OH vitamin D levels, normal calcium levels, and normal renal function (creatinine <2.0mg/dl). The patient reports a T score <-2.5 or Z score <-1.5 on evaluation of total hip bone mineral density (BMD), indicating significant loss of bone mass. The patient is capable of positioning for dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) measurements and undertaking the weight-bearing exercise regime. The patient expresses willingness and ability to self-administer PTH (Forteo 20ug sc) or have a family member assist with administration. The patient reports no history of malignancy, radiation therapy, or surgical intervention that would preclude obtaining DEXA and/or MRI measurements. The patient is not currently prescribed any bone-active agents or anti-convulsants, glucocorticoids, or other medications that would exclude participation in the study. The patient expresses a desire to participate in the study and is able to return for all follow-up visits.

The patient is a 30-year-old Kenyan male who is currently healthy and HIV-1 uninfected. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an HIV-1 vaccine. He has no history of immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease and is not currently taking any medication. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and is available for follow-up for the planned duration of the study. He is willing to undergo HIV-1 testing, counseling, and receive the test results. He has no history of severe or very severe local or systemic reactogenicity events after vaccination or history of severe or very severe allergic reactions. He is not pregnant or planning a pregnancy any time from enrollment to 4 months after the last vaccination. He is willing to forgo donating blood during the study. He does not have any relevant abnormality on history or examination and has normal laboratory parameters, including haematology, biochemistry, and urinalysis. He has no history of hepatitis B or C virus infection and has not received any investigational HIV-1 vaccine within the last 6 years. He is mentally stable and has no major psychiatric illness in the previous 3 years.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been previously treated for HIV infection. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 6 years with an undetectable viral load. He has no known hypersensitivity to darunavir or any of its excipients. The patient is in need of a change in his current antiretroviral regimen and has agreed to participate in this non-interventional study on the use of darunavir in daily practice. The patient has provided a signed and dated Informed Consent Form. The patient does not have severe hepatic impairment or any other medical condition that would exclude him from this study. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has not been previously treated with darunavir that was discontinued for any reason. The patient will be administered darunavir according to the Italian label and will be observed for at least 48 weeks from baseline visit. The patient's data will be collected at approximately 0, 1, 3 and 6 months after starting treatment and subsequently every 3 months in accordance with routine practice. The patient will be withdrawn from the study if the treatment with darunavir has been stopped. At the end of study visit, information on therapy given after darunavir discontinuation will be collected.

This clinical trial is not recruiting patients. It is a study that will be conducted on a representative sample of Norwegian adults who are currently living in Norway and experiencing the same non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) related to the COVID-19 pandemic. The study will investigate the association between the use of different information sources to obtain information about the pandemic and symptoms of depression and anxiety. The study will require participants to provide digital consent to participate and will not include children or adolescents under 18 years of age or adults who are not residing in Norway during the measurement period.

This is a 56-year-old female with a diagnosis of ovarian cancer. She has undergone surgery and received platinum-based chemotherapy in the past, but the cancer has returned. She is experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty eating. She has been referred to this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. She is in good overall health and is able to comply with the study requirements, including taking folic acid, vitamin B12 supplementation, and corticosteroids. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

Pt is a 52yo F with a BMI of 42, presenting for bariatric surgery. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well-controlled on medications. She has no known allergies to medications. She reports occasional episodes of nausea and vomiting after meals, but no history of PONV after previous surgeries. The patient has an Apfel score of 3. She consents to participate in the clinical trial and is randomized to receive either dexamethasone and ondansetron or normal saline. She is continuously monitored in the PACU and the medical floor for 24 hours postoperatively, recording any episodes of nausea, vomiting, and administration of rescue therapy. The severity of nausea is evaluated by the patient using a standard verbal response scale (VRS) ranging from 0-10. She is given 4 mg ondansetron followed by 0.625 mg droperidol if necessary as rescue therapy for PONV episodes.

A 55 year old male with a history of primary degenerative osteoarthritis of both knees, with chronic pain for the past 6 months that is not responding to conservative management. The patient has previously undergone knee arthroscopy with no significant relief of symptoms. Pain is localized to the medial and lateral compartments of both knees, with a visual analog score (VAS) of 8/10. The patient has no known history of neuropathy, bony tumors, traumatic fractures or diabetes mellitus. The patient is willing to undergo genicular nerve ablation procedure and has signed the informed consent form.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of glaucoma and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) came to the clinic for a routine check-up. She has been on medication to control her IOP for several years. She has no other ocular or systemic disease. She takes daily multivitamins and fish oil supplements, and has a well-balanced diet rich in vegetables and fruits. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no known allergies to any food or drugs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the relationship between macular pigment and visual performance in glaucoma patients.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage III lung cancer and has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He reports shortness of breath and difficulty breathing during daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. He has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or any other respiratory conditions prior to his cancer diagnosis. He does not take any calcium or Vitamin D supplements currently. His creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits according to his most recent blood work. The patient is able to swallow oral medications without difficulty.

A 32 year old pregnant woman diagnosed with chronic hypertension at 12 weeks gestation. She has been taking antihypertensive medication since then. She is now at 25 weeks gestation and presents with symptoms of preeclampsia, including hypertension, proteinuria, and edema. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will undergo blood draws and ultrasound evaluations as part of the research. She is a non-smoker, has no history of diabetes, and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far.

Patient is a healthy adult male or female between the ages of 18 to 50 years. The patient must not be pregnant, lactating or planning to conceive during the study period. The patient must have a weight that is at least 60% of the median weight for Bangladesh as measured by the "weight-to-length" index. The patient must be willing and able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures. The patient must not have participated in another clinical trial investigating a vaccine, drug, medical device or medical procedure in the 4 weeks preceding the first trial vaccination. The patient must not have received any vaccine in the 4 weeks preceding the first trial vaccination or planned receipt of any vaccine in the 4 weeks following the trial vaccination. The patient must not have a history of pneumococcal infection (confirmed microbiologically) within 5 years. The patient must not have a known or suspected congenital or acquired immunodeficiency or have received immunosuppressive therapy such as anti-cancer chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the preceding 6 months. The patient must not have a known systemic hypersensitivity to any of the vaccine components, or history of a life-threatening reaction to the vaccine used in the trial or to a vaccine containing any of the same substances. The patient must not have a bleeding disorder, including thrombocytopenia contraindicating intramuscular (IM) vaccination, or receipt of anticoagulants in the 3 weeks preceding inclusion. The patient must not be deprived of freedom by an administrative or court order, or in an emergency setting, or hospitalized involuntarily. The patient must not have a chronic illness that, in the opinion of the Investigator, is at a stage where it might interfere with trial conduct or completion. The patient must not have a febrile illness (temperature ≥38.0°C) or moderate or severe acute illness/infection (according to Investigator judgment) on the day of vaccination.

72-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF) and hypertension, who presented with acute onset of left-sided weakness, slurred speech, and facial droop. He was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke and treated with tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. After the acute phase of the stroke, the patient was deemed to be at high risk for recurrent stroke due to his history of AF and was prescribed warfarin for stroke prevention. However, the patient and his family are concerned about the potential side effects of warfarin and are interested in learning about alternative options for anticoagulation. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the safety and effectiveness of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin for stroke prevention in patients with AF. He has no history of valvular disease or prior cardiac valve surgery, venous thromboembolic disease, hemodialysis, or hip, femur, or knee surgery in the past year, and has not been diagnosed with antiphospholipid syndrome.

The patient is a newborn baby boy who was born at 32 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1200g. He was breathing spontaneously at birth but started to develop respiratory distress shortly after. He was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) where he received oxygen therapy and was started on mechanical ventilation due to worsening respiratory distress. He has been diagnosed with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and is currently receiving surfactant therapy. The baby has no congenital malformations or genetic diseases. His Apgar score at 5 minutes was 7. The parents have provided informed consent for their baby to participate in the clinical trial investigating the use of Early Bubble CPAP (EBCPAP) as an alternative respiratory support for premature newborns with respiratory distress. The investigators will monitor the baby's respiratory status and analyze the number of days he needs oxygen therapy, mechanical ventilation, and surfactant therapy. Other outcomes such as the incidence of pulmonary airleak, intraventricular hemorrhage, persistent ductus arteriosus, retinopathy of prematurity, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) at 28 days and 36 weeks corrected gestational age will also be evaluated.

The patient is a 45-year-old female recently diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with at least 3 extracranial metastatic lesions on imaging. She has undergone one line of chemotherapy with or without immune therapy in the advanced setting. Her PD-L1 status is positive, and she has tested negative for gBRCA1/2 pathogenic variants. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and HIPPA for the trial. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she has a KPS of 80%. She has not received previous PARPi treatment or radiation therapy to the metastases to be treated on this protocol. She has received no systemic glucocorticoid or immunosuppressive medications at the time of enrollment. She does not have any severe, active co-morbidity such as CHF or unstable angina within the last 6 months or acute bacterial or fungal infection requiring IV antibiotics at the time of registration. She is not HIV positive with CD4 count <200 cells/ microliter, and she is not currently on hormone replacement therapy. She has normal organ function and has no history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the trial, interfere with the subject's participation for the full duration of the trial, or is not in the best interest of the subject to participate, in the opinion of the treating investigator. She is willing to use two effective methods of contraception or complete abstinence during the course of the study and for 7 months after the last dose of study drug. She has the psychological ability and general health that permits completion of the study requirements and required follow-up.

Patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He has a history of diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. He requires mechanical ventilation and is being treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics. His creatinine levels are within normal range and he has not had any recent urologic procedures or surgeries. The patient is expected to be alive in the ICU for at least 48 hours after enrollment. The patient has not previously been enrolled in this study during a prior admission to the ICU.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is generally in good health with no significant medical history. She has no known allergies to any medications, food or any other substances. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and has not had any drug or alcohol abuse in the past 6 months. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the trial. Additionally, she has not participated in any clinical research trials within the last 30 days. The patient is willing to consume the investigational product, complete questionnaires, and attend all clinic visits. She has given voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not lactose intolerant and has not taken antibiotics within the previous 30 days.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been using methamphetamine for the past 5 years. He has tried to quit several times but has not been successful. He reports using methamphetamine on an average of 3-4 times a week for the past month. He is seeking treatment for his addiction and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him quit using methamphetamine. He has no significant medical history, is not currently taking any medications, and is willing and able to comply with study procedures. He understands the consent forms and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been scheduled for a general anesthesia for an elective surgery. He has no known allergies to any medications, including propofol, sufentanil, remifentanil, or morphine. He has no history of central nervous system disease or any psychotropic treatment. His blood pressure and heart rate are within normal range, and he has no known cardiovascular issues. He has not been diagnosed with hypovolemia or severe hepatic insufficiency. The patient does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has not undergone any previous surgeries.

A 50-year-old man with a history of diabetes and hypertension presents with thick and discolored toenails. He reports that he has suffered from this condition for the past 6 months and has tried various over-the-counter treatments, but has not seen any improvement. Clinical examination reveals subungual hyperkeratosis and onycholysis. A fungal culture and microscopy confirm the diagnosis of toenail onychomycosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of methylene blue-mediated photodynamic therapy versus 5% amorolfine nail lacquer for the treatment of his condition. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a 45 pack-year smoking history and a diagnosis of moderate-severe COPD. He has been on a therapeutic regimen for COPD for the past year and has not had any exacerbations in the past 4 weeks. Spirometry shows post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio <0.70 and post-bronchodilator FEV1 of 50% of predicted normal value. He has a history of hypersensitivity to Acetylcysteine and has never used mucolytics or xanthines derivatives or ephedrine routinely. He has no history of myocardial infarction, heart failure, acute ischemic coronary disease, or severe cardiac arrhythmia requiring treatment within the last 6 weeks. He has no history of lung cancer or lung volume reduction operation. Patient has no known serious prostatic hypertrophy or narrow-angle glaucoma requiring drug therapy. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and has signed written informed consent prior to participation.

The patient is a 28-year-old male active-duty military personnel who served in Operation Iraqi Freedom/Operation Enduring Freedom (OIF/OEF). He complains of persistent and distressing memories, flashbacks, and nightmares related to traumatic experiences during his deployment. He reports avoiding situations, thoughts, or feelings associated with the trauma and is easily startled. He has been feeling anxious and irritable for the past 6 months. He is not using any drugs and does not smoke. He drinks alcohol occasionally but denies any alcohol dependence. He has no significant medical or psychiatric history. He is married and has one child. His HAM-D score is 16.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) for several months. He reports frequent urination, especially at night, difficulty starting and stopping urination, weak urine stream, and the feeling of incomplete emptying of the bladder. He is otherwise in good general health and has no medical conditions that would confound the efficacy evaluation of the study. He is not taking any concomitant drugs that would be unsafe with the alpha-blocker being tested or that would confound the efficacy evaluation. He is willing to comply with the study requirements, including physical exams, electrocardiograms, clinical laboratory tests, vital signs, the International Prostate Symptom Score, maximum urine flow rate, pharmacokinetics, adverse events, concomitant medications, quality of life, and compliance. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance the development of a new drug for BPH and potentially improve his own symptoms.

Patient is a 68-year-old woman with a diagnosis of moderate severity Alzheimer's disease based on the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke (NINCDS)/Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association (ADRDA) and Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders-Fourth Edition (DSM-IV-TR) criteria. She has been receiving treatment with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEIs) in combination with memantine for at least 4 months before screening, with her dose and formulation stabilized at least 3 months before screening. She has a Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score at screening between 13 and 20, inclusive, with a Modified Hachinski Ischemia Score of less than or equal to (</=) 4, and Cornell Scale for Depression in Dementia (CSDD) scores </= 13 at screening. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 36 kilograms per square meter (kg/m^2) (inclusive) at screening. The patient is generally healthy and ambulatory or ambulatory-aided (i.e., walker or cane), and has a reliable caregiver or some other identified responsible person who has frequent contact with the participant. The patient does not have any neurological or psychiatric condition that may impair cognition or functioning that is not associated with Alzheimer's disease. The patient is not a smoker and does not have alcohol and/or substance abuse or dependence (DSM-IV-TR) in the past 2 years. The patient does not have poorly controlled hypertension, poorly controlled diabetes, or any unstable or clinically significant cardiovascular disease that could bias the assessment of the clinical or mental status of the participant. She is not requiring nursing home care, and is not currently treated for Alzheimer's disease other than those listed in the inclusion criteria. The patient has not participated at any time in an active Alzheimer's disease vaccine study or in a passive Alzheimer's disease immunization study less than 1 year before screening except for a) participants where documented medical history indicate that they were randomized to the placebo group in these studies, b) participants treated with bapineuzumab where a 6-month exclusion period applies. The patient is not currently treated with any antidepressant, antipsychotic, anxiolytics/hypnotics, anti-Parkinson's agents, anticonvulsants, opioids, or sympathomimetic drugs.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation that is refractory to drug treatment. He has been experiencing symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He has no history of stroke or other cardiovascular events. His laboratory studies are within normal limits. He has been advised to undergo pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for his AF and has been provided with all the necessary information about the procedure and the risks involved. He has consented to participate in the study and has been randomized into one of the two treatment groups. Anticoagulation therapy with warfarin has been discontinued five days before the procedure and low molecular weight heparin has been initiated at that time. The patient will undergo TCD recording throughout the entire period of the PVI procedure from the preparation of trans-septal LA access until the termination of the procedure. The transducer will be held in place by a proprietary headpiece supplied with the system. The patient will be informed about the possibility of microembolism on brain MRI scan, which is a potential risk associated with the procedure. All statistical analysis and manuscript drafting will be performed at the Tel Aviv medical center.

A 62-year-old female presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past 2 months. She has a history of smoking for 40 years and quit 5 years ago. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the right lung, and further testing confirms a diagnosis of stage 4 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no known genetic mutations or translocations in EGFR, ALK, BRAF, ROS1, or NTRK. She has measurable tumor lesions according to RECIST 1.1 criteria, and is willing to release a tumor biopsy specimen for exploratory molecular profiling. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, organ transplant, or pneumonitis. She is not currently taking any medications or participating in any other clinical trials, and is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol. She is not pregnant or nursing, and agrees to use effective contraception for up to 1 year after completion of therapy.

45 yo F with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and degenerative joint disease, experiencing chronic pain and stiffness in her knees and hips that has limited her ability to perform daily activities. She has tried various medications and physical therapy with limited success. She is seeking alternative treatments and has heard about cellular and biocellular regenerative therapy. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore these therapies to alleviate her pain and improve her mobility. She has adequate donor adipose tissue and is able to provide informed consent. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable and she is not currently taking any medications that would disqualify her from participating in the study. She is eager to learn more about the study and the potential benefits it may provide for her quality of life.

The patient is a 58-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. The diagnosis was confirmed through a biopsy of a mass in the lung. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any history of smoking or other lung diseases. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her cancer, but has agreed to participate in a study that involves collecting blood samples to identify epidermal growth factor receptor mutations. She is willing to undergo blood collection for analysis and has a tumor tissue block available for further analysis. The patient is generally in good health and is not currently receiving any other concurrent therapy.

72-year-old postmenopausal female with no significant medical history and not taking any medications presents for enrollment in a clinical trial for a Staphylococcus aureus vaccine. She is in good health and has no history of chronic medical conditions or surgical procedures in the past 3 months. She is sexually inactive and does not require contraception. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, laboratory tests, and other study procedures, including completion of an electronic diary from Day 1 to Day 14 following vaccination. She is available for the entire duration of the study and can be contacted by telephone during study participation. The patient is not a nursing home resident or in need of semiskilled nursing care. She has never received a Staphylococcus aureus vaccination, and she has not had any infections proven or suspected to be caused by Staphylococcus aureus within the past 6 months. The patient has no contraindications to vaccination or vaccine components, and she is not immunocompromised or on immunosuppressive therapy. She has not participated in any investigational studies within the past 30 days and is not an investigational site staff member or a family member of one. The patient does not have a planned surgical procedure within 30 days following vaccination.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been consistently weight training for over 2 years. He is currently training each muscle group twice a week and his body mass has been stable for the past month. He has a BMI of 28 and meets the strength relative to body weight guidelines for both bench press and leg press. He does not regularly use tobacco, illicit drugs, or supplements such as creatine and beta-alanine. He is willing to adhere to the protocol guidelines of the study, including abstaining from alcohol and caffeine consumption. He does not plan to increase or decrease his body mass in the next 3 months. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand his protein requirements as a resistance-trained individual.

45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and has undergone mastectomy. She is now seeking delayed breast reconstruction and has been referred to a participating center. She has been found best suited for reconstruction with a pedicled tissue flap from the back. She has no severe dementia and is able to provide informed consent. She is fluent in Danish and has a good understanding of the trial requirements. She meets all the eligibility criteria for the study and has agreed to participate. She will undergo randomization immediately after written informed consent has been obtained.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU after a motor vehicle accident resulted in multiple fractures and internal bleeding. He is currently intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and smoking. He has no history of diabetes or heart disease. The physician plans to order enteral nutrition for the patient to aid in his recovery. The patient has no known allergies and is able to tolerate enteral nutrition.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman diagnosed with muscle invasive bladder cancer. She has undergone transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) followed by neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and cisplatin. The CT scan after chemotherapy showed no remaining tumor in the bladder or any signs of lymph node involvement. The patient is scheduled for a radical cystectomy and has been given the option to choose between conduit diversion and orthotopic neobladder. She is interested in participating in the study to help her make an informed decision about which operation to choose by evaluating the impact on her health-related quality of life (HRQoL). She is able to provide informed consent and is 18 years of age or older.

A 72-year-old retired male veteran with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the clinic with memory problems and a lack of motivation. His wife has noticed that he has been less interested in his hobbies and does not initiate tasks around the house like he used to. His MMSE score is 23, and he meets the modified Mayo Clinic criteria for mild cognitive impairment. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no history of seizures or cranial surgeries, and his EEG is normal. He has not had a change in dose of dementia medications or antidepressants in the past 30 days. He is not currently experiencing a major depressive episode and is not using any stimulants. He has a caregiver, his wife, who can accompany him to the treatment sessions. He meets the apathy threshold on the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI). He has not been diagnosed with bipolar disorder or Tourette's syndrome and does not have a history of alcohol-related disorders or drug use. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia two years ago. She has been taking risperidone for the last year to treat her symptoms. She has a family history of metabolic syndrome, including type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She has no history of drug abuse or illicit drug use. She has a BMI of 29, indicating she is overweight. She has not been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes prior to taking risperidone. She has not been diagnosed with anemia or any other medical conditions that would affect weight changes. She is interested in participating in the study to help gain a better understanding of the metabolic side effects of antipsychotic medication and to potentially benefit from folic acid supplementation.

A 35 year old man who was diagnosed with HIV 5 years ago and has been receiving follow-up care at Kaohsiung VGH. He has a history of injection drug use, but he has been clean for the past 2 years. He is currently taking a combination of antiretroviral therapy (ART) medications and has been virally suppressed for the past 3 years. He has a CD4 count of 550 cells/mm3 and has not developed any opportunistic infections. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies smoking or using any illicit drugs. He has a history of depression but is currently stable on medication. He is interested in participating in this study to contribute to research on HIV disease progression and comorbidities.

45 year-old Japanese male patient with a history of persistent asthma for the past 5 years. He has been treated with medium dose ICS/LABA combination for the past 3 months and has been stable on this regimen for the past 4 weeks. He reports symptoms of cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath that have been impacting his daily activities. His ACQ-7 score is 2.5 at Visit 2. His pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is 60% of predicted normal value after withholding bronchodilators at Visit 2. He demonstrates reversibility with an increase in FEV1 of 15% and 300 mL within 20 minutes after administration of 400 µg of salbutamol at Visit 2. He has no history of asthma attack/exacerbation requiring systemic steroids or hospitalization or emergency room visit within 6 weeks prior to Visit 1. He has no history of intubation for a severe asthma attack/exacerbation. He has no clinical condition likely to be worsened by ICS administration. He has no history of narrow-angle glaucoma, symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) or bladder-neck obstruction or severe renal impairment or urinary retention. He has no history of chronic lung diseases other than asthma, including COPD, sarcoidosis, interstitial lung disease, cystic fibrosis, clinically significant bronchiectasis, and active tuberculosis. He is not pregnant or nursing.

A healthy 27 year old male with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 who has no history of any significant illnesses or allergies is needed for a clinical trial investigating the effects of repeated administration of itraconazole on the pharmacokinetics of JNJ-42847922. The participant must not have smoked for at least 3 months prior to screening and must be willing to use a barrier method of birth control if sexually active with a woman of childbearing potential. The study involves the participant receiving single oral doses of 5 mg of JNJ-42847922 on Day 1 and Day 6, with a daily dose of 200 mg of itraconazole administered from Day 2 to Day 6. Blood samples will be collected for evaluation of pharmacokinetics before and after drug administration, and safety will be monitored throughout the study. The participant must have signed an informed consent document indicating that they understand the purpose of and procedures required for the study and are willing to participate in the study and comply with the study procedures and restrictions.

A 35-year-old man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) has been on hemodialysis for the past two years. He has no significant comorbidities and is eager to receive a renal transplant. He has been informed about the Everolimus in Combination with Cyclosporine Microemulsion clinical trial and is interested in participating. He has a viable donor kidney available, which has a renal cold ischemic time of less than 36 hours. The donor is a 25-year-old unrelated living donor. The patient has never received any organ transplant before and has a panel reactive T-cell antibody titer of less than 50%.

A 35-year-old woman underwent bilateral mastectomy for breast cancer. She has no history of any other medical conditions and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She does not have lupus or scleroderma, and her diabetes is well-controlled. Her tissue characteristics are suitable for mammaplasty. She has no abscess or infection anywhere in her body at the time of study entry. Her psychological evaluation indicates that she is mentally stable and understands the risks involved with the surgical procedure and the prosthesis. She is willing to undergo any further surgery for revision if required. She prefers silicone gel-filled mammary prostheses over saline implants. She has signed the Informed Consent Document and agreed to complete all required follow-up visits.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with high-risk acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). He has a WBC count of 20 GPt/l and is experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and bruising easily. He has no history of cancer but has a family history of leukemia. He is otherwise in good health with no significant medical history. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial for his treatment and has provided informed consent. He has no allergies to trial medication or excipients in study medication. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with asthma since the age of 3. He experiences frequent wheezing, cough, and shortness of breath, which affects his daily activities. He has been treated with inhaled corticosteroids and inhaled short-acting β2-agonists (SAB), but sometimes he still experiences asthma exacerbations that require hospitalization. He has no other chronic medical conditions, no fever, and no history of allergies to acetylcholine, albuterol, or magnesium. He has not used any bronchodilator agents before the clinic day. His parents are concerned about his asthma symptoms and are willing to consider new treatment options.

A 58-year-old male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy due to coronary artery atherosclerotic disease and old myocardial infarction is being considered for a clinical trial. He has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 20% and has been experiencing symptoms of refractory heart failure (NYHA Class III). He is a candidate for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and has viable tissue in the infarct area as measured by cardiac delayed hyperenhancement magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). He is not on dialysis, has no liver cirrhosis, and has well-controlled diabetes. He has not had any evidence of malignant disease in the past 3 years and has no known allergies to gelatin. He is interested in participating in the trial and has given his written informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a family history of Huntington's Disease (HD). She has no symptoms of HD at present, but genetic testing has confirmed that she carries the gene mutation that causes the disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance research towards finding a cure for HD. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders and is in good overall health. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with all study procedures, including adequate contraceptive measures. She has no contraindications to MRI and has not undergone any procedures that would preclude her from participating in the study.

Patient is a 10-year-old child who presents with abdominal swelling, increasing weight, and respiratory distress. The patient has no significant medical history, but the parents report that the child has been complaining of abdominal pain and has had decreased appetite for the past month. On physical examination, the child has a distended abdomen, hepatosplenomegaly, and lower limb edema. There is also tachycardia and tachypnea. Laboratory tests reveal elevated liver enzymes and low albumin levels. An abdominal ultrasound shows ascites in the peritoneal cavity. The patient is diagnosed with ascites and is eligible for the clinical trial to investigate the diagnosis and treatment of ascites in infants and children.

The patient is a 26-year-old first-time mother who is currently pregnant with a single fetus. She is in her 38th week of gestation and has no significant medical history. She has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications thus far. She is planning for a vaginal delivery and has an open mind about the different techniques that can be used during the second stage of labour. She is excited to participate in this clinical trial to help advance knowledge in the field of obstetrics and improve maternal and newborn health outcomes. She is willing to provide informed consent and follow the study protocol. She is looking forward to having a healthy delivery and a healthy newborn.

A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman was referred to the clinic due to significant symptoms of heart failure. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and tiredness for the past few months which has limited her ability to perform daily physical activities such as walking. She has a history of heart disease and her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was found to be between 20-40% in a recent assessment. She has been diagnosed with symptomatic HF (Class III NYHA) for at least 30 days prior to the baseline visit. Her ambulatory status is good and she can walk without assistance of another person or device such as a cane or walker. Her medical history reveals no neuromuscular or rheumatologic conditions that limit her ability to improve walking distance. She has not experienced pulmonary edema, multiorgan failure or cardiogenic shock within the past 30 days. She has no history of congenital heart disease or infiltrative myocardial disease. She has not experienced unstable angina or myocardial infarction within the past 30 days. Her blood pressure and heart rate are currently within normal limits. She does not have any undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding, breast cancer, breast surgery or breast disease contraindicating estrogen/hormone therapy. She has no history of polycystic ovary syndrome or any other condition known to be adversely affected by testosterone treatment. She is not taking any prescription or over the counter medications/ nutraceuticals that may have anabolic or steroid hormonal effects within 30 days prior to the baseline visit. She has not used any marketed or investigational oral, sub-lingual, topical, transdermal injectable, or vaginal androgen therapy including dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) at any time within 3 months prior to the baseline visit. She has not used systemic corticosteroids within 30 days prior to the baseline visit (acute use for fewer than 7 days is acceptable).

A 52-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia presents for a bone marrow transplant. She received a myeloablative conditioning regimen and is set to receive peripheral blood stem cells from an unrelated donor. She is at high risk for developing graft versus host disease (GVHD) due to the mismatched donor, and is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial to detect GVHD with [18F]F-AraG PET scans. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with the study, and has provided informed consent. She has been informed that the study involves two PET scans, one on day 4 +/- 2 days post transplant and another between day 14-21 post transplant. The patient is willing to participate and hopeful that the study will help detect and manage GVHD early, which could improve her chances of a successful transplant outcome.

The patient is a sexually active 25-year-old male who recently had unprotected sex with an HIV-positive partner. The encounter occurred less than 72 hours ago, and the patient is concerned about the risk of contracting HIV. The patient is HIV-negative based on a recent rapid test and has no known allergies or intolerance to the study drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the importance of taking the medication as prescribed. The patient is not actively trying to conceive a child and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have chronic hepatitis B or prior antiretroviral therapy for hepatitis B.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a recent exacerbation of symptoms requiring hospitalization. He was intubated and started on invasive mechanical ventilation for respiratory support. He has been on the ventilator for five days and is now stable with minimal respiratory distress. His oxygen saturation levels are adequate, and his arterial blood gas analysis shows partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) of 85 mmHg and partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) of 45 mmHg. He has no history of tracheostomy or upper airway obstruction. He has a smoking history of 20 pack-years but has quit smoking for the past five years. He has no other significant medical history and is not on any medications other than those required for his current hospitalization. The patient is conscious and able to follow commands but is experiencing some mild anxiety related to being on the ventilator.

The patient is a 45-year-old male presenting to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of shortness of breath, chest pain, and coughing up blood. CT angiography revealed a large pulmonary embolism in the right pulmonary artery. The patient's systolic blood pressure is 100mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. The patient is conscious and alert, but in moderate distress. The patient has no history of pulmonary hypertension, hematologic or coagulation disorders, or recent major surgery. The patient has not received tPA in the past 14 days, and has no known contraindications to anticoagulation therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

45-year-old male with a history of glioblastoma. The patient underwent surgery and radiation therapy but has now experienced a recurrence of the tumor. The MRI scan shows unequivocal radiographic evidence for tumor progression by contrast-enhanced MRI scan. The patient has not undergone any recent surgery for their glioblastoma. The patient has passed an interval of 6 months or greater between completion of prior radiotherapy and registration. The patient has not received prior treatment with an inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) or VEGFR (including bevacizumab). The patient has no history of severe, active co-morbidity, defined as follows: unstable angina and/or congestive heart failure requiring hospitalization within the last 6 months prior to registration, transmural myocardial infarction within the last 6 months prior to registration, history of stroke or transient ischemic attack within 6 months prior to registration, significant vascular disease, acute bacterial or fungal infection requiring intravenous antibiotics at the time of registration, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation or other respiratory illness requiring hospitalization or precluding study therapy at the time of registration, hepatic insufficiency resulting in clinical jaundice and/or coagulation defects, acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) based upon current Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) definition, pregnancy or women of childbearing potential and men who are sexually active and not willing/able to use medically acceptable forms of contraception, prior allergic reaction to the study drug (bevacizumab), prior history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy, history of a non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture within 90 days (3 months) prior to registration, gastrointestinal bleeding or any other hemorrhage/bleeding event Common Terminology Criteria for adverse Events (CTCAE), v. 4 grade 3 or greater within 30 days prior to registration, major surgical procedure, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to registration (with the exception of craniotomy). The patient is willing and able to provide study-specific informed consent prior to study entry.

54-year-old male with a history of multiple myeloma, who has undergone standard of care workup, is scheduled to undergo F-18 FDG PET scan for staging. He has no history of active non-multiple myeloma malignancy and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He weighs less than 300 pounds and has no contraindication to PET MRI. He can provide informed consent and is an English-speaking patient. The patient has not been diagnosed with Type I or Type II Diabetes Mellitus and has a fasting blood glucose level below 150 mg/dl.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her left knee for the past year. She is finding it difficult to perform daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and even getting up from a seated position due to the pain. She has been taking acetaminophen and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents for pain relief but has not found significant relief with these medications. Her average pain score on the Brief Pain Inventory is 7/10. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis in her left knee and has also been experiencing depression and anxiety due to the pain and limitations it has caused. She is able to read and write in English and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to try Venlafaxine for her pain relief. She does not have any history of psychosis or mania, suicidal ideation, substance abuse or dependence, and has not used any investigational drug within the past month.

35-year-old female with a history of ragweed-induced allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and asthma for the past 3 years. She has received treatment during the previous ragweed season and has a positive skin prick test response to Ambrosia artemisiifolia. She has a positive specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) against Ambrosia artemisiifolia and her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) is greater than 70% of predicted. Safety laboratory tests and vital signs conducted at the screening visit are within normal limits. She is willing to give written informed consent and adhere to dose and visit schedules. She is using a medically acceptable form of birth control and has a negative urine pregnancy test at screening. She has no clinical history of symptomatic seasonal allergic rhinitis and/or asthma due to another allergen during or potentially overlapping the ragweed season. She has not received immunosuppressive treatment within 3 months prior to the screening visit, except steroids for allergic and asthma symptoms. She has no history of severe asthma or asthma requiring medium or high dose inhaled corticosteroids. She has no history of anaphylaxis with cardiorespiratory symptoms, chronic urticaria and angioedema, chronic sinusitis, or severe atopic dermatitis. She is not currently breastfeeding, pregnant, or intending to become pregnant. She has not had previous treatment by immunotherapy with ragweed allergen or any other allergen 5 years prior to the screening visit. She has no history of allergy, hypersensitivity or intolerance to the ingredients of the investigational medicinal products (except for Ambrosia artemisiifolia), rescue medications, or self-injectable epinephrine. She has no clinically significant condition or situation, other than the condition being studied that, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with the study evaluations or optimal participation in the study. She is able to comply with the use of self-injectable epinephrine and has no greater risk of developing adverse reactions after epinephrine administration.

A 62-year-old woman with Type 2 diabetes has been experiencing a non-healing ulcer on her left foot for over 5 weeks. She has tried various treatments, including antibiotics, but the wound has not shown any signs of healing. She is concerned about the possibility of infection and the potential consequences of amputation. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed all necessary consent forms. She is able to attend all scheduled appointments and comply with study procedures. Her HbA1C score is 9.2, and her blood pressure and flow to the foot are appropriate for the study. The size of the ulcer is appropriate for the study, and she has not received any cell or tissue products for the treatment of the wound. She is not pregnant, nursing, or a prisoner. She has no history of osteomyelitis in the foot with the ulcer in the last 30 days. She is compliant with her medications and has never received therapy for the study ulcer with any cell and/or tissue product (CTP). She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

This clinical trial is seeking incoming undergraduate students at the University of Kentucky who are interested in participating in a pilot program aimed at evaluating the relative efficacy of bystander training elements in addressing sexual violence and substance abuse. The study will consist of two training conditions: Green Dot Intensive Bystander Training or Student Wellness Training. The study will last for 9 months, one academic year, and students will be followed up with surveys at baseline, 2-3 months after training, and 6 months following training. Students who are interested in participating in this study must be incoming undergraduate students at the University of Kentucky in 2015. Any current or non-incoming University of Kentucky student or any student primarily enrolled at another college or university will be excluded from the study.

This is an 70 year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain on exertion, and was found to have significant coronary artery disease on cardiac catheterization. She has been scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. She is able to read and understand English and has agreed to participate in the study. She has no history of neurological disease or cognitive dysfunction and is expected to be able to complete the 1 week and 3 months post-operative visits.

A 35-year-old female was diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) a year ago after experiencing several severe respiratory tract infections. She has been receiving regular intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) replacement therapy with a constant IVIg dose for the past six months. Her IgG trough levels have been stable and above 5 g/L. The patient reports feeling fatigued and experiencing frequent infections despite her current treatment. She has a history of asthma and allergies, but no other significant medical conditions. She is not pregnant and uses reliable contraceptive measures. She works part-time as a teacher and lives with her husband and two children. She has no known allergies to human proteins or study products. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She has not participated in any other clinical study in the past 30 days and is not currently taking any systemic steroids or immunosuppressant drugs. She has never had a thrombotic event and does not have any significant risk factors for thrombotic events. She has not received any live-attenuated virus vaccines in the past three months and has no known selective, absolute immunoglobulin A (IgA) deficiency or antibodies to IgA. She has tested negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV. She does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse and is motivated to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for over 2 years, with HbA1c levels around 7.8%. He is currently using insulin therapy and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. He has no history of heart or kidney disease, and his retinopathy is under control. He has not experienced any severe hypoglycemia in the past. The patient has no history of brain disorders or psychiatric illness, and does not abuse drugs or alcohol. He is not taking any selective beta-blockers, oral steroids, oral anticoagulants, or benzodiazepines. He has no eating disorders, and has not experienced any severe head trauma accompanied by loss of consciousness. He is willing to undergo MRI and has visual acuity of 0.8. There are no known allergies to the trial product or related products.

A 25-year-old female athlete who specializes in long jump presents with a history of frequent lower limb injuries. She reports experiencing pain in her knees and ankles after prolonged periods of training and competing. She is currently participating in regional and national competitions and is looking for ways to improve her sports performance. The physical examination reveals mild tenderness over the patellar and Achilles tendon. She has no history of any other medical conditions. She is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effectiveness of lower limb proprioception exercises in improving sports performance. She has no previous experience with such exercises but is willing to commit to attending two sessions per week for four weeks. She signs the informed consent document and meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 35 year old woman with no history of eye disease or ocular surgery presents for a routine eye exam. She is in good health and takes no medications. She has no family history of eye diseases. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with correction. Anterior segment examination is unremarkable. Intraocular pressure is within normal limits in both eyes. She has no complaints of visual disturbances or eye discomfort. The optometrist recommends her to participate in a clinical trial to examine the vessel density of healthy adults' optical coherence tomography angiography images with two semi-manual methods and an automated quantification program. She agrees to participate in the study after being informed about the procedures and risks involved.

A 25-year-old female university student who spends a significant amount of time using electronic devices for both academic and leisure purposes. She has no known medical conditions and is fluent in English. She owns a laptop and smartphone, and regularly uses them for several hours per day. She is interested in participating in research studies related to her lifestyle and is willing to commit to completing the required questionnaires and diaries over the eight-week period.

A 55 year old woman with a history of heart failure is admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and fatigue. She has been experiencing chest pain for the past few days and her condition is managed with medication. She is alert and oriented and speaks fluent English. Her SVR is greater than 1200 dyne · sec · cm-5. She has no allergies to dogs and her white blood cell count is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

This is a 9-year-old boy named Jack who has been diagnosed with ADHD. He has been experiencing symptoms such as difficulty staying focused, impulsivity, and hyperactivity both at home and in school. Jack has not been on any medication for ADHD for the past 6 months. He comes from a stable family background with both parents employed in white-collar jobs. Jack's mother had a normal pregnancy and delivery. Jack's parents have agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the relationships between neuroendocrine substrates, candidate genes, and the phenotype and endophenotypes of ADHD. Jack will undergo a structured interview using the Kiddie Epidemiologic Version of the Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (K-SADS-E) to confirm his diagnosis of ADHD. DNA from Jack and his biological parents will be collected using cheek swab to identify the genotypes of the STS gene, SULT2A1 gene, TH gene, and NR3C1 gene. Saliva samples will be collected from Jack using the passive drool method at 7:00-8:00 in the morning to analyze the levels of neuroendocrine substrates. Jack will undergo assessments for his clinical symptoms and neurocognitive function. After the initial assessment, Jack will begin to receive methylphenidate (MPH) treatment for his ADHD. At week 4 and week 52, procedures similar to those performed at baseline will be repeated to assess Jack's short-term and long-term efficacy symptoms and cognitive function. The results of this study may help to further elucidate the complexity of the pathophysiology of ADHD and may serve as an important reference for the direction of future study and clinical treatment for patients with ADHD.

The patient is a 26-year-old Caucasian woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes when she was 16. She has been using insulin pumps for the past 5 years. She has noticed that her blood sugar levels have been fluctuating and her HbA1c level is currently at 9.2%. She has been monitoring her blood sugar levels daily but she is unsure if she is doing it correctly. She is concerned about the long-term complications of uncontrolled diabetes and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve her diabetes control. She has no history of hypoglycemia unawareness and is mentally stable. She has not gained or lost more than 3kg in the last year. She is currently taking insulin glargine and insulin aspart. She is willing to learn and make changes to her lifestyle if necessary. She is currently under the care of a diabetes specialist at Stavanger University Hospital. She has provided her written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) for the past year. He has not yet started dialysis and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 55 ml/min. His serum phosphorus levels are consistently high, measuring at 4.2 mg/dL during his last visit with his nephrologist. He is currently taking phosphate binders and vitamin D supplements as prescribed by his physician. He has no known allergies to shellfish or chitin. He has not had any dental work done in the past few months and has no active infections or known immunodeficiency diseases. He is a non-smoker and does not abuse drugs or alcohol. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure diagnosed 6 months ago. The patient has been experiencing shortness of breath and ankle swelling (NYHA II-III symptoms) despite being on optimal medical therapy, including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and aldosterone antagonists. The patient is currently taking a daily dose of furosemide (≥40mg per day) to maintain euvolemia. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is ≤40% on a clinically indicated echocardiogram obtained within the past 6 months. The patient's systolic blood pressure is ≥110 mmHg at the time of informed consent. The patient has suitable renal artery anatomy for Renal Sympathetic Denervation (RSD) procedure, with a treatable length of at least 20mm in each renal artery, diameter in treatable segments must be ≥4mm, and lone main renal vessel feeding each kidney. The patient is able to maintain stable medications for 52 weeks and has not had changes in heart failure medication regimen (including diuretics) for the previous 14 days. The patient does not have evidence of orthostatic hypotension or known dysautonomia. The patient does not have evidence of or a history of renal artery stenosis, nephrectomy, or renal transplant. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is ≥45 ml/min/1.73m2 determined by Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) equation, and the patient does not have significant proteinuria (>2g protein/daily protein excretion). The patient does not have a body mass index (BMI) >35 kg/m2. The patient has not had an acute coronary syndrome within the last 4 weeks and has not had coronary revascularization procedures (percutaneous coronary intervention or cardiac artery bypass graft) or valve surgery within 30 days of screening or expected procedures within the next 6 months. The patient does not have hypertrophic or restrictive cardiomyopathy, constrictive pericarditis, active myocarditis, active endocarditis, or complex congenital heart disease. The patient is not currently or anticipated to use a ventricular assist device or IV vasoactive drug therapy for HF management within the next 6 months, is not a listed cardiac transplant candidate, and does not have known allergic reactions to iodinated radiological contrast media or iodinated antiseptics. The patient does not have greater than moderate mitral or aortic stenosis, and/or severe tricuspid regurgitation. The patient is not suffering from a terminal illness (other than HF) with expected survival of less than 1 year. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or of childbearing potential not practicing effective birth control. The patient is not enrolled or planned to be enrolled in another clinical trial within the next 12 months. The patient does not have a history of urinary outflow tract obstruction, bladder retention and/ or moderate to severe prostate hypertrophy. The patient does not have a history of adrenal insufficiency or untreated hypothyroidism. The patient does not have non-cardiac dyspnea or fatigue due to frailty, motivational factors, pulmonary disease or orthopedic problems that preclude them from performing 6MWT (Six-Minute Walk Test).

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of Hemophilia A. He has no history of inhibitor development and has been receiving treatment with turoctocog alfa (NovoEight®) for the past year. He is scheduled to undergo a surgical procedure and is considering participating in the SERAPHINE study to contribute to the research on the therapeutic management and use of turoctocog alfa in surgery for patients with Hemophilia A. He has expressed no objections to participate in the study and has no other inherited hemorrhagic disorders.

Patient A is a 65-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of acute respiratory infection such as cough, sputum production, and shortness of breath for the past 3 days. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension. He is currently taking albuterol inhaler and lisinopril for his medical conditions. His oxygen saturation is 92% on room air, and he requires supplemental oxygen. The patient tested positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) within 72 hours of screening. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. The patient does not have a history of allergy to any components of the study drug. He is not taking any medications that are contraindicated with presatovir. The patient has not received any bone marrow, stem cell, or solid organ transplant, or radiation or chemotherapy within the last 12 months. He is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has a Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) score of 4 at baseline.

45-year-old male with chronic low back pain for more than 6 months with a minimum pain intensity of greater than 5 out of 10 on an 11-point numerical rating scale in the 7 days preceding study entry. The patient has previously undergone two diagnostic, intra-articular blocks for sacroiliac joint pain and has achieved greater than 80% reduction in pain following each block. The patient has not received any prior sacroiliac joint radiofrequency neurotomy. The patient has no history of major trauma to the lumbar spine or infection in the lumbar spine in the six months preceding study entry. The patient has no documented or suspected alcohol or drug abuse and is not suspected of having an addictive personality. The patient is not breastfeeding and is not currently receiving anti-psychotic medication. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study assessments and complete the questionnaires.

Group 2: Myocardial Infarction A 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within 24 hours of symptom onset. He is now stable and has been discharged from the hospital. He has no significant past medical history except for a history of smoking which he quit 5 years ago. He is currently taking aspirin and a statin for secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. He has no known allergies to contrast agents. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance research in the field of cardiovascular disease. He has the ability to give written informed consent and is deemed eligible for the study by the physician investigator.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with intermediate (INT-1) risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and has a history of transfusional iron overload. She has received a lifetime minimum of 30 previous packed red cell transfusions due to her MDS. Her serum ferritin level has been found to be greater than or equal to 1000 µg/mL on at least two occasions, at least two weeks apart, during the prior year. She has not received any prior treatment for iron chelation. Her renal and hepatic function are normal. She has no history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is not planning to become pregnant during the trial. She has no systemic diseases that would prevent study treatment. She is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the trial. She is able to provide written informed consent.

Patient is a 56-year-old woman from Canada who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for over a year. She is a current smoker with a 20 pack-year history. She has been on maintenance therapy with a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) for the past 4 months and has not experienced any acute worsening of her COPD symptoms recently. Her post albuterol/salbutamol forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio is <0.70 and her FEV1 is at 65% of predicted. She has no history of asthma. She is not pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or lactating. She is capable of giving informed consent and is willing and able to comply with study procedures and restrictions. She is able to read, comprehend, and record information in English. She has not used the ELLIPTA or HANDIHALER inhalers in the past 6 months. She has no history of significant cardiac, neurological, renal, hepatic, immunological, endocrine or hematological abnormalities that are uncontrolled. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is not an immediate family member of the participating investigator, sub-investigator, study coordinator, or employee of the participating investigator.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The cancer has spread to other areas of his body, making it unresectable. He has already undergone standard treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer is still progressing. He is experiencing pain and difficulty swallowing due to the tumor. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 1, and his blood work shows a white blood cell count of 4,500/mm^3, hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, and platelet count of 150,000/mm^3. His bilirubin level is within normal limits, and his AST/ALT levels are slightly elevated but within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. His creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL.
