He has no history of heart or lung disease, and his pulmonary function tests are within normal limits. He has never had an allergy to eggs or chicken embryo-based vaccines. The patient has not undergone surgery within the last four weeks and has no plans to undergo any other concurrent investigational or commercial therapies for treatment of malignancy. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 47 year old woman who has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and is scheduled to undergo an elective pancreatic resection. She has no history of significant weight loss and has not shown any signs of distant metastasis. She has no known respiratory, renal, or heart disease. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent prior to enrollment. She has a history of type 2 diabetes and her last HbA1c was 7.5%. She is currently taking metformin and glipizide to control her blood sugar levels. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history.

A 6-year-old boy was referred to the Pediatric Otolaryngology clinic by his pediatrician due to recurrent episodes of sore throat and snoring at night. He has no significant past medical history, and his immunizations are up to date. The boy's mother reports that he snores loudly at night, which sometimes wakes her up. She also reports that he often has a stuffy and runny nose, and he has trouble breathing through his nose. The boy is otherwise healthy and active, attending school without difficulty. During the clinic visit, the Otolaryngologist recommends flexible nasendoscopy to assess the boy's upper airway. The study coordinator approaches the family to ask if they would be interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing different intranasal sprays for nasal prep before the procedure. The boy's mother agrees to participate, and after providing fully informed consent, the boy is randomized to receive one of three different intranasal sprays: (A) placebo (isotonic saline solution), (B) decongestant (0.05% xylometazoline hydrochloride), or (C) decongestant with local anesthetic (0.05% xylometazoline hydrochloride with 1% lidocaine hydrochloride). The boy is assessed for discomfort experienced during the procedure using a validated pediatric pain score.

Linda is a 55-year-old woman who has been postmenopausal for the past three years. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens (BZA/CE) combinations. Linda's body mass index (BMI) is 26 kg/m2 and her body weight is 60 kg. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. Linda has no history of thrombophlebitis, thromboembolic disorders, or coagulopathies. She has never experienced any drug allergies to conjugated estrogens (CE) or selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs). Linda is interested in participating in this study to help advance research on menopause therapies and improve women's health.

The patient is a 65 year old man who presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with a heart attack and developed cardiogenic shock. He was treated with medication and mechanical support but developed severe mitral regurgitation. His echocardiogram showed a severely dilated left ventricle and a flail posterior mitral valve leaflet. He was evaluated for MitraClip therapy and found to be a suitable candidate. He has no known allergies and is on medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol use but quit both several years ago. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and taking walks but has been limited by his recent heart condition. His BMI is 29 and his blood pressure is 150/90. He has mild peripheral vascular disease and his kidneys are functioning normally. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his outcomes and help advance medical knowledge.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital due to a stroke that affected the right side of his body. He has been hospitalized for stroke rehabilitation and has been receiving treatment for the past 3 months. He has a facial impairment according to the House-Brackmann criteria ≥2. The patient is able to undergo psychophysical testing and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. He has no history of acute pain in the oro-facial sphere or any additional neuro-muscular disease. The patient is able to chew and swallow foods but has noticed a reduced chewing performance and dysphagia following the stroke. He has a good oral hygiene and regularly visits the dentist.

Sarah is a 55 year old woman who has been experiencing trigeminal neuralgia for the past year. She has been recommended for microvascular decompression (MVD) surgery and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial studying the effects of preoperative scopolamine patch application on postoperative nausea and vomiting. Sarah has no known allergies and has normal liver and kidney function. She is classified as ASA Physical Status Classification 2 as she has mild hypertension that is controlled with medication. She is able to communicate well and understands the objectives of the study. Sarah will be discharged to a general ward after surgery and does not have any history of narrow-angle glaucoma, pyloric stenosis, intestinal obstruction, bladder obstruction, bradycardia, or voiding difficulty.

This is a 68-year-old female with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. She has been experiencing significant sleep disturbances for the past year, which have been affecting her quality of life and the ability to perform daily tasks. She has tried various medications in the past, including melatonin and benzodiazepines, but has not found any relief. She is currently living at home with her husband who has been her primary caregiver. Her husband is also experiencing caregiver burnout due to the lack of sleep and constant worry about her well-being. She has no history of major depression, schizophrenia or other mental illnesses. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past month and is not taking any other medications that may affect her sleep. She is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve her sleep quality and overall quality of life.

As this is a clinical trial focused on early care and education centers, there are no individual patients who would be eligible for enrollment. However, the study is looking for eligible ECEC centers in neighborhoods with a high proportion of Hispanic or Latino residents, who are licensed and enroll at least 35 children aged 3-4 years old, and have space available for a garden install. ECEC centers that are not participating in the CACFP or have less than 35 children aged 3-5 years old enrolled would be excluded from the trial.

A 40-year-old woman residing in the Shuang area of Taipei has regular access to healthcare and is able to read. She has no known history of breast cancer or any other significant medical conditions. She has a family history of breast cancer in her mother and aunt. She is interested in participating in breast cancer screening activities and is willing to comply with recommended behaviors to promote breast cancer prevention. She has a positive attitude towards health and is willing to participate in the study to help promote health behavior in her community.

A 28-year-old Hispanic male who has been smoking for 10 years and has tried to quit several times without success. He is interested in trying an Internet-based method to quit smoking and is fluent in both English and Spanish. He has access to email and is willing to participate in a follow-up survey at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months after entering the study. He is aware that participation is voluntary and can stop participating at any time. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is excited to take part in helping researchers determine the effectiveness of an internet-based stop smoking site.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a growth hormone secreting pituitary adenoma (GHoma) a year ago. She has undergone surgery, but her GH and IGF-1 levels have not normalized. She presents with symptoms of acromegaly, including enlarged hands and feet, prominent jaw, and excessive sweating. She is currently treated with somatostatin analogues, but her GH and IGF-1 levels remain elevated. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of pituitary tumors or endocrine disorders. She is not allergic to rosiglitazone and has no liver or kidney dysfunction, respiratory failure, heart failure, edema, severe hyperlipidemia, osteoporosis, or history of non-traumatic fractures. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not received radiation therapy in the past 3 years. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months and has no other neoplastic diseases or mental and neurological disorders.

A 58-year old retired teacher was recently diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma. She is currently experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has never smoked or used any illicit drugs. She lives with her husband and they have two adult children. She is an active volunteer in the community and enjoys gardening. The patient has a performance status of 1 and can perform most activities of daily living independently. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits. She has no known CNS lymphoma and has not received any prior immunotherapy or chemotherapy. Her lab results show a WBC count of 3,000/mm^3 and a platelet count of 110,000/mm^3. Her bilirubin, ALT, and AST levels are within normal limits. Her creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dL and her calcium level is 10.5 mg/dL. She is HIV negative and has no other concurrent serious medical condition or active infection.

The patient is a healthy Caucasian infant aged between 8-12 weeks, born between 37 and 42 weeks of gestation, with both parents being of Caucasian ethnicity. The infant has not yet received their routine infant immunisations and has no history of meningococcal B disease, allergies to any component of the vaccine, major congenital defects or serious chronic illness, neurologic disorders or seizures, and confirmed or suspected immunodeficiency. The infant is not on any immunosuppressants or immune modifying drugs, and has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products since birth or planned administration during the study period. The parent or legal guardian is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and has internet access for the duration of the study. The infant is not planned to receive any other vaccines or drugs during the study period except for Hepatitis B vaccine and Influenza vaccines (which can be given 14 days before or after study vaccines), or BCG (which can be administered 28 days before or after study vaccines).

A 55 year old male presented to the hospital with complaints of headache and dizziness for the past week. He was diagnosed with an unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIA) of 12mm size located in the anterior circulation. His hemoglobin (Hb) level was 11.5 g/dl, ferritin level was 80 ng/ml, and transferrin saturation was 18%. He had no history of chronic inflammatory disease or underlying disease causing anemia. He was eligible for clipping surgery for UIA and was diagnosed with iron-deficiency anemia (IDA) based on the inclusion criteria. The treating physician decided to enroll him in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of preoperative intravenous ferric carboxymaltose for correcting his anemia before surgery to reduce the need for intra-/postoperative RBC transfusions and improve surgical outcomes.

A 58-year-old woman presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with an acute coronary syndrome. She underwent a primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and was discharged from the hospital after 5 days. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is otherwise healthy. She is a non-smoker and has never consumed alcohol. She is fluent in Dutch and is able to attend a supervised exercise program. She has signed informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of heart failure, impaired left ventricular function, psychic or cognitive impairments, severe arrhythmias, heart valve disease, congenital disease, severe co-morbidities which limit the CR, or an ICD. She is eligible to participate in the OPTICARE study.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of overactive bladder syndrome for at least 6 months. She reports feeling a strong urge to urinate frequently throughout the day and night, and has had several instances of urinary incontinence. These symptoms have been interfering with her daily life and causing her significant distress. She has not been treated for OAB previously, and has no history of urinary tract infections or other bladder-related conditions. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the medication mirabegron for the treatment of OAB.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has had a history of abdominal surgery due to ovarian cancer. She was diagnosed with incisional hernia after her surgery and is in need of elective surgical repair. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She is not experiencing any other abdominal complications and has been cleared by her physician for elective surgery. She has no history of other medical conditions and does not take any medications. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her labs are within normal limits. She is able to tolerate the surgical procedure and is willing to comply with the follow-up requirements of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with primary progressive multiple sclerosis 3 years ago. She has been experiencing a gradual worsening of her symptoms, including difficulty walking and fatigue. Her EDSS score is currently 6.5. She has not received any alternative therapy for MS. She is a retired teacher who enjoys reading and spending time with her grandchildren. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or dementia. She has no contraindications to MRI, lumbar puncture, or Trendelenburg position. She has not had any infections or immunosuppressive treatments in the past 6 months. She has not been treated with rituximab before. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her progressive MS.

45-year-old male with a history of opioid addiction and currently enrolled in methadone maintenance treatment for the past 2 years. He has been a continuous smoker for the past 10 years, smoking at least 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He has attempted to quit smoking multiple times but has never been successful in quitting for longer than 24 hours. He is interested in participating in a study to assess patient views on smoking cessation and tobacco harm reduction during drug treatment. He has no history of significant medical conditions and is able to provide informed consent.

Pt is a 65yo F with a diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease according to the 2011 NIA-AA criteria and at least a 6 month decline in cognitive function documented in the medical record. The patient has a long history of forgetfulness and difficulty with word recall, and has recently started experiencing difficulty with daily tasks, such as cooking and cleaning. The patient has undergone an amyloid PET scan which confirmed the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. The patient has a caregiver, her daughter, who is willing and able to participate in all clinic visits and some study assessments. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant comorbidities or medications that may interfere with the study. The patient is able to swallow capsules and has no contraindications to undergoing an LP. The patient has a formal education of 12 years and is capable of providing written informed consent to the study procedures and for use of protected health information. The patient has no history of active major depression, schizophrenia or bipolar disorder and has a GDS score of 4. The patient's MMSE score is 24. The patient is not currently taking any antipsychotic agents, antiepileptics, centrally active anti-hypertensive drugs, sedatives, opioids, or benzodiazepines. The patient does not have any disorders that could interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of drugs.

62-year-old male former smoker with a 30-pack year history presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but has been otherwise healthy. A chest x-ray reveals a suspicious mass in the left lung, and a biopsy confirms non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Further imaging studies reveal metastases to the liver and bones. The patient is otherwise in good general health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no significant cardiac history or neuropathy. Laboratory studies show normal organ function, with a white blood count of 5.2 x 10(9)/L, platelet count of 205 x 10(9)/L, and hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL. His total bilirubin is 0.8 x upper limit of normal (ULN), and his AST and ALT levels are both within normal limits. His serum creatinine is 1.0 x ULN. The patient has not received prior chemotherapy for his NSCLC, but he did receive radiation therapy to the chest for Hodgkin's lymphoma 20 years ago. He is willing to participate in the study and has no plans to father children during the study period.

Patient is a 10-year-old boy from Denmark who suffers from bladder dysfunction and is dependent on bladder emptying by catheterization. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and has undergone previous urological interventions. His current medication includes antibiotics for the treatment of the urinary tract infections. He has a BMI of 18 and his vital signs are within normal limits. The patient and his parents have been informed about the study and have provided consent for his participation.

A 28-year-old woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the response of vaginal and cervical tissue after exposure to three vaginal products. She is in good health, does not smoke and is not currently on any hormonal contraceptives. Her menstrual cycle is regular, occurring every 28 days. She has no history of abnormal pap smears or genital warts, and has tested negative for STIs. She has not had any surgery or biopsy on her vulva, vagina, or cervix in the past 30 days. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with study procedures and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male with a history of chronic hepatitis C presented to the clinic for a follow-up visit. He was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C 6 months ago and has been on treatment with peginterferon alfa-2a for 14 weeks. His laboratory workup showed a positive HCV antibody, elevated liver function tests, and a viral load of 3.2 million IU/mL. He is currently receiving 180mcg of peginterferon alfa-2a subcutaneously once a week using a pre-filled syringe. The patient complains of discomfort during the injection and difficulty in handling the syringe. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker, non-alcoholic, and has never used illicit drugs. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the tolerability and handling of administering peginterferon alfa-2a using an autoinjector versus a pre-filled syringe.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who is generally healthy but has a total cholesterol level between 5 and 7 mmol/L. He is not currently taking any medication or antioxidants, and does not have any chronic diseases. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the potential health effects of aronia intake. The intervention cross-over study will involve taking standardized amounts of aronia berry tablets or placebo for three months, followed by a washout period of three months, and then another three months of either aronia or placebo tablets. The study will measure various parameters such as blood pressure, lipid fractions, testosterone levels, phase II markers, HbA1c, HSCRP, F2-isoprostanes, and semen quality before and after each period of tablet intake. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and provide all necessary information for the study.

A 52-year-old man with a history of end-stage renal disease secondary to hypertension is scheduled to undergo a kidney transplant. The patient has been on hemodialysis for the past 3 years and has a high immunological risk for graft rejection due to a previous kidney transplant failure. The patient's panel reactive antibody percentage at transplantation is greater than 20%, and his estimated glomerular filtration rate using MDRD formula is greater than 29ml/min. The patient does not have a history of cancer or any previous non-kidney transplantation. The patient is currently receiving tacrolimus, prednisone, and mycophenolate as immunosuppressive therapy. The patient's urinary protein/creatinine ratio is less than 0.3, and he does not have active HBV, HCV, or HIV infection. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 42-year-old man with chronic lower back pain resulting from a car accident 3 years ago. Pain intensity ranges from moderate to severe and is often accompanied by difficulty sleeping. The patient is currently taking pain medication as prescribed by his physician, but has not noticed significant improvement. He has an Android smartphone and is willing to use the Pain Monitor app for daily monitoring. The patient is able to use the app without assistance and is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his pain management.

A 60-year-old female who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago and underwent surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. She lives with her husband and has two adult children who live in a different state. She experienced anxiety and depression during her cancer treatment, and still struggles with fear of recurrence. She has been seeing a therapist and participating in a support group for cancer survivors. She is interested in sharing her cancer experience and providing feedback to help improve care for others impacted by cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with essential hypertension for the past 3 years. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high despite his efforts to control it with lifestyle changes. He has no history of cardiac disease, renal disease or cerebrovascular disorder. He is not pregnant and not nursing. He has no known allergies to AII receptor antagonists, calcium channel blockers or dihydropyridine derivatives. He has not been diagnosed with type I diabetes mellitus on treatment with insulin, or type II diabetes with poor glucose control. He has not been diagnosed with malignant or severe life-threatening diseases in the past 5 years. He is not on any investigational product and has not received any in the last 12 weeks. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

A 35 yo F self-identifying African American with a history of asthma since childhood. The patient has been prescribed an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) for the past 2 years but has had suboptimal adherence due to forgetfulness and concerns about side effects. The patient reports experiencing asthma symptoms at least once a week and has had to use a rescue inhaler on several occasions. The patient has presented at Duke Primary Care clinic for asthma management and is willing to participate in a study aimed at improving ICS adherence in adult African Americans.

A 45-year-old office worker who has a family history of diabetes. He is concerned about his risk of developing the disease and wants to be screened as soon as possible. He has no known medical conditions, but he has been experiencing some fatigue and thirst lately. He has tried to modify his diet and increase his physical activity to reduce his risk of developing diabetes, but he finds it challenging to stick to a long-term plan. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive a diabetes risk assessment to better understand his risk and receive educational sessions to help him manage his risk of developing diabetes. He is comfortable with using web-based self-screening and is willing to participate in surveys to provide feedback on the feasibility and acceptability of the self-screening tool.

A 50-year-old overweight man with a BMI of 30 was referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of green-plant thylakoid supplementation to a restricted diet intervention study. He is otherwise healthy, a non-vegetarian, and a non-smoker. He has not taken any medication for metabolic disturbances, undergone bariatric surgery, or suffered from diabetes. He has not been on a diet or treated with antibiotics during the last 3 months and has no known food allergies. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his metabolic health and is willing to follow the strict diet recommendation and low intensive exercise regimen.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with dysgnathia and is scheduled for surgery. She has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with Lisinopril. She is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. She reports occasional nausea and vomiting after meals, but no other significant gastrointestinal symptoms. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She does not have diabetes mellitus. She has no known drug allergies. Her BMI is 24, and her laboratory tests are within normal limits.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. She underwent a curative surgery for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and there is no evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease as confirmed by CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she has adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. She has not received prior chemotherapy or radiation for her pancreatic cancer. The patient has available tissue for IHC testing of hENT1, and she is willing to comply with study treatment and follow-up. She has the ability to read, understand, and sign an informed consent. She has no other serious medical condition and is not pregnant.

40-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) from an HLA-identical sibling. On day +20, he developed skin rash, diarrhea and elevated bilirubin with aGVHD grade III. He was initially treated with methylprednisolone 2mg/kg/d but had no improvement. Tacrolimus and MMF were added to the therapy, but his symptoms worsened and the aGVHD progressed to grade IV. The patient was then referred to this clinical trial for treatment with mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) from a third-party donor. The patient provided informed consent and will be randomly assigned to the MSCs group. The patient has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or other chronic diseases. He is currently on no medications other than those prescribed for aGVHD and is eager to participate in this trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with leukemia. She is currently admitted to the leukemia/lymphoma/bone marrow transplant floor at Barnes Jewish Hospital. She has been feeling anxious and overwhelmed since her diagnosis and is struggling to cope with her illness. Her husband has been her primary caregiver and is also feeling stressed and worried about her health. They are both interested in learning mindfulness techniques to help them cope with their emotions and improve their overall well-being.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who recently sustained an incomplete spinal cord injury due to a traumatic event. She underwent initial treatment and rehabilitation in a hospital and has been discharged home with assistance. She is able to maintain assisted standing up and is motivated to continue her recovery. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no history of heart or lung disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her improve her balance, gait, and overall quality of life. She understands the study involves aquatic physiotherapy and will require her to attend therapy sessions three times a week for six weeks. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and sign the informed consent form.

A 25-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) in her first remission. She is in good physical condition with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has an HLA-identical sibling donor available for transplantation. She has no history of splenectomy or splenic irradiation. Her bilirubin level is within normal range. She has no known sensitivities to E.coli derived products and is not currently taking any non-licensed drugs that may affect GVHD or engraftment. She is not pregnant or lactating and is HIV negative. She has not received a bone marrow or peripheral blood progenitor cell transplant before.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who was referred to the nephrology clinic after routine urinalysis showed proteinuria and hematuria. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He denies any symptoms such as fatigue, edema, or decreased urine output. Physical examination was unremarkable with normal blood pressure and no peripheral edema. Laboratory tests revealed elevated serum creatinine level (1.3 mg/dL), serum albumin level (3.5 g/dL), and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (0.7 g/g). Renal ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys with no signs of obstruction or cysts. Renal biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of IgA nephropathy. The patient was informed about the clinical trial and agreed to participate. He will be randomly assigned to the TW group (TW at dosage of 90 mg/d), ARB group (valsartan at dosage of 160 mg/d), or combined treatment group (TW at dosage of 60 mg/d and valsartan at dosage of 80 mg/d). The patient will undergo periodic follow-up according to the research arrangement.

The patient is a 48-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with indolent lymphoma (specifically, follicular lymphoma) six months ago. He was initially treated with rituximab and bendamustine chemotherapy, which resulted in a partial response, but the disease relapsed three months later. His most recent PET/CT scan showed multiple lymph node enlargements in the neck, axilla, and groin, and he has been experiencing symptoms such as night sweats, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. He has not received any prior BTK inhibitor treatment, and his laboratory parameters meet the eligibility criteria for the study. A biopsy of his lymphoma tissue is available for evaluation. The patient has no history of autoimmune hemolytic anemia or idiopathic thrombocytopenia purpura, clinically significant cardiovascular disease, severe bleeding disorder or history of spontaneous bleeding requiring blood transfusion or other medical intervention, severe or debilitating pulmonary disease or hypersensitivity reaction to BGB-3111 or rituximab or any of the other ingredients of the study drugs. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of ovarian cancer, which has metastasized to her lungs. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with different combinations of drugs in the past. Her current treatment plan involves paclitaxel and carboplatin, which has been effective in slowing down the growth of the cancer cells. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. She has no history of thromboembolic disease or bleeding diatheses in the past 6 months and has no significant cardiac disease. She is not allergic to Cremophor EL®. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the possibility of combining BMS-690514 with her current treatment regimen to potentially improve the efficacy of the treatment and prolong her survival.

Patient A is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has been advised to undergo mastectomy and is now considering immediate breast reconstruction. She is feeling overwhelmed with the decision-making process and is looking for additional information to help her make an informed decision. She has access to the internet and is comfortable with using online resources. She speaks Dutch fluently and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a web-based patient decision aid for women considering breast reconstruction. She understands the importance of making an informed decision and hopes that participating in this trial will help her feel more confident in her decision-making process.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who is scheduled to undergo a tonsillectomy under general anesthesia. The child has a history of recurrent tonsillitis and snoring during sleep, which has resulted in sleep apnea. The child's medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no known allergies or underlying medical conditions. The child's parent or legal guardian has consented to participate in the study. The surgery is expected to take less than two hours, and no opioids will be used during the operation. The child has no history of ophthalmologic disease or medication use that can affect sympathetic nervous activity.

The patient is a 49-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has no family history of breast cancer, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She underwent a lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy, and the results showed that the cancer had not spread to her lymph nodes. She will be receiving adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy to the breast and axilla. She has no history of any other invasive malignancies or cardiac conduction disturbances. She is not pregnant and is not currently using diuretics. She is able to walk without assistance and is willing to return to the study site for the duration of the study.

A 52-year-old Chinese man was diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer last month. He has no previous history of chemotherapy. He is currently employed as a construction worker but has taken off work due to his diagnosis. He is married with two children. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not smoke but has a history of heavy alcohol use in the past. He exercises occasionally and has no known allergies. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

62-year-old female with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented to her primary care physician with complaints of shortness of breath and fatigue. An echocardiogram was performed and demonstrated a decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) of 35%. The patient was referred to a cardiologist for further evaluation and management. The cardiologist recommended that she participate in a clinical trial to test the performance of a single-lead ECG based algorithm to identify people with decreased left ventricular EF. The patient speaks English, is able and willing to provide informed consent, and has agreed to complete a clinical echocardiogram within 7 days before or after study procedures. She is not currently hospitalized.

The patient is a 28-year-old male from Southeast Asia who presents with a fever and chills. He has a history of P. vivax malaria infection and has been diagnosed with a mono-infection by microscopy. The patient's weight is within the range of 20-80 kg and he has a quantitative glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity that is ≥70% of the population median. The patient is willing to be followed for 6 months and is able to understand the study instructions and provide written informed consent. He is excluded from the study if he is pregnant, lactating, has Hb < 8 g/dL, severe malaria, blood transfusion in the last 3 months, any previous history of a haemolytic event, history of allergic response to an 8-aminoquinoline or the nationally recommended schizonticide (e.g. chloroquine, artesunate-mefloquine, artemether-lumefantrine), or presence of any condition which in the judgement of the investigator would place the patient at undue risk or interfere with the results of the study (e.g. chronic disease, medications that potentiate or inhibit CYP2D6 or CYP2C8 isoenzyme function).

A 33-week gestational age male infant was born via emergency Cesarean section due to maternal pre-eclampsia. The infant was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. The infant was treated with surfactant therapy and remained intubated for 4 days. The infant's respiratory status has improved, and the clinical team has deemed the infant ready for extubation. The infant's weight is 1.9 kg, and the physical exam shows no signs of major cardiopulmonary malformations or upper airway obstruction. The parents have provided written informed consent for the infant's participation in the clinical trial.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, as it focuses on employees at Vitality's partner corporations who have not completed their annual health risk assessment. Therefore, a patient description cannot be generated for this trial.

The patient is a 29-year-old man who is on probation due to a drug-related offense. He has been smoking cigarettes for 10 years, and he smokes about a pack a day. He has tried to quit smoking before, but he has been unsuccessful. He also struggles with substance use disorder and has been in and out of rehab programs. He is currently enrolled in a probation program in Douglas County, NE. He is willing to participate in the study and to provide personal contact information for follow-up interviews. He is able to pass the Mini-Cog test.

10-month-old child presenting to a clinic in Mbarara, Uganda with fever, vomiting, and lethargy for the past 2 days. The child is currently breastfeeding and has received all recommended immunizations, including the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. The parents report that the child has not had any recent illnesses or infections. A lumbar puncture is performed and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is collected for analysis. The child meets the case definition for suspected meningitis and is eligible for inclusion in the study. The parents or guardians of the child provide informed consent for their participation in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis. He is currently admitted to the hospital for a scheduled central line insertion due to poor peripheral venous access for dialysis. He has no known coagulopathy or history of neck surgeries. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy presenting with symptoms of abdominal pain and diarrhea for the past few weeks. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal disease, and his parents are seeking medical attention for their child's discomfort. The patient has not taken any medication or nutritional supplements related to these symptoms. The parents have consented to the child's participation in the study, and the child will undergo a colonoscopy to determine the cause of the symptoms. If the colonoscopy confirms a diagnosis of Crohn's disease, the child will be asked to participate in the second part of the study, which involves logging data in an app and collecting fecal samples at home. The child will also be asked to provide information about their medical and family history, and participate in follow-up visits where anthropomorphic measurements and blood samples will be taken. If the colonoscopy does not confirm the diagnosis of Crohn's disease, the child will be considered for the control group of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman complaining of pelvic pain that has been ongoing for more than 3 months. She experiences cyclical pain associated with her menstrual cycle. She has been diagnosed with minimal to mild endometriosis. She has a regular menstrual cycle (24-35 days) and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has no history of liver disease and is willing to participate in the study. She has no major psychiatric conditions or history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is not infected with hepatitis or HIV. The patient has not been diagnosed with any malignancy or other chronic pelvic pain. She is not a diabetic, nor does she have heart failure. She is willing to use nonhormonal contraception during the study. The patient is seeking a solution to manage her pelvic pain while also having the potential to conceive in the future.

A 35-year-old healthy woman came to the clinic for a routine check-up. She works as a marketing executive and has no underlying disease. She is married for 8 years and uses oral contraceptives. Her menstrual cycle is regular. She does not smoke. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is unremarkable. She has never participated in any clinical trial before.

The patient is a 59-year-old man who smokes a pack of cigarettes a day and has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has been experiencing persistent coughing, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past 3 months. Further evaluation shows that he has stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with metastases to the liver and bones. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of FDG-labeled PET scan in planning chemotherapy for patients with stage IIIB or IV NSCLC. The patient will receive paclitaxel and carboplatin on day 1, followed by an FDG-PET/CT scan between days 18-21. Based on the scan results, the patient will be assigned to one of two treatment groups. If the patient responds to the initial treatment, he will receive paclitaxel and carboplatin for up to 3 additional courses. If the patient is an initial non-responder, he will receive gemcitabine hydrochloride and docetaxel for up to 3 courses. The patient's response to treatment will be evaluated by FDG-PET and CT scans, and he will be followed up periodically after completing the study treatment.

56-year-old female diagnosed with brain metastases from breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo whole brain radiation therapy with a total planned radiation prescription dose between 30 Gy and 37.5 Gy in 10 to 15 treatments. She has been experiencing mild hair thinning and is concerned about significant hair loss following radiation. She is otherwise healthy with no history of scalp dermatologic disease or previous radiation to the scalp. She has not received concurrent or sequential chemotherapy with agents known to commonly cause alopecia. She is interested in participating in a pilot feasibility study to determine if a compression headband can prevent hair loss during whole brain radiation therapy.

The patient is a 67-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He was admitted to the hospital with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue for the past week. The patient reports that he has been compliant with his medications and has not experienced any recent changes in diet or exercise. Upon physical examination, the patient has crackles in his lungs, peripheral edema, and a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. The patient's laboratory results show elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and creatinine levels, indicating decompensated heart failure. The patient's arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.52 and bicarbonate (HCO3) level of 32 mEq/L, suggestive of metabolic alkalosis. The patient is started on diuretics for management of his heart failure symptoms. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and agrees to participate.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who fell down from stairs and suffered a proximal femur fracture. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She takes medications for hypertension and calcium supplements for osteoporosis. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She reports severe pain in her hip and is unable to bear weight on her affected leg. She has been admitted to the hospital for surgical intervention under subarachnoid block in a sitting position. She has no known allergies. Her baseline Numeric Rating Scale for pain at rest and movement is 8/10. She is scheduled to receive either 0.3mg/kg of intravenous ketamine or 1.5mcg/kg of intravenous fentanyl before changing position from supine to sitting for subarachnoid block. She has given written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and a persistent sore throat for the past few months. Examination shows a mass in his throat, and biopsy confirms the diagnosis of locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Further evaluation shows that the cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes. The patient is not a candidate for synchronous chemotherapy or cetuximab due to underlying medical conditions. The patient is otherwise healthy, with a WHO status of 1. The patient is willing and able to undergo radiotherapy with nimorazole and is expected to complete treatment. The patient has not undergone chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the past 6 months within the planned radiation field. The patient's blood work shows adequate renal and liver function, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2.0 x 109/L, creatinine within normal limits, platelets of 150 x109/L, and total bilirubin within normal limits. The patient has no history of malabsorption syndrome or severe and/or uncontrolled medical disease. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with relapsing platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. She has undergone a complete clinical response after the first treatment of relapse with a platinum-based regimen. Her physical exam and chest X-ray are normal, and her CA-125 levels are normal. She has undergone a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy before entering the study and received platinum-based chemotherapy as adjunctive or neo-adjunctive treatment at the first presentation. She has received at least 5 and no more than 8 cycles of platinum combination therapy (i.e. doublet) as treatment for the first relapse. All side effects from chemotherapy have been resolved or are grade 1. The interval between the last dose of the treatment with platinum that achieved clinical CR (complete response) and the first dose of Hu3S193 is less than or equal to 8 weeks. She has a Karnofsky performance status of at least 70%. Her laboratory exams in the first 2 weeks before drug infusion are within normal limits. She has an expected survival of at least 12 months. She has not received Bevacizumab as part of her treatment on relapse. Her diagnosis of primary tumor relapse is not made exclusively based on elevated levels of serum CA-125 with values less than 2-fold the upper limit of normality. She has no mucinous or clear cell histology. She does not have a diagnosis of primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer. She has expression of antigen Ley documented by immunohistochemistry of archived primary or metastatic tumor samples. She has not had concomitant use of systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents. She has no known CNS involvement by the tumor. She has no clinically significant heart disease or ECG indicating clinically significant arrhythmia. She has no history of myocardial infarction within 6 months. She has no other serious diseases that may interfere in the obtainment of accurate study results. She has not undergone radiotherapy treatment, radiopharmaceuticals, biological therapy, anti-estrogen therapy (including tamoxifen), immunotherapy or surgery within 4 weeks before the first administration of investigational product and has recovered from toxic effects of any of these therapies within 6 weeks prior to study inclusion. She has not been exposed to any investigational product within 4 months prior to study inclusion and has no previous treatment with a humanized murine antibody and/or fragment of such antibody.

As this clinical trial is focused on elementary school children, there are no specific patient descriptions needed. However, all students who are enrolled in the elementary school where the trial is taking place are eligible to participate. The only exclusion criteria is if parental consent is not given for the child to participate.

This clinical trial does not require patient recruitment. Instead, it utilizes preexisting data from two national cardiovascular disease registries (Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project and National Audit of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention) in the UK. Therefore, there is no specific patient description needed for this study.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma with liver metastases. She has a positive family history of breast cancer (her mother and sister) and a history of smoking for 25 years. She underwent a complete resection of her primary tumor and has no evidence of residual disease by abdominal/pelvic CT scan or MRI with IV contrast. She has a total of 6 liver metastases, of which 4 were completely resected and 2 were treated by ablation. All resected lesions had a negative surgical margin (R0). The patient has no extrahepatic metastases and her chest CT scan was negative for any disease. She is medically fit to begin chemotherapy between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery. Her performance status is ECOG 1, and her laboratory tests are within normal limits except for elevated alkaline phosphatase (2.2 times upper limit of normal). She has no active hepatitis B or C infection and no histological evidence of cirrhosis. She has not received any prior chemotherapy within 4 weeks before hepatic resection or hepatic ablation. She is not receiving any concurrent immunologic or biologic therapy and has no prior hepatic arterial infusion pump malfunction, malperfusion, or infection.

The patient is a 36-year-old Caucasian woman who has been trying to conceive for the past two years. She has been diagnosed with poor ovarian reserve, with an AMH level of 0.8ng and only 3 mature oocytes retrieved during her previous IVF cycle. Her partner has normal semen parameters according to the WHO 2010 criteria. They are planning to undergo ICSI with fresh embryo transfer. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications or supplements. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Her BMI is 22. She has regular menstrual cycles and has been ovulating regularly. She is married and has been trying to conceive for the past two years. She has no history of any surgeries or medical procedures in the past. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

52-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma. He presents with a history of constipation and rectal bleeding for the past 6 months. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals a 5 cm mass in the rectum with no evidence of distant metastases. He has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy with a Karnofsky Performance Status Index of 80%. His blood counts, liver and renal function are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent. He has not undergone any previous treatment for this cancer and has not been recruited for any other clinical trial in the past 4 weeks. He does not have any planned major surgeries during the study period. He has no history of heart disease or uncontrolled hypertension and is not taking any anticoagulant or thrombolytic agents. He has no malabsorption syndrome and is able to take oral medications. He is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any other significant medical conditions or infections.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with moderate-to-severe COPD for the past five years. He has been a non-smoker for the past two years and is not currently on oral corticosteroids. He experiences shortness of breath during physical activity and has a chronic cough with sputum production. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He lives with his wife and has two adult children who live nearby. He enjoys reading and watching TV. He currently uses a salmeterol inhaler for his COPD symptoms. He has no known allergies or other medical conditions. He is interested in participating in the study as he hopes it may help him better manage his COPD symptoms.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who presents with symptoms of pain during urination, frequent urination, and a strong urge to urinate. She has not experienced these symptoms before and has not been diagnosed with any urinary tract infections in the past. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has a history of occasional urinary tract infections, but has not taken any antibiotics for at least 2 weeks prior to the start of the study. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 16666 & Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 in non-pregnant women with uncomplicated cystitis. She is willing to take the study product twice per day for 12 days and to attend follow-up visits as required. She understands the study requirements and is willing to sign the informed consent form to participate in the trial.

54-year-old male with a history of genotype 1 hepatitis C who had received a previous course of pegylated interferon alfa 2a with ribavirin but did not achieve a Sustained Viral Response (SVR). The patient has no other significant medical history and is in general good health. HCV RNA levels are detectable at >=10,000 international units per milliliter (IU/mL). The patient has not participated in any clinical trial of an HCV protease inhibitor of any duration, nor has he participated in more than 2 drug studies in the last 12 months. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse in the last year and agrees to use two effective methods of birth control during the study and for 6 months after stopping study medication. The patient is not infected with Human Immunodeficiency Virus or hepatitis B and is not pregnant or nursing if female.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who participated in a breast cancer screening program in Spain between 2000 and 2009. She was diagnosed with invasive breast cancer during the screening process. She underwent a lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy and adjuvant radiotherapy. Her tumor was estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-negative, and HER2-negative. She has no family history of breast or ovarian cancer. She has no history of tobacco or alcohol use. She has a body mass index of 24 and practices moderate exercise 3 times per week. Her mammography showed a heterogeneously dense breast tissue. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. Her follow-up visits have been regular, with no evidence of relapse or second neoplasms. She has agreed to participate in this trial to help evaluate the effectiveness of screening programs and the impact of interval cancer on survival and disease-free period.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the neurological intensive care unit (NICU) following a traumatic brain injury resulting from a fall. An external ventricular drain (EVD) has been inserted to measure pressure and drain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the ventricles. The patient has been in the NICU for 2 weeks and is currently stable but at risk for EVD-associated infections (EVDIs). The study aims to test the assumption that blood is homogeneously distributed in the CSF by sampling CSF in patients. The patient will be included in the study based on written informed consent from his nearest of kin. Exclusion criteria are patients admitted with bacterial or viral CNS infections. The patient's EVD will be sampled bi-weekly or during workup for suspected infection. Paired CSF samples will be collected, and the resulting extra collected CSF from paired samples will amount to approximately 1-2 mL per session. The patient's demographic information, admission diagnosis, and date of study inclusion will be collected. The study will evaluate differences between sample groups using one-way tests such as the Wilcoxon signed rank test and the Fligner-Killen test of variance. The patient's ID will be included as a random effect to eliminate inter-individual differences.

A 56 year old woman comes to the clinic after experiencing a sudden onset of severe headache and confusion. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports no history of head trauma or recent surgery. The physical exam reveals right-sided weakness and facial drooping. A CT scan of the brain shows a small intracranial hemorrhage. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to determine the positive and negative predictive value of the Infrascanner in patients with intracranial hemorrhage.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. He works as a construction worker and has noticed that the pain has been interfering with his ability to perform his job duties effectively. He has not sought medical attention for the pain but has tried over-the-counter pain medications and exercises to alleviate the pain. He has no history of knee surgery or injury. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in this study as he believes that a new measurement tool for knee joint function may benefit him and others who suffer from knee pain.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his left knee for several months. He has previously been diagnosed with an articular cartilage defect in the knee and has been advised by his orthopedic surgeon to undergo articular cartilage repair surgery. He has no history of generalized or inflammatory arthritis, and has no significant medical co-morbidities, such as hypertension or COPD. He is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. His MRI scan shows a grade III/IV cartilage lesion of size 5 square cm. He is eligible for the study and will be randomly allocated to receive either the Autologous Collagen Induced Chondrogenesis (ACIC) or Mesenchymal Cell Induced Chondrogenesis (MCIC) treatment. He will be followed up at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year and 2 years following the surgery by visits to the clinic and assessed clinically. His surgical outcomes will be measured by IKDC, KOOS and Lysholm scores, and cartilage growth will be measured by the MOCART score. He will be advised partial weight bearing on the operated leg for 6 weeks after the surgery and will also undergo 5 sessions of physiotherapy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer 2 years ago. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with no significant improvement. The cancer has spread to her lungs and liver, and she has been experiencing persistent coughing and abdominal pain. She has stopped chemotherapy for 4 weeks and all adverse events have resolved. Her ECOG performance score is 2 and she has a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. Her bone marrow, renal, and liver function are adequate. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant. She provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up assessments and procedures.

The patient is a 53-year-old female with a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) confirmed through a biopsy. She has no previous history of chemotherapy. Her platelet count has been consistently low, ranging from 60-70 × 109/L, and she is scheduled to receive the first-line GC/GP regimen chemotherapy. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities, and all her laboratory tests are within normal limits except for the platelet count. She has an ECOG PS of 1 and has been informed about the clinical trial on the prevention of thrombocytopenia after first-line chemotherapy. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study and follow-up process.

A 65-year-old English-speaking female caregiver who lives with her husband, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. The caregiver primarily uses a smartphone and has wireless internet in her home. She has no history of providing care for individuals with non-neurodegenerative conditions affecting behavior and cognition, longstanding Axis I psychiatric disorder, metabolic disorder or major organ dysfunction, alcohol abuse or dependence within 5 years of dementia onset, head trauma with loss of consciousness greater than 30 minutes, contraindications to MRI imaging, large confluent white matter lesions, significant systemic medical illness, or use of medication likely to affect central nervous system functions adversely.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 5 years visits the clinic complaining of swollen and painful joints, fatigue, and stiffness in the morning. She is currently taking methotrexate and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for the management of her RA symptoms. However, she still experiences frequent exacerbations and is looking for additional treatment options to improve her condition. She has noticed that her oral health has deteriorated over the past year, with bleeding gums and bad breath. Upon examination, she is found to have at least one site with periodontal probing depth ≥ 4 mm and clinical attachment level ≥ 3 mm on at least 4 teeth, indicating the presence of periodontitis. She has six natural teeth with root and is fluent in French. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the effectiveness of periodontal treatment to reduce the severity of her RA symptoms. She is informed about the potential risks and benefits of participation and agrees to give her informed consent after a 1-week cooling-off period.

57-year-old male with a history of NSTEMI and mild left ventricular systolic impairment (EF 45%) in the LAD territory. He presents with chest pain and is scheduled for coronary angiogram for a view for PCI. He has no history of stroke, TIA or reversible ischaemic neurological disease within the last 6 months, and no severe valvular abnormalities. He has not undergone any previous PCI to LAD or coronary bypass artery grafting. He is not on warfarin or other medications that may interfere with the test. He is willing and able to give informed consent.

The patient is a newborn infant born to a mother who is a resident of Povungnituk, Inukjuak, and Kuujjuarapik, Quebec or Nuuk, Greenland. The infant's mother is willing to participate in the study, which aims to examine the effects of prenatal exposure to environmental contaminants on cognitive and behavioral development and physical growth in Inuit infants. The study will involve measuring umbilical cord blood samples obtained at birth, milk samples obtained from breast-feeding mothers, and hair samples obtained from the mothers to assess the levels of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), methylmercury, selenium, organochlorine pesticides, lead, Omega-3, and Omega-6 fatty acids. The goal is to determine the potential impact of these contaminants on infant development and to assess the degree to which Omega-3 and Omega-6 fatty acids may offer protection against these effects. The infant's mother is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in this study and is willing to provide informed consent for her infant's participation.

A 32-year-old female presents with a history of chronic moderate to severe asthma for the past 2 years. She has been under treatment with inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting bronchodilators. Her symptoms include wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, especially during exercise. She has never been hospitalized for asthma exacerbation. She does not smoke and has no history of illicit substance abuse, alcohol abuse, or psychiatric illness. During the screening process for this clinical trial, she reports that she has not used systemic corticosteroids in the previous two weeks and is not pregnant or lactating. She gives written informed consent and is within the age range of 18 to 60 years. She is deemed eligible for the study based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma. He has a history of high intraocular pressure (IOP) ranging from 23 to 28 mmHg despite not receiving any medical treatment. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/20, but he has one or more papillary signs on conventional color stereo-slides, including a localized loss of neuroretinal rim, thinning of the neuroretinal rim, and peripapillary splinter hemorrhages. His refractive error is between -1.00 and +1.00 spherical equivalent. The patient does not have a previous history or presence of any disease involving cornea, lens, macula, retina, optic neuritis, or any other disease involving the visual pathways. His pupil diameter is greater than 3 mm without mydriatic or miotic drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to adhere to the treatment regimen.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and a persistent cough for the past week. He was admitted to the hospital with severe respiratory distress and was placed on a ventilator in the intensive care unit. His condition has continued to worsen despite treatment with various medications, including antibiotics and antivirals. He has been screened for transmissible diseases and has tested negative for hepatitis A virus, hepatitis E virus, and Parvovirus B-19. He has no known allergies to hemoderivatives or immunoglobulins. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his informed consent.

A 46-year-old woman was diagnosed with hypertension by her primary care physician 8 months ago. She has been taking antihypertensive medication since then. Her blood pressure during the last checkup was 148/96 mmHg. She reports feeling stressed and anxious at work and at home. She is a full-time employee and has two children who she takes care of in addition to her job. She has some experience with yoga but has not practiced regularly. She is interested in participating in the study to see if yoga can help her manage her blood pressure and reduce her stress levels. She is willing to attend group yoga sessions or practice at home with exercises provided by her doctor. She has no physical or mental disabilities that would prevent her from participating in the study. She speaks fluent Swedish and does not require an interpreter.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with CD123 positivity of more than 20% of blasts. He has received prior treatment with standard of care chemotherapy and has experienced relapse. He has no history of bone marrow failure syndromes, cardiac disease, or pulmonary disease with clinical relevant hypoxia. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 2 months. He has adequate renal and hepatic laboratory assessments and cardiac function, with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥ 45 %. He has a permanent venous access existing (e.g. port-system) and is able to give written informed consent. The patient weighs 65 kg and is using a highly effective method of birth control. He has not undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation within the last two months or developed Graft versus host disease (GvHD) requiring immunosuppressive therapy. The patient has not received treatment with any investigational drug substance or experimental therapy within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives (whatever is shorter) of the substance prior to the day of apheresis. He has no prior treatment with gene therapy products, use of checkpoint inhibitors within 5 half-lives of the respective substance, or autoimmune diseases requiring systemic steroids or other systemic immunosuppressants. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or active/chronic infection with hepatitis C virus (HCV) or hepatitis B virus (HBV). He has no known hypersensitivity to cellular component (UniCAR02-T) and/or targeting module (TM123) excipients or to compounds of the lymphodepletion therapy or tocilizumab or corticosteroids. The patient is capable of understanding the purpose and possible consequences of the trial and is able to follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 27-year-old male diagnosed with hereditary angioedema (HAE) at the age of 15. He experiences recurrent episodes of swelling in various parts of his body including his face, arms, legs, and abdomen. His episodes are often triggered by stress, anxiety, or physical trauma. During his last episode, he experienced severe swelling in his throat which made it difficult for him to breathe. He was rushed to the emergency room and received treatment with C1 esterase inhibitor (C1INH-nf) which helped alleviate his symptoms. He is currently on prophylactic treatment with danazol to prevent future attacks but is still experiencing breakthrough episodes. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of C1INH-nf for the treatment of acute HAE attacks. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and does not have any medical conditions that would interfere with his ability to participate in the study.

50-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of breast cancer, currently undergoing chemotherapy with paclitaxel. The patient reports moderate to severe muscle and joint pain that has persisted for several days after each treatment. Previous interventions attempted to alleviate the pain have failed to produce satisfactory results. The patient has no history of pregabalin or gabapentin use and does not have renal failure with a GFR less than 30ml/min. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has legal competence for expression of consent.

Patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 6 months ago. She has a positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) with a titer of 1:160 and has tested positive for anti-double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (dsDNA) and anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibodies. She has active arthritis and a rash. Her total Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) score is 8. She has not been diagnosed with severe active lupus nephritis or active central nervous system (CNS) lupus. She has no current or recent clinically serious viral, bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infection. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of LY3471851 in adults with SLE.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of heart failure NYHA Class III. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. He has been taking medications for heart failure but has not noticed significant improvement. The patient is scheduled for an ICD implantation due to his condition. He has no history of neurological events or autonomic dysfunction. His ejection fraction is greater than 25% and his systolic blood pressure is above 120 mm Hg on the day of the implant. He has no significant mitral or aortic regurgitation or stenosis. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of right-sided flank pain for 6 months. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. Imaging studies reveal a 10 cm solid mass in the right kidney with no signs of metastasis. The patient undergoes a radical nephrectomy and histological examination confirms the diagnosis of clear cell renal cell carcinoma. The Leibovich score is calculated to be 6. The patient has normal organ function and no history of autoimmune or inflammatory disorders. The patient agrees to provide at least one sample (FFPE tumour block from nephrectomy, or a minimum of 10 unstained slides), as well as a baseline EDTA blood sample for future translational research. He has not received any prior anticancer treatment and has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to durvalumab or tremelimumab. He provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with the trial policy on contraception during the treatment phase of the study and 6 months afterwards.

This is a 58 year-old male who presented with chest pain, shortness of breath and diaphoresis. His ECG showed ST-segment depression and elevated troponin levels were found on admission. A diagnosis of non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome was made and he was admitted for further management. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking atorvastatin and lisinopril. An invasive strategy with PCI has been chosen and he is scheduled for coronary angiography. He has no known allergies or renal insufficiency. His estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) is >60 mL/min/1.73m2. He has no comorbid conditions with a life expectancy of less than one year and is not currently participating in any other trials. He is able to read and write.

As this is an observational study with no patient intervention, there is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial. All patients meeting the inclusion criteria for ARDS during the first two days after AHRF onset will be included in the study. The study will collect data from the existing LUNG SAFE database on patient demographics, arterial PCO2, pH in the first 48 hours, data on P/F ratio over the course of illness, duration of ventilation, ICU stay, hospital survival in patients identified as being exposed to hypocapnia and hypercapnia, and main ventilatory variables. The study will analyze the impact of these factors on the progression of ARDS, duration of ventilation, ICU stay, hospital stay, and patient outcome.

The patient is a 10-year-old Caucasian female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and scheduled for elective colorectal surgery. The patient has a history of allergic reactions to opioids and is currently on maintenance therapy with mesalamine. She has no known allergies to lidocaine or related medications. The patient has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health with a BMI of 22. The patient has a PICC line in place for venous access. The patient and her parents have provided written informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who resides in a nursing home. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which is well-controlled with medications. He is able to perform his activities of daily living with minimal assistance. He has not received any influenza vaccination in the current season. He has not taken any probiotic supplement in the past 2 weeks. He has no known allergies to antibiotics, egg proteins, or adjuvants and excipients of the flu vaccine. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effect of a probiotic supplement on the immune response to influenza vaccination in elderly individuals residing in nursing homes.

Patient is a 62-year-old man from the United States who has previously undergone a prostate biopsy due to an abnormal digital rectal examination. The previous biopsy showed no evidence of cancer, but due to persistently elevated PSA levels, the patient is scheduled for a second biopsy using the ClariCore System. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of bleeding disorders or use of blood thinning agents. He is otherwise healthy and his physical exam is unremarkable. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 7-year-old boy diagnosed with Very-Long Chain Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD) deficiency presents with symptoms of fatigue, muscle weakness, and recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia. He has been on a low-fat diet and has been taking medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) oil, but his symptoms have been difficult to manage. He has been hospitalized several times due to hypoglycemia and is missing school frequently. His parents are concerned about his quality of life and the impact of the disease on his development. They are interested in exploring alternative treatment options and have heard about triheptanoin (C7) oil. They are willing to travel to Pittsburgh, PA to participate in this compassionate use study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and has a documented VLCAD deficiency. His acylcarnitine profile and genetic test are positive for the disorder. His parents are willing to cover any out-of-pocket costs associated with the study and are willing to commit to the required travel and monitoring schedule.

This is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past two years with no success. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and her doctor has recommended that she undergo a stimulated Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) cycle. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. During the cycle, she produced several mature (metaphase II) oocytes which were denudated. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial as she underwent a stimulated ICSI cycle. She does not meet the exclusion criteria as she produced more than one mature oocyte at the time of denudation.
