As a clinical trial specialist, I must clarify that this study does not involve patients, but rather participants. With that being said, here is a potential participant description for this clinical trial:  A 35-year-old female of African American descent who resides in a suburban area of the United States is interested in participating in a study on organ donation attitudes. She is currently employed full-time as a marketing specialist and has a Bachelor's degree in Communications. She has no personal or family history of organ donation but is aware of the importance of organ donation and is willing to participate in a study that investigates the factors that may affect decisions to donate organs.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma. She has been on treatment with topical eye drops for the past 3 years, but her intraocular pressure (IOP) has remained elevated. She has no significant medical history except for mild hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient has no history of ocular trauma or surgery, and she is not currently wearing contact lenses. Her corrected visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes. Her visual field test shows mild peripheral visual field loss in the right eye, but the left eye is normal. Her IOP measurement at baseline is 28 mmHg in the right eye and 26 mmHg in the left eye. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with recurrent SCCHN complains of difficulty swallowing and hoarseness of voice for the past 3 months. He had surgery and radiation therapy for his initial diagnosis of SCCHN 2 years ago. He has a history of smoking for 20 years and quit smoking 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no other medical history. He has been on anti-PD1 therapy for the past 4 months. He is experiencing fatigue and weakness in his legs. He has lost 5 kg of weight in the past 2 months. He is married and has 2 children. He is retired and used to work as a carpenter. He has no other medical history. His ECOG performance status is 1. His tumors are measurable.

35-year-old female with a BMI of 28.5 who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs, but has not been able to achieve sustained weight loss. She has a family history of obesity and is concerned about the health risks associated with being overweight. She is currently a patient at the Institute Orthopedic Rizzoli and has been recommended for a personalized nutritional program. She is interested in participating in a study comparing the effectiveness of a counseling monthly phone call versus a self-help informative booklet in achieving weight loss. She is willing to give informed consent and is not currently taking any medications or food supplements that could alter weight loss. She does not have any history of psychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing lower back pain and stiffness for the past year. The pain is worse in the mornings and improves with exercise. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they only provide temporary relief. She has a family history of ankylosing spondylitis, and her sister was recently diagnosed with the condition. The patient has not been diagnosed yet, but her rheumatologist suspects axial spondyloarthritis based on her symptoms and medical history. She is currently receiving routine care at the Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases in Bath. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates manual spinal mobilisation and its effect on spinal mobility in patients with axial spondyloarthritis. She is willing to provide observational data on her wellbeing and is open to taking part in future trials of interventions that aim to improve outcomes for patients with axSpA. She understands that she may or may not receive the experimental intervention in this trial and is willing to consent to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks gestation, presents to the obstetrics department for elective cesarean section due to a previous cesarean delivery. She has been experiencing occasional mild contractions but has had an otherwise uncomplicated pregnancy. The patient has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is classified as ASA grade I. She does not have any significant medical history, allergies to medications or a history of psychiatric or drug abuse. She speaks the local language and is able to understand and give informed consent for the study. She has no contraindications to spinal anesthesia and agrees to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old French man who has recently undergone bilateral upper limb amputation due to a traumatic injury sustained in a car accident. He is currently in rehabilitation and has not yet received any prosthetic devices. He reports experiencing significant emotional distress and difficulty adjusting to life without his arms. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and is willing to participate in the observational study to help improve understanding of the French population of bilateral upper limb amputees. He does not have any finger amputations and has not previously received a prosthesis for his first amputation.

46-year-old female with a history of benign uterine fibroid tumors and scheduled for transcatheter embolization. The patient has a history of anxiety and reported high levels of distress during previous procedures. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of mental illness, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or adverse reactions to midazolam or fentanyl. The patient is fluent in English and willing to participate in the study.

42-year-old woman presenting with symptoms of depression, including persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities. She reports difficulty sleeping and loss of appetite. The patient has not received treatment with SSRI medication in the past 3 months. She has no history of bipolar disorder or other major psychopathology. The patient's BMI is within normal range. She denies any current thoughts of self-harm or suicide. She is interested in participating in a pilot study to map the peripheral plasma micro-RNA and proteomics patterns in depressive patients, treated with SSRI medications.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). He was diagnosed with low-risk MDS three years ago and has been receiving red blood cell transfusions due to anemia. He has also been experiencing thrombocytopenia for the past 21 days. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has not received prior treatment with azacitidine, decitabine, other hypomethylating agents, or lenalidomide in the past eight weeks. He has not undergone allogeneic or autologous stem cell transplant and is not eligible for such treatment. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, gastrectomy, or upper bowel removal. He does not have thrombocytopenia due to any other possible causes, including medication(s), congenital disorder(s), immune disorder(s), or microvascular disorder(s). He has not used cytotoxic, chemotherapeutic, targeted or investigational agents/therapies, thrombopoiesis-stimulating agents (TSAs), erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) and other red blood cell hematopoietic growth factors within the last 28 days. The patient does not have ongoing medically significant adverse events from previous treatment. He does not have concurrent use of iron-chelating agents, corticosteroids (except for subjects on a stable or decreasing dose for ≥ 1 week prior to randomization for medical conditions other than MDS), or any significant medical condition, laboratory abnormality, or psychiatric illness that would preclude his participation in the study.

This is a 55 year old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented with abdominal pain and rectal bleeding. Colonoscopy revealed two lesions in the colon, both measuring greater than 6mm. The patient has no history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease or familial adenomatous polyposis. Bowel preparation was deemed sufficient for the procedure. A biopsy of the lesions showed benign adenomatous polyps. The patient was recommended for either endoscopic resection or surgery, and magnification narrow band imaging (NBI) was used to accurately evaluate the depth of the neoplasia to determine the appropriate course of treatment.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on enrolling eligible participants who meet the inclusion criteria of being HIV-infected and actively injecting drugs, and who are willing to provide locator information for their sexual and/or injecting partners. The trial will be conducted in Nairobi, Kenya, and will enroll 1000 participants through a needle and syringe exchange program.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with a history of good general health. He has a modified gingival index score of 2.5 and greater than 60 percent bleeding sites at initial presentation. He has a minimum of 20 natural teeth and is not currently wearing any orthodontic appliance. He has not received antibiotic therapy in the last 30 days nor has he been taking any chronic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications. He is not immune-compromised and does not have a history of any medical conditions or medications that might affect the assessment of the study treatment or periodontal tissues. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and protocols and does not have any history of participation in another clinical trial within the last 30 days. He is not pregnant or breast-feeding, nor is he a woman of child-bearing potential refusing to use an acceptable method of birth control. His liver and kidney function tests are within the normal range.

57 yo M with a history of long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (>1 year) with symptoms of palpitations, fatigue, and dyspnea on exertion despite prior treatment with anti-arrhythmic drugs. He has good left ventricular function and no significant valvular heart disease. He is interested in pursuing a more definitive treatment for his AF and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial comparing catheter ablation to thoracoscopic surgical ablation. He has no contraindications to anticoagulation and has not had a cerebrovascular accident within the last 6 months. He has not undergone prior thoracic or cardiac surgery, and has not had a prior left atrial catheter ablation for AF. He is able to provide informed written consent and has no active malignancies or other severe concomitant conditions that would preclude him from undergoing study-specific procedures. He does not have any implanted intracardiac devices that are not MRI-compatible.

A 56-year-old man was diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma, which is located within 10cm of the anal verge. He underwent rectal MRI, which showed clinical stage T3N1. The tumor sample obtained during biopsy was confirmed to be adenocarcinoma, and the patient is willing to provide additional samples for MGMT expression and hypermethylation testing. He has no prior history of chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiation therapy, and his major organ functions are adequate. He is in otherwise good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no evidence of systemic metastasis or other malignancy within the past 5 years. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has given written informed consent.

35 y/o female diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) for 3 years. The patient has been on methotrexate and prednisone for the past year but has been experiencing frequent joint pain and stiffness, affecting her daily activities. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is interested in improving her medication adherence and clinical outcomes. The patient has no history of pregnancy or lactation. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in exploring other options to manage her RA.

A 55-year-old man presents with a history of snoring and interrupted sleep. He reports feeling fatigued throughout the day and has difficulty staying alert while driving. He has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and is otherwise healthy. He has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorders in the past, but his partner has reported that he snores loudly and gasps for air during the night. A sleep study was conducted, which revealed an apnoea/hypopnea index (AHI) of 10 events/hour, with events occurring at a frequency of 2:1 when supine. His total % supine sleep is 70% of total sleep. He has no other secondary sleep pathology or cardiac disease. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and is able to wear the device around his neck during treatment demonstration and initiation. His neck circumference is 16 inches (40cm). He does not have any skin sensitivity or open wounds around his neck, tics, or tremors of the head. He is able to sleep in a non-supine position. He is not a female of child-bearing potential.

Patient is a 52-year-old male with a confirmed advanced melanoma with superficial and visceral metastases. The patient has received prior therapy with anti-CTLA4 and anti-BRAF/anti-MEK treatment, and is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial. The patient has measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1, a performance status of 2 on the ECOG Performance Scale, and adequate organ function. The patient has cutaneous or subcutaneous metastases from melanoma that are accessible for the application of electric pulses using the single-use, sterile CLINIPORATOR™ electrodes. The patient has lesions clearly requiring palliative treatment, and has a treatment-free period of three weeks before enrolling in the study. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 3 months, and is willing to use an adequate method of contraception as outlined in the eligibility criteria. The patient has no active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years, no history of non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids or current pneumonitis, and no active infection requiring systemic therapy. The patient has no known history of active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C, and no primary ocular melanoma.

The patient is a 35 year old female with a history of headaches and seizures that started 2 years ago. MRI shows a left temporal lobe mass with surrounding edema. She underwent surgical resection and the pathology report shows Grade II astrocytoma with IDH1 mutation confirmed by DNA sequencing. She received radiation therapy and has been on observation since then. However, her recent MRI showed an increase in the size of the tumor and she has been experiencing new onset symptoms of headaches, nausea, and vomiting. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria, including having written documentation of IDH1 mutation, histopathological diagnosis of a glioma of WHO grade II, unequivocal progression on brain MRI, and measurable tumor of at least 1 cm x 1 cm in diameter by MRI. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) of 80 and fulfills hematologic, hepatic, and renal function requirements. She has not been previously treated with any therapy targeting IDH1, nor has she received any cytotoxic chemotherapy. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use highly effective contraception methods during dosing and for 30 days after the use of the investigational medication.

A 58-year-old man who was admitted to Bonsucesso Federal Hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes confirmed the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. The patient was stable and classified as Killip I. The patient has no history of unstable angina or pacemaker, and his systolic blood pressure is above 80 mmHg. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and will be randomized to receive either CPAP or Bilevel ventilation for 30 minutes. The patient's age is within the eligibility criteria of 45 to 80 years old. The patient will have ventilatory and hemodynamic variables registered, as well as electrocardiogram signals recorded for the posterior analyses of HRV.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been living with HIV for the past 3 years. He has been receiving treatment for the past 60 weeks as part of ACTG 328 and his viral load is currently less than 2,000 copies/ml. He has not experienced any opportunistic infections related to HIV. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial testing an HIV vaccine called Remune to see if it can improve his immune system's response to HIV-related antigens. He is willing to continue his current treatment until after completing 24 weeks on the study. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not taking any prohibited medications.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been diagnosed with stage 4 chronic kidney disease and has been under the care of a nephrologist for a year. His most recent lab work shows a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, serum ferritin level of 250 ng/mL, and a transferrin saturation (TSAT) level of 22%. He has not received any phosphate binder medication in the past 4 weeks. He has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding, inflammatory bowel disease, inflammatory bowel syndrome, or Crohn's disease. He has not received any intravenous iron or erythropoiesis-stimulating agents in the past 4 weeks. He has no history of hemochromatosis and is not currently taking any investigational drugs. He has a negative serum pregnancy test (for females of child-bearing potential), and he does not have any known allergies to iron products. He is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and is not planning any surgery or hospitalization during the trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy Caucasian male with no prior history of serious medical conditions. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 80 kg with a BMI of 26 kg/m^2. He works as an accountant and exercises regularly. He does not smoke or use recreational drugs, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no allergies or hypersensitivity to medications or any excipients. He has not participated in any clinical trials or received investigational medicinal products within the past 3 months or 5 half-lives. He has not received live vaccinations within the past 4 weeks and does not plan to receive any during the study. He has not been exposed to more than 4 new chemical entities within the past 12 months. He has no clinically significant abnormalities in laboratory assessments and has a normal eGFR by CKD-EPI calculation. He has not had any major surgeries or blood loss exceeding 500 mL within the past 3 months. He has a normal neutrophil and lymphocyte count and his ALT and bilirubin levels are within the normal range. He has a normal QTc interval of less than 450 msec. He is capable of giving signed informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form and the protocol. He meets the

The patient is a 25-year-old male who lives in Tbilisi, Republic of Georgia. He was recently diagnosed with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis and has not received any anti-TB therapy for more than a week. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial being conducted at the Georgia National Center for Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases (NCTBLD) in Tbilisi. He will be randomized to receive either a Vitamin D pill or a placebo for a period of sixteen weeks, while also receiving standard TB therapy. The patient has no history of significant medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to attend all seven study visits at the NCTBLD in Tbilisi and is committed to completing the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old African American woman who presented with generalized bone pain, fatigue, and decreased appetite for the past 2 months. She reported no significant medical history and was not on any regular medication. Laboratory tests revealed anemia, hypercalcemia, and elevated creatinine levels. Further evaluation with bone marrow biopsy and serum protein electrophoresis confirmed the diagnosis of multiple myeloma. The patient is eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation as per institutional guidelines. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and her renal function is borderline with a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min. The patient is postmenopausal and has no plans to conceive. She has no known allergies or intolerances to monoclonal antibodies or human proteins. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and has given voluntary written consent.

55 yo M with a history of stage IV colon cancer and currently undergoing chemotherapy. The patient reports experiencing breakthrough pain despite being on strong oral opioid analgesics. The patient reports taking the short-acting narcotic analgesics at least twice daily due to breakthrough pain for the past 3 days. The patient is able and willing to comply with the overall study requirements, including keeping a participant diary for pain. Past Medical History: - Stage IV colon cancer - Currently undergoing chemotherapy - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Depression - Anxiety - GERD - Osteoarthritis of the knee - History of smoking (quit 10 years ago)

A 55-year-old male who recently underwent surgery for stage II squamous cell cancer of the head and neck is seeking participation in a clinical trial to prevent the recurrence of cancer. He has a history of smoking but has quit within the past year. The patient is currently in good health, with normal blood counts and normal liver and kidney function. He has not undergone any other cancer treatments, and he has no history of peptic ulcer disease or gastritis/esophagitis within the past 60 days. The patient has not used NSAIDs within the past 30 days at a frequency of 3 or more times a week for more than 2 weeks and is not currently taking any other COX-2 inhibitors. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help prevent the recurrence of his cancer and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who is morbidly obese with a body mass index (BMI) of 40. She has a history of hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea. She is scheduled for an elective surgery that requires endotracheal intubation. She is alert and oriented with no shortness of breath or coughing. Her airway assessment reveals a Mallampati score of 3, and she has a neck circumference of 47 cm. She has no history of difficult intubation or airway obstruction. Her vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, a heart rate of 85 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. She has no allergies to medications or anesthesia. She has been fully informed about the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic melanoma. He has previously received treatment with a PD-1 inhibitor. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is considered medically fit to undergo procurement of starting material and ATL001 administration procedures. He has measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1. His organ function is adequate, and his anticipated life expectancy is ≥ 6 months. He has no known leptomeningeal or CNS metastases, and he has no ocular, acral or mucosal melanoma. He does not have active infectious disease or require immunosuppressive treatments or regular treatment with systemic steroids. He has no clinically significant, progressive, and/or uncontrolled renal, hepatic, haematological, endocrine, pulmonary, cardiac, gastroenterological or neurological disease. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he has not undergone major surgery in the previous 3 weeks. He has no active concurrent cancer or a history of cancer within the past 3 years (except for in situ carcinomas or non-melanomatous skin cancers) or a history of organ transplantation. He has not received any investigational cell or gene therapies and has no contraindications for protocol specified agents. He is willing to undergo highly effective contraception if female partner of childbearing potential.

A 52-year-old male veteran diagnosed with stage 4 chronic kidney disease with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 30 ml/min/1.73 m2. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is currently well controlled with antihypertensive medications. He also has a history of smoking but has quit 5 years ago. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and weakness. His hemoglobin level is 9.5 gm/dL, and he has been diagnosed with anemia of CKD. The patient is a candidate for erythropoietin therapy but is concerned about the increased risk of stroke and heart disease associated with high doses of erythropoietin. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of low-dose erythropoietin given more frequently and the same cumulative dose of erythropoietin administered as a high dose once every two weeks. The patient is willing to undergo non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging to assess the progression of carotid artery plaque and isolate endothelial cells from blood vessels to investigate the signaling pathways triggered by activation of the heterodimeric beta common receptor. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up assessments.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for the past 4 years. She has ANA-positive, as per the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 1997 criteria. She is currently on standard of care therapy for SLE, which includes hydroxychloroquine and steroids. Her platelet count is 80 × 10^9/L, leukocyte counts are 3.5 × 10^9/L, CD19+ B cell counts are 150/μL, and hemoglobin is 13 g/dL. Her liver function tests and renal function tests are normal. She is using an IUD for contraception. She does not have any active CNS lupus or bleeding disorders. She does not have any significant unstable or uncontrolled acute or chronic diseases other than SLE. She does not have any significant lupus complications, such as lupus pneumonitis or lupus gastrointestinal diseases. She does not have any bleeding disorder secondary to SLE. She does not have any active, severe lupus kidney disease. She has not had any acute or chronic infections requiring systemic antibiotic, antifungal, or antiviral therapy within the past 60 days. She does not have known HIV infection, hepatitis B virus infection or hepatitis C antibody positive. She has not received any live-attenuated vaccine within the past 2 months. She has not received injectable corticosteroids within the past 2 weeks. She has not received abatacept, anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha agents, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasmapheresis, mycophenolate, MTX and leflunomide or therapies not otherwise specified in protocol within the past 2 months. She has not received cyclophosphamide or chlorambucil within five half-lives of screening. She has not received rituximab, belimumab, or any other B cell-depleting or modulating therapies within the past 6 months. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not received any investigational therapeutics within the past 30 days or 5 half-lives prior to screening, whichever is greater. The patient is able to provide written informed consent in accordance with federal, local, and institutional guidelines.

The patient is a 10-month-old female infant who is scheduled for a non-emergent surgical procedure that requires moderate or deep neuromuscular blockade with either rocuronium or vecuronium. She is categorized as American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Class 2. The infant has no significant medical history and has not participated in any clinical trials previously. The infant is not on any medication that can interfere with the study treatments given in this trial. She has no neuromuscular disorder that may affect NMB and/or trial assessments. The infant is alert and active with a normal growth and development chart. She has no allergies to study treatments or its/their excipients, to opioids/opiates, muscle relaxants or their excipients, or other medication(s) used during general anesthesia, and is not expected to require mechanical ventilation after the procedure. The parents have provided written informed consent for the infant's participation in the study.

52-year-old female with Sjögren's syndrome and a history of dry eye symptoms for the past 6 months. The patient reports experiencing burning, itching, and redness in both eyes, along with a gritty sensation and excess tearing. She has been using over-the-counter artificial tears with minimal relief. The patient has been diagnosed with corneal and conjunctival damage by an ophthalmologist. The patient has not had any punctal plugs or surgery for occlusion of the lacrimal puncta. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for dry eye treatment and meets the inclusion criteria for this Phase III study.

Patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who exercises regularly but does not perform strength training. She has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary or metabolic disease, and is not currently taking any medications that affect endocrine or cardiovascular function. She is not pregnant and does not smoke. She has a body weight of 132 pounds and is 5'6" tall. She is willing to have blood samples taken and is comfortable with needles. She has no dietary restrictions and is willing to complete food preference questionnaires and Automated Self-Administered 24-hour Recall (ASA24) for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effects of resistance training on her body and to contribute to scientific research.

46-year-old African American female residing in Wisconsin with a history of depression. The patient has been previously diagnosed with depression and has received treatment in the past, but often feels reluctant to seek professional help due to cultural and religious beliefs. The patient is interested in participating in the "Oh Happy Day: Still I Rise Class" to learn more about depression and how to manage it with the use of a guided class and self-help workbook. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. The patient is willing to attend the one-time 4-hour class and complete workbook activities as well as participate in follow-up assessments at the end of the class and 3-months post-class. The patient hopes to gain a better understanding of depression and improve her self-management of depression.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer. Her lung biopsy revealed the presence of an EGFR sensitising mutation, specifically Ex19del. She has no history of any other malignancies and has not received any prior treatment for her lung cancer. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has a predicted survival of at least 3 months. She has at least one measurable tumour lesion as per RECIST v1.1. She has agreed to use effective contraception during the study period and for at least 3 months after completion of the study treatment. The patient has provided informed consent prior to any study procedure.

53-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) presents with palpitations, lightheadedness, and shortness of breath. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of smoking. The patient is currently on metoprolol and atorvastatin. He has been symptomatic despite medical therapy, and after evaluation, it was decided that catheter ablation with THERMOCOOL SMARTTOUCH®SF (STSF) Catheter guiding by Ablation Index (AI) is the best course of action. The patient is willing and able to comply with all pre-, post- and follow-up testing and requirements. He is able to sign an informed consent form and does not have any exclusion criteria. The patient will be included in the study data to evaluate the effectiveness and safety outcomes of catheter ablation with STSF and AI for PAF up to 12-month follow-up.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo elective major abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She has no known allergies. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for mild obesity. Her lab studies are within normal limits, and she has no history of skin or systemic disease with itching. She has been informed about the study and has consented to participate.

35-year-old female with a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) by American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria. She has active SLE disease and is autoantibody-positive. She is currently on a stable SLE treatment regimen which includes corticosteroids (prednisone), antimalarial (hydroxychloroquine) and immunosuppressants (azathioprine). She is not pregnant or nursing and has not received treatment with belimumab or any B cell targeted therapy (for example, rituximab) in the past year or any biological agent (for example, adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, or anakinra) in the past 90 days. She has not received a live vaccine within the past 30 days. She does not have severe active lupus kidney disease or severe active central nervous system (CNS) lupus. She is negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B, and hepatitis C. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further enhance knowledge regarding the side effects of belimumab when given with other lupus medicines to adults with active SLE.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing menstrual pain since she started having her periods. She has been diagnosed with endometriosis after undergoing laparoscopic surgery. She has moderate to severe pelvic pain, which is located in the lower abdomen and radiates to the back and legs. The pain is dull and crampy and often interferes with her daily activities. She has a regular menstrual cycle that lasts for 5-7 days, and the pain is worse during the first few days of her period. She has tried non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and oral contraceptives, but they have not provided adequate pain relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a new medication, ASP1707, for endometriosis-associated pelvic pain. She is not currently using any hormonal contraceptives and has not undergone any recent surgeries or procedures for endometriosis. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with recurrent chordoma in her sacrum. She has previously undergone surgical resection and radiation therapy. She complains of persistent pain in her lower back and difficulty walking. Her performance status is 1 on the ECOG scale. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and migraines. She takes lisinopril and sumatriptan for these conditions. She has no history of other malignancies. She has no known allergies to medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has adequate bone marrow and end organ function, as defined by the eligibility criteria. She has had a recent MRI scan that shows measurable disease. She is willing to participate in the pharmacokinetic studies and has signed informed consent. She has not received any other investigational agents within the past 28 days. She is not on enzyme inducing anticonvulsants or valproic acid. She does not have any Grade III/IV cardiac problems and has normal cardiac function. She does not have a known diagnosis of HIV infection. She has not received chemotherapy within the past 4 weeks. She has not had a major surgery within the past 2 weeks.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with subacute pain in her right arm that has been present for the past two weeks. She reports a sharp, localized pain overlying a soft tissue area of her arm, which is consistent with a herniated trigger point. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study. She has access to text messaging services, email, and the internet and is able to be reached by telephone for follow-up. The patient does not have any major neurovascular structures underlying the area of pain and does not have any chronic systemic illness or medication treatment that would make her prone to prolonged bruising or significant swelling after manipulation. She does not have any connective tissue, dermatologic, neurologic, orthopedic, or vascular conditions that would exclude her from participation in the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for the intervention and standard care.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for fluconazole tablets. He has no significant medical history and does not take any regular medications or supplements. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He reports that he is able to consume a normal diet and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. He has not used any drugs or substances known to be strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP enzymes in the past 10 or 28 days, respectively. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

Sarah is a 35-year-old woman who works as a teacher. She has been experiencing sensitivity in her teeth for the past 6 months, especially when she drinks cold beverages or eats sweets. She has been using a desensitizing toothpaste, but it only provides temporary relief. She has no history of dental caries or trauma. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she takes no medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has good oral hygiene and visits the dentist regularly for check-ups. On examination, she has a noncarious cervical lesion on her left mandibular first molar with a depth of 1.5 mm. The lesion is located on the buccal surface of the tooth and is not associated with any other restorations. The tooth is not mobile, and there is no inflammation or bleeding on probing in the surrounding gingival tissue. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and expresses interest in participating to find a long-term solution for her tooth sensitivity.

A 65-year-old Chinese man with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents with shortness of breath on exertion, cough, and wheezing for the past year. He has a 30-pack-year history of smoking and has quit smoking for the past 5 years. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and he is on medication for it. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and wheezing on lung auscultation. Spirometry shows a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 45% predicted and a FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio of 0.5. Echocardiography showed an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) of 55 mmHg. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of being a stable COPD patient and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 25-year-old college student who has been an active athlete since high school. He recently tore his ACL while playing basketball and is scheduled for ACL reconstruction surgery in the next few weeks. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He lives a healthy lifestyle, exercises regularly, and maintains a healthy diet. He is motivated to return to his active lifestyle and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially enhance his rehabilitation process after surgery. He understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to sign an informed consent form. He has no history of peripheral vascular disease, deep vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism. He has no contraindications to moderated blood flow restriction therapy and is able to comply with post-operative ACL reconstruction rehabilitation. He meets the age criteria and has an isolated ACL tear.

The patient is a 30 year old male who is generally healthy and has no history of diabetes or any other major illnesses. He is not taking any prescription medication or supplements that affect glycemia. His blood pressure is within normal range and he is a non-smoker. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about the potential benefits of American ginseng root on glycemia. The patient has a fasting plasma glucose level of 5.2 mmol/l and has normal renal and hepatic function. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all study visits.

Patient is a 34 year old male who sustained deep partial thickness and full thickness burns in a house fire. He has burns on his left arm, chest, abdomen, and left leg, amounting to approximately 30% of his total body surface area. Despite receiving standard of care treatment for 4 weeks, it is expected that more than 90cm2 of his wounds will remain open. He has no known allergies to amphotericin B, gentamicin, penicillin, streptomycin, or bovine collagen. He has not participated in any other clinical trials with conflicting endpoints within the last 30 days and is not expected to become pregnant or father a child during the clinical course of the study. He is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and has provided signed informed consent.

The patient is a 35 year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 45 kg/m2. She has a history of morbid obesity and has attempted diet and exercise programs in the past with limited success. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has no history of gastrointestinal conditions such as ulcers, esophageal varices, big hiatus hernia or gastric vascular malformations. She is psychologically stable and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic constipation for the past year. She reports having bowel movements less than three times a week and has tried over-the-counter laxatives without much relief. She describes her stools as hard and lumpy and sometimes experiences pain when passing them. She has not had any recent changes in diet or exercise routine. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription medications. The patient is willing to try alternative therapies and is interested in the potential benefits of acupuncture. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit substances. She is not pregnant and has never received acupuncture or herbal therapy in the past.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been previously diagnosed with breast cancer that has metastasized to her bones. She has been experiencing bone pain and her medical history shows that she has already received chemotherapy and radiation therapy for her cancer treatment. She is currently taking bisphosphonates to manage her bone metastases. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and she has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2,000/mcL and a platelet count of 120,000/mcL. She has no history of peripheral neuropathy or other serious medical conditions. Her cardiac function is normal, and she is negative for HIV and hepatitis B and C. She has not been pregnant or breastfeeding in the past year and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. She is currently not taking any immunosuppressive medication. Based on the eligibility criteria, the patient is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial testing the addition of radium-223 dichloride to the usual chemotherapy treatment for advanced breast cancer that has spread to the bones.

45-year-old woman recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. She underwent mammography which showed a suspicious lesion and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma. Physical examination did not reveal any palpable lymph nodes. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery and sentinel lymph node biopsy. She has no history of breast cancer or breast surgery. She has no breast implants and is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in this study and has voluntarily agreed to do so.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastases to the liver and lymph nodes. She has no significant medical history. The patient has been receiving anti-PD-1 immunotherapy for the past 6 months as part of her treatment regimen. The electronic patient file "DxCare" at the University Hospitals of Montpellier confirms that the patient has received the therapy. The file also shows that the patient has a documented % eosinophilia level. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

A 24-year-old woman visited the clinic complaining of blurred vision, redness, and pain in her left eye for the past week. She has a history of autoimmune disease and was diagnosed with idiopathic intermediate uveitis in her right eye two years ago. Her medical history is significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus, for which she takes insulin. On examination, her visual acuity is 20/20 in the right eye and hand motions in the left eye. Intraocular pressure is 18 mm Hg in both eyes. Slit-lamp examination reveals cells in the anterior chamber and vitreous haze in the left eye. She was prescribed prednisone, but her symptoms did not improve, and she developed steroid-induced glaucoma. She is now being considered for the MUST trial to compare systemic therapy versus fluocinolone acetonide implant therapy. She has no history of scleritis, ocular toxoplasmosis scar, or HIV infection. She is willing to participate in the trial and understands the risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who is scheduled to undergo hip replacement surgery under general anesthesia. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. He does not have any cognitive impairment or psychiatric disorders, and his MMSE score is 28. He has completed high school education and is functionally independent. He is not currently taking any sedative or antidepressant drugs. He has not taken vitamin B12, folic acid, or their derivatives in the past 6 months. He has never undergone cardiac or neurological surgery in the past year. He has no history of alcohol or drug dependence. He does not have any severe visual or auditory problems. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

50-year-old male with a history of HIV infection for 10 years. The patient is currently on HAART with a CD4 count of 220 and an undetectable viral load. The patient was recently diagnosed with HCV infection and is HCV RNA positive. The genotype of the HCV virus is unknown. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and joint pain for the last few months. The patient also has a history of type 2 diabetes that is well-controlled with oral medications.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II with rapid cycling. She has a history of cocaine and alcohol abuse within the past six months. She has no past medical history of major medical illness. She has no history of intolerable side effects to lithium or divalproex sodium at levels of 0.6 mEq/L, or to lamotrigine. She has not been previously treated with lithium, divalproex sodium, and lamotrigine concurrently, nor has she been treated with an adequate trial of lamotrigine that was considered a treatment failure. She is not currently pregnant or at risk of becoming pregnant during the study. She has not been diagnosed with a CNS neoplasm, uncontrolled metabolic, demyelinating or progressive degenerative disorder, active CNS infection or any progressive neurological disorder. She has not been treated with any dose or duration of a tricyclic antidepressant within the last three months. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old female with a history of high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) diagnosed 2 years ago. She has received several rounds of chemotherapy including fludarabine but her disease has relapsed and progressed since her last treatment. She has not undergone stem cell transplantation and is ineligible for arsenic therapy. She has an International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS) score of at least 1.5 based on more than 10% marrow blasts, cytopenias in at least 2 lineages, and adverse cytogenetics. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and she has no history of hemolytic anemia or G6PD deficiency. Her hepatic and renal function is normal, and she has no active heart, pulmonary, or psychiatric disease. She has no active uncontrolled infection and is not pregnant or nursing. She has undergone previous chemotherapy and radiotherapy treatments and has recovered from prior chemotherapy with no greater than grade 1 chronic toxic effects.

A 68-year old retired librarian fell from a ladder at home and experienced a proximal humeral fracture. She was taken to the emergency room and was diagnosed with a 3-part fracture. The patient complains of pain and limited movement of her affected arm. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She lives alone but has close family and friends who can help her with daily activities during her recovery. The patient is alert and oriented, with no signs of dementia. She is able to understand and follow instructions in both Finnish and Swedish. She has no history of previous fractures or injuries to her upper limbs. She is not a heavy drinker, and her breathalyzer test shows no signs of intoxication. The treating surgeon has determined that she is a suitable candidate for the study and has explained the study to her in detail.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage II colorectal cancer. He is scheduled to undergo surgery at The Ottawa Hospital in the next few weeks. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He reports occasional fatigue but denies any other symptoms. He has no known allergies and has not had any recent infections. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable mass in the left lower quadrant of his abdomen. His vital signs are within normal limits. Blood tests reveal normal liver and kidney function. He provides informed consent to participate in the trial and agrees to provide fresh blood samples before and after surgery for the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who had previous exposure to sulfur mustard gas during military service many years ago. He presents with worsening dyspnea over the past 10 days, with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.30, PaCO2 of 55 mmHg, and PaO2 of 48 mmHg. The patient is conscious, alert, and able to cooperate with the study procedures. However, he has facial lesions that may preclude the use of NIPPV. The patient's oxygen saturation is 89% on room air. The patient has not experienced a pneumothorax in the past month and does not have severe respiratory failure or hemodynamic instability that would require intubation. The patient is currently receiving a FIO2 of 0.5 via nasal cannula.

A 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia has been experiencing auditory hallucinations for the past 3 years. He is currently taking antipsychotic medications but has not shown significant improvement. He has difficulty concentrating and completing daily tasks. His family history includes schizophrenia in his mother's side of the family. He works part-time as a delivery driver but has been struggling with his job due to his symptoms. He has no history of substance abuse or major physical illnesses. His hearing is normal based on recent audiometry tests. He has no metal implants or pacemaker. He is able and willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the protocol-related procedures.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who is scheduled for hernia repair at Ain Shams University. He has no significant medical history and has never undergone surgery before. He is currently in good health, with no recent illnesses or hospitalizations. He is expected to receive sevoflurane anesthesia during the surgery. His parents report that he has no allergies or adverse reactions to medications. The patient is able to communicate and follow instructions, and his cognitive and developmental abilities are considered age-appropriate. He has no known neurological or psychological disorders. His airway is expected to be normal and no bleeding disorders are reported. The parents have given informed consent for their child to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old woman with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presents with symptoms of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. She has been refractory to at least one Class 1 or Class 3 antiarrhythmic medication. She has no history of left ventricular dysfunction, LA enlargement, atrial thrombosis, or valvular heart disease. She has not undergone prosthetic heart valve replacement, has no history of atrial fibrillation ablation, and has no existing liver or kidney disease. She does not have any malignant tumors or hematological system diseases. She is not pregnant. She has been diagnosed with hyperlipidemia but has not been taking statins.

A 52-year-old male with a history of heartburn, dysphagia, and chest pain is diagnosed with a large paraesophageal hernia of greater than 5 cm on an upper gastrointestinal study. He complains of postprandial abdominal pain, early satiety, and chronic anemia. He has undergone treatment with proton-pump inhibitors (PPI) for the past year with minimal relief of symptoms. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no other significant medical history. He is able to participate in follow-up evaluations and is free of cognitive impairment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

Samantha is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy, and the pathology report showed that her cancer was hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, and stage II. Her oncologist recommended that she undergo chemotherapy, and she agreed to participate in the CALGB 40101 trial. Samantha is married and has two children, ages 12 and 15. She works full-time as a project manager at a software company and is the primary breadwinner for her family. She is concerned about how her cancer and its treatment will affect her ability to work and support her family. Samantha's mother had breast cancer when she was in her 50s, but Samantha has no other significant medical history. She speaks English fluently and is comfortable communicating in English.

This is an 80-year-old male who has been admitted to the cardio thoracic surgery department for a cardiac procedure. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild cognitive impairment. Given his age and medical history, he is at high risk for developing delirium during his hospital stay. As part of the Clinical Evaluation Program of DeltaScan, he will be enrolled in a prospective multicenter stepped wedge cluster randomized trial to test the effectiveness of the DeltaScan in detecting delirium. During the 12-month study period, he will undergo EEG recordings using the CE-certified DeltaScan, which will be applied using a strip with EEG electrodes mounted to his head using self-adhesive gel. The EEG recording will be performed two to three times daily and takes 3-4 minutes. The primary endpoints of the study are the delirium detection rate and duration of admission at the non-ICU department. The secondary endpoints include time interval between admission and the first delirium positive assessment, number of days with at least one positive delirium assessment, delirium incidence, hospital mortality, and direct medical costs of hospitalization. Based on the study design and previous research on the DeltaScan, the burden and risk of misclassification are considered to be minimal.

A 54-year-old male presents to the emergency department with sudden onset chest pain radiating to his left arm. The pain began about 1 hour ago and is not relieved by rest. He has no history of chest pain or heart disease. He is a smoker and has a history of high blood pressure. The patient is alert and oriented, with a blood pressure of 142/90 mmHg, heart rate of 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. The electrocardiogram shows ST segment elevation in the anterior leads. The patient is diagnosed with STEMI and is immediately transferred to the catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention. He receives aspirin, heparin, and clopidogrel. The procedure is successful, with no complications. After the procedure, the patient is admitted to the intensive care unit for monitoring. His vital signs remain stable, and he is started on beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors. He has no family history of cardiovascular disease. He agrees to participate in the study and signs the consent form.

Patient is a 67-year-old female from the United States who is diagnosed with osteoporosis with a T-score of -3.1 on her DXA scan. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and does not smoke or use any drugs that could affect bone metabolism or physical function. She is able to walk independently and has not had any recent bone fractures or orthopedic surgeries. The patient is interested in participating in a pilot study to investigate the possible association between sarcopenia and the risk of fall in osteoporotic postmenopausal women. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to undergo blood sampling and thigh muscle quality evaluation through MR.

Pt is a 60yo postmenopausal woman who has a history of fragility fractures of the hip and wrist. She has a T score of -3.2 at the lumbar spine and -2.7 at the total hip on DXA scan. She has not used any osteoporosis medication in the past 6 months and is willing to adjust her dietary calcium to <750mg (i.e. two servings per day of calcium rich food). She has a BMI of 25 and is a non-smoker with no alcohol use. She is not on any medication that is known to affect bone metabolism. She has no history of metabolic bone disease, hyper- or hypoparathyroidism, hypo- or hypercalcemia, renal disease, history of kidney stones, or hypercalciuria. Her serum vitamin D level is 30 ng/dL. She is willing to undergo bone biopsies for histomorphometry and micro computed tomography (µCT), bone marrow aspirates for molecular studies, peripheral blood to detect circulating bone progenitor cells, and dual X-ray absorptiometry. She is not on medication that would interfere with the trial and meets all other inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety for the past several months. She reports feeling overwhelmed, hopeless, and having difficulty sleeping. She has tried counseling in the past but found it difficult to maintain due to her busy work schedule. She is interested in trying a self-guided digital format that can be done at her own pace and from the comfort of her own home. She has access to a computer and mobile phone with internet connection. Upon screening, her scores on the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 are both 7, indicating significant depression and anxiety symptoms. She has no history of suicidal ideation or attempts and is not currently experiencing any psychiatric or somatic problems that would interfere with the intervention. She is fluent in Swedish and is able to participate in the study for the full duration of four weeks.

Pt is a 35yo F with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and no known history of metabolic diseases, not currently taking any medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol regularly. She is not on oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not experienced significant weight loss or gain in the past 6 months. She does not have any contraindications to calorie restriction or exercise. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at improving metabolic function and preventing type 2 diabetes. She is willing to undergo a single day of negative energy balance induced by either calorie restriction or aerobic exercise, and is willing to have her insulin sensitivity, beta-cell function, and glucose tolerance assessed. She understands that the study may involve some discomfort, such as having an IV inserted and blood draws, and may require her to stay at the study center overnight. She has read and understood the informed consent form and agrees to participate in the study.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) according to the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) criteria. The patient has advanced HCC defined as unresectable disease which is not amenable or refractory to local-regional therapy or with extra-hepatic involvement. The patient has received prior systemic treatment with sorafenib for at least 14 days, resulting in disease progression or intolerance with sorafenib treatment. Sorafenib must be the last antineoplastic treatment before enrollment. The patient is suitable for percutaneous tissue biopsy and has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. The patient's hematological, renal, and hepatic function are adequate as assessed by blood tests sampled at the screening visit. The patient's life expectancy is longer than 12 weeks, and the patient has at least one measurable lesion assessed by CT scan or other imaging within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of PEG-BCT-100. The patient has a normal ECG and is willing to provide written informed consent prior to any study-specific screening procedures with the understanding that the patient has the right to withdraw from the study at any time, without prejudice.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 35 who has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath for the past six months. She has not received any periodontal treatment in the past four months and has not been on any antibiotics or steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during this period. She has a full complement of teeth and is not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of obesity on non-surgical periodontal therapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo mastectomy. She is considering immediate breast reconstruction using a tissue expander. The patient has no history of radiation therapy to the breast(s) and has a BMI of 30. She is a non-smoker and is fluent in English. The patient is willing to use acellular dermal matrix (ADM) in the reconstruction procedure. She has no chronic pain or other medical conditions that would interfere with the study. The patient has been informed of the two options for tissue expander placement - subcutaneous versus subpectoral - and is willing to participate in the study to help determine which option may provide a better outcome in terms of pain, wellbeing, and overall satisfaction with reconstruction.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage liver disease (ESLD) and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). He has been experiencing fatigue, jaundice, and abdominal swelling for the past few months. His lab results show elevated liver enzymes, low albumin levels, and high bilirubin levels. Imaging studies reveal cirrhosis of the liver and portal hypertension. After undergoing an evaluation, he is considered a candidate for Adult-to-Adult Living donor Liver Transplantation (LDLT). The patient has no history of cardiac arrhythmias or hepatopulmonary hypertension. He is informed about the clinical trial investigating somatostatin as a liver inflow modulator and is interested in participating.

A 35-year-old Hispanic man reported a history of fatigue, night sweats, and intermittent fever for 2 months. He also noticed weight loss of approximately 10 pounds during this period. Laboratory investigations showed pancytopenia with a white blood cell count of 2.9 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin level of 8.2 g/dL, and a platelet count of 72 x 10^9/L. A bone marrow biopsy revealed a diagnosis of high-risk acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with complex cytogenetics. The patient was started on induction chemotherapy with 7+3 (cytarabine and daunorubicin) and achieved complete remission. However, he had a relapse after 6 months of follow-up. The patient's family members were evaluated for a potential stem cell donor, and a partially matched related donor was identified. The patient is now being considered for a peripheral stem cell transplant in combination with a preparative regimen comprising total body irradiation, cyclophosphamide, thiotepa, and fludarabine, in order to prevent further relapse of AML. He has no significant past medical history and has never undergone any surgical procedures. The patient's vital signs are stable, and he does not have any significant comorbidities. He has agreed to participate in this clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who presents with a history of decreased visual acuity in his left eye for the past 4 months. He reports no significant medical or ocular history. His best corrected visual acuity is 50 in the left eye and 80 in the right eye. Examination reveals a central retinal vein occlusion with macular edema in the left eye. The OCT central subfield thickness is 290. The patient has not received any intravitreal anti-VEGF or steroid treatments in the study eye within the past 6 and 8 weeks, respectively. Additionally, there is no evidence of active iris neovascularization. The patient has no uncontrolled systemic diseases and has not experienced any IOP elevation in response to corticosteroid treatment in the past that required more than 2 glaucoma medications.

A 16-year-old female named Rose has been living with HIV for the last two years. She has been receiving treatment at a clinic in Uganda and is currently taking ART medication. However, Rose has been struggling with adherence to her medication regimen and has missed at least one dose per week on average. She has access to a mobile phone and has agreed to participate in the study to improve her adherence. Rose speaks and understands both English and Luganda, and intends to stay at the clinic for the study period. She is not in boarding school where phones are forbidden. The study will involve weekly SMS reminders and support messages to help Rose adhere to her medication regimen.

45-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years, currently taking metformin and sulfonylurea for glycemic control with a HbA1c of 8.5%. She regularly consumes a light breakfast consisting of yogurt and fruit. She has no history of severe hypoglycemia in the past 24 weeks and has no contraindications to study medications. She is willing to follow the study protocol and has given written consent for participation in the clinical trial. She has no significant cardiac, renal, or liver disease and is not currently undergoing therapy for a malignancy. She has a regular sleep/wake cycle and a body mass index of 28 kg/m^2.

This is a 30 year old male with a history of chronic periodontitis and bleeding on probing. He is a non-smoker and has not used antibiotics in the past three months. He is not pregnant and does not have any diagnosed cardiac conditions. He does not have any uncontrolled medical conditions or allergies to tetracycline. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and is interested in participating in a randomized controlled clinical trial to investigate the effects of scaling and root planing (SRP) with and without minocycline HCl microspheres, 1 mg on periodontal pathogens and overall bacterial load.

65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and smoking presents with abdominal discomfort and back pain. Imaging reveals an abdominal aortic aneurysm measuring 5.5 cm in diameter. The patient has no previous history of surgery or stent placement. The patient is otherwise healthy and has a life expectancy greater than 2 years. The patient is interested in exploring endovascular treatment options and is willing to comply with the study's follow-up schedule.

The patient is a 42-year-old man scheduled to undergo bariatric surgery due to his obesity-related health issues such as diabetes, hypertension and sleep apnea. He has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. His BMI is 45 and he has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years. He is currently taking metformin and lisinopril for his diabetes and hypertension, respectively. He has no history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease. He is an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) 3 status. He is interested in participating in the study to help further understanding of the relationship between melatonin levels and postoperative pain management in bariatric surgery patients.

This is a 25 year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past year. She has never been on any medication for her depression and has not been in therapy. She reports a lack of energy, feeling sad most days, and difficulty concentrating. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence, and is not currently taking any medication. She has no medical conditions that would contraindicate treatment with naltrexone, and does not have any metal implants or foreign metallic objects in her body. She has no history of seizures or epilepsy. She is fluent in English and has signed the written informed consent. She is willing to stop taking any antidepressant medication for at least 21 days prior to the collection of imaging data. She is not currently suicidal or considered a high suicide risk. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 13-year-old female presents to the optometry clinic with complaints of blurred vision while reading, double vision, and headaches. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past six months. She has no significant medical or ocular history, and her family history is negative for ocular disorders. On examination, the patient has a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20 in each eye at distance and near. She has a near point of convergence of 10 cm with a break of 6 cm, which is receded. Her fusional convergence at near is 10 prism diopters base-out, and her exophoria at near is 10 prism diopters greater than at distance. The patient's stereopsis is 40 seconds of arc with Randot stereoacuity test. Based on the patient's history and clinical findings, she is diagnosed with convergence insufficiency. She is eligible for the Convergence Insufficiency Treatment Trial (CITT) and is randomized to receive either Home-based Pencil Push-Up Therapy, Home-based Pencil Push-ups with Computer Vision Therapy/Orthoptics, Office-based Vision Therapy/Orthoptics, or Placebo Office-based Vision Therapy/Orthoptics. The patient will be followed up for 12 weeks, with additional follow-up visits at 6 and 12 months after completion of the active treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 10 years. She has noticed that her gums bleed easily and are swollen, and she has been experiencing bad breath. She has been avoiding visiting the dentist due to fear of pain and high expenses. She has a family history of periodontitis, and her father lost his teeth due to this condition. She has a healthy diet and exercises regularly. She is not on any antibiotics, fungicidal, hormone or corticotherapy. She has never been pregnant and is not under guardianship. The patient is well-nourished and well-groomed. Upon examination, it is noted that she has gingival inflammation and bleeding upon probing at multiple sites. The teeth are mobile and there is evidence of bone resorption. The patient is eligible for the trial as she has a minimum of 10 teeth and is a diabetic patient with periodontitis.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia. He has been experiencing symptoms for the past 2 years, including delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized speech. He has been previously treated with risperidone but was non-compliant with his medication regimen. He has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 at screening and a PANSS score of 65. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently experiencing suicidal thoughts or violent behavior. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with study procedures.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is focused on comparing the effectiveness of two different methods of training healthcare professionals in detecting and managing delirium in patients. The trial is looking to recruit ICU nurses, general ward nurses, private ward nurses, and nurse anesthetists who have not previously been exposed to the CAM-ICU assessment tool. The trial aims to assess the trainees' satisfaction with e-learning and identify any problems associated with its implementation, as well as investigate the causes of inaccurate CAM-ICU assessment for improvement in future training sessions.

A 28-year-old male patient, who was born with a congenital upper limb structural abnormality, experiences significant loss of function. His right arm is shorter than the left arm, and he has limited range of motion and muscle weakness on his right side. He has tried various treatments but has not seen significant improvement. He is not a candidate for surgical intervention due to the complexity of his condition, and he is interested in trying orthoses to improve his function. He has no history of pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) or other implantable electrical devices. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol as prescribed.

A 54-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presented with complaints of persistent cough, fatigue, and weight loss of 10 pounds in the last three months. A CT scan revealed a large mass in the right lung, as well as mediastinal and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. A biopsy of the lung mass confirmed a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with PD-L1 expression of 60%. The patient was started on treatment with Immune Checkpoint Blockade (ICB) and has completed the first infusion. She is interested in participating in the Immunosup study to help identify immune-related biomarkers that can predict the efficacy of immunotherapy. She is compliant with follow-up appointments and has no contraindications to the study procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of diabetes for 10 years. She has been experiencing some vision problems recently, including blurred vision and difficulty seeing at night. She is concerned about the possibility of diabetic retinopathy and would like to have her eyes checked. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently involved in any other clinical trials. She has good visual acuity and is able to take clear fundus photographs. She understands the nature of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

A 30-year-old female with a long history of epilepsy comes to the Epilepsy Monitoring Unit (EMU) for seizure monitoring. She has experienced tonic-clonic seizures in the past and has been on anti-epileptic medications for several years. Despite the medication, she still experiences breakthrough seizures and her physician has recommended that she be admitted to the EMU for further evaluation. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and has agreed to participate. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or any other respiratory conditions that would exclude her from participation.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired man who is concerned about his memory and language abilities. He is currently living alone and has noticed difficulty recalling words during conversations with friends and family. He has a history of hypertension, controlled with medication, and has never smoked or used any recreational drugs. He is currently not engaged in any consistent exercise program and spends most of his day sitting and watching TV. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the trial procedures. He has not participated in any experimental study for at least 3 months prior to enrollment. He has received consent from his primary health care physician to participate in the aerobic exercise. He is determined to improve his cognitive abilities in order to maintain his independence and quality of life.

A 23-year-old college student is interested in participating in a clinical trial to earn some extra money. She is of average height and weight, with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives. She has a regular menstrual cycle and had a negative pregnancy test at screening. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for 90 days following completion of therapy. Overall, she is in good health and has no history of seizures, hypertension or orthostatic hypotension. She has no history of suicidal ideation or significant head trauma. She is willing to give written informed consent and is interested in participating in Part A of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who spends most of her day sitting at a desk working on a computer. She has been experiencing neck pain and stiffness, particularly at the end of the day, and has noticed that her head seems to be tilted forward. She has tried stretching and adjusting her posture, but the problem persists. Her craniovertebral angle (CVA) is measured to be less than 52 degrees, which confirms the diagnosis of forward head posture.
