She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of Body-blade exercises on her neck posture, function, and muscle strength. The patient does not have any musculoskeletal system diseases and is not diagnosed with any other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with end-stage renal disease who is preparing for a living donor renal transplantation. He has been on dialysis for the past 3 years and has not had any prior organ transplants. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are currently well-controlled with medication. The patient has no significant cardiac or hepatic dysfunction, and his coagulation function is normal. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve the outcomes of renal transplantation.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 18. She has been using a tethered insulin pump with Lispro insulin for the past 2 years. Her latest Hemoglobin A1c level was 8.5%. She consumes more than 60 grams of carbohydrate each day and has no known tape allergies. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to follow the protocol and sign informed consent. She is comfortable wearing experimental infusion sets and having photographs taken of her infusion sites. The patient has good communication skills in the language of the investigators. She has never had diabetic ketoacidosis or severe hypoglycemia resulting in seizure or loss of consciousness within the past 3 months. She has no active infections and no known medical conditions that might interfere with the completion of the protocol. The patient has not had any cardiovascular events in the last 6 months and does not have acute proliferative diabetic retinopathy, adrenal disorder, or current treatment for a seizure disorder. She has not been in inpatient psychiatric treatment in the past 6 months and has been stable on her medication for the past month. The patient does not use SGLT inhibitors and does not have end-stage kidney disease.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease (stage 3b) due to diabetic nephropathy. He has been on a stable drug regimen, including renin angiotensin system (RAS) blockade, for at least 4 weeks. Despite this, his blood pressure remains uncontrolled with an office (attended) systolic blood pressure of 150 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 95 mmHg and 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 85 mmHg. He is not on any other medications that could cause secondary hypertension, and he has not had a prior renal denervation procedure. He has not experienced a myocardial infarction, unstable angina pectoris, or a cerebrovascular accident within the past 3 months. He is not pregnant, nursing, or intending to become pregnant. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol and attend all required visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 2 years. He has been managing his diabetes with oral hypoglycemic agents and diet control. His fasting plasma glucose level is consistently under 200 mg/dL. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has mild renal impairment with a GFR of 60 ml/min/1.73m2 based on the Japanese GFR estimation equation. He has no history of insulin use, diabetic ketoacidosis, dysuria or urinary tract infections, genital infections, or significant renal, hepatic or cardiovascular diseases. He does not have any severe gastrointestinal diseases. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical research and improve treatment options for patients with diabetes mellitus and renal impairment.

The patient is a 35-year-old mother of a 6-year-old daughter who has been struggling with her daughter's eating habits. Her daughter is a picky eater and often prefers fast food over healthier options. The mother works full time as a marketing executive and often finds herself short on time to prepare healthy meals at home. She frequently takes her daughter to a popular quick-service restaurant chain for lunch or dinner. The mother is interested in participating in the study to learn about healthier options for her daughter and to see if the messaging campaign will help her make better choices when dining out. The family lives in the intervention community and visits the restaurant at least twice a week.

A 30-year-old male presents with premature ejaculation (PE) and is generally healthy. He does not have a history of cardiovascular disorders and does not have any type of implanted pacemaker/defibrillator. The patient reports no hypertension, diabetes mellitus, local dermatological disease, or any neurological or psychiatric disorders or medications. He is able to follow study instructions and complete study assessment tools. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of a new treatment for PE using electrical stimulation delivered to the perineum.

The patient is a 6-year-old child who will undergo a minor-medium elective surgical procedure with a general anesthesia indication. The child has been experiencing preoperative anxiety and the parents are concerned about the impact it may have on the child's well-being during and after the procedure. The child has no psychomotor deficits, does not use psychoactive drugs, and has no hearing or visual impairment. The parents are not illiterate and have agreed to participate in the study. The child and parents have been randomly allocated into one of four groups: control group (receiving only conventional verbal information), informative group (receiving a leaflet containing information about the anesthetic procedure), smartphone group (receiving only conventional verbal information and the child receiving a smartphone application before entering the operating room), and smartphone and informative group (receiving a leaflet containing information about the procedure and the child receiving a smartphone application before entering the operating room). The child's anxiety will be assessed using the modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (m-YPAS) on three occasions: at the ward, in the waiting room, and at the operating room. The study aims to determine whether the quality of information provided to relatives and the use of a smartphone application can have an impact on the prevalence and level of the child's preoperative anxiety.

A 54-year-old woman presents with persistent stomach pain and discomfort, bloating, and nausea. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. The patient reported no history of tobacco use or alcohol consumption. Physical examination revealed no significant findings except for mild epigastric tenderness. Diagnostic workup, including endoscopy and biopsy, revealed adenocarcinoma of the stomach. Imaging studies showed metastases to the liver and peritoneum. The patient's laboratory values were within normal limits except for a slightly elevated alkaline phosphatase (AP) level of 130 U/L and a mildly elevated AST level of 45 U/L. Her ECOG performance status was 1. The patient has not received any prior therapy for her metastatic disease. She is not pregnant and has no history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to docetaxel or other drugs formulated with polysorbate 80. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during and for at least 3 months after the completion of study therapy.

A 45-year-old man with a history of chronic lower back pain came to the clinic seeking treatment. He has tried various pain medications with no significant improvement and has been experiencing chronic pain for the past 6 months. He completed the expected double-blind treatment period of the pivotal Tapentadol (CG5503) Phase 3 trial in low back pain (R331333-PAI-3011, KF5503/23). He is not lactating, sexually active, or planning to have children. He is willing to take Tapentadol (CG5503) extended release (ER) and the rescue medication supplied for the duration of the trial. He does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse, seizures or epilepsy, brain injury, or uncontrolled hypertension. He has normal renal and hepatic function and is not taking neuroleptics, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, or tricyclic antidepressants within 14 days prior to screening.

A 27-year-old man works as a software engineer and has no significant medical history. He is in good health and has not been exposed to COVID-19. He lives alone in a rented apartment and practices social distancing as recommended by the health authorities. He is interested in participating in the SARS-CoV-2 Inactivated Vaccine clinical trial to contribute to the fight against the pandemic. He has no history of allergies to vaccines or vaccine ingredients and has never had a severe adverse reaction to any vaccine. He has not received any vaccination within the last month and has no plans to move from the study area before the end of the study period. He is willing to comply with the instructions of the investigator and the schedule of the trial. He has read and signed the informed consent form and is committed to participating in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with permanent atrial fibrillation three years ago. He reports experiencing occasional palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he has been taking lisinopril 10 mg daily for the past year. His blood pressure has been well-controlled on this medication, with readings averaging around 130/80 mmHg. His echocardiogram shows a normal ejection fraction. He has no history of heart failure or myocardial infarction. He is currently not taking any other medications, but he is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate new treatments for his atrial fibrillation. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome, currently not treated with thiazolidinediones. The patient reports experiencing chest pain and underwent testing that showed objective documentation of myocardial ischemia. The patient is scheduled to undergo percutaneous coronary angiography and the coronary arteriogram shows one or more 20% to 70% stenosis in at least one coronary artery. The baseline MDCT coronary angiogram also reveals one or more discernible plaques untreated by stenting in at least one coronary artery. The patient has no history of Class III or IV heart failure, creatinine levels are within normal limits, and the patient does not have hepatic disease. The patient reports moderate glycemic control with an HbA1c level below 9.0% and fasting triglycerides below 1000 mg/dl. The patient is able to understand and cooperate with protocol requirements and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient B is a 55-year-old female who has been diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer. She has previously undergone surgery and chemotherapy but has experienced disease progression. She is experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. She has adequate organ function with leukocytes of 4,500/mcL, absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mcL, platelets of 150,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal limits, AST of 50 U/L, creatinine within normal limits, and creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The patient is wild type for KRAS and BRAF oncogenes, and has known PIK3CA mutation status and PTEN expression status. She is not receiving any medications or substances that are inhibitors or inducers of CYP450 3A4. The patient has no active CNS metastases or carcinomatous meningitis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of angina pectoris for the past 5 years. He has been taking nitroglycerin as needed for chest pain but his symptoms have become more frequent and severe in the past few months. He underwent balloon angioplasty 2 months ago due to a significant lesion in his LAD, but the procedure was not successful due to the presence of calcified plaque. His current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, and atorvastatin. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a BMI of 30 and has been a smoker for the past 40 years, but quit 2 years ago. He has no history of cancer or stroke. His recent echocardiogram showed an LVEF of 45%. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the use of rotational atherectomy in patients with balloon-resistant calcified coronary lesions.

45 yo F with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis, diagnosed at age 35, presents to clinic for routine follow-up. Patient reports occasional right upper quadrant pain and intermittent pruritus, but denies any significant changes in her bowel movements or abdominal swelling. She has a history of ulcerative colitis, which is well-controlled on mesalamine. The patient denies a history of liver transplant, hepatic encephalopathy, or malignancy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provides informed consent. The patient will be sent home with a survey to complete and return via mail. Demographic information and clinical data will also be obtained from the patient's electronic medical record.

A 48-year-old male with a history of melanoma that has metastasized to the liver, lungs, and brain is currently undergoing treatment with pembrolizumab. He has received a total of 20 doses of pembrolizumab and has progressed on therapy. He has not received any other anti-cancer therapy since starting pembrolizumab. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has submitted initial imaging. He has adequate organ function and has provided a baseline tumor biopsy. He has no history of immunodeficiency or chronic systemic steroid therapy. He has no active infections and has no history of tuberculosis, hepatitis B or C, or HIV. He has no gastrointestinal conditions that might affect the absorption of lenvatinib. He has not undergone major surgery within the past 3 weeks and has no pre-existing gastrointestinal or non-gastrointestinal fistula. He has no radiographic evidence of major blood vessel invasion/infiltration and no clinically significant hemoptysis or tumor bleeding within the past 2 weeks. He has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease within the past 12 months and has not received prior radiotherapy within the past 2 weeks. He has not received a live vaccine within the past 30 days and is not currently participating in or has participated in a study of an investigational agent or used an investigational device within the past 4 weeks. He has no history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the study or interfere with participation for the full duration of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing neck pain, numbness, and weakness in his right arm for the past 3 months. He has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and pain medication but has not seen any improvement. He has no history of previous cervical spine surgery or cancer. He does not have osteoporosis or any other disease that affects bone quality. He has only one level of degeneration in his cervical spine and is within the age range of 30-70. He has not been diagnosed with ossification of posterior longitudinal ligament, kyphosis at the index level, or developmental stenosis. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

32F with a history of asthma since childhood was referred to the study for evaluation of persistent asthma symptoms. She reports experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness at least twice a week despite the use of albuterol as needed. She reports occasional cough, particularly at night or with exercise. Her asthma exacerbations have been infrequent and have not required hospitalization. She reports no recent changes in her symptoms and no new allergies. She currently uses albuterol as needed but has not been on any maintenance therapy. She does not smoke and has no significant co-morbidities. Spirometry performed during her visit showed a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 70% predicted and a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 85% predicted. Her FEV1 increased by 15% and 250 mL after administration of albuterol. She met the inclusion criteria for the study and provided informed consent to participate.

A 60-year-old man presents with stiffness, tremor and slowness of movement which have been present for the past 2 years. He has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease by a neurologist and has been treated with levodopa/carbidopa. He reports that his symptoms have improved with medication but he still experiences occasional freezing of gait episodes. He has no history of falls or fractures related to his gait disorder. He has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. He reports no significant cognitive impairment and is able to follow oral commands. He has no history of major depression or other significant mood disorders.

The patient is a 45-year-old healthy woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, peripheral arterial occlusive disease, coronary arterial disease, liver cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, stroke, anemia, asthma, chronic bronchitis, any metabolic diseases, any hematologic disease, uncured cancer, or chronic uncontrolled infection. She does not have any other disease that may limit her daily activities. She is a native English speaker and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She has regular menstrual cycles and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her blood pressure is within the normal range, and her body temperature is also normal. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to give informed consent.

Patient is a 52-year-old man from the United States with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking metformin for his diabetes and is not taking any sulphonylureas or insulin. He has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has no known history of malabsorption, renal or liver disease, and has not been treated with steroids. He is interested in participating in this study to help further understand the effects of glutamine on blood glucose levels and GLP-1 and insulin secretion in individuals with type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with lymphoma. He has previously undergone chemotherapy, but his disease is still in partial remission. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is married and has two children. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies. His performance status is less than 2. He has a matched unrelated donor, and no HLA identical sibling is available. He has not been previously exposed to Campath or Rituximab. His serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. His cardiac EF is 60% of predicted levels, and his PFTs are normal. He lives in Houston and is willing to stay in the area for about 100 days after the transplant.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and ischemic cardiomyopathy. He had a CRT device implanted 6 months ago but has not shown any improvement in his heart failure symptoms. He reports ongoing shortness of breath, fatigue, and exercise intolerance despite receiving optimal medical therapy for heart failure. His echocardiogram shows severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 25%. He has no other significant medical history and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. He has no contraindications to undergoing a cardiac MR, and his renal function is normal.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has had a stoma for the past three years due to colorectal cancer. He has been using an adhesive strip for the past year to secure his ostomy bag in place. He has intact skin around the stoma area and has not received radiotherapy or chemotherapy in the past two months. He is not currently taking any medication that may affect the peristomal skin. He has no known dermatological problems in the peristomal or abdominal area. He has given written informed consent and is willing to participate in the evaluation of the performance of a new adhesive strip.

Pt is a 10-year-old male with a history of ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency with multiple hyperammonemic episodes in the past year, despite adherence with a low protein diet and sodium phenylbutyrate (NaPBA). The patient is experiencing frequent headaches and vomiting and has a venous ammonia level of 120 μmol/L at enrollment. The patient is enrolled in the study to evaluate the long-term safety of HPN-100 for the treatment of his urea cycle disorder. The patient will be monitored monthly for safety and control of their venous ammonia. Adverse events and concomitant medications will be recorded on an ongoing basis. The patient and their legally acceptable representative have provided signed informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not currently taking any medications known to increase venous ammonia levels. The patient does not have a history of QTc prolongation or a QTc interval ≥ 450 msec. The patient is not currently breastfeeding or lactating.

A 55-year-old male patient was diagnosed with peripheral artery disease based on a recent ankle brachial index test, which revealed an index of 0.8. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He reports that he frequently experiences leg pain, cramping, and numbness, which has been affecting his ability to walk and perform daily activities. He is currently taking medications for his blood pressure and has tried exercise therapy, but it has not significantly improved his symptoms. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his peripheral artery disease.

A male or female child between the ages of 3 to 24 months or between 7 to 17 years old, who has documented evidence of HIV-1 infection. The child must have a body weight of more than 2.5 kg and an absolute CD4+ cell count of 200 cells/mm3 or higher. The child can either be ART-naïve or ART-experienced, with certain exceptions. The parent or legal guardian of the child must provide written informed consent for the child's participation in the study. Female subjects of childbearing potential must have a negative serum beta human chorionic gonadotropin (Beta-HCG) test at Screening, confirmed by a negative urine pregnancy test at Baseline. The subject must be willing to use an effective method of contraception while enrolled in the study and for at least 1 month after the last dose of emtricitabine if sexually active and/or of childbearing potential. Subjects with certain laboratory parameters at Screening and other clinical or laboratory abnormalities are excluded from the study. The subject must not have a history of acute or chronic (clinical or biological) pancreatitis.

The patient is a 25-year-old female smoker who has been smoking for the past six years. She works as an administrative assistant and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in any physical activity. She has a history of asthma but has not experienced any symptoms for the past year. She is not on any medication and has no history of cardiovascular disease. She has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. She is interested in participating in the study as she wants to improve her cardiovascular health and reduce her smoking habits. She is willing to commit to a 12-week resistance training program and is open to using nicotine replacement therapy if she is randomized to that group. She is excited to learn about new strategies to improve her health and is willing to follow the study protocol.

23 year old woman who has been recruited by the Air Force and is preparing to attend Basic Military Training (BMT). She has no active or past injury that has precluded her from participating in physical activity or that she has sought medical attention for, and does not have a medical profile that excludes her from running. She has a baseline level of fitness and has some experience with running, but has not received any previous gait analysis or personalized training recommendations. She will undergo baseline fitness testing when she is within 16 weeks of attending BMT, which will consist of a timed mile and a half run, two-minute timed pushup test, and two-minute timed sit up test. After fitness testing, she will undergo the RunDNA Analysis within three days to assess mobility, strength, and running form. Based on the results, she may be assigned to an intervention group that will receive personalized training programs to improve mobility, strength, and running form, or a control group that will not receive the intervention. She will then go through a minimum of 8 weeks of training at a Developmental Training Flight using the mobile app and GPS watches to track compliance and training loads, and will undergo a second RunDNA Analysis within 2 weeks of attending BMT to monitor changes in fitness, mobility, strength, and running form. She will be monitored through the mobile application during BMT to assess Fitness Test performance, injury rates, utilization of medical services, graduation rate, and subjective pain and fatigue reports.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been suffering from fibromyalgia for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing widespread pain throughout her body and has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by a rheumatologist based on the ACR criteria. She has tried various treatments, including pain medications and physical therapy, with limited success. She does not have any other severe pain conditions such as diabetic peripheral neuropathy or post-herpetic neuralgia. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is willing to participate in the long-term safety and tolerability study of [S,S]-reboxetine for fibromyalgia.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage II Hodgkin's lymphoma. He underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. He had a mandatory PET scan at diagnosis which showed PET positivity after 2 cycles of ABVD (Deauville score 5). He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any other abnormalities. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a software engineer and is married with no children. He provided voluntary written informed consent and is affiliated with the social security system. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

Mary is a 62-year-old female who was diagnosed with angle closure glaucoma in her left eye. She has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication to control it. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. Mary has no history of keloid formation or bleeding disorders. She has not undergone any previous surgeries in her left eye, except for a cataract removal surgery a year ago. She currently wears glasses and has been advised to discontinue the use of contact lenses during the study. Mary is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the research in glaucoma treatments.

This is a 60 year-old male with a diagnosis of metastatic hormone refractory prostate cancer (HRPC). He has undergone multiple treatments for his cancer, including surgery and radiation therapy, but his cancer has progressed and is no longer responding to conventional hormonal therapy. He has not received any previous cytotoxic therapy or anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab or thalidomide. He has well-controlled hypertension on anti-hypertensive medication. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status between 0 and 1 and is able to swallow capsules. He is willing to use effective means of contraception for the study duration and for at least 3 months after the completion of protocol therapy. The patient has adequate hematopoietic and organ function and is able to provide informed consent. He has not participated in a clinical trial in the past 4 weeks and is able to comply with study and follow-up procedures.

A 65-year-old man with end-stage renal disease is undergoing hemodialysis via a non-tunneled catheter due to the lack of appropriate vascular access. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is on medications for these conditions, including amlodipine, metformin, and atorvastatin. He is allergic to heparin and has experienced adverse reactions, including hives and difficulty breathing. His physician recommends the use of a sodium bicarbonate solution as a catheter lock solution to prevent lumen thrombosis and catheter-related infections. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to compare the effectiveness and complications of sodium bicarbonate to heparin in his hemodialysis catheter.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus 7 years ago. Despite efforts to manage her diabetes with diet and exercise, her HbA1c level has been consistently above 7.5%. She has also been diagnosed with hypertension and has been taking amlodipine 5mg daily for the past year. Her blood pressure averages around 140/90 mmHg when measured at the clinic. She has been experiencing occasional dizziness and headaches, which she attributes to her blood pressure medication. Her recent blood test showed her 25 (OH) vitamin D levels at 20 ng/ml, indicating a deficiency. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of vitamin D replacement on blood pressure control and vascular disease in vitamin D deficient hypertensive patients with diabetes. She is not taking insulin for diabetes treatment and her HbA1c level is 7.8%. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to undergo the required testing and take the study medication as prescribed.

A 56-year-old man underwent cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass due to severe aortic stenosis. The surgery was successful, but he developed vasoplegia postoperatively, requiring norepinephrine infusion to maintain his blood pressure. The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidemia. He is a former smoker and currently takes medication for his chronic conditions. The patient is conscious and alert, but complains of weakness and fatigue. He is currently admitted to the ICU for postoperative care. The patient has not received any steroids in the past 7 days and has not been on any vasopressors prior to surgery. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his recovery after surgery.

65-year-old female patient seeking replacement of her previous maxillary and mandibular complete dentures due to poor fit and esthetics. The patient reports a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently managed with medications. She denies any history of neuromuscular dysfunction, auditory problems, mental conditions, oral pathology, xerostomia, or tied tongue condition. The patient has been completely edentulous for the past 5 years and has been using complete dentures for the same duration. She complains of difficulty in chewing and complains of occasional discomfort while speaking. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares patients' reported satisfaction with their complete dentures and oral health related quality of life, when provided with a denture with a reproduction of their rugae on the anterior palatal area as opposed to a polished palatal surface. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and has approved and consented to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old African-American woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 9 months ago. She has completed all of her initial therapies, including surgery, radiation and chemotherapy. She is currently receiving adjuvant hormonal therapy. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has gained some weight during her treatment. She experiences fatigue and poor quality of sleep. Her BMI is 31. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her overall health and quality of life. She is willing to travel to the Gathering Place in Beachwood, OH to participate in the exercise program under the supervision of the trained and certified staff. She has no history of connective tissue disorder and has no language barriers. She is willing to provide informed consent and has obtained clearance from her cardiologist to participate in the exercise program. She is excited to learn more about how exercise can benefit African-American women with breast cancer and is motivated to comply with the study requirements.

Patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of low-risk prostate cancer on active surveillance. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2 and is physically able to undertake a diet and exercise program. He has not participated in any weight loss programs or taken appetite suppressants in the past year. He is not on steroid hormone therapy for the past 12 months and has no significant cardiovascular disease, including recent myocardial infarction or stroke, pulmonary edema, myocarditis, pericarditis, unstable angina, pulmonary embolism/deep venous thrombosis, uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled arrhythmia, or heart failure. He is not insulin dependent and is not on metformin for diabetes. He does not have cognitive impairment or current alcohol or narcotic abuse. The patient is interested in participating in a diet and exercise program that may improve his prostate health and promote weight loss.

45 yo female with genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolaemia (LDL receptor mutation) on atorvastatin 80 mg daily with elevated triglycerides (2.5 mmol/L) presents to the clinic. She has a history of hypertension and smokes 10 cigarettes per day. She follows a typical Western diet with regular alcohol consumption. She has no history of diabetes or major systemic illnesses. She is interested in potentially participating in a clinical trial examining the effects of fish oil supplementation on postprandial lipid metabolism in patients with FH.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a diagnosis of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) for the past 3 years. He is currently on a stable medication regimen for the past 6 months. He lives at an altitude of 500m above sea level and has not traveled to an altitude above 1500m in the past 4 weeks. He reports mild dyspnea on exertion and fatigue with physical activity. His recent echocardiography showed an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 60 mmHg. His six-minute walk test (6MWT) distance was 350 meters. His baseline blood gas analysis was normal at rest but showed mild hypoxemia (PaO2: 78 mmHg) during the 6MWT. He has not experienced any high altitude-related symptoms in the past. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year with no success. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles and no significant past medical history. On evaluation, her anti-mullerian hormone (AMH) level was found to be 0.9 ng/mL and her antral follicle count (AFC) was 6. She underwent two previous cycles of in vitro fertilization (IVF) with conventional stimulation protocols but had a poor ovarian response with only 2-3 oocytes retrieved. She fulfills the "Bologna criteria" for poor ovarian response and is thus eligible for this clinical trial. She has no contraindications for ovarian stimulation and is willing to undergo the novel treatment protocol with 150μg corifollitropin alfa followed by 300IU hMG in a short GnRH agonist protocol.

The patient is a 22-year-old Asian male with mild to moderate myopia (-2.50D of spherical equivalent myopia and less than 2.00D of refractive astigmatism) who is interested in refractive surgery. He is a military serviceman and is concerned about the risk of flap dislodgement associated with LASIK due to his occupation. The patient does not have any corneal or anterior segment pathology, myopic peripheral retinal degeneration or myopic macular degeneration. He has a stable keratometry and a minimum cornea thickness of 460um as measured by Orbscan pachymetry. His best corrected visual acuity is at least 20/20 and he has not worn soft contact lenses for at least 2 weeks and hard lenses for at least 3 weeks. He has not undergone any previous ocular surgery and does not have a history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus or herpes simplex keratitis. The patient does not have a history of steroid-responsive rise in intraocular pressure or a preoperative intraocular pressure of more than 21 mmHg in either eye. He does not have diabetes mellitus, auto-immune disease, severe dry eye, connective tissue disease or significant atopy. The patient is not on chronic systemic corticosteroid or immunosuppressive therapy, and has a cornea thickness which would result in more than 250 microns of remaining posterior corneal thickness below the flap postoperatively. His central corneal endothelial cell count is above 1500 cells/mm2 in either eye.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent pain in her right wrist and forearm for several months. She has been diagnosed with a condition that requires surgical intervention to alleviate the pain. She is scheduled to undergo surgery in two weeks and has been advised by her surgeon to consider participating in a clinical trial evaluating a new technique for brachial plexus block that may improve postoperative pain control. She is in good health, with no known allergies or significant medical history, and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

This clinical trial is looking for individuals who have been diagnosed with a glioma, meningioma, or acoustic neuroma and are over the age of 18. The trial is also interested in the first-degree relatives of these individuals, particularly if they have a history of cancer or other related diseases. The study involves completing a Family Health Questionnaire to update medical history and provide contact information for relatives. First-degree relatives over the age of 18 will be contacted and invited to complete a modified risk factor interview over the telephone, which will obtain information about personal and family history of cancer and other diseases, as well as risk factor exposures. Participants who complete the interview will be asked to provide buccal cells as a source of DNA for future genotyping. The study aims to examine both genetic and environmental causes of brain tumors in adults, and this information will be used to identify new genes conferring susceptibility to brain and possibly related tumors.

Mrs. Johnson is an 83 year old woman who has been experiencing vision problems for the past year. She has been diagnosed with neovascular glaucoma in her right eye and is currently being monitored by an ophthalmologist. Mrs. Johnson has a history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. She has never had any previous ocular surgeries. Mrs. Johnson is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She is cooperative and able to follow instructions given by the ophthalmologist.

A 28 year old woman is currently 33 weeks pregnant and plans to exclusively breastfeed her infant for at least six months postpartum. She is in good health and has no history of endocrine dysfunction or abnormal calcium parameters related to renal disease. The baby is expected to be born at term and is not anticipated to require any special medical care beyond routine newborn care. The woman is willing to participate in a study that will determine the effectiveness and safety of vitamin D supplementation during lactation, and is open to being randomized to one of three treatment groups.

A 45-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer during a routine mammogram. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to medications. She has never undergone any breast surgery or radiation therapy. Her physician recommended total mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection and she consented to the procedure. She is currently affiliated with the French social security system and is willing to participate in the study. She has been informed about the study procedures and has the capacity to make informed medical decisions.

A 35-year-old male who underwent a renal transplant 2 weeks ago is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. He has a history of end-stage renal disease due to IgA nephropathy and was on dialysis for 2 years prior to the transplant. At screening, he had a Kerr score of 3, indicating active disease at the time of transplantation. He is currently receiving tacrolimus and an inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) inhibitor, which were initiated less than or equal to 30 days after transplantation, and has been on both for the past 30 days. The patient has no history of multiple organ transplants, FSGS, or MPGN. He has no evidence of active systemic or localized major infection, and has not received any investigational drugs or devices within the past 30 days. The patient is not known to be HIV positive and is not breastfeeding. He has no known allergies to sirolimus, tacrolimus, IMPDH inhibitors, macrolide antibiotics, iodine-containing products, or shellfish. The patient has not had any major illnesses or conditions that would preclude his participation in the study. At the time of randomization, he will be between 90 to 150 days post-transplantation and will have remained on tacrolimus and an

This is a 60-year-old male with a history of recurrent pTa low grade bladder tumors. He has undergone previous trans urethral resection of bladder tumor (TUR-B) procedures and is scheduled for another one. He has been informed of a new laser treatment option being offered as part of a clinical trial at the Department of Urology, Bispe

An 80-year-old woman presents with a history of falling twice in the past year, resulting in a fracture of her left hip and a sprained wrist. She has been experiencing fear and anxiety about falling again, which has limited her mobility and social activities. She has a history of chronic lower back pain and osteoarthritis in both knees, which have been managed with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She is widowed and lives alone in her house. Her children live nearby and visit her regularly. She uses a cane to assist with walking and has received physical therapy after her hip fracture. She has no history of dementia, Parkinson's disease, or other neurological disorders. She has not had any recent fractures or surgeries, and she does not have any lower limb prostheses. She has no history of psychiatric disease or mucocutaneous lesions. Her weight is within normal limits for her height. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her mobility and reduce her fear of falling.

A 65 year old man came to the clinic with a complaint of blurred vision and difficulty in reading. He had a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His visual acuity was 20/60 OD and 20/50 OS. The slit-lamp examination showed grade 3+ nuclear sclerosis cataract with pseudoexfoliation material on the anterior lens capsule. Intraocular pressure was within normal limits, and there were no signs of glaucoma. His corneal astigmatism was 1.5 diopters in both eyes. The axial length was 23.5 mm in the right eye and 23.1 mm in the left eye. The patient had no history of previous eye surgeries, and his corrected distance visual acuity was better than 20/40. He was interested in undergoing cataract surgery and was willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the refractive outcomes of cataract surgery in eyes with pseudoexfoliation syndrome.

A 6-year-old girl is scheduled for lower abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. She is generally healthy, with no known seizure disorder, craniofacial abnormalities, cardiopulmonary or neuromuscular defects, hepatic or renal insufficiency. She has had no recent illnesses, and her skin color is light enough to facilitate IV cannulation. Both the child and the parent are willing to participate in the study. She will be premedicated with midazolam as per the study protocol.

A 28-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m² is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He works as a software engineer, and his medical history is unremarkable. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. He takes no medication or supplements. He exercises regularly, at least 3 times a week, and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension or orthostatic hypotension. His resting pulse rate is 70 bpm. He has no history of asthma, immunodeficiency or acute illness within the past 2 weeks. He has not participated in any clinical trial in the past 30 days. His laboratory parameters, including serum iron, Hb, MCV, ferritin, and total iron binding capacity, are all within the reference range. He is interested in learning more about the study and is able to provide written informed consent.

40 yo M with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and chest pain. On arrival, he is tachypneic and hypoxic with an oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. The patient is quickly evaluated by the emergency department team and is found to have an elevated troponin level. Due to his worsening respiratory status, the anesthesiology department is consulted and the patient is intubated and transferred to the ICU. The patient's predicted mortality rate is calculated using Apache II and SAPS II values based on the worst or most critical physiological and laboratory parameters in the first 24 hours in the Emergency Department. The clinical diagnosis is acute myocardial infarction with acute respiratory distress syndrome. The patient is monitored closely and further diagnostic tests are performed to determine the extent of his cardiac injury. The patient is also evaluated for the presence of terminal cancer.

A 35 year old woman was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two months ago and has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past few weeks. She developed a fever of 39°C and was admitted to the hospital for management of febrile neutropenia. She has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses. Her blood counts showed a PMN count of 200/mm3, making her eligible for the study. She is currently being treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and is experiencing some side-effects such as nausea and diarrhea. She has been apyrexial for the past 48 hours and meets the criteria for early discontinuation of antibiotics according to the ECIL-4 recommendations. The study team will monitor her closely for any signs of infection and will stop the antibiotics if she remains apyrexial.

16 yo F who completed chemotherapy and radiation for Hodgkin's Lymphoma 8 months ago. Patient is currently in remission and has a life expectancy of over a year. However, the patient reports being less active and has gained weight since finishing treatment compared to before her diagnosis. She reports engaging in less than 420 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week, which is below the recommended guidelines. The patient is ambulatory and does not have any medical contraindications to increasing physical activity. She is able to read and write in English and has no significant physical or cognitive impairments that would prevent her from using electronic devices. The patient and her legal guardians have signed a written informed consent form to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant in the next year. The patient did not undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplant.

A 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22 and no known medical conditions came to the clinic expressing interest in participating in a clinical trial. He reports a regular exercise routine and balanced diet. He has no family history of diabetes and has never been diagnosed with any metabolic, hormonal, hepatic, renal, or cardiovascular diseases. His fasting glucose levels are within normal range and he has not been taking any medications. He is interested in learning more about the effects of different types of milk on glucose and hormone responses in the body.

52-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presenting with symptoms of sudden onset left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The patient was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke and underwent a CT scan and MRI confirming the diagnosis. Blood sampling was conducted within 36 hours of the event, and the patient has provided written agreement to participate in the trial. The patient has no history of stroke, myocardial infarction, or major operations prior to the current stroke. The patient is not known to have any hypercoagulable states or severe chronic diseases. There is no indication of any current infections based on anamnesis, physical examination, and lab tests. The patient has not undergone thrombolytic treatment.

A 52-year-old woman presents with a 10-year history of rheumatoid arthritis. She has been on DMARD therapy for the past 3 years, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient reports experiencing pain, stiffness, and swelling in multiple joints, including the hands, wrists, and knees. She has also reported difficulty with daily activities, such as dressing and grooming. The patient has no known allergies to human immunoglobulin proteins or other ingredients of golimumab. She has not previously experienced or is currently suffering from any collagen diseases other than rheumatoid arthritis, latent or active granulomatous infections such as histoplasmosis and coccidioidomycosis, Felty syndrome, or any severe, advanced, or poorly controlled disease. The patient has at least 6 swollen joints and 6 tender joints at the time of registration and immediately before the first injection. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol as directed.

55 yo M with a history of end-stage liver disease secondary to non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) who underwent a deceased donor liver transplantation 3 months ago. Patient is on immunosuppressive therapy and has been experiencing some episodes of fatigue and abdominal discomfort. Lab results showed elevated liver function tests and creatinine levels. Liver biopsy was done which showed mild rejection. Patient is a good candidate for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and is willing to participate. Past Medical History: - End-stage liver disease secondary to NASH - Deceased donor liver transplantation 3 months ago - Hypertension - Type II Diabetes Mellitus - Dyslipidemia - Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) - Obesity

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male who has previously donated peripheral blood progenitor cells (PBPC) using standard granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilization. He has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. He works as a software developer and has a supportive family. He is willing to participate in the study to donate PBPCs following a single subcutaneous injection of AMD3100. He has normal renal and liver function, normal blood count, and is eligible for normal blood donation. He is able to comprehend the investigational nature of the study and provide informed consent. He does not have any active infections, autoimmune diseases, or a history of cancer within the past 5 years. He has not experienced any cardiac or cerebrovascular diseases, and does not have severe psychiatric illness or mental deficiency.

A 42-year-old woman presents with occasional headaches and fatigue. Her blood pressure readings at the clinic visits have been within normal limits (< 130/80 mmHg), but she is concerned about her blood pressure because she has a family history of hypertension. Her BMI is 27 kg/m2, and she reports no other medical conditions or medication use. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She agrees to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of different antihypertensive medications in individuals with masked hypertension. During the screening period, her clinic BP measurements remain within normal limits, but her ambulatory BP monitoring reveals an average 24-hour BP of 140/90 mmHg, with higher readings during the day than at night. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is randomized to receive either carvedilol or amlodipine for 4 weeks, followed by a 1-month washout period, and then crossed over to the alternate medication for another 4 weeks. She will be monitored for electrolyte imbalances, kidney function, and ECG changes throughout the study, and will provide 24-hour urine samples to assess medication adherence. She is hopeful that participating in the trial will help her better manage her blood pressure and reduce her risk of developing hypertension in the future.

The patient is a 65 year old male who was recently admitted to the hospital after experiencing a sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. After further evaluation, he was diagnosed with a stroke. He has no history of oropharyngeal dysphagia or previous stroke. He is able to communicate effectively with healthcare providers but has difficulty swallowing both liquids and solids. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided signed informed consent.

45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 by nasopharyngeal swab and mild to moderate symptoms according to the national protocol classification of patients. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine. He denies any current symptoms of dyspnea or respiratory distress. He has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 30 days and is not pregnant or lactating. He understands the study design, procedure, risks, and benefits and has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a preterm neonate born at 30 weeks gestational age with a birth weight of 1200 grams. The baby is currently on nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) with a positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 7 cm H2O and fraction of oxygen (FiO2) of 35% to maintain a saturation goal of 92%. The baby's parents have given written informed consent for the baby to participate in an observational study to collect data on vital signs, oxygen requirements and other data related to ventilator care in preterm neonates. The baby does not have any life-threatening congenital anomalies or genetic syndromes and is not currently participating in any interventional studies.

58 yo M with a history of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, previously treated with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, which was discontinued due to disease progression. Patient has also undergone FOLFIRINOX and radiation therapy, but was discontinued due to intolerable side effects. Patient has no known curative or standard palliative therapy options left. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of 3 months. The patient's ANC is 1,900/mm^3, platelets are 110,000/mm^3, SGOT is 2.3-times upper limit of normal, SGPT is 2.1-times upper limit of normal, total bilirubin is within normal limits, creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL, and creatinine CL is 80 ml/min (measured 24hr). The patient has not received any radiotherapy or chemotherapy treatment for the past 6 weeks and has completely recovered from any previous treatment-related toxicity. The patient has not received any treatment with nitrosourea or bleomycin. The patient is not on any enzyme-inducing anticonvulsant agents and has not undergone any major surgery in the past 4 weeks. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to undergo the study procedures.

A 35-year-old male veteran who served in Afghanistan has been experiencing mild post-traumatic and chronic tension-type headaches for the past year. He works in an office job that requires him to sit for long periods of time, which exacerbates his headaches. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they only provide temporary relief. He is interested in non-pharmaceutical treatment options and has heard about the potential benefits of yoga. He has no physical limitations and is in good health overall. He has never practiced yoga before but is eager to learn. He does not have a history of psychiatric hospitalizations or substance abuse. He is available to participate in the 6-week yoga program and is willing to complete the 2-month follow-up assessment.

A 56-year-old male patient is diagnosed with head and neck cancer (HNC) and is scheduled to receive at least 4 weeks of radiotherapy (RT) with at least 20 fractions. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 2 or lower and has an informal family caregiver, his wife, who is willing to participate in the study. The patient and caregiver are both fluent in English and able to read and provide informed consent. The patient has no history of participating in yoga in the year prior to their diagnosis and does not have any cognitive deficits that would impede the completion of self-report instruments. The patient has a smartphone, which will be used in phase 2 of the study.

A 28-year-old man presents to the ED with complaints of mild to moderate lower back pain that started after lifting heavy objects at work. The patient rates his pain as a 3 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). The physical examination shows tenderness in the lumbar region but no neurological deficits. The patient has no history of peptic ulcer disease, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, or renal or hepatic insufficiency. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he does not have any known allergies to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). He has not taken any analgesic medication prior to arrival at the ED. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has been routinely treated with oral ibuprofen in the past for similar episodes of back pain.

A 24-year old college student who is currently studying psychology and enjoys attending music festivals and socializing with friends. She reports having tried MDMA (also known as Ecstasy) on several occasions in the past, with her first experience occurring when she was 19 years old. She describes her experiences with MDMA as positive, with feelings of euphoria, empathy, and increased sociability. She reports no history of psychiatric disorders or suicide attempts. She is a non-smoker and is not currently taking any medications. She is able to speak, read, and understand English fluently. She has no plans to move out of the area during the study period. She is willing to receive an MRI and comply with study procedures. She has a BMI within the healthy range of 18-30. She has not used cannabis in the past 7 days, alcohol in the past 24 hours, or any other illicit recreational drugs in the past 48 hours. She does not have any MRI contraindications and does not have any direct physical access to or routinely handle addicting drugs in the regular course of work duties. She does not have any allergies or hypersensitivity to MDMA. She does not have any current mood, anxiety, eating, or psychotic disorders. She is not currently using any psychotropic medications. She reports no family history of schizophrenia. She has no concurrent use of any medication that might increase the risk of participation. She has normal renal and hepatic function, as assessed via laboratory tests during the initial screening appointment. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits at the initial screening appointment. She has never had epilepsy, convulsions, seizures, or loss of consciousness for more than 10 minutes.

The patient is a 10-year-old child who has been referred to the MRI department for a brain scan. The child has a history of seizures and has been experiencing headaches and dizziness for the past few months. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The MRI scan is part of the standard diagnostic workup to determine the underlying cause of the patient's symptoms. The child is able to lie still for the duration of the MRI scan without the need for sedation. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for the child to participate in the SyMRI clinical trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is scheduled to undergo allogeneic bone marrow transplantation (BMT). She has a 6/6 HLA-matched family member donor. She is currently on chemotherapy and has completed four cycles with good response. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or chronic skin disease. She has no known allergies to medications. She is post-menopausal and does not plan to become pregnant. She has no active infections or other medical conditions that would prevent her from undergoing BMT. She is interested in participating in the study to prevent acute GVHD and is willing to adhere to the study requirements, including taking the study drug and being monitored closely for any adverse effects.

A 30-year-old woman who has regular menstrual cycles and is not currently taking any form of birth control presents at the clinic. She has no history of any medical conditions and is generally healthy. Her weight is 130 pounds, and she meets the age criteria for the study. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to scientific research and learn more about her own health.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been suffering from a chronic venous leg ulcer for the past 4 months. She has no other medical condition and is not taking any medication. The ulcer is located on the inner side of her right leg, below the knee, and is about 4 cm² in size. The wound is covered with fibrinous tissue and has not decreased in size by more than 30% during the 2-week run-in period. The patient has been compliant with compression therapy during the run-in period, with no more than 2 days without compression. The patient has given her consent to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria, including having an ABPI of ≥0.7 for both legs and a wound duration of 8 weeks to 60 months. The patient has no history of infection requiring systemic antibiotic therapy, no systemic infection not controlled by suitable antibiotic treatment, and no allergy/hypersensitivity to the ingredients of the dressings and/or Granulox®. The patient is not currently undergoing radiotherapy, chemotherapy, immunosuppressant drugs or high doses of oral corticosteroids, and has not had deep vein thrombosis within the past 3 months. The patient is eligible to participate in the study and will be randomized to either the standard of care group or the standard of care with Granulox added as an adjunct therapy.

A 32-year-old woman with primary infertility seeks treatment for her inability to conceive despite trying for over a year. She has no history of previous surgeries on the uterus or ovaries and has no known uterine factor infertility. Her partner's semen analysis shows no signs of severe male factor infertility. She has undergone a long ovulation induction protocol and is eligible for the study. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare thawed cleavage embryo transfer and transfers of blastocysts from thawed cleavage embryos. She has not experienced recurrent abortions and does not have poor ovarian reserve. She will sign a written consent form before participating in the study.

A 65-year-old man who has been having frequent episodes of heart palpitations and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and occasional palpitations since his 40s, which he attributed to stress at work. However, over the past few months, he has had several episodes of palpitations that last several minutes and are associated with shortness of breath. He went to the emergency department once during one of these episodes, and an ECG showed atrial fibrillation. His primary care physician referred him to a cardiologist, who recommended treatment with direct current cardioversion. As part of the treatment, the patient will be provided with a smartphone that he will be using for 30 days after the treatment to record his heart rhythm measurements in his home environment. The novel smartphone-based method, which uses the smartphone camera as a sensor, will be validated against simultaneous recordings with mobile ECG. The patient will also be instructed in using the smartphone recordings and mobile ECG in the weeks before the treatment to study the possible benefit of detecting spontaneous conversions to normal heart rhythm and missed doses of treatment with blood thinning medication, both of which will lead to cancellation or detention of the cardioversion procedure. The objective of this study is to validate the use of a novel smartphone-based method for heart rhythm diagnostics when used by patients in their home environment after receiving treatment with direct current cardioversion. The patient will be required to sign a written consent form and undergo a screening visit to confirm eligibility for the study.

A 55 yo male who presents with a history of epigastric pain, early satiety, and weight loss. An upper endoscopy was done which showed a gastric ulcer. Biopsy results from the ulcer revealed adenocarcinoma of the stomach. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed a 5cm mass in the stomach with metastases to the liver. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or immune therapy. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. The patient's lab values show neutrophils of 2.5 x 1000000000/L, platelets of 120 x 1000000000/L, hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, bilirubin of 0.8 x ULN, AST and ALT of 1.5 X UNL, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) of 2.0 X ULN. The patient's serum creatinine is 0.9 x ULN. The patient has no known drug allergies or history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits and laboratory tests required for the study.

A 65-year-old male with a history of heart failure and a cardiac pacemaker implanted 2 years ago is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He has been experiencing periodic breathing with symptoms of breathlessness, fatigue, and disrupted sleep for the past year. His left ventricular systolic function is normal, as assessed by echocardiogram. He has no significant respiratory disease and is able to lie comfortably on a bed for 90 minutes. He is not currently on haemodialysis and has no other medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

50-year-old female with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 5 years, managed with oral hypoglycemic agents, and hypertension for the past 2 years, managed with ACE inhibitors, presents for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating sublingual microcirculation data in patients with systemic diseases. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2, and has not been diagnosed with any other systemic diseases. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo the examination of sublingual microcirculation by using incident dark field video microscope.

A 16-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with severe aplastic anemia, characterized by fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising. She has a history of recurrent infections and has been hospitalized multiple times in the past year. She underwent a bone marrow biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis. She has no matched related or unrelated donor for allogeneic transplantation. Her Karnofsky score is 80%, her bilirubin level is within normal range, and her ALT level is 2 times the upper limit of normal. Her pulmonary function is 60% predicted, and her left ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. Her serum creatinine level is within normal range for her age. She has no history of CNS leukemic involvement, myelofibrosis, or other malignancies with moderate-severe bone marrow fibrosis. She has not undergone an autologous stem cell transplant within the preceding 6 months or any prior allogeneic stem cell transplant. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she and her parents have given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

27 year old healthy male with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m², with no significant medical history or allergies, and no currently prescribed systemic or topical medications. The patient does not smoke, consume more than 28 units of alcohol per week, or have a significant history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse/dependence. The patient has a normal creatinine clearance and blood pressure, and has not donated or lost more than 50 milliliter (mL) of whole blood within the past 30 days, or more than 499 milliliter (mL) whole blood within 56 days preceding first dose administration. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial involving an investigational product within the last 30 days, and is not concurrently enrolled in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study. The patient is willing to use appropriate contraception from the time of the first dose until 3 months after the final dosing occasion. The patient is willing to avoid smoking for durations of at least 10 hours and has no significant history of drug allergy or clinically significant allergic disease.

A 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has been taking a sulfonylurea medication for the last 5 months but has not been able to achieve adequate blood sugar control. He works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle, but he has a family history of diabetes. He has no allergies to any food or drugs and is not on any other medications to lower blood sugar. He exercises regularly and has no major heart, liver, or kidney problems. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to see if adding saxagliptin to his current medication regimen can help him achieve better blood sugar control.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who works as a sales representative. She experiences intense fear and anxiety when she has to give presentations in front of colleagues and clients. She reports avoiding public speaking situations whenever possible and experiences physical symptoms such as sweating, trembling, and rapid heartbeat when faced with such situations. She has never sought treatment for her anxiety before. She is currently not taking any medications for anxiety or depression. She lives in the greater Philadelphia area and is willing to travel to the treatment site.

32 year-old male who exercises regularly at least 3 times a week. He enjoys weight lifting and running as his primary forms of exercise. He typically eats breakfast every day but is unsure if his current breakfast choices are optimal for his exercise routine. He is interested in learning more about sports nutrition and how to properly fuel his body before and after workouts. He is willing to complete a one-time survey regarding his breakfast habits, food preferences, and exercise routine. He is excited to contribute to research that may help him and others like him make more informed decisions about their nutrition and exercise habits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man of Turkish descent who has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. He has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension, but is not on any medication for his atrial fibrillation. He has expressed interest in learning more about his condition and how to manage it, and has agreed to participate in the ARENA Migration arm of the study. He is fluent in Turkish and German, and has lived in the Rhein-Neckar region for the past 20 years. He is willing to attend educational sessions and provide feedback on the effectiveness of the program.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic seeking help to quit smoking. She has been smoking for 25 years and smokes an average of 20 cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit smoking several times but has failed. She is highly motivated to quit and is in the preparation stage according to Prochaska and Di Clemente's stages of change model. She has no history of myocardial infarction in the preceding 3 months and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not use any form of smokeless tobacco or other nicotine replacement therapy. She is willing to participate in a trial that will help her quit smoking. She is looking for a substitute for nicotine and is open to using a nicotine nasal spray. She is willing to be randomized to either the ad libitum group or the hourly intake group and is willing to follow the instructions given to her. She is committed to quitting smoking and is willing to be monitored during the first three weeks of use.

A 45-year-old male patient presents to the Hand and Upper Extremity Service at Massachusetts General Hospital with musculoskeletal pain. He has been experiencing pain in his wrist and hand for several months, which has been affecting his daily activities and work. He has been taking pain medication and has tried physical therapy, but without significant improvement. The patient is fluent in English and literate. He has no significant history of psychopathology that would interfere with participation in the study. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn more about acceptance-based mindfulness exercises and their potential benefits for managing his pain and anxiety.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability. He has no chronic pain and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has signed the consent form to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has a sibling without autism or developmental disorder who will also participate in the trial as a control group member. The patient will undergo pain reactivity testing using an experimental model of pain, including thermic stimulations (tonic heat pain stimulation and cold-pressor test) to test excitatory and inhibitory pain mechanisms. Salivary cortisol and automatic nervous system (heart rate and blood pressure with an electrocardiogram) will also be tested, as well as behavioral responses to thermal stimulation assessed by an inspired behavior scale. The patient's demographic and clinical data will also be collected, including sensory profile, sleep disorders, and depression inventory.

The patient is a 30 year old healthcare worker who had a high-risk exposure to a confirmed case of Ebola virus disease while working in a treatment center in West Africa. The patient is in good health and able to tolerate oral medication. The patient has no known allergies to any medications and is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study results. The patient is willing to use adequate methods of contraception during the study and for at least 6 months after their last dose of BCV.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who is currently 20 weeks pregnant with a singleton fetus. She has a history of cervical shortening and has been recommended by her clinician to undergo an exam-indicated cervical cerclage. The patient has agreed to the procedure and the provider has decided to perform a pre-cerclage amniocentesis to rule out any infections. The patient has no major anomalies on ultrasound and her cervical dilation is less than 2cm. The patient has no previous history of preterm birth, but is willing to participate in the study to help determine if a vaginal fluid test can predict very early preterm birth. The patient is able to understand the study procedures and has provided consent to participate.

The patient is a 2-year-old boy scheduled for elective surgery. He has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA class 1. His guardian is able to understand and sign the agreement for the clinical trial. The patient has no history of hip dislocation or limited hip movement. He has no known vascular malformation of the femoral vein. The patient is hemodynamically stable and is not in an emergency situation.

A 35-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a complaint of chronic constipation and bloatedness. She had been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and had tried several over-the-counter remedies without success. She reported having a bowel movement once in 2-3 days and had to strain to pass stool. She also complained of feeling bloated and uncomfortable after eating. She had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications. Her physical examination was unremarkable, and there were no signs of organic diseases of the colon or rectum. She had a negative pregnancy test and was using oral contraceptives for the last 6 months. She was willing to maintain a diary throughout the study and signed the informed consent form. She had no known allergies to the study drugs. She was otherwise in good health and met all the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 57-year-old female with a history of metastatic neuroendocrine tumors, presenting with radiological documentation of progressive disease over the past year. She has measurable disease according to RECIST criteria and adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. Her fasting serum cholesterol is below 300 mg/dL and fasting triglycerides are below 2.5 x ULN. She has not received prior therapy with RAD001 (everolimus) or other rapamycins (sirolimus, temsirolimus), and is not taking concomitant medications known to inhibit, induce, or be a substrate to isoenzyme CYP3A. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule of the study.

35-year-old female with a history of stress urinary incontinence and has failed conservative management with pelvic floor exercises and pessary.
