She is interested in pursuing injectable bulking agent treatment for her symptoms. She has no contraindications to the use of Durasphere EXP per the Directions for Use. She has not had any prior surgical or non-surgical treatment for her urinary incontinence. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of the Needle Guide as an assist in properly guiding the injection needle during the procedure.

29 year old male with a history of keratoconus diagnosed at age 22 presents with worsening vision and increasing difficulty with contact lens wear. Best corrected visual acuity is 20/200 in both eyes. Slit lamp exam reveals corneal thinning and scarring. The patient has no other ocular pathology and is interested in the possibility of corneal transplant surgery to improve his vision.

Patient is a 30-year-old male who is scheduled for dental extraction of his upper molar teeth due to severe decay and pain. He has a history of dental anxiety and has experienced discomfort during previous dental procedures. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications that would interfere with the assessment of local anesthesia. The patient is able to comprehend the visual analog scale and verbal rating scale used to assess pain during injection and effectiveness of anesthesia. He has given written, informed consent to participate in the study along with his legal guardian.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who is scheduled to undergo an elective open abdominal surgery for the treatment of a hernia. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has never had any bleeding disorders or coagulation issues. He does not have any known allergies to bovine, porcine, or human substances. He has not taken any antiplatelet medications for at least 5 days prior to surgery. He is able to provide written consent or has an authorized legal representative who is able to provide consent for his participation in the study. He meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The surgeon is able to identify a target bleeding site (TBS) for which conventional means for hemostasis are ineffective or impractical.

A 46-year-old male was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. He has a past medical history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and overweight. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He is married and has two children. The patient reports that he has been taking metformin for the past 4 years and has recently started taking a GLP-1R agonist. He has noticed a significant improvement in his blood sugar control and has lost some weight. However, he is concerned about the long-term side effects of the medication and is looking for alternative therapies. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to participate in the study to help other patients with diabetes and to learn more about his condition.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath for several weeks. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in her right lung, as well as metastases to her liver and bones. The patient has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis, and takes medications for both conditions. She lives alone and is able to perform activities of daily living independently, but has recently experienced some fatigue and decreased appetite. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has not received any prior treatment for her cancer. Her laboratory studies show: Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL, eGFR >60 mL/min, Total Bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL, GOT: 25 U/L, GPT: 20 U/L, ANC: 2.1 x 10^9/L, Platelets: 150 x 10^9/L. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her cancer that may have fewer side effects than traditional chemotherapy.

A 75-year-old Italian woman, born and currently residing in Abbiategrasso, was invited to participate in a comprehensive assessment of cognitive functions, physical health, and biological parameters for a longitudinal multidimensional population study on brain aging. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She has been seeing her family doctor regularly for the past 10 years, who referred her to participate in the study. She agreed to participate and attended the first appointment, where blood samples were taken, and social questionnaire, anthropometric, and walking speed evaluations were done. She was contacted by phone for the second appointment, where she underwent clinical examination and neuropsychological assessments of mood and cognitive function. She completed the study's screening process and was found to have normal cognitive function. She will be followed up for two more times over the next six years to track any changes in her cognitive function and physical health.

A 45-year-old woman was referred for evaluation of a solid nodule identified incidentally during a routine chest X-ray. The CT scan showed a solid nodule with a maximal dimension of 12mm in the right lung. The Mayo risk prediction algorithm determined the pre-test risk of cancer as 35%. She has no history of lung cancer or any other type of cancer. She has never smoked and has no significant past medical history. She provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all protocol requirements. She has not received any blood products in the past 30 days and is not participating in any other clinical trial that may impact or alter the management of the nodule.

A 60-year-old male with a history of Alzheimer's disease for the past year and a Folstein MMSE score of 14, presents with a reliable caregiver. The patient has adequate vision, hearing, speech, motor function, and comprehension for compliance with all testing procedures. There is no evidence of other neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease or normal pressure hydrocephalus. The patient has no history of major psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia or unipolar or bipolar depression. There is no significant medical disorder that might cause or contribute to dementia such as B12 or folic acid deficiency, untreated hypothyroidism, or alcohol abuse. The patient has no recent hematologic/oncologic disorders and no history of myocardial infarction, peripheral vascular disease, or coronary artery bypass surgery. There is no clinically significant or unstable active GI, hepatic, or pulmonary disease. The patient has not had a documented stroke or more than one confirmed TIA. The patient is not hypersensitive to Donezepil HCL or other piperidine containing drugs.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and a recent diagnosis of liver cancer. He is scheduled to undergo a hepatic resection procedure to remove a portion of his liver. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of two hemostatic agents in controlling local bleeding during and after the surgery. The patient has no hematologic disorders and is not participating in any other clinical trials. He does not have any significant allergies or conditions that would interfere with the study. The patient has been advised to avoid having a child within one year after the surgery. He has been instructed to avoid skin infections in the targeted incisional area and has been cleared for the surgery by his physician.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who is scheduled to undergo a living donor kidney transplantation. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and chronic kidney disease for 10 years. The patient has been on dialysis for the past two years and has a history of low bone density. He has never received bisphosphonates or any other medication for bone loss. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 27.5 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. The patient agrees to participate in the study and undergo bone biopsies, DEXA scans, and bone hormonal studies at regular intervals. He understands that he will be randomized to receive either a placebo or risedronate 35 mg weekly and will be followed up for one year after the transplantation.

This is a 42 year-old male who underwent arthroscopic surgery for a cartilage injury in his left knee. He was part of a previous clinical trial (AAG-G-H-1220) where he was randomized to the Microfracture treatment group. Unfortunately, his Microfracture treatment failed and he continues to experience pain and functional limitations in his left knee. He is willing to participate in the prospective single arm extension study to receive NOVOCART 3D treatment and improve his knee function. He has not undergone any other cartilage repair procedures on his knee and does not have any other conditions that would interfere with the healing process or evaluating outcomes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing facial pain and nasal congestion for the past 4 days. He has been diagnosed with acute sinusitis and has been prescribed amoxicillin/clavulanate by his primary care physician. He is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any other drugs. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial, and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He will be required to record his symptoms in a diary four times a day, and will be randomly assigned to use either Sinuclean DM® spray or saline for symptom relief. He will also undergo a CT scan to assess the status of his paranasal sinuses before and after the treatment. He understands that anti-histaminic, steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are forbidden during the study. He has provided written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) 2 years ago. She has been on various Disease Modifying Treatments (DMTs) but has been recently recommended to switch to Plegridy by her neurologist. She has experienced injection site reactions with her previous DMTs, including redness, burning sensation, and pain. She has no known allergies to any medication or skin products. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of depression or other psychiatric disorders. The patient is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

A 40-year-old female diagnosed with primary biliary cirrhosis (PBC) with elevated ALP after 6 months of UDCA therapy. She has been maintained on UDCA at a dose of 13-15 mg/kg for 6 or more months. She has a positive serum AMA and has not altered the dose of any medications used to treat PBC within the last 6 months. She has no advanced liver disease, esophageal varices, INR > 1.2, Albumin < 35 g/L, platelets < 120,000/mm3, Childs Pugh class B or C cirrhosis, presence of varices or previous variceal hemorrhage, spontaneous encephalopathy, ascites, or need for liver transplantation. She has no secondary diagnosis such as HIV, viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury, extrahepatic biliary obstruction, primary sclerosing cholangitis, metabolic liver diseases, or alcoholic liver disease. She does not regularly use more than 30 grams of alcohol per day in the last year. She does not have clinically apparent pancreatitis or with a predicted survival of less than 3 years from malignant or other potentially life-threatening disease. She has no previous allergic reaction to study medications. Her creatinine clearance is greater than 70 mL/min. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding a child, or a young sexually active patient not using contraception.

35-year-old Caucasian female with a history of atopic dermatitis presented to the dermatology clinic complaining of worsening skin symptoms including itching, redness, and scaling of her skin. She has a history of eczema since childhood and has tried various topical medications and moisturizers with limited success. She has not received any systemic treatment for her condition. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no known drug allergies. She denies any history of hepatitis B or C, immunodeficiency, or immunosuppressive medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has a negative urine pregnancy test. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol and provide written informed consent. The investigator's global assessment score of her atopic dermatitis is 3. The patient is interested in participating in this study to help develop a non-invasive method to measure mRNA levels in skin samples for patients with her condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past year. He has been prescribed a variety of antidepressant medications, but has not experienced significant improvement in his symptoms. He has been prescribed an augmentation therapy medication from Table 1 and has filled the prescription at least once between 01 January 2005 and 30 November 2008. He has had continuous medical and pharmacy benefits for 12 months before and after the index date. He has a primary diagnosis of MDD (ICD-9-CM codes 296.2x, 296.3x, 311.xx) during the pre-index period. He is at least 18 years old as of the year of the pre-index period. He has not been diagnosed with non-MDD episodic mood disorders or schizophrenia during the pre-index or post-index periods.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in his left knee. He reports chronic pain, stiffness, and difficulty in walking, which has significantly impacted his quality of life. He has tried several non-surgical interventions, including physical therapy and pain medication, but has not found significant relief. He has no history of significant comorbidities, such as heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes. His BMI is 28. He is willing to undergo a unilateral TKA and has been approached to participate in the VISIONAIRE™ Value Study. He understands the study and is willing to sign the IRB/IEC approved consent form.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He has a history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation. His current medications include lisinopril, carvedilol, and warfarin. His cardiologist has recommended him for implantation of a cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) pacemaker to help improve his heart function. The patient has agreed to participate in the Physiologic Pacing Registry to help further understand the physiologic pacing implant and follow-up workflows. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the prescribed follow-up tests and schedule of evaluations.

A 56-year-old man was scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones. He has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia, all well controlled with medications. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. His preoperative evaluation was unremarkable, and he was classified as ASA II. He was brought to the operating room, and standard monitors were applied. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and fentanyl, and endotracheal intubation was facilitated with rocuronium. The patient was then placed on mechanical ventilation, and anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane and remifentanil. The surgery was uneventful, and the patient received a total of 40mg of rocuronium during the procedure. The surgery lasted for 90 minutes. The patient was then transferred to the postanesthesia care unit (PACU). Upon arrival to the PACU, the patient was breathing spontaneously, but the TOF ratio was 0.4 on the AMG monitor, indicating residual neuromuscular blockade. The patient was given neostigmine and glycopyrrolate to reverse the blockade, and the TOF ratio was monitored every 5 minutes. The patient was not extubated until the TOF ratio was 0.9 or greater.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing occasional headaches and difficulty sleeping. She has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. She has never been diagnosed with either condition but is concerned about her risk. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any medications. She has not taken melatonin in the past year.

There are no specific patient descriptions for this clinical trial as it does not involve patients. The study aims to assess the accuracy of defibrillation pad placement by untrained members of the public, and therefore, it is not applicable to any specific patient.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with gastric cancer. He underwent radical resection with wide lymph node dissection, and post-operative staging revealed that he is at stage IIIB. He has provided written informed consent to participate in this study. He has no history of neoplasm in his stomach or any other malignant disease. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. He has no history of myocardial infarction or severe/unstable angina, coronary/peripheral artery bypass, NYHA class III or IV congestive heart failure, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or serious cardiac arrhythmia requiring treatment. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential. He has no history of hypersensitivity to the investigational products (S1 and Oxaliplatin). He is willing to use generally accepted effective method of birth control during the study treatment period and for at least 6 months after the end of study treatment.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has difficulty pronouncing the /r/ sound. He has been receiving traditional speech therapy for the past year with limited improvement. His parents are concerned about his speech and how it may impact his social and academic development. The boy has no history of hearing loss and speaks English as his dominant language. He has no other speech or language disorders, and his oral structure and function are within normal limits. He is currently in the 7th grade and is performing well academically. He has no diagnosis of developmental disability or major neurobehavioral syndrome. He is willing to participate in a research study to improve his speech.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 2 years. Despite following a strict diet and lifestyle changes, her blood sugar levels are not adequately controlled, and she requires additional medication. Her current medication regimen includes metformin 1000 mg twice a day. The patient has no history of heart failure or chronic insulin therapy. She has no known allergies or intolerances to any medication. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with amlodipine 5 mg daily. The patient has normal kidney function with a creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is postmenopausal.

55 yo African American female with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, currently being managed with metformin and glipizide, presents to the church-based health promotion program being conducted as part of the clinical trial. She reports a history of poor blood sugar control, with recent HbA1c level of 9.2%, despite taking her medications as prescribed. She also reports difficulty with adhering to a healthy diet and exercise regimen due to lack of motivation and social support. The patient expresses a fatalistic attitude towards her diabetes, believing that her condition is out of her control and that nothing she does will make a difference. She reports attending church regularly and is hopeful that the health promotion program will help her to better manage her diabetes and reduce her risk of cardiovascular disease. Past Medical History: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, HTN, Dyslipidemia.

A 30-year-old male presents with a history of cocaine dependence for the past 3 years. He has tried to quit multiple times but has been unsuccessful. He is currently employed and has a supportive family. He is seeking help and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of cocaine dependence. He has no history of any other substance abuse, gambling problems or psychiatric disorders. He is in good health, with no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He lives within a commutable distance of the Treatment Research Center at the Penn/VA Center for Studies of Addiction, University of Pennsylvania. He understands and signs the informed consent.

A 52 yo F who was admitted to the ICU after a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries including a left femur fracture requiring surgical repair, and a laceration on her face. She is currently intubated and sedated with fentanyl and propofol for mechanical ventilation. She is responsive to painful stimuli and has been communicating her pain levels on a VAS when prompted by her nurses. She is cooperative and not agitated. She is scheduled for a planned procedure to remove her chest tube in the next 24 hours.

A 26-year-old female presented with a history of schizophrenia with a duration of 4 years. She had been prescribed different antipsychotic medications including risperidone, quetiapine, and aripiprazole, but none of them provided significant improvement. She had been experiencing hallucinations and delusions, and she had a PANNS-derived BPRS total score of 30. She had no history of diabetes, hypertension, cardiac conduction abnormalities, blood dyscrasias, neurological or endocrinological disorders, and cancer. She was not pregnant or lactating. She had a history of substance use disorder, but she had been abstinent for the past 8 months. She was willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the study and did not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 1-year-old boy who was diagnosed with MPS IIIA. The diagnosis was confirmed through genomic DNA analysis which demonstrated homozygous mutations in the SGSH gene and no detectable SGSH enzyme activity by leukocyte assay. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is able to sit without support but cannot crawl or walk yet. His cognitive development has been assessed to have a Developmental Quotient (DO) of 70 according to Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development - Third Edition. He has not received any viral attenuated vaccines within the last 30 days. His parents have been informed and have given their consent for him to participate in the clinical trial.

A 55 year old man with a history of heavy smoking came to the clinic with complaints of difficulty swallowing and hoarseness. After further investigation, he was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx. The patient is scheduled to undergo chemoradiation therapy for curative treatment. He has no history of neurological disease or oropharyngeal swallowing disorder prior to cancer diagnosis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a non-drinker and non-smoker since the diagnosis. The patient is currently not using oxygen and has no history of severe COPD. He is motivated to improve his swallowing function and quality of life during and after treatment.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic sclerosis (SSc) for the past 5 years. She has tried several medications such as vasodilators, PDE5 inhibitors, and endothelin receptor antagonists to treat her skin lesions, but they have been ineffective. She has several digital ulcers and sclerosing skin on her hands, which have been causing her physical pain and emotional distress. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She lives with her husband and two children. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m², and she does not have any cognitive dysfunction or psychologic problems. She has not undergone any previous sympathectomy or amputation. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive autologous Stromal vascular fraction injection to improve her skin lesions.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who presents with a history of occasional tooth sensitivity and discomfort while chewing. She has a past medical history of hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with levothyroxine. She reports good oral hygiene practices and no current orofacial pain. Upon examination, it is found that she has two carious lesions in her posterior molars requiring composite restorations. She has no history of temporomandibular joint problems or any other systemic diseases. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer and was scheduled for a mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection. She has no significant past medical history and her physical examination was unremarkable, except for a palpable mass in her right breast. Her preoperative laboratory tests showed a hemoglobin level of 11.2 g/dL and a platelet count of 220,000/mm3. Her anesthesia evaluation revealed an ASA status of 2. She was scheduled for surgery as an inpatient with an expected length of stay of 2-3 days. The patient was consented to participate in the ARCA-1 study to evaluate the association between perioperative blood transfusions and 1-year mortality, postoperative complications and cancer progression after major oncologic non-cardiac surgery. She was randomized to the group that will receive standard of care treatment and have her medical records reviewed at 30 days and at 1 year after surgery.

A 12-year old girl was diagnosed with Crohn's disease two years ago. She has been on medication since then, but lately, she has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain and rectal bleeding. Her gastroenterologist recommended an upper and lower endoscopy to evaluate the extent of her disease. The patient is alert and oriented, and she speaks English fluently. She lives with her parents and two siblings. She is currently on Infliximab and Azathioprine. She reports no allergies and has no history of asthma or respiratory issues. Her BMI is within the normal range. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with atopic dermatitis for the past 2 years. Her condition is in active stage with an overall IGA-Score of 3. She has two comparable areas of stable atopic eczema on bilateral symmetric corresponding sides of the extremities, each of at least 10 cm² with a modified, objective local SCORAD of 8 and 10 respectively. She has not received any treatment for the past 2 weeks. She is willing to adhere to the schedule of the investigation, concomitant therapy prohibitions, restrictions, treatment regimen and procedures described in the CIP. She has no known allergies to the ingredients of the test products and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the clinical investigation. She is willing to use a contraceptive method for the duration of the investigation. She has no history of substance abuse, autoimmune diseases, or severe infectious diseases.

A 45 year old male with Type II diabetes and controlled hypertension is being invited to participate in a clinical trial to study the effects of cocoa on the cardiovascular and renal systems. The participant has no history of heart attack, stroke, or chest pain within the past 6 months and has not been diagnosed with kidney or heart disease. His blood pressure is consistently below 165/105 and he is not currently taking any medication for hypertension. The participant is willing to provide urine and blood samples for routine physiologic parameters and hormone assessment, and understands that the study will involve cranial ultrasound, retinal blood flow measurement, and peripheral blood flow measurement by plethysmography.

As this is a clinical trial involving local health departments and public health practitioners, there are no patients involved. Instead, the study aims to improve diabetes prevention and control programs and policies among local health departments in Missouri.

The patient is a 50 year-old male who has been experiencing frequent heartburn and regurgitation for several years. He has tried various medications for GERD without significant improvement. He reports experiencing discomfort and difficulty swallowing at times. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has a BMI of 28 and is generally in good physical health. He has agreed to undergo surgery for his GERD symptoms and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing different surgical options.

A 45-year-old man with a history of colorectal cancer was recently diagnosed with metastatic cancer that has spread to his liver and portal lymph nodes. He had previously undergone adjuvant chemotherapy with fluorouracil but the disease progressed in spite of the treatment. He has no history of other cancers and is otherwise healthy. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He is married and has three children. He works as a software engineer and has no history of smoking or drug use. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new treatment option that could help him fight his cancer.

A 35-year-old female employee of a technology company comes to the clinic complaining of stress-related symptoms such as fatigue, irritability, and difficulty concentrating. She has been working in the company for 3 years and has been feeling increasingly overwhelmed and stressed due to the high workload and pressure to meet deadlines. She has a college degree and has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders or substance abuse. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and has not sought any treatment for it. She does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively.

56F diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma was recommended for surgical intervention. The patient has no known allergies to anesthetics and has undergone previous surgeries under general anesthesia without complications. She has no history of renal or hepatic failure, nor does she have any hematological diseases. The patient is currently not undergoing chemotherapy or any other treatment for cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided signed informed consent. The patient has no contraindications for epidural anesthesia.

Patient A is a healthy 25-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He has a BMI of 22.5 kg/m^2 and has no significant medical history or current medical conditions. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. He is able to understand the objectives and contents of the clinical trial and has given his written informed consent to participate. The clinical trial will evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of HCP1801 in healthy subjects.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with COVID-19 infection. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, difficulty in breathing, fever, cough and fatigue for the past few days. He has been admitted to the hospital and has been diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Despite receiving standard medication, his blood pressure remains low, and he has been started on noradrenaline for the past 6 hours. He has no history of cancer or any other chronic illness. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial, and he has given his verbal and written consent to participate. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and will be randomly assigned to receive either angiotensin II or standard medication as an add-on vasopressor. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse effects or changes in clinical outcomes.

35F with a history of chronic periodontitis and no prior antibiotic or periodontal therapy in the last 6 months. She reports bleeding while brushing and flossing, bad breath, and sensitivity while eating hot or cold foods. On examination, there is moderate to severe gingival inflammation, bleeding on probing, probing depths of 5mm or greater, clinical attachment loss of 3mm or greater, and vertical bone loss of 3mm or greater on intraoral periapical radiographs. The patient has no systemic conditions or medications altering the periodontal condition, no immune-compromised state, no hematologic disorders, and has a platelet count of greater than 200,000/mm3. She does not have aggressive periodontitis or substance/tobacco abuse and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has not had any previous statin therapy and does not have a history of statin allergy.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is 37 weeks pregnant and scheduled for a cesarean delivery due to breech presentation. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Her height is 5'6" and her weight is 150 lbs, with a BMI of 24.2. She speaks English fluently. She has no history of hypertension. She presents to the birthing centre with contractions and is admitted for the cesarean delivery. She has a baseline blood pressure and heart rate within normal limits. She is eligible for the study and consents to participate.

A 58-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years presented to the clinic. He has been experiencing difficulty with motor coordination and has been noticing tremors in his hands and legs. He is currently taking Levodopa-Carbidopa for his symptoms. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medications. He is married and has two adult children. He used to work as a teacher before he retired. He has no history of allergies or any previous surgeries. He is a non-smoker and drinks occasionally. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help find better treatment options for Parkinson's disease.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from migraines for over 10 years. She has chronic migraines, experiencing headaches on more than 15 days per month. She reports having photophobia during her migraines and between attacks. She has been treated with several abortive and prophylactic medications, but has not found significant relief. She has a history of iritis and blepharospasm, but these conditions have been well controlled with medication. She has no significant ocular history, but is nearsighted with a prescription of -3.5 diopters. She does not abuse alcohol or use illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in clinical research that may provide relief from her migraines.

28-year-old nulliparous woman at 39 weeks of gestation presents to the labor and delivery unit in request of epidural analgesia for labor pain management. She has had regular prenatal care and has no significant medical history. Her vitals are stable, and her temperature is within normal limits. She has no known allergies to steroids and is not currently taking any medications. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female patient presents with a history of Hodgkin's lymphoma. She underwent chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past, but unfortunately, her cancer has relapsed and is now resistant to traditional treatments. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and recurrent fevers. A biopsy confirmed relapsed Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that she can carry out light work, but cannot perform any strenuous activities. She has no known cerebral metastases or epidural tumor, and has no "currently active" second malignancy unrelated to HL or NHL. She has completed anti-cancer therapy and is in complete response. She is expected to live for more than three months. She practices effective contraceptive methods and has a negative serum pregnancy test. She has no serious medical illness that would increase her risk of toxicity. She has no active uncontrolled bleeding or bleeding diathesis, and no history of abdominal fistula or gastrointestinal perforation. She is willing to follow protocol requirements and has no active heart disease. She has no known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. She has not received cancer immunotherapy of any type within the past 2 weeks prior to initiation of CPI-613 treatment, and does not require immediate palliative treatment of any kind including surgery.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He has been taking medications for the past few years, but is now experiencing severe motor complications such as dyskinesia and freezing of gait. His tremors have also worsened and are impacting his speech. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medications regularly. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and enjoys reading and playing chess in his free time. He is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent. He has been scheduled for deep brain stimulation (DBS) implantation and is interested in participating in this research study to help further the understanding of Parkinson's disease and improve treatment options for future patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who tested positive for COVID-19 seven days ago. She has been experiencing fever, cough, sore throat, and fatigue. Her respiratory symptoms have worsened in the past 24 hours, but her oxygen saturation level is currently above 93% on room air. She has no known allergies to any of the components used in the formulation of the study drug or placebo. She has not received any medication for the treatment of COVID-19, including antiviral agents, convalescent serum, or anti-viral antibodies. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ensovibep in treating COVID-19.

A 28-week gestational age male preterm infant was born via emergency caesarean section due to premature rupture of membranes. The baby was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with a birth weight of 1.1 kg. His Apgar scores were 7 and 8 at 1 minute and 5 minutes, respectively. The baby has been intubated and started on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. He received surfactant replacement therapy and was started on prophylactic antibiotics. On day 7 of life, he developed temperature instability, apnea, and had positive blood cultures for gram-negative bacteria. The diagnosis of late onset sepsis was made, and the antibiotics were changed accordingly. The baby is now stable, but still requires oxygen support and antibiotic therapy. The baby meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of Pentoxifylline in late onset sepsis in preterm infants.

This is a 42-year-old active male who recently suffered a rupture of his Achilles tendon while playing basketball. He is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. He underwent surgical repair of his tendon and is now being invited to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of platelet concentrate injection in improving the mechanical properties of the repaired tendon. The patient has no counterindications for surgical treatment and meets the inclusion criteria for the trial. He is interested in participating in the study as he hopes it may improve his recovery and allow him to return to his active lifestyle sooner.

A 55-year-old male presents with a history of chronic stable angina and a recent abnormal exercise tolerance test showing ST-segment depression. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history. He has no prior history of diabetes and is not taking any anti-diabetic medication. His current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. He reports occasional chest pain with exertion that resolves with rest or sublingual nitroglycerin. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild hypertension (blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg). His resting electrocardiogram (ECG) shows normal sinus rhythm without any conduction disturbance. Echocardiography reveals normal left ventricular function. Coronary angiography confirms a >70% stenosis in a main epicardial artery. He is able to confidently walk on a treadmill. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is enrolled in the study. He is randomly assigned to either the GLP-1 treatment arm or the placebo arm and receives the corresponding injections for the next three weeks. His progress is monitored with serial exercise stress tests to evaluate the effect of GLP-1 receptor activation on exercise haemodynamics.

Pt is a 30yo F with a history of asthma, prescribed with low-dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) and short-acting beta agonist (SABA) as needed. Despite regular use of medication, the patient still experiences symptoms of asthma including wheezing and shortness of breath. The physician has decided to switch the patient to combination therapy of ICS and long-acting bronchodilator (LABA) via fixed-combination inhaler. The patient will be randomly assigned to either fluticasone propionate/salmeterol (Seretide®) via pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI) or dry-powder inhaler (DPI), with as-needed (prn) reliever therapy (salbutamol as DPI, BAI, or pMDI), or budesonide/formoterol (Symbicort®) via DPI with prn reliever therapy (salbutamol as DPI, BAI, or pMDI, or bricanyl as DPI). The patient will be asked to complete questionnaires about their asthma symptoms and medication use, as well as undergo lung function tests and provide blood samples. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of these combination therapies in managing asthma symptoms and improving lung function.

25-year-old healthy male non-smoker with a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2 is eligible for participation in this clinical trial. The patient has no history of respiratory disease and has never participated in a clinical trial or received any investigational product. The patient has not consumed any alcohol within the last six months and has no history of regular alcohol consumption. The patient is willing and able to follow the outlined procedures in the protocol and is capable of providing written informed consent. The patient has not used any prescription or non-prescription drugs, dietary supplements, or herbal remedies within seven days prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient has no clinically relevant abnormality identified at the screening medical assessment, including physical examination, medical history, clinical laboratory tests, or electrocardiogram. The patient has a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) greater than or equal to 80% predicted and a FEV1/Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) ratio greater than or equal to 0.7. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and is using an appropriate form of contraception. The patient is not a night shift worker and has not been exposed to more than four new chemical entities within the past 12 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American woman who has been diagnosed with stage 2 hypertension. Her blood pressure readings have consistently been above 160/100 mmHg at her last few visits to the doctor. She has a family history of hypertension and her father had a stroke in his 60s. She is currently not taking any medications for her hypertension. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known allergies to any medications. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days. She is currently not pregnant or nursing and is using reliable contraception. She has no history of malignancy or long QT syndrome. Her ECG shows a normal QTc interval. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who has been admitted to the hospital for elective surgery. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. The patient has previously undergone surgery and has had central lines inserted. He is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria. The patient has no contraindications to left jugular vein insertion and has no permanent or temporary pacemaker. The patient understands the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is presenting to the emergency department with a dislocated shoulder. She reports that the injury occurred while playing basketball earlier that day. The patient reports a history of anxiety and panic attacks, but she is not currently experiencing any anxiety symptoms. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and migraines, for which she takes lisinopril and sumatriptan, respectively. The patient denies any allergies to medications. Her baseline vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/76 mmHg, heart rate of 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. The patient weighs 70 kg. The physician determines that she requires procedural sedation for reduction of the dislocated shoulder. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent for procedural sedation. She is given ketofol in a 1 on 4 ratio as per the protocol, with a loading dose of 7 ml, followed by stepwise titration in aliquots of 3.5 ml. The procedural sedation is successful, and the patient is discharged home with instructions for follow-up with orthopedics.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer. He has no significant medical history and has never received chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He presents with abdominal pain, weight loss, and changes in bowel habits. CT scans reveal multiple liver and lung metastases. He is scheduled to begin first line treatment with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, indicating he is ambulatory and able to carry out light work. He has no history of central nervous system metastases or recent major surgical procedures. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and learning more about the potential benefits of adding bevacizumab to his chemotherapy regimen.

A 43-year-old female patient with a history of hypertension and obesity was admitted to the adult critical care unit at the Mayo Clinic, Rochester. The patient's lungs were mechanically ventilated, and she required elective transfusion of at least one unit of red cells. The patient is of African American ethnicity and is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with the study's outcomes. The patient will be randomized into one of two groups, one receiving red cells stored for 5 days or less, and the other receiving red cells stored conventionally (median 21 days). The patient will be monitored for mild alterations in pulmonary function and immune activation. The trial will be double-blind, and the patient's participation will be voluntary.

A 45-year-old male hydrocephalus patient, who underwent endoscopic ventriculostomy (EVT) four years ago, presented with worsening headaches, vision impairment, and difficulty in walking. MRI revealed enlarged ventricles and increased intracranial pressure. He was advised to undergo a valve shunt-based derivation system with the Polaris® 24 adjustable valve system. The patient is on medication for hypertension and is otherwise healthy. He has given his informed consent to participate in the SAPPHYRE study to evaluate the safety and performance of the Polaris® 24 adjustable valve system.

Patient A is a 10-year-old boy who has a history of peanut allergy with characteristic signs and symptoms, including hives, itching, and difficulty breathing. His allergy was diagnosed by a physician and confirmed by a positive skin prick test and serum IgE to peanut. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is currently using effective birth control as he is sexually active. There is no history of severe or life-threatening episode of anaphylaxis or anaphylactic shock within the past 60 days. The patient has mild asthma which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of eosinophilic esophagitis, other eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease, severe gastroesophageal reflux disease or any other chronic diseases. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and willing to be randomized to either receive AR101 or standard of care alone.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past year. She reports feeling a shooting pain down her legs when she stands or walks for prolonged periods. Her pain is usually relieved by sitting or lying down. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but has not found any lasting relief. She has been diagnosed with moderate to severe spinal canal stenosis on MRI. She has no history of previous spine surgeries. She lives alone and is independent in her daily activities. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially alleviate her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

A 58-year-old woman was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer that has metastasized to her liver. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, unexplained weight loss, and loss of appetite for the past 2 months. She has a history of smoking for 25 years but has quit 5 years ago. Her past medical history is unremarkable. She is currently taking no medications. Upon physical examination, the patient was found to have a palpable mass in the upper right quadrant of her abdomen. Laboratory workup showed a white blood cell count of 3,500/mm^3, a neutrophil count of 1,900/mm^3, and a platelet count of 110,000/mm^3. Her bilirubin level was within the normal range, as was her creatinine level. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 70%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help treat her cancer.

Patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma after presenting with abdominal pain and difficulty swallowing. Imaging studies showed no evidence of metastases, but staging laparoscopy is indicated by the internal work-up protocol. The patient has no known allergies or sensitivities to iodine. The patient has not received any prior treatment for gastric cancer. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and will undergo intravenous injection of ICG at different dosages and timepoints before the intervention. The patient will be evaluated for the feasibility and effectiveness of fluorescence-enhanced peritoneal carcinomatosis detection during staging laparoscopy. The study aims to establish if fluorescence imaging increases sensitivity and/or specificity of staging laparoscopy in detecting peritoneal carcinomatosis from gastric cancer. Improved accuracy may translate in better care path selection.

The patient is a 30-year-old first-time mother who recently gave birth to a premature baby at 31 weeks gestation. Her baby was admitted to the NICU at Vanderbilt Hospital due to respiratory distress syndrome and is anticipated to remain in the unit for at least two weeks. The mother is experiencing high levels of anxiety and stress due to her baby's hospitalization and is struggling to cope with the emotional toll of the situation. She has a history of depression and anxiety, but is currently not on any medication for these conditions. She is open to participating in the journaling program to help alleviate her anxiety and depression. She lives with her husband who is supportive and involved in their baby's care. She has a strong support system with her family and friends who have offered to help during this challenging time.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been diagnosed with asthma for the last 15 years. He has a history of frequent asthma exacerbations and is currently prescribed a combination of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists. Despite this, he still experiences shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness on a daily basis, which affects his daily activities. He is a non-smoker and works in an office environment. He has a BMI of 27 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He has never received biologic therapy for asthma before. He has no history of significant lung illness apart from asthma. He is interested in participating in clinical trials to help find a better treatment for his asthma.

A 4-month-old male infant was referred to the Clinic with a complete cleft lip and palate. The patient was born at term with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. The infant has been gaining weight appropriately and is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. The parents are eager to have the cleft lip repaired and have consented to participate in the clinical trial. The infant has no history of surgery and has not undergone any previous procedures. The patient is free of any systemic conditions and is medically fit for surgery. The patient meets all inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible for surgery.

The patient is a 34 year old Hispanic male who works as a construction worker. He has a history of hypertension and has been seeing the primary care physician at the local community clinic for the past 2 years. He is married and has two children. He is fluent in English and is comfortable using computers and mobile devices. He is interested in learning more about his electronic health records and wants to have more control over who can access his personal health information. He is willing to participate in the study and provide his preferences for access to his health records. He has not experienced any major health issues in the past year and is generally in good health.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy, approximately 8 weeks gestation. She is experiencing high levels of stress, as evidenced by her responses to the Perceived Stress Level Questionnaire. This is her second pregnancy, her first child is a healthy two-year-old. The patient has a history of mild morning sickness in her prior pregnancy, but it did not interfere with her ability to take supplements. She does not have any history of diabetes or major medical illnesses. She is interested in participating in this study to explore natural supplements as a way to mediate the effects of stress on fetal development.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with mucosal melanoma. She has no history of any other type of cancer or previous anti-cancer treatments. She is currently experiencing no symptoms related to her cancer. The tumor is located in her nasal cavity, which is considered resectable. The patient is medically fit and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has no known autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency, or active infection requiring systemic therapy. She has no history of major surgeries within the past 4 weeks, and adequate wound healing has been confirmed. Her cardiovascular function is good, with no history of congestive heart failure, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, cerebral vascular accident, or cardiac arrhythmia associated with hemodynamic instability. Her urine protein level is normal, and the prolongation of QTc interval is not observed. The patient is willing to provide a biopsy at baseline and is able to swallow and retain oral medication. The patient is willing to use an adequate method of contraception and has a negative urine pregnancy test. She has no known hypersensitivity to the components of the study therapy or its analogs.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently not pregnant and has never been pregnant before. She is in good health and has no known medical conditions. She does not smoke, use any illicit drugs, or consume more than two alcoholic drinks per week. She has no family history of heart disease or any other significant medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent. She has no other commitments or medical issues that would prevent her from completing the study requirements.

The patient is a 23-year-old male who is physically active and participates in organized sports 2 times per week. He does not have any chronic medical conditions such as diabetes or renal disease, and his BMI is within the normal range. He is not a vegetarian and does not follow a special diet that deviates from the standard of young adults. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the impact of different types of carbohydrates on the absorption kinetics of protein-derived amino acids and the impact on myofibrillar protein synthesis. He is willing to perform a bout of whole body resistance exercise and consume a meat hydrolysate supplement labeled with D5-phenylalanine together with randomized and double blinded type of carbohydrate consisting of either glucose or cluster dextrin. He understands that the study involves a randomized double blinded crossover design and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently returned from a business trip to China. He started experiencing symptoms such as fever, cough, and shortness of breath within a week of his return. He went to the hospital and was diagnosed with COVID-19 through a laboratory test (RT-PCR) and imaging showed lung damage. He is currently in the early stages of the disease, having been diagnosed less than 8 days ago. He has no history of liver or renal disease, and his pregnancy test is negative. He has not taken any experimental treatment drugs for COVID-19 in the last 30 days. He does not have a history of thromboembolism except for those caused by PICC. He is concerned about the progression of the disease and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive treatment with Thalidomide. He is a smoker with a history of smoking a pack a day for the last 20 years. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure is 135/80. He works in the IT sector and is currently working remotely due to the outbreak. He lives with his wife and two children.

A 45 year old woman with no history of traumatic brain injury (TBI), and no current neurological conditions, comes to the clinic for screening in the Brain Injury Biomarkers in the General Population study. She is fluent in English and willing to provide consent for the study. She has not donated blood in the past week and venipuncture is feasible. She is in good health with no medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. The principal investigator believes she is an appropriate candidate for the study.

This is a 45 year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 2 years, despite being treated with an antiarrhythmic drug for more than 6 weeks. He has experienced multiple episodes of AF, with symptoms of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history, and is currently not taking any other medications. He has been advised to undergo catheter ablation, and has been referred for the Ultra-High-Resolution Mapping Guided Partial Antral Ablation for AF clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the trial and is available for a follow-up of at least three months after the catheter ablation.

A 21-year-old woman with social phobia came to the clinic for the study. She reported feeling extremely anxious in social situations, such as parties and public speaking, which has affected her personal and professional life. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 years. She has tried cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) in the past but did not see significant improvement. She is currently not taking any psychotropic medications, and her medical history is unremarkable. She has no history of neurological disorders or substance use. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo physical examination, urine test, and an electrocardiogram (EKG), as well as tests involving problem-solving and memory, and to prepare and present a speech to a "virtual audience" using virtual reality goggles. She understands that she will be randomly assigned to receive either d-cycloserine (DCS) or a placebo (sugar pill) before each of the 12 CBT sessions. She is willing to participate in the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) while performing tasks that involve looking at pictures, remembering things, testing reaction times, and making simple choices. She is also willing to complete a follow-up assessment 3 months after her last CBT session.

A 42-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 who has struggled with obesity for most of her adult life. She has already tried multiple diets and exercise regimens, but has not been able to achieve significant weight loss. She is interested in weight loss surgery, but is uncertain which procedure would be best for her. She has no history of diabetes, psychiatric disorders, or substance abuse, and is not currently taking any medications that affect body weight or blood glucose. She is willing to remain weight stable for the duration of the study if assigned to the non-surgical group.

A 35-year-old highly myopic woman presenting with decreased vision in her left eye, which started 2 weeks ago. She has a history of high myopia since childhood and was previously treated with contact lenses. Examination showed a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/400 in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye. Slit-lamp examination was normal in both eyes. Fundus examination revealed a full-thickness macular hole associated with macular detachment in the left eye. The axial length of the left eye was measured as 28.2 mm. Optical coherence tomography confirmed the diagnosis. The patient was enrolled in the study as she met the inclusion criteria and did not have any exclusion criteria. Her medical history was otherwise unremarkable.

32 F with a history of migraines since age 18, currently experiencing chronic daily headaches with an average of 20 headache days per month. She has been taking over-the-counter pain medication daily for the past 6 months and has noticed that the effectiveness of the medication has decreased over time. She has tried to stop taking the medication but experiences rebound headaches. She presents to the headache clinic seeking a solution to her chronic headaches and medication overuse. Physical exam is unremarkable. She meets the criteria for migrainous headaches and medication-overuse headaches according to the International Headache Society. She has not been on any prophylactic treatment for migraines. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the feasibility of a home withdrawal treatment with normobaric oxygen therapy delivered by a high flow concentrator as a therapeutic measure to treat headache through the withdrawal period. She is willing to sign informed consent and agrees to attend all study visits.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of gross hematuria and lower abdominal pain. He underwent cystoscopy and biopsy, which revealed muscle-invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder (stage III). Imaging studies showed no evidence of metastatic disease. He is deemed ineligible for neoadjuvant cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy by the attending medical oncologist. He is willing to undergo radical cystectomy and is eligible for the surgery. He has no prior history of malignancy except for adequately treated basal cell skin cancer. He is not taking any investigational agent and has not received any systemic chemotherapy for transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder in the past. He is willing to take oral medication (dasatinib) and is able to comply with the treatment schedule. He is on stable doses of medications for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. His ECOG Performance Status is 1, and his life expectancy is not specified. His hematopoietic parameters are within normal limits. Total bilirubin is within normal limits, and liver enzymes (AST and ALT) are within 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. His serum creatinine is within normal limits. He has no uncontrolled angina, congestive heart failure or MI within 6 months prior to registration on the study. He has no diagnosed congenital long QT syndrome or history of clinically significant ventricular arrhythmias. His QTc interval is within normal limits. He is willing to use an effective method of contraception until 4 weeks after treatment discontinuation. He does not have any significant infections, pleural or pericardial effusion, or bleeding disorders.

A 63-year-old man was admitted to the ICU with septic shock and acute kidney injury (AKI) following a urinary tract infection. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and required invasive mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. His medical history included hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His serum creatinine on admission was 200 µmol/L and his urine output was < 0.5 cc/kg over > 4 hrs. He required a contrast-enhanced CT scan to evaluate for possible septic emboli. He was considered 'at risk' for the development of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) and was approached for enrollment in the study. He consented and met all inclusion criteria. He did not have CK > 5,000 or the presence of myoglobinuria, a known allergy or hypersensitivity reaction to radiographic contrast dye or NAC, serious illness with imminent threat of dying (low likelihood of survival within 48-hours) or poor prognosis, pregnancy, patients with cardiogenic shock (NYHA class 3 or 4 symptoms), known or suspected nephritic, nephrotic or pulmonary-renal syndromes, a post renal etiology of renal impairment, previous renal transplant, known solitary kidney, serum creatinine > 200 µmol/L or recent exposure to radiographic contrast within 14 days of randomization.

Patient A is a 40-year-old male who recently suffered a closed femur fracture due to a high-energy trauma. He is scheduled for surgery within the next 10 days and has been informed about the AO Multicenter Intervention Trial for Prevention of Surgical Site Infection. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent. He has no history of chronic bone or joint infection, and is not pregnant or planning to conceive within the study period. He is not currently participating in any other medical device or medicinal product study that could influence the results of the present study.

The patient is a 17-month-old baby boy who has been diagnosed with congenital heart disease and requires heart surgery. The surgery will be performed using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and the child will be receiving dexmedetomidine as per standard of care. The child has sufficient venous access to permit administration of the study medication. The parents/legal guardians are available and willing to provide written informed consent for the child's participation in the study. The child is not less than 38 weeks post menstrual age and does not have any concomitant condition that would preclude their participation in the study. Additionally, the CPB circuit is not primed with clear fluid. The child will be closely monitored during the study to evaluate how the heart-lung bypass machine affects dexmedetomidine levels in the body.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who received a renal transplant from a deceased donor due to end-stage renal disease. He has been on immunosuppression therapy with a calcineurin inhibitor since the transplantation. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2 and no history of cardiac arrhythmia or lower limb occlusive arterial disease. He is able to understand the information form and has provided written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

58 year old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking, who presented to the emergency department with a sudden onset of left sided weakness and slurred speech. A CT scan showed an acute ischemic stroke in the right middle cerebral artery territory. The patient received intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of symptom onset and was subsequently transferred to a stroke ICU for further management. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to be contacted by telephone during the follow-up period.

A 65-year-old African American man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and facial droop. He was diagnosed with a mild ischemic stroke and was admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He is able to comply with all study procedures and will be available for the duration of the study. He met the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria such as a history of bleeding diathesis, active peptic ulcer disease, or inability to swallow oral medications. He does not have a pre-stroke modified Rankin scale score of 3 or higher, which means he has no significant disability before the stroke. The patient is not currently taking any antiplatelet medications for an indication other than ischemic stroke during the study period, which would prevent the investigator from following the study algorithm. He has no known contraindications to aspirin, clopidogrel, Aggrenox®, or ticagrelor. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity that would prevent the investigator from following the study algorithm. He is not currently participating in another non-observational clinical study. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 1 year, in the opinion of the investigative team.

The patient is a 70-year-old man diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease according to the NINCDS-ADRDA criteria. He has mild-moderate symptoms of dementia, including memory loss, confusion, and difficulty with daily living activities. He has been taking cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine for the last month. His Mini Mental Test score is between 13-24 points. He lives with his wife, who is proficient in the use of technology. He understands instructions given in Turkish. He does not have any other pulmonary, neurological, musculoskeletal or rheumatological disease that may prevent exercise. He is in a stable medical condition with controlled diabetes and hypertension. His Modified Charlson Comorbidity Index score is less than or equal to 6. He does not receive any rehabilitation service from an institution or person. He does not have regular exercise habits. He does not have any visual or auditory deficits or behavioral problems that would make communication difficult.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with nonmetastatic pancreatic cancer that is not removable by surgery. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, jaundice, and unintended weight loss for the past few months. He underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. He has a WHO performance status of 1 and his bilirubin level is 1.5 mg/dL. His creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL, and his WBC count is 4,500/mm³. He has no major organ disorders and his prothrombin time is 85%. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this cancer. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently undergone a complete resection of a lung tumor. The surgery was successful, and the patient's resection margins were negative for any residual tumor. The patient has a history of heavy cigarette smoking, with a smoking history of 40 pack-years. The patient had no prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy, and the histological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell lung carcinoma of stage pT2N2M0. The patient was determined to be at high risk of locoregional recurrence based on a clinical risk prediction model that included heavy cigarette smoking history, cN2 status, and the number of involved lymph nodes. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, with no severe perioperative complications, and an expected postoperative lifespan of more than 4 months. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has good compliance with the study procedures and is willing to cooperate with the relevant examination, treatment, and follow-up. The patient has no prior or concurrent malignancies except for basal cell carcinoma of the skin. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has not undergone prior preoperative Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) treatment or other targeted therapy.

The patient is a healthy adult who is 25 years old and fluent in English. They are interested in participating in a study that collects vocalization data during regular daily activity. The patient has no history of skin allergies to medical adhesive tape and is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol. They are excited to contribute to the research and help advance understanding of adult social interaction.

This is a 56-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with NSTEMI and is scheduled for subacute PCI in native vessels. He has a significant culprit lesion with more than 50% of coronary stenosis at the catheterization laboratory in Odense. He has been on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel for the past week. He has no history of allergies to aspirin, ticagrelor, clopidogrel, and prasugrel. He has a normal renal function with a serum creatinine level of 98 ug/L. The lesion length is less than 28 mm, and he has no aorta-ostial lesions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing coronary healing after optical coherence tomography guided versus conventionally angiography guided PCI with the Magmaris bioresorbable scaffold.

The patient is a 13-year-old male diagnosed with anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) that has relapsed after receiving first-line treatment. He was initially diagnosed with ALCL six months ago and received standard chemotherapy. However, recently he has been experiencing worsening symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. The patient has no known history of other systemic diseases, severe infections, or critical illnesses. He has never been a smoker, and he does not use any illicit drugs. His family history is negative for any history of cancer. The patient's current medications include acetaminophen for pain relief. The patient is currently receiving care at the Shanghai Children's Medical Center. The patient's physician has recommended vinorelbine monotherapy as a potential treatment option for his recurrent ALCL. The patient and his family have been informed about the clinical trial and have expressed interest in participating.

A 56-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer. He underwent 4 cycles of first-line chemotherapy with cisplatin and pemetrexed, which resulted in a partial response. He has no history of brain metastases or any other significant medical history. His performance status is ECOG 1. He is currently not receiving any other anti-tumor therapy or radiation. He is willing to report medication taken, concomitant medications, and adverse events. He is willing to use a medically accepted method of contraception or be surgically sterilized prior to screening, while receiving study drug, and for 30 days after stopping study drug. He has no symptomatic, progressive, or new bone metastases following the first-line chemotherapy with or without radiation therapy. He is able to adhere to the dosing and visit schedules. He is willing to participate in this study for the purpose of investigating the potential benefits of maintenance temozolomide.

The clinical trial is seeking children between the ages of 0 to 6 years with non-progressive chronic neurological involvement, such as cerebral palsy or Down Syndrome, and respiratory complications such as pneumonia or bronchitis. The study will assess the effectiveness of chest therapy and postural hygiene workshops in improving respiratory clinical signs, increasing expectoration of bronchial secretions, and improving the quality of life of children with these conditions. The study will involve 30 children from various centers of early care and foundations in the Community of Madrid. Participants must have their parents or guardians sign informed consent, and must not have previous respiratory pathology in itself or be affected by immunodeficiency or hemato-oncological process. The study will exclude patients with cardiovascular instability, drained pneumothorax, recent pneumonectomy, severe bullae, and hemoptysis.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer. The patient has opted for a robotic prostatectomy, which will be performed by a participating surgeon. The patient is willing to be randomized between the intervention and control arms of the study. The patient has not undergone any prior pelvic radiation, androgen deprivation therapy, localized ablative therapy, TURP, or any other surgical BPH treatment. The patient is in good health with no other significant medical conditions. The patient has undergone CT scans and MRIs, and the digital virtual reality models will be created using these images. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve patient care for future generations.

A 25-year-old healthy female came to the clinic for a routine eye exam. She has no known ocular or systemic diseases and her medical history is unremarkable. She wears glasses for mild myopia and has not worn contact lenses for over a month. She has no known hypersensitivity to any medication and is not taking any chronic topical or systemic medications. She uses reliable contraception and has a negative urine pregnancy test. Her best corrected visual acuity is at least 20/40 in each eye. She has not participated in any ophthalmic drug or device research study within the last 30 days.
